title: Fix OpenAI Client error with single request via batch api
author: ravi03071991
body:
Hello,

The current OpenAI Client Batch API fails when the batch contains only a single request, returning the following error:

![Screenshot 2025-05-10 at 1 58 06 PM](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7a1ea179-b098-47cd-8b43-b6cf1fa95c8e)

This issue becomes a blocker when running evaluations at varying batch sizes (e.g., 1, 100, 200, etc.). This PR fixes the problem by ensuring that batches with a single request are handled correctly.

We can reproduce the issue using the following code:

```python
from sglang.utils import launch_server_cmd
from sglang.utils import wait_for_server, print_highlight, terminate_process

import json
import time
from openai import OpenAI


server_process, port = launch_server_cmd(
    "python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path qwen/qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct --host 0.0.0.0 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --port 80000" 
)

wait_for_server(f"http://localhost:{port}")
print(f"Server started on http://localhost:{port}")

client = OpenAI(base_url=f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/v1", api_key="None")

requests = [
    {
        "custom_id": "request-2",
        "method": "POST",
        "url": "/chat/completions",
        "body": {
            "model": "qwen/qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct",
            "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is Python?"}],
            "max_tokens": 50,
        },
    },
]

input_file_path = "batch_requests2.jsonl"

with open(input_file_path, "w") as f:
    for req in requests:
        f.write(json.dumps(req) + "\n")

with open(input_file_path, "rb") as f:
    file_response = client.files.create(file=f, purpose="batch")

batch_response = client.batches.create(
    input_file_id=file_response.id,
    endpoint="/v1/chat/completions",
    completion_window="24h",
)

print_highlight(f"Batch job created with ID: {batch_response.id}")
```

Fixes #6200

title: [Bug] Fix accidental logger override caused by internVL.
author: lifuhuang
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation

I noticed that sglang stopped logging info level logs whenever I use multimodal models. E.g. there is no "the server is fired up and ready to roll" when I load any multimodal model:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/021471a2-9407-4e6c-a1dc-a82ca229a870)

I debugged a little bit and found out it's introduced in #5350: sglang loads all processors when loading multimodal model, and internvl introduced numpy.distutils which has a known bug (see: https://github.com/numpy/numpy/issues/24213). 
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b3b56b6-a49a-4762-9e5f-f67dfc95c7c1)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9113a836-1e8e-474b-9348-1bab5566ee5c)

Upon further reading, I found out the introduction of this package might have been a bug itself, as the only location where `cpu` is used is actually expecting `decord.cpu` instead of `numpy.distutils.cpuinfo.cpu`, so I removed the line and the logging is working again:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c570b9c0-fe60-490a-9e4b-abb8f27faffe)

## Modifications

title: fix: allow `launch_dummy_health_check_server` to start inside of running asyncio loop
author: ishandhanani
body:
When running a model across multiple nodes, if the engine API is called from inside of an asyncio loop, running the `launch_dummy_health_check_server` will fail with the error 

```bash
File "/workspace/examples/sglang/components/worker.py", line 57, in __init__
    self.engine = sgl.Engine(server_args=self.engine_args)
                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/opt/dynamo/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/sglang/api.py", line 45, in Engine
    return Engine(*args, **kwargs)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/opt/dynamo/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py", line 125, in __init__
    tokenizer_manager, scheduler_info = _launch_subprocesses(
                                        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/opt/dynamo/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py", line 609, in _launch_subprocesses
    launch_dummy_health_check_server(server_args.host, server_args.port)
  File "/opt/dynamo/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/sglang/srt/utils.py", line 1869, in launch_dummy_health_check_server
    uvicorn.run(
  File "/opt/dynamo/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/uvicorn/main.py", line 580, in run
    server.run()
  File "/opt/dynamo/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/uvicorn/server.py", line 66, in run
    return asyncio.run(self.serve(sockets=sockets))
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/lib/python3.12/asyncio/runners.py", line 190, in run
    raise RuntimeError(
RuntimeError: asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop
sys:1: RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'Server.serve' was never awaited
```

To solve this - we change the function to first check if there's a running loop. If so we use `uvicorn.serve()` otherwise we use the default `uvicorn.run`.

title: [fix] illegal memory in _fwd_kernel_ep_scatter_2 and _fwd_kernel_ep_gather
author: xutizhou
body: ## Motivation when deploying large scale ep deepseek, the prefill node sometimes meets illegal memory error with heavy workload as following this is caused by the index overflow in _fwd_kernel_ep_scatter_2. ## Modifications replace int32 index with int64 to avoid overflow. CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 python test.py to reproduce the illegal memory error: ``` import torch from sglang.srt.layers.moe.ep_moe.kernels import ep_scatter, ep_gather import time N, D, D_ = 235234*3, 7168, 56 E = 9 N_ = 304000*3 recv_x = torch.randn((N, D), device="cuda").to(torch.float8_e4m3fn) recv_x_scale = torch.randn((N, D_), device="cuda").to(torch.float) num_recv_tokens_per_expert = 3*torch.tensor([0, 107904, 178304, 240000, 273536, 284288, 292736, 296832, 301440, 304000], device="cuda").to(torch.int32) num_recv_tokens_per_expert[1:] = num_recv_tokens_per_expert[1:] - num_recv_tokens_per_expert[:-1] recv_topk = torch.empty((N, E), device="cuda").to(torch.int64) recv_topk.fill_(-1) recv_topk_weight = torch.empty((N, E), device="cuda").to(torch.float) for i in range(E): num = num_recv_tokens_per_expert[i + 1].item() recv_topk[-num:, i] = i expert_start_loc = torch.empty_like(num_recv_tokens_per_expert) output_tensor = torch.zeros((N_, D), device="cuda").to(torch.float8_e4m3fn) output_tensor_scale = torch.empty((N_, D_), device="cuda").to(torch.float) m_indices = torch.empty(N_, device="cuda").to(torch.int32) output_index = torch.randn((N, E), device="cuda").to(torch.int64) ep_scatter( recv_x, recv_x_scale, recv_topk, num_recv_tokens_per_expert, expert_start_loc, output_tensor, output_tensor_scale, m_indices, output_index, ) down_output = torch.randn((N_, D), device="cuda").to(torch.bfloat16) gather_out = torch.empty((N, D), device="cuda").to(torch.bfloat16) ep_gather(down_output, recv_topk, recv_topk_weight, output_index, gather_out) print(output_tensor[0]) print(gather_out[0]) print("passed examine") ``` Many thanks to Ch-Wan () for identifying the index overflow as the cause and for providing main part of the test script. ``` Co-authored-by:ch-wan ``` ## Checklist - author: chen700564
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Explain the purpose of this PR and the goals it aims to achieve. -->
Adjust the input for the OpenAI API

1. Keep the full `tool` dictionary in the input, consistent with vLLM, instead of only retaining the `function` field.

2. After a `tool_call` is generated, it is structured as:
```python
{
  ...,
  "function": {
    "name": "xxx",
    "arguments": "json.dumps(...)"
  }
}
```

When `tool_call` appears in the conversation history, using `tokenizer.apply_chat_template` causes the `arguments` part to be the result of `json.dumps`, which does not align with the original output. title: fix: force synchronization between TP workers when update_weights
author: dangkai4u
body:
## Motivation

In VerlEngine, when TP0 worker in verl sends generate or update_weights_from_tensor requests to the scheduler, other TP workers are not blocked. This can lead to potential issues, such as inconsistent parameter updates (if loaded_weights is a temporary Tensor buffer that is frequently overwritten) and slow generation speed (40 tokens/s, causing nccl timeout). This issue is particularly prominent when loading large-scale models with tensor parallelism.

## Modifications

* add synchronization  barrier in VerlEngine and Scheduler to ensure consistency

## Explaination

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/46c33e4c-0139-4f3f-a121-c9db93640ae8)

* After SGLang `TP=0` updated the `lm_head.weights` parameters, ShardingManager performed an all-gather operation on `embed_tokens.weights` and overwrote the old tensor buffer (a custom optimization to solve OOM issues during param sync). At this point, when SGLang `TP=1` attempts to update lm_head.weights parameters, it would be updating with incorrect parameter values.


Special thanks to @hapsunday for helping resolve this issue.

title: fix(deepseekv3): Fix DeepSeekV3Detector tool_index assignment and multi-tool call streaming support
author: CatherineSue
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation
This PR focuses to fix the current two issues in `DeepSeekV3Detector`.

1. tool_index: Current the tool_index of each ToolCallItem is assigned based on the index of the function name in the tools list passed by the request. See: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/6550#discussion_r2105523139
The correct behavior should be the index of the current tool call in the response tool_calls list.
2. DeepSeekV3Detector is not parsing multi-tools correctly. See: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/6589#issuecomment-2908033411

<!-- Explain the purpose of this PR and the goals it aims to achieve. -->

## Modifications
- Fix tool_index to use call sequence position instead of tool array position
- Add support for detecting subsequent tool calls without bot_token prefix
- Implement smart buffer management to preserve multiple tool calls
- Maintain adapter.py integration state arrays for streaming compatibility

This resolves issues where:
1. Tool calls were assigned incorrect indices based on tool definition order
2. Second and subsequent tool calls were treated as normal text
3. Buffer was cleared completely, losing subsequent tool call data

<!-- Describe the changes made in this PR. -->

title: refactor(tool call): Fix BaseFormatDetector tool_index issue and refactor `parse_streaming_increment`
author: CatherineSue
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation
1. Fix #6310 
2. Non-stream function call response in OpenAI doesn't have index. We should remove that. See: https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/chat/object
3. Refactor `parse_streaming_increment` in `BaseFormatDetector`

The current  `parse_streaming_increment` in `BaseFormatDetector` has some issues:

### The Original Problem

1. For a single tool call in streaming, the first tool_index should be 0, but it was assigned as the index of the function in the tools list passed by user's request.

2. When there were multiple tool calls, the tool_index was always 0 instead of being sequential (0, 1, 2, etc.). This was because:
- `self.current_tool_id = len(tool_call_arr) - 1` jumped directly to the last tool in the current `tool_call_arr`, which is reinitialized as [] every time of the function call. But the current_tool_id should be the index of the tool processed in the `calls` list
- Complex array handling logic caused state inconsistencies in the entire function

### Refactor Details

1. Removed tool_call_arr and is_complete arrays

**Why:**
- The array `tool_call_arr` was being **rebuilt from scratch** on every streaming increment, but `self.current_tool_id` update based on `len(tool_call_arr)`. 
- This caused state inconsistencies because previous state was lost
- The logic was overly complex and hard to maintain
- They seemed to be designed for a different use case (single JSON array with multiple tools). However, based on the following content, it then assumes the obj is never a list but a dictionary:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/bdb962d75581faa8d472fbbc8b05987c27df6a88/python/sglang/srt/function_call/base_format_detector.py#L158-L164

**Why it won't affect us:**
- We're focusing on the common case where obj is always a single tool object (dict)
- Each tool call is processed independently
- We don't need to track multiple tools in a single parsing call

2. Removed the Entire `Case 1: Handle new tool discovered in array` Section

**Why we removed Case 1:**
Case 1 was unreachable in the original case, because
- `tool_call_array = [obj]` always has length 1 (single tool object)
- So `1 > current_tool_id + 1` is only true when current_tool_id = -1 (initialization) , but the initialization can be easily handled in Case 2.

**Why it won't affect us:**
- Tool switching now happens naturally when each tool completes in Case 2
- Each tool call is processed in separate streaming sessions
- We don't need complex logic to detect "new tools in an array"

3. Proper State Management
- Ensured `streamed_args_for_tool` is properly sized for each new tool, as it is used in `adapter.py` (Not sure the reason yet)
- Added bounds checking for prev_tool_call_arr access
- Correct tool_index assignment using the right ID for completing vs. ongoing tools

4. The Flow Now Works Like This
- Tool 1 starts: `current_tool_id = 0`, sends tool name with tool_index=0
- Tool 1 completes: `current_tool_id` increments to 1, buffer clears
- Tool 2 starts: Uses `current_tool_id = 1`, sends tool name with tool_index=1
- Tool 2 completes: `current_tool_id` increments to 2, and so on...

<!-- Explain the purpose of this PR and the goals it aims to achieve. -->

## Modifications

<!-- Describe the changes made in this PR. -->

- Simplify parsing logic by removing `tool_call_arr` and `is_complete` arrays 
- Add proper current_tool_id increment when tool completes (original `Case 3: Handle streaming arguments` with is_complete=True)
- Ensure correct `tool_index` assignment before incrementing `current_tool_id`
- Remove index in non-stream tool call in `adapter.py`

title: Fix incorrect LoRA weight loading for fused gate_up_proj
author: lifuhuang
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation

During testing, I identified two bugs introduced in my previous PR for supporting phi-4-mm.

1. (Major impact) I introduced fused LoRA weight support in my prev PR, however, I did not correctly handle gate_up_proj shape. This problem was not caught earlier because pytorch implicitly handled shape mismatch through broadcast. 

3. (Minor impact) I had an incorrect understanding of the seqlens calculation for Idefics embedding. When tgt_sizes is absent, input_embeds should not have been masked. **MMMU score for phi4 mm increased from 47 to 53.1 after these two fixes, consistent with vLLM (difference within random error). Both vLLM and SGLang are slightly lower than the benchmark reported in the original paper, but the difference might be due to different sampling params or benchmark script**.
| Framework        | MMMU          |
|------------------|---------------|
| **SGLang**          |    **53.1**           |
| vLLM           |     52.5          |
| original paper |   55            |

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/207b908c-ba98-4788-89d4-1e10f7bae2eb)

title: [CPU] fix all_reduce and all_gather
author: chunyuan-w
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation
Fix the error of all_reduce and all_gather on CPU
all_reduce:
```
  File "/home/user/sglang/python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py", line 418, in all_reduce
    import intel_extension_for_pytorch as ipex
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'intel_extension_for_pytorch'
```
I guess the code is directly ported from vllm [here](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.6.4.post1/vllm/distributed/parallel_state.py#L367-L368) while SGLang does not have the dependency on ipex.

all_gather:
```
  File "/home/user/sglang/python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py", line 496, in all_gather_into_tensor
    torch.ops.sglang.reg_all_gather_into_tensor(
  File "/home/user/miniforge3/envs/sglang-dev/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/_ops.py", line 1123, in __call__
    return self._op(*args, **(kwargs or {}))
NotImplementedError: Could not run 'sglang::reg_all_gather_into_tensor' with arguments from the 'CPU' backend. This could be because the operator doesn't exist for this backend, or was omitted during the selective/custom build process (if using custom build). If you are a Facebook employee using PyTorch on mobile, please visit https://fburl.com/ptmfixes for possible resolutions. 'sglang::reg_all_gather_into_tensor' is only available for these backends: [CUDA, Meta, BackendSelect, Python, FuncTorchDynamicLayerBackMode, Functionalize, Named, Conjugate, Negative, ZeroTensor, ADInplaceOrView, AutogradOther, AutogradCPU, AutogradCUDA, AutogradXLA, AutogradMPS, AutogradXPU, AutogradHPU, AutogradLazy, AutogradMTIA, AutogradMeta, Tracer, AutocastCPU, AutocastXPU, AutocastMPS, AutocastCUDA, FuncTorchBatched, BatchedNestedTensor, FuncTorchVmapMode, Batched, VmapMode, FuncTorchGradWrapper, PythonTLSSnapshot, FuncTorchDynamicLayerFrontMode, PreDispatch, PythonDispatcher].
```


## Modification
- For all_reduce and all_gather, use `torch.ops.sgl_kernel.shm_allreduce` and `torch.ops.sgl_kernel.shm_allgather` for CPU.
- For the `shm_allreduce` and `shm_allgather` OPs, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/7486 will remove the `process_group` input parameters  and this PR handles it in python code to fix the below error:
```
RuntimeError: sgl_kernel::shm_allreduce() Expected a value of type '__torch__.torch.classes.c10d.ProcessGroup (of Python compilation unit at: 0)' for argument 'process_group' but instead found type 'ProcessGroup'.
```

title: fix(PD-disaggregation): Can not get local ip
author: storyicon
body:
## Motivation

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7158769d-ff58-4935-b9dd-61a699e8e53a)

While performing a PD-disaggregation deployment, I encountered an issue with the `get_local_ip_by_remote` function. From the source code, I observed that it first attempts to obtain the local IPv4 address by connecting to `8.8.8.8`. If this fails, it silently falls back to connecting to `2001:4860:4860::8888` to retrieve the local IPv6 address.

The code comments state, "Doesn't need to be reachable," which holds true if the local host has public internet access (even if restricted by a WAF). However, in enterprise networks or private cloud environments (e.g., VPC), access to the public internet is typically blocked, with no gateway available for public internet connectivity. This leads to the issue shown above, where the function fails entirely.

## Modifications

This PR introduces a fallback mechanism via hostname resolution to ensure the correct local IP is returned even in environments without public internet routing. It enhances the function's robustness in restricted networks while maintaining cross-platform compatibility and simplicity.

Now everything is working smoothly.

title: bugfix(OAI): Fix image_data processing for jinja chat templates
author: CatherineSue
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation

This PR fixes a critical issue where multimodal inference fails when using custom .jinja chat templates with the OpenAI API adapter. The problem prevents models like Llama4 from processing images correctly.

When using custom .jinja chat templates (via `chat_template_name = None` path), image data was being incorrectly processed:
- Image content extraction: The adapter was stripping out `image_url` content from messages before passing them to `apply_chat_template()`
- Missing image tokens: Without image content in messages, jinja templates couldn't generate proper <|image|> tokens
- Broken multimodal pipeline: `load_mm_data()` couldn't find image tokens to match with image data, causing `process_mm_data()` to fail

Current Behavior (before fix):

Start a Llama-4 server with a jinja template:

```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model /models/meta-llama/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct 
--tp-size=4 
--host=0.0.0.0 
--mem-fraction-static=0.95 
--context-length=196608 
--enable-multimodal 
--tool-call-parser=pythonic 
--chat-template=examples/chat_template/tool_chat_template_llama4_pythonic.jinja 
```

Send an image request, you will always get:
```
ChatCompletion(id='574d680bce7b4df4b2e44103129c0f8e', choices=[
Choice(finish_reason='stop', index=0, logprobs=None, 
message=ChatCompletionMessage(
content="I don't see an image. I'm a text-based AI assistant and do not have the capability to visually see or access images. I can only respond based on text input. If you'd like to describe the image, I'd be happy to try and help!", refusal=None, role='assistant', audio=None, function_call=None, tool_calls=None, reasoning_content=None), matched_stop=200008)], created=1749061840, 
model='/models/meta-llama/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct', object='chat.completion', service_tier=None, system_fingerprint=None, usage=CompletionUsage(
completion_tokens=51, prompt_tokens=16, total_tokens=67, completion_tokens_details=None, prompt_tokens_details=None))
```

PR Behavior (after fix):
Send an image request:
```
ChatCompletion(id='941f649e9fe5434abc3e1e170009f73e', choices=[
Choice(finish_reason='length', index=0, logprobs=None, message=ChatCompletionMessage(
content='The image presents a line graph illustrating the relationship between 
Output Inference Speed per Request and Output Throughput of Server, with a 
specific scenario labeled as D(2000,200). The graph features a blue line connecting 
data points, each marked by a blue dot. The x-axis represents the Output Throughput of Server in tokens per second (tokens/s), ranging from 0 to 3000, while the y-axis represents the Output Inference Speed per Request in tokens/s, spanning from 25 to 200.\n\nHere is a detailed breakdown of the data points:\n\n*   The first data point is located at approximately (0, 200), although the exact x-coordinate is not provided.\n*   The subsequent data points are positioned at:\n    *   (approximately 250, 150) with a label of 2\n    *   (approximately 500, 125) with a label of 4\n    *   (approximately 750, 100) with a label of 8\n    *   (approximately 1250, 90) with a label of 16\n    *   (approximately 1750, 75) with a label of 32\n    *   (approximately 2250, 60) with a label of 64\n    *   (approximately 2750, 40) with a label of 128\n    *   (approximately 3000, 25) with a label of 256\n\nThe graph reveals a', refusal=None, role='assistant', audio=None, function_call=None, tool_calls=None, reasoning_content=None), matched_stop=None)], created=1749075539, model='/models/meta-llama/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct', object='chat.completion', service_tier=None, 
system_fingerprint=None, usage=CompletionUsage(
completion_tokens=300, prompt_tokens=1033, total_tokens=1333, completion_tokens_details=None, prompt_tokens_details=None))
```

Both image response and prompt_tokens are correct. 

<!-- Explain the purpose of this PR and the goals it aims to achieve. -->

## Modifications

### Solution
**Adapted vLLM's jinja content format detection approach:**

1. **AST Analysis**: Parse Jinja template to detect content format expectations
   ```python
   # Detect if template has: {%- for content in message['content'] -%}
   template_format = detect_template_content_format(chat_template)
   ```

2. **Format-Aware Processing**:
   - **OpenAI format** (llama4): Preserve structured content lists, normalize types
   - **String format** (deepseek): Flatten to text for simple string templates

3. **Content Normalization**: `image_url` → `image`, `audio_url` → `audio` for template compatibility

### Key Changes
1. **Template Format Detection** (`openai_api/utils.py`):
   - AST analysis functions adapted from vLLM
   - `detect_template_content_format()` - main detection function
   - `process_content_for_template_format()` - content processing

2. **Adapter Updates** (`openai_api/adapter.py`):
   - Replace `openai_compatible_messages` handling with `process_content_for_template_format`
   - Global caching for performance (analyze template only once)

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Explain the purpose of this PR and the goals it aims to achieve. -->
While the KV cache for a request should normally be the total length of the request minus 1, when enable_overlap is active, req.seqlen does not include the token generated in the previous inference round (t-1) due to the overlap between CPU scheduling and GPU inference. As a result, during the t-th scheduling round, this token is not added to req.seqlen, making the subtraction unnecessary.

author: Xu-Wenqing
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation

Fix this: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/7048

## Modifications

Test Script:
```
from openai import OpenAI

openai_api_base = ""
openai_api_key = ""

client = OpenAI(
    api_key=openai_api_key,
    base_url=openai_api_base + "/v1",
)

tools = [
    {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "get_current_temperature",
            "description": "Get current temperature at a location.",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "location": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": 'The location to get the temperature for, in the format "City, State, Country".',
                    },
                    "unit": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "enum": ["celsius", "fahrenheit"],
                        "description": 'The unit to return the temperature in. Defaults to "celsius".',
                    },
                },
                "required": ["location"],
            },
        },
    },
    {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "get_temperature_date",
            "description": "Get temperature at a location and date.",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "location": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": 'The location to get the temperature for, in the format "City, State, Country".',
                    },
                    "date": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": 'The date to get the temperature for, in the format "Year-Month-Day".',
                    },
                    "unit": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "enum": ["celsius", "fahrenheit"],
                        "description": 'The unit to return the temperature in. Defaults to "celsius".',
                    },
                },
                "required": ["location", "date"],
            },
        },
    },
]


tool_calls_stream = client.chat.completions.create(
    model=client.models.list().data[0].id,
    messages=[
        {
            "role": "system",
            "content": "现在的日期是: 2024-09-30",
        },
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": "北京今天的天气如何？明天呢？",
        },
    ],
    tools=tools,
    tool_choice="auto",
    stream=True,
    max_completion_tokens=8192,
)

for chunk in tool_calls_stream:
    if chunk.choices[0].delta.tool_calls:
        print(chunk.choices[0].delta.tool_calls)

```

title: Fix Deepseek R1 0528 FP4 tensor name mismatch issue during weights loading.
author: pyc96
body:
## Motivation

This PR tries to fix a weights loading issue for Deepseek R1 0528 Fp4 from Nvidia.

To reproduce the issue: (i'm using blackwell image)

```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --port=7080 --model-path=nvidia/DeepSeek-R1-0528-FP4  --trust-remote-code --tp=8  --host=0.0.0.0 --quantization=modelopt_fp4 --kv-cache-dtype=auto


[2025-06-13 22:09:17 TP5] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 2527, in run_scheduler_process
    scheduler = Scheduler(server_args, port_args, gpu_id, tp_rank, pp_rank, dp_rank)
                ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 312, in __init__
    self.tp_worker = TpWorkerClass(
                     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/tp_worker_overlap_thread.py", line 64, in __init__
    self.worker = TpModelWorker(
                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/tp_worker.py", line 78, in __init__
    self.model_runner = ModelRunner(
                        ^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py", line 212, in __init__
    self.initialize(min_per_gpu_memory)
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py", line 253, in initialize
    self.load_model()
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py", line 547, in load_model
    self.model = get_model(
                 ^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/model_loader/__init__.py", line 22, in get_model
    return loader.load_model(
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py", line 381, in load_model
    self.load_weights_and_postprocess(
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py", line 389, in load_weights_and_postprocess
    model.load_weights(weights)
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py", line 2202, in load_weights
    param = params_dict[name]
            ~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^
KeyError: 'model.layers.5.self_attn.kattn_mqa.k_scale'
```

If we look into the weight file and model config, the k_scale name is actually `model.layers.5.self_attn.attn_mqa.k_scale`. 

Also it didn't update `attn_mha`'s k_scale.

body:

## Motivation
Previously, the EBNF grammar for function calls with optional parameters could generate invalid JSON with trailing commas when optional fields were omitted. For example: {"location": "Paris",} instead of {"location": "Paris"}

This is because `EBNFComposer` wasn't handling the optional parameter generation correctly

title: ci: Fix test_ebnf_generate_all_optional_function_params
author: CatherineSue
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation
The CI failed [here](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/15717655035/job/44291325000) because the output

```
{"name":"config_service", "arguments":{"language":"en","notifications":true}}` failed to match the pattern
```

failed to match the pattern

```
r'^\{"name":"config_service", "arguments":\{"language":"(en|es|fr)", "notifications":(true|false)\}\}$'
```

The problem is spacing. The regex pattern expects a space after the comma:

```
"language":"(en|es|fr)", "notifications":(true|false)
                        ↑ space here
```

But the actual generated JSON has no space after the comma:

```
"language":"en","notifications":true
               ↑ no space here
```
<!-- Explain the purpose of this PR and the goals it aims to achieve. -->

## Modifications
- Add \s* check to allow space / no space in the arguments

author: ch-tiger1
body:
When I deploy a deepep+1p1d service and stress test for short input and long output scenarios, for example: isl-1k/osl-48k scenarios, chunk too big appears.

```
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/starlette/_exception_handler.py", line 53, in wrapped_app
    raise exc
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/starlette/_exception_handler.py", line 42, in wrapped_app

  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/starlette/routing.py", line 714, in __call__

  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/starlette/routing.py", line 734, in app

  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/starlette/routing.py", line 74, in app
    await response(scope, receive, send)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/starlette/responses.py", line 262, in __call__
    with collapse_excgroups():
  File "/usr/lib/python3.10/contextlib.py", line 153, in __exit__
    self.gen.throw(typ, value, traceback)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/starlette/_utils.py", line 82, in collapse_excgroups
    raise exc
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/starlette/responses.py", line 266, in wrap
    await func()
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/starlette/responses.py", line 246, in stream_response
    async for chunk in self.body_iterator:
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/mini_lb.py", line 158, in stream_results
    async for chunk in decode_response.content:
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/aiohttp/streams.py", line 52, in __anext__
    rv = await self.read_func()
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/aiohttp/streams.py", line 352, in readline
    return await self.readuntil()
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/aiohttp/streams.py", line 380, in readuntil
    raise ValueError("Chunk too big")
ValueError: Chunk too big
```
**Main analysis**
aiohttp will read "as much as possible" from the underlying buffer each time. If the data sent by the server is large and has no natural separation (such as no newline or large chunks), aiohttp will continue to read data into the buffer until the end of the stream is encountered or an internal limit is triggered.

aiohttp's StreamReader has a self._low_water(default 64KB) and a self._high_water (default 128KB). When the data read in a single time exceeds this limit, it will throw ValueError: Chunk too big

The call is StreamReader.iter_chunked(n). This method will read only n bytes at most (here 64KB) each time. Even if the server has a large packet, it will force the big data to be cut into pieces (each piece is at most 64KB) and handed over to you.

In this way, the _limit limit will never be triggered, because you can only get 64KB at most each time, which is much less than the default limit of 128KB. After modification, verification is normal

author: ehuaa
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation

In the initial version @CatherineSue  of the parse_streaming_increment method, it used a generic if-condition to determine whether the text started with a tool call. This approach did not differentiate between models, causing models like Qwen2.5 or Qwen3 (which don't use curly braces as the starting indicator for tool calls) to be incorrectly identified as making tool call requests.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/084dac9c-d44c-428a-af75-8273bde29531)


## Modifications

The solution is to modify the generic if-condition to call self.has_tool_call, which will invoke the corresponding subclass method, enabling model-specific differentiation.

title: Fix: resolve prefill of retracted request out-of-memory issue when ignore_eos is enabled
author: GaoYusong
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation

For retracted requests, the prefill length includes more than just `len(req.origin_input_ids)`. Using `len(req.origin_input_ids)` in `add_one_req_ignore_eos` to determine the prefill length leads to incorrect calculation, and can cause _**RuntimeError: Prefill out of memory. Try to lower your batch size**_. It should be replaced with `req.extend_input_len`, which correctly reflects the actual prefill length.

```
2025-06-18 13:43:34 ERROR 31423 [ TP6 PP0 scheduler.py:2547] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last):^M
2025-06-18 13:43:34 ERROR 31423 [ TP6 PP0 scheduler.py:2547]   File "/home/SGLang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 2528, in run_scheduler_process^M
2025-06-18 13:43:34 ERROR 31423 [ TP6 PP0 scheduler.py:2547]     scheduler.event_loop_pp()^M
2025-06-18 13:43:34 ERROR 31423 [ TP6 PP0 scheduler.py:2547]   File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/torch/utils/_contextlib.py", line 116, in decorate_context^M
2025-06-18 13:43:34 ERROR 31423 [ TP6 PP0 scheduler.py:2547]     return func(*args, **kwargs)^M
2025-06-18 13:43:34 ERROR 31423 [ TP6 PP0 scheduler.py:2547]   File "/home/SGLang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 735, in event_loop_pp^M
2025-06-18 13:43:34 ERROR 31423 [ TP6 PP0 scheduler.py:2547]     mbs[mb_id] = self.get_next_batch_to_run()^M
2025-06-18 13:43:34 ERROR 31423 [ TP6 PP0 scheduler.py:2547]   File "/home/SGLang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 1356, in get_next_batch_to_run^M
2025-06-18 13:43:34 ERROR 31423 [ TP6 PP0 scheduler.py:2547]     new_batch = self.get_new_batch_prefill()^M
2025-06-18 13:43:34 ERROR 31423 [ TP6 PP0 scheduler.py:2547]   File "/home/SGLang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 1512, in get_new_batch_prefill^M
2025-06-18 13:43:34 ERROR 31423 [ TP6 PP0 scheduler.py:2547]     new_batch.prepare_for_extend()^M
2025-06-18 13:43:34 ERROR 31423 [ TP6 PP0 scheduler.py:2547]   File "/home/SGLang/python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py", line 1240, in prepare_for_extend^M
2025-06-18 13:43:34 ERROR 31423 [ TP6 PP0 scheduler.py:2547]     out_cache_loc = self.alloc_token_slots(extend_num_tokens)^M
2025-06-18 13:43:34 ERROR 31423 [ TP6 PP0 scheduler.py:2547]   File "/home/SGLang/python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py", line 973, in alloc_token_slots^M
2025-06-18 13:43:34 ERROR 31423 [ TP6 PP0 scheduler.py:2547]     raise RuntimeError(error_msg)^M
2025-06-18 13:43:34 ERROR 31423 [ TP6 PP0 scheduler.py:2547] RuntimeError: Prefill out of memory. Try to lower your batch size.^M
2025-06-18 13:43:34 ERROR 31423 [ TP6 PP0 scheduler.py:2547] Try to allocate 5736 tokens.^M
2025-06-18 13:43:34 ERROR 31423 [ TP6 PP0 scheduler.py:2547] Available tokens: 5504^M
```

<!-- Explain the purpose of this PR and the goals it aims to achieve. -->

## Modifications

<!-- Describe the changes made in this PR. -->
```
-        cur_rem_tokens = self.cur_rem_tokens - len(req.origin_input_ids)
+        cur_rem_tokens = self.cur_rem_tokens - req.extend_input_len
```

author: CatherineSue
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation
Execute Notebooks is failing in a lot of PRs.

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/15857984814/job/44707935719?pr=7491

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/15857584056/job/44706615579?pr=7499

Python's `argparse` does have automatic `prefix matching` (also called `abbreviation matching`), but it only works when there's no ambiguity.

author: TomQuartz
body:

While initializing the GroupCoordinator, `local_rank` is used to bind device. title: [bugfix] fix runtime dropping panic in editable
author: slin1237
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Explain the purpose of this PR and the goals it aims to achieve. -->
This PR fixes a PanicException that occurs when using the sgl-router Python bindings in editable/development mode:  

- `pyo3_runtime.PanicException`: Cannot drop a runtime in a context where blocking is not allowed. 
- This happens when a runtime is dropped from within an asynchronous context.

The issue occurred because the router was creating an `actix_web::rt::System` runtime and immediately dropping it when the `start()` method returned. When called from Python in certain async contexts, this caused a panic.


## Modifications

 Replaced `actix_web::rt::System::new().block_on()` with `tokio::runtime::Runtime::new()` and `runtime.block_on()`. This approach:

  - Uses tokio's runtime which handles dropping more gracefully in async contexts
  - Avoids the panic when used in editable mode installations
  - Has no performance impact since tokio is already a dependency
  - Maintains the same blocking behavior expected by the Python bindings

<!-- Describe the changes made in this PR. -->

title: fix(model loader): use safe_open to prevent file handle leaks.
author: SimonCqk
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Explain the purpose of this PR and the goals it aims to achieve. -->

Unclosed file descriptors cause underlying I/O buffers to remain allocated. In environments that use a FUSE-based file system to accelerate model loading, this leads to excessive and prolonged memory consumption by the FUSE daemon, significantly impacting performance.
Ensures that each safetensors file is properly closed immediately after its contents are read, preventing resource leaks and releasing associated buffers promptly.

## Modifications

<!-- Describe the changes made in this PR. -->

replaces `load_file` with the `with safetensors.safe_open(...)` context manager.

title: Fix the issue of incorrect finish reason in final stream response chunk returned during tool call
author: xianzhiT
body: ## Motivation Current release v0.4.8 in order to comply with the OpenAI protocol, class OpenAIServingChat adds an additional chunk at the end of the streaming output to describe the reason for the end of the streaming output. When the streaming output ends with tool_calls, the finish_reason in the reply chunk should be tool_calls. The current code did not perform a tool call check, which resulted in the final chunk always having a 'stop' instead of the expected 'tool_calls' value for the' finish.rason '. This can lead to unpredictable behavior in some open source software (eg. strand agent). ## Modifications Corrected the logic for obtaining finish_reason, returning and setting finish_reason to tool_calls in the final chunk after determining it as a tool call. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci). - [ ] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation-running-docs-ci). - [ ] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/accuracy_evaluation.html). - [ ] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging the PR. - [ ] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR.

title: [bugfix] Fix sgl-router get_server_info endpoint compatibility issue
author: slin1237
body:
## Motivation

  The sgl-router's PD (Prefill-Decode) router was returning an incompatible response format for the `/get_server_info` endpoint, causing `bench_one_batch_server.py` to
  fail with an `UnboundLocalError` when attempting to extract the `tokenizer_path`. The benchmark script expects the server info to contain either a top-level
  `tokenizer_path` field or a `prefill` array with objects containing `tokenizer_path`, but the router was only returning `internal_states` and `decode_servers` fields.

  ## Modifications

  - Updated the `get_server_info` method in `pd_router.rs` to directly forward the response from the decode server instead of reconstructing it
  - This ensures the response includes all expected fields from the sglang server, including the `tokenizer_path` field that the benchmark script requires
  - Removed unnecessary response transformation that was causing the incompatibility

title: [CPU]convert topk_weights to fp32 for INT8 and FP8 paths (for llama4) and fix LmHead weight pack
author: chunyuan-w
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Explain the purpose of this PR and the goals it aims to achieve. -->
1. Convert `topk_weights` to fp32 for INT8 and FP8 paths since the CPU kernel requires it to be fp32.
Previously we've fixed this issue in BF16 path for `llama4`. The same fix is needed for INT8 and FP8.
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/3646f6bb3e42ef31b29e4bae3244a14333a2ba9b/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py#L320-L322

2. For the weight pack check in `ParallelLMHead`, we previously checked that `self.quant_config` should be None to ensure it's not quantized. But `self.quant_config` could be `Fp8Config` for FP8 model or `W8A8Int8Config` for INT8 model while the weight of `ParallelLMHead` is still `torch.bfloat16`. We updated the code to explicitly check the weight dtype to device whether weight pack is supported or not on CPU.

title: [Quantization][w8a8_int8] Fix weight loading issue for w8a8_int8 path with "ignore" layer list in quantization config

title: Refactor dynamic LoRA update to fix incorrect handling of variant weight shapes
author: lifuhuang
body:
## Motivation

The current implementation of the dynamic LoRA update has several major limitations, most notably:

- Issue 1 [Known limitation] (#7463 ). User must provide at least one initial `--lora-paths`, and 
- Issue 2 [Bug]  (#7808 ). the initial adapter shapes (target modules, lora_rank) must be either the same or "larger" than ALL subsequent dynamically loaded adapters, otherwise, the process might fail, or even worse, produce incorrect result (when CUDA graph is enabled).

This PR is focusing on addressing the Issue 2 in a **backward-compatible** way, such that:
1. User can explicitly customize lora weight info via the newly introduced server args (similar to vLLM) to avoid having to find a "large enough" initial adapter.

2. Existing programs / commands would work equivalently in both result and performance.

```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --max-loras-per-batch 1 --model-path meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct  --disable-radix-cache --lora-paths lora=algoprog/fact-generation-llama-3.1-8b-instruct-lora
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang  --num-prompt 480 --request-rate 8 --lora-name lora
```

| Main (cb9d91ea) | This PR |
|--------|--------|
| ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/db4afd07-a809-4e79-95a2-dcc8ac40b72f)  | ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/65b36570-f55c-4cb3-9d94-eaca6a2ed370) | 

3. User can get explicit and comprehensible error response when dynamically loaded adapters are incompatible with the current setup. No crashing server or implicit wrong result.

## Modifications

1. Refactor LoRAManager and LoRAMemoryPool to correct handle weight shape updates.
2. Add validation logic to ensure unsupported behaviors are denied in a user-friendly and predictable way without crashing server or producing unexpected behavior.
3. Add tests to cover both positive and negative cases.

title: Fix the Wrong Return Type of `Scheduler.recv_requests`
author: Arist12
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Explain the purpose of this PR and the goals it aims to achieve. -->

The current type annotation for `recv_requests()` is incorrect and misleading. The method is annotated as returning `List[Req]`, but it actually returns a list of various input request types (like `TokenizedGenerateReqInput`, `TokenizedEmbeddingReqInput`, etc.) that are received via ZMQ from the tokenizer manager and RPC calls.
These input types are only transformed into Req objects later in the pipeline by `process_input_requests()` → `_request_dispatcher` → specific handler methods like `handle_generate_request()`. 

The current annotation suggests the transformation happens in recv_requests(), which is confusing for developers trying to understand the request processing flow.

## Modifications

<!-- Describe the changes made in this PR. -->
The method can actually receive 20+ different request types, but TokenizedGenerateReqInput and TokenizedEmbeddingReqInput represent the core text generation and embedding functionality that most users interact with.

Updated the type annotation of recv_requests() from:
```python
def recv_requests(self) -> List[Req]:
```
to 
```python
def recv_requests(self) -> List[Union[TokenizedGenerateReqInput, TokenizedEmbeddingReqInput, Any]]:
```

This change explicitly highlights the two main request types that handle core functionality while keeping the annotation readable without listing all 20+ possible types.

Alternative approaches considered:
`List[Any]` - Simple but loses information about the main types
Full Union with all types - Accurate but seems too verbose

A complete type annotation can be like below:
```python
def recv_requests(self) -> List[Union[
    # Core requests
    TokenizedGenerateReqInput, TokenizedEmbeddingReqInput,
    # System management  
    FlushCacheReqInput, AbortReq,
    # Sessions
    OpenSessionReqInput, CloseSessionReqInput,
    # Weight updates
    UpdateWeightFromDiskReqInput, UpdateWeightsFromDistributedReqInput,
    UpdateWeightsFromTensorReqInput, InitWeightsUpdateGroupReqInput,
    # LoRA management
    LoadLoRAAdapterReqInput, UnloadLoRAAdapterReqInput,
    # Introspection
    GetWeightsByNameReqInput, GetInternalStateReq, SetInternalStateReq,
    # Memory management
    ReleaseMemoryOccupationReqInput, ResumeMemoryOccupationReqInput,
    # Performance & debugging
    SlowDownReqInput, ProfileReq, ExpertDistributionReq,
    # RPC
    RpcReqInput
]]:
```

title: [RPC] Fix handle_rpc_request with `**recv_req.parameters`
author: CharlieFRuan
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation
Currently the method passed into `collective_rpc()` can only take in `**kwargs`, e.g. `def save_remote_model(self, **kwargs)`. Thus, the following script
```python
import sglang as sgl

def foo(self, a, b):
    print(f"foo called with {a} and {b} at rank {self.tp_rank}")

import sglang.srt.managers.scheduler
sglang.srt.managers.scheduler.Scheduler.foo = foo

def main():
    server_args = {
        "model_path": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B",
        "disable_cuda_graph": True,
        "tp_size": 2,
    }
    sampling_params = {"max_new_tokens": 10}
    llm = sgl.Engine(**server_args)
    llm.collective_rpc("foo", a=1, b=2)

    outputs = llm.generate("Hello, my name is", sampling_params)
    print(outputs['text'])

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```
would fail with error
```sh
[2025-07-09 20:00:31 TP0] Failed to call rpc foo: foo() missing 1 required positional argument: 'b'
[2025-07-09 20:00:31 TP1] Failed to call rpc foo: foo() missing 1 required positional argument: 'b'
```

<!-- Explain the purpose of this PR and the goals it aims to achieve. -->

## Modifications

<!-- Describe the changes made in this PR. -->

In Scheduler's `handle_rpc_request()`, I updated `func(recv_req.parameters)` to `func(**recv_req.parameters)` when it is not `None`, so it can handle both scenarios (`**kwargs` and positional arguments).

I understand that this `collective_rpc()` is not really user-facing but thought this fix makes sense regardless. Otherwise, feel free to close this PR. Thanks!

title: [fix]Update unitest for fp8_blockwise_scaled_grouped_mm kernel
author: HydraQYH
body: Follow https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/7278, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/7782 Setting the correct **scale factor layout** for the fp8_blockwise_scaled_grouped_mm kernel can be confusing. In this PR, we updated the **unit test** of fp8_blockwise_scaled_grouped_mm to show an e2e example using the fp8_blockwise_scaled_grouped_mm kernel. Whether it is SM100 or SM90, the input matrix A must be Row-Major, the input matrix B must be Column-Major, and the output matrix is ​​Row-Major. For SM90, CUTLASS only supports the scale factor layout of MN-Major, so SFA and SFB must follow the following format: - The Shape of SFA is **(m, k)** and the Stride is **(1, m)** - The Shape of SFB is **(n, k)** and the Stride is **(1, n)** For SM100, CUTLASS supports both MN-Major and K-Major, but since the scale factor layout is hardcoded as K-Major in the code, the fp8_blockwise_scaled_grouped_mm kernel only supports the following format: - The Shape of SFA is **(m, k)** and the Stride is **(k, 1)** - The Shape of SFB is **(n, k)** and the Stride is **(k, 1)** For the accuracy test method, the traditional allclose cannot adapt to the fp8_blockwise_scaled_grouped_mm kernel, so we align the accuracy test method with [DeepGEMM](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP). Thanks @LyricZhao @MARD1NO @Alcanderian a lot. We have conducted extensive experiments on the Hopper & Blackwell architecture, and the accuracy results are in line with expectations: Hopper: Blackwell: We hope this PR can help you adapt the fp8_blockwise_scaled_grouped_mm kernel to your business scenarios. ## Motivation Assist developers to adapt the fp8_blockwise_scaled_grouped_mm kernel based on CUTLASS. ## Modifications sgl-kernel/tests/test_fp8_blockwise_moe.py ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci). - [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation-running-docs-ci). - [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/accuracy_evaluation.html)--**Blackwell** - [ ] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging the PR. - [x] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR.

title: [Fix] Orphan process in data parallel
author: Capronir
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation
When dp_size > 1, the process tree is "launch_server -> data_parallel_controller -> sglang::scheduler_*". 
However, the data_parallel_controller process does not watch the state of its parent process (launch_server). As a result, if launch_server crashes, data_parallel_controller will become an orphan process (its parent will become the init process with PID 1), and its child processes will not be cleaned up either, leading to process leaks.
<!-- Explain the purpose of this PR and the goals it aims to achieve. -->

## Modifications
Add a mechanism for the data_parallel_controller process to watch its parent process launch_server. If launch_server crashes, this will trigger the cleanup of the data_parallel_controller process, which in turn will also clean up its sglang::scheduler_* child processes.
<!-- Describe the changes made in this PR. -->

author: JustinTong0323

### Summary
This PR fixes a redundant rotary embedding cache recomputation in the MiniCPM model that was bypassing proper dtype handling.

If a user erroneously enables the ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM environment variable in non-FP8 model scenarios (e.g., when using Qwen3-235B-FP16), sglang will enter a failed state during launch and sglang‘s rank scheduler will stuck at the following stack:

title: fix:reorder topk experts to ensure shared expert replaces minimal score
author: erictanjn
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation

In the MoE (Mixture of Experts) layer, in the original design, to achieve integration between the shared expert and routed experts, when selecting top-k experts for each token, we need to reorder the selected experts to guarantee the last expert in the list has the smallest score. The original implementation uses torch.topk with sorted=False, which means the returned experts aren't necessarily in score order. When we replace the last expert with the shared expert, we might accidentally replace a unexpected expert, altering the layer's expected behavior. This fix ensures proper expert selection by sorting the top-k experts before replacement.

## Modifications

Before: Used raw torch.topk(..., sorted=False) output for expert replacement

After: Now sorts selected experts by score before shared expert substitution

title: Fix suffix mismatch for the metrics.
author: CharlesRiggins
body:
## Motivation

The suffix matcher for the suffix "duration" does not match the metric names "sgl_router_request_duration_seconds" or "sgl_router_pd_request_duration_seconds". As a result, the matcher doesn't set the bucket for those metrics as expected. Without the bucket info, the histogram metrics fall back to summary metrics, and it looks like this:
```
sgl_router_generate_duration_seconds{route="/generate",quantile="0.9"} 10
sgl_router_generate_duration_seconds{route="/generate",quantile="0.95"} 20
sgl_router_generate_duration_seconds{route="/generate",quantile="0.99"} 15
sgl_router_generate_duration_seconds{route="/generate",quantile="0.999"} 50
sgl_router_generate_duration_seconds{route="/generate",quantile="1"} 15
```
But it was originally intended to be like this:
```
sglang:time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket{le="0.1",model_name="meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct"} 6.0
sglang:time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket{le="0.25",model_name="meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct"} 6.0
sglang:time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket{le="0.5",model_name="meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct"} 6.0
sglang:time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket{le="0.75",model_name="meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct"} 6.0
sglang:time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket{le="1.0",model_name="meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct"} 27.0
```

## Modifications

Give a correct suffix for the matcher. It should be "duration_seconds" as the suffix to match the name "sgl_router_request_duration_seconds", not "duration".

title: [CPU] Fix TP padding case with weight block size
author: jianan-gu
body:
### Motivation
Fixes the [Kimi-K2-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K2-Instruct) (FP8) TP=6 failure on CPU.

ValueError: Weight output_partition_size = 2112 is not divisible by weight quantization block_n = 128.

### Modifications
Considering `weight_block_size `when padding TP, to make self.num_heads * self.qk_head_dim / tp_size divisible by `weight_block_size `in the below ColumnParallelLinear.
```
  self.q_b_proj = ColumnParallelLinear(
      q_lora_rank,
      self.num_heads * self.qk_head_dim,
      bias=False,
      quant_config=quant_config,
      prefix=add_prefix("q_b_proj", prefix),
      tp_rank=attn_tp_rank,
      tp_size=attn_tp_size,
  )
```
In our case, self.num_heads = 64, self.qk_head_dim =192, tp_size = 6, block_size = 128

Before this PR, self.num_heads is padded to 66, self.num_heads * self.qk_head_dim / tp_size = 2112, which is not divisible by 128.
After this PR, self.num_heads is padded to 72, self.num_heads * self.qk_head_dim / tp_size = 2304, which is divisible by 128.



**MISC.**
This PR also covers a minor fix for unquant MoE module with `apply_router_weight_on_input` config, sine CPU AMX path supports now.

title: Extract update_weights from RL Engine to SGLang to keep simplicity and fix torch reduce
author: hebiao064
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

Co-authored-by: CuiBo [82354186+SuperCB@users.noreply.github.com](mailto:82354186+SuperCB@users.noreply.github.com)
Co-authored-by: GeLee [865038696@qq.com](mailto:865038696@qq.com)
Co-authored-by: 杨睿 <yangruipis@163.com>


## Context
Builds on the earlier work from [#2620](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/pull/2620) to further simplify and unify the update weights logic 


## Motivation

We've received numerous complaints that the update weights logic in VERL SGLang is difficult to understand and error-prone during development. For example, [a recent refactor from VerlEngine to AsyncEngine](https://github.com/hebiao064/verl/commit/fe23634116ab69cacc38e7570e3c0e344eb1c711) accidentally broke the torch reduce patch logic, leading to a 3× slowdown in weight updates.

Additionally, when changing the tensor update logic from per-tensor to batched updates, we had to duplicate the logic across both [Megatron SGLang Sharding Manager](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/pull/2418) and [FSDP SGLang Sharding Manager](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/pull/2559). This not only introduced unnecessary complexity, but also made maintenance and future improvements harder.

To address these issues, we propose simplifying and centralizing the update weights logic within core SGLang, exposing a unified API that is transparent to all RL engines. This abstraction reduces duplication, improves reliability, and accelerates future development.

### Benefits
- ✅ Unified and transparent update weights API for all RL engines (FSDP, Megatra, etc.)
- 🚀 Speedup QWen3 MoE weight updates from 110s to 30s
- 🔧 Torch patch MP serializer to avoid inefficient P2P communication that slows down weight updates

| `HF_TOKEN: "<secret>"`              | ✅ Valid  |
| `HF_TOKEN: <secret>`                | ❌ Invalid (unquoted value) |


## Modifications

This PR updates the environment variable syntax to use the proper ​​shell-style format​​ expected by Docker Compose when using the list syntax for environment variables.

Additionally, the GPU usage has been modified to ​​remove the fixed binding to device 0​​, making it more flexible.

title: [router] fix pd model completion request
author: slin1237
body:
## Motivation

The `/v1/completions` endpoint in sgl-router was failing in PD (Prefill-Decode) mode because it was converting OpenAI's `CompletionRequest` format to an internal `GenerateReqInput` format before forwarding to backend servers. This conversion changed field names (e.g., `prompt` → `text`) and structure, causing backend servers that expect standard OpenAI format to reject the requests with errors like "Field 'prompt' required".

This PR fixes the issue by preserving the original OpenAI request format when routing `/v1/completions` requests, ensuring compatibility with OpenAI-compatible backend servers.

addressing #8201 

  ## Modifications

  1. **Added Bootstrap support for CompletionRequest**:
     - Added optional bootstrap fields (`bootstrap_host`, `bootstrap_port`, `bootstrap_room`) to `CompletionRequest` struct in
  `openai_api_types.rs`
     - Implemented the `Bootstrap` trait for `CompletionRequest` in `pd_types.rs` to enable PD routing without format conversion

  2. **Created new routing method**:
     - Added `route_completion_openai()` method in `pd_router.rs` that preserves the OpenAI format while adding bootstrap information
     - This method extracts text for cache-aware routing without modifying the request structure

  3. **Updated routing logic**:
     - Modified `route_completion()` to use the new `route_completion()` method instead of converting to `GenerateReqInput`
     - Removed the fallback logic for PD format since `/v1/completions` should always use OpenAI format

  4. **Fixed tests and benchmarks**:
     - Updated all test cases in `request_adapter.rs` to include the new bootstrap fields
     - Updated benchmark code in `request_processing.rs` to include bootstrap fields

title: fix bug when eos_ids==0
author: bzantium
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation

This PR aims to fix a bug in the `get_hf_eos_token_id` function that causes a `TypeError` when the `eos_token_id` is `0`.

Currently, the conditional check `if eos_ids:` incorrectly evaluates to `False` for the value `0`. This prevents `eos_ids` from being properly converted to a `set`, which later results in an `unsupported operand type(s) for |: 'int' and 'set'` error when performing a set union.

This change ensures that `0` is handled as a valid token ID. This resolves issue \#8313.

## Modifications

The fix is to change the conditional statement from a "truthiness" check to an explicit `None` check. This ensures that `eos_ids` is always converted to a `set` before any union operations are attempted.

```diff
- if eos_ids:
+ if eos_ids is not None:
```

title: Fix: Improve test_openai_function_calling unit test and fix reasoning_parser.py think_start_token logic
author: byjiang1996
body: ## Motivation & Modifications As part of the collaboration with Zhipu team on https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/8224. we noticed: * `reasoning_parser.py's detect_and_parse think_start_token logic` is inconsistent with `reasoning_parser.py's detect_and_parse parse_streaming_increment logic`. In the latter case, it uses `self.think_start_token in current_text` to tell whether the current model output is in reasoning mode but the former case uses `current_text.startswith(self.think_start_token)`. It leads to something like `\n${self.think_start_token}` text are not treated as reasoning mode due to one extra \n in the begining. In vllm, it uses `start_token in text` check too in both cases: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6d8d0a24c02bfd84d46b3016b865a44f048ae84b/vllm/reasoning/qwen3_reasoning_parser.py#L99 * Add one more unit test for https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/7708 to check whether `test_function_calling_streaming_args_parsing` finishes with `finish_reason=tool_call` instead of `finish_reason=stop` to catch any regression. The regression will break Zhipu team's key feature integration. * Add `_test_function_calling_multiturn` to `test_openai_function_calling` unit test to catch future regressions b/c this test is critical for Zhipu team's business integration * Add `max_tokens=2048` to all unit tests in `test_openai_function_calling`. Sometimes i noticed the LLM never stops which takes forever to run the unit tests.... Adding max token should help fail faster. * Change ` messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the temperature in Paris?"}]` to `{"role": "user", "content": "What is the temperature in Paris in celsius?"}`. The provided tool function has both celsius and fahrenheit option. If we ask LLM `What is the temperature in Paris`, it may reply with `what temperature unit you need` instead of calling tool function directly. It will fail the unit test in a flaky way. Asking `What is the temperature in Paris in celsius?` significantly improves the unit test success rate * Fix finish_reason != tool_call bug when tool_call and reasoning are both open. This PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/7708 only fixes the bug when only `tool-call-parser` is defined. If both `tool-call-parser` and `reasoning-parser` are defined, it will skip (due to `for-loop's continue`) _process_tool_call_stream's `yield None, tool_calls` logic: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/7708/files#diff-20a5bbe903ddc72a708cae54cfc9bd1ba42f3693a90dab09fc10904329bb6377R931 - Before this change in GLM4: this `TestOpenAIServerFunctionCalling's test_function_calling_streaming_simple` unit test will fail with `finish_reason != 'tool_calls'` - After the change, it works. Also added one more unit test `test_function_calling_streaming_no_tool_call` ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci). - [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation-running-docs-ci). - [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/accuracy_evaluation.html). - [x] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging the PR. - [x] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR.

author: slin1237
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation
The issue is that completion api has an internal inconsistency:
  1. The `/v1/completions` Pydantic validation expects single bootstrap values
  2. But the backend processing code expects arrays when handling array prompts

  - If we send arrays, validation fails with "Input should be a valid string"

Update the Pydantic model to accept `Union[str, List[str]]` for bootstrap fields

## Motivation

```
|     |       |strict-match    |     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9454|±  |0.0063|
```

```
sglang (pretrained=nvidia/DeepSeek-R1-0528-FP4,trust_remote_code=True,quantization=modelopt_fp4,tp_size=8,max_model_len=32768,add_bos_token=True,enable_flashinfer_moe=True,enable_ep_moe=True), gen_kwargs: (None), limit: None, num_fewshot: 5, batch_size: 512

|     |       |strict-match    |     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9500|±  |0.0060|
```

```
sglang (pretrained=nvidia/DeepSeek-R1-0528-FP4,trust_remote_code=True,quantization=modelopt_fp4,tp_size=8,max_model_len=32768,add_bos_token=True), gen_kwargs: (None), limit: None, num_fewshot: 5, batch_size: 512
```

## Modifications

A previous PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/6970 moved routed expert scaling into `moe_sum_reduce` and removed it from the model forward. However the `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod` code path does not use `moe_sum_reduce`, so the routed expert scales were not being applied.

title: [Bugfix][Feat] Add XML-ish grammar in EBNFComposer and fix misc bugs in Qwen3 detector
author: CatherineSue
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation
Follow up to #8260 

Here are some issues of `Qwen3XMLDetector`:

1. **EBNFComposer XML Support:** `tool_choice="required"` and specific tool selection fail because EBNFComposer only supported JSON/Pythonic formats, not XML
2. **Structural Tag Compatibility:** `strict=True` mode fails as Xgrammar doesn't support non-JSON formats with structural tags
  https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/12cb760a3773fe1a97d5a00fca26412f814f20fa/python/sglang/srt/function_call/function_call_parser.py#L157-L158
3. **Streaming Bug:** Incorrect tool call indexing in streaming mode
4. **Missing Tests:** No unit tests for Qwen3XMLDetector
5. **Incorrect Registry:** Should use `qwen3_coder` key since regular qwen3 models should use Qwen25Detector

This PR focuses on resolving item 1, 4 and 5. Item 2 is temporarily fixed with limitation.

<!-- Explain the purpose of this PR and the goals it aims to achieve. -->

## Modifications

**EBNFComposer XML Format Support**

- Added "xml" format alongside "pythonic" and "json"
- Created shared BASE_PRIMITIVE_GRAMMAR to eliminate duplication
- Simplified type mappings using base + overrides pattern:
  Before: 3 duplicate dictionaries
  After: DRY approach
```
  BASE_TYPE_MAPPING = {"string": "basic_string", ...}
  FORMAT_TYPE_OVERRIDES = {
      "pythonic": {"boolean": '"True" | "False"', "null": '"None"'},
      "xml": {"string": "xml_text"},
  }
```
- Refactored `_handle_enum()` and `_handle_type()` for better modularity

**Detector Refactoring**

- Renamed qwen3_detector.py → qwen3_coder_detector.py
- Renamed Qwen3XMLDetector → Qwen3CoderDetector
- Updated registry: "qwen3" → "qwen3_coder"
- Enhanced documentation to match codebase standards

**Structural Tag Support (Limited)**

- Added supports_structural_tag() method to BaseFormatDetector
- Override returns False for PythonicDetector and Qwen3CoderDetector

**Testing**

- Added `TestQwen3CoderDetector` with 11 test cases covering:
  - Basic detection and parsing
  - Streaming (simple, incomplete, incremental)
  - Type conversion and edge cases
  - EBNF generation and validation

author: mickqian
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation

Cuda tensor IPC only supports exporting a handle from a "clean tensor" (not cuda-ipced before) from the "original thread".

In TP-scenario, when Scheduler on tp0 received a cuda-ipc tensor from TokenizerManager on tp0, it will try broadcasting that tensor to Schedulers on tp!=0, causing the warning, which leads to further issue

```
Attempted to send CUDA tensor received from another process; this is not currently supported. Consider cloning before sending.
```

<!-- Explain the purpose of this PR and the goals it aims to achieve. -->

## Modifications

Force `.cuda()` on the cuda-ipc tensor. If it is on-device already, no overhead will be introduced.

## TODO

Prevent a tensor storage handle that is received from IPC from being **forwarded**.

## Motivation

This follows up a prior PR fixing synchronization bug: #8372

<!-- Explain the purpose of this PR and the goals it aims to achieve. -->

When a set operation fails, completed_token is 0. In this case, performing a split operation would result in an empty node, and subsequent Evict operations would hit an assertion. The fix adds a check to prevent splitting nodes with completed_token 0.
