title: bugfix: Fix multiple finish_reason chunks and tool_calls finish reason check
author: CatherineSue
body: ## Motivation This PR focuses on resolving multiple issues with `finish_reason` handling in OpenAI-compatible streaming responses. ### OpenAI Standanrd vs SGLang Issues: **1. Duplicate finish_reason chunks during streaming** OpenAI Standard: Only one finish_reason chunk at the end during streaming. SGLang Behavior: Two finish_reason chunks sent, causing duplication. See **Root Cause:** At L524 in serving_chat.py, when processing regular content, we incorrectly send finish_reason in content chunks. Then at L545, we send the final finish_reason chunk again, creating duplicates. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/22e00eeb4a4cb3a81e930619649234e34e8bd5fd/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py#L524-L533 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/22e00eeb4a4cb3a81e930619649234e34e8bd5fd/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py#L545-L563 **Fix:** Remove finish_reason from regular content chunks (L534) and only send it in the final loop. **2. Multi-choice streaming only sends finish_reason for last index** OpenAI Standard: When request.n > 1, each choice gets its own finish_reason chunk individually. Each index may have different finish_reason values. SGLang Behavior: Only sends one finish_reason chunk for the last index, missing finish_reason for other indices. See: **Root Cause:** Lack of finish_reason tracking for different indices - we weren't maintaining per-index state. **Fix:** Added finish_reasons dict to track finish_reason for each index separately, then loop through all indices to send individual finish_reason chunks. **Note:** The current check here is incorrect. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/22e00eeb4a4cb3a81e930619649234e34e8bd5fd/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py#L945-L946 It causes bug when there are no tool_calls in the results. The actual finish_reason determination should happen at the end of streaming when we have the final finish_reason_type and can check if the choice had tool calls. **3. Incomplete tool argument streaming on generation end** OpenAI Standard: When generation ends (any finish_reason), remaining tool call arguments should be streamed to complete the tool call. SGLang Behavior: Only checks for `finish_reason == "stop"`, missing cases where `finish_reason == "length"` and tool calls are incomplete. **Root Cause:** Incomplete condition check - tool calls can be cut off by length limits, not just natural stops. **Fix:** Added comprehensive check for any `finish_reason_type` to ensure remaining tool arguments are always streamed when generation ends, regardless of the specific finish_reason. ## Modifications **Summary of the Fix:** 1. Track finish_reason per index: finish_reasons[index] = finish_reason 2. Remove finish_reason from regular content: Always finish_reason=None during streaming 5. Send finish_reason chunks for all indices: Loop through all completed indices and send finish_reason chunks 6. Apply tool_calls logic per index: Check has_tool_calls.get(idx, False) for each specific index Now the behavior will be: With tool calls (n=2): - Index 0 completes → tracked in finish_reasons[0] - Index 1 completes → tracked in finish_reasons[1] - At the end → send finish_reason chunk for index 0 ("tool_calls") and index 1 ("tool_calls") Without tool calls (n=2): - Index 0 completes → tracked in finish_reasons[0] - Index 1 completes → tracked in finish_reasons[1] - At the end → send finish_reason chunk for index 0 ("stop") and index 1 ("stop") **Add Tests** Test 1: `test_streaming_multiple_choices_finish_reason` - Tests: Multiple choices (n=2) with tool calls in streaming mode - Verifies: Each choice (index 0 and 1) gets its own finish_reason chunk - Expected: Both indices should have finish_reason="tool_calls" - Catches: The bug where only the last index got a finish_reason chunk Test 2: `test_streaming_multiple_choices_without_tools` - Tests: Multiple choices (n=2) without tools in streaming mode - Verifies: Each choice gets its own finish_reason chunk for regular content - Expected: Both indices should have finish_reason="stop" or "length" - Catches: The bug where regular content with multiple choices had issues Test 3: Added Check in run_chat_completion_stream: 1. Track finish_reason counts per index (line 249): Each time a finish_reason is encountered, increment the counter for that index 2. Verify exactly one finish_reason per choice (lines 290-292): - Each index should appear in finish_reason_counts - Each index should have exactly 1 finish_reason chunk **Additional changes:** - Remove `TestOpenAIServerEBNF` in test_openai_server.py. As it is a duplication of `test/srt/openai_server/features/test_openai_server_ebnf.py`. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci). - [ ] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation-running-docs-ci). - [ ] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/accuracy_evaluation.html). - [ ] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging the PR. - [ ] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR.

title: Fix incorrect KV cache allocation for MTP models.
author: lifuhuang
body:
## Motivation

#8472 

We have been encountering various unexpected behavior while tuning `mem-fraction-static` for GLM4.5. For example:
1. None of the GLM4.5 model can run without explicitly specifying `mem-fraction-static` when MTP is enabled.
2. The full weight (300B) model can start successfully with 0.8, but the lighter weight Air version (100B) instead will run into OOM unless we adjust `mem-fraction-static` to 0.5 or below.

Upon investigation, I noticed that when we create KV cache for the draft model, currently we for ALL model layers while we only needed the last MTP layer. 

## Modifications

Use `num_nextn_predict_layers` to determine draft model kv cache size.

## Result

After the change, all the 4 GLM 4.5 models can be started without `--mem-frac-static` override with comparable GSM scores:

* zai-org/GLM-4.5
 ```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model zai-org/GLM-4.5 \
  --tp 8 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 3 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4
```
* zai-org/GLM-4.5-Air
```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model zai-org/GLM-4.5-Air\
  --tp 8 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 3 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4
```

* zai-org/GLM-4.5-FP8
 ```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model zai-org/GLM-4.5-FP8 \
  --tp 8 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 3 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4
```
* zai-org/GLM-4.5-Air-FP
 ```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model zai-org/GLM-4.5-Air-FP \
  --tp 4 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 3 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4
```

title: [sgl-kernel performace] fix fp8 quant kernels dispatch __nv_fp8_e4m3 bug to improve performance 10%-20%
author: BBuf
body: ## Motivation Follow: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/8449 Thanks to @strgrb . To boost kernel performance, we recommend using the `__nv_fp8_e4m3` data type instead of `c10::Float8_e4m3fn` to do float->fp8 dtype. This change reduces the number of instructions needed for data conversion, which in turn optimizes overall execution efficiency. From the SASS code in ncu, we can find that current kernel use many instructions to do convert float to fp8 : ```shell // 第1次调用 MOV R8, 0xc50 CALL.REL.NOINC 0x7fce7d7975c0 // 第2次调用 MOV R8, 0xe50 CALL.REL.NOINC 0x7fce7d7975c0 // 第3次调用 MOV R8, 0x1080 CALL.REL.NOINC 0x7fce7d7975c0 // 第4次调用 MOV R8, 0x1290 CALL.REL.NOINC 0x7fce7d7975c0 // 第5次调用 MOV R8, 0x14b0 CALL.REL.NOINC 0x7fce7d7975c0 // 第6次调用 MOV R8, 0x16c0 CALL.REL.NOINC 0x7fce7d7975c0 // 第7次调用 MOV R8, 0x18e0 CALL.REL.NOINC 0x7fce7d7975c0 // 第8次调用 MOV R8, 0x1af0 CALL.REL.NOINC 0x7fce7d7975c0 // 第9次调用 MOV R8, 0x1d10 CALL.REL.NOINC 0x7fce7d7975c0 ``` With pr fix: The performance degradation of `c10::Float8_e4m3fn` primarily stems from its reliance on software-implemented conversion functions instead of hardware-accelerated FP8 conversion instructions. Also noticed significant regression when running epmoe during recent GLM4.5 support work: GSM8K accuracy drops from 0.965 to 0.745 when EPMOE is enabled. Accuracy is good for TP & DeepEP.

```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model  /shared/public/elr-models/zai-org/GLM-4.5 --tp-size 8 --trust-remote-code

python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py
```

## Modifications

There is a bug in DeepSeek-V2 and GLM-4.5 related to how routed_scaling_factor is applied in MoE (Mixture-of-Experts) layers.

Currently, the routed_scaling_factor is applied in three different places, leading to ambiguity:
- self.topk.forward: The scaling is applied only in the n out of m condition, but not in the m - n out of m condition.
- self.experts.forward: Same as above — the factor is only applied in n out of m.
- Model-level logic: The model itself may apply routed_scaling_factor, but it cannot know whether self.topk or self.experts have already done so.

This results in uncertain and inconsistent scaling, as the model layer has no visibility into whether routed_scaling_factor has already been applied upstream.

🎪 TL;DR: The model can't know if it should apply * routed_scaling_factor or not, because topk and experts may or may not have already done it, depending on the code path.

My PR forces model layer to apply * routed_scaling_factor when EPMOE is enabled because from the current codebase, epmoe won't apply *routed_scaling_factor by itself. 

Need to follow up and possibly refactor sglang moe codebase to make it clear which layer should apply * routed_scaling_factor 

## Accuracy Test
- GLM4.5 GSM8K accuracy jumps from 0.745 to 0.965 under EPMOE which is the same as TP & DeepEP results
- Need to run gsm8k for deepseek-v3 too - WIP

hit count will incorrect increase in the following situations, which will cause hiradix cache to offload a large amount of worthless cache, leading to increased costs.

title: [ci] fix genai-bench execution cmd
author: slin1237
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation
1. GitHub Actions setup-python installs packages in its tool cache path:
`/home/keru/action-runner/_work/_tool/Python/3.11.13/x64/lib/python3.11/site-packages`
2. genai-bench executable is installed in the user's local bin:
`/home/keru/.local/bin/genai-bench`
3. When genai-bench runs, it's looking for its dependencies in:
`/home/keru/.local/lib/python3.11/site-packages`

This path mismatch occurs because:
  - The `setup-python` action creates an isolated Python environment
  - The pip install with `--break-system-packages` flag installs to the system Python location
  - But the `genai-bench` script gets installed to the user's local directory
  - When executed, genai-bench uses the Python interpreter's default paths, which don't include the GitHub Actions tool directory

  The issue is that `genai-bench` is installed as a console script entry point, and when it runs, it might not have the same Python path configuration as when it was installed.

title: [bug] limit bootstrap room to to [0, 2^63 - 1]
author: slin1237
body:
## Motivation

This PR fixes a critical bug in the PD (Prefill-Decode) router that causes `KVTransferError` and server hangs when routing requests to disaggregated prefill and decode nodes. The error manifests as:

```
Decode transfer failed for request rank=0 decode_req.req.rid='9a8d4c5f3ebf4fb2a60c04ae4bfeb72e' 
decode_req.req.bootstrap_room=3217994150080674400 with exception 
KVTransferError(bootstrap_room=3217994150080674400): Aborted by AbortReq.
```

The issue occurs because the Rust PD router generates `bootstrap_room` values in the full unsigned 64-bit range (0 to 2^64 - 1), while the Python backend expects signed 64-bit values (0 to 2^63 - 1). This mismatch causes failures when `bootstrap_room` values exceed 2^63 - 1.

## Modifications

- `sgl-router/src/routers/pd_types.rs`: Fixed bootstrap_room generation to match Python's expected range

title: Fix triton kernels topk with keyword arguments
author: ispobock
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation

For the triton kernels topk routing function, the meaning of `sm_first` is not exactly the same as `renormalize`. Use keyword arguments to avoid confusion and unknown bugs.
- If `sm_first` = True, the softmax will before the topk, so the result can be unnormalized before sort. `renormalize` is not supported in triton kernels rounting funciton.
- If `sm_first` = False, the softmax will after the topk, so the result is already normalized, so we don't need to renormalize.

title: Replace torch.jit.script with torch.compile in get_masked_input_and_mask to fix benchmark underreporting
author: YyWangCS
body:
## Motivation
The benchmark script, **bench_one_batch** reports lower prefill performance than what SGLang can actually achieve (40% lower in some cases). This is due to unexpected performance fluctuation in `@torch.jit.script` optimization for `get_masked_input_and_mask`, and in this PR we propose to replace it with `torch.compile`. 

The `get_masked_input_and_mask ` is used to mask out the valid input ids for each TP partition of the vocabulary embedding. This method involves several element-wise computations and SGlang uses `@torch.jit.script` to accelerate it. However, using `torch.jit.script ` makes the benchmark performance unexpectedly low. The first **several** executions (not only the first one) of this method call have performance issue, which I will provide some detailed data. In **bench_one_batch** , there will be a warmup which runs the model only **once**, so this does not solve the problem.  Scripts like bench_serving  or bench_offline_throughput have no such issue.

Following is some performance data reported by SGLang with `@torch.jit.script` and `@torch.compile`

```
# 2*H20, Qwen3-8B-fp8
python -m sglang.bench_one_batch --model-path Qwen3-8B-fp8/ --batch 1 --input-len 8192 --output-len 1 --load-format dummy --tp 2 

# Performance with torch.jit.script
Prefill. latency: 0.37688 s, throughput:  21736.12 token/s

# Performance with torch.compile
Prefill. latency: 0.34327 s, throughput:  23864.91 token/s
```

```
# 8*H20, Qwen3-8B-fp8
python -m sglang.bench_one_batch --model-path Qwen3-8B-fp8/ --batch 1 --input-len 8192 4096 16384 --output-len 1 --load-format dummy --tp 8

# Performance with torch.jit.script
Prefill. latency: 0.17894 s, throughput:  45781.70 token/s
Prefill. latency: 0.07149 s, throughput:  57295.01 token/s
Prefill. latency: 0.50967 s, throughput:  32146.33 token/s

# Performance with torch.compile
Prefill. latency: 0.13622 s, throughput:  60136.72 token/s
Prefill. latency: 0.07155 s, throughput:  57565.63 token/s
Prefill. latency: 0.37688 s, throughput:  54287.58 token/s
```

I benchmark the method `get_masked_input_and_mask ` method alone, with random input ids of different length, and get the following results:

``` 
Running get_masked_input_and_mask with random ids
1, seq_len 8192, time elapsed: 0.076(s)
2, seq_len 8192, time elapsed: 0.050(s)
3, seq_len 8192, time elapsed: 4.46e-5(s)
4, seq_len 8192, time elapsed: 4.04e-5(s)
5, seq_len 4096, time elapsed: 1.82e-4(s)
6, seq_len 4096, time elapsed: 0.040(s)
7, seq_len 4096, time elapsed: 4.35e-5(s)
8, seq_len 4096, time elapsed: 2.86e-5(s)
9, seq_len 16384, time elapsed: 1.53e-4(s)
10, seq_len 16384, time elapsed: 0.202(s)
11, seq_len 16384, time elapsed: 6.28e-5(s)
12, seq_len 16384, time elapsed: 3.56e-5(s)
```

Here we want to update `torch.jit.script` with `torch.compile`, rather than add more warmup iterations in bench_one_batch script, with following reasons:

1. The reason why `@torch.jit.script` has performance fluctuation is still not very clear, and the performance pattern is strange. As noted in the above data, we can see random slowdown. 
1. `torch.compile` is a more advanced feature than `torch.jit.script` , and we have better support (like debug info) in SGLang and PyTorch for it.

vLLM also has made the same change with this PR[[[5/N\][torch.compile] torch.jit.script --> torch.compile by youkaichao · Pull Request #10406 · vllm-project/vllm](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/10406)], but performance number is not analyzed in detail.

## Modifications
Replace `torch.jit.script`  with  `torch.compile`.

## Accuracy Test
I have written a unit test which compares the result of `get_masked_input_and_mask ` optimized with `torch.jit.script` and `torch.compile`, the results are the same.

## Benchmark & Profiling
The end-to-end prefill performance can be seen from the above data. And I also benchmarked the decoding performance, which shows no difference.

```
# 2*H20, Qwen3-8B
python -m sglang.bench_one_batch --model-path Qwen3-8B --batch 128 --input-len 128 --output-len 1024 --load-format dummy --tp 2 

# Performance with torch.jit.script
Prefill. latency: 7.25567 s, throughput:  18064.76 token/s
Decode 0. Batch size: 128, latency: 0.02340 s, throughput:   5469.01 token/s
Decode 1. Batch size: 128, latency: 0.02229 s, throughput:   5741.24 token/s
Decode 2. Batch size: 128, latency: 0.02228 s, throughput:   5744.25 token/s
Decode 3. Batch size: 128, latency: 0.02228 s, throughput:   5744.43 token/s
Decode 4. Batch size: 128, latency: 0.02229 s, throughput:   5741.20 token/s
Decode.  median latency: 0.02659 s, median throughput:   4814.38 token/s
Total. latency: 34.267 s, throughput:   7650.10 token/s

author: ovowei
body:
## Motivation

<!-- Explain the purpose of this PR and the goals it aims to achieve. -->

## Modifications

In the current implementation, `padded_scales` is initialized with shape `(B, M_padded, K_padded)`, but later reshaped to `(B, M, K)` or `(M, K)` depending on `scale_ndim`. This leads to a mismatch and potential runtime errors or incorrect memory alignment, especially during NVFP4 quantized inference using ModelOpt in SGLang.

title: [bug fix] Ensure local token and global token buffers are pointing to different storage
author: elfiegg
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation

coauthored by: @trevor-m 

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/8631 introduced layernorm before communication.

Root cause from @trevor-m:
 LayerNorm allocates a new output tensor. Since it's now applied before AllGather, the updated hidden states no longer reside in gathered_buffer, which breaks the assumption used by dp_scatter later.

 This is not allowed in `dp_scatter` as `dp_scatter` happens in place and might cause data corruptions.

To avoid the unpleasant behavior, alway assign new buffer for dp_scatter when above happens.

Accuracy test:
```
Accuracy: 0.962
Invalid: 0.000
Latency: 55.633 s
Output throughput: 950.633 token/s
```
Server command
```
SGL_ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM=0 python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-0528" --trust-remote-code --attention-backend trtllm_mla --page-size 64 --tp-size 8 --max-running-requests 64 --cuda-graph-max-bs 64 --enable-dp-attention --dp-size 8 --host "0.0.0.0" --port 30000 --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --dist-timeout 1800
```

Client
```
python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-shots 8 --num-questions 500 --parallel 5000 --port 30000
```


Original server crush log:

```
 File "/opt/mycode/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py", line 2037, in forward
    hidden_states, residual = layer(
                              ^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1751, in _wrapped_call_impl
    return self._call_impl(*args, **kwargs)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1762, in _call_impl
    return forward_call(*args, **kwargs)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/opt/mycode/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py", line 1893, in forward
    hidden_states, residual = self.layer_communicator.postprocess_layer(
                              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/opt/mycode/python/sglang/srt/layers/communicator.py", line 237, in postprocess_layer
    return self._communicate_summable_tensor_pair_fn(
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/opt/mycode/python/sglang/srt/layers/communicator.py", line 544, in _scatter_hidden_states
    dp_scatter(hidden_states, global_hidden_states, forward_batch)
  File "/opt/mycode/python/sglang/srt/layers/dp_attention.py", line 350, in dp_scatter
    local_tokens.untyped_storage() is not global_tokens.untyped_storage()
AssertionError: aliasing between local_tokens and global_tokens not allowed
```

title: fix crash of DeepSeek-V3 update_weights_from_disk
author: parkeychen
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation

This PR fixed the crash of DeepSeek-V3 `update_weights_from_disk` due to losing all extra attrs after `process_weights_after_loading`, which is similar to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/16854.

Specifically, calling `update_weights_from_disk` with DeepSeek-V3 will encounter an error as below. This is because `sglang.srt.models.deepseek_v2.DeepseekV2ForCausalLM.load_weights` accesses `param.weight_loader`, while the `param` is changed from `sglang.srt.layers.parameter.ModelWeightParameter` to `torch.nn.parameter.Parameter` in `sglang.srt.layers.quantization.fp8.Fp8LinearMethod.process_weights_after_loading`, losing the `weight_loader` attr.
```
  File "/root/conda/lib/python3.10/site-packages/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py", line 752, in update_weights_from_disk
    model = model_load_weights(self.model, iter)
  File "/root/conda/lib/python3.10/site-packages/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py", line 742, in model_load_weights
    DefaultModelLoader.load_weights_and_postprocess(model, iter, target_device)
  File "/root/conda/lib/python3.10/site-packages/sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py", line 445, in load_weights_and_postprocess
    model.load_weights(weights)
  File "/root/conda/lib/python3.10/site-packages/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py", line 2488, in load_weights
    weight_loader = param.weight_loader
AttributeError: 'Parameter' object has no attribute 'weight_loader'
```

title: Bug fix: use correct mm_items in embed_mm_inputs
author: byjiang1996
body: ## Motivation For a multimodal model, if there are more than one modalities in one request, it will lead to server crash. More details can be found here: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/8366 ## Modifications In this logic, it tries to get all the `mm_items` matching the give modality for the same request from a request batch and then calculates its `item_size=len(mm_items)` & `item_offset=flatten_nested_list([item.offsets for item in mm_items])` In the later logic, it will calculate `_get_chunked_prefill_embedding` using `item_size`, `item_offset`, `prefix_length` and `extend_length`. In the logic before this PR, it accidentally adds other modality's `mm_items` into `items_offset` list and thus causing unexpected results: **this bug only occurs if there are more than one modalities in one request** ## Accuracy Test Triggered the same tests mentioned in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/8366. sglang server can now successfully return the response instead of server crash. Added UTs to prevent regressions ## Benchmark & Profiling ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci). - [ ] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation-running-docs-ci). - [ ] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/accuracy_evaluation.html). - [ ] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging the PR. - [ ] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR.

title: [Fix] HiCache Bugfix & Mooncake Error Handling Enhance
author: ykwd
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Explain the purpose of this PR and the goals it aims to achieve. -->

## Modifications

<!-- Describe the changes made in this PR. -->

1. **Add error handling logic** for functions that call Mooncake-store operations such as `exists`, `get`, and `set`, to gracefully handle both full and partial failures.

2. **Fix several bugs in `generic_page_transfer`:**
   A) When the retrieved `page_data` is `None`, the function returned early without freeing the memory, leading to a memory leak.
   B) `set_from_flat_data_page` was called *after* incrementing the operation’s completed token. During the window between these two steps, the request processor might read from the destination before the data is actually copied, potentially causing incorrect reads.
   C) `storage_backend.batch_get` may return `None` for pages that fail to load. The current loop did not properly handle this case.

3. **Chore:** Introduce `_generic_storage_hit_query` and `_mooncake_storage_hit_query` to improve code modularity.

4. **Chore:** Remove the `MOONCAKE_LOCAL_BUFFER_SIZE` parameter, as the zero-copy method no longer requires a local buffer.

title: Fix chunked prefill size validation for disabled state
author: chi2liu
body:
## Motivation

This PR fixes an assertion error that occurs when `chunked_prefill_size` is set to -1 (disabled state).

As reported in #8935, users encountered a server crash when trying to disable chunked prefill using `--chunked-prefill-size -1`. The error message was:
```
AssertionError: chunked_prefill_size must be divisible by page_size
```

This is a critical bug because:
1. The value `-1` is the documented way to disable chunked prefill throughout the codebase
2. Many existing tests use `chunked_prefill_size=-1`
3. Certain configurations (e.g., B200 with DP attention and specific models) require disabling chunked prefill to work correctly

## Modifications

The fix adds a conditional check in `server_args.py` to skip validation when chunked prefill is disabled:

```python
# Before (causes assertion error with -1)
assert (
    self.chunked_prefill_size % self.page_size == 0
), "chunked_prefill_size must be divisible by page_size"

# After (correctly handles -1)
if self.chunked_prefill_size > 0:
    assert (
        self.chunked_prefill_size % self.page_size == 0
    ), "chunked_prefill_size must be divisible by page_size"
```

The change:
- Preserves validation for positive values to ensure correctness
- Skips validation for values ≤ 0 (disabled state)
- Aligns with the existing logic in `scheduler.py` where negative values are treated as disabled

## Accuracy Test

This PR only modifies validation logic and does not affect model-side code, kernels, or model architecture. No accuracy impact is expected.

## Benchmark & Profiling

This PR only modifies startup validation logic and has no performance impact on inference. The change:
- Does not affect runtime performance
- Only impacts server initialization validation
- Enables configurations that were previously blocked by incorrect validation

title: [Fix] Fix wrong backend chosen in hybrid backend
author: DarkSharpness
body:
## Motivation

When both `--prefill-attention` and `--decode-attention` are set to the same backend, the current logic may incorrectly fall back to a different backend, which may be misleading.

**Reproduction:**
```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
    --prefill-attention fa3 \
    --decode-attention fa3 \
    --enable-hierarchical-cache
````

This code will choose `flashinfer` as the attention backend. However, when both `--prefill-attention` and `--decode-attention` are explicitly specified as `fa3`, the configuration should be overridden accordingly. This is caused by the logic [here](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/f352b793be65a555194db31280a69b53dd40c4d4/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py#L1336), which fails to handle the case where `--prefill-attention` and `--decode-attention` are the same and not `None`.

While this is admittedly a rare edge case, the behavior should still be correct.

## Modifications

Fix the fallback logic when `--prefill-attention` and `--decode-attention` are identical. It will override the `attention-backend` in this case.

title: [Fix] Fix hicache backend
author: DarkSharpness
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, feel free to submit your PR and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation

It is a known issue that FA3 kernels do not work well with hicache kernels.  
When running FA3 decode kernels while hicache kernels are writing from GPU to CPU, an `illegal memory access` error may occur.

Previously, we worked around this by either:
- Avoiding the FA3 backend entirely, or  
- Using direct `cudaMemcpyAsync` instead of hicache kernels  

However, these workarounds can lead to suboptimal performance.

This PR addresses the issue by enabling the hybrid attention backend and using **flashinfer** for decode.  
This way, we can still leverage the high performance of FA3 prefill kernels while avoiding `illegal memory access` during decode.

## Modifications

- When the default attention backend is FA3 and hicache kernels are enabled, use **flashinfer** for decode.
- If override is not possible, fall back to using direct `cudaMemcpyAsync` in hicache (same behavior as before this PR).

title: [fix] Set Radix tree root node hash to None  - Nvidia Dynamo Integration
author: faradawn
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! We appreciate it. The following guidelines will help improve your pull request and facilitate feedback. If anything is unclear, don't hesitate to submit your pull request and ask the maintainers for assistance. -->

## Motivation

Problem: Sglang's tree nodes cannot be attached to Nvidia Dynamo's root node.

Solution: This occurs because we set the parent hash to be `hash(empty array)`, which is not `None`. However, we want the hash to be `None`, so that Dynamo knows that this is the first node and will attach it correctly to the root node. 

This fix addresses the problem from: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/6824/files

SGLang roadmap: https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/2261

title: [CPU] fix OOM when mem-fraction is not set
author: ZailiWang
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

In `server_args.py`, we set [the default `mem-fraction-static` as 0.88](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/server_args.py#L354) when it's not set at the command line. This is well applied for accelerator devices, yet need to be adjusted for CPU servers in which the memory is shared among all the TP ranks.

On CPU, the absence of `--mem-fraction-static` setting or a straightforward setting (e.g. 0.8, 0.9) without `--max-total-tokens` specified may lead to OOM.

## Modifications

For CPU, inquire the per-numa available memory amounts with the APIs provided in `py-libnuma`.
Since the per-rank memory status is unavailable if user specify `SGLANG_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND`, warning message are added in both doc and code to inform that the user should take care of the memory status and avoid OOM.

Update: Due to the compatibility issue of `py-libnuma` (it does not work with py311/py313), The per-numa free memory inquiry approach has changed to invoking the APIs in `libnuma.so` directly.

title: bugfix: Fix the commentary msg extraction in GptOssDetector
author: CatherineSue
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Fix the extraction of `commentary` messages in gpt-oss with non-stream tool-call.

The root cause is when the regex matches `<|start|>assistant<|channel|>commentary<|message|>`, the `match.start()` points to the beginning of this string. Then `rfind("<|channel|>commentary", 0, match_start)` will find the `<|channel|>commentary` in a different match, not within the same match.

For instance, 
```
clean_text = '<|channel|>commentary to=functions.sales_search 
  <|constrain|>json<|message|>{\n  "firstName": 
  "John"\n}<|call|><|start|>assistant<|start|>assistant<|channel|>commentary<|message|>{\n  "error": "No 
  data found for the given first name."\n}<|call|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>I’m sorry,
   but I couldn’t find any sales data for a representative named\u202fJohn. If you have additional 
  details (such as a last name, employee ID, or a different time range), please let me know and I’ll try 
  again.'
```

- rfind finds the `<|channel|>commentary` at position 0 (the previous one)
- It then checks if `to=` exists between position 0 and wherever `<|message|>` is found after position 0
- This gives wrong results because it's checking the wrong commentary section

title: Fix Harmony reasoning parser for and auto-separation for gpt-oss models
author: jonaslsaa
body:
## Motivation

This PR fixes critical regressions in Harmony reasoning output parsing that were introduced in PR #9043. After that change, gpt-oss models were incorrectly concatenating analysis and final content into `message.content` instead of properly separating reasoning into `message.reasoning_content`.

**Fixes issues:** #9139

**Issue symptoms:**
- `reasoning_content` was always `null` 
- `content` contained raw concatenated text like: `"analysisUser asks 'hi'...assistantfinalHello! How can I help?"`
- Broke OpenAI Harmony spec compliance for Chat Completions API

**Root causes:**
1. Text-based Harmony format parsing was broken due to regex word boundary issues
2. gpt-oss models weren't automatically enabling reasoning separation 
3. Several edge cases in both streaming and non-streaming parsing

## Modifications

### `python/sglang/srt/reasoning_parser.py`

**Major rewrite of GptOssDetector parsing logic:**
- **Text-based format support**: Added comprehensive regex patterns to handle gpt-oss output format:
  - `analysis...assistantfinal...` → split into reasoning + content
  - `assistantfinal...` → content only 
  - `analysis...` (truncated) → reasoning only
- **Simplified parsing**: Replaced complex sequential parsing with clear pattern matching
- **Commentary handling**: Removed incorrect extraction of commentary as reasoning content (per Harmony spec, commentary can be user-visible preambles)
- **Force reasoning fix**: Respect caller's `force_reasoning` parameter instead of hard-coding `True`
- **Streaming improvements**: Added proper incremental parsing for text-based formats with state management
- **Safe operations**: Fixed concatenation to handle `None` values safely

**Before vs After:**
```python
# Before: Complex sequential parsing that failed on text-based format
# After: Clean regex-based parsing that handles both formats:

# Text-based: "analysisUser reasoning...assistantfinalFinal answer"  
text_analysis_then_final = re.compile(
    r"^\s*(?:assistant)?\s*(analysis|commentary)(.*?)\s*assistantfinal\s*(.*)\s*$"
)

# Channel-based: "<|channel|>analysis<|message|>...<|end|>"
analysis_channel_pattern = re.compile(
    r"(?:<\|start\|>assistant)?<\|channel\|>analysis<\|message\|>(.*?)<\|end\|>"
)
```

### `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py`

**Auto-reasoning separation for gpt-oss models:**
- **Model detection**: Automatically detect gpt-oss models via `model_config.hf_config.model_type`
- **Parser auto-configuration**: Set reasoning parser to "gpt-oss" when not explicitly configured
- **Always separate**: Apply reasoning parsing for gpt-oss models regardless of `separate_reasoning` flag
- **Both code paths**: Updated streaming and non-streaming request handlers
- **Backwards compatibility**: Non-gpt-oss models unchanged

**Key changes:**
- Added gpt-oss detection logic to both streaming and non-streaming paths
- Modified reasoning parser selection to use auto-detected parser type
- Enhanced `_process_reasoning_stream` to accept dynamic parser type

## Testing

Verified fix handles all documented Harmony patterns:

**Text-based formats:**
- `analysis...assistantfinal...` → `reasoning_content` + `content` split
- `assistantfinal...` → `content` only, `reasoning_content: null`  
- `analysis...` (truncated) → `reasoning_content` only

**Channel-based formats:**
- `<|channel|>analysis<|message|>...<|end|>` + `<|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>...<|return|>`
- Tool calls preserved in content for downstream processing
- Commentary preambles kept in content (not extracted as reasoning)

## Result

Chat Completions now correctly return:
```json
{
  "message": {
    "content": "Hello! How can I help you today?",
    "reasoning_content": "User asks 'hi'. Simple greeting, respond politely."
  }
}
```

Instead of the broken:
```json  
{
  "message": {
    "content": "analysisUser asks 'hi'...assistantfinalHello! How can I help?",
    "reasoning_content": null
  }
}
```

Fixes compliance with OpenAI Harmony specification for gpt-oss models.

title: [router] preserve original worker response header in router
author: slin1237
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

The sglang router was not preserving HTTP response headers from backend workers when proxying responses. This caused issues where important headers like `Content-Type`, cache control headers, CORS headers, and custom application headers were being lost. Clients receiving responses from the router would not get the headers that the backend services intended to send. #8887 

## Modifications

  - Added a new `header_utils` module with functions to preserve and filter HTTP headers
  - Updated both the regular router and PD (Prefill-Decode) router to preserve response headers from backend workers
  - Implemented proper filtering of hop-by-hop headers (Connection, Keep-Alive, Transfer-Encoding, etc.) that should not be forwarded per HTTP specification
  - Ensured streaming responses maintain the correct `Content-Type: text/event-stream` header while preserving other headers
  - Applied header preservation to all response types: GET requests, POST requests (both streaming and non-streaming), and error responses

title: fix unexcepted answer in EAGLE mode
author: zyksir
body: ## Motivation This PR is to fix #8671 ## Modifications In the `filter_batch`, previous we had `self.topk_p = self.topk_p[: len(new_indices)]`, This line should never be used to filter since it makes no meaning if `len(new_indices) !=len(self.topk_p)` - Before Verification, we will filter finished requests. That's why we cannot use `self.topk_p = self.topk_p[new_indices]`. Since after verification, `len(topk_p)` might not be equal to `len(new_indices)`. - While After Draft Extend, we won't filter finished requests. Consider the case that the json schema is invalid. The request will still be sent to Extend, and will be filtered right after Extend. In this case, using `self.topk_p = self.topk_p[: len(new_indices)]` will cause the useful info to be filtered, and keep the info that belongs to the bad request. My Modification is to add one filter after extend. This should minimize the modification. ## Accuracy Tests The test script can be found in #8671 Before the modification: After the modification: ## Benchmarking and Profiling ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [router] introduce prefill response draining for http compliance
author: slin1237
body:
## Motivation

This PR fixes a critical HTTP/1.1 compliance violation in the prefill-decode (PD) router that was causing connection errors under high concurrency. 

Previously, when `return_logprob=false`, the router used a fire-and-forget approach with `tokio::spawn` that would close HTTP connections before fully consuming the prefill server's response body. This violates HTTP/1.1 specification (RFC 7230) which requires the entire response to be read before closing the connection. Under high load, this caused the prefill server to throw errors due to prematurely closed connections, often leading to `KVCacheError`.

## Modifications

### 1. **Added Background Drain Worker System**
   - Introduced a bounded channel (`prefill_drain_tx`) with 2000 buffer capacity to queue prefill responses for draining
   - Implemented a background coordinator task that spawns limited drain workers (max 100 concurrent via semaphore)
   - Each drain worker efficiently streams the response body to completion, ensuring HTTP compliance

### 2. **Fallback Mechanism for Extreme Load**
   - When the drain channel is full (>2000 pending), falls back to inline draining with 1s timeout
   - Ensures HTTP compliance even under extreme concurrency while preventing system overload
   - Added metrics and logging for monitoring drain queue health

### 3. **Zero-Latency Decode Processing**
   - Decode responses are processed immediately without waiting for prefill draining
   - Streaming passthrough for optimal performance

title: Fix gpt-oss response api streaming issue
author: key4ng
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

The streaming response API for gpt-oss models was experiencing two critical errors that prevented proper functionality. These issues needed to be resolved to ensure the API works correctly with streaming requests. 
Error shown from client side: `curl: (18) transfer closed with outstanding read data remaining`

## Issue 1: Pydantic Validation Error

### Problem
`ResponseOutputText` validation failed during streaming response generation.

### Raw Error Message
```
File "/home/ubuntu/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/pydantic/main.py", line 253, in __init__
    validated_self = self.__pydantic_validator__.validate_python(data, self_instance=self)
pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for ResponseOutputText
text
  Field required [type=missing, input_value={'content': [Content(text...text', 'logprobs': None}, input_type=dict]
    For further information visit https://errors.pydantic.dev/2.11/v/missing
```

### Root Cause
In streaming response handler (`serving_responses.py`), `ResponseOutputText` objects were created with `logprobs=[]` (empty list) instead of `logprobs=None`, inconsistent with the non-streaming code.

### Modification
Changed `logprobs=[]` to `logprobs=None` in two locations:
- Line 947: Fixed `ResponseContentPartAddedEvent` for final channel  
- Line 995: Fixed `ResponseContentPartAddedEvent` for analysis channel

### Files Modified
- `/home/ubuntu/sglang/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py`

## Issue 2: IndexError in Streaming

### Problem
Runtime crash when accessing message list during streaming response generation.

### Raw Error Message
```
File "/home/ubuntu/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/starlette/routing.py", line 76, in app
    await response(scope, receive, send)
  File "/home/ubuntu/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/starlette/responses.py", line 270, in __call__
    with collapse_excgroups():
  File "/usr/lib/python3.10/contextlib.py", line 153, in __exit__
    self.gen.throw(typ, value, traceback)
  File "/home/ubuntu/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/starlette/_utils.py", line 83, in collapse_excgroups
    raise exc
  File "/home/ubuntu/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/starlette/responses.py", line 274, in wrap
    await func()
  File "/home/ubuntu/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/starlette/responses.py", line 254, in stream_response
    async for chunk in self.body_iterator:
  File "/home/ubuntu/sglang/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py", line 831, in responses_stream_generator
    async for ctx in result_generator:
  File "/home/ubuntu/sglang/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py", line 1232, in _generate_with_builtin_tools
    if not context.need_builtin_tool_call():
  File "/home/ubuntu/sglang/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/context.py", line 110, in need_builtin_tool_call
    last_msg = self.messages[-1]
IndexError: list index out of range
```

### Root Cause
The method tried to access the last message without checking if the messages list was empty. In `StreamingHarmonyContext`, `self.messages` returns `self.parser.messages` which starts empty during streaming.

### Modification
Added safety check `if not self.messages: return False` before accessing `self.messages[-1]`, consistent with the existing `call_tool()` method.

### Files Modified
- `/home/ubuntu/sglang/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/context.py`

title: [NVIDIA] Fix trtllm fp4 moe backend when used in MTP
author: kaixih
body:
This PR addresses the issue mentioned [here](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/9238#issuecomment-3199279509).

The root cause is that some MoE layers may use an unquantized method. For example:
```
model.layers.3.mlp.experts → quantized  
model.decoder.mlp.experts  → unquantized
```

This may be triggered by the MTP settings.

`FusedMoE` works with both quantized and unquantized methods, which explains why the `flashinfer_cutlass` fp4 backend works fine.

`FlashInferFP4MoE` (i.e. the `flashinfer_trtllm` backend), however, only supports the modelopt_fp4 quantized method and fails with unquantized ones.

This PR fixes the issue by checking the quantization config. If no quantization config is found, we fall back to `FusedMoE`.

cc. @pranavm-nvidia @zhyncs @kushanam

title: fix: HiRadixCache: fix prefetch completion race
author: pabloiyu
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

SGLang allows for hierarchical KV caching. Under the default storage prefetch policy `best_effort`, the scheduler doesn’t have to wait for prefetch to finish: it can proceed to stage the request, which terminates the prefetch early and inserts no pages from storage. To wait for prefetch, we can use `wait_complete`.

 However, there is a race under `wait_complete`: the scheduler can call `self.tree_cache.check_prefetch_progress()` before the prefetch thread populates `operation.hash_value`. The completion check then treats 0 completed == 0 planned as done.

Fix: In `HiRadixCache.can_terminate_prefetch()`, only consider prefetch complete when `operation.hash_value` is non-empty and `operation.completed_tokens == len(operation.hash_value) * page_size`. This ensures the scheduler waits until the page list is prepared (and with `wait_complete`, until IO finishes).

title: Fix FlashInfer GPU <-> CPU sync
author: thecodingwizard
body:
## Motivation

There is an unnecessary GPU <-> CPU synchronization when running FlashInfer with tensor cores + page size 1. This is caused by moving `last_page_len` from the GPU to the CPU [here](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/f96413c444a4ce16c6b01770e28a636350df24bf/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashinfer_backend.py#L1375). When the page size is 1, `last_page_len` is always 1, so we do not need to transfer this tensor from the GPU to the CPU.

## Modifications

When `page_size = 1`, we directly construct a tensor of ones rather than moving `last_page_len` from the GPU to the CPU.

title: [fix] Fix mxfp4 triton MoE tp bug
author: hlu1
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/9433 broke GPT-OSS on Hopper because the MoE intermediate size was not padded after sharding on Hopper. Adding padding would fix the issue. However, it's only a workaround. The correct fix is to change the way of the weight sharding for block scaling data formats (mxfp4, nvfp4 etc) to the following before creating the weights and then add padding on top of that:

```
        intermediate_size_block = intermediate_size // mxfp4_block
        per_rank_intermediate_size_block = math.ceil(
            intermediate_size_block / moe_tp_size
        )
        per_rank_intermediate_size = per_rank_intermediate_size_block * mxfp4_block
```
This is a bigger change and will require more testing. I will do this in a followup PR.

## Modifications

Added intermediate size padding to triton MoE

## Accuracy Tests

8 x H100 tp8
```
before
[{'eval_name': 'gpqa', 'model_name': 'gpt-oss-120b-high_temp1.0_20250822_210411', 'metric': 0.7556818181818182}]

After
[{'eval_name': 'gpqa', 'model_name': 'gpt-oss-120b-high_temp1.0_20250823_015440', 'metric': 0.7986111111111112},
{'eval_name': 'mmlu', 'model_name': 'gpt-oss-120b-high_temp1.0_20250823_024653', 'metric': 0.8889759293547927}, 
{'eval_name': 'aime25', 'model_name': 'gpt-oss-120b-high_temp1.0_20250823_024653', 'metric': 0.9041666666666667}]
```

Perf on Hopper is going to regress a little bit because of padding, which means more computation than necessary. But the padding is necessary. Previously the weights were not even fully loaded so the computation is less that what it should have been.

title: [router] fix router load guard tracking for streaming
author: slin1237
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

When handling streaming responses, `WorkerLoadGuard` was being dropped too early (when `execute_dual_dispatch_internal` returns), causing load to be decremented while streaming was still in progress in background tasks.

#9484 

1. **Conditional guard creation**: Only create `WorkerLoadGuard` for non-streaming responses in `execute_dual_dispatch_internal`
2. **Manual load management for streaming**: In `create_streaming_response`, manually increment load at the start and decrement after streaming completes
3. **Proper cleanup in spawned task**: Extract worker URLs before spawning, then find and decrement the correct workers after streaming ends

## Modifications

- Modified `execute_dual_dispatch_internal` to conditionally create the guard based on `context.is_stream`
- Updated `create_streaming_response` to manually manage load tracking with proper cleanup in the spawned task
- Added `test test_streaming_load_tracking` to verify the fix works correctly

`
and the Client is a class in kube.So I revert kube(from 1.1.0 to 0.88.1)and kubeapi(from 0.25.0 to 0.21.0)
it works well.

just fix kube & kubeapi version in cargo.toml
update:
if we add 0.23 rustls dependency, it works as well, but 0.21 version could meet a crypto-not-found bug

title: [RL] fix register the same ops multiple times
author: hebiao064
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
Fix duplicate operator registration error in multi-engine scenarios

### Problem
When import SGLang multiple times within the same Python process (e.g., in the VERL framework), users encounter a `RuntimeError` due to duplicate PyTorch operator registration:
```
RuntimeError: Tried to register an operator (sglang::deep_gemm_fp8_fp8_bf16_nt(...)) with the same name and overload name multiple times. Each overload's schema should only be registered with a single call to def().
```

This occurs because PyTorch doesn't allow the same custom operator to be registered multiple times, but SGLang was attempting to register operators every time a module was imported.

### Solution
Enhanced the `direct_register_custom_op` function in `utils.py` to gracefully handle duplicate registrations by:

1. **Pre-registration check**: Before attempting to register an operator, check if it already exists in the target library namespace
2. **Silent duplicate handling**: Catch and silently ignore `RuntimeError` exceptions specifically related to duplicate operator registration
3. **Backward compatibility**: Maintain existing functionality for single-engine scenarios

### Changes Made

#### 🔧 `python/sglang/srt/utils.py`
- Added pre-registration existence check using `hasattr(torch.ops, lib_name)`
- Enhanced error handling to catch and ignore duplicate registration `RuntimeError`
- Added comprehensive documentation explaining the multi-engine support
- Improved code formatting for better readability


#### 🔧 `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py`
- Removed redundant hasattr checks (now handled in `direct_register_custom_op`)
- Simplified exception handling to focus on `AttributeError` only
- Cleaned up registration flow for both `dequant_mxfp4` and `quant_dequant_mxfp4` operators

### Testing
This fix has been designed to:
- ✅ Allow multiple SGLang engines to run in the same Python process without errors
- ✅ Maintain backward compatibility with existing single-engine deployments
- ✅ Preserve all existing operator functionality
- ✅ Support frameworks like VERL that spawn multiple engines

### Impact
- **Users**: Eliminates crashes when using SGLang in multi-engine frameworks like VERL
- **Developers**: Provides a robust foundation for operator registration that handles edge cases
- **Performance**: No performance impact; checks are minimal and only occur during initialization

### Related Issues
Fixes the duplicate operator registration error reported when using SGLang with VERL framework (2-4 engines in the same process).

title: [fix] Relax white space rules in EBNFComposer
author: LukasBluebaum
body:
## Motivation

Grammar changes related to this issue: #9311 

I think the problem is that the grammar in the EBNFComposer is too strict when it comes to whitespace. In xgrammar there is a setting to allow arbitrary whitespace inside a json. This is also set to true in vLLM. With these changes the examples from the issue run and output the URL as expected, so apparently DeepSeek is just very sensitive to this setting.

The question is if it should actually be the default behavior in general now or if it should maybe be an optional setting as in xgrammar (e.g. `allow_arbitrary_whitespace`) or each detector could also just set it directly in it’s `build_ebnf` function.

## Modifications

1. Change some grammar rules inside the EBNFComposer adding `ws` around separators like `:` or `,`

title: fix: allow user to specify function as role
author: GavinZhu-GMI
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
When serving DeepSeek v3.1, the OpenAI API endpoint encounters a validation error due to protocol version incompatibility. The error occurs because:
1. Client Request Issue: The incoming request contains messages with role: 'function', which is part of the OpenAI API v1 function calling format.
2. Protocol Validation Failure: The current SGLang OpenAI protocol implementation only supports these roles: system assistant tool user

When user prompt with role function (OpenAI compatible), sglang will return 400.


## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
Update the role literal to include function then update the field validator to accept function.

title: Quick fix for loading processor for supporting internvl3_5 series
author: yilian49
body:
## Motivation

InternVL 3.5 models fail to start in SGLang with `transformers==4.56.0.dev0` because `AutoProcessor.from_pretrained` instantiates `InternVLProcessor`, which expects tokenizer attributes (e.g. `start_image_token`) missing from `Qwen2TokenizerFast`.  
Upstream issue: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/40475

## Reproduction

```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path OpenGVLab/InternVL3_5-30B-A3B
```

## Error Trace

```

error reported: Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<frozen runpy>", line 198, in _run_module_as_main
  File "<frozen runpy>", line 88, in _run_code
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/launch_server.py", line 14, in <module>
    launch_server(server_args)
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/http_server.py", line 1071, in launch_server
    tokenizer_manager, template_manager, scheduler_info = _launch_subprocesses(
                                                          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py", line 819, in _launch_subprocesses
    tokenizer_manager = TokenizerManager(server_args, port_args)
                        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py", line 212, in __init__
    _processor = get_processor(
                 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/hf_transformers_utils.py", line 371, in get_processor
    processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(
                ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/sgl-workspace/transformers/src/transformers/models/auto/processing_auto.py", line 391, in from_pretrained
    return processor_class.from_pretrained(
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/sgl-workspace/transformers/src/transformers/processing_utils.py", line 1304, in from_pretrained
    return cls.from_args_and_dict(args, processor_dict, **kwargs)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/sgl-workspace/transformers/src/transformers/processing_utils.py", line 1105, in from_args_and_dict
    processor = cls(*args, **valid_kwargs)
                ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/sgl-workspace/transformers/src/transformers/models/internvl/processing_internvl.py", line 81, in __init__
    self.start_image_token = tokenizer.start_image_token
                             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/sgl-workspace/transformers/src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py", line 1099, in __getattr__
    raise AttributeError(f"{self.__class__.__name__} has no attribute {key}")
AttributeError: Qwen2TokenizerFast has no attribute start_image_token

## Modification

In hf_transformers_utils.get_processor:
- Detect InternVL 3.5 repos (simple string check: "InternVL3_5" in tokenizer_name).

title: Fix get_ip when no external network
author: whybeyoung
body:
When all worker nodes fail to connect to the external network, the current logic for retrieving the outbound IP becomes invalid and will return 0.0.0.0. To address this, we will add a fallback method to obtain the local IP via the hostname.

This fallback mechanism works by resolving the local hostname to its corresponding IP address (using system calls like gethostbyname or framework-specific functions such as Python’s socket.gethostbyname(socket.gethostname())). It ensures that even in offline environments (where external network-dependent IP retrieval fails), the node can still obtain a valid local IP for internal communication or logging purposes.

The implementation will prioritize the original outbound IP check first, then seamlessly switch to the hostname-based method if the former fails, maintaining compatibility while enhancing robustness in network-restricted scenarios.

CC @ShangmingCai @zhyncs @merrymercy

title: [router] Fix short timeout for the prefill client
author: LukasBluebaum
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Currently, the timeout for the prefill client in the `return_logprobs = False` path is set to only 2 secs. This leads to many premature request aborts as soon as some load is on the server: #9266 . Here I also set the `request_timeout_secs` on the prefill client in that path. It might also make sense to decouple this and have an extra timeout variable for the prefill client.

I think in a future PR further improvements could be to cancel the decode in this path immediately if the prefill fails for some reason and also to maybe set a timeout on the background drains too.

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Modifications

- Propagate `request_timeout_secs` to the prefill client

title: [Bug Fix] Fix Glm4vVisionBlock norm
author: sdpkjc
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

This PR fixes a runtime crash in `Glm4vVisionBlock` when running vision prefill. After #9709, `Qwen2_5_VisionBlock` calls `norm2(x2d, residual=attn2d)` and expects a residual-aware interface that returns `(norm2d, after_add2d)`. `Glm4vVisionBlock` was still overriding `norm1/norm2` with `Glm4vRMSNorm`, whose `forward` did not accept `residual`, causing a `TypeError` and the worker to die.

**Minimum Reproduce**

```python
import sglang as sgl
from PIL import Image
from io import BytesIO
import requests
from transformers import AutoTokenizer


model_path = "zai-org/GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking"
image_url = "https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/test/lang/example_image.png?raw=true"

if __name__ == "__main__":
    image = Image.open(BytesIO(requests.get(image_url).content))

    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_path)
    messages = [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "image"}, {"type": "text", "text": "What's shown here?"}]}]
    prompt = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)

    engine = sgl.Engine(model_path=model_path)
    ret = engine.generate(prompt=prompt, image_data=[image])

    print("\n=== Prompt ===\n", prompt)
    print("\n=== Completion ===\n", ret["text"])

'''
ERROR INFO:
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1773, in _wrapped_call_impl
    return self._call_impl(*args, **kwargs)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1784, in _call_impl
    return forward_call(*args, **kwargs)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/sglang/srt/models/qwen2_5_vl.py", line 188, in forward
    x_norm_2d, x_after_add_2d = self.norm2(x2d, residual=attn2d)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1773, in _wrapped_call_impl
    return self._call_impl(*args, **kwargs)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1784, in _call_impl
    return forward_call(*args, **kwargs)
TypeError: Glm4vRMSNorm.forward() got an unexpected keyword argument 'residual'
'''
```

**Packages Versions:**

* sglang: 0.5.2rc0
* torch: 2.8.0
* transformers: 4.56.0
* model: `GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking`

**Bug cause:**

* `Qwen2_5_VisionBlock` (post-#9709) reshapes to 2D and invokes `self.norm2(..., residual=...)`.
* `Glm4vVisionBlock` overrides `self.norm1/self.norm2` with `Glm4vRMSNorm`, whose `forward(x)` signature lacked the `residual` kwarg.
* When the parent `forward()` path executed, Python raised `TypeError` due to the unexpected keyword.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

* Do **not** override `self.norm1` / `self.norm2` in `Glm4vVisionBlock.__init__`.
* Rely on the parent `Qwen2_5_VisionBlock`’s `RMSNorm` modules introduced in #9709, which natively support the `residual` path and 2D reshape semantics.

This is the smallest change that fully restores compatibility and matches the new canonical behavior.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

After the fix, the same script can run successfully, and the output is as expected.

title: [Fix] DeepSeek EP accuracy issue on B200 GPUs
author: alhridoy
body:
## Problem

DeepSeek models with expert parallelism (EP) experience accuracy issues on NVIDIA B200 GPUs while working correctly on H200 GPUs. This affects GSM8K benchmark and other accuracy-sensitive workloads.

**Affected Configuration:**
```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324 --tp-size 8 --ep-size 8 --trust-remote-code
python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py
```

**Symptoms:**
- ✅ Works correctly on H200 GPUs (SM90 architecture)
- ❌ Produces incorrect results on B200 GPUs (SM100 Blackwell architecture)
- No error messages, but accuracy degradation in model outputs

## Root Cause

The issue is caused by Blackwell-specific optimizations in the DeepEP dispatcher:

1. **Architecture Detection**: B200 GPUs are automatically detected as Blackwell architecture (SM100)
2. **UE8M0 Scaling**: Blackwell-specific UE8M0 FP8 scaling optimizations are automatically enabled
3. **Accuracy Impact**: These optimizations prioritize performance over numerical precision, causing accuracy degradation

**Key Code Location:**
```python
# python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/deepep.py
if deep_gemm_wrapper.ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM:
    hidden_states = sglang_per_token_group_quant_fp8(
        hidden_states,
        128,
        column_major_scales=deep_gemm_wrapper.DEEPGEMM_SCALE_UE8M0,  # This causes issues on B200
        scale_tma_aligned=deep_gemm_wrapper.DEEPGEMM_SCALE_UE8M0,
        scale_ue8m0=deep_gemm_wrapper.DEEPGEMM_SCALE_UE8M0,
    )
```

## Solution

Add a new server argument `--disable-deepgemm-ue8m0` to disable Blackwell-specific optimizations when accuracy is critical.

### Changes Made

1. **Server Argument**: Added `--disable-deepgemm-ue8m0` flag in `server_args.py`
2. **Configuration Function**: Added `update_deepgemm_scale_ue8m0()` in `configurer.py` to control UE8M0
3. **Integration**: Connected server args to DeepGEMM configuration in `compile_utils.py`

### Usage

**For B200 GPUs (with accuracy fix):**
```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324 \
    --tp-size 8 --ep-size 8 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --disable-deepgemm-ue8m0
```

**For H200 GPUs (no change needed):**
```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324 \
    --tp-size 8 --ep-size 8 \
    --trust-remote-code
```

**Environment Variable Alternative:**
```bash
export SGL_ENABLE_DEEPGEMM_UE8M0=false
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324 --tp-size 8 --ep-size 8 --trust-remote-code
```

author: mss1213
body: ### BUG Description When use wait_complete policy for HiCache prefetch and batch_get meet error, it will occur that the req in prefetch will not be scheduled because the operation will not be completed; This PR would change the operation complete condition, add one flag "failed" for the unexpected error. ### Reproduction use hicache_storage_prefetch_policy = 'wait_complete' and produce some error on batch_get(such as modify its return value)。You can also use offline script， and the program will hang up. ``` import sglang as sgl from sglang.lang.api import Engine import json import os import time import random model_path = "/data01/models/DeepSeek-R1" def generate_prompts(): random.seed(100) prompts = [] for i in range(4): prompt = [] for j in range(1000): prompt.append(random.randint(0, 16000)) prompts.append(prompt) return prompts def main(): prompts = generate_prompts() print(f"prompts: {len(prompts)}") llm = Engine( model_path=model_path, enable_hierarchical_cache=True, hicache_write_policy="write_through", mem_fraction_static=0.3, hicache_ratio=1.1, hicache_io_backend='kernel', hicache_mem_layout='page_first', hicache_storage_backend='file', hicache_storage_prefetch_policy='wait_complete', log_level="info", trust_remote_code=True, tp_size=8, page_size=16, enable_torch_compile=False, json_model_override_args='{"num_hidden_layers": 10}', ) sampling_params = {"temperature": 0, "max_new_tokens": 20, "ignore_eos": True} logprob = True extra_params = {} if logprob: extra_params["return_logprob"] = True extra_params["top_logprobs_num"] = 5 bs = 1 for i in range(0, len(prompts), bs): batch_prompts = prompts[i:i + bs] print(f"batch {i // bs}: {len(batch_prompts)}") start_time = time.perf_counter() outputs = llm.generate(sampling_params=sampling_params, input_ids=batch_prompts, **extra_params) end_time = time.perf_counter() print(f"outputs: {outputs}") print(f"batch {i // bs} cost time: {end_time - start_time:.4f}s") print(f"all done") if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` ### Thoughts I think 'wait_complete' means that scheduler should wait for the operation complete (success or fail both are completed) but not all tokens are prefetched success. Actually batch_get can not always return success even use retry (or use batch_exists first) when use remote storage.

title: fix: fp8 quantization failure of qwen 2.5 VL 7B model
author: PanJason
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Fix this bug https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/6828 of qwen 2.5 VL 7B where fp8 quantization was reported to fail in the visual model part.

## Modifications

1. Make the initialization of the intermediate size in qwen 2.5 VL 7B 8-aligned
2. Change both `weight_loader` and `weight_loader_v2` in `linear.py` to add zero padding when loading weights that are not 8-aligned. After this fix, both `w8a8_fp8` and `fp8` can work
3. Change `w8a8_int8.py` to fix the runtime crash when using `w8a8_int8`

We don't change the kernel as the previous version did #7448

## Remaining work
While fixing the quantization failure for qwen2_5_VL model, I found two other issues. Since they are not exactly related to VL model, I created two other issues. The fix of them will go to different patch series
1. When sending two concurrent requests to qwen2_5_VL model, rotary_embedding crashed regardless of quantization, this is reported in #10623 
2. When fixing w8a8_int8, I found qwen2.5 7B instruct base model generates gibberish. This is reported in #10626

title: [Fix] KV-cache eviction mismatch across PP ranks in DeepSeek V3/R1
author: qhsc
body: ## Motivation Fix KV-cache size mismatch across PP ranks that causes crashes with radix cache. In a PP=2 setup with the DeepSeek V3/R1 model, the maximum total tokens reserved for the KV cache in pp0 and pp1 are not equal. When radix cache is enabled, after some time, the prefix cached num of tokens for the same req will be in-consistent among pp ranks due to asymmetric cache evict, which will lead to system crash. title: [fix CI] Fix logical condition in fused MoE layer for compressed tensor quantization
author: BBuf
body:
### Background

The bug is caused by https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/8118 cc @chenxijun1029 

The current code in `fused_moe_triton/layer.py` has a logical operator precedence issue in the condition check for input scales validation (lines 615-620). The problematic condition was:

```python
if (
    "compressed" in self.quant_method.__class__.__name__.lower()
    or "w4afp8" in self.quant_config.get_name()
    and (param.data[expert_id] != 1).any()
    and ((param.data[expert_id] - loaded_weight).abs() > 1e-5).any()
):
```

Due to operator precedence (`and` has higher precedence than `or`), this condition is actually parsed as:

```python
if (
    "compressed" in self.quant_method.__class__.__name__.lower()
    or (
        "w4afp8" in self.quant_config.get_name()
        and (param.data[expert_id] != 1).any()
        and ((param.data[expert_id] - loaded_weight).abs() > 1e-5).any()
    )
):
```

This means that **any** model using compressed tensors quantization will unconditionally trigger the ValueError, regardless of whether the input scales are actually equal or not.

### Error Observed

When loading models with compressed tensors quantization (e.g., `neuralmagic/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-FP8`), the following error occurs:

```
ValueError: input_scales of w1 and w3 of a layer must be equal. But got 1.0 vs. tensor([0.1011], device='cuda:1', dtype=torch.bfloat16)
```

### Solution

Add parentheses to ensure correct operator precedence:

```python
if (
    ("compressed" in self.quant_method.__class__.__name__.lower()
    or "w4afp8" in self.quant_config.get_name())
    and (param.data[expert_id] != 1).any()
    and ((param.data[expert_id] - loaded_weight).abs() > 1e-5).any()
):
```

Now the condition correctly checks:
- The quantization method is either `compressed` OR `w4afp8` 
- AND the parameter data is not equal to 1
- AND the difference between existing and loaded weights exceeds the threshold

This ensures the validation only runs when appropriate and doesn't incorrectly fail for valid compressed tensor models.

### Testing

This fix resolves the model loading failure for compressed tensor quantized models like `neuralmagic/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-FP8` in the nightly GSM8K evaluation tests.
