title: Fix BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper query/qo_inptr mismatch for EAGLE
author: wenscarl
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
When the batch dimension of the query does not match `qo_indptr[-1]` in `BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper` (as described in FlashInfer issue #[2236](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/2236)), an invalid memory access can occur as below. 
```
  File "/workspace/build/aot/generated/batch_mla_attention_dtype_q_bf16_dtype_kv_bf16_dtype_o_bf16_dtype_idx_i32_head_dim_ckv_512_head_dim_kpe_64_profiler_False/batch_mla_run.cu", line 123, in BatchMLAPagedAttentionRun(tvm::ffi::TensorView, tvm::ffi::TensorView, tvm::ffi::Array<long int>, tvm::ffi::TensorView, tvm::ffi::TensorView, tvm::ffi::TensorView, tvm::ffi::TensorView, tvm::ffi::TensorView, tvm::ffi::TensorView, tvm::ffi::Optional<tvm::ffi::TensorView>, int64_t, int64_t, int64_t, double, bool)::<lambda()>
RuntimeError: Check failed: (status == cudaSuccess) is false: Failed to run MLA, error: an illegal memory access was encountered

```

The root cause is that the forward_metadata—including `qo_indptr`—is not updated in the TRTLLM MLA backend, leading to inconsistent metadata being used during execution.

title: [Fix] Add --disable-draft-model-update to control draft model updates(especially in RL)
author: bingyang-lei
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
This PR does:
- Add `--disable-draft-model-update` parameter to determine whether to update the draft model.

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
The motivation is as follows:

In PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/7415, they support update_weights_from_tensor for mtp. However, in many cases, the RL framework only supports mtp layer updates, not external draft model updates. So If I only want to use an external draft model (e.g., trained by SpecForge) to accelerate inference during the RL rollout process without updating the draft model, the current SGlang engine will incorrectly load the main model weights into the draft model, causing issues like https://github.com/THUDM/slime/issues/1177

Therefore, we need to introduce an additional parameter to determine whether to update the draft model. If the external draft model is solely used to enhance inference speed, weight updates should not be performed during RL training.

## Modifications

title: Fix GLM-4.7 MoE Detector complex JSON Schema type parsing
author: Leoyzen
body:
- Modify get_argument_type function to correctly parse complex JSON Schema structures including anyOf/oneOf/allOf and OpenAI-style array types like ["string", "null"]
- Improve _format_value_complete function to properly handle object/array types as JSON rather than strings
- Add additional parsing strategies in parse_arguments for object/array type handling
- Add comprehensive test cases to verify complex type definitions are correctly parsed as their appropriate data types (e.g., arrays) rather than strings

This fixes the issue where array values like [] were being parsed as string "[]" instead of actual array [].

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

This pull request addresses a bug in the GLM-4.7 MoE Detector where complex JSON Schema types were not being parsed correctly. Specifically, when a tool parameter was defined with complex structures like `anyOf` (e.g., `{"anyOf": [{"type": "array"}, {"type": "null"}]}`), the values were being treated as strings instead of their actual types (like arrays). For example, an array value `[]` would be parsed as the string `"[]"` rather than the actual array `[]`.

## Modifications

- Modified `get_argument_type` function in `glm47_moe_detector.py` to correctly parse complex JSON Schema structures including anyOf/oneOf/allOf and OpenAI-style array types like ["string", "null"]
- Improved `_format_value_complete` function to properly handle object/array types as JSON rather than strings
- Added additional parsing strategies in `parse_arguments` for object/array type handling
- Added comprehensive test cases in `test_function_call_parser.py` to verify complex type definitions are correctly parsed as their appropriate data types (e.g., arrays) rather than strings

## Accuracy Tests

The fix has been validated with test cases that confirm complex JSON Schema types are now correctly parsed. The tests verify that array values like `[]` are correctly interpreted as arrays instead of strings.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

No performance impact is expected from these changes as they only affect the parsing logic when complex types are encountered.

title: Fix: Handle empty func_name and None values in GLM MoE detectors
author: Leoyzen
body:
- Fix AssertionError when func_name is empty by adding proper checks
- Handle None values before calling strip() method to prevent AttributeError
- Add boundary case handling for partial matches in GLM-4.7 and GLM-4 MoE detectors
- Add test cases to verify the fixes for empty function name handling

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

This pull request addresses critical issues in the GLM-4.7 and GLM-4 MoE function call parsers that were causing runtime errors. Specifically, the parsers were throwing AssertionError when encountering empty function names and AttributeError when trying to call strip() on None values. These issues occurred when the model outputted only the start token without a complete function name, which is a common occurrence during streaming inference. The fixes ensure robust handling of partial and incomplete function call patterns, improving the reliability of function call parsing for GLM models.

See also 

* https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/15721

## Modifications

1. **GLM-4.7 MoE Detector** (`python/sglang/srt/function_call/glm47_moe_detector.py`):
   - Added proper null checks before accessing regex match groups
   - Implemented safe handling of empty function names to prevent AssertionError
   - Added None checks before calling strip() method to prevent AttributeError
   - Improved boundary case handling for partial matches during streaming

2. **GLM-4 MoE Detector** (`python/sglang/srt/function_call/glm4_moe_detector.py`):
   - Applied similar fixes as GLM-4.7 to ensure consistency
   - Added safe checks for function name validation
   - Improved handling of None values in parameter processing

3. **Test Cases** (`test/registered/function_call/test_function_call_parser.py`):
   - Added `test_empty_function_name_handling` test cases for both detectors
   - Verified that the parsers handle partial function call patterns gracefully
   - Ensured that no exceptions are thrown when processing incomplete function names

## Accuracy Tests

No specific accuracy tests were required as this PR addresses robustness and error handling rather than changing the core functionality of the parsers. The existing test suite ensures that the functional behavior remains unchanged while improving error handling.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

No performance impact is expected from these changes as they only add null checks and safe handling of edge cases. The core parsing logic remains unchanged, ensuring the same performance characteristics.

title: [MTP][spec_v2] Fix TRTLLM MLA backend crash in EAGLE draft_extend mode
author: YAMY1234
body: ## Motivation Fix a crash in TRTLLM MLA backend during EAGLE speculative decoding in `draft_extend` mode when sequences have varying `accept_length` values. This can be reproduced by the following agg command (and also intermittency issues in the disagg setup in benchmark section): ``` SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1 SGLANG_FLASHINFER_FP4_GEMM_BACKEND=cutlass SGLANG_DISABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path ${MODEL} --served-model-name dsr1 --tp 4 --attention-backend trtllm_mla --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm --moe-dense-tp-size 1 --quantization modelopt_fp4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --disable-radix-cache --chunked-prefill-size -1 --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 2 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 3 --mem-fraction-static 0.80 ``` Error: ``` File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/trtllm_mla_backend.py", line 1046, title: [HiCache] Fix deadlock when creating new group
author: XucSh
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
This PR fixes a critical deadlock (hang) issue during the initialization of HiCacheController when running sglang in a multi-node distributed environment (e.g., 2 nodes with 8 GPUs each).

When launching the server with --enable-hierarchical-cache  --hicache-storage-backend on multiple nodes, the initialization process hangs at torch.distributed.new_group.

Root Cause Analysis: torch.distributed.new_group is a collective operation. It requires all ranks in the default world group to call it in the same order with the exact same arguments (specifically the ranks list).

In the previous implementation of HiCacheController （PP2 TP8）:

Node 0 (Ranks 0-7) called new_group(ranks=[0...7]).

Node 1 (Ranks 8-15) called new_group(ranks=[8...15]).

Because the arguments differed across ranks, the internal distributed store  could not match the creation requests, causing a deadlock where Node 0 waited for Node 1 to acknowledge the creation of Group A, while Node 1 was attempting to create Group B.

reported by: @whybeyoung 
CC @stmatengss

title: [CI] Fix LoRA downloading issues and respect offline flag
author: Prozac614
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

Currently, the maybe_download_model utility in hf_diffusers_utils.py fails when downloading LoRA adapters. This is because it enforces a strict verification check (expecting transformer/ and vae/ directories) which LoRAs do not possess. This leads to false positives where the code assumes the download failed and triggers a forced re-download, often causing ConnectionErrors in CI environments.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
CI fix: Fixed the cache problem for CI pip/uv .

Robust HF Downloads:

Increased retry limits (from 3 to 5) and extended etag_timeout to handle handshake delays better.

Refined snapshot_download to specifically target *.safetensors and *.json for LoRAs using allow_patterns, significantly reducing request volume.

LoRA Logic Fix: Skipped strict structural verification (transformer/vae folder checks) for LoRA models, as they follow a different file structure.

OOM Retry: Implemented a try-catch block for torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError, allowing the system to attempt a retry (potentially after clearing cache) instead of crashing immediately.

title: [Bugfix] fix npu get kv_item_lens in PD separation when use ASCEND_US…
author: XDaoHong
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
Original `k_buffer` shape is` (layer_num, size // page_size + 1, page_size, head_num, head_dim)`,
when enable `ASCEND_USE_FIA` `k_buffer `shape is `(layer_num, (size // page_size + 1) * page_size, 1, head_num, head_dim)`.

The element size of `self.get_key_buffer(i)[0]` in `def get_contiguous_buf_infos()`:
original is `page_size * head_num * head_dim`,
when enable `ASCEND_USE_FIA` is `1 * head_num * head_dim`.

So when enable `ASCEND_USE_FIA`, The calculation of kv_item_lens requires the addition of `* page_size`.

## Modifications

Fix kv_item_lens for FIA, in order to compute data size in PD transfer cases.

title: [PP] fix wrong weight logic for tie_word_embeddings model
author: XucSh
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
see #15843 

This PR fixes a bug where models with tie_word_embeddings=True (e.g., Qwen3-4B) output garbage text (random characters) when running with Pipeline Parallelism (e.g., PP=2).

In Pipeline Parallelism, the Last Rank is responsible for the lm_head. For models with tied embeddings, lm_head.weight shares the same data as model.embed_tokens.weight.

The previous implementation of load_weights had a logic flaw:

It filters weights based on layer_id.

model.embed_tokens.weight is effectively treated as Layer 0.

The Last Rank (which handles the final layers) skips model.embed_tokens.weight because Layer 0 is outside its assigned layer range (start_layer > 0).

The current code works for Qwen3-0.6b(with tie_word_embeddings set) is that its model.safetensors contains lm_head.weight

title: [scheduler] fix: correcting `extend_logprob_start_len` calculation
author: ch-wan
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

The original calculation for `extend_logprob_start_len` was incorrect ([code](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/656f4d69a1bc8bc9c2addd1a33b0409b454136e5/python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py#L1509)). When kv retraction happens, it should be determined based on `len(fill_ids)` (the total number of original input ids and output ids) when `return_logprob` is `False` but `logprob_start_len` is set as `len(origin_input_ids) - 1`.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

We set `logprob_start_len` as -1 by default when `return_logprob` is `False` so that `extend_logprob_start_len` can be set as `len(fill_ids) - 1` during `prepare_for_extend`. We also reverted changes in #12115 as it's no longer needed.

## Accuracy Tests, Benchmarking and Profiling

title: [bugfix] fix mamba slot leak when scheduling fails with radix cache (#15840)
author: kuafou
body:
## Motivation

This PR fixes a server crash caused by a false positive "memory leak detected" error when serving Mamba models with `radix-cache` enabled.

The issue was discovered during the investigation of #15840 but is a distinct issue regarding the scheduler's failure path cleanup. It occurs when the scheduler is temporarily resource-blocked (e.g., during request retraction), causing `check_memory()` to flag a temporarily untracked Mamba slot as leaked.

## Modifications

* Explicitly release the COW-allocated Mamba slot if `add_one_req` fails (returns `NO_TOKEN` or `IDLE`) during the scheduling phase.
* Add a regression test `test_mamba_slot_release_after_match_prefix_cow` to verify the cleanup logic.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — resource cleanup only, no model output changes.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

N/A — failure-path fix, no performance impact.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).
- [ ] Work with maintainers to merge your PR. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process)

### Details
**The Problem:**
1. In `init_next_round_input()`, a Mamba slot is allocated via Copy-On-Write (COW) / `match_prefix`.
2. Subsequently, `add_one_req()` is called but returns `NO_TOKEN` (e.g., because the KV cache pool is full).
3. The scheduler enters an "Idle" state (which technically means "resource-blocked" in this context) and triggers `self_check_during_idle()` -> `check_memory()`.
4. `check_memory()` fails because the slot allocated in step 1 is:
    * Not in `free_slots` (it was allocated).
    * Not yet tracked by `tree_cache` (the request didn't finish scheduling).
    * **Result:** The server crashes with `ValueError: token_to_kv_pool_allocator memory leak detected!`.

**The Fix:**
When scheduling fails, we now explicitly free the temporary Mamba slot. The request remains in the `waiting_queue` and will safely re-allocate (and copy) the Mamba state in the next scheduling round.

### Error Log
The server crashes with the following error during high load/retraction:

```text
ValueError: token_to_kv_pool_allocator memory leak detected! full_available_size=6016, full_evictable_size=390685, self.token_to_kv_pool_allocator.size=396701, self.tree_cache.full_protected_size()=0
mamba_available_size=315, mamba_evictable_size=138, self.req_to_token_pool.mamba_pool.size=454, self.tree_cache.mamba_protected_size()=0, leaked_full_pages=None, leaked_mamba_pages={191}

title: Fix KeyError when logprobs=false in completions endpoint
author: haikux
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

The /v1/completions endpoint crashes with a KeyError: 'output_top_logprobs' when logprobs=0/invalid (like False) in the request. This occurred because the code unconditionally accessed
ret_item["meta_info"]["output_top_logprobs"] regardless of whether logprobs were requested.
The /v1/chat/completions endpoint already handles this correctly using .get() with a default value.

## Modifications

Changed serving_completions.py:245 and serving_completions.py:404 to use
.get("output_top_logprobs", []) instead of direct dictionary access
This prevents KeyError when logprobs is not requested in /v1/completions endpoint (both
streaming and non-streaming)

title: [VLM] Fix CUDA IPC OOM

## Motivation

Close https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/16106.
<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
The feature Memory Pool based CUDA IPC has a fallback mechanism, if the slice can't be allocated, it will fallback to use the legacy Tensor.
If it is the case, the current implementation forgets to call D2H, the memory leak and OOM happens very frequently.

title: [Bugfix] fix some memory computation bugs for qwen3next with mtp
author: yizhang2077
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
I think there are some memory initialization computation issues for qwen3next when using mtp:
1. miss computing mtp mamba memory footprint when disable radix cache
2. do not need `additional_ratio` if `mamba_scheduler_strategy` is `no_buffer`
3. `max_num_reqs` for mtp should no large than `max_running_requests / dp_size` when use dp attention, since `max_running_requests` for per-rank needs be divided by `dp_size`.

title: [Fix] Distinguish between video generation and image generation in the bench serving of the diffusion model.
author: jiapingW
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
Because discrepancies in the description and functionality of image generation commands in bench serving could lead to user misunderstandings, the commands for video generation and image generation have now been separated.
The current task is listed below:
```

python3 -m sglang.multimodal_gen.benchmarks.bench_serving \
    --backend sglang-video --dataset vbench --task t2v --num-prompts 1 --max-concurrency 1

# For image to video(input have text but not use it):
python3 -m sglang.multimodal_gen.benchmarks.bench_serving \
    --backend sglang-video --dataset vbench --task i2v --num-prompts 1 --max-concurrency 1

# For image-text to video:
python3 -m sglang.multimodal_gen.benchmarks.bench_serving \
    --backend sglang-video --dataset vbench --task ti2v --num-prompts 1 --max-concurrency 1

# For text to image:
python3 -m sglang.multimodal_gen.benchmarks.bench_serving \
    --backend sglang-image --dataset vbench --task t2i --num-prompts 1 --max-concurrency 1

# For image-text to image:
python3 -m sglang.multimodal_gen.benchmarks.bench_serving \
    --backend sglang-image --dataset vbench --task ti2i --num-prompts 1 --max-concurrency 1

title: [DP]Fix sync bubble in adjust_num_token_non_padded_for_attn_tp
author: Fridge003
body: ## Motivation Currently in function `adjust_num_token_non_padded_for_attn_tp` (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py#L543) Two on-device tensors `self.num_token_non_padded` and `num_tokens_per_dp` are passed into `compute_local_num_token_non_padded` function, where the torch.clamp function (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py#L219) implicitly calls `item()` method and causes sync between gpu and cpu. This PR removes this bubble by making all these tensors of on cpu in `adjust_num_token_non_padded_for_attn_tp` The bubble can be reproduced with Spec-V2 and DEP: ``` SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path nvidia/DeepSeek-R1-0528-FP4-v2 \ --served-model-name dsr1 \ --tp 4 \ --dp 4 \ --ep 4 \ --enable-dp-attention \ --attention-backend trtllm_mla \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm \ --quantization modelopt_fp4 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \ --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 ``` ## Accuracy Tests On GSM8K ``` python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-shots 8 --num-questions 200 --parallel 200 Accuracy: 0.980 Invalid: 0.000 Latency: 25.679 s ``` ## Benchmarking and Profiling On main branch: ``` python3 -m sglang.test.send_one +-------------+--------+------------+-----------------+ | Latency (s) | Tokens | Acc Length | Speed (token/s) | +-------------+--------+------------+-----------------+ | 1.934 | 186 | 1.879 | 96.19 | +-------------+--------+------------+-----------------+ ``` On PR branch: ``` python3 -m sglang.test.send_one +-------------+--------+------------+-----------------+ | Latency (s) | Tokens | Acc Length | Speed (token/s) | +-------------+--------+------------+-----------------+ | 1.703 | 186 | 1.879 | 109.22 | +-------------+--------+------------+-----------------+ ``` ## Checklist - title: Re-enable temp_prefill_info assertion after pairing fix
author: harvenstar
body:
## Summary

  This PR re-enables the temp_prefill_info assertion that was temporarily disabled in PR #16008 to unblock CI.

  ## Background

  The assertion was disabled because log_prefill_stats and log_prefill_stats_late were not properly paired in some execution paths, leading to assertion failures:

  
  1. PR #16008 - Temporarily disabled the assertion to unblock CI 
  2. PR #15946 - Added the maybe_prepare_mlp_sync_batch_and_log_stats() helper method to ensure proper pairing in:
     - Pipeline parallelism (PP) mode (scheduler_pp_mixin.py)
     - Disaggregation prefill mode (disaggregation/prefill.py)

  ## Changes

  This PR simply re-enables the assertion by uncommenting line 140 in scheduler_metrics_mixin.py:

  ```python
  assert self.temp_prefill_info is None
```
  Why This Matters

  The assertion serves as an important safeguard:
  - Ensures log_prefill_stats and log_prefill_stats_late are always properly paired
  - Prevents metrics loss for prefill batches
  - Catches potential bugs early in the scheduling logic

  Testing

  All affected execution paths have been fixed in PR #15946:
  - Normal scheduler mode (scheduler.py) - calls log_prefill_stats_late(ret) at the end
  - PP mode (scheduler_pp_mixin.py) - uses helper method
  - Disaggregation prefill mode (disaggregation/prefill.py) - uses helper method
  - Multiplexing mode - independent, does not conflict with the above modes

  The assertion should pass in CI if all pairing issues have been resolved.

  Related PRs

  - Fixes #16008 (temporary disabling of assertion)
  - Depends on #15946 (pairing fix)

title: test(tree): add comprehensive unit tests and fix input_char_count bug
author: slin1237
body:

- Empty string and single character operations
- Prefix relationship edge cases (subset/superset)
- prefix_match_with_counts validation and UTF-8 handling
- Node splitting edge cases
- High contention stress tests
- ASCII/UTF-8 consistency
- Eviction edge cases
- Last tenant cache behavior
- Boundary conditions (10KB strings, 100 tenants, special chars)

title: Fix: Allow build-wheels to run when target_stage is set
author: alisonshao
body:
## Summary
Revert the `!inputs.target_stage` check from `sgl-kernel-build-wheels` and `sgl-kernel-build-wheels-arm` jobs.

**Problem:** PR #16308 incorrectly added `!inputs.target_stage` to the build-wheels jobs, causing them to be skipped when `/rerun-stage` is used. This broke stage jobs that depend on the built wheel artifacts.

**Error:**
```
+ ls -alh sgl-kernel/dist
ls: cannot access 'sgl-kernel/dist': No such file or directory
```

**Fix:** Build-wheel jobs must run when `sgl_kernel == 'true'` regardless of `target_stage`, because stage jobs need the wheel artifacts. Only the kernel TEST jobs (`sgl-kernel-unit-test`, `sgl-kernel-mla-test`, `sgl-kernel-benchmark-test`, `sgl-kernel-b200-test`) should have the `!inputs.target_stage` check since they don't produce artifacts needed by other jobs.

**Error example:** https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/20669833795

Followup to #16308

title: [diffusion] Fix RuntimeError in SageAttention3 on Nvidia Blackwell with Qwen-Image
author: qimcis
body:
## Motivation

On Blackwell (SM12x), `sglang generate` may auto-select SageAttention3 (`sage_attn_3`) when `sageattn3` is installed and no `--attention-backend` is provided. SageAttention3 assumes MHA (`num_heads == num_kv_heads`). For GQA/MQA models like `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2512` (28 query heads, 4 KV heads), this leads to a runtime error from a head-count mismatch.

This PR avoids SM12x/Blackwell crashes by (1) making SageAttention3 opt-in so it is not auto-selected by default, and (2) when `--attention-backend sage_attn_3` is explicitly requested, falling back to Torch SDPA (with `enable_gqa=True`) for GQA/MQA layers (`Hq != Hkv`) while continuing to use SageAttention3 for MHA layers (`Hq == Hkv`), addressing the first issue mentioned in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/16302 (SageAttention3 failure), but not the second issue mentioned (NVML “Not Supported” failure)
## Modifications

- `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/attention/backends/sage_attn3.py`: detect GQA/MQA (`Hq != Hkv`) and fall back to `torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(..., enable_gqa=True)`; keep SageAttention3 for MHA

- `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/platforms/cuda.py`: make SageAttention3 opt-in on SM12x by removing its auto-selection in the default backend path (still available when explicitly requested via `--attention-backend sage_attn_3`).

## Accuracy Tests

I verified that Qwen/Qwen-Image-2512 no longer crashes during the text encoding stage when running with `--attention-backend sage_attn_3`.

Tested on 1x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell WS

**Before the fix (main branch):**

```
sglang generate --model-path Qwen/Qwen-Image-2512 --prompt "Draw a picture of LA in the rain."
. . . 
[01-03 06:40:24] [TextEncodingStage] started...
[01-03 06:40:24] [TextEncodingStage] Error during execution after 762.1626 ms: The size of tensor a (28) must match the size of tensor b (4) at non-singleton dimension 1
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/workspace/sglang/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/executors/parallel_executor.py", line 90, in _execute
    batch = stage(batch, server_args)

title: Fix parallel tool call parsing bug when tool parameters contain arrays
author: Leoyzen
body:
## Motivation

This PR fixes a critical bug in parallel tool call parsing where the parser incorrectly identifies `[` characters inside array parameters as the start of a new tool call when processing the second and subsequent tools in a parallel tool call sequence.

**Bug Scenario:**
When a model outputs multiple parallel tool calls in JSON array format (e.g., `tool_choice='required'`), and both tools have array parameters like `"title": ["some value"]`, the parser would fail on the second tool with the error:
```
AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'
```

This happens because the parser finds the `[` character in the second tool's array parameter (e.g., `"title": ["4.8"]`) and incorrectly treats it as the `bot_token` marking the start of a new tool array, instead of correctly identifying the tool separator comma.

## Modifications

### 1. Fixed parsing logic in [`base_format_detector.py`](python/sglang/srt/function_call/base_format_detector.py:168-183)

**Root Cause:** The if-elif logic checked for `bot_token` ('[') before checking if we're processing a subsequent tool (`current_tool_id > 0`). This caused the parser to find '[' inside array parameters and mistakenly identify it as the start of a new tool.

**Fix:** Reordered the if-elif logic to prioritize checking for the tool separator when `current_tool_id > 0`. This ensures that when processing subsequent tools in parallel calls, we correctly identify the tool separator comma first, rather than being misled by '[' characters in parameter values.

**Code Change:**
```python
# Before (incorrect):
tool_call_pos = current_text.find(self.bot_token)
if tool_call_pos != -1:
    start_idx = tool_call_pos + len(self.bot_token)
elif self.current_tool_id > 0 and current_text.startswith(self.tool_call_separator):
    start_idx = len(self.tool_call_separator)

# After (correct):
if self.current_tool_id > 0 and current_text.startswith(self.tool_call_separator):
    # Priority check for subsequent tools
    start_idx = len(self.tool_call_separator)
else:
    # Only search for bot_token if not processing subsequent tool
    tool_call_pos = current_text.find(self.bot_token)
    if tool_call_pos != -1:

title: fix【hicache】fix the KV cache resource occupation  and invalid loading from prefetch when pending requests are aborted.
author: CLFutureX
body:
**Background**
Currently, when processing pending scheduled requests ， if the number of requests in the waiting queue exceeds the set threshold, the system will interrupt low-priority requests and return directly based on the priority policy. However, the preempted and aborted low-priority requests may have triggered corresponding prefetch operators. These uninterrupted prefetch operations will continue to occupy KV cache resources, resulting in invalid occupation of cache space and reduced overall resource utilization.
path:python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py#_abort_on_queued_limit

**Optimization**
Interrupt Corresponding Prefetch Requests When Pending Scheduled Requests Are Aborted to Release KV Cache Resources

title: [Diffusion] Fix `--warmup` conflicts with CacheDiT by preserving real step count for CacheDiT init
author: BBuf
body: ## Motivation ```shell CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED=true \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_WARMUP=4 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_MC=8 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_RDT=0.24 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_FN=1 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_BN=0 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_TAYLORSEER=true \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_SECONDARY_WARMUP=2 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_SECONDARY_MC=20 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_SECONDARY_RDT=0.24 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_SECONDARY_FN=1 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_SECONDARY_BN=0 \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_SECONDARY_TAYLORSEER=true \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_SCM_PRESET=fast \ SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_SCM_POLICY=dynamic \ sglang generate --model-path Wan-AI/Wan2.2-I2V-A14B-Diffusers --pin-cpu-memory --num-gpus 4 --ulysses-degree 2 --ring-degree 2 --prompt "Summer beach vacation style, a white cat wearing sunglasses sits on a surfboard. The fluffy-furred feline gazes directly at the camera with a relaxed expression. Blurred beach scenery forms the background featuring crystal-clear waters, distant green hills, and a blue sky dotted with white clouds. The cat assumes a naturally relaxed posture, as if savoring the sea breeze and warm sunlight. A close-up shot highlights the feline's intricate details and the refreshing atmosphere of the seaside." --save-output --output-path outputs --output-file-name "output1_video.mp4" --image-path="https://github.com/Wan-Video/Wan2.2/blob/990af50de458c19590c245151197326e208d7191/examples/i2v_input.JPG?raw=true" --720p --num-frames 81 --fps 16 --guidance-scale 3.5 --guidance-scale-2 4 --num-inference-steps 27 --enable-warmup ``` This PR fixes a crash when running diffusion `generate` with both CacheDiT enabled and `--enable-warmup`. The warmup request uses `num_inference_steps=1`, which previously caused CacheDiT’s SCM mask generation to fail (e.g., `total_steps=1` assertion). CacheDiT SCM presets don’t support very small `total_steps` (e.g., 1), which makes warmup crash and can cascade into scheduler/worker failures. This preserves the warmup semantics while ensuring CacheDiT is configured using the real inference step count. main: pr: ## Modifications ## Accuracy Tests ## Benchmarking and Profiling ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. title: fix: unimplemented methods in BaseIndexerMetadata

title: Fix radix cache key to include generated tokens in multi-turn (regression)
author: ycchen-tw
body:
## Motivation

In multi-turn usage, SGLang radix cache currently only reuses the original prompt tokens, but **does not reuse the previous turn’s generated tokens**. This forces unnecessary prefill over already-generated continuation tokens in the next request and significantly hurts multi-turn performance.

### Repro (minimal)

* Round 1: prompt=100 tokens, generated=50 tokens
* Round 2: input=200 tokens (100 prompt + 50 generated + 50 new tokens)

  * **Expected cache hit**: 150 (prompt + generated)
  * **Actual cache hit**: 100 (only prompt)

Example log (before fix):

```
Round 1: Prompt=100, Output=50, Cached=0
Round 2: Input=200, Cached=100  (only prompt) ❌
```

After fix:

```
Round 1: Prompt=100, Output=50, Cached=0
Round 2: Input=200, Cached=150  (prompt + generated) ✅
```

## Modifications

### Root cause

In `sglang/srt/mem_cache/radix_cache.py::cache_finished_req()`:

* `token_ids` is correctly computed as `(req.origin_input_ids + req.output_ids)[:kv_committed_len]`
* However, the code uses `req.fill_ids` as the cache insertion key:

  * `fill_ids` is set at `init_next_round_input()` time (before decode), so it **does not include** `output_ids`
  * As a result, radix cache only stores/matches the prompt prefix, not the generated continuation

### Fix

Use `token_ids` (prompt + output, up to committed KV length) as the insertion key:

```python
keys = convert_to_bigram_key(token_ids) if self.is_eagle else token_ids
```

This keeps the EAGLE bigram-key behavior intact while fixing the non-EAGLE path regression.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A. This change only affects radix cache key selection for KV reuse and does not modify model forward / sampling behavior, so model outputs are unchanged.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

I did not run full end-to-end throughput benchmarks in this PR. However, the repro script shows `cached_tokens` increases from `prompt_only` to `prompt + previous_generation`, which directly reduces the amount of prefill work in multi-turn scenarios.

If needed, I can provide:

* multi-turn latency comparison (prefill time / end-to-end latency)
* throughput (req/s) under a chat workload

## Checklist

* [ ] Format code with pre-commit
* [ ] Add unit tests (regression coverage for multi-turn generated-token caching)
* [ ] Update documentation (not needed)
* [ ] Provide accuracy tests (N/A)
* [ ] Provide benchmarking (optional; can be added if requested)
* [ ] Follow SGLang code style guidance

title: [AMD] Fix aiter page-size handling, DeepSeek MLA tuple inputs, and HiCache/FA3 decode-backend override
author: hubertlu-tw
body:
## Motivation

I hit a few issues while running DeepSeek-R1 MXFP4 on ROCm with aiter + hierarchical cache:

- aiter MLA metadata creation was effectively hard-coding `page_size=1`, and the draft backend also asserted `page_size==1`, which breaks configs like `--page-size 64`.
- `DeepseekV2AttentionMLA` can receive `hidden_states` as a tuple in some quantization paths, which makes shape-based allocations fail.
- When HiCache kernel I/O is enabled, the FlashAttention3 compatibility workaround should only kick in when the *effective* decode backend is FA3; otherwise we should not override the user’s chosen backend (e.g., `aiter` on ROCm).

## Modifications

- **aiter attention backend**
  - Use the backend’s configured `page_size` when building MLA metadata (instead of hard-coding `1`).
  - Remove the strict `page_size == 1` assertion in the multistep draft backend to allow non-1 page sizes.
- **DeepSeek v2 MLA forward**
  - Handle `hidden_states` being a tuple by using the first tensor for `shape/device/dtype` when allocating `q_input`, while still passing the original `hidden_states` through the linear ops.
- **Server args / backend selection**
  - Only apply the HiCache-kernel/FA3 workaround when the *effective* decode backend would be `fa3` (respect user-selected `--attention-backend aiter` otherwise).
  - If the user explicitly requests FA3 decode under hierarchical cache, fall back to direct I/O and warn.

## Accuracy Tests

### Setup / Launch command

```bash
SGLANG_AITER_MLA_PERSIST=1 \

  --model-path /data/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4-Preview \

## Motivation

Wan2.2 inference uses sequence-parallel attention (Ulysses/Ring) and can be combined with tensor parallelism (TP).  
Before this PR, Ulysses/Ring process groups were created assuming that sequence-parallel (SP) ranks are **consecutive global ranks**.
This assumption happens to be safe when **TP = 1**, because SP groups are contiguous in global rank space, so building Ulysses/Ring groups with a contiguous-rank layout does not mix unrelated ranks.
However, when **TP > 1** (with the current `tp-sp-...` rank ordering), SP groups become **strided** in global ranks (e.g. ranks like `[0, 2, 4, 6]` instead of `[0, 1, 2, 3]`). In that case, constructing Ulysses/Ring groups using contiguous global ranks causes **cross-group communication** (mixing ranks from different SP/TP partitions), leading to incorrect outputs.

## PR Changes

- Build Ulysses/Ring process groups using the **actual SP rank groups** (from rank_generator.get_ranks("sp")) instead of assuming contiguous global ranks.
- Ensure Ulysses/Ring communication is always scoped within the correct SP group, even when TP is enabled.

## Why Ulysses=2 / Ring=2 did not fail before
With **TP = 1**, `ulysses_degree=2` and `ring_degree=2` still produce SP groups that are contiguous in global ranks, so the previous contiguous-rank-based group construction matched the real SP layout and did not introduce cross-group communication.

The bug only appears after scaling out with **TP > 1**, where the SP layout becomes strided and the contiguous assumption no longer holds.

title: Fix v32 continue_final_message not work
author: whybeyoung
body:
Fix https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/16501

 According to the official disscuss https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2/discussions/4, and  in the pr: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/14249 we implement an new encoding for ds3.2
 
However, this new modification ignores the original handling of the continue_final_message continuation mode in SGLang.
The core logic changes of this PR are as follows:

Abstracted a unified processing method for the latest message in the user-input messages.

The specific processing logic is:

1. For the new encoding mode of DS3.2, added a judgment for the continue_final_message mode.

2. If the role of the user's latest input message is assistant but the continue_final_message mode is not enabled, the last assistant message will be forcibly converted to a user message with the content unchanged.

3. If the role of the user's latest input message is assistant and the continue_final_message mode is enabled, the continuation mode will be triggered.

## Motivation

The goal is to improve runtime stability and prevent null pointer/attribute errors during multi-stream execution on NPU backends.

title: fix: 8-gpu-b200 increase timeout length
author: dougyster
body:
## Motivation

**TLDR: Timeout is too tight for Dpsk v32, so relaxing the total suite timeout limit to 300 should give plenty of room for variance.**

The B200 nightly 8-GPU tests sometimes times out due to insufficient time budget. Analysis of CI logs shows the timeout is a structural problem, not a flaky test.

**Failed run:** https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/20766554118/job/59647300496
**Successful run:** https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/20733676806/job/59627365421

### Test Duration Analysis

**Failed B200 Run (timed out but was running without error):**

| Test | Duration |
|------|----------|
| test_deepseek_v31.py | 22 min |
| test_qwen3_235b.py | 15 min |
| test_minimax_m2.py | 10 min |
| test_mistral_large3.py | 22 min |
| test_kimi_k2.py | 23 min |
| test_glm_46.py | 20 min |
| test_glm_46_fp8.py | 24 min |
| **Subtotal** | **~136 min** |
| test_deepseek_v32.py | started, then **timed out** |

**B200 Run (no timeout):**

| Test | Duration |
|------|----------|
| test_deepseek_v31.py | 23 min |
| test_deepseek_v32.py | **62 min** |
| test_glm_46.py | 11 min |
| test_glm_46_fp8.py | 13 min |
| test_kimi_k2.py | 17 min |
| test_minimax_m2.py | 6 min |
| test_mistral_large3.py | 15 min |
| test_qwen3_235b.py | 8 min |
| **Total** | **~155 min** |

Dpsk v32 usually takes 60 minutes (+/- some variation). With a 200 minute timeout, if the other tests take more than 120 minutes, this puts too much pressure for Dpsk v32 to complete within an hour. 

## Modifications

Increase B200 8-GPU common tests timeout from 200 → 300 minutes.

title: fix(function_call): group batch decode by options instead of fallback
author: ruokee
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Follow up #15155 #16122. Fix #14695 #15042.

DeepSeek v3.2 function calls require `skip_special_tokens=False`. Function call control markers (e.g. `"| DSML |"`) are encoded as special tokens and must not be stripped during decoding.

> At the very beginning, the bug arose because the detokenizer manager defaulted to using the `skip_special_tokens` value from the first request when calling `batch_decode`.
>
> But why does SGLang sometimes work as expected? This behavior is actually limited to the first request in the batch, which is random. For tool calls, the request's `skip_special_tokens` is explicitly set to `False` (it is `True` by default).
>
> Thanks to community feedback and PR #15155, the above abnormal behavior seems to be mitigated.
>
> However, the incorrect judgment still introduces bugs. `batch_decode` can only be safely used when the `skip_special_tokens` values of all requests in a batch are uniform.

This PR implements grouped batch decoding: requests are grouped by flags, `batch_decode` is applied to each group separately, and results are reassembled in original order. This preserves batch decoding efficiency while correctly handling heterogeneous decode options.

## Modifications

- Added `_grouped_batch_decode` helper method to `DetokenizerManager` that groups requests by `(skip_special_tokens, spaces_between_special_tokens)` and applies `batch_decode` to each group
- Modified `_decode_batch_token_id_output` to use the new grouped batch decode instead of assuming uniform options across all requests

title: [Diffusion] model: fix zimage tp
author: CPFLAME
body:
# Tensor Parallelism Support for Z-Image Model

In Z-Image, there is a bug when TP > 1: qkv uses ReplicatedLinear but o uses row linear, which causes a size mismatch error when tensor parallelism is enabled.

## Test Environment
- **Hardware**: NVIDIA H100 GPU
- **Model**: Z-Image-Turbo
- **Image Resolution**: 2048×2048 pixels

## Performance Results Summary

| Configuration | GPUs | TP Type | Execution Time | Speedup vs TP1 | Scaling Efficiency |
|--------------|------|---------|----------------|----------------|-------------------|
| **TP1** | 1 | None | 5.38 seconds | 1.00× | 100% |
| **TP2** | 2 | Col+Row | 3.74 seconds | **1.44×** | **72%** |
| **TP2** | 2 | Col+Col | 4.93 seconds | 1.09× | 54.5% |

## Server && Request

### server
```bash
#!/bin/bash
export LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1
# Script to serve Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo using SGLang multimodal_gen with optimizations

# Set default values
MODEL_PATH="Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo"
PORT=30000

done

# export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED=true
# export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_WARMUP=4
# export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_MC=8
# export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_RDT=0.24

### Request
```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Test script for Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo model served by SGLang multimodal_gen.
This script demonstrates how to generate images using the Z-Image-Turbo model via OpenAI-compatible API.
"""

import argparse
import json
import requests
from typing import Optional


def test_image_generation(
    host: str = "127.0.0.1",
    port: int = 30000,
    prompt: str = "A beautiful sunset over mountains",
    negative_prompt: Optional[str] = None,
    width: int = 1024,
    height: int = 768,
    num_inference_steps: int = 8,
    guidance_scale: float = 3.5,
    seed: Optional[int] = None,
    save_output: bool = True,
    output_path: str = "./outputs"
):
    """
    Test image generation with Z-Image-Turbo model using OpenAI-compatible API.
    """
    url = f"http://{host}:{port}/v1/images/generations"

    # Prepare the request data (OpenAI-compatible format)
    data = {
        "prompt": prompt,
        "model": "Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo",
        "size": f"{width}x{height}",
        "num_inference_steps": num_inference_steps,
        "guidance_scale": guidance_scale,
        "response_format": "b64_json",  # Only b64_json is supported for generations endpoint
        "n": 1
    }

    if negative_prompt:
        data["negative_prompt"] = negative_prompt
    if seed is not None:
        data["seed"] = seed

    print(f"Sending request to {url}")
    print(f"Prompt: {prompt}")
    print(f"Image size: {width}x{height}")
    print(f"Inference steps: {num_inference_steps}")
    print(f"Guidance scale: {guidance_scale}")
    if negative_prompt:
        print(f"Negative prompt: {negative_prompt}")
    if seed is not None:
        print(f"Seed: {seed}")

    try:
        response = requests.post(url, json=data, timeout=300)  # 5 minute timeout
        response.raise_for_status()

        result = response.json()
        print("\nResponse received:")
        # import pdb; pdb.set_trace()
        # print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))

        # Check if generation was successful
        if "data" in result and len(result["data"]) > 0:
            image_data = result["data"][0].get("b64_json")
            if image_data:
                # Decode and save the base64 image
                import base64
                image_bytes = base64.b64decode(image_data)
                output_file = f"generated_image_{seed if seed is not None else 'random'}.png"
                with open(output_file, "wb") as f:
                    f.write(image_bytes)
                print(f"\nImage saved as: {output_file}")
                print(f"Image size: {len(image_bytes)} bytes")
            else:
                print("Warning: No image data received in response")
                print(f"Response data keys: {list(result['data'][0].keys())}")

        return True

    except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
        print(f"Error making request: {e}")
        if hasattr(e, 'response') and e.response:
            print(f"Response status: {e.response.status_code}")
            print(f"Response content: {e.response.text}")
        return False
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        print(f"Error parsing response: {e}")
        print(f"Raw response: {response.text}")
        return False


def test_generation_via_sglang_cli(
    prompt: str = "A beautiful sunset over mountains",
    negative_prompt: Optional[str] = None,
    width: int = 1024,
    height: int = 1024,
    num_inference_steps: int = 8,
    guidance_scale: float = 3.5,
    seed: Optional[int] = None
):
    """
    Alternative: Test using sglang generate command directly.
    """
    import subprocess
    import sys

    cmd = [
        sys.executable, "-m", "sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.entrypoints.cli.main",
        "generate",
        "--model-path", "Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo",
        "--prompt", prompt,
        "--width", str(width),
        "--height", str(height),
        "--num-inference-steps", str(num_inference_steps),
        "--guidance-scale", str(guidance_scale),
        "--save-output",
        "--output-path", "./outputs"
    ]

    if negative_prompt:
        cmd.extend(["--negative-prompt", negative_prompt])
    if seed is not None:
        cmd.extend(["--seed", str(seed)])

    print(f"Running command: {' '.join(cmd)}")

    try:
        result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600)
        print("STDOUT:")
        print(result.stdout)
        if result.stderr:
            print("STDERR:")
            print(result.stderr)
        return result.returncode == 0
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        print("Command timed out")
        return False
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error running command: {e}")
        return False


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Test Z-Image-Turbo model")
    parser.add_argument("--host", type=str, default="127.0.0.1", help="Server host")
    parser.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=30000, help="Server port")
    parser.add_argument("--prompt", type=str, default="A beautiful sunset over mountains", help="Image generation prompt")
    parser.add_argument("--negative-prompt", type=str, help="Negative prompt")
    parser.add_argument("--width", type=int, default=1024, help="Image width")
    parser.add_argument("--height", type=int, default=768, help="Image height")
    parser.add_argument("--steps", type=int, default=8, help="Number of inference steps")
    parser.add_argument("--guidance-scale", type=float, default=3.5, help="Guidance scale")
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, help="Random seed")
    parser.add_argument("--use-cli", action="store_true", help="Use sglang CLI instead of server API")
    parser.add_argument("--output-path", type=str, default="./outputs", help="Output path for generated images")

    args = parser.parse_args()

    if args.use_cli:
        success = test_generation_via_sglang_cli(
            prompt=args.prompt,
            negative_prompt=args.negative_prompt,
            width=args.width,
            height=args.height,
            num_inference_steps=args.steps,
            guidance_scale=args.guidance_scale,
            seed=args.seed
        )
    else:
        success = test_image_generation(
            host=args.host,
            port=args.port,
            prompt=args.prompt,
            negative_prompt=args.negative_prompt,
            width=args.width,
            height=args.height,
            num_inference_steps=args.steps,
            guidance_scale=args.guidance_scale,
            seed=args.seed,
            output_path=args.output_path
        )

    if success:
        print("\nTest completed successfully!")
        return 0
    else:
        print("\nTest failed!")
        return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys
    sys.exit(main())
```

title: diffusion: Fix LoRA weight merging when using layerwise offload
author: niehen6174
body: ## Motivation When using layerwise offload strategy, offloaded layers only keep placeholder weights on GPU while the actual weights are stored on CPU. This prevents LoRA from reading the real weights and merging them correctly, causing LoRA operations to fail. ## Modifications **`layerwise_offload.py`:** - Add `load_all_layers()` to load all layers from CPU to GPU - Add `sync_layer_to_cpu()` and `sync_all_layers_to_cpu()` to sync modified weights back to CPU - Add `remove_forward_hooks()` to remove forward hooks - Add `disable_offload()` / `enable_offload()` in `OffloadableDiTMixin` for bulk offload control **`lora_pipeline.py`:** - Add `_temporarily_disable_offload()` context manager to unify offload handling - Handle offload in `convert_to_lora_layers()`, `set_lora()`, `merge_lora_weights()`, and `unmerge_lora_weights()` ## Accuracy Tests WAN models enable layerwise offload by default. When using layerwise offload, offloaded layers only keep placeholder weights on GPU while the actual weights are stored on CPU. This prevents LoRA from reading the real weights and merging them correctly. Before this fix, set_lora() and LoRA API calls failed. After the fix, LoRA operations work correctly. I do some test in `z-image` with set `dit_layerwise_offload`. ```python from sglang.multimodal_gen import DiffGenerator generator = DiffGenerator.from_pretrained( model_path="Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo", dit_layerwise_offload=True, ) prompt = "elusarca anime style. 1girl, solo, white hair, double bun, blue eyes, blue shirt, sitting, leaning on hand, coffee mug, desk, office, tired." input_data = {"prompt":prompt, "seed":1024, "save_output":True, "width":720, "height":1280} output = generator.generate(input_data) generator.set_lora("qwenimage", "reverentelusarca/elusarca-anime-style-lora-z-image-turbo") output = generator.generate(input_data) generator.unmerge_lora_weights() output = generator.generate(input_data) generator.merge_lora_weights() ``` From left to right are the four test results. Based on the results, it appears that `set_lora`, `unmerge_lora_weights`, and `merge_lora_weights` all work correctly when using `dit_layerwise_offload`. ## Benchmarking and Profiling ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. title: fix(gateway): rewrite gauge_histogram.rs for zero-allocation hot path
author: slin1237
body:
PROBLEMS WITH ORIGINAL IMPLEMENTATION:

1. Memory leak via Box::leak
   - Original used `Box::leak(s.into_boxed_str())` to create static strings
   - This leaked memory for every label combination

2. Hot path allocated on every call
   - `gauge!` macro creates Key + Vec<Label> on every invocation
   - No way to reuse registered gauge handles

3. No dynamic label support
   - Original had no way to pass custom labels (worker, model, etc.)
   - Made it unusable for the intended routing-key tracking use case

4. Missing functionality
   - No cache for dynamic label values
   - No cleanup mechanism for auto-scaling scenarios

SOLUTION:

Redesigned with pre-registration pattern:

1. BucketBounds<const N: usize>
   - Compile-time validated bucket boundaries
   - compute_counts_into() for zero-alloc counting into pre-allocated buffer

2. GaugeHistogramHandle
   - Stores pre-registered metrics::Gauge handles
   - set_counts() is TRUE zero-allocation: just N+1 atomic gauge.set() calls

3. GaugeHistogramVec<const N: usize>
   - Factory that creates handles via register()
   - Registration allocates once, handle reused forever

4. CachedGaugeHistogram<const N: usize>
   - DashMap cache for dynamic labels discovered at runtime
   - First call registers (allocates), subsequent calls zero-alloc
   - remove() and retain_only() for auto-scaling cleanup

PERFORMANCE:

| Operation              | Original          | New                    |
|------------------------|-------------------|------------------------|
| Hot path allocation    | Vec + Key + Label | Zero                   |
| Hot path key lookup    | HashMap lookup    | None (pre-registered)  |
| Atomic ops per emit    | Unknown           | N+1 gauge.set() only   |

KNOWN LIMITATIONS:

- remove() allocates a temporary Vec for zeroing (minor)
- Single dynamic label key per CachedGaugeHistogram
- Metrics registry cannot unregister gauges (metrics crate limitation)
- Only u64 observations (Python supports float)

USAGE:

```rust
static BOUNDS: BucketBounds<10> = BucketBounds::new([1,2,3,5,7,10,20,50,100,200]);
static HISTOGRAM: GaugeHistogramVec<10> = GaugeHistogramVec::new("metric", &BOUNDS);

// For dynamic labels (auto-scaling workers):
let cached = CachedGaugeHistogram::new(&HISTOGRAM, "worker");
cached.observe("worker-1", &observations);  // zero-alloc after first call

// Cleanup when workers removed:
cached.retain_only(&active_workers);
```

title: [FixBug] [Diffusion] Fix Qwen-Image-Edit Lightning LoRA alpha/rank scaling (read per-layer *.alpha)
author: qichu-yun
body: ## Motivation Some LoRA checkpoints (e.g., Lightning distill) encode per-layer scaling via an additional ".alpha" entry. Without reading this value, the runtime may apply an incorrect default scaling (effectively assuming α=r), leading to mismatched LoRA strength and degraded/incorrect outputs compared to the original training/inference setup. This PR improves compatibility with such checkpoints by detecting and using the per-layer alpha when available, following the standard LoRA scaling rule scale=α/r. ## Modifications `lora_pipeline.py:` - Infer per-layer rank (r) from the loaded lora_A tensor shape (shape[0]) when applying LoRA weights. - Detect optional per-layer alpha from ".alpha" in the adapter state dict; if present, parse it as an integer. - Populate layer metadata by setting layer.lora_rank and layer.lora_alpha prior to layer.set_lora_weights(). - Safe fallback behavior: if alpha is missing/unreadable, default lora_alpha to rank (maintaining existing behavior); if rank inference fails, do not override these fields. ## Accuracy Tests Here is my test scripts: ```bash export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED=true export SGLANG_DIFFUSION_ATTENTION_BACKEND=AITER LORA_PATH=lightx2v/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511-Lightning/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511-Lightning-4steps-V1.0-bf16.safetensors SERVER_ARGS=( --model-path /data/models/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 --lora-path "${LORA_PATH}" --num-gpus 2 --tp-size 1 --ulysses-degree 2 ) SAMPLING_ARGS=( --prompt "make the clothes to red" --image-path ./768x1024.png --output-path qwen_image_edit/ --save-output --height 1024 --width 768 --num-inference-steps 4 --guidance-scale 1 --output-file-name "red_clothes_edit_upstream.png" ) sglang generate "${SERVER_ARGS[@]}" "${SAMPLING_ARGS[@]}" ``` the input image is: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelscope/DiffSynth-Engine/dev/qz/qwen_app_amd/examples/input/768x1024.png **before fix:** **after fixed using this PR:** ## Benchmarking and Profiling ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

author: YAMY1234
body: ## Motivation 1. Enable CUDA graph draft extend support for `trtllm_mla_backend` 2. Fix accept length degradation (~35% drop) when draft extend CUDA graph is enabled with DP Attention ## Modifications 1. Add `TRTLLMMLAMultiStepDraftBackend` support in `eagle_worker_v2.py` to enable CUDA graph capture for draft extend 2. Fix `num_tokens_for_logprob_per_batch` / `global_num_tokens_for_logprob_gpu` to match `num_tokens_per_batch` in CUDA graph runners: - `eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py`: capture and replay stages - `multi_layer_eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py`: replay stage - `multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py`: draft extend initialization **Root Cause**: `num_tokens_for_logprob_per_batch=1` caused `LogitsMetadata.compute_dp_attention_metadata` to calculate incorrect `dp_local_num_tokens`, resulting in MLP sync only processing partial tokens. ## Accuracy Tests **Before (accept_len ~1.5)**: ``` [DP0 TP0] Decode batch, accept len: 1.52, accept rate: 0.51, cuda graph: True [DP1 TP1] Decode batch, accept len: 1.42, accept rate: 0.47, cuda graph: True ``` **After (accept_len ~2.3)**: ``` [DP0 TP0] Decode batch, accept len: 2.20, accept rate: 0.73, cuda graph: True [DP1 TP1] Decode batch, accept len: 2.34, accept rate: 0.78, cuda graph: True [DP2 TP2] Decode batch, accept len: 2.54, accept rate: 0.85, cuda graph: True [DP3 TP3] Decode batch, accept len: 2.41, accept rate: 0.80, cuda graph: True ``` **Config**: TP4 + DP4 + EP4, `speculative-num-steps=2`, `speculative-eagle-topk=1`, `trtllm_mla` backend ``` export SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2="1" python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /home/hostuser/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--nvidia--DeepSeek-R1-0528-NVFP4-v2/snapshots/25a138f28f49022958b9f2d205f9b7de0cdb6e18 --served-model-name dsr1 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --data-parallel-size 4 --expert-parallel-size 4 --enable-dp-attention --moe-dense-tp-size 1 --attention-backend trtllm_mla --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm --quantization modelopt_fp4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --disable-radix-cache --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 2 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 3 --port 30000 --host 127.0.0.1 --watchdog-timeout 1800 --dist-timeout 3600 ``` ``` python -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name longbench_v2 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 --model nvidia/DeepSeek-R1-0528-NVFP4-v2 --max-context-length 128000 --max-tokens 16384 --num-threads 16 ``` **LongBench V2**: Score = 0.576 ## title: [logprob] Fix logprob + streaming for long concurrent decode by caching already processed logprob
author: ByronHsu
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

When we use logprob + streaming, tokenizer manager could hang because for every chunk, it re-process (`detokenize_logprob_tokens`) every token from the beginning. Say if we have 1000 tokens, it process 1, 2, 3, ..., 1000 tokens in each chunk. For each token (in the topk case), it creates a new python list which triggers GC and slows down and potentially hang the tokenizer.

Before the fix. The following could hang:

```python
# send.py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Batch script to send multiple generation requests to the SGLang server.
"""

import argparse
import random
import string
import sys
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
from threading import Lock
from typing import Any, Dict, Optional

import requests


def send_request(
    url: str,
    text: str,
    sampling_params: Dict[str, Any],
    request_id: Optional[int] = None,
) -> None:
    """
    Send a single generation request to the server and consume the streaming response.

    Args:
        url: The endpoint URL
        text: The input text prompt
        sampling_params: Sampling parameters dictionary
        request_id: Optional request ID for tracking
    """
    payload = {
        "text": text,
        "sampling_params": sampling_params,
        "return_logprob": True,
        "logprob_start_len": -1,
        "top_logprobs_num": 4,
        "token_ids_logprob": None,
        "return_text_in_logprobs": False,
        "stream": True,
    }

    headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}

    try:
        response = requests.post(
            url, json=payload, headers=headers, timeout=None, stream=True
        )
        response.raise_for_status()

        # Consume the streaming response
        for line in response.iter_lines():
            if line:
                # Decode the line if it's bytes
                if isinstance(line, bytes):
                    line = line.decode("utf-8")

                # print(line)
                # input()
                # Stream is consumed but not printed to avoid cluttering output
                # The stream will finish when the server closes the connection
    except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
        print(f"Error sending request {request_id}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        if e.response is not None:
            try:
                print(f"Response: {e.response.text}", file=sys.stderr)
            except Exception:
                pass
        raise


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Send batch generation requests to SGLang server"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "-n", type=int, required=True, help="Number of requests to send"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--input-len",
        type=int,
        default=1000,
        help="Input text length in characters (random text will be generated)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--output-len",
        type=int,
        default=100000,
        help="Number of new tokens (sets both min_new_tokens and max_new_tokens)",
    )

    args = parser.parse_args()

    url = "http://127.0.0.1:30000/generate"
    # Generate random text of specified length
    text = "".join(
        random.choices(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " ", k=args.input_len)
    )
    sampling_params = {
        "temperature": 0,
        "min_new_tokens": args.output_len,
        "max_new_tokens": args.output_len,
    }

    print(f"Sending {args.n} concurrent requests...")

    success_count = 0
    error_count = 0
    lock = Lock()

    def send_with_tracking(request_id: int):
        nonlocal success_count, error_count
        try:
            send_request(
                url=url,
                text=text,
                sampling_params=sampling_params,
                request_id=request_id,
            )
            with lock:
                success_count += 1
                print(f"Request {request_id}/{args.n} completed")
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            with lock:
                error_count += 1
                print(f"Request {request_id} failed: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return False

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=args.n) as executor:
        futures = {
            executor.submit(send_with_tracking, i + 1): i + 1 for i in range(args.n)
        }

        # Wait for all requests to complete
        for future in as_completed(futures):
            future.result()

    print(f"\nSummary: {success_count} succeeded, {error_count} failed")

    sys.exit(0 if error_count == 0 else 1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Server launch:
```
$ python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-8B 
```

Client 1:
```
$ python send.py -n 10 --input-len 4096 --output-len 10000  
```

Client 2:
```
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30000/generate -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "text": "Hello world",
  "sampling_params": {
    "temperature": 0
  }
}'
```
Client 2 will hang and never get a response.

title: [CI] Fix max_parallel for scheduled runs
author: alisonshao
body:
## Summary

Fix `stage-b-test-large-1-gpu` running slowly on scheduled CI due to incorrect max_parallel setting.

**Problem**: Scheduled runs were using `max_parallel=3` (the default for regular PRs), causing the 14-partition `stage-b-test-large-1-gpu` job to run in batches of 3 instead of all at once.

**Fix**: Set `max_parallel=14` for scheduled runs to enable full parallelism.

| Run Type | Before | After |
|----------|--------|-------|
| Scheduled runs | 3 | **14** |
| High priority PRs | 15 | **14** |
| Regular PRs | 3 | 3 |

Note: Changed high priority from 15 to 14 to match the actual partition count.

title: [Bug Fix] Fix reasoning parser when continue_final_message=true
author: laixinn
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
Sending a request with `continue_final_message=true` and `enable_thinking=true` populates `reasoning_content` with the continued message.

**Reproduction**
Request:
```bash
#!/bin/bash

curl -X POST http:///127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer EMPTY" \
  -d @- << 'EOF'
{
  "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B",
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "system",
      "content": "You are great mathematicians."
    },
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "
1.1+1.3=?
"
    },
    {
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": "<think>
Okay, let's see. The problem is 1.1 plus 1.3. Hmm, I need to add these two decimal numbers. Let me think about how to do this step by step.

First, I remember that when adding decimals, it's important to align the decimal points. So, I should write them vertically to make sure the tenths place is lined up. Let me try that.

So, writing it out:

  1.1
+ 1.3
------
?

Now, adding the tenths place first. The tenths digit in 1.1 is 1, and in 1.3 it's 3. So 1 + 3 equals 4. Then, the units place: both numbers have 1 in the units place. So 1 + 1 is 2. Putting it all together, that would be 2.4. Wait, is that right?

Let me check again. 1.1 is the same as 1 and 1/10, and 1.3 is 1 and 3/10. Adding the whole numbers: 1 + 1 = 2. Adding the fractions: 1/10 + 3/10 = 4/10. So combined, that's 2 and 4/10, which is 2.4. Yeah, that makes sense.

Alternatively, I can think of it in terms of money. If I have $1.10 and add $1.30, that would be $2.40. So that's another way to confirm it's 2.4.

Wait, but maybe I should convert them to fractions to be thorough. 1.1 is 11/10 and 1.3 is 13/10. Adding those together: 11/10 + 13/10 = 24/10, which simplifies to 2.4. Yep, same result.

I don't think I made any mistakes here. All the methods point to 2.4. So the answer should be 2.4.
</think>

To solve the addition problem $1.1 + 1.3$, we can approach it step by step:

---

### Step 1: Align the Decimal Points

Write the numbers vertically, aligning the decimal points:

```
  1.1
+ 1.3
------
```

---

### Step 2: Add the Tenths Place

- The tenths digit in 1.1 is **1**.
- The tenths digit in 1.3 is **3**.
- Adding these: $1 + 3 = 4$.

---

### Step 3: Add the Units Place

```

failed_reqs_all = all_gather(failed_reqs_i)

title: [BUGFIX] fix radix cache memory consumption to avoid OOM
author: yizhang2077
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
When radix tree does splitting, new_node and child both hold the view for inserted value, so when child is evicted, `child.value` will not return to torch memory pool until all nodes along path hold the view of value are evicted. It may cause dynamic CUDA OOM when tree shares long prefix
This bug may also happen in other radix cache types.

use clone to release original value when do slice, it may cause overhead but I think it is small and can be hidden by overlap schedule

see ut, before this pr,  `torch_allocated_memory / tree total_size` is more than 400, which is abnormal. After this pr, it is less than 10 (it should be value dtype theoratically)

```

When deploying SGLang with HiCache using Mooncake as the storage backend in a distributed environment (e.g., Kubernetes), we encountered intermittent startup failures during the `MooncakeStore.warmup()` phase.

The error manifests as an assertion failure:

```
AssertionError: assert self.store.put(warmup_key, warmup_value) == 0
```

This occurs because the Mooncake Transfer Engine may not be fully initialized when `warmup()` is called. In a multi-pod deployment, there is a race condition where:

1. Multiple SGLang pods start simultaneously
2. Each pod initializes its `MooncakeStore` and calls `warmup()` immediately after `setup()` returns
3. However, the internal RPC server (used for RDMA bootstrap handshake) is started asynchronously via `coro_rpc_server::async_start()`, which returns immediately without waiting for the server to be fully ready to accept connections
4. When `put()` attempts to perform RDMA data transfer, it needs to exchange Queue Pair (QP) information with peer nodes via RPC. If the target node's RPC server has not finished its asynchronous startup, the connection is refused or times out, causing `put()` to fail

This race condition is particularly likely to occur when:
- **Simultaneous startup**: Multiple pods start at nearly the same time, causing all RPC servers to undergo asynchronous initialization concurrently
- **Resource contention**: High CPU/memory load during startup delays the RPC server's internal thread pool from becoming ready
- **First RDMA connection**: The very first `put()` requires establishing new RDMA connections, which involves RPC-based QP exchange that may fail if peers are not ready

## Modifications

Add a retry mechanism to the `warmup()` method in `MooncakeStore`:

- **Max retries**: 10 attempts (configurable via code)
- **Retry delay**: 2 seconds between attempts
- **Logging**: Warning logs on each failed attempt with the return code for debugging
- **Error handling**: Raise a clear `RuntimeError` after all retries are exhausted, indicating the Transfer Engine might not be ready

### Testing
Tested in a Kubernetes environment with multiple SGLang pods using Mooncake storage backend. The retry mechanism successfully handles the startup race condition, and pods that previously failed intermittently now start reliably.
