title: [PD] MORI-IO: Add state transfer, inline transfer model, and high-concurrency fixes
author: maning00
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #14626 which introduced MORI-IO as the RDMA-based KV transfer backend for PD disaggregation on AMD hardware. This PR addresses the known limitation (no state transfer) and resolves several performance bottlenecks and correctness issues discovered under high-concurrency workloads:

1. State data transfer was not implemented for hybrid models (Mamba, SWA, NSA).
2. TP slice head mapping was incorrect for `prefill_tp_size > decode_tp_size` with GQA/MQA.
3. ZMQ-based auxiliary data transfer caused message flooding and transfer queue hangs under high concurrency (AUX RDMA path added as opt-in alternative).
4. The `_connect()` function does not reuse connections, resulting in all available ports being occupied.

## Modifications

All changes are confined to `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/mori/conn.py`.

### 1. State Transfer Support (Mamba, SWA, NSA)

- Added `send_state()` method on `MoriKVManager` that dispatches to `_send_mamba_state()` or `_send_swa_nsa_state()` based on `state_type`.
- `_send_mamba_state()`: Single-index Mamba SSM state transfer with TP-mismatch slice support (computes per-dimension offsets when prefill TP != decode TP).
- `_send_swa_nsa_state()`: Multi-token SWA/NSA state transfer using `group_concurrent_contiguous()` and batched RDMA writes.
- Extended `TransferInfo` with `dst_state_indices` and `KVArgsRegisterInfo` with `dst_state_item_lens` / `dst_state_dim_per_tensor`.

### 2. Inline Transfer Model with Caller-Driven Polling

Refined the inline transfer architecture (no worker threads):

- **`add_transfer_request()`**: Inline execution with reduced lock scope — RDMA posting happens outside `transfer_lock`, allowing bootstrap thread to register new requests concurrently.
- **`MoriKVSender.poll()`**: Caller-driven RDMA completion checking via `_all_transfers_finished()`, with decode notification fired immediately on completion.
- **Transfer plan precomputation**: `GroupedIndexPlan` / `BatchTransferPlan` dataclasses compute offsets once and reuse across all layers, eliminating redundant per-layer list comprehensions.
- **Error resilience**: Transfer submission failures are caught and recorded without crashing the scheduler; `_maybe_finalize_if_room_failed()` bridges manager-side errors to sender lifecycle.

### 3. AUX Data Transfer

- Default path remains ZMQ TCP (`send_aux_tcp()`), which is stable under all concurrency levels.
- Added `send_aux_rdma()` as opt-in alternative via `SGLANG_MORI_SEND_AUX_RDMA=1` env var, with automatic fallback to TCP when remote AUX descriptors are unavailable.
- Added `_connect_threadsafe()` with thread-local ZMQ sockets for thread-safe TCP communication.

### 4. Bug Fixes

- **TP slice fix**: Corrected head mapping for `prefill_tp_size > decode_tp_size` with GQA/MQA. Introduced `src_replication` and `unique_head_idx` for correct replicated head mapping.
- **Stale metadata guard**: `_handle_transfer_message()` now acquires `transfer_lock` and rejects metadata when room status is past Bootstrapping, preventing race conditions.
- **`update_status()` state machine guard**: `Failed` is terminal and never overwritten by non-Failed states.
- **CP rank support**: `_compute_prefill_unique_rank()` now correctly encodes TP/PP/CP ranks for decode notification.
- **TCP connection reuse**: The new `_connect thread-safe()` function can reuse TCP connections, resolving the issue of the original `_connect()` potentially causing too many connections in high-concurrency scenarios.

### 5. Default Parallelism Tuning

| Parameter | Before | After |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| `SGLANG_MORI_QP_PER_TRANSFER` | 1 | 4 |
| `SGLANG_MORI_NUM_WORKERS` | 1 | 4 |

## Benchmarking

### Hardware Configuration
- **GPUs**: 8x AMD Instinct MI355X per node
- **Network**: 8x AMD Pensando Pollara 400 AI-NIC per node (`ionic_0` ~ `ionic_7`)
- **Model**: DeepSeek-R1 (671B, FP8) with TP=8, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`
- **Setup**: 2-node PD disaggregation (1 prefill + 1 decode) + router
- **Software**: `--attention-backend aiter --fp8-gemm-backend aiter`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`

### Single-Request Latency (MORI vs Mooncake)

`--num-prompts 1 --max-concurrency 1 --random-output-len 16`, each input length run twice:

| Input Tokens | MORI TTFT (ms) | MORI TPOT (ms) | MORI E2E (ms) | Mooncake TTFT (ms) | Mooncake TPOT (ms) | Mooncake E2E (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 77 | 6.92 | 153 | 68 | 7.03 | 146 |
| 2048 | 81 | 7.26 | 162 | 73 | 7.40 | 154 |
| 4096 | 82 | 7.29 | 162 | 73 | 7.40 | 154 |
| 8192 | 196 | 7.56 | 280 | 196 | 7.79 | 281 |


### High-Concurrency Throughput (MORI vs Mooncake)

`--num-prompts 2048 --max-concurrency 2048 --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024`:

| Metric | MORI | Mooncake |
|---|---|---|
| Successful requests | 2048 | 2048 |
| Request throughput (req/s) | **7.49** | 6.80 |

title: Fix trtllm mla chunked-prefill zero-length bug (#22291)
author: yhyang201
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation


### Background

Issue #22291 reported significant accuracy degradation when using the `trtllm_mla` backend with chunked prefill to process multiple prompts in parallel on Blackwell GPUs. Benchmarks showed that certain sequences under `trtllm_mla` exhibited MSE values as high as 1.0–3.0, whereas the `fa4` and `flashinfer` backends produced MSE values consistently below 0.07 under identical conditions. Notably, the issue only manifested when processing multiple prompts concurrently (batch size > 1); single-request inference produced correct results.

### Root Cause

DeepSeek MLA compresses the KV cache into low-dimensional latent vectors. During prefill, these latents must be decompressed via `kv_b_proj` to recover the full multi-head K and V tensors. For long prefixes, performing this decompression all at once would exceed GPU memory, so a chunked strategy is employed: the prefix KV cache is decompressed and attended to in smaller chunks, with results merged incrementally via `merge_state`.

Within a single batch, different sequences may have different prefix cache lengths depending on their radix tree match results. The total number of chunks is determined by the longest prefix in the batch. Sequences with shorter prefixes will have exhausted their cached KV in earlier chunks, resulting in kv_len=0 for subsequent chunks. Under correct semantics, these rows should produce `out=0` and `lse=-inf`, allowing `merge_state` to safely ignore their contribution.

However, the TRT-LLM ragged attention cubin kernel (invoked through FlashInfer) does not correctly handle the kv_len=0 edge case — stale data remains in the workspace's softmaxStats buffer, producing non-zero outputs and non-`-inf` LSE values. This corrupts the `merge_state` accumulation. This also explains why the issue only appears with concurrent multi-prompt inference — kv_len=0 only arises when prefix lengths differ across sequences within a batch.

### Current Workaround (PR #22688)

PR #22688 introduces a lightweight fixup kernel that runs after the TRT-LLM kernel call: for any rows where kv_len=0, it forces `out=0` and `lse=-inf`. A precomputed per-chunk CPU flag (`prefix_chunk_has_zero_kv`) ensures the fixup kernel is only launched for chunks that actually contain zero-KV rows, keeping overhead minimal. Ideally, the proper long-term fix would be for the TRT-LLM kernel itself to handle kv_len=0 correctly.

### Root Cause Fix

Here is the root cause fix for the FlashInfer TRT-LLM cubin kernel. Currently, when calling `trtllm_ragged_attention_deepseek` with a batch where some sequences have `kv_len=0` (but `q_len>0`), the cubin kernel produces incorrect results for those sequences — the output contains non-zero stale data and the LSE values are not `-inf`. The expected behavior for zero-KV sequences is `out=0` and `lse=-inf`, since there are no key-value tokens to attend to. This appears to be caused by uninitialized or residual data in the workspace's softmaxStats buffer within the cubin kernel. The issue surfaces in practice during chunked prefix cache attention, where sequences with shorter prefixes naturally have `kv_len=0` in later chunks. The incorrect LSE values then corrupt downstream `merge_state` operations, leading to significant accuracy degradation (MSE increasing from ~0.05 to ~3.0). A minimal repro would be to call the kernel with a two-sequence batch where one sequence has `kv_len=0`, and verify that its output rows are non-zero.

Fix #22291

```
  Doc 0 ( 10752 tokens): MSE = 0.021289
  Doc 1 (  5909 tokens): MSE = 0.050858
  Doc 2 (  2471 tokens): MSE = 0.059414
  Doc 3 ( 18993 tokens): MSE = 0.006363
  Doc 4 ( 12526 tokens): MSE = 0.064755
  Doc 5 ( 20001 tokens): MSE = 0.000000
  Doc 6 ( 15570 tokens): MSE = 0.016094
  Doc 7 (  2781 tokens): MSE = 0.091810
```

Report: https://gist.github.com/yhyang201/3ffcf354b8bb1b6c6b3d4b045e83edb4

title: [Bug Fix] Fix RunAI streamer: corrupted weights, missing quant init, and broken URIs for multimodal models
author: junliu-mde
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #22701.

Found while testing #17948 (*Direct model loading from object storage with Runai Model Streamer*) on an 8×H200 cluster with Kimi-K2.5 (WNA16 Marlin MoE) and DeepSeek-V3-0324 (BF16 MoE) via `az://` paths with TP=8.

Three independent bugs prevent RunAI streamer from working correctly with multi-GPU quantized / multimodal models:

1. **`RunaiModelStreamerLoader` omits `quant_config`** — quantized models initialize as BF16, causing OOM or wrong inference.
2. **Stale tensor views from distributed buffer reuse** — the RunAI distributed streamer reuses GPU staging buffers across batches; two code paths (Kimi-K2.5 list accumulation, DeepSeek MLA `cached_a_proj`) hold references across batches, resulting in silently corrupted weights (model outputs all `!`).
3. **`get_processor()` does not resolve object-storage URIs** — unlike `get_config()` and `get_tokenizer()`, `get_processor()` passes raw `az://`/`s3://`/`gs://` URIs to HuggingFace, crashing all multimodal models loaded from object storage.

## Modifications

Four atomic commits, one per root cause:

| Commit | File | Change |
|--------|------|--------|
| `7292838` | `python/sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py` | Pass `quant_config` to `_initialize_model()` in `RunaiModelStreamerLoader.load_model()`, consistent with every other loader |
| `a5f7a2d` | `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/deepseek_weight_loader.py` | `.clone()` tensors cached in `cached_a_proj` so they survive buffer reuse across streamer batches |
| `29590bc` | `python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k25.py` | Refactor `load_weights()` from accumulate-then-process to streaming pattern for language weights; clone only the small vision weights that need batching |
| `fef3c44` | `python/sglang/srt/utils/hf_transformers_utils.py` | Add `is_runai_obj_uri()` / `ObjectStorageModel.get_path()` normalization to `get_processor()`, matching `get_config()` and `get_tokenizer()` |

## Accuracy Tests

Tested end-to-end on 8×H200, Azure Blob Storage (same-region):

**Kimi-K2.5 (WNA16 Marlin, TP=8, `az://`)**
- Before fix: server starts, but all chat responses are `!` (token 0, all-zero logits from stale buffers)
- After fix: coherent multi-turn chat output, correct reasoning and vision responses

**DeepSeek-V3-0324 (FP8, TP=8, `az://`)**
- Before fix: OOM during `_initialize_model()` (missing quant_config causes BF16 allocation for FP8 layers)
- After fix: loads successfully in ~386s (8 GB streamer memory limit), correct inference output

title: [Bugfix] Fix Hunyuan3D-2 DiT checkpoint param mapping
author: jy-song-hub
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
Loading the official Hunyuan3D‑2 DiT checkpoint with the existing mapping fails with an unsupported “new parameter” error for fused text attention weights, for example:                                                                                                                                
- ValueError: New parameter 'double_blocks.10.txt_attn.qkv.weight' is not supported. Checkpoint-specific synthesized parameters should either match ['gate_compress', 'wcscales', 'wtscale', 'input_scale', 'bias', 'norm_q', 'norm_k'] or declare missing_param_init.                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                       
Similar issues show up for single‑stream blocks when the checkpoint uses separate  `proj_out`  /  `attn.to_out`  projections instead of the packed `linear2`  layout used by ` Hunyuan3D2DiT `.  

## Modifications
High‑level change 
- Fix and generalize the Hunyuan3D‑2 DiT parameter‑name mapping so that
  - Split Q/K/V projections in the checkpoint are fused into the model’s `qkv`  tensors. 
  - Out‑projection weights/biases map cleanly to the model’s  `proj` /  `linear2` tensors. 
  - Norm parameters map from HF‑style  `.weight`  names to the internal  `.scale`  fields. 

Details
- Prefix strip for HF‑style exports: This enables subsequent rules to match  `double_blocks.*`  as expected.
  - Add an initial rule to drop the  `model. ` prefix that appears in the official Hunyuan3D‑2 safetensors:  `^model\.(.*)$ → \1 ` 
- Double‑stream MLP renames: This matches how ` _FluxDoubleStreamBlock`  structures its MLPs.
  - Map MLP indices to the internal  `fc_in ` /  `fc_out ` layout for both image and text streams
    - `double_blocks.N.img_mlp.0.*  → double_blocks.N.img_mlp.fc_in.*`
    - `double_blocks.N.img_mlp.2.*  → double_blocks.N.img_mlp.fc_out.* `
    - `double_blocks.N.txt_mlp.0.*  → double_blocks.N.txt_mlp.fc_in.* `
    - `double_blocks.N.txt_mlp.2.*  → double_blocks.N.txt_mlp.fc_out.*`
- Double‑stream QKV fusion for both txt/img attention: This directly resolves the “unsupported new parameter … txt_attn.qkv.weight” error for the Hunyuan3D‑2 checkpoint.  
   - Collapse separate Q/K/V projections in the checkpoint into the fused  `qkv`  tensors used by  `_FluxSelfAttention`  in `double_blocks.*.(txt_attn|img_attn)`
     - `double_blocks.N.(txt_attn|img_attn).(to_q|q_proj|query).*  → (target: .qkv.*, merge_index=0, num_to_merge=3)`
     - `double_blocks.N.(txt_attn|img_attn).(to_k|k_proj|key).*   → (target: .qkv.*, merge_index=1, num_to_merge=3)`
     - `double_blocks.N.(txt_attn|img_attn).(to_v|v_proj|value).* → (target: .qkv.*, merge_index=2, num_to_merge=3)` 
- Double‑stream out‑projection mapping: This handles both standard  `to_out`  and text‑only  `to_add_out`  variants used by some Flux‑style exports. 
   -  Normalize various out‑projection spellings to the model’s  `proj`  tensors on both streams, but only for weights and biases
     - `double_blocks.N.(txt_attn|img_attn).to_out[.0].(weight|bias) → …proj.(weight|bias)`
     - `double_blocks.N.txt_attn.to_add_out[.0].(weight|bias) → …txt_attn.proj.(weight|bias)` 
- Double‑stream Q/K norm remapping and  `.weight → .scale`
   - Map HF‑style norm names to the internal  `_FluxQKNorm`  structure
      - `double_blocks.N.(txt_attn|img_attn).norm_q.* → …norm.query_norm.* `
      - `double_blocks.N.(txt_attn|img_attn).norm_k.* → …norm.key_norm.* `
   - Convert RMSNorm parameter names from  `.weight`  to  `.scale`: 
      - `*.norm.query_norm.weight → *.norm.query_norm.scale`
      - `*.norm.key_norm.weight   → *.norm.key_norm.scale` 
- Single‑stream block packing (shared rules for  single_blocks  and  single_transformer_blocks ) 
   - Support both `single_blocks.N.*`  and  `single_transformer_blocks.N.*`  exports by normalizing them into the internal  `single_blocks.N.*`  layout.
   -  Fuse Q/K/V and MLP projections into the 4‑way packed  `linear1`  used by ` _FluxSingleStreamBlock`
      - `…attn.(to_q|q_proj|query).*    → single_blocks.N.linear1.* (merge_index=0, num_to_merge=4)`
      - `…attn.(to_k|k_proj|key).*      → single_blocks.N.linear1.* (merge_index=1, num_to_merge=4)`
      - `…attn.(to_v|v_proj|value).*    → single_blocks.N.linear1.* (merge_index=2, num_to_merge=4)`
      - `…(proj_mlp|mlp_fc1).*          → single_blocks.N.linear1.* (merge_index=3, num_to_merge=4)`
- Single‑stream out‑projection mapping (fixes  `single_blocks.N.linear2.*`  errors) 
   - Map various output projections to the single `linear2` layer
      - `…(proj_out|out_proj)[.0].(weight|bias) → single_blocks.N.linear2.(weight|bias)`
      - `…attn.to_out[.0].(weight|bias)        → single_blocks.N.linear2.(weight|bias)` 
   - This addresses earlier failures like:
      - ValueError: New parameter 'single_blocks.20.linear2.weight' is not supported. 
- Single‑stream Q/K norm aliases
   - As with double‑stream blocks, map single‑stream attention norms to the internal RMSNorm layout
      - `…attn.norm_q.* → single_blocks.N.norm.query_norm.*`
      - `…attn.norm_k.* → single_blocks.N.norm.key_norm.*`

title: Fix streaming session busy-check double-counting via active_pool_idxs
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Background

This is part of the streaming session memory accounting fix series (#22651). All streaming session tests pass on H200 with strict busy check (`SGLANG_ENABLE_STRICT_MEM_CHECK_DURING_BUSY=2`), including retract, abort, speculative (eagle v1/v2), and SWA variants. Zero leak assertions across all runs.

## Problem

During a streaming session's borrow period (`restore_to_req` -> forward -> `save_from_req`), both `session_held_tokens()` and `_get_total_uncached_sizes()` claim the same KV pages:

- `session_held_tokens()` sees `slot.is_holding_kv == True` and counts `allocated - protected`
- `_get_total_uncached_sizes()` iterates batch reqs and counts `allocated - protected` again

This makes `total_accounted > total`, triggering a false-positive assertion under `SGLANG_ENABLE_STRICT_MEM_CHECK_DURING_BUSY=2`.

PR #22213 introduced `SessionSlot.is_active` as a boolean flag (`restore_to_req` sets True, `save_from_req` sets False) to filter out active slots. However, retract / abort / speculative-v2-overlap paths break the lifecycle pairing -- the flag can get stuck in the wrong state.

## Fix

Replace the cached flag with a per-check recomputation from the scheduler's batch state:

```python
def _active_pool_idxs(self) -> set:
    """Pool idxs currently owned by batch reqs."""
    idxs = set()
    for batch in [self.last_batch, self.running_batch]:
        if batch is None or batch.is_empty():
            continue
        for req in batch.reqs:
            if req.req_pool_idx is not None:
                idxs.add(req.req_pool_idx)
    return idxs
```

`session_held_tokens(active_pool_idxs)` excludes slots whose `req_pool_idx` is in this set. Single source of truth -- no lifecycle pairing required. New scheduler paths (retract, abort, spec) don't need to know about this check.

After this change `is_active` has zero readers, so the field and its two write sites are deleted.

title: [fix] Fix deadlock and TOCTOU race in pause-aware weight update locking
author: maocheng23
body:
## Summary
- Fix writer lock deadlock in `update_weights_from_ipc` and `post_process_weights` during `pause_generation` mode

title: Fix for the low-probability garbled output issue in the GLM-5 series models.
author: zRzRzRzRzRzRzR
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

When serving GLM-5 with L2 HiCache, there is a small probability of corrupted outputs (on the order of a few in ten thousand). However, deeper investigation shows that garbled text is just one manifestation. Due to the sparsity characteristics of the DSA model, cache corruption can affect requests in multiple ways, including garbled text, repetition, rare or unusual characters, and even degradation in model accuracy.

### Root cause

Serving NSA model with L2 HiCache enabled, there is a race between asynchronous layer-wise cache loading and NSA indexer reads.

For NSA ragged top-k paths, index buffers are fetched via `get_index_k_scale_buffer()` / `get_index_k_continuous()` / `get_index_k_scale_continuous()` without enforcing `layer_transfer_counter.wait_until(...)`.
In contrast, other accessors (e.g. `get_kv_buffer()` and `get_index_k_with_scale_buffer()`) do gate on layer-transfer completion.

As a result, the indexer can occasionally read  `indexer_k_scale_buffer`before the corresponding layer’s HiCache load has fully completed on the load stream, causing stale/partial cache reads. Because DSA relies heavily on sparse index correctness, this manifests as non-deterministic corruption patterns (garbled text, repetition, rare tokens, and occasional quality drops), not just simple gibberish.

### Fix

This PR makes NSA index-buffer reads follow the same layer-transfer synchronization contract as other KV accessors under HiCache.

Specifically, we add layer-wise readiness gating (`layer_transfer_counter.wait_until(layer_id - start_layer)`) before NSA ragged-path index reads, including:

- `get_index_k_scale_buffer()`
- `get_index_k_continuous()`
- `get_index_k_scale_continuous()`

With this change, NSA indexer reads can no longer race with asynchronous CPU->GPU cache loading on the load stream. The fix ensures each layer’s `index_K_scale_buffer` is only consumed after transfer completion, eliminating the stale/partial-read window and keeping output accuracy for NSA model + L2 HiCache workloads.

### Acknowledgement

This fix was a joint effort by the teams at [Z.ai](https://z.ai) and [XCORESIGMA CO., LTD.](https://xcoresigma.com/), spanning root-cause analysis, validation, and rollout preparation.

title: Streaming session: fix retract tail leak via _free_tail
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Streaming session: free orphaned KV tail via `_free_tail`

Streaming sessions leak KV pool indices whenever the next turn's `prefix_len` is less than the slot's `kv_allocated_len`. The existing `common.py` spec-tail-trim only handles the speculative-decoding source. This PR replaces it with a single `_free_tail` call in `match_prefix` that handles every source by construction, plus the page-aligned cleanup needed for `PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator`.

### Root cause

When a streaming session resumes, `alloc_for_extend` writes new pool indices into `req_to_token[pool_idx, prefix_len : seq_len]`. Old indices already in that range get overwritten — the allocator still tracks them as in-use, but no `req_to_token` entry references them. Pure leak.

The leaked range is always `[prefix_len, kv_allocated_len)`. Two mechanisms produce a non-empty gap:

- **Over-allocation pushes `allocated` above `committed`** — today this is speculative decoding (alloc `num_draft+1`, commit `num_accepted+1`); any future general over-allocation pattern produces the same gap.
- **Retract retry pulls `prefix_len` below `committed`** — `init_next_round_input` passes `fill_ids[:input_len-1]` on retract retry, so `len(token_ids)` is one short of the saved committed length, dropping `prefix_len` by 1.

### Old design and what it missed

`release_kv_cache` had a streaming-session branch that trimmed `[committed, allocated)` before `save_from_req`. Two gaps it didn't catch:

- **Logit-reserve off-by-1 leaks per turn** — the trim handles `committed < allocated` but not `prefix_len < committed`. Even when the slot saves with `committed == allocated = K`, the next turn computes `prefix_len = K-1` (logit reserve) and `alloc_for_extend` overwrites position `K-1`. Slow drip: 1 token per turn under retract or any path that triggers the reserve.
- **Couples streaming logic into `common.py`** — violates the decorator pattern. Reviewers of the generic release path have to remember the streaming special case, and the trim duplicates work that `match_prefix` is better positioned to do.

### New design: `_free_tail` in `match_prefix`

Runs once per turn, immediately after `restore_to_req` and before `alloc_for_extend`. Frees `[prefix_len, kv_allocated_len)`, then clamps slot + req lengths.

Why this location is correct, not just convenient:

- **`prefix_len` is the exact boundary `alloc_for_extend` will overwrite** — freeing `[prefix_len, kv_allocated_len)` matches the overwrite range. No leak, no over-free.
- **Single source covers every gap** — spec push, retract pull, future scenarios that produce `prefix_len < kv_allocated_len`. No per-source branching.
- **No-op in the common case** — non-spec, non-retract turns satisfy `prefix_len >= kv_allocated_len` and early-return. Zero overhead.
- **Decorator pattern preserved** — `common.py` has zero streaming-session awareness now.

### Page-aligned cleanup

`PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator.free` returns whole pages to the free list (`free_index // page_size`), so freeing a partial page would corrupt pages that still hold committed tokens. `_free_tail` ceil-aligns `prefix_len` to `page_size` before freeing; the unaligned tail in `[prefix_len, free_start)` stays attached to the slot and is freed when `release_session` returns the whole page.

### Bonus

- Drop the buggy `prefix_len = min(committed, max(len(token_ids) - 1, 0))` to `prefix_len = min(committed, len(token_ids))`. The extra `-1` was double-counting the already-applied 1-token logit reserve.
- Add `assert prefix_len >= slot.cache_protected_len` — the append-only invariant established by #22790's `finish_req` pattern is now a checked property.

title: test: fix flaky required function calling assertion
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Summary
- fix the flaky `test_function_call_required` semantics around `tool_choice="required"`
- assert that a tool call is produced and that the chosen tool is one of the provided candidates
- reduce sampling randomness to make the test deterministic

## Root cause

`tool_choice="required"` only guarantees the model **must call some tool** — it does not specify *which* tool. The old test hard-coded `assertEqual(function_name, "get_weather")`, but at `temperature=0.8` with constrained decoding (`strict=True`), `Llama-3.2-1B` occasionally selects `sub` instead.

This flaky was introduced by #21593 (changed `tool_choice="required"` protocol semantics). #22586 fixed the 30% empty-argument failure (`'city' not found in {}`) by adding `strict=True`, but did **not** fix the tool-selection flaky (`got: sub`).

## Evidence of flakiness (before this PR)

| Run | PR | Failure |
|-----|-----|---------|
| [job/71373855817](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/24393739160/job/71373855817?pr=22702) | #22702 | `Function name should be 'get_weather', got: sub` (twice, including retry) |
| [run/24278712753](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/24278712753) | #22586 evidence | 1st try: `'city' not found in {}`; retry: `got: sub` |

## This fix
1. `temperature=0` — eliminate sampling randomness
2. Assert `function_name in valid_tool_names` — only verify the semantic contract of `tool_choice="required"` (any provided tool is valid)
3. Only verify arguments are parseable JSON, not specific content

## Validation

Ran `test_openai_function_calling.py` via `/rerun-test` on this PR — **3/3 pass**:

| # | Run | Result |
|---|-----|--------|
| 1 | [run/24499351599](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/24499351599) | ✅ pass (11 tests, 89.8s) |

title: fix(hicache): emit KV events for L2 host cache insertions
author: ishandhanani
body:
## Summary

- Emit `_record_store_event(new_node)` when a new suffix node is materialized in the host (L2) radix tree during `_insert_helper_host`
- Without this, L2 cache insertions are invisible to downstream KV cache indexers (e.g. Dynamo's radix-tree router), causing blind spots in overlap scoring for pages fetched from shared cache into host memory

## Context

This is a prerequisite for shared KV cache routing in [ai-dynamo/dynamo#7536](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/7536). The Dynamo router relies on KV events to build its radix tree for device-level overlap scoring. When HiCache fetches pages from L3 (Mooncake) into L2 (host), the router needs to see those events to update its view of what each worker has cached.

Credit: @jthomson04 (cherry-picked from `jthomson04/sgl-exists-query`)

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify KV events are emitted for L2 insertions during HiCache prefetch
- [ ] Confirm Dynamo router radix tree reflects L2-cached pages after shared cache fetch

title: [Bug Fix] Remove follow_bootstrap_room fast path in PD disaggregation DP rank resolution
author: ByronHsu
body:
## Motivation

In PD (Prefill-Decode) disaggregation mode with data parallelism, the decode server needs to know which prefill DP worker handled a given request to establish the correct KV transfer connection. There are two mechanisms for determining the DP worker:

1. **Explicit DP rank**: The request carries `data_parallel_rank` (mapped to `routed_dp_rank`), which the DP controller dispatcher respects with highest priority via `maybe_external_dp_rank_routing`, overriding any load balance method.
2. **Load balance method**: If no explicit rank is specified, the DP controller dispatches according to the configured method (e.g., `round_robin`, `follow_bootstrap_room`, etc.).

To communicate the actual prefill DP rank to the decode server:
- Prefill calls `_register_prefill_dp_rank` to register the request's assigned DP rank to the bootstrap server.
- Decode calls `query_prefill_dp_ranks` to retrieve the actual DP rank used by prefill.

**Bug**: When the prefill load balance method is `follow_bootstrap_room`, there were two fast-path optimizations that assumed the prefill DP rank is always `bootstrap_room % dp_size`:

1. **Prefill side** (`CommonKVSender.__init__`): Skipped calling `_register_prefill_dp_rank` when `load_balance_method == "follow_bootstrap_room"`, since the decode side could infer the rank from the bootstrap room number.
2. **Decode side** (`_resolve_prefill_dp_rank`): Returned `bootstrap_room % dp_size` directly when `prefill_info.follow_bootstrap_room` was true, bypassing the `query_prefill_dp_ranks` call.

This assumption breaks when an external router (e.g., the model gateway) sets `routed_dp_rank` on the request. The DP controller routes to the externally-specified rank (which may differ from `bootstrap_room % dp_size`), but prefill never registers the actual rank and decode computes the wrong one.

## Revised Fix

The original approach removed the fast path entirely and always fell through to register/query. This causes unnecessary perf regression for strict `follow_bootstrap_room` deployments (extra HTTP round-trip per request).

`follow_bootstrap_room` is a strict dispatch policy — SGLang assumes that if prefill uses it, the rank is always `bootstrap_room % dp_size`, and decode infers the rank accordingly without querying. The real issue is that `routed_dp_rank` can silently override this policy on the prefill side, causing a mismatch that decode cannot detect.

The revised fix takes a different approach:

- **Preserve the fast path**: Decode still infers `bootstrap_room % dp_size` when `follow_bootstrap_room` is active. No perf regression for existing deployments.
- **Detect conflict on prefill side**: If `follow_bootstrap_room` is configured but the actual `attn_dp_rank != bootstrap_room % dp_size` (i.e., an external `routed_dp_rank` overrode the dispatch), the request is **aborted** with a clear error message. This prevents decode from silently computing the wrong rank.
- **Env var escape hatch**: `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_FORCE_QUERY_PREFILL_DP_RANK=1` disables the fast path on both sides — prefill always registers, decode always queries. This supports non-strict routing (e.g., external router overriding `follow_bootstrap_room`) at the cost of an extra round-trip.

title: [Fix/Kernel] Add JIT rmsnorm_hf kernel to fix transformers backend MMLU accuracy regression
author: Jiminator
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

Commit `34ddf135fd` introduced `recursive_replace()` in `TransformersBase`, which replaced every HF `*RMSNorm` module with SGLang's `sgl_kernel.rmsnorm`. The two kernels differ in rounding order: `sgl_kernel.rmsnorm` multiplies the weight in fp32 then casts, while HF's `LlamaRMSNorm` casts the normalized output to the activation dtype first, then multiplies. Under int4wo-128 quantization this ~1-ULP difference compounds across 32 transformer layers and flips 3 borderline MMLU questions (0.703 → 0.656).  

#22435 introduced a naive fix which was reverting the change, but that led to a significant perf regression.
                                                  
This PR adds a JIT kernel (`rmsnorm_hf`) that replicates HF's cast-before-weight-multiply order exactly, recovering accuracy with less throughput regression.                     

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
  - **`python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/elementwise/rmsnorm_hf.cuh`** (new): 512-thread scalar-strided RMSNorm kernel with HF semantics. Caches input   
  values in per-thread registers between the two passes to halve global memory reads. Supports fp16/bf16, PDL (Hopper+).                             
  - **`python/sglang/jit_kernel/rmsnorm_hf.py`** (new): Python wrapper using `cache_once` + `load_jit`. Supports `hidden_size` that is a multiple of 
  512 (covers all Llama/Qwen/Mistral models).                             
  - **`python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_rmsnorm_hf.py`** (new): Correctness tests against PyTorch HF reference, out-param test, hidden-size
  predicate test. Registered for `stage-b-kernel-unit-1-gpu-large` and `nightly-kernel-1-gpu`.                                                       
  - **`python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py`**: When `cast_x_before_out_mul=True`, `forward_cuda` dispatches to `jit_kernel.rmsnorm_hf` (falls back
  to `forward_native` for unsupported hidden sizes or non-CUDA).          
  - **`python/sglang/srt/models/transformers.py`**: Sets `cast_x_before_out_mul=True` in `replace_rms_norm_class` for the non-Gemma path so the
  transformers backend uses HF rounding.    

## Accuracy Tests
On a H100:
<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

Before Fix: 0.6562
After Fix: 0.703 (Accuracy fully recovered)

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->
Before Fix: 868.824 tok/s
With Naive Fix: 780.230 tok/s
After Fix: 845.62 tok/s

author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #22772 for the B200 ModelOpt diffusion CI coverage. This PR now focuses on preserving generated outputs for the B200 ModelOpt cases and fixing the FLUX.2 NVFP4 CI launch path.

## Modifications

- Removes the BF16 quality-comparison test and related threshold/config plumbing from the B200 suite.
- Saves generated media artifacts for all ModelOpt diffusion CI cases when `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_ARTIFACT_DIR` is set.
- Requests 5-second generation for the ModelOpt video CI cases and saves video artifacts with a `_5s.mp4` suffix.
- Fixes the FLUX.2 NVFP4 CI case to run the base `black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-dev` model with `--transformer-weights-path black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-dev-NVFP4`.
  - The NVFP4 repo is a raw safetensors export and does not contain a Diffusers `config.json`, so passing it as `--transformer-path` causes the `_class_name`/`config.json` load failure seen in CI.

title: fix(loads): preserve include filtering after watching mode switch
author: hnyls2002
body:
Follow-up to #22919. After switching `get_loads_communicator` to watching mode, the scheduler always receives `include=["all"]` (since concurrent callers share one request). This made the `include` query parameter a no-op — callers always got all sections regardless of what they requested.

Add client-side filtering to preserve the original API contract: sections not in the `include` list are set to `None` before returning, so the external behavior stays the same as before the watching mode switch.

title: [KV-Events] Fix kv events events publishing for CP
author: vladnosiv
body:
KV events were enabled on every scheduler with `attn_tp_rank == 0`. With context parallelism, multiple CP ranks can have `attn_tp_rank == 0`, so each CP rank tried to publish KV events for the same DP rank. For ZMQ this caused duplicate publishers, including a bind conflict on the same endpoint (tcp://*:5557), and semantically it would duplicate KV cache events for replicated CP KV state.

This change gates KV event publishing on both `attn_tp_rank == 0` and `attn_cp_rank == 0`, matching the TP behavior while ensuring only one KV event stream is emitted per DP rank.

Added a regression test for Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 with TP2 + attn-cp-size 2.

title: [Bug Fix] Ensure prefill_info_table is populated before honoring disagg_prefill_dp_rank
author: ByronHsu
body:
## Motivation

If the **first** request to the PD engine carries `disagg_prefill_dp_rank`, the request fails with:

> `Prefill server with bootstrap_addr: {self.bootstrap_addr} is healthy before`

However, if the first request does **not** contain `disagg_prefill_dp_rank` but a later request does, the subsequent requests work because the first request triggers the prefill info query and caches it.

### Root cause

In `DecodePreallocQueue._resolve_prefill_dp_rank`, the `req.disagg_prefill_dp_rank` early-return is checked *before* `self.kv_manager.prefill_info_table.get(_bootstrap_addr(req))`. When the client explicitly supplies `disagg_prefill_dp_rank`, we short-circuit and never trigger the slow path that queries and caches the prefill info. The subsequent prefill-server health check then has no cached info to validate against, producing the "healthy before" error.

## Modifications

Move `prefill_info = self.kv_manager.prefill_info_table.get(_bootstrap_addr(req))` to the top of `_resolve_prefill_dp_rank`. If the lookup returns `None`, return `None` so the request falls through to the slow path (`_ensure_prefill_info`), which queries and caches the prefill info. Only *after* prefill info is available do we honor the client-provided `req.disagg_prefill_dp_rank`.

## Reproduction

```bash
# Prefill
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B \
    --tp 4 --dp 4 --enable-dp-attention --disaggregation-mode prefill

# Decode
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B \
    --tp 4 --dp 4 --enable-dp-attention --disaggregation-mode decode \
    --base-gpu-id 4 --port 30010

# Load balancer
python -m sglang_router.launch_router --mini-lb --pd-disaggregation \
    --prefill http://127.0.0.1:30000 --decode http://127.0.0.1:30010 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
```

Send the very first request with `disagg_prefill_dp_rank` set — before the fix, this fails with the "healthy before" error; after the fix, it succeeds:

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/generate \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{
        "text": "Hello World How are you?",
        "sampling_params": {"max_new_tokens": 128, "temperature": 0.0},
        "stream": false,
        "routed_dp_rank": 0,
        "disagg_prefill_dp_rank": 0
    }'
```

title: [Pipeline Parallelism][Bug] Fix scheduler hang in pipeline parallelism setup
author: jonahbernard
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
There is a bug in SGLang servers that use pipeline parallelism. The bug causes the server to hang for prefill requests due to  `_get_new_batch_prefill_raw` always returning `None` on every iteration of the main scheduler event loop.

I'll run through an example using `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B` with `self.pp_size=2`:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B \
    --moe-runner-backend triton \
    --disable-cuda-graph \
    --disable-piecewise-cuda-graph \
    --chunked-prefill-size 64 \
    --max-running-requests 1 \
    --port 30004 \
    --pp-size 2
```

The bug occurs here in sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:

```python
        if (
            self.get_num_allocatable_reqs(running_bs) <= 0
            and self.chunked_req is not None
            and not self.enable_priority_preemption
        ):
            self.running_batch.batch_is_full = True
            return None
```

In this SGLang server PP=2, so `get_num_allocatable_reqs = min((pp.max_micro_batch_size - running_bs), self.req_to_token_pool.available_size())`.

`pp.max_micro_batch_size = max(self.max_running_requests // self.pp_size, 1)` so `pp.max_micro_batch_size = 1`.

`self.req_to_token_pool.available_size() = len(self.free_slots)` and the free slots are initialized to `self.free_slots = list(range(size))`.

In ou server's `req_to_token_pool`, `size = max_num_reqs` and `max_num_reqs = min(max_num_reqs // self.dp_size, max(min(int(token_capacity / self.model_config.context_len * 512), 4096), 2048))`

`self.dp_size=1`, which gives us:

`max_num_reqs = min(max_num_reqs, max(min(int(token_capacity / self.model_config.context_len * 512), 4096), 2048))`

This gives us `get_num_allocatable_reqs = min((max(self.max_running_requests // self.pp_size, 1) - running_bs), min(max_num_reqs, max(min(int(token_capacity / self.model_config.context_len * 512), 4096), 2048))`

We have `token_capacity = 4960064` and `self.model_config.context_len = 40960`, which gives us:

`get_num_allocatable_reqs = min((max(self.max_running_requests // self.pp_size, 1) - running_bs), min(max_num_reqs, 4096))`

`max_running_requests=1` so we get:

`get_num_allocatable_reqs = min((1 - running_bs), 1)` before any requests are sent, which will allow the first prefill batch to be returned by `_get_new_batch_prefill_raw`.

If a single large prompt is sent, it will be broken into chunks. The prompt's `Req` instance will be assigned to `self.chunked_req` and a req slot will be allocated in the req_to_token_pool, which started with 1 free slot so now it will have 0 free slots. Thus,

`get_num_allocatable_reqs = min((1 - running_bs), 0 (len(free_slots)) = 0` which means

```python
        if (
            self.get_num_allocatable_reqs(running_bs) <= 0
            and self.chunked_req is not None
            and not self.enable_priority_preemption
        ):
            self.running_batch.batch_is_full = True
            return None
```

will evaluate to True on every iteration of the scheduler's event loop, and no new requests will make progress, nor will the current request. Thus, the server will hang for lots of users.

When pipeline parallelism was first added to SGLang (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/5724), this check actually always allowed the next chunk of a chunked prefill prompt to be returned in the new batch, and the check was `not self.chunked_req` instead of `self.chunked_req is not None`, which are logically opposite.

A bug was introduced in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/14883 when that check was subtly inverted. The check went from `if not self.chunked_req` to `if self.chunked_req is not None`. 

## Modifications

Change `if self.chunked_req is not None` back to `if self.chunked_req is None`.

title: [Bug Fix] Resolve EAGLE cuda graph IMA under PD + DP + MTP with GLM-5.1
author: zRzRzRzRzRzRzR
body:
Under long-running PD + DP + MTP, decode crashes with
`vectorized_gather_kernel: index out of bounds`.

Two paths feed garbage into the next cuda graph replay:

1. **Shared buffer view.** `logits_output` fields are views into
   the cuda graph's pre-allocated output buffers. Assigning them
   to `spec_info` directly means the next `replay()` overwrites
   the data `spec_info` still holds.

2. **Padded region staleness.** `EAGLEDraftCudaGraphRunner` only
   overwrites `[:raw_bs]` of its input buffers before replay.
   Padded slots `[raw_bs:bs]` retain stale values
   (e.g. `topk_index = -4886055425978319163`) and get gathered
   as OOB indices inside the graph.
   
  All guards are no-ops on healthy data.

title: [XPU] Fix DeepSeek-OCR tests under transformers 5.x
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Summary

The XPU DeepSeek-OCR tests (`test/srt/xpu/test_deepseek_ocr.py`, `test_deepseek_ocr_triton.py`) failed under transformers 5.x after #21569 with:

```
ImportError: cannot import name 'LlamaFlashAttention2' from
'transformers.models.llama.modeling_llama'
```

### Root cause

`AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(..., trust_remote_code=True)` internally resolves `AutoConfig` first. DeepSeek-OCR's `config.json` has an `auto_map` entry pointing at remote code (`modeling_deepseekocr.py` → `modeling_deepseekv2.py`). That chain imports `LlamaFlashAttention2`, which transformers 5.x removed in favor of a unified `LlamaAttention`.

Notably, the tokenizer itself is `LlamaTokenizerFast` (a built-in class, no `auto_map` in `tokenizer_config.json`) — it does not need `trust_remote_code` at all.

The NVIDIA DeepSeek-OCR test in `test/registered/vlm/test_vision_openai_server_a.py` already uses `trust_remote_code = False` for the same reason, which is why that side is unaffected. The XPU test hit this because it passes `trust_remote_code=True` for the client-side tokenizer.

Additionally, before hitting the `LlamaFlashAttention2` error, the XPU CI container was actually failing even earlier with `ImportError: matplotlib not found` (transformers 5.4+ `check_imports` preflight). Both errors originate from the same issue — chasing DeepSeek-OCR's remote code when the tokenizer doesn't need it.

### Fix

Switch from `transformers.AutoTokenizer` to `sglang.srt.utils.hf_transformers.get_tokenizer`, which:
- defaults to `trust_remote_code=False` → skips remote-code resolution → the tokenizer loads as `LlamaTokenizerFast` without touching `modeling_deepseekv2.py`
- importing the package triggers `_apply_compat()` (compat patches including the `LlamaFlashAttention2 = LlamaAttention` alias) as a side effect — an extra safety net for any other code paths that still drag remote code in

`use_fast=False` was dropped because transformers 5.x AutoTokenizer always returns the fast tokenizer regardless (see comment in `tokenizer.py::get_tokenizer`), so it was a no-op — dropping it clarifies intent.

## Test plan

- [ ] Trigger `PR Test (XPU)` workflow and confirm `xpu/test_deepseek_ocr.py` + `xpu/test_deepseek_ocr_triton.py` no longer fail at tokenizer load
- [ ] Verify pre-commit hooks pass (locally: green)

title: [fix] Fix dynamic chunking profiling crash on GLM-5 models
author: Baichuan7
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Fixes #23057 

When `--enable-dynamic-chunking` is used with GLM-5  (have DeepEP ), the profiling phase crashes with `AttributeError: _is_extend_in_batch`. This silently disables dynamic chunking and also causes KV cache memory leaks and NCCL timeouts on non-first PP ranks.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_pp_mixin.py` (`profile_and_init_predictor`):
  - Call `set_is_extend_in_batch(True)` before `model_runner.forward()` in the profiling loop, since the profiling path bypasses `prepare_mlp_sync_batch` which normally sets this value
  

## Speed Tests and Profiling

- Before: dynamic chunking silently disabled on model, with KV cache leak and
  NCCL timeout as side effects
- After: profiling completes successfully, dynamic chunking works as intended

title: [bugfix]fix(qwen3_5): broadcast per-tensor scale in _make_packed_weight_loader for FP8 models
author: kkyyxhll
body: ## Motivation Loading FP8 per-tensor quantized Qwen3.5 models (both dense and MoE) crashes during weight loading with: ``` RuntimeError: split_with_sizes expects split_sizes to sum exactly to 1, but got 3 ``` This is a regression introduced in 0.5.10 by the GatedDeltaNet fused projection refactoring. | SGLang Version | Result | |---|---| | ✅ 0.5.9 | Loads and runs correctly | | ❌ 0.5.10.post1 | Crashes during weight loading | SGLang fuses GatedDeltaNet input projections via `stacked_params_mapping`: ```python ("in_proj_qkvz.", "in_proj_qkv.", (0, 1, 2)), # tuple shard_id ("in_proj_qkvz.", "in_proj_z.", 3), ``` When loading checkpoint weight `in_proj_qkv.weight_scale` (per-tensor scale, shape=`[1]`), `_make_packed_weight_loader` intercepts the tuple `shard_id=(0, 1, 2)`. `_get_split_sizes_for_param` returns `[1, 1, 1]` for `PerTensorScaleParameter`, so `split_sizes` sums to 3, but the tensor only has 1 element — `torch.split` raises `RuntimeError`. This affects **all** FP8 per-tensor quantized Qwen3.5 models (static and dynamic, dense and MoE), regardless of TP size or quantization tool. Fixes #23051 ## Modifications In `_make_packed_weight_loader`, a per-tensor scale is a global scalar that applies equally to every logical shard. It should be **broadcast** (replicated), not **split**. 1. **Scalar branch** (shape=`[]`): Remove the `assert len(split_sizes) == 1` guard and broadcast to all shards via `* len(loaded_shard_id)`. 2. **New `elif` branch** (shape=`[1]`, `numel()==1`): Broadcast single-element tensors (e.g. per-tensor `weight_scale`) to every logical shard instead of splitting. 3. **Normal tensors**: Unchanged — still split by `split_sizes`. ```diff if len(loaded_weight.shape) == 0: - # Scalar only makes sense for a single logical shard. - assert len(split_sizes) == 1 and split_sizes[0] == 1, (...) - chunks = [loaded_weight.reshape(1)] + # Scalar: broadcast to each logical shard. + chunks = [loaded_weight.reshape(1)] * len(loaded_shard_id) +elif loaded_weight.numel() == 1: + # Single-element tensor (e.g. per-tensor scale [1]): + # broadcast to every logical shard. + chunks = [loaded_weight] * len(loaded_shard_id) else: split_dim = getattr(param, "output_dim", 0) chunks = loaded_weight.split(split_sizes, dim=split_dim) ``` ## Accuracy Tests Tested with the following FP8 per-tensor static quantized models, all loading successfully and producing correct outputs: Non-quantized (bf16) models are unaffected — their weights are large matrices that never hit the `numel() == 1` branch. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No speed impact. This change only affects the weight loading path (model initialization), not the forward pass. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [docker] Fix stray backslash dropping sgl-model-gateway COPY
author: mispa-ms
body:
## Summary
- Remove a stray trailing backslash in `docker/Dockerfile` (line 626) that was silently consuming the subsequent `COPY --from=gateway_builder /build/sgl-model-gateway-bin /usr/local/bin/sgl-model-gateway` as shell tokens appended to the preceding `RUN`.
- Because the RUN ended with `|| true \`, the shell error was masked; `framework_final` built successfully but without the gateway binary, causing the later `runtime` stage COPY to fail.

## Failure Signature
BuildKit warned: `NoEmptyContinuation: Empty continuation line (line 630)`.

Build error:
```
COPY --from=framework_final /usr/local/bin/sgl-model-gateway /usr/local/bin/sgl-model-gateway:
ERROR: failed to calculate checksum of ref ...: "/usr/local/bin/sgl-model-gateway": not found
```

In the BuildKit trace you can see the RUN literally ended with:
```
... || true COPY --from=gateway_builder /build/sgl-model-gateway-bin /usr/local/bin/sgl-model-gateway
```
confirming the COPY was swallowed into the RUN.

## Fix
Drop the trailing backslash so the `RUN` terminates and both gateway `COPY --from=gateway_builder ...` instructions are honored as real Dockerfile directives.

## Test plan
- [ ] `docker build` of the full Dockerfile (runtime target) completes without the `sgl-model-gateway: not found` checksum error.
- [ ] Resulting runtime image contains `/usr/local/bin/sgl-model-gateway` and `sgl-router` Python bindings installed from `/build/gateway_wheels`.
- [ ] BuildKit no longer emits the `NoEmptyContinuation` warning for this line.

author: yctseng0211
body:
## Motivation

Fix `multimodal-gen-test-2-gpu-amd` consistently timing out on partition 0.
**Root cause:** The 2-gpu suite has 1 standalone file (`test_disagg_server.py`). The partitioning logic reserves one partition for each standalone file:

title: fix: fallback to triton for attention-sink models (flashinfer unsupported)
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

The FlashInfer attention backend does not accept a `sinks` kwarg, but hybrid-SWA models like `GptOssForCausalLM` and `MiMoV2FlashForCausalLM` (when `add_{swa,full}_attention_sink_bias=True`) pass per-head sink scalars to the attention call. Two auto-selection paths used to fall back to `flashinfer` without considering this, which could leave sink models on an unsupported backend.

## Modifications

- Add `ModelConfig.has_attention_sinks`, derived in `_derive_hybrid_model` via a new `_detect_attention_sinks()` helper:
  - `GptOssForCausalLM` always has sinks
  - `MiMoV2FlashForCausalLM` / `MiMoV2MTP` have sinks only when `add_swa_attention_sink_bias` or `add_full_attention_sink_bias` is set on `hf_text_config`
- In `ServerArgs._get_default_attn_backend`, the non-MLA fallback branch now picks `triton` instead of `flashinfer` when `model_config.has_attention_sinks` is true
- In `ServerArgs._resolve_io_decode_attention_compatibility`, the hicache kernel-io + FA3 avoidance path applies the same check before setting `decode_attention_backend`

## Scope of Behavior Change

Only the implicit auto-selection paths are affected:

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Sink model, no `--attention-backend`, non-Hopper / non-Blackwell GPU | flashinfer (unsupported) | triton |
| Sink model, hicache `io_backend=kernel` with FA3 effective decode | flashinfer (unsupported) | triton |
| Non-sink models, all configurations | unchanged | unchanged |
| Explicit `--attention-backend ...` | unchanged | unchanged |

title: [AMD] Pin peft<0.19 in pyproject_other.toml to fix ROCm CI ImportError
author: bingxche
body:
## Summary

Pin `peft>=0.18.0,<0.19.0` in both the `diffusion_hip` and `test` extras of `python/pyproject_other.toml` to unblock AMD ROCm CI.

## Motivation

[`peft 0.19.0`](https://github.com/huggingface/peft/releases) (released Apr 14, 2026) bumped its required `torchao` floor from `>=0.4.0` to `>=0.16.0` inside `peft.import_utils.is_torchao_available` ([huggingface/peft#3101](https://github.com/huggingface/peft/commit/2d488820ab039f31e1289e5b4f66e4fee176593b)). The ROCm Docker image used by AMD CI (`rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.x-rocm700-mi30x-*`) ships `torchao==0.9.0`, so any test path that imports `peft.tuners.lora.torchao.dispatch_torchao` now hits:

```
ImportError: Found an incompatible version of torchao.
Found version 0.9.0, but only versions above 0.16.0 are supported
```

This kills HFRunner subprocesses with `exit code 1 before producing output`, breaking two LoRA reference-comparison tests:

- `test/registered/lora/test_multi_lora_backend.py::TestMultiLoRABackend::test_ci_lora_models_multi_batch`
- `test/registered/lora/test_lora_hf_sgl_logprob_diff.py::test_lora_logprob_comparison_basic`

Fingerprint in baseline AMD nightly [run 24527146590](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/24527146590) (partitions 11 & 12 of `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd`):https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/24527146590/job/71700328208#step:6:1348

```
File ".../peft/tuners/lora/torchao.py", line 142, in dispatch_torchao
File ".../peft/import_utils.py", line 143, in is_torchao_available
ImportError: Found an incompatible version of torchao. Found version 0.9.0, but only versions above 0.16.0 are supported
```

## Why `python/pyproject_other.toml`

`scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh:123` renames `pyproject_other.toml` to `pyproject.toml` inside the container before `pip install -e`:

```bash
docker exec ci_sglang bash -c \
  'rm -rf python/pyproject.toml && mv python/pyproject_other.toml python/pyproject.toml'
```

So `pyproject_other.toml` is the file AMD CI actually resolves dependencies from. #23072 covers the AMD wheel pyproject (`3rdparty/amd/wheel/sglang/pyproject.toml`); this PR covers the CI install path.

## Verification

[Run 24563832425](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/24563832425) on `bingxche/fix-peft-torchao-amd` (workflow_dispatch, `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd` only):

| Test | Partition | Baseline | After pin |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_multi_lora_backend.py` | 11 | `Ran 3 tests in 144s → FAILED (errors=1)` | **PASS, 30.0 min** |
| `test_lora_hf_sgl_logprob_diff.py` | 12 | `subprocess died with exit code 1` | **PASS, 196s** (overall logprob 2/2 + 5/5 + 5/5) |

Tier 3 re-verification on [run 24599716745](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/24599716745): both tests continue to PASS in partitions 11 / 12, no regression in any other partition.

## Modifications

`python/pyproject_other.toml`:

- `diffusion_hip` extras: `peft>=0.18.0` → `peft>=0.18.0,<0.19.0`
- `test` extras: `peft>=0.18.0` → `peft>=0.18.0,<0.19.0`

Diff stat: `1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)`.

## Note on long-term fix

Bumping `torchao` in the ROCm image to `>=0.16.0` would also fix this and let us stay on the latest peft. Pinning here is the immediate unblock; image bump can be a follow-up PR.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] CI verified green on this pin (run 24563832425 + 24599716745).

title: Fix hybrid swa chunked prefill oom
author: ispobock
body:
## Motivation

`PrefillAdder.add_chunked_req` caps a chunked req's remaining tokens at `min(rem_chunk_tokens, rem_total_tokens, rem_swa_tokens)` in the hybrid SWA path. But `alloc_extend` reserves `extend_num_tokens + page_size` per request. When `rem_swa_tokens == extend_num_tokens`, the chunked req is admitted with the entire SWA budget, leaving no room for the extra page and OOMing at alloc time.

A second issue in the same path: when `_rem_tokens <= 0`, the fallback assigns `rem_chunk_tokens` unconditionally, which bypasses the SWA budget entirely and triggers the same OOM under sustained pressure. With the fix, the req is deferred to the next round instead.

## Accuracy

Launch:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --model openai/gpt-oss-120b --tp 2 --trust-remote-code --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000
```

Bench:

```bash
python benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-questions 1319 --parallel 128 --port 30000
```

this PR:

```
Accuracy: 0.843
Invalid: 0.000
Latency: 52.902 s
Output throughput: 3383.183 token/s
```

title: [LoRA] Fix EP + per-expert MoE LoRA illegal memory access
author: jybsuper
body:
## Summary

Two related bugs prevent `--tp N --ep M --enable-lora --lora-backend triton --moe-runner-backend triton` from running on any MoE model with per-expert LoRA adapters; both reliably crash in the first forward pass with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`. This PR fixes both and adds unit coverage.

### Bug 1 — `LoRAMemoryPool` sizes per-expert buffers for the global expert count

`FusedMoEWithLoRA` allocates LoRA A/B buffers via `LoRAMemoryPool`, whose per-expert shape was `[num_loras, num_global_experts, ...]`. Under EP, however, `StandardDispatcher` remaps `topk_ids` from global → local IDs *before* the MoE kernel (see `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/standard.py`), so both the base MoE weights and the LoRA delta kernels are indexed with IDs in `[0, num_local_experts)` plus a `-1` sentinel. A LoRA buffer sized `[..., 128, ...]` being indexed with local IDs `[0, 32)` therefore reads the wrong expert's weights (or, combined with bug #2, triggers the illegal access).

### Bug 2 — `moe_lora_align_block_size` doesn't filter the `-1` sentinel in one branch

`_count_and_sort_expert_tokens` only rejected `expert_id >= num_experts`:

```cpp
for (size_t i = tid; i < numel; i += stride) {
  int32_t expert_id = topk_ids[i];
  if (expert_id >= num_experts) { continue; }      // <-- no `< 0`
  ...
  int32_t rank_post_pad = atomicAdd(
    &cumsum_buffer[(model_offset * (num_experts + 1)) + expert_id], 1);
  sorted_token_ids[max_num_tokens_padded * model_offset + rank_post_pad] = i;
}
```

`-1` passes that guard and produces:
- `atomicAdd(&cumsum_buffer[model_offset * (num_experts+1) + (-1)], 1)` — OOB write (negative stride), and
- `sorted_token_ids[offset + rank_post_pad]` with a garbage `rank_post_pad`.

Both sibling call sites in the same file already guard `expert_id < 0 || expert_id >= num_experts`. This PR makes the third call site consistent.

## Changes

- **`python/sglang/srt/lora/mem_pool.py`**
  - Capture `(moe_ep_size, moe_ep_rank)` and `moe_use_local_expert_ids` at pool init. The latter is `True` iff `moe_ep_size > 1` **and** the active runner remaps to local IDs (Triton/DeepGEMM/Marlin) — the check is skipped for runners that keep global IDs (FlashInfer CUTLASS / CuteDSL / TRTLLM-routed), so their buffers stay globally-keyed.
  - Size per-expert LoRA buffers by `num_local_experts` (`get_lora_A_shape` / `get_lora_B_shape`).
  - Route all four per-expert load paths in `load_lora_weight_to_buffer` through a new `_iter_local_expert_weights(weights)` helper that filters and remaps global → local expert IDs for both `dict` and 3D-tensor inputs, then zeros unowned/unloaded slots.
  - No-op for pure TP and for runners that keep global IDs — verified by the TP-only LoRA unit tests, which still pass unchanged.

- **`python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/lora/moe_lora_align_kernel.cu`**
  - Add `expert_id < 0` to the guard in `_count_and_sort_expert_tokens`, matching the two other call sites; adds a comment explaining the sentinel contract with `StandardDispatcher`.

- **`test/registered/unit/lora/test_mem_pool_ep_unit.py`** (new, 22 cases, hermetic CPU-only)
  - `_get_num_experts` covering `num_experts`, `num_local_experts`, `n_routed_experts`, and fallbacks.
  - `_get_num_local_experts` under no-EP / EP=1 / EP=4 and uneven splits.
  - `_global_to_local_expert_id` ownership filter.
  - `_iter_local_expert_weights` for dict and 3D-tensor inputs, with correct remapping under EP.
  - `LoRAMemoryPool.__init__` EP-context capture for no-EP, Triton+EP, and FlashInfer+EP.

## Compatibility

- **Pure TP (any `--tp`, no `--ep`)**: `moe_ep_size == 1` → `moe_use_local_expert_ids == False` → buffers and iteration are identical to pre-fix behavior. Verified end-to-end with `--tp 2` + LoRA.
- **Pure EP**: per-rank buffers and remapping via `_iter_local_expert_weights`.
- **Mixed TP + EP**: same as pure EP — TP slicing already happened when the base model loaded; the LoRA fix only affects the expert dimension.
- **FlashInfer CUTLASS / CuteDSL / TRTLLM-routed**: `_moe_runner_keeps_global_expert_ids()` returns `True`, `moe_use_local_expert_ids` stays `False` → buffers stay globally-keyed, matching what those runners expect.
- **Non-LoRA paths**: untouched.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest test/registered/unit/lora/test_mem_pool_ep_unit.py` — 22 passed.
- [x] `pre-commit run --files ...`
- [x] End-to-end regression that originally reproduced the crash:
  ```bash
  python -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 \
    --tp 4 --ep 4 \
    --enable-lora --max-loras-per-batch 1 --max-lora-rank 32 \
    --lora-target-modules all --lora-paths lora_alpha=<per-expert adapter> \
    --lora-backend triton --moe-runner-backend triton
  # curl /v1/completions -> before: CUDA illegal memory access in first forward
  #                        after : returns a completion successfully
  ```
- [x] `--tp 4 --ep 4` base (no `--enable-lora`) still works.
- [x] `--tp 2` (no EP) + LoRA still works (regression for the non-EP path).

title: [Bugfix] Fix DeepEP timeout when compiling DeepGeMM in EP+DP+TP
author: ByronHsu
body:
## Motivation

When compiling DeepGeMM for Kimi K2 EP+DP+TP 32, I hit a DeepEP timeout:

```
File "/root/code/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/deepep.py", line 458, in _dispatch_core
    ) = buffer.dispatch(
        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/root/code/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/deep_ep/buffer.py", line 376, in dispatch
    return self.internode_dispatch(x, handle, num_tokens_per_rank, num_tokens_per_rdma_rank, is_token_in_rank,
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/root/code/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/deep_ep/buffer.py", line 489, in internode_dispatch
    recv_src_meta, send_rdma_head, send_nvl_head, event = self.runtime.internode_dispatch(
                                                          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
RuntimeError: DeepEP error: timeout (dispatch CPU)
```

Compile only happens on `local_rank=0` on each node, however, each node can compile at a different speed. Say DeepEP timeout is 100s — if the compile time differs by more than 100s across nodes, we hit the DeepEP timeout. This symptom is amplified when chunked prefill size is large (I set it to `8192*32`, so per-DP chunk prefill size is 8192).

## Modifications

1. **Add torch distributed barrier before EP all-to-all (`deepep.py`)**: DeepEP's all-to-all has a much shorter timeout compared to `torch.distributed`. By adding a barrier before each EP all-to-all during the compile stage, DeepEP is protected by the much longer torch distributed timeout. The barrier is only active during the compile stage to avoid extra overhead at runtime.

2. **Send warmup requests to all DP ranks (`compile_deep_gemm.py`)**: Previously, the custom warmup stage (`warm_up_compile`) only sent a request to one rank. In the EP+DP+TP 32 case, only the first node was compiled, but the rest were not. In the actual warmup stage, requests go to each DP rank, but only the first node has cache — resulting in very different forward times that can hit the timeout even with the torch distributed barrier. The fix sends warmup requests to all DP ranks so every node compiles during the custom warmup stage.

Co-authored-by: Cheng Wan <ch-wan@users.noreply.github.com>
