```bash
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30030
```

### Router (native PD-disaggregation router)

```bash
python3 -m sglang_router.launch_router \
  --pd-disaggregation \
  --prefill http://<PREFILL_IP>:30020 8998 \
  --decode  http://<DECODE_IP>:30030 \
  --prefill-policy cache_aware --decode-policy round_robin \
  --disable-circuit-breaker \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8100
```

Then send multi-turn / prefix-reusing traffic at the router (`:8100`). Before this PR, on ROCm the first prefill HiCache write-back crashes with `RuntimeError: Destination indices must be a CUDA tensor`, and the first prefix-cache hit crashes with `Tensor match failed ... device=rocm:N`. With this PR both paths run cleanly.

## Accuracy / functional tests

- JIT HiCache module compiles and loads with hipcc on gfx942 and gfx950 (ROCm 7.2).
- ISA check on gfx950: the ROCm `load_nc`/`store_nc` emit single `global_load_dwordx2/x4` and `global_store_dwordx2/x4` with the non-temporal (`nt`) flag.
- End-to-end on a 2P1D Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4 disaggregated deployment (TP=8, HiCache `page_first` + `kernel`, `write_through`) running the AgentX v0.3 agentic trace replay at concurrency 64: warmup + 900s profiling complete (328 requests, 0 errors) with no `Destination indices must be a CUDA tensor` and no `Tensor match failed ... device=rocm:N` crashes (both crashed pre-fix on the first write-back / first prefix-cache-hit load).

## Speed tests and profiling

To check that the staged write-back path is worth keeping on ROCm (rather than degrading to `layer_first` per #28473), I ran the equivalent of the #21631 write-back micro-benchmark on **AMD MI355X / gfx950, ROCm 7.2**, comparing the installed `sgl_kernel` LF->PF kernels against the JIT staged LF->PF kernels on the same host-destination write-back workload.

Setup mirrors #21631: `dtype=bf16`, `page_size=64`, `batch_pages=64`, `total_pages=128`, timing via `triton.testing.do_bench(warmup=5, rep=25)`. Each kernel is fed indices in the residency it requires (baseline `*_lf_pf`: device `dst_indices`; staged: pinned-host `dst_indices`); correctness is verified with `torch.testing.assert_close` for every row before timing. MHA bandwidth counts `K + V`; MLA counts a single buffer. `speedup = staged_jit / sgl_kernel_lf_pf`. title: [AMD][DSV4] fix nonetype issue when enabling hicache
author: billishyahao
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Enabling hicache will hit the following issue for dsv4 unified kv triton

```
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'kv_buffer
```
This patch is to solve it through forcing `SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=tilelang` by default to avoid unimplemented error.

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/environ.py`: register `SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND = EnvStr("tilelang")` so the backend can be read/overridden through the `envs` descriptor API.
- `python/sglang/srt/server_args.py`: add `_resolve_unified_kv_hicache_compatibility()` to the `_handle_hicache` normalization
chain. When `--enable-hierarchical-cache` is set **and** `SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton`, fall back to `tilelang` with a warning, so `is_unified_kv_triton()` returns `False`, the multi-subpool layout is used, and HiCache attaches normally instead of crashing.

The override happens in `ServerArgs.__post_init__`, which runs in the main process before the memory pool / attention backend are created and before scheduler subprocesses are spawned, so the change is picked up by the subprocesses and the `is_unified_kv_triton()` `lru_cache` is not yet populated.

title: [diffusion] Fix FP8 fused TP scale loading
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

Fix fused per-tensor FP8 scale loading for diffusion tensor-parallel linear layers.

## Root Cause

ModelOpt FP8 checkpoints can store fused linear per-tensor scales as scalar tensors with shape `[1]`. For fused `MergedColumnParallelLinear` / `QKVParallelLinear` parameters, the loader previously routed the scalar through the shard-0 path only. The remaining logical scale slots stayed uninitialized, and later quantization setup used `.max()` over the fused scale buffer, which could pick garbage values and corrupt FP8 TP outputs.

## Changes

- Broadcast scalar `PerTensorScaleParameter` checkpoint tensors into every logical fused scale slot.
- Copy full fused scale vectors directly when checkpoint and parameter shapes already match.
- Add CPU unit coverage for scalar and full-vector scale loading in `MergedColumnParallelLinear` and `QKVParallelLinear`.
- Move FLUX.2 ModelOpt FP8 e2e coverage from 1GPU to a 2GPU TP consistency case: `flux2_modelopt_fp8_tp2_t2i`.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --files python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/gpu_cases.py python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/linear.py python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_parallel_linear_weight_loading.py`
- 4x H200 FLUX.2 ModelOpt FP8 smoke generate with TP4/SP1 and TP2/SP2 produced normal images after the fix.
- 4x H200 warmup/no-save repeat after the fix:
  - TP4/SP1: ~114.4 ms/denoise step, peak reserved 20844 MB
  - TP2/SP2: ~110.0 ms/denoise step, peak reserved 39248 MB
- Triggered GT generation for new `flux2_modelopt_fp8_tp2_t2i` consistency case: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/27730695244

title: fix: speculative draft worker clobbering target attention backend
author: cctry
body:
## Summary

Fix #28528 

## Root cause
### The bug

`ModelRunner._get_attention_backend()` wrote its resolved backend into the global server_args for dispatch seeing it. This is anti-pattern because it relies on correct initialization order for multiple runners in spec dec. In this buggy case,
1. Target runner init: writes the global `prefill_backend = trtllm_mla`
2. DFLASH draft runner init: overwrites the global with its own `prefill_backend = flashinfer`


### The trigger
[DeepSeek attention dispatch ](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/3e97c9239f5ccf9a7df084c081b04609d172d752/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py#L1737-L1757) decides MLA-absorbed vs materialized by looking up the attention backend, and it read that from a shared global: `get_global_server_args().prefill_attention_backend`

At serving time target's prefill dispatch to flashinfer (the draft's backend). The flashinfer has a `chunked_prefix_cache_threshold` gate which dispatch the absorbed inputs to materialized kernel when prefix shorter than 8192. So it crashed with
```
AssertionError: Unsupported head dimensions: query=576, key=576, value=512. Supported: (192, 192, 128) for DeepSeek-R1, (128, 128, 128), or (256, 256, 256) for GLM-5
```

More importantly, if draft backend is specified by `--speculative-draft-attention-backend`, [it does not override the global server args](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py#L2420-L2428) so it is free from this bug but causing inconsistency.


## Fix
Stop passing the resolved backend through the mutable global. Instead, each runner records its own resolution and the dispatch reads it per-forward:

  1. model_runner.py : `init_attention_backend` stamps the resolved prefill/decode_attention_backend_str onto the runner's own backend object (and the draft branch records its single backend for both modes).
  2. deepseek_v2.py: the dispatch reads the strings off the active forward's backend (get_attn_backend())

title: [Fix] Reuse an already-running server in bench_one_batch_server instead of forking an orphan
author: hnyls2002
body:
When `bench_one_batch_server` is run without `--base-url` against a host:port that already has a server, it still forks a second server onto the occupied port. The readiness poll is satisfied by the pre-existing server, so the benchmark proceeds, but the forked child keeps loading the model in the background, OOMs (GPU already full), and its SIGQUIT kills the whole benchmark. Whether this manifests depends on a race between benchmark duration and child startup.

Fix: probe the target host:port before forking; if a server already answers, reuse it (with a warning) instead of launching. Also fail fast if the forked server dies during startup, and kill it on timeout so it does not linger as an orphan.

title: [Fix] Return streaming logprobs when reasoning/tool parser is active
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #28456. In the OpenAI chat completions **streaming** path, log probabilities disappear entirely once a `--reasoning-parser` or `--tool-call-parser` is enabled. The reporter saw logprobs with plain content but lost them as soon as reasoning or tool parsing was active, expecting parity with vLLM.

Root cause: in `_generate_stream_content`, `choice_logprobs` was only attached in the regular-content `else` branch. When reasoning or tool calls are active, output flows through those branches instead, which never carried logprobs — so they were silently dropped.

(The non-streaming path is unaffected — `_process_response_logprobs` already attaches logprobs regardless of parser.)

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py`, `_generate_stream_content`:

- Introduce a consume-once `remaining_logprobs` token initialized to the step's `choice_logprobs`.
- Attach it to the **first** chunk emitted that step — reasoning, tool-call, or regular content — then clear it. This prevents both dropping (when reasoning/tool branches run) and duplicating (a single step can emit reasoning + content chunks).
- Flush any still-unattached logprobs on a trailing standalone chunk, covering the case where the tool-call parser consumed/buffered the delta and no content chunk was emitted.

No schema change is required — `StreamChoice` / `build_sse_content` already support a `logprobs` field.

### Notes / known limitations

- `choice_logprobs` covers all tokens generated in a step (computed from `output_token_logprobs` before reasoning/tool parsing splits the text), so logprobs are bundled per-step rather than split token-exactly across reasoning-vs-content boundaries. Clients accumulating `choices[].logprobs.content` across chunks (incl. the official `openai` SDK) still get the complete, correctly-ordered sequence. Token-exact per-segment alignment would require threading the logprob cursor through the parsers — a larger change.
- Tool-call argument logprobs are delivered on a standalone chunk rather than piggybacked on the `tool_calls` delta, to avoid invasive changes to `_process_tool_call_stream`.

## Reproducer

Self-contained unit-style reproducer that drives `_generate_stream_content` directly with a mocked `TokenizerManager`. No GPU / model download required. Two scenarios cover the two flows that lose logprobs on `main`:

1. **`reasoning`** — `reasoning_parser="deepseek-r1"`, mid-thinking chunk (no `</think>` yet) so only a `reasoning_content` chunk is yielded. On `main` that chunk has `logprobs: null`; with the fix it carries the step's logprobs.
2. **`tool-buffered`** — `tool_call_parser="qwen25"`, partial opener (`<tool_call>`) that the parser buffers and emits **no** content delta for. On `main` zero chunks are yielded → logprobs lost; with the fix a trailing flush chunk carries the logprobs.

Full script: https://gist.github.com/kpham-sgl/2210c2d967f78e052ce96c538510e6b5

### Run

```bash
curl -sL https://gist.githubusercontent.com/kpham-sgl/2210c2d967f78e052ce96c538510e6b5/raw/repro_28601.py -o repro_28601.py
python repro_28601.py
echo "exit=$?"
```

### Before fix (on `main` @ `fac11f3b`) — exits **1**

```
[reasoning] yielded 1 chunk(s); logprob-bearing: 0
  chunk[0]: data: {"id":"chatcmpl-test-reasoning",...,"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"reasoning_content":"Let me think about this."},"logprobs":null,"finish_reason":null,"matched_stop":null}]}
FAIL reasoning: BUG: logprobs missing from all chunks when reasoning_parser is active

[tool-buffered] yielded 0 chunk(s); logprob-bearing: 0
FAIL tool-buffered: BUG: logprobs missing when tool_call_parser buffers the delta

2 scenario(s) failed.
exit=1
```

### After fix (this PR) — exits **0**

```
[reasoning] yielded 1 chunk(s); logprob-bearing: 1
  chunk[0]: data: {"id":"chatcmpl-test-reasoning",...,"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"reasoning_content":"Let me think about this."},"logprobs":{"content":[{"token":"ans","logprob":-0.5,"bytes":null,"top_logprobs":[]}]},"finish_reason":null,"matched_stop":null}]}
PASS reasoning

[tool-buffered] yielded 1 chunk(s); logprob-bearing: 1
  chunk[0]: data: {"id":"chatcmpl-test-tool",...,"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"reasoning_content":null},"logprobs":{"content":[{"token":"ans","logprob":-0.5,"bytes":null,"top_logprobs":[]}]},"finish_reason":null,"matched_stop":null}]}
PASS tool-buffered

All scenarios passed.
exit=0
```

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — does not change model outputs, only which streaming chunk carries the already-computed logprobs.

title: Fix Qwen MoE precision issue with PP and all-reduce fusion
author: 1e4ves
body: ## Motivation Fixes #27744 This is a small patch to fix the Qwen MoE precision issue when pipeline parallelism is used together with tensor parallelism and FlashInfer all-reduce fusion. When all-reduce fusion is enabled, the post-expert all-reduce can be deferred and fused into the next layer's prepare_attn path. This deferred reduction is tracked by _sglang_needs_allreduce_fusion, and the marker is normally consumed by the next layer. However, at a PP boundary, hidden states are wrapped into PProxyTensors and sent to the next pipeline stage. The Python-side fusion marker is not preserved across this boundary. As a result, one pending post-expert all-reduce can be skipped entirely, which leads to larger KL drift in PP+TP runs. ## Modification This patch simply flushes the pending MoE all-reduce before returning PPProxyTensors at the PP boundary, so the deferred reduction is completed before the tensor is handed to the next PP stage. The same issue can also happen with EP, because EP also requires a post-expert all-reduce. This patch handles that case as well by flushing the pending EP all-reduce at the PP boundary. ## Testing ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. title: [Bugfix] Fix Intern-S1 FP8 expert count lookup
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

Fix Intern-S1 FP8 MoE weight loading by reading `num_experts` from `self.config.text_config`, where Intern-S1 stores the text model MoE config.

## Root cause

`InternS1Config` does not expose `num_experts` at the top level. The FP8 MoE weight-loader path passed `self.config.num_experts` into `maybe_dequant_moe_weight_scale`, so `internlm/Intern-S1-FP8` failed during `load_weights` before the server became ready.

## Validation

Validated on Verda B300, 8x NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC, container `sglang_bbuf_b300`.

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \

  --host 127.0.0.1 \

  --skip-server-warmup \
  --tp-size 8 \
  --ep 2 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --attention-backend flashinfer \
  --tokenizer-path internlm/Intern-S1
```

Before, on `origin/main` repro commit `b7ae7149e8`, model loading failed with `AttributeError: 'InternS1Config' object has no attribute 'num_experts'`.

title: [Docker] Fix cu12 dev image build: pin torch reinstall + JIT-fallback for missing x86 cubins
author: dougyster
body:
## Problem

The nightly **Build and Push Development Docker Images** workflow fails on the x86 `build-and-publish / build-x86` job at **Build and push AMD64 image (CUDA 12)** ([example run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/27727050537/job/82025624777)). arm64 and (would-be) cu13 are unaffected.

Fatal error in the `framework_final` editable-install step:

```
kernels download python
Cannot find a build variant for this system in kernels-community/sgl-flash-attn3
Available variants: torch29/210/211-cu128, torch29-cu129, torch29/210/211-cu130
→ retried 3x, exit 1
```

## Root cause (two compounding issues)

1. **Unpinned torch reinstall floated to torch 2.12.** In `docker/Dockerfile`, the cu12-only fixup does:
   ```dockerfile
   pip install --index-url .../cu${CUINDEX} torch torchvision torchaudio --force-reinstall
   ```
   With no version, it grabbed `torch-2.12.1+cu129` once 2.12 landed on the PyTorch cu129 index — diverging from the `torch==2.11.0` the `.[all]` install (and the cu13 path) use. This is the regression trigger; it's an upstream torch release leaking in, not a code change.

2. **cu129 has a cubin hole.** `kernels-community/sgl-flash-attn3` publishes **no** variant for `torch>=2.10` on cu129 (only `torch29-cu129`); `torch211` exists only for cu128/cu130, and there is no `torch212` variant at all. So even pinned to 2.11, the cu129 image cannot find a prebuilt cubin.

## Fix

1. **Pin** the cu12 torch reinstall to `torch==2.11.0 torchvision==0.26.0 torchaudio==2.11.0` (matches the rest of the build). Stops the silent 2.12 float.
2. **Make the x86 `kernels download` non-fatal**: still attempt the download (so prebuilt cubins are used when available), but fall back to **runtime JIT** when no variant matches — exactly what the aarch64 branch already does. This decouples the release build from upstream's cubin publish matrix.

Net effect on cu12 x86: ships without prebuilt `sgl-flash-attn3` cubins (JIT-compiled on first use, a few seconds once) — same behavior arm64 already ships. cu13 x86 is unchanged (its `torch211-cu130` cubin still downloads).

Note: the pinned versions mirror the `.[all]`/cu13 path and should be bumped together with any future torch upgrade.

title: [codex] Fix DSA indexer in prefill piecewise CUDA graph
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

- Skip the DSA indexer in TC piecewise prefill CUDA graph when the resolved attention backend is not `dsa`/`nsa`, matching the eager path that returns `None` when indexer metadata is unavailable.
- Add a clearer assertion if the true DSA piecewise path is entered without indexer metadata.

## Root Cause

`GLM-5-NVFP4` can be launched with the DSA model architecture but an explicit non-DSA attention backend, e.g. `--attention-backend flashinfer`. In eager mode, `Indexer.forward_cuda` asks the active attention backend for indexer metadata and returns `None` when that backend does not provide it.

The TC piecewise CUDA graph path skipped that eager metadata check to avoid Dynamo guards and always entered the split op. The split op then received `metadata=None` from the non-DSA backend and crashed in `_get_topk_ragged` at `metadata.get_page_table_64()`.

## Reproduction Before Fix

Base failure was reproduced on B300 with main commit `105e095e00`; `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/dsa_indexer.py` is unchanged between that commit and current base `bb9d31f22d`.

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path nvidia/GLM-5-NVFP4 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 32003 \
  --skip-server-warmup \
  --tp-size 4 \
  --attention-backend flashinfer \
  --enforce-disable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass \
  --cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled \
  --disable-flashinfer-autotune
```

Failure excerpt:

```text
Capture piecewise CUDA graph begin
Piecewise CUDA Graph failed with error: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get_page_table_64'
block_tables = metadata.get_page_table_64()
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get_page_table_64'
```

## Validation After Fix

Validated on 4x B300 using current base `bb9d31f22d` plus this patch with the same launch command above. The server completed piecewise prefill CUDA graph capture without adding `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled`:

```text
Capture piecewise CUDA graph end. Time elapsed: 172.86 s.
Capture piecewise CUDA graph end. Time elapsed: 173.13 s.
Capture piecewise CUDA graph end. Time elapsed: 173.64 s.
Capture piecewise CUDA graph end. Time elapsed: 173.81 s.
The server is fired up and ready to roll!
```

Smoke request:

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:32005/v1/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"nvidia/GLM-5-NVFP4","prompt":"Hello, my name is","max_tokens":16,"temperature":0}'
```

Result:

```text
POST /v1/completions HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
completion_tokens: 16
```

Additional local checks:

```bash
git diff --check
python3 -m compileall -q python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/dsa_indexer.py
python3 -m ruff check --select F821,F822,F823,E999 python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/dsa_indexer.py
```

title: Fix Kimi-VL GPU image preprocessing crash on non-RGB images
author: kflansburg
body:
The GPU image-preprocessing path for Kimi-K2.5 batches per-image tensors with `torch.cat(resized, dim=0)` in `_gpu_preprocess_images`, and stacks per-image patch tensors with `torch.cat(all_patches, dim=0)`. Both require a consistent channel dimension across the images in a request.

Only PIL inputs are RGB-normalized, via `_pil_to_cuda_chw` (`np.asarray(image.convert("RGB"))`). Pre-decoded tensor inputs keep their native channel count, so a grayscale (1-channel) or RGBA (4-channel) image -- alone, or mixed with RGB images in the same request -- raises:

  RuntimeError: Sizes of tensors must match except in dimension 0.
  Expected size 3 but got size 1 for tensor number 1 in the list.

in `_gpu_preprocess_images`, which propagates to the OpenAI serving handler as an uncaught 500 on /v1/chat/completions for every affected multimodal request.

Add `_ensure_chw_rgb`, which coerces any already-decoded (C, H, W) image tensor to 3 channels (grayscale -> repeat to 3, RGBA/other -> first 3 channels), and apply it to non-PIL inputs at both conversion sites. This guarantees a consistent channel dimension at all torch.cat sites and is a no-op for well-formed RGB inputs.

title: disaggregation: Fix FakeKVSender queue accumulation
author: kpjeeja
body:
## Motivation
 FakeKVSender.poll() only leaves KVPoll.WaitingForInput once send() has been
  called, and two paths could leave send() uncalled forever. Such a request stays on
  disagg_prefill_inflight_queue for the lifetime of the process and its KV cache lock
  is never released. To be precise about scope: this prevents stuck fake-bootstrap
  requests from accumulating and pinning KV/tree-cache resources; it does not reduce
  normal peak memory usage. Healthy requests allocate and release exactly as before.

  This is not limited to --disaggregation-transfer-backend fake: every
  FAKE_BOOTSTRAP_HOST request is served by FakeKVSender regardless of the
  configured backend, so startup warmup, /health_generate, compile_deep_gemm
  and the benchmark scripts all go through this path on a real NIXL/Mooncake
  deployment.

## Modifications

  - Override `should_send_kv_chunk()` as `num_pages > 0 or last_chunk`, matching
    `CommonKVSender`, instead of inheriting `BaseKVSender`'s `num_pages > 0`. A
    fully cached request whose last chunk carries zero pages was gated out of
    `send_kv_chunk()` entirely and could never conclude.
  - Conclude a stuck sender as `KVPoll.Failed` after a waiting timeout, so the
    scheduler aborts it and unlocks the tree cache. Same knob as the real
    backends, `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_WAITING_TIMEOUT` (default 300s), but read by
    the sender rather than off `kv_mgr` — a `FAKE_BOOTSTRAP_HOST` request on a real
    backend pairs `FakeKVSender` with that backend's `KVManager`, which defines
    `waiting_timeout` only in decode mode. The clock starts at the first poll after
    `init()`, not at `init()` itself, because nothing polls the sender while the
    request queues and computes prefill; a sender still in the bootstrap queue has
    no deadline at all.
  - Rename `FakeKVSender.init()`'s first parameter to `num_kv_indices`, matching
    `BaseKVSender.init()` and the caller, which passes a page count.

  Healthy requests are unaffected: repeated polls before `send()` keep returning
  `WaitingForInput`, and `poll()` after `send()` still concludes `Success`
  instantly.

  ## Accuracy Tests

  Not applicable — no change to kernels or model forward code.

  ## Speed Tests and Profiling

  Not applicable. The timeout only fires on a request that would otherwise never
  conclude; it adds one `time.monotonic()` per poll of an unsent sender.

  ## Tests

  - `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_fake_kv_sender.py` (new, 13 cases,
    `base-a-test-cpu`): the zero-page last chunk, the timeout and its env
    override, the manager-independent knob, the arming point, and the
    normal/abort/metric paths. The two regression cases were verified to fail
    against the pre-fix `fake/conn.py`.
  - `pytest test/registered/unit/disaggregation/` — 351 passed.
  - Prefill server on a real backend, the path this actually regressed on:
    `python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B
    --disaggregation-mode prefill --disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl` reaches
    `End of disaggregation warmup` and serves.

title: [Apple Silicon] [MLX] Fix MlxModelRunnerStub.initialize() signature desync with base
author: jlee5814
body:
## Motivation

The MLX backend fails to initialize on `main`. Every start of the MLX runner (`bench_one_batch`, `launch_server`) raises during init, before any weight load:

```
TypeError: MlxModelRunnerStub.initialize() missing 1 required positional argument: 'pre_model_load_memory'
```

from `ModelRunner.__init__` -> `self.initialize()`.

### Root cause

`MlxModelRunnerStub.initialize(self, pre_model_load_memory)` was correct when the stub was introduced (#20342). #23862 then changed the base contract: it moved `pre_model_load_memory` to an instance attribute and made base `ModelRunner.initialize(self)` parameterless. It updated the base, CUDA path, `tp_worker`, and spec workers, but not the MLX stub override, which still requires an argument the base no longer passes. The MLX path has no upstream CI, so nothing caught it.

This is the MLX-path instance of the same #23862 caller-update fan-out already addressed on
other paths (#28559, #28096, #28571 and #28583).

## Modifications

Drop the parameter so the override matches `ModelRunner.initialize(self)`. The stub never used it (it builds a
zero-GPU dummy KV cache), so this removes a dead parameter rather than changing behavior. It introduces no
new None-handling or validation path.

## Verification

- Base `self.initialize()` now matches the override; the `TypeError` no longer fires and init proceeds past
   the previously failing point.
- The model-free MLX unit test `test_metal_profiler` passes (10/10); `test_attention_patching` is unaffected.
- The change touches `model_runner_stub.py`; the base/CUDA `initialize(self)` contract is unchanged. A
   sweep of all `ModelRunner.initialize` overrides confirms this stub was the only stale one.

title: [Fix] compressed-tensors block FP8: requantize weight scales to UE8M0 for DeepGEMM on Blackwell
author: Jiminator
body:
## Motivation

Block-wise FP8 checkpoints loaded through the compressed-tensors path (`CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8`, `BLOCK` strategy) produce NaN / empty output on Blackwell (SM100), making such models unusable on Blackwell with the default GEMM backend (e.g. `poolside/Laguna-M.1-FP8`: GSM8K 0.00%, all generations empty).

On Blackwell the block-FP8 linear dispatches to DeepGEMM, which quantizes activations to UE8M0 scales and expects the weight scales to be UE8M0-packed as well. `Fp8LinearMethod` already requantizes the weight scales to UE8M0 (via `requant_weight_ue8m0_inplace`) when DeepGEMM is the active runner, but the `BLOCK` branch of `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8.process_weights_after_loading` never did — it kept the raw float32 block scales. DeepGEMM then combined UE8M0 activation scales with float32 weight scales and emitted NaN logits.

(NVFP4 is unaffected — CUTLASS path; the compressed-tensors FP8 MoE experts are unaffected — they do not dispatch DeepGEMM.)

## Modifications

- **compressed-tensors block FP8 fix.** In the `BLOCK` branch of `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8.process_weights_after_loading`, requantize the weight scales to UE8M0 when DeepGEMM is the active runner, so DeepGEMM no longer pairs UE8M0 activation scales with float32 weight scales. Non-Blackwell hardware and the `triton` / `cutlass` backends keep float32 scales unchanged.
- **Shared requant helper.** Extract the UE8M0 weight-scale requant decision into a single helper `maybe_requant_block_scale_ue8m0()` in `fp8_utils.py`, and route all three call sites through it — `Fp8LinearMethod`, `Fp8MoEMethod`, and the compressed-tensors scheme — so the gate (DeepGEMM runner selected + 128×128 block + bf16/aligned shape + not-already-UE8M0) lives in one place instead of being duplicated. This is a behavior-preserving refactor of the existing `Fp8LinearMethod` / `Fp8MoEMethod` paths.
- **Tests.** Add a registered CPU unit test `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_deepgemm_ue8m0_requant.py` (mockable; checks the requant decision fires once for a supported DeepGEMM / bf16 / 128×128 layer and skips for non-bf16 output, DeepGEMM-unsupported shape, a non-DeepGEMM runner, and non-128×128 block sizes), plus a Blackwell-only end-to-end regression test `test/manual/quant/test_compressed_tensors_fp8_block_ue8m0.py` (skips unless SM100 + DeepGEMM).

Gated by `should_deepgemm_weight_requant_ue8m0()` (requires SM100 + `DEEPGEMM_SCALE_UE8M0`), so it is a no-op on non-Blackwell hardware and non-DeepGEMM backends.

## Accuracy Tests

`poolside/Laguna-M.1-FP8`, 8×B200, `--tp 8`, default GEMM backend, GSM8K (1319, greedy):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K | 0.00% (empty output) | 92.80% |

92.80% matches the same checkpoint on H200 (FP8, 93.25%).

The added unit tests assert the weight scales are requantized to UE8M0 and that the layer output is finite and within tolerance of a bf16 dequant reference (pre-fix: NaN). Passes on B200.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No new kernels — this only fixes weight-scale preparation at load time, so the steady-state GEMM is unchanged. The fix restores the fast default (DeepGEMM) path on Blackwell; the pre-existing `--fp8-gemm-backend triton` fallback also produces correct output but is slower, so before this fix the only way to run the model produced either NaN (default) or degraded throughput (triton).

`poolside/Laguna-M.1-FP8`, 8×B200, `--tp 8`, `python -m sglang.bench_serving` (random, 1024 in / 512 out), same workload per backend:

| backend | output tok/s | total tok/s | median TTFT | median ITL | single-stream decode tok/s | single-stream TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **default (DeepGEMM)** | **1363.6** | **4088.1** | 790 ms | 20.4 ms | **103.6** | **9.59 ms** |
| `triton` | 1084.2 | 3250.4 | 826 ms | 25.7 ms | 67.0 | 14.87 ms |

The default DeepGEMM path is **+25.8%** output throughput at concurrency 32 and **+54.8%** decode throughput single-stream versus the `triton` fallback. No profiling delta is expected since no kernels change; the win is purely from using DeepGEMM instead of the triton GEMM fallback.

## Checklist

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (n/a — no user-facing API or behavior change beyond fixing the NaN)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [Bug] fix(DummyModelLoader): run post_load_weights before process_weights_after_loading
author: shuwang21
body:
## Motivation BailingMoE models (Ring-2.5-1T) crash on startup when --load-format dummy is used (reported by @ch-wan ). To reproduce: ``` sglang serve --model-path inclusionAI/Ring-2.5-1T --trust-remote-code --load-format dummy --tp 8 ``` The error message: ``` File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/models/bailing_moe_linear.py", line 1221, in post_load_weights w, scale = channel_quant_to_tensor_quant(weight, weight_scale) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py", line 1431, in channel_quant_to_tensor_quant x_dq_channel = x_q_channel.to(torch.float32) * x_s ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^~~~~ RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (512) must match the size of tensor b (2048) at non-singleton dimension 0 ``` ### Root cause: operation ordering difference **DefaultModelLoader** ([loader.py](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/f7632ef8603bf966cc2062cd45e6fd369ec83931/python/sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py#L778)): ``` model.load_weights(weights) └─ ... └─ self.post_load_weights(...) ← called at end of load_weights (bailing_moe_linear.py:1596) # after load_weights returns: process_weights_after_loading(module) ← loader.py:L799, transpose happens AFTER post_load_weights ``` `post_load_weights` sees the **untransposed** weight: ```python weight = [2048, 512] # out/tp × kv_lora_rank weight_scale = [2048, 1] # dim0: 2048 == 2048 ✓ ``` **DummyModelLoader** ([loader.py](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/f7632ef8603bf966cc2062cd45e6fd369ec83931/python/sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py#L1379), before this fix): ``` _initialize_model(...) # weight shape: [2048, 512] process_weights_after_loading(...) # transposes weight → [512, 2048] initialize_dummy_weights(model) # fills random values, shape unchanged _post_load_weights(model) # calls post_load_weights ``` `post_load_weights` sees the **already-transposed** weight ([bailing_moe_linear.py](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/f7632ef8603bf966cc2062cd45e6fd369ec83931/python/sglang/srt/models/bailing_moe_linear.py#L1218)): ```python weight = [512, 2048] # kv_lora_rank × out/tp — already transposed weight_scale = [2048, 1] # channel_quant_to_tensor_quant([512, 2048], [2048, 1]) # dim0: 512 ≠ 2048 → CRASH ``` ## Modifications Fix the operation order in `DummyModelLoader.load_model` to match `DefaultModelLoader` semantics — `_post_load_weights` must run before `process_weights_after_loading`: ``` initialize_dummy_weights(model) # fill random values while weight is still [2048, 512] _post_load_weights(model) # post_load_weights sees untransposed weight ✓ process_weights_after_loading(...) # transpose happens last, as intended ``` ## Accuracy Tests

No model output is affected. This fix only unblocks --load-format dummy, which is used for performance benchmarking (weights are random). Real weight loading via DefaultModelLoader is unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A — this is a bug fix for dummy loading only.

## Unit Tests Since this change only affects dummy-load testing and the modification is straightforward, we did not add extra unit tests. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #27835318499](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/27835318499) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #27835318308](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/27835318308)

title: [RL] fix deepseek v4 MXFP8 flashinfer_trtllm_routed MoE weight update
author: xiuhu17
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4 (MXFP8) on the `flashinfer_trtllm_routed` MoE path breaks after the
first RL weight update: `train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff` jumps from ~0.06 to
**~3.83**. Steady-state is fine — the bug is specific to the weight-reload path.

## Root cause

`align_mxfp8_moe_weights_for_flashinfer_trtllm` shuffles MoE weights/scales into
the kernel layout using row-permutation index tensors that depend only on shape,
so they're memoized in the GPU cache `_flashinfer_trtllm_shuffle_row_indices_cache_mxfp8`
(added in #21280).

These cached index tensors are GPU-resident and live in the pauseable weights memory region. On a weight update sglang releases that region's physical memory on pause and reallocates it on resume; since the cache is a plain module global outside the saved/restored static state, its tensors are left pointing at stale memory. We drop it so the indices get recomputed. 

The cachestill hits (same shape) but the contents are now garbage, so the post-update
`align` permutes the new weights with stale indices → corrupted layout → the 3.83
blowup. Affects any FP8 MoE on the flashinfer-trtllm path that goes through a
weight update, not just V4.

## Changes

1. **Bug fix** — add `clear_mxfp8_shuffle_index_cache()` in `flashinfer_trtllm.py`
   and call it from the weight-load funnel in `fused_moe_triton/layer.py`
   (`_weight_loader_impl` + `weight_loader_fused`, gated on `Fp8MoEMethod`). This
   funnel covers both the colocate and distributed/EP update paths, so the next
   `align` recomputes correct indices after any reload.
2. **V4 enablement** — implement `apply_routed_scaling_factor_on_output` in
   `hash_topk.py` (store the flag, drop the `not implemented` assert, apply
   `topk_weights *= routed_scaling_factor` in `forward`), as required by the
   routed kernel.

## Testing

5-step Pinaster/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8-4layer MXFP8 RL run (weight update before each step):

| step | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|------|------|------|------|------|------|
| `train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff` | 0.069 | 0.062 | 0.068 | 0.065 | 0.062 |

All steps healthy (~0.06), no 3.83 blowup.

title: fix(runner): size eager static buffers for prefill budget and MLP-sync autotune
author: ch-wan
body:
## Problem

The eager runner's static buffers were under-sized on two independent axes.

### 1. Token axis — the profiler hang
The prefill buffer was sized to `chunked_prefill_size`. That is the correct cap for normal chunked prefill (`PrefillAdder` admits against the remaining chunk budget), but under PP `--enable-dynamic-chunking`:
- the runtime predictor can grow a chunk toward `max_prefill_tokens`, and
- the latency profiler probes prefill at `chunked_prefill_size * 1.25`.

Both overflow the buffer — most visibly the hang at `Profiling prefill latency for dynamic chunking`.

### 2. Batch axis — autotune / load_batch at an unaligned shape
The FlashInfer autotune dummy forward runs at the eager bs ceiling `max_running_requests`, but under MLP sync the scheduler pads real batches in `prepare_mlp_sync_batch` (ceil-align to `attn_tp_size`, then to `get_cp_padding_align_size()`), and `_dummy_run` no longer re-pads. So the registry can be smaller than the padded batch `load_batch` copies in, and autotune would tune at a shape the scheduler never produces.

## Fix

- Add `ServerArgs.max_prefill_buffer_tokens()` as the single source of truth for the prefill-buffer ceiling: `chunked_prefill_size`, raised to `max(max_prefill_tokens, ceil(chunked_prefill_size * 1.25))` **only** under PP dynamic chunking (so non-dynamic configs are not over-sized). The eager runner reads it.
- Mirror the full `prepare_mlp_sync_batch` padding on the eager bs ceiling (`ceil_align` to `attn_tp_size`, then to the CP padding size) under MLP sync.

Both keep the sizing policy in server args / the runner's own ceiling rather than re-padding inside `_dummy_run`. Stacked on #28388.

title: Fix CP page filtering by request-local position
author: shihaoustc
body:
## Summary

Fix CP KV page filtering to partition pages by request-local page position instead of numeric global KV page ids.

The previous implementation assumed that pages for a request occupy a contiguous global KV page id range. That is not guaranteed: KV page ids are physical pool indices and can be non-contiguous or unordered. CP ownership should be computed over the request page sequence, then intersected with the current transfer chunk.

## Changes

- Add a helper to compute CP rank page bounds in request-local position space.
- Update `page_indices_to_cp_rank_page_indices` to slice by request position.
- Update `filter_kv_indices_for_cp_rank` to use the full request `total_pages` and intersect with `index_slice`.

title: [cookbook] drop redundant serve flags (GLM-5.2) + fix M3 page-size note
author: JustinTong0323
body:
Per Lianmin's feedback (2026-06-19): make the default arguments just work — drop hand-set serve flags where the runtime default is correct or better, instead of overriding in the cookbook.

## GLM-5.2 (`zai-org/glm-5.2.jsx`)
- `--mem-fraction-static`: keep it explicit (0.85 / 0.8 / 0.9). Earlier in this PR the flags were dropped to take the runtime auto-mfs, but verification showed the explicit values are the safer choice across the H200/B200/B300/GB300 cells, so they were put back.
- Drop `--cuda-graph-max-bs` (32/128/256 caps) — use the runtime default (512).
- `--max-running-requests`: drop on low-latency (spec defaults to 48) and high-throughput (let KV capacity bound it); keep a high 256 ceiling on balanced so KV capacity, not an artificial cap, bounds concurrency.
- Keep `--chunked-prefill-size 32768` on balanced (the dominant prefill lever).
- GB300 high-throughput keeps `env SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=512`. DeepEP's low_latency dispatch asserts `x.size(0) <= num_max_dispatch_tokens_per_rank` (deep_ep.cpp:1262, default 128). The decode cuda-graph capture builds a dummy batch of `bs` tokens per rank (not DP-split), so the 256/512 capture buckets trip the assert at default 128; GB300 (DP4) also hits bs/4 = 256 > 128 at c1024 runtime. Raising the buffer to 512 fixes both and lets HT drop `--max-running-requests`. The other HT cells (H200/B200/B300, DP8) split the batch 8 ways and the capture clamp is handled by `--max-running-requests 256`, so they need no env.

## MiniMax-M3 (`MiniMax-M3.mdx` §2.1)
Corrected the note: `--page-size 128` must stay explicit. The `fa4` backend auto-forces `page_size` to 128 only when set via `--prefill-attention-backend fa4`; the M3 recipe sets the combined `--attention-backend fa4`, whose auto-force path is not covered, so omitting `--page-size 128` would fall back to page size 1.

## Note on MiniMax-M3 flags
The M3 cells keep `--mem-fraction-static` and `--chunked-prefill-size` unchanged. Verified on 8×B200 that dropping `--mem-fraction-static` (runtime default 0.807) OOMs at the prefill piecewise cuda-graph dummy forward — these are a hard constraint of the piecewise prefill graph (needs large activation headroom), not a redundant override.

## Benchmark methodology
All GLM-5.2 speed numbers are re-measured on `main @ 09ca4fc` with real weights, `--random-range-ratio 1.0` (the bench_serving default 0.0 randomizes each request's isl/osl in [1, max], which makes runs incomparable), and `--flush-cache` per run. `sglang_version` records the commit (`main @ 09ca4fc`) rather than the release tag. Spec cells pin the EAGLE acceptance length via env so the numbers are stable and comparable across runs: low-latency (5-1-6) uses `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.5` (match-expected: 50% accept 3 / 50% accept 4), balanced (1-1-2) uses `=2` (accept 2 of 2). HT has no spec. `--load-format dummy` was verified to diverge from real weights (dummy is ~39% faster on spec cells, ~19% on HT — dummy weights skew MoE routing), so all cells use real weights.

## Verification (public GLM-5.2-FP8, main @ 09ca4fc, real weights)
- **GB300 (4×GB300, TP4)** — low-latency: c1 51 / c16 264 tok/s/GPU; balanced: c64 493 / c256 756; HT: c1024 671. HT serve verified: with `env ...=512` all 52 decode buckets capture and `health=200`; without the env the `deep_ep.cpp:1262` assert trips at the bs=512 capture bucket, so the env is required for capture (not just runtime) and the recipe does not depend on the in-flight capture-clamp PR.
- **B200 (8×B200, TP8)** — low-latency: c1 32 / c16 164; balanced: c64 342 / c256 558; HT: c1024 451. Weights read from the verda cluster-storage model cache (no download). HT keeps `--max-running-requests 256` (clamps the decode capture list to ≤32 < the 128 DeepEP buffer); no env buffer bump.
- **H200 / B300**: benchmark pending re-measurement (serve recipes are in glm-5.2.jsx; cells render "pending" until measured).
- **MiniMax-M3** 8×B200: patched command (no mfs) → OOM; original command → serve ready (1M context).

title: [Diffusion] Fix FastWan2.1 default 480p resolution
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

**This PR fixes: FastWan2.1 T2V default sampling requested `832x448`, while the `FastWanT2V480PConfig` class and model support table define the 480p landscape size as `832x480`.**

Before this PR, the default path generated at an unsupported resolution and emitted this warning:

```text
Unsupported resolution: 832x448, output quality may suffer. Supported resolutions: 832x480, 480x832
```

The fix changes the default height from `448` to `480`, and adds a regression test that checks the FastWan2.1 default `(width, height)` is included in `supported_resolutions`.

## Generated Video Comparison

Prompt:

```text
A calm cinematic shot of a red tram crossing a rainy city street at night, neon reflections on wet pavement, smooth camera motion
```

Run settings: seed `42`, `61` frames, `16` fps, `3` steps, `ion-b200` GPU4.

| Run | Size | Unsupported warning | SHA256 | Artifact |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| `main` default | `832x448` | yes | `4bbd553f7535d106ca19ecffb9301757261c7b1e749ab818280b54efd7875a45` | [main_default.mp4](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/fastwan21-resolution-validation-20260620/main_default.mp4) |
| `main --width 832 --height 480` | `832x480` | no | `64c19f1a42346c9fa535f7cfb732ca97101ea3569a266110d540d3e1386581e7` | [main_explicit_480p.mp4](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/fastwan21-resolution-validation-20260620/main_explicit_480p.mp4) |
| this PR default | `832x480` | no | `64c19f1a42346c9fa535f7cfb732ca97101ea3569a266110d540d3e1386581e7` | [pr_default.mp4](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/fastwan21-resolution-validation-20260620/pr_default.mp4) |

`main` with explicit `832x480` and this PR's default output are byte-identical, so the PR does not introduce a new generation path. It makes the default request match the already-supported 480p path.

title: [AMD] Fix Load and Inference of MLA models with Quark PTPC FP8 attention on ROCm
author: ColinZ22
body:
## Motivation

Loading and running MLA models with quark-quantized MXFP4 weights + per-token-per-channel FP8 attention (like `amd/GLM-5.2-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`) on ROCm/gfx95 fails with multiple errors.

The root cause is that the aiter gfx95 `_gfx95_quant_format="fp8"` path fuses RMSNorm + FP8 quantization into a single kernel (`fused_rms_fp8_group_quant`), passing pre-quantized **tuples** instead of plain bf16 tensors downstream. This pattern was already handled for compressed_tensors attention quantization across three prior PRs:

- **#12181** added the `apply_fp8_ptpc_linear` routing in `compressed_tensors_w8a8_fp8.py` for pre-quantized tuple inputs
- **#21403** added the `isinstance(input, tuple)` branch in `apply_fp8_ptpc_linear` itself
- **#22258** added the 3-tuple `(fp8, scale, bf16)` passthrough from `fused_rms_fp8_group_quant` in `communicator.py`, and the corresponding unwrap in `dsa_indexer._project_and_scale_head_gates`

None of these extended to **quark** attention quantization, and this PR closes that gap.

## Modifications

**`fp8_utils.py`: `channel_quant_to_tensor_quant`**  
Reshape 1D per-channel scale `[N]` -> `[N, 1]` before multiplying against the 2D weight. Quark's `kv_b_proj` has a per-channel FP8 weight with a 1D scale vector that failed to broadcast correctly against the `[N, K]` weight.

**`fp8_utils.py`: `apply_fp8_ptpc_linear`**  
Unpack pre-quantized input tuple as `input[0], input[1]` instead of destructuring, to tolerate both 2-tuples and 3-tuples (the 3-tuple was introduced in #22258 but the unpack assumed exactly 2 elements).

**`quark_w8a8_fp8.py`: `apply_weights`**  
Mirror the handling that #12181 added to `compressed_tensors_w8a8_fp8.apply_weights`, extended for quark's weight layout and both tuple formats
Note: unlike compressed_tensors which stores `shuffle(w)`, quark stores `shuffle(w).t()`, making the weight layout incompatible with `apply_fp8_ptpc_linear`/`gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle`; So we dequantize to bf16 and use the existing `apply_fp8_linear` path without requiring weight storage changes.

**`dsa_indexer.py`: `_get_q_k_bf16` and `_get_k_bf16`**  
Mirror the unwrap added in #22258 for `_project_and_scale_head_gates`, applied to the two remaining methods that also receive `x` and call `self.wk`. 

## Validation

Accuracy is evaluated using [lm_eval](https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness) on MI355X.

Model: `amd/GLM-5.2-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`

| Task  | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K | 93.93% ± 0.66% | 93.71% ± 0.67% |

## Reproduction

### Launch server

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 sglang serve \
    --model-path amd/GLM-5.2-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8 \
    --trust-remote-code --tp 8 \
    --json-model-override-args '{"qk_rope_head_dim": 64}' \
    --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
    --speculative-num-steps 5 \
    --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
    --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 \
    --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
    --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \
    --watchdog-timeout 1200 \
    --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 8}' \
    --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000
```

### Accuracy

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions \
    --model_args model=amd/GLM-5.2-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8,base_url=http://localhost:30000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=128,max_retries
  =10,max_gen_toks=2048,timeout=60000 \
    --batch_size auto --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 8
```

## Performance

Benchmarked on MI350X, tp=4, `sglang.bench_serving` random workload (1k input / 1k output, 128 prompts, concurrency 64), averaged across 5 runs.

| Checkpoint | Config | Output tput (tok/s) | Median TPOT (ms) | Median ITL (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 | EAGLE spec-decoding | 2524 | 15.74 | 14.02 |
| **amd/GLM-5.2-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8** (this PR enables) | EAGLE spec-decoding | 2721 (**+7.8%**) | 14.83 (**-5.8%**) | 13.47 (**-3.9%**) |
| amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 | No spec-decoding | 1941 | 32.63 | 32.48 |
| **amd/GLM-5.2-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8** (this PR enables) | No spec-decoding | 2187 (**+12.7%**) | 28.92 (**-11.4%**) | 28.76 (**-11.5%**) |

title: [Diffusion] Fix SANA VAE dtype and TurboWan backend selection
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

**This PR fixes: SANA used a bf16 VAE decode default where a conservative fp32 VAE path is closer to the intended Diffusers dtype semantics, and TurboWan could report/select a generic attention backend before silently replacing it with an SLA backend.**

This PR intentionally does not touch FastWan2.1 resolution handling because #28733 already fixes that mismatch.

Changes:

- Set SANA DC-AE VAE default precision from `bf16` to `fp32`.
- Resolve TurboWan sparse attention backend before the generic backend selector, so logs/profile metadata match the backend that actually runs.

## Problem Logs And Signals

SANA precision issue:

```text
Before: SanaT2I... vae_precision = bf16
After:  SanaT2I... vae_precision = fp32
```

The model-backed rerun could not be repeated in the current remote environment because the SANA snapshot was no longer available locally and outbound HF downloads were disabled. This is the exact blocker from the rerun attempt:

```text
Could not read model config for 'Efficient-Large-Model/SANA1.5_1.6B_1024px_diffusers': Could not find model at Efficient-Large-Model/SANA1.5_1.6B_1024px_diffusers and failed to download from HF Hub: Cannot find an appropriate cached snapshot folder for the specified revision on the local disk and outgoing traffic has been disabled. To enable repo look-ups and downloads online, set 'HF_HUB_OFFLINE=0' as environment variable.

ValueError: Could not get model info for 'Efficient-Large-Model/SANA1.5_1.6B_1024px_diffusers'. If using a safetensors file, please specify pipeline_class_name
```

TurboWan backend selection issue:

```text
TurboWan now only supports `sla_attn` or `sage_sla_attn` and has been automatically set to attention_type. Please set --attention-backend to `sla_attn` or `sage_sla_attn`.
```

That warning was emitted after the generic backend selector had already been asked for a backend such as `fa`. The new code resolves the TurboWan sparse backend first. For an explicit unsupported request, the warning now says which request was overridden and which sparse backend is actually used:

```text
TurboWan only supports `sla_attn` or `sage_sla_attn`; got attention_backend='fa'. Using `sage_sla_attn` from attention_type='sagesla'.
```

## SANA VAE Precision Basis

Diffusers' SANA docs distinguish the recommended transformer dtype from the text encoder and VAE dtype requirement: the docs note that the text encoder and VAE weights must stay in `torch.bfloat16` or `torch.float32` for correct model behavior. Reference: https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/main/docs/source/en/api/pipelines/sana.md#L35-L50

SGLang already keeps the SANA DiT-side precision policy separate through `precision`. This PR only moves the VAE default to `fp32`, which is the conservative decode path and avoids making the VAE follow a bf16 decode default just because the transformer can run in bf16.

## Generated Image Comparison

Historical B200 output artifacts from the earlier validation run were preserved and uploaded here:

https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/tag/diffusion-config-backend-validation-20260620

Prompt:

```text
A futuristic cyberpunk city at night
```

| Run | Output | SHA256 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `main` SANA output | [png](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/diffusion-config-backend-validation-20260620/A_futuristic_cyberpunk_city_at_night_20260616-052950_63d30a51.png) | `0166787b0c0b05bb90cef26ce0ea51e779274975570047e1b1d2ca7f60ac9173` |
| this PR SANA output | [png](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/diffusion-config-backend-validation-20260620/A_futuristic_cyberpunk_city_at_night_20260616-053112_f037a5fb.png) | `eedc04208f9fbad2cd20a3365b39a19013d3c2cfc219a38d4c24b962e2c8ff3e` |
| contact sheet | [png](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/diffusion-config-backend-validation-20260620/sana_contact.png) | `ca68ee6090ce6d792cb1ce527fccc8fe9c3d1ad0c414ca4289dd20bc7ab87835` |

![SANA comparison](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/diffusion-config-backend-validation-20260620/sana_contact.png)

TurboWan has no generated media artifact in this PR because the change is backend-resolution/log correctness: it makes the selected backend match the actually supported sparse implementation.

## Benchmark / Behavior Table

No speedup is claimed by this PR.

| Area | Before | After | Benchmark note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SANA VAE dtype | default VAE decode policy used `bf16` | default VAE decode policy uses `fp32` | Model-backed rerun blocked by missing/offline SANA cache; image artifacts above are from prior B200 validation. |
| TurboWan unsupported explicit backend, e.g. `--attention-backend fa` with `attention_type=sagesla` | generic backend could be selected/logged first, then replaced locally with Sage SLA | request is resolved to `sage_sla_attn` before backend selection | Media/latency output is not applicable because this is backend-resolution/log correctness. |
| TurboWan supported explicit backend, e.g. `sage_sla_attn` | supported, but path was less direct | preserved exactly | No output change expected. |

## Validation

Local:

- `git diff --check`
- `python3 -m py_compile python/sglang/multimodal_gen/configs/pipeline_configs/sana.py python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/attention/turbo_layer.py`

title: [diffusion] fix: restore Hunyuan3D-2 image-to-3D
author: mickqian
body:
## What

Hunyuan3D-2 image-to-3D is currently broken on `main`, and the bug slipped in
unnoticed because its e2e CI case never actually runs. This restores both.

### 1. Runtime regression — `Hunyuan3DShapeDenoisingStage._predict_noise_with_cfg`

`#23736` ("refactor cfg parallelism framework to support multi-branch CFG for
LTX2") changed the base denoising loop to call `_predict_noise_with_cfg(...,
cfg_policy=..., cfg_gate_state=...)`, but the Hunyuan3D shape override kept the
old `image_kwargs`/`pos_cond_kwargs`/`neg_cond_kwargs` signature. Every
`tencent/Hunyuan3D-2` generation crashes at the first denoising step:

```
TypeError: Hunyuan3DShapeDenoisingStage._predict_noise_with_cfg() got an
unexpected keyword argument 'cfg_policy'
```

Hunyuan3D pre-stacks `[uncond, cond]` in `prompt_embeds` and runs a single
batched forward + manual CFG combine, so it doesn't use the shared multi-branch
machinery. The fix aligns the override with the base signature (accepting and
ignoring `cfg_policy`/`cfg_gate_state`) and sources the conditioning from
`batch.prompt_embeds`.

**Validated on H200**: `tencent/Hunyuan3D-2` image-to-3D now runs end-to-end and
exports a textured `.glb` mesh (≈14.8 MB) with no crash.

### 2. Why CI didn't catch it — `diffusion_case_parser` missed guarded `.append()`

The `hunyuan3d_shape_gen` e2e case exists, but it is registered with a platform
guard:

```python
if not current_platform.is_hip():
    ONE_GPU_CASES.append(DiffusionTestCase("hunyuan3d_shape_gen", ...))
```

The diffusion partition planner extracts cases from source via AST, but only
scanned **module-top-level** `LIST.append(...)` expressions — appends nested
inside an `if` block were invisible. So `hunyuan3d_shape_gen` (and
`turbo_wan2_1_t2v_1.3b`) were never parsed, never placed in a partition, and
never ran. Adding `visit_Expr` lets `generic_visit` reach `.append()` mutations
at any nesting level.

Before: `ONE_GPU_CASES` parsed = 39, `hunyuan3d_shape_gen` absent.
After:  `ONE_GPU_CASES` parsed = 41, `hunyuan3d_shape_gen` + `turbo_wan2_1_t2v_1.3b` present.

## Test plan

- H200: ran `tencent/Hunyuan3D-2` image-to-3D end-to-end → textured `.glb` produced, no `cfg_policy` crash.
- Parser: confirmed both previously-missing cases are now collected for the `1-gpu` suite.

title: [AMD] Fix RMSNorm batch-invariance on ROCm under deterministic inference
author: yuankaichen-amd
body:
The fused `rms_norm`/`fused_add_rms_norm` kernels used by `RMSNorm.forward_hip` are not batch-invariant: the per-row normalization reduction depends on batch shape, so identical rows can produce slightly different outputs in different batch compositions. Under `--enable-deterministic-inference` this breaks batch-invariance and shows up as logprob "wobble" across batch sizes.

`forward_cuda` already guards against this by falling back to the native path in batch-invariant mode; `forward_hip` did not. Mirror the same guard so ROCm deterministic inference is actually batch-invariant.

title: [AMD] Fix int32 offset overflow in Triton decode-attention kernels
author: yuankaichen-amd
body:
The decode-attention stage1/stage1-grouped/stage2 kernels index the flat `Mid_O`/`Mid_O_1` scratch buffers using `cur_batch * stride`, where `cur_batch = tl.program_id(0)` is int32. When `max_kv_splits` is large (e.g. ceil(context_len/256) ~ 792 for long-context MLA models) and CUDA graph captures large batch sizes, so `batch * num_head * max_kv_splits * head_dim` can exceed 2**31. The int32 offset then overflows and the kernel reads/writes out of bounds, crashing CUDA graph capture with "Memory access fault by GPU".

Widen the program id to int64 at each kernel entry so offset arithmetic is computed in int64.

title: fix(schedule_batch): trim stop string when EOS matches in the same step
author: EazyReal
body:
## Motivation

`Req.update_finish_state` checked the token-based finish (EOS / stop-token-id) **before** the stop-string finish. When a single decode step accepts a stop string and an EOS token together — reachable under speculative decoding, which can accept more than one token per step — the request finished as `FINISH_MATCHED_TOKEN` and trimmed only the last token. The stop string was left in the output even though `include_stop_str_in_output=False`.

Ports the same precedence fix as vllm-project/vllm#23938.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py` (`update_finish_state`): run `_check_str_based_finish` before `_check_token_based_finish` so a stop string matched in the same step wins and `finished_len` trims past the stop string instead of after the EOS token. The vocab-boundary check still runs first to sanitize NaN/out-of-range token ids before any decode; `max_new_tokens` / grammar early-returns and `finished_len` semantics are otherwise unchanged.
- `test/registered/unit/managers/test_stop_str_speculative.py`: add `test_stop_str_wins_over_eos_in_same_step` — a step accepting both `"STOP"` and EOS must finish as `FINISH_MATCHED_STR` with `finished_len` past the stop string (fails before the fix).

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable — no change to kernels or the model forward path.

title: [Tiny] Fast fix for #28809
author: Oasis-Git
body:
#28809 folds the EAGLE-target fix into the single unified condition the BCG/PCG consolidation (#23906) left in PrefillCudaGraphRunner.__init__, which applies one rule to every backend. Pre-#23906 the two runners differed:

  BreakableCudaGraphRunner (BCG, now Backend.BREAKABLE):
    return_hidden -> FULL; EAGLE target -> FULL, EAGLE draft -> LAST
  PiecewiseCudaGraphRunner (PCG, now Backend.TC_PIECEWISE):
    return_hidden or dflash -> FULL; EAGLE -> NULL

So the unified form (1) leaves EAGLE draft prefill at NULL on breakable, but _draft_extend_for_prefill emits LAST -> can_run rejects -> eager fallback + dead captured graph (mirror of the target bug, still open on the draft); and (2) applies EAGLE target -> FULL to tc_piecewise, where PCG always captured NULL.

Branch hidden-mode selection on the configured prefill backend and reproduce each old runner verbatim.

title: [server_args] fix FA4 page_size auto-force for combined --attention-backend fa4
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Root cause
The generic FA4 `page_size→128` auto-force in `server_args.py::_handle_attention_backend_compatibility` (main, ~L3124) only checks the `prefill_attention_backend` field:

```python
# main (broken) — only checks the prefill field
if (
    self.prefill_attention_backend == "fa4"      # ← only prefill
    and not self.use_mla_backend()
    and is_sm100_supported()
):
    self.page_size = 128
```

When FA4 is set via the **combined** `--attention-backend fa4`, `prefill_attention_backend` / `decode_attention_backend` stay `None` (they are only derived later by `get_attention_backends()`, which returns a derived str and does **not** write back into the fields). So on the combined path this auto-force never fires, `page_size` falls back to its default, and FA4 is broken on non-MLA Blackwell unless the user also passes `--page-size 128` explicitly.

This is a pre-existing bug on `main` — not introduced by #27944.

## Fix
Align with the sibling `trtllm_mha` / `cutedsl_mla` checks, which already OR across all three fields:

```python
if (
    self.attention_backend == "fa4"
    or self.decode_attention_backend == "fa4"
    or self.prefill_attention_backend == "fa4"
) and not self.use_mla_backend() and is_sm100_supported():
    self.page_size = 128
```

## Tests
`TestFa4PageSizeAutoForce` covers both paths:
- `--attention-backend fa4` (combined) → `page_size` 128 (previously broken)
- `--prefill-attention-backend fa4` (explicit) → `page_size` 128 (already worked)

## Relationship to MiniMax-M3 (#27944)
M3 itself does **not** hit this bug. When M3 support was added (#27944, commit e2c0988ffa, 2026-06-12) it shipped a **localized workaround** — an M3-specific force early in the model-arch dispatch (on the #27944 branch) that uses the combined `attention_backend` field:

```python
if self.page_size is None and self.attention_backend == "fa4":   # ← combined field, sidesteps the bug
    self.page_size = 128
```

Because that workaround reads `attention_backend`, M3 forces 128 correctly whether FA4 is auto-selected or passed via `--attention-backend fa4` — which is why M3 e2e served fine despite the generic bug.

This PR fixes the **generic** bug itself, so every non-MLA Blackwell model using combined `--attention-backend fa4` benefits — not just M3.

## Timeline
add M3 (06-12, with workaround) → review M3 cookbook, find the cookbook still has to set `--page-size 128` explicitly → trace to the generic force bug → open this PR to fix the root cause.

## Scope
- `base=main`, independent of #27944 (not part of the M3 split).
- The hunk touched here (generic force ~L3181) does not overlap the M3 hunk (model-arch dispatch ~L2022), so rebasing #27944 onto a main containing this PR should be conflict-free.
- After this lands, the M3-specific force on the #27944 branch becomes redundant (the generic now covers M3 too). Keeping it is harmless (it is gated on `page_size is None`, so no spurious "128 → 128" warning); removing it is optional polish for the #27944 line, not required here.

author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

title: [codex] Fix SANA-WM CFG-parallel tensor devices
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

- Move SANA-WM scheduler tensors and denoising timesteps to the local rank device under CFG-parallel execution.
- Add focused unit coverage for scheduler tensor device migration.

## Root Cause

Under 2-GPU CFG parallel, local latents can live on rank-local devices while scheduler tensors remain on rank 0. This caused cuda:0/cuda:1 tensor mismatch during SANA-WM denoising and could later poison distributed control endpoint handling.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --files python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/model_specific_stages/sana_wm/base.py python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/sana_wm/test_pipeline_config.py`
- Remote H200 unit coverage included `TestSanaWMDenoisingStage::test_scheduler_tensors_move_to_target_device`.
- Remote SANA-WM 2-GPU CFG-parallel repro completed denoise, refiner, and decode; ffprobe reported 512x288, duration 1.0s, 8 frames.

title: [Fix][BCG][Spec] Restore EAGLE prefill plumbing dropped by #23906
author: Oasis-Git
body:
The cuda graph runner refactor (#23906) consolidated BCG and PCG into PrefillCudaGraphRunner but dropped four #25795 hooks needed for BCG+EAGLE end to end:

  * __init__: capture_hidden_mode for BCG+EAGLE — draft worker LAST, target worker FULL.
  * __init__: allocate static_draft_hidden_states buffer for BCG+draft+EAGLE (captured segments hold its address).
  * capture_prepare: pass spec_info=EagleDraftInput(hidden_states=...) aliasing the static buffer instead of spec_info=None.
  * load_batch: copy live forward_batch.spec_info.hidden_states into the static buffer before replay.

Also narrow the existing model_runner.py skip block to non-BCG so the restored target-FULL capture isn't short-circuited to eager_runner. tc_piecewise stays on the skip — it has no pre-#23906 logic to restore here, and its dead-graph capture corrupts FP4 / TRTLLM-MoE decode replay (see #28386).

Alternative to PR #28809, which only attempted the target-worker capture_hidden_mode flip, botched the tc_piecewise branch (codex P1), and dropped the skip block — reproducing the #28386 corruption end to end (gsm8k=0.0 on test_deepseek_v3_fp4_mtp_small in PR Test (Base)).

title: [Lint] Fix black formatting of DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4 MI35x tests
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Problem

The `Lint` workflow is red on `main`: [run 27930042667](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/27930042667) (triggered by #27243) fails the `black-jupyter` pre-commit hook with:

```
reformatted test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_deepseek_r1_mxfp4_tp2_mi35x.py
reformatted test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_deepseek_r1_mxfp4_tp4_mi35x.py
pre-commit hook(s) made changes.
```

Because `lint.yml` runs `pre-commit run --all-files`, a single unformatted file on `main` turns the job red on **every** push and cascades to every PR branching off `main` (fast-fails the whole `pr-test` suite).

## Root cause

PR #27243 inlined the `get_model_path()` helper into a single-line call:

```python
cls.model = os.environ.get("DEEPSEEK_R1_MXFP4_MODEL_PATH", "amd/DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4-Preview")
```

With 8-space class-method indentation this exceeds black's default 88-char line width, so `black-jupyter` (black 26.1.0, pinned in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`) wants it wrapped. `isort`/`ruff` don't enforce line length, so only `black-jupyter` catches it.

(Note: PR #27243's own lint run was already red — run 27668777918 — but the merge went through anyway, which is how the break reached `main`.)

## Fix

Reformat the two affected files with black 26.1.0:

```python
cls.model = os.environ.get(
    "DEEPSEEK_R1_MXFP4_MODEL_PATH", "amd/DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4-Preview"
)
```

Pure formatting, no semantic change.

## Verification

- `pre-commit run --files <the two files>` → all hooks Passed (incl. `black-jupyter`, `isort`, `ruff`, `codespell`, `validate registered test CI registries`)
- No runtime / forward / kernel / quant / attention code touched (test-file formatting only), so no e2e needed.

## Motivation

In `NixlKVManager.__init__`,

```py
        if self.disaggregation_mode == DisaggregationMode.PREFILL:
            # ...
            for i, queue in enumerate(self.transfer_queues):
                # ...
                threading.Thread(
                    target=self.transfer_worker,
                    args=(queue, staging_buffer),
                    daemon=True,
                ).start()
            self._start_bootstrap_thread()
```
`transfer_worker` runs `self.agent.check_xfer_state` and `_start_bootstrap_thread` runs `self.agent.add_remote_agent`. The two functions run with released GIL and race on `std::unordered_map<std::string, nixlRemoteSection> remoteSections_;` in NIXL `src/core/agent_data.h`.

There is a lock protecting `remoteSections_`, but it requires configuring the agent to use the lock
```cpp
nixlAgentData::nixlAgentData(const std::string &name, const nixlAgentConfig &config)
    : name_(name),
      config_(config),
      useEtcd_(detectEtcd()),
      needsCommThread_(useEtcd_ || config.useListenThread),
      lock(effectiveSyncMode(config.syncMode, needsCommThread_)) {
```
where the `lock` argument decides whether to actually lock. The current config is to set `syncMode` to none, meaning no locking. This results in a data race, which is hard to hit unless you have a large disagg setup. When you do, it may manifest as a segfault

title: fix(anthropic): detect-and-passthrough mid-conversation system messages
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Summary

PR #26773 fixed the hard 400 on mid-conversation `role:"system"` by hoisting every such turn into the top-level `system` field. That breaks inline-capable chat templates (GLM, Kimi, Qwen3): the rotating system reminder Claude Code emits each turn gets moved to the front, forking the prefix cache and forcing a full re-prefill every turn, and it silently rewrites the request's intended structure.

This replaces the unconditional hoisting validator with **chat-template auto-detection** (the approach vLLM converged on in vllm-project/vllm#46025): probe the template at `AnthropicServing` init; merge into the leading system block only when the template can't render mid-conversation system inline, otherwise pass the system turn through at its original position.

Detection runs in `template_detection.py` (alongside `detect_reasoning_pattern` / `detect_*_parser`), where the tokenizer is reachable. The protocol-layer `model_validator` that used to hoist is removed — it couldn't see the template. Both `/v1/messages` and `/v1/messages/count_tokens` go through the same conversion path.

Fixes #28883.

## Changes

- `protocol.py`: drop the `move_mid_conversation_system_messages` `model_validator`. The `"system"` role stays in `AnthropicMessage.role` (the correct half of #26773).
- `managers/template_detection.py`: new `detect_inline_system_support(chat_template) -> bool` — renders a `[system, user, system, user]` probe and requires the second system's sentinel text to appear in the output. Returns `False` (merge) when the template raises (e.g. a system-first guard) **or silently drops** the non-leading system turn. Explicit `import jinja2`/`jinja2.ext`/`jinja2.sandbox`.
- `serving.py`: `__init__` calls `self._merge_inline_system = not detect_inline_system_support(self._chat_template())`; `_convert_to_chat_completion_request` merges inline system into the leading block when `_merge_inline_system` is True, otherwise leaves it in place. `handle_count_tokens` reuses the same path.
- Tests: the four #26773 unit tests rewritten detection-aware (merge + passthrough), plus `TestDetectInlineSystemSupport` covering guarded / inline / silent-drop / missing-template cases.

## Why the sentinel check

A render that doesn't raise isn't proof the template renders mid-conversation system: some templates render only the leading `system` turn and silently ignore later `role:"system"` messages. The probe asserts the second system's sentinel text appears in the rendered prompt, so such templates fall back to merging instead of dropping the instruction.

## Real-world impact: Claude Code "steer" prompt

A user reported that Claude Code's mid-conversation "steer" (type a message while a tool is running, press Enter — it's queued and read after the current action completes) appeared to do nothing when the backend was `sglang:latest`. Tracing the actual `/v1/messages` body revealed three distinct failure modes across sglang versions, all stemming from how `role:"system"` messages are handled:

**1. `sglang:latest` (0.5.13.post1, pre-#26773) — hard 400.** `AnthropicMessage.role` was `Literal["user","assistant"]` with no `"system"`, so a mid-conversation `role:"system"` turn fails Pydantic validation at the route layer and the entire request is rejected with `400 Input should be 'user' or 'assistant'`. The model never sees the steer; from the user's side the feature is dead. (This also blocks the `SessionStart` hook injection, which is itself a ~40K-char `role:"system"` message listing agent types + skills.)

**2. `sglang:dev` (#26773 hoist) — prefix-cache fork.** #26773 added `"system"` to the role Literal (fixing the 400) but also added `move_mid_conversation_system_messages`, a `model_validator` that strips every `role:"system"` turn out of `messages` and concatenates its text into the top-level `system` field. The steer text reaches the model, but its mid-conversation position is lost (it becomes a leading global system instruction), and — worse for the multi-turn agent workload this feature targets — the top-level `system` now changes every turn (each steer has different text), so the radix/prefix cache is invalidated and the long tool+history prefix is re-prefilled from scratch each turn. This is the regression #28883 reported.

**3. This PR (detect-and-passthrough) — correct.** `role:"system"` stays at its original position in `messages`; the top-level `system` field is untouched, so the cached prefix remains stable across turns, and the steer is read by the model at the point the client intended (after the preceding `tool_result`, before the next assistant decision).

### Evidence (interactive Claude Code v2.1.185 trace)

Captured by patching `AnthropicServing.handle_messages` to dump the raw `/v1/messages` body, then driving a real interactive Claude Code session against `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` TP1 + EAGLE spec v2 + `--mamba-scheduler-strategy extra_buffer` on an H200 devbox.

The steer (user typed `sleep 5s` while `Bash(sleep 10)` was running) arrives on the wire as:

```json
{"role": "system", "content": "The user sent a new message while you were working:
sleep 5s

IMPORTANT: After completing your current task, you MUST address the user's message above. Do not ignore it."}
```

placed in `messages` immediately after the preceding `tool_result` — not as `role:"user"`. (A steer typed after a turn completes, with no tool in flight, does arrive as `role:"user"`; both shapes need to be handled correctly.)

Across an 11-request interactive trace, `role:"system"` turns appear at `messages` indices `[1, 4, 9]` in the raw body. With this PR applied:

| | raw `system` indices | parsed `system` indices | top-level `system` |
|---|---|---|---|
| stock `sglang:dev` (hoist) | `[1, 4, 9]` | `[]` (stripped) | grows each turn (forks cache) |
| + this PR (passthrough) | `[1, 4, 9]` | `[1, 4, 9]` (unchanged) | stable |

The model follows the steer correctly (e.g. a `continue to sleep 5s` steer issued mid-`sleep 12` is executed), and `#cached-token` stays high across turns (30K+ prefix reused), confirming the cache is preserved.

## Verification

- Unit: `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/anthropic/test_serving.py` — 59 passed.
- Detection probed against real model chat templates on an H200 devbox:
  - `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8` → passthrough ✅
  - `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` → passthrough ✅
  - `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` → passthrough ✅
  - a guarded template that `raise_exception`s → merge ✅
  - a silent-drop template (renders only leading system) → merge ✅
- e2e on GLM-5.2-FP8 TP8: mid-conversation `role:"system"` does not 400, returns correct responses (Paris / BLUE-7421), two-turn prompt-token delta small (41→68), indicating prefix reuse.
