title: [AMD] Pin cmake==4.3.4 in ROCm Dockerfile to fix MoRI gtest_discover build break
author: yctseng0211
body:
## Motivation
Both AMD nightly ROCm image builds started failing on 2026-07-11, which also
breaks the AMD PR-CI **Install dependencies** step (it reinstalls MoRI from the
Dockerfile-pinned commit). Both variants share `docker/rocm.Dockerfile`.
| Nightly image | Last green (07-10) | First red |
| ------------- | ------------------ | --------- |
| ROCm 7.0 (`release-docker-amd-nightly.yml`)        | `29093958349` | `29152576569` (07-11) |
| ROCm 7.2 (`release-docker-amd-rocm720-nightly.yml`) | `29093667269` | `29152436775` (07-11) |
### Root cause
`docker/rocm.Dockerfile` installed cmake **unpinned**
(`pip install --upgrade ... cmake ...`), so every daily build pulled the latest
cmake. Between 07-10 and 07-11 cmake drifted **4.3.4 → 4.4**. CMake 4.4's
`gtest_discover_tests` fails to parse the JSON test list of MoRI's `umbp` unit
tests (parallel discovery), aborting the MoRI cmake build:
```
.../cmake-4.4/Modules/GoogleTest/ParseTestList.cmake:96 (string): string sub-command JSON failed parsing json string ninja: build stopped: subcommand failed. CalledProcessError: Command '['cmake', '--build', '.', '-j', '128']' returned non-zero exit status 1
```
MoRI itself did not change — `MORI_COMMIT` is pinned (`e31d426...`) — so cmake is
the only differing input.
## Modifications
Pin **`cmake==4.3.4`** (last known-good) on the Dockerfile dependency-upgrade
line. Since this image is rebuilt daily and is the base for all downstream CI, an
exact pin gives reproducible builds and eliminates the version drift that caused
this break (rather than a floating range). This also protects the other in-image
cmake builds (TileLang, sgl-kernel) from the same 4.4 regression.

title: Fix --moe-a2a-backend silently ignored for LongCat-2.0 (moe_topk missing from gate)
author: whn09
body:
## Motivation

When serving **LongCat-2.0** with `--moe-a2a-backend deepep`, the flag is **silently ignored**: the model runs with `StandardDispatcher` instead of the requested DeepEP expert-parallel all-to-all.

Root cause is in `Scheduler`: `initialize_moe_config()` (the only place that sets the global `MOE_A2A_BACKEND` from `server_args`) is called only when the model config exposes one of a fixed tuple of top-k attribute names (`moe_topk_attrs`). LongCat-2.0 names its attribute **`moe_topk`** (see `configs/longcat_flash.py`), which is **not** in that tuple — note `moe_top_k` *with* an underscore is present, but LongCat uses `moe_topk` without one.

Consequently, for LongCat-2.0:
- `initialize_moe_config()` is never called → global `MOE_A2A_BACKEND` stays `None`
- `get_moe_a2a_backend()` falls back to `MoeA2ABackend.NONE` even though the user passed `--moe-a2a-backend deepep`
- `get_moe_impl_class()` sees `is_deepep()==False` → builds `FusedMoE` + `StandardDispatcher` instead of `DeepEPMoE`

So the requested DeepEP/EP backend never takes effect. (This was confirmed at runtime on H200: `get_moe_a2a_backend()==NONE`, `dispatcher==StandardDispatcher`, despite `--moe-a2a-backend deepep` and the "DeepEP MoE is enabled" log line.)

## Modifications

Add `"moe_topk"` to the `moe_topk_attrs` tuple in `Scheduler` (`python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`) so LongCat-2.0 is recognized as a MoE model and `initialize_moe_config()` runs, honoring `--moe-a2a-backend`.

## Accuracy Tests

No change to model math. The change only controls whether `initialize_moe_config()` runs; it does not alter dispatch/compute for models already recognized (all existing names are kept). Verified on 4x p5en H200 (tp16/ep16) that with this change LongCat-2.0 correctly resolves `get_moe_a2a_backend()==DEEPEP` and builds `DeepEPMoE`, whereas without it the backend was `NONE`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable to the gating fix itself. Note: enabling the DeepEP path for LongCat-2.0 (top-k=12) additionally requires UCCL/DeepEP `kNumMaxTopK >= 12` in the low-latency internode launcher; the stock value 9 will otherwise abort. That is a separate concern in the EP backend, not in this PR.

title: [UnifiedRadixCache][mamba] Fix mamba state corruption and slot leak when load_back aborts
author: Jialin
body:
## Motivation
An aborted mamba load-back silently corrupts that request's output. The mamba
LOAD_BACK transfer build allocates a CoW device slot and publishes it on
`req.mamba_pool_idx` **before** the load-back is known to proceed. When `load_back`
aborts — memory quota, insufficient eviction, or `cache_controller.load()` returning
`None` — nothing unwinds that: the request proceeds and decodes reading a slot whose
H->D copy never ran, i.e. uninitialized memory or the **previous occupant's stale
recurrent state**. Silently wrong generation, reproducing only under host-memory
pressure plus abort timing. Secondarily, the slot stays allocated until request end
(a bounded leak); the corruption is the severe half.

## Modifications
Component-specific state handling lives inside `TreeComponent` (per review feedback):
- `prepare_build_hicache_transfers(node, phase, *, req) -> PrepareTransfersResult` —
  runs before the transfer build. The mamba implementation allocates + publishes the
  CoW slot (with the evict-retry) and records it as `allocated_mamba_slot` in the
  result; the transfer build no longer allocates (it asserts the slot exists).
- `postprocess_build_hicache_transfers(req, prep, success)` — receives the prepare
  result plus whether the load went through; the mamba implementation frees the slot
  **and clears `req.mamba_pool_idx`** on failure, forcing any later path through a
  legitimate state initialization.
- `load_back` stores the results per `ComponentType` and invokes postprocess once in
  a `finally`, so every exit — the abort legs, the success path, and unexpected
  exceptions — settles the prepared state at a single site.
Note on partial success: `cache_controller.load()` is a single composite call (KV +
all aux pools) returning indices-or-None, so per-component success is not observable
at this layer; the global `success` flag matches the API. If per-pool status ever
exists, the postprocess hook is the natural seam for it.
Three tests (Full+Mamba), each verified red without the fix: quota abort and
`load()`-failure both recover the slot and clear the request reference; a request
that owned its slot before the call keeps it untouched. Full unit suite green
(`test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py`: 850 passed / 702 skipped).

## Accuracy Tests
The bug itself is an accuracy issue (decode from uninitialized/stale mamba state on
aborted load-backs); the fix removes that path. No model forward changes.

N/A — no-op hooks for non-mamba components; allocation work unchanged, only relocated.

title: [Disagg][Qwen3.5] Fix heterogeneous attn-TP scatter transfer: GDN conv sub-block slice + GQA replicated-KV head map
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

PD disaggregation of a hybrid GDN + GQA model (Qwen3.5) silently corrupts decode output when prefill and decode use different attention-TP sizes on the **scatter** direction (`prefill attn_tp < decode attn_tp`, e.g. `DEP4` prefill → `TP4` decode): gsm8k drops to ~0.44 vs 0.99 aggregation. Two independent bugs in the hetero-TP state transfer cause it:

1. **GDN `conv_state`** is `cat([q | k | v])` with each sub-block head-sharded independently, but was sliced as one contiguous `1/tp` block — decode ranks `> 0` straddle the q/k/v boundaries and get wrong channels.
2. **GQA KV with replicated heads** (`num_key_value_heads < decode attn_tp`) mapped decode rank → source head with modulo (`r % nkv`) instead of `QKVParallelLinear`'s `tp_rank // num_kv_head_replicas`, so replicated ranks fetch the wrong head.

PR #19086 fixed the head map for the gather direction only; this completes the scatter side. The same two bugs were first fixed by @lixuwei2333 in #23744 against an earlier `main` (before the disaggregation state-transfer refactor).

## Modifications

- **conv_state sub-block slice**: record `conv_shard_groups = [key_dim, key_dim, value_dim]` on `Mamba2StateShape`, plumb it per-tensor to the mooncake/nixl senders, and slice each sub-block independently in both the scatter and aggregation directions. Empty for non-GDN states, so temporal_state and all Mamba2 models keep the single contiguous slice (byte-identical).
- **GQA replicated-KV head map** (mooncake sender + staging helper), scatter branch:
  ```python
  dst_replication = max(1, dst_attn_tp_size // total_kv_heads)
  unique_dst_head_idx = dst_tp_rank_in_group // dst_replication
  src_head_start = (unique_dst_head_idx * dst_heads_per_rank) % src_heads_per_rank
  ```
  `dst_replication == 1` for equal-TP / `nkv ≥ tp`, so behavior is unchanged there.
- Add `TestDisaggregationGDNHybridHeteroTP` (prefill TP1 → decode TP4, small GDN-hybrid model).

Files: `configs/{mamba_utils,qwen3_next}.py`, `disaggregation/{base/conn,utils,mooncake/conn,nixl/conn,common/staging_buffer}.py`, `mem_cache/memory_pool.py`, and the test.

## Accuracy Tests

Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, `DEP4` prefill → `TP4` decode:

| Benchmark | Without fix | With fix |
|---|---|---|
| gsm8k (1319) | 0.44 | **0.9756** (agg 0.99, TP4→TP4 0.97) |

Applying only the conv-state fix reaches 0.58; the KV-GQA head-map fix recovers the rest.

title: Fix GLM/DeepSeek NVFP4 + flashinfer_trtllm long-context "!!!!" collapse (NaN routing)
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #30989.

Serving `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` with `--quantization modelopt_fp4 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm`, long-context requests return nothing but `!!!!!!...` (every output-token logprob is `null`, i.e. NaN). Short requests and FP8 checkpoints are unaffected.

### Root cause

`MoEGate.__init__` creates `e_score_correction_bias` as **fp32** for `modelopt_fp4`, and the FP4 moe_runner passes it **unconverted** to flashinfer's `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe` as `routing_bias` — whose documented contract requires `bfloat16` (the kernel does not validate the dtype). With an fp32 bias, flashinfer's DeepSeekV3 routing kernel emits NaN expert weights when several experts' selection keys `sigmoid(logit) + bias` are bitwise-equal and the tie group straddles the top-k boundary.

GLM-5.2-NVFP4 makes such exact ties inevitable: its bias has only 196/256 unique values (all ≈ 11.13–11.32), and on long-context tokens whose 256 router logits are all very negative, the tiny `sigmoid` contributions fall below the fp32 ulp of the ~11.3 bias and vanish in the addition — so the key collapses to a duplicated bias value → bitwise tie at the top-8 boundary → NaN. The NaN propagates to all logits; greedy argmax degenerates to token id 0, which is `!` in GLM's vocab.

This is a regression from #29783, which removed the bf16 cast for `modelopt_fp4 + flashinfer_trtllm`. The FP8 path already casts the bias to bf16 in `moe_runner/flashinfer_trtllm.py`; the FP4 path passes it raw.

### Fix

Restore the bf16 dtype for the correction bias on `modelopt_fp4 + flashinfer_trtllm` (mirrors the FP8 path). The coarse bf16 quantization (ulp 0.0625 at 11.3) spaces bias values far wider than any sigmoid contribution, so no exact tie can form. The root defect (tie-handling + missing dtype validation) belongs in flashinfer's `routingCustom`.

## Reproduction & verification

Reproduced on 4×B300 (SM 10.3), flashinfer 0.6.12, torch 2.11.0+cu130, with the exact launch command and the issue's pinned `openai/graphwalks` probe.

**Before (buggy `main`):**
```
chars=  10000  COLLAPSED  out='!!!!...!'  null_logprobs=40/40
chars=  20000  COLLAPSED  out='!!!!...!'  null_logprobs=40/40
chars=  40000  COLLAPSED  out='!!!!...!'  null_logprobs=40/40
chars=  80000  COLLAPSED  out='!!!!...!'  null_logprobs=40/40
RESULT: reproduced
```

**After (this PR):**
```
chars=  10000  ok  out='1.  **Analyze the Request:**...'  null_logprobs=0/40
chars=  20000  ok  out='The user wants me to reply with the sing'  null_logprobs=0/16
chars=  40000  ok  out='The user is asking me to reply with the ' null_logprobs=0/17
chars=  80000  ok  out='The user is asking me to reply with the ' null_logprobs=0/17
RESULT: not reproduced
```

## Checklist

- [x] Reproduced the bug and verified the fix on real hardware (4×B300, `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`).
- [x] Change is minimal and mirrors the existing FP8 path.

title: [NPU] Fix DSA top-k seed buffer shape for MTP IndexShare
author: stellaxcpeng
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
PR #29787 introduced DSA top-k seed reuse from draft-extend to avoid recomputing the DSA indexer top-k in the draft-decode loop.

The seed buffers were allocated using the CUDA-style 2D layout:

```text
[num_tokens, index_topk]
```
However, the Ascend lightning indexer and sparse attention use a 3D TND sparse-index layout:
```text
[num_tokens, index_kv_heads, index_topk]
```
For the current NPU DSA implementation, the Index KV cache uses one MQA head, so the expected NPU seed shape is:
```text
[num_tokens, 1, index_topk]
```
The incorrect buffer shape caused two startup failures during graph capture:
With speculative_num_steps=1, copying the draft-extend indexer output into the 2D seed buffer failed with a broadcast shape error.
With speculative_num_steps>1, draft-decode graph capture passed a 2D sparse_indices tensor to npu_sparse_flash_attention, which requires a 3D tensor.
This PR enables NPU to use the draft-extend DSA seed reuse feature without disabling the optimization.

## Modifications

Updated the draft-extend graph capture buffer to use the platform-native seed shape.
Updated the draft-decode graph seed buffer to use the same platform-native shape.
Updated the eager draft-extend seed buffer allocation and reallocation logic to preserve all trailing dimensions.
Added validation for missing index_topk configuration.
Kept the existing NPU Draft Extend → Draft Decode DSA top-k reuse path enabled.
The NPU middle dimension is derived from the Index KV cache contract rather than index_n_heads. index_n_heads describes the lightning indexer's query heads, while sparse attention expects the sparse-index N dimension to match the single-head MQA Index KV cache.

title: [CI] Fix CUDA 12 NVIDIA wheel cleanup
author: HanHan009527
body:
## Motivation

The CUDA 13 cleanup introduced by #29844 uninstalls every installed `nvidia-*-cu12` distribution. CUDA 12 and CUDA 13 NVIDIA component wheels can own the same paths under `site-packages/nvidia/`. For example, both `nvidia-nvshmem-cu12==3.4.5` and `nvidia-nvshmem-cu13==3.4.5` own `nvidia/nvshmem/lib/libnvshmem_host.so.3` in their wheel RECORDs.

Uninstalling the CUDA 12 distribution removes that shared file. The CUDA 13 `dist-info` metadata remains installed, so a subsequent normal dependency installation considers the CUDA 13 wheel satisfied and does not restore the missing payload. `import torch` then fails with `ImportError: libnvshmem_host.so.3: cannot open shared object file`.

Affected CI/UT jobs:

- [First environment-corrupting H20 job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/28709094411/job/85147036563): the log removes 15 CUDA 12 NVIDIA wheels, including NVSHMEM, and then fails to import torch because `libnvshmem_host.so.3` is missing.
- [Later base H20 failure](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/28758504924/job/85289402652): the same runner continues failing with the missing NVSHMEM payload.
- [Later nightly H20 failure](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/28760994711/job/85276299725): confirms that the damaged runner state persists across jobs.

## Modifications

- Snapshot every installed NVIDIA wheel as an exact `name==version` spec before removing stale `nvidia-*-cu12` wheels from CUDA 13 jobs.
- Uninstall the stale CUDA 12 wheels as before.
- Force-reinstall every remaining NVIDIA wheel at its recorded version with `--force-reinstall --no-deps` so files deleted through overlapping wheel ownership are restored.
- Preserve the existing no-op path when no stale CUDA 12 NVIDIA wheels are installed.

CUDA 13 NVIDIA package names do not use a uniform suffix: some are named like `nvidia-cublas`, while others are named like `nvidia-cudnn-cu13` and `nvidia-nvshmem-cu13`. Recording the installed non-CUDA-12 set avoids a hard-coded package mapping or a package-specific `.so` health check. Exact versions prevent accidental upgrades, and `--no-deps` avoids re-resolving or changing the dependency graph.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable. This change only repairs CI dependency installation and does not affect model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. This change does not affect inference runtime or performance.

## Test Logs

- `bash -n scripts/ci/cuda/ci_install_dependency.sh` and `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed.
- In a fresh Kubernetes Pod, we installed `nvidia-nvshmem-cu12==3.4.5` and `nvidia-nvshmem-cu13==3.4.5` into the same venv and confirmed that both wheel RECORDs own `nvidia/nvshmem/lib/libnvshmem_host.so.3`.
- **Failure reproduction:** uninstalling only the CUDA 12 wheel leaves the CUDA 13 metadata installed but removes `libnvshmem_host.so.3`. This reproduces the runner corruption.
- **Pass with this PR:** running `remove_stale_cuda12_nvidia_wheels` removes the CUDA 12 wheel, force-reinstalls the exact CUDA 13 wheel version, and leaves both the CUDA 13 metadata and `libnvshmem_host.so.3` present.
- **Pass on an already-clean environment:** running the function again finds no CUDA 12 wheel, performs no reinstall, and leaves the CUDA 13 payload intact.

No permanent test file is included because this is a narrow CI bootstrap repair. The Kubernetes validation exercised the real overlapping CUDA 12/13 wheel transition end to end.

title: [CI] Fix SGLANG_JIT_KERNEL_RUN_FULL_TESTS never activating the nightly full jit-kernel sweep
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Found while investigating the `test_custom_all_reduce.py` nightly timeout in #30999: `nightly-test-nvidia.yml` sets `SGLANG_JIT_KERNEL_RUN_FULL_TESTS: "1"` for the two "JIT kernel full unit tests" jobs, but `should_run_full_tests()` compared the raw string against `"true"` only:

```python
def should_run_full_tests() -> bool:
    return os.getenv(_FULL_TEST_ENV_VAR, "false").lower() == "true"   # "1" -> False
```

So the nightly full-sweep expansion has **never actually been active** — those jobs have silently run the same reduced grids as PR CI since they were added.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/environ.py`: register `SGLANG_JIT_KERNEL_RUN_FULL_TESTS = EnvBool(False)` in the `# SGLang CI` section, per env-var conventions.
- `python/sglang/jit_kernel/utils.py`: `should_run_full_tests()` reads it via `envs....get()` — `EnvBool` accepts `1/true/yes` (case-insensitive), and a malformed value now raises instead of silently meaning "false". Removes the last raw `os.getenv` read of this variable.
- `.github/workflows/nightly-test-nvidia.yml`: since this genuinely activates the expanded grids, give the 8-GPU nightly kernel suite an explicit `--timeout-per-file 3600`. The full custom-all-reduce sweep runs ~7x the in-CI parametrizations per world size, which cannot fit the 1200s default (measured reduced sweep on a slow H200 runner: 98s @ 2 GPUs / 209s @ 4 GPUs / ~620s @ 8 GPUs — data from #30999's logging). The 1-gpu suite keeps the default budget; job-level `timeout-minutes` are unchanged and remain the backstop.

## Heads-up for reviewers

This makes the two nightly kernel jobs actually do what their name says, so their wall-clock will increase accordingly (that was the stated intent when they were added — it just never fired). #30999 additionally scales `test_custom_all_reduce`'s per-torchrun budget when the full sweep is active, and its cache/phase-timing logs will attribute any remaining nightly timeout. If the expanded runtime turns out to be more than the nightly capacity wants to pay, dialing back is a one-line change to the job env — but that should be an explicit decision rather than a string-parsing accident.

## Validation

```
$ SGLANG_JIT_KERNEL_RUN_FULL_TESTS=1 python -c 'from sglang.jit_kernel.utils import should_run_full_tests, get_ci_test_range; print(should_run_full_tests(), get_ci_test_range([1,2,3,4,5],[1,2]))'
True [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
# 'true'/'TRUE' -> True; '0'/'false'/unset -> False; reduced range still returned in CI when unset
```

- [x] Format your code with pre-commit
- [x] Add unit tests (N/A — 3-line env-var registration + parsing fix, exercised by every jit-kernel CI job)

<!-- codex-pr-description:start -->
The SGLang runtime image now installs `libssl-dev` instead of only `libssl3`. This supplies the OpenSSL headers and linker metadata required when the HiCache native hash extension JIT-compiles at runtime.

- Replace the runtime-stage `libssl3` package with `libssl-dev`.
- Rely on `libssl-dev`'s exact-version dependency to retain the matching `libssl3` runtime library.

#### Mental model

The HiCache native hash loader compiles `hash_binding.cpp` with `torch.utils.cpp_extension.load`. That source includes `openssl/sha.h` and links `-lcrypto`, so the production image needs both the runtime library and its development files.

#### Boundaries and limitations

This only changes the CUDA production runtime image package set. It does not change hashing behavior or precompile the extension.

</details>

title: [PD] Fix optimistic prefill inflight-queue hangs on parked/aborted reqs
author: cctry
body:
## Problem

Optimistic prefill parks a request in the prefill inflight queue when its prefill finishes before bootstrap completes. Two paths never drove such requests to a terminal state, so PD prefill could hang / spin the inflight queue:

- A parked (`pending_bootstrap`) request that had already reached `KVPoll.WaitingForInput` was re-appended to the inflight queue indefinitely instead of finalizing bootstrap, sending its KV, and progressing to transfer. Aborted/failed parked requests were likewise never terminated.
- A request polling a genuinely unexpected state (e.g. a non-pending request seeing `KVPoll.Bootstrapping`) hit the fallthrough branch, which logged `warning_once` and re-queued the request forever.

## Fix

- Route parked requests through the existing `handle_pending_bootstrap` helper in `process_disagg_prefill_inflight_queue`, so they finalize, retry, or terminate deterministically (same state machine already used elsewhere).
- Replace the silent re-queue fallthrough with a hard `RuntimeError` on truly unexpected poll states, so the queue can no longer spin.
- Factor the transfer-failure handling into `handle_inflight_transfer_failure`.
- Add no-op `clear()` / `abort()` to the `BaseKVSender` interface (`BaseKVReceiver` already has them) so the success path can call `clear()` unconditionally instead of an `hasattr` guard.

## Test

Covered by `test/registered/disaggregation/test_disaggregation_optimistic_prefill.py` (`TestOptimisticPrefill`, `TestOptimisticPrefillFailure`), which exercise the retry/abort inflight paths.

Follow-up to #30951.

title: [ROCm/gfx95] Fix fp8 per-channel attention for Kimi-K2.7-code-mxfp4 o…
author: Emmanuel0612
body: ## Motivation Models with mixed quantization (mxfp4 MoE + fp8 per-channel attention, e.g. Kimi-K2.7-code-mxfp4) failed on gfx95 (MI355X) because the hardcoded `weight.dtype == float8_e4m3fn` checks in the forward pass unconditionally applied fused fp8 block-scale quantization kernels to all fp8 layers, including per-channel fp8 attention layers (QuarkW8A8Fp8) which cannot accept the resulting (fp8, group_scale[M, K/128]) tuple inputs. Root cause: per-channel fp8 layers have weight_scale shape [N, 1] (one scale per output channel), while block-scale fp8 layers have weight_scale shape [N, K/128]. The fused fused_rms_fp8_group_quant / fused_flatten_fp8_group_quant kernels are only compatible with block-scale weight layouts. Fix: add a per-channel detection guard before each fused fp8 path: weight_scale.dim() == 2 and weight_scale.shape[-1] > 1 → block-scale (use fused path) weight_scale.dim() == 2 and weight_scale.shape[-1] == 1 → per-channel (use bf16 path) This matches vLLM's behavior (VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=0) while being surgical: the optimized block-scale fused path is preserved for models that use it. ## Modifications models/deepseek_common/deepseek_weight_loader.py models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py models/deepseek_v2.py ## Accuracy Tests Validated on MI355X (gfx950) with Kimi-K2.7-code-mxfp4: Before: crashes / 79.9% accuracy (precision loss from double quantization) After: 94.7-95.3% accuracy (matches/exceeds vLLM 94.4%) ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. title: [AMD] Fix DSV4 JIT build on rocm
author: yctseng0211
body:
## Motivation

The Jul-14 scheduled Nightly Test (AMD MI355X 2N 1P1D Disagg) (run 29305625618) failed on every DeepSeek-V4 config (flash/pro × fp8/fp4 × base/dp8ep8/mtp) at scheduler init:

    utils.cuh:245: error: use of undeclared identifier 'cudaDevAttrComputeCapabilityMajor' → ninja exited with status 1 → Rank 0 scheduler died during initialization (exit code: -3)

#30438 added getSMVersion() to jit_kernel/include/sgl_kernel/utils.cuh using the CUDA-only enums cudaDevAttrComputeCapabilityMajor/Minor. The JIT path (tvm-ffi + hipcc) does not run hipify — unlike the compiled sgl-kernel, whose ROCm build hipifies cudaDevAttr* → hipDeviceAttribute* — so on gfx950 those identifiers are undeclared, the DeepSeek-V4 compress-plan JIT fails to build, and the scheduler dies. (Kimi-K2.6 doesn't build this JIT, so it was unaffected.)

## Modifications

Adopting the reviewed approach from #31141 (thanks @kangwangamd, @DarkSharpness): instead of guarding the CUDA-only calls with `#ifndef USE_ROCM`, **move `getSMVersion` out of `utils.cuh` into `runtime.cuh`**, where the `cuda*`→`hip*` attribute shims already live — so it compiles on both CUDA and HIP with no guard.

- Add the `cudaDevAttrComputeCapabilityMinor` → `hipDeviceAttributeComputeCapabilityMinor` `#define` (the Major one was already present).
- Add `get_cc_minor()` mirroring the existing `get_cc_major()`, and express `get_sm_version(id) = get_cc_major(id) * 10 + get_cc_minor(id)` to deduplicate the compute-capability queries.
- Remove `getSMVersion` from `utils.cuh`. It has **no caller in the JIT tree** (its only reference was its own definition; SM120 gating is done in Python via `is_sm120_supported()`), so there is no use-site change. No CUDA-path behavior change.

title: Fix LongCat n-gram embedding in PD-disaggregated scheduler loops
author: whn09
body:
## Motivation

The standard scheduler loop calls `_maybe_prepare_ngram_embedding(batch)` inside `get_next_batch_to_run` before `run_batch`, which fills `batch.ne_token_table` for models that use n-gram embedding (`model_config.use_ngram_embedding=True`, e.g. LongCat).

The four PD-disaggregation scheduler loops build their batch via `get_next_disagg_{prefill,decode}_batch_to_run` instead, and never call `_maybe_prepare_ngram_embedding`. As a result `batch.ne_token_table` stays `None` and the first forward crashes on every disagg TP rank:

```
# prefill
TypeError: Mismatched type on argument #7 when calling `_ngram_embedding::compute_n_gram_ids`. Expected `DLTensor*` but got `None`
# decode
TypeError: Mismatched type on argument #1 when calling `_ngram_embedding::update_token_table`. Expected `DLTensor*` but got `None`
```

Non-disaggregated serving of the same model works fine; only the PD-disaggregated path is affected.

## Modifications

- Call `self._maybe_prepare_ngram_embedding(batch)` in all four disaggregation loops — `event_loop_{normal,overlap}_disagg_{prefill,decode}` — right after the batch is selected (`self.cur_batch_for_debug = batch`) and before `run_batch`, mirroring the non-disaggregated scheduler loop.
- The method already guards with `if batch is None or not self.use_ngram_embedding: return batch`, so this is a no-op for models that do not use n-gram embedding.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable to models without n-gram embedding (no-op). For a LongCat model with `use_ngram_embedding=True`, this change makes PD-disaggregated prefill/decode run at all (it crashes at the first forward without it); the n-gram token-table preparation is identical to the already-tested non-disaggregated path.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The added call is a no-op for models that do not use n-gram embedding, and for those that do it performs the same token-table fill already done in the non-disaggregated loop.

title: fix: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-AWQ w2_weight KeyError and related params for CPU
author: nzr-niu
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

During testing, the following case failed with an incomplete inference result:
Model: `QuantTrio/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-AWQ`
Format: INT4-AWQ | TP: 6 | Input/Output: 1024/1024
The inference job crashed with the following error:
KeyError: `'model.layers.0.mlp.experts.w2_weight'`
The root cause is that the AWQ quantization method lacked explicit handling for FusedMoE layers. When a FusedMoE layer was encountered during quantization scheme assignment, no proper method was returned, causing expert weight keys (e.g., w2_weight) to be missing or unresolvable during model weight loading. This is not a regression, but an unhandled code path for AWQ-quantized MoE models.

## Modifications
1. Add layer skip check for `FusedMoE` in AWQ quantization dispatch:
Added an `is_layer_skipped_awq` check for FusedMoE layers in the AWQ quantization dispatch logic. If the target layer is found in `modules_to_not_convert`, the method now returns `None` early, skipping the quantization scheme assignment and `AWQMoEMethod `creation.

2. Replace `config.torch_dtype` with `torch.get_default_dtype()` in MoE weight initialization:
Replaced `config.torch_dtype` with `torch.get_default_dtype()` in the MoE expert weight initialization to ensure the dtype is resolved at runtime rather than derived from the model config.

## Accuracy Tests

Accuracy was evaluated using the GSM8K benchmark:
Start server
```
python -m sglang.launch_server \
      --model-path QuantTrio/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-AWQ \
      --trust-remote-code \
      --device cpu \
      --disable-overlap-schedule \
      --tp-size 2 \
      --disable-radix-cache \
      --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
      --max-total-tokens 65536 \
      --dtype bfloat16 \
      --log-requests --log-requests-level 3
```
Test
```
cd benchmark/gsm8k
python bench_sglang.py --parallel 1
```
GSM8K accuracy reaches 95%.

title: fix: skip unsafe automatic prefill graph capture
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

Prevent an automatically selected prefill CUDA graph from trying multi-bucket capture when there is insufficient physical GPU headroom after model weights, KV cache, and eager static buffers are allocated.

The gate applies only to the automatic backend selection. An explicitly chosen prefill backend remains an operator override and retains the existing behavior.

## NVIDIA Kimi-K2.7-Code result

Hardware: 8x NVIDIA H100 80GB, TP=8, `--mem-fraction-static 0.97`.

Before this change, automatic TC prefill graph capture began with only 2.05--2.28 GiB free per rank and failed to make reliable startup progress. With this change, the server logs the reason, skips automatic capture, and completes launch/serving normally.

The threshold is 4 GiB. This is intentionally conservative: the matching `.945` configuration consumes 1.75--1.79 GiB/GPU for the TC graph alone and has little remaining safety margin. This is a startup/reliability fix, not a claimed online-throughput improvement.

## Validation

- `ruff check` on changed source and test

title: Qwen3.5-MoE: support modelopt_fp4 checkpoints that quantize attention (+ load baked FP8 KV scales)
author: vroomfondel
body:
## Motivation

`#18937` ("[Qwen3.5] Enable nvfp4 checkpoint") added SGLang support for
NVIDIA's released `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4` checkpoint. That
checkpoint quantizes only the MoE experts and excludes attention
(attention ships in BF16), so the PR hard-forced `quant_config` to
`None` for the linear-attention and full-attention modules whenever
`quant_config.get_name() == "modelopt_fp4"`, and never wired FP8 KV
scale loading for attention.

That override is unconditional on the quant method name rather than
being derived from the checkpoint's own `exclude_modules`, so it also
silently forces BF16 attention on any other `modelopt_fp4` checkpoint,
including ones that deliberately quantize attention (uniform W4A4).
This was flagged in review on #18937 itself
(https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/18937#issuecomment-3931578174):

> Why hardcode quant_config=None instead of deriving it from the model
> configuration? Bypassing quantization logic at the SGLang level is
> counterproductive since NVFP4 checkpoints do not contain native BF16
> weights. Consequently, this PR breaks compatibility with the
> majority of NVFP4 models available on Hugging Face.

The author acknowledged this and said they would look at a fix
(https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/18937#issuecomment-3937106915),
but it was not addressed there. This PR is that fix.

## Modifications

1. **Allow modelopt_fp4 to quantize attention.** In
   `Qwen3_5LinearDecoderLayer.__init__` and
   `Qwen3_5AttentionDecoderLayer.__init__`, remove the hardcoded
   `quant_config = None if ... modelopt_fp4 ... else quant_config` and
   pass `quant_config` straight through. `ModelOptFp4Config`'s
   `is_layer_excluded()` already makes the correct per-prefix
   quantized/BF16 decision from the checkpoint's own
   `exclude_modules`, so the override was both unnecessary and wrong
   for checkpoints that quantize attention. For NVIDIA's MoE-only
   NVFP4 checkpoint this is a no-op: attention stays listed in
   `exclude_modules`, so `is_layer_excluded()` still returns
   `UnquantizedLinearMethod` for it and behavior is unchanged.

2. **Pass `quant_config` to `RadixAttention`** in
   `Qwen3_5AttentionDecoderLayer` (mirrors the pattern already used in
   several other models, e.g. `deepseek.py`, `apertus.py`,
   `baichuan.py`) so a checkpoint's FP8-KV quant method registers
   `k_scale`/`v_scale` parameters on it. Without this there is nowhere
   for baked KV scales to load into, so they silently default to 1.0.

3. **Load the baked FP8 KV scales in `load_weights()`** via a
   declarative `WeightsMapper` (reworked per review -- the first
   revision used a bespoke remap-and-load helper). A module constant
   `QWEN3_5_KV_SCALE_MAPPER` maps the ModelOpt checkpoint names
   `...self_attn.k_proj.k_scale` / `...self_attn.v_proj.v_scale` onto
   the RadixAttention param names `...attn.k_scale` / `...attn.v_scale`,
   and every `load_weights()` in `qwen3_5.py` (all four model classes:
   `Qwen3_5ForCausalLM`, `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`,
   `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`,
   `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration`) applies it to the incoming
   weight stream before its name-munging loop. After the rename the
   scale names contain no `k_proj`/`v_proj`, so the stacked `qkv_proj`
   shard matching (which used to consume and silently drop them) never
   fires, and they load through the loop's existing generic
   `weight_loader` fallback branch -- no custom load path. The stock
   `maybe_remap_kv_scale_name()` cannot be used here: these
   `load_weights()` strip `.self_attn` early (the sglang module tree
   has no `self_attn` level), and the helper both keys off
   `.self_attn.`/`.mixer.` still being present and checks its remapped
   name against `params_dict`, so it returns `None` in either call
   position. The mapper only renames keys that exist, so it is a no-op
   for NVIDIA's MoE-only NVFP4 checkpoint (which never emits attention
   `k_scale`/`v_scale`). `qwen3_5_mtp.py` is deliberately not covered
   (no MTP checkpoint with baked attention KV scales to verify
   against).

## Backward compatibility

All three changes are inert for NVIDIA's MoE-only NVFP4 checkpoint:
change 1 is a no-op because `is_layer_excluded()` still excludes
attention via `exclude_modules`; change 3 is a no-op because that
checkpoint does not emit `k_scale`/`v_scale` keys for attention.
Change 2 only adds a registration point on `RadixAttention` that is
unused unless a quant method is actually attached.

## Verification

These changes are ports (to clean source form) of launch-time patches verified working end to end on a DGX Spark GB10/sm121, serving a uniform-W4A4 NVFP4 checkpoint (Ornith-1.0-35B, attention AND experts quantized) through SGLang with the `flashinfer` attention backend and `flashinfer_cutlass` MoE backend:

- The checkpoint loads and serves without the previous silent drop-to-BF16 / dropped-KV-scale behavior.
- It produces coherent, on-topic completions (e.g. correctly answering "Canberra" for the capital of Australia and computing 17x24=408).
- The baked per-layer FP8 KV scales load into the runtime: the `k_scale_float`/`v_scale_float` that `Attention.forward()` reads hold the calibrated per-layer values (roughly 0.01 to 0.045 across the full-attention layers 3, 7, ..., 39), not the 1.0 fallback. (Note: SGLang's "no scaling factors provided" startup log is gated only on the legacy `--quantization-param-path` flag and is unrelated to the per-layer modelopt scales, so it is not a signal either way.)

GSM8K (chat + reasoning, 4-shot, N=400) on this checkpoint: strict == flexible = **0.9675** (387/400; 0 errors). The public, reproducible checkpoint and the full result are in the comment below. Maintainers with the NVIDIA reference checkpoint can confirm this does not regress `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4` on the MoE-only path.

**Re-verification of the `WeightsMapper` revision** (same GB10/sm121 setup, serving via launch-time application of exactly this PR's diff), now covering both an MoE and a dense model class with the two public uniform-W4A4 NVFP4 checkpoints:

- **MoE VL** ([vroomfondel/Ornith-1.0-35B-NVFP4-ModelOpt](https://huggingface.co/vroomfondel/Ornith-1.0-35B-NVFP4-ModelOpt), `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration`): loads and serves coherently; all 10 full-attention layers hold calibrated per-layer KV scales at runtime (k_scale 0.028-0.045, v_scale 0.012-0.037; verified by logging `k_scale_float`/`v_scale_float` at `process_weights_after_loading`). GSM8K: 0.9575 strict == flexible (383/400, 0 errors) vs 0.97 for the helper revision -- within sampling noise for two temp-0.6 runs.
- **Dense VL** ([vroomfondel/Ornith-1.0-9B-NVFP4-ModelOpt](https://huggingface.co/vroomfondel/Ornith-1.0-9B-NVFP4-ModelOpt), `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` -- a class the first revision did not cover): loads and serves coherently; calibrated per-layer KV scales at runtime (k_scale 0.026-0.042, v_scale 0.041-0.276). GSM8K: 0.9375 strict (375/400, 0 errors) vs 0.94 for the helper-revision baseline of this checkpoint -- within noise.

## Known limitation (not addressed here)

This PR only changes the load path (module construction +
`load_weights()`). It does **not** address
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/29577, which reports that
a text-only Qwen3.5 `modelopt_fp4` checkpoint reaches
`RadixLinearAttention.forward()` -> base `AttentionBackend.forward()`
with a `TypeError` on the `triton` attention backend, because
`model_runner.hybrid_gdn_config` does not recognize the text-only
`qwen3_5_text`/`qwen3_5_moe_text` config classes and so never installs
`HybridLinearAttnBackend`. Our own verification used the `flashinfer`
attention backend, not `triton`, so it does not exercise that path.
That is a separate, forward-path bug and needs its own fix.

Related: #29577

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit) (ran `black`, `isort`, and `ruff --select=F401,F821,UP037` on the changed file; pinned tool versions matched by hand, no `pre-commit` binary on the box used).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). Added `test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_5_modelopt_fp4.py`: CPU-only unit tests (no checkpoint, no GPU) covering all three changes -- the `ModelOptFp4Config.is_layer_excluded` attention decision, `RadixAttention` k_scale/v_scale registration, and the `QWEN3_5_KV_SCALE_MAPPER` name mapping + generic-branch load path (8 tests, passing against the installed sglang on CPU). A full end-to-end *load* test would still need a small public NVFP4 checkpoint that quantizes attention; the verification checkpoints are public ([vroomfondel/Ornith-1.0-35B-NVFP4-ModelOpt](https://huggingface.co/vroomfondel/Ornith-1.0-35B-NVFP4-ModelOpt), [vroomfondel/Ornith-1.0-9B-NVFP4-ModelOpt](https://huggingface.co/vroomfondel/Ornith-1.0-9B-NVFP4-ModelOpt)) but at ~21 GB / ~8 GB are large as CI fixtures, so that part is left to a manual / GPU-runner run.
- [ ] Update documentation (no user-facing behavior change for the checkpoints this repo currently documents).
- [x] Provide accuracy results (GSM8K, chat + reasoning, 4-shot, N=400, GB10/sm121: 0.9675 on the first revision, and 0.9575 / 0.9375 for the `WeightsMapper` revision on the 35B MoE / 9B dense checkpoints vs their 0.97 / 0.94 baselines -- see Verification). Speed was not benchmarked.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance (matched existing naming and comment density; black/isort/ruff as above).

title: Fix Ministral3 accuracy issue by aligning YaRN RoPE scaling with Transformers implementation
author: e-martirosian
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

The current YaRN RoPE scaling implementation in SGLang does not fully match the Transformers implementation. In particular, it does not handle the `mscale` and `mscale_all_dim` parameters from `rope_scaling`, which leads to different RoPE scaling behavior.

This mismatch causes accuracy degradation for YaRN-based models such as Ministral3, where SGLang generation produces significantly lower accuracy compared with the Transformers implementation.

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Modifications

Added `mscale` and `mscale_all_dim` parameters to the `YaRNScalingRotaryEmbedding` constructor to accept corresponding `rope_scaling` configuration values.
Added Transformers-compatible YaRN scaling logic ([YaRN scaling logic](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/63f32a8782cb70da3365acab16f2b67947737985/src/transformers/modeling_rope_utils.py#L412)) to recompute `mscale` when `mscale` and `mscale_all_dim` are provided.

title: [EPD] Fix HTTP dispatch lock blocking cross-request encoder batching
author: cccccya
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
Cross-request batching for the image/audio encoder was introduced in #25964. It relies on concurrent `/encode` handlers submitting requests to `EncoderScheduler.pending_queue`, allowing the scheduler worker to collect multiple requests into one batch.

After the dispatch lock introduced by #22587 was combined with the batch scheduler path, `encoder_scheduler.submit()` was executed while holding `encode_dispatch_lock`.

`submit()` waits for the request future until the entire encode operation finishes. Therefore, the first HTTP handler held the lock for the full encode duration, preventing other handlers from entering the pending queue. In practice, concurrent requests were dispatched as separate batches of size 1.

The dispatch lock is still required for the direct encode path. It ensures that the ZMQ request order observed by non-zero TP ranks matches the NCCL launch order on rank 0. However, the batch scheduler already has a single worker that serializes batch dispatches, so the HTTP handlers do not need to hold this lock while submitting requests.


## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
- Move `EncoderScheduler.submit()` outside `encode_dispatch_lock` so concurrent HTTP requests can enter the batching queue.
- Keep the lock only around the direct ZMQ dispatch and rank 0 encode path to preserve TP/NCCL ordering.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->
Not applicable. This PR does not change model inputs, preprocessing results, model forward logic, or generated outputs.
All requests in the E2E tests completed successfully with HTTP 200 responses.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

Validated with both `zmq_to_scheduler` and `Mooncake` transfer backends.

For 8 concurrent image requests:

- `zmq_to_scheduler`, encoder TP=1: `1 + 4 + 3`
- `zmq_to_scheduler`, encoder TP=2: `1 + 6 + 1`
- Mooncake RDMA, encoder TP=1: `1 + 4 + 3`
- Mooncake RDMA, encoder TP=2: `1 + 3 + 4`

All requests returned HTTP 200, with no timeout, NCCL hang, or RDMA transfer error.

title: fix: warm up Kimi VLM vision encoder at startup
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

Kimi K2.5/K2.7 uses dynamically compiled MoonViT position interpolation. The existing generic VLM warmup sends a 32x32 image, so it does not exercise a representative image shape and leaves the first customer image request paying the one-time compilation cost.

This keeps the generic 32x32 warmup unchanged, but selects a 512x512 image only for `KimiK25ForConditionalGeneration`. The server logs this decision, exercises the representative compiled position-interpolation path before it becomes ready, and leaves other VLM startup behavior unchanged.

Kimi K3 was audited separately. The current SGLang K3 implementation uses a dedicated MoonViT-family tower whose position interpolation is not wrapped in `torch.compile`; changing its warmup from 32x32 to 512x512 would increase the Vision input from 16 to 1,444 patches without evidence of the same compilation benefit. K3 therefore remains on the minimal warmup and is covered by a regression test. Any K3-specific representative warmup requires a real-weight startup/first-request A/B first.

## Cold first-image validation

NVIDIA GB300, 4 GPUs, Kimi-K2.7-Code compressed-tensors, TP4/EP4, context length 4096, DP vision encoder, FlashInfer LLM attention, FA4 Vision attention, CUDA IPC feature transport. `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill` is not passed: Kimi resolves to the automatic `tc_piecewise` prefill graph configuration (`[512, 1024, 2048, 4096]`).

The client workload is two seeded (`505`) random 512x512 JPEG requests at `request_rate=inf`, with zero client warmup. The after run uses fresh private TorchInductor and Triton cache directories, then waits for the server's new startup warmup to complete before the client is allowed to connect.

| Startup image | Mean TTFT | P99 TTFT | Request throughput |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Existing generic 32x32 warmup | 7,661.55 ms | 7,678.41 ms | 0.260 req/s |
| This PR: Kimi-only 512x512 warmup | 290.45 ms | 302.00 ms | 6.397 req/s |

This removes **96.2%** of external first-image TTFT (26.4x lower) by moving the one-time MoonViT compilation into the pre-ready startup path. It is a cold-start latency validation, not a steady-state throughput claim.

### Random image-size follow-up

On a second fresh-cache launch, the server performed the same 512x512 startup warmup, then received one seeded random JPEG request at each previously unseen resolution (zero client warmup):

| First external image size | TTFT |
| --- | ---: |
| 256x256 | 120.58 ms |
| 1024x1024 | 202.08 ms |

Neither request triggered the prior seconds-long Vision compile stall. This checks that the representative Kimi warmup covers these broader random image sizes without adding a blanket multi-shape startup cost.

## Test

- `python test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_server_warmup.py` on an NVIDIA H200 devbox (2 passed; K2.5/K2.7 selects 512x512 while K3 and Qwen retain 32x32)
- End-to-end Kimi-K2.7-Code server launch and cold first-image validation

title: [PD] Fix send_multipart blocking after prefill failure
author: amote-i
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

PR #29570 introduced RECONNECT_IVL=-1 on CommonKVReceiver's ZMQ PUSH socket alongside LINGER=0. title: Fix LongCat-2.0 real EP (deepep): double all-reduce + ScMoE RoPE crash
author: whn09
body:
## Motivation

LongCat-2.0 crashes or emits garbage under a real MoE all-to-all backend
(`--moe-a2a-backend deepep`, tp16/ep16). Two coupled bugs, both specific to the
real-EP path (no-ops when `a2a=none`):

1. **`LongcatFlashMoE.forward` double all-reduce.** `forward()` ends with an
   unconditional post-experts `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce`. Correct for
   `a2a=none` (EP-over-TP: experts are TP-sharded partial sums), but under a real
   a2a backend `self.experts` is a `DeepEPMoE` whose forward already does
   `dispatch -> run_moe_core -> combine`, and the combine reduces expert outputs
   across EP ranks. The extra TP all-reduce sums the already-combined result a
   second time → the MoE branch output is inflated ~`tp_size`× → coherent-but-garbage
   output. DeepSeek-V2 already gates the identical all-reduce via
   `should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce()`; LongCat's single MoE path never gated it.

2. **ScMoE dense-branch RoPE crash / branch-merge mismatch.** The ScMoE dense branch
   (`forward_mlp`: `mlps[0] -> self_attn[1] -> mlps[1]`) is pure TP and must run on
   replicated-full tokens (each mlp does an all-reduce; `self_attn[1]`'s RoPE needs
   full `positions`). Under a real a2a backend the moe branch scatters hidden to
   1 token/rank, so `forward_mlp` receives scattered input →
   `shape '[16,-1,64]' invalid for input of size 256` at the RoPE view, and a later
   branch-merge shape mismatch at the final norm.

## Modifications

- `LongcatFlashMoE.forward`: gate the post-experts all-reduce on
  `get_moe_a2a_backend().is_none()` so it only runs in the EP-over-TP path.
- `LongcatFlashDecoderLayer.forward_mlp`: when a real a2a backend is active, all-gather
  the dense-branch `hidden`(+`residual`) to full tokens before `mlps[0]` (helper
  `_scmoe_align_rows`), and reconcile row counts against the moe branch at the merge.
- Both paths are gated so `a2a=none` behavior is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

`meituan-longcat/LongCat-2.0-FP8`, tp16/ep16 over EFA, `--moe-a2a-backend deepep`:
- Without the fixes: server crashes at the RoPE reshape, or (with the RoPE fix alone)
  emits garbage due to the double all-reduce.
- With both fixes: coherent output on EN/ZH/math prompts (e.g. "The capital of France
  is Paris"), in both deepep `normal` and `low_latency` modes; a norm probe confirms
  the MoE branch magnitude drops from ~4–5 (inflated) back to ~1.1 (matching the
  correct `a2a=none` baseline).

- [x] Format your code according to pre-commit (isort/black/ruff all pass).
- [ ] Add unit tests.
- [x] Provide accuracy results (above).

author: whn09
body:
## Motivation

Two padded-batch shape bugs crash the LongCat-2.0 n-gram embedding path. Under
cuda-graph (or EP eager) padding, `seq_lens` / `next_token_ids` / `req_pool_indices`
are padded to the graph batch size while `batch_size` is the real request count, so
per-request tensors get indexed inconsistently.

## Modifications

1. **`update_ngram_token_table_after_sampling`** (`ngram_embedding_manager.py`):
   `out_column_starts[:batch_size] = seq_lens` and the `update_token_table` call pass
   full padded tensors →
   `RuntimeError: The expanded size of the tensor (N) must match the existing size (M)`.
   Slice `seq_lens` / `next_token_ids` / `req_pool_indices` / `out_*` to `batch_size`
   so only real requests update the table (padded rows must not pollute it).

2. **`NgramEmbedding.forward`** (`layers/n_gram_embedding.py`): the cumsum out-slice
   and the `compute_n_gram_ids` req loop are driven by `forward_batch.batch_size`, but
   `ngram_embedding_info.req_lens` / `column_starts` can be shorter in mixed/overlap
   batches → the kernel reads `column_starts` / `req_lens` out of bounds
   (`cudaErrorIllegalAddress`; async, so it surfaces at a later sync point). Clamp the
   effective batch to `min(batch_size, req_lens.shape[0], column_starts.shape[0])`.

## Accuracy Tests

`meituan-longcat/LongCat-2.0-FP8`, tp16/ep16 over EFA:
- Without the fixes: decode crashes with the expanded-size error, or an illegal
  memory access from the out-of-bounds n-gram kernel read.
- With them: the n-gram token table updates cleanly and output is correct
  (EN/ZH/math), across concurrency 1–64.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to pre-commit (isort/black/ruff all pass).
- [ ] Add unit tests.
- [x] Provide accuracy results (above).

title: [diffusion] test: fix GLM-Image AR model-path to resolve local snapshot subfolder
author: kangwangamd
body:
## Motivation

`multimodal-gen-test-2-gpu-amd` shard running `test_ar_models.py::TestGLMImage` fails every nightly, and the job runs to the 150-minute workflow timeout. The GLM-Image autoregressive sub-encoder is launched as a separate `sglang serve`, and it crashes at startup:

```
OSError: Repo id must be in the form 'repo_name' or 'namespace/repo_name':
        'zai-org/GLM-Image/vision_language_encoder/'. Use `repo_type` argument if needed.
```

### Root cause

`zai-org/GLM-Image` is an HF repo whose weights live in subfolders (`vision_language_encoder/`, `processor/`, `transformer/`, …). `ARCluster._launch_roles` builds the AR server's model path by concatenating the subfolder onto the repo id:

```python
"--model-path",   f"{self.model}/vision_language_encoder/",   # zai-org/GLM-Image/vision_language_encoder/
"--tokenizer-path", f"{self.model}/processor/",
```

A HuggingFace repo id can only be `namespace/name` — a subfolder cannot be appended (HF expects a separate `subfolder=` argument), and sglang's model-path resolution has no HF-subfolder support. So the value fails `HFValidationError`, the AR server never starts, `wait_for_server_health` times out, and `TestGLMImage` errors at setup. No GPU/HIP involved — pure HF repo-id validation.

## Modifications

Resolve the repo to a local snapshot first via `maybe_download_model(self.model)` (the same helper `test_update_weights_from_disk.py` uses), then pass the local `vision_language_encoder` / `processor` **directories** as `--model-path` / `--tokenizer-path`. A local directory path that ends in a subfolder is a valid filesystem path and bypasses repo-id validation. 1 file, +11/-2.

## Test

Verified offline on MI300X (gfx942, ROCm image v0.5.15-rocm700, GLM-Image vision_language_encoder + processor subfolders downloaded):
- **Stock** `--model-path zai-org/GLM-Image/vision_language_encoder/` → `HFValidationError: Repo id must be in the form ...` (reproduces the CI failure).
- **Patched** (local snapshot subfolder path) → no repo-id error; the AR server proceeds through config parse into weight loading: `Load weight end. type=GlmImageForConditionalGeneration, mem usage=18.99 GB` and CUDA-graph capture. The exact failure point is cleared.

cc @Makcum888e

title: fix: prevent ReqTimeStats from being dropped during IPC serialization
author: JinuJeong
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
### Problem
`queue_time` is always 0.0 in `/generate` responses even when the server is launched with `--enable-metrics`

### Root Cause
`SchedulerReqTimeStats` is propagated across two IPC hops:

1. Scheduler → Detokenizer
2. Detokenizer → TokenizerManager

The object is serialized and deserialized through `zmq.send_pyobj()` and `zmq.recv_pyobj()` at each hop.

However, `SchedulerReqTimeStats.__getstate__()` does not include enable_metrics in the serialized state. After the first deserialization in the Detokenizer, `enable_metrics` falls back to its default value of `False`.

When the object is serialized again for the second IPC hop, the following guard causes all timing fields to be dropped:
```
if not self.enable_metrics:
    return {}
```
As a result, the request timing fields are dropped before reaching the `TokenizerManager`.
The `TokenizerManager` then calculates `queue_time` using zero-initialized timestamps, resulting in `0.0`.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

Include `enable_metrics` in the serialized state returned by `SchedulerReqTimeStats.__getstate__()`.

This preserves the metrics-enabled state across both IPC hops and prevents request timing fields from being dropped before reaching the `TokenizerManager`.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

Launched the server with `--enable-metrics` and sent a request to the `/generate` endpoint.

### Before

The request timing fields were missing, and `queue_time` was always reported as 0.0.
```
{
  "meta_info": {
    "queue_time": 0.0
  }
}
```
### After

The request timing fields are preserved, and queue_time is correctly reported.
```
{
  "meta_info": {
    "forward_entry_time": 1784120656.9927032,
    "prefill_finished_time": 1784120657.1656446,
    "queue_time": 0.0002529621124267578
  }
}
```

title: fix(dsa): fail fast on fp8_e4m3 KV with tilelang DSA backend on CUDA
author: mosya415
body:
## Motivation

`--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` and the tilelang DSA backend (`--dsa-prefill-backend tilelang` / `--dsa-decode-backend tilelang`, or the deprecated `--nsa-*-backend` aliases) are each valid on their own, and on CUDA the server accepts them together. The combination is not implemented there.

The tilelang DSA sparse-attention kernel only has an fp8_e4m3 KV path under ROCm/HIP, in the `if _is_hip:` branch of `tilelang_sparse_fwd`. On CUDA the `else` branch calls `sparse_attention_fwd_kernel_v2`, whose q and kv buffers are declared with a hardcoded `dtype = "bfloat16"`, and `_forward_tilelang` hands it the raw fp8 key buffer with no dequantization. Nothing rejects this up front, so the server boots, loads the weights, allocates the KV pool, and only then dies at decode CUDA-graph capture.

This is not a rare configuration. tilelang on CUDA is used in production together with a bfloat16 KV cache, and it is also the documented recipe on ROCm, from where the same flags get copied. Switching such a deployment to fp8_e4m3 to save memory lands directly on this failure.

What the user sees today is this:

```
Exception: Capture cuda graph failed: kernel main input KV dtype expected bfloat16, but got float8_e4m3fn
Possible solutions:
1. set --mem-fraction-static to a smaller value (e.g., 0.8 or 0.7)
2. set --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode to a smaller value (e.g., 16)
3. disable decode CUDA graph by --cuda-graph-backend-decode=disabled. (Not recommended. Huge performance loss)
```

The dtype mismatch itself is stated, so the cause is recoverable by a careful reader. What is missing is the link to the flags. Neither `tilelang` nor `--kv-cache-dtype` appears in the message, so getting from "the kernel wanted bfloat16" to "my `--dsa-decode-backend tilelang` is the problem" requires knowing that tilelang compiled that kernel and that its fp8 path is ROCm only. The message also does not say which of the two flags to change, or which backends do accept an fp8 KV cache. The three suggestions printed below it are the generic advice for running out of memory during graph capture and do not apply to a dtype mismatch. On top of that the failure only appears after the full model load, so every attempt on a multi-node deployment is expensive.

Auto-resolution never selects tilelang on CUDA. For fp8 it picks `flashmla_kv` on Hopper and `trtllm` on Blackwell, and tilelang only under HIP, so this only affects an explicit backend choice.

## Verification

Both runs below are on unmodified upstream builds, so the behaviour is not affected by this patch.

Kernel level, calling `tilelang_sparse_fwd` directly on one H100, once with a bfloat16 KV cache as a control and once with fp8_e4m3, everything else identical:

```
NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, compute capability (9, 0)
driver 570.124.06, CUDA 12.8, torch 2.9.1+cu129

control, bfloat16 KV
  q       (4, 64, 576) torch.bfloat16
  kv      (4096, 1, 576) torch.bfloat16
  indices (4, 1, 2048) torch.int32
  -> returned (1, 4, 64, 512) torch.float32, no nan/inf,
     min=-0.246094 max=0.255859 mean=0.000602381

same call, fp8_e4m3 KV
  kv      (4096, 1, 576) torch.float8_e4m3fn
  -> RuntimeError: kernel main input KV dtype expected bfloat16,
     but got float8_e4m3fn
```

Server level, a DSA model on 4 nodes of 8x H100 with `--tp-size 8 --pp-size 4` and tilelang for both prefill and decode. The only change from a configuration that serves correctly is the KV cache dtype, bfloat16 to fp8_e4m3:

```
File "python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", in init_model_worker
    self.init_all_cuda_graphs()
File "python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", in init_all_cuda_graphs
    self.tp_worker.init_cuda_graphs()
File "python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py", in init_cuda_graphs
    self.init_decode_cuda_graph()
File "python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py", in init_decode_cuda_graph
    self.decode_cuda_graph_runner = graph_runners[self.device](self)
File "python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py", in capture_one_shape
    self.backend.capture_one(
File "python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_backend/full_cuda_graph_backend.py", in capture_one
    forward_fn()
File "python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py", in forward
    hidden_states = self.model(
...
File "tilelang/jit/adapter/tvm_ffi.py", in func
    executable(*tensor_list)
RuntimeError: kernel main input KV dtype expected bfloat16, but got float8_e4m3fn

Exception: Capture cuda graph failed: kernel main input KV dtype expected bfloat16, but got float8_e4m3fn
```

With this patch the same flags are refused during argument resolution, before any weights are loaded.

The kernel-level run was done on 0.5.11, where this code was still named NSA and lived under `srt/layers/attention/nsa`. The server-level run was done on 0.5.14. The kernel body and the backend resolution logic are unchanged on main, only the names and the module path moved, so the behaviour reproduces identically.

## Modifications

Adds a pure `_check_tilelang_dsa_fp8_kv(kv_cache_dtype, prefill_backend, decode_backend, *, hip)` helper in `arg_groups/overrides.py`. It raises `ValueError` when `kv_cache_dtype == "fp8_e4m3"` and tilelang is the prefill or decode DSA backend on a non-HIP platform, and points the user at `--kv-cache-dtype bfloat16` or at an fp8-capable DSA backend.

It is called from `_dsa_split_backend_resolution` once the prefill and decode backends are resolved, guarded by `is_hip()` so the working ROCm fp8 tilelang path is untouched. The check runs before the "Set DSA backends ..." log line, so the failure happens at argument resolution rather than in a half-booted server.

Adds a CPU-only unit test (`test/registered/unit/test_dsa_tilelang_fp8_validation.py`) covering the kv dtype, backend and platform matrix: CUDA with fp8 and tilelang is rejected for both prefill and decode, while HIP with fp8 and tilelang, CUDA with bf16 and tilelang, and CUDA with fp8 and a non-tilelang backend are all still allowed.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable, this is argument validation only, with no change to model outputs or kernels.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit) (black 26.1.0 + isort 7.0.0).

title: [diffusion] fix: don't self-kill diffusion worker when PID 1 is the real parent
author: Jyothirmaikottu
body:
## Motivation

`kill_itself_when_parent_died()` in `multimodal_gen/utils.py` arms `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` and then, since #30110, self-`SIGKILL`s when `os.getppid() == 1`. That check was added to cover the race where the parent dies in the `fork`→`prctl` window: the child gets reparented to init, so `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` never fires and the worker would leak.

The problem is that `os.getppid() == 1` is also true when the process **legitimately** runs as the direct child of PID 1 — e.g. when the diffusion server is the init process of a container. A bare `exec python3 -m sglang.multimodal_gen ...` entrypoint makes the server PID 1, so `run_scheduler_process()` (which calls this helper as its first line) self-kills with exit code `-9` **before loading any model**, and the server never becomes ready. The `srt` (LLM) copy of this helper has no such suicide line, so only the diffusion path is affected.

## Modifications

Capture the parent pid *before* arming `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`, then compare after:

```python
parent_pid = os.getppid()
... prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, SIGKILL) ...
if os.getppid() != parent_pid:
    os.kill(os.getpid(), signal.SIGKILL)
```

`getppid()` only changes when the real parent dies (reparenting), so this still detects the orphan race #30110 targeted — and additionally catches reparenting to a `PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER` whose pid `!= 1`, which the `== 1` check missed — without misfiring when PID 1 is the legitimate parent.

Known limitation (deliberate trade-off): a parent that dies *before* the initial `getppid()` still cannot be distinguished from being legitimately parented by PID 1 using `getppid()` alone; this favors the common container case.

## Accuracy Tests

No model-output change — process-lifecycle fix only.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No inference-path change; no perf impact.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit (black clean; comment-only + one local var, no import changes)
- [ ] Unit tests
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Accuracy/speed benchmarks (N/A — lifecycle fix)

title: [AMD][PD] Fix early-send cached-prefix KV racing the prefill forward on mori
author: Lzy17
body:
## Summary

Fixes a decode-accuracy regression from #29316 (early-send of cached-prefix KV) on the **mori** transfer backend, by adding the forward-completion synchronization that the RDMA read was missing. Early-send stays **enabled** — this is a "fix forward", not a disable.

Supersedes #31239 (which disabled the optimization globally). Thanks @cctry for pushing back on that approach and for the AMD-RDMA hint — it was correct.

## Root cause

`maybe_send_cached_prefix_chunk` issues the cached-prefix KV transfer in `run_batch` **before** the current scheduler step's forward is enqueued. Under overlap scheduling (default on; only forced off for MPS/XPU), the **prior** step's prefill forward that wrote those prefix pages can still be in flight on `forward_stream` when the transfer starts.

- **nixl** and **mooncake** are race-free by construction: they gather KV into a staging buffer on a dedicated stream and **synchronize that stream** before posting the RDMA transfer.
- **mori** posts RDMA reads **directly** from the KV pool (`send_kvcache` → `_submit_batch_transfer_plan`) with no gather and no forward-completion sync — so the read can race the still-running forward and transfer torn KV.

This is why NV backends pass while only mori regresses. It is also model-dependent: plain-MLA models (Kimi-K2.6) corrupt, while DSA models are immune because their last-chunk payload re-sends the full sequence after all writes complete.

## Fix

- `prefill.py`: in the early-send path, under overlap, record a completion event on `forward_stream` (captures the prior forward, since the current step's forward is not yet enqueued) and stash it on the KV sender.
- `mori/conn.py`: carry the event on the transfer chunk and have the transfer **worker thread** `synchronize()` on it before issuing the RDMA read.

Only the mori worker thread blocks, so overlap is preserved. Other backends ignore the stashed event.

## Validation (MI355X, 1P1D, mori, early-send ON)

GSM8K (1319Q, 8-shot), gate 0.92:

| config | accuracy |
| --- | --- |
| early-send ON, before fix | 0.888 (fail) |
| early-send OFF (optimization disabled) | 0.944 |
| **early-send ON + this fix** | **0.945 / 0.942** (two runs) |

DeepSeek-V4 unchanged at 0.926 (was already immune).

Perf (concurrency sweep, this fix vs early-send OFF baseline): throughput identical within <0.5% at every matching concurrency, median TTFT equal-or-better — the added worker-thread sync is effectively free because the prior forward has already completed by the time the mori worker dequeues the chunk.

## Test plan

- [x] Kimi-K2.6 fp8 1P1D GSM8K on MI355X (mori), early-send ON — 0.945 and 0.942
- [x] DeepSeek-V4 fp8 1P1D GSM8K on MI355X (mori) — 0.926 (no regression)
- [x] Concurrency-sweep perf vs baseline — no regression

title: Fix mamba track-boundary seqlen under overlap scheduler
author: sshleifer
body:
## Motivation

`SchedulerBatchResultProcessor._mamba_check_track_boundary` detects the per-interval mamba tracking boundary (and records `mamba_last_track_seqlen`) from `req.kv_committed_len`:

```python
if req.kv_committed_len % interval == 0:
    return True, req.kv_committed_len
```

Under the **overlap scheduler**, `prepare_for_decode` for batch N+1 runs *before* `process_batch_result` for batch N, and it increments `kv_committed_len`. So when the boundary check runs for batch N, `kv_committed_len` already carries the next batch's increment — it leads the true decode seqlen by a **jittering lookahead** in (0,1).

 Instrumenting a hybrid (mamba + sliding-window + MoE) model over ~1000 decode-boundary samples, `kv_committed_len - true_seqlen` was **1 on ~85% of steps and 0 on ~15%** (the split tracks whether a prefill batch interleaved).

Consequences: the tracking boundary fires one decode step early on most steps, and `mamba_last_track_seqlen` is recorded against a seqlen the tracked state doesn't correspond to. A later request that reuses (or donates) that tracked mamba prefix then extends from a state a cold prefill recompute would not reproduce → **wrong logprobs for that request**. It's episodic (only requests whose tracked prefix is later reused), so it surfaces as rare per-sequence output divergence under high concurrency with the mamba radix cache + overlap scheduler, while small/single-stream tests pass.

## Modification

Use the lookahead-invariant seqlen — a pure function of tokens the request has produced — matching what the forward's tracking mask used:

```python
seq_len = len(req.origin_input_ids) + len(req.output_ids) - 1
if seq_len % interval == 0:
    return True, seq_len
```

The just-decoded token is already appended to `output_ids` before this runs (`process_batch_result_decode`), so `output_ids` is non-empty and this equals the forward-N tracking seqlen. The spec-decode branch already used `req.seqlen - 1` and is unchanged.

## Test

Validated in a downstream integration: a bitwise sampler↔recompute logprob-parity RL run on a d24 hybrid (sconv + SWA + MoE) model showed sustained episodic per-sequence divergence with the original code and **exact parity** with this fix, tracking still enabled, over multiple optimizer steps at ~1000-request concurrency. Single-file change, no interface change.

title: [Bugfix] Fix min-new-token EOS handling
author: milesial
body:
## Summary

- include model-config EOS token IDs in the minimum-new-token penalty mask
- ignore missing tokenizer EOS metadata when constructing stop-token tensors
- cover model-config EOS handling when tokenizer EOS is absent

## Motivation

Requests can carry valid EOS IDs from the model configuration even when the tokenizer does not expose an EOS ID. The minimum-new-token penalizer omitted those IDs and attempted to convert `None` into an integer tensor, crashing batch preparation. Using the same request EOS set as normal finish detection avoids the crash and ensures configured EOS tokens remain suppressed until the minimum length is reached.

author: hnyls2002
body:
With `--tokenizer-worker-num > 1` and `--soft-watchdog-timeout` set, the detokenizer's `multi_http_worker_event_loop` never disables the watchdog while parked on `sock_recv` and never feeds it after processing, so the watchdog times out unconditionally every interval on a healthy pod — triggering a py-spy dump of all server processes every N seconds. title: ci: fix runner utilization report undercounting busy time ~25x
author: alisonshao
body:
## Motivation

The nightly Runner Utilization Report showed `4-gpu-h100` at 4.1% utilization while ground truth had all 4 hosts busy 26–27h out of 24 (fully saturated, 90min+ queues, 61/78 jobs waiting).

Root causes:
1. **5000-run listing cap**: the repo creates ~15–18k runs per 24h; the unfiltered newest-first listing silently dropped the oldest ~2/3 of the window while the denominator still assumed 24h coverage.
2. **Job-execution lag**: under backlog, jobs run hours after their run is created, so the surviving newest slice held mostly still-queued jobs — the busy jobs belonged to the truncated-away older runs (~33h of in-window busy time came from runs created before the window).
3. `PR States` (~25% of all runs) and other bookkeeping workflows were missing from the non-GPU skip list, wasting the API budget that motivated the cap.

## Modifications

- Server-side `created`-filtered run listing with a cursor walkdown past GitHub's 1000-results-per-filtered-query cap (`created={since}..{oldest_fetched}`, dedup by run id).
- Lookback listing (default `min(12h, hours/2)`, `--lookback-hours`) so long-queued jobs from pre-window runs contribute in-window busy time; completed runs finished pre-window are pruned without job fetches.
- Honest degradation: if the request budget still truncates, shrink the analysis window to actual coverage and add a warning banner instead of silently diluting utilization.
- Expanded non-GPU skip list; step timeout 30→55 min (~2–3x larger full-coverage fetch, ~9–10k API requests).
- 8 new unit tests (1000-cap walkdown, truncation reporting, coverage banner, pre-window job filtering).

Validated live: small-window report now shows internally consistent numbers for `4-gpu-h100` (busy time from lookback runs counted; 15 queued + 3 running, 150m max wait).

## Follow-up: fix the resulting ~110% overestimation

With truncation fixed, saturated pools reported ~110% — impossible for real runners. Verified live: when a run is re-run, the completed jobs that were NOT re-run reappear in the new attempt as brand-new job records (different job id, identical name/runner/timestamps), and `jobs?filter=all` returns every attempt, double-counting each carried-over job's busy time and pass count.

- Dedup completed job records by execution fingerprint (`run_id, name, runner, started_at, completed_at`) — id-based dedup can't work since the copies get new ids.
- Per-host busy time is now the **union** of its job intervals rather than the sum (a named runner executes one job at a time), so any remaining overlap artifact (e.g. orphaned in_progress jobs) can't push a host past 100%.

title: [AMD] Bump MoRI to f7e6ac6 to fix ROCm install_dependency build break
author: yctseng0211
body:
## Motivation
The AMD **PR Test (AMD)** `Install dependencies` step is broken on `main`. It started failing after MoRI was bumped in `docker/rocm.Dockerfile`.
- Failing run: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/29461421122 (sglang `b0b2dfb`) — `Install dependencies` fails
- Last good run: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/29415344552 (sglang `495ae9a`) — passes
Both runs use the **same** CI image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.15.post1-rocm700-mi30x-20260715`, so the only variable is the MoRI commit that `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` re-clones and rebuilds from the Dockerfile-pinned `MORI_COMMIT`.
#30706 bumped `MORI_COMMIT` `e31d426` → `6f07277`. The newer MoRI adds a `cco` module whose `src/cco/cco_init.cpp:95` uses `hipMemAllocationTypeUncached`:
```
/sgl-workspace/mori/src/cco/cco_init.cpp:95:48: error: use of undeclared identifier 'hipMemAllocationTypeUncached'; did you mean 'hipMemAllocationTypeInvalid'?
```

`hipMemAllocationTypeUncached` (0x40000000) was only added to HIP on 2025-09-11 (ROCm/hip@642cd90) and is not present in the HIP headers of the currently pinned `rocm700` CI image, so the MoRI build fails → `Install dependencies` exits 1.

MoRI has since landed a hotfix commit (`f7e6ac6`) that makes the `cco` module build against this ROCm version.
## Modifications
- Bump `MORI_COMMIT` in `docker/rocm.Dockerfile`: `6f07277` → `f7e6ac6863c53821bc7afb91a578cc6ce38fcad0` (ROCm/mori hotfix).
- Keeps the `SGLANG_MORI_COMBINE_DTYPE=fp4` feature from #30706 working, unlike a plain revert of the pin.
