title: Fix dropped Inkling reasoning at stream end
author: ispobock
body:
## Motivation

With `stream_reasoning=False`, the Inkling reasoning detector buffers the thinking block into `_pending_reasoning` and only flushes it when a control/end token closes the block. When generation is cut mid-block (e.g. `max_tokens` truncates a `<|content_thinking|>` block), the stream ends with no end token, so the buffered trace is dropped entirely — the whole reasoning disappears from the streamed response.

The non-streaming `detect_and_parse` path already flushes `_pending_reasoning` at the end, but `InklingDetector` had no `finish()` override, so at stream end `parse_stream_end()` fell through to the base `finish()` (which only handles `_force_nonempty_content`/`_in_reasoning`, neither used by this detector) and emitted nothing.

## Modifications

- Override `InklingDetector.finish()` to emit any buffered `_pending_reasoning` (when mid-reasoning under `stream_reasoning=False`) and reset the detector's block state, mirroring the non-streaming flush.
- Add a regression test that streams a thinking block truncated before its end token and asserts `finish()` surfaces the trailing reasoning (fails on the pre-fix code, passes after).

Verified on a live server that BFCL live tool-calling accuracy is unchanged (`tool_parse_errors=0`), i.e. the added stream-end flush does not perturb the tool-call path.

title: [Fix][AMD] Qwen3.5 MoE: disable global-slot shared-expert fusion under per-rank EP backends (MoRI + dp-attention init crash)
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #31336.

Serving **Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8** (512 routed + 1 fused shared expert) with `--moe-a2a-backend mori --enable-dp-attention` on MI355X/ROCm crashes at model init. Every scheduler rank aborts in `FusedMoE.__init__`:

```
File ".../srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py", line 227, ...
    assert (num_experts - num_shared_slots) % self.moe_ep_size == 0
AssertionError
```

With `--enable-dp-attention`, `moe_ep_size` is promoted to `tp_size` (8). `has_per_rank_fused_shared_slots()` is `True` for MoRI (deepep-class), so `num_shared_slots = 1 * 8 = 8`, and `(513 - 8) % 8 = 505 % 8 = 1 != 0`.

### Root cause (and why the layout matters)

MoRI's dispatcher (`token_dispatcher/moriep.py`) masks experts with a **contiguous per-rank block**: `expert_mask[ep_rank * num_local_experts : + num_local_experts] = 1`. This is valid only when the blocks tile the id space exactly, i.e. `num_experts == num_local_experts * ep_size`, which requires **per-rank** shared slots (one shared slot per EP rank). DeepSeek-V2 already builds `num_experts` this way for per-rank backends.

Qwen's shared-expert fusion, however, is a **global-slot** design: `Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock` constructs its `TopK` **without** `num_fused_shared_experts` (so the per-rank remap in `topk.py` never fires) and instead appends the shared expert manually at a **single global id** (`_append_shared_to_topk_output`, base id `N == num_experts`) with a **per-token `shared_expert_gate`**. This global-slot-with-gate layout cannot be expressed in MoRI's per-rank contiguous tiling, and it can't reuse DeepSeek's (gate-less) per-rank remap machinery.

The alternative floated in the issue — treating MoRI as "global" (`num_shared_slots = 1`) — passes the `__init__` assertion but then breaks MoRI's contiguous dispatch mask (`num_local_experts * ep_size = 65 * 8 = 520 != 513`, so rank 7's block runs out of bounds) and silently misroutes experts.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2_moe.py`: when shared-expert fusion is enabled **and** a per-rank EP shared-slot backend is active (`uses_per_rank_fused_shared_slots()`) **and** `moe_ep_size > 1`, disable the fusion and fall back to the separate (correct) shared-expert MLP path. A one-time warning is logged. `moe_ep_size == 1` and non-per-rank backends are unaffected (fusion stays on).

This is the correct-by-construction fix: with fusion off, `num_experts = 512` tiles exactly (`64 * 8`), the shared expert is computed by the dense `shared_expert` MLP (with its gate) and added after the experts. The fully-fused per-rank shared expert with a per-token gate is a larger enablement task (needs a per-rank remap+append kernel that also applies the gate) and is left as follow-up.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K sweep on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 (MI355X), **with this PR applied** so the MoRI configs get past the #31336 init crash. Flags added one at a time. `Accuracy` = correct fraction, `Invalid` = unparseable/garbage fraction.

```
┌─────┬───────────────────────────────────────────┬──────────┬─────────┬───────────────┐
│ Run │                Added flag                 │ Accuracy │ Invalid │    Verdict    │
├─────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────┼─────────┼───────────────┤
│ R0  │ (baseline)                                │    0.925 │   0.005 │ ✓             │
├─────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────┼─────────┼───────────────┤
│ R1  │ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3                 │    0.915 │   0.010 │ clean         │
├─────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────┼─────────┼───────────────┤
│ R2  │ --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head │    0.935 │   0.000 │ clean         │
├─────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────┼─────────┼───────────────┤
│ R3  │ --moe-a2a-backend mori                    │    0.010 │   0.420 │ ← breaks      │
├─────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────┼─────────┼───────────────┤
│ R4  │ mori + fp8-KV                             │    0.010 │   0.455 │ breaks (mori) │
├─────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────┼─────────┼───────────────┤
│ R5  │ full (dp-attn + mori + fp8-KV)            │    0.000 │   0.415 │ breaks (mori) │
└─────┴───────────────────────────────────────────┴──────────┴─────────┴───────────────┘
```

Reading:
- **This PR's scope (init crash) is resolved:** the MoRI + dp-attention configs now load and run instead of aborting in `FusedMoE.__init__`.
- **No regression on the clean paths:** baseline (R0), fp8-KV (R1), and `--enable-dp-attention` alone (R2, **0.935**) are all healthy. R2 is the path this PR most directly enables and it is clean.
- **A separate MoRI issue remains:** every run that adds `--moe-a2a-backend mori` (R3/R4/R5) collapses to ~0.01 accuracy with a high invalid rate, **independent of dp-attention and of fp8-KV**. That is a MoRI all-to-all correctness problem, **out of scope for this init-crash fix** and tracked separately (likely part of the ROCm-MoRI enablement in #21886). This PR is a prerequisite that lets that issue be reached and debugged at all.

Assertion-level validation (mocked MoRI, `ep_size=8`): pre-fix `num_experts=513, num_shared_slots=8` → assertion fails; with fix, fusion disabled → `num_experts=512, num_shared_slots=0` → assertion passes and MoRI's contiguous mask tiles `[0, 512)` exactly. `ep_size==1` and non-per-rank backends keep fusion (no behavior change).

## Checklist

- [x] Linked the issue (#31336)
- [x] Added a clear explanation of the root cause and the tradeoff

title: [AMD][Fix] Qwen3.5: guard zero-grid launch in fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm(_with_gate) (HIP invalid configuration on idle DP rank)
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

Bringing up **Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8** with MoRI expert-parallel all-to-all (`--moe-a2a-backend mori`) and `--enable-dp-attention` on MI355X/ROCm surfaces three connected failures. This PR fixes the two that live in the model / idle-rank path (bug #2 and bug #3 below); bug #1 is the prerequisite init fix already handled in #31793.

**Bug #1 — Qwen shared-expert fusion vs. per-rank EP layout (prerequisite, fixed in #31793).** Qwen uses a single global shared-expert slot with a per-token gate, while MoRI / DeepEP-family backends use per-rank expert slots. The mismatch trips a model-init assertion / mis-maps the shared-expert id. #31793 disables the global-slot shared-expert fusion under per-rank EP backends. It must be applied for the model to load past init.

**Bug #2 — idle DP-attention ranks launch zero-sized grids (fixes #31350, #31594).** Under DP attention an active rank may hold e.g. 80 tokens while the other DP ranks hold 0. Many Triton/AITER kernels grid on the token count, so an empty rank launches with grid `(0, ...)`. CUDA tolerates a zero-sized grid as a no-op; **HIP rejects it with `invalid configuration argument`** (surfacing asynchronously later, e.g. during decode CUDA-graph capture / the Mamba allocator).

```
File ".../srt/models/utils.py", in fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_with_gate
    _fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_gate_kernel[(q_rows,)](...)   # grid == (0,)
torch.AcceleratorError: HIP error: invalid configuration argument
```

**Bug #3 — MoRI was misrouted through the plain TP-MoE path (root-cause collective fix).** `Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock` only took the EP dispatch/combine path for `get_moe_a2a_backend().is_deepep()`. MoRI uses EP dispatch/combine but is not `.is_deepep()`, so it fell into the ordinary TP path and ran a `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce()` **after** combine. Combine already returns each token to its source rank, so the trailing all-reduce mixed mismatched per-rank shapes — active rank `[80, 4096]` vs. idle rank `[0, 4096]` — a heterogeneous collective that crashes or deadlocks custom all-reduce.

## Modifications

**MoRI routed through the EP path — `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2_moe.py`** (three `get_moe_a2a_backend().is_deepep()` → `is_deepep_class_backend()` swaps, kept together):
- Shared expert built with TP1 (`tp_rank=0, tp_size=1`) so each source rank computes its full shared-expert output locally, matching the DeepEP/MoRI dispatch/combine model.
- EP metadata (`ep_size`, full expert count, `top_k`) initialized for MoRI instead of plain TP-MoE metadata.
- `forward()` dispatches to `_forward_deepep()` for MoRI, so combine returns tokens to the source rank and the block no longer falls into `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce()` — eliminating the `[80,4096]` vs `[0,4096]` heterogeneous all-reduce.

**Idle-rank zero-grid guards** (all are rank-local computations with no cross-rank collective, so an early empty return is safe):
- `python/sglang/srt/models/utils.py` — `fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm` and `fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_with_gate` return the already-allocated, correctly-shaped empty outputs when `q_rows == 0` (fixes #31350).
- `python/sglang/jit_kernel/triton/gdn_fused_proj.py` — `fused_qkvzba_split_reshape_cat`, `..._contiguous`, and `fused_qkv_split_gdn_prefill` skip the kernel launch on empty batch, returning the pre-shaped empty tensors.
- `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/gdn_backend.py` — GatedDeltaNet decode/prefill return an empty `[1, 0, num_v_heads, head_v_dim]` before entering `causal_conv1d_fn` / `chunk_gated_delta_rule` on an empty batch (fixes #31594).
- `python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py` — return an empty token-id tensor when `logits.shape[0] == 0` instead of launching greedy/softmax/sampling kernels on a 0-row batch.

Non-empty behavior on every path is unchanged (each guard is a single `== 0` check before the launch).

## Accuracy Tests

E2E on MI355X/ROCm with the full failing stack — Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, `--moe-a2a-backend mori`, `--enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head`, `--tp-size 4 --dp-size 4`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, `--attention-backend aiter` (repro: `repro_bug23_fp8.sh`):

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Server bring-up (CUDA-graph capture + warmup) | crash: HIP `invalid configuration argument` | completes, `/health` 200 |
| MoRI combine all-reduce | `[80,4096]` vs `[0,4096]` crash/deadlock | no heterogeneous all-reduce |
| **gsm8k accuracy** | — (server never served) | **0.94** |

Unit-level (fused QK-RMSNorm guard):
- **Non-empty (seq=5):** fixed outputs are bit-exact (`max_abs_diff == 0.0`) vs an eager GemmaRMSNorm reference for `q_out`/`k_out`, and the deinterleaved `gate_out` matches exactly.
- **Empty (seq=0):** both functions return the correct empty shapes (`(0, head_dim)`) without launching the kernel.

## Benchmarking

No perf-relevant change on the hot path: every guard is a single `== 0` check and non-empty launches are untouched; the MoRI change only selects the already-existing `_forward_deepep()` path instead of the TP path for MoRI.

## Checklist

- [x] Format with `pre-commit run --all-files` (isort/ruff/black/codespell pass)
- [x] Linked the issues (#31350, #31594); prerequisite init fix #31793
- [x] Guards applied to all sibling functions (QK-RMSNorm, GDN proj, GDN backend, sampler)
- [x] E2E verified: server serves and gsm8k = 0.94 with MoRI + DP-attention

title: [Bugfix] Fix DeepSeek V4 Pro TP24 vocabulary-padding failure on Hopper
author: mikekg
body:
## Motivation

Fixes the vocabulary-padding failure in [#31799](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/31799).

DeepSeek-V4-Pro fails while constructing `VocabParallelEmbedding` on GPU at global TP24:

~~~text
AssertionError: 129280 is not divisible by 24
~~~

The model has 129,280 vocabulary entries. Padding to the usual multiple of 64 leaves that number unchanged, but 129,280 is not divisible by 24:

~~~text
pad_vocab_size(129280, 64) = 129280
129280 % 24 = 16

pad_vocab_size(129280, 64 * 24) = 130560
130560 / 24 = 5440 rows per rank
~~~

`VocabParallelEmbedding` already increases the padding quantum when the initially padded vocabulary does not divide evenly across TP ranks. That adjustment was gated by `_is_cpu`, so the GPU constructor failed instead of applying the same padding. TP8 and TP16 did not expose this particular failure because 129,280 is divisible by both.

This PR fixes **vocabulary padding**, not arbitrary attention parallelism. It removes a false initialization blocker so the model can continue to its normal downstream checks.

## Modifications

- Apply the existing non-divisible-vocabulary padding adjustment on GPU as well as CPU.
- Add a registered, parameterized vocabulary-layer test that forces accelerator semantics and covers TP sizes 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, and 48.

The current PR changes only `python/sglang/srt/layers/vocab_parallel_embedding.py` and `test/registered/unit/layers/test_vocab_parallel_embedding_padding.py`. It adds no attention-topology validator, new error message, or inference-time operation. When the initially padded vocabulary is already divisible by TP, behavior is unchanged.

## Reproduction: vocabulary fix alone

The initialization diagnostic used `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-NVFP4` on 24 H100 GPUs with flat global TP24. On each of the three 8-GPU nodes, set `NODE_RANK` to 0, 1, or 2 and `MASTER_ADDR` to the rendezvous address.

**Before — unpatched source.** Run:

~~~bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-NVFP4 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
  --tensor-parallel-size 24 \
  --nnodes 3 \
  --node-rank "$NODE_RANK" \
  --dist-init-addr "$MASTER_ADDR:29500" \
  --disable-cuda-graph \
  --disable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000
~~~

The GPU embedding constructor stops at:

~~~text
AssertionError: 129280 is not divisible by 24
~~~

**After — source with this PR's vocabulary change, and no attention change.** Run the same command with the same checkpoint:

~~~bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-NVFP4 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
  --tensor-parallel-size 24 \
  --nnodes 3 \
  --node-rank "$NODE_RANK" \
  --dist-init-addr "$MASTER_ADDR:29500" \
  --disable-cuda-graph \
  --disable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000
~~~

All 24 ranks pass the embedding constructor and initialize the NCCL group. Model construction then reaches the first attention layer and stops at its existing assertion:

~~~text
AssertionError: 65536 is not divisible by 24
~~~

This is a **passing before/after test of the vocabulary-padding fix**, not a successful flat-TP24 serving run. CUDA graphs are disabled only for this initialization diagnostic, not for the serving evaluations below.

That second assertion is a separate, real constraint—not a vocabulary-padding regression. DeepSeek-V4-Pro has 128 attention heads with head dimension 512 and 16 output groups. Its `wq_b` output width is `128 * 512 = 65,536`; neither 128 heads nor 16 output groups divide evenly across **flat attention TP24**. This PR intentionally does not suppress that check or claim flat TP24 is supported.

For 24 GPUs, use **global TP24/DP3 with DP attention**, giving effective attention TP8:

~~~bash
--tensor-parallel-size 24 \
--data-parallel-size 3 \
--enable-dp-attention \
--enable-dp-lm-head
~~~

This keeps the total of 24 ranks while using a supported attention partition. The DP-attention gather correction in [#31700](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31700) is already merged and is separate from this vocabulary fix.

## Accuracy Tests

### Before/after: vocabulary constructor

The registered test forces the accelerator path with `_is_cpu=False` and constructs the real layer. Its TP24 case is equivalent to:

~~~python
parallel = SimpleNamespace(tp_rank=0, tp_size=24)

with (
    patch.object(vocab_embedding, "_is_cpu", False),
    patch.object(vocab_embedding, "get_parallel", return_value=parallel),
):
    layer = vocab_embedding.VocabParallelEmbedding(129_280, 1)

assert layer.padding_size == 1_536
assert layer.num_embeddings_padded == 130_560
assert layer.weight.shape == (5_440, 1)
~~~

**Before:** construction fails with `AssertionError: 129280 is not divisible by 24`, before any of these assertions can run.

**After:** all three TP24 assertions pass. The full parameterized test passes **9/9 cases locally**. It also checks TP48, which needs a larger padding quantum (`3,072`, producing 132,096 padded entries), and TP40, whose original padded vocabulary is already divisible by 40 and therefore remains unchanged. These are vocabulary-layer tests, **not** claims that every model or attention topology serves end-to-end at those widths.

### End-to-end serving with related fixes

Separate serving evaluations used **global TP24/DP3/attention-TP8** on 24 H100s and 24 H200s with the independent, merged [#31700 DP-attention gather fix](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31700). The H100 setup used `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-NVFP4`, DP attention and DP LM head, `--chunked-prefill-size 3072`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.94`, `--context-length 2200`, `--max-running-requests 256`, FP8 KV cache, Marlin backends, and CUDA graphs with `--cuda-graph-max-bs 256`. 

To run a public five-shot GSM8K evaluation against a ready server at `localhost:8000`, use:

~~~bash
OPENAI_API_KEY=EMPTY python3 -m lm_eval \
  --model local-chat-completions \
  --apply_chat_template \
  --tasks gsm8k \
  --num_fewshot 5 \
  --output_path gsm8k-results \
  --log_samples \
  --model_args 'model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,api_key=EMPTY,eos_string=</s>,max_retries=5,num_concurrent=64,timeout=1800,tokenized_requests=False,max_length=2200' \
  --gen_kwargs 'max_tokens=512,temperature=0,top_p=1'
~~~

The separate five-shot GSM8K serving evaluations at client concurrency 64 completed all 1,319 questions:

| GPU and layout | Requests | Strict exact match | Flexible exact match |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 24×H100, TP8×DP3 | 1,319/1,319 | 0.919636 | 0.919636 |
| 24×H200, TP8×DP3 | 1,319/1,319 | 0.912055 | 0.918878 |

These serving results exercise the supported attention layout; the direct regression test for **this PR's change** is the vocabulary constructor test above.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable to this PR's code change: vocabulary padding is determined at layer initialization, and this PR adds no request-time branch or inference operator. No inference-speed improvement is claimed.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with [pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit); hooks passed on both changed files.
- [x] Add [registered unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests); 9/9 vocabulary-padding cases passed locally.
- [x] Review [documentation](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations); no user-facing API or flag changed.
- [x] Provide [accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed) applicability above, distinguishing this PR's tests from related-PR serving results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang [code style guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: Fix LoRA usage-counter accounting across request lifecycle paths
author: shafeeqibraheem
body:
## Motivation

`LoRARegistry` tracks per-adapter in-flight usage with a `ConcurrentCounter`:
`acquire()` (+1 per request entry) when `_resolve_lora_path` runs, `release()`
(−1) when the request finishes. `/unload_lora_adapter` →
`LoRARegistry.wait_for_unload()` waits for the counter to reach **exactly
zero** before unloading. Any accounting imbalance therefore turns into one of
two production failures:

- **counter stuck > 0** (leaked acquire): the unload hangs forever, and
  because the tokenizer manager serializes LoRA update operations, every
  subsequent load/unload wedges behind it;
- **counter < 0** (extra release): `wait_for_zero` can also never fire (it
  waits for equality), same hang — and had it fired, the adapter could be
  unloaded while requests still use it.

We hit this in an RL setting (adapter hot-swap between rollout waves,
engine-native parallel sampling, occasional client disconnects/aborts): usage
counters drifted by hundreds per adapter per rollout, after which every
generation-used adapter's unload hung (>130 s with an external watchdog, vs
0.03 s for an unused adapter on the same engine).

Related: #23141, #5525, #8162, #2686, #6184, #14338.

## Root causes fixed

1. **Parallel sampling (`n>1`) over-release** — `_handle_batch_request`
   sends a prefix-cache warm-up sub-request (`max_new_tokens=0`) that is
   `copy.copy`'d from the parent with `lora_id` intact. Acquire is once per
   entry of the expanded `lora_path` list (= n per prompt), but finishers are
   n expansions **+ 1 warm-up** per prompt → net −1 per prompt on the pure
   success path. Fixed by clearing `lora_path`/`lora_id` on the
   tokenizer-side state object only (the scheduler-side object keeps them so
   the radix prefix is cached under the right adapter key).
2. **Droppable success release** — the success path released via a bare
   `asyncio.create_task(...)` with no strong reference; the event loop keeps
   only weak refs, so the release can be garbage-collected unrun.
3. **Abort-ack leak** — `_handle_abort_req` (the scheduler's abort ack for
   `/abort_request`, or a client disconnect while queued) marked the request
   finished, deleted the `rid_to_state` entry, but never released. Note this
   is not limited to queued aborts: the ack races the final batch output for
   *running* aborts (see the existing comment in `_handle_abort_req`), and
   when the ack lands first it deletes the state entry, the batch output is
   skipped, and the success-path release is lost too — so running aborts
   leak timing-dependently.
4. **`BAD_REQUEST` abort finish leak** — the `BAD_REQUEST` branch of
   `_handle_abort_finish_reason` raised/returned without releasing (and
   without dropping the `rid_to_state` entry, unlike the adjacent
   `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` branch).
5. **Validation-failure leak** — `_resolve_lora_path` acquires **before**
   tokenization/validation, so a request rejected by `_validate_one_request`
   (e.g. oversized prompt) has acquired but never reaches the scheduler — no
   output or abort ack can ever balance it.
6. **Parallel-sampling parent-state hazard** — the `n>1` path re-sends every
   sub-request under regenerated rids, leaving the parent-entry `ReqState`s
   created by `_init_req_state` orphaned (all but the first per prompt were
   also never removed from `rid_to_state`). `create_abort_task` aborts the
   *parent* rids on streaming disconnect, so naively adding a release to the
   abort ack (fix 3) would release counters the expanded finishers already
   own, driving them negative.

## Modifications

All completion paths now route through one idempotent guard:

- `ReqState.lora_released` flag + `TokenizerManager._release_lora_once(state)`
  (releases exactly once per tracked request state; keeps a strong reference
  to the release task in `self._lora_release_tasks`).
- Success path (`_handle_batch_output`), abort ack (`_handle_abort_req`), and
  both error branches of `_handle_abort_finish_reason` call the guard; the
  `BAD_REQUEST` branch now also cleans up `rid_to_state`, mirroring the
  `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` branch.
- `_discard_pending_req_states` (already called from `generate_request`'s
  `except`) now releases the counter for each dropped state, closing the
  validation-failure leak.
- The `n>1` branch pops all parent-entry states up front and marks their
  accounting as transferred (`lora_released = True`) to the regenerated
  copies; parent-rid abort acks become harmless no-ops, and the
  `rid_to_state` growth from orphaned parent entries is gone.
- The `n>1` prefix-cache warm-up sub-request no longer carries
  `lora_path`/`lora_id` on the tokenizer-side state object.

Behavioral invariant: for every request shape, total releases == total
acquires, exactly once each, regardless of which combination of batch
output / abort ack / error branch / dispatch failure observes the finish.

## Test & verification

New `test/registered/lora/test_lora_usage_counter.py` drives one lifecycle
shape per test against a freshly loaded adapter and asserts
`/unload_lora_adapter` completes promptly (a leaked counter blocks it
forever): parallel-sampling success, mid-generation client disconnect (n=1
and n=4), `/abort_request` on queued + running requests, oversized-prompt
400, invalid-grammar 400, and streaming n=4 disconnect.

Standalone verification against the official nightly image built from main
(`lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20260708-b3632494`, single GPU, tiny model,
instrumented registry that logs the counter value at unload time). Counter
value at unload per case:

| case | stock main | with this PR |
|---|---|---|
| unused adapter (control) | 0 | 0 |
| `n=4` success | **−1** (hang) | 0, instant |
| disconnect mid-gen (n=1 + n=4) | **+3** (hang) | 0, instant |
| `/abort_request` queued + running | **+1** (hang) | 0, instant |
| oversized prompt → 400 | **+1** (hang) | 0, instant |
| invalid `json_schema` → 400 | 0 | 0 |
| streaming `n=4` disconnect | **−1** (hang) | 0, instant |

("hang" = `wait_for_unload` never returns upstream; bounded in the harness
only to keep the runs finite. The same matrix on 0.5.12.post1 differs only
in the disconnect case: +2 instead of +3, because there the running abort's
release always arrived via batch output, while on main the abort ack can
preempt it — root cause 3.)

- [x] Format your code with `pre-commit run --all-files` *(run before push)*
- [x] Add unit tests
- [x] Update documentation as needed *(no user-facing docs affected)*

title: Fix MiniMax-M3 crash on ROCm by making its override fields resolvable
author: zijiexia
body:
## Problem

Starting MiniMax-M3 on ROCm (MI355X, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`) without `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion` crashes the launcher before the engine comes up:

```
File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/overrides.py", line 2211, in validate_declarations
    raise ValueError(
ValueError: _minimax_m3_overrides: ['disable_custom_all_reduce'] not model-overridable; declarations are limited to the fields the publish gate accepts.
```

## Root cause

`_minimax_m3_overrides` on ROCm declares config values through the override registry:

- `disable_custom_all_reduce=True` whenever aiter allreduce fusion is off (the default path), and
- `enable_aiter_allreduce_fusion=False` on the standard-EP path (deferred fused all-reduce corrupts sparse MoE partial outputs).

Both fields lacked `Arg(..., resolvable=True)`, so they are not on the declaration whitelist. `validate_declarations` rejects the declaration at its slot and the launcher aborts.

Passing `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion` only *masks* the default-path crash: it flips `aiter_fusion_resolved` to `True`, so the illegal `disable_custom_all_reduce` declaration branch is skipped. It does not fix the standard-EP path, which would still crash on the `enable_aiter_allreduce_fusion` declaration.

## Fix

Tag both fields `resolvable=True` so the model override may legally declare them, and extend the exact whitelist pin in `test_model_overrides.py` in the same commit (as its docstring requires). Defaults are unchanged.

## Repro

Before this PR, the following crashes with the `ValueError` above:

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 sglang serve \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 \
  --tp 8 --quantization mxfp8 --dtype bfloat16 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000
```

## Validation (MI355X, tp8 mxfp8)

With this fix, the same command (no `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion`) boots and serves:

```
[TP0] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 186, #cached-token: 0, ...
INFO:     127.0.0.1 - "POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
The server is fired up and ready to roll!
```

title: Fix pad-row top-k masking with custom_routing_function under DP attention
author: hanming-lu
body:
## Motivation

`select_experts` asserts `num_token_non_padded is None` on the `custom_routing_function` branch, so any model that routes through a custom routing function cannot pass it. Under DP attention with CUDA-graph padding this is a correctness problem, not just a missing feature: the padded rows' router logits are garbage, and without the mask every padded row keeps its unmasked top-k expert ids through EP dispatch. Since the padded rows are identical, they all pick the same experts, which skews per-expert dispatch counts and can overflow per-expert buffers in fused EP MoE kernels — we debugged this to NaN/garbage MoE output on an internal DP-attention + EP deployment of a model using a custom routing function.

## Modifications

**Commit 1 — allow `num_token_non_padded` with `custom_routing_function`.** Drop the assertion. It is unnecessary: `_post_process_topk_ids` already masks rows `>= num_token_non_padded` (`-1` on CUDA via `_mask_topk_ids_padded_region` / `_biased_grouped_topk_postprocess`, expert `0` with zeroed weights on HIP) after the logical→physical remap, and it runs on the shared path after both routing branches — the standard-routing branches already rely on exactly this. A comment now documents why the padding-unaware custom routing output is safe. Callers that don't pass `num_token_non_padded` are unaffected.

**Commit 2 — recompute `num_token_non_padded` against the capture bucket at prefill CUDA-graph replay.** Replay pads the raw token count up to the capture bucket, which moves the attn-TP shard boundary (`tokens_per_rank = bucket/attn_tp`, not `raw/attn_tp`). The forward batch's `num_token_non_padded` was localized against the RAW length on the eager prep path, so for `raw < bucket` it undercounts rank 0's real rows and the in-graph pad-row mask blanks REAL tokens (global rows `[raw/attn_tp, bucket/attn_tp)`), corrupting their MoE output. Fix: a `post_fill` hook on the prefill registry's `num_token_non_padded` slot recomputes the local count against the padded bucket from the batch's un-adjusted global count (`num_token_non_padded_cpu`) — mirroring the decode registry's `post_fill`, which already uses `ctx.padded_num_tokens` the same way. Applies only under gathered-buffer DP attention without prefill context parallelism.

**Commit 3 — refactor + tests.** Share the attn-TP shard-bound math via `_attn_tp_local_shard_bounds` between `compute_local_num_token_non_padded` and a new int-scalar twin `compute_local_num_token_non_padded_cpu` (the registry `post_fill` uses it: `Tensor.fill_` on a host int, no per-replay host-to-device staging copy). Adds:
- `test_cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py::TestPrefillNumTokenNonPaddedPostFill` — rank 0 must use the bucket shard (512), not the raw-localized FB value (509); rank 1 masks exactly the true pads (506); non-gathered keeps the plain FB copy.
- `test_topk_padded_region.py::TestSelectExpertsCustomRoutingPadMask` — GPU regression for commit 1: a degenerate custom router emitting the same expert id in every top-k slot on NaN pad rows → padded tail comes out `[-1] * top_k`, real rows untouched.

## Testing

- `test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py` + `test/registered/moe/test_topk_padded_region.py`: 43 passed locally (CPU + single B200; the 2 skips are the HIP-only classes).
- Verified on an internal DP-attention + EP deployment that previously produced NaN outputs from overflowed pad-row dispatch: padded rows are masked to `-1` before dispatch and the NaNs are gone. The replay recompute was validated against a deterministic repro where the raw-length localization blanked real rows in upper attn-TP shards under the breakable prefill graph.

## Original commits

- `6a1b86383`
- `e38da1579`
- `d3844a45b`
- `debcd2c35`
- `fc2fd3526`

author: michaelzhang-ai

## What

Enable 3 more nested `multimodal_gen` `unit/` files on AMD, each of which needs a small **test-harness stub fix**. These stub gaps are pre-existing and would also fail on CUDA, so the fixes are portable rather than AMD-specific; the files are enabled on AMD only for now, consistent with #31483.

| File | Fix |
|---|---|
| `unit/progressive_resolution/test_progressive.py` (3 tests) | give the `_on_resolution_change` ctxs a non-None `cfg_policy` (stage early-returns when it is `None`) |
| `unit/sana_wm/test_streaming_realtime_path.py` (4 tests) | add `enable_breakable_cuda_graph` to the `_global_args` stub (`DenoisingStage.__init__` reads it) |
| `unit/realtime/test_lingbot_causal_denoising.py` (2 tests) | set `stage.transformer = None` on the two `__new__`-built stubs so `_reset_causal_cache_config_defaults()` is a no-op |

Each file is added to `_AMD_READY_NESTED_UNIT_TESTS` (`gpu_cases.py`) and `_MM_GEN_FILE_BACKENDS` (`ci_coverage_report.py`).

## AMD-only by construction

Every part of this change is inert on non-AMD lanes:

- **Test edits cannot run on CUDA.** `_discover_unit_tests()` returns only the flat `unit/test_*.py` glob unless `current_platform.is_hip()`. All three files here live in nested subdirs (`progressive_resolution/`, `sana_wm/`, `realtime/`), so no non-HIP lane collects them. The CUDA `multimodal-gen-unit-test` job is byte-identical.
- **Allowlist entry is HIP-gated.** `_AMD_READY_NESTED_UNIT_TESTS` is only consulted inside the `is_hip()` branch.
- **Coverage entry is AMD-tagged.** `_MM_GEN_FILE_BACKENDS` maps each of the 3 files to `("AMD",)`.
- No production code is touched — only test-harness stubs and the coverage classifier.

Verified by running the real report on this head: the 3 files are credited to AMD with no extras, and the files deferred to #31844 / #31846 correctly remain CUDA-tagged.

## Rebase

#31483 has merged, so this is no longer stacked. Rebased onto current `main` as `3dfe2a3ecde3`; git dropped the already-merged commit automatically. The PR is now **1 commit, 5 files, +25/-0**.

title: fix(diffusion): keep fused qk-norm-rope out of dynamo tracing
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

With `torch.compile` enabled (e.g. `performance_mode=speed`), every qwen-image request fails with HTTP 500:

```
torch._dynamo.exc.AsPythonConstantNotImplementedError: SymNodeVariable() is not a constant
```

`can_use_fused_inplace_qknorm_rope` is decorated with `@torch.compiler.assume_constant_result`, but the qwen call sites pass `head_dim=img_query.shape[-1]` / `rope_dim=cos_sin_cache.size(-1)`, which become SymInts under dynamo tracing; `assume_constant_result` cannot fold SymInt arguments (wrapping in `int()` does not help — dynamo keeps them symbolic).

## Modifications

- Gate the fused inplace qk-norm-rope path with `not torch.compiler.is_compiling()`. Under compile, the unfused path is traced and inductor fuses it on its own; the handwritten fused kernel remains active for eager.
- Pass the static `self.head_dim` at the two qwen-image call sites instead of a runtime shape.

## Test

On 2×H100 (Qwen-Image-2512, 1024x1024, 50 steps, ulysses=2, torch.compile on): requests return 500 before this change and 200 after, with the compile path serving normally.

title: Fix dropped tool calls when a stream delta carries several
author: ispobock
body:
## Motivation

`InklingDetector.parse_streaming_increment` (tool-call parser) parses at most one complete tool call per delta and re-buffers the remainder into `self._buffer`, relying on the *next* delta to drain it. When a single delta carries two or more complete tool calls, the trailing calls are left stranded: there is no `finish()`/`parse_stream_end` on this detector, and the stream-end hook `_check_for_unstreamed_tool_args` only tops up the remaining argument bytes of the last *tracked* call, so the extra calls are silently dropped. The non-streaming `detect_and_parse` path already emits all calls (it iterates matches), so this is a streaming-only gap.

This bites whenever one delta batches multiple complete calls — e.g. a larger `--stream-interval`, or multi-token decode steps. Reproduced end-to-end with `--stream-interval 1000`: a 4-tool-call response streamed **1** call before this change and **4** after (matching the non-streaming result); 2/3/5-call prompts likewise collapsed to 1 without the fix.

## Modifications

- Split the per-delta body into `_parse_buffered_increment`, which parses at most one complete call and reports whether it consumed one, and loop it in `parse_streaming_increment` until a pass makes no progress (partial/re-buffered call or plain text). This drains every complete call in a delta at arrival, matching the non-streaming path. Termination holds: each consumed call strictly shrinks `self._buffer`, and a partial trailing call hits the existing early-return.
- Add a regression test: a single delta with two complete tool calls now emits both (`tool_index` 0 and 1 with per-call args); it fails on the pre-fix code and passes after.

title: [lora] Fix WAR race: never write MoE runner output into hidden_states in place
author: sshleifer
body:
## Motivation

- We have a long decode lora eval that improves with this fix. Generates some occasional gibberish without.



## Root cause

A write-after-read race between the LoRA MoE runner and dual-stream shared experts:

- With LoRA, the marlin MoE path writes its final reduction **into `hidden_states`**: `output = hidden_states if inplace else torch.empty_like(hidden_states)` with `MoeRunnerConfig.inplace=True` by default. The fused non-LoRA kernels allocate their own output buffer — only the LoRA path aliases, which is why base-model decode is unaffected.
- `DeepseekV2MoE.forward_normal_dual_stream` (taken during decode cuda-graph capture) reads `hidden_states` for the shared experts on the alt stream. The only fork edge (`alt_stream.wait_stream(current_stream)`) is recorded before the router, so there is no ordering between the routed-experts write and the shared-expert read. The in-code comment documents a read-only assumption ("the routed deep_gemm does not free hidden_states, which the shared expert reads on the alt stream") — disposal is handled, mutation is not.
- The eager path already knows about this contract: `forward_normal` orders shared-vs-routed off the flag (`defer_shared = not self.experts.moe_runner_config.inplace`). The dual-stream path has no equivalent handling.

Inside the captured decode graph, whether the alt-stream read beats the main-stream write is scheduling luck. When it loses, the shared expert consumes routed-output rows instead of layer input — subtly corrupted logits every affected step, compounding through the KV cache. This matches all observed properties: LoRA-only, stochastic per run, variable onset, tail-worst, text coherent with non-canonical token boundaries.

## Modifications

- Force `inplace=False` at `FusedMoEWithLoRA` construction, mirroring the existing FlashInfer TRTLLM force-disable in `fused_moe_triton/layer.py`. 
- This makes the LoRA runner match the allocation behavior of every fused non-LoRA path and covers all models with dual-stream MoE forwards in one place. 

## Validation

3072-token forced-greedy probe, scored by re-tokenizing the generated text (canonical ≈ 3070/3072; fragmented generations re-tokenize far lower). GB300 tp4, Kimi-K2.5 int4 marlin + MoE LoRA, 8 reps per server:

| arm | reps | collapsed (<90% canonical) | min |
|---|---|---|---|
| inplace write active (2 servers + field runs) | 16 | 4 | 2332/3072 |
| write removed | 24 | 0 (nothing below 2700) | 2992/3072 |

Steady-state decode throughput and tpot are unchanged by the fix.

title: [NPU] FIX garbled characters illusion problems, in prefix cache mtp scenarios.
author: McZyWu
body: ## Motivation For NPU, when the input and output reach tens of thousands of tokens, enabling radix cache in MTP scenarios can occasionally cause the illusion of garbled characters. Opening images or using PlanStream will exacerbate this issue. The principle is as follows: - When `accept_lens=1`, `last_steps=[0]`, and the SSM state at step=0 is the recurrent state that was just calculated. - The model forward has already written it to the correct position, so it doesn't need to be copied again. - The NPU's intermediate_ssm has bfloat16 rounding differences; each copy accumulates error → drift after a long sequence. The intermediate_ssm copy path is only used when `all_step0=False` (when `accept_lens>1`). --- --CODE-- ``` if cache_len is None or cache_len == 0: # Nothing to cache: free KV and mamba slots without inserting # a key_len=0 ghost node into the radix tree. Such empty nodes # poison subsequent match_prefix calls by serving as a stale # mamba COW source with best_value_len=0 (see cache_finished_req # of a short request with no track boundary). Only free the unprotected # part of kv_indices. self.token_to_kv_pool_allocator.free( kv_indices[req.cache_protected_len :] ) self.req_to_token_pool.free_mamba_cache(req) self.dec_lock_ref(req.last_node) return ``` Scenario: The warmup request only has 80 tokens, far less than `mamba_cache_chunk_size=256`, so during the extend phase, `mask=False` — no track checkpoint was ever created, and `mamba_last_track_seqlen` is always `None`. Original code: `cache_len=None` → set to 0 → inserting `key_len=0`, `value_len=0` into the radix tree, creating an empty ghost node. Subsequent requests will match this ghost node in `match_prefix`, with `best_value_len=0` and `mamba_value=yes`, triggering COW to copy a never-correctly-initialized Mamba slot → resulting in garbled characters. This fix: When `cache_len is None` or `cache_len == 0` is detected, directly free the KV and Mamba slot, skipping the radix insert and eliminating the ghost node. This is the correct protection logic. ---- --CODE-- ``` for i, req in enumerate(batch.reqs): if to_track[i] and req.mamba_next_track_idx is not None: req.mamba_next_track_idx = ( pool.get_mamba_ping_pong_other_idx( req.mamba_next_track_idx ) ) ``` In``prepare_mamba_track_for_verify`` , it calls``set_mamba_track_indices_from_reqs(batch)`` which rebuilds mamba_track_indices from req objects. But if``req.mamba_next_track_idx`` never gets flipped, then``mamba_track_indices`` stays the same. In decode, the non-spec path flips it in``prepare_for_decode`` . For spec decode, the flip was missing The absence of this flip will cause the same track slot to be repeatedly overwritten. After a boundary crossing, the next verify will write to the same slot that was just committed. ---- ## Accuracy Tests aime qwen3.6-35b--prefix cache--0.9 The above hallucination problem didn't appear title: [Bug] Fix multi-tokenizer BatchEmbeddingOutput repack dropping fields
author: lijrjyan
body:
## Motivation

Embedding serving with `--tokenizer-worker-num > 1` is broken: every response — including the server's own warmup request — crashes the tokenizer workers with

```text
  File ".../tokenizer_manager.py", line 1894, in _handle_batch_output
    "num_retractions": recv_obj.retraction_counts[i],
TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable
```

Root cause: the per-worker output repack (`_handle_output_by_index` in `multi_tokenizer_mixin.py`) rebuilds `BatchEmbeddingOutput` with only 5 of its fields. The scheduler's output streamer always populates `retraction_counts`, but the repack drops it, so the per-worker copy arrives at its `None` default and the unconditional index crashes. The same repack also silently drops `time_stats` (per-request time stats / metrics), `cached_tokens_details`, and `pooled_hidden_states` (breaking `return_pooled_hidden_states` through multi-tokenizer mode). The neighboring `BatchTokenIDOutput` / `BatchStrOutput` branches extract these fields; the embedding branch was never completed.

Single-tokenizer mode (the default) is unaffected, which is presumably why this went unnoticed. Fixes #31890.

## Modifications

Complete the `BatchEmbeddingOutput` repack with the four missing fields, using the same `_extract_field_by_index` form as the adjacent branches (8 lines in `multi_tokenizer_mixin.py`).

## Accuracy Tests

- Unit (CPU, `test/registered/unit/managers/test_multi_tokenizer_embedding_repack.py`, `base-a-test-cpu`) — **2 passed**: the repack preserves every per-request field (including the four previously dropped), and still passes `None` through for absent optional fields.
- End-to-end on an A6000: `--is-embedding --tokenizer-worker-num 2` previously died on the warmup request; with this fix the server serves a full saturation benchmark (2048 requests, c=128) with zero failures. Also validated as part of a same-GPU DP study where extra tokenizer workers are what make colocated data parallelism pay off (805.8 -> 1367.8 req/s at dp2; details in the companion PR).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable — the change only carries fields that were already produced by the scheduler; no additional work per response.

title: [AMD] Add msgpack to ROCm diffusion deps (fix multimodal-gen unit test ModuleNotFoundError)
author: kangwangamd
body:
### Problem

The `multimodal-gen-unit-test-amd-rocm720` job fails **every night** (7/8 days in the CI window) with:
```
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'msgpack'
FAILED test/unit/test_pi05_action_api.py::test_msgpack_roundtrip_preserves_string_keys_and_numpy_payloads
```

`msgpack` is a **runtime** dependency of `multimodal_gen`: `runtime/entrypoints/vla/protocol.py` uses `pack_msgpack`/`unpack_msgpack` (`msgpack.packb` / `msgpack.unpackb`), and the unit test imports them.

### Root cause

The ROCm wheel/image installs deps from `python/pyproject_other.toml` (via `pip install python[srt_hip,diffusion_hip]` in `docker/rocm.Dockerfile`, which swaps `pyproject_other.toml` in as the active manifest). Its `diffusion_common` group is **missing `msgpack`**, while the mainline `python/pyproject.toml` `diffusion` group already lists it.

The ROCm 7.0 lane (`multimodal-gen-unit-test-amd`) happens to pass because its base image ships `msgpack` transitively, but the ROCm 7.2 `rocm/pytorch` base does not — so the dependency must be declared explicitly.

### Fix

Add `msgpack` to the `diffusion_common` group in `python/pyproject_other.toml` (alphabetical position, matching the file's sorting convention). All AMD platforms (`diffusion_hip`/`diffusion_musa`/`diffusion_mps`) pull `diffusion_common`, so this covers them all.

### Scope

One line, dependency-only. No code change. Fixes the `msgpack` `ModuleNotFoundError` on the ROCm 7.2 multimodal-gen unit-test job.

title: [UnifiedTree] fix: drop prefetched host refill under an un-backed-up parent
author: decajoin
body:
## Motivation

**Two storage tiers.** HiCache keeps each radix-tree node's KV in two places: fast **device** (GPU) memory and larger **host** (CPU) memory. A node that has a host copy is *backed up*. Under the `write_through` policy, host copies are written eagerly and form a **contiguous chain from the root** — the cache maintains the invariant that **a node may be backed up only if its parent is backed up** (there must be no backed-up node whose ancestor was never backed up).

**The prefetch commit.** When an incoming request's prefix only partially matches the tree, L3 prefetch fetches the missing suffix from external storage into host memory and splices it into the tree: it hangs a new **host (backed-up)** node under the *match anchor* — the deepest node the request matched. This splice is done by `UnifiedRadixCache._insert_helper_host`.

**The bug.** `_insert_helper_host` attaches that new host child by writing its `host_value` **directly**, without checking the anchor. But the anchor is frequently a **device-only** node — it holds device KV from an earlier request but was never backed up (e.g. its write-through backup hadn't run yet). Splicing a backed-up child under a device-only anchor produces exactly the forbidden shape: **a backed-up node whose parent is not backed up**, breaking the invariant.

**Why it crashes.** The broken invariant then blows up in two different places, which is what we saw in actual use:

1. **Idle self-check.** The scheduler periodically verifies tree invariants while idle. It catches the broken chain directly and aborts:
   Sanity check FAILED: node N backed up but parent M not backed up

2. **Eviction.** The device-only anchor is still a valid *device leaf*, so under memory pressure eviction selects it. Because it isn't backed up, write-through eviction takes the **delete-from-tree** path (`_remove_leaf_from_parent`), which assumes the node being removed is a true leaf. But prefetch has left a host child hanging off it, so deleting the anchor orphans that child subtree and trips the structural assertion, crashing the scheduler:
   _evict_device_leaf -> _remove_leaf_from_parent -> assert v == node

Both failures share one root cause seen from two angles: the idle checker catches it early; eviction, if it reaches the node first, corrupts the tree and takes the process down.

## Modifications

- **`_insert_helper_host`**: prefetch refill is best-effort, so when the anchor is a non-root nodedrop the refill** (freeing its host pages) instead of attaching a backed-up child under it. Thiskeeps the backup invariant intact, so eviction no longer detaches a node from under an attached child.
- Added regression test `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_radix_prefetch_corruption.py`ant + eviction safety). Both are **red before the fix, green after**. Registered on`base-b-test-1-gpu-small`.

_Scope note:_ this targets `UnifiedRadixCache` (`unified_radix_cache.py`). #30106 covers the same — different cache class, no file overlap, so the two look complementary.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — cache-tree bookkeeping correctness only; no change to model forward code or kernels, so mode full `test_unified_radix_cache_unittest` suite (1495 cases) passes with the fix.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A for inference speed. Dropping an un-backupable refill just turns it into a cache miss; the hot path does one extra `node.backuped` check.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit
- [x] Add unit tests (regression test, red-before/green-after)
- [ ] Update documentation — N/A (bug fix, no user-facing surface)
- [ ] Accuracy/speed benchmarks — N/A (no model-output or perf impact)

title: [KDA] Fix mixed exponent bases in Triton chunk prefill
author: yuan-luo
body: ## Motivation KDA defines each per-channel decay gate in natural-log space. Let $g_t \in \mathbb{R}^{D_k}$ be the per-token log-decay gate and let its chunk-local cumulative gate be $$ G_t = \sum_{s=1}^{t} g_s $$ The decay that propagates information from position $j$ to position $i$ is $$ D_{i,j} = \exp\left(G_i - G_j\right) $$ The Triton chunk-prefill implementation mixed two exponent domains for the same cumulative-gate tensor: - several intra-chunk kernels evaluated gate differences with `exp2`; - the state-update, output, and fused-recompute paths evaluated them with natural `exp`; - the cumulative sum remained in natural-log space. Using `exp2` directly on a natural-log cumulative gate instead computes $$ 2^{G_i-G_j} = \exp\left(\ln(2)\left(G_i-G_j\right)\right) $$ rather than $\exp(G_i-G_j)$. Since KDA gates are non-positive, multiplying the exponent by $\ln(2) < 1$ weakens the decay and retains too much history. Because different stages used different bases, the combined chunk computation did not correspond to one consistent KDA recurrence. The correct conversion is performed once at the cumulative-gate producer: $$ \widehat{G}_t = G_t \log_2(e) = \frac{G_t}{\ln(2)} $$ All downstream KDA chunk kernels can then use base-2 exponentiation while preserving the original recurrence exactly: $$ 2^{\widehat{G}_i-\widehat{G}_j} = 2^{(G_i-G_j)/\ln(2)} = \exp\left(G_i-G_j\right) $$ This affects the Triton KDA chunk-prefill path for both pre-activated gates and the fused raw-gate activation path. Recurrent decode continues to consume a raw per-token natural-log gate and is not affected. GDN also keeps its existing natural-exponent contract. ## Modifications - Convert KDA's chunk-local cumulative gate from natural-log space to log2 space at its single producer boundary by passing `RCP_LN2` to both: - `kda_gate_chunk_cumsum`, for raw gates activated in the cumsum kernel; - `chunk_local_cumsum`, for gates already activated by the caller. - Make all consumers of the KDA cumulative gate use `exp2`, including: - scaled KKT/QK construction; - standalone and fused W/U/KG recomputation; - intra-chunk fused solve/recompute; - recurrent-state chunk updates; - final chunk output construction. - Add a compile-time `use_exp2` option to the shared `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h` state kernel. It defaults to `False`, preserving the existing GDN natural-exponent behavior; KDA passes `use_exp2=True`. - Keep the XPU override's Python/kernel signature aligned with the shared state kernel. - Add an independent pure-PyTorch recurrent oracle test. It checks both output and the in-place final state for: - fixed-length prefill crossing multiple 64-token chunks; - ragged varlen prefill around sub-chunk/chunk boundaries; - pre-activated gates and fused raw-gate activation. This PR intentionally does not change recurrent decode, GDN's exponent domain, safe-gate kernel selection, or non-Triton KDA backends. ## Accuracy Tests The new regression test uses a token-by-token PyTorch recurrence with natural `torch.exp` as an implementation-independent reference. Restoring the pre-fix sources makes the test fail by a large margin: | Case | Pre-fix output relative RMSE | This PR | | --- | ---: | --- | | fixed length `[129]`, pre-activated gate | 19.7575% | output and final state < 1% | | ragged `[15, 16, 17, 63, 65]`, fused raw gate | 14.9267% | output and final state < 1% | - KDA gate cumsum and fused recurrent regression: `6 passed`. - Shared GDN state-kernel regression: `1 passed`. - Projected Triton KDA backend correctness: `1 passed`. No end-to-end model accuracy benchmark was run for this kernel-only fix. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No dedicated performance benchmark was run. The change adds no kernel launch, allocation, synchronization, or intermediate tensor: - the `RCP_LN2` multiplication is fused into the existing cumsum kernel; - natural `exp` instructions are replaced by `exp2` in KDA consumers; - `USE_EXP2` is a Triton compile-time specialization, so it adds no runtime branch to either KDA or GDN. The expected performance impact is neutral to slightly positive, but this PR makes no performance claim without a dedicated benchmark. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No user-facing documentation change is required; the exponent-domain contract is documented in code and tests. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Kernel accuracy is covered above; a dedicated speed benchmark has not been run. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`. 4. title: [Mooncake] Fix silent SSD offload corruption when TP/PP ranks share ssd_offload_path
author: ironashram
body:
## Motivation

Each scheduler rank embeds its own `MooncakeDistributedStore` client, and `MooncakeStore.__init__ `passes all of them the same ssd_offload_path. Mooncake's SSD tier assumes one client per storage location, and a shared directory corrupts silently:

- bucket ids are generated per process (`timestamp<<12` seed with a plain atomic increment, `mooncake-store/src/storage_backend.cpp`)
- after a restart every client resumes from the same scanned max_bucket_id, making filename collisions deterministic
- bucket files are opened with `O_CREAT|O_TRUNC`, so a collision truncates another rank's bucket and subsequent reads return wrong KV bytes with no error

## Modifications

Give every rank a private subdirectory `ssd_offload_path/rank_<dp_rank>_<tp_rank>_<pp_rank>` (created before setup()). The suffix mirrors the per-rank key convention already used in this file (mha_suffix). When storage_config is None the path is used as-is, unchanged from today.

The dp_rank component is required, not cosmetic: with dp-attention, `HiCacheController` reports the attention-group-local rank as tp_rank, which is 0 on every DP rank when attn_tp_size == 1 (e.g. tp8/dp8 DeepSeek), so tp_rank alone collapses all ranks onto one directory. We hit exactly this in a production deployment: 8 clients started in the same second shared one seed and truncated each other's buckets within minutes. `HiCacheStorageConfig` gains a `dp_rank` field (default 0) populated from the dp_rank the controller already computes.

Note for existing SSD-offload deployments: previously offloaded buckets at the directory root are orphaned by the layout change (a one-time cache loss, recomputed on miss - not corruption). They can be deleted.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A - no change to model outputs (client-side storage path handling only).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A - one os.makedirs at engine startup.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: Fix extra_buffer_lazy guard bypass
author: ispobock
body:
## Motivation

#30437 blocks `extra_buffer_lazy` for the DFLASH/DSPARK spec algorithms (their verify bypasses `prepare_mamba_track_for_verify`, so the lazy pending slot never receives the checkpoint scatter yet is still promoted in result processing). The guard was nested under `if view.speculative_num_draft_tokens is not None`, but `_validate_mamba_extra_buffer` runs before `handle_speculative_decoding` resolves that value, and DFLASH derives it from `--speculative-dflash-block-size`. So `--speculative-algorithm DFLASH --speculative-dflash-block-size N --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer_lazy` (without an explicit `--speculative-num-draft-tokens`) sees `None` at validation and the guard is skipped; a lowercase `dflash` also slips past the uppercase string compare.

This keys the check on the algorithm name (present and case-normalized at validation time) instead of `speculative_num_draft_tokens`, so the unsupported combination is rejected regardless of how the block size is passed or cased.

Verified the previously-bypassing configs (`DFLASH`+block_size, lowercase `dflash`, `DSPARK`) now raise at startup, while `EAGLE` / `NEXTN` + `extra_buffer_lazy` stay allowed.

title: [Fix] Reject online weight updates while the HPC-Ops router GEMM split cache is active
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #30247 (merged), addressing @VAthree's [review comment](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30247#discussion_r3619585198): the bf16xfp32 split cache (`w_high`/`w_low` derived from the fp32 router weight) went stale after SGLang's online weight-update APIs. The loaders write parameters in place via `param.data.copy_()`, which changes none of the fields the cache can observe (`data_ptr`/shape/stride/device/dtype, and `.data` writes do not bump `_version` either), so after `update_weights_from_disk/tensor/distributed/ipc` the HPC router kept computing logits from the old weights. Fixed-weight serving was unaffected.

## Modifications

This optimization targets fixed-weight serving, so rather than wiring the derived cache into the weight-update lifecycle, **online weight updates are rejected while the optimization is enabled**, and the enablement signal is **startup-determined and rank-uniform** (addressing the [DP-divergence review catch](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31943#discussion_r3635423390)):

- `kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/gemm.py`: `LongcatFlashRouter.__init__` declares the HPC router GEMM path via `mark_hpc_bf16xfp32_gemm_enabled()` (no-op when the kernel is unavailable); the generic env opt-in (`SGLANG_OPT_BF16_FP32_GEMM_ALGO=hpc`) is a startup constant already. `hpc_bf16xfp32_gemm_enabled()` therefore depends only on startup facts — installed packages, GPU arch, model config — and is **identical on every rank**. It is never set lazily from a forward pass: a lazily set flag would diverge across DP ranks (only ranks whose local batch clears `min_m` build a cache), letting a weight update be rejected on some workers while others proceed, or split a distributed collective. The split-cache path raises if a future call site forgets to declare itself at init.
- `model_runner_components/weight_updater.py`: the four online update entry points (`update_weights_from_disk`, `update_weights_from_tensor` incl. direct/custom/flattened-bucket formats, `update_weights_from_distributed` incl. bucketed, `update_weights_from_ipc`) fail fast with a clear error message — before touching any weight or entering any collective — when the optimization is enabled. Since the check is rank-uniform, an update is either rejected on all workers or proceeds on all workers.
- **CUDA-graph hazard fixed**: the cache key is layout-only (`_version` dropped). Captured graphs replay the split buffers by address, so the buffers are allocated once and can never be reallocated out from under a captured graph by an in-place write.
- Regression tests: (1) the weight updater rejects updates when the optimization is enabled; (2) split-buffer addresses stay stable across `param.data.copy_()` under CUDA-graph capture/replay, with eager and replay staying consistent.

## Validation (H200)

`test/registered/gemm/test_linear_bf16_fp32_hpc.py` — 5 tests / 6 subtests pass on H200 with HPC-Ops installed, plus the LongCat router dispatch unit test:

```
============== 5 passed, 21 warnings, 6 subtests passed in 12.13s ==============
```

In CI (no `hpc` package on runners) the GPU suite skips cleanly; the CPU dispatch test runs as before.

title: [sglang-miles] Fix flush_cache() no-op after pause_generation in retract
author: Zhichenzzz
body:
## Summary

`is_fully_idle()` requires an empty `waiting_queue`, but `pause_generation(mode="retract")`
re-queues every retracted request into `waiting_queue` via `_add_request_to_queue`. So calling
`flush_cache()` right after a retract-mode pause always returned `success=False` and skipped the
actual `tree_cache`/pool reset. One internal caller, `weight_updater.py`'s
`flush_cache_after_weight_update`, asserts on that return value and crashes the whole scheduler
process outright when it hits this (confirmed live -- see below).

Retracted requests already released their KV (`release_req` -> `release_kv_cache(is_insert=False)`,
tagged via `req.is_retracted = True`, cleared on re-admission) and hold no pool/tree_cache state,
so they were never a real reason to block a flush -- the `waiting_queue` check just wasn't written
to distinguish them from a genuinely new, still-pending request.

An `is_retracted`-only exemption turned out to be insufficient under production load: with high
concurrency (in-flight target > engine parallelism) the `waiting_queue` always *also* holds
requests that were **never scheduled at all**. Those carry `is_retracted=False` yet hold no
KV/pool state either -- by definition they never prefilled, and `chunked_req` is cleared by the
retract pause path. Gating the paused-engine flush on them starves weight updates until the
caller's retry budget times out, reproducing the original symptom (hit in RL training at 512
in-flight requests, and in a minimal repro: 64 requests with `--max-running-requests 8` leaves a
~56-request never-scheduled backlog that fails every flush attempt).

**Fix**: `is_fully_idle()` gets an opt-in, default-off `ignore_waiting` param that exempts the
whole `waiting_queue` -- while generation is paused and `running_batch` is drained, nothing queued
holds allocator state, whether it was retracted here or never scheduled. Every existing caller
(`on_idle`, `attach/detach_hicache_storage_wrapped`, `process_input_requests`,
`SchedulerFlushWrapper`) is provably unaffected (regression-tested, default path unchanged).
`flush_cache()` passes `ignore_waiting=self._engine_paused` -- gated on the pause flag
specifically so a flush issued without pausing first can't become silently permissive. Same fix
applied to `release_memory_occupation`'s `assert self.is_fully_idle()`, which crashed outright
under the same condition today.

## Verification

- New test `test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_flush_cache_after_retract.py` (5 cases:
  retracted-only, never-scheduled, and mixed queues flush successfully while paused; the default
  `is_fully_idle()` path and the unpaused flush stay strict).
- Live-server repro on an 8xH200 dev box: raced a real in-flight `/generate` request against
  `pause_generation(mode="retract")` + `/flush_cache`. Pre-fix: `400 "Flush cache failed."`. Same
  scenario post-fix: `200 "Cache flushed."`, with debug instrumentation confirming `retract_all`
  really does move the request into `waiting_queue` in both cases -- the scheduler fix alone
  changes the outcome.
- Never-scheduled-backlog repro (single GPU, Qwen3.5-4B, 64 requests with
  `--max-running-requests 8`): with only the `is_retracted` exemption, every flush attempt after
  a retract pause returns `400`; with the widened gate, the first attempt returns `200`.
- Separately confirmed this fixes a full scheduler crash for callers whose weight-update RPC
  doesn't pass `flush_cache=False` explicitly (defaults to `True` on
  `UpdateWeightsFromTensorReqInput`): reproduced the exact sequence
  (`pause_generation(mode="retract")` with a genuinely in-flight request -> standalone
  `flush_cache` -> `begin_weight_update` -> `/update_weights_from_tensor` with the default
  `flush_cache=True`) against a real Qwen3-4B server. Pre-fix: `AssertionError: Cache flush
  failed after updating weights` inside `flush_cache_after_weight_update`, `SIGQUIT`, engine dies.
  Post-fix: every step returns `200 {"success": true}`.
- Full qwen3.5-4b RL training run on the miles project's torchtitan backend (100/100 rollouts, no
  crashes, functional correctness + GPU utilization confirmed via 3 samples spanning the run) --
  see the paired miles PR (radixark/miles#1750) for the full validation writeup.
- High-concurrency RL stress run (miles fully-async megatron backend, 512 in-flight requests,
  4 retract-mode weight broadcasts per rollout, 20 rollouts ≈ 80 broadcasts, pause-the-world
  eval bursts of 1319 requests): previously died at the first deep-queue weight update; with the
  widened gate it completes with zero flush warnings and intact eval version pinning.

title: [Disagg][NIXL] Fix heterogeneous attn-TP KV transfer for replicated GQA heads (NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND)
author: waynel96
body:
## Motivation

PD disaggregation with the **NIXL** backend crashes with `NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND` on
the first request when prefill and decode use different attention-TP sizes on a
GQA model whose `num_key_value_heads` is smaller than the decode attn-TP size
(e.g. prefill attn_tp=1 -> decode TP=4, Qwen3.5 with 2 KV heads). Fixes #31295.

`NixlKVManager._init_hetero_tp_prep_handle` builds the source dlist with
`num_groups = decode_tp_size // prefill_tp_size`. When `decode_tp_size >
total_kv_heads`, consecutive decode ranks *replicate* a shared KV head, so the
number of *unique* source head-slices is `total_kv_heads`, not `decode_tp_size`.
The old code interleaved one group per decode rank (4) over only 2 KV heads, so
the source descriptors addressed past the registered KV region and
`prep_xfer_dlist("", src_array, "VRAM")` raised `NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND`:

```
File ".../disaggregation/nixl/conn.py", in _init_hetero_tp_prep_handle
    src_handle = self.agent.prep_xfer_dlist("", src_array, "VRAM")
nixl._bindings.nixlNotFoundError: NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND
```

PR #30997 fixed exactly this replicated-KV head map for the **mooncake** backend
and the shared `compute_head_slice_params` helper, but the **NIXL** KV path
(`_init_hetero_tp_prep_handle`) was not updated, so it still crashes. (On
mooncake the same root cause surfaced as silent accuracy loss; on NIXL it is a
hard crash at descriptor-prep time.)

## Modifications

- `_init_hetero_tp_prep_handle` (`prefill_tp <= decode_tp` branch): compute
  `dst_replication = max(1, decode_tp_size // total_kv_heads)`, divide
  `num_groups` by it, and map decode ranks to source heads by integer division
  (`unique_dst_head_idx = dst_tp_rank_in_group // dst_replication`) instead of
  the previous per-rank modulo. Mirrors `compute_head_slice_params` / the
  mooncake backend. When `total_kv_heads >= decode_tp` (or equal-TP),
  `dst_replication == 1` and the arithmetic reduces to the original values
  byte-for-byte -- no behavior change for existing configs.
- Add `TestDisaggregationNixlHeteroTPReplicatedKV` (NIXL, prefill TP1 -> decode
  TP4, GDN-hybrid GQA model) covering this scatter path, which the equal-TP NIXL
  matrix did not.

## Accuracy Tests

Minimal single-node NIXL PD repro (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, `num_key_value_heads=2`),
prefill TP1 + decode TP{1,2,4}, `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_NIXL_BACKEND=UCX`:

| decode TP | branch | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | equal (homogeneous) | PASS | PASS |
| 2 | hetero, groups x heads = 2 = kv_heads | PASS | PASS |
| 4 | hetero, groups x heads = 4 > kv_heads(2) | **NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND** | **PASS** |

After the fix, decode TP4 returns the same tokens as the homogeneous TP1 run
(`" Paris. The capital of France is also"`), confirming correct KV data, not
just a suppressed crash.

title: Fix reward/classification models broken by `load_weights` v2 dispatch (#28671)
author: Jialin
body:
## Motivation
#28671 refactored `LlamaForCausalLM`/`Qwen2ForCausalLM.load_weights` to dispatch to `self._legacy_load_weights` / `self._load_weights_v2`. The reward and classification wrappers (`llama_reward`, `llama_classification`, `qwen2_rm`, `qwen2_classification`) borrow the base loader via an unbound call `Base.load_weights(self, ...)` but inherit only `nn.Module`, so `self` has no `_legacy_load_weights` and weight load fails with `AttributeError` (default path, since v2 is opt-in). This breaks loading of every reward/classification model built on Llama or Qwen2 — e.g. `LxzGordon/URM-LLaMa-3.1-8B` crashes at startup with `'LlamaForSequenceClassificationWithNormal_Weights' object has no attribute '_legacy_load_weights'`.
Call `_legacy_load_weights` directly, restoring the pre-#28671 behavior. These wrapped models are not AutoWeightLoader v2 citizens, so legacy is the correct path.

## Modifications

title: fix(hisparse): correct DSA KV memory budget
author: daii-0818
body:
## Summary

- reuse `calculate_mla_kv_cache_dim()` when profiling MLA KV memory so the budget matches the layout allocated by `DSATokenToKVPool`, including scaled FP8 KV
- scale only the HiSparse DSA indexer term by `host_to_device_ratio`
- add CPU regression coverage for BF16 and FP8 HiSparse layouts

## Root cause

`HiSparseDSATokenToKVPool` allocates the indexer buffer with `size * host_to_device_ratio`, while the profiler budgeted it at `size`. The profiler also used the raw `kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim` for FP8 DSA, although the allocated scaled layout includes FP32 scales and stores RoPE in BF16.

For GLM-5.2 with 78 layers and `host_to_device_ratio=4`, applying only the indexer fix from #28752 estimates 86,112 bytes/token. The actual FP8 MLA and indexer pools require 92,352 bytes/token, leaving 6,240 bytes/token (about 5.8 GiB at one million tokens) unbudgeted.

Supersedes #28752. Thanks @whybeyoung for identifying and implementing the original indexer-ratio fix.

## Test plan

- `PYTHONPATH=python python3 test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_hisparse_pool_configurator.py`
- `pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/model_executor/pool_configurator.py test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_hisparse_pool_configurator.py`
- H20 allocation smoke test with 2 layers and 4,096 FP8 tokens: `kv_cache_dim=656`, `index_buf_size=16,384`, and 9,800,192 allocated bytes matched the expected tensor layouts

title: :bug: [llm][npu][quant] Fix ModelSlim MXFP4 packed weight loading
author: TallMessiWu
body:
# Summary

Fixes offline ModelSlim `W4A4_MXFP4` checkpoint loading on Ascend NPU.

Current ModelSlim exports FP4 weights as packed `uint8` tensors with shape `[out, in//2]`, while SGLang still registered the legacy `float8_e4m3fn [out, in]` checkpoint layout. This caused a shape mismatch when loading newly exported checkpoints.

# Root Cause

ModelSlim now applies `pack_fp4_to_uint8` when exporting `W4A4_MXFP4` weights. The existing SGLang implementation still expected the older one-FP4-per-byte representation and called `npu_dtype_cast` after loading, which would also repack an already-packed weight.

# Changes

- Register `W4A4_MXFP4` weights as packed `uint8 [out, in//2]`.
- Transpose the already-packed weight directly during post-load processing.
- Remove the redundant `npu_dtype_cast` repacking step.

# Validation

- Manually validated with a current ModelSlim `W4A4_MXFP4` packed checkpoint on Ascend NPU.
- Python compilation check passed.
- Black and isort checks passed.

## GSM8K Accuracy
Tested using Qwen3-32B model.
| Configuration | Accuracy (%) | Δ vs bf16 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| bf16 (baseline) | 95.98 | — |
| Offline W4A8 | 95.45 | -0.53 pp (-0.55%) |
| Offline W4A4 | 96.13 | +0.15 pp (+0.16%) |

Note: GSM8K exact match accuracy. Single run each. Δ = (quantized – baseline) in percentage points and relative %.

# Related Issues

Follow-up fix for #23795.

Related to #21584.

title: [Fix] Evict only the KV shortfall in evict_from_tree_cache
author: hnyls2002
body:
- The standard-allocator arm of `evict_from_tree_cache` evicts the full `num_tokens` requirement instead of the shortfall; the SWA arm in the same function already computes `max(0, num_tokens - available)`
- The helper runs on every memory-pressured decode round (`check_decode_mem`) and on the token-allocation paths, so each pressure event destroys up to `available_size` of extra cached prefixes; on `MambaRadixCache` an evicted leaf also frees its mamba checkpoint, which cannot be rebuilt incrementally
- Evict `num_tokens - available` instead, matching the SWA semantics; the predicate outcome is unchanged
