title: [NVIDIA][comm] Merge EP+MoE-TP post-experts all-reduces into one _TP reduction
author: wenscarl
body:
##   Problem statement
With `--tp-size 4 --ep-size 2`, the post-experts reduction requires two
  all-reduces over orthogonal groups (`_MOE_EP` then `_MOE_TP`). The allreduce
  fusion gate was skipping *both* once `fuse_mlp_allreduce` was published, then

  Observed as GSM8k accuracy 0.012 on `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4` with
  silently returning under-reduced activations with no error.

  Observed as GSM8k accuracy 0.012 on `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4` with
  the fused residual+LN kernel reduced over only `_MOE_EP` (2 of 4 peers) —
  silently returning under-reduced activations with no error

## Motivation

  Under hybrid MoE EP+TP (`moe_ep_size > 1` **and** `moe_tp_size > 1`), allreduce
  fusion silently produces under-reduced activations. There is no error — the model
  just returns garbage.

  Reproduced on `main`, 4×GB200:

  ```bash
  python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B \
      --tp-size 4 --ep-size 2 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000
  ```
  ```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:30000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B",
    "messages": [
      {
        "role": "user",
        "content": "Where is capital city of France? Answer in one short word."
      }
    ],
    "chat_template_kwargs": {
      "enable_thinking": false
    },
    "max_tokens": 8,
    "temperature": 0
  }'
  ```

  The completion is garbage unless `--enforce-disable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion`
  is passed. `--ep-size 4` and `--ep-size 1` are both fine.

  ### Root cause

  With `--tp-size 4 --ep-size 2`, the post-experts reduction spans **two** disjoint
  groups (`Qwen3MoeSparseMoeBlock.forward_normal`):

  ```
  moe_expert_parallel_all_reduce        -> _MOE_EP
  moe_tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce  -> _MOE_TP
  ```

  `_MOE_EP × _MOE_TP` is an orthogonal decomposition of the TP world
  (`moe_tp_size = tp_size // moe_ep_size // moe_dp_size`), so both reductions are
  needed to cover all 4 ranks.

  When the decoder publishes `fuse_mlp_allreduce`, `should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce()`
  skips **both** of them — it keys off `should_skip_mlp_all_reduce()`, which does not
  distinguish the EP path from the TP path. The reduction is then supposed to be
  absorbed by the next layer's fused residual+RMSNorm, but that kernel reduces over a
  **single** group: the MoE fusion workspace, which `ensure_workspace_initialized()`
  rendezvouses on `_MOE_EP` when `moe_ep_size > 1`. Net effect: the MoE output is
  reduced over 2 of the 4 required ranks.

  `--ep-size 4` (`moe_tp_size == 1`) and `--ep-size 1` (`moe_ep_size == 1`) are
  unaffected, because there a single group already covers every peer.

  This is pre-existing on `main` and independent of any in-flight FlashInfer work. It
  was surfaced while reviewing #30700 (thanks @mmangkad for the hybrid EP+TP question
  that led here).

 ### Graph illustration

  ## Why hybrid EP+TP specifically

  With `--tp-size 4 --ep-size 2`, `moe_tp_size = 4 // 2 // 1 = 2`, and the MoE
  output needs reducing over two orthogonal subgroups that together tile the TP
  world:

  ```
    rank:      0     1     2     3
    ep_rank:   0     0     1     1     <- which expert shard it holds
    tp_rank:   0     1     0     1     <- which FFN shard it holds

    _MOE_EP:  {0,2}  {1,3}             _MOE_TP:  {0,1}  {2,3}
  ```

  output needs reducing over two orthogonal subgroups that together tile the TP
  world:

  ```
    rank:      0     1     2     3
    ep_rank:   0     0     1     1     <- which expert shard it holds
    tp_rank:   0     1     0     1     <- which FFN shard it holds

    _MOE_EP:  {0,2}  {1,3}             _MOE_TP:  {0,1}  {2,3}
  ```

  Either reduction alone covers 2 of the 4 ranks; both are required.

  ```
    layer N (MoE output)                          | layer N+1
    ----------------------------------------------|------------------------
    main
      experts --> [EP skipped]  [TP skipped] -----|--> fused AR + RMSNorm
                                                  |    workspace group = _MOE_EP
                                                  |    sums {0,2} only  ->  WRONG

    this PR
      experts --> AR(_MOE_EP) --> AR(_MOE_TP) ----|--> RMSNorm
                     {0,2}          {0,1}         |    all 4 ranks summed -> ok
  ```

  Publishing `fuse_mlp_allreduce` makes `should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce()`
  drop **both** reductions, because it keys off that flag without distinguishing
  the EP path from the TP path. The next layer's fused residual+LN then reduces
  over a single group — the MoE fusion workspace, which
  `ensure_workspace_initialized()` rendezvouses on `_MOE_EP` when
  `moe_ep_size > 1`. Half the peers never contribute, and the result is wrong
  without any error.

  No other configuration breaks, because no other configuration has two distinct
  subgroups:

  ```
    ep_size=1  ->  moe_tp_size == tp_size,  _MOE_TP *is* _TP   (parallel_state.py:2483)
    ep_size=4  ->  moe_ep_size == tp_size,  _MOE_EP *is* _TP   (parallel_state.py:2454)
    ep_size=2  ->  neither aliases _TP  ->  the only broken case

  ## Modifications

  `LayerCommunicator.should_fuse_mlp_allreduce_with_next_layer()` now returns `False`
  when `moe_ep_size > 1 and moe_tp_size > 1`. Fusion is only valid when one group
  covers every peer of the reduction, which is not the case here. Both post-experts
  all-reduces then run inline as usual.

  The guard sits before the backend-specific checks, so it covers the aiter fusion
  branch too — that path reduces over a single group for the same reason.

  Attention-side fusion is untouched: it uses the attention-TP workspace
  (`use_attn_tp_group=True`) whose group spans the full TP world, and it is gated on
  `apply_flashinfer_allreduce_fusion` alone, not on `fuse_mlp_allreduce`.

  New unit test `test/registered/unit/layers/test_layer_communicator_fusion_gate.py`
  (CPU, 3 cases): hybrid EP+TP must not fuse; pure-TP and pure-EP must still fuse. The
  hybrid case fails on pre-fix code and passes on the fix; the other two guard against
  the gate degrading to always-off.

After fix:
```
{"id":"0dc05777d22f4efdbbba2ba896d4d196","object":"chat.completion","created":1785440815,"model":"nvidia/Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct-NVFP4","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"Paris","reasoning_content":null,"tool_calls":null},"logprobs":null,"finish_reason":"stop","matched_stop":151645}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":25,"total_tokens":27,"completion_tokens":2,"prompt_tokens_details":null,"reasoning_tokens":0},"metadata":{"weight_version":"default"}}
```

  ## Accuracy Tests

  - `--tp-size 4 --ep-size 2` on 4×GB200 with Qwen3-30B-A3B: garbage before, correct
    completions after, **without** `--enforce-disable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion`.
  - `--ep-size 4` and `--ep-size 1` re-checked for no regression.
  - `python -m pytest test/registered/unit/layers/test_layer_communicator_fusion_gate.py` — 3 passed.

GSM8k:
```
on GB200
python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-shots 8 --num-questions 1316 --parallel 1316
reference: (--tp-size 4 --ep-size 4)
Accuracy: 0.743
Invalid: 0.001
Latency: 18.692 s
Output throughput: 17213.786 token/s

before fix: (--tp-size 4 --ep-size 2)
Accuracy: 0.012
Invalid: 0.014
Latency: 37.922 s
Output throughput: 17453.860 token/s

after fix: (--tp-size 4 --ep-size 2)
Accuracy: 0.777
Invalid: 0.003
Latency: 17.508 s
Output throughput: 16609.659 token/s
```

Also support DSV4:
```
python -m sglang.launch_server --trust-remote-code --model-path nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4 --ep-size 2 --tp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --disable-flashinfer-autotune --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm_routed --max-running-requests 1024 --mem-fraction-static 0.8
  ```
  gsm8k:
  ```
python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-shots 8 --num-questions 1316 --parallel 1316
Accuracy: 0.954
Invalid: 0.000
Latency: 90.583 s
  ```

title: fix: preserve priority for batched embedding requests
author: nikhilkulkarni1755
body:
## Motivation

Closes #32844.

`EmbeddingReqInput.__getitem__` does not forward `priority` to the per-request
sub-objects it builds, so batched embedding requests are scheduled as if no
priority was set. Both the normal and the cross-encoder branch omit it.

The rest of the chain is already correct — `_create_tokenized_object` passes
`obj.priority` through and `handle_embedding_request` reads it. The value is
lost only at the batch split, which `_handle_batch_request` reaches via `obj[i]`.
This also drops the default from `_set_default_priority`, so
`--enable-priority-scheduling` deployments lose their configured default too.

`GenerateReqInput.__getitem__` already forwards `priority`; this makes the
embedding path match.

## Modifications

- Add `priority=self.priority` to both branches of `EmbeddingReqInput.__getitem__`.
- Add a regression test to `test/registered/unit/managers/test_io_struct.py`,
  which is already CI-registered.

## Test Results

- Issue repro, before → after: `None None` → `7 7` (normal),
  `None None` → `3 3` (cross-encoder).
- `pytest test/registered/unit/managers/test_io_struct.py -q` → 25 passed.
  Reverting the fix commit (`git checkout HEAD~2 -- ...`) fails the new test: `[None, None] != [7, 7]`.
- `pre-commit run` passes on both files.

Accuracy and speed tests do not apply — no kernel or model forward code is touched.

title: [diffusion] Fix GLM-Image resolution alignment
author: AuFlow
body:
Fixes #32996

## Motivation

GLM-Image requires image dimensions to be divisible by 32. Previously, different stages could derive incompatible grids for an unaligned request.

For example, with `size="500x500"`, the AR stage used a 30 x 30 token grid (900 tokens), while the diffusion path used a 31 x 31 grid (961 tokens). This caused an internal tensor shape mismatch and an HTTP 500 response.

This PR establishes one consistent D32 policy across the GLM-Image pipeline: each effective dimension is rounded up to the next multiple of 32, while already aligned dimensions remain unchanged. For example:

- `550x1009` becomes `576x1024`.
- An edit input of `1280x720` becomes `1280x736` when `size` is omitted.

## Modifications

- Round each effective GLM-Image dimension up to the next multiple of 32.
- Keep the minimum aligned dimension at 32.
- Normalize explicit dimensions in `GlmImageSamplingParams` before scheduling.
- Emit a warning containing the requested and adjusted resolutions.
- Apply the same alignment in the GLM-Image AR stage for runtime-inferred dimensions.
- Resize unaligned edit condition images consistently for both AR encoding and diffusion conditioning.
- Remove the AR stage's independent floor-based adjustment.
- Validate that dimensions entering AR token generation are aligned.
- Add an optional `data[].resize` field to OpenAI image responses for GLM-Image. The field reports the actual returned image dimensions, including any post-generation upscaling.
- Add unit coverage for upward alignment, minimum dimensions, warnings, edit-image propagation, response dimensions, internal validation, and `size`/`width`/`height` precedence.

## Accuracy Tests

The updated implementation was manually verified with GLM-Image. Previously failing unaligned requests now complete successfully, edit inputs without an explicit `size` use the expected aligned dimensions, and already aligned resolutions remain unchanged.

Targeted unit tests:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest -q \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_glm_image_ar.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_openai_image_api.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_openai_utils.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_sampling_params.py
```

All targeted tests passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance benchmark was run. This change adds only constant-time alignment arithmetic during request preparation and a lightweight read of the generated image dimensions before upload. It does not modify model kernels or the denoising loop.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the changed code with the repository pre-commit configuration.
- [x] Add unit tests for the bug fix.
- [x] Documentation impact was considered. Documentation is deferred to a follow-up PR after the behavior is accepted.
- [x] Provide applicable accuracy and performance information above.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

title: fix(fa4): isolate sheared-bias workspaces by CUDA stream
author: lucifer1004
body:
## Motivation

FA4 uses a reusable staging buffer when converting relative bias into the
column-aligned sheared-bias layout consumed by the attention kernel. The
workspace is currently cached only by CUDA device.

Each relative-bias call launches a producer-consumer pair on its current
stream:

1. the shearing kernel writes the staging buffer;
2. the attention kernel reads that buffer.

CUDA preserves this ordering within one stream, but not between independent
streams. Two concurrent calls on the same device therefore reuse the same
buffer without cross-stream synchronization, allowing one shearing kernel to
overwrite data that another attention kernel has not consumed yet.

## Modifications

- Cache eager-mode sheared-bias workspaces by CUDA device and raw stream
  identity instead of device alone.
- Preserve the existing grow-only reuse policy independently for each stream.
- Query the raw current stream directly to avoid allocating a
  `torch.cuda.Stream` wrapper on the host hot path.
- Add `clear_shear_bias_workspace()` so callers can explicitly drop retained
  staging buffers.
- Keep the existing fake-tensor and CUDA Graph capture behavior unchanged;
  both paths continue to bypass the eager workspace cache.
- Add a deterministic two-stream regression test covering buffer isolation,
  same-stream reuse, event-ordered concurrent access, and cache clearing.

## Accuracy Tests

Run this script against upstream and this PR. CUDA events force stream B's
write between stream A's write and read, so the result does not depend on
scheduler timing:

```python
import torch

from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.flash_attn.cute.interface import (
    _shear_bias_empty,
    _shear_bias_workspace,
)

device = torch.device("cuda", torch.cuda.current_device())
stream_a, stream_b = torch.cuda.Stream(), torch.cuda.Stream()
_shear_bias_workspace.clear()

with torch.cuda.stream(stream_a):
    workspace_a = _shear_bias_empty((4096,), torch.uint8, device)
with torch.cuda.stream(stream_b):
    workspace_b = _shear_bias_empty((4096,), torch.uint8, device)

a_ready, b_done = torch.cuda.Event(), torch.cuda.Event()
observed_a = torch.empty_like(workspace_a)

with torch.cuda.stream(stream_a):
    workspace_a.fill_(1)
    a_ready.record()
with torch.cuda.stream(stream_b):
    stream_b.wait_event(a_ready)
    workspace_b.fill_(2)
    b_done.record()
with torch.cuda.stream(stream_a):
    stream_a.wait_event(b_done)
    observed_a.copy_(workspace_a)

torch.cuda.synchronize()
print(
    {
        "same_pointer": workspace_a.data_ptr() == workspace_b.data_ptr(),
        "cache_entries": len(_shear_bias_workspace),
        "observed_by_a": observed_a.unique().tolist(),
    }
)
assert torch.all(observed_a == 1)
```

Observed results:

| Implementation | Workspace pointers | Cache entries | Value observed by stream A |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Upstream device-only cache | Aliased | 1 | 2 |
| This PR | Distinct | 2 | 1 |

Focused test result:

```text
test_shear_bias_workspace_is_stream_local_and_clearable: 1 passed
```

The test also verifies that a smaller request on the same stream reuses the
existing allocation and that `clear_shear_bias_workspace()` empties the
workspace cache.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

A host-only cache-hit microbenchmark ran 50,000 workspace requests per sample
for seven samples:

| Implementation | Median host time per cache hit |
| --- | ---: |
| Upstream device-only cache | 4.34 us |
| This PR | 4.53 us |

The stream-safe lookup adds approximately 0.19 us per relative-bias call. This
uses the raw current-stream query; constructing a `torch.cuda.Stream` wrapper
on every call was measured separately and intentionally not used.

No attention-kernel instructions or launch configuration are changed by this
PR.

## Checklist

- [x] Format changed code with the repository `prek` hooks.
- [x] Add a deterministic multi-stream regression test.
- [x] No user-facing documentation update is required for this internal
  workspace-management fix.
- [x] Provide correctness reproduction and host-overhead measurements.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code-style guidance.

title: fix(kimi-k3): neutralize a literal image placeholder in user text
author: hnyls2002
body:
A text-only conversation that merely *mentions* `<|kimi_image_placeholder|>` is rejected. Reaching the encoder as a string it surfaces as

```
400 More image placeholders than image prompts.
```

and since the text stays in history, every later request in that conversation fails the same way. The token shows up in ordinary content: `python/sglang/srt/configs/kimi_k3.py` on this branch defines `image_placeholder: str = "<|kimi_image_placeholder|>"`, so simply discussing a model config triggers it.

## Why it happens

K3 images reach the encoder **out of band**: `_flatten_kimi_k3_content` keeps them as structured `image_url` parts, and `_render_content_segments` turns each part into one `image_state.next_prompt()`. sglang never passes an image through the text channel.

The encoder additionally supports an **in-band** form -- a literal placeholder inside text also consumes an image prompt (`_append_text` splits on it). sglang doesn't use that form, but user text containing the literal falls into it anyway, consuming a slot that no image asked for, so the count check fails.

`_flatten_kimi_k3_content` already tried to prevent this by rejecting such text outright, but that guard only ran for list-form `content`. String-form content -- tool results, folded system turns -- bypassed it entirely and hit the encoder's much less obvious error instead. Before this change, all four combinations failed:

| literal in | images | before |
|---|---|---|
| list-form text block | 0 | `ValueError: ... is reserved for Kimi-K3 image input` |
| list-form text block | 1 | same |
| string-form content | 0 | `400 More image placeholders than image prompts.` |
| string-form content | 1 | same |

## Change

Neutralize the literal (`<|kimi_image_placeholder|>` -> `<| kimi_image_placeholder |>`) on both paths instead of rejecting it. A user asking about the token is a legitimate request, and out-of-band image binding is unaffected.

`image_prompts` keeps its exact-count semantics: `["<|media_pad|>"] * len(image_data)` is left as is, so if any future path forgets to neutralize, the encoder still fails loudly rather than silently turning user text into an image token.

## Verification

Driving the real K3 encoder, all four combinations plus the no-literal regression:

```
                                          images  media_pad  literal-as-special
list: text w/ literal, no image                0          0                   0
list: text w/ literal + 1 image                1          1                   0
str:  text w/ literal, no image                0          0                   0
str:  literal + earlier turn w/ image          1          1                   0
regression: 2 images, no literal               2          2                   0
```

`media_pad` always equals the image count, the literal is never promoted to a special token, and it appears in the rendered text as ordinary escaped text.

title: [Fix] attention: Honor selected FlashAttention implementation
author: lucifer1004
body:
## Motivation

`FlashAttentionBackend` selects the requested FlashAttention implementation
during initialization and stores its varlen entry point in
`self.flash_attn_varlen_func`.

The KV-cache-skipping prefill path bypasses that selected callable and invokes
the module-level generic wrapper instead. Because the call does not pass
`ver`, the wrapper uses its default `ver=3`. A backend configured for FA4 can
therefore silently execute FA3 when `fa_skip_kv_cache` is enabled.

## Modifications

- Route KV-cache-skipping prefill through the varlen callable selected by the
  backend.
- Leave the generic module-level wrapper available to the existing MLA paths
  that explicitly pass `ver`.

## Accuracy Tests

Run this minimal reproduction against upstream and this PR:

```python
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import patch

import torch

from sglang.test.test_utils import maybe_stub_sgl_kernel

maybe_stub_sgl_kernel()

from sglang.srt.layers.attention import flashattention_backend
from sglang.srt.layers.radix_attention import AttentionType

q = torch.randn(2, 1, 4)
k = torch.randn(2, 1, 4)
v = torch.randn(2, 1, 4)
calls = []


def generic_flash_attn(**kwargs):
    calls.append("generic")
    return torch.zeros_like(kwargs["q"])


def selected_flash_attn(**kwargs):
    calls.append("selected")
    return torch.ones_like(kwargs["q"])


metadata = SimpleNamespace(
    cache_seqlens_int32=torch.tensor([2], dtype=torch.int32),
    cu_seqlens_k=torch.tensor([0, 2], dtype=torch.int32),
    cu_seqlens_q=torch.tensor([0, 2], dtype=torch.int32),
    fa_skip_cu_seqlens_q=None,
    fa_skip_max_seqlen_q=None,
    local_attn_metadata=None,
    max_seq_len_q=2,
    page_table=torch.tensor([[0, 1]], dtype=torch.int32),
)
backend = object.__new__(flashattention_backend.FlashAttentionBackend)
backend.__dict__.update(
    attention_chunk_size=None,
    attn_cp_size=1,
    fa_impl_ver=4,
    fa_skip_kv_cache=True,
    flash_attn_varlen_func=selected_flash_attn,
    forward_metadata=metadata,
    has_local_attention=False,
    kv_cache_dtype_str="auto",
    kv_cache_is_mxfp8=False,
    num_splits=1,
    page_size=1,
    token_to_kv_pool=SimpleNamespace(get_kv_buffer=lambda _: (k, v)),
    topk=1,
    use_mla=False,
)
layer = SimpleNamespace(
    attn_type=AttentionType.DECODER,
    head_dim=4,
    is_cross_attention=False,
    k_scale=None,
    layer_id=0,
    logit_cap=0.0,
    scaling=0.5,
    sliding_window_size=-1,
    tp_k_head_num=1,
    tp_q_head_num=1,
    tp_v_head_num=1,
    v_head_dim=4,
    v_scale=None,
)
forward_batch = SimpleNamespace(
    _attn_output=None,
    attn_cp_metadata=None,
    extend_num_tokens=2,
    forward_mode=SimpleNamespace(
        is_context_parallel_extend=lambda: False,
        is_target_verify=lambda: False,
    ),
)

with patch.object(
    flashattention_backend,
    "flash_attn_varlen_func",
    generic_flash_attn,
):
    output = backend.forward_extend(q, k, v, layer, forward_batch)

print({"calls": calls, "output": output.unique().tolist()})
assert calls == ["selected"]
assert torch.all(output == 1)
```

Observed results:

| Implementation | Called entry point | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Upstream | Generic wrapper (`ver=3` default) | Assertion fails |
| This PR | Backend-selected FA4 callable | Passes |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No attention kernel, launch configuration, or tensor transformation is
changed. The patch replaces the generic Python dispatcher with the callable
already selected and stored by `FlashAttentionBackend`; no additional host or
device work is introduced.

## Checklist

- [x] Format changed code with the repository `prek` hooks.
- [x] Provide a minimal reproduction that fails on upstream and passes with
  this fix.
- [x] No user-facing documentation update is required for this internal
  backend-dispatch fix.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code-style guidance.

title: [Fix] Clear stale FlashInfer BF16 MoE index cache
author: zianglih
body:
## Motivation

@humansand

Colocated RL weight updates pause and offload the rollout model before loading new weights. `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod` caches FlashInfer permutation-index tensors on the GPU, so those tensors can point to released memory after the model resumes. Reusing them during post-load processing can corrupt the shuffled BF16 expert weights.

[sgl-project/sglang#28676](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28676) fixed the equivalent MXFP8 cache, but mixed-precision checkpoints with BF16 experts use this separate cache in `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod`.

ModelOpt NVFP4 quantized experts do not need the same clear: `prepare_static_weights_for_trtllm_fp4_moe()` creates its permutation-index dictionary locally for each post-load call. The BF16 experts in the first/last layers, plus the BF16 shared experts, use `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod`, whose persistent instance cache is what this PR clears.

## Modifications

Clear the FlashInfer TRT-LLM BF16 permutation-index cache once at the start of each post-load processing cycle. The rebuilt indices are still reused across experts within that cycle.

## Accuracy Tests

- Targeted external regression test for two consecutive BF16 FlashInfer post-load cycles: `1 passed`.
- DeepSeek V3.2 5-layer MXFP8 Miles E2E on 8x B200 with 8-GPU training and 8-GPU colocated rollout:
  - dense FP8 GEMM backend: `flashinfer_cutlass`
  - MoE backend: `flashinfer_trtllm_routed`
  - 3/3 rollouts and 24/24 training steps completed
  - the one injected rollout-engine failure was detected and one engine was recovered
  - weight-checker lifecycle completed and the Ray job succeeded
- GLM-5.2 5-layer ModelOpt NVFP4 Miles E2E on 8x B200 with 8-GPU training and 8-GPU colocated rollout:
  - environment: FlashInfer `0.6.15.post1`; image-pinned SGLang commit `3fe50eddf881b4f33c60c1867af84eeb1626d91d` with only this PR's patch applied
  - rollout: four TP2/DP2/EP2 engines with `flashinfer_trtllm_routed`
  - 2/2 rollouts, 2/2 training steps, and 3/3 weight-update/resume cycles completed
  - Ray job succeeded without a crash or hang
- `pre-commit run --all-files`: passed.

No test file is included in this PR.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The cache clear runs only during weight post-processing, not in the model forward path.

title: [rust-server] fix TCP-layer TTFT stalls
author: sherlockwu
body:
Two TCP-layer TTFT stalls in the Rust server, found benchmarking Rust vs Python TM (gpt-oss-120b + MiMo-V2.5-Pro, 8×B300, `bench_serving` c=1, seed 42, `--disable-radix-cache`):

1. **~200 ms on large request bodies.** A headers+body burst larger than the kernel's initial rcvbuf (`tcp_rmem[1]` = 87380 B) drops its tail before hyper polls the body; recovery is the client's RTO retransmit (~200 ms, measured `tcpi_total_retrans=3`; threshold bisected to 75→91 KB). Hits the first large-body request of every connection — i.e. every request for fresh-connection clients like `bench_serving`. **Fix:** `SO_RCVBUF` 16 MiB on the listener (inherited by accepted sockets; covers a 1M-token body; lazily allocated; clamped by `net.core.rmem_max`).
2. **+13 ms on keep-alive connections.** hyper/axum doesn't set `TCP_NODELAY` (Python's asyncio does); Nagle + delayed-ACK. **Fix:** `set_nodelay(true)` via `ListenerExt::tap_io`.

All rows measured on current `main` (`55b6769b0e`), unfixed vs this PR, Python TM on the same base as reference:

| TTFT (mean ms) | before | after | Python TM ref |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| gpt-oss 16K in | 192 (P99 369) | **157 (P99 161)** | 166 |
| gpt-oss 64K in | 1253 (P99 1463) | **1047 (P99 1060)** | 1080 |
| MiMo 64K in | 2197 | **1957** | 1986 |
| MiMo 256K in | 9716 | **9513** | 9669 |
| gpt-oss in=1, keep-alive ×128 | 40.9 | **26.4** | 26.4 |

Raw-socket probe (headers+390 KB in one `send`, time to response headers): 208 ms → 0.4 ms. Decode path unaffected (ITL parity with Python through c=256).

title: [Fix] Disable --enable-symm-mem under CUDA graphs on Kimi hybrid models
author: hnyls2002
body:
Symmetric-memory allocations are per-forward, so an address taken from that pool during graph capture is neither reserved for the graph's lifetime nor at the same offset on every rank. Under capture this corrupts DSPARK speculative decoding: accept collapses to 1.000, or (worse) the server silently emits garbage while reporting accept pinned at the ceiling, with no error. The flag is now forced off on Kimi hybrid archs unless every phase runs eager; the auto-probed K3 fused all-reduce is faster than the symm-mem path anyway.

title: [diffusion] fix: bind each rank to accelerator before distributed init
author: dayanandav
body:
maybe_init_distributed_environment_and_model_parallel() only bound CUDA/NPU devices, and did so after the process groups were created. On XPU/MUSA no branch ran at all, so current_device() stayed 0 on every rank and index-less allocations piled all ranks onto GPU 0 (OOM with GPUs 1..N-1 idle). Even on CUDA/NPU, GroupCoordinator built its groups and communicator against device 0. Separately,
GPUWorker.init_device_and_model() called argless torch.get_device_module().set_device(), which raises AttributeError on MPS (torch.mps has no set_device).

Add a Platform.set_device() classmethod dispatching through torch.get_device_module(device).set_device(device) -- one path for CUDA, ROCm, NPU, XPU, MUSA and CPU -- overridden as a no-op on MPS, and call it via current_platform before process-group creation. 

## Motivation
Fixes #33031.

`maybe_init_distributed_environment_and_model_parallel()` in `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/distributed/parallel_state.py` bound each rank to its accelerator incorrectly in three ways:

1. **Non-CUDA/NPU platforms were never bound.** The device-setting block only covered `is_cuda_alike()` and `is_npu()`, so on XPU/MUSA no branch was taken and `current_device()` stayed `0` on every rank. Any allocation without an explicit index — torch.empty(..., device="xpu")`, `.to(device_type)`, module materialization during model load — landed on device 0 for all ranks. With `--num-gpus N` this piles all N ranks' weights and activations onto GPU 0, causing OOM at a fraction of expected capacity while GPUs 1..N-1 sit idle, plus cross-device traffic on every collective.

2. **The binding ran too late.** Even on CUDA/NPU the block sat *below* `init_distributed_environment()` and `initialize_model_parallel()`. `GroupCoordinator.__init__` calls `torch.distributed.new_group()` and initializes its device communicator before any `set_device` had run, so group and communicator setup bound against device 0.

3. **`GPUWorker.init_device_and_model()` crashed on MPS.** It called argless `torch.get_device_module().set_device(self.local_rank)`. Argless `get_device_module()` returns the current accelerator's module; on MPS that is `torch.mps`, which has no `set_device`, raising `AttributeError: module 'torch.mps' has no attribute 'set_device'`.

## Modifications

- `runtime/platforms/interface.py`: add a `Platform.set_device(device)` classmethod that dispatches through `torch.get_device_module(device).set_device(device)`. This covers CUDA, ROCm,  NPU, XPU and MUSA through one code path instead of a per-platform `if/elif` chain that has to be extended for every new accelerator. CPU is covered too `torch.cpu.set_device` exists and is a no-op.
- `runtime/platforms/mps.py`: override `set_device()` as a no-op, since MPS exposes a single device and `torch.mps` has no `set_device`.
- `runtime/distributed/parallel_state.py`: call `current_platform.set_device(device)` *before* `init_distributed_environment()` so process-group and communicator creation happen on the correct device, and delete the trailing CUDA/NPU-only block. `device` already comes from `get_local_torch_device()`, which is per-rank, so the local recomputation of `torch.device(f"cuda:{local_rank}")` was redundant.
- `runtime/managers/gpu_worker.py`: replace `torch.get_device_module().set_device(self.local_rank)` with `current_platform.set_device(current_platform.get_device(self.local_rank))` which is MPS-safe and resolves the device type per platform.

## Accuracy Tests

This PR does not touch kernels or model forward code, so outputs are unchanged on any platform that was already binding correctly (CUDA/NPU single-GPU).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No kernel or scheduling changes, so there is no expected throughput change on platforms that were already binding correctly.

title: fix(xpu): enable compressed-tensors FP8 W8A8 on XPU (RedHatAI FP8-dynamic models)
author: vshekhawat-hlab
body:
## Motivation

compressed-tensors FP8 W8A8 quantized models (e.g. RedHatAI's `*-FP8-dynamic` family — `Apertus-8B-Instruct-2509-FP8-dynamic`, `Mistral-Small-3.1-24B-Instruct-2503-FP8-dynamic`, `granite-4.0-h-small-FP8-dynamic`, `NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2-FP8-dynamic`) currently fail to serve on XPU. The very first failure happens at layer-construction time, before any kernel dispatch:

```
AssertionError: Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled
```

Fixing that surfaces two further, distinct XPU-specific issues before the model actually serves and generates correctly.

## Modifications

- `compressed_tensors.py` (`CompressedTensorsConfig`): `_check_scheme_supported` unconditionally called `torch.cuda.get_device_capability()`, which is CUDA-only. Only `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8` has a real XPU-usable kernel path today (via the existing device-agnostic `_apply_fallback_scaled_mm` in `fp8_utils.py`, not a missing native kernel); every other capability-gated scheme (NVFP4/cutlass, Marlin-based W8A16Fp8, WNA16, ...) is explicitly rejected with a clean `RuntimeError` on XPU instead of crashing on the CUDA-only call.
- `fp8_kernel.py`: the non-CUDA/non-MUSA branch never imported `sgl_per_token_quant_fp8`/`sgl_per_tensor_quant_fp8` for XPU, even though sgl-kernel-xpu registers both natively — this caused a `NameError` on the first forward pass once the above crash was fixed.
- `fp8_utils.py` (`apply_fp8_linear`): the activation-quant padding decision (`num_token_padding=17`, meant to make `torch._scaled_mm` more performant on CUDA for small batches) was only skipped when `cutlass_fp8_supported` (CUDA-only). sgl-kernel-xpu's per-token quant kernel requires `output_q` to exactly match `input`'s shape and doesn't support padded output, raising a shape-mismatch `RuntimeError` whenever a forward pass had fewer than 17 rows (e.g. small prefill/decode steps).
-  fp8.py (Fp8MoEMethod.apply): the native sgl-kernel-xpu MoE fast path was taken unconditionally on XPU, before checking the explicitly-selected MoE runner backend.
  This made --moe-runner-backend triton a no-op on XPU for this quantization scheme — the native kernel path was still hit and raised "current MoE does not support
  use_fp8_w8a8" even when the Triton runner had been explicitly requested. Now skips the native XPU path when the runner backend is explicitly triton, falling through to
  the existing Triton dispatch below.
- internvl.py: InternVLChatConfig has no top-level num_experts — the MoE config lives on the nested llm_config (the text-backbone config). Fixes an AttributeError when
  loading MoE-based InternVL variants.
- runtime_context.py (get_stream): replaced a hardcoded torch.cuda.Stream() with torch.get_device_module(device).Stream(), so the named process-level side stream is 
  created on whichever device backend is active instead of always assuming CUDA.
- topk.py (biased_grouped_topk_gpu, XPU path): the topk_sigmoid kernel requires correction_bias to be float32. The CUDA branch a few lines above already casts it; the 
 XPU branch passed it through unchanged, raising RuntimeError: correction_bias must be float32 on the first generation request for some MoE models. Now cast to float32 
  before the call, matching the CUDA branch.

## Accuracy Tests

Verified locally end-to-end in a docker container (XPU backend, Intel Arc Pro/BMG) with the patched sglang installed in place of the image's baked-in copy:

- `RedHatAI/Apertus-8B-Instruct-2509-FP8-dynamic` (TP=1, `--attention-backend intel_xpu`) serves and evaluates gsm8k (5-shot) correctly:
  - `exact_match,flexible-extract = 0.5891 ± 0.0136`
  - `strict-match = 0.5390 ± 0.0137`
- Regression check that the shared code paths touched here don't affect other backends/schemes:
  - All three changes are gated behind `if _is_xpu:` / `elif _is_xpu:` branches that are new no-ops on every other platform; `cutlass_fp8_supported`-driven CUDA behavior is unchanged (verified by re-reading every other call site of the touched functions — `scaled_fp8_quant`'s other callers in `fp8_utils.py` are gated by `if _is_cuda:`/`if _is_hip:`, never reaching the changed XPU branch on other devices).
  - No currently-passing XPU model can regress from these changes: any compressed-tensors quantized model on XPU previously hit the `_check_scheme_supported` crash unconditionally at layer-construction time (before this PR), so none could have been passing beforehand.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable — these are correctness/compatibility fixes for an existing fallback code path (`_apply_fallback_scaled_mm`), no new kernel or scheduling changes. The activation-quant padding skip on XPU has a minor performance implication (an extra kernel-launch on small batches that would otherwise reuse a padded buffer), but padding was never functional on XPU before this PR (it crashed), so there's no regression relative to current behavior.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Fix] [AMD] dsa: Align Aiter paged rows with DP-attention metadata
author: dorado269
body:
## Motivation

With DP-attention padding, `Indexer._get_topk_paged` can receive physical query and weight rows beyond the real query count `q_offset`. Aiter sizes its logits from the query tensor, while top-k sizes from the real-row metadata, so padded inputs fail the top-k row check. The padding restoration after top-k also excluded HIP.

Reproduced on MI355X (DeepSeek-V3.2, TP8 + `--attn-dp-size 8`, EAGLE MTP 3/1/4, eager steps above `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16`): on unpatched main an eager step arrives with `q_offset=60` real rows and 64 physical rows, and the server dies in `sgl_kernel.fast_topk_transform_fused` with `RuntimeError: lengths must have one entry per score row`.

## Modifications

- Slice the Aiter query and weight inputs to `q_offset`, the same real-row contract the other paged backends use.
- Restore trailing `-1` top-k rows on HIP as well, so callers still get one row per physical query row.
- When `q_offset == 0`, return all-`-1` int32 indices without launching Aiter or top-k. This is a defensive guard: Aiter's [SplitKV scheduling](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/blob/7559e3411beecb04d2f64ac488d6990a3b03534e/aiter/ops/triton/attention/pa_mqa_logits.py#L711) divides by the query count, and no run below reached this branch.
- Add a CPU regression test for the row contract with Aiter and top-k stubbed (`base-a-test-cpu`).

## Accuracy and validation (8x MI355X)

| Test (8x MI355X) | This PR | Unpatched main |
|---|---|---|
| `test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_deepseek_v32_dp_eval_mi35x.py` (TP8, attn-dp 8, tilelang DSA) | **OK**: GSM8K 0.957 (threshold 0.935), bs1 64.5 tok/s | not run |
| `test/registered/amd/test_deepseek_v32_basic.py` (AMD CI mode: TP class runs, DP class skipped) | **OK**: GSM8K 0.958, bs1 97.1 tok/s | not run |
| Same DP server as the mi35x DP eval + EAGLE MTP 3/1/4, `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16 --max-running-requests 512` so steps also run eagerly | **OK**: GSM8K 0.951, accept length 3.07; padded rows reached in DECODE (e.g. 55 real / 57 physical) and DRAFT_EXTEND_V2 (e.g. 224 / 232) | **server crash**: DECODE with 60 real / 64 physical rows, then `RuntimeError: lengths must have one entry per score row` |
| `test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi30x/test_deepseek_v32_dp_eval_amd.py` (MI300 config, triton DSA backends; run on MI355X) | FAIL: GSM8K 0.569 / 0.331 (two attempts) | FAIL: GSM8K 0.353 / 0.398 |

The MI300 config fails on MI355X with and without this PR, so the failure exists on main and is not caused by this change. It still needs a real MI300 run.

Setup: image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.23-rocm10-mi35x-20261101`, this PR installed with `pip install --no-deps -e python`, AMD CI env (`SGLANG_IS_IN_CI=1 SGLANG_IS_IN_CI_AMD=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT=0 GPU_ARCHS=gfx950`, `/opt/tilelang` on `PYTHONPATH`), weights `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2`. The GPU runs used head `ab4407a57c` (base `23c6442cde`); those results remain specific to that source and hardware. The current published head is `31d19a218f`, rebased onto main `732d34b93c`. A November 5 audit also applied the unchanged patch to main `c07ec416da` in an isolated checkout: all 12 CPU row-contract cases passed on both the published head and that integration, while unpatched `c07ec416da` failed the 10 padded/empty-row cases and passed the two unpadded controls. The patched `_get_topk_paged` method is AST-equivalent to the GPU-tested `ab4407a57c`; surrounding code has changed since those GPU runs. This source audit and CPU regression do not constitute a new GPU or end-to-end qualification.

Notes for reviewers:
- The two DP eval files are not wired into any workflow, and `/rerun-test` has no AMD job, so they were run manually as listed. `test_deepseek_v32_basic.py` skips its DP class under AMD CI, so its CI-mode run covers TP only.
- No MI300 host was available. `test_deepseek_v32_dp_eval_amd.py` (MI300 config) was run on MI355X; an MI300 run is still welcome.
- By code reading, the plain DP eval does not reach the padded branch (without MTP, decode keeps `q_offset == rows`); it is a no-regression check. The MTP + eager run is the one that exercises the fix, as its trace shows.

## Checklist

- [x] CPU regression test registered in `base-a-test-cpu`.
- [x] DeepSeek-V3.2 DP-attention accuracy on MI355X, with and without MTP.

title: [Fix] Honor FlashMLA natural-log LSE in DCP reduction
author: CyberSecurityErial
body:
## Motivation

FlashMLA returns natural-log softmax LSE, while the MLA DCP merge paths currently treat all decode LSE as base-2. As a result, FlashMLA + DCP computes incorrect cross-rank softmax weights and attention output.

For partition functions `Z = [2, 8]` and a second-shard local output of `10`, the correct contribution is `8`. Interpreting `[ln(2), ln(8)]` with `exp2` produces `7.2330317` instead.

Fixes #33064.

## Modifications

- Make the AG/RS Triton correction kernel select `exp/log` or `exp2/log2` through a compile-time LSE-base flag.
- Propagate that flag through `cp_lse_ag_out_rs_mla`.
- Select natural-log LSE for the `flashmla` attention backend in both MLA DCP communication paths:
  - all-gather LSE + reduce-scatter output;
  - A2A/FlashInfer-A2A LSE reduction.
- Keep base-2 as the default, so FlashInfer MLA behavior is unchanged.
- Add a GPU regression for the exact natural-log weighting error and a routing test for backend selection.

## Accuracy Tests

Tested on one NVIDIA H20 GPU with the branch source based on `585a7d05e384c79ee17bf3185c7469fe8ce75946`:

```text
PYTHONPATH=/work/flashmla-lse/python python3 -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/kernels/test_dcp_lse_combine.py \
  -k "flashmla_natural_log_lse_correction or flashmla_selects_natural_log_lse"

2 passed, 21 deselected in 24.83s
```

The full related test file also passes:

```text
PYTHONPATH=/work/flashmla-lse/python python3 -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/kernels/test_dcp_lse_combine.py

23 passed in 25.88s
```

The warnings emitted by the container are unrelated environment/deprecation warnings; there were no test failures.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. This fixes output correctness. The log-base branch is a Triton `tl.constexpr`, so it is specialized at compilation rather than selected per element at runtime.

- [x] Format the modified files according to the project formatter.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [ ] Update documentation (not needed: no public API or user-facing configuration change).

title: [Fix] Allow flashinfer_sparse_mla DSA backend for HiSparse on SM120 FP8 KV
author: gongwei1027
body:
## Motivation

`--enable-hisparse` cannot start at all on SM120/SM121 (RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 5090) with FP8 KV cache, because two parts of the argument pipeline disagree about which DSA backend is legal.

The resolution pass already selects `flashinfer_sparse_mla` for GLM DSA models on SM120 with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` — it is the only DSA kernel available on that architecture (`_dsa_split_backend_resolution`, `is_glm_sm12_fp8` arm in `python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/overrides.py`). But the HiSparse validator in `hisparse_hook.py` still whitelisted only `flashmla_kv` for FP8 KV, so the server dies during argument validation:

```
ValueError: HiSparse supports DSA prefill backend(s) ['flashmla_kv'] on this
platform with --kv-cache-dtype=fp8_e4m3, but got
--dsa-prefill-backend=flashinfer_sparse_mla. Please use
--dsa-prefill-backend=flashmla_kv or omit it.
```

The suggestion in that message is also unsatisfiable on SM120: `flashmla_kv` is not available there, and omitting the flag re-derives `flashinfer_sparse_mla` and fails again.

The runtime path already supports this combination on current `main` — `flashinfer_sparse_mla` and its SM120 kernel path landed in #26928 — so only the startup-time allow-list was stale. The end-to-end run below confirms this.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/hisparse_hook.py`:
- Add `flashinfer_sparse_mla` to `HISPARSE_CUDA_DSA_BACKENDS_BY_DTYPE["fp8_e4m3"]` and to the unknown-dtype fallback set in `_hisparse_allowed_backends`.
- Fix the error message to list the full allowed set instead of suggesting a single default backend.

No supported configuration changes for other platforms or KV-cache dtypes:
- BF16 KV still allows only `flashmla_sparse`.
- ROCm still allows only `{tilelang, aiter}`.
- Arch/model/device narrowing for `flashinfer_sparse_mla` is unchanged and still enforced later by `flash_mla_sm120._validate_flashinfer_sparse_mla_backend`, which rejects it for anything other than GLM DSA + FP8 KV + SM120/SM121. This change only stops HiSparse from pre-emptively rejecting a backend the resolver itself chose.

`docs_new/docs/advanced_features/hisparse_guide.mdx`: document the SM120/SM121 GLM + FP8 case in the DSA backend note and Key Notes.

`test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py`: add `test_hisparse_accepts_flashinfer_sparse_mla_on_cuda_fp8` to `TestHiSparseDsaBackendPolicy`, asserting both prefill and decode validators accept `flashinfer_sparse_mla` under FP8 KV.

## Unit Tests

Run on real SM120 hardware in the nightly image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20260729-16a52bff` (`sglang.__version__ == 0.0.0.dev1+gcb12a1547` — the tag carries the pipeline trigger SHA, the built source is `cb12a1547`). That revision's `hisparse_hook.py` is byte-identical to this PR's base, so the baseline behavior it exhibits is the behavior this PR changes:

```
$ git diff cb12a1547 e3d4f48e55 -- python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/hisparse_hook.py
(empty)
```

```
$ pytest test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py -k HiSparse -q
# baseline (before this PR's test case)
12 passed, 106 deselected, 15 warnings in 8.73s

# with this PR's test case added
test_hisparse_accepts_flashinfer_sparse_mla_on_cuda_fp8 PASSED [ 30%]
13 passed, 106 deselected, 15 warnings in 7.39s
```

Allow-set assertions with the patched hook:

```
ALLOWSET_fp8  = ['flashinfer_sparse_mla', 'flashmla_kv']
ALLOWSET_bf16 = ['flashmla_sparse']
Set DSA backends for GLM FP8 KV Cache on SM120/SM121: prefill=flashinfer_sparse_mla, decode=flashinfer_sparse_mla.
Ran 4 tests in 0.827s
OK
```

Negative control — reverting only the fp8 allow-set entry, everything else unchanged, reproduces the original startup failure:

```
REVERTED allow-set: ['flashmla_kv']
ValueError: HiSparse supports DSA prefill backend(s) ['flashmla_kv'] on this platform
with --kv-cache-dtype=fp8_e4m3, but got --dsa-prefill-backend=flashinfer_sparse_mla.
```

CI coverage note: the upstream SM120 PR-test runners are 5090 (32 GB), which cannot host GLM-5.2, so no CI job exercises this configuration end-to-end. CI covers the allow-list policy through the CPU-only unit test above; the hardware validation below covers the rest.

## Accuracy Tests

Full PD-disaggregated GLM-5.2-NVFP4 deployment:

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| GPU | 2 nodes × 8 × RTX PRO 6000 (SM120, 96 GB), TP=8 per node |
| Model / quantization | GLM-5.2, `modelopt_fp4` |
| KV cache dtype | `fp8_e4m3` |
| Attention backend | `dsa`, prefill = decode = `flashinfer_sparse_mla` |
| HiSparse config | `{"top_k": 2048, "device_buffer_size": 4096, "host_to_device_ratio": 10}` |
| Topology | P (prefill, no HiSparse) → D (decode, `--enable-hisparse --disable-radix-cache`), mooncake transfer over `mlx5_0` |
| SGLang build | same image as the unit tests above (`nightly-dev-20260729-16a52bff`), with this PR's `hisparse_hook.py` applied |

Decode instance startup with the fix:

```
Set DSA backends for GLM FP8 KV Cache on SM120/SM121: prefill=flashinfer_sparse_mla, decode=flashinfer_sparse_mla.
The server is fired up and ready to roll!
```

Without the fix the decode instance never reaches this point — it aborts in argument validation with the `ValueError` quoted above.

Single-request correctness through the P→D path:

```
$ curl http://router:8000/generate -d '{"text":"What is 1+1?","sampling_params":{"max_new_tokens":20,"temperature":0,"ignore_eos":true}}'
{"text":" I will give brainliest.\n\nStep-by-step explanation:\n\n1+1=2\n\n(If this", ...
 "finish_reason":{"type":"length","length":20},"prompt_tokens":7,"completion_tokens":20,
 "e2e_latency":0.5475991275161505}
HTTP=200 TIME=0.549638
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This PR only changes a startup-time allow-list — no kernel, no forward path — so it cannot affect throughput on any platform. As a liveness check that the unblocked path is usable rather than merely startable, a sustained load through the PD router (54 in-flight requests, input 32k / output 4k, 660 s) held steady state at 54/54 running requests with 701.73 tok/s average gen throughput (354 decode batches) and zero retractions.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).

title: [Fix] Make wait_port_available actually wait timeout_s seconds
author: elvischenv
body:
## Motivation

`wait_port_available` loops `for i in range(timeout_s)` but sleeps `0.1s` per iteration, so the real wall-clock wait is `timeout_s / 10`. The default 30s timeout gives up after ~3s, and CI's `SGLANG_WAIT_PORT_TIMEOUT=120` (`python/sglang/test/test_utils.py:933`) waits only ~12s.

Everything around the loop already assumes one second per iteration — the progress log reads `"Waiting for {i} seconds for {port_name} to be available"` using the raw loop counter, and the failure raises `"not available in {timeout_s} seconds"`. The `0.1s` sleep has been the odd one out since #7748.

This is what #31281 needs in order to work as intended: it introduced `SGLANG_WAIT_PORT_TIMEOUT` because a killed server on GB300 can hold its ports for >30s while GPU teardown completes, but with the `0.1s` sleep even the 120s CI setting only bought ~12s of patience.

## Modifications

Sleep `1s` per iteration in `wait_port_available`, so the advertised timeout is the real one.

Impact:

- **No added latency on the happy path.** `is_port_available` is checked at the top of the loop body, so an available port returns before the first sleep. All call sites (`python/sglang/srt/server_args.py:9229-9241`, the `PortArgs` precheck) hit this path during normal startup.
- **A genuinely occupied port now errors after 30s instead of ~3s.** That is the documented contract, but it is a user-visible change for the "launched twice on the same port" case.
- The `i > 10 and i % 5 == 0` diagnostic log now fires at 15s/20s/25s instead of three times within 3 seconds, matching the "Waiting for {i} seconds" wording.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — startup-time port precheck only, no effect on model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A — no effect on inference; the happy path does not sleep at all.

title: [Fix] Repair verify mask test fixture
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Summary

- fix the current-main Base CPU CI failure by adding the missing `model_config.context_len` contract to the verify-mask hybrid backend fixture
- remove a stale test description and correct the `FULL_MASK` capacity documentation

## Root cause

This fixes a deterministic Base CI failure present on current `main`, reproduced by [`base-a-test-cpu (1)` in run #30633567943](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30633567943/job/91165643750).

`HybridAttnBackend.__init__` now reads `model_runner.model_config.context_len`, but the lightweight fixture in `test_verify_mask.py` did not provide `model_config`. The registered Base CPU test therefore failed during backend construction before reaching its assertions.

## Regression timeline

- **06:13 UTC — [#32920](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32920) merged.** It introduced the lightweight `_make_hybrid_backend` fixture. At that point `HybridAttnBackend` did not read `model_runner.model_config`, so the fixture still matched the constructor contract.
- **11:43 UTC — [#32690](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32690) merged.** It added the unconditional `model_runner.model_config.context_len` read and updated other lightweight fixtures, but missed `test_verify_mask.py`. From this point, current `main` contained the deterministic regression.
- **13:21 UTC — [#33074](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33074) reproduced the failure after incorporating `main`.** Its own diff touches neither `HybridAttnBackend` nor `test_verify_mask.py`; [`base-a-test-cpu (1)`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30633567943/job/91165643750) failed with the missing-`model_config` `AttributeError`. Therefore #33074 is an affected PR, while #32690 is the direct regression trigger.

## Impact

This restores the registered verify-mask CPU test and prevents the deterministic fixture failure from cascading into unrelated PR checks.

## Validation

title: [AMD][Fix] Restore aiter-padded MoE weight dims for serialized checkpoints
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

`dcd9014f15` ("[AMD][MXFP4] Reland Online MXFP4 quantization 2/N - FP8 to MXFP4 requantization on AMD GPUs", #28291) silently broke accuracy for **serialized** MXFP4 Quark MoE checkpoints on ROCm whenever the per-rank MoE intermediate size needs aiter padding.

On Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4 at TP8 on MI355 this drops GSM8K from **0.99 to 0.54**. The failure is not obvious garbage — output stays fluent English, but the model loses knowledge and frequently fails to terminate (runs to `max_tokens`), so a single smoke prompt does not reliably catch it.

Bisected over the 422 commits between the `v0.5.16` branch point (`8905cbd42f`, good) and current main (`fd28242b6`, bad); `git bisect` names `dcd9014f15` as the first bad commit, and its parent `696e8f80d1` is good.

### Root cause

In `QuarkW4A4MXFp4MoE.create_weights`, #28291 changed the **weight** allocation from the aiter-aligned dims returned by `get_moe_weight_sizes()` to raw dims:

```python
-  w13_weight = torch.empty(num_experts, w13_up_dim,  hidden_size // 2, ...)
-  w2_weight  = torch.empty(num_experts, hidden_size, w2_down_dim,      ...)
+  w13_shape  = (num_experts, 2 * intermediate_size_per_partition, hidden_size // 2)
+  w2_shape   = (num_experts, hidden_size, intermediate_size_per_partition // 2)
```

but the corresponding **scales** in the very same function were left on the padded dims:

```python
   w13_weight_scale = torch.ones(num_experts, w13_up_dim,  hidden_size // OCP_MX_BLOCK_SIZE, ...)
   w2_weight_scale  = torch.ones(num_experts, hidden_size, (w2_down_dim * 2) // OCP_MX_BLOCK_SIZE, ...)
```

`get_moe_weight_sizes()` is still called and its `weight_padded` flag is still advertised through `extra_weight_attrs` (driving `FusedMoE.use_padded_loading`), so the layer claims padding it no longer has. The weights and their block scales therefore describe different intermediate sizes.

### Why only TP >= 8

`get_moe_weight_sizes()` only pads when `w2_down_dim = (moe_intermediate_size / TP) / 2` is not already a multiple of `AITER_PADDING_SIZE` (128). Below that threshold the new raw expressions happen to equal the padded ones, so the commit is a no-op; at and above it they diverge. For Qwen3.5 (`moe_intermediate_size = 1024`):

| TP | per-rank inter | old (padded) w13 / w2 | new (raw) w13 / w2 | aiter `inter_dim` | affected |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1024 | 2048 / 512 | 2048 / 512 | 1024 -> 1024 | no |
| 2 | 512 | 1024 / 256 | 1024 / 256 | 512 -> 512 | no |
| 4 | 256 | 512 / 128 | 512 / 128 | 256 -> 256 | no |
| 8 | 128 | 512 / **128** | 256 / **64** | 256 -> **128** | **yes** |
| 16 | 64 | 512 / **128** | 128 / **32** | 256 -> **64** | **yes** |

So the trigger condition is `moe_intermediate_size / TP < 256`. This is not specific to Qwen3.5 or to TP8 — any serialized MXFP4 Quark MoE whose per-rank intermediate is not already 128-aligned is affected.

There is a secondary, silent performance cost: the wrong `inter_dim` also drops the model off its tuned aiter FlyDSL MoE configs. Before the fix the server logs `[fused_moe] no tuned FlyDSL config for (...), using 2stage default` for every token bucket; after the fix it resolves tuned kernels again (`using 2stage (kernelName1='flydsl_moe1_afp4_wfp4_bf16_...')`).

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py` — in `QuarkW4A4MXFp4MoE.create_weights`, use `w13_up_dim` / `w2_down_dim` from `get_moe_weight_sizes()` for the `is_checkpoint_mxfp4_serialized` branch so the weights match the scales again. The online-quantization branch (`else`) is untouched and keeps the shapes introduced by #28291.

Two lines of real change plus a comment explaining why the serialized branch must stay on the padded dims.

## Accuracy Tests

Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4, 8x MI355 (gfx950), TP8, `--attention-backend aiter`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1`, identical aiter / sgl-kernel / flags across all rows — only the sglang Python tree differs.

GSM8K, 5-shot, `--thinking-mode qwen-3`, `--max-tokens 32768`, temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95.

| sglang build | GSM8K (n=100) | aiter MoE `inter_dim` | tuned FlyDSL configs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `v0.5.16` | 0.99 | 256 | resolved |
| `696e8f80d1` (parent of the bad commit) | 0.975 (n=40) | 256 | resolved |
| `dcd9014f15` (first bad commit) | 0.525 (n=40) | 128 | none |
| main `fd28242b6` | **0.54** | 128 | none |
| **main + this fix** | **0.98** | 256 | resolved |

Qualitative check on the same builds, prompt "What do you know about Kalevipoeg?" (`max_tokens` 10000):

| build | result |
|---|---|
| `v0.5.16` | correct ("the national epic of Estonia"), 2177 tokens, `finish_reason=stop` |
| main `fd28242b6` | denies the term exists, rambles to the 10000-token cap, `finish_reason=length` |
| main + this fix | correct, 2016 tokens, `finish_reason=stop` |

Full bisect ledger (GSM8K n=40 per point, same harness): `8905cbd42f` 0.975 / `66ea79dc2e` 0.975 / `696e8f80d1` 0.975 — all `inter_dim` 256; `dcd9014f15` 0.525 / `f369a820d4` 0.525 / `1a53f231d6` 0.575 / `6f55de0468` 0.525 / `d708969f68` 0.500 / `eb242b6c03` 0.525 — all `inter_dim` 128.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No dedicated speed run; this is an accuracy fix. It does restore the tuned aiter FlyDSL MoE kernel selection that the regression disabled, so it should recover MoE throughput lost since #28291 as well. Counting kernel-selection log lines on an identical TP8 startup:

| build | tuned FlyDSL selections | `no tuned FlyDSL config` fallbacks |
|---|---|---|
| `v0.5.16` | 112 | 0 |
| main `fd28242b6` | 0 | 112 |
| main + this fix | 112 | 0 |

Happy to add a throughput sweep if reviewers want it.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Note on unit tests: this regression was invisible to the existing suite because the weight and scale shapes are each individually self-consistent — only their relationship is wrong, and only at TP >= 8. A cheap guard would be a shape assertion in `create_weights` tying the weight dims to the scale dims (deliberately left out of this PR to keep it minimal, happy to add it here or in a follow-up). `test/registered/quant/test_quark_mxfp4.py` added by #28291 does not cover the serialized + aiter-padded path.

3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.

title: [PD] Fix false health-503 during decode retraction re-admission
author: cctry
body:
## Motivation

A PD decode engine under KV pressure retracts running requests into `disagg_decode_prealloc_queue.retracted_queue`. `is_fully_idle(for_health_check=True)` did not count that queue, so once `running_batch`/`waiting_queue` drained, the engine looked idle to the health probe. The probe then issued a fake-bootstrap generate request that could not make progress until re-admission finished — timing out into a `/health_generate` 503 — even though the engine was actively self-healing. A router acting on that 503 can eject a healthy decode engine and fail requests with `no available engines`.

Non-PD is unaffected: retracted requests return to `waiting_queue`, which is already counted.

## Modifications

- `is_fully_idle(for_health_check=True)` now counts a non-empty decode `retracted_queue` as active (except while the engine is explicitly paused).
- `on_idle` flushes any health-check signal deferred while the engine was busy, so probes are answered promptly once the engine actually goes idle.

Verified on an internal PD setup: decode retraction under KV pressure no longer flips `/health_generate` to 503 during re-admission.

## Original commits

- `a0d5870ea`

title: [Fix] Bound FULL_MASK verify-mask reuse by the captured max_bs
author: hnyls2002
body:
`VerifyMask.fits()` skipped the capacity check for FULL_MASK, so an eager batch past the captured `max_bs` reused a buffer sized for `max_bs` and ran off its end during target-verify mask extraction -- device-side `index out of bounds` assert and a dead scheduler. Both layouts are sized per request off worst-case per-request bounds, so `bs <= max_bs` is a sufficient bound for either; oversized batches now fall back to allocating, as they already did for QLEN_ONLY.

Reproduces on current main as `TestHybridAttnBackendSpeculativeDecodingPrefillBackend.test_gsm8k` (gsm8k score 0.0), whose server runs `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 8` with `max_running_requests=48`. Regression from #32920, which started routing `HybridAttnBackend` to its child's preallocated mask.

title: Fix the chunked-prefix-cache gate writing config the backends never read
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

The load-time chunked-prefix gate (`maybe_disable_chunked_prefix_cache`) still writes its `ServerArgs` instance, but every reader has moved to the published config: the attention backends assert / branch on `get_schedule().disable_chunked_prefix_cache` when they initialize. The flip never reaches them, so an MLA model on a backend outside `CHUNKED_PREFIX_CACHE_SUPPORTED_ATTENTION_BACKENDS` keeps chunked prefix enabled instead of being gated off.

## Modifications

- `misc_utils.maybe_disable_chunked_prefix_cache`: the gate writes through `get_context().override` (lands on the published bags) and its own pre/post checks read the bag.
- `prefill_cuda_graph_runner`: the `_capture_chunked_prefix` flag reads the bag the gate writes, not the runner's `ServerArgs` copy.
- New regression test pins the three contracts: the gate lands on the bag, the pristine `ServerArgs` instance stays untouched, and the draft-worker guard never writes.
- `ServerArgs.override` call-site ratchet drops 39 -> 38.

## Checklist

- [x] Unit test added (`test_chunked_prefix_cache_gate.py`)
- [x] `test/registered/unit/model_executor/` battery green locally

title: Fix DeepSeek-OCR batching crash on variable local-crop counts
author: pavansivaram
body:
## Summary

`_process_image_input` in `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_ocr.py` batches multiple `MultimodalDataItem`s into a single vision-encoder forward pass. It used `torch.stack` to fuse each item's `images_crop` tensor:

```python
images_crop = torch.stack([item.images_crop for item in mm_items], dim=0)
```

Each item's `images_crop` has shape `[1, num_patches, 3, 640, 640]`, where `num_patches` depends on the image's aspect ratio / resolution. Two OCR requests batched into the same forward pass with different tile counts (e.g. 6 vs 4) therefore crash the scheduler:

```
RuntimeError: stack expects each tensor to be equal size,
  but got [1, 6, 3, 640, 640] at entry 0
      and [1, 4, 3, 640, 640] at entry 1
```

Reproduced via `benchmark/ocr/bench_sglang.py --concurrency 8` on olmOCR-bench (`multi_column` split).

## Fix

`_pixel_values_to_embedding` already loops item-by-item internally and returns a list of per-item feature tensors that get concatenated by the caller, so the cross-item stack was never needed for correctness — only for convenience. Iterate `mm_items` instead, run each through `_pixel_values_to_embedding` with a 1-sized batch, and concat the resulting features. Downstream `merge_multimodal_embeddings` sees the same flat sequence.

## Regression test

Added `TestDeepSeekOCRProcessImageInputBatchedUnequalCrops` in `test/registered/xpu/test_deepseek_ocr.py`. Builds two `MultimodalDataItem`s with `images_crop` shapes `[1, 6, 3, 640, 640]` and `[1, 4, 3, 640, 640]` — the exact 6-vs-4 mismatch from the crash traceback — stubs `_pixel_values_to_embedding`, and calls `_process_image_input`. Parameterized over three devices; each test method skips cleanly when its device is unavailable on the host runner:

- `test_batched_unequal_num_patches_no_crash_cpu`
- `test_batched_unequal_num_patches_no_crash_xpu`
- `test_batched_unequal_num_patches_no_crash_cuda`

### Test results

Verified on a host with CPU + XPU (no CUDA), running the new test class against **both** the fixed code (this PR) and the pre-fix `torch.stack` code:

| Device | Pre-fix (bug present) | With patch (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| CPU | ❌ `RuntimeError: stack expects each tensor to be equal size, but got [1, 6, 3, 640, 640] at entry 0 and [1, 4, 3, 640, 640] at entry 1` | ✅ OK |
| XPU | ❌ same `RuntimeError` | ✅ OK |
| CUDA | ⏭  skipped (no CUDA device on this runner) | ⏭  skipped (no CUDA device on this runner) |

Full run:

```
$ cd test/registered/xpu && PYTHONPATH=../../../python python -m unittest -v \
    test_deepseek_ocr.TestDeepSeekOCRProcessImageInputBatchedUnequalCrops

test_batched_unequal_num_patches_no_crash_cpu ... ok
test_batched_unequal_num_patches_no_crash_cuda ... skipped "device 'cuda' not available on this host"
test_batched_unequal_num_patches_no_crash_xpu ... ok

Ran 3 tests in 0.128s

OK (skipped=1)
```

Total wall-clock: ~0.13s (no server spin-up; regression is exercised via a stubbed `_pixel_values_to_embedding` so the test doesn't need real vision-encoder weights).

### E2E sanity

Also confirmed on the OCR benchmark that used to crash:

```
python benchmark/ocr/bench_sglang.py \
    --port 30000 --split all --concurrency 8 \
    --output-dir logs/ --bench-dir /data/olmOCR-bench/bench_data/
```

Runs to completion post-patch (was crashing on the `multi_column` split before).

## Checklist

- [x] Pre-commit clean on both modified files (`pre-commit run --files ...`).
- [x] Regression test fails on pre-fix code, passes on the fix (verified on CPU and XPU).
- [x] Single-image requests still work — no regression for `--concurrency 1`.
~

title: [Fix] deepseek-v4: Fix DeepSeek-V4 non-EP TBO for attention TP > 1
author: mikekg
body:
## Motivation

Depends on #31700 (merged).

DeepSeek-V4 two-batch overlap (TBO) with DP attention, `moe_a2a_backend=none` and attention TP > 1 applied full-TP variable-length collectives to tensors replicated within each attention-TP group. On older `main` this corrupted the gather and combine layouts and produced invalid output (the H100 report below); on current `main` the same configuration fails in the TBO gather, because each child's DP counts have one entry per TP rank (`dp_slot_in`: "a per-replica sequence of 4 entries does not belong to a DP gather of width 2").

This change gives each full-TP rank one shard of its replicated DP-local tensor and reconstructs the DP-local result across the attention-TP group after the combine, and fixes the problems the same configuration hit next.

## Modifications

Original commits:
- Derive and validate DP-local token counts and full-TP shard counts for each TBO child batch.
- Shard replicated hidden states and input IDs across attention-TP ranks before the full-TP variable-length gather.
- Reduce-scatter the MoE output into one shard per full-TP rank, then all-gather within the attention-TP group to reconstruct the replicated DP-local output.
- Select the non-EP TBO strategy for CP 1, multi-rank DP and SUM_LEN padding; MAX_LEN batches take the non-overlapped path.
- Exercise attention TP in the registered DeepSeek-V4 TBO tests (AMD and H200) and add focused tests for collective-size mapping and validation.

Added after review:
- **Empty micro-batch.** TBO can split a short extend so that one micro-batch has no tokens on any DP rank; the overlapped MoE then ran the experts on zero rows, and the triton runner's fused SiLU-and-mul with the SwiGLU clamp rejected the zero-block launch, crashing the server on a single short request (also on `main`). The experts are now skipped for such a micro-batch; every rank gathers the same rows, so all skip together.
- **Eager decode at attention TP > 1.** TBO children are padded to a multiple of attention TP tokens, but a decode child kept its request count, so a one-request child carried two token rows and DeepSeek-V4's decode metadata asserted (`req_pool_indices 1, out_cache_loc 2`). A decode child now pads its requests with its tokens, as `prepare_mlp_sync_batch` does for the whole batch.
- **Shared expert locality.** The TBO path again computes a replicated TP1 shared expert on local rows only under `SGLANG_DP_SHARED_EXPERT_LOCAL`; inside the MoE it is added on TP rank 0 and the reducing combine counts it once (verified below).
- **AMD unit test stub.** `DeepseekV2MoE` now always sets `shared_experts`, and `forward_normal` reads it directly; the MoE stub in `test_deepseek_v4_amd_tp4.py` is built with `__new__` and failed with "no attribute 'shared_experts'" on MI35x. The stub now sets it to `None`.
- **AMD chat probe.** The single-request check added to the AMD TBO test runs on a server that thinks by default (`SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1`), so the reasoning counted against `max_tokens: 32` and the reply was cut off before the answer (`'7 + 5 equals'`). The budget is now 512 tokens, and a failure reports `finish_reason`.
- **ROCm.** The combine's attention-TP all-gather runs on the TBO communication stream while the other micro-batch's attention uses the same group's collectives on the compute stream. On ROCm `all_gather_into_tensor` takes aiter's custom all-gather, and MI355X failed later in unrelated kernels with "invalid configuration argument" (this PR's AMD CI failure), passing with `SGLANG_USE_AITER_AG=0`. The shards now go through the attention-TP device process group.

## Accuracy Tests

### H200, after review

8×H200, torch 2.14.1+cu130, sgl-kernel 0.4.10, FlashInfer 0.7.2.

- `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`, 5-shot GSM8K (200 questions, greedy) through `sglang.Engine` with the arguments of `TestDSV4FlashFP4TboH200` (TP 8, attention DP 2, so attention TP 4; `--moe-a2a-backend none --moe-runner-backend marlin`, `SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1=1 SGLANG_DP_USE_GATHERV=1 SGLANG_DP_USE_REDUCE_SCATTER=1`): **0.970 with TBO, 0.970 without TBO** (0.965 at the previous head).
- `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`'s config reduced to 4 layers and 8 experts, dummy weights, triton MoE; each TBO run compared with the same build's non-TBO run (7 requests, 8 new tokens, prompt and output logprobs): **identical** at TP 4 / attention DP 2 (attention TP 2) with eager decode, with decode CUDA graphs, and with `SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1=1` with and without `SGLANG_DP_SHARED_EXPERT_LOCAL=1`; identical at TP 2 / attention DP 2. At the previous head the eager-decode case failed at the first decode step.
- Single short requests (TP 2 and TP 4, attention DP 2, TBO): 6/6 served; `main` crashes on the first.

### MI355X

8×MI355X, `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm10-mi35x-20261025`, the reduced config with 256 experts and FP8 weights and the AMD TBO test's environment, TP 8 / attention DP 2:
- previous head: TBO fails ("invalid configuration argument"), the same requests without TBO pass;
- `SGLANG_USE_AITER_AG=0`: TBO passes 6/6.
- With the device-group all-gather, AMD CI at `10313c2757` ([job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40296194792/job/121526401095)): the AMD TBO test's GSM8K (`sgl-project/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8`, TP 8 / attention DP 2, so attention TP 4; 1319 questions) scored **0.955** (threshold 0.91); the non-TBO DeepSeek-V4-Flash FP4 and FP8 tests in the same job scored 0.957 and 0.951. The chat probe failed on its token budget (fixed above); the fixed probe has not run yet.

<details>
<summary>H100 validation reported before the review (TP16 / DP2 / attention TP 8)</summary>

### H100 end-to-end setup

- Model: `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-NVFP4`
- Hardware: 2 hosts × 8 NVIDIA H100 80GB
- Container: `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260801-e4c4faf8`
- Topology: TP16 / DP2 / attention-TP8
- MoE A2A backend: `none`
- TBO enabled
- Infrastructure: [NemoRL Sandbox Infrastructure Report](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1sT9QbbzXC110IC4f6T964OgKCnUouaSLYKznNnw35O8/edit?tab=t.0)

The failure was reproduced both on pristine upstream `574ead753` and on the

and returned HTTP 200 responses with corrupted generated text.

title: Fix padded positions in breakable CUDA Graph attention
author: YAMY1234
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Breakable CUDA Graph pads token buffers to a captured bucket. The attention wrapper already narrows Q/K/V and cache locations to the real token count, but it still passes padded `positions` to the backend. Decode context parallelism (DCP) uses these positions to determine key-value (KV) ownership, so virtual padded tokens can compete with real tokens for the same physical KV slots and silently corrupt the cache.

## Modifications

- Narrow `forward_batch.positions` to the real query-token count together with `out_cache_loc` for the attention call.
- Restore both tensors on the shared `ForwardBatch` after the call.
- Extend the existing Breakable CUDA Graph test to verify the narrowed backend view and restored batch metadata.

## Accuracy Tests

The targeted GPU regression was run before and after the change:

- Before: the attention backend received five padded positions for three real cache locations, and the test failed.
- After: the backend received only the three real positions. The targeted test passed, and the full `TestBreakableCUDAGraphBasic` suite passed (`9 passed`).

An end-to-end matched A/B used Qwen3.5-397B-A17B FP8 with TP16/DCP4, FP8 KV cache, Breakable CUDA Graph prefill, full decode CUDA Graph, GSM8K-128, 8-shot prompting, temperature 0, and `max_tokens=16384`. The validation stack included #32795 and #32858; the only runtime-code difference between before and after was this PR's four-line positions fix.

| Version | Runs | GSM8K |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Before | 1 | 0.875 (112/128) |
| After | 3 | 0.984375 (126/128) in every run |

All four runs completed 128/128 requests with HTTP 200 and no non-200 responses.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not benchmarked. This correctness fix does not change kernels or CUDA Graph configuration; it creates a tensor view and restores the original reference around the existing attention call.
