title: [rust-server] Reland: fix TCP-layer TTFT stalls (#33026)
author: sherlockwu
body:
Relands #33026, resolving the issue of `runtime::tests` failing in the `test_cargo_workspace` CI job ([log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30723127006/job/91430085608)), which caused the revert (#33257): `tokio::net::TcpSocket::listen()` needs a reactor, so #33026 moved `listen()` from the synchronous `runtime::start()` onto the async api runtime, and tests connecting right after `start()` returned raced it (`ECONNREFUSED`). This reland builds the listener with `socket2` instead — it can set `SO_RCVBUF` before bind while staying synchronous, so `start()` binds **and** listens before spawning any thread, restoring the tested guarantee with no test changes.

--- 

Two TCP-layer TTFT stalls in the Rust server, found benchmarking Rust vs Python TM (gpt-oss-120b + MiMo-V2.5-Pro, 8×B300, `bench_serving` c=1, seed 42, `--disable-radix-cache`):

1. **~200 ms on large request bodies.** A headers+body burst larger than the kernel's initial rcvbuf (`tcp_rmem[1]` = 87380 B) drops its tail before hyper polls the body. Hits the first large-body request of every connection. **Fix:** `SO_RCVBUF` 16 MiB on the listener (inherited by accepted sockets; covers a 1M-token body; lazily allocated; clamped by `net.core.rmem_max`).
2. **+13 ms on keep-alive connections.** hyper/axum doesn't set `TCP_NODELAY` (Python's asyncio does); Nagle + delayed-ACK. **Fix:** `set_nodelay(true)` via `ListenerExt::tap_io`.

All rows measured on `main` at `55b6769b0e`, unfixed vs this fix, Python TM on the same base as reference:

| TTFT (mean ms) | before | after | Python TM ref |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| gpt-oss 16K in | 192 (P99 369) | **157 (P99 161)** | 166 |
| gpt-oss 64K in | 1253 (P99 1463) | **1047 (P99 1060)** | 1080 |
| MiMo 64K in | 2197 | **1957** | 1986 |
| MiMo 256K in | 9716 | **9513** | 9669 |
| gpt-oss in=1, keep-alive ×128 | 40.9 | **26.4** | 26.4 |

Raw-socket probe (headers+390 KB in one `send`, time to response headers): 208 ms → 0.4 ms. Decode path unaffected (ITL parity with Python through c=256).

## Test

`cargo test --workspace` passes locally (including the two tests that failed in CI); `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace` clean.

title: Fix DSV4 DSpark shared expert loading
author: mmangkad
body:
## Summary

#33889 moved shared-expert fusion to a per-runner decision installed from each model's entry class. The DSV4 target exposes that gate, but the standalone DSpark entry class did not, so the draft used the wrong layout and skipped its bundled shared-expert tensors.

This makes DSpark use the DSV4 gate and retain the resolved layout when it is built. Shared experts stay separate by default, while explicitly forced fusion remains supported and maps those weights into the fused expert slot.

title: [diffusion] Fix component accuracy topology reuse
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

- rebuild diffusion model-parallel groups when the Ulysses/Ring decomposition changes even if total SP stays constant
- omit the no-op all-true synthetic attention mask from ring component-accuracy cases
- reset CUDA-IPC all-to-all state when its process group is replaced
- give the 2-GPU Z-Image accuracy threshold enough margin for the observed H100/H200 FlashAttention variance

## Root cause

The component-accuracy harness reused model-parallel groups based on TP/SP/DP/CFG sizes only. In the failing suite, `fsdp-inference` initialized SP=2 as Ulysses-2/Ring-1 immediately before the Qwen Ring case requested Ulysses-1/Ring-2. Because total SP remained 2, the harness skipped reinitialization and the Qwen ring canary ran with the stale Ulysses topology.

Once the topology check is corrected, the harness's synthetic all-true text mask reaches the unsupported masked-ring path even though that mask has no semantic effect. Ring cases now omit that synthetic no-op mask.

The Z-Image failure is a separate threshold-edge issue: the failing H100 run produced 0.993382 against 0.9935, while H200 produced 0.993504 with CUDA-IPC both enabled and disabled. The override is moved to 0.993 to cover the observed backend variance without hiding a material regression.

Related CI failure: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30753555033/job/91516481836?pr=33282

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --files` on all changed files
- H200 targeted unit tests: 5 passed
- H200 same-process topology switch: Qwen Image Ring-2 0.998509, then Z-Image Ulysses-2 0.993504 (2 passed, 38 deselected)
- Z-Image CUDA-IPC A/B: 0.993504 with both enabled and disabled

title: [Fix] Treat an empty grammar constraint as unset in SamplingParams
author: hnyls2002
body:
An empty grammar constraint (e.g. `structural_tag=""` from `/generate`) passes the `is not None` entry check in `GrammarManager.process_req_with_grammar` but matches no branch in the selection chain, so the key lookup runs with nothing assigned and raises `UnboundLocalError`.

Fold `""` to `None` for all four grammar fields in `SamplingParams.__post_init__`, and align the `structural_tag` branch with the other three so the chain stays in sync with its entry condition.

title: fix: always capture default prefill CUDA graph
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

- remove the fixed 4 GiB runtime gate added by #31204
- always capture an automatically selected prefill CUDA graph instead of silently falling back to eager execution based on free memory
- remove the defensive `getattr` and replace the obsolete threshold tests with a regression test that verifies capture still proceeds with 3.99 GiB free

Existing explicit disable and model/backend compatibility guards are unchanged.

## Root cause

The memory gate used a model-agnostic fixed threshold after weights, KV cache, and eager buffers were allocated. That allowed default configurations to disable prefill CUDA graphs at runtime and introduced a silent performance regression for otherwise supported models.

Memory sizing should be handled by the configured cache/capture parameters. An automatically selected prefill graph should not be overridden by a hard-coded free-memory threshold.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner_components/cuda_graph_setup.py test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py`
- `python3 -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py`: 5 passed, 2 subtests passed
- H100 smoke with default `sglang serve --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-8B` (only host/port added):
  - resolved `prefill.backend='breakable'`
  - captured all 58 prefill buckets
  - prefill capture completed in 26.30s using 1.74 GiB
  - server reached health-ready and warmup logged `cuda graph: True`

Follow-up to #31204 and its review feedback.

title: [diffusion] Fix local-path detection for MiniMax-H3 and other non-diffusers models
author: TobyMint
body:
## Problem

`KNOWN_NON_DIFFUSERS_DIFFUSION_MODEL_PATTERNS` (`python/sglang/utils.py`) only carries **org-prefixed** patterns for some entries (`minimaxai/minimax-h3`, `fal/ideogram-v4-*`), while other families in the same list already ship bare-name patterns (`pi05`, `pi0.5`, `hunyuan3d`, `flux.2-dev-nvfp4`).

As a result, a local model directory downloaded by repo name alone — the standard way to point at local weights:

```bash
sglang serve --model-path /data/models/MiniMax-H3 --model-variant fl2va
```

fails in **both** detection layers:

1. **CLI auto-detection** (`is_known_non_diffusers_diffusion_model`, substring-only) misses the path and falls back to the standard LLM server parser, which rejects the diffusion-only args (`--num-gpus`, `--ulysses-degree`, `--model-variant`, ...).
2. **Registry pipeline resolution** (`get_non_diffusers_pipeline_name`, substring-only) misses the path; `maybe_download_model_index` finds no top-level `model_index.json` (H3 keeps it under `FL2VA/` / `Ref2VA/` partitions); backend `auto` then falls back to the generic diffusers pipeline, which attempts a Hub download of the absolute local path and crashes with `HFValidationError`.

Workaround today: symlink the directory to `/data/models/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3` (matching the org-prefixed pattern) or pass `--model-type diffusion` — but the bare local path should just work, as it does for the other families in the list.

## Fix

Add a **short-name fallback** to the two substring-only matchers, consistent with the short-name matching already used by `_get_config_info` (step 2) and `has_registered_diffusion_model_path`:

- `is_known_non_diffusers_diffusion_model` (`python/sglang/utils.py`): after substring matching fails, compare the directory **basename** against the short names of registered patterns (e.g. `"MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3"` → `"minimax-h3"`).
- `get_non_diffusers_pipeline_name` (`python/sglang/multimodal_gen/registry.py`): same basename fallback, returning the pipeline name.

The fallback uses **exact equality**, not substring containment, so a future `MiniMax-H3.5` or `MiniMax-H3-4B` directory will not false-positive. It only triggers when substring matching already failed, so behavior for every other model path is unchanged; the diffusers-layout models (top-level `model_index.json`) are unaffected.

## Verification

- Unit checks: `/data/models/MiniMax-H3` → detected + `MiniMaxH3Pipeline`; negative cases (`minimax-h3.5`, `MiniMax-H3-4B`, unrelated dirs) → not matched; existing bare-name families (`pi05`, `hunyuan3d`) and HF cache paths (`models--MiniMaxAI--MiniMax-H3/...`) still match.
- End-to-end: `sglang serve --model-path /data/models/MiniMax-H3 --num-gpus 4 --ulysses-degree 4 --performance-mode speed --use-fsdp-inference true --model-variant fl2va` (no `--model-type`, no symlink) starts, loads `MiniMaxH3Pipeline` from `/data/models/MiniMax-H3/FL2VA`, and passes the 1344x768x124f server warmup.

This also fixes the same gap for the Ideogram entries (`ideogram-v4-fast`, `ideogram-v4-instant`, `ideogram-4`), which have the identical prefix-only problem.

title: fix: pi05 models does not apply scale factor for language embeddings
author: zealoct
body:
## Motivation

The official OpenPI PyTorch Pi0.5 implementation scales language token embeddings by `sqrt(hidden_dim)` before concatenating them with image embeddings. SGLang omitted that scale, causing a systematic action-output mismatch.

Reference: [OpenPI `embed_prefix`](https://github.com/Physical-Intelligence/openpi/blob/15a9616a00943ada6c20a0f158e3adb39df2ccac/src/openpi/models_pytorch/pi0_pytorch.py#L217).

The original CI did not catch this because `pi05_action_http` used an older SGLang-generated GT, while the Python consistency test only checked repeatability/cache reuse. The manual benchmark also compared normalized SGLang model actions with postprocessed OpenPI robot actions.

## Modifications

- apply the official language-embedding scale
- compare SGLang and OpenPI in normalized model space with identical OpenPI-transformed inputs and deterministic noise
- tokenize the 14-dimensional Aloha state before model-dimension padding
- match OpenPI byte-image resize/rounding behavior
- preserve already-normalized `float32[-1, 1]` images and their `-1` letterbox padding
- add focused unit coverage and document the official parity result

## Accuracy Tests

Environment: one H100, OpenPI PyTorch revision `15a9616a00943ada6c20a0f158e3adb39df2ccac`, LeRobot checkpoint revision `b211f3d44c36b6acfcf7ae94a64e8e96f75a64ba`, bf16 model weights with fp32 stability-sensitive parameters.

| Comparison | Max abs. diff. | Mean abs. diff. | P95 abs. diff. |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| First velocity, identical transformed inputs | 0.026767 | 0.003443 | 0.009845 |
| Final 10-step action, production raw-observation path | 0.008127 | 0.000920 | 0.002642 |

Both values are normalized model-space `[50, 32]` actions before robot-specific unnormalization or horizon slicing. The existing CI limits remain unchanged at `0.05` max and `0.005` mean absolute difference.

Validation:

- 22 Pi0.5 unit tests passed
- real `sglang serve` HTTP `/v1/actions/generations` passed the official OpenPI action GT
- after pinning upstream GT revision `d05810e3ea3eff1d137dec723f6e66d9c11b470f`, the real server consistency case passed without `SGLANG_CONSISTENCY_GT_DIR`
- the rebased head passed the same server consistency case with Run:ai direct GPU streaming (`13.5 GiB` in `1.81 s` on RTX 5090)
- official GT generation was reproduced twice with identical SHA256 `319c1a1e622a4984155c78ca99f7c7d771da6127e1129a7fd0baf549bd01e42e`

The provenance-backed GT was merged in [sgl-project/ci-data-diffusion#1](https://github.com/sgl-project/ci-data-diffusion/pull/1), and this PR pins its upstream merge revision. The old GT is expected to fail because it encodes the pre-fix behavior.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This is a correctness fix, not a kernel-path change. The production validation retained native attention and the action CUDA graph. The scale is one elementwise multiply during prefix construction and does not affect the denoise loop.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add focused unit tests.
- [x] Update documentation.
- [x] Provide official accuracy results.
- [x] Follow SGLang code style guidance.

title: [AMD][DI][CI] Auto-mount  latest host ionic/ibverbs userspace in the MI355X nightly launcher (fix ABI mismatch)
author: Lzy17
body:
## Summary

When a node's host ionic provider is newer than the container's rdma-core, the in-container libibverbs rejects the provider — `Driver ionic does not support the kernel ABI ... No IB devices found` — and RDMA fails, taking that node out of the disagg nightly pool (observed on `mia1-p01-g20`).

`launch_mi355x.sh`'s `docker run` mounted only `/it-share` and `$HOME`. The disagg container script (`scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_start_container_disagg.sh`) already handles this by mounting the host ionic/ibverbs userspace into the container; this ports the same mount set to the Slurm launcher.

## How
- Generate `$WORKDIR/ionic_mounts.sh` (literal heredoc) that resolves the host ionic provider + provider dir + `/etc/libibverbs.d` + libnl/libmnl and exports `IONIC_MOUNTS`.
- The prefill/decode/bench role scripts `source` it before `docker run` and pass `$IONIC_MOUNTS`.
- Detection runs on the compute node (the ionic `.so` version is node-specific), is existence-guarded (no-op on a host without ionic), mounts only the provider (not core `libibverbs.so`), and leaves `DOCKER_COMMON` / `EXTRA_DOCKER_ARGS` unchanged.

## Test plan
- [ ] 1P1D leg pinned to include g20, no manual ionic mount: no `No IB devices found`, `ibv_devinfo` lists the ionic HCAs, GSM8K gate passes.
- [ ] p02-only run unchanged (no regression).

title: Fix _pa_swa_prefill_lens off-by-one in FlashAttentionBackend
author: DmiSergeev
body:
## Motivation

`FlashAttentionBackend.__init__` allocates a prefill-aware-SWA scratch buffer for models that opt into `is_prefill_aware_swa()` (e.g. `python/sglang/srt/models/unlimited_ocr.py`):

```python
max_bs = model_runner.req_to_token_pool.size
self._pa_swa_prefill_lens = torch.zeros(max_bs, dtype=torch.int32, ...)
```

This buffer is not indexed by batch position — it's indexed directly by raw `req_pool_idx` values:

```python
self._pa_swa_prefill_lens[forward_batch.req_pool_indices[:batch_size]] = ...
```

(and read the same way inside the `_build_pa_page_table` Triton kernel). `ReqToTokenPool` reserves row 0 as a padding slot for CUDA-graph-padded batches and hands out real slots `1..size` (`_alloc_size = size + 1`), so the valid `req_pool_idx` range is `[0, size]` inclusive — `size + 1` distinct values. Sizing the buffer to `size` (valid indices `0..size-1`) is off-by-one: a request landing on `req_pool_idx == size` overflows it.

This was latent because `ReqToTokenPool.alloc()` used to pop free slots from the head of `free_slots` in ascending order (`1, 2, 3, ...`), so index `size` was only ever handed out once the pool was nearly fully saturated — unreachable in ordinary CI runs. It stopped being latent in #32208 ("O(1) slot allocation in `ReqToTokenPool.alloc()`"), which pops from the tail instead (descending: `size, size-1, ...`), so the very first allocation into a fresh pool now gets `req_pool_idx == size`. This surfaced as a CUDA `index_put` "index out of bounds" device assertion in `base-b-test-1-gpu-large` / `test_unlimited_ocr_server.py`, right after decode CUDA-graph capture, on the first real request: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30669370441/job/91419918042.

Grepped the rest of `python/sglang/srt` for the same pattern (a buffer sized off `req_to_token_pool.size` but indexed by raw `req_pool_idx` rather than by batch position) and found no other occurrence — the many other `max_bs = req_to_token_pool.size`-sized buffers elsewhere (`kv_indptr`, `qo_indptr`, `kv_last_page_len`, etc.) are all indexed positionally (`[:bs]`), not by pool-slot id, so they're unaffected.

## Modifications

- Size `_pa_swa_prefill_lens` to `req_to_token_pool.size + 1`, matching `ReqToTokenPool`'s own allocation (`req_to_token.shape[0] == size + 1`), so every valid `req_pool_idx` in `[0, size]` is addressable regardless of which order `ReqToTokenPool.alloc()` hands out slots in.
- This fixes the actual bound bug rather than papering over it by reverting the allocator to low-index-first behavior, which would only make the off-by-one latent again.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable — this only changes the size of a preallocated scratch buffer; it does not change any tensor values, KV cache contents, or model outputs.

## Testing

Added `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_flashattention_pa_swa_prefill_lens_size.py`, registered on `base-b-test-1-gpu-small`. It builds a minimal fake `ModelRunner` that opts into `prefill_aware_swa`, constructs a real `FlashAttentionBackend`, and asserts:
- `_pa_swa_prefill_lens.shape[0] == req_to_token_pool.size + 1`
- writing at `req_pool_idx == req_to_token_pool.size` (the exact write that crashed in CI) stays in bounds.

Verified locally (stubbing the CUDA-only `sgl_kernel` import, running the real `__init__` on CPU) against both versions of the file:

```
pre-fix:  IndexError: index 8 is out of bounds for dimension 0 with size 8
post-fix: passes, buffer shape is 9 for pool_size=8
```

The pre-fix failure is the CPU equivalent of the CUDA `index_put` device assertion seen in the CI run above.

title: [Feat] speculative: Seed rejection-sampling draft proposals for deterministic inference
author: ajit283
body:
## Motivation

Classic EAGLE/NEXTN rejection sampling draws each draft proposal with `fast_sample()`. Although target sampling and verify-side rejection coins support request-local seeds, this proposal draw used the global PyTorch RNG (`exponential_()`), so `--enable-deterministic-inference` still changed outputs with batch shape and CUDA graph replay.

This is the draft-worker follow-up documented in #30822. Before this change, Qwen3.5-9B NEXTN rejection sampling produced 12 unique outputs in 12 changing-batch trials with a fixed sampling seed.

## Modifications

- Add an optional deterministic path to `fast_sample()` keyed by:
  - request sampling seed
  - absolute sequence position
  - draft step / MTP layer
  - vocabulary entry
- Domain-separate draft proposal randomness from target sampling and verify-side rejection coins.
- Convert MurmurHash32 output to open-interval uniforms with midpoint binning, then use exponential-race categorical sampling in float64.
- Preserve the existing RNG-backed fast path when deterministic inference is disabled.
- Plumb request seeds and positions through eager and CUDA-graph EAGLE/NEXTN workers.
- Support both ordinary and multi-layer EAGLE, including the single-CUDA-graph multi-layer draft-extend path.
- Keep deterministic rejection sampling guarded on non-CUDA-compatible devices because this implementation uses a Triton hash kernel.
- Add sampler tests for replay, batch permutation/splitting, seed/position/step separation, hash endpoints, CUDA graph updates, and categorical distribution sanity.
- Add dedicated deterministic E2E smoke tests without changing the existing unseeded rejection-sampling and chain-MTP test configurations.
- Add a reproducible seeded/unseeded sampling microbenchmark.

## Accuracy Tests

### Regular EAGLE/NEXTN

Qwen3.5-9B, TP2, NEXTN, rejection sampling, temperature 1.0, sampling seed 42:

| Version | Changing-batch trials | Unique outputs |
|---|---:|---:|
| Before | 12 | 12 |
| After | 12 | 1 |

The deterministic harness also passed changing batch sizes, prefix batching, bitwise logprob comparison, and radix-cache consistency.

Post-rebase validation on B200:

```text
7 passed, 16 warnings, 2 subtests passed
Total samples: 6, Unique samples: 1
OK
```

The unit suite includes 100,000 distinct seeded draws from `[0.1, 0.2, 0.7]` and verifies that observed frequencies are within 0.01 absolute tolerance.

### Multi-layer EAGLE

`stepfun-ai/Step-3.5-Flash`, TP8 on 8x B200, FA4, three MTP layers, single-CUDA-graph draft extend:

```text
Total samples: 6, Unique samples: 1
MULTI_LAYER_EAGLE_REJECTION_SAMPLING_IS_DETERMINISTIC
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

B200, vocabulary size 163,840, CUDA-graph replay:

| Batch | Unseeded | Seeded | Slowdown |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 31.9 us | 47.2 us | 1.48x |
| 8 | 38.0 us | 63.5 us | 1.67x |
| 32 | 54.5 us | 131.9 us | 2.42x |
| 128 | 138.9 us | 544.1 us | 3.92x |

Peak allocated memory for batch 128 and vocabulary 163,840:

```text
Input probabilities:       80.00 MiB
Baseline allocated:        80.00 MiB
Peak allocated:           321.25 MiB
Incremental seeded peak:  241.25 MiB
```

The deterministic mode is opt-in. A fused hash/exponential/argmax kernel can be considered separately if end-to-end profiling shows that the materialized hash and score matrices materially affect serving throughput.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code and pass Ruff / `git diff --check`.
- [x] Add unit and registered E2E tests.
- [x] Preserve existing unseeded rejection-sampling and chain-MTP coverage.
- [x] Provide accuracy, latency, and peak-memory measurements.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.
- [x] No documentation update is needed; this fixes an existing flag combination without adding user-facing options.

title: [AMD] [Fix] Enable aiter hd256 FP8 prefill FMHA on gfx950
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation
Follow-up of https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32046.

`AiterAttnBackend.forward_extend` has a fast path that routes head_dim-256 FP8 prefill attention to aiter's `flash_attn_varlen_fp8_pertensor_func`. It was gated behind `SGLANG_AITER_FMHA_FP8_ASM`, defaulting to `"False"` — because turning it on made every prefill die with:

```
RuntimeError: invalid argument for fmha_fwd
```

The error names the ck-tile kernel, so it reads like a missing ck-tile build. The actual trigger is a tensor *shape* two layers up.

**Root cause.** aiter only dispatches hd256 FP8 to the gfx950 ASM kernel (`fmha_fwd_hd256_fp8_causal_group_gfx950`) when `is_fmha_v3_fp8()` in `aiter/ops/mha.py` passes, and that predicate requires all three descales to be 1-D:

```python
ret = ret and (q_descale.shape == (1,) or q_descale.shape == (batch_size, nhead_k))
```

`BaseKVCacheMethod.create_weights` (`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/kv_cache.py`) creates `layer.k_scale` / `layer.v_scale` as **0-D** tensors (`torch.tensor(-1.0)`, `shape == ()`). Passing them straight through fails the check, so `can_impl_fmha_v3_fwd()` rejects hd256 and dispatch **silently** falls back to ck-tile `mha_varlen_fwd`. ck-tile's receipt-200 codegen filter emits FP8 group-mode instances only for hdim 128 and 192 — never 256 — so no instance matches, `aiter::mha_fwd` returns -1, and `TORCH_CHECK` raises.

Minimal reproduction, identical shapes, only the descale rank differs:

| descale | shape | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `torch.tensor([1.0])` | `(1,)` | OK — output `(2048, 16, 256)` |
| `torch.tensor(1.0)` | `()` | `RuntimeError: invalid argument for fmha_fwd` |

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py`, single call site:

- Reshape the q/k/v descales to 1-D (`.reshape(1)`) so `is_fmha_v3_fp8()` passes and the gfx950 ASM kernel is selected. These scales are always per-tensor scalars here, so the reshape is a pure view with no numerical effect.
- Drop the `SGLANG_AITER_FMHA_FP8_ASM` env-var gate. It only ever existed to keep a broken path switched off; the remaining conditions (`is_gfx95_supported()`, extend mode, no prefix, no SWA, no sinks, no logit cap, `qk_head_dim == v_head_dim == 256`, FP8 KV cache) already scope the path correctly.

Net diff is 4 insertions, 5 deletions.

Widening the ck-tile receipt-200 filter to hdim 256 also makes the crash go away, but only by providing a slow ck-tile fallback instead of the ASM kernel — that is not the fix, and it is not part of this PR.

## Accuracy Tests

Model `Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4`, MI355 (gfx950), TP2, `--attention-backend aiter --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --page-size 16`.

| | Accuracy | Invalid |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before (path enabled) | n/a — server crashes on first prefill | n/a |
| After | **0.970** | 0.000 |

`python -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 200 --parallel 100 --max-new-tokens 8192` (8192 output tokens because Qwen3.5 is a thinking model; a short cap depresses the score independently of this change).

Dispatch confirmed from the server log — the ASM kernel is actually the one running:

```
[aiter] LoadKernel: _ZN5aiter38fmha_fwd_hd256_fp8_causal_group_gfx950E
        hsaco: aiter/hsa/gfx950/fmha_v3_fwd/fwd_hd256_fp8_causal_group.co
```

Zero occurrences of `invalid argument for fmha_fwd` across server startup and the full eval.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

**No performance claim is made in this PR.** The prior state of this path was a hard crash, so there is no before/after throughput baseline to compare against — this is an enablement/correctness fix. A separate perf evaluation of the hd256 FP8 ASM kernel against the paged `mha_batch_prefill` path is left to follow-up work.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the code with `pre-commit run --all-files`
- [x] Add accuracy results (gsm8k above)
- [ ] Benchmark results — intentionally omitted, see above

title: Fix deterministic inference for Inkling
author: ispobock
body:
## Motivation

`--enable-deterministic-inference` does not hold for Inkling -- scoring the same context twice returns different logprobs. On the checkpoint the per-commit consistency test uses (bf16, tp=1, fa4) it reports **4380 mismatching observations out of 6072**, and on `Inkling-Small-NVFP4` at tp=8 **50302 out of 116k**. Three code paths pick an implementation from the batch shape:

- **fa4 derives its masked/unmasked KV-block split from `seqlen_q`** (`BlockInfo.get_n_block_min_causal_local_mask`), so a block lands on a differently-rounding path depending on query-tile alignment -- a prefill and a cache-hit extend covering the same row disagree. A model-free repro clusters the output by `qo_len <= seqlen_k % tile_n`, and page-aligned `seqlen_k` gives one cluster. The modulus is `tile_n`, not `page_size`: sweeping page_size 128 to 1 leaves the boundary unmoved. `num_splits=1` fixes the KV-side split but not this one. `batch_invariant` masks every block instead, which is identity below the diagonal.
- **`RelLogitsProj` picks its implementation from the token count**, so a row's kernel follows the batch composition. Custom kernels bypass the aten overrides `batch_invariant_ops` installs.
- **`should_torch_symm_mem_allreduce()` takes the symmetric-memory path only below a byte threshold**, so which reduce runs follows the token count. Deterministic inference already pins `NCCL_ALGO=allreduce:tree` and disables custom all-reduce for tp>1; symmetric memory was the one path that block did not cover, and at tp=8 it dominates -- every layer all-reduces.

flashinfer autotune also selects configs per problem shape and is skipped as well. All are gated on `enable_deterministic_inference`; the default path is unchanged.

## Accuracy

Ablation on the per-commit configuration (Inkling bf16, tp=1, fa4, 6072 observations):

| fa4 split | dispatch gates | mismatches |
|---|---|---|
| – | – | 4380 |
| ✓ | – | 1844 |
| – | ✓ | 4070 |
| ✓ | ✓ | **0** |

Both are required. On `Inkling-Small-NVFP4` at tp=8 with `--enable-torch-symm-mem`, over a 116k-observation workload (10 prefixes, 10 requests each, 2048-4096 token prefixes, 2048 new tokens), the symmetric-memory gate takes **50302 mismatches to 0**.

Max-abs distance to an fp32 reference is unchanged by the fa4 change (`7.040e-04` before and after at `seqlen_k=400`), so it moves rounding, not accuracy.

The 8-GPU variant of the consistency test follows in a separate PR: it passes on this branch (27 min, 116k observations, 0 mismatches) but is a nightly-suite addition worth reviewing on its own.

title: Reduce startup log noise and fix Dynamo / CUDA-graph edge cases
author: merrymercy
body:
## Summary

Server startup emits several redundant or misleading log lines, and two small
correctness issues were found alongside them.

**Log noise:**
- The eight per-backend `"<X> MoE is enabled. The expert parallel size is adjusted ..."` warnings in `server_args.py` all say the same thing and fire unconditionally, even when `ep_size` already equals `tp_size`. They are replaced by one `logger.info` inside the `_a2a_ep_size` post-process, which is the single place the adjustment actually happens, and which only logs when the value really changes.
- The `"DeepGemm is enabled but the scale_fmt of checkpoint is not ue8m0"` warning fires on every non-ue8m0 checkpoint and is not actionable. Removed along with the now-unused `use_scale_ue8m0` attribute (it had no other readers).
- A missing `generation_config.json` is normal for many checkpoints and HF surfaces it as a generic `OSError`, not `FileNotFoundError`, so the fallback path logged a `WARNING` on every such startup. Both exception types are now handled together at `DEBUG`.
- The TRTLLM MoE deferred-finalize line used `print_info_once`, which keys on the full message; because different MoE layers can resolve to different quant methods, it printed once per distinct quant method. A module-level flag makes it once per rank.

**Correctness:**
- `load_jit` is now `@torch.compiler.disable`d. JIT compilation is pure Python/filesystem plumbing (`.resolve()` calls `os.lstat`, etc.) that Dynamo cannot trace, so a lazily-loaded kernel first reached from inside a `@torch.compile`d region produced spurious `Dynamo does not know how to trace the builtin 'posix.lstat'` graph breaks. The load is memoized, so keeping it out of the graph costs nothing.
- `BreakableCudaGraphBackend` constructed `BreakableCUDAGraph()` with no argument, so despite mixing in `DedupedCudaGraphMixin` its segments were never registered with the dedup registry. It now passes `self.deduped_cuda_graph`.
- The VLM `mem_fraction_static` adjustment is skipped when `disaggregation_mode == "decode"`. The vision encoder only runs during prefill, so PD decode engines were reserving encoder headroom they never use, shrinking the KV pool. Prefill and non-PD engines are unaffected.

Behavior for non-PD and non-multimodal serving is unchanged apart from the log output.

## Test plan

- `uv run pre-commit run --files <the 7 changed files>` — all hooks pass.
- `python3 -m py_compile` on all 7 changed files — clean.
- Verified `use_scale_ue8m0` has no remaining readers anywhere in `python/` or `test/` before removing it.
- Verified no test asserts on any of the removed/reworded log strings.
- Verified `BreakableCUDAGraph.__init__` already accepts an optional `deduped_cuda_graph` and that `DedupedCudaGraphMixin` provides the `deduped_cuda_graph` attribute, so the new argument needs no signature change.
- Not run: GPU end-to-end serving, PD-disaggregated decode startup, and the `torch.compile` + JIT-kernel path. These need multi-GPU hardware not available in this environment; the change relies on CI for runtime coverage.

## Original commits

- `26164eb83`

title: [Fix] Skip padded state slots in the chunked GDN kernel
author: Oasis-Git
body:
_forward_metadata poisons padded request rows with state index -1, and the decode kernel already skips them (fused_recurrent: `if idx >= 0`). The chunked extend kernel had no such guard, so -1 reached `initial_state + index * stride_init_state` for both the initial-state load and the in-place final-state store, addressing before the state pool. boundary_check does not help: it validates against the declared block shape, not the allocation.

Under breakable-CUDA-graph prefill with DP attention an idle DP rank replays an extend with an all-padded batch, so every row carries -1 and the kernel faults with cudaErrorIllegalAddress. Reproduced on Qwen3-Next-80B and Qwen3.5-397B on pristine main; a single request against --dp 4 is enough. No per-commit suite covers a linear-attn hybrid with DP attention, which is why this went unseen.

Add a regression test in the existing base-b (1-GPU, per-commit) kernel suite; it fails without the guard.

title: fix(mem_cache): state the MLA KV bound in the DCP index space
author: Oasis-Git
body:
set_mla_kv_buffer receives a widened logical loc under DCP — set_mla_kv_buffer_kernel keeps `loc % DCP_WORLD_SIZE == DCP_RANK` and then divides by the world size to reach the physical row — but the bounds check compared that logical index against the physical capacity, so it fires spuriously once the pool is small enough for logical indices to exceed it.

Repro on 4x GB300 with test/registered/dcp/test_kimi_linear_dcp4.py and SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT=1: as written it passes 3/3, and adding only --max-total-tokens 8192 fails with

    index >= 8256 (out of range): set_mla_kv_buffer (MLA)

Graded async asserts placed the offending index in [2x, 4x) of the physical bound, matching the dcp_size=4 logical space rather than a stray write; with the assert disabled the same configuration serves correctly (GSM8K 0.90). After this change that configuration passes 3/3 with the assert enabled.

attn_dcp_size is 1 when DCP is off, so non-DCP bounds are unchanged.

title: fix: support FA4 backend for GLM4.7-flash
author: zyzshishui
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Enable GLM-4.7-Flash to serve correctly with `--attention-backend fa4` on Blackwell using default non-deterministic decode and CUDA Graphs. SGLang's absorbed MLA presents 20 Q/QV heads over one latent KV head at TP1, but FA4's packed kernel requires the ratio to be compatible with its 128-row tile.

The current `pack_gqa=False` QV varlen decode path is incorrect for bs>1: queries after the first sequence can read another sequence's paged KV. Even if that upstream bug is fixed, unpacking would schedule Q heads separately instead of folding them into the M tile, repeating traversal of the shared latent KV and badly underutilizing 128-row decode tiles. Padding keeps the packed path; using one split also avoids unsupported automatic split-KV for QV MLA.

## Modifications

- Pad each Q/QV KV group to a tile-compatible power-of-two ratio (20 to 32 for GLM TP1), then crop output and LSE to the original heads.
- Use one split when a QV call requests automatic split selection.
- Materialize dense Q/K/V for the dedicated head-dimension-256 kernel.
- Add QV coverage to `test_flash_attn_varlen_output`. All runtime changes stay in the SGLang FA4 wrapper.

title: Fix fractional simulated acceptance in DSpark
author: weireweire
body:
## Summary

- share the existing simulated acceptance-length sampler across MTP, DFlash, and DSpark
- resample the configured acceptance length on every DSpark verify step while continuing to reuse the output tensor
- rebuild the cached tensor when its size, dtype, or device changes

## Root cause

DSpark rounded `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN` once when allocating its cached output buffer. Fractional values therefore became a fixed integer and the cached result was never refreshed, unlike the `match-expected` behavior used by the other speculative decoders.

## Validation

- Kimi K3 actual-weight TP8 DSpark inference with CUDA Graph enabled
- configured acceptance length: `4.7`, method: `match-expected`
- observed scheduler acceptance length: `4.68–4.78` across logged decode intervals
- workload: 128 input tokens, 32 output tokens, concurrency 8
- requests: 80/80 successful
- output throughput: 210.59 tokens/s
- mean TTFT: 702.51 ms; mean TPOT: 12.94 ms

title: Fix NextN weight loading by sharing the unified-loader mappings
author: yueming-yuan
body:
Loading EAGLE draft weights for a DeepSeek-V3 NextN model through the unified weight loading API crashes on missing attributes.

`DeepseekV3ForCausalLMNextN.__init__` calls `nn.Module.__init__` and rebuilds the parts of the parent init it needs, so it never reaches where `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM.__init__` sets `fuse_qkv_a_proj`, `stacked_params_mapping` and `expert_params_mapping` — the three attributes the unified loader reads off the model.

Rather than copy that block into the subclass, this extracts it into `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM.init_unified_loader_mappings()` and calls it from both `__init__`s, right after `determine_num_fused_shared_experts()` (which `expert_params_mapping` depends on). A subclass that builds its own `__init__` now has one call to make instead of a block to keep in sync.

`fuse_qkv_a_proj` is still assigned early in the parent, before `packed_modules_mapping` needs it; the helper recomputes the same value from config, so the parent behaviour is unchanged.

Repro: GLM-5.2 744B with `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE` on the glm_moe_dsa (DeepSeek-V3 lineage) path.

title: Fix MXFP4 scale placeholder initialization
author: weireweire
body:
## Summary

- Initialize serialized MXFP4 MoE scale placeholders with the raw UE8M0 encoding of 1.0 instead of zero.
- Keep packed weight placeholders zero-filled; real checkpoint loading still overwrites the scale placeholders.

## Failure

A real-weight Kimi K3 presharded reload with the MegaMoE/DeepGEMM path failed while rebuilding the post-processed parameter layout. Reload invokes process_weights_after_loading on a fresh model skeleton before copying the cached tensors, and the fresh MXFP4 scale placeholders reached DeepGEMM first.

The workers aborted in deep_gemm/include/deep_gemm/impls/smxx_layout.cuh:131, surfaced as CUDA error 719 from transform_sf_into_required_layout. This happened before the cached scales could be restored.

## Root cause

Serialized MXFP4 scales are stored as raw uint8 UE8M0 bytes. Fresh modules previously zero-filled these tensors. UE8M0 byte 0 represents 2^-127; converting it to FP32 produces a subnormal value instead of the normalized power-of-two representation required by the DeepGEMM layout transform.

Dummy initialization only randomizes floating-point tensors, so the uint8 scale tensors also retained their zero placeholders.

## Fix

Initialize the two serialized MXFP4 MoE scale tensors with byte 127, the UE8M0 representation of 1.0. This provides a neutral normalized placeholder for post-load processing and dummy execution while preserving normal checkpoint-loading behavior.

## Validation

The behavior was validated with actual Kimi K3 weights by seeding the same scale placeholders to byte 127 immediately before post-processing, which is equivalent to the initialization performed by this change. A TP8 disaggregated deployment with one prefill worker and eight decode workers completed all 144 target/draft rank reloads without the DeepGEMM assertion. An 8K-input/1K-output benchmark then completed 1280/1280 requests.

The full pre-commit suite also passed.

title: Fix NaN logits from deterministic Triton extend on the unified memory pool
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

`--enable-unified-memory` + `--attention-backend triton` + `--enable-deterministic-inference` together produce `NaN` logits. Any two of the three are fine, which is why no existing test caught it. Found while adding a PD-disaggregation test in #33362; this is a pre-existing defect on `main`, unrelated to PD, and #33362 works around it by not setting those flags together.

The failure is nastier than a crash: it only *aborts* when `SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT` is armed (which CI does):

```
_assert_async_cuda_kernel: Assertion `NaN detected! sampler: next_token_logits` failed.
```

Without that flag the run completes and returns finite top-k logprobs, so the corruption is silent locally.

## Root cause

`--enable-deterministic-inference` routes Triton extend through `TritonAttnBackend._forward_extend_unified`, a 1-stage kernel that reads **both** the prefix and the extend half of the KV out of the pool — unlike the default 2-stage path, which takes the extend half from its `k`/`v` arguments and only reads the prefix from the pool.

That kernel was given `forward_batch.out_cache_loc` untranslated. On the unified memory pool `out_cache_loc` holds **virtual** ids, and the prefix `kv_indices` are already translated in `init_forward_metadata`. So the prefix was read at physical ids while the just-written extend tokens were read at virtual ones; the mismatched reads produce garbage that becomes NaN by the LM head.

This also explains the three-way condition exactly:
- **without deterministic** — the 2-stage kernel never reads the extend half from the pool;
- **without unified memory** — `out_cache_loc` is already physical, so no translation is needed;
- **without Triton** — another backend doesn't use this kernel.

## Modifications

Use the translation already computed once per forward for the KV write (`forward_metadata.out_cache_loc_full_physical`) as the extend read indices. This matches the idiom a few lines above in the same function's `k is None` branch (SWA translate first, else the unified translate), which is where the pattern was established — line 1600 was simply missed.

- SWA layers keep taking the raw virtual loc: `translate_loc_from_full_to_swa` consumes virtual ids by contract.
- Reuses the per-forward translation rather than re-translating, because `_forward_extend_unified` runs once per layer.
- **No effect on static pools**: `out_cache_loc_full_physical` is `None` unless the allocator exposes a virtual→physical translate, and `translate_kv_loc` / `translate_kv_loc_dense` are defined only in `multi_ended_allocator.py` (the unified allocators).

Incidentally this also repairs unified **SWA** pools under deterministic Triton extend, whose full-attention layers hit the same path (not covered by the test below; the test uses the MLA hybrid-Mamba pool).

## Validation

On `yujiepan/kimi-linear-tiny-random`, 257-token prompt, `SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT=1`:

| config | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| unified + triton + deterministic | **NaN abort** | `[-11.908, -11.918, -11.880, -11.880]` |
| static + triton + deterministic (reference) | same values | same values |

The fixed unified run is bit-identical to the static pool, which is the real confirmation — not merely "no longer NaN".

New regression test `test/registered/attention/test_unified_memory_deterministic.py` asserts unified-vs-static parity under the three flags. Verified it **fails on the unfixed code** (1 NaN assert) and **passes on the fix**. Triton is pinned there on purpose: the defect lives in the Triton deterministic kernel, so a resolved default backend would not exercise it.

title: Multiple flexibility fixes for DP attention
author: merrymercy
body:
## Motivation

Some custom adaptive speculative-decoding workers construct a `ForwardBatch` outside of
`ForwardBatch.init_new`, and the DP-attention MLP sync metadata was only
reachable as an inline block inside `init_new`. Those workers can also produce
draft inputs whose hidden states have not been materialized yet, which trips
the unconditional pad/unpad on `hidden_states`.

Separately, the DP CUDA graph batch size was derived by dividing the synced
token counts by the captured request width, but only for an explicitly
enumerated set of spec algorithms. Any externally registered algorithm outside that list — or any
algorithm with a variable per-request draft width — got a mis-sized graph.
`can_run_graph` already used the raw per-rank request counts, so the two sites
could disagree.

## Modifications

- Extract the inline "For MLP sync" block in `init_new` into a reusable
  `ForwardBatch.init_mlp_sync_metadata` method. Behavior in the `init_new` path
  is unchanged.
- Guard the speculative `hidden_states` pad and the target-verify unpad on
  `hidden_states` being present.
- Use `num_tokens_per_req` instead of `draft_token_num` for the target-verify
  unpad width, so it stays correct when the per-request draft width varies.
- Add `DecodeCudaGraphRunner._max_dp_batch_size` and use it for both
  `can_run_graph` and the replay path. It reads the raw per-rank request counts
  directly, dropping the width division and the per-algorithm enumeration, and
  raises instead of silently mis-sizing the graph when the counts are missing.

## Original commits

- `166283bed`

## Test plan

- `python test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_mlp_sync_pad_unpad.py -v` —
  5 tests pass, including three new ones covering speculative width scaling in
  `init_mlp_sync_metadata`, padding a draft input with no hidden states, and
  `_max_dp_batch_size` (both the normal path and the missing-counts raise).
- `pre-commit run --files <the three changed files>` — all hooks pass.
- Verified on an internal DP-attention setup with adaptive speculative decoding
  enabled.
- Not run locally: multi-GPU DP-attention end-to-end and CUDA graph capture
  tests, which need a multi-GPU environment. Relying on CI for those.

title: fix(metrics): clear forward occupancy on idle
author: merrymercy
body:
## Motivation

When a scheduler becomes idle, the forward-occupancy gauge can retain its last active value because cached stats are published before the device-timer window is reset. The idle-reporting rate limit can then suppress the finite-to-NaN transition indefinitely.

## Modifications

- Reset both live and cached forward occupancy before idle reporting.
- Bypass the idle-reporting throttle once when occupancy becomes stale.
- Consolidate device-timer reset handling in the idle metrics path.
- Add CPU coverage for immediate idle publication and metrics-disabled resets.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable; this changes observability state only and does not affect model outputs.

title: [Fix] Restore data_parallel_rank alias on native /generate (dp-aware gateway routing is silently dropped)
author: sshleifer
body:
# Motivation

`sgl-model-gateway`'s dp-aware mode injects `data_parallel_rank` into every request it forwards ([`DPAwareWorker::prepare_request`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/7adf2f4a9a4389d1c021a2caf128cf7e2f4adb35/sgl-model-gateway/src/core/worker.rs#L1106-L1118); the worker's own unit test [asserts this exact spelling](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/7adf2f4a9a4389d1c021a2caf128cf7e2f4adb35/sgl-model-gateway/src/core/worker.rs#L1806)). On the native `/generate` path, current servers silently drop that field, so the gateway's routing decision never reaches the DP controller and dispatch falls back to load balancing. **dp-aware routing over native `/generate` is currently a silent no-op.**

## How this happened

- #19268 renamed `GenerateReqInput.data_parallel_rank` → `routed_dp_rank`, keeping a deprecated alias that mapped to `routed_dp_rank` (with a `DeprecationWarning`) in `normalize_batch_and_arguments()`.
- #29214 (a cleanup, merged 2026-06-25) removed that alias from `GenerateReqInput` — but the gateway still emits the old spelling, and the alias still exists on the two other ingress paths: the OpenAI-compat layer ([`_migrate_deprecated_dp_rank`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/7adf2f4a9a4389d1c021a2caf128cf7e2f4adb35/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py#L303-L315)) and [`Engine.generate()`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/7adf2f4a9a4389d1c021a2caf128cf7e2f4adb35/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py#L313-L325). Native HTTP `/generate` is the only entrypoint that lost it.

## Why it's silent

FastAPI parses `GenerateReqInput` as a (pydantic) dataclass that ignores unknown keys, so nothing errors; `routed_dp_rank` stays `None`; and the DP controller has a legitimate fallback for that case — [load balancing](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/7adf2f4a9a4389d1c021a2caf128cf7e2f4adb35/python/sglang/srt/managers/data_parallel_controller.py#L736). The failure mode is pure performance (prefix-cache hit rate and routing quality quietly degrade), which makes it hard to notice and hard to bisect.

We hit this in production on a dp=4 deployment with the gateway in dp-aware mode (session-keyed manual routing): prefix-cache hit rate was ~0.49 with the routing silently dropped vs ~0.97 with the rank honored, roughly 2x decode throughput on an agentic workload. Verified mechanically: `/generate` with `routed_dp_rank=2` moves only rank 2's prefill counters, while `data_parallel_rank=2` moves whichever rank load balancing picks.

# Modifications

Restore exactly what #29214 removed from `GenerateReqInput`: the deprecated `data_parallel_rank` field, plus the mapping in `normalize_batch_and_arguments()` (explicit `routed_dp_rank` wins) with the original `DeprecationWarning`. This mirrors the aliases still present in `protocol.py` and `engine.py`.

Unit tests in `test/registered/unit/managers/test_io_struct.py`: alias maps to `routed_dp_rank`, alias does not override an explicit `routed_dp_rank`, alias propagates to batch items.

# Alternatives considered

We recognize a deprecated alias is not the cleanest end state, so laying out the option space explicitly:

1. **Fix the gateway instead: emit `routed_dp_rank`.** The right long-term spelling, but insufficient alone. The gateway/router is released and deployed separately from the server, so every already-shipped gateway keeps emitting the old name; and a gateway that emits *only* the new name still leaves servers built between #29214 and this fix broken. The server-side alias repairs **all released gateway versions at once** on the next server upgrade. Compatibility matrix:

   | server version \ gateway | emits `data_parallel_rank` (all released) | emits both (proposed follow-up) |
   |---|---|---|
   | #19268 → #29214 | works (alias) | works |
   | #29214 → this fix | **silently broken** | works |
   | ≥ this fix | works (alias restored) | works |

   We'd suggest a follow-up where the gateway emits **both** spellings for a deprecation window, then switches to `routed_dp_rank` only — happy to send that PR.

2. **Map the alias at the HTTP boundary (`http_server.py`) instead of the dataclass.** Keeps `io_struct` clean, but `/generate` is not the only constructor of `GenerateReqInput` (Vertex endpoint, engine API), and `normalize_batch_and_arguments()` is the existing normalization choke point — it's also where #19268 originally put this exact mapping.

3. **Reject unknown fields on native `/generate`.** Strict parsing would have turned this silent no-op into a loud 422 and would catch future drift between what the gateway injects and what the server accepts. It's a breaking change for clients that send extra keys, so out of scope here, but possibly worth a separate discussion.

4. **Do nothing and require clients to migrate.** Leaves every deployed dp-aware gateway silently broken on the native path.

If maintainers prefer option 1 with a hard break (no server-side alias), we're glad to rework — but the gateway change should then land and be *released* before the alias is (re-)removed, i.e. the ordering that #29214 missed. A cheap recurrence guard would be a test asserting that every key `DPAwareWorker::prepare_request` injects is accepted by `GenerateReqInput`; happy to add one if there's appetite.

# Test

```
pytest test/registered/unit/managers/test_io_struct.py
30 passed
```

title: Fix Whisper transcription for audio over 30 seconds
author: shenxiul
body:
## Summary

Whisper's feature extractor pads or truncates input to its fixed 3000-mel-frame (30-second) encoder window, so `/v1/audio/transcriptions` silently drops everything after 30 seconds when the serving layer sends a long file as one generation.

This change:

- splits long Whisper audio into contiguous chunks of at most 30 seconds;
- places each seam at the quietest 100 ms RMS window within the final second of the chunk, matching the former vLLM speech-to-text behavior;
- runs non-streaming chunks concurrently and stitches results in audio order;
- streams chunks sequentially with one final finish frame;
- offsets `verbose_json` segment timestamps by each chunk's start time;
- preserves fused language auto-detection and reports the first chunk's detected language;
- gates chunking through the transcription adapter, so Qwen3-ASR and other adapters remain unchanged.

Each chunk receives an independent sampling-parameter dictionary because the multimodal processor consumes transcription-only keys while preparing decoder prompts.

## Validation

- Added CPU unit coverage for energy-aware split points, contiguity, maximum duration, waveform preservation, short-audio behavior, ordered stitching, chunk failures and aborts, streaming, fused auto-detection, spaceless scripts, and verbose timestamp offsets.
- Added GPU endpoint coverage using a 40-second clip whose speech begins after Whisper's 30-second encoder window: JSON transcription, `verbose_json` timestamps past 30 seconds, and streaming.
- The audio splitter tests pass locally (5 tests).
- Changed Python files pass AST, isort, Ruff, Black, codespell, CI registry, merge-conflict, and private-key checks; `compileall` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Live validation with `openai/whisper-large-v3` on a 57.06-second file produced the complete transcript, including segments after 30 seconds, with one streaming stop frame. Split points and explicit-language output matched vLLM 0.11.0.

title: [Spec] Fix Dspark and Dflash state divergence across TP rank
author: JackZeng0208
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Related to: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33289

To fix https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33289 bug, upgrade NCCL to the newest version (2.30.7).

When TP > 1, Dspark makes serveral sampling decisions on reach rank: 
1. The draft Markov chain samples proposal tokens step by step (with in-graph philox noise introduced since https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33298)
2. Target verify derives `correct_len` / `bonus` / `cap_trim_lens`
3. Prefill samples `next_token_ids`

In order to maintain the speedup, SGLang skips cross-rank sync of sampled tokens by default (I found the comment here: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py#L496). So nothing forces these values to agree. Once one rank commits a different token or accept length, sequence lengths and KV state drift apart and a later collective deadlocks (demonstrated by fault injection in the Accuracy Tests section below).

## Modifications

Broadcast rank 0's sampling decisions before they affect state. The idea follows the existing `verify_lens` handling in `dspark_planner.py` and the EAGLE proposals in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/29003 and https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31478:
1. Broadcast every Markov proposal token in **both** eager and graph-folded sampling. Sync only at the end of a draft block is too late because each step depends on the previous token.
2. Broadcast `correct_len`, `bonus`, and `cap_trim_lens` in the eager verify path and the captured verify epilogue, before finalization, token output, or KV commit. Separate `all_reduce(MIN)` calls could combine fields from different ranks.
3. Broadcast prefill `next_token_ids` before entering the draft path.

`DsparkTpSync` in `dspark_tp.py` (newly added file) uses the TP group's PyNCCL communicator. Process-group collectives cannot be captured in CUDA graphs, and using the model's existing TP communicator preserves collective ordering across eager and captured execution. With DP attention, it uses `attn_tp_group`, matching `verify_lens_broadcast_group` in original `dspark_planner.py`. TP=1 is a no-op.

The reason why I don't match RNG seeds is because ranks can still diverge if they consume different numbers of random values, and it does not cover non-RNG differences.

In addition, for TP > 1, this add `gamma + 3` broadcasts of a `[bs]` tensor per decode step, all within the captured graphs.


## Accuracy Tests

All tests below on following configs: 
- 2 DGX Sparks
- TP=2
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 with 131k context
- Decode CUDA graphs and folded sampling enabled
- Add https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33407 code. It fixes an unrelated bug for SM12x sparse-MLA topk dispatch crash at boot. Dspark + DeepSeek V4 Flash cannot start on DGX Sparks without it.
- **NCCL 2.30.7** for SGLang's PyNCCL communicator via `SGLANG_NCCL_SO_PATH` (torch's bundled 2.28.9 wedges this workload's graph/eager mix with or without this patch; a separate problem from this fix)

For accuracy test, we run`python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 200` (temp=0): accuracy 0.965, invalid 0.000. This is expected since there's no mathematical changes.

To demonstrate the failure mode this patch addresses, we fault-injected a rank-local accept divergence into both builds: rank 1 lowers every accept length by one (`correct_len = torch.clamp(correct_len - 1, min=0)`, NCCL 2.30.7 in both _runs).
**_Note: the fault reproduction code has been removed before submitting PR._**
 
Without the fix, the server deadlocks before finishing startup warmup. With the fix, the same injection is harmless: rank 0's broadcast overwrites the divergent values, the server boots, and a temp=0 request returns the expected output.

As a stability check on the fix itself (its broadcasts run inside the captured decode graphs), I sent 42 sequential chat requests with `ignore_eos=true` and `max_tokens=512` (30 at temp=1, then 12 at temp=0) and probed `/health_generate` after every request with a 180s client timeout, so a stuck collective surfaces as a failed request instead of a silent hang. As the result, all 42 returned HTTP 200 with `finish_reason=length`. 21504 tokens generated in total and mean acc_len during the temp=1 run was 2.86 (block_size=4). Same for temp=0, neither of them occur any error.


## Speed Tests and Profiling

Test on 24 natural prompts, 256 output tokens, concurrency=1, temp=1, same setup as above:

| Requests | Output throughput | TTFT mean/median/P90 (ms) | TPOT mean/median/P90 (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 24 | 31.9 tok/s | 157.6 / 153.7 / 178.6 | 30.8 / 31.7 / 35.5 |

Comparing with pre-fix TP baseline is impossible because it cannot survive under such load.

title: Fix serving benchmark post-warmup cache flush race
author: mmangkad
body:
## Summary

Fixes a post-warmup cache flush race in the serving benchmark exposed by #32481. Warmup requests can return before the scheduler is fully idle, causing `/flush_cache` to return 400 and abort the benchmark.

The benchmark now passes a timeout to `/flush_cache` so it can wait for the scheduler to become idle, configurable with `--flush-cache-timeout` and defaulting to 60 seconds.

title: fix(mamba): widen causal_conv1d token offsets to int64
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

`_causal_conv1d_fwd_kernel` indexes `x` and `o` with 32-bit arithmetic:

```python
x_base = x_ptr + sequence_start_index * stride_x_token + idx_feats * stride_x_dim
```

Under a channel-last layout `stride_x_token` is the full token pitch (for a fused QKV projection this is the whole projection width, e.g. 36864), so the product overflows int32 once the packed batch reaches `2**31 / stride_x_token` tokens. The offset wraps negative and the kernel reads outside the allocation.

The tail read at

```python
x_ptrs = x_ptr + ((sequence_start_index + idx_tokens_last) * stride_x_token)[:, None] + ...
```

reaches the end of each sequence, so the trigger is the batch's **total token count** times the token pitch — a single long sequence is enough, no unusual batch composition required. With a 36864 token pitch the limit is ~58k tokens, which a long-context prefill reaches easily.

The same file already casts a neighbouring index (`conv_state_batch_coord`) to `tl.int64`, so this looks like an oversight rather than an intentional 32-bit contract.

## Modifications

Cast the token-offset products to `tl.int64` at the five sites that scale an index by `stride_x_token` / `stride_o_token`:

- `x_base` (sequence base)
- `x_ptrs` (tail read for the initial-state window)
- `prior_tokens` (prior-token read for `chunk_offset > 0`)
- `x_base_1d` (chunk base)
- `o_ptrs` (output write)

No functional change below the overflow threshold; the casts only widen the index arithmetic.

## Accuracy Tests

Throughout: **Before** = this branch's base, **After** = the same tree with the five casts in this PR. Nothing else differs.

### Kernel, in isolation

`causal_conv1d_fn` driven directly (no model), channel-last input of pitch 36864 and 8192-token sequences. Every sequence in a packed batch is compared against the same sequence run alone at start offset 0, which cannot overflow. NVIDIA GB300, torch 2.11.0+cu130.

The script calls `causal_conv1d_fn` directly with `TOKEN_PITCH = 36864`, `SEQ_LEN = 8192`, and takes the number of packed sequences as its only argument:

```bash
python repro_conv1d_int32.py 7    # 57,344 tokens — stays under 2^31
python repro_conv1d_int32.py 9    # 73,728 tokens — crosses 2^31
```

| Packed batch | `tokens x pitch` | Before | After |
|---|---:|---|---|
| 7 sequences, 57,344 tokens | 2,113,929,216 — under 2^31 | all sequences match | all sequences match |
| 9 sequences, 73,728 tokens | 2,415,919,104 — over 2^31 | `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` | all sequences match, max abs diff 0.000000 |

The 7-sequence control stays below `2**31` and passes unmodified, so the failure is attributable to crossing the int32 boundary rather than to tensor size.

### End to end

The same threshold is reachable from a single request. Kimi-K3, `pp_size=8` `tp_size=1`, 2 nodes, `--chunked-prefill-size 65536`, one 64001-token prompt (`64001 * 36864 = 2,360,315,904`).

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path "$MODEL" --trust-remote-code \
  --tp-size 1 --pp-size 8 \
  --nnodes 2 --node-rank "$SLURM_PROCID" --dist-init-addr "$MASTER:29500" \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \
  --attention-backend flashinfer \
  --chunked-prefill-size 65536 --max-prefill-tokens 65536 \
  --max-running-requests 64 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000
```

`--attention-backend flashinfer` is required here: at `tp_size=1` a single rank holds all 96 attention heads, which `trtllm_mla` (the model default) does not support. Then one request, which tokenises to 64,001 tokens:

```python
prompt = "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. " * 6400
requests.post("http://localhost:30000/generate",
              json={"text": prompt,
                    "sampling_params": {"max_new_tokens": 8, "temperature": 0}})
```

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| serving one 64,001-token prompt | `SERVER-READY`, then `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` while serving the request; client sees `RemoteDisconnected` | `Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 64001`, then a normal completion |

The crash surfaces at `prepare_chunk_indices` in the linear-attention path, which is an asynchronous synchronisation point rather than the faulting kernel — the attribution here comes from the controlled comparison, not from the traceback location.

### GSM8K, no regression

200 questions, same Kimi-K3 `pp_size=8` setup:

| `--chunked-prefill-size` | Before | After |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 16384 | 0.985 | 0.990 |
| 65536 | 0.985 | 0.985 |

Below the overflow threshold the casts are bit-exact — the per-sequence comparison above reports max abs diff 0.000000 for every sequence that does not cross `2**31` — so this is a no-regression check rather than a measurement that could move. Note the "After" tree also carries the pipeline-parallel mamba pool sizing fix, since that is what lifts the concurrency ceiling far enough for a packed batch to reach the threshold at all; the isolated evidence for this PR is the per-sequence comparison, not this table.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run; the change only widens index arithmetic inside the existing kernel and adds no new work.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). See the note below.
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

### On the missing unit test

A faithful regression test has to actually cross `2**31`, which means a real backing buffer of a bit over 2^31 elements (~5 GiB at bf16) — the offset only wraps if the memory behind it exists, otherwise both the patched and unpatched kernels read out of bounds and the test stops discriminating. That seemed too heavy to add to the default suite without a maintainer's call on where it belongs, so the reproduction above was run out of tree. Happy to add it behind a memory guard if that is preferred.

title: fix(PP): size the mamba pool per pipeline stage, not per whole model
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

`KVCacheConfigurator._handle_max_mamba_cache` sizes the mamba state pool from `config.mamba2_cache_params.mamba_cache_per_req`, which is computed over the whole model's mamba layer list:

```python
) * len(self.layers)      # configs/mamba_utils.py
```

Under pipeline parallelism each rank only allocates state for the layers in its own `[start_layer, end_layer)` slice — the allocation paths in this same file already filter on that range. Charging the whole model against a single stage over-estimates the per-slot cost by roughly `pp_size`, so the pool is sized for a fraction of the requests that actually fit.

On Kimi-K3 (93 layers, 69 linear-attention layers) at `pp_size=8` this resolves to a 26-slot pool, which clamps `max_running_requests` to 6. That propagates: `resolve_max_num_reqs` clamps `max_running_requests` to `max_mamba_cache_size // ratio`, which in turn sets `pp_max_micro_batch_size`.

## Modifications

Scale the per-request cost (and the ReplaySSM ring, which is sized the same way) by the stage's share of the mamba layers.

The scale is taken from the stage holding the **most** mamba layers, not from this rank's own count. Both give the same system-wide capacity — the system is limited by the heaviest stage either way — but the maximum is identical on every rank, so `max_mamba_cache_size`, `max_running_requests` and `pp_max_micro_batch_size` stay uniform across stages without a collective. Scaling by each rank's own share instead makes those values diverge whenever the mamba layers do not split evenly, which is the common case: at `pp_size=8` a 93-layer model distributes its 69 mamba layers as `[9, 8, 8, 9, 9, 9, 9, 8]`.

Sweeping 145 mamba budgets from 4 to 40 GiB on that layout:

| scaling | budgets where `pp_max_micro_batch_size` diverges across stages |
|---|---|
| this rank's own share | 95/145 (65.5%) |
| largest stage's share (this PR) | 0/145 |

`pp_max_micro_batch_size` has to agree on every stage: it decides how a batch is split into microbatches, so a stage that picks a different split disagrees with its neighbours about which sequences are in flight.

Every rank computes the layer distribution locally from `get_pp_indices`, so nothing is communicated. At `pp_size=1` the rank holds every mamba layer and the scale is exactly 1.

## Accuracy Tests

End to end on Kimi-K3 with real weights, `pp_size=8` `tp_size=1`, 2 nodes, `--attention-backend flashinfer`, GSM8K 200 questions:

| | `max_mamba_cache_size` | `max_running_requests` | GSM8K |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| before, `--chunked-prefill-size 16384` | 26 | 6 | 0.985 |
| after, `--chunked-prefill-size 16384` | **210** | **52** | 0.990 |
| before, `--chunked-prefill-size 65536` | 26 | 6 | 0.985 |
| after, `--chunked-prefill-size 65536` | **210** | **52** | 0.985 |

The pool grows 8.1x and the concurrency ceiling 8.7x, while the score stays in the same band (the 0.985/0.990 spread is one question out of 200). The change only lifts a capacity limit; it does not touch any compute path.

What that "before" column looks like in the startup log: the unpatched tree allocates a per-stage pool but charges the whole model against it, so every stage lands on the same starved cap.

```
PP0  max_mamba_cache_size: 26   conv_state 0.05GB   ssm_state 1.42GB
PP1  max_mamba_cache_size: 26   conv_state 0.04GB   ssm_state 1.27GB
PP2  max_mamba_cache_size: 26   conv_state 0.04GB   ssm_state 1.27GB
PP3  max_mamba_cache_size: 26   conv_state 0.05GB   ssm_state 1.42GB
PP4  max_mamba_cache_size: 26   conv_state 0.05GB   ssm_state 1.42GB
PP5  max_mamba_cache_size: 26   conv_state 0.05GB   ssm_state 1.42GB
PP6  max_mamba_cache_size: 26   conv_state 0.05GB   ssm_state 1.42GB
PP7  max_mamba_cache_size: 26   conv_state 0.04GB   ssm_state 1.27GB

all stages: max_running_requests is capped to 6 by the mamba state cache
            (max_mamba_cache_size=26, 4 state slots per request)
```

The allocated `ssm_state` already varies with what each stage holds — 1.42 GB on the stages with 9 mamba layers, 1.27 GB on those with 8 (the layers distribute as `[9, 8, 8, 9, 9, 9, 9, 8]`). The pool size does not: all eight stages are sized as if they held all 69.

The same over-charge also applies when the pool size is given explicitly. `--max-mamba-cache-size` skips the auto solve, so the pool itself comes out right, but the memory the solver then books for it still uses the whole-model per-request cost — leaving too little for the KV pool. Same layout, 70 GiB handed to the solver:

| `--max-mamba-cache-size` | KV budget left, before | after |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 112 | 39.36 GiB | 66.00 GiB |
| 144 | 30.69 GiB | 64.87 GiB |
| 210 | 12.80 GiB | 62.54 GiB |
| 328 | **-19.20 GiB** | 58.37 GiB |

At 328 the budget goes negative and there is no KV pool left to build, which is what an operator sees as "raising `--max-mamba-cache-size` makes startup fail".

Driving `_handle_max_mamba_cache` once per rank on the same layer layout with an 8 GiB budget isolates the same effect:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `pp_size=1` pool | 8 | 8 (unchanged) |
| `pp_size=8` pool, per rank | 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8 | 74, 74, 74, 74, 74, 74, 74, 74 |

`TestPPMambaPoolSizing` in `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mamba_donated_alloc_ratio.py` adds two CPU-only tests. `test_stage_is_not_charged_for_the_whole_model` fails on the unpatched tree and passes with this change; running that file goes from `1 failed, 7 passed` to `8 passed`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The pool size this PR unlocks is what an agentic serving configuration actually wants. On a 1P1D deployment (8 GPUs running PP8 prefill, 8 running TP8 decode) with a trace-replay workload of 98,827 requests — mean input 219k tokens, p90 549k, ~98% theoretical prefix reuse — a 144-slot mamba pool with a 14.5M-token KV pool sustains:

| client concurrency | effective total | per GPU | TTFT p50 | prompt cache read |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16 | 70,756 tok/s | 4,422 | — | 94.7% |
| 24 | 78,437 tok/s | 4,902 | 7.05 s | 93.6% |
| 32 | 26,184 tok/s | 1,637 | 85.10 s | 92.8% |
| 32, decode `--decode-context-parallel-size 8` | 82,977 tok/s | 5,186 | 6.8 s | 71.2% |

"Effective total" counts prompt tokens including cache hits, which is what the client sees; at 93.6% reuse the recomputed share is far smaller. The per-GPU column divides by all 16 GPUs in the deployment. The last row is the mean of two runs; the drop at concurrency 32 is a decode-side KV limit, not a mamba one, and decode context parallelism removes it.

That operating point is not reachable without this change: the auto solve gives roughly `1/pp_size` of it, and setting `--max-mamba-cache-size` by hand instead runs into the accounting problem above. The numbers are a capability statement, not a before/after delta — there is no matched "before" run at this pool size because the configuration does not come up.

Per-token cost is unchanged; this PR only lifts a capacity limit.

### Note for existing deployments

Correcting the over-charge frees real memory, so at an unchanged `--mem-fraction-static` the solver hands the KV pool what the mamba pool was previously over-booking. On a Kimi-K3 PP8 prefill instance that moved `max_total_tokens` from 2,123,072 to 21,287,872 at the same flag value, and the instance then failed to start. The old over-charge was acting as unintended headroom. Deployments tuned against the previous accounting may need to lower `--mem-fraction-static` or pin `--max-total-tokens` after this change.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

### Merge order

This PR raises the concurrency ceiling, which makes packed prefill batches larger. On the same hardware that turns out to be what makes the int32 overflow in #33665 reachable in practice: before this change `max_running_requests` is clamped to 6 and a batch never gets near the 2^31 threshold, after it the ceiling is 52. Worth landing that one first.

title: [Fix] Correct W4AFP8 DeepEP scaling and mode-specific dtypes
author: CyberSecurityErial
body:
## Motivation

W4AFP8 with DeepEP had two independent failures in the same normal/prefill path.

First, `cutlass_w4a8_moe_deepep_normal` called `deepep_post_reorder_triton_kernel` without the required `routed_scaling_factor`, causing the original first-request `TypeError` in #33660. The model forward applies routed scaling after the cross-rank DeepEP combine, so this rank-local reduction must receive the neutral value `1.0`; using the model factor here would scale twice.

After the first fix, the reporter reproduced a second failure on 4xH200: DeepEP `intranode.cu:926` reported `Unsupported type`. That line is the normal **combine** dtype switch, not an INT4-weight dispatch site; DeepEP only transports activations and its normal combine accepts BF16. The actual problem was SGLang's dtype selection:

- W4AFP8 normal/prefill requantizes BF16 activations with checkpoint static scales, so its DeepEP payload must remain BF16.
- W4AFP8 low-latency/decode consumes DeepEP FP8 activations together with per-token-group scales, so that payload must remain FP8.
- With `--deepep-mode auto`, the previous global default selected FP8 for both implementations. The normal W4AFP8 path discarded the returned FP8 scale; a zero-token expert rank then returned an FP8 tensor directly to DeepEP's BF16-only normal combine, producing the reported assertion. Globally forcing BF16 would fix prefill but break low-latency decode.

Fixes #33660.

## Modifications

- Pass neutral `routed_scaling_factor=1.0` to the W4AFP8 DeepEP-normal post-reorder kernel.
- Let each concrete DeepEP implementation resolve a mode-specific dispatcher dtype.
- Configure W4AFP8 as normal=`bf16`, low-latency=`fp8`, including `auto` mode and TBO wrappers through the existing dispatcher configuration propagation.
- Add explicit guards for invalid normal and low-latency payloads, avoiding silent scale loss.
- Add CPU regressions for the kernel argument, per-mode dtype resolution, zero-token normal behavior, and missing low-latency scales.

## Accuracy Tests

The original routed-scale regression was run in the H20 SGLang image and passed before this update. The issue reporter independently confirmed that it fixes the original missing-argument `TypeError`.

For the mode-specific dtype update, the available H20s are serving traffic and the exact W4AFP8 checkpoint is not locally available, so a full model E2E was not run. The following non-GPU checks pass on current `main`:

```text
Black: passed
isort: passed
Ruff (F401, F821, UP037): passed
Python compilation: passed
scripts/ci/check_registered_tests.py: passed
Rebase/diff checks: passed
```

The new CPU regression is registered in `base-a-test-cpu`; an H200 retest is requested from the reporter.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. This corrects payload format and a required kernel argument without changing the MoE algorithm.

## Checklist

- [x] Rebased onto current `main`.
- [x] Formatted with repository-compatible tools.
- [x] Added targeted CPU regression coverage.
- [x] Documentation is not affected.
- [x] No public API behavior is changed.
