title: [Fix] detokenizer router: Route by rid without tokenizer worker ipcs and broadcast logging config
author: adityasingh2400
body:
`MultiDetokenizerRouter` keys each request on its `http_worker_ipc`, which is only stamped with more than one tokenizer worker. Two failures follow:

- With `--tokenizer-worker-num 1 --detokenizer-worker-num > 1`, the scheduler sends `http_worker_ipcs` as a list of `None`, and the router fails its assertion on the first batch (`AssertionError: ... has invalid http_worker_ipcs`).
- `ConfigureLoggingReq` is routed like a single request, so only one detokenizer gets the new logging config. With one tokenizer worker, it hits the same assertion.

Changes:

- When a request has no `http_worker_ipc`, the router hashes its `rid` instead. Requests that have one keep the current key, so the grouped sends from #42238 and #44288 are unchanged.
- `ConfigureLoggingReq` is broadcast to every detokenizer, like `FreezeGCReq`.
- `_split_batch_by_key` takes the per-request keys and copies `http_worker_ipcs` from the output.

Verified on one H200 with Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct: on main, `--tokenizer-worker-num 1 --detokenizer-worker-num 2` crashes the router on the first request. With this PR, `/generate` and `/configure_logging` return 200 at 1/2 and 2/2 tokenizer/detokenizer workers.

Tests: `test_router_keys_on_rid_without_tokenizer_worker_ipcs` and `test_router_broadcasts_logging_config_and_routes_single_req_by_rid` in `test/registered/unit/managers/test_multi_tokenizer_mixin.py`.

title: Fix Grok-2 nightly: derive image-understanding capability from is_multimodal
author: yctseng0211
body:
## Motivation
The `nightly-amd-accuracy-8-gpu-grok2` suite has been failing since #32914 merged. `xai-org/grok-2` never finishes startup:
```
[2026-08-05 08:28:43] INFO:     127.0.0.1:56094 - "POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 400 Bad Request
[2026-08-05 08:28:43] Initialization failed. warmup error: Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/sglang-checkout/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/http_server.py", line 2281, in _execute_server_warmup
    assert res.status_code == 200, f"{res.text}"
AssertionError: {"object":"error","message":"Model only supports text input; received unsupported content type 'image_url'.","type":"BadRequestError","param":null,"code":400}
[2026-08-05 08:28:43] kill_process_tree called: parent_pid=5123, include_parent=True, pid=5123
...
Exception: Server process exited with code -9. Check server logs for errors.
```
Root cause: `ModelConfig` derives two modality flags from two independent heuristics with no enforced relationship between them.
`is_multimodal` is `False` for grok-2. #23383 made that correct on purpose — grok-2's HF config (`model_type="git"`) auto-populates a `vision_config` in `__post_init__`, so the sub-config heuristic is gated behind `model_impl == TRANSFORMERS`. The architecture is `Grok1ForCausalLM`, which is not in `multimodal_model_archs` (only `Grok1VForCausalLM` / `Grok1AForCausalLM` are).
`is_image_understandable_model` was missed by that fix and still keyed on the raw `hasattr(hf_config, "vision_config")`, so it is `True` for grok-2. That value reaches `/model_info` as `has_image_understanding`, which the warmup reads back as `is_vlm` and uses to build a `/v1/chat/completions` request carrying an `image_url` part.
#32914 then added `_validate_media_content`, which rejects media input based on `is_multimodal`. The server now answers its own warmup request with a 400, the warmup assertion fires, `kill_process_tree` takes the process down, and `popen_launch_server` reports exit `-9`.
Before #32914 the same bogus image request was sent, but the non-multimodal path silently dropped the media parts and returned 200, so the wrong flag went unnoticed. `/model_info` has also been advertising a capability grok-2 does not have.
## Modifications
Derive `is_image_understandable_model` from `is_multimodal` instead of re-deriving it from `enable_multimodal` plus the `vision_config` attribute:
```diff
+        # Gated on `is_multimodal` because this flag is advertised via /model_info
+        # and drives the VLM warmup request, while the OpenAI serving layer rejects
+        # media input for models that are not `is_multimodal`. A text-only model
+        # with an auto-populated `vision_config` (see above) would otherwise warm up
+        # with an image request that its own serving layer answers with 400.
         # TODO: requires further polishing
-        self.is_image_understandable_model = enable_multimodal and hasattr(
+        self.is_image_understandable_model = self.is_multimodal and hasattr(
             self.hf_config, "vision_config"
         )
```
Image understanding is logically a refinement of `is_multimodal` — a model the engine does not run in multimodal mode cannot consume image input. Expressing it as a derivation rather than a parallel heuristic makes the two values unable to diverge by construction, which is why no change is needed in the warmup or in `_validate_media_content`.
Scope and risk:
- Since `is_multimodal = enable_multimodal and (...)`, `is_multimodal` implies `enable_multimodal`. The new condition is therefore strictly stronger than the old one and can only flip `True` → `False`, never the reverse.
- The models that flip are exactly those with a `vision_config` that are neither registered as a multimodal arch nor detected through a sub-config. Those load a text-only model class with no vision tower and no multimodal processor, and `_validate_media_content` rejects images for them, so `has_image_understanding: true` was factually wrong. Real VLMs keep `is_multimodal == True` and a `vision_config`, so their value is unchanged.
- `is_image_understandable_model` has exactly two consumers in the SRT engine: the `/model_info` payload (`http_server.py`) and the warmup gate that reads it back from `/model_info`. The identically named symbols under `multimodal_gen/` belong to the separate image-generation runtime and are untouched.
This continues the decision already made in #23383 (stop trusting an auto-populated `vision_config` for grok-2) by applying it to the flag that PR missed.
Alternatives considered and rejected: relaxing `_validate_media_content` would forward images into a model with no vision encoder, turning a clean 400 into a deeper failure for real users; making the warmup tolerate a 400 would leave `/model_info` advertising a capability the model lacks and would suppress genuine VLM warmup regressions, which is what the warmup exists to catch.

title: [Fix] moe: Fix flashinfer TRT-LLM BF16 expert weight reload on refit
author: Kh4L
body:
## Motivation

BF16 MoE expert weights are converted to the FlashInfer TRT-LLM BlockMajorK
layout on cold load. The inverse restore previously ran only for the routed
backend, although both `flashinfer_trtllm` and `flashinfer_trtllm_routed` use
the transform. A subsequent checkpoint-format copy into a blocked parameter
can therefore fail with:

```
The size of tensor a (64) must match the size of tensor b (2048) at
non-singleton dimension 2
```

A shape-only restore is insufficient: unchanged expert values must also be
returned to checkpoint order before the next pack, or repeated refits can
silently scramble them.

Fixes #27787

## Modifications

1. Gate the inverse on `use_flashinfer_trtllm_moe`, matching the transform for
   both routed and non-routed BF16 backends.
2. Restore both the canonical shape and values in place, preserving parameter
   storage and rejecting non-bijective row permutations or wrong element counts.
3. Implement `restore_weights_before_loading` so `begin_weight_update` restores
   both expert parameters for direct tensor and P2P/RDMA writes that bypass
   model weight loaders. Retain loader-side restoration for disk reloads,
   which do not open a weight-update session.
4. Shape-guard the post-load pack: canonical weights are converted to kernel
   layout, while already-blocked weights remain unchanged. The existing
   `end_weight_update` finalizes once per session, not once per bucket, using
   the existing LoRA-aware model-loader traversal. No new updater/base hook or
   per-bucket `finally` callback is introduced.

Files changed relative to main:
`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/unquant.py` and
`test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_flashinfer_trtllm_bf16_moe_reload.py`.

## Accuracy Tests

The CPU-registered unit file contains 10 test methods. It covers exact layout
round trips, bucketed tensor/flattened/distributed updates, mixed
canonical/blocked parameters, unchanged and inactive-backend behavior, invalid
permutations and element counts, LoRA-wrapped traversal, and three successive
loader-free refits through both direct tensor updates and simulated P2P flat
copies. Runtime topology is scoped with `get_parallel().override(tp_rank=0)`.
Loader-free tests assert exact cold-load byte equality and unchanged storage
pointers, while forbidding any call to the model weight loader.

October 5 validation of commit `493fab0f593649c3c22a19302bab1b597a70aada`,
including main `70f0b7351e74b372cc928db533824d3993d65922`: all 10 methods and
5 format subtests pass, plus 22 nearby session/cache-guard methods. Controls
reproduce the three pre-fix TP-rank failures and fail the new loader-free case
in both formats when only the production restore hook is removed. Native XML,
exact source hashes and terminal accounting were independently checked;
all applicable pinned pre-commit hooks pass.
FlashInfer's layout entry points are deterministic, order-changing CPU
stand-ins; this is not on-device kernel accuracy, real RDMA transport, or
end-to-end RL validation.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speed benchmark is claimed. Forward kernels are unchanged. Canonical restore
and pack are paid once per weight-update session; disk reloads retain their
existing load/postprocess lifecycle. This fixes representation correctness,
not rollback of partially written weight values.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with the pinned pre-commit configuration.
- [x] Add CPU-registered regression coverage with failure controls.
- [ ] Update external documentation if needed.
- [ ] Provide on-device accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow SGLang code style guidance.

## Review and Merge Process

Required review and green CI remain necessary. Full upstream GPU CI needs a
maintainer to restore the `run-ci` gate; no fresh GPU CI success is claimed.

title: Fix the router GEMM inaccuracy when using _front_w in Kimi-K3
author: b8zhong
body:
## Problem

The Kimi-K3 MoE layer computes the router logits in bf16. The router then
selects the experts from these bf16 logits. The selection is not accurate.

Other implementations use fp32 for this GEMM:

- vLLM sets `out_dtype=torch.float32` on its gate
- the SGLang EP front (`moe_front.fused_front`) uses `out_dtype=torch.float32`

Measurement with the layer-1 gate weight and the fp32 correction bias:

- 5.27% of the tokens get a different top-16 expert set
- 0.33% of the routed weight goes to different experts (mean); the p99 is 6.4%

Previously, as https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29783 shows in GLM-5.2, this is not safe, and can drop the SWE-Bench Verified score by 79 -> 67. In fact since this path is gated by num_tokens, it will be really difficult to diagnose bugs in the future (when running evals quickly with large batch sizes, vs real world use at small batch sizes)

## The `_front_w` fusion

Three projections in the MoE layer read the same `hidden_states`:

| projection | weight shape at TP8 |
|---|---|
| `shared_experts.gate_up_proj` | `[1536, 7168]` |
| `gate` (the router) | `[896, 7168]` |
| `routed_expert_down_proj` | `[3584, 7168]` |

`_merge_front_weights()` concatenates the three weights along the row axis into
one tensor, `_front_w [6016, 7168]`. One GEMM then replaces three GEMMs. Each
module keeps a view of the merged tensor, so the memory does not increase.

```
hidden_states [M, 7168] --> _front_w [6016, 7168] --> fused [M, 6016]
                                                        |
      cols    0:1536  gate_up  --> SiTU --> shared down_proj
      cols 1536:2432  logits   --> router (sigmoid + bias + top-16)
      cols 2432:6016  latent   --> mxfp8 quant --> trtllm-gen MoE
```

The fusion saves 11-16 us for each MoE layer. The fusion also causes the problem. `fused` is one tensor, and one tensor has one dtype. Two of the three consumers need bf16 (SiTU, MXFP8 quant). Thus the router got bf16, which works functionally but not numerically correct.

## The fix

The GEMM writes fp32. The two other consumers read fp32 directly. No cast pass
and no new kernel are necessary.

- **`cutedsl_bf16_gemm`** can now write an fp32 destination. The output dtype
  can be bf16 or fp32. The accumulator was already fp32, and the store is a
  plain `st.global`. Only the epilogue cast goes away. The operands stay bf16.
  This keeps the TGV kernel at m <= 8, where it is 3 us faster than cuBLAS.
- **`situ_and_mul`** takes different input and output types. It converted to
  fp32 internally before this change, so a wider input only changes the load
  width.
- **`QuantTrait`** gets an fp32 input path. `kVecSize` is now 16 elements and no longer depends on
  the input width, because `route_quant_fused` derives its CTA geometry from
  `kNumLanes`.
- **`route_quant_fused`** is templated on the activation dtype.

The other MoE runners (marlin, triton) take `routed_input` in bf16. These
runners already made a dense copy of that strided slice. The copy now also does
the cast. Only a one-token batch adds a launch, because its slice was already
dense. Thus every CUDA runner gets the fp32 router, on SM90 and on Blackwell.

`routed_input` stays bit-identical to the previous output, because
`bf16(tgv_fp32) == tgv_bf16`. The GEMM output for `gate_up` is also
bit-identical, but SiTU now reads the fp32 values. Thus the shared-expert
activation changes. It becomes more accurate: the maximum relative error
against an fp32 reference decreases from 3.9e-03 to 2.5e-03.

## Results

Time for each MoE layer at TP8 decode shapes. This is the complete front: the
GEMM, SiTU, and the route/quant. CUPTI, with CUDA graph capture.

| tokens | 1 | 8 | 32 | 64 | 128 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 (before) | 25.28 | 25.41 | 28.42 | 27.27 | 34.82 |
| fp32 (after) | 24.35 | 24.74 | 27.46 | 26.40 | 33.57 |
| delta | -0.93 | -0.67 | -0.96 | -0.87 | -1.28 |

The accurate path is faster than the path it replaces. The gain comes from
SiTU: an fp32 input halves the vector for each lane, which doubles the number
of threads on a latency-bound kernel.

The other runners pay for the cast of `routed_input`. Time for the front GEMM
and that cast, at the same shapes:

| tokens | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 | 128 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 + copy | 20.45 | 23.58 | 23.58 | 24.06 | 25.47 | 25.95 | 24.74 | 25.66 |
| fp32 + cast | 21.95 | 23.17 | 23.58 | 23.42 | 25.60 | 26.11 | 24.86 | 26.34 |

Only one token shows a cost, because the cast is a new launch there.

## Notes

- ROCm keeps the bf16 front. `torch.mm` with `out_dtype` and the aiter routing
  path are not verified for the fp32 chain.
- `test_per_token_group_quant_8bit_v2.py::test_v2_jit_matches_aot` fails 66
  cases on main. This failure is not related to this PR. I confirmed it with
  the changes removed.

title: Fix Mistral-Large-3 EAGLE draft skipping DeepseekV2Model.__init__
author: b8zhong
body:
## Motivation

The nightly `nightly-test-general-8-gpu-b200` job fails on `test/registered/8-gpu-models/test_mistral_large3.py`, in the **`Mistral-Large-3-675B-Instruct-2512 [TP8+MTP]`** variant. Plain TP8 and NVFP4 pass accuracy and perf.

> **Two independent problems, one stacked on the other.** Commit 1 fixes a real crash (`AttributeError`). Commit 2 suppresses a warmup-only NaN probe that the crash was hiding, matching what the Nemotron-3 nightlies already do. See [Two bugs, not one](#two-bugs-not-one) — the second is a **suppression, not a fix**.

The reported error is misleading:

```
✗ Performance test exception ...: Server process exited with code -9. Check server logs for errors.
```

`-9` is not an OOM kill — it is `kill_process_tree(SIGKILL)` firing after the scheduler sent SIGQUIT. The actual crash, during EAGLE draft CUDA graph capture:

```
File ".../srt/speculative/eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py", line 478, in capture_one_shape
  maybe_flashinfer_autotune_speculative_draft(...)
File ".../srt/models/mistral_large_3_eagle.py", line 92, in forward
  output = super().forward(...)
File ".../srt/models/deepseek_v2.py", line 2725, in forward
  dsa_forward_uses_topk = self._dsa_forward_uses_topk()
File ".../srt/models/deepseek_v2.py", line 2710, in _dsa_forward_uses_topk
  if not self.use_dsa:
AttributeError: 'MistralLarge3EagleModel' object has no attribute 'use_dsa'
```

### Root cause

`MistralLarge3EagleModel` subclasses `DeepseekV2Model` but **skips its `__init__`** — it calls `nn.Module.__init__(self)` and hand-builds its own `embed_tokens` / `layers` / `norm` / `fc`, re-deriving a subset of the parent's state. It still **inherits `DeepseekV2Model.forward`**, so every attribute `forward` reads off `self` has to exist on the draft too.

#28785 (`643ee748c6`, 2026-06-21) added `self._dsa_forward_uses_topk()` as the first statement of `DeepseekV2Model.forward`, and that reads `self.use_dsa` — which the draft never set. Before that commit `self.use_dsa` was only read in the non-first-rank PP branch, which never runs in this TP8 config, so the gap was latent. `next_full_attention_layer_id`, `first_k_dense_replace` and `cp_size` were missing the same way and would have been the next three crashes.

## Change

One file, net −40 lines: the draft model calls `super().__init__()`.

Everything the hand-rolled init built, the parent already builds — `embed_tokens`, the `DeepseekV2DecoderLayer` stack, `start_layer` / `end_layer`, `norm`. All the draft has to add is `fc`. Subclass state can no longer drift from the parent's, because there is only one init.

Calling the parent init is not a leap: `DeepseekV2ForCausalLM.__init__` **already** builds a full `DeepseekV2Model` from this same draft config today (`deepseek_v2.py:2928` — the "discarded" one `MistralLarge3ForCausalLMEagle` then replaces), so the config is known to satisfy it, and the module count is unchanged.

Three things the hand-rolled version got wrong come out in the wash:

- **`embed_tokens` now routes through `get_embedding_tp_kwargs()`.** That helper's docstring makes this mandatory for EAGLE drafts: *"the target and every draft that shares it MUST use the same vocab-parallel layout — otherwise the draft's masking/index math runs against a tensor with a different layout and accept_len silently drops."* `DeepseekModelNextN` already routes through it; this draft was the only one that did not. **Same values under the nightly config** (`enable_tp=True, use_attn_tp_group=False` either way), divergent under DP attention or `SGLANG_ENABLE_EMBED_REPLICATION`.
- **`add_prefix(name, prefix)` was called with its arguments swapped** — `add_prefix(prefix, f"layers.{i}")` and `add_prefix(prefix, "fc")` named the weights `layers.0.model` / `fc.model` instead of `model.layers.0` / `model.fc`. That prefix is what quant config resolution keys off, and the `remapping` table in this same file targets `model.fc.*`.
- **Decoder layers now get `alt_stream`** and the offloader hooks `make_layers` wires up.

⚠️ Reviewers: the prefix correction changes which quant method resolves for the draft's layers and `fc`. That is the intended direction (the old names were malformed), but it is a behavior change on the quantized draft path and worth a second opinion.

## Two bugs, not one

Running the nightly test on this branch (B200, run [31064571801](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31064571801)) confirms the `AttributeError` is gone — the draft `forward` now executes. It then fails **further down**, in the same draft-capture path:

```
Assertion `NaN detected! draft_forward step 0` failed.     (all 8 ranks)
→ Rank 0 scheduler died during initialization (exit code: -6)
```

**That NaN is older than the `AttributeError` and unrelated to this PR.** Nightly history for the same test/partition:

| nightly | head | `[TP8+MTP]` | failure |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-06-06 | `b3e4c204fd` | ✅ PASS | — |
| **2026-06-07** | `5160f7914e` | ❌ FAIL | `NaN detected! draft_forward step 0` |
| 2026-06-13 | | ❌ FAIL | `NaN detected! draft_forward step 0` |
| 2026-06-20 | | ❌ FAIL | `NaN detected! draft_forward step 0` |
| 2026-06-21 | | ❌ FAIL | `NaN detected! draft_forward step 0` |
| *#28785 lands 2026-06-21 23:55* | | | |
| 2026-07-29 … 2026-08-05 | | ❌ FAIL | `AttributeError: ... 'use_dsa'` (masks the NaN) |
| this PR | `eda61de5eb` | ❌ FAIL | `NaN detected! draft_forward step 0` (mask removed) |

So the sequence is: the NaN starts being *reported* on **2026-06-07**; two weeks later #28785 added an earlier crash that **masked** it; this PR removes the mask and the failure reverts to its original, older form — byte-identical to the 2026-06-20/21 signature, with zero `use_dsa` errors in those older logs. Note the 06-07 date is when the *probe* was enabled, not when the NaN began — see below.

### The 06-07 date is the probe turning on, not a NaN appearing

The window `b3e4c204fd..5160f7914e` contains **#27461 — "Enable async-assert invariant probes by default in CI"** (`032c9efb46`, 2026-06-06 16:23 PDT), which added:

```yaml
SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT: true
```

to `nightly-test-nvidia.yml` (and `rerun-test.yml`, which is why the rerun above hits it too). `maybe_detect_nan` is a **no-op** without that flag:

```python
def maybe_detect_nan(tensor, msg=""):
    if not envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT.get():
        return
```

That commit is **not** an ancestor of the 06-06 nightly head and **is** an ancestor of the 06-07 head. So 06-06 was the last nightly that ran with the probe off.

And on 06-06, with the probe off, the MTP variant was not merely "passing" — it was **healthy**:

```
Model 2: mistralai/Mistral-Large-3-675B-Instruct-2512
  Performance: PASS, output: 1445.7 tok/s, accept_len: 2.45
  Accuracy: PASS
  Score: 0.960
```

`accept_len 2.45` out of 4 draft tokens means the draft was working well in real decoding. The NaN fires only in the **CUDA-graph-capture / flashinfer-autotune warmup** path (`maybe_flashinfer_autotune_speculative_draft` → `run_once` → `draft_forward`), not in steady-state decode.

Corroborating that this is not Mistral-specific: on the first probe-on nightly (06-07), a **second, unrelated** b200 partition also began reporting NaN at a different probe site — `NaN detected! verify` — across `deepseek_v3_fp4_*` / `nemotron_3_super_nvfp4` / `qwen3_next_fp4`. Two models, two probe sites, both appearing exactly when the flag flipped.

I checked and **ruled out** the obvious explanation: the capture-time static buffers are `torch.zeros`, and the MLA KV pool is `torch.zeros` too — so this is not uninitialized-memory garbage. The actual source of the NaN values is still unknown.

So the open question is not "which commit introduced a NaN" but **"is a NaN during warmup on a degenerate all-zeros batch actually a defect, or is the probe asserting somewhere it should not?"** That is a question for the probe's author (#27461) and the spec-decode owners.

### What this PR does about it

Suppresses the probe for this test, exactly as `test_nvidia_nemotron_3_super_nightly.py`, `test_nvidia_nemotron_3_ultra_nightly.py` and `test_nvidia_nemotron_3_super_nvfp4.py` already do:

```python
with envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT.override(0):
    run_combined_tests(...)
```

Those Nemotron opt-outs are why the *other* partition that lit up on 06-07 (`NaN detected! verify`) is quiet again today — the same latent condition was papered over there first.

**This is a suppression, not a fix.** It restores the nightly to the behaviour it had on 06-06, where this variant was measurably healthy (`accept_len 2.45`, gsm8k `0.960`). If the warmup NaN turns out to be a genuine defect, it should be fixed at the probe or in the draft warmup path, and this override removed.

## Test

Repro script that builds `MistralLarge3EagleModel` on one GPU from a synthetic DeepSeek-V3-shaped config (1 real `DeepseekV2DecoderLayer`) and reads the state `forward` needs.

**Against unpatched `main`** — reproduces the CI failure exactly:

```
AttributeError: 'MistralLarge3EagleModel' object has no attribute 'use_dsa'
```

**With this PR:**

```
--- state DeepseekV2Model.forward reads ---
  use_dsa = False
  next_full_attention_layer_id = {}
  first_k_dense_replace = 0
  cp_size = None
  layers_to_capture = []
  llama_4_scaling_config = None
  padding_id = 0
  start_layer = 0
  end_layer = 1
_dsa_forward_uses_topk() -> False
--- embedding layout (must match target) ---
  enable_tp        = True
  use_attn_tp_group= False
--- weight prefixes ---
  layer0 module names: ['self_attn.q_proj.weight']
  fc in state_dict   : ['fc.weight']
BUILD OK
```

On hardware, `/rerun-test test/registered/8-gpu-models/test_mistral_large3.py`:

- B200 [31064571801](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31064571801) — `AttributeError` gone, now fails on the pre-existing NaN (above).
- H200 [31064565297](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31064565297) — green, but **skipped**: `Ran 1 test in 0.000s / OK (skipped=1)` via `@skipIf(not is_blackwell_system())`. Not evidence of anything.

title: fix(gdn): skip the -1 padding sentinel in the chunked extend kernel
author: Oasis-Git
body:
`_forward_metadata` poisons padded request rows with state index -1 (`mamba_cache_indices[_real_bs:] = -1`). The decode kernel honors that sentinel (`fused_recurrent.py` guards with `if idx >= 0`), but the chunked gated-delta-net extend kernel fed it straight into pointer arithmetic for both the initial-state load and the in-place final-state store, addressing before the state pool. `boundary_check` does not catch it: that validates against the declared block shape, not the allocation.

Breakable prefill CUDA graph + DP attention is the exposer, since padded / fabricated rows are what carry the sentinel.

Measured on 4xGB300 (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, tp4/dp4, --enable-dp-attention, gsm8k 200q @ parallel 32), holding everything else constant:

  prefill CG | spec  | guard   | result
  -----------+-------+---------+---------------------------------------
  breakable  | EAGLE | absent  | NCCL AllGather deadlock (x3, incl. a
             |       |         | negative control after the fix)
  breakable  | none  | absent  | SIGSEGV in CUDAGraph::replay at warmup
  disabled   | EAGLE | absent  | passes, 0.955
  breakable  | none  | present | passes, 0.965
  breakable  | EAGLE | present | passes, 0.965, 1780 tok/s

title: fix: make Cache-DiT actually cache on MiniMax-H3
author: Elaine4CY
body:
## Motivation

Cache-DiT (DBCache) has been wired up for MiniMax-H3 for a while (`_CUSTOM_BLOCK_ADAPTER_SPECS` already maps `MiniMaxH3DiTModel`), but it never actually cached anything: enabling `SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED=1` gave a 1.00x speedup and byte-identical output, with no error and no warning.

## Root cause

`CachedBlocks_Pattern_3_4_5` retains the block-stack input **by reference** at two points, to measure the residuals that drive the hit/miss decision — once in `forward` for the Fn residual, and again in `call_Mn_blocks` for the Bn residual:

```python
original_hidden_states = hidden_states
hidden_states = self.call_Fn_blocks(hidden_states)
Fn_hidden_states_residual = hidden_states - original_hidden_states
```

`MiniMaxH3DiTBlock.forward` applies its first gated residual with an in-place Triton kernel, which rewrites that same buffer. The snapshot aliases the mutated output, the residual is identically zero, and the similarity test degenerates to `0/0 = NaN`; `NaN < threshold` is always False, so the cache never hits — silently.

Measured on upstream without the fix: **45 of 49 cache decisions produced a NaN residual diff, 0 hits**, output bit-identical to running with caching disabled.

## Fix

A block must not overwrite the input Cache-DiT is holding. `MiniMaxH3DiTModel.set_cache_dit_input_preservation(enabled)` flips every block at once, and only the **first** gated residual of a block honours it — the second operates on a buffer the block just allocated, so it keeps the in-place fused kernel either way.

`indexed_modulation.py` gains an out-of-place variant `indexed_gate_bf16` that shares the same `_indexed_gate_bf16_kernel` as the in-place `indexed_gate_bf16_`, with an added output-row stride, and still applies the shared `numerics.round_bf16_to_fp32`. Both variants execute the same kernel arithmetic; the preserved path costs one allocation rather than falling back to eager.

`MiniMaxH3DenoisingStage` owns the lifecycle, so `cache_dit_integration.py` stays model-agnostic. Preservation is armed before delegating to the parent — `cache_dit.enable_cache` swaps `blocks` for a single `CachedBlocks` wrapper, after which the real blocks are unreachable — and disarmed when the parent turns out not to have mounted. If the mount raises, the stage unmounts first and disarms only once that succeeds; if the unmount itself fails it stays armed and logs, because disarming with the cache still attached is the silent case. Normal disable follows the same order.

The stage arms whenever an H3 mode requests caching and caching is not already enabled, without predicting whether the parent will accept the mount. Predicting means mirroring the parent's gates, and a mirror can fail open if the parent relaxes one: it would then mount unpreserved blocks and reproduce the original silent failure. Arming and disarming only loops over the blocks setting a boolean, with no model execution in between, so a call that turns out not to mount never takes the out-of-place path; what preservation costs while caching is actually running is measured below. For the same reason the setter fails closed: if the H3 model cannot be reached it raises rather than skipping, because skipping is indistinguishable from the bug.

## Verification

B200, T2VA 768p, 8.7s, 50 steps, seed 1101, default cache params (`Fn=1, Bn=0, warmup=4, RDT=0.24, MC=3`).

| check | result |
|---|---|
| reproduces the bug, upstream without the fix | 45/49 NaN diffs, 0 hits; output md5-identical to caching disabled |
| with the fix | 34/49 hits, 0 NaN |
| this rework does not change the output | the uncached hash is unchanged across it, and the cached hash is unchanged across it |

Merging main moved the baselines, so the md5 values quoted earlier in this PR no longer apply to the current head:

| head | cache off | cache on |
|---|---|---|
| `462f9bc` — before the merge | `c9242e50…` | `f5326803…` |
| `a0cf4c2ab` — after the merge, before this rework | `7fdffc7c…` | `48423260…` |
| current head — after this rework | `7fdffc7c…` | `48423260…` |

`a0cf4c2ab` is the merge commit itself, so the shift between the first two rows came in with the merge rather than from this branch — we checked that the merge carries no manual resolution. The rework then leaves both arms unchanged, and the cached value reproduced across two separate jobs on different nodes.

Scope: this is one fixed case. It shows the implementations agree bit-for-bit there; it does not establish equivalence across other prompts, Fn/Bn settings, tasks, or parallel configurations.

### Latency and peak memory: all-block versus Fn/Mn-only

A = the previous Fn/Mn-only implementation, B = this rework, both from frozen
worktrees where B's parent commit is A, so the only delta is this change.
Interleaved A1 → B1 → A2 → B2 in one job on one B200, same input, same cache
params.

| arm | generate | denoising stage | torch peak allocated | torch peak reserved | hits | NaN |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | 118.1s | 102.68s | 131279 MiB | 137346 MiB | 34/49 | 0 |
| B1 | 115.3s | 101.82s | 131715 MiB | 137346 MiB | 34/49 | 0 |
| A2 | 114.7s | 101.59s | 131279 MiB | 137346 MiB | 34/49 | 0 |
| B2 | 114.9s | 101.64s | 131715 MiB | 137346 MiB | 34/49 | 0 |

All four produce md5 `48423260a94f11c759df7281941ab8fc`, so the all-block rework
did not change the output in this case.

**Peak memory: +436 MiB allocated (+0.33%).** The delta reproduced exactly in
both repeats — 131279 MiB in both A runs and 131715 MiB in both B runs. Peak
reserved is identical across arms (137346 MiB), so the extra sits inside the same
allocator pool, and no corresponding increase was observed in the 2-second
`nvidia-smi` samples. We are reporting the number rather than a mechanism: one
extra activation-sized live buffer is a plausible hypothesis, but 436 MiB does
not match the hidden-state tensor size and we have not taken a memory snapshot to
confirm it.

**Latency: no regression distinguishable from run-to-run drift at n=2.** A1 is
the slowest run on both metrics, and both B runs fall between A1 and A2 on both
metrics. With the fixed A → B → A → B ordering, the difference between the arm
means (1.1% on generate) is confounded with run order, and the three runs after
A1 sit within about 0.5% of each other. This cannot establish equivalence or rule out a
smaller effect.

Scope: one prompt, one configuration, two repeats per arm, single node,
A → B → A → B ordering (not fully counterbalanced against time drift).

### Sequence-parallel scaling

Measured on 462f9bc, before the merge, each degree against its own uncached baseline. Merging main shifted both arms of the acceptance case, so these numbers describe the pre-merge tree; they are kept because the code path they exercise — Cache-DiT deciding on all-reduced means — is unchanged by the merge and by this rework.

| config | end-to-end | speedup | denoising stage | stage speedup | SSIM (Y) | PSNR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 GPU | 332.2s → 116.9s | 2.84x | 307.4s → 103.8s | 2.96x | 0.804 | 25.35 dB |
| SP=2 | 222.1s → 93.2s | 2.38x | 203.6s → 82.0s | 2.48x | 0.823 | 25.66 dB |
| SP=4 | 107.5s → 44.1s | 2.44x | 90.6s → 33.5s | 2.70x | 0.832 | 25.98 dB |
| SP=8 | 72.3s → 37.5s | 1.93x | 56.5s → 26.2s | 2.15x | 0.795 | 25.00 dB |

SP is covered deliberately: with `sp_group` set, Cache-DiT installs `_patch_cache_dit_similarity` and decides on all-reduced means — a different code path. The bug reproduces there without the fix (45 NaN, output md5-identical to uncached) and the fix holds.

The `ipc_a2a_sync` JIT extension does not build in our environment (CCCL header/compiler version check), so SGLang takes its fallback path for SP>=2. The latencies and ratios above therefore characterise that fallback environment and do not necessarily transfer to the optimized path.

Method: ffmpeg decodes the H.264 MP4s and computes whole-clip SSIM/PSNR on the decoded frames, cached versus uncached, each configuration against its own baseline — outputs are not bit-comparable across parallel configurations, since TP/SP change reduction order. We report Y-plane SSIM and average PSNR. Because the frames went through an H.264 round trip rather than being scored with `cache-dit-metrics` directly, the absolute values are not directly comparable to Cache-DiT's documented thresholds. One sample per configuration; we do not infer a quality trend across SP degrees.

title: [diffusion] fix: crop GLM-Image output to requested size
author: AuFlow
body:
## Summary

GLM-Image requires its generation resolution to be divisible by 32. After the requested resolution is rounded up to the D32 generation grid, the decoded output currently keeps the aligned dimensions instead of the dimensions requested by the user.

This PR:

- preserves the original requested width and height before D32 alignment;
- generates and performs VAE decoding on the aligned canvas;
- center-crops the final decoded output back to the requested dimensions;
- applies the same crop to `trajectory_decoded`;
- preserves the requested dimensions when offline/CLI requests are cloned per prompt;
- reports the actual final output dimensions through the OpenAI-compatible image response.

For example:

```text
Requested: 1280x720
Generated: 1280x736
Final output after decoding: 1280x720
```
Both text-to-image and image-editing requests use the same output restoration path.

## Follow-up

This PR follows #32999, which has already been merged. The branch has been rebased onto the latest `main` and now contains only the output-cropping changes.

Scope

This change only restores aligned outputs to the user-requested dimensions.

title: [diffusion] fix: MiniMax-H3 text encoder device mismatch under --text-encoder-cpu-offload
author: triple-mu
body:
## Motivation

`--text-encoder-cpu-offload` is unusable on MiniMax-H3: every request fails during text encoding with

```
RuntimeError: Expected all tensors to be on the same device, but got mat2 is on cpu,
different from other tensors on cuda:0 (when checking argument in method wrapper_CUDA_bmm)
  transformers/models/qwen3_vl/modeling_qwen3_vl.py:367  (Qwen3VLRotaryEmbedding.forward)
```

Reproduced 3/3 on 1x RTX PRO 5000, and it blocks the flag for both the model-wise-only
combination and any combination that mixes it with DiT layerwise offload.

Root cause: `MiniMaxH3Qwen3VLEncoder.device` returned `next(self.parameters()).device`.
`--text-encoder-cpu-offload` routes this component through `maybe_load_fsdp_model` with an
FSDP CPU offload policy, which keeps the sharded parameters on CPU and all-gathers them to
the accelerator for the forward. The parameter device then names the *storage* side, not
the *compute* side.

`encode_ids` places `input_ids`, `attention_mask` and `position_ids` with `.to(self.device)`,
so those inputs stayed on CPU while the forward ran on the accelerator. Instrumented run:

```
self.device=cpu  cpu_params=902/902  cpu_buffers=0/3
inputs={'input_ids': cpu, 'attention_mask': cpu}
hidden=cuda:0  pos_ids=cpu  inv_freq=cuda:0
```

The rope forward hard-pins one operand to the activation device
(`inv_freq_expanded = ... .to(x.device)`) but leaves `position_ids_expanded` on the device
`position_ids` arrived on, so the mismatch surfaces as a failing `bmm`.

## Modifications

- `MiniMaxH3Qwen3VLEncoder.device` now reports `get_local_torch_device()` — the device the
  forward actually runs on — instead of the parameter storage device. The property is used
  in exactly four places, all of them placing inputs for the forward.
- Added `test_minimax_h3_encoder_device.py` pinning the invariant: with a parameter on CPU,
  `device` must still report the local compute device.

When the encoder is GPU-resident both expressions already evaluate to the same device, so
only the offloaded path changes behaviour.

## Accuracy Tests

MiniMax-H3 t2va, 1344x768, 124 frames @ 24fps, 5 denoise steps, BF16, `quality=lossless`,
1x RTX PRO 5000 (72 GB), whole-node exclusive.

| Config | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `--layerwise-offload-components dit --dit-layerwise-resident-layers 20 --text-encoder-cpu-offload` | device mismatch | **ok**, peak 43.4 GB, e2e 85.2 s |
| `--dit-cpu-offload --text-encoder-cpu-offload --vae-cpu-offload` | device mismatch | OOM |

The second row now reaches the memory check instead of crashing in text encoding; a
model-wise DiT needs the full 62 GB resident, so OOM is the correct outcome for that
combination on a single 72 GB card (it matches the independently measured
`--dit-cpu-offload` + text-encoder-layerwise result).

Outputs verified with `ffprobe`: 1344x768, 124 frames, 24 fps, audio track present.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Regression check on a path that does not use `--text-encoder-cpu-offload`
(`--layerwise-offload-components dit text_encoder --dit-layerwise-resident-layers 0
--dit-offload-prefetch-size 1 --vae-cpu-offload`):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `peak_reserved` | 23138.0 MB | **23138.0 MB** |
| e2e | 84.4 s | 85.4 s |

Peak memory is byte-identical. The 1.2% e2e difference is run-to-run noise; the "after" run
shared the node with another tenant.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: Fix DSpark + DeepSeek V4 prefill CP compatibility
author: whybeyoung
body:
## Summary
Two related fixes so DSpark speculative decoding works together with DeepSeek V4 prefill context parallelism (`--enable-nsa-prefill-context-parallel --nsa-prefill-cp-mode round-robin-split`) at PD co-located deployment.

## Changes
1. **`deepseek_v4_dspark.py`: use lm_head's shard group for markov_w2 TP-shard**
   `configure_tp_shard` hard-coded `attn_tp_group` for the per-step all-gather. Under prefill CP (`attn_cp_size == tp_size`) `attn_tp_group` degenerates to `world_size == 1` while `lm_head` still shards over the full TP group, so the geometry check failed and the gather (if forced through) would be a no-op leaving half the vocab missing. Now we pick the group that matches `lm_head`'s own choice: `attn_tp_group` when `use_attn_tp_group=True`, otherwise the full TP group.

2. **`deepseek_v4.py`: enable DSpark aux capture under prefill CP**
   Drop the `NotImplementedError` blocking DSpark + CP and all-gather + rerange each `dspark_aux_hidden_states` tensor on the last PP rank with the same CP token split used for `hidden_states`, so downstream `logits_processor` indexing sees the global token layout.

## Test
Verified with:
```
--tp 8 --speculative-algorithm DSPARK
--enable-nsa-prefill-context-parallel --nsa-prefill-cp-mode round-robin-split
--page-size 256 ...
```
No more `NotImplementedError`; markov_w2 TP-shard geometry check passes.

title: Fix sgl-deep-ep builder dependencies
author: Fridge003
body:
## What changed

- explicitly enable the AlmaLinux PowerTools repository so `libfabric-devel` resolves in the x86 manylinux builder
- register `/usr/local/lib` with `ldconfig` so the freshly installed `libgdrapi.so.2` is discoverable during the image build
- upgrade the DeepEP release workflow, build-script default, and Docker image to `torch==2.13.0`
- make the Docker smoke assertion read `TORCH_VERSION` instead of duplicating a hard-coded version

## Root cause

The x86 CUDA 12.9 and CUDA 13.0 builder images had PowerTools disabled, so dependency installation failed before compilation. After enabling it, the next guard failed because `/usr/local/lib` was not in the image dynamic-linker search path.

SGLang `main` now requires PyTorch 2.13. Because `deep_ep_cpp` is a PyTorch C++/CUDA extension, the workflow, container, and wheel metadata must use the same exact version to avoid an ABI-incompatible wheel.

## Validation

- prior builder validation produced Python 3.12 CUDA 12.9 and 13.0 wheels on both x86_64 and aarch64; `twine check` passed for the CUDA-tagged and CUDA 13 PyPI artifacts
- release workflow YAML parsing, `bash -n scripts/build_sgl_deepep.sh`, pre-commit hooks, the cross-repository PyTorch-version contract, and `git diff --check` passed after the 2.13 update
- built and installed the CPython 3.12 CUDA 13 x86_64 wheel on a 4× NVIDIA B300 host with PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130
- verified wheel metadata contains `Requires-Dist: torch==2.13.0` and `import deep_ep` succeeds with both `libgdrapi.so` and `/dev/gdrdrv` absent
- DeepEP 4-rank low-latency test passed over IBGDA after NVSHMEM disabled unavailable GDRCopy, reaching about 180–181 GB/s dispatch+combine bandwidth
- latest SGLang `main@b38caebf09` `TestDSV4FlashFP4B200Balanced`: `Ran 9 tests in 795.371s`, `OK`; GSM8K score 0.96, average speculative accept length 1.9402, and batch-1 speed 201.71 token/s

## Release status

The RC workflow has not been dispatched from this PR. The implementation and x86 B300 runtime gate are ready for review first.

title: [diffusion] Fix 4/8-step distilled MiniMax-H3 Turbo LoRA merge
author: niehen6174
body:
## Motivation

MiniMax-H3 at full quality needs 20+ denoising steps. The community [`larryvrh/MiniMax-H3-Turbo-Lora`](https://huggingface.co/larryvrh/MiniMax-H3-Turbo-Lora) distills the model so **4–10 steps** produce usable T2VA on the native FL2VA base — a large latency win for serving.

Turbo keys already match native H3 naming; the blocker was a merge crash on fused 2D `lora_B` weights. This PR fixes that so users can run **`--num-inference-steps 4` or `8`**.

## Root Cause

`MergedColumnParallelLinearWithLoRA` assumed 3D stacked `lora_B` (`B[:, start:end, :]`), but H3 Turbo ships fused **2D** weights (e.g. `qkv_proj` `(21504, 64)`, `fc1` `(28672, 64)`), causing `IndexError` at merge.

**Fix:** keep the 3D path; add 2D per-section TP sharding in `runtime/layers/lora/linear.py`.

Most other LoRAs (Wan, HunyuanVideo) split Q/K/V into separate keys that `lora_pipeline` stacks to 3D — H3 Turbo’s native fused layout never hit the old slicer in CI.

## Experiments (4 vs 8 Steps)

Bench on `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3` FL2VA with [`larryvrh/MiniMax-H3-Turbo-Lora`](https://huggingface.co/larryvrh/MiniMax-H3-Turbo-Lora) (`minimax_h3_turbo_4step_ema_ckpt500.safetensors` preferred), 4 GPUs, 1344×768 / 5 s, `flow_shift=12`, `audio_flow_shift=3`, seed **1101**, `lora_scale=1.0`. Same LoRA and seed; only steps change (4 vs 8).

**Prompt:** *At night, while their owner sleeps in a bedroom, three cats march in loudly playing tiny brass instruments, then abruptly file out.*


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/106de712-4f9c-4930-ac9d-878d1eafc29f


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5c4b43a9-ba75-4589-b049-eec0a4eeb4d6


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/40de65c5-88d0-478f-a601-8d73c821f0a3



| Steps | Effect (qualitative) |
|-------|----------------------|
| **4** | Scene coherent; softer detail, more motion blur |
| **8** | Same composition; sharper subjects and cleaner edges |

Turbo LoRA targets **usable few-step output vs. broken base@4-step**, not 20-step base parity. Prefer **ckpt500 + 4 steps** for speed; use **8 steps** when quality matters more.



## Example
```bash
sglang generate \
  --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 --model-variant fl2va \
  --lora-path larryvrh/MiniMax-H3-Turbo-Lora \
  --lora-weight-name minimax_h3_turbo_4step_ema_ckpt500.safetensors \
  --lora-scale 1.0 \
  --num-inference-steps 4 \
  --flow-shift 12.0 --audio-flow-shift 3.0 \
  --seed 1101
```

## ComfyUI LoRAs (Not Supported)

Community LoRAs like **[H3-GalaxyAce](https://civitai.com/models/2200329/galaxyace-lora?modelVersionId=3201619)** (Civitai) target the **ComfyUI pruned** graph, not SGLang’s native FL2VA:
| | SGLang native | ComfyUI pruned |
|--|---------------|----------------|
| Timestep → adaln | `SiLU(t_emb)`, **2688-d** | `adaln_t_table`, **8-d** |
| GalaxyAce `adaln_proj.lora_A` | `(32, 8)` ✗ | `(32, 8)` ✓ |

Partial loading (~416/516 keys) drops the adaln style path and is not equivalent to ComfyUI.

title: Fix prefill CP graph overflow with larger bucket search
author: Fridge003
body:
## Motivation

The 4-GPU GPT-OSS MXFP4 context-parallel test crashed during prefill BCG replay ([failing job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31098531699/job/92606388948)). A live multi-request zigzag layout can require more CP-local physical rows than the single-request layout captured for the same global token bucket (for example, 520 live rows versus 512 captured rows).

The first version of this fix fell back to eager immediately. That is safe, but unnecessarily gives up BCG when a slightly larger captured graph can hold the live CP layout.

## Modifications

- Compute the maximum aligned CP-local row requirement inside the CP BCG helper from the live zigzag layout.
- Record the CP-local row capacity of every captured global token bucket.
- Starting from the normal lower-bound token bucket, choose the smallest larger capture whose CP-local capacity fits the live layout.
- Preserve the existing 2x token-padding limit; fall back to eager when no admissible capture fits.
- Reuse the same bucket selector in graph admission and `load_batch()`, so replay pads to the graph shape that admission selected.
- Keep graph admission and replay overrides behind CP-v2-active checks. DP bucket consensus is intentionally out of scope.

Example: a 2048-token batch requiring 520 CP-local rows skips the 2048 capture with capacity 512 and reuses the 2304 capture with capacity 576. Every CP rank chooses 2304 because the selector uses the maximum requirement across all CP ranks.

## Accuracy Tests

No model math changes. Relevant CPU regression tests cover:

- selecting 2304 when 2048 lacks CP-local capacity;
- identical selection on all four CP ranks;
- preserving eager fallback when no capture has enough capacity;
- preserving the 2x padding limit;
- confirming `load_batch()` actually pads replay to 2304;
- existing non-CP 2x padding behavior.

Validation performed locally:

- 6 registered CPU tests passed;
- relevant modules passed `py_compile`;
- pre-commit passed on all changed files;
- `git diff --check` passed.

The original four-GPU test requires CUDA hardware and is delegated to GitHub Actions.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No benchmark run. The new search uses CPU list arithmetic during eligibility and scans the existing capture bucket list. Reusing a larger graph may execute additional padded rows, but candidates remain bounded by the existing 2x limit; otherwise execution falls back to eager.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit
- [x] Add registered CPU regression coverage
- [x] Preserve eager fallback and the 2x padding limit
- [x] Keep DP graph-bucket synchronization out of scope
- [ ] GPU CI rerun of the original 4-GPU test

title: Fix Qwen3.5 GDN multi-item scoring
author: daii-0818
body:
## Motivation

Qwen3.5 hybrid models use recurrent GDN layers alongside full-attention layers. Multi-item scoring already gives the full-attention layers an item-branching mask, but the GDN prefill path previously processed the packed suffix as one continuous recurrent sequence. As a result, later items could inherit convolution and SSM state from earlier items.

Fixes #31969.

## Modifications

- Add a read-only final-state mode to the Triton chunk gated-delta-rule path while preserving in-place updates by default.
- Build GDN-specific MIS metadata once per forward for compact query and item segments.
- Run GDN MIS prefill in two phases: compute each request query once, then branch every item from the query-end convolution and SSM states.
- Keep item recurrence read-only against the request SSM pool and use unique cloned convolution slots per item.
- Reject unsupported combinations, including non-Triton GDN prefill, page-major layout, cached prefixes, non-prefill requests, and hybrid linear backends without MIS support.
- Add kernel, causal-convolution, backend, metadata, validation, and Qwen3.5 end-to-end coverage.

## Reproduction

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --enable-mis \
  --attention-backend flashinfer \
  --linear-attn-prefill-backend triton \
  --disable-radix-cache \
  --disable-cuda-graph \
  --chunked-prefill-size -1 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 30000
```

## Accuracy Tests

Tested on one NVIDIA H20 with `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B` in BF16, FlashInfer full attention, and Triton linear-attention prefill.

- Qwen3.5 MIS end-to-end: 3 tests passed, covering empty queries, concurrent requests, varied item counts and lengths, and sibling modification/reordering.
- Focused recurrent, causal-convolution, GDN backend, metadata, and validation suite: 27 tests passed with 46 subtests.
- Full recurrent and causal-convolution test files: 275 tests passed.
- Multi-item scores match per-item MIS scoring with `atol=2e-2, rtol=2e-2`.
- Formatting, import checks, spelling, syntax compilation, CI registration validation, and whitespace checks passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Single H20, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B`, query length 120, item length 180, 10 items per request, 10 warmup requests, followed by three 60-second runs. CUDA graph, radix cache, and chunked prefill were disabled in both modes.

| Mode | Items/s/GPU | P50 latency | P99 latency |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Independent pointwise scoring | 52.80 | 189.06 ms | 195.25 ms |
| Multi-item scoring | 62.75 | 158.74 ms | 167.21 ms |

This is an 18.84% throughput increase, with P50 latency reduced by 16.04% and P99 latency reduced by 14.36%.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the code with the repository formatters and static checks.
- [x] Add unit and end-to-end tests.
- [x] Documentation is not required because this does not change the public API or Score API schema.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process.
2. Get approvals from CODEOWNERS and other reviewers.
3. Trigger the required CI tests.
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls to merge the PR.

title: fix: route scheduler aborts to multi-tokenizer workers
author: jeremyzhang866
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #33858.

When the scheduler rejects a request because `--max-queued-requests` is exceeded, it sends an `AbortReq` back to the tokenizer side. In multi-tokenizer mode, scheduler-internal `Req` objects carry the originating worker's `http_worker_ipc`, but `SenderWrapper` only copied that route from IPC `BaseReq` objects. The resulting `AbortReq` had no destination, so `MultiTokenizerRouter` dropped it and the HTTP request waited indefinitely.

## Modifications

- Let the shared `SenderWrapper` inherit `http_worker_ipc` from scheduler-internal request objects, without changing already-routed outputs.
- Add a CPU regression test using the real scheduler `Req` and verify that the resulting `AbortReq` reaches the expected `MultiTokenizerRouter` worker.

## Reproduction Conditions

The bug requires both multi-tokenizer mode and scheduler queue overflow. The original report used:

```text
--tokenizer-worker-num 2
--max-running-requests 128
--max-queued-requests 96
```

under a much higher offered concurrency. It does not require a particular model or tensor-parallel size.

For a minimal local MLX reproduction, use:

```text
--tokenizer-worker-num 2
--max-running-requests 1
--max-queued-requests 1
12 concurrent requests
```

Once the single waiting slot is exceeded, the scheduler returns queue-full `AbortReq` messages. Before this fix, those messages lose their tokenizer-worker return route and the affected HTTP requests time out.

## Accuracy Tests

This change only affects response routing for control messages and does not modify model computation or sampling.

- Latest targeted CPU routing and scheduler tests: `26 passed`.
- Minimal multi-tokenizer MLX reproduction above:
  - Before: 2 HTTP 200 responses and 10 client timeouts.
  - After: 2 HTTP 200 responses and 10 HTTP 503 responses in about 0.08 seconds, with no timeouts or missing-IPC warnings.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The runtime change is one attribute lookup at the existing shared output boundary.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format code with the full pre-commit environment.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the test guidelines.
- [x] Documentation is not needed for this internal routing fix.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed-test rationale above.
- [x] Follow the existing SGLang code style.

title: fix(vlm): stream-order CUDA IPC feature pool lifecycle and streamline multimodal transport module
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

- Publish CUDA IPC producer readiness on the producer CUDA stream.
- Acknowledge each consumer only after its local copy on the consumer CUDA stream, preventing early pool reuse.
- Replace per-slice POSIX shared memory and the global file lock with generation-tagged GPU control words.
- Move CUDA IPC and its stream-ordered pool implementation under `srt/multimodal/transport`; keep the old utility module as a thin compatibility import.
- Keep the default cached-handle path stream ordered. When handle caching is explicitly disabled, synchronize only the consumer stream before releasing the uncached mapping.
- Stop the recycler before releasing backing memory and remove the obsolete process-global `tp_size` read.

## Compatibility and memory policy

- `SGLANG_MM_FEATURE_CACHE_MB` remains the total CUDA IPC HBM budget across tokenizer workers.
- `SGLANG_USE_IPC_POOL_HANDLE_CACHE` remains supported and defaults on.
- Pool pressure still falls back to CPU for that tensor.
- This PR no longer contains or shares code with the superseded custom FABRIC transport; multi-node transport comes from CUDA VMM in #33899/#33936.

## Why

The old producer could serialize a proxy immediately after enqueueing its pool copy, while the consumer incremented a CPU acknowledgement immediately after enqueueing its local copy. That could expose incomplete bytes or recycle and overwrite a slice before the copy completed. The new ready/wait/ack protocol is ordered on CUDA streams and tags every reused slot with a generation.

## Server benchmark

Real `Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct`, NVIDIA H200 x8, TP8 encoder DP, `--mm-feature-transport cuda_ipc`, 1 GiB bounded pool, OpenAI Chat `bench_serving`. Base `42a62553961a` (#33936) and head `e0c94d36c52a`; the later main-only merges do not change this PR's transport or test files.

The request-rate sweep uses 48 requests/rate, 1-4 seeded random JPEG images/request, random 256-1024 px dimensions, 64 text input tokens, and 8 output tokens. All 288 A/B requests completed successfully.

| Request rate | Base req/s | Head req/s | Base p50 TTFT | Head p50 TTFT |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2 | 1.947 | 1.948 | 73.1 ms | 71.2 ms |
| 8 | 9.238 | 9.249 | 87.3 ms | 85.9 ms |
| unlimited | 36.269 | 34.434 | 816.5 ms | 840.3 ms |

Because the short unlimited run is sensitive to new-shape warmup, a second saturated comparison used 64 requests/run, three paired seeds after both servers had completed three warmup sweeps, and reports the median.

| Metric | Base | Head | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Request throughput | 47.33 req/s | 49.43 req/s | +4.4% |
| Input throughput | 47.70k tok/s | 50.71k tok/s | +6.3% |
| Median TTFT | 803.9 ms | 772.7 ms | -3.9% |
| P99 TTFT | 1286.1 ms | 1237.0 ms | -3.8% |

The result supports a small steady-state gain while the primary reason to merge remains correctness: stream-ordered ready/ack prevents incomplete reads and premature pool reuse.

## Validation

- Pre-commit passes on all changed files.
- Spawned-process CUDA IPC regression does not synchronize the producer and verifies recycling after the GPU acknowledgement.
- Multi-consumer and encoder-owner tests cover generation reuse, full-group acknowledgement, duplicate release rejection, recycler shutdown, and uncached-mapping lifetime.
- CPU tests cover the hard per-node pool budget and transport configuration.
- Real-weight H200 server A/B completed with zero request failures; latest-head NVIDIA CI is running after the main merge.

## Base integration

#33899 and #33936 are merged into `main`; this PR now targets `main` directly and contains only the stream-ordered CUDA IPC lifecycle changes.

title: [diffusion] fix: stop RunAI Model Streamer's rank-discovery collective from firing on independent per-rank loads
author: mickqian
body:
## Problem

Multi-rank diffusion serving with layerwise offload + RunAI Model Streamer (`--layerwise-offload-components ..., use_runai_model_streamer=True`) can hang during weight loading. Observed on MiniMax-H3, 2×5090, TP=2: intermittent — most launches load fine, some hang indefinitely with zero I/O progress partway through a component's weights.

## Root cause

`runai_model_streamer`'s `DistributedStreamer.stream_files()` calls `_distributedStreamerParams.set_params()` **before it even inspects the caller's `is_distributed` argument**:

```python
def stream_files(self, file_stream_requests, credentials, device, is_distributed):
    self.params.set_params(file_stream_requests)      # <-- unconditional
    self.set_is_distributed(is_distributed, device)    # <-- checked only after
    ...
```

`set_params()` in turn unconditionally calls `find_local_ranks()` the first time it runs for a given streamer instance:

```python
def set_params(self, file_stream_requests):
    ...
    if self.num_processes_on_node is None:
        self.num_processes_on_node, self.my_global_rank, self.groups_by_ranks = self.find_local_ranks()
```

And `find_local_ranks()` issues a **real collective** whenever `torch.distributed.is_initialized()` and world_size > 1:

```python
sandbox_global_group = dist.new_group(ranks=list(range(world_size)), timeout=self.broadcast_timeout)
all_hostnames = [None] * world_size
dist.all_gather_object(all_hostnames, socket.gethostname(), group=sandbox_global_group)
dist.destroy_process_group(group=sandbox_global_group)
```

This runs **regardless of `is_distributed`** — even for the library's own internal header-only metadata reads, which explicitly pass `is_distributed=False`. Its only purpose is to populate `RUNAI_STREAMER_PROCESS_GROUP_SIZE`, a bookkeeping env var for the library's own distributed-streaming path.

sglang's diffusion weight loader never opts into that path — every `stream_files()` call in `weight_utils.py` passes `is_distributed=False` (each rank loads its own independent full copy of the checkpoint; there's no sharded/collaborative loading here). So this collective is pure overhead, and worse, a genuine hazard: it's re-issued once per component per rank (a fresh `SafetensorsStreamer()` resets the `num_processes_on_node` cache each time a component is loaded). Since sglang's layerwise offload determines per-rank memory-aware component load order independently on each rank, any divergence between ranks in load order or timing (different available memory, warm vs. cold page cache, ...) can call this ad-hoc `new_group()` out of lockstep across ranks — one rank's Nth `stream_files()` call rendezvousing with another rank's Mth — and hang.

Upstream: https://github.com/run-ai/runai-model-streamer/issues/84 frames the distributed-streamer feature as a bandwidth-sharing optimization, not something every caller must accept collateral collective traffic for.

## Fix

`find_local_ranks()` already has an early-return path for the genuinely-single-process case (`if not dist.is_initialized(): return 1, 0, [[0]]`). Since this loader never wants the distributed-streaming feature, patch `find_local_ranks` (defensively, guarded by `hasattr` so a future upstream rename/removal degrades to a logged no-op rather than a crash) to always take that path, reporting "1 process, no peers" without ever touching `torch.distributed`. No upstream env var gates this specific call, so there's no cleaner opt-out available from the caller side.

## Validation

- New unit tests (`test_weight_utils.py`) confirm the patched `find_local_ranks` never calls `dist.new_group`/`all_gather_object`/`destroy_process_group` even when `torch.distributed.is_initialized()` is mocked True with world_size > 1, is idempotent across repeated application, and degrades safely if the target attribute is absent.
- GPU validation on 2×5090 (MiniMax-H3, TP=2, `--layerwise-offload-components dit,text_encoder,vae`, RunAI streamer): with the fix, both ranks stream all components (including the 61.7 GiB transformer) in lockstep — e.g. rank0/rank1 finished the transformer stream within 0.2s of each other (18.07s vs 18.26s @ 3.4 GiB/s) — full load-through-warmup-through-ready in ~3.5 minutes, ready to serve, with no hang across repeated launches.

title: [unified memory] Support DSPARK speculative decoding + fix two NaN root causes (page hand-out zeroing, CuTe int32 slot-stride wrap)
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

`--enable-unified-memory` currently hard-blocks speculative decoding (`server_args.py`: `assert self.speculative_algorithm is None`). This PR wires chain DSPARK through the unified pool and fixes the two real NaN/corruption root causes found while validating it end to end on Kimi-K3 (TP8, 2x4 GB300) and Kimi-Linear-48B (TP1 x8 B300-class). Other speculative algorithms (EAGLE / tree / DFLASH / NGRAM) remain blocked pending their own virtual-vs-dense loc audits.

## Modifications

Five commits, reviewable independently:

1. **`unified-memory: wire DSPARK chain speculative decoding`**
   - `server_args.py`: relax the unified gate to `speculative_algorithm in (None, "DSPARK")`, chain only (`speculative_eagle_topk in (None, 1)`).
   - `trtllm_mla_backend.py`: extend the capture-stable DENSE write-loc fill from `is_decode_or_idle()` to `is_target_verify()`, and route the `forward_extend` KV write through it (`loc_is_dense=True`) when set — the verify graph must not capture a translate allocation (same class as the decode path that already exists).
   - `mamba_state_scatter_triton.py`: replace the blanket `dst.is_contiguous()` asserts with the kernels' true contract (arbitrary layer/slot strides — already consumed via real int64-promoted strides — with contiguous trailing entry dims), so the unified pool's envelope-strided conv/temporal views pass. CPU layout-contract tests + a CUDA envelope-dst end-to-end test added.
   - `hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py`: `update_mamba_state_after_mtp_verify` translates the ScheduleBatch-side (VIRTUAL) `mamba_track_indices` to physical at a single point (identity on static pools) — using them raw silently mis-addresses within bounds on the unified pool.
   - `kv_cache_configurator.py`: size the DSPARK draft pool by the shared unified allocator's virtual-id space (`size_full`, page-aligned up) instead of `max_total_num_tokens` — the draft pool is direct-indexed by virtual ids which range over the whole virtual space; keep the draft pool on the plain contiguous layout (page-major is a target-pool layout choice).

2. **`debug(unified): SGLANG_DEBUG_POISON_POOL`** — env-gated: fill the pool with bf16-NaN bit patterns at boot instead of zeros. Turns the "does freed GPU heap happen to contain NaN patterns" boot lottery into a deterministic switch; kept as the permanent regression harness for the class of bug below (zero default overhead).

3. **`fix(unified): zero page envelopes on allocator hand-out`** — root cause 1. The trtllm-gen MLA kernel reads whole pages and masks rows beyond `seq_len` arithmetically (NaN-unsafe); the unified pool zeroes its raw buffer only at boot, so page recycling re-exposes historical bytes and NaN in a request's last partial page tail leaks into the attention output. Speculative decoding amplifies exposure (every verify window lands on a fresh page at the sequence tail). Static pools are safe by construction (`torch.zeros` + only finite KV ever written); this gives the shared pool the same guarantee at the alloc boundary. Cost: one contiguous page-envelope memset per handed-out page on the schedule stream — benched at zero (below).

4. **`fix(kda_decode_mtp): promote slot ids to int64 before state-stride multiplies`** — root cause 2, and the reason this presented as a "weird" load-dependent heisenbug. The DSPARK KDA verify kernel (`nv_cutedsl` fast path) compiles with STATIC CuTe layouts: state-pool strides are compile-time constants. On the unified pool the envelope-strided KDA state views carry slot strides of ~14M (fp32 ssm) / ~28M (bf16 conv) elements; each constant individually fits int32, so it folds into 32-bit arithmetic and `slot * stride` silently wraps mod 2^32 once slot ids exceed ~153 (conv) / ~306 (ssm) — reads land inside other slots' bytes (silent state corruption on a CLEAN boot: GSM8K 0.120, fake accept-rate bursts) or fly off the allocation (illegal access). Static contiguous pools never reach the wrap point (slot stride ~197K elements); Kimi-Linear never engages this kernel (head dims fail the 128 contract → triton fallback); cold boots hand out low slot ids — which is exactly why it was unified-only, K3-only, and load-only. Proven with an offline replay sentinel (dump one real in-system call; rebuild states contiguous vs faithful strided replicas with zero/NaN gap fill; sweep slot magnitudes): before — slots ≤75 bit-exact, 100–150 illegal access, ≥155 silent divergence; after — bit-exact everywhere.

5. **`unified+spec: keep lazy compaction ON`** — reverts an over-conservative eager forcing from an earlier draft of commit 1 after verifying the actual ordering: the scheduler registers the in-flight write-set (`set_inflight_forward(forward_done, batch.out_cache_loc)`) AFTER `forward_batch_generation()` returns, and the DSPARK verify executor has by then rebound `ScheduleBatch.out_cache_loc` to the verify-window locs (never restored) — so lazy compaction's write-race classification covers verify writes exactly like decode writes, and the event-gated freed-page reuse orders the hand-out zeroing (commit 3) after the in-flight forward.

## Accuracy

GSM8K 200q (`sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k`), Kimi-K3 TP8 2-node GB300, marlin MoE, trtllm_mla, verify graph captured:

| config | fixes | GSM8K | accept rate/len |
|---|---|---|---|
| unified, no spec (baseline) | pristine base | 0.985 | — |
| unified + DSPARK rand draft, POISONED pool | none | 0.005 / Invalid 0.985 | **1.00 / 8.00 (fake — argmax(NaN)=0 token chains)** |
| unified + DSPARK rand draft, POISONED pool | zeroing only | 0.125 / Invalid 0.745 | 0.00 (still corrupt via int32 wrap) |
| unified + DSPARK rand draft, **clean** pool | zeroing only | 0.120 / Invalid 0.715 | 0.52 (fake) — the int32 wrap needs no poison |
| unified + DSPARK rand draft, POISONED pool | **both** | **0.985 / Invalid 0.005** | 0.00 / 1.00 ✓ (correct full-reject semantics) |
| unified + DSPARK **real draft** ([RadixArk/Kimi-K3-DSpark](https://huggingface.co/RadixArk/Kimi-K3-DSpark)), clean | **both** | **0.990 / Invalid 0.005** | 0.53 / 4.74 (real multi-accept commit path) |
| unified + DSPARK real draft, `--disable-radix-cache`, 500q, lazy-compaction stats on | both | 0.976 / Invalid 0.002 | 0.49 / 4.45 |

Poison acceptance criterion: a poisoned boot must score identically to a clean boot — it does (0.985/0.990 both). Kimi-Linear-48B TP1: unified+DSPARK poisoned 0.910 = clean 0.905 = static twin 0.910.

## Performance (fix cost = zero)

`sglang.benchmark.one_batch_server`, isl 8192 / osl 1024, bs sweep, 2 reps per arm, K3 TP8:

- **Zeroing fix A/B** (unified no-spec, fix vs no-fix, only var = checkout): output tok/s deltas bs 1/8/16/24/32 = **−0.07% / −0.02% / +0.05% / +0.03% / +0.02%**; TTFT within ±0.34%. Rep-to-rep variance exceeds the fix delta at every point.
- **Unified vs static under DSPARK** (rand draft, both arms at tip): deltas −0.83%…+0.07% (bs=1 single-request noise); TTFT +0.31~0.37% = the pool's known pre-existing translate overhead, present without these fixes too.
- **int64 slot promotion micro-bench** (offline replay, 200 calls ×3): 416 vs 411 µs/call, run-to-run spread ±4% ≫ delta — one scalar 64-bit multiply against a memory-bound kernel.

## Limitations / follow-ups

- The branch base is an ancestor of current main (no divergence; merge-tree is conflict-free). Happy to rebase before merge — flagging that the accuracy/perf numbers above are bound to the base as validated.
- Compaction MOVE racing an in-flight verify write was not dynamically exercised (short GSM8K sequences free at the watermark frontier → `moves=0` in the stats run); its correctness rests on the verified write-set ordering (commit 5) plus poison acceptance. A fragmenting long-generation stress is a good follow-up before enabling this in latency-critical production lanes.
- fa3 / flashinfer as the target-verify backend under unified+spec are not exercised (K3 lane = trtllm_mla; flashinfer decode is already role-scope-blocked by the allowlist).
- The kernel-owner-side fix for the arithmetic (NaN-unsafe) masked-tail reads remains an upstream flashinfer/trtllm-gen item; commit 3 makes the pool safe regardless.

```diff
-GATE_ATTR = "_sgl_vae_fast_path_gate"
-    setattr(vae, GATE_ATTR, gate)
+    register_vae_fast_path_gate(vae, gate)
```

but this test still reaches for `vae_opt.GATE_ATTR`, so every PR's `jit-kernel-unit-test` is red.

Toggling now goes through `use_vae_fast_path()`, matching how `stages/decoding.py` drives it. That context manager is a no-op when nothing registered a gate, which would make the fast-path assertion pass vacuously, so the install check the old `assert gate is not None` gave us is kept by asserting the wrappers are in place.

Verified on B200: the test passes, and the gate registers (`FusedGroupNormSiLU` / `FusedUpsample2xConv2d` installed). Note the fast paths are skipped entirely when Triton is unavailable — the same precondition the previous version had.

title: [Fix] Judge the phase-checker device-assert test by its FAIL line, not the exit code
author: hnyls2002
body:
What this test verifies is that the kernel-side check fired, and the `SimplePhaseChecker FAIL`
line in stdout is the evidence -- which it already asserts on. The exit code is not evidence:
CI runs with `SGLANG_CUDA_COREDUMP=1`, so the coredump handler may abort the process, and
otherwise `torch.cuda.synchronize()` raises either `cudaErrorAssert` ("device-side assert
triggered") or a generic `cudaErrorLaunchFailure` ("unspecified launch failure"). The subprocess
only matched the first wording and exited 2 on the other, which the assertion rejected.

That is how `base-b-test-1-gpu-small (3)` failed on two different runners while the same test
passed on one of those runners in a different shard: coredump generation ran in one shard and
not the other, and the FAIL line was present either way.

Drops the exit-code assertion and keeps a check that it is not 1 -- that path means the assert
never fired at all.

title: [srt] Fix sconv state memory corruption on specdec
author: ekzhang
body:
## Motivation

DFlash/DSpark speculative pools corrupt sconv (short-conv) state when the radix cache is enabled for hybrid-SWA models such as Inkling and Inkling-Small.

This is because the mamba tracking was gated on prefill-graph capture, and any requests with a radix cache hit would resolve with all-zero sconv cache tensors.

It would especially affect long-context. We were able to find a 70-problem subset of (SWEBench Verified, SWEBench Pro, and SWEBench Multilingual) where DFlash reduces the pass rate from 55% to 35% due to long-context Inkling rollouts getting stuck and being "forgetful" due to the sconv cache corruption.

After this fix, DSpark / DFlash has parity without speculation on nvfp4.

```
┌─────────────────────────────┬────────┬────────┬───────┐
│ Arm (fixed build, same day) │ Reward │ Tokens │ Turns │
├─────────────────────────────┼────────┼────────┼───────┤
│ DSpark                      │ 0.486  │ 76.3k  │ 110.9 │
├─────────────────────────────┼────────┼────────┼───────┤
│ nospec                      │ 0.471  │ 74.4k  │ 106.9 │
└─────────────────────────────┴────────┴────────┴───────┘
```

## Modifications

1. Drop the `spec_algorithm.is_none()` from mamba index tracking guard
2. Capture-safety in the sconv backend: a capture warmup batch with no tracking metadata substitutes was inert
3. Zero the `mamba_track_*` padding rows in the prefill graph's static input buffers

## Verification

- A/B on one warm DSpark pool: byte-identical 10.5k-token prompts under a fresh vs cache-resumed prefix (cached=8960). Pre-fix: verify logits deviate 0.5–3.0 with greedy top-1 flips from the second step. Post-fix: **bit-identical (0.0000) at every step**, and the donated checkpoints match a non-speculative pool's values exactly.
- 70-problem SWEBench subset, same-day arms on the fixed build: DSpark reward 0.486 vs non-spec 0.471 (parity within noise; pre-fix 0.257 vs 0.457), with matching token/turn counts.
