title: [Fix] Account resident weight memory in KV sizing
author: galletas1712
body:
## Motivation

The IPC weight-cache daemon keeps model weights resident before the engine
starts, so `ModelRunner` samples its pre-load free-memory baseline after those
weights have already reduced free memory. Without correcting that baseline, KV
sizing reserves headroom from only the remaining free memory and can
over-allocate the KV cache.

The correction must be rank-local before the distributed `MIN`: adding
preloaded weight memory after ranks have already reduced their baselines is
incorrect when rank footprints differ. Target KV sizing also happens after
draft loading, so target, multi-runner, and future speculative draft weights
must be aggregated before sizing.

## Modifications

- Add a generic rank-local `BaseModelLoader.preloaded_weights_bytes` contract,
  defaulting to zero, and validate loader-provided values before use.
- Aggregate preloaded bytes across target, multi-runner, and speculative draft
  workers. The current built-in IPC weight cache plus speculative decoding
  combination remains explicitly rejected because draft-model daemon support
  is not implemented yet, but the accounting path is ready for it.
- Immediately before target KV-pool allocation, compute
  `MIN(local pre-load baseline + local preloaded weight bytes)` and update
  `pre_model_load_memory`, so initial sizing and post-capture resizing use the
  same corrected value.
- Measure the daemon's process-local PyTorch allocator growth during model
  loading and return it through the IPC protocol as
  `preloaded_weights_bytes`.

## Accuracy Tests

Ran a real persistent-daemon restart A/B with
`Qwen/Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct` in BF16 at TP=1 on an 80 GB GPU. The standalone
daemon retained 63,004 MiB of GPU memory while two independent engine clients
were started sequentially against the same daemon.

| Result | Without this fix | With this fix |
|---|---:|---:|
| Client pre-load available memory | 17.23 GB | 17.23 GB |
| Reported preloaded weights | Not available | 65,546,485,760 bytes (61.045 GiB) |
| KV cache tokens | 63,434 | 38,430 |
| K + V allocation | 15.48 GB | 9.38 GB |
| Memory before decode graph capture | 0.88 GB | 4.37 GB |
| First client start | CUDA OOM during graph capture | Healthy; inference succeeded |
| Second client start | Same CUDA OOM | Healthy; inference succeeded |

Without the correction, both starts selected the same oversized KV cache and
failed during decode CUDA graph capture while the daemon remained alive. With
the correction, both starts completed graph capture, reached health, and served
a completion against the same persistent daemon.

This validates the final implementation and reproduces the accounting defect
as a deterministic startup failure with a model whose resident weights occupy
more than half of GPU memory.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not benchmarked. The steady-state inference path is unchanged. Startup adds
two process-local allocator reads and one existing-world-group reduction before
KV-pool allocation.

## Validation

- Large-model persistent-daemon restart A/B passed as described above
- Python syntax checks passed for all changed production files
- Ruff error checks passed for all changed production files
- Full Ruff checks passed for the central accounting and IPC modules
- Diff whitespace checks passed

## Checklist

- [x] Format code according to the repository hooks.
- [x] Validate the exact final implementation with a persistent GPU daemon and
      two engine starts.
- [ ] Update documentation — not applicable; no user-facing option or workflow
      changed.

title: [Bugfix] Fix batched KV free aliasing
author: YazhiGao
body:
## Summary

- make deferred KV free queues own their tensor inputs at enqueue time
- preserve batched frees while preventing later request-row writes from changing queued indices
- cover token, paged, SWA, NPU, HiSparse, and unified allocators with the same ownership rule
- restore `RadixCache.cache_unfinished_req` to freeing its original `kv_indices` view

## Root cause

Free groups retained tensor views backed by a mutable request-to-token row. `cache_unfinished_req` can overwrite that row during radix-cache rematching before `free_group_end()` consumes the queued view.

```text
Before

req_to_token row: [old request KV indices]
        |
        +---- view --------------------------+
        |                                    |
        |                              free_group queue
        |                                    |
        +---- cache rematch overwrites ------+
                    row storage
                       |
                       v
              [cached/tree KV indices]
                       |
                       +---- free_group_end()
                                  |
                                  v
                         frees replacement indices
                         instead of old request slots
```

This can make radix-cache eviction accounting diverge from physical allocator state: entries are counted as logically evicted while their SWA mappings remain allocated. Eventually a request can fail allocation even though the cache reports ample evictable capacity.

## Fix

Every deferred allocator queue now snapshots its input immediately:

```text
After

req_to_token row: [old request KV indices]
        |
        +---- view ---- clone() ----> free_group queue
        |                              [owned snapshot]
        |
        +---- cache rematch overwrites row
                       |
                       v
              [cached/tree KV indices]

free_group_end() ----> frees owned old request indices
```

The ownership rule lives at the allocator boundary so callers can safely pass views. Paged `free_segment` copies only page representatives, and the separate SWA queue also owns its input. This keeps batching enabled while removing the aliasing hazard.

## Validation

- unified-cache alias reproduction: logical SWA evicted / physical SWA freed changes from `20 / 5` to `20 / 20`
- `57 passed, 76 subtests passed` in radix, SWA, and paged-free suites
- `71 passed` in multi-ended and HiSparse allocator suites
- all repository-native pre-commit hooks pass for the changed files

title: [Fix] overlap scheduler: record_stream mix_running_indices for the forward-stream relay gather
author: shenxiul
body:
## Motivation

> Revision note: this PR previously also pinned the draft-extend ForwardBatch under the opt-in plan stream (`SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1`); that hunk and its test arms are dropped to keep the PR single-seam — the flag is default-off, and that hazard is latent on the default allocator besides.

A cross-stream tensor-lifetime violation in the overlap scheduler
(torch.Tensor.record_stream contract: a tensor allocated on stream A and
consumed on stream B must stay alive until B finishes, or be
record_stream'd; wait_stream orders execution but does not protect
deallocation). Reachability is allocator-config-dependent, measured on
B200-class hardware with the production stream ordering:

    default native allocator          latent (0/40 corruptions: free-list
                                      eventing happens to order the reuse
                                      write after pending readers)
    expandable_segments:True          corrupts 19/20
    backend:cudaMallocAsync           corrupts 19/20

The seam (non-spec overlap + mixed chunked prefill): `mix_with_running`
aliases the running batch's `req_pool_indices` into `mix_running_indices`.
`last_batch` / the 2-slot record ring usually keep the running batch alive,
but that ages out: intervening non-mixed prefills advance `last_batch` and
overwrite both ring slots; a later mix leaves the staging field as the LAST
owner, and `resolve_forward_inputs` clears it right after enqueueing the
forward-stream gather. Recycled in-range values read the wrong relay rows —
silently wrong decode input_ids, no crash; out-of-range recycled values fire
the device-side IndexKernel assert.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/managers/overlap_utils.py`: `record_stream` the
  mixed-gather indices on the gathering stream, immediately before the relay
  gather (CPU-device guarded — CPU has no cross-stream reuse hazard, and
  `record_stream` rejects CPU tensors). One line plus a comment; no stream or
  value changes.
- `test/registered/unit/managers/test_spec_v2_overlap_lifetime.py`: new
  3-arm suite for this seam (see Test below).

## Test

Tests (`test_spec_v2_overlap_lifetime.py`, CPU CI `base-a-test-cpu`; CUDA CI
`base-b` / `1-gpu-small`): the arms walk the real aging-out sequence (real
mix alias, real 2-slot record ring, real `resolve_forward_inputs`) and prove
last-owner death with a weakref; only kernel latency (`torch.cuda._sleep`)
and next-round allocation pressure are compressed for determinism. The
corruption arm runs in a subprocess pinned to
`PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` so red/green is
deterministic regardless of the CI host's allocator default.

Red/green at the base pin 6e2f87d589 (test file alone on a pristine main
worktree; executed twice, identical):

```
$ python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/managers/test_spec_v2_overlap_lifetime.py -q
...
E       AssertionError: arm subprocess produced no result: ...
E         .../aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/IndexKernel.cu:111: operator(): block: [0,0,0], thread: [0,0,0] Assertion `-sizes[i] <= index && index < sizes[i] && "index out of bounds"` failed.
E         .../aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/IndexKernel.cu:111: operator(): block: [0,0,0], thread: [1,0,0] Assertion `-sizes[i] <= index && index < sizes[i] && "index out of bounds"` failed.
...
FAILED test/registered/unit/managers/test_spec_v2_overlap_lifetime.py::TestMixRunningIndicesLifetime::test_gather_survives_aging_out
1 failed, 2 passed, 19 warnings in 23.98s
```

`test_gather_survives_aging_out` FAILS: the recycled block values reach the
still-queued gather; at this pin they land out of range, so the arm
subprocess dies on the device-side IndexKernel assert before it can report —
the loud variant of the same reuse (in-range recycled values corrupt
silently, which is the production failure mode).

With the fix (run twice):

```
$ python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/managers/test_spec_v2_overlap_lifetime.py -q
3 passed, 19 warnings in 41.54s
3 passed, 19 warnings in 27.66s
```

(the corruption arm reports CLEAN across its retries)

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No kernel or scheduling change. `record_stream` on mixed prefill+decode
batches is O(1) host-side and fires only on the mixed chunked-prefill path.

title: feat(cache-sim-tee): concurrent ingest sender (fix peak tee-drop / oracle undercount)
author: NLRX-WJC
body:
## Problem

The cache-sim ingest tee drained its bounded **4096-slot** channel with a **single background task that `.await`ed each POST serially** (`run_sender`). Throughput was capped at **~1 / POST-latency** — ~110 req/s at a ~9 ms in-cluster POST.

Any sustained arrival above that filled the channel and dropped the excess (`sgl_router_cache_sim_tee_total{result="dropped"}`), so the theoretical-cache **oracle undercounted vs the engine at peak**. Measured on `deepseek-v4-flash` from real S3 record counts:

- healthy mid-day window: coverage ≈ **1.1** (oracle ≥ engine, tee keeping up)
- peak days: **0.77** and **~0.50** pre-outage (`dropped` ≈ 4.6M / 15.6M) — coverage falling as traffic outgrew the ~110/s ceiling.

Root cause is the **serial sender**, not the channel size — a bigger channel only *delays* the drop when arrival persistently exceeds drain rate.

## Fix

Fan the sender out to **N concurrent in-flight POSTs**, bounded by a semaphore:

- The semaphore backpressures only the **drain** loop (parks the consumer when saturated) — **never** the offer/serving path, which stays the non-blocking `try_send`.
- Drain ceiling rises to **~N / POST-latency**.
- The per-POST 2s timeout still bounds a hung cache-sim.
- Each POST runs in its own task, so a panic there can't kill the sole consumer (permit releases on unwind).

`N` is configurable — `--cache-sim-send-concurrency` / `RADIXARK_CACHE_SIM_SEND_CONCURRENCY`, **default 8** (~880 req/s ceiling, ~8× the old serial ceiling and above observed peak). Deliberately **conservative**: the cache-sim pod is a **single-consumer** task, so raising the router ceiling only helps until the pod becomes the bottleneck. Start moderate and dial **up** via the env knob while watching the pod's `sglang_theoretical_cache_queue_high_water` / `_ingest_dropped_total` — if those climb, the drop simply moved to the pod (fail-loud, counted, never silent).

The **4096 `CHANNEL_CAPACITY` is unchanged** (now just burst absorption; a bigger channel would add memory cost — each slot holds the request's `input_ids` `Vec` — for little gain once the drain is fast).

## Rollout

The pod's ingest queue peaked at only **1812 / 8192 (22%)** with **zero** `ingest_dropped_total` over the last 3 days (incl. peak), so it has headroom at current load — but that's under the old ~110/s router ceiling and can't be extrapolated 8×. Deploy conservative (8), watch the two pod gauges, dial the env knob up as headroom allows. If the pod saturates: raise its `CHANNEL_CAPACITY`, or shard the single consumer.

## Test

`sender_posts_concurrently_not_serially` — a mock that holds each POST while tracking live in-flight count; asserts peak concurrency > 1 (**fails against the serial sender**, which pins it at 1). All 11 `cache_sim_tee` tests + 103 `config` tests pass; `cargo fmt --check` + `clippy` clean.

## Files

- `server/cache_sim_tee.rs` — concurrent `run_sender`; extract `post_one`; `spawn` takes `send_concurrency`.
- `config/types.rs`, `config/cli.rs` — the `cache_sim_send_concurrency` knob (env + CLI + default 8).
- `server/app_context.rs` — thread it into `spawn`.

title: [Diffusion] Fix cache-first fast path accepting a metadata-only snapshot
author: dayanandav
body:
maybe_download_model_index() fetches only model_index.json via hf_hub_download, which writes a full cache entry (blobs/, refs/main, snapshots/<sha>/). maybe_download_model()'s snapshot_download( local_files_only=True) then returns that one-file directory as a valid hit, and the force_diffusers_model=False branch returned it unchecked — callers got a weightless path with the download silently skipped.

Detect it via _is_metadata_only_pipeline_snapshot() and fall through to the download block. LoRA short-circuits first; download=False now raises instead of returning an unusable path.

Fixes #34117

## Motivation

Fixes #34117. maybe_download_model() returns a path with no component weights when a model_index.json-only cache entry exists.

hf_hub_download(repo_id, "model_index.json") (hf_diffusers_utils.py:711) writes a complete cache entry — blobs/, refs/main, snapshots/<sha>/. A later snapshot_download(local_files_only=True) resolves that ref and returns the one-file snapshot as a legitimate hit: offline there is no remote file list to distinguish "cached" from "fully cached", so completeness has to be read off disk. The force_diffusers_model=False branch returned it unchecked.

Reachable on normal startup: ServerArgs._adjust_parallelism → _model_default_uses_cfg() → maybe_download_model_index (registry.py:443) probes the repo during arg validation, before weights are fetched. Overlay models then fetch the source with force_diffusers_model=False (model_overlay.py:723, :762) and get the stub.

Why it went unreported: the overlay path self-heals via ensure_overlay_source_dir_complete, so the symptom is a spurious multi-GB re-download rather than a crash. pi05_policy.py:399 and component_accuracy/utils.py:228 do hard-fail, but rm -rf of the cache entry fixes it permanently — so it reads as cache corruption. force_diffusers_model=True was never affected, since _verify_diffusers_model_complete already rejects the stub.

A second, adjacent cache-resolution bug is fixed here too: an empty refs/<revision> makes the offline resolver join "" onto snapshots/ and hand back the parent directory, which contains only revision subdirectories and no model files.

## Modifications

_is_metadata_only_pipeline_snapshot() — true only when model_index.json declares weight-bearing components and all of them are missing.

_is_revisionless_snapshot_root() — detects a resolved path whose basename is snapshots under a models--* / datasets--* / spaces--* folder.

Cache-first branch (maybe_download_model) — the revisionless root now raises LocalEntryNotFoundError, which the pre-existing handler at :961 already treats as a cache miss, so the download block re-resolves and rewrites the ref. The not force_diffusers_model early return is now guarded by the stub check: a stub raises when download=False, otherwise logs and falls through to the download; anything else returns as before. The following if became elif so the complete-model check isn't re-entered.

Two scoping calls for reviewers:

- All-missing, not any-missing. This matches the probe state exactly and avoids false positives on allow_patterns-restricted fetches, which legitimately leave components absent (pi05_policy.py:399 passes an explicit pattern list). The empty-declared guard keeps bare component repos, which have no model_index.json, from matching via 0 == 0.
- download=False now raises ValueError — a new exception for callers threading download, i.e. model_overlay.py:723/:762.

The local-path branch (os.path.exists(model_name_or_path)) is deliberately left untouched: a filesystem path is not a repo id, so the download block cannot re-fetch it, and the guard would only convert a usable path into a hard failure. Also unchanged: LoRA repos, force_diffusers_model=True, and complete cache hits.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — no kernel, model, or forward-pass code. The change only affects which path is returned and whether a download runs. If anything it prevents a weightless directory from reaching a loader.

18 unit tests added to test/unit/test_hf_diffusers_utils.py (24 pass total, up from 6):

$ python -m pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_hf_diffusers_utils.py -q
24 passed, 15 warnings in 0.29s

Coverage: parametrized _is_revisionless_snapshot_root truth table (real SHA dir, trailing slash, datasets--*, local_dir legitimately named snapshots); corrupt ref → cache miss; metadata-only stub rejected with download=False and falling through with download=True; complete, partially-populated, and no-model_index repos all served without download; LoRA stub served as a hit; force_diffusers_model=True path unchanged. The stubbed snapshot_download records each call as probe or download, so the tests assert exact call sequences — a cache hit cannot silently start fetching, and the fall-through cannot double-fetch.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No inference-path impact; this is startup-only and does no device work, so there is nothing meaningful to profile.

- Added cost: one json.load plus one glob per declared component (typically 4–6) against an already-warm cache directory - sub-millisecond, once per call. _is_revisionless_snapshot_root is pure string manipulation.
- Removed cost: the force_download=True full re-fetch that ensure_overlay_source_dir_complete previously triggered — multi-GB for models like Lightricks/LTX-2.3.

Net effect on a cold cache is one avoided re-download.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [diffusion] perf_logger: SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING must drain the GPU queue for stage records too (fixes 2-3x inflated DecodingStage readings)
author: BBuf
body:
Branch: `p5-stage-sync-fix`, one commit rebased onto current `main`, standalone.
Measurement-infrastructure correctness only — the flag defaults off, so the
production path is untouched.

## The bug (the "95 ms mystery")

`SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1` promises synchronized stage
timings, but `StageProfiler` gated **both** its entry and exit
`synchronize()` on `_should_record_as_step()` — i.e. only
`denoising_step_*` records ever synced. Stage-type records (DecodingStage,
etc.) got **no sync at all**:

- the denoise loop's per-step exits do sync, but the DenoisingStage keeps
  launching GPU work *after* the last step context closes (scheduler /
  guidance / latent post-ops);
- that queued tail is then awaited by whichever later stage blocks first —
  typically DecodingStage's first dependent op —
- so the DecodingStage wall-clock silently included the previous stage's
  GPU tail. In this round's three-model comparison the stage readings came
  out **2-3x too high** (the prH "95 ms" hunt was chasing exactly this
  phantom).

## The fix

When the flag is on, `_maybe_sync_device()` runs at the **timing start and
end of every record** — stages and steps alike. The entry sync attributes
queued work to the stage that launched it (it drains *before* `start_time`),
and the exit sync includes the stage's own queued work. Two call sites, one
helper, no change with the flag off (default).

## Verification

**Unit test** (`test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_stage_profiler_sync.py`,
CUDA): a producer stage queues ~0.5 s of `torch.cuda._sleep` without awaiting
it; a consumer stage runs a trivial blocking op. Pre-fix the consumer reads
~500 ms (the leak); post-fix producer > 250 ms, consumer < 100 ms. Passes on
H200 GPU 1; fails on `main` as expected.

- fixed: `1 passed` — producer holds the queued time, consumer < 100 ms.
- main (same test file, `PYTHONPATH` pointed at main): `1 failed` with
  `producer: 0.0115 ms, consumer: 471.6 ms` — the entire ~0.5 s queued tail
  billed to the consumer stage.

**Krea2 repro** (H200 GPU 1, `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1`,
Krea-2-Turbo 1024x1024 / 8 steps, seed 42, steady requests):

| arm | DecodingStage (s) | DenoisingStage (s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| main @ 52afe87a08 | 0.164-0.166 | 1.314-1.315 |
| **this PR** | **0.067-0.068** | **1.461-1.462** |

The ~0.1 s denoise tail that used to be billed to DecodingStage (a 2.4x
inflation of its reading) moves back into DenoisingStage where it was
launched; only the diagnostic attribution changes.

## Checklist

- [x] Flag-off behavior byte-identical (default path never reaches the sync).
- [x] Unit test red on main, green with the fix.
- [x] `pre-commit run --files ...` (pinned) passes.

title: Fix inflated row pitch when a CP round-robin shard has a single row
author: AMD-yanfeiwang
body:
## Motivation

`dsa_cp_round_robin_split_data` can hand downstream kernels a shard whose row pitch is `cp_size` times too large, which on DeepSeek-V4 prefill context parallelism causes a GPU memory fault.

The last line of the function is

```python
return input_.view(-1, cp_size, *input_.shape[1:])[:, cp_rank].contiguous()
```

When a prefill chunk holds exactly `cp_size` tokens, every rank's shard has a **single row**. A size-1 outer dimension imposes no contiguity constraint, so `is_contiguous()` returns `True` regardless of `stride(0)` — and `.contiguous()` becomes a no-op. The shard keeps the `cp_size`-inflated row pitch, `cp_size * row_numel` instead of `row_numel`.

Any kernel that takes its row pitch from `stride(0)` then treats the shard as `cp_size` times larger than it is. On DeepSeek-V4 (`hc_mult=4`, `hidden_size=7168`, `cp_size=8`) the pitch is `229376` instead of `28672`; aiter's `mhc_pre` sizes its buffer descriptors from it and addresses past the tensor:

```
Memory access fault by GPU node-N on address 0x... (8 GPUs, 8 distinct addresses)
Fatal Python error: Aborted
  deepseek_v4.py:1541 hc_pre -> aiter/ops/mhc.py:372 mhc_pre
```

### Reproducer (deterministic, no GPU fault needed)

```python
import torch
HC, HID, CP = 4, 7168, 8
for tokens in (8, 16, 24):
    x = torch.randn(tokens, HC, HID, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")   # contiguous
    out = x.view(-1, CP, *x.shape[1:])[:, 7].contiguous()                   # the current line
    print(f"tokens={tokens:3d} m={out.shape[0]} stride0={out.stride(0):7d} "
          f"expected={HC*HID} is_contiguous={out.is_contiguous()}")
```

```
tokens=  8 m=1 stride0= 229376 expected=28672 is_contiguous=True    <-- no-op, pitch is 8x
tokens= 16 m=2 stride0=  28672 expected=28672 is_contiguous=True
tokens= 24 m=3 stride0=  28672 expected=28672 is_contiguous=True
```

## Modifications

Compare the shard's row pitch against the parent's and copy with `clone(memory_format=torch.contiguous_format)` only when they differ, plus a comment explaining why `.contiguous()` cannot be used here.

Copy behaviour versus the current code (`row_numel = prod(shape[1:])`):

| `cp_size` | shard rows | current | this PR | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | any | no copy | **no copy** | shard is genuinely contiguous |
| >1 | 1 | **no copy** (pitch stays `cp_size * row_numel`) | copy | this is the bug being fixed |
| >1 | >=2 | copy | copy | unchanged |

So the only added copy is the one that is required for correctness, and it copies a single row. An unconditional `clone()` would also have copied for `cp_size == 1`, where `.contiguous()` correctly does nothing, so the pitch comparison is used instead. Values are unchanged in every case.

Verified alternatives that also work: `torch.empty(shape).copy_(shard)`, `shard.reshape(-1, *shard.shape[1:])`.
Does **not** work: `.contiguous()`, and `input_[cp_rank::cp_size].contiguous()`.

## Accuracy Tests

Values are bit-identical to the current code in all cases (the change only affects the layout of a shard whose contents are already correct):

```
tokens=  8 rank=0: m=1 old_stride0=2272 new_stride0=284  torch.equal(old, new) = True
tokens=  8 rank=7: m=1 old_stride0=2272 new_stride0=284  torch.equal(old, new) = True
tokens= 16 rank=0: m=2 old_stride0= 284 new_stride0=284  torch.equal(old, new) = True
tokens= 24 rank=7: m=3 old_stride0= 284 new_stride0=284  torch.equal(old, new) = True
```

Separately, feeding a strided shard to the affected kernel produces wrong results, which is what this fix prevents downstream (same logical values via a strided view vs a compacted copy, DeepSeek-V4 dims):

```
m=2 cp=8  max|diff| in y = 7.42
m=4 cp=8  max|diff| in y = 10.31
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The copy runs only for single-row shards. Measured on MI355X, `(1, 4, 7168)` bf16 = 56 KB:

```
clone(memory_format=contiguous_format) on (1, 4, 7168) bf16 = 56 KB : 0.1 us per call
observed frequency: 8 calls per ~5,200 mhc_pre calls in a 3600 s run
=> ~1 us added per hour-long run
```

The `m >= 2` path is unchanged — `.contiguous()` already copied there — and `cp_size == 1` still copies nothing.

### End-to-end validation

1P1D DeepSeek-V4-Pro FP4 on MI355X, prefill TP8/EP8/**CP8** (`interleave`), decode TP8/EP8/DP8, agentic trace replay.

Instrumented runs logging every `mhc_pre` shard's strides, before the fix:

| runs | mhc_pre calls | shards with the inflated pitch | GPU memory faults |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 7 runs | ~45,000 | 0 | 0 |
| 1 run | 5,240 | **8** (one per CP rank) | **8** |

The condition is rare by default because a request's tail chunk is `extend_len % chunked_prefill_size`, so at 8192 a chunk small enough to leave a rank with one token occurs for roughly 1 request in 1000. Forcing it with `chunked-prefill-size 256` raises the rate to ~3%:

| run | forced | fix | single-row shards | inflated pitch | faults | outcome |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| A | yes | no | yes | **8** | **8** | crash after ~15 min |
| B | yes | **yes** | **8** | **0** | **0** | no fault |

Same trigger and the same number of single-row shards; the fix removes the inflated pitch and the faults.

## Related observation (not changed here)

`python/sglang/srt/layers/utils/cp_utils.py:194` has the same pattern:

```python
input_ids = input_ids[cp_rank::cp_size].contiguous()
```

I verified this `.contiguous()` is also a no-op for a single-element shard (it leaves `stride(0) == cp_size`). It is not known to cause a failure today — `input_ids` is consumed by ops that honour strides — so I left it alone to keep this PR focused, but it may be worth the same treatment.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit.
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests. — the function calls `get_parallel()` and needs a distributed context, so the reproducer above is given instead; happy to add a test if you can point me at the right harness.
- [ ] Update documentation according to Write documentations. — not applicable.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

title: Fix deterministic inference all-reduce for tp>1
author: ispobock
body:
## Motivation

`--enable-deterministic-inference` pins the NCCL algorithm to `allreduce:tree` and disables custom / symmetric-memory all-reduce, which makes a reduction reproducible for a given message size. It does not make it invariant to the message size: NCCL picks the channel count from the message size and each channel carries a differently shaped tree, so the same element is reduced in a different order depending on how many tokens share the batch. Prefill and decode consequently disagree on a token's logprob even under deterministic inference.

Pinning the channel count closes that gap. On Inkling-Small-NVFP4 at tp=4 the prefill-vs-decode check goes from 0.151 to **bit-identical**, and all three `kl_test_utils` helpers -- including both cache-hit variants -- report 0 differing logprobs out of 16384.

This is necessary but not always sufficient. A model that still runs kernels outside the aten overrides in `batch_invariant_ops` keeps a nonzero divergence from those; Qwen3-Next at tp=4 goes 6.44e-4 -> 5.06e-4 rather than to zero. What this change removes is the all-reduce as a source.

`SGLANG_DETERMINISTIC_NCCL_NCHANNELS` (default 8) trades the pinned count back for bandwidth.

## Accuracy

`Inkling-Small-NVFP4`, tp=4, 32 prompts x 512 tokens, `--enable-deterministic-inference`:

```
avg_kl_div (input vs output logprobs)   before      after
match                                   0.151464    0.000000
```

Isolating the all-reduce (same config, 16 prompts x 256 tokens):

```
tp=1, deterministic                 0.000000   (no all-reduce)
tp=4, deterministic                 0.182534
tp=4, deterministic + this change   0.000000
```

title: fix: preserve GQA head mapping in Triton DCP prefill
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

After #32858, K/V heads are replicated within a DCP group while Q heads remain sharded. The Triton DCP current-chunk prefill path passed each local Q shard together with all replicated K/V heads to the generic extend kernel.

For Qwen3.5 TP4/DCP4, every rank has 8 local Q heads and 2 replicated KV heads. The kernel therefore inferred a local 4:1 GQA mapping on every rank, even though the correct global mapping is 32:2 (16:1): ranks 0-1 belong to KV head 0 and ranks 2-3 belong to KV head 1. This corrupted every fresh prompt's prefill and reduced GSM8K accuracy from the expected ~0.95 to 0.75-0.77.

This was exposed by #34133. The original [4xB200 run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31279352796) timed out during cold startup; a subsequent [rerun](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31296982051) completed and exposed the accuracy regression.

## Modifications

- Select the contiguous replicated current-chunk K/V range corresponding to each DCP rank's Q shard before calling the Triton extend kernel.
- Keep Q sharded during prefill; no collective is added, and the existing prefix-attention path is unchanged.
- Add a CPU regression test for the TP4/DCP4 global GQA mapping.

## Accuracy Tests

Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, Triton attention, `--disable-radix-cache`:

| Configuration | GSM8K score |
| --- | ---: |
| Unpatched DCP4 CI full run | 0.772 (retry: 0.751) |
| Unpatched TP4/DCP4 on 4xB300, 256 examples | 0.773438 |
| Patched TP4/DCP4 on 4xB300, full 1,314 examples | **0.953577** |
| Patched normal TP4/DCP1 on 4xB300, full 1,314 examples | **0.949772** |

The registered DCP test threshold is 0.90. The normal TP4 result verifies that the fix does not regress the non-DCP path.

Additional validation:

- `python -m pytest -q test/registered/dcp/test_dcp_layout_unit.py`: 12 passed
- `pre-commit run --files ...`: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed

## Speed Tests and Profiling

| Configuration | Evaluation latency | Output throughput |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Patched TP4/DCP4 | 187.14 s | 1,133.58 tok/s |
| Patched normal TP4/DCP1 | 125.10 s | 1,704.64 tok/s |

Both rows use the full 1,314-example GSM8K evaluation. This change adds no communication; it narrows replicated K/V to the heads consumed by the local Q shard.

title: fix(vlm): preserve Kimi-K3 GPU JPEG accuracy
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

- decode Kimi-K3 JPEG inputs with interpolated chroma upsampling through NVIDIA nvImageCodec
- pass decoded images to PyTorch through DLPack without a device copy
- bound the per-GPU decoder pool at two instances to cap HBM overhead
- use the same path for normal serving and GPU-enabled encoder disaggregation, with a PIL fallback when the dependency or codec is unavailable
- install the pinned nvImageCodec package in the Kimi-K3 CUDA 12 and CUDA 13 images

## Root cause

`torchvision.io.decode_jpeg(..., device="cuda")` creates nvJPEG with its default flags. For common 4:2:0 JPEGs, that path uses nearest-neighbor chroma upsampling, while PIL and the Kimi reference processor use interpolated chroma reconstruction. CPU torchvision and 4:4:4 JPEGs match PIL, isolating the loss to JPEG chroma reconstruction rather than K3 normalization.

This PR enables nvImageCodec's `fancy_upsampling`, keeps the result on GPU through DLPack, preserves K3's original EXIF/prompt-coordinate semantics, and retains PIL as a safe fallback.

## Real-weight Kimi-K3 validation

Setup: exact PR head `9318484f429c`, exact `kvv-k3` head `cfa72f13bdad`, `/scratch/models/Kimi-K3`, OCRBench 1,000 images, TP8 on 2x4 GB300 nodes. The same NCCL Socket fallback was used for both sides because MNNVL `cuMemMap` is unavailable in this devbox environment.

| KVV run | Image path | Accuracy | Time | Errors |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| KVV protocol (`temperature=1`, thinking) | GPU fancy nvJPEG | 0.885 +/- 0.010 | 33:16 | 0 |
| Paired deterministic (`temperature=0`) | GPU fancy nvJPEG | **0.895** | 33:07 | 0 |
| Paired deterministic (`temperature=0`) | Official PIL | **0.895** | 33:22 | 0 |

The paired per-sample score matrix was:

| GPU | PIL | Samples |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| correct | correct | 889 |
| correct | incorrect | 6 |
| incorrect | correct | 6 |
| incorrect | incorrect | 99 |

There were zero prompt-token-count mismatches. The six flips in each direction cancel exactly, so the GPU path has no systematic OCRBench loss relative to PIL. The earlier stochastic score difference is within the run's `0.010` standard error.

## Accuracy and performance breakdown

On all 1,000 OCRBench JPEGs:

| Path | Mean raw-pixel MAE vs PIL | p99 | Maximum | Decode throughput |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| torchvision nvJPEG (before) | 0.476081 | 3.061401 | 93 | 1,771.76 img/s |
| fancy nvJPEG (after) | **0.000034** | **0.000334** | **1** | **1,815.07 img/s** |

The decoder change is both more accurate and 2.44% faster in this seeded decode benchmark. Full current GPU preprocessing measured 955.4 img/s versus 51.33 img/s for PIL (~18.6x). The paired server run was 16.3 seconds faster on GPU (~0.81%); output lengths differ slightly, so this is treated as no end-to-end regression rather than an isolated processor speedup.

The two-decoder pool retains roughly 30-50 MiB HBM per process/device pool and does not scale with the I/O worker count.

An exact Pillow fixed-point bicubic GPU kernel was also prototyped. It reduced residual post-resize error to numerical noise, but was 11.4% slower than the current antialiased PyTorch resize and produced no paired benchmark accuracy gain, so it is intentionally not included.

## Tests

- pre-commit hooks on all changed files
- `test_base_processor_image_decode.py`: 11 passed
- `test_kimi_k3_encoder_mode.py`: 15 passed
- exact-commit H200 and GB300 GPU checks: 4:2:0 parity, CHW/uint8/contiguity, 16-thread concurrent decode, and PIL fallback
- RGB 4:4:4/4:2:2/4:2:0, progressive JPEG, grayscale, CMYK, and EXIF-orientation parity checks

title: [DSA] Fix top-k v2 dropping non-primary ranks' output on CUDA 13.1+ (root cause for #33835)
author: DarkSharpness
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4 DSA decode can return a corrupt top-k from the fused small-batch
cluster kernel, which downstream sparse attention then dereferences as garbage KV
indices (the illegal memory access reported in #33835).

The trigger is the **CUDA toolkit version, not the GPU architecture**: identical
source and identical hardware (H200, sm_90a) are correct when built with nvcc
12.9/13.0 and wrong when built with 13.1/13.2/13.3.

## Root cause

`TopKCluster::forward` picked its phase-3 scatter destination up front:

```c
const auto cur_out = is_primary ? problem.out : smem->tmp_out;
...
cur_out[pos] = idx;
```

`problem.out` can be a `shared::cluster` (DSMEM) alias of the elected rank's
buffer, while `smem->tmp_out` is `shared::cta`. Merging both into one pointer
variable makes cicc 13.1+ mis-lower the block-local arm on sm_90a and **silently
drop every non-primary rank's staged output** — `tmp_out` stays zero, and phase
3.5 then faithfully copies zeros to perfectly correct DSMEM addresses.

Slot-diffing one row against a CUDA 12.9 build shows exactly one contiguous bad
run:

```
correct slots: 129/512      bad-slot runs: [(61, 443, 383)]
```

Slots 0–60 are the primary's own scatter and 444–511 are the `handle_tie` tail;
the 383 lost slots are exactly the seven peers' contributions. Read-back
instrumentation confirms the mechanism — `tmp_out[0] == 0` on all seven peers
under 13.3 versus valid indices (8161, 10064, 16264, …) under 12.9, while
`count_gt` reports 34–64 candidates found.

Verified *not* the cause (each tested and ruled out): `enable_smem_spilling`,
`__restrict__` on `TopKProblem::out`, the store's address space (forcing a
generic `st.u32` at the emit changes nothing), the load side (`volatile` loads),
and memory ordering (explicit `barrier.cluster.arrive.release` /
`wait.acquire`, `__threadfence()`). Pointer values, `start_write`/`num_write`,
and the store addresses were all dumped and are **correct in both toolchains** —
only the data was wrong.

## Changes

**1. Keep the two scatter destinations in separate code paths** so neither
pointer ever carries two address spaces, with a comment so nobody merges them
back. This is the actual fix.

**2. Drop the `peer_problem` copy from #32910**, stating the block-local pointer
at the read-back site instead. That `__builtin_assume` is load-bearing, not an
optimization: removing it reproduces the #32830 cicc segfault on 13.1/13.2/13.3.

**3. Make top-k v1 take a runtime `topk`** (second commit, separable). v1 baked
`topk` in via `-DSGL_TOPK`, building one module per k; since the macro fed a
`constexpr` rather than a template parameter, the modules exported identically
mangled symbols, and `setup_kernel_smem_once`'s function-local static is emitted
as `STB_GNU_UNIQUE` — merged across every loaded object regardless of
`RTLD_LOCAL`. The module used *second* therefore skipped its
`cudaFuncSetAttribute` opt-in and failed to launch with 64 KB of dynamic shared
memory (`CUDA error: invalid argument`). `bench_topk.py` hits this because it
sweeps k in {512, 1024} in one process; a server only ever uses one k.

## Scope correction vs #33835

#33835 attributes this to Hopper and to rows just above the 32K small-batch
floor. Measured here, **every** fused small-batch cluster shape is affected
(`batch <= 30` and `seq_len > cluster_floor`), including 65537 and 98304 which
that PR reports as fine — the floor only makes the path reachable at
`batch <= 15`. The persistent-pool path was never affected because it stages
output in global memory. With the root cause fixed, no arch gate is needed and
the fused path keeps working on Hopper.

The boundary regression test added by #33835 is still worth keeping; it covers a
real gap (`batch <= 15` with `seq_len` in (32768, 65536]).

## Validation

H200 (sm_90a), 157-row suite = the report's shapes + a boundary sweep +
register/streaming/persistent controls, k in {512, 1024, 2048}:

| nvcc | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 12.9 | 0 bad | 0 bad |
| 13.0 | 0 bad | 0 bad |
| 13.1 | **157 bad** | 0 bad |
| 13.2 | **157 bad** | 0 bad |
| 13.3 | **157 bad** | 0 bad |

Those are all five stable nvcc minors >= 12.9. Additionally: 1500-iteration
randomized stress and 500 CUDA-graph replays clean; builds for **sm_90a and
sm_100a** on every toolchain; v1's runtime-topk path passes 80 cases spanning
k in {1, 2, 7, 31, 64, 100, 255, 256, 257, 300, 511, 512, 513, 777, 1023, 1024}
against trivial / boundary / radix shapes.

**No performance regression** (CUDA 12.9, where both old and new are correct, so
the comparison is at equal correctness):

| case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| register 8x8192 | 3.882 | 3.884 |
| streaming 100x65536 | 14.276 | 14.261 |
| fused-cluster 8x33000 | 8.387 | **8.230** |
| fused-cluster 8x98304 | 9.431 | **9.309** |
| fused-cluster 30x131072 | 13.805 | **13.564** |
| 1 long + 7 short (report shape) | 9.740 | **9.575** |
| persistent 128x131072 | 42.010 | 42.025 |

Worst case +0.1% (noise); the fused cluster path gets 1.3–2.9% faster.

## Caveats

- **sm_100a is compile-verified only** — no Blackwell was available to run on.
  Runtime confirmation there would be welcome.
- CI builds cu130, which is a clean cell, so **CI cannot currently catch this
  class of bug**. Worth considering a toolkit-version guard or moving a build to
  13.1+.
- The remaining exported-weak-symbol hazard in v1 (the kernel host stub itself)
  is not addressed here. Compiling JIT modules with hidden visibility would be
  the general fix; it matters because that half fails *silently* rather than
  erroring.

## Checklist

- [x] Root cause identified and the disproven hypotheses documented
- [x] Verified across every stable nvcc minor >= 12.9, before and after
- [x] Performance measured at equal correctness; no regression
- [ ] Blackwell (sm_100a) runtime validation
- [ ] CI

title: Fix stale track rows corrupting conv checkpoints under the prefill graph
author: ispobock
body:
## Motivation

A prefix-cache hit on a hybrid-SWA model can decode off a conv state it never produced. The replayed prefill graph reads `_capture_req_slots` rows, but `mamba_track_mask` / `mamba_track_indices` keep whatever the previous replay left past the live batch, so the captured track scatter lands the current window in an earlier request's checkpoint. Whichever request later restores that prefix is wrong for its whole generation.

The sentinel tail directly above exists for this reason -- "the captured graph reads all req_slots entries, so stale values from the previous replay must be cleared" -- and clears six fields. The two track buffers live in the buffer registry instead, and their clear is guarded by `bs != raw_bs` in `PrefillInputBuffers.fill_from`; the prefill graph passes `padded_bs == raw_bs` because it pads tokens rather than requests, so that branch never runs.

This needs no speculative decoding. It takes the prefill CUDA graph, chunked prefill, concurrency and a prefix hit together, and disabling the prefill graph alone makes it go away. #34043 fixed a neighbouring failure on the spec path -- the scatter being specialised out of the capture -- whereas here the checkpoint is written and scattered to a stale destination; it still reproduces with #34043 in.

## Modifications

Zero the two track rows alongside the six the sentinel tail already covers.

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34168 `test_inkling_small_nvfp4.py` drops the `--disable-prefill-cuda-graph` it was carrying. That flag was steering the deterministic KL case around this bug, and that case is the regression guard for it, so it belongs back on the graph path.

The alternative is to make `padded_bs` report the captured slot count, which makes `fill_from`'s clear live and stops its `bs != raw_bs` branch from being dead code. That is the more honest shape -- while the request dimension claims to be unpadded, the next captured kernel that reads `req_slots` rows repeats this -- but it changes behaviour under every phase sharing those buffers, so this PR takes the local fix. Happy to switch.

## Accuracy

Shrunken Inkling checkpoint, tp=1, 32 concurrent prompts, prefill graph on, `--enable-deterministic-inference`. Differing logprobs against a flushed reference prefill:

```
              prefill_cache_hit                match
           512 tokens    8 tokens
before     1022/16384      16/256              0
after         0/16384       0/256              0
```

The two corrupted checkpoints were observed rather than inferred: instrumenting the slot at insert time shows exactly two whose conv state differs from the same run without the graph, and their claimed track seqlens are the prefixes of the two requests that go wrong.

The A/B above is the shrunken checkpoint at tp=1. The CI case runs the real NVFP4 weights at tp=4, where the batch packs differently and picks different victims, so I have not reproduced-and-fixed on that exact configuration -- if it stays red, the same shape of gap exists somewhere else and the instrumentation above finds it.

title: [Kimi K3] Rework skipped-think fix as opt-in force_nonempty_content with streaming coverage
author: JustinTong0323
body:
Stacked on top of #33995. Keeps @yhyang201's original commit `d11868d7d9` in history and supersedes it with a rework.

## Problem

K3 sometimes closes its think channel before producing any answer (EOS inside think), so responses come back with `reasoning_content` but empty `content`. #33995 fixed the non-stream path by treating marker-less output as content, which has two leaks:

- **Truncated reasoning becomes content**: a `max_tokens` cut also produces zero think markers, so truncated thinking gets misclassified as the answer.
- **Streaming stays broken**: the branch only exists in `detect_and_parse`; `parse_streaming_increment` starts in `force_reasoning=True` and streams the raw payload as `reasoning_text`, so `stream=True` still returns `content=""`.

## What this PR does

Reworks the fix as an opt-in, K3-native `force_nonempty_content`:

- `KimiK3Detector.__init__` accepts `force_nonempty_content` so the existing `chat_template_kwargs` plumbing in `ReasoningParser` works (previously `TypeError`).
- `detect_and_parse` reclassifies only on positive evidence: `RESPONSE_CLOSE` or `MESSAGE_CLOSE` present and zero think markers (full or partial). Bare marker-free text (truncated reasoning) stays reasoning.
- Streaming **never holds chunks back**. A hold-back would starve SSE during long thinking runs (no delta until the channel decision) and trip client idle timeouts (observed: ~300 s client-side `terminated` while the server is still decoding). Instead, undecided prethink text streams as `reasoning_content` in real time, and `finish()` re-emits the cleaned payload as `content` once the response/message close proves skipped-think — mirroring the base class's `finish()` re-emit of accumulated reasoning.
- The `finish()` re-emit is gated on `_in_reasoning`, i.e. it only fires when no channel decision ever happened mid-stream. Without the gate, answers that already streamed as `content` (`RESPONSE_OPEN` expressible, or `force_reasoning=False`) would be emitted a second time.
- Under `stream_reasoning=False`, reasoning buffered past a mid-stream cut (e.g. `max_tokens`) still flushes: the non-fnc path delegates to the base `finish()`, and the fnc path flushes the buffer as `reasoning_text` itself, because the base implementation would reclassify it as `content` under fnc — the leak this flag exists to prevent.

Clients therefore see: live `reasoning_content` while the model thinks → final `content` delta carrying the actual answer for skipped-think runs; long thinking runs stream uninterrupted end to end.

No behavior change for `force_nonempty_content=False`; all existing K3 parser tests unchanged.

## Tests

- `test_fnc_non_stream_skipped_think_vs_truncated_reasoning` — non-stream skipped-think vs truncated reasoning under `force_nonempty_content=True`.
- `test_fnc_streaming_skipped_think_answer` — real-time reasoning deltas + finish() content re-emit, across chunk sizes 1/5/13.
- `test_fnc_streaming_truncated_reasoning_stays_reasoning` — no close evidence → stays reasoning.
- `test_fnc_streaming_long_think_streams_without_close` — 20k chars of marker-free thinking streams every chunk live; no hold-back.
- `test_fnc_streaming_response_open_not_reemitted` / `test_fnc_streaming_force_reasoning_off_not_reemitted` — answer streams exactly once; the finish() re-emit never duplicates it.
- `test_stream_reasoning_off_truncation_flushes_reasoning` — truncated reasoning flushes as reasoning, fnc on and off.
- `test_fnc_stream_reasoning_off_skipped_think_reemits_content` — skipped-think re-emit still works when nothing streamed live.

The duplication and flush-regression tests fail on the pre-gate code (verified by stashing the fix); everything passes after it.

```
$ pytest test/registered/unit/parser/test_kimik3_reasoning_parser.py test/registered/unit/parser/test_reasoning_parser.py
138 passed
```

## Validation (BEAM 1M)

Full [BEAM](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/Kimi-Vendor-Verifier/tree/main/beam) 1M run (700 long multi-turn questions near 1M context) on a 2-node 8×GB300 devbox, `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` TP8, `--default-chat-template-kwargs '{"force_nonempty_content": true}'`:

| | empty content | overall (LLM-judged) |
|---|---|---|
| flag on (n=700) | **0.71%** (5/700) | 0.333 |
| flag off (n=700) | **17.57%** (123/700) | 0.288 |

- Empty-answer breakdown by failure mode: with the flag on, only **1/700 (0.14%)** is the skipped-think mode (finish=stop, empty content); the other 4 are finish=length at the 32k-token cap mid-reasoning, which no parser-side fix can address. With the flag off, **116/700 (16.6%)** are the skipped-think mode — the fix eliminates two orders of magnitude of them (16.6% → 0.14%).
- A/B improvement is consistent across two independent judges (kimi-k3 self-judge +0.042, deepseek-v4-flash +0.045, full 700-question arms); the control arm's judged score (0.274/0.288 across judges) matches the externally reported 0.264 for this endpoint, so the eval setup lines up with theirs.

Judge caveat: no official judge endpoint available, so absolute scores carry a judge-identity caveat; the empty-rate claim does not depend on the judge.

title: [DSV4] Fix silent KV corruption when speculative draft tokens > 4
author: hnyls2002
body:
Supersedes #33872.

## Motivation

The compress write plan decides which tokens' raw KV get persisted into the compress-state ring for a *future* compression window to read. A speculative verify batch plans from the optimistic `seq_len = prefix_len + num_draft_tokens` but rolls back to `prefix_len + accept_len`, so every committed token must stay resident whatever the accept length turns out to be.

`c_plan.cuh` capped that pad at a hard-coded 4:

```cpp
constexpr int32_t kMaxMTPDraftTokens = 4;
const auto mtp_pad = std::min(ring_size - compress_ratio, kMaxMTPDraftTokens);
```

With `--speculative-num-draft-tokens > 4` the plan under-writes the ring, and a later compression reads stale slots. This fails silently -- no illegal access, no NaN, no assertion, just wrong compressed state. The host planner path was additionally missing the pad term entirely, so the CPU and GPU planners disagreed.

## Modifications

**The pad is a property of the ring, not of the batch.** A write at `w` aliases onto `w - ring_size`, and the earliest position a future compression can still need is `prefix_len - window_size + 2` (the next batch commits at least one token, and `run_prefill` launches the compress kernel before the write kernel, so a batch's own compressions read the pre-write ring). So the ring's capacity is `ring_size - window_size + 2`, and the plan can simply always pad that far:

```cpp
const auto mtp_pad = ring_size > window_size ? ring_size - window_size + 2 : 0;
```

Padding past a batch's own extend range is harmless -- the planner loops only span `[prefix_len, seq_len)`. A non-speculative ring is exactly one window wide, so the pad is 0 there and the write set is unchanged.

All three planner paths (both `plan_compress_prefill_kernel0` branches and the C++ host loop) now share this value, fixing the CPU/GPU divergence.

**Capacity is validated at startup.** `DSV4PoolConfigurator` rejects a draft count the ring cannot serve, using `max_speculative_num_draft_tokens` since the ring is sized once and must serve the largest adaptive tier. The planner itself cannot do this -- it cannot tell an over-configured verify batch from an ordinary long prefill -- so an over-configured server now fails at startup instead of corrupting state at run time.

The current rings serve `num_draft_tokens <= 10` for c4 and `<= 130` for c128. Raising the c4 bound means growing the ring, which scales the c4 state pool; that tradeoff is left out of this PR.

## Accuracy Tests

`test_deepseek_v4_compress_plan_draft_pad.py` (kernel, ~8s in CI):

- `test_c4_ring_residency` / `test_c128_ring_residency` -- for every draft count the ring serves, crossed with residues of `seq_len % compress_ratio`, assert `plan_w` covers all of `[prefix_len, seq_len)`. This is the sufficient condition: if each step writes its whole extend range, the next compression window is resident by induction whatever the accept length. Reverting the pad turns these red for `D > 4`.
- `test_cpu_and_gpu_planner_agree` -- pins `plan_compress_prefill_kernel0` to the host-loop plan, so the fix has to hold on both paths.
- `test_plain_prefill_write_set` -- non-speculative rings produce the pre-existing write set for both ratios, i.e. no change for non-speculative serving.
- `test_over_capacity_under_writes` -- past the ring capacity the plan silently under-writes, which is why the bound is enforced at startup rather than in the planner.

`test_dsv4_compress_write_pad.py` (CPU unit, ~1s) covers the capacity helper: 0 without speculation, 10/130 for the speculative rings, and 0 for the online-c128 ring of 1.

### The kernel test fails on the pre-fix planner

A regression test that also passes on the buggy code proves nothing, so this was checked directly — running the test file above against the pre-fix planner gives **19 failures**:

| test | failing cases before the fix |
|---|---|
| `test_c4_ring_residency` | D = 5, 9, 10 (each across 4 residues of `seq_len % 4`) |
| `test_c128_ring_residency` | D = 129, 130 |
| `test_cpu_and_gpu_planner_agree` | compress_ratio=128, D=130 |

Two things worth calling out. c4 starts losing positions at **D=5**, exactly `D > kMaxMTPDraftTokens` — the boundary is sharp, which is why an `ndt` of 4 or 2 never sees it. And c128 only breaks near the ring's capacity: its `first_w_pos = min(last_c_pos, seq_len - pad)` usually takes `last_c_pos` (as `seq_len % 128` is typically much larger than the pad), which already reaches far enough back. The exposure is concentrated in the c4 layers.

The third row is a separate defect the pre-fix code also had: the C++ host loop carried no pad term at all, only the GPU kernel did, so the two planner paths emitted different write sets.

### End-to-end

DeepSeek-V4-Flash + DSPARK at `--speculative-dspark-block-size 7` (D=8, past the old cap of 4), TP=4, `--moe-runner-backend marlin`; two servers launched identically apart from the checkout.

| | GSM8K (200) | GPQA diamond (198, 5 rounds) | latency | throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 0.990 | 0.7172 | 65.1s | 354.8 tok/s |
| after | 0.985 | 0.7374 | 64.7s | 352.7 tok/s |

Plus an opaque-id echo probe (200 requests, 4000-token prefix, greedy): 200/200 exact on both.

**These numbers show no regression; they are not evidence the fix works.** GPQA leans positive (4 of 5 rounds, +0.02 mean) but is not significant — paired t = 2.0 at df=4, p ~ 0.12. At `temperature=0` over a fixed question set the five rounds should have been identical yet spanned ~4.5pp, so concurrent-batch nondeterminism puts the noise floor above the effect size.

That the fix is not visible end-to-end is expected. The skipped positions are the head of the draft tail, and consecutive verify batches have heavily overlapping write sets, so the next step usually rewrites what the previous one skipped. Corruption needs a position to stay unwritten until a compression actually reads it, which depends on accept-length distribution, sequence length, and compression-point alignment lining up.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance impact expected. The change replaces a compile-time constant with an expression over values the planner already receives; no extra memory traffic, no new launches, no change to the compress kernels. A speculative verify batch writes more rows than before, which is the fix, bounded by the ring capacity.

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

title: [diffusion] Z-Image single-GPU BCG: fix the replay crash and make output bit-exact vs eager (#34183)
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #34183 completely: **single-GPU BCG on the Z-Image family both crashed and, once uncrashed, produced drifted output.** This PR fixes both halves; with it, single-GPU Z-Image BCG is functional **and bit-exact vs eager** under the default flags.

The nightly `zimage` numbers never caught either problem because that preset runs TP=2, whose per-layer NCCL syncs mask the crash race (as does `compute-sanitizer`'s serialization), and latency tables don't compare md5.

## Fix 1 — crash: pin cache values consumed under BCG capture

Z-Image's forward keeps **single-slot shape-keyed caches** (`_cached_{x,cap}_rope_cache`, `_cached_{x,cap,joint}_attn_mask_meta`, `_cached_batched_freqs_cis`), each one `(cache_key, value)` slot. The rope keys include **`data_ptr()` of the per-signature static input buffers**, so capturing the *next* text bucket replaced **every** slot (image-side included) and freed the old tensors, while the previously captured graph had their device addresses baked in — the first replay dereferenced freed memory. Symptom depended on allocator timing: `CUDA illegal memory access` by default, an indefinite hang with `--dit-cpu-offload=false`.

Localization chain (H200, per-segment-sync instrumentation): default 5 buckets → crash at the **first replayed segment (0/35)**; single bucket → clean; two buckets → crash; **private mempool per capture → still crashes** (pool block reuse ruled out); CFG-off / base-vs-Turbo → CFG and weights ruled out; TP=2 / memcheck → clean (serialization masks the race).

`_pin_for_active_capture(value)` keeps every cache value consumed while a capture is active alive for the module's lifetime. The values are pure functions of their keys, so pinned tensors stay numerically correct as well as address-stable; growth is bounded by O(cache sites × captured signatures) small tensors; nothing is pinned outside capture. Guarded by `is_in_breakable_cuda_graph()` with `torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()` as fallback (the latter raises on CPU-only builds, hence the `is_available()` guard).

## Fix 2 — numerics: capture at the native caption length, not text buckets

With the crash fixed, BCG-vs-eager md5 could be measured for the first time: the default text buckets produced a **visibly drifted image** (PSNR 21.24 dB vs eager; different-seed baseline 12.8 dB), deterministically.

Root cause (measured by elimination): eager is fully deterministic (same md5 across 3 fresh processes and 2 in-process requests); the first divergent block is **`context_refiner.0`** (first caption self-attention, maxdiff ≈ 6 on *valid* rows) while image-only blocks stay bit-identical; caption freqs prefix, varlen meta content, and block inputs are all bit-equal; `flash_attn_varlen_func` is insensitive to `max_seqlen` in a standalone microtest. A mask-query spy delivered the verdict: **Z-Image attends its caption slots unmasked by design** — the pipeline pads captions to the native length (a multiple of 32) with learned pad-token embeddings acting as *attended registers*, and the DiT derives the attention span from the full padded tensor (`lens == target` → mask=None) on the natural path too. Padding to a 48/64 bucket changes how many registers every token attends; no mask configuration can reproduce the reference semantics at a larger bucket.

The Z-Image prompt padder now captures at the **incoming native caption length** (`max(seq, cap_freq_len)`) instead of `select_text_bucket`: the ladder's warmup captures dedupe to one graph per native length, signature cardinality stays bounded by the pipeline's own length quantization, and unseen lengths keep the existing serving-time eager fallback. The old `test_zimage_prompt_lengths_share_bucket_signature` guarded exactly the removed shared-bucket contract and is rewritten to pin the new one (native length kept; equal lengths share a signature; distinct lengths intentionally don't).

## Validation (H200)

| check | result |
| --- | --- |
| default 5-bucket single-GPU BCG (previously 100% crash) | **clean**, Turbo + base `Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image` both complete |
| TP=2 | unchanged |
| **BCG vs eager md5, default flags** | **identical** (`d7e71ba8…`), 1 captured graph (was `977fb1da…`, PSNR 21.24 dB) |
| eager determinism | same md5 across 3 processes and 2 in-process consecutive requests |
| unit tests | BCG padding suite 18/18, incl. the rewritten `test_diffusion_bcg_padding.py` contract case (native length kept; equal lengths share a signature; distinct lengths intentionally don't) |

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests (each red on pre-fix code).
- [x] Provide accuracy and repro results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

title: [Fix] [AMD] DSP: skip unused QuickAllReduce allocation for DCP groups
author: tanth47
body:
## Motivation

On ROCm, `GroupCoordinator` currently initializes QuickAllReduce whenever custom all-reduce is enabled. That is useful for TP, but current DCP communication paths do not dispatch to QuickAllReduce:

- `ag_rs`: all-gather plus reduce-scatter for MLA, or an FP32 all-reduce for MHA.
- `a2a` / `fi_a2a`: all-to-all.

In a Kimi-K3 TP8/DCP8 profile on MI350X, constructing the DCP QuickAllReduce communicator reserved 4.002 GiB per GPU. Across 1,152 recorded rank-0 DCP collective dispatches, QuickAllReduce was selected zero times. TP QuickAllReduce remains useful and must stay enabled.

Related to #29736.

## Modifications

- Add an optional `use_quick_allreduce` control to `GroupCoordinator` and `init_model_parallel_group`.
- Preserve the existing behavior by default: the new option inherits `use_custom_allreduce` when unspecified.
- Disable QuickAllReduce only for the DCP group.
- Keep the AITER custom-all-reduce and PyNccl setup unchanged.
- Add a unit test that verifies DCP opts out while TP retains the default behavior.

## Accuracy Tests

This does not change model math or the collective selected by current DCP paths. The targeted construction test passes:

```
1 passed, 5 deselected
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This PR targets static memory rather than latency. Measured DCP communicator initialization on MI350X:

| Component | Reserved per GPU |
| --- | ---: |
| PyNccl | 1.883 GiB |
| AITER custom all-reduce | 3.002 GiB |
| QuickAllReduce | 4.002 GiB |

QuickAllReduce had zero selections in the recorded DCP dispatches, so this change reclaims the 4.002 GiB DCP allocation without removing TP QuickAllReduce.

## Checklist

- [x] Ran pre-commit on the changed files.
- [x] Added a focused unit test.
- [x] No documentation change is required; the default API behavior is preserved.
- [x] No model kernel or output math is changed.

title: [Fix] lfm2 detector: recover tool calls dropped by common model-outpu…
author: fatday
body:
# [Fix] lfm2 detector: recover tool calls dropped by common model-output quirks

## Motivation

Running real LFM2/LFM2.5 agent traces (SWE-agent / shell-command workloads)
through `Lfm2Detector` turned up three distinct kinds of problem. They are
listed separately because they are not equally the parser's fault, and
reviewers may want only some of them.

**1. The detector rejects valid Python.** The model wrote a correct tool call
and the call was dropped anyway.

| Model output | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `limit=+7` | only `USub` handled — call dropped | `7` |
| `tags={'a', 'b'}` (set) | rejected — call dropped | `["a", "b"]` (JSON has no set type) |
| `query=f'hello'` (placeholder-free f-string) | `JoinedStr` rejected — call dropped | `"hello"` |

**2. The detector emits wrong data.** A call is reported as successful but its
arguments are corrupt or unusable, so the tool runs on the wrong input — worse
than reporting nothing.

| Model output | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `limit=1e999` | `{"limit": Infinity}` — **not valid JSON** | call skipped; every emitted `parameters` parses |
| `get_weather('Paris', unit='celsius')` | `{"unit": "celsius"}` — `'Paris'` silently gone | call rejected |
| `search(**{'query': 'cats'})` | the `**` kwargs silently missing | merged (later binding wins); non-dict rejects the call |
| `[read(path='/x'), send(payload=b'raw')]` | the bytes argument dropped **both** calls | only the offending call is skipped |
| `[read(path='/x'), bash(command='grep 'e' a.log')]` | the sibling's broken quote makes the whole block a SyntaxError — the **valid** `read` dropped with it | `read` survives; the block splits at top-level commas and each segment parses alone |

**3. The model wrote invalid Python and the detector gives up.** These are
model mistakes: the output is not parseable and dropping it is defensible.
The fixes are recovery — deterministic, value-preserving rewrites applied
only after `ast.parse` has already failed. They are the debatable group; I
am happy to drop them if you would rather keep the pressure on the model.

| Model output | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `query='line one\nline two'` (raw newline) | `SyntaxError` — call dropped | value keeps the newline |
| `query='printf a\x00b'` (NUL byte) | `ValueError` from `ast.parse` — call dropped | `\u0000` in JSON |
| `day=07` (zero-padded int) | `SyntaxError` — call dropped | `{"day": 7}` |
| `query='sed -n '360,450p' f.py'` (nested quotes) | `SyntaxError` — call dropped | recovered when exactly one closing quote yields parseable text (ast-validated), never a reading that absorbs a sibling call |

One case sits outside all three: `from=1`. A tool may legitimately declare a
parameter named `from`, so the model is right and the pythonic format simply
cannot express it — the name is rewritten for parsing and restored afterwards.

The block splitting above has a side effect worth naming: when *every*
call in the block carries the nested-quote mistake
(`[bash(command='sed -n '1,5p' a.py'), bash(command='sed -n '9,12p' b.py')]`),
each split segment is exactly the single-call shape the nested-quote
recovery already handles, so both calls come back. That is not a new
recovery policy — it removes the inconsistency where the same call was
recovered alone but dropped next to a sibling.

Genuinely ambiguous nesting (two plausible closing quotes that both parse,
e.g. `city='echo 'hi', unit='celsius'`) is still rejected rather than guessed
at. Streaming buffers the complete block and delegates to `detect_and_parse`,
so it inherits all of the above unchanged.

These mirror the fixes recently merged for the same tool-call format in vLLM
(vllm-project/vllm#48171); this port is adapted to `Lfm2Detector`'s structure
(per-call salvage, buffered streaming) and touches no other detector. Each fix
class is its own commit with its regression test. The vLLM PR covered a few
extra classes that need no port here: negatives, tuples, sentinel whitespace,
dotted names and lowercase `true/false/null` are already handled by this
detector, and the bracket-counting / backslash-run / truncated-stream classes
only exist in vLLM's incremental streaming completion — this detector's
buffer-complete streaming design is immune to them.

## Alignment with the vLLM fixes

This detector now matches the behavior of the same fixes in vLLM
(vllm-project/vllm#48171, merged, and the follow-up #51649): the same 42
payloads — vLLM's own test constants, adversarial quote/escape cases and
real SWE-agent traces — produce identical calls and arguments through both
implementations.

`PythonicDetector` gets the two defects that are observable there too
(non-finite arguments serialized as `Infinity`; one unconvertible argument
dropping every sibling call in the block). Its regex gate already rejects
positional and `**`-unpacked arguments wholesale, so those fixes would have
no observable effect there and are not ported.

## Modifications

- `lfm2_detector.py`: module-level pure rewrite helpers
  (`_escape_ctrl_chars_in_strings`, `_normalize_leading_zero_ints`,
  `_escape_nested_quotes_in_strings`, `_rename_reserved_kwargs` /
  `_restore_reserved_kwarg_names`, `_recovery_candidates`) + a recovery loop
  in `_parse_pythonic_content`; `_get_parameter_value` gains `UAdd`, `Set`,
  constant-`JoinedStr`, and restricts `Constant` to JSON-representable types;
  `_parse_pythonic_call` serializes with `allow_nan=False` and skips the call
  on failure, merges `**`-unpacked dict literals (later binding wins), and
  rejects calls with positional arguments instead of silently dropping the
  values.
- `test_function_call_parser.py`: 17 regression cases in `TestLfm2Detector`,
  each verified to fail on the pre-fix detector (the ambiguous-nesting case
  is the negative-branch guard).

## Checklist

- **19 new regression cases**, each verified to fail without its fix.
  `TestLfm2Detector` 40 pass, `TestPythonicDetector` 17 pass; the pre-existing
  cases in both are unchanged.
- A 42-payload differential harness (vLLM test constants, adversarial
  utils-level cases, real SWE traces) shows this detector and vLLM's merged
  lfm2 parser now produce identical calls and arguments on every payload.
- `black` / `isort` / `ruff` (pinned pre-commit versions) clean.

title: fix(scheduler): track max prefill batch size over recent real admissions
author: hanwlax
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
`Scheduler.max_prefill_bs` previously decayed on every scheduler pass. Because the value was converted to an integer before being passed to `PrefillDelayer`, small but valid high-watermarks such as `2` could quickly become `0`, especially when many decode-only or idle passes occurred between real prefill admissions.
Once `max_prefill_bs` reached `0`, the `all` path's `slot_condition` became ineffective. This allowed prefill work to interfere with decode batches and degraded TPOT.
This change makes the high-watermark reflect recent real prefill admissions instead of scheduler-pass frequency.

## Modifications
>  Use env var `SGLANG_PREFILL_DELAYER_MAX_PREFILL_BS_WINDOW_SIZE` to control the sliding window.
Updated the implementation from per-scheduler-pass decay to a sliding-window maximum over the latest 16 non-empty prefill attempts. Successful admissions record the actual prefill batch size, while rejected non-empty attempts are also added using a conservative estimate based on the waiting queue and available request slots. Idle and decode-only passes do not advance the window. This allows a rejected small prefill batch to evict a stale large spike after 16 attempts instead of waiting for unrelated scheduler passes. Unit tests covering a BS=100 spike followed by rejected BS=2/3/4 attempts all pass.
- Added `RecentPrefillBatchSizeTracker`, which tracks the maximum prefill batch size over the latest 64 non-empty admissions.
- Updated the tracker only after a real prefill admission.
- Removed the `per-scheduler-pass` `0.998` decay.
- Changed `max_prefill_bs` from a floating-point value to an integer.
- Added unit tests covering:
  - Expiration of an old admission peak after it leaves the sliding window.
  - Preservation of recurring small prefill batch sizes.
  - Rejection of invalid or empty admission updates.
- Kept the existing `PrefillDelayer` negotiation behavior unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable. This change only affects prefill scheduling and does not modify model forward computation or model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Test workload:
```text
Model: Kimi-K2.6-W4A8
Requests: 256
Input length: 3500 tokens
Output length: 1500 tokens
DP size: 16
```
Results:

title: [diffusion] Fix H3 rank-local FSDP QKV loading
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

- preserve custom weight-loader semantics in rank-local FSDP checkpoint loading
- apply MiniMax-H3's grouped-QKV layout transform before selecting each FSDP shard
- fall back to the existing full loader for unsupported custom loaders instead of silently loading incorrect values

## Root cause

MiniMax-H3 stores attention QKV rows in per-head grouped order, while the native runtime consumes concatenated Q, K, and V blocks. The ordinary H3 weight loader performs this reorder, but the rank-local FSDP fast path read shape-compatible safetensors slices directly and bypassed that loader. The resulting parameters had valid shapes but incorrect values, so serving completed without errors while producing corrupted video and audio.

The fast path now requires standard loader semantics or an explicit rank-local layout transform. H3 registers its existing QKV reorder as that transform, which is applied before DTensor shard selection.

## Validation

- focused loader and H3 contract tests: 18 passed
- pre-commit passed for all changed files
- 4x H200 standard `sglang serve` T2VA E2E: fixed FSDP4 + Ulysses4 output was byte-identical to the resident Ulysses4 output

Fixes #34227.

title: [metrics] Fix prefill FLOPs estimate to count prefix and per-request causal pairs
author: Lenoplus42
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #34298.

`SchedulerMetricsReporter._estimate_prefill_perf` computes the causal attention pair count using only `sum(extend_lens)`. In other words, when a chunk of `c` tokens is resumed at prefix `P`, the estimator scores it as if it were a brand-new sequence of length `c`. This produces two independent errors.

1. Pairs against the cached prefix are dropped
The `c * P` attention pairs between the chunk and its cached prefix are never counted. Because both FLOPs terms depend only on `sum(extend_lens)`, a fixed `--chunked-prefill-size` makes the estimated numerator identical for every chunk of a request. The reported `est. prefill TFLOPS/s` then becomes proportional to `1 / gap_latency` rather than to any real measure of throughput.
Later chunks take longer as their prefix grows, so the number trends down while the GPU is doing more work per chunk, which is the opposite of the intended signal for the metric.

2.  Separate requests are merged into one sequence
The batch is summed before the pair count is computed, which collapses all requests in the batch into a single sequence. But a token only attends within its own request. For example, two 100-token prefills actually cost `2 * (100*101/2) = 10,100` pairs, while scoring them as one 200-token sequence gives `200*201/2 = 20,100` — charging 10,000 pairs between tokens that never attend to each other.

`_estimate_decode_perf` directly below the code already uses the full context for both its FLOPs and its KV read term, so the prefill path is the outlier here rather than a deliberate simplification.

Mixed prefill+decode batches feed the same estimator and are affected too. ScheduleBatch.mix_with_running appends each running request as extend_len = 1 with prefix_len set to its current context length, but that 1 only nudges the batch-wide token count, and the request's actual context never enters the estimate.

## Modifications

Accumulate the token-context product per request, using the `prefix_lens` the batch already carries:

```
context_product = sum(
    c * p + c * (c + 1) / 2.0
    for c, p in zip(batch.extend_lens, batch.prefix_lens)
)
```

c * p covers each new token against every token already in the request's KV cache. c * (c + 1) / 2 covers the causal pairs within the chunk itself.

This PR deliberately omits the `prefix_lens` fallback and the `c <= 0` guard proposed in #34298. The two lists are written together on every code path that touches them (`prepare_for_extend`, `mix_with_running`, `prepare_encoder_info_extend`), so they stay index-aligned, and `c == 0` already contributes zero to the sum.

tokens, read_bytes and write_bytes are unchanged.

Note for reviewers: this raises the absolute value of sglang:estimated_flops_per_gpu_total, potentially by one to two orders of magnitude at long context. Any alerting thresholds calibrated against the current (incorrect) values will need revisiting.

Left open in #34298: 
- @fzyzcjy — one open question on this: read_bytes has no prefix-dependent term, so prefill reports no KV-cache read traffic for a cached prefix. Adding one needs a call on whether estimated_read_bytes_per_gpu_total is meant to represent logical traffic or actual HBM traffic, since the two differ a lot once kernel tiling and reuse are involved.
Update: implemented logical fix as noted.
- The MLA / MoE / sparse-attention constants need architecture-specific modelling.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable — observability only

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The estimator runs on the logging path once per prefill batch; the change replaces one sum over a list of ints with one generator over zip of two lists whose length is the batch's request count.
