title: [Diffusion] Fix H3 swap PEFT SwiGLU lora_B halves when loading FFN Lora
author: niehen6174
body:
## Motivation

MiniMax-H3 fuses SwiGLU `gate` / `up` into one `(28672, 5376)` matrix. The two official layouts store that fused tensor with opposite row order:
- diffusers / LightX2V: `ff.net.0.proj` = `[up; gate]`
- sglang native: `mlp.fc1` = `[gate; up]`

Loading a LightX2V LoRA already renames `ff.net.0.proj` → `mlp.fc1`, but does not swap `lora_B` rows. Shapes match and nothing errors, so the FFN adapter is applied with the two halves reversed. Attention LoRA is unaffected.

The two layouts are defined by the `forward` implementations:

diffusers [`SwiGLU`](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/v0.37.0/src/diffusers/models/activations.py#L143-L146) (`ff.net.0.proj`):

```python
hidden_states, gate = hidden_states.chunk(2, dim=-1)
return hidden_states * self.activation(gate)   # [up; gate]
```

sglang [`_silu_mul`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/minimax_h3.py#L271-L272) (`mlp.fc1`):

```python
gate, up = hidden.chunk(2, dim=-1)
return F.silu(gate) * up                       # [gate; up]
```

The MiniMax-H3 repo ships the same DiT twice, which confirms the row-order mismatch is in the official weights, not a sglang-only convention:
- `FL2VA/transformer/` → `blocks.N.mlp.fc1.weight` (what sglang loads)
- `transformer/` → `transformer_blocks.N.ff.net.0.proj.weight` (what LightX2V trains against)

| tensor | as-is | after swapping the two 14336-row halves |
|---|---|---|
| fused FFN `fc1` / `ff.net.0.proj` (52 / 52 blocks) | 0 exact | **52 / 52 exact** |
| `fc2` / `ff.net.2` | exact | n/a |

They are the same model: native fused `qkv_proj` is bit-identical to diffusers `to_q/to_k/to_v` after the documented per-head `[q,k,v]` pack.

LightX2V's own two exports of the same adapter repeat the same signature:

| | as-is | swapped |
|---|---|---|
| `fc1` `lora_A` (50 / 50) | exact | n/a |
| `fc1` `lora_B` (50 / 50) | 0 exact | **50 / 50 exact** |
| `fc2` `lora_B` (50 / 50) | exact | n/a |

`lora_A` lives on the input side, so it does not need a row swap.

## Modifications

Swap the two 14336-row halves of `lora_B` only on the `ff.net.0.proj.lora_B` → `mlp.fc1.lora_B` path in `load_lora_adapter`.
Leave `lora_A` and `fc2` unchanged. Native fused `mlp.fc1` keys and other models' `ff.net.0.proj` (e.g. Flux) do not match both sides of the guard, so they are not rewritten.

## Accuracy Tests

Prompt: `A cat walking on a sunny beach, gentle waves.` Config: MiniMax-H3 FL2VA + `lightx2v/Minimax-h3-Turbo`
(`minimax_h3_fl2v_turbo_4step_v0.1.safetensors`), 1344×768 / 5 s, `seed=1101`, `lora_scale=0.0625`, `flow_shift=12`, `audio_flow_shift=3`, one H200. Same LoRA, 4-step and 8-step, before vs after this change.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/37ee7943-0d37-462a-96c3-fc2be88fca26



Before the fix the fur is smeared; after the fix hair, face, and eyes resolve. Audio RMS also rises (4-step 0.0063 → 0.0097, 8-step 0.0067 → 0.0129). Latency and peak memory are unchanged.

title: [misc] Rename shared-read boundary to shared-read ends and fix wrapper delegation
author: hnyls2002
body:
Follow-up to #34916. Three things: name the read-end concept after what it is, make wrapper backends answer for the child that actually reads, and cut the fence tests down to what they guard.

### `SharedReadBoundary` -> `SharedReadEnds`

The values now say where they sit relative to the two init hooks, instead of leaving the reader to infer it:

```python
PRE_REPLAY  = auto()  # After the init_forward_metadata_out_graph
IN_REPLAY   = auto()  # After the init_forward_metadata_in_graph
POST_REPLAY = auto()  # Metadata snapshot not implemented
UNKNOWN     = auto()  # not audited -> coarse whole-forward fence
```

`POST_REPLAY` is worth calling out: it is not a design state, it marks a backend whose metadata snapshot is incomplete. Naming it that way is what makes the remaining users of it auditable.

Also `shared_read_boundary()` -> `shared_read_ends()`, `_resolve_shared_read_boundary` -> `_resolve_shared_read_ends`, and the local in the resolver -> `declared` (the backend's declaration, as distinct from the resolved point the function returns).

### Wrapper backends now delegate the declaration

A wrapper drives one or more child backends but inherited the base declaration and answered for itself. Fixed for all four, via a new `SharedReadEnds.max_of` (the record must cover every child, so the latest end wins):

| wrapper | |
|---|---|
| `HybridAttnBackend` | delegates to `_select_backend(mode)` |
| `TboAttnBackend` | max over primary + children |
| `HybridLinearAttnBackend` | max over `attn_backend_list` |
| `MiniMaxHybridAttnBackend` | max over sparse + dense |

This is a real fence bug wherever a wrapped child overrides the default. Concretely, `TboAttnBackend` wrapping `DeepseekV4AttnBackend`: the child declares `POST_REPLAY` for non-DSPARK target verify, the wrapper reported `IN_REPLAY`, so the scheduler was released while the child was still reading across graph segments.

Behavior is otherwise unchanged -- children that inherit the default all report `IN_REPLAY`, so the aggregate matches what the wrapper returned before.

### Fence tests: 136 -> 80 lines

Dropped the `execute()` harness (fake backend, `ShapeKey`, `PPProxyTensors`, `load_batch`, `device_module`) and the three cases built on it -- ~60 lines guarding six lines of `if` wiring. What is left tests the two methods directly: a five-row table over the resolver, and both branches of `_publish_read_done`.

The backend stub is now `create_autospec(AttentionBackend, instance=True)` rather than a `SimpleNamespace`. A hand-rolled stub supplies whatever name the caller asks for, so a renamed method leaves a stale call site in the runner green in CI and broken at runtime; spec'd against the real ABC it fails in the test.

Not covered anymore: that the pre-replay record lands before `backend.replay()`. That ordering assertion was the only thing needing the full harness.

### Not in this PR

- The default stays `IN_REPLAY`. Moving a backend to `PRE_REPLAY` is a per-backend optimization worth one audit each, not a global flip.
- `_resolve_shared_read_ends` still answers two questions (does this phase own the publish, and where do the reads end). Splitting the ownership predicate out is the next step.
- The `IN_REPLAY -> PRE_REPLAY` fallback demotes to a point earlier than the declared end; `POST_REPLAY` is the sound direction. Left as a TODO in code -- it is only reachable under `--debug-cuda-graph` and on platforms without external-event support, where the barrier is off anyway.

title: [diffusion] fix: make MiniMax-H3 AdaLN cache rebuild transactional
author: Dayuxiaoshui
body:
## Motivation

MiniMax-H3 can rebuild AdaLN outputs from checkpoint weights on demand and memoize the resulting timestep plans across requests. Two cache bookkeeping paths could leave the cache inconsistent:

1. When a new request exceeded `max_plans`, the cache cleared all resident plans but rebuilt only the plans that had been missing before the clear. If the request also reused an existing plan, that plan disappeared from the slab and its later lookup failed during denoising.
2. A plan was added to the host-side `_slots` index before all checkpoint reads and projections completed. If rebuilding raised midway, a retry treated the incomplete plan as a cache hit, skipped rebuilding it, and then failed because its zero `plan_lengths` entry remained invisible to lookup.

The cache also accepted non-positive plan capacities, which could create degenerate slabs and fail later with less actionable errors.

## Modifications

- Rebuild every plan required by the current request after a capacity reset, including plans that were cache hits before the reset.
- Validate the request's plan count and width before clearing resident cache metadata, so an invalid request does not destroy a usable cache.
- Keep new slot assignments in a pending host-side map while checkpoint weights are read and projected.
- Publish `_slots` only after every layer has been written and the corresponding `plan_lengths` entries have been activated. A failed rebuild therefore leaves the incomplete slots invisible and allows a later request to retry.
- Reject non-positive `max_plans` and `max_plan_width` values at cache construction time.

## Accuracy Tests

The change only updates cache admission and metadata publication. It does not change timestep embeddings, checkpoint reads, tensor-parallel sharding, GEMM shapes, collectives, or cached output tensors.

- Forced the capacity-reset path with a request containing both a previously resident plan and a new plan. All plans required by the request remained available to lookup after rebuilding.
- Checked 470,367,744 AdaLN output elements against resident `adaln_proj` projections at both TP1 and TP2: zero mismatches.
- Compared online-rebuild and resident-weight end-to-end outputs at TP1 and TP2. For both cold and cached cases, the online-rebuild MP4 MD5 matched the corresponding resident-weight run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. This is a correctness-only cache bookkeeping change. The normal successful rebuild path performs the same checkpoint reads, projections, and collectives as before.

title: [Fix] Correct dense FP8 Marlin bias ordering
author: qeternity
body:
## Motivation

Dense FP8 Marlin preparation permuted the bias into the Marlin tile layout. However, the dense wrapper does not pass bias into the Marlin GEMM; it adds bias after the kernel returns. The post-GEMM addition therefore requires the original logical output-channel order. The old behavior produces incorrect biased projections, including the Qwen2 QKV projection.

title: Fix sconv track refresh on graph capture
author: ispobock
body:
## Motivation

Serving Inkling with MTP crashes at startup while capturing the draft-extend CUDA graph, with `forward_batch.extend_prefix_lens` being `None` in `_refresh_track_conv_indices`. Fixes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/35039.

The read has been there since https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33023, but it was unreachable: a batch without tracking metadata returned early. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34043 changed the graph path to fill inert track buffers and continue, so that this capture still launches the track scatter, and that made the read reachable for the first time. Only `prefill_cuda_graph_runner` populates `extend_prefix_lens`; a capture batch is constructed directly instead of through `ForwardBatch.init_new`, and none of the speculative capture runners fill it, so on the EAGLE draft-extend capture it is `None`.

The substitution is gated on `on_graph_path` rather than on `extend_prefix_lens is None` alone. A live batch always carries prefix lengths, so a `None` outside capture means something is genuinely wrong and should still raise rather than track against an invented prefix. Only DRAFT_EXTEND_V2 reaches this function; DSpark and DFlash run target-verify, which does not call it.

## Accuracy

Inkling with MTP and CUDA graphs enabled (`disable_cuda_graph=False`), one GPU, `--speculative-num-steps 2 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 3 --enable-multi-layer-eagle --speculative-use-rejection-sampling`:

```
                                              starts   crash   /generate   accept len
main                                            no      crash      -            -
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34043 sconv hunk reverted                     yes       0        200      1.73 / 2.08
guard on `extend_prefix_lens is None`          yes       0        200      1.82 / 1.98
guard on the inert-fill branch                  no      crash      -            -
this PR (`None` and `on_graph_path`)           yes       0        200      1.73 / 1.85
```

The revert row identifies the regression; it is not a candidate fix, since https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34043 fixes a real state corruption. The third row works but relaxes the invariant: any future live path with a missing prefix would silently track against zeros. The fourth row is instructive and is why the guard is not keyed on "we just filled the inert buffers" — the inert fill writes `mamba_track_mask` back onto the batch, and a capture reuses one `ForwardBatch` across warmup and capture, so the second call takes the other branch.

A per-commit guard for MTP under the unified radix cache is tracked in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/34899 and is blocked on this fix.

title: [XPU][Fix] Pack device-pointer tables as uint64 to avoid 64-bit address overflow
author: dayanandav
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #35047.

Several kernels pass base addresses to the device in a side table and bitcast each entry back to a pointer (`tl.load(meta_ptr + i).to(tl.pointer_type(...))`). Those tables were built with `dtype=torch.int64`, which cannot hold an address `>= 2**63`: `torch.tensor()` unpacks Python ints through `long long`, so the build raises

```
ValueError: Overflow when unpacking long long
```

on the host, before any kernel is launched. Note this is device-independent — the unpacking happens while building the tensor, so even a `device="cpu"` table raises. Intel XPU (Level Zero / SYCL USM) device addresses have the top bit set, e.g. `0xffff85abd4e00000`, so every Mamba/GDN model hits this in conv-state scatter and `MambaPool` slot maintenance. CUDA/HIP VAs stay in the low canonical half, which is the only reason `int64` looks lossless there.

## Modifications

- New `sglang.kernels.ops.memory.ptr_table.make_ptr_table(rows, device)`: builds the table as `uint64` (the only dtype that accepts a full 64-bit address) and `view`s it back to `int64`. `view` moves no bits, so kernels keep their existing signed element type — no kernel-side change. Companion columns (strides, element counts, block offsets) are non-negative, so their bits are unchanged too.
- Route the two affected table builders through it: `_conv_multi_build_meta` (`mamba_state_scatter_triton.py`) and `build_conv_slot_descriptor` (`mem_cache/mamba_slot_fused.py`). Both build device-resident tables from `data_ptr()` values, so both overflow on XPU.
- `MambaPool`: replace three hardcoded `device="cuda"` allocations with the pool's own device.

## Tests

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/memory/test_ptr_table.py` (new): covers the full `[0, 2**64)` address range, and asserts both call sites' tables round-trip a spoofed top-bit-set `data_ptr()` while leaving companion columns identical to a real-address build. It spoofs the address because a backend whose VAs stay `< 2**47` can never catch this regression — the guard has to run on any runner.
- `test_mamba_slot_fused.py` and `test_mamba_state_scatter_triton.py` now select the accelerator via `get_device()` instead of hardcoding CUDA. Added coverage for `fused_conv_window_scatter_multi` (single-type, multi-type, and with the second/track index set), which had no test on any backend and is the kernel most exposed to the packing.
- Registered the touched tests on the XPU suites so these paths actually run there: `stage-b-test-1-gpu-xpu` for `test_ptr_table.py`, `test_mamba_state_scatter_triton.py`, `test_mamba_slot_fused.py` and `test_mamba_unittest.py`; `nightly-xpu-2-gpu` for `test_mamba2_mixer.py`, which asserts `NUM_GPUS` rather than skipping and so needs the 2-GPU pool.

Verified on Intel Arc Pro B60 (torch 2.13.0+xpu): the new cases fail with the reported `ValueError` when `make_ptr_table` is reverted to `int64`, and all 27 tests (+16 subtests) pass with the fix. `est_time` values are measured, not estimated. `pre-commit run --all-files` is clean.

title: [Fix] Select custom all-reduce v2 by topology capability

## Motivation

This fixes a regression introduced by #32541. Before that PR, custom all-reduce v2 was enabled by default and eligible TP16 groups reached the topology and allocator capability check. The added TP2-8-specific multinode policy disabled `SGLANG_OPT_USE_CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_V2` for TP16 before capability detection, forcing an otherwise eligible configuration to fall back.

title: docs: fix Qwen3.8-27B mamba ratio calculator for speculative decoding
author: Jiminator
body:
The Qwen3.8-27B mamba ratio calculator (`docs/src/snippets/_qwen38_mamba_ratio_calculator.jsx`) was derived from the Kimi K3 one but lost four behaviours along the way, so it emitted the wrong `--mamba-full-memory-ratio` and `--max-mamba-cache-size` for **every** speculative configuration. The K3 sibling is correct on all four — this brings Qwen3.8 back in line with it.

### The four bugs

**1. ReplaySSM ignored.** `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec` moves the `D` intermediate SSM states off the per-request slot budget onto a fixed ring, so `D` is 0 even with spec on. The calculator counted `D=4`, emitting `r=2.08` where the truth is `1.04` — a 2x over-provision of the state pool, and the surplus comes straight out of KV.

**2. DSPARK draft count.** DSPARK never emits `--speculative-num-draft-tokens`; its verify window is `--speculative-dspark-block-size` (gamma) + 1, auto-inferred from the draft checkpoint when omitted. `Number(null) || 4` therefore returned **4** where the truth is **8**, emitting `r=2.08` against `2.60` and under-provisioning.

> 1 and 2 err in **opposite directions**, which is why no single spot-check surfaced them.

**3. The pin double-counted D.** The engine divides the main state pool by `S` alone — `kv_cache_configurator.py`, `mamba_cap = max_mamba_cache_size // ratio` with `ratio = _calculate_mamba_ratio() = S` — and sizes the spec intermediate buffer separately from `D`. So the pin is `C * S`, not `C * (S + D)`.

**4. `S` was hardcoded 5/4/3/1**, ignoring `SGLANG_OPT_MAMBA_SKIP_DECODE_LOCK` (base 3 -> 2) and a disabled overlap scheduler / `--pp-size > 1` (ping-pong 2 -> 1). Replaced with the same expression the K3 calculator uses. `derive()` now takes `env`, matching K3's signature.

### Measured impact

RTX 5090, NVFP4 W4A4 + fp8 KV, radix cache on, 8192 ISL / 1024 OSL, concurrency 1:

| config | old r | correct r | effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| EAGLE (ReplaySSM) | 2.08 | **1.04** | KV pool 19,469 -> 11,992 tokens (**-38%**) |
| DSPARK | 2.08 | **3.12** | under-provisions the state pool |
| no-spec | 1.04 | 1.04 | unaffected |

At bs=1 both still served with identical latency/throughput, so nothing published was broken at the documented operating point — but the KV loss bites at longer context or above concurrency 1.

### Verification

The patched `derive()` reproduces the ratio actually used in each of the 10 servable RTX 5090 configurations (3 spec x 2 tiers x 2 state dtypes, minus 2 unachievable), where the old code was wrong for every speculative one. Also checked: `no_buffer` -> S=3, radix-off -> S=1, skip-lock and overlap-off each drop one slot, and an explicit `--speculative-dspark-block-size 7` -> D=8.

title: [Fix] Support Kimi-K3 ModelOpt mixed NVFP4/FP8 checkpoint
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

The official [nvidia/Kimi-K3-NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Kimi-K3-NVFP4) checkpoint is a ModelOpt mixed-precision checkpoint:

- routed MoE experts use NVFP4 with SiTU (`beta=4`, `linear_beta=25`);
- supported attention projections use weight-only `FP8_PB_WO` with 128x128 block scales.

Current `main` cannot serve this checkpoint with the FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE backend. It rejects gated `situ` during startup, and it does not instantiate/load the checkpoint's block-FP8 attention scales. The K3 fused-front also needs to pass its row-strided FP32 router output through the stride-aware precomputed-routing interface.

## Modifications

- Add gated `ActivationType.Situ` support to the FlashInfer TRT-LLM FP4 runner.
- Pass the model-provided SiTU coefficients as GEMM1 alpha/beta and keep the W13 up-dequant scale inside the SiTU activation, avoiding double application through `g1_scale_c`.
- Route K3 SiTU fused-front output through SGLang's stride-aware FP32 precomputed-routing path while keeping fused-front enabled.
- Dispatch ModelOpt `FP8_PB_WO` layers to SGLang's native serialized block-FP8 linear method with dynamic activation quantization and 128x128 weight blocks.
- Load ModelOpt's logical 4-D block scales into SGLang's 2-D `weight_scale_inv` parameters, including fused MLA projections and TP-sharded KDA projections.
- Dequantize the FP8 MLA `kv_b` weight before K3's post-load absorption.
- Dequantize only K3's small `f_a`/`f_b`/`b` projections once after loading into BF16 buffers for the existing fused tiny-GEMM path; the main KDA projections remain on native block-FP8 GEMMs.
- Compile the KDA recompute kernel for the BF16 activation/parameter dtype rather than the serialized FP8 weight dtype.
- Add regression coverage for the SiTU scale contract, `FP8_PB_WO` dispatch, block-scale dequantization, and the fused B/F_a path.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated the released checkpoint on 8x GB300 with TP8:

- GSM8K-200: **197/200 = 0.985**
- `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm`
- `trtllm_mla` prefill and decode attention backends
- fused-front enabled
- K3 all-reduce fusion enabled
- prefill CUDA Graph enabled; decode CUDA Graph enabled for batch sizes 1/2/4
- concurrency 4
- no fused-front-disable environment workaround

Both raw completion and chat-completion smoke tests produced coherent, correct answers before the evaluation.

The validation used the final patch contents in this PR. The branch was then rebased onto `eafbe2cb6f` from `main`; the intervening upstream commits do not touch this PR's files.

Targeted checks:

- 13/13 ModelOpt NVFP4 SiTU scale tests passed.
- The ModelOpt mixed `FP8_PB_WO` dispatch test passed.
- The K3 B/F_a fused-path tests passed, including CUDA Graph replay and block-FP8 dequantization.
- Black, Python 3.12 `py_compile`, and `git diff --check` passed on the changed files.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not measured. This PR is a correctness and checkpoint-compatibility change.

title: [AMD] Fix DSV4 unified attention sink TP slice
author: AMD-yanfeiwang
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4 stores `attn_sink` as a global per-head parameter. The non-unified path slices it by attention-TP rank, but the unified-KV branch passed the global tensor directly. Unified prefill truncated it to the first `H` entries and unified decode indexed from head zero, so every nonzero attention-TP rank consumed rank 0's sink values.

This affects pure TP configurations such as TP8/DP1. Baseline/candidate token comparisons cannot detect it when both arms share the same routing bug.

## Modifications

- Pass the existing TP-local sink slice to the unified backend.
- Strip the FlashMLA-only zero padding so the unified backend receives exactly `[n_local_heads]` values.
- Add a real `MQALayer.forward` regression for TP8 ranks 0, 3, and 7 with distinct per-head sink values.

## Accuracy Tests

The bug predates this PR: `attn_sink=self.attn_sink` entered upstream main with unified-KV support in `f2bcdb050` (#27380). It is present in this PR's base (`92b1d382c`) and was still present in upstream main `4b06f917c` when rechecked.

MI355X, ROCm 7.2.26015, real DeepSeek-V4-Pro checkpoint sink (`layers.0.attn.attn_sink`), TP rank 3 / heads 48-63:

- Production OPUS prefill vs independent FP32 PyTorch softmax-plus-sink reference: max abs `0.0009765625`, mean abs `5.66e-05`, passed `atol=rtol=0.02`.
- Production Triton decode vs the same reference: max abs `0.001953125`, mean abs `6.20e-05`, passed `atol=rtol=0.02`.
- Old rank-0 sink slice negative control: prefill max abs `0.0341796875`, decode max abs `0.0458984375`; both failed the same tolerance.

Full DeepSeek-V4-Pro TP8 GSM8K (`unified_kv_triton`, FP4 experts, 1,319 questions, 8-shot, greedy, 512 max tokens, 32 clients):

- Base `92b1d382c`, run 1: `1252/1319 = 94.9204%`.
- Base `92b1d382c`, repeat: `1259/1319 = 95.4511%`.
- Fix `3b0dfaace`: `1257/1319 = 95.2995%`.
- Fix vs base run 1: `+5` questions (`+0.3791` percentage points), exact paired McNemar `p=0.424`.
- Fix vs base repeat: `-2` questions (`-0.1516` percentage points), exact paired McNemar `p=0.856`.
- The fix result is inside the base repeat range; therefore GSM8K establishes no regression but does **not** establish an attributable score improvement. The kernel-level reference remains the direct correctness proof.

Focused tests in the official ROCm MI355X image:

- Sink regression plus adjacent DeepSeek-V4 model tests: `6 passed`, `5 subtests passed`.
- Ruff format/check, `py_compile`, and `git diff --check` passed.

## Checklist

- [x] Add nonzero-rank TP regression coverage.
- [x] Validate production prefill and decode kernels against an independent reference.
- [x] Keep the production change scoped to sink routing.
- [ ] Run repository CI.

title: [diffusion] Fix width/height silently dropped on multipart /v1/videos requests
author: zetyquickly
body:
## Summary
- `create_video()` declares explicit `Form(...)` parameters for `seconds`, `size`, `fps`, `num_frames`, `seed`, etc., but not for `width`/`height`. Because those two names are already declared fields on `VideoGenerationsRequest`, the generic "extra form field" fallback explicitly excludes already-declared fields, so a multipart request's `width`/`height` are never read — the pipeline's `SamplingParams` subclass default silently wins instead.
- Fix: add `width`/`height` as explicit `Form(None)` parameters, threaded through the same `form_value()` precedence already used for `fps`/`num_frames`.
- Not model-specific: any multipart `/v1/videos` request with explicit `width`/`height` hits this, for any model (surfaced here while building an image-to-video client against LTX-2.5, #35107). The JSON body path was already unaffected.

## Test plan
- [x] Before: multipart request for `width=704&height=512` produced a `960x544` video (LTX25SamplingParams' hardcoded default), confirmed via `ffprobe` on the actual output.
- [x] After: same request produces `704x512` output, confirmed via `ffprobe`.
- [x] JSON body path re-verified unaffected (worked before and after).

title: [AMD] Fix DSV4 FP4 dequant path for AITER on ROCm
author: yuzhouo7
body:
## Motivation

On ROCm with AITER enabled, `SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_DEQUANT=1` is silently ignored
for routed FP4 expert weights. `Fp8MoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading_block_quant()`
returns through the native AITER FP4 branch before checking
`dequant_fp4_to_fp8`. The server later fails with:

```text
RuntimeError: Unsupported kernel config for moe heuristic dispatch
```

This is a ROCm/AITER weight-processing bug. It is distinct from
[#32333](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32333), which changes
backend selection in `get_quant_method`.

Fixes #35122

## Modifications

- Skip the native AITER FP4 early return when dequantization is requested.
- Convert routed FP4 experts to block FP8.
- Normalize `e4m3fn` to native gfx942/gfx950 `e4m3fnuz`.
- Apply the `(16, 16)` weight shuffle only when the resolved MoE runner is
  AITER; Triton receives unshuffled weights.

The existing CUDA dequantization and DeepGEMM `ue8m0` path is unchanged. The
default ROCm path with the flag unset is also unchanged.

**Review update (2026-09-17):** Renamed the helper to `_dequantize_aiter_fp4_experts`, removed the added unit test as requested, and merged upstream `main` at `c525ed8f0` without conflicts.

## Accuracy Tests

Tested on 8x MI308X (gfx942), TP8, the original DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 FP4
checkpoint, with `SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_DEQUANT=1` and
`--moe-runner-backend auto`.

| Configuration | Result |
|---|---|
| v0.5.17, no patch | Does not start; fails with the dispatch error above |
| v0.5.17, this patch | Starts; CUDA graph capture is clean on all 8 ranks; no OOM |
| GSM8K, n=200 | **187/200 = 93.5%**, 0 errors |
| Runner guard, 43 layers x 8 ranks | **344/344** selected AITER shuffle; 0 false/ambiguous cases |

The results above are historical validation on v0.5.17; GPU integration and accuracy tests have not been rerun on the updated branch. Local Ruff lint, formatting, and Python syntax checks passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. This is a load-time correctness fix; no speedup is claimed.

- [x] No documentation update is required for this internal code-path fix.

title: Fix NIXL cleaner grouping for hybrid cache keys
author: yangweigbh
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #32702.

The NIXL FILE L3 cleaner must evict every physical shard of a logical cache entry atomically. `_parse_group_key()` removed only a trailing `_k`/`_v` and then a trailing TP-rank suffix, but hybrid names append their pool component after the rank (for example, `page-a_model_0_8_swa_k`), so the anchored rank match failed and one entry was split into independently evicted groups.

## Modifications

- Build the hybrid pool-name pattern from `PoolName`, ordered longest-first for overlapping names such as `swa` and `draft_swa`.
- Strip the generated hybrid component shapes (`_{pool}`, K/V, indexed, Mamba temporal, and Mamba convolution suffixes) before applying the existing K/V and TP-rank parsing.
- Add CPU regression coverage for every component shape and for `_tick()` deleting legacy K/V files, hybrid components, and TP ranks as one logical group.

For example, `page-a_model_0_8_swa_k` previously grouped as `page-a_model_0_8_swa`; it now groups as `page-a_model`, together with the entry's other ranks and components.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: this changes only background disk-eviction grouping and does not modify cache contents, transfer logic, or model computation.

Focused CPU unit test: **9 passed, 8 subtests passed**. The test was run in a dependency-light Python 3.10 harness because this macOS checkout cannot install SGLang's CUDA-only runtime dependencies. Cleaner module coverage from the focused test is **76%**.

title: fix(unified-memory): four boot/correctness fixes on the hybrid model paths
author: caihuali95
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

Four independent bugs on the hybrid model paths, each of which either
prevents a model from booting or silently degrades behaviour. They are 
grouped here because they are all small, self-contained fixes to the same 
subsystem, each with its own regression test.

1. **A model that is both mambaish and hybrid-SWA cannot boot on
   `--attention-backend triton`.** `TritonAttnBackend.__init__` resolves
   `v_head_dim` from one of three branches; the middle one calls
   `token_to_kv_pool.get_v_head_dim()`, which `SWAKVPool` never implemented:

       AttributeError: 'SWAKVPool' object has no attribute 'get_v_head_dim'

   The branch is taken when the model is mambaish **and** its SWA and full
   value head dims match (the asymmetric case is handled earlier from
   `model_config`). Mamba hybrids own the method via `HybridLinearKVPool`, and
   a pure hybrid-SWA model is not mambaish so the branch never fires — which
   is why nothing hit it until a family that is both was served. This is a
   static-pool bug, not a unified one.

2. **Inkling's SConv JIT kernels reject a non-contiguous conv-state view.**
   Every conv-state matcher used the bare `TensorMatcher` form, whose default
   is a hard `is_contiguous()` check, while the kernel bodies are already
   stride-aware (they index via `cache.stride(0)/stride(1)` and only need the
   channel dim contiguous). The matcher was strictly stronger than the
   kernels' real contract.
   
3. **The unified free path performed two host syncs**, either of which parks
   the scheduler thread behind the in-flight forward: `t[idx] = -1` tombstone
   scatters (torch materialises `-1` on CPU and issues a host-blocking
   pageable H2D copy) and `torch.unique` recovering page ids from freed token
   ids (data-dependent output shape forces a D2H count read).
 
 4. **SWA locked-full recovery crashes the scheduler under the unified pool.**
   `SWAComponent`'s `RecoverSWAWithLockedFull` handler assumed the static
   allocator's shape and reached for a mapping tensor the unified SWA
   composite does not have. Declining the recovery is not an option: the
   insert path's `new_prefix_len <= len(new_indices)` assert makes a skipped
   recovery a correctness error rather than a degradation.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

One commit per fix, each with its regression test.

- **`get_v_head_dim` on the SWA pool** — `swa_memory_pool.py`: return the
  full side's value head dim, mirroring `HybridLinearKVPool`. Read through the
  full sub-pool at its own `start_layer`, not layer 0, which need not be a
  full-attention layer (and keeps pipeline parallelism correct).
  `UnifiedSWAKVPool` inherits it.

- **Strided conv-state** — seven matchers across six
  `kernels/jit/csrc/inkling/*.cuh` files relax to `.with_strides({-1, -1, 1})`:
  slot/window strides wildcarded, channel stride pinned to 1, which is the
  only contract the vectorized state loads rely on. Contiguous callers verify
  as before.

- **Host-sync-free free path** — `multi_ended_allocator.py`: tombstone writes
  become `index_fill_`; `free_segment` on the base allocator and both
  composites derives page representatives from `start_pos` by stride math
  (the rule `allocator/paged.py` already uses) instead of `torch.unique`; a
  second group buffer carries those representatives through `free_group_end`,
  since concatenating raw tokens destroys the per-segment shape. Plain
  `free()` keeps `torch.unique` — without a position there is nothing to
  derive from. `environ.py`: drop the now-unreachable
  `SGLANG_SORT_FREE_LIST_AFTER_MERGE` knob.

- **SWA locked-full recovery** — `swa_component.py`: the handler branches once
  on the composite type. The unified branch transfers ownership of the
  incoming ids' SWA pages onto the kept ids (a v2p rebind, no data copy), then
  frees through the composite, whose tombstone filter releases only the full
  side; pages are paired by first occurrence, never `torch.unique`, which
  sorts by id value and would pair unrelated pages. The static branch keeps
  its recipe with the tombstone routed through `set_full_to_swa_mapping`
  rather than indexing the mapping tensor.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

GSM8K, `n=200` per cell, unified vs. static pool comparisons.

| Model | mean Δ | median Δ | worst | best |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (dense) | +0.06 pt | +0.00 pt | −0.5 | +1.0 |
| Qwen3.5-9B (hybrid GDN) | +0.06 pt | +0.00 pt | −1.0 | +1.5 |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B (KDA + MLA) | +0.00 pt | +0.00 pt | −1.5 | +1.5 |
| Falcon-H1-7B-Instruct (Mamba) | +0.06 pt | +0.25 pt | −2.0 | +2.0 |
| gpt-oss-20b (hybrid SWA) | −0.31 pt | −0.50 pt | −6.5 | +6.0 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

`bench_serving`, unified vs. static pool. Two workloads:
`heavy-decode` (512 in / 4096 out, 100 prompts, concurrency 128) and
`radix-retract` (shared-prefix dataset: one group of 192 requests sharing a
4096-token system prompt, 2048 out, concurrency 192 — sized to force
`retract_decode`). Product configuration (`radix` + cuda graph on + page
size 256; Kimi at its pinned `ps=1`). 

TPOT, unified relative to static (negative = unified faster):

| Model | overlap schedule (default) | normal schedule (diagnostic) |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-9B (GDN) | **+0.4 %** | +1.8 % |
| gpt-oss-20b (SWA) | **−0.7 %** | +2.4 % |
| Falcon-H1-7B (Mamba) | **−0.4 %** | +2.2 % |
| Kimi-Linear-48B (KDA+MLA) | n/a (pinned to normal) | +1.7 % |

title: [Bugfix] Fix int32 destination offset overflow in CUTLASS MoE pre-reorder
author: cognaiger9
body: ## Motivation `pre_reorder_triton_kernel_for_cutlass_moe` loads `dst_idx` from the `src2dst` mapping as an `int32` and uses it to calculate the destination address: ```python dst_ptr_offs + dst_idx * hidden_size ``` Because `dst_idx` is 32-bit, `dst_idx * hidden_size` can overflow signed 32-bit arithmetic when the destination activation buffer contains more than `2**31` elements. For example, with `hidden_size = 6144`, the first overflowing destination row is: ```text ceil(2**31 / 6144) = 349,526 ``` This is reachable during large expert-parallel prefill workloads. The wrapped offset can cause a CUDA illegal memory access or write to an incorrect GPU address. ## Modifications Promote `dst_idx` to `tl.int64` immediately after loading it: ```python dst_idx = tl.load(token_src2dst_ptr + idx).to(tl.int64) ``` This ensures that the multiplication by `hidden_size` and the destination pointer offset are evaluated using 64-bit arithmetic. The `src2dst` mapping remains `int32`; only the address calculation is widened. ## Accuracy Tests The change only affects destination address arithmetic. Outputs below the signed 32-bit offset boundary remain unchanged. The overflow boundary can be validated with an FP8 destination buffer using: - `hidden_size = 6144` - `dst_idx = 349,526` - A destination element offset greater than `2**31` - One BF16 input row converted and written to the selected FP8 row Expected behavior: - Before the fix: CUDA illegal memory access or an incorrect destination write. - After the fix: the selected destination row matches the FP8-converted input row. Large-offset validation requires a CUDA GPU with enough memory for a contiguous allocation larger than 2 GiB. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not benchmarked. The change adds one scalar `int32`-to-`int64` conversion for each valid routed destination. It does not change the number of loads, stores, kernel launches, or transferred elements. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Documentation changes are not required for this internal kernel fix. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #32833006827](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32833006827) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32833007031](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32833007031) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): :x: [Run #32833006686](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32833006686)

title: fix(kernel) Fix Helion small-token prefill bug
author: ethche
body:
## Motivation

Fix shape handling in the wrapper for Helion KDA for short prefill requests. Also clearly reject non power of 2 head dim in decode.

## Modifications

The Helion KDA backend had three issues.
- For short prefill, the prefill Q/K/V may contain only the active tokens while gate and beta remain padded to a CUDA-graph bucket. Deriving the token count from the padded gate tensor caused invalid reshapes for short prompts.
- Edge case: If the first prefill request had `T=1`, PyTorch could specialize size-one dimensions in the generated Helion trace. This issue only occurs if the first prefill is `T = 1`, `T > 1` is fine.
- Decode used padded `hl.arange` lanes without masks when the key or value dimension was not a power of two.

We made the following changes.
- Validate that gate and beta cover every Q token, then trim their padded rows at the public Helion prefill boundary. This keeps direct callers consistent with the Triton `chunk_kda` contract.
- Route only `T=1` prefill through Triton, preventing a size-one trace from poisoning later Helion shapes. The normal `T>1` Helion path is unchanged.
- Reject non power of two head dim for decode (both kimi linear and kimi k3 have head dim = 128 so they're fine).

## Accuracy Tests

A standalone sweep compared the public Helion and Triton prefill wrappers, including output, intermediate chunk states, and the mutated final state. Gate and beta padding was filled with large values so the comparison could not pass if either backend consumed padded rows. This not only confirms that Helion works now on short seqs, but that the accuracy is preserved.
- input lengths `1, 3, 7, 15, 17, 31, 51, 63, 65, 127, 255, 513, 1023, 2047, 2049, 3001, 8191, 16385`;
- fixed and two-sequence packed-varlen layouts;
- `H=32`, `H=16`, and `H=12`;
- FP32 and BF16 state.

All **216/216 cases passed** with `atol=0.02, rtol=0.02`.

| Compared value | Maximum absolute difference |
|---|---:|
| Output | 9.77e-4 |
| Intermediate state | 7.81e-3 |
| Final state | 4.02e-3 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The change does not affect performance.

title: [AMD] Fix Quark Shared Experts Fusion Gate after load-time-override Removal
author: ColinZ22
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

PR #33889 replaced process-global load-time config overrides with per-runner model-class gates and deleted `declare_load_time_override`. PR #29328 landed afterward still calling that deleted function from `QuarkConfig.__init__`, so any Quark checkpoint or online quantized checkpoint that cannot fuse shared expert(s) due to precision mismatch now raises `ImportError` at load. This PR restores the mixed-precision shared-experts decision path through the new gate architecture instead of the deleted global-override path.

## Modifications

- `quark/quark.py`: remove `_maybe_disable_shared_experts_fusion` and its `__init__` call. Quark no longer imperatively pushes a decision; `its can_fuse_shared_expert()` reader stays as the source of truth.
- `models/deepseek_v2.py`: DeepseekV3ForCausalLM.shared_experts_fusion_disable_reason now checks `quant_config.can_fuse_shared_expert()`, matching `qwen2_moe.can_fuse_shared_expert`'s implementation. The decision flows through the per-runner gate the loader calls (`install_shared_experts_fusion_decision`) instead of the deleted global override. This covers the whole DeepSeek family (V2/V3, Kimi-K2.5, Kimi-VL, DeepSeek-VL2/OCR, dots_vlm).

## Tests

Verified on **AMD MI355X** with both native AMD Quark MXFP4 checkpoint and online NVFP4 to MXFP4 requantization
(`--quantization quark_mxfp4` introduced in PR #29328) with both quantized and excluded shared expert.

title: [Quant] Load compressed-tensors quantized lm_head instead of value-casting it
author: Jiminator
body:
## Motivation

compressed-tensors checkpoints that quantize `lm_head` (e.g. FP8 per-channel weights targeted via `re:.*lm_head`) currently load as gibberish: `CompressedTensorsConfig.get_quant_method` returns `None` for `ParallelLMHead`, so the head falls back to `UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod` — the packed fp8 weight is value-cast into a bf16 parameter and `lm_head.weight_scale` is silently dropped (`Parameter lm_head.weight_scale not found in params_dict` at load).

## Modifications

- `CompressedTensorsConfig.get_quant_method`: add a `ParallelLMHead` branch that resolves a linear scheme and returns `CompressedTensorsLinearMethod` (mirroring the existing ModelOpt handling); unquantized heads keep the current embedding default.
- New `get_lm_head_scheme`: the head is treated as quantized only when a config target names it by layer name (exact, `re:` regex, or dotted suffix) and it is not in `ignore`. Module-type targets like `Linear` are not consulted, so checkpoints following the common convention (head unquantized and unmentioned) are unaffected. The resolved target is passed through to `get_scheme_dict` so suffix matches are not re-derived by the stricter `find_matched_target`. Block-FP8 heads are rejected with a clear error (the vocab-parallel weight loader cannot shard `vocab/block_n` weight scales).
- Unit test: `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_lm_head.py` (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`).

No other changes needed: the vocab-parallel weight loader already shards `output_dim=0` params, the model loader already runs `process_weights_after_loading` on the head, and the logits path already routes through `should_apply_lm_head_quant_method`.

Known limits: models that construct `ParallelLMHead` without a `prefix` keep today's unquantized-head behavior (the empty layer name never matches a target); `update_weights_from_disk` with a quantized head is untested; speculative-decoding draft paths that borrow the target head are a separate follow-up.

## Accuracy Tests

A/B on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell with a Qwen3.8-27B mixed-precision compressed-tensors checkpoint (NVFP4 MLPs, FP8 per-channel `lm_head`), identical flags, `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 200`:

| | GSM8K | Invalid |
|---|---|---|
| main | 0.000 | 0.850 |
| this PR | 0.955 | 0.000 |

On main, greedy decoding degenerates into repetition loops on any prompt; with this PR the head loads through `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8` and the `weight_scale` warning is gone.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No impact on unquantized-head checkpoints (resolution happens once at init). A quantized head replaces a bf16 matmul with the standard fp8 linear path.

title: [AMD] Fix registered HiCache host pointer aliases
author: AMD-yanfeiwang
body:
## Motivation

Registered HiCache host allocations can have different CPU and GPU virtual addresses. This is observable on MI355X, where `hipDeviceAttributeCanUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem` is false. Passing the CPU VA to a custom kernel causes a GPU memory fault even though runtime copy APIs can still accept that address.

The affected paths include AOT/JIT HiCache transfers, Mamba transfers, HiSparse copies, and host-pool pointer tables. CPU-side storage and disaggregation metadata must continue to expose the original CPU VA.

## Modifications

- Add a target-device-aware `get_device_accessible_ptr` AOT API using `cudaHostGetDevicePointer` / `hipHostGetDevicePointer`.
- Resolve direct registered-host tensor operands at AOT and JIT kernel launch boundaries while preserving the caller's current device.
- Build CUDA/ROCm host-pool kernel pointer tables from device-accessible aliases for MHA, MLA, K-only, DSV4 paged/state, and DSA pools.
- Keep raw CPU addresses for unregister, contiguous-buffer metadata, page metadata, and storage/disaggregation consumers.
- Preserve unpinned, NPU, and MUSA pointer behavior.
- Add registered-mmap regressions for pointer domains, AOT/JIT transfers, and CUDA graph capture/replay.

## Accuracy Tests

ROCm 7.2 / MI355X (`gfx950`), Docker image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260813`:

- Fresh ROCm AOT build: passed.
- `test_hicache_page_first_write_back.py`: `15 passed`.
- `test_transfer_mamba.py`: `16 passed`.
- `test_hisparse.py`: `16 passed, 2 skipped`.
- `test_mem_pool_host.py`: `9 passed`.
- Registered-mmap post-rebase regressions: `3 passed`.
- Native HIP runtime comparison: alias matches `hipHostGetDevicePointer`; wrong-device input is rejected; current device is restored.
- Repository pre-commit hooks over the rebased PR diff: passed.

CUDA validation in `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.17-cu130` (compile-only because this host has no NVIDIA GPU):

- HiCache, Mamba, and HiSparse JIT modules compiled and loaded for SM90.
- Modified AOT `transfer.cu` and `common_extension.cc` translation units compiled for SM90.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run. This is a correctness fix for registered-host pointer address domains; it does not change kernel bodies or transfer algorithms.

title: [Fix] Transformers-fallback (GPT-NeoX) + KV pool config (DeepSeek-VL2)
author: pavansivaram
body:
## Summary

Three small fixes surfaced by consecutive downstream accuracy runs. All three are one-liners (plus comments); the first two live in the Transformers-fallback layer, the third in `ModelConfig`.

### 1. `hf_to_sglang_mapper` — map `gpt_neox.` and `embed_out.`

`GPTNeoXForCausalLM` has no native SGLang impl → falls back to `TransformersForCausalLM`. The fallback calls `AutoModel.from_config(config)`, which returns the bare `GPTNeoXModel` backbone (`embed_in`, `layers`, `final_layer_norm`) as `self.model`; `self.lm_head` is materialized separately by `CausalMixin`. Pythia / NeoX checkpoints were saved from `GPTNeoXForCausalLM.state_dict()`, so keys carry a `gpt_neox.` wrapper prefix for the backbone and a top-level `embed_out.` for the LM head. The base mapper has no rule for either, so the catch-all `""` → `"model."` fires and produces `model.gpt_neox.embed_in.weight` — which the loader can't find (`ValueError: No module or parameter named 'model.gpt_neox' ...`).

**Fix:** add two prefix rules alongside the existing `"transformer.": "model."` (GPT-2 analogue):
- `"gpt_neox.": "model."` — strip the wrapper prefix so backbone keys land under `self.model.*`.
- `"embed_out.": "lm_head."` — route the LM head to SGLang's `self.lm_head` slot.

### 2. `skip_substrs` — skip GPT-NeoX-style `.attention.bias` causal-mask buffer

Older GPT-NeoX checkpoints include a persistent causal-mask buffer named `gpt_neox.layers.N.attention.bias`. Newer transformers versions register the same buffer with `persistent=False`, so it is absent from the constructed model's tree. `self.skip_substrs` already skips GPT-2-style `.attn.bias` / `.attn.masked_bias` (attention module named `attn`), but not GPT-NeoX-style `.attention.bias` (attention module named `attention`). Result: `ValueError: No module or parameter named 'model.layers.0.attention.bias' ...`.

**Fix:** add `.attention.bias` to the skip list. The already-present `.masked_bias` catches the fill-value counterpart regardless of attention module name.

### 3. `ModelConfig.v_head_dim` — treat `0` as unset (fixes DeepSeek-VL2 non-MLA V-cache)

`deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl2-tiny`'s `language_config` sets `use_mla=False` **and** `v_head_dim=0` — the `0` is an MLA-disabled sentinel from the checkpoint's DeepseekV2-flavored config, not a real head dimension. `ModelConfig.__init__` currently substitutes `head_dim` for `v_head_dim` only when the attribute is `None`, so a `getattr` that returns `0` slips through into `self.v_head_dim`. `pool_configurator.py` then reads `model_config.v_head_dim` directly in the non-MLA branch, and per-slot V-buffers get allocated with last dim = 0. The first extend prefill fails:

```
File ".../mem_cache/memory_pool.py", line 192, in _set_kv_buffer_impl
    v_cache[indices] = v
RuntimeError: shape mismatch: value tensor of shape [432, 10, 128]
    cannot be broadcast to indexing result of shape [432, 10, 0]
```

DeepSeek-VL2 explicitly selects the standard (non-MLA) `DeepseekForCausalLM` language model when `use_mla=False` (`sglang/srt/models/deepseek_vl2.py`), which produces real V with the usual `num_kv_heads * head_dim` layout — the attention layer is correct; the pool is what's mis-sized.

**Fix:** swap the guard to `if not self.v_head_dim:` so both `None` and `0` fall back to `self.head_dim`. MLA architectures are unaffected — their architecture-specific `elif` branches later in the same block overwrite `self.v_head_dim` with the real value from the text config.

## Test plan

- [x] `pre-commit run --files <changed>` — passes locally for all three files.
- [x] `EleutherAI/pythia-12b` (TP=2, triton) — reproduces the missing-mapper failure on `main`; loads through with fix 1.
- [x] `EleutherAI/gpt-neox-20b` (TP=2, triton) — with fix 1 applied, reproduces the missing-skip failure on `main`; loads through with fix 2, warmup succeeds, first `POST /generate` returns 200.
- [x] `deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl2-tiny` (TP=1, triton, `--disable-radix-cache`, mem-fraction 0.55) — reproduces the `_set_kv_buffer_impl` shape-mismatch on `main`; with fix 3, KV cache allocates `K size = V size = 3.38 GB` (previously `V size = 0.00 GB`), text `POST /generate` returns 200 with valid tokens.

title: Fix: abort handling for dispatched requests after client disconnect
author: Dovis01
body:
## Summary

  This PR fixes an issue where a request could continue decoding after the client disconnected, wasting GPU resources and repeatedly logging:

```text
  Received output for rid=... but the state was deleted in TokenizerManager.
```

## Root Cause

When a request handler was cancelled after dispatch, TokenizerManager removed its `rid_to_state` entry immediately. The disconnect abort path checks this state before sending an AbortReq, so the abort was skipped while the request continued running in the scheduler.

 A related race also existed for chunked-prefill requests: if a request moved out of the chunked-prefill slot before its deferred abort was processed, the abort could be lost.

 ## Changes
  - Track whether each request has been dispatched to the scheduler.
  - Remove undelivered request states locally on handler failure.
  - Abort dispatched requests and retain their state until scheduler cleanup completes.
  - Deduplicate abort requests and abort metrics.
  - Preserve retry behavior when abort dispatch fails.
  - Track generated request IDs used by parallel sampling.
  - Retry deferred chunked-prefill aborts after a request moves to another scheduler queue.
  - Add regression tests for disconnect cleanup, abort deduplication, dispatch failures, parallel sampling, and chunked-prefill transitions.

## Original commits

- `f9ad78ba2471abbc9a55ff4b4b1f3fa88a798a9e`

title: [Bug][Spec] fix startup crash and reduce CUDA graph memory usage for speculative adaptive
author: Deleter-D
body:
## Motivation

Three separate problems show up when `--speculative-adaptive` is enabled:
1. **Startup crash.** `ModelRunner.max_decode_logits_rows()` sizes the shared logits buffer from the *static* `decode_num_tokens_per_req()`, but adaptive speculative decoding replays runners built for larger draft-token widths. The buffer is too small and the server fails to start. (mentioned in #30549)
2. **IMA on the first replay.** `DecodeCudaGraphRunner.capture_one_shape` looked up `on_after_cuda_graph_warmup` on `self.model_runner.attn_backend` instead of on the backend this capture actually ran against (`attn_backend` from `capture_prepare`). For the runner the `ModelRunner` owns these are the same object, but adaptive speculative decoding builds extra runners bound to their own freshly created backend while `model_runner.attn_backend` still points at the active one. Hooking the wrong backend leaves this capture's warmup-upgraded metadata (raw→full, FlashMLA scheduler meta) frozen into the graph, which produces an illegal memory access on the first replay.
3. **Redundant CUDA graph memory.** Each capture pass opened `graph_capture()` without a stream, so every pass captured on a fresh stream. The caching allocator partitions the graph pool's segments **by stream**, so each pass re-reserved the pool's MoE / DeepEP scratch instead of reusing what an earlier pass left inactive. With adaptive speculative decoding that is one pass per candidate step × three runners — tens of GB of segments that all read back `inactive`.

## Modifications
1. `max_decode_logits_rows()` now derives `num_tokens_per_req` from `max_speculative_num_draft_tokens`, so the shared logits buffer is sized for the widest adaptive graph. (Same fix as #30554.)
2. `decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:1226-1237` — resolve `post_warmup_hook` from the capture-local `attn_backend` rather than `model_runner.attn_backend`, with a comment recording why.
3. Added `get_or_create_global_graph_capture_stream()` in `runner_utils/pool.py` (a named stream lease in the `Resources` tier, alongside the existing process-wide graph memory pool) and used it as the `graph_capture(stream=...)` argument in both `DecodeCudaGraphRunner.capture` and `PrefillCudaGraphRunner.capture`. All capture passes therefore share one stream and reserve that scratch exactly once. Captures are strictly serial (`Scheduler.init_all_cuda_graphs` runs target and draft workers in turn; the adaptive controller builds one runtime state at a time), so a single shared stream is safe.

Also added a CPU unit test `test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_graph_capture_resources.py` covering both the pool and the new capture-stream lease.

## Accuracy Tests

Server launched following the cookbook:

```bash
sglang serve \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
    --tp 4 \
    --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \
    --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
    --speculative-num-steps 3 \
    --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
    --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
    --speculative-adaptive \
    --disable-flashinfer-autotune \
    --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 30000
```

Evaluated on the three datasets shown in the cookbook:

|          | GPQA Diamond | AIME25 | GSM8k |
| -------- | ------------ | ------ | ----- |
| cookbook | 88.1         | 95     | 96.13 |
| before   | 88.13        | 98.33  | 96.89 |
| after    | 88.04          | 97.29  | 96.97 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No throughput change is expected; the win is memory. With the launch command above and the default adaptive speculative decoding parameters, CUDA graph memory drops from **14.4 GB → 10.13 GB**. With my own serving config and adaptive speculative decoding parameters, it drops from **44.3 GB → 16 GB**, which frees the corresponding capacity for the KV cache.

title: fix: default Inkling to fa4 on Hopper
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

A bare `python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small-NVFP4 --trust-remote-code` dies at startup on Hopper.

The Inkling model override defaults the attention backend to `fa4` only on SM100 and to `triton` everywhere else, while `apply_inkling_prefill_cuda_graph_default` unconditionally opts Inkling into FULL prefill CUDA-graph capture. `TritonAttnBackend` cannot capture EXTEND, so capture fails with:

```
ValueError: Invalid forward mode: forward_mode=<ForwardMode.EXTEND: 1> for CUDA Graph replay.
```

Both defaults date from the original Inkling support (#31681). Users following the cookbook never hit it because the H200 recipe passes `--attention-backend fa4` explicitly: fa4 runs on SM90, so the triton fallback on Hopper was never needed.

## Modifications

- `model_overrides/inkling.py`: when every attention-backend flag is unset, default to `fa4` on SM90 and SM100 (was SM100 only) and `triton` elsewhere (SM120/GB10, ROCm), written as an inline platform branch like the other model overrides.
- `apply_inkling_prefill_cuda_graph_default`: opt into FULL only when prefill runs on fa4, i.e. an explicit `--prefill-attention-backend` / `--attention-backend` of `fa4`, or no backend flag on SM90/SM100. Otherwise the generic prefill-graph default applies, which triton captures fine.
- Net effect: Hopper now matches the cookbook (fa4 + FULL prefill graph); an explicit `--attention-backend triton` boots instead of crashing; Blackwell is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

2x H200, `thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small-NVFP4`, TP2, cookbook H200 flags without `--attention-backend` (TP2 with `--max-mamba-cache-size 1024 --max-total-tokens 1572864` instead of TP8). Probes: 5 prompts (arithmetic, factual, code, Chinese, listing) x `reasoning_effort` none/high, greedy. GSM8K: `few_shot_gsm8k`, 200 questions.

| tree | extra flags | attention / prefill graph | boot | probes | GSM8K | output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | - | triton / full | `ValueError ... EXTEND` | - | - | - |
| this PR | - | fa4 / full | OK | 10/10 | 0.840 | 2407 |
| this PR | `--attention-backend triton` | triton / breakable | OK | 10/10 | 0.850 | 1904 |

No tracebacks in any server log; GSM8K invalid rate 0 in both arms.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Startup argument resolution only. On H200 the new fa4 default is faster than the triton fallback (2407 vs 1904 output tok/s on the GSM8K run above; single runs, noisy).

title: [Fix] DCP: advertise the logical KV-event block size
author: Jiminator
body:
## Motivation

Under DCP, SGLang runs two page sizes: the configured **physical** `page_size`, and a **logical** page `page_size * dcp_size` that the allocator is built with (`mem_cache/kv_cache_configurator.py`) and that the radix tree inherits (`mem_cache/kv_cache_builder.py`). KV events are chunked by the tree's page size, so they go out at the logical width.

`/server_info`'s `kv_events` descriptor advertised the **physical** `page_size`. A KV-aware router honoring the documented contract — *"subscribers MUST hash prompts at this size"* — then hashes requests at a width no emitted block can ever match. Stores apply cleanly, every lookup misses, and the router's KV hit rate is silently **exactly 0** while all local metrics look healthy.

## Modifications

- Add `ServerArgs.kv_event_block_size` (property): `page_size * dcp_size`, the width events are actually emitted at.
- `describe_kv_events_publisher` advertises it instead of the physical `page_size`. The `page_size` field itself is unchanged — only the advertised value is corrected.
- Document that the descriptor's `dp_size` is deliberately *not* DCP-scaled: DCP shards within a rank rather than adding publishers.

No working configuration changes behavior — under DCP the advertised value was unusable (hit rate 0), and without DCP the value is identical.

## Verification

Measured on 4x H200 with Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct (`tp=4 dcp=4 page_size=64`):

- **Engine only, no router:** plain `sglang.launch_server` — before, `/server_info` reported `kv_events.block_size=64` while the ZMQ wire carried `BlockStored.block_size=256`; after, it reports 256, matching the wire.
- **End to end through a KV-aware router:** the equivalent consumer-side mistake gave a hit rate of **exactly 0** over six identical 1,686-token prompts, against **4.814814814814815 / 6** (the 96.3% arithmetic maximum, `5 * 26/27`) on otherwise identical no-DCP arms — including a same-attention-backend control arm, which rules out the backend. Correcting the width restored it to `5 * 6/7 = 4.285714285714286 / 6`, the arithmetic maximum for the 256-token logical page, and again to `3 * 6/7` on fresh content.
- The same consumer-side bug in Dynamo's SGLang integration (reading `server_args.page_size` directly, bypassing this descriptor) was fixed independently in ai-dynamo/dynamo#12765. This PR fixes the engine's own advertised contract, so any subscriber that honors it — e.g. sgl-router, whose `BlockSizeOracle` takes its width from this field and whose hashes must reach bit-parity with SGLang's `hash_page` at that width — is correct without needing DCP awareness of its own.
- **Unit tests** (`TestDcpKvEventContract`): red on `main`, green with the fix; covers `page_size=1 + dcp` (paged at `dcp_size`) and the non-DCP default. `pre-commit` passes.

## Note on scope

An earlier revision of this PR also added an args-time `tp_size % dcp_size` guard. That was **dropped**: `parallel_state.py` already raises `RuntimeError("tensor_model_parallel_size (N) must be divisible by decode_context_parallel_size (M)")` during dist init, before weights load. Confirmed by launching `--tp-size 1 --dcp-size 2` on `main`. Thanks @alexnails for questioning whether that check was needed — it wasn't.

title: fix(openai): avoid duplicate routed expert in response when `return_meta_info = True`
author: guapisolo
body:
## Summary
Avoid duplicate routed-expert payloads in non-streaming chat completion responses.

## Symptom & Reproduction
- **Symptom:** The base64 `routed_experts` payload appeared in both `choices[*].meta_info` and response-level `sglext` when both return flags were enabled.
- **Reproduction:** Build and serialize a non-streaming `/v1/chat/completions` response with both flags enabled.
  - **Expected:** Each choice contains its routed experts once in `meta_info`.
  - **Observed before the fix:** `sglext.routed_experts` repeated the first choice's routed experts.

## Root Cause
1. `_build_chat_response` projected first-choice `routed_experts` into `SglExt`.
2. `choice_meta_info` serialized the same routed payload for every choice.

## Fix
When `return_meta_info` is enabled, omit only response-level `sglext.routed_experts` and keep each choice's `meta_info` authoritative for routed experts. Independently requested `cached_tokens_details` and `spec_tokens_details` remain in `sglext`; `return_meta_info=false`, streaming chat, and `/v1/completions` behavior remain unchanged.

## Verification
- `env PYTHONPATH=/tmp/sglang-dedupe-chat-meta-sglext/python python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_completions.py`: 130 passed and 55 subtests passed.

title: [AMD][Fix] Qwen3.5: make empty-batch guard tuple-aware on fused AR+quant path
author: bingxche
body: ## Problem [#24651](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/24651) made Qwen3.5's AMD fused AR+RMSNorm+per-group-quant path return quantized activations as tuples: - GDN layers: `(bf16, fp8, scale)` - full-attention layers: `(fp8, scale)` [#34474](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34474) later added empty-batch guards that read `hidden_states.shape[0]`. On the fused path, those guards run before attention unpacks the tuple, so decode CUDA-graph capture fails: ```text AttributeError: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'shape' ``` The scheduler failure then surfaces in the test as `Server process exited with code -9`. The `SGLANG_DISABLE_FUSED_AR_QUANT=1` control stays on the tensor path and is unaffected. ## Fix Use the tuple's first tensor for the row-count check at both Qwen3.5 decoder guards, while passing the original `hidden_states` to attention unchanged. Both sites are required: GDN receives the 3-tuple, while full attention receives the 2-tuple. Zero-token inputs are handled before fused quantization, so they remain tensors and the empty-batch behavior from #34474 is preserved. title: [diffusion] make --vae-tiling honest, fix the decode OOM advice, gate NVFP4 on Blackwell
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary
Three failures that all present as something other than what they are. Found while auditing consumer-GPU support.

**`--vae-tiling` was a silent no-op on any VAE without `enable_tiling`.** The call sat under a bare `except Exception: pass`. MiniMax-H3's VAE is one of those, and it happens to tile anyway because `decoder_tiling` is set from its VAE config at construction — so the flag looked accepted while doing nothing, and the OOM message below told users to reach for it. `AutoencoderKL` now has `enable_tiling` (`decoder_tiling` is read per decode in `_adaptive_decode`, so setting it takes effect on the next call), and the caller's guard narrows to `AttributeError` and names the VAE class instead of discarding the request. Every `enable_tiling` implementation in the tree takes only optional arguments, so narrowing the guard cannot turn a previously swallowed error into a crash.

**The decode OOM handler recommended `--vae-cpu-offload`,** which moves VAE weights and does nothing for the activations that overflow. Decode runs after denoising, so the DiT and encoders are idle but may still hold VRAM — freeing them is the actual lever. The message now points at `--cpu-offload-components`, then tile size, then resolution.

**`ModelOptFp4Config.get_min_capability()` declared 100 but was never called.** The only real gate was whether flashinfer imports, so on a pre-Blackwell card with flashinfer installed the load succeeded and then failed inside the CUDA kernel with an opaque error. The FP4 linear method now enforces the declared minimum. A GPU whose capability cannot be read is left alone, so this only ever turns a crash into a message and never blocks a card that would have worked.

## Test plan
- [x] New unit test covers the gate's three branches: reject below the minimum (8.6 / 8.9 / 9.0), allow Blackwell (10.0 / 12.0), and leave an undetectable capability alone.
- [x] Real hardware, H200 (compute capability 9.0): the gate rejects with `NVFP4 checkpoints need compute capability 10.0 or newer (Blackwell); this GPU is 9.0.` instead of reaching the kernel.
- [x] Verified on the same box that `MiniMaxH3VideoVAE` now resolves `enable_tiling`, and that its `decoder_tiling` is already true at construction.
- [x] Audited all four `enable_tiling` implementations for required arguments before narrowing the guard.

**Not covered:** the allow path on live Blackwell silicon — no B200/B300/5090 capacity was free. It is exercised with a mocked capability, and the values match this repo's own detection (`is_blackwell()` is `major == 10`, `is_sm120()` is `major == 12`, both ≥ 100 via `DeviceCapability.to_int()`). The two OOM log branches are also not triggered end to end; they are message-only changes.

author: beyondHJM

# [Kimi-K3] Exclude SM120 from the attention-residual TMA path

## Summary

The Kimi-K3 attention-residual dispatcher previously enabled the TMA fast path
for every CUDA architecture with a compute-capability major version greater
than or equal to 10. This incorrectly selected the SM100-oriented TMA kernel on
SM120 GPUs such as the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090, where the required
`tcgen05`/TMEM path is not supported.

This PR changes the capability gate to:

major >= 10 and major != 12

SM12x devices now use the existing Triton fallback. The fast path remains

## Scope

This is a standalone Kimi-K3 attention-residual dispatch fix.

title: [NVIDIA] Fix SM107 MXFP8 activation prep
author: csahithi
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
Fix MXFP8 activation preparation for the FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE backend on SM107.

GPT-OSS on SM107 can reach the FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE kernel without a pre-quantized route handoff. Previously, SGLang used the Triton per-token-group quantizer in this case. This does not reliably produce the activation representation expected by the FlashInfer SM107 path.

The quantizer producing the activations must follow the same MXFP8 and UE8M0 layout contract as the FlashInfer MoE kernel consuming them. Using FlashInfer for both operations on SM107 avoids the incompatible producer/consumer path.
The fake custom-op implementation also needs the real scale-buffer shape. Returning a placeholder one-element tensor can produce incorrect metadata during `torch.compile`.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
- Use FlashInfer's MXFP8 quantizer on SM107 when no route/quant handoff is available.
- Preserve Kimi K3's existing fused route/quant handoff.
- Preserve the existing Triton activation-quantization path on other SM10x architectures.
- Preserve FlashInfer quantization for padded hidden dimensions.
- Correct the FlashInfer custom-op fake scale-buffer size for both linear and swizzled layouts so `torch.compile` metadata matches the real quantizer.
- Add CPU regression tests covering dispatch behavior, padded inputs, route handoff, and fake output shapes.

title: [Fix] Land the decode mamba checkpoint depth on the tree page under DCP
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

A donated mamba checkpoint is only reusable at a depth the radix tree can name. `cache_finished_req` / `cache_unfinished_req` floor the insert key with `page_aligned(tree_page)`, so a checkpoint taken off that grid is attached to the *preceding* node while its state already covers tokens past it — a later request matching that node resumes the linear-attention recurrence mid-stream and then re-consumes those tokens. Silent, no assert, wrong output.

#34808 fixed this for the **extend** path with `mamba_checkpoint_grid(tree_page)`, and scoped itself explicitly:

> Only the prefill donation depth changes here. Decode tracking keeps its own `--mamba-track-interval` grid.

That decode grid does not land on the tree page. `--mamba-track-interval` has one guard, `assert mamba_track_interval % view.page_size == 0` (`server_args.py`), against the **configured** page — and is never resolved anywhere (`grep` over `arg_groups/` and `configs/` is empty). Under DCP the tree allocates on `page_size * dcp_size` (`kv_cache_builder.py`: `page_size=... else token_to_kv_pool_allocator.page_size`), so that guard stops implying the invariant.

The insert-time guard that would have caught this was deferred to #34760 and #34780 — **both closed, never merged** — and there is no mamba depth check on the insert in `main` today, so the misalignment stays silent.

**Break condition:** `mamba_track_interval % (page_size * dcp_size) != 0`.

| page | dcp | tree page | interval | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 64 | 4 | 256 | 256 | ok |
| 64 | 8 | **512** | 256 | **broken** |
| 128 | 4 | 512 | 256 | broken |
| 256 | 2 | 512 | 256 | broken |

Two shipped recipes are on the broken row today, both in `test_kimi_k3_b300.py`: `TestKimiK3B300Balanced` (`--tp-size 8 --dcp-size 8 --enable-hierarchical-cache`) and `TestKimiK3B300MegaMoE` (`--dcp-size 8` + DSPARK — spec is only rejected under DCP *with* HiCache, so the mamba grid is live there too). Kimi-K3 DCP forces `cutedsl_mla`, which pins `page_size` to 64, and `KimiK3Config.text_config` is a `KimiLinearConfig` so the tree carries a `MAMBA` component. The tree pages at 512 while decode checkpoints every 256, so every odd multiple of 256 names a depth no node carries.

Every other DCP hybrid config in tree is page 64 × dcp 4, where `64 * 4 == 256` — the default interval — and the two grids line up by coincidence. That is also why the DCP HiCache KL case (#35380) cannot catch this.

## Modifications

`mamba_track_grid(tree_page)` beside `mamba_checkpoint_grid` — the same `lcm`, carrying the requested interval as well:

```python
def mamba_track_grid(tree_page: int) -> int:
    return math.lcm(
        mamba_checkpoint_grid(tree_page), get_exec().mamba.mamba_track_interval
    )
```

Read where a checkpoint depth is picked: `schedule_batch.prepare_for_decode`, the three `batch_result_processor` boundary sites, and the spec verify/prepare paths in `spec_utils`, `dspark_worker_v2`, `dflash_worker_v2`. Pure derivation — nothing is mutated, and `server_args.mamba_track_interval` keeps the value the operator typed.

The tree page is a process constant, so each site only needs a live handle to the tree. `prepare_for_decode` and the spec paths take it off the batch, as the extend path already does. The batch-result processor takes it off **its own** `tree_cache`: the batch it is handed is the result-queue `copy()`, whose field list is scoped to what `process_batch_result` needs and does not carry one.

Going through `mamba_checkpoint_grid` rather than just rounding onto the page keeps the decode depth chunk-aligned too, which the extend path relies on: a decode-donated depth becomes the prefix of a later extend, and `_force_track_h` asserts `i % mamba_cache_chunk_size == 0` there.

Two readers stay on the raw arg because they are flush/write cadence rather than checkpoint depth: `hybrid_linear_attn_backend`'s ReplaySSM force-flush mask and Inkling's `sconv` (which holds only a `ForwardBatch`). `lcm` makes the derived grid a multiple of the raw interval, so every snapshot step is still a flush step and the flush mask's invariant survives. Note the comment at `hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py:403` says the two "fire on the same steps"; after this change they fire on nested sets of steps.

`test_batch_result_processor_mamba_boundary.py` is a pre-existing test (#33477) whose hand-built `ScheduleBatch` and processor double now need a `tree_cache`, since `prepare_for_decode` did not read one before this change. Same edit #34808 made to its own double. Page and chunk are set to the interval already under test, so the derived grid stays 4 and every existing boundary expectation is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

**Not yet measured — this is why the PR is a draft.** #34808 shipped a cold-vs-warm teacher-forced logprob comparison on a live Kimi-Linear dcp8 server for the prefill half; the decode half deserves the same evidence, and this PR currently argues from page alignment alone. An 8×B300 run on the `TestKimiK3B300Balanced` recipe, before and after, is the next step.

What is verified statically:

- **Cache reuse is unchanged.** The insert floors the donated depth to the tree page, so the node it lands on is `floor(min(N, floor(N/grid)·grid) / 512) · 512` — which collapses to the same `512q` under both grids (checked for every request length in [0, 4096): zero differ). Same number of cached checkpoints, same node depths, same KV prefix. What changes is *which state* is attached: previously a state that had already consumed 256 more tokens than the node it hung on. Snapshot writes into the ping-pong buffer halve on the affected recipes — less decode work, not fewer cache entries.
- **Grid unchanged everywhere else:** page 64 × dcp 4, page 32 × dcp 4 (tree 128), and every non-DCP config.

New CPU unit case in `test_mamba_checkpoint_depth.py`, beside #34808's extend cases since it is the same invariant from the other end.
