title: [CPU] Fix wrongly causal-masked bidirectional attention
author: chunyuan-w
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

On the Intel AMX CPU attention backend, `extend_attention_cpu` always masked the extend stage of attention as causal. This is correct for decoder-style self-attention, but wrong for bidirectional, encoder-only self-attention (e.g. BERT-family rerankers/embedders like bge-reranker). Such models silently got causally-masked attention scores, producing incorrect outputs.

When running `BAAI/bge-reranker-base` on CPU:
For the below request:
```
{
  "model": "BAAI/bge-reranker-base",
  "query": "what is panda?",
  "documents": [
    "hi",
    "The giant panda (Ailuropoda melanoleuca), sometimes called a panda bear or simply panda, is a bear species endemic to China."
  ],
  "return_documents": true
}
```
Before this fix:
`"hi"` and  `"The giant panda ..."` both get the same score: 2.611328125, which is not reasonble.

After this fix:
Scores diverge correctly, matching what a real cross-encoder should produce:
`"The giant panda ..."`: score is 6.1875 (more relevant to the query so got a higher socre)
`"hi"`: score is -8.15625

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
- `python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/cpu/extend.cpp`: add an `is_causal` parameter (default `true`) to `extend_attention_cpu`. The stage-2 loop now iterates over the full extend range and only applies the causal mask when `is_causal` is set, instead of unconditionally limiting keys to `[0, m + BLOCK_M)` and masking `n + n_size - 1 > m`.

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/intel_amx_backend.py`: compute `is_causal = not (layer.is_cross_attention or layer.attn_type == AttentionType.ENCODER_ONLY)` and pass it into `extend_attention_fwd`, mirroring the existing pattern in `triton_backend.py`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/ee1f2e8dfdbb264727134aeac4b8dec155ec6efe/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/triton_backend.py#L1360-L1368.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

```sh
python test/registered/cpu/test_extend.py -k test_extend_attention_bidirectional
```

author: aurickq

Full-prefill CUDA graph buckets are sized by aggregate batch tokens, which can exceed the maximum context length of any single request. title: [Quant] Load compressed-tensors kv_cache_scheme scales
author: Jiminator
body:
## Motivation

compressed-tensors checkpoints that declare a `kv_cache_scheme` ship calibrated per-tensor attention `k_scale` / `v_scale` tensors, but they are silently dropped at load (`Parameter model.layers.N.k_scale not found in params_dict`), so `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` runs the cache unscaled. Three gaps compound:

- `CompressedTensorsConfig.from_config` never forwarded `kv_cache_scheme`, leaving it `None` even when declared.
- `get_quant_method` had no `RadixAttention` branch, so the `k_scale` / `v_scale` parameters were never created (ModelOpt has `ModelOptFp8KVCacheMethod` for this; the compressed-tensors equivalent was missing).
- The qwen3_5 weight mapper only knew the ModelOpt-style `.k_proj.k_scale` serialization; compressed-tensors stores the scales on the attention module (`.self_attn.k_scale`).

## Modifications

- Forward `kv_cache_scheme` in `from_config`.
- New `CompressedTensorsKVCacheMethod(BaseKVCacheMethod)`, returned for `RadixAttention` when a `kv_cache_scheme` is declared. It accepts only what `BaseKVCacheMethod` can represent — static, symmetric, per-tensor FP8. A declared-but-unsupported scheme is skipped with a warning instead of failing the boot: such checkpoints serve correctly with an unquantized-scale KV cache, so refusing to load them would regress working deployments.
- A `kv_cache_quant_algo` property on the config: `configure_kv_cache_dtype` duck-types this field to resolve `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, so a declared supported scheme gets the fp8 pool its scales calibrate (ModelOpt parity). Without this, an auto-resolved bf16 pool would store unscaled entries while the attention backends apply the loaded scales on read.
- Two `orig_to_new_substr` entries in `QWEN3_5_KV_SCALE_MAPPER` for the attention-level scale names, and the mapper applied in the Qwen3.5 MTP loader for symmetry.
- Unit test: `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_kv_cache.py` (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`).
- The pre-existing `kv_cache_scheme` remap in `apply_weight_name_mapper` (dead until this PR forwarded the scheme) is removed: the scheme holds schema fields, never module names, and `apply_dict` drops keys that match a mapper deletion rule.

Checkpoints without a `kv_cache_scheme` are unaffected (`get_quant_method` returns `None` for `RadixAttention` as before), and unloaded scales keep the existing default-to-1.0 behavior in `BaseKVCacheMethod.process_weights_after_loading`.

## Accuracy Tests

RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, Qwen3.8-27B mixed-precision compressed-tensors checkpoint with a declared FP8 `kv_cache_scheme`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 200`:

- Before: 32 `k_scale`/`v_scale` drop warnings at load; GSM8K 0.960 (cache unscaled — accuracy-benign on this checkpoint because the calibrated scales are near 1, but incorrect).
- After: zero drop warnings; GSM8K 0.965, invalid 0.000. Parity within the script's documented variance — this is a correctness fix for the calibration path, not an accuracy rescue.
- With `--kv-cache-dtype` left as `auto`: the pool now auto-resolves to `float8_e4m3fn` (previously bf16, ignoring the checkpoint's declared KV calibration); zero drop warnings; GSM8K 0.940 / 0.960 across two runs — statistically identical to the explicit-fp8 lane, as expected since both resolve to the same pool and scales.

Note: an MTP draft loaded from the same checkpoint carries the same config, so the draft worker's pool auto-resolves to fp8 as well (its scales default to 1.0; write/read stay symmetric). A standalone bf16 draft export without a `quantization_config` keeps a bf16 pool.

Known limit: an explicit bf16 `--kv-cache-dtype` override on a checkpoint with declared scales attaches scales to an unquantized pool — the same pre-existing exposure ModelOpt has today; a shared fix belongs in `BaseKVCacheMethod`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No runtime impact: scale resolution happens once at init; the scales feed the existing fp8 KV cache path.

title: [Fix] Pass Anthropic thinking history as reasoning_content for custom chat encoders
author: mmangkad
body:
## Motivation

Run Kimi-K3 with `--reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --tool-call-parser kimi_k3` and talk to it on `/v1/messages` with `thinking` on. Any agentic client sends assistant `thinking` blocks back in history — the Messages API requires it for tool-use turns — and a few turns in, raw XTML channel markers show up in visible assistant text:

```
turn 3  [text] '<|open|>think<|sep|<|sep|>Something is very strange. […]'
turn 4  [text] '<|open|>think<|sep|'
```

Turns 1-2 are fine, then every turn after that is corrupted — it never recovers. Drop the `thinking` blocks from the replayed history and it never happens at all, so the problem is how prior reasoning gets fed back, not the reasoning parser.

**Root cause.** K3 ships no Jinja chat template, so SGLang renders it through the checkpoint's own XTML encoder. That encoder frames the `think` / `response` / `tools` channels itself and wants prior reasoning in an assistant `reasoning_content` field. The Anthropic adapter never used it — instead it wrapped prior thinking in the reasoning detector's markers and spliced that into assistant **content**. Here is what the two forms actually render to, straight from the K3 tokenizer:

```
# before — think channel empty, reasoning nested inside the response channel
<|open|>think<|sep|><|close|>think<|sep|><|open|>response<|sep|><|open|>think<|sep|>PRIOR
<|close|>think<|sep|>Here is my answer.<|close|>response<|sep|>

# after
<|open|>think<|sep|>PRIOR<|close|>think<|sep|><|open|>response<|sep|>Here is my answer.<|close|>response<|sep|>
```

Every replayed turn taught the model the same lesson: think channel empty, think block sitting inside the response channel. Two turns of that and it starts writing `<|open|>think<|sep|>` as ordinary response text.

None of this is K3-specific. All four Python chat encoders that bypass `apply_chat_template` frame their own reasoning channel and read `reasoning_content`, so the splice was wrong for every one of them.

## Modifications

- **`entrypoints/openai/chat_encoding.py`** — adds `spec_owns_reasoning_history(spec)`, right under `resolve_chat_encoding_spec` so the contract sits with the specs it describes. It covers the whole custom-encoder family (`spec is not None`) rather than listing specs, so whoever adds the fifth one gets the safe default for free. An encoder that ignores the field drops history — what the splice path already does for models with no reasoning detector — instead of leaking.
- **`entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py`** — `supports_native_reasoning_history()`, a one-line delegate.
- **`entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py`** — `_convert_assistant_thinking_blocks` now returns `(reasoning_content, text)`. Custom encoders get the history in the field, everyone else keeps the splice untouched. `redacted_thinking` still raises before the branch, and the best-effort drop for detector-less models survives.

Nothing needed a schema change: `ChatCompletionMessageGenericParam` already declared `reasoning_content`, and messages are dumped without `exclude_none`, so it flows straight through. `wrap_reasoning_history` has exactly one production caller, so that is the whole mechanism. `dsv4`/`dsv32` also land on their official multi-turn contract now instead of bypassing it. Jinja-path models stay on the splice on purpose — their markers (`<think>`, `[THINK]`, `◁think▷`) really do live in the content stream, so it reproduces what the model emitted anyway.

## Test Plan

### Live server

Same deployment before and after — `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` on 2x4 GB300, TP8, DSPARK spec-decode — same scripts, `temperature=0`:

| run | main | with the fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 12-turn tool loop, streaming `/v1/messages` | leaks turns 3-12, all ten of them | clean, and the loop converges at turn 9 |
| 8-turn tool loop, non-streaming | leaks turns 3-8 | clean |
| 6 concurrent sessions x 5 turns | all six leak, every one first at turn 3 | none leak |
| thinking dropped from replayed history | clean | clean |
| `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` | clean | clean |
| reasoning passed as `reasoning_content` on `/v1/chat/completions` | clean | clean |
| thinking-only history turn, and a turn with two thinking blocks | clean | clean |
| `redacted_thinking` history | 400 | 400 |

On main the onset is turn 3 every single time, and it never recovers — the `thinking` block stops appearing at all from there on and the markers move into `text`. That is also why the loop never converges: each turn re-reads its own corrupted history and re-diagnoses the same phantom problem. With the fix, `thinking` comes back on essentially every turn and the model finishes the task.

Asked what it had just been thinking, the model quoted the injected reasoning back — the history really does land in the think channel rather than being quietly dropped. Prompt rendering was also diffed against the real K3 tokenizer for a thinking + text + tool_use turn.

### Unit tests

`anthropic/test_serving.py` — 61/61. Two new cases: history reaches a channel-framing encoder as `reasoning_content` and never through the wrap path, and a thinking-only turn keeps its reasoning across the empty-content placeholder branch. Both go red against pre-fix code, and the existing wrap-path test still covers the default encoder.

`openai/test_serving_chat.py` — 111/111. Two more: the real `OpenAIServingChat` predicate across all four specs plus `None`, and a guard that parses the literals `resolve_chat_encoding_spec` can return and checks them against the tuple the capability test iterates. Add an encoder without classifying it and CI fails. Mutation-checked, so it is not passing vacuously.

title: [Responses] Fix empty-prompt routing for token-first chat encoders (kimi_k3, inkling)
author: hhy-seven
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

A `/v1/responses` request against a **multimodal Kimi-K3** deployment fails immediately:

```json
{"error":{"message":"texts cannot be empty and tokenizer must be initialized","type":"invalid_request_error","param":null,"code":400}}
```

The equivalent `/v1/chat/completions` request with the same messages and tools works, so the bug is specific to the `/v1/responses` path.

The same failure class applies to **inkling**, the other token-first chat encoder: text-only requests to a multimodal deployment hit the same 400, and media requests silently lose the entire rendered prompt — `TokenizerManager` substitutes `input_ids=[]` when text is empty but media is present, so the engine receives the image with none of the text.

## Why

Token-first chat encoders (`kimi_k3`, `inkling`) produce `prompt_ids` directly (via `apply_chat_template(tokenize=True, ...)` / a custom renderer) and leave `prompt == ""` — the only `prompt = decode(prompt_ids)` assignment lives in the default-template branch these encoders never enter. Each serving endpoint re-implemented the text-vs-`input_ids` routing on its own and they drifted: `serving_chat` accumulated per-spec guards, while `serving_responses` forwarded the empty `prompt` as `text` unconditionally, producing `GenerateReqInput(text="")` → `_tokenize_texts("")` → the 400 above.

A text-only deployment (`is_multimodal == False`) always routes through `prompt_ids`, so it is unaffected — which is why the bug only surfaces on multimodal deployments.

Fixes #35460

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/chat_encoding.py`: add `spec_renders_prompt_ids` (`"inkling"`, `"kimi_k3"`), alongside the existing `spec_owns_reasoning_history` family predicate.
- `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py`: centralize the routing in `OpenAIServingChat._engine_prompt`; the per-spec `if/elif` chain in `_convert_to_internal_request` collapses to one call.
- `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py`: `_make_request` uses the same shared helper instead of forwarding the empty `prompt`.
- `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_responses.py`: the regression test now runs for both token-first specs via `subTest`.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — no kernel or model-forward change; this only fixes which prompt field the serving layer hands to the engine. Unit tests: `test_serving_responses.py` + `test_serving_chat.py` pass (169 passed on a CPU devbox).

title: Fix dummy initialization of inverse weight scales
author: weireweire
body:
## Summary

- Initialize floating-point `weight_scale_inv` tensors to the neutral value `1.0` when loading dummy weights.
- Preserve randomized dummy initialization for regular floating-point weights.

## Problem

The dummy loader randomized every floating-point tensor into a small interval around zero. Inverse weight scales must be positive, and DeepGEMM paths that convert them to UE8M0 additionally require power-of-two inputs. DSV4 FP4 expert and FP8 attention post-load processing therefore aborted in `transform_sf_into_required_layout` before the server could start.

This complements #33500, which fixed serialized MXFP4 scale placeholders stored as raw integer UE8M0 bytes. The affected DSV4 paths here expose floating-point inverse scales, so the integer-placeholder fix does not cover them.

## Fix

Use `1.0` for floating-point state-dict entries whose names end in `weight_scale_inv`. It is a neutral, valid inverse scale for the post-load transforms. Real checkpoint loading is unchanged.

## Validation

- Full pre-commit suite passed.
- A TP4 DSV4 DSpark dummy startup completed target and draft weight loading and post-processing without the DeepGEMM scale-layout assertion.

title: fix(moe): support Llama4 NVFP4 router input weights on SM120
author: janbernloehr
body:
## Motivation

Fixes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/34192.

Llama 4 constructs its MoE layers with `apply_router_weight_on_input=True`. For ModelOpt NVFP4 on SM120/SM121, SGLang selects the FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE runner, which previously rejected this configuration during server warmup.

For top-1 routing, the required semantics can be implemented exactly by multiplying each token's hidden states by its router weight before activation quantization and passing unit final scales to CUTLASS. This follows the existing pattern in the AITER MoE runner.

The fix remains intentionally restricted to top-1 routing. With top-k greater than one, each selected expert would require a differently scaled copy of the input.

## Modifications

- Add top-1 router-weight pre-scaling to the common FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE execution path.
- Replace the kernel's output-side router scaling with float32 unit `token_final_scales` when pre-scaling is active.
- Normalize all `token_final_scales` passed through this CUTLASS path to float32, as required by the binding.
- Remove the ModelOpt NVFP4 and FlashInfer CUTLASS assertions that rejected `apply_router_weight_on_input=True`.
- Preserve explicit rejection for:
  - top-k greater than one;
  - activations already quantized before dispatch, including the FlashInfer CUTLASS FP4 all-gather path.
- Add focused CPU unit tests covering:
  - top-1 activation pre-scaling;
  - float32 unit final scales;
  - preservation of expert IDs;
  - top-k greater than one rejection;
  - pre-quantized dispatch rejection.

The normal `apply_router_weight_on_input=False` path is unchanged apart from enforcing the CUTLASS binding's float32 scale requirement.

## Accuracy Tests

Added:

```text
test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_flashinfer_cutlass_router_weight.py
```

The tests compare the transformed hidden states and final scales against the expected top-1 formulation and verify that unsupported configurations fail explicitly.

Local validation:

```text
python -m py_compile \
  python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutlass.py \
  python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py \
  test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_flashinfer_cutlass_router_weight.py
```

Result: passed.

All commit-time pre-commit checks passed, including Python AST validation, isort, Ruff, Black, codespell, and registered-test validation.

The focused pytest test could not be executed in the local development environment because PyTorch is not installed. No real-checkpoint accuracy test was run for this checkout.

The equivalent patch and its SM120/SM121 validation evidence are documented in #34192. That validation used dummy weights for end-to-end liveness, so it is not claimed as a model-accuracy result.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speed test or profiling was run for this checkout.

The equivalent patch validation documented in #34192 completed both SM120 scenarios without errors and did not show a decode throughput regression. Those results used dummy weights and a separate validated build, so they are included only as prior evidence, not as performance results for this commit.

title: [Diffusion] Fix multi-group layerwise offload startup memory
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

- initialize every non-MPS layer group before moving non-layer parameters to the accelerator
- release managed groups in descending parameter-byte order during initialization while preserving declared manager order for runtime behavior
- preserve each group’s independent prefetch and forward-hook lifecycle
- add regression coverage at the real `configure_layerwise_offload` boundary

## Motivation

Models can expose multiple entries in `layer_names`. Previously, each manager moved the entire model immediately after replacing only its own layer group. Earlier managers therefore treated later groups as non-layer parameters and transiently moved them to the accelerator, making startup peak memory depend on `layer_names` ordering.

The coordinated initialization now replaces all managed groups first, moves the actual non-layer parameters once, and only then finalizes per-group prefetch and hooks. Processing the largest groups first also releases the most device memory earliest when checkpoint loading has already placed weights on the accelerator.

title: [Responses] Fix max_output_tokens overestimate on multimodal requests
author: hhy-seven
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Summary

The Responses API pre-computed `default_max_tokens = context_len - prompt_length`.
For **multimodal** requests `prompt_length` came from
`len(tokenizer.encode(engine_prompt_string))`, which only counts the `<image>`
placeholder — not the engine-side **post-expansion** token count. So
`default_max_tokens` was overestimated, and `_validate_one_request` then rejected
`input + default_max_tokens > context_len` with a spurious 400 (any model on the
multimodal arch path, e.g. KimiK2.6 sharing `KimiK25ForConditionalGeneration`).

The expanded count isn't available at the `serving_responses` layer (image
tokens are only expanded engine-side), which is why a serving-side recompute
can't be made accurate.

Fixes #29287.

## Fix

Mirror the Chat Completions route: stop pre-computing `default_max_tokens` and
pass `None`, leaving `max_new_tokens` unset so the **scheduler clamps** the
budget against the real post-expansion `input_len` — one source of truth.

- `ResponsesRequest.to_sampling_params`: `default_max_tokens: Optional[int] = None`,
  with `None`-safe handling (`max_output_tokens` is still honored and capped when
  a concrete default is supplied).
- `serving_responses.py`: drop the `prompt_length` / `default_max_tokens`
  computation and pass `None`.

This reuses the exact path Chat already uses for unspecified `max_tokens`
(`tokenizer_manager` skips the total check when `max_new_tokens is None`, the
scheduler substitutes a sentinel and clamps to the real input/system limits), so
text Responses requests behave identically to before.

## Tests

`test_responses_protocol.py::ResponsesSamplingParamsTestCase`: `None` default +
no `max_output_tokens` leaves `max_new_tokens=None`; `None` default +
`max_output_tokens=100` → `98`; an explicit `default_max_tokens=128` still caps
to `126` (backwards compatible). Pass locally.

Per the issue thread @hhy-seven preferred this (option 2); opening as draft for
maintainer confirmation.

title: [diffusion] fix: stop reserving NCCL device buffers for single-rank groups
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

On a single GPU, ~5 GiB of VRAM is gone before a single weight is loaded. On a 12 GiB consumer card that is 44% of the device, and it makes VAE decode fail at any resolution.

The cause is that a single-GPU run still builds every parallel group — DP, CFG, TP, SP, PP, VAE_DECODE, DIT, VAE, ulysses, ring — each with one rank, and each got an NCCL-backed process group. NCCL sizes its per-channel device buffers when the communicator is created, so every one of those groups reserved ~390 MiB (the first, the world group, ~470 MiB).

None of that memory can ever be used. Every collective in `GroupCoordinator` returns early on `world_size == 1` ("Bypass the function if we are using only 1 GPU"), and the device communicator is only constructed when `world_size > 1`. `pynccl` already skips communicator creation for single-rank groups; the underlying `torch.distributed.new_group` did not.

Measured on an RTX 3060 12 GiB with a bare `torch.distributed` repro:

| | device memory |
|---|---|
| CUDA context only | 114 MiB |
| + world group | 584 MiB |
| each additional `new_group([0])` | **+388 MiB** |

`NCCL_MAX_NCHANNELS=1` drops the per-group cost to 10 MiB, which confirms these are
per-channel buffers for channels a one-rank communicator can never use.

## Modifications

Add `new_device_group()` in `group_coordinator.py`, which gives single-rank groups the gloo backend and leaves multi-rank groups on the requested backend. Route the nine device-group creation sites through it: `GroupCoordinator.__init__`, the`PipelineGroupCoordinator` single-rank branch and its `skip_device_group`, `_DIT` and `_VAE` in `parallel_state.py`, and the four ulysses/ring groups in `parallel_groups.py`.

The two-rank `device_group_0_1` / `device_group_1_0` pipeline pair is left alone; it is only reached when the group has exactly two ranks.

One consumer needed a matching guard. cache-dit averages its residual-difference statistics across the TP x SP slice using the DIT group, and that all-reduce had no world-size check, so on a single GPU it would now stage device tensors through the host on every cached block of every step. Averaging over one rank returns the input, so the patched `similarity` returns the local value instead of running the collective.

Every other consumer of these groups already short-circuits: collectives in `GroupCoordinator` return early on `world_size == 1`, the device communicator is built only above 1, the ulysses/ring groups are reached only under `sp_size > 1` in `attention/layer.py` and behind `world_size <= 1` early returns in `usp.py`, and the VAE group has no consumer outside its getter.

## Accuracy Tests

Bit-exact. RTX 3060 12 GiB, `Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers`, layerwise offload of dit/text_encoder/vae, 320x576, 9 frames, 8 steps, seed 1234.

| | free VRAM after load | peak VRAM | VAE decode | output SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 6.51 GiB | 11552 MiB | **OOM** | no output produced |
| `NCCL_MAX_NCHANNELS=1` control | 11.31 GiB | 6886 MiB | ok | `78a2a963…` |
| this PR | 11.06 GiB | 6830 MiB | ok | `78a2a963…` |

Two-GPU regression on the same box, `--num-gpus 2`: patched and unpatched produce the same output, SHA-256 `361bb915…`, so the multi-rank path is unaffected.

New unit test `test_single_rank_device_group.py` covers backend selection for single-rank and multi-rank groups (3 tests, 5 subtests). Existing `test_cache_dit_integration.py` passes with the guard (12 tests together).

CI note: `multimodal-gen-test-1-npu-a3` is red here, but every diffusion testcase on that runner is red on unrelated branches too (see #35511, where `ernie_image_t2i_1npu`, `flux_image_t2i_npu`, `flux_2_klein_4b_t2i_1npu`, `z_image_t2i_1npu` and `wan2_1_t2v_1.3b_1_npu` all fail and the job ends with `Executing the custom container implementation failed`). The NPU lane cannot vet this change right now.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No change to per-step time — 1.10 s/step before, 1.06 s/step after, within the run-to-run noise band measured across this configuration. The groups involved never carried traffic.

author: liupeng374

title: [sampling] Fix int32 offset overflow in top-k renorm Triton kernels
author: merrymercy
body:
## Motivation

The top-k renorm Triton kernels in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/sampling/renorm_triton.py` compute flattened element offsets as `row * vocab_size + offsets` and `program_id * BLOCK_SIZE + arange(...)`. Both products are computed in int32, so for large `batch x vocab_size` tensors the offsets can silently overflow, corrupting loads/stores.

## Modifications

Cast the row / program id to `tl.int64` before the multiplication in `_mask_and_partial_sum_kernel` and `_normalize_kernel`, so offset arithmetic is done in 64-bit.

## Checklist

- Ran `pre-commit` on the changed file (passed).
- Verified on an internal setup exercising the top-k renorm path.

title: docker: fix CUDA-13 build — rename NCCL_VERSION ARG to avoid base image ENV collision
author: datdo-msft
body:
## Problem
The CUDA-13 branch in `docker/Dockerfile` runs:
```
pip install --force-reinstall --no-deps "nvidia-nccl-cu13==${NCCL_VERSION}"
```
The `nvidia/cuda:13.0.3-cudnn-devel-ubuntu24.04` base image sets `ENV NCCL_VERSION=2.28.3-1` (Debian/apt format), which **shadows** the Dockerfile's `ARG NCCL_VERSION=2.30.7` at `RUN` time. So pip requests `2.28.3-1`, which is not a valid PyPI version, and the build fails:
```
ERROR: No matching distribution found for nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.28.3-1
```

## Fix
Rename the ARG to `SGL_NCCL_VERSION` so it no longer collides with the base image's `ENV NCCL_VERSION`; the intended `2.30.7` is used. This matches `scripts/ci/cuda/ci_install_dependency.sh`'s `install_nccl()`, which already hardcodes `2.30.7`.

title: [Bugfix] Fix full prefill CUDA graph padding and EAGLE capture
author: aurickq
body:
## Motivation

Full prefill CUDA graphs replay fixed token buckets that may be larger than the live batch. Models that mask padded hidden states need the live `num_token_non_padded` boundary even when attention tensors are not gathered. Without it, padded rows can propagate through the captured graph.

EAGLE target prefill also consumes the full target hidden-state sequence. FullCG previously captured the configured return-hidden-state mode, which could be insufficient and force target prefill back to eager execution.

## Modifications

- Register and populate `num_token_non_padded` for FullCG, including non-gathered execution.
- Capture `FULL` hidden states for EAGLE target prefill under FullCG while retaining `LAST` for breakable draft workers.
- Keep the EAGLE eager fallback specific to `tc_piecewise`, whose fixed capture ceiling can remain below `FULL`.
- Add focused regression tests for the non-gathered token boundary and FullCG EAGLE admission.

## Accuracy Tests

No model math or kernels are changed.

- 42 focused unit tests passed, including 2 parameterized subtests.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The changes update CUDA graph metadata and capture mode; they do not add work to attention or model kernels.

title: [Fix] Support 128-aligned hidden sizes in the W4AFP8 DeepEP low-latency requant kernel
author: alexnails
body:
## Motivation

`fp8_per_token_to_per_tensor_quant_triton()` requantizes DeepEP low-latency's per-token-group
fp8 payload into the per-tensor fp8 that the first CUTLASS W4A8 grouped GEMM consumes. It
required the hidden size to fill a whole number of 1024-element blocks:

```python
K_BLOCK_SIZE = 1024
assert x.size(2) % K_BLOCK_SIZE == 0
grid = (x.size(2) // K_BLOCK_SIZE, 32, x.size(0))
```

so it rejected any expert hidden size that is only 128-aligned — 3584, for example. Since
`W4AFp8MoEMethod` pins the low-latency wire format to fp8
(`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/w4afp8.py:286-295`) and `apply_deepep_ll()` rejects a
payload that carries no per-token-group scales (`w4afp8.py:347-351`), such a model has no
working low-latency path at all: the fp8 payload it is handed trips the assert during decode
CUDA-graph capture.

1024 was the only constraint of its kind on that path. `w1_scale` is `[E, K // 512, N * 8]`, so
512-alignment is genuinely required; DeepEP's low-latency fp8 scales are `[E, M, hidden // 128]`
(column-major in the last two dims for TMA), so the payload is always a whole number of 128-wide
scale groups. A hidden size of 3584 satisfies both — 7 × 512, 28 groups — and was rejected only
by the 1024 block.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/ep_moe_kernels.py`:

- Take the grid from `triton.cdiv` and drop the assert.
- Mask the k lanes in `_fp8_per_token_quant_to_per_tensor_quant_kernel`: on the hidden load, on
  the store, and on the scale load, whose offsets derive from `k_offsets` and would otherwise
  read past the scale tensor in the tail block.
- Put the masked form behind `HAS_K_TAIL: tl.constexpr`, so hidden sizes that fill every block
  keep the original unmasked loads and the same launch geometry. This mirrors
  `_silu_and_mul_post_per_tensor_quant_kernel` in the same file, which already pairs a `cdiv`
  grid with a masked fast axis.

Adds `test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_fp8_per_token_to_per_tensor_quant.py`
(`base-b-kernel-unit`, `1-gpu-large`).

## Accuracy Tests

The new test checks k ∈ {7168, 3584, 1152} — one exact multiple of 1024 and two tailed, so both
specializations compile — against a torch reference, and asserts that rows past `masked_m` are
left exactly as the caller wrote them. Inputs are integers in [-8, 8] with power-of-two group
scales, so every intermediate is exactly representable in e4m3 and the comparison can be
`rtol=0, atol=0`.

(The kernel saturates fp8 overflow — `cvt.rn.satfinite`, clamping to 448.0 — where
`Tensor.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)` produces NaN, so a torch-reference test has to stay inside range
deliberately.)

One H200, torch 2.11.0+cu130 / triton 3.6.0:

```
test_masked_rows_and_k_tail[7168] PASSED
test_masked_rows_and_k_tail[3584] PASSED
test_masked_rows_and_k_tail[1152] PASSED
3 passed in 16.75s
```

Swapping this commit's kernel for the current `main` file makes the two tailed cases fail while
7168 still passes, so the test covers the change rather than just passing alongside it.

A wider matrix run out of tree — both scale layouts (contiguous and DeepEP's column-major) ×
`masked_m` ∈ {0, 1, 17, m} × E ∈ {4, 8, 56} × K_BLOCK ∈ {1024, 2048} × num_warps ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8} —
is bit-exact against the reference everywhere, with padding rows untouched.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Hidden sizes that already worked are unaffected, checked two ways on H200 and B200 (torch 2.11 /
triton 3.6; kernel timed inside a CUDA graph so Triton's Python launch cost is excluded; DeepEP
scale layout, `K_BLOCK_SIZE=1024`, m-grid 32).

Codegen: the compiled kernel has the same opcode multiset as before at num_warps ∈ {2, 4, 8},
differing only in instruction scheduling order. Access widths are unchanged in the tail path too
(warps=2 → `ld/st.global.v4.b32`, warps=4 → `v2.b32`, warps=8 → scalar `b32`), so the mask costs
no vectorization.

Timing at k=7168, relative to the kernel this replaces:

| live rows / expert | H200 w8 | H200 w4 | B200 w8 | B200 w4 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 32 | −0.18% | −0.38% | −0.59% | +1.11% |
| 256 | −0.65% | −0.10% | −1.66% | +1.46% |
| 1024 | +0.09% | +0.20% | −0.32% | 0.00% |

For reference, a newly-working shape (no prior number — it asserted): k=3584, 8 experts, 1024
live rows per expert — 25.4 µs on H200, 14.6 µs on B200.

Reproduction note: in a CUDA-graph A/B loop the first variant measured reads roughly 10% fast on
sub-2 µs shapes; interleave the variants and swap their order before trusting a small gap.

Not covered here: a multi-node end-to-end decode run on a model whose routed-expert hidden size
isn't 1024-divisible. This change unblocks the fp8 low-latency path for those models at the
kernel level; that e2e run is still outstanding.

title: [diffusion] fix: keep large vocab tables in host memory under layerwise offload
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Layerwise offload streams a component's layers and then moves everything left over
to the device, on the reasonable assumption that the remainder is small — norms, a
patch embed, a time embed. For a text encoder it is not: umT5-XXL's token table is
`256384 x 4096` in fp32, so **3.91 GiB stays resident**, which on a 12 GiB card is a
third of the device.

That residency buys almost nothing. A vocab table is read by **gather, not GEMM** —
one row per token — so Wan's 512-token prompt touches 8 MiB of those 3.91 GiB, and it
does so once per request rather than once per denoising step:

| | |
|---|---|
| resident | 3.91 GiB |
| read per request | 512 x 4096 x 4 B = 8 MiB |
| utilisation | 0.2% |

Streaming it layer by layer would be worse still (3.91 GiB moved to read 8 MiB), so
the table belongs in host memory with the lookup running there and only the result
crossing PCIe.

This is what made `--performance-mode auto` unusable on a 12 GiB card: warmup at the
model's default workload had no headroom left and failed at every probe size.

## Modifications

Before the post-streaming `.to(device)`, swap tables above 256 MiB for placeholders;
restore them afterwards and hook the module so its input goes to the host and its
output comes back. Both call sites are covered — `LayerwiseOffloadManager._initialize`
and the multi-group path in `configure_layerwise_offload`.

Sharded tables are left alone: they are already divided by the world size, and their
output feeds an all-reduce that expects a device tensor.

## Accuracy Tests

Bit-exact. RTX 3060 12 GiB, `Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers`, layerwise offload of
dit/text_encoder/vae, 320x576, 9 frames, 8 steps, seed 1234 — **three runs each way,
six runs, one SHA-256** (`78a2a963...`).

New `test_host_resident_vocab_table.py` covers selection (large table picked, small
table, plain weight matrix and sharded table left alone), the detach/restore round
trip, and that the hooked gather matches a plain lookup — 7 tests. The existing
layerwise/offload/residency suites pass unchanged (136 tests together).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same runs, mean of three:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| peak VRAM | 8540 MiB | **4447 MiB** (-4.0 GiB, -48%) |
| `TextEncodingStage` | 3374.9 ms | 3384.4 ms (+0.28%) |
| total request | 13838.5 ms | 13815.8 ms |

The encode-stage cost is the CPU gather plus an 8 MiB host-to-device copy, once per
request. It does not separate from noise: the per-run ranges overlap (patched 3377–3389
vs baseline 3369–3382), and the total request is lower after the change. Peak VRAM is
also markedly steadier (4420–4500 vs 8000–9180).

title: fix: detect cross-node multimodal transport by nnodes
author: yuanlehome
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

`determine_tensor_transport_mode()` currently treats a non-empty `dist_init_addr` as evidence that the deployment spans multiple nodes.

However, `dist_init_addr` is a process-group rendezvous endpoint rather than a topology signal. Single-node multi-GPU TP deployments may also set it to bootstrap the TP process group.

The inverse is also possible: in Ray multi-node TP/PP, the generated rendezvous address is injected into scheduler-actor copies of `ServerArgs`, while the `TokenizerManager` can retain the original `dist_init_addr=None`. External launchers using an `env://` rendezvous can produce the same state. Requiring both `nnodes > 1` and a non-empty address would therefore let the tokenizer select node-local CUDA IPC/SHM while schedulers select the default transport.

The original false positive selects the `"default"` transport on a single node, causing `wrap_shm_features()` to become a no-op. Large multimodal pixel tensors are then pickled and broadcast through Gloo for every request. In an affected five-image document workload, this resulted in 2.2–6.5 GB transfers and 18–33 seconds spent in `recv_requests`.

`nnodes` directly represents whether the deployment is multi-node and is therefore the appropriate source of truth.

## Modifications

- Determine cross-node topology using `server_args.nnodes > 1`, independently of `server_args.dist_init_addr`.
- Move `TensorTransportMode` and `determine_tensor_transport_mode()` into the existing `sglang.srt.multimodal.transport` package as the shared implementation.
- Update the tokenizer manager, disaggregated encoder receiver, native Rust multimodal path, and `mm_utils` to use the shared helper.
- Remove the duplicated implementations and the reverse lazy import from `mm_utils` to `tokenizer_manager`.
- Add a truth-table regression test covering all four combinations of single-node/multi-node topology and present/absent rendezvous address.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable. This change only affects multimodal tensor transport selection and does not modify model computation or outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Before this fix, the affected five-image document workload observed 2.2–6.5 GB of pickled/Gloo-broadcast data and 18–33 seconds per `recv_requests` call.

This change restores the existing shared-memory transport path for single-node multi-GPU TP deployments. No standalone post-change benchmark was run in the local development environment.

- [x] This change has no model accuracy impact.

title: fix(multimodal): keep LLaVA image fetch off the CPU-preprocess timeout budget (flaky test_mixed_batch)
author: ShangmingCai
body:
## Summary

Fixes the flaky `test/registered/vlm/test_vision_openai_server_a.py::TestLlavaServer::test_mixed_batch` (and removes a real robustness gap that affects all LLaVA‑family models in production).

`LlavaImageProcessor._process_single_image` ran the **entire** image pipeline — network fetch **+** decode **+** CPU preprocessing — inside a single `cpu_executor` (ProcessPool) task, wrapped in:

```python
timeout = int(os.environ.get("REQUEST_TIMEOUT", "10"))
return await asyncio.wait_for(fut, timeout=timeout)
```

So the **network fetch was inside the CPU‑preprocessing timeout budget**. When the image host is transiently slow (e.g. `raw.githubusercontent.com` under CI network contention), the fetch pushes the task past the budget → `asyncio.TimeoutError` → **HTTP 500**.

Two things make it worse:
1. **A `ProcessPoolExecutor` future can't be cancelled once it's running.** On timeout `wait_for` abandons the asyncio wrapper, but the worker keeps grinding the slow fetch. With a small pool and a burst of requests (`test_mixed_batch` fires 12 via a 4‑thread client), stuck workers saturate the pool and **cascade 500s** across otherwise‑fast requests — defeating both the OpenAI client's auto‑retries and the CI test‑level `retry()`.
2. Only LLaVA‑family models hit this: every other VLM uses the base `load_mm_data` path, which already separates cancellable io loading from CPU work. That's why this one test is the flaky one.

## Fix

Split the two phases, matching `BaseMultimodalProcessor`'s existing io/cpu design:

- **fetch + decode** in the shared **io thread pool** (`self.io_executor`), with a couple of retries for transient network blips;
- **CPU‑only preprocessing** in the ProcessPool, so `asyncio.wait_for` now bounds **CPU work only**, never the network.

No new config is required; `SGLANG_MM_LOAD_MAX_RETRIES` (default `2`) tunes the load retries.

## Evidence — flake probability before/after

Controlled fault injection on 1×H200 with `lmms-lab/llava-onevision-qwen2-0.5b-ov`. Each image fetch is made "slow enough to cross the budget" with probability **p = 0.12** (`REQUEST_TIMEOUT=3`, `SGLANG_CPU_WORKERS=4`), reproducing transient network slowness at exactly the point the real code fetches the image. Images served locally (`file://`) so there is **zero real‑network variance** — the only variable between runs is the fix. The exact `test_mixed_batch` body (`image_ids=[0,1,2]*4`, 4‑thread pool) is run **100×** per condition, OpenAI client auto‑retries disabled to expose the raw server‑side rate.

| Metric | Before fix | After fix |
|---|---|---|
| Per‑request server 500 rate | **7.95 %** (159/2001) | **0 %** (0/1200) |
| Single‑attempt `test_mixed_batch` failure | **67 %** (67/100) | **0 %** (0/100) |
| CI‑equivalent failure (`retry(max_retry=1)`) | **42 %** (42/100) | **0 %** (0/100) |
| Server `TimeoutError` / 500 log lines | many | **0** |

## Test plan

- ✅ Before/after fault‑injection measurement above.
- ✅ Real upstream test with the fix, real image URLs, default timeout, no injection:
  `pytest test/registered/vlm/test_vision_openai_server_a.py -k TestLlavaServer` → **6 passed** (incl. `test_mixed_batch`, `test_image_prefix_cache_reuse`).

title: [diffusion] fix: fix loading a block-FP8 quantized MiniMax-H3 DiT
author: decajoin
body: Quantizing the MiniMax-H3 DiT with SGLang's own per_block_cast_to_fp8 yields a standard block-FP8 checkpoint that loads without error and then generates broken output: H3 stores qkv grouped per head, so the DiT already permutes those rows into [q_all, k_all, v_all] as it loads, but the accompanying weight_scale_inv tensor was passed through untouched, leaving every 128x128 tile scaling rows it no longer covered. Apply the same reorder to the scale, counting its rows in blocks rather than channels; head_dim and the block are both 128 so each head's q/k/v occupies whole scale rows, a block size that straddles heads cannot be fixed by a row permutation and now raises. ## Motivation A block-FP8 MiniMax-H3 DiT loads **without any error** and then generates a blank frame. Nothing in the log says anything is wrong: dtypes match, shapes match, `Detected fp8 checkpoint` is printed, the server reaches ready and serves requests at normal speed. Only the output is gone. H3 checkpoints store qkv grouped per attention head — `[h0_q, h0_k, h0_v, h1_q, ...]` — while `QKVParallelLinear` expects `[q_all, k_all, v_all]`. The DiT has always handled this: `_install_qkv_weight_loader` permutes those rows at load time. A block-FP8 checkpoint carries a second tensor alongside the weight, one scale per 128x128 tile, and #35740's row-count gate passes that tensor through untouched: it compares against 21504, while the scale's leading dim is 168. Once the weight rows moved, every tile was still scaling the rows it covered *before* the permutation. This is not specific to any one quantizer. The scale is produced in checkpoint layout — which is correct, a checkpoint should keep the released layout — and applying the reorder is the runtime's job, so any standard block-FP8 H3 checkpoint hits this. `per_block_cast_to_fp8` is SGLang's own quantization helper, so the bug reproduces with SGLang alone: ```python from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.fp8_utils import per_block_cast_to_fp8 # blocks.0.attn.qkv_proj.weight of MiniMax-H3: [21504, 5376] bf16, 56 heads x 128 q, s = per_block_cast_to_fp8(weight.cuda()) # q [21504, 5376] fp8_e4m3 # s [168, 42] fp32 (168 = 56 heads x 3, so one scale row per head's q / k / v) ``` ## Modifications `_install_qkv_weight_loader` now scales both the permutation and the row count gating it down by the block height for a `BlockQuantScaleParameter`, so the same `_install_qkv_row_reorder` from #35740 covers both layouts and the `weight_loader` and `rank_local_weight_transform` paths stay in step. A new module-level `_qkv_scale_block_rows` reads `weight_block_size[0]` off the projection's quant config. - `head_dim` and the block size are both 128, so each head's q/k/v occupies whole scale rows and the row permutation is exact. - A `weight_block_size` that straddles heads cannot be repaired by a row permutation and now raises instead of silently corrupting the model. - Anything not block-quantized — BF16, online fp8, per-tensor fp8, NVFP4 — reports one weight row per scale row and takes the previous path unchanged. - The GGUF path is unaffected: it already stores qkv as `[q_all, k_all, v_all]` and is gated out of the reorder entirely. Files:`python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/minimax_h3.py`, `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_minimax_h3_dit_contract.py`. ## Accuracy Tests **End to end.** Served on 2x RTX 5090, TP=2, layerwise offload for dit and text_encoder, same prompt / seed 42 / 10 steps / 4s / 768p. | | output | frame contrast | frame-to-frame motion | encoded size | |---|---|---|---|---| | BF16 (reference) | normal | 62.5 | 13.6 | 1.7 MB | | block-FP8, **with** this fix | normal | 67.5 | 15.9 | 1.9 MB | | block-FP8, **without** this fix | blank | **4.0** | **0.7** | **0.5 MB** | Without the fix the frame carries no content at all: spatial contrast collapses 16x and inter-frame motion 19x. With the fix, block-FP8 tracks the BF16 reference at PSNR-Y 16.5 dB / SSIM-Y 0.68; the residual difference is sampling-trajectory divergence from fp8 rounding rather than corruption — the two videos show the same scene, subject and action with a mild composition drift. **Unit tests.** New cases in `test_minimax_h3_dit_contract.py` cover the reorder itself, the straddling-block guard, and the untouched non-block-quantized path. The H3 and quantization suites under `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/` pass. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Same configuration as above. This PR does not change any compute path — it only fixes what the loader writes into the scale parameter — so the speed difference is simply block-FP8 versus BF16 weights under layerwise offload: | | time | |---|---| | BF16 | 104.7s | | block-FP8 with this fix | **70.4s** (1.49x) | ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — no user-facing surface changes; block-FP8 checkpoints were already meant to load. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #33395837881](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33395837881) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #33395837928](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33395837928) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): :x: [Run #33395837967](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33395837967)

title: [AMD] Fix Qwen3.5 MTP dropping fused shared-expert weights
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

Since #33889, Qwen3.5 MXFP4 with MTP speculative decoding on MI355X lost about 12% throughput. The cause is that the MTP draft model is loaded without its shared-expert weights.

**What fusion does to the weight layout.** When a Qwen3.5 MoE layer fuses its shared expert, it deliberately does not build a separate `shared_expert` module — the shared expert becomes one more routed expert, living in slot `num_experts`. Any loader for such a layer therefore has to route `mlp.shared_expert.*` into that slot. `qwen3_5.py` does exactly that; `qwen3_5_mtp.py` never learned to.

**Why the target model is unaffected.** In this checkpoint the target's routed experts are MXFP4 while its shared expert stays bf16. Fusing them would push a higher-precision tensor through the quantized routed-expert path, so `can_fuse_shared_expert()` refuses. The target therefore always takes the unfused path, keeps its `shared_expert` module, and loads normally — the gap in the MTP loader is invisible from here.

**Why the draft model is affected, and only recently.** The MTP module is excluded from quantization in full: all 1536 `mtp.*` routed-expert tensors and its shared expert alike. The draft is thus uniformly bf16, nothing is mixed-precision, and fusing it is perfectly valid — the gate correctly says yes. It simply never had the chance before. Until #33889, the target's Quark config installed a single process-wide `disable_shared_experts_fusion` override, which switched fusion off for every runner, draft included. #33889 made that decision per-runner, so the draft started fusing for the first time and immediately ran into the loader gap.

**Why nobody noticed.** With fusion on there is no `shared_expert` module to load into, and the expert mapping only covers slots `0 .. num_experts-1`, so each `mlp.shared_expert.{gate,up,down}_proj.weight` matches nothing and ends at `logger.warning_once("Parameter ... not found in params_dict, skip loading")` — three tensors per TP rank, one suppressed log line, no error. The draft then runs with an uninitialized shared expert. Since a speculative draft cannot corrupt verified output, accuracy is unaffected; the damage appears only as a fall in accept rate, from 0.65 to 0.51, and hence in throughput.

This PR teaches the MTP loader to place those weights into the fused slot, so the draft that #33889 legitimately enabled actually receives them.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5_mtp.py`, mirroring `qwen3_5.py`:

- Size the expert mapping as `num_experts + num_fused_shared_experts` so slot `num_experts` has an entry. The fusion count is read from the constructed modules, because `num_fused_shared_experts` is set on `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration` and the MTP wraps a `Qwen3_5ForCausalLM`, which does not carry it.
- Rewrite `mlp.shared_expert.` to `mlp.experts.{num_experts}.` before the mapping loops.

Both are keyed on the model's actual fusion state rather than on a platform check. When nothing fuses, `num_fused_shared_experts` is `0`, the mapping size is unchanged and the rewrite never fires, so this is a no-op for every non-fusing configuration.

Not covered: the fused-checkpoint variant (a single `experts.gate_up_proj` tensor). `qwen3_5.py` handles that with a dedicated branch that chunks the tensor into `w1`/`w3`; the MTP loader's `load_fused_expert_weights` indexes per expert id and cannot serve a single shared-expert tensor. Adding that path untested seemed worse than leaving it, since no checkpoint on hand exercises it.

## Accuracy Tests

No accuracy change is expected: only the draft model changes, and a speculative draft cannot alter verified output. The visible effect is the accept rate. Measured over ~100 decode-batch samples per point.

| conc | accept_len before | after | accept_rate before | after |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 2.5278 | 2.9533 | 0.5097 | 0.6509 |
| 8 | 2.5507 | 2.9374 | 0.5168 | 0.6457 |
| 16 | 2.5144 | 2.9508 | 0.5054 | 0.6501 |

Skipped weights during load go from 3 per TP rank to 0.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Summary at conc=4

| Config | Total Throughput | Median E2E (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `eda0ddc260d4` (last good) | 5365.74 | 5992.71 | 326.84 | 6.25 |
| `b61a06921e` (#33889) | 4716.15 | 6662.60 | 322.72 | 7.05 |
| `b61a06921e` + PR #35719 | 5429.77 | 5912.64 | 326.93 | 6.11 |

The third row was obtained by switching shared-expert fusion off on `b61a06921e`, which removes the unloaded-shared-expert condition from the draft; this PR removes the same condition by loading the fused weights instead of dropping them.

### Full sweep

MI355X, `amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4`, TP=2, EAGLE MTP (3 steps / topk 1 / 4 draft tokens), page-size 16, `fp8_e4m3` KV, `--attention-backend aiter`, ISL=8192 / OSL=1024, `num_prompts = 10 x conc`, server relaunched per concurrency with `--max-running-requests = conc`. Server flags follow `benchmarks/single_node/fixed_seq_len/qwen3.5_fp4_mi355x_mtp.sh`. Before and after were run back to back on the same GPU pair, both at `7f8f030000`.

| conc | Total Throughput before | after | Delta | Median E2E (ms) before | after | Median TTFT (ms) before | after | Median TPOT (ms) before | after |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 4746.11 | 5417.31 | **+14.14%** | 6726.7 | 5969.1 | 333.3 | 336.7 | 7.07 | 6.22 |

title: [NPU][Bugfix] Fix OOB gather in decode KV allocation when free pool is tight
author: xdtbynd
body: ## Motivation NPUPagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator.alloc_decode crashes with an out-of-bounds gather when the free-page pool is exactly tight (len(self.free_pages) == num_new_pages). start_new_pages = torch.cumsum(need_new_pages, 0) - need_new_pages is a prefix index into self.free_pages. For rows that do not need a new page (need_new_pages == 0), start_new_pages == end_new_pages; for the last row this equals num_new_pages. The subsequent self.free_pages[start_new_pages] then indexes past the end (valid range is [0, len(free_pages) - 1] == [0, num_new_pages - 1]). When the pool has slack, the index still lands in-bounds, so the bug is latent; it only fires under exact exhaustion. Observed in CI (test_npu_schedule_conservativeness.py, gsm8k) — the NPU index-check kernel aborts with exactly this condition, then the server traps and dies: ``` Index out of range in dimension 0: index value 1 exceeds bounds 1! [AIV Block ...] [ASSERT] .../index_check/index_check.h:130: ... Assertion `(idx < bound)' failed. ... EZ9999 ... exception of aivec error ... "AI Core Error" ... http.client.RemoteDisconnected: Remote end closed connection without response ... ConnectionRefusedError: [Errno 111] Connection refused Ran 1 test in 251.536s FAILED (errors=1) ``` ## Modifications - In alloc_decode, clamp the gather index: start_new_pages = start_new_pages.clamp(max=num_new_pages - 1). - The clamp is safe: the clamped rows all satisfy need_new_pages == 0, and out_indices weights them by need_new_pages (via (1 - need_new_pages) and * need_new_pages), so their gathered value is masked out and never used. - The num_new_pages == 0 path returns early, so num_new_pages - 1 >= 0 holds whenever the clamp line executes (no max=-1 degeneracy). ## Accuracy Tests Verified on an Ascend NPU machine. The previously failing test_npu_schedule_conservativeness.py now passes — 2 runs, both OK: - run 1: - run 2: No Index out of range assertion and no EZ9999 ... AI Core Error trap remain. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A: adds one element-wise clamp per decode batch (O(batch size)), negligible versus the free_pages gather. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. title: [multimodal] Fix NVFP4 diffusion models on sm_120 (RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 50xx)
author: whn09
body:
## Motivation

NVFP4 diffusion checkpoints cannot be served on sm_120 GPUs (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell / RTX 50xx). Two independent defects in the shared ModelOpt FP4 path are involved; neither is model-specific.

**1. The default FP4 GEMM backend does not exist on sm_120.**
`CudaPlatformBase.get_modelopt_flashinfer_fp4_backend()` defaults to `"trtllm"`, and `flashinfer.mm_fp4` rejects it there:

```
ValueError: mm_fp4 does not support backend 'trtllm' with capability 120
```

so the first quantized linear aborts and no NVFP4 model runs at all.

**2. The block-scale layout is chosen by a heuristic whose negative branch is unreachable.**
In `ModelOptFp4LinearMethod.process_weights_after_loading()` the `trtllm` branch fetches its own shuffled scale layout and **returns**. Everything still executing below it is therefore a TMA-layout consumer (`cutlass`, `cudnn`, `auto`) — but the layout was instead selected by a module-name test:

```python
uses_flux1_scale_layout = not getattr(
    self.quant_config, "checkpoint_uses_packed_qkv", False
) and getattr(layer, "prefix", "").startswith(
    ("transformer_blocks.", "single_transformer_blocks.")
)
if flashinfer_backend is None or uses_flux1_scale_layout:
```

Any model whose blocks are not named with the FLUX.1 prefixes skips the swizzle and hands the kernel block scales in the wrong layout. This does not raise — it silently produces broken output.

## Modifications

- `runtime/platforms/cuda.py`: default the FP4 GEMM backend to `"auto"` on sm_120 (which resolves to flashinfer's sm_12x NVFP4 kernel) and keep `"trtllm"` elsewhere. `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_FLASHINFER_FP4_GEMM_BACKEND` still overrides. Uses the pre-existing `is_sm120()`, so no other capability changes behaviour.
- `runtime/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py`: apply the 128x4 TMA reshape unconditionally, and delete the unreachable heuristic. This also removes two defensive `getattr()`s and the now-redundant second `_get_fp4_gemm_op()` call.
- `test/unit/test_modelopt_fp4_backend.py`: new unit test pinning the default-backend resolution (sm_120 vs other, all explicit env spellings, unknown value falls back to the platform default).

## Accuracy Tests

Verified on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120) with an NVFP4 MiniMax-H3 checkpoint:

- before: startup fails on (1); forcing a backend past it renders grey noise, which is (2).
- after: output is **bit-identical** (md5 of the produced mp4) to the previously env-forced workaround, with no environment variables set. Same seed, same request, three runs.

`python -m pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_modelopt_fp4_backend.py` — 4 passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance change is expected or measured: the same kernel is selected, and the scale reshape is a one-time weight-load step. Paired single-GPU runs before/after differ by 0.2%, inside this box's run-to-run floor.

title: [multimodal] MiniMax-H3: fix quantized qkv scales and missing-param policy
author: whn09
body:
## Motivation

Two MiniMax-H3 model-side defects that only appear on a quantized checkpoint (NVFP4 or fp8).

**1. Per-output-row quantization metadata is not reordered with its rows.**
MiniMax-H3 checkpoints store qkv grouped, so `_install_qkv_weight_loader()` permutes the fused qkv weight's output rows into `q|k|v` order via `_reorder_grouped_qkv_to_qkv()`. NVFP4 block scales and fp8 per-channel scales are indexed by that same output row, and they were loaded unpermuted — every scale ends up attached to the wrong row. The weights are correct; the dequantized values are not. The symptom is grey mush, with no error anywhere.

**2. `_mark_missing_params_required()` overwrites each quant method's own missing-parameter policy.**
A quant method declares in `create_weights()` what it can synthesize when a scale is absent from the checkpoint — weight-only NVFP4 has no `input_scale` and marks it `missing_param_init = "ones"`. H3 then blanket-stamps every parameter `"error"`, so the declaration is lost and the loader raises:

```
ValueError: Required checkpoint parameter '...input_scale' was not loaded
```

## Modifications

- New module-level helper `_install_qkv_row_reorder()` wraps a qkv parameter's weight loader (and its `rank_local_weight_transform`, needed by rank-local FSDP) with the same row permutation used for the weight. Applied to every `qkv_proj` parameter except the weight itself.
  The gate is the row count: a tensor whose leading dim is not the checkpoint's qkv row count is passed through untouched, which covers per-tensor scalars and swizzled block-scale layouts that are not row-indexed. It reads the **loaded checkpoint tensor**, not the local parameter, so it also holds under tensor parallelism, where the local parameter only owns its own shard of the rows.
- `_mark_missing_params_required()` now only claims parameters that have no declared policy.
- `test/unit/test_minimax_h3_qkv_scale_reorder.py`: new unit test covering both branches of the row-count gate (row-indexed metadata is permuted, swizzled and per-tensor metadata is not) on the wrapped loader and on `rank_local_weight_transform`.

Depends on nothing else, but on sm_120 both this and #35739 are required to get a working NVFP4 MiniMax-H3 (the two fixes are in different layers, hence separate PRs).

## Accuracy Tests

On one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120) with an NVFP4 MiniMax-H3 checkpoint:

- (2) alone is a hard load failure.
- With (2) fixed, (1) renders grey mush.
- With both fixed, output is structurally the same as the bf16 checkpoint, and bit-identical across repeated runs at the same seed.

The reorder is only reachable for a quantized checkpoint with per-row scales; a bf16 run has no parameters other than the weight on `qkv_proj`, so it is unaffected.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Weight-load-time only; no change to the forward path and none measured (paired runs within 0.2%).

title: Fix overlap prebuilt row reuse race
author: jasonjk-park
body:
Wait for outstanding overlap forward work before prebuilt batch processing can seed a reused request-pool row.

## Motivation

Bug fix for race condition in FutureMap.

publish() call can happen in two cases:
(1) in forward stream after draft+verify.
(2) in schedule stream, when PD disagg is enabled, and prefill request is arriving.

publish() modifies shared states in FutureMap, so they must be ordered correctly to avoid race.

publish_ready cannot be used for synchronization because stash() after record also has FutureMap shared state modification.

## Modifications

(1) schedule stream to wait for forward stream before calling publish in PD disagg
(2) remove unnecessary chaining in record as (1) guarantees ordering
(3) unit test

title: fix: FA4 paged-KV zero-size page-table registers on SM90
author: razorback16
body:
## Motivation

Serving `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8` with `--attention-backend fa4` on a GH200 (Hopper, SM90) crashes in the scheduler during startup warmup, before the server ever accepts a request:

```
Generate warm up request for compiling DeepGEMM...
[2026-08-20 14:09:01] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 5174, in run_scheduler_process
    scheduler.run_event_loop()
  [...]
  File "sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py", line 1212, in self_attention
    attn_output = self.attn(q, k, v, forward_batch)
  File "sglang/srt/layers/attention/hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py", line 1134, in forward_extend
    return self.full_attn_backend.forward_extend(
  File "sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashattention_backend.py", line 1496, in forward_extend
    result = flash_attn_with_kvcache(
  File "sglang/kernels/ops/attention/flash_attention_v4.py", line 276, in flash_attn_with_kvcache
    result = flash_attn_varlen_func(
  File "sglang/kernels/ops/attention/flash_attn/cute/interface.py", line 1628, in _flash_attn_fwd
    _flash_attn_fwd.compile_cache[compile_key] = cute.compile(
  [... CUTLASS DSL trace-building frames elided ...]
  File "sglang/kernels/ops/attention/flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd_sm90.py", line 806, in then_block_9
    self.load(
  File "sglang/kernels/ops/attention/flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd_sm90.py", line 983, in while_after_block_2
    paged_kv_manager = PagedKVManager.create(
  File "sglang/kernels/ops/attention/flash_attn/cute/paged_kv.py", line 119, in create
    tPrPage = cute.make_rmem_tensor((page_entry_per_thread,), Int32)
  [...]
  File "nvidia_cutlass_dsl/dsl_packages/cutlass/cute/core.py", line 339, in _check_shape
    raise ValueError(
        f"Expected size in shape to be strictly positive, but got {shape}"
    )
ValueError: Expected size in shape to be strictly positive, but got 0
```

Environment: GH200 480GB (SM90), CUDA 13.2, `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` 4.6.2, sglang built from source at `eac91ac36` (line numbers above are from that commit). Reproduced with:

```
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 \
  --attention-backend fa4 --kv-cache-dtype auto \
  --speculative-algorithm DFLASH \
  --speculative-draft-model-path z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 8
```

### Root cause

`PagedKVManager.create()` sizes its per-thread page-table registers with a floor division:

```python
page_entry_per_thread = n_block_size // num_threads   # num_threads = 128
```

When `tile_n < 128` this evaluates to `0`, and `cute.make_rmem_tensor((0,), Int32)` fails the shape check above.

Qwen3.8-27B's full-attention layers have `head_dim=256`, and `_tile_size_fwd_sm90()` returns `tile_n = 80` for that head dim (64 with a sliding window). sglang's default `page_size=1` never equals `tile_n`, so the non-TMA cp.async path — the one that stages the page table in registers — is always the one selected. So every paged-KV FA4 run on SM90 at `head_dim=256` hits this; `head_dim=192` is affected too (`tile_n` 112 / 96).

This is the same assertion seen in #32118 (merged) and #31903, but those addressed the SM100 diff-headdim split-KV case by not shrinking `tile_n` to 64 in `interface.py`; the division itself was left as-is. That doesn't cover SM90, where `tile_n = 80` is not a conditional shrink but the tile the heuristic picks unconditionally — there is no configuration that steers around it.

Upstream FA4 (`Dao-AILab/flash-attention`, `flash_attn/cute/paged_kv.py`) already uses ceiling division here, with a comment about counting the final partially populated wave of rows. sglang's vendored copy diverged.

## Modifications

One line in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/flash_attn/cute/paged_kv.py`: use `cute.ceil_div` instead of floor division.

Why `ceil` is the right size rather than merely non-zero: `load_KV()` indexes `tPrXPtr[m // gmem_threads_per_row]` for `m` in `range(n_block_size * gmem_threads_per_row / num_threads)`, so the largest index used needs exactly `ceil(n_block_size / num_threads)` entries. The entries this over-allocates when `n_block_size < num_threads` are already predicated off by the `row < n_block_size` check in `load_page_table()` (which writes `page = 0`), and are never consumed by the `shuffle_sync` in `load_KV()`.

Risk is limited to configurations that cannot currently run: `ceil == floor` whenever `n_block_size % num_threads == 0`, which is true of every tile that compiles today, so those kernels are bit-identical.

## Accuracy Tests

Standalone script calling `flash_attn_with_kvcache` on the paged path, checked against an fp32 SDPA reference, on GH200 (SM90). Deliberately shuffled page tables so page-index/offset mix-ups can't hide. Every case fails to compile on `main` and passes with this change:

| case | page_size | causal | window | max abs err |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| b1, s_q=s_k=512 | 1 | yes | – | 0.0156 |
| b3 ragged, s_q=[300,17,128], s_k=[300,1000,128] | 1 | yes | – | 0.0156 |
| b4 spec-decode, s_q=8, s_k=[513,80,81,1024] | 1 | yes | – | 0.0039 |
| b2, non-causal | 1 | no | – | 0.0039 |
| b2, multi-token pages | 64 | yes | – | 0.0156 |
| b2, sliding window (tile_n=64) | 1 | yes | (256, 0) | 0.0078 |

(`ref_absmax` ≈ 1.3–4.1, so these are bf16 rounding.)

End-to-end: `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8` on GH200 with `--attention-backend fa4` now completes startup warmup and serves. A 7044-token prompt with a needle placed mid-context returned the needle exactly, which exercises many `n_block` iterations of the cp.async page-table path rather than just compilation.

Not covered: SM100. `ceil == floor` for the tiles that arch uses, so no behavior change is expected there, but I don't have Blackwell hardware to confirm.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No impact. `page_entry_per_thread` is a compile-time constant and the generated kernel is unchanged for every configuration that compiles today.

## Follow-up (deliberately not in this PR)

With the root cause fixed, the `not (page_table is not None and q_stage == 1)` guard added by #32118 could likely be relaxed to restore its SMEM-saving `tile_n = 64` for SM100 diff-headdim decode. I can't validate that without Blackwell, so I've left it alone.

## Note on test coverage

`test/registered/attention/unittests/dense/test_fa4.py` runs `HEAD_DIM = 64` only, which is why this went unnoticed — no FA4 test exercises a `tile_n` that isn't a multiple of 128. Precedent: #32118 fixed the same assertion in this subsystem and validated it with a standalone repro rather than a committed test. Happy to add a regression case (here or under `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/`) gated to SM90 if reviewers want one; `1-gpu-large` is an H100 runner, so it would genuinely guard this.
