title: fix(unified-memory): evict Full KV for Mamba byte shortfalls
author: seokwoosong
body:
## Motivation

Full KV and Mamba states share one byte arena when unified memory is enabled, but a Mamba allocation is constrained by two independent resources:

- free Mamba virtual IDs; and
- enough backing bytes in the shared Full/Mamba arena.

The Full and Mamba allocators grow from opposite ends of that arena. Free Mamba virtual IDs describe the remaining ID space, while schedulable Mamba capacity is also bounded by the bytes that can be obtained from the shared gap after peer compaction. A request can therefore have enough free Mamba IDs but still be unable to allocate a state because the Full frontier occupies the bytes needed for another Mamba state.

Before this change, allocation recovery routed every Mamba shortfall to the Mamba cache only. This works when the shortfall is caused by virtual-ID pressure, because evicting a cached Mamba state recycles its virtual ID and backing bytes. However, it cannot resolve a byte-only shortfall. Once no evictable Mamba state remains, Mamba eviction cannot reclaim bytes held by
Full KV. Full rows must be evicted to create peer holes that compaction can convert into additional shared gap for Mamba.

The failing sequence was therefore:

```text
free Mamba IDs > 0
but schedulable Mamba slots == 0 because Full occupies the shared bytes
-> Mamba-only eviction makes no allocator-visible capacity gain
-> the Mamba allocation retry fails
```

The subsequent retry could fail with:

```text
AssertionError: Not enough space for mamba ping pong idx, try to increase --mamba-full-memory-ratio.
```

## Modifications

- Treat `EvictParams.mamba_num` as an allocation shortfall and reconstruct the absolute Mamba allocation target from the allocator-visible capacity.
- Separate virtual-ID pressure from shared-byte pressure:
  - evict cached Mamba states only for the missing virtual IDs; and
  - reclaim Full cache rows only for any remaining Mamba byte shortfall.
- Recheck the Mamba virtual-ID target after Mamba eviction and skip the Full
  donor pass if that target is still unsatisfied, because Full rows can supply
  shared bytes but cannot create Mamba virtual IDs.
- Allow a Full-cache donor pass to stop on the Mamba allocator's schedulable-capacity target, so it evicts only as much Full KV as the pending Mamba allocation needs.
- Convert the aggregate Mamba byte shortfall to Full-token rows with one ceiling operation, avoiding per-slot over-eviction.
- Add CPU regression coverage for byte-only pressure, ID-only pressure, mixed pressure, unavailable or partially recovered IDs, target-aware stopping, and aggregate byte conversion.

This change is limited to `UnifiedMambaTokenToKVPoolAllocator`. It does not add the unvalidated reverse Mamba-to-Full donor path, and it does not change the existing non-unified allocation paths.

PR #34441 identifies the same shared-byte starvation root cause, but wires full-cost eviction into individual count-based allocation call sites. This PR centralizes the fix in current `main`'s allocation-aware `evict_for_alloc()` path, separates virtual-ID from byte pressure, and stops at actual allocator capacity to avoid unnecessary Mamba/Full eviction and repeated per-slot rounding.

## Accuracy Tests

Model-output accuracy is not expected to change. The relevant risk is allocation/eviction correctness.

Focused unit tests:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_multi_ended_allocator.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_radix_allocation_eviction.py
# 77 passed

PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py::TestUnifiedRadixAllocationEvictionRealComponents::test_allocation_target_stops_after_one_internal_tombstone \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py::TestUnifiedRadixAllocationEvictionRealComponents::test_explicit_evict_continues_across_internal_steps
# 2 passed, 8 subtests passed

PYTHONPATH=python python \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_radix_allocation_eviction.py
# Ran 11 tests: OK
```

Formatting and repository checks:

```bash
pre-commit run --files \
  python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/multi_ended_allocator.py \
  python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_radix_allocation_eviction.py
# Passed

pre-commit run --all-files
# All Python and common repository hooks passed.
# Rust-only hooks could not run because cargo/rustup are not installed in the
# local test environment; this PR does not modify Rust files.
```

The patch was also tested with a real Unified-only server:

- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090, 32 GB, driver 610.62
- Model: Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B, BF16
- Relevant server options: `--enable-unified-memory --max-total-tokens 120000 --max-mamba-cache-size 24 --max-running-requests 8 --chunked-prefill-size 1024 --max-prefill-tokens 16384 --disable-cuda-graph --attention-backend triton --mamba-backend triton`
- Workload: 16 groups x 2 rounds, 10,000 input tokens, 64 output tokens, concurrency 4, shared-prefix ratio 0.95
- Result: 32/32 requests completed, 0 failed
- Observed pressure: 417,136 Full tokens evicted across 371 eviction events
- The Mamba allocation assertion did not recur.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The new logic runs only on allocation-driven eviction; it does not add work to model forward or allocation attempts that already have sufficient capacity.

A same-base, three-run low-pressure comparison was performed before the final upstream rebase. Each run used Qwen3.5-0.8B BF16 on the same RTX 5090, Unified-only mode, 12 groups x 2 rounds, 3,000 input tokens, 64 output tokens, concurrency 4, and no eviction:

| Variant | Mean total throughput | Mean TPOT |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline (`a7e3f590ca`) | 18,704.479 tok/s | 9.553452 ms |
| Patch on the same base | 18,527.228 tok/s | 9.582765 ms |
| Delta | -0.95% | +0.31% |

The result is within the observed run-to-run variance and does not indicate a material steady-state regression. The final rebased commit was separately revalidated with the pressure workload described above; that run reached 18,895.58 total tok/s, but it is reported as a functional stress result rather than a baseline comparison.

(Model accuracy is N/A because model math is unchanged; allocation correctness and speed results are provided above.)

title: [Diffusion] Fix the five unit tests failing on main
author: kevin-mii
body:
## Motivation

Five tests under `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit` fail on current main. They
never ran in CUDA CI — the nested unit directories (`realtime/`, `sana_wm/`) sit outside
the CI file glob, and one expectation depended on the host GPU — so the failures
accumulated silently. Two of the five are real runtime bugs in the realtime camera
stack, three are stale test pins. This PR fixes all five so the full diffusion unit
suite runs green.

## Modifications

Three commits, one per failure class:

1. **Report no camera signal until a control has arrived** (runtime bug,
   `runtime/realtime/control_signals.py`, `runtime/realtime/states/camera_control.py`).
   `ControlStateQueue.sample_chunk` synthesized held-state transitions even when nothing
   had ever been pushed, so a fresh realtime session reported its default camera state
   as an active signal instead of no signal. The queue now tracks whether any control
   was received: before the first push `sample_chunk` returns `None`; after one —
   including a camera action script, which is itself a signal, so a drained script holds
   its final state rather than reverting to no-signal — the current state is held as
   before. Also repairs two stale expectations in the runtime test (fresh-session
   samples; a latent-prep stub missing config fields the code under test reads).
2. **Restore the RMS downscale in the cached camera branches** (runtime bug,
   `runtime/models/dits/sana_wm_components.py`). The dense camera branches
   (`_cam_branch`, `_cam_branch_softmax`) downscale post-UCPE q/k/v to the pre-UCPE
   per-token RMS before attending; the cached streaming wrappers skipped it, so a single
   chunk with no carried state no longer reduced to the dense computation — the contract
   both the cached scans' comments and `test_cam_gdn_cached_single_chunk_reduces_to_dense`
   pin. Both cached wrappers now apply the same downscale. Non-streaming (dense) outputs
   are unchanged; the cached streaming path now matches the dense path's numerics.
3. **Repair stale webui pins and pin the consistency platform** (test-only,
   `test/unit/realtime/test_realtime_webui.py`, `test/unit/test_consistency_metrics.py`).
   The webui test pinned asset versions and UI strings several revisions behind the
   shipped webui; the pins are updated to the current assets. The consistency-metrics
   test asserted ground-truth candidate paths hard-coded with an `h100/` prefix while
   the code under test derives the platform from the host GPU
   (`get_consistency_platform()`: sm120 -> `5090`, Blackwell -> `b200`, else `h100`),
   so the test only passed on Hopper-class hosts. The tests now pin
   `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_CONSISTENCY_PLATFORM=h100` via monkeypatch — the suite's existing
   idiom for platform-dependent cases — so the candidate-resolution logic is tested
   against a fixed input on every host. Product behavior (auto-detect with env
   override) is unchanged.

title: Fix DFLASH aux hidden-state capture on mHC models
author: zijiexia
body:
## Motivation

`Glm5NextModel._prepare_aux_hidden_state()`, added in #36708, unconditionally computes `hidden_states + residual`. GLM-5.3-Flash sets `mhc=True`, and under mHC every `MHCLayerCommunicator.postprocess_layer()` branch returns `residual=None` — the residual is folded into the widened `[tokens, hc_mult * hidden]` state that `hc_contract()` on the very next line is there to merge back down.

So serving GLM-5.3-Flash with `--speculative-algorithm DFLASH` dies on every TP rank during decode CUDA-graph capture (weights load fine first, so the failure looks late):

```
File "python/sglang/srt/models/glm5_next.py", line 1081, in _prepare_aux_hidden_state
    aux_hidden_state = hidden_states + residual
TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'Tensor' and 'NoneType'
```

## Modifications

- Skip the add when there is no separate residual to fold in, and widen the annotation to `Optional[torch.Tensor]`.
- Cover the `residual=None` case for both the DFLASH and the plain EAGLE3 capture paths. The existing tests only exercised the residual-is-a-tensor case, which is the state that cannot occur on an mHC model.
- Register `test/registered/unit/models/test_glm5_next_dflash_capture.py` with `register_cpu_ci` and give it a `__main__` entry. Without them `test/run_suite.py` never discovers the file, so none of its tests have ever run in CI — that is why this crash landed green.

## Accuracy Test

8xB300, TP8/EP8, real checkpoint, draft `incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2`, `--dsa-{prefill,decode}-backend trtllm --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --speculative-draft-attention-backend fa4`. The server now reaches ready, and 5-shot GSM8K (temperature 0) gives:

| parallel | accuracy | accept length (token-weighted) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (60 q) | 0.950 | 4.85 |
| 32 (200 q) | 0.910 | 4.86 |

Unit tests, CPU-only, via the CI invocation `python3 <file> -f`: 5 passed. Reverting only the model change while keeping the new tests makes exactly the 2 new tests fail.

title: fix: report the real backend for non-CUDA CI registrations in /rerun-test
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

`/rerun-group hicache` replies with:

> ⛔ `registered/hicache/test_hicache_storage_umbp_backend.py`: No `register_cuda_ci(runner_config=...)` or `register_cpu_ci()` found in `test/registered/hicache/test_hicache_storage_umbp_backend.py`. This file may not be a registered CI test.

That is false. The file *is* registered — `register_amd_ci(suite="nightly-amd-8-gpu-mi35x-deepseek-v4-flash")` — and it already runs on every PR touching the main package, via `stage-c-dsv4-flash-fp4-fp8-amd-mi35x-rocm720` in `pr-test-amd-rocm720.yml`. `detect_suite` simply doesn't recognise non-CUDA/CPU registrations, so every AMD/NPU/XPU/MUSA/MLX file lands in the "unregistered" fallback. Measured over `test/registered/`, **354 files** get this wrong message today.

It sends readers down the wrong path: the message says "fix the registration", when the registration is correct and the actual answer is `/rerun-failed-ci` (which reruns every failed workflow on the head SHA, `pr-test-amd*.yml` included).

## Modifications

`detect_suite` now recognises `register_{amd,npu,xpu,musa,mlx}_ci` and names the backend, its suite, and where the rerun actually lives:

> `test/registered/hicache/test_hicache_storage_umbp_backend.py` is registered for AMD (suite `nightly-amd-8-gpu-mi35x-deepseek-v4-flash`), not for CUDA or CPU; rerun-test.yml has no AMD job. Rerun it with /rerun-failed-ci, or dispatch the AMD workflow manually.

Message-only: nothing about dispatch changes. The new branch sits after the CUDA / CPU / legacy-`suite=` checks, so it can only replace the final fallback.

Scope deliberately kept to accuracy. Two things considered and left out:

- **Making `/rerun-test` dispatch AMD/NPU.** `rerun-test.yml` has cuda / multimodal_gen / cpu jobs only, and `runner_configs.yml` — which turns "where does this run, how are deps installed" into data — is CUDA-only; each AMD job hardcodes `runs-on` plus `amd_ci_start_container.sh` / `amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` / `ensure_vram_clear.sh`. Extracting that is worth doing on its own, and would make an AMD job here nearly free, but it should not be driven by a wrong error string. Meanwhile `/rerun-failed-ci` already covers these at job granularity.
- **Filtering these files out of `/rerun-group` / wildcard expansion** so a directory sweep doesn't report them at all. Reasonable, but it needs a skipped-vs-failed distinction plumbed through the resolver; not worth it to silence one accurate line.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the code with pre-commit.
- [x] Verified over all of `test/registered/`: 1240 dispatchable resolutions and the 4 legacy-`suite=` messages are byte-identical before and after; the 354 files that previously got "may not be a registered CI test" now report their real backend (AMD / NPU / XPU / MUSA / MLX, each spot-checked).

SGLang's Base CPU CI installs development dependencies with `--prerelease allow`. title: fix(qsa): route exact SM120 to FlashInfer sparse decode
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #36537.

`Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` on RTX PRO 6000 (SM120) can enter a token-ID-0 (`!`) loop for thinking + tools, or fail earlier while capturing the QSA/NEXTN decode graphs. The returned token IDs are already zero before `qwen3_coder` post-processing, so the parser exposes the symptom but does not generate the corrupt tokens.

The QSA sparse-decode resolver is the failing boundary:

```text
current qwen4-main-squashed
  SM120 -> resolver rejects the arch -> packed FA4 varlen fallback -> CuTe MLIR failure
  SM121 -> FlashInfer paged decode -> silent long-context corruption

after this PR
  SM100 -> FlashInfer paged decode (unchanged)
  SM120 -> FlashInfer paged decode (enabled and validated)
  SM121 -> excluded from this path (no silent-corruption claim)
```

The existing `is_sm120_supported()` helper matches compute-capability major 12, including SM121/GB10. That family-wide predicate is unsafe here: real-weight SM121 testing reports token-0 corruption rising from 1/4 runs at 120K tokens to 4/4 at 210K tokens when this decode path is forced ([data](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36556#issuecomment-5448079828)); #36716 independently reports NaN logits on the same architecture. Conversely, real-weight SM120 testing is clean at 229K-244K tokens.

This is intentionally a focused correctness hotfix for `qwen4-main-squashed`:

- it narrows the architecture handling proposed in #36556 after the later SM121 corruption evidence;
- it corrects #36649, which currently enables SM121 while leaving the validated SM120 device on the failing fallback;
- it does not duplicate the direct-paged Triton kernel and broader SM120 optimization work in draft PR #36787.

## Modifications

- Add exact `is_sm120()` detection for compute capability `(12, 0)`, symmetric with the existing exact `is_sm121()` helper.
- Route the existing FlashInfer paged sparse-decode API on SM100 or exact SM120 only.
- Preserve the existing fallback and all non-SM12x behavior.
- Add regression coverage for exact capability detection and the SM100 / SM120 / other-SM12x resolver matrix.

The second commit is the formatting-only commit from #36667, kept separate from
the functional fix. `qwen4-main-squashed` predates the repository-wide
pre-commit formatting baseline, while the lint workflow runs
`pre-commit --all-files`; consequently even one-file PRs against this branch
fail lint. This commit contains no behavior changes and will disappear from the
PR diff once #36667 lands on the base branch.

The earlier candidate also rerouted SM120 to SGLang FA4 when FlashInfer was unavailable. That hunk is deliberately not included: short-shape numerics passed, but long-context evidence shows the packed fallback itself can corrupt after crossing a KV page. This PR only enables the path with real-weight long-context validation.

## Accuracy Tests

### Local SM120 hardware validation

Environment: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, compute capability `(12, 0)`, CUDA 13.0.3, torch 2.13.0, FlashInfer 0.6.17, base `639db13527`.

Kernel correctness uses the model's QSA decode shape (`q=[1,24,256]`, `kv=[2051,2,256]`, BF16, page size 64) against a PyTorch reference:

| Mode | Max absolute error | Mean absolute error | Finite |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| eager | 0.00055800 | 0.00008352 | yes |
| CUDA Graph replay | 0.00066295 | 0.00008163 | yes |

Reduced-config RED/GREEN replay retained the official QSA, NEXTN, CUDA Graph, chat-template, reasoning-parser, and tool-parser paths while using dummy weights (4 layers, 8 experts, PLE vocab 200K):

- base: `_resolve_trtllm_sparse_decode()` returned `None`; warmup failed in pip `flash_attn.cute` with `expects coord and shape of view are weakly congruent`;
- patched: FlashInfer resolver selected; target-verify, draft-decode, and draft-extend CUDA graphs all captured; the server became healthy;
- the issue-shaped thinking + tools request completed 32 tokens with zero token ID 0.

Dummy weights do **not** measure semantic model accuracy. The full NVFP4 checkpoint is about 125.9 GiB and was not available on this assigned node, so no local GSM8K/MMLU score is claimed.

### Independent real-weight SM120 results

These results were posted by independent users running the same active SM120 resolver path. They are attributed here rather than presented as local measurements.

| Validation | Result | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Exact #36537 thinking + tool-call repro | structured tool call; reasoning active; zero `!` | [RTX PRO 6000 report](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/36537#issuecomment-5442716073) |
| Needle-in-a-haystack, real NVFP4 weights, TP1 | **5/5 exact** at about 229.5K prompt tokens, depths 0.1/0.3/0.5/0.7/0.9 | [report](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36556#issuecomment-5446778791) |
| Needle-in-a-haystack, real NVFP4 weights, TP2, gate-only patch | **5/5 exact** at 244,437 prompt tokens | [report](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36556#issuecomment-5444818241) |
| 65-task repository-fixing agent benchmark | **59/65 resolved (90.8%)**, 852,214 generated tokens, 0 infrastructure failures or decode degeneration | [report](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36556#issuecomment-5446110226) |

### Tests

- RTX PRO 6000: `PYTHONPATH=python pytest -q test/registered/kernels/test_qsa.py` -> **58 passed**
- `SKIP=no-commit-to-branch pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure` -> passed with a clean second pass
- `python3 -m compileall` on all changed files -> passed
- `ruff check --select F821,UP037` on all changed files -> passed
- `git diff --check` -> passed

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This PR changes correctness routing, not kernel implementation. A like-for-like SM120 baseline throughput comparison is not meaningful because the base path fails during warmup. The larger direct-paged performance work remains in #36787; this patch keeps the existing SM100 route unchanged and adds a regression test for it.

title: perf: fix overlap scheduling for NVIDIA Confidential Computing(CC) on Blackwell
author: elvischenv
body:
## Motivation

Under NVIDIA Confidential Computing (CC), `cudaMemcpyAsync` (D2H) is forced synchronous — it blocks at issue — so the per-step readback of `next_token_ids` / logprobs serializes onto the scheduler's critical path and kills decode overlap.

## Modifications

**`async device->host result-readback worker`** (afdde3e4a0)
- New `python/sglang/srt/managers/async_d2h_copy_worker.py` (`AsyncD2HCopyWorker`): runs the per-step D2H copy on a dedicated thread with its own private CUDA stream, off the scheduler's critical path, so overlap is preserved. `submit()` returns a `HostCopyDone` that is a drop-in for the `copy_done` CUDA event, so no result-processing code changes.
- Wired into `scheduler.py` / `managers/utils.py`; only routed through the worker when CC is detected.
- Adds `is_confidential_compute()` to `srt/utils/common.py`.

**`TRTLLM-style CC detection`** (512bd0994a)
- Prefers `nvmlSystemGetConfComputeSettings` and treats PPCIE as CC, falling back to the simple query on older GPUs.

**Review follow-ups** (0d4f4717df, 437dc1b347, cc18c816fe)
- The worker thread pins itself to the creating thread's device. Without this it defaults to device 0, and the stream context manager's enter/exit opens a CUDA context there on every non-zero rank — measured at **+622 MiB on GPU 0** from a single rank-1 process (2xB200).
- CC detection is gated on `is_cuda()` rather than `torch.cuda.is_available()`, which is also true on ROCm. AMD launches were reaching the NVML path and logging at ERROR on every scheduler process; the "cannot query" cases are now `warning`, since the fallback (`False`) is correct.
- The override moved to `envs.SGLANG_FORCE_CONFIDENTIAL_COMPUTE` (`EnvBool(None)`, `FORCE_` verb for an autodetect override) per `.claude/skills/env-var-conventions`. This also fixes a footgun: the previous `forced == "1"` check made `SGLANG_CONFIDENTIAL_COMPUTE=true` silently read as *off*.
- Test moved to `test/registered/unit/managers/` to match the current registered-test layout.
- Comments trimmed per `.claude/rules/comment-style.md` (class docstring 30 -> 9 lines; file 147 -> 106).

## Tests

`test/registered/unit/managers/test_async_d2h_copy_worker.py` — worker unit tests. `test_copy_waits_for_the_producing_stream` queues `torch.cuda._sleep` + `fill_()` on a side stream and submits with that stream current, so it fails if the readiness event is dropped or recorded on the wrong stream (verified against a patched-out `src_ready`: it reads zeros).

`test/registered/scheduler/test_async_d2h_copy_worker_server.py` — server-level coverage. CI GPUs never run CC, so the force override is what makes this path reachable. Launches a server with the worker on and runs concurrent greedy `return_logprob` requests, asserting identical completions and 1:1 logprobs. title: [diffusion] Fix the XPU capability gates that broke the Wan2.2 A14B DiT path
author: ckvermaAI
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
Wan2.2-A14B at 720p OOMs on Intel XPU even though peak *allocated* memory is only ~7 GiB on a 24 GiB card. The cause is not capacity but a **vendor string used where a capability check belongs**: several places test for CUDA rather than for the capability they need. XPU therefore takes eager fallbacks that materialise fp32 hidden states (1.44 GiB each at 1280x720x81f, TP=4), a missing `forward_xpu` default aborts the transformer's customized load and falls back to native diffusers (which ignores the offload flags), and the post-eviction cache release never fires. Upstream had already renamed `_module_on_cuda` to `_module_on_supported_device`; XPU was never added to the list.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

1. **`CustomOp.forward_xpu` default**, matching the existing tpu/oot/npu defaults. Without it any subclass lacking one raised `AttributeError` at construction, aborting the customized load.
2. **Eviction learns XPU**: `is_xpu()` in `_module_on_supported_device`, and the `memory_intensive` precondition exempted on XPU only. CUDA/ROCm/NPU unchanged.
3. **`gpu_worker`'s device guard** : `torch.cuda.is_initialized()` is `False` on every non-CUDA build; replaced by `is_cuda() or is_rocm() or is_xpu()`, resolving the module from `current_platform.device_type` rather than torch's accelerator autodetection. MUSA and NPU keep their previous (never-fired) behaviour. `_oom_exceptions()` collapses to `(torch.OutOfMemoryError,)`, which `torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError` already aliases.
4. **Wan causal-VAE encode takes the fused path** — the cat/pad and dup-up3d Triton kernels were gated on `is_cuda` and need the NDHWC weights `_should_use_channels_last_3d` refused on XPU, so encode tried a 1018 MiB stage-0 allocation against a full pool.
5. **fp32 hidden states removed at four sites** — `platform_key()` reports `"xpu"` (upstream), which selects Triton over the pure-torch fallback for five `select_impl` bindings; `fuse_scale_shift_kernel`'s per-frame 4D-shift broadcast is widened past `is_hip()`; `FP32LayerNorm.forward_xpu` stays in bf16 (ATen already accumulates stats in fp32) and falls back to `forward_native` when an affine parameter differs in dtype **or device**, since `forward_native` is what moves weight/bias onto `inputs.device`; `_ScaleResidualNormScaleShift.forward_xpu` gets a Triton kernel that accumulates in fp32 registers and stores in `x.dtype`, because the CUDA (CuTe-DSL) and ROCm (FlyDSL) variants are vendor-specific. Its admission predicate rejects `hidden > 8192`, the bound `forward_cuda` falls back on, and the gate offset is chosen by a `GATE_PER_FRAME` constexpr so the broadcast-vs-per-frame layout contract lives in the code. `MulAdd.forward_xpu` delegates to `forward_cuda`.
6. **Every device test added is an allowlist** (`in ("cuda", "xpu")`), so a new backend is not admitted to a Triton launch or an allocator API it does not implement.
7. **`decoding.py`** covers XPU alongside MPS.

title: fix(qsa): restore SM121 correctness with Humanize and Kernel Design Agent
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #36806; fixes the remaining SM121 / GB10 part of #36537.

QSA decode needs different paths on SM120 and SM121:

- Exact SM120 is numerically correct with FlashInfer's TRT-LLM paged decode.
- On SM121, that path silently corrupts long-context decode. The 120k, 190k,
  and 210k reproductions all returned 32/32 token id 0 (`!`) while the server
  remained healthy and returned HTTP 200.
- Excluding SM121 avoids the corruption, but the existing FA4 CuTe varlen
  implementation does not compile for QSA's packed one-query shape on GB10
  (`expects coord and shape of view are weakly congruent`).

Disabling FlashInfer autotune only makes the incorrect SM121 kernel start; it
does not fix its numerics.

## Changes

- Add one optimized Triton kernel for the exact Qwen3.8 packed-QSA decode
  contract on SM121: BF16, D=256, 12:1 GQA, TP1 24Q/2KV or TP2 12Q/1KV,
  one query per sequence, `1 <= bs <= 128`, and selected KV capacity <=2055.
- Route SM121 directly to this kernel. There is no opt-in switch and no second
  generic SM121 attention kernel in this PR; unsupported calls fail with a
  descriptive contract error.
- Keep SM100/SM120 on the TRT-LLM sparse-decode path and leave the existing
  FA2/FA4 selection unchanged on other architectures.
- Register the kernel and preserve its KDA-1.5 provenance using the integration
  structure from #36865.
- Add reference, architecture-gating, integration, CUDA Graph replay, complete
  validated batch coverage, and repeated atomic-state tests.

The kernel reads live sequence lengths on device, so captured graphs can replay
with changed `cu_seqlens` without host readback.

## Agent workflow

Humanize provided the iterative implementation and review workflow used for
this change. The Kernel Design Agent ran through KDA-1.5 with Codex and Kimi K3
and produced the winning SM121 QSA kernel. This PR fixes SM121 QSA correctness
and integrates that single optimized Triton kernel. Humanize and the Kernel
Design Agent had distinct roles: Humanize structured the workflow, while the
Kernel Design Agent produced the kernel selected for integration.

## Optimized kernel

The original correct Triton implementation launched one CTA per query head, so
the 12 query heads sharing one KV head repeatedly loaded the same K/V rows. The
optimized kernel groups those 12 heads into one CTA, uses BF16 tensor-core QK/PV
products with FP32 online-softmax state, and splits long KV rows across CTAs.
The final split performs a stable FP32 merge and resets its device counter in
the same launch.

Provenance:

- Task: [radixark/KDA-1.5#4](https://github.com/radixark/KDA-1.5/pull/4)
  at `414ce456e14ae8546f77d9356d2c4d955c5bb7f1`
- Winning submission: `b4181149c8884ddb`
- Exact submitted source SHA256:
  `4f9977f88abfea4393a2add3a2c9255699f7e13b981dbc1a976b024b3b00e909`
- Coverage: 15 real TP1/TP2 tensors captured from one- and two-DGX-Spark runs

The packaged kernel passes 15/15 real replays against both the pinned
production output and an independent FP32 reference (`relative-L2 <= 2e-3`),
with exactly one CUDA activity per invocation. Its all/large/small geomean over
the original correct Triton implementation is **2.0702x / 1.6951x / 2.3653x**.
The final source also passed 150,000 consecutive launches with every counter
reset to zero.

An additional GB10 sweep covers both TP topologies, every batch size from 1 to
16, and short plus saturated selected-KV rows: **64/64 passed**, maximum
relative L2 `0.002422`, and speedup `1.41x-5.09x` over the original Triton
implementation.

| Batch | Geomean speedup | Minimum speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 2.72x | 1.71x |
| 2 | 2.31x | 1.76x |
| 3 | 2.02x | 1.79x |
| 4 | 1.93x | 1.63x |
| 5 | 1.82x | 1.56x |
| 6 | 1.67x | 1.41x |
| 7 | 1.77x | 1.68x |
| 8 | 1.72x | 1.57x |
| 9 | 1.73x | 1.61x |
| 10 | 1.67x | 1.54x |
| 11 | 1.64x | 1.48x |
| 12 | 1.61x | 1.48x |
| 13 | 1.79x | 1.52x |
| 14 | 1.77x | 1.51x |
| 15 | 1.82x | 1.55x |
| 16 | 1.83x | 1.58x |

The follow-up extended-batch sweep covers both TP topologies, batch sizes
17/24/32/48/64/96/128, and short, medium, plus saturated KV: **42/42 passed**,
maximum relative L2 `0.002410`, `4.48x` geomean speedup, and `1.58x` minimum
speedup. No case regressed. The worst-case TP1 scratch allocation at the
largest qualified batch is 32.3 MiB.

| Batch | Geomean speedup | Minimum speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 17 | 1.86x | 1.58x |
| 24 | 1.94x | 1.70x |
| 32 | 2.53x | 1.82x |
| 48 | 4.39x | 2.64x |
| 64 | 8.37x | 6.19x |
| 96 | 10.15x | 8.96x |
| 128 | 10.66x | 9.75x |

These are isolated-kernel measurements against the original correct Triton
implementation. End-to-end serving remains intentionally measured at low
concurrency because a single GB10 cannot sustain medium/high-concurrency model
serving without changing the workload.

## End-to-end performance and accuracy

Hardware: one NVIDIA GB10 / SM121 DGX Spark, CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.13.

Model: `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` TP1 with ModelOpt NVFP4,
FlashInfer CUTLASS FP4/MoE, exact FP8 PLE from NVMe, 262,144 context, and NEXTN
(3 steps, top-k 1, 4 draft tokens). The benchmark compared the original
correct Triton implementation with the final KDA kernel under otherwise
identical server flags.

Three-round low-concurrency A/B, 12/12 successful requests per round and the
same 45,946 input plus 1,667 output tokens:

| Concurrency | Metric | Original Triton | KDA | Change |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | Total throughput (tok/s) | 644.51 | 673.19 | **+4.45%** |
| 1 | Mean E2E latency (ms) | 6,173.50 | 5,899.09 | **-4.45%** |
| 1 | Mean TTFT (ms) | 1,914.83 | 1,753.04 | **-8.45%** |
| 4 | Total throughput (tok/s) | 1,068.37 | 1,111.08 | **+4.00%** |
| 4 | Mean E2E latency (ms) | 13,423.72 | 13,080.11 | **-2.56%** |
| 4 | Mean TTFT (ms) | 3,207.84 | 3,073.10 | **-4.20%** |

Accuracy A/B uses the first 50 official GSM8K test examples, five-shot Chat API
prompting, Qwen thinking, greedy decoding, concurrency 4, and a 2048-token
output limit:

| Route | Score | Failed examples |
|---|---:|---:|
| Original Triton | **49/50 (98%)** | index 7 |
| KDA | **49/50 (98%)** | index 7 |

The original correctness validation also passes 20/20 sequential requests,
4/4 concurrent requests, structured tool parsing, and exact NIAH retrieval at
120k, 190k, and 210k tokens with zero token-id-0 output.

Full commands, TPOT/ITL results, replay tables, and the output-limit sensitivity
check are in [this validation comment](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36845#issuecomment-5459371995).

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --files ...`: pass
- `compileall`: pass
- `git diff --check`: pass
- `pytest -q test/registered/kernels/test_qsa.py test/registered/kernels/test_kda_qsa_sm121.py -s`:
  **73 passed** on SM121 after deleting the old implementation
- CUDA Graph replay with changed device-side `cu_seqlens`: pass
- Real tensor replay: **15/15**, production output + FP32 reference
- Synthetic baseline differential: **106/106** cases across bs 1-128
- Complete low-concurrency sweep: **64/64**, TP1/TP2 x bs 1-16 x short/long KV
- Extended-batch sweep: **42/42**, TP1/TP2 x bs 17-128 x short/medium/long KV
- State stress: **150,000/150,000** launches, counters zero

The Base/Extra/AMD workflow failures below are the repository rebase gate, not
test failures in this change: CI currently requires `main@1ec20fd`, while this
PR intentionally targets `qwen4-main-squashed`, so the test jobs were skipped.

title: fix(security): pin multimodal-gen ZMQ scheduler ingress to loopback on wildcard --host
author: wildoranges
body:
## Motivation

Align the multimodal-generation scheduler ingress with the localhost-binding
principle established by PR #21435 ("[Security] 1/N: Bind ZMQ sockets to
localhost to prevent unauthenticated remote access").

PR #21435 bound the ZMQ **broker** to `127.0.0.1`, but the **scheduler** ingress
was left out: `ServerArgs.scheduler_endpoint_for()` derives its bind address
from the public `--host` verbatim, so the standard `--host 0.0.0.0` deployment
binds it to `tcp://0.0.0.0:<port>` (observed `0.0.0.0:5641`). That endpoint
deserializes client bytes with `pickle.loads` over an unauthenticated ZMQ
ROUTER socket (`managers/scheduler.py` `recv_reqs`), i.e. the same unsafe-
deserialization exposure class as CVE-2026-3059 remains remotely reachable
whenever the HTTP API is served on all interfaces.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/server_args/server_args.py`
  - `scheduler_endpoint_for()` now pins wildcard hosts (`0.0.0.0`, `::`) to
    `127.0.0.1`, consistent with the existing `localhost` normalization. An
    explicit non-wildcard host (intentional cross-machine deployments) is still
    honored.
- `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_server_args.py`
  - New `TestSchedulerEndpointBinding` (5 tests): wildcard IPv4/IPv6 pinned to
    loopback, default stays loopback, explicit host honored, replica port
    increment on loopback.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — bind-address logic only; no model/kernel code touched.

title: [Fix] Route the Mooncake MoE A2A backend through Kimi K3's EP-A2A / SP-MoE fast path
author: kyx1999
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!--
Suggested PR title:
[Fix] Route the Mooncake MoE A2A backend through Kimi K3's EP-A2A / SP-MoE fast path
-->

## Motivation

Kimi K3 selects two backend-specific optimizations at construction time:

- `self._ep_a2a` — when the MoE A2A backend routes each row to its experts directly, the MoE region consumes the rank-local rows (an SP-MoE token shard or the DP-local batch) with **no DP gather and no TP reduce**, and every global token is dispatched exactly once.
- `self._sp_moe` — on top of `_ep_a2a`, MoE layers with `attn_tp > 1` convert the deferred `o_proj` attention-TP all-reduce into a reduce-scatter, so the whole MoE front (norms, gate, latent projections, tp1 shared experts, A2A dispatch) runs on `1/attn_tp` of the rows and all-gathers back afterwards.

Both predicates already list the EP-A2A family — `is_megamoe()`, `is_deepep()`, `is_ascend_fuseep()`, `is_mori()` — but **Mooncake was missing**, even though `is_deepep_class_backend()` already classifies Mooncake as a DeepEP-family backend, `DeepEPMoE` documents that Mooncake shares the same interface, and the dispatcher factory builds the same `MaybeTboDeepEPDispatcher` with the `DEEPEP_LL` output format for both.

As a result, `moe_a2a_backend='mooncake'` correctly reached the Mooncake dispatcher on the data plane, but Kimi K3 still treated it as a plain TP/DP MoE:

| Backend  | `_ep_a2a` | `_sp_moe` |
| -------- | --------- | --------- |
| DeepEP   | True      | True      |
| Mooncake | False     | False     |

With `_ep_a2a=False`, K3 first gathers all DP replicas into a global batch before the A2A; with `_sp_moe=False`, the attention output keeps the full `B` rows on every attn-TP rank instead of a `B/attn_tp` shard. On a `TP=32, DP=4` (attn-TP=8) decode config this inflates each process's dispatch input to `~32x` DeepEP's, replicating dispatch, expert GEMM and combine work. The service stays numerically correct but is significantly slower, and it also skews QP-level profiling comparisons because the two backends were being fed very different token-row counts.

The Mooncake side of Kimi K3 support has already been merged into its main branch: https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/3727. This PR is the SGLang-side counterpart so Mooncake reaches full parity with DeepEP on the K3 path.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py`:

- Add `is_mooncake()` to the `_ep_a2a` predicate so Mooncake takes the EP-A2A fast path (no DP gather, no TP reduce) exactly like DeepEP.
- Add `is_mooncake()` to the `_sp_moe` predicate so Mooncake MoE layers with `attn_tp > 1` also perform the reduce-scatter / all-gather sequence-parallel MoE optimization.
- Both predicates are updated together on purpose: changing only `_sp_moe` would shard the input to `B/attn_tp` rows while the MoE still enters the DP-gather path under `_ep_a2a=False`, and the shape assumptions would conflict.
- Update the surrounding comments to include Mooncake (and Ascend-FuseEP) in the enumerated EP-A2A backend list.

Note on memory: enabling `_ep_a2a` for Mooncake switches its shared experts from TP-sharded to per-rank replicated (`_shared_experts_tp1`), matching DeepEP. This adds roughly ~264 MB/layer of replicated shared-expert weights (~24 GB/rank across the MoE layers) — the same cost DeepEP already pays — so H200 memory headroom should be re-checked when deploying with Mooncake.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: fix(glm): mirror should_use_dp_reduce_scatterv() into the MHC communicator
author: ehsan
body:
Fixes the two `should_use_dp_reduce_scatterv()` omissions reported in #36879.

Based on this PR's head (`aa8c950a3d`) rather than `main`, since
`communicator_mhc.py` only exists on this branch.

## Why

Under DP attention with `moe_a2a_backend == none` and
`tp_size == attn_dp_size == moe_ep_size` (e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash
`--tp-size 4 --ep-size 4 --dp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention`),
`should_use_dp_reduce_scatterv()` is true, so
`should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce()` skips the MoE post-experts all-reduce
— on the promise that the layer communicator's scatter performs a
`reduce_scatterv` combine instead. `communicator_mhc.py` was adapted from a
`communicator.py` snapshot predating #24785 and is missing that branch in two
places:

1. **`MHCCommunicateSummableTensorPairFn._scatter_hidden_states`** never
   reduces under SUM_LEN padding (which is every eager DP prefill), so every
   token leaves every MoE layer holding only its owner DP rank's local expert
   shard — 1/4 of the routed experts at EP4. Output is deterministically
   degenerate: repetition loops to the token limit, prompt echo, wrong answers.

2. **`MHCLayerCommunicator.should_use_reduce_scatter`** publishes
   `mlp_reduce_scatter=False` under SUM_LEN. `should_skip_mlp_all_reduce()`
   consults only that flag (unlike `should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce()`,
   which also consults the predicate directly), so once the scatter starts
   reducing, `RowParallelLinear` is still all-reducing the dense MLPs (GLM
   layers 0–2) and the scatter then sums four identical fully-reduced buffers
   — dense-MLP output scaled by exactly **4×**. This second defect is only
   reachable once the first is fixed, so both are fixed here; landing only the
   first ships a quieter regression (fluent output, 22% of tool calls failing
   schema validation).

`main`'s `LayerCommunicator` has had both branches since #22642 (2026-04-14)
and #24785 (2026-05-10) respectively — the latter titled *"Fix reduce_scatterv
producer contract for SUM_LEN"*, i.e. the identical bug class fixed on the base
path 3.5 months before this file was added. The override carries the pre-#24785
fused single-`if` shape but the post-2026-05-20 `dsa_use_prefill_cp` name, and
its docstring notes it was *"Adapted from the GLM reference"* — a stale copy,
not a deliberate divergence.

## Two things deliberately not mirrored from the base

- The fn-identity check stays against
  `MHCCommunicateSummableTensorPairFn._scatter_hidden_states`. Naming the base
  fn (as a verbatim copy would) makes the branch dead on MHC instances.
- The `input_scattered` branch keeps its lack of base's
  `and not self.is_last_layer`. MHC's `_trivial` reduce-scatters the last layer
  itself and needs the flag True there; adding the exclusion would introduce a
  new last-layer double reduction.

`MHCHybridDSACPLayerCommunicator` inherits `should_use_reduce_scatter`, so it
is covered by this change.

## Validation

4×B200, fp8 KV cache, `deep_gemm` MoE runner, CUDA graphs on. Per-rank sum of
input-token logprobs on a fixed 26-token completion prompt, temperature 0,
pinned per DP rank via `routed_dp_rank`; plain-TP reference on the same host
and weights is **−29.7**:

| | rank0 | rank1 | rank2 | rank3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | −127.4 | −155.1 | −55.0 | −54.5 |
| hunk 1 only | −36.1 | −41.1 | −33.8 | −36.7 |
| this PR | **−30.6** | **−30.2** | **−32.4** | **−31.3** |

tau2-airline through an OpenAI-compatible gateway, complete runs:

| | task score | schema-valid tool calls |
|---|---|---|
| hunk 1 only | 5 of 6 tasks `too_many_errors` | 49/63 |
| this PR | 44/50 (88.0%) | 354/354 (100%) |
| plain-TP reference | 44/50 (88.0%) | 372/372 (100%) |

Exact task-score parity with plain TP, zero InvalidJson / UnknownName /
SchemaMismatch, 50/50 normal terminations. This change is deployed in
production-equivalent serving.

The state before hunk 1 was never benchmarked (it produces degenerate output,
not scoreable completions) — the benchmark rows above measure the hunk-2
defect.

## Follow-up suggestion (not in this PR)

The skip predicates are global (`moe/utils.py`) while the compensating combine
is per-communicator, and `should_use_reduce_scatter` gates on function
identity, which silently excludes subclass overrides. A startup assertion — if
`should_use_dp_reduce_scatterv()` holds, the active communicator must have a
reducing combine and must report reduce-scatter under SUM_LEN — would catch
this class rather than these two instances. Happy to send that separately if
you want it.

title: fix(kda): stop remapping the -1 padding sentinel onto a live mamba slot
author: ehsan
body:
Fixes the padding-slot aliasing reported in #36880.

Based on this PR's head (`aa8c950a3d`) rather than `main`, since the remap
being removed exists only on this branch — `main`'s `TritonKDAKernel.extend`
already passes `cache_indices` through unmodified.

## The bug

`TritonKDAKernel.extend` routed padded rows away from the `-1` sentinel and
onto `ssm_states.shape[0] - 1`, described in the comment as *"MambaPool's
trailing sentinel slot"*. That slot is not reserved — the reservation is at the
other end of the pool:

- `MambaPool` allocates `size + 1` rows.
- `MambaSlotAllocator` reserves **slot 0** as the dummy write target and hands
  out `1..size` inclusive
  (`allocator/mamba.py`: `# Slot 0 is reserved as a dummy write target for
  padded tokens.` / `self.free_slots = torch.arange(1, self.size + 1, ...)`).

So `ssm_states.shape[0] - 1 == size` — the last *allocatable* slot. A padded
row remapped there reads that slot's contents as its initial state and writes
its final state back into it, because making the index non-negative is exactly
what defeats `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h`'s `valid_state = index >= 0` guard
(which gates both the load and the `INPLACE_UPDATE` store). If a live request
or a mamba radix checkpoint owns slot `size` at that moment, its recurrent
state is silently corrupted and it produces wrong output with no error. The
slot is handed out under memory pressure, so the profile is rare and
load-dependent.

## The fix

Drop the remap and pass the sentinel through, matching the same call on `main`.
The remap is not merely misdirected but unnecessary: the guard added in #33810
already handles `-1` in the chunked extend path, and
`chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h` is the only consumer of `initial_state_indices`
in the `chunk_kda` pipeline (`chunk_kda` / `chunk_kda_fwd` just thread it
through).

Remapping to slot `0` instead would also close the aliasing if you would rather
keep an explicit scratch target; passing through is proposed here because it
converges with `main` and avoids the pool write entirely.

The `.to(torch.int32)` cast goes away with the `torch.where` — the mamba index
mapping is already `int32` (`req_index_to_mamba_index_mapping`), and the
`main` call site passes `cache_indices` without a cast. Happy to keep the cast
if you prefer it retained.

## Status

Found by code audit during an unrelated DP-attention investigation (#36879), not
by an observed failure — our configuration does not produce the padded extend
rows that trigger it, so this is offered as a latent-correctness fix rather
than a validated one. The reasoning above is verified against this PR's head;
the runtime behavior change is confined to batches that actually carry `-1`
rows into the KDA extend path.

Two smaller observations from the same audit are recorded in #36880 rather than
fixed here, since both are latent and touch shared kernels: `chunk_kda` writes
its output into the caller's `v` tensor in place, and the `T=1` chunked path
reads uninitialized memory (visible as NaNs under
`torch.utils.deterministic.fill_uninitialized_memory = True`).

title: [Memory] Size the CUDA graph pool from warmup measurements and fix graph-pool borrowing
author: cctry
body:
## Motivation

This PR sizes the CUDA graph pool from measurements taken during graph warmup, and hardens graph-pool borrowing (#35375) against failure modes we hit under speculative-decoding serving loads.

Warmup-based sizing:

- **Pre-carve** (opt-in): the graph pool grows segment by segment during capture, fragmenting free space. Measuring the eager warmup's reserved footprint and minting it as one contiguous span right before capture carves the pool out of a single region.
- **Sampling prewarm hook**: sampling paths allocate full-vocabulary temporaries after graph capture; a rehearsal hook right after capture lets their memory needs surface at startup instead of under traffic.

Borrow-path fixes:

1. **Supply was counted per segment.** Only wholly-free segments counted as borrowable, so a single live block hid an entire segment's free space. Anything that stays live inside the graph pool (e.g. lazily initialized workspaces that land in the pool during the first capture) could hide multiple GB. On a GB300 TP4/EP4 speculative-decoding shape this hid 2.3 GB of borrowable space even on a healthy tree.
2. **First fit starved large borrows.** Extents are sorted largest first, so first fit carved every small allocation out of the run that a full-vocabulary probability matrix needs, and the arena could refuse a ~340 MiB request with GBs free in aggregate.
3. **The arena rebuilt itself too eagerly.** Rebuilding the borrow `MemPool` once the bump cursor passed half the extents discarded the caching allocator's reusable segments. A cold borrow must serve each request from a single extent, so a large request could raise an allocator OOM even though the arena was ~73% free in aggregate.

Separately, keeping EAGLE verify sampling inside the borrow scope (as introduced in #35375) turned out to be unsafe: with stochastic sampling enabled, probability temporaries reuse graph-owned inactive blocks that are not safe across EAGLE's repeated graph pipeline, and decoding can hang. EAGLE sampling now stays on the normal allocator.

## Modifications

- `runner_utils/pool.py`
  - New `GraphPoolPrecarve` (opt-in via `SGLANG_ENABLE_GRAPH_POOL_PRECARVE`): measures the eager warmup's reserved-memory footprint and mints it as one contiguous span right before capture, so the graph pool is carved out of a single region instead of grown segment by segment.
  - `find_free_graph_pool_runs` now walks contiguous inactive runs across **all** pool segments; live and pending-free blocks break runs, so a returned run never overlaps live data (the borrow protocol already assumes the next replay may rewrite any inactive range). Measured on the shape above: borrowable free 7.35 GB → 9.68 GB (+32%), largest run 1.13 GB → 2.30 GB (+103%).
  - The borrow arena now only rebuilds when the caching allocator actually released an arena segment (`freed_bytes`), not on a high cursor. Measured with the cursor guard removed: 1,200 sampling steps over batch sizes 1–32 in a 514 MiB arena held a 388 MiB high-water mark with 9 cached segments and zero raw frees.
  - `disable_graph_pool_borrow` now also tears down a live borrow pool, so disabling borrowing at runtime falls back cleanly to the normal allocator.
- `utils/cuda_vmm_utils.py`: `BumpArenaStub` gains an opt-in best-fit mode (`set_best_fit`); the borrow path enables it. First fit remains the default for callers that map physical pages at the offsets they are handed.
- `speculative/eagle_utils.py`: revert the `borrow_graph_pool` scope around EAGLE verify sampling (see Motivation).
- `model_runner.py` / `scheduler.py` / `base_spec_worker.py`: after graph capture, the scheduler runs a `prewarm_sampling` rehearsal hook on the forward stream (delegated to the spec worker when one exists). The base implementation is a no-op returning `SamplingPrewarmResult`; a follow-up will implement the EAGLE rehearsal (warm the top-k/top-p renorm workspaces outside graph storage and measure sampling memory), which is also the prerequisite for safely re-enabling borrow for EAGLE.
- Unit tests: mixed-segment run extraction never overlaps live blocks; oversized borrows raise OOM and regular allocation still succeeds after disablement; cached-segment reuse across borrows; scheduler prewarm ordering/stream routing.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable — allocator and startup-path changes only; no model forward or kernel changes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

See the borrowable-supply and arena-reuse measurements under Modifications. The changes were validated end to end on GB300 with TP4/EP4 EAGLE3 dummy-weight serving with borrowing enabled globally: stochastic and `json_schema` requests completed (the previous hang is gone), and two full batch-size sweeps from 8 through 39 ran with the graph-pool cursor stable and no OOM.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [AMD] Fix eager metadata for AITER EAGLE draft extend
author: zijiecode
body:
## Motivation

The AITER unified-attention path for non-MLA EAGLE draft extend can pass stale query sequence metadata to the kernel during eager execution. The regression was introduced by #30105, which enabled this path by default through `SGLANG_AITER_UNIFIED_DRAFT_EXTEND`.

The CUDA Graph metadata path builds the correct query indptr, so tests whose batch sizes remain within the captured graph range do not expose the issue. The failing path is the eager fallback used when CUDA Graph is disabled or when the live batch exceeds the captured maximum.

The issue was reproduced on the latest `main` at `2a96ebf6486de5016f40c3f8c6b43536c01f5cc5` using AMD MI355X, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4, TP2, AITER attention, EAGLE with 3 speculative steps and 4 draft tokens, FP8 KV cache, and real draft acceptance. With CUDA Graph disabled, server warmup deterministically failed before the server became ready. With CUDA Graph enabled but `--cuda-graph-max-bs 32 --max-running-requests 64`, the high-concurrency workload entered the same eager fallback.

Instrumentation of the failing eager batch showed the metadata mismatch on both TP ranks:

```text
DRAFT_EXTEND_DEBUG q_shape=(4, 4096) qo_indptr=[0, 80] expected_q_len=4 metadata_max_q_len=0 kv_indptr=[0, 80] seq_lens=[84]
```

The query and output tensors contained 4 token rows, but `cu_seqlens_q=[0, 80]` instructed `unified_attention` to process 80 query rows. The resulting out-of-bounds write was reported as:

```text
Memory access fault by GPU node-3 (...) on address (...). Reason: Write access to a read-only page.
Memory access fault by GPU node-2 (...) on address (...). Reason: Unknown.
```

In longer CUDA Graph-enabled runs, the asynchronous corruption could first surface in speculative decode accounting before the HIP fault was reported:

```text
File "sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py", line 1260, in update_spec_correct_drafts_histogram
    self.spec_correct_drafts_histogram[num_correct_drafts] += 1
IndexError: list index out of range

HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_APERTURE_VIOLATION: The agent attempted to access memory beyond the largest legal address. code: 0x29
Fatal Python error: Aborted
```

`generate_attn_arg_prefill()` already returns the token-level `kv_indices`, `kv_indptr`, and `qo_indptr` required by this speculative batch, but the eager draft-extend setup discarded those values, left `ForwardMetadata.qo_indptr` unset, and later passed the backend's reusable `self.qo_indptr` buffer to `unified_attention`.

## Modifications

- Build eager non-MLA draft-extend `ForwardMetadata` directly from the values returned by `spec_info.generate_attn_arg_prefill()`.

title: fix: KT's last MoE layer stops deferring experts again
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

`create_kt_config_from_server_args` resolves `num_layers` for one reason: so the
KT wrapper can recognise the model's final layer, which must defer no experts.

```python
if (self.kt_config.max_deferred_experts_per_token is not None
        and self.kt_config.num_layers is not None
        and self.kt_config.layer_idx == self.kt_config.num_layers - 1):
    layer_max_deferred = 0
```

That branch has not fired since December 2025.

#12834 wrote the read as `server_args.get_hf_config()`, which was correct at the
time. #15298 removed `ServerArgs.get_hf_config` and rewrote the three call sites
*inside* `server_args.py` to `get_model_config().hf_config` — but not this one,
which lives in another file. The call has raised `AttributeError` on every
invocation since.

Three things kept it quiet:

- the read sat inside a bare `except Exception: pass` whose comment described the
  intended case (*"If we can't get the config, num_layers will be None"*), so the
  failure was indistinguishable from the handled one;
- the consumer guards on `num_layers is not None`, so the symptom is a rule that
  silently stops applying, not an error;
- the function returns early unless `kt_weight_path` is set, so only
  KTransformers runs reach it at all.

## Modifications

The read becomes `server_args.get_model_config().hf_config` — the same spelling
#15298 moved everything else to — and the swallow is gone. Three lines in, eight
out.

## Accuracy Tests

Measured on an 8×H200 box against a 7-layer checkpoint:

| | `KTConfig.num_layers` | layer 6 recognised as last |
|---|---|---|
| main | `None` | no |
| this PR | `7` | yes |

`sa.get_hf_config()` on main raises `AttributeError: 'ServerArgs' object has no
attribute 'get_hf_config'`, confirming the call could never have succeeded.
`test/registered/unit/layers/moe/` is green (54 passed).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

None. One attribute read replaces one that always raised.

title: [Fix] Fall back to the process-group broadcast for DSA topk when PyNCCL is absent
author: hnyls2002
body:
`SGLANG_DSA_TOPK_BROADCAST=1` cannot start under DP attention whenever attention is TP-sharded (`attn_tp_size > 1` and `< tp_size`, e.g. `--tp 4 --dp 2`). A split attn-TP group is built without a PyNCCL communicator, and the capture path raised instead of falling back:

```
RuntimeError: SGLANG_DSA_TOPK_BROADCAST requires PyNCCL during CUDA graph capture.
RuntimeError: Rank 0 scheduler died during initialization
```

PyNCCL is not a precondition here — the process-group broadcast captures and replays correctly. With the fallback the same config boots, captures the decode graph, and at temperature 0 produces output token-identical to the same build with the broadcast disabled. PyNCCL stays the preferred path where it exists; measured in graph replay it is 8.82 us vs 10.57 us for a 64 KB broadcast.

title: [Kernel] Fix SM90 FP8 decode regression with benchmarked M/K/N routing
author: RunFMe
body:
## Motivation

The SM90 row/column-scaled FP8 selector introduced by #34318 can route decode GEMMs to `torch._scaled_mm` based on K/N alone. The [reported H100 W8A8 regression](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34318#issuecomment-5461656173) is:

- model: `Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-dynamic`
- test: `test/registered/quant/test_w8a8_quantization.py::TestW8A8Fp8.test_throughput`
- batch size: 1
- throughput: approximately 215 tok/s before #34318, approximately 190 tok/s after it
- affected down projection: `M=1, K=14336, N=4096`

Direct profiling of that shape on both H200 and H100 showed that the AOT kernel is substantially faster at decode M, even though K and N are large.

## Modifications

Constrain Torch/NVJet routing to the benchmarked large-prefill envelope (doing m >= 6144 is not really worth the gain from my measurements):

```python
m >= 8192 and (
    (k >= 4096 and n >= 6144) or
    (k >= 7168 and n >= 5376)
)
```

This keeps the following on AOT:

- all decode and small-prefill calls with `M < 8192`
- the reported `K=14336, N=4096` Llama down projection
- narrow TP8 projections `K=5376, N=3584` and `K=3584, N=5376`
- shapes outside the measured projection envelope

Torch remains selected for stable large-prefill wins: wide QKV/gate/up projections and broad down projections.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Common software:

- PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130 (`70d99e998b4955e0049d13a98d77ae1b14db1f45`)
- CUDA 13.0
- `sgl_kernel==0.4.4`
- CUDA-event timing with randomized/interleaved AOT and Torch samples

The broad grid used 11 projection families and 12 M values (132 cases): 1, 16, 64, 256, 1024, 2048, 4096, 6144, 8192, 8320, 12288, and 16384. Percentages below are Torch speedups over AOT.

### H200 (SM90)

Protocol:

- broad grid: 5 warmups and 15 samples per arm
- two randomized boundary confirmations: 44 cases and 33 cases, with 8–10 warmups and 30–40 samples per arm
- exact-workload conditioning before timing

Reported regression shape:

| M | K | N | AOT | Torch | Result |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | 14336 | 4096 | 26.50 µs | 51.12 µs | AOT is 1.93× faster |

Routing boundary:

| K | N | Projection family | M=8192 | M=8320 |
|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 4096 | 28672 | gate/up | 1.74% | 3.30% |
| 4096 | 6144 | QKV | 0.94% | 2.14% |
| 5376 | 21504 | QKV | 2.59% | 4.64% |
| 5376 | 28672 | gate/up | 2.39% | 5.17% |
| 5376 | 14336 | gate/up TP2 | 2.91% | 2.62% |
| 7168 | 5376 | down TP4 | 1.26% | 3.29% |
| 14336 | 5376 | down TP2 | 1.82% | 3.25% |
| 28672 | 5376 | down TP1 | 1.66% | 3.09% |

Across the H200 broad grid, every one of the 32 measurements selected by the new predicate favored Torch. Their median speedup was 2.50%, with a measured range of 0.17–5.97%. Two independent randomized boundary passes added 48 repeated routed measurements, all of which also favored Torch.

### H100 80 GB HBM3 (SM90)

Protocol:

- randomized broad grid: 5 warmups and 20 samples per arm after 0.5 s of exact-workload conditioning per case
- randomized boundary confirmation: 44 cases, with 10 warmups and 40 samples per arm after 2 s of conditioning per case

Reported regression shape:

| M | K | N | AOT | Torch | Result |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | 14336 | 4096 | 32.19 µs | 53.55 µs | AOT is 1.66× faster |

Routing boundary:

| K | N | Projection family | M=8192 | M=8320 |
|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 4096 | 28672 | gate/up | 21.02% | 43.21% |
| 4096 | 6144 | QKV | 5.39% | 3.07% |
| 5376 | 21504 | QKV | 25.44% | 57.38% |
| 5376 | 28672 | gate/up | 26.58% | 52.16% |
| 5376 | 14336 | gate/up TP2 | 15.87% | 48.31% |
| 7168 | 5376 | down TP4 | 2.72% | 4.43% |
| 14336 | 5376 | down TP2 | 8.72% | 7.08% |
| 28672 | 5376 | down TP1 | 10.02% | 8.57% |

Across the H100 broad grid, every one of the 32 measurements selected by the new predicate favored Torch. Their median speedup was 19.48%, with a measured range of 1.36–56.53%. The stronger randomized boundary pass added 24 repeated routed measurements, all favoring Torch, with a 21.02% median and a 2.72–57.38% range.

On both GPUs, the excluded Llama down and narrow TP8 families had weak large-M results that were near parity or changed sign across passes, so this change deliberately leaves them on AOT rather than routing on noise.

title: fix(hicache): isolate decode offload state per request
author: CyberSecurityErial
body:
## Motivation

`DecodeKVCacheOffloadManager` tracks asynchronous D2H offload state by the caller-provided `rid`. A completed request is removed from `rid_to_state` before its copy necessarily finishes, so a new request reusing the same `rid` can inherit stale progress and be modified by a late callback from the old request.

### Reproduction

This reproduces deterministically without relying on GPU timing. It restores only the regression test onto the exact base commit, then runs that single test:

```bash
git fetch origin pull/37026/head:pr-37026
git switch --detach 4d53767b09429c67a4137352c762372923853eb6
git restore --source pr-37026 -- test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_specv2_kvcache_offloading.py
PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_specv2_kvcache_offloading.py \
  -k reused_rid_does_not_share_offload_lifecycle
```

Expected result on the base commit:

```text
FAILED ...::test_reused_rid_does_not_share_offload_lifecycle
AssertionError: False is not true
```

The failure is at the second `offload_kv_cache(new_req)` call: `new_req` reuses the old request state because both requests have the same `rid`. The same test passes on this PR.

## Modifications

- Key decode offload state and in-flight counters by the concrete `Req` instance.
- Keep `rid` only for external identity and logging.
- Add a regression test with two distinct requests that reuse the same `rid` while the first request's D2H copy is still pending.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable. This change does not modify the model forward path or model outputs.

The focused regression test passes:

```text
PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_specv2_kvcache_offloading.py

14 passed
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

title: fix(frontend): bound stop strings and regex patterns
author: CyberSecurityErial

## Motivation

A request can currently include an unbounded number of stop strings or stop regex patterns. These are checked during decoding, so oversized inputs can waste CPU and slow down other requests.

title: [vlm] fix: preserve per-request vit graph metadata for qwen-vl
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

- key generic ViT CUDA graphs by full/window attention boundaries in addition to total sequence length
- keep each captured graph bound to the rotary workspace address it captured when a later request grows the workspace
- build Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL layout keys from CPU metadata to avoid a GPU synchronization on graph lookup

## Why

Equal-token VLM batches can have different image boundaries. Reusing a graph by total token count alone replays stale `cu_seqlens`. Qwen3-VL can also grow the shared rotary workspace after smaller graphs were captured; those graphs retain the old address while replay updates the replacement allocation. Both cases feed request-stale vision metadata into attention.

## Coverage

- equal total tokens with different full/window attention layouts
- small graph replay after a larger request grows rotary storage
- real CUDA graph capture and replay with metadata-dependent outputs
- Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL generic ViT graph callers

title: fix(vlm): contain multimodal feature transport failures
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary
- defer scheduler-side SHM open/reconstruction failures until request handling
- synchronize per-request failures across TP/CP ranks before model collectives
- release abandoned SHM features and convert only the affected VLM request to an internal error

## Why
A rank-local SHM open, clone, reshape, or cleanup failure currently escapes the scheduler receive loop. That can kill one scheduler rank while peers continue with the request, turning malformed or resource-constrained multimodal input into a process-level failure.

## Coverage
- single and batched image-feature requests
- local and peer-rank materialization failures
- TP and DP-attention TP/CP consensus
- SHM handle cleanup on open, clone, and unlink failures

Stacked on #37030.

title: [ROCm] Fix EAGLE spec-decode verify silently sampling greedy on HIP
author: xiaobochen-amd
body:
## Problem

EAGLE spec-decode verify has been committing `argmax` on ROCm, ignoring
`temperature` and `top_p` entirely, with nothing in the log saying so. At
`temp > 0` it degenerates into repetition loops.

The cause is one line in `eagle_sample`:

```python
if sampling_info.is_all_greedy or _is_cpu or _is_npu or _is_hip or _is_xpu:
    target_predict = torch.argmax(next_token_logits, dim=-1)
```

`_is_hip` sits next to `is_all_greedy`, so HIP takes the greedy path
unconditionally. It is there because the sampling branch needs
`tree_speculative_sampling_target_only`, `top_k_renorm_prob` and
`top_p_renorm_prob`, all of which are CUDA/MUSA-only in `sgl_kernel`.

## Fix

Route HIP through the pure-Triton chain sampler in `reject_sampling.py` when
rejection sampling is active and the batch is not all-greedy, with a Triton
renorm (`_renorm_top_k_top_p_hip`) standing in for the CUDA-only renorm ops.

The gate becomes a pure helper, `_verify_uses_greedy`. On every non-HIP platform
it reduces to the predicate it replaces: with `is_hip` False the added term drops
out and the expression is the original one.

`_renorm_top_k_top_p_hip` follows the same shape as the op it replaces — a
threshold search, matching `top_p_renorm_prob`'s ternary pivot search on
`f(x) = sum(probs[probs > x])` — so it agrees with CUDA rather than with a
sort-based nucleus. `top_p >= 1.0` short-circuits to an exact pass-through, to
stay bit-exact with CUDA's `top_p_renorm_prob(p, 1.0) == p`. top-k uses a sort,
skipped entirely when no row restricts it.

Defaulting the flag on matters: without it the fix only reaches users who pass
`--speculative-use-rejection-sampling`, and everyone else still silently gets
argmax verify. It flips only on HIP, for EAGLE/EAGLE3 with `topk=1`, default
accept thresholds and non-deterministic inference — the same conditions the
validation below raises on, so the flip can never turn a working config into an
error. Setting it also makes the draft worker emit the target-vocab proposal
(`draft_probs`) the Triton chain sampler consumes.

## Two shapes that come from the current tree, not from the fix

Worth pointing out so they don't read as gratuitous:

**`sampling_fn` dispatch.** It used the eager `A if cond else B` form, which
resolves `tree_speculative_sampling_target_only` whether or not that branch is
taken. HIP must not import it at all, so the dispatch becomes an `if`/`else`
that imports inside the arm needing it. Non-HIP behaviour is unchanged.

**One `cfg` read becomes `resolved_view`.** `_handle_eagle_family` writes through
`declare_resolution`, whose contract is that a field it decides is *not* visible
to a later `cfg.` read. The rejection-sampling validation immediately below was
reading `cfg`, so it would have skipped every auto-enabled config — including its
own "rejection sampling is enabled" log. That read becomes
`resolved_view(server_args)`, which is what the `declare_resolution` docstring
prescribes for exactly this case.

## Test

- `test/registered/unit/spec/test_eagle_gate_routing.py` — gate truth table, CPU.
  Pins that the helper reduces to the original predicate off HIP, and that HIP
  only leaves greedy when rejection sampling is on and the batch is not
  all-greedy. 4 tests.
- `test/registered/spec/eagle/test_rocm_eagle_renorm.py` — renorm numerical
  equivalence against an independent torch reference, plus the `top_p == 1.0`
