title: [AMD][Fix] Fix aiter bpreshuffle GEMM for output sizes it cannot dispatch for qwen3.5 mxfp-attn-fp8-v2 TP4
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

Serving a quark-quantized Qwen3.5 (`amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4-AttnFP8-V2`, which quantizes `*linear_attn*` to fp8 `per_channel` / dynamic) at TP4 on MI355X crashes on the first real prefill:

```
File "sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py", line 686, in _forward_input_proj
File "sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_w8a8_fp8.py", line 178, in apply_weights
File "sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py", line 1987, in apply_fp8_linear
RuntimeError: gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle failed for shape M=16384, N=32, K=4096,
              dtype=torch.bfloat16, config=None: This GEMM is not supported!
```

aiter's CK `gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle` instances are generated with `GemmSpecialization::Default` -- pre-shuffled weights are never N-padded -- so an instance only accepts `N % NPerBlock == 0`. `rowwise_heuristic_dispatch` in `csrc/ck_gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle/gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle.cu` picks by shape:

```cpp
if (K >= 1536) {
    if (M < 256 && K % 512 == 0) {
        if (N < 1536) return a8w8_bpreshuffle_128x16x32x512_...;  // NPerBlock=32
        ...
    } else {
        if (N < 1536 || N % 128 != 0)
                      return a8w8_bpreshuffle_256x128x64x128_...; // NPerBlock=64
```

`linear_attn.in_proj_ba` is a `MergedColumnParallelLinear` with total `N=128`, which TP4 shards to `N=32`. Measured on gfx950, K=4096, N=32:

```
M=    1 : OK      M < 256  -> NPerBlock=32 instance
M=    4 : OK
M=   64 : OK
M=  255 : OK
M=  256 : FAIL    branch switches -> NPerBlock=64 instance
M=  512 : FAIL
```

So warmup and decode pass and only prefill fails, which is why the server reaches "ready to roll" and then dies under load. TP1 (N=128) and TP2 (N=64) are unaffected.

## Modifications

The weight layout is decided at load time: `quark_w8a8_fp8.py` pre-shuffles whenever `SGLANG_USE_AITER` is set, and by the time the GEMM raises there is no unshuffled weight left to fall back with. So a `try`/`except` around the call cannot fix this -- the load-time shuffle and the runtime kernel choice have to be gated on one shared predicate, or the fallback silently returns garbage.

`fp8_utils.use_aiter_bpreshuffle_gemm(output_size)` is that predicate, used at all four sites:

- `fp8_utils.apply_fp8_linear` -- picks the aiter kernel only for shapes it can dispatch; everything else takes the existing rowwise `torch._scaled_mm` branch.
- `quark/schemes/quark_w8a8_fp8.py` -- gates the load-time shuffle (the path in the traceback).
- `fp8.py` `Fp8LinearMethod` -- same gate at both shuffle sites (online-quantized and serialized-fp8 checkpoints).

MoE and block-quant `shuffle_weight` calls feed different kernels and are untouched.

`torch._scaled_mm` is the fallback rather than aiter's cktile instance (which does accept `N=32`, being compiled with per-kernel padded variants) because it is much faster on exactly the skinny shapes that need rescuing -- see below. A companion aiter PR adds the cktile fallback so the library stops raising for any caller; this PR is about not entering that path in the first place.

## Accuracy Tests

Unit level, `apply_fp8_linear` against a bf16 reference, M=7237/K=4096, weights shuffled iff the predicate says so:

```
N= 128 shuffled=True  rel_err=2.65e-02   TP1
N=  64 shuffled=True  rel_err=2.66e-02   TP2
N=  32 shuffled=False rel_err=2.65e-02   TP4  <- previously raised
```

The fallback path is as accurate as the aiter path; the residual is fp8 per-token quantization error itself.

End to end on 4x MI355X, TP4 + EAGLE MTP, ISL 8192 / OSL 1024, concurrency 4 -- this configuration could not complete a single request before:

```
Successful requests:              40 / 40
Benchmark duration (s):           51.59
Total token throughput (tok/s):   6415.37
Output token throughput (tok/s):   713.46
Median TTFT (ms):                  221.67
Median TPOT (ms):                    4.52
```

No `Scheduler hit an exception` in the server log.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The three ways to compute M=16384 / N=32 / K=4096 on gfx950:

```
gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle_ck     : FAIL -> This GEMM is not supported!
gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle_cktile : OK    91.9 us
torch._scaled_mm rowwise     : OK    14.1 us
```

cktile is bit-exact against `torch._scaled_mm` here (max abs err 0) but spends half its MFMA issue on N-padding. TP1/TP2 and every other `N % 64 == 0` layer keep the aiter kernel, so no shape that works today changes path.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: fix: restore missing get_component_forced_attn_backend import in minimax_h3
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

`main` is currently red on `lint`: `ruff` reports an undefined name in `minimax_h3.py`.

```
F821 Undefined name `get_component_forced_attn_backend`
   --> python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/minimax_h3.py:717:44
    |
717 |         self._selected_attention_backend = get_component_forced_attn_backend()
    |                                            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

This is a semantic merge conflict between two diffusion PRs that do not textually conflict:

- #36907 (`62c470697`) dropped `get_component_forced_attn_backend` from the `selector` import block in `minimax_h3.py`, because its last call site there was replaced by `claim_deferred_component_attn_backend()`.

This is not only a lint failure: the call is in `MiniMaxH3Attention.__init__`, so constructing a MiniMax-H3 model raises `NameError` at runtime.

## Modifications

Restore the `get_component_forced_attn_backend` import. One line, no behavior change beyond making the existing call resolve.

## Accuracy Test

title: Fix buffer-mode idle tracking and VLM memory sizing
author: merrymercy
body:
## Motivation

Buffer-only HiCache can report idle while write-through or load-back work is still in flight, allowing lifecycle transitions before staging activity drains. Post-capture KV sizing also needs fixed runtime headroom for multimodal execution instead of the standard capacity-scaled heuristic.

## Modifications

- Include write-through and buffer load-back operations in buffer-pipeline idle detection.
- Reserve an additional fixed 8 GiB for multimodal runtime allocations when post-capture KV sizing is active; preserve the existing heuristic outside that mode and exclude decode-only workers.
- Add focused regression coverage for both behaviors.
- Reuse the current tree snapshot path, which already carries storage sharding context.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable; this does not change model numerics.

- `LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib64/libnuma.so.1 uv run --no-sync pytest -q test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py::TestBufferModePipelineIdle` — 193 passed, 20 subtests passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable; no inference hot path is changed.

title: Fix overflow in legacy and v1 DSA top-k selectors
author: ormandj
body:
## Motivation

Legacy DSA top-k selection can drop candidates when a coarse radix bin reaches its fixed buffer capacity, selecting lower-scoring tokens before full scores are compared. This patch covers the DeepSeek-V4 JIT v1, legacy CUDA AOT and DeepSeek-V4 AOT selectors. KPool JIT already rescans overflowing bins on main (#39273), so its kernel is unchanged here and only gains regression coverage.

## Modifications

Keep normal-bin selection. For a coarse bin larger than the stash, find the exact FP32 cutoff one key byte per row scan; each scan also emits the scores the previous byte placed strictly above the cutoff, and the last scan emits the remaining ones and the cutoff ties (six scans of the row including the coarse histogram, down from seven). Preserve page mapping, `-1` padding and synchronization around shared-memory reuse. The JIT header takes its CUDA/HIP types from `sgl_kernel/utils.cuh`. Retain the additive ROCm tests. Co-authored with Benjamin Oldenburg (@bold84).

Add a CUDA test for `topk_transform_paged` (JIT v1) covering threshold bins on both sides of the 8192-entry stash, strictly higher values ahead of an oversized bin, cutoff ties, clusters that separate only in one of the lower three FP32 key bytes, runtime `topk` values, short rows, score rows padded past their lengths, a noncontiguous score view, and both raw and page-mapped outputs. Add KPool regressions at its 4096-entry stash for oversized and exact-capacity bins, cutoff ties, clusters that separate in the lower three key bytes, padded rows and page-table expansion, registered for CUDA and AMD.

The v2 changes are removed from this PR so the legacy/v1 fix can be reviewed and merged independently. I will submit the v2 changes in a separate PR.

## Accuracy Tests

On RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), a combined build passed 12 KPool JIT tests/38 subtests and 7 focused legacy CUDA AOT cases, including oversized coarse bins. One ROCm-only case was skipped. Those results predate the rebase onto main's KPool implementation.

On RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), torch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0, at this branch, `test_topk_v1.py` passed (15 tests) and `test_dsa_kpool_topk_transform.py` passed against main's KPool kernel (12 tests, 38 subtests). Against main's unpatched `topk_v1.cuh`, 9 of the 15 v1 tests fail (the overflow cases). The AOT header was compiled for sm_120 in a standalone harness and matched a CPU reference on random rows, single-bin rows above the stash, and strictly higher values plus cutoff ties. The AOT test matrix and ROCm tests have not been run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Rows whose coarse threshold bin exceeds the stash take six row scans; other rows are unchanged. No speed benchmark was run.

## Checklist

- [x] Format changed code.
- [x] Run regression tests described above.

Developed with AI assistance.

title: [AMD] Fix FP4 indexer OOR
author: RolaoDenthu
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
On MI355X, DeepSeek-V4-Pro with the FP4 indexer aborts under long-running agentic workloads:
```
HSA_STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES ... Available Free mem : 0 MB
  at fused_moe_triton_kernels.py:1353 fused_append_shared_experts
```
The indexer allocates a fresh torch.empty(num_tokens, max_seq_len) for logits on every layer of every forward. If no cached block is large enough to reuse, it has to allocate a new one. Torch does release the tensor when it's done, but only back to its own caching allocator — the driver still sees that memory as taken. And max_seq_len follows the context length, which in an agentic session only grows, so each request is slightly larger than the last, the older blocks never get a chance to be reused, and they just pile up in the pool. Driver-visible memory drains block by block until the allocation fails with out of resources.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
1. Pooled fixed-size logits buffer (fp4_indexer_hip.py)

Prefill logits are served as a view into one pre-allocated block instead of a fresh torch.empty per call. The request size becomes constant, so the block is always reused and nothing strands. Decode keeps the plain allocation: its rectangle is bounded by the capture shapes and lives in the graph memory pool, and creating the pooled block mid-capture would hand graph-pool memory to later replays. Budget is set by SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_LOGITS_BUDGET_MB (default 2048).

2. Row chunking (indexer.py)

A fixed block alone isn't enough — a batch that doesn't fit would fall back to a dynamic allocation and start stranding again. logits_rows_per_chunk() reports how many rows fit, and the FP4 prefill path loops over row chunks, running each chunk's top-k before reusing the block. This decouples peak scratch from context length. Rows are scored and reduced independently, so the result is elementwise-identical to a single pass; the single-chunk case (the common one) passes the whole batch through without slicing. The KV payload/scale getters are hoisted out of the loop since they await the layer's KV transfer, and topk_v2 metadata is re-planned per chunk because the cached plan routes rows by their index in the full range.

## Accuracy Tests

title: [Fix] Broadcast PP dynamic-chunk profiling failures so every rank disables together
author: hnyls2002
body:
Follows up on #37674.

## Summary
- `DynamicChunkSizer.profile_and_fit` catches a PP0 profiling failure and broadcasts `None` instead of raising; every rank returns `False` and `maybe_init_dynamic_chunk_sizer` leaves `dynamic_chunk_sizer = None`
- `ChunkSizePredictor.fit` failures take the same path; every rank fits identical samples, so the outcome is rank-symmetric
- Replace the two-step relay (attn-TP/CP broadcast inside PP0, then a per-column `pp_group.broadcast_object_list`) with one `broadcast_pyobj` over the world group from global rank 0: the samples are global rather than per-DP-shard, so a single gloo broadcast reaches every stage and attention rank and no NCCL communicator is created for it

## Background
- Previously only the raising rank disabled dynamic chunking (the `try/except` sat around the whole call in the scheduler), while the other PP ranks stayed blocked in `pp_group.broadcast_object_list` until the NCCL timeout, so any profiling exception surfaced as a 600 s health-check hang (the secondary failure described in #23057, seen again in #37509)

title: [sglang-miles] Kimi K3 colocated RL: LoRA fixes and in-place MXFP4 Marlin reload
author: yueming-yuan
body:
The Kimi K3 RL serving work reached `sglang-miles` through `main`, and the miles K3 PR (radixark/miles#1825) now runs against `sglang-miles` instead of the old `sglang-miles-k3` branch. Running it on `radixark/miles:dev` found five places where the merge lost or never had what colocated K3 LoRA RL needs. Each commit is one of them; all were found by reading the traceback back to the branch diff, and the last two by `--check-weight-update-equal` / `--check-lora-weight-equal`.

- `num_shared_experts` (K3's config key) was not recognized when sizing the shared-expert LoRA buffers, so `init_state` died with `KeyError('gate_up_proj')` on the first dense layer.
- The output gate K3 installs by patching `o_proj.forward` never ran under LoRA: `RowParallelLinearWithLoRA` calls `quant_method.apply` on the base layer, so the MLA output went out ungated and the gate GEMM on the alt stream was never joined (`capturing stream has unjoined work`). Restores the `lora_input_transform` hook from the K3 branch (3768a8788a).
- Routed-expert LoRA buffers were sized by `hidden_size`; K3's latent MoE feeds the experts `routed_expert_hidden_size` (3584).
- `post_load_weights` read `o_proj.params_dtype` through the LoRA wrapper.
- `_merge_bfa_weights` stored `f_b_proj.weight` as a second Parameter on the attention module, which hides `f_b_proj.weight` from `named_parameters()`; every weight update silently skipped it (fb03504c93). Alias the storage instead.

Running the full model on 16 GB300 nodes (TP16, Marlin, `--no-lora-use-virtual-experts`) then showed the train/rollout KL growing with the adapter norm (0.0023 at step 0, 0.0047 by step 60) while the July stack stayed flat. A line-by-line diff of the LoRA path against that stack found four more losses, each its own commit:

- `Mxfp4MoEMethod` never exposed `get_marlin_quant_info`, so `FusedMoEWithLoRA` refused the Marlin backend outright; the LoRA Marlin runner also only ran `silu_and_mul`, so K3's gated SiTU experts failed at CUDA-graph capture.
- The Marlin tile padding of the expert intermediate (K3 at TP16: 192 -> 256) was ignored by the MoE LoRA hooks: the up delta was written at the logical stride into the gate padding and the down LoRA-A consumed the padded activation. Restores `output_slice_stride` in `fused_moe_lora` and the `marlin_intermediate_size` plumbing.
- The interleaved gate/up LoRA-B layout keyed on `gemm1_alpha` alone; K3 sets it for SiTU but loads w1/w3 contiguously, so every routed-expert gate/up delta was scrambled.
- The fused MoE front read the shared-expert base weights straight through the LoRA wrappers, so the shared_experts adapters the trainer streams were never applied.
- The LoRA Marlin runner used atomic-add for MXFP4 where the base runner does not.
- `--lora-no-cpu-backup`: the streamed adapter no longer keeps a per-TP-rank host copy (~45 GB/rank for the 896-expert adapter); the IPC views are installed into the pool at apply time.

Full-parameter RL re-pushes the MXFP4 base on every sync, which needs one more piece:

- `Mxfp4MoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading` repacked the experts into fresh Parameters, so a later `load_weights` found no `weight_loader` on them and the runner's `begin_weight_update` had nothing to restore. The method now records the checkpoint and Marlin layouts per layer, `restore_weights_before_loading` views the storage back to the checkpoint shape, and the repack runs expert by expert into the same storage, so the Parameter objects (and their `weight_loader`) survive. Unit test: `test/registered/e2e/rl/test_mxfp4_marlin_inplace_reload.py`.
- The last commit (`Mxfp4MarlinComparable` accepting the checker's `is_shuffled`) is a temporary cherry-pick of a standalone fix for `sglang-miles`; it drops out of this PR once that lands.

## Validation

miles CI (radixark/miles#1825, `run-ci-model-scripts` on 8xH200, `radixark/miles:dev` + this branch synced at test time) on `Pinaster/Kimi-K3-4layer-64experts`:

- `test_kimi_k3_4layer_lora_ci.py`: two rollouts and syncs; `--check-lora-weight-equal` matches on every rank and the base weight checker compares equal after each sync.
- `test_kimi_k3_4layer_ci.py` (full-parameter): the MXFP4 base is re-quantized and re-pushed on every sync; `--check-weight-update-equal` compares the Marlin experts equal in dequantized space (sgl-project/sglang#40028) after the in-place reload.

The Marlin-padding, interleave and shared-expert fixes were validated on the 4-layer TP8 layout with a trained adapter re-sharded from the 16-node run (rollout-0 logprob abs diff back to the zero-adapter floor); the padded-intermediate path itself only triggers at TP16 and was validated on the 16-node GB300 run.

sglang's own CI does not run on `sglang-miles` PRs (the `check-changes` maintenance gate), so the registered tests that exercise the touched files were run by hand on a fresh 8xH200 devbox (`radixark/miles:dev`, this branch at `e5dbafcada` installed in place of the baked sglang):

| test | result |
|---|---|
| `e2e/rl/test_mxfp4_marlin_inplace_reload.py`, `e2e/rl/test_weight_checker_mxfp4_marlin.py` | 1 + 9 passed |
| `unit/utils/test_weight_checker_comparator.py` | 11 passed |
| `lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py` | 108 passed |
| `quant/test_marlin_moe.py`, `kernels/ops/moe/test_moe_wna16_marlin.py` | 2 passed / 678 subtests; 7 passed, 24 skipped |
| `lora/test_virtual_experts_kernels.py`, `unit/lora/test_experimental_sgl_marlin_{multi_prefill,shared_outer_reduce}.py` | 13 + 2 + 4 passed |
| `unit/models/test_kimi_k3_bfa_overlap.py`, `kernels/ops/test_kimi_k3_prerequisite_ops.py`, `unit/layers/quantization/test_mxfp4_sm90_cutlass.py` | 4 + 12 + 19 passed |
| `rl/test_lora_load_from_tensor.py`, `lora/test_multi_lora_backend.py`, `lora/test_lora_overlap_loading.py`, `lora/test_lora_eviction.py` | 6 + 3 + 9 + 2 passed |
| `lora/test_lora_qwen3_8b_logprob_diff.py`, `lora/test_lora_moe_tp_logprob_diff.py` (TP2) | 2 passed; 2 passed, 1 skipped |
| GPT-OSS-20B MXFP4, Marlin runner vs `triton_kernel`, greedy 32 tokens x 4 prompts | 3/4 identical text, max abs logprob diff <= 0.056; the 4th diverges after 20 identical tokens |

Five files fail identically on plain `sglang-miles` (reproduced on the same devbox with the base branch installed) and are not touched by this PR: `unit/utils/test_weight_checker.py` (a helper returns 2 values, the test unpacks 3), `rl/test_weight_checker_e2e.py` and `rl/test_update_weights_from_tensor.py` (they push weights without `begin_weight_update`, which the scheduler has asserted on since the RL session protocol), `lora/test_moe_lora_info.py` (its fake `forward_batch` lacks `global_dp_buffer_len`), `lora/test_lora_spec_decoding.py` (EAGLE3 draft context-length check). Not runnable on H200: the B200/B300-only registrations.

## Follow-ups not in scope

- The AR-fusion (`_symm_o_proj_forward`) and SP-MoE (`_sp_o_proj_forward`) patches on `o_proj.forward` are bypassed by the LoRA wrapper the same way the output gate was; neither is active in the smoke run (auto-probe off, no symm mem). They need an output-side hook before K3 LoRA runs with AR fusion.

title: [AMD] Fix DSv4 draft extend taking the target compression path during prefill
author: Duyi-Wang
body:
## Motivation

On MI355X (gfx950), DeepSeek-V4-Pro with EAGLE/MTP at **TP 4 with DP attention** aborts within
90 s of the server becoming ready — on the first batch of real prefills, before a single decode
step completes:

```
HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION: An HSAIL operation resulted in a hardware exception. code: 0x1016
torch.AcceleratorError: HIP error: unspecified launch failure  (hipErrorLaunchFailure)

  eagle_worker_v2.py         _draft_extend_for_prefill
    deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py  init_forward_metadata_prefill
      _attach_unified_kv_prefill_meta -> torch.repeat_interleave
```

Deterministic, reproduced on clean nodes across several configurations. The reporting rank
varies (DP1 and DP2 observed), so it is not rank-specific.

### Root cause

Two call sites reach the prefill branch of `init_forward_metadata` for a draft model, and only
one rewrites `forward_mode`:

| path | call site | `forward_mode` |
|---|---|---|
| decode | `eagle_worker_common.prepare_for_draft_extend()` | sets `ForwardMode.DRAFT_EXTEND_V2` |
| **prefill** | `eagle_worker_v2._draft_extend_for_prefill()` | hands over the target's batch untouched → stays `ForwardMode.EXTEND` |

The backend decides compression from `forward_mode` alone (`need_compress = not is_draft`), so on
the prefill path a draft model is sent down the compression path. It owns no compression pool to
begin with — the two pools initialise as

```
draft:  c4_size=0        c128_size=0
target: c4_size=1832064  c128_size=57252
```

so this is not a draft/target size mismatch but compression metadata computed against a pool that
does not exist. The resulting out-of-bounds access is reported asynchronously and surfaces at the
next synchronisation point — the `repeat_interleave` in `_attach_unified_kv_prefill_meta`, which
omits `output_size` and therefore implies a `sum()` D2H copy. **That line is where the fault is
observed, not where it occurs.**

Instrumenting the branch confirms it at runtime: on the failing ranks the draft worker is handed
`ForwardMode.EXTEND`, and the write offsets it computes (`c4_out_loc` up to 64) point into a pool
of size 0.

## Modifications

The backend already reads `model_runner.is_draft_worker` in `__init__` (for the dspark check).
Keep it as a named attribute and use it as a second, mode-independent source of truth:

```python
is_draft = (
    forward_batch.forward_mode.is_draft_extend_v2() or self.is_draft_worker
)
```

A draft worker now never takes the compression path regardless of the `forward_mode` it is
handed. Only draft-worker backend instances are affected; the target is unchanged.

Fixing it here rather than by rewriting `forward_mode` in `_draft_extend_for_prefill` keeps the
blast radius to this backend — `forward_mode` is read by the logits processor, the CUDA-graph
runners and several other backends.

## Tests

Full agentic replay (long-context, tool-heavy, multi-turn) on a single MI355X node, TP 4 + DP
attention, EAGLE MTP (3 steps, topk 1, 4 draft tokens), hierarchical cache, concurrency 32.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `hipErrorLaunchFailure` | crash 57 s after ready | **0** |
| `Prefill batch` | stops at the crash | **915** |
| `Decode batch` | **0** | reached |
| client warmup | `returned=1/354`, then stalled | **`returned=330/354`, `errors=0`** |

Same image, same node class, same workload; the only difference is this patch.

title: [NPU] Fix ViT graph key layout handling
author: qybnb
body:
## Motivation

PR #37043 made ViT graph keys layout-aware by changing ViTCudaGraphRunner._get_graph_key to accept cumulative sequence boundaries and return a composite hashable key. ViTNpuGraphRunner still called the old single-argument API, causing Qwen3.6-27B multimodal requests with ViT NPU graph enabled to fail with:

    TypeError: ViTCudaGraphRunner._get_graph_key() missing 2 required positional arguments: 'cu_seqlens' and 'cu_window_seqlens'

The NPU runner also used the old integer graph key as the first dimension of a tensor workspace. That is invalid after graph keys become tuples.

## Modifications

- Pass cu_seqlens and the attention layout key when creating and looking up NPU ViT graphs.
- Preserve the Qwen3-VL attention layout before moving cumulative sequence lengths to CPU.
- Use the actual sequence length for NPU attention workspace allocation.
- Update NPU graph key type annotations from int to Hashable.
- Add a CPU regression test verifying that equal token counts with different cumulative sequence boundaries create distinct cached graphs and retain correctly shaped workspaces.

## Accuracy Tests

There is currently no registered Qwen3.6-27B multimodal accuracy test. The existing Qwen3.6-27B GPQA tests are text-only and do not exercise the ViT graph path.

Functional validation used the registered Qwen3.6-27B multimodal performance case on Ascend NPU with ViT graph and DP encoder enabled. Both benchmark attempts completed 240/240 image requests without the original exception.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Command target:

    test/registered/npu/performance/qwen3_6_27b/test_npu_qwen3_6_27b_1p_in1024x1024_30_out1024_50ms.py

Configuration: Qwen3.6-27B BF16, TP=2, 240 requests, concurrency=60, one 1024x1024 image per request.

- Attempt 1: TPOT 61.60 ms, output throughput 655.62 tok/s.
- Attempt 2: TPOT 56.84 ms, output throughput 789.25 tok/s.

The functional regression is fixed. The performance test still fails its pre-existing TPOT gate of 51.0 ms; this PR does not target performance.

Unit tests:

    PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest -q       test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_vit_npu_graph_runner.py       test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_vit_cuda_graph_runner.py
    # 7 passed

Formatting and lint:

    python3 -m ruff check       python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/graph_runner/vit_npu_graph_runner.py       python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py       test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_vit_npu_graph_runner.py
    python3 -m ruff format --check       python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/graph_runner/vit_npu_graph_runner.py       python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py       test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_vit_npu_graph_runner.py

- [x] Add a regression unit test.

title: [observability] Fix missing e2e/decode/inference latency span attributes
author: 123liuziming
body:
## Motivation

When tracing is enabled, the root span of a finished request is missing three latency attributes:

- `gen_ai.latency.e2e`
- `gen_ai.latency.time_in_model_decode`
- `gen_ai.latency.time_in_model_inference`

while `gen_ai.latency.time_in_model_prefill` and `gen_ai.latency.time_to_first_token` are present. This makes it impossible to see end-to-end or decode latency from exported traces, even though the same numbers are correctly reported through `meta_info` and Prometheus metrics.

The cause is a call ordering problem. `convert_to_gen_ai_span_attrs()` only emits an attribute when the timestamps it derives from are non-zero, and `_handle_batch_output()` built the attribute dict and wrote it onto the root span **before** calling `set_finished_time()`:

```python
if state.finished:
    if state.time_stats.trace_ctx.tracing_enable:
        state.time_stats.trace_ctx.trace_set_root_attrs(
            self.convert_to_span_attrs(state, recv_obj, i)   # finished_time is still 0.0 here
        )
    state.time_stats.set_finished_time()
```

At that point `finished_time` is still `0.0`, so the three attributes derived from it are silently dropped. The two attributes that survive are exactly those that depend only on `created_time` / `api_server_dispatch_finish_time` / `first_token_time`, which are already stamped — matching the observed symptom.

They cannot be attached afterwards either: `trace_req_finish()` ends the root span and sets `root_span = None`, so any later `trace_set_root_attrs()` is a no-op.

## Modifications

- `APIServerReqTimeStats.set_finished_time()` now takes an optional `span_attrs` and derives the latency attributes itself, after `finished_time` is stamped and before the root span is closed. The ordering can no longer be got wrong by callers.
- `_handle_batch_output()` passes the non-latency span attributes (token usage, sampling params, finish reason) into `set_finished_time()` instead of writing them to the root span separately.
- `convert_to_span_attrs()` no longer adds the latency attributes, so there is a single place that computes them.

As a side effect the abort path (`_handle_abort_req`) and the crash-dump path, which call `set_finished_time()` directly, now also get the latency attributes on their root span.

Extended `test/registered/unit/observability/test_req_time_stats.py` with coverage for:

- `convert_to_gen_ai_span_attrs()` omits the `finished_time`-derived attributes before the request finishes, and populates all five afterwards.
- `set_finished_time()` merges the derived latency attributes into the `trace_req_finish()` call and forwards caller-supplied attributes without mutating the caller's dict.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable — observability only, no change to model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable — no change on the hot path. The latency attributes were already being computed once per finished request; this only moves where that happens.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: Fix mamba radix cache ssm state indexing
author: ispobock
body:
## Motivation

Supersedes #33450 and closes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/31833, which was closed as completed but never landed a fix. The root-cause analysis and the kernel-side fix in the first commit are @adityakamat24's work from #33450, rebased onto current main.

With `--mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer` on a Mamba2 model, the mamba radix cache stores the wrong intermediate SSM state for most requests in a multi-request prefill batch. No crash, no assert, just a state taken at the wrong token position, so later prefix-cache hits continue from a corrupted state.

`_init_track_ssm_indices` indexes the packed per-chunk states `h` as a per-request concatenation of chunk grids. For Mamba2 it is one global grid over the flattened batch: `_chunk_state_fwd` computes `nchunks = ceil(seqlen / chunk_size)` where `seqlen` is the whole prefill batch, and `mamba.py` calls the kernel with `hidden_states_p.view(1, num_prefill_tokens, ...)`. The state for request `i` lives at flat token `query_start_loc[i] + aligned_len`, which is on the grid only when `query_start_loc[i]` is chunk-aligned. The first request in a batch always is, later ones generally are not, which is why single-request batches never see it.

The FLA branch is a genuine per-request grid and is untouched, so GDN/KDA models are unaffected. This is Mamba2 only.

The second commit keeps the read path where the position is on the grid, and rebuilds only the off-grid positions. Rebuilding everything is numerically correct but not bit-exact, and the rebuilt value depends on the flat offsets, so a chunk-aligned batch stops being reproducible.

Measured with sglang's own KL helpers on `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2` (`--mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer --enable-deterministic-inference`):

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `logprobs_match` (floor) | 1.6608e-4 | 1.6608e-4 |
| `prefill_cache_hit` | 2.5834e-2 | **1.6835e-4** |
| `decode_cache_hit` | 5.2860e-5 | 5.2860e-5 |

`prefill_cache_hit` drops **153x** onto the model's own prefill/decode floor. The other two are bit-identical to main, so nothing outside the tracked-state path moved.

A cached state must not depend on what else was in the prefill batch that produced it. Filling the cache at concurrency 1 vs 16 and rescoring serially, on chunk-aligned prompt lengths:

| | main | #33450 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| max abs logprob delta | 0.000000 | 1.059 | 0.000000 |

## Accuracy

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2 \
  --trust-remote-code --tp 1 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \
  --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer
```

```bash
sgl-eval run aime26 --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 \
  --n-repeats 8 --max-tokens 64000 --temperature 1.0 --top-p 0.95 \
  --num-threads 64
```

```
== aime26 ==
30 examples x 8 repeats  |  1804.8s  |  2901 tok/s  |  5.2M tokens

* pass@1[avg-of-8]  =  80.83% +/- 2.95% (SEM 1.04%)
  pass@8            =  93.33%
  majority@8        =  88.33%
  no_answer         =  0.83%
  stop_rate         =  99.17%
  truncated_rate    =  0.83%
  error_rate        =  0.00%
```

title: [Fix] Prevalidate JSON Schema support per grammar backend
author: JustinPerlman
body:
## Problem

SGLang currently treats successful grammar compilation as proof that a JSON Schema is supported. Some backends instead compile successfully while silently dropping constraints:

- XGrammar ignores unsupported assertion keywords and prioritizes `format` over `pattern` over `minLength`/`maxLength`.
- Outlines Core 0.1.x similarly ignores unsupported assertions and chooses one constraint family based on parser dispatch order.

The request then succeeds, but generated output can violate the schema the client supplied.

## Change

- Prevalidate JSON Schemas against the configured grammar backend before compilation.
- Reject XGrammar keywords and string-constraint combinations that XGrammar 0.2.x cannot fully enforce.
- Reject Outlines constraints and combinations that Outlines Core 0.1.x silently ignores or weakens.
- Traverse only actual subschema positions, so schema-shaped values inside `const`, `enum`, `default`, and `examples` are not misclassified.
- Include a JSON Pointer in errors to identify the unsupported nested subschema.
- Keep each backend native compiler as the final authority for malformed schemas and explicitly unsupported syntax.

Rejected schemas use the existing `InvalidGrammarObject` path, which terminates the request as an HTTP 400 instead of generating against a weakened grammar. llguidance is unchanged because its native JSON Schema conversion and matcher construction already reject unsupported input.

This does not introduce an automatic backend-selection mode; validation follows the backend selected at server launch.

## Tests

Adds CPU tests for supported schemas, every known silently ignored XGrammar keyword, unknown formats, mixed string constraints, Outlines semantic-loss cases, safe nested traversal, JSON Pointer escaping, and rejection before backend compilation.

Related: #28804, #37707, #37726, mlc-ai/xgrammar#798.

title: [HiCache] Fix sparse hybrid transfer layer IDs
author: alphabetc1
body:
### Summary

Fix hybrid HiCache transfer coverage for sparse layer IDs with **pipeline parallel size 1 (`PP=1`)**. Nemotron-H interleaves attention/Mamba layers with uncached MLP layers, so the number of cache-eligible layers is smaller than the layer-ID span.

The hybrid assembly sites previously used `len(union_of_layer_mappings)` as the exclusive transfer-ID bound. For IDs such as `{0, 2, 6}`, that bound is 3: H2D iteration misses layer 6, and the per-layer event array is too short for its consumer index.

### Fix

- Use `max(union_of_mapping_keys) + 1` at the four hybrid assembly sites. Existing per-pool mappers skip absent IDs, so holes do not cause copies of uncached layers.
- Rename the bound to `transfer_layer_id_limit` throughout the controller, L2 transfer, assembler, draft lookup, linker, and retraction call chain. Physical pool layer counts retain their separate meaning.
- Remove the duplicate layer-count field from `StackBuildResult`; logging uses the controller's effective bound.

The confirmed count/span defect concerns H2D traversal and per-layer completion-event indexing. The current all-layer D2H backup path traverses physical buffers and does not use this global-ID loop bound.

### Scope: PP=1

At PP=1, `start_layer=0`, so global layer IDs and consumer wait indices agree. This PR fixes sparse-ID coverage in that configuration.

HybridLinear/Mamba HiCache with PP>1 has a **pre-existing** producer/consumer coordinate mismatch: transfer completion uses global IDs while consumers wait with `layer_id - start_layer`. Increasing the bound does not resolve that mismatch. PP correctness, broader auditing, and GPU qualification are tracked separately in #38866. This PR does not add PP support or a new PP configuration guard.

The existing [PP review comment](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37870#discussion_r3928254343) identifies a valid limitation; its follow-up is #38866. This scope statement does not imply that every other HiCache + PP implementation has the same defect.

### Verification

PP=1 on H200:

- Tiny `nemotron_h`, pattern `M-M-M-M*-M-M-M-M-M*-`, dummy weights: 11 cache-eligible layer IDs, highest ID 18, corrected bound 19.
- Actual BF16 Nemotron Nano 9B v2: 56 model layers, 31 cache-eligible layer IDs, highest ID 54, corrected bound 55.
- For both models: prime with 3072 tokens, evict using three distinct 3072-token prompts, then replay. Replay reported `cached_tokens_details={"device":0,"host":2048}`. The 16 generated token IDs matched the prime response, with maximum output-logprob difference 0.
- Focused HiCache unit tests: 37 passed, 1 skipped. Sparse-mapping tests verify the exclusive bound and mapper behavior; dispatch tests cover the renamed parameter chain.

These checks cover the patched PP=1 path. The latest validation did not run a pre-fix GPU A/B, PP>1, NVFP4 KV cache, or GLM hybrid DSA qualification.

### Related

Supersedes #31745, which addressed the count/span defect against an earlier assembly layout. PP follow-up: #38866.

title: Fix UNO test adapter subdirectory resolution
author: yyihuang
body:
## Summary

- resolve the default UNO LoRA from the model repository's `adapter/` subdirectory
- download only the adapter config and safetensors before the server subprocess enables offline mode
- preserve `SGLANG_TEST_UNO_LORA_PATH` overrides unchanged
- add focused mocked coverage for default and override path resolution
- retain per-mode TPF and AR-parity gates without ranking two independent stochastic generations

## Why

The current `s-sahoo/uno-qwen3-8B` revision is a composite model repository. Its LoRA files are `adapter/adapter_config.json` and `adapter/adapter_model.safetensors`, while the UNO test passes the repository root as a standard LoRA directory. The loader therefore looks for a nonexistent root `adapter_config.json` and the Base shard fails before exercising UNO.

After resolving the adapter, Base run [33802809898](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33802809898) exercised linear and tree UNO successfully but reproducibly measured tree TPF `2.704` below linear TPF `3.254` on its H100 runner. The originating H200 run measured the opposite ordering. Because the modes consume independent stochastic samples, their relative ranking is not a portable correctness invariant. The test still requires both modes to perform verify steps, achieve TPF above `1.5`, satisfy their exact server configuration, and preserve the 32-token greedy AR prefix for every prompt.

## Validation

- `python3 -m py_compile test/registered/spec/uno/test_uno.py`
- `git diff --check`
- Base run 33802809898 confirmed the fixed adapter path loads and reached every UNO serving mode; its sole causal failure was the removed cross-mode stochastic ranking assertion
- the existing CUDA UNO end-to-end test remains the loader, AR-parity, configuration, verify-step, and per-mode TPF gate in CI

title: [Fix] Register triton.runtime.cache.triton_key in the MPS stub so torch.compile keeps working
author: alexnails
body:
## Symptom

On macOS arm64 with MPS and no real Triton installed, `torch.compile` is broken **process-wide** for any code, not just sglang's own, as soon as `sglang` has been imported:

```bash
# without sglang -> works
python -c "import torch; torch.compile(lambda x: x*2+1)(torch.randn(8))"

# with sglang imported first -> fails
python -c "import sglang, torch; torch.compile(lambda x: x*2+1)(torch.randn(8))"
# torch._dynamo.exc.BackendCompilerFailed: backend='inductor' raised:
# TypeError: 'module' object is not callable
```

## Cause

`python/sglang/_platform_stubs.py::install_platform_stubs()` installs a fake `triton` package plus a `_TritonFinder` meta-path finder so sglang's own `import triton` / `@triton.jit` kernel files can load on a box with no real Triton. This is gated on darwin+arm64, then `torch.backends.mps.is_available()`, then genuine absence of `triton`.

Torch 2.13's inductor FX-graph cache fingerprinting (`torch/_inductor/codecache.py::CacheBase.get_system()` -> `triton_key()`) unconditionally probes for a triton version string, on every `torch.compile`, regardless of the compile target device. It does this via `torch/_inductor/runtime/triton_compat.py`, which tries:

```python
try:
    from triton.runtime.cache import triton_key
except ImportError:
    from triton.compiler.compiler import triton_key
```

The stub already defines a working callable at the fallback location (`triton.compiler.compiler.triton_key = lambda: "triton-stub"`), but never registers `triton.runtime.cache` at all — that path was presumably added for an older torch that only checked the fallback location.

Because `triton.runtime.cache` isn't pre-registered, the import falls through to the catch-all `_TritonFinder.find_spec()`, which returns a `ModuleSpec` with `loader=None`. Python's import machinery treats a loader-less package spec as a **namespace package**: it materializes a brand-new, real, empty `types.ModuleType` and silently overwrites/bypasses our `_MockModule` (with its `__getattr__`/`__call__` behavior) in `sys.modules`. So `from triton.runtime.cache import triton_key` doesn't raise `ImportError` (which would correctly trigger the fallback) — it "succeeds" by binding `triton_key` to an inert, non-callable module object. Torch then calls it and blows up with `TypeError: 'module' object is not callable`.

This exact failure mode — the catch-all finder materializing something that torch expects to be more specific than a generic mock — is the same class of bug the stub already worked around once, for `triton.runtime.autotuner.{OutOfResources,PTXASError}` ("Torch 2.13 imports these as classes while initializing Inductor... Define them explicitly so the catch-all meta-path finder does not materialize class names as modules").

## Fix

Register `triton.runtime.cache.triton_key` explicitly, as a real callable, mirroring the existing `triton.compiler.compiler.triton_key` stub (both now share one `_triton_key()` helper returning a stable `"triton-stub"` string). This makes torch's *primary* lookup path succeed with a genuinely callable stub, directly, without relying on exception-driven fallback through the buggy catch-all finder path.

### Why this shape, and not the alternatives

- **Not a meta-path-finder rewrite.** The root architectural issue (loader-less specs get treated as namespace packages, silently discarding `_MockModule` instances) is real and could in principle also bite other dynamically-materialized `triton.*` submodules accessed via `import`/`from...import` statements. But fixing it generally is a much larger, riskier change with wide blast radius across the whole mock system. Registering the one concrete symbol torch actually needs, the same way the file already does for the autotuner exception classes, is the smaller and more robust fix and matches existing precedent in this file.
- **Not `torch.utils._triton.has_triton()`.** That function isn't on this call path at all — `torch/_inductor/runtime/triton_compat.py` derives triton availability from its own bare `try: import triton except ImportError: triton = None`, independent of `has_triton()`. Making `has_triton()` return `False` would not prevent this crash.
- **`triton.__version__` left untouched.** It advertises `"3.0.0"`, which is arguably dishonest ("the stub's job is to survive `import triton`, not to claim Triton works"), but it isn't part of this crash's causal chain (the crash happens before any version string is consulted). Several sglang kernel files branch on it at *module import time* (`kernels/ops/attention/extend_attention.py`, `kernels/ops/mamba/triton_ops/mamba_ssm.py`, `kernels/ops/attention/fla/utils.py`, `srt/layers/attention/dsa/utils.py`, etc.), so changing it is unrelated risk with no benefit to this bug and was left out of scope.

## Blast radius

Any Python process that imports `sglang` on an Apple-Silicon box without a real Triton installed had `torch.compile` broken for the remainder of the process — including completely unrelated, non-sglang code sharing the interpreter.

## Verification

- `import sglang, torch; torch.compile(lambda x: x*2+1)(torch.randn(8))` now succeeds.
- `import sglang` and `import sglang.srt.mem_cache.allocator.paged` still succeed with no real Triton installed.
- `test/registered/unit/platforms/` and `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_asymmetric_mha_pool_host_unit.py` pass (71 passed) with no `torch.compile` shim required.
- A handful of other module-scope `@triton.jit` / `triton.Config` / `triton.__version__`-gated modules (`merge_state`, `rotary_triton`, `extend_attention`, `decode_attention`, `dsa_metadata`, `mla_kv_pack_quantize_fp8`, `mamba_ssm`, `ssd_combined`, `ssd_chunk_scan`, `fla/utils`, `lora_tuning_config`, `dsa/utils`, `aiter_mla_gluon`, `fused_moe_triton_config`) still import cleanly, confirming no regression to the no-Triton import path.
- Added a regression test in `test/registered/unit/platforms/test_mps_triton_stub.py` that actually runs `torch.compile(...)` after `import sglang` (the existing test in that file only checked an import, not a compile).
- `ruff format` / `ruff check --select=F401,F821,UP037` clean on both changed files.

### Limitation of the regression test

The stub installs only on darwin+arm64 with MPS and no real Triton, so on Linux CI the new test passes trivially -- it exercises nothing. The same is true of the test already in that file. It has teeth only when run on Apple Silicon, which is where the bug lives; it is a guard for local development and for anyone running the suite on a Mac, not a CI gate.

title: [Fix] dsa: Make the fused top-k exact on an overflowing threshold bin
author: xiaofei-zheng
body:
## Motivation

The coarse histogram bin comes from the top bits of the fp16 cast, so one bin spans a quarter-binade. The collect pass stores at most 2048 threshold-bin candidates; when the bin is larger, `handle_tie` ranks whichever arrived first and silently returns a wrong top-k set.

Found while profiling GLM-5.2 decode on MI355X: ~0.04% of rows entered this path across all 8 ranks, with a largest observed bin of 4139 against the 2048 cap and none of those rows bit-identical. #35257 reports the same defect independently from the CUDA side — referenced, not closed.

## Modifications

When the threshold bin overflows, narrow it with three exact-key radix rounds (12 / 12 / 8 bits), then make one final input scan to emit candidates above the selected bucket and re-stage the bucket for the existing tie handler. The refinement histogram overlays the dead arrival-order buffer, so LDS is unchanged.

The cold scan uses a separate reversed-lane load path. This keeps its load-address state out of the fast path's registers and restores most of the CUDA regression reported in review.

Replace the fp16-bin boundary conversion with exact fp32 bounds. In particular, when a bin's high edge is `+0.0`, the boundary advances to the smallest positive subnormal so `-0.0` cannot be misclassified as above the bin.

The ROCm long-row split path from #39931 gets the same refinement: each block publishes its uncapped bin count, and the last block refines the whole row when the bin overflows.

The fast path only adds the overflow comparison. The ROCm `__launch_bounds__` argument also states the physical floor of 4 waves/SIMD; the CUDA spelling is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

The exactness test covers register, streaming and split (4×65536) shapes with six distributions, including adjacent fp32 values and `-0.0`; on CUDA it skips rows longer than 24576, which can reach the still-unrefined cluster path.

| suite | result before the fix |
|---|---|
| 300 pre-existing cases | 300 passed |
| 10 overflowing non-identical cases | 10 failed |
| 2 `all_equal` controls | 2 passed |

The signed-zero cases also fail on the pre-review refinement and pass with the new boundary conversion. All 330 cases pass on the merged tree; on the split shape, 4 of the 6 distributions failed before the refinement.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

MI355X (gfx950), five paired runs per arm on one GPU, 200 iterations after warmup:

| distribution | shape | main | this PR | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `randn` (hot path) | 6×8192 | 5.430 µs | 5.338 µs | −1.7% |
| `randn` (hot path) | 4×32768 | 12.270 µs | 12.188 µs | −0.7% |
| `narrow_bin` | 6×8192 | 16.821 µs | 20.937 µs | +24.5% |
| `narrow_bin` | 4×32768 | 29.652 µs | 50.030 µs | +68.7% |
| `two_values` (32-bit refinement) | 6×8192 | 11.487 µs | 34.862 µs | +203.5% |
| `two_values` (32-bit refinement) | 4×32768 | 36.314 µs | 117.756 µs | +224.3% |

The cold-path delta is the cost of exact work that main skips by returning a wrong answer. It is entered on ~0.04% of rows in the serving traffic above. Against the previous PR implementation, the new scan is 2.6–5.3% faster on `narrow_bin`. On the latest tree, a clean local JIT build is 10.50 s versus 10.02 s on main (+4.8%), rather than the nearly 2× CUDA increase reported before this rewrite.

Without overflow the split path is unchanged (15.5–20.1 µs for batch 1–8, 64K–128K, before and after).

On gfx950: 63 → 71 VGPRs, zero spills, LDS unchanged at 26928 B. We do not have NVIDIA hardware; CUDA register pressure and B200 performance need CI/reviewer measurement.

## Known gap

The CUDA-only `TopKCluster` path still truncates. Refining there needs cluster-wide histogram and emit counters rather than the block-local ones used here.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add exactness tests.
- [x] Provide accuracy and performance results.
- [x] Keep documentation and comments synchronized.

title: fix(qwen3_5): let the GDN gated norm follow the model's device
author: Zhichenzzz
body:
## What

`Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet` builds its gated norm with an explicit
`device=torch.get_device_module().current_device()`. The loader already builds
the whole model inside `with torch.device(device_config.device)`, and
`RMSNorm.__init__` defaults `device=None` precisely so its parameter inherits
that context — so passing the accelerator explicitly is what overrides it.

Dropping the argument is the whole change; `dtype` is left alone since
`set_default_torch_dtype` makes it equivalent either way.

## Why it matters

The norm's weight lands on CUDA even when the caller asked for a CPU model: 24
of Qwen3.5-4B's 627 parameters, 128 elements each. A few kilobytes, but enough
to break any path that needs a genuine CPU replica. SGLang's own p2p/RDMA weight
transfer stages one and pins it, which fails outright:

```
RuntimeError: cannot pin 'CUDABFloat16Type' only dense CPU tensors can be pinned
```

Every training backend hits this, since the replica is built before any weights
are streamed.

## Evidence

Reproduced with no training backend in the picture, by building the replica the
way the transfer does:

```python
get_model(
    model_config=ModelConfig(path),
    load_config=LoadConfig(load_format="dummy"),
    device_config=DeviceConfig(device="cpu"),
)
```

| model | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-4B | 24 of 627 params on CUDA, `pin_memory` raises | **0 of 627, `pin_memory` ok** |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B | 0 of 435 (no GDN layers) | 0 of 435, unchanged |

Also confirmed end to end: with this fix the p2p weight-transfer path completes
on Qwen3.5-4B, where it previously failed during `connect`.

title: [diffusion] fix: preserve mapped courier tensor lifetime
author: Grypse
body:
## Motivation

The mapped-layer courier creates device tensors on a private copy stream and hands them to the compute stream. `_collect_mapped_layer()` waited for copy completion but did not register the consuming stream with PyTorch's caching allocator. Once the layer post-hook dropped the last Python reference, the allocator could reuse storage while compute kernels were still reading it, silently corrupting MiniMax-H3 output into colored noise.

Fixes #37963.

## Modifications

- Capture the current compute stream and wait for the courier copy event.
- Call `record_stream(compute_stream)` for each non-CPU courier tensor before binding it to the target parameter.
- Add a deterministic regression test that verifies collected mapped weights register their consuming stream without requiring a GPU.

## Accuracy Tests

On one NVIDIA L20 with `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3` FL2VA, the comparison held the model revision, prompt, seed, 20 inference steps, 480p target, and `torch_sdpa` backend constant:

- courier enabled before the fix: colored-noise video;
- courier disabled: correct 15-second MP4;
- courier enabled after the fix: correct 15-second MP4, byte-identical to the courier-disabled baseline.

Both correct paths produced SHA-256:

```text
d66baa8ab742b1be5068cb14d8d35c01bc81f2dc43cc4ba8e9ea2d2e895a7701
```

Local checks:

```text
PASS: exact deterministic regression test
Ruff 0.15.1: All checks passed
Ruff 0.15.1 format: 2 files already formatted
git diff --check: passed
```

The exact regression test was executed through an isolated source harness on macOS because a full SGLang import requires Linux/CUDA-only dependencies. The repository CI remains the authoritative full-suite run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Single-run L20 comparison with identical generation inputs:

| Metric | Courier disabled | Patched courier | Difference |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Denoising | 895.0266 s | 822.8433 s | -72.1833 s (-8.06%) |
| Total generation | 938.53 s | 876.85 s | -61.68 s (-6.57%) |
| Peak VRAM | 23,120 MB | 26,160 MB | +3,040 MB |

This is correctness evidence that the fix preserves courier overlap, not a generalized benchmark claim.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No public API or configuration changed; the issue and regression test document the CUDA lifetime contract.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: fix(glm4v): disambiguate mixed image video offsets
author: DUXin-ece
body:
## Motivation

GLM-V models use different placeholders for images and videos before tokenization, but video frames are represented using the image token ID after tokenization:

```python
image_token_id=self.IM_TOKEN_ID
video_token_id=self.IM_TOKEN_ID
```

The generic multimodal offset collection logic currently finds placeholder spans using only the modality token ID. Therefore, when a request contains both images and a video, the image and video items can both receive all image-token spans.

For example, a request containing six images and one video sampled into 31 frames produced an image item with six image grids but 37 offsets:

```text
6 image spans + 31 video-frame spans = 37 offsets
```

During chunked prefill, the incorrect offsets caused the number of expected multimodal tokens to exceed the available image embeddings:

```text
RuntimeError: Insufficient multimodal embedding length:
num_mm_tokens_in_input_ids=16325
vs num_mm_tokens_in_embedding=5391
```

Image-only and video-only requests are unaffected because there is no ambiguity between modalities.

Fixes #37968 

## Modifications

- Added `BaseMultimodalProcessor.get_mm_item_offsets()` as an overridable hook for assigning placeholder offsets to a specific modality.
- Preserved the existing token-ID-based behavior as the default implementation for other multimodal processors.
- Overrode the hook in `Glm4vImageProcessor`.
- Used the distinct `<|begin_of_video|>` and `<|end_of_video|>` boundary tokens to identify which shared image-token spans belong to videos.
- Assigned spans inside video boundaries to `Modality.VIDEO`.
- Assigned the remaining spans to `Modality.IMAGE`.
- Performed the classification before `get_new_expanded_mm_items()` splits bundled multimodal features.
- Added CPU unit tests covering:
  - Multiple images followed by a multi-frame video.
  - Interleaved image and video content.
  - Existing behavior when image and video token IDs are distinct.

The implementation uses video boundaries instead of assigning the first `N` offsets to images, so it also works when images and videos are interleaved.

## Accuracy Tests

This change only corrects multimodal placeholder ownership during request preprocessing. It does not modify model weights, kernels, or forward computation.

Before the fix, the mixed image-video request failed with HTTP 500:

```text
IMAGE item:
  image_grid_thw shape: (6, 3)
  offset count: 37

offset_mm_tokens=16325
embedding_tokens=5391
```

The expected assignment after the fix is:

```text
IMAGE item:
  image grids: 6
  offsets: 6 image spans

VIDEO item:
  video grids: 1
  offsets: 31 video-frame spans
```

A regression test was added:

```bash
pytest -q test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_glm4v_mixed_offsets.py
```

The test is registered in the CPU CI suite:

```python
register_cpu_ci(est_time=2, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
```

Local validation:

```text
Python syntax compilation: passed
git diff --check: passed
pre-commit hooks: passed
```

The complete pytest run was not executed on the local development host because PyTorch is not installed there. The test is registered to run in the SGLang CPU CI environment.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

The additional classification only runs while constructing multimodal request metadata. It does not affect model execution, CUDA kernels, attention, or decoding.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [formatting guide](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [unit testing guide](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Documentation is not required because this is an internal correctness fix with no user-facing API changes.
- [x] Accuracy and speed benchmarks are not applicable because this change only corrects request preprocessing metadata.
- [x] Follow the SGLang [code style guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, and `/rerun-failed-ci`.
4. After CI passes and the required approvals are obtained, ask Merge Oncalls or a maintainer with write permission to merge the PR.

title: [BugFix] Pass token-major Q/K tensors from Gemma-3 to RadixAttention
author: janbernloehr
body:
## Motivation

Serving `google/gemma-3-12b-it` with FlashInfer at `tp=1` can fail during breakable-prefill CUDA-graph replay with:

```text
ValueError: q.shape[0] (8) does not match qo_indptr[-1] (7)
```

`RadixAttention` expects Q and K to use the token-major layout `[tokens, heads, head_dim]`. The Gemma-3 native and CPU attention paths instead pass `[1, tokens, heads, head_dim]`. When a seven-token request replays in an eight-token graph bucket, token-based narrowing therefore operates on the singleton batch dimension instead of the token dimension, leaving eight query rows for a `qo_indptr` that describes seven tokens.

This supersedes #36857 and addresses the review feedback there by fixing the Gemma-3 model code rather than changing the shared `RadixAttention` input semantics.

## Modifications

- Convert Q and K to token-major rank-3 tensors before calling `RadixAttention` in both `forward_native` and `forward_cpu`.
- Reshape the attention result to `[tokens, q_size]` before the output projection, covering the layouts returned by the supported attention backends.
- Add focused CPU tests for both Gemma-3 paths. The tests verify the Q/K/V shapes observed by `RadixAttention`, the input shape seen by the output projection, and the final output shape.

The shared `RadixAttention` implementation is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

### Focused tests

```text
python3 test/registered/unit/models/test_gemma3_attention_layout.py
Ran 2 tests in 0.001s
OK
```

Ruff checks and Python bytecode compilation also pass for the modified files.

### End-to-end regression

The exact candidate commit was applied to an upstream SGLang development image and exercised with `google/gemma-3-12b-it`, FlashInfer, `tp=1`, and breakable prefill CUDA graphs.

The formerly failing seven-real-token/eight-token-graph case completed successfully:

```text
Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 7, ..., cuda graph: True
POST /generate HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

No `q.shape`/`qo_indptr` mismatch or attention exception occurred.

The unpatched FP8 and NVFP4 configurations had previously reproduced the same `(8)` versus `(7)` mismatch.

### Additional multimodal validation

A separate run with multimodal serving enabled completed:

- concurrency 1: 5/5 valid responses, zero errors;
- concurrency 16: 80/80 valid responses, zero errors;
- concurrency 64: 305/320 valid responses; 15 client connection timeouts were within the workload's acceptance threshold.

The concurrency-128 phase was stopped by an external time limit before completion. This separate run validates multimodal request handling, but it is not the CUDA-graph regression proof because enabling multimodal serving disables breakable prefill CUDA graphs for Gemma-3.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The Q/K normalization uses `squeeze(0)` after the existing layout transformation and adds no model computation. The output `reshape` replaces the previous backend-dependent conditional flattening.

No controlled before/after performance claim is made because the unpatched target path crashes. The completed multimodal profiling phases above remained stable through concurrency 64; the final phase was limited by external runtime rather than a model or attention error.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No documentation change is required for this model tensor-layout correction.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [diffusion] fix host-resident vocab tables loaded on GPU
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

Layerwise offload keeps declared large vocabulary tables on the host and moves embedding indices to the host before the gather. However, `detach_host_resident_tables` retained `weight.data` on its current device. Model-owned loading paths can place the embedding on the accelerator before layerwise offload is configured, so restore put the weight back on CUDA while the pre-hook moved the indices to CPU:

```
RuntimeError: Expected all tensors to be on the same device, but got index is on cpu,
different from other tensors on cuda:0 (wrapper_CUDA__index_select)
```

## Fix

- Normalize the detached vocabulary-table storage to CPU before installing the placeholder.
- Keep the gather hook contract narrow: move only the embedding input (`args[0]`) to the host and move the result back to the compute device.
- Replace the previous direct-hook tests with a CUDA regression that starts with a GPU-resident `nn.Embedding`, performs the real forward after detach/restore, and checks the weight remains on CPU while the result returns to CUDA.


## Reproduction

The regression requires a CUDA GPU. Fetch the PR first:

```bash
git fetch https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang.git \
  refs/pull/38012/head:refs/remotes/pr/38012
```

To reproduce the original CPU-index/CUDA-weight failure on the previous PR head:

```bash
git switch --detach e405db08c4ebdd541fb15179f0ed55db2b8225d3
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 PYTHONPATH=python python - <<'PY'
from unittest.mock import patch

import torch

from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.managers.memory_managers import layerwise_offload
from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.managers.memory_managers.layerwise_offload import (
    detach_host_resident_tables,
    restore_host_resident_tables,
)


class Model(torch.nn.Module):
    host_resident_table_names = ["embed"]

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.embed = torch.nn.Embedding(4096, 64)


model = Model().to("cuda")
ids = torch.tensor([[1, 2, 3]], device="cuda")
threshold = f"{layerwise_offload.__name__}.HOST_RESIDENT_TABLE_MIN_BYTES"
with patch(threshold, 1024):
    detached = detach_host_resident_tables(model)
    model.to("cuda")
    restore_host_resident_tables(detached, "cuda")

model(ids)
PY
```

Expected result: `RuntimeError: Expected all tensors to be on the same device ... index is on cpu ... tensors on cuda:0`.

To verify the fix on the updated PR head:

```bash
git switch --detach refs/remotes/pr/38012
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 PYTHONPATH=python pytest -q \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_host_resident_vocab_table.py::TestDetachAndRestore::test_a_device_resident_table_is_parked_on_the_host
```

Expected result: `1 passed`.


## H200 validation

Validated on one otherwise idle NVIDIA H200 (GPU 1), using the same regression test against three revisions:

| Revision | Result |
| --- | --- |
| latest `main` (`f1f2380d2b`) | fails with the exact CPU-index/CUDA-weight `index_select` error |
| previous PR head (`e405db08c4`) | fails with the same error |
| updated PR | passes |

Related suites on latest `main` plus this patch:

```
pytest -q \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_host_resident_vocab_table.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_layerwise_offload.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_component_residency.py

174 passed
```

Pre-commit passes for both changed files.

The original `fal/ideogram-v4-fast` end-to-end command could not be rerun on this H200 because its `ideogram-ai/ideogram-4-nf4-diffusers` dependency is gated for the machine account. The GPU regression above reproduces the exact failing embedding operation without relying on that checkpoint.

title: [diffusion] fix: do not interleave comfy-kitchen MXFP8 scales twice
author: TyGu888
body:
## Motivation

`comfy-kitchen` serializes MXFP8 block scales **already in the `SWIZZLE_32_4_4` byte
order** that FlashInfer's cutlass / cutedsl kernels consume, while safetensors keeps
their logical `[N, K // 32]` shape. Nothing in the file distinguishes those bytes from
row-major scales, so `Fp8LinearMethod._process_mxfp8_linear_weight_scale`
(`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py`, cutlass/cutedsl branch) runs
`block_scale_interleave` over bytes that are already interleaved.

The second permutation is **silent**. No exception, no warning, no shape mismatch: the
checkpoint loads, the kernels run at full speed, and the sample decodes to dark,
low-amplitude colour noise. A user has no signal to distinguish this from a bad prompt
or a bad checkpoint.

## Modifications

- Add `ComfyMXFP8LinearMethod`, a thin `Fp8LinearMethod` subclass that hands FlashInfer
  the serialized scale bytes flattened instead of re-interleaving them.
- Route `MXFP8Config.get_quant_method` through it.

Blast radius is limited to comfy checkpoints by construction. `layer_markers` is only
ever populated by `resolve_comfy_checkpoint_quantization`
(`runtime/utils/quantization_utils.py`), which is also the sole construction site of
`MXFP8Config` with markers; `MXFP8Config.from_config` (the `config.json` path) leaves it
`None`. The same predicate already gates `checkpoint_uses_native_qkv_layout` in
`MXFP8Config.__init__`. For every non-comfy MXFP8 checkpoint, for every backend
other than cutlass / cutedsl, and for an explicit `scale_u8` (row-major scales
converted from block-FP8, added in #40039), the call falls through to `super()`
unchanged.

Two unit tests in `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_transformer_quant.py`,
both CPU-only and free of checkpoint fixtures:

- `test_comfy_mxfp8_scales_are_not_interleaved_twice` — a comfy-marked config yields
  `ComfyMXFP8LinearMethod` and its scale bytes survive load in order. It also asserts
  that `Fp8LinearMethod._process_mxfp8_linear_weight_scale` still exists, so renaming
  the SRT hook fails loudly instead of silently restoring the double interleave, and
  that an explicit `scale_u8` is still handed to SRT's interleave.
- `test_config_driven_mxfp8_keeps_srt_scale_processing` — a `config.json`-driven config
  still delegates to SRT.

The existing `test_minimax_h3_global_mxfp8_metadata_selects_srt_per_layer` continues to
pass: `ComfyMXFP8LinearMethod` is a `Fp8LinearMethod`.

## Accuracy Tests

Measured on an RTX 5090 (sm_120) with a MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA MXFP8 single file
(`rzgar/...minimax_h3_ref2va_mxfp8.safetensors`, 47.6 GB), one real attention weight
matrix, compared against the dequantized reference:

| scale handling | cosine | relative L2 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| checkpoint bytes flattened (this PR) | 0.999641 | 0.02679 |
| `block_scale_interleave` applied again (today) | 0.739481 | 0.77703 |

End to end on a fixed-seed 768p Ref2VA request: before the fix the run completed in
746.16 s and decoded to colour noise; after the fix the same request produces a valid
video. A locally converted INT8 checkpoint through the same pipeline was clean
throughout, which isolates the fault to the MXFP8 loading path rather than the prompt,
reference, text encoder, VAE or model code.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No measurable change. The edit is on the load path only, and it replaces a
`block_scale_interleave` call with a `view(-1)`. The fixed-seed request above ran
746.16 s before and after within run-to-run noise; nothing in the forward path is
touched.

## Checklist

- [x] Formatted. `pre-commit` itself could not be installed on this machine (no PyPI
      egress), so the configured hooks were run individually and all pass on both files:
      `isort --check-only` (7.x and 8.x), `ruff check --select=F401,F821,UP037`,
      `ruff format --diff`, and `black --check` as a cross-check.
- [x] Unit tests added, in the existing `multimodal_gen` unit test file next to the
      other MXFP8 tests. That file uses plain `unittest.TestCase`; `CustomTestCase` and
      `register_*_ci` apply to registered suites under `test/registered/`, not here.
- [ ] Documentation — not applicable. No user-facing interface, flag or default
      changes; this restores correct output for checkpoints that already load today.
- [x] Accuracy results above. Speed: unchanged, load-path only.
- [x] Code style: no duplication, no device synchronization, no in-place argument
      mutation beyond what the base method already does, config class kept at the top of
      the file.

## Notes for reviewers

`block_scale_interleave` "may pad and/or reshape scales". Every Linear in the checkpoint
tested here has `N % 128 == 0`, so flatten-only matches. If comfy-kitchen ever
serializes an unpadded scale block for a shape FlashInfer would pad, this path needs the
padding applied without the permutation. Happy to add a shape guard if you would prefer
to fail loudly there rather than assume.

Found while evaluating self-describing single-file MiniMax-H3 checkpoints on a single
RTX 5090 32 GB (sm_120, driver 616.56, Windows 11 + WSL2 + Docker, TP=1) against
`20621aa14bda7726a8a968f326198eac61717fef`. Since then `main` gained the
`MXFP8OnlineLinearMethod` branch (#37903) and the `scale_u8` hook argument (#40039);
both are merged into this branch, and the cutlass/cutedsl branch in `srt/.../fp8.py`
still re-interleaves `layer.weight_scale_inv` on `main`, so the bug still reproduces
there.

title: fix(mamba): unify causal_conv1d col* dtype to x (MiniCPM-V-4.6 GDN prefill bf16/fp16 mismatch)
author: BBuf
body:
## Problem
MiniCPM-V-4.6 fails to serve on SGLang with a Triton compile error in the GDN prefill conv1d kernel:

```
AssertionError: Mismatched type for col0 between then block (<['256'], bf16>) and else block (<['256'], fp16>)
```

Root cause: MiniCPM-V-4.6 runs a Qwen3.5 LLM (bf16 conv-state cache) but its vision resampler emits **fp16** activations, so the GDN prefill mixes an fp16 `x` stream with a bf16 conv-state cache. The `col0..col3` sliding-window registers then disagree on dtype across the kernel — the `chunk_offset==0` branch loads them from the bf16 conv-state cache while the `chunk_offset>0` branch and the per-token sliding-window reassignment produce fp16 — and Triton's if/else phi type check aborts.

## Fix
Cast the conv-state loads to `x_ptr.dtype.element_ty` (and keep the zero-init on the same x dtype) so `col*` have a single dtype across the whole kernel. Zero-cost when the dtypes already match (the common case).

## Validation
- MiniCPM-V-4.6 now loads, captures decode CUDA graphs, and serves on RTX 5090 (bf16). Paired throughput 591/1885/5608/8013 tok/s at bs=1/4/16/32. (vLLM 0.28 cannot load this model at all — unrelated `k_proj` vs `qkv_proj` weight-mapping bug — so SGLang is the only working engine.)
- No change for models where x and the conv-state cache already share a dtype (the cast is a no-op).
