title: fix: gather CP-sharded tokens before TP-sharded dense MLP under prefill CP
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Summary

- make `LayerScatterModes` mark the dense MLP boundary `MOE_FULL` when strategy prefill CP actually shards tokens (`attn_cp_size > 1`, `--enable-prefill-cp`, generic CP-v2 platform), so the existing moe_cp all-gather runs before a TP-sharded dense MLP and the scatter after it
- refuse to fuse the MLP all-reduce into the next layer for `MOE_FULL` layers (fusion skips the postprocess scatter)
- add a unit test for the dense-layer scatter mode under prefill CP and a fusion-gate case for `MOE_FULL` layers

Replaces the workaround in #38070, which kept Qwen3 + HiCache on the legacy prefill-CP implementation.

## Root cause

`Qwen3ForCausalLM` (and every other dense MHA model) builds its MLP with `RowParallelLinear` over the whole TP group, which spans all CP ranks. Since #36223 made strategy prefill CP canonical, a CP-sharded prefill batch reaches that MLP with each CP pair holding a different half of the tokens, and the `down_proj` all-reduce sums partial outputs of unrelated tokens. `LayerScatterModes._compute_mlp_mode` returned `FULL` for dense layers, and `process_group_sizes[FULL] == attn_tp_size`, so `LayerCommunicator` performed no CP gather. MoE layers already handle this through `MOE_FULL`; MLA/DSA models through `DSACPLayerCommunicator`.

Before #36223 this test passed only because `Qwen3ForCausalLM` was outside the CP-v2 allowlist and `qwen3.py` has no legacy CP code: `--enable-prefill-cp` was a no-op and every CP rank prefilled the full sequence.

The corrupted hidden states produce generations that never emit EOS. With `max_new_tokens=16000` and `--max-total-tokens 14000`, every request runs to the cap, which is the KV-pool-full retraction loop seen in #38019 (each retraction frees 2.3K-6K tokens in the failing CI log). HiCache is incidental: the same configuration without HiCache reproduces.

## Validation

1x GB300 node, Qwen3-32B, `--tp-size 4 --attn-cp-size 2 --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy zigzag` (trtllm_mha):

| arm | GSM8K (200 q, few-shot) | output probe (20 q, max_new 2048) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main, no HiCache | 0.075 (invalid 0.115) | mean 640 tokens, 5/20 hit the length cap, completions repeat the question |
| this PR, no HiCache | 0.935 | mean 356 tokens, 20/20 stop |
| this PR, HiCache flags from the registered test | 0.940, 0 retractions | mean 356 tokens, 20/20 stop |
| this PR, `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_cp.py` (4 tests) | `Ran 4 tests in 274 s OK`, multiturn avg KL 0.0039 (threshold 0.005) | CI on main hit the 60 min stage timeout |

- new unit test fails on unfixed main and passes with this PR; existing `test_layer_communicator_fusion_gate.py` and `test_cp_strategy_unit.py` pass
- pre-commit hooks on changed files (isort, ruff, ruff-format, registered-test registry) pass

The change affects every model with dense layers when prefill CP is enabled on the generic CP path (no behavior change when prefill CP is off, in decode, for `--attn-cp-size` without `--enable-prefill-cp`, or for MLA/DSA CP). Please also run `test/registered/cp/test_gqa_prefill_cp.py` and `test/registered/cp/test_gpt_oss_4gpu_mxfp4_cp.py` to confirm the MoE path is unaffected.

title: [GLM-5.3] Fix DFlash graph counts and startup DeepGEMM memory budget
author: Fridge003
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #36507, based on `xinyuan/glm-5.3-flash-support` at `fead323b8f04938dbec66d19f18a1af03830d846`. Addresses the two distinct failures in [the targeted B200/H200 E2E results](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36507#issuecomment-5547761469).

- Preserve the CUDA graph registry's skip-missing-field behavior when a direct dense DFlash draft `ForwardBatch` omits both optional non-padding token-count tensors.
- Refresh the existing DeepGEMM auto-layout memory budget once at the end of scheduler worker startup, after target/draft/adaptive graph capture, sampling prewarm, post-capture KV sizing and weight-load finalization. Do this **before elastic-EP rejoin**, whose healthy peers do not participate in startup collectives. Retain the pre-capture initialization and world-wide minimum. No per-forward memory query is added.
- Clamp the compact DeepGEMM runner's exclusively owned gate/up workspace in place, avoiding two clamped copies plus their concatenation. Preserve the original BF16 values and asymmetric bounds.
- No test changes are included. Per review, restore the three modified unit-test files to the PR base and remove the newly added `test_deep_gemm_swiglu_limit.py`; keep all production fixes unchanged.

## Failure evidence

### B200: DFlash2 cannot finish startup

[Run 33930930911 / job 101209195354](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33930930911/job/101209195354) failed twice during DFlash2 health warmup:

```text
cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py: _num_token_non_padded_post_fill
buf.copy_(fb.num_token_non_padded)
TypeError: copy_(): argument 'other' (position 1) must be Tensor, not NoneType
```

The direct dense draft batch does not initialize either optional count; EP on the target still enables the slot. #37546 made this fallback copy unconditional, unlike the previous skip-missing behavior. **No B200 test method ran**; later classes were not validated by that run.

### H200: stale masked-layout budget after adaptive graph capture

[Run 33930938042 / job 101209216190](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33930938042/job/101209216190) passed HighThroughput GSM8K **0.938**, and LowLatency bs=1 **231.65 tok/s**, acceptance **4.446**. LowLatency GSM8K then OOMed on the first batched prefill while allocating a **2.25 GiB** masked DeepGEMM gateup tensor; subsequent HTTP errors and zero accuracy were cascade.

The auto budget was **3.83 GiB**, sampled before draft/adaptive graph allocations. After graph capture only **3.49 GiB** was free, yet the stale budget still admitted the large masked workspace. The final refresh lets the existing auto selector use compact layout for large eager prefill while captured decode graphs retain their recorded kernels. This is a startup budget refresh, not continuous memory tracking.

### H200 follow-up: avoidable copies in the compact SwiGLU clamp

The first patch's [H200 rerun 33934926587](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33934926587/job/101220871520) and the 8×H200 devbox independently reached the same second OOM. title: fix(moe): cast filtered-activation expert_ids to int32 for torch.compile
author: BBuf
body:
## Problem

Running a filtered MoE model (e.g. `baidu/Unlimited-OCR`) with `--enable-torch-compile` crashes during CUDA-graph capture:

```
RuntimeError: Failed at .../kernels/jit/csrc/elementwise/activation.cuh:233: expert_ids must have dtype int32
Exception: Capture cuda graph failed: ... expert_ids must have dtype int32
```

## Root cause

The compiled `inplace_fused_experts` custom op forces `filter_expert=True` and reaches the non-TMA path where `expert_ids` is `topk_ids.view(-1)`. `topk_ids` is int64 (from `torch.topk`), and under torch.compile AOTAutograd realizes it at its true dtype, while the JIT activation kernel (`run_activation_filtered`) asserts `is_type<int32_t>(expert_ids)`. Eager avoids this path, so the crash only reproduces with `--enable-torch-compile`.

## Fix

Normalize `expert_ids` to int32 in `run_activation` before the filtered dispatch, instead of asserting downstream. No-op when the dtype is already int32 (the normal eager path).

## Validation

- Before: `--enable-torch-compile` on Unlimited-OCR dies in graph capture with the int32 assertion.
- After: server boots, all decode CUDA graphs capture, greedy output coherent.

## Note

Measured on RTX 5090, torch.compile gives no end-to-end gain for this model (SGL runtime torch.compile `579/1558/4176/6455` vs non-compile `594/1516/4061/6382` at bs 1/4/16/32) — the fix just removes the hard crash so the flag is usable.

title: [CI][NPU] Fix pr-test-npu failing at Install dependencies with set: Illegal option -o pipefail
author: cherryblo
body:
## Motivation

Since #37990 was merged (2026-09-05 12:58 UTC), **every** `pr-test-npu` run fails at the `Install dependencies` step about 1 minute in, and all remaining NPU jobs are cascade-skipped. Example: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33970347999/job/101318577758

```
/__w/_temp/xxx.sh: 1: set: Illegal option -o pipefail
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

## Root Cause

#37990 rewrote the `Install dependencies` step in `_npu-pr-test-stage.yml` to start with `set -euo pipefail` (plus `[[ ]]` conditionals), but did not declare `shell: bash` for that step.

The self-hosted k8s NPU runners execute steps without an explicit `shell:` as `sh -e` (dash on Ubuntu), which does not support `set -o pipefail` — so the script aborts on its very first line.

## Modification

Add `shell: bash` to the `Install dependencies` step, matching the existing convention of the `Run test` step in the same file.

Verified all other `run:` steps in this template either already declare `shell: bash` or contain no bash-only syntax, and `_npu-single-node-test-stage.yml` is unaffected.

title: [Unified Memory] fix: preserve FP8 dtype in unified MHA pool
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

`UnifiedMHATokenToKVPool` currently builds its parent `MHATokenToKVPool` with the MHA sub-pool storage dtype. For FP8 KV cache, the storage dtype is `torch.uint8`, while the logical KV dtype must remain FP8. Passing `uint8` as the parent dtype makes inherited read/write paths treat KV values as integers instead of FP8 values.

## Modifications

- Add `kv_cache_dtype` to `MHASubPoolSpec` so MHA unified sub-pools keep both logical KV dtype and storage dtype.
- Keep FP8 storage backed by `torch.uint8`, including `torch.float8_e4m3fnuz` on ROCm.
- Pass the logical dtype into `UnifiedMHATokenToKVPool` while preserving the existing uint8 backing views.
- Preserve the logical dtype on the composite `UnifiedSWAKVPool` and assert full/SWA logical dtype consistency.
- Add one focused CPU unit regression for the SWA factory path, which is the production path that previously passed uint8 as the logical dtype.

## Accuracy Tests

Not run locally. This change fixes dtype plumbing before attention kernels consume the pool; full model accuracy should be covered by CI/GPU E2E.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

title: Fix #38166: Restore non-layer placeholders before releasing host copies
author: yu-depend
body:
## Summary

When `finish_active_use` + `finish_request` trigger `park_non_layer_weights` twice, the second call may see enough device headroom to release the parked host copies. Without first restoring parameters still bound to `(1,)` placeholders, clearing the host copies leaves those weights as placeholder tensors.

This was observed with the MiniMax-H3 VAE, where `post_quant_conv.weight` could be left as a `(1,)` placeholder after decode, corrupting subsequent runs.

## Changes

- Call `restore_non_layer_weights()` before `_parked_non_layer_weights.clear()` in the early-return headroom branch of `park_non_layer_weights`.
- Add regression test `test_releasing_host_copies_restores_placeholders`.

PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_layerwise_offload.py::test_releasing_host_copies_restores_placeholders -xvs

title: fix: keep queued Mooncake linker loads after abort
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Summary

- Stop canceling queued Mooncake direct-linker loads after the unified cache wrapper has already published the restored tree node.
- Keep the pending Mooncake load so the normal layer-wise load path can fill the device slots and release the wrapper lock.
- Match the existing UMBP direct-linker behavior for this abort window.

## Why

`UnifiedCacheLinkerWrapper.load_back()` inserts/publishes the restored prefix into the tree before it queues the backend load. If the request aborts in that window, `release_request()` calls `cache_linker.cancel_queued_load(rid)`.

Mooncake previously popped the pending backend transfer and returned `True`, so the wrapper also dropped its pending load entry and released the lock. The published tree node can then remain visible as a device-cache hit even though its device slots were never populated by Mooncake.

## Reproduction

I set up an H200 rx devbox with Mooncake using `MooncakeTestServices`; RDMA initialization succeeded on `mlx5_0` and the Mooncake metadata/master/store services started successfully.

I also tried to run a service-level E2E with the external linker enabled:

- `Qwen3-4B` could not exercise this path because plain KV uses `_PlainKvStrategy`, which rejects the direct external linker.
- `AgainstEntropy/GLM-5.2-FP8-2L` is a DSA model and matches the supported direct-linker strategy, but the devbox cache only had config/index files, not weights; trying the HF model id also failed with repository 404.

The deterministic state-machine repro below uses the real `UnifiedCacheLinkerWrapper.release_request()` and `MooncakeDirectLinker.cancel_queued_load()` on the same devbox. It models the exact post-publish/pre-layer-load state: wrapper pending exists and Mooncake backend pending exists for the same request.

Before this fix:

```text
before wrapper_pending ['rid-1']
before backend_pending ['rid-1']
before dec_lock_calls []
after wrapper_pending []
after backend_pending []
after dec_lock_calls [(123, 'lock-token')]
```

After this fix:

```text
before wrapper_pending ['rid-1']
before backend_pending ['rid-1']
before dec_lock_calls []
after wrapper_pending ['rid-1']
after backend_pending ['rid-1']
after dec_lock_calls []
```

This confirms the unsafe state transition: the old Mooncake path drops the queued transfer after the tree node has already become visible. The patch keeps the transfer pending so the existing completion path can populate the slots and release the lock.

## Testing

- `python3 -m py_compile python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store/mooncake_direct_linker.py`
- `pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store/mooncake_direct_linker.py`

title: fix: collect prefix hash values iteratively
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Summary

- Collect prefix hash values iteratively instead of recursively appending lists.
- Apply the same helper fix to unified radix, legacy radix, and mamba radix nodes.

## Why

The previous implementation recursively walked parent nodes and used `parent_prefix + node.hash_value` at each level. On deep radix chains, this can hit Python's recursion limit; before that, repeated list concatenation copies the growing prefix repeatedly.

This keeps the same root-to-parent output order while making the walk iterative and copying each hash once.

title: [Fix] tracing: Fix OTel tracing context lost in multi-tokenizer router processes
author: enternal111
body:
﻿## Motivation

Fix #38210

With `--tokenizer-worker-num > 1`  `--detokenizer-worker-num > 1`, every request passes through the `MultiTokenizerRouter` (main server process) and scheduler outputs pass through the `MultiDetokenizerRouter` subprocess. Neither process ever calls `process_tracing_init`, so with the default full-pickle IPC the routers materialize request objects whose pickled `TraceReqContext` gets permanently disabled by `__setstate__` (no tracer provider initialized in that process; no exporter daemon either under `SGLANG_TRACE_ASYNC=1`). The scheduler then rebuilds a `TraceNullContext` and all scheduler-side spans (`prefill_waiting`, `prefill_forward`, `decode_forward` ... ) are silently dropped, only the HTTP-side spans survive.

## Modifications

- Call `process_tracing_init(...)` in `MultiTokenizerRouter.__init__` and `run_multi_detokenizer_router_process` when `--enable-trace` is set, guarded by `get_global_tracing_enabled()` so the call is idempotent. The routers create no spans of their own, so this only provides the tracer provider/exporter that the request-context round-trip needs.
- Add `TestTraceServerMultiTokenizer` to `test/registered/observability/test_tracing.py`: starts the server with `--tokenizer-worker-num 2 --detokenizer-worker-num 2` and asserts the level-3 spans, including `prefill_forward` / `decode_forward`.

## Accuracy Tests

No model output changes.

Manually verified with `--tokenizer-worker-num > 1`  and `--detokenizer-worker-num > 1` that scheduler-side spans (`prefill_forward`, `decode_forward` ... ) reach the OTLP collector again, both in standalone and PD-disaggregated deployments, with `SGLANG_TRACE_LEVEL=1` and `SGLANG_TRACE_ASYNC=1`.
## Speed Tests and Profiling

no performance impact (initialization only runs when `--enable-trace` is set; the routers create no spans).

title: fix: wait for HiCache load-back before hybrid MLA KV reads
author: LoCinder
body:
## Motivation

Attention forward must wait for the corresponding layer's HiCache load-back to complete before reading its KV data. `MLATokenToKVPool` already performs this wait before reading MLA KV data.

However, when used inside `HybridLinearKVPool`, this inner wait is disabled because the hybrid wrapper owns synchronization. `HybridLinearKVPool.get_mla_kv_buffer()` forwards the read without the required outer wait, allowing KV data to be read before asynchronous load-back completes.

## Modifications

- Wait for layer load-back before remapping the layer ID and reading MLA KV data.
- Add a CPU regression test verifying that the correct layer is waited on before the read.

## Tests

We ran an additional GPU correctness test on B300 using a two-layer FP8 MLA cache wrapped by `HybridLinearKVPool`, with 16K tokens and a page size of 64.

Random KV data was backed up to host memory, then the device buffers were cleared. We started asynchronous load-back and immediately called `get_mla_kv_buffer()` to read layer 0, then compared the returned data against the original data.

Across 20 trials:
- Before the fix: 20/20 reads returned incorrect data.
- After the fix: 0/20 reads returned incorrect data.

The PR also adds a CPU regression test that records the wait and read calls, checking that the hybrid wrapper waits for the correct layer before forwarding the read.

In end-to-end serving, Q and suffix KV projections typically run before cached-prefix reads, giving HiCache load-back more time to complete, so this bug may not surface consistently. Overall, our fix and the added test restore a robust correctness safeguard that already exists in `MLATokenToKVPool` but was missing from `HybridLinearKVPool`.

## Checklist

- [x] Formatting: pre-commit checks passed.
- [x] Unit tests: added focused regression coverage.
- [x] Documentation: N/A; no API or configuration changes.
- [x] Accuracy/speed benchmarks: N/A; this is a correctness fix with no steady-state performance impact expected.
- [x] Followed SGLang code style.

title: [diffusion] fix: stabilize H3 reference audio across repeated requests
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Identical MiniMax-H3 `ref2va` requests can produce different video and audio on the first and subsequent requests in the same server.

The audio encoder's scripted `snake` activation switches from its initial execution graph to a fused `TensorExprGroup` after profiling. The different floating-point rounding perturbs reference-audio conditioning, which joint audio/video denoising amplifies. The default Ref2VA synthetic warmup uses an image reference, so it does not warm this audio encoder path.

## Modifications

- Remove profiling TorchScript from the encoder activation without changing its formula or any global backend settings.
- Add a fresh-process CUDA regression test comparing the first call with repeated calls exactly, also checking that inputs and parameters remain unchanged. A fresh process prevents earlier tests from hiding the cold-call difference.
- Keep this independent of the sequential-request test harness in #38185. No diagnostic hooks, threshold changes, or new knobs.
- Refresh only the H100 Ref2VA frame GT after two independent CI runs produced byte-identical PNGs; keep the audio GT unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Remote H200 validation on `6c0f58b`: **10 tests passed**, pre-commit passed. The new regression test failed against the original implementation.

Real server comparison on **2x H200**, PyTorch **2.13.0+cu130**, Transformers **5.12.1**, checkpoint revision `42ed227ee7df40d41602854ae760620d6eb651fe`: Ref2VA, TP2, 4-second target, 8 requested steps, seed 42, the same video/audio reference, memory mode with DiT/text encoder layerwise offload and resident VAEs.

| Direct request-to-request comparison | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First/middle/last video-frame SSIM | 0.826824 / 0.801041 / 0.732987 | 1 / 1 / 1 |
| Reference-audio latent max absolute difference | 5.878508e-6 | 0 |
| Audio PCM max absolute difference | 0.184578 | 0 |
| Complete MP4 bytes | Different | Identical |

Stage dumps localized the first difference to reference-audio encoding; text embeddings, reference-video latents, and initial noise were identical. After the change, three diagnostic requests matched exactly. A separate two-request run **without diagnostic instrumentation** also produced identical complete MP4 files and audio PCM.

These e2e measurements used the same production patch before rebasing this standalone PR, with the request harness from #38185. They are not a claim that the final rebased head has passed full H100 CI.

The fixed H200 outputs did not match the previous H100 video GT's SSIM threshold (0.8918 vs 0.92); performance, peak-VRAM, and audio-GT checks passed in that H200 experiment. H200 outputs were not used to replace H100 GT.

### H100 CI Baseline

The [first H100 run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34040811875/job/101507227805) and [rerun](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34040811875/job/101513507507), both on source `6c0f58b`, produced **byte-identical first, middle, and last PNG frames**. Both reported SSIM 0.801429 against the old scripted-encoder GT. The checkpoint, sampling recipe, and thresholds were unchanged.

The three stable H100 frames are published in [ci-data-diffusion commit 285ffa7](https://github.com/sgl-project/ci-data-diffusion/commit/285ffa7fa7a8afcfb90e2344e3f9d6ca12a5e2ea), and this PR pins that revision. No other model's GT or consistency thresholds were changed.

On the final pin commit `e21f059`, **39 remote tests and pre-commit passed**. A remote smoke loaded all three frames and their CLIP embeddings through the pinned GT resolver with no local GT override; each downloaded PNG's Git blob hash matched the H100 CI artifact.

This confirms frame repeatability across independent server runs, not a new H100 same-session audio test: the old fixture stops after video consistency fails, and these artifacts contain no WAV. The existing audio GT remains unchanged; #38185 makes video/audio checks independent. The rerun also reported a separate Qwen-Image performance failure; its performance threshold is unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Uninstrumented real server runs, same configuration:

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Request 1 e2e | 65.7466 s | 65.7376 s |
| Request 2 e2e | 65.5186 s | 65.5613 s |
| Loading peak VRAM | 15,242 MiB | 15,242 MiB |
| Runtime peak VRAM | 34,560 MiB | 34,560 MiB |

No material e2e regression was observed in this workload; this is not a throughput benchmark or a guarantee for every configuration.

- [x] Add a regression test and verify it fails before the fix.
- [x] Provide remote accuracy and e2e performance measurements.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.
- Documentation: no public interface or configuration changes.

title: [diffusion] fix: quiet internal warmup frame searches
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary
Internal warmup frame searches repeatedly called the user-facing frame adjustment path. LongLive2 rounds sub-block candidates back to 29 frames, emitting both Wan and causal-frame warnings for each candidate and again for each spatial reduction.

- Add an optional `log_adjustment` argument to the frame contract and all built-in overrides; normal requests keep existing warnings.
- Keep candidate searches quiet and stop immediately when the halved target is below the model's minimum frame count.
- Replace the hand-written LongLive2 test contract with its real configuration, and cover quiet internal search, preserved user warnings, and the measured-workload probe floor.

The measured-workload floor already exists on main; this PR adds LongLive2 regression coverage rather than changing memory estimation or placement policy.

On a remote NVIDIA environment:
- 63 tests passed across warmup probe degradation, LongLive2 pipeline configuration, CFG-parallel warmup, and server warmup progress.
- pre-commit passed.

Full model generation was not rerun; no throughput or memory improvement is claimed. Out-of-tree configurations overriding `adjust_num_frames` should accept the optional keyword as well.

title: fix(inkling): translate unified-memory checkpoint destinations to physical slots
author: seokwoosong
body:
## Motivation

On the unified memory pool the scheduler hands out virtual Mamba slot ids, while the Inkling short-conv kernels write checkpoints to physical slots. #41144 fixed the main path by rewriting `forward_batch.mamba_track_indices` in place to a physical buffer. Two gaps remain:

- `commit_conv_state_after_mtp_verify` passes the scheduler's virtual `mamba_track_indices` to the verify scatter untranslated. DSPARK on the unified pool reaches it.
- The EAGLE draft-extend CUDA-graph runners do not pass checkpoint destinations. As a result, the captured graph writes the draft model's conv checkpoint into reserved slot 0 instead of the intended checkpoint slot, while eager draft extend writes to the correct slot. This PR makes the captured graph write to the intended checkpoint slot as well. This issue is not specific to unified memory.

The in-place rewrite also assumes one backend prepares each batch. When several do, as multi-layer EAGLE does with one draft backend per step, every backend after the first translates the already-physical ids again (`v2p[v2p[v]]`). Main currently rejects `--enable-unified-memory` with speculative algorithms other than DSPARK, so serving does not reach this today; keeping the batch virtual removes the hazard instead of relying on that restriction.

## Modifications

- `ForwardBatch.mamba_track_indices` stays virtual. `InklingShortConvAttnBackend` translates it into a fixed-address int64 buffer it owns and stores the physical ids in `InklingShortConvMetadata.track_cache_indices`. All Inkling checkpoint consumers (fused and unfused, decode, extend and draft extend) read that field. The static pool keeps the identity path. #41144's in-place rebind and its buffer are removed.
- `commit_conv_state_after_mtp_verify` translates the checkpoint destinations, as the GDN backend already does.
- Both EAGLE draft-extend runners allocate a checkpoint-destination buffer when `enable_mamba_extra_buffer` is set, pass it at capture, staging and replay, refresh live ids on replay and zero only the padded rows. The ordinary runner folds the refresh into its grouped copy. Helpers live in `speculative/draft_checkpoint.py`.
- Draft extend no longer runs the prefill-style track scatter. It writes its accepted-window checkpoint in its own cache update, and the inert prefill scatter would overwrite that destination during capture.
- GPU regression tests cover real allocator compaction, physical checkpoint writes, graph replay, repeated metadata preparation across backends, strided ids, padding, disabled tracking, buffer bounds and the verify commit.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated on an NVIDIA B200 against main `048b2a07f3`, with this PR rebased onto it; the end-to-end runs also include #39982 and #42072.

- `test_inkling_checkpoint_indices.py`: 17 tests and 29 subtests pass. The 33 related existing test files give the same results as main.
- The draft-extend checkpoint path is specifically covered by `test_draft_runners_capture_and_replay_checkpoint_destinations`, which checks checkpoint destinations during CUDA graph capture and replay.
- Inkling (`thinkingmachines/Inkling`, revision `test`), `--enable-deterministic-inference`, 32 LongBench prompts: logprob match, prefill cache hit and decode cache hit are at `avg_kl_div=0.0` on the static, lazy and unified pools, and multi-layer EAGLE MTP (two heads) on the static pool is at 0.0 as well. `test_inkling.py` passes 5/5 and `test_inkling_unified.py` 9/9.
- Inkling-Small NVFP4 + DSPARK, TP4, static pool: all three KL checks at 0.0.
- Unified pool + DSPARK: main allows only the triton attention backend for this pairing, and its prefill and decode are not bit-identical here (`avg_kl_div=0.116` with no cache hit, the same on main and with this PR), so the end-to-end KL check cannot isolate the verify-commit translation. The unit test above covers it.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Speculative accept length over the same workloads, read from the decode log (main / this PR):

| Setup | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Inkling MTP, multi-layer EAGLE, static pool | 2.736 | 2.736 |
| Inkling-Small NVFP4 + DSPARK, TP4, static pool | 2.118 | 2.118 |

Per step, the unified pool adds one translate and an int64 copy of at most `bs` entries; the ordinary draft-extend runner folds its refresh into the existing grouped copy, and the multi-layer runner adds one copy.

### Follow-up: shared-prefix checkpoint restoration

Compared the merge parent (`1e490772e5`) with the merged fix
(`1d02a36bb7`) on 12 varied inputs. Eight baseline cases had draft
acceptance below 100%.

| Shared-prefix result | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Aggregate draft acceptance | 72.67% (452/622) | 73.06% (453/620) |
| Aggregate completion tokens / verify calls | 768/311 (2.4695) | 768/310 (2.4774) |
| Proof case: verify calls for 64 output tokens | 30 | 29 |
| Proof case: draft acceptance | 55.00% | 58.62% |

The proof-case change reproduced in five additional cache-flush/reseed
repetitions per revision. Its cold control required 29 verify calls on
both revisions. All paired output token IDs matched between revisions.

<details>
<summary>Setup and limitations</summary>

RTX 5090 / WSL, reduced 8-layer Inkling test checkpoint, FA4, static
pools, extra_buffer, page/track interval 128, and two-head multi-layer
EAGLE with draft-extend CUDA graphs. Both revisions used the same
SM120 MoE compatibility override and diagnostic instrumentation.

Each seed generated 640 tokens. Follow-up requests reused a generated
768- or 896-token checkpoint with exactly one uncached input token.
Logs confirmed draft graph replay and checkpoint restore calls for
both draft pools.

The five proof-case repetitions were selected after the initial
comparison and were not independent server replicates.

Results were not uniformly positive: a separate 8-token continuation
experiment used 49 verify calls on both revisions, with accepted drafts
changing from 48/98 to 47/98. Two inputs had warm/cold output differences
identically on both revisions; their causes remain unestablished.

These results demonstrate a small, workload-specific acceptance
improvement, not a general throughput gain.

</details>

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [NPU] fix pp 2 hang on npu
author: liupeng374

When pp=2, both pp0 and pp1 may send data simultaneously: pp0->pp1 sends a proxy, and pp1->pp0 sends an output. This situation can cause the NPU to get stuck.

title: [qwen4-main-squashed] Cherry-pick #36811: avoid zero-bias allocation in fused softmax routing (fixes GB10 NEXTN collapse)
author: Jiminator
body:
Cherry-pick of #36811 (main commit 221a6273ce) onto `qwen4-main-squashed`. One trivial conflict resolved: this branch still had the `assert bias.dtype == torch.float32` line that #36811 deletes.

## Why

On DGX Spark (GB10) every NEXTN cell of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 built from this branch sporadically collapses to repeated `!` (NaN logits, #37111). Root cause: `fused_topk` passes a fresh `torch.zeros` bias to the Triton router kernel, which loads it before its PDL wait, so under programmatic dependent launch it can read the buffer's previous bytes; on GB10 the MTP draft leaves NaN there. An instrumented run captured the kernel consuming NaN bias before the wait, zeros after it, with correct logits. #36811 removes the zero-bias allocation for softmax routing, so there is no buffer left to read early.

## Validation (1x DGX Spark, RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4, NEXTN 3/1/4, radix cache off, 8 running requests, GSM8K 1319 + churn client, the shape that collapsed within 2 to 25 min in most runs on this branch tip)

With only this cherry-pick applied: 0.971 accuracy, 0 invalid, 1319/1319 stopped normally, 0 NaN events, 0 routing mismatches against a settled reference recomputed after the kernel. The unpatched branch collapsed twice in the same hours on the same shape.

The kernel-side hardening (wait before the bias load, Triton + radix) is proposed separately against main in #38290 and is not required for this branch's cells.

title: [AMD] Fix EAGLE crash when no kv_index_translator is bound on the DSA fp8 read door
author: jiaryang
body:
## Motivation

`_get_mla_kv_buffer_from_fp8_for_dsa` translates its read ids through the attention backend's `kv_index_translator` unconditionally:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py#L659

But only the FlashAttention and FlashInfer backends bind a translator. `BaseAttentionBackend` documents its `None` default as meaning "no translate":

```python
# The runner's KVIndexTranslator; backends that read through it set the
# instance attribute in __init__. None means "no translate" -- a backend
# that never set it cannot serve the unified pool, which the server-args
# allow-list enforces.
kv_index_translator = None
```

The DSA backend keeps that default. Under EAGLE the draft model runs on the DSA backend and reaches this door, so on gfx950 with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` every TP rank dies on the first request:

```
  File "python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha_rocm.py", line 211, in forward_normal_rocm_prepare
    kv_a, k_pe = self._get_mla_kv_buffer_from_fp8_for_dsa(forward_batch)
  File "python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py", line 659, in _get_mla_kv_buffer_from_fp8_for_dsa
    kv_indices = get_attn_backend().kv_index_translator.translate_dcp_read_ids(
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'translate_dcp_read_ids'
```

The server comes up fine and dies the moment the first request arrives, taking down all four ranks. A target-only (non-speculative) run has no draft model and never reaches this door, which is why the crash is specific to speculative decoding.

Repro (crashes on current `main`, serves normally with this PR):

```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --tp 4 --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --disable-radix-cache --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend triton --dsa-decode-backend triton \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1
```

## Modifications

Honor the documented contract at the read door: skip the translation when no translator is bound. With no translator the ids were never widened to VIRTUAL, so there is nothing to collapse. Behavior for the backends that do bind a translator is unchanged.

```python
translator = get_attn_backend().kv_index_translator
if translator is not None:
    kv_indices = translator.translate_dcp_read_ids(kv_indices)
```

One file, guard only, no functional change on any path that previously worked.

## Accuracy Tests

GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MI355X (gfx950), TP4, GSM8K, three runs. Before the fix the speculative server could not serve a single request, so there was no MTP result to compare against.

| | run 1 | run 2 | run 3 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EAGLE (this PR) | 0.941 | 0.932 | 0.927 |
| target-only, same build | 0.929 | 0.932 | 0.932 |

Speculative decoding lands in the same band as the target-only reference, as expected.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: the change adds a single `None` check and leaves every previously working path byte-for-byte identical.

- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [AMD][Fix] Fix regression in jit build error with FLUX.2-dev on gfx1250
author: sogalin
body:
## Motivation
FLUX.2-dev fails on gfx1250 as soon as denoising starts:
```
Failed to build JIT module sgl_kernel_jit_flux2_gated_resnorm
flux2_gated_resnorm.cuh:57:9: error: invalid output constraint '=&f' in asm
flux2_gated_resnorm.cuh:64:43: error: invalid output constraint '=f' in asm
amd_warp_sync_functions.h:297:62: error: static assertion failed due to requirement
    'sizeof(unsigned int) == 8': The mask must be a 64-bit integer.
3 errors generated when compiling for gfx1250.
```
The kernel added in #37112 is CUDA-only — it uses PTX inline asm with
float-register operand constraints and `__shfl_down_sync` with a 32-bit mask,
and AMDGPU has neither.
It gets selected because `_blackwell_or_newer()` only tests the device
capability. On ROCm that capability is derived from the gfx number, so gfx1250
reports `(12, 5)` and clears the `major >= 10` test, with
`torch.cuda.is_available()` already true under HIP.
Same class of issue as #34481, for a kernel added after it.
## Modifications
Require a CUDA build in `_blackwell_or_newer()`, matching the guard
`rope/qwen_qkv_epilogue_jit.py` already applies to the same capability test:
```python
 def _blackwell_or_newer(device: torch.device) -> bool:
     return (
-        torch.cuda.is_available() and torch.cuda.get_device_capability(device)[0] >= 10
+        torch.version.cuda is not None
+        and torch.cuda.is_available()
+        and torch.cuda.get_device_capability(device)[0] >= 10
     )
```
Both entry points, `can_defer_flux2_gated_residual()` and
`can_use_flux2_gated_resnorm()`, route through the guard, so ROCm now takes the
`residual_gate_add` + eager norm path for both. CUDA is unaffected.
## Accuracy Tests
ROCm falls back to the same unfused path it used before #37112, so there is no
new numerical behavior to validate on either platform.

title: fix(qsa): clamp the compress gather to the rows this forward has
author: ehuaa
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Related to the IMA error described in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/37633.
In the indexer every group spans`compress_ratio` rows, so a padded entry gathers rows `0..ratio-1` of `token_k`.
A forward that carries fewer than `compress_ratio(4)` token rows — the 1..3 token chunk that ends a request under chunked prefill — therefore reads past `token_k`.
The read almost always lands in neighbouring allocated memory and is absorbed silently, it faults only when it happens to cross an unmapped page.


## Modifications
Clamp the gather row index to the rows this forward actually has:

```python
group_locs = group_locs.clamp_max(source_keys.shape[0] - 1)
```

This is exact rather than a mask over the symptom: padded entries write the
reserved slot 0 and their gathered values are discarded, and real entries are
provably in range, so the clamp cannot change any real computation.

title: fix(npu): fix hybrid KV transfer with PP prefill in PD disaggregation
author: JinyanYi

## Summary

title: [Fix] Wait for PDL before reading DeepSeek V4 K cache locations
author: aurickq
body:
## Motivation

The fused DeepSeek V4 K normalization/RoPE kernel reads `out_loc` before `PDLWaitPrimary`. Cache locations can be produced immediately before this kernel: [`get_swa_out_cache_loc`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/5aab054ec8ce6b6100fbfb7aafe67d632a7df3aa/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend.py#L1633-L1654) falls back to gathering the SWA mapping and converting it to int32, and its result is passed directly to the fused cache-store call.

[CUDA's PDL contract](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/04-special-topics/programmatic-dependent-launch.html#api-description) requires the dependency wait before consuming the preceding kernel's results, including when the producer uses an implicit launch trigger. Reading `out_loc` before that wait can select a stale cache slot.

## Modifications

Move only the `out_loc` load after the existing wait. Preserve the early position load and frequency-pointer calculation, retaining their prefetch overlap and the existing assumption that positions are already prepared.

```diff
   const auto position = static_cast<int32_t>(static_cast<const PosT*>(params.positions)[work_id]);
-  const auto out_loc = params.out_loc[work_id];
   const auto freqs_cis = params.freqs_cis + position * kRopeDim;

   PDLWaitPrimary<kUsePDL>();
+  const auto out_loc = params.out_loc[work_id];
```

## Accuracy Tests

Standalone GPU validation on GB300 with CUDA 13.2 (`sm_103a`): **320/320 trials passed**, covering 20/128/512/2048 rows, int32/int64 positions, stream/CUDA-graph launches, and PDL enabled/disabled. Positions were precomputed; an ordinary preceding kernel freshly converted valid cache locations from int64 to int32. Full cache output bytes matched the reference with prepared metadata and PDL disabled.

This checks ordinary producer-to-consumer execution, not a failing-before/passing-after reproduction of the ordering bug. All applicable pre-commit hooks passed. No test or documentation files are added.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Standalone CUDA-graph benchmark on GB300, with fully initialized immutable inputs and 128 invocations per chain. Median paired change across four interleaved rounds versus the unmodified kernel:

| Rows | Change in time per invocation |
| ---: | ---: |
| 20 | +0.11% |
| 128 | +1.73% |
| 512 | +1.69% |
| 2048 | +0.04% |
| 8192 | -0.02% |

The largest median increase was approximately 24 ns. These measure steady-state kernel-chain time, not end-to-end serving throughput or overlap with a cache-location producer.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [ ] Add unit tests.
- [x] Documentation: no interface or usage changes to document.
- [x] Provide runtime accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

title: Fix DSA compression tail capacity for PD decode request slots
author: HanHan009527
body:
## Motivation

GLM-5.3-Flash's NextN draft shares the target's hybrid request pool. PD decode adds preallocation slots beyond `max_running_requests`, but the plain DSA builder uses that running limit to size compression tails indexed by `req_pool_idx`.

With 32 running requests and 64 extra slots, slot 96 is valid but the tail has only 33 rows:

```text
index 96 is out of bounds for dimension 0 with size 33
```

**The same model's [target hybrid branch](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/f8f03910f20329cb4f920ec8685eaa9f7eda81fc/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_configurator.py#L1833) already sizes tails from the actual request table.** The plain draft branch missed this distinction. Graph replay also preserves these request IDs.

## Modifications

- At the plain DSA builder call site, pass `req_to_token_pool.req_to_token.shape[0]` as `max_running_requests`, matching the target hybrid branch. Keep the existing parameter name, function signature and constructor `+1`; the scheduler's running limit stays unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

The results below were collected at `7f66f7e5af` with `shape[0] - 1`. This revision aligns with the target hybrid branch by using `shape[0]`, allocating one additional row; runtime tests were not rerun. No new UT is included.

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| CPU/CUDA capacity check (prior revision) | Old capacity: `assert torch.Size([33, 6, 128]) == (97, 6, 128)`; 4 failures | **16/16 pass** |
| Real PD requests | Earlier eager run: `torch._dynamo.exc.InternalTorchDynamoError: AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` | **130/130 pass** |

The regression uses a controlled restoration of the old capacity. Serving used TileLang/BF16, TP8/EP8, EAGLE 1/1/2, Prefill eager and Decode full Graph. Prefill draft Graph still has the separate width issue in #37573. No model-quality benchmark was run.

title: [AMD] Fix DeepSeek block-FP8 loading on gfx94x
author: bingxche
body: ## Motivation On MI300/MI325, SGLang converts checkpoint FP8 weights to the FP8 form used by the GPU. That conversion creates a new scale tensor and drops the small label that says whether the scale holds normal numbers or raw UE8M0 bytes. Later code reads the missing label and crashes before DeepSeek can start. Seen in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34070685413/job/101587367851 . ## Modifications - Remember whether the original scale contains raw UE8M0 bytes before conversion. - Keep the existing conversion unchanged for normal block-FP8 scales. - Do not treat raw UE8M0 bytes as normal numbers; let the existing requantization handle them. This keeps non-FNUZ paths unchanged and preserves the UE8M0 support added in #36805. ## Accuracy Tests - [Targeted ROCm 7.2.4 / MI300 8-GPU CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34200061802) ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable; this is a load-time condition fix. ## Checklist - [x] Code is formatted. - [x] Documentation is not needed for this internal loader fix. - [x] Accuracy validation is listed above. - [x] The change follows the existing code style. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #34242452181](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34242452181) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #34242451829](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34242451829) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #34242452279](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34242452279)

body:
## Motivation

HiCache can corrupt a value being written to L3 storage when a radix-tree node is split while its write-back SET is still in flight.
The SET reads directly from host KV-cache blocks. A split creates a new prefix node for the shared tokens, but that fragment does not inherit the parent's full host lock. Duplicate-host reclamation may therefore free and reuse the prefix blocks before the storage backend has finished reading them, this causes **wrong data to be written to storage**. The backend behaves correctly: it stores exactly what is in those buffers when its SET runs. The stale write is caused by SGLang changing ownership of the buffers too early.

## Modifications

* Propagate a full host lock from the original node to the prefix fragment created by a split.
* When the asynchronous SET finishes, release the lock across every fragment created after the SET began, stopping at the recorded pre-split parent. 
* Require the acquisition result when releasing a host lock. Without its pre-split boundary, a parameterless release could unlock only the original child and permanently leak the copied prefix lock.
* Apply the same ownership rule to the Python and Rust unified radix-tree implementations.

This keeps every zero-copy SET source block owned by the SET until the backend call has returned, even if the radix node is split in the meantime.


## Accuracy Tests

I tested this with both unit tests (in this PR) an [end2end reproducer (not in this PR)](https://github.com/lluki/sglang/blob/751ee8dd1656f365ba555267fd706dc054ef3d97/scripts/repro_hicache_nixl_stale_set_frontend.py). 

The e2e verifier runs SGLang with hicache nixl backend and slows down the `batch_set_*` artificially to reliably trigger the bug:
* Send an 832-token victim prompt whose deterministic answer is ZEBRA4821.
* Send a 3500-token unrelated prompt. This evicts the victim to host and starts its delayed POSIX SET.
* Send a prompt that shares the first 704 victim tokens and then diverges.
* This splits the host-backed node while its SET is in flight.
* Send a 3000-token unrelated prompt to create host pressure. On buggy code, the split prefix is reclaimed and its host blocks are reused.
* Wait for the SET, flush the memory tiers, and send the original victim completion request again so it must be loaded from POSIX storage.

The second request reports a 768-token storage hit, proving that it exercised L3. On buggy upstream code its answer changes from ZEBRA4821 to repeated Answer: tokens. This is visible entirely through the completion API.

I ran this validation and testsuite with both python and rust cores.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.

title: [HiCache] Yield idle scheduler so storage workers can drain
author: alphabetc1
body:
Completed buffer-only HiCache requests can leave file-store backups draining so slowly that `/flush_cache?timeout=30` returns HTTP 400; a subsequent 60-second flush also times out. This reproduces with both Python and Rust TreeCore on main (`554f817948`), independently of #37584.

When there is no GPU batch but storage work remains, `Scheduler.on_idle()` immediately returns into a tight polling loop. File backup workers need to reacquire the GIL between I/O calls and can be starved by that loop. Native stacks show the scheduler holding the GIL while backup workers wait inside `numpy.tofile` / `os.replace`. In a same-process diagnostic experiment, enabling a scheduler yield drained the backlog within about one second without restarting or changing the queue.

Yield with `time.sleep(0)` on the not-fully-idle path when HiCache storage is enabled. The shared scheduler covers both TreeCore backends; no separate Rust implementation change is needed. The full-idle guard and flush timeout remain intact.

Update the existing scheduler unit-test fixture for the storage flag. Validation used a standalone GPU/file-store script with both backends and two groups of four 40,960-token requests. The script is not added to the regular CI suite.

Validation on one H200 with GPT-OSS-20B, page size 64, chunk size 16,384, buffer-only/write-through/file storage:

| Source / TreeCore | Before: first post-request flush | After: two post-request flushes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main / Rust | 30 s timeout | 1.521 s / 1.536 s |
| main / Python | 30 s timeout | 1.728 s / 1.770 s |
| #37584 / Rust | 30 s timeout | 1.635 s / 1.643 s |
| #37584 / Python | 30 s timeout | 1.632 s / 1.627 s |

Across all four comparisons, generated text, output-token logprobs, and cache hits match before/after for the first four requests. Measurements above use the diagnostic reproduction harness; the standalone regression was also run without diagnostic patches or signals.

- Scheduler idle-load and flush unit suites: 9 passed.
- Pre-commit checks passed.
- Uninstrumented standalone GPU regression: both backend subtests fail on unpatched main with `Timed out waiting for idle state`; both pass with the scheduler fix.

title: [Fix] sampling: deterministic top-p / top-k renorm when tp_size > 1 (TP rank divergence in DFlash/DSpark)
author: gilfordting
body:
## Summary

flashinfer's default top-p / top-k renorm kernels are non-deterministic (float `atomicAdd`); because of this, TP ranks that renormalize the same logits can produce different results. Every consumer of this output (plain sampler, spec-verify) samples against a deterministic coin and commits the result to per-rank KV/radix state. A coin that lands in between the cross-rank gap causes divergence across ranks, and NCCL collectives hang.

Previous PRs (#33549, #33289; #33614) work around this issue by broadcasting rank 0's decision. This PR addresses the root cause and avoids an extra collective, by routing the renorm through flashinfer's `is_deterministic=True` variants. This is turned on where it matters:

| configuration                         | renorm kernels  | why                                                            |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| single rank                           | fast            | nothing to agree with                                          |
| `attn_tp_size > 1`                    | deterministic   | each rank computes the same result; bit-identical across ranks |
| `--enable-deterministic-inference`    | deterministic   | self-explanatory                                               |
| `SGLANG_RENORM_DETERMINISTIC=1` / `0` | forced on / off | explicit override                                              |

Repro + results are below. With all relevant broadcasts turned off, the fast kernels reproduce the hang on H100 and B200 in every run. The deterministic kernels never diverge, and the end-to-end cost to TPOT is marginal.

## Root cause

- `sgl_kernel.top_p_renorm_prob` and `top_k_renorm_prob` forward to flashinfer.
    - Top-p on rows longer than 2048 uses the AIR radix kernel (>= 0.6.7, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#2752) whose default histogram is a float atomic.
    - Top-k (`RadixTopKRenormProbMultiCTA`) pools the kept mass with a float atomic.
    - flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4831 (0.7.x, sglang pins 0.7.2) added a fixed-point `is_deterministic=True` at unchanged latency.
- In non-greedy verification, each rank compares its own `target_probs` (top-p/top-k output) against a shared coin and samples the bonus token from `relu(q - p)`.
    - If ranks differ slightly, the coin might cross the acceptance or bonus thresholds on some ranks and not others; this will cause KV state to drift and a later prefix match will cause NCCL collectives to hang.
- The sampler's `min_p` path calls the same kernels with no broadcast (`SGLANG_SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP` is off by default).
- Earlier synthetic repros were clean because they used `top_p=1.0`, which skips the kernel entirely.

## Repro

**Setup**

- Image: current main (nightly `ed8c3139`, flashinfer 0.7.1, sgl_kernel 0.4.10) with this PR applied.
- Model, config, workload: TP=2 DFlash, Llama-3.1-8B + `z-lab/LLaMA3.1-8B-Instruct-DFlash-UltraChat`, `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.9`, 32 concurrent multi-turn streams, fp8 KV.
- Broadcast collectives off:
    - Hard-coded broadcast is only on for the EAGLE path. We use DFlash.
    - `SGLANG_SPEC_TP_SYNC=off` turns off #33614's broadcasts.
    - `SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP`, `SGLANG_SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP` are off by default.
- Deterministic renorm kernels on using a new environment variable, `SGLANG_RENORM_DETERMINISTIC=1`.
- A probe all-gathers per-verify-step fingerprints of `{rng state, prefix_lens, draft_tokens, target_logits, target_probs, accept_len, bonus, commit_lens, out_tokens}` and reports the first field that differs.
    - It also calls `top_p_renorm_prob` twice on the same input on one rank, counting mismatches after.

**Results**

"knob" below refers to the new env-var, `SGLANG_RENORM_DETERMINISTIC=1`.
| broadcast | renorm | runs | requests per run | first cross-rank `target_probs` difference | rank-local mismatches (top-p calls) | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| off | fast (knob=0, same kernels as main) | 4 x H100, 2 x B200 | 1.4k to 6.5k | 1 to 22 s | 0.4 to 0.9 % | **all 6 hung**, at 190 to 610 s |
| off | deterministic (knob=1) | 3 x H100, 2 x B200 | 22.6k to 35.4k | never | 0 of 276,000 | all 5 clean, full 30 min |
| all (#33614) | fast (knob=0) | 1 x H100 | 25.2k | 14 s | 0.9 % | clean: 436 `target_probs` divergences, none reaches a token |
| all (#33614) | deterministic (knob=1) | 1 x H100 | 24.4k | never | 0 of 46,000 | clean, 0 divergences |

Every fast-kernel run with the broadcast off hung, with the same recorded chain each time:

- `target_probs` differs between ranks while logits, `prefix_lens` and RNG are identical.
- `bonus` / `out_tokens` differ on one rank.
- Next step's `draft_tokens` differ.
- Hang.

Toggling only the knob to 1 on the same image, model, load and probe consistently results in zero divergences, zero rank-local mismatches, and no hang.

## Kernel measurements

We perform 99 repeated calls on byte-identical input. Settings: flashinfer 0.7.1, vocab 128256, H100. B200 and B300 give the same results.

`nondet` refers to calls that differ from call 0.

| rows | input distribution | kernel | current default        | `is_deterministic=True` |
| ---- | ------------------ | ------ | ---------------------- | ----------------------- |
| 32   | flat               | top-p  | 0.136 ms, nondet 99/99 | 0.169 ms, 0/99          |
| 32   | peaky              | top-p  | 0.127 ms, 0/99         | 0.149 ms, 0/99          |
| 32   | flat               | top-k  | 0.042 ms, 99/99        | 0.042 ms, 0/99          |
| 32   | peaky              | top-k  | 0.042 ms, 77/99        | 0.042 ms, 0/99          |
| 256  | flat               | top-p  | 0.603 ms, 98/99        | 0.815 ms, 0/99          |
| 256  | flat               | top-k  | 0.288 ms, 99/99        | 0.289 ms, 0/99          |

We observe the following:

- Top-k performs near-identical between both fast and deterministic arms.
- Top-p adds 20 to 45% to a 0.1 to 0.8 ms kernel. We measure how much this matters in the next section.
- The deterministic wrapper adds no host sync and no `cudaMalloc`, so there is no overhead.

## End-to-end speed

**Setup**

- Workload: `sglang.bench_serving`, random 512-in / 256-out, 400 prompts, concurrency 32.
- Model, config: Llama-3.1-8B, fp8 KV, triton attention, H100.
- One container boots four servers in sequence with the knob 1 / 0 / 1 / 0, two trials each, so both arms share a host and an image.
- We look at TPOT, since this code change is exercised during decode. The first trial (warmup) is dropped, and we calculate mean TPOT. We see that differences are on the order of 0.01 ms.

| config                                                                           | knob=1   | knob=0   | delta  | accept len    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------- | ------ | ------------- |
| plain TP2 `min_p=0.05` (the path the default policy makes deterministic), host A | 4.974 ms | 4.976 ms | -0.0 % |               |
| same, host B, order 0 / 1 / 0 / 1                                                | 5.058 ms | 5.062 ms | -0.1 % |               |
| plain TP1 `min_p=0.05`                                                           | 8.065 ms | 8.067 ms | -0.0 % |               |
| DFlash TP2 `top_p=0.9` (knob=1 forces the verify path deterministic too)         | 3.992 ms | 3.983 ms | +0.2 % | 4.563 / 4.564 |
| EAGLE3 TP2 `top_p=0.9`                                                           | 7.191 ms | 7.175 ms | +0.2 % | 1.929 / 1.930 |

Thus, we see that there is no measureable end-to-end cost, including the forced-deterministic verify path; the accept length is also unchanged.

The renorm kernel runs once per step over `batch_size` rows (sampler) or `batch_size x draft_tokens` rows (verify), so deterministic top-p adds ~0.03 ms at 32 rows and ~0.2 ms at 256 rows, which is small compared to a step of several ms.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/sampling_renorm.py` (new):
    - `renorm_deterministic(ranks_agree)` policy.
    - `top_p_renorm_prob` / `top_k_renorm_prob` for the sampler and `spec_top_p_renorm_prob` / `spec_top_k_renorm_prob` for verify, calling flashinfer with `is_deterministic=True` when appropriate (`sgl_kernel` as before otherwise).
    - The flag's presence is checked once at import (`inspect.signature`), so an older flashinfer degrades to the fast kernel rather than failing on the first sampled request.
    - Without flashinfer (MUSA, XPU) `sgl_kernel`'s own single-CTA kernel is already deterministic; no int32-sensitive code is added there.
- `layers/sampler.py`, `speculative/dflash_utils.py`, `speculative/eagle_utils.py` are the only renorm call sites, and now they import from the module above.
    - The `_sync_token_ids_across_tp` and `spec_tp_sync.py` comments name the renorm kernels as a known source of nondeterminism and point at the knob.
- `environ.py`: `SGLANG_RENORM_DETERMINISTIC` next to the other determinism knobs.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/sampling/test_renorm.py`: existing correctness tests run through the new module; regression tests call each deterministic renorm 30 times on a flat 256 x 128256 input and assert bit-identical output (the default kernels fail this 30 of 30); scoped runtime-context fixture.
- `test/registered/unit/sampling/test_renorm_policy.py` (CPU): single rank fast; TP=2 sampler deterministic and verify fast; `--enable-deterministic-inference` forces on; env overrides both ways.

The fix lives in `sglang` rather than the `sgl_kernel` wrappers, because `sglang-kernel` ships as a pinned prebuilt wheel. A wrapper change there is not testable in CI, and is not delivered until the next kernel release.

This fix is Complementary to #33614: the broadcast keeps replicated state safe against any future non-deterministic operator. This removes the one we found, so rank 0's own output and every other consumer of `target_probs` (logprobs, sampling masks) become reproducible too.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: Fix KV-canary workspace accounting after graph capture
author: cctry
body:
## Motivation

Eager KV-canary forwards allocate plans after post-capture KV sizing has assigned the available memory to the KV pool. On large pools, this unaccounted workspace can approach a gigabyte and cause an otherwise memory-tight configuration to OOM.

## Modifications

Compute the workspace from the installed `VerifyPlan`, `WritePlan`, `ExpectedInputs`, and `PlanInput` capacities, and subtract it in addition to the existing headroom. Target and draft forwards execute sequentially, so reserve their largest workspace. Canary-disabled configurations retain exactly the same byte budget.

Canary capacities remain fixed across post-capture resizing. The reserve uses those actual capacities, including the three verify entries per pool slot.

Add regression coverage for allocation byte counts, pool-slot scaling, additive headroom, canary-disabled budgets, and draft-runner forwarding.

## Accuracy Tests

- Sizing, headroom, startup, and capacity tests: **82 passed, 50 subtests passed**.
- Canary unit and kernel tests on GB300: **390 passed, 23 subtests passed**.
- Canary mock tests: **9 passed**; E2E helper tests: **2 passed**.
- Final startup-forwarding test rerun: **22 passed, 18 subtests passed**.
- `python -m pytest -q test/registered/mem_cache/test_post_capture_kv_sizing.py`: **3 passed** in 178.97 s, including the GSM8K accuracy check. Post-capture sizing backed a 230.25 GiB KV pool.
- `SGLANG_ENABLE_POST_CAPTURE_KV_SIZING=1 python -m pytest -q test/registered/kv_canary/test_self_e2e_baseline.py::TestBaselineMha`: **1 passed** in 193.80 s.
- `pre-commit run`: passed.

Server tests used a separate environment with the upstream PyTorch 2.13 and kernel dependencies. No multi-GPU, SWA, speculative, or disaggregated serving validation was run.

title: [metrics] Fix non-streaming TTFT by flushing the first output through detokenization
author: chromecast56
body:
Related metrics PRs: #39706, #40275. Each is independent and they can merge in any order.

## Motivation

Non-streaming requests only flush output to the tokenizer every `SGLANG_FORCE_STREAM_INTERVAL` (50) tokens, so `first_token_time` is stamped at token 50 or at completion. Non-streaming TTFT therefore includes most of the decode time.

## Modifications

- `output_streamer.py`: flush a non-streaming request's first output through detokenization as soon as it exists; later outputs keep the regular interval. The first output can carry several tokens (PD decode, a deferred stop-prefix flush), so the check keys on `send_token_offset`. The first flush is held while a stop-string prefix is pending, when a stop regex is set (a partial regex match can't be detected, and flushing early leaked the matched prefix into the final text), and for beam candidates.
- `environ.py`: the `SGLANG_FORCE_STREAM_INTERVAL` comment now says the interval only batches outputs after the first.
- `production_metrics.mdx`: two sentences defining TTFT and the non-streaming caveat.

Side effects for non-streaming requests:
- `sglang:time_to_first_token_seconds` drops to the real first-output time, so non-streaming TTFT dashboards will show a drop.
- `sglang:inter_token_latency_seconds` now counts tokens 2..50, which used to be folded into TTFT.
- `meta_info.first_token_latency`, `meta_info.decode_throughput`, and the OTel latency spans move the same way.
- A request that finishes before the stream interval now sends one extra scheduler-to-detokenizer message.

## Tests

`test/registered/unit/managers/test_output_streamer_customized_info.py::TestFirstTokenFlush`, 5 methods:
- multi-token first output flushes immediately (1, 8, 49 tokens with interval 50);
- later outputs keep batching and never duplicate tokens;
- the first output waits for a pending stop-string prefix to clear;
- a stop-regex request holds its first output (fails without the stop-regex check, which let the matched prefix leak into the final text);
- finished requests flush despite a stop prefix, and beam candidates don't flush early.

title: fix(openai): recover logprobs token bytes from token_id (UTF-8 fragments)
author: mindlab-bot
body: ## Problem Byte-level BPE splits characters absent from the vocab (rare CJK extension-B, some combining sequences) into **single-byte fragment tokens** — e.g. `𠮷` (U+20BB7) becomes `[F0] [A0] [AE] [B7]`, each a distinct vocab token. The engine always keeps the real token id in every `(logprob, token_id, token_text)` triple. But the OpenAI serving layer rebuilt `logprobs.content[].bytes` with `token.encode("utf-8")` on the **detokenized display string**. A lone byte has no valid UTF-8 text form, so each fragment decodes to `\ufffd`, yielding `[239,191,189]` (the U+FFFD encoding) **instead of the real fragment bytes** `[240]/[160]/[174]/[183]`. ``` expected: bytes = [240], [160], [174], [183] <- the engine's real fragment bytes actual: bytes = [239,191,189] x4 <- '\ufffd' UTF-8 encoding ``` Complete tokens are unaffected (` 中文` -> `[32,228,184,173,230,150,135]`, `🙂` -> `[240,159,153,130]`), since those are in the vocab and decode cleanly. ## Root cause `bytes` is byte-level information and must be recovered from the **token id**, never from the detokenized display text. The text channel is inherently lossy for fragments — a lone byte has no legal UTF-8 text form, so *any* tokenizer (tiktoken included) decodes it to `\ufffd`. Recovering bytes from that text is what corrupts fragments. ## Fix Recover the bytes through the GPT-2 `bytes_to_unicode` inverse table. - **utils.py**: add `_BYTE_DECODER`/`_build_byte_decoder()` and `token_id_to_bytes()`, which maps a token id back to its raw bytes. Add `_lossless_token_text()` so the legacy completions string channel (no per-token `bytes` field) renders fragments losslessly as latin-1 (one char per byte, reversible). `to_openai_style_logprobs` now accepts a `tokenizer`. - **serving_chat.py**: new `_build_token_logprobs_from_raw()` consumes the engine's `(logprob, token_id, token_text)` triples directly (incl. `top_logprobs`). Both non-streaming `_process_response_logprobs` and streaming `_process_streaming_logprobs` route through it. Removed the text-based `_process_logprobs_tokens` and now-unused imports. - **serving_completions.py**: pass `tokenizer` to both `to_openai_style_logprobs` call sites. ## Verification - `𠮷`'s four fragments recover to `[240], [160], [174], [183]` (previously `[239,191,189]` x4). - The decoder table is the exact inverse of GPT-2 `bytes_to_unicode` over all 256 bytes. - Complete tokens round-trip unchanged (` 中文`, `🙂`, `\n`, `hello`). - Unknown / non-byte-level / raising tokenizers fall back to the display text (no panic). - `py_compile` and `ruff check --select F401,F811,F821` pass on all three files. --- ✨ Presented to you with Mind Lab — A Lab for Experiential Intelligence. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #35388226038](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35388226038) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #35388225669](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35388225669) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #35388226162](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35388226162)

title: [Fix] MiniMax H3: honor requested inference step count
author: bookinstock
body:
`minimax_h3_time_shift_sigmas(num_steps=N)` currently returns `N` sigma points, but the H3 denoise loop executes `len(sigmas) - 1` transitions. A 1-step request therefore fails admission, and every larger request performs one fewer denoise update than requested.

title: [Fix] observability: Correct speculative FPM timing and decode lengths
author: tedzhouhk
body:
## Summary

Fix speculative-decoding FPM timing ownership and decode-length statistics. Each result retains its own timing span and immutable count/sum/variance instead of combining overlapped iterations or reading a missing/stale CPU length mirror. Attention-DP ranks with no local requests retain their timed dummy-forward records. Idle heartbeats now follow scheduler state, so a long forward cannot look idle merely because the publisher queue is quiet.

## Implementation

DeviceTimer exposes generic interval observers. FPM timing, schemas and publication live in `forward_pass_metrics.py`; all corresponding test cases and fixtures live in `test_forward_pass_metrics.py`, with one CPU CI registration. The DeviceTimer dependency is imported only for type checking. FPM groups existing intervals by run_batch result, preserves the same-stream check, and carries timing through rank-local PP metadata, including PREBUILT recursion, skipped output communication and the speculative-output relay. PP metadata retains both the upstream forward-time microbatch/KV snapshot and rank-local FPM timing. At _resolve_spec_v2_tokens entry, after existing result-copy synchronization and before settlement, supported EAGLE/EAGLE3/DSPARK paths freeze req.seqlen - 1 statistics on the result. Queued statistics remain a per-rank scheduler-queue snapshot and stay immutable during deferred publication.

Remove unused start/end-event fields and the unreachable monotonic fallback, inline the extra timing context manager with exception-safe sealing, remove duplicate emission-time polling, and skip per-interval elapsed-time calculations when there are no reporters. Algorithm selection is a module-level constant; shared test fixtures replace duplicate fake intervals. Full PP round-trip and skip-output regression coverage remains.

## Overhead

Production adds no CUDA events, GPU kernels, D2H transfers or explicit synchronization. FPM-off keeps the original forward method and skips decode-statistics reduction. FPM-on performs CPU bookkeeping, stream checks, statistics reduction and asynchronous publication. wall_time is the first-start/last-end span of existing instrumented intervals on one stream, including segment gaps; work outside those boundaries is excluded. The FPM v1 wire schema is unchanged. These structural checks do not quantify CPU overhead; the earlier AgentX comparisons remain in the performance-evidence comment.

## Validation

- 98 CPU tests across eight focused files passed at head `8d8616abd2778ab2c9341fbc55d664ced38449d9`, including FPM timing/publication, speculative grammar/bookkeeping, auxiliary output, PP rank offsets/DSpark relay, PP communication overlap and scheduler metrics. CPU tests stub optional compiled operators. Changed-file pre-commit and git diff --check passed. The timing regression now uses real interval completion caching and confirms active-state sampling does not consume or duplicate FPM callbacks. AST comparison confirms `forward_pass_metrics.py` (wire schema, span aggregation and publisher) matches pre-merge head `09a6cba18ec20bf4ecd621b7b8c5fc66fc7dbd37`.
- Computelab job 4285576 used two A100-SXM4-80GB GPUs, driver `595.58.03`, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`, `sglang-kernel==0.4.7`, and matching FlashInfer Python/cubin/JIT-cache `0.6.18` packages. The container base was amd64 digest sha256:f856a45537f82e1900ea7607edcbaa7f77fbb2e70220eae522d1d50d0046727e; full PR Python source was overlaid, and changed production-file hashes matched `9babf79d21a412f56d1a9a958d764d58dcc3464e`.
- EAGLE3 uses Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B at c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca and Nicolassuez/Qwen3-0.6B-eagle3 at `00b7c41f32655e90ee65ac5b90bb381905ce1700`. Native MTP uses Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B at `2fc06364715b967f1860aea9cf38778875588b17`.

| GPU case | Forward FPM records | Dummy records | GPU length samples | Nonempty queue checks |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| EAGLE3 / TP1 / graphs | 700 | 0 | 687 | 639 |
| EAGLE3 / attention DP2 / graphs | 2334 | 758 | 2776 | 1284 |
| EAGLE3 / attention DP2 / eager + 1.2s delay | 52 | 26 | 34 | 0 |
| No SD / attention DP2 / graphs | 3592 | 1202 | 0 | 1998 |
| Native MTP / TP1 / eager | 359 | 0 | 346 | 331 |
| EAGLE3 / attention DP2 / forced retraction | 4144 | 1311 | 2772 | 2521 |

All six cases passed. SD count/sum/population-variance matched an independent GPU-length oracle. Independently associated timing intervals matched emitted spans, bounded by separate run_batch events. Every dummy record had no scheduled requests and positive timing matching its own GPU events. Raw streams matched oracle records with no counter gaps or skipped scheduler-forward ordinals in these runs.

Asymmetric and simultaneous routed request bursts checked each rank's actual waiting queue and request ownership. The forced-retraction case additionally checked 525/521 queued-decode snapshots on ranks 0/1. Scheduler-driven idle heartbeat checks found no busy-period violations, including repeated 1.2-second forward delays; receipt-time checks exclude 100 ms around state transitions for IPC delivery latency, complemented by deterministic publisher-state unit tests.

GPU oracles add validation-only events, D2H, synchronization and logging outside the production patch; these are correctness runs. GPU coverage is aggregated PP1 with TP1 / attention DP2; PP and unsupported SD algorithms retain their stated validation boundaries. Initial environment/coverage setup attempts are excluded from the six-case matrix and retained in the experiment records.

Merged main `efb62ce269b499123e2d1c89005ee4cea8c31098`. The scheduler active-event timestamp API and cached device-event state are retained alongside FPM idle-heartbeat gating and interval observers. The GPU results above belong to head `9babf79d21a412f56d1a9a958d764d58dcc3464e` on main `5c2de3f35567ffceec6cea86ba18e075692e9101`; GPU tests were not rerun for the current head. title: [Fix] moe: Preserve FP32 router precision across model gates
author: seongyun1104
body:
## Motivation

Addresses the independent model fixes called out in #38695.

Several MoE models still discard router precision at model-specific boundaries:

- MiMo-V2, Ernie4, and Kimi Linear can construct the checkpoint correction bias in bf16, even though expert selection consumes it in fp32-sensitive score arithmetic.
- Bailing MoE and Bailing MoE Linear compute with fp32 router weights when configured, then cast the logits back to the hidden-state dtype before top-k.

These paths either collapse checkpoint bias values or throw away the fp32 router output immediately before expert selection.

LLaDA2 originally had the same router-output downcast, but #31768 fixed that path independently. The current PR therefore leaves LLaDA2 untouched.

## Modifications

- Keep `e_score_correction_bias` parameters in fp32 for MiMo-V2, Ernie4, and Kimi Linear.
- Return the gate GEMM output at the router-weight dtype for Bailing MoE and Bailing MoE Linear.

The patch is limited to five model files. It does not introduce a shared `RouterGate`, add a kernel, or change expert computation.

## Accuracy Tests

No new unit test is included, following the maintainer guidance in #38695 that these model-file fixes do not require one. The changes only preserve the dtype already selected for the correction bias or router GEMM output.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. No kernel is added. The Bailing paths remove a dtype-conversion operation when the router is configured for fp32.
