title: [Fix] [AMD] dsa: Fix AITER prefill with an FP8 KV cache
author: pbkowalski
body:
# [AMD] Fix AITER DSA prefill with an FP8 KV cache

 ## Motivation
  SGLang gathers the KV entries selected by DeepSeek Sparse Attention into a compact buffer before calling AITER. `kv_indptr` describes each query’s range within that buffer, so AITER must use this compact layout rather than
  apply another fixed top-k interpretation.
  The current integration has two independent problems.
  First, it violates AITER’s FP8 contract. It leaves `q_scale` unset, passes `1.0` instead of the layer’s actual KV-cache scale, and allocates FP8 output even though AITER’s reduction kernel writes BF16. With an FP8 KV cache,
  the stock path aborts on its first forward because the required query scale is missing.
  Second, SGLang builds AITER metadata as if the compact buffer still used a fixed sparse top-k layout. It also forces 64 work splits instead of allowing AITER to derive the split policy from `kv_indptr` and the workload. After
  correcting the FP8 dtype and scale contract, this legacy metadata path causes output-quality collapse rather than mild numerical drift. In our 60,000-token test, both 64-token generations diverged from TileLang at the first
  generated character and produced repetitive malformed text. We have reproduced this failure at 60,000 input tokens but have not established the minimum failing context length.
  This change affects only DSA calls using AITER with an FP8 KV cache. Other DSA backends and non-FP8 KV-cache paths are unchanged. It assumes that affected calls:
  - have already gathered the selected KV entries into a compact buffer;
  - describe that layout with `kv_indptr`;
  - provide a scalar `layer.k_scale`;
  - require BF16 output when the query is FP8; and
  - support AITER v1.2 fast metadata for their head count and shape.
  These assumptions are correct for the tested GLM path, but not yet demonstrated for every DSA model.


## Modifications

- Select AITER's v1.2 metadata builder with `fast_mode=True`.
- Disable the legacy v1.0 path with `intra_batch_mode=False`.
- Pass `topk=-1` because the KV entries are already compact. This makes AITER
  use the ranges in `kv_indptr`; it does not disable DSA top-k selection.
- Remove the fixed `max_split_per_batch=64` value so AITER derives the split
  count from the workload.
- Allocate BF16 output when the query input is FP8.
- Pass query scale `1.0` and the layer's KV-cache scale to AITER.
- Add AITER to the existing DSA FP8-prefill test matrix.

Cross-layer metadata reuse is intentionally excluded and will be submitted
separately.

## Accuracy Tests

Hardware: AMD MI355X, TP4, FP8 KV cache.

The existing DSA attention test suite passed the AITER BF16 and FP8 sparse
prefill cases:

```bash
python3 test/registered/attention/unittests/dsa/test_dsa.py
```

For a long-context output test, the same two fixed-seed random prompts were run
once with AITER prefill and once with TileLang prefill. Each prompt used 60,000
input tokens and 64 output tokens, with `temperature=0` and `top_p=1`. The
generated texts matched for both prompts.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This is a correctness fix. The metadata builder changes from a fixed split
policy to AITER's workload-adaptive policy, but this PR does not claim a
standalone serving-speed improvement.

## Checklist

- [x] Format and code-style checks pass.
- [x] Existing DSA accuracy tests cover the AITER FP8-prefill path.
- [x] Long-context output matches TileLang for both test prompts.
- [x] No user-facing documentation change is required.

title: [Fix] Seed raw tokenizer_path for smg-grpc-servicer in gRPC mode
author: ShangmingCai
body:
## Motivation

The `PR Test (SMG)` job `chat-completions-4gpu` has been red on every PR and on main itself (e.g. runs [34544453982](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34544453982), [34617263712](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34617263712), [34587282881](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34587282881)). The qwen-30b gRPC worker dies at startup with:

```
File ".../smg_grpc_servicer/sglang/servicer.py", line 224, in __init__
    self.tokenizer = get_tokenizer(
File ".../sglang/srt/utils/hf_transformers/tokenizer.py", line 481, in get_tokenizer
    if tokenizer_name.endswith(".json"):
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'endswith'
```

**Root cause:** since the resolution pipeline moved off the record (#36789), the default `tokenizer_path = model_path` is *declared* into the resolution stash (`serving_hook.handle_missing_default_values`) and never written back to `ServerArgs`. `smg-grpc-servicer` (<= 0.9.1, unchanged on PyPI since Aug 26) builds its tokenizer from the **raw** `server_args.tokenizer_path` field, which now stays `None` unless `--tokenizer-path` is passed explicitly. The breakage was masked until #38801 raised the servicer floor past an earlier `ImportError`; since then every gRPC-mode launch without `--tokenizer-path` crashes here.

## Modifications

Seed the default as raw input in `launch_server.run_server`, before `resolve_once()` seals the record (the only writable window — `serve_grpc` itself runs post-resolution where `__setattr__` correctly refuses writes). To the resolution pipeline this is indistinguishable from the operator passing `--tokenizer-path` equal to `--model-path`, which `model_path_hook` already supports (it keeps the two in sync through path resolution).

Longer-term, `smg-grpc-servicer` should read the resolved value (it already imports `publish` and other resolution-aware entry points), at which point this seed can be dropped; this change unbreaks CI without requiring a new servicer release.

## Verification

Reproduced and verified on a GPU box against this exact commit pair, emulating the servicer's read (intercepting `serve_grpc` inside `run_server`, then calling `get_tokenizer` with the raw field exactly as `servicer.py:224` does):

```
# main (ddf02a4f58)
STEP1 raw tokenizer_path after prepare_server_args: None
STEP2 raw tokenizer_path as the servicer sees it: None
STEP3 servicer get_tokenizer crashed: AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'endswith'

# this PR
STEP1 raw tokenizer_path after prepare_server_args: None
STEP2 raw tokenizer_path as the servicer sees it: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B
STEP3 servicer get_tokenizer OK: Qwen2Tokenizer
```

Note: `chat-completions-4gpu` also intermittently fails with `NCCL error: unhandled cuda error` during TP=4 init on the `h100-novita5-gpu-0123` / `h100-novita10-gpu-0123` runners specifically (other runners pass NCCL init). That is a runner-fleet issue independent of this fix and needs an ops look.

title: [Mamba] Fix checkpoint depth for prefixes that end off the radix page
author: klshuster
body:
## Motivation

With DCP the radix-tree page is wider than the scheduler page (e.g. 512 vs 64), so a prefill chunk can leave `prefix_indices` at 64 with no node inserted. The next extend picks the Mamba checkpoint depth relative to that prefix, `64 + 512 = 576`, a position no 512-token page can hold. On finish the two freed kv-row tails `[512, 576)` and `[576, 605)` share a page and the scheduler dies:

```
AssertionError: segment at 576 shares a page with the one ending at 576
```

Without the assertion the node would carry a Mamba state 64 tokens past its end. Reproduced on Kimi-K3 with `--dcp-size 8` and radix cache on.

## Modifications

`_mamba_radix_cache_v2_req_prepare_for_extend` picks the depth on the absolute checkpoint grid and donates only where an h snapshot exists (`(depth - prefix_len) % cache_chunk_size == 0`).

```diff
-        mask = req.extend_range.length >= checkpoint_grid
+        prefix_len = len(req.prefix_indices)
+        seq_end = prefix_len + req.extend_range.length
+        mamba_track_seqlen_aligned = (seq_end // checkpoint_grid) * checkpoint_grid
+        mask = (
+            mamba_track_seqlen_aligned > prefix_len
+            and (mamba_track_seqlen_aligned - prefix_len) % cache_chunk_size == 0
+        )
```

## Accuracy Tests

`test/registered/unit/managers/test_mamba_checkpoint_depth.py` gains one table-driven case (prefix off the widened page, short extend crossing a page, extend crossing no page, prefix off the kernel chunk grid). Three of its four rows fail on main and pass with this change. Kimi-K3 dcp=8 agentic serving with the radix cache runs to completion instead of crashing.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not affected: a few scalar ops per request at batch preparation.

title: [AMD] Fix Dspark accept length and reduce host bubble on DSV4
author: RolaoDenthu
body: ## Motivation Fix accept length for dspark and reduce bubble in draft (labeled as target verify) ## Modifications **1. Refresh captured SWA write locations in place** - UnifiedKvMetadata.copy_ previously rebound swa_loc through assign_fields. For metadata built outside the graph, this updates the Python reference but leaves the buffer referenced by captured kernels unchanged. - DSPARK's draft KV-store path consumes swa_loc, so subsequent replays can write KV to stale ring locations. - Move swa_loc to copy_fields to update the captured buffer in place while preserving its address. **2. Reduce metadata preparation overhead** - Use the existing Triton causal-expansion kernel for uniform and ragged prefill layouts, replacing the per-request Python loop. - Pass output_size to torch.repeat_interleave when the exact token count is known, avoiding its implicit device-to-host synchronization. - Preserve dynamic sizing for padded ragged layouts and the existing target-prefill path. **3. title: Fix multimodal embedding cache retaining full batches through views
author: cctry
body:
## Motivation

Caching a `torch.split` view can keep an entire batch allocation alive while the cache accounts only for the slice's bytes. Retained tensor storage can therefore exceed the configured multimodal embedding cache budget.

## Modifications

Account for backing-storage bytes and clone admitted tensors only when their storage exceeds their payload. Full-storage tensors and reshapes, duplicate keys, and rejected insertions avoid unnecessary copies. Update the existing CPU regression test to require compact cache entries.

## Test plan

- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `uv run --no-project --with pre-commit pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/multimodal_cache.py test/registered/chunked_prefill/test_mm_chunked_embedding_unit.py` — all applicable hooks passed.
- `uv run --no-project --with torch --with numpy python /tmp/sglang-mm-cache-port.SPt3Dg/check_cache.py` — local CPU smoke checks passed with PyTorch 2.14.0. Checked ordinary, detached, strided, and inference-mode slices; unchanged tensor values; full-storage and expanded tensors; LRU eviction and accounting; and avoiding copies for duplicate/rejected insertions. The temporary harness imports the real cache and allocator base directly, bypassing unrelated runtime imports.
- `PYTHONPATH=python uv run --no-project --with torch --with pytest python -m pytest test/registered/chunked_prefill/test_mm_chunked_embedding_unit.py -q` — blocked during collection: the minimal local environment lacks runtime dependencies (`ModuleNotFoundError: numpy`). title: fix(kda_prefill): fence shared writes before async proxy reads
author: willhu-jpg
body:
## Motivation

`chain_body` writes the widened L tile to shared memory through the generic proxy, then consumes it through the tcgen05 async machinery. `__syncthreads()` synchronizes participating threads, but it does not establish ordering between generic-proxy shared-memory writes and async-proxy reads. On affected SM103 KDA prefill runs, that missing proxy fence can race and cause incorrect results or device faults.

## Modifications

Add a small PTX helper for `fence.proxy.async.shared::cta` and issue it immediately after `widen_map_tf32`, before the existing tcgen05 thread fence and CTA synchronization.

## Accuracy Tests

- `clang-format` 20.1.7 passes.
- `git diff --check` passes.

An isolated A/B stress test on B300 (SM103) compiled two extensions from the
same source. The second variant removed exactly the three-line fence helper and
its one call. A CUDA profile confirmed all tested shapes selected
`kda_fused<0, true, true>`, which exercises the multi-piece prefix-composition
path containing this fence. Two fixed input sets were alternated between calls
to expose stale shared-memory data.

| Tokens | Heads | Fenced mismatch vs. its baseline | Unfenced mismatch vs. fenced baseline | Unfenced mismatch vs. its own first result |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8,192 | 12 | 0 / 100 | 86 / 100 | 100 / 100 |
| 16,384 | 12 | 0 / 100 | 82 / 100 | 89 / 100 |
| 8,192 | 16 | 0 / 100 | 75 / 100 | 100 / 100 |

The unfenced mismatches affected both BF16 output and FP32 final state. Sampled
mismatches were finite, and this run did not produce a device fault. The
fenced variant was bitwise stable across every repetition.

A CPU unit test would not exercise this hardware memory-ordering requirement. A regression test intended to provoke the race on SM103 would also be nondeterministic, so this PR does not add one.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not separately benchmarked. The change adds one CTA-scoped proxy fence only on the affected chain path; this PR makes no performance claim.

## Checklist

- [x] The code is formatted with the repository-pinned clang-format version.
- [x] The change is limited to the KDA prefill memory-ordering fix.
- [x] Accuracy evidence and its limitations are described above.
- [x] No documentation update is needed for this internal kernel synchronization change.

title: [Qwen3.8] Enable NVIDIA NVFP4 on DGX Spark with file-backed PLE and PDL router fix
author: Jiminator
body:
## Motivation

Combining these changes into one PR also saves CI resources by avoiding three separate PRs running overlapping CI suites.

Enable single-node DGX Spark / GB10 deployment of `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` from upstream main, with or without its embedded MTP head. Main still lacks the NVIDIA mixed-precision loader handling and file-backed PLE storage needed for this deployment, and both PDL routers read bias before waiting for the preceding producer.

Consolidates and supersedes #38568, #38569 and #38570. Preserves their commits and authorship, upstreaming the original PDL fix #38290, NVIDIA loader work #38121 / #37752, file-backed PLE backend #37068 by @hashd1ve, and TP prefetch correction #38123 by @yhyang201.

## Modifications

- Move the PDL dependency wait before bias and score loads in both Triton and radix routers. Preserve register zeros for the no-bias path.
- Resolve ModelOpt mixed-precision checkpoint prefixes, normalize omitted exclusion lists, dispatch FP8_BLOCK_SCALES layers, and select FP8 PLE storage from the mixed config. Preserve existing FP8_PB_WO support.
- Retain mixed quantization for checkpoints with quantized `mtp.*` layers; preserve BF16 MTP behavior otherwise. Add the original mixed-expert runner selection and use the Triton FP8 MoE fallback when the global NVFP4 runner is FlashInfer CUTLASS/CuteDSL.
- Add `--ple-offload-backend {pinned,file}` and `--ple-offload-dir`, using a sparse file-backed table on supported unified-memory devices. Add prefetching and resident-memory trimming.
- Filter prefetch IDs to the local TP vocabulary shard and subtract the shard start before computing file offsets.
- Include the original ports' regression tests and CLI/environment documentation.

Based on `main@45715e7f20629d1813ff8f543a23bb437128db2e`. All three changes merge cleanly, and the combined tree is identical to merging the empirically tested integration branch onto this base. No additional source edits were introduced during consolidation. Direct source review confirms all three gaps remain in this main revision.

## Accuracy Tests

**Empirical host deployment on 1x DGX Spark / GB10 (sm121), TP=1; no patched Docker image.** SGLang and its native extensions were installed from the combined source checkout. NVIDIA checkpoint revision: `fab0aecb760cec45227f6656abcaafa11abca87a`.

September 11 tests used `main@165d8dd17736fa4938f2e73018f26835cd6e0778` plus these exact component heads:

- #38568: `626f614f7bcd5dc531de5c268a694ff1a9f31f28`.
- #38569: `825663897b1fd9ee5c341eeb113b795e4ecfc3f8`.
- #38570: `b14d2c55f37f8d3dc2b5fe21175b56fbe62771e1`.

Tested combined revision: `69d38ccbd8a03646cae9168c971b3783883c2903`. The newer PR base received source and clean-merge review; the numbers below are not relabeled as a GPU run on that newer base.

GSM8K first 200 test questions, greedy chat API, thinking disabled, 8,192-token generation limit:

| Configuration | Accuracy | Request errors / invalid / truncated | Ready | Effective max input |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| MTP, concurrency 8 | **195/200 (97.5%)** | **0 / 0 / 0** | 763.26 s | 180,282 tokens |
| Non-MTP, concurrency 24 | **194/200 (97.0%)** | **0 / 0 / 0** | 633.17 s | 262,138 tokens |

Both arithmetic smoke tests passed and CUDA graphs were active. MTP selected the intended FP8 Triton expert fallback and reported average draft acceptance **3.52925**. No serving NaN/OOM/CUDA-error/exception reports appeared before intentional shutdown. This is log-level evidence, not internal NaN instrumentation. Cancellation tracebacks during intentional SIGTERM were recorded separately; both servers stopped after evaluation.

Environment: Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, driver 580.173.02, FlashInfer 0.6.18, Triton 3.7.1, sglang-kernel 0.4.6.post1, Transformers 5.12.1. The isolated host environment was updated from main and native extensions rebuilt. Runs reused previously compiled host kernels with `MAX_JOBS=2`; startup timings exclude cold kernel compilation. The NVIDIA cuSPARSELt package reports a platform-tag warning on aarch64; GPU imports and both deployments succeeded.

Common serving flags (using the local NVIDIA checkpoint copy and a fresh local-NVMe PLE directory per boot):

```bash
sglang serve \
  --model-path nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 \
  --tp 1 \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass \
  --fp4-gemm-backend flashinfer_cutlass \
  --page-size 64 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \
  --context-length 262144 \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 \
  --ple-offload-embedding --ple-offload-backend file
```

MTP adds `--speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --max-running-requests 8 --max-mamba-cache-size 40`. Non-MTP adds `--mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer_lazy --max-running-requests 24 --max-mamba-cache-size 96`.

Prior component checks recorded in the superseded PRs: 15 router GPU tests; 18 mixed-loader tests; 3 FP8 fallback tests; 34 fusion-gate tests; 2 Qwen MoE override tests; 26 file-table/Qwen argument tests; 13 embedding tests. Changed-file pre-commit hooks passed on the component ports. Consolidation passes `git diff --check` and exact merged-tree comparison; these component tests were not rerun merely to combine branches.

Scope: TP=1 text/chat validation, not a deterministic PDL-race reproduction, TP>1 prefetch validation, other-hardware validation, or the full 1,319-question benchmark. No full-length 262K prompt was tested; the configured MTP memory budget limits effective input to about 180K.

Known PLE startup limitation: populated files are rewritten on boot and can be much slower than fresh sparse files. Stop all servers using the directory before removing its `ple_table_*.bin` files for a fresh boot. Automatic cache lifecycle changes are not included.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

| Configuration | Generated tokens | Evaluation wall time | Aggregate output |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| MTP, concurrency 8 | 79,489 | 855.91 s | **92.87 tokens/s** |
| Non-MTP, concurrency 24 | 79,954 | 893.02 s | **89.53 tokens/s** |

These are end-to-end chat-evaluation aggregates including prefill and the lower-concurrency tail, not a controlled before/after speed comparison or an isolated measurement of the router fix. The final non-MTP response discussed salary timing for 4,632 tokens, finished normally, and was scored incorrect against the dataset label.

title: [Fix] Preserve GLM tool argument types across JSON Schema unions
author: willhu-jpg
body:
## Motivation

The GLM-4.7/GLM-5 tool-call parser currently commits to one inferred JSON Schema type before the complete argument value is available. This produces different or incorrect arguments between complete and streamed responses. For example, a field declared as `{"type": ["string", "null"]}` can serialize a model-emitted `null` as the strings `"None"` or `"null"` instead of JSON `null`.

The same early choice affects local references, enums, and root `anyOf`/`oneOf` schemas whose sibling discriminator appears after the value. Streaming numeric prefixes can also be emitted before the parser knows whether the completed value is valid JSON.

## Modifications

- Resolve local `$ref`, `type` arrays, `enum`, `const`, `anyOf`, `oneOf`, and `allOf` without discarding possible argument types early.
- Use completed argument values and sibling discriminators to select a root union branch.
- Buffer ambiguous and numeric streaming values until they are complete and can be serialized consistently.
- Keep plain string fields incremental and preserve strings that resemble JSON values.
- Add focused complete/streaming tests across multiple chunk sizes for nullable values, references, unions, discriminators, numeric values, and parser state resets.

## Related Work

- #36626, already merged, discovers properties inside top-level schema combinators. This change builds on it but avoids selecting the first duplicate property type when the completed value or a sibling discriminator selects another branch.
- #35564 tracks streaming/non-streaming parity across several parsers. #35625 is its broad proposed fix, and #36688 is a narrower GLM version that defers to #35625. They overlap with buffering schema-less values and preventing invalid streamed numeric tokens; they do not cover nullable coercion, local references, enum/const narrowing, or sibling-discriminated root unions addressed here.

## Accuracy Tests

- `python test/registered/unit/function_call/test_glm47_schema_types.py -q`: 11 tests passed.
- Existing `TestGlm47MoeDetector` parser behavior tests: 11 tests passed. The structural-tag capability test requires a newer local `xgrammar` API and does not exercise this change.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `check_registered_tests.py`, `check_no_bare_pytest_main.py`, Python compilation, and `git diff --check` passed.

The new matrix checks both parsed values and their native Python types for complete parsing and streaming with 1-character, 7-character, and whole-message chunks.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This changes only GLM tool-call parsing. Plain string arguments continue to stream incrementally. Arguments are buffered only when their type cannot be determined safely from the schema or when a root union requires completed sibling values; no model execution or kernel path changes.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No documentation change is needed for this parser correction.

title: [Session + MM] Fix text positions in session continuations
author: ByronHsu
body:
## Why?

- Text appended to a session after an image can receive too few position values and produce control tokens instead of an answer.

## What?

- Fill missing text positions using the saved position delta.
- Keep existing image positions and precomputed decode positions.

- Related: #35485 addresses the same issue. This patch keeps the change specific to session continuations and reuses the existing decode-position helper.

## Verification?

- Reproduce with Qwen2.5-VL-3B: open a regular or streaming session, send a 56x56 red image with turn 1, then append turn 2 using the previous request ID. Use `temperature=0`, `max_new_tokens=4`, and `ignore_eos=true` for both turns.
- mRoPE supplies three position values per token. The three rows are identical for the appended text, so one row is shown below. This image leaves a saved position offset of `-2`: text position = token index - 2.

```text
Turn 1: red image + "What color is this image?"
        -> "The image is red" (4 generated tokens)
Turn 2: "Name that color again." (15 tokens including chat markers)

Token indices:  0..19          20..23         24..38
Contents:       first prompt   first reply   appended text
Cached KV:      <------ 24 tokens -------->
Saved mRoPE:    <20 columns>
Needed now:                                  <15 columns>

Before:
  saved_positions[:, 24:39] -> empty (saved table has only 20 columns)
  Single-token fallback   -> [36]                 shape [3, 1]
  Result: only 1 position column for 15 input tokens.

After:
  Fill the missing text positions using token index + saved offset:
  [24, 25, ..., 38] - 2    -> [22, 23, ..., 36]     shape [3, 15]
  Full-history replay     -> [22, 23, ..., 36]     exact match

Observed model output:
  Before -> <|im_start|>\n<|im_start|><|im_end|>
  After  -> "The color is red" (same four token IDs as full replay)
```

- Model outputs were observed on one H200 for both session modes; full-history replay used a separate cache key. The position arrays above were reproduced separately on the box with the base and patched position helpers, using the same image, prompt, and recorded first reply.

## Test?

- Same external position checks: **12 failed / 8 passed before; 20 passed after**. Covers partial/empty saved positions, position deltas, and decode fallback.
- Model replay comparisons: **2 passed**; server health returned 200 after each session closed.
- Existing session, multimodal cleanup, and position encoder tests: **22 passed**.
- Ruff formatting/lint, Python compilation, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Base: `5f3606c7b2`; CI: pending.

title: [Session] Fix image append positions and parent metadata
author: ByronHsu

- Appending an image after a generated reply can leave session positions incomplete and modify the saved parent's metadata. Stale positions can also prevent scheduler recomputation.

## What?

title: [Fix] Don't free the multi-CTAs KV counter the decode graphs captured
author: mmangkad
body:
## Motivation

`DeepseekSparseAttnBackend._forward_trtllm` rebound the counter buffer:

```python
self._multi_ctas_kv_counter_buffer = grow_multi_ctas_kv_counter_buffer_if_needed(...)
```

`grow_..._if_needed` returns a **new** `torch.zeros` when it grows, so the assignment frees the buffer the decode CUDA graphs captured. Later replays write through a dangling pointer.

`batch_size` is `page_table_1.shape[0]` — **query rows, not requests** — so a *prefill* batch trips it, not decode. Reasoning in decode batch sizes (`max_running_requests x draft_tokens`) makes `TRTLLM_MLA_MAX_BATCH_SIZE=8192` look unreachable, which is why it hid.

Stock main, default flags, GLM-5.3-Flash tp4 / 4x GB300, 8192 in / 1024 out, temporary logging on all 4 ranks:

```
capture uses ptr=0xf0eb9d06dc00 bs=288      target-verify graph
capture uses ptr=0xf0e91ee00000 bs=48       draft-decode graph
grow fired: bs=16384 old_ptr=0xf0eb9d06dc00 new_ptr=0xf0e7c8e00000
            mode=EXTEND OLD_IS_THE_CAPTURED_ONE=True
```

Last capture ended 22 s before the first grow. Latent, not benign: a probe right after the grow did not land on the freed block, so today the stale writes hit memory nothing owns. Perturb the allocation pattern and it becomes a reproducible illegal access inside `fmhaSm100fKernel...DynamicTokenSparse`, the kernel that consumes the counter.

## Modifications

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `_multi_ctas_kv_counter_for` | oversized eager call takes a temporary; the captured allocation is never replaced |
| `_ensure_multi_ctas_kv_counter_capacity` | `init_cuda_graph_state` sizes for `max(max_bs, max_num_tokens)` before any capture; grow-only |
| class default `= None` | `init_cuda_graph_state` sizes it for every backend, but only the TRT-LLM branch allocates one |

Capture-time growth is then unreachable, and the assert guarding it is an invariant check rather than a live path.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable — buffer lifetime only, no numerics touched.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

GLM-5.3-Flash tp4 / 4x GB300, 8192 in / 1024 out, 3 runs each, same build:

| | tok/s | TTFT | TPOT |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main | 404.0 | 269.3 ms | 2.21 ms |
| + fix | 402.4 | 269.9 ms | 2.22 ms |

TTFT is the number at risk (the oversized path now allocates per call across 11 DSA layers), so it was measured rather than assumed. All inside noise.

## Checklist

- [x] `test/registered/kernel/attention/test_dsa_multi_ctas_counter.py`, 7 cases
- [x] Each fix mutated independently: `2 / 1 / 1` failures, `7` passed unmutated
- [x] `check_registered_tests.py` and `git diff --check` exit 0

title: Fix Mistral3 retaining every vision-tower layer to read one
author: alisonshao
body:
Serving Mistral Medium 3.5 with images OOMs inside the Pixtral vision tower minutes after a clean start, on a tiny allocation, while the KV pool looks healthy.

`get_image_feature` asks the tower for `output_hidden_states=True`, so it builds and holds one hidden-state tensor per layer — 49 of them (input embedding + 48 layers) — and they stay resident for the whole item loop. The config selects `vision_feature_layer: -1`, so exactly one of those is read. For a 1540px image that is 1.84 GiB retained per image against 38 MB for the layer itself, and the cost scales with images in the batch.

Requesting the final layer alone is the same tensor: `PixtralVisionTransformer.forward` appends to `all_hidden_states` as it goes and returns `hidden_states` when the list isn't built, so the last entry and the plain return are the same value from the same ops. Non-final `vision_feature_layer` keeps the existing path.

Measured on 4 GPUs with memory held back to emulate 80 GB cards, TP4 + EAGLE, `--mem-fraction-static 0.83 --context-length 65536`, 1540x1540 images:

- retained per image: **1.84 GiB -> 0.07 GiB**
- outputs bit-identical to before the change (text and logprobs, zero delta, 1/2/3-image requests)

| workload | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 3 images | ok, peak pinned at 139.6 GiB | ok, 128.9 GiB |
| 4 images | 500 | ok, 129.0 GiB |
| 2 concurrent x 1 image | scheduler died | ok, 128.8 GiB |
| 2 concurrent x 4 images | scheduler died | ok, 129.2 GiB |
| 8 concurrent x 4 images | — | ok, 130.8 GiB |

Peak GPU stays flat near 129 GiB instead of pinning at the 139.8 GiB ceiling, with no config change.

title: [Fix] Don't write conv state from the fused KDA verify kernel
author: mmangkad
body:
## Motivation

`fused_kda_conv_gating_verify` rolled the conv state back into `conv_state` at the end of the kernel. Every V tile loads that same Q/K conv history at entry, but only `i_v == 0` writes it, so a tile scheduled in a later wave reads what the owner already overwrote.

The writeback is also dead: verify is speculative, and the commit scatter sets `conv_state` from the selected intermediate window. `accept_lens` is at least 1, so `last_correct_step_indices` is never negative for a real request and the scatter always overwrites.

So the stores are removed rather than guarded. `conv_state` and the SSM state are read-only in verify.

## Modifications

| | |
| --- | --- |
| kernel | drop the 9 `tl.store(cs_base, ...)` at the end of `fused_kda_conv_gating_verify_kernel` |
| docstring | state ownership: conv and SSM state are read-only, the commit scatter advances them |
| tests | `conv_state` must come back untouched; output must not vary with CTA scheduling |

Reached only with `SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_KDA_VERIFY=1` (default off), on the KDA Triton verify path at `topk == 1`.

## How the race shows

H=1 with HV=16, so 16 V tiles share one Q/K history. Same inputs, against the unfused pair:

| | max abs | max rel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| full GB300, one wave | 2.98e-8 | 7.2e-3 |
| 8-SM green context, waves serialized | **5.0e-2** | **188** |

Removing the stores makes both configurations identical. The residual ~1 ulp is reduction-order difference and is unaffected by the fix.

## Accuracy Tests

Ling-3.0-flash BF16, 4x GB300 TP4, NEXTN, fused verify on. Full GSM8K, thinking on, `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, `max_tokens=8192`, 1 repeat.

| | score | stop | error |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before | 96.06% | 99.70% | 0.00% |
| after | 95.83% | 99.17% | 0.00% |

Unchanged — the gap is inside the ~0.55pp 1-sigma band at n=1319. The race is below eval resolution when the grid fits one wave.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same server, 8192 in / 1024 out at concurrency 1, 64 warmup, `--flush-cache`, 3 runs per arm. Accept length 3.01 on all six.

| | runs (tok/s) | mean |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before | 355.23, 361.47, 363.72 | 360.14 |
| after | 370.64, 369.38, 375.18 | **371.73** |

**+3.22%**, arms disjoint. The kernel does strictly less work with the stores gone.

## Checklist

- [x] `pre-commit` clean
- [x] 9 cases in `test_fused_kda_conv_recurrent_verify.py`; all 9 fail against the unfixed kernel
- [x] Accuracy and speed measured above

title: Fix MegaMoE buffer allocation and caching for effective SM budgets
author: aurickq
body:
## Why is this change needed?

DeepGEMM derives MegaMoE buffer size and layout from the runtime SM count ([buffer sizing](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/66081d4c9c7d7c44f13fea402e5b622aa0f409c2/csrc/apis/mega_moe.hpp#L44)). SGLang applies an SM budget to kernel execution, but previously allocated outside that context and cached without the effective SM count.

For the CPU test's 132-SM ambient count and 130-SM cap:

```diff
- Allocate at 132 SMs; execute at 130.
+ Allocate and execute at 130 SMs.
- Reuse that buffer when an outer context limits execution to 96 SMs.
+ Allocate a separate buffer for the 96-SM budget.
```

The shared helper now allocates under the existing SM context and includes `deep_gemm.get_num_sms()` in the cache key. Equal effective budgets still reuse their buffer. Kernel code, dependencies, and caller APIs are unchanged; distinct budgets can retain additional buffers.

## Test Plan

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python3 test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_mega_moe_deepgemm_api.py
pre-commit run --files \
  python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_moe.py \
  test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_mega_moe_deepgemm_api.py
```

- All 9 CPU tests pass. The effective-budget/cache and allocation-failure checks fail against unmodified upstream.
- Coverage includes equal-budget reuse, different-budget separation, no-override behavior, and state restoration on cache hits, misses, and allocation failure.
- Pre-commit checks pass for both changed files.
- GPU numerical correctness, CUDA graph behavior, and performance have not been validated for this PR.

title: Fix /model_info serialization when a config value is a class
author: raghotham
body:
## Motivation

`GET /model_info` builds a plain `result` dict and returns it directly, unlike the other handlers in the `/server_info` family which pass their payload through `msgspec_to_builtins`. When any value in that dict is a Python **class object** rather than an instance, it reaches the JSON encoder unchanged and the request fails with HTTP 500.

`load_format` is the common way to hit this: it holds a class when a custom loader is configured instead of one of the built-in string formats, so `/model_info` 500s for the whole server even though every other field is serializable.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/http_server.py` — `model_info()` now returns `msgspec_to_builtins(result)`, matching the other `/server_info`-family handlers. `msgspec_to_builtins` was already imported in this module.
- `python/sglang/srt/utils/msgspec_utils.py` — `msgspec_to_builtins` renders a class as its dotted `module.qualname` string. The new branch sits after the existing dataclass check, which already excludes types via `not isinstance(obj, type)`, so dataclass classes keep their current handling and no other call site changes behavior. Previously a class fell through to the terminal return and came back unconverted.
- `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_server_info.py` — regression test that `/model_info` renders a class-valued `load_format` as its dotted path and that the resulting payload is `json.dumps`-able.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable — this is a serialization fix on an introspection endpoint and does not affect model outputs.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Not applicable — no change on any inference path.

## Checklist

- `ruff check --select=F401,F821,UP037` and `ruff format --check` (at the pinned `v0.15.1`) pass on all three files.
- `python3 -m py_compile` passes on all three files.
- The new unit test was not executed in this checkout, which has no test environment installed; it is a CPU-only test registered to `base-a-test-cpu` and will run in CI.

## Original commits

title: [Fix][Qwen-VL] Normalize <image> sentinel on artifact fast path
author: arathi-hlab
body:
## Summary

- Root cause: PR #36411 routes every Qwen3-VL image request through the new artifact fast path (`compose_image_artifacts` → `_build_image_prompt_template` → `build_input_ids`). The scan only counts image slots when the prompt contains `<|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>` triples, so `/generate` requests using sglang's `<image>` sentinel raise `ValueError: Qwen-VL image artifacts do not match prompt placeholders` and the client sees `KeyError: 'meta_info'` (HTTP 400 body served as if it were a normal response).
- This regresses XPU CI (`test/registered/xpu/test_encoder_attention_backend.py`, which POSTs `"<image>\n Tell me..."` to `/generate`) and would fail identically on any CUDA caller that uses `<image>` against Qwen3-VL, since `uses_media_artifacts_without_cache` is unconditional on `qwen3_vl` / `qwen3_vl_moe`.
- Fix normalizes the raw prompt in the fast path and defensively falls back to `_process_mm_data_uncached` when the invariant cannot be recovered.

## What changed

`python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/qwen_vl.py`:

1. **`mm_tokens.image_token_regex`** now also matches sglang's `<image>` sentinel:
   ```
   r\"<\\|vision_start\\|>(?:<\\|image_pad\\|>)+<\\|vision_end\\|>|<image>\"
   ```
2. **`_normalize_prompt_for_fast_path(input_text, expected_image_count)`** — new protected helper. For string prompts, `regex.subn` replaces each recognized placeholder with the model's wrapped `<|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>` and checks the count against `len(artifacts)`. Chat-template inputs (already wrapped) substitute to themselves, so the hot path is a no-op with a single `subn` call. Returns `None` on mismatch.
3. **`compose_image_artifacts`** now returns `Optional[MultimodalProcessorOutput]`: normalizes first, and catches a residual `ValueError('...prompt placeholders...')` from `_build_image_prompt_template` to signal a fallback rather than propagating a 500.
4. **`process_mm_data_async`** falls through to `_process_mm_data_uncached` (the pre-#36411 authoritative path) when `compose_image_artifacts` returns `None`. The user never sees a 400; only a debug log records the miss.

## Why this is the right layer

- Uses the existing `MultimodalSpecialTokens` machinery — teaching the processor which prompt shapes represent an image slot is exactly what `image_token_regex` is for. Extending it once also fixes `load_mm_data`'s `<image>` handling on the uncached path (previously it fell through to `legacy_load_mm_data` which never actually substitutes `<image>`).
- Preserves the H100 win: chat-template inputs match the wrapped triple, `subn` is a self-replacement, `_cached_image_prompt_template`'s LRU cache still hits, and `_build_image_prompt_template` still avoids the HF processor. No new tensor allocations on the hot path.
- Small, contained: one file, ~60 net-added lines, no API surface changes outside a return-type widening (`MultimodalProcessorOutput` → `Optional[MultimodalProcessorOutput]`) on a Qwen-VL-only method that has a single caller inside the same class.

## Repro (before this PR, on `main` at `0a57403468` or later)

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \\
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Thinking \\
  --device xpu --mm-attention-backend xpu_attn --port 21000

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:21000/generate -H content-type:application/json -d \\
  '{\"text\":\"<image>\\n Tell me what you can see from the image.\",
    \"image_data\":\"examples/assets/example_image.png\",
    \"sampling_params\":{\"temperature\":0,\"max_new_tokens\":32}}'
# -> {\"error\":{\"message\":\"Qwen-VL image artifacts do not match prompt placeholders\"}}
```

Same repro on CUDA hits the same error (has to; `uses_media_artifacts_without_cache = True`).

## Failing CI runs

- https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34740216597
- https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34739837263
- https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34738318077 (push on `main`, not a PR — so this landed as a `main` regression, not just a PR failure)

## Test plan

- [ ] `test/registered/xpu/test_encoder_attention_backend.py` (XPU) — expected PASS
- [ ] Existing Qwen3-VL CUDA benchmarks / accuracy tests exercising `/v1/chat/completions` — expected UNCHANGED (fast path still taken; substitution is a no-op)
- [ ] Manual `/generate` with raw `<image>` — returns a normal `meta_info["finish_reason"]`
- [ ] Manual `/generate` with mismatched placeholder count (e.g. two `<image>` markers, one image) — falls back to uncached path; error, if any, surfaces from the HF processor rather than an internal 500

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Add a regression test that POSTs `<image>` to `/generate` on CUDA — the XPU test is the only current guard and it lives under `test/registered/xpu/`.
- Consider a similar audit for other processors that inherit `MediaArtifactCacheMixin` and set `generates_input_ids_from_raw_prompt = True`.

cc @BBuf / @xzhang711 (author of #36411), @jianan-gu (original author of the failing XPU test).

title: [Fix] unified-memory: Bound joint reclaim and preserve cached prefixes
author: seokwoosong
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #44097
* __->__ #39294 (merged)

CI is run only on the top PR, #44097, which contains both changes.

Merged into main as `ee30dc4d40993045273f0a90260db7efa302c214`. #44097 has been rebased onto this merge and now targets main directly.

Current head: `1adc6a6229fecca1b58cb56df6732c395ea65334`.

## Motivation

Joint FULL/SWA allocations can evict more cached prefixes than needed. FULL/SWA/Mamba allocations can fail despite recoverable capacity, or discard the entire cache before rejecting an impossible demand.

Seokwoo Song's original commits are preserved, rebased onto `ae28306a74fc9ba56daab9ccb06dcf45659f58af`.

## Modifications

- Stop allocation-driven eviction at a read-only sufficient-reclaim predicate; prepare and verify the physical layout at bounded phase boundaries.
- Reject demands proven impossible by byte or ID bounds before eviction, and bound token/state reclaim quotas.
- Compute exact unsharded paged-extend demand for the unified SWA allocators while preserving conservative demand elsewhere.
- Update the dLLM KV-reuse test allocator to implement the paged-demand interface with the conservative default, fixing the CPU CI failure.
- Adapt the closed-move-gate regression to the current physical-page copy interface. Preserve main's SWA-preferred reclaim planning for storage-backed HiCache and decode disaggregation.

## Accuracy Tests

Latest main rebase: `ae28306a74fc9ba56daab9ccb06dcf45659f58af`. Both PRs replayed without conflicts, and all eight patches are unchanged by `git range-diff`. The exact combined top commit passed **87 tests / 211 subtests** on H200 (Python 3.12 / Torch 2.13.0+cu130), covering dLLM KV reuse, prefill budget, joint reclaim, SWA page estimation, Mamba/Conv compaction and views (CPU and CUDA), and adjacent HiCache ordering/regressions. All changed-file pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` passed.

Earlier CI follow-up, before this main rebase: reproduced the `get_extend_allocation_demand` failure in `test_dllm_fdfo_kv_reuse.py` before the correction. After updating the fake allocator in #39294, **66 tests / 162 subtests passed** across the dLLM KV-reuse, prefill-budget, joint-eviction, tri-pool reclaim, and SWA paged-extend suites on the H200 host (Python 3.12 / Torch 2.13.0+cu130). All six dLLM tests passed. Changed-file pre-commit checks passed.

Earlier validation before this main rebase:

- H200 host, Python 3.12 / Torch 2.13.0+cu130: **220 tests / 1,050 subtests passed** across 14 allocator/cache files using Python TreeCore. These are CPU allocator tests.
- Freshly built current-main Rust TreeCore on the H200 host: **38 tests / 155 subtests passed** in the focused reclaim suite; session cases use the supported Python fallback. A separate probe asserted that the ordinary cache selected `RustUnifiedTreeCore`.
- With the compaction fix from #44097 applied in a separate combined snapshot on B300, Torch 2.14.1+cu130: **61 tests / 201 subtests passed**, including the CUDA compaction cases.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` passed.

Controlled real-allocator comparisons against unchanged main production code, with the same test fixtures, reproduced these results in both eager and lazy modes:

| Case | Main | This change |
|---|---|---|
| FULL/SWA, 6-token demand | Succeeds; evicts 5 cached tokens | Succeeds; evicts 3 |
| FULL/SWA/Mamba, 4-token demand | Fails | Succeeds; evicts 1 cached token |
| FULL/SWA/Mamba, 200-token impossible demand | Fails; evicts all 96 cached tokens | Fails; preserves all 96 |

The selected regression cases fail on main and pass on the candidate. Review checked quota semantics, deferred frees, page rounding, locked prefixes, changing move gates, pending reuse, and the compatibility of the rebase.

The FLOAT geometry predicates are sufficient certificates, not a complete feasibility solver. No fresh model-serving, full HiCache, or multi-GPU result is claimed. Historical serving evidence is retained below and is not validation of this head.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The controlled allocator comparisons above validate cache preservation and successful recovery, not serving throughput. No new serving-speed claim.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add and validate regression tests.
- [x] Follow SGLang code style.
- [ ] Documentation: not applicable; no new user-facing API or configuration.
- [ ] Fresh model accuracy / serving performance benchmarks: not run for this rebase.

<details>
<summary>Historical description and validation before the current rebase</summary>

## Motivation

In unified-memory configurations, KV + SWA allocation can evict more prefix cache than necessary. Mamba + KV + SWA allocation can also fail despite recoverable joint capacity, or discard cached entries before rejecting an impossible request. This change bounds joint reclaim for these allocators to preserve reusable cache and recover capacity for feasible allocations.

## Modifications

- Stop the victim walk when the allocator’s sufficient reclaim predicate is satisfied, then prepare and check the actual allocation.
- Keep the per-victim feasibility predicate read-only and bound preparation to reclaim phase boundaries.
- Use the exact unsharded paged-extend demand where supported, retaining the conservative fallback for other allocators and sharded layouts.
- Reject demands proven impossible by byte/ID bounds before eviction, preserving cached entries in those cases; bound remaining recovery attempts. This is not a complete feasibility solver for every FLOAT layout.

## Accuracy Tests

The focused three-file CPU suite passed **54 tests / 162 subtests** (23.73 seconds). Both lazy modes reproduced the allocator results below: two-pool demand 6 reclaimed 5 → 3 cached tokens; three-pool demand 4 changed failure → success; impossible three-pool demand 200 preserved all 96 cached tokens instead of evicting them. Baseline production code was unchanged; only test fixtures and regression files were supplied for comparison. These checks used Python TreeCore.

The current revision `3af4a9dd2bdb6cc0c5e7f27e3a09cbd5438fc647` additionally clarifies the two `evict_for_alloc` parameter contracts in docstrings only; executable ASTs are unchanged relative to the tested revision. Changed-file pre-commit checks passed. All-files pre-commit also passed for the preceding API migration. GPU, Rust TreeCore, and serving results below remain historical results from the explicitly listed older revisions and were not rerun after this rebase.

Validation comparing upstream (`e17935820a47`) with this fix (`fb1d221b849d`):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| CPU, 14 files | 281 tests / 1,628 subtests passed |
| Rust TreeCore focused tests | 38 tests / 155 subtests passed |
| GPU allocator payload tests, RTX 5090 | 3 passed in both unit and serving environments; real KV and Mamba moves exercised |
| Formatting | All-files pre-commit passed |

| Actual allocator case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Two-pool demand 6 | 5 cached tokens reclaimed; allocation succeeds | 3 reclaimed; allocation succeeds |
| Three-pool demand 4 | Allocation fails | Allocation succeeds, reclaiming 1 cached token |
| Impossible three-pool demand 200 | Rejects after deleting all 96 cached tokens | Rejects while preserving all 96 |

These are controlled allocator cases, not serving throughput claims. The real-GPU pending-reuse race branch was not reached; no coverage is claimed for that branch. Request-owned SWA `WINDOW_FREE` events were also not observed in the serving workloads, including the supplemental longer-prefix lane.

| Serving comparison | Result |
|---|---|
| Mellum (KV + SWA) | 48/48 primary correctness sequences and 3,840/3,840 paired measured primary sequences match; mapping/concurrent output differences require the qualifications below |
| Reduced Inkling (KV + SWA + Mamba) | 48/48 primary correctness sequences and 3,840/3,840 paired measured primary sequences match |
| Qwen3.5-4B (KV + Mamba) | Both versions show the same two concurrent text variants; no universal token-ID parity or causal explanation is claimed |

Supplemental C2 collection is complete. A separate 128-output-token smoke test matched all 29 paired request sequences (Mellum 13, Inkling 16), with 58 requests, zero errors and zero reported retractions. This is limited longer-output coverage, not a throughput or quality benchmark. Output variability in other workloads is retained below.

<details>
<summary>Serving output comparisons, targeted diagnostics, and limitations</summary>

The primary Mellum and reduced Inkling correctness comparisons matched all 96 token-ID sequences. All 7,680 paired measured request sequences also matched across the 16 primary performance runs; the supplemental results and qualifications are reported separately below. The completed pressure mapping compared 636 requests across six paired configurations: 635 token-ID sequences matched. The one Mellum mismatch occurred at the 4K cap when a revisit retained 896 rather than 512 prefix tokens. It reproduced with caching enabled; all seven requests matched with caching disabled. A focused 48-request diagnostic reproduced the split and controlled retained-prefix depth: both versions produced identical 32-token outputs and full-vocabulary logits when matched at 512 tokens, and also when matched at 896 tokens. Changing depth from 512 to 896 reproduced the same output change on the baseline alone. Retained FULL/SWA KV matched seed bytes at prefix matching and immediately before each consuming forward. This localizes the observed reproducer to retained-prefix/compute-path sensitivity; the synchronizing diagnostic does not exclude unobserved races or establish output equivalence for other workloads.

Across two supplemental Mellum C2 pairs, 254/260 measured token-ID sequences and 46/52 warmup sequences matched. Both revisions produced all observed variants for the same input and retained-prefix depth, including the initially candidate-only warmup variant. All six measured differences correlated with request forward-entry order; that association alone is not an exact batch or kernel-level causal proof. A separate 232-request CPU-trace diagnostic found identical outputs in all three actual batch-sequence groups shared by both revisions. A fourth sequence group appeared only on the baseline, and all four attempted same-batch admission conditions were not realized. The diagnostic added 12 short warmups per server absent from the original C2 runs. CPU metadata and observed output prefixes do not prove actual GPU inputs, KV payload integrity, the final sampling decision, or race freedom. These descriptive C2 results are kept separate from primary performance measurements.

In fresh Qwen performance runs, one concurrent request produced the same two observed text variants in both versions; no candidate-only text variant was observed. Earlier token-ID triage also found within-candidate variation, and a candidate repeat matched both baseline runs. The allocator/scheduling/numerical cause remains unresolved. Performance text hashes are not complete token-ID parity coverage.

</details>

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Fresh RTX 5090 / WSL measurements, using four Before/After pairs per workload. Historical serving numbers are excluded. Changes below are medians of paired changes; CPU is scheduler process time.

| Model / workload | Cached tokens per revisit, Before → After | TTFT p50 change | Output tokens/s change | CPU change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Mellum (KV + SWA) / eviction threshold | 512 → 512 | -0.54% | +0.45% | -0.42% |
| Reduced Inkling (KV + SWA + Mamba) / eviction threshold | 0 → 512 | **-25.57% (-10.85 ms)** | +0.60% | -0.58% |
| Qwen3.5-4B (KV + Mamba) / serial control | Unchanged | -0.24% | +0.90% | -0.87% |
| Qwen3.5-4B (KV + Mamba) / C4 control | Unchanged | -0.42% | +1.05% | -0.99% |

Mellum and Inkling use the preselected 8K-cap, oldest-first conditions at their baseline-calibrated eviction thresholds (9 and 12 cold requests). Inkling's revisit TTFT decreased in all four pairs (-23.35% to -26.49%). Whole-workload throughput changes were small, and cache reuse did not increase in every condition. A separate diagnostic replay at Inkling's threshold observed scheduled prefill work for the two revisits decrease from 2,048 to 1,024 tokens; this is the scheduler's extend-token count, not measured GPU FLOPs. None of the predeclared performance alerts triggered; this is not statistical equivalence or a general speedup claim. Qwen's output-variability limitation above remains.

<details>
<summary>All Mellum and Inkling primary conditions</summary>

Changes are median paired percentages; throughput ranges retain every pair, including outliers. Each condition has 20 measured episodes plus two warm episodes per server, with two hot-prefix revisits per episode.

| Model / cold requests | Cached tokens per revisit, Before → After | Tokens/s change (range) | Revisit TTFT p50 change | CPU change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Mellum (KV + SWA) / 7 | 896 → 896 | +0.85% (-0.38% to +14.91%) | -0.94% | -0.80% |
| Mellum (KV + SWA) / 9 | 512 → 512 | +0.45% (+0.14% to +12.67%) | -0.54% | -0.42% |
| Mellum (KV + SWA) / 11 | 0 → 0 | -0.55% (-5.24% to -0.05%) | +2.79% | +0.55% |
| Mellum (KV + SWA) / 5 (2K hot prefixes) | 1536 → 1536 | -0.47% (-0.83% to +8.67%) | -0.78% | +0.46% |
| Reduced Inkling (KV + SWA + Mamba) / 10 | 512 → 512 | -0.34% (-1.38% to +0.46%) | +0.21% | +0.29% |
| Reduced Inkling (KV + SWA + Mamba) / 12 | 0 → 512 | +0.60% (-1.09% to +1.09%) | -25.57% | -0.58% |
| Reduced Inkling (KV + SWA + Mamba) / 14 | 0 → 0 | -0.05% (-0.73% to +0.51%) | +0.58% | +0.03% |

Mellum's highest short-prefix pressure had lower throughput in all four pairs (median -0.55%, range -5.24% to -0.05%); its revisit TTFT p50 increased by a median 1.99 ms. This stays below the predeclared alert thresholds but is retained rather than described as zero regression. Some Mellum pairs had large positive throughput outliers; they are not the claimed benefit. Primary Mellum cache-hit totals were unchanged; separate mapping shows retention improvements at other capacities.

The 16 primary servers completed 15,360 measured requests and 1,728 warmup requests, with no request errors or reported retractions. All paired measured token-ID sequences matched. The additional 2K-prefix Mellum lane was specified before outcome inspection and retains its separate supplemental status.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Supplemental concurrent hot-prefix revisits</summary>

Two AB/BA pairs per model, using fixed seed 3001 at nominal cap 8192 and the baseline-calibrated threshold. Seeding and cold pressure remain serial; only the two hot revisits overlap (C2). Each server has 10 measured and two warm episodes, with no additional short warmups. These are descriptive two-pair results, separate from the four-pair primary measurements.

| Model | Cached tokens per revisit, Before → After | Revisit TTFT p50, pair 1 / pair 2 | Tokens/s, pair 1 / pair 2 | CPU, pair 1 / pair 2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Mellum (KV + SWA) | 704 → 704 | +0.30% / -2.40% | -0.86% / -0.76% | +0.85% / +0.74% |
| Reduced Inkling (KV + SWA + Mamba) | 0 → 512 | -22.01% / -24.38% | +0.82% / +0.59% | -0.73% / -0.53% |

All eight servers completed 1,392 requests (1,160 measured and 232 warmup), with zero request errors or reported retractions. Inkling matched 320/320 measured and 64/64 warmup paired token-ID sequences. Mellum matched 254/260 measured and 46/52 warmup sequences; the output-variability investigation and its limitations are described above. The small Mellum throughput decreases in both pairs are retained; no equivalence or broad throughput improvement is claimed.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Mellum / Inkling setup and workload</summary>

Before: upstream `e17935820a47`; After: `fb1d221b849d`. RTX 5090 (32 GB), WSL, Python 3.12.3, Torch 2.14.1, Triton 3.8.0, sglang-kernel 0.4.9. TP1, Python TreeCore, HiCache off, CUDA graph capture disabled, page size 128, chunked prefill 512, context length 4096, max running requests 4. Greedy 32-token outputs with EOS ignored; fixed token-ID inputs, not a language-quality benchmark.

| Model | Pool layout | Attention | Static memory fraction | Actual shared arena at nominal cap 8192 |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| Mellum2-12B-A2.5B-Base (KV + SWA) (`271755e48ab6`) | FULL + SWA | FA4 | 0.90 | 398,196,736 bytes |
| Inkling (KV + SWA + Mamba) (`85b071f87d9b`), local 8-layer / hidden-size-768 configuration | FULL + SWA (FLOAT) + Mamba | FA4 | 0.65 | 105,906,176 bytes |

Inkling uses the same local SM120 compatibility override in both arms (`inkling_moe.is_sm121 = lambda: True`), Triton MoE/Mamba/linear attention, 128 Mamba slots, Mamba/full ratio 0.1, and `extra_buffer` tracking every 128 tokens. This is the stated local model configuration, not a claim about the full original model. Per-pool address limits share one arena and are not additive reservations; nominal token caps are not physical capacities. Both arms' actual allocator geometry was checked.

Each serial episode flushes cache, seeds two independent 1024-token hot prefixes, sends 512-token distinct cold requests, then revisits both hot prefixes oldest-first. Baseline-only calibration (seed 1001) finds the first cold request that triggers eviction; primary conditions use N-2, N, N+2 at cap 8192. Mellum's separate 2048-token hot-prefix condition has its own threshold of 5. Calibration does not use candidate outcomes. Four pairs use seeds 3001–3004 and AB/BA/BA/AB order, with the same seeded condition permutation in both arms. Each server has 12 short warmup requests and two full warm episodes per condition, excluded from measured aggregates. Flush/checkpoint work is outside timed episodes; client timing includes request setup/bookkeeping. Detailed diagnostic hooks are absent from performance runs.

Inputs are independently generated Python-style assignments. For each seed/case, `random.Random(seed * 1000 + case)` supplies an identifier, then 700 lines using names from `record,item,cache,count,entry,result,value,index,table,request` and integers below 100000. Each line has the form `name_j = value  # Store this independent record and preserve its value.` The model tokenizer's `encode(..., add_special_tokens=True)` is truncated to the required length. Hot cases are 0/1, cold cases begin at 100; the maximum shared prefix is below one 128-token page. The long lane extends the same hot inputs and keeps their first 1024 IDs unchanged.

Alerts require a median throughput loss >5% or CPU increase >10%, or specified latency increases >5% and >2 ms, with at least three of four pairs adverse. Revisit TTFT p50 and phase E2E p50 are primary latency checks; p95 checks are exploratory. A triggered condition receives one bounded confirmation block; none triggered here. These thresholds do not establish equivalence or exclude smaller overhead.

</details>

title: [observability] Fix negative queue_time for retracted requests
author: surajm20061998
body:
## Motivation

A request put back into the waiting queue after it has already run reports a
**negative `queue_time`**.

`SchedulerReqTimeStats.set_wait_queue_entry_time()` overwrites
`wait_queue_entry_time` on every queue entry, but `set_forward_entry_time()`
records `forward_entry_time` only once. After re-entry,
`get_queueing_time() = forward_entry_time - wait_queue_entry_time` subtracts the
latest re-entry time from the first forward time.

Paths that re-queue a running request:

- `pause_generation(mode="retract")`, which re-queues **every** running request on each RL weight refit
- KV-cache-full decode retraction (`update_running_batch`)
- priority preemption (`adder.preempt_list`)
- PD decode re-bootstrap after retraction

Where it shows up:

- `meta_info["queue_time"]` with `--enable-metrics`, right next to `num_retractions`
- the `--enable-request-time-stats-logging` line (`queue_duration=-2990.79ms`)
- the module's own invariant: with `SGLANG_TEST_REQUEST_TIME_STATS=1`,
  `convert_to_duration()` raises `AssertionError` and **takes down the scheduler**

Reproduced on a real server (MLX backend, Qwen3-0.6B-4bit, `--enable-metrics`).
4 concurrent requests were retracted via `/pause_generation {"mode": "retract"}`
for 2 s during decode:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `meta_info.queue_time` (s) | -2.991, -2.991, -3.014, -2.991 | 2.000, 2.008, 2.008, 2.008 |
| `num_retractions` | 1, 1, 1, 1 | 1, 1, 1, 1 |
| with `SGLANG_TEST_REQUEST_TIME_STATS=1` | scheduler crash: `AssertionError: queue_duration=-3.013 < 0` | no assertion |

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/observability/req_time_stats.py`, `SchedulerReqTimeStats` only:

- `queue_time` is now the total time spent in the waiting queue across every
  entry. Each queue entry opens a wait. The next forward, or a decode quick
  finish, closes it into `queue_duration_s`.
- Closing is idempotent, so chunked prefill (which calls
  `set_forward_entry_time` every chunk) doesn't add time.
- The accumulator is named `queue_duration_s` because `__setstate__` clock-rebases
  every field ending in `time`.
- `__getstate__` sends the accumulated value and folds in a wait that is still
  open, since the tokenizer side cannot close it.
- `reset_prefill_retry_time()` clears the accumulator, keeping today's
  "retried prefill is measured fresh" semantics.
- `convert_to_duration()` uses `get_queueing_time()` in all three disagg modes.

Deliberately unchanged:

- `wait_queue_entry_time` / `forward_entry_time`, and every scheduling decision
  that reads them: priority FCFS ordering, priority preemption,
  `SGLANG_REQ_WAITING_TIMEOUT`, the LoRA drainer. Keeping the original entry time
  instead would make a long-running retracted request hit the waiting timeout
  immediately.
- The `sglang:queue_time_seconds` histogram: still one sample per request, the
  wait before the first forward. On the real server above both runs added
  exactly 4 samples.
- Requests that are never retracted: `queue_time` and histogram samples are
  exactly equal (`==`) to the old implementation. Checked on 9,504 random
  non-retracted lifecycles. On the tokenizer side the value is now computed
  before the cross-process clock rebase, so the last float digits (~1e-10 s)
  can differ.

## Tests

Added `TestQueueTimeAcrossRetraction` to
`test/registered/unit/observability/test_req_time_stats.py`. Each case guards a
distinct failure mode:

| Test | Fails before this PR |
|---|---|
| `test_retracted_request_reports_total_queue_time` (meta_info + log line with test-mode asserts on) | yes |
| `test_queue_time_survives_clock_rebase_across_hops` | yes |
| `test_prefill_chunks_do_not_extend_queue_time` | yes |
| `test_decode_quick_finish_after_rebootstrap_counts_both_waits` | yes |
| `test_queue_time_histogram_keeps_one_first_wait_sample` | no: pins the histogram contract |
| `test_prefill_retry_reset_discards_earlier_attempt_waits` | no: pins the reset lifecycle |

The two contract tests were validated by mutation: re-sampling the histogram on
re-admission, or dropping the reset, turns each red. The same holds for renaming
the accumulator to end in `time`, closing the wait on every chunk, and dropping
it from the wire state (6/6 mutants killed).

Also run locally:
- all 303 unit tests touching time stats / scheduling: identical results before
  and after, except the 4 new tests (2 macOS-only failures in
  `test_swa_unittest.py` are pre-existing: HiCache native hash is Linux-only)
- 20,000 randomized scheduler lifecycles (unified / PD decode / PD prefill,
  chunked prefill, retraction, quick finish, retry reset) against a reference
  model: `queue_time >= 0`, equals the total wait, survives a two-hop pickle
  with different clock anchors, histogram unchanged, test-mode asserts never trip
- `pre-commit` hooks for the touched files (isort, ruff, ruff-format, codespell,
  registered-test checks)

Not covered end-to-end: the KV-full retraction and PD re-bootstrap paths. MLX
chains decodes without calling `update_running_batch`, so `SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT`
doesn't fire on Apple Silicon, and I don't have a PD setup. Both funnel into the
same `set_wait_queue_entry_time` call exercised above, and are covered by the
unit tests and the randomized check.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A: metrics/logging only; no model output or scheduling change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A: one float add and one bool per queue entry / first forward.

## Questions for reviewers

1. Should re-queue waits also be visible in Prometheus? Kept out of
   `sglang:queue_time_seconds` to preserve one sample per request; a separate
   metric seems cleaner if wanted.
2. For PD prefill optimistic retries this keeps today's behaviour (only the
   final attempt's wait is reported). Happy to accumulate across attempts instead.
3. Related but out of scope: re-stamping `wait_queue_entry_time` on retraction
   moves a preempted request behind newer same-priority arrivals and makes it the
   next preemption victim. I can open an issue if that's not intended.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests.
- [x] Update documentation: no user-facing docs describe `queue_time`; semantics are documented on the field.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results: N/A (see above).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

title: [NPU] Fix device mismatch in SWA mask for DSpark verify graph capture
author: iridiumine
body:
## Motivation

DSpark verify reuses `DFlashVerifyInput`, so `_is_dflash_verify()` routes it into the `seq_lens_cpu` branch of the SWA mask update in the NPU attention backend. Unlike DFlash (whose target verify graph runs through the NPU graph runner with on-device `seq_lens`), DSpark's verify graph goes through `decode_cuda_graph_runner`, which passes a CPU tensor (`forward_batch.seq_lens.cpu()` during capture, `buffers.seq_lens_cpu` on replay). Comparing it against the on-device `swa_indices` buffer raised:

```
RuntimeError: Expected all tensors to be on the same device. Expected NPU tensor, please check whether the input tensor device is correct.
```

This crashes the target model at graph capture time, so DSpark cannot run on Ascend NPU with hybrid SWA layers.

## Modifications

One-line fix in `ascend_backend.py` (`_apply_cuda_graph_metadata`): move `seq_lens_int` to the backend device before the SWA mask comparison:

```python
seq_lens_int = seq_lens_cpu[:bs].int().to(self.device)
```

- No-op for the DFlash path (its `seq_lens_cpu` is already on-device).
- Side benefit: DSpark now also gets the correct SWA mask window (`seq_lens_cpu` = prefix + block_size), so draft KV positions stay unmasked instead of being masked out by the prefix-only `seq_lens`.
- The copy runs in replay prep (outside the captured graph) and moves `bs × 4` bytes, so the performance impact is negligible.

## Accuracy Tests

No impact — this change only fixes a crash at graph capture time (device placement of metadata tensors); it does not alter any compute logic. On devices where capture previously succeeded (DFlash path), `.to(self.device)` is a no-op.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No impact — the added transfer is a host-side `bs × 4` byte copy executed outside the captured graph (~µs level), and it is a no-op when the tensor is already on-device.

title: [DSV4] fix: keep the TileLang JIT cache under SGLANG_CACHE_DIR
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

`third_party_cache_defaults()` gathers the compiled-kernel caches under
`SGLANG_CACHE_DIR` so that "a run's compiled kernels can be cleaned, warmed or
volume-mounted as one directory". It covers Triton, Inductor, the CUDA cubin
cache and FlashInfer. It does not cover TileLang, which keeps its own default of
`~/.tilelang/cache`.

That matters for DeepSeek-V4, whose MHC prenorm kernels are TileLang. Everything
that warms a deployment reads the one directory: the docs, an image bake, a JIT
cache pushed to object storage. The most expensive compile in a DSV4 cold start
is not in it, so every fresh container pays for it again.

## Modifications

Add `TILELANG_CACHE_DIR` to `third_party_cache_defaults()`, pointing at
`$SGLANG_CACHE_DIR/tilelang`. `redirect_third_party_caches()` runs at
`import sglang`, well before anything imports TileLang, and it uses
`os.environ.setdefault`, so an explicit user value still wins.

Also list `~/.tilelang/cache` in `_log_legacy_kernel_cache_dirs`, which is the
existing one-line notice for cache directories sglang no longer writes to.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable. This moves where compiled artifacts are written; it does not
change what is compiled or executed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The deployment shape this is for: take the `~/.cache/sglang` a warm run
produced, wipe every compiled-kernel cache on the machine, restore only that one
directory, and start. This is what an image bake or a mounted cache volume looks
like.

`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, 4x GB300, TP4:

| | time to first HTTP 200 | MHC prewarm |
|---|---|---|
| before | 472.7 s | 246.6 s (recompiled) |
| after | 134.5 s | 2.6 s (cache hit) |

Before the change the restored directory carries sglang's own JIT cache but not
TileLang's, so the MHC kernels are rebuilt on every cold container. It is 246.6 s
rather than a full 286 s because the sglang-side half of the cache did come back.

A plain cold start with no restored cache is unaffected by this PR on its own.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Notes for reviewers

Two consequences worth a release note, which is part of why this is a draft:

- **One-time recompile on upgrade.** Anyone whose `~/.tilelang/cache` is already
  warm, baked or mounted starts from an empty `$SGLANG_CACHE_DIR/tilelang` and
  pays the compile once. The legacy-directory notice points at the old path but
  does not migrate it. Happy to add a copy-on-first-use instead if that is
  preferred.
- **No more cross-framework sharing.** Other TileLang users on the same box
  previously shared `~/.tilelang/cache` with sglang. After this they do not,
  which is better isolation but costs disk and loses the reuse.

Also worth deciding: whether the JIT-cache warming tooling needs to be re-run so
the new `tilelang/` subdirectory is collected. Without that, this PR makes the
cost collectable but nobody collects it.

title: fix: stop shadowing the DSpark shared-experts fusion guard
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

`DeepseekV4ForCausalLMDSpark` defines `shared_experts_fusion_disable_reason`
twice. The second definition wins, so the first one, the only one with the NPU
branch, is dead code:

```python
    @classmethod
    def shared_experts_fusion_disable_reason(cls, hf_config, quant_config):
        if _is_npu:
            return (
                "NPU DSpark ModelSlim weight loading does not support mapping "
                "shared experts into fused expert slots."
            )
        return DeepseekV4ForCausalLM.shared_experts_fusion_disable_reason(...)

    @classmethod                                   # <- this one shadows it
    def shared_experts_fusion_disable_reason(cls, hf_config, quant_config):
        return DeepseekV4ForCausalLM.shared_experts_fusion_disable_reason(...)
```

The effect is that on NPU, shared-experts fusion is not disabled for the DSpark
draft even though the guard was written to disable it. Per the message that
guard carries, NPU ModelSlim weight loading cannot map shared experts into
fused expert slots, so the draft ends up fusing experts on a path that does not
support it.

CUDA is unaffected: both definitions fall through to the same base
implementation there.

The NPU-aware version arrived in #33676 alongside the plain one from #33312; the
overwrite looks like a merge artifact rather than an intentional revert.

## Modifications

Delete the second, shadowing definition. No other change.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable on CUDA, where both definitions were equivalent and behavior is
byte-identical.

I do not have NPU hardware, so the restored branch is not exercised here. It
restores the behavior #33676 intended; an NPU reviewer confirming that intent
would be the right check before merge.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. Dead-code removal with no CUDA behavior change.

title: Fix disagg PP MTP for GLM-5.2
author: nvpohanh
body:
Supersedes #39052 while @nvjullin is OOTO. The original two commits are preserved with Julien as their author; this branch rebases the change onto current `main` and addresses every review comment on the original PR.

## Motivation

GLM-5.2 could not run disaggregated PP prefill with MTP because:

1. PP + speculative decoding was rejected outside NPU even though the prefill path already forwards PP proxy tensors from stages that do not host the draft.
2. The NextN draft is hosted on the last PP stage and borrows the target embedding, but only the first PP stage materialized and loaded `embed_tokens`.
3. The PP ring dropped the draft model's DSA IndexShare seed (`dsa_topk_indices`), which could make decode ranks diverge between eager and CUDA-graph paths.
4. NIXL needed to map each heterogeneous PP prefill stage to the corresponding layer span in an unpipelined decode worker's MLA pool.

## Modifications

- Allow single-layer EAGLE with PP only for disaggregated prefill on the DeepSeek/GLM model path that supplies the last-stage draft embedding. Decode/null PP + speculative decoding and unsupported model families remain rejected.
- Materialize and load `embed_tokens` on the last DeepSeek/GLM PP stage when speculative decoding is enabled.
- Preserve `dsa_topk_indices` through PP serialization and reconstruction.
- Map heterogeneous plain-MLA NIXL transfers through one destination-index dispatcher, while retaining layer-ID/positional pairing for other layouts.
- Add regression coverage for PP/MLA transfer mapping, PP/EAGLE validation, embedding ownership, and DSA seed round trips (including the `None` case).

## Accuracy Tests

Negative control on the exact parent commit (`f539c1fc65e3a0de79b2a0d08805b096fdc85865`): launching the same GLM-5.2-NVFP4 PP4 disaggregated-prefill configuration with EAGLE steps 3 on a GB300 failed before server readiness in `check_server_args`:

```text
AssertionError: Pipeline parallelism is not compatible with overlap schedule, speculative decoding
```

This confirms that PP4 prefill with EAGLE did not start before this PR; the failure is the pre-change non-NPU PP + speculative-decoding restriction removed by this change.

GLM-5.2-NVFP4 on GB300 with Dynamo router:

- Prefill: 1 worker, PP4, EAGLE steps 3
- Decode: 1 worker, TP4, EAGLE steps 3
- GSM8K: 1,319-example dataset, 20-shot (1,299 scored examples), `--max-tokens 16384`
- Model revision: `53e0691e21895a3863a606dfd12910c69eba94ab`
- Hardware: 2 GB300 nodes in one NVL72 segment

| configuration | GSM8K score | decode acceptance length |
|---|---:|---:|
| PP4 prefill + TP4 decode, steps 3/3 | 94.69% (1230/1299) | 3.745 mean (3.00-4.00) |

This is within 0.76 percentage points of the original PR's 95.45% steps1/steps3 result. The decode acceptance length is the mean of 143 scheduler samples and is higher than the original PR's reported 3.589.

## Tests

- `BLACK_NUM_WORKERS=1 SKIP=no-commit-to-branch pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure`
- Targeted PP/MLA, PP/EAGLE, embedding-ownership, and PP DSA round-trip unit tests on the GB300 validation container: 28 passed, 264 deselected, 32 subtests passed.
