title: fix(dsv4): support R3 capture and MXFP4 online updates
author: bobboli
body:
Replaces #38282, which GitHub auto-closed when its base branch was deleted and recreated.

## Summary

- Capture logical expert IDs from DeepSeek V4 HashTopK before logical-to-physical remapping for R3 replay. Mask CUDA-graph padding, disable target capture from draft modules, and reject the unsupported HashTopK waterfill/capture combination.
- Synchronize CUDA IPC tensor imports in the weight updater before returning to the producer, including flattened buckets and other tensor load formats.
- Support repeated TRT-LLM MXFP4 online loads: permute expert weights in place, retain checkpoint-layout scale parameters, and maintain separate shuffled scale copies with stable kernel addresses. Pass unsigned byte views at the FlashInfer packed-FP4 call boundary without changing load parameters.
- Register the GEMM1 clamp limit as a non-persistent buffer so memory offload preserves it.
- Keep the padded-row Triton fast path off CPU tensors.

## Current rebase (2026-10-02)

Rebased the PR-only commits onto `sglang-miles` at `6c94e57f9ff5b84ba9746f5983ff13ce7e84c68b`. Current head: `0f0a367bad0d693ed8af044316111c25d919ed67`.

- `091bc49cf3`: restore the capture helper's original API, keep device checks at launch sites, validate routed MXFP4 hardware before model construction, and make the flattened-bucket helper's exception-only return contract explicit.
- `ec8a0fbf1c`: integrate upstream expert padding and input prequantization with hot reload. Recognize signed packed weights when computing hidden size and clear padding before repeat shuffles. Adapt existing tests to the current loader/runtime-context interfaces.

## Experiment terminology

- **P1:** TE MXFP8 training with MXFP8 rollout.
- **P2:** TE MXFP8 training with MXFP4 weights × MXFP8 activations for rollout routed experts, without trainer-side QAT.
- **P3:** The P2 setup with routed-expert MXFP4 fake quantization during training; trainer GEMMs still use TE MXFP8.

## Review follow-up (2026-10-02)

`0f0a367bad` adds inverse-shuffle restore for partial MXFP4 updates, live layer-buffer ownership for the clamp, XPU-compatible launch guards, in-place activation constant refresh, and first-build-only allocator cleanup. Empty/weight-only/scale-only sessions failed all six new cases before the restore fix and pass afterward.

The source stack also passed an ARM/GB300 preflight: 69 Miles integration tests, 6 QAT GPU tests and 30 SGLang tests (7 HashTopK, 9 MXFP4 GPU, 5 FP8 ownership, 9 UE8M0). Checkpoint metadata, optimizer/scheduler/RNG state and rollout data-state were audited before the pending P2 resume. This preflight is not an end-to-end training pass.

GitHub CI remains gated on `run-ci`. The PR author's attempt to add it was denied by GitHub permissions; a maintainer must add the label.

## Validation of the preceding rebase

- **320 CPU tests passed**, run one test file per process: HashTopK (7), model loader (3), derived-weight cache (2), FP8 runner fallback (4), runner ownership/static buffers (5), MegaMoE (6), routed capture (5), UE8M0 requantization (9), and server arguments (279).
- **3 B300 GPU tests passed**: fresh-load versus hot-reload parity and storage-address preservation for aligned/padded expert sizes, plus real MXFP4 x MXFP8 forward/reload with standard and FlashInfer dispatch inputs.
- All applicable changed-file pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` passed.
- No new end-to-end RL run was performed after this rebase. These local checks do not establish a full GitHub CI pass.

The results below are historical, from earlier heads.

## FP8/MXFP8 activation-state follow-up (2026-09-23)

Commit `104716dc91` also fixes the TRT-LLM activation tensors introduced in the new base's FP8/MXFP8 path. These alpha/beta/clamp tensors were ordinary attributes, so the memory-saver static-state backup omitted them. Repeated postprocessing also replaced their storage even though CUDA graphs retained the old addresses. Register them as non-persistent buffers and copy into existing storage on reload.

Evidence: an isolated reproduction using the actual preparation and static-state export/import functions left the old clamp at zero after simulated storage loss; re-preparation created a different pointer holding 10. The same function-level check passes after the fix (restored values, stable storage, no checkpoint entries). The existing runner-ownership test fixture now also covers this lifecycle.

The prior `23837cdabf` source passed 7 HashTopK tests and the GPU MXFP4 hot-reload test on GB300, but an end-to-end P1 run subsequently exhibited repetitive output and could not collect valid training groups. The activation-state defect is confirmed; attributing the complete rollout failure to it still requires a new RL run. Updated-source integration job completed successfully on GB300: 51 Miles integration tests, 6 GPU MXFP4 QAT tests, and 12 SGLang tests (HashTopK, MXFP4 hot reload, and FP8 runner ownership/activation-state lifecycle). Changed-file pre-commit passed with `GITHUB_BASE_REF=sglang-miles`. P1 smoke, with all other source/config pins unchanged, collected valid normal-mode samples and completed one valid optimizer step (`ppo_kl=0`, rollout/train log-prob absolute difference 0.02877). It then failed with host-memory OOM during trainer CPU offload; this is not a three-step end-to-end pass. The first `actor_train` timer was 703.9 seconds, not a steady-state performance measurement. P1 retry subsequently **passed all three optimizer steps** and exited successfully (1:03:47), with the same source pins and training settings and additional host-memory diagnostics. `actor_train`: 699.8 / 127.0 / 105.5 seconds; `ppo_kl=0` for all three steps; train/rollout log-prob absolute difference 0.02852 / 0.02860 / 0.02731. No host or CUDA OOM was observed in this run. This does not establish the earlier host-OOM root cause: the physical nodes and Ray-head/PP-stage placement differed. P2 and P3 both failed during the initial SGLang autotune forward, before online weight sync or training: `ValueError: Unsupported trtllm-gen input tensor`. The MXFP4 method passed signed checkpoint parameters directly to FlashInfer instead of zero-copy unsigned-byte views; the same issue exists in the pre-rebase PR head. The idle outer launchers were cancelled. SGLang commit `f9cfbec2d2` fixes that boundary with zero-copy uint8 views, preserving signed load parameters and storage. The new real-kernel case fails with the original exception before the fix; after the fix, all 13 local B300 SGLang tests pass (including real MXFP4 x MXFP8 forward and reload). ARM preflight completed successfully: **70 tests passed** (51 Miles, 6 GPU QAT, 13 SGLang), exit `0:0`. P2 retry and P3 retry used `f9cfbec2d2` and subsequently failed at initial FP32 export quantization, as detailed below. The completed P1 run above used SGLang `104716dc91`; it predates this MXFP4-only follow-up.

## FP32 export compatibility follow-up (2026-09-23)

P2 retry and P3 retry passed SGLang initialization but failed during initial online weight sync, before any optimizer step: the UE8M0 blockwise-FP8 helper rejected Bridge's FP32 export (`[2048, 4096]` shared-expert weight). This is separate from the preceding packed-MXFP4 kernel boundary bug.

SGLang commit `becddd92ece674066025b3e132768391b658214a` accepts BF16 or FP32 without changing the quantization math or rounding through BF16. Both new CPU regression cases fail before the fix. After it: 9 CPU tests and 13 related B300 GPU tests pass; the actual failing shape produces byte-identical FP8 weights and packed scales for BF16 weights versus their lossless FP32 exports. Changed-file pre-commit passes with `GITHUB_BASE_REF=sglang-miles`.

ARM preflight completed (`0:0`, 4:35): **79 tests passed** (51 Miles, 6 GPU QAT, 22 SGLang).

### Completed direct-HF smoke, without Bridge #36

All three arms completed **three valid optimizer steps**, including repeated online weight updates and normal-mode rollout, and exited successfully. No host/CUDA OOM was observed in these successful runs; all nine logged `ppo_kl` values are zero, and loss/gradient norms are finite.

| Arm | Elapsed | Three actor_train timers (seconds) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | 1:03:47 | 699.8 / 127.0 / 105.5 |
| P2 | 1:04:46 | 698.6 / 122.6 / 115.9 |
| P3 | 1:04:32 | 704.2 / 118.8 / 141.3 |

Pins: Miles P1 `946b00a41c`, P2/P3 `f7c4529350`; unmodified Bridge `bridge` base `2e09c234a`; Megatron-LM `f2fc0efcb`. P1 used SGLang `104716dc91`; P2/P3 used `becddd92ec`, which adds the packed-MXFP4 boundary fix and FP32 UE8M0 input support. **P1 was not rerun at the final SGLang head.** All code was committed source; no runtime/site-packages patches or offline weight conversion.

Setup: Preview, TE MXFP8 training, native/cuDNN attention, 8 x 4 GB300, normal mode, R3 enabled, 4K response cap, eval disabled, GPU optimizer with CPU trainer offload; independent experiment records. P3's routed-expert QAT hook installation was confirmed in the runtime log.

This establishes that Bridge #36 is not required for this tested recipe. It does not establish long-run stability, eval quality, QAT benefit, or the cause of the earlier host-OOM failure. First-step timings include warm-up; the subsequent 105.5–141.3 seconds are below the historical 185-second reference-attention figure but are not a controlled comparison with the historical 82.6-second cuDNN result. This is targeted validation, not a full CI pass.

## Motivation

PR #38968 changed the Docker image WORKDIR to `/sgl-workspace`. title: [NPU][Bugfix] Disable pinned memory to fix DeepSeek-V2 DP-attention hang
author: iridiumine
body:
## Motivation

#36472 introduced the in-tree `NPUSRTPlatform` and made NPU machines resolve to it instead of the base `SRTPlatform`. Unlike the base default (`is_pin_memory_available=False`), the new class returns `True`, silently switching hot paths such as the next-token-logits copies and the xgrammar bitmask allocation to pinned memory with `non_blocking` H2D copies.

torch_npu's pinned-memory + async-copy semantics are not verified against CANN on this stack. The correctness of `non_blocking` H2D depends on a stream-ordering guarantee that has not been established for NPU, and under DP attention — where compute, copy, and HCCL communication streams run concurrently — inference intermittently hangs (deadlock) with DeepSeek-V2.

Two independent reproductions confirm this:

- The #36472 author observed DeepSeek-V2 hanging during normal DP-attention inference with pin_memory enabled.
- We reproduced the same hang on Ascend 910C under DP-attention retraction stress (`TestDPRetract`, i.e. `SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT=1` + a small KV budget).

Both hang and disappear with `is_pin_memory_available=False`. Since the per-step benefit of pinning is limited to KB-scale decode-path buffers, disabling it is the safe choice until the async-copy stream semantics are validated.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/platforms/npu.py`: force `is_pin_memory_available` to return `False`, restoring the pre-#36472 behavior. Re-enable only after the pinned-memory async-copy semantics are validated against CANN (optionally behind a debug env var first).
- `test/registered/unit/platforms/test_platform_interface.py`: align the NPU pin-memory unit test with the restored behavior.

## Accuracy Tests

Reran the `TestDPRetract` stress repro (DP attention + 4500-token KV budget + radix retract stress + regex/JSON constrained generation) multiple times on NPU: all passed with this change, while the server previously hung intermittently during DP-attention inference.

title: Fix unified HiCache physical transfers
author: ZYHowell
body:
> **Description corrected after merge** to match the merged code, following review https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39479#pullrequestreview-5405433075. Struck text is what this description originally said; **Corrected** is the behavior as merged; **Follow-up** is what https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42708 changes (not part of this PR).

Original PR: [#37496](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37496) — previous reviews and comments.

## Motivation

Unified HiCache must preserve index ownership and address lifetimes while device or shared host pages can move. Main now provides per-pool L2 translation, SWA load binding, device move gates, and Python SWA write-back demotion. This PR retains the remaining shared-host buffer and storage support while using those upstream contracts.

The preceding #39478 has merged. This PR now targets `main`; the conflict resolution preserves the existing head history and incorporates main `f404db94d425b1a10dd4954e9f9a70d6ecb65402`.

## Modifications

- Reuse main's L2 engine translation, ~~virtual-owner SWA allocation/rollback,~~ independent host-transfer move gate, deferred D2H batching, and sparse layer-ID span. Remove duplicate eager physical translation ~~and allocator reservation/event bookkeeping~~.
  - **Corrected:** SWA H2D targets are physical reservations (`alloc_physical` / `cancel_physical_reservation` / `free_physical`), not main's virtual-owner SWA binding. The allocator keeps that bookkeeping: `set_hicache_transfer_done_event` records the transfer-done events, and `_pending_hicache_load_pages` blocks page moves until the load is queued. That count covered only lazy pools. In the FULL/SWA/Mamba tri-pool the SWA pool floats and is not lazy, so its reservations were not counted. A Mamba allocation could then move a reserved SWA page before its load was queued, while the queued copy kept the old address. Main's binding path stayed in the code but became unreachable.
  - **Corrected:** as merged, free-page allocation (`_alloc_bind_fast_or_slow`, `alloc_physical`) also waited on the registered transfer-done events whenever a lazy hole existed.
  - **Follow-up:** removes the unreachable binding path, and the allocation-time wait. Compaction and frees keep their waits. It also counts the floating SWA pool's reservations, so they block page moves until the load is queued or cancelled.
- Preserve main's unified pool-shape support ~~and host-pool selection~~, removing the original extra storage-backend allowlist `{None, file, sim, mori, shm}` along with the superseded broad model/~~PP~~/I/O restrictions. Retain the direct external-cache-linker guard because that path bypasses the L2 translation/lifetime contract.
  - **Corrected:** host-pool selection changed. Only no storage backend, or `mori`, selects the shared page envelope, in every host memory mode. `file`, `sim`, `shm`, `mooncake` and the other backends use separate host pools, in cache mode too.
  - **Corrected:** for unified memory with HiCache, this PR added two argument-layer asserts: `--pp-size 1`, and lazy compaction (`SGLANG_DISABLE_LAZY_COMPACTION` unset).
  - **Follow-up:** removes both asserts. This is not a claim that pipeline-parallel serving is validated. The allocator's own lazy-compaction checks predate this PR and are unchanged.
- Support shared FULL/SWA host arenas in `buffer_only` for eligible two-ended layouts ~~except Mooncake~~, with byte-based staging admission, load reserve, occupancy, atomic prefetch allocation, ~~rank consensus,~~ and rollback.
  - **Corrected:** only a backend that selects the envelope gets the shared arena; in `buffer_only` that is `mori`. The shared-host allocation consensus collectives were removed before merge. Other consensus checks are unchanged.
- Keep Mooncake buffer-only startup on main's separate K/V host pools. Reject runtime Mooncake attachment to an already-created shared buffer arena before storage threads/distributed groups are created; restarting with `--hicache-storage-backend mooncake` selects compatible pools.
  - **Corrected:** the runtime rejection applies to every backend that needs separate host pools, not only Mooncake, and in either host memory mode. Attaching one of them at runtime to an existing envelope arena is rejected; main accepted that attach in cache mode.
- Store each unified page envelope as one UMBP object; ordinary MHA K/V and split-head object cardinality remain unchanged.
- Keep Python's upstream best-effort SWA demotion. Retain the Rust backup-action bridge, align failed-backup behavior to preserve FULL/descendants while dropping only SWA, and provide the resident/new FULL anchor segments required by main's SWA load-back controller.
  - **Follow-up:** the Rust backup-action bridge (a SWA write-back eviction barrier) fired only after the pending-node barrier from PR 39627 had already backed up any unbacked SWA window, and then ran a FULL write-back that SWA preservation does not need. The resident/new FULL anchor segments fed only the unreachable binding path. The follow-up removes both.
- Preserve bounded decode prefix matching across L1/L2/L3 and unified-storage error-to-miss cleanup. Remove an identical test left at the obsolete singular `kernel/` path.

~~Known inherited limitation: main already permits Mooncake in cache mode and selects a shared envelope for eligible FULL/SWA pools, but Mooncake's MHA metadata still expects two K/V pointers per page while that envelope supplies one. This raises even with `page_first`; an uncaught backup-worker exception can prevent ACK/release completion. This PR preserves that upstream cache-mode behavior and does not claim it is supported. The buffer-only fallback prevents the newly added shared-buffer support from extending the mismatch to main's working separate-pool path. Switching an existing shared buffer to Mooncake at runtime requires restart. Other untested backend/layout combinations are not claimed compatible.~~

**Corrected:** the limitation above does not apply to the merged code. In cache mode, Mooncake selects separate host pools, not the shared envelope. Other untested backend/layout combinations are still not claimed compatible.

**Corrected:** these merged behavior changes were not listed above:
- **Write-through host refill.** Under write-through, `insert_host` keeps host slots already filled by an L3 prefetch when the matching node has device KV but no host copy. This is a cache-mode change and starts no extra D2H copy. Buffer-only completion takes the staging path before `insert_host`. See https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39479#issuecomment-6006005597.
- **Load-back admission.** `PrefillAdder` takes a host lock on the selected host match from before `prepare_load_back`'s reclaim until `init_load_back` holds its own locks, and builds a FULL load-back spec. **Follow-up:** the FULL spec is built only for `SharedSWAPrefillBudget`, the budget that reads it. The host lock stays.
- **Joint reclaim quotas.** `evict_to_free_tokens` passes the FULL/SWA reclaim quotas together to one `evict(EvictParams(...))` call instead of `evict_for_alloc`. This also applies to unified memory without HiCache. See the comment linked above.
- **Host-pool retraction.** It is allowed for unified hybrid-SWA and for the decode radix cache.
- **Write-policy attach check.** Attaching storage with write_through over a write_back cache first runs `is_write_through_compatible`. Host trees that write-through cannot hold are rejected before any policy change. Buffer-only mode is not checked.

## Accuracy Tests

No model accuracy or serving runs were performed. Focused CPU contract tests passed, including the actual compiled Rust extension. Existing host-pressure/index-domain expectations were updated to the main contracts; no new permanent test cases were added.

**Follow-up:** https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42708 adds CPU regression tests for these mechanisms: physical reservations (including the tri-pool's floating SWA pool), allocation and transfer order, the transfer lifecycles, load-back admission, the write-policy attach check, envelope selection for every storage backend choice, host-pool retraction (including decode radix retraction with a shared prefix) and SWA write-back eviction. CPU only; no GPU, serving or performance runs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance runs or speedup claims. Main's move gate can defer compaction until transfers are acknowledged; main's D2H batching is retained.

## Test plan

- Focused existing host-pool, shared-buffer, index-domain, staged-transfer, and decode-lock tests: 63 passed, 1 CUDA skipped.
- Tree/prefetch selection: 163 passed, 164 CUDA skipped; the changed host-pressure and retraction contract tests subsequently passed (2 tests, 4 subtests).
- Compiled Rust SWA/load-back/backup/eviction selection: 30 passed.
- Temporary CPU probes passed for mixed resident/new FULL anchors into the SWA controller, native component-only fallback, and UMBP key cardinality; these are not backend end-to-end tests.
- Existing tombstone positive-write/completeness and buffer snapshot sanity cases: 4 passed, 20 subtests; all substantive assertions retained. Empty backup staging explicitly supplies zero occupied units. Existing pool/buffer/prefetch modules: 26 passed, 20 subtests.
- Temporary CPU probe passed for actual Mooncake metadata cardinality (separate FULL/SWA: two keys/two pointers; shared envelope: confirmed two-key/one-pointer mismatch), pool selection versus main, and rejection before attachment side effects. No Mooncake client/IO ran.
- Changed Python pre-commit hooks, targeted Rust crate Clippy/rustfmt, and `git diff --check` against main passed.
- UMBP's test module could not collect because `mori` is absent in the existing environment. GPU/serving, storage backend IO, multi-rank/multi-node PD, and performance/accuracy tests were not run.

## Checklist

- [x] Format changed code with applicable pre-commit and Rust checks.
- [x] Run focused existing unit tests and preserve their coverage under the upstream contracts.
- [x] Update the PR description for its current main-based implementation.
- [ ] Provide model accuracy and performance results (not run).
- [x] Follow existing pool/controller/tree ownership boundaries.

## Review and Merge Process

Prior discussion remains on the original PR linked above. This conflict fix preserves the current PR and branch history; review and CI must be evaluated against its new head.

title: [Fix][DCP] Localize widened KV ids in MLA retraction CPU backup/restore
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #38645 (related draft: #38790). On a PD decode node with `--dcp-size > 1`, `retract_decode` backs up the retracted request's KV through `MLATokenToKVPool.get_cpu_copy`, which indexes `kv_buffer` with the widened `req_to_token` ids. Ids past this rank's rows trip a CUDA device-side assert; in-range ones back up and restore the wrong token's row.

## Modifications

- `HostKVCache.maybe_dcp_kernel_indices` moves to `layers/dcp/layout.py` as a pure function `maybe_dcp_kernel_indices(indices, dcp_size, dcp_rank)` next to the other DCP index math; the HiCache MLA host pool and the PD retraction path both call it. Its whole-widened-page assert is dropped because a retracted prefix (`seqlen - 1` tokens) is ragged; the strided select only needs the run to start page-aligned. `test_ragged_run_is_rejected` goes with it.
- `MLATokenToKVPool.get_cpu_copy` / `load_cpu_copy` run their ids through it with `dcp_size = _write_loc_dcp_span`, so the unified pool's already-physical ids (`write_loc_is_dcp_resolved`) pass through untouched. Mamba/KDA state indices are not touched.
- Regression cases added to `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_decode_retraction_backup.py`: the DCP backup/restore round-trip fails on `main` with an out-of-range row index, and the resolved-pool case guards against double translation.

## Testing

- CPU unit tests: the new `TestDcpRetractionBackup` cases in `test_decode_retraction_backup.py` pass here and the round-trip case fails on `main`; `test_hicache_dcp_host_pool.py` index cases pass.
- 4xB200, Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B, PD TP2 prefill -> TP2/DCP2 decode (tokenspeed_mla, fp8 KV, page 64), forced retraction via `SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT=1 SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT_INTERVAL=6` on the decode node, 48 concurrent requests x 256 tokens, decode `--max-total-tokens 122880` so widened ids exceed the per-rank row count:
  - `main` (433c999d): CUDA `index out of bounds` device-side assert in `MLATokenToKVPool.load_cpu_copy` on the first round (~12 retractions in).
  - this branch: repeated 2-3 round runs, ~140-200 retractions each, no assert, all requests completed; per-token logprob delta vs a no-retraction reference within the batch-composition noise of a no-retraction rerun.
- Not addressed here: with forced retraction some resumed requests (~4/48 per round) degenerate into token repetition. This reproduces identically with `--dcp-size 1` on the same PD setup, so it is a separate retraction issue, not DCP.

title: [AMD][Bugfix] Fix vattn_asm HIP error 709 under CUDA graph capture on ROCm 10
author: chuyeh
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

#37465 puts EAGLE verify / draft-extend / q_len-1 decode on the gfx950 `vattn_asm` kernel, launched through ctypes `hipModuleLaunchKernel` on the current torch stream. On ROCm 10 images, `SGLANG_ASM_VERIFY_ATTN=1` fails during EAGLE verify HIP-graph capture:

```
RuntimeError: vattn_asm: hipModuleLaunchKernel failed: 709 (context is destroyed)
```

`hipModuleLoad` succeeded, so the kernel reports itself active, and the default stream (handle 0) still works. Only a torch stream fails — graph capture included, which is the path decode takes.

#### Root cause

ROCm 10 ships the HIP runtime (`_rocm_sdk_core`) and the toolchain (`_rocm_sdk_devel`) as separate wheels. Torch maps core's `libamdhip64.so.7`, which the unversioned `CDLL("libamdhip64.so")` does not match, so the loader takes devel's copy off `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` as a **second** HIP runtime: the module loads in devel while the stream belongs to core.

Unpatched, on MI355X:

| Image | torch | HIP runtimes mapped | `CDLL("libamdhip64.so")` binds | Fix needed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rocm720` | 2.9.1 | 1 | torch's, via the `/opt/rocm` symlink | no |
| `rocm724` | 2.11.0 | 1 | torch's, `torch/lib/libamdhip64.so` | no |
| `rocm10` | 2.11.0 | **2** | devel's, **not** torch's | **yes** |

So the trigger is the SDK split, not torch 2.11 — `rocm724` has torch 2.11 and one runtime — and the change is a no-op wherever the soname already resolves to torch's object. Same failure mode #30870 fixed for CUDA, where TileLang's `libcudart_stub.so` could win over the real runtime.

## Modifications

- `vattn_asm_gfx950/__init__.py`: initialize CUDA so torch's HIP is mapped, then bind ctypes to it with the existing `find_loaded_library()` helper from #30870 rather than to the SONAME. Ten lines in one function; no new private API, no second `/proc/self/maps` parser.

No disambiguation between the two ROCm 10 copies is included, because none is needed: only torch's copy is ever mapped. After `import torch`, after CUDA init, and after importing `aiter`, `unified_attention_3d_mtp` and `aiter_backend`, `/proc/self/maps` holds exactly one `libamdhip64`:

```
maps after torch import: [.../_rocm_sdk_core/lib/libamdhip64.so.7]
maps after cuda init:    [.../_rocm_sdk_core/lib/libamdhip64.so.7]
maps after sglang+aiter: [.../_rocm_sdk_core/lib/libamdhip64.so.7]
```

The devel copy only enters the process if something explicitly `dlopen`s it, which is precisely the bug being removed. Should a future image map both, `find_loaded_library()` is the single place to teach the preference, for CUDA and HIP at once.

## Accuracy Tests

`test/registered/amd/test_vattn_segplan_mi35x.py::TestVattnSegPlan::test_launches_on_a_side_stream_and_under_graph_capture` (`stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`) launches the kernel on a torch side stream, then captures and replays it in a HIP graph, checking both against the file's existing fp32 reference. It lives with the other gfx950 asm kernel tests and reuses their fixtures.

Verified on MI355X (gfx950):

| Image | Unpatched | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `v0.5.18-rocm10-mi35x-20260902` | `FAILED ... 709 (context is destroyed)` | `3 passed, 16 subtests passed` |
| `v0.5.19-rocm720-mi35x-20260913` | passes | `3 passed, 16 subtests passed` |
| `v0.5.18-rocm724-mi35x-20260825` | passes | `3 passed, 16 subtests passed` |

The ROCm 10 unpatched column is a negative control: reverting only `_hip_lib()` to `CDLL("libamdhip64.so")` makes the new test fail with exactly the reported 709, so the test guards the regression rather than merely passing. With the fix, ctypes binds `/opt/venv/.../_rocm_sdk_core/lib/libamdhip64.so.7`, the same runtime torch uses.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speed change: one extra library-path lookup, once per process, at kernel load. This restores the assembly verify path under ROCm 10 HIP-graph capture; the kernel and launch geometry are untouched.

title: [Fix] HiCache startup ImportError on the pinned kernel wheel
author: mmangkad
body:
## Summary

#35233 landed an AOT op and its caller in one PR, skipping the order [Update sglang-kernel](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#update-sglang-kernel) asks for. PR CI builds a PR-local wheel, so it went green. Main and scheduled CI run the pinned `sglang-kernel==0.4.7`, where any server that builds a registered host pool dies at startup on `ImportError: cannot import name 'get_device_accessible_ptr'`. That was 32 jobs in the last scheduled run.

Reverting re-breaks MI355X, since ROCm builds the kernel from this tree and is already running the fix, and it drops an op that has to ship anyway. So this takes the exception that section allows: check the op is there, keep an equivalent fallback until a released wheel catches up.

The CUDA fallback is the raw host address, which under UVA is the device alias, so nothing changes past one warning. ROCm gets no fallback, since the two addresses really do differ there and a missing op means a broken build, so it raises. The registered test goes through the same helper and skips without the op, and a new test checks that the aliased and fallback tables match on CUDA.

Once a released kernel carries the op and the pin moves, those skips run for real and the fallback can go or stay as skew insurance.

title: [Fix] Don't write conv state from the fused KDA verify kernel
author: mmangkad
body:
> Reland of #39219, which was reverted in #39405 because it was merged by mistake.

## Motivation

`fused_kda_conv_gating_verify` rolled the conv state back into `conv_state` at the end of the kernel. Every V tile loads that same Q/K conv history at entry, but only `i_v == 0` writes it, so a tile scheduled in a later wave reads what the owner already overwrote.

The writeback is also dead: verify is speculative, and the commit scatter sets `conv_state` from the selected intermediate window. `accept_lens` is at least 1, so `last_correct_step_indices` is never negative for a real request and the scatter always overwrites.

So the stores are removed rather than guarded. `conv_state` and the SSM state are read-only in verify.

## Modifications

| | |
| --- | --- |
| kernel | drop the 9 `tl.store(cs_base, ...)` at the end of `fused_kda_conv_gating_verify_kernel` |
| docstring | state ownership: conv and SSM state are read-only, the commit scatter advances them |
| tests | `conv_state` must come back untouched; output must not vary with CTA scheduling |

Reached only with `SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_KDA_VERIFY=1` (default off), on the KDA Triton verify path at `topk == 1`.

## How the race shows

H=1 with HV=16, so 16 V tiles share one Q/K history. Same inputs, against the unfused pair:

| | max abs | max rel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| full GB300, one wave | 2.98e-8 | 7.2e-3 |
| 8-SM green context, waves serialized | **5.0e-2** | **188** |

Removing the stores makes both configurations identical. The residual ~1 ulp is reduction-order difference and is unaffected by the fix.

## Accuracy Tests

Ling-3.0-flash BF16, 4x GB300 TP4, NEXTN, fused verify on. Full GSM8K, thinking on, `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, `max_tokens=8192`, 1 repeat.

| | score | stop | error |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before | 96.06% | 99.70% | 0.00% |
| after | 95.83% | 99.17% | 0.00% |

Unchanged — the gap is inside the ~0.55pp 1-sigma band at n=1319. The race is below eval resolution when the grid fits one wave.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same server, 8192 in / 1024 out at concurrency 1, 64 warmup, `--flush-cache`, 3 runs per arm. Accept length 3.01 on all six.

| | runs (tok/s) | mean |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before | 355.23, 361.47, 363.72 | 360.14 |
| after | 370.64, 369.38, 375.18 | **371.73** |

**+3.22%**, arms disjoint. The kernel does strictly less work with the stores gone.

## Checklist

- [x] `pre-commit` clean
- [x] 9 cases in `test_fused_kda_conv_recurrent_verify.py`; all 9 fail against the unfixed kernel
- [x] Accuracy and speed measured above

title: [Fix] Aggregate all IPC weight update responses
author: bojiang-li
body:
## Motivation

`update_weights_from_ipc` uses only the first collected scheduler response. If that response succeeds but a later worker reports failure, the tokenizer returns success, clears its preprocessing cache, and records the requested weight version. Reversing the reply order changes the outcome.

## Modifications

Use `FanOutCommunicator.merge_results` after either the paused or non-paused update path, matching the distributed/tensor update handlers. Every response contributes to success and diagnostics; tokenizer-side success actions only run when all replies succeed. This does not roll back weights already changed on successful workers.

Add a CPU regression covering both pause states, single-worker success/failure, all-success replies, and mixed replies in both orders, including cache and version side effects.

Related #35093 addresses rank-local tensor-update failures inside the scheduler, not this IPC tokenizer response aggregation.

## Accuracy Tests

- Before: the regression fails; in particular, both pause states report success and advance the version for `[success, failure]`.
- After: all 10 scenario combinations pass.
- Repository pre-commit checks pass for both changed files, including registered-test validation.

Local execution used Python 3.12 and loaded the complete production control module with unrelated serving imports stubbed. The actual IPC handler, `FanOutCommunicator.merge_results`, asyncio locks, and the committed test ran; only worker responses were simulated. No server, checkpoint-engine transport, GPU update, or model-output accuracy test was run.

Installed development environment test command:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python test/registered/unit/managers/test_ipc_weight_update_results.py
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run; this changes control-plane result handling, with no claimed inference performance improvement.

AI assistance: Codex investigated the issue, implemented the fix and tests, and ran local validation.

title: [Fix] Release NCCL on scheduler exit and let the ASGI server own shutdown
author: hnyls2002
body: ## Summary - A scheduler rank aborts its communicators in its own teardown instead of leaving them to process reclaim - The shutdown watchdog hands the exit back to the ASGI server instead of calling `sys.exit(0)` from inside an asyncio task ## Background - `run_scheduler_process` releases host buffers on the graceful path but never drops its process groups, so a clean stop logs `destroy_process_group() was not called before program exit` - `TokenizerManager.sigterm_watchdog` ended with `sys.exit(0)`. `SystemExit` is a `BaseException`, so it escapes the task wrapper and stops the event loop the ASGI server is awaiting on; the server's lifespan shutdown is never reached and every clean stop prints a `CancelledError` traceback at ERROR ## Changes **Release** - Add `abort_distributed_environment()`, called from `run_scheduler_process`'s `finally` on the graceful path, after `release_host_resources()` - Abort rather than destroy: `destroy_process_group` is collective and blocks when a peer is already gone, which on a shutdown path is the common case - Degrades in place rather than through a flag: returns early when the process group was never initialized or when torch exposes no `_abort_process_group`, and logs a warning if the abort itself raises **Handoff** - Add `TokenizerManager.set_server_stop_hook()`. The watchdog calls it and returns, cancelling its own tasks first so no pending `handle_loop` is reported as destroyed on the way out - Wired for all three in-process servers: uvicorn default, uvicorn SSL-refresh, and granian HTTP/2. Multi-worker paths re-import the app in child processes, so the parent's manager is not the one serving; Engine and gRPC own no server and keep the direct exit - The uvicorn default path builds a `Server` instead of calling `uvicorn.run()`, so shutdown has an object to ask **Visibility** - Name the scheduler pids still alive when the grace period ends, before they are SIGKILLed mid-release - `wait_for_gpu_release` reports how long it waited, so a slow release is no longer silent ## Test plan Shutdown probed on a single node at tp 1, 2 and 4, under the uvicorn default and under `--enable-http2`. Every configuration was run twice: once at the merge base, once at this PR. | per-shutdown log counts | merge base | this PR | |---|---|---| | `asyncio.CancelledError` | 1 | 0 | | ERROR tracebacks | 2 | 0 | | `destroy_process_group() was not called` | 1 | 0 | - Every run exits 0, with no hang, no `Task was destroyed but it is pending`, and no `NCCL abort on shutdown failed` - GPU memory returns to zero immediately after SIGTERM in every run, and teardown wall time is unchanged from the merge base --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :no_entry_sign: [Run #35020743172](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35020743172) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #35020742885](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35020742885) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :no_entry_sign: [Run #35020743337](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35020743337)

title: [misc] Fix tool-call index, graph padded-row count, and prefill-graph input_embeds refresh
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Summary

Five independent fixes in the OpenAI chat server, the CUDA graph runners, and the MoE runners. Each is one or two commits and stands on its own.

## Changes

**1. Non-streaming `tool_calls[i].index` is the call ordinal.**
`_process_tool_calls` numbered calls by the detector's `tool_index`, which for most detectors is the tool's position in the request. Two calls to the same tool therefore both got `index=0`, while the streaming deltas number them 0 and 1. The non-streaming path now enumerates the parsed calls. Regression test added in `test_serving_chat.py`.

**2. `num_token_non_padded` is only handed out when it is maintained.**
The decode graph runner allocated the `num_token_non_padded` slot unconditionally, wrote it at capture, and refreshed it at replay only under expert parallelism. Without EP the static ForwardBatch carried a stale capture-time count, while eager batches carry `None` (`ForwardBatch.init_new` only fills it under EP). `DecodeInputBuffers.create` and the dummy-run buffers now allocate the slot only when `enable_num_token_non_padded()`; the capture-time writes are guarded. Graph and eager batches now follow the same rule: no count unless it is live.

**3. The standard MoE path masks padded rows like the a2a path.**
`DeepseekV2MoE.forward_normal` and `forward_normal_dual_stream` pass `forward_batch.num_token_non_padded` into top-k, as `forward_deepep` already does. With EP and the standard dispatcher, padded rows of a CUDA graph batch are now routed to expert id -1 instead of real experts, which also keeps them out of the expert-distribution statistics. Without EP the count is `None` and routing is unchanged. The dual-stream variant is additionally skipped inside a breakable CUDA graph capture, matching the guard the hc path already has.

**4. Prefill CUDA graph replay refreshes the `input_embeds` slot from `input_ids`.**
When the outer forward calls the captured stack without `input_embeds`, the replay closure previously left the slot untouched and the graph read the previous batch's embeddings. It now computes them from `input_ids` via `get_input_embeddings()`.

**5. Deferred finalize accepts fp32 expert weights.**
FlashInfer >= 0.6.18 types the `do_finalize=False` weight buffer by content: bf16 for packed routing, the caller's dtype for unpacked routing. The fp32 -> bf16 bit reinterpretation in `_make_deferred_finalize_output` was only correct for older versions and would corrupt genuine fp32 weights; `moe_finalize_fuse_shared` already accepts both dtypes.

Also drops the unused `ngram_embedding_n/k` attributes from the decode graph runner.

## Behavior on existing models

- EP off: MoE routing is bitwise unchanged; the count is `None` on eager and graph batches alike.
- EP on with the standard dispatcher: padded rows in CUDA graphs are skipped instead of routed.
- `tool_calls[i].index` in non-streaming responses changes for detectors whose `tool_index` is the tool position, only when several calls appear in one response.

## Verification

- `test_serving_chat.py`, `test/registered/unit/model_executor`, `test/registered/unit/batch_overlap`, the dp-attention, LoRA MoE and EPLB unit tests: pass.
- Kimi-VL-A3B `test_vision_openai_server_a.py` (mixed image/text batch, decode CUDA graph, EP off): an earlier revision of this branch crashed with an illegal memory access in the fused MoE kernel because the graph ForwardBatch still carried the stale count; the current head passes, with outputs identical to `main`. The mixed-batch client was replayed six times.

title: [Fix][PD] Give prefill and decode their own RDMA NICs in disaggregation tests
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Summary
- PD tests pick one RDMA NIC pair without knowing either side's GPUs, so a decode server pinned with `--base-gpu-id` reaches its NICs across the socket boundary and its first KV transfer burns the full 300s `KVPoll.WaitingForInput` timeout
- `test_disaggregation_different_tp.py` drops from 1184s to 859s on CI once each side gets its own NICs

## Background
- `get_rdma_devices_args()` derived NICs from `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, but PD tests separate the two sides with `--base-gpu-id` and never set it, so every call landed in the blind-pair fallback and both sides shared one pair
- With four NICs in `SGLANG_CI_RDMA_ALL_DEVICES` that pair is `mlx5_1, mlx5_3`, both on NUMA 0, while decode runs on GPU 4-5 on NUMA 1; `nvidia-smi topo -m` reports `SYS` for every one of those paths
- Only the first request pays the timeout and the rest succeed, so the test stays green and the cost stays invisible

## Fix
- `get_rdma_devices_args()` takes an optional `gpu_indices` and maps an **absolute** GPU id to its NIC. Ids taken relative to a group base mapped every side back onto the first NICs, which is what crossed the socket boundary
- `PDDisaggregationServerBase.rdma_devices_for()` hands each server the NICs for the GPUs it actually occupies -- in the fixture's own `start_prefill` / `start_decode`, and at the 42 sites that override them
- Folds three device-selection helpers into one function (141 -> 57 lines), dropping a `len(gpu_indices) > 4` bail-out that silently disabled affinity and a `base_rdma_group` check that only emitted a warning

## Measured
Same node, same test class, only the device list differs:

| device list | decode NIC | eval latency |
|---|---|---|
| auto-detected, 8 devices | `mlx5_0, mlx5_4` | 2.47s |
| four devices, before | `mlx5_1, mlx5_3` | **301.33s** |
| four devices, after | `mlx5_4` | **2.10s** |

## Test plan
- `base-c-test-8-gpu-h20`: all three partitions green; `different_tp` 1184s -> 859s, and the `StagingRadixPrefillLargerTP` eval that used to take 301.3s now takes 3.87s with unchanged gsm8k scores
- `base-c` green on 8-gpu-h200, 4-gpu-h100, 8-gpu-b300, 4-gpu-b200, plus `base-b-test-2-gpu-large`
- `/rerun-test` on the label-gated files: `hybrid_attention`, `hisparse`, `decode_radix_cache_swa`, `inkling_mxfp8`, `dwdp_gpt_oss`, `decode_offload`

## Notes
- AMD disaggregation tests are unaffected: every class there resolves `start_prefill` / `start_decode` to its own file's implementation, which reads `cls.rdma_devices` -- none of them reach the fixture defaults this PR changes
- #39367 reports the same 300s deadline on this lane at the earlier `KVPoll.Bootstrapping` stage; whether it shares this cause is not tested here

title: [NPU][CI] Scope NPU nightly artifact dirs by image; fix stale glm5_2 case
author: pllimax
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

NPU nightly results are persisted to a shared directory tree whose prefix is derived only from the branch / workflow / run metadata. When the same test case is executed with different images inside one workflow run (CANN 9.0.0 vs CANN 9.1.0, and a3 vs a5), both runs resolve to the same directory, so the later run overwrites the earlier run's metrics, log and plog artifacts. This affects the multi-node POC suites (`deepseek_v4_flash`, `glm_5_2`, `kimi_k3`) that run on both CANN images, and it makes the persisted results impossible to attribute to an image.

While inspecting this area, the CANN 9.1.0 multi-node mix suite was also found to reference a test case file that no longer exists, so the job aborts before running anything.

## Modifications

Persist the image identity in the directory prefix:
- `nightly-test-npu-e2e-multi-node.yml` and `_npu-single-node-test-stage.yml` (nightly branch): append the image tag to the `workflow_name` path segment, e.g. `Nightly_Test_NPU--main-cann9.0.0-a3` vs `Nightly_Test_NPU--cann9.1.0-a3-nightly`. The tag is extracted with `sed 's#.*[/:]##'`, dropping the registry/repository part, and the segment is suffixed (not extended) so the existing segment-count based consumers keep working.
- The pod-side `RUN_LABEL` is derived from the output prefix, so `logs/log` and `logs/plog` are isolated as well, with no change to the Python or shell helpers. The PR (legacy) layout and `full-test-npu.yml` are untouched.

Fix the stale test case reference:
- `nightly-test-npu.yml`: the CANN 9.1.0 multi-node mix suite now points at `test/registered/npu/accuracy/glm5_2/test_npu_glm_5_2_w8a8_16p_gpqa.py`, matching the 9.0.0 mix suite. The referenced `w4a8` case no longer exists, so the job previously failed with `The testcase does not exit`.

Comment-only additions (no behavior impact):
- `python/sglang/test/ascend/e2e/test_npu_performance_utils.py`: document that `DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASH_DEFAULT_MODEL_PATH` is the default model used by the a5 cases.
- Both stage templates carry the same comment above the image-tag appending logic.

Not applicable: this change only affects CI workflow configuration and artifact directory layout, not model or kernel code.

title: [Fix] dLLM: Preserve prompt tails and literal mask tokens across prefix reuse
author: 0z5a
body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39592/files) against `main`.

dLLM prefix lookup can consume a partial prompt block and its synthetic masks when a cached prompt contains the same literal mask IDs. Literal mask IDs in a real prompt can also be denoised and emitted as generated tokens, causing KV accounting errors and a serving crash.

Bound cache lookup by complete real-token blocks and classify the request after matching its cache prefix. Carry an explicit committed-position mask into LowConfidence, JointThreshold and JointThresholdInDel so literal prompt IDs and previously emitted outputs stay immutable after retraction. Repeated denoising no longer subtracts the current block from the reported cached-token count. The change preserves autoregressive lookup and logprob boundaries.

The GPU/HTTP results below are historical qualification of the previous revision; they were not rerun for the October 10 refresh.

| Test | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Real RadixCache collision, five prompt tokens with block size 4 | Matches 8 tokens and skips the tail | Matches 4; tail preserved |
| SDAR HTTP prompt containing a literal mask in a full block | Service exits with KV pool overcount on baseline and initial lookup-only patch | Cold/hot requests complete; prompt remains intact |
| Prefix boundary, FDFO KV reuse, and literal-prompt algorithm regressions | Original boundary matrix: 122 failures out of 210 | 11 tests and 228 subtests pass |
| LowConfidence, FDFO, radix enabled | — | 8 prompt cases plus synthetic-mask collision pass |
| LowConfidence, explicitly synchronous (`--no-dllm-fdfo`) | — | Same 9 cases pass; exact output IDs/text match FDFO |
| LowConfidence, FDFO, radix disabled | — | Same 9 cases pass; exact output IDs/text match cache-enabled run |
| JointThreshold, FDFO, radix enabled | — | Same 9 cases pass; cold/hot IDs/text identical |
| JointThreshold, explicitly synchronous | — | Same 9 cases pass; exact IDs/text match JointThreshold FDFO |
| HTTP cached-token accounting | Negative counts during repeated denoising | Nonnegative and equal to the first traced prefix match |

HTTP tests use `JetLM/SDAR-1.7B-Chat-b32`, BF16, TP=1, Triton, CUDA graphs disabled, block size 32, threshold 0.95, greedy sampling, 32 new tokens, and `ignore_eos=true`. Hardware: RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell 24 GB; Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, sglang-kernel 0.4.7. Each configuration runs 19 actual `/generate` requests. An observation-only wrapper records cache matches after `Req.init_next_round_input`.

| Prompt length | Expected hot cache hit | Radix-disabled hit |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 31 | 0 | 0 |
| 32 | 32 | 0 |
| 33 | 32 | 0 |
| 63 | 32 | 0 |
| 64 | 64 | 0 |
| 65 | 64 | 0 |
| 129 | 128 | 0 |
| 65, including literal mask ID | 64 | 0 |

The collision test first caches a 33-token prompt followed by 31 literal mask IDs, then submits the original 33-token prompt. Its output matches a clean-cache request and only 32 tokens are reused. Unit tests additionally exercise both JointThreshold implementations and both scheduling modes. These results do not qualify CUDA graph execution or multi-block prefill.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dllm_fdfo_kv_reuse.py \
  test/registered/unit/dllm/algorithm/test_joint_threshold_indel.py \
  test/registered/unit/dllm/test_gemma4_renoise.py
```

Contributes to the prefix-cache / prompt-tail item in #39499. The post-cache phase ordering overlaps the prerequisite in #31586; this PR does not add its multi-block scheduler.

Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #39056280293](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39056280293)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end -->

<!-- pr-states:end -->



### October 10 review follow-up

Merged main `c55790d38ba0c41170cec8993e7a85d5c687149c` and addressed the remaining review items:

- Batch CPU-known committed lengths into the same pinned, nonblocking transfer as positions. LowConfidence uses `torch.where` to exclude committed positions. Algorithms read the declared ForwardBatch field directly, and test doubles provide it explicitly.
- Retraction phase selection and position masks include both prompt tokens and committed outputs, independently of KV residency.
- JointThresholdInDel uses the explicit immutable mask for state initialization and excludes those positions from mask counts and transfers, while retaining its contiguous-prefix fallback when metadata is absent.
- Existing registered CPU test files now contain regressions for a literal-mask cache collision, immutable literal prompts in synchronous/FDFO decoding, retracted outputs, repeated-pass cached-token accounting and InDel behavior.

All scoped pre-commit checks passed, including CI registry validation. CPU source execution passed 25 exact repository algorithm tests, committed-token phase/prefix controls over 72 prompt/output layouts, three actual position-branch controls and the repeated-pass cache-accounting guard. Negative controls reproduced the literal-prompt InDel failure; these tests also caught and corrected its mask-count/transfer path. This source-level run omits package initialization and native dependencies. Full registered-suite and HTTP reruns require the complete SGLang environment and were not executed in this refresh; no GPU performance or memory measurement is claimed.

## Motivation

`registered/disaggregation/test_disaggregation_dwdp_gpt_oss.py` flakes in CI at `setUpClass` ([example run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34963250954/job/104361598197)):

```
torch.distributed.DistNetworkError: The server socket has failed to listen on any local
network address. port: 45623, useIpv6: false, code: -98, name: EADDRINUSE, message: address already in use
...
RuntimeError: Rank 0 scheduler died during initialization (exit code: -3)
RuntimeError: Server process exited with code 1
```

`PDDisaggregationServerBase` pins distinct torch.distributed rendezvous ports for the two sides precisely to avoid this, and its comment says so:

```python
# Pin distinct nccl (torch.distributed rendezvous) ports below the
# ephemeral range; otherwise both sides derive them from get_free_port()
# and can race onto the same port, failing at init_process_group with EADDRINUSE.
cls.prefill_nccl_port = f"{int(base_port) + 300}"
cls.decode_nccl_port = f"{int(base_port) + 400}"
```

But this test overrides `start_prefill`/`start_decode` and rebuilds the arg lists from scratch, dropping `--nccl-port`. You can see it in the failing job's echoed command lines — neither has the flag:

```
command=python3 -m sglang.launch_server ... --disaggregation-mode prefill --tp 2 --dwdp-size 2 ...
command=python3 -m sglang.launch_server ... --disaggregation-mode decode  --tp 2 --dp 2 ...
```

Both servers therefore fall back to `nccl_port = get_free_port()` in `PortArgs.init_new`, which binds port 0, reads back an *ephemeral* port (45623 sits in the usual 32768-60999 range) and immediately releases it. Prefill and decode launch back-to-back, so the kernel can hand the same port to both. Prefill rank 0 loses the bind, rank 1's TCPStore client gets `Connection reset by peer`, and the scheduler dies during init.

The prefill side here is non-dp-attention, which takes the `PortArgs.init_new` branch that has no `wait_port_available` precheck, so nothing catches the collision earlier.

## Modifications

Drive the base fixture's launchers instead of reimplementing them — set `prefill_tp_size` / `decode_tp_size` / `decode_base_gpu_id` / `extra_prefill_args` / `extra_decode_args` and call `launch_all()`, matching the pattern in `test_disaggregation_basic.py`.

The resulting server command lines are unchanged apart from the added `--nccl-port` (prefill `11300`, decode `11400`). Those are outside the ephemeral range and don't collide with the decode side's dp-attention derived block (`11433`-`11439`), the bootstrap port (`11500`), or the HTTP ports. `launch_all()` additionally installs the subprocess fail-fast watcher, so a mid-test server death surfaces immediately rather than as a downstream timeout.

Net: -63/+25 lines, no non-test code touched.

## Note

`test/registered/disaggregation/test_disaggregation_dp_attention.py` has the identical latent bug — it also overrides both launchers and omits `--nccl-port`. Left out to keep this PR scoped to the test that is actually failing; happy to fold it in if reviewers prefer.

title: fix(function_call): buffer complete DeepSeek DSML invokes
author: kflansburg
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek V3.2/V4 streaming tool parsing can corrupt `function.arguments` when a partial non-string parameter changes serialization shape. The current detector emits a common prefix of provisional serializations, then slices the final serialization using the number of bytes already sent. If malformed inner JSON changes from an array/object to the raw-string fallback, the emitted bytes are no longer a prefix of the final value and the slice drops bytes from the middle.

This has been observed with large nested array arguments. It can produce syntactically invalid calls without raising an exception. vLLM avoids this class of failure by buffering a complete DSML invoke before parsing and serializing it.

A second problem surfaced once complete invokes were validated: when a closed invoke could not be parsed, the detector returned the raw DSML block as assistant content and dropped the call. In production this branch fired for roughly 4-6% of tool-bearing DeepSeek V4 requests, so agents received tool markup as text with no tool call, and that markup then poisoned the following turns. The detector now fails closed instead.

Supersedes the narrower partial-value fix in #36748 and provides a conservative alternative to #36339.

## Modifications

- Buffer each DeepSeek DSML invoke until `</｜DSML｜invoke>` arrives.
- Parse and serialize arguments once, then emit one `ToolCallItem` containing both the name and complete arguments.
- Validate the full XML or direct-JSON invoke body before mutating streaming state.
- Reject malformed outer parameter syntax and non-standard JSON constants.
- Fail closed on a malformed closed invoke: discard that invoke on its own, keep parsing, and let well-formed invokes before and after it still become calls with contiguous indexes. The prose ahead of the block is still released; DSML is never surfaced as content, in streaming, non-streaming, `finish()`, or the unexpected-exception path.
- Keep main's tolerance for stray prose inside an invoke body (text around the parameter tags is ignored and the call is still emitted). An invoke is only treated as malformed when the leftover text contains a DSML fragment, i.e. a parameter tag that did not match (unclosed, self-closing, missing `string=`), or when the body has no parameter tags at all. In those cases emitting the call would silently drop an argument, which main did; this PR drops the call instead.
- Hold trailing whitespace in the streaming buffer so the blank line ahead of a DSML block is trimmed regardless of delta boundaries, instead of leaking as content.
- Drop incomplete invokes at stream end while preserving preamble text.
- Reasoning parser: the DeepSeek V4 detector ended reasoning at the first `<｜DSML｜`, so a mid-sentence mention of `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` while thinking (the system prompt shows the model that tag) cut the block and returned the rest of the reasoning, tag included, as content. Add an opt-in `tool_start_at_line_start` to the base reasoning detector; DeepSeek V4 now interrupts only on the full `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` tag at a line start, matching the reference parser's `\n\n<｜DSML｜tool_calls` split. Streaming remembers the last streamed reasoning character so a tag at the head of a chunk still counts. Replaces the previously "accepted divergence" test with a chunk-invariance test. Tradeoff: a block that neither follows `</think>` nor starts a line stays in reasoning; that double format violation is not tolerated by the reference parser either, and a test documents it.
- When `--reasoning-parser` is configured, strip the reasoning detector's think start/end tokens from the free-text `excludes` of any tool-call structural tag. xgrammar's builtin tags forbid `<think>`/`</think>` in free text, but DeepSeek V4 sometimes emits an empty `</think>` before prose in non-thinking requests; with `SGLANG_TOOL_STRICT_LEVEL` set the grammar rejected that token, and under PD disaggregation (prefill samples unconstrained, decode enforces) the request aborted with `Grammar accept_token failed`. Observed in production. Consistent with the existing rule that the reasoning parser, not xgrammar, owns the reasoning prefix.
- Keep final-flush bookkeeping synchronized so arguments are not emitted twice.

## Accuracy Tests

No model output changes. Valid streaming calls are required to match non-streaming parsing. Malformed non-string values retain the existing complete-parse fallback to JSON strings. Malformed invoke structure now yields no call and no DSML rather than raw markup.

Behavior on the shapes discussed in review, for the same input at every chunk width:

| Invoke body | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `<parameter name="text" string="true">SF</parameter>` followed by stray prose | `emit({"text": "SF"})` | `emit({"text": "SF"})` |
| `<parameter name="text">SF</parameter>` (missing `string=`) | `emit({})`, argument silently lost | no call, no DSML in content |
| `<parameter name="text" string="true">SF` (unclosed) | `emit` with truncated, invalid `arguments` `{"text": "SF` | no call, no DSML in content |
| prose only, no parameter tags | `emit({})` | no call, no DSML in content |

`test_reasoning_parser.py` covers the DSML mention inside reasoning (one-shot and every chunk width), a mention followed by a real block, a line-start block without `</think>`, and the mid-line tradeoff case.

`test_structural_tag_excludes.py` covers stripping only think tokens across nested free-text sections and, when xgrammar builtin tags are available, that the `deepseek_v4` auto tag no longer excludes them.

CPU-only parser coverage includes valid nested arrays, malformed nested values, every fixed chunk width for both valid and malformed invokes, multiple invokes, malformed first and later invokes alongside valid ones, stray prose inside the body, unmatched parameter tags, direct JSON, incomplete stream finalization, unexpected parser exceptions, and non-standard constants.

```text
22 passed (test_deepseekv4_detector.py)
3 passed (test_structural_tag_excludes.py)
137 passed (test_reasoning_parser.py)
```

Command:

```bash
python3 -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/function_call/test_deepseekv4_detector.py test/registered/unit/function_call/test_structural_tag_excludes.py test/registered/unit/parser/test_reasoning_parser.py
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No model-forward or GPU impact. The parser removes repeated partial JSON parsing, serialization, and common-prefix scans. Tool-call arguments are intentionally delayed until the invoke closes.

- [x] Provide accuracy and speed impact.

title: ci: fix always-failing coverage job, add by-GPU-count view
author: alisonshao
body:
The Unit Test Code Coverage job has been red on every scheduled run since 2026-08-18. It's a step timeout, not a test failure: the unit suite finished in 9m45s on the last green day, just under the 10-minute cap, and has since grown to ~11k tests needing ~22 minutes. Caps raised to 45 min (step) and 60 min (job).

That last green run also reported `127 failed, 6294 passed` as a success, because `pytest | tee` takes its exit status from `tee`. This adds `set -o pipefail` and an explicit non-gating `|| echo`, so the job stays advisory on purpose and the counts show up in the step summary. Those failures are cross-test contamination from running the whole tree in one process (duplicate process-group init, leaked default device); CI proper runs one file per process, and the same files are green in `base-b-test-1-gpu-small`. Worth fixing separately.

Second half adds a runner-size view: a GPU Count Summary table, `--section by-gpu-count` with a per-backend/per-suite drill-down, a `Tests by GPU Count` job, and `gpu_count_summary` in the JSON export. Current numbers: 914 enabled 1-GPU registrations (590 CUDA), 146 2-GPU, 223 4-GPU, 200 8-GPU.

title: [Metrics] Fix PD latency histogram accounting
author: chromecast56
body:
Related metrics PRs: #38600, #40275. Each is independent and they can merge in any order.

## Motivation

On PD prefill workers, the first output reports `completion_tokens=0` while the per-request baseline starts at 1. The resulting negative delta reached `sglang:inter_token_latency_seconds` through the default histogram path, which writes bucket internals directly, and left negative bucket counts and sums. Negative, non-monotonic buckets break `histogram_quantile` and `rate()`. A decrease in reported tokens on decode workers had the same effect. Aborted requests with no output also recorded a TTFT sample.

## Modifications

- `metrics_collector.py`: `observe_inter_token_latency` ignores token weights `<= 0`. This is the single guard; the caller no longer checks too.
- `tokenizer_manager.collect_metrics`:
  - PD prefill workers never observe ITL.
  - TTFT is skipped only when the finish reason is an abort. Embedding, reward, and classify requests, and `max_new_tokens=0` scoring, still record TTFT.
  - The existing baseline reset on a token-count decrease is kept; the comment now describes only that case.

## Tests

Added `TestTokenizerLatencyAccounting` to `test/registered/unit/observability/test_ray_wrappers.py`, reusing its collector fixture on the default (`_histogram_cls = None`) path. 3 methods:
- TTFT is skipped only for aborts (subtests: abort on null and decode roles; embedding and zero-output requests still record);
- prefill never observes ITL (every bucket and the sum stay 0);
- a token-count decrease resets the baseline (all samples non-negative, count 2).

On `main`, all three fail: the abort subtests record TTFT, and the other two produce negative buckets (`-2` and `-8`). The embedding and zero-output subtests failed on the previous `completion_tokens > 0` gate. `test_ray_wrappers.py` passes: 36 tests.

title: [Fix] Fix GLM5 mHC PP forward
author: yilin-void
body:
# [Bugfix] Fix GLM5 mHC pipeline-parallel forward

## Motivation

GLM5 mHC layers carry their residual streams inside the widened hidden state.
The pipeline receive buffers therefore contain `hidden_states` without a
separate `residual` tensor. `Glm5NextModel.forward` currently assumes that every
incoming pipeline payload has a `residual` key, causing non-first stages to fail:

```text
residual = pp_proxy_tensors["residual"]
KeyError: 'residual'
```

Its outgoing payload also includes a `None` residual for mHC layers. This PR
aligns the model's PP inputs and outputs with the mHC hidden-state-only contract,
allowing GLM-5.3 Flash to run with PP4 in the tested environment.

## Modifications

- Select the PP payload contract explicitly using the model's `mhc` configuration.
- Receive and send only `hidden_states` on the mHC path.
- Preserve strict residual lookup and the two-tensor payload for ordinary layers.
- Leave mHC computation, final-layer contraction, normalization, and PP transport
  unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

### End-to-end GSM8K check

Tested `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` on the same four NVIDIA RTX 6000D GPUs,
comparing PP4 (`TP=1, PP=4`) with TP4 (`TP=4, PP=1`). Both runs used the same
source, checkpoint, and backend dependencies, changing only the parallelism
settings and their PP-specific options.

- Evaluator: `python -m sglang.test.run_eval`, chat API, with the normal model
  chat template and no manually inserted assistant `</think>` prefix.
- Dataset: a fixed 50-example GSM8K test subset with 5-shot prompting; test rows
  `[5:55]`, with rows `[0:5]` used only as demonstrations (zero-based indices).
- Settings: temperature 0, top-p 1, reasoning effort `low`, max output tokens
  8192, concurrency 4, and server seed 42.

| Parallelism | Correct | Accuracy | Normal stops | Truncated / failed / empty final answers |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| PP4 | 49/50 | 98% | 50/50 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| TP4 | 49/50 | 98% | 50/50 | 0 / 0 / 0 |

All 50 extracted numeric answers and per-question scores matched between PP4
and TP4. Both missed the same question by treating the break-even year as the
first profitable year. There were no evaluation retries; warmup and health-check
requests are excluded from the table.

This is a small-sample end-to-end regression check, not a full GSM8K accuracy
evaluation or a claim of token-by-token equivalence.

Tested revisions: SGLang main `a9bb4d7d` plus this fix (`392764b1`), checkpoint
revision `09b04e5e`, and the same frozen SM120 attention/quantization backend
dependencies in both runs (SGLang #38430, FlashInfer integration `b5804cfc`, and
`sglang-kernel 0.4.7`). These backend dependencies are not included in this PR;
the hardware test does not imply that this PR alone enables SM120 deployment.

The model implementation is unchanged since these tests. The newly added CPU
unit-test file was removed following review; this PR now changes only the model
forward implementation.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This is a correctness fix, with no performance improvement claimed. No dedicated
speed comparison or profiling was performed for this PR. Both PP4 and TP4 also
completed an ISL 8192 / OSL 1 smoke test (4/4 requests each); these are functional
checks, not performance results.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). Full `pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure` passed; the no-applicable-files hook was skipped.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). N/A per review: the newly added unit-test file was removed. End-to-end validation is reported above.

Small-sample accuracy results above; dedicated speed testing N/A for this correctness-only submission, with no performance claim.

title: [Fix] disaggregation: Clean-up and optimize the KV checksum implementation
author: ShangmingCai
body:
## Motivation

With `--disaggregation-enable-kv-checksum` on, a mismatch on one TP rank hangs the decode engine, and healthy traffic is aborted on several supported configurations. This PR fixes those paths so the flag can be turned on.

## Modifications

**All-reduce the mismatch decision.** Corruption is per rank, so a rank-local drop left the TP peers building different batches and hanging on the next collective. The drop set is MAX-reduced over `attn_tp_cpu_group` with `all_reduce_flags` before any request is aborted.

**Verify once.** The digest covers whole pages, and after a retraction the restored row's last page holds tokens the decode wrote, so re-verifying on resume was a false mismatch at `page_size > 1`. A request is digested when it first enters a batch and its expectation is then cleared.

**Ship a layout signature with the digest.** `kv_layout_signature(kv_args)` hashes the page size and the per-page KV and state item lengths; the prefill writes it into slot 1 of the `kv_checksum` row. A prefill with another TP width or a PP stage is admitted unverified with one warning instead of aborting every request. A prefill that wrote no digest is skipped silently.

**Refuse the decode-side radix cache.** The digest covers `[0, seq_len)` while the prefill then sends only `[decode_prefix_len, seq_len)`, so every prefix hit looks like corruption. The decode logs once at startup and runs without the checksum.

**Survive a metadata buffer count mismatch.** The aux buffers pair positionally, and the Mooncake and NIXL send loops walked the decode's list (Mori's TCP loop the prefill's), so an engine with one more buffer than its peer was an `IndexError` in a transfer thread. The loops stop at the shorter list and the prefill logs an error at registration naming the optional buffers that can differ. The decode resets the checksum row together with the bootstrap room when a metadata slot is freed, so a later occupant whose prefill writes no digest cannot read the previous one.

**Test hook.** `SGLANG_TEST_DISAGG_KV_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH_PROB` flips a decode rank's computed digest with that probability, drawn from a per-rank generator (the global `random` is seeded identically on every TP rank, so the ranks would otherwise inject the same requests). The in-CI raise is suppressed while it is set.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_kv_checksum.py`: new cases for the signature, the slot reset, verify-once, the reduced drop set, the signature in the prefill's metadata write, and the injector not tripping the in-CI raise. The CPU-only cases pass on a CPU box; the CUDA cases need a runner.
- `test/registered/disaggregation/test_disaggregation_kv_checksum.py` (new, `base-c` / `4-gpu-h100`): TP2 on both sides, because at TP1 the reduce is a no-op. Mismatches injected per decode rank at p=0.3 over 16 requests with a multi-chunk prompt: some must abort, some must complete, and both engines must stay up.

No GPU here; the CUDA unit cases and the e2e test need a runner.

- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: Fix corrupted chat prompts on mistral_common tokenizers (tool_choice auto never fires)
author: alisonshao
body:
On Mistral3 models, `tool_choice: "auto"` never produces a tool call — the model emits one token, EOS, and returns empty content. `tool_choice: "required"` works, which makes it look like a tool-calling bug. It isn't: the prompt is corrupted for every request.

`_render_and_encode_chat_template` renders the chat template to a string and re-encodes it. mistral_common tokenizers emit control tokens that have no text form, so that round-trip destroys them. Comparing the server's prompt token ids against `apply_chat_template(tokenize=True)` for the same request:

```
server:   ['<s>', '<', 's', '>[', 'A', 'VAIL', 'ABLE', '_TO', 'OL', 'S', '][', ...]   103 tokens
template: ['<s>', '[AVAILABLE_TOOLS]', '[', ...]                                       82 tokens
```

`[AVAILABLE_TOOLS]` (control token id 5) comes back as the letters `A`,`VAIL`,`ABLE`,`_TO`,`OL`,`S`, and a second BOS is prepended. The model never sees the tool block as a control structure. transformers warns about exactly this: `MistralCommonBackend.apply_chat_template(..., tokenize=False)` is unsafe and may lead to unexpected behavior. Please consider using `tokenize=True` instead and don't encode the output manually.

The margin is thin, which is why it reads as arbitrary: the first sampled token is `</s>` at logprob -1.413 with ` [` right behind at -1.476. `required` hides it by constraining the output.

Every request takes the text path because `_engine_prompt` sends text whenever the model `is_multimodal`, and Mistral3 carries a `vision_config`.

This patch probes once at startup whether the render-then-encode round-trip reproduces `tokenize=True`, and when it does not, encodes straight to ids and sends those. Requests carrying media keep the text path, since the multimodal processor still has to tokenize it to expand placeholders.

Verified on Ministral-3-3B (same `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration` class and tekken tokenizer as Mistral Medium 3.5):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `tool_choice: "auto"` | no tool call, 1 token generated | `get_weather{"location": "Paris, France"}` |
| prompt | 103 tokens, doubled BOS | 82 tokens, control tokens intact |
| plain chat, no tools | 21 tokens, reply began `<s>[EVAL]` | 12 tokens, clean reply |

The last row is the wider point: this degraded ordinary chat too, not only tool calls.

The probe discriminates correctly — Ministral-3-3B renders to 12 junk tokens against 4 correct ones (`<s>[INST]x[/INST]`) and is flagged lossy; Qwen3-0.6B round-trips to identical ids and keeps the existing path.
