title: [ROCm] fix: remove extra bf16 -> fp32 cast in jit grouped topk kernel path
author: RuibinCheung
body: ## Motivation On ROCm with `SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_KERNEL_GROUPED_TOPK=1`, every MoE layer pays an avoidable `bfloat16 -> float32` copy kernel on the routing bias. `select_experts` unconditionally converts `correction_bias` into the gating dtype whenever `_use_aiter and use_grouped_topk`: ```python if _use_aiter and use_grouped_topk and correction_bias is not None: correction_bias = topk_config.correction_bias_for_dtype(router_logits.dtype) ``` That conversion exists for `aiter_biased_grouped_topk`, which wants the bias in the same dtype as the gating logits. But when the JIT router is enabled, `biased_grouped_topk_gpu` returns from its `jit_grouped_gate` branch long before the aiter branch is reached, and that branch immediately converts the bias back: ```python return jit_grouped_gate( gating_output, correction_bias.to(dtype=torch.float32), ... ) ``` So a model that stores `e_score_correction_bias` in fp32 (GLM-5.2 does, deliberately — its bias sits at an offset whose spread is only a few bf16 ULPs wide) gets downcast to bf16 once, then upcast back to fp32 on **every call, for every MoE layer**. The consumer that wanted the bf16 copy never runs. The upcast is also redundant on its own terms: the Triton `moe_fused_gate` already accepts a fp32/fp16/bf16 bias and `_router_triton_kernel` widens it in-register on load, so no host-side copy is needed in either direction. Measured on GLM-5.2-MXFP4 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, 78 layers, 256 routed experts), MI355X / TP8 / conc 1 / ISL 100k / MTP: **76 extra kernel launches per target-verify forward, 0.32 ms/step.** Each launch is ~4 us of pure launch overhead for a `[256]` tensor. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py` — skip the downcast when the JIT grouped-topk router is the actual consumer: ```python # Only aiter_biased_grouped_topk wants the bias in the gating dtype. The JIT # router returns before it in biased_grouped_topk_gpu and upcasts the bias # in-register, so downcasting here would only buy it a per-call cast back. if ( _use_aiter and use_grouped_topk and correction_bias is not None and not envs.SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_KERNEL_GROUPED_TOPK.get() ): correction_bias = topk_config.correction_bias_for_dtype(router_logits.dtype) ``` Scope: - `SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_KERNEL_GROUPED_TOPK` is `EnvBool(False)` by default, so the default path is byte-for-byte unchanged — the aiter branch still receives the bias in the gating dtype exactly as before. - With the flag on, `correction_bias.to(dtype=torch.float32)` in the `jit_grouped_gate` branch degenerates to a no-op for an fp32 bias, and still converts correctly for a model that genuinely stores the bias in bf16. It is kept rather than deleted so the branch stays correct regardless of what dtype the caller hands it. - The CUDA grouped-fallback branch further down `biased_grouped_topk_gpu` has the same `correction_bias.to(...)` call and is left untouched. It was never affected by this downcast anyway, since the downcast is guarded by `_use_aiter`. ## Accuracy Tests The bias reaching `_router_triton_kernel` is now the original fp32 tensor instead of a `fp32 -> bf16 -> fp32` round trip, so if anything this removes a precision loss rather than introducing one. For a model whose bias is stored in bf16 the value is identical, since bf16 -> fp32 widening is exact. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Setup: GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MI355X (gfx950), TP8, ROCm 7.2.26015, torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.0, conc 1, ISL 100k, MTP with `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.61`, `SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_KERNEL_GROUPED_TOPK=1`. Numbers are steady-state means over decode steps 2-4 (steps 0-1 are skipped, they carry JIT warmup). Before, per `step[TARGET_VERIFY]`: | kernel | count | time | | ------------------------------------------------ | ----- | -------- | | `at::native::bfloat16tofloat32_copy_kernel_cuda` | 76 | 0.321 ms | Expected after: 76 -> 1 per verify (only the `logits_processor` one remains), about -0.32 ms/step. trace: ## Checklist - Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #35549170704](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35549170704) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #35549170601](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35549170601) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #35549170702](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35549170702)

title: [Fix] mem-cache: Budget the non-DSA EAGLE draft KV pool at its DCP-widened size
author: jiaqiang-dot-liu
body:
## Motivation

Under DCP a non-DSA EAGLE / MTP draft pool is allocated over the allocator's widened ids: `KVCacheConfigurator.loc_space_scale` is `dcp_size` for that draft worker, and `_derive_pool_sizes` allocates `max_total_num_tokens * dcp_size` draft rows per rank. `DefaultPoolConfigurator` prices the DSA draft term and the DFLASH draft term with `dcp_size`, but its non-DSA EAGLE / STANDALONE branch prices one row of the target's per-layer KV. For an MLA draft, whose latent is the size of the target's, that is `dcp_size` times too small: `max_total_num_tokens` comes out too large, and the static pools take `(dcp_size - 1)` draft layers' worth of KV per rank out of the memory that `--mem-fraction-static` leaves for activations and CUDA graphs. A GQA/MHA draft cannot be priced from the target's per-layer KV either way: `ModelConfig.get_num_kv_heads` replicates the target's KV heads over DCP but not the draft's.

This is the MTP + DCP deployment of MLA models such as DeepSeek-V3 / R1. On DeepSeek-R1 at TP8 / DCP8 the draft pool is 20.68 GB per GPU while the budget charges it 2.59 GB, so about 18 GB of the reserve is gone before the first request. The sizing code is shared by all platforms.

An MLA draft writes only its owner rows (`loc // dcp_size`), so most of its widened allocation is never written; #43599 sizes the MLA draft pool in physical rows. This PR does not change the allocation; it makes the budget price the draft rows the pool allocates today.

## Modifications

`DefaultPoolConfigurator`: price the non-DSA EAGLE / STANDALONE draft term as `dcp_size` rows per token, each at the draft's own per-layer KV size from `_compute_cell_size(..., dcp_size=1)`. For MLA that is the target's per-layer size; a GQA/MHA draft keeps its unreplicated KV heads. At `dcp_size == 1` nothing changes.

## Accuracy Tests

The patch changes only how many KV tokens the pools hold; no kernel or model path changes.

`test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_pool_configurator.py`: 71 passed, 36 subtests passed. `test/registered/unit/managers/test_dcp_logical_capacity.py`: 3 passed.

The new `test_eagle_dcp_replicated_draft_does_not_exceed_budget` runs an MLA model and a GQA model (8 KV heads, TP8) at `dcp_size` 1 and 4 and checks that the memory the pools take, with the draft at `dcp_size` rows of its own per-layer KV, stays within the budget and uses more than 99% of it. On `main` the MLA `dcp_size=4` subtest fails with `10907136 not less than or equal to 10000000`; pricing the GQA draft from the target's per-layer KV fails the GQA `dcp_size=4` subtest with `9157632 not greater than 9900000.0`.

## Pool Sizing Measurements

`amd/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4-v2` (61 layers + 1 MTP layer), MI355X, TP8, `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, default `--mem-fraction-static` (0.7718), with and without this patch. Numbers are TP0 startup logs with `--load-format dummy`. With the real weights at DCP 8 the token counts differ by fewer than 60 tokens (4,818,943 before, 4,330,064 after) and the free memory is the same.

| DCP | `max_total_num_tokens` before | after | Draft pool before | after | Free after pools before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5,035,505 | 5,035,505 | 2.70 GB | 2.70 GB | 63.43 GB | 63.43 GB |
| 4 | 4,842,479 | 4,618,980 (−4.6%) | 10.39 GB | 9.91 GB | 53.74 GB | 61.61 GB |
| 8 | 4,819,001 | 4,330,117 (−10.1%) | 20.68 GB | 18.58 GB | 43.69 GB | 61.76 GB |

"Free after pools" is the `Memory pool end. avail mem` line after the draft pool is allocated. Without the fix the unbudgeted draft rows take 7.9 GB (DCP 4) and 18.1 GB (DCP 8) out of that reserve.

The capacity change matches the layer count: the budget now prices `61 + dcp` layer-equivalents instead of `61 + 1`, and `4,842,479 × 62/65 = 4,618,980` and `4,819,001 × 62/69 = 4,330,117` match the measured values. The lower capacity is the cost of pricing the draft rows that are allocated today; the previous capacity was only reachable by spending the activation reserve.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The patch only changes how many KV tokens the pools hold; no kernel or scheduling path changes.

No end-to-end throughput comparison: DeepSeek-R1 with EAGLE and DCP does not serve on ROCm `main`, with or without this patch. The non-DSA NextN draft keeps `dcp_size > 1` (`DeepseekV2AttentionMLA.__init__` only resets it for DSA drafts), so `forward_absorb_rocm_core` sends `draft_extend_v2` into the DCP decode branch with `k_window=None`, and `AiterAttnBackend.forward_extend` fails on `k.shape` while capturing the draft-extend CUDA graph. Both builds stop there, with dummy and with real weights. Pool sizing happens before that point, so the measurements above come from the full startup path.

## Reproduce

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path amd/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4-v2 --trust-remote-code --tp 8 --dcp-size 8 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --load-format dummy
```

Compare the two `KV Cache is allocated` lines (target, then draft) and the `Memory pool end. avail mem` line that follows each, at `--dcp-size 1` and `--dcp-size 8`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — internal sizing correction, nothing user-facing to document.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [AMD] Resolving bug in per batch size graph capture due to multiple capture runs per batch size
author: mohbasit
body:
## Motivation

Per-batch-size CUDA-graph capture traces (`SGLANG_GRAPH_BATCH_CAPTURE`) assume
exactly **one** capture per batch size. That assumption was broken on **16 Aug
2026** by #31324 ([AMD][GLM5] dense k-only fast path), which made DSA models
capture **two** decode graphs per batch size (`dense` + `sparse`). #38993 later
generalized this to `AttentionGraphVariants`, but the trace bookkeeping was
never updated.

The capture loop walks `bs × lora variant × attention variant` and each
combination drives its own profiler cycle, while `on_trace_ready` indexed a flat
list of batch sizes. With DSA the cursor advances twice per batch size, so it:

1. **mislabels every trace** — the `dense` and `sparse` traces for bs=64 are
   written as `bs_64` and `bs_56`; and
2. **crashes the server** once the list runs out, halfway through capture:

```
File ".../runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py", line 786, in on_trace_ready
    bs = self._profile_bs_list[self._profile_bs_idx]
IndexError: list index out of range
```

Repro: GLM-5.2-FP8 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`), TP=8, MI300X,
`--enable-profile-cuda-graph` + `SGLANG_GRAPH_BATCH_CAPTURE=1`. The server dies
during `init_cuda_graphs` and never becomes ready. `UnoDecodeCudaGraphRunner`
hits the same bug via `record_nolora_graph` (two LoRA variants), independent of
ROCm.

## Modifications

Replace the positional cursor with the identity of the capture being recorded:

- `_profile_bs_list` / `_profile_bs_idx` → `_profile_trace_tag`, set by
  `_capture_one_stream` before each capture and read by `on_trace_ready`.
  No indexing, so the profiling path can no longer raise.
- New `_set_profile_trace_tag(bs, stream_idx, variant_label, attention_variant)`
  appends only the parts that vary, so **single-variant models keep the existing
  `bs_<n>` filenames byte-for-byte**. DSA models gain a suffix:

```
DecodeCudaGraphRunner_bs_64_dense_rank0.json.gz
DecodeCudaGraphRunner_bs_64_sparse_rank0.json.gz
```

The tag is set in the shared loop rather than in `capture_one_shape`, because
five subclasses override that method (`FrozenKVMTP` discards the variant args
outright) while all of them inherit the loop.

## Tests

Unit (`test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_decode_cuda_graph_runner.py`,
CPU): dual dense/sparse naming, `bs_<n>` back-compat, tag composition, and a
regression case asserting more flushes than batch sizes no longer raises.

| Model | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GLM-5.2-FP8 (DSA) | crash at bs 7 of 12 | 192 traces (12 bs × dense/sparse × 8 ranks) |
| GLM-5.2-FP8 + MTP | crash | 736 traces; target split dense/sparse, both EAGLE draft runners unchanged |
| DeepSeek-R1-0528 | 160 traces | 160 traces, **filenames unchanged** |
| Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-FP8 | 96 traces | 96 traces, **filenames unchanged** |

The MTP run confirms scope: only the DSA target runner gains suffixes, while
`EAGLEDraftCudaGraphRunner` / `EAGLEDraftExtendCudaGraphRunner` keep `bs_<n>`.

title: [CI] Fix missing elfutils headers in CUDA 13.4 DeepGEMM build
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

The CUDA 13.4 nightly image build fails while compiling DeepGEMM's DeepJIT exception handling with `fatal error: elfutils/libdwfl.h: No such file or directory`. title: [Fix] HiCache: carry registered Mamba slot side states (Qwen4-Exp PLE) through the host tier
author: JarJarBeatyourattitude
body:
## Motivation

`MambaPool.register_slot_state` attaches state that lives in the **same physical checkpoint slot** as `conv`/`temporal` but is neither per-layer nor a field of `mamba_cache`. Qwen4-Exp registers two of them (`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py`, `_init_mamba_pool`): the PLE short-conv window `[num_slots, 10240, 9]` bf16 and the PLE N-gram token history `[num_slots, 2]` int64.

Every other mover of a slot already carries them:

| mover | carries side state |
|---|---|
| `MambaPool.copy_from` (device CoW) | `sibling.copy_slots(...)` |
| `MambaPool.clear_slots` (fresh slot) | `sibling.reset_slots(...)` |
| `MambaPool.get_cpu_copy` / `load_cpu_copy` | `sibling.get_cpu_slots(...)` / `load_cpu_slots(...)` |
| `MambaPool._iter_transfer_state_entries` (RDMA / PD) | `sibling.iter_transfer_state_entries()` |
| **`MambaPoolHost` (HiCache L2/L3)** | **no** |

`MambaPoolHost` reaches into `device_pool.mamba_cache.conv` and `.temporal` directly, so a checkpoint written to the host tier loses those rows. Nothing zeroes them on the way back either: the load-back path allocates its destination slot in `MambaComponent.prepare_load_back`, which sets `req.kv.mamba_pool_idx` directly instead of going through `HybridReqToTokenPool.alloc_mamba`, so `mamba_needs_clear` stays `False`. **A slot restored from the host tier therefore keeps the previous occupant's PLE state**, and `_prepare_ple_batch` prepends that other request's token history to the batch.

## Measurement

Qwen4-Exp (`Qwen3.8-Flash-Next`, 36 GDN + 12 full-attention layers) on 1x RTX PRO 6000, sglang `2929a399` + a LoRA-enablement delta only (nothing in `mem_cache/`), served with:

```
--enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-size 96 --hicache-write-policy write_through \
--hicache-mem-layout page_first --hicache-io-backend direct \
--max-mamba-cache-size 48 --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer --page-size 64
```

Every component of a Mamba checkpoint was fingerprinted on both legs of the host round trip. Four restores:

| component | restored correctly, before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `temporal` (GDN SSM state) | 4 / 4 | 4 / 4 |
| `conv0` (GDN conv state) | 4 / 4 | 4 / 4 |
| `ShortConvPool.ple_short_conv` | **0 / 4** | **4 / 4** |
| `NGramPool.ple_ngram` | **0 / 4** | **4 / 4** |

Verbatim from the trace of one restore, before the change:

```
backup   from device slot 19 : ngram = [11, 321]
before   destination slot 29 : ngram = [310, 279]     <- the previous occupant
after    destination slot 29 : ngram = [310, 279]     <- unchanged by the restore
                               temporal, conv0 : exactly the backup's values
```

## Cost

184,336 bytes per checkpoint against 58.8 MB of conv+SSM state, i.e. **0.3%**. At `--hicache-size 96` the host pool goes from 945 checkpoints to 942 (`size_per_token` 58,834,944 -> 59,019,280, confirmed on the running serve).

## What is in the change

- `pool_host/mamba.py`: collect the registered entries at init; one pinned host buffer per entry, with its own dtype and its own slot axis; both transfer legs; the L3 whole-page payload; host capacity accounting.
- `pool_host/mamba.py`: refuse the zero-copy storage metadata paths (`get_page_buffer_meta`, `is_stride_page_aligned`) when side states are present, rather than silently omitting them; reject a page written by an older build with a clear error instead of failing inside a reshape half-way through a restore; and handle one flat page now holding components of different element sizes (an int64 row can start at a byte offset its own dtype cannot be viewed at).
- `memory_pool.py`: `get_ngram_context` is read once per forward **before** the decoder-layer loop, so unlike `short_conv_layer_cache` it has no per-layer barrier of its own. Since the host tier now restores side state on the first Mamba layer's transfer, it waits for that layer.

A model that registers no slot side states takes an unchanged path: `slot_state_entries` is empty, no buffer is allocated, `get_size_per_token` is unchanged and both legs are a no-op (covered by a test).

## Test

`test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_mamba_slot_side_states.py`, CPU, 5 cases:

```
python -m unittest test.registered.unit.mem_cache.test_hicache_mamba_slot_side_states -v
```

- the round trip through the real `backup_from_device_all_layer` / `load_to_device_per_layer` call sites (the CUDA conv/temporal kernels are stubbed; the side-state legs run for real),
- the L3 page carries the rows and restores them,
- `get_size_per_token` accounts for them,
- a short page is refused rather than half-applied,
- a model with no side state is unaffected.

## What this does NOT fix

**This is not a fix for #39830.** On the same build, with this change applied and verified live, a host-restored prefix still produces wrong output: 0/10 usable answers against 10/10 cold and 10/10 device-hit on the same prompts in the same process. A watchword planted at token ~0 of the prompt is recalled 3/3 cold and 3/3 on a device hit and **0/3 out of the host tier**, while 48 of 48 sampled KV rows come back byte-identical to their backup — so the restored bytes are right and the model still cannot read the prefix it was given. That is a separate defect; the diagnosis so far is in #39830.

title: Fix DSA partial DP-TP mode log to use derived attn_tp_size
author: hunhokim
body:
## Motivation

When DSA runs in partial DP attention mode (`dp_size < tp_size`), the application gives a wrong log about sharded attention weights, as below.

```
[2026-09-17 02:01:26] DSA with TP mode is active, dp_size=2, tp_size=16, attn_tp_size=16, attention weights will be sharded across 16 ranks.
```

This is wrong: In this case, it should be `attn_tp_size=8`. With DP attention enabled, the actual attention TP width is `tp_size // dp_size // attn_cp_size`, so the log overstates the sharding.

## Modifications

- Compute the real value with `derive_attention_widths` from `runtime_context` (the same helper used for the parallel-width derivation) and log that instead of `cfg.tp_size`.
- Log-only change; no behavioral impact on parallelism.

## Accuracy Tests

Not necessary, since this is logging only.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Not necessary, since this is logging only.

#39652 (`13d593b6cf`) breaks the JIT build. It added the V4.1 row quantizers behind`#ifndef USE_ROCM` in `kv_layout.cuh`,

#37810 (`a813224e78`) breaks target-verify metadata. It added the `req_pool_indices_repeated` parameter to `_attach_unified_kv_prefill_meta` and updated one of its two call sites. title: fix: preserve QSA indexer state through HiCache
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

QSA compressed index keys live outside `full_kv_pool`, so the hybrid HiCache stack restores KV and Mamba state without restoring the indexer state used to select attention blocks. After device eviction, a prefix hit can therefore read valid KV through stale QSA block selections and produce incorrect output.

Related to #39830. The independent PLE slot-state fix in #39862 is **not included**; it is applied only to both builds in the full-model validation environment to isolate the QSA failure.

## Modifications

- Add a page-aligned QSA indexer host pool using the existing whole-page transfer and storage interfaces. Register it as a required KV sidecar for L2/L3, including packed MTP and separate draft pools.
- Wait on the existing layer completion event before indexer access. Fixed host budgets reserve space for the sidecar; old L3 entries without indexer data become cache misses.
- Add GPU regressions for indexer transfers, the consumer fence, and File L3 sidecar handling.

## Accuracy Tests

Six real B200 GPU tests pass, covering reordered physical pages, four transfer/layout combinations, File L3 reader recreation and missing sidecars, and packed target/draft indexer restoration. Removing the consumer fence makes the delayed-copy regression fail with 93.8% mismatched elements.

Full-model validation: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4, 1x B200, TP=1, ~12.5K-token prompts, three independent documents with five random codes each. Both builds include the same validation-only PLE patch from #39862. Every host/storage leg restores 12,480 tokens from the asserted tier.

| Retrieval leg | Baseline + PLE | QSA fix + PLE | QSA fix + PLE + NEXTN |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Cold | 15/15 | 15/15 | 15/15 |
| Device hit | 15/15 | 15/15 | 15/15 |
| Host restore after eviction | 0/15 | 15/15 | 15/15 |
| Device hit after host restore | 0/15 | 15/15 | 15/15 |
| File L3 after server restart | Not run | 15/15 | 15/15 |
| Device hit after L3 restore | Not run | 15/15 | 15/15 |

NEXTN uses 3 speculative steps, top-k 1, and 4 draft tokens. The validation-only [E2E reproduction script](https://github.com/alphabetc1/sglang/blob/4515250c443274eb861b15081bfe2f2fcbe1b51c/test/manual/test_qsa_hicache_e2e.py) is preserved in commit history, not included in this PR's final diff. It requires #39862 and a fresh output directory.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No standalone speed benchmark. The fix adds the missing indexer transfer bytes and uses existing per-layer completion events without adding a device-wide synchronization.

## Checklist

- [x] Changed-file pre-commit checks pass.
- [x] GPU regression tests added and run.
- [x] Historical E2E reproduction script linked above.
- [x] Full-model accuracy regression tested.
- [ ] Standalone speed benchmark (not run).
- [x] Follow SGLang code style.

title: [DP Attn] Fix crash for no token all-gather case
author: ByronHsu
body:
## Why?

With DP attention, DeepEP, DP LM head, `--moe-dense-tp-size 1`, and breakable prefill graphs, one request can crash an idle DP rank:

```text
One request routed to rank 0
  |
  +-> Rank 0: processes the prompt
  |
  +-> Rank 1: IDLE, 0 local tokens
        |
        v
      Prefill graph padding creates a dummy EXTEND request of length 0
        |
        v
      Empty batch falls back to eager execution
        |
        v
      Logits selection: cumsum([0]) - 1 = [-1]
      hidden_states[-1] -> IndexError on the empty tensor
        |
        v
      Worker fails; client connection closes without a response
```

## What?

- Preserve the original `IDLE` mode in logits metadata so idle ranks skip last-token selection. Attention and MLP execution keep the padded batch mode.
- Add one CPU regression test to the existing `test_mlp_sync_pad_unpad.py`.

## Verification?

Reproduced on upstream `main` (`2733afe54e`) with two H200s and `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8`. Both runs used the same source and environment; the after run applies only the logits fix. Runtime: PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`, Transformers `5.12.1`, and `sglang-kernel==0.4.7`.

Server command, from the source checkout with `MODEL_PATH` pointing to the local model:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=8 \
SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=256 \
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31899 \
  --tp-size 2 --dp-size 2 --ep-size 2 \
  --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head \
  --moe-dense-tp-size 1 \
  --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode auto \
  --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm \
  --attention-backend fa3 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.5 --context-length 8192 \
  --max-running-requests 32 --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 8 \
  --cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill 128 \
  --skip-server-warmup --watchdog-timeout 120 --random-seed 636278555
```

After the server is ready, send exactly one request without a generation health check first:

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:31899/generate \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "text": "The capital city of France is",
    "routed_dp_rank": 0,
    "sampling_params": {
      "temperature": 0,
      "max_new_tokens": 8,
      "ignore_eos": true
    },
    "stream": false
  }'
```

Observed on upstream `main`:

```text
Before: rank 1 raises IndexError at hidden_states[last_index];
        server exits and the client connection closes without a response.
After:  HTTP 200; 8 generated tokens; 0.137 s client request time.
```

The patched response starts with ` Paris. Which of the following is the` and reports `completion_tokens: 8`, `dp_rank: 0`. No warmup or generation health request was sent before the test request.

## Test?

- Regression command: `PYTHONPATH=python python test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_mlp_sync_pad_unpad.py TestMlpSyncPadUnpad.test_idle_rank_does_not_index_dummy_last_token`

  Observed against upstream main (`2733afe54e`) and this patch:
  ```text
  Before: FAIL - IndexError on the empty hidden-state tensor
  After:  PASS
  ```
- Full `test_mlp_sync_pad_unpad.py`: all 7 tests pass.
- Ruff, isort, and `git diff --check`: pass.
- CI on `a0d36515d1`: all 10 CPU partitions pass, including the regression above.
- Focused CUDA CI: [47 DP-attention tests and 4 DP-attention graph tests pass](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35190648225), [15 breakable-graph tests pass](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35190656482), and [original-logprob tests pass](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35190664312).
- Remaining broad CI jobs: pending.

title: [Moe] Fix flashinfer_trtllm silently dropping swiglu_limit clamped SwiGLU activation
author: Dovis01
body:
## Motivation

Models with a clamped SwiGLU activation (e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash / GLM-5-Next, Qwen3-Next style) plumb the clamp limit through `FusedMoE(swiglu_limit=...)` -> `MoeRunnerConfig.swiglu_limit`. All MoE runner backends are supposed to honor it: `triton` passes it into the fused kernel, `deep_gemm` applies it via `silu_and_mul_clamp` / `_apply_swiglu_limit`, but `flashinfer_trtllm` **silently ignores it**.

The flashinfer_trtllm FP8 path only materializes `gemm1_clamp_limit` (the TRT-LLM kernel parameter), which stays `None` for models that use the `swiglu_limit` field. With no error and no warning, the expert activation degrades from the trained `silu(clamp(gate, max=L)) * clamp(up, -L, L)` (with L = 10.0) to a plain `silu(gate) * up`, which measurably hurts accuracy.

On GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 (blockwise 128x128 FP8, 288 routed experts, top-8, 1 shared expert, `swiglu_limit=10.0`), GSM8K 5-shot with only `--moe-runner-backend` varying:

| moe_runner_backend | GSM8K strict-match (runs) | mean |
|---|---|---|
| triton | 0.9356 / 0.9363 | 0.9360 |
| deep_gemm | 0.9249 / 0.9287 / 0.9295 / 0.9310 / 0.9340 / 0.9348 | 0.9305 |
| flashinfer_trtllm (before) | 0.9265 / 0.9280 / 0.9287 | 0.9277 |
| **flashinfer_trtllm (this fix)** | **0.9348 / 0.9371** | **0.9360** |

Before/after ranges do not overlap (within-group variance is ~0.2pp); after the fix flashinfer_trtllm matches the triton baseline exactly. fix https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/39797. Thx for finding this issue. @NolenLiang

## Modifications

Single-file change in `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py`, `Fp8MoEMethod._prepare_flashinfer_trtllm_activation_params()`: when `gemm1_clamp_limit` is not explicitly set, fall back to `swiglu_limit`.

Why here and not in the model code: this function is the only consumer that builds the TRT-LLM SwiGLU parameters (`gemm1_alpha/beta/clamp_limit`), so the two naming pipelines (`gemm1_clamp_limit` used by gpt_oss / bailing_moe_v3, `swiglu_limit` used by DeepseekV2MoE-family models) converge at a single point; `triton` consumes both fields independently (`gemm1_limit` and `swiglu_limit`), so setting both at the model level would change behavior of unrelated backends, while this fallback is scoped to the flashinfer_trtllm preparation only. Models that already set `gemm1_clamp_limit` explicitly (gpt_oss, bailing_moe_v3) are unaffected, and the same silent drop is fixed for every other model that routes the clamp through `swiglu_limit` (e.g. Qwen3-Next) whenever flashinfer_trtllm is used.

The TRT-LLM kernel natively supports the clamp: with `ActivationType.Swiglu`, `gemm1_clamp_limit=L` computes `X2 = clamp(X2, max=L)`, `X1 = clamp(X1, -L, L)`, `out = X2 * sigmoid(alpha * X2) * (X1 + beta)` (alpha defaults to 1.0, beta to 0.0), which matches the reference `swiglu_clamped` in `models/glm5_next.py` exactly. Verified against flashinfer 0.6.18 (`trtllm_fp8_block_scale_moe`, `Fp8QuantizationType.DeepSeekFp8`).

## Accuracy Tests

Model: `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (FP8, blockwise 128x128), 4x B200, TP=4/EP=4. Launch (only `--moe-runner-backend` varies between runs):

```bash
 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --tp-size 4 --ep-size 4 --mem-fraction-static 0.75 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend trtllm --dsa-decode-backend trtllm \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm \
  --context-length 16384 --disable-radix-cache \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --served-model-name glm-5-next-fp8
```

Eval (lm-evaluation-harness, `local-completions`):

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args "model=glm-5-next-fp8,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer_backend=None" \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 \
  --gen_kwargs temperature=0,max_gen_toks=512 --seed 1234 --log_samples
```

Results (exact_match, strict-match):

| config | run 1 | run 2 | run 3 | mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| flashinfer_trtllm before | 0.9287 | 0.9265 | 0.9280 | 0.9277 |
| flashinfer_trtllm **after** | 0.9371 | 0.9348 | – | **0.9360** |
| triton (baseline) | 0.9363 | 0.9356 | – | 0.9360 |

Fixed server sanity-checked with deterministic generation (temperature=0) on GSM8K-style prompts before running the evals.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not affected. The change only materializes one extra per-expert fp32 tensor (`[num_local_experts]`, 288 bytes here) once at weight-load time; the hot kernel call is unchanged (the `gemm1_clamp_limit` argument was already being passed, as `None`). No throughput regression expected or observed.

title: [AMD] Fix AITER weight slicing for CP decode TP
author: AMD-yanfeiwang
body:
## Summary

AITER B-preshuffled RowParallel weights cannot be sliced directly along physical dim 1 because it does not represent a logical K shard. Restore the logical layout before slicing, then re-preshuffle and cache the rank-local shard for CUDA graph capture.

## Results

- GSM8K accuracy with `--enable-cp-decode-attn-tp`: **95.36%**.
- Fixed 8K/1K, concurrency 8 (80 requests): output throughput **438.93 -> 514.41 tok/s (+17.20%)**.

## End-to-end validation on DeepSeek-V4 prefill CP (with #34200)

`wo_b` is a `RowParallelLinear` and is not exempt from AITER B-preshuffling (only `wo_a` sets `skip_aiter_bpreshuffle`), so it is precisely the weight a physical dim-1 narrow would shard incorrectly.

Measured on top of #34200 head `86c7cb1c36` with this patch applied. Image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.19-rocm724-mi35x-20260916`, 8×MI355X, ROCm 7.2.4, `unified_kv_triton`, TP8/DP1, prefill CP8 (`--cp-strategy interleave --attn-cp-size 8`). Fixed 8K in / 1K out, exact lengths, two warmup waves per point. The two arms differ only by `--enable-cp-decode-attn-tp` and run back-to-back in one allocation on a single node.

### Effect of the flag under CP8 (flag off -> on)

Output throughput, token/s; higher is better.

| Checkpoint | Speculation | C1 | C16 | C32 | C48 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| DeepSeek-V4-Pro | EAGLE | 164.99 -> 206.56 (+25.2%) | 1299.91 -> 1524.30 (+17.3%) | 1731.80 -> 1967.71 (+13.6%) | 1986.08 -> 2362.87 (+19.0%) |
| DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 | DSpark-5 | 271.08 -> 318.21 (+17.4%) | 1419.77 -> 1773.92 (+24.9%) | 1592.91 -> 1886.99 (+18.5%) | 1878.67 -> 2097.73 (+11.7%) |

Mean TPOT, milliseconds; lower is better.

| Checkpoint | Speculation | C1 | C16 | C32 | C48 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| DeepSeek-V4-Pro | EAGLE | 5.836 -> 4.617 (-20.9%) | 10.262 -> 8.537 (-16.8%) | 14.373 -> 12.157 (-15.4%) | 19.575 -> 16.081 (-17.9%) |
| DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 | DSpark-5 | 3.470 -> 2.930 (-15.6%) | 8.968 -> 7.323 (-18.3%) | 12.243 -> 10.407 (-15.0%) | 17.194 -> 13.315 (-22.6%) |

TTFT is unchanged by the flag (EAGLE C48: 2763 -> 2765 ms), confirming it is decode-only as designed.

### Correctness

- Mean accept length is preserved: EAGLE 3.524 -> 3.506; DSpark-5 at matched batch sizes 5.37 -> 5.30 (bs≈16), 5.57 -> 5.43 (bs≈32), 5.43 -> 5.41 (bs≈48). A mis-sliced `wo_b` would surface here first, since a corrupted target distribution collapses draft acceptance.
- All arms answer the sanity prompt correctly, and every request completed at every concurrency point across both checkpoints.
- `Enable CP decode attention TP` is emitted on all 8 ranks in the flag-on arm and on none in the control arm.

The full three-way comparison against pure TP8 (no CP) is in the validation section of #34200.

### Note for reviewers

`_slice_cache` retains the re-shuffled shard for the lifetime of the context. That is what gives every CUDA graph capture a stable pointer, but it also keeps a rank-local copy of each sliced `wo_b` resident alongside the full weight. This was not an issue at `--mem-fraction-static 0.85`; worth being aware of at more aggressive settings.

## AgentX performance

This result requires the combined [#34200](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34200), [#39950](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39950), and [#40543](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40543) stack: HIP CP-v2 support, correct AITER B-preshuffled slicing, and removal of unnecessary CP decode-graph alignment.

Single-node DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 on 8×MI355X, TP8, DSpark gamma 6, static verify, 3,600 seconds per point. C4/C16 use GPU KV; C32/C48/C64 use HiCache. `PCP8 + DTP` enables `--enable-prefill-cp --attn-cp-size 8 --enable-cp-decode-attn-tp`.

Values are `TP8 → PCP8 + DTP`; latency is lower-is-better and throughput is higher-is-better. Deltas are relative to TP8.

| C | TTFT avg | TTFT p90 | TPOT avg | TPOT p90 | Total tok/s/GPU | Output tok/s/GPU |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 1.074 → 0.929 s (-13.5%) | 1.957 → 1.687 s (-13.8%) | 4.86 → 5.36 ms (+10.3%) | 6.09 → 6.07 ms (-0.3%) | 3,139 → 3,266 (+4.1%) | 23.62 → 24.52 (+3.8%) |
| 16 | 1.206 → 1.019 s (-15.5%) | 2.314 → 1.948 s (-15.8%) | 7.20 → 7.39 ms (+2.6%) | 10.56 → 10.21 ms (-3.3%) | 11,299 → 11,252 (-0.4%) | 78.59 → 78.49 (-0.1%) |
| 32 | 2.176 → 1.711 s (-21.4%) | 4.263 → 3.155 s (-26.0%) | 11.26 → 10.31 ms (-8.4%) | 16.93 → 14.38 ms (-15.1%) | 20,608 → 21,506 (+4.4%) | 130.79 → 136.27 (+4.2%) |
| 48 | 3.715 → 2.802 s (-24.6%) | 8.027 → 5.821 s (-27.5%) | 15.67 → 13.49 ms (-13.9%) | 21.03 → 17.52 ms (-16.7%) | 24,786 → 26,911 (+8.6%) | 172.36 → 187.30 (+8.7%) |
| 64 | — → 7.745 s | — → 18.477 s | — → 18.34 ms | — → 23.08 ms | — → 28,413 | — → 222.15 |

At C32/C48, PCP8 + DTP reduces average/P90 TTFT by 21–27%, reduces average/P90 TPOT by 8–17%, and improves per-GPU throughput by 4–9%. C64 reaches 28,413 total tok/s/GPU. All five PCP8 + DTP points completed with zero profiled request errors; C64 has no TP8 reference point.

title: [Unified Tree] fix: exempt host-locked aux nodes from the sanity_check host-LRU check
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

`sanity_check` raises while a storage-backup or load-back host lock is in flight.

The aux (SWA / Mamba) host-lock acquire delists its node from the host LRU on the
`0 -> 1` transition and relists it on `-> 0`, so the eviction walker cannot pick a
node whose host slice is being read. `sanity_check` did not know about that: it
required every host-only aux node to be in the host LRU, so any outstanding host
lock was reported as `<component> host LRU mismatch`.

`SGLANG_ENABLE_TREE_CACHE_SANITY_CHECK` defaults to on in CI, and
`InvariantChecker._check_tree_cache` runs it for hybrid-SWA / hybrid-SSM models, so
a HiCache backup in flight when the checker fires turns into an intermittent CI
failure that is not a product defect.

## Modifications

Exempt nodes with `host_lock_ref > 0` from the aux host-LRU membership comparison in
both tree cores. The exemption is two-sided on purpose: acquire delists a node, but a
node locked while already listed stays listed (eviction relists it at the device
tombstone), so both states are legal for a locked node.

The unlocked invariant is unchanged and still enforced -- an unlocked host-only value
missing from the LRU is still a violation
(`sanity_check_detects_a_host_only_value_missing_from_the_lru`).

`sanity_check_detects_a_host_locked_value_missing_from_the_lru` asserted the behaviour
being removed, so it becomes the positive case and now shares the fixture helper with
its two siblings. No production behaviour changes; this is a diagnostic-only fix.

## Accuracy Tests

- `cargo test --locked --lib`: 867 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored.
- `test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py`: 1256 passed, 1435 skipped, 70 subtests.
- Targeted repro on one H200, driving a real `UnifiedRadixCache` at the tree API:
  `sanity_check` passes before, during and after an outstanding storage-backup host
  lock (it raised during the lock before this change).
- Randomized lock-ledger stress (insert / match / split / lock / early SWA release /
  release / evict), 6 seeds x 150 steps for `full`, `full,swa` and `full,swa,mamba`:
  0 invariant violations in all three.

title: [Bugfix] Fix unified-memory compaction gates and pending page reuse
author: seokwoosong
body:
## Motivation

Lazy compaction in the unified-memory allocator moves live pages to close holes. A moved page's source cannot be reused until the forward that may still read it has finished, so it waits in `_pending_reuse`, keyed by that forward's done event. Two problems follow:

- When two move batches wait on the same event, the second batch overwrites the first batch's entry. The first batch's source pages are then neither live nor free, and that capacity is lost for the rest of the run.
- While a move gate is closed (a disaggregation or host transfer is reading pages), `_flush` returns early. Sources whose event has already fired stay out of the free list until the gate reopens, so the scheduler cannot see that capacity for the length of the transfer.

Separately, `schedulable_available_size` keys its memo on the gate of every chain member, so every query walks the whole chain and calls every gate, although only the neighbour whose holes it credits can change the answer.

## Modifications

- Batches pending on the same event share that event's `_pending_reuse` entry: one CPU id list plus a list of per-batch GPU tensors, concatenated once at drain.
- A flush while a move gate is closed still returns fired pending sources to the free list. It is non-urgent and copies nothing.
- `schedulable_available_size` keys its memo on the chain epoch plus whether each credited neighbour can drain now: the growth-side neighbour for an end pool, the low and high neighbours for a float. The neighbours are memoized on the epoch. The key and the credit share one predicate, `_drains_on_urgent_flush`.
- `FloatMultiEndedAllocator.make_room` checks the move gate before settling the in-flight forward. `_move_pages_and_rebind` and `_commit_move_batch` assert the gate is open, so a mover that skips the check fails instead of relocating pages under a transfer.
- Shared allocator test fixtures move to `python/sglang/test/unified_allocator_fixtures.py`, including the tri-pool fakes from `test_unified_tri_pool.py`. New regression tests cover shared-event batches, gated drains, gate-driven capacity and float movers under a gate.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated on an NVIDIA B200 against main `048b2a07f3`, with this PR rebased onto it:

- The new regression tests pass: `test_unified_pending_event_batches.py` (2 tests, 29 subtests), `test_unified_dynamic_gate_capacity.py` (10 tests, 15 subtests) and `test_unified_float_move_gate.py` (3 tests, 15 subtests). The 33 related existing test files (unified memory pools and radix cache, Mamba pool, streaming sessions, short-conv kernels) give the same results as main, with no failures.
- Together with #38229 and #42072, Inkling (`thinkingmachines/Inkling`, revision `test`) on the unified pool with `--enable-deterministic-inference`, 32 LongBench prompts: logprob match, prefill cache hit and decode cache hit are all at `avg_kl_div=0.0`. `test_inkling_unified.py` passes 9/9, including the unified-vs-static parity check.

These runs install no move gate (no disaggregation), so the gated paths are covered by the CPU regression tests only.

Earlier serving runs on H100 (unified memory, non-PD, no move gate installed; one hour per model at concurrency 32, on an earlier revision of this change): Qwen3.5-4B (FULL + Mamba), Mellum2-12B (FULL + SWA) and Inkling-0.6B (FULL + SWA + Mamba) served 96,539 requests with 0 request errors and 0 retractions.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Host cost of one `schedulable_available_size()` call per chain member (one sweep), real CPU pools with lazy compaction, single thread, median of 7 × 30,000 sweeps, two alternating rounds per tree. Both trees return identical capacities.

| Layout | Gate | main (µs/sweep, round 1 / 2) | this PR (µs/sweep, round 1 / 2) | ratio |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FULL + SWA | none | 1.031 / 1.039 | 0.601 / 0.600 | 0.58x |
| FULL + SWA | open | 1.088 / 1.116 | 0.631 / 0.625 | 0.57x |
| FULL + SWA + Mamba | none | 2.134 / 2.211 | 1.156 / 1.163 | 0.53x |
| FULL + SWA + Mamba | open | 2.303 / 2.396 | 1.228 / 1.211 | 0.52x |

These are allocator costs, not end-to-end throughput.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not applicable: no public option changes.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [Spec][PP] Fix hybrid recurrent-state commit and micro-batch pairing under PP x speculative decoding
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

#30775 enabled PP x speculative decoding (`SGLANG_ENABLE_PP_SPEC=1`). On hybrid linear-attention targets (KDA / GDN / Mamba-style recurrent state) it is currently incorrect in two independent ways, both found while validating PP + MTP across model families (tracking: #39634):

1. **Non-last PP stages never commit the accepted recurrent state.** The last stage commits KDA/Mamba state inside `run_eagle_verify`; earlier stages only run target verify and relay the result, so their recurrent state stays at the pre-verify value while the last stage advances. GLM-5.3-Flash PP2 + MTP: GSM8K 0.745 vs 0.990 without spec, accept length looks normal (3.5), so the bug is silent.
2. **With more than two stages the relayed accept result is paired with the wrong micro-batch.** The commit hook took its destination slots from the backend's active `forward_metadata`, which on a non-last stage still belongs to the previous forward (slot `(i-1) % N`), and the KDA verify scratch was written at positional rows `0..bs-1` that in-flight micro-batches overwrite before the relay returns. With PP2 `(i-1) % 2 == (i+1) % 2`, so both errors are masked; with PP4 the first concurrent batch crashes with `indices length mismatch: dst_indices_raw.shape[0]=7 vs step_indices_raw.shape[0]=12`, and after fixing only the destination the accuracy is 0.485.

Pipeline-parallel speculative decoding can receive verify acceptance after a later micro-batch has overwritten positional hybrid-state scratch. When `SGLANG_ENABLE_PP_SPEC=1`, hybrid verify scratch and the delayed recurrent-state commit therefore use request-pool stable rows; with the gate off, the existing positional / active-metadata path is unchanged.

## Modifications

- `scheduler_pp_mixin`: relay `accept_index` unconditionally (chains too). On non-last stages `_pp_spec_commit_relayed_accept` commits the acceptance relayed for that same micro-batch (same `commit_mamba_states_after_verify` the last stage uses) before `seq_lens` advances, then compacts the accepted KV. The scheduler snapshots each PP-spec micro-batch and clones `req_pool_indices` (the Mamba-track tensor is rebound, never mutated, so the snapshot shares it).
- Gating: `pp_spec_stable_rows_enabled()` (`layers/attention/linear/utils.py`) is the single predicate for the stable-row policy; kernels take `stable_rows=` from the backend instead of reading the env.
- Hybrid Mamba commit (`hybrid_linear_attn_backend`, `mamba_state_scatter_triton`): under the PP-spec gate, when the caller carries `req_pool_indices`, rebuild and translate destination state indices from the matching forward snapshot instead of the active `forward_metadata`; with the gate off, or without rows, the existing path runs.
- KDA / GDN verify (`kda_backend`, `gdn_backend`, `gdn_flashinfer`): the request-pool slot is the stable scratch row (padding still goes to the discard row); row selection is shared in `select_verify_intermediate_state_indices`. The FlashInfer GDN MTP kernel writes positional `0..B-1` and takes no row indices, so the PP-spec path uses a positional scratch and remaps to the stable rows after the kernel. KDA PP verify falls back from the FlashInfer kernel to Triton; ReplaySSM verify reads its source rows from the same stable mapping (`src_indices_raw` / `dst_indices_raw` across backends).
- Qwen PLE short-conv / n-gram side state (`ple_state_pool`, `qwen4_exp`) gets the same request-row pairing.

No change to the attention math or the acceptance algorithm; only where state is stored and how relayed results are paired.

## Accuracy / validation (GB300, GSM8K 200 questions, `SGLANG_ENABLE_PP_SPEC=1`, EAGLE/MTP steps 3 topk 1)

title: Fix/compressed tensors nvfp4 hopper
author: jlqibm
body:
## Motivation

On pre-Blackwell GPUs (SM < 100), every compressed-tensors NVFP4 checkpoint fails
at quant-scheme construction on the first attention linear -- it never reaches
weight loading:

| variant | group_size | strategy | failure today |
|---|---|---|---|
| `nvfp4` (w4a4) | 16 | `tensor_group` | `NotImplementedError: Current platform does not support w4a4 nvfp4 quantization.` |
| `nvfp4a16` | 16 | `tensor_group` | `ImportError` about `W4A16Sparse24` |

Two independent root causes:

1. **`_is_wNa16_group_channel` never checks `type == INT`**, so a weight-only
   4-bit *float* config satisfies it. It runs first, outside the
   `is_activation_quantization_format` gate, and short-circuits with `raise
   ImportError` for any non-`pack_quantized` format -- which is why `nvfp4a16`
   reports a misleading sparse-24 import error. vLLM has the identical missing
   check but escapes it by predicate ordering.
2. **No weight-only Marlin path exists for CT fp4 linears.** The only fp4 linear
   scheme, `CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4`, reports `get_min_capability() == 100` and
   calls `fp4_gemm` unconditionally.

The dense FP4 Marlin kernel already implements exactly what NVFP4 needs --
`group_blocks == 1` (gs=16) and E4M3 group scales -- and NVFP4 always carries a
real global scale. So NVFP4 can be served weight-only (fp4 weights, bf16/fp16
activations) on SM80+ with no kernel changes.

## Modifications

- **`compressed_tensors.py`**
  - `_is_wNa16_group_channel` now requires `type == INT`. This is narrower than
    reordering the predicates: int4 `pack-quantized` is INT by definition so it
    cannot regress, and it closes the trap for the next float4 variant instead of
    stepping around it.
  - New `_is_fp4a16_nvfp4` predicate dispatching `nvfp4a16` to the weight-only
    scheme.
  - The SM100 `NotImplementedError` becomes a graceful downgrade to the
    weight-only scheme with a `warning_once`, following the existing precedent two
    branches below where `_is_fp8_w8a8` falls back to `CompressedTensorsW8A16Fp8`.
  - A present-but-not-NVFP4 input quant still raises rather than silently
    downgrading.
- **New `CompressedTensorsW4A16Fp4` sibling scheme** with
  `get_min_capability() -> 80`, rather than vLLM's single-class `use_a16` flag.
  `get_min_capability` is a `@classmethod` resolved on the instance's class, so one
  shared class returning `<= 90` would silently lower the Blackwell gate for the
  real w4a4 path too. `has_input_global_scale` distinguishes a downgraded w4a4
  checkpoint (which carries `input_global_scale` on disk, dropped post-load) from a
  native a16 one.
- **`compressed_tensors_w4a4_nvfp4.py`** gains the Marlin branch in
  `process_weights_after_loading` / `apply_weights`. Three attribute fixes are
  prerequisites, since the prep helper reads what CT does not set: `params_dtype`
  (a missing value trips a raise), `quant_config` (the group_size guard is
  `if getattr(...) is not None`, so a missing attr means *no validation at all*),
  and rebinding `weight_packed -> weight`.

Note the global-scale inversion: compressed-tensors stores NVFP4 global scales as
divisors (`1/scale`) while Marlin wants the scale. Missing the inversion overflows
the bf16 dequant bias multiply to `inf`, zeroing all logits and emitting token 0
forever -- which is why the end-to-end checks below assert on coherent text, not
just a clean load.

No change to Blackwell behavior. MXFP4 is deliberately out of scope: the dense
kernel has no `group_blocks == 2` instantiation, its template cannot decode E8M0
scales, and it requires a non-empty `global_scale` that MXFP4 lacks. MXFP4 now
fails with an honest "no compatible scheme" instead of the sparse-24 `ImportError`.

## Accuracy Tests

End-to-end on H100 (SM90), offline `Engine`, greedy, prompt `"The capital of
France is"`. `downgrade` is whether the weight-only substitution
warning fired -- it must fire for a w4a4 checkpoint and stay silent for a16:

| model | TP | rc | dropped experts | downgrade warning | generation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| granite-5.0-20b nvfp4a16 | 1 | 0 | 0 | silent | `" Paris.\" We need to output the same sentence..."` |
| granite-5.0-20b nvfp4 | 1 | 0 | 0 | fires | `" Paris.\" We need to output the same sentence. So answer:..."` |
| granite-5.0-120b nvfp4a16 | 4 | 0 | 0 | silent | `" Paris. The capital of France is Paris..."` |
| granite-5.0-120b nvfp4 | 4 | 0 | 0 | fires | `" Paris. The capital of France is Paris..."` |
| granite-5.0-230b nvfp4a16 | 8 | 0 | 0 | silent | `". Question1: What is the capital of France? Answer1"` |
| granite-5.0-230b nvfp4 | 8 | 0 | 0 | fires | `". The capital of France is Paris. The capital of..."` |

The warning fires for every w4a4 checkpoint and stays silent for every a16
checkpoint at every TP size. No regression on the bf16 base, both fp8 variants,
or `w4a16-c4` (the int4 path most exposed to the `type == INT` change).

Also verified on real SM90 with no capability mock:
`nvfp4(w4a4) -> CompressedTensorsW4A16Fp4 has_input_global_scale=True`,
`nvfp4a16 -> CompressedTensorsW4A16Fp4 has_input_global_scale=False`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not a performance change -- this makes previously-unloadable checkpoints load.
Weight-only FP4 Marlin is the same kernel path `ModelOptNvfp4A16LinearMethod`
already uses on these GPUs.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No doc change: no new user-facing flag or option -- previously-failing checkpoints now load.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Tests added:

- `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_fp4_linear_scheme.py` -- 11 CPU scheme-selection tests (`register_cpu_ci`, `override_platform(is_sm90=True)`): SM90 downgrade for both variants, SM100 still selecting native `CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4` (guarding the Blackwell gate), int4 `pack-quantized` still selecting `CompressedTensorsWNA16` (guarding the `type == INT` fix), non-NVFP4 input quant raising, and the downgrade warning firing for w4a4 but not a16.
- `test/registered/kernel/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_fp4_linear_numeric.py` -- GPU numeric test for the weight-only NVFP4 dense Marlin path (`rtol=atol=0.04`), modeled on the existing `test_nvfp4_marlin.py`.
- The existing GPU numeric test `test/registered/kernels/ops/quantization/test_nvfp4_marlin.py` passes unchanged (4 passed).

title: [Fix] [CPU] memory: Honor cgroup memory.max when sizing CPU memory
author: ZailiWang
body:
## Motivation

Re-submit of #38260.

On CPU, sglang auto-computes mem_fraction_static from total host memory and does not honor container cgroup memory limits. This makes a single server reserve a huge KV-cache pool regardless of the actual model size, and makes it impossible to run multiple sglang containers on one host safely.

Added a `get_instance_memory_status` function which tries to retrieve the cgroup memory limit from /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max and memory status from /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.current . Existing CPU mem acquisition approach  psutil.virtual_memory().total is used as a fallback.

title: [Fix] Preserve inline instructions for Responses and Kimi K3 Messages
author: chromecast56
body:
Related entrypoints PRs: #39711, #39716. Each is independent and they can merge in any order.

## Motivation

Responses always moves an inline `developer`/`system` input into the leading system message. Appending an instruction to a conversation therefore rewrites the start of the prompt and throws away the whole cached prefix, which is common for agentic clients.

- **Controlled test on a production Kimi K3 deployment:** a ~50K-token Responses conversation hit 50,176 cached tokens when repeated or extended with a user turn. Appending one developer instruction dropped the hit to **0**. Replaying the original right afterwards hit 50,176 again, so the prefix was still cached.
- **Production:** after deploying this change on a production Kimi K3 deployment, token-weighted prefix-cache hit rate for `/v1/responses` went from **25.5% to 90.7%**, and from 12.9% to 92.2% for prompts ≥128K tokens. Chat Completions stayed flat (91.8% → 93.0%). This compares two 30-minute windows on 2026-09-18. They weren't matched, and the deploy included other changes, so treat it as supporting evidence rather than an A/B test.

Anthropic Messages already keeps inline system messages when the chat template renders them (#28906), but it probes the tokenizer's Jinja template. Kimi K3 renders with a native encoder and has no Jinja template, so K3 Messages requests are still hoisted.

## Modifications

- `OpenAIServingChat.supports_inline_system` is resolved once at startup from the renderer that actually builds the prompt: the native encoder allowlist (`spec_supports_inline_system`, currently `kimi_k3`) when a native encoder is active, `False` for a conversation `--chat-template`, and otherwise the existing Jinja probe (`detect_inline_system_support`).
- Anthropic Messages and Responses both read that attribute. Responses skips the system-message merge when it is set.
- Behavior change: Responses now keeps inline instructions in place for any HF Jinja template that renders mid-conversation system messages, the same rule #28906 applied to Messages. Messages now merges under a conversation `--chat-template` or a native encoder outside the allowlist, since the probed Jinja template is not what renders those prompts.
- #39518 made the same fix for DeepSeek V4.1 Messages but targeted the `dsv4.1` branch and was closed unmerged when that branch was deleted. Adding `dsv41` to the allowlist is a one-line follow-up once its encoder is checked.

## Tests

- `test_serving_responses.py::test_inline_instruction_keeps_history_prefix` (4 cases): the K3 and inline-Jinja cases fail on main because the instruction is hoisted. The conversation-template and dropping-Jinja cases pin the merge fallback; the conversation-template case fails if the resolver ignores `--chat-template`.
- `anthropic/test_serving.py::test_inline_system_support_comes_from_the_prompt_renderer` fails on main, where Messages probes a missing Jinja template and hoists.
- `test_serving_responses.py`, `test_serving_responses_stream.py`, `test_serving_chat.py`, and `anthropic/test_serving.py` pass.

title: [Fix] disaggregation: Preserve sampler customized_info across PD
author: aurickq
body:
## Why is this change needed?

Prefill samples the first output token, but its sampler-provided `customized_info` does not reach decode. For a sampler that copies each generated token into metadata, output tokens `[101, 102, 103]` currently produce:

```diff
- "sampled_token_ids_copy": [102, 103]
+ "sampled_token_ids_copy": [101, 102, 103]
```

Transfer this metadata through the existing P/D buffers using MessagePack and the existing NumPy/tensor codecs. Tensors are restored on CPU.

Transfer is disabled by default (`SGLANG_DISAGG_CUSTOMIZED_INFO_MAX_BYTES=0`), preserving the legacy buffer layout and registration messages. To enable it, upgrade both peers and set the same positive capacity, such as `4096`, on each. Invalid or oversized payloads fail only the affected request and are cleared before its abort response.

With transfer enabled, NIXL and Mooncake validate buffer sizes before writing and use the receiver's row strides. Decode-only speculative decoding can use wider hidden-state rows, and the optional trailing checksum buffer need not be enabled on both peers. Resumed requests keep their existing metadata rather than appending the prefill token again.

## Test Plan

- Reuse the existing customized sampler and three unified-memory P/D parity variants to check scalar and array metadata for every output token. Fixed the assertion hook to match the current parity fixture.
- CPU fixture check: the old hook silently accepted missing first-token metadata; the repaired hook rejects it and accepts complete metadata across all three variants. This verifies assertion dispatch, not GPU transport.
- Cover opt-in/legacy layouts, optional checksums, capacity and row strides, serialization failures, request-local abort/recovery, and metadata preservation during rebootstrap in existing unit suites.
- CPU regression suites: 510 tests and 412 subtests passed; 17 skipped.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks passed. GPU end-to-end validation is pending CI.

title: [Docs] Fix benchmark table column overflow in cookbook deployment panel
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Problem

On cookbook pages with a `benchmarks` prop, the Benchmark card renders one grid column per speed measurement. The GLM-5.3-Flash GB300 Low Latency FP8+TRT-LLM cell (added in #39213) has 6 measurements across 2 workloads, and since its isl/osl differ per row, the column headers become long strings (`in/out=1000/1000, max-concurrency=16`).

The grid uses `minmax(0, 1fr)` columns with `whiteSpace: nowrap` cells, so 6 columns shrink to ~79px each while the header text needs ~240px — the text overflows and overlaps neighboring columns, and the last column bleeds past the card edge.

Reproduce: open https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/GLM/GLM-5.3-Flash and select GB300 / Low Latency / FP8 / FP8 + TRT-LLM, then look at the Speed table in the Benchmark card.

## Fix

In `renderBenchTable` (`docs/src/snippets/_deployment.jsx`):

- `minmax(0, 1fr)` → `minmax(max-content, 1fr)`: a column can never shrink below its content
- wrap the grid in `overflowX: auto`: tables wider than the card scroll horizontally instead of overflowing

Tables that already fit (1–3 columns) render as before; the scroll container only kicks in when the content exceeds the card width.

## Verification

Local `mint dev` + headless Chromium:

- 6-column GLM-5.3-Flash cell: every column's rendered width now equals its content width (233–245px), no overlap, table scrolls inside the card
- 2-column (H100) and 3-column (GB300 High Throughput) cells: layout unchanged, no scrollbar
