title: [Fix] [NPU] attention: Use FIA TND for MLA prefix attention and add Gemma norm fallback
author: McZyWu
body:
## Motivation

Replace the ATB RingMLA implementation of MLA prefix-cache prefill with FIA TND so this path works without ATB. The formerly RingMLA-based prefix path now always uses two FIA V2 calls and `npu_attention_update`; it requires no environment-variable opt-in.

Honor `SGLANG_NPU_FORWARD_NATIVE_GEMMA_RMS_NORM` in `Gemma3RMSNorm` on NPU.

## Modifications

- Remove the `self.use_fia` dispatch and both `torch_npu.atb.npu_ring_mla` calls from the MLA prefix path. Use FIA TND for current-token causal attention and prefix attention, then merge their outputs in FP32 and restore the query dtype.
- Remove the unused RingMLA mask allocation and backend mask reference, preserving the original attention mask builder interface.
- Gather cached latent and RoPE pages through `gather_mla_cache_pages`, restoring logical token order for PA-NZ storage before projection and attention.
- Preserve cumulative TND sequence lengths, contiguous inputs, empty-prefix handling and output padding.
- Test against full prefix-first dense SDPA with FP16/BF16, mixed zero/nonzero prefixes, padding and large logits. Verify two FIA calls plus one merge for either value of the backend FIA flag, with ATB unavailable.
- Apply the existing native Gemma RMSNorm flag to `Gemma3RMSNorm.forward_npu`. This flag remains disabled by default; `Gemma4RMSNorm` already falls back to native on NPU.

The MLA prefix path covered by this change uses FIA TND whether `ASCEND_USE_FIA` is unset, `0`, or `1`. Other attention paths retain their existing dispatch behavior. The existing equal-QK/V-dimension MLA path is unchanged.

To select the native Gemma normalization implementation on NPU:

```bash
export SGLANG_NPU_FORWARD_NATIVE_GEMMA_RMS_NORM=1
```

## Accuracy Tests

### Default FIA TND validation (2026-10-14)

At commit `dd8bbb875f7a0bc7f8cea96cf0123aace7e45e37`, all 59 CPU-compatible attention unit tests passed through an isolated runner that compiles the unchanged production definitions and repository test classes from their AST, avoiding unrelated NPU imports. FIA and merge kernels use the tests' numerical PyTorch reference implementations; this does not validate the full package import path or real NPU kernels. The prefix tests cover 13 scenarios, including `use_fia=False` and `True` with ATB unavailable, FP16/BF16, mixed zero/nonzero prefixes, output padding and large logits. A mask-builder initialization check also passed without RingMLA or environment flags.

Ruff 0.15.1 lint/format, isort, codespell, Python syntax parsing, debug-statement/merge-marker checks and `git diff --check` passed. An AST comparison confirms that `forward_extend` matches the prior implementation with only its RingMLA/FIA dispatch replaced by the existing FIA body, preserving the FIA computation and other attention branches.

No new NPU model accuracy or performance evaluation was run for this change. The records below belong to their explicitly named earlier commits; their FIA/ATB environment-flag comparisons describe the older implementation.

### Prefix dispatch refactor validation (2026-09-28)

Commit `ee3dfe96a1bcc93bcdf3d6f4c04eb489b659de28` reorganizes the MLA prefix path into one complete `if self.use_fia` / `else` block. For each fixed value of `self.use_fia`, the old and new Python ASTs contain the same executable statements in the same order, including operator arguments, NZ cache handling, empty-prefix handling and output padding. Ruff 0.15.1 formatting and lint (`F401,F821,UP037`), Python syntax parsing and `git diff --check` passed. No new unit tests or NPU model evaluations were run for this structural change; the numerical and performance results below retain their recorded commit attribution.

### NZ cache validation (2026-09-24)

Commit `0c8ebbce034c11b5e0b9c2fec3193def9de2aa74` passed the original full HiCache MLA GSM8K case on A3/151 with FIA enabled in both runs: NZ disabled **473/1319 (35.860500%)**, NZ enabled **465/1319 (35.253980%)**. Both exceed the 34% case threshold. The 18 operator-path cases and 6 independent reruns also passed, with fixed NZ outputs bitwise equal to the ND baseline. See the NZ validation section under **Speed Tests and Profiling** for the complete environment, comparison, numerical checks, performance table and limitations. Python syntax parsing and `git diff --check` passed; no new unit tests were added.

### Latest validation (2026-09-24)

At commit `ef8a80be18d4d1e6efa84252cca07dd31284850a`, Python syntax parsing and `git diff --check` passed for the three changed files. The quantization implementation and its test file match the PR base; the remaining PR changes concern MLA prefix attention and Gemma normalization. No additional unit tests or model evaluations were run for this update. The accuracy and performance measurements below remain attributed to their explicitly recorded earlier commits.

### Gemma native fallback validation (2026-09-22)

Commit `ec72a1dd7c4292477bdd8e317a55f87c44f04357` changes only `layernorm.py`. Python syntax compilation and `git diff --check` passed. No additional unit tests or NPU model evaluations were run for this change. The model accuracy measurements below belong to their explicitly recorded earlier commits.

### Validation of updated PR head 3ba07ddc43 on machine 216 (2026-09-21)

After the author merged community main, tested **the actual PR head `3ba07ddc43d55782e2195f5cd2457297b1eef9fd`**, which includes main `62ba9648482e1b0a253187c8dc6ac5d23bbbd403`. Main is already an ancestor of the PR; `git merge-tree` succeeds and GitHub reports MERGEABLE. This rerun uses the published PR commit directly, rather than the earlier temporary integration snapshot.

Ran its original `test/registered/npu/basic_function/HiCache/test_npu_hicache_mla.py` on machine **216**, physical **A3 devices 0–3**, with **CANN 9.1.0 / torch_npu 2.10.0.post4 / PyTorch 2.10.0 / Transformers 5.12.1**. Reused the same full DeepSeek-V2-Lite-W8A8 checkpoint and GSM8K dataset. Both modes used TP=4, mem_fraction_static=0.8, HiCache enabled (current defaults: ratio=2.0, host memory fraction=0.8), all **1319 questions**, 5-shot, temperature=0, max_new_tokens=512, concurrency=128, and seed=42. The PR smoke shortcut was disabled. No additional unit tests were added or run.

| ASCEND_USE_FIA | Correct / total | Accuracy | Invalid answers | Case result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| unset | 472 / 1319 | 35.784685% | 5 | passed |
| 1 | 469 / 1319 | 35.557240% | 5 | passed |

FIA minus baseline: **-3 correct answers / -0.227445 percentage points**. 681 final numerical predictions differed: 111 changed from correct to incorrect, and 108 from incorrect to correct. This single pair does not establish lossless replacement. The existing backend-wide ASCEND_USE_FIA flag also affects other attention paths, so this does not isolate the new prefix branch alone.

Source hashes (including files updated by the merged main), dataset, devices, model path, evaluation settings, and actual server argument dictionaries were checked for consistency. Device-prefix cache hits: 1319/1319 unset and 1319/1319 enabled, 1012992 and 1012992 cached tokens respectively. Host-cache reload hits: 0 and 0; this case does not force host-cache eviction/reload. Full logs, metrics and per-question answers were retained.

Observed accuracy-evaluation runtime / output throughput: unset **198.626 s / 794.967 token/s**, enabled **207.717 s / 755.773 token/s**. These are not controlled performance measurements. A2/A5 and CANN 9.2 remain untested. Earlier validation records are preserved below.

### Latest-main integration rerun on machine 216 (2026-09-21)

Community main `176dbcb85d3b7737564e4911947035cc0af65f0a` and PR head `1344e1e2a5ca3e07bf6140b8c606e38465fbc55c` merged without conflicts in both `git merge-tree` and an actual isolated merge. GitHub reports MERGEABLE; the CI gate is blocked by the missing `run-ci` label, independently of merge conflicts. Tested the resulting temporary merge `2b388ce85710f74030b266f8446a01b91c556d48` without pushing it to the PR branch.

During the run, main advanced to `ab03a8e7eb82d35907bfbeb645bf0af8b4ce290e` (#40201, import/startup changes). A final `git merge-tree` check against that main also succeeded and GitHub still reports MERGEABLE. It does not modify this PR's NPU attention/quantization files or the HiCache MLA case. The accuracy results below belong to the fixed merge snapshot above; the full model test was not repeated on this newer main commit.

Ran the current merged-source `test_npu_hicache_mla.py` on machine **216**, four **Ascend A3** devices (physical 0–3), **CANN 9.1.0 / torch_npu 2.10.0.post4 / PyTorch 2.10.0 / Transformers 5.12.1**. Used the same full DeepSeek-V2-Lite-W8A8 checkpoint as the previous runs, copied from machine 209, with TP=4, `mem_fraction_static=0.8`, HiCache enabled, all 1319 GSM8K questions, 5-shot, temperature 0, max 512 new tokens, concurrency 128, and seed 42 for both modes. The updated main test no longer explicitly sets `hicache_ratio=1.2`; this rerun preserved its defaults, resolving to **ratio 2.0 / host_memory_fraction 0.8**. No additional unit tests were added or run for this rerun.

| ASCEND_USE_FIA | Correct / total | Accuracy | Invalid answers | Case result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| unset | 473 / 1319 | 35.860500% | 3 | passed |
| 1 | 484 / 1319 | 36.694466% | 4 | passed |

FIA minus baseline: **+11 correct answers / +0.833965 percentage points**. This single paired run does not establish lossless replacement or isolate the new prefix branch: `ASCEND_USE_FIA` affects other existing attention paths too. 661 final numerical predictions differed; 102 changed from correct to incorrect and 113 from incorrect to correct.

Both runs used matching source, dataset, devices, model path, evaluation parameters and actual server argument dictionaries. All 1319 requests in each run reused 768 device-cached prefix tokens; neither run forced host-cache reload. Full logs, exact metrics, source hashes and per-question answers were retained. Observed evaluation runtime / output throughput: unset **227.836 s / 691.215 token/s**, enabled **205.004 s / 768.774 token/s**. Other devices on the host had existing workloads; these observations are not a controlled performance benchmark. A2, A5 and CANN 9.2 remain untested.

### Historical validation on machine 209 (2026-09-18)

Ran the existing `test/registered/npu/basic_function/HiCache/test_npu_hicache_mla.py` at commit `1344e1e2a5ca3e07bf6140b8c606e38465fbc55c` on four **Ascend910_9362 (A3)** devices with **CANN 9.1.0, PyTorch 2.10.0, torch_npu 2.10.0.post4 and Transformers 5.12.1**.

Used the full `vllm-ascend/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-W8A8` checkpoint, adapting its local filesystem path. Each run used TP=4, HiCache enabled, `hicache_ratio=1.2`, `mem_fraction_static=0.8`, all **1319 GSM8K questions**, 5-shot prompts, temperature 0, `max_new_tokens=512` and concurrency 128. The PR-pipeline single-request smoke shortcut was disabled.

| Run pair | ASCEND_USE_FIA | Correct / total | Accuracy | Invalid answers |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Original case defaults | unset | 477 / 1319 | 36.163760% | 5 |
| Original case defaults | 1 | 469 / 1319 | 35.557240% | 7 |
| Both servers use `--random-seed 42` | unset | 481 / 1319 | 36.467020% | 6 |
| Both servers use `--random-seed 42` | 1 | 470 / 1319 | 35.633055% | 7 |

All four runs passed the case's 34% accuracy threshold. FIA scored **0.606520 percentage points lower** in the first pair and **0.833965 percentage points lower** in the fixed-seed pair. These measurements do **not** establish accuracy parity or lossless replacement; the ATB default and opt-in gate are retained.

In the fixed-seed pair, 686 final numerical predictions differed: 123 questions changed from correct to incorrect and 112 from incorrect to correct. Both actual server argument dictionaries matched, including seed 42. The first pair used automatically generated server seeds; both pairs are reported. The ATB runs themselves differed on 625 predictions between these two runs, so per-question changes cannot all be attributed to FIA from this experiment alone.

All 1319 requests in each run reused 768 device-cached prefix tokens, exercising prefix prefill with HiCache attached. This workload did not force host-cache eviction/reload. Source hashes, full server logs, exact metrics and per-question answers were retained. `ASCEND_USE_FIA` is an existing backend-wide flag, so this model comparison includes every path affected by the flag rather than isolating only the new prefix branch.

Additional validation performed before the model runs:

- CPU regression: 3 test methods / 11 parameter cases passed, covering FP16/BF16, variable lengths, mixed empty prefixes, noncontiguous inputs, padding, large logits and both operator routes. These tests use numerical substitutes for NPU kernels and compare with full dense SDPA.
- NPU quantization unit suite: all 25 tests passed in the torch_npu 2.10.0.post4 container. These are CPU/mocked tests, including shape, bias and dtype behavior for MXFP8 linear operations.
- Re-ran the gated production `forward_extend` prefix branch on **Ascend910_9362 (A3), CANN 9.1.0, PyTorch 2.10.0 and torch_npu 2.10.0.post4**: **18/18 cases passed**. Cache gather, KV projection, FIA, merge and padding execute on NPU; the reference attention executes on CPU. The branch is loaded unchanged from source with unrelated imports isolated; this is not a complete serving/model test.
- NPU cases cover page sizes 1/128, heads 2/4/8/16/128, query lengths up to 257, prefixes up to 2048, mixed empty prefixes and zero/nonzero padding. NoPE/RoPE/V dimensions are 128/64/128.

| dtype | Maximum absolute error | Maximum per-case RMSE | atol / rtol |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| FP16 | 0.001953125 | 0.000209168 | 0.003 / 0.003 |
| BF16 | 0.015625 | 0.001710953 | 0.02 / 0.02 |

All NPU branch cases also check output device, shape, dtype, finite values and zero padding. A2/A5 and CANN 9.2 have not been hardware tested.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### NZ prefix-cache validation on A3 (2026-09-24)

Commit `0c8ebbce034c11b5e0b9c2fec3193def9de2aa74` uses the existing `gather_mla_cache_pages` helper from #39589 for both latent and RoPE prefix reads in the two-FIA branch. It restores logical token order before projection and TND attention when the KV cache uses PA-NZ storage. The helper is byte-identical to #39589 after newline normalization. ND behavior is preserved.

**Environment:** machine 151, Ascend910_9362 (A3), CANN 9.1.0, PyTorch 2.10.0, torch_npu 2.10.0.post6. The patch changes only the two cache-gather calls; it does not reintroduce the reverted quantization API changes.

**Operator-path validation and performance:** 18 cases plus 6 independent reruns passed. The fixture uses the actual `NPUMLATokenToKVPool._set_fia_nz_kv_buffer` and its index helper, executing real NPU scatter with randomized token write order. Both latent and RoPE readback are bitwise equal to the logical ND cache. Across all cases, the fixed NZ branch and fixed ND branch outputs are bitwise equal to the original ND branch output. Sampled CPU FP32 reference checks also pass (maximum RMS relative error 0.2995%). The unfixed NZ branch is retained as a negative control and shows RMS relative errors of 6.55%-119.16% on these synthetic cases.

The independent rerun below measures median amortized wall time for cache gather, BF16 projection, attention, copies and merge. QK=192, V=128, latent=512, page=128, H=4; BF16/eager. It uses 20 warmups and 9 rounds of 30 calls per method with randomized method order. NZ BSND explicitly selects the existing per-request branch for the same inputs, without changing production dispatch. NZ here describes cache storage; the two attention calls still use TND inputs after gathering.

| Case | ND before (ms) | ND fixed (ms) | NZ fixed (ms) | NZ overhead vs ND | NZ BSND (ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| b1_q100_p768_h4 | 0.507 | 0.509 | 0.567 | +11.39% | 0.440 |
| b8_q100_p768_h4 | 0.563 | 0.565 | 0.627 | +11.04% | 2.061 |
| b32_q100_p768_h4 | 0.630 | 0.629 | 0.712 | +13.16% | 6.819 |
| b1_q1024_p8192_h4 | 0.550 | 0.552 | 0.611 | +10.60% | 0.494 |
| b4_q1024_p8192_h4 | 1.746 | 1.745 | 1.833 | +5.03% | 1.718 |
| b8_q1024_p8192_h4 | 3.365 | 3.364 | 3.502 | +4.09% | 3.518 |

NZ layout restoration adds about 4%-13% to the two-FIA prefix branch in this rerun. With NZ disabled, the helper adds no layout conversion; the first sweep measured ND before/after differences within approximately -0.34% to +0.65%. Short-query batched two-FIA remains faster than per-request BSND. These are branch measurements and do not establish whole-model speedup.

**Full model accuracy:** ran the original `test_npu_hicache_mla.py` on the same physical devices 0-3 with DeepSeek-V2-Lite-W8A8, TP=4, HiCache enabled, radix enabled, seed=42, all 1319 GSM8K questions, 5-shot, temperature=0, max_new_tokens=512 and concurrency=128. Both runs set `ASCEND_USE_FIA=1`; only `SGLANG_USE_FIA_NZ` changes. The source, model path, dataset, devices, launch arguments and evaluation settings match.

| SGLANG_USE_FIA_NZ | Correct / total | Accuracy | Invalid | Result | Eval runtime (s) | Output token/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 473 / 1319 | 35.860500% | 6 | passed | 229.363 | 701.845 |
| 1 | 465 / 1319 | 35.253980% | 5 | passed | 246.641 | 652.957 |

NZ minus ND: **-0.606520 percentage points**. Final numerical predictions differ on 581 questions (96 correct-to-incorrect, 88 incorrect-to-correct). These full-model runs exercise other NZ-dependent cache/decode paths as well, so model-level differences cannot be attributed to the prefix gather alone. Evaluation runtime and token/s are observations from accuracy runs with variable generation lengths, not a controlled serving performance benchmark. The host is shared; another process was observed on device 3 at the end of the NZ run, so model-run timing is not a device-exclusive measurement.

Device-prefix cache hits: ND 1319/1319, NZ 1319/1319; cached tokens: ND 1012992, NZ 1012992. Host-cache reload hits: ND 0, NZ 0. This does not establish host-cache eviction/reload correctness when those counts are zero. A2/A5 and CANN 9.2 are not hardware-validated by this run. Full logs, inputs, source hashes, timing samples and per-question predictions were retained.

### Controlled prefix-branch comparison on A3 (2026-09-22)

Measured commit `ec72a1dd7c4292477bdd8e317a55f87c44f04357` on 2026-09-22, machine 151: **one Ascend910_9362 (A3), CANN 9.1.0 (B070 container), PyTorch 2.10.0, torch_npu 2.10.0.post6**, BF16, NZ disabled, eager execution. The main shape uses QK=192 (NoPE=128 + RoPE=64), V=128, latent=512, page size=128 and H=4 per rank (the DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP=4 head shape); no TP communication is executed.

The comparison is between two **FIA** implementations of MLA prefix prefill:

- **Two FIA V2 + merge:** this PR's batched TND current-token attention and prefix attention, followed by `npu_attention_update`.
- **Concat + BSND FIA:** the existing `if layer.qk_head_dim == layer.v_head_dim` branch, concatenating prefix/current K/V and issuing one BSND FIA call **per request**. B requests therefore issue B FIA calls.

The benchmark extracts both branch bodies directly from the recorded source and uses identical Q/K/V, cache, projection weights and sequence metadata. To compare the same DeepSeek input, it explicitly selects the BSND body for QK=192/V=128 despite the production dispatch condition; this CANN build accepted that shape and passed the numerical checks. The production condition and kernel arguments were not changed. This is not a comparison with ATB or an end-to-end comparison of `ASCEND_USE_FIA` enabled/disabled.

Times include cache gather, BF16 `kv_b_proj`, FIA, concatenation/contiguous copies, dtype conversions and merge. They exclude the rest of the model, QKV preparation, scheduling, decode and TP communication, and do not reproduce W8A8 projection. Each value is the median amortized wall time per complete prefix branch, with synchronization at each measurement block. Method order is randomized with a fixed seed. The first sweep uses 12 warmups and 7 rounds of 20 calls per method; an independent rerun uses 20 warmups and 9 rounds of 30 calls. Individually synchronized calls and NPU event spans were also recorded; event spans can include host submission gaps.

**Independent rerun (8 cases).** B = requests, Q = new query tokens per request, P = cached prefix tokens per request, H = heads per rank. A BSND / two-FIA time ratio above 1 favors the PR's two-FIA path.

| B | Q per request | Prefix per request | H | Two FIA V2 + merge (ms) | Concat + BSND FIA (ms) | BSND / two-FIA time |
| ---: | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 100 | 768 | 4 | 0.513 | 0.395 | 0.77 |
| 2 | 100 | 768 | 4 | 0.520 | 0.629 | 1.21 |
| 8 | 100 | 768 | 4 | 0.524 | 1.862 | 3.55 |
| 32 | 100 | 768 | 4 | 0.619 | 6.677 | 10.80 |
| 128 | 100 | 768 | 4 | 2.434 | 26.031 | 10.70 |
| 1 | 1024 | 8192 | 4 | 0.542 | 0.457 | 0.84 |
| 4 | 1024 | 8192 | 4 | 1.715 | 1.645 | 0.96 |
| 8 | 1024 | 8192 | 4 | 3.306 | 3.374 | 1.02 |

**Result:** for Q=100/P=768, the two-FIA branch wins from B=2 in this sweep, reaching **3.55x at B=8** and **10.80x at B=32** in the rerun. At B=1, concatenation is faster: about **23% lower latency** for Q=100/P=768 and **16% lower** for Q=1024/P=8192. With Q=1024/P=8192, B=4 favors BSND by about 4%, while B=8 is near parity; a 1-2% gap should not be treated as a significant stable win. These are prefix-branch ratios, not whole-model speedups.

The source structure is consistent with the trend: per-request concatenation and B FIA submissions become expensive for short-query batches, while the TND path batches requests into two FIA calls plus one merge. B=1 avoids the second call and merge with BSND. This interpretation has not been confirmed by kernel-level profiling. The results support retaining the batched two-FIA path; a B=1 specialization is a possible follow-up, subject to device/version and full-model validation.

| ---: | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 100 | 768 | 4 | 0.526 | 0.386 | 0.73 |

| 4 | 100 | 768 | 4 | 0.611 | 1.204 | 1.97 |

| 1 | 256 | 2048 | 4 | 0.500 | 0.381 | 0.76 |
| 4 | 256 | 2048 | 4 | 0.500 | 0.986 | 1.97 |
| 16 | 256 | 2048 | 4 | 0.939 | 3.446 | 3.67 |
| 32 | 256 | 2048 | 4 | 1.828 | 6.595 | 3.61 |
| 1 | 1024 | 8192 | 4 | 0.549 | 0.457 | 0.83 |

| 16 | 100 | 768 | 16 | 1.181 | 3.011 | 2.55 |
| 32 | 100 | 768 / 0 alternating | 4 | 0.844 | 6.740 | 7.98 |
| 10 | mixed (see below) | 768, then nine zeros | 4 | 0.671 | 1.906 | 2.84 |

The mixed B=10 case uses query lengths `[101,870,876,874,869,864,904,863,837,768]` and prefix lengths `[768,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]`, matching an earlier observed batch shape with synthetic tensor values. It favors two FIA by **2.84x**. B=128/Q=100 contains 12,800 query tokens and is an extended sweep point, not a claim that default chunk limits produce that batch.

</details>

**Numerical checks:** all 18 sweep cases and all 8 rerun cases passed full-output pairwise comparison (`atol=0.02`, `rtol=0.02`) and sampled CPU FP32 full-attention reference checks. Maximum full-output absolute difference between methods was **0.001953125**; maximum per-case pairwise RMS relative difference was **0.3022%**. Maximum sampled RMS relative error against CPU FP32 was **0.2995%** for two FIA and **0.2296%** for BSND. The CPU reference uses the same projected K/V. This checks the sampled operator paths; it is not a new GSM8K accuracy run. Hardware conclusions here are limited to this A3/CANN/torch_npu configuration.

The fixed-seed full GSM8K runs measured 193.304 s / 814.391 output tokens per second with FIA unset, and 196.474 s / 801.729 output tokens per second with FIA enabled. The first pair measured 225.281 s / 697.903 and 195.270 s / 802.929 respectively. These are accuracy-run measurements with differing generation lengths and dynamic batches, not a controlled performance benchmark; no speedup is claimed. At the commits measured in this section, the FIA path was opt-in and used a separate merge with FP32 intermediate outputs. The current MLA prefix path selects FIA TND unconditionally.

title: [Fix] [Intel] cpu-kernel: Fix rope for VLA model
author: jianan-gu
body:
## Motivation
`torch.ops.sgl_kernel.apply_rotary_pos_emb_cpu` kernel only takes 3D `[num_tokens, num_heads, head_size]` inputs and had no `unsqueeze_dim` argument. Pi0.5 calls it with 4D `[batch, num_heads, seq_len, head_size]` q/k and `unsqueeze_dim=1`, so it failed on CPU:

```
"/python/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/vlas/pi05_core.py", line 382, in forward
    query_states, key_states = native_apply_rotary_pos_emb(
  File "//lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/_ops.py", line 1350, in __call__
    return self._op(*args, **kwargs)
RuntimeError: sgl_kernel::apply_rotary_pos_emb_cpu() expected at most 4 argument(s) but received 5 argument(s). Declaration: sgl_kernel::apply_rotary_pos_emb_cpu(Tensor query, Tensor key, Tensor cos, Tensor sin) -> (Tensor, Tensor)
```
- https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/vlas/pi05_core.py#L902C32-L902C59

## Modifications

- `apply_rotary_pos_emb_cpu` now takes `unsqueeze_dim` (default 1) and supports q/k of 3D and higher, with the head dim at `unsqueeze_dim` (e.g. `[B, H, S, D]` or `[B, S, H, D]`). It is out-of-place, matching `apply_rotary_pos_emb_native`.
- The neox rope path now handles float32 inputs, and the CPU graph fake op is updated for the new signature.

## Test Coverage

- pi0.5 model functionality

- `test_apply_rotary_pos_emb` in `test/registered/cpu/test_rope.py`. It compares against the native reference for:
  (1) 3D with GQA, 4D `[B, H, S, D]` with `unsqueeze_dim=1`, and (2) 4D `[B, S, H, D]` with `unsqueeze_dim=2`

title: Fix TopK v2 fallback when 16-block cluster capacity is zero
author: luoroger37
body:
## Motivation

TopK v2 can launch an unsupported 16-block cluster even when the device occupancy probe reports zero capacity. The loader swallows the zero-capacity exception and retains the default C16 capacity of `7`.

On NVIDIA H20, this was reproduced with `batch=4`, `seq_len=65536`, and `topk=512`, which failed with `cluster misconfiguration`.

This PR passes the zero-capacity result into JIT compilation so the unsupported path is disabled and the existing fallback is used.

## Modifications

- Handle the 8-block and 16-block probes in one loop and always emit the corresponding capacity macro after each successful query, including zero-capacity results.
- Distinguish zero schedulable clusters from unexpected probe errors. Zero disables the corresponding cluster path; other errors propagate for both probes.
- Default the optional 16-block path to disabled unless a positive probe result enables it.
- Reuse the existing dispatch guards: a zero C16 capacity falls back to C8 when available; zero C8 capacity skips the persistent pool and permits the existing non-cluster path.
- Remove the PR-specific mocked host tests and shape-only GPU regressions as requested in review. The existing upstream TopK v2 test file is unchanged.

The fix uses occupancy probing and requires no H20-specific device-name checks.

## Accuracy Tests

Previously recorded validation on NVIDIA H20 (78 SMs), PyTorch `2.11.0+cu130`, CUDA `13.0`, using upstream base `3401b75240d7` and the initial fix `f453a06894e7`:

| Check | Original upstream | Initial fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Probed 16-block capacity | `0` | `0` |
| Compiled 16-block capacity | `7` | `0` |
| `batch=4, seq_len=65536, topk=512` | `cluster misconfiguration` | Pass |
| TopK v2 regression file | Stops after 72 passes at the failing case | 292 passed |

The 292 passes included four PR-specific GPU cases that have now been removed. This is historical evidence for the initial fix, not a GPU rerun of the review revision.

Validation of the review revision:

- Repository pre-commit checks passed for the affected files.
- Local host-logic smoke checks passed for positive/zero capacities, unexpected probe errors, and architectures without cluster probing, using isolated source functions and mocked probe/JIT boundaries.
- CUDA compilation and GPU regression tests have not been rerun for this revision. A device with positive C16 capacity and the zero-C8 fallback have not been validated on hardware.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This is a launch compatibility fix; no performance improvement is claimed. The affected inputs fail before the fix, so there is no valid pre-fix execution time for comparison.

The change reuses existing kernels and adds no per-call device-to-host synchronization or additional kernel launches.

title: [Fix] [NPU] glm5.2: support pcp v2 with interleave & zigzag
author: gjsheu
body:
## Summary

Adapt GLM-5.2 (GlmMoeDsa) DSA prefill context parallelism to the CP V2 strategy flow, mirroring the DSV4 CP V2 support merged in #39427. After CP V1 was deprecated upstream, the NPU DSA path still referenced removed V1 metadata fields and could no longer run with --enable-prefill-cp.

## Changes

- **ascend_backend.py**: add prepare_dsa_cp_metadata which builds per-token local metadata for the Ascend sparse kernels (q/kv lengths from sharded local positions, per-token block-table rows selected by local batch ids); rewrite do_cp_balance_attn to a single npu_sparse_flash_attention call on the strategy-sharded local Q (no V1 prev/next balance split).
- **dsa_npu_indexer.py**: read V2 local metadata instead of the removed V1 attn_cp_metadata fields (actual_seq_q_prev_tensor / kv_len_prev_tensor / ...); rewrite do_npu_cp_balance_indexer as a single npu_lightning_indexer call.
- **deepseek_v2.py**: prepare DSA CP metadata at the inner-model entry (the eager CP runner invokes DeepseekV2Model directly); restore rebuild_cp_kv_cache, gathering the rank-local latent KV into full sequence order via cp_gather_full_sequence_states.
- **forward_mha.py**: on NPU with CP active, gather kv_a/k_pe to full sequence order before writing, since out_cache_loc spans the full sequence under CP V2.
- **unit tests**: add `test/registered/unit/layers/cp/test_dsa_cp_metadata.py` covering the zigzag/interleave block layout, local row selection, padding alignment, the `is_cp_active` gate, and the GLM DSA layer-split helpers.

The first commit fixes the attn_cp_tp_broadcast_pyobj broadcast order for attn-CP > 1 (broadcast along the attn-TP 0 line first, then TP).

## Testing

Full-model verification on a 4-node Ascend 910B3 cluster (32 NPUs/node) with GLM-5.2-w8a8 (GlmMoeDsa) in PD disaggregation:

- **Prefill** (2 nodes, 209/212): `--tp-size 8 --pp-size 4 --attn-cp-size 8 --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 65536 --mem-fraction-static 0.88`, NEXTN spec (num-steps 1, draft 2)
- **Decode** (2 nodes, 216/217): `--tp-size 32 --dp-size 32 --ep-size 32`, NEXTN spec (num-steps 3, draft 4)
- Key envs: `DEEPEP_HCCL_BUFFSIZE=2048`, `SGLANG_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=18,20,24,16`, `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_ALL_CP_RANKS_TRANSFER=1`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1`, `MALLOC_CHECK_=3`
- Client: vllm bench serve through the sglang PD router (16 prompts, concurrency 4, input 65536 / output 2500)

### Throughput / latency results

| config | result | TTFT mean / median / P99 | TPOT | throughput |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| zigzag + chunk 4096 | :white_check_mark: 16/16 | 9.45s / 5.85s / 26.05s | 26.89 ms | 3370 tok/s |
| interleave + chunk 8192 (fixed len) | :white_check_mark: 16/16 | 9.12s / 6.08s / 20.05s | 25.70 ms | 3570 tok/s |
| interleave + chunk 8192 (variable input 40960–90112) | :white_check_mark: 16/16 | 7.82s / 6.94s / 15.53s | 25.85 ms | 3550 tok/s |

The zigzag + chunk 8192 crash is a deep_ep CAM dispatch buffer overflow (`HCCL_BUFFSIZE is too SMALL`, 3304MB needed > 2048MB) triggered when a pass dispatches the whole 8076-token batch per rank; chunk 4096 caps the per-rank dispatch at ~1.78GB. Interleave keeps CP active on every pass (1024 tokens/rank, ~604MB), so it is safe with chunk 8192.

### Accuracy (gpqa_diamond)

evalscope 90.4%

### Unit tests

`test/registered/unit/layers/cp/test_dsa_cp_metadata.py` — **21/21 passed** (CPU, no NPU needed):

```
PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/layers/cp/test_dsa_cp_metadata.py -v
```

### Request / bench scripts

<details>
<summary>start_glm_5_2_w8a8_2p2d.sh (prefill+decode launcher, runs on all 4 nodes, auto-detects role)</summary>

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# GLM-5.2-w8a8 2p2d (prefill-decode disaggregation) launcher.
# Same script on all 4 nodes; the role is picked from the local IP.
#   prefill (2p): 192.168.25.209, 192.168.25.212   tp8 x pp4 = 32 cards
#   decode  (2d): 192.168.25.216, 192.168.25.217   tp32 = 32 cards
# KV pool capacity: --mem-fraction-static 0.88 gives the decode pool ~82k
# tokens (>= 68036 needed for 64k in + 2.5k out).

echo performance | tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor >/dev/null 2>&1
sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0 >/dev/null 2>&1
sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0 >/dev/null 2>&1
sysctl -w kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000 >/dev/null 2>&1

export SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY=1
unset https_proxy http_proxy HTTPS_PROXY HTTP_PROXY ASCEND_LAUNCH_BLOCKING
source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh

# ---- common env ----
export TRANSFORMERS_VERBOSITY=error
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export STREAMS_PER_DEVICE=32
export SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT=1200
export SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_WAITING_TIMEOUT=1200
# P has CP but D has none: KV transfer must involve all CP ranks (both sides)
export SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_ALL_CP_RANKS_TRANSFER=1

P_IP=('192.168.25.209' '192.168.25.212')
D_IP=('192.168.25.216' '192.168.25.217')
MODEL_PATH=/home/weights/GLM-5.2-w8a8

LOCAL_HOST1=$(hostname -I | awk '{print $1}')
LOCAL_HOST2=$(hostname -I | awk '{print $2}')
mkdir -p /home/gjs/glm/logs

# =============================================================================
# prefill (2p)
# =============================================================================
for i in "${!P_IP[@]}"; do
    if [[ "$LOCAL_HOST1" == "${P_IP[$i]}" || "$LOCAL_HOST2" == "${P_IP[$i]}" ]]; then
        echo "role=prefill node=${P_IP[$i]} node_rank=$i"

        export ASCEND_MF_STORE_URL="tcp://${P_IP[0]}:24666"
        export DEEP_NORMAL_MODE_USE_INT8_QUANT=1

        export DEEPEP_HCCL_BUFFSIZE=2048
        export SGLANG_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=18,20,24,16
        export MALLOC_CHECK_=3
        export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=enp196s0f0
        export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=enp196s0f0
        # Note: DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_* is NOT used (native long-seq path
        # double-frees on this deep_ep build); small chunks instead keep the
        # per-rank dispatch <= the default capacity.
        export SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=128
        export SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1
        export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1
        export SGLANG_ENABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK=0
        export SGLANG_DISAGG_PREFILL_EARLY_SEND_CACHED_PREFIX=1

        nohup python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
          --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \
          --disaggregation-mode prefill \
          --tp-size 8 --attn-cp-size 8 --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave \
          --nnodes 2 --node-rank "$i" --dist-init-addr "${P_IP[0]}:5000" \
          --mem-fraction-static 0.88 \
          --attention-backend ascend --device npu --quantization modelslim \
          --disaggregation-transfer-backend ascend \
          --max-running-requests 64 \
          --served-model-name glm-5 \
          --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 65536 \
          --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode normal \
          --load-balance-method round_robin \
          --disable-shared-experts-fusion --disable-cuda-graph --dtype bfloat16 \
          --speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant \
          --pp-size 4 \
          --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 1 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 2 \
          --reasoning-parser glm45 --tool-call-parser glm47 \

    fi
done

# =============================================================================
# decode (2d)
# =============================================================================
for i in "${!D_IP[@]}"; do
    if [[ "$LOCAL_HOST1" == "${D_IP[$i]}" || "$LOCAL_HOST2" == "${D_IP[$i]}" ]]; then

        export SGLANG_NPU_USE_MULTI_STREAM=1
        export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=enp196s0f0
        export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=enp196s0f0

        nohup python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
          --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \
          --disaggregation-mode decode \
          --tp-size 32 --nnodes 2 --node-rank "$i" --dist-init-addr "${D_IP[0]}:5000" \
          --dp-size 32 --enable-dp-attention --ep-size 32 \
          --mem-fraction-static 0.88 \

          --served-model-name glm-5 \
          --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode low_latency \

          --host "${D_IP[$i]}" --port 8000 \
          > /home/gjs/glm/logs/decode_$i.log 2>&1 &

    fi
done
```

#!/bin/bash

## Performance: single-call vs two-call DSA attention (zigzag)

Measured on the 4-node 2p2d GLM-5.2-w8a8 stack (b072 image; 2 prefill nodes tp8 x cp8 x pp4 zigzag + 2 decode nodes tp32 x dp32, NEXTN 1x2/3x4), fixed-length 64k-input x 8-concurrent requests:

| variant | success | wall | TTFT mean (min/max) | e2e mean (min/max) | decode tok/s |

| single fused call (shipped) | 8/8 | 38.13s | 21.70s (8.72 / 33.32) | 26.05s (12.96 / 38.12) | 53.7 |
| two calls, per-sequence metadata (experiment) | 8/8 | 38.21s | 21.79s (8.81 / 33.43) | 26.10s (12.95 / 38.20) | 53.6 |

The two-call variant splits the local Q into prev/next halves and issues two `npu_sparse_flash_attention` calls with per-sequence metadata. title: [Fix] diffusion/lora: revalidate FLUX.2 FP8/NVFP4 fast paths after LoRA attach
author: heiculi98
body:
Fix a crash when attaching a LoRA adapter at runtime to a FLUX.2 (multimodal_gen) model loaded from an FP8-quantized checkpoint (ModelOpt FP8).

## Motivation

`Flux2ParallelSelfAttention.__init__` decides the fused fast-path flags
`_enable_fp8_token_cat` / `_enable_nvfp4_token_cat` by inspecting
`self.to_out.quant_method` on the raw quantized `RowParallelLinear`. When a
LoRA adapter is attached, the LoRA pipeline replaces those quantized linears
with wrapper modules that do not expose `quant_method` / `input_scale`. The
init-time flags then go stale, and `forward()` reads those attributes off the
wrapper, crashing instead of falling back to the unfused path.

Reproduced on an L20 GPU (SM89) with the official FLUX.2-klein-9b-fp8
checkpoint and a runtime-attached LoRA adapter (locally trained, cannot be
shared): the model crashes on the first forward pass after the adapter is
mounted.

Related: #35970 (diffusion LoRA + FP8 crash on static merge) — the merge-policy
half is handled by the `can_merge_base_weight` dynamic fallback; this PR fixes
the stale fast-path flags on the dynamic path.

## Modifications

  attributes, the fusion is simply disabled.
- Add `Flux2Transformer2DModel.revalidate_fp8_fast_paths()` which also re-runs
  `configure_fp8_norm_quant()` per block.
- Call the hook from `LoRAPipeline` after the wrappers are installed (for
  modules that expose it, e.g. `transformer` / `transformer_2`).

No behavior change when no LoRA is attached — the revalidation hook only runs
after LoRA wrappers are installed.

## Accuracy Tests

End-to-end A/B on a single L20 GPU (SM89) with the official
FLUX.2-klein-9b-fp8 checkpoint and a runtime-attached LoRA adapter (locally
trained, cannot be shared), built on this PR branch (latest main):

- Without the patch: non-LoRA generation succeeds; after `POST /v1/set_lora`
  (merge_mode=dynamic), the first LoRA generation fails immediately with
  `AttributeError: 'ColumnParallelLinearWithLoRA' object has no attribute
  'input_scale'` inside `Flux2Transformer2DModel.forward`.
- With the patch: the same request completes normally and produces valid
  1024x1024 output; no errors in the server log.
- Non-LoRA inference is untouched: same prompt/seed before and after the
  patch yields bit-identical output images.
- ruff / ruff-format / isort pass per pre-commit rules.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A — this change only disables fused fast paths that would otherwise crash
under LoRA; it does not affect the non-LoRA serving path.

title: [AMD][DSV4] fix: drop shadowing local get_exec import that breaks model startup on ROCm
author: amd-danli103
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
DeepSeek-V4 cannot start on ROCm: every scheduler rank dies building the memory pools, so the server never comes up.

`DSV4PoolConfigurator.__init__` reads `get_exec` at line 986 and then imports it again, locally, at line 1083. The local import makes the name local to the whole function, so the earlier read raises:

```
    _is_hip and get_exec().kernel.enable_deepseek_v4_fp4_indexer,
UnboundLocalError: local variable 'get_exec' referenced before assignment
```

The module already imports the same symbol at line 46, which is what line 986 was meant to resolve to.

Only ROCm hits it: the read is `_is_hip and get_exec()...`, so elsewhere `_is_hip `is False, and short-circuits, and the name is never evaluated — which is why CI is green.
Repro on any ROCm host, on `main` — this repo's own test for the class already fails, no model or GPU work needed:

```bash
$ pytest -q test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_pool_configurator.py \
      -k dsv4_paged_dspark_budget
UnboundLocalError: local variable 'get_exec' referenced before assignment
1 failed, 43 deselected in 24.51s
```

Seen on `main` at `9784d5f979`, MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.
The local import came in with #38798 (`a6cf05817f`); the read at 986 predates it, so ROCm startup regressed when the two met.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
Delete the redundant function-local import:

```diff
-        from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_exec
-
         self.encoder_replay = get_exec().features.enable_encoder_swa_bounded_replay
```
One file, one statement; no signature or platform-gating change.
Why it is safe: line 46 binds the identical function at module scope, and the two call sites in the file (986, 1083) now both resolve to it. 

### Verification

Two checkouts on one MI355X host, differing only by this diff — pristine `main` at `9784d5f979` with no local modifications, and the same tree plus the deletion:
| | `-k dsv4_paged_dspark_budget` |
| --- | --- |
| pristine `main` | `1 failed` — `UnboundLocalError`, `pool_configurator.py:986` |
| with this change | `1 passed` |

- Whole file on the fixed tree: **45 passed, 7 subtests passed**.
- A DeepSeek-V4 server on the same host gets past pool sizing into weight loading (`Load weight begin`, `Detected fp8 checkpoint`), where it previously aborted on every rank.

No new test is included: the existing case already covers the regression on ROCm.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->
Not applicable. No kernel or model-forward code is touched; the change removes a redundant import of a symbol already bound at module scope.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->
Not applicable, for the same reason.

title: [Bugfix] Fix top-1 MoE routing with non-unit scaling
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

`TestFusedMOE.test_single_expert_routing` intermittently fails on H100 for
`topk=1` with `routed_scaling_factor=1.5` (for example,
[this scheduled CI job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35338273981/job/105578255653)).

For top-1 routing, `_use_intermediate` was false regardless of the routed
scaling factor, so the down-projection kernel wrote directly to
`out_hidden_states`. The non-unit scaling path then reduced
`intermediate_cache3`, which had never been populated, overwriting the valid
output with uninitialized memory. This made the failure allocator-dependent.

### Regression history

**Bottom line:** the regression that remained in `main` was reintroduced by [#6970](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/6970), authored by [@BBuf](https://github.com/BBuf). [#6220](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/6220), also authored by @BBuf, had first introduced the same mismatch, but it was fully reverted by [#6968](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/6968). [#22660](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/22660) only added the test coverage that eventually exposed the bug; it did not introduce the production issue.

- [#3988](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/3988) introduced the
  top-1 direct-output fast path. This was valid at the time because the path
  did not perform post-GEMM routed scaling.
- [#6220](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/6220) first added
  `routed_scaling_factor` to the reduction path without updating the
  down-projection output selection for top-1 routing. It introduced this exact
  mismatch, but was reverted by
  [#6968](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/6968).
- [#6970](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/6970) reintroduced the
  routed-scaling implementation. This is where the bug that remained in the
  current codebase came from.
- [#9269](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/9269) and
  [#23019](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23019) subsequently
  refactored and moved the code while preserving the faulty condition.
- [#22660](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/22660) later added
  `test_single_expert_routing`, including coverage for scaling factors `1.0`
  and `1.5`; it did not introduce the production bug. Because the invalid path
  reads uninitialized memory, the test failure was intermittent.

## Modification

Keep the intermediate path enabled for non-unit routed scaling factors. The
down-projection kernel now populates `intermediate_cache3` before the existing
scaled reduction. The unit-scaling top-1 fast path is unchanged.

The existing `test_single_expert_routing` coverage already exercises both
`1.0` and `1.5` scaling factors.

## Tests

- [Targeted H100 rerun](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35351058879): `test_fused_moe.py` passed, including `test_single_expert_routing`
- `python3 -m compileall -q python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py`
- `pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py`

## Checklist

- [x] Format the code with pre-commit.
- [x] Reuse the existing regression test.
- [x] No documentation update is needed.

title: [AMD][DSV4] fix: skip compressed-KV metadata on the draft worker in the HIP radix backend
author: amd-danli103
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
DeepSeek-V4 won't start on ROCm with any speculative algorithm. The draft worker dies during CUDA graph capture:

```
  File "python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py", line 922,
    in make_forward_metadata_from_raw_verify
  File "python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py", line 620,
    in init_forward_metadata_indexer
  File "python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py", line 1833, in _indexer_pool
    assert pool is not None, (
AssertionError: No indexer pool for compression ratio 4
```
A draft pool has no ratio-4 layer. Its ratios get overwritten, the checkpoint isn't consulted (`kv_cache_configurator.py:1361-1372`):
```python
if self.is_draft_worker:
    compression_ratios = [COMPRESS_RATIO_NEXTN_LAYER] * self.layer_info.num_effective_layers
else:
    compression_ratios = self.model_config.compress_ratios
```

`COMPRESS_RATIO_NEXTN_LAYER` is 0. #38798 then started filtering `compressed_pool_configs` to the ratios a model actually has (`deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py:948`), so the draft pool's `index_pools` is now empty, while three metadata builders in the HIP backend still pass `need_compress=True` unconditionally. Before that filter a ratio-4 indexer was always allocated and the draft worker found one it never used, which is why this went unnoticed.

Guarding the indexer alone isn't enough. The same builders then call `_attach_unified_kv_decode_streams`, which does
`csa_width=core.c4_sparse_page_indices.shape[1]` on a field that's `None` for the same reason, so the assert just becomes an `AttributeError`. That one only shows up under `SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton`; the assert happens either way.

Repro on `main` at `9784d5f979`, MI355X, ROCm 7.2. #40186 has to be applied first or startup dies earlier in pool sizing on an `UnboundLocalError`; it merged and current `main` already carries it.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
One file, `deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py` (ROCm only).

`need_compress` is derived once in `__init__` instead of being hardcoded `True` at three call sites. `init_forward_metadata_target_verify_old` passes it down to `init_forward_metadata_prefill`, which already has the guard; the two `make_forward_metadata_from_raw_*` builders skip the indexer and fall back to the existing `_create_dummy_paged_compress_data`.

`_attach_unified_kv_decode_streams` is the one that can't just be skipped, since the draft worker reads `unified.verify_store_state_slot` in its target-verify forward to write K into the SWA ring. It still builds the SWA streams and passes zero lengths, an `(N, 0)` page table and `csa_width=0` for the compressed half, which is already how `build_decode_streams` is told there's nothing compressed to read. No kernel or signature changed.

Target workers keep `need_compress=True` and take the same branches as before. `is_draft_worker` isn't a guess, it's the predicate the configurator itself branches on above.

## Verification

MI355X, TP8 + DP8, DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813, `unified_kv_triton`. Before/after differ only by this patch, both with #40186.

```bash
SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton \
SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_BATCHED_GEMM=1 \
SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=0 \
AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path <DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813> --attention-backend dsv4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --dp-size 8 --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head \
  --page-size 256 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.10 \
  --disable-shared-experts-fusion --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --max-running-requests 64 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 \
  --disable-radix-cache \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 5
```

| arm | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DSPARK` block-size 5 | assert, no server | up in 150 s, `/v1/chat/completions` answers |
| `EAGLE` 3/1/4 | assert, no server | assert gone, reaches the draft tree build (see below) |

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->
GSM8K, all 1319 questions, same server config as above with this patch applied. The two arms differ only by the speculative flag.

| arm                 | accuracy | invalid | latency | accept len       |
| ------------------- | -------- | ------- | ------- | ---------------- |
| DSPARK block-size 5 | 0.9363   | 0.000   | 124.4 s | 4.04 (3.67–4.41) |
| no speculation      | 0.9340   | 0.000   | 151.0 s | n/a              |

There is no before number to compare against: with speculation on, the server didn't start.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->
Not applicable. The new condition resolves from an attribute set in `__init__`, and the target path is unchanged.

## The second EAGLE/MTP blocker, since fixed upstream

When this PR was opened, DSpark served but EAGLE/MTP still did not. The assertion was gone, but the draft tree build then turned it away on a device check that only accepted CUDA:

```
  python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_utils.py:275 in build_tree_kernel_efficient
tvm.error.InternalError: Tensor match failed for Tensor<1, 3>[... device=rocm:2]
  at python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/speculative/tree.cuh:52
- Root cause: Device value [rocm:2] not in the allowed options: [cuda]
```

Three of `tree.cuh`'s `TensorMatcher` calls hardcoded `.with_device<kDLCUDA>(...)` while the rest took the device from the tensor, introduced with #40033. #40325 has since relaxed those three (lines 51, 141, 186) to `kDLGPU`, so that blocker is off `main` and nothing further is needed from this side.

title: Fix mxfp4 padding test stubbing an accessor the module no longer imports
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

`test_mxfp4_trtllm_padding.py` fails to even start on `main`:

```
AttributeError: <module 'sglang.srt.layers.quantization.mxfp4_flashinfer_trtllm_moe'>
does not have the attribute 'get_tp_group'
```

`patch.object(mxfp4, "get_tp_group", ...)` needs the accessor to be an attribute of
the module under test. That module now reads the group through
`get_parallel().tp_group` and no longer imports the free accessor, so the stub has
nothing to replace. The test is registered for CI (`base-b-kernel-unit`,
`4-gpu-b200`), so it is red on every run.

Stubbing `use_symmetric_memory` is not a substitute. Its argument is evaluated
before the context manager gets a chance to skip the allocation:

```python
with use_symmetric_memory(get_parallel().tp_group, disabled=...):
```

The group is read whatever the stub returns, so the read has to be answered rather
than bypassed.

## Modifications

The test states a TP group on the runtime context for the length of the block
instead of rebinding a module attribute:

```python
with (
    get_parallel().override(tp_group=None),
    patch.object(mxfp4, "is_allocation_symmetric", return_value=False),
    patch.object(mxfp4, "use_symmetric_memory", return_value=nullcontext()),
):
```

Same value the stub supplied (`None`), same two remaining stubs, one added import.
No production code changes.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: test-only change, and the value the test feeds the module is
unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

author: wookjeHan
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Fix missing SWA eviction during disaggregated decode preallocation for hybrid full-attention/SWA models using separate KV buffers.
Admission budgets include both free and evictable pages. However, `_pre_alloc()` previously reclaimed only full-attention pages. Resuming a retracted request could therefore pass admission but fail allocation with `KV cache is full!` because eligible SWA pages had not been evicted.

- Exclude request-ring and HiSparse allocation paths from SWA page reclamation.
- Include SWA capacity information in allocation-failure diagnostics.

title: [HiCache] fix: bound the controller reset join so a stalled storage thread cannot hang the scheduler
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

`HiCacheController.reset()` previously set `storage_stop_event` and called
untimed `join()` on four storage threads. If a thread does not exit, reset can
wait indefinitely and block the scheduler. This change hardens the reset
teardown by reusing the existing detach helper, `_stop_storage_threads()`.

## Modifications

`reset()` now uses the helper's queue wakeup sentinels, bounded joins, and final
thread-liveness check before clearing shared state and restarting storage threads.
Sentinels can wake threads waiting on queues; they cannot interrupt an in-progress
`all_reduce()`. Likewise, a join timeout only bounds the caller's wait and does
not terminate the worker or cancel its collective.

The helper joins four threads sequentially, with `timeout=10` for each, so the
combined join wait can reach approximately 40 seconds, not 10 seconds total.
After all joins, it raises `RuntimeError` if any thread remains alive. This prevents
reset from clearing shared state and starting replacement threads while an old
thread is still running. The queue clearing, stop-event clearing, and thread
re-creation after a successful stop remain unchanged.

A prefetch thread blocked in a cross-rank collective is a possible stalled-thread
scenario inferred from the source, not a reproduced failure. This PR bounds the
reset wait; it does not resolve the underlying collective stall. Treat it as a
hardening change pending validation of that scenario's reachability.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py` + `test_hicache_staged_write_back_dispatch.py`:
  1278 passed, 1436 skipped, 70 subtests.
- `test_storage_prefetch_lifecycle.py`, `test_unified_cache_linker.py`,
  `test_radix_cache_unit.py`: 95 passed, 71 subtests.

author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Restore CI paths broken by recent main-branch interface migrations. Scheduler/MLX profiler fixtures still provide ranks through `ps`, the Q8KV8 prefill fixture lacks `swa_kv_pool`, and ROCm speculative tree launches are rejected by a CUDA-only tensor device check.

These failures are present on main `567d5925fe`, independently of #39957. The rank consumers changed in #40071, the KV-pool access changed in #38792, and the tree wrappers moved to JIT in #40033.

## Modifications

- Use scoped `get_parallel().override(...)` in the idle-counter and MLX profiler tests, including the PP size/depth configuration.
- Give the Q8KV8 test pool the `swa_kv_pool.page_size` interface used by the backend.
- Use the existing platform-dependent `kDLGPU` in all three speculative tree entry points. It resolves to CUDA for CUDA builds and ROCm for HIP builds, while retaining the same-device checks for the remaining tensors.

Four existing files changed; existing assertions and kernel computation are unchanged. No new test files or CI skips.

## Accuracy Tests

Compared unmodified main against the patch:

| Existing tests | Main | Patched |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test_disagg_idle_step_counters.py` | Rank/group and PP fixture failures | 10 passed on Linux |
| `test_metal_profiler.py` | 1 failure out of 10: TP group not initialized | 10 passed on Apple Silicon, `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1`, PyTorch 2.13.0 / MLX 0.32.2 |
| `test_q8kv8_sparse_prefill_backend.py` | 3 failures: missing `swa_kv_pool` | 14 passed on H100 CI; 12 passed, 2 SM90-only tests skipped on GB300 |
| `test_build_eagle_tree.py`, `test_eagle_utils.py`, `test_ngram_utils.py` | — | 4 passed on both H100 CI and GB300 |

Pre-commit passed for all changed files. [Targeted H100 CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35435326799) passed all 18 tests on PR head `8985b2437bab2f119d53fa179d5fbef6469df3d5`, including the two SM90-only real-kernel cases. title: [DSV4] fix: size the C4 state ring by the page it is addressed by
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

The DSV4 C4 compress-state pool is allocated with twice the rows it can ever address.

Before this fix, two sides used a field spelled `swa_page_size` but held different quantities:

- **sizing** — `DSV4PoolConfigurator.swa_page_size = cfg.window_size` (128 for V4):
  `c4_state_pool_size = swa_tokens // swa_page_size * c4_ring_size`
- **addressing** — the pool's own `swa_page_size` is the scheduler page size (256,
  asserted in `kv_cache_configurator`):
  `translate_from_swa_loc_to_state_loc` does `swa_loc // swa_page_size * ring + swa_loc % ring`

So the ring is sized by the sliding window and indexed by the page. `c4_ring_size`
appears on both sides and cancels, leaving exactly `page_size / window_size` = **2x**.

Measured by driving the production `CompressStatePool` and the production
`translate_from_swa_loc_to_state_loc` on a GPU (`ratio=2.00` in every configuration):

| swa_tokens | spec | ring | allocated rows | reachable rows | ratio |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 262144 | no | 8 | 16396 | 8192 | 2.00x |
| 262144 | yes | 16 | 32788 | 16384 | 2.00x |
| 524288 | no | 8 | 32780 | 16384 | 2.00x |
| 524288 | yes | 16 | 65556 | 32768 | 2.00x |

Each C4 layer builds two such pools (attention state, head_dim 576; indexer state,
head_dim 128), so the waste is `176 B` per SWA token per C4 layer.

The same ratio also feeds `_get_bytes_per_swa_token`, so the per-token cost estimate is
inflated too and the token budget comes out smaller than the hardware allows. Both
effects come from the same two expressions.

**Impact.** `_unified_kv` is ROCm-only and off by default, so CUDA always takes the
SWA-addressed branch this patch fixes. Using the real `compress_ratios` from the
published checkpoints (V4-Flash: 21 ratio-4 layers of 43; V4-Pro: 30 of 61):

| model | phantom share of each SWA token | same memory buys | per 10k SWA tokens |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| V4-Flash | 10.5% | +11.7% SWA tokens | 35.2 MiB |
| V4-Pro | 10.5% | +11.8% SWA tokens | 50.4 MiB |

In absolute terms, 0.90 GiB/rank (V4-Flash, 262k SWA tokens) up to 5.16 GiB/rank
(V4-Pro, 1M SWA tokens), at PP=1.

## Modifications

`DSV4PoolConfigurator.swa_window_size` holds `cfg.window_size` for
`get_swa_ring_size`. `swa_page_size` holds `get_schedule().page_size` for C4 state
pool sizing and per-token byte accounting, matching the pool's addressing.

`test_dsv4_accepts_pool_above_floor` uses the page-size divisor (`3072 // 256 * 8`),
and its fixture sets `swa_page_size` to the supplied page size.

## Accuracy Tests

- Post-fix safety check on GPU, same probe: allocated rows now `>=` reachable rows with
  the pool's own `+ring+1` padding as headroom (12-20 rows), never under-allocated.

  | swa_tokens | spec | sized | allocated | reachable | headroom |
  |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | 262144 | no | 8192 | 8204 | 8192 | 12 |
  | 262144 | yes | 16384 | 16404 | 16384 | 20 |
  | 524288 | no | 16384 | 16396 | 16384 | 12 |
  | 524288 | yes | 32768 | 32788 | 32768 | 20 |

- `test/registered/unit/model_executor/` + `test_dsv4_hicache_l2.py`: 285 passed,
  145 subtests.

### End-to-end GSM8K accuracy (2026-09-24)

Tested head: `402d7de3c2d30c152fe866dbc03900d4fa87cc64`.
The baseline uses the same head with only `swa_page_size` restored to
`cfg.window_size`; the PR variant uses the original head without measurement
instrumentation. Runs were executed in baseline → PR → PR → baseline order,
with a fresh server process and a cache flush for each run.

- **Model/hardware:** DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 4×GB300, TP4/PP1, non-speculative,
  FP32 compress state, FP8 KV, `flashinfer_mxfp4`.
- **Checkpoint:** `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` revision
  `60d8d70770c6776ff598c94bb586a859a38244f1`; all 46 weight shards verified
  against the official SHA256 manifest.
- **Serving:** automatic token capacity, `swa-full-tokens-ratio=0.1`,
  `mem-fraction-static=0.70`, context length 32768.
- **Evaluation:** all 1,319 GSM8K test questions, zero-shot Chat API with native
  DSV4 encoding, thinking disabled, temperature 0, top_p 1, seed 42,
  max_tokens 4096, fixed cohorts of 16 concurrent requests. Responses were
  requested to end with `#### <numeric answer>` and scored using this head's
  `sglang.test.simple_eval_mixed_prefix_gsm8k.get_answer_value`.

| Variant | Run 1 | Run 2 | Mean accuracy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline (old sizing) | 1280/1319 (97.0432%) | 1277/1319 (96.8158%) | 96.9295% |
| PR | 1276/1319 (96.7400%) | 1280/1319 (97.0432%) | 96.8916% |

The mean difference is **−0.0379 percentage points**, smaller than the
within-version rerun changes (0.2274 points for the baseline and 0.3033 for
the PR). A paired bootstrap over questions, retaining both runs per question,
gives a descriptive 95% interval of **[−0.3033, +0.2274] percentage points**.

All **5,276 evaluation requests succeeded**, with **zero invalid answers and
zero length truncations**. No question was correct in both baseline runs and
wrong in both PR runs. Cross-version predicted answers matched on 1310/1319
and 1309/1319 questions; within-version reruns matched on 1311/1319 and
1308/1319 questions, respectively.

**Conclusion:** no stable GSM8K accuracy regression was observed in this
configuration. Full response text is not bitwise identical, including across
reruns of the same version. This does not establish universal equivalence or
cover AIME, Pro, speculative decoding, long-context accuracy, or saturated-cache
behavior. The pool-level checks above establish a separate allocation/addressing
property, not model accuracy.

title: [Fix] Keep mHC context out of non-V4 compiled MoE forwards
author: BBuf
body:
DeepSeek-R1's compiled prefill path now fails during startup with `Dynamo does not know how to trace method get of class ContextVar`. The mHC overlap hooks added in #39704 are reached by non-V4 models through the shared `DeepseekV2MoE` implementation, even though these models never install an mHC context.

Store the existing `is_deepseek_v4` constructor flag and use it to guard the new context lookups in both normal and dual-stream MoE forwards. Non-V4 models retain their usual all-reduce path; V4 retains its mHC stats scheduling before all-reduce.

Failure: [post-merge AMD MI35x job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35442575830/job/105895883223), `TestDeepseekR1MXFP4.setUpClass` in `test_deepseek_r1_mxfp4_8gpu.py` with `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill=tc_piecewise`.

Validation:

- Applicable pre-commit hooks, `git diff --check`, [PR lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35444621183), and all 10 [Base CPU CI partitions](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35444621535) pass.
- CPU harness executes the actual `forward_normal` function body with GPU operations stubbed, using `torch.compile(backend="eager", fullgraph=True)`. On both PyTorch 2.9.1 and 2.11.0, the original code reproduces the `ContextVar.get` error for TP4/TP8 with both empty and nonempty batches; all six TP1/4/8 × empty/nonempty cases pass after the fix. This isolates compiler/control-flow behavior, not GPU numerics.
- Eager checks retain the V4 context callback for TP4/TP8 and leave TP1 unchanged.
- All three existing [AMD MI35x test shards](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35444636712) pass on this PR head. [Partition 2](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35444636712/job/105901392505) passes all four DeepSeek-R1 tests: compiled-prefill GSM8K 0.94693 and BS1 speed 151.46 token/s; MTP GSM8K 0.945 and BS1 speed 232.89 token/s. Its Kimi K2.5 and Qwen3-Coder-Next tests also pass. The original ContextVar error is absent. These are existing CI checks, not a controlled performance comparison. No CI thresholds or test coverage are removed.

title: [Fix] [NPU] dspark: Fix attn_tp > 1 draft wo_b all_reduce group
author: unclezhou486
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
DSpark speculative decoding with a DeepSeek-V4 (MoE) draft supports DP attention
(`attn_tp_size < tp_size`) on Ascend NPU, but the draft attention's output
projection `wo_b` reduced its partial results over the wrong process group,
which corrupted the draft output and collapsed the accept rate to ~0.

`DSparkAttention` (`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4_dspark.py`) subclasses
`MqaAttentionBase` and hard-codes `wo_b_reduce_results=True`, overriding the
base's default `reduce_results = (attn_tp_size == tp_size and attn_tp_size > 1)`.
As a result, under DP attention (`attn_tp_size < tp_size`) `wo_b` still performed
a row-parallel all-reduce, but over the **full DP × TP** group, while its weight
is sharded over the **attn-TP** group only. That summed partial outputs that
belong to different DP ranks' _different_ batches, so the draft attention output
was garbage and the accept rate collapsed to ~0.

A guard in `DSparkWorkerV2` rejected this whole configuration
(`attn_tp > 1` + DP attention + MoE draft), which blocked the feature on NPU.

(Note: the guard's error string referred to the "MoE-under-DP all-reduce", but
the actual corruption was the draft attention's `wo_b` reduce group; the draft
MoE path itself handles `attn_tp > 1` via `_dp_gather_via_all_gather`.)

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Modifications

1. `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`
   - `MqaAttentionBase.wo_b` now passes
     `use_dp_attention_reduce=is_dp_attention_enabled()`, so its row-parallel
     all-reduce runs over the attn-TP group (`get_parallel().attn_tp_group`)
     when DP attention is enabled, matching the weight sharding.
   - `DSparkAttention.forward` calls `self.wo_b(...)` directly (it does not use
     `_project_wo_b`), so this single flag fixes the draft reduce with no
     double-reduce.

2. `python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py`
   - Allow the `attn_tp > 1` MoE-draft + DP-attention configuration on NPU by
     adding `and not _is_npu` to the guard. CUDA/ROCm still reject it.

3. `python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/attention/ascend_dsv4_backend.py`
   - Pad the draft `ori_sparse_indices` tail with `-1` ("skip") up to the
     attn-TP-padded token count, matching `out_cache_loc`
     (`prepare_mlp_sync_batch` pads the query to an attn_tp multiple, but
     `seq_lens` is not).

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

## Accuracy Tests

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

title: [Fix] dsv4: Skip DP-attention pad rows in the engram hasher and low-ratio sources
author: JiaShuai0209
body:
## Motivation

With DP attention and `attn_tp_size > 1`, `prepare_mlp_sync_batch` pads each DP rank's token count up to a multiple of `attn_tp_size`. The pad rows sit after the live tokens, and `extend_seq_lens` covers only the live tokens. Two DeepSeek V4.1 paths did not expect those rows and crashed the scheduler.

### Crash 1: `EngramHasher` on a padded idle batch

An idle DP rank runs an IDLE forward with pad rows to stay in lockstep. `EngramHasher.forward` fell through to `assert mode.is_extend()`:

    engram serves extend, target-verify and decode, not 4

### Crash 2: low-ratio sources on a padded eager extend

At metadata init, an eager extend already builds the low-ratio request ids and positions over the live tokens (`low_ratio_req_indices`, `low_ratio_pos_i64`). With pad rows, `positions` is longer than those rows, so `forward_low_ratio_sources` skipped them and rebuilt request ids with `token_req_indices(num_tokens=positions.shape[0])`. That `repeat_interleave` has an `output_size` larger than the sum of `extend_seq_lens`; the extra ids are uninitialized, and the compressor hit a CUDA device-side assert.

## Modifications

- `forward_low_ratio_sources`: when the prebuilt rows are shorter than `positions`, slice `x`, `q_lora`, and `positions` to those rows, then use the prebuilt request ids and positions. Indexer outputs are reset to -1 before each write, so the pad rows stay masked.
- `EngramHasher.forward`: an IDLE batch takes the same early return as an empty one, with zero hashes, and never writes engram history.

No behavior change on any path where the prebuilt rows are not shorter than `positions`: prefill CUDA graph, eager breaks inside it, the late-layer tail, decode, and target verify. An IDLE batch with tokens previously always hit the assert.

## Accuracy Tests

Model outputs on live tokens are unchanged; only pad rows and idle output, which are discarded, are affected. Selected V4.1 accuracy and unit tests are running through `/rerun-test`. No CI test runs V4.1 with DP attention and `attn_tp_size > 1`, so the crash itself is covered only by the original repro (DP attention, CUDA graph on and off): it ran to completion on the first version of this fix and has not been rerun on the current one.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

No perf impact expected: the idle path returns early, and the padded extend works on fewer rows.

- [x] Format with pre-commit

title: [Test] Fix OOT DFlash hook test resolving the draft config over the network
author: hnyls2002
body:
`test/registered/unit/spec/test_oot_dflash_hooks.py` has been red on `base-a-test-cpu` since it landed in #38740, for two independent reasons.

- It drove the whole `handle_speculative_decoding` hook to test one decision. That hook also resolves the speculative algorithm alias, which calls `get_config(speculative_draft_model_path)` -- and the fixture passes the placeholder `"draft"`, so the CPU lane tries to reach HuggingFace and fails with `OSError: draft is not a local folder`. The test mocks `current_platform` and `attention_backends_of` but not this path.
- It read the result back as `args.speculative_draft_attention_backend`. `declare_resolution` records into the declaration stash and never writes the field, so that read returns the input. Three of the assertions would still fail once the network error was gone; the two that passed did so because input and expectation happened to match.

Call `_resolve_dflash_draft_attention_backend` directly (the same pattern `test_uno_tree_config.py` uses for `_handle_uno`) and read the outcome through `resolution_result`. The resolver has no HF lookup on the paths these cases take -- `trtllm_mha` is rejected by `is_supported_backend` before the branch that would load a config -- so the fixture needs no new mock, and a future step added to the hook no longer breaks this test.

title: [Fix] [NPU] requantization: gate arch35 block-FP8 -> MXFP8 requantization
author: iridiumine
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #39823. That PR made plain block-FP8 checkpoints (fp32 block scales) on arch35 (Atlas A5) requantize to MXFP8 at load time unconditionally, so dense linears run on the native quantized GEMM instead of the Triton emulation path.

As raised in the post-merge review of #39823: fp8 per-block quantization with fp32 scaling factors is semantically different from MXFP8. Only DeepSeek-style UE8M0 checkpoints can be converted losslessly (a 128×128 block's power-of-two scale can be duplicated to its 1×32 sub-blocks exactly). For plain fp32-scale checkpoints, the load-time conversion is a lossy re-quantization (dequant to BF16 → npu_dynamic_mx_quant , granularity 128×128 → 1×32, scales rounded to powers of two), which changes the checkpoint numerics:

- Dataset-level evals are largely insensitive to this error magnitude
- Training-time consumers are not: e.g. RL rollouts served by sglang vs. reference logprobs computed elsewhere can see importance-ratio drift from the systematic numerics change
The safe default should be to serve the checkpoint as-is; the native-GEMM path should be opt-in for deployments that have validated accuracy for their workload.

## Modifications

- environ.py : add SGLANG_NPU_ARCH35_REQUANT_BLOCK_FP8 (default False )
- Fp8LinearMethod.process_weights_after_loading : only enter process_npu_arch35_mxfp8_linear_weights for UE8M0 checkpoints (lossless re-layout, unchanged) or when the env var is set; plain block-FP8 checkpoints now fall through to the generic path and keep their original layout
- fp8_utils._dispatch_auto_backend : select npu_w8a8_mxfp8_linear under the same condition ( act_scale_ue8m0 or the env var) — this must stay in sync with the weight-layout gate, otherwise the kernel and layout mismatch. arch35 + plain block-FP8 now resolves to triton_w8a8_block_fp8_linear
- w8a8_mxfp8.py : docstring updated to document the gate

## Accuracy Tests

No numeric output changes by design:

- Default path (env unset) restores the pre-#39823 bit-faithful serving path for fp32-scale checkpoints — Triton emulation on the untouched checkpoint layout
- UE8M0 checkpoints are unaffected (lossless path, unconditional)
- env=1 is opt-in and numerically identical to what #39823 shipped
Dispatch verified locally for all three combinations (mocked is_npu_arch35 ): env-unset + fp32 scales → triton_w8a8_block_fp8_linear ; env=1 + fp32 scales → npu_w8a8_mxfp8_linear ; env-unset + ue8m0 → npu_w8a8_mxfp8_linear . Also verified the fall-through path stays clean: requant_block_scale_ue8m0_for_deepgemm is a no-op without DeepGEMM, and block_fp8_as_mxfp8 requires UE8M0 + 32-wide K blocks so it cannot mis-enable on plain block-FP8.

Behavior matrix on arch35:

| Checkpoint | Env var | Weight layout | GEMM |
|---|---|---|---|
| UE8M0 (DeepSeek V3.1+) | any | MXFP8 re-layout (lossless) | native (unchanged) |
| fp32 block scales | unset (default) | plain block-FP8 | Triton emulation (pre-#39823 behavior) |
| fp32 block scales | `=1` | MXFP8 (lossy requant) | native (perf path, as merged in #39823) |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

None — this PR adds no new fast path. The perf characteristics of each path are unchanged from #39823: native MXFP8 GEMM vs. Triton emulation (~100ms per large-M linear) applies only when the env var is explicitly enabled.
