title: [Simulator] Fix meta host memory budgets on constrained runners
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

After #40135, HiCache checks available host memory through a scoped, cgroup-aware budget. The CPU simulator still overrides module-local `psutil`, so metadata-only host pools can fail initialization on smaller runners with `Not enough host memory available`. The scheduler then kills the parent pytest process, leaving only exit code 137 in captured CI output ([example](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35501289844/job/106056052533)).

## Modifications

Initialize simulated host pools directly within `host_memory_budget_scope`. Remove the obsolete `_PsutilProxy` and legacy fallback. Keep the import inside the helper so native pool classes are loaded after simulator hooks are installed. Disable pytest output capture for simulator CI so fatal worker tracebacks remain visible.

Two files, three added lines and 27 deleted lines; no new tests or production-runtime changes.

## Validation

- Before merging main, reproduced startup failure with the CI run's prebuilt Rust extensions under a 12 GiB cgroup limit; the scoped-budget fix passed all nine existing simulator tests under the same limit.
- [GitHub simulator CI passed](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35504114385/job/106060987180) on `24728e8fbe`.
- Merged main at `efa7be2091`, preserving its simulator implementation and test updates exactly. Pre-commit checks passed after conflict resolution and simplification. Focused source-isolated checks verified budget restoration on success and exceptions, argument/result forwarding, and explicit failure when the required interface is absent. The full simulator suite has not been rerun after the merge and simplification.

title: [Fix][NPU] fix dp-attn hang when pin_mem is True on NPU
author: litmei
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

In theory, the NPU platform supports `pin_memory=True` just like the CUDA platform. Combined with `non_blocking=True`, this allows host-to-device operations to be performed completely asynchronously. However, with the current implementation, enabling `pin_memory=True` causes non-DSA models in the DP-Attn scenario to hang.

Also see [issue 38971](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/38971).

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->


For this sample ci test case (NPUGraph, DP-ATTN, MLA arch):

```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /path/to/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-W8A8 --trust-remote-code --tp 2 --dp 2 --enable-dp-attention --chunked-prefill-size 1024 --attention-backend ascend --device npu --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8880 --max-running-requests 32 --cuda-graph-bs-decode 2 8 16
```

Do gsm8k test:

```
python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 1600 --num-shots 2 --data-path /path/to/gsm8k.josnl --max-new-tokens 512 --parallel 4 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8880
```

If we change the return value of `NPUDeviceMixin.is_pin_memory_available` to `True`, the system will occasionally hang during normal inference. The dumped stacks typically show Prefill on one side and Decode on the other, with one side having just transitioned from the IDLE state.

I set `TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=0` to rule out the impact of operator submission order. I also compared the `plog` logs from both cards and ruled out issues involving extra or missing communication operations. In addition, I injected hooks through the WatchDog framework to collect the inputs to the DP operators on both sides, as well as the inputs used for graph replay on both sides. All of these inputs appeared to be correct.

I then narrowed down the issue to `_local_decode_cuda_graph_vote`. When modified so that one side returns `False` and falls back to Eager mode as soon as it detects an IDLE state, the hang no longer occurs. However, with this change, a single cURL request will no longer follow the graph execution path, resulting in a significant performance degradation.

Further investigation narrowed it down to `AscendAttnBackend.forward_decode_graph`. After commenting out the CANN-style FIA operator executed by DSV2 and directly returning `query`, the hang also disappeared. The issue was narrowed down to the FIA operator.

Eventually, I identified the root cause as `NPUCudaGraphBackend.replay_with_input_update`. Adding a synchronization operation at this point resolves the hang. The final solution is to retrieve the Event from the graph operation and synchronize the Event from the previous iteration before executing the graph in the next iteration, ensuring safe graph execution.

title: [Fix] Keep Inkling automatic tool grammar active across the response
author: jshanson7
body:
## Motivation

With reasoning enabled, `ReasonerGrammarObject` defers constraints until the encoded reasoning-end marker is observed. Inkling emits the native `END_MESSAGE` token (`200010`), while encoding its printed spelling as ordinary text produces a different token sequence. The wrapper can therefore remain in its reasoning phase and never apply the automatic tool-call grammar, even after a thinking or text block.

For example, this synthetic token stream leaves the outer JSON object open (the marker spellings below represent native framing tokens):

```text
<|message_model|><|content_invoke_tool_json|>{"name":"tool","args":{}
```

Previously, both native `END_MESSAGE` and `CONTENT_MODEL_END_SAMPLING` remained allowed at this point. With this change, both are masked until the JSON is complete; adding the missing `}` permits the tool block to close and the response to terminate.

## Modifications

- In non-strict mode, return the canonical Inkling automatic tool grammar directly so it sees the entire response. This schema permits reasoning and ordinary text outside native tool triggers and owns the tool payload's boundaries.
- Identify that exception by comparing the complete decoded schema with the existing canonical builder. Matching only `token_triggered_tags` would be too broad: modified schemas can require a tag, exclude a reasoning terminator, or trigger on ordinary text. Those schemas retain reasoning deferral, as do other answer constraints.
- Resolve the scheduler's reasoning-end IDs through the reasoning detector, using Inkling's native ID and preserving the existing tokenizer encoding for other detectors. Ordinary text tokenization is unchanged.
- Add real XGrammar mask regressions for direct, thinking-prefixed, and text-prefixed tool calls; incomplete and complete JSON; plain text and literal marker strings; and modified schemas. Preserve strict-thinking behavior, the `full_assistant_ebnf` bypass, and the existing CPU CI registrations; use `CustomTestCase` for the registered test file.

This change covers the canonical automatic tool schema in non-strict mode and native reasoning-end ID resolution. It does not change required/named tool schemas or claim to fix the separate no-thinking `reasoning_tokens` overcount tracked in #34634.

## Accuracy Tests

Revalidated on PR head `01b8d93ebd6b3341a0f64f892886c2187eef0e76` (including upstream `367e3700cfb6a0b03b2fa41a4524febf18ec1f15`) on 2026-09-22, using Python 3.13.13, PyTorch 2.13.0, and XGrammar 0.2.1 on macOS/Apple Silicon. These are CPU component tests with a synthetic vocabulary; no model weights or serving process were used.

**Before:** on upstream `791c7850d0960fd768102f71e7d999b036bb75ba`, with only the new test file applied, this selection reported four failures: the three reasoning-enabled tool-mask subcases allow premature termination, and scheduler initialization returns the printed marker's token sequence instead of native ID `200010`.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest \
  test/registered/unit/constrained/test_reasoner_grammar_backend.py \
  -k 'inkling_tool_masks_cover_the_whole_stream or inkling_scheduler_uses_native_reasoning_end' \
  -q --disable-warnings --tb=short
```

**After:** all **183 tests and 114 subtests pass** across the three suites, including those regressions:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest \
  test/registered/unit/constrained/test_reasoner_grammar_backend.py \
  test/registered/unit/parser/test_reasoning_parser.py \
  test/registered/unit/parser/test_inkling_renderer.py \
  -q --disable-warnings --tb=short
```

The direct-file CI entry point also passes **34 tests** with fail-fast enabled:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python \
  test/registered/unit/constrained/test_reasoner_grammar_backend.py -f
```

All applicable pre-commit checks pass, including formatting, lint, syntax, and test registration:

```bash
pre-commit run --files \
  python/sglang/srt/constrained/reasoner_grammar_backend.py \
  python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py \
  python/sglang/srt/parser/reasoning_parser.py \
  test/registered/unit/constrained/test_reasoner_grammar_backend.py
```

GPU execution, live serving, full-model generation, and end-to-end accuracy evaluations were not run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run. Schema comparison occurs during grammar dispatch; the canonical grammar now also applies its masks during the reasoning prefix. No throughput, latency, or profiling results are claimed.

- [x] Add focused regression tests using the public CPU test conventions and verify failure before the fix.

title: fix(dsv4): ship the fp8 unified_kv rope pool through the direct external linker
author: TianDi101
body:
## Problem

Under `SGLANG_DSV4_UNIFIED_KV_FP8=1` a unified_kv row is **two parallel pools** —
`unified_kv_pool.kv_buffer` (512 B packed fp8 nope) and `unified_kv_pool.kv_buffer_rope`
(128 B bf16 rope) — and one row index addresses both.

`_build_deepseek_v4_device_pool_group()` registers the compressed regions through
`_dsv4_compressed_region_buffers()` → `unified_region_buffers()`, which returns **the nope
pool only**. The direct external linker therefore offloads and restores 512 of every 640
bytes, and the rope half of a restored row keeps whatever the slot last held.

HiCache already ships the sibling (`_dsv4_rope_sibling` / `_build_dsv4_rope_entry` in
`hybrid_pool_assembler.py`); this is the linker-side mirror of it. It is backend-agnostic —
`umbp_direct_linker.py` and `mooncake_direct_linker.py` both resolve through
`resolve_hybrid_device_pool_group()`.

## Why nothing catches it

`DevicePoolEntry` derives its row stride and page size from the buffers it is handed and has
no view of the logical row width, so a short row is not a crash — it is wrong output. That is
what the pool's own docstring on `unified_rope_region_buffers()` warns about.

There is also no full-resolution fallback to mask it. With the unified layout the SWA pool is
a per-request ring, so `unified_cache_linker.py` sets `_skip_swa` and tombstones the range as
`swa_evicted_seqlen`. A linker-restored prefix therefore exists *only* as compressed c4/c128
rows, and `unified_kv_kernels/runtime.py` passes `unified_kv_rope` to both paged decode and
paged prefill as the prefix pool.

## Evidence

A plain before/after A/B **cannot** see this: `/flush_cache` frees device rows without
overwriting them, so a nope-only restore lands on rope that is still correct for exactly
those tokens. gsm8k accuracy was unchanged across five configurations up to 81.7% linker
exposure, including one that wrote 560k tokens of unrelated KV between the flushes.

To get a real signal, fill the compressed rope rows with a marker at flush time and count how
many still carry it after the next pass. DeepSeek-V4-Pro, MI355X (gfx950), TP8 +
DP-attention, `--page-size 256`, EAGLE MTP, UMBP direct external linker; gsm8k, 200
questions, temperature 0, warm → flush → measure:

| pass | marker written at flush | before this PR | with this PR |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 1 (cold) | none | 0.965 | 0.975 |
| 2 | rope pool | **0.775** | **0.955** |
| 3 | rope + nope pools | 0.825 | 0.975 |

Rope rows written during pass 2, mean per rank, of 181,136,962: **67,465 before** vs
**268,858 with this PR**. Without the fix only the extend fraction is written — 99.96% of
rows keep the marker, and the model reads them.

## Test

`test_unified_deepseek_v4_fp8_ships_the_rope_half` fails on `main` (and only that test) and
passes with the fix. The existing bf16 unified test gains an explicit
`unified_rope_region_buffers` stub returning `None`, pinning that the bf16 path ships exactly
what it did before. `test_linker_pool_assembler.py`: 10 passed before, 11 passed after.

## Scope

`unified_rope_region_buffers()` returns `None` on every non-fp8 layout, so bf16 unified and
all other layouts are untouched. For fp8 unified_kv the linker now moves the rope half as
well: 512 → 640 B per row transferred.

title: [Fix] moe: Preserve negative routing sentinel in EP mapping
author: willhu-jpg
body:
## Motivation

`select_experts` marks padded routing rows with `topk_ids = -1`. Under expert
parallelism, `StandardDispatcher` translated IDs with
`local_expert_mapping[topk_ids]`; PyTorch negative indexing therefore mapped the
drop sentinel through the table's final entry.

On the EP rank that owns the final expert, every padded top-k slot can therefore
collapse onto that expert and violate dispatch capacity assumptions.

## Modifications

- Preserve negative routing sentinels while translating valid global expert IDs
  to local IDs.
- Add a CPU dispatcher regression test covering a mix of padded, local, and
  non-local expert IDs.

title: [Fix] Raise on undelivered embeddings in `send_with_url`, fix broken tests
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Summary
- `send_with_url` reported an embedding that reached no destination as a success; it now raises
- Fix three tests that were broken independently of that change

## Encoder delivery
- `send_with_url` logged delivery failures and returned normally, so a request whose embedding reached nobody was answered with HTTP 200 and counted as `status="success"` in `encoder_requests_total`
- Raise instead, so the existing error path in `execute_encode_pipeline` reports it: 504 on destination timeout, 502 on send failure
- A cancelled per-destination send also delivered nothing, and `CancelledError` is not an `Exception`, so it now counts as failed; outer cancellation never reaches that loop because `gather` re-raises it
- The success path is unchanged: with no failure recorded, control flow is identical to before

## Test fixes
**Encoder rendezvous (2 tests, same root cause)**
- `test_encoder_server_metrics.py` and `TestEPDDisaggregationGrpcEncoderOnly` each registered a receive URL and only then issued the encode call
- The encoder creates the request state when the encode dispatches, so a serial register-then-encode blocks the registration for its full `SGLANG_ENCODER_REQ_TIMEOUT` and drops it; the HTTP one then also waited out `SGLANG_ENCODER_SEND_TIMEOUT`
- A scheduler issues both concurrently (`_start_registration` submits in the background); both tests now do the same and assert the registration result
- `test_encoder_server_metrics.py` drops from ~390s to ~35s, back to its registered `est_time=32`; the gRPC one went from a 90s `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` to passing in 39s

**NVFP4 MoE dispatch fake**
- `_trtllm_prepared_layer()` builds a `SimpleNamespace` layer but omitted `_mega_moe_nvfp4`, which `FusedMoE.__init__` sets and `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod.apply` reads, so all three cases raised `AttributeError` on `base-a-test-cpu` (failfast reported only the first)
- Add the field, matching how `test_mega_moe_deepgemm_api.py` already builds its fake

## Not covered
- Multi-destination delivery (`receive_count > 1`) is where the new failure semantics matter most, but the tests that exercise it (`TestEPDDisaggregationMultiEncoders`) are skipped in CI, so this PR does not verify it

title: [Fix] [NPU] qwen: Fix shared-expert routing with Ascend FuseEP
author: McZyWu
body:
## Motivation

Qwen3.5-35B-A3B with ModelSlim W8A8 produces garbled output with `--moe-a2a-backend ascend_fuseep --fuseep-mode 2 --tp-size 4`, while the unfused baseline answers the same prompts correctly.

`Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock`, also used by Qwen3.5, omits FuseEP from its dispatch/combine path. FuseEP has already combined routed experts for each source token, but the block keeps a TP-sharded shared expert and applies the ordinary TP all-reduce to different ranks' token rows.

## Changes

Include Ascend FuseEP in the existing shared-expert dispatch/combine path in `qwen2_moe.py`:

- Construct the shared expert with `tp_rank=0, tp_size=1`.
- Initialize the expert-parallel metadata.
- Route through `_forward_deepep` to add the complete shared contribution without the ordinary TP all-reduce.

## Validation

Previously recorded A3 validation of this model change used Qwen3.5-35B-A3B W8A8, TP4, and FuseEP mode 2. Concurrent arithmetic changed from garbled output to all four correct answers. Against the unfused baseline, aligned input-logprob mean absolute error decreased from 5.716665 to 0.051821, and maximum error decreased from 21.028971 to 0.451154.

The runtime model change is unchanged from that validation. The final PR diff is limited to `qwen2_moe.py`; both test trees match the PR merge base. Python syntax and diff checks pass. No new NPU inference run was performed for this test-only removal.

title: [sgl-router] Fix reorg admission proxy test build after BucketResolver::new
author: ShangmingCai
body:
Stacked on #40271 — **merge #40271 first**. Until it lands, the diff here also shows its commit; afterwards this PR is the three-file change below.

## Problem

`BucketResolver::new` returns `Result<Self, PickError>` as of #40366, which added `bucket.validate()`. The proxy test added in #40271 was written against the older infallible signature, so the `proxy` test target does not compile:

```

error: could not compile `sgl-router` (test "proxy")
```

This is not visible on #40271's checks: the `PR Test (sgl-router)` gate reported *"PR is missing the 'run-ci' label; skipping sgl-router tiers"* and finished green in 24s without building the crate.

## Fix

- Unwrap the `Result`, matching the existing helper at `reorg.rs:127` in the same file.
- Drop the last references to `AllowAll`, which #40271 replaced with `AdmissionLimits::default()` — three in `POLICY_DESIGN.md` and one comment in `session_aware.rs`.

No behavior change: `ChatRouting::Reorg` is constructed only in tests, and `AdmissionLimits::default()` admits everything.

title: fix(cuda-graph): remove unnecessary CP batch alignment
author: AMD-yanfeiwang
body:
### Summary

Decode CUDA graph capture aligned batch sizes to `attn_cp_size`, even though prefill CP is inactive for `DECODE` and `TARGET_VERIFY`. DCP and `--enable-cp-decode-attn-tp` partition KV/head dimensions rather than token rows, so they do not require CP-width batch alignment.

Remove the CP factor while retaining the existing TBO and gathered-buffer attention-TP alignment.

## AgentX performance

This result requires the combined [#34200](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34200), [#39950](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39950), and [#40543](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40543) stack: HIP CP-v2 support, correct AITER B-preshuffled slicing, and removal of unnecessary CP decode-graph alignment.

Single-node DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 on 8×MI355X, TP8, DSpark gamma 6, static verify, 3,600 seconds per point. C4/C16 use GPU KV; C32/C48/C64 use HiCache. `PCP8 + DTP` enables `--enable-prefill-cp --attn-cp-size 8 --enable-cp-decode-attn-tp`.

Values are `TP8 → PCP8 + DTP`; latency is lower-is-better and throughput is higher-is-better. Deltas are relative to TP8.

| C | TTFT avg | TTFT p90 | TPOT avg | TPOT p90 | Total tok/s/GPU | Output tok/s/GPU |

author: kangwangamd
body:
## Motivation
`test_kimi_k3_kda_decode.py` fails at **import**  as AITER is advanced to [`f0966b0ae`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/f0966b0aed0b38198e2e1ca1cff8cca343bbcb7e); 
due to aiter removed aiter.ops.flydsl.utils see table below
**Two independent AITER removals are involved, and only the first is test-only:**

| # | AITER file removed | AITER commit | breaks in SGLang |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `aiter/ops/flydsl/utils.py` | [`3b2a9ce60`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/3b2a9ce60) ([#5116](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5116), 09-02) | `is_flydsl_available` — **test only** |
| 2 | `aiter/ops/flydsl/kernels/vector.py` | [`08d73a192`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/08d73a192) ([#5303](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5303), 09-09) | `from aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels import vector` — **production kernel code** |

## Modifications

**3 files, +4 / −14.** No behaviour change on the current pin.

### 1. Test — `test/registered/kernels/ops/kimi_k3/flydsl_ops/test_kimi_k3_kda_decode.py`

```diff
 pytest.importorskip("flydsl")
-from aiter.jit.utils.chip_info import get_gfx
-from aiter.ops.flydsl.utils import is_flydsl_available
+pytest.importorskip("aiter")

-def _gfx950_flydsl_available() -> bool:
-    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or not is_flydsl_available():
-        return False
-    try:
-        return get_gfx() == "gfx950"
-    except (AssertionError, KeyError, RuntimeError):
-        return False
-
 pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
-    not _gfx950_flydsl_available(),
+    not is_flydsl_kimi_k3_kda_decode_supported(),
     reason="gfx950 FlyDSL required",
 )
```

The removed gate asked three things; all three are still answered:

| old condition | now covered by |
|---|---|
| `torch.cuda.is_available()` | first line of `is_flydsl_kimi_k3_kda_decode_supported()` |
| `is_flydsl_available()` | `pytest.importorskip("flydsl")` + `importorskip("aiter")` — under AITER's new contract, importing `aiter.ops.flydsl` already fails when flydsl is missing or too old |
| `get_gfx() == "gfx950"` | `_rocm_arch(device) == "gfx950"` inside the same function (reads `gcnArchName`) |

`is_flydsl_kimi_k3_kda_decode_supported()` is **already imported by this test** and is the predicate the
production code itself uses to decide whether this kernel can run — so the skip condition can no longer
drift from what the kernel actually supports, which the duplicated local helper could.

### 2. Production kernels — `kimi_k3_kda_decode.py` and `kimi_k3_kda_decode_fb.py`

One line each, under `python/sglang/kernels/ops/kimi_k3/flydsl/kernels/`:

+from flydsl._mlir.dialects import vector

title: [NPU][CI] Fix paths-filter negation that makes every PR run the NPU tier
author: ShangmingCai
body:
## Problem

`.github/workflows/pr-test-npu.yml` runs on every `pull_request` and gates the NPU stages on a `dorny/paths-filter` result. Since #39411 the `main_package` filter has been:

```yaml
main_package:
  - "python/sglang/**/!(*.md)"
  - "!python/sglang/multimodal_gen/**"
  - "!python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/**"
  - ...
```

`dorny/paths-filter` ORs the patterns within one filter — `predicate-quantifier` defaults to `some`, visible in every run log — and picomatch treats a leading `!` as inversion of the rest of the pattern. So `!python/sglang/multimodal_gen/**` matches *every* file that is not under `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/`, and `main_package` is `true` for any change anywhere in the repo.

Consequences:

- Every PR since 2026-09-15 has run the full `base-a-test-1-npu-a2` -> `base-b-test-*-npu-a3` tier, including router-only, docs-only and `sgl-kernel`-only PRs. For example #40271 and #40537 touch only `experimental/sgl-router/**`, and the GPU suites correctly skip on them while all NPU base stages run.
- The exclusions never worked for their intended purpose either: a `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/**` change still sets `main_package = true` via the *other* negation entry.

Evaluating the predicate for a few paths under the current filter (leading `!` = inversion, filter = OR over patterns):

| changed file | `main_package` | matched by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `experimental/sgl-router/src/policies_reorg/admission.rs` | `true` | both `!...` entries |
| `README.md` | `true` | both `!...` entries |
| `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/engine.py` | `true` | `python/sglang/**/!(*.md)`, `!.../diffusion/**` |

## Fix

Keep every pattern positive and express the exclusions as extglobs inside a single pattern — the idiom already used by `_pr-test-check-changes.yml` (`python/sglang/!(multimodal_gen|kernels)/**/!(*.md)`, `python/sglang/kernels/!(aot)/**/!(*.md)`) and by this workflow before #39411.

Setting `predicate-quantifier: every` is not an option here, since it would also AND the unrelated `python/pyproject_npu.toml` / `test/registered/npu/**` entries.

Filter semantics after the change — the intent of #39411 is preserved, including its widening of `main_package` to `python/sglang/srt/**` and to top-level `python/sglang/*` files:

| changed file | `main_package` |
| --- | --- |
| `experimental/sgl-router/**`, `docs/**`, `sgl-kernel/**` | `false` |
| `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/engine.py` | `false` |
| `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/triton/npu_fallback.py` | `false` |
| `python/sglang/srt/README.md` | `false` |
| `python/sglang/srt/server_args.py` | `true` |
| `python/sglang/version.py` | `true` |
| `python/sglang/kernels/__init__.py`, `kernels/ops/topk.py`, `kernels/aot/setup.py` | `true` |
| `test/registered/npu/**`, `python/pyproject_npu.toml` | `true` |

`multimodal_gen` is untouched — it has no standalone negation and is already correct.

## Validation

- The filter block still parses as YAML (paths-filter parses `filters` as YAML; the added lines are YAML comments).
- Both pattern sets evaluated offline against the table above with globstar + extglob + dot matching and the `some` quantifier: the new filter gives the expected value for all 16 probe paths; the current one returns `true` for all of them.
- This PR touches only `.github/workflows/pr-test-npu.yml`, which is itself in the `main_package` list, so its own NPU run still exercises the tier.

title: [Fix] hicache: Fail fast on a null pointer from the Mooncake host allocator
author: qidaye
body:
Fixes #40564

## Motivation

`MooncakeHostTensorAllocator.allocate` feeds the raw return value of
`MooncakeHostMemAllocator.alloc(size)` into `ctypes.from_address` and
`torch.frombuffer` without checking it. When the underlying allocator cannot map the
host segment it returns a null pointer, and both of those happily accept address 0, so
`allocate()` returns a normal-looking tensor whose `data_ptr()` is `0`.

Nothing fails where the allocation actually failed. The error surfaces much later and
far from its cause: pinning the host pool calls `cudaHostRegister` on address 0 and
gets `cudaErrorInvalidValue`, or the process segfaults on the first access to the
buffer. Neither message mentions host memory, so in a prefill deployment we spent a
long detour on the CUDA side before identifying the host memory shortage as the real
problem.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store/mooncake_store.py`: check
  `ptr_int` right after `self.allocator.alloc(size)` and raise a `RuntimeError` naming
  the requested size in both bytes and GB, pointing at host memory availability and
  the mooncake allocator logs. Nothing else in the allocation path changes; a
  successful allocation behaves exactly as before.
- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mooncake_host_allocator.py`: new CPU unit test.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable — this is a pure error path, and a successful allocation is untouched,
so no model output changes.

A CPU unit test covers the new behaviour. It bypasses `__init__` with `__new__` (so it
needs neither a mooncake install nor a mappable host segment) and mocks the underlying
allocator into returning `0` and `None`, asserting that `allocate()` raises a
`RuntimeError` whose message carries the requested size:

```
$ python -m pytest test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mooncake_host_allocator.py -q
1 passed, 2 subtests passed in 4.36s
```

The existing mooncake unit tests in `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/`
(`test_mooncake_ssd_offload_path.py`, `test_mooncake_store_config.py`,
`test_mooncake_tenant_config.py`, `test_mooncake_group_semantics.py`,
`test_mooncake_standalone_dummy_mamba.py`) still pass: 32 passed before the change,
33 passed with the new test added.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The added check is a single truthiness test on an integer that runs
once per host pool allocation, and it only changes behaviour on the failure path.

title: [AMD][Fix] AgentX HIP TPOT regression when SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN is set
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

This PR fixes an AgentX TPOT regression on HIP after [#37134](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37134).

Agent mode (InferenceMax AgentX) sets `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.39` for Qwen3.5 (`match-expected` / `real-draft-token`). The server still runs a full EAGLE verify, then overwrites accept length. #37134 auto-enables `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling` on HIP, so every decode step also runs the Triton chain sampler; that result is then thrown away. Extra verify work shows up as ~14% worse AgentX TPOT (TP4 conc=4) vs pre-#37134 / a 0915 baseline.

Fixed-length MTP does not set `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN`, and the client is greedy (`temperature=0`), so verify stays on `argmax` and does not hit this regression.

Skip the HIP auto-enable when `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN > 0`. Real eval / serving (env unset or `< 0`) still auto-enables as in #37134.

## Modifications

- `_should_auto_enable_hip_rejection_sampling` now takes `simulate_acc_len` and returns false when `simulate_acc_len > 0`.
- `_handle_eagle_family` passes `envs.SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN` into that gate.
- Explicit `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling` is unchanged (the helper already no-ops when the flag is already on).
- Unit test `test_simulate_acc_len_stays_off` in `test/registered/unit/spec/test_eagle_gate_routing.py`.

## Accuracy Tests

No new EVAL_ONLY / quality run. The `EVAL_ONLY=true` AgentX path does not set `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN`, so HIP still auto-enables rejection sampling as in #37134. This change only affects the simulated-accept throughput path, whose accept length is overwritten after verify. The new unit test covers the auto-enable predicate for `simulate_acc_len=3.39` vs `-1.0`.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

InferenceX arm `qwen3.5-fp4-mi355x-sglang-agentic-mtp`, recipe `benchmarks/single_node/agentic/qwen3.5_fp4_mi355x_sglang_mtp.sh`, TP4, conc=4, `DURATION=1200`. Same container (`rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.19-rocm720-mi35x-20260915`), weights, GPUs, and recipe; only the SGLang SHA / this patch changes.

title: Fix GLM-5.3 forget-gate shape for nvCUTEDSL verify
author: willhu-jpg
body:
## Summary

- normalize the KDA forget gate to the 4D layout required by the nvCUTEDSL target-verify kernel
- support GLM-5.3-Flash flattened gates without changing the already-shaped Kimi-K3 path

## Motivation

Glm5NextLinearAttention passes the target-verify forget gate as [1, T, H*K], while Kimi-K3 passes [1, T, H, K]. The shared fused_kda_decode_mtp_dspark wrapper requires g to have shape [1, T, H, K] and rejects the flattened GLM tensor.

Normalize the gate at the shared nvCUTEDSL fast-path boundary using the same runtime token, local-head, and head-dimension metadata already used to shape q, k, and v. For Kimi-K3 this is an unchanged view; for GLM it exposes the missing head dimension. No other backend is affected.

## Validation

- python -m py_compile python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/kda_backend.py
- git diff --check
- production-shaped GLM-5.3-Flash run on B300 TP2/EP2 with FP32 SSM state, ReplaySSM, and nvCUTEDSL verify reached active CUDA-graph decode and reported finite multi-token acceptance and throughput

title: Fix multimodal feature offload races
author: cctry
body:
## Summary

Asynchronous multimodal offload can release a GPU source allocation while encoder reads or the host copy are still queued. A later embedding-cache miss can also read the CPU destination before the copy finishes, corrupting inputs and producing NaNs.

Record the consuming stream on GPU sources and lazily create one reusable completion event per worker. `general_mm_embed_routine` records that event after actual device-to-host copies. The worker submits offloads on the same execution stream, so the latest record also covers older CPU backups retained across prefill batches.

`_move_items_to_device` synchronizes the event before encoders prepare inputs on CPU or features move to a non-CUDA device. CUDA uploads enqueue a stream wait before the nonblocking copy. CPU readers of precomputed embeddings synchronize before concatenating them.

`general_mm_embed_routine` also accepts an optional per-modality `feature_dtypes` mapping. For opted-in modalities, it casts CUDA features before embedding-cache lookup, records the consuming stream before releasing the original allocation, and saves the prepared tensor in `item.feature`. Offload then retains the encoder-ready dtype for later chunks, including on an embedding-cache hit, avoiding repeated dtype conversion. This saved feature remains separate from the embedding cache. CPU features are unchanged, and callers that omit the mapping retain their existing feature placement, transport, and dtype behavior.

## Test plan

- `uv run --no-project --with pre-commit pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_schedule.py python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_utils.py`: passed. Commit hooks passed.
- `uv run --no-project --with pre-commit pre-commit run --from-ref 1d3243d05f --to-ref HEAD`: passed on the final two-file diff, without overrides.
- Compared this update against its source commit: all added and removed lines match. Syntax parsing passed. Verified that `schedule_batch.py` is restored to the PR base. Reviewed the optional dtype argument, existing callers, cast source lifetime, and CPU, CUDA, and precomputed-embedding consumer paths.
- Historical downstream validation, before the readiness restructuring, passed a real-model CUDA race regression for all four image/video × BF16/FP32 cases. It exercised preprocessing, CUDA transport, encoding, pending offload, cache eviction, and the next prefill chunk. Removing either source `record_stream` or the host wait independently failed all four cases. These historical results do not validate the current revision.
- The updated downstream regression covers reuse and re-recording of the worker event, prepared-feature reuse on embedding-cache hits, and allocator pressure after shared dtype conversion. It has not run on CUDA. Local CUDA is unavailable and the prepared remote environment remains inaccessible. Downstream local collection also stopped because NumPy was missing.
- The prior generic-test attempt at `201c1fcabf` with `uv run --no-project --with pytest pytest -q test/registered/unit/managers/test_mm_embedding_length.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_mm_hashes.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_mm_process_config.py test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_gpu_feature_transport.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_msgpack_ipc_roundtrip.py --tb=short --disable-warnings` stopped during collection because local runtime dependencies were missing.
- Full serving evaluation and throughput benchmarking were not run.

title: [Kimi K3] Fix CUDA graph stream explosion
author: kpham-sgl
body: ## Motivation Kimi K3 target CUDA graph replay expands to 96 streams on B300. Repeated attention forks move subsequent layers onto new replay streams. Record the main attention branches before their auxiliary kernels to fix this stream explosion: the same workload now uses 4 target streams on all eight TP ranks. ## Modifications - Record the KDA main projection before the side-stream gate GEMVs. - Fork the MLA output gate before attention, then record its kernel at the output-projection boundary after the attention core. Keep the original fork/join dependencies so the GPU work can still overlap, and close skipped gate branches. - Extend changed-input CUDA graph correctness coverage. ## Accuracy Tests `python test/registered/unit/models/test_kimi_k3_bfa_overlap.py`: **5 tests passed on B300**. [Overlap unit CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35662649445) and [B300 end-to-end CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35662661359) also passed on the current PR head; both Kimi K3 B300 end-to-end files passed two tests each. KDA bitwise parity covers token counts 1, 4, and 12, both `defer_f_b` settings, and three changed-input replays. MLA checks an in-graph input producer and changed-input parity, including eager and breakable-graph fallback selection. Full-model traces retain identical kernel-name/count multisets: 1,950 target kernels per replay on every rank. ## Speed Tests and Profiling In TP8/DCP1 traces, target replay streams fall from **96 to 4 on all eight TP ranks**, with stable assignments across 16 profiled replays and identical kernel-name/count multisets. This is reproduced with both real and dummy weights. Separate **N=5 unprofiled runs per variant and batch size**, using dummy MXFP4 target and dummy draft weights: 8× B300, CUDA 13.0, TP8, 60k input / 1k output, DSpark block 7, simulated acceptance 5.5, FP8 E4M3 KV, FP32 SSM, CuTe DSL MLA, FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE, connections=8. **TP8/DCP1:** | Batch size | Before, tok/s (mean ± SD) | After, tok/s (mean ± SD) | Change in mean | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 493.06 ± 2.41 | 498.12 ± 2.14 | +1.03% | | 16 | 3139.65 ± 252.29 | 3249.41 ± 15.07 | +3.50% | BS1 improves in all five matched pairs (+0.77% to +1.14%). **The BS16 mean is distorted by one slow baseline sample (2689.09 tok/s), retained in the results.** The other four matched pairs differ by −0.10% to −0.15%; these results do not establish a BS16 speedup. Full-batch steady-state throughput gives the same interpretation. Order: baseline (3 samples), patched (3), patched (2), baseline (2), each with a fresh server and a full-shape warmup pair excluded in advance. Client/server seeds are 42; actual acceptance lengths match in every corresponding pair. All requests generated the requested tokens. Measurements share two server launches per variant, so N=5 is limited evidence. Dummy weights and simulated acceptance do not test model accuracy. **TP8/DCP8**, same N=5 design and workload, with `fi_a2a` and replicated Q projection: | Batch size | Before, tok/s (mean ± SD) | After, tok/s (mean ± SD) | Change in mean | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 470.94 ± 2.23 | 474.87 ± 2.26 | +0.83% | | 16 | 3060.60 ± 14.24 | 3060.26 ± 13.92 | −0.01% | Every BS1 matched pair improves (+0.72% to +0.88%); BS16 decode is unchanged (paired changes −0.028% to +0.001%). Acceptance matches in every pair. All samples are retained and all requests complete their requested output length with a valid full-batch decode window. BS16 mean total latency is 44.845 → 45.105 s (+0.58%), driven by last-TTFT/prefill time (39.617 → 39.876 s), including one slower patched prefill sample. N=5 does not establish whether the small prefill difference is noise; the flat decode result is not a claim about all end-to-end timings. The DCP benchmark uses `--skip-token-capacity-check` because the client guard reads physical capacity while DCP exposes eight times the logical capacity; server memory settings are unchanged. Both repeated comparisons use baseline `0f6761b54` with the PR patch applied for the patched runs. DCP8 was not profiled in this timing experiment. ## Profile **Before** **After** ## Checklist - [x] Pre-commit checks pass for all changed files. - [x] Registered CUDA unit tests extended and run. - [x] Correctness and full-model profiling results provided above. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #35662490950](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35662490950) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #35662490698](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35662490698) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #35662491074](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35662491074)

title: [Fix] Run KV canary hooks for context-parallel prefill
author: ch-wan
body:
CP prefill calls the transformer body directly and bypasses the outer `model.forward` patched by KV canary. This skips the canary pre/post hooks and triggers `SimplePhaseChecker: phase mismatch` (`expect=3`, `actual=1`) in both `log` and `raise` modes.

When prefill CP is enabled, also wrap the transformer body's forward with the existing canary hooks. The shared bracket scope keeps decode, which still enters through the outer model, from running those hooks twice. Add a CP=2 regression covering prefill followed by CUDA-graph decode in `raise` mode with real-KV hashing enabled. The registered test starts the server once; `log` uses the same hook path and was checked separately.

Validation on two H200 GPUs:

title: fix(grpc): expose native response timeout as a server argument
author: jain-ria
body:
## Motivation

Native gRPC requests can exceed the default 300-second wait for a response chunk under heavy queueing. The Rust binding already accepts a timeout, but the Python launcher does not expose it.

## Modifications

Add `--grpc-response-timeout-secs` (default: 300, positive integer) and pass it to the native Rust gRPC server. For example, `--grpc-response-timeout-secs 1800` allows up to 30 minutes waiting for the first or each subsequent response chunk. This is not an overall request deadline and does not affect legacy SMG gRPC.

Document the option in CLI help. Add one compact argument test and extend the existing native launch test to verify the override reaches the binding.

## Accuracy Tests

- Focused `TestGrpcServerArgs` suite: 19 passed (default, override, invalid values, and launcher forwarding).
- Pre-commit checks on changed files and `git diff --check` passed.
- No model-output changes; the GB300 workload was not rerun.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: configuration plumbing only; default timeout and request execution are unchanged.

title: [Fix] Keep diffusion encoder TP context bindings consistent
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

The LTX-2 two-GPU encoder accuracy test fails while entering `use_tensor_parallel_group`: diffusion initialization stamps a TP=1 attention group, but encoder folding only overrides the TP group and widths. The context then reports `attn_tp_size=2` alongside an `attn_tp_group` of size 1 and rejects the scope before loading the encoder.

This is present on main (`00986c81be687d82e66651fb3ce9a096070b06e6`) and was exposed by [this component accuracy CI failure](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35662705674/job/106543345637?pr=40638).

## Modifications

Override `attn_tp_group`, `attn_tp_rank`, and `moe_tp_rank` alongside the folded TP group. The existing context manager restores these bindings when the scope exits.

Strengthen the existing folding tests to start from diffusion's stamped TP=1 context, cover both ranks of TP=2, and check restoration after an exception in a nested folding scope.

## Accuracy Tests

- On a clean checkout of current main `00986c81be687d82e66651fb3ce9a096070b06e6`, the strengthened folding regressions fail in all three cases before applying the fix.
- After the fix: `PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_component_accuracy_parallel_runtime.py -q` — **9 passed**.
- Pre-commit checks passed.

The full LTX-2 model-weight accuracy test has not been rerun.

The [manual rerun](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35668648916/job/106559927349) stopped at the first Wan VAE test because the generic rerun workflow started only one process for a two-GPU test. That launcher issue is fixed separately in [#40652](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40652); this run did not reach the LTX-2 encoder case.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: this changes the encoder-loading context, with no kernel or forward-path changes.

title: fix(nccl): disable graph buffer registration for pausable graph pools
author: guapisolo
body:
<!-- lint: profile=evidence-heavy -->
## Summary
Disable NCCL graph buffer registration when the CUDA graph pool is pausable under memory saver.

## Symptom & Reproduction
- **Symptom:** a two-node TP16/EP16 MoE engine with `--enable-memory-saver` and `SGLANG_MEMORY_SAVER_CUDA_GRAPH=1` never finishes a decode step after a `release_memory_occupation` / `resume_memory_occupation(kv_cache, cuda_graph)` cycle; all 16 schedulers wait in `copy_done.synchronize()` until the 300 s scheduler watchdog fires.
- **Reproduction:** zai-org/GLM-5.3 FP8 on two 8x H200 nodes with `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=1 NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1`, `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 256`, memory saver, one release/resume cycle, then 512 requests ([recipe](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40648#issuecomment-5771709834)); expected 512/512, `main` gives 0/512 and a 16-rank watchdog.

## Root Cause
1. `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER` (default on) registers graph-captured collective buffers for the graph lifetime.
2. `SGLANG_MEMORY_SAVER_CUDA_GRAPH` captures the graphs into a `torch_memory_saver` region.
3. `release_memory_occupation(cuda_graph)` releases its pages; resume maps new pages at the same addresses.
4. Registered NVLS/network paths keep the released pages, so ranks diverge and the `tp_group` deadlocks.
5. `CustomAllreduce` skips its registration under `tms_cudagraph`, but multi-node TP disables it.

## Fix
`handle_data_parallelism` calls `_disable_nccl_graph_buffer_registration` (added in #38936 for the TP LM-head all-to-all) for a second trigger, `_graph_pool_is_pausable` (`enable_memory_saver` and `SGLANG_MEMORY_SAVER_CUDA_GRAPH`), so the schedulers inherit `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER=0` from the launcher before any communicator exists. This is the mitigation torch_memory_saver documents for the same interaction (fzyzcjy/torch_memory_saver#88, fzyzcjy/torch_memory_saver#107). The helper takes a `reason` for its warning when `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER` is set explicitly, which still wins. Engines whose graph pool is not pausable, including DP-attention engines, are unchanged.

## Verification
- GLM-5.3 TP16 recipe, `main` vs the pausable-pool trigger: 0/512 with 30752 `register comm` lines per node vs 512/512 in 109 s with none, both on the first commit and after the rebase onto 81cb895b85 ([re-run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40648#issuecomment-5806688391)). The DP-attention rule dropped at this head never fires in this recipe.
- GLM-5.3 DP-attention recipe (`--enable-dp-attention --dp-size 2`, same pool and cycle): `main` 1/512 in 2/2 runs vs 512/512 with the pausable-pool trigger alone ([recipe](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40648#issuecomment-5805522206)).
- Downstream tree (pausable-pool trigger, earlier base), two-node TP16/EP16, memory saver, seven-step release/resume lifecycle: unpatched 0/512 vs patched 512/512 with zero registrations and no throughput change.
- Downstream RL colocated-training run, four engines with weight updates and graph release/resume every step: three rollout/train cycles completed.
- `test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py -k NcclGraphRegister`: not rerun at this head; the test file now matches `main`.

## Review Focus
- `handle_data_parallelism` / `parallel_hook.py`: the guard must run in the launcher before any NCCL communicator exists.
- Cost: memory-saver engines lose NCCL zero-copy registration for graph-captured collectives; the pausable-pool run measured no throughput change.
- Scope: an earlier revision also disabled registration for DP-attention decode graphs (#40649); it is dropped because no run isolated a hang with registration on a non-pausable pool.

title: fix(nccl): disable graph buffer registration when DP attention replays decode graphs
author: guapisolo
body:
> **Depends on:** #40648
> Stacked on the parent PR's branch. Review / merge the parent first.

## Summary
Disable NCCL graph buffer registration when DP attention replays decode CUDA graphs.

## Symptom & Reproduction
- **Symptom:** a two-node TP16/EP16 MoE engine with `--enable-dp-attention --dp-size 2` (or 4) and default decode CUDA graphs stops on its GPUs within the first decode steps; all 16 schedulers wait on the first device synchronisation after a replay (`copy_done.synchronize()` under the overlap scheduler, the routed-experts D2H copy with `--disable-overlap-schedule`), with no CUDA or NCCL error, until the scheduler watchdog fires on every rank.
- **Reproduction:** RL rollout of 128 requests, engine `--max-running-requests 64 --chunked-prefill-size 1024 --mem-fraction-static 0.8` (DP2) or `0.85` (DP4), prefill graph disabled, default decode graph (`bs=[8, 16, 24, 32]` for DP2); 0/9 graph-on DP runs completed, while the same configuration with `--cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled` completes 128/128.

## Root Cause
1. With DP attention the decode graphs capture the attention-DP gather/scatter over the TP group (`all_gather_into_tensor` / `reduce_scatter`) on graph-pool buffers.
2. `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER` (default on) registers those buffers at capture for the graph lifetime.
3. `NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=REG` shows `register comm … size 136314880` on every hanging run.
4. The registered `all_gather_into_tensor` / `reduce_scatter` exchange deadlocks once DP groups sit at different points of their schedules.
5. Same family as the TP LM-head all-to-all hang of #38936 (`_disable_nccl_graph_buffer_registration`); dedicated buffers alone did not help.
6. Single-variable lanes still hang with `SGLANG_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH_DEDUP`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_GRAPH_POOL_BORROW`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_GRAPH_POOL_PRECARVE` off, without the routed-experts capture, and with `--disable-overlap-schedule`.

## Fix
`_dp_attention_replays_decode_graphs`: when `enable_dp_attention`, `dp_size > 1` and `cuda_graph_config.decode.backend != DISABLED`, `handle_data_parallelism` calls `_disable_nccl_graph_buffer_registration` so the schedulers inherit `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER=0`. `handle_cuda_graph_config` runs earlier in the pipeline, so the guard sees the resolved decode backend. An explicit value still wins with a warning. Engines without DP attention, or with eager decode, are unchanged.

## Verification
- `test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py -k NcclGraphRegister` on this branch (H200): the 3 existing all-to-all cases pass; the "without all-to-all" case now pins eager decode so the new rule stays out of that check.
- Paired GPU runs with this patch on a downstream tree (same code, earlier base), two-node TP16/EP16, DP2, 128 requests at max-running 64: fixed 128/128 in 7:46 with zero `register comm` lines, 16 schedulers attesting `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER=0`; unpatched control hung after the second decode step (16 ranks in `copy_done.synchronize()`, 35 `register comm` lines, watchdog).
- Fixed tree on DP4: 128/128 in 5:48; fixed DP2 rerun: 128/128 in 7:59.

## Review Focus
- The condition reads `cuda_graph_config` from the resolving view; it relies on `handle_cuda_graph_config` staying ahead of `handle_data_parallelism` in `arg_groups/pipeline.py`.
- Cost: DP-attention engines lose NCCL user-buffer registration for graph collectives; no slowdown was visible, but there is no non-hanging graph-on baseline to compare against.
- Related: sgl-project/sglang#38936 (same guard, all-to-all), fzyzcjy/torch_memory_saver#88.

title: [Fix] diffusion: Fix the load duration missing from subclassed server tests
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
## Motivation

The AMD nightly `nightly-1-gpu-zimage-turbo` has failed on all three ROCm variants since the 2026-09-21 run ([job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35633070401/job/106443720276)), and was still failing on 2026-10-12:

```
PerformanceValidationError: [performance] zimage_image_t2i: Load duration missing or invalid: None
```

Image generation succeeds; the failure is in recording the result. #39206 added a `load_time_ms=None` parameter to `DiffusionServerBase._validate_and_record`, and a check in `_record_performance_result` that rejects a missing load duration, but only updated the base class's own call site. Three tests override `test_diffusion_generation` and call `_validate_and_record(case, perf_record)` directly, so they record `None` even though the server measured its load time:

- `test/registered/amd/test_zimage_turbo.py`
- `test/registered/xpu/test_xpu_zimage_turbo.py`
- `test/registered/xpu/test_xpu_flux2_dev.py`

## Modifications

`_validate_and_record` now takes the `ServerContext` and reads `ctx.load_time_ms` itself, as `_validate_realtime_performance` already does. The three overrides, the base-class call site and `test_performance_failure_policy.py` pass the context. Since `ctx` is required, an override still using the old call fails with a `TypeError` instead of silently recording `None`.

NVIDIA behaviour is unchanged: the base class used to pass `diffusion_server.load_time_ms` and now passes `diffusion_server`.

## Verification

- The NVIDIA diffusion suites (1/2/4-GPU, 5090, `diffusion-coverage-check`) and `multimodal-gen-unit-test` passed on this branch at e9616a3e ([run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38293317709)).
- The AMD zimage nightly, dispatched on this branch at c1e4114d with `continue_on_error=false` ([run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38473414064)), passes on rocm10, rocm724 and rocm720. Each job records the server's load time (52.3–58.6 s) instead of failing on `None`.

An earlier revision also added a guard test that drove the three overrides with a stub server. It has been removed: with `ctx` required, it no longer catches anything the signature doesn't.

## Notes for reviewers

Two XPU issues are left alone because this regression did not cause them:

title: [DSpark] Fix draft CUDA graph stream explosion
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

DSpark draft CUDA graph replay expands to seven streams on B300 with TP8/DCP1. Its seven dependent token broadcasts go through ProcessGroupNCCL even while the graph capture context has enabled PyNccl.

## Modifications

Use the enabled PyNccl communicator for CUDA broadcasts, keeping broadcasts on the current capture stream. Preserve the torch.distributed fallback when PyNccl is disabled or unavailable. Keep the existing typed PyNccl broadcast unchanged. Audited SRT callers use supported integer or floating-point payloads; no bool/complex broadcast support is added.

## Accuracy Tests

Existing Kimi K3 B300 correctness tests are being retriggered on the updated head. Dummy weights and simulated acceptance do not validate model accuracy. Pre-commit checks passed for the runtime change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

8× B300, TP8, 60k input / 1k output, DSpark block 7, simulated acceptance 5.5, dummy MXFP4 target and dummy draft weights, FP8 E4M3 KV, FP32 SSM, CuTe DSL MLA, FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE, CUDA device connections 8.

- TP8/DCP1 draft replay streams: **7 → 1**; target remains at **4**.
- The initial typed-broadcast DCP1 profile has the exact same runtime patch as the current head: 137 draft kernels and 1,950 target kernels per replay on all eight ranks, with stable stream assignments across 16 replays. The stream fix does not depend on byte broadcasting.

**Earlier-revision measurements:** the following N=5 table was collected at `ff17b2e04b`, which included byte broadcasting. These timings have not been rerun after restoring the existing typed broadcast at `e91dd97ff0`. The earlier DCP8 traces showed one draft stream and four target streams before and after.

**N=5 unprofiled samples per variant, topology, and batch size:**

| Configuration | BS | Before, tok/s (mean ± SD) | After, tok/s (mean ± SD) | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| TP8/DCP1 | 1 | 498.28 ± 2.33 | 498.57 ± 2.38 | +0.06% |
| TP8/DCP1 | 16 | 3262.63 ± 19.96 | 3260.56 ± 19.76 | −0.06% |
| TP8/DCP8 | 1 | 474.95 ± 2.24 | 474.95 ± 2.20 | +0.002% |
| TP8/DCP8 | 16 | 3070.06 ± 19.06 | 3070.47 ± 19.26 | +0.01% |

Decode throughput is effectively unchanged in these runs; full-batch steady-state throughput gives the same conclusion. Mean total latency changes are +0.10%, +0.09%, +0.12%, and −0.26%, respectively. The last mean includes one slower baseline prefill, retained in the results; no end-to-end speedup is established.

Baseline is main `c4d3770a68`; patched is `ff17b2e04b`. Each variant/topology uses one fresh server, an excluded full-shape BS1/BS16 warmup pair, then five alternating measured pairs. Order: baseline DCP1, patched DCP1, patched DCP8, baseline DCP8. Client/server seeds are 42, corresponding acceptance lengths match, and all requests complete the requested output length. Samples share a server launch, so this is limited regression evidence rather than a general performance guarantee. DCP8 uses `fi_a2a` with replicated Q projection. The client capacity check is skipped because it reads physical capacity while DCP exposes logical capacity; server memory settings are unchanged.

- [x] Typed-broadcast DCP1 profile verified; earlier-revision repeated timings identified above.

title: [Fix] Don't let a failed deep_ep import-time check kill servers that never use DeepEP
author: LiRunGuo
body:
## Motivation

Since #33932 (2026-08-07), `sgl-deep-ep` is a hard dependency of the `sglang` wheel, so `deep_ep` is always installed.
`deep_ep/__init__.py` runs host checks at import time:

- `check_nccl_so()` asserts that exactly one libnccl is mapped and that it is byte-identical to the pip NCCL (`AssertionError`, or `FileNotFoundError` when a mapping reads `(deleted)`).
- `find_cuda_home()` asserts that a CUDA home is found (`AssertionError`).
- `init_jit()` initializes the C++ JIT runtime.

The guard in `token_dispatcher/deepep.py` dates from when "not installed" was the only failure mode, and catches only `ImportError`; `deepep_v2.py` catches `(ImportError, OSError)`.
Every server process imports these modules, including the launcher:

```
launch_server -> http_server -> engine -> data_parallel_controller -> scheduler
  -> disaggregation/decode -> managers/utils -> layers/logits_processor
  -> layers/logprob_processor -> model_executor/runner_utils/__init__
  -> runner_utils/deepep_adapter -> layers/moe/token_dispatcher -> deepep -> deep_ep
```

So one failed check stops the server at import time, even for dense models where DeepEP is never requested.

### Reproduction (H200, Qwen3-1.7B, dense, no DeepEP flags)

```bash
# any second libnccl on the host; here a source build of NCCL 2.32.3 vs the pip 2.29.7
export LD_PRELOAD=/path/to/nccl/build/lib/libnccl.so.2
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B --port 30006
```

Before (main @ 00986c8): the launcher exits with code 1 during import.

```
File "python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/deepep.py", line 53, in <module>
File ".venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/deep_ep/__init__.py", line 91, in <module>
AssertionError: Duplicate NCCL runtime found in the current system: .../nccl/build/lib/libnccl.so.2.32.3 and .../site-packages/nvidia/nccl/lib/libnccl.so.2
```

After: the server starts with the custom NCCL mapped, and `/generate` returns ` Paris. The capital of the United States is Washington, D` for "The capital of France is".
The same failure also happened without `LD_PRELOAD` on a shared network filesystem, where the detokenizer saw the NCCL mapping as `(deleted)` and `filecmp` raised `FileNotFoundError`.

## Modifications

- `deepep.py`: catch any exception from the optional import, keep it in `_deepep_import_error`, and chain it into the `ImportError` raised when a DeepEP dispatcher is created. The message now says "not available" instead of "not installed", because the package usually is installed.
- `deepep_v2.py`: widen `(ImportError, OSError)` to `Exception` for the `deep_ep` import. The v2 module already stores and reports the original error.

Users who request DeepEP still get a hard error, now with the root cause instead of a misleading "not installed".
The v1 `try` block also covers the `sglang_per_token_group_quant_fp8` import, as before; a failure there is reported the same way.

Follow-up, not in this PR: `runner_utils/__init__.py` eagerly re-exports `DeepEPCudaGraphRunnerAdapter`, so importing `runner_utils.pool` from `logprob_processor` pulls every MoE dispatcher (and `deep_ep`) into the launcher, tokenizer and detokenizer. Making that re-export lazy would stop these processes from loading DeepEP at all.

## Accuracy Tests

No model forward, kernel or sampling code is touched; only the import guard of the two DeepEP dispatcher modules changes.

- New CPU test `test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_deepep_import_guard.py` runs a fresh interpreter with a stand-in `deep_ep` whose import raises `AssertionError`. It checks that the dispatcher package imports, that both `use_deepep` flags are false, and that creating a DeepEP dispatcher raises `ImportError` chained to the original error. It fails on main and passes with this change.
- Existing DeepEP unit tests: `test_deepep_v2_buffer_lifecycle.py`, `test_deepep_v2_masked_slab.py`, `test_deepep_v2_wire_dtype.py`, `test_w4afp8_deepep_dtype.py`, `test_w4afp8_deepep_post_reorder.py`, plus the new test: 39 passed.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass.
- No model code is touched; the dense end-to-end run above is the functional check.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The change only affects module import, not any runtime path.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not needed: no user-facing option changes.
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Not applicable: import-time change only.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Fix] Decide the MoE padded-row bound from the layer scatter mode
author: mmangkad
body:
## Summary

A more general fix for the truncation reported in #40643, which #39574 introduced: rather than special-casing DP attention, the bound is decided from the layer communicator's scatter mode, which also covers the non-DP and CP gathered cases and the other MoE models on the same path.

`forward_batch.num_token_non_padded` is **LOCAL** (`forward_batch_info.py`). It bounds a sparse MoE's input only while that input is this rank's own shard. On a gathered buffer each source rank contributes its own padded slot, so the real rows are not a prefix — masking with the local count drops every peer rank's tokens, and under `--moe-a2a-backend none` each rank sums a truncated partial output.

This moves that decision to `ForwardBatch.moe_num_token_non_padded()`, keyed on the scatter mode the layer communicator already computes for a sparse MLP.

**Decision table**

| MoE input | Condition | Bound |
|---|---|---|
| `SCATTERED` | a2a dispatch, FP4 all-gather, dwdp | `LOCAL` |
| `MOE_FULL` | CP extend — MoE-CP all-gather runs | none |
| `MOE_FULL` | any other forward — no gather, FULL layout | *as FULL below* |
| `FULL` | DSA / MLA CP prefill — CP all-gather, zigzag rows | none |
| `FULL` | `attn_dp_size > 1` — `dp_gather` interleaves slots | none |
| `FULL` | `attn_dp_size == 1`, attn-TP sharded — all-reduce, not gather | `GLOBAL` |
| `FULL` | `attn_dp_size == 1`, replicated | `LOCAL` |
| any | `num_token_non_padded is None` (no EP) | none |

**Changes**

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `forward_batch_info.py` | `moe_num_token_non_padded()` — the one definition |
| `communicator.py` | `_compute_mlp_mode`'s sparse branch extracted as `sparse_mlp_scatter_mode()` |
| 17 model files + `mega_moe.py` | 24 MoE routing sites read the accessor instead of the raw field |
| `deepseek_v4.py` | inline `num_token_non_padded = None` around its MoE call dropped as redundant |
| `test_num_token_non_padded_localization.py` | table above locked; cases fail against the pre-fix behavior |

**Verification**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `test/registered/unit/model_executor` + scatter-modes test | 297 passed, 181 subtests |
| Pre-fix simulation (accessor returns raw local count) | 9 subtests fail |
| Pre-`MOE_FULL`-gate simulation (unconditional `None`) | 4 subtests fail |
| `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` over the accessor's function-level import | no graph break |
| Raw `num_token_non_padded=` MoE routing reads left in `srt/` | 0 |

title: Fix the Inkling per-expert sync test and collect it in the weekly CPU run
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

`test/srt/models/test_inkling_per_expert_sync.py` fails all four of its cases on `main`.

It saves and restores `get_moe_expert_parallel_world_size`, `get_moe_expert_parallel_rank` and `get_moe_tensor_parallel_rank` on `sglang.srt.models.inkling`, then reassigns them to drive a simulated EP x MoE-TP grid. The loader stopped importing those names, so `setUp` raises `AttributeError` before any case does work, and the assignments would in any event have created three attributes nothing reads.

Nothing reported this, because the file sits under `test/srt/`, which no workflow collects.

## Modifications

- The test publishes the topology its rank is standing in and lets the loader read the placement off the context, the same way it does in a real process. MoE-TP is what is left of TP after EP takes its share, so a global rank of `ep_rank * tp_size + tp_rank` under `tp_size = ep_size * tp_size` reproduces exactly the grid the test asserts over. `lora_compatible_layout_enabled` is still a module-level binding and stays a stub.

No production code changes; this is a test fix.

title: [Hisparse] fix: account for MiniMax HiSparse full-pool memory
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

MiniMax HiSparse allocates dense KV and index caches at `size * host_to_device_ratio`, while sparse main KV stays at `size`. The memory estimator currently budgets all three at `size`, so automatic token capacity can exceed available GPU memory and fail during cache initialization. This fixes the capacity accounting introduced by #31446.

## Modifications

Apply the HiSparse ratio to dense layers and index-cache bytes when computing the MiniMax per-slot cost. Sparse main KV keeps its original cost; disabling HiSparse or using ratio 1 preserves the existing estimate.

For a 3-dense/57-sparse layout with one KV head per rank, 128-dimensional bf16 main/index caches and K-only index layers, ratio 2 changes the estimate from 45,312 to 61,440 bytes per slot.

## Validation

- All applicable pre-commit checks passed.
- Ran 648 local arithmetic/layout checks against the changed calculation, covering ratios 1/2/4, dense/sparse layer counts, KV heads, element sizes, and K-only/mixed/KV index layers. No test files added.
- Prior H200 A/B E2E on the original #31446 review head (`d0fb09af10ad36fc9b2458e6672f710bae387e9a`), with an equivalent formula fix: at `mem_fraction_static=0.80` and ratio 2, automatic capacity dropped from 2,629,667 to 1,939,380 slots. The original failed with CUDA OOM during index K allocation; the corrected budget completed startup, decode CUDA graph capture, and six HTTP generation requests (short, longer than the working set, and concurrent).
- That E2E used a small random-weight M3 fixture preserving the 60-layer KV layout, not the full pretrained model. GPU E2E has not been rerun on this main-based branch.

## Accuracy Tests

title: [AMD] Critical fix enabling Qwen3.8 FP8: restore dropped fused shared-expert weights
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

Text-only Qwen3.5-MoE checkpoints (architecture `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`, e.g. `Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-FP8`) load into `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`, whose `load_weights` was missing the shared-expert fusion remapping that the multimodal `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration.load_weights` already implements. On ROCm with aiter shared-expert fusion enabled (`SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`), `Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock` serves the shared expert as an extra fused MoE slot at index `num_experts`, but `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM.load_weights` kept `num_experts` unchanged and never remapped `mlp.shared_expert.*` onto that slot. Every layer's shared-expert weights were therefore silently dropped ("Parameter ...mlp.shared_expert... not found in params_dict") and the fused slot was left uninitialized, zeroing the shared expert across all layers and collapsing accuracy (gsm8k near random) while the server still loaded and served.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py`, class `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`:
  - `__init__`: compute `num_fused_shared_experts` / `enable_shared_expert_fusion` when aiter fusion is active, via a new `_get_num_fused_shared_experts()` that scans local MoE layers (PP-safe: non-local slots are `PPMissingLayer` with no `.mlp`).
  - `load_weights`: grow `make_expert_params_mapping(num_experts=...)` by the fused shared count when fusion is on; extend `fused_expert_params_mapping` with the shared-slot entries; remap `mlp.shared_expert.* -> mlp.experts.{num_experts}.*`; load the fused shared slot into `experts.w13_weight` / `experts.w2_weight`.
- This mirrors the existing, working handling in `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration.load_weights` (added in #20736 for the multimodal path) so the text-only entry class behaves identically.

## Accuracy Tests

Verified on `Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-FP8`, TP8 / PP2, 2x MI300X, `--attention-backend aiter`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`:

| Metric | Before fix | After fix |
|---|---|---|
| `mlp.shared_expert.* not found in params_dict` warnings (per rank set) | 1104 | 0 |
| Shared expert loaded (per layer) | dropped (zeroed) | loaded into fused slot |
| Sample gsm8k generations | incoherent / wrong | coherent and correct |

Full gsm8k sweep (sglang few-shot, 1314 questions):

| Run | gsm8k score |
|---|---|
| Reference (known-good, pre-regression) | 0.9749 (97.49%) |
| After fix | 0.9741 (97.41%) |

The shared expert is loaded and accuracy matches the known-good baseline.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

N/A - this change only fixes weight loading; it does not alter the compute path or inference speed.

title: fix: partition selective CI reruns into matrix jobs
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

A selective rerun currently executes all tests sharing a runner/install configuration in one job. The five unified-cache files in [this run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35306615118/job/105480010351) exhausted the 60-minute test-step timeout after the first four files passed. The same combination also timed out in runs 35108771902 and 34695253228.

## Modifications

Keep one workflow run per dispatch configuration and partition its commands into independent matrix jobs before execution. A lightweight hosted job statically reads test registrations from the requested revision and packs commands into partitions of at most 40 estimated minutes. Unknown-duration and individually oversized tests run alone; multiple registrations use the largest estimate conservatively. No test modules are imported.

CUDA, CPU, and multimodal jobs consume their partition's commands with `fail-fast: false`. The finalizer waits for the matrix jobs and reports their aggregate result through the existing reply marker. Coredump artifact names include the partition ID. The precision-baseline refresh guard continues to validate the original full input.

The reported combination becomes two jobs in one run: four files totaling 2,036 estimated seconds and DSV4 KL totaling 1,865 seconds. Direct workflow dispatches receive the same partitioning. The hard 60-minute test-step limit remains; estimates cannot guarantee that an individual test finishes before it.

## Accuracy Tests

No inference changes. Local checks exercised the actual five-file combination, command preservation, exact budget boundaries, unknown/oversized tests, CPU positional registration, multiple registrations, selectors, empty inputs, the matrix-size limit, and the real CLI output consumed by the workflow. Workflow wiring, actionlint, Ruff, isort, the job-name checker, and `git diff --check` passed. No test files or documentation changes are included. The fork PR runs exercised the test code but used the workflow from main, so they did not validate the matrix partitioning. Validation through `/rerun-group radix_cache/unified_radix_tree` on this upstream branch confirmed that [prepare-partitions succeeds and creates two CUDA matrix jobs](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35751395868): partition 1 contains linker DSV4, HiCache PP, CP, and Mamba; partition 2 contains DSV4 KL alone. GPU execution is still pending/in progress; this confirms partition generation and workflow wiring, not full GPU test success.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable; this changes CI orchestration only.

Supersedes #40180. This upstream branch allows slash-command dispatches to load the modified workflow and validate partitioning before merge.

title: [NVIDIA][MegaMoE] Fix the default spec decoding moe backend when the target model uses flashinfer megamoe
author: wenscarl
body:
## Summary

- Fixes an `illegal memory access` crash (sgl-project/sglang#40623) that occurs when `--moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_megamoe` is combined with `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE` on a checkpoint whose MTP/NextN draft layer is unquantized (e.g. GLM-5.2-NVFP4, DeepSeek-NVFP4). The draft's MoE runner/a2a backend silently inherited the target's `flashinfer_megamoe`, so `StandardDispatcher.skip_local_expert_mapping` (`token_dispatcher/standard.py`) assumed the mega kernel's own global-expert-ID routing and skipped the EP global->local expert-id remap — but the unquantized draft layer actually falls back to the plain Triton MoE kernel, which needs that remap. Under EP (`ep_size > 1`) this feeds Triton out-of-range expert indices into EP-sharded local weight tensors, crashing `invoke_fused_moe_kernel`.
- `_speculative_moe_runner_default` (`arg_groups/overrides.py`) now falls back to `auto` instead of `flashinfer_megamoe` when defaulting the speculative runner backend from the target's backend; `initialize_moe_config()` (`layers/moe/utils.py`) applies the same default for both `speculative_a2a_backend` and `speculative_runner_backend` for call paths that construct the MoE flags directly (e.g. benchmark scripts) rather than through the full CLI resolution pipeline. `--speculative-moe-runner-backend` / `--speculative-moe-a2a-backend` still take precedence when set explicitly.
- Adds `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` (GLM-5.2/5.3-NVFP4) to `validate_flashinfer_megamoe_model`'s supported-architectures list, so megamoe is reachable for this family at all.

## Root cause

- `create_moe_dispatcher` (`layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py`) routes both `a2a_backend.is_none()` and `a2a_backend.is_flashinfer_megamoe()` to the same `StandardDispatcher` class.
- `StandardDispatcher.__init__` (`layers/moe/token_dispatcher/standard.py`) independently reads `get_moe_runner_backend()` to decide `skip_local_expert_mapping`; it skips the remap whenever the ACTIVE runner backend is `flashinfer_megamoe`, trusting the mega kernel to route by global expert ID internally.
- `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod.create_moe_runner` (`layers/quantization/unquant.py`) has no `flashinfer_megamoe` branch, so an unquantized layer (the MTP/NextN draft) always falls through to the plain Triton runner regardless of the configured backend.
- Because `speculative_moe_runner_backend` defaulted to inheriting the target's `moe_runner_backend`, the draft's dispatcher believed it was running the mega kernel (skipping the remap) while its actual runner was Triton (which needs the remap) — global-space expert IDs then index into EP-sharded local weight tensors sized for only `num_experts / ep_size` experts.

## Repro

DEP4 on Blackwell:

​```bash

python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/glm-5.2-nvpf4 \
  --load-format dummy \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tp-size 4 \
  --dp-size 4 \
  --enable-dp-attention \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_megamoe \
  --moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 3 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.7
​```

Before this fix: crashes during CUDA graph capture of the draft decode step with `RuntimeError: Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal memory access was encountered` (`invoke_fused_moe_kernel`). `--speculative-moe-a2a-backend none --speculative-moe-runner-backend triton` is necessary to workaround. After this fix, `server_args` resolves `speculative_moe_runner_backend=auto` / `speculative_moe_a2a_backend=none`, the server starts cleanly, and `/generate` requests (and a gsm8k `bench_sglang.py` smoke run) complete without crashing.

cc. @nvpohanh 
## Test plan

- [x] Manual repro above on a Blackwell (SM100) node: server starts and serves requests without the illegal-memory-access crash.
- [ ] `test/registered/unit/test_runtime_context.py::TestMoeFlagsGroup`: add a case asserting `speculative_a2a_backend`/`speculative_runner_backend` default to `none`/`auto` when the target backend is `flashinfer_megamoe` and the speculative flags are unset, and that explicit `--speculative-moe-runner-backend`/`--speculative-moe-a2a-backend` still override.
