title: [Fix] Plan NextN / MTP draft layers as one-layer models and fix the Bailing V2 NextN draft
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #41200
* #41199
* #41191
* #41198
* #41197
* #41196
* #41195
* __->__ #41194
* #41193

## Motivation

This PR fixes three defects in NextN / MTP draft layers. Each commit fixes one.

1. **Layout plan.** `LayerScatterModes` treats `layer_id == 0` as the first layer (it takes the model's input layout) and `layer_id == num_layers - 1` as the last (it returns the model's output layout). Two draft layers were planned as middle layers instead:
   - the Bailing V2 / V2.5 NextN layers, passed as layer 0 of `num_hidden_layers`;
   - the Step-3.5 MTP layer, passed as layer 45 of 1.

   When the draft's MLP runs on SCATTERED tokens with attention TP > 1, the draft returned this rank's shard of tokens to the logits and to the next step. The SCATTERED triggers are an a2a backend, dwdp, FP4 cutlass allgather, or `moe_dense_tp_size` 1. The Step-3.5 MTP layer also planned an all-gather for an input that is already full. Separately, the Bailing V2.5 NextN plan treated the layer as dense whenever the model's first layers are dense, even though the layer builds an MoE. DeepSeek NextN and Bailing V3 already pass layer 0 of 1 (the same fix as #7420 for DeepSeek).
2. **Unloaded Bailing V2 NextN MLP.** `BailingMoEBlock` chose between the MoE and the dense MLP with `is_nextn=False`. So the NextN layer (layer 0) became a dense MLP whenever `first_k_dense_replace >= 1`, while the checkpoint's NextN layer holds expert weights (Ling-mini-2.0: `model.layers.20.mlp.experts.*`). `load_weights` skips names with no matching parameter, so the draft ran an MLP whose weights were never loaded (all zeros).
3. **Bailing V2 NextN could not start.** Every Bailing draft is renamed `BailingMoeForCausalLMNextN`, and `_derive_model_shapes` sent that name down the MLA branch added for V2.5. V2 is GQA and has no `kv_lora_rank`, so NextN speculative decoding on a V2 target failed at startup with `'BailingMoeV2Config' object has no attribute 'kv_lora_rank'`.

## Modifications

- **`models/bailing_moe.py`, `models/bailing_moe_linear.py`, `models/step3p5.py`:** draft layers pass `layer_id=0, num_layers=1` to `LayerScatterModes.init_new`. The Step-3.5 layer id still indexes its per-layer config. The Bailing V2.5 NextN plan is sparse.
- **`models/bailing_moe.py`:** the NextN layer builds `BailingMoESparseMoeBlock`.
- **`configs/model_config.py`:** the MLA branch takes `BailingMoeForCausalLMNextN` only when the draft config carries `kv_lora_rank`, which the V2.5 and V3 drafts do. A V2 draft now derives its shapes the way its target does. V3 drafts still take this branch rather than the V3 one, as before.
- **Tests:**
  - `test_last_layer_communicator.py` now records the `LayerScatterModes.init_new` arguments. It checks that every draft layer is planned as layer 0 of 1, that the V2.5 NextN plan is sparse, and that the V2 NextN layer builds the MoE block.
  - `test_model_config_shapes.py`: a GQA and an MLA Bailing draft each keep their attention architecture.

  All of these fail on main.

Configurations whose MLP does not run on SCATTERED tokens plan the same layouts before and after.

## Accuracy Tests

**GPU, H200, Ling-mini-base-2.0 TP2.** 4 greedy requests × 32 tokens; text, token logprobs and top-5 logprobs compared. NextN speculative decoding with 1 step, topk 1 and 2 draft tokens; also the default 3 / 1 / 4. Accept length = completion tokens / verify steps.

Runs before the third commit need a test-harness shim that only derives the draft's shapes. It is applied identically to every tree and is not needed after the third commit.

| Tree | Config | Result | Accept length |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | speculative off | reference | – |
| main / first commit | speculative | identical to the reference | 1.600 / 1.600 |
| second commit | speculative | text identical to the reference | **1.939** |
| main / first / second | speculative, default 3 / 1 / 4 | text identical | 1.684 / 1.684 / **2.462** |
| main | speculative, `moe_dense_tp_size=1` | **crash** on the first draft forward: index out of bounds in `logits_processor._get_logits` | – |
| first / second commit | speculative, `moe_dense_tp_size=1` | identical to the target-only run with the same setting | 1.580 / 1.910 |
| third commit, no shim | the configurations above | starts; identical to each shimmed run | 1.939 / 2.462 / 1.910 |

- **Draft-layer audit:**
  - main under `moe_dense_tp_size=1`: `mlp=SCATTERED, layer_output_mode=SCATTERED`;
  - first commit: `layer_output_mode=TP_ATTN_FULL`;
  - second commit: the NextN layer is `BailingMoESparseMoeBlock`.
- **Weight checksums before and after `load_weights`:**
  - on main, the draft's dense `gate_up_proj` / `down_proj` stay all zeros;
  - after the second commit, only the `word_embeddings` / `lm_head` shared with the target are untouched.

**GPU, H200, Step-3.5-Flash BF16 TP8 MTP** (EAGLE 3 / 1 / 4):

- **Default configuration:** main and this PR are bit-identical (accept length 2.560).
- **With `moe_dense_tp_size=1`:** main crashes in the draft's CUDA graph capture (`size of tensor a (32) must match ... b (4)`: the MTP layer returned its shard), and this PR does not.
- **Caveat:** the Step-3.5 target and its MTP draft are not correct under that setting. `Step3p5MLP` always shards over TP and all-reduces, so on SCATTERED tokens it sums different ranks' tokens. Only the crash fix is verified here, not end-to-end output; the dense MLP under `moe_dense_tp_size=1` is left for a follow-up.

Rebased onto main `9dc4c5d891`: every commit's patch is unchanged, and the related unit tests pass on the new base. The GPU results above were measured on the previous base, `5bb850d536`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not measured. The layout plans change only under the SCATTERED triggers, and the second commit makes the draft's MLP the MoE the checkpoint was trained with.

title: [Fix] Stop counting a deferred FFN sum more than once: replicated TP1 shared expert, dense reduce_scatterv
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #41200
* #41199
* #41191
* #41198
* #41197
* #41196
* __->__ #41195
* #41194
* #41193

## Motivation

This PR fixes two cases where a layer's output was summed more than it should be when its FFN reduction runs later than the FFN.

1. **Replicated TP1 shared expert.** With `SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1=1`, Laguna and `DeepseekV2MoE` (DeepSeek-V2/V3, GLM5-Next without MHC) replicate the shared expert on every TP rank and add its full output after the MoE all-reduce. When that all-reduce is left to a later step, the MoE block returns a partial sum and every rank still adds the shared output. So the later sum counts it `tp_size` times. The later step is either fused into the next layer's residual norm, or, under DP attention, the reduce-scatter back to the local tokens.
2. **Dense layers under DP attention reduce_scatterv.** Under DP attention with tp == dp == ep and no a2a backend, `postprocess_layer` reduce-scatterv'd every FULL-mode layer's output, whether or not the layer allows reduce-scatter.
   - A MoE block leaves its all-reduce out under the same condition, so that sum is owed.
   - A dense MLP leaves it out only under the published `mlp_reduce_scatter`, which needs `allow_reduce_scatter`. Without it, the MLP has already all-reduced, and the reduce-scatterv sums the output `tp_size` times.

   The layers affected are the dense layers of Qwen3, MOSS-VL, Step3-VL, LongCat-Flash and Bailing-MoE-Linear, and the MiMo-V2 MTP layer. The MoE blocks of Step3-VL (`Step3TextMoEMLP`) and LongCat-Flash (`LongcatFlashMoE`) all-reduce inside the block, so reduce_scatterv still sums their output twice; this PR does not change them. Separately, the LongCat-Flash NextN dense MLP never reduced its output at TP > 1; only reduce_scatterv summed it, by accident.

## Modifications

- **TP1 shared expert:**
  - `should_add_replicated_moe_output()`: when a later step still owes the TP sum, only TP rank 0 adds the replicated shared output; otherwise every rank adds it. Paths that reduce inside the MoE block, or whose output is already complete, keep their numerics.
  - A source guard requires every model that reads `SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1` to add the shared output under this predicate.
- **Dense reduce_scatterv:**
  - postprocess uses reduce_scatterv only when the layer is sparse or allows reduce-scatter, and otherwise scatters without summing. `LayerScatterModes` records `is_layer_sparse` for this.
  - The LongCat-Flash NextN MLP all-reduces its own output like the other dense layers.
  - `test_postprocess_reduce_scatterv.py` pairs every (sparse × allow) combination with the FFN's own skip predicate, so postprocess sums exactly when the FFN left the sum out.

## Accuracy Tests

**TP1 shared expert, B200, DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP2 with the env on** (4 greedy requests × 32 tokens; text, token logprobs and top-5 logprobs compared; TP1 is the reference):

| Config | First diverging token (4 requests) | Max step-0 top-5 \|Δlogp\| |
|---|---|---|
| parent, fusion on | 1, 1, 1, 0 | 1.846 |
| this PR, fusion on | 32, 4, 32, 32 | 0.112 |
| parent, fusion off (noise reference) | 1, 32, 32, 32 | 0.092 |
| parent, DP attention (dp 2) | 1, 1, 1, 2 | 1.075 |
| this PR, DP attention (dp 2) | 32, 32, 32, 32 | 0.073 |

The configurations that owe no later sum are bit-identical to the parent: env on with fusion off, and env off with fusion on.

**Dense reduce_scatterv, B200:**

| Config | Result |
|---|---|
| main, Qwen3-0.6B TP2 DP2 ep 2 | diverges at tokens 0, 0, 6, 1 (max step-0 top-5 \|Δlogp\| 1.75); output turns into garbage |
| main, same with ep 1 (reduce_scatterv does not apply) | TP2 noise level |
| this PR, ep 2 vs this PR, ep 1 | identical (for a dense model, ep only changes the reduce_scatterv decision) |
| this PR ep 1 vs main ep 1 | identical |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 TP2 DP2 ep 2 (sparse, allows reduce-scatter), parent vs this PR | identical |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP2 DP2 ep 2, parent vs this PR | identical |

The unit tests for MoE output reduction, the layer-stack exit, aux capture, postprocess reduce_scatterv, the layout and the CP dense MLP all pass.

Rebased onto main `9dc4c5d891`: every commit's patch is unchanged, and the related unit tests pass on the new base. The GPU results above were measured on the previous base, `5bb850d536`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No collective is added. The dense reduce_scatterv fix replaces a reduce-scatter with a scatter on the affected layers.

title: [Fix] processor: Restore BOS/EOS flags for processor-owned tokenizers
author: zyt329
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Transformers v5 may drop `add_bos_token` and `add_eos_token` settings when
loading a tokenizer backed by `tokenizer.json`. It assumes that the serialized
tokenizer post-processor already handles BOS/EOS insertion, but that is not true
for every tokenizer configuration.

SGLang already compensates for this behavior in `get_tokenizer()` by reading
`tokenizer_config.json`, restoring the supported flags, and rebuilding the
tokenizer post-processor.

SGLang has two related loading entry points:

- `get_tokenizer()` returns a tokenizer directly and is typically used by
  text-only loading paths.
- `get_processor()` returns a multimodal processor that owns a tokenizer in
  addition to image, audio, or other preprocessing components.

Both entry points ultimately tokenize the text portion of a request, so their
tokenizer compatibility behavior should be consistent. Before this change,
only the direct `get_tokenizer()` path applied the Transformers-v5 BOS/EOS
repair. The tokenizer embedded in a processor bypassed it.

This does not affect every model. The compatibility helper is limited to
tokenizer classes that supported these flags before Transformers v5, currently
including Llama, Code Llama, Gemma, and Cohere tokenizers. It is a no-op for
other tokenizer classes and for configurations whose values are already
correct.

Multimodal models commonly load the same tokenizer through `get_processor()`.
That path extracts the processor-owned tokenizer and applies several post-load
fixes, but it does not apply the existing BOS/EOS compatibility repair. The same
checkpoint can therefore tokenize a prompt differently depending on which
loading entry point is used. For affected Gemma tokenizers, the processor path
can omit the expected BOS token.

This change does not alter Transformers itself or introduce a new compatibility
policy. It applies SGLang's existing policy consistently to the tokenizer owned
by a processor.

## Modifications

- Apply the existing `_fix_v5_add_bos_eos_token()` helper to the final tokenizer
  selected by `get_processor()`.
- Keep the compatibility policy in one place rather than duplicating it in the
  processor loader.
- Add a CPU-only regression test that loads a local Gemma tokenizer
  configuration through the processor path and verifies that `add_bos_token`
  is restored and the tokenizer post-processor is rebuilt.

The helper already limits restoration to tokenizer classes that supported
these flags before Transformers v5. Unsupported tokenizer classes and
tokenizers with correct settings remain unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

This changes tokenizer initialization rather than model execution. The added
CPU regression test verifies the affected tokenization state without model
weights or accelerator hardware.

- Focused unit test: pending GitHub CI.
- Python syntax check: passed.
- `black --check`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The compatibility repair runs once while loading a processor
and does not affect the inference hot path.

title: [Fix] [XPU] runtime: Fix XPU rotary embeddings and tokenizer padding
author: vshekhawat-hlab
body:
## Motivation

Two independent, unrelated-but-small fixes found:

1. Partial rotary embeddings crash on XPU's fallback kernel path.
2. Custom remote-code tokenizers with a stale `_pad()` override crashing on every request once `padding_side` started being forwarded (found via `zai-org/chatglm2-6b`).

## Modifications

### 1. `RotaryEmbedding.forward_xpu()` partial rotary embeddings (`python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py`)

The fallback-kernel branch (used when `head_size` is not in `[128, 256, 512]`) calls `torch.ops.sgl_kernel.rotary_embedding(...)` without slicing to `rotary_dim` first. That compiled kernel asserts `rotary_dim == head_size` internally and raises `RuntimeError: Rotary dim doesn't match query head_size` for any model with partial rotary embeddings (`rotary_dim < head_size`) on XPU, e.g. `adept/persimmon-8b-chat`, `microsoft/phi-2`, `stabilityai/stablelm-2-1_6b`, `stabilityai/stablelm-3b-4e1t`, `stabilityai/stablelm-zephyr-3b`. Independent of `--attention-backend`, since rotary embedding dispatch is keyed on device type (`is_xpu()`).

Fix: add an `elif self.head_size != self.rotary_dim` branch that falls back to `forward_native()`, mirroring the existing pattern where `forward_cpu`/`forward_npu` already fall back to `forward_native` for their own unsupported cases.

### 2. Tokenizer `_pad()` compat shim for stale custom signatures (`python/sglang/srt/utils/patch_tokenizer.py`)

transformers 5.x's `PreTrainedTokenizerBase.pad()` now always forwards `padding_side` down to `_pad()`. Custom remote-code tokenizers with a stale, fixed `_pad()` signature (no `padding_side` param, no `**kwargs` catch-all -- e.g. `zai-org/chatglm2-6b`'s `ChatGLMTokenizer`, unchanged for years) crash with:

```
TypeError: ChatGLMTokenizer._pad() got an unexpected keyword argument 'padding_side'
```

on every single generation request, regardless of memory/backend settings.

Fix: detects the mismatch structurally via `inspect.signature` (not a name/class check), so any other custom tokenizer with the same stale signature is covered too, and wraps `_pad()` to drop the `padding_side` kwarg before delegating to the original implementation (which already reads `self.padding_side` directly, so behavior is unchanged). Also adds `_PadPaddingSideShim.unpatch()`, wired into the shared `unpatch_tokenizer()` entrypoint, so the pad shim no longer leaks across test/tokenizer instances.

## Accuracy Tests

Both fixes were validated end-to-end on real Intel XPU hardware, not just reasoned about statically:

- **Rotary fix**: 20-example accuracy smoke checks (server + client, real GPU) for `adept/persimmon-8b-chat` (intel_xpu backend, gsm8k), `microsoft/phi-2` (triton backend, gsm8k), `stabilityai/stablelm-3b-4e1t` (triton backend, hellaswag), `stabilityai/stablelm-zephyr-3b` (triton backend, gsm8k) -- all previously crashed with `RuntimeError: Rotary dim doesn't match query head_size`, all now serve and produce results.
- **Tokenizer `_pad()` shim**: confirmed on real Intel XPU hardware against `zai-org/chatglm2-6b`: the `TypeError` no longer occurs and generation requests proceed past tokenization/padding to a correct completion.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. Both fixes are either startup-time compatibility shims or exception-path corrections -- neither touches inference-loop math or kernels.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit) guide -- `pre-commit run` passes clean on every changed file.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests) guide -- added for the tokenizer `_pad()` shim (patch/unpatch lifecycle, idempotency, per-call override, restoration on raise); the rotary fix was validated by reproducing the original crash on real hardware and confirming it's gone (see Accuracy Tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations) -- not applicable; both are internal bug fixes with no user-facing API or CLI changes.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed) -- see Accuracy Tests above; no speed impact.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Closes #41088. Supersedes and replaces #41796 (folded in here at the author's request to land together; that PR will be closed in favor of this PR).

The `UnifiedRadixCache.dec_lock_ref` fix originally bundled here has been dropped from this PR per review feedback (the "restore the default" approach could mask a real missing-receipt bug); that fix is tracked separately in #41142.

title: [Fix] glm47: Disable tool grammar for `tool_choice="none"`
author: toulzx
body:
## Motivation

With `--tool-call-parser glm47`, a request that supplies tools but explicitly sets `tool_choice="none"` still receives the GLM47 `full_assistant_ebnf` grammar.

That grammar describes a complete assistant turn. Reaching its terminal state finishes generation through the grammar path, which does not consult `ignore_eos`. An `ignore_eos=true` request can therefore stop at the model's end-of-turn token instead of reaching `max_tokens`, even though the request disabled tool calls.

### Behavior scope

| Request | Expected behavior | Ownership |
|---|---|---|
| No `tools` | Do not install the GLM47 tool-call grammar | Already fixed and tested by #39273 |
| `tools` + `tool_choice="none"` | Do not install the GLM47 tool-call grammar | Core fix in this PR |
| `tools` + `tool_choice="auto"` | Preserve the existing GLM47 grammar behavior | Regression coverage |
| `tools` + `tool_choice="required"` | Preserve the existing behavior | Regression coverage |
| `tools` + named tool choice | Preserve named-tool selection semantics | Regression coverage |
| Tools on `system`/`developer` messages | Include them in the active GLM47 grammar | Adjacent consistency fix requested during review |

### Relationship to #39273

The original version of this PR covered two cases:

1. requests with no tools; and
2. requests with tools plus `tool_choice="none"`.

While this PR was under review, #39273 independently added the `bool(effective_tools)` guard and a no-tools regression test as part of its GLM-5.3 work. Commit `f17f7705a5a67c137edf279edfdbd5460f2ceb6e` therefore already fixed case 1.

This branch was subsequently rebased onto main commit `4b384df0c94dbd0fe30627c27c98c0441b4ebd96`, which contains #39273. The duplicated no-tools production change and duplicated test were removed. The remaining core fix in this PR is case 2: tools are available, but the request explicitly disables tool calls with `tool_choice="none"`.

The no-tools history is retained here so reports that found the original analysis through this PR can follow that part of the fix to #39273.

## Modifications

Scope the GLM47 grammar to requests that provide tools and allow tool calls:

```python
glm_constraint = (
    self.tool_call_parser == "glm47"
    and bool(effective_tools)
    and request.tool_choice != "none"
    and not any(tool.function.strict for tool in effective_tools)
)
```

`auto`, `required`, and named-tool choices retain their existing grammar behavior. Other tool-call parsers are unchanged.

### Message-scoped tool consistency

`_effective_tools(request)` includes tools declared on `system` and `developer` messages. That effective set decides whether the GLM47 grammar is active, but the parser previously received only top-level `request.tools`. A request with message-scoped tools could therefore activate a grammar that omitted those functions.

The GLM47 parser now receives `effective_tools`. The regression test uses the real XGrammar parser and verifies message-scoped tools for `auto`, `required`, and named-tool choices, as well as the disabled `none` case.

### Test cleanup

- Keep the existing #39273 no-tools regression test.
- Remove the combined mocked no-tools/none test, which duplicated #39273 and the retained real-parser matrix.
- Remove the mocked auto test, which passed before this fix and only checked mock-result propagation.

Deliberately not changed:

- GLM47 grammar generation or grammar-terminal finish handling.
- Generic Jinja rendering of message-scoped tools, which affects multiple model families and needs separate cross-model coverage.
- Template compatibility for the `developer` role.

## Accuracy Tests

No model forward code or kernel is changed. The checks below validate request semantics and grammar construction rather than model accuracy.

### Unit tests

Environment:

- Python 3.12.3
- pytest 9.1.1
- XGrammar available in the test image

Command:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=/tmp/pr41233-src/python python3 -m pytest \
  test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py \
  -k glm47 -v
```

On baseline `4b384df0c94dbd0fe30627c27c98c0441b4ebd96`, with the regression test applied but without the production fix:

```text
24 failed, 2 passed, 154 deselected, 16 warnings
```

The existing #39273 no-tools test passed. The new matrix failed for the message-scoped-tool cases and, importantly for this PR, for every `tool_choice="none"` subtest, including the case with a top-level tool.

With the fix applied:

```text
2 passed, 154 deselected, 16 warnings, 24 subtests passed
```

The complete serving-chat unit file was also run on the fixed snapshot:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=/tmp/pr41233-src/python python3 -m pytest \
  test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py -v
```

```text
156 passed, 63 warnings, 126 subtests passed in 46.16s
```

### GLM-5.3 end-to-end reproduction

The E2E comparison specifically tested **tools plus `tool_choice="none"`**; it was not a no-tools test.

Source snapshots:

- Before: main commit `99463390f83a39776d452ba12199941b96a4f36f`
- After: the same source snapshot plus the production diff from local fix `c5649e50245567827c63ac9d9dc3fafb2334a00b`
- The relevant production code in that fix is identical to the subsequently rebased branch.

Hardware and model:

- 1 node with 8 x NVIDIA H200 GPUs
- Model path: `/models/zai-org/GLM-5.3`
- Served model name: `glm-5.3`
- Container tag: `sglang:dev-cu13-260921` 
- Launch requested TP=8 and DP-attention DP=8. The effective server log reported `tp_size=8`, `attn_dp_size=8`, and `dp_size=1`.
- The launch command passed `--chunked-prefill-size 32768`; the normalized server arguments logged an effective `chunked_prefill_size=4096`.
- `SGLANG_SKIP_SGL_KERNEL_VERSION_CHECK=1` was set. 

Server command:

```bash
SGLANG_SKIP_SGL_KERNEL_VERSION_CHECK=1 \
PYTHONPATH=/tmp/pr41233-src/python \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/zhipuai/GLM-5.3 \
  --served-model-name glm-5.3 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 30000 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --context-length 102400 \
  --tp 8 \
  --dp 8 \
  --enable-dp-attention \
  --moe-a2a-backend deepep \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 1 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 2 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \
  --max-running-requests 16 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85
```

Request, repeated five times against each server:

```bash
curl --fail --silent --show-error \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions \
  --data-binary @- <<'JSON'
{
  "model": "glm-5.3",
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "Answer exactly with the word OK and nothing else."
    }
  ],
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "get_weather",
        "description": "Get the weather for a city.",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}},
          "required": ["city"]
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "tool_choice": "none",
  "temperature": 0,
  "seed": 42,
  "ignore_eos": true,
  "max_tokens": 300,
  "stop": null,
  "stream": false
}
JSON
```

Results:

| Snapshot | Completion tokens (5 runs) | Finish reason | `matched_stop` | Tool calls |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Baseline `99463390f8` | 66, 61, 47, 54, 67 | `stop` for all runs | 154827 for all runs | none |
| Fix `c5649e5024` | 300, 300, 300, 300, 300 | `length` for all runs | null for all runs | none |

Expected behavior: because the request explicitly disables tool calls and sets `ignore_eos=true`, no tool grammar should be installed and generation should continue until the 300-token cap. The fixed snapshot did so in all five runs.


## Speed Tests and Profiling

No throughput benchmark was run or claimed. Requests that continue to use the GLM47 grammar retain the same grammar-masking path. This PR only removes an inapplicable grammar from requests that explicitly disable tool calls.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the changed code according to the repository style.
- [x] Add regression coverage according to the unit-test admission rules.
- [x] Record the exact source snapshots and commands used for validation.
- [ ] Documentation update. Not needed for this internal request-routing fix.
- [ ] Accuracy/speed benchmark. No model-forward or performance change is claimed; targeted unit and E2E correctness results are provided above.

title: Fix KV offload synchronization
author: yueming-yuan
body:
## Motivation

`flush_cache()` can return while cache-clearing CUDA kernels are still pending. The KV memory-saver region is then unmapped without waiting for those kernels, causing `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`. Synchronization at the end of `release_memory_occupation()` is too late.

This defect was reproduced while investigating the Qwen3.8 Next failure in radixark/miles release CI [36114613496](https://github.com/radixark/miles/actions/runs/36114613496). That integration run reported the asynchronous CUDA fault while cloning static model buffers after KV pause; the complete model path now passes the targeted validation below.

## Modifications

Synchronize the device after flushing and before pausing KV memory. Extend the existing flush-order unit test to require synchronization before pause.

## Accuracy Tests

- H200, frozen Miles v0.1.1 CI image, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, torch_memory_saver b5588e83de86412a48689a6583a4b567e75f7acc.
- Controlled A/B through the actual pinned SGLang release/resume handler, with 128 MiB of KV memory and an event proving pending cache-clearing work. Original code fails in the first cycle on both default and independent CUDA streams with CUDA 700. The fix passes 10 release/resume cycles per stream, freeing 128 MiB each cycle.
- Updated unit regression fails on the original implementation and passes with the fix.
- The original Qwen3.8 Next 4-layer test now passes on 8 H200s: [Miles run 36144564076](https://github.com/radixark/miles/actions/runs/36144564076). Both TP4/EP4 engines complete the first release/resume and all five training rollouts complete normally. The frozen release image and Megatron SHA are unchanged; SGLang is pinned to this PR head. This validates that test configuration; full release-matrix validation remains pending.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No throughput claim. Synchronization is added only to KV release, outside steady-state decoding.

## Checklist

- [x] File-scoped pre-commit checks pass.
- [x] Existing unit test extended with a discriminating regression assertion.
- [x] Minimal change; no public API or documentation changes needed.

title: [PD] fix: cache resumed decode-radix requests from root instead of an unlocked re-match
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

With `--disaggregation-mode decode --disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache`, a request that is retracted and later resumed goes back through `_get_new_prebuilt_batch` with `last_node is None` (cleared by `reset_for_retract`). The prebuilt path then re-matches the tree via `init_next_round_input(tree_cache)`, which takes no lock, and `cache_unfinished_req` releases the matched node with the empty receipt:

- If another running request holds that prefix, its lock is stolen. Once the resumed request finishes, the holder's prefix becomes evictable while it is still decoding; its KV slots return to the free list and are handed to new requests, so the holder attends over another request's KV. Its own final release then fails (`KeyError`).
- If nobody holds the prefix, the release hits `FULL segment release hit lock_ref=0` and the scheduler dies.
- `cache_protected_len` is set to the matched length while the row still holds the request's own restored copy of that prefix, so those slots are never freed.

The same path is taken by rebootstrapped requests.

## Modifications

A resumed (or rebootstrapped) request owns its whole KV row, which is exactly the case the host-receive preallocation already handles by starting the request at the root. Extract that block into `_bind_root_prefix` and use it in `_get_new_prebuilt_batch` instead of re-matching. `cache_unfinished_req` then inserts from position 0: the tree frees the duplicate prefix copy, the rematch points the row at the tree's slots, and the lock is taken by the normal inc/dec pair.

## Accuracy Tests

`test_resumed_retracted_req_keeps_other_holders_lock` drives `_get_new_prebuilt_batch` with a real `Req` and checks that another holder's prefix lock survives and that the row ends on the tree's slots. It fails on main with `AssertionError: 1 != 2` (the stolen lock) and passes with this change.

The same flow on a `UnifiedRadixCache` (FULL) fixture:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| holder prefix `lock_ref` after resume | 1 (stolen) | 2 |
| resumed row `[0, P)` | own copy, orphaned | tree slots |
| holder prefix after evict, holder still running | evicted, slots reused | resident |
| holder release | `KeyError` | ok, allocator back to baseline |

`test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_decode_radix_lock_ref.py` and `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/`: 493 passed, 1 skipped.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [diffusion] fix: LoRA-wrapped linears crash Qwen-Image and MiniMax-H3 inference
author: Rockdu
body:
## Motivation

Loading any LoRA crashes plain inference for two models on `main`. Each crash comes from a forward path that reads a field of a linear layer, while the LoRA wrapper (`*WithLoRA`) does not expose that field:

| Model | Crash | Introduced by |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image | `'MergedColumnParallelLinearWithLoRA' object has no attribute 'output_partition_sizes'` | #36680 (packed `to_added_qkv` split path) |
| MiniMax-H3 | `'RowParallelLinearWithLoRA' object has no attribute 'quant_method'` | #37903 (`_accepts_mxfp8_input` gate) |

## Modifications

title: [Fix] deepseek-v4.1: Match KV capacity to physical layouts
author: ischencheng
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4.1 ratio-1/2 owners can allocate V41 FP8 or FP4 global KV, but their capacity coefficient still uses the V4 584-byte row. This underestimates V4 page padding and overestimates V41 storage, reducing the token capacity selected at startup. Finalize only updates state-pool sizes, and DeepSeek-V4 is excluded from post-capture resizing.

## Modifications

- Use the existing layout-aware paged-byte helper for ratio-1/2 growth, retaining the existing owner and backend selection rules.
- Charge reserved main/indexer pages separately, including index-page rounding at the candidate capacity, then lower capacity by full pages until the budget fits.
- Add focused CPU tests whose expected bytes come from the real main/index/state pool constructors: three layout-growth cases (V4, V41 FP8, default V41 FP4), two FP4 exact-fit/one-byte-under capacity cases including index-page rounding, stage-local owner/reuse accounting, and backend guards. Full-page 128 and stage slices are arithmetic checks; they do not extend V41 serving support.

## Accuracy Tests

Before test simplification, the larger regression matrix had 84 failing allocation/capacity subcases on the pre-fix source; 98 tests and 115 subtests passed with the fix across the five files below. Those counts describe the earlier test revision. The current revision reduces the main matrices to five representative configurations, removes repeated finalize/token-cap assertions, and retains owner/reuse and backend coverage. Ruff lint/format and diff checks pass; local execution of the revised tests was blocked by missing dependencies (NumPy/PyTorch). Targeted CI is being requested for the revised head, including DSV4 and DSV4.1 model regressions. No kernels, quantization, model forward code or allocation layout are changed. Model accuracy is not yet established.

```sh
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_pool_configurator.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dsv4_compressed_pools.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dsv4_unified_fp8_pool.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dsv4_c4_state_lifecycle.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dsv4_compress_write_pad.py
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Allocation validation only, on one B200 without model weights or attention execution. At 1,048,576 tokens, full page 256, index page 128 and owners at layers 2/8/14/20, corrected global main+index tensor budgets equal the production constructors' measured CUDA tensor bytes:

| Layout | Old budget (B) | Corrected / measured tensor bytes (B) | Capacity under the same 1,709,178,880 B global budget |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| V4 | 1,709,178,880 | 1,712,477,696 | 1,046,528 |
| V41 FP8 | 1,709,178,880 | 1,562,997,248 | 1,146,624 |
| V41 FP4 | 1,709,178,880 | 933,605,888 | 1,920,000 |

Each corrected capacity fits the tensor budget; one additional full page exceeds it. SWA, weights, state and CUDA allocator overhead are outside this table. The test image did not advertise V41 FlashMLA reader support; explicit V41 tensor construction was checked, not reader execution. Index page 128 was selected explicitly (the image's native setting was 64). No end-to-end throughput or latency claim.

## Checklist

- [x] Focused pre-commit and full default-stage non-Rust hooks pass; unrelated Rust hooks skipped.
- [x] Add focused regression tests.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.
- [ ] Model accuracy / service benchmark (not run; allocation-budget change only).

title: [Fix] compressed-tensors: Serve split-expert MXFP4 MoE via FP4 Marlin
author: jlqibm
body:
## Motivation

Stacks on #41288  (`fix/compressed-tensors-mxfp4-marlin`), which fixed MXFP4 **dense
linear**. This fixes MXFP4 **MoE**.

A compressed-tensors `mxfp4-pack-quantized` MoE checkpoint whose experts are
stored **split per expert** (`experts.{e}.{gate,up,down}_proj.*`, as emitted by
llmcompressor) cannot load today. The A/B control, same node and same venv:

- On #41288 : `KeyError: 'model.layers.0.block_sparse_moe.experts.w2_weight_packed'`
  at `granitemoe.py:93`.
- On this PR: loads, 0 tensors dropped, coherent output.

The cause is a layout mismatch, not a missing kernel. `Mxfp4MoEMethod` and
`Mxfp4MarlinMoEMethod` handle the **fused** GPT-OSS layout and register
`w13/w2_weight`; a split-expert checkpoint's per-expert tensors have no
destination there.

## Modifications

Add `CompressedTensorsW4A16Mxfp4MoE`, a weight-only MXFP4 MoE scheme registering
the `_packed` parameter names and routing to the FP4 Marlin MoE runner. It serves
both `mxfp4a16` and `mxfp4` w4a4; the latter's activation quantization is
dropped, since the Marlin MoE kernel is weight-only. A w4a4 checkpoint still
ships input global scales and the split-expert loader raises `KeyError` on any
tensor with no registered destination, so they are registered and only then
dropped in `process_weights_after_loading`.

Unlike NVFP4 there is no `weight_global_scale`, so the compressed-tensors
reciprocal convention (CT stores `1/scale` where Marlin wants `scale`) does not
arise here.

`check_moe_marlin_supports_layer` is deliberately not called: it tests
`group_size` against the GPTQ/AWQ set and reports on int4 zero-point parameters
this layout does not have. The shape constraints it would have covered
(`hidden_size % 128 == 0`, `intermediate_size_per_partition % 64 == 0`) are
validated explicitly instead.

### How the two layouts are told apart

They cannot be told apart from the config. GraniteMoe and Kimi-K3 ship
indistinguishable `mxfp4-pack-quantized` configs — same `quant_method`, same
`format`, `config_groups` targeting `["Linear"]` in both, both using
`make_expert_params_mapping`. The real difference lives in the model loader:
Kimi-K3 renames `weight_packed`→`weight` and substitutes `Mxfp4Config` before
building its experts.

So the selection is an explicit opt-out rather than config sniffing: `FusedMoE`
gains a `serves_fused_mxfp4: bool = True` constructor parameter, and
`granitemoe.py` passes `False`. It must be a constructor parameter, not a
post-construction attribute, because `get_quant_method` runs inside
`FusedMoE.__init__`.

**Every existing fused MXFP4 MoE keeps the default and is unaffected.** That is
asserted in both directions by a new test, since a silent kernel change on the
GPT-OSS path would be the worst failure mode here.

## Accuracy Tests

Granite MoE (`GraniteMoeForCausalLM`), H100 80GB, all coherent text:

| model | TP | mxfp4 | mxfp4a16 | nvfp4 | nvfp4a16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20b  | 1 | OK | OK | OK | OK |
| 20b  | 2 | OK | OK | OK | — |
| 20b  | 4 | OK | OK | OK | — |
| 120b | 4 | OK | OK | — | — |

13 `[OK]`, rc=0, 0 tensors dropped. 120b is independently valuable: 128 experts
vs 56, hidden 3072 vs 2048.

18 CPU scheme-selection tests + 8 subtests, covering the MXFP4/NVFP4 predicate
boundary (both are FP4 group quant; only `group_size` and `strategy` separate
them, so a widened predicate would silently steal the other's checkpoints), the
registered-parameter contract against the checkpoint's names/shapes/dtypes, and
the fused-bypass gate in both directions.

Dense MXFP4 output is byte-identical to PR 2's, confirming the MoE scheme does
not perturb the dense path.

The fused GPT-OSS MXFP4 MoE path is covered by the CPU gate test rather than
end-to-end: GPT-OSS uses native `Mxfp4Config`, so it never enters
`CompressedTensorsConfig.get_quant_method`, and no compressed-tensors fused MXFP4
MoE checkpoint was available to test against. The gate test asserts the dispatch
branch directly, which is a stronger check than inferring it from generated text.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No benchmark run. Weight-only via the existing FP4 Marlin MoE runner — no new
kernel, and activations stay bf16. `get_min_capability()` is 80 and the routing
is capability-independent, so Blackwell takes the same MoE path as Hopper. The one
asymmetry: an **NVFP4** w4a4 MoE checkpoint on SM100 still keeps the native
`CompressedTensorsW4A4Nvfp4MoE` scheme (capability 100); the weight-only fallback
must not lower that gate, which is why they are separate classes and is asserted
by `test_nvfp4_w4a4_keeps_native_scheme_on_blackwell`.

title: [Fix] gemma4: Honor OOT attention defaults
author: zyt329
body:
## Motivation

SGLang's generic attention-backend resolution lets an out-of-tree platform provide its default through `SRTPlatform.get_default_attention_backend()`. Gemma4 bypasses that contract: its model-specific override resolves the backend earlier to a built-in `triton` or `trtllm_mha` default, and its subsequent static allowlist rejects a platform-provided backend.

As a result, an out-of-tree platform cannot use its registered attention backend as the Gemma4 default even though the same platform API works for other MHA models.

## Modifications

- Use the active out-of-tree platform's declared default for non-diffusion Gemma4 models when no attention backend was explicitly selected.
- Accept that same platform-owned default in Gemma4's backend validation.
- Preserve the existing built-in CUDA/SM100 defaults, the DiffusionGemma `triton` default, and explicit common or split backend selections.
- Add focused unit coverage for out-of-tree defaulting, explicit selection, split prefill/decode selection, validation, and DiffusionGemma behavior.

## Accuracy Tests

This change only affects startup-time backend resolution and does not modify model math.

- Added a fake out-of-tree platform regression test in `test/registered/unit/test_model_overrides.py`.
- Isolated behavior checks passed for unset, explicit common, split prefill, split decode, validation allowlist, and DiffusionGemma cases.
- Full registered unit tests have not yet been run locally because the current development environment does not contain the SGLang test dependencies.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The new checks run only during server-argument resolution and do not affect the inference hot path.

title: [Fix] deepseek-v4.1: Keep the full SWA window for short bounded-replay extends
author: vineelbhat
body:
## Motivation

With DeepSeek-V4.1's `--enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay`, the layers after the last kv_source layer attend over only the last `min(window, extend_len)` rows of each prefill extend. An extend shorter than the window therefore gives the prompt's first sampled token a truncated window.

This happens on a prefix-cache hit that leaves fewer than `window` uncached rows, and on a chunked prefill whose final chunk is shorter than `window`.

## Modifications

- A prefix-cache hit now stops at least one sliding window short of the prompt when decoder bounded replay is on. Only a hit that would have left less than a window is shortened, by at most one page. `swa_reprefill_tail_tokens()` returns `sliding_window_size` when the new `CacheInitParams.decoder_swa_bounded_replay` is set.
- The late-layer window of a final prefill chunk shorter than the window is now floored at `seq_len - window` instead of at the chunk start, so the chunk reads the previous chunk's tail rows, which already hold their late-layer KV. This is a two line change in `late_layer_tail_layout`.
- A streaming session turn that borrows its slot's record skips the hold-back: the record is the request's own KV, whose last window is already written. `swa_reprefill_tail_tokens(req)` takes the request for this.
- A prefix hit now runs the same rows with the same window floors as a cold prefill. A short final chunk does not: its tail reads the previous chunk's tail rows, which were computed under that chunk's floor. The short-chunk table below measures the difference.

## Accuracy Tests

4xB200, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP4/EP4, greedy, 12 prompts per row, at the first generated position. Flips count prompts whose sampled token changed; shift is the median change of the reference's sampled-token logprob, in nats.

**Prefix hit.** An 8192-token cached prefix plus N fresh tokens, against a cold prefill of the same prompt.

| uncached rows | flips, stock | flips, fixed | shift, stock | shift, fixed |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 10/12 | 1/12 | 2.40 | 0.03 |
| 2 | 7/12 | 3/12 | 0.90 | 0.15 |
| 8 | 3/12 | 2/12 | 0.44 | 0.09 |
| 32 | 2/12 | 0/12 | 0.003 | 0.002 |
| >= 127 | 0/12 | 0/12 | 0.000 | 0.000 |

**Short final chunk.** A cold 16384 + m token prompt prefilled with a 16384-token chunk size, so its final chunk has m rows, against the same prompt prefilled as one 8192 + m extend after priming its first 8192 tokens.

| final chunk rows m | flips, stock | flips, fixed | shift, stock | shift, fixed |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 5/12 | 0/12 | 0.45 | 0.000 |
| 2 | 4/12 | 1/12 | 0.26 | 0.000 |
| 4 | 1/12 | 0/12 | 0.005 | 0.000 |
| 8 | 1/12 | 0/12 | 0.003 | 0.000 |
| 16 to 127 | 0/12 | 0/12 | 0.000 | 0.000 |

`test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py`: 2789 run on 1xH100, OK (1504 config skips), 1 new case. `test_unified_cache_linker.py`: 32 passed, one existing test updated.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The prefix-match limit only applies when a hit would leave fewer than `window` uncached rows, and then recomputes at most one page. The floor change costs each token of a short final chunk at most a full window of 128 keys to score.

title: [DSA] Fix the pooled-indexer breakable prefill bridge under DP attention
author: mmangkad
body:
## Summary

Fixes a crash with `--enable-dp-attention` + `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable` on GLM-5.3-Flash:

Tested on 4x GB300 (TP4, DP2 and DP4, concurrent uneven prompts): crash before, pass after.

title: [MLX] Fix startup after logical token capacity change
author: Manfredss
body:
## Motivation

MLX servers fail during startup after #39731 with `AttributeError: 'MlxModelRunnerStub' object has no attribute 'kv_cache_configurator'`. The new capacity query reaches the Torch configurator, which the MLX stub does not create.

## Modifications

Report logical token capacity from the MLX pool, keeping the request pool's capacity adjustment. Add a regression covering worker startup and the request limits reported to the scheduler.

## Accuracy Tests

title: [Fix] Require admin auth for /load_lora_adapter_from_tensors and /set_trace_level
author: stanleys12
body:
## Motivation

`/load_lora_adapter_from_tensors` and `/set_trace_level` have no `@auth_level` decorator, so `_get_auth_level_from_app_and_scope` resolves them to `AuthLevel.NORMAL`. `decide_request_auth` only gates `NORMAL` routes when `api_key` is set, so on a server started with `--admin-api-key` and no `--api-key` both routes accept unauthenticated requests. Every other route in their blocks is `ADMIN_OPTIONAL`: `/load_lora_adapter` and `/unload_lora_adapter` for the first, `/start_profile`, `/stop_profile` and `/freeze_gc` for the second.

For `/load_lora_adapter_from_tensors` this is a regression of a fix that already landed, not an original gap. #35818 (merged 2026-08-21) added this exact line alongside the `SafeUnpickler` hardening, but its squash commit `27e5e97` is not an ancestor of today's `main` (`compare/27e5e97...main` reports `diverged`, merge base `f3fe815`, which was `main`'s tip when #35818 landed), so nothing from that PR is in the current history. The `SafeUnpickler` half came back on 2026-09-17 via #39858, which its own description calls a "focused port" of #35818 and which touched only `python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py` and `test/registered/unit/utils/test_safe_unpickler.py`. The `http_server.py` hunk was never re-applied, so the deserialization hardening is live on `main` while the auth gate is missing. I have not found what dropped `27e5e97` from `main`; the PR shows as merged, so the commit appears to have been removed from the branch rather than reverted by a commit.

`/set_trace_level` is a separate instance of the same omission, found while checking whether any other route sits at the default level among admin peers. It flips the process-global trace level through `set_global_trace_level`, so it belongs with the profiling routes it is declared between. After this change the routes that still resolve to `NORMAL` are only inference, health, model-info and session endpoints.

Addresses the remaining auth gap in #30165 (the SafeUnpickler half already landed via #39858 / #40259). The deny-list half of GHSA-h74r-pwx2-6qr2 landed in #39858; the missing auth gate described in that report is the remaining item.

Related in-flight work: #34370 carries the same one-line `@auth_level` decorator for `/load_lora_adapter_from_tensors` inside a much larger SafeUnpickler allowlist change whose CI is currently failing. This PR is only the auth fix plus a CPU regression test so it can land on its own; if #34370 merges first I will close this.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/http_server.py`: add `@auth_level(AuthLevel.ADMIN_OPTIONAL)` to `/load_lora_adapter_from_tensors` and `/set_trace_level`.
- `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_http_server_auth_levels.py`: new CPU unit test that resolves the auth level of the LoRA and profiling routes off the real FastAPI app and asserts each one is rejected without the admin key and allowed with it.

`ADMIN_OPTIONAL` is a no-op when no keys are configured, so deployments that pass no key, or that already pass an admin key, are unaffected.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: request routing and auth middleware only, no change to model outputs.

title: [DSV4.1][HiCache] fix: wait for the layer transfer before reading low-ratio index-K
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

`DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool.get_low_ratio_index_k_dequant` and `get_low_ratio_index_k_fp4` read index-K rows without `wait_layer_transfer(layer_id)`, while every other getter in the pool waits first. Their callers are the V4.1 low-ratio indexer paths (`deepseek_v4_backend.py`: dense fp4 prefill on SM100, and the SM90 torch path), and nothing earlier in those layers waits. With HiCache L2 load-back, the indexer can therefore read index-K before the host-to-device copy of that layer lands and pick top-k from stale rows (silent quality loss, no crash).

This reproduced on V4.1-Flash TP4 with HiCache L2: re-reading the same rows after `wait_layer_transfer` showed up to 98% of the rows changed at a late layer once the per-layer load window was widened.

## Modifications

Wait for the layer's transfer at the top of both getters, like the sibling getters.

## Accuracy Tests

`test_indexer_access_uses_layer_ratio_and_waits_only_for_reads` now also covers the two low-ratio getters and checks the wait precedes each read. It fails without this change and passes with it; `test_dsv4_compressed_pools.py`: 9 passed.

title: [HiSparse] fix: return HiSparse slots on PD decode waiting abort and DeepSeek V4 free
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

Two request exits give a request's KV back without returning its HiSparse slots, and the idle leak check is skipped under HiSparse, so both leaks are silent:

1. **PD decode abort of a waiting request.** Transferred requests are admitted with `admit_request_direct` (device buffer + host slots) before they enter `waiting_queue`. Aborting one from the queue only calls `release_kv_cache`; `alloc_device_buffer` already zeroed the mapping, so nothing frees the buffer or the host pages. Every such abort leaks `padded_buffer_size` device slots plus the request's host pages, and `hisparse_req_budget` shrinks with it.
2. **DeepSeek V4 `free()`.** `DeepSeekV4HiSparseTokenToKVPoolAllocator.free()` frees only the logical pool, while the non-V4 allocator also calls `free_hisparse`. `alloc_extend` maps every compressed token to a C4 slot, so any exit that does not go through the coordinator (a request finished at prefill, an aborted chunked request) leaks its C4 pages, and `full_available_size` (bounded by the C4 pool) shrinks until admission stalls.

## Modifications

- `Scheduler.abort_request`: on a PD decode waiting-queue abort, call `hisparse_coordinator.request_finished(req)` before `release_kv_cache`, as the finish paths do.
- `DeepSeekV4HiSparseTokenToKVPoolAllocator.free`: call `free_hisparse` after the logical free, matching the non-V4 allocator. Paths that already went through the coordinator zeroed the mapping, so this frees nothing twice.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test_free_returns_c4_slots` (real `DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool` with HiSparse + real allocators): on main the C4 pool ends at `192 != 256` (one page leaked); with this change it returns to baseline and the mapping is cleared.
- Before removing the mocked waiting-abort test, `test_hisparse_allocator.py`, `test_priority_scheduling_disaggregation.py`, and `test_hisparse_unit.py`: 45 passed, 2 skipped. The suites have not been rerun after that test removal.

title: [HiSparse] fix: reject speculative decoding and mixed chunk at startup
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

`validate_hisparse` accepts two combinations that crash the scheduler on the first request:

- **Speculative decoding + HiSparse.** The draft worker's `HiSparseDSATokenToKVPool` never gets a HiSparse mapping registered, so the first draft extend dies in `translate_loc_to_hisparse_device`:
  `AttributeError: 'HiSparseDSATokenToKVPool' object has no attribute 'full_to_hisparse_device_index_mapping'`.
- **`--enable-mixed-chunk` + HiSparse.** Mixing a prefill into the HiSparse decode batch fails in `merge_batch`:
  `TypeError: can only concatenate list (not "NoneType") to list`.

Both were reproduced on a 4-layer DeepSeek-V3.2 config with dummy weights (one H200, greedy, `--disable-radix-cache`). The control arms are identical to each other, so each crash is specific to the combination:

| arm | result |
|---|---|
| no spec, no HiSparse | reference |
| HiSparse only | identical to reference |
| EAGLE/MTP only | identical to reference |
| EAGLE/MTP + HiSparse | scheduler crash on the first request |
| mixed chunk only (concurrent requests) | ok |
| mixed chunk + HiSparse | scheduler crash on the first mixed batch |

## Modifications

Reject both at startup with a clear error, until HiSparse supports them (speculative decoding is in progress in #40670 / #37771, which can drop the check).

## Accuracy Tests

- With this change the speculative + HiSparse launch above exits at startup with `ValueError: --enable-hisparse does not support speculative decoding yet.`
- `test_server_args.py`, `test_model_overrides.py`: 385 passed.

title: [Fix] epd: Accept tokens-in requests on scheduler-side transfer backends
author: KrishnanPrash
body:
## Motivation

With encoder disaggregation (EPD), a tokens-in multimodal request (`input_ids` plus `image_data`, no text) fails on the language server with HTTP 500 when the scheduler assembles the multimodal inputs. The `zmq_to_scheduler` and `mooncake` transfer backends and the gRPC zmq receiver all use this scheduler-side path. This affects a default EPD launch, because `--encoder-transfer-backend auto` picks `zmq_to_scheduler` for every model except Kimi-K3 with TP > 1. The scheduler stores `input_ids` as `array("q")`. A tokens-in request has no text (`None` over HTTP, `""` from the gRPC servicer), so the scheduler gives this array to the processor as the prompt. The shared base processor, which Qwen3-VL uses, reads a `list` prompt as token IDs and any other prompt as text, so the HF tokenizer gets the array as text and rejects it. #32541 added this fallback to `input_ids` without the `list()` conversion that the tokenized-input branch already has. `zmq_to_tokenizer` is not affected, because the tokenizer side already passes a list. This PR makes the scheduler side do the same.

## Modifications

- Scheduler-side EPD prompt selection converts `input_ids` to `list[int]` before it gives them to the processor.
- Text-in requests and processors that set `prefer_tokenized_input` keep the same behavior.
- A new unit test checks that a tokens-in prompt reaches the processor as a list, for `input_text=None` (HTTP) and `input_text=""` (gRPC).

## Accuracy Tests

`Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct`, encoder-only and language-only servers on one GPU, `zmq_to_scheduler`, temperature 0:

| Request | main (`5ed306bd69`) | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Tokens-in | HTTP 500 `Failed to assemble multimodal inputs: text input must be of type str ...` | HTTP 200, 1041 prompt tokens, correct image description. Same text and token count as `zmq_to_tokenizer`. |
| Text-in | HTTP 200 | HTTP 200 |

The E2E run covers `zmq_to_scheduler` only. `mooncake` and the gRPC zmq receiver call the same function, but I did not run them end to end.

Unit tests: `test_encode_receiver.py` passes 9/9. Both subtests of the new test fail on main.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The change adds one `list()` copy of `input_ids` each time the scheduler assembles a multimodal request.

title: [Fix] Stop PD-decode queue_time from counting decode time before a retraction
author: sohom-cs
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #39312 (cc @surajm20061998 @sufeng-buaa).

Since #39312, `queue_time` adds `forward entry - wait_queue_entry_time` at the first forward after each retraction. That relies on the retraction re-stamping `wait_queue_entry_time`, which happens in NULL mode through `set_wait_queue_entry_time()`. On a **PD decode** worker, though, a retracted request goes `_add_request_to_queue(is_retracted=True)` → `retracted_queue` → `resume_retracted_reqs()` → `waiting_queue`, and the scheduler only calls `set_retract_time()`. Nothing on that path re-stamps the wait. At re-admission the accumulator therefore subtracts the **first** wait stamp and counts all the decoding before the retraction as queueing.

Example: a request waits 0.1 s, decodes for 10 s, is retracted, and is re-admitted 2 s later. `meta_info["queue_time"]` reports 12.1 s instead of 2.1 s, and so does the per-request time-stats log line. The Prometheus queue-time histogram only samples the first wait, so it is not affected.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`, in the DECODE branch of `_add_request_to_queue`: for a retracted request, call `set_wait_queue_entry_time()` instead of `set_retract_time()`. For a request that has queued before, that method performs `set_retract_time(ts)` (including the trace event) and then re-stamps the wait. Queue time after a retraction then runs from retraction to re-admission, the same as NULL mode.

Rebootstrap (`hold_rebootstrap`) is unchanged: it stamps the wait after the re-transfer (`decode.py`), as `test_decode_rebootstrap_counts_both_waits` pins.

The alternative is to stamp in `resume_retracted_reqs()` instead, so that only the `waiting_queue` time counts and the time held in `retracted_queue` does not. Happy to switch if you prefer that definition.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: metrics only.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the pre-commit hooks.
- [x] Add unit tests: `test_decode_retraction_queue_time_excludes_decoding_before_it` in `test/registered/unit/managers/test_priority_scheduling_disaggregation.py`. It drives `Scheduler._add_request_to_queue(req, is_retracted=True)` in DECODE mode with a real `SchedulerReqTimeStats`. On `main` it fails with `12.1 != 2.1`; it passes with the fix. `test/registered/unit/observability/test_req_time_stats.py` passes unchanged.
- [ ] Update documentation (not needed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude); every changed line was reviewed and the tests were run locally by me.

title: [HiCache][PD] fix: keep decode load-back polling out of rank-local collectives
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

PD decode with `--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache --enable-hierarchical-cache` and TP > 1 crashes on the first L2 load-backs. `_process_hicache_local_restores` enters TP collectives based on each rank's own CUDA event:

- Phase A: `is_load_back_event_done` ran `loading_check()` (a TP `all_reduce`) only on ranks whose event had fired.
- Phase B: new load-backs were gated on the `producer_index + 1` event, so the same `all_reduce`, plus `init_load_back` / `start_loading`, ran on a subset of ranks.

On Qwen3-8B, prefill TP1 + decode TP2, the decode scheduler dies with:

```
gloo::EnforceNotMet ... op.preamble.length <= op.nbytes. 8 vs 1. Received data size doesn't match expected size. Is there a distributed collective mismatch in your code?
```

With `SGLANG_ENABLE_RANK_CONSENSUS_CHECKER=1` and probes on this path's collective entries (see Reproduction), the first divergence is:

```
[TP0] Found rank divergence ... events = ['loading_check(all_reduce) from _process_hicache_local_restores:285']
[TP1] Found rank divergence ... events = ['loading_check(all_reduce) from _process_hicache_local_restores:295']
```

TP0 entered from Phase A and TP1 from Phase B. The two same-shape `all_reduce`s pair silently; the gloo crash is the next, differently sized collective. #29483 covered only Phase A, on the removed `hiradix_cache.py`.

## Modifications

- `is_load_back_event_done` only polls the local event. Load acks are already reaped in lockstep by `check_hicache_events`, and a rank-local READY is harmless because the gated KV poll is MIN-reduced.
- Phase B gates on `has_free_load_back_slot()`: `len(ack_load_queue) < num_counters`. The queue grows in `start_loading` and shrinks by a MIN-reduced count, so all ranks agree, with no new collective. A reaped ack was synchronized, so the reused slot's events are done. A slot is reused at most one step later.

## Reproduction

<details>
<summary>repro.py, sitecustomize.py, commands</summary>

```python
# repro.py
import concurrent.futures as cf
import os
import random

import requests

from sglang.test.server_fixtures.disaggregation_fixture import PDDisaggregationServerBase


class Run(PDDisaggregationServerBase):
    prefill_tp_size = 1
    decode_tp_size = 2
    decode_base_gpu_id = 1
    extra_prefill_args = ["--mem-fraction-static", "0.8"]
    extra_decode_args = [
        "--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache",
        "--enable-hierarchical-cache",
        "--hicache-ratio", "4",
        "--hicache-write-policy", "write_through",
        "--max-total-tokens", "24000",
        "--enable-metrics",
    ]
    extra_decode_env = {
        k: v for k, v in os.environ.items()
        if k.startswith(("REPRO_", "SGLANG_ENABLE_RANK"))
    }


def gen(ids):
    r = requests.post(
        f"{Run.base_url}/generate",
        json={"input_ids": ids, "sampling_params": {"max_new_tokens": 16, "temperature": 0, "ignore_eos": True}},
        timeout=180,
    )
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.json()["meta_info"]["cached_tokens"]


Run.setUpClass()
Run.model = "Qwen/Qwen3-8B"
Run.launch_all()
try:
    rng = random.Random(0)
    prefixes = [[rng.randint(1000, 30000) for _ in range(3000)] for _ in range(24)]
    with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(32) as ex:
        for rnd in range(8):
            jobs = [ex.submit(gen, p + [rng.randint(1000, 30000) for _ in range(32)]) for p in prefixes]
            print(f"round={rnd} cached={sum(j.result() for j in jobs)}", flush=True)
finally:
    Run.tearDownClass()
```

```python
# sitecustomize.py
# REPRO_H2D_SLEEP_MS: delay rank 1's H2D stream so the ranks see the same load-back event at different times.
# REPRO_PROBES=1: record every collective entry on this path with the rank consensus checker; the sleep lets
#   the checker's worker compare events before the mismatched collective aborts the process.
import os
import sys
import time

MS = float(os.environ.get("REPRO_H2D_SLEEP_MS", "0"))
PROBES = os.environ.get("REPRO_PROBES") == "1"
if MS > 0 or PROBES:
    import torch
    from sglang.srt.disaggregation import decode
    from sglang.srt.managers import cache_controller as cc
    from sglang.srt.mem_cache import unified_radix_cache as urc
    from sglang.srt.utils import rank_consensus_checker as rdc

    orig_start_loading = cc.HiCacheController.start_loading

    def start_loading(self):
        if MS > 0 and self.load_queue and torch.distributed.get_rank() == 1:
            with torch.cuda.stream(self.l2_transfer_engine.host_to_device_stream):
                torch.cuda._sleep(int(MS * 1.98e6))
        if PROBES:
            rdc.assert_same("start_loading qlen=%d", len(self.load_queue))
        return orig_start_loading(self)

    cc.HiCacheController.start_loading = start_loading

    if PROBES:
        orig_loading_check = urc.UnifiedRadixCache.loading_check

        def loading_check(self, finish_count=None):
            if finish_count is None:
                f = sys._getframe(2)
                rdc.assert_same("loading_check(all_reduce) from %s:%d", f.f_code.co_name, f.f_lineno)
                time.sleep(2)
            return orig_loading_check(self, finish_count)

        urc.UnifiedRadixCache.loading_check = loading_check

        orig_poll = decode.poll_and_all_reduce

        def poll_and_all_reduce(pollers, *args, **kwargs):
            rdc.assert_same("poll_and_all_reduce n=%d", len(pollers))
            return orig_poll(pollers, *args, **kwargs)

        decode.poll_and_all_reduce = poll_and_all_reduce
```

```bash
python repro.py   # main on H200: gloo crash in round 1-2
# force divergent events, and let the checker name the divergence:
SGLANG_ENABLE_RANK_CONSENSUS_CHECKER=1 REPRO_H2D_SLEEP_MS=30 REPRO_PROBES=1 \
  PYTHONPATH=<dir of sitecustomize.py>:$PYTHONPATH python repro.py
```

Without `REPRO_PROBES` the checker does not catch it: `loading_check` and `poll_and_all_reduce` carry no `@rank_consensus`, so the gloo abort comes first.

</details>

## Accuracy Tests

4xH200, 8 rounds per run, rounds 1-7 served entirely from L2 (`sglang:load_back_tokens_total` = 72,000 per rank per round):

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| natural, checker on | gloo crash | healthy |
| 30 ms H2D sleep on rank 1, checker on | gloo crash | healthy |
| + probes | `Found rank divergence` above | healthy, checker silent |

A temporary 2-rank Gloo test with rank-divergent events failed on main and when either Phase A or Phase B was reverted alone, and passed with this PR (not kept in the diff).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- No test files are changed in the final diff; validation is recorded above.

title: [Fix] Keep one copy of CP-replicated rows in the DP gather
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #41443
* #41442
* #41441
* #41440
* #41439
* #41438
* #41437
* #41436
* #41435
* #41434
* #41433
* #41432
* #41431
* #41430
* #41429
* #41428
* #41427
* #41426
* #41425
* #41424
* #41423
* __->__ #41422
* #41421
* #41420
* #41419
* #41418
* #41417

## Motivation

Under attention DP with attention CP, the CP ranks of a DP group hold the same rows wherever a DP gather runs on them: decode, short prefills, and the logits of every forward (a CP extend gathers its hidden states across CP before the logits). The DP gather did not account for the CP ranks.
- **All-reduce path:** every CP rank wrote its copy at the DP group's offset, so the sum came out multiplied by the CP size.
  - The logits gather always takes this path. With attention TP 1 (MLA prefill CP, DSA zigzag prefill CP), every CP rank writes.
  - So the logits came out scaled by the CP size. Greedy tokens are unchanged, but sampling and the returned logprobs are not.
- **All-gather path (MAX_LEN padding):** it gathered one block from every rank of the TP group into a buffer sized for the DP groups alone, and failed the size check.

## Modifications

- **`_dp_gather`:** under attention CP it always takes the all-reduce path. The all-gathers take one block from every rank of the TP group, which also spans the CP ranks.
- **`_dp_gather_via_all_reduce`:** only CP rank 0 writes its rows. Which attention-TP ranks write is unchanged.
- **Contract, in the `_dp_gather` docstring:** under attention CP the CP ranks of a DP group must hold the same rows. A caller whose CP ranks hold different rows has to restore the full rows on every CP rank first.
- **Without attention CP nothing changes:** every rank is CP rank 0, and the gather keeps its path.
- **New `test_dp_attention_cp_replicas.py`:** 8 ranks (DP × CP × TP) call `dp_gather_partial`, `dp_gather_replicate` and `dp_scatter` directly. It covers SUM_LEN and MAX_LEN padding and an idle DP group, and checks that each DP slot holds its group's rows once.
- **Notes:**
  - The gatherv path needs `tp_size == attn_dp_size`, so it never runs under CP.
  - A caller that gathers rows which differ across CP ranks (CP-sharded rows during a CP extend) is still not supported by this gather. On main the overlapping shards were summed, or the MAX_LEN size check failed; now only CP rank 0's rows are kept. The next PR in this stack adds optional shard placement (`cp_shard_counts`), which the dense FFN input under attention DP × CP uses.

## Accuracy Tests

- **New test:** 6 of 6 cases fail on main and pass with the fix.
- **No regressions:** all 235 unit files under `layers`, `models`, `model_executor` and `distributed`, plus the other DP-attention and CP unit tests, were run one process per file on main and on the fix. No file fails only with the fix. Seven fail on both (quantization, DeepEP, FlashInfer, graph pool tests), unrelated to this change.
- **Mutants:** both are caught:
  - every CP rank writing its copy;
  - MAX_LEN keeping the all-gather under CP.
- **In this stack:** the call-sequence comparisons are identical to the parent, and 172 related unit files pass.
- **GPU (H200 × 8):**
  - Setup: 4-layer DeepSeek-V3 (bf16), MLA prefill CP under attention DP 2. The config hook sets attention TP 1, DeepEP, ep = tp and a dense MLP on every rank; the MoE runner is DeepGEMM.
  - Requests are sent one at a time, so the other DP group is idle. The outputs are compared with a TP1 reference.
  - Measured with this commit applied directly on main. Maxima over 4 requests:

  | Run | Greedy tokens vs TP1 | Prefill top-5 max \|Δlogprob\| | Decode max \|Δlogprob\| |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | main, attention CP 2 (tp 4, dp 2) | identical | 3.459 | 2.96 |
  | **fix**, attention CP 2 (tp 4, dp 2) | identical | 0.031 | 0.059 |
  | main, attention CP 4 (tp 8, dp 2) | request 0 flips at token 6 | 4.96 | 3.823 |
  | **fix**, attention CP 4 (tp 8, dp 2) | request 0 flips at token 6 | 0.001 | 0.06 |
  | DeepEP without CP (tp 4, dp 2), main and fix | request 3 flips at token 5 | 0.062 | 0.061 |

  - On main the logprob distance grows with the CP size. With the fix it drops to the no-CP control's noise level.
  - The flip at token 6 under attention CP 4 is at the same position on main and with the fix. It is numerical noise under ep 8: scaling the logits does not change the argmax.
  - Without CP, main and the fix are bit-identical.

The whole stack was also compared with main at its tip; the results are in #41443.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Nothing changes without attention CP. Under attention DP × CP the DP gather now always takes the all-reduce path; the all-gather path failed there.

Decode latency, time to first token and memory for the whole stack against main are in #41443.
