title: [Fix] Gather a dense FFN's input across attention DP and CP in one DP sum
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #41443
* #41442
* #41441
* #41440
* #41439
* #41438
* #41437
* #41436
* #41435
* #41434
* #41433
* #41432
* #41431
* #41430
* #41429
* #41428
* #41427
* #41426
* #41425
* #41424
* __->__ #41423
* #41422
* #41421
* #41420
* #41419
* #41418
* #41417

## Motivation

With attention DP, CP and TP all above one, a dense FFN runs over the whole TP group. Each rank holds its DP group's tokens, split across CP on a CP extend. The scatter-mode path ran the ordinary DP gather and then a MoE-CP all-gather on its output, and it failed on main (`output tensor size must be equal to world_size times input tensor size`):
- the DP gather placed each rank's rows at its DP group's offset, so on a CP extend the CP shards landed on the same rows;
- the MoE-CP all-gather saw the whole DP buffer and failed its size check;
- an idle DP group returned early on its empty tensor and skipped the DP all-reduce the other groups were waiting in;
- the CP shards are padded to one physical length with the real rows in front, so placing the physical rows would run past the DP slot.

## Modifications

- **Shard placement in the DP gather.** `dp_gather_partial`, `dp_gather_replicate` and `dp_scatter` take an optional `cp_shard_counts`: the rows of each CP rank's shard that hold tokens.
  - With it, a rank places its real rows in its DP slot, after those of the CP ranks before it (`_cp_shard_rows`), and takes the same rows back.
  - The padding rows are left out and come back as zeros.
  - The one all-reduce over the TP group then gathers both axes.
  - Without it nothing changes: the CP ranks hold the same rows and CP rank 0 writes them.
- **A dense layer under attention DP and CP takes the declarations.**
  - Its ordinary batches run the plain DP steps.
  - A CP extend runs the same DP steps with each rank placing its CP shard (`places_cp_shards`, counts from `per_rank_logical_token`).
  - It takes its shard back from where the gather put it, at the shard's padded length (`CommunicateSummableTensorPairFn._take_back_cp_shard`).
- **The FFN completes its own sum under attention CP, on every batch.** The next layer's input holds only this rank's chunk, and a reduce-scatter back over attention DP would split across the CP ranks. Nothing changes for CP without attention DP, whose FFN exit never deferred or reduce-scattered.
- **Idle DP groups:** the declared DP steps have no early return, so an idle DP group joins the DP sum.
- **Still on the scatter-mode path:** a MoE layer under attention DP and CP. It behaves as on main.
- **Tests:**
  - new `test_dp_attention_cp_gather.py`: 8 ranks run `prepare_mlp` and `postprocess_layer` through the real communicator construction. It covers a CP extend in every DP group, one beside an idle DP group and one beside a short prefill, decode with both paddings (rows the same on every CP rank), and the norm before the gather with and without attention TP. After the round trip every rank's rows match the reference.
  - `test_declared_decoder_boundary.py` checks that under attention DP one DP sum gathers both axes, and that a MoE layer under attention DP and CP keeps the scatter-mode steps.
- **Notes:**
  - This is a behavior fix: DP × CP dense layers failed on main.
  - `_cp_shard_rows` and `_take_back_cp_shard` slice with host-side counts, so they are not CUDA-graph capturable. Prefill under DP × CP runs eagerly today: the breakable prefill CUDA graph under CP requires `attn_cp_size == tp_size`, which DP × CP never has.

## Accuracy Tests

Main fails on this configuration, so correctness is checked against a TP1 reference; the configurations main runs are checked bit for bit against the parent.
- **Call sequences through the real constructor**, with the CP axis extended to attention DP 2: 187,392 cases. 1,152 differ, all of them DP × CP (out of 3,072 DP × CP cases): the parent takes main's path, and the change runs one DP sum. The other comparisons are identical to the parent.
- **Unit tests:** 86 related unit files pass, including the new 8-rank test. A wider run of 174 related unit files at this commit has one failure, `test_zaya_cca.py`, which fails on the parent too.
- **Mutants:** all are caught:
  - a CP extend not placing its shards;
  - the output taken from the DP slot instead of the shard;
  - the FFN leaving its sum under CP;
  - a forced norm before the gather applied to the attention-TP partial.
- **GPU (H200 × 8):** Qwen3-0.6B bf16, fa3, zigzag, prefill CUDA graph off, decode CUDA graph on. Compared with a TP1 reference (maxima over the requests):

  | Run | Greedy tokens vs TP1 | Prefill top-5 max \|Δlogprob\| | Decode max \|Δlogprob\| |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | **DP2 × CP2 × TP2, long prompts** | identical | 0.05 | 0.081 |
  | DP2 × TP8 (no CP), long prompts | identical | 0.118 | 0.075 |
  | CP2 × TP2, long prompts | identical | 0.104 | 0.067 |
  | **DP2 × CP2 × TP2, short prompts** | identical | 0.099 | 0.081 |
  | DP2 × TP8, short prompts | identical | 0.159 | 0.075 |

  - DP × CP is within the range of the other shapes. The long-prompt run covers a CP-active prefill, an idle DP group (one request reaches only one DP group) and the decode CUDA graph.
  - A runtime audit counted 28 / 28 layers on the declared path on all 8 ranks.
- **Shapes without DP × CP, parent vs change:**
  - CP2 × TP2: bit-identical.
  - DP2 × TP8: bit-identical. In the first run the change's two batched long prompts differed; its rerun, and two runs of the parent, are all bit-identical. This is run-to-run batching variation: with CP 1 the new placement is off and the path is the parent's.
- The GPU runs cover this PR together with the DP-gather fix below it, on the same production code, measured before the stack was rebased onto main after #41257.

The whole stack was also compared with main at its tip; the results are in #41443.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Nothing changes without attention DP × CP. Main does not run DP × CP, so there is no parent to compare. The table is a baseline of the new path.

Setup: H200 × 8, Qwen3-0.6B bf16, fa3, zigzag; prefill CUDA graph, custom all-reduce and radix cache off; random-token requests with 1 new token; median of 5 runs after one warm-up.

| Shape (GPUs) | 4k × 1 | 4k × 2 (one per DP group) | 16k × 1 | 16k × 2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP2 × CP2 × TP2 (8, FFN TP8) | 43.9 ms | 45.3 ms | 158.3 ms | 161.2 ms |
| DP2 × TP4 (8, no CP) | 35.2 ms | 34.6 ms | 126.8 ms | 135.1 ms |
| CP2 × TP2 (4) | 36.6 ms | — | 69.7 ms | — |
| TP2 (2) | 24.1 ms | — | 55.3 ms | — |

- The model is small and the time is mostly communication, so only the relative cost between shapes means anything.
- At 16k, DP × CP costs about 31 ms more than DP2 × TP4 on the same 8 GPUs. This is the cost of one DP sum: each layer runs a TP8 all-reduce over the whole DP buffer. An all-gatherv would first need the (DP, CP) ranks' row counts exchanged.
- With one request per DP group, latency matches a single request, so throughput doubles.

Decode latency, time to first token and memory for the whole stack against main are in #41443.

title: [Fix] Run MoE layers under attention DP and GQA prefill CP on the declared DP × CP gather
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #41443
* #41442
* #41441
* #41440
* #41439
* #41438
* #41437
* #41436
* #41435
* #41434
* #41433
* __->__ #41432
* #41431
* #41430
* #41429
* #41428
* #41427
* #41426
* #41425
* #41424
* #41423
* #41422
* #41421
* #41420
* #41419
* #41418
* #41417

## Motivation

Under attention DP with GQA prefill CP, `_declared_sides` still sent MoE layers to the scatter-mode steps. On a CP extend, those steps gather the FFN input over DP and then over the MoE-CP group. The second gather fails the all-gather's size check (`output tensor size must be equal to world_size times input tensor size`), so these models crash on the first prefill that shards over CP.

Dense layers in the same configuration already take the declared boundary. It gathers over DP and CP in one DP sum, with each CP rank placing its own shard.

## Modifications

- `_declared_sides` narrows the exclusion to a MoE dispatched per DP shard (a2a, the fp4 all-gather, DWDP). Such a MoE would dispatch each rank's CP shard of the tokens, which the steps do not cover, so those layers keep the scatter-mode steps.
- A MoE on the TP group now has the same declarations as a TP-sharded dense MLP, except for its sum group (`SumGroup.MOE_OUTPUT`):
  - **ordinary batch:** DP gather (partial or replicate order) and DP scatter back, as without CP;
  - **CP extend:** one DP sum gathers `{DP, CP}`, each CP rank placing its shard, and the output is taken back per shard;
  - **under CP:** the MoE completes its own sum, because `should_use_dp_reduce_scatterv` is never true with CP > 1.
- **Tests:**
  - In the scope table of `test_declared_decoder_boundary.py`, a MoE on the TP group under attention DP and GQA CP now takes the declared entry, and a MoE dispatched per DP shard still does not.
  - `test_dp_attention_cp_gather.py` adds an 8-rank gather and take-back round trip for a MoE layer.
- **Scope:** only MoE layers that are not dispatched per DP shard change, and only under attention DP > 1 with GQA prefill CP.

## Accuracy Tests

- **Call-sequence comparison through the real constructor, 256,128 cases.** 3,072 cases change, all of them MoE layers not dispatched per DP shard under attention DP 2 and GQA CP:
  - 2,816 match the calls of a TP-sharded dense layer of the same shape.
  - 256 follow a layer that runs a dense MLP on every rank, at attention TP 2. They add an attention-TP gather, because the previous layer hands on local rows, and match the same shape with CP off.

  The other eight comparisons are identical.
- **Unit tests:** the related unit files pass, and the 125-file CPU unit suite has no new failures. Two mutants are caught.
- **GPU (H200 × 8):** Qwen3-30B-A3B bf16, fa3, zigzag CP, prefill CUDA graph off, decode CUDA graph on. TP8 × DP2 × CP2 means `--tp 8 --dp 2 --attn-cp-size 2` (attention TP 2).
  - The parent crashes at TP8 × DP2 × CP2 with the size-check error above.
  - This PR runs TP8 × DP2 × CP2, with and without `--ep-size 8`. The table compares long prompts against a TP1 greedy reference, per request:

    | Shape | First differing token | Max \|Δlogprob\| over the prefill top-5 |
    |---|---|---|
    | TP8 × DP2 × CP2 (this PR) | 0, 0, 9, 0 | 0.416, 0.553, 0.080, 0.134 |
    | TP8 × DP2 × CP2, EP8 (this PR) | 0, 0, 16, 0 | 0.432, 0.194, 0.121, 0.143 |
    | TP8 × DP2 (supported shape) | 0, 16, 16, 0 | 0.467, 0.521, 0.074, 0.273 |
    | TP4 × CP2 (supported shape) | 8, 16, 16, 0 | 0.410, 0.432, 0.197, 0.165 |

    This bf16 MoE can differ from TP1 at the first token on the supported shapes too. The DP × CP distances fall within their range, except one value of 0.553 against 0.521. Short prompts behave the same.
  - A runtime audit counted the layers on the declared entry: 48 / 48 on every rank.
  - Shapes without DP × CP, against the parent:
    - TP4 × CP2 is bit-identical.
    - On TP8 × DP2, one run of this PR differed on two requests. In reruns, both parent runs and the second run of this PR were bit-identical. This PR cannot reach that shape, since the change needs attention CP > 1.
- **Not covered on GPU:**
  - a single request that leaves one DP group idle during a CP extend;
  - DeepEP under this shape (a2a MoE layers keep the scatter-mode steps here).

The whole stack was also compared with main at its tip; the results are in #41443.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No kernel changes. At TP8 × DP2 × CP2, MoE layers on a CP extend now run one DP-sum gather and a per-shard take-back, where the parent crashed. No other configuration changes.

Decode latency, time to first token and memory for the whole stack against main are in #41443.

title: [Fix] Falcon-H1: count the Mamba mixer's output once under tensor parallelism
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #41443
* #41442

* #41440
* #41439
* #41438

* #41436

* #41427

* #41425
* #41424
* #41423
* #41422
* #41421
* #41420
* #41419
* #41418
* #41417

## Motivation

Falcon-H1 runs an attention mixer and a Mamba mixer on the same input and adds their outputs before the FFN. `prepare_mlp` then completes that sum with one all-reduce over attention TP.
- The attention's `o_proj` leaves its partial sum for that step (`reduce_results=False`).
- `MambaMixer2` reduces its own output whenever attention DP is off, which is its default. The Mamba output was therefore summed again, and counted tp times.

At TP2, "The capital of France is" continues with "the city of paris. however, paris is not the capital of france"; at TP4 the text is garbage. TP1 and attention DP were right: under attention DP the Mamba default already leaves the sum.

## Modifications

- Build the Mamba mixer with `reduce_results=False`, like `o_proj`.
- New `test_falcon_h1_mixer_sums.py` builds the decoder layer and checks that neither mixer reduces its own output, at TP1 and TP2. Both subtests fail without the fix.
- Nothing else changes. Under attention DP the default was already `False`, and at TP1 the flag has no effect.

## Accuracy Tests

H200, Falcon-H1-1.5B-Instruct, 4 greedy requests × 32 tokens, compared against TP1:
- **Before the fix:**
  - At TP2, three requests differ from their first token, including the answer above, and the fourth from token 25.
  - At TP4, all four differ from their first token.
- **With the fix:**
  - TP2 with the fused AR + norm kernel and TP4 match TP1 on all 32 tokens of all four requests.
  - TP2 without the fused kernel matches on three requests; the other first differs at token 1.
  - The first request now answers " Paris.".
- **Unit tests:** the 126-file CPU unit suite has no new failures.
- **Not covered:**
  - CUDA graph: Falcon-H1 fails under CUDA graph at TP1 and TP2 on every tree (illegal memory access, device-side assert, CUBLAS failure), so these runs are eager.
  - Attention DP: TP2 × DP2 fails on every tree (`The size of tensor a (6704) must match the size of tensor b (3352)`). Falcon-H1 with attention DP does not run on main.

The whole stack was also compared with main at its tip; the results are in #41443.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Removes one all-reduce per Falcon-H1 decoder layer under TP > 1 without attention DP: the Mamba mixer's own.

Decode latency, time to first token and memory for the whole stack against main are in #41443.

title: [Fix] LongCat-Flash under attention DP: branch and merge the dense FFNs through the communicators
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #41443
* #41442
* #41441
* #41440
* #41439
* #41438
* #41437
* __->__ #41436
* #41435
* #41434
* #41433
* #41432
* #41431
* #41430
* #41429
* #41428
* #41427
* #41426
* #41425
* #41424
* #41423
* #41422
* #41421
* #41420
* #41419
* #41418
* #41417

## Motivation

Each LongCat-Flash layer runs a MoE shortcut beside a dense branch (mlp0 → attention 1 → mlp1). Both branches start from the same FFN input and are added at the end. The model did the row bookkeeping itself:
- mlp0 took the input the MoE's boundary read. When an a2a MoE had that input on each rank's slice, `_scmoe_align_rows` gathered it over attention TP, and it aligned the two branches' rows again before the merge.
- Both dense MLPs completed their sums with hand-written `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce` calls.
- The MoE output went through `postprocess_layer` with a zero residual.

Under attention DP this is wrong:
- mlp0's output stays on the DP-gathered rows while the residual is on this rank's rows, so the second attention's norm fails (`Norm token mismatch`).
- With an a2a MoE, mlp0 does not see every token, so its TP sum adds partial outputs of different tokens.
- Under reduce_scatterv, the sparse postprocess would reduce-scatter the MoE's already-summed output.

## Modifications

- **New `move_rows(value, rows, to, forward_batch)`** moves a complete value between two row layouts with the existing moves. It gathers over the axes `to` does not shard (attention TP, then attention DP) and cuts to this rank's share of the axes it does shard (attention DP, then attention TP). CP is not supported.
- **Three new `LayerCommunicator` methods** work on the rows each communicator declares for its ordinary batches (`_branch_rows`). `_branch_rows` raises `NotImplementedError` on a CP, LayerNorm SP or input-scattered batch; LongCat runs none of these.
  - `branch_input(source, hidden_states, residual, forward_batch)`: takes the FFN input and residual that `source`'s boundary read, and moves them to this layer's FFN rows and residual rows.
  - `branch_output(hidden_states, forward_batch)`: moves a complete FFN output to the rows the layer hands on. The output is a contribution that does not write the residual.
  - `merge_branch(contribution, hidden_states, residual, source, forward_batch)`: moves what `source`'s layer hands on to this layer's output rows and adds the contribution to it.
- **LongCat-Flash:**
  - mlp0's input comes from `mlp_layer_communicator[0].branch_input(moe_layer_communicator, ...)`.
  - Both dense MLPs run inside their communicators' `ffn_exit`, built with `allow_deferred_ffn_reduction=False`, and reduce in `down_proj` (`reduce_results=True`).
  - The MoE output goes through `branch_output`, and the merge through `merge_branch`.
  - `_scmoe_align_rows`, the two hand-written all-reduces and the zero-residual `postprocess_layer` are removed.
- **FFN-exit guard:** it counts `mlps` as an FFN attribute and looks into `nn.ModuleList([...])`, so it covers `LongcatFlashMLP`.
- **Tests:**
  - The stand-ins in `test_longcat_flash_shortcut.py` are communicators with declared rows; the assertions are unchanged.
  - `test_declared_decoder_boundary.py` adds `TestBranchRows`: each branch's rows, what the fork and the merge move, and the order in which `move_rows` gathers and cuts.
- **What changes and what doesn't:**
  - Without attention DP, the layer computes the same bits. The fork's gather is the same all-gather as `_scmoe_align_rows`, the `down_proj` all-reduce is the same `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce`, and nothing is deferred.
  - Under attention DP, the layer now matches the same layers without DP over the same TP width.
  - The MoE block's own all-reduce, the zero-expert math and the NextN layer are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

- **GPU (H200), probe.** No LongCat-Flash checkpoint was available, so the GPU evidence is a two-layer probe:
  - **Real parts:** the decoder layer, dense MLPs, RMSNorm and TP / DP collectives.
  - **Stand-ins:** the attention, whose whole partial sum is on attention-TP rank 0 so the sum is exact at any width, and a MoE with its combine already done.
  - **Cases:** with and without a2a, sum-len and max-len padding, ragged and empty ranks.

  Results:
  - **Without attention DP** (TP1 / TP2 / TP4, 8 cases each): within tolerance of a full-tensor reference (max 0.047). Bit-identical to the parent's model file, with the same collective sequence on every group of more than one rank.
  - **TP2 × DP2 (attention TP 1):** the DP ranks' outputs, put together, are bit-identical to TP2 on the same input (8 / 8). The parent is off by 0.1875 with a2a, and fails without it (`Norm token mismatch: [8, 32] vs [4, 32]`).
  - **TP4 × DP2** differs from TP4 by 0.047, within tolerance of the reference. Under DP the residual is added in bf16 into the attention sum before the gather and the norm; without DP, the fused add + norm runs in fp32. This is main's DP path, not LongCat's.
  - **Dense MLP weights 8× stronger:** the parent's a2a is off the reference by 57.25 (TP2 × DP2) and 31.6 (TP4 × DP2); this PR by 1.0 and 1.75.
  - **CUDA graph:** capture (2 per shape) and replay (6 per shape) are bit-identical to eager.
  - **GPU mutants:** three are caught (no move at the fork, no move at mlp0's exit, the dense MLP not reduced).
- **CPU:**
  - The ten call-sequence comparisons are identical to the parent, including the declared-boundary comparison (269,952 cases).
  - The related unit tests pass. The 126-file CPU unit suite has no new failures.
  - Seven mutants are caught.
- **Not covered:** a real checkpoint end to end, and a real DeepEP dispatch.

The whole stack was also compared with main at its tip; the results are in #41443.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Without attention DP, the same collectives run; the explicit all-reduce moves into `down_proj`. Under attention DP, the dense branch now gathers over DP before mlp0 when the MoE is a2a, and mlp0's output is scattered back to this rank's rows.

Decode latency, time to first token and memory for the whole stack against main are in #41443.

title: [MUSA] Fix fused MoE GEMV registration and torchada pin
author: googs1025
body:
## Summary

- register the MUSA fused MoE GEMV implementation under the schema name used by the Python wrapper
- update the MUSA CI torchada artifact from 0.1.82 to 0.1.90
- align all three MUSA torchada dependency lower bounds at `>=0.1.90`
- refresh the pinned SHA256 for the official `torchada-0.1.90-py3-none-any.whl` artifact

## Root cause

`musa_fused_moe_gemv` was defined and invoked with the MUSA-prefixed operator name, but its dispatcher implementation was registered as `fused_moe_gemv`. The reviewed target version is now 0.1.90 across the CI artifact and dependency declarations.

- verified the 0.1.90 wheel SHA256 against PyPI metadata and the downloaded wheel content
- parsed all three TOML files and verified their torchada lower bounds are `>=0.1.90`

MUSA validation completed on an x86_64 MTT S5000 host using the `linux/amd64` container:

- MUSA runtime is available: `torch.musa.is_available()=True`, `device_count=1`
- PyTorch: `2.11.0.post1+musa5.2.0`

- Triton: `3.2.0`, with the `mtgpu` backend available

title: [HiCache][PD] fix: clamp the decode restore to the prefix promised to prefill
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

PD decode with `--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache --enable-hierarchical-cache` commits `decode_prefix_len` (L1 + L2 + L3) to prefill at admission, but `_try_hicache_queue_load_back` re-matches the full `origin_input_ids` later. If the tree grew in between (typically a request with the same prompt finished and inserted its prefix while this one waited for its L3 -> L2 prefetch), the re-match covers more than `decode_prefix_len`. The restored indices are then longer than the `[l1_prefix_len, decode_prefix_len)` slice `_commit_hicache_local_restore_to_req` writes, and the scheduler dies:

```
RuntimeError: The expanded size of the tensor (2944) must match the existing size (3008) at non-singleton dimension 0.
```

Reproduced with Qwen3-8B, prefill TP1 + decode TP1, decode HiCache with the file storage backend and `--page-size 64`: warm 24 prompts, flush decode L1/L2, then send each prompt twice 20 ms apart. The first round crashes (re-match 3008 tokens vs 2944 promised).

## Modifications

Keep only the `restore_token_count` tokens prefill was promised. The extra tokens belong to tree nodes, not to the request, so nothing needs to be rolled back; the request still locks `restored_node`, and its own copies past `decode_prefix_len` are deduplicated on insert as usual (`cache_protected_len == decode_prefix_len`).

## Accuracy Tests

Same setup, 6 rounds: healthy, with 13 over-long re-matches observed and handled (both device-side and host-side overshoot). Without this change the first round crashes. `test/registered/unit/{mem_cache,disaggregation,managers}`: same results as main.

title: [PD][Mamba] fix: free the COW mamba slot of decode requests dropped before preallocation
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

With `--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache` on a Mamba hybrid model, `_match_prefix_and_lock` runs with `cow_mamba=True`, which gives the request its own Mamba slot at admission time. If the request then does not fit and stays in the prealloc queue, it keeps that slot, and if it is later aborted (client disconnect, handshake failure) or rejected by the SWA reclaim check, it leaves through `failed_reqs` without ever getting a KV row. Nothing frees the slot, so every such request leaks one Mamba slot.

Reproduced with Qwen3.5-2B, prefill TP1 + decode TP1, decode radix with `--mamba-radix-cache-strategy no_buffer` and a small `--max-total-tokens`: warm one prompt, then send bursts of requests extending it with a large `max_new_tokens` and a 3 s client timeout. The idle check then reports `[mamba] total=3248, available=3174, evictable=67 ... leaked_mamba_pages={...}` (7 slots) and, under the strict idle check, the scheduler exits.

## Modifications

Before returning, `pop_preallocated` releases every failed request that holds a Mamba slot but no KV row through `release_kv_cache`, whose "freeing before alloc" branch already handles exactly this case.

## Accuracy Tests

Same workload, 6 rounds with 91 COW allocations: no leak reported. Without this change the leak check fires. `test_decode_queue_cleanup.py`: the fake requests now carry a real `ReqKvInfo`; `test/registered/unit/{mem_cache,disaggregation,managers}`: same results as main.

title: [NPU] [Diffusion] Fix NPU multimodal-gen CI
author: OrangeRedeng
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

This PR addresses three issues in NPU diffusion CI:

- MiniMax-H3 and Qwen-Image need updated reference outputs after the CANN and torch_npu upgrade in #40524.
- GLM-Image fails when transferring a request between workers because its `task_type` enum cannot be encoded as JSON.
- MiniMax-H3 misses a text encoder preparation step after #40470 changed when encoder weights are prepared. Its text encoding stage also exceeds the old performance limit with the new conditioning cache enabled.

## Modifications

- Update the NPU ground-truth pin using outputs from [this CI run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36325400104/job/108637133421).
- Convert enums to their names before JSON transfer, including enums inside nested containers. Add a regression test that transfers and rebuilds a `TI2I` request.
- Prepare MiniMax-H3's text encoder before its direct encoding call so the memory manager can track and finish its use correctly.
- Update the MiniMax-H3 text-stage baseline from 134.59 ms to 421.11 ms, based on two CI measurements with the conditioning cache enabled.

## Accuracy Tests

Accuracy and GLM-Image end-to-end validation are pending on the updated PR head. 

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MiniMax-H3 text encoding became slower in the reported stage timings after the upstream conditioning-cache change:

| Metric | Earlier passing run | Run with conditioning cache enabled |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Text encoding | 158.17 ms | 422.67 / 419.55 ms |
| End-to-end generation | 155.51 s | 155.41 / 155.32 s |

Sources: [earlier passing job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36398889383/job/108920979452), [later job at `796e369c`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36693080568/job/109814703741).

The text stage increased by about **263 ms (2.66x)**, exceeding its old 254.59 ms limit. The end-to-end measurements show no corresponding slowdown in these runs.

The cache adds input hashing, rank coordination, and a host copy of the output. Stage timing normally does not synchronize the device, so the host copy may also make the timer include device work that previously completed after the stage returned. We have not profiled how much of the increase comes from each operation.

The new baseline is the median of the two measurements: **421.11 ms**. With the existing tolerance, the limit becomes **758.00 ms**. This accepts the observed stage timing with caching enabled; it does not demonstrate a performance improvement.

title: [diffusion] fix: validate SageAttention 2 head sizes without overriding component policy
author: Seas0
body:
## Motivation

Narrow this PR to SageAttention 2 head-size validation while preserving the existing component-aware selection policy.

Upstream SageAttention 2 pads positive head dimensions up to 128 internally, including 32 and 72. Restricting it to `[64, 96, 128]` incorrectly rejects supported shapes; the existing SGLang metadata also advertises unsupported dimensions above 128. See the [upstream padding logic](https://github.com/thu-ml/SageAttention/blob/v2.2.0/sageattention/core.py#L559).

## Changes

- Align `SageAttentionBackend.get_supported_head_sizes()` with the supported SageAttention 2 implementation.
- When the CUDA resolver selects SageAttention 2, raise `ValueError` for unsupported head sizes instead of substituting FlashAttention or SDPA inside the platform layer.
- Let the existing selector handle that error: an auxiliary component inheriting the global backend can fall back, while an explicit component override or explicit DiT selection remains strict for this mismatch.
- Remove the SageAttention 3 special case. No new flags, shared selector changes, forward-kernel changes, or changes to other backend resolvers.

An encoder can already be pinned independently of the DiT:

```bash
--attention-backend sage_attn \
--component-attention-backends text_encoder=torch_sdpa
```

## Validation

On an isolated Linux CUDA development environment (PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Transformers 5.12.1, Diffusers 0.37.0):

- CUDA backend selection, shared selector, and Qwen3-VL text tests: **50 passed, 17 subtests passed**.
- Qwen3-VL vision and request-level backend override tests: **38 passed**.
- The new regressions fail against the previous PR implementation and pass with this revision.
- Pre-commit passed.

The new tests exercise the real selector, CUDA resolver, and Sage backend metadata, with the optional Sage kernel dependency mocked. Real Sage kernel execution and Qwen-Image end-to-end generation were not rerun. The original report that head size 72 always fails is not claimed for the supported SageAttention 2 implementation; reproducing that report requires its exact installed package and traceback.

title: [Diffusion] Fix concurrent server perf dump writes across ranks
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

In server mode, every rank in a diffusion replica can write the same `perf_dump_path` with `open(..., "w")`. Concurrent writes can leave malformed JSON or replace the output rank's metrics with another rank's report. The September 19 nightly comparison artifact contains seven malformed perf reports out of 36 (`JSONDecodeError: Extra data`).

Evidence: [nightly comparison job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35447786547/job/105909616906).

## Modifications

- Write the server perf report only on the replica's existing `is_output_rank`.
- Keep replica peak-memory collection outside that guard so all participating ranks still enter the reduction.
- Add a regression test covering output/non-output ranks and warmup/non-warmup requests, using the real JSON writer. Non-writing ranks must leave an existing report untouched.

This fixes report ownership rather than tolerating corrupted JSON or changing performance thresholds.

## Accuracy Tests

No model-compute changes. The regression test exercises `GPUWorker._execute_forward_common`, JSON serialization, and the call boundary for replica memory collection; it does not substitute for a real multi-GPU collective test.

At head `0f090c53c24`, an isolated B200 development environment passed all 48 tests in `test_performance_metrics.py`, `test_logging_utils.py`, and `test_diffusion_nightly_comparison.py` (PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Diffusers 0.37.0).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No inference speedup claim. This change improves the integrity of server-side performance evidence without changing benchmark configuration or ground truth.

title: [Fix] [NPU] qwen: adapt pcp-v2
author: gjsheu
body:
## Problem

Prefill context parallel is broken for **every model that uses the generic (non-DSA) Ascend attention backend** — Qwen3, Qwen3-MoE, and anything else going through `AscendAttnBackend.forward_extend` under CP. The CP v1 runtime was removed for platform backends, but this path was left calling into the removed implementation, so it fails twice:

**1. The KV all-gather call is gone (fails before the first token is produced)**

```
File ".../hardware_backend/npu/attention/ascend_backend.py", line 1902, in forward_extend
File ".../hardware_backend/npu/attention/ascend_backend.py", line 1478, in do_cp_attn_fia
File ".../layers/utils/cp_utils.py", line 19, in cp_all_gather_rerange_kv_cache
    _deprecated_platform_cp()
ValueError: Prefill CP on HIP/NPU/MUSA is deprecated; CP support will be refactored soon.
```

`cp_utils.py` is now an import-only shim; the NPU generic path is its only remaining real caller. Every scheduler rank dies on the first prefill, so the server exits with SIGQUIT.

**2. FIA tiling fails on the padded CP shard (fails once the KV write is fixed)**

```
RuntimeError: npu_fused_infer_attention_score_symint ... NPU function error:
  call aclnnFusedInferAttentionScoreV3 failed, error code is 561002
Execution_Error(EZ1008): Failed to execute operator FusedInferAttentionScore_0.
  Reason: Failed to execute tiling function.
```

`do_cp_attn_fia` handed FIA the **physical** query shard while advertising only the **logical** token counts in `actual_seq_lengths`. The model runner pads the shard to `per_rank_actual_token[0]` rows, so the advertised cumulative sequence lengths did not match the query row count. Traced live on an A3 machine (tp2 + attn-cp2, 6-token prompt, cp_rank 0):

```
q_local=4  per_rank_actual_token=[4, 4]  split_list=[2, 2, 1, 1]  zigzag_index=[0, 3]
prev_list=[2]  next_list=[1]   ->  logical tokens = 3, physical rows = 4
```

and the mismatch is reproducible in isolation — `actual_seq_lengths=[1]` with a 2-row query fails, `[2]` with a 2-row query succeeds:

```
OK   asl=[2] kv=5    FAIL asl=[1] kv=5    FAIL asl=[1] kv=6
```

## Change

`python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/attention/ascend_backend.py`:

- `_cp_allgather_and_save_kv_npu` now goes through the CP v2 strategy
  (`get_cp_strategy().materialize_full_kv(...)`), with a plain KV write when CP
  is off — the same contract as the `cp_active` branch of
  `flashattention_backend`. The deprecated helper import is dropped.
- `do_cp_attn_fia` trims the physical pad rows before the two FIA calls
  (`logical_tokens = total_q_prev_tokens + total_q_next_tokens`) and re-appends
  zero rows to the output so downstream code still sees the physical shard.

A unit test is added at
`test/registered/unit/npu/attention/test_npu_prefill_cp_backend.py` covering both
paths on CPU tensors (no hardware needed).

(`--enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy zigzag`, `ASCEND_USE_FIA=1`).

title: [KDA] Fix ptx_kda prefill NaN without a gate lower bound and workspace growth
author: yuan-luo
body:
## Motivation

Validating `--linear-attn-prefill-backend ptx_kda` end to end on B200 turned up two problems in the PTX prefill path. Neither depends on the arch: both exist on SM103, where ptx_kda runs today.

1. **Models without a gate lower bound get NaN.** On Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct, ptx_kda scored GSM8K 0.000 against 0.902 for Triton, every prompt logprob of a 6K-token prefill was NaN, and nothing was logged. The kernel only handles the safe gate (`lower_bound` set, as in Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3-Flash).
2. **The workspace cache grows with every batch shape until the process runs out of memory.** A GLM-5.3-Flash TP4 server on ptx_kda hit CUDA OOM about 20 s into GSM8K, while Triton on the same args ran the full eval.

## Modifications

- `srt/layers/attention/linear/kernels/kda_ptx.py`: batches from a model without a gate lower bound take the wrapper's existing Triton fallback, the same path as spec draft-extend, track-state snapshots and unsupported shapes. It logs one warning.
- `kernels/jit/csrc/attention/kda_prefill.cu`: `get_workspace` clears its cache once it holds 4 entries. The device code is unchanged.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_kda_prefill.py`, one regression case per fix. Like the existing ptx cases they run on SM103 (GB300 CI).
  - `test_ptx_without_lower_bound_matches_triton`: with no lower bound and `exp(A_log)` near 200, the output must be finite and match Triton.
  - `test_ptx_workspace_memory_is_bounded`: 16 new batch shapes must not keep one workspace each.

## Accuracy Tests

Unit tests on B200, with the companion PR's SM100 enablement applied so the ptx cases run there (on this branch alone they run on SM103 only):

```
test_kda_prefill.py::TestKdaPrefill::test_nvidia_prefill PASSED
test_kda_prefill.py::TestKdaPrefill::test_ptx_padded_raw_beta PASSED
test_kda_prefill.py::TestKdaPrefill::test_ptx_prefill PASSED
test_kda_prefill.py::TestKdaPrefill::test_ptx_without_lower_bound_matches_triton PASSED
test_kda_prefill.py::TestKdaPrefill::test_ptx_workspace_memory_is_bounded PASSED
5 passed in 152.71s
```

Both new cases fail on the code before this change: the output has NaN, and 16 shapes keep 107.6 MB against a 37.9 MB bound.

End-to-end on B200, same setup:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Kimi-Linear-48B, TP2, ptx_kda: GSM8K | 0.000 (Triton 0.902; 500 questions, 5-shot) | 0.93 (200 questions, 5-shot) |
| GLM-5.3-Flash, TP4, ptx_kda: GSM8K, 500 questions, 20-shot | CUDA OOM during the eval | 0.932 (Triton 0.924) |

- Kimi-Linear now runs its prefill on Triton, and the server logs the fallback once per rank.
- GLM-5.3-Flash uses the cookbook Blackwell recipe plus `--disable-radix-cache`, which keeps its tracked batches off the Triton fallback. Its prompt logprobs on a 2040-token prefill are bit-identical with and without the cache bound.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

The bound can make a cache hit into a miss, so this measures what a miss costs: the latency of the first call of a batch shape against a repeat of it. B200, 16 heads, safe gate, 16K tokens, CUDA events:

| batch | new shape (miss) | repeated shape (hit) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 sequence (fused route) | 895–939 µs | 764–798 µs |
| 2–9 sequences (builder + chain) | 573 µs | 532 µs |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the pre-commit hooks (isort 7.0.0, ruff 0.15.1 check and format are clean on the changed Python files).
- [x] Add unit tests (a regression case for each fix).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.

title: [Fix] deepseek-v4: Refresh attn_sink after loading weights
author: parkeychen
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

When attention TP > 1, `MqaAttentionBase._local_attn_sink()` builds a padded, TP-local copy of `attn_sink` (`_attn_sink_local`) on the first forward, and never refreshes it afterwards. Online weight updates (e.g. `update_weights_from_tensor` in RL) write new values into `attn_sink`, but `MQALayer.forward()` keeps reading the stale copy. As a result, the model silently serves the startup sinks; with `load_format=dummy`, the sinks stay dummy for the whole run.
## Modifications

- Record the head slice used to build the copy, and add `MqaAttentionBase.refresh_attn_sink_cache()`. It copies the updated `attn_sink` slice into the existing `_attn_sink_local` in place.
- Call it from `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM.post_load_weights()`, next to `refresh_mhc_norm_weight_cache()`.

title: Fix XQA draft extend with FP8 KV cache in trtllm_mha
author: elvischenv
body:
## Motivation

On SM90/SM120, `trtllm_mha` runs `draft_extend_v2` through the XQA decode kernel, same as `target_verify`, but only `target_verify` was handled for XQA:

- With `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, Q was cast to FP8 for draft extend. XQA requires Q to match the bf16 output, so EAGLE draft-extend CUDA graph capture fails at startup:
  ```
  AssertionError: Output and query must have the same dtype
  ```
- The draft-block mask added in #32269 is only passed for `target_verify`. XQA asserts `Mask is required for speculative decoding` whenever `q_len_per_req > 1`, which draft extend always has (`speculative_num_draft_tokens` per request).

Repro: a Nemotron-H MTP model on H100 with `--attention-backend trtllm_mha --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6`.

## Modifications

- Skip the FP8 Q cast on XQA for both decode-kernel modes (`target_verify` and `draft_extend_v2`), matching `forward_decode`.
- Pass `_xqa_spec_dec_mask` whenever `max_seq_len_q > 1`. Draft extend's block is a causal chain of `speculative_num_draft_tokens` tokens, which is what the mask encodes.
- Tests in `test_trtllm_mha_graph_metadata.py`:
  - mask forwarding for `draft_extend_v2` with width > 1;
  - Q dtype with an FP8 KV cache: bf16 for XQA verify/draft extend, FP8 for trtllm-gen.

## Accuracy Tests

Unit tests on H100 (`lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260928-81f27fb3`, FlashInfer 0.6.18):

- `test/registered/attention/test_trtllm_mha_graph_metadata.py`: 195 passed.
- Without the fix, the new cases fail (4 failed: 3 draft-extend mask cases, 1 FP8 draft-extend Q dtype).

End-to-end MTP accuracy (GSM8K) on H100: pending.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A. No kernel change; draft extend on SM90/SM120 with FP8 KV previously failed to start.

title: [Fix] Keep MiMo-V2 processor available without TorchCodec
author: janbernloehr
body:
## Motivation

Fixes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/41568.

MiMo-V2 imports TorchCodec while registering its multimodal processor. On Linux ARM64, where SGLang excludes TorchCodec from its dependencies, this prevents even text/image serving from starting. The reported failure occurred on 4 x GB200. Installed TorchCodec can also fail to import when native decoding libraries are unavailable.

Related: [#32681](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32681) includes optional TorchCodec handling within a larger Rust-server change. This PR isolates the Python processor fix.

## Modifications

- Reuse the optional decoder import from `mimo_audio.py` instead of importing TorchCodec unconditionally in `mimo_v2.py`.
- Handle `ImportError`, `OSError`, and `RuntimeError` from the optional import, including native-library load failures.
- Raise `ValueError` before automatic video audio-track detection when the decoder is unavailable, so the OpenAI endpoint returns HTTP 400 with an actionable dependency message.
- Limit the warning to video audio-track detection and decoding through `AudioDecoder`; audio already decoded by the shared loader remains supported.

Head: [`janbernloehr:jbernloehr/fix-mimo-v2-torchcodec`](https://github.com/janbernloehr/sglang/tree/jbernloehr/fix-mimo-v2-torchcodec). Target: `sgl-project/sglang:main`. Based on upstream `090439bf8f9a73ba999faac2a1179c6714adac58`, fetched September 28, 2026.

Commit: [`b2c69dbd2c`](https://github.com/janbernloehr/sglang/commit/b2c69dbd2c645f233dcb8fbdd4051d91b6694532).

## Accuracy Tests

GPU validation used upstream `090439bf8f9a73ba999faac2a1179c6714adac58` plus [TorchCodec revision `859a890348`](https://github.com/janbernloehr/sglang/commit/859a8903482e1f629b6e1ca27d01abfacf71d0ee), individually and together with [MXFP4 revision `18cb0c382c`](https://github.com/janbernloehr/sglang/commit/18cb0c382c0325eb4fa72c99f1a8553e2eb94364). Each run verified that every server rank imported the selected source checkout.

Environment: **4 x NVIDIA GB200**, Linux ARM64, driver 580.178.04, CUDA 13.0.3, Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Transformers 5.12.1, FlashInfer 0.6.18, and sglang-kernel 0.4.7. TorchCodec was absent. Model: `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL` at revision `5711b268169967567844e1e560e8a3966da959b1`, TP=4, context 4096, memory fraction 0.79, seed 1234.

The isolated TorchCodec run used `--ep 4 --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode auto` to isolate processor registration from the separate runner-selection bug.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Unpatched startup without TorchCodec | Reproduced `No processor registered for architecture: ['MiMoV2ForCausalLM']` |
| Patched startup, greedy text, repeat determinism, and chat | Passed |
| WAV `audio_url` | Processed successfully through the shared audio loader |
| Video with audio / silent video | Both returned the TorchCodec dependency error; server remained healthy |
| Both fixes with automatic MXFP4 selection | Startup and generation passed; GSM8K 5-shot full set: 90.07% flexible extract, 90.30% strict match |

**Changes after GPU validation:** the current revision narrows the warning and changes the missing-decoder exception from `RuntimeError` to `ValueError`. The validated revision returned HTTP 500 for video; the current revision maps this condition to HTTP 400. A focused check exercised the processor method and OpenAI request-handler bodies and confirmed the 500-to-400 change. That check isolated unrelated serving dependencies; the current revision has not been rerun end to end on GB200. Import handling and successful inference paths are unchanged.

**Video limitation:** automatic audio-track detection still requires TorchCodec for all videos, including silent ones. The patch does not infer that a video has no audio when its decoder is unavailable.

Repository pre-commit checks pass. No new standalone CI test file is included.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The combined validated revisions completed an ISL/OSL 1000/1000 benchmark on 4 x NVIDIA GB200, with output throughput of **267.4 / 2713 / 7430 tokens/s** at concurrency **1 / 16 / 64**. These measurements include the separate MXFP4 runner fix and do not isolate the effect of this import-handling change. No speedup is attributed to this patch.

- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Fix] Select the MXFP4 MoE runner for MiMo-V2 packed experts on SM100
author: janbernloehr
body:
## Motivation

Fixes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/41569.

MiMo-V2 mixed checkpoints advertise `quant_method=fp8` while storing routed experts as packed MXFP4. On SM100, automatic runner selection ignores the detected expert layout and selects the ordinary FP8 runner. The reported 4 x B200 launch fails because that kernel expects FP8 weights and receives packed `int8` weights.

This builds on the loader support from [#40448](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40448). Related [#40722](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40722) addresses automatic MXFP4 selection on SM120; this PR addresses SM100.

## Modifications

- Consult cached `ModelConfig.is_fp4_experts` during automatic MiMo-V2 backend selection on SM100.
- Select the existing `flashinfer_mxfp4` runner for packed experts when no all-to-all backend is configured.
- Retain the ordinary FP8 default and explicit runner choices. Leave all-to-all configurations to their existing runner resolution.
- Extend the registered model-override tests for both MiMo-V2 architecture names, explicit runner choices, and DeepEP configurations; provide the detected layout in the ordinary FP8 test fixture.

Head: [`janbernloehr:jbernloehr/fix-mimo-v2-sm100-mxfp4`](https://github.com/janbernloehr/sglang/tree/jbernloehr/fix-mimo-v2-sm100-mxfp4). Target: `sgl-project/sglang:main`. Rebased onto upstream `a21dcbd3204f485ef43d24adea03543d0897ac9b` on October 2, 2026. Preserves upstream's FA4 attention default on SM100 and updates the existing regression test to expect it alongside runner selection.

Commit: [`3f319741ec`](https://github.com/janbernloehr/sglang/commit/3f319741ec543939192743cfc155ed63787eabe2).

## Accuracy Tests

Rebase verification: the registered model-override suite passed with **111 tests and 155 subtests**, with **1 skipped**. Repository pre-commit checks passed.

The NVIDIA GPU results below validate the pre-rebase commit `18cb0c382c0325eb4fa72c99f1a8553e2eb94364` on upstream `090439bf8f9a73ba999faac2a1179c6714adac58`. GPU startup, generation, accuracy, and performance have not been rerun for rebased commit `3f319741ec543939192743cfc155ed63787eabe2`, which incorporates upstream's new FA4 default. Each run verified that every server rank imported the selected source checkout.

Environment: **4 x NVIDIA B200**, Linux x86-64, driver 580.82.07, CUDA 13.0.3, Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Transformers 5.12.1, FlashInfer 0.6.18, sglang-kernel 0.4.7, and TorchCodec 0.15.0+cu130. Model: `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL` at revision `5711b268169967567844e1e560e8a3966da959b1`.

Common server settings: `--tp 4 --context-length 4096 --mem-fraction-static 0.79 --random-seed 1234 --trust-remote-code --enable-metrics --weight-loader-prefetch-checkpoints`.

- Unpatched `--moe-runner-backend auto --moe-a2a-backend none` reproduced `gemm1_weights must be fp8`.
- Patched `auto`/`none` selected `flashinfer_mxfp4` and passed startup, greedy text, determinism, chat, WAV audio, and both silent and audio-bearing video checks.
- Unpatched explicit `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 --moe-a2a-backend none` served as the reference.
- Patched `--ep 4 --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode auto` remained functional.

GSM8K, 5-shot, full 1,319-question test set, seed 1234, 32 concurrent requests, maximum context 4096:

| B200 configuration | Flexible extract ± standard error | Strict match |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Patched automatic MXFP4 | 90.90% ± 0.79 pp | 91.43% |
| Unpatched explicit MXFP4 | 90.07% ± 0.82 pp | 90.60% |
| Patched explicit DeepEP | 89.46% ± 0.85 pp | 90.30% |

The auto-versus-explicit difference is within one combined standard error. Fixed seeds do not fix concurrent batch composition; these runs do not establish statistical equivalence.

Additional validation on **4 x NVIDIA GB200**, Linux ARM64, driver 580.178.04, with [TorchCodec fix `859a890348`](https://github.com/janbernloehr/sglang/commit/859a8903482e1f629b6e1ca27d01abfacf71d0ee): automatic MXFP4 startup and generation passed, with GSM8K **90.07% flexible / 90.30% strict**. A control with only the TorchCodec fix still reproduced the incompatible FP8-runner failure.

`test/registered/unit/test_model_overrides.py` passed on both NVIDIA systems: **107 tests and 62 subtests**. Repository pre-commit checks passed. The initial open-ended text probe was corrected to Q/A framing, and all final runtime cases passed; baseline/control cases passed by reproducing their expected failures.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

AIPerf on 4 x NVIDIA B200: streaming completions, ISL/OSL 1000/1000, concurrency 1/16/64, 5 × concurrency requests, one warmup request, fixed 1000-token output with `ignore_eos=true`.

| Configuration | c=1 output tok/s | c=16 output tok/s | c=64 output tok/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Patched automatic MXFP4 | 264.8 | 2683 | 7223 |
| Unpatched explicit MXFP4 | 269.8 | 2676 | 7230 |
| Patched explicit DeepEP | 133.2 | 1539 | 4666 |

Patched-auto throughput differed from explicit MXFP4 by **−1.8% / +0.3% / −0.1%**. Mean TTFT was **91 / 217 / 422 ms** versus **87 / 218 / 431 ms**; mean ITL was **3.68 / 5.75 / 8.44 ms** versus **3.62 / 5.76 / 8.42 ms**. The c=1 sample contains only five requests, so these measurements do not establish a speed difference between automatic and explicit selection.

The combined fixes on 4 x NVIDIA GB200 measured **267.4 / 2713 / 7430 output tokens/s** at the same concurrencies. No profiler trace is included.

title: [Fix] [AMD] dsa: Limit AITER decode metadata to the active batch
author: pbkowalski
body:
# [AMD] Limit AITER DSA decode metadata to the active batch

## Motivation

The AITER DSA backend preallocates `kv_indptr` for the maximum request-pool
capacity and reuses that buffer for smaller decode batches. The AITER metadata
builder consumes the logical length of the tensor it receives. Passing the
capacity-sized tensor exposes entries beyond the active batch and can construct
invalid persistent MLA work metadata.

On MI355X TP4 with an FP8 KV cache, the invalid metadata caused eager and CUDA
graph execution to fault in:

`aiter::mla_a16w8_qh16_m16x4_n16x1_coex0_mask1_ps`

## Modifications

Pass only the active `bs + 1` entries to the AITER metadata builder:

```python
kv_indptr = kv_indptr[: bs + 1]
```

The backing buffer remains preallocated and reused. This change only corrects
the logical range passed to `get_mla_metadata_v1`.

## Accuracy Tests

AITER is included in the existing registered FP8 DSA decode matrix.

On MI355X TP4 with `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4`, FP8 KV cache, AITER DSA prefill/decode,
and CUDA graphs through decode batch 64, the parent revision faulted in
`aiter::mla_a16w8_qh16_m16x4_n16x1_coex0_mask1_ps`. The corrected path
completed 60k-input/600-output eager execution and CUDA graph capture/replay
without the fault. Eager and graph-enabled runs produced identical output.

The serving reproduction used 60,000 input tokens, 600 output tokens,
concurrency 4, 32 prompts, and seed 15.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This is a correctness fix. No standalone serving-speed improvement is claimed;
decode metadata reuse is submitted separately.

## Reproduction

Launch the parent or candidate revision on MI355X:

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 \
  --tp 4 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --attention-backend dsa \
  --dsa-prefill-backend aiter \
  --dsa-decode-backend aiter \
  --dsa-topk-backend sgl-kernel \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --page-size 64 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 \
  --disable-radix-cache \
  --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \
  --max-prefill-tokens 32768
```

Run 60,000 input tokens and 600 output tokens at concurrency 4 with 32 prompts
and seed 15. The parent revision faults during eager execution or CUDA graph
capture/replay; the candidate completes the workload.

## Checklist

- [x] Format and code-style checks pass.
- [x] Reuse the registered FP8 decode matrix for AITER coverage.
- [ ] Run the registered matrix on the exact rebased head.
- [x] Run exact-head MI355X eager and CUDA graph validation.
- [x] No user-facing documentation change is required.

title: [Fix] [AMD] mamba: Keep a chunked prefill cut on the mamba chunk grid so DCP can donate checkpoints
author: chien-an-chen
body:
## Motivation

Under DCP, #39115 donates a mamba checkpoint only when
`prefix_len % mamba_cache_chunk_size() == 0`. `PrefillAdder` cuts a chunk
wherever the prefill budget runs out, and every later chunk inherits that
offset, so a request donates every checkpoint or none. With nothing donated,
`effective_cache_len` is 0 and the KV segment never enters the radix tree.
#40907 restored the old rule only on the non-DCP branch. This PR keeps the
DCP mask and makes the cut land on the grid.

Kimi-K3 MXFP4, 8×MI355X, TP=8 DCP=8, fp8 KV, `page_size=32`,
`chunked_prefill_size=8192`, `max_running_requests=96`,
`mamba_radix_cache_strategy=extra_buffer`, HiCache on, agentic workload at
concurrency 48. Each row is the same 240 s window after warmup. The last two
rows share a host, so the recovery is a within-host measurement. The first two
identify the commit that introduced the regression.

| tree | `kv_evictable_tokens` | `mamba_evictable_tokens` | device cache hit | prompt tokens / 240 s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fa8d22e665` (#39115's parent) | 11,382,528 | 473/480 | **91.5%** | 59.8 M |
| `6460082c05` (#39115) | 620,800 | 123/480 | 50.3% | 4.8 M |
| `main` (`8d1643b21e`) | 392,448 | 88/480 | **30.4%** | 3.3 M |
| `main` + this PR | 11,614,464 | 464/480 | **90.7%** | 59.5 M |

## Modifications

No-op unless `enable_mamba_extra_buffer` is set.

- `Scheduler.init_mamba_truncation_align()` folds `mamba_cache_chunk_size()`
  into `truncation_align_size` with an LCM, the same way DSA kpool alignment
  does. This covers `exact_chunk_fill`.
- `PrefillAdder.floor_chunked_tokens()` rounds a truncated chunk down to that
  grid in `add_chunked_req` and `add_one_req_ignore_eos`.

A chunk that finishes a request may stop anywhere. A cut shorter than one
chunk is not rounded to zero. The unit test walks a 100k prompt through six
chunks cut to arbitrary leftover budgets and checks that each one still donates.

Once donation works, the mamba pool's working set grows. A 60-slot pool that
was sized while donation was failing can assert in `_alloc_ping_pong_buffer`
at concurrency 4 and long context. Raise `--max-mamba-cache-size`.
Concurrencies 8, 16 and 48 were unaffected.

## Accuracy Tests

Tested at head `a5f74268` on 8×MI355X with Kimi-K3, TP8 + DCP8,
`mamba_radix_cache_strategy=extra_buffer`, `page_size=32`, and
`chunked_prefill_size=8192`.
For eight concurrent 17k–31k prompts followed by identical repeats, the
repeated requests reported:
| main (`4e0609ea27`) | this PR |
|---|---|
| 121,856 / 201,718 cached tokens (60.4%) | 200,704 / 201,718 cached tokens (99.5%) |
GSM8K was also run with the same DCP8/extra-buffer configuration:
- 1,319 questions, 5-shot
- Accuracy: **95.3%**
- Invalid: **0.1%**
- Exit status: 0
No accuracy regression was observed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

kimi-k3 AgentX 3600 s, concurrency 48, non-speculative. 2026-09-01 (pre-#39115) was
7272 tok/s/GPU; 2026-09-28 plus this PR is 7492 (103%), GPU hit 84.6%.
The rows span weekly images, so the eviction-pool table above is the
controlled measurement.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: Fix CFG normalization to use per-sample norm instead of batch-flattened norm
author: OnePunchMonk
body:
Fixes #41705

## What

`_apply_cfg_normalization` in `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/distributed/cfg_policy.py` called `torch.linalg.vector_norm` with no `dim` argument, so the norm was computed over the whole flattened batch. The clamp decision and the rescale factor were shared across every sample in the batch rather than computed per sample.

This changes it to compute per sample norms with `dim=list(range(1, ndim)), keepdim=True`, matching the pattern already used by the sibling function `_rescale_noise_cfg` in the same file. The Python `if` becomes `torch.where` because the comparison is now a tensor rather than a scalar.

## Why it matters here

`runtime/pipelines_core/stages/latent_preparation.py` concatenates independent `Req` objects into a single DiT forward pass (`latents = torch.cat(raw_latents, dim=0)`). With a batch global norm, the clamp decision and rescale factor are shared across the batch, so one request's result depends on which other requests happen to be co-scheduled with it.

Three conditions all have to hold for that to bite, and it is worth being precise about them:

- **Batching above 1 must be enabled.** `batching_max_size` defaults to `1` (`runtime/server_args/server_args.py:542`), so a default deployment never forms a batch larger than one and is unaffected. This needs `--batching-max-size > 1`.
- **The config must actually run CFG.** Z-Image-Turbo sets `guidance_scale=0.0` and `cfg_normalization=False` (`configs/sample/zimage.py:21-22`), so `CFGPolicy.combine` returns at the single-prediction early exit and never reaches this function. The non-Turbo `ZImageSamplingParams` (`configs/sample/zimage.py:44-45`) does: `guidance_scale=5.0` and `cfg_normalization=True`.
- **The batch must be heterogeneous.** If the co-scheduled samples are identical the two norms agree exactly, since the shared `sqrt(N)` factor cancels in `max_norm / new_norm`, and the output is unchanged either way.

Verified on an L40S with `Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image` at default sampling params, no overrides. Instrumenting the function's input shape, two independently submitted requests merged into one forward pass:

```
Dynamic batch dispatch: requests=2, outputs=2/2, stop_reason=config_cap:2
CFGNORM_HIT shape= (2, 16, 1, 128, 128)
Processed dynamic batch of 2/2 request(s)
```

against the same request on its own:

```
CFGNORM_HIT shape= (1, 16, 1, 128, 128)
```

So the path is genuinely reachable with a batch dimension above 1. The divergence itself is a tensor level claim, pinned by the unit tests below. I could not isolate it at the pixel level and do not think that is achievable: a batch 1 forward and a batch 2 forward select different kernels, and same seed generations are not bit reproducible at fixed batch size either, so that noise sits above the effect.

## Relationship to upstream

Both the official Z-Image implementation (`Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image`) and `huggingface/diffusers` (`pipelines/z_image/pipeline_z_image.py`) use the same dim-less norm. This patch is therefore a deliberate divergence from upstream, not a transcription fix.

The mitigation is that behavior at batch size 1 is unchanged, since a global norm and a per sample norm are identical when there is only one sample. That case stays bit identical to the reference, and a test below pins it. The divergence only appears at batch size greater than 1, which is the case upstream does not exercise the way this serving path does.

If maintainers would rather keep this matching upstream exactly, say so and I will close this in favour of documenting the behavior instead.

## Checklist before this is ready for review

Tests to add:

- [x] `test_sample_result_is_independent_of_batch_composition`: run a sample alone and co-batched with an outlier, assert its result is identical. This is the test that encodes the actual claim in #41705 and fails on `main`.
- [x] `test_every_sample_respects_its_own_threshold`: assert every sample's post-clamp norm ratio is `<= cfg_normalization`, not just the batch aggregate.
- [x] `test_batch_size_one_unchanged`: assert batch size 1 behavior is unchanged, pinning reference parity and guarding the divergence argument above. Landed as `test_batch_size_one_matches_global_norm_reference`, comparing against the global-norm reference inline.

Verification still outstanding:

- [x] Run the new tests and confirm they fail on `main` and pass with this patch. On this branch: 5 passed. With `cfg_policy.py` reverted to `main`: 2 failed, and they are the two that encode the claim. `test_every_sample_respects_its_own_threshold` reports per-sample ratios `[1.347, 0.013, 0.013, 0.015]` against a 0.7 threshold, so the first sample is left unclamped by the batch-global norm. `test_batch_size_one_matches_global_norm_reference` passes both ways by design.
- [x] Run the existing `test/unit/test_cfg_policy.py` to confirm no regression. Now observed rather than inferred: `test_cfg_parallel_uses_parallel_arithmetic_order` passes on this branch. It exercises `cfg_normalization=0`, so it does not reach the changed code.
- [x] Confirm the input dtype is preserved for bf16 and fp16 predictions. It was not, and this was a real bug in the first version of the patch, caught in review by @adenzhou1350. The per-sample `scale` is fp32 and shaped `[N, 1, ...]`, so `noise_pred * scale` promoted bf16/fp16 output to fp32. The previous batch-global scale was 0-dim, and a 0-dim operand does not promote a dimensioned one, so `main` was unaffected; the old unclamped path also returned `noise_pred` untouched, while the new one always multiplies. Fixed by casting the product back with `.to(noise_pred.dtype)`, and pinned by a dtype case over fp32/fp16/bf16 across the clamped and unclamped branches.
- [x] Check the other `cfg_normalization` consumers reached through `_apply_cfg_postprocess`. There are two, `CFGPolicy.combine` and `run_cfg_parallel` in `cfg_parallel_utils.py`. Both pass a real tensor and feed the return straight into the next operation, so neither relied on a scalar return or on identity when no clamping occurs. One edge the per-sample change introduces: `dims` is empty for a 1-D prediction, and `torch.linalg.vector_norm(x, dim=[])` still reduces over every element, so 1-D inputs behave exactly as they did on `main`.

Optional, probably not required:

- [x] End to end check on a GPU. Reachability is confirmed and written up under "Why it matters here": the normalization does receive a batch dimension of 2 from two independently scheduled requests on non-Turbo Z-Image at default params. A pixel level comparison is not achievable, since changing the batch size changes kernel selection and same seed output is not bit reproducible, so the tensor level unit tests stand as the evidence for the divergence.

title: [diffusion] Fix the OOM hint's placement advice and add a 24 GB Wan2.1 recipe
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

With no placement flags, Wan2.1-I2V-14B runs out of memory on RTX 4090 24 GB, and the OOM message's own advice mostly does not get it running. Each remedy was tried on its own on main (`c7be3e9`), 1 and 8 GPUs, 480x832, 81 frames, 40 steps:

| remedy in the message | result |
|---|---|
| component CPU offload | the default on this card, and what runs out of memory: it moves the whole 30.5 GiB DiT onto the GPU |
| `--dit-layerwise-offload` | OOM in warmup: it streams only the DiT, and the FP32 text encoder (~22 GB) stays on component offload |
| keep the default `--performance-mode auto` (multi-GPU) | OOM: it is the configuration that just failed |
| `--use-fsdp-inference true` (multi-GPU) | OOM on main, runs with #41722 |
| `--performance-mode memory` | runs: 840.4 s on 1 GPU, 197.6 s on 8 |

The OOM also came in the first request (the server's warmup), when component offload moved the DiT onto the GPU, not during loading. So the message's runtime section (reduce resolution or frames) is the one that seemed to apply, and it cannot help when the weights do not fit.

## Modifications

- `gpu_worker.py` `OOM_MSG`, load-time section:
  - also covers an OOM on the first request with a component on CPU offload, since that is where oversized weights surface;
  - single GPU: leads with an explicit `--layerwise-offload-components` list, which works for any model with layerwise support; says `--dit-layerwise-offload` streams only the DiT and `--performance-mode memory` streams the DiT only for models that validate it, and that component CPU offload helps only when each component fits on its own;
  - multi-GPU: drops "keep the default `--performance-mode auto`" (the FSDP line is unchanged; #41722 makes it work on small GPUs);
  - links the cookbook for tested launch commands.
- `docs/cookbook/diffusion/Wan/Wan2.1.mdx`: new section 3.3, 24 GB NVIDIA GPUs, with the 1- and 8-GPU commands and the measured time per video, time per step, peak GPU memory and host memory. Each GPU's worker keeps its own ~60 GiB copy of the streamed weights, so 8 GPUs need close to 500 GiB of RAM; the section says so.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: message text and documentation only.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The cookbook numbers come from these runs, RTX 4090 24 GB (PCIe, no P2P), BF16, eager, one request after warmup:

| command | e2e | per step | peak GPU memory | host memory |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `--performance-mode memory` | 840.4 s | 20.7 s | 12.5 GiB | 59 GiB |
| `--num-gpus 8 --enable-cfg-parallel --ulysses-degree 4 --performance-mode memory` | 197.6 s | 4.8 s | 11.9 GiB | 483 GiB |

Host memory is the drop in `MemAvailable` from the idle box to its low point, from launch until 60 s after the server was ready.

Related: #41721 (auto mode streams an oversized DiT, so no flag is needed there), #41722 (`--use-fsdp-inference true` alone works on small GPUs).

* __->__ #41749

## Motivation

Under attention DP, prefill CUDA graph capture uses about 62 MiB more memory than before the layer boundary refactor (#41547–#41557). The FFN all-reduce of a dense layer is now deferred to the next layer's input, so the unreduced output — gathered over the DP ranks, 2N rows for N local tokens — is stored in the residual stream's pending contribution. The next stage's `prepare()` consumes it, but the model loop still holds the returned handle until the next layer returns, and the handle keeps the tensor alive. Inside the graph memory pool that block cannot be reused.

## Modifications

- `Contribution.release()` drops a contribution's tensors.
- `ResidualStream.write()` releases the contribution it replaces. It is called only where a pending contribution is consumed: a successful `prepare()`, `fold()` and branch merge. `complete_output()`, `snapshot()` and export (`to_pp()`, the final norm) do not release. Stale handles were already rejected by the stream, so nothing can read a released contribution.
- Test: a consumed partial is freed while the caller still holds its handle. It fails on the parent commit.

## Accuracy Tests

B200, `--tp-size 2 --dp-size 2 --enable-dp-attention`, `python -m sglang.benchmark.one_batch --correctness-test`: the printed prefill logits and all three generations are identical to the parent commit for Qwen3-0.6B and for Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Prefill CUDA graph capture memory, same B200 configuration (58 capture shapes, 4–8192 tokens):

| Tree | Capture memory |
|---|---|
| Before the refactor (`6582425854`) | 1124.0 MiB |
| Parent of this PR (`f731e82f09`) | 1186.0 MiB |
| This PR | 1124.0 MiB |

Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B, same flags: 2.51 GB on the parent (the same on a repeat run), 2.26 GB with this PR, 2.26 GB before the refactor.

For Qwen3-0.6B the graph pool size after every shape equals the pre-refactor tree. Kernels and collectives are unchanged, so no latency run was made.

title: [Fix] Reduce the Sarvam dense MLP through its row-parallel projection
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #41779
* #41778
* #41754
* #41753
* __->__ #41752
* #41751
* #41750
* #41749

## Motivation

The dense MLP of `SarvamMoEMLADecoderLayer` is built with `reduce_results=False`, and the decoder then all-reduces its output over the TP group whenever attention TP is larger than one and the FFN exit published neither skip flag. That gate tests the wrong group:

- Under attention DP with attention TP 1, the dense MLP still spans the full TP group. When the exit completes the output in this layer (for example with EAGLE, or a padding mode without reduce-scatter), the output is never summed.
- With `moe_dense_tp_size=1`, the dense MLP runs on each rank's own rows and owes no sum, but with attention TP > 1 the decoder sums rows that belong to different tokens.

## Modifications

- Build the dense MLP's projection with the default `reduce_results=True`, as BailingMoE does. `RowParallelLinear` reduces over the MLP's own group and skips the reduction exactly when the exit publishes a flag.
- Remove the decoder's own all-reduce.

## Accuracy Tests

B200, `sarvamai/sarvam-105b` cut to its first four layers (layer 0 dense, layers 1–3 MoE) in bf16, `python -m sglang.benchmark.one_batch --correctness-test`. Four layers do not produce meaningful text, so logits and tokens are compared. For scale, the TP2 and TP4 references differ by at most 0.09 in the printed logits.

- `--tp-size 2` and `--tp-size 4`: identical to the parent commit.
- Attention TP 1 with the sum completed in the layer (`--tp-size 4 --dp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention --ep-size 2`, eager prefill, triton attention): the parent never reduces the dense MLP output. Against the `--tp-size 4 --ep-size 2` reference, the parent differs by up to 4.25 in the logits and generates different tokens; this PR differs by 0.03 and generates the same tokens.
- `--tp-size 4 --dp-size 2 --enable-dp-attention --moe-dense-tp-size 1` (batch size 2): the parent all-reduces the dense MLP output over the four-rank TP group, adding rows of different tokens. This PR runs no such reduction, and its output matches `--dp-size 4` with the same dense setting (within 0.05). This configuration still differs from the TP4 reference for another reason that this PR does not change: under `--moe-dense-tp-size 1` the MoE layers' shared experts are also built with TP size 1 and then summed over the TP group.
- `--tp-size 2 --dp-size 2 --enable-dp-attention` and `--tp-size 4 --dp-size 2 --enable-dp-attention`: identical to the parent, and close to the reference. There the sum is left to a later step.

97 affected unit test files pass.

Not applicable: in the configurations that were already correct, the same all-reduce runs.

title: [Fix] Step-3.5: build the shared expert without TP under all-to-all MoE backends
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #41779
* #41778
* __->__ #41754
* #41753
* #41752
* #41751
* #41750
* #41749

## Motivation

Step-3.5 adds the outputs of its routed experts and its shared expert, then runs one TP all-reduce on the sum. That is correct when both parts are TP partial sums. Under DeepEP, fuseep and the other all-to-all MoE backends, the combine already returns each token's routed output in full, on the rank that owns the token, but the shared expert stayed TP-sharded:

- The all-reduce summed the complete routed output again, so it was counted TP times.
- The shared expert's partial sums were computed on the tokens each rank holds, so the all-reduce added outputs of different tokens.

DeepSeek-V2 and GLM-4-MoE avoid both by building the shared expert with TP size 1 under these backends.

## Modifications

- Build `share_expert` with `tp_size=1` under the backends GLM-4-MoE uses for this: DeepEP, Mooncake, NIXL, MORI, Ascend fuseep, the FlashInfer and FlashInfer MegaMoE all-to-all, and the FlashInfer CUTLASS FP4 all-gather.
- `Step3p5MoEMLP` takes the shared expert's output and adds it in place, without allocating a third tensor: into the routed output before `reduce_moe_output()` on the TP path; on the DeepEP path, where nothing is left to sum, the combined routed output is added into the shared expert's output.
- The decoder no longer forces the MoE block to skip its reduction and then all-reduces by hand. The FFN exit's flags reach `reduce_moe_output()` as for the other MoE models.

## Accuracy Tests

H200, `stepfun-ai/Step-3.5-Flash` cut to its first five layers (three dense, two MoE):

- `--tp-size 2`, `python -m sglang.benchmark.one_batch --correctness-test`: identical to the parent commit, and to a second run of the parent.
- `--tp-size 4`, greedy `sglang.Engine` runs with per-step logits: all 99 steps bitwise identical to the parent.
- `--tp-size 4 --ep-size 4 --moe-a2a-backend deepep --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm`, against the TP4 run as the reference. The DeepEP forward does not apply `moe_router_scaling_factor` (3.0 here), which this PR does not change, so the comparison also applies it with a test hook in both trees:
  - This PR: max |Δlogit| 0.17 (logits up to 9.2), all 99 argmax steps agree.
  - Parent: max |Δlogit| 8.09, and the first generated token differs for all three prompts.
  - This PR without the hook: max |Δlogit| 1.36, all 99 argmax steps agree; the remaining difference is the missing scaling factor.
- 109 affected unit test files (2,697 tests) pass at the top of this stack, the same as on `main`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Without an all-to-all backend the same kernels and collectives run. Under the all-to-all backends each rank now runs the whole shared expert on its own tokens instead of a TP shard of it on the same tokens, as in DeepSeek-V2 and GLM-4-MoE; no latency run was made.
