title: fix: route Thor SM110 FP8 and ModelOpt NVFP4 auto backends
author: janbernloehr
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #41764.

On NVIDIA Thor (SM110), SGLang's automatic backend choices prevent Qwen3.6-35B-A3B server startup:

- FP8 enters DeepGEMM JIT warmup and fails with `/deepgemm/csrc/apis/gemm.hpp:220: Unsupported architecture`.
- ModelOpt NVFP4 MoE enters the TensorRT-LLM path and fails with `AttributeError: 'FusedMoE' object has no attribute 'g1_scale_c'`.

Both failures reproduced on SGLang `g79cafec01` with the backend flags left at `auto`. These jobs already selected FlashInfer attention; this patch addresses the remaining GEMM and MoE routing failures, separate from the earlier attention restriction in [#35080](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/35080).

## Modifications

- Add an SM110 platform probe requiring CUDA 12.8 or newer.
- Route automatic FP8 GEMM selection on SM110 to Triton instead of DeepGEMM. Preserve explicit backend choices and the existing SM120 CUTLASS route.
- Route automatic ModelOpt FP4 MoE selection on SM110 to `flashinfer_cutlass`, extending the existing SM120 rule. Preserve explicit backend choices and other quantization schemes.
- Add CPU regression tests for the platform probe and the automatic/explicit routing boundaries.

Implementation: [`janbernloehr:fix/sm110-auto-backend-routing`](https://github.com/janbernloehr/sglang/tree/fix/sm110-auto-backend-routing), commit [`8fdf1be4e8c706c849085f0085671f7a31efaac9`](https://github.com/janbernloehr/sglang/commit/8fdf1be4e8c706c849085f0085671f7a31efaac9).

## Accuracy Tests

The Thor validation image applied the four production routing edits from the linked commit to installed SGLang `g79cafec01`, retaining its matching Rust TreeCore extension. All three single-GPU Thor accuracy workloads completed successfully with automatic backend selection. Recorded `gsm8k_10perc` scores (132 examples):

| Model variant | Score | Correct |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3.5-27B FP8 | 0.795455 | 105/132 |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B FP8 | 0.454545 | 60/132 |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B NVFP4 | 0.151515 | 20/132 |

An earlier prototype containing the same SM110 GEMM/MoE routing plus a subsequently retired attention override also completed its accuracy pipeline (4/4 jobs) at SGLang `g06008c170`. Its Thor scores were 0.795455 (105/132) for Qwen3.5-27B FP8, 0.515152 (68/132) for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B FP8, and 0.121212 (16/132) for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B NVFP4. These are separate validation runs on different SGLang revisions, not an accuracy A/B comparison.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Both Qwen3.6-35B-A3B throughput workloads completed on the Thor validation image with the standard `auto` backend selections. Recorded average output-token throughput at concurrency 1:

| Model variant | ISL 2,000 / OSL 128 | ISL 2,000 / OSL 1,000, 32,000-token prefix |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| FP8 | 48.974 tokens/s | 43.575 tokens/s |
| NVFP4 | 60.789 tokens/s | 54.146 tokens/s |

For an earlier controlled A/B at SGLang `g0f6761b54`, the unpatched Thor pipeline failed at startup, while the prototype containing this routing change and the now-retired attention override passed 3/3 jobs. The patched prototype recorded 48.362 and 31.309 tokens/s for FP8, and 60.572 and 43.253 tokens/s for NVFP4, for the same two benchmark shapes above. A second patched pipeline at SGLang `g582389cec` also passed 3/3 jobs.

## Checklist

- [x] The linked commit includes CPU regression coverage for SM110 detection, FP8 and ModelOpt FP4 automatic routing, and preservation of explicit backend choices.
- [x] The Thor image build passed the fork regression suite (3/3) and installed-package routing checks (3/3).
- [x] Python 3.12 `compileall` passed for all five changed files; targeted Ruff checks (`F401,F821,F823,UP037`), the new test file's Ruff formatting check, and `git diff --check` passed.
- [x] Thor accuracy and speed results are reported above.
- [x] No documentation change is needed for this automatic backend-selection correction.

title: [Fix] multimodal: Keep every image, video and audio of a request when n > 1
author: sohom-cs
body:
## Motivation

A single request with more than one image, video or audio breaks when `n > 1`:

```python
GenerateReqInput(text="Compare these", image_data=["a.png", "b.png"], sampling_params={"n": 2})
# normalize_batch_and_arguments() -> ValueError: The length of image_data should be equal to the batch size.
```

The same happens on `/v1/chat/completions` with two `image_url` parts and `n=2`: a 400 error, while `n=1` works. For video and audio nothing is raised, but each sample only gets the **first** item (`obj[0].video_data == "v1"`), so the model answers about one video.

Cause: with `n > 1`, `_handle_parallel_sampling` turns a single request into a batch of one and wraps `text` / `input_ids` / `input_embeds`, but not the media fields. The batch helpers then read the request's flat media list as one entry per request. This is the same issue #7830 fixed for `input_embeds`.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py`: when the single request is converted to a batch, also wrap a non-empty flat list in `image_data`, `video_data`, `audio_data`, `mm_hashes` and `mm_content_hashes`. A list already given as one entry per request (`[["a.png", "b.png"]]`), a single non-list item and an empty list keep their current paths, so those requests and `n = 1` are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: request normalization only.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the pre-commit hooks.
- [x] Add unit tests: `test_parallel_sampling_keeps_every_media_item_of_a_single_request` in `test/registered/unit/managers/test_io_struct.py`. For images, videos and audios (and `mm_hashes` alignment), `req[0]` must carry both items. It fails on `main` (a `ValueError` for images and hashes, `'m1' != ['m1', 'm2']` for video and audio) and passes with the fix. `test_parallel_sampling_keeps_media_already_nested_per_request` checks that media and hashes already nested per request (`[["m1", "m2"]]`) are not wrapped again; it passes on `main` and with the fix.

  `pytest test/registered/unit/{managers,observability,utils,disaggregation,entrypoints/openai}` gives 2085 passed on this branch vs 2084 on `main`, with an identical set of failures on both (my CPU-only environment has no GPU or HF access).
- [ ] Update documentation (no user-facing change beyond the fix).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

Related: #41546 (open) edits the same `_handle_parallel_sampling` for input validation and LoRA metadata, but doesn't touch the media fields, so the two don't overlap in behavior; whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

cc @mickqian, who added the `mm_hashes` normalization.

title: [Fix] dp-controller: Keep one input_embeds request from killing a DP server under total_tokens
author: sohom-cs
body:
## Motivation

With `--dp-size > 1` and `--load-balance-method total_tokens`, a single `/generate` request that passes `input_embeds` takes the whole server down. Such a request carries `input_ids=None`, so `len(req.input_ids)` in `total_tokens_scheduler` raises `TypeError`. The exception escapes the DP controller's `event_loop`, `run_data_parallel_controller_process` sends SIGQUIT to the parent, and every in-flight request is lost. `input_embeds` is a documented `/generate` field, so an ordinary client can hit this.

## Modifications

`total_tokens_scheduler` sizes an `input_embeds` request by its number of embedding rows, which is how the scheduler sizes it too.

An earlier version of this PR also dispatched PD requests without `bootstrap_room` round-robin instead of asserting. Reaching that path needs a client that bypasses the router, so I dropped it and kept the assert. Other exceptions in the controller still take the server down; a general reject path would need a socket back to every frontend, so this PR fixes only this trigger.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A: request dispatch only.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A: no change for requests with `input_ids`.

- [x] Format your code according to the pre-commit hooks.
- [x] Add unit tests: `test_input_embeds_request_is_counted_by_embedding_rows` in `test/registered/unit/managers/test_data_parallel_controller.py`. On main it fails with `TypeError: object of type 'NoneType' has no len()`; with the change the file passes.

title: [Fix] Restore deferred layer dumps and pin SentencePiece for InternVL
author: Fridge003
body:
## Motivation

Two NVIDIA nightly failures in [release validation run 36541308424](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36541308424) have reproducible causes:

- Deferred layer outputs introduced by #41196 are wrappers rather than tensors. The non-intrusive dumper ignores them, so the precision test fails with `no non-initial transformer layer input dumps found`. Current main also uses `OwedOutput`.
- An unpinned SentencePiece dependency lets the environment select 0.2.2, which rejects a null piece in the InternVL2.5 tokenizer vocabulary. Transformers swallows that tokenizer exception and falls back to `CLIPImageProcessor`, producing the misleading missing-`tokenizer` error.

## Modifications

- Dump `UnreducedOutput.partial` and `OwedOutput.contribution.value` under the existing tensor names without reducing, finalizing, or consuming the residual stream. Opaque and consumed outputs with no tensor remain omitted.
- Pin `sentencepiece==0.2.1` consistently in all five Python package manifests.
- Keep InternVL in the existing `test_vlms_mmmu_eval.py` suite and register its estimated duration as 3600 seconds so `/rerun-test` accepts it. The server launch timeout remains unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

- [InternVL MMMU evaluation](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36647841240): passed on `db54619074`, using the same 100 samples and accuracy/latency thresholds as the existing suite. This validation used a temporary standalone entry; the final patch retains the original combined suite.
- [CPU dumper regression](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36647444423): passed on `c7a576d85c`. The temporary regression test is not included in the final patch.
- [H200 precision test](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36647456280): progressed past the missing layer-input dump failure, but the overall run failed on `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8`, tensor `non_intrusive__model.layers.56.self_attn.inputs.hidden_states`, relative difference `0.0010324691814137532`. This run is not a full precision pass.
- Cached InternVL tokenizer verification: changing only SentencePiece from 0.2.2 to 0.2.1 restores `InternLM2Tokenizer` loading and encoding `hello` as `[1, 15115]`.
- Changed-file pre-commit hooks pass for the final test changes. Production fixes are unchanged from the tested commits.

No inference kernels or model computations are changed. The dumper change only affects enabled non-intrusive dumping.

title: [Fix] Emit Responses reasoning content-part events
author: ai-jz
body:
## Motivation

While testing SGLang with [DeepSeek Provider Verifier](https://github.com/smg-project/deepseek-provider-verifier), we found that non-Harmony Responses streams emit `response.reasoning_text.delta/done` without the corresponding `response.content_part.added/done` events. The final reasoning content is present, but clients consuming the content-part lifecycle receive no opening or closing event for that content.

This follows the [OpenAI SDK maintainer's clarification](https://github.com/openai/openai-python/issues/2634#issuecomment-5683978987): reasoning text uses `response.content_part.added/done` with `part.type="reasoning_text"`. SGLang's pinned `openai==2.6.1` already supports these event types.

## Modifications

Add the two missing events to the existing non-Harmony, non-summary reasoning path:

```diff
 response.output_item.added
+response.content_part.added
 response.reasoning_text.delta
 response.reasoning_text.done
+response.content_part.done
 response.output_item.done
```

The closing part comes from the finalized reasoning item, with the same item ID and indexes as its deltas. Regression tests cover completed, truncated, and aborted streams, matching terminal output, event sequence numbers, and the existing summary event path.

The production change is 23 added lines. It adds no configuration or dependency and leaves Chat Completions, Harmony, and reasoning-summary emission unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

CPU tests against base `cae69be584b8fc2daf0b03ec552710592f8738cb`, using Python 3.12.3 and `openai==2.6.1`. The baseline run applies only the new tests; the fixed run also applies the production change.

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Minimal reproduction below | Assertion failure: missing content-part events | Pass; reasoning content remains `work` |
| New lifecycle regression | All three subtests fail: completed / incomplete / failed | All three pass |
| Full `test_serving_responses_stream.py` | 16 tests run; only the lifecycle test fails | 16 tests pass, including summary, Harmony, and tool-call regressions |
| Native pre-commit hooks on both changed files | — | Pass |
| Hosted [Lint workflow](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36650762569) | — | Pass, including repository-wide pre-commit and documentation checks |

Run the regression file from the repository root in a SGLang development environment:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 SGLANG_TEST_MAX_RETRY=0 PYTHONPATH=python \
  python test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_responses_stream.py -v
```

<details>
<summary>Minimal reproduction: no GPU, model weights, API key, or running server required</summary>

Run from the repository root with SGLang's development dependencies installed. This uses the existing CPU fixtures to feed synthetic engine output through the real reasoning parser and Responses SSE generator. The same script runs on the base revision and this branch.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 SGLANG_TEST_MAX_RETRY=0 PYTHONPATH=python python - <<'PY'
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai")
from utils import StreamFixture, engine_chunk, event_payloads, make_serving
from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import ResponsesRequest

serving = make_serving()
serving.reasoning_parser = "deepseek-v41"
serving.tool_call_parser = None
request = ResponsesRequest(model="x", input="hi", stream=True, store=False)
events = StreamFixture(serving, request, require_reasoning=True).run(
    [engine_chunk("<think>work</think>answer", 4, finish=True)]
)
payloads = event_payloads(events)
reasoning = payloads[-1]["response"]["output"][0]
types = [
    p["type"] for p in payloads
    if p.get("item_id") == reasoning["id"]
    or p.get("item", {}).get("id") == reasoning["id"]
]
print("\n".join(types), flush=True)
print("Final reasoning content:", reasoning["content"], flush=True)
assert "response.content_part.added" in types
assert "response.content_part.done" in types
PY
```

Before the fix, the output contains only the four unprefixed events in the diff above, followed by an assertion failure. After the fix, it contains all six events and exits successfully. Both runs print:

```text
Final reasoning content: [{'text': 'work', 'type': 'reasoning_text'}]
```

</details>

These are serving-layer protocol tests. No model accuracy benchmark or GPU inference was run for this isolated PR.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run. This adds two SSE metadata events per emitted reasoning item; it does not change model execution or scheduling.

- [x] Add unit tests using the existing registered CPU test suite.

- Documentation: N/A; no new user-facing option.

title: [Fix] Read TensorCast's WORLD placement under its current names
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #41818

## Motivation

When no placement is passed in, the TensorCast host allocator reads `get_parallel().world_rank` and `get_parallel().world_size`. Those names had already been split into `launch_world_rank` / `launch_world_size` when the backend landed, so both production paths (`TensorcastStore.__init__` and `get_tensorcast_host_allocator_from_runtime`) raise `AttributeError`. The package's own TensorCast tests miss this: they replace `get_parallel` with a namespace that carries the old names.

## Modifications

- Read `launch_world_rank` / `launch_world_size`, and give the in-package test stubs the same names.
- Add a census to `test_runtime_context.py`: every `get_parallel().<name>` read in the package, direct or through a name bound to the context, must name a declared parallel field. The one remaining read of an undeclared name, the KV-shard control plane's enable flag (`mem_cache/page_interleave.py`, currently unreachable), is listed with its reason. The census fails once that read goes away, so the exception cannot go stale.

The engine fills `CacheConfig.moe_dp_size` with `get_moe_cp_size()`, the width of the MoE communicator. title: [Fix] Shard MoE WNA16 and Quark INT4-FP8 weights by the MoE placement
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #41818
* #41817
* #41816
* #41815
* #41814
* #41813
* #41812
* #41811
* #41810
* #41809
* #41808
* __->__ #41807
* #41806
* #41805

## Motivation

Both loaders split expert weights into `moe_tp_size` shards of `intermediate_size_per_partition`, but pick the shard with the full TP rank:
- `moe_wna16` indexes `view(layer.moe_tp_size, ...)[tp_rank]` for the qzeros;
- `quark_int4fp8_moe` narrows at `shard_size * tp_rank`.

Under EP or MoE-DP the MoE-TP width is smaller than the TP width, so every rank with `tp_rank >= moe_tp_size` indexes past the shards and fails to load.

The WNA16 qzeros have a second problem under EP. They are written outside the layer's weight loader, at the checkpoint expert id, and that id runs past the rank's `num_local_experts` slots.

## Modifications

- Both loaders shard by `layer.moe_tp_rank`, the rank the layer itself shards by. Without EP or MoE-DP it equals the TP rank, so nothing changes there.
- The WNA16 qzeros go to the local slots that the layer's own loader picks for that expert, EPLB replicas included (`_local_expert_ids`).
- Unit tests load both qzeros paths (`w13`, `w2`): under an EP layout, the shard matches the non-EP load for the same MoE-TP rank, and each EP rank writes only its own experts.

Quark's scale writes still index by the checkpoint expert id, so Quark under EP is still unsupported. That path is HIP-only and is not exercised here.

## Accuracy Tests

H200, `QuantTrio/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ --quantization moe_wna16`, GSM8K 200 questions:

| | `--tp 2` | `--tp 2 --ep-size 2` |

| parent commit | | fails at load (`IndexError`) |

title: [Fix] Size the prefill delayer's gather buffer to its TP group
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #41818
* #41817
* #41816
* #41815
* #41814
* #41813
* #41812
* #41811
* #41810
* __->__ #41809
* #41808
* #41807
* #41806
* #41805

## Motivation

The prefill delayer all-gathers one info row per rank over the TP group, but sizes the receive buffer `(dp, attn_tp_size, 5)`. The TP group is `dp * attn_cp_size * attn_tp_size` wide. With attention context parallelism the buffer is `attn_cp_size` times too small, and the first gather takes the scheduler down.

## Modifications

- Size the buffer `(dp, attn_cp_size * attn_tp_size, 5)`, the layout the MLP sync batch info uses. `[:, 0, :]` still selects the first rank of each DP group. Without attention CP the shape is unchanged.
- `test_prefill_delayer_gather.py` runs `_gather_info` against an all-gather that enforces what `all_gather_into_tensor` does (the output holds one input per rank of the TP group). It checks that each DP group's first rank comes back across TP, attention CP, DP attention, and DP attention with attention CP.

## Accuracy Tests

H200, Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8, `--tp-size 4 --moe-dp-size 1 --ep-size 4 --attn-cp-size 2 --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy zigzag --cuda-graph-backend-prefill=disabled`, GSM8K 200 questions:

title: [Fix] Make the Solar model constructible and runnable
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #41818
* #41817
* #41816
* #41815
* #41814
* #41813
* #41812
* #41811
* __->__ #41810
* #41809
* #41808
* #41807
* #41806
* #41805

## Motivation

`SolarForCausalLM` cannot be built or run:

- `SolarModel` calls `make_layers` without the pipeline position. In that case `make_layers` returns only the layer list, which is then unpacked as `(start_layer, end_layer, layers)`, so construction fails with `too many values to unpack`.
- The forward passes call `self.pp_group()`, which is a group rather than a function. The causal-LM forward also drops `pp_proxy_tensors`, so a later pipeline stage would never receive the previous stage's hidden states.
- The logits processor is built and called with another framework's signatures: `LogitsProcessor(vocab_size, org_vocab_size, logit_scale)` and `(lm_head, hidden_states, forward_batch)`.

## Modifications

- Build the layers of this pipeline stage and read `self.pp_group` as an attribute.
- Pass `pp_proxy_tensors` through `SolarForCausalLM.forward`.
- Build and call the logits processor the way other models do. Under `--enable-dp-lm-head`, the LM head sits on the attention-TP group, as the processor expects.
- Solar's backbone skip connections mix hidden states saved at an earlier layer into a later one. A pipeline split that puts the two on different stages is now rejected at construction, naming the layer. `test_solar_pipeline_split.py` checks this against the checkpoint's skip layout: PP 1 and 2 are accepted, PP 4 is rejected.

## Accuracy Tests

H200, `upstage/solar-pro-preview-instruct` (`--trust-remote-code`), GSM8K 200 questions:

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `--tp-size 2` | fails at construction | 0.905 |
| `--tp-size 2 --pp-size 2` | | 0.895; greedy output identical to TP2 on 4 prompts × 64 tokens |
| `--pp-size 4` | | rejected: layers 16 and 48 read skip states saved on the previous stage |

title: [Fix] Stop the namespace census at the leaf a read names
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

`test_the_readers_agree_with_the_namespace_metadata` checks every `get_<bag>()...` read in `srt` against the namespace metadata. It took the last attribute of each chain as the leaf and everything before it as the namespace. So a chain that reads a value and then one of that value's attributes was misread: `get_parallel().tp_group.device` was reported as a `device` leaf under a `parallel.tp_group` namespace, although `tp_group` is a process group and `device` is its attribute.

## Modifications

- The scan (`_config_reads`) follows only the sub-namespaces a chain names, such as `get_exec().moe`, and checks the first other name, which is the leaf. Attributes past the leaf belong to its value and are not checked.
- `test_the_scan_reads_the_leaf_a_chain_names` pins both sides:
  - correct reads pass: `get_exec().moe.moe_a2a_backend`, `get_parallel().config.tp_size`, `get_parallel().tp_group.device`;
  - wrong reads are reported: `get_exec().moe_a2a_backend` (skips the `moe` sub-namespace), `get_exec().moe.chunked_prefill_size` and `get_schedule().device` (leaves of another bag).

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: test-only change.

- On `main`, the scan checks about 2,800 reads, 565 of them through a sub-namespace, and none disagree. The test file passes (5 tests).
- On a tree containing `device = get_parallel().tp_group.device`, the old scan fails and the new one passes.
- Replacing one real `get_exec().moe.moe_a2a_backend` read with `get_exec().moe_a2a_backend` makes the new scan fail, naming that line.

title: [Fix] MiniMax-M3: default to the breakable prefill CUDA graph
author: thanhhao98
body:
## Motivation

MiniMax-M3 defaults to the `tc_piecewise` prefill CUDA graph, and on main that launch dies at boot (reproduced on `nightly-dev-cu13-20261005-f70e8c68`, GB300 TP4):

```
Capture prefill CUDA graph failed: Unsupported object.__new__ user-defined class construction
  ... object.__new__(DeclaredSum) is not safe
```

`tc_piecewise` is being removed (#41634), so this PR moves M3 to `breakable`. That needed one fix: under `breakable`, `RadixAttention` ran M3's sparse attention inline instead of as an eager break, so the graph replayed the capture batch's metadata and the server died on its first requests with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`.

## Modifications

- Run sparse attention as an eager break under `breakable`, like dense attention and like DSA's indexer and QSA (#41729).
- Add both M3 archs to the breakable allowlist, so M3 defaults to `breakable`.
- A routing test fails without the fix.

## Accuracy Tests

End to end on GB300, MiniMax-M3-NVFP4: this PR at its default (`breakable`) vs main with the prefill graph disabled, each pair on one node.

| config | GSM8K 1319 q, this PR | GSM8K 1319 q, main without prefill graph |
|---|---|---|
| TP4 | 0.870 | 0.864 |
| TP4, EP4, DP attention 4 | 0.864 | 0.877 |

Across our other runs (two nightlies, with and without DP attention), both settings stay within 0.864-0.877. Image requests replay the graph too: a colored-shape probe (nine images, sent one at a time and all at once) answers 18/18 in every arm. Every arm also passes a bs=1 GSM8K canary and an EOS-termination check.

## Speed Tests

Same pairs, ISL 8192 / OSL 1024, median TTFT and output throughput:

| config | concurrency | TTFT (ms), this PR / main | tok/s, this PR / main |
|---|---|---|---|
| TP4 | 1 | **181** / 232 | 205 / 203 |
| TP4 | 16 | 1502 / 1505 | 1441 / 1429 |
| TP4 | 64 | **4868** / 4946 | 2838 / 2812 |
| TP4, EP4, DP attention 4 | 1 | 505 / **438** | 112 / 112 |
| TP4, EP4, DP attention 4 | 64 | **4313** / 4670 | **2854** / 2699 |

With DP attention the graph makes every DP rank replay a shared MAX_LEN bucket, so at concurrency 1 the idle ranks run the busy rank's length. TPOT is unchanged except DP attention at concurrency 64 (19.13 to 18.15 ms).

## Reproduce

Container `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261005-f70e8c68` with `python/sglang` at this PR's head (baseline: main `efb62ce269`), checkpoint `nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4`, one 4-GPU GB300 node.

```bash
# This PR (breakable is the default). Baseline: the same command on main plus --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled.
# DP-attention rows add: --ep-size 4 --enable-dp-attention --dp-size 4
SGLANG_DISABLE_MSA=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 --trust-remote-code \
  --tp 4 --context-length 1048576 --reasoning-parser auto --tool-call-parser auto --port 30000

# GSM8K: 5-shot, temperature 0, 128 in parallel. The bs=1 canary runs --num-questions 40 with --parallel 1 and with --parallel 40.
python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-shots 5 --num-questions 1319 --port 30000

# Speed: --num-prompts 12 / 64 / 256 for --max-concurrency 1 / 16 / 64.
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1.0 \
  --flush-cache --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 12
```

title: [Fix] scheduler: stop latching batch_is_full when nothing can run
author: he-yufeng
body:
Fixes #41841.

## Problem

When a prefill round ends in `AddReqResult.NO_TOKEN` with an empty running batch and an empty `can_run_list`, the plain path set `running_batch.batch_is_full = True` unconditionally. `batch_is_full` is only cleared on the decode path (`update_running_batch`, the last-batch merge, retract), and an empty batch never reaches decode. So once the pool momentarily ran dry on an otherwise idle engine, the flag stuck and every later `_get_new_batch_prefill_raw` call bailed at the `batch_is_full` gate. From the outside the server stops prefilling: requests sit in the waiting queue forever even after memory frees up again.

The hicache / lmcache / unified branches right next to it already guard this latch with "only when something can actually be served". An empty batch has no such guarantee, so the guard now applies to every NO_TOKEN outcome.

## Fix

Drop the unconditional `= True` branch and use the guarded form for all NO_TOKEN results:

```python
running_batch.batch_is_full = len(adder.can_run_list) > 0 or (
    not running_batch.is_empty()
)
```

Behavior only changes in the empty + nothing-admitted case (True -> False). When work exists the flag still latches, and decode clears it as before.

NO_TOKEN is not the only site that latches an empty batch: the no-free-slot checks (`get_num_allocatable_reqs(...) <= 0`, before and inside the admission loop) set the flag the same way, for example when streaming sessions hold the request slots. So `_get_new_batch_prefill_raw` also clears the flag at the read site when the running batch is empty, which covers every set site on this path.

## Test

`test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_batch_is_full_latch.py`: an empty running batch with `batch_is_full` already set still reaches admission, and the flag is cleared. It does not depend on which site set the flag, so it covers the NO_TOKEN and no-free-slot latches alike. It fails without the read-site clear and passes with it.

Full `test/registered/unit/managers/` suite: 825 passed; the 9 remaining failures are pre-existing macOS environment issues in the mm/shm/snapshot tests, identical with and without this change (verified via stash comparison). The changed logic is pure admission bookkeeping, exercised here by CPU unit tests; happy to add more if reviewers want e2e coverage.

title: [Fix] hicache: Key MLA Mamba state per TP rank in the file backend
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

MLA shares KV storage keys across TP ranks, but Mamba checkpoints are sharded. Give file-backend Mamba keys a TP rank/size suffix so one rank cannot overwrite another rank's checkpoint. Keep existing keys for other pools. Same fix as #43594 for NIXL; SeaweedFS and HF3FS have the same bug and are fixed in #43816 and #43817.

## Modifications

- `HiCacheFile._get_suffixed_key` gives Mamba component keys (`<key>.mamba`) the TP rank/size suffix (`tp_config_suffix`); other pools keep their existing keys. Public `get/set/exists` signatures are unchanged.
- `LRUFileEvictor` takes `owned_suffixes` instead of MLA flags: every rank owns its TP-sharded files, and MLA rank 0 also owns the shared files. With file eviction enabled, MLA ranks > 0 can now store their own Mamba state, while replicated KV is still created by rank 0 only.
- On MLA models `max_size` now applies per rank to that rank's own files, as it already did on non-MLA models, so a shared directory can exceed one cap.

Old unranked Mamba files are not reused because their owning rank is ambiguous; rank 0 owns them and evicts them through LRU.

## Validation

- GLM-5.3-Flash TP4 with file L3, L3-only restore of a 16K prefix: 408/544 wrong-rank Mamba payloads on main, 544/544 correct with per-rank keys (earlier revision of this patch; key format unchanged since).
- New unit tests (two-rank Mamba round trip, MLA rank 1 creating its own Mamba file under eviction) fail on main and pass with this PR; the file-backend unit test modules pass.

title: [Fix] Make tokenizer request-state initialization atomic
author: C1ves
body:
## Motivation

`TokenizerManager._init_req_state` inserts one `ReqState` into `rid_to_state` per
(sub-)request, but the duplicate-rid guard (`raise ValueError("Duplicate request ID
detected")`) sits *inside* the insert loop, and `_init_req_state` is called *before*
the `try/except BaseException -> _release_req_states_on_failure` cleanup block in
`generate_request`. When a batch request's rid list collides with an in-flight rid at
position k, the states for items 0..k-1 have already been inserted and are never
removed: the request fails with 400, but the leaked rids stay in `rid_to_state`
forever — every later reuse fails with "Duplicate request ID", and each leaked state
holds an `asyncio.Event` plus the sub-request object.

A client fully controls the rid list, so each crafted batch (N fresh rids + 1
colliding rid) permanently leaks N-1 states; repeating this grows the tokenizer
process memory without bound and progressively poisons the rid namespace.
(Within-batch duplicates are already rejected at normalization in `io_struct.py`;
this hole is collisions with rids already in `rid_to_state`.)

Reproduced on the official `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.20` image, default flags, no auth:

1. Long in-flight request with `rid="victim2"`, then batch
   `{"rid": ["leak-y1", "leak-y2", "victim2"], ...}` -> 400 `Duplicate request ID
   detected: victim2`.
2. Fresh request with `rid="leak-y1"` -> 400 `Duplicate request ID detected:
   leak-y1` (the rid never ran, yet is permanently occupied).
3. A fresh rid still returns 200.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py`: in `_init_req_state`, check all
  rids for duplicates before inserting any state. No behavior change for valid
  requests; the duplicate error message is unchanged.
- `test/registered/unit/managers/test_init_req_state_duplicate_rid.py` (CPU):
  - duplicate at tail of batch -> raises, earlier states not leaked (fails before
    this fix);
  - all-unique batch registers all states;
  - single-request duplicate raises and preserves the existing state.

`pre-commit run` passes on the changed files.

title: [XPU] Fix test_qsa_indexer_xpu after defer_expansion change
author: arathi-hlab
body:
#40972 made `QSAIndexer._forward_impl` pass `defer_expansion=` to `select_decode_tokens`. It updated the fake `_DispatchIndexer` in the CUDA test (`test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/qsa/test_qsa.py`), but not the XPU copy in `test/registered/xpu/test_qsa_indexer_xpu.py`. Since then, XPU stage-a fails on every PR that reaches this test:

```
TypeError: _DispatchIndexer.select_decode_tokens() got an unexpected keyword argument 'defer_expansion'
```

The failure is a TypeError, which the CI retry logic treats as non-retriable, so the job fails straight away.

## Change

Give the XPU fake the same signature as the CUDA one: `select_decode_tokens(self, *args, defer_expansion=False)`.

## Tests

- pre-commit passes.
- XPU stage-a on this PR is the real check.

title: [Fix] sampling: Make top-k/top-p filtering consistent across sampling paths
author: alvion427
body:
Supersedes #36173 and addresses its final review findings.

## Motivation

SGLang normally computes the top-p cutoff from the original probability distribution and intersects that support with top-k. Some sampling paths instead applied top-k, renormalized the remaining probabilities, and then applied top-p. That applies top-p to whatever probability mass happens to remain after top-k, making its effect unpredictable and inconsistent with other sampling paths using the same parameters.

The affected paths are the FlashInfer min-p path, the shared EAGLE-family/standalone/n-gram verifier, and the target-distribution builder shared by DFlash, DSpark, and UNO. UNO's separate compact top-k path also needed the same fix; its behavior could otherwise depend on other requests in the batch.

## Modifications

- Apply top-p before top-k in the FlashInfer min-p path.
- Apply the same ordering in the shared EAGLE-family, standalone, and n-gram verifier.
- Correct dense/sparse target distributions shared by DFlash, DSpark, and UNO.
- Preserve the sparse top-k path by translating the top-p cutoff into the renormalized top-k distribution using the top-k support's original probability mass.
- Apply the same correction to UNO's separate compact top-k path.
- Fuse CUDA unseeded top-p rescaling by reusing the retained top-k maximum, avoiding a full-vocabulary maximum reduction and exponential intermediate.
- Preserve logsumexp for seeded/non-CUDA callers; UNO rejects deterministic inference.
- Document that fused FP32 rounding can change cutoff membership, without promising bitwise identity or trainer alignment.
- Reject `min_p > 0` for built-in speculative decoding, where it is not currently applied.
- Add focused CUDA regression tests for each corrected implementation.

## Accuracy Tests

The regressions use probabilities `[0.35, 0.25, 0.20, 0.05, 0.03, ...]`, `top_k=4`, and `top_p=0.82`. The FlashInfer min-p case also uses `min_p=0.1`.

The original top-p nucleus includes token 3 because the probability mass before it is `0.80`. Applying and renormalizing top-k first changes that mass to `0.80 / 0.85`, causing token 3 to be incorrectly removed.

Validated rebased commit `50e6ca6b73cc49214b5e9e28068b187ac3d7de2f` on an NVIDIA H200 with Python 3.12.3, CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.13.0, FlashInfer 0.6.18, and Triton 3.7.1.

`TestSamplingMaskCapture` and `test_speculative_sampling.py`: **18 passed, 6 subtests passed**, no failures/errors/skips.

Each regression passed with the fix and failed with pre-fix filtering:

| Path | With fix | Before fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FlashInfer min-p | Pass | Support length 3 instead of 4 |
| EAGLE, using the production FlashInfer kernels | Pass | Token-3 probability mismatch |
| Shared target builder, dense | Pass | Token-3 probability mismatch |
| Shared target builder, sparse | Pass | Token-3 probability mismatch |
| UNO compact | Pass | Compact support probability mismatch |

The same tests exercised pre-fix filtering from public base `d2a436446cca3d955358e7b4a5bf6881ea8591cd`; EAGLE retained the extracted helper signature for testability.

Ruff 0.15.1, isort 7.0.0, syntax, whitespace, and registry checks passed. The H200 results above apply to `50e6ca6b73cc49214b5e9e28068b187ac3d7de2f`, not current-head CI.

[Base CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39500026515) passed at `f0c0a64ad1b70d9a72f9d741b9eaa2b51d088c03`; Extra/AMD had failures. CI States below tracks newer runs.

<!-- lint: profile=evidence-heavy -->

### Historical HTTP validation at `f0c0a64`

All 10 HTTP checks passed at `f0c0a64ad1b70d9a72f9d741b9eaa2b51d088c03` on H200 using `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` revision `7ae557604adf67be50417f59c2c2f167def9a775`, Transformers 5.19.0, and the runtime below.

NGRAM accepted `min_p=0`. With `min_p=0.1`, non-streaming requests returned HTTP 400; streaming requests emitted `abort`, embedded status 400, and `[DONE]`. Each rejection mode ran twice; all four following valid requests succeeded. Ordinary sampling accepted `min_p=0.1`. Both servers remained healthy before teardown. Other speculative modes and PD deployment were not exercised. Source Rust extensions used `SGLANG_RUST_BUILD_MODE=auto`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

These measurements predate fusion in `b94a95d5e805e0ee214c6d355a3a6cc79dd5e073`; see the [fused-helper validation summary](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41916#issuecomment-6328764169) for results and limitations.

Historical head `f0c0a64ad1b70d9a72f9d741b9eaa2b51d088c03` versus base `f0b65907227480afc376a66db62931b7e9c46c38`:

| Setup | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Hardware/runtime | H200; driver 595.71.05; Python 3.12.15; PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130; FlashInfer 0.7.2; Triton 3.8.0 |
| Functions | Production head functions and exact base definitions with unchanged dependencies; UNO retains `torch.compile(dynamic=True)` |
| Inputs | Seed 41916; FP32 normal logits, std=2; temperature=0.8; top-k=50; top-p=0.9; draft width=6 |
| Timing | Median microseconds/call; five alternating base/head samples; 200 CUDA Graph replays/sample; compilation and warmup excluded |
| Shape order | Vocabulary 32,768 then 128,256; batch 1, 16, 64 for each |

Outputs were finite and normalized; base/head sampling semantics intentionally differ.

| Path | Batch | Vocabulary | Base (us) | Head (us) | Added (us) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DFlash sparse | 1 | 32,768 | 79.85 | 99.50 | 19.65 |
| UNO compact | 1 | 32,768 | 28.75 | 38.01 | 9.26 |
| DFlash sparse | 16 | 32,768 | 130.29 | 158.38 | 28.09 |
| UNO compact | 16 | 32,768 | 30.45 | 48.85 | 18.40 |
| DFlash sparse | 64 | 32,768 | 373.87 | 437.04 | 63.17 |
| UNO compact | 64 | 32,768 | 61.63 | 119.92 | 58.30 |
| DFlash sparse | 1 | 128,256 | 101.42 | 139.81 | 38.40 |
| UNO compact | 1 | 128,256 | 49.55 | 70.68 | 21.13 |
| DFlash sparse | 16 | 128,256 | 320.54 | 442.95 | 122.41 |
| UNO compact | 16 | 128,256 | 59.51 | 116.82 | 57.31 |
| DFlash sparse | 64 | 128,256 | 896.05 | 1211.86 | 315.81 |
| UNO compact | 64 | 128,256 | 163.58 | 369.16 | 205.58 |

With top-p disabled at batch=16, vocabulary=128,256, DFlash measured 300.17 -> 300.31 us; UNO measured 57.71 -> 56.90 us. Costs increased 17-38% for DFlash and 32-126% for UNO in this sweep. End-to-end serving throughput and latency remain unmeasured.

`torch.profiler` CPU/CUDA traces used ten graph replays and three ordinary calls, after warmup. At batch=64, vocabulary=128,256:

| Path | Additional full-vocabulary work | Profile attribution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DFlash sparse | Eager `logsumexp`: max, subtract, exp, sum, final normalization | 9 kernels, ~350 us; ~188 MiB temporary tensor. Total kernel count: 30 -> 52. Unprofiled rerun: 886 -> 1199 us. |
| UNO compact | Compiled full-vocabulary max and exp-sum reductions | 4 kernels, ~206 us; two scans dominate. Total kernel count: 6 -> 10. Unprofiled rerun: 163 -> 369 us. |

DFlash's top-p kernel fell from ~53 to 5 us; kernel durations attribute costs but do not replace unprofiled timings.

UNO depends on shape warmup order. Starting with vocabulary=128,256 and batch 1 then 64 generated a single full-vocabulary reduction kernel (~113 us), with unprofiled timings 161 -> 275 us. Repeating the sweep restored 163 -> 369 us; the percentage is not universal.

import ast
import gc
import hashlib
import importlib.metadata
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import statistics
import subprocess
import time
from types import SimpleNamespace

import torch

from sglang.srt.speculative import dflash_utils as dflash
from sglang.srt.speculative import uno_utils as uno

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
OUT = ROOT / 'benchmark-results.json'


def source_node(path, name):
    source = Path(path).read_text()
    node = next(n for n in ast.parse(source).body if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name == name)
    return source, node


def load_base(path, names, module):
    namespace = dict(vars(module))
    source = Path(path).read_text()
    nodes = [n for n in ast.parse(source).body if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name in names]
    assert len(nodes) == len(names)
    exec(compile(ast.Module(body=nodes, type_ignores=[]), str(path), 'exec'), namespace)
    return namespace


def capture(fn):
    # Compilation and allocator warmup are outside the measured region.
    for _ in range(4):
        fn()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
        output = fn()
    for _ in range(10):
        graph.replay()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    tensors = output if isinstance(output, tuple) else (output,)
    assert all(torch.isfinite(t).all().item() for t in tensors)
    probs = tensors[-1]
    assert torch.allclose(probs.sum(-1), torch.ones_like(probs.sum(-1)), atol=2e-5, rtol=2e-5)
    return graph, output


def measure(graph, repetitions=200):
    start, end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True), torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
    start.record()
    for _ in range(repetitions):
        graph.replay()
    end.record()
    end.synchronize()
    return start.elapsed_time(end) * 1000 / repetitions


def main():
    base_dflash = load_base(ROOT / 'base_dflash_utils.py', {'build_speculative_verify_target_probs'}, dflash)
    base_uno = load_base(ROOT / 'base_uno_utils.py', {'_normalize_sparse_topk_probs', '_build_sparse_target_support_tensors'}, uno)
    for helper in ('_dflash_top_p_renorm_prob', '_dflash_top_k_renorm_prob'):
        _, before = source_node(ROOT / 'base_dflash_utils.py', helper)
        _, after = source_node(dflash.__file__, helper)
        assert ast.dump(before) == ast.dump(after), f'Dependency changed: {helper}'
    metadata = {
        'head': 'f0c0a64ad1b70d9a72f9d741b9eaa2b51d088c03',
        'base': 'f0b65907227480afc376a66db62931b7e9c46c38',
        'torch': torch.__version__, 'cuda': torch.version.cuda,
        'gpu': torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
        'driver': subprocess.check_output(['nvidia-smi', '--query-gpu=driver_version', '--format=csv,noheader'], text=True).strip(),
        'packages': {p: importlib.metadata.version(p) for p in ('flashinfer-python', 'triton', 'transformers')},
        'method': 'Production head functions, exact base function ASTs with unchanged production dependencies; UNO torch.compile(dynamic=True) retained. CUDA Graph replay, warmup and compilation excluded, 5 paired samples alternating order, 200 replays/sample. Synthetic fixed-seed float32 logits, std=2; temperature=.8; top_k=50; draft_width=6.',
        'scope': 'Sampling function microbenchmark only. No model inference or end-to-end latency claim. Base/head intentionally implement different distributions.',
        'source_sha256': {str(p.name): hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in (ROOT/'base_dflash_utils.py', ROOT/'base_uno_utils.py', Path(dflash.__file__), Path(uno.__file__), Path(__file__))},
    }
    results = []
    cases = [(b, v, True) for v in (32768, 128256) for b in (1, 16, 64)] + [(16, 128256, False)]
    for bs, vocab, enabled in cases:
        torch.manual_seed(41916)
        width, k = 6, 50
        logits = torch.randn(bs * width, vocab, device='cuda', dtype=torch.float32) * 2
        temperatures = torch.full((bs, 1), .8, device='cuda')
        top_ks = torch.full((bs,), k, device='cuda', dtype=torch.int32)
        top_ps = torch.full((bs,), .9 if enabled else 1.0, device='cuda')
        info = SimpleNamespace(temperatures=temperatures, top_ks=top_ks, top_ps=top_ps, need_top_k_sampling=True, need_top_p_sampling=enabled)
        for path in ('dflash_sparse', 'uno_compact'):
            print(json.dumps({'starting': path, 'batch': bs, 'vocab': vocab, 'top_p_enabled': enabled}), flush=True)
            if path == 'dflash_sparse':
                args = dict(next_token_logits=logits, sampling_info=info, draft_token_num=width, bs=bs, max_top_k=k, uniform_top_k_value=k, use_sparse_topk=True)
                before = lambda: base_dflash['build_speculative_verify_target_probs'](**args)
                after = lambda: dflash.build_speculative_verify_target_probs(**args)
            else:
                args = (logits, temperatures, top_ks, top_ps, bs, width, k)
                before = lambda: base_uno['_build_sparse_target_support_tensors'](*args)
                after = lambda: uno._build_sparse_target_support_tensors(logits, temperatures, top_ks, top_ps if enabled else None, bs, width, k)
            bg, bo = capture(before)
            hg, ho = capture(after)
            samples = {'base': [], 'head': []}
            for round_id in range(5):
                pairs = [('base', bg), ('head', hg)] if round_id % 2 == 0 else [('head', hg), ('base', bg)]
                for label, graph in pairs:
                    samples[label].append(measure(graph))
            bm, hm = statistics.median(samples['base']), statistics.median(samples['head'])
            row = dict(path=path, batch=bs, vocab=vocab, top_p_enabled=enabled, base_us=bm, head_us=hm, delta_us=hm-bm, ratio=hm/bm, samples_us=samples)
            results.append(row)
            OUT.write_text(json.dumps({'metadata': metadata, 'results': results}, indent=2)+'\n')
            print(json.dumps(row), flush=True)
            del bg, bo, hg, ho, before, after
            gc.collect()
            torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    print('BENCHMARK_COMPLETE', flush=True)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

cat > check_min_p_http.py <<'PR41916_PYTHON'
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import time

import psutil
import requests

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
BASE_URL = 'http://127.0.0.1:31916'
RESULT = {'head': 'f0c0a64ad1b70d9a72f9d741b9eaa2b51d088c03', 'model': json.loads((ROOT/'model.json').read_text()), 'checks': [], 'launches': []}


def save():
    (ROOT/'http-results.json').write_text(json.dumps(RESULT, indent=2)+'\n')


def request(min_p, stream, expected_rejection, label):
    payload = {'text': 'The capital of France is', 'sampling_params': {'temperature': .7, 'top_k': 50, 'top_p': .9, 'min_p': min_p, 'max_new_tokens': 8}, 'stream': stream}
    start = time.monotonic()
    response = requests.post(BASE_URL+'/generate', json=payload, timeout=(10, 60))
    duration = time.monotonic()-start
    body = response.text
    if expected_rejection:
        assert 'min_p is not supported with NGRAM speculative decoding' in body, (response.status_code, body)
        assert response.status_code in (200, 400, 422), response.status_code
        if stream:
            assert 'data:' in body or response.status_code != 200, body
    else:
        assert response.status_code == 200, (response.status_code, body)
        parsed = response.json()
        assert isinstance(parsed.get('text'), str), parsed
        assert parsed['meta_info']['completion_tokens'] > 0, parsed
        assert parsed['meta_info']['finish_reason']['type'] != 'abort', parsed
    RESULT['checks'].append({'label': label, 'request': payload, 'status_code': response.status_code, 'elapsed_seconds': duration, 'response': body, 'passed': True})
    save()
    print(json.dumps({'label':label, 'status':response.status_code, 'seconds':duration, 'passed':True}), flush=True)


def stop_server(process):
    try:
        children = psutil.Process(process.pid).children(recursive=True)
    except psutil.NoSuchProcess:
        children = []
    try:
        os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
    except ProcessLookupError:
        pass
    try:
        process.wait(timeout=45)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
        process.wait(timeout=15)
    for child in children:
        try:
            if child.is_running(): child.terminate()
        except psutil.NoSuchProcess:
            pass
    _, alive = psutil.wait_procs(children, timeout=15)
    for child in alive:
        try: child.kill()
        except psutil.NoSuchProcess: pass
    _, alive = psutil.wait_procs(alive, timeout=15)
    assert not [p.pid for p in alive if p.status() != psutil.STATUS_ZOMBIE], 'server children survived'


def run_server(speculative):
    label = 'ngram' if speculative else 'ordinary'
    cmd = [sys.executable, '-m', 'sglang.launch_server', '--model-path', str(ROOT/'model'), '--host', '127.0.0.1', '--port', '31916', '--attention-backend', 'flashinfer', '--dtype', 'bfloat16', '--mem-fraction-static', '.5', '--max-running-requests', '8', '--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode', '8', '--context-length', '2048']
    if speculative:
        cmd += ['--speculative-algorithm', 'NGRAM', '--speculative-num-draft-tokens', '16']
    env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONPATH=str(ROOT/'source/python'), HF_HOME=str(ROOT/'hf'), HF_HUB_CACHE=str(ROOT/'hf/hub'), TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=str(ROOT/'inductor'), TRITON_CACHE_DIR=str(ROOT/'triton'), SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE='0', SGLANG_RUST_BUILD_MODE='auto', SGLANG_CACHE_DIR=str(ROOT/'sglang-cache'))
    with open(ROOT/f'server-{label}.log', 'w') as log:
        process = subprocess.Popen(cmd, env=env, cwd=ROOT/'source', stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, start_new_session=True)
        RESULT['launches'].append({'mode':label, 'command':cmd, 'pid':process.pid})
        save()
        try:
            deadline = time.monotonic()+600
            while time.monotonic()<deadline:
                if process.poll() is not None:
                    raise RuntimeError(f'{label} server exited: {process.returncode}; see server-{label}.log')
                try:
                    if requests.get(BASE_URL+'/health',timeout=2).status_code == 200:
                        break
                except requests.RequestException:
                    pass
                time.sleep(2)
            else:
                raise TimeoutError(f'{label} server startup exceeded 600 seconds')
            print(f'SERVER_READY {label}',flush=True)
            if speculative:
                request(0, False, False, 'ngram valid initial control')
                for iteration in range(2):
                    for stream in (False, True):
                        request(.1, stream, True, f'ngram reject min_p=.1 stream={stream} repeat={iteration}')
                        request(0, False, False, f'ngram valid after rejection stream={stream} repeat={iteration}')
            else:
                request(.1, False, False, 'ordinary accepts min_p=.1')
            assert requests.get(BASE_URL+'/health',timeout=10).status_code == 200
            assert process.poll() is None
        finally:
            stop_server(process)
            RESULT['launches'][-1]['stopped'] = True
            save()


try:
    run_server(True)
    run_server(False)
    RESULT['complete'] = True
    print('HTTP_CHECK_COMPLETE',flush=True)
except Exception as exc:
    RESULT['error'] = repr(exc)
    raise
finally:
    save()

title: [sglang-miles] Fix Kimi-K3 weight reloads after graph capture
author: XinyuJiangCMU
body:
## Motivation

**Graph replay can keep reading the old weight buffer after a reload.**

Kimi combines several BF16 projection weights into a contiguous buffer so it can compute them with a fused GEMM. When CUDA Graph captures this computation, it records the buffer's address.

During RL, new weights arrive in chunks, each handled by `load_weights`. The original code creates a new merged buffer after every chunk and points the model parameters to that new buffer. However, the captured graph still reads the old address. Later chunks update the new buffer, while the old one can be left with stale values. This is particularly visible in the CI weight-update check, which deliberately overwrites the weights before restoring them: the graph can end up reading weights that were only partially restored.

This change reuses the original merged buffer during reloads, updating its contents while keeping the address stable.

**The ROCm fused KDA path can hide a parameter from the weight loader.**

That path saves `f_b_proj.weight` as `self._bfa_f_b_w` for use in computation. Assigning a Parameter this way also registers it under the new name. Since `named_parameters()` removes duplicates by default, it can report only `_bfa_f_b_w` and omit the original name, `f_b_proj.weight`. A reload that looks up weights by their original names can then skip this parameter.

Storing `f_b_proj.weight.data` instead keeps a Tensor view of the same weight storage without registering another Parameter, so the original name remains available to the loader.

## Modifications

- Reuse the existing merged storage for generic BFA, ROCm KDA input projections, and MoE front projections. Skip copying weights that already share the destination view.
- On the block-FP8 BFA path, copy the reloaded dequantized weights into the existing `_bfa_w` and `_bfa_f_b_w` buffers.
- Keep the ROCm `f_b` alias as a Tensor view (`.weight.data`), matching the generic path.

## Accuracy Tests

- Earlier method-level HIP graph probes reproduced stale reads before the fix and passed with the same buffer-reuse logic for all three merge paths.
- The same HIP graph probe on the block-FP8 BFA path: stale after a reload before this change, matches the reloaded weights after.
- Earlier ROCm10/BF16/TP8 four-layer LoRA A/B: per-token mean absolute logprob difference fell from **3.827 / 3.808** to **0.108 / 0.110** across two steps, with graph replay and the existing numerical checker enabled. Both arms already included the parameter-alias fix.
- The [September 30 H200 nightly](https://github.com/radixark/miles/actions/runs/36734875490/job/109959415110) also reports large differences: **3.806 / 2.770** for full-parameter training and **3.755 / 3.750** for LoRA. Both tests disable the logprob checker. **NVIDIA before/after validation is pending; these logs alone do not establish the same root cause.**

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance benchmark yet. The forward kernels and fusion choices are unchanged; buffer reuse is in weight reload processing.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code and run the relevant lint checks.
- [ ] Complete NVIDIA before/after validation and rerun GPU checks on this branch.

title: [PD] Fix crash for allocation when mamba + pd + decode radix cache
author: ByronHsu
body:
## Why?

With Mamba/KDA, PD decode, and decode radix cache, [PD admission on `main`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/a9c97c9f6973c03e778d1fe1e63a6b9f58a55012/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode.py#L1373-L1387) checks whether **zero** Mamba slots are free. It does not evict cached states when one slot is free, even though a fresh request needs **three** slots with overlap scheduling: one live state and [two tracking buffers](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/a9c97c9f6973c03e778d1fe1e63a6b9f58a55012/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py#L1450-L1471). The [buffer allocation](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/a9c97c9f6973c03e778d1fe1e63a6b9f58a55012/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py#L1599-L1613) then asserts and exits the decode worker.

```text
Fresh request: 1 free slot, cached states are evictable
  -> PD admission sees free > 0 and skips eviction
  -> request row and live Mamba state allocate (1 -> 0 free)
  -> two tracking buffers cannot allocate
  -> AssertionError: Not enough space for mamba ping pong idx
```

## What?

- Extract `ensure_mamba_capacity` from the [combined-engine allocation logic on `main`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/a9c97c9f6973c03e778d1fe1e63a6b9f58a55012/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocation.py#L300-L323). It counts the live state and tracking slots each request still needs, evicts enough cached states to cover any shortfall, then rechecks capacity.
- Use that check before PD decode preallocation and before resuming a retracted request. If capacity is still short, leave the request queued rather than partially allocating it.
- Keep combined serving's existing behavior: attempt eviction, then let its allocator run. Only PD uses the capacity check to defer a request.

## Verification?

On one H200 node, two GPUs ran the tiny Kimi Linear model with real weights, NIXL PD, decode radix cache, overlap scheduling, and 16 sequential distinct requests (257 input / 256 output tokens each):

```text
Unpatched, 5 Mamba slots: 3 requests complete; request 4 crashes
                         at 2 free + 3 evictable slots
Patched,   5 Mamba slots: all 16 complete
Unpatched, 128 slots:     all 16 complete (capacity control)
Patched, repeated prompt: request completes with 256 cached tokens
```

Relevant traceback, with framework wrappers omitted:

```text
DecodePreallocQueue.pop_preallocated
  -> DecodePreallocQueue._pre_alloc          (decode.py:2075)
  -> HybridReqToTokenPool.alloc              (memory_pool.py:1471)
  -> HybridReqToTokenPool._alloc_ping_pong_buffer
  -> AssertionError: Not enough space for mamba ping pong idx
```

## Test?

- On the current source tree, pinned isort `7.0.0`, Ruff `0.15.1` selected checks and formatter, Python syntax checks, and `git diff --check` pass.
- On the original pinned source (`7b079c9c26`), the Mamba-capacity and decode-queue tests passed: **13 passed, 3 subtests passed** on H200. The end-to-end H200 comparison above also used that source, before the per-request sizing refinement.

title: [Diffusion][MiniMax-H3] Fix int32 offset overflow in SubBlock router kernels
author: saatwiknagpal
body:
## Motivation

Without sequence parallelism (e.g. MiniMax-H3 on one GPU), each SubBlock attention call routes all heads; Ulysses SP would shard them across ranks. The pool (`S*H*D`), score (`L*Gq*Gk`) and top-k (`row*G`) kernels then compute element offsets past 2^31 in int32, which wrap and crash with an illegal memory access (Xid 13).

Boundary on B200, D=128: at S=491,520, H=34 passes and H=35 crashes; at H=56, S=299,584 passes and S=299,648 crashes.

## Modifications

Compute the overflowing offsets in int64: the program ids in `_pool_kernel` and `_topk_kernel`, and the per-head output base pointer in `_score_kernel` (its per-element offsets stay int32). Add one regression test that fails before the fix.

## Accuracy Tests

- At H=34 (where stock works), scores and index are bitwise equal to stock.
- With the fix at 491,520x56 and 299,648x56, the last heads' scores and index are bitwise equal to the same heads routed alone. Pooled values match torch (max abs err 0.002).
- `test_subblock_sparse_attention.py`: the new test fails on stock (illegal memory access) and passes with the fix. All other tests pass.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

B200, mean +- std over 8 interleaved fresh-process runs of 100 reps each (ms). The pool and top-k kernels are unchanged within 0.001 ms.

| S, H | score kernel, stock | score kernel, fix | `route`, stock | `route`, fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 491,520, 14 | 19.677 +- 0.004 | 19.732 +- 0.008 (+0.28%) | 25.47 +- 0.05 | 25.54 +- 0.09 |
| 491,520, 7 | 9.828 +- 0.002 | 9.852 +- 0.004 (+0.24%) | 12.80 +- 0.08 | 12.78 +- 0.06 |
| 98,304, 56 | 3.192 +- 0.001 | 3.198 +- 0.001 (+0.19%) | 4.522 +- 0.001 | 4.543 +- 0.028 |

End to end, MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA 15 s at 1312x736 on 4xB200 (sparse, warm runs): 232.1 s and 232.0 s without the fix vs 232.1 s with it.

With this fix, the 1-GPU crash is gone. A 15 s H3 generation on one B200 then runs out of memory in the attention path; #41985 fixes that separately.

title: [PD][NIXL] Fix prepared dlists for KV entries of different lengths (DeepSeek-V4)
author: Stelath
body:
## Motivation

NIXL indexes prepared descriptors as `i * num_slots + p`, using the **first entry's** slot count for every entry. This assumes all KV entries have the same length.

DeepSeek-V4 breaks that assumption: one prefill pool has 40,025 C4 KV pages, 40,022 indexer pages, and 40,149 C128 KV pages. This causes two failures:

- **Wrong source pages.** Lists are built with each entry's length but indexed with the first entry's. Requesting C128 layer 1, page 20, for example, returns layer 0, page 73. Short prompts look fine, but our DeepSeek-V4-Pro PD deployment lost track of content beyond roughly 16k tokens.
- **Invalid destination descriptors.** Decode advertises the first entry's count, so prefill builds descriptors beyond the shorter indexer pool, causing the `NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND` in #41163.

Mooncake doesn't prebuild these lists and is unaffected.

## Changes

Add `num_kv_slots()`, the minimum slot count across registered KV entries, and use it for:

- Prefill's `_num_slots_src` and source lists, including equal-TP and mixed-memory paths.
- Decode's advertised `dst_num_slots`.

All allocator-issued page indices fit within this minimum, so no valid pages are lost. Models with equal-length entries are unchanged.

## Tests

`test_nixl_dsv4_kv_slots.py` builds real DeepSeek-V4 pools on CPU and exercises NIXL's prep/send path with a fake agent. It verifies that each entry reads and writes its own pages and that destination descriptors stay in bounds.

Both tests fail on `main` and pass with this change. The disaggregation unit suite's existing failures are unchanged.

End-to-end A/B testing used DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 PD on GB300 (TP4 prefill/decode, NIXL over UCX, fp8 KV), with identical configs except for this change. Novel prompts contained random six-digit codes at known positions:

| Test | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 32k prompt, 10 codes at 12k–21k | 2/10; repeats codes | 10/10 |
| 96k prompt, 5 codes | 1/5; invents sequential codes | 5/5 |
| 250k prompt, 5 codes | 0/5 | 5/5 |
| Summarize 96k of Moby-Dick | Front matter only | Full arc through Ahab's oath |

title: [router] Fix power_of_two with --dp-aware
author: AMD-yanfeiwang
body:
## Motivation

With `--pd-disaggregation --dp-aware --decode-policy power_of_two`:

1. 1P1D / 2P1D cannot start (`Power-of-two policy for decode requires at least 2 decode workers`). Validation counts URLs, but each URL expands into `dp_size` workers at runtime.
2. p2c is effectively random. The load monitor requests `http://host:port@rank/v1/loads`, which never reaches the engine (`host:port` is parsed as userinfo). It also reads `aggregate.total_tokens`, which current `/v1/loads` no longer returns (it returns per-rank `loads[]`). Every rank gets `-1`, which is cached, so p2c compares `-1 vs -1` and keeps the random first pick.

## Modifications

- Skip the p2c "at least 2 workers" validation when `dp_aware` is set.
- Fetch `/v1/loads` once per engine and map `loads[].num_total_tokens` by `dp_rank`. Non-DP workers use the sum, and legacy `aggregate.total_tokens` is still accepted.
- Don't publish failed loads, so p2c falls back to request counts. On token-load ties, p2c also compares request counts.
- Count PD streaming requests as in flight from dispatch, not after upstream headers arrive. Otherwise a streaming burst sees zero in-flight requests everywhere and p2c is random again.

## Test

CPU-only, in `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.20-rocm724-mi35x-20260930`, with fake DP engines and 64 concurrent requests:

| | stock | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1P1D / 2P1D, decode dp8 | fails to start | starts; 7..9 req/rank |
| 1P + 2D x dp8 (16 ranks), non-streaming | `-1 vs -1` in every decision; 0..12 req/rank | no `-1`; 2..6 req/rank; 1 `/v1/loads` per engine per poll |
| 1P + 2D x dp8 (16 ranks), streaming | 0..8 req/rank (stddev 2.0, same as random) | 2..5 req/rank (stddev 0.74) |
| one rank reports +500k tokens | still selected | never selected |

The added unit test covers `/v1/loads` parsing (per-rank and legacy formats). `cargo test --lib` and clippy pass.

## End-to-end (MI355X)

DeepSeek-V4-Pro AgentX trace replay, 1P1D, decode TP8 with DP attention (8 decode ranks), router `--policy consistent_hashing --dp-aware`. Router built from this PR on `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.21-rocm724-mi35x-20261007`; each point is a 1 h measurement.

Absolute values; in parentheses, the change against `round_robin` on the same image. Columns marked ¹ are from the `v0.5.21-rocm724-mi35x-20261002` image. Poll is the load monitor interval (`--worker-startup-check-interval`).

**Output throughput (tok/s/GPU)**

| conc | `round_robin` | `power_of_two`, poll 1 s | `round_robin` ¹ | `power_of_two`, poll 30 s (default) ¹ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 192 | 369.9 | 366.7 (-0.9%) | 359.7 | 353.8 (-1.6%) |
| 256 | 439.4 | 438.4 (-0.2%) | 432.8 | 425.2 (-1.8%) |
| 384 | 563.5 | 568.4 (+0.9%) | 560.6 | 549.1 (-2.1%) |
| 512 | 590.7 | 601.1 (+1.8%) | 588.9 | 581.7 (-1.2%) |

**TPOT p50 (ms)**

| conc | `round_robin` | `power_of_two`, poll 1 s | `round_robin` ¹ | `power_of_two`, poll 30 s (default) ¹ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 192 | 12.45 | 12.63 (+1.4%) | 13.78 | 14.26 (+3.5%) |
| 256 | 13.92 | 14.07 (+1.1%) | 14.59 | 15.69 (+7.5%) |
| 384 | 17.34 | 16.67 (-3.9%) | 17.50 | 18.99 (+8.5%) |
| 512 | 18.45 | 18.72 (+1.5%) | 19.01 | 19.58 (+3.0%) |

**TPOT p90 (ms)**

| conc | `round_robin` | `power_of_two`, poll 1 s | `round_robin` ¹ | `power_of_two`, poll 30 s (default) ¹ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 192 | 14.82 | 14.85 (+0.2%) | 15.97 | 16.54 (+3.6%) |
| 256 | 16.35 | 16.58 (+1.4%) | 16.93 | 18.25 (+7.8%) |
| 384 | 20.67 | 19.82 (-4.1%) | 20.63 | 22.71 (+10.1%) |
| 512 | 22.22 | 22.21 (0.0%) | 22.72 | 23.37 (+2.9%) |

- p2c now starts on 1P1D and reads each rank's load. The token load evens out KV across decode ranks (busiest / mean rank KV tokens 1.24-1.43 -> 1.08-1.23) but not the number of requests per rank, which sets the DP-attention decode step time, so throughput and TPOT stay close to `round_robin`. #43483 adds a request-count load.
- The load monitor polls at `--worker-startup-check-interval` (default 30 s), not at the policy's `load_check_interval_secs` (5 s). A 30 s snapshot is stale enough to make p2c worse than `round_robin` (last column). Not changed here.

### Concurrency 512 over the hour

![All three arms over the hour, concurrency 512](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AMD-yanfeiwang/sglang/pr-assets-router-p2c/c512-three-arms-over-the-hour.png)

With this PR, p2c on tokens leaves the request count across decode ranks less even than `round_robin` (bottom). The in-flight request load from #43483 keeps it flat for the whole hour. At 512 more than half (55-57%) of each rank's in-flight requests are still waiting on KV transfer, so the busiest rank's running batch (top) improves less than at lower concurrency.

![Running requests per decode rank, p2c in-flight requests (1s), concurrency 512](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AMD-yanfeiwang/sglang/pr-assets-router-p2c/c512-per-rank-running-p2c-inflight.png)

With #43483 every decode rank's hourly mean running batch is within 2% of the 8-rank mean, and no rank is the busiest more than 17% of the time (`round_robin`: DP6 at +6.3% and 21%; 12.5% if even).

title: fix(unified-memory): propagate unified-memory lazy checkpoint policy and handle unallocated session slots
author: seokwoosong
body:
## Motivation

With `--mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer_lazy`, a request holds one ping-pong checkpoint slot and the second is allocated only when a track boundary needs it. The unified-memory pool factories never forwarded `enable_mamba_extra_buffer_lazy`, so unified pools allocated both slots up front while the scheduler ran the lazy policy.

Forwarding the flag means unified pools now hold ping-pong buffers whose unallocated entries are `-1`. `free_mamba_cache` already filters those, but streaming-session cleanup freed the whole buffer and counted `numel()` slots. The same gap exists on the static pool in lazy mode.

## Modifications

- Forward `enable_mamba_extra_buffer_lazy` through `init_unified_mamba_pools`, `init_unified_mamba_swa_pools` and `UnifiedHybridReqToTokenPool`, as a required keyword, so a caller that drops it fails with a `TypeError` instead of silently running eager.
- `StreamingSession._free_slot_mamba` frees only the allocated (`!= -1`) ping-pong entries, and `session_held_mamba_slots` counts only those. This applies to every pool, not just unified ones.
- The shared unified allocator test fixture (`python/sglang/test/unified_allocator_fixtures.py`) passes the flag explicitly.
- Regression tests: the policy reaches both unified factories through the production configurator, and session cleanup and accounting with `-1` entries on unified and static allocators.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated on an NVIDIA B200 against main `048b2a07f3`, with this PR rebased onto it:

- `test_unified_tri_pool.py`: 49 tests and 100 subtests pass, including the two new ones (47 on main). The related unified-memory, Mamba and streaming-session test files give the same results as main.
- Inkling (`thinkingmachines/Inkling`, revision `test`) with `--enable-unified-memory --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer_lazy` and `--enable-deterministic-inference`, 32 LongBench prompts:
  - main: the scheduler aborts at its first idle leak check with `pool memory leak detected!`, the Mamba pool counting 32 slots more than it holds, one per request;
  - with this change (run together with #39982 and #38229): logprob match, prefill cache hit and decode cache hit are all at `avg_kl_div=0.0`.

After rebasing onto main `6cec8f98ce` (which includes #39982), the tests that build pools through the shared fixture pass: `test_unified_pending_event_batches.py`, `test_unified_dynamic_gate_capacity.py` and `test_unified_float_move_gate.py`, along with `test_unified_tri_pool.py` (49 tests).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speed impact expected; the session count adds one device read per held slot, and it runs only in the idle leak check.

title: [Fix] qwen3.8: Fix batch-invariant kernels for Qwen3.8 Flash-Next
author: Misaka9468
body:
## Motivation

With deterministic inference enabled, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next can produce different logprobs and generated tokens when the same prompt is placed in a different batch. Compiled HC projections use an unregistered `aten::mm.out` overload, shared-expert gating changes its reduction configuration at 1024 token rows, and QSA changes both its attention launch configuration and selected-index ordering.

## Modifications

- Register `aten::mm.out` using the existing batch-invariant matmul and write the result into the supplied output tensor.
- Apply the shared-expert gate's warp cap to every batch size in batch-invariant mode.
- Use one QSA prefill launch configuration in batch-invariant mode.
- Use FlashInfer deterministic CUDA QSA top-k with smaller-index tie breaking and canonical index ordering, including the decode shortcut.
- Add regressions for output-buffer semantics, cross-batch reductions, ragged top-k inputs, cutoff ties, and CUDA graph replay.

## Accuracy Tests

Validation environment: 8 H20 GPUs, TP=8, BF16 weights, FP32 GDN state, Triton GDN and MoE, decode CUDA graphs enabled, prefill CUDA graphs disabled. PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, and sglang-kernel 0.4.8.

- All 8 GPU regression cases passed on this PR's code. Independently reverting the mm.out, gate, QSA prefill, top-k, or decode-routing change reproduced its corresponding failures.
- Existing QSA tests: 74 passed, 1 skipped.
- Full-model batch probes with radix cache disabled: 27 comparisons against 3 single-request references matched exactly in generated token IDs, selected-token logprobs, and top-5 logprobs. Input lengths were 256, 2560, and 16384, with 32 generated tokens per request. This matrix preceded removal of a redundant post-sort already performed by the pinned FlashInfer implementation; the final operator regressions were rerun.

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/batch_invariant_ops/test_qwen_batch_invariance.py \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/qsa/test_qsa_determinism.py
```

GSM8K: all 1319 test questions, 5 training-set examples, non-thinking chat template, greedy decoding, max 2048 output tokens, concurrency 64, radix cache enabled, and prefill chunks of 8192. The baseline runs and final PR run use identical evaluation settings.

| Variant | Correct | Accuracy | Invalid / truncated |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Unmodified, ordinary inference | 1275/1319 | 96.66% | 0 / 3 |
| Unmodified, deterministic inference | 1278/1319 | 96.89% | 0 / 1 |
| This PR, deterministic inference | 1278/1319 | 96.89% | 0 / 1 |

Against the deterministic baseline, 7 answers changed from wrong to correct and 7 changed from correct to wrong. This measures task accuracy; it does not establish cached-prefix equivalence.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Both variants were benchmarked sequentially in the same environment: 16 requests, 2560 input tokens and exactly 256 output tokens per request, radix cache disabled, prefill chunks of 32768, one warmup and three timed rounds. Throughput includes prefill and decode.

| Variant | Median output tokens/s |
| --- | ---: |
| Unmodified, deterministic inference | 349.50 |
| This PR, deterministic inference | 324.68 |

The fixes reduce throughput by 7.1% on this workload relative to the unmodified deterministic mode.

- [x] Follow the repository's Python formatting and code style.
- [x] Add focused unit/regression tests.
- [x] Provide final-scope accuracy and speed benchmark results.

title: fix(diffusion): load serialized H3 INT8 in ComfyUI integrated mode
author: Tokha233
body:
## Motivation

Loading an H3 single-file INT8 ConvRot checkpoint through the ComfyUI integrated path currently fails with `Parameter ...comfy_quant not found in custom model state dict`. The loader reads the H3 metadata but discards its per-layer quantization markers, so it builds ordinary floating-point Linear parameters.

## Modifications

Resolve the serialized INT8 config using the existing H3 loader utilities, pass it into model construction, and filter metadata-only keys. Preserve CPU checkpoint placement for layerwise offload. Reject conflicting runtime quantization, FSDP, and unsupported serialized formats explicitly. The existing ComfyUI QKV layout remains unchanged.

## Compatibility after upstream #38040

The loader fix uses the shared checkpoint quantization resolver, which now returns `ConvRotInt8Config`. The regression covers both `comfy_kitchen` and `jit` serialized loading with their kernel initialization mocked; this validates metadata, weight and scale loading, not JIT inference. The full Larry8 GPU timing below was measured on the earlier Kitchen-backed revision and is not a benchmark of the new automatic JIT backend.

## Accuracy Tests

- Regression writes a real small safetensors checkpoint and runs the shared loader. INT8 weights and FP32 scales must remain exactly equal, parameters frozen, and ComfyUI QKV ordering preserved.

The original integrated loader fails before sampling, so there is no valid speedup ratio. No experimental attention or row-splitting changes are included in this PR.
