title: [Fix] Guard DeepSeek NVFP4 shared-expert fusion for LoRA and FP4 backends
author: jybsuper
body:
## Problem and fix

DeepSeek's NVFP4 shared-expert GEMM + SwiGLU fusion can be enabled with incompatible configurations:

- With LoRA, the fused path accesses quantization attributes on a LoRA wrapper and bypasses the gate/up adapter computation.
- With Marlin or TRT-LLM, weight preparation does not create the interleaved weights required by the fused path.

This PR disables that fusion when LoRA is enabled or the FP4 GEMM backend does not support it, using the ordinary unfused path instead.

## Tests

- New backend compatibility test in `test_modelopt_nvfp4.py`: **PASS**, covering all five backends in a dependency-isolated local run.
- `pre-commit run --all-files`: **PASS**.
- The three before/after server tests below ran on **4× GB300** with **DeepSeek-V3-0324-FP4**. Each successful server completed **3/3 generation requests** with nonempty output and finite output-token logprobs. These are startup/generation smoke tests, not a full accuracy benchmark.

### 1. TRT-LLM, no LoRA

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 /opt/sglang/bin/python3 -B -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /cluster-storage/models/models--nvidia--DeepSeek-V3-0324-FP4/snapshots/d03662cdc34b56eab1315d4557e395e6b4944782 \
  --trust-remote-code --tp 4 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 27770 --nccl-port 28770 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --moe-runner-backend marlin \
  --fp4-gemm-backend flashinfer_trtllm \
  --disable-shared-experts-fusion --disable-radix-cache \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.80 --max-running-requests 4 \
  --context-length 4096 --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --max-prefill-tokens 4096 \
  --cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled
```

- **Before:** startup fails with `AttributeError: 'MergedColumnParallelLinear' object has no attribute 'weight_swiglu_interleaved'`.
- **After:** server starts successfully; **3/3 requests pass**.

### 2. Marlin, no LoRA

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 /opt/sglang/bin/python3 -B -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /cluster-storage/models/models--nvidia--DeepSeek-V3-0324-FP4/snapshots/d03662cdc34b56eab1315d4557e395e6b4944782 \
  --trust-remote-code --tp 4 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 27770 --nccl-port 28770 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --moe-runner-backend marlin \
  --fp4-gemm-backend marlin \
  --disable-shared-experts-fusion --disable-radix-cache \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.80 --max-running-requests 4 \
  --context-length 4096 --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --max-prefill-tokens 4096 \
  --cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled
```

- **Before:** startup fails with `AttributeError: 'MergedColumnParallelLinear' object has no attribute 'weight_swiglu_interleaved'`.
- **After:** server starts successfully; **3/3 requests pass**.

### 3. LoRA with CUTLASS

Uses a synthetic rank-16 gate/up adapter; generation requests select `lora_path="aHI"`.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 /opt/sglang/bin/python3 -B -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /cluster-storage/models/models--nvidia--DeepSeek-V3-0324-FP4/snapshots/d03662cdc34b56eab1315d4557e395e6b4944782 \
  --trust-remote-code --tp 4 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 27770 --nccl-port 28770 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --moe-runner-backend marlin \
  --fp4-gemm-backend flashinfer_cutlass \
  --disable-shared-experts-fusion --disable-radix-cache \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.80 --max-running-requests 4 \
  --context-length 4096 --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --max-prefill-tokens 4096 \
  --cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled \
  --enable-lora --lora-backend triton \
  --max-loras-per-batch 2 --max-lora-rank 16 \
  --lora-target-modules gate_proj up_proj --lora-strict-loading \
  --lora-paths aHI=/scratch/deepseek-fusion-pr-20261002/gate-up-adapter
```

- **Before:** startup fails with `AttributeError: 'MergedColumnParallelLinearWithLoRA' object has no attribute 'input_scale_inv'`.
- **After:** server starts successfully; **3/3 LoRA requests pass**.

`--disable-shared-experts-fusion` controls the separate shared-into-routed-MoE optimization, not the GEMM + SwiGLU fusion fixed here. The paths shown are from the test node; use the corresponding model, adapter, and Python environment when reproducing.

title: [Fix] Validate per-layer rope_parameters on transformers 5.17 (Laguna-S/XS-2.1 nightly)
author: Jiminator
body:
## Motivation

`test/registered/e2e/models_large/test_laguna_nvfp4_nightly.py` has failed on the Nvidia nightly since 10/1 ([job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36874298733/job/110409841450)). The server dies while loading the config for `poolside/Laguna-S-2.1-NVFP4`:

```
transformers/modeling_rope_utils.py, line 850, in validate_rope
    rope_type = rope_parameters.get("rope_type", rope_parameters.get("type", "default"))
AttributeError: 'float' object has no attribute 'get'
```

Laguna-XS-2.1-NVFP4 fails the same way; that nightly only ran the S test.

**Cause.** #39012 bumped transformers from 5.12.1 to 5.17.0. In 5.17, `validate_rope` treats `rope_parameters` as nested as soon as one key is a layer type, then calls `.get` on every value (huggingface/transformers#48435). Laguna's remote config stores per-layer dicts (`full_attention`, `sliding_attention`), and the base `convert_rope_params_to_dict` adds a top-level `rope_theta` beside them, so validation reaches a float. 5.12.1 used `issubset`, which classified that dict as flat.

Upstream fixed this in huggingface/transformers#48798, which uses Laguna-XS-2.1 as its reproducer. The fix shipped in 5.18.0.

**Bisect** (scheduled `Nightly Test (Nvidia)`, job `nightly-test-4-gpu-b200 (1)`; config-load repro of each commit at its pinned transformers):

| | Commit | transformers | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nightly, 9/29 | `98fce73d5b` | 5.12.1 | pass |
| Parent of #39012 | `036a3b3e14` | 5.12.1 | pass |
| #39012 | `547286bb5a` | 5.17.0 | fail |
| Nightly, 10/1 | `41cbe65de0` | 5.17.0 | fail |

Swapping the variables isolates the transformers version: the parent's code on 5.17.0 fails, and #39012's code on 5.12.1 passes. The runner (`b200-di01` passed on 9/23) and the Hub repo (unchanged since 8/25) are ruled out.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/utils/hf_transformers_patches.py`: add `_patch_nested_rope_validation`, a backport of huggingface/transformers#48798 shaped like `_patch_layer_types_validation`. It wraps the `validate_rope` class validator. Only when the original raises `AttributeError` on a `rope_parameters` dict that mixes layer-type keys with other keys does it re-run the original on the layer-type entries, then restore the full dict. Every config that validates today takes the unchanged path. Drop it once sglang requires transformers >= 5.18.

The Laguna nightly already covers this, so the PR adds no unit test.

Alternatives considered:

- **Bump transformers to 5.18.0**, which contains the upstream fix. Opened separately as a draft for comparison.
- **Special-case Laguna in `HfModelConfigParser.parse`** so it skips the remote config. Not chosen: the bug is in a transformers validator, sglang already re-parses Laguna with its own `LagunaConfig`, and a parser special case would ignore `--trust-remote-code` for one model while leaving the validator bug in place for any other remote config with this shape.

## Accuracy Tests

Ran `test_laguna_nvfp4_nightly.py` on 1x B300 with main's pins (torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.17.0, tokenizers 0.23.2, sglang-kernel 0.4.8, flashinfer 0.7.0.post1):

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| main, no fix (control) | fails with the same `AttributeError` as CI |
| main + this PR | `Ran 2 tests in 1278.9s`, `OK` |

| Model | GSM8K, this PR (B300) | Last green nightly, 9/29 (B200) | Test threshold |
|---|---|---|---|
| Laguna-S-2.1-NVFP4 | 0.970 | 0.985 | 0.89 |
| Laguna-XS-2.1-NVFP4 | 0.910 | 0.900 | 0.87 |

The test samples 200 examples at temperature 1.0, so these deltas are within noise. At the config level, `get_config` returns the same rope values as on 5.12.1 for both checkpoints.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A: only config loading changes.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). All hooks pass on the changed files.
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). None added; the existing `test_hf_transformers.py` passes on transformers 5.17.0 and 5.18.0 with this change.

- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [AMD] Fix DSpark draft bucket tests for the raw in-graph metadata default
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
## Motivation

#42014 turned on `SGLANG_HIP_DSPARK_DRAFT_RAW_METADATA` by default on HIP. Since then, a DSpark draft `TARGET_VERIFY` bucket holds `DSV4RawDSparkDraftMetadata` until `init_forward_metadata_in_graph` materializes it. Two tests in `test/registered/amd/test_dsv4_hip_bcg_metadata.py` still read `core_attn_metadata` straight after `init_forward_metadata_out_graph`, so `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` now fails on every PR:

```
AttributeError: 'DSV4RawDSparkDraftMetadata' object has no attribute 'core_attn_metadata'
```

Example: [#42061's mi35x job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36866676354/job/110392706972), where this file was 2/54 and the lane stopped there. #42014's own mi35x lane was cancelled, so CI did not catch the failure before merge.

## Modifications

Test-only, `test/registered/amd/test_dsv4_hip_bcg_metadata.py`:

- `TestDsparkDraftBlockWindowHip`: the block-window replay check now runs with the flag both off and on. On the raw path it asserts that the bucket holds `DSV4RawDSparkDraftMetadata`, calls `init_forward_metadata_in_graph` the way the graph would, and checks the same window rows, lengths and positions. This also adds coverage for the new default.
- `TestAiterSparseLengthFoldPerStep`: patched to the eager path. That is the only path whose bucket keeps one core object across steps, which is the cache-reuse bug this test guards. The raw path builds a fresh core inside the graph on every forward.

No backend change.

## Checklist

- [x] Still needed on current main: main's own `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` shard 0 fails `test_dsv4_hip_bcg_metadata.py` with the same `'DSV4RawDSparkDraftMetadata' object has no attribute 'core_attn_metadata'` ([job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37309524661/job/111761345486))

A normal PR run stops shard 0 at its first failure, `test_fused_kda_conv_recurrent_verify.py` (file 5 of 27; this file is 18), so this is a `continue_on_error` dispatch of the stage on the PR head. The three files that still fail there — `test_quark_mxfp4.py` (fixed by #41980), `test_fused_kda_conv_recurrent_verify.py` and `test_compact_attention_hip.py` — are exactly the ones that fail on main's shard 0, which fails `test_dsv4_hip_bcg_metadata.py` on top of them.

title: [diffusion] fix: keep residual_gate_add on the JIT CUDA path for cont…
author: niehen6174
body:
## Motivation

#41305 replaced the shared `residual_gate_add` JIT CUDA operator with Triton kernels, benchmarked on SANA-Video on H200 where it gained 1.6–1.7% E2E. That PR's profiling confirmed the branch executing there is `_rga_transposed`.

The kernel is also shared by Ideogram, Flux-2, Qwen-Image 2.1, ERNIE-Image and LTX-2, which call it on **contiguous** layouts. There the Triton path costs **13–15.6 µs more host time per call**. The cost is flat in tensor size, so it is per-call dispatch overhead, not slower math — negligible when bandwidth-bound, dominant when launch-bound.

LTX-2 is launch-bound: ~800 calls per denoise step at `(1, 384, 4096)` and `(1, 26, 2048)`, from 8 call sites across 48 layers. That adds ~8 ms per step and moved `ltx_2_two_stage_t2v` and `ltx_2_3_two_stage_ti2v_2gpus` from ~1.12× to 1.20–1.23× of their `h100.json` baselines. The `pr_test` limit is 1.20×, so about half of CI runs now cross it.

Found by bisecting 315 commits on 2× H200. Reverting this one file on current main removes the regression entirely.

## Modifications

One file, +9/−4.

1. Take the Triton path only for the transposed-dense layout it was benchmarked on; contiguous layouts go back to the JIT CUDA kernel. The SANA-Video path is untouched.
2. Drop two redundant `can_use_residual_gate_add_cuda` calls — it ran 3× per invocation at ~2.7 µs each (pre-#41305 ran it twice).
3. Call the custom op directly from `residual_gate_add`, which has already run the same predicate. `residual_gate_add_cuda` stays public and keeps validating.

## Accuracy Tests

The CUDA and Triton backends were compared on **37 configurations** (bf16/fp16, six shapes, full / broadcast / per-token gates, plus transposed-dense) and are **bit-identical** on all of them (`torch.equal`). Both already claimed bit-exact rounding, so routing between them by layout cannot change output.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

2× H200, dependencies pinned, sglang commit the only variable.

Host time per call, bf16, at the shapes LTX-2 actually issues (confirmed by counting dispatch branches over a real run):

| shape | gate | #41305 | this PR | pre-#41305 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `(1, 26, 2048)` | broadcast | 36.50 µs | **23.80 µs** | 23.46 µs |
| `(1, 384, 4096)` | broadcast | 39.18 µs | **23.92 µs** | 23.43 µs |
| `(1, 1536, 4096)` | full | 34.43 µs | **19.91 µs** | 19.19 µs |

`ltx_2_two_stage_t2v` avg denoise step, three runs each:

| build | runs | median |
|---|---|---:|
| `544e46c080` (current main) | 164.7 / 162.5 / 161.6 | 162.5 ms |
| **main + this PR** | 158.2 / 158.1 / 157.4 | **158.1 ms** |
| main + whole file reverted | 157.1 / 156.8 / 157.0 | 157.0 ms |
| `fc9e1c8d29` (before #41305) | 156.3 / 157.9 / 154.7 | 156.3 ms |

Recovers 4.4 ms of the 6.2 ms regression. A ~1.1 ms gap to the full revert remains: 672 of 24000 calls (gate same shape as residual) still fall through to the eager path. Can follow up separately.

The microbenchmark covers contiguous layouts only — I did not measure whether Triton also wins there at SANA-Video's sizes. If it does, the dispatch can be widened on the back of a benchmark covering the other models sharing this kernel; `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/diffusion/bench_residual_gate_add.py` already has workloads for most of them.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). — no new behaviour; existing kernel tests plus the bit-exactness check above apply
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — no user-facing change
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [diffusion] Fix native FP8 format handling for FLUX 3 rowwise linears
author: Tokha233
body:
## Motivation

The MI300 diffusion unit run on #42121 fails the FLUX 3 FP8r checkpoint test with `Expected b.dtype() == at::kFloat8_e4m3fnuz, got Float8_e4m3fn` ([job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37030627223/job/110916375120)). The rowwise linear currently passes serialized E4M3FN weights and activations directly to `_scaled_mm`, although gfx94 requires FNUZ. ModelOpt already normalizes that format, but two of its regression tests still assume FN and unadjusted scales.

## Modifications

- Normalize FLUX 3 FP8r weights at load time on FNUZ platforms and match activation format before `_scaled_mm`, reusing the existing FN-to-FNUZ helper. Both scales are adjusted; negative zero is normalized to avoid NaN. Clone checkpoint weights before the helper's in-place byte normalization.
- Preserve the CUDA FN path and the serialized FP8r format.
- Cover both native formats, padded zero rows, tensor/tuple outputs, exact dequantized values and checkpoint immutability. Update ModelOpt tests to verify native dtype/scales and dequantized equivalence, including negative zero and CPU offload.

## Accuracy Tests

Tested on an isolated RTX 5090 D v2 host, Python 3.12 / PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, based on upstream `f6fcda8`.

- New FLUX format regressions against unchanged production code: **2 failed / 2 passed**; only the FNUZ contract cases fail.
- Candidate: `test_flux3_action.py`, `test_modelopt_fp8_layerwise_offload_load.py`, `test_transformer_quant.py`: **107 passed, 24 subtests passed**. Includes the real CUDA FP8 `_scaled_mm` checkpoint forward.
- FNUZ contract tests use CPU tensors and a checked/dequantized GEMM substitute; they are **not MI300 GPU execution**. ModelOpt tests parameterize format conversion and check exact dequantized values.

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_flux3_action.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_modelopt_fp8_layerwise_offload_load.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_transformer_quant.py
```

Please authorize AMD CI to verify the actual MI300 GEMM/offload path. This fixes the concrete format mismatch; it does not yet establish that the separate full FLUX Action non-finite-output failure is resolved. No thresholds or tolerances were relaxed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Compatibility fix; no throughput claim. CUDA uses its existing FP8 path. The FNUZ path adds format normalization to make the previously invalid GEMM operands usable.

- [x] Changed-file pre-commit checks pass.
- [x] Add unit tests.

title: [HiCache] Fix write-back SWA insert backups tripping the write-through pending-ack assert
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

With HiCache in write-back mode on a sliding-window-attention model, a prefill batch can crash every rank with:

```
AssertionError: node N is already pending under a different write-through ack
```

Write-back backs up Full KV only at eviction, but the SWA component still publishes its window to the host at insert time. The insert tail built that publish as a write-through chain, so it walked the target's unbacked Full ancestors and asked to mark them pending as well. When two requests in one batch finish under a shared unbacked prefix, the first request's SWA window walk has already marked that prefix pending under its own ack; the second request's chain then tries to mark the same prefix under a different ack and trips the assert.

```
            root
             |
             C   Full unbacked
            / \
  (backed) B   D  Full unbacked
           |   |
          T1   T2  (both Full backed)

insert #1 -> ack T1 covers {T1, B, C}   (SWA window walk)
insert #2 -> old chain [C, D, T2] -> mark C under ack C -> assert
             new chain [T2]       -> ack T2 covers {T2, D}; the walk stops at C
```

## Modifications

- `UnifiedTreeCore._insert_tail_step` (Python core) and `insert_tail_step_` (`rust/sglang-radix-tree`) now build the insert backup with the cache's own write policy instead of always building a write-through chain. In write-back mode the chain is just the target node, so the SWA window publish never re-marks an ancestor that another ack still holds; the unbacked Full prefix is backed up at eviction, which is what write-back defers anyway. Write-through behaviour is unchanged.
- The assert stays: a node's lock and transfer lifetime follow exactly one ack.
- Regression test `write_back_swa_publish_leaves_an_ancestor_pending_under_another_ack_alone` in the shared Python suite (`test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py`, so it runs on both the Python and the Rust inspector) and as a native test in the Rust crate. It builds the tree above, inserts at T1 then T2 without draining either ack, and checks that each insert emits exactly one single-node backup chain and that C stays pending under T1. On the previous code the Python test fails with the assertion above and the Rust test fails on the chain assert (`[C, D, T2]` vs `[T2]`).

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: the change only affects which nodes a write-back insert asks the host tier to back up. Host copies are unchanged and the Full KV of the prefix is still written at eviction.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: no hot-path change. Write-back inserts enqueue fewer host transfers than before.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit): ruff, isort, codespell, `check_registered_tests.py`, `cargo fmt --check` and the clippy hook flags on the changed files.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests): `test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py -k write_back_swa_publish` passes on the Python backend (2 passed, 17 skipped for configs without SWA or with a window too short to reach C), `test_rust_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py -k write_back_swa_publish` passes on the Rust backend with the same split, `-k "write_back or swa"` on the Python backend passes, and `cargo test --locked --no-default-features` for `rust/sglang-radix-tree` passes through `test/registered/rust/test_run_sglang_radix_tree_rust_tests.py`.

title: [Fix] Step-3.5 DeepEP routed scaling and Sarvam shared expert under dense TP1
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #42312
* #42311
* #42310
* #42309
* #42308
* #42307
* #42306
* #42305
* #42304
* #42303
* __->__ #42302
* #42301
* #42300

## Motivation

Two independent defects found while migrating these models to stage boundaries, both on `main` today.

## Modifications

**Step-3.5, DeepEP path does not apply the routed scaling factor.** The non-DeepEP path scales the routed experts' output by `routed_scaling_factor`; the DeepEP path returns the combine result unscaled, so every DeepEP run produces a differently weighted mixture. The gate is also computed in a lower precision than the non-DeepEP path.

**Sarvam counts the shared expert twice under `--moe-dense-tp-size 1`.** With a fully-DP dense FFN the shared expert is replicated on every rank, and the MoE output still owes a TP sum, so the replicated part is multiplied by the TP width. Build the shared expert sharded over TP when the output still owes a sum.

## Accuracy Tests

Both are verified against a TP1 reference on H200. The Step-3.5 scaling fix brings the DeepEP path back to the non-DeepEP output; the Sarvam fix brings `--moe-dense-tp-size 1` back to the default dense TP layout.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No change to the collective sequence; the Sarvam fix shards a replicated GEMM, which is less work per rank.

## Motivation

Five configuration and pipeline-parallel defects in the EXAONE and ERNIE 4.5 VL MoE model files, all present on `main` and all found while migrating these models to stage boundaries. They are separated from the migration so each one can be reviewed and reverted on its own.

## Modifications

- **K-EXAONE's architecture name is not accepted.** HuggingFace renamed the architecture to `ExaoneMoeForCausalLM`; the registry does not list it, so the newest checkpoints silently fall back to the Transformers backend instead of the native model.
- **EXAONE needs an explicit attention backend when sliding windows are used.** Default it instead of requiring the flag.

- **ERNIE 4.5 VL MoE does not reject DP attention**, which it does not implement; it is now refused at configuration time rather than producing wrong output.

Verified on H200: K-EXAONE now loads natively (truncated to 4 layers, TP2 bitwise identical to the parent after the architecture fix); the EXAONE 4.0 and EXAONE MoE PP2 servers load and produce output identical to TP2; ERNIE 4.5 VL MoE TP2 is bitwise identical and its DP2 run now reports the expected refusal instead of running.

author: ch-wan
body:

## Motivation

Two independent defects on `main`.

## Modifications

- **Jet-Nemotron no longer builds or runs.** Fix the construction so the model loads again.
- **Granite MoE hybrid re-adds a stale residual in its final norm.** The layer stack's last output already carries the residual; adding it again in the final norm counts it twice.

## Accuracy Tests

**The Granite final-norm fix changes this model's output, by design.** Granite MoE hybrid h-1b at TP2 produces different logits from `main`, and the change comes from this fix alone: `main` normalized the stream plus a second copy of the last layer's pre-FFN stream, and one of those two addends should not be there. The models without a MoE are otherwise bitwise identical to the parent, and h-tiny's output is verified against a TP1 reference.

Jet-Nemotron builds and runs at TP1, which it does not do on the parent at all -- there it raises `TypeError: JetNemotronDecoderLayer.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'start_layer'` during construction.

**TP > 1 is out of scope for Jet-Nemotron and still does not work**, for a reason this PR does not touch: its linear-attention block splits the `qkvabz_proj` output with `total_k_dim` / `total_v_dim` / `num_heads` taken straight from the config, while the projection is a `MergedColumnParallelLinear` whose output is sharded, so at TP2 the split sizes sum to exactly twice the tensor width. `A_log` and `dt_bias` are allocated unsharded for the same reason. That is pre-existing on `main` and is only observable now that the model gets past construction.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

title: [Fix] GigaChat 3.5: apply the sandwich norms to the complete sums
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #42312
* #42311
* __->__ #42310
* #42309
* #42308
* #42307
* #42306
* #42305
* #42304
* #42303
* #42302
* #42301
* #42300

## Motivation

GigaChat 3.5 applies a sandwich norm to a stage output before it is added into the residual. Under DP attention that output is still a partial sum when the norm runs, so the norm is applied to one rank's share instead of the complete value. A normalization is not linear, so this cannot be reordered with the sum.

## Modifications

Apply both sandwich norms to the completed sums, using the attention-side output transform added in the PR below this one. Also fix the combined `post` / `pre` norm, which returned a tuple where a single tensor was expected.

## Accuracy Tests

H200: verified against a TP1 reference. On the parent, the DP attention run diverges from TP1; with the fix it returns to the no-DP noise level.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same number of collectives; the norm moves after the sum.

title: [Fix] Count attention-DP ranks in one-batch bench running cap
author: mmangkad
body:
## Motivation

With `--attn-dp-size N`, the server reports `dp_size=1` and `attn_dp_size=N`, so `one_batch_server` set its running-request cap N times too low. It skipped every batch size above that cap and wrote no results. This fails the GB300 nightly perf tests in `test_kimi_k25_nvfp4_dp.py`, `test_qwen35_fp8_dp.py`, and `test_deepseek_v4_pro_fp4_high_throughput.py`.

## Modifications

Count DP ranks as `dp_size * attn_dp_size`, and rename the variable to `num_dp_ranks`.

## Verification

Each server used the CI args; the benchmark ran at the batch size that failed:

| Model | bs | Before: cap -> results | After: cap -> results |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4 | 16 | 12 -> 0 | 48 -> 1 |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 | 16 | 12 -> 0 | 48 -> 1 |

title: [Fix] Load a draft's tensor weight update from its deployment TP rank
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #42348
* #42347
* __->__ #42346

## Motivation

With EAGLE3 and attention data parallelism, a draft worker owns attention and is built inside the draft TP scope, where the context answers its narrowed attention-TP rank. `WeightUpdater` records that rank at construction. But `update_weights_from_tensor` receives a `LocalSerializedTensor` holding one entry per *deployment* TP rank, so indexing it with the narrowed rank opens another rank's CUDA IPC handle: the draft loads another rank's tensor whenever the entries differ, and creates a context on that rank's device.

## Modifications

Index the payload with the deployment TP rank, read at update time. The scheduler runs weight updates outside any draft placement scope, so `get_parallel().tp_rank` there is the deployment rank.

`init_weights_update_group` keeps the recorded rank: only the target joins that group.

## Accuracy Tests

H200, Qwen3-8B with the `AngelSlim/Qwen3-8B_eagle3` draft, `--tp-size 2`, GSM8K 300 questions:

| config | base | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| plain | 0.953 / 0.947 (two runs) | 0.950 |
| `--attn-dp-size 2` | 0.950 / 0.950 (two runs) | 0.947 |

Greedy text (4 prompts × 48 tokens) is byte-identical across all three plain runs and all three attention-DP runs. Accept length and throughput sit inside the base spread.

The premise was confirmed on a live server: under `--attn-dp-size 2`, world rank 1 reports the draft's recorded rank as 0 while its deployment rank is 1, so the pre-fix index would have opened rank 0's handle. Under plain `--tp 2` both are 1, matching the claim that the bug needs attention DP.

`test_weight_update_tensor_rank.py` fails with the one line reverted and passes with it.

`unit/spec` and `unit/model_executor`: same results as the parent commit.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

title: [Fix] Skip a draft's decode recapture when it owns no decode graph
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #42348
* __->__ #42347
* #42346

## Motivation

`update_weights_from_disk(recapture_cuda_graph=True)` recaptures the decode CUDA graph of every selected runner, draft runners included. A speculative worker that captures its draft's graphs inside the draft placement scopes asks the draft runner for no decode graph of its own (`init_cuda_graphs(capture_decode_cuda_graph=False)`), which leaves the runner's eager runner in the decode slot.

Recapturing there runs outside those scopes. For a draft the capture clears the slot and then raises, so the runner is left without even the eager fallback it had.

## Modifications

A draft runner recaptures only a decode graph it captured itself: the slot holds neither `None` nor its own eager runner. Target runners recapture as before.

## Accuracy Tests

H200, Qwen3-8B with the `AngelSlim/Qwen3-8B_eagle3` draft, `--tp-size 2`, GSM8K 300 questions: 0.950 plain and 0.947 with `--attn-dp-size 2`, against base runs of 0.953 / 0.947 and 0.950 / 0.950. Greedy text (4 prompts × 48 tokens) is byte-identical across every run.

On a live server, both draft runners report their eager runner in the decode slot, in plain and attention-DP layouts alike, which is the state the guard now recognises. `test_draft_graph_recapture.py` fails with the guard reverted and passes with it.

`unit/spec` and `unit/model_executor`: same results as the parent commit.

title: [sglang-miles] Fix the bf16 triton MoE path and mhc_pre splitk for DeepSeek-V4.1
author: Zhichenzzz
body:
## Motivation

Two startup failures hit while validating DeepSeek-V4.1 RL support (radixark/miles#3179) on GB300 with the **unquantized (bf16)** model. Both kill the engine before serving starts; neither affects the native fp8/fp4 path.

**1. The triton fused-experts path crashes on packed topk output.** `StandardTopKOutputPacked` carries a fourth field (`packed_topk_ids`), so the strict 3-tuple unpack in `triton_utils/fused_moe.py` raises `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3)` for any model whose router emits the packed format and which runs the unquantized triton runner. DSV4.1 bf16 dies in warmup.

**2. `mhc_pre` splitk refuses `hc_hidden_size` 20480.** The splitk kernel hardcoded `hidden_block` for hc_hidden_size 16384/28672 and raised `NotImplementedError` otherwise. DSV4.1 (hidden 5120 × hc_mult 4 = 20480) dies in cuda-graph warmup on the non-deepgemm prenorm path.

## Modifications

- `triton_utils/fused_moe.py`: read `topk_weights`/`topk_ids` by attribute, which works for every `TopKOutput` variant (both the main unpack and the xpu branch). The same latent unpack exists in `fused_moe_native.py`, `kt_ep_wrapper.py`, `ascend_tp.py` and `moe_runner/deep_gemm.py`; left untouched here because those paths were not exercised.
- `kernels/ops/layernorm/mhc.py`: derive `hidden_block` instead of hardcoding shapes — pick the largest value in {256, 128} that divides both `hc_hidden_size` and `hc_hidden_size // split_k`, matching the kernel's own asserts. This reproduces the existing choices exactly (16384→256, 28672→128) and admits 20480→128.

## Accuracy Tests

On GB300 (2 nodes × 4 GPUs), DSV4.1 bf16 (dequantized from the fp8/fp4 drop) with these two patches:

- 4-layer cut, first-token top-5 logprobs vs the native fp8/fp4 engine: match within quantization noise at tp1, tp4 and tp8-across-2-nodes (e.g. top-2 logprobs −0.796/−0.921 bf16 vs −0.887/−1.012 fp8, same token ids).
- Full 40-layer bf16 serving generates coherent text (temperature-0 `/generate` probe).
- miles RL e2e with the patched engines: 10 rollouts, `train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff` 0.019–0.023 every step, raw rewards 0.57–0.79.
- The mhc derivation was regression-checked against the previous hardcoded mapping (16384→256, 28672→128 unchanged).

Without fix 1 the bf16 engine dies at startup in warmup; without fix 2 it dies in cuda-graph warmup — so these paths had no passing baseline to compare against.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No kernel behavior changes for previously-working shapes: the unpack rewrite is loader-side Python, and the mhc derivation selects the same `hidden_block` values as before for 16384/28672.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code and run the relevant lint checks (repo pre-commit: ruff, ruff format, isort, codespell all green on the touched files).

title: [HiCache] Fix cgroup page-cache accounting and the sizing fallback when cgroup discovery fails
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

Two problems in how HiCache sizes its host pools against the process cgroup.

1. **Charged page cache counted as used.** Since #40135 the host-pool budget is bounded by the cgroup headroom `limit - memory.current` (`memory.usage_in_bytes` on v1). Charged usage includes the page cache the process populated, most visibly the checkpoint it just read. That cache is reclaimable, and host `MemAvailable` (psutil's `available`) already treats it as free, but the cgroup bound treated it as used. Right after a large model loads, an explicitly sized host pool could therefore fail with `Not enough host memory available` although the kernel would have served it by reclaiming the cache, and the same command passed or failed depending on how much cache the job happened to have charged.

2. **Auto-sizing against host RAM when the container limit is unreadable.** #42120 made a missing cgroup filesystem size the pool against host available memory with a warning, and added `SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_MEMORY_BYTES` as an override. For the default auto-sized pool that is the wrong failure mode: when the limit cannot be read, assuming the host's RAM is the container's allowance sizes a pool the limit may not hold, and the OOM kill arrives later and far from the cause. An explicit `--hicache-size` or `--hicache-ratio` is different: the user has stated what they want, so the probe is only a sanity check and a warned fallback is appropriate.

The page-cache accounting is the same fix as #42039; this PR carries it together with the sizing-policy change because both edit the same function and tests, and the second part depends on the `memory.stat` read the first one introduces.

## Modifications

- `mem_cache/host_memory.py`
  - At each limited cgroup level, charged usage is now `usage - (active_file + inactive_file)` (`total_active_file + total_inactive_file` on v1, whose unprefixed counters omit descendants), clamped at zero. These are the file-LRU pages `MemAvailable` counts as reclaimable; shared memory sits on the anonymous LRU and stays charged, which is why `memory.stat`'s `file` / `cache` totals are not used. A missing `memory.stat` for a known limit is an error like a missing usage file.
  - `available_host_memory_bytes(*, allow_cgroup_fallback=False)`: when cgroup discovery fails (no cgroupfs mounted, a mounted hierarchy that does not contain the process, or an unreadable counter for a known limit), it raises `RuntimeError` asking for an explicit `--hicache-size`. With `allow_cgroup_fallback=True` it logs a warning and checks against host available memory instead. Readable limits are enforced in both modes.
  - The one-time "no cgroup filesystem" warning and the `SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_MEMORY_BYTES` override are removed.
- `mem_cache/pool_host/base.py`: `host_memory_budget_bytes(requested_bytes=0, *, auto_size=False)`; the explicit-size checks in the host pools keep the default and so get the warned fallback.
- `mem_cache/hicache_auto_size.py`: the auto-sizing path passes `auto_size=True`, so it requires successful cgroup discovery.
- `environ.py`: `SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_MEMORY_BYTES` is unregistered. It was added in #42120, which is not in any release tag, so it is removed outright rather than deprecated; `--hicache-size` is the supported way to size the pool without cgroup discovery.
- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_host_memory.py`: the synthetic procfs now writes `memory.stat`; a regression test covers the page-cache accounting on v2 and v1 (hierarchical counters, a shared-memory decoy, and the clamp when v1 usage trails the counters); the no-cgroupfs, unmatched-hierarchy and missing-counter cases assert the actionable error by default and the host-memory fallback when allowed. The tests for the removed override are dropped.

Behavior is unchanged when cgroup discovery succeeds and no page cache is charged, and when the process has no cgroup membership.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A: model outputs are unaffected.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A: the only cost is one extra `memory.stat` read per limited cgroup level at host-pool init.

Validation: `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_host_memory.py`, `test_hicache_auto_size.py` and `test_mem_pool_host.py::TestHostMemoryBudget` pass locally; the new page-cache test fails on the previous accounting.

title: [diffusion] Fix TeaCache CFG state lifecycle and skip boundaries
author: fusheng-ji
body: Fixes #35054. TeaCache used the previous CFG branch to decide when to reset request state. That discarded the positive cache during serial CFG, and kept the previous request's state on the negative CFG-parallel rank. This PR resets from the current branch and topology instead. It also measures the Wan skip window in denoising steps rather than in local forward calls. Serial CFG, CFG parallel, and CFG gating (which stops running the negative branch after the gate step) now share one definition. Before, a CFG-gated run started skipping late, and could skip the final step that `end_skipping` should always compute. `TeaCacheParams` now uses `get_skip_step_range()`; the obsolete forward-count `get_skip_boundaries()` API is removed, and its tests now check denoising-step ranges. Based on @Oxygen56's unmerged implementation in #35136. Adds regressions that call the production Wan methods with real tensors. They cover branch isolation, completed/interrupted requests, and the skip window under serial CFG, CFG parallel, and CFG gating. Supersedes #42154 (branch renamed to follow the repository's branch naming). > **CI note:** this changes the output of `wan2_1_t2v_1.3b_teacache_enabled`. Its server sends warmup requests with TeaCache before the test request, and on `main` the test request inherits their stale state. On the same GPU, the test's key frames differ between `main` and this PR (max abs pixel diff 211–228), while each tree reproduces itself exactly across runs. The case's H100 ground truth in `sgl-project/ci-data-diffusion` was produced with `main`'s behaviour and will likely need regenerating. ### Validation **Unit:** the new lifecycle tests, run against upstream `main`, `main` with both fixes, and both fixes with this PR's step-based skip window reverted (Wan counts the window in forward calls again): | Test | `main` | `main` + both fixes | both fixes, skip window in forward calls | |---|---|---|---| | `test_new_request_clears_completed_or_interrupted_state` | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | | `test_serial_cfg_preserves_both_branches_at_first_timestep` | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | | `test_skip_window_is_measured_in_denoising_steps` | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | | `test_wan_skip_window_follows_timesteps_under_cfg_gating` | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | | `test_wan_skip_window_matches_timesteps_on_each_cfg_rank` | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | `test_skip_window_is_measured_in_denoising_steps` checks the new `get_skip_step_range()` API itself, so only `main` fails it. `test_new_request_clears_completed_or_interrupted_state` also needs the step-based window: its CFG-parallel case relies on step 1 being inside the window. Together with the other fix on top of `main`, the Spectrum/TeaCache lifecycle tests, existing Spectrum forecaster, MiniMax-H3 Spectrum, CFG gating/policy, DiT config boundary and sampling-parameter tests give 77 passed and 59 subtests passed. Repository pre-commit hooks pass. **End to end** on B200 (Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers, 832x480, seed 42, guidance 3.0, Torch SDPA; compile/BCG/warmup off), comparing upstream `main` with `main` + both fixes. *Request isolation:* a different 13-frame request runs first, then the 9-frame, 12-step target is compared with a fresh instance. | Topology | `main` | `main` + both fixes | |---|---|---| | 1 GPU, serial CFG | crash: `size of tensor a (4680) must match … (6240)` (stale residual from the previous request) | bit-identical to fresh (frames and latents) | | 2 GPU, CFG parallel | crash on the negative rank → other rank hangs until timeout | bit-identical to fresh | *CFG gating:* 30 steps, serial CFG, compared with the per-step decisions of the ungated run. | Window | Gate step | Window in forward calls | Step-based window (this PR) | |---|---|---|---| | 1.3B preset (start 5) | 3 | skipping starts at step 7 instead of 5 | same decisions as ungated | | start 1, end −1, threshold 10 (stress: the L1 test never forces a compute) | 9 | **final step skipped** | same decisions as ungated; final step computed | At the default thresholds, TeaCache's L1 test happened to compute the final step anyway, so the end-boundary miss only shows once the window alone decides. *Cost:* 33 frames, 30 steps, 3 prompts × 3 requests each. TeaCache skips 30% of DiT forwards in both topologies: 1.35× (1 GPU) and 1.28× (2 GPUs, CFG parallel) median speedup, mean PSNR vs no cache 32.4 / 33.7 dB (worst prompt 23.8 / 23.4 dB). title: [sglang-miles] [diffusion] fix: give the scheduler its own host
author: Rockdu
body:
## Motivation

The scheduler's ZMQ endpoint was built from `host`, the address the HTTP server binds and advertises. Once `host` is routable — needed whenever the HTTP server must be reached from another process or machine, e.g. RL rollouts — `is_local_endpoint` treats the in-tree scheduler hop as remote. The scheduler still spills reply tensors to `CudaIpcRef`, but the client only materializes them on local endpoints, so the ref leaks to callers:

```
TypeError: 'CudaIpcRef' object is not subscriptable
```

`/generate` and `/rollout/generate` both index `OutputBatch.output` and fail this way. It also exposed the scheduler socket, which unpickles whatever it receives, on that routable address.

## Modifications

- Add `scheduler_host` / `--scheduler-host` (default `127.0.0.1`) and build the scheduler endpoint from it instead of `host`, as `disagg_p2p_hostname` already does for the P2P transport.
- Bind both disaggregated `DiffusionServer` frontends on `server_args.scheduler_endpoint`, the address their in-process HTTP client connects to; the role result endpoints stay on `host`.
- Gate the reply-side `spill_cuda_tensors` on `is_local_endpoint` of this replica's own endpoint, like the file-ref spill next to it, so both ends of the hop apply the same condition.

Unchanged when `host` is `None`, `localhost` or `127.0.0.1`. With a routable `host`, request-side IPC (`update_weights_from_tensor`) now turns on too. A remote `DiffGenerator(local_mode=False)` must set `--scheduler-host` on both ends: the server no longer exposes the scheduler socket just because `host` is routable, and the connection error now says so.

## Tests

One test in `test/unit/test_ipc_array.py`, collected by the `unit` suite: with a routable `host`, a reply round trip through `Scheduler.return_result` and the client's receive path hands the caller a tensor, over IPC on a local hop and over pickle on an explicitly remote one. Not run yet; draft until verified.

Same change as #42435, for `sglang-miles`: radixark/miles_diffusion stage-c has failed on this since its Oct 2 nightly.

title: [AMD][CI] Fix ROCm kernel wheel sources: drop eagle_utils, add DSV4 kernels
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
## What

Bring the ROCm kernel wheel's source lists (`3rdparty/amd/wheel/sgl-kernel/CMakeLists_rocm.txt` and `rocm_hipify.py`) back in line with `setup_rocm.py` and `common_extension_rocm.cc`:

- Remove `csrc/speculative/eagle_utils`.
- Add `csrc/elementwise/deepseek_v4_topk` and `csrc/elementwise/dsv4_norm_rope`.

## Why

The release workflow does not build with `setup_rocm.py`. `build-rocm-matrix` copies `3rdparty/amd/wheel/sgl-kernel/*` into the AOT directory, and `build_rocm.sh` builds with `CMakeLists_rocm.txt`. Those lists have drifted, which causes two problems.

**The build fails (0.4.8, 0.4.9).** #40033 moved the EAGLE tree kernels to JIT. It reduced `eagle_utils.cu` to an include of `python/sglang/kernels/jit/include/sgl_kernel/speculative/eagle.cuh`, and dropped the file from `setup_rocm.py` and its op registrations from `common_extension_rocm.cc`. The wheel lists still compiled it, and the JIT include directory is neither on that include path nor mounted into the build container:

```
/sgl-kernel/csrc/speculative/eagle_utils.hip:28:10: fatal error: 'sgl_kernel/speculative/eagle.cuh' file not found
```

- 0.4.9: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37155260604/job/111315213887
- 0.4.8: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36649756025/job/109710303032

No ROCm wheels were published for either version.

**The published wheels fail at import.** `common_extension_rocm.cc` registers `deepseek_v4_topk_transform_512` and the three `dsv4_fused_*` ops, and `setup_rocm.py` compiles their sources, but the wheel lists never included them. In the published `0.4.6.post1+rocm720`, `0.4.7+rocm720` and `0.4.7+rocm1000` wheels, `common_ops.abi3.so` has all four as undefined `R_X86_64_GLOB_DAT` relocations. Those are resolved at load time, so loading the library fails. The ROCm Docker images build with `setup_rocm.py` and are not affected.

## Test plan

Built both ROCm wheel legs with `release-whl-kernel.yml` at version 0.4.9 on a test branch, with all publish steps disabled: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37189886891

| Leg | Result |
|---|---|
| `build-rocm-matrix (3.10, 720)` | pass, `sglang_kernel-0.4.9+rocm720` built |
| `build-rocm-matrix (3.10, 1000)` | pass, `sglang_kernel-0.4.9+rocm1000` built |

- All 16 sources compile for gfx942 and gfx950 together, so both `HIP_FP8_TYPE_FNUZ` and `HIP_FP8_TYPE_E4M3` are defined. The DSV4 files had previously only been built single-arch through `setup_rocm.py`.
- A build-only step ran `nm -D --undefined-only` on `common_ops.abi3.so` in each wheel. No sgl_kernel op is left unresolved; the only undefined symbols are from Python and torch.
- The wheels were not imported or run on a GPU.

title: [diffusion] fix: pin the JoyAI-Echo overlay's source revision
author: niehen6174
body:
## Motivation

`joy_echo_t2v_2gpu` fails on every 2-GPU runner that does not already have the old JoyAI-Echo checkpoint in its HF cache. Since Oct 1 23:11 UTC, all 14 `multimodal-gen-test-2-gpu (0)` jobs that landed on the new `h100-novita2-gpu-*` hosts failed this way, while the same case passed 59 times on the older hosts:

```
Overlay source model jdopensource/JoyAI-Echo is missing required files ['JoyAI-Echo-release.safetensors']. Re-downloading source snapshot.
ValueError: Overlay source model jdopensource/JoyAI-Echo is still missing required files ['JoyAI-Echo-release.safetensors'] after re-download.
ERROR ...test_diffusion_generation[joy_echo_t2v_2gpu] - RuntimeError: Server exited early (code 1).
```
([example job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37106982213/job/111157440618))

Root cause: upstream `jdopensource/JoyAI-Echo` restructured the repo for the Echo 1.5 release (`a7d585b1`, Aug 27) and deleted the 46.1 GB `JoyAI-Echo-release.safetensors`. That file is what `Niehen6174/JoyAI-Echo-overlay` splits into diffusers components. The registry pins the overlay repo's revision but not the source repo's, so both the first source download and the forced re-download in `ensure_overlay_source_dir_complete` fetch upstream `main`, which no longer has the file. Older hosts pass only because their cache still has the file from before Aug 27.

## Modifications

- Overlay specs accept `source_revision`. The registry entry wins, and the overlay manifest is the fallback for overlay repos loaded directly. It is passed to the first source download (`maybe_download_model(revision=...)`, which already supported it) and to the forced re-download.
- JoyAI-Echo is pinned to `4187f9a53c6eff3a76c51e79bd27f70d10f7591b` (Jun 18), the last upstream commit that ships `JoyAI-Echo-release.safetensors`. I checked with `HfApi.list_repo_files` that at this revision the manifest's `source_allow_patterns` match exactly that file; on `main` it is gone.
- The materialized-model cache key is unchanged, so hosts that already materialized JoyAI-Echo keep that directory and do not re-split the checkpoint. The marker file now also records `source_revision`.
- Other overlays carry no `source_revision` and behave exactly as before.

## Accuracy Tests

No numerical change: the pinned revision is the same checkpoint the passing hosts already use.

Added `test_registry_source_revision_survives_upstream_removing_required_file`. It fakes a source repo whose `main` lacks the required file while the pinned commit has it. On current `main` it fails with the CI error above (`still missing required files ... after re-download`); with this PR it passes. `test_model_overlay.py`: 5 passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

None. The only runtime effect is on a host with no JoyAI-Echo cache: it now downloads the pinned checkpoint once instead of failing.

title: [Fix] Offer the fused MoE finalize all-reduce only to a block that owes the sum
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #42481
* #42480
* __->__ #42479
* #42478
* #42477

## Motivation

The fused MoE finalize kernel in `DeepseekV2MoE` carries a tensor-parallel all-reduce inside it and sets `all_reduce_done`, but its eligibility never consulted `reduce_results`, while the unfused path below it does. A DeepSeek V4 MoE built with `reduce_results=False` would therefore still sum its output there and have its caller sum it a second time, scaling the block's contribution by the tensor-parallel width with nothing raised.

No block reaches it that way today: the fused path needs `is_deepseek_v4`, and the only construction that passes it leaves `reduce_results` at its default. So this changes no behavior; it makes the contract hold for a block built either way, which the DeepSeek V4 decoder needs once its stage boundary, rather than the MoE, completes the sum.

## Modifications

- Offer the fused finalize only when the block owes its own sum (`reduce_results`).
- `test_stage_producers_leave_sums.py` could not see this case. It matched a sum by call name, so a fused kernel that performs the sum internally was invisible; and it recognized the `reduce_results` guard only when spelled inline in the branch, so a predicate computed once and branched on later read as unguarded. It now counts every `moe_finalize_all_reduce*` kernel as a sum (the plain one and its `_mhc`, `_mhc_combine` and `_mhc_quant` variants), and follows a name bound from a condition that requires `reduce_results`. Only such a condition guards a sum: the flag itself, or an `and` with it as a conjunct; a negation, a comparison such as `is False`, or an `or` does not require it. Across the 57 files that build stages, the second change admits exactly one predicate, the one in this file.
- A synthetic case pins both: a fused finalize variant under a guard computed earlier is accepted, while sums under a negated guard computed earlier, an inline `not`, an `is False` comparison and an `or` are all reported.

## Accuracy Tests

No behavior change by construction: the added condition is always true on the only path that reaches the fused kernel today (DeepSeek V4 builds its MoE with the default `reduce_results=True`).

The guard reports no violation across the 57 files that build stages; removing the new `reduce_results` condition makes it report all four fused finalize calls. CPU: the 114 test files that import the models or the layer boundary package show no new failure against `main`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: no path that runs today changes.

title: [Fix] GigaChat 3.5: build the stage boundaries once
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #42481
* __->__ #42480
* #42479
* #42478
* #42477

## Motivation

`GigaChat35DecoderLayer` builds its stage boundaries twice. It calls `DeepseekV2DecoderLayer.__init__`, which builds the attention and FFN boundaries from the DeepSeek norms, then builds them again from its own norms and output transforms and drops the first pair. Building that pair is wasted work against norms the layer replaces straight away, and it stops being harmless once stages are connected to their neighbours in the order they are built: the dropped pair would be wired in as the live attention's producer.

## Modifications

- `DeepseekV2DecoderLayer.__init__` takes `build_stages` (default `True`); GigaChat 3.5 passes `False` and builds its stage boundaries once, after its norms exist.
- `test_stage_boundaries_built_once.py`: a source guard that no decoder layer builds its stage boundaries after a base `__init__` that already built them, unless it passes `build_stages=False`. Which functions build stages is derived from the code (any function that reaches a stage builder, transitively), so a new helper is covered without being listed. A sanity bound on the number of stage-building classes keeps the guard from passing vacuously if the builders are renamed. Without the fix it reports exactly `GigaChat35DecoderLayer`; a synthetic case covers `super().__init__` and `Base.__init__(self)` calls, inherited constructors, and an explicit `build_stages=True`.

## Accuracy Tests

No behavior change: the boundaries the layer keeps are the second pair, built exactly as before; only the discarded first build is skipped.

B200, CPU: the 114 test files that import the models or the layer boundary package (1,258 cases, one process per file) show no new failure against `main`, the new guard passes 2/2, and every module under `srt/models/` imports with the same result on both trees.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: model construction skips one discarded stage build per layer; nothing at runtime changes.

title: [AMD] Fix RoPE cache dtype and diffusion CI failures
author: BBuf
body:
ROCm Llama startup fails during graph capture because #41282 keeps the RoPE cache in FP32 while the fallback kernel assumes the query dtype. Let the kernel read FP32 caches and round cos/sin to the query dtype before the existing arithmetic. This preserves the FP32 cache used by QSA without converting the whole cache on every forward.

The diffusion fixes defer quantization imports to break the linear-layer import cycle, enable the existing MiniMax H3 denoising path on HIP, pass the existing HF credential to dual-GPU tests, and install ffmpeg/ffprobe for H3 media validation.

The existing ROCm RoPE test now runs even with AITER enabled, checks FP32-cache outputs against the same-dtype kernel bit for bit, and runs in Stage A so it catches this failure before the longer suites. Correctness, performance and startup thresholds are unchanged.

Validation:
- Changed-file pre-commit checks passed, including clang-format and test registration.
- Latest-head AMD Stage A: 9/9 test files passed, including Llama and EAGLE3 (18 tests each, MMLU 0.69 for both) and the ROCm RoPE regression: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37210510566/job/111460697051.
- AMD kernel unit tests: 7,141 passed, 123 skipped. CUDA kernel unit tests: 13,992 passed, 2,132 skipped. Both tested the merge containing bf114442d1. Latest-head GitHub lint passed.
- MI300X cold-L2 diagnostic: 24 cases were bitwise equal to the query-dtype cache path. Each timed call follows a 512 MiB read/write eviction outside event timing. This compares cache specializations in the same candidate, not a full baseline commit. A repeat using identical Q/K addresses and 1,500 interleaved samples per path measured a 1.008 geomean latency ratio (individual medians 0.989–1.036). BF16 shows a small 1–3.6% kernel overhead; this is not a claim of zero performance impact. Diagnostic run: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37212045202/job/111465214461.
- LTX-2.5 warmup and the remaining diffusion CI results are still under investigation; this PR does not claim all checks have passed.

Follow-up to #42391. The RoPE failure was already present in the base code and is fixed here as part of the ROCm CI follow-up.

title: [diffusion] CI: fix qwen cache-dit step 10/49 perf baselines
author: niehen6174
body:
## Motivation

`qwen_image_t2i_cache_dit_enabled` fails its H100 per-step perf check at random. From 09-30 to 10-04, 71% of attempts went over the step-49 limit. Every final 1-GPU failure in that window came from this case.

The cause, found in the debug runs in #42546, is how the step time is measured. It is not a regression.

- Steps 10 and 49 are the first cached step after a full step.
- Per-step times are host wall times with no device sync.
- The cache-dit residual check in that step is the first point where the host blocks, so that step absorbs the previous full step's queued GPU work.

Debug run on CI H100, 3 launches per arm, times in ms:

| Arm | Full step | Steps 10 / 49 | Other cached steps | E2E |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Fused QK-norm/RoPE epilogue on, unsynced (CI today) | 178 | 64 / 66 | 6.3 | 4310 |
| Fused off, unsynced | 196 | 55 / 56 | 6.5 | 4455 |
| Fused on, `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1` | 238 | 7.0 / 7.1 | 6.3 | — |
| Fused off, synced | 245 | 7.2 / 7.1 | 6.5 | — |

With synced timing, steps 10 and 49 take about 7 ms, like every other cached step. #38584 enabled the fused epilogue on Hopper, which cut host launches from 3031 to 2007 per profiled window. The real GPU time got about 3% faster. But the host now enqueues faster too, so more GPU work spills into steps 10 and 49.

## Modifications

`perf_baselines/h100.json`: steps 10 and 49 of `qwen_image_t2i_cache_dit_enabled` are set to their CI medians, 64.58 / 66.38 ms (previously 48.7 / 45.11). The medians come from 328 H100 CI measurements between 09-30 and 10-04. They are the unsynced host wall times this check measures. No other baseline or tolerance changes.

The `ltx_2_5_diffusion_decoder_2gpus` timing tolerance from earlier commits is dropped. Its host-bound slowdown will be handled in a separate PR.

## Validation

PR CI on fe3b48d passed with the same qwen baselines.

title: [diffusion] fix: load community ComfyUI-GGUF Qwen-Image-2.1 transformers
author: niehen6174
body: ## Motivation Community ComfyUI-GGUF exports of Qwen-Image-2.1 (e.g. [`abenzerps/Qwen-Image-2.1-Uncensored-GGUF`](https://huggingface.co/abenzerps/Qwen-Image-2.1-Uncensored-GGUF)) fail to load. Unlike the native-name exports validated earlier, they also quantize the plain `nn.Linear` layers outside the blocks (`modulation`, `time_text_embed`, `norm_out`, `proj_out`), which have no packed-weight parameter to load into. ## Modifications - Dequantize those layers to BF16 on load through a new `gguf_dequantize_prefixes` on the DiT, the same mechanism the GGUF text-encoder path uses. - `packed_qkv_weight` skips quantized projections instead of reading `.weight`, which GGUF layers do not have. - CPU unit tests for both fixes (they fail on `main`), plus a GGUF docs/cookbook validated-scope update. ```bash sglang generate --model-path Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1 \ --component-weights-paths.transformer abenzerps/Qwen-Image-2.1-Uncensored-GGUF/qwen-image-2.1-UC-Q4_K_M.gguf \ --prompt "..." --save-output ``` ## Accuracy Tests 1x RTX 5090, default sampling params (1024x1024, 40 steps, guidance 1.0), seed 42, default auto memory policy. | Transformer | PSNR vs official BF16 (fox prompt) | | --- | ---: | | `qwen-image-2.1-Q8_0.gguf` (`base` revision, plain quantization) | 38.8 dB | | `qwen-image-2.1-UC-Q4_K_M.gguf` | 23.8 dB | The UC checkpoint is not a pure quantization. A tensor-level diff of its BF16 export against the official weights shows that every non-attention tensor is bit-identical. The attention `to_q/k/v/out` weights equal `bf16(W + 1.0 * B @ A)` using the rank-16 LoRA shipped in the same repo, which explains the lower PSNR. Visually, the UC Q4_K_M output keeps the composition, subject, text rendering, and lighting of the official model on all three prompts tested: ## Speed Tests and Profiling Same setup as above, `main` + this PR: | Transformer | DiT weights | Peak VRAM | Denoise s/step | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Official BF16 | 14.2 GB | 17.0 GB | 0.43-0.48 | | GGUF Q8_0 | 7.6 GB | 11.1 GB | 0.47 | | GGUF Q4_K_M | 4.6 GB | 8.25 GB | 0.47 | As the GGUF guide notes, GGUF is a capacity option: the packed linears are dequantized each step and then run the native GEMM, so per-step latency is slightly higher. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). title: [Fix] dsa: Fix ragged seed indices before MTP draft decode
author: cognaiger9
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
Fused DSA prefill can produce top-k indices into the batch’s flattened logical KV space. The draft model captures these indices as MTP seeds and reuses them in the next draft decode, which expects physical KV slots.
This mismatch can select incorrect KV entries or cause out-of-bounds reads, particularly when long requests share cached prefixes and logical offsets exceed physical cache capacity.

The engine config that exercises this error:
```
SGLANG_DSA_FUSE_TOPK=1 \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/PhalaCloud/GLM-5.3-W4AFP8 \
  --quantization w4afp8 \
  --tp 8 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.75 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend flashmla_sparse_q8 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 3 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4
```

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- Add `prepare_mtp_seed_indices()` to map fused RAGGED seeds through the producer’s page table before capture.

title: [Fix] Quantize reloaded FP8 weights after native sharding
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #42590
* #42589
* #42588
* #42587
* #42586
* __->__ #42585
* #42484
* #42468
* #42426

## Motivation

Reloading an unchanged checkpoint can change FP8 weights and scales because reload quantization runs before native TP sharding and scale updates use the wrong partition. With Qwen3-0.6B, TP4/attention-DP2, this caused GSM8K subset accuracy to fall from **45% to 1.5%** after QKV reload.

## Changes

- Quantize each local destination after its native parameter loader performs sharding and packing. Write into the existing FP8/scale storage and preserve untouched per-channel rows.
- Preserve one native `model.load_weights()` call with the complete input. Defer FP8 parameter callbacks, then replay each destination with one local BF16 staging matrix; non-FP8 parameters, including norms and tied embeddings, follow native loading.
- Avoid old-weight dequantization, cross-call BF16 staging caches and duplicate quantization at session finalization.
- Validate per-tensor destination coverage and checkpoint names before mutation. Require the audited deferred-write contract: Qwen2 legacy/v2 and Qwen3 loaders are supported; other loaders fail during initialization.

## Validation

Rebased PR head `e2d57acc14` on main `59740a728f`. Prior validation is recorded at combined stack head `5a863f8592`. No CI or GPU tests were rerun for this rebase.

**Accuracy fix.** Four B200 GPUs, Qwen3-0.6B online FP8, TP4/attention-DP2; first 200 GSM8K test questions, 5-shot, greedy non-thinking decoding, maximum 512 new tokens:

| Reload path | Cold | After unchanged reload |
|---|---:|---:|
| Unfixed QKV scale placement | 90/200 (45%) | 3/200 (1.5%) |
| Correct destination layout, QKV reload | 90/200 (45%) | 90/200 (45%) |
| Fixed complete-checkpoint public update session | 90/200 (45%) | 90/200 (45%) |

The complete session updates all **311 keys in 29 chunks** through public begin/update/end APIs. All 200 output texts/token sequences, **21,082 generated token logprobs** and **3,995 teacher-forced gold token logprobs** match cold inference exactly. The 200-question complete-session measurement uses loader `0d891b82de`; the audited single-call loader also passes a 32-question cold/reload smoke with identical outputs and logprobs (15/32 in both runs). These are bounded subset measurements, with CUDA graphs disabled.

**Reload latency and memory.** Complete Qwen2.5-0.5B checkpoint, 24 layers / 290 keys / tied embeddings, one B200, TP1, per-channel FP8, GPU BF16 inputs; 5 warmups and 25 alternating repeats (`fbc7656eb6`). The parent-loader comparison holds the native model method constant:

| Native loader | Parent median | Fixed median | Parent extra allocated peak | Fixed extra allocated peak |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen2 legacy | 12.92 ms | 10.47 ms | 350.71 MiB | 16.63 MiB |
| Qwen2 v2 | 15.53 ms | 12.37 ms | 350.71 MiB | 16.63 MiB |

Both use one native call per reload; fixed parameters match cold loading and retain storage addresses. These are reload-only timings, not serving throughput.

**Correctness coverage.** The TP4/attention-DP1/2 integration matrix passes 104 native cold-load comparisons, including Qwen2/Qwen3 KV replication, independent query/KV layouts and full/partial per-channel updates. Retained native Qwen2 legacy/v2 and Qwen3 regressions cover tied-head copying, storage stability, failure restoration and rejection before mutation. Tests use kernel 0.4.8 with the documented compatibility override; these results do not certify every current-head model/format combination.

title: [Fix] Make the fused KDA beta sigmoid bit-identical to torch.sigmoid
author: vincentzed
body:
Part of #41609. This PR fixes the sigmoid part of that issue.

- #39688 moved the beta sigmoid into the `kda_gate_chunk_cumsum` kernel and wrote it as `tl.sigmoid`.
- `tl.sigmoid` does not return exactly the same bits as `torch.sigmoid`, because `tl.exp` and Triton's `/` are approximate on CUDA. KDA feeds its state back into itself, so this small difference grows along the sequence.
- This PR uses `tl.div_rn(1.0, 1.0 + libdevice.exp(-x))` instead. It matches `torch.sigmoid` on all 2^32 fp32 inputs. `tl.sigmoid` differs on 95.7M of them.
- The tests now require exact equality and check every finite bf16 value.
- Not fixed here: the fused KDA projection and the separate projections still give different results (mean |Δlogp| 0.255 in the same test). One concatenated GEMM is not bit-identical to the separate GEMMs. To match v0.5.20 exactly, the projection fusion from #39688 also has to be turned off for these checkpoints.

Test on a B300 with `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4`. I feed the same 8 x 2048 tokens to each build (teacher forcing) and compare the logprobs. The reference is main with the `beta.float().sigmoid()` that was used before #39688.

| | mean \|Δlogp\| | p99 |
|---|---|---|
| main | 0.240 | 2.35 |
| this PR | 0.000 | 0.000 |

There is no slowdown. Kernel time measured with CUPTI at H=64, K=128: 54.8 -> 54.4 us at 2857 tokens, and 2327 -> 2312 us at 131072 tokens.

title: [Fix] sglang-server: Keep the matched stop token in output_ids
author: shodoco
body:
## Motivation

The Rust detokenizer pops a matched stop token from the chunk's token IDs before decoding, so the token disappears from the decoded text and also from `output_ids` in `/generate` and gRPC responses. The Python detokenizer trims the stop token only from the IDs it decodes and passes `output_ids` through unchanged. The two servers therefore return different token IDs for the same request, and clients that count or replay `output_ids` (RL rollouts, token-in/token-out pipelines) see a missing final token in Rust mode.

## Modifications

- The matched stop token is left out of the decode slice only. The scheduler's token IDs, and therefore `output_ids`, stay intact.
- Text trimming, `no_stop_trim` and `completion_tokens` are unchanged, except that a matched stop token id 0 is now trimmed like any other. Python has done so since #41590 (`if matched is None`); the Rust guard predated that change.
- Chunk events record when their last token ID was left out of the text. Chat passes reasoning parsers the IDs without that token (`stop_trimmed_token_ids()`), because the GPT-OSS parser builds content from token IDs and the raw IDs would put the stop token back into chat content. Parsers therefore see the same IDs as before this PR.
- Out of scope: with `--tool-call-parser gpt-oss`, Python keeps `<|call|>` (200012) for the tool parser. Rust mode doesn't support that tool parser yet (it isn't mapped to Dynamo's `harmony` parser), so that exception is left to a follow-up.
- Tests: `stop_token_is_preserved_in_output_ids` replaces `stop_token_trimmed_from_output_ids` and covers stop id 0; `stop_trimmed_token_ids_exclude_only_a_trimmed_stop_token` covers the parser view with and without a trimmed stop token.

## Tests

title: [Fix] quantization: Preserve BF16 NaNs in per-token FP8 quantization
author: aurickq
body:
## Motivation

BF16 NaNs currently become finite FP8 values during per-token group quantization. For example, the UE8M0 path converts a NaN lane to `+448`, hiding invalid activations from downstream NaN checks. Preserve those NaNs so callers can detect the original numerical failure.

This intentionally changes the BF16 FP8 sanitization behavior introduced in #32188 and optimized in #32296. FP16 retains its existing behavior because its scaling multiplier can overflow for finite inputs.

## Modifications

- Use NaN-preserving clipping for BF16 with UE8M0 scales.
- Use the saturating FP8 conversion directly for BF16 with FP32 scales. It preserves NaNs while still saturating infinite and out-of-range scaled values.
- Keep FP16, FP32-input, and INT8-output behavior unchanged.
- Add plain/fused and flat/masked regression cases, including fully NaN groups, masked padding, and CUDA graph capture/replay. Retain the existing non-finite sanitization cases for FP16.

## Accuracy Tests

- Python syntax, Ruff checks/formatting, Clang-format 20.1.7, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Full CUDA regression suite: **123 passed, 0 skipped** on GB300 with CUDA 13.2. Command: `SGLANG_JIT_KERNEL_RUN_FULL_TESTS=1 pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/quantization/test_per_token_group_quant.py`. This includes finite-input regressions, BF16 NaN preservation, FP16 sanitization, and capture/replay with finite and NaN-containing inputs.
- Graph tests cover the quantizer itself. Full-model graph warmup with async assertions enabled remains a separate validation requirement because warmup may read uninitialized buffers.

## Speed Tests

No benchmark completed on this upstream revision. The change adds no host synchronization or separate GPU kernel.
