title: [Fix] HiCache: stale host KV from write-through copies racing the in-flight forward
author: jumanzii
body:
## Motivation

With HiCache on, a conversation's later turns can produce different output depending on whether its prefix was reused from device memory or loaded back from host memory. The host copy of the previous turn's last output token can be stale, so a load-back restores wrong KV for that token.

Under the overlap scheduler, `process_batch_result` for step N runs after step N+1 was launched. A request that finished at step N is still in batch N+1, and that forward writes the KV of the request's last output token on the forward stream. Meanwhile `release_kv_cache` already inserts that token into the tree and the write-through starts. `HiCacheController.start_writing` -> `L2TransferEngine.submit_device_to_host` orders the device-to-host copy only after an event recorded on the scheduler stream, never after the forward stream, so the copy can read that token's KV before or while it is written. Load-back already has the equivalent fence (`load_fence_stream`, set by the scheduler to the forward stream and used in `start_loading`); write-through had none.

The stale token sits at the end of the previous reply, which is exactly where the next turn's prompt resumes, so the next turn diverges within its first few tokens.

## Modifications

- `HiCacheController.start_writing`: before submitting the copy, make the device-to-host stream wait on `load_fence_stream` (the forward stream). `wait_stream` orders the copy after the work queued so far, which at this point is the forward that writes the node's last token; forwards launched later still overlap with the copy. When `load_fence_stream` is unset (no scheduler wiring) nothing changes.
- The comment on `load_fence_stream` now names both uses.
- Test `test_write_copy_waits_for_queued_forwards` in `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_staged_write_back_dispatch.py`: a write submitted through a real `L2TransferEngine` must wait on the forward stream before its copy. It fails without the fix. Five existing tests in that file build controllers with `__new__` and now set `load_fence_stream = None`, as the load-path test there already does.

This is the default behavior, not an option. The alternative is a data race that silently corrupts host KV, and the fence only adds a GPU-side stream dependency on work already queued (no CPU synchronization). Its costs: a write ack can arrive up to one forward later, so a just-written node stays unevictable a little longer; and on the paths that wait synchronously for a write (write-back on eviction), the scheduler also waits for the in-flight forward in that step. Without the overlap scheduler the forward stream is idle when the write is submitted, and the wait is free.

Other device-to-host copies checked:
- Write-back on eviction, buffer mode and `flush_pending_backups` all go through `start_writing` and get the fence.
- `UnifiedRadixCache.backup_kv_cache` (PD decode retraction backup) copies only `seqlen - 1` tokens; the forward in flight at retraction writes position `seqlen - 1`, so that copy is not exposed.
- `DecodeKVCacheOffloadManager` builds its own controller without `load_fence_stream`, but offloads `origin_input_ids + output_ids[:-1]`, so it is not exposed either.

HiSparse orders its decode backups the same way (`decode_backup_stream.wait_stream(self.decode_producer_stream)` in `hisparse_coordinator.py`).

Related: #42702 orders PD decode retraction restores after the in-flight forward, the same kind of race on the restore side. The two PRs are independent.

## Accuracy Tests

Greedy multi-turn outputs at concurrency 1 on a public model, `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` (no sliding window), one RTX 5090. Six sessions x three turns. Each turn sends the previous turn's `input_ids` + its `output_ids` + 200 new tokens, so a turn reuses the previous sequence including its last output token. Turns run turn-major (all sessions' turn 0, then turn 1, ...).

- Reference: no HiCache, default device pool, so every later turn reuses its prefix from device.
- HiCache: `--enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-size 4 --hicache-write-policy write_through --max-total-tokens 8192`. The small device pool evicts each session's prefix to host between its turns, so every later turn is a load-back. Defaults otherwise (flashinfer attention, `kernel` io backend, `page_first` layout, overlap scheduler on).

Both arms report the same `cached_tokens` for every turn (3128 for turn 1, 3456 for turn 2).

| run (order) | turn 0 identical to reference | turns 1-2 identical to reference |
|---|---|---|
| main, 1st | 6/6 | 0/12 (first differing token at 3-51) |
| this PR, 1st | 6/6 | 12/12 |
| this PR, 2nd | 6/6 | 12/12 |
| main, 2nd | 6/6 | 0/12 |

Reproduce:

```bash
# reference
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-8B --port 30000
python multiturn_exact.py --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B --out ref.json
# HiCache with load-backs
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-8B --port 30000 \
  --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-size 4 --hicache-write-policy write_through \
  --max-total-tokens 8192
python multiturn_exact.py --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B --out hicache.json
python compare_exact.py ref.json hicache.json
```

<details>
<summary>multiturn_exact.py / compare_exact.py</summary>

```python
# multiturn_exact.py
import argparse, json, random
import requests
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
p.add_argument("--url", default="http://127.0.0.1:30000")
p.add_argument("--model", required=True)
p.add_argument("--sessions", type=int, default=6)
p.add_argument("--turns", type=int, default=3)
p.add_argument("--out", required=True)
args = p.parse_args()

tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.model)
vocab = [i for i in range(min(tok.vocab_size, 60000))
         if (s := tok.decode([i])).startswith(" ") and s[1:].isalpha() and len(s) > 3]
rng = random.Random(0)
seqs = [rng.choices(vocab, k=3000) for _ in range(args.sessions)]
records = []
for turn in range(args.turns):
    for s in range(args.sessions):
        if turn > 0:
            seqs[s] += rng.choices(vocab, k=200)
        r = requests.post(args.url + "/generate", json={
            "input_ids": seqs[s],
            "sampling_params": {"temperature": 0, "max_new_tokens": 128, "ignore_eos": True},
        }).json()
        records.append({"session": s, "turn": turn,
                        "cached_tokens": r["meta_info"]["cached_tokens"],
                        "output_ids": r["output_ids"]})
        seqs[s] += r["output_ids"]
json.dump(records, open(args.out, "w"))
```

```python
# compare_exact.py
import json, sys
ref, run = (json.load(open(p)) for p in sys.argv[1:3])
for turn in sorted({r["turn"] for r in ref}):
    pairs = [(a, b) for a, b in zip(ref, run) if a["turn"] == turn]
    same = sum(a["output_ids"] == b["output_ids"] for a, b in pairs)
    print(f"turn {turn}: {same}/{len(pairs)} identical")
```

</details>

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`Qwen/Qwen3-8B` on one RTX 5090 with `--enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-size 8 --hicache-write-policy write_through` and the default device pool, so every finished request starts a write-through. Load: `python -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random-ids --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts 320 --max-concurrency 32 --request-rate inf --seed 1`. Runs interleaved ABBA, a fresh server per run.

| run (order) | output tok/s | median TPOT (ms) | median TTFT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| main, 1st | 772.1 | 24.07 | 3353 |
| this PR, 1st | 771.6 | 23.11 | 3364 |
| this PR, 2nd | 772.4 | 23.09 | 3356 |
| main, 2nd | 773.1 | 24.23 | 3350 |

Output throughput: main 772.6 mean, this PR 772.0 (-0.08%). That is inside the spread between the two `main` runs (0.13%), so no throughput cost is measurable at this load. Median TPOT is not worse.

An earlier measurement on a heavier HiCache load: Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it (FP8) at 20-32 concurrent multi-turn sessions with frequent load-backs, one RTX 5090, single runs per point against the unfenced build. It showed -1.0% to -1.8% output tok/s, consistent across points. Without repeats that is close to noise, so a small real cost under heavy write-through cannot be excluded.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (no user-facing change)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Unit tests (pytest on a GPU host, rebased on f2f0be731c): `test_hicache_staged_write_back_dispatch.py` and `test_hicache_pp_sync_drain.py` pass (25). Before the rebase, `test/registered/unit/managers` and `test/registered/unit/mem_cache` matched `main` plus the new case; the one failure there (`test_mm_process_config.py::TestStreamOrderedMmFeaturePool::test_consumer_slot_uses_global_tp_rank`) also fails on `main` in the same environment.

title: [Fix] PD: retraction restores racing the in-flight decode forward
author: jumanzii
body:
## Motivation

On a PD decode server with the overlap scheduler, a retracted request's KV restored on resume can be overwritten by a forward that is still running. This holds for both retraction backups (`--disaggregation-decode-retraction-backup host_pool` or `cpu_tensor`; one of them is picked by default).

The decode event loop processes step N-1's results only after launching step N. A request that finished in step N-1 is still in batch N, so that forward writes the KV of its last token into a slot the request owned. Its slots, that one included, go back to the allocator when step N-1's result is processed (the decode radix cache is off by default). In the next iteration, `process_decode_queue` -> `DecodePreallocQueue.resume_retracted_reqs` can allocate those slots to a resumed request, and `restore_kv_cache` copies the backup into them:
- the `host_pool` backend issues a host-to-device copy on the L2 transfer stream, ordered only after an event on the scheduler stream;
- the `cpu_tensor` backend copies on the scheduler stream.

The scheduler stream does not wait for forward N's KV writes. `_apply_war_barrier` waits only for the forward's shared reads, unless it falls back to the coarse barrier. So the restore can land first, and forward N then overwrites a restored token with the finished request's KV. The resumed request continues decoding with one corrupted token in its context.

The prebuilt path in `get_new_prebuilt_batch` already drains the in-flight forward for the same reason, from #35748: `self.schedule_stream.wait_stream(self.forward_stream)` before a prebuilt request seeds a possibly reused row and before its host-received KV is restored. `resume_retracted_reqs` had no such wait.

## Modifications

- `DecodePreallocQueue.resume_retracted_reqs`: under the overlap scheduler, make the scheduler stream wait for the forward stream before each `restore_kv_cache`. Both backends issue their copy after work on the scheduler stream (the `host_pool` copy waits on an event recorded there), so both are ordered after the forward that may still write the reused slots. As with the prebuilt path, this gives up overlap for the step in which a retracted request resumes; resuming is rare (after retraction under memory pressure).
- `test_decode_queue_cleanup.py`: the hand-built scheduler of `test_paged_swa_retraction_resume_uses_physical_page_budget` sets `enable_overlap=False`.
- Test `test_resumed_restore_lands_after_the_inflight_forward` in `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_decode_retraction_backup.py` (CUDA). It uses real pools and a real `UnifiedRadixCache` with a host pool, and reproduces the interleaving deterministically:
  - a "forward" stream sleeps (`torch.cuda._sleep`) and then writes the slots that the resumed request is given;
  - `resume_retracted_reqs` then runs on the scheduler stream;
  - the restored KV must survive.
  On `main` the stale write lands after the restore and the test fails. A first pass with a short sleep loads every kernel first: CUDA lazy loading synchronizes the device on a kernel's first launch, which would otherwise order the race by accident.

Default behavior, not an option: the alternative is silent KV corruption, and the wait applies only in the iteration that resumes a retracted request.

This came out of auditing the retraction backup (`UnifiedRadixCache.backup_kv_cache`) for the overlap write-through race fixed in #42701. The backup is not exposed: it copies only `seqlen - 1` tokens, and the forward in flight at retraction writes only position `seqlen - 1`, so every copied position was written by a forward whose result the scheduler has already processed. The restore side, here, is exposed.

Out of scope: KV that the prefill server writes over RDMA into slots preallocated in the same iteration (`pop_preallocated`) is not ordered after the in-flight forward either. Transfer latency likely hides it, and I have not verified it.

Related: #42701 fences HiCache write-through copies for the same kind of race. The two PRs are independent and can merge in either order.

## Accuracy Tests

Not run end to end: reproducing this needs a PD deployment under enough memory pressure to retract and resume decode requests, and I did not set one up. The unit test above reproduces the interleaving on a GPU against the real pool, cache and restore code.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not measured. The wait runs only in a scheduler iteration that resumes a retracted request.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (no user-facing change)
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Test results (RTX 5090, CUDA 13, torch 2.14.1, rebased on f2f0be731c):
- New test on `main`: fails, the restored KV is replaced by the in-flight write. With this PR: passes. Reproduced on two machines.
- `test_decode_retraction_backup.py` and `test/registered/unit/disaggregation`: 662 passed.
- Before the rebase, `test/registered/unit/managers` and `test/registered/unit/mem_cache` matched `main` plus the new case; the one failure there (`test_mm_process_config.py::TestStreamOrderedMmFeaturePool::test_consumer_slot_uses_global_tp_rank`) also fails on `main` in the same environment.

title: [Spec] Fix wrong tokens from compact-verify CUDA graphs when a token tier is captured more than once
author: ormandj
body:
## Motivation

With compact ragged verify (`SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=compact`), `DecodeCudaGraphRunner` captures a token tier more than once when there are several attention graph variants (for example the DSv4.1 candidate graphs `candidate_unfiltered` / `candidate_filtered`) or several PD-mux streams. Each capture calls `_capture_ragged_verify_layout`, which allocated a new `RaggedVerifyLayout` and replaced `_captured_ragged_layouts[num_tokens]`. At replay, `_stage_ragged_verify_layout` copies the live `verify_lens` / `qo_indptr` only into that registered layout, which belongs to the last capture. Graphs from the earlier captures still read the layout they were captured with. That layout holds synthetic capture offsets, and replay no longer refreshes it.

A graph that reads an earlier capture's layout tensors directly computes with the wrong offsets whenever the live layout differs from the capture-time one. On current main, PD-mux with the TRT-LLM MLA backend is exposed: its ragged verify path pads and unpads queries with the captured `verify_lens` / `qo_indptr` inside the graph. For DSv4.1 target verify on current main the defect is latent, because its backend copies the live layout into its own buffers outside the graph. The ragged Engram hashing and `token_req_indices` in #40567 read `qo_indptr` inside the DSv4.1 verify graph; with them, the `candidate_unfiltered` graphs map tokens to the wrong requests.

I measured an A/B on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (TP4, 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, SM120, DSpark gamma 5, compact verify, #40567 applied) with an earlier revision of this fix, which copied the live layout into each capture instead of sharing one layout per tier. I compared the log-prob of each generated token with a plain prefill of the same text:

- Without the fix, per-token differences reached 14.4 nats. At temperature 1, 9 of 32 streams looped to the length cap.
- With the fix, the maximum difference was 0.79-0.86 nats, and none of the 32 streams looped or hit the cap.

Eager verify was correct in both builds.

## Modifications

`_capture_ragged_verify_layout` creates the layout once per token tier and returns the same object for later captures of that tier. Every graph of the tier now captures the tensors that replay refreshes.

## Accuracy Tests

- `TestRaggedVerifyLayoutPerTier` (CPU, `test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_decode_cuda_graph_runner.py`) calls the capture-layout helper twice for tier 24 with two variant labels, stages a live layout, and checks both returned layouts' `qo_indptr_device` / `verify_lens` against the live padded layout. On main the first layout keeps its synthetic offsets (7 of 9 `qo_indptr` entries differ).
- The end-to-end A/B in Motivation (earlier revision of the fix).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not benchmarked. The replay staging code is unchanged; capture reuses one registered layout per token tier across attention variants and PD-mux streams.

title: [Fix] [AMD] hicache: Serve encoder-replay prefix hits with a paged DSpark draft SWA
author: ormandj
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4.1 with DSpark and `--enable-encoder-swa-bounded-replay` keeps the target's SWA state in a per-request window (`DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool.request_window`), which replay rebuilds on admission. Since #44673 the CUDA DSpark draft keeps its SWA in a per-request ring, so on CUDA the radix tree has no SWA component under encoder replay. On HIP the draft still addresses a paged SWA pool through the target's allocator, so the tree keeps an SWA component that only the draft uses. `SWAComponent.create_match_validator` and the Rust tree core's validator skip the SWA gate only for the per-request SWA ring (`is_swa_req_ring`). With HiCache on and no SWA host pool, every host-only node fails that check: `host_hit_length` stays 0 and `load_back` never runs, so the host tier fills up but never serves a hit. Device nodes whose draft SWA was evicted are rejected the same way, although replay rebuilds the target window in both cases.

Measured before #44673, while the CUDA draft still used paged SWA: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4 on 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), DSpark, encoder SWA replay, HiCache ratio 2: send a 54K-token prompt, then about 2.74M tokens of unrelated prompts to evict it from the 2.64M-token device pool, then the same prompt again. I measured this with an earlier revision of this fix, on an older upstream base; this exact diff was not benchmarked.

| | host-hit tokens | TTFT after eviction (cold) |
|---|---|---|
| before | 0 | 4.98 s (7.43 s) |
| after | 53,760 | 0.72 s (7.30 s) |

Both runs recovered the passkey from the prompt.

#42446 changes the same Python gate for HiCache without an SWA host pool. This PR also covers the Rust tree core and request windows with HiCache off, and keeps the SWA match gate for paged allocators without a request window.

## Modifications

- `CacheInitParams.swa_gates_prefix_match` declares whether tree-held SWA gates prefix matching. `kv_cache_builder` sets it to `False` for a per-request SWA ring, and for paged SWA beside the target's encoder-replay `request_window`, which only the draft then uses (after #44673, on HIP only). The tree no longer inspects the allocator or the pool.
- `SWAComponent`'s validator reads the flag, and `RustUnifiedTreeCore` passes it to the Rust core's existing `swa_req_ring` gate flag. No Rust change; the ring check `is_swa_req_ring` moves from the validator into the builder.
- `test_rust_tree_core_integration.py`, parameterized over both tree cores with stand-in request windows:
  - `test_swa_match_ignores_tombstones_with_a_request_window`, with and without HiCache: an SWA tombstone no longer truncates the reusable device prefix.
  - `test_swa_host_only_prefix_matches_with_a_request_window`: a backed-up prefix demoted to host, with no SWA host pool, is a host hit (`host_hit_length == 8`) with a request window and still a miss with paged SWA.
  - All request-window cases pass with this change.

Note for reviewers: without an SWA host pool, host load-back does not restore the DSpark draft's paged SWA history. Encoder replay rebuilds the target window; ordinary prefill injects draft state for uncached tokens. Whether the missing draft history lowers initial acceptance is unmeasured. Draft tokens are verified against the target logits.

## Accuracy Tests

The passkey check above (earlier revision); the unit tests listed in Modifications.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The comparison in Motivation (earlier revision): TTFT after eviction 4.98 s before, 0.72 s after.

title: [Fix] dsv41: Run DSpark compact verify by mapping packed verify tokens to their requests
author: ormandj
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #39173.

With `SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=compact`, DSpark target verify can pack unequal numbers of tokens per request. A compact CUDA graph tier can also hold more requests than full verify windows: for example, 42 tokens over 8 slots captures as `[6, 6, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5]`. Two DeepSeek-V4.1 components still assume `draft_token_num` tokens per request:

- `EngramHasher.forward` asserts `num_tokens == bs * draft_token_num`. Capture fails with `engram target-verify expects one equal block per request, got 42 tokens for 8 requests of 6`.
- `token_req_indices` calls `repeat_interleave(req, draft_token_num, output_size=num_tokens)`, which fails, or maps tokens to the wrong request, once the layout is not uniform.

As a result, DeepSeek-V4.1 compact verify fails on these layouts.

#40567 by @lidekang160122 identified both call sites and fixes them as part of a larger PD change. This PR fixes only the crash. It derives the token-to-request mapping in one shared helper and reuses Engram's existing extend kernel path, so it needs no kernel changes.

Depends on the shared-layout fix from #42709, now in main: both components read the verify layout inside the CUDA graph, and without it the DeepSeek-V4.1 graph variants captured first for a token tier would read a layout that replay does not refresh.

## Modifications

- `ragged_verify.py`: add `ragged_verify_token_rows(layout, num_tokens)`. It is a fixed-size `searchsorted` over the layout's `qo_indptr`, so it is safe under CUDA graph capture. Empty rows own no tokens, and the graph-padding tail maps to row `bs`.
- `EngramHasher.forward`: with a ragged layout, target verify uses the existing `MODE_EXTEND` path with `row = ragged_verify_token_rows(layout, num_tokens).clamp_max(bs - 1)` and `starts = layout.qo_indptr_device[:-1]`. As before, verify commits no history. Graph-padding tokens are hashed with the row the staged layout assigns them (a padding row, or the last row for the tail) and then discarded.
- `token_req_indices`: with a ragged layout, each token gets its request's pool index. The tail past the last request gets pool slot 0, like the padded rows of a dense verify graph; padding the staged layout assigns to a row gets that row's slot.
- Without a layout (static verify), both functions take the existing dense path unchanged.
- No change to capture slot sizing. The current `min(num_tokens, max_bs)` slots are valid once these components accept unequal rows.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/test_dsv41_compact_verify.py` (CPU tests and a CUDA graph replay test; all pass on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell):
  - Packed Engram hashes equal the hashes of each request verified alone on the dense path. Cases: the 42-token / 8-slot capture geometry, a batch with empty rows and a graph-padding tail, and one request in a 3-token graph. All three cases run with maximum n-gram sizes 4 and 8 and include a short prefix; the first two also include an image token. Engram history is unchanged.
  - A uniform layout gives the same Engram hashes and request indices as the dense path.
  - `token_req_indices` maps empty rows and the padding tail correctly.
  - A CUDA graph captured once is replayed with three different layouts, and Engram hashes on real tokens and request indices on all tokens match eager.
- `TestCapturedVariantsReadStagedLayout` (CPU, same file) calls `DecodeCudaGraphRunner`'s layout-capture helper twice for a 12-token tier, as the two DeepSeek-V4.1 attention variants do, stages live lengths [6, 1] for request slots 7 and 9, and checks that `token_req_indices` and `EngramHasher` read the live boundaries from either variant's layout. Without the shared layout from #42709, the first variant maps the real tokens to [7, 7, 9, 9, 0, 0, 0]. All six tests in the file, including the CUDA graph replay test, pass on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell.
- `test/registered/spec/dspark/test_ragged_verify.py`: unit test of `ragged_verify_token_rows`.
- An ad-hoc comparison with #40567's implementation on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), not part of this PR, gave bit-identical Engram hashes on real tokens and bit-identical request indices on all tokens. Coverage was 146 eager layouts (73 at each of n-gram sizes 4 and 8) and 22 CUDA graph replays, including the 42-token geometry, single-request graphs of 1 to 5 tokens, empty rows, and padding tails.
- End to end, I served DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with #40567's implementation and #42709 (not with this exact diff). Setup: 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120, PCIe), TP4/EP2, DSpark gamma=5, compact verify with a profiled SPS table. I compared target log-probs of generated tokens with a plain prefill of the same text. The maximum per-token difference was 0.79-0.86 nats, the same as static verify. A temperature-1 run of 32 streams had no repetition loops.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The change itself adds one `searchsorted` per Engram call and per low-ratio request lookup in compact verify. Static verify is unchanged. Not benchmarked separately.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [DSA] Fix pooled page table refresh for target verify CUDA graph replay
author: mmangkad
body:
## Motivation

Fixes wrong DSA indexer page ids in speculative verify under CUDA graphs, which dropped `TestGLM53FlashB200DFlash2` below its GSM8K threshold. Caused by a semantic conflict between two PRs:

- #42178 changed `build_pooled_page_table_64` to return logical page ids (`real page id // pool_size`).
- #42489, branched before that change and merged ~6h later without a rebase, added a target-verify refresh in `update_pooled_paged_mqa_metadata` that writes the undivided `real_page_table[:, ::pool_size]`.

On main, target-verify replay therefore passes page ids `pool_size`× too large (4× for GLM-5.3-Flash).

## Modifications

Refresh the table with `torch.floor_divide(real_page_table[:, ::pool_size], pool_size, out=pooled_real_page_table)`. This matches `build_pooled_page_table_64` exactly and writes in place into the captured buffer in a single kernel.

## Accuracy Tests

`test_glm53_flash_b200.py::TestGLM53FlashB200DFlash2`, 4× GB300, GSM8K (500 questions, 20-shot, threshold 0.93):

| | GSM8K |
|---|---|
| Before | 0.892 |
| After | 0.930 |

`test_dsa_metadata_replay.py` fails on main (1596/12288 mismatched pooled page-table entries in `TARGET_VERIFY`) and passes after.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Per-call cost of the refresh on GB300 (24×2048 int32 table, `pool_size=4`):

| Variant | Time |
|---|---|
| `build_pooled_page_table_64` + `copy_` | 55.0 µs |
| `floor_divide(..., out=)` (this PR) | 16.9 µs |

title: [rust-processor] Fix chat-template precedence wording in the processor README
author: ShangmingCai
body:
Follow-up to #42662.

## Motivation

The processor README added in #42662 describes `load_chat_formatter` as resolving, in order: a built-in name, a legacy template inferred from the model path, the tokenizer config's Jinja template, then a `--chat-template` file. That reads as if the tokenizer config takes precedence over an explicit file.

`render/loader.rs` does the opposite: a `--chat-template` file replaces the tokenizer config's template, and the model-path legacy inference only runs when no argument was given. A host author following the README would expect the wrong precedence.

## Modifications

Reword the one sentence in the `render` section to match the loader:

- built-in name first;
- with no `--chat-template`: legacy template inferred from the model path, then the tokenizer config's Jinja template;
- with a `--chat-template` file (`.jinja` or JSON): that file.

Docs only, no code change.

title: [Fix] model_loader: Avoid unsafe pickle fallback when loading PyTorch checkpoints
author: nguyendvk
body:
## Motivation

`torch.load(weights_only=False)` deserializes with pickle, so a crafted checkpoint can execute code when it is loaded. `_load_pt_file` fell back to it for legacy tar checkpoints, and several loaders called `torch.load` on model files without `weights_only=True`. This is the same class of issue as #35653 (RIFE) and is consistent with the contribution guide's rule against unpickling untrusted data.

- Pass `weights_only=True` to `torch.load` in `deepseek_ocr.py` (x2), `roberta.py` and `rife_interpolator.py`.
- Add unit tests for `_load_pt_file`: a tensor state dict still loads, and a pickle payload is not executed.
- `srt/debug_utils` is unchanged: it reads developer-written tensor dumps, not model weights.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: only the checkpoint deserialization path changes; no model forward code is touched.

title: fix(dsa): align FA3 metadata with unpadded queries
author: Jzz1943
body: ## Motivation GLM-5.3-Flash fails during breakable prefill CUDA Graph capture when using FA3 with MegaMoE: ```text RuntimeError: batch_size must be equal to batch_size_k ``` MoE synchronization can pad the DSA length metadata, while the prefill attention bridge narrows the query tensors and page table to the real token count. FA3 then receives inconsistent batch dimensions. For example, 19 real query tokens can be passed with 20 entries in `cache_seqlens` and 21 entries in the cumulative sequence-length arrays. #41311 addressed the pooled-indexer output row mismatch. This PR fixes the remaining FA3 metadata mismatch. ## Modifications Update `DeepseekSparseAttnBackend._forward_fa3()` to: - Detect trailing metadata padding for the one-token-per-sequence sparse DSA layout. - Validate that the page table matches the query count and that both cumulative-length arrays match the padded metadata count. - Slice `cache_seqlens`, `cu_seqlens_q`, and `cu_seqlens_k` to the effective query count before calling FA3. The slices are local views and do not modify the original metadata tensors. The change adds no tensor-value reads or CPU/GPU synchronization. Inputs without excess metadata remain unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests ### Server launch command ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \ sglang serve \ --model-path /path/to/GLM-5.3-Flash \ --served-model-name llm \ --trust-remote-code \ --tp-size 4 \ --ep-size 4 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.75 \ --max-mamba-cache-size 240 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill 8192 \ --cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable \ --dsa-prefill-backend fa3 \ --dsa-decode-backend fa3 \ --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 \ --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm \ --moe-a2a-backend megamoe \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \ --speculative-num-steps 5 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 \ --reasoning-parser glm45 \ --tool-call-parser glm47 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` The same command was used before and after applying the fix. ### End-to-end reproduction Tested on **4 × NVIDIA H200** with **GLM-5.3-Flash**, based on upstream commit `49bafb58cd6`. Configuration: - TP4 / EP4 - Breakable prefill CUDA Graph, chunk size and maximum capture size: 8192 - FA3 for both DSA prefill and decode - BF16 KV cache - DeepGEMM MoE runner with MegaMoE all-to-all - EAGLE: 5 speculative steps, top-k 1, 6 draft tokens **Before:** startup fails during prefill graph capture with the error above. **After:** graph capture and server startup complete successfully with the same configuration. ### GSM8K Evaluated the patched server using: - 100 examples, 5-shot - 8 concurrent evaluation threads - 2 repetitions - Temperature 0, maximum output length 4096 - `reasoning_effort=low` | Run | Accuracy | | --- | --- | | 1 | 99/100 | | 2 | 99/100 | The unpatched configuration cannot complete startup, so no end-to-end accuracy baseline is available for this configuration. ### Isolated FA3 validation Separate H200 kernel-level validation passed eight cases covering padded and unpadded inputs, NoPE and RoPE, eager execution, and CUDA Graph replay. title: [DSv4] Fix shared index cache accessor page size
author: kpham-sgl
body:
DSv4's non-paged FP8 indexer prefill crashes because `DeepSeekV4IndexerPool` does not expose the storage page size expected by the shared DSA accessor. #42178 introduced this dependency; #42671 renamed the field to `index_page_size`. Reported in [this comment](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42671#issuecomment-6026933917).

Set `index_page_size` to the pool's physical page size.

Validation:
- Pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed.
- Manual H200 check using real DSv4 pools and the unmodified Triton gather: main raises the missing `index_page_size` error for 64- and 128-slot pages; the PR returns exactly the expected keys and scales for two sequences with non-sequential pages and partial final pages.
- Manual DSv4 Flash FP8 server comparison on 4 H200s, TP4: a 9000-token prefill enters the non-paged gather on all four ranks with its default enablement and 8192-row threshold. Main crashes with the reported attribute error; the PR completes prefill and generates 8 tokens (HTTP 200).
- Server comparison used a 16384-token prefill chunk, 32768-token cache budget, SWA/full ratio 1, and disabled graphs/radix caching to keep the full request eligible. DeepGEMM compiled on demand. This was a functional reproduction, not an accuracy or performance benchmark.

title: [Fix] moe_sum_reduce: gate the bf16 vectorized path on hidden % 16
author: Monishver11
body:
## Motivation

`moe_sum_reduce` has a vectorized bf16 path for `token_num > 256` that sums 16-element chunks per lane (`VEC = 16` in `moe_sum_reduce_warp_per_token_vec_kernel`), but the launcher gates it on `hidden_dim % 8 == 0` and sizes the grid from `hidden_dim / 8`. A bf16 input whose hidden dim is 8 mod 16 (e.g. 104, 120, 1032) therefore takes the vectorized path and its last 8 columns are never written, so the output keeps whatever the buffer held. At `hidden_dim = 8` no column is written at all. No shipped model config has such a hidden dim, so this is latent, but the kernel is reachable from the Triton fused-MoE runner for any `topk != 2` and it silently returns garbage for those shapes.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/moe/moe_sum_reduce.cu`: the gate and the chunk count now derive from one shared `BF16_VEC` constant that the kernel also uses, so the three literals cannot drift again. Rows that are 8 mod 16 fall through to the scalar warp-per-token path, which writes every column. Also drops a redeclared `stream` inside the fast path that shadowed the one three lines above. 13 lines.
- `python/sglang/kernels/aot/tests/test_moe_sum_reduce.py`: regression test, three cases at 257 tokens: hidden 8 and 104 (the broken shapes) and 2048 (still on the vectorized path, guards the gate change). The output buffer is pre-filled with NaN so an unwritten column cannot pass.

## Accuracy Tests

RTX 4090, torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0. The patched `.cu` was built standalone with `torch.utils.cpp_extension` against the installed `sglang-kernel==0.4.7` wheel's headers and compared with the wheel's kernel.

| bf16, 257 tokens, topk 8 | wheel (main) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| hidden 8 | 8 NaN columns | matches fp32 reference |
| hidden 104 | 8 NaN columns | matches fp32 reference |
| hidden 2048 | correct | correct |

On the shapes the wheel handles correctly the output is bit-identical to the wheel (`torch.equal`) across fp16/bf16/fp32, tokens {1, 32, 257, 1024}, topk {2, 8, 9, 17}, hidden {16, 100, 2048, 7168}: 0 mismatches over 192 combinations.

The new test fails 2 of 3 cases on the current wheel and passes with the fix.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance change. Shapes with `hidden_dim % 16 == 0` take exactly the same path and launch as before; the only shapes that move are the broken ones, which now go to the scalar path instead of producing unwritten columns.

title: [Fix] Merge DeepSeek-V4 two-batch-overlap microbatches without a residual
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #42936
* #42898
* #42897
* #42896
* #42895
* #42894
* #42893
* #42892
* __->__ #42891

## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4 runs its own two-batch-overlap layer loop (`DeepseekV4Model._forward_layers_tbo`), and its layers carry no residual between them, so each microbatch's output has `residual=None`. Since #42307, the shared `_model_forward_tbo_merge_outputs` reads both outputs' residual as a `ResidualStream`, so DeepSeek-V4 prefill with `--enable-two-batch-overlap` fails at the first merge:

```
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'pending'
```

The AMD nightly `test_deepseek_v4_flash_fp8_tbo.py` fails with this error; there is no NVIDIA test for DeepSeek-V4 two-batch overlap.

## Modifications

- Move the token-range concatenation into `_model_forward_tbo_merge_key(output_a, output_b, name, original_len)`. DeepSeek-V4 merges its hidden states with it directly; the stream-carrying merge keeps its single caller, `model_forward_stages`. The old path only completed an owed sum on DeepSeek-V4's output, and `hc_post` returns a plain tensor, so dropping it changes no value.
- Add the NVIDIA counterpart of the AMD nightly: `test_deepseek_v4_flash_fp4_b200_tbo.py` (registry `nightly-4-gpu-b200`) launches DeepSeek-V4-Flash with TP 4, attention DP 4, DeepEP and `--enable-two-batch-overlap`, gated on GSM8K ≥ 0.93.

title: [Fix] Return an FFN's output to the attention rows at a pipeline handoff
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #42936
* #42898
* #42897
* #42896
* #42895
* #42894
* #42893
* __->__ #42892
* #42891

## Motivation

With an a2a MoE backend and attention TP above 1, an FFN leaves its output and the residual on this rank's attention-TP slice of the rows, and the next layer's attention gathers its input from there. That holds within a rank but not across a pipeline handoff. The sending rank's last FFN is bound against the next rank's first stage rather than as the end of the stack, so it hands over the slice. The receiving rank's PP buffers hold every token's row, so its first FFN fails with a row mismatch. Qwen3-30B-A3B with DeepEP at TP 2 × PP 2 × EP 2 fails on `main` at PP rank 1's first FFN:

```
The size of tensor a (64) must match the size of tensor b (128)
```

## Modifications

- An FFN whose output crosses to another pipeline rank returns it to the attention's rows (`exit_rows=ATTENTION`), so both ranks agree on what the handoff carries:
  - The sending rank marks its last stage that way before any stage of the stack binds, so a branch that reads that stage (`prepared_from`) binds against the same declaration.
  - The receiving rank marks the neighbour stage it reads the same way.
- An FFN that computes on this rank's own rows (`_ffn_on_rank_rows`, the predicate `_resolve_ffn` already used) also writes its output into the residual at the handoff, on every batch (`StageDeclaration.writes_at_handoff`), so the handoff carries the written stream alone. Its exit completes the output there rather than leaving work for the next stage, which is on another rank.
- The receiving rank knows the stream arrives written from the producer's declaration, as it already does for MHC's written streams (`residual_in_hidden`), not from which tensors arrive. A captured decode CUDA graph's PP input buffers hold a `residual` for every non-MHC model whether or not the sender sent one. An FFN on the attention's rows still hands off its residual, and `from_pp` still requires it.
- `test_append_stages.py` (`TestPipelineHandoff`):
  - The sending rank's last FFN returns its output to the attention rows and writes it, also when its move leaves the residual.
  - The receiving rank's first stage reads the attention rows, and reads the stream as written even with a residual beside it.
  - A handoff from an FFN on the attention's rows carries its residual, which the receiver requires.
- `build_stages` in `boundary_fixtures` uses the stack's neighbour hooks to stand in for this rank's own neighbouring layers, so it turns the handoff off.

## Accuracy Tests

- Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepEP + `deep_gemm`, TP 2 × PP 2 × EP 2 on B200: crashes on `main`; with this change it serves, and two launches give identical logprobs.
- Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepEP, TP 2 × PP 2 × EP 2 on H200 (fa3, deterministic inference):
  - GSM8K (200): 0.935. Decode with CUDA graphs and eager decode give identical answers on all 200; `main` crashes.
  - One request at a time, answers are identical on 60/60 to one rank handing off at the same layer (layer 23 of 48), and with CUDA graphs off every layer's input matches that run bit for bit, in prefill and in decode.
  - With `--disable-attn-tp-gather`, decoding a request alone and then four at once gives coherent output with CUDA graphs. Graphs and eager decode still pick different greedy tokens on some prompts, as they do in that configuration without PP; `main` fails to serve it.
- Unchanged where no FFN leaves a slice. On H200, GSM8K with TP 2 × PP 2 (deterministic inference, fa3) matches `main` exactly: 0.930 on both arms, 200/200 identical answers. This was measured at the top of this stack.
- CPU: at the top of this stack, a 217-file battery shows no new failure against `main`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: only configurations that crashed before (a2a MoE with attention TP across a pipeline handoff) change.

title: [Fix] Kimi K3 KDA value head size and SiTU input alignment
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #42936
* #42898
* #42897
* #42896
* #42895
* #42894
* __->__ #42893
* #42892
* #42891

## Motivation

`inference-optimization/Kimi-K3-0.40B`, a small Kimi K3 checkpoint, fails on `main` at two places that the full-size model never reaches:

1. `KimiK3DeltaAttention` takes its value head size from `config.v_head_dim`, which is the MLA layers' value head size. The KDA layers use `linear_attn_config["head_dim"]` for keys and values alike, as the reference modeling code and the KDA state cache do. When the two sizes differ (32 vs 64 here), the value projection and the decode output do not match the state cache, and the first packed decode fails:
   ```
   ValueError: `out` must have shape (512, 1, 4, 32) (got out.shape=(512, 1, 4, 64)).
   ```
2. `situ_and_mul` passes a row-strided 2D input straight to the kernel, which reads each row in vectors of up to 32 bytes and rejects a stride that is not a whole number of them. Kimi K3's fused MoE front hands it the shared experts' `gate_up` as a slice of `[gate_up | router logits | latent]`. With few experts, that slice's stride is not a vector multiple.

## Modifications

- Size the KDA values by `linear_attn_config["head_dim"]`.
- `situ_and_mul` takes the dense copy for a row stride that is not a whole number of the kernel's 32-byte vectors of the wider dtype, as it already does for any other input the kernel cannot read in place.

## Accuracy Tests

- With the full-size Kimi K3 dimensions, neither path changes: the KDA head size equals the MLA value head size (128), and with 896 experts the slice's stride is aligned.
- Kimi-K3-0.40B now gets past both failures. On B200, serving it end to end still needs an MLA backend that accepts its `kv_lora_rank=128` and `qk_rope_head_dim=32`; `trtllm_mla` rejects those, and the triton backend does not compile them.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: the copy is taken only for misaligned strides, which the full-size model does not produce.

title: [Fix] Shard Kimi K3's shared experts over the TP group they sum over
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #42936
* #42898
* #42897
* #42896
* __->__ #42895
* #42894
* #42893
* #42892
* #42891

## Motivation

Without an a2a MoE backend, a Kimi K3 MoE runs its shared experts on the TP group, and `_reduce_shared` all-reduces their output over it. The shared experts were built without explicit TP arguments, so under DP attention with `--enable-dense-mlp-attn-tp` they took the dense MLP's attention-TP sharding instead. Each attention-TP replica then computed the full shared output, and the TP all-reduce added `attn_dp_size` copies of it.

## Modifications

- Build the shared experts on the TP group explicitly.
- Every other configuration already resolved to that group, and an a2a backend keeps its own shared-expert layouts.
- `test_kimi_mlp_parallel_groups.py` also checks the shared experts' placement at TP 4 × attention DP 2 with `--enable-dense-mlp-attn-tp`: without an a2a backend they shard over the full TP group.

## Accuracy Tests

B200, synthetic Kimi K3 without dense layers (`first_k_dense_replace=0`), TP 4 × DP 2, deterministic inference. The reference is the same configuration without `--enable-dense-mlp-attn-tp`:
- `main` with `--enable-dense-mlp-attn-tp` differs by 0.69 in logprob, and its greedy tokens differ.
- This change with `--enable-dense-mlp-attn-tp` is bit-identical to the reference.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: only `--enable-dense-mlp-attn-tp` under DP attention changes, where each rank now computes its TP shard of the shared experts instead of all of them.

title: [Fix] Run attention on a padded extend batch's real rows
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #42936
* #42898
* #42897
* __->__ #42896
* #42895
* #42894
* #42893
* #42892
* #42891

## Motivation

MLP sync pads each rank's extend batch to a multiple of attention TP (`input_ids`, `positions`, `out_cache_loc`), while the attention metadata still covers only the real tokens. The prefill CUDA graph path already runs attention on the real rows. In eager mode, though, the backends got the padded queries:

- flashinfer's paged and ragged prefill and flashinfer MLA's ragged path reject them. Qwen3-30B-A3B with DeepEP at TP 2 fails as soon as prefill runs eager, as it does by default under pipeline parallelism:
  ```
  q.shape[0] (6) does not match qo_indptr[-1] (5)
  ```
- The other backends compute only the rows their metadata covers and leave the rest of the output uninitialized.

## Modifications

- `RadixAttention` does in eager what the prefill graph path does:
  - it runs the backend on the real rows, with the cache locations and positions narrowed for the call;
  - it allocates the padded output up front, with the graph branch's allocation (`_new_attention_output`, now shared). A backend that writes into `forward_batch._attn_output` (flashattention, triton, aiter, trtllm_mha's NVFP4 output) fills the real rows in place; another backend's output is copied in. Only the padded tail is zeroed. A backend that returns more than its output (its LSE, or a sparse indexer's output beside it) returns a tuple, which is padded as it comes, so no output is allocated for that call.
- K and V go with the queries unless the caller gives them an extent of their own, the layer is a cross-attention (K and V are the encoder's), or they have a different row count. K and V that hold a cached prefix declare their extent: the chunked-prefix chunks did, and DeepSeek's one-shot MHA, whose K and V cover every token of the sequences, now does too, so they are never taken for padded rows when their row count happens to equal the padded query count.
- The other per-row inputs are narrowed with the rows they belong to:
  - `rel_bias`, `aux_tensors`, the q/k/v descales and the mxfp8 deferred norm/RoPE inputs, from the list the graph path's extra-kwargs route already narrows (`_PER_ROW_EXTRA_KWARGS`, now shared);
  - `k_rope` and the k/v descales follow K and V; a sparse indexer's `idx_q` follows the queries and its `idx_k` / `idx_v` the keys, as the prefill graph's sparse attention already narrows them (MiniMax's backend trimmed them itself only while it received the padded queries).
- The FA4 wrappers (`flash_attn_varlen_func` and `flash_attn_with_kvcache` in `flash_attention_v4.py`) pass `out=` on to the kernel. They dropped it, so FA4 allocated a second output that was then copied in; the output the prefill graph path preallocates now reaches FA4 too. Where the wrapper pads MLA query heads, or the kernel is a released flash-attn-4 build without `out=`, the result is still a new tensor.
- trtllm_mha's FMHA-v2 prefill (SM90 and SM120) also writes into the output it is given, as its other prefill kernel already did, so the padded call and the prefill graph path no longer copy a second output in.
- DeepSeek's born-FP8 query for DSA's `flashmla_sparse_q8` prefill (`SGLANG_ENABLE_DSA_Q8KV8_BORN_FP8_Q`) is prepared for every row but handed to the backend for the rows its attention call takes: the stash records the real rows of a padded extend (`padded_extend_real_tokens`, the same test the narrowing uses), which the backend reads as a prefix of the rows written.
- Target verify, which plans its padded rows itself, is left as it is.
- The real count comes from `global_num_token_non_padded_cpu`, which every batch carries.
- Kimi K3 trimmed its own attention to the real rows for the same reason, counting them from `extend_seq_lens_cpu`, which GPU-only batches leave unset. That trim is removed, together with:
  - the padded o_proj output it kept for the SP collectives;
  - the trimmed `out_cache_loc` it left on the batch.
- `test_radix_attention_padded_extend.py` covers:
  - only padded extend batches are narrowed;
  - the backend sees the real rows and the tail is zero;
  - keys with their own extent or row count, or a cross-attention's, are left whole, also when they are as long as the padded queries (a cached prefix, or encoder rows);
  - the per-row inputs follow the rows they belong to, a sparse indexer's too (each index output shaped by the query rows);
  - the output is written in place or copied, with `_attn_output` restored afterwards.

## Accuracy Tests

- Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepEP, TP 2, deterministic inference (flashinfer), eager prefill, on B200: crashes on `main`, both with and without PP 2; runs with this change.
- `trtllm_mha` in eager prefill, which ran on the padded batch before: identical before and after.
- The output buffer handling and the per-row narrowing change no value. Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepEP, TP 2, deterministic inference, eager prefill, 24 prompts of uneven length (every process takes the padded path 51–351 times): with the backend's own output copied in (flashinfer) or written in place (triton and fa4 on B200, fa3 on H200), input and output logprobs are bit-identical to narrowing Q, K and V alone.
- FA4 output reuse, counted at the FA4 kernel call (Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepEP, TP 2, deterministic inference, B200), two launches per tree:
  - eager prefill: all 381 padded attention calls per process now hand the preallocated output to FA4 and get it back (none before). A padded attention call's peak memory drops from 609 KiB to 309 KiB, one real-row output (75 rows × 2048 × 2 bytes);
  - prefill CUDA graph: the 6,465 FA4 calls that have a preallocated output now write into it (none before);
  - input and output logprobs are bit-identical to before in both modes.
  - the same on an HGX B300 (SM103): the same counts and peak memory, and bit-identical logprobs in both modes.
- DeepSeek one-shot MHA over a cached prefix on a padded extend (a 4-layer DeepSeek-V3 config with dummy weights, DeepEP TP 4, flashinfer, eager prefill, `SGLANG_CHUNKED_PREFIX_CACHE_THRESHOLD=1`, B300): a 3-token cached prefix and 9 new tokens padded to 12, so K and V have as many rows as the padded queries. Without the declared extent, K and V were cut to 9 rows on every MLA layer and the greedy tokens changed; with it, the output is bit-identical to the same request without the prefix cache, in two launches.
- MiniMax-M3's sparse attention (its released config cut to 6 layers, index values on in two of the five sparse layers, dummy weights), TP 4 × DP 2 attention, eager prefill, on B300. Narrowing q, K and V without the indexer's inputs fails in `store_kv_index`, whose `idx_k` keeps the padded rows. With them narrowed, every padded call hands the backend the real rows for q, `idx_q` and `idx_v`, and the index output comes back on those rows. Sending the 24 prompts one at a time, so that each launch runs the same batches (9 of the 24 prefills padded), the greedy tokens match `main` on all 24 prompts. The logprobs differ from `main`'s by at most 0.0073; `main` differs from its own second launch by 0.0068.
- trtllm_mha's FMHA-v2 on H200 (Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepEP TP 2, eager prefill, requests one at a time): all 192 padded attention calls per process now hand FMHA-v2 the preallocated output and get it back (none before), saving one real-row output per call; input and output logprobs are bit-identical to before.
- DSA's born-FP8 query (`SGLANG_ENABLE_DSA_Q8KV8_BORN_FP8_Q=1`, `flashmla_sparse_q8` prefill, FP8 KV cache) on H200: a DeepSeek-V3.2 config cut to 4 layers with bf16 dummy weights, TP 4 × DP 2 attention, eager prefill, 12 long prompts sent one at a time. On the padded prefill, every layer's stash records the real rows the attention call reads; stashing every written row instead fails the backend's check (`q8kv8 born-fp8 q stash mismatch: stashed (num_tokens=2082, layer_id=0) but consuming (num_tokens=2081, layer_id=0)`). Input and output logprobs are bit-identical to `main`, to the same run with the born-FP8 query off, and across two launches.
- Inkling-Small-NVFP4 with FA4's sheared relative bias, TP 4 × DP 2 attention, eager prefill on B200: narrowing Q, K and V alone fails FA4's `assert rel_bias.shape == (total_q, num_head, rel_extent)` on all four ranks; with the per-row inputs narrowed too it serves. (Inkling's output under DP attention is wrong on `main` as well, GSM8K 0.03, so that configuration has no accuracy to compare; at TP 4 this PR and `main` both score 0.74 with identical answers on the first questions.)
- Kimi K3 (synthetic, DeepEP TP 2, eager prefill, 5-token prompt padded to 6 rows), its own trim against this narrowing, per layer and per rank:
  - with the attention-residual bank: real and padded rows identical;
  - standard residual path: identical, except one launch of the trimmed tree that also differs from the trimmed tree's own second launch.
- H200 (fa3, deterministic inference), Qwen3-30B-A3B GSM8K at the top of this stack, against `main`: TP 4, TP 4 × DP 2 attention, TP 2 × PP 2, TP 4 × EP 4 DeepEP, and TP 4 × DP 4 attention × EP 4 DeepEP all give the same accuracy (0.915–0.930) and 200/200 identical answers.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: unpadded batches are unchanged; a padded eager batch now runs the backend on its real rows only, and FA4 writes into the output buffer it is given instead of allocating another.

Memory, on B300 (Qwen3-30B-A3B's config with dummy weights, DeepEP TP 2, eager prefill, deterministic inference):
- A padded attention call's own peak, 127 real of 128 rows × 2048: triton, which writes in place, 528,384 bytes, the padded output; flashinfer, whose output is copied in, 1,044,480 bytes, the padded output plus its real-row output, released at the end of the call. FA4 writes in place too (above).
- The whole run's peak allocated and reserved memory per rank is identical to `main`'s to the byte with triton and with FA4.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Fix] unified-memory: enabling trtllm_mha with decode graphs and speculative decoding
author: caihuali95
body:
## Motivation

Under `--enable-unified-memory`, trtllm_mha could not run with decode CUDA graphs (the gate refused them, because each replay's page-table refill took the previous replay's lengths), and it was not in `TRANSLATED_MHA_RAILS`, the MHA backends allowed to read a speculative draft's KV through the unified pool's index translation, so no speculative algorithm could use it as a target or a draft. #42753's per-iteration `KVLocPlan` closes the read side: the graph refill copies the plan's table, built from this batch's `seq_lens` plus the window it writes, and the graphs-off path reads the same table. This PR fixes the remaining trtllm_mha defects on the unified pool, two of which also affect the static pool, and adds trtllm_mha to `TRANSLATED_MHA_RAILS`. Seven commits on main: 11 files, +840/-61.

## Modifications

1. **Lift the decode-graph refusal** (`arg_groups/kv_cache_hook.py`). With #42753 the refill covers every page a replay reads: plain decode, and the draft decode, target verify and draft extend replays of speculative decoding.
2. **Zero MHA pages when they are handed out** (`allocator/unified_sub_pool.py`, `unified_memory_pool.py`, `kernels/ops/kvcache/zero_pages.py`). trtllm_mha's fmha_v2 prefill (SM90/SM120) loads K and V a whole page at a time and masks the positions past a request's length only in the scores, so their V rows still enter P·V with a zero probability, and 0 × NaN is NaN; XQA decode does the same with an fp8 KV cache (its bf16 kernel zero-fills those rows). MLA pools already zero on hand-out (#33974); MHA pools did not, and under a mamba hybrid those bytes can hold fp32 recurrent state that reads as bf16 Inf/NaN (Qwen3.5-9B GSM8K 0.49 against 0.90 at `--mem-fraction-static 0.30`).
3. **Require packed page tables on the graphs-off path** (`layers/attention/trtllm_mha_backend.py`). XQA decode and fmha_v2 prefill are handed only a page table's data pointer and take its row length from its width; they ignore its strides. The plan's table is a column view of a wider tensor only when a captured graph had it built in its own buffer earlier in the same iteration and the batch is narrower than that buffer, which no known configuration produces; such a table would be misread silently. The backend now asserts that both of its tables (full and sliding-window) are packed. These tables stay as wide as the batch needs, while the captured and static ones are `max_num_pages` wide, and XQA sizes its multi-block split from the width: graphs-off decode can round differently, the same attention but not bit-identical.
4. **Keep the reserved page 0 out of the debug poison fill** (`unified_memory_pool.py`). `SGLANG_DEBUG_POISON_POOL` also filled page 0, which the pool reserves as the target of a sliding window's freed slots and which XQA reads at zero weight, so a poisoned window-model run reported NaN that serving never sees.
5. **Keep fmha_v2 prefill out of XQA's workspace semaphores** (`trtllm_mha_backend.py`; static pool too). On SM90/SM120 both kernels share one workspace, and fmha_v2's tile counter sat on XQA's first multi-block semaphore. After any prefill, the next small-batch XQA launch dropped a tile of its output: Qwen3.5 with NextN or DFLASH on trtllm_mha hit NaN in the first draft step and scored 0.19-0.55 on GSM8K, against 0.89 on triton. XQA's 8 MiB of semaphores now come on top of the configured workspace, and fmha_v2 gets the part past them, so fmha_v2 and XQA's scratch each keep the whole configured size.
6. **Copy only the batch's pages for the fmha_v2 prefill** (`trtllm_mha_backend.py`; static pool too). fmha_v2 takes K and V as one `[pages, 2, page_size, heads, head_dim]` tensor, and the backend stacked the layer's whole pool for every prefill layer: 0.4-2.6 ms per layer, about 6x that on the unified pool's strided views. It now copies each row's own pages, back to back, straight into one buffer, so a prefill's extra memory is the copy itself; a batch that reads no fewer pages than the pool holds keeps the whole-pool stack.
7. **Add trtllm_mha to `TRANSLATED_MHA_RAILS`** (`kv_cache_hook.py`, `mem_cache/kv_cache_configurator.py`). trtllm_mha reads every path a draft forward takes through the plan, so it joins that list, which gates the EAGLE/EAGLE3 target of an MHA model, every EAGLE/EAGLE3 draft, the DFLASH target, and the decision whether a draft's KV is fused into the target's pages. DSPARK's target set is unchanged. The comment and docstring that named trtllm_mha as a draft that declines fusion go.

Tests (each fails without its change):

- `test_trtllm_mha_graph_metadata.py`: decode, draft-decode, target-verify, draft-extend and ragged-verify replays, through the real `KVLocPlan` and a page map rewritten before every replay, read only the current replay's pages (a refill bounded by `cache_seqlens_int32`, or a table without the read extent, fails them); a graphs-off table that is a strided view of a wider buffer fails the packed-table assert; fmha_v2's workspace stays off the semaphores and keeps the configured size, at the default and at an explicit `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_SIZE`; its prefill copies only each row's own pages, and the copy's peak memory stays within the copy's own size, from a packed and a strided pool alike.
- `test_unified_handout_zeroing.py`: MHA pools, Mamba pools and pools that combine Mamba state with sliding-window layers zero pages on hand-out; the poison fill spares page 0.
- `test_unified_prefill_cuda_graph_gate.py`, `test_unified_memory_spec_gate.py`, `test_fused_draft_placement.py`: decode capture boots; trtllm_mha is admitted for EAGLE/EAGLE3 (target and draft) and DFLASH and stays refused for DSPARK's target; a trtllm_mha draft fuses.

## Accuracy Tests

SM90, TP1, radix cache, trtllm_mha on both arms (page size 64). Baseline: the static pool. Unified: `--enable-unified-memory` with lazy compaction (the default), plus eager compaction (`SGLANG_DISABLE_LAZY_COMPACTION=1`) where a table lists it. GSM8K, all 1314 test questions, 5-shot, greedy. Every unified arm ran on a poisoned pool (`SGLANG_DEBUG_POISON_POOL=1`, every never-written byte a bf16 NaN), so a read of a slot nobody wrote collapses the score instead of hiding. Everything below ran on this PR's current commits, based on main 7224fce1b5 with FlashInfer 0.7.1.

No speculation (`--mem-fraction-static 0.8`):

| model | CUDA graphs | baseline | unified | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-9B | off | 0.896 | 0.896 | +0.0 |
| Qwen3.5-9B | on | 0.894 | 0.894 | +0.0 |
| gpt-oss-20b | off | 0.534 | 0.529 | -0.5 |
| gpt-oss-20b | on | 0.552 | 0.565 | +1.3 |

Qwen3.5-9B with NextN and DFLASH on trtllm_mha (`--mem-fraction-static 0.3`, overlap scheduler). The draft fuses into the target's pages on every unified arm; the NextN draft runs on trtllm_mha itself.

| draft | CUDA graphs | GSM8K baseline / unified eager / unified lazy | accept length |
|---|---|---|---|
| NextN | off | 0.897 / 0.897 / 0.893 | 3.50 / 3.50 / 3.51 |
| NextN | on | 0.895 / 0.893 / 0.897 | 3.50 / 3.50 / 3.50 |
| DFLASH | off | 0.896 / 0.895 / 0.896 | 6.32 / 6.32 / 6.27 |
| DFLASH | on | 0.897 / 0.896 / 0.896 | 6.26 / 6.31 / 6.29 |

The same NextN and DFLASH configurations on main's static pool score 0.186-0.188 (NextN) and 0.554-0.559 (DFLASH): the workspace collision that commit 5 fixes.

gpt-oss-20b with EAGLE3, page size 64, `--mem-fraction-static 0.3`, overlap scheduler, with per-step pool checks and the allocator invariants on (`SGLANG_ENABLE_STRICT_MEM_CHECK_DURING_BUSY=1 SGLANG_CHECK_KV_PAGE_INVARIANTS=1 SGLANG_INVARIANT_CHECK=1`), the static pool run twice. These ran with the four fixes listed below applied (#43168 is needed for gpt-oss EAGLE3 at a page size above 1 on any backend). No leak, double free, invariant violation or illegal memory access on any arm; accept length 1.27-1.28 on every arm.

| backend | CUDA graphs | baseline / baseline repeat / unified eager / unified lazy |
|---|---|---|
| triton | off | 0.543 / 0.492 / 0.557 / 0.557 |
| trtllm_mha | off | 0.570 / 0.532 / 0.545 / 0.552 |
| triton | on | 0.556 / 0.554 / 0.559 / 0.502 |
| trtllm_mha | on | 0.511 / 0.537 / 0.524 / 0.535 |

gpt-oss-20b's GSM8K score moves by several points between identical runs: the two static-pool runs of the triton graphs-off row differ by 5.1. Paired per question, the triton graphs-on unified lazy arm sits within that spread, and its accept length matches the other arms.

GPU unit tests for unified memory: 4123 passed, 0 failed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`bench_serving` with random prompts at concurrency 64, in two shapes: 2048 input / 512 output tokens (200 prompts) and 8192 input / 64 output tokens (100 prompts). trtllm_mha on both arms, radix cache, overlap scheduler, CUDA graphs on, `--mem-fraction-static 0.55`, one server at a time. The baseline runs twice, and each delta is unified against the mean of the two baseline runs, with the spread between those two runs (A/A) beside it. These ran on this PR's current commits with the four fixes below applied: without #43170 and #43171, main's own unified-pool costs on these two models (host syncs in gpt-oss-20b's sliding-window frees, Triton GDN prefill on Qwen3.5) dominate the gaps.

2048 input / 512 output tokens:

| model | speculation | req/s | mean TTFT | mean ITL | mean TPOT | mean E2E |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-9B | none | -0.7% (A/A 0.3) | +3.2% (0.4) | +0.3% (0.3) | -0.1% (0.2) | +0.7% (0.3) |
| gpt-oss-20b | none | -0.3% (0.2) | +0.2% (0.0) | +0.3% (0.2) | +0.3% (0.2) | +0.3% (0.2) |
| Qwen3.5-9B | NextN | -0.2% (0.0) | +0.4% (0.0) | -0.1% (0.0) | -0.6% (0.0) | +0.2% (0.0) |
| Qwen3.5-9B | DFLASH | +0.8% (0.0) | -0.8% (0.0) | -1.4% (0.1) | -3.4% (0.0) | -0.9% (0.0) |

8192 input / 64 output tokens:

| model | speculation | req/s | mean TTFT | mean ITL | mean TPOT | mean E2E |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-9B | none | -0.5% (A/A 0.1) | +1.3% (0.1) | -0.1% (0.2) | -0.2% (0.1) | +0.4% (0.1) |
| gpt-oss-20b | none | -0.2% (0.0) | +1.0% (1.9) | -0.3% (1.3) | +0.2% (0.6) | +0.2% (0.0) |
| Qwen3.5-9B | NextN | -0.4% (0.1) | +0.6% (0.1) | +0.5% (0.1) | +0.7% (0.1) | +0.5% (0.1) |
| Qwen3.5-9B | DFLASH | -0.3% (0.1) | +0.2% (0.1) | +0.2% (0.0) | +0.1% (0.0) | +0.2% (0.1) |

- Qwen3.5-9B's higher TTFT without speculation comes from scheduling: on the unified pool the radix cache keeps more (79.2k vs 23.6k cached tokens over the run), so the arms schedule different prefill batches.
- On prefill batches with identical new and cached token counts in both arms' logs, unified prefill throughput is 0.997-1.000 of the baseline's in every configuration above.
- Accept length is the same on both arms: NextN 3.49, DFLASH 7.09 (median over each run).
- On the static pool alone, this PR is faster than main (same configuration, no speculation, the static pool run twice on each side), because the fmha_v2 prefill no longer copies the whole pool: at 2048 input / 512 output tokens, Qwen3.5-9B +3.6% req/s and -4.0% mean ITL, gpt-oss-20b +11.6% req/s and -11.7% mean ITL; at 8192 input / 64 output tokens, Qwen3.5-9B +1.5% and gpt-oss-20b +5.8% req/s.

## Notes for reviewers

- The gpt-oss-20b EAGLE3 accuracy runs and the unified-pool speed tests ran with four other unified-memory fixes applied on top of this PR: #43168 (page-aligned sliding-window retention for unaligned windows), #43170 (sliding-window frees without a host sync), #43171 (FlashInfer GDN prefill on page-major pools) and #43169 (allocation eviction against the joint full/sliding-window fit). Each is independent of this PR.
- Validated on SM90 only. Through the same list, a draft that a model hook puts on trtllm_mha on SM100 (Kimi-Linear / Kimi-K3 with DSPARK) now fuses into the target's pages, and an MLA target's EAGLE draft may run on trtllm_mha; neither runs on this hardware.

title: Fix EVS for NemotronH_Omni_Reasoning_V3
author: elvischenv
body:
## Motivation

EVS on `NemotronH_Omni_Reasoning_V3` breaks outside the single-video case:

- Image + video in one request crashes the scheduler (`AssertionError` in EVS redistribution).
- Multiple videos with `video_temporal_patch_size=2`: tubelets span video boundaries (shape mismatch with EVS, wrong embeddings without).
- A 1-2 frame video crashes the scheduler (`AttributeError: 'EVSEmbeddingResult' object has no attribute 'reshape'`): it takes the per-image path, which expects a tensor.

## Modifications

- Processor: videos sent with dynamic-res images now get EVS metadata; video items carry `frames_per_video`.
- Model: encode temporal tubelets per video; always store padded ids in `pre_chunked_input_ids` so EVS redistribution keeps image pad values.
- EVS: return unpruned features when every video is a single frame/tubelet (nothing to prune).
- Match the HF tubelet label format (`Frame N ... and frame M`).
- Unit tests for each fix; each fails on the old code.

## Accuracy Tests

TP4 H100, `video_pruning_rate` 0.7 and 0.0: single video, odd-frame video, image + video, two videos, and a video crossing the chunked-prefill boundary all run and give correct answers. Before this PR, image + video crashed the server.

TP2 B200, `video_pruning_rate` 0.7: a 1-frame video crashed the server before the single-frame fix and now answers correctly; single video, two videos, and image + video still pass.

title: [Fix] [NPU] mla-pool: DCP allocator page and index-K bound, short-pool warning
author: TamirBaydasov
body:
## Motivation

Small fixes to the NPU MLA KV pool, found while serving GLM-5.2 with 1M-token contexts on Ascend A3.

1. **DCP on NPU: the allocator page and the index-K bound.** `_alloc_page_size` did not ask the NPU allocator,
   whose page is `page_size * dcp_size` (CUDA, HIP and XPU already do). This only changes behaviour at
   `--page-size 1`, which DSA on Ascend cannot run today (the Lightning Indexer needs a block size that is a
   multiple of 16), so it is a latent bug. Index-K writes also had no bounds check against the widened index range.
2. **A pool that cannot hold one full-length request fails late.** When the pool is smaller than
   `--context-length`, nothing is logged at startup. Long requests are refused or truncated at serving time.

This PR first also removed the `is_arch35` gate on the compact index-K layout. #44436 has since made the same
change on main, so that part is gone from this diff. Only a test that both sides agree is left (see Tests).

## Modifications

- `allocation.py`: `_alloc_page_size` returns the NPU allocator's page size under DCP, as on CUDA/HIP/XPU.
- `memory_pool_npu.py`: `set_index_k_buffer` checks writes against the widened index range (async
  out-of-bounds check, active with `SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT=1`).
- `TpModelWorker.get_worker_info`: a startup warning when the served `kv_capacity` is below `--context-length`.
  It is checked there because that is the final served value, so DCP and page-interleave widening are counted.
- `kv_cache_configurator.py`, `pool_configurator.py`: comments on why the NPU DCP allocator is widened and why
  the indexer term scales with `dcp_size`.

**Behaviour change for users without DCP:** none, except the new warning when the pool is short.

## Accuracy Tests

No forward-path change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speed change.

## Tests

- `test/registered/unit/managers/test_dcp_logical_capacity.py` (CPU), new case
  `test_short_pool_warning_uses_served_capacity`: dcp1 serves fewer tokens than the context and warns; dcp2
  widens the same rows past it and does not.
- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_npu_index_k_elision.py` (CPU): on A2/A3 the memory budget and the pool
  count the same Indexer layers. The tests #44436 added check each side on its own; this one fails if only one
  side changes.

title: [AMD][Fix] Saturate FP8 KV commits instead of reproducing e4m3fnuz NaN overflow
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
## Motivation

`jit-kernel-unit-test-amd` has been red on `main` since #40785 merged. Every run that has executed the job since has failed identically — #40785's own run, two on #34537, and one on an unrelated branch, all reporting `30732 / 65536` mismatched elements at the same index. The job only runs when a PR touches `python/sglang/kernels/`, so most PRs skip it and it went unnoticed.

Full evidence in #42981.

## Modifications

torch's `float8_e4m3fn` cast saturates to its max finite value. `float8_e4m3fnuz` has no infinity, so `fp8e4m3fnuz_from_fp32_value` returns NaN (`0x80`) for every magnitude at or above 256.0. Triton's cast saturates on both types, so the fused commit kernel from #40785 matches eager on CUDA and diverges on gfx94x.

This is not only a test problem. `set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid` has a fused path and an eager fallback, and on ROCm they now write different bytes for the same input — the fallback writes NaN into a committed KV slot, which poisons attention for that slot on every later read.

Rather than have the test chase whichever cast runs, this makes saturation the defined contract and clamps before the FP8 cast in all three places:

- `cache_move.py` — the kernel clamps, with the limit passed as a `tl.constexpr`; NaN falls through both `tl.where` arms. Two vector ops added to a memory-bound kernel.
- `memory_pool.py` — the eager fallback clamps identically, so the two production paths agree.
- `test/kernels/prefix_valid.py` — the shared oracle clamps identically.

The limit is `torch.finfo(fp8).max`, not the conservative `fp8_max` constant (224.0 on fnuz): clamping at 224.0 would pull values that eager rounds to 240.0 down a step.

All three are no-ops on CUDA, where the eager cast already saturates to 448.

## Test plan

`jit-kernel-unit-test-amd` on MI300 / ROCm 10: **42/42 files passed** ([job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37648241557/job/113082433719)), including `test_prefix_valid_fp8.py` and `test_prefix_valid_fp8_pool.py`. For reference, the same job on current `main` fails at 6/42 with 30732/65536 mismatched elements.

An earlier revision of this branch clamped in FP32, which turned the `bf16/fp16 -> fp8` cast into `fp32 -> fp8`; those lower to different conversions and left 2/65536 elements off by one FP8 subnormal step at fp16 with a host scalar scale. Clamping in the source dtype restores the original lowering, and that is the version here.

Still red on this PR, all reproducing on #40785 or unrelated to this path:

- `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd (7)` — MiniMax sparse decode kernel requests 128 KiB LDS against a 64 KiB limit (`OutOfResources`), same partition red on #40785.
- `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x (1)` — red on #40785.
- `extra-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd` — `test_e2e_spec_eagle.py`; the server stops responding mid-stream (`RemoteDisconnected`), with no CUDA/HIP fault, scheduler exception or OOM in the log. That test runs `kv_cache_dtype=auto`, so `self.dtype` is not FP8 and neither the fused branch nor the eager clamp in this PR is reached — the non-FP8 commit path goes through `set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid_tiled`, which is untouched here. The same job is also red on #40785, on a different test.
- NPU jobs — `set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid` returns early for non-CUDA/non-HIP before reaching any line this PR touches.

If you would rather the kernel reproduce eager's `e4m3fnuz` NaN-on-overflow instead of saturating, I can invert the patch — but that writes NaN into the KV cache on AMD and diverges from the CUDA path, so saturation looks like the better contract.

## Checklist

- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).
