title: fix(openai): preserve zero cached tokens when cache reporting is enabled
author: ai-jz
body:
## Motivation

With `--enable-cache-report`, zero means reporting was enabled and no prompt tokens came from cache. The current OpenAI-compatible usage path filters that valid value into `prompt_tokens_details: null`, making it indistinguishable from disabled reporting:

```diff
-"prompt_tokens_details": null
+"prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0}
```

The [OpenAI Responses SDK model](https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/v2.21.0/src/openai/types/responses/response_usage.py#L8-L15) represents `cached_tokens` as an integer, and [SGLang's Responses serializer](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/7760d5264ac16b85392aefb1bf5c13ce38d9632e/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py#L2138-L2152) already emits an explicit zero when no cache details are present. Preserving zero when cache reporting is enabled makes the existing Chat Completions and Completions usage behavior unambiguous and consistent with that Responses behavior.

This distinction matters for workload-level metrics such as AgentX: its [run-level cache-read percentage](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/agentx-harness/blob/56a0cf70f4c0359454ee4bd15a17770b541a3e3e/src/aiperf/metrics/types/usage_total_metrics.py#L320-L362) includes cache observations across requests, its [trace accounting includes zero-hit first turns](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/agentx-harness/blob/56a0cf70f4c0359454ee4bd15a17770b541a3e3e/tests/unit/dataset/loader/test_weka_trace.py#L978-L993), and it [distinguishes an explicit zero from missing cache reporting](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/agentx-harness/blob/56a0cf70f4c0359454ee4bd15a17770b541a3e3e/src/aiperf/metrics/cache_reporting_hint.py#L35-L45). Filtering zero therefore turns a valid cold observation into missing telemetry.

Credit to @EazyReal for identifying the issue and implementing the original fix in #28801. This PR reapplies only the zero-value fix on current `main`; the separate legacy Completions continuous-usage change remains out of scope.

## Minimal Reproduction

Start a server with cache reporting enabled and the radix cache disabled. Disabling the cache makes the zero-hit case deterministic.

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 30000 \
  --enable-cache-report \
  --disable-radix-cache
```

Then issue one non-streaming Chat Completions request:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with OK."}],
    "temperature": 0,
    "max_tokens": 1
  }' | jq '.usage.prompt_tokens_details'
```

Before this fix:

```json
null
```

After this fix:

```json
{
  "cached_tokens": 0
}
```

The same presence rule applies to buffered and final streaming usage.

## Modifications

- Gate cache details on `enable_cache_report`, not on whether the count is positive.
- Apply the same rule to buffered, final-stream, and existing Chat continuous-usage paths.
- Add focused CPU coverage for zero, positive, and disabled-reporting cases.

This does not enable cache reporting on paths that do not already provide it, and it does not change cache accounting, scheduling, model execution, or model output.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable; generated tokens and model outputs are unchanged. The source-level protocol matrix passed for zero, positive, and disabled reporting in buffered and final-stream usage. Pre-commit, `py_compile`, and `git diff --check` passed for all changed files. The registered CPU test remains for hosted CI because the local host lacks SGLang's PyTorch/FastAPI runtime.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable; this does not change inference, scheduling, kernels, or cache lookup.

## Compatibility and Merge Danger

- **Door:** Two-way; reverting restores the previous omission behavior.
- **Blast radius:** OpenAI-compatible usage metadata with `--enable-cache-report`.
- **Preserved behavior:** Disabled reporting remains absent and positive counts are unchanged.
- **Canary:** Verify integer `cached_tokens` values for one uncached and one cache-hit request in buffered and streaming usage.

## Checklist

title: fix(openai): honor tool_choice=none in DeepSeek encoders
author: ai-jz
body:
## Motivation

OpenAI defines `tool_choice: "none"` as generating a message without calling any tool. SGLang's [shared prompt-building path](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/7760d5264ac16b85392aefb1bf5c13ce38d9632e/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py#L1386-L1400) already leaves active `tools` unset for this value, and its [response path disables tool-call parsing](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/7760d5264ac16b85392aefb1bf5c13ce38d9632e/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py#L1015-L1025). However, the [custom DeepSeek branch](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/7760d5264ac16b85392aefb1bf5c13ce38d9632e/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py#L1590-L1602) bypassed the shared input decision by reading `request.tools` directly and rendered the tool schema plus [DSML call instructions](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/7760d5264ac16b85392aefb1bf5c13ce38d9632e/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/encoding_dsv41.py#L76-L92) into the model prompt.

The custom DSV4.1 encoder was introduced in [#39665](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39665), which preserves client-supplied tool fields and ordering and validates the encoding against the V4.1 reference. This PR leaves that serialization unchanged; it only withholds the tool payload when SGLang's shared active-tool decision is `none`.

That mismatch can expose the model to DSML tool-call instructions while the response path treats its output as ordinary text. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, the minimized failure had this shape:

```text
request.tool_choice = "none"
response.message.tool_calls = null
response.message.content contains a raw <｜DSML｜ calls> invocation
response.finish_reason = "stop"
```

Minimal HTTP reproduction:

```bash
curl http://localhost:30000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Solve 100 divided by 7."}],
    "tools": [{
      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "calculator",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {"expression": {"type": "string"}},
          "required": ["expression"]
        }
      }
    }],
    "tool_choice": "none",
    "temperature": 0
  }'
```

Expected: a normal assistant message with no tool call and no DSML tool-invocation syntax in `content`.

This restores SGLang's existing input/output decision for `none`, while preserving the observable [OpenAI Chat Completions contract](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/chat/subresources/completions/methods/create): the model does not call a tool and instead generates a message.

## Modifications

- Reuse `_process_messages`' normalized active-tool decision when populating the custom DeepSeek encoder input.
- Omit tool schemas from `dsv4`, `dsv32`, and `dsv41` prompts when `tool_choice` is `none`.
- Preserve the existing typed payload and prompt behavior for active tool modes.
- Add a CPU unit test covering `none` and `auto` for all three DeepSeek encoding specifications.

This PR does not change tool parsing, detector behavior, tool schema serialization, or inference kernels.

## Accuracy Tests

This is a request-contract fix, not a model-forward change. The registered CPU test covers `none` and `auto` across `dsv4`, `dsv32`, and `dsv41`. Pre-commit, `py_compile`, and `git diff --check` passed for all changed files. The unit test and an end-to-end `none`/`auto`/`required` canary remain for hosted CI because the local source environment lacks PyTorch.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. This PR does not change model execution, scheduling, or kernels. Requests using `tool_choice: "none"` render a shorter prompt because unused tool definitions are omitted.

## Compatibility and Merge Danger

- **Door and blast radius:** Two-way; limited to OpenAI-compatible chat requests using `dsv4`, `dsv32`, or `dsv41` encoders.
- **Intentional behavior change:** `tool_choice: "none"` no longer exposes tool schemas or tool-call instructions to the model.
- **Preserved behavior:** Active modes retain the original typed payload, including DSV4.1 serialization.\n

(Not applicable to model accuracy or kernel performance; targeted contract evidence is included above.)

title: fix(openai): keep chat stream created timestamp stable
author: ai-jz
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek's Chat Completions contract states that every streaming chunk has [the same timestamp](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/api/create-chat-completion/). OpenAI likewise defines `created` as the time when the chat completion was created, and its [streaming example](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/chat/subresources/completions/methods/create) reuses one value for the role, content, and finish chunks.

The [DeepSeek Provider Verifier](https://github.com/smg-project/deepseek-provider-verifier/blob/161fee64de1a59eb21e2c19563f0d64347a1fc78/src/deepseek_provider_verifier/protocols/chat.py#L227-L242) treats `(id, created, model)` as the streaming response identity and reports a response-envelope violation if any member changes. This exposed an SGLang behavior difference: Streaming Chat Completions currently recompute `created` while emitting chunks. A response that crosses a one-second boundary can therefore keep the same `id` and `model` while changing `created`.

SGLang calls `time.time()` while constructing the [role and finish chunks](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/7760d5264ac16b85392aefb1bf5c13ce38d9632e/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py#L2088-L2140), as well as content, tool-call, extension, and usage chunks. This PR captures one response-level creation time and reuses it without adding a provider-specific mode.

## Minimal Reproduction

Start an SGLang server with any chat model, then request a stream long enough to cross a one-second boundary:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 30000
```

```python
import json

import requests

payload = {
    "model": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct",
    "messages": [
        {"role": "user", "content": "Write a detailed 1,000-word explanation of radix trees."}
    ],
    "max_tokens": 1024,
    "stream": True,
    "stream_options": {"include_usage": True},
}

with requests.post(
    "http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions",
    json=payload,
    stream=True,
) as response:
    response.raise_for_status()
    chunks = [
        json.loads(line[6:])
        for line in response.iter_lines(decode_unicode=True)
        if line.startswith("data: {")
    ]

created = [chunk["created"] for chunk in chunks]
print(sorted(set(created)))
assert len(set(created)) == 1
```

Before this fix, a stream that crosses a second boundary prints more than one timestamp and fails the assertion. After this fix, every role, content, finish, extension, tool-call, and usage chunk carries the same response creation time.

## Modifications

- Capture `created` once when `_generate_chat_stream` starts.
- Pass that value through all content and tool-call helpers and reuse it for every response chunk.
- Add a focused CPU test whose mocked clock advances between calls and verifies that all parsed chunks keep the first timestamp.
- Extend existing tool-stream tests to verify that helper-generated chunks use the caller's response timestamp.

This does not change model execution, generated tokens, chunk ordering, usage placement, or provider-specific behavior.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable to model accuracy; this changes response-envelope metadata only. Targeted pre-commit checks, `py_compile`, and `git diff --check` passed for all changed files. The registered CPU test was added but remains for hosted CI because the local source environment does not include SGLang's PyTorch runtime.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. This does not change inference, scheduling, kernels, or token streaming. It replaces repeated wall-clock reads with one read per streaming response.

## Compatibility and Merge Danger

- **Door:** Two-way; reverting restores per-chunk timestamp calculation.
- **Blast radius:** OpenAI-compatible streaming Chat Completions only.
- **Intentional behavior change:** Long streams now retain one response-level `created` value instead of changing at wall-clock second boundaries.
- **Preserved behavior:** Response IDs, model names, content, finish reasons, tool calls, extensions, usage, and chunk ordering are unchanged.
- **Canary:** Run one stream that crosses a second boundary with usage enabled and verify that every JSON chunk has exactly one distinct `created` value.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No documentation change is needed for this response-envelope bug fix.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Not applicable; generated tokens and inference performance are unchanged.)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: fix(openai): omit absent tool_calls from chat responses
author: ai-jz
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek's Chat Completions response schema defines [`tool_calls` as an optional array](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/api/create-chat-completion/), and its no-tool response example omits the field. When a model does not call a tool, SGLang instead serializes `tool_calls: null` in every non-streaming Chat Completions assistant message. Some streaming paths, including normal text emitted while a tool parser is active, have the same behavior.

The [DeepSeek Provider Verifier](https://github.com/smg-project/deepseek-provider-verifier/blob/161fee64de1a59eb21e2c19563f0d64347a1fc78/src/deepseek_provider_verifier/protocols/chat.py#L93-L97) exposed this difference by rejecting a present non-array value. OpenAI also defines `tool_calls` as optional, and its [no-tool response and streaming examples](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/chat/subresources/completions/methods/create) omit the field. Omitting an absent optional field therefore aligns with DeepSeek's documented response shape while remaining OpenAI-compatible.

The [`/v1/chat/completions` endpoint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/7760d5264ac16b85392aefb1bf5c13ce38d9632e/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/http_server.py#L1779-L1787) uses one `OpenAIServingChat` implementation for every served model. Its [non-streaming response builder](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/7760d5264ac16b85392aefb1bf5c13ce38d9632e/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py#L2419-L2464) initializes `tool_calls` to `None` and always constructs the shared [`ChatMessage`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/7760d5264ac16b85392aefb1bf5c13ce38d9632e/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py#L1209-L1214). This makes the non-streaming behavior model-independent rather than specific to DeepSeek. SGLang's ordinary streaming fast path already omits absent tool calls; only Chat Completions paths that serialize `DeltaMessage` through `ChatCompletionResponseStreamChoice` need the same rule.

## Minimal Reproduction

Start an SGLang server with any chat model:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 30000
```

Then issue a non-streaming request without tools:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with amber."}],
    "temperature": 0,
    "max_tokens": 4
  }' | jq '.choices[0].message'
```

Before this fix, the message includes:

```json
{
  "role": "assistant",
  "content": "amber",
  "tool_calls": null
}
```

After this fix, `tool_calls` is omitted. Requests that produce tool calls still return the existing array unchanged. Chat Completions streaming choices that use `DeltaMessage` follow the same presence rule; the ordinary streaming fast path already omits the field.

The observed verifier failure is non-streaming. The narrower streaming surface is covered separately by the focused unit test rather than claimed as a second end-to-end reproduction or an all-streaming-path failure.

## Modifications

- Omit `ChatMessage.tool_calls` when its value is `None`.
- Omit `delta.tool_calls` only when `DeltaMessage` is serialized inside a Chat Completions stream choice. `DeltaMessage` itself is unchanged because the transcription API also reuses it.
- Preserve actual tool-call arrays and explicitly supplied empty arrays.
- Add focused CPU coverage for absent, empty, and populated tool-call values in complete buffered and streaming Chat Completions JSON payloads.

This does not change prompting, tool parsers, constrained decoding, model output, finish reasons, or tool-call contents.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable to model accuracy; this changes JSON field presence only. Targeted pre-commit checks, `py_compile`, and `git diff --check` passed for all changed files. The registered CPU tests were added but remain for hosted CI because the local source environment does not include SGLang's PyTorch runtime.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. This does not change inference, scheduling, kernels, or token generation.

## Compatibility and Merge Danger

- **Door:** Two-way; reverting restores explicit `tool_calls: null` values.
- **Blast radius:** OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions only: all non-streaming messages without a tool-call list, independent of model, plus streaming choices that use the Pydantic response path. Transcription serialization is unchanged.
- **Intentional behavior change:** Raw JSON consumers see an omitted optional field instead of `null`.
- **Preserved behavior:** Populated tool-call arrays and explicitly supplied empty arrays serialize unchanged.
- **Compatibility basis:** DeepSeek documents an optional array and omits absent tool calls in its example; OpenAI also omits the optional field in its no-tool examples.
- **Canary:** Verify one no-tool buffered response, one no-tool stream, and one actual tool-call response.

A server-wide configurable policy for absent tools could be discussed separately. This PR intentionally limits itself to Chat Completions response serialization.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: fix: use dp_size instead of attn_dp_size for msprobe rank id
author: is-not
body:
The msprobe debugger derives its rank id from attn_dp_size (the attention data-parallel width), which stays 1 when data parallelism is configured via --dp-size without attention DP. As a result every DP replica falls back to rank id None and dumps into the same rank directory, so only rank0 data is collected. Use dp_size (the number of data-parallel replicas) instead so each replica gets a distinct rank id.

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

Fixes #43040 

## Motivation

When launching SGLang with data-parallel replicas (`--dp-size=2`) without attention data parallelism, the msprobe precision dump only collected data from rank 0. This PR fixes the rank-id selection so every DP replica dumps into a distinct rank directory.

In `ModelRunner.forward()`, the msprobe rank id was derived from `attn_dp_size`:

```python
rank_id = self.gpu_id if get_parallel().attn_dp_size > 1 else None
```

`attn_dp_size` is the *attention* data-parallel width (the number of DP attention groups inside a TP group, configured via `--attn-dp-size` / the deprecated `--enable-dp-attention`). It is 1 for plain data-parallel replicas (`--dp-size=2`). As a result `rank_id` was `None`, so msprobe fell back to `torch.distributed.get_rank()`, which is 0 in every replica (each replica is a separate single-rank process). All replicas therefore wrote into the same `rank0/` directory, and only rank 0's data survived.

## Modifications

Use `dp_size` (the number of data-parallel replicas) instead of `attn_dp_size`:

```python
rank_id = self.gpu_id if get_parallel().dp_size > 1 else None
```

Each DP replica runs on a distinct `gpu_id`, so this produces a unique rank id per replica.

## Verification

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <model> --dp-size=2 --msprobe-dump-config ./config.json
```

- Before: dump output contains only `step*/rank0/`.
- After: dump output contains `step*/rank0/` and `step*/rank1/`.

title: [Fix] VLM: harden Kimi image cache identity across preprocessing and radix hashing
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Supersedes #41792. Thank you to **@rchalamala (Rahul Chalamala)** for identifying the Kimi image-cache identity problem and implementing the original fix. This PR retains his original authored commit and builds on that implementation.

Multimodal padding previously reduced an item hash to 30 bits. Different images can therefore share radix-prefix keys and reuse incorrect KV entries. Kimi K2.5/K3 also need image identities that distinguish preprocessing configuration and patch grids, not only feature bytes.

## Modifications

- Share four 62-bit sentinel generation through `MultimodalDataItem.set_hash`, `set_pad_value`, and `set_identity`. Common padding repeats the pattern without changing image-token counts; existing scalar-padding consumers retain the first wide sentinel.
- Derive Kimi image identities from source content, preprocessing configuration, and grid. Cover ordinary, preprocess-cache, preprocessed/precomputed-input, and EPD item-construction paths, including HF `grid_thws` aliases and multi-image splitting. Reject caller overrides of Kimi cache identities.
- Hash the exact input snapshot before decoding and carry its digest alongside the decoded image, avoiding a GPU-to-CPU copy solely to hash ordinary nvJPEG output. Include normalization, patch settings, and the effective backend in the processor fingerprint.
- Recognize all sentinels in embedding scatter and ERNIE's visual mask, including partial chunks.
- Support wide placeholder tokens in C++/Rust page hashing instead of disabling PD, HiCache storage, or KV events. Existing uint32-only page hashes remain unchanged; wide pages use a distinct encoding.

**Why 62 bits per sentinel, not four 30-bit values?** Radix matching can stop after the first sentinel. Actual Python and Rust radix tests reproduce a false image-token hit with four 30-bit values at page size 1, and at page size 16 with 15 preceding text tokens. Later sentinels do not prevent that partial hit.

This hardens prefix-cache identity; it does **not** make every cache key 256 bits or eliminate all theoretical collisions. Generic item hashes and the embedding-cache integer hash remain 64 bits; expanding a 64-bit hash does not create additional entropy. Other models retain their existing identity semantics.

## Validation

Validated at `b28fc89a0b6501b52bd84f375920fce0d051fbc8` on NVIDIA B300 with PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130:

- **153 focused Python tests + 74 subtests passed**, covering Kimi identity, ordinary/EPD item construction, CPU/CUDA embedding scatter, nvJPEG input snapshots, shared hash assignment, and ERNIE's visual mask.
- **82 radix/native hash tests passed**, including 80 combinations across actual Python/Rust trees, page sizes 1/16, image-span lengths, and text-prefix alignment.
- **Four real-weight Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct serving tests passed**: raw images, processor outputs, precomputed embeddings, and a low-30-bit hash-collision regression. Model revision: `66285546d2b821cf421d4f5eb2576359d3770cd3`.
- The same serving regression **fails on the previous PR head `0be7358013f`**: after caching a red image, a blue image with a different caller hash but identical low 30 bits incorrectly receives “Red”; the cold blue control receives “Blue”. The fixed head passes the identical test.
- CPU-hidden validation at `485cfee3ed95` (same production code): 58 tests + 44 subtests passed, with CUDA device count verified as zero.
- Changed-file pinned pre-commit hooks passed. Current-head lint and Rust workspace CI passed. NVIDIA Base is blocked by an unrelated [DeepSeek-V4 test-fixture failure](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39094516913/job/117582869201): main #44920 added a `token_to_kv_pool` access, but the test constructs the backend without that attribute. Both affected files are identical between the tested CI merge `5423749ec971` and its main parent `a0b77db84d9e`; this is not a multimodal identity regression. Remaining CI jobs have not been cancelled, and the full Base cycle has not passed.

Full-weight Kimi serving, two-node PD/EPD, and end-to-end accuracy/performance benchmarks have **not** been run. Qwen serving and item-construction tests do not establish all-model or multi-node deployment compatibility. No serving speedup is claimed.

title: [Spec] Fix DFLASH verify mask policy for wrapped attention backends
author: elvischenv
body:
## Motivation

With DFLASH and split attention backends (`--prefill-attention-backend flashinfer --decode-attention-backend trtllm_mha`, default `--speculative-attention-mode prefill`), target-verify output is corrupted (GSM8K 0.03).

`resolve_dflash_verify_mask_policy` checks the skip list by class name, so `HybridAttnBackend` is not matched and verify CUDA graphs are captured with a custom mask. DFLASH replay always passes `custom_mask=None`, so FlashInfer runs the captured custom-mask kernel on a stale mask buffer.

## Modifications

- Resolve `HybridAttnBackend` / `TboAttnBackend` to the backend that runs `TARGET_VERIFY` before checking the skip list.
- FlashInfer: raise if a verify graph captured with a mask buffer is planned without a mask.
- Add unit tests.

body:

## Motivation

With DP attention and a TP MoE, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode on MI355X produced NaN in the MoE output under CUDA graph and crashed after a few minutes, and decoder SWA bounded replay was rejected for every DP attention layout. title: [Fix] hicache: Defer query beliefs until the rank-synchronized hit drain
author: alphabetc1
body:
In `buffer_only` mode, revoking a storage prefetch can update storage-existence beliefs from rank-local query results before their reduction. TP ranks can then disagree about whether a prefix is already stored and make different backup decisions. Cancellation can also cause a rank to skip the query; that lack of query evidence must not be treated as a storage miss.

This change updates beliefs only when consuming the rank-synchronized `prefetch_hit_queue`:

- Remove query-driven belief updates from `revoke_pending_prefetch`.
- Apply query evidence at the start of each hit-queue drain iteration, before handling removed requests, terminated operations, or below-threshold hits.
- Skip belief updates when the reduced result has no KV verdict, indicating that a rank did not query storage. An explicit zero-page KV verdict remains a real miss and can invalidate existing beliefs.

The added sidecar unit test uses the actual query and synchronization methods with a stub storage backend and simulated MIN reduction. It checks that cancellation preserves existing KV beliefs when the peer skipped the query (`-1`), but invalidates them when the peer reports a miss (`0`). The terminated-query lifecycle fixture also gains `all_hash_values=None` for the belief-update path now reached during draining.

Belief updates reuse the existing synchronized drain and add no collective.

title: [Fix] hicache: Resolve derived sidecars over every source transfer
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

A derived sidecar must follow every independent transfer of its source pool. Taking only the first transfer loses data when a component stages a pool in multiple segments, or when a Mamba host checkpoint is restored to both a radix-cache slot and a request-owned slot.

For split D2H backups, the sidecar can copy only the first segment while storage persists keys for the entire span, leaving stale tail pages. For H2D restores, host slot 2 may need to initialize device slots 4 and 7, but the sidecar previously followed only slot 4.

This fixes the generic multi-transfer sidecar contract introduced by #42633. Mamba load-back can emit two source transfers; the CPU regression explicitly registers a Mamba-derived sidecar. Default packed Mamba draft buffers use a separate dispatch path, so this is not a claim of model-level validation for that path.

## Modifications

- Add `merge_source_transfers` and use it in D2H allocation, H2D allocation, non-KV storage-side resolution, and sidecar descriptor construction. Preserve transfer order, repeated host indices, explicit sidecar device indices, and the single-source tensor aliases.
- Resolve sidecar sources by pool name across component transfers, including component-owned pools outside the fixed SWA/Mamba mapping. Only independent source transfers own their allocations.
- Sum repeated source transfers for byte accounting while retaining current rank-local `transferred_tokens` filtering.
- Move the split-pool CUDA/file-storage regression into the current `unified_radix_cache/test_unified_radix_cache_storage.py` suite and adapt its fixture to the explicit host-pool geometry API.
- Incorporate the six CPU restore/sharding regression cases from #46707. Sam Shleifer is credited with `Co-authored-by: Sam Shleifer <sshleifer@gmail.com>` in the integration commit.

## Accuracy Tests

Updated against main `de6c211a490`. No model weights or model-accuracy benchmark were used.

**CPU restore and staged-transfer regression:** 33 passed, 1 skipped, 8 subtests passed.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_sidecar_restore.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_staged_write_back_dispatch.py
```

**CUDA buffer/storage coverage:** 143 passed, 35 skipped, 12 subtests passed (102 deselected). All 13 supported split-pool sidecar configurations pass, with real D2H copies and file-storage reads verifying every persisted sidecar page against its source.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache/test_unified_radix_cache_storage.py \
  -k "buffer_only or split_pool_sidecar" --disable-warnings
```

**Related regressions:** 60 passed, 40 subtests passed.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_hicache_regressions.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mem_pool_host.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_buffer_mode_sidecar.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_storage_prefetch_lifecycle.py \
  --disable-warnings
```

**Negative controls against main's resolver implementations, using the same new tests:**

- CPU regression: 4 failed, 2 passed. Both active-request restore cases and both repeated-source rank-local accounting cases fail; single-destination controls pass.
- Storage regression (`-k split_pool_sidecar`): 13 failed, 4 skipped, 263 deselected. The old fixed component map rejects the component-owned source pool.
- Reverting only `HostPoolGroup.resolve_host_transfers` to main while retaining the other fixes: `Test_FULL_ps1::test_buffer_only_split_pool_sidecar_storage_roundtrip` fails the persisted-page data comparison. This confirms the test catches stale sidecar data independently of source-pool dispatch.

Pre-commit passed for all six changed files; the final fixture adaptation also passed the commit hooks. GitHub CI results are tracked separately below and are not included in these local validation counts.

title: [Diffusion] Fix int32 offset overflow in the Ulysses packed-QKV pack kernel
author: saatwiknagpal
body:
## Motivation

With Ulysses SP, `_pack_qkv_destination_major_kernel` packs each rank's q/k/v rows for all heads using int32 offsets. Once a rank packs more than 2^31 elements (`rows*3*H*D`), the offsets wrap: part of the output is never written and attention reads garbage. When q/k/v are views of a fused qkv projection, the load offsets wrap too.

Boundary for MiniMax-H3 (H=56, D=128): 99,865 rows per rank. A stock 15 s Ref2VA request at 1312x736 packs 358,667 rows, so Ulysses 2 (179,334 rows/rank) renders pure noise while Ulysses 4 works. At Ulysses 2, 8 s works, 9 s breaks partway, and 10 s or longer is noise.

## Modifications

Add an `IDX64` constexpr, as in `wan_causal_cache_triton.py`: the launcher picks int64 offsets only when the output or a strided q/k/v view can pass 2^31 elements. Smaller shapes keep the int32 kernel. Add one regression test that fails before the fix.

## Accuracy Tests

- H3 Ref2VA 15 s at 1312x736, Ulysses 2 on 2xB200: stock is noise on all 362 frames (SSIM 0.17 vs the Ulysses-4 render). With the fix, SSIM is 0.95, the expected cross-degree difference. Peak memory is unchanged. (Run with an always-int64 build, which takes the same path at this shape.)
- `test_layout.py`: the new test fails on stock (illegal memory access) and passes with the fix; it covers the output, the q/k/v views, and both passing 2^31. All other tests pass.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

B200, H=56, D=128, mean +- std over 8 interleaved fresh-process runs of 100 reps each (ms).

| rows, world size | stock | fix |
|---|---|---|
| 89,667, 4 | 1.152 +- 0.004 | 1.153 +- 0.002 (+0.1%) |
| 44,834, 8 | 0.584 +- 0.000 | 0.586 +- 0.000 (+0.3%) |
| 41,750, 8 | 0.545 +- 0.000 | 0.547 +- 0.000 (+0.4%) |
| 179,334, 2 | n/a (overflows) | 2.548 +- 0.006 |

Always-int64 offsets cost +9.5 to +10.5% at the same shapes in the same run, hence the `IDX64` switch.

title: [Fix] swa: Retain a whole window behind insertion pages
author: caihuali95
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #44973
* #44972
* #44971
* #44970
* #44969
* #43326
* #43325
* #43171
* #43170
* __->__ #43168

Current head `dd96b50e68`, based on main `e17fed6ea7`. Stack predecessor: main `e17fed6ea7`. This PR targets `main` after its stack predecessor merged.

## Motivation

When an SWA window is not page-aligned, decode eviction can leave less than a full window below the page where a prefix-cache insertion ends. For a 127-token window at page size 64, the residue `pre_len = 63 mod 64` retains only 64 tokens there, so the inserted prefix cannot be reused.

## Modifications

Round `max(window, page)` up to whole pages before deriving the eviction frontier. Page-aligned windows and page size 1 keep the same frontier; an unaligned window retains at most one more SWA page per request.

The regression uses a 7-token window at page size 4. After eviction at `pre_len=23`, it directly checks that the insertion boundary at 20 still has at least 7 live SWA tokens below it, then verifies release accounting. Restoring the old rounding makes the new frontier assertion fail (4 < 7).

## Accuracy Tests

Earlier combined stack `b550cacde6` adds a test-fixture correction in #43326: the Gemma4 read-stream fixture declares its FULL address space, and the HiSparse registry test uses real `CacheInitParams` for the retained-window calculation. Both complete test files pass locally with GPUs hidden: 4 Gemma4 tests and 26 registry tests. Pre-commit passed. The five descendant patches are unchanged (`git range-diff`); this follow-up changes no production code. The earlier 455-test run did not cover these two files; GitHub CI has not yet been revalidated for this head.

Validation before the test-fixture follow-up, on combined stack `4cf27a551c`: 455 tests and 921 subtests passed on B300, plus the two widened-history regressions against Rust TreeCore. The new FULL-fallback metadata cases cover eager execution and CUDA graph replay. New allocation-reclaim, explicit-prefill and JIT-reuse regressions fail on the previous code and pass with the fixes. These are combined-stack checks, not independent model reruns of each PR.

The measurements in this section are historical results from before this rebase, at the revisions/configurations stated below. Current combined-stack validation is linked above.

SM90, TP1, gpt-oss-20b with EAGLE3 on triton, page size 64, radix cache, overlap scheduler, `--mem-fraction-static 0.55`. GSM8K, all 1314 test questions, 5-shot, greedy. Every server ran with the per-step pool checks and the allocator invariants on (`SGLANG_ENABLE_STRICT_MEM_CHECK_DURING_BUSY=1 SGLANG_CHECK_KV_PAGE_INVARIANTS=1 SGLANG_INVARIANT_CHECK=1`), which stop a server at the step that leaks or frees a page twice. Baseline: the default pool, run twice. Unified: `--enable-unified-memory` with lazy compaction (the default) and eager compaction (`SGLANG_DISABLE_LAZY_COMPACTION=1`), on a poisoned pool (`SGLANG_DEBUG_POISON_POOL=1`). These ran on this commit over main 7224fce1b5.

| CUDA graphs | baseline / baseline repeat / unified eager / unified lazy | accept length |
|---|---|---|
| off | 0.533 / 0.561 / 0.552 / 0.530 | 1.27-1.28 |
| on | 0.552 / 0.558 / 0.557 / 0.521 | 1.27-1.28 |

Every server answered all 1314 questions with no leak, double free, invariant violation or illegal memory access. Without this change the same configuration leaked and double-freed KV on every arm, the default pool's included. gpt-oss-20b's GSM8K score moves by several points between identical runs: #42930's EAGLE3 table, which includes this change, has two identical default-pool runs 5.1 points apart (paired per question, z = 3.05). Here the lowest run, unified lazy with CUDA graphs, is at z = -1.9 and -2.2 against the two baseline runs, with the same accept length as every other arm.

GPU unit tests for unified memory, including this test file, which is registered for CUDA: 4102 passed, 0 failed.

title: [NPU] Diffusion CI fixes
author: OrangeRedeng
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Fix 5 failures in NPU diffusion CI:

- **D001 — MiniMax-H3 slowdown after #42370.** That PR made consistency tests request `quality="exact"`. For MiniMax-H3, this turns off the Cache-DiT mode enabled by the CI configuration, so the 2-NPU test no longer uses its intended acceleration.
- **D002 — GLM-Image requests rejected after #41585.** That PR added strict validation to `/generate`, but the schema omitted `image_grid_thw`, which GLM-Image sends to its autoregressive encoder. Valid GLM-Image requests therefore fail with HTTP 400 before generation.
- **D003 — JoyAI times out downloading its input image.** The test fetches an image from GitHub Releases while running. A network timeout stops the test before generation. 
- **D004 — failure analyzer blind to diffusion failures.** `Analyze failure report` only downloads `selected-test-logs-*`, so diffusion consistency failures (published as `diffusion-failures-*` artifacts) never appear in the report, and empty input is reported as `Failed: 0`.
- **D005 — MiniMax-H3 consistency regression after #38671.** That merged PR makes `num_inference_steps=50` run 50 denoising updates instead of 49, shifting the sampled trajectory. The Ascend golden pinned at `609c4cef` was generated on the old 49-update trajectory and no longer matches (min SSIM 0.74 vs threshold 0.92) while the performance check stays green.

## Modifications

- Let the MiniMax-H3 2-NPU test keep its configured Cache-DiT mode. Other tests keep their existing quality settings.
- Add `image_grid_thw` to the API schema and update the generated Python/Rust types. Include the encoder's response body in error logs so future validation failures are easier to diagnose.
- Download and cache JoyAI's input image during CI setup, through the CI proxy. Verify its checksum and install it atomically so parallel jobs can safely share the cache. The test then reads the local file; standalone runs can still use the original URL.
- Teach `Analyze failure report` to also download `diffusion-failures-*` artifacts, parse each partition's `consistency_failures/summary.json` into the failed list plus a dedicated metrics section, and state explicitly when no input artifacts were found instead of a misleading `Failed: 0`. Also move `continue-on-error` to step level — it is not a `download-artifact` input and logged a warning on every run.
- Bump the Ascend consistency GT pin to `2173af2f` (sgl-project/ci-data-diffusion). The MiniMax-H3 frames were regenerated by the NPU GT generation workflow on this branch (run 38069422051) with Cache-DiT enabled (steps=50, Fn=2, Bn=1, rdt=0.4) — the exact code path the test runs. CLIP/SSIM/PSNR thresholds are unchanged.

The input-image cache is inspired by #37426, which caches reference outputs for consistency checks. This PR uses the same prefetch approach for an input image and can merge independently.

## Follow-up: Ascend NPU quality choices

Tracked in #43351. Start with MiniMax-H3: define explicit quality choices for Ascend and how each choice controls Cache-DiT, then validate output consistency and latency on A3. Once that support is validated, the NPU test can select a quality tier directly and remove the test-side quality-pinning exception introduced here. Extend support to other Ascend diffusion models as their configurations are validated.

This is follow-up work; this PR preserves the existing MiniMax-H3 cache configuration.

title: [Fix] Unblock CUDA graph startup for hybrid parallelism
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

`test_hybrid_dp_ep_tp_mtp.py::Test03` times out during server startup in the weekly H200 suite. With TP=8, `--moe-dense-tp-size 1`, and FlashInfer all-reduce fusion, prefill CUDA graph capture stalls at the 28-token shape. The capture batch bypasses eager padding, leaving different token-shard widths across ranks. The same failure appears in the [October 4 weekly run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37166616108/job/111330769101) and the August 16 run, on different H200 runners.

Running the rest of the file also exposed a startup OOM in Test12 (V3, attention DP8, DeepEP). DeepGEMM's warmup memory estimate excludes FP8 scale buffers: it estimates 8.375 GiB for a masked GEMM executor whose buffers actually need about 8.485 GiB. With 8.459 GiB available, decode graph initialization fails while allocating the output buffer. Test17 exposes a second omission: DeepGEMM also needs a 112 MiB temporary TMA-aligned LHS scale copy on Hopper. Its executor buffers fit into the 8.498 GiB available, but scale conversion runs out of memory.

## Modifications

- Round prefill capture buckets up using the existing CUDA graph parallelism alignment helper, then sort and deduplicate them. Capture buffers and replay padding use the same aligned buckets. A custom maximum such as 28 tokens rounds up to 32 rather than losing its coverage.
- Include FP32 token and block scale buffers and architecture-specific scale-conversion workspace in all FP8 DeepGEMM warmup memory estimates. Hopper needs a temporary TMA-aligned LHS copy; Blackwell needs packed UE8M0 scales, RHS broadcasting, and any grouped packing fallback buffers. MUSA does not receive the Hopper workspace allowance. The existing budget check can then choose a smaller warmup range before allocating the buffers.
- Add regression coverage for TP8, attention DP, configurations that do not require gathered token buffers, capture/replay at an unaligned custom ceiling, and memory estimates against the actual buffers constructed by every warmup executor and the strided storage needed for scale conversion. The memory test uses meta tensors and includes non-aligned scale dimensions and the V3 OOM shape across Hopper, Blackwell, and MUSA. Remove the redundant warmup-memory comment.

Keep the weekly file's models, launch flags, and accuracy thresholds.

## Accuracy Tests

- **All 60 configurations passed across batches before the architecture-specific review follow-up**, retaining the weekly file's models, launch flags, 64-example / 32-thread MMLU evaluation, and `score > 0.48` threshold. Scores range from **0.546875 to 0.921875**, with request error rate **0** in every configuration.
- Test00–Test09 passed after capture-bucket alignment. They use the BF16 Lite model and are unaffected by the FP8 memory-budget changes. With the Hopper scale-workspace fix, Test10–Test16 passed together (**7 tests**) and Test17–Test59 passed together (**43 tests**).
- Before fixing alignment, Test03 reproducibly stalled at the 28-token capture shape. After alignment it scored **0.625**. Before the budget fixes, Test12 failed while allocating executor buffers and Test17 failed while converting scales, each in both startup attempts. Both now pass without changing launch flags or reducing test coverage.
- Prefill helper suite: **22 tests passed**. The expanded memory regression passes **36 cases**: six executor variants, two shapes, and three architecture settings. It measures meta-tensor storage and live scale-conversion allocations, including the grouped packing fallback. The review follow-up fails 12 Blackwell/MUSA cases on the preceding implementation and passes afterward.
- Real Blackwell scale-conversion probes pass for all three FP8 executors with both direct packing and the grouped fallback, allowing for CUDA allocator rounding. The review follow-up preserves Hopper budgets exactly in **24 comparisons**; the 60-configuration GPU suite was not rerun after this follow-up.
- Applicable pre-commit checks passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Prefill graph capture for the original failing configuration completed in approximately 17 seconds after alignment. No throughput benchmark was run.

title: [Fix] nccl: Disable graph buffer registration whenever a captured graph can hold a collective
author: zhihengy
body:
## Problem

`NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER` is on by default and registers the send/recv buffers of every graph-captured collective for the lifetime of the graph. Those buffers are graph-pool temporaries, and the pool hands the same addresses to other tensors, so a replay can find its registration pointing at memory that now belongs to something else.

Both existing guards key on a feature flag rather than on that aliasing:

- `enable_tp_lm_head_all_to_all` additionally requires PD-decode, DP attention, `dp_size > 1` and `tp_size == dp_size`
- the pausable-pool check (dcf4e18) requires `enable_memory_saver` plus `SGLANG_MEMORY_SAVER_CUDA_GRAPH`, which is off by default

A plain multi-node TP deployment matches neither, so the registration stays on and the hang is reachable.

Features: more likely to appear under large batch size (> 128); not directly related to torch_memory_saver; currently does not appear in PREFILL stage but we still use any stage as gate to not regressing from the previous gate.

## Reproduction

Two TP16 engines spanning two H200 nodes each, decode batch 128, CUDA graph on, radix cache on, `max-running-requests 128`, a 501B MoE model. Load is 160 concurrent 4096-token generations per engine plus a pause/flush/continue cycle every 120s. `enable_tp_lm_head_all_to_all` and `enable_memory_saver` are both false in every run below.

Every TP rank hits the 300s scheduler watchdog within the same second:

```
cuEventSynchronize
  cudaEventSynchronize
    torch/cuda/streams.py:254  synchronize
      batch_result_processor.py:927  process_batch_result_decode
        scheduler.py:4785  process_batch_result
          scheduler.py:1999  event_loop_overlap

[TP0..TP7] Scheduler watchdog timeout (watchdog_timeout=300.0, soft=False)
scheduler.cur_batch_for_debug.batch_size()=128
```

| run | peak decode batch | NCCL | `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER` | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 66 | 2.29.7 | default (on) | clean for 1h |
| 2 | 128 | 2.29.7 | default (on) | hang at 19 min |
| 3 | 128 | 2.29.7 | default (on) | hang at 17 min |
| 4 | 128 | 2.29.7 | default (on), dcf4e18 applied | hang at 37 min |
| 5 | 128 | 2.29.7 | `0` | clean for 5h — 76k requests, 70M tokens, 148 cycles |
| 6 | 128 | **2.32.3** | default (on) | hang at 32 min |
| 7 | 128 | **2.32.3** | `0` | clean for 40 min |

Run 4 is why the dcf4e18 cherry-pick alone is not enough: it is in the tree, neither of its conditions matches, so the variable is never set and the hang is unchanged.

Runs 6 and 7 rule out a stale NCCL as the cause. 2.32.3 carries the fix for NVIDIA/nccl#2389, which has a similar signature, and the hang still reproduces with the registration on and still disappears with it off.

Two further conditions were tested and are *not* required: `NCCL_PXN_DISABLE=1` still hangs (7 min), and all of the above runs have the TP LM-head all-to-all and the memory saver off. Disabling GDR (`NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL=0`) does hold for 50 min with the registration on, which points at the network registration path, but that is not something this layer can detect at argument-resolution time.

## Cost

Same engine, same tree, same load, 10 minutes each:

| registration | requests | tokens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| on | 1,765 | 2,060,061 |
| off | 1,781 | 2,066,577 |

No measurable throughput difference. Single run per configuration, not repeated for variance. Worth noting that the non-registered path is the one every deployment used before the default flipped, so it is not a new or lightly-exercised code path.

## Change

One condition replaces both: `max(tp_size, ep_size, dp_size) > 1` with any graph phase still enabled means a capture can hold a collective, which is exactly when a registration can outlive the pool's claim on the address. It errs toward disabling — later passes can still narrow `cuda_graph_config`, and a false positive costs nothing measurable.

Keying on any phase rather than decode alone keeps the pausable-pool case that dcf4e18 added: with the decode capture off and the memory saver on, a prefill capture still lands in that pool.

The test that asserted the variable stays unset without the TP LM-head all-to-all encoded the old contract and now asserts the new one. Added alongside it: the pausable pool in isolation, a prefill-only capture, a single rank, and a fully disabled graph.

Draft while the deployment-shape coverage gets a second opinion — happy to narrow the condition if there is a configuration where the registration is known to be safe and worth keeping. The root cause is still open: these runs establish which conditions reproduce it and which do not, not the mechanism inside NCCL.

title: Quantized weight-update fixes: Qwen3.5 draft KV budget, UE8M0 partial blocks, mxfp8 fused indexer, NVFP4 input scales
author: yueming-yuan
body:
Stacked on #42820. The model- and format-specific engine fixes miles' p2p weight update needs; #42820 keeps the general engine support.

**Derived state after writes that bypass a model's loader** (moved from #42820, plus one gap the review found):

| fix | symptom | cause |
|---|---|---|
| GemmaRMSNorm `gemma_weight` | Qwen3.5 serves the old norm after a p2p update; fused allreduce kernels read `gemma_weight` | the norm's weight loader derives `gemma_weight = weight + 1`, and p2p, remote-instance, sharded-state and dummy loads write the weight without it; `post_load_weights` now refreshes it |
| `gemma_weight` at every session end | a session whose `direct` or custom load wrote the norm weight kept the old `gemma_weight` | those loads bypass the norm's loader yet mark the session loaded, so `end_weight_update` skipped `post_load_weights`; it now refreshes `gemma_weight` either way |
| GLM-lite NextN post-load | the GLM-4.7-Flash draft skipped its NextN post-load after a p2p update | `post_load_weights` ran the target's path on the draft; the NextN draft now pins `is_nextn=True` |

**Quantized checkpoints.** Four fixes found by running miles' p2p weight-update e2e with quantized rollout checkpoints on GB300 (fp8 block, mxfp8, nvfp4 on GLM-5.2 cut to 5 layers; fp8 on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B cut to 4 layers with its MTP draft). None is specific to p2p: each also hits sglang's own weight update or its startup. One commit each.

| fix | symptom | cause |
|---|---|---|
| EAGLE draft KV budget for Qwen3.5 | the draft's KV pool is allocated outside `mem_fraction_static`; OOM at startup on the 4-layer cut (127.6 GB draft pool, 82 GB left at 0.7) | `_resolve_eagle_aux_hidden_state` reads the draft depth from `num_nextn_predict_layers`; Qwen3.5 names it `mtp_num_hidden_layers`, so the target's per-token cost counted no draft layer |
| UE8M0 scales of non-128-multiple rows | `RuntimeError: shape '[20, 128, 48]' is invalid for input of size 125952` in the weight checker on every GLM-5 fp8 update on Blackwell | `_inverse_transform_scale_ue8m0_impl` viewed the per-row packed scales as whole 128-row blocks; GLM-5's fused q_a + kv_a has 2624 rows |
| mxfp8 shards of the fused indexer | the fused bf16 `wk_weights_proj` off by up to 5e4 after loading an mxfp8 checkpoint with a quantized `wk` | `_load_fused_indexer_wk` dequantized with `block_quant_dequant`, multiplying by the uint8 UE8M0 exponents as integers |
| NVFP4 MoE input scales in the weight check | every NVFP4 MoE update fails the check on `w13_input_scale` / `w2_input_scale` only | they are calibrated activation scales no update carries (miles' quantizer emits `weight`, `weight_scale`, `weight_scale_2`); the checker reset them to random before the update. Now `_skip_weight_check`, as the KV cache scales |

On the draft budget: with Qwen3.5-35B-A3B's 10 full-attention layers the unbudgeted draft is a tenth of the KV pool, which fits at 0.6–0.7 and so went unnoticed; the 4-layer cut makes it as large as the target's.

**Tests**
- `unit/model_loader/test_default_model_loader.py`: `gemma_weight` follows a norm weight written without its loader (CPU).
- `unit/model_executor/model_runner_components/test_weight_updater_published_storage.py`: a session whose load bypassed the norm's loader still refreshes `gemma_weight` (CPU); fails on its parent.
- `unit/models/test_glm4_moe_lite_nextn_post_load.py`: the GLM-lite NextN draft runs the NextN post-load (CPU).
- `unit/model_executor/model_runner_components/test_spec_aux_hidden_state.py`: an MTP depth named `mtp_num_hidden_layers` counts as the EAGLE draft's layers (CPU).
- `unit/layers/quantization/test_fp8_utils.py`: the UE8M0 round trip also covers GLM-5's (2624, 6144) (CUDA).
- `unit/models/test_deepseek_fused_indexer_mxfp8.py`: mxfp8 `wk` and `weights_proj` reach the fused param dequantized with their UE8M0 scales (CPU).
- `unit/layers/quantization/test_modelopt_nvfp4_moe_weight_check.py`: the checker skips the NVFP4 MoE input scales and still checks the weight scales (CPU).

On an H200 devbox (`radixark/miles:dev`), all changed test files of this branch and #42820 pass (35 passed, 1 skipped: an SM100-only case). On #42820's head each quantized case fails for its cause: `None == 1`, the `[20, 128, 48]` view error, the fused `wk` mismatch, `w13_input_scale` not skipped.

End to end on GB300 with the UE8M0 fix applied: GLM-5.2 5-layer fp8 compares every fp8 tensor within quantization ULP, `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` included. What remains there is on miles' side: its fp8 / mxfp8 converters quantize the interleaved indexer's `wk`, which sglang keeps in bf16 and the trainer sends in bf16.

title: [diffusion] fix: share the IPC all-to-all transport between AllToAll4D and USP
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

`test_ipc_a2a_2_gpu.py` fails on main (reported on 2×H200, reproduced on 2×B200 NVLink at f6569bce4d9):

```
rank0 MISMATCH: ['AllToAll4D never took the IPC path (exchange count stayed at 6)']
IPC_A2A_PARITY FAIL (staged keys=3)
```

AllToAll4D does still reach the IPC transport. None of the steps on that path changed after #31854 (checked with `git log -L` on `sequence_model_parallel_all_to_all_4D`, then `GroupCoordinator.all_to_all_4D`, `DeviceCommunicatorBase.all_to_all_4D`, `AllToAll4D.forward` and `_ipc_all_to_all_4d`). The other recent commits under `runtime/distributed/` (#37547, #39293, #41284, #40069) don't change it either.

The regression is #33317 (f829fb3ff7c). It made `ipc_a2a_ready` reset the transport whenever the caller passes a different ProcessGroup *object*, and the two entry points pass different objects for the same two ranks:

- USP (`_ipc_ready_group`) passes `get_sp_group().ulysses_group`, which `set_seq_parallel_pg_by_sp_groups` creates.
- AllToAll4D passes the SP coordinator's own `device_group`.

So every switch between the two entry points tears the transport down and rebuilds it. Lifecycle trace of the test on main, identical on both ranks:

```
INIT(ulysses_pg) | 6 exchanges | RESET(calls=6) | INIT(sp.device_group) | 6 exchanges | RESET(calls=6) | INIT(ulysses_pg) | 3 exchanges
```

The reset sets `calls` back to 0. The 6 AllToAll4D exchanges then bring it back to exactly 6, which the test reports as "never took the IPC path". The second reset also puts `max_buffers` back to its default, so the eviction check in the test has not been testing eviction. If you remove only #33317's two-line reset from main, the test passes.

**Impact.** Since #33923, wan-VSA (`UlyssesAttention_VSA`) is the only production model that calls AllToAll4D, and it never uses USP in the same process. So the models we ship today did not hit these resets (see the e2e below). A model that uses both entry points would rebuild the transport twice per layer, about 6.3 ms per switch on B200 (benchmark below). Each rebuild also drops staging buffers that kernels captured earlier in a CUDA graph may still point to.

**Why CI missed it.** This file is listed in `STANDALONE_FILES["2-gpu"]`, but the NVIDIA 2-GPU partition plans contain no standalone files (scheduled run 37768448360 has `standalone_files=[]` in all three partitions), and AMD skips the test because it needs CUDA. I'll follow up on that separately.

## Modifications

- `ipc_a2a.py`: the peer mappings depend on which two ranks are paired, not on which group object is passed. Store the pair's global ranks in `init`. In `ipc_a2a_ready`, reset only when a group over a *different* pair arrives; passing the same object still skips the check. `destroy_model_parallel()` still resets explicitly, so the topology-switch case #33317 fixed is unaffected.
- `test_ipc_a2a_lifecycle.py`: parametrize the replaced-group test. `different_pair` must still reinitialize. `same_pair` must reuse the transport; it fails on main.
- `test_ipc_a2a_2_gpu.py`: before reading the exchange count, check that the transport was not re-initialized (`IPC_A2A.flag` identity), so this failure now names its cause. Also update the comment: zimage and hunyuanvideo moved to USPAttention in #33923, and wan-VSA is the only AllToAll4D user left.

## Accuracy Tests

All runs: 2×B200 (NV18), `lmsysorg/sglang:dev`, torch 2.14.1+cu130. No pair of H200s was free. The bug is in Python-level transport state, so it is the same on any NVLink pair.

`pytest -v python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/single_test_file/test_ipc_a2a_2_gpu.py`

| tree | result |
|---|---|
| main f6569bce4d9 | FAIL, same output as the H200 report |
| main with only #33317's identity reset removed | PASS |
| this PR | PASS. Trace: one `INIT`, all AllToAll4D exchanges reuse the USP staging buffers, no `RESET` |
| this PR's test file on main's `ipc_a2a.py` | FAIL: `AllToAll4D re-initialized the IPC transport USP set up` |

`test_ipc_a2a_lifecycle.py`: 9 passed. With main's `ipc_a2a.py`, `[same_pair]` fails.

**E2E on the only production AllToAll4D model.** Settings: FastVideo/FastWan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers, `--attention-backend video_sparse_attn` (`VSA_sparsity=0.8`), `--num-gpus 2 --ulysses-degree 2`, 480x832x61, 3 DMD steps, seed 42. There is no cookbook page for wan-VSA, so this is a test configuration, not a recommended deployment. Each run sends two requests. Worker log lines were added temporarily for this test and are not part of the PR.

| run | IPC transport | exchanges in request 0 | frames sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| this PR | initialized once on ranks [0, 1], no reset | 180 (30 layers × 2 × 3 steps) | `56d9347f…` |
| this PR, `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_IPC_A2A=0` (NCCL) | not initialized | 0 | `56d9347f…` |
| main | initialized once, no reset | 180 | `56d9347f…` |

All six outputs are bit-identical (0 differing values). wan-VSA only uses AllToAll4D, so it already took the IPC path on main, and its output does not change with this PR.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Nothing changes when only one entry point is used, because the identity check still short-circuits. The table below times a process that alternates the two entry points, using one FastWan-1.3B layer shape (12480 tokens per rank, 12 heads × 128) on 2×B200, averaged over 50 iterations:

| | USP input A2A | AllToAll4D (qkvg) | alternating | overhead from alternating | resets |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| main | 0.110 ms | 0.378 ms | 13.075 ms | +12.59 ms | 100 |
| this PR | 0.110 ms | 0.380 ms | 0.480 ms | ~0 | 0 |

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Fix] DSA/KDA: Handle MoE padding in hybrid MTP verification
author: Jzz1943
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

GLM-5.3-Flash can fail during MTP verification with TP4/EP4 MegaMoE when Decode CUDA Graph is disabled. MoE pads the token tensors, while attention metadata still describes the valid verification sequences. For example, one 6-token verification sequence is padded to 8 rows.

This mismatch causes KDA verification to fail when reshaping QKV. After correcting that path, DSA KPool verification also fails at `assert bn % num_draft_tokens == 0` because it includes the extra padding rows.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- Use the logical verification length from attention metadata to trim KDA QKV and gate inputs before convolution and state updates. Restore zero padding in the output to preserve the downstream tensor layout. Keep the ragged verification path unchanged.
- Restrict DSA KPool key, score, and cache-location writes to the token rows covered by the verification write plan.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

Validated on 4×H200 with GLM-5.3-Flash, BF16 KV, TileLang DSA, MegaMoE, and MTP 5/1/6.

### Reproduction and validation command

```bash

  --served-model-name llm \

  --cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 48 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang \

  --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
  --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm \
  --moe-a2a-backend megamoe \
  --speculative-moe-runner-backend deep_gemm \
  --speculative-moe-a2a-backend none \

```

Before the fix, this configuration fails during startup warmup. After the fix, startup and requests at concurrency 1/3/7/19 pass. The same request checks also pass with `--cuda-graph-backend-decode full`.

### Full GSM8K evaluation

```bash

title: [Fix] disaggregation: Fix the early-send wait event on non-CUDA devices and in nixl
author: kpjeeja
body:
## Motivation

Under overlap scheduling, `maybe_send_cached_prefix_chunk` can start the KV transfer for a cached prefix while the *previous* step's prefill forward is still writing those pages on `forward_stream`. It records a completion event and attaches it to the KV sender, so the transfer worker can wait for those writes before reading the pages. Two bugs broke this:

1. **The prefill scheduler crashes on non-CUDA devices.** The event came from `torch.cuda.Event()`, which raises `Tried to instantiate dummy base class Event` on torch builds without CUDA. On Intel XPU with PD + hierarchical cache, the prefill scheduler died on the first request that reused a cached prefix.
2. **nixl reads KV that may still be being written, with no error.** #41395 made the mooncake worker wait on the event, but nixl's `add_transfer_request` had no `wait_event` parameter. The event was recorded, attached and then dropped, so the RDMA read raced the writes it was meant to wait for. `SGLANG_DISAGG_PREFILL_EARLY_SEND_CACHED_PREFIX` defaults to `True`, so this is the default nixl PD path. Nothing fails visibly: the bytes do arrive, they just may not be final yet, and only an output-quality check catches it.

## Modifications

- `disaggregation/prefill.py`: create the event with `self.device_module.Event()`. `device_module` is set once from `self.device` in `init_overlap()`, the same module `forward_stream` was built from, so the event and the stream are always on the same accelerator. Using the process-default accelerator would bring that mismatch back whenever `--device` is not the default.
- `disaggregation/nixl/conn.py`: `add_transfer_request` now accepts `wait_event` and puts it on the queued `TransferKVChunk`. The transfer worker waits on it the same way mooncake's does:
  - before the failed-room check and before the staging gather, since the gather also reads the source pages;
  - not for a room that has already failed;
  - then clears it, so a chunk re-enqueued on a staging-watermark defer doesn't wait again.
- `disaggregation/common/conn.py`: add a `CommonKVSender._take_early_send_wait_event()` helper (returns the event and clears it), and set `_early_send_wait_event` in `__init__`. mooncake, mori and nixl now all read the event through this helper instead of `getattr`.

## Tests

- `test_prefill_abort_result_cleanup.py`: injects a stub device module and checks that the event comes from it and is recorded on `forward_stream`. This fails on the old code, which never touches the stub. The env flag is pinned with `override(True)`.

title: [Fix] Adapt NPU Qwen-VL processor patch to transformers 5.19 resize() signature change
author: sigama-w
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Running Qwen2.5-VL / Qwen3-VL on NPU with transformers >= 5.19 crashes with: TypeError: Qwen2VLImageProcessor.resize() missing 2 required positional arguments: 'images' and 'factor' Transformers 5.19 refactored Qwen2VLImageProcessor.resize() and Qwen3VLVideoProcessor.resize():

- Old (<= 5.15): resize(image, size, resample) — the caller computed smart_resize() itself and passed the target SizeDict(height, width).
- New (5.19): resize(images, size, resample, factor[, temporal_factor]) -- smart_resize() moved inside resize(), which now takes the original size (shortest_edge/longest_edge) and the patch factor.

The NPU _preprocess patch in sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/modules/qwen_vl_processor.py still called resize() with the old signature: image= was swallowed by **kwargs while the required images/factor params were missing.

## Modifications

1. Image path: drop the manual smart_resize() call and invoke self.resize(images=..., size=size, resample=resample, factor=patch_size * merge_size), matching the upstream 5.19 _preprocess implementation.
2. Video path: drop the manual smart_resize() call and the 5D->4D fold/unfold around resize; call self.resize(videos=..., size=size, resample=resample, factor=..., temporal_factor=...) directly, since the new resize() handles the (B, T, C, H, W) tensor natively.
3. Remove the now-unused smart_resize / smart_resize (video) imports. The NPU-specific flattening logic (transform_patches_to_flatten, avoiding tensors > 8 dims on Ascend) is unchanged.

title: [AMD] Patch aiter's group32 MXFP8 GEMM masked-scale fix
author: RolaoDenthu
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation


`TestMxfp8AiterRouteGfx95` (added in #41970) keeps failing in `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`, e.g. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37709475489/job/113091795880:

```
[CI Test Method] TestMxfp8AiterRouteGfx95.test_within_one_bf16_ulp_of_the_bf16_route
  File "test/registered/kernels/ops/quantization/test_mxfp8_amd_gfx95.py", line 199, in test_within_one_bf16_ulp_of_the_bf16_route
    self.assertTrue(
AssertionError: False is not true : (1792, 5120, 1, nan)
retry() failed once (0th try, maximum 1 retries). Will delay ... and retry. Error: False is not true : (1792, 5120, 1, nan)
...
Exception: retry() exceed maximum number of retries.
```

`(1792, 5120, 1, nan)` is (N, K, M, max error in bf16 ulps): the very first case already has NaN in the output. Running the test file alone always passed, so it could not be reproduced locally at first.

Running the whole CI partition on MI355X reproduced it, and so did running just the two tests that precede it on the same GPU. Narrowing it down showed the NaN comes from aiter's group32 GEMM itself: the inputs are clean and the reference side is fine, but whole 16-column output tiles come back as NaN, and only from the packed small-M kernel. Filling LDS with `0xFF` before the GEMM makes the original kernel return NaN every time, while aiter main is clean under the same condition.

The cause is that the packed kernel loads the masked K-tail E8M0 scales with `other=127`, but on gfx950 those lanes end up with whatever earlier kernels left in LDS. The matching data is 0, so the result is usually unaffected, but a leftover `0xFF` byte (E8M0 NaN) turns the tile into NaN. That is why it only fails after other tests have run on the same GPU. Upstream fixed this in ROCm/aiter#6007 by defaulting masked scales to 0. That commit sits on top of the ROCm/aiter#5862 refactor and does not apply to our pin, so this PR applies the same one-line change to `gemm_a8w8_blockscale_group32.py` in the Dockerfile.

title: [Fix] hicache: Keep unified memory off the direct page_first_direct copies
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

With `--enable-unified-memory`, each layer's device KV rows are strided: a unified-pool entry holds every layer's K and V for one token (#40326). The direct `page_first_direct` copies (`transfer_kv_all_layer_direct_lf_pf` / `transfer_kv_per_layer_direct_pf_lf`) still copy a page as one contiguous `page_size * row_stride` span. On Inkling that is 8x the page's real size, so:

- a backup writes past its host page into the neighbouring host pages;
- a load-back rewrites the row's other layers and the next rows on the device;
- when the overrun crosses an allocation end, the copy fails with `cudaMemcpyBatchAsync failed ... error=invalid argument` and the scheduler dies.

`page_first_direct` forces the direct io backend, and storage backends such as Mooncake resolve to it, so this is reachable from ordinary HiCache flags.

## Modifications

- `resolve_unified_memory_layout_io`: with unified memory, a `page_first_direct` layout resolves to `page_first` with the kernel io backend, whose JIT kernels address rows by stride. It runs after the storage-layout step, which can itself pick `page_first_direct`.
- `MHATokenToKVPoolHost` / `MLATokenToKVPoolHost`: the direct `page_first_direct` copies call `_require_packed_device_rows`, so strided rows fail loudly instead of corrupting memory.

## Tests

- `test_server_args.py::TestHiCacheArgs`: two cases, unified memory with `page_first_direct`, and with Mooncake + direct + `layer_first`.
- `test_hicache_strided_device_rows.py`: the direct `page_first_direct` backup and load on strided rows raise `NotImplementedError`. Host pools now call `destroy()` on cleanup, so a later pool in the same process does not hit `cudaHostRegister` error 712 on a reused address.

On H200, all three new assertions fail on main and pass with this PR. Inkling with unified memory, a 0.35 GB pool and `--hicache-mem-layout page_first_direct` crashes on main within seconds; with this PR it resolves to `page_first`/kernel and serves. The surrounding host-pool unit suites match main; `test_kvcacheio_asymmetric.py::test_asymmetric_mha_kernel_page_first_roundtrip` fails on main too.

Not shown: a wrong-output reproduction. The HiCache KL test with unified memory did not load anything back from host, so it cannot see the corruption.

title: [XPU] Fix XPU CI breaks from #41105 (KDA chunk_offsets) and #42588 (int4 test tp_group)
author: arathi-hlab
body:
## Motivation

#41105 added a `chunk_offsets` argument to the generic `fla/chunk_delta_h.py::chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h` and made `chunk_kda_fwd` pass `chunk_offsets=chunk_offsets`. On XPU, `kda.py` imports the XPU override instead:

```python
if is_intel:
    from sglang.srt.hardware_backend.xpu.kernels.fla.chunk_delta_h import chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h
```

That override's signature was not updated, so every `chunk_kda` call on XPU fails:

```
File ".../sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fla/kda.py", line 1235, in chunk_kda_fwd
    h, v_new = chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h(
TypeError: chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h() got an unexpected keyword argument 'chunk_offsets'
```

This breaks `test/registered/xpu/test_kda_track_state_xpu.py` on `main`, and because the error isn't retried, the XPU suite stops there (16/38 files run): https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37893946145/job/113701033110

#41105's own XPU job failed at "Checkout code" (infra), so this wasn't caught before merge.

## Modifications

Mirror the generic change in the XPU `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h`: accept `chunk_offsets`, and only derive it with `prepare_chunk_offsets` when the caller doesn't pass one. Behaviour is unchanged when `chunk_offsets` is `None`.

## Notes

Independent of #43306 (int4 dense test fix); both are needed for a green XPU suite on `main`.

cc @yuan-luo
