title: [Fix] [AMD] aiter: Fix garbage decode output for non-sliding-window models on the vectorized_5d KV layout
author: jiaqiang-dot-liu
body:
## Motivation

On the AITER backend, the SHUFFLE 5D KV layout (`SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=vectorized_5d`) silently produces garbage output for every model without sliding-window attention: decode reads the wrong KV pages and nothing reports an error. GSM8K on Qwen3-14B-FP8 drops from 0.885 to 0.000 on MI325X. This has been the case since the layout was added in #27063. Setting `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1` works around it today.

Root cause: `forward_decode_vectorized_5d` passes `forward_metadata.kv_indices` to `pa_decode_gluon` as its `block_tables`, a 2-D `(bs, max_num_blocks_per_seq)` table of page ids, and its docstring says the same ("Full-attn → `kv_indices` page table"). But the decode metadata only builds that table on the unified-attention branch:

```python
if not self.use_triton_unified_attention:
    # flat per-token kv_indices, addressed through kv_indptr
    create_flashinfer_kv_indices_triton[(bs,)](...)
else:
    # 2-D page table
    ...
```

`use_triton_unified_attention` is forced on for sliding-window models, which is why gpt-oss (the model the 5D path was added for in #27063) is unaffected. Every other model leaves it off by default, so `pa_decode_gluon` reads token ids as page ids with a row stride of 1. The eager path, the CUDA-graph page-table buffer and CUDA-graph capture/replay all make the same choice.

## Modifications

The decode metadata format and the decode kernel are separate choices, so this PR names the former explicitly:

```python
self.decode_uses_page_table = (
    self.use_triton_unified_attention or self.kv_cache_is_vectorized_5d
)
```

and uses it at the five sites that decide between the flat indices and the page table: the eager decode path (plain and speculative), the CUDA-graph page-table buffer allocation, and both checks in `_apply_cuda_graph_metadata` (shared by capture and replay).

`use_triton_unified_attention` itself is unchanged. The 5D layout already has dedicated KV-write, extend and decode branches, so the only things the flag still controls for it are the metadata format and the target-verify kernel choice (`_use_unified_verify`). Forcing the flag on would also switch the verify kernel, which is outside this fix. The NHD layout is unaffected: `decode_uses_page_table` equals `use_triton_unified_attention` there.

Tests: `test/registered/amd/test_aiter_vectorized_5d_decode.py` launches the CI default model (`meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct`, dense, no sliding window) with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, the 5D layout and `--page-size 64`, and runs GSM8K. Registered in `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`.

The branch is rebased onto `main` @ `e45cbce599` without conflicts.

## Accuracy Tests

### MI325X (gfx942)

MI325X (gfx942, 304 CU), ROCm 7.2, torch 2.11.0, Triton 3.7.0, AITER `c16d44b93`. This image ships a `sgl-kernel` that current `main` does not run against, so these runs use the image's sglang (`dc6b5d1f5a`, 2026-09-04), with and without this patch, which applies to it unchanged.

Qwen3-14B-FP8, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, `--attention-backend aiter`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.85`, CUDA graph on, GSM8K 200 questions, 5-shot, greedy, one server at a time:

| Config | GSM8K |
|---|---|
| NHD layout, `--page-size 1` | 0.870 |
| NHD layout, `--page-size 64` | 0.885 |
| 5D layout | **0.000** |
| This PR, 5D layout | 0.890 |
| 5D layout + `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1` | 0.890 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No change on the NHD layout. On the 5D layout the fixed path builds the same page table as the unified-attention path.

Long-context serving on MI325X, same setup as the gfx942 accuracy table: `bench_serving --dataset-name random-ids`, 8192 input / 1024 output tokens, `--random-range-ratio 1.0`, 3 × concurrency prompts after a warmup of one concurrency's worth:

| Config | c=64 output tok/s | c=64 mean TPOT (ms) | c=128 output tok/s | c=128 mean TPOT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NHD layout, `--page-size 1` | 351.9 | 133.0 | 389.2 | 190.7 |
| NHD layout, `--page-size 64` | 349.0 | 133.3 | 383.6 | 194.5 |
| This PR, 5D layout | 358.9 | 128.6 | 395.2 | 186.2 |
| 5D layout + `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1` | 358.0 | 128.9 | 392.1 | 187.4 |

At the same page size, the 5D layout lowers mean TPOT by 3.5% (c=64) and 4.3% (c=128) on this dense model. The runs are prefill-heavy (mean TTFT is about 50 s at c=64 and 110 s at c=128 for every config), so these numbers are about the decode side only.

title: [diffusion] fix: keep MiniMax-H3 VAE fused norms off ROCm
author: niehen6174
body:
## Motivation

Since #41906, `minimax_h3_ref2va_video_audio_2gpu_h100` fails on AMD MI300 in the scheduled PR Test (AMD) runs on main. `MiniMaxH3DecodingStage` returns a video that is entirely NaN: 331,333,632 NaN values in a `[1, 3, 107, 768, 1344]` tensor ([example job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37709475489/job/113091795394)).

In the scheduled AMD runs on main:

- **Before #41906 merged (10-05 09:30 UTC):** this case either passed or failed with a server startup timeout, never with NaN.
- **After the merge:** every run that reached the case (7 runs, 10-06 to 10-09) failed with the all-NaN decode.

#41906 enables its fused Triton kernels (block RMSNorm, scale-add-RMSNorm, and the QK RMSNorm+RoPE) when the tensors satisfy `is_cuda`. On ROCm, `tensor.is_cuda` is also true, so MI300 takes the fused path.

## Modifications

- `vae_vit._fused_blocks_available` and `attention._try_fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope` now also require `current_platform.is_cuda()`, which is true only on NVIDIA. ROCm keeps the unfused fp32-norm path. NVIDIA behavior is unchanged.
- The fused-vs-unfused unit test now runs only on NVIDIA.
- A new unit test simulates a non-NVIDIA platform and checks that neither fused kernel is called.

Re-enabling the fused path on ROCm needs a separate root-cause fix on AMD hardware.

## Validation

- On an RTX 5090, `test_minimax_h3_vae_parallel_modes.py` passes (15 tests). The new test fails if the gate is removed.
- To confirm on MI300: PR Test (AMD) should run `minimax_h3_ref2va_video_audio_2gpu_h100` without the NaN decode.

title: [diffusion] fix: keep a LoRA unmerged under merge_mode auto when merging would round its update away
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

`--lora-merge-mode auto`, the default, merges an adapter into regular BF16 weights. Distilled adapters carry updates far smaller than a BF16 ulp of the weights they modify, so the merge rounds most of the update away. The MiniMax-H3 Turbo LoRA (`larryvrh/MiniMax-H3-Turbo-Lora`) is one: a merge drops 77–97% of the update in typical layers, and 75% over the whole transformer.

Nothing fails or warns when this happens. The output just comes out softer than the adapter's reference, which applies the LoRA at runtime for exactly this reason. So the default silently degrades these adapters.

## Modifications

- `BaseLayerWithLoRA.merge_rounding_norms()` estimates, over an even sample of rows, how much of the active update a merge into the weight dtype would round away. It uses the same slicing and scaling as the merge, and writes nothing.
- Under `auto`, `set_lora` with one adapter now does the following:
  - attaches the adapter unmerged and measures the share of the update a merge would lose;
  - if that share is above 50% (`AUTO_MERGE_MAX_ROUNDING_LOSS`), i.e. the merge would destroy most of the update, keeps the adapter dynamic and logs why;
  - otherwise merges as before.
- The result is cached per (module, paths, strengths, alphas), so repeated `set_lora` calls do not measure again.
- **Why 50%.** The threshold has to separate adapters a merge destroys from adapters it only trims. CI's style LoRAs lose 14% (`Cseti/Wan-LoRA-Arcane-Jinx-v1`) and 31% (`reverentelusarca/elusarca-anime-style-lora-z-image-turbo`) in a merge. Earlier cuts at 10% and 30% made them dynamic, and the dynamic path then cost Wan2.1 1.3B +52% and Z-Image +44% per step, failing both cases' latency checks. At 50% they merge exactly as before, while the distilled H3 Turbo adapter (75%) stays dynamic.
- Explicit `merge` and `dynamic` are unchanged, and so are FSDP-sharded and quantized weights, which `auto` already keeps dynamic.
- The `--lora-merge-mode` help and the MiniMax-H3 cookbook describe the new rule.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test_lora_auto_merge_rounding.py` (new, CPU) checks:
  - the estimate against the rounding of an actual merge;
  - that an update below a BF16 ulp is mostly lost and one above it survives;
  - that FP32 weights report nothing;
  - that the pipeline decision measures once and follows the threshold.

  The existing LoRA unit tests still pass (27 passed).
- End to end on 2×H200, MiniMax-H3 T2VA at Ulysses 2 with the Larry Turbo v4 adapter, `num_inference_steps: 9`, same seed:

  | `--lora-merge-mode` | log | MP4 md5 | latency |
  |---|---|---|---:|
  | `auto` (this PR) | "stays unmerged on transformer: merging it into the base weights would round away 75% of its update" | `95a418705f7b` | 27.60 s |
  | `dynamic` | — | `95a418705f7b` | 27.59 s |
  | `merge` | — | `342c3151970f` | 25.78 s |

  `auto` now gives the dynamic output byte for byte. Side by side, the merged video is visibly softer: the cats blur and the scene loses detail that the dynamic run keeps.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Keeping the Turbo LoRA dynamic costs 1.8 s on the 9-point schedule (27.6 against 25.8 s), which is the price of getting the adapter's full effect. A faster dynamic path, for example adding the LoRA delta inside the second GEMM, can follow separately. Adapters whose updates survive a merge, which covers the usual style LoRAs, still merge as before.

title: [Fix] unified_cache: Prevent misaligned Mamba checkpoints after speculative truncation
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

With Mamba `no_buffer` + speculative decoding, verify advances the live state before CPU grammar/finish truncation. Donating that state under a shorter cache key corrupts subsequent prefix reuse.

## Changes

Require the live state length to match `owned_kv_len()` before donation, accounting for grammar-retained tokens and each algorithm's non-draft count. Otherwise skip the finished request's insertion, preserving existing prefixes and normal resource cleanup. The decision survives deferred release and adds no GPU synchronization.

Extend `test/registered/radix_cache/test_mamba_cache_kl.py` with `TestMambaSpecTruncationKL`. NEXTN count/story requests end at short length limits; the test compares full-vocabulary next-token distributions for identical probe token IDs using warm cache versus a cold recompute. It also checks that speculative verify accepted drafts and that cache reuse actually occurred. Shared HTTP/distribution helpers retain the existing lazy checkpoint test.

This branch includes #43567's shared test file and should merge after #43567. The no_buffer fix itself is independent of the lazy extra-buffer fix.

## Validation

GB300, TP1, Qwen3.5-0.8B pinned at `2fc06364715b967f1860aea9cf38778875588b17`, NEXTN (3 steps, topk 1, 4 draft tokens), no_buffer, page size 1, overlap/CUDA graphs disabled. The negative control retains #43567 and removes only #43387's finished-state guard.

| Scenario | KL without guard | KL with guard | Warm cache length without / with guard |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Count, max_new_tokens=9 | 0.876971 | 0.000235300 | 51 / 42 |
| Story, max_new_tokens=5 | 4.107031 | 0.000941570 | 27 / 22 |

KL is `D_KL(cold || warm)` over all 248,320 vocabulary entries at the same next-token position. The threshold is 0.005: valid prompt-prefix reuse versus cold prefill has numerical differences, while the corrupted-state cases are much larger. Unsafe finished suffixes now fall back to the cached prompt; this can reduce cache hits for truncated requests.

- Registered in `extra-a`, `1-gpu-large`; the new GPU test covers NEXTN length truncation. Grammar, EOS/stop, zero-commit, deferred release, and dedicated-slot controls remain covered by CPU tests.
- GPU: each NEXTN case repeated three times with identical KL values; all six negative controls failed and all six fixed cases passed. The existing lazy in-place KL test also passed with KL=0.
- CPU: 8 tests and 11 subtests passed after integrating #43567.
- Pre-commit passed. GPU validation is limited to GB300; no throughput benchmark.

```bash
python test/registered/radix_cache/test_mamba_cache_kl.py TestMambaSpecTruncationKL
python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/managers/test_batch_result_processor_spec_grammar.py
```

title: [Fix] attn_residual: int64 program ids in the score/combine kernels (int32 overflow at 37,451 tokens)
author: jiuqiant
body:
## Motivation

`_score_kernel` and `_combine_kernel` in `srt/layers/attn_residual.py` read the attention-residual bank `[T, NB, H]` at `bank_ptr + pid_t * stride_bm`. `pid_t = tl.program_id(0)` is int32 and so is the product. With Kimi-K3's `NB = 8`, `H = 7168`, `stride_bm = 57,344`, so the offset passes 2^31 − 1 at `pid_t = 37,450`: any call with **≥ 37,451 tokens** reads at a negative offset and dies with `an illegal memory access was encountered`. The error is reported asynchronously, usually at a later, unrelated launch.

Where this path runs:
- **SM100+ (Blackwell):** the main aggregation uses the int64-safe TMA kernel, but `_mix_fused` still runs for the DSpark aux-hidden capture (`aggregate_stream`). So a DSpark prefill pass with more than 37,450 tokens (e.g. `--chunked-prefill-size` ≥ 40k) crashes.
- **GPUs without the TMA path:** `_mix_fused` is the main aggregation of every layer.
- `attn_res_hip.py`'s `_agg_kernel` has the same `t * stride_bm` pattern.

## Modifications

- Cast the token program id to int64 in `_score_kernel`, `_combine_kernel` (`attn_residual.py`) and `_agg_kernel` (`attn_res_hip.py`). Only addressing changes.
- New GPU test `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_attn_res_mix_large_tokens.py`: runs `_mix_fused` at T = 37,451 and checks the tail rows bitwise against a run on the tail alone (rows are independent).

## Accuracy Tests

Only addressing changes. Outputs are bitwise identical to the current kernels at T = 16 / 512 / 8,192 / 32,768 (1×GB300).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`_mix_fused` latency, NB = 8, H = 7168, nvb = 7, 1×GB300 (mean of 2 runs per arm):

| T | main (µs) | this PR (µs) |
|---|---|---|
| 16 | 58.4 | 56.0 |
| 512 | 60.0 | 57.3 |
| 8,192 | 606.6 | 608.7 (+0.3%) |
| 32,768 | 2,388.7 | 2,397.6 (+0.4%) |

New test on 1×GB300: passes with this PR. On main it fails with `Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal memory access was encountered`.

Tested on v0.5.21 (the `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.21-cu130` image; main needs sglang-kernel ≥ 0.4.9). The kernels are unchanged between v0.5.21 and main. The HIP kernel change was not run on ROCm.

title: [Fix] Keep request-pool row generations monotonic across clear()
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

`ReqToTokenPool.clear()` and `DecodeReqToTokenPool.clear()`, which run on `/flush_cache` and on a disaggregation role switch, reset `req_generation` to zero. Readers of that tensor detect row reuse by comparing a generation they stored against the live value. After a flush, the first request on a row gets generation 1 again, which is exactly what the row's previous request carried whenever the row served one request since the previous flush or startup (always the case when a client flushes between batches). The stored generation then still matches, and state kept for the previous request is attributed to the new one.

The speculative verify-budget planner is such a reader (`HostConfidenceBudgetPlanner.compute_budget` compares the relayed generation with the current one): with a flush between batches it can budget a request's first verify steps from the confidence of the row's previous request. Any future reader that keys per-row state on `req_generation` inherits the same hole.

## Modifications

- `ReqToTokenPool.clear()` and `DecodeReqToTokenPool.clear()` keep `req_generation` instead of zeroing it. `HybridMambaDecodeReqToTokenPool.clear()` already did. Generations only increase, so a stored generation never matches a later request on the same row.
- `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_decode_req_to_token_pool.py`: a parametrized CPU case over both pools allocates a row, clears the pool, re-allocates the same row and checks that its generation moved. Both cases fail before this change (`assert 1 != 1`).

No kernel, model or sampling change. Behaviour changes only for a request that reuses a row after a flush or role switch, and only for readers of `req_generation`; with none active this is a no-op.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: the change is bookkeeping for generation readers only. Model outputs change only on the verify-budget path after a flush, where the budget now comes from the request's own confidence instead of the previous occupant's; verification itself is unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: one tensor zero-fill removed from a flush path.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit): ruff 0.15.1 (check and format), isort 7.0.0 and codespell 2.4.1 are clean on the three files, as are `scripts/lint/check_registered_tests.py` and `scripts/lint/check_no_bare_pytest_main.py`.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests): `test_decode_req_to_token_pool.py` 5 passed with the change, 2 failed / 3 passed with only the test applied on main. Also run locally on CPU with the change: `beam_search/test_fork.py`, `mem_cache/test_swa_unittest.py`, `mem_cache/test_mamba_unittest.py`, `mem_cache/test_dsv4_c4_state_lifecycle.py`, `managers/test_hisparse_unit.py` (60 passed, 2 skipped) and `spec/dspark/test_dspark_scheduler.py`, `spec/dspark/test_dspark_dp_tier.py` (30 passed).

title: [Scheduler] Fix the deterministic-inference hang when a prefill chunk is shorter than its alignment
author: hnyls2002
body:
- Deterministic inference truncates each prefill chunk to a multiple of an alignment (4096 by default). A per-rank chunk below it, from `--chunked-prefill-size` < 4096 or from DP attention splitting the chunk across ranks, truncated every chunk to zero tokens, so a prompt longer than the chunk waited in the queue forever
- Triton: drop the alignment; `align_window_kv_to_tiles` pads each sliding-window KV list to an absolute multiple of 128, so a chunked prefill sums keys in the same tiles as an unchunked one (built once per forward, deterministic inference only; the attention kernel is unchanged)
- Flashinfer and the DSA kpool alignment: a per-rank chunk shorter than the alignment fails at startup instead of hanging; decode servers are exempt
- Deprecate `SGLANG_TRITON_PREFILL_TRUNCATION_ALIGN_SIZE`
- Add `test_deterministic_chunk_align.py` and a chunked-vs-unchunked sliding-window case in `test_triton_attention_kernels.py`

No behavior change without deterministic inference. With it, triton prefill chunks are no longer aligned (chunked and unchunked outputs stay bitwise equal), and flashinfer configurations that used to hang now fail at startup.

title: [Fix] deepseek_v4: Fix mHC prewarm when chunked prefill is disabled
author: maocheng23
body:
## Motivation

`prewarm_mhc_pre` sizes its token buckets from `chunked_prefill_size`. With `--chunked-prefill-size -1` (chunked prefill disabled) that produces a single bucket of `-1` tokens, so `residual.new_zeros(-1, ...)` raises while weights load. DeepSeek V4 cannot start with chunked prefill disabled.

Servers that capture prefill hidden states turn chunked prefill off, so a request's states arrive in one forward. They hit this on DeepSeek V4.

## Modifications

When chunked prefill is disabled or unset, size the prewarm buckets from `max_prefill_tokens`, which bounds a prefill batch in that case. This is the same rule `pre_capture_activation_reserve_mb` uses.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: startup-only change. No kernel or forward code changed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: startup-only change.

## Tests

No unit test: removed per review. The fallback cases (`-1` / `0` / `None` chunked prefill) were exercised by a since-removed CPU test that failed without the fix and passed with it.

title: [Fix] Keep residual rows and sums consistent across appends and pipeline handoffs
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #43460
* #43459
* #43458
* #43457
* #43456
* #43455
* __->__ #43454
* #43453

## Motivation

Five defects in how a stage boundary places the residual and completes sums, each reachable on main:

1. After an append that ends on an attention which always leaves its sum, the next append rebuilt that attention's incoming boundary from a declaration without its history, took the attention as the start of the stack, and sliced a residual that was already on this rank's attention-TP slice a second time. ZAYA1's one-stage appends hit this with an a2a MoE and TP > 1: a size mismatch, or on a small batch wrong values without an error.
2. A stack (or a pipeline rank) ending on such attentions after an FFN that runs on its own rows (a2a MoE, or a dense FFN fully data-parallel) left the residual on the slice, while the next rank and the final norm expect the attention's rows.
3. DeepSeek on a later pipeline rank read the batch size and device off the owed-sum handle it received on an input-scattered batch: `AttributeError` on every later rank.
4. The FFN before a pipeline handoff resolved the rows its residual is on while it runs with two different rules, one for its entry and one for its exit. With input-scattered attention the handoff sent the attention-TP slice where the next rank expects every row; with attention DP and a dense FFN fully data-parallel, binding failed with `NotImplementedError` when a rank's last FFN followed such a dense layer.
5. `to_pp()` sent a declared partial sum unreduced for the next rank to complete. The pipeline sends one slice per attention-TP rank and gathers the slices on the receiver, so the receiver reassembled a mixture of different ranks' partials. Nemotron-H cut between a mixer and the FFN after it, and DeepSeek with input-scattered attention and a reduce-scatter boundary reduction, produced wrong outputs under PP with attention TP > 1; with an all-reduce boundary reduction, input-scattered attention summed the received output a second time.

## Modifications

- **Bind an append after an attention with the residual rows it ran on.** The stack keeps the boundary each pending stage is bound with and hands it to the stage after it. The attention-after-attention step that keeps the residual on the slice reduce-scatters over the full TP group, so binding rejects it under attention DP instead of summing across ranks that hold other sequences.
- **Return the residual on the attention's rows before a stack's last attention.** That FFN returns the residual on the attention's rows, as an FFN does when it ends the stack.
- **Read a DeepSeek pipeline rank's batch from positions, not hidden states.**
- **Keep an FFN's residual on one set of rows across a pipeline handoff.** The entry rewrite is removed; entry and exit use the FFN's own resolution.
- **Complete every sum an output owes before a pipeline handoff.** `to_pp()` completes every sum before transport and `from_pp()` declares none; the receiving stage takes the path it already binds for an input whose sum is complete.
- **Test that a pipeline cut keeps a stack's rows and values.** For stacks of two to four stages (an attention that always leaves its sum, a mixer whose exit may leave its sum to an FFN, a dense FFN, a sparse FFN), cut at every stage boundary under four parallel configurations and two boundary reductions (6,384 cuts): within each rank both sides of every boundary agree on the residual's rows, the handoff carries the residual on the attention's rows, the stages away from the cut bind as they do uncut, and a cut rejects only what the stack rejects uncut. A second test runs the sender, `to_pp()`, a transport that sends one slice per attention-TP rank and gathers them back, `from_pp()` and the receiver on simulated attention-TP ranks, and checks the values against the uncut run, that every owed sum completes once and that the receiver sums nothing.

## Accuracy Tests

How the stack is checked:
- **Unit tests**: the 39 layer-boundary test files pass at the head of every PR in the stack, apart from the two AMD-only `test_aiter_allreduce_fusion_amd` cases that fail on NVIDIA on main too; the test files that changed most recently pass on every commit. The full `test/registered/unit` suite (926 files, one process per file) shows no failure on the stack's head that main does not have.
- **Plan comparison**: an out-of-tree harness binds every stage plan for seven stack shapes (decoder layers with and without an output transform, MHC, Nemotron-H patterns, Kimi K3, Qwen4-exp, NemotronNAS-style attention-only layers, single-stage appends) over 23 parallel configurations, four boundary reductions and one or two pipeline ranks (3,928 scenarios), and compares each bound plan leaf by leaf with the parent commit's.
- **GPU**: dummy weights are seeded per TP rank and scaled (0.05, norms 1.0), so that a sum taken twice or a mixture of rank partials changes the output; the default dummy weights give every rank the same shard and would hide both.
- GPU results below were measured on these commits as based on main `516fd1c1b5` unless marked as on the merge candidate; rebasing onto current main had no conflicts, and the CPU checks were run again after it.
- **On the merge candidate** (head of this stack against main `961bcf481d`, H200, asymmetric dummy weights unless noted): DeepSeek-V2-Lite input-scattered PP2 is bit-identical to PP1 (main crashes on it); Nemotron-H cut between a mixer and its FFN differs from PP1 only at the rounding level of the FFN-to-mixer cuts (main: 0.93 and 2.21); Llama, Qwen3-MoE, GPT-OSS and DeepSeek-V2-Lite are bit-identical to main at PP1 and PP2; GSM8K (real DeepSeek-V2-Lite weights, 250 questions, TP4 with attention DP2 and the dense FFN fully data-parallel) gives 0.360 at PP2, 0.364 at PP1 and 0.368 on main at PP1, medians of three runs whose run-to-run spread is 0.012–0.016. The last revision of the stack changed only comments, docstrings, an equivalent condition and explicitly set attributes after these runs; its bound plans are identical.

For this PR:
- Each fix has a regression test that fails on its parent commit.
- (1) and (2): running ZAYA1-shaped stacks (attention, a2a MoE, attention, FFN; and attention, FFN, attention with a final norm) on simulated attention-TP ranks with fake collectives, the parent fails with a size mismatch or gives wrong values on small batches; this PR matches a per-token reference exactly.
- (3)-(5) on H200, PP2 against PP1 of the same tree (DeepSeek on this PR's tree; the other two on the stack's head, whose PP path is this PR's):
  - DeepSeek-V2-Lite (synthetic 4 layers, q_lora), TP2, input-scattered attention, `rs` with 2+2 and 1+3 layer splits and `ar` with 2+2: PP2 is bit-identical to PP1 (before: crash at the receiver, then wrong outputs, up to 2.4 in prompt logprob).
  - Nemotron-H (6 layers), TP2, cut between a mixer and its FFN: the PP2 difference drops from 0.93 / 2.21 (prefill logprob, first token diverging) to 0.011 / 0.016, the level of the FFN-to-mixer cut that never carried a partial.
  - TP4, attention DP2, dense FFN fully data-parallel, PP2: the 2+2 split is bit-identical to PP1. The 1+3 split differs by 0.098 because the dense FFN's output is written into the residual before the handoff (bf16 add, then norm on the next rank) instead of a fused add+norm; with the fused kernel replaced by add-then-norm in both runs, PP2 and PP1 are bit-identical. Main shows the same 0.098 on the 1+3 split: its PP2 output is bit-identical to this PR's (the 2+2 split fails to construct on main).
- The plan comparison differs from the parent only in the configurations each fix names.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The sum a PP rank used to leave to the next rank now completes before the handoff (one all-reduce or reduce-scatter over attention TP on the sending rank instead of one on the receiving rank). No other path changes.

Measured on the merge candidate against main (H200, dummy weights, decode with CUDA graph, three runs per tree, a difference counted only if it exceeds the same-tree spread): Qwen3-8B at TP1 and TP2, DeepSeek-V2-Lite at TP2, and DeepSeek-V2-Lite at TP4 with attention DP2, the dense FFN fully data-parallel and PP2 (1+26 layers) show no difference in prefill throughput (4k tokens, batch 1 and 8), decode throughput (batch 1, 16, 64), peak allocated / reserved memory per rank, or steady-state memory. DeepSeek-V2-Lite with input-scattered attention at TP2 PP2 runs only on this stack (main crashes), so it has no baseline.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [MemCache] Fix the strict busy check on prefill-aware SWA and tidy small leftovers
author: hnyls2002
body:
- `kv_private_swa_tokens`: count `[cache_protected_len, swa_dead_lo)` as still held. title: [Fix] Repair multimodal VMM lease cleanup and source-stream ordering
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

Fix multimodal GPU transport lifetime bugs found while investigating #43402. Thanks to @StarDuster for the report and native-stack evidence.

- Release unconsumed features on queued aborts, early rejection, and peer reconstruction failure. Session aborts release the current turn's media without invalidating borrowed history or skipping KV cleanup.
- Keep publisher rollback alive across repeated asyncio cancellation.
- Acknowledge only the current consumer, not its peers; keep unused raw features available for later re-prefill. Match consumer slots to the routed attention-DP group.
- Poll VMM acknowledgements outside the allocator lock and recheck allocation identity before reclaiming. Disable incompatible IPC borrowing for VMM.
- Wait for the producing CUDA stream before VMM publication or CPU fallback, including across the asynchronous publisher's thread boundary.

No pool-size, default-backend, or fixed-HBM-budget change.

## Validation

Remote NVIDIA GB300 development validation at `193aa211b191267f7d75ae70ccf83ab00275469b`:

Current head `7e8e24ec5bd64146e76a2db96102dc97c20dd93c` adds test-fixture corrections only; production source is unchanged. Its nine related CI-entrypoint suites passed all 169 cases in an isolated development checkout with CUDA hidden (exit 0).

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Real CUDA queued-abort A/B | Original main `e8fb52c5`: 1 / 2 / 3 occupied slices after successive cancellations; fixed: 0 / 0 / 0 |
| Source-stream race | Before: received zeros while the producing stream was writing 73; after: received 73 |
| Focused regression suites | 235 passed, including 15 CUDA VMM and 6 CUDA IPC tests; exit 0 |
| CPU-only lifecycle tests | 13 passed with CUDA hidden; exit 0 |
| Two-node, eight-rank FABRIC stress | 10,000 rounds with random 9–35 MiB features and forced CPU fallback; all ranks passed and full pool capacity recovered each round |
| Concurrent fallback smoke | Separate frontend process and 8 consumers, 1 GiB pool, concurrent GPU preprocessing and GEMM/NCCL load: 9,599 dispatches (6,344 VMM / 3,255 CPU fallbacks) in 120 seconds; both nodes exited 0 |
| Real-weight server | Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct, TP8 / two nodes, encoder DP, torchvision, explicit `cuda_vmm`, 8 MiB pool: 64 confirmed queued cancellations followed by 8 successful image requests and healthy generation; pool returned to 0 occupied bytes |

The real server hit pool-full CPU fallback and continued serving. Graphs and radix caching were disabled, with one running request at a time to exercise the waiting queue. This is a correctness regression test, not a performance benchmark.

Regression/server runtime: PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, torchvision 0.29.1+cu130, sglang-kernel 0.4.9, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, transformers 5.19.0. The short FABRIC stress used PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 / sglang-kernel 0.4.7. Driver: 580.159.04. The existing CUDA IPC teardown storage-lifetime warning remains visible.

## Remaining investigation

This fixes the reproduced leak and stream-ordering defects, **not a proven fix for the reported CUDA-driver D2H hang**. A two-hour synthetic baseline soak on original `e8fb52c5` completed 454,724 dispatches (302,413 VMM / 152,311 CPU fallbacks), with all eight consumers passing, both node exits 0, and the full 1 GiB pool free at shutdown. The paired two-hour fixed-source soak at `193aa211` also completed: 453,447 dispatches (301,495 VMM / 151,952 CPU fallbacks), all eight consumers passed, both node and wrapper exits were 0, and the full 1 GiB pool was free at shutdown. Its independent preprocessing loop completed 2,095,671 iterations; maximum observed wrap duration was 0.4287 seconds. Both nodes' logs and exit markers were preserved and SHA-256 verified. Both explicitly synchronize the source stream to isolate the unresolved hang from the separately reproduced stream-ordering bug; this is not a performance comparison.

Neither version reproduced the production hang on driver 580.159.04. This synthetic workload does not replay customer traffic or load full Kimi-K3 weights; the reporter's driver 580.126.20 remains untested. Keep #43402 open for the separate hang investigation.


### Current-head CI limitation

At `7e8e24ec`, lint and the NVIDIA small-GPU job passed, as did 13/14 CPU partitions; Rust artifacts were restored successfully (rebuild skipped). [CPU partition 11](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38025996635/job/114137022062) fails on main-side `self.enterContext` calls introduced by #43442 under Python 3.10. The affected file has the same Git blob in the CI merge and its main parent and is unchanged by this PR. Downstream GPU stages were skipped by that failure gate, so this is **not a fully green CI cycle**. No rerun or unrelated main fix is included here.

title: [diffusion] comfyui: consolidate FluxAdapter correctness fixes
author: OnePunchMonk
body:
## Summary

Consolidates four separate FluxAdapter correctness fixes in the ComfyUI SGLDiffusion plugin, all touching `executors/flux.py` (plus one checkpoint-loader fix), into one PR with one commit per fix:

1. **Pad odd-sized latents to patch size.** `_pack_latents` viewed latents straight into 2x2 patches without padding; a ComfyUI latent whose height/width isn't a multiple of 2 raised a `RuntimeError`. Pads before packing and crops back in `unpack`, matching `QwenImageAdapter`.
2. **Zero-fill missing pooled vector + reject Kontext/ControlNet.** `pack()` previously sent `y=None` straight through (crashing the DiT embedding layer) and silently dropped `ref_latents`/`control`, running Kontext/ControlNet workflows as plain text-to-image with no error. Now zero-fills a missing `y` like native ComfyUI Flux, and raises a clear `ValueError` for Kontext/ControlNet instead of silently producing a wrong result (full support is out of scope; the backend `FluxPipeline` has nothing to route these into).
3. **Resolve `guidance_embeds` from checkpoint keys.** The checkpoint loader always assumed `guidance_embeds=True`; FLUX.1-schnell checkpoints don't have `guidance_in.*` weights, so loading schnell checkpoints failed with a misleading `ValueError`. Now resolves from the checkpoint's safetensors header, matching how ComfyUI itself decides.

Fixes #43487 (tracking issue covering all four: #43115, #43488, #43489, #43395).

## Test plan

- Added/kept regression tests in `test_comfyui_adapters.py` for the odd-latent-size roundtrip, pooled zero-fill, and Kontext/ControlNet rejection.
- Added regression tests in `test_comfyui_profile.py` for `guidance_embeds` resolution (dev-shaped vs schnell-shaped checkpoints).
- `py_compile` clean on all touched files; full suite needs CI (no local `sglang` install in this environment).

title: [diffusion] comfyui: consolidate executor conditioning-cache fixes
author: OnePunchMonk
body:
## Summary

Consolidates the ComfyUI SGLDiffusion executor's conditioning-cache correctness fixes into one PR, 4 commits:

1. **Key cached conditioning on full content.** `_cond_key` truncated conditioning to a (shape, first value, last value) tuple; two different conds with the same shape and matching endpoints could collide and the worker would serve stale conditioning. Switches to hashing everything `drop_cached_fields` removes with blake2b, so a cache hit always means the worker can restore the whole thing. Fixes #43107.
2. **Cache H3 extras per cond and key them too.** MiniMax-H3 caches extra per-cond fields beyond `image_latent`; those weren't included in the cache key or dropped on a hit, so they could go stale the same way.
3. **Split batched DiT calls into per-row requests.** ComfyUI can call the executor with a batch of concatenated conds; the executor treated the whole batch as one cond, causing cross-talk between rows.
4. **Slice batched kwargs by ComfyUI's batch contract.** Companion to (3): `transformer_options` entries that are per-chunk (`cond_or_uncond`, `uuids`, `sigmas`) need slicing the same way the main tensors do.

Fixes #43111.

## Test plan

- Added/kept regression tests in `test_comfyui_session.py` and `test_comfyui_adapters.py` covering cache-key collisions, H3 extras, and per-row batch splitting.
- `py_compile` clean on all touched files; full suite needs CI (no local `sglang` install in this environment).

title: [diffusion] comfyui: plugin fixes
author: OnePunchMonk
body:
## Summary

Consolidates 6 unrelated, non-overlapping ComfyUI SGLDiffusion plugin fixes into one PR, 6 commits, to cut down on review/CI overhead:

1. **Implement `VideoInput.as_trimmed` and resolve cloud-uploaded video URLs.** `SGLDVideoInput` never implemented `as_trimmed`, which ComfyUI made abstract in ComfyUI#12107, so `SGLDiffusionGenerateVideo`/`SGLDiffusionGenerateH3` failed to instantiate their output on any ComfyUI since that change. Fixes #43190.
2. **Preserve odd-size MiniMax H3 ComfyUI layouts.**
3. **Fix ComfyUI session routing with DP.**
4. **Resend conditioning after an SGLD worker rebuild mid-run.** When `ensure_executor` rebuilds a dead worker mid sampler-run, the new worker's session cache starts empty, so stale `_sent_conds` bookkeeping dropped conditioning the new worker never had. Fixes #43189.
5. **Fix `QwenImageEditAdapter` dropping extra reference images.** Fixes #43116.
6. **Fix `SGLDiffusionServerAPI.get_model_info` hitting a 404.** It stripped `/v1` before building the request URL, but the server only registers `/models` under `/v1`, so every call 404'd and the ComfyUI "Load Server" node always failed. Also unwraps the OpenAI-style `{"object": "list", "data": [...]}` envelope the server actually returns.

Each commit touches a distinct file with no overlap between them, so there's no merge-conflict risk from bundling.

title: [Fix] DSv4.1: Size the encoder-replay SWA pool by the DSpark draft's stages, and keep more prefix tails
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --trust-remote-code \
  --tp 4 --ep-size 4 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --max-running-requests 64 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 5 \
  --enable-encoder-swa-bounded-replay --enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay
# startup, TP0: DSV4 SWA sizing: ... prefix_tails=256 / DSV4 memory calculation: ... swa_fixed=4.55 GB ... full_token=60815360
```

**The pool is priced at the wrong layer count.**
- Under encoder SWA bounded replay the target keeps its window per request, so the paged SWA pool holds only the DSpark draft's KV.
- `DSV4PoolConfigurator` prices that pool at `paged_draft_layers` = `dflash_draft_num_layers`, the draft config's `num_hidden_layers`. The DSpark head bundled with DeepSeek-V4.1 inherits the target's 40.
- `DeepseekV4ForCausalLMDSpark` builds `len(dspark_target_layer_ids)` = 3 stages. The configurator therefore reserves about 13× the bytes the draft allocates and takes them out of the full KV pool: 3.8 GB per GPU at the default, 33.5 GB at `--swa-prefix-tails 4096`. That memory stays free after graph capture.

**256 prefix tails are too few for multi-turn agentic traffic.**
- A cached prefix is reusable only while its last window still has paged SWA slots (the radix match stops at a tombstoned window).
- On a one-hour agentic-coding replay at 16 concurrent sessions, conversations idle for 3–5 minutes lose their tail while their full KV is still on the GPU. They re-prefill 130K–755K tokens, which blocks everything queued behind them for 2–13 s.
- 3.5% of requests wait more than 1 s. One request with a 104,704-token cached prefix and 311 new tokens waited 11.6 s.

## Modifications

- Record the DeepSeek-V4 DSpark draft's stage count (`SpecAuxHiddenStateConfig.dspark_num_stages`; the dense DSpark draft builds `num_hidden_layers` stages, so it is left unset there) and price the encoder-replay paged SWA by it, falling back to `dflash_draft_num_layers`.
- Under encoder replay with DSpark, default `--swa-prefix-tails` to `4 × max_running_requests × (num_layers_total // paged_draft_layers)`.
  - This keeps the byte budget of the non-replay default, which prices all target layers, and spends it on cheaper tails: 3,328 tails, ≈2.3 GB per GPU, at 64 running requests.
  - An explicit flag still wins.
- Tests:
  - `test_spec_aux_hidden_state_resolver.py`: a 40-layer draft config with three `dspark_target_layer_ids` resolves to 3 stages for the DeepSeek-V4 draft and leaves the field unset for a dense DSpark draft;
  - `test_pool_configurator.py`: the DSpark budget test now uses a 40-layer draft config with 3 stages; the default tails rule and its override.

## Accuracy Tests

Only pool sizes change. GSM8K first 50 test questions, 5-shot, greedy, launch command above; each arm runs the 50 questions cold and then again as prefix hits:

| GSM8K-50 | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| cold | 49/50 | 50/50 |
| hit | 49/50 | 49/50 |

<details><summary>GSM8K requests (our client)</summary>

- Data: `test.jsonl` (first 50) and `train.jsonl` from openai/grade-school-math.
- Prompt: the first 5 train examples as `Question: …\nAnswer: …\n\n`, then `Question: <question>\nSolve the problem. End your answer with #### followed by the numeric answer.`, sent as one user message rendered by `encoding_dsv41.encode_messages(messages, thinking_mode="chat")` and tokenized without special tokens.
- One request per question, 50 in flight:

  ```
  POST /generate {"input_ids": <prompt ids>, "cache_salt": "L1-v1-gsm8k-<index>", "sampling_params": {"temperature": 0, "max_new_tokens": 1024}, "stream": false, "return_logprob": false}
  ```
- `POST /flush_cache`, then the cold pass, then the same 50 requests again as the hit pass. Every cold response reported `meta_info.cached_tokens == 0`, and every hit response `cached_tokens >= (len(input_ids) - 1) // 256 * 256` (50/50 in both arms).
- Score: the last number in the output (commas removed) equals the last number in the reference answer.

</details>

Unit tests on CPU: `test_pool_configurator.py` 56 passed, `test_spec_aux_hidden_state_resolver.py` 4 passed. With these tests on main's source, the 4 DSpark tests fail. Results below were measured at `c5130ca00ba`; the later review commits only restrict the stage count to the DeepSeek-V4 draft, and this checkpoint still resolves to 3 stages.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same node, 4×GB300; each arm uses its default prefix tails. The static benchmark below adds `--enable-cache-report --enable-metrics --tokenizer-backend fastokens --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --reasoning-parser auto --tool-call-parser auto` to the launch command above; the startup values are the same with and without them.

| startup (TP0) | main `3831e7e0918` | this PR `c5130ca00ba` |
|---|---:|---:|
| default prefix tails | 256 | 3,328 |
| `swa_fixed` | 4.55 GB | 2.66 GB |
| full KV pool tokens | 60,815,360 | 62,058,752 |

Static prefix reuse: N distinct 16K-token prefixes at concurrency 16, one output token. Pass 1 caches them; pass 2 revisits them in reverse order with 256 new prompt tokens. All prefixes fit in the full KV pool in both arms.

```bash
python3 static_client.py --url http://127.0.0.1:<port> --out <dir>   # same command for main and this PR
```

It flushes the cache before each population, then runs N=100, N=200 and N=1000 (this PR's job reached its time limit in N=1000 pass 2, so N=1000 is not reported). Prefix hits are pass-2 requests with `cached_tokens >= 16384`; uncached prompt tokens are prompt minus cached tokens; TTFT is request start to the first streamed choice, p50 linearly interpolated.

<details><summary>static_client.py</summary>

```python
import argparse, concurrent.futures, json, math, random, statistics, time, urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

p=argparse.ArgumentParser(); p.add_argument('--url',required=True); p.add_argument('--out',required=True); a=p.parse_args()
out=Path(a.out); out.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)

def api(path, body=None):
    req=urllib.request.Request(a.url+path,data=None if body is None else json.dumps(body).encode(),headers={'Content-Type':'application/json'})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req,timeout=300) as r:
        raw=r.read()
        if path.startswith('/flush_cache'):
            assert raw.startswith(b'Cache flushed.'),raw
            return raw.decode()
        return json.loads(raw)

def request(i, n, stage):
    rng=random.Random(42+i)
    ids=[100+i]+[rng.randrange(2000,10000) for _ in range(16383)]
    if stage==2: ids += [rng.randrange(2000,10000) for _ in range(256)]
    body=json.dumps({'model':'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash','prompt':ids,'max_tokens':1,'temperature':0,'ignore_eos':True,'stream':True,'stream_options':{'include_usage':True},'return_token_ids':True},separators=(',',':')).encode()
    req=urllib.request.Request(a.url+'/v1/completions',data=body,headers={'Content-Type':'application/json'})
    start=time.perf_counter(); first=None; usage=None; token_events=0
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req,timeout=300) as r:
        for raw in r:
            if not raw.startswith(b'data:'): continue
            payload=raw[5:].strip()
            if payload==b'[DONE]': break
            d=json.loads(payload)
            if d.get('error'): raise RuntimeError(d['error'])
            if d.get('choices'):
                if first is None: first=time.perf_counter()
                token_events+=1
            if d.get('usage'): usage=d['usage']
    assert first is not None and usage is not None,(i,usage)
    assert usage['prompt_tokens']==len(ids),(i,usage,len(ids))
    assert usage['completion_tokens']==1,(i,usage)
    # Upstream UsageProcessor deliberately omits prompt_tokens_details when cached_tokens==0.
    details=usage.get('prompt_tokens_details')
    cached=0 if details is None else details['cached_tokens']
    assert 0<=cached<=len(ids),(i,cached,len(ids))
    return {'population':n,'pass':stage,'prefix_id':i,'ttft_ms':1000*(first-start),'elapsed_ms':1000*(time.perf_counter()-start),'prompt_tokens':len(ids),'cached_tokens':cached,'uncached_tokens':len(ids)-cached,'usage':usage,'stream_events_with_choices':token_events}

def percentile(values, p):
    v=sorted(values); x=(len(v)-1)*p; i=int(x); return v[i]+(v[min(i+1,len(v)-1)]-v[i])*(x-i)

def run(n):
    api('/flush_cache?timeout=30',{})
    result={'N':n,'prefix_tokens':16384,'extension_tokens':256,'concurrency':16,'generation_tokens':1,'seed':42,'pass1_order':'ascending prefix ID','pass2_order':'descending prefix ID, newest first','timing':'HTTP request start after client prompt construction to first streamed choices event; server emits this on first generated token','passes':{}}
    for stage in (1,2):
        order=list(range(n)) if stage==1 else list(reversed(range(n)))
        started=time.time(); rows=[]
        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=16) as pool:
            futures=[pool.submit(request,i,n,stage) for i in order]
            with (out/f'n{n}-pass{stage}.jsonl').open('w') as f:
                for j,future in enumerate(concurrent.futures.as_completed(futures),1):
                    row=future.result(); rows.append(row); f.write(json.dumps(row)+'\n')
                    if j%100==0: print(f'STATIC_PROGRESS N={n} pass={stage} completed={j}/{n}',flush=True)
        elapsed=time.time()-started; t=[r['ttft_ms'] for r in rows]; prompt=sum(r['prompt_tokens'] for r in rows); cached=sum(r['cached_tokens'] for r in rows)
        result['passes'][str(stage)]={'requests':len(rows),'errors':0,'elapsed_seconds':elapsed,'prompt_tokens':prompt,'cached_tokens':cached,'uncached_tokens':prompt-cached,'usage_cache_hit_rate':cached/prompt,'requests_with_cached_prefix':sum(r['cached_tokens']>0 for r in rows),'requests_with_full_16384_prefix':sum(r['cached_tokens']>=16384 for r in rows),'ttft_ms':{'mean':statistics.mean(t),'p50':percentile(t,.5),'p90':percentile(t,.9),'max':max(t)}}
        print('STATIC_PASS_DONE '+json.dumps(result['passes'][str(stage)]),flush=True)
        (out/f'n{n}-summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+'\n')
    return result

summary={'protocol':'independent deterministic raw token-ID prefixes via OpenAI streaming completions, one output token, max_workers16; identical order per arm; flush between populations','populations':{}}
summary['populations']['100']=run(100)
summary['populations']['200']=run(200)
summary['populations']['1000']=run(1000)
(out/'static-summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(summary,indent=2)+'\n')
print('STATIC_DONE',flush=True)
```

</details>

| pass 2 | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| N=100: prefix hits | 21/100 | 100/100 |
| N=100: uncached prompt tokens | 1,319,936 | 25,600 |
| N=100: TTFT p50 (ms) | 7,728 | 3,982 |
| N=200: prefix hits | 21/200 | 153/200 |
| N=200: uncached prompt tokens | 2,983,936 | 821,248 (−72%) |
| N=200: TTFT p50 (ms) | 7,944 | 4,028 |

At N=200, `--swa-prefix-tails 8192` reaches 200/200 (same client, N=200 only). The remaining misses at the default come from finished requests keeping their whole last chunk of SWA (~8.7K slots per 16K prefix) instead of one window; that retention is a separate issue and is not changed here.

## Checklist

- [x] Add unit tests.
- [ ] Update documentation as needed (the `--swa-prefix-tails` help text is updated; no other docs).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.

title: [Fix] comfyui: Fix GGUF detection, import guard and VRAM accounting in SGLDiffusion plugin
author: OnePunchMonk
body:
Fixes #43874

## Summary

Integrated-mode fixes for `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/apps/ComfyUI_SGLDiffusion/`, narrowed per review. Bug numbers match the issue.

- **Bug 1: GGUF unets could not be detected or loaded.** Detection now reads names and logical shapes from the GGUF header with `read_gguf_tensor_meta()` and runs ComfyUI's detection on them, like safetensors, so no BF16 companion file is needed. A GGUF picked in `SGLDUNETLoader` is loaded as the DiT. The GGUF loader maps tensor names through the spec's param mapping for both quant lookup and weight loading: Z-Image `qkv` -> `to_qkv`, `w1`/`w3` packed shards are concatenated into the fused `w13`, and packed tensors whose layer builds without GGUF (adaLN `ReplicatedLinear`) are dequantized on load.
- **Bug 2: `.gguf` leaked into ComfyUI's global `diffusion_models` registry.** `SGLDUNETLoader` now builds its own list with ComfyUI's `recursive_search` / `filter_files_extensions`, so the stock loader no longer offers GGUF files.
- **Bug 3: detection failure returned a bare `None`** ("cannot unpack non-iterable NoneType"). It now raises `ValueError` with the model path.
- **Bug 4: a missing runtime made every node vanish silently.** `executors/minimax_h3.py` guards its runtime imports like `base.py`, and `__init__.py` logs why registration failed.

Dropped from this PR: Cache-DiT (#43696), worker sleep/wake (#44086), server-mode items (#44082), and VRAM accounting (moved to #44086).

## Tests

Regression tests live in the existing unit files and reuse their fixtures (`test_comfyui_checkpoint_spec.py`, `test_comfyui_generator.py`, `test_comfyui_lora_node.py`); no new test file. Targeted CPU run: 52 passed.

ComfyUI v0.39.2 headless, 1x L40S, Z-Image Turbo, 1024x1024, 8 steps, seed 42:

| Path | Time | GPU mem used | vs native BF16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Native ComfyUI BF16 | 2.87 s | - | - |
| SGLD BF16 | 2.79 s | 23.7 GB | 24.2 dB PSNR / 0.879 SSIM |
| SGLD `z-image-turbo-Q4_K_M.gguf` | 3.09 s | 14.7 GB | 14.2 dB PSNR / 0.431 SSIM |

The GGUF image keeps the same composition; the lower PSNR is Q4 drift in fine detail against a BF16 reference.

H3 GGUF: checked the real `minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned-Q4_K.gguf` header against the new name mapping; 0 of 532 tensor names change, so the H3 path loads as before.

- [ ] TODO: H3 GGUF end-to-end ComfyUI run still pending.

Known gap: Flux ComfyUI GGUF likely still needs its `_convert_weights` reshapes on the GGUF path; left as a follow-up.

title: [Fix] hicache/pd: Promise prefill only the L3 span the decode prefetch takes
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

Fixes the request failures reported in #30322 (`HiCache load_back failed ... expected decode_prefix_len=64 (l1=0, l2=0, l3=64)`), which the stale #32278 tried to address by deferring the metadata send.

With a decode-side radix cache and an L3 backend, decode promises prefill a prefix that includes the L3 hit (`decode_prefix_len`) before the L3 prefetch is accepted:

1. `_build_decode_prefix_match` queries L3 with the whole suffix. `query_storage_hit_length` only requires the *suffix* to reach `prefetch_threshold` (default 256), so the returned hit can be any page multiple below it.
2. `_pre_alloc` and `_send_kv_metadata` commit `L1 + L2 + L3` to prefill, so prefill skips those tokens.
3. `_start_hicache_prefetch` then prefetches only the hit span. `prefetch_from_storage` declines spans shorter than `prefetch_threshold` (and rate-limited ones) without registering anything.
4. `check_prefetch_progress` returns True for the unregistered request, load-back covers only L1 + L2, the restore is marked `FAILED`, and the request is aborted with a 500.

So every request whose L3 hit is shorter than `prefetch_threshold` (e.g. one shared 128-token system prompt at page size 64) fails deterministically.

## Modifications

- `_start_hicache_prefetch` now uses the prefill scheduler's span shape: the whole suffix, `matched_prefix_tokens` and `storage_hit_end`. The prefetch reuses the queried hit (no second L3 query) and carries the bigram boundary token, as `Scheduler._prefetch_kvcache` does.
- If the prefetch is neither registered nor ticketed, the L3 span is cleared.
- `_start_hicache_prefetch` runs before `_pre_alloc`, and `total_prefix_len` is re-read afterwards, so `decode_prefix_len`, `cache_protected_len` and the restore reservation only cover what will actually load.

An L3 span that is accepted but later completes short (e.g. the object is evicted between query and read) still fails the restore. That is a narrower race than the deterministic failure fixed here.

## Tests

`test_decode_promises_only_the_prefetched_l3_span` (`test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py`) drives the real `_build_decode_prefix_match` and `_start_hicache_prefetch` against a real `UnifiedRadixCache` and file L3 backend (`prefetch_threshold=16`):

- an 8-token L3 hit is queried (8) but no longer promised (`decode_prefix_len == 0`);
- a 24-token hit is promised, prefetched, and lands as a 24-token host hit.

On `main` the test fails with `8 != 0`. title: [Fix] [SM120] quantization: Requantize block-FP8 MoE weights to UE8M0 for DeepGEMM
author: lucifer1004
body:
## Motivation

On SM120, `should_deepgemm_weight_requant_ue8m0` returns False for every caller, so block-FP8 MoE experts served by the DeepGEMM runner keep their FP32 checkpoint scales. SM120's grouped GEMM converts FP32 scales to UE8M0 itself, and it faults (CUDA error 719) on scales that are not powers of two.

With `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` and `--speculative-moe-runner-backend deep_gemm`, the block-FP8 MTP draft experts crash at the first prefill graph capture, at every token count. The same weights with power-of-two scales run.

#39065 (open, fixing #39063) makes the same guard change by inferring a grouped layer from `weight.ndim == 3`, without tests. This PR differs in two ways:
- `Fp8MoEMethod` passes `grouped_moe=True` explicitly.
- It adds a regression test.

Split out of #42566 at a maintainer's request. #42566 now carries only the TP block-scale refinement, which depends on this change for its DeepGEMM path on SM120.

Fixes #39063

## Modifications

- Keep the SM120 exemption for dense block-FP8 GEMMs, which run on CUTLASS or Triton with FP32 scales there.
- Requantize grouped MoE weights to UE8M0 as on SM90 and SM100.
- `should_deepgemm_weight_requant_ue8m0` and `requant_block_scale_ue8m0_for_deepgemm` take a keyword-only `grouped_moe` flag, which `Fp8MoEMethod` sets for its expert weights.

## Accuracy Tests

`test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_deepgemm_ue8m0_requant.py` adds a case for the SM120 grouped-MoE requant.

Two existing tests in that file fail on SM120 hosts both with and without this PR:
- `test_helper_requants_supported_deepgemm_bf16_once`
- `test_compressed_tensors_block_processing_preserves_ue8m0_marker`

They patch DeepGEMM's UE8M0 flags on but not the device, and SM120 deliberately skips the dense requant they exercise. The file passes on the CPU runner it is registered for.

End to end, together with the TP refinement in #42566:
- `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` at TP2 with its own MTP head (NEXTN 3/1/4, draft experts on DeepGEMM) scores 0.976 on GSM8K through the chat template (lm-eval `gsm8k`, 1,319 questions, flexible-extract) on 2x RTX PRO 6000.
- Without this change, the same draft experts on DeepGEMM fault on SM120 at TP1 already.

title: [Fix] mamba: Release consumed lazy Mamba prefix locks before donation retry
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Dependency

Depends on #43567, now merged and included in this branch. Releasing the prefix lock alone can expose stale in-place checkpoint donation under slot pressure.

## Problem and change

With lazy overlap, the next decode can consume the temporary tracking slot before the previous prefill donates its checkpoint. Donation then needs a replacement slot while the consumed prefix state is still locked, exhausting the pool and asserting.

On a failed lazy donation allocation, release this request's consumed Mamba prefix reference before eviction/retry. Preserve KV locks and other requests' references; record the release to avoid a double decrement. Keep the allocation assertion and existing capacity formulas unchanged.

The CPU regression covers full 3-slot and 4-slot per-request pools and the subsequent normal unlock. A registered GPU regression additionally uses exactly 4 Mamba slots and 1 running request: warm a 128-token prefix, then extend it to 255 tokens and generate 32 tokens with overlap and decode CUDA graphs enabled. The first decode takes the fourth slot before prefill donation, which must reclaim the consumed prefix instead of requiring a fifth slot. It reuses the existing Mamba KL test server and CI registration. Checkpoint invalidation is handled separately in #43567.

## Validation

- Exact base/head red-green check with the same new testcase on GB300: base `f05da43d44067e4e4f95302b6d3bd40f7deb3b1d` plus the testcase fails in `prepare_for_caching_req` -> `_alloc_mamba_slot` with `AssertionError: Can not alloc mamba cache` (exit 1); PR head `c29503969e33f5c8e103cde6abb1caba209abd99` passes (exit 0). The base run uses the unmodified base runtime, not a selectively reverted fix.

- Added GPU regression validated on GB300 with Qwen3.5-0.8B: both tests in `test_mamba_cache_kl.py` pass (49.7 seconds), including the existing checkpoint-reuse test with KL=0.
- Negative control: remove only this PR's prefix-lock release block while retaining #43567; the new test fails in prefill checkpoint donation with `AssertionError: Can not alloc mamba cache`.
- Pre-commit passed for the added test.

- This branch independently: 14 CPU tests and 12 subtests passed; pre-commit passed.
- The two PRs merge without conflicts. Their combined runtime files are identical to the previously validated combined fix (43d6c962aa).
- Combined E2E on GB300 with overlap and decode CUDA graphs: Qwen3.5-0.8B passes 24 requests with 1 running request / 4 slots and 96 with 4 / 16; Qwen3.5-4B + NEXTN passes 24 with 1 / 4. Original main asserts in these cases. Both single-request 4-slot runs exactly match their 8-slot references in output tokens and logprobs. Ordinary and NEXTN 3-slot runs also complete 24 requests each.

The earlier combined GPU results cover both fixes together. The new negative control isolates the prefix-lock release change while retaining checkpoint invalidation.

title: [Fix] Account for captured inputs in DeepGEMM masked workspace budget
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

DeepGEMM's automatic standard-layout policy can select a masked workspace that OOMs during prefill CUDA Graph capture. The estimate assumes the runner input is released after the gate/up GEMM, but capture makes `dispose_tensor` a no-op: the input and its scales remain live during activation and the down GEMM.

Reproduced on H200 with the default memory fraction, prefill chunk size, and graph settings:

| Model | TP | Failing prefill shape | Masked budget | Failing `down_output` allocation |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 | 1 | 4608 | 3.15 GiB | 2.38 GiB, with 1.20 GiB free |
| Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 | 2 | 3072 | 5.37 GiB | 4.88 GiB, with 1.89 GiB free |

The 30B failure reproduces with a warm compilation cache. Minimal 30B reproduction: `python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 --tp-size 1 --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm`.

## Modifications

Include the retained input and scales in the activation/down-GEMM peak estimate. Use the same conservative bound during warmup and capture so layout selection stays consistent. Extend the existing layout-policy test with the two failing geometries and packed/unpacked scales; no new test files.

Explicit layout overrides and the budget fraction are unchanged. Automatic selection can switch to compact earlier on other models too: the existing 397B-shaped fixture now selects compact at 8K under its 42.5 GiB budget, while 4K remains masked. That can change performance near the selection boundary.

## Accuracy Tests

- Existing `test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_minimax_quant_scatter.py`: **53 passed** on GB300. The six parameterized policy cases fail against the original estimator.
- Both affected models complete startup, graph capture, serving benchmarks, and GSM8K with the fix on H200. Validation base: `e35f60b9`.
- GSM8K: 1,314 held-out cases, greedy, 2,048-token cap, identical case IDs/prompt hashes. Qwen3-30B fixed-auto scored **1215 / 1217** across two runs; forced-compact controls scored **1223 / 1221**. All requests stopped normally, with no errors. The reverse pair loses 13 and gains 9 cases; these results do not establish numerical equivalence.
- Qwen3.5-122B fixed-auto scored **1275**, versus **1277** with the default Triton MoE runner. Both have the same two length-capped cases, retained in scoring, and no request errors. Original DeepGEMM auto cannot supply an accuracy baseline because startup fails.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Qwen3-30B, one H200, 320 requests, nominal 8K input / 1K output, concurrency 64. Saved prompts and actual token counts match across all four runs. Repeated in reverse order:

| Configuration | Output token/s, runs 1 / 2 | Median TPOT ms, runs 1 / 2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Forced compact | 1852.52 / 1853.72 | 30.608 / 30.596 |
| Fixed auto | 2083.69 / 2083.45 | 26.780 / 26.779 |

Fixed auto retains masked decode while using compact for large prefills: about **12.4%** faster than the forced-compact workaround, with median TTFT around 4.04 seconds in both configurations. The default Triton runner remains faster at 2140.95 token/s; this fixes capture reliability rather than establishing a generally faster backend. Qwen3.5-122B also remains slower with DeepGEMM than with its default Triton runner.

## Checklist

- [x] Pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed.
- [x] Extended an existing test file; GPU suite passed.
- [x] GPU startup, accuracy, and serving comparisons completed.
- [x] No public API or launch-option changes requiring documentation.

title: [Fix] Reserve remaining tokens for ignore_eos requests during prefill admission
author: BBuf
body:
When admitting a new prefill batch with prefix caching enabled, `PrefillAdder` discounts the remaining output tokens of running requests by `new_token_ratio`, including requests with `ignore_eos=True`. These fixed-length requests cannot finish through early EOS. On Qwen3-32B/H200, the ratio decays to 0.098 while the workload still requires 1,024 output tokens, allowing prefills that subsequently force running requests to retract.

Use a ratio of 1.0 for running `ignore_eos` requests, preserving the existing `CLIP_MAX_NEW_TOKENS` cap and the normal EOS-aware policy. Extend the existing admission-budget tests with a real `PrefillAdder` regression covering fixed-length, ordinary, and partially decoded requests. Related earlier investigation: #7328.

Validated against `e35f60b9` on the same H200, Qwen3-32B revision `9216db5781bf21249d130ec9da846c4624c16137`, TP1, C32, 160 requests, nominal 8,192-token inputs and fixed 1,024-token outputs. Request hashes and actual input/output token lengths match across each pair. These are single paired runs; the small throughput differences are not claimed as a stable speedup.

| Mode | Version | Timed retractions | Output tok/s | Median TTFT (s) | Median TPOT (ms) | p99 E2E (s) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Default | Baseline | 5 | 465.44 | 16.719 | 45.32 | 124.58 |
| Default | Fix | 0 | 466.95 | 15.792 | 44.65 | 120.28 |
| Mixed chunk | Baseline | 5 | 467.89 | 6.643 | 56.76 | 122.29 |
| Mixed chunk | Fix | 0 | 469.21 | 6.629 | 55.57 | 119.88 |

Validation:
- Existing `test_prefill_memory_budget.py` and `test_prefill_adder.py`: all 65 tests and 46 subtests pass. The new admission regression fails on the baseline. Updated the existing request mock to include the default `ignore_eos=False`, as required by the running-request budget calculation.
- Both fixed runs complete without a retraction; the separate baseline profiles each contain one additional retraction beyond the five timed above.
- Full held-out GSM8K, matched prompts: default 1250/1314 before and after, with identical correctness per case; mixed 1246/1314 before and after, with five losses and five gains. Every request ends with `stop`, with zero errors or token-limit finishes. Equal aggregate scores do not imply identical mixed-batch outputs.
- Pre-commit checks pass. No new test files.

This fixes under-reservation in cached admission; it does not claim to close the entire Qwen3-32B latency gap or remove retractions for every workload.

title: [Fix] diffusion: OpenAI API hardening
author: OnePunchMonk
body:
Part of #43875 (items 1-7). This PR used to also carry items 8-33. Those are now split into two follow-up PRs so each one can be reviewed on its own:
- runtime/utils fixes (items 8-24): #44887
- pipeline and model-helper fixes (items 25-33): #44888

The three PRs touch disjoint files and can merge in any order.

## Summary
Hardens the diffusion HTTP API. Item numbers match #43875.

1. Invalid `output_quality` returned 500; it now returns 400 (`adjust_output_quality` raised outside the try block).
2. `response_format="url"` with no cloud storage and no `output_path` ran the whole generation before returning 400. It is now rejected up front. Unsupported `response_format` values are also rejected before generation.
3. A cloud-upload failure (storage enabled but upload failed) returned a misleading 400 "requires cloud storage". It now returns 502. When `output_path` is not set, the generated file is still removed with the request's temp directory. Behavior change: clients that matched on the old 400 will see 502.
4. URL image inputs were read fully into memory. Downloads now stream into a temp file with a 50 MiB cap, enforced on Content-Length and on bytes received (chunked bodies). The file is moved into place only on success and removed on any error.
5. `upscaling_model_path` / `frame_interpolation_model_path` accepted any URL and the server fetched it. Network entry points (OpenAI, realtime, Vertex, rollout) now reject URLs with 400 in `build_sampling_params`, which they all share. Local paths and HF repo ids still work, and the CLI and Python API still accept URLs (the check is not in `SamplingParams`).
6. The upscaler and RIFE model caches (and the resolved-path cache) grew without bound with client-chosen paths. They are now small LRU caches, guarded by one lock.
7. `frame_interpolation_scale` (0.25-4.0) and `upscaling_scale` (1-8) are range-checked in `SamplingParams._validate` (finite, non-bool). The bounds are chosen, not derived; they match the shipped RIFE scale values and Real-ESRGAN x2/x4/x8 weights. `frame_interpolation_exp` is bounded separately by #43014 (merged).

## Tests
- New cases are added to existing files: `test_openai_security.py` (download cap, response_format, output_quality, LRU caches and lock), `test_multiple_task_types.py` (URL model paths rejected over HTTP, 502 and temp-dir cleanup through the real endpoint), `test_sampling_params.py` (scale ranges, CLI still accepts URL model paths).
- Those three files plus `test_openai_image_api.py`: 149 passed on CPU.
- No GPU run: these are request-handling and validation changes.

## Notes
- 50 MiB download cap and LRU sizes (4 models, 256 paths) are arbitrary constants.
- Local file paths for model weights are still accepted over HTTP (loaded with weights_only=True).

title: [CI] Fix Kimi-Linear DCP PD test startup
author: mmangkad
body:
## Summary

The DCP arm of `test_disaggregation_kimi_linear.py` fails at startup on main:

```
ValueError: Chunked prefill is aligned to 4096 tokens, but each rank's chunked prefill size is 64; ...
```

#43444 added `check_truncation_align_fits_chunk`. Deterministic flashinfer aligns prefill chunks to `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_PREFILL_SPLIT_TILE_SIZE`, which must be `<=` the chunk size:

| | Split tile | `--chunked-prefill-size` | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before | `4096` (default) | `64` | every chunk truncates to 0, so startup is rejected |
| After | `64` | `64` | chunks keep all 64 tokens |

The fix sets the tile through `DCP_ENV` on the prefill and decode servers. The reference server reads the same env, so parity is unchanged. The TP arm doesn't use flashinfer and is untouched.

OK

title: [Fix] kimi-k3: Preserve pipeline graph bank inputs and bound chunk profiling
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR was part of the following stack (oldest at bottom; all merged):

* #43607
* #43606
* #43605
* __->__ #43604

## Motivation

The text-only Kimi K3 wrapper does not expose its pipeline layer range to the model runner. A receiving stage consequently captures an empty inherited attention-residual bank: block-aligned cuts produce incorrect decode results, and cuts inside a block fail graph capture. Dynamic chunk profiling can also allocate requests longer than the request-to-token mapping, leaving KV slots unreachable during release.

## Changes

Expose the text model's actual start/end layers. Bound complete profiling requests by model context and request mapping capacity, preserve the existing 1.25x chunk probe range when capacity allows, and release each prepared profiling request even if its forward fails. The prefill budget continues to constrain predicted chunks.

## Validation

- B200, synthetic 6-layer Kimi K3, bank block size 4, asymmetric dummy weights, TP2, NCCL: unchanged main reproduces the 3+3 capture assertion, 4+2 decode logprob difference of 0.06181, and 477,708 leaked KV slots after dynamic profiling.
- Fixed chunk size 16: graph PP2 at both 3+3 and 4+2 cuts, and eager PP2 at 3+3, match graph PP1 bitwise across all six prompts, including prefill and decode logprobs.
- Dynamic chunking: default chunk budget startup succeeds; both cuts complete eight prompts up to 4,104 tokens with live chunk predictions and graph decode, without idle pool invariant failures. Their complete outputs match bitwise.
- CPU coverage includes three model-range regression methods and two profiler methods. The updated profiler methods pass, covering context/mapping limits, a 20,480-token probe for a 16,384-token base chunk with sufficient context, and forward-failure cleanup. Two probe-range subcases fail with the prior prefill-budget cap. All pre-commit checks pass.

GPU results are from the prior revision. Removing the prefill-budget cap leaves profiling lengths unchanged for those configurations: their 8,192-token context or 1.25x chunk limit is tighter. GPU comparisons were not rerun for this profiler-only revision.

The two fixes are rebased onto main `72730d6360` with unchanged patch IDs. The adapter PRs above this one build on these fixes. CPU regressions were rerun on the resulting stack; prior B200 comparisons were not rerun.

## Current Stack Validation

All three updated adapter commits passed pre-commit independently; the two K3 commits are unchanged. The final stack CPU suite passed **481 tests and 7,409 subtests**, with **21 hardware-specific skips**. Independent common-layer and Inkling boundary suites passed **372 tests / 7,315 subtests** and **386 tests / 7,329 subtests**, respectively.

Four new regressions fail on the prior implementation and pass with the fixes. They cover terminal export releasing state retained by an old output handle (including a failing final norm), terminal reader binding for written/pending/fused output with two contexts, rejection and cleanup when binding changes read capabilities, and rejection of bindable update results on both immediate and deferred exit paths. Existing tests cover the converted containers, short-convolution positions and stateless V4 terminal reads.

The earlier callback-selection, transformed-reader and row-transport context regressions remain covered. No GPU tests or formal performance benchmarks were rerun for these fixes; prior GPU evidence retains its stated limitations.

## Landing

Rebased onto main `71a17dbc24` for merge. Validation above predates this rebase; no tests or benchmarks were rerun as part of landing.

title: [diffusion] fix: Qwen-Image BCG prompt padding misses every graph and attends the pad
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

With `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph`, Qwen-Image and Qwen-Image-2512 replayed no captured graph, and every miss produced a wrong image.

- **Every request missed.** The Qwen-Image padder buckets `freqs_cis` but not the complex RoPE cache `freqs_complex`. Its text half keeps the prompt length, so the serving signature never matches a captured one.
- **A miss attended the pad.** A miss runs the padded kwargs eagerly. The padder had also bucketed `txt_seq_lens`, and the eager forward builds its varlen text ranges from that, so the zero-padded text rows were attended as real tokens. Against the same prompts run eager: Qwen-Image-2512 17.6–37.6 dB PSNR, Qwen-Image 25.7–34.1 dB. In one prompt the composition and the person changed. This hits any BCG miss, including resolutions that were never warmed up.

## Modifications

- Pad `freqs_complex` together with `freqs_cis`.
- Leave `txt_seq_lens` unset on padded inputs, so the mask alone marks the valid text. The eager fallback builds its varlen ranges from the mask; replay is unchanged (`DynamicVarlenMaskMeta`).
- Remove the now-unused `bucket_txt_seq_lens`.

## Accuracy Tests

1x H200, 1024x1024, 20 steps, torch.compile off. Four prompts, BCG output against eager:

| | before | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image-2512, warmed resolution | 17.6–37.6 dB, every request MISSED | 0 MISSED; 2/4 bit-identical, the others 43.4 / 32.8 dB |
| Qwen-Image, warmed resolution | 25.7–34.1 dB | 0 MISSED; 2/4 bit-identical, the others 54.0 / 33.9 dB |
| Qwen-Image-2512, 768x768 (not warmed, so a miss) | attends the pad | 2/4 bit-identical, the others 34 / 43 dB |

The remaining non-identical prompts are short ones (under ~48 tokens). For those, the text-stream GEMMs (txt_in, qkv, mlp_down) pick a different cuBLAS kernel at M = prompt length than at M = bucket. That is floating-point reordering, not attention over the pad. Qwen-Image-2.1 is unaffected: its prefix runs eager at the exact length.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not a performance change. The captured graphs now replay instead of every request falling back to eager.
