title: [diffusion] fix: replay Qwen-Image-2.1 BCG graphs across prompt lengths
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Qwen-Image-2.1 with `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph` never replays a captured graph for a prompt whose length differs from the warmup placeholder. On GB300 (main 3831e7e09) the warmup captures 33 segments with 72 inputs, yet every real request logs `serving signature MISSED` and runs eager, on 1 GPU and under TP2 alike.

`QwenImage21DenoisingStage` disables prompt padding on purpose. Prefill (step 0) is eager anyway. After it, a DiT step reads nothing of the prompt except each layer's prefix K/V and the target RoPE, and the K/V are at the exact prompt length. 72 = 4 step inputs + 4 layout tensors + 32 layers x K/V.

## Modifications

- `model_padders/qwen_image21.py` acts only on cached steps (single sample, caches filled, sp == 1). It left-pads the prefix K/V to the text bucket and stacks all layers into one tensor, so a replay copies one input instead of 64. It also drops the prefill-only inputs and adds a 0-d `prefix_pad`. A prefix longer than the largest bucket is left alone; the runner reports the miss once.
- The DiT's target attention runs at a model-level `eager_on_graph` break point (`attend_past_prefix_pad`). It reads the live pad once per forward and slices `k[:, pad:]`. Because the pad is on the left, the valid K/V form one strided view, so the kernel receives exactly the eager K/V.
- The stage-level override that disabled padding is removed.

## Accuracy Tests

BCG against eager, four prompt lengths (including ~350 tokens in the 512 bucket): bit-identical (max_abs = 0), on 1x H200, on 2x H200 TP2 and on 2x GB300 TP2. Before this PR the comparison was trivially identical, because every request ran eager.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Qwen-Image-2.1 1024x1024, served. Median of 5 per round, three interleaved rounds; the arms differ only in `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph`.

| | eager | BCG, this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1x H200 | 4.521 / 4.525 / 4.518 s | 4.546 / 4.540 / 4.544 s (+0.5%) |
| 2x H200, TP2 | 2.788 / 2.790 / 2.792 s | **2.737 / 2.731 / 2.740 s (−1.9%)** |

On one H200 the step is GPU-bound (103 ms), so replay saves no launch time. What remains is BCG's own cost: each attention break copies its output into the bridge buffer, plus 33 graph launches. Under TP2 each rank's GPU work halves, the launch cost shows, and BCG wins.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests:
  - `test_diffusion_bcg_padding.py`: prefix lengths in one bucket share a signature, and calls without a replayable prefix are not padded.
  - `test_qwen_image21_cuda.py`: one captured graph replays bit-exact across prompt lengths.

  On GB300 (main 5730345 + this PR), with `test_qwen_image21.py`: 141 passed.
- [ ] Update documentation: N/A.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

This PR and its sibling PR for Qwen-Image / 2512 padding both edit `prompt_padding.py` and `test_diffusion_bcg_padding.py`. Whichever lands second may need a trivial rebase.

title: [Fix] Kimi-K3: Fix derived weight buffers across CUDA graph reloads
author: wolfcomos
body:
## Motivation

Reloading Kimi-K3 weights after CUDA graph capture can leave captured operations reading old derived-weight storage. AttnRes also retains its cached norm/projection product after the underlying weights change, affecting eager execution as well.

## Changes

- Preserve MLA absorbed projection buffers across reloads.
- Reuse merged MoE front and CUDA BFA buffers, restoring parameter views into the merged storage. Preserve the dequantized BFA projection buffer as well.
- Reuse the ROCm fused KDA input-projection buffer across reloads, preserving whole-buffer, BFA-tail, and parameter-view addresses.
- Refresh CUDA KDA fused-decode tensor arguments in place.
- Refresh both BF16 and FP32 AttnRes cached products in place during post-load processing.
- Add repeated-reload regressions and replace dynamic attribute access in the MLA test with direct tensor access.

The reload contract assumes unchanged model configuration, shapes, dtypes, and devices. Native ROCm kernels and all quantized loader variants are not covered by this validation. This is not a claim that every K3 hot-update path has been validated.

## AMD/ROCm follow-up

The Python buffer-lifecycle fix for the ROCm fused KDA input projection is included and regression-tested on H100 by invoking `_merge_kda_inproj_weights_hip()` with an eligible fixture. Native AMD/ROCm graph replay, fused kernels, and token-threshold branches still need validation, tracked in [#47508](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/47508). H100 results do not establish ROCm end-to-end hot-update correctness.

## Validation

The original MLA regression failed before its fix and passed after it on one H100, with exact graph/eager projection equality after two successive updates.

The four additional regressions exercise front-weight views, dense/dequantized BFA buffer lifetime, CUDA KDA static buffers, and both AttnRes cache dtypes. Each performs two updates after CUDA graph capture, checks changed values, exact replay/eager buffer equality, and stable addresses. The dequantized BFA branch uses a mocked dequantization boundary returning fresh tensors; it does not validate an FP8 quantizer.

On one H100 80GB using PyTorch `2.14.1+cu130` / CUDA 13.0 and `lmsysorg/sglang:dev` at digest `sha256:78142f9f4b7fb3ee27f59065615dc7bb263f643ed256c9299c3861086ade4d47`:

- All four new cases reproduce failures on the previous PR head `f05814ad4eaa02f28afd6d86c3b1fc8fd049e098`, using the same image and test source.
- The complete registered test file passes **10/10** in **11.659 seconds** with commit `cc5159e`.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python test/registered/unit/models/test_kimi_k3_bfa_overlap.py -v
```

Follow-up commit `810b49e2bc3ee7d80ebc3beb520638f77d2a29fb` adds the HIP input-projection storage regression. On one H100 PCIe with PyTorch `2.14.1+cu130` / CUDA 13.0 and image digest `sha256:77ff63ee69fd7ebef20df3a6d036ee4b8a4ffe0734efb0028c3b7643386e3ccf`:

- The same new test fails against parent `58a5db50225e8aad6b3a3ee9652b90e122a4e8ea` (including stale replay values after the second update) and passes after the fix.
- The complete registered test file passes **11/11** in **10.802 seconds** using full SGLang imports.
- The regression captures tensor copies, checks exact replay/current-buffer equality and stable addresses across two reloads, verifies parameter aliases and zero padding, and does not execute AMD fused kernels.

Applicable pre-commit checks pass. Full-model accuracy, real rollout weight synchronization, and performance benchmarking are outside this validation.

title: [diffusion] fix: select VSA-H3 for FastH3 when no transformer backend is given
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

FastH3 8-Step V2 was distilled with VSA-H3 (`fastvideo_inference.json`: `attention_backend: VIDEO_SPARSE_ATTN_H3`, `vsa_sparsity: 0.8`). Since #37662, sglang runs VSA-H3 only when it is selected with `--component-attention-backends transformer=video_sparse_attn_h3`. A FastH3 server started without it serves dense FlashAttention: the trained `to_gate_compress` branch is skipped, and on 4x H200 a request takes 12.6 s instead of 10.0 s.

That is easy to miss. Our cross-framework benchmark profile predated #37662 (#41839 selected VSA-H3 itself) and ran dense attention for three days, while vLLM-Omni served the same checkpoint with VSA. sglang went from ahead to 15% behind on H200, and the server log only says `Using fa attention backend`.

## Modifications

- `FastH3PipelineConfig.validate_server_args` selects `video_sparse_attn_h3` for the transformer when the user gave no transformer backend (neither `--attention-backend` nor a transformer entry in `--component-attention-backends`). The text encoder and VAEs keep their own backends, as the cookbook recommends.
- It does not select it, and dense attention stays, where VSA-H3 cannot run: off CUDA, on GPUs other than SM90 / SM100 / SM103 (the backend's supported set, now `VSA_H3_CAPABILITIES` in `platforms/cuda.py`), or with torch.compile, the breakable CUDA graph or ring attention, which VSA-H3 rejects.
- `ServerArgs.set_automatic_component_attention_backend` records the choice as automatic (`is_component_attention_backend_automatic`), the same way LTX-2 records its text-encoder backend.
- Cookbook: describe the default and how to select dense attention (`--component-attention-backends transformer=fa`).

## Accuracy Tests

With no transformer backend given, the default now goes through the same path as passing `--component-attention-backends transformer=video_sparse_attn_h3` explicitly. Nothing changes when a backend is given.

4x H200, base `53295c697` (main) vs this branch (`f6f923520`), the FastH3 V2 T2VA request (1344x768, 124 frames, seed 1101, 8 steps), two requests per server, MP4 md5 of each request:

| server | transformer backend | md5 (request 1 / 2) |
|---|---|---|
| main, no transformer backend | `fa` | `25b927f2` / `9de1795b` |
| **this PR, no transformer backend** | `video_sparse_attn_h3` (automatic) | **`4a7fb255` / `e62efe95`** |
| this PR, `--component-attention-backends transformer=fa` | `fa` | `25b927f2` / `9de1795b` |
| main, `--component-attention-backends transformer=video_sparse_attn_h3` | `video_sparse_attn_h3` | `4a7fb255` / `e62efe95` |

The new default matches the explicit VSA-H3 flag bit for bit, and an explicit `fa` still matches main's dense output bit for bit. Both rounds gave the same md5s.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Same box, the four servers interleaved twice, client wall clock per request (median of two after warmup), sglang eager (`--ulysses-degree 4 --performance-mode speed --enable-torch-compile false`):

| server | round 1 (s) | round 2 (s) |
|---|---:|---:|
| main, no transformer backend (dense FA) | 12.656 | 12.639 |
| **this PR, no transformer backend** | **10.064** | **10.027** |
| this PR, `transformer=fa` | 12.646 | 12.706 |
| main, `transformer=video_sparse_attn_h3` | 10.053 | 9.994 |

On this box vLLM-Omni eager serves the same checkpoint with VSA in 10.95–11.06 s.

## Checklist

- [x] Format with pre-commit.
- [x] Unit tests: `test_server_args.py` (default on SM90 / SM100 / SM103; kept dense for an explicit transformer backend, an explicit `--attention-backend`, torch.compile, and SM80) and `test_minimax_h3_fasth3.py`.
- [x] Docs: cookbook FastH3 section.

title: [diffusion] fix: shard Qwen-Image adaLN modulation and text FFN under TP
author: niehen6174
body:
## Motivation

On 2x RTX 5090 (32 GB, PCIe, no P2P), Qwen-Image under `--tp-size 2` cannot keep or swap the DiT. The rank-local TP checkpoint slice is **29.60 GiB per rank**, so TP2 only removes about 22% of the ~38 GiB DiT:

- `--dit-cpu-offload true --text-encoder-cpu-offload true` OOMs while moving the DiT onto the GPU.
- Keeping the DiT resident leaves no room for the text encoder.
- The only working option was streaming the DiT layer by layer every step: 62.2 s, or 41.7 s with 30 resident layers.


Two groups of weights are copied in full on every rank:

- `img_mod` / `txt_mod` are `ReplicatedLinear(dim, 6*dim)`, holding 6.8B of the 20B parameters.
- `txt_mlp` is replicated whenever `tp <= 2`, holding 4.5B parameters. This default was tuned on H100 with NVLink, where it gave -8% latency at tp=2.

## Modifications

Four commits (the fourth simplifies the second; the net change is what is described here):

1. **Shard the adaLN modulation projections under TP.**
   - The modulation input is one token per sample, so the output can be column-sharded and the `[B, 6*dim]` result all-gathered at negligible cost.
   - When `tp > 1` and the checkpoint is unquantized, `img_mod` / `txt_mod` become `ColumnParallelLinear(gather_output=False)`.
   - `_gather_modulation_shards` all-gathers the img and txt shards in one collective per block. It also covers `zero_cond_t`, where the two batch sizes differ.
   - The modulation cache stores the gathered tensors, so cache behavior is unchanged.
   - `tp == 1`, quantized and Nunchaku checkpoints keep `ReplicatedLinear`.
   - The rank-local TP loader already slices `ColumnParallelLinear` weights by output dim, so the loader needs no change.
2. **Shard the text FFN under TP.**
   - `txt_mlp` was replicated whenever `tp <= 2`. It now uses the same column/row-parallel layout as `img_mlp`.
   - The replication came from an H100 measurement (-8% latency at tp=2). That win is given up on H100-class devices; it was not re-measured here.
   - On the 5090 the sharded layout was also slightly faster than the replicated one (21.25 vs 21.72 s).
   - There is no new env var or config knob.
3. **Docs:** a Qwen-Image cookbook section for two 32 GB GPUs.
4. **Drop the memory gate and env override from (2).** An earlier revision of this PR replicated `txt_mlp` on devices with at least 48 GiB and added `SGLANG_QWEN_IMAGE_REPLICATE_TXT_MLP`. Both are removed, so `txt_mlp` is always sharded under TP and no knob is added.

New unit test `test_qwen_image_tp_shard.py` checks that the gathered modulation layout equals the full projection, including the `zero_cond_t` 2:1 case.

Qwen-Image-2.1 uses its own `qwen_image21.py` and is not affected.

## Accuracy Tests

Setup: 1024x1024, 50 steps, CFG off, seed 42, same prompt.

| Comparison | PSNR | max-abs |
|---|---|---|
| New TP2 vs old TP2 (layerwise) | 44.6 dB | 44 |
| New TP2 vs 1 GPU | 24.8 dB | 202 |
| Old TP2 vs 1 GPU (reference) | 24.9 dB | 203 |
| tp=1 before vs after | identical | 0 |

TP2 drifts from 1 GPU by the same amount before and after this change, and the new TP2 output looks the same as the old TP2 output side by side.


## Speed Tests and Profiling

Setup: 2x RTX 5090 32 GB (SM120, PCIe, no P2P). Client wall-clock median of 5 runs after 2 warmup runs, concurrency 1.

| Config | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Per-rank DiT slice (TP2) | 29.60 GiB | 19.06 GiB |
| TP2, `--dit-cpu-offload --text-encoder-cpu-offload` | OOM | **21.3 s** (peak ~22 GB/GPU steady) |
| TP2, DiT resident, `--text-encoder-cpu-offload` | does not fit | **19.7 s** (peak 31.75 GB) |
| TP2, `--dit-layerwise-offload` (no resident layers) | 62.2 s | **43.0 s** (peak 14.5 GB) |
| TP2, previous replicated `txt_mlp` layout, with DiT CPU offload | – | 21.7 s |
| 1 GPU, DiT layerwise (regression check) | 72.01 s | 72.00 s |

Previous best sglang TP2 result: 41.7 s (DiT layerwise, 30 resident layers).

Layerwise offload also gets faster: each streamed layer shrinks from about 0.49 to 0.32 GiB per rank.

Ulysses2 + layerwise runs the tp=1 code path, which this PR does not touch. It takes 75.0 s, slower than TP2 because Ulysses does not shard the weights and every rank streams the full DiT each step.

Not re-measured on H100. There this PR shards `txt_mlp` too, which gives up the -8% at tp=2 noted in the removed comment. The modulation sharding adds one small all-gather per block (`[B, 6*dim]`, B = batch).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).

title: [PD][NIXL] Fix staging buffer startup by accepting slot_layer_ids
author: michal-shalev
body:
## Motivation

Enabling `SGLANG_DISAGG_STAGING_BUFFER=1` with the nixl transfer backend fails at scheduler init:

```
File "sglang/srt/disaggregation/prefill.py", line 365, in _init_kv_manager
    kv_manager.set_kv_buffer_tensors(
TypeError: NixlKVManager.set_kv_buffer_tensors() got an unexpected keyword argument 'slot_layer_ids'
```

5f216fc33f (#35758) added `slot_layer_ids` to both call sites (`prefill.py` and `decode.py`) and to `MooncakeKVManager.set_kv_buffer_tensors`, but left `NixlKVManager.set_kv_buffer_tensors` with the three argument signature from #22536. Both call sites pass the keyword unconditionally, so the NIXL staging path cannot start.

## Changes

Accept and store `slot_layer_ids` in `NixlKVManager.set_kv_buffer_tensors`, matching `MooncakeKVManager`. NIXL calls its own `send_kvcache_staged` rather than the shared `PrefillStagingStrategy.transfer`, and that path does no pipeline parallel layer pairing, so storing the value is sufficient.

## Validation

Two node PD, 8x H100 80GB per node, DeepSeek R1 Distill Qwen 32B, prefill TP 2 feeding decode TP 4, NIXL over UCX. On main both roles raise the TypeError during init and the server exits. With this change both roles come up and serve requests through the staging path.

No unit test is added because the coverage gap is in fixture configuration rather than in this file. `server_fixtures/disaggregation_fixture.py` pins the transfer backend to mooncake under CI, so `TestDisaggregationStagingDecodeLargerTP` only ever exercises mooncake, and `test_nixl_backend_basic.py` sets `SGLANG_DISAGG_STAGING_BUFFER` to `false`. Can push that separately.

title: [Fix] diffusion: keep ZMQ ingress sockets on their configured port
author: Shan2L
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #43731.

The scheduler ingress ROUTER and the disagg orchestrator's frontend/result sockets are bound with `get_zmq_socket`'s default retry policy, which moves to `port + 42` when the configured port is taken. Their peers keep connecting to the configured endpoint, so with two instances starting at the same time the second instance's request is executed by the first instance and the second one hangs.

## Modifications

- `Scheduler`: bind the ingress with `same_port=True`, i.e. retry on the configured port (TIME_WAIT) and fail with `EADDRINUSE` instead of moving.
- `DiffusionServer` orchestrator: same for the frontend ROUTER and the encoder/denoiser/decoder result PULL sockets. Pool workers already did this.
- `get_zmq_socket`: the final error log printed a `+42` port even in `same_port` mode; it now prints the endpoint actually tried.
- New CPU unit test `test_zmq_bind_port.py`: the same-port helper fails/succeeds as expected, and the scheduler requests `same_port=True`. The scheduler test fails on `main`.

The race in `settle_port` (checked at parse time, bound later) is not addressed here. After this change, the instance that loses the race fails with a clear error and does not steal or lose requests.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A, no compute changes.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

N/A.

## Tests

- `pytest test_zmq_bind_port.py test_scheduler_client.py test_dp_routing.py`: 18 passed.
- End to end, MiniMax-H3 TP2, two concurrent `sglang generate` with `--scheduler-port 7000`:
  - `main`: instance 2 rebinds to 7042, instance 1 executes both requests (its log shows instance 2's `output_file_path`), instance 2 hangs until killed.
  - this PR: instance 1 retries 7000 for about 9 s, then exits with `ZMQError: Address already in use (addr='tcp://127.0.0.1:7000')`. Instance 2 finishes normally.

title: [Fix] Link cuda_ipc JIT against CUDA driver stubs dir
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## What

`_init_ipc_manager` links the `cuda_ipc` JIT module with a bare `-lcuda`. Where `libcuda.so` isn't on the linker search path, the build fails (`ld: cannot find -lcuda`); `parallel_state.py` catches it with a warning and continues with custom allreduce disabled, so affected setups fall back to NCCL (~5x slower per call in the incident we measured). Fix: use `cuda_stubs_dir()`, same as `dsv4/wo_a.py` and `kda_ptx_prefill`.

## Why it wasn't caught before

Not a recent regression — bare `-lcuda` dates to the v2 rewrite (#31049). It's masked only in images that symlink the stub into the system libdir (AOT, sgl-deep-ep). The main `docker/Dockerfile` (release + dev images) doesn't; we hit it on a dev-image GB300 box with no `/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so`.

Sibling with the same flags: `vsa_block_sparse_sm100_jit.py` (untouched here — different subsystem, source-level exposure only).

## Verification (GB300, previously failing)

- old flags → build fails (control)
- fixed flags → links, `register_once()` succeeds
- no change where the link already worked

title: [Fix] [AMD] diffusion: Compare ReduceOp by identity so the compiled TP all-reduce stays one graph
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
## What

Makes `GroupCoordinator.all_reduce` compare its `op` argument by identity (`op is ReduceOp.SUM`) instead of with `==`. This fixes `test_compiled_all_reduce_is_one_graph` on the ROCm lanes, e.g. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38249882022/job/114813200452

## Why

Dynamo in torch 2.9 and 2.11 (the AMD images run these) cannot trace `RedOpType.__eq__`. The compiled all-reduce therefore raises `Unsupported: Builtin operator.* comparison with constant self failed` under `fullgraph=True`, and graph-breaks otherwise. torch 2.14 handles `==`, which is why CUDA CI passes.

The CPU shm branch of the same method already uses `is`. Every caller passes the `ReduceOp.SUM` class attribute itself (the default or `cfg_model_parallel_all_reduce`'s default), so the fast path is chosen exactly as before. A caller passing another op still falls through to `torch.distributed.all_reduce`.

The IPC all-to-all test failure in the same job is handled in #44096.

## Test plan

- A standalone repro of this condition under `torch.compile(fullgraph=True, backend="eager")` on CPU torch wheels: `==` fails on 2.9.1 and 2.11.0 and passes on 2.14.1. `is` passes on all three.
- ROCm 10 (MI300): `test_compiled_all_reduce_is_one_graph` passes in [multimodal-gen-test-1-gpu-amd (rocm10, 1)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38429220418/job/115408085238), and the TP2 server case `flux2_modelopt_fp8_tp2_t2i` passes in [multimodal-gen-test-2-gpu-amd (rocm10, 0)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38429220418/job/115408085022). The other failures in that run are unrelated: tests that already fail on `main`, Hugging Face rate limits on LoRA downloads, and a GPU hang in a single-GPU server test.

title: [Fix] [AMD] deterministic: Bypass AITER GEMM and MoE in deterministic mode on gfx950
author: aarnetalman
body:
## Motivation

This PR makes `--enable-deterministic-inference` deterministic on MI350X/MI355X (gfx950) with AITER enabled, the default in the ROCm images. In deterministic mode it keeps unquantized linear and MoE layers off AITER's GEMM and fused-MoE kernels, which pick a different kernel depending on the batch size. Those layers use SGLang's batch-invariant matmul and Triton MoE runner instead, as the CUDA path already does.

**Which models this affects.** Every unquantized (bf16) linear or MoE layer on gfx950 in deterministic mode, so not only bf16 checkpoints but also the bf16 layers inside quantized ones:

- **gpt-oss** (20b, 120b): the attention projections and the router are bf16 (the experts are MXFP4 and go through ROCm/aiter#6583). Without this PR, gpt-oss-20b and -120b in deterministic mode give 50 and 47 different outputs for 50 identical requests; with it, one (below).
- **Qwen3.8 / Qwen3.5** (bf16 checkpoints): every linear, including the Gated DeltaNet projections. With the GDN fixes (#44076, #44194, #44195) Qwen3.8-27B is deterministic with this PR and not without it (table below).
- **MiniMax-M3**: its unquantized layers (for example the router); MiniMax-M3 passes every exact check at TP2/TP4 with this PR, ROCm/aiter#6583 and #46397/#46786.
- **DeepSeek-V4.x, GLM-5.3**: their unquantized layers take the same path, but these models are not deterministic yet for other reasons (FP8 block-scale and MXFP4 GEMMs), so this PR is one prerequisite there.

The numbers below use gpt-oss-20b/-120b and Qwen3.8-27B, plus Qwen3-8B, the model AMD CI's deterministic test runs.

Today, unquantized linear layers call AITER's GEMM directly, and unquantized MoE layers use AITER's CK fused-MoE. Both choose the kernel, tile and split-K from the number of tokens, and neither goes through the batch-invariant `aten::mm`. So a request's log-probabilities change with whatever else is in its batch. For example, Qwen3-8B's QKV projection runs four different kernels at M = 1, 60, 32 and 1920.

This is the ROCm counterpart of an existing rule in the same file. On Blackwell, deterministic mode resolves `--bf16-gemm-backend auto` to `torch` instead of `cutedsl`, and rejects an explicit `cutedsl` as batch-size dependent (#33945). AITER's GEMM and fused MoE are batch-size dependent in the same way, by design: they are tuned per token count. ROCm had no equivalent rule, and AMD CI runs the deterministic test with AITER on only on MI300, so this went unnoticed.

If AITER later offers a batch-invariant mode for these kernels (as ROCm/aiter#6583 does for the MXFP4 MoE), deterministic mode can call AITER with it instead of skipping it; the check added here is where that switch would go.

## Modifications

- `unquant.py`: in deterministic mode on gfx95, unquantized linear and MoE layers skip AITER and use the batch-invariant matmul and the Triton MoE runner. The decision is made once per layer and applies to the GEMM branch, the expert-weight shuffle and the MoE runner selection.
- An explicit `--moe-runner-backend aiter` with deterministic mode on gfx95 now raises a clear error, like the existing `cutedsl` check.
- `test_deterministic.py`: also registered on the MI35x per-PR suite (`stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`) as the regression test.
- Unchanged: serving without the flag, other GPUs (including MI300), quantized layers and all other AITER kernels.

With tensor parallelism, determinism also needs the all-reduce fix in #34543.

## Accuracy Tests

1x MI350X (gfx950), newest nightly `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm724-mi35x-20261011`, comparing the image's `unquant.py` (before) with this PR's (after). TP1, `--attention-backend triton --enable-deterministic-inference`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`. Checks: `python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic --test-mode prefix --return-logprob` and `--test-mode radix_cache` (50 trials), plus a bitwise comparison of 1,275 responses (batch sizes 1-50) against batch size 1.

| Model | Before | After (this PR) |
| --- | --- | --- |

title: [AMD] Fix Flux2 kv-gather abort on non-contiguous K/V
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

Flux2 packs Q, K, and V in one projection and then `chunk`s them. Those K/V tensors are views, so they are not contiguous. With `--num-gpus 2` and sequence parallel left on its default, SGLang selects `kv_gather_degree=2`. The full-sequence gather then calls `all_gather_into_tensor` on that view. PyTorch's NCCL process group (`check_gpu_single_tensor`) rejects it with `ValueError: Tensors must be contiguous` before the collective runs. The same check is in the CUDA build, so NVIDIA hits it on this path too. The prefix and suffix branches already called `.contiguous()`. The unsliced branch did not, and that is the branch Flux2 takes.

## Modifications

- `USPAttention._gather_sharded_sequence` materializes the unsliced K/V tensor with `.contiguous()` before `sequence_model_parallel_all_gather`.
- `GroupCoordinator.all_gather` does the same immediately before `all_gather_into_tensor`, so any other non-contiguous caller of that collective meets the NCCL/RCCL requirement. An already-contiguous tensor is returned unchanged.
- `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_sp_kv_gather_contiguous.py` builds a K tensor with `chunk`, asserts it is not contiguous, and asserts the tensor passed into the gather is contiguous and equal to the original view. CPU CI: `base-a-test-cpu`.

## Accuracy Tests

Same prompt, seed 42, 720p, 50 steps, `torch.compile` on. The 1-GPU image is `20261012-055625`. The 2-GPU kv-gather image after this fix is `20261012-071319`. Both are 1280x720. The broken run saved no image, so this is 1-GPU versus 2-GPU sequence parallel, not a before/after of the copy. The unit test checks that `.contiguous()` keeps the same values as the view.

| metric | value |
| --- | --- |
| mean abs (0-255) | 2.46 |
| RMSE | 8.42 |
| max abs | 255 |
| PSNR | 29.6 dB |
| pixels with abs diff > 8 | 8.6% |

## Benchmarking and Profiling

MI355, Flux2-dev, 720p, 50 steps, seed 42, `torch.compile` on. The 2-GPU kv-gather run aborted before the fix, so it has no latency.

| config | result | denoising | per step |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 GPU | completed | 24.79 s | 0.409 s |
| 2 GPU kv-gather, before | abort: `Tensors must be contiguous` | — | — |
| 2 GPU kv-gather, after | image saved | 20.19 s | 0.351 s |

title: [Fix] Preserve HTTP errors for non-streaming /v1/messages
author: Vegetog
body:
## Motivation

Non-streaming `/v1/messages` requests currently turn an upstream `HTTPException(503)` into `500 api_error`. In particular, a queue-full rejection loses its overload status because the Anthropic handler catches it as a generic exception.

This fixes the non-streaming follow-up explicitly listed in #43779. It is independent of that PR and can be merged separately.

## Modifications

- Catch `HTTPException` before the generic exception handler and preserve its status code, mapping it through `ERROR_TYPE_MAP`. A queue-full rejection now returns `503 overloaded_error`.
- Reuse the existing message sanitization: 4xx messages retain useful details after sanitization, while all 5xx responses continue to return `Internal server error`.
- Log the original status code and detail server-side without duplicating the generic error-response log.
- Add regression coverage for raised exceptions, including integer and `HTTPStatus` 503, message sanitization, diagnostic logging, and unexpected exceptions. Existing returned-error tests continue to run.

The exception handler covers both internal request conversion and non-streaming execution, so HTTP exceptions raised during conversion also retain their status. Streaming behavior is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A. No model outputs or inference kernels are changed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A. This changes HTTP error handling only.

## Tests

- Before the status fix, both integer 503 and `HTTPStatus.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` regression cases failed with `500 != 503`.
- Before the logging fix, both 500 and 503 logging regression cases failed because the original detail was missing.
- After both fixes, the Anthropic unit test file passed all 71 tests on Linux x86_64 with GPUs hidden, using the repository's existing CPU kernel stub.
- After pruning redundant subtests and dropping a `CancelledError` identity test that failed on CI's Python 3.10, the file passes all 68 tests on Python 3.10.
- Ruff checks (`F401,F821,F823,UP037`), Ruff formatting, isort, and `git diff --check` passed for the changed files.

The environment used Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu129, and Transformers 5.19.0; this was a native unit-test run, not the full CI dependency lock or a model-server end-to-end test.

title: [Fix] [AMD] deterministic: Refuse RCCL all-reduce in deterministic mode above TP2
author: aarnetalman
body:
## Motivation

This PR makes `--enable-deterministic-inference` on ROCm refuse `--disable-custom-all-reduce` when `--tp-size` is above 2. That combination sends every tensor-parallel all-reduce through RCCL, which is not batch-invariant at four or more ranks: the server starts normally, but a request's output depends on what else is in its batch.

On ROCm, deterministic mode relies on SGLang's one-stage custom all-reduce, in which every rank reduces all inputs in a fixed order. CUDA instead disables the custom all-reduce and pins NCCL (tree algorithm, fixed channel count); ROCm has no such pinning, and pinning RCCL's algorithm and protocol (`NCCL_ALGO=Ring NCCL_PROTO=Simple`) does not make it batch-invariant either (results below). At TP2 each output element is the sum of two operands, which has only one order, and RCCL passes every check there, so TP2 stays allowed.

Impact: only ROCm users who pass both flags with `--tp-size` above 2. They now get a startup error instead of silently batch-dependent results; dropping `--disable-custom-all-reduce` fixes it.

## Modifications

- `arg_groups/overrides.py`: a validation pass, `_deterministic_rocm_rccl_check`, raises a `ValueError` for deterministic mode + ROCm + `tp_size > 2` + `disable_custom_all_reduce`.
- `arg_groups/attention_hook.py`: runs it in the ROCm branch of the existing tensor-parallel check in `handle_deterministic_inference`.
- `test/registered/unit/test_model_overrides.py`: two CPU cases. One for the refusal; one for the setups it must leave alone (CUDA, deterministic mode off, TP2, custom all-reduce on).
- Unchanged: deterministic mode without the flag, TP1 and TP2, CUDA, and everything without `--enable-deterministic-inference`.

Independent of #34543, which makes the custom all-reduce itself batch-invariant for inputs larger than its buffer.

## Accuracy Tests

**Why RCCL is refused.** Qwen3-8B, BF16, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-8B --tp <N> --attention-backend triton --enable-deterministic-inference --disable-custom-all-reduce`, `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm724-mi35x-20261006`. Checks: `python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic --test-mode prefix --return-logprob` and `--test-mode radix_cache` (50 trials), plus a bitwise comparison of 1,275 responses (batch sizes 1-50) against batch size 1.

| RCCL setting | GPU | TP2 | TP4 | TP8 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| default | MI350X | pass all | fail all | - |
| default | MI355X | pass all | fail all (81/1275 bitwise-identical) | - |
| `NCCL_ALGO=Ring NCCL_PROTO=Simple` | MI355X | pass all | fail all (347/1275) | fail all (121/1275) |

**This PR.** MI350X, `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm724-mi35x-20261011`, the image's files before and with this change.

| Deterministic, `--attention-backend triton` | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TP2, TP4, TP8 | accepted | accepted |
| TP2 + `--disable-custom-all-reduce` | accepted | accepted; the server starts and generates |
| TP4 or TP8 + `--disable-custom-all-reduce` | accepted | `ValueError` at startup |

- Checked with `ServerArgs.resolve_once()` for all six combinations, and with `launch_server` for TP2 and TP4.
- The new test cases pass, and every other test in `test_model_overrides.py` has the same outcome with and without this PR.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance effect: this is a startup-time argument check.

title: [Fix] [NPU] disaggregation: Fix host-pool backup for decode retraction
author: wutaosang
body:
## Motivation

Enable the existing `--disaggregation-decode-retraction-backup host_pool` option and automatically selected host-pool backup on Ascend NPU decode servers.

When a decode server uses host-pool backup without enabling hierarchical caching or decode KV offload, it still needs Ascend HiCache IO and memory-layout settings. These settings were only applied to hierarchical caching and KV offload. In addition, `page_first_direct` host buffers used the wrong dimension when building per-layer views, which could cause incorrect KV transfers or out-of-bounds indexing when the host pool has fewer pages than model layers.

## Modifications

- **`python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/utils.py`**: Apply the Ascend HiCache configuration when the server role is `decode` and the retraction backend is explicitly `host_pool` or unset for automatic selection. This selects `kernel_ascend` IO and the existing NPU layout selection; MHA uses `page_first_direct`.
- **`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/mha.py`**: Build per-layer views for `page_first_direct` by transposing the page and layer dimensions, as already done for `page_first`.
- **`test/registered/unit/npu/test_decode_retraction_backup.py`**: Add eight registered NPU tests covering configuration selection, FIA and non-FIA buffers, exact KV restoration into newly allocated device pages, partial pages, exhausted host capacity, and the `none` backend.

## Accuracy Tests

On the rebased head `ac5429a08b`:

- All **8 NPU unit tests passed** in `sglang-wt-a3`, including actual NPU KV backup/restore with both `cpu_tensor` and `host_pool`.
- `git diff --check` and Python syntax checks passed.

Integration validation before the rebase used actual **Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct** weights with BF16, MHA, TP=1, Ascend transport, and eager prefill/decode. Each scenario used four concurrent requests generating 64 tokens:

| Scenario | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Baseline | All four requests completed without retraction. |
| `cpu_tensor` | All four requests completed after eight retractions; generated token IDs matched the baseline exactly. |
| `host_pool` | All four requests completed after eight retractions; generated token IDs matched the baseline exactly. |
| Automatic selection | Resolved to `host_pool`; all four requests completed after eight retractions and matched the baseline exactly. |
| `none` | Retracted requests returned HTTP 503; the remaining request completed. |
| Exhausted host pool | The request that could not be backed up returned HTTP 500; the other three completed. |

All six decode instances remained healthy after their requests. These PD integration scenarios have not been rerun after the rebase.

Shared CPU cache regression tests before the rebase: **32 passed, 1 skipped**, with the optional NPU-only Mamba copy kernel disabled for CPU fixtures. This fixture adjustment was not used for the NPU unit tests or PD integration runs. Ruff and isort also passed before the rebase.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No throughput or latency benchmark was run. Validation focused on KV preservation and request recovery; integration coverage is limited to the MHA, TP=1, eager configuration described above.

title: [Fix] hicache: Key MLA Mamba state per TP rank in the HF3FS backend
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

MLA shares KV storage keys across TP ranks, but Mamba checkpoints are sharded. On MLA models all HF3FS ranks use rank 0's file and metadata, so Mamba pages from different ranks used the same key. Give Mamba keys a TP rank/size suffix so one rank cannot overwrite another rank's checkpoint. Keep existing keys for other pools. Same fix as #43594 for NIXL.

Old unranked Mamba entries are not reused because their owning rank is ambiguous.

Validation: the new two-rank Mamba round-trip test fails before and passes after.

title: [Fix] DSA: skip-topk pipeline handoff for owed outputs
author: AaravMehta-07
body:
Fixes #43580

## Motivation

`DeepseekV2Model.forward` exports the stage output through `residual_batch.to_pp()` before checking whether a non-idle batch has rows that require DSA top-k indices. A residual-stream output may still be represented locally by an opaque `OwedOutput`, so reading `hidden_states.shape` after export raises `AttributeError` during the PP handoff.

## Modifications

- Read the row count from the exported `proxy_tensors["hidden_states"]` tensor.
- Use the same exported tensor when allocating empty top-k indices for the zero-row case, preserving its device and the existing `torch.int32` shape contract.
- Add a CPU regression that runs the real `DeepseekV2Model.forward` PP branch with an `OwedOutput`, exercises `residual_batch.to_pp()` / `ResidualStream.export()` for declared-sum and deferred-finalize outputs, and covers nonempty/empty rows.

## Tests

- Baseline: the new real-forward regression raises the reported `AttributeError: OwedOutput has no attribute shape` before this fix.
- `pytest test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_pp_mtp_embedding.py -q -s` (CPU-only): 5 passed, 18 environment/deprecation warnings.
- Independent root rerun after rebasing to `1809335`: 5 passed. The native-filesystem Python source copy used for faster imports was SHA-256 verified against the submitted production file; the test file was loaded directly from the submitted worktree.
- `pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_pp_mtp_embedding.py`: all applicable hooks passed.

No GPU/model-load or throughput benchmark was run. The change is confined to PP metadata bookkeeping and empty-index allocation; the focused test uses CPU tensors and mocks only the parallel reduction/finalization work.

title: Fix autograd retention in CUDA graph capture tail hooks
author: ix-48
body:
## Motivation

CUDA graph capture tail hooks run after the model forward returns, outside the forward's no-grad scope. The scheduler's event-loop grad-mode guard does not cover startup graph capture either. As a result, hooks that use trainable parameters can build autograd history during warmup and capture even though the model forward itself disables gradients.

For example, `DsparkDraftSampler` computes Markov corrections and confidence scores using parameters with `requires_grad=True`, then copies the results into persistent output buffers. Without no-grad, these writes attach `CopySlices` history to the buffers and keep saved tensors from successive warmup/capture calls alive. With Qwen3-8B + DSpark and a decode capture limit of 256, disabling grad during startup capture eliminates this history and reduces ready-process GPU memory by **806 MiB**.

## Modifications

- Decorate `Scheduler.init_all_cuda_graphs` with `@torch.no_grad()`. It is the single startup entry for CUDA graph capture of the target and draft workers, so everything capture runs around the model forward (tail hooks, input preparation, draft-worker graphs) no longer records autograd history. Recapture after startup already runs inside the guarded event loops.
- Plain `torch.no_grad` rather than `DynamicGradMode`: with `SGLANG_ENABLE_TORCH_INFERENCE_MODE=1`, buffers created during capture would become inference tensors, which the `no_grad` disagg event loops cannot write in place.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test_decode_cuda_graph_runner.py`: 20 passed (unchanged).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

A/B configuration:

- Hardware: one NVIDIA H20, TP=1.
- Target model: `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`.
- Speculative decoding: `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK`, with draft model `deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_8b_block7`.
- Attention backends: `--attention-backend fa3 --speculative-draft-attention-backend fa3`.
- Ragged verify: `SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=compact`.
- Capture and concurrency limits: `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 256 --max-running-requests 256`.
- Captured buckets: default prefill graphs enabled, with 58 token buckets up to 8192; target verify and draft decode each use 51 sparse request buckets up to 256.

Only the no-grad guard differs between the two runs.

| Measured quantity | Without no-grad | With no-grad | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Server process GPU memory after startup | 91.171875 GiB | 90.384766 GiB | **806 MiB** |
| Physical GPU memory added during draft graph initialization (warmup + capture) | 2,684 MiB | 1,878 MiB | **806 MiB / 30.03%** |
| Autograd nodes retained by persistent sampler output buffers after capture | 7,501 | 0 | 7,501 |
| GPU storage kept alive for backward by those buffers (excluding model parameters; counted once per storage) | 1,648.319 MiB | 0 | 1,648.319 MiB |

The first row includes model weights and KV cache. The last row measures retained tensor storage; its reduction need not equal the physical memory reduction because the allocator can keep freed storage for reuse. No inference-speed benchmark or full accuracy evaluation was run.

### Single H200 re-check of the scheduler-level guard

Same launch configuration as above (Qwen3-8B + DSpark, fa3, `SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=compact`, `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 256 --max-running-requests 256`), on one H200.

| Variant | Server process GPU memory (MiB) | Draft verify graph capture (GB) | Target prefill + verify capture (GB) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| main | 138,968 | 2.78 | 3.06 + 2.59 |
| `no_grad` around tail hooks only | 138,162 | 1.99 | 3.06 + 2.59 |
| `no_grad` on `init_all_cuda_graphs` (this PR) | 138,162 | 1.99 | 3.06 + 2.59 |

All three variants return the same greedy `/generate` output.

title: [Fix] tokenizer_manager: Prevent scheduler crash and has_audio_understanding misreport for audio-declaring models without an audio tower
author: enternal111
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #43864

An audio request sent to a model whose multimodal processor defines an audio token but has no audio tower - e.g. `gemma-4-31B-it`, a non-audio variant of the Gemma 4 family whose `config.json` ships `audio_config: null` - is not rejected at the API layer. It reaches the scheduler, where `get_audio_feature()` raises inside `model.forward`, and the whole scheduler process dies.

Two underlying problems, both fixed here:

1. Request validation only checks `is_multimodal`, not per-modality capability, so the audio request passes tokenization/dispatch and fails deep in the scheduler, killing the scheduler process.
2. `ModelConfig.is_audio_understandable_model` used `hasattr(hf_config, "audio_config")`. Because the config key is present with a `null` value, `hasattr` is `True` even though no audio tower exists, and the model is misreported as audio-capable (`/get_model_info`: `has_audio_understanding: true` for `gemma-4-31B-it`).

Scope:

- The crash (problem 1) affects only models whose processor defines an audio token while the model has no audio tower. For all other models the audio never reaches the scheduler: models whose processor defines no audio token drop it in the processor, and text-only LLMs have no multimodal processor at all.
- The misreport (problem 2) is a config-level issue: it affects any model whose `config.json` carries `audio_config` with a `null` value.
- Existing behavior is otherwise unchanged: for models whose processor defines no audio token, requests are handled exactly as before (verified on `glm-5.3-flash`, see Production verification). The only intentional exception is the corner case noted under Limitations.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/configs/model_config.py`: `is_audio_understandable_model` now requires `audio_config` to be present and non-`None` (top-level and under `thinker_config`) instead of `hasattr`. This makes the capability flag - and the `/get_model_info` report - correct for models with a `null` audio config.
- `python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py` (`_tokenize_one_request`): reject with a per-request error when a request carries audio data, the model's multimodal processor defines an audio token, and the top-level audio_config is present but explicitly None (audio tower disabled), return 400 with :

  ```
  Audio inputs are not supported by <served_model_name>
  ```
  Limitations:
  - Audio only; the same shape of problem could exist for other modalities but is out of scope here.
  - Corner case : on the native `/generate` path, a request that passes valid `audio_data` for a model whose processor defines an audio token but which has no audio tower, while the prompt carries no audio placeholder, used to succeed (the base processor drops the surplus audio with a warning); it is now rejected with the same 400 error. The OpenAI path is unaffected - it always inserts the placeholder, and those requests previously crashed the scheduler. We keep the broader guard because an explicit error is preferable to silently discarding user-provided audio.

## Accuracy Tests

No model output path is changed (the guard rejects requests that would otherwise crash the engine; the config-flag change only corrects a misreported capability), and existing behavior for models whose processor defines no audio token is preserved. 

Verified on `gemma-4-31B-it` (4x H20): an audio request now returns a clean per-request error instead of killing the scheduler, and the engine keeps serving:

```json
{"object":"error","message":"Audio inputs are not supported by gemma-4-31B-it","type":"BadRequestError","param":null,"code":400}
```

Existing behavior also verified on `glm-5.3-flash` (whose processor defines no audio token): an audio request still returns 200 exactly as before this change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable - no change to the forward path; the only addition is a lightweight per-request validation at tokenization time.


## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations) - N/A: the Gemma 4 cookbook page already documents which variants support audio; no doc change needed.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed) - N/A: no model-output or performance change (see above).

author: chrikrah
body:
## Motivation

An image above twice `Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` (178,956,970 pixels) makes `Image.open` raise `DecompressionBombError`, before any decode. That class subclasses `Exception`, not `OSError`, so neither `except (OSError, SyntaxError)` in `_load_image` nor `CLIENT_MEDIA_EXCEPTIONS` catches it. `_load_single_item` then reports the image the client sent as a server fault, a 500, where `test_base_processor_bad_input.py` says client media that cannot be decoded raises `ValueError`.

```
$ PYTHONPATH=python python bomb.py   # main 279f1fa, Pillow 12.3.0
PNG 27385 bytes, 225,000,000 pixels, Pillow limit 89478485
RuntimeError <- DecompressionBombError: 0...: Image size (225000000 pixels) exceeds limit of 178956970 pixels, could be decompression bomb DOS attack.
```

Refs #43707: once #43713 restores the Pillow limit for NanoNemotron, those requests reach this path too.

## Modifications

- `utils/common.py`: add `Image.DecompressionBombError` to `CLIENT_MEDIA_EXCEPTIONS`. Every user of the tuple (`llava.py`, the encoder preprocessor, `systemone/serving.py`) gets the same 400.
- `test_base_processor_bad_input.py`: a 15000 x 15000 1-bit PNG, about 27 KB, must raise `ValueError` caused by `DecompressionBombError`. The class also joins `test_tuple_covers_the_documented_families`.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no model output changes.

```
$ PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_base_processor_bad_input.py
11 passed, 2 warnings, 16 subtests passed in 10.87s
# not run: a live server; ValueError to 400 rests on serving_chat.py:2301
```

Baseline on `279f1fa` is `10 passed, 2 warnings, 15 subtests passed`. With the `common.py` change reverted and the tests kept, it is `2 failed, 10 passed`: `test_decompression_bomb_image` and the `DecompressionBombError` subtest. `ruff` 0.15.1 (`--select=F401,F821`, `format --check`), `isort` 7.0.0 and `codespell` 2.4.1 pass on both files.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: one more class in an `except` tuple.

title: [Fix] glm4v: Clamp request video budgets to the deployment limit
author: cipheraxat
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #43705.

GLM-V video requests could raise `fps`, `max_frames`, `max_tokens_per_frame`, and `max_image_tokens` above the deployment budget before frames were decoded. A large request could then make the worker decode far more frames, at higher resolution, than the default config allows.

## Modifications

- Clamp each request knob to the deployment limit, so a request can only tighten the budget. Omitted knobs stay unset, so an `fps`-only request does not inject `max_frames` and bypass the HF sampler.
- The `max_frames` limit comes from the processor's `max_frames`, or from `--mm-process-config`. GLM-4.1V/4.5V/4.6V processors have no `max_frames`; their HF sampler stops at `max_duration * fps` (600 by default), so that value is the limit there. It follows a server `fps` override.
  - Note: GLM-4.6V's own HF sampler allows up to 640 frames, so a request asking for 601-640 frames now gets 600. This is deliberate: the limit stays at or below what the default config samples.
- At decode time, drop a request `max_tokens_per_frame` when its total pixels (`cap * 28^2 * frame_count`) exceed the shared presize budget. The frames then go through the shared presize path. A server-configured per-frame cap keeps per-frame mode.
- On the DP encoder path, make that decision with the full clip length, so every shard picks the same resizer.
- Reject non-positive, non-numeric, and non-finite values. `ChatCompletionMessageContentVideoURL` now declares `gt=0` (and `allow_inf_nan=False` for `fps`), so OpenAI-path requests get a 400 before batching. The processor keeps the same check for the native `/generate` path.
- Log a one-time warning when a request value is clamped.
- Docs: `multimodal_language_models.mdx` now says GLM-V request knobs can only tighten the budget, and operators raise the limits with `--mm-process-config`.

## Accuracy Tests

No model-forward or kernel change. Tests in `test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_glm4v_mixed_offsets.py` build budgets with the real `glm_processor_video_config`. They cover:
- per-knob clamps, including the server-raised limit and the GLM-4.xV `max_duration * fps` limit;
- a 1-hour clip where a request can no longer sample more frames than the default HF sampler;
- the pixel-based per-frame drop and the DP full-clip count;
- the server per-frame mode;
- rejected values at both the processor and the API schema.

The GLM-4.xV frame-limit, per-frame pixel, and schema tests fail on the previous head and pass now.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No inference-speed change. The clamp bounds decode work that a request could otherwise raise.

title: [Fix] multimodal: Preserve empty media in parallel sampling
author: KrishnanPrash
body:
## Motivation

The nonempty multimodal `n > 1` fix has already landed in #41768. This PR now covers only the remaining empty-list boundary cases:

- Promoting a single request with empty media/hash lists to a parallel-sampling batch must preserve the request dimension.
- Empty video/audio lists in an existing batch must behave as absent inputs rather than causing `IndexError` when extracting a request.

## Changes

- Normalize single-request media and hash lists through a small shared helper, with explicit field access.
- Expand absent video/audio inputs consistently with absent images.
- Test empty media with text, input IDs, and input embeddings; batched inputs; and rejection of empty hashes when images are nonempty.

The earlier gRPC caller-hash override is removed: #47120 makes cache identity content-derived. This PR has no net protobuf or Rust changes and does not allow a caller-supplied hash to substitute for content identity. Previously reported nonempty `n > 1` serving results are historical, not validation of this narrowed diff.

- Head `ac8f08fc29ef174c4926d0a1c8ebafebb539743a`, compared with pinned main `7c8ada7ec6890b045245adac4787b410be5ac909`.

title: [Fix] scheduler: Abort held decode requests, and read live requests from the lists
author: hnyls2002
body:
With every live request in a list (`Scheduler.request_lists()`), a few places that walk their own subset of queues and batches either miss requests or repeat the list of holders. This makes them read the lists, and lets an abort reach the one list it skipped.

- `abort_request` also aborts a PD decode request held for rebootstrap while generation is paused (`DecodePreallocQueue.held_rebootstrap_reqs`). Such a request holds no KV and no step uses it, so it finishes and is released at once. `DecodePreallocQueue.take_aborted` now removes the retracted and held requests an abort matches; the scheduler only releases them.
- `_has_active_sampling_mask_request` reads every list instead of its own set of batches and queues. It now also sees requests in the PD prefill bootstrap and transfer queues, launched prefills, the dLLM queue, PD decode requests releasing their KV, HiSparse staging and parked uOCR windows.
- `is_fully_idle` reads the request part of each variant (default, health check, `ignore_waiting`) from the lists. Its result is unchanged: the default counts every list except the ones counted elsewhere or deliberately left out (running and launched prefills through the batches, dLLM through its staging check, held decode requests, parked uOCR windows through `blocks_flush`, finished deferred responses); the health check counts chunked, waiting and, unless paused, retracted decode requests, as before.

Behavior changes: the held-request abort, and the sampling-mask check covering more lists.

## Test plan
- A held-request abort during a retract pause finishes only the matching request, and resume enqueues the rest.
- The unit tests this PR touches pass locally with `SGLANG_IS_IN_CI=1`, apart from failures main has too.

title: [Fix] scheduler: Tell a step's middle chunk from the batch's chunked request, not a per-request counter
author: hnyls2002
body:
Facts about work in flight now come from what each step recorded when it was built or launched, instead of a per-request counter or a batch snapshot. This fixes a miscount of chunked prefill on main.

## The fix
`Req.inflight_middle_chunks` was raised whenever a chunked request existed after an admission pass that admitted something, even when the chunked request got no chunk in that pass. Under the hybrid-SWA joint prefill budget, a chunk whose remaining prompt does not fit with its new-token headroom is parked, while a smaller waiting request can still be admitted in the same pass. The counter then never came back down, and the request's final chunk was processed as a middle chunk: its first token was not committed (PD prefill: it was requeued as if it had yielded).

The same state made `contains_last_prefill_chunk` False for a batch whose only row ran a final prefill, so pipeline parallelism with `SGLANG_PP_SKIP_PURE_CHUNKED_OUTPUT_COMM` skipped its output exchange.

A pause that retracts under pipeline parallelism reset the counter while other micro-batches still carried the request, so their results could be labelled wrongly too; each step's own record labels it by itself.

## Changes
- Result processing (prefill, embedding, PD prefill, the pipeline-parallel output check, the grammar skip) asks whether a row is its batch's `chunked_req`, which the batch already records at build: the request that runs a chunk in this batch and is still chunked after it. A parked request is named there too but is not a row, so it is never asked about. `copy()` now carries `chunked_req`, since overlap processes the copy. The counter, its resets and the never-read dLLM increments are removed.
- `contains_last_prefill_chunk` counts the chunked request only when it is admitted in this pass.
- A PD optimistic request that yields the chunked slot is requeued once no step of it is in flight (`Req.inflight_steps`): at once at the yield, otherwise when its last step in flight is processed. This replaces the overlap flag and the `extend_end` inference; both rules agree wherever the yield can happen (optimistic prefill is off with pipeline parallelism, and a request otherwise has at most one step in flight).
- `_reqs_finishing_inflight` finds running requests whose queued result finishes them by `inflight_steps > 0` instead of reading the queued batch copy, and drops the one-batch assert. Same result: only the overlap loop enables it, and there the queued step is the only step in flight.

Behavior changes: only the parked-chunk and pipeline-parallel retract states above.

## Test plan
- `test_chunked_prefill_does_not_yield_for_decode_admission` covers a yield with and without a step in flight.
- The unit tests under `test/registered/unit/managers/`, `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/` and `test/registered/unit/dllm/` pass locally with `SGLANG_IS_IN_CI=1`, apart from failures main has too.

title: [Fix] hisparse: Release HiSparse rows on the KV checksum mismatch and chunked abort exits
author: hnyls2002
body:
Two exits free a request's KV with `release_kv_cache` without releasing its HiSparse state first, so the rows leak. Both now call `hisparse_coordinator.request_finished` before the KV free, under the same `enable_hisparse` guard as the other exits.

- PD decode KV checksum mismatch (`_handle_kv_checksum_mismatch`): the transfer has already admitted the request into HiSparse, so its host pages and device buffer were never returned.
- Chunked prefill abort (`process_pending_chunked_abort`): a request aborted between chunks holds only the spec scratch row its extend allocated; `request_finished` frees exactly that (its no-device-buffer branch), and the prefill KV is still freed by `release_kv_cache`.

No change without `--enable-hisparse`. No stream wait is added or moved; `request_finished` keeps its own wait on the forward stream, as at the other exits.

## Test plan
- One unit test per exit checks that the HiSparse release runs, and runs before the KV free; both fail without the fix.
- `/rerun-test` on this head:
  - `test_hisparse_unit.py` (1-gpu-5090): passed, [run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41746839763)
  - `test_disaggregation_hisparse.py` (8-gpu-h200, PD + HiSparse, DeepSeek-V4-Flash): passed, [run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41746854792)
  - `test_dsa_glm52_hisparse.py` (8-gpu-b200, HiSparse + speculative decoding): passed, [run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41746870316)
  - `test_kv_checksum.py` (1-gpu-h100): queued, [run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41746823280)
- The leaks are found by reading the exits and confirmed by the unit tests; an end-to-end reproduction on a server is in progress.

title: [Fix] parser: Accept whole-number floats for integer tool arguments
author: yonigozlan
body:
When tool schemas are passed to the response parser, an `integer` argument written as a whole-number float like `"3.0"` is now cast to `3` instead of being left as the raw string.

- JSON Schema (draft 6 onward, including 2020-12) defines `integer` as any number with a zero fractional part, so `3.0` is a valid `integer` value. `jsonschema` (Draft 7 and 2020-12 validators) and Pydantic v2 both accept it, and Pydantic returns `3`.
- Models do sometimes write integer arguments this way, and the tool then receives a string where its schema declares an integer.
- Values with a fractional part (`"3.5"`), `inf` and `NaN` still fail the `integer` cast, so they fall through to the next declared type or stay raw, as before.
- Adds a unit test next to the existing argument coercion tests.
- Same change as in Transformers: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49547.

title: [Fix] [AMD] diffusion: Prevent ComponentResidencyError after compile warmup
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

**What goes wrong**
On gfx1250, the first real request after torch.compile warmup raises ComponentResidencyError for transformer_2 on Wan 2.2 A14B. That request always calls disable_offload(), which sets manager.enabled to false. The user passed --dit-layerwise-offload, so the residency plan for transformer_2 is still layerwise offload, and preparing that component fails the check.

**Where it shows up**
The disable_offload() call is shared, so any device that compiles with explicit layerwise offload can hit it. gfx1250, and any machine where both DiTs still fit, keeps the weights resident. Putting them back after the compile window matches that plan, so there is no residency error. It shows up on the low-memory Wan 2.2 A14B path, including the gfx1250 multi-GPU run: visible memory is not enough for both DiTs, so layerwise offload has to stay on after compile. The cleanup path treats that the same as a temporary compile window.

**How to fix**
Call disable_offload() only when the user did not ask for layerwise offload, so a compile-only window still restores GPU residency and an explicit request stays enabled.

## Reproduction

This Wan 2.2 A14B config is the low-memory run that raised `ComponentResidencyError` for `transformer_2`. `offload_during_compile` is left at its default, `true`.

```bash
sglang generate \
  --model-path /mnt/raid/models/Wan2.2-T2V-A14B-Diffusers/ \
  --prompt "A cat and a dog baking a cake together in a kitchen." \
  --height 720 --width 1280 \
  --num-inference-steps 8 \
  --num-frames 193 \
  --seed 42 \
  --num-gpus 2 \
  --enable-cfg-parallel \
  --performance-mode auto \
  --dit-layerwise-offload true \
  --enable-torch-compile true \
  --warmup-mode server \
  --attention-backend aiter
```

## Modifications

- `DenoisingStage._explicit_dit_layerwise_offload()` is true when `dit_layerwise_offload` is set or `is_dit_layerwise_offload_selected` is true.
- `_offload_for_torch_compile_warmup` calls `disable_offload()` only when that helper is false. An explicit layerwise request stays enabled. A compile-only window still restores GPU residency.
- Unit tests cover both cases: an explicit request does not call `disable_offload()`, and a compile-only window still does.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A - this change does not affect model outputs. It only decides whether compile warmup is allowed to turn layerwise offload back off.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

N/A - this change does not affect inference speed. The failing path raised `ComponentResidencyError` before a timed request.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Fix] [AMD] kda: Match the fused verify Q/K norm to its reference kernel
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
#42486 switched the default Q/K L2 norm in `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update` to "compute `1 / sqrt(...)`, then multiply", but `fused_kda_conv_recurrent_verify` still computes `b_q / sqrt(...)`. `x / y` and `x * (1 / y)` round differently, so the fused verify kernel stopped matching its reference bit for bit, and the ROCm-only `test_glm_fp32_weights_bit_exact_on_rocm[8,9]` fails on MI35x:

```
assert torch.equal(ic_fus[valid], ic_ref[valid])
AssertionError: assert False
```

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38317177892/job/115041491933

The test's `_run_reference` is `causal_conv1d_update` + `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update`, so this switches the fused kernel to the same reciprocal form, with the same order of operations. The case only runs on ROCm, which is why #42486's validation reports "2 ROCm-only cases skipped".

The other KDA failure on ROCm (`TestKDAVerifyDecodeParity`) has an unrelated cause and is fixed separately in #44089.

## Notes for the reviewer

This changes the fused verify kernel's numerics on every platform, not just ROCm, by moving it onto the form its reference already uses. `fused_recurrent.py`, `gdn_replayssm_spec_{decode,fold}.py` and `kda_replayssm_spec_decode.py` still divide. I left them alone because no test compares them bit for bit against `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update`.

## Test plan

Locally on MI355X (gfx950), `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm10-mi35x-20261007`:

- [x] `test_glm_fp32_weights_bit_exact_on_rocm`: 2 failed → 2 passed
- [x] Full `test_fused_kda_conv_recurrent_verify.py`: 25 passed, 1 skipped (CUDA green contexts)

CI, `test_fused_kda_conv_recurrent_verify.py`:

- [x] MI35x, `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` part 0, the partition that failed on it before: passed on the [current head](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38519810686/job/115714219438) and [before the main merge](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38355361655/job/115164272858)
- [x] NVIDIA, `jit-kernel-unit-test-1-gpu-large`: passed on the [current head](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38519810721/job/115706908811) and [before the main merge](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38355361603/job/115157428852). This is the change in the pair that affects NVIDIA

## Remaining red checks

- `stage-b-test-1-gpu-large-amd` part 2 fails `TestKDAVerifyDecodeParity.test_bf16_state_verify_matches_single_token_launches` ([log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38519810686/job/115714219452)). That is the other half of the KDA ROCm fix, in #44089.
- CUDA base-b stops at `vlm/test_unlimited_ocr_server.py`, which can't load `baidu/Unlimited-OCR` without `trust_remote_code` ([log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38519810721/job/115719715621)). The other base-b partitions fast-fail behind it, and it fails the same way on #44089.

title: [Fix] chat-template: Pass return_dict=False to apply_chat_template(tokenize=True) for transformers 5
author: zijiexia
body:
## Motivation

transformers 5 returns a `BatchEncoding` from `apply_chat_template(..., tokenize=True)` unless `return_dict=False` is passed (`return_dict: bool = True` in 5.12.1, flipped to `False` only when `tokenize=False`). `len()`, `list()` and iteration on that object act on its two keys, not on the token ids. #43929 reports this for the `openai` bench loader (fix in #34511); the same call pattern exists at four more sites, none covered by a test. Each one was reproduced against transformers 5.12.1:

| Site | Observed on current main |
|---|---|
| `benchmark/datasets/speed_bench.py` | every row records `prompt_len == 2` (`decode()` accepts the dict, so the `except` fallback is never taken) |
| `entrypoints/openai/chat_encoding.py` (`encode_simple_chat`, HF-template branch) | `one_batch_server --apply-chat-template` sends `['input_ids', 'attention_mask']` as the prompt |
| `entrypoints/ollama/serving.py` (`/api/chat`) | the dict is passed as `GenerateReqInput.input_ids` |
| `multimodal/processors/voxtral.py` | with the real Voxtral tokenizer (`MistralCommonBackend`), `_build_input_ids_with_audio` raises `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'dict' and 'list'` |

## Modifications

- Pass `return_dict=False` at the four sites, the convention the other loaders and the server chat endpoint already use (#13229). It is a no-op on transformers 4.
- `test_speed_bench_sampler`: replace `prompt_len > 0` (which 2 satisfies) with the templated token count of the source prompts.
- New CPU tests, each failing on the old code: `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_chat_template_token_ids.py` (`encode_simple_chat` and the Ollama chat route, with a tiny word-level tokenizer carrying a chat template) and `test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_voxtral_processor.py` (audio tokens spliced after the last `[INST]`).

`openai_dataset.py` is intentionally left to #34511. `cosmos3.py` already handles both return types.
