title: [Fix] openai: Validate sampling bounds and preserve chat output limits
author: TheDuyIT
body:
## Motivation

Several invalid sampling values pass request parsing and only fail later, in serving or in the scheduler. Chat output-limit handling also used `max_completion_tokens or max_tokens`, so an explicit `0` fell back to the legacy limit.

Observed on a live server (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, vocab size 151936):

- A huge `n` is rejected only after the request has been expanded `n` times: `/generate` with `n=3,000,000` took ~113 s and grew server memory by ~18 GB before returning 400. On `main`, `n=300,000` did not complete within 15 minutes and server memory passed 90 GB. `n=0` was not rejected with a clear message.
- `top_logprobs` above the vocab size (for example 200000) kills the server, because `torch.topk` fails past the vocab size. A list or negative `top_logprobs_num` garbles a batch. A request with logprobs off can crash it too: its count is not checked, but the scheduler takes `topk` over every request's count when any request in the same prefill batch wants logprobs.
- A large `logit_bias` overflows to `inf` in the float32 bias tensor, or after the sampler divides by a temperature below 1, and NaNs the softmax. A sampled request with a `1e39` bias, or `3e38` at `temperature=0.5`, returns garbage tokens (`[0, 0, 0, 0]`) and, with `top_p`, kills the scheduler.
- A stop id outside the vocab (for example `-1` or `999999`) kills the server with a CUDA device-side assert once the `min_new_tokens` penalizer runs. The penalizer covers the whole batch when any request sets `min_new_tokens`, so the stop id and the `min_new_tokens` can come from different requests. With beam search, a stop id from `2**63` to `2**64 - 1` fails the scheduler's int64 tensor build and kills the server.
- An explicit `max_completion_tokens=0` is ignored.

## Modifications

- `n` is validated by one function, `sampling_params.validate_n`. It requires an `int` (`bool` rejected) of at least 1, at most `SGLANG_MAX_BATCH_REQS_PER_HTTP_REQ` (default 4096, the limit the Rust server already applies to `n`). A negative value disables the upper bound, as in the Rust server. `GenerateReqInput._handle_parallel_sampling` calls it before any input is multiplied by `n`, for dict and list `sampling_params`, and `SamplingParams.verify` calls it as a backstop.
- The chat and completions request models keep OpenAI's limit, `OPENAI_MAX_N = 128` (`protocol.py`). OpenAI requests then also pass `validate_n`, so their effective limit is the smaller of the two.
- `top_logprobs_num` must be an integer in `[0, vocab_size]` when logprobs are requested (checked next to `token_ids_logprob` in `tokenizer_manager`). When logprobs are off the count is not checked and is forwarded to the scheduler as `0`, so it cannot reach a shared `topk`.
- `SamplingParams.verify` validates `logit_bias` values (numeric, finite, `|bias| <= 1e30`). The sampler divides by a temperature of at least `1e-6`, so this bound keeps the float32 bias finite.
- The `min_new_tokens` penalizer and beam search drop stop ids outside `[0, vocab_size)` before building their tensors. Such ids can never be sampled, so they are accepted and never match, as before, and no longer crash the server.
- Chat `top_logprobs` and `temperature` reject negative values, and `temperature` rejects `inf`/`nan`.
- `ChatCompletionRequest.effective_max_tokens` gives `max_completion_tokens` precedence, including an explicit `0`. Chat conversion and the context-length check both use it. `max_tokens` and `max_completion_tokens` must be non-negative and are not booleans (lax integer parsing would read `false`/`true` as a 0- or 1-token limit).

### Deliberately not enforced

OpenAI documents `temperature` in 0-2, `top_logprobs` <= 20, `logit_bias` values in [-100, 100], and `top_logprobs` only with `logprobs=true`. SGLang does not enforce these. The engine applies those values correctly (`temperature=3` flattens the sampled distribution, `top_logprobs=50` returns 50 entries, a `-1e4` bias suppresses the token) and existing clients rely on that, so rejecting them would only break working requests. `ChatCompletionRequest` carries a comment saying so. Happy to revisit if maintainers prefer strict OpenAI parity on the OpenAI routes.

### Behavior changes

| Request | Before | After | Routes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_completion_tokens=0` | runs with the default limit | 0 tokens, `finish_reason=length` | chat |
| `max_tokens=5, max_completion_tokens=0` | 5 tokens | 0 tokens | chat |
| `max_tokens=-1, max_completion_tokens=1` | 200, 1 token | 400 | chat |
| `max_tokens` or `max_completion_tokens` set to `true`/`false` | read as a 1- or 0-token limit | 400 | chat |
| `n` > 128 | accepted (for example 256 choices) | 400 | chat, completions |
| `n` > `SGLANG_MAX_BATCH_REQS_PER_HTTP_REQ` (default 4096) | accepted, expanded `n` times | 400, checked before inputs are expanded | `/generate`, `Engine.generate` |
| `n=0` | no clear error | 400 with a clear message | chat, completions, `/generate` |
| `top_logprobs` / `top_logprobs_num` > vocab size, negative, or non-integer, with logprobs requested | scheduler crash or garbled batch | 400 | chat, `/generate` |
| `top_logprobs` / `top_logprobs_num` > vocab size with logprobs off, in a prefill batch with a logprob request | scheduler crash | count ignored, no crash | chat, `/generate` |
| `logit_bias` with `\|bias\| > 1e30` | accepted; garbage output or scheduler crash when sampling | 400 | all |
| `logit_bias` non-numeric or non-finite value | rejected only by the request parser where one applies | 400 from `SamplingParams.verify` | native `/generate`, completions |
| `stop_token_ids` outside `[0, vocab_size)` | ignored, but the server crashes when the batch uses `min_new_tokens` (or beam search gets an id from `2**63` to `2**64 - 1`) | ignored, no crash | all |

Notes:

- A single negative `max_tokens` or `max_completion_tokens` already returned 400. Only the combined case above changes.
- `max_tokens=0` alone already produced an empty completion. Chat now accepts `0` for both fields, while `/v1/completions` and the Anthropic route still require `> 0`.
- The same filter covers stop IDs supplied by the model (the `generation_config` EOS, tokenizer additional stop IDs).
- Native `n` from 129 to 4096 behaves as before. Raise or disable the limit with `SGLANG_MAX_BATCH_REQS_PER_HTTP_REQ`.

### Known limits (not in this PR)

- The opt-in Rust HTTP server (`SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1`, `rust/sglang-server`) does not go through `tokenizer_manager`, so these admission checks do not apply there. The stop-id filters run in the scheduler, so they cover it too. It reads the same `SGLANG_MAX_BATCH_REQS_PER_HTTP_REQ` limit for `n` and rejects `max_tokens=0`. Mirroring the other checks in Rust is a separate change.
- `batch_size * n` is still unbounded, and `max_tokens` / `max_completion_tokens` have no upper bound.
- Zero-length generation with speculative decoding enabled is not covered by tests. In-tree senders (`lang/ir.py`, `benchmark/serving.py`) only send these fields with real values.

## Accuracy Tests

No model forward or kernel change. Request-level checks on a live server (single H200, Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, `--sampling-backend pytorch`), against `main` at e109bc1832 and this branch (stop-id rows re-run on 2026-10-29 against `main` f59cc7e45f, the main merged into this branch):

| Request | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `/generate` `n=300000` (main) / `n=3000000` (PR) | no reply, server killed | 400 in ~3 ms, server healthy |
| chat `top_logprobs=200000` with `logprobs=true` | server dies | 400, server healthy |
| `top_logprobs_num=10000000` with logprobs off, in one prefill batch with a logprob request (`/generate` and chat) | server dies (`selected index k out of range`; measured on this branch before the fix, 46f3d08505, which forwarded the count unchanged like `main`) | 200, server healthy |
| `stop_token_ids=[-1]` with `min_new_tokens=2` | server dies | 200, id ignored, server healthy |
| `stop_token_ids=[999999]` sent while another request with `min_new_tokens=2` is decoding | both requests lost, server dies | both 200, outputs unchanged, server healthy |
| beam search (`beam_width=2`) with `stop_token_ids=[2**63]` | server dies (`Overflow when unpacking long long`) | 200, same output as without the id, server healthy |
| `logit_bias` `1e39` (sampled) | garbage output `[0, 0, 0, 0]` | 400 |
| `logit_bias` `3e38` at `temperature=0.5` | garbage output | 400 |
| same, with `top_p=0.9` | server dies | 400 |
| chat `max_completion_tokens=0` | 45 tokens | 0 tokens |

Unchanged on both: `n=1, 3, 128` return the expected number of outputs; `temperature=3`, `top_logprobs=50` (with or without `logprobs`), and a large `logit_bias` on chat, completions and native all return 200; `logit_bias` of `+-1e30` at `temperature=0.0005` still works.

Reproduction (synthetic input only):

```bash
# huge n: rejected before the request is expanded
curl -s localhost:30000/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"text":"Hi","sampling_params":{"max_new_tokens":1,"n":3000000}}'

# top_logprobs above the vocab size
curl -s localhost:30000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"m","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hi"}],"max_tokens":2,"logprobs":true,"top_logprobs":200000}'

# stop id outside the vocab, with min_new_tokens: kills main, ignored here
curl -s localhost:30000/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"text":"Hi","sampling_params":{"max_new_tokens":8,"min_new_tokens":2,"stop_token_ids":[-1]}}'

# logit_bias beyond the float32-safe bound
curl -s localhost:30000/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"text":"Hello","sampling_params":{"max_new_tokens":4,"temperature":0.5,"logit_bias":{"0":3e38}}}'
```

Unit tests (CPU), on the current head (main d213124956 merged in):

- Touched suites pass: `test_io_struct` (67, 2 CUDA-only skips), `test_protocol` (48), `test_serving_decisions` (28), `test_serving_chat` (175), `test_serving_completions` (21), `test_sampling_params` (83), `test_sampling_mask_validation` (6), `test_tokenizer_manager_rid_cleanup` (49), `test_penaltylib` (42), `test_sampling_batch_info` (50), `test_beam_search_core` (11). One `test_serving_chat` subtest (Inkling streaming) needs the optional `tml-renderers` package and fails identically on `main` without it.
- Before main was merged in (base e109bc1832), the full `base-a-test-cpu` suite gave 806 of 887 files passing; the 81 failing files fail identically on plain `main` in the same environment (missing ffmpeg/torchcodec, prebuilt Rust extensions out of date, model-cache access). It has not been rerun since the merge.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. Admission-time validation, plus a host-side bounds filter when the `min_new_tokens` penalty or a beam group is built.

## Checklist

- [x] Format with pre-commit (`ruff`, `ruff-format`, `isort`)

title: [Fix] sgl-router: Send disagg_prefill_dp_rank to decode under --dp-aware
author: AMD-yanfeiwang
body:
## Motivation

With `--dp-aware` in PD mode, sgl-router pins the prefill DP rank but does not tell decode which rank that is. Decode needs it to set up its KV receiver. It can derive it from the bootstrap room only if prefill runs `--load-balance-method follow_bootstrap_room`; with any other method, decode asks prefill's bootstrap server, which learns the room only when prefill's scheduler picks the request up, so decode polls until then. Every decode handshake therefore waits on prefill's scheduler loop, and with the default `--optimistic-prefill-attempts 0`, prefill does not run a request until it sees decode ready. `sgl-model-gateway` and `mini_lb` already send `disagg_prefill_dp_rank` to decode.

## Modifications

- When `--dp-aware` pins the prefill rank, the decode body also carries it as `disagg_prefill_dp_rank`, for `/generate`, `/v1/completions`, `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/messages`. The prefill body is unchanged, and batch / `n > 1` requests, which leave the prefill rank to the engine, send none.
- README: DP-rank routing.

## Testing

- `dp_rank_routing::pd_generate_carries_each_rank_in_its_body`: decode's `disagg_prefill_dp_rank` equals prefill's `routed_dp_rank` (fails without this change). `pd_fan_out_leaves_the_prefill_rank_to_the_engine`: decode gets none.
- Passing: `cargo +nightly fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --release --workspace -- --skip parity_matrix`.

## Benchmark (MI355X)

DeepSeek-V4-Pro, 1 prefill + 1 decode engine with 8 DP-attention ranks each, AgentX trace replay with AIPerf (multi-turn agentic sessions, 96% prefix-cache hit), 1 h per concurrency, prefill `--optimistic-prefill-attempts 2`. Router `--policy sticky --routing-key-header X-SMG-Routing-Key --decode-policy power_of_two --dp-aware`, decode ranks round-robin (#43511), built at 1e86143bf0.

The runs predate this patch, so both arms use the same router binary and differ only in prefill's load-balance method:

- **before**: `round_robin`, so decode looks every room up, as on main today;
- **after**: `follow_bootstrap_room`, so decode computes the rank from the room. That is the information this PR sends, so decode's handshake is the same.

Handshake, mean over the hour (before → after):

| conc | decode handshake (ms) | prefill bootstrap (ms) | decode prealloc queue |
|---|---|---|---|
| 192 | 595 → 0 | 1619 → 49 | 3.2 → 0 |
| 256 | 613 → 0 | 1642 → 56 | 4.3 → 0 |
| 384 | 682 → 0 | 1555 → 53 | 6.1 → 0 |
| 512 | 749 → 0 | 1458 → 63 | 6.9 → 0 |

The first two columns are each engine's `kv_transfer_bootstrap_ms`: until decode's receiver is ready, and until prefill sees it ready. The prealloc queue is decode's `#prealloc-req`, summed over its 8 ranks. For reference, `sgl-model-gateway` on the same engines, which sends the rank like this PR, measured 0 ms, 30–34 ms and 0 at every concurrency. With least-in-flight decode ranks (main's default), decode's handshake went from 587–723 ms to 0.

End to end, AIPerf (before → after):

| conc | output tok/s/GPU | TTFT p50 (s) | TTFT p90 (s) | TPOT p50 (ms) | TPOT p90 (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 192 | 369.5 → 369.9 | 3.26 → 3.38 | 10.68 → 10.54 | 14.59 → 14.61 | 16.31 → 16.22 |
| 256 | 441.6 → 438.2 | 3.71 → 3.76 | 13.70 → 13.90 | 16.98 → 16.93 | 18.53 → 18.45 |
| 384 | 562.6 → 561.4 | 7.02 → 7.59 | 30.01 → 31.01 | 19.98 → 19.80 | 22.85 → 22.45 |
| 512 | 577.0 → 599.8 | 19.54 → 16.84 | 64.17 → 57.90 | 21.24 → 23.13 | 24.47 → 25.50 |

- Decode's receiver is ready when its request arrives, so prefill sees the handshake done about as fast as with the gateway, and decode's prealloc queue and bootstrap-server lookups are gone.
- At 192–384, throughput and latency stayed within run-to-run noise (TTFT p50 at 384 ranges 8.07–9.32 s across four gateway runs that differ only in decode policy). In these runs `--optimistic-prefill-attempts 2` let prefill start requests before decode was ready, which kept the late handshake off the critical path. With the default of 0, prefill holds each request until it sees decode ready, which took about 1.5 s here instead of about 50 ms; that case was not measured.
- At 512, the arms differ in both directions because prefill ranks are pinned by a hash of the benchmark's routing keys, which are random per run. The before run had the most uneven prefill split of six c512 runs.

title: [Fix] sgl-router: Resend on a closed pooled connection; add --disable-circuit-breaker
author: AMD-yanfeiwang
body:
## Motivation

With one prefill and one decode worker, sgl-router fails a few requests per hour:

- SGLang closes idle keep-alive connections after 5 s, while sgl-router reuses them for up to 90 s. A request sent as the engine closes one fails before any response; with one worker per role, neither hyper nor `--retry-max-attempts` resends it, so the client gets a 502.
- Three such resets open the worker's circuit breaker, which then rejects that role's requests (502/503) while the worker is serving. It cannot be turned off, although `--cb-threshold` is documented as enabling it.

## Modifications

- Idle pooled connections expire after 3 s, and an HTTP/1.1 send that fails with a reset, broken pipe or EOF before any response is resent once to the same worker. The engine never read it, so it cannot run twice; only a failed resend reaches the breaker.
- The breaker stays on by default: under `--worker-urls` it is the only thing that takes a dead worker out of routing. New `--disable-circuit-breaker` turns it off, and `--cb-cool-down-secs` no longer requires `--cb-threshold`.
- A worker without a breaker config gets `CircuitBreaker::disabled()`, which ignores failures and reports closed; tests that rely on a breaker now configure one.
- `hyper` becomes a direct dependency (`Cargo.lock` unchanged); docs are in `REFERENCE.md`.

## Testing

- New `proxy::tests::closed_connection_is_retried_once`, against a raw HTTP/1.1 worker: a reset or EOF on the first connection is resent and returns 200 (502 without this change); a worker that closes every connection returns 502 after exactly two; one that never answers returns 504 after one.
- New `workers::registry::tests::breaker_without_config_never_opens`: a worker added without a breaker config stays routable after 10 failures (fails without this change).
- New `config::cli` tests: the breaker is on by default, and `--disable-circuit-breaker` turns it off and rejects the tuning flags.
- Passing: `cargo +nightly fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --release --workspace -- --skip parity_matrix`.

## Benchmark (MI355X)

Same setup as #44072: DeepSeek-V4-Pro, 1 prefill + 1 decode engine with 8 DP-attention ranks each, AgentX trace replay with AIPerf, 1 h per concurrency, sgl-router built at 1e86143bf0, no `--cb-threshold`.

In the concurrency-256 run, three sends to the only prefill worker failed with `Connection reset by peer` within 0.2 ms (the keep-alive race fixed here). That opened the worker's default breaker, and the router rejected three more requests before an in-flight request to the worker succeeded and closed it:

| status | router error | cause |
|---|---|---|
| 502 | `worker circuit breaker open` | breaker |
| 503 | `breaker_open` | breaker |
| 503 | `no_prefill_workers_available` | breaker: no routable prefill worker |

- These three were 30% of the run's 10 failed requests; the other seven were the resets themselves.
- At this concurrency an in-flight success closed the breaker within milliseconds. With few requests in flight nothing closes it early, so every request for that role would get 503 for up to the 30 s cool-down (not measured).
- The reruns used `--cb-threshold 1000000` (equivalent to `--disable-circuit-breaker`) with `SGLANG_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE=300` on the engines, which removes the race from the engine side, and had no errors in 8 runs (c192–c512, two decode policies); before, every run hit the race (2–11 failed requests per hour, or an aborted warmup). The `sgl-model-gateway` arms of the same benchmark run with `--disable-circuit-breaker`.

title: [Fix] PD: Skip the cached-prefix early send in batches that start a HiCache load-back
author: mattteochen
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #44070. On a PD prefill server with HiCache, a request re-matched after another request's load-back in the same batch build counts the not-yet-loaded pages as device prefix. `maybe_send_cached_prefix_chunk` then hands those pages to the KV transfer before the H2D copy writes them, so decode silently gets stale KV.

## Modifications

- `Scheduler.run_batch`: if this batch's build submitted a load-back (`batch.hicache_consumer_index >= 0`), skip the early send for its requests. The post-forward send covers the range after the forward has waited for every load layer.
- `maybe_send_cached_prefix_chunk`: new `allow_send` argument. It returns before sending, after the staging snapshot.
- Unit test: no early send when the batch started a load-back; the early send still happens when it didn't.

## Accuracy Tests

The #44070 repro (1P1D, NIXL, HiCache `write_back`, `--disaggregation-enable-kv-checksum` on both roles) on the 2026-10-13 SGLang nightly image, with only this PR's two source files overlaid. The image's copies of those files are identical to this PR's base.

| `--hicache-io-backend` | Trials | KV checksum mismatches, before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| `direct` | 30 | 29 | **0** |
| `kernel` | 30 | not run | **0** |

With the fix, both concurrent requests' greedy outputs match a fresh run (30/30 each). Batches without a load-back still early-send (every device-hit request did).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Batches whose build starts a load-back lose the early-send overlap: their KV goes out after the forward. In the repro this was about 54 ms later for a 100K-token prefix. Other batches are unchanged.

Follow-up: keep the overlap by handing the load's completion event to the sender and waiting on it before the read. That needs every connector to honor a wait event; see #43299 for NIXL.

title: [Fix] [AMD] kda: Reject match_cutedsl_decode on ROCm and skip its parity tests
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
`match_cutedsl_decode` (#42251) reproduces FlashInfer's CuTe DSL decode kernel, including PTX `ex2.approx` / `lg2.approx` emitted through `inline_asm_elementwise` with `"=f,f"` constraints. AMDGCN rejects that asm (`error: could not allocate output register for constraint 'f'`), but the launch still runs and returns wrong values. So on ROCm both `TestKDAVerifyDecodeParity` tests that set `match_decode=True` fail. CI shows only the first because the suite stops early:

```
FAIL: test_bf16_state_verify_matches_single_token_launches (head_dim=128)
AssertionError: False is not true
```

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38317177892/job/115041491883

No production caller sets `match_cutedsl_decode`; the parity test is its only user. So the wrapper now raises `NotImplementedError` on ROCm instead of returning wrong values. The two parity tests skip on ROCm, and a ROCm-only test checks that the error is raised. The default-path test in the same class keeps running on ROCm.

Everything here is gated on `_is_hip`, so NVIDIA behaviour is unchanged.

The other KDA failure on ROCm (`test_glm_fp32_weights_bit_exact_on_rocm`) has an unrelated cause and is fixed separately in #43991.

title: [Fix] wan-animate-2: Size the in-context slot from both input grids
author: ankitdhall
body:
## Motivation

`POST /v1/videos` on Wan-Animate-2 at `size=720x1280` with a reference image and a driving video of slightly different aspect ratios (1072x592 and 538x304) fails in the first DiT forward of the first clip, on both checkpoints:

```
RuntimeError: The expanded size of the tensor (3520) must match the existing size (3555) at non-singleton dimension 2
```

**How the inputs are sized.** The requested `size` is a pixel-area budget, not an output resolution. `resize_by_area` fits the reference image and the driving video to that area independently, each at its own aspect ratio, with both sides floored to a multiple of 16. At 720x1280 the two inputs land on different grids:

| Input | Aspect | Canvas | Latent grid | Tokens per frame |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: |
| Reference image, drives the output | 1.811 | 1280x704 | 80x44 | 3520 |
| Driving video | 1.770 | 1264x720 | 79x45 | 3555 |

The video grid is one latent row taller and one column narrower, and holds 35 more tokens.

**Where it breaks.** The in-context attention lays the generated frames and the reference-video frames side by side in one sequence, with one fixed-size slot per frame. `_InContextLayout` sized every slot from the generation grid alone (3520 here), so the copy that lays each reference-video frame into its slot was asked to place 3555 tokens into 3520 positions. Which input ends up with the larger grid depends on the fractional parts the floor to 16 discards, not on which aspect ratio is larger, so other budgets fail for other input pairs (576x1024 with the same inputs: 2240 against 2268).

## Modifications

`_InContextLayout.max_tokens_per_frame` is now `max(generation tokens per frame, reference-video tokens per frame)`. Everything downstream already keys on that one value: the generation and reference K/V copies, `block_mask_fn`, `_make_score_mod` (the biased keys are still generation frame 1) and the block-mask cache key, so nothing else changes. The official implementation sizes the slot from the budget itself (`width * height // 256`, 3600 here) and so holds either grid; `max(...)` is the tighter bound and needs nothing new passed into the layout.

Three CPU unit tests: the layout slot for the measured grids, with the mirrored and equal-grid cases unchanged; a 5-token reference frame against a 4-token generation frame through `_in_context_attention`, which raises on main; and `resize_by_area` on the measured inputs at 720x1280, giving the two grids and a slot equal to the larger.

No cookbook change here: the output-resolution paragraph is reworded to describe the per-input fit in the distilled Wan-Animate-2 PR (#44085), which touches the same lines.

## Accuracy Tests

Bit-identical for every request that runs today: when the two grids agree, or the video's is the smaller, `max(...)` equals the previous value, so the layout, mask, score bias and every padded tensor are unchanged. The CI case (720x1280 image and 480x832 video at 576x1024: 2304 against 2268 tokens per frame) is in that set, so its pinned ground truth stays valid.

GPU check (one GPU, base checkpoint, 4 steps, `clip_len` 37, the 1072x592 / 538x304 pair): the 720x1280 request that fails on main with the error above completes with this change and returns 237 frames at 1280x704; the same request at the default 640x800 gives a byte-identical MP4 (same md5, per-frame PSNR inf) on main and with this change.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Fix] unified-memory: Avoid gather scratch during Mamba and Conv compaction
author: seokwoosong
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* __->__ #44097
* #39294 (merged)

CI is run only on the top PR, #44097, which contains both changes.

#39294 was squash-merged as `ee30dc4d40993045273f0a90260db7efa302c214`. This PR is now based directly on main and contains only the compaction commits.

Current head: `683cf507a5e16833fe815ec5691405b0e62b4ea7`.

## Motivation

Unified Mamba/Conv compaction uses a gathered state tensor when relocating slots, which can OOM precisely when the allocator is reclaiming memory.

Seokwoo Song's four compaction commits are preserved, rebased onto main after #39294 was squash-merged.

## Modifications

- Copy disjoint physical state envelopes directly with the existing `copy_pages` kernel, removing the main-state gather temporary.
- Preserve main's `move_physical_pages` entry point, which calls the optimized move implementation.
- Retain sibling-state copying and ordinary copy-on-write behavior.
- Cover Mamba and Conv-only pools, both growth directions, eager/urgent/opportunistic compaction, state payloads and mappings, CUDA stream ordering, and CUDA graph readback.

## Accuracy Tests

Pre-merge validation base: `ae28306a74fc9ba56daab9ccb06dcf45659f58af`. Both PRs replayed without conflicts, and all eight patches are unchanged by `git range-diff`. title: [Fix] [XPU] nightly: Fix rerank, zimage, flux2 and EAGLE parity
author: arathi-hlab
body:
## Motivation

Four tests fail in the Intel XPU nightly on `sglang-kernel-xpu==0.4.0`:

| Test | Suite | CI error |
|---|---|---|
| `test_xpu_rerank` (exit -9) | 1-GPU | `RuntimeError: store_cache only supports k/v dtype in {fp16, bf16, uint8}; got Float` |
| `test_xpu_zimage_turbo` (exit 1) | 1-GPU | `fixture 'perf_results' not found` |
| `test_spec_eagle_parity` (exit 1) | 1-GPU | `torch.OutOfMemoryError: XPU out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.25 GiB` |
| `test_xpu_flux2_dev` (exit 1) | 4-GPU | `fixture 'perf_results' not found` |

Seen in e.g. `nightly-xpu-kernel-wheel-1-gpu` [run 38281560127 / job 114919788483](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38281560127/job/114919788483) and the kernel-main [run 38299359135](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38299359135).

The workflow split that was originally in this PR moved to a separate PR.

## Modifications

- `test_xpu_rerank.py`: sgl-kernel-xpu 0.4.0 `store_cache` rejects fp32 K/V, and the bge-reranker-v2-m3 cross-encoder runs fp32. Per review, `memory_pool.py` is left unchanged because more XPU KV cache dtypes are being upstreamed. `TestXPUCrossEncoderRerank` is skipped (`@unittest.skip` with the error and a re-enable note) until then. `TestXPUDecoderRerank` (bf16) still runs.
- `test/registered/xpu/conftest.py` (new): re-export `perf_results` so `DiffusionServerBase`'s autouse fixture resolves, same as `test/registered/amd/conftest.py`.
- `test_xpu_zimage_turbo.py`, `test_xpu_flux2_dev.py`: pass `load_time_ms=diffusion_server.load_time_ms` to `_validate_and_record`; it became mandatory in #39206, so without it the tests fail with `Load duration missing or invalid: None` once the fixture resolves.
- `test_xpu_flux2_dev.py` + `perf_baselines/xpu_b60.json`: flux2 then fails with `Testcase 'flux2_dev_image_t2i' not found in .../xpu_b60.json`, because `_validate_and_record` requires a scenario and always applies the e2e/load guards even with `run_perf_check=False`. Added a `flux2_dev_image_t2i` scenario and set `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1` via `env_vars` on this case only, so its step timings record device time like the other `xpu_b60.json` scenarios. Values are the max over 3 local runs on 4x Arc Pro B70 (denoise spread <0.5%); `zimage_image_t2i` in the same file already serves the B70 nightly. The multimodal-gen XPU suite (`1-gpu-xpu`) does not run this case.
- `test_spec_eagle_parity.py` (`TestEagle3ParityXPU` only): `mem_fraction_static = 0.70`. XPU captures target-verify (2.78 GB), draft-decode (1.76 GB) and draft-extend full graphs; at 0.80 the 2.25 GiB draft-extend `attn_logits` buffer OOMs at capture, and at 0.75 capture succeeds but the first prefill hits `UR_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES`.

## Accuracy Tests

Reproduced locally on Arc Pro B70 with `intel/sglang-dev:latest-kernel-main` (sglang-kernel-xpu 0.4.0, torch 2.14.0+xpu); each test run separately (CI runs files serially):

title: [Fix] qwen3_coder: Preserve structured values in qwen3_coder mixed unions
author: rystewart-nvidia
body:
## Motivation

Closes #44120

When a tool parameter allows a string or an object, `qwen3_coder` treats the model's object JSON as a string. After one decode of `function.arguments`, callers get `{"location": "{\"city\": \"Paris\"}"}` instead of `{"location": {"city": "Paris"}}`. String/array unions have the same problem, including streamed responses.

This can affect any model using `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder`. The string result is schema-valid, but it loses the structured value emitted by the model.

Related work: [#30832](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30832) added nullable-array support, and [#36626](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36626) fixed top-level schema property lookup. This addresses a separate case: a known parameter whose own union allows both strings and structured values.

## Modifications

In the detector's existing string conversion branch, check `anyOf`/`oneOf` parameters for complete object or array JSON. Keep the decoded value only when it satisfies the parameter schema.

Plain strings, scalar unions, malformed JSON, values that do not match the schema, and unresolved references keep their existing behavior. Schema validation does not fetch external references.

This intentionally prefers an allowed object or array when mixed-union text could also be read as a string. String-only parameters still keep JSON-looking text as strings.

The change is limited to the Qwen3-Coder detector and its existing registered tests. The shared inference helper, other detector implementations, public APIs, and dependency lists are unchanged. `step3p5` and `nanbeige` also use this detector and receive the same behavior. Type arrays and root-level reference resolution are outside this fix.

## Accuracy Tests

Does not change kernel or affect model forward code, but does affect structured output correctness.

- Verified the regression on native v0.5.21 before the fix: 24 structured-value subtests failed at the expected assertions.
- With the fix on v0.5.21, all 20 Qwen3-Coder tests and 60 subtests pass. Coverage includes complete parsing, one- and seven-character streaming chunks, both union types and branch orders, objects/arrays, schema constraints, and string compatibility.
- Replayed six outputs captured from the live v0.5.21 Qwen3-Coder server through complete and streaming parsing. All three previously lost objects stay objects; the genuine date string and both object-only controls keep their values and types.
- A live patched v0.5.21 server using Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct (BF16, TP1, one B200) passed health, model listing, deterministic chat, and all 12 tool requests, including three streams. Object/array unions stay structured after one arguments decode; object-only, string-only JSON text, and numeric/string controls pass.
- Changed executable production lines have 100% coverage (11/11).

Validation used `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.21` (digest `sha256:b1259f3ea3275f66237c498ea388919729018bc9f01c3d638391e06e2cf3f469`). Baseline raw-output logging left conversion unchanged; the patched serving run installed only the exact candidate detector. The regression tests ran against the native runtime without adding compatibility modules.

The full original detector and relevant type-inference function are byte-identical to main (`7dc2930585782c09630d617a510bec08c1724845`), so I didn't run a separate test on main. 

These checks were only for parser correctness; no general model accuracy benchmark was run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speed benchmark was run. This adds JSON parsing for string-inferred `anyOf`/`oneOf` parameters, followed by schema validation when the decoded value is an object or array. Model execution and decoding kernels are unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit] (https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). All-files pre-commit passed
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). Extended the existing registered Qwen3-Coder test class.
- [x] (N/A) Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No documentation change included.

title: [Fix] DSv4.1: Fix BCG image handling and add multimodal bounded replay coverage
author: Oasis-Git
body:
[codex/claude generated]

## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4.1 multimodal prefill can produce incorrect results with breakable CUDA graphs (BCG). The eager model wrapper remaps image hash placeholders to model token IDs, but the captured transformer body kept reading the original IDs. Its Engram image-row mask was also omitted when capture used a dummy batch without multimodal inputs.

On four GB300 GPUs, the same 200 MMMU-Pro questions scored 76.5% with TP4+EP4 and 68.0% with BCG before this fix. BCG scored 78.0% after the fix; BCG with decoder bounded replay scored 78.5%.

## Modifications

- Refresh the captured body's static input IDs from the eager wrapper's prepared IDs, preserving the scheduler's original cache-key IDs.
- Capture the DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram image-token mask independently of dummy-batch multimodal metadata.
- Add CPU regressions for prepared image IDs and image-row Engram masking; both reproduce failures before the fix.
- Replace MMLU with MMMU-Pro in the existing GB300 TP4+EP4 and DP4+EP4 DSPARK tests, and add TP4+EP4 with decoder SWA bounded replay inside BCG. Keep GSM8K and speculative acceptance checks in all three configurations.
- Use sgl-eval 0.1.3 with the V4.1 preset. MMMU-Pro uses 200 examples, a 32768-token output cap, and a 0.75 threshold; GSM8K retains its 0.95 threshold.

## Accuracy Tests

Local validation on four GB300 GPUs, using the same 200 MMMU-Pro questions, DSPARK block size 5, 64 client threads, 32 maximum running requests, memory fraction 0.7, and 8192-token prefill chunks:

| Configuration | MMMU-Pro accuracy | Truncation rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TP4+EP4, BCG disabled | 76.5% (153/200) | 4.0% |
| TP4+EP4 + BCG, before fix | 68.0% (136/200) | 6.0% |
| TP4+EP4 + BCG, after fix | 78.0% (156/200) | 4.5% |
| TP4+EP4 + BCG + decoder bounded replay, after fix | 78.5% (157/200) | 3.5% |

All four evaluations completed with zero request errors. Each is one run at temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, without a fixed sampling seed; these measurements are not a deterministic equivalence proof. Encoder bounded replay was disabled throughout. The first three configurations also disabled decoder bounded replay.

- 39 related unit tests and 45 subtests passed, including the new regressions and existing prefill-runner tests.
- Applicable pre-commit hooks passed.
- This validation used the PR base revision `961dd5f` plus the fix. GSM8K and DP4 were not rerun locally after the fix; CI validation of the updated head remains pending.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No controlled performance benchmark or profiling was performed.

title: [Fix] moe: gated NVFP4 MoE intermediate alignment for FlashInfer TRTLLM
author: Qiaolin-Yu
body: ## Summary Gated NVFP4 experts using FlashInfer TRTLLM currently round each intermediate partition to a multiple of 128 before the quantization method allocates weights. This unnecessarily expands a 192-wide partition to 256. The gated FP4 layout needs 64-aligned intermediate partitions because gate and up are combined. Let the NVFP4 method select alignment before allocating weights and scales: 64 for gated TRTLLM layout, 128 otherwise. Keep the existing generic TRTLLM alignment for other quantization methods and synchronize the runner configuration with the allocated dimensions. No new base-class API is introduced. ## Memory impact Measured on 4x B200 with a 48-layer, 512-expert gated NVFP4 MoE model at TP4 (rank-local intermediate 192), FlashInfer TRTLLM MoE, identical launch configuration and `mem_fraction_static` for both runs; only this PR's source differs. Per GPU (all four ranks identical): | | Before | After | Change | |---|---|---|---| | Target model weights after load | 29.14 GB | 22.86 GB | **-6.28 GB** | | `max_total_num_tokens` | 11,610,688 | 12,311,616 | **+700,928 (+6.0%)** | | Attention KV cache (K+V) | 66.44 GB | 70.44 GB | +4.00 GB | | Mamba cache slots | 2082 | 2203 | +121 (+5.8%) | The weight reduction matches the removed MoE padding (192 -> 256 per rank across 48 layers x 512 experts, 6.33 GiB). Total device usage at startup is unchanged; the freed memory goes to the KV and Mamba caches. ## Validation - B200: real checkpoint-shard loading, weight processing and TRTLLM forward against the existing independent dequantized reference at intermediate widths 160, 192, 256 and 1024. - New regression fails on the unchanged baseline for widths 160 and 192 (256 allocated instead of 192). - Constructor checks preserve 128 alignment for non-gated NVFP4, FP8 and unquantized TRTLLM paths. - All applicable pre-commit hooks pass (formatting, lint, AST, CI registration and secret checks). verified on AIME26, not affected Kernel time doesn't change before, after, --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #39313778552](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39313778552) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #39313778702](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39313778702) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #39313778587](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39313778587)

title: [Fix] offloader: Preserve cached weights during CPU offload
author: yao-matrix
body:
## Summary

Fix CPU-offload loading and cached-weight aliasing without changing graph or quantization defaults:

- Centralize GemmaRMSNorm's `weight + 1` refresh in `refresh_gemma_weight()`. Copy CPU parameter data directly into the existing device buffer and add in place, preserving its storage and avoiding a temporary device tensor. Both checkpoint loading and presharded rebinding use it.
- Match cached ordinary tensor attributes against parameter storage by `(device, untyped_storage().data_ptr())`, across the owner and its children. Apply this residency protection in OffloaderV1 and OffloaderV2, including V2 aliases held outside the selected submodule. Preserve the existing MLA protection.
- Share convolution-view rebuilding through `RadixLinearAttention.refresh_conv_weights()` in the presharded and IPC loaders.
- Move accelerator regressions to `test/registered/model_loading/test_cpu_offloader.py`, use `CustomTestCase`, and retain CUDA/XPU CI registration. Exercise real `ColumnParallelLinear`/`MergedColumnParallelLinear` layouts, renamed aliases, Gemma checkpoint/rebind paths, V2 whitelist selection, and both loaders' view rebuilding.

## Problem

CPU offload moves parameters to host memory while buffers can remain on the accelerator. GemmaRMSNorm's loader and reload helper currently add the CPU parameter directly into the accelerator `gemma_weight` buffer, causing a device mismatch during loading.

Separately, Qwen3.5 GDN constructs `attn.conv_weights` as an ordinary tensor view of `conv1d.weight`. `functional_call` substitutes registered parameters and buffers, but does not substitute that ordinary attribute. Offloading the parameter can therefore leave attention reading stale accelerator storage after checkpoint loading. The existing protection recognizes KDA's `qkv_conv1d` spelling but misses GDN's `conv1d`.

This can silently produce incorrect speech even when serving returns HTTP 200. In a small accelerator reproducer, GDN returned `[0, 0]` after weight updates when the expected forward output was `[6, 6]`. KDA's already-protected equivalent returned the expected result. After this fix, both pass and ordinary projection parameters still reside on CPU.

The shared loader/offloader fixes preserve CPU offload, quantization, and graph defaults.

## Verification

Tested source commit: `492280b22cccc1f6b75b8f3c5b6f06c64f504e54`, following the latest PR branch head `90758a60c383a47f6b8cdac30ac05d2577287ae3`.

On a physical Intel Arc Pro B60 with PyTorch `2.13.0+xpu`:

- `python test/registered/model_loading/test_cpu_offloader.py -v`: **5 tests passed**. Checks actual accelerator convolution outputs, CPU residency of unrelated weights, and correct Gemma buffer values with stable storage.
- The V2 regression exercises public module wrapping and actual parameter residency/loading, including a cached view outside the selected submodule. Runtime configuration, CUDA stream lookup, and CUDA memory telemetry are mocked; V2's CUDA stream transfers and prefetch are not exercised.
- Four regression-sensitivity checks passed: restoring name-based alias detection, removing V2 filtering, restoring the cross-device Gemma add, or disabling convolution refresh each makes its corresponding committed regression fail.
- Fresh loader-first import: passed.
- Pre-commit checks for all changed files, including registered-test validation: passed.

CUDA hardware was not available locally. The shared accelerator regressions remain registered for both CUDA and XPU CI.

### End-to-end speech checks

The earlier equivalent source fixes were exercised through SGLang-Omni's Drama 3 serving pipeline on patched SGLang v0.5.21 (`e00930c5489053f26d86b179cee0d087f846acbb`). These are prior serving results; the latest review changes were verified by the accelerator regressions above. 

Configuration: two Intel Arc Pro B60 cards (24 GB each), 28 GiB CPU offload, native BF16/FP8 engine weights, FP16 vocoder, seed 1234. Drama 3 checkpoint: `dd64a85cd82e9521f7202610ede97b367fc83946`; S2-Pro codec: `1de9996b6be38b745688de084d87a5633f714e4e`.

| Request | Engine execution | HTTP | ASR transcript |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hello, how are you? | Eager | 200 | Hello, how are you? |
| Hello, how are you? | Graph replay | 200 | Hello, how are you? |
| Get the trust fund to the bank early. | Graph replay, cookbook reference audio | 200 | Get the trust fund to the bank early. |

The graph-enabled checks were freshly run against the SGLang-Omni publication tree `09ede4d3c7ca5fd57d6633736d40e3a5069f8451`. Server logs confirm prefill and decode graph replay. Vocoder windows ran eagerly because of a separate XPU SDPA graph-capture restriction. ASR checks establish the recorded requests' speech content, not speaker identity or general model accuracy.

## Related PR

Prerequisite for the CPU-offloaded recipe in sgl-project/sglang-omni#2785.

title: [Fix] Work around a CPython fork deadlock in the CPU preprocess pool
author: hnyls2002
body:
- Forked `ProcessPoolExecutor` workers inherit the parent's `concurrent.futures.process._threads_wakeups`. Since Python 3.12.8 / 3.13.1 each `_ThreadWakeup` has a lock, and a worker's exit hook (`_python_exit`) takes the lock of every inherited wakeup. If a parent thread held one at fork time, the worker never exits and `shutdown(wait=True)` hangs.
- The multimodal CPU preprocess pool hits this after `_replace_broken_cpu_executor`: the replacement forks its worker while the broken pool's manager thread and the cleanup thread still take that pool's wakeup lock. `test_llava_processor_pool.py::test_replacement_pool_runs_after_real_worker_exit` hung until the 15-minute job timeout in `base-a-test-cpu` on #39730 and #43480 (Python 3.12.15).
- The pool now passes an `initializer` that clears the inherited wakeups in each worker; a worker has no executors of its own.
- This works around a CPython regression from python/cpython#125451 (the fix that added the lock), still present on CPython main; it relies on the private `_threads_wakeups`. Moving the pool off `fork` would avoid it too, at the cost of slower worker startup for everyone.

No behavior change otherwise.

Verification (Linux):
- A stdlib-only replay of the test, 16 processes x 300 rounds: hung in 16/16 on Python 3.12.14 and 0/16 on 3.12.3; with the initializer, 0/16 on 3.12.14. A stuck worker's stack ends in `_ThreadWakeup.wakeup` called from `_python_exit`.
- `test_llava_processor_pool.py` on Python 3.12.14, 400 runs each: main hung 6 times, this PR 0.

title: [Fix] Qwen3.8next: Stop retaining per-size PLE outputs in breakable prefill CUDA graphs
author: Qiaolin-Yu
body:
## Summary

During breakable prefill CUDA graph capture, `eager_on_graph` keeps a strong reference to each eager break's return value so replay can copy fresh output into it. That return value is allocated outside the graph pool, so a break that returns a newly allocated tensor keeps one buffer per captured size for the lifetime of the graphs.

`_breakable_ple_forward` returned a fresh `[num_tokens, hc_count * hidden_size]` tensor, so the PLE layer retained one such buffer for every prefill capture size. With the default prefill capture sizes up to 16384 tokens this adds up to several GiB per GPU, while only the largest size can ever be live.

Use the output-argument pattern already used by `breakable_unified_attention_with_output` and the DSA indexer: `_add_ple_embedding` allocates the output inside the captured segment, from the graph pool, and the eager break writes `residual + ple(...)` into it in place and returns nothing. Graph-pool memory is then reused across capture sizes, and the residual add no longer needs a second graph-pool tensor.

## Memory impact

Measured on 4x B200 with a Qwen4 PLE model at TP4 using breakable prefill CUDA graphs (74 capture sizes up to 16384 tokens), identical launch configuration for both runs; only this change differs. Per GPU (all four ranks consistent):

| | Before | After | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Target prefill CUDA graph capture | 14.59 GB | 8.42 GB | **-6.17 GB** |
| Device memory used after startup | 167,601 MiB | 161,549 MiB | **-5.91 GiB** |

The removed retention matches the PLE output size summed over all capture sizes (296,032 tokens x 20,480 B = 5.65 GiB). KV and Mamba cache sizes are unchanged because they are sized before graph capture; the freed memory is left free at startup.

## Validation

- Greedy generation (64 tokens) for prompts of 43, 395, 1931, 7051 and 16651 tokens, cache flushed before each request, with output logprobs, compared against three independent runs of the unchanged code.
  - 43, 395 and 1931 tokens: all 64 output tokens identical and logprob differences exactly 0 against every baseline run.
  - 7051 and 16651 tokens: the unchanged code already diverges between its own runs (first differing token 5-16, max logprob difference up to 0.66); this change stays within that range.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks pass.

title: [Fix] multimodal: Preserve caller hashes and offsets for precomputed inputs
author: michaelfeil
body:
## Motivation

Caller-provided `hash` and `offsets` on a `precomputed_embedding` input currently land in `model_specific_data`. The native item therefore has no hash or offsets, so SGLang rediscovers spans and hashes the feature instead of using the supplied identity.

Preserve those fields, matching the existing processor-output metadata handling. This is a small first step toward #44159.

## Modifications

Two production lines move `hash` and `offsets` into the existing `MultimodalDataItem` fields. Inputs without them retain the current defaults. The caller payload and embedding tensor are unchanged.

The hash uses SGLang's existing integer representation and is trusted as the precomputed item identity. Its hash-derived pad IDs participate in prefix-cache keys and downstream KV-event hashes. This is separate from the raw-media `content_hash` trust setting; no new SHA-string field or cache-key format is introduced.

## Accuracy Tests

Added a regression to the existing CPU-CI-registered `test_precomputed_embedding_validation.py` (`base-a-test-cpu`). One small regression exercises native item finalization and checks that the supplied hash and offsets survive.

Six isolated source-extracted CPU checks pass; the new regression fails against the pre-change source. Full-package execution is pending upstream CI: the local lightweight environment could not import the suite because it lacks `psutil`. Ruff formatting/import checks and whitespace checks pass.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No kernel/model-math changes; no model benchmark run.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code and check imports.
- [x] Extend an existing registered CPU-CI test module.
- [ ] Upstream CPU CI passes.

title: [Fix] dsa: Route mixed-chunk batches to the RAGGED top-k transform for bf16-only sparse prefill
author: yunyang1999
body:
## Motivation

With an FP8 KV cache, `--enable-mixed-chunk` kills the DSA backend on the first mixed batch when the prefill backend is `flashmla_sparse`, `flashmla_sparse_q8` or `triton_sparse_mla`. The root cause is one routing predicate: `get_topk_transform_method` returns `TopkTransformMethod.RAGGED` for `ForwardMode.EXTEND` only, and a mixed-chunk batch carries `ForwardMode.MIXED`. The rest of the stack already treats such a batch as an extend-shaped batch (its decode rows are one-token extends with a full prefix), which is exactly how the gap surfaces:

- The eager runner runs a mixed batch as EXTEND (`eager_runner.execute` rewrites the mode), so without a prefill CUDA graph the backend never sees MIXED and nothing fails.
- The prefill CUDA graph runner (breakable, the CUDA default) builds the attention metadata from the real MIXED batch and replays the EXTEND-captured graphs, whose in-graph ops see a static batch with mode EXTEND. The metadata is therefore prepared for PAGED and has no `topk_indices_offset`, while the in-graph indexer asks for the RAGGED transform:

  ```
  RuntimeError: RAGGED topk_transform requires topk_indices_offset; expected extend-without-speculative metadata.
  ```

- Runs that hand MIXED straight to `forward_extend` (context parallel, NPU) take the PAGED path and the bf16-only kernel receives the packed FP8 pool:

  ```
  RuntimeError: kv must have dtype torch::kBFloat16          # flashmla_sparse, flashmla_sparse_q8
  TypeError: sparse_mla_prefill needs a bf16 KV cache, got torch.float8_e4m3fn   # triton_sparse_mla
  ```

The gap was pointed out by @ch-wan in the review of #32779 as a pre-existing issue shared with `flashmla_sparse`; this PR fixes it for all three backends.

## Modifications

`get_topk_transform_method` routes `ForwardMode.MIXED` exactly like `ForwardMode.EXTEND` for these three prefill impls (an FP8 pool, or `flashmla_sparse_q8` with any pool since #41790), so the metadata the backend builds from a MIXED batch agrees with what the EXTEND-replaying graph ops, and the eager runner, expect. Nothing else changes: the extend branch of `init_forward_metadata` already builds `page_table_1_flattened` and `topk_indices_offset` for MIXED (it enters through `is_extend()`), and the indexer already runs its ragged top-k for MIXED (`is_extend_without_speculative()`), with the transform method as a parameter. FP8-native impls (`flashmla_kv`, `flashinfer_sparse_mla`, `trtllm`) and bf16 pools keep PAGED in both modes, which is why they never hit this. Born-fp8 q for `flashmla_sparse_q8` stays EXTEND-only; a MIXED batch reaches the q8 helper on the bf16-q hand-off, which casts. The q8 launch validator used to refuse `--enable-mixed-chunk` because a MIXED batch took PAGED; that refusal, its parameter and its test case are removed, and the `forward_extend` message for q8 now names the two shapes that remain unsupported (SPLIT_PREFILL, DLLM_EXTEND).

The alternative, building the replay metadata from the mode-rewritten static batch inside the prefill graph runner, would change every attention backend's replay contract to fix a predicate that only this backend has; the backend-local change keeps `get_topk_transform_method` consistent with the backend's own `is_extend()` branches.

Cost: a RAGGED mixed batch dequantizes the batch's whole ragged KV (`sum(seq_lens)` tokens) per layer, the same work a chunked EXTEND with prefixes already does, now including the decode rows' contexts. That is the price of running a bf16 kernel on an FP8 pool; `flashmla_kv` (main's default for FP8 KV on SM90) is unaffected. Numbers below.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test/registered/attention/unittests/dsa/test_dsa.py`: new `test_sparse_fp8_mixed_chunk_prefill_cases` runs a `ForwardMode.MIXED` FP8 case (one 4-token chunk plus two one-token rows, all with a 2048 prefix) through every prefill impl against the kit's bf16 reference. On the previous code `flashmla_sparse` fails with `kv must have dtype torch::kBFloat16` and `triton_sparse_mla` with the bf16 `TypeError`; `flashmla_kv` passes before and after (PAGED is correct for it); the bf16-only impls skip as before.
- `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_dsa_q8kv8_bf16_prefill_routing.py`: five MIXED rows in the shared `get_topk_transform_method` table (RAGGED for `flashmla_sparse` and `triton_sparse_mla` on an FP8 pool and for `flashmla_sparse_q8` on any pool; PAGED for `flashmla_sparse` on a bf16 pool and for `flashmla_kv`); the RAGGED rows are red on the previous code.
- End to end (on the tree of 2026-10-06, main `05340e9ecb` plus this change; the branch has since been merged with main and the unit tests re-run on it), SM90, GLM-5.2-FP8 real weights, TP8, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --enable-mixed-chunk`, default (breakable) prefill CUDA graph. Eight short natural prompts start decoding (96 tokens each) and a 12000-token prompt arrives 0.5 s later, so its three chunks are each merged with the eight decode rows. A probe in the server records what reaches `forward_extend`; the mixed batch is `extend_seq_lens = [4088, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1]` with prefixes `[4032, 30, 32, ...]`.

| tree | prefill backend | prefill graph | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | `flashmla_sparse` | breakable (default) | server dies on the first mixed batch: `RuntimeError: RAGGED topk_transform requires topk_indices_offset` |
| main | `flashmla_sparse`, chunk 1024 (fits the graph buckets) | breakable | same error |
| main | `flashmla_sparse` | disabled | runs: the eager runner runs the batch as EXTEND, so this path never failed |
| main | `flashmla_sparse_q8` | breakable | same error |
| this PR | `flashmla_sparse` | breakable | runs; mixed batch on RAGGED, kernel invoked |
| this PR | `triton_sparse_mla` | breakable | runs; mixed batch on RAGGED, kernel invoked |
| this PR | `flashmla_sparse` | disabled | runs (unchanged path) |
| this PR | `triton_sparse_mla` | disabled | runs (unchanged path) |
| this PR | `flashmla_sparse_q8` | breakable | runs (merged tree, launch guard removed); mixed batch on RAGGED, q8 kernel invoked |
| this PR | `flashmla_sparse`, chunk 1024 (fits the graph buckets) | breakable | runs |
| either | `flashmla_kv` (FP8-native control) | breakable | runs; mixed batch stays on PAGED |

<details>
<summary>How to reproduce (launch commands, client, probe)</summary>

Hardware: one SM90 node, 8 GPUs, TP8. Image: `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261006-f3fe7534` for the 2026-10-06 runs; the re-validation after merging main ran in `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261014-684fea8a` (sgl_kernel 0.4.9). Model: `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8`.

Server, one per row of the table (the pre-fix rows run main at `05340e9ecb`, the others this branch):

```bash
PYTHONPATH=<checkout>/python:<dir containing sitecustomize.py> \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --attention-backend dsa \
  --dsa-prefill-backend <flashmla_sparse | triton_sparse_mla | flashmla_sparse_q8 | flashmla_kv> \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.75 --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --enable-mixed-chunk \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30100
# rows marked "disabled": add --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled
# rows marked "chunk 1024": --chunked-prefill-size 1024
# rows marked "no mixed chunk": drop --enable-mixed-chunk
```

Client (forms the mixed batches; note the deliberate absence of `return_logprob`, which the scheduler treats as a reason not to mix):

```bash
python3 mixed_client.py http://127.0.0.1:30100 out.json 12000
```

```python
"""Drive a server into MIXED batches and record greedy outputs.

Eight short natural prompts start first (max_tokens 96) so they are decoding
when, half a second later, one long prompt arrives whose chunked prefill then
mixes with them. Outputs go to a JSON file for cross-server comparison.

Usage: mixed_client.py <base_url> <out.json> [long_len]
"""

import asyncio
import json
import random
import sys
import time

import aiohttp

URL = sys.argv[1].rstrip("/")
OUT = sys.argv[2]
LONG_LEN = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 6000

SHORT_PROMPTS = [
    "The capital of France is",
    "Water boils at a temperature of",
    "In computer science, a hash table is",
    "The theory of general relativity was published by",
    "A sonnet is a poem that has",
    "Photosynthesis converts sunlight into",
    "The largest planet in the solar system is",
    "To sort a list in Python you can call",
]


async def gen(session, payload):
    t0 = time.time()
    async with session.post(f"{URL}/generate", json=payload) as r:
        body = await r.json()
    body["_latency"] = time.time() - t0
    return body


async def main():
    rng = random.Random(1234)
    long_ids = [rng.randint(1000, 60000) for _ in range(LONG_LEN)]
    sampling = {"temperature": 0.0, "max_new_tokens": 96}
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession(timeout=aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=1800)) as s:
        shorts = [
            asyncio.create_task(
                # No return_logprob: the scheduler skips mixing whenever the running
                # batch or the new batch asks for logprobs (scheduler.py, mixed-style
                # chunked prefill condition), which would hide the very path under test.
                gen(s, {"text": p, "sampling_params": sampling})
            )
            for p in SHORT_PROMPTS
        ]
        await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
        long_task = asyncio.create_task(
            gen(s, {"input_ids": long_ids, "sampling_params": {"temperature": 0.0, "max_new_tokens": 32}})
        )
        short_res = await asyncio.gather(*shorts)
        long_res = await long_task
    out = {
        "short": [
            {
                "prompt": p,
                "text": r.get("text"),
                "output_ids": r.get("output_ids") or (r.get("meta_info") or {}).get("output_token_ids"),
                "completion_tokens": (r.get("meta_info") or {}).get("completion_tokens"),
                "latency": r["_latency"],
            }
            for p, r in zip(SHORT_PROMPTS, short_res)
        ],
        "long": {
            "text": long_res.get("text"),
            "prompt_tokens": (long_res.get("meta_info") or {}).get("prompt_tokens"),
            "latency": long_res["_latency"],
        },
    }
    json.dump(out, open(OUT, "w"), indent=1)
    print("short latencies:", [round(x["latency"], 2) for x in out["short"]])
    print("long: prompt_tokens=%s latency=%.2fs text=%r" % (out["long"]["prompt_tokens"], out["long"]["latency"], (out["long"]["text"] or "")[:60]))
    for x in out["short"]:
        print("  %-48r -> %r" % (x["prompt"], (x["text"] or "")[:70]))


asyncio.run(main())
```

Probe (drop this file as `sitecustomize.py` on the server's `PYTHONPATH`; set `PROBE_REFCHECK=1` for the fp32 row check, which writes its tensors to `DUMP_DIR`):

```python
"""sitecustomize for the mixed-chunk probe.

Counts DSA forward_extend calls per (forward_mode, topk transform, impl,
use_mha, in-graph), logs the first mixed batches by shape (the breakable graph
replays a mixed batch with the static batch's mode, EXTEND), and, with
PROBE_REFCHECK=1, recomputes layer-0 attention in fp32 for the decode rows and
the last chunk rows of the first mixed batches from the KV pool and the top-k
the kernel received, logging cosine / max abs against the kernel's output.
Logs every 200 calls because the servers are stopped with docker stop.
"""

import os
from collections import Counter

_TAG = os.environ.get("PROBE_TAG", "probe")
_REFCHECK = os.environ.get("PROBE_REFCHECK", "0") == "1"
_DUMP = os.environ.get("DUMP_DIR", "/dump")


def _refcheck(self, layer, forward_batch, q, kw, out, method, in_bcg):
    import torch

    from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsa.dequant_k_cache import (
        dequantize_k_cache_paged,
    )

    if not self.use_fused_topk:
        print("[REFCHECK %s] skipped: unfused topk" % _TAG, flush=True)
        return
    topk_indices = kw.get("topk_indices")
    q_rope = kw.get("q_rope")
    if topk_indices is None:
        print("[REFCHECK %s] skipped: no topk_indices" % _TAG, flush=True)
        return
    h = layer.tp_q_head_num
    T = q.shape[0]
    if q_rope is None:
        q_all = q.reshape(T, h, -1)
    else:
        q_all = torch.cat([q.reshape(T, h, -1), q_rope.reshape(T, h, -1)], dim=-1)
    d_qk = q_all.shape[-1]
    d_v = layer.v_head_dim
    out3 = out.reshape(T, h, -1)[:, :, :d_v]
    ext = list(forward_batch.extend_seq_lens_cpu)
    starts = [0]
    for e in ext[:-1]:
        starts.append(starts[-1] + e)
    decode_rows = [s for s, e in zip(starts, ext) if e == 1]
    ci = max(range(len(ext)), key=lambda i: ext[i])
    chunk_rows = list(range(starts[ci] + ext[ci] - 4, starts[ci] + ext[ci]))
    pool = self.token_to_kv_pool.get_key_buffer(layer.layer_id)
    md = self.forward_metadata
    pt = topk_indices.reshape(T, -1)
    kv_ragged = None
    if method == "RAGGED":
        kv_ragged = dequantize_k_cache_paged(pool, md.page_table_1_flattened).reshape(
            -1, d_qk
        )

    def ref_row(t):
        idx = pt[t]
        idx = idx[idx >= 0].long()
        if kv_ragged is not None:
            K = kv_ragged[idx].float()
        else:
            K = dequantize_k_cache_paged(pool, idx.to(torch.int32)).reshape(-1, d_qk).float()
        p = torch.softmax(q_all[t].float() @ K.T * layer.scaling, dim=-1)
        return p @ K[:, :d_v], int(idx.numel())

    rec = {"rows": [], "out": [], "ref": [], "nvalid": [], "group": []}
    for group, rows in (("decode", decode_rows), ("chunk", chunk_rows)):
        cos_min, mabs_max = 1.0, 0.0
        for t in rows:
            ref, nvalid = ref_row(t)
            o = out3[t].float()
            cos = torch.nn.functional.cosine_similarity(o.flatten(), ref.flatten(), dim=0).item()
            mabs = (o - ref).abs().max().item()
            cos_min, mabs_max = min(cos_min, cos), max(mabs_max, mabs)
            rec["rows"].append(t); rec["out"].append(o.cpu()); rec["ref"].append(ref.cpu())
            rec["nvalid"].append(nvalid); rec["group"].append(group)
        print(
            "[REFCHECK %s] layer=%d %s rows=%d (%s, %s, %s): min cosine %.8f, max abs %.3e, ref |x| max %.3e"
            % (_TAG, layer.layer_id, group, len(rows), method, self.dsa_prefill_impl,
               "bcg" if in_bcg else "eager", cos_min, mabs_max,
               max(r.abs().max().item() for r in rec["ref"][-len(rows):]) if rows else 0.0),
            flush=True,
        )
    torch.save(rec, "%s/%s_refcheck_l%d_%d.pt" % (_DUMP, _TAG, layer.layer_id, os.getpid()))


def _install():
    from sglang.srt.layers.attention.dsa_backend import DeepseekSparseAttnBackend
    from sglang.srt.model_executor.runner_backend_utils.breakable_cuda_graph.context import (
        is_in_breakable_cuda_graph,
    )

    counts = Counter()
    state = {"n": 0, "mixed_logged": 0, "checked": 0}
    orig = DeepseekSparseAttnBackend.forward_extend

    def forward_extend(self, q, k, v, layer, forward_batch, *a, **kw):
        mode = forward_batch.forward_mode.name
        method = self.get_topk_transform_method(forward_batch.forward_mode).name
        in_bcg = is_in_breakable_cuda_graph()
        key = (mode, method, self.dsa_prefill_impl, bool(self.use_mha), "bcg" if in_bcg else "eager")
        counts[key] += 1
        state["n"] += 1
        ext = forward_batch.extend_seq_lens_cpu or []
        looks_mixed = mode == "MIXED" or (len(ext) > 1 and max(ext) > 1 and min(ext) == 1)
        if looks_mixed and state["mixed_logged"] < 3 and layer.layer_id == 0:
            state["mixed_logged"] += 1
            print(
                "[PROBE %s] MIXED batch: mode=%s extend_seq_lens=%s prefix_lens=%s method=%s impl=%s use_mha=%s %s"
                % (_TAG, mode, ext, forward_batch.extend_prefix_lens_cpu, method,
                   self.dsa_prefill_impl, self.use_mha, "bcg" if in_bcg else "eager"),
                flush=True,
            )
        if state["n"] % 200 == 0:
            print("[PROBE %s] counts=%s" % (_TAG, dict(counts)), flush=True)
        out = orig(self, q, k, v, layer, forward_batch, *a, **kw)
        if (
            _REFCHECK and looks_mixed and layer.layer_id == 0
            and state["checked"] < 2 and not self.use_mha
        ):
            state["checked"] += 1
            try:
                _refcheck(self, layer, forward_batch, q, kw, out, method, in_bcg)
            except Exception as exc:  # the check must never take the server down
                print("[REFCHECK %s] failed: %r" % (_TAG, exc), flush=True)
        return out

    DeepseekSparseAttnBackend.forward_extend = forward_extend
    print("[PROBE %s] hook installed (refcheck=%s)" % (_TAG, _REFCHECK), flush=True)


try:
    _install()
except Exception as exc:  # never take the server down
    print("[PROBE %s] hook install failed: %r" % (_TAG, exc), flush=True)
```

</details>

Correctness of what the mixed batch computes, checked in the server itself: for the first mixed batches at layer 0 the probe recomputes attention in fp32 from the KV pool and the top-k the kernel received, for the eight decode rows and the last four chunk rows, and compares with the kernel's output.

| prefill backend | transform | rows checked (per rank, 8 ranks) | min cosine | max abs error | max abs of reference |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `flashmla_sparse` (this PR) | RAGGED | 8 decode rows | 0.99999833 | 6.2e-05 | 1.6e-02 |
| `flashmla_sparse` (this PR) | RAGGED | 4 chunk rows | 0.99999845 | 3.1e-05 | 1.5e-02 |
| `triton_sparse_mla` (this PR) | RAGGED | 8 decode rows | 0.99999821 | 6.9e-05 | 1.8e-02 |
| `triton_sparse_mla` (this PR) | RAGGED | 4 chunk rows | 0.99999833 | 3.1e-05 | 1.5e-02 |
| `flashmla_sparse_q8` (this PR) | RAGGED | 8 decode rows | 0.98844880 | 1.2e-03 | 1.9e-02 |
| `flashmla_sparse_q8` (this PR) | RAGGED | 4 chunk rows | 0.99982989 | 6.5e-04 | 1.5e-02 |
| `flashmla_kv` (control, unchanged) | PAGED | 8 decode rows | 0.99999666 | 7.0e-05 | 1.8e-02 |
| `flashmla_kv` (control, unchanged) | PAGED | 4 chunk rows | 0.99999833 | 3.3e-05 | 1.5e-02 |

The two bf16 kernels land at the same distance from the fp32 recomputation as the FP8-native `flashmla_kv` control, i.e. bf16 output rounding (max error ~0.3% of the largest value); these rows are from the merged tree in the 2026-10-14 image, and the 2026-10-06 tree gave the same figures. `flashmla_sparse_q8` computes attention in FP8 (q and KV cast to e4m3 with identity scales), so its rows sit at that kernel's own precision: on plain extend chunks without mixed chunk, the same check gives the same figures (min cosine 0.99978, max abs 6.7e-04 on the chunk rows, against 0.99999845 / 3.1e-05 for `flashmla_sparse` on the same chunks), so the mixed batch adds nothing to the q8 error. Its decode rows sit lower (0.988) because they attend over a dozen keys, where FP8 rounding of P and V does not average out; note that this is the price of sending decode rows through the q8 prefill kernel, which only `--enable-mixed-chunk` does, and that without this PR the configuration does not start at all. The second mixed batch of each run, which fits a graph bucket and replays in-graph, gives the same figures.

Greedy outputs across servers are not a usable metric for this change: the no-mixed `flashmla_sparse` server reproduces its own eight short continuations exactly on a rerun (8/8), but every mixed server agrees with it on only 0-2 of the 8 (first divergence after 0-9 tokens), including the FP8-native `flashmla_kv` control and the eager-prefill `flashmla_sparse` run, neither of which this PR changes. Merging a 4088-token chunk with the decode rows changes the MoE GEMM shapes those rows run under, and on this FP8 stack that is enough to flip near-tie tokens. The row-level check above is the one that isolates the kernel.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Latency (the eight short prompts, 96 tokens each / the 12000-token prompt): `flashmla_sparse` mixed 5.04 s / 3.88 s, `triton_sparse_mla` mixed 3.78 s / 2.62 s, `flashmla_kv` mixed 5.07 s / 3.92 s, `flashmla_sparse` without mixed chunk 5.08 s / 3.86 s and 4.89 s / 3.68 s on a rerun. With three chunks the decode rows only gain three tokens during the prefill, so mixing does not move these numbers; the dequant cost described above is inside the noise here.

title: [Fix] nemotron_vl: Preserve tokenized prompts during media expansion
author: Stelath
body: ## Motivation Nemotron VL image requests fail when callers supply a tokenized prompt through `generate(input_ids=...)`: the processor assumes a string and calls `.replace()` on the list. ## Modifications - Accept tokenized prompts and expand media placeholders directly in token IDs, without re-tokenizing surrounding text. - Use the original text IDs for image budgeting and validate image/video placeholder counts before loading. - Preserve text unknown IDs when normalizing generated video markers. The existing string-prompt path remains supported. This replaces the original decode/re-encode implementation with the token-preserving processor fix previously included in #44581; it does not change the vision encoder or weights. ## Why expand token IDs directly? The immediate 500 occurs because `generate(input_ids=..., image_data=...)` passes a list to a processor that assumes a string and calls `.replace()`. Decoding that list to text would avoid the exception, but a decode/re-encode round trip can change the surrounding text IDs. `_media_token_ids` identifies placeholders represented by a single token; `_splice_media` expands those placeholders directly in the ID list and leaves surrounding text IDs unchanged. These helpers are not required merely to avoid `.replace()` on a list; they make tokenized-prompt support preserve the caller's text IDs. ## Accuracy Tests All **5 CPU tests** in the existing `test_nano_nemotron_vl_processor.py` pass, covering tokenized image expansion/budgeting, invalid image counts, text unknown-ID preservation, and the existing tubelet/EVS cases. Project isort/ruff checks pass. GPU/serving validation has not been rerun for this split. ## Related PR **Merge first in the stack:** #44581 adds offset-based image padding to prevent literal `` / `` text from being mistaken for image boundaries. That follow-up is a separate fix. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not benchmarked; no performance claim or kernel changes. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #39506916262](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39506916262) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #39506916549](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39506916549) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #39506916289](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39506916289)

title: [Test] dsv4: Fix Hopper indexer replay test after DeepSelect decode (#41561)
author: nvpohanh
body:
[by Claude Code]

## Motivation

Fixes #44183.

`test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_fp4_indexer.py::test_hopper_indexer_backends_replay[1]` and `[2]` fail on every Hopper runner since #41561 landed. This breaks `call-jit-kernel-tests / jit-kernel-unit-test-1-gpu-large (0)` in `PR Test Base` for every PR based on current `main` (for example #36652, #43448, and #43826):

```
AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'page_table'
  python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/v41_indexer/full_topk.py:149 (_torch_decode)
```

#41561 made `FullTopKIndexer` use DeepSelect for decode when `is_deep_select_supported()`. That path reads `paged_metadata.page_table` and `paged_metadata.compressed_page_size`, but this test mocks `paged_metadata` with only `max_compressed_seq_len`.

## Modifications

The test now sets `full.use_deep_select_decode = False`, so this CUDA-graph replay test keeps exercising the paged `select_decode` path it was written for. DeepSelect itself is covered by `test_deep_select.py`.

Adding a `page_table` mock instead would not be enough. The test also checks that output padding (row `batch`, and the columns past `topk`) is `-1`, and that the page indices come out in sorted order. The DeepSelect branch writes only `out_page_indices[:bs, :topk]`, with `sorted_index=False`. @yuyu5333, could you check whether production callers rely on `select_decode` resetting those padding entries? If they do, the DeepSelect branch may need the same reset. I haven't verified this.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A: this is a test-only change.

N/A.

title: [Fix] [AMD] mamba: Import the causal conv1d kernels for Mamba2 layers on ROCm
author: aarnetalman
body:
## Motivation

Mamba2 hybrid models (Granite 4.0-H, Falcon-H1, Nemotron-H) do not start on ROCm. `mamba.py` binds `causal_conv1d_fn`, `causal_conv1d_update` and their Triton variants only in its CUDA, NPU and XPU branches, so on ROCm none of them is defined. The server fails while capturing the decode CUDA graphs:

```
NameError: name 'causal_conv1d_update_triton' is not defined
```

(`causal_conv1d_update` for Falcon-H1). `mamba1.py` imports those names from `mamba.py`, so it cannot be imported on ROCm either ("Ignore import error when loading sglang.srt.models.mamba").

`causal_conv1d.py` already handles ROCm: the compiled kernel is CUDA-only, and it falls back to the Triton kernels there.

## Modifications

- `mamba.py`: take the CUDA import branch on ROCm too (`is_cuda() or is_hip()`).
- No change on CUDA, NPU, XPU or CPU.

## Accuracy Tests

MI350X, `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm724-mi35x-20261019` (upstream/main of 2026-10-19) with this change applied, `--attention-backend triton`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0`. GSM8K: all 1,319 questions, temperature 0, `sgl-eval` 0.1.2.

| Model | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tiiuae/Falcon-H1-7B-Instruct` | `NameError: name 'causal_conv1d_update' is not defined` at startup | serves; GSM8K 85.37% (85.82% on the 2026-10-12 nightly); with `--enable-deterministic-inference` 86.05% |
| `ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny` | `NameError` at startup | serves; GSM8K 86.20%; with `--enable-deterministic-inference` 86.73% |
| `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2` | fails at startup | needs ReLU2 on ROCm as well, added by #44198 (merged); with both, starts; with `--enable-deterministic-inference` GSM8K 75.28% (26% of answers hit the 2,048-token limit) |

Not addressed here, for reviewers trying other settings on ROCm:
- With AITER enabled (`SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, the ROCm image default), Falcon-H1 serves but its output is wrong (GSM8K 0.5%, on the 2026-10-13 to 2026-10-19 nightlies alike) and a 50-sequence prefill batch hit a GPU memory fault. Granite 4.0-H is fine with AITER (GSM8K 86.35% with Triton attention, 72.25% with the default AITER attention).
- `--enable-deterministic-inference` without `--attention-backend` selects FA3, which the ROCm image does not ship; with `--attention-backend triton` these models start.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance change on other platforms; on ROCm these models did not run before.

title: [Fix] [AMD] activation: Run ReLU2 natively on ROCm
author: aarnetalman
body:
## Motivation

`ReLU2` (squared ReLU, used by Nemotron-H's MLP) has no `forward_hip`. On ROCm the dispatcher falls back to `forward_cuda`, which calls the JIT `relu2` kernel; that kernel is CUDA-only and is only imported on CUDA, so the model fails to start:

```
NameError: name 'relu2' is not defined
```

## Modifications

- `ReLU2.forward_hip`: use `forward_native` (`relu(x) * relu(x)` in torch).
- No change on CUDA or other platforms.

## Accuracy Tests

MI350X, `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm724-mi35x-20261019` (upstream/main of 2026-10-19), `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2`, `--attention-backend triton --enable-deterministic-inference`, with this change and the Mamba2 import fix (#44197; without it the model stops earlier): before, `NameError: name 'relu2' is not defined` at startup; after, the server starts and serves (GSM8K 75.28%, all 1,319 questions, temperature 0, `sgl-eval` 0.1.2; 26% of answers hit the 2,048-token limit). `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0`.

Normal mode on ROCm still needs `flashinfer`, which the ROCm image does not ship (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'flashinfer'`, from the model's other code paths); not addressed here.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

ROCm only, and the model did not run before.
