title: [Fix] diffusion: Invalidate merged LoRA cache after adapter rewrites
author: Alex-Wengg
body:
## Motivation

Rewriting a local LoRA adapter with different weights of the same serialized size leaves the persistent merge-cache key unchanged. A subsequent startup can silently adopt the previous adapter's merged weights.

## Modifications

Include the adapter file's nanosecond modification time in the key, using one `os.stat` call in place of the existing size lookup. Add CPU regressions for in-place rewrites and atomic replacement, including unchanged-file cache hits and round-tripping the updated merged weights.

This remains metadata-based invalidation: updates preserving both file size and modification time are outside its scope. Existing entries incur a one-time cache miss under the new key format.

## Accuracy Tests

Both regression cases fail before the fix with `updated adapter adopted stale merged weights`, and pass afterward:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/multimodal_gen/test_lora_merge_cache_key.py -p no:cacheprovider
# 2 passed
```

The five existing merge-cache tests plus the two new cases also pass in an isolated CPU harness. The harness preloads the real cache module without the GPU-dependent `pipelines_core.__init__` and disables the unrelated diffusion-wide conftest. No cache behavior is mocked; the tests use tiny real safetensors. Full-model generation was not run.

Pre-commit passes for both changed files, and `git diff --check` passes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run; no inference-speed claim. Key generation still uses one filesystem metadata lookup per adapter.

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add regression tests and verify failure before / success after the fix.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style.
- Documentation: no CLI or configuration changes.
- Full-model accuracy and speed benchmarks: not run; validation is limited to the cache contract above.

title: [Fix] sglang-server: Honour extra_key on the Rust frontend's /generate
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

`extra_key` is the request's prefix-cache namespace: the scheduler keys radix-cache entries by it, so two requests share cached prefixes only under the same key. The Python `/generate` route honours it (`GenerateReqInput._normalize_extra_key`), and the OpenAI-compatible processors in `rust/sglang-processor` already forward it into the native body (`"extra_key": request.extra_key`), but the Rust frontend's `/generate` schema did not carry the field. In Rust mode it was dropped as an unknown key, so every request landed in one cache namespace and requests sent under different keys could reuse each other's cached prefixes.

## Modifications

- `proto/sglang/api/v1/generate.proto`: add `extra_key` (tag 23, `StringOrList`) to `GenerateRequest`; regenerated `api_types.py`, `sglang.api.v1.rs` and `sglang.api.v1.serde.rs` with `cargo gen-api`.
- `rust/sglang-server/src/message/request.rs`: fan `extra_key` out with the Python semantics: one key broadcasts to every item, a list is per item and must match the batch size, an empty key means none, and a list on a single (non-batch) request is a 400 (`extra_key should be a string for a single request.`), as in `GenerateReqInput`.
- `rust/sglang-server/src/message/io_struct.rs`: carry it into the scheduler header's `extra_key` slot. The header is decoded positionally (`TokenizedGenerateReqInput` is an `array_like` msgspec struct), so the three slots before it (`routing_key`, `require_reasoning`, `priority`) are now emitted at their defaults; the header grows from 32 to 36 entries. Everything after `extra_key` still has a msgspec default and stays omitted.
- `test/registered/unit/api/v1/test_parity.py`: `extra_key` leaves the pinned list of Python-only request fields.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: the change only affects which prefix-cache namespace a request is placed in, not the generated tokens.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Not applicable.

title: [Fix] DeepSeek-V4.1: Align paged indexer score rows for DeepSelect decode
author: mmangkad
body:
## Motivation

On SM90 the full top-k decode of the ratio-1/2 index layers (`FullTopKIndexer._torch_decode`) runs DeepSelect `topk_page_transform` on the paged fp4 index scores from `fp4_index_logits_paged`. DeepSelect requires 128-byte-aligned rows, but the scores were padded to eight floats only, so any score width that is not a multiple of 32 floats fails:

```
Tensor<256, 524290>[strides=<524296, 1>, dtype=float32]
Root cause: Tensor stride for dimension 0 is not aligned to 128 bytes
```

With the cookbook H200 recipe for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, every TP rank hits this at startup and the server exits.

`test_fp4_indexer.py::test_hopper_indexer_backends_replay` also fails on main, first with `AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'page_table'`, because its fake metadata predates the DeepSelect path.

## Modifications

- `fp4_index_logits_paged`: allocate the scores with `aligned_new_empty` at DeepSelect's input stride alignment (128B) instead of padding rows to eight floats; that alignment also covers candidate-amax.
- `decode_scores`: build the top-k v2 plan only when the caller uses it. The SM90 full top-k selects with DeepSelect and never read it, so it no longer launches the plan kernel every decode step; `select_decode` asserts the plan is present.
- `test_hopper_indexer_backends_replay`: give the full top-k a real per-row page table, kept in sync with the shuffled request table on every replay, and an output buffer of exactly live rows by `topk`, as at runtime. The candidate outputs keep their padded shape and padding checks.

## Tests

- The updated test fails on main with the 128B stride error and passes with this change.
- On H200, each registered file that exercises this code passes when run as CI does (`python3 <file> -f`): `test_fp4_indexer.py`, `test_deep_select.py`, `test_dsv4_nonpaged_indexer.py`, `test_dsv41_candidate_blocks.py`, `test_dense_prefill_indexer.py`, `test_dsv41_prefill_sparse_indexer.py`, `qsa/test_qsa.py`, `test_dsv32_indexer_fusion.py`, `test_dsv4_indexer_quant.py`.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash launches and serves on 8xH200 with the cookbook H200 Low-Latency recipe, which fails at startup on main.

title: [Fix] compressed-tensors: Serve NVFP4 W4A4 linears via FP4 Marlin when --fp4-gemm-backend marlin is set on SM100
author: koladefaj
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #43988.

With a compressed-tensors NVFP4 W4A4 checkpoint on SM100, `--fp4-gemm-backend marlin` crashes during CUDA-graph capture:

```
flashinfer.utils.BackendSupportedError: mm_fp4 does not support backend 'marlin' with capability 100
```

`_get_scheme_from_parts` returns the native `CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4` linear whenever the capability check passes. That scheme hands the backend name straight to FlashInfer `mm_fp4`, which has no `marlin` backend. FP4 Marlin is weight-only, and #40022 already added the weight-only path (`CompressedTensorsW4A16Fp4(has_input_global_scale=True)`) for W4A4 checkpoints, but it is only taken when the capability check fails.

## Modifications

- `compressed_tensors.py`: when `--fp4-gemm-backend marlin` is set, W4A4 NVFP4 dense linears take the existing weight-only Marlin path on SM100 too, the same way ModelOpt NVFP4 honors the flag. Without the flag, SM100 still uses the native W4A4 scheme.
- The warning now names the reason for each case. For an explicit marlin request it also says that NVFP4 MoE layers follow `--moe-runner-backend` and stay W4A4.
- `test_compressed_tensors_fp4_schemes.py`: a CPU regression test for SM100 + `marlin`. It asserts that the linear gets the weight-only scheme, the MoE keeps `CompressedTensorsW4A4Nvfp4MoE`, and the warning says both. It fails on `main` and passes with this change.

## Accuracy Tests

1x NVIDIA B200 (compute capability 10.0), image `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13`, `python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <model> --tp 1 [--fp4-gemm-backend marlin]`, then `python -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 200`.

| Model | Code | `--fp4-gemm-backend` | Result | GSM8K |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-NVFP4 | main | marlin | crashes (`BackendSupportedError`, below) | n/a |
| RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-NVFP4 | this PR | marlin | serves, dense linears via FP4 Marlin | 0.935 |
| RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-NVFP4 | this PR | auto (native W4A4) | serves, unchanged path | 0.905 |
| RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4 | this PR | marlin | serves, dense via Marlin, MoE stays W4A4 | 0.910 |

The weight-only Marlin result is in line with the native W4A4 path. 200 questions is too small to read anything into the 0.03 difference.

Note: both main and this PR were run on the image's checkout (`684fea8`). For the "this PR" rows, this commit was applied on top as a patch, because the image could not fetch from GitHub. It applies cleanly and touches only `compressed_tensors.py`, so the only difference between the before and after rows is this change.

### Before (main 684fea8, `--fp4-gemm-backend marlin`)

```
  File ".../layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py", line 1324, in apply
    return scheme.apply_weights(layer, x, bias=bias)
  File ".../compressed_tensors/schemes/compressed_tensors_w4a4_nvfp4.py", line 158, in apply_weights
    out = fp4_gemm(
  File ".../layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py", line 168, in fp4_gemm
    return flashinfer_fp4_gemm(
  File ".../flashinfer/utils.py", line 1553, in wrapper
    raise BackendSupportedError(
flashinfer.utils.BackendSupportedError: mm_fp4 does not support backend 'marlin' with capability 100
```

### After (this PR, `--fp4-gemm-backend marlin`)

Qwen3-8B-NVFP4:
```
--fp4-gemm-backend marlin is weight-only; serving NVFP4 w4a4 dense linears weight-only via FP4 Marlin, so their activation quantization is ignored. MoE layers follow --moe-runner-backend and stay w4a4.
/generate "The capital of France is" -> " Paris. The capital of Germany is Berlin. The capital of Italy is Rome."
Accuracy: 0.935  Invalid: 0.000
```

Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4:
```
--fp4-gemm-backend marlin is weight-only; serving NVFP4 w4a4 dense linears weight-only via FP4 Marlin, so their activation quantization is ignored. MoE layers follow --moe-runner-backend and stay w4a4.
Using CompressedTensorsW4A4Nvfp4MoE
Accuracy: 0.910  Invalid: 0.000
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. This only changes which scheme is picked for an explicit `--fp4-gemm-backend marlin`; the default path on SM100 is unchanged.

title: [Fix] cuda_graph: Wait for in-flight layer-wise cache loads before prefill graph replay
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

HiCache L2 load-back, HiCache storage load-back (e.g. `buffer_only`), and the unified-cache external linker load KV/SWA/Mamba state into the device pools layer by layer, overlapped with the prefill forward. The forward waits for each layer inside the pool accessors (`get_key_buffer`, `mamba2_layer_index`, ...) through the registered `layer_transfer_counter`.

A prefill CUDA graph replay never runs those Python-level waits: the captured graph is launched as a whole. Nothing stops the graph from replaying a batch whose load is still in flight (`scheduler.py` has carried `# todo: disable cuda graph execution if hicache loading triggered` since 2025-06). The forward then reads layers that have not landed yet and produces wrong logits silently. Computed KV for the following pages is built on the corrupted state, and can be cached and backed up under the same content-addressed keys.

This is reachable on main today whenever a model replays the prefill graph for a loading batch. Inkling defaults to the Full prefill CUDA graph backend, so its HiCache path is affected. Whether it shows up depends on the race between the H2D copies and the replay: the existing Inkling HiCache bit-exact tests pass on main only because the copies usually win.

## Modifications

- `PrefillCudaGraphRunner.execute`: before a Full replay, if the KV pool's layer transfer counter has an active consumer (this batch is loading), wait until the last layer has landed. Works for both counters (HiCache `LayerDoneCounter`, a stream wait; linker `LayerWiseLoadCounter`, a CPU wait), since both complete layers in order.
- Eager and breakable prefill are unchanged and keep per-layer load/compute overlap: breakable replay runs the pool accessors at its eager breaks, so their per-layer waits still apply (except a captured state-reading linear extend, see below). A loading batch that replays a Full graph now waits for the whole load first; batches without a load are unaffected.
- Test hook `SGLANG_TEST_HICACHE_H2D_DELAY_CYCLES` (default 0, off): a GPU sleep on the host-to-device stream before each layer's load, so a replay that skips the load wait reliably reads unloaded layers.

## Accuracy Tests

Inkling (`thinkingmachines/Inkling --revision test`, deterministic inference, Full prefill graph default).

New `TestUnifiedHybridHiCacheSlowLoadBitExact` (the existing HiCache bit-exact class with `SGLANG_TEST_HICACHE_H2D_DELAY_CYCLES=50000000`):

| GPU | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1x H200 (CI arch) | avg KL 4.4e-3 (fail) | 0.0 |
| 1x GB300 | avg KL 1.7e-2 (fail) | 0.0 |

The existing `TestUnifiedHybridHiCacheBitExact` passes on both trees: without the delay the H2D copies usually win the race, which is why CI has not caught this.

Earlier probe on 1x GB300 with the same kind of injected H2D delay, also covering storage load-back; the logs confirm graph replays with an in-flight load:

| Tree | Injected H2D delay | `TestUnifiedHybridHiCacheBitExact` (L2) | `TestUnifiedHybridBufferOnlyBitExact` (L3) |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | no | avg KL 0.0 | avg KL 0.0 |
| main | yes | **avg KL 3.1e-3 (fail)** | **avg KL 6.4e-3 (fail)** |
| this PR | yes | avg KL 0.0 | avg KL 0.0 |

The same fix also restores KL 0.0 for the Mooncake direct linker on Inkling (#41343), which hits the race without any injected delay (avg KL 2.5e-3 before; 0.0 in 3/3 runs after, and 0.0 with a 0.2 s per-layer injected load delay).

Breakable check: Inkling forced to `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable` with the same injected delay gives avg KL 0.0 on main and on this PR (4 replays with an in-flight load each); its state reads run at eager breaks.

**Out of scope, fixed in #44414:** a breakable graph that captures a state-reading linear extend (the Triton KDA extend captured since #41105) skips those reads' waits. GLM-5.3-Flash on 4x GB300 with the Triton KDA extend forced and the same delay: median KL 3.5-4.1e-3 on main and on this PR vs a 1.9e-4 floor; 1.4e-4 when every replay waits or when the KDA capture is disabled. Not a regression from this PR.

## Benchmark and Profiling

Host-tier (L2) hit TTFT, Inkling-Small bf16, TP4 on 4x GB300, Full prefill graph, 512 new tokens on a cached prefix, median of 5 (ms). `eager` is the alternative of running a loading batch eagerly instead of replaying the graph.

| Prefix | main (no wait) | this PR | eager |
|---|---|---|---|
| 160k | 113.0 | 115.0 | 195.4 |
| 320k | 176.0 | 182.2 | 247.7 |
| 500k | 254.9 | 255.0 | 306.7 |

Cold and device-hit TTFT are unchanged.

## Tests

- `test_prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py::TestPrefillCudaGraphRunnerLayerLoads`: the replay wait blocks until the last layer of an in-flight load completes, and is a no-op without a counter. Negative control: removing the wait fails `test_replay_waits_for_every_layer_of_an_inflight_load`.
- `test_prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py`: 18 passed, including `test_breakable_replay_keeps_per_layer_load_overlap` (fails if the wait is not limited to Full).

title: [Fix] [XPU] gemma3: Enable bidirectional image attention
author: desmond-intel
body:
…-xpu

Gemma-3 image tokens attend bidirectionally in prefill (text stays causal). On the intel_xpu backend they ran plain-causal, degrading vision tasks (docvqa_val ANLS 59.4 on B60 vs 65.0 on H200). Use the sgl-kernel-xpu bidirectional_block_ids prefill mask (kernel-side) rather than a Python attention fallback:

- gemma3_mm.prepare_attn_masks: for XPUAttentionBackend build a per-token image-block id over whole sequences (image index, -1 for text) and store it on the backend (is_xpu()-guarded lazy import; Triton path unchanged). None when this extend holds fewer than two tokens of any image.
- xpu_backend.forward_extend: when present, run non-causal and pass bidirectional_block_ids to flash_attn_with_kvcache; the kernel re-imposes causal for text and keeps image tokens bidirectional. With a cached prefix (radix hit or a later chunk) pad q to whole sequences so the kernel sees a full prefill, then keep the extend rows. On sliding-window layers drop the window only when it cannot clip a key; longer prompts keep local attention.
- layernorm.forward_xpu: make the input contiguous before gemma_rmsnorm (it requires a contiguous last dim, which a sliced hidden state may not have), so Gemma-3 loads on XPU.
- test/registered/xpu/test_xpu_gemma3_bidirectional_attn.py: sliding-window bound and image-after-cached-prefix against a dense reference.

Requires the companion sgl-kernel-xpu bidirectional_block_ids kernel. docvqa_val (full 5349) 59.4 -> 67.5 on Intel Arc Pro B60, above H200 (65.0).

title: [Doc] cookbook: Mirror SA cluster NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE in AgentX launches, fix GPU counts
author: nvpohanh
body:
[by Claude Code]

## Motivation

The cookbook's **Agentic Long-Context Deployment** sections (#42726, #43083, #43799, #43983, #44065) on GLM-5.2, DeepSeek-V4, DeepSeek-V4.1, Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next mirror SemiAnalysis InferenceX AgentX submissions as raw launch commands, each linked to the run that measured it. A review of [InferenceX #3953](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3953) found two places where the pages differ from what SemiAnalysis actually ran:

1. **`NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1` was missing from many worker environments.** SemiAnalysis's B300, B200, GB200 and GB300 clusters export it into every worker container, and most recipes do not set it themselves. SGLang sets it to `int(enable_symm_mem)` when it is unset ([`engine.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/07c8f7294daa12087e969c89a11f773d36b9d42d/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py#L1658-L1659) at `07c8f729`, one of the pinned images). A reader who copied a single-node command without `--enable-symm-mem` therefore ran with cuMem off, while SemiAnalysis ran with it on.
2. **The GPU count on many deployment chips was wrong.** The chip counted whole nodes, so a TP4 engine on 4 of an 8-GPU B300 node showed "8 GPUs".

This PR also pins [InferenceX #3953](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3953) to its measured run, which now has a `/use` comment. Apart from the generated data files, the only change is one line in the AgentX component (`_agentx.jsx`): the chip now says "1 GPU" instead of "1 GPUs", because single-GPU deployments now appear. Page text, Deployment panels and Playgrounds are unchanged.

## Source

[InferenceX](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX) `main` (`6fff051b`), with these open InferenceX PRs overlaid:

| PR | Page | Lane(s) | Pinned to |
|---|---|---|---|
| [#3953](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3953) GLM-5.2 NVFP4 B300 Dynamo+SGLang | GLM-5.2 | `glm5.2-fp4-b300-dynamo-sglang-agentic-agg-tp4` | [run 38356572105](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/38356572105) (`/use`), verified |
| [#3927](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3927) DSV4.1 GB200 SGLang | DeepSeek-V4.1 | `dsv41flash-fp4-gb200-sglang-agentic-dspark` | [run 38266927261](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/38266927261) (`/use`), verified |

The overlay list is the same as in #44065. InferenceX `main` moved from `01e3b46a` to `6fff051b` without changing any mirrored lane.

## What this PR does

| Page | Lanes | Deployments | Points | Hardware |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.2 | 16 | 27 | 67 | GB300, GB200, B300, B200, H200 |
| DeepSeek-V4 | 10 | 20 | 61 | GB300, GB200, B300, B200, H200 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 | 9 | 19 | 66 | GB300, GB200, B300, B200, H200, H100 |
| Qwen3.5 | 18 | 46 | 216 | GB300, GB200, B300, B200, H200, H100 |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next | 4 | 4 | 22 | GB300, B300, B200, H200 |

- **`NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1` from the cluster environment.** It is added to the worker environment of every lane that ran on one of these clusters and whose recipe leaves it unset. A recipe value always wins. Lanes whose recipes already set it are unchanged.
  - **Evidence.** Each cluster was checked against the worker fingerprints (the environment captured inside the worker container) of measured runs whose recipe does not set the variable:
    - SA's B300 cluster: [run 35628368631](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/35628368631) (2026-09-21), [run 36463674051](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/36463674051) and [run 38356572105](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/38356572105).
    - B200 cluster: [run 35345548475](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/35345548475) (2026-09-18) and [run 37420473448](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/37420473448).
    - GB200 cluster: [run 38266927261](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/38266927261).
    - GB300 cluster: [run 38221097558](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/38221097558).
  - **Bash-launcher lanes.** On the B300 and B200 clusters these also started their servers through the same `srun --container-image` path, so they ran in the same environment.
  - **Not changed.** The H200 cluster does not set it ([run 34857875250](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/34857875250)). Lanes on three clusters with only bash-launcher runs (one B200, one B300 and the H100 cluster) have no worker fingerprint, so they are unverified and left unchanged. NIC names, log levels and timeouts from the cluster environment stay out, as before.
  - **Scope.** 22 lanes and 978 of the 2,144 command sets change, and only by this variable.
    - **Behavior changes (642 command sets in 16 lanes).** These are single-node workers without `--enable-symm-mem`, where the reader's SGLang would otherwise turn cuMem off:
      - DeepSeek-V4: B200 Dynamo agg, B200 and B300 SGLang HiCache MTP, B300 EAGLE.
      - DeepSeek-V4.1: B200, B300, GB200 and GB300 DSpark, GB300 Dynamo agg.
      - GLM-5.2: B200 FP4/FP8 MTP, B300 FP4/FP8 MTP, B300 Dynamo agg TP4.
      - Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: B200 and GB300.
    - **Already 1 (the other 336).** SGLang sets it to 1 anyway: `--enable-symm-mem` forces it (Qwen3.5 B200/B300/GB300 lanes, GLM-5.2 B300 TP4 c32), and multi-node GB200/GB300 workers default it on (DeepSeek-V4 GB200/GB300 Dynamo agg). There the variable only makes the measured environment explicit.
- **GPU count (fix).** A deployment's chip now counts the GPUs its workers use: TP × PP per worker, times DP when DP attention is off. Before, it counted every node a worker touched. 40 deployments change, and nothing else about them:
  - Examples: GLM-5.2 B300 Dynamo agg TP4 8 → 4; Qwen3.8-Flash-Next TP1 on B200/B300 8 → 1 and on GB300 4 → 1; DeepSeek-V4.1 B300 TP2 8 → 2; Qwen3.5 B300 1P1D TP2 prefill + TP2 decode 16 → 4; GLM-5.2 B200 1P4D (DEP8 prefill + 4 × TP4 decode) 40 → 24.
  - Every new count fits the worker's node count, which the pipeline now checks.
- **GLM-5.2 NVFP4 B300 Dynamo+SGLang ([InferenceX #3953](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3953)) pinned.** Both deployments ("Agg TP4", c1/c8/c16/c20; "Agg TP4·DPA4", c24/c32/c48) now point to [run 38356572105](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/38356572105) at `caa2199e` and show as verified, instead of "in progress" at the PR head `56b2949a`.
  - The commands are unchanged apart from `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE`. The head only merged InferenceX `main`'s recipe refactor, and #44065 showed that it renders the same server commands.
  - The derived HiCache tier of the DPA4 deployment now takes its flags from this measured lane instead of `glm5.2-fp4-b300-sglang-agentic-mtp`. The flags are identical.

## How the commands are produced

The pipeline and rules are the same as in #44065, with these changes:

- **Cluster environment.** The rules now list, per SemiAnalysis cluster, the environment variables it exports into workers whose absence changes SGLang's own defaults. Today that is only `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE`; `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE` and `NCCL_GRAPH_MIXING_SUPPORT` are tracked but no cluster sets them.
  - Each entry cites the run and host whose worker fingerprint showed the value.
  - Every sync re-checks the table against measured worker fingerprints and fails on a mismatch or an unlisted cluster.
  - The round-trip check now also fails on any worker variable that comes from neither the launch nor this table.
- **GPU count.** The formula above.

Each lane is still rendered at the exact commit of the run that produced its dashboard data. SA-only settings are removed: the benchmark harness, cluster paths and caches, telemetry, and InferenceX's synthetic speculative acceptance (disclosed per deployment). Placeholders replace IPs, ports and NICs. Router and KV-offload variants that were not run are derived and labeled "Derived — not run".

The data files are generated. The only hand-written change is the one-line pluralization in `_agentx.jsx`.

## Validation

- `mint validate` (strict build) and `mint broken-links --check-anchors --check-redirects` pass. `node docs/scripts/check_cookbook_configs.mjs` passes, and so does `pre-commit run --all-files`.
- **Browser click-through.** A headless browser clicked through every combination of hardware, checkpoint, deployment, concurrency, KV tier and router on all five pages under `mint dev`, opening every tab. That is 2,144 command sets: GLM-5.2 328, DeepSeek-V4 316, DeepSeek-V4.1 396, Qwen3.5 1,028 and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 76.
  - The rendered commands match the expected text exactly.
  - The "Copy link" URL of every deployment was reopened in a fresh tab and restored the same selection and tab (116 links).
  - The Deployment-panel footer link and the copy buttons work as before.
  - This ran after the component change. The final re-sync before pushing changed only the recorded InferenceX `main` SHA.
- **Decoder and KV flags.** The component's own decoder, run through Node, reproduces the Python-generated commands for all 2,144 combinations, including every point's measured tier. Every KV-cache flag in a shown command exists in the SGLang commit of its deployment's image (190 image/flag pairs).
- **Diff against `main`.** 978 command sets differ, each only by `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1` in the worker environment. The other 1,166 are byte-identical, including every derived router and KV-offload variant. The other changes are the 40 GPU chips and the #3953 provenance.
- **Cluster environment.** The table matches the worker fingerprints of measured runs on every cluster that has srt-slurm lanes. Each mirrored worker variable comes either from the launch or from this table.
- **Argument parsing.** No command line changed. All 1,848 distinct `sglang.launch_server`, `dynamo.sglang`, `sglang_router.launch_router` and `dynamo.frontend` commands are identical to commands already parsed with their own submission images for earlier cookbook PRs. Environment variables are not part of that check.

No serving or benchmark runs were performed for this PR; the numbers live in the linked SemiAnalysis runs. SGLang CI was not triggered.

title: [Fix] metrics: Populate pending_prealloc_token_usage
author: SovietPower
body:
## Motivation

`sglang:pending_prealloc_token_usage` has reported `0` on every scrape since it was added. `SchedulerStats` declares the field with a `0.0` default and `log_stats` reads it, but nothing ever assigns it. The metric came from #11625, an automated `scripts/copy_from_oss.py` sync that only touched `collector.py`, and the producer-side change never followed. `gemini-code-assist` flagged this on that PR, but the comment was not addressed before merge, and `git log -S pending_prealloc_token_usage` shows no other commit. #45970 added `prealloc_{full,window,swa}_token_usage` next to it but still leaves this field unassigned.

Its name and description ("pending preallocated tokens (not preallocated yet)") describe decode-side admission backlog: tokens of requests still waiting for KV space. The decode side currently exposes no token-level signal for this. `num_decode_prealloc_queue_reqs` only counts requests, and `prealloc_full_token_usage` from #45970 covers the other side, KV space already preallocated for transfers that have not finished.

## Modifications

- Fill `pending_prealloc_token_usage` in `_update_decode_queue_stats()`, the single place where the other decode queue stats are set, and which every reporting path reaches. The value is the tokens that requests in the prealloc queue and the retracted queue still need to allocate (`pre_alloc_fill_len`), divided by `max_total_num_tokens`. A value above 1 is expected when decode cannot keep up.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable. This changes metrics only.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The value is a sum over the prealloc and retracted queues, computed once per metrics report.

title: [Fix] sglang-processor: Follow Python's OpenAI layer through #43027, #37577, #43006, #43026, #43005
author: sherlockwu
body:
## Motivation

sgl-router and the Rust server serve OpenAI chats through `/generate`, using `rust/sglang-processor` to do what Python's OpenAI layer does. Five Python changes merged to main after the processor's parity fixtures were recorded, so the Rust path no longer matches Python's:

| Python change | What the `/generate` path did instead |
|---|---|
| sgl-project/sglang#43027 — omit absent `tool_calls` | sent `"tool_calls": null` in chat messages and in tool-parsing stream deltas |
| sgl-project/sglang#37577 — request `watermark` | **served the request through `/generate` without the field**, so a client that asked for a watermark got unwatermarked output |
| sgl-project/sglang#43006 — DeepSeek honors `tool_choice: "none"` | still rendered every tool into DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 prompts (279 tokens instead of 5 for the fixture case) |
| sgl-project/sglang#43026 — stable stream `created` | stamped each chat stream chunk with the current time |
| sgl-project/sglang#43005 — report zero cached tokens | dropped `prompt_tokens_details` when the cached count was 0 under `--enable-cache-report` |

The fixtures were recorded before these changes, so the tests kept passing. I found the first two by running Qwen3.8-27B through the router against the engine's own `/v1/chat/completions` (sgl-project/sglang#43689). The other three surfaced when I regenerated the fixtures from Python on main.

## Modifications

- `openai/chat.rs`, `openai/completions.rs`: forward `watermark` into `sampling_params` (validation stays with the engine's tokenizer manager, which serves both routes); omit null `tool_calls` from unary messages and tool-parsing stream deltas; give each chat stream a single `created`.
- `openai/wire.rs`: keep `prompt_tokens_details` with `cached_tokens: 0` when cache reporting is on.
- `render/models/deepseek_v4.rs`, `deepseek_v41.rs`: render request tools only when `serving_chat` passes them on (`tool_choice` other than `"none"`, and a named choice must match a request tool). The tools are still validated either way, as pydantic does.
- Fixtures regenerated from Python on main: `openai_parity/*` (offline, reusing the recorded engine outputs), the DeepSeek render fixtures in `tests/fixtures/parity/`, and sgl-router's `tests/fixtures/deepseek/`. Added synthetic `watermark` cases for chat (GLM-5.3) and completions (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731).
- `tests/openai_parity.rs`: a streamed response fails if its chunks disagree on `created`. `wire.rs` gets a unit test for zero cached tokens.
- sgl-router's `generate_deepseek_parity.py` passed `tools=None` to `_apply_jinja_template`, which the DeepSeek branch ignored until #43006. It now passes the tools `_process_messages` would. With that, regeneration only changes the two `tools_none` cases.

The fixture diffs are mostly churn: `created` timestamps, random `call_` ids (the test ignores both), the new `watermark` / `return_flat_raw_output_top_logprobs` defaults, and `chat_encoding_spec` for the DeepSeek fixtures. The semantic changes are the removed `tool_calls: null` keys and the two `tools_none` prompts.

## Accuracy Tests

- `cargo test -p sglang-processor --all-features` passes, with token ids checked against the cached pinned checkpoints. Run against the old `src/`, the regenerated fixtures fail.
- sgl-router `cargo test` passes (1077 + 208 + 138 + 8), as do `sglang-renderer` and `sglang-server`. Clippy and pre-commit are clean.
- Live, Qwen3.8-27B: one engine plus sgl-router (`--chat-routing reorg`) built from sgl-project/sglang#43689 with this branch merged in. In the 48-case router-vs-engine suite, every case served through `/generate` matches the engine's route in `input_ids` and response, apart from the expected `n: 2` stream interleaving and seeded sampling. No result masking was needed. Before this change, the `watermark: None` sampling key and `"tool_calls": null` had to be masked to get there.
- A `watermark` request through the router now takes `/generate` and gets the same 400 as the engine's own route, both for a bad key and when the server was not started with `--enable-watermark`. All 62 chunks of a streamed chat share one `created`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Feat] sgl-router: Fix cache-aware routing for MTP/EAGLE on hybrid (Mamba/KDA) models
author: sherlockwu
body:
Stacked on https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44243.

## Motivation

With `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE` (MTP), cache-aware routing never matches on hybrid linear-attention models (Qwen3.5, GLM-5.3-Flash):

- The router picks bigram block hashing whenever `speculative_algorithm` is EAGLE-family (`classify_bigram`).
- The engine uses bigram radix keys for EAGLE only when the model has **no** Mamba/linear-attention layers (`unified_tree_core.py`, `rust_tree_core/adapter.py`).

So hybrid workers publish unigram block hashes, the router queries with bigram hashes, and same-prefix requests spread by load instead of following the cache.

## Modifications

Router only. `/server_info` already reports `uses_mamba_radix_cache`, so both discovery paths (`workers/introspect.rs`, primary; `state/kv_events/discovery.rs`, fallback) now use
`is_bigram = classify_bigram(speculative_algorithm) && !uses_mamba_radix_cache`.
No engine change is needed, so this also fixes routing for engines already deployed.

Known gap: `uses_mamba_radix_cache` comes from an architecture list (`arg_groups/overrides.py`), while the engine's bigram rule uses `uses_ssm_state()`. They agree for every hybrid model I checked (GLM-5.3-Flash / `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`, the Qwen3.5/3.8 family, Kimi Linear, NemotronH), except `MiniCPMSALAForCausalLM`. That model with EAGLE would still hash bigrams, which is no worse than today.

## Verification

- `cargo test --lib -- is_bigram introspect kv_events::discovery`: 35 passed, including a new test (EAGLE + `uses_mamba_radix_cache: true` gives `is_bigram=false`).
- End to end against the **stock** engine (no engine patch): 2× Qwen3.5-27B workers with the cookbook MTP flags (`--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4`), `--policy cache_aware`, and 11 same-prefix chat requests after flushing both caches:

| Router | `is_bigram` at subscribe | Split |
|---|---|---|
| base | `true` | 5/6 |
| this PR | `false` | 11/0 |

title: [Fix] glm5.2: Align PD HiSparse prefill KV layout
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

The GLM-5.2 PD + HiSparse + MTP test introduced in #37771 fails on its first GSM8K request with `NaN detected! verify: target model logits`:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38354570978/job/115154648003

The prefill worker leaves its DSA backend unspecified. On Blackwell with FP8 KV, this defaults to `trtllm`, whose raw MLA KV layout is 576 bytes/token (512 FP8 NoPE + 64 FP8 RoPE). The decode worker explicitly selects `flashmla_kv`, which consumes 656 bytes/token (512 FP8 NoPE + 16 bytes of FP32 scales + 128 bytes of BF16 RoPE).

The original CI logs confirm this backend mismatch. The ordinary Mooncake MLA transfer copies bytes without converting the formats and computes destination page offsets using the sender's item length. Decode therefore interprets incompatible KV bytes as FlashMLA's packed layout. Captured inputs in the reproduction contained negative quantization scales, and layer-level assertions caught NaNs in early attention computation.

## Modifications

- Explicitly select `--dsa-prefill-backend flashmla_kv` for this test's prefill worker so its KV layout matches decode.
- Document why the backend must be explicit.
- Remove both the CI registry `disabled` marker and the class-level `unittest.skip` added in #44192, restoring the registered 8-GPU B300 suite and selective reruns with the corrected KV layout.

## Accuracy Tests

Real-weight end-to-end reproduction on 4 x GB300, using `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`, prefill TP2, decode TP2 + attention DP2, Mooncake TCP, FlashInfer 0.7.1, and Mooncake 0.3.13.post1. The experiment used main at `4560da58eebe5660dc2e8833178351085d6f9dac`.

Retained FP8 KV, EAGLE MTP (3 steps, top-k 1, 4 draft tokens), rejection sampling, HiSparse (top_k=2048, device_buffer_size=4096, host_to_device_ratio=5), and CUDA Graph.

| Configuration | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Original backend defaults, real 24-shot GSM8K prompt | First 4,198-token request reproduces `NaN detected! verify: target model logits` |
| Original layout mismatch with CUDA Graph disabled | Also fails with an early attention NaN |
| Both workers using the FlashMLA KV layout, CUDA Graph enabled, diagnostic instrumentation removed | The same request succeeds; another 16 GSM8K requests at concurrency 8 all succeed, each generating 64 tokens; harness exits 0 |

The aligned experiment explicitly set both DSA backend flags to `flashmla_kv`; on the prefill worker, `calculate_mla_kv_cache_dim` determines the pool layout from the active prefill backend. This patch sets that active backend; the test already explicitly configures the decode worker's active backend.

These are reproduction and NaN-regression checks, not a full GSM8K accuracy or speculative acceptance-length evaluation. The complete 500-question suite, long-context cases, and original 8 x B300 / RDMA topology have not been rerun. Eight-GPU capacity was unavailable during the investigation.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance benchmark was run. This change updates test configuration.

## Checklist

- [x] Follow the repository's existing formatting and code style; `git diff --check` passes.
- [x] Provide real-weight E2E reproduction and comparison results above.
- [ ] Validate the re-enabled full registered suite on 8 x B300 in PR CI.

title: [Fix] flux: use true_cfg_scale as the FLUX CFG weight
author: fusheng-ji
body:
## Motivation

Native FLUX turns on true CFG when `true_cfg_scale` is set with a negative prompt, but then combines the two branches with `guidance_scale`. A request with `true_cfg_scale=4` and the default `guidance_scale=3.5` therefore runs CFG at 3.5, unlike diffusers `FluxPipeline`, where `true_cfg_scale` is the CFG weight and `guidance_scale` only feeds the distilled guidance embedding.

## Modifications

`FluxPipelineConfig.get_classifier_free_guidance_scale` returns `true_cfg_scale` when it is set, the same override Qwen-Image already has. Without `true_cfg_scale`, the weight is still `guidance_scale`, so requests that do not set it are unchanged. FLUX.2 inherits the override.

Docs: the FLUX cookbook gains a "Negative prompts (true CFG)" section (which flag sets the CFG weight, an example, and the over-exposure seen at higher weights), and the `--true-cfg-scale` help now names FLUX.1.

## Accuracy Tests

Unit: `test_flux_true_cfg_scale.py` (new), `test_cfg_policy.py`, `test_cfg_gating.py`: 14 passed.

Against diffusers `FluxPipeline` on FLUX.1-dev (B200, seed 42, four prompts, guidance 3.5, BF16, both uncached), median over prompts:

| Setting | `main` vs diffusers | this PR vs diffusers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1024x1024, 50 steps, no true CFG | 25.04 dB / LPIPS 0.076 | identical to `main` |
| 512x512, 20 steps, no true CFG | 29.94 dB / LPIPS 0.020 | identical to `main` |
| 512x512, 20 steps, `true_cfg_scale=4` | 19.92 dB / LPIPS 0.165 | 26.67 dB / LPIPS 0.064 |
| 512x512, 50 steps, `true_cfg_scale=4` | 8.89 dB / LPIPS 0.589 | 17.53 dB / LPIPS 0.218 |

At 50 steps the strongly guided trajectory amplifies small numerical differences, so a gap to diffusers remains.

Note: true CFG 4 on top of FLUX.1-dev's distilled guidance (3.5) over-exposes images in diffusers as well (about 41-43% of pixels clipped to 0 or 255, up to 82% on a bright watercolor prompt), so that is not addressed here.

Two other differences from diffusers are left unchanged:
- the guidance embedding uses the server's `embedded_cfg_scale` (3.5 for FLUX.1), not the request's `guidance_scale`;
- a negative prompt alone enables CFG at weight `guidance_scale`, while diffusers defaults to `true_cfg_scale=1` (no CFG).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No change in the amount of work: only the CFG combination weight changes.

- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

### Re-verification (2026-10-15)

On the current head: `test_flux_true_cfg_scale.py`, `test_cfg_policy.py` and `test_cfg_gating.py` 14 passed, 8 subtests passed, 0 skipped; `pre-commit run --all-files` passes (Rust hooks skipped: no `cargo` here, no Rust files touched). title: [Fix] [AMD] qwen3: Fix KV cache write in the fused QK-norm + mRoPE decode path
author: jiaqiang-dot-liu
body:
## Motivation

On ROCm with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` (the default in the ROCm images), dense Qwen3-VL decode goes through `Qwen3Attention.forward_prepare_aiter_fused_mrope`, which calls aiter's `fused_qk_norm_mrope_3d_cache_pts_quant_shuffle` to run QK-norm + 3D mRoPE + the KV cache write in one kernel. That path currently produces garbage:

| `Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct`, default server args | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K (1319 questions, chat API, greedy) | **0.005** | **0.942** |
| "What is the capital of France? Answer in one sentence." | `The capital of France's capital of France is Paris of France is Paris is Paris is …` | `The capital of France is Paris.` |
| Image with the text "MI355X 2026", a red circle and a blue square | `BasedThe text: The text: The text: The text: …` | `… The text written at the top of the image is: M1355X 2026 … Left Shape: A solid red circle. Right Shape: A solid blue square.` |

**Root cause.** Since ROCm/aiter#4531 (in the AITER pin since #37784), the kernel reads `k_cache` / `v_cache` strides as `(block, token, head, head_dim)`: dim 1 is the per-token stride and dim 2 the per-head stride. `Qwen3Attention` passes the NHD pool buffers `(slots, num_kv_heads, head_dim)`, whose dim-1 / dim-2 strides are `head_dim` / `1`, so the K/V of slot `s`, head `h` is written at element offset `s * head_dim + h` instead of `(s * num_kv_heads + h) * head_dim`. The decode token's own slot is not written by it, and other slots — including the prompt KV of running requests — are overwritten. Nothing faults and throughput is unchanged, so performance runs do not notice. Prefill uses the unfused path, which is why the first token is still sensible.

Affected: dense Qwen3-VL (`Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration`) on ROCm with the default aiter attention backend. Qwen3-VL-MoE uses `Qwen3MoeAttention` and does not take this path; the AMD VLM accuracy test runs `Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct`, which is why CI did not catch it.

The same path also cast `cos_sin_cache` to the activation dtype on every layer of every decode step. On HIP that cache is kept in fp32, and for Qwen3-VL-8B (`max_position_embeddings = 262144`) it is 128 MiB, so each step moved about 6.75 GiB (36 layers × 128 MiB read + 64 MiB write) just to recreate the same bf16 table.

## Modifications

- `aiter_fused_qk_norm_rope_set_kv` (new, `models/qwen3.py`) holds the kernel call and passes the NHD buffers as one-slot blocks, `k_cache.unsqueeze(1)` → `(slots, 1, num_kv_heads, head_dim)` with `block_size = 0`, which gives the kernel the token stride `num_kv_heads * head_dim` and the head stride `head_dim`.
- `Qwen3Attention.forward` takes the fused path only when the pool buffer is that 3D NHD layout in the activation dtype. The kernel's quantized write uses a fixed per-tensor scale of 1.0 rather than the layer's `k_scale` / `v_scale`, and the HND and `vectorized_5d` layouts are not NHD; those configurations use the unfused path.
- `RotaryEmbedding.cos_sin_cache_as(dtype)` returns `cos_sin_cache` in `dtype` and reuses the cast copy until `cos_sin_cache` is replaced (`_ensure_cos_sin_cache_length`, device moves). The first call happens in the eager warmup before CUDA graph capture, so the captured graphs contain no cast.
- `test/registered/amd/test_qwen3_aiter_fused_qk_norm_rope.py` calls the helper with NHD buffers and checks q and the K/V written at `out_cache_loc` against `RMSNorm.forward_native` + `MRotaryEmbedding.forward_native`, that no other slot is written, and the `cos_sin_cache_as` reuse/invalidation. With the 3D buffers passed as before, 98% of the written K elements mismatch; with this PR it passes.

## Accuracy Tests

MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.0, torch 2.9.1, Triton 3.7.0, transformers 5.19.0, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, default server args (attention backend resolves to `aiter`, decode CUDA graphs on). The pinned AITER `e7d2453f` has the same stride handling in both fused kernels.

**Unit test.** `test/registered/amd/test_qwen3_aiter_fused_qk_norm_rope.py`: 2 passed, 8 subtests passed.

**`Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct`, end to end:** see the table above. GSM8K via `python -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 1319 --max-tokens 2048`; the text and image prompts are single chat requests at temperature 0.

Dense Qwen3 (plain RoPE) does not take this path and is unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct`, `python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random-ids --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 --random-range-ratio 1.0`, `--num-prompts = max(16, 4 × concurrency)`, prefix cache flushed before each run, one benchmark at a time. Both servers generate the same number of tokens per request, so the comparison holds even though the `main` output is wrong.

| Concurrency | Median TPOT `main` (ms) | Median TPOT this PR (ms) | Delta | Output throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5.960 | 4.818 | **−19.2%** | +14.5% |
| 8 | 6.782 | 5.462 | **−19.5%** | +22.5% |
| 32 | 8.797 | 7.490 | **−14.9%** | +15.9% |
| 64 | 12.359 | 11.190 | −9.5% | +9.2% |

The saving is a roughly constant 1.1–1.3 ms per step across concurrencies, the order expected for the ~6.75 GiB per-step `cos_sin_cache` cast that is no longer launched.

## Reproduce

```bash
MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path $MODEL --port 30000
python -m sglang.test.run_eval --port 30000 --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 1319 --max-tokens 2048
python -m pytest test/registered/amd/test_qwen3_aiter_fused_qk_norm_rope.py
```

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — no user-facing behaviour change, nothing to document.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [Fix] moe: Fix --enable-fused-moe-sum-all-reduce outside CUDA and with LoRA hooks
author: ZhengGong-amd
body:
## Motivation

With `--enable-fused-moe-sum-all-reduce` (#19672) the Triton down GEMM sums the experts into `out_hidden_states` and leaves `intermediate_cache3` unwritten, but `_fused_moe_kernel_sequence` honours that only under `_is_cuda or _is_musa` and ignores LoRA's `after_down` hook; this PR handles the fused case before the platform dispatch and disables the fusion when `hooks.after_down` is set.

On HIP, XPU and the fallback, the combine reduces the unwritten `intermediate_cache3` over the result. On every platform the LoRA down delta, added to `intermediate_cache3`, is dropped. On ROCm every Triton-runner MoE layer with `topk > 2` breaks; GSM8K is 0 % for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Kimi-Linear-48B with `--moe-runner-backend triton`, and for GLM-5.3, MiniMax-M2.7 and Qwen3-Next/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next FP8 with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0`. gemma-4-26B-A4B (I=704) runs Triton by default, so the flag alone breaks it.

## Modifications

- In the fused case, apply `routed_scaling_factor` as the platform's unfused combine does: everywhere except the aiter path, whose `moe_sum` skips it too. The CUDA/MUSA code is moved, not changed.
- An empty `LoRAHooks()` (LoRA enabled, no active adapter) keeps the fusion on.
- Add `TestFusedMoeSumAllReduce`: flag-on output must match flag-off and the fused kernel launch is asserted, for routed scale None/2.5 with no hooks, empty hooks or an `after_down` hook. Without the LoRA guard the 6 `after_down` cases fail with ~20 % relative error.

## Accuracy Tests

On MI355X at main `b960aa903a`, `TestFusedMoeSumAllReduce` passes with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0` and `=1` (main fails 18/18 in both), as does the rest of `test_fused_moe.py`.

`sgl-eval` gsm8k, temperature 0, MI355X. First two rows: 1319 items, Triton runner, main flag-off run twice as noise control. Rest: 200 items, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0`, `auto` resolves to Triton:

| model | main off | main on | this PR, on |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | 94.09 / 94.16 | 0.00 | 94.31 |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B (routed scale 2.45) | 91.28 / 91.96 | 0.00 | 92.42 |
| GLM-5.3 FP8, TP4 | 51.5¹ | 0.0 | 49.0 |
| MiniMax-M2.7, TP2 | 96.0 | 0.0 | 96.0 |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 | 96.5 | 0.0 | 96.0 |
| Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-FP8 | 96.0 | 0.0 | 96.0 |

¹ GLM-5.3 loops on most answers in this aiter-off config regardless of the flag; the gap is within n=200 noise.

Block-FP8 MoE with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` and `--moe-runner-backend triton` is broken on main even flag-off; #41636 fixes that separately.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speed change is intended. gemma-4-26B-A4B-it, cookbook command, flag off, TP1, `sglang.benchmark.serving` random 1937/389, 307 prompts, concurrency 61, median of runs 2–4 of 4: total 13870.9 → 13935.4 tok/s (+0.5 %), TTFT and TPOT flat. With the flag on, gemma-4 runs ~60 % below its flag-off throughput on gfx950 (`acq_rel` atomics), so the flag should stay off on ROCm.

title: [Fix] sglang-processor: Send watermark only when the request sets it
author: ShangmingCai
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #44243, merging into its branch.

#44243 adds `"watermark": request.watermark` to the `/generate` sampling params for chat and completions, so every lowered request now carries `"watermark": null`. The engine side of `watermark` (#37577) merged on 2026-10-14. Older engines build `SamplingParams(**sampling_kwargs)` strictly (a msgspec struct, and since #41585 the `/generate` contract also rejects unknown sampling keys), so they raise:

```
TypeError: Unexpected keyword argument 'watermark'
```

sgl-router lowers OpenAI completions (and chats for verified renderers) to `/generate` under the default `--chat-routing legacy`, with no engine version gate. A router built from #44243 therefore fails every lowered request against any engine older than #37577, which is the usual state during a router-first rollout.

Reproduced on an H200 devbox: engine `lmsysorg/sglang:latest` (v0.5.21, no `watermark` field) serving Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, with sgl-router built from each tree and the default routing:

| sgl-router | unary `/v1/completions` | streaming `/v1/completions` | engine `TypeError`s |
|---|---|---|---|
| main before #44243 (`6daae9c98ec`) | 200 | 200 | 0 |
| #44243 (`2bbcbbef6d`) | 500 | empty reply | 2 |
| #44243 + this PR | 200 | 200 | 0 |

## Modifications

`openai/chat.rs`, `openai/completions.rs`: put `watermark` into `sampling_params` only when the request sets it. Leaving it out is equivalent for the engine, whose default is the same `None`. A request that does set `watermark` is still forwarded and validated by the engine, as in #44243.

## Accuracy Tests

- `cargo test -p sglang-processor --all-features` passes with no skipped cases, including #44243's synthetic `watermark` cases (GLM-5.3 chat, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 completions). The parity test drops default-valued keys before comparing bodies, so the fixtures need no change.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p sglang-processor --all-targets --all-features -D warnings` are clean.
- The devbox run above.

## Note for #44243 (not in this PR)

#44243 is 3+ commits behind main. Merged with current main, `openai_parity` fails on `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B "chat"`: the `qwen3.8-27b.json` fixture from #43689 was recorded before #43027, so it still expects `"tool_calls": null`. This PR also removes the extra `"watermark": null` body diff that fixture would otherwise show, but the fixture still needs regenerating from Python on main after a rebase.

title: [Fix] diffusion: Fix VMoBA chunk selection bugs
author: OnePunchMonk
body:
## Summary
Fixes several selection bugs in `vmoba_attn/vmoba/vmoba.py`, each reproduced on main first.

- `topk` + `head_global` never applied `valid_gate_mask`, so topk could pick -inf entries from other sequences in the batch.
- The "select everything" fallback used `full_like(any_cond, C-1)`, which is bool, so the cutoff became 1 (`query_head`, `block`). Now `torch.full(..., dtype=torch.long)`.
- `threshold` + `overall` raised `IndexError` (argmax on empty tensor) when every sequence fits in one chunk. Now returns the self-chunk mask early.
- When nothing was selected, the code ran dense attention over the whole sequence. It now attends within the self chunk (`cu_chunk`).
- Threshold mode always added one extra chunk even when the self chunk already met the threshold. Cutoff is now -1 in that case (all four modes).
- Zero-length sequences corrupted the chunk layout. The caller drops them, `calc_chunks` raises on them.
- Removed `lru_cache` on `calc_chunks` (tensor-identity key, stale on in-place updates). Fixed the topk/threshold error messages.

Not included: the `kernel.attn.vmoba_attn` import path (needs a packaging decision) and host-sync cleanup.

## Tests
New `tests/test_vmoba_selection.py`, CPU only, fakes only the flash-attn kernel. 13 of 16 fail on main, 16 pass with this change. `black` clean. Independent review found no blocking issues.

## Limitations
No GPU end-to-end run, so flash-attn kernel integration is untested.

title: [Fix] sgl-router: Receive kv-indexer-bridge event batches outside tokio's coop budget
author: lixiufei-leo
body:
## Motivation

`kv-indexer-bridge` never finishes a ZMQ batch over about 1 MiB: it spins at 100% CPU, events back up in the socket, and the router silently loses cache affinity. Such batches come from long contexts with large pages, since every `BlockStored` carries its `token_ids` (e.g. 1,800 events with 256 tokens each is ~1.4 MB).

zeromq's fair queue re-polls a woken stream within the same poll. Once tokio's cooperative budget runs out mid-message, each read returns `Pending` and wakes itself at once, so the task never yields and the budget never resets.

## Modifications

- Receive batches with `tokio::task::unconstrained`.

## Speed Tests

One bridge and one indexer, 54,000 events (30 batches of 1,800) published by pyzmq:

| | with 256 token ids (40 MB) | without token ids (4.9 MB) |
|---|---|---|
| main | not indexed after 600 s | 0.11 s |
| this PR | 0.22 s | 0.11 s |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).

title: [Fix] Z-Image: Synchronize device after warmup request
author: Allor-maker
body:
## Motivation

Since #44069 removed the per-forward host sync in the Z-Image DiT, the request-mode warmup finishes on the host while its DiT step and decode are still queued on the device. The warmup saves no output, so nothing waits for that work. The next request's first blocking op, the text-encoder offload in TextEncodingStage, waits for it instead. This fails the NPU CI perf check for z_image_t2i_1npu:

TextEncodingStage: ~350 ms → ~600 ms on A3; limit 442 ms.
With SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1 the regression disappears

## Modifications

`gpu_worker.py`: synchronize the device at the end of a warmup request in _finalize_output_batch. The warmup's device work then completes inside the warmup instead of being billed to the next request. Regular requests are unaffected

title: [Fix] lora: Load fused-module members into their own buffer slots
author: yueming-yuan
body:
## Motivation

An adapter may target any subset of the members SGLang packs into one fused LoRA module: `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` -> `qkv_proj`, `gate_proj`/`up_proj` -> `gate_up_proj`, `q_a_proj`/`kv_a_proj_with_mqa` -> `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa`, Inkling `wq_du`/`wk_dv`/`wv_dv`/`wr_du` -> `qkvr`. The loader concatenated the members into the fused key at normalization time, assuming specific members are present. On Qwen3-0.6B with `sglang-miles`:

| adapter targets | before |
|---|---|
| q, o | `KeyError: ...self_attn.v_proj.lora_A.weight` |
| k, v | `ValueError: Cannot find target module name` |
| up, down | `ValueError: Cannot find target module name` |

A trainer could only work around this by exporting zero A/B pairs for untrained members, with widths computed from its own copy of the engine's layout.

## Modifications

Members are no longer concatenated in `LoRAAdapter`. The memory pool writes each member into its own slot of the fused buffer:

- A: member `i` goes to rows `[i*r, (i+1)*r)`; B: member `i` goes to the member's row range of the local output. Absent members are left zero, so the fused module computes exactly the partial adapter.
- The per-member geometry (full rows, TP-local offsets, TP slice incl. KV-head replication and MLA `first_output_dim`) comes from the `*WithLoRA` wrapper that already owns the fused layout: `lora_b_member_full_rows()`, `lora_b_member_local_offsets()`, `slice_lora_b_member()`. `slice_lora_b_weights` is rebuilt from the same methods, so there is one definition per wrapper. `packed_modules_mapping` is not used; it is absent on Llama/Qwen2/Qwen3 and does not match the LoRA modules on Qwen3.5 / NemotronH.
- `LORA_FUSED_MEMBERS` in `lora/utils.py` is the single member table; `params_mapping` and `stacked_rank` derive from it.
- An adapter that already carries the fused key (`qkv_proj`, `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa`, ...) is split by the same geometry; carrying both the fused and the per-member form is rejected.
- MoE (routed / shared expert) gate/up keep the existing stacked path.

Behavior: an adapter covering all members loads byte-identical buffers to the old concatenating loader (unit test, all TP ranks, `max_lora_rank` = r and r+1). Partial adapters that raised before now load. An MLA adapter with a fused `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` key is newly accepted.

## Tests

`test/registered/unit/lora/test_lora_fused_member_load.py` (CPU, 37 cases) on fake QKV / MergedColumn / Inkling qkvr / MLA wrappers:

- complete adapter == old concatenating loader (oracle copied from `sglang-miles@4076a68579`), every TP rank, `max_lora_rank` in {r, r+1}
- every member subset loads, absent members are zero
- fused-key adapters (shared and stacked A) match their per-member form; fused + per-member is rejected
- `LoRAAdapter` keeps dense members separate and still stacks expert gate/up

E2E on H200, Qwen3-0.6B, r=8: each adapter is compared against the same SGLang running the PEFT-merged weights (`merge_and_unload`). Mean |logprob diff|, rows = LoRA run, columns = merged model:

| | full | q_o | k_v | up_down |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| full | **0.046** | 0.610 | 0.545 | 0.650 |
| q_o | 0.613 | **0.038** | 0.212 | 0.243 |
| k_v | 0.543 | 0.226 | **0.045** | 0.236 |
| up_down | 0.649 | 0.258 | 0.241 | **0.037** |

The diagonal is bf16 rounding of the merged weights; every LoRA run matches only its own merged model. The full adapter's logprobs are identical (`==`) to `sglang-miles` before this change.

## Not in this PR

Fused modules whose members are not plain row blocks of B, and MoE gate/up, keep the current path: GDN `in_proj_qkvz` / `in_proj_ba`, Mamba `in_proj`, routed/shared-expert `gate_up_proj`.

## Consumer

radixark/miles#4101 drops the trainer-side zero-fill and exports only the trained members.

title: [Fix] dsv41: Bound MoE routing to live SWA graph-tail rows
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

During DeepSeek V4.1 bounded decoder SWA replay inside a breakable prefill graph, attention switches to the live tail while MoE can retain the full-prefill GPU row bound. A 128-row tail can therefore expose a routing bound of 16,384 rows.

## Modifications

Bind the global and local GPU routing counts to a persistent tail scalar while the late layers run. Clamp the existing count so an idle DP peer stays at zero, then restore the original CPU count and GPU tensor references on exit. Reuse the scalar across replays so captured MoE kernels retain a stable address.

This is an independent fix against main, separated from the MegaAttention integration in #43922.

## Accuracy Tests

- The same routing method implementations previously passed eight CUDA graph checks across two GB300s, covering counts 128, 7, idle 0, and 256. Those checks ran on the optimization branch; AST comparison confirms both extracted routing methods are identical here.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

A separate end-to-end throughput benefit has not been measured for this fix alone. The earlier AgentX comparison combined it with the Mega query-layout optimization. Eager tails already use compact tensors; this fix addresses the padded graph-tail path.

title: [Fix] scheduler: Drop finished requests from the running batch before every admission
author: hnyls2002
body:
- Drop finished requests from `running_batch` in `get_next_batch_to_run` on every step, after the `last_batch` merge, and reopen admission (`batch_is_full = False`) when that shrinks the batch. This replaces the prefill-only special case.
- Cause: under overlap, a prefill batch merges into `running_batch` before its result marks the requests that finish at prefill (`max_new_tokens=1`, or a stop on the first token). The only other cleanup, `update_running_batch`, runs on decode steps, which never come while chunked prefill keeps producing batches, so `#running-req`, `num_running_reqs`, and `/v1/loads` grow for the whole run.
- Add a CPU unit test that fails on main, and give two existing scheduler test fixtures the `batch_size` / `filter_batch` the new code reads.

Behavior change: finished requests now leave the running batch before admission on every step, so a workload whose running batch is full can admit a waiting request one step earlier than on main.

Fixes #43961; supersedes #43960.

<!-- pr-states:start -->

title: [Fix] diffusion: Log LoRA merge decisions only on first evaluation
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Automatic LoRA merging caches the rounding-loss estimate, but currently repeats the same INFO message whenever a cached adapter configuration is evaluated again. Reactivating adapters can therefore emit identical explanations without a new decision.

## Modifications

- Emit the existing rank-zero diagnostic only when populating the rounding-loss cache.
- Preserve the first explanation for each newly evaluated configuration, including changed adapter strengths.
- Add parametrized coverage for cache hits, configuration changes, both ranks, and high, low, or unavailable loss estimates.

This does not change the merge threshold, adapter weights, or inference kernels, and introduces no additional deduplication state.

## Accuracy Tests

No model-output change is intended. Regression coverage is in `test_lora_auto_merge_rounding.py`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No inference speedup is claimed; this is a log-hygiene change.

title: [Fix] scheduler: Keep PD decode non-idle while deferred KV releases are held
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

On PD decode, a failed or aborted transfer is held for deferred release (#35049, on by default). Its KV pages, request row, tree lock and metadata slot stay with it until every prefill rank acks that its writes drained, or until the timeout (30 s by default).

`Scheduler.is_fully_idle` never looks at these holds. Its decode branch checks the prealloc, retracted and transfer queues, but a held request has already left the transfer queue. So `flush_cache` runs while a hold is outstanding:

1. The flush clears the tree, the request pool and the allocator. The held pages go back to the free list.
2. When the hold resolves, `_do_release` → `release_kv_cache` frees the same pages again.
3. The allocator now has every one of those pages twice. Two later requests get the same pages and overwrite each other's KV.
4. With the decode radix cache on, the held `req.lock` points at a node of the old tree.
5. If the prefill write was still landing, which is always the case for a room #43719 poisons, it lands on pages that already have a new owner.

RL rollouts hit this without any unusual timing. The flow is abort, `pause_generation`, then `update_weights(flush_cache=True)`. While paused, the decode loop skips `process_decode_queue`, so nothing resolves the holds before the flush.

The idle leak check already knew about these holds and skipped itself while they were pending. Only the flush gate was missing.

## Modifications

- In `is_fully_idle`, the decode branch now requires `has_pending_deferred_releases()` to be False.

The same gate also covers attach / detach of a storage backend and `release_memory_occupation`. The last of these currently drops held entries and pauses KV memory while a prefill write may still be landing.

## Tests

- No new unit test. The existing retracted-queue idle test stubs the transfer queue with a `SimpleNamespace`, which now also needs `has_pending_deferred_releases`.
- `test_decode_queue_cleanup.py` passes (14 tests).
- Allocator-level repro on an H200, with the real `is_fully_idle`, the real `DecodeTransferQueue` defer / resolve and a real allocator. On main, a flush followed by the deferred release raised available pages above the pool total (272 of 256), and one alloc returned 16 pages twice. With this change the flush is refused, and the pool returns to 256 with no duplicates.

Related: #36869 rewrites `is_fully_idle` as `not_idle_reasons()`. When it rebases, this condition becomes one more `require_empty` entry.

title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] allreduce-fusion: Decline MNNVL fusion across NVLink cliques
author: wenscarl
body:
## Motivation

On a multi-node TP group whose GPUs are in different NVLink cliques (e.g. a SLURM job placed across topology blocks), MNNVL allreduce fusion fails at workspace creation with `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE`. SGLang then logs one warning and silently falls back to NCCL ring allreduce. On our TP8 (2 nodes x 4 GPUs) decode workload this raised the verify step from 8.756 ms to 31.975 ms (3.65x), and AllReduce from 14.3% to 72.6% of the step, with no error.

Root cause: the fabric-handle decision uses `is_mnnvl_fabric_supported(device)`, a per-GPU query that is True on every rank, while whether rank A can import rank B's fabric handle is a property of the group. The group-aware `is_one_nvlink_clique` already exists (used by custom-AR v2) but the fusion path never called it.

Evidence: NVML probe on two nodes in different NVLink blocks gives different `clusterUuid`, same `cliqueId` (65534), and `is_mnnvl_fabric_supported` True on both. TP8 jobs placed inside one block enable fusion normally (`backend=mnnvl, world_size=8`).

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/layers/flashinfer_comm_fusion.py`, `FlashInferWorkspaceManager.initialize`:
- For `backend == "mnnvl"` and a group that spans nodes, run `is_one_nvlink_clique` once (all ranks reach it, result cached on the manager so re-creation does not issue a second collective). If False: set `_flashinfer_allreduce_unavailable`, warn with the topology reason, and return before any CUDA allocation. No POSIX-FD fallback (host-local handles cannot work across nodes).
- If `INVALID_HANDLE` is still hit on a cross-node group, the warning now carries a topology hint.
- The success log includes `one_nvlink_clique=...`.

`_make_flashinfer_workspace_allocation_prop` is intentionally untouched: it is only the memory-sizing preflight, not the path that throws.

## Behavior before / after

Same TP8 job (2 nodes x 4 GPUs) placed across two NVLink blocks.

**Before**
```
[TP0] [SymmDeviceMemory] Rank: 0, Group size: 8, device_idx: 0, Signal pad offset: 150994944
[TP0] Failed to initialize FlashInfer workspace (backend=mnnvl): CUDA error code=400(b'CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE'). Disabling flashinfer allreduce fusion permanently.
```
Only a raw CUDA code, no cause, raised after allocation started. The run then completes with no error on `ncclDevKernel_AllReduce_Sum_bf16_RING_LL`.

**After**
```
[TP0] FlashInfer AllReduce fusion disabled: the 8 ranks of this group span more than one NVLink clique, which the MNNVL backend does not support. On SLURM this usually means the job was placed across topology blocks; set --segment equal to --nodes.
```
Names the cause and the fix; no `SymmDeviceMemory` allocation and no `CUDA error code=400`. The NCCL fallback still happens, but is now visible and actionable.

**Same job inside one NVLink block (unchanged behavior, one new field)**
```
FlashInfer AllReduce Fusion enabled and workspace initialized: backend=mnnvl, rank=0, world_size=8, one_nvlink_clique=True, max_token_num=..., hidden_dim=...
```

The "before" log is from a production run; the "after" text is the new warning string, covered by `test_declines_when_not_one_clique`. A real cross-block cluster run is not included.

## Accuracy / Tests

Unit tests in `test/registered/unit/layers/test_flashinfer_comm_fusion.py` (`TestMnnvlCliqueGate`): declines without creating a workspace and warns "NVLink clique"; proceeds when one clique; clique collective runs exactly once across a re-create. `pytest test/registered/unit/layers/test_flashinfer_comm_fusion.py`: 24 passed.

This PR is irrelevant to any compute/accuracy.

title: [Fix] scheduler: Count a request's held req_to_token row once at admission
author: hnyls2002
body:
- Count a request that already holds a `req_to_token` row once at admission. Such a request (a continuing chunked prefill, a streaming-session borrow, a dLLM staging request) is in `can_run_list`, and its row is already excluded from `req_to_token_pool.available_size()`, so the gate `len(can_run_list) >= get_num_allocatable_reqs(...)` counted it twice and declared the batch full with a row still free.
- `get_num_allocatable_reqs` takes `num_held_rows` and adds those rows back to the pool term only; the `pp_max_micro_batch_size` term still counts every request. The main gate, the PD-prefill gate, and the dLLM gate pass `sum(r.kv.holds_kv for r in adder.can_run_list)`.
- Under chunked prefill this capped the running batch at `max_running_requests - 1`, and when the final chunk's pass set `batch_is_full`, nothing cleared it until a request finished, so the waiting queue starved meanwhile.
- Fix two stale comments: a chunked request keeps its row across chunks (no longer "just released"), and `update_running_batch` is no longer the only other place that clears `batch_is_full`.
- Add a CPU unit test that drives `_get_new_batch_prefill_raw` with a final chunk, two running requests, and one free row, in normal and PD-prefill mode; it fails on main.

Behavior change: a prefill pass whose batch already contains a row-holding request now admits one more request per held row; with no such request, admission is unchanged.

Fixes #38118, fixes #35537; supersedes #30295, which found the chunked-prefill case.

title: [Fix] [AMD] mori: Look up elided DSA state entries by the paired dst index
author: Lzy17
body:
## Motivation

#41769 added `is_elided_entry(src_len, dst_lens, dst_index)` to mori's `_send_swa_dsa_state`, and #37358 changed the same loop to `for i, j in pairs`. The merged loop still passes `i`, but `dst_state_item_lens` is in decode entry order, like `dst_state_mem_descs[j]`.

When a prefill PP stage pairs with decode entries at different positions (`i != j`), the check reads the wrong decode entry. It either skips an entry that must be sent (decode never gets that layer's index-K), or sends to an elided entry whose descriptor is `None`. PP-equal setups and runs without index-K elision are not affected.

`i != j` needs per-layer ids for the DSA state entries. `append_state_component(..., StateType.DSA, ...)` does not register them today, so PP-mismatched DSA state currently stops earlier with "PP-heterogeneous transfer requires layer ids on both peers" (seen with GLM-5.2-MXFP4, prefill PP2 to decode TP). This change is therefore not reachable yet; it keeps the loop correct for when layer ids are registered.

nixl and mooncake already index by the paired dst entry.

## Modifications

- mori: pass `j` to `is_elided_entry`.
- Two unit tests for a PP prefill stage against full-model decode, with the elided decode entry before and after the paired one.

## Testing

`test_mori_backend_basic.py` in `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.21-rocm10-mi35x-20261013` on an MI355X node:

- with this change: 6 passed
- same tree with the one-character fix reverted: 2 failed (both new tests), 4 passed

Drafted with Claude Code.

title: [Fix] imports: Bind FlashInfer lazily at four import sites so the server starts without it
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

Four modules import FlashInfer at module level behind `is_cuda()` alone: `layers/sampler.py`, `speculative/dflash_utils.py`, `layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py` and `layers/attention/vision.py`. Importing `sglang.srt.entrypoints.http_server` reaches all four, so a CUDA environment without FlashInfer fails at import time before any backend is chosen:

```
File ".../sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py", line 255, in <module>
    from flashinfer import bmm_fp8 as _raw_bmm_fp8_batched
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'flashinfer'
```

Every other FlashInfer-dependent path is already selected at runtime (attention backend, sampling backend, the per-tensor fp8 helper guarded by `is_flashinfer_available()`); these four were the remaining hard import-time dependencies.

## Modifications

- Replace the four eager imports with `LazyImport` from `sglang.utils`, which resolves the attribute on first call. With FlashInfer installed the bound names resolve to the same objects (checked with `is` for all six names), so behaviour is unchanged. Without it the server imports and starts, the sampling backend defaults to `pytorch` as it already does when FlashInfer is absent, and a path that really needs FlashInfer still raises `ModuleNotFoundError` at the call instead of at import.
- Add `test/registered/unit/test_import_without_flashinfer.py` (base-b, 1-gpu-small): imports the HTTP entrypoint in a subprocess with `flashinfer` blocked in `sys.modules`. It fails on current main at the `fp8_utils` import and passes with this change.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no numerics change. The lazily bound names are the same FlashInfer functions once resolved.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: `LazyImport.__call__` adds one attribute lookup per call after the first resolution; the four names are called from already Python-dispatched paths.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes, including `check-no-bare-pytest-main` and `check-registered-tests`.
