title: [Feat] [NPU] scheduler: align cross-request ViT batching with CUDA and fix NPU graph buffer ownership
author: Suxing224
body:
[**Related issue**: [#25598 — NPU Development Roadmap 2026 H2](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/25598) 

---

## Motivation

NPU currently encodes per-image cache misses separately for each request. Enable the existing CUDA cross-request batching path on NPU, so eligible cache misses from multiple requests can be encoded together, without introducing a new environment variable. Retain the existing per-request behavior on HIP/XPU.

Cross-request batching also requires cached embeddings to remain valid after later ViT invocations. The NPU graph runner must preserve caller inputs and returned embeddings across capture, replay, and reuse of the shared graph pool.

## Modifications

1. **Scheduler:** remove NPU from the per-request fallback condition so eligible cache misses follow the existing CUDA batching path. Keep deduplication, cache refill, and request-order assembly. HIP/XPU retain the per-request path. No new environment variable or model capability flag is introduced.
2. **NPU graph ownership:** give captured inputs and returned embeddings independent storage where needed, preventing in-place vision blocks and later graph executions from overwriting caller inputs or retained embeddings.
3. **Regression tests:** cover cross-request merge/split behavior and graph input/output ownership, plus NPU image association, multi-image ordering and embedding-cache reuse. The block/deepstack/merger computation and graph lifecycle retain the main implementation.

## Unit tests and static checks

| Test | Result |
|---|---:|
| Chunked multimodal embedding unit tests | Included in combined run: 32 passed |
| NPU ViT graph runner unit tests | Included in combined run: 1 passed |
| CUDA ViT graph runner unit tests | Included in combined run: 6 passed (CPU test; no CUDA hardware validation) |
| Combined current-runner test command | 39 passed, 15 warnings, 13.58s |

<details>
<summary>Execution command and output summary</summary>

```bash
python -m pytest test/registered/chunked_prefill/test_mm_chunked_embedding_unit.py test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_vit_npu_graph_runner.py test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_vit_cuda_graph_runner.py -q
# 39 passed, 15 warnings, 13.58s

python -m py_compile \
  python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/graph_runner/vit_npu_graph_runner.py \
  test/registered/chunked_prefill/test_mm_chunked_embedding_unit.py \
  test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_vit_npu_graph_runner.py
git diff --check
# Exit 0 for both checks.
```

</details>

The embedding tests exercise merge/split, deduplication, cache refill and request ordering. The NPU runner test covers attention-boundary keys and independent input/output storage. These tests include mocked device boundaries; real-device checks are described separately.

author: gkswns0531
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Speculative decoding relocates KV rows with `move_kv_cache`: accepted draft tokens are moved into place after verification (`spec_utils.py`, EAGLE with topk > 1 and NGRAM), and with page_size > 1 the prefix tail page is copied to each branch (`eagle_worker_common.py`). `MLATokenToKVPoolFP4` inherits `MLATokenToKVPool.move_kv_cache` (#26982), which copies `kv_buffer` rows only. Each moved FP4 latent is then dequantized with whatever block scales were left at its target slot, typically a rejected draft token's, and nothing reports an error.

The other quantized pools already move scales with their data (`MHATokenToKVPool`, `MHATokenToKVPoolMXFP8`, `DSATokenToKVPool`).

## Modifications

- `MLATokenToKVPoolFP4.move_kv_cache`: run the MLA move for the latent, then copy the `kv_scale_buffer` rows with the same indices.
- `test_quantized_kv_pool.py`: a CPU `MLATokenToKVPoolFP4` test that moves two slots and checks that data and scales arrive in every layer.

Out of scope: other methods inherited from `MLATokenToKVPool` also handle `kv_buffer` only (`get_cpu_copy`/`load_cpu_copy`, `get_contiguous_buf_infos`, the HiCache host pool, `get_kv_size_bytes`). As with MXFP8 (#35888, #35718), each needs its own PR.

## Accuracy Tests

Found by code inspection and verified at the unit level; not reproduced end to end, which needs an MLA model served with the FP4 KV cache and EAGLE topk > 1 or NGRAM decoding. The change only moves the scale rows of slots that the existing move already relocates.

- `python3 test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_quantized_kv_pool.py`: OK (2 tests). On main the new test fails at the scale assertion.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

One extra gather and `index_put_` per layer per move, on `[n, kv_cache_dim / 16]` uint8 rows. Only moves on an FP4 MLA cache pay it.

title: [Fix] deterministic: Validate the per-phase attention backends
author: aarnetalman
body:
## Motivation

Deterministic mode checked only `--attention-backend`, but this does not guarantee that prefill and decode attention are deterministic: `--prefill-attention-backend` and `--decode-attention-backend` override it for their phase, and they were not checked. This PR adds the check for both flags. Without it, deterministic mode could be on while prefill or decode used a backend that is not deterministic, with no warning.

For example, on MI350X this starts without an error and runs AITER's paged-attention kernels for decode, although `aiter` is not on the deterministic list:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
  --attention-backend triton --decode-attention-backend aiter \
  --enable-deterministic-inference
```

The same applies on every platform and to any backend outside the list (for example `flashmla` or `trtllm_mha` for one phase on NVIDIA).

**Which models this affects.** All of them: the check is model-independent. It matters wherever the per-phase flags are set: AMD serving configurations use them to pick AITER per phase (the MI35x configuration for Qwen3.8 sets `--prefill-attention-backend aiter --decode-attention-backend aiter`), and some model defaults set them (Kimi-K3, below). Without this check, such a configuration silently loses the deterministic guarantee.

AITER decode attention is in fact batch-invariant on gfx950; #44489 allows it there on top of this PR, with the evidence. This PR only makes deterministic mode check the per-phase flags at all.

## Modifications

- `_deterministic_attention_backend` (in `arg_groups/overrides.py`): in deterministic mode, also check `prefill_attention_backend` and `decode_attention_backend` against `DETERMINISTIC_ATTENTION_BACKEND_CHOICES` when they are set. The error names the flag and the backend.
- `test_model_overrides.py`:
  - a non-deterministic backend in either per-phase flag is refused, even when `--attention-backend` is on the list;
  - per-phase backends that are on the list are accepted.
- Unchanged:
  - deterministic mode off;
  - per-phase flags unset (the existing fallback for `--attention-backend` is untouched);
  - which backends are on the list.
- Scope: the check runs where deterministic mode is resolved, so it covers per-phase backends that are set explicitly or by model-specific defaults before it. Two later automatic choices are not covered here:
  - the NVFP4 KV-cache prefill/decode pair;
  - CuteDSL MLA's `trtllm_mla` prefill pairing.

  Both are tied to opt-in features (NVFP4 KV cache, CuteDSL MLA decode). Covering them needs a check after those passes; I'd leave that to a follow-up.
- Behaviour change: configurations that combine `--enable-deterministic-inference` with a per-phase backend outside the list now fail at startup instead of running without the deterministic guarantee. This includes model defaults that set such a backend, for example Kimi-K3's backends for decode context parallelism.

## Accuracy Tests

No numerical change: this only refuses configurations at startup.

Unit tests, `python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/test_model_overrides.py -k deterministic` (MI350X, `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm724-mi35x-20261013`): before, the new refusal test fails for both flags (2 failed, 5 passed); after, 5 passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No runtime change: the check runs once while the server arguments are resolved.

title: [Fix] utils: Allowlist torch.bcomplex32 in SafeUnpickler
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

torch 2.14 adds the `torch.bcomplex32` dtype. A pickled tensor carries its dtype as a GLOBAL opcode, so with the pinned torch 2.14.1 `safe_pickle_loads` refuses any payload that holds a bcomplex32 tensor:

```
RuntimeError: Blocked unsafe global (torch.bcomplex32) during pickle deserialization
```

Every other dtype the installed torch exposes is already in `SafeUnpickler.ALLOWED_GLOBALS`; this one was missed when the pin moved.

## Modifications

- Add `("torch", "bcomplex32")` to `SafeUnpickler.ALLOWED_GLOBALS` in `python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py`.
- Add `test_allowlist_covers_torch_dtypes_and_tensor_classes` to `test/registered/unit/utils/test_safe_unpickler.py`. It diffs the allowlist against the dtypes, storage classes and tensor classes the installed torch exposes, so the next dtype torch introduces fails a CPU unit test instead of refusing a payload at runtime.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no model or kernel code changes.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Not applicable.

title: [Fix] [AMD] mhc: Bound the Triton fused post+pre buffer cache
author: maning00
body:
## Motivation

`_get_fused_hc_post_pre_buffers` caches one set of `mhc_post_pre` buffers per distinct `num_tokens` and never evicts them. The cache was added together with the `num_tokens <= _FUSED_HC_POST_PRE_M_THRESHOLD` (64) gate in #26383, so it stayed small. Since #36871, gfx1250 runs the Triton fused post+pre for every batch size, so each distinct prefill size adds a set that is never freed. For DeepSeek-V4-Pro (hidden 7168, `hc_mult` 4), one set is about 160 KB per token, or about 330 MB at 2048 tokens; over half of that is the fp32 `acc_partial`.

On gfx1250, a DeepSeek-V4-Pro prefill server (TP4, `--chunked-prefill-size 2048`) running a multi-turn agentic workload kept growing until it hit `torch.OutOfMemoryError` about an hour in. Live-tensor scans showed a growing set of `(896, M, 24)` fp32 buffers, one for each distinct M.

## Modifications

- Cache buffers only for `num_tokens <= _FUSED_HC_POST_PRE_M_THRESHOLD`, the bound the cache was designed for. The bound applies to every caller.
- Larger calls allocate their buffers per call; they go back to the caching allocator after use. Small (decode) batches keep using cached buffers.
- Today only gfx1250 runs this path above the threshold, so that is the only place behavior changes:
  - gfx95 enters it only for up to 64 tokens, when the aiter HIP kernel declines;
  - GLM-5-Next calls the boundary only for up to 16 tokens;
  - other platforms never reach it.
- Add a CPU regression test, `TestAmdFusedMhcBufferCache`. It fails on main (sizes 65 and 2048 stay cached) and passes with this change.

## Accuracy Tests

Outputs are not expected to change. The kernel and the buffer shapes are the same; for `num_tokens > 64` the buffers are just no longer reused across calls.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not benchmarked separately. Calls above 64 tokens make six extra caching-allocator allocations, and small batches are still served from the cache.

End-to-end memory on gfx1250: DeepSeek-V4-Pro, PD disaggregation 1P (TP4) + 1D (TP4), multi-turn agentic benchmark at concurrency 64, `--mem-fraction-static 0.82`. The run used a downstream build whose `deepseek_v4_fused_mhc.py` matches main, with an env-gated variant of this change that caches up to 512 tokens.

| Prefill server | TP0 `torch.cuda.memory_allocated` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| main | 427 GiB at failure (432 GiB device) | OOM about 58 min into the benchmark |
| bounded cache | 362.6 GiB -> 363.0 GiB over 2 h 11 min | benchmark completed (3,042 requests, 0 errors) |

cc @inkcherry

title: [Fix] pp: Order output send/recv by rank parity to fix cross-node hang
author: Robin930
body:
## Motivation With pipeline parallelism across nodes, both PP stages hang once two microbatches are in flight. We hit this on a cross-node PP2 PD-prefill deployment (two 8×B300 nodes). Concurrent requests arriving a few milliseconds apart are split into different microbatches; both stages then block in `d2h_event.synchronize()`, and after 10 minutes the NCCL watchdog fails a `SEND` on the PP device group. A single request, or requests that land in the same microbatch, never trigger it. **Root cause.** On every scheduler loop iteration, `_pp_send_recv_and_preprocess_output_tensors` makes each PP rank send one microbatch's output downstream and receive another microbatch's output from upstream. The last rank returns its output to rank 0, and the other ranks relay what they received last iteration. On CUDA every rank posts its send first. The comment says that is safe because `isend` is async, but only the CPU call is async. NCCL p2p ops between a pair of ranks run in order on one stream. A send can complete before the peer posts its matching recv only while the connection's buffer has free slots: about two ops over NET/IB (any cross-node PP), and about eight over NVLink. With two microbatches in flight on PP2, the per-pair stream order is: ``` PP0: recv out(mb2) -> send relay(mb2) -> recv out(mb0) PP1: send out(mb2) -> send out(mb0) -> recv relay(mb2) ``` - PP0's `send relay(mb2)` waits for PP1's `recv relay(mb2)`. - That recv is queued behind PP1's `send out(mb0)`. - PP1's `send out(mb0)` waits for PP0's `recv out(mb0)`, which is queued behind PP0's send. Once the buffer cannot absorb the queued sends, the waits form a cycle and both GPUs hang. #30775 already moved PP + speculative decoding to parity ordering for the same reason ("enqueueing that many sends before any recv can form the same ring wait on CUDA"). XPU uses parity ordering too. The non-spec CUDA path kept send-first. Single-node CI runs over NVLink, where the larger buffer hides the problem. **NCCL-only check** (no SGLang, script below). The script replays the op order above, with each message carrying K device tensors of 2048 floats, on 2 × B300 with NCCL 2.30.7: | Transport | send-first (main) | parity (this PR) | |---|---|---| | NET/IB loopback (`NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 NCCL_SHM_DISABLE=1`) | K=2 OK, **K≥3 hangs** | OK at every K tested (up to 64) | | SHM (`NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1`) | K=8 OK, **K=16 hangs** | not tested | | NVLink (default) | K=8 OK, **K≥9 hangs** | OK at every K tested (up to 64) | ## Modifications - `scheduler_pp_mixin.py`: `_pp_send_recv_and_preprocess_output_tensors` now orders send/recv by `pp_rank` parity on every backend (even: send → recv, odd: recv → send), the order XPU and PP + spec already use. Even ranks keep their current order. Odd ranks now post their recv first, so every adjacent pair has one recv-first side. - The function is shared by `event_loop_pp`, `event_loop_pp_disagg_prefill`, and `event_loop_pp_disagg_decode`. - The NPU PP2 `batch_isend_irecv` path is unchanged. - The unused `is_xpu` import is removed and the comment is rewritten. - New CPU unit test `test/registered/unit/managers/test_pp_output_exchange_order.py`. It runs the real function for both PP2 ranks with two microbatches in flight and records the device p2p ops each rank posts. It then checks that the ops pair up under the worst case, where every send waits for the peer's recv at the head of its stream. On main the non-spec case fails and the spec case passes; with this PR both pass. ## Accuracy Tests **End-to-end reproduction** on one node with 2 × B300 (PP2), Qwen3-0.6B, `--pp-size 2 --mem-fraction-static 0.5`. NCCL is forced onto NET/IB loopback so the transport matches cross-node PP: ```bash NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 NCCL_SHM_DISABLE=1 NCCL_IB_HCA== NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX= NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME= ``` The client (script below) runs rounds of 4 concurrent `/generate` requests: - 37 / 201 / 600 / 1800 random input tokens, with `return_logprob=True`, `logprob_start_len=0`, and `max_new_tokens=8`. - Requests within a round are offset by 0, 2, 5, or 10 ms, with 6 rounds per offset. - A round that does not finish within 30 s counts as a hang. | Config | main | This PR | |---|---|---| | NET, 3 fresh server launches × 24 rounds | **hangs in all 3 launches**, within the first 3 rounds | 72 / 72 rounds pass | | NET, `/flush_cache` before every round | - | 24 / 24 | | NET, 12 concurrent requests up to 15000 tokens, 3 ms offset, `top_logprobs_num=5`, 8 rounds | - | 8 / 8 | | NVLink (default) | 48 / 48 (with and without `/flush_cache`) | 24 / 24 | On main, when the hung server is left running, PP0 and PP1 both hit `Scheduler watchdog timeout` with the batch still in flight. **Output equivalence:** on the Qwen3-8B benchmark servers below, a greedy request with input and output logprobs (16 new tokens) returns bit-identical logprobs on main and on this PR, over both NVLink and NET (6 server launches). **Unit tests:** `test_pp_output_exchange_order.py` (new) and `test_pp_cp_rank_offsets.py` pass. The same change fixed the original cross-node PD-prefill hang in our fork. On upstream main it was verified with IB loopback on a single node, as above. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Qwen3-8B, PP2 on 2 × B300, `--mem-fraction-static 0.5`, benchmarked with `python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random-ids --random-range-ratio 1.0 --seed 1`. The benchmark sends no logprobs, so main does not hang. The server was restarted for each run, and main and PR runs were interleaved. NVLink (default), each version run twice to show run-to-run noise (order: main, PR, main, PR): | Workload | Metric | main, run 1 | main, run 2 | PR, run 1 | PR, run 2 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 2048 in / 256 out, concurrency 64, 512 prompts | Output tok/s | 4784.2 | 4762.1 | 4882.7 | 4814.6 | | | TTFT p50 (ms) | 526.5 | 528.1 | 482.7 | 521.8 | | | ITL p50 (ms) | 9.7 | 9.9 | 9.6 | 9.8 | | 2048 in / 256 out, concurrency 256, 1024 prompts | Output tok/s | 9493.4 | 9615.7 | 9292.2 | 9635.3 | | | TTFT p50 (ms) | 997.2 | 1584.2 | 1176.7 | 1516.6 | | | ITL p50 (ms) | 16.6 | 16.4 | 16.4 | 16.6 | | 4096 in / 8 out, concurrency 64, 512 prompts | Input tok/s | 137740.0 | 138143.9 | 137614.1 | 138004.3 | | | TTFT p50 (ms) | 1006.4 | 1003.7 | 1025.4 | 1017.9 | NET/IB loopback, one run each: | Workload | Metric | main | PR | |---|---|---|---| | 2048 in / 256 out, concurrency 64, 512 prompts | Output tok/s | 4733.2 | 4745.3 | | | TTFT p50 (ms) | 542.4 | 562.7 | | | ITL p50 (ms) | 9.8 | 9.7 | | 2048 in / 256 out, concurrency 256, 1024 prompts | Output tok/s | 8959.2 | 9361.1 | | | TTFT p50 (ms) | 1623.6 | 1059.9 | | | ITL p50 (ms) | 16.6 | 16.5 | | 4096 in / 8 out, concurrency 64, 512 prompts | Input tok/s | 131870.5 | 130743.0 | | | TTFT p50 (ms) | 1065.0 | 1096.8 | The differences are within run-to-run noise; for example, TTFT at concurrency 256 ranges from 1.0 s to 1.6 s across runs of the same code. Odd ranks now block on the upstream metadata recv before posting their sends. Their even peer sends first, so that wait is short, and the benchmarks show no measurable change. Not tested: real multi-node runs on upstream main, the PD disaggregation event loops on upstream main, and `pp_size > 2`.
NCCL-only repro: pp_output_exchange_nccl.py ```python """NCCL-only repro of the PP2 output exchange with two microbatches in flight. PP0: recv out(mb2) -> send relay(mb2) -> recv out(mb0) PP1: send out(mb2) -> send out(mb0) -> recv relay(mb2) (send_first, main) PP1: send out(mb2) -> recv relay(mb2) -> send out(mb0) (parity, this PR) Each message is K small device tensors. Usage: python pp_output_exchange_nccl.py {send_first,parity} K """ import os import random import sys import time import torch import torch.distributed as dist import torch.multiprocessing as mp def worker(rank, order, k, port): os.environ.update(MASTER_ADDR="127.0.0.1", MASTER_PORT=str(port)) torch.cuda.set_device(rank) dist.init_process_group("nccl", rank=rank, world_size=2, device_id=torch.device("cuda", rank)) peer = 1 - rank buf = lambda: torch.ones(2048, device="cuda") for _ in range(2): # warm up the connection in both directions if rank == 0: dist.send(buf(), peer); dist.recv(buf(), peer) else: dist.recv(buf(), peer); dist.send(buf(), peer) torch.cuda.synchronize() dist.barrier() works = [] send = lambda: works.extend(dist.isend(buf(), peer) for _ in range(k)) recv = lambda: works.extend(dist.irecv(buf(), peer) for _ in range(k)) if rank == 0: recv(); send(); recv() elif order == "send_first": send(); send(); recv() else: send(); recv(); send() deadline = time.time() + 15 while not all(w.is_completed() for w in works): if time.time() > deadline: print(f"rank{rank} HANG order={order} k={k}", flush=True) os._exit(1) time.sleep(0.01) print(f"rank{rank} OK order={order} k={k}", flush=True) dist.destroy_process_group() if __name__ == "__main__": order, k = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]) mp.spawn(worker, args=(order, k, random.randint(20000, 40000)), nprocs=2) ```
Server repro client: repro_pp_hang.py ```python """Staggered concurrent logprob requests against a PP server; detect hangs.""" import argparse import concurrent.futures as cf import random import sys import time import requests p = argparse.ArgumentParser() p.add_argument("--url", default="http://127.0.0.1:30000") p.add_argument("--rounds", type=int, default=6) p.add_argument("--stagger-ms", type=float, nargs="+", default=[0, 2, 5, 10]) p.add_argument("--lens", type=int, nargs="+", default=[37, 201, 600, 1800]) p.add_argument("--max-new-tokens", type=int, default=8) p.add_argument("--top-logprobs-num", type=int, default=0) p.add_argument("--timeout", type=float, default=30) p.add_argument("--flush", action="store_true") args = p.parse_args() def one(n, seed, delay): time.sleep(delay) rng = random.Random(seed) payload = { "input_ids": [rng.randint(100, 30000) for _ in range(n)], "sampling_params": {"max_new_tokens": args.max_new_tokens, "temperature": 0}, "return_logprob": True, "logprob_start_len": 0, } if args.top_logprobs_num: payload["top_logprobs_num"] = args.top_logprobs_num r = requests.post(args.url + "/generate", json=payload, timeout=args.timeout) r.raise_for_status() for stagger in args.stagger_ms: for rnd in range(args.rounds): if args.flush: requests.post(args.url + "/flush_cache", timeout=30) with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(len(args.lens)) as ex: futs = [ex.submit(one, n, rnd * 1000 + i, i * stagger / 1000) for i, n in enumerate(args.lens)] try: [f.result() for f in futs] except Exception as e: sys.exit(f"HANG stagger={stagger}ms round={rnd}: {e}") print(f"ok stagger={stagger}ms round={rnd}", flush=True) print("ALL PASSED") ```

title: [Fix] metrics: Handle process CPU clock resets after restore
author: rst0git
body:
## Motivation

After CRIU restore, the process CPU clock can be below the scheduler's saved accounting baseline. The resulting negative delta causes the Prometheus counter to raise `ValueError`, terminating the restored scheduler when metrics are enabled.

Without a time namespace, restoring on a host with less uptime also moves the monotonic clock backwards. Scheduler time accounting then stalls until the clock catches up, and stage metrics accumulate negative wall time that crashes the same way when drained.

## Modifications

- Count the restored CPU clock reading as CPU time since restore instead of a negative delta, so the counter never decrements.
- Flush buffered idle and stage totals before rebasing scheduler time accounting when the monotonic clock moves below the last sample.
- Preserve the active stage and reset the forward-occupancy window.
- Drop backwards spans in `SchedulerStageMetricsRecorder` so drained totals stay non-negative.

Add regressions for repeated CPU clock resets during idle and active scheduling, monotonic clock resets, and preservation of buffered totals and an active stage across a reset between reporting ticks.

## Accuracy Tests

Model outputs are unaffected.

Six accounting tests pass in an isolated source harness. Twelve additional repeated-reset cases pass using real Prometheus counters, covering idle and active transitions with metrics and device timing enabled independently.

Direct test execution is blocked locally by missing `sgl_kernel`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: this change affects scheduler metrics accounting and does not change inference execution.

## Checklist

- [x] Add focused regression coverage.
- [x] Syntax and whitespace checks pass.
- [x] Ruff checks pass with existing E402/F841 violations excluded.
- Documentation: not applicable; no user-facing interface changes.
- Accuracy and speed benchmarks: not applicable.

title: [Fix] moe: Map expert ids for layers whose runner needs local ids under EP
author: adi-suresh01
body:
This PR was part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #44994 (merged)
* #44993 (merged)
* #44991 (merged)
* __->__ #44480 (merged)

## Motivation

Branch update: rebased onto `main` at `553836c1647b3bfbeb266b49d76ec2c9df012425`. Current head: `aba4640fc85fa75d0dfb85cd0756a7cc6e3bd422`. The original fix and author are preserved; this PR keeps its bounded one-way local-ID mapping rule. The three dependent PRs extend the per-layer contract separately. Post-rebase CPU results are listed below; original model/benchmark measurements were not rerun.

`Fp8MoEMethod.create_moe_runner` runs fp8 experts on triton when `--moe-runner-backend` is `flashinfer_cutlass` or `flashinfer_cutedsl`, since `Fp8MoEMethod` has no path on either. NVFP4 checkpoints pin `flashinfer_cutlass` on sm120, and `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` keeps its MTP experts in FP8 block-scaled form, so the NEXTN draft layer ends up on triton. `StandardDispatcher` only looks at the global backend when it decides whether to translate expert ids. It sees `flashinfer_cutlass`, sets `skip_local_expert_mapping`, and the triton runner gets global ids. With `--ep-size 2` each rank holds 256 of the 512 experts, so on both ranks ids 256 to 511 index past the local weights, and on rank 1 ids 0 to 255 run the wrong experts.

This is the EP2 crash in #44291 (attempts 2 and 3), and it is what the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next cookbook means when it says these experts "fault on the triton fp8 path under EP". `MoeRunner.__init__` already guards the same hazard for `hpc_ops` (it fails at startup when a quant method falls back to another runner); the flashinfer_cutlass fallback has no guard, so it runs and faults.

Reproduced on 2x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120, PCIe only, GPU0-GPU1 `SYS`), driver 595.91.07, `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` at a6a8c5601 (torch 2.14.1+cu130, flashinfer 0.7.1, triton 3.8.0), `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` @ fc694b54, `--tp-size 2 --ep-size 2 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass --ple-offload-embedding --disable-custom-all-reduce`, NEXTN 3/1/4:

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| no speculation, CUDA graphs | serves |
| NEXTN, CUDA graphs | `CUDA error: an illegal memory access` during draft prefill graph capture |
| NEXTN, `--disable-cuda-graph`, `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` | `Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal memory access` in `fused_moe_kernel`, called from `Fp8MoEMethod.apply` in `_draft_extend_for_prefill` |
| NEXTN + #40172 | same crash as NEXTN with graphs: #40172 changes the mapping branch, which this layer skips |
| NEXTN + this PR | serves with CUDA graphs, GSM8K 0.975, accept length 2.94 |

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py`: `create_moe_dispatcher` passes the backend of the runner the quant method built (`quant_method.runner.runner_backend`). The layer calls `create_moe_runner` before it builds the dispatcher, so that runner is already known. Methods with no runner of their own, including wrappers that build one on an inner scheme (compressed-tensors, Quark, AWQ/GPTQ), pass `None` and keep today's behavior.
- `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/standard.py`: `StandardDispatcher` takes an optional `runner_backend`. Every flag still comes from `--moe-runner-backend`. The runner can only turn local-id mapping on: when the global backend keeps global ids (`_keeps_global_expert_ids`, the list that used to be inline) and the layer's runner does not. Under `auto`, AITER, or any layer whose runner keeps global ids, nothing changes. With LoRA and EP on a remapped layer it raises at startup, because the LoRA pool keys experts by the global backend's convention and would read the wrong adapters.
- `test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_standard_dispatcher_runner_backend.py` (new, CPU): under a `flashinfer_cutlass` pin with EP2, a dispatcher built for a triton runner maps global ids to local ones and turns the other rank's experts into `-1`; `Fp8MoEMethod`'s triton fallback reaches the dispatcher through `create_moe_dispatcher`; a runner never turns mapping off (auto + `flashinfer_trtllm`); the AITER flag still follows the global backend; LoRA + EP on a remapped layer is rejected.
- `test/registered/unit/lora/test_mem_pool_ep_unit.py`: that test execs the dispatcher's `__init__` from source in a hand-built namespace, so it now also loads `_keeps_global_expert_ids` and provides `Optional` and `MoeRunnerBackendLike` for the new signature.

Not changed here: `should_use_flashinfer_cutlass_moe_fp4_allgather()` still reads the global backend (DP-attention fp4 all-gather only). Wrapper methods keep the global layout, so a wrapper whose inner scheme runs triton under a `flashinfer_cutlass` pin (Quark W8A8 FP8 per-tensor, for example) is still affected; I left that out because I could not test it.

## Validation after rebase

Head: `aba4640fc85fa75d0dfb85cd0756a7cc6e3bd422`. Rebased onto main `553836c1647b3bfbeb266b49d76ec2c9df012425`; base `main` is `553836c1647b3bfbeb266b49d76ec2c9df012425`.

- At this exact head, 2 focused CPU module(s) passed: 56 tests plus 4 reported subtests. Across all four PR heads, 15 focused modules completed 482 test executions plus 347 reported subtests, all passing.
- Each PR's full incremental tree matches the pre-rebase change applied to its rewritten base, retaining prior merge-only integration fixes. The stack remains #44480 -> #44991 -> #44993 -> #44994.
- Configured pre-commit checks passed over all 152 changed files in the full stack. Strict registration/entrypoint checks passed: 2,478 files / 3,012 registrations. CPU tests used Python 3.12.15 and Torch 2.14.1+cu130 with GPUs hidden.

GPU, full-model accuracy/throughput and full CI were not rerun for this rebase. Prior hardware measurements below remain evidence for their named earlier revisions; checked CUTLASS/Marlin/GGUF consumer sources are unchanged, which is source evidence rather than a new GPU run.

## Earlier accuracy tests (before rebase)

- New test: without this PR `6 failed, 1 passed` (the `Fp8MoEMethod` case fails on `assert not dispatcher.skip_local_expert_mapping`), with it `7 passed`.
- With this PR, the new test, `test_hpc_ops_runner_guard.py`, `test_flashinfer_dispatcher.py`, `test_moe_runner_config_placement.py` and `test_mem_pool_ep_unit.py`: `80 passed`.
- Server, EP2 + NEXTN + CUDA graphs + this PR: `python -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 200 --max-tokens 16384` scores 0.975, per-request accept length 2.94 (min 2.36, max 3.33).
- That server run used the first revision of this fix, which took every dispatcher flag from the runner. A review pointed out that it would change ROCm AITER BF16 MoE under EP, so I narrowed it to the version here; for this layer the two dispatch identically. The final revision was rechecked on the same pod: boots with graphs, GSM8K 50 scores 0.980, accept length 2.95.
- Without speculation, EP2 already served on main; TP2 + NEXTN with #42566 and both EP2/TP2 with the RadixArk BF16 draft also serve, so the only EP2 + NEXTN blocker on this checkpoint was this dispatcher path.

## Earlier speed tests and profiling (before rebase)

`sglang.bench_serving`, random 1024 in / 512 out, EP2 + NEXTN + CUDA graphs + this PR:

| Concurrency | Output tok/s | Median TPOT | Median TTFT | Accept length |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 181.0 | 5.21 ms | 120 ms | 2.99 |
| 16 | 950.1 | 15.41 ms | 173 ms | 2.95 |
| 64 | 1362.6 | 27.23 ms | 9500 ms | 2.90 |

There is no "before" column because main does not start in this configuration. The c=64 TTFT is queueing: the mamba state cache caps `max_running_requests` at 39 here.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (no user-facing change)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Fix] diffusion: stabilize FLUX.3 serving and reuse static conditioning
author: mickqian
body:
Follow-up to #44418, now merged. Latest `origin/main` (`09b7383624c1`) is merged into this branch; the PR now contains only the serving fixes, hoisting, tests and cookbook updates.

## Changes
- Stabilize reference SDPA priority across requests. A preceding DiT forward could otherwise switch the text encoder from cuDNN to memory-efficient attention, changing an identical request's output.
- Hoist invariant text/reference embeddings, modulations and positional preparation into request-owned state, extending the existing mode-block reuse. No model-global conditioning cache or new public knob.
- Check exact repeatability both before and after grouped requests and multi-output generation, without loosening assertions.
- Update measured deployment recipes and document TP/SP, streaming, consumer GPU and numerical-validation boundaries. Keep untested resource shapes explicitly unverified.

## Validation
- H200 after merging current main: **81 tests and 21 subtests passed** across native DiT, quantized loading, served configuration, stages, VAE, SDPA priority and normalization dispatch.
- Fresh H200 server: real Base T2I/I2I, concurrent requests, `n=2`, immediate/final repeated requests, and mixed-size multi-reference edits pass.
- Pre-commit, cookbook config validation and 64 generated command combinations pass.

### Hoisting A/B

Same H200, Base BF16 checkpoint `d8acde427a698bdb98b5c1c941c60fa4c97e9f28`, Torch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0, Torch SDPA, eager, all components resident. Both arms include the SDPA-priority fix. Batch 1, 1024x1024 output/reference, 50 steps, CFG 3.5, exact-quality PNG; two prompts/seeds and two timed repetitions after warmup. Local HTTP submission through client PNG decoding; loading and warmup excluded.

| Workload | Existing partial hoist | Full hoist | Runtime peak allocated, before / after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| T2I | 7.2853 s | 7.2844 s | 22265.63 / 22263.13 MiB |
| I2I | 15.2640 s | 15.0395 s | 22267.76 / 22265.26 MiB |

T2I is effectively unchanged; I2I latency is 1.47% lower in this small sample. These are allocator peaks, not node-wide NVML totals. Both arms repeat exactly internally; cross-arm outputs are **not bit-exact** (SSIM 0.9957-0.9989, MAD 0.158-0.373 / 255 across four PNGs). Component tests cover the unchanged function, not official full-checkpoint accuracy.

## Follow-up Experiments
- [x] Matched hoisting E2E latency/memory comparison.
- [x] Measured recipe and numerical-boundary documentation.
- [x] Matched GB300 FlashInfer 0.7.1 versus 0.7.2rc3, with matching cubin packages; no change to the main dependency pin.
- [x] NVFP4 startup-LoRA generation and unload/restore check on merged-main head `f674e9537bb`: synthetic rank 4, 512x512, 8 steps. Startup and API-applied adapters agree exactly; adapted output changes, repeats exactly, and unloading restores the same generic-layout base output exactly. API memory release succeeds.
- [ ] CI on the latest follow-up head.

Official Diffusers parity remains deferred as requested.

### FlashInfer version A/B

Single GB300, same code `78f3ef2182a`, Torch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0, FA4, eager, all components resident, batch 1, exact quality, PNG. Base revision `17333191c36bae1b61b0a247e33ba284f1df07fa`; distilled revision `875076bf83d4364b68dccdbf8307f4f01475f68d`. Base: 50 steps/CFG 3.5; distilled: 16 steps/no CFG. 1024x1024 output and reference; two prompts/seeds, two timed repeats after warming each request shape. HTTP submission through client PNG decoding, excluding loading/warmup/JIT. Only one server generates at a time. FlashInfer Python and cubin versions match in each environment; no version-check suppression or jit-cache package.

| Checkpoint / precision | T2I 0.7.1 / 0.7.2rc3 | I2I 0.7.1 / 0.7.2rc3 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Base BF16 | 3.200 / 3.208 s | 6.261 / 6.280 s |
| Base FP8R | 2.156 / 2.172 s | 4.424 / 4.448 s |
| Base NVFP4 | 2.120 / 1.932 s | 4.255 / 3.921 s |
| Distilled BF16 | 0.688 / 0.688 s | 1.298 / 1.302 s |
| Distilled FP8R | 0.676 / 0.665 s | 1.012 / 1.015 s |
| Distilled NVFP4 | 0.615 / 0.640 s | 0.974 / 0.918 s |

All 24 version-paired PNGs match pixel-for-pixel, each arm repeats exactly, and per-server runtime peak allocated memory is unchanged in all 12 workload rows. This does not make FP8R/NVFP4 lossless relative to BF16. Base NVFP4 improves by 8.88% T2I / 7.84% I2I; distilled NVFP4 T2I instead regresses by 4.05% in this sample. BF16 and FP8R show no consistent material gain. Keep the stable dependency pin rather than requiring an RC globally for this model-specific benefit.

title: [Fix] metrics: Handle CPU monitor clock resets after restore
author: rst0git
body:
## Motivation

CRIU restore can reset process CPU time below the monitor’s saved baseline. The resulting negative delta causes the Prometheus counter to raise ValueError, terminating the monitoring thread and leaving CPU metrics stale.

## Modifications

Count the current CPU reading as time since restore when the delta is negative, then update the baseline for subsequent samples.

Add a regression using a real Prometheus counter covering repeated resets and normal increments after each reset.

## Accuracy Tests

Model outputs are unaffected.

Both mocked CPU-monitor tests pass directly without GPU dependencies or stubs. The new regression reproduces the negative-counter failure against the original implementation.

Full-file execution encounters existing interference from the smoke test’s background thread. Real CRIU restore validation remains outstanding.

title: [Fix] nvfp4: Own streamed tensors while waiting for paired weights
author: sshleifer
body:
## Motivation

RunAI reuses streamed tensor buffers after the synchronous loader callback returns. Online NVFP4 conversion can retain those borrowed tensors while waiting for a gate/up pair or an FP8 weight/scale pair, including across checkpoint files. A later callback can therefore quantize overwritten data and produce corrupted expert scales or NaNs.

## Modifications

Mark RunAI storage as borrowed so packed-expert slices and detached aliases retain the ownership information. Keep the existing tensor marker for compatibility. Copy borrowed tensors to owned CPU storage only when placing them in a pending queue, covering gated w1/w3 weights, FP8 weights, and FP8 scales. Immediate conversion and tensors with normal ownership keep their existing behavior.

## Accuracy Tests

12 CPU regressions pass. They overwrite the streamer's buffer between paired loads, covering both gate/up arrival orders and both FP8 weight/scale arrival orders for direct tensors, packed views, and detached views. The four direct-tensor cases fail on upstream main (`c4870d98cf`); the eight alias cases fail on the original PR revision (`774e2a19ac`). Tests exercise storage marking through the RunAI iterator with a fake streamer and verify that owned clones do not inherit the borrowed marker.

```bash
python -m pytest test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_nvfp4_online_weight_loader.py -q
```

The tests exercise the real loader and replace GPU quantization with a recording CPU function. No new full-model GPU evaluation was run for this upstream port.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No serving-path change. The additional CPU copy is restricted to borrowed tensors that must survive a loader callback; load-time overhead was not benchmarked.

title: [Fix] [NPU] glm-ocr: Fix M-RoPE section for GLM-OCR on Ascend and add A3 validation
author: chaijiacheng888
body:
<!-- PR title: [Perf] [NPU] glm-ocr: Run 3-axis M-RoPE on the Triton kernel on Ascend -->

## Motivation

GLM-OCR on Ascend A3 applies M-RoPE for real: `mrope_section=[16,24,24]`, and image prefill carries `(3, seq_len)` positions. After `#32745` (merged), every 2-D position tensor is answered by `forward_native`, so those rotations are correct but computed by the eager path — and on this model it is not only prefill: `ForwardBatch._compute_mrope_positions_decode` repeats `seq_lens - 1` three times, so decode keeps the 2-D shape too and pays the eager path once per layer per step.

This PR sends that one case to the Triton kernel `forward_cuda` already uses for 3-axis positions. Measured end to end on 4×910: **output throughput +18.8 %, TPOT −1.55 ms (−17.5 %)**, request latency −15.6 %.

`torch_npu.npu_mrope` is not an alternative here: passing the real section repairs only the contiguous map, the interleaved map stays wrong (max abs 6.9 vs `forward_native`, versus 1.6e-2 for bf16 rounding) whichever section it is given, and CANN rejects splits outside its whitelist (`aclnnRopeWithSinCosCache`, error 161002). At 32k tokens the Triton kernel is also 1.45x faster than the fused op (2.77 vs 4.03 ms), so nothing is given up by moving this case off it.

## Modifications

**1. `python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/mrope.py`** — send 2-D positions to the Triton kernel and keep the rest as it was:

```python
        assert positions.ndim == 1 or positions.ndim == 2
        if query.shape[0] == 0:
            return query, key
        self._match_cos_sin_cache_dtype(query)
        if positions.ndim == 2 and self.mrope_section:
            return self.forward_triton(positions, query, key)
        # 1-D text: the fused CANN op; an all-zero section means plain RoPE.
        if query.shape[1] > 4096:
            return self.forward_native(positions, query, key, fused_set_kv_buffer_arg)
```

The condition is the one `forward_cuda` already uses. Inside sglang a 2-D position tensor only comes from the M-RoPE index (`(3, seq_len)`, always with a section), and `Ernie4_5_VLRotaryEmbedding` overrides `forward()` and dispatches to its own kernels, so it never enters `forward_npu`. The 1-D branch is unchanged, including the `query.shape[1] > 4096` fallback; the 0-token early return and the cos/sin cache dtype match are new relative to `#32745`.

**2. `test/registered/rotary/test_mrope_npu.py`** (new) — compares `forward_npu` with `forward_native` for the contiguous, interleaved and glm-interleaved maps, at fp32 and bf16, plus the 1-D and 0-token paths. Registered as `register_npu_ci(est_time=30, suite="full-1-npu-a3", nightly=True)`, next to the existing cpu and amd files in `test/registered/rotary/`; verified to fail on the pre-fix code and pass with it.

**3. `docs/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/reference/support_models.mdx`** (+6) — add the GLM-OCR row (A3) to the Multimodal table.

## Accuracy Tests

Against `forward_native` on NPU, over the three axis maps: fp32 is bit-identical, bf16 is within 1 ulp (max abs 0.031). The alternative — passing the real section to `npu_mrope` — is off by 2.0 (contiguous) / 6.9 (interleaved) on 2-D input, and an interleaved map is off by 6.9 even with the real section.

End-to-end through the GLM-OCR official SDK self-hosted pipeline (PP-DocLayoutV3 layout → region crop → GLM-OCR → merge), OmniDocBench v1.6 `full` (1651 pages, Ascend A3):

| metric          | this branch | published GLM-OCR |
| --------------- | ----------- | ----------------- |
| Overall         | **95.26**   | 95.22             |
| Text Edit       | **0.0378**  | 0.0440            |
| Formula CDM     | 96.4113     | **97.1800**       |
| Table TEDS      | **93.1399** | 92.8300           |
| Table TEDS-S    | **95.7556** | 95.3900           |
| Read Order Edit | 0.1394      | **0.1330**        |

The published column is Zhipu's cloud `layout_parsing` service, so the layout detector differs from the local PP-DocLayoutV3 used here; a gap within ~0.4 points is expected from that alone. Overall = `((1 − Text Edit) × 100 + TEDS + CDM) / 3`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### End to end A/B (4×910)

ABBA so drift cancels: arm A = current main (`#32745`, 2-D → `forward_native`), arm B = this PR. Same weights, same image, only `mrope.py` replaced.

4×910, `--tp 4`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.70 --chunked-prefill-size 32768 --max-prefill-tokens 65536`; first 10 pages of the OmniDocBench v1.6 demo set sent as whole pages, concurrency 1, `max_tokens=256 temperature=0 ignore_eos=true` (same output length in both arms).

| run        | output tok/s | TPOT        | request mean |
| ---------- | ------------ | ----------- | ------------ |
| A1         | 65.70        | 8.91 ms     | 3.893 s      |
| B1         | 76.01        | 7.39 ms     | 3.365 s      |
| B2         | 88.19        | 7.21 ms     | 2.899 s      |
| A2         | 72.53        | 8.79 ms     | 3.526 s      |
| **A mean** | **69.1**     | **8.85 ms** | 3.71 s       |
| **B mean** | **82.1**     | **7.30 ms** | 3.13 s       |

TTFT is inside the noise on this set (pages span 4.2k–6.1k prompt tokens) and is not part of the claim. The gain lands on decode: under graph replay the change replaces ~15 eager nodes per layer with one kernel, which is why the per-token saving is 1.55 ms and not `layers × operator time`.

### Single call of the rotation (1×910)

One 910 chip, GLM-OCR shapes (`head_size = rotary_dim = 128`, `heads/kv_heads = 16/8`, `mrope_section = [16,24,24]`), bf16, median of 30 after 10 warmups.

#### Contiguous map (GLM-OCR)

| seq   | native (ms) | triton (ms) | speedup |
| ----- | ----------- | ----------- | ------- |
| 1024  | 0.479       | 0.172       | 2.79x   |
| 4096  | 0.715       | 0.421       | 1.70x   |
| 32768 | 4.942       | 2.773       | 1.78x   |

#### Interleaved map (Qwen2-VL)

| seq   | native (ms) | triton (ms) | speedup |
| ----- | ----------- | ----------- | ------- |
| 1024  | 1.022       | 0.199       | 5.13x   |
| 4096  | 1.763       | 0.507       | 3.47x   |
| 32768 | 10.759      | 3.465       | 3.10x   |

fp32 gains are larger (2.12x at 4096, 2.89x at 32768). The interleaved map gains more than the contiguous one because native does it as a series of copies.

## Relationship to other PRs

`#32745` (merged) introduced the behaviour this PR refines: it sends every 2-D input to `forward_native`. This PR changes only the case that has an axis map; the "2-D without a section" and "1-D" branches behave as before. The dispatch test that `#32745` added (`test_npu_dispatch_preserves_multimodal_positions`) needs the same edit — 2-D to `forward_triton`, 1-D to `npu_mrope` — and lands with the rebase onto main.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.

title: [Fix] sgl-router: Bump rustls to 0.23.46 for RUSTSEC-2026-0346..0349
author: ShangmingCai
body:
## Motivation

On 2026-10-14 RustSec published four advisories against rustls < 0.23.46 (advisory-db commit `caee11f41f`):

- RUSTSEC-2026-0346: `Debug` impls for client session values expose TLS secrets
- RUSTSEC-2026-0347: buffered application data sent to the outer server after ECH rejection
- RUSTSEC-2026-0348: Brotli certificate decompression can allocate up to 1 GiB before authentication
- RUSTSEC-2026-0349: an unauthenticated ServerHello can downgrade later connections to classical key exchange

`experimental/sgl-router/Cargo.lock` pins rustls 0.23.45, unchanged since #39457. `cargo deny check advisories` fetches the advisory database on every run, so the router's tier-1 lint now fails on every PR that runs router CI, with no code change involved. Example: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38679761043/job/116241458548 (#42674). Main's own router runs look green only because their tiers are skipped.

## Changes

Lockfile only, via `cargo update -p rustls`: rustls 0.23.45 → 0.23.46. The new rustls depends on getrandom 0.3.4, which is already in the lockfile, so no package is added.

## Tests

In `experimental/sgl-router`:
- `cargo deny check licenses bans sources advisories`: advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok. Before this change it failed with the four advisories above.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test --locked`: lib 1083, component 138, proxy 211, all passing.

Not in scope: `rust/Cargo.lock` pins rustls 0.23.43, which is also affected, but no CI job runs `cargo deny` on that workspace.

title: [Fix] step5: Register Step5 HiCache pool names in the Rust tree core
author: alphabetc1
body:
`_reduce_prefetch_ack` passes every Python `PoolName` member to the Rust tree core, but `parse_pool_name` does not know the three Step5 pools. Verified on Step-5-Preview, 4x GB300 TP4, BF16 KV, HiCache + Mooncake L3: greedy outputs on storage hits match device hits bit for bit (8/8), and no scheduler crash. Before the fix it crashed on the first storage prefetch.

title: [Fix] runtime: Version FlashInfer caches for default-tactic tuning.
author: leejnau
body:
## Motivation

#43927 enables FlashInfer v2's default-tactic (`-1`) comparison on cache misses. Existing v1 winners are accepted before that comparison, and their cache paths did not change. Version the cache identity so fresh startup retunes these configurations with the expanded candidate set.

This continues v2 candidate-selection adoption with existing v1 persistence.

## Modifications

Add a stable `candidate_selection=v2_default` component to the existing cache key.

All previous cache files become cold once, including caches created since #43927 and MegaMoE namespaced records sharing the file. Existing files remain untouched for rollback; subsequent startups reuse the new namespace through the existing v1 load/save path.

Measurement policy remains unspecified. Cache-disabled behavior, skip controls, streams, and distributed synchronization are unchanged. No managed-store migration or MegaMoE integration changes.

## Accuracy Tests

- Current head `6a32decdb5a216b53f35cfb53659308f223da91c`: existing registered autotune suite **12 tests in 19.625 seconds; 11 passed, 1 CUDA-only skipped**. macOS arm64, Python 3.12.12, Torch 2.14.1, installed FlashInfer 0.7.1.

title: [Fix] true-on-policy: Allocate the graph logits buffer in the logits dtype
author: HJSang
body:
## Summary

Under a true-on-policy contract (e.g. `qwen3_dense_true_on_policy_v1`), the lm head runs in bf16 and eager forward returns bf16 next-token logits. CUDA-graph decode copies the same logits into the shared `next_token_logits_buffer`, which was always fp32. As a result, decode `log_softmax` and top-k ran in fp32 and stopped matching the trainer bitwise. Prefill, which uses no buffer, matched. In `LogitsProcessor._copy_logits_to_buffer`, the buffer branch came before the force-bf16 branch, so the bf16 cast never ran under CUDA graph.

The fix gives the buffer the dtype the logits processor returns:
- `get_next_token_logits_dtype(config)` in `logits_processor.py` returns bf16 when the contract forces a bf16 lm head, and fp32 otherwise.
- `GraphSharedOutput.get_logits_buffer` takes a required `dtype` and keys its cache by `(vocab_size, dtype)`.
- Every runner that allocates a `next_token_logits_buffer` passes that dtype: decode and prefill CUDA graph, EAGLE and multi-layer EAGLE draft extend, and the base runner's dummy-run buffers.
- `_copy_logits_to_buffer` asserts that the buffer dtype matches, so a mismatched allocation fails loudly instead of converting silently.
- Default serving is unchanged and keeps the fp32 buffer.

An alternative was rejected: checking for force-bf16 before the buffer branch would drop the shared buffer, so each captured batch size would hold its own logits output. With this fix the shared buffer stays, and halves in size under the contract.

Only `sglang-miles` needs this. On `main`, `_copy_logits_to_buffer` upcasts every path to fp32, so prefill and decode already agree.

## Rebased onto the rebuilt sglang-miles (`bff3f6ae7e`)

The rebuilt branch adds a fused cast-and-softcap path in `_copy_logits_to_buffer` that always writes fp32 logits and asserts an fp32 buffer. `get_next_token_logits_dtype` therefore returns fp32 when the config sets `final_logit_softcapping`, and the softcap lookup is shared through `_final_logit_softcapping(config)`. The unit test adds a contract-plus-softcap case. The GPU results below were measured before the rebase; the CPU unit tests were re-run on the new base:
- the new tests: 6 passed (plus 5 subtests);
- `true_on_policy/` and the logprob suites: no new failures. The 10 failures and 1 error also fail on base, from stub subprocesses and missing CUDA.

## GPU validation of the current head (`7b6ae42fef`, 2026-10-21)

Run with Qwen3-4B on 2x H200, with CUDA graph on, using the radixark/miles#4109 checks (k=128, 3 rollouts):

| Run | SGLang | Result | top-k logprob diff / set mismatch | `train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| top-k, native `/generate` | this PR | pass | 0 / 0 every rollout | 0 |
| top-k, session (flat base64, 48/48 records) | this PR | pass | 0 / 0 every rollout | 0 |
| existing `test_qwen3_4B_fsdp_true_on_policy.py` | this PR | pass | n/a | 0 every step |
| top-k, native `/generate` | base `bff3f6ae7e` | fails, as expected | 0.109 / 0.995 | n/a |

GPU unit tests (`unit/true_on_policy/`, `unit/spec/`, `unit/layers/test_logprob_*`): the only difference from base is the new `test_graph_logits_buffer_dtype.py`, which passes 4/4. The same 10 tests fail on both commits: `test_dense_deterministic_math` (3) and `test_on_policy_wiring` subprocesses (7).

## Results

Qwen3-4B, 2x H200. Measured on `sglang-miles` `4076a6857` plus this commit, which applies unchanged on top of `7b6993a31`.

- **miles true-on-policy CI** (FSDP, k=128; radixark/miles#3952 and its follow-up CI test). The trainer scores SGLang's recorded top-k candidates with the same weights. Values are max |trainer - SGLang| over the candidates / fraction of tokens whose candidate set differs:

  | Rollout path | CUDA graph on, before | CUDA graph on, after |
  |---|---|---|
  | native `/generate` | 0.109 / 0.995 | 0 / 0 |
  | session chat (flat b64 top logprobs) | 0.109 / 0.995 | 0 / 0 |

  With `--disable-cuda-graph`, both runs were already 0 before the fix. The existing `test_qwen3_4B_fsdp_true_on_policy.py` passes, with `train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff` 0.
- **SGLang decode vs prefill rescore** (raw floats, 8 prompts, 1,221 decode tokens, top-20):

  |---|---|---|
  | before | 418 / 1221 | 52 / 1221 |
  | after | 1221 / 1221 | 1221 / 1221 |

- **Throughput** (64 x 512 tokens): with the contract, 7,186 to 7,264 tok/s. Without the contract, 13,343 to 13,249 tok/s (noise), and the output is bitwise identical to before.
- **Memory:** decode graph capture uses 1.22 GB instead of 1.30 GB. KV capacity is unchanged.

title: [Fix] rust-server: Honour cache_salt and require_reasoning on /generate
author: metamergebot
body:
Stacked on #44312 (`priority` and the `x-override-*` headers on the Rust frontend): this branch is based on `oss-sync-fc133deaf0`, and the diff against it is this change alone. Once #44312 merges, this will be rebased onto `main`.

## Motivation

The Rust frontend's `/generate` schema ignores unknown top-level keys, so request fields the Python server honours are dropped silently in Rust mode. Four of them change the result:

- `cache_salt`: the prefix cache's second namespace key, beside `extra_key`. Dropping it lets requests sent under different salts share cached prefixes.
- `require_reasoning`: the scheduler applies grammar constraints only after the reasoning section. Dropping it constrains the reasoning output from the first token.
- `lora_path` and `session_params`: dropping them returns base-model or stateless output with a 200. Python returns a 400 for both on a server without LoRA or without that session.

## Modifications

- `cache_salt` and `require_reasoning` become `GenerateRequest` schema fields (proto tags 25 and 26; `api_types.py`, `sglang.api.v1.rs` and `sglang.api.v1.serde.rs` regenerated with `cargo gen-api`). `cache_salt` follows Python's `_normalize_cache_salt`, the same rules as `extra_key`: one value broadcasts, a list is per item and needs a batch of the same length, and an empty value means none (`message/request.rs`). Both reach the scheduler header, whose default slots are now filled through `cache_salt`, slot 45, so the header is 46 entries long (`message/io_struct.rs`).
- `lora_path` and `session_params` are declared as raw JSON fields (tags 27 and 28) so that a non-null value is a 400 ("… is not supported by the Rust server"). `null` still passes, so the `bench_serving` payload parses as before.
- The four fields leave the pinned list of Python-only request fields in `test_parity.py`. The rest of that list (`custom_labels`, `log_metrics`, `no_logs`, …) stays ignored; dropping those changes only logging.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: the change only affects which request fields the Rust frontend forwards to the scheduler, not the generated tokens.

Not applicable.

title: [Fix] tokenizer_manager: re-report only emitted customized_info keys on cumulative streams
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

Cumulative (non-incremental) streaming re-reports every key in `ReqState.customized_info_accumulated` on each frame, so a key that arrived on an earlier queued output still reaches the client when only the last queued output is returned (#43772). title: [Fix] dsa-eagle-topk: Copy token keys and scales when relocating index cache
author: sshleifer
body:
Fix for dsa with speculative_eagle_topk=2


## Motivation

`DSATokenToKVPool.move_kv_cache` passes token-slot IDs to `IndexKeyCache.move`, but that method indexes its page buffer with them. With 64-token pages, slot 319 is page 4, offset 63; treating it as page 319 can access out of bounds. Small IDs that fit in the page dimension silently copy entire pages and overwrite unrelated keys.

This matters when speculative decoding relocates accepted tree tokens. The ordinary single-chain (`speculative_eagle_topk=1`) path skips that compaction.

## Modifications

Move each selected token's FP8 index key and scale within the physical-page view used by the cache writers and readers. Advanced-index gathering before assignment preserves overlapping swaps. Layers that reuse another layer's indexer remain skipped.

Nonempty moves with pooled index keys (`index_kpool > 1`) now fail explicitly: relocating individual tokens would require rebuilding their pooled keys.

## Accuracy Tests

On upstream main `87211088c98ae4f5b60625eebcce007db36aa6af`, the new small-ID regression fails: swapping slots 1 and 2 corrupts neighboring keys without a CUDA error. With this patch, all three GPU cases pass on one GB300:

- Small token IDs that previously selected whole pages.
- Cross-page overlapping swaps, including the final allocated slot.
- Empty moves.

The tests use a real DSA pool and its production key/scale writers and readers, checking exact key bytes, scales, unchanged neighbors, latent KV, and a layer that reuses another layer's indexer.

```bash
python -m pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_dsa_index_cache_move.py
# 3 passed
```

These are cache correctness tests; no full-model branching-speculation accuracy run was performed for this PR.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Correctness fix; no performance claim or benchmark.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit (all applicable hooks passed).
- [x] Add and register GPU regression tests.
- [x] Follow SGLang code style.
- Documentation: no user-facing configuration change.

title: [Fix] multimodal: Keep shared-memory feature transport for multi-node pipeline parallelism
author: knlb-tml
body:
_Posted by Kunal's robot (Claude Opus 5.5) ↓_
>
> ## Motivation
>
> `determine_tensor_transport_mode()` falls back to inline (pickled) feature transport whenever `nnodes > 1`. With pipeline parallelism, only the first stage's TP group reads tokenizer output, so shared memory still works when that group sits on node 0 with the tokenizer:
>
> ```
> node 0                            node 1..n
> tokenizer --shm--> PP0 TP group   PP1..PPn (requests relayed by PP0)
> ```
>
> Launchers that start one process group per GPU report even a single-host PP engine as `nnodes == pp_size`. In that setup the tokenizer manager pickles every request's decoded pixel tensors (hundreds of MB for several large images) on its event loop, which stalls all other requests and `/health`.
>
> ## Modifications
>
> - Keep shared-memory transport when `nnodes > 1` if each TP group fits on one node (`nnodes <= pp_size`), there are no data-parallel replicas (`dp_size == 1`), and the launch does not use Ray, whose placement groups can put any rank on any node.
> - Extend `test_tensor_transport_mode.py` with the PP, DP and Ray cases.
>
> The first stage still pickles materialized features when it relays requests to the next stage. That is unchanged by this PR and could be a follow-up.
>
> This PR is independent of #44575 and #44576, which address the same workload.
>
> ## Accuracy Tests
>
> Not applicable: the change only picks the transport for feature tensors.
>
> ## Speed Tests and Profiling
>
> A PP8 prefill server under image traffic for 30 minutes: 0.2 requests per second, 4 images per request, 59k to 74k prompt tokens. Base is `main`; fixed has this PR and #44575 and #44576.

title: [Fix] attention: Opt FlashMLA scheduler into dynamic shared memory
author: Oasis-Git
body:
[codex/claude generated]

## Motivation

The FlashMLA scheduling kernel can fail with `CUDA error: invalid argument` near its accepted shared-memory limit. Its guard permits up to 48 KiB of dynamic shared memory, but the kernel also declares static shared memory. Without explicit opt-in, the combined allocation can exceed the default launch allowance.

On GB300 (152 SMs), a standalone call with 2,211 rows succeeds, while 2,212 rows requests 49,108 dynamic bytes and fails. The existing guard permits up to 2,214 rows. This reproducer calls only the scheduling kernel, independently of request-window KV copying.

## Modifications

- Use the existing per-device initialization helper to opt the kernel into 48 KiB of dynamic shared memory before launch.
- Preserve the schedule algorithm and existing dynamic-memory bound.
- Add four boundary cases validating schedule entries and split offsets against independently calculated expectations.

## Accuracy Tests

All 41 scheduling tests passed locally on GB300: 37 existing tests and four boundary cases. Existing coverage compares metadata with FlashMLA and checks attention-output parity where applicable. Pre-commit passes.

The patch applies to main at `91f6ef232`; the affected kernel, runtime helper, and existing test file are unchanged from the tested base. GitHub CI has not been run for this fix.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speedup is claimed. Initialization uses the existing per-device cache to avoid setting the attribute on every launch.

title: [Fix] hicache: Bound the storage prefetch timeout from the first blocked admission poll
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

Under the `timeout` stop policy a storage prefetch is timed from the operation's own start. Every re-issued fetch for the same request therefore begins a fresh budget, sized by the current (possibly shrunken) hit chain, so a request can wait indefinitely across retries, and the per-request wait metric (`storage_prefetch_wait`) and the policy budget are timed by two unrelated mechanisms. Two further problems follow from how a cut read is handled: it is reported as `storage_transfer`, which heals the storage-existence beliefs for pages the store still holds, and a rank that has not yet reached its admission poll can re-issue a prefetch its peers already agreed to drop.

This PR also carries the deadline-cut attribution guards (the `deadline_expired` flag on `PrefetchOperation`, the `deadline` unfulfilled reason, the belief-healing skips, and the retracted-request admission close), which were previously proposed on their own in #44338 (closed); the timeout budget depends on them.

## Modifications

- `PollTimer` (new `python/sglang/srt/utils/poll_timer.py`) times an interval from its first blocked poll to its first ready poll. `SchedulerReqTimeStats` uses it for the storage prefetch and staging waits in place of two hand-rolled start timestamps; the serialized fields and the `meta_info` keys are unchanged.
- `UnifiedRadixCache` keeps a per-request `_StoragePrefetchWait` under the `timeout` policy. It starts at the first blocked admission poll, is sized from the span first requested (`prefetch_timeout_base + pages * prefetch_timeout_per_page`), survives re-issued fetches, and is closed by `finish_storage_prefetch_admission` or `release_aborted_request` (and by `StorageAttachment` on reset). A complete KV read that only waits on a sidecar is never cut.
- A rank-agreed expiry (the existing `_can_terminate_prefetch` consensus, now evaluating the shared budget on PP rank 0) marks the operation `deadline_expired`, cancels its pending retries, and suppresses further fetches for the request on every rank, including a rank that had not yet started its own budget.
- A deadline-cut operation is resolved under the new `deadline` unfulfilled reason instead of `storage_transfer`, its KV and auxiliary-pool storage beliefs are left untouched, `_invalidate_absent_from_hit_query` skips it (its agreed hit may be a MIN over skipped lookups), and the prefetch-outcome counters skip it since a deadline is not a storage verdict.
- `PrefillAdder` closes storage-prefetch admission for a retracted request after discarding its accounting, so the wait budget is dropped with the rest of its per-request state. `test_prefill_adder.py` asserts the call.
- Tests: `TestStoragePrefetchTimeout` in `test_storage_prefetch_lifecycle.py` covers budget start and survival across refetch, metric episodes not restarting the budget, the complete-KV-with-pending-sidecar guard, the stop-policy matrix, and a two-rank gloo case where only one rank has started waiting. Existing `SimpleNamespace` operation fixtures gain `deadline_expired=False`.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no change to model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: the change only affects when a storage prefetch under the `timeout` policy is cut and how the cut is attributed.

Unit tests run locally on this head (CPU, `pytest`): `test_storage_prefetch_lifecycle.py`, `test_hicache_pp_sync_drain.py`, `test_pp_prefetch_ticket.py`, `test_prefill_adder.py`, `test_req_time_stats.py`, `test_buffer_mode_sidecar.py`, `test_hybrid_pool_assembler.py`, `test_prefill_result_polling.py`, `test_admission_abort_not_enqueued.py`, `test_decode_hicache_tree_core.py`, `test_prefill_complete_integration.py`, `test_priority_scheduling_disaggregation.py`, `test_scheduler_chunked_abort_race.py`, `test_tokenizer_manager_rid_cleanup.py`, `test_scheduler_held_row_admission.py`, `test_scheduler_hicache_events.py`: 309 passed, 277 subtests passed.

title: [Fix] monokernels: Honor resolved CUDA graph configuration
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #44353. Enabling a monokernel can override an operator's decode CUDA graph budget: with the AMD plugin, `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 4` expands the capture buckets from `[1, 2, 4]` to `1..48`. Explicit bucket lists are also replaced.

The runtime additionally checks the legacy disable booleans instead of the resolved decode backend. Disabling graphs through `--cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled` or JSON therefore leaves graph-key filtering active and can send supported eager draft shapes to the normal forward. Conversely, an explicit backend that overrides a disable flag is treated as disabled.

## Modifications

- Keep automatically aligned buckets within the configured capture ceiling, and preserve explicitly supplied decode bucket lists.
- Skip bucket alignment when the resolved decode backend is disabled.
- Use the resolved decode backend when building monokernel capture keys, so every graph-disable spelling retains full supported eager coverage and explicit backend precedence is respected.
- Extend the existing CPU tests for small ceilings, explicit buckets, unchanged default alignment, disabled graph configuration, eager draft dispatch, and backend precedence.

## Accuracy Tests

The new regression cases fail against the original production code. After the fix, the following passes on macOS ARM64 with Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.14.1, and Transformers 5.19.0:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest \
  test/registered/unit/monokernels \
  test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_cuda_graph_config_backends.py -q
# 32 passed, 28 subtests passed
```

All applicable pre-commit hooks pass for the three changed files, including test registration checks. `git diff --check` passes. No GPU model-accuracy run was performed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No GPU timing or profiling was performed. CPU tests verify that capture sizes stay within the configured limit and that supported eager draft batches use the plugin when graphs are disabled.

title: [Fix] metrics: record HTTP request metrics in tokenizer workers
author: hope1262946533
body:
## Motivation

With `--enable-metrics` and `--tokenizer-worker-num > 1`, the HTTP request
metrics are silently missing from `/metrics`:

- `sglang:http_requests_total`
- `sglang:http_responses_total`
- `sglang:http_requests_active`
- `sglang:routing_keys_active`

Per-endpoint request rates, in-flight counts and 5xx ratios therefore cannot be
monitored on a multi-tokenizer deployment, even though `/metrics` itself is
served fine.

## Modifications

The track-response middleware was registered from `_setup_and_run_http_server`,
which runs in the parent process. With `--tokenizer-worker-num > 1` the server
is started with `uvicorn.run("...:app", workers=N)`: uvicorn spawns the HTTP
workers and each one re-imports `http_server`, so the app they actually serve is
a fresh object that never received the middleware.

- Register the middleware while the module is imported (next to the existing
  `CORSMiddleware` / `RequestDecompressionMiddleware` registrations) so that
  every tokenizer worker picks it up, and drop the parent-process registration.
- Create the metrics themselves in a separate step, `init_http_request_metrics`,
  called from the lifespan once the process has published its config.
  `prometheus_client` fixes its value backend when it is first imported, and
  SGLang only sets `PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR` in `_set_envs_and_config`, which
  runs *after* `http_server` has been imported. Creating the metrics at import
  time would therefore leave them in the in-memory registry, where the
  `MultiProcessCollector` behind `/metrics` never sees them -- including in
  single-tokenizer mode.
- The middleware now runs inside each worker, so also expose that worker's
  in-flight request count as `sglang:http_worker_active_requests{worker_id}`.
  This is the number to watch when a shared listening socket concentrates
  connections on a few workers.

A unit test in `test/registered/unit/observability/test_http_request_metrics.py`
covers all three: that the middleware is on the module-level app, that importing
`http_server` does not pull `prometheus_client` in early, and that a worker
process records the counters and labels the per-worker gauge.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A - metrics only.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A - no change to the inference path. With metrics enabled the per-request work
is unchanged; with metrics disabled the middleware returns after one config
lookup.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with
      pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit
      tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write
      documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
      Not applicable: `docs/docs/references/production_metrics.mdx` does not
      document the HTTP request metrics at all, so adding only the new one would
      be inconsistent.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the
      accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy)
      and [Benchmark the
