title: [Fix] [AMD] diffusion: Keep gfx1250 FlyDSL BF16 attention out of torch.compile
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

**What goes wrong**
With `--enable-torch-compile`, the first DiT forward on gfx1250 fails inside the aiter attention backend with `RuntimeError: An MLIR function requires a Context but none was provided`. #27702 removed `@torch.compiler.disable` from `AITerImpl.forward` so the BF16 `aiter.flash_attn_func` call could be compiled. On gfx1250, aiter (ROCm/aiter#5168) routes that call to the FlyDSL `flash_attn_batch_m32x8` kernel, which JIT-compiles in Python. Dynamo traces into it (`torch_dynamo_resume_in_flash_attn_batch_m32x8_at_2181`), FlyDSL's `JitFunction.__call__` sees an MLIR context and takes the nested-trace branch, and `capture_user_location` then finds no context and raises.

**Where it shows up**
Only gfx1250 (MI450), with the aiter attention backend and torch.compile. It is not model-specific -- any diffusion model that selects the aiter backend hits it. Confirmed end to end on two, which compile very differently:

- **Wan2.2-T2V-A14B** -- `--enable-torch-compile true --regional-compile --attention-backend aiter`, `ENABLE_CK=1`. Warmup request fails in `DenoisingStage`.
- **FLUX.2-dev** -- `--enable-torch-compile true` (whole-transformer compile, no regional compile), `ENABLE_CK=0`. Request fails with the same `An MLIR function requires a Context`.

That the two differ in compile granularity (regional vs whole-transformer) and in `ENABLE_CK` and still fail identically is the point: the trigger is Dynamo reaching the FlyDSL dispatch, not any model-specific graph shape. Note `ENABLE_CK=0` does not avoid it either -- the FlyDSL attempt in `aiter/ops/mha.py` happens *before* the `if not ENABLE_CK:` branch, so turning CK off does not route around FlyDSL.

**Why the fix is gated on gfx1250 and not on ROCm**
gfx942/gfx950 are structurally immune, for two independent reasons:

1. The FlyDSL dispatch is arch-gated at the source. `aiter/ops/flydsl/fmha_kernels.py` makes `get_gfx() == "gfx1250"` the first condition of its support check, so on gfx942/gfx950 `flydsl_flash_attn_batch_func` returns `None` and FlyDSL is never entered.
2. Those arches fall through to the CK-tile / OPUS ASM kernels, which are `@compile_ops` stubs bound to precompiled pybind symbols and carry a registered fake-tensor implementation (`gen_fake=gen_mha_fwd_fake_tensors`). Dynamo records them as opaque graph nodes; no Python-level compilation runs during tracing.

FlyDSL is the opposite kind of object: a Python JIT that compiles MLIR at call time. Tracing it means Dynamo rewrites another compiler's dispatch internals, which is exactly what the `torch_dynamo_resume_in_*` frames in the traceback show.

So disabling compile across all of ROCm would add a graph break on gfx942/gfx950 that buys nothing and costs the fusion #27702 enabled there. Hence `USE_AITER_GFX1250` rather than `is_hip()`.

**How to fix**
On gfx1250, call the BF16 `flash_attn_func` through a `@torch.compiler.disable` helper, so the FlyDSL kernel runs eagerly while the rest of the DiT block stays compiled.

## Modifications

- `runtime/platforms/aiter.py`: add `USE_AITER_GFX1250`.
- `runtime/layers/attention/backends/aiter.py`: move the BF16 call into `_forward_bf16`; on gfx1250 route through `_forward_bf16_eager` (`@torch.compiler.disable`). gfx942/gfx950 and NVIDIA paths are unchanged.
- `test/unit/test_aiter_attention_impl.py`: regression test that compiles `AITerImpl.forward` with gfx1250 enabled and asserts `flash_attn_func` runs outside Dynamo. It fails on the pre-fix code (`[True] != [False]`) and passes with the fix.

## Accuracy Tests

**Wan2.2-T2V-A14B**, 1x gfx1250, 1280x720, 8 steps, seed 42, torch.compile + aiter attention (with the VAE fix from the companion PR applied so decode completes):

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Warmup / first request | `RuntimeError: An MLIR function requires a Context` in DenoisingStage | completes |
| FlyDSL `flash_attn_func` vs PyTorch SDPA (B=1, H=40, D=128) | - | max abs diff 2e-3 at S=4096, 2e-4 at S=90000, no NaN |
| 33-frame video | no output | correct content (cat and dog baking in a kitchen), consistent across frames |

Long-video (193-frame) validation is still in progress and will be added.

**FLUX.2-dev**, 1x gfx1250, 720p, 50 steps, seed 42, torch.compile + aiter attention, `ENABLE_CK=0`:

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Warmup / first request | `RuntimeError: An MLIR function requires a Context` | completes |
| Image output | no output written | correct content (cat measuring flour, dog stirring with a wooden spoon) |

## Benchmarking and Profiling

| Config | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Wan2.2-T2V-A14B, 1280x720x193f, 8 steps, denoise time per step | crash | 7.73 s |
| FLUX.2-dev, 720p, 50 steps, warmed request (warmup excluded) | crash | 48.88 s |

Both "before" cells are a hard failure, not a slow path: on current main these two configurations do not produce output at all, so there is no pre-fix number to compare against.

The extra cost is one graph break per attention call on gfx1250 only. Wrapping the FlyDSL path as an opaque custom op in aiter would remove it; then this workaround can be dropped.

title: [Fix] [AMD] diffusion: Accept residual and skip_bias in the ROCm Conv3d-to-Conv2d VAE patch
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

**What goes wrong**
Wan VAE decode on ROCm fails with `TypeError: RocmPlatform._replace_conv3d_with_conv2d.<locals>._patched_forward() got an unexpected keyword argument 'residual'`. #38650 made the Wan VAE decoder call `WanCausalConv3d` with `residual=` and `skip_bias=` (the fused conv-bias epilogue). The ROCm Conv3d-to-Conv2d replacement installs its own `forward` that only takes `(x, cache_x)`, so the decoder's first patched conv call raises.

**Where it shows up**
Any ROCm device that enables the patch (`SGLANG_USE_ROCM_VAE_CONV2D=1` or `SGLANG_USE_ROCM_VAE_CONV2D_BF16=1`) and decodes with the Wan VAE through the non-fused cache path. Reproduced with Wan2.2-T2V-A14B on gfx1250: denoising completes, then DecodingStage fails.

**How to fix**
Accept `residual` and `skip_bias` in the patched forward with the same contract as `WanCausalConv3d.forward`: drop the bias when `skip_bias` is set, add `residual` to the conv output.

## Modifications

- `runtime/platforms/rocm.py`: `_patched_forward` takes `residual=None, skip_bias=False`, passes `None` as bias when `skip_bias`, and adds `residual` to the output.
- `test/unit/test_rocm_conv3d_patch.py`: regression test that the patched conv matches the original `WanCausalConv3d` with `residual` and with `skip_bias`. It fails on the pre-fix code with the same `TypeError` and passes with the fix.

## Accuracy Tests

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Patched vs original conv, fp32 (residual / skip_bias) | `TypeError` | max abs diff 1.9e-6 |
| Patched vs original conv, BF16 compute, channels_last_3d (96ch, 90x160) | `TypeError` | rel. error 0.17% to 0.34%, no NaN |
| Wan2.2-T2V-A14B 1280x720, 33 frames, gfx1250 | DecodingStage `TypeError` | decodes; correct content across frames |

Long-video (193-frame) validation is still in progress and will be added.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

| Config | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Wan2.2-T2V-A14B, 1280x720x193f, VAE decode | crash | 119.6 s |

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the PR flow. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`, `/tag-and-rerun-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls to merge.

title: [Fix] deepseek-v4.1: Keep the DSpark draft SWA out of the radix tree
author: hnyls2002
body:
- Under `--enable-encoder-swa-bounded-replay` the target already keeps SWA in a per-request window, but the DSpark draft still forced a paged SWA allocator, so the radix tree kept an SWA component only the draft used. Evicting the draft's SWA then cut prefix hits on Main KV the target could still reuse (#42716 skips the same match gate).
- The DSpark draft SWA now lives in a per-request ring on CUDA: `swa_ring_rows` (`req_pool_idx * ring + pos % ring`) and `get_draft_swa_ring_size` (sliding window + max draft tokens) own its layout for every reader and writer. No pool needs `needs_paged_swa_allocator`, so the tree holds no SWA component.
- Writes reuse the existing ring path (`_ring_inject_loc`, and `build_unified_commit_inject_layout` renamed to `build_ring_commit_inject_layout`), now keyed on the draft pool's `swa_req_ring_size` instead of the unified_kv gate.
- Reads: `get_dspark_swa_page_indices` builds the draft window from the ring (`BuildDsparkSwaRingIndices`), and the draft block writes its ring rows, both eagerly and in the graph.
- A request placed by a prefix hit starts its ring at the hit (`swa_req_ring_valid_from`), so the draft masks earlier positions instead of reading rows left by the slot's previous request.
- The ring is budgeted as a fixed reservation next to the request windows instead of per SWA token.

Only DeepSeek-V4.1 with encoder SWA bounded replay and DSpark on CUDA changes; HIP keeps the paged draft SWA, and every other configuration is unchanged. After a prefix hit, the draft attends only to rows written since the hit until its window fills again.

On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (4x GB300, TP4, DSpark, encoder replay), a prompt whose draft SWA was evicted by 400 other prompts re-hits 8448 of its 8565 tokens instead of 0. GSM8K stays at 98.0% with and without decoder replay, and the average accept length is 3.81 against 3.78 before.

title: [Fix] symm-mem: Name the window registration in the scheduler watchdog dump
author: hope1262946533
body:
## Motivation

With `--enable-symm-mem`, `ncclCommWindowRegister` is called from the forward
path whenever the symmetric-memory pool grows a new segment. That call blocks
in NCCL's Unix-domain-socket fd-exchange rendezvous, which has no timeout of
its own. When the rendezvous wedges, every rank in the group parks in `recvmsg`
and nothing is ever printed: the engine stays up, `/health` keeps returning
200, and no batch makes progress (#36943).

We hit exactly this on a single-node TP8/EP8 Kimi-K3 deployment with MegaMoE:
the engine hung on the first warmup prefill and the server log contained no
error line at all — the only way to tell it apart from an idle engine was to
notice that the log had stopped advancing. Roughly one cold-compile-cache start
in five hung this way.

The scheduler watchdog does eventually notice and dumps, but it cannot say
*what* was in flight, and it waits its full `--watchdog-timeout` (300 s by
default) before it does.

## Modifications

- The registration runs on a worker thread bounded by
  `SGLANG_SYMM_MEM_REGISTRATION_TIMEOUT_S` (default 120 s), so a wedge is
  reported sooner than the watchdog would report it.
- On timeout the registration is named in the log, `pyspy_dump_schedulers()` and
  `faulthandler.dump_traceback()` capture the native and Python stacks, and the
  parent is sent `SIGQUIT` — the same exit path the scheduler and the watchdog
  use, so the normal crash handling runs. The process does not continue: the
  wedged thread still holds the C++ segment mutex, so it could never register
  again.
- `describe_registration_in_progress()` publishes what is in flight, and the
  scheduler watchdog's `dump_info()` includes it, so a stall there reads as
  "symmetric-memory registration in progress: comm=… group=…" instead of a bare
  watchdog timeout.

This does **not** remove the underlying deadlock; it makes it named, fast and
diagnosable. The root cause is tracked in #36943.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A - no change to numerics.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A - the registration call itself is unchanged. The added work is one thread
start plus one join per registration round, and a round only happens when the
symmetric-memory pool grows a segment.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with
      pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit
      tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
      `test/registered/unit/distributed/test_pynccl_allocator_registration_timeout.py`
      covers the bound, the exception passthrough, the timeout path and the
      published state; 5 tests pass on the 0.5.21 image.
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write
      documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
      Not applicable: the new env var is a diagnostic bound, not a user-facing
      feature, and no behaviour changes when the registration succeeds.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the
      accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy)
      and [Benchmark the
      speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
      N/A, see above.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style
      [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Fix] muse: Support Responses namespace tools and defer_loading
author: Fridge003
body:
## Motivation

For Muse Spark, `/v1/responses` drops function-tool `defer_loading` and namespace definitions before rendering the prompt. Namespace calls also need separate `namespace` and `name` fields in Responses outputs, while the model and tool-call parser use qualified names such as `browser.search`.

Original author: [sid-rp](https://github.com/sid-rp) (`sid-rp <sidrp@meta.com>`).

## Modifications

- Gate namespace expansion, nested template tools, deferral forwarding, output-name splitting, and replay-name qualification on `tool_call_parser == "muse"`. Other parsers retain their existing function/custom-tool conversion, rendered schemas, and call names.
- Preserve nested namespace definitions and namespace/member deferral flags for the chat template, while registering qualified names for tool-call parsing.
- Accept both flat and OpenAI-wrapped function members, matching the official Muse Spark chat template. Use the same member normalization for prompt construction, parser registration, and output-name mapping.
- Preserve standalone custom tools when they appear alongside namespaces, including their existing function shim, grammar description, and deferral flag.
- Split qualified names in full/streaming Responses outputs and rejoin them when replaying calls.
- Extend the existing CPU unit tests to exercise the real message-processing/Jinja path and native Muse ATEM parsing, including mixed custom tools and both namespace-member shapes. Add non-Muse regressions for Qwen, Llama, and requests without a parser, including full/streaming dotted function names and replay.

## Validation

Validated on `main` at `f05ad5ec0139d1a41e04115384f6f03b0ac4d19f`. Namespace handling uses main's current Responses parsing helpers and preserves incomplete streaming-call status.

Compared against [the official Muse Spark NVFP4 chat template at revision `4239e4db19376904f2e82c167e78f70abb5455fe`](https://huggingface.co/meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4/blob/4239e4db19376904f2e82c167e78f70abb5455fe/chat_template.jinja), SHA-256 `2341a2d3b1f1b0ac92b6237d46e2fff495109bd3305cacdea54726f5e98411db`.

Cases cover both member shapes, absent/false/true namespace deferral, inherited/explicit member deferral, both deferred-render modes, and mixed standalone function/custom tools. Qualified tool-call and tool-result replay also passed. This checks rendered text, not model-tokenizer token IDs.
- **30 tests and 26 subtests passed**:
  ```bash
  python -m pytest test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_responses_namespace_tools.py test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_responses_custom_tools.py -q
  ```
- The non-Muse regression tests reproduce 12 expected subtest failures against the original PR head `f4a52b7d17`, and pass with the Muse-only guards.
- The broader OpenAI-entrypoint and function-call suites ran **1,141 passed / 9 failed**. All nine failures reproduce on untouched `main` (`f05ad5ec01`) in the same local environment; they involve missing `torchaudio`/`mlx` and related audio paths.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed.
- No model-forward/kernel changes; GPU accuracy/performance benchmarks were not rerun.

<details>
<summary>Pre-existing local-environment failures reproduced on untouched main</summary>

title: [Refactor] kernels/diffusion/tests: Prune dead code and fix tests that never ran
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Six months of fast kernel and diffusion work left a lot behind in `python/sglang/kernels`, `python/sglang/multimodal_gen` and the kernel/diffusion test trees: kernels nothing calls, registry metadata nothing reads, per-model copies of the same fused-op glue, env knobs that do nothing, and tests that pass without testing anything. This PR removes that, and fixes the real bugs the audit turned up along the way (several were silently shipping).

**408 files, +3,629 / -26,346.** About 1.3K of the additions are test oracles and helpers moved out of production modules into `python/sglang/test/kernels/`.

## Bugs fixed (please review these first)

| Area | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| SANA (diffusion) | Since #37816 the VAE loader calls `vae.state_dict()` before `load_state_dict`; `AutoencoderDC` builds its inner diffusers model lazily, so that call built it with random init and the later load returned early. **All 375 VAE tensors were random; every SANA T2I image on main is noise.** | `load_state_dict` loads into an already-built inner model. Regression test in `test_vae_loader.py` (fails on main). |
| GLM-Image (diffusion) | #33555 added an unconditional `query[:, t:] = q_img` write-back after an in-place RoPE; torch 2.14 rejects the self-copy, so **every GLM-Image request fails** in the first DiT block. | Copy back only when the rotation returned new memory. Regression test `test_glm_image_attention.py`; `test_ar_models` re-enabled (fails on main, passes here in 175 s on 2xH200). |
| MiniMax-H3 VAE | The default-on `h3_vae_qk_rmsnorm_rope` path ran in `quality=exact` but was not bit-exact (~25% of rotated channels differ). A second, faster, quality-gated fused path for the same op already existed. | Removed the non-bit-exact path. **Behavior change:** the exact tier now runs the native chain (bit-identical to native); lossless is unchanged. |
| Diffusion CI | `STANDALONE_FILES` moved to `server/gpu_cases.py` in #24630 but the CUDA partition planner kept reading the runner, so **no CUDA standalone file has run since June** (12 2-GPU files + the 1-GPU ones). | Planner reads the case config. All 15 newly scheduled files were run on H200 through the CI code path; one rotted test fixed. |
| Env vars | Code read the legacy `SGL_*` names while docs/`environ.py` define `SGLANG_*`, and the rewrite is one-directional, so the documented names did nothing: `SGLANG_USE_DEEPGEMM_BMM` (5 models), `SGLANG_DG_USE_NVRTC`, `SGLANG_CPU_QUANTIZATION`, `SGLANG_DSA_TOPK_ROW_SPLIT`. | Read via `envs`; legacy names still work. |
| `BaseFusedOp` | `KernelBackend.FLYDSL` mapped to a missing `forward_flydsl`, so `SGLANG_FORCE_FUSED_OP_BACKEND=flydsl` raised `AttributeError`. | Stub added + test. |
| Tests that never ran | `test_fp8_kernel` returned early on every CUDA GPU with sm>=90; `test_swapab_attention` was registered on H100 but gated to sm_10x (production SM100 kernel had no CUDA coverage); sm_100 / sm_120 / 2-GPU / 4-GPU diffusion unit tests sat on a 1-GPU H100 lane; `test_qwen_image21` cache tests exercised a test-local re-implementation of the fix. | Each now runs on hardware that satisfies its gate (or was deleted with its dead kernel); the qwen_image21 tests drive the real block and fail when the fix is reverted. |
| SenseNova-U1 | `FlowMatchingHead` called `SimpleMLPAdaLN` with a signature the class doesn't have (crash for `fm_head_layers > 2`). | Restored the timestep-conditioned head; test fails on main. |

## Modifications

### Kernels (`python/sglang/kernels`, -13.8K)
- **Dead / test-only kernels removed** (each re-verified with whole-repo grep incl. string lookups): seg_la kernel, dsv4 `fused_ape_pool_norm_rope`, tilelang `fp8_index`, KDA prefill timing scaffolding, nvlink push/pull all-reduce wrappers, inkling two-shot all-reduce, `cutedsl_gdn_mtp_ring` T=1 entry, non-`f_b` FlyDSL KDA decode, dsa `GetK/GetS`, adler32 whole-tensor entry points, ReplaySSM circular commit, cvt helpers, mxfp8 v-cache update, fp8 ue8m0/hopper/transpose helpers, `w8a8_block_fp8_matmul`, `awq_gemm_triton`, rocm `tkw1`, `moe_fused_gate_jit`, inkling gate v1, `post_reorder_triton_kernel`, `fused_inplace_qknorm_across_heads`, elementwise `silu_and_mul_triton`/autotune path, `rms_normalize_triton`, stale `top_p_renorm_triton` copy, and others.
- **Legacy DSV4 compressor path removed** (`compress_old.py`, `fused_compress_triton.py`, srt `dsv4/compress_hip.py`, the old `CompressorBackendMixin`): every CUDA/HIP backend uses `compressor_v2`; `fused_norm_rope_inplace` (live) moved to `dsv4/elementwise.py`. AOT dsv4 q/k norm+RoPE ops (duplicates of the JIT ones) removed.
- **Registry (option A):** the KernelSpec inventory stays; write-only metadata goes (`FormatSignature`, `KernelSpec.format_signature/description/group/name`, `BaseFusedOp.format_signature/descriptions/dispatch_forward`, unused selector/platform helpers). `spec.CUDA_ONLY` replaces ~44 inline frozensets. Unused `BaseFusedOp`s (4 RMSNorm, Gelu/GeluTanh/ReLU2/QuickGELU) removed; facade wrappers nobody imports removed (this also fixes facade functions shadowed by same-named submodules). `Fp8ScaledMMOp` no longer declares an SM90 heuristic as a capability.
- **#42184 criteria applied** to the four remaining gate sites (route-quant, engram, vision_rope, minimax_m3): gates check eligibility, launchers enforce contracts.
- **Duplicates:** sparse-MLA decode reuses the shared kernels (bit-exact, 720 cases x 2 archs incl. fully masked rows); mxfp8 gfx95 reuses `mxfp8_quant`. Forks that are *not* bit-exact stay, each with a one-line comment (grok RMSNorm, gfx1250 qk-RMSNorm, int8 group quant on ROCm, marlin SiTU, minimax Gemma RMSNorm).
- **Test oracles shipped in op modules moved to `sglang.test.kernels`** (LPLB, dsa transform index, DCP LSE combine, dsv4 K-cache quant refs, extend attention, dspark window, multigpu launcher, mhc, per-token-group quant dispatch).

### Diffusion (`python/sglang/multimodal_gen`, -9.4K)
- **Dead code:** SenseNova-U1 unreachable chat/interleave/it2i paths (~2.6K; T2I output byte-identical), auto-residency estimators and the warmup stage-iteration calibration chain nothing read, SANA-WM parity debug harness (`SANAWM_*` env hooks incl. `torch.load` input injection), `MINIMAX_H3_USE_FUSED_NORM` path, unresolved MiniMax-H3 euler scheduler, registry subprocess-inspect path (pointed at a nonexistent module), delta-gzip realtime encoding (server + web UI), bundled-overlay lookup, `EncodingStage`, bitsandbytes 4-bit swap, `generate_with_lora` (could never run), `convert_hf_to_fp8.py`, unused platform hooks, unread `ServerArgs` fields, etc.
- **Env:** 12 `envs.py` entries nothing read removed (+ the docs rows presenting 5 of them as working knobs); raw reads of `SGLANG_ENABLE_FUSED_QKNORM_ROPE` / `MINIMAX_H3_VAE_*` declared in `envs.py` with identical parsing; unprefixed GDN dev knobs dropped.
- **Refactors (bit-exact):** `BitExactFusionGate.run()` replaces 24 hand-written verify-once/fallback blocks and the `mismatch_msg` boilerplate; one LayerNorm+modulate helper for FLUX.3/GLM/LongCat; `sites/` exports one `QualityGatedFusion` per family instead of four wrappers each (~50 facade entries, 28 imports gone). Sites that are hand-tuned for launch overhead, re-raise, verify inside the try, or differ in reference were left as they are (listed in the commit messages).

### Tests and CI
- Deleted always-skipped tests (env var set nowhere, `skipif(True)`, hard-coded dev paths), tautologies (default/literal echoes, `inspect.getsource` shape tests, log-format echoes, torch-behavior tests), duplicate cases and duplicate helpers; trimmed grids with no extra coverage (`fused_fp8_qkv_kv_cache` 1,344 -> 288 cases, AOT `moe_align` 4,368 -> 144, AOT per-token-group quant 3,632 -> 320). CI-tooling meta-tests are intentionally kept.
- New lane wiring: swapab on B200; Blackwell, SM120 and 4-GPU diffusion unit steps; 2-GPU diffusion unit files as 2-gpu standalone files; `quant-videogen` installed for its tests; comm benches no longer register no-op AMD runs; HPC-Ops tests (always skipped: the package isn't in the CI venv) disabled explicitly.
- **CI cost:** the standalone-file fix adds runners (1-GPU H100: 5 -> 6 partitions; 2-GPU: 3 -> 5 by current estimates). The estimates are 2-15x above the measured H200 times; I'll copy this PR's CI-measured values into `STANDALONE_FILE_EST_TIMES` before merge.

## Accuracy Tests

End-to-end, same GPU, fixed seed, base vs this branch (fused paths confirmed active by a gate tracer on both sides; no gate disabled):

| Model | Paths exercised | Result |
|---|---|---|
| ERNIE-Image, LongCat-Image, FLUX.2-klein-4B, Joy, MOSS-Image, Anima, Qwen-Image, Wan2.1-1.3B, Helios-Distilled | `BitExactFusionGate.run`, LN+modulate helper, QK-norm+RoPE, handler-table sites, gated residual | byte-identical |
| GLM-Image (1024², 30 steps) | LN+modulate helper, QK-LN | identical to main+fix; fused == native |
| SANA 600M (512², 20 steps) | VAE fix | identical to main+fix; reproducible across processes (main is noise) |
| SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT T2I | dead-path removal | PNG md5 identical |
| Z-Image-Turbo server warmup | residency/warmup cleanup | PNG identical, same peak memory |
| MiniMax-H3 VAE decoder | lossless in-place path / exact tier | lossless identical; exact == native |

Kernel dedups were checked bit-for-bit on H200 and GB300 (scripts in the commit messages' descriptions).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No perf-path changes intended. `BitExactFusionGate.run` was not applied to the launch-overhead-tuned sites (the closures add ~160-180 ns per call on the host).

## Validation

- **H200 (sm_90):** every file under `test/registered/kernels/ops`, `test/registered/unit` and `multimodal_gen/test/unit` (1,624 files). Failures were re-run on main: identical failing test ids (rust extensions not built in the source tree, NPU-only, multi-GPU tests on one GPU, pre-existing diffusion kernel failures); 2 port collisions from parallel runs pass alone. 
- **GB300 (sm_103):** every file under `test/registered/kernels/ops` (334 files): failing ids identical to main.

title: [Fix] bailing: MoE gate dtype follows config.router_dtype
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Motivation

`BailingMoeV3` forces the MoE gate GEMM to bf16, overriding `router_dtype="fp32"` from Ling checkpoints. The bf16 gate perturbs top-k routing enough to cause output variance (reported by the Ling team on Ling-3.x checkpoints; the fp32 gate is what the checkpoint was trained/tuned against).

## Modifications

Gate dtype follows the checkpoint config: `router_dtype == "fp32"` (or absent) → fp32 gate; any other value → bf16. No behavior change for configs that don't set `router_dtype="fp32"`.

## Accuracy Tests

Routing-affecting change: greedy outputs shift back to the fp32-gate reference. Ling team validated on their internal branch and the ling-v3-open branch.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

On Hopper the fp32 gate GEMM does not use tensor cores, so decode gives back part of the bf16-gate speedup; correctness takes priority.

Co-authored-by: 文贤 <luoyuan.luo@antgroup.com>

title: [Fix] Inkling: frame constrained output in native message tokens
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Motivation

With `--reasoning-parser inkling`, `response_format` / `regex` / `ebnf` constraints do not follow Inkling's wire format: Inkling frames every message with native tokens (`<|message_model|><|content_text|>…<|end_message|>`), but on `main` the constraint neither waits for the real think-end token nor admits the answer frame. Live on `thinkingmachines/Inkling-NVFP4` @ `06b81b120e`: the answer header is missing, prose or extra data surrounds the JSON, whitespace runs to `max_tokens`, regex payloads repeat (`Yesyes`), and `continue_final_message` + constraint fails 54/54.

## Modifications

Inkling's format knowledge lives with its reasoning detector: `BaseReasoningFormatDetector.get_answer_frame()` returns `None` by default; Inkling's returns an `InklingAnswerFrame` (`parser/answer_frame.py`) owning the framed constraint types, framing token IDs, open-text-block check, the frame's structural tag and the canonical auto-tool tag. `ReasonerGrammarBackend` only composes a detector's frame with the payload grammar; detectors/backends without a frame keep their existing dispatch.

- **Native think-end** (contains #40894): the reasoning-deferred grammar takes think-end IDs from the detector, so Inkling's native `<|end_message|>` (200010) ends thinking; the canonical auto-tool tag skips deferral.
- **Whole-turn frame**: `json` / `regex` / `ebnf` constraints compile into one token-level structural tag — optional thinking message, answer header, payload, `<|end_message|>`. With `continue_final_message`, the payload starts inside the already-open text block.
- **Strict thinking**: the frame caps thinking at the request's `thinking_budget`, else the server's `SGLANG_MAX_THINK_TOKENS` (request overrides server). Distinct budgets compile distinct frames, cached under a normalized key (negatives → unlimited, server value → default key), bounded to 32 variants.
- **xgrammar backend**: framed grammars compile on an uncached `GrammarCompiler` — the cached one mixes token-level structural tags of different shapes (fixed upstream by mlc-ai/xgrammar#943, unreleased; [reproducer](https://github.com/mlc-ai/xgrammar/issues/951#issuecomment-6159764165)). Framing token IDs are reserved from matching text in the framing compiler only.

Split out of #42844, which moves Inkling prompt rendering and output parsing to `tml-renderers` and builds on this change. Works with `main`'s existing Inkling renderer and parsers.

## Accuracy Tests

Devbox: 4x GB300, `thinkingmachines/Inkling-NVFP4`, cookbook GB300 NVFP4 TP4 recipe plus `--reasoning-parser inkling --tool-call-parser inkling` (strict rows add `--enable-strict-thinking` with `SGLANG_MAX_THINK_TOKENS=48`).

| Check | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Constrained output: Chat + Responses `json_schema` / `json_object` / `regex` / `ebnf`, thinking on/off, stream and non-stream, required and named tools (3 rounds) | 11/28 | 84/84 |
| Same rows, reasoning parser only | — | 40/40 |
| `continue_final_message` with `regex` / `json_schema` / `ebnf` (3 rounds) | 0/54 | 48/54* |
| Strict thinking budgets 6/20/48/none (3 rounds) | — | 24/24 (stops at exactly N tokens, then a valid answer) |
| Strict thinking, one thinking message, natural and budget-forced end | — | 12/12 |
| Constrained rows on the strict server | — | 28/28 |

\* The 6 misses are effort-high `ebnf` `[0-9]+` answers that keep adding digits (`426`) — a digits-only grammar cannot end the sentence, a grammar/prompt mismatch, not framing.

Unit tests (xgrammar 0.2.7): `unit/constrained/` + `unit/function_call/` 775 passed; recipe incl. `test_serving_chat.py` 271 passed @ `4c0c9a0530`. The detector-ownership refactor at that head is behavior-identical to the pre-refactor head: compiled grammars, dispatch and per-step token masks match on 200 probe cases (Inkling and Qwen3 detectors, strict on/off, `json`/`regex`/`ebnf`/`structural_tag`, plain and continuation prompts, five budgets).

Unconstrained requests without strict thinking do not take the changed paths.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not performance-related. Framed grammars compile once per distinct constraint (and budget variant); the compiled grammar is cached as before.

title: [Fix] gateway: Drop unused npyz dev-dependency to unbreak builds after zip yank
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Motivation

On 2026-10-16 the `zip` maintainer yanked every release except 9.0.3 after security advisories GHSA-vv5m-jxxh-4627, GHSA-4v9h-p7m9-rh26, and GHSA-4684-h2q9-2vcp; old lines such as 0.6.x will not get backports (zip-rs/zip2#1075). `sgl-model-gateway` declares `npyz` with the `npz` feature as a dev-dependency, which requires `zip ^0.6` (still the case in the latest npyz, 0.9.1). The gateway does not commit a `Cargo.lock`, so every fresh resolve — docker image builds, fresh checkouts — now fails:

```
error: failed to select a version for the requirement `zip = "^0.6"`
required by package `npyz v0.8.0`
    ... which satisfies dependency `npyz = "^0.8"` of package `sgl-model-gateway v0.3.2`
```

Example: the release-docker build in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38871712398 fails at the `maturin build` step with this error.

## Modifications

- Remove the `npyz` dev-dependency. No gateway code references `npyz`, and with it gone `zip` is no longer in the dependency graph.
- Remove `scripts/generate_vision_golden.py`, the CI step in `pr-test-rust.yml` that installs torch/transformers to run it, and the `.gitignore` entry for its output. No gateway test reads the `.npz` fixtures it produced.

## Verification

On clean `git archive` trees of `sgl-model-gateway`:

| | `cargo metadata --format-version 1 -q` |
|---|---|
| `upstream/main` | exit 101 (`failed to select a version for the requirement zip = "^0.6"`) |
| this PR | exit 0 |

On this PR, `cargo fetch` succeeds, `cargo metadata` from `bindings/python` (the maturin entry point) and `bindings/golang` exits 0, and `cargo tree -e normal,build,dev -i zip` finds no `zip` package.

title: [Fix] minimax_h3: Support out-of-tree platforms
author: labAxiaoming
body:
## Motivation

MiniMax H3's full-loop denoising stage rejects out-of-tree platforms because its platform allowlist only includes CUDA, HIP, CPU, MPS, NPU, and XPU.

This prevents out-of-tree backends from reaching the denoising loop, even when they provide the required device APIs and operators.

## Modifications

- Accept `current_platform.is_out_of_tree()` in the full-loop denoising platform check.
- Update the error message to include out-of-tree platforms.

This change removes the platform gate for out-of-tree backends. Each backend remains responsible for implementing the required operations.

## Testing

Tested on `<4687bb92b7ed6fad5cd2d11350b90b8f1bd6c6b6>`:

```bash
SGLANG_DIFFUSION_PLATFORM_OVERRIDE=cpu PYTHONPATH=python \
python -m pytest -q \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_minimax_h3_denoise_loop.py
```

Result: 11 passed, 18 warnings.

Added a regression test verifying that an OOT platform passes the
platform check when all built-in platform predicates are false.
Confirmed that removing the OOT condition makes this test fail.

author: fsaady
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.

Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

Nemotron-H’s ModelOpt mixed-precision override rejects flashinfer_cutedsl for checkpoints containing W4A16_NVFP4 experts, even when the existing W4A16 opt-in is enabled.
Allow this supported explicit configuration, following the Qwen precedent in #39126 and using the implementation already introduced in #35120. Preserve the automatic Marlin selection established by #33543.

## Modifications

- Allow --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutedsl when SGLANG_FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL_NVFP4_W4A16=1 on SM100-family GPUs.
- Preserve auto → marlin, explicit Marlin support, and Nemotron’s existing --moe-a2a-backend none requirement.
- Update the validation error and add regression coverage for backend selection, the environment flag, unsupported hardware, and A2A restrictions.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K, 200 questions, thinking enabled, using the existing Nemotron CI evaluator.
B200, TP1, SGLang 0.5.21 / FlashInfer 0.6.18, Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4;
temperature 0, seed 42, concurrency 32, 16,384-token cap, speculation disabled.
Results from the confirmation run:

| Backend | Correct | Accuracy |
|---|---:|---:|
| Marlin | 188/200 | 94.0% |
| CuTe DSL W4A16 | 190/200 | 95.0% |

No degradation observed in this run. The small difference is consistent with noise.


## Speed Tests and Profiling

### End-to-end serving

B200, TP1, SGLang 0.5.21 / FlashInfer 0.6.18, same NVFP4 checkpoint, concurrency
32, static 57,600 shared-prefix + 6,400 new input tokens and 400 output tokens,
8 warmup + 160 measured requests, AIPerf 0.12.0.

| MoE backend | Output tokens/s | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|
| Marlin | 1,576.63 | 1.00× |
| CuTe DSL W4A16 |  2,199.04 | 1.40× (+39.9%) |

Both measurements completed all 160 requests with zero errors and 64,000 output 
tokens.

### Isolated grouped-GEMM microbenchmarks

A separate B200 study invoking kernels directly (FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1).
Replayed nine expert-assignment patterns captured from Nemotron-3.5-Lightning,
using its checkpoint's NVFP4 expert weights and BF16 activations. These exercise
Nemotron's actual MoE workloads and help explain the serving speedup above.
Logical up K→N: 2688→1856; down: 1856→2688.

Selected cases below. Times are median milliseconds per grouped-GEMM invocation,
covering all assigned experts for one projection, without activation or final
combine. 
T is the number of input tokens before routing, and each case replays its full
captured per-expert assignment vector. These measurements help illustrate 
the kernel-level gains behind the serving speedup.

| Case | T | Projection | Marlin (ms) | CuTe DSL (ms) | Speedup |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A | 32 | Up | 0.0439 | 0.0242 | 1.81× |
| A | 32 | Down | 0.0430 | 0.0231 | 1.86× |
| F | 16 | Up | 0.0675 | 0.0431 | 1.57× |
| F | 16 | Down | 0.0665 | 0.0448 | 1.48× |
| G | 2,129 | Up | 0.8267 | 0.1986 | 4.16× |
| G | 2,129 | Down | 0.7558 | 0.1988 | 3.80× |
| H | 14,896 | Up | 4.1495 | 0.8799 | 4.72× |
| H | 14,896 | Down | 3.4406 | 0.8886 | 3.87× |
| I | 15,436 | Up | 4.2833 | 0.9067 | 4.72× |
| I | 15,436 | Down | 3.5455 | 0.9163 | 3.87× |

CuTe DSL was faster in every tested case: **1.44–4.72×** for pure up/down GEMMs
and **1.67–5.10×** for up+ReLU² (fused CuTe DSL versus Marlin plus standalone
activation), across all nine measured patterns.

title: [Fix] dsv41: Preserve tool-result image order and current-turn thinking
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Motivation

Port the upstream chat-encoding fix [deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash@314113f](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash/commit/314113f8a7dadb388215396ba5fbee2c610a04d6) into the V4.1 prompt encoder, which has the same two bugs:

1. **Tool-result images out of order.** `encode_messages()` collected images before tool messages were merged and tool results re-sorted by call order. When tool results arrive out of `tool_call` order and carry images, the prompt's `<｜deepseek_image｜>` placeholders are reordered but the returned image list keeps arrival order, so images bind to the wrong placeholders.
2. **`drop_thinking` drops current-turn reasoning across tool calls.** A merged tool-result-only user message counted as a new user turn, so the reasoning of the current-turn assistant message preceding the tool results was stripped. Tool results alone do not start a new user turn; the current turn's reasoning should be kept until a real new user request arrives.

## Modifications

In `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/encoding_dsv41.py`:

- `encode_messages` validates textual fields for image placeholders, then merges tool messages and sorts tool results by call order, and only then collects images — the returned image list now matches the placeholder order in the prompt.
- `merge_tool_messages` keeps structured tool content (list `content` / `content_blocks`) instead of flattening it to joined text.
- `find_last_user_index` skips user messages holding only tool results, so `drop_thinking` keeps the current turn's reasoning across tool calls and drops it once a new user request arrives. The existing `developer`-as-user-turn behavior is kept.

## Accuracy Tests

Prompt-encoding logic only; no model forward / kernel changes. Unit tests in `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py`:

- `test_dsv41_tool_result_images_follow_prompt_order` — 4 input formats (`content_blocks`, `tool_messages`, `tool_content_blocks`, `context`); asserts prompt-tail order, media URL order, and that inputs are not mutated. Subtests fail on pre-fix code.
- `test_dsv41_drop_thinking_without_tools` — current-turn reasoning kept across a tool result, dropped once a real new user turn arrives. Fails on pre-fix code.
- `test_dsv41_rejects_image_placeholder_in_text` — placeholder rejection for `user` and `tool` messages.

`test_serving_chat.py` full run: 159 passed. `test_deepseekv41_detector.py`: 10 passed. pre-commit clean.

title: [Fix] diffusion: Unmerge LoRA layers the next adapter does not cover
author: OnePunchMonk
body:
## Problem
If adapter A is merged into a layer and `set_lora` switches to adapter B that does not cover that layer, the layer is only marked `disable_lora`. Its base weight still holds A's merged delta, so `forward` keeps applying A. `unmerge_lora_weights` also returned early on `disable_lora`, so deactivate/unmerge could not remove it either.

## Fix
- `_apply_lora_to_layers`: a layer no new adapter covers is unmerged (if merged) and cleared before being disabled. Clearing matters: `merge_lora_weights` re-enables any layer that still has `lora_A` set.

title: [Fix] srt: Apply --gc-threshold in every server process and freeze every tokenizer worker
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

`--gc-threshold` is applied with `gc.set_threshold` in the launching process only. The scheduler and detokenizer subprocesses keep Python's default thresholds, so a deployment that raised the gen2 threshold to stop periodic full collections still sees them in the scheduler, where they cost the most.

The post-warmup `/freeze_gc` request freezes the scheduler and detokenizer, but with `--tokenizer-worker-num` greater than one it is served by whichever tokenizer worker receives it, so only that worker's interpreter is frozen. The other workers keep scanning their long-lived heap on every collection.

Defaults are unchanged: with no `--gc-threshold` nothing new is set, and the single-tokenizer path still freezes exactly where it did.

## Modifications

- `freeze_gc` (`python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py`) takes an optional `gc_threshold` and applies it with `gc.set_threshold` before `gc.freeze()`; `None` leaves the thresholds alone.
- `FreezeGCReq` carries `gc_threshold: Optional[List[int]] = None`. `TokenizerManager.freeze_gc` reads the configured threshold off the device args, sends it with the request, and passes it to its own local freeze; the scheduler and detokenizer handlers pass `recv_req.gc_threshold` through.
- `_wait_and_warmup` (`python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/http_server.py`) gains `post_warmup_callback`, run after warmup and before the routed `/freeze_gc` request. In multi-tokenizer mode each worker's warmup thread gets a callback that freezes that worker's interpreter with the configured threshold, so every worker freezes locally and the routed request still covers the scheduler and detokenizer.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no change to model execution or outputs. Only garbage-collector thresholds and freeze points move, and only in the processes that were previously skipped.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable as a benchmark: the change removes recurring gen2 collections from the scheduler and the extra tokenizer workers when a threshold is configured, and is a no-op otherwise.

Unit tests on this head (CPU, `pytest`): `test/registered/unit/utils/test_common.py` and `test/registered/unit/managers/test_multi_tokenizer_mixin.py`, 37 passed. New cases: `freeze_gc` preserves the thresholds without a configuration and applies a configured one; each tokenizer worker freezes locally with the configured threshold after warmup and before the routed request.

title: [Fix] [AMD] moe/topk: Preserve fp32 bias across aiter routing paths
author: Kylinny
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #44794. `select_experts` rounded an fp32 correction bias to bf16 before the AITER grouped router could select its existing fp32 path. This loses bias distinctions and can change the selected experts.

## Changes

Preserve fp32 correction biases in `select_experts`. In the AITER branch, choose one logits/bias dtype pair before dispatching to either radix4 or AITER: an fp32 bias keeps fp32 routing, while other biases keep the existing logits-dtype conversion. Both dispatches now receive the same precision across the radix4 1024-token cutoff, and the fp32 path avoids an unused bias downcast.

Consolidate the CPU regressions into the existing correction-bias cache test file. They exercise `select_experts` through the actual grouped-router dispatch, mocking only native calls. Add eight native integration cases to the existing AMD radix4 test file; their offset fp32 bias has unique winners that collapse under bf16 rounding.

## Affected configurations

This changes AITER routing when the gate supplies an fp32 correction bias alongside lower-precision logits: `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, Kimi-K3, DeepSeek-family configurations that retain an fp32 bias, and `ExaoneMoeForCausalLM`. Non-fp32 bias conversion, the JIT router, dynamic-bias handling, and non-AITER paths retain their existing behavior.

The fix preserves the supplied bias precision. It does not recover precision already lost when producing bf16 gate logits; router-GEMM precision is tracked separately in #34857.

## Validation

The results below were executed at `d7a09baf8b3f` against base `3927a73a3407`, before rebasing onto `main` at `7e142dd9fdc4`. Tests were not rerun for this merge.

- CPU: all five correction-bias cache/dispatch tests and all five GLM gate-bias tests passed. The fp32 dispatch regressions fail on unpatched main.
- One AMD Instinct MI355X: all 55 tests in `test_moe_route_radix4.py` passed, including GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V3 routing shapes, K3 batches of 1024/1025 tokens, and radix4 enabled/disabled. All eight new integration cases fail on unpatched main `3927a73a3407`.
- Native environment: Torch `2.9.0a0+git7bcbafe`, HIP `7.0.51831-a3e329ad8`, AITER `285579b6211b0da30f35b91a890c29c823597cd1`, Triton `3.6.0`, FlyDSL `0.4.0`.
- Pre-commit checks passed for all changed files.

Full-model GSM8K and decode-throughput comparisons for GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3 (radix4 on/off), and an fp32-bias DeepSeek-V3 configuration have not been run. The native results above cover router kernels and dispatch, not model accuracy or serving throughput.

title: [Fix] hicache: Order write-back host copies after the forward that produced the KV
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

With `--hicache-write-policy write_back`, KV pages could be copied to host before the forward pass that produced them had finished. The host copy then held whatever the page contained at submit time, and a later load-back served that stale KV to another request. Two paths reached the device-to-host copy without any dependency on the forward stream:

- **Insert-time SWA window backups.** Write-back defers Full and Mamba backups to eviction, but the tree core still published an unbacked SWA window when a request's nodes were inserted. That backup was queued while the request's own forward could still be writing the window.
- **The blocking write-back drain.** Eviction submits everything queued in the tick on the device-to-host stream with no fence, and an evicted SWA page can belong to a checkpoint whose producing forward has not completed.

## Modifications

- `UnifiedTreeCore` (Python) and `unified_tree_core.rs` (Rust): under write-back, insertion never returns a `BackupKV` action, so SWA windows are no longer published at insert time. The incremental-component check no longer special-cases SWA under write-back.
- `HiCacheController.start_writing(wait_for_forward=...)`: a new keyword-only flag. When set and a `write_fence_stream` is configured, the device-to-host stream waits on it before the copies are submitted. The scheduler sets `write_fence_stream` to the model runner's forward stream next to the existing `load_fence_stream`.
- `UnifiedRadixCache.writing_check(write_back=True)` passes `wait_for_forward=True` on the blocking drain. Write-through and the asynchronous write-back flush are unchanged, and the default keeps every other caller as it was.
- Tests:
  - `test_hicache_write_back_ordering.py` (new): a checkpointed request whose forward is still writing on a separate stream; evicting an older SWA window of that request must copy the values the forward wrote, not the pre-forward contents.
  - `test_unified_hicache_regressions.py`: the blocking drain waits for the fence stream before copying both a tick's queued backup and the eviction victim.
  - `test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py` and the Rust crate tests: write-back insertion of backed Full nodes publishes no SWA window and leaves no pending ack; the Mamba pending-ack eviction test now queues its window backup explicitly instead of relying on insert-time publication.

## Accuracy Tests

- `cargo test` for `rust/sglang-radix-tree` (`--no-default-features`, as `pr-test-rust-workspace.yml` runs it): 931 passed, 0 failed.
- On one CUDA GPU, with both `SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND=rust` and `=python`: `test_hicache_write_back_ordering.py`, `test_unified_hicache_regressions.py::TestTransferStreamOrdering`, and the two touched cases in `test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py` pass.
- Without the runtime changes, `test_hicache_write_back_ordering.py` fails on both backends: the host copy holds the pre-forward contents instead of what the forward wrote.
- No numerics change: the fix only orders existing copies after their producer and removes an early backup that eviction performs later.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The new wait is a single `wait_stream` on the blocking write-back drain, which already blocks on every ack; the asynchronous paths do not take it.

title: [Fix] deepseek_v4: route unquantized BF16/F16/F32 checkpoints off the MXFP4 expert path
author: Kylinny
body:
## Motivation

Fixes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/44810.

A DeepSeek-V4 BF16 checkpoint carries no `quantization_config`. In `ModelConfig`, `is_fp4_experts` is initialized from the `SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_EXPERTS` env var (default `True`) and is only overridden when `try_detect_fp4_experts()` returns a non-`None` value. That detector returned `None` for any dtype other than the mxfp4-packed (`U8`/`I8`/`F4`) or FP8-converted (`F8_E4M3`) layouts — including unquantized `BF16`/`F16`/`F32`. As a result, an unquantized DSV4 checkpoint kept `is_fp4_experts=True` under default settings and the auto MoE-runner backend routed it to the `flashinfer_mxfp4` path, while the rest of the stack treated it as unquantized, crashing the first request with `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3)`.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/configs/deepseek_v4.py`: `try_detect_fp4_experts()` now returns `False` for unquantized routed-expert dtypes (`BF16`/`F16`/`F32`), so unquantized checkpoints take the unquantized expert path instead of falling back to the FP4-experts env default. Genuine MXFP4 (`U8`/`I8`/`F4` → `True`) and FP8-converted (`F8_E4M3` → `False`) detection is unchanged; unknown or unreadable headers still return `None` and fall back to the user/env default.
- `test/registered/unit/configs/test_deepseek_v4_fp4_detect.py`: new unit tests covering `BF16`/`F16`/`F32` → `False`, `U8`/`I8`/`F4` → `True`, `F8_E4M3` → `False`, and `None` for unreadable/empty checkpoint dirs.

## Reproducer (no GPU required)

A full GPU repro is infeasible here (needs 8x B300 plus a DSV4 BF16 checkpoint), so the bug is demonstrated at the config-routing layer where it lives. Save the script below as `repro_44810.py` in the repo root and run `python3 repro_44810.py`. It builds fake checkpoint dirs (a single safetensors shard whose header declares one routed-expert weight tensor of the given dtype) and drives the real `try_detect_fp4_experts()` plus the real `probe_routed_expert_weight_dtype()` (AST-extracted from the repo; the only stubs are `transformers`/`QuantizationConfig` class-level deps and `find_local_repo_dir`, which is unreachable for local dirs), then applies the same `None`-vs-env-default logic `ModelConfig` uses.

```python
import ast, json, os, re, struct, sys, tempfile, types
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional

REPO = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

weight_utils_src = open(f"{REPO}/python/sglang/srt/model_loader/weight_utils.py").read()
tree = ast.parse(weight_utils_src)

def _wanted(n):
    if isinstance(n, ast.Assign):
        return any(getattr(t, "id", "") == "_ROUTED_EXPERT_KEY_RE" for t in n.targets)
    return getattr(n, "name", None) == "probe_routed_expert_weight_dtype"

seg = [n for n in tree.body if _wanted(n)]
wmod = types.ModuleType("sglang.srt.model_loader.weight_utils")
wmod.__dict__.update({"re": re, "json": json, "struct": struct, "os": os,
                      "Path": Path, "Optional": Optional,
                      "logging": __import__("logging")})
exec(compile(ast.Module(body=seg, type_ignores=[]), "<wu>", "exec"), wmod.__dict__)

def make_pkg(name):
    m = types.ModuleType(name); m.__path__ = []; sys.modules[name] = m; return m

for pkg in ["sglang", "sglang.srt", "sglang.srt.configs",
            "sglang.srt.model_loader", "sglang.srt.utils"]:
    make_pkg(pkg)
sys.modules["sglang.srt.model_loader.weight_utils"] = wmod
sys.modules["sglang.srt.utils"].find_local_repo_dir = lambda *a, **k: None

dv4_tree = ast.parse(open(f"{REPO}/python/sglang/srt/configs/deepseek_v4.py").read())
fn_node = next(n for n in dv4_tree.body
               if getattr(n, "name", None) == "try_detect_fp4_experts")
dv4 = types.SimpleNamespace()
dv4.__dict__.update({"os": os, "logging": __import__("logging"), "Optional": Optional})
exec(compile(ast.Module(body=[fn_node], type_ignores=[]), "<dv4>", "exec"), dv4.__dict__)

KEY = "model.layers.0.mlp.experts.0.w1.weight"

def make_ckpt(dtype_str):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    header = json.dumps({KEY: {"dtype": dtype_str, "shape": [2048, 4096]}}).encode()
    with open(os.path.join(d, "model.safetensors"), "wb") as f:
        f.write(struct.pack("<Q", len(header))); f.write(header)
    return d

for dtype in ["BF16", "F16", "F32", "U8", "I8", "F4", "F8_E4M3"]:
    detected = dv4.try_detect_fp4_experts(make_ckpt(dtype))
    is_fp4_experts = detected if detected is not None else True  # env default
    print(f"safetensors dtype={dtype:8s} -> try_detect_fp4_experts()={detected!s:5s}"
          f"  is_fp4_experts={is_fp4_experts}")
```

**Before** (also logs `Unexpected routed-expert safetensors dtype=BF16 for DeepSeek V4` to stderr):

```
safetensors dtype=BF16     -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=None   is_fp4_experts=True
safetensors dtype=F16      -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=None   is_fp4_experts=True
safetensors dtype=F32      -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=None   is_fp4_experts=True
safetensors dtype=U8       -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=True   is_fp4_experts=True
safetensors dtype=I8       -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=True   is_fp4_experts=True
safetensors dtype=F4       -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=True   is_fp4_experts=True
safetensors dtype=F8_E4M3  -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=False  is_fp4_experts=False
```

**After**:

```
safetensors dtype=BF16     -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=False  is_fp4_experts=False
safetensors dtype=F16      -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=False  is_fp4_experts=False
safetensors dtype=F32      -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=False  is_fp4_experts=False
safetensors dtype=U8       -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=True   is_fp4_experts=True
safetensors dtype=I8       -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=True   is_fp4_experts=True
safetensors dtype=F4       -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=True   is_fp4_experts=True
safetensors dtype=F8_E4M3  -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=False  is_fp4_experts=False
```

title: [Fix] unified_cache: Resize test allocator before allocating backed pages
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

The `resize with live allocations` subtest in `test_unified_post_capture_sizing.py` finalizes a 64 MiB reservation to 16 MiB, then allocates before resizing the allocator. The full-attention allocator still grows down from the old 64 MiB frontier, so allocation-time `_zero_pages_kernel` writes into the unbacked tail instead of reaching the intended `non-empty` assertion.

Observed in [this CI failure](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38988923342/job/117270212489): `CUDBG_EXCEPTION_WARP_MMU_FAULT` in `_zero_pages_kernel`, process exit code -6. The affected test and allocator code are also present on main; this is independent of #43387.

## Modifications

Resize the empty allocator immediately after finalizing backing, before creating the live allocation. The subsequent resize still verifies that a non-empty allocator is rejected. This matches the production startup ordering and changes only the test setup.

## Validation

- Python syntax and `git diff --check` passed.
- Pre-commit checks run on the changed file.
- CUDA execution is pending CI; the local machine has no NVIDIA GPU. The diagnosis is based on the failing CI log and the allocation/backing code path.

title: [Fix] deepseek-v4.1: Serve prompt-logprob requests under decoder SWA bounded replay
author: hnyls2002
body:
- `late_layer_whole_extend` picks the requests that read prompt rows: prompt logprobs, or every hidden state outside DSpark. Their late-layer tail is their whole extend, so these requests are served instead of raising in the forward and taking every scheduler down.
- `late_layer_tail_layout(whole_extend=...)` gives every row of a whole extend its plain sliding window, so no row of these requests is truncated; other requests keep the window tail and its floor. Both the CUDA and the HIP backend use it.
- A step whose tail outgrows the prefill CUDA graph's tail block runs eagerly. The backend answers the same question from the schedule batch (`vote_prefill_cuda_graph`), which the DP prefill-graph vote calls, so no DP rank replays the graph while another runs the step eagerly.
- DSpark's exemption comes from the server's speculative algorithm, since prefill-graph capture batches carry DSpark's `FULL` capture mode without it.
- `_check_late_layer_tail_readers` now raises only when the tail misses rows a reader needs; the DSpark logits path moves prompt-logprob starts into the tail.
- `--enable-return-hidden-states` makes every tail a whole extend, so decoder SWA bounded replay now resolves off with it; passing both flags still runs correctly.
- The DeepSeek-V4.1 cookbook and the flag's help now say that prompt-logprob requests are served, and that RL rollouts whose logprobs must match the trainer should pass `--no-enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay`.
- Unit tests in `test/registered/unit/layers/test_dsv41_late_layer_tail_readers.py`.

Supersedes #41448 and #42719.

No behavior change for requests that read no prompt rows: their tail layout, prefill-graph decision, and logits path are unchanged.

title: [Fix] deepseek-v4.1: Keep the cached KV of folded encoder replay rows
author: hnyls2002
body:
- Folded encoder SWA replay rows now get the padding slot (`raw_out_loc` 0) as their compressor write location (`_compressor_out_loc`); their main KV, compressed groups and index keys keep what the prefill that cached them wrote
- The fused c1/c2 compressors (SM100+) used to rewrite those rows on every prefix hit: `compress_skip` only reached the c2 ring write-back, while the c1 store, the c2 pooling store and the index-K store ran over every row
- The unfused compressor (e.g. Hopper) used to drop the replay rows from its input but not from its slots, so each new row landed on another row's slot (since #43166); it now takes every row, and the padding slot skips the replay rows
- Drop `compress_skip`, which the padding slot replaces
- Add `test_extend_metadata_puts_replay_rows_on_the_padding_slot` (on main no row gets the padding slot) and `test_unfused_compressor_writes_each_row_at_its_own_slot` (on main 90 of 282 rows reach the compressor)
- Checked on GB300 by snapshotting the replay rows' cached c1/c2 bytes before each prefix-hit prefill and comparing after it: main changed 3308-3712 of 3712 checked rows per hit on the fused path and all 3712 on the unfused path; this PR changes 0 on both

No behavior change outside `--enable-encoder-swa-bounded-replay`, where a prefix hit no longer rewrites the cached KV of its replayed tokens and every new token's KV goes to its own slot.

title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] modelopt-nvfp4: Read w13 global scales in the TRT-LLM [up, gate] order
author: mmangkad
body:
## Motivation

On the FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE backend, ModelOpt NVFP4 experts whose gate (w1) and up (w3) global scales (`weight_scale_2`) differ are dequantized with the two scales swapped. Under this layout the loader stores w13 rows, and their per-tensor scales, as `[up, gate]`, but `_compute_gemm1_alphas` (#27588) reads column 0 as gate.

Standard ModelOpt exports tie gate/up scales (NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer#1033), so most checkpoints are unaffected. Before Model-Optimizer 0.45 (NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer#1560), experts never reached during calibration could stay untied, e.g. 6 of 3,840 in `nvidia/Gemma-4-26B-A4B-NVFP4`. It was reported on an in-house checkpoint with untied scales. Online NVFP4 (`nvfp4_online.py`) quantizes gate/up together with one shared scale, so it is unaffected.

## Modifications

- `_compute_gemm1_alphas` takes `up_first` and reads the columns in w13 row order; `process_weights_after_loading` passes `up_first=self.use_flashinfer_trtllm_weight_layout`. Other backends are unchanged.
- The TRT-LLM SwiGLU params move into `_compute_trtllm_gated_act_params`. Beta is added to the raw up half, so it now uses `g1_alphas_up`. The kernel applies one clamp limit to both raw halves, which can't be exact for both when their scales differ; it stays in gate-half units and logs a warning.
- Unit tests: the beta/clamp units and the SiTU branch of the moved helper.
- E2E (weekly, 4x B200): serve [`mmangkad/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4-untied-gate-up`](https://huggingface.co/mmangkad/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4-untied-gate-up) on `flashinfer_trtllm` and require GSM8K >= 0.90 (sgl-eval). Locally: 0.960 with this PR, 0.305 on the base commit.

## Accuracy Tests

`mmangkad/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4-untied-gate-up` is `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4` with `up_proj.weight_scale_2 *= 4` and `up_proj.weight_scale /= 4` in every expert: gate/up differ, dequantized weights are bit-identical.

sgl-eval 0.1.3 GSM8K, 200 examples, `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm`, TP1, 1x B300 (Qwen3 cookbook recipe, but with an NVFP4 checkpoint and a forced MoE backend):

| Checkpoint | Thinking, before | Thinking, after | Non-thinking, before | Non-thinking, after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Original (tied) | 98.0% | 97.5% | 95.0% | 95.0% |
| Untied | **51.0%** | **97.0%** | **29.0%** | **95.0%** |

Thinking: temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95, max_tokens 32768. Non-thinking: temperature 0.7, top_p 0.8, max_tokens 2048.

Kernel checks for the SwiGLU params: one expert with gate/up scale ratio 0.30, run through `prepare_static_weights_for_trtllm_fp4_moe` and `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe` against a dequantized reference (alpha 1.702). Relative error; FP4 noise floor 0.09.

Beta: `1/up_alpha` gives 0.089, `1/gate_alpha` gives 0.508.

Clamp, real limit L, kernel given P. Each row is a hypothesis for the real thresholds the kernel applies:

| Real thresholds | P = L/gate_alpha | P = L/up_alpha |
|---|---|---|
| gate <= P * gate_alpha, abs(up) <= P * up_alpha (both raw) | **0.072** | **0.133** |
| both at P * up_alpha | 0.608 | 0.742 |
| gate only, up unclamped | 0.611 | 0.873 |
| both at P * gate_alpha | 1.989 | 2.155 |

The kernel clamps both raw halves at P, so with untied scales no single P gives both halves the real limit L.

title: [Fix] kda: Align graph tracking branch dtype with the recurrent state pool
author: Jzz1943
body:
## Motivation

KDA graph tracking can read an FP32 chunk-boundary snapshot or a recurrent-state pool entry. With a BF16 state pool, these branches produce different Triton types, causing compilation to fail before the final store cast.

Observed during GLM-5.3-Flash prefill BCG initialization with BF16 recurrent state:

```text
triton.compiler.errors.CompilationError: at 19:4:
    stride_h_row,
    numel,
    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
):
    r = tl.program_id(0)
    mode = tl.load(track_mode + r)
    if mode == 0:
        return
    dst = tl.load(track_dst + r).to(tl.int64)
    offs = tl.program_id(1) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
    mask = offs < numel
    if mode == 1:
    ^
AssertionError("Mismatched type for val between then block (<['1024'], bf16>) and else block (<['1024'], fp32>)")
```

A cast after the `if/else` cannot resolve this error: Triton requires matching types for `val` when merging the branches, before compiling the subsequent cast.

## Modifications

Cast the snapshot to the state-pool element type before the branches merge. The stored dtype is unchanged, and FP32 state pools retain their existing behavior.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated in GLM-5.3-Flash PD serving on 8 × H200 with BF16 recurrent state and MTP516: GSM8K, 1,314 examples × 2 rounds, scored **95.4% / 95.9%**. These results are from the existing integration configuration containing this fix and the separate Decode RadixCache changes, not a new full-model run on this rebased PR branch.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

This is a correctness fix; no inference speed improvement is claimed.

title: [Fix] diffusion: runtime utils bug fixes
author: OnePunchMonk
body:
Part of #43875 (items 8-24). Split out of #43585 so it can be reviewed on its own. It touches only `runtime/utils` and its tests, and does not depend on the other two PRs (#43585, #44888).

## Summary
Bug fixes in `multimodal_gen/runtime/utils`, one commit per item. Item numbers match #43875.

Downloads and inputs
8. `load_video` never deleted the video it downloaded from a URL, so `/tmp` filled up over time. It now cleans up (also on failure) and the download has a timeout.
9. Line-wrapped base64 images were silently cut at the first line. The data URL regex now matches across newlines.

Hub, cache and config loading
10. An unreachable Hub was treated as "this repo has no model_index.json", so the cache fallback never ran. It now falls back to the cached copy.
11. The same condition sent `maybe_download_model_index` down the single-model path with a misleading "-Diffusers" error. It now reports the download failure.
12. A local cache dir of `ltx-2.3-distilled` matched the `ltx-2.3` overlay by substring. Cache dirs are now matched by path component.
13. An overlay repo resolved by Hub id downloaded only its manifest, so `model_index.json` was missing on a fresh cache. It now downloads the full overlay metadata.
14. `scheduler` anywhere in a component's path made every component read `scheduler_config.json`. Only the component dir name counts now.
15. Normalizing a ModelOpt `config.json` wrote through the HF cache symlink and changed the shared blob. The file is now replaced instead.
16. The ModelScope LoRA path raised a `TypeError` when no weights were found. It now raises a `FileNotFoundError` that says so.
17. Corrected a comment claiming CI validation failures after download are retried (they are not).

Precision, logging and misc
18. `temporary_module_dtype` restored the whole module to the first parameter's dtype, undoing mixed precision (bf16 weights with fp32 norms). Each tensor keeps its own dtype now.
19. All `RequestMetrics` instances compared equal. They compare by identity now.
20. `log_request_summary` ignored its `tag` argument. It is honored now, with the previously written value as the default, so existing callers see no change.
21. `get_git_commit_hash` ran `git rev-parse` in the current directory. It now runs in the sglang install dir.
22. The "log on every rank at DEBUG" rule read the log level when the logger was created, before `configure_logger`. It reads it at log time now.
23. Enabling the NVTX hooks between a module's pre- and post-hook popped a range that was never pushed. Push and pop stay balanced across toggles.
24. `get_bool_env_var` warned once per bad value instead of once per variable. It is keyed by name now.

## Tests
- New unit tests for each item except 16, 17 and 21 (error message, comment, and cwd-only changes). They extend the existing test files and fixtures. `test_runtime_utils_regressions.py` is new because `vision`, `image_io` and `common` have no unit test file yet.
- PR, the 7 touched test files: 136 pass. 101 ran on a CPU Modal container; `test_performance_metrics.py` (35) ran on an A10G because it imports `vsa`, which needs a GPU at import time.
- main with these tests: 16 of the 18 new cases fail. The two that pass guard behavior main already has: the cached single-model path (`test_unreachable_hub_model_index[True]`) and rejecting a newline in the media type.
- Not run: the full unit suite and a GPU end-to-end run.

title: [Fix] diffusion: pipeline and model-helper bug fixes
author: OnePunchMonk
body:
Part of #43875 (items 26-33). Split out of #43585 so it can be reviewed on its own. It does not depend on the other two PRs (#43585, #44887).

Item 25 (Plucker rays in float32 for LingBot-World) moved to its own PR, as asked in review, so it can get a GPU check without holding these up.

## Summary
Fixes in pipelines and the model helpers they use. Item numbers match #43875.

26. The blank default texture and the bake buffers used `(width, height)` where `(height, width)` is needed, which breaks non-square textures.
27. `ImageProcessorV2.load_image` raised `UnboundLocalError` for an ndarray or tensor. ndarrays are handled like PIL images and other types raise a `TypeError`.
28. `DiffusersPipeline` output layout: NumPy videos were permuted twice, a nested PIL list kept only the first video, and several images from an image pipeline were stacked as video frames. A nested list is now stacked to `(B, T, C, H, W)` for every video.
29. `DiffusersPipeline.add_stage` took its arguments in the reverse order of the base class. It now swaps the legacy order and delegates to `ComposedPipelineBase.add_stage`, so it also gets the disagg role filtering.
30. SANA-Video always encoded the negative prompt at 300 tokens. It uses `max_sequence_length` now.
31. ErnieImage treated a `[null, null]` `pe` entry as a real prompt-enhancement model. It is treated as absent.
32. HunyuanImage3 ignored `--revision` when downloading weights.
33. Hunyuan3D picked an arbitrary checkpoint when several matched the fallback glob. It picks the first by name now.

## Tests
- New `test_pipeline_regressions.py` (CPU): 12 cases. The layout test uses distinct values per sample, frame and channel, so swapped axes or a dropped video fail. The ndarray case compares against the same image given as PIL.
- With the source changes reverted, 10 fail. The 2 that still pass are guards: a real Ernie `pe` entry is still detected, and the legacy `add_stage` order still works.
- Unit tests that import the touched modules (25 files) on CPU, PR vs base: 590 passed vs 578 on base. The same 5 failures and 4 GPU-only collection errors occur on base too.
- No tests for 32 and 33 (a passed-through kwarg and a sort). No GPU run; these are API, shape and loading fixes.

title: [Fix] [H200] ci: Split GLM-5.3-Flash serving recipes into separate tests
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

The GLM-5.3-Flash H200 test runs High Throughput and Low Latency recipes in one process, sharing the default 1200-second per-file CI budget. In [this failure on #44220](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38998797308/job/117297505340), High Throughput completed GSM8K with 97.12% accuracy, but the file timed out during the Low Latency evaluation.

## Modifications

Split the recipes into independently registered test files, each with an estimated duration of 1200 seconds. Each gets its own existing per-file timeout and can be partitioned separately. Move the unchanged server setup and cleanup into a shared helper. Preserve all model arguments, accuracy thresholds, speculative acceptance checks, and decode performance checks.

## Validation

- AST comparison confirms every original class, function, and constant is preserved exactly once.
- The CI collector discovers both executable CUDA tests in `extra-b-test-8-gpu-h200`; partitioning treats them independently.
- Python syntax, isort, Ruff lint, Ruff formatting, and whitespace checks pass. All commit-time pre-commit hooks pass.
- [H200 validation](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39032680509/job/117396243462) passed on commit `66fcf904f261d2ece679de80c3fdb2d8b95b7ca6`, triggered with `/rerun-test` without adding CI labels. Both files finished below the ordinary suite's 1200-second per-file budget:

| Recipe | File wall time (including setup/cleanup) | GSM8K | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| High Throughput | 569 s | 97.19% | Passed |
| Low Latency | 314 s | 97.12% | Passed |

The files ran sequentially in one rerun job (883 s total). The rerun workflow does not enforce the ordinary suite's per-file timeout, so the measured file wall times were checked explicitly. This is one successful run on an 8-H200 runner; it does not establish a worst-case cold-start bound.

## Accuracy Tests

Both recipes passed the unchanged full 1319-example GSM8K check and 0.96 accuracy threshold (results above).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Low Latency passed `test_bs_1_speed` on its first attempt: acceptance length 4.478 > 4.0 and speed 343.75 token/s > 200. All three unittest methods across the two files passed.
