title: [Fix] Anthropic: accept thinking.display="updates"
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Motivation

Claude Code sends `thinking: {"type": "adaptive", "display": "updates"}` on its `/v1/messages?beta=true` requests. `AnthropicThinkingParam.display` only accepts `"summarized"` and `"omitted"`, so the first request of every Claude Code session against sglang fails with:

```
400 invalid_request_error: thinking.display: Input should be 'summarized' or 'omitted'
```

Claude Code then retries without the field, so sessions work, but each one starts with a rejected request.

`"updates"` is a documented Anthropic value, not a client quirk. The anthropic Python SDK defines it on the beta thinking configs:

- `BetaThinkingConfigAdaptiveParam.display: Literal["summarized", "omitted", "updates"]`
- `BetaThinkingConfigEnabledParam.display: Literal["summarized", "omitted", "updates"]`

The non-beta configs list only `"summarized"` and `"omitted"`. The [thinking docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking#controlling-thinking-display) describe `"updates"` (beta header `thinking-display-updates-2026-08-18`) as: reasoning blocks come back with an empty `thinking` field, as with `"omitted"`, and only short progress updates between tool calls carry text.

## Modifications

- `entrypoints/anthropic/protocol.py`: `AnthropicThinkingParam.display` accepts `"updates"`. Other values are still rejected, and `display` with `type="disabled"` is still a 400.
- `entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py`: `"updates"` is served like `"omitted"`. Reasoning stays on and its text is still emitted, because the OpenAI-side pipeline cannot blank reasoning blocks or produce progress-update blocks. A warning names the requested value.

Nothing else in Claude Code's opening request needs a change. Replaying the captured request through `AnthropicMessagesRequest` with only `display` adjusted passes validation: `output_config.effort="high"` is already accepted, and `context_management` (`clear_thinking_20251015`) is ignored as an undeclared field.

## Accuracy Tests

Request validation only; generation is unchanged.

Unit tests (`test/registered/unit/entrypoints/anthropic/test_serving.py`):

- `test_request_claude_code_display_updates_is_accepted` uses Claude Code's opening-request shape: adaptive + `display="updates"` + `output_config` + `context_management` + `metadata`. It fails before this change and passes after.
- `test_request_thinking_unknown_display_is_rejected` checks that a value outside the SDK set still fails validation.
- 70 passed.

Live: Claude Code 2.1.296 (`claude -p` with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` pointing at an sglang server built from this branch, serving `thinkingmachines/Inkling-NVFP4` on 8x H200):
- Both `/v1/messages?beta=true` requests carried `thinking={"type": "adaptive", "display": "updates"}`, and both returned 200. The server log shows 2x 200 and no 400.
- The session completed its tool call and ended with `end_turn`.
- Before this change, the same CLI's first request returned the 400 above.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not performance-related.

title: [Fix] scheduler: Exclude accepted storage-tier hits from the waiting prefill load
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

`SchedulerLoadInquirer.get_num_waiting_uncached_tokens` is the prefill-load figure behind `LoadSnapshot.num_waiting_uncached_tokens`, which feeds DP balancing and `/v1/loads`. With per-request prefix matching on, it counts `seqlen - num_matched_prefix_tokens` for every waiting request. That matched length only covers the device and host tiers at match time. A waiting request whose prefix is being fetched from the storage tier through the buffer pipeline still has those tokens counted as work to prefill, although the scheduler will never run them: the prefetch was accepted for exactly that span, and the staged hold keeps it until admission. A rank that is absorbing storage hits therefore reports more prefill load than it will do, and the balancer steers traffic away from the rank that is about to serve cheaply.

## Modifications

- `BasePrefixCache.waiting_storage_span(request)` (`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/base_prefix_cache.py`): new hook returning the expected storage-hit span of a waiting request as logical token offsets, `None` by default so caches without a storage tier are unchanged.
- `UnifiedRadixCache.waiting_storage_span` (`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py`): in buffer mode, an ongoing prefetch that the scheduler has accepted (host indices assigned) reports the accepted logical span `[storage_start, storage_start + storage_hit_count)`, independent of how far the worker has progressed; a completed prefetch held in `staged_prefetches` reports `[matched_len, matched_len + num_tokens)`. A prefetch whose result is still awaiting acceptance, a released hold, and resident mode all report `None`.
- `SchedulerLoadInquirer` (`python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/load_inquirer.py`): optional `get_waiting_storage_span` provider. With per-request matching, the overlap between the reported span and the uncached suffix `[matched, seqlen)` is subtracted, clipped so a span inside the matched prefix or beyond the prompt removes nothing. The historical hit-rate path is untouched because the measured hit rate already includes admitted storage hits. `Scheduler.init_load_inquirer` wires `tree_cache.waiting_storage_span`.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: only the reported load estimate changes; no change to scheduling decisions, model execution or outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable as a benchmark: one dictionary lookup per waiting request at load-reporting time.

Unit tests on this head (CPU, `pytest`): `test/registered/unit/managers/test_load_inquirer.py` and `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_storage_prefetch_lifecycle.py`, 31 passed with 44 subtests. New cases: the exclusion is clipped to the uncached prompt across eight span placements; it is applied only under per-request matching, never in decode mode, and never changes the hit-rate estimate; a missing provider keeps the original figure; the scheduler wires the provider; the cache reports no span before acceptance, the accepted logical span regardless of worker progress, the staged span until the hold is released, and nothing in resident mode.

title: [Fix] test-utils: Allow expected server exits in canary tests
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

The fail-fast watcher added in #45053 aborts `TestPerturbRaiseMha` when its intentionally corrupted KV cache makes the server exit. The canary correctly reports `verify_real_kv_hash`, but the watcher exits the test runner before it can assert the captured violation. This caused [this CI failure](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39220756454/job/117959479275) on #44623.

## Modifications

- Add `CustomTestCase.expect_server_exit`, defaulting to false. Opted-in tests run their assertions without a fail-fast watcher or retries against a terminated server.
- Opt in only the canary raise-mode fault-injection test; preserve its violation assertions.

## Validation

- Pre-commit checks passed for the changed Python files.
- Use the existing `test/registered/kv_canary/test_self_e2e_perturb_raise.py` as the regression test: it must complete its `verify_real_kv_hash` violation assertions after the intentional server exit. It remains registered for CUDA and AMD CI.
- Targeted GPU rerun passed on `1-gpu-5090` at commit `f5333ca417c`: [workflow run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39257555152). The existing canary test triggered the expected `verify_real_kv_hash` violation and completed successfully: `Ran 1 test in 51.741s`, `OK`.

No model execution or inference performance changes.

title: [Fix] Minimax-M3: Deterministic tie-breaking in the CUDA radix decode top-k
author: Godmook
body:
>pr description is generated by AI tool

## Motivation

`minimax_decode_topk` has three selection regimes. Two of them already break exact score ties by block id (the lower id wins):

- the small path (`num_blocks <= 128`): `is_greater(...)`, "lower block id wins"
- the ROCm path: a packed `(score, ~id)` total order

The CUDA radix paths (`num_blocks > 128`, i.e. contexts above 16k tokens at block size 128) place the final-round ties in `atomicAdd` order instead. When tied blocks straddle the top-k boundary, the selected set changes from run to run. ROCm indexer CP already depends on a fixed tie order ("requires ... the ROCm radix top-k tie ordering"); the CUDA paths gave no such guarantee.

Exact ties are common for indexers whose keys carry no RoPE: the block score is the max over units, so repeated text produces equal scores. On such a model, serving the same prompts twice from a cold cache with the radix cache on gave 43/45 identical greedy outputs; with this change, 45/45.

## Modifications

- Final radix round: rank the tied candidates by block id (warp ballot + prefix sum) and keep the lowest ids, matching the small and ROCm paths. Applied to both the single-element path and the multi-element (register bucket) path.
- Fast path: when every tie is selected (`equal_count <= topk_remain`), the order does not matter (the output is sorted ascending), so the ties are written with a plain atomic as before and the ranking is skipped.
- Removes the now unused `counter_final`.
- Adds `test_decode_topk_ties_pick_lowest_ids`, which checks the selected set against `(score desc, id asc)` for 300 to 9,000 blocks with heavy ties.

ROCm is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

MiniMax-M3 (bf16, TP8, H200, radix cache on), main vs this PR:

- Greedy outputs on 40 MMLU-Pro prompts plus needle-in-text prompts up to 60k tokens (radix path): 45/45 identical.
- GPQA-Diamond (n=1, max_tokens 32k): 89.4 (main) vs 90.4 (this PR). (range in noise)

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MiniMax-M3, TP8, H200, one request at a time, radix cache flushed before each request:

| input tokens | prefill TTFT, main / PR | decode TPOT, main / PR |
|---|---|---|
| 4k | 0.395 / 0.396 s | 13.42 / 13.11 ms |
| 16k | 1.496 / 1.499 s | 13.62 / 13.26 ms |
| 32k | 3.042 / 3.051 s | 13.68 / 13.46 ms |
| 48k | 4.639 / 4.643 s | 13.76 / 13.54 ms |
| 60k | 5.936 / 5.951 s | 13.81 / 13.59 ms |

Kernel microbenchmark (2 heads, 8 to 64 rows, 2k to 8k blocks): within ±0.2 us of main for distinct scores; equal or faster with ties.

title: [Fix] humming: Free replaced MoE weights after each sublayer transform
author: DarkraiHL
body:
## Motivation

`--moe-runner-backend humming` replaces every MoE sublayer tensor with a padded, repacked copy of a different size while loading. The originals stay referenced until the next sublayer, and later allocations split their cached blocks, so much of that memory is never returned. On 8× H20-3e (141 GB), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with TP-sharded experts holds 100.6 GB per GPU after loading at TP4 (81.8–82.2 GB with this PR) and 57.1 GB at TP8 (50.0 GB). At TP4, with or without DSpark, the server fails to start with the default `--mem-fraction-static 0.8` (TP4 + DSpark shown):

```
RuntimeError: The DSV4 SWA pool cap (707840 tokens, 15.81 GB) leaves no room for the full KV pool within the available 9.62 GB. ...
```

## Modifications

- After each sublayer transform, drop every reference to the replaced tensors (including the loop variables) and call `torch.cuda.empty_cache()`, in both Humming MoE paths. Padding, kernels and the forward pass are unchanged.
- CPU unit test `test_humming_moe_release_replaced.py`: no replaced tensor is still referenced when the cache is emptied, for both paths. It fails on main.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K (`python -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k`, 1319 questions):

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| TP4 | fails to start | 0.913 |
| TP4 + DSpark | fails to start | 0.919 / 0.920 / 0.926 |
| TP8 | 0.920 / 0.926 / 0.919 | 0.920 / 0.926 / 0.920 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

8× H20-3e, `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20261019-3c560089`, the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash H200 low-latency cookbook recipe with `--moe-runner-backend humming --ep-size 1`, `SGLANG_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG='{"dtype": "float8e4m3"}'` and `SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE=1`. Decode: `python -m sglang.bench_serving --dataset-name random-ids --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512`; TP8 is the mean of 3 alternating runs on one node.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| TP4: weights per GPU | 100.6 GB, fails to start | 81.8–82.2 GB, KV 10.18M tokens |
| TP4 + DSpark | fails to start | KV 6.92–7.02M tokens |
| TP8: weights per GPU / KV tokens | 57.1 GB / 26.2–26.6M | 50.0 GB / 31.1M |
| TP8: output tok/s, c1 / c32 / c64 | 149.6 / 1795 / 2452 | 150.3 / 1790 / 2435 |
| TP8: median TPOT at c64 | 20.40 ms | 20.41 ms |

With #45083 (TP4 + CP4 + DSpark), KV grows from 4.88M to 10.88M tokens. Loading is not slower. With Humming's generic SM90 heuristics (the ones H100/H200 select) forced on the same machine, the memory numbers are the same and TP4 + DSpark starts.

title: [Fix] multimodal: Compact CPU tensor views before inline transport
author: ggboooy
body:
## Motivation Large multi-image requests can block the tokenizer event loop while preparing a message for the scheduler when multimodal features travel inline as CPU tensors (`nnodes > 1`, or fallback after SHM allocation fails). `get_new_expanded_mm_items()` splits a batched feature tensor into per-image views. A view can be contiguous while still retaining the entire batch's storage. PyTorch's pickle reducer serializes that storage for each distinct view, so the payload grows quadratically with the number of images. For 96 images at 1024 x 1024, the processed float32 features occupy 2.25 GiB in total. Each image view contains 24 MiB of useful data but references the same 2.25 GiB storage. Pickling one view produces about 2.25 GiB; serializing all 96 would contribute about 216 GiB of storage data. In the serving reproduction, `send_pyobj()` did not return before tokenizer RSS reached the 128 GiB experiment limit, and `/model_info` timed out. The 216 GiB figure is a storage-size estimate, not a completed wire transfer. The measured 8-image request expands 192 MiB of features into a 1.50 GiB ZMQ message. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Image preprocessing
96 images: one 2.25 GiB CPU storage"] --> B["Split into 96 Tensor views
24 MiB logical data each
Each still references the full 2.25 GiB storage"] B --> C{"Feature transport"} C -->|"SHM succeeds"| D["Copy each image's valid bytes into SHM
ZMQ carries SHM descriptors"] D --> S["Scheduler and TP ranks
obtain image features"] C -->|"CPU inline: multiple nodes or SHM fallback"| E{"At the send boundary"} E -->|"Before"| F["pickle serializes the full storage per view
96 x 2.25 GiB = about 216 GiB estimated"] F --> G["Tokenizer event loop stalls
RSS grows; scheduler waits for the request"] E -->|"This PR"| H["Compact only oversized CPU Tensor storage
Each image now owns 24 MiB"] H --> I["pickle / ZMQ carry about 2.25 GiB
Payload scales with useful feature bytes"] I --> S classDef bug fill:#fff1f0,stroke:#cf222e,color:#24292f; classDef fix fill:#dafbe1,stroke:#1a7f37,color:#24292f; classDef shared fill:#ddf4ff,stroke:#0969da,color:#24292f; class F,G bug; class H,I fix; class D shared; ``` ## Modifications - Compact dense CPU tensors whose backing storage is larger than `numel() * element_size()` before inline transport. Use a real clone: `contiguous()` alone can return the original view. - Apply this to features, precomputed embeddings, and nested model-specific data. Memoize compacted tensors within a request so repeated references share the same replacement. - Compact the tensor when SHM allocation fails and transport falls back to inline. - Keep successful SHM feature transport, non-CPU tensors, and tensors with no oversized storage on their existing paths. Preserve the main branch's opt-in model-specific SHM wrapping and shape-only OCR crop placeholders; compact only the tensors remaining inline after that wrapping. Never enable model-specific SHM on default inline or skip-tokenizer paths. - Add CPU regression tests through the actual image-splitting and transport-preparation functions, including pickle round trips and payload-size bounds. This bounds the existing pickle/ZMQ path; it does not introduce a new wire format or make inline transport zero-copy. Affected views incur one logical-size copy before serialization. ## Current-base verification (2026-11-06) Rebased onto `2fd45ed82fe07ec64ef7f4d2dbd9071b0eb01763`. Resolved the overlap with Unlimited-OCR v2 model-specific SHM transport, updated test imports/request types, and added three regression tests covering SHM pointers alongside nested inline views, model-data SHM allocation failure, and keeping SHM disabled on inline/skip-tokenizer paths. Validated on Python 3.12 with PyTorch 2.14.1+cpu, Transformers 5.19.0 and pyzmq 27.1.0. The actual main-branch image-splitting and transport-preparation functions were exercised with controlled transport selection and ENOSPC injection. An in-process ZMQ PAIR socket sent each request through `send_pyobj()`; the receiver measured the received bytes and checked exact tensor equality. Each synthetic image has 16 × 128 float32 feature elements (8 KiB). These small CPU cases test storage amplification without launching a model or allocating the original 96-image workload. | Images | Useful feature bytes | Unmodified main: inline / SHM fallback message bytes | Rebased fix: inline / SHM fallback message bytes | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 8,192 | 9,695 | 9,695 | | 8 | 65,536 | 531,730 | 71,564 | | 32 | 262,144 | 8,434,298 | 283,679 | | 96 | 786,432 | 75,780,580 | 849,383 | The 96-image amplification falls from 96.36× to 1.08× (including request metadata). All 12 cases (four sizes × inline, failed-SHM fallback, successful SHM) preserve exact values. The successful SHM path remains functional; its 96-image message also falls from 260,953 to 41,940 bytes by compacting inline metadata. The original payload regressions fail on unmodified main under PyTorch 2.14.1. After the fix, **37 tests and 22 subtests pass** across: ```bash PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q \ test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_mm_inline_storage.py \ test/registered/unit/managers/test_mm_shm_error_consensus.py \ test/registered/unit/managers/test_async_shm_materializer.py ``` Ruff checks/format, isort, registered-test validation, indirect-import checks, runtime-import checks, package-test placement checks, and `git diff --check` pass. This update reruns CPU transport/regression tests; the GPU serving numbers below are historical measurements from the original base and were not rerun on this rebase. ## Original accuracy and serving checks (2026-10-20) Base: `8e7601ae4a48c1127afd1bcdccf0a0ad61dbf043`. Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0, sglang-kernel 0.4.10. 18 local unit tests pass: 8 new inline-storage tests and 10 existing SHM tests. Coverage includes float32/bfloat16 value and dtype preservation, per-image offsets, strided and empty views, repeated references, nested embeddings/metadata, SHM allocation failure, skip-tokenizer mode, and avoiding feature clones on the successful SHM path. The payload-size regressions fail on the unmodified base. ```bash PYTHONPATH=python python test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_mm_inline_storage.py PYTHONPATH=python python test/registered/unit/managers/test_mm_shm_error_consensus.py ``` Qwen3.5-35B-A3B serving smoke tests also complete after the fix. The 96-image request reports `prompt_tokens=130048`, `image_tokens=98304`, and, after flushing the radix cache, `cached_tokens=0`. No model-level accuracy benchmark was run; tensor round trips are checked for exact equality. ## Original speed tests and profiling (2026-10-20) One physical H800/SM90 host, TP4, two logical nodes with two GPUs each (`--nnodes 2`) to exercise CPU inline transport. The SHM control uses single-node TP4. This is a transport reproduction, not a cross-host network benchmark. Inputs are deterministic random JPEGs (1024 x 1024, approximately 1.018 MB each). The 8-image request has 16,384 input tokens; the 96-image request has 130,048. Both generate one token with temperature 0. Relevant settings: context length 131,072, chunked prefill 8,192, static memory fraction 0.75, FA3 attention, and CUDA graphs disabled. | Measurement | Base | This PR | | --- | ---: | ---: | | 8 images: serialized ZMQ message | 1.50 GiB | 192.6 MiB | | 8 images: `send_pyobj()` call | 1.312 s | 0.156 s | | 8 images: end-to-end | 10.62 s | 5.34 s | | 96 images: serialized ZMQ message | Not completed; about 216 GiB storage estimated | 2.25 GiB measured | | 96 images: `send_pyobj()` call | Still blocked after 36.35 s | 1.925 s | | 96 images: end-to-end, no cached prefix | No response before experiment termination | 17.07 s, HTTP 200 | | Tokenizer peak sampled RSS, inline test run | 129.99 GiB, stopped by the guard | 7.64 GiB | | 96 images: single-node SHM control, end-to-end | 12.09 s | 12.01 s | These are individual serving observations, not repeated-run medians. RSS was sampled every two seconds, with a 128 GiB per-process stop threshold. `send_pyobj()` time includes serialization but excludes the preceding storage-compaction step; end-to-end time includes that step. The blocked base run was deliberately terminated and is not evidence of a permanent deadlock. ## Checklist - [x] Ruff lint/format, isort, registered-test validation, and `git diff --check` pass. - [x] Add CPU regression tests registered in `base-a-test-cpu`. - [x] Verify exact tensor round trips and existing SHM regressions. - [x] Provide serving results and measurement limits above. - [ ] User-facing documentation update: not applicable; no configuration or API change. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #42206455103](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42206455103) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #42206454986](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42206454986) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #42206454978](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42206454978) > [!TIP] > Base CI only covers the core cases, and its workload may not exercise your change. Use `/rerun-test` to run the tests your change touches, or copy this prompt for an agent: > > ```text > Find the registered tests this PR affects and run them with /rerun-test, following https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.agents/skills/rerun-test/SKILL.md > ```

title: [Fix] mamba: Skip zero-width conv pools in the MTP verify scatter
author: mmangkad
body:
## Summary

Fixes the nightly `test_ling_2_6_flash.py` crash on the first MTP verify step:

```
ValueError: fused_conv_window_scatter_with_mask: dst entry dims (dims 2..3) must be contiguous; got shape=(28, 257, 0, 0) strides=(257, 1, 1, 1)
```

Lightning linear-attention layers (Ling-2.5/2.6, MiniCPM lightning hybrids) have no conv state, so their conv pool is zero-width. `dst.is_contiguous()` accepted it, but #44971's explicit stride check rejects it. The pool then falls back to the per-pair scatter, which raises.

- `scatter_mamba_states_after_mtp_verify` skips empty conv pairs, like the existing SSM guard, so mixed sets keep the single-launch path.
- `fused_conv_window_scatter_with_mask` returns early on an empty `dst`, as a safety net.

New `TestScatterAfterVerifyZeroWidthConv` and `test_ling_2_6_flash.py` both fail before the fix and pass after.

title: [Fix] [AMD] grok: accept allow_patterns_overrides in presharded _prepare_weights patch
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
## What

`_prepare_presharded_weights` in `grok.py` now accepts the `allow_patterns_overrides` argument that `DefaultModelLoader._prepare_weights` gained in #33572.

## Why

`Grok1ForCausalLM.__init__` replaces `DefaultModelLoader._prepare_weights` with `_prepare_presharded_weights` when `tp_size > 1`. Since #33572, `_get_weights_iterator` and the resolve-sources path call `_prepare_weights` with four positional arguments, but the Grok replacement only takes three, so every Grok launch with TP > 1 dies during weight loading:

```
TypeError: _prepare_presharded_weights() takes 4 positional arguments but 5 were given
```

In the latest AMD nightly, all 12 Grok jobs (grok1-int4 and grok2, MI300 and MI35x, all ROCm versions) fail this way: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39150288819/job/117742354680

## Notes for the reviewer

When an override is passed, the patch hands off to the original `_prepare_weights` instead of applying the per-rank shard patterns, because the override means "load exactly these patterns". Grok itself never sets an override, so its loading path is unchanged; this only matters if some other model is loaded in the same process after the class-level patch.

## Test plan

- Checked that the new signature binds both call shapes used in `loader.py` (four positional args, and `download_model`'s `fall_back_to_pt=` keyword).
- Dispatched the four Grok nightly jobs on this commit (rocm10): https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39304489973. All four load weights and serve; no `TypeError`.

  | Job | GSM8K acc (threshold) |
  |---|---|
  | MI35x grok2 | 0.930 (0.9) |
  | MI35x grok1-int4 | 0.840 (0.8) |
  | MI300 grok1-int4 | 0.810 (0.8) |
  | MI300 grok2 | 0.910 (0.915) on attempt 1, 0.930 on rerun |

  The first MI300 grok2 attempt missed by one question out of 200; the rerun passed, in line with the 0.925–0.945 it scored before the break. All four jobs are green on attempt 2.

title: [Fix] radix-cache: Separate logical and reclaimable value lengths in tree components
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

A tree node's device value has two lengths that the tree cores treated as one: the logical length of the stored index tensor, which slicing, prefix matching and `collect_path_info` spans read, and the number of allocator slots the pool gets back when the value is evicted, which the evictable/protected ledgers count. A component whose backing is released or shared under a value can occupy fewer pool rows than the logical value describes, and the ledgers then drift from what the allocator actually reclaims: prefill admission adds the evictable ledger to the allocator's free space and the eviction walk counts it toward its request, so both over-report.

## Modifications

- Python: `TreeComponent.reclaimable_tokens` becomes `reclaimable_value_len`, and every ledger site in the Full, SWA and Mamba components (insert, lock, release, materialize, evict, recount) reads it instead of `len(value)`. `value_len` stays the logical length.
- Rust: `Node` gains `device_reclaimable_value_len`, zero for roots and absent values, and the same ledger sites in the Full, SWA and Mamba components and the core use it instead of `device_value_len` or the tensor's first dimension. The SWA component's private `value_len` helper goes away.
- `adjust_component_size` rejects a delta that would drive a ledger negative with `ValueError` and leaves the counters untouched, on both cores; the interface docstring says so.
- `evict_device_next_node` reports progress when a step freed device or host backing even though no node was consumed, so an eviction walk over zero-accounted nodes keeps going instead of stopping early.

Nothing changes for components whose reclaimable length equals the logical one, which is every in-tree component today.

title: [Fix] srt: Admit only allowlisted peers on TCP-bound ZMQ IPC sockets
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

With data-parallel attention and a non-loopback `--dist-init-addr`, the data-parallel controller binds its worker-facing ZMQ sockets on a host-reachable address so that the other nodes can connect. Those sockets decode pickle-wrapped payloads, so anything that can reach the port can push a payload at them (CVE-2026-93034, GHSA-w4hv-c72g-pqx6). Today nothing restricts who may connect.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/environ.py`: new `SGLANG_ZMQ_ALLOWED_PEERS`, a comma-separated list of peer IP addresses admitted by TCP-bound IPC sockets. Unset or empty admits every peer, which is today's behaviour.
- `python/sglang/srt/utils/network.py`: `restrict_zmq_peers(context, socket)` starts one ZAP `ThreadAuthenticator` per `zmq.Context` (libzmq allows a single ZAP handler per context, so sockets created from the same context share it), allows the configured addresses, and sets `zap_domain` on the socket so that libzmq vets NULL-mechanism connections. Must run before the socket binds; a no-op when the allowlist is unset. `get_zmq_socket` applies it to every TCP bind (random port and explicit endpoint). `get_zmq_socket_on_host` gains `restrict_peers=False`, off by default because disaggregation sockets accept peers from other jobs.
- `python/sglang/srt/managers/data_parallel_controller.py` and `python/sglang/srt/ray/data_parallel_controller.py`: the controller's worker PUSH sockets pass `restrict_peers=True`.
- `python/sglang/srt/managers/load_snapshot.py`: `ZmqShmLoadSnapshotReader` restricts peers when its endpoint is `tcp://`.

IPv6 entries may be written in any valid form; each is normalized to the compressed form that libzmq reports for a peer address, so `2001:DB8:0:0::1` matches a peer at `2001:db8::1`.

A multi-node deployment sets the variable to the addresses of its own nodes before launching every node, for example `SGLANG_ZMQ_ALLOWED_PEERS=10.0.0.1,10.0.0.2`. Single-node serving, serving without data-parallel attention and disaggregation traffic are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no change to scheduling, model execution or outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: with the variable unset the only addition is one empty-tuple check per socket bind; with it set, libzmq's ZAP check runs once per connection.

Functional check on this head with real sockets (pyzmq 27.2.0, libzmq 4.3.5): a PUSH client at the loopback address is delivered to a PULL socket from `get_zmq_socket` when the allowlist is unset, empty, or contains `127.0.0.1` (also when listed in long-form IPv6 company), and is dropped when the allowlist names only another address; the same holds for an explicit `tcp://` endpoint; `get_zmq_socket_on_host` keeps admitting any peer unless `restrict_peers=True`, which then drops a non-member and admits a member. `isort`, `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `codespell` at the repository's pinned versions pass on the five files.

title: [Fix] deepseek-v4: Keep the draft MoE out of the target's expert placement
author: weireweire
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4.1 with DSpark and MegaMoE cannot run EPLB. With `--enable-eplb --ep-num-redundant-experts 16`, the server dies while capturing the draft decode CUDA graphs: DeepGEMM's MegaMoE kernel times out in its grid barrier (`Grid sync timeout`, `barrier.cuh`), which later surfaces as `unspecified launch failure`.

DeepSeek-V4 draft MoE layers (DSpark stages and NextN) are `DeepseekV2MoE` layers built with `is_nextn=True` and zero-based layer ids. DSpark stages also own a smaller expert set: 128 routed experts, against the target's 384 over 40 layers.

EPLB only rebalances the target. The draft never gets an EPLB manager and exposes no `routed_experts_weights_of_layer`, yet the target's expert placement leaked into the draft in three ways:

- the draft MoE was sized with the target's redundant expert slots;
- `FusedMoE.weight_loader` indexed the draft's own expert tensors through the target's logical-to-physical map for layer 0..2;
- the MegaMoE paths (CUDA `mega_moe` and AMD `mega_moe_flydsl`) built `ExpertLocationDispatchInfo` for `layer_id` 0..2 from the target's metadata.

With redundant experts, DSpark draft top-k ids were remapped to physical slots the draft MegaMoE does not own, and the kernel hung. For NextN MTP with the target's expert count, the same leak routed draft tokens by the live target map after a rebalance, while the draft weights stayed at the startup placement.

#34846 (closed) opted DSpark draft layers into dispatch instead. That cannot work for DeepSeek-V4.1, where the draft's expert count differs from the target's.

## Modifications

- `FusedMoE` takes `uses_expert_location: bool = True`. When it is False, `weight_loader` ignores the global expert-location metadata and uses the plain global-to-local mapping.
- `DeepseekV2MoE` passes `uses_expert_location=False` for DeepSeek-V4 nextn layers. Those layers get no redundant expert slots.
- `mega_moe._run_mega_routed` and `mega_moe_flydsl._run_mega_routed` pass no dispatch info for such layers. The other MoE paths in `deepseek_v2.py` already skip nextn layers.
- `moe_wna16` places qzeros with the same plain mapping for such layers, matching the weight loader.
- The DSpark loader numbers the fused shared expert, and sizes its expert param mapping, after the stage's own routed experts, matching the plain mapping.

Target layers and non-DeepSeek-V4 models are unchanged. With redundant experts, a DeepSeek-V4 NextN layer on MegaMoE now gets its own MegaMoE buffer, since its expert count no longer matches the target's.

Out of scope, left for a follow-up:
- non-V4 NextN layers on MegaMoE with EPLB, which keep today's behavior;
- `--enable-waterfill`, which sizes the draft's balancer from the target's expert count plus redundant slots.

## Accuracy Tests

GB300, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, EP4 with attention DP 4, MegaMoE, DSpark, `--enable-eplb --ep-num-redundant-experts 16`:

- main: dies in draft decode CUDA graph capture.
- This change: all graphs capture and the server serves.

GSM8K (sgl-eval, 400 questions, native speculative acceptance) shows no accuracy loss:

| | score | accept length |
|---|---|---|
| no EPLB | 97.50% | ~4.26 |
| EPLB, 16 redundant experts, two rebalances during the eval | 98.00% | ~4.16 |

Only DSpark was run on GPU; DeepSeek-V4 NextN MTP with EPLB was not. The isolated draft paths were also checked: on main, the MegaMoE draft path builds target dispatch info, and the draft weight loader indexes its experts through the target's map. Neither happens with this change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Unchanged for target layers. For DeepSeek-V4 draft layers, behavior changes only when the target's placement is non-trivial (`--enable-eplb`, redundant experts, or a non-trivial `--init-expert-location`). This makes EPLB usable on DeepSeek-V4.1 DSpark + MegaMoE decode.

title: [Fix] deepseek-v4.1: Keep the padded query buffer inside decoder tail graphs
author: hnyls2002
body:
- With attention TP > 1 and a FlashMLA backend that pads the query to 64 heads (not `trtllm`, not `flashmla_mega`), DeepSeek-V4.1 caches the zeroed padded query buffer on the step's attention metadata (`q_pad_buffer`) and replaced it whenever the shape changed.
- A decoder tail graph step captures every row bucket on that one metadata, largest first. Each smaller bucket replaced the buffer, so the larger buckets' graphs kept the address of a freed one: their replays wrote the query into memory the allocator had reused, and after `flush_cache` (which empties the CUDA cache) they hit an MMU fault in `fused_q_norm_rope`.
- The metadata now keeps one buffer that only grows, and each call takes a row slice (`MqaAttentionBase._zero_padded_q`). Every bucket a tail step captures shares the largest one, which the graphs keep through the metadata they hold. The padding is still zeroed once and never rewritten. The graphs keep that one largest buffer alive (128 MiB at 2048 rows with TP8 heads padded to 64), where before each bucket's buffer was freed under it.
- The buffer must not grow after a CUDA graph has captured it, so a capture marks the metadata (`q_pad_captured`) and a later growth fails an assert instead of freeing a captured buffer. HIP's breakable-graph metadata keeps the mark across replays like the buffer.
- Paths without query padding are unaffected: DP attention (attention TP 1), `trtllm`, and `flashmla_mega`.
- Verification: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4, DSpark, `--dsv4-attn-backend flashmla` (pads the query on this GPU too), the external-linker load-back KL cases, which flush the cache between requests.
  - Before: in the encoder SWA replay class (eager prefill + tail graphs), the second case fails with a CUDA error after a flush, in both of two runs.
  - After: both classes pass, the paged-SWA one (prefill graph, tail graphs, decode graphs) and the encoder SWA replay one; the new assert never fires.
  - The same failure shows on 8xH200 CI, where the default backend pads the query.

title: [Fix] [NPU] DSA: Correct DSA Models Sparse offload index-cache budgeting
author: JinyanYi
body:
## Summary

Fix NPU sparse KV offload memory estimation for models with shared Top-K layers. Compact allocation already stores index-K only for indexer-owner layers (#44436), but the offload estimator still charges every layer. Count local owner layers using the existing compaction guard, preserving dense and draft-worker fallback.

The NPU sparse KV offload path uses NPUMLATokenToKVPool and a separate SparseKVCacheManager for the MLA KV buffers. Because its pool layout and memory accounting differ from the regular path, it has a separate cell-size calculation that returns before the existing indexer sizing logic. This change fixes the indexer layer count in that offload-specific calculation.

## How the estimate affects serving

The offload estimate becomes `self._cell_size`, the bytes charged per token. [Pool sizing](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/f6f4a42d3d5e7212a2fed9a4d70aeec6e2c7bde9/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/pool_configurator.py#L636-L646) computes:

```python
available_bytes = max(available_bytes - self._fixed_overhead_bytes, 0)
max_total_num_tokens = (
    available_bytes // self._cell_size
    if self._cell_size
    else self._zero_kv_max_tokens
)
max_total_num_tokens = max_total_num_tokens // page_size * page_size
```

Overestimating bytes per token produces an unnecessarily small token pool. [Request-length limits](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/f6f4a42d3d5e7212a2fed9a4d70aeec6e2c7bde9/python/sglang/srt/managers/tp_worker.py#L568-L572) also depend on that capacity:

```python
max_req_len = min(
    self.model_config.context_len - 1,
    kv_capacity - 1,
)
max_req_input_len = max_req_len - 5
```

For concurrent requests, the pool must hold their combined token histories; without shared prefixes, its approximate concurrency ceiling is `token capacity / tokens per request`, with additional headroom needed for generation.

## Validation and impact

A3 and A5 GLM-5.2 config-only NPU pool tests passed with BF16 index-K and page size 64:

- Per-token charge: **19,968 → 5,376 bytes** (78 layers → 21 owners).
- At a **512 MiB index budget**, automatic capacity: **26,880 → 99,840 tokens (3.71x)**. The larger candidate pool allocates successfully; dummy-page padding is additional to the per-token accounting budget.
- At a fixed **16,384 tokens**, both versions retain the same 21-owner layout and **88,424,448-byte tensor footprint**. Boundary read/write checks pass. Static checks also pass.

The change recovers index capacity previously left unused by the overestimate. It can allow longer requests or more concurrent long-context requests when token capacity is the bottleneck. It does not change Top-K computation or the per-request resident KV window, and it does not reduce HBM at a fixed token capacity.

These tests load no model weights and do not run a serving workload. End-to-end concurrency and throughput gains are not measured; request-slot limits, resident KV buffers, DRAM, MTP and runtime memory can impose other limits.

title: [Fix] [AMD] diffusion: Enable `--quantization fp8` on gfx1250 (torch.compile lowering + per-channel weight scales)
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

`--quantization fp8` does not work on gfx1250. With `--enable-torch-compile` it dies in Inductor lowering on the first warmup request, before a single image:

```
LoweringException: AssertionError: target: aten._scaled_mm.default
  args[3]: ... FixedLayout('cuda:0', torch.float32, size=[], stride=[])
```

`args[3]` is the weight scale, and it is a **rank-0 scalar**. Inductor's `_scaled_mm` template loads it with two index symbols against a zero-length stride, so the `len(index) == len(stride)` assert at `ir.py:2034` fires.

The scalar comes from the missing-CUTLASS fallback: `cutlass_fp8_supported()` is `False` for every ROCm device (`fp8_utils.py:398` is `if not _is_cuda: return False`, before it looks at compute capability), so `process_weights_after_loading` falls to `input_to_float8`, whose single `aminmax()` yields a 0-dim `weight_scale` instead of a per-channel `[N]` vector. **The crash and the quality loss are therefore one bug**: a per-tensor scale that Inductor cannot lower *and* that throws away the range a BF16 checkpoint needs to survive FP8. NVIDIA takes the per-channel CUTLASS branch and sees neither symptom, which is why this is gfx1250/ROCm-only.

Avoiding the lowering is not enough on its own: hipBLASLt ships no tuned gfx1250 kernels, so at the FLUX.2-dev 720p shapes `torch._scaled_mm` FP8 reaches 471-506 TFLOPS while the BF16 torch.compile templates it replaces already reach 645-710.

**The scheme here is A8W8** -- a fully FP8 GEMM. Both operands are `e4m3`: per-token dynamic scales on the activations, per-channel scales on the weights, FP32 accumulate. It is explicitly *not* weight-only (A16W8); the activations are quantized too, so the matrix cores actually issue FP8 MFMA, which is where the speedup comes from.

**The fix** is two changes for two different reasons, either of which alone stops the crash:

* `process_weights_after_loading` takes the per-channel branch (`per_token_group_quant_fp8`), giving a real `[N]` scale. This is the *accuracy* fix; the ranks line up as a side effect.
* `apply` quantizes the activations per token and routes both operands to an A8W8 Triton tile, so `aten._scaled_mm` is never reached. This is the *performance* fix: 1150-1255 TFLOPS instead of 471-506.

This affects any gfx1250 run passing `--quantization fp8` with a BF16 checkpoint. Nothing in the fix is model-specific -- it is the shared `Fp8LinearMethod` in the diffusion stack -- though the reproduction here is FLUX.2-dev at 720p, where linears are 83% of GPU kernel time. MI300X, MI355X and NVIDIA are unaffected: `is_gfx1250_supported()` is false there, and `cutlass_fp8_supported` already routes NVIDIA to a per-channel CUTLASS GEMM.

## Modifications

* New `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/fp8_gfx1250.py`: an A8W8 (per-token activation / per-channel weight) FP8 `[M, K] @ [K, N]` Triton tile plus the per-token activation quantizer that feeds it. The tile indexes its operands modulo M and N rather than masking the loads (masked loads cost ~10% on this target and the tail is at most one tile), and masks only the store. `_select_config` carries the tile sizes an offline sweep picked for the served shapes.
* `multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/quantization/fp8.py`: `Fp8LinearMethod.__init__` computes `use_gfx1250_triton_fp8` once; when set, `process_weights_after_loading` takes the **per-channel** branch for a non-FP8-serialized checkpoint -- replacing the rank-0 `input_to_float8` scale that both breaks the lowering and drops the checkpoint's range -- and `apply` tries `_apply_gfx1250_triton_fp8` first, returning `None` to the existing path for any shape the tile does not cover.
* `srt/environ.py`: `SGLANG_DISABLE_GFX1250_FP8_GEMM`, a diagnostic kill switch.
* The quantized weight is stored **row-major** `[K, N]` rather than as the transposed view of `[N, K]` that this method has always produced. A BLOCK_N slice of one k-row otherwise reads N single bytes strided by K instead of BLOCK_N contiguous ones; making it contiguous once at load is worth 1.05-1.33x per GEMM and 1.06x end to end. The tile's config table is tuned for that layout, and a unit test pins it, since a refactor that drops the transpose would be a silent regression.
* `test/registered/amd/test_fp8_gemm_gfx1250.py`: tile correctness against a dequantized reference, and the dispatch seam itself.

**BLOCK_SIZE_K is capped at 64 on purpose.** On gfx1250 with triton 3.8.0, an FP8 `tl.dot` miscompiles for `BLOCK_SIZE_K >= 128`: it silently returns NaN for every `num_warps` x `num_stages` combination tested (16 of 16), and the broken kernel *times about 40% faster than a correct one*. An autotune sweep without a correctness gate will therefore select it and report a phantom ~1730 TFLOPS. This also means 1150-1255 TFLOPS is the ceiling for correct Triton FP8 on this target today, not the hardware's ceiling. Note that `triton_scaled_mm`'s own heuristic picks `(128, 128, 128)` for M 128, so callers must not route gfx1250 FP8 there until the compiler is fixed.

## Accuracy Tests

No accuracy harness applies -- this is a diffusion image model, so there is no gsm8k-style score. The gate is instead split into the two questions that can actually be answered separately: is the kernel numerically correct, and did the image get worse.

Measured on one gfx1250 (DPX half-package), FLUX.2-dev 720p, 50 steps, seed 42, `--enable-torch-compile true`, aiter attention, all offload off. The "before" arm is BF16 at this PR's merge base. There is no "FP8 without this PR" arm, because that configuration does not run at all -- it is the lowering crash described in Motivation.

### 1. Trajectory divergence -- is the kernel correct

Comparing the per-step denoise latents of the two arms (`[1, 50, 3600, 128]`) separates the error the GEMM introduces from the amplification the sampler applies to it afterwards. One seed is sufficient here: this measures numerics, not a sample distribution.

| step | relative L2 | cosine | mean bias | growth vs prev |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.00149 | 0.999956 | +5.75e-05 | -- |
| 2 | 0.00224 | 0.999954 | +1.71e-04 | x1.51 |
| 3 | 0.00288 | 0.999952 | +2.47e-04 | x1.28 |
| 5 | 0.00407 | 0.999949 | +2.01e-04 | x1.18 |
| 10 | 0.00778 | 0.999926 | -7.04e-05 | x1.14 |
| 20 | 0.03700 | 0.999273 | +1.41e-03 | x1.13 |
| 30 | 0.11282 | 0.993576 | -6.01e-04 | x1.10 |
| 50 | 0.31035 | 0.951731 | +3.72e-04 | x1.00 |

**Mean bias stays within +-1e-3 at every step and changes sign.**

### 2. Image quality -- did it get worse

| Prompt | CLIP BF16 | CLIP FP8 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cat and dog baking in a kitchen (many small props) | 36.31 | 35.96 | -0.35 |
| Watchmaker's hands close-up (skin and metal micro-detail) | 24.66 | 24.91 | +0.25 |
| **mean** | **30.49** | **30.44** | **-0.05** |

All deltas are within +-0.5 CLIP points and go both ways (mean -0.05), i.e. no quality change. n=2 at a single seed.

### 3. Pixel similarity to BF16 -- reported, not the gate

| Prompt | PSNR (not a gate) | SSIM (fine: > 0.8) | LPIPS (fine: < 0.1) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cat and dog baking | 18.30 | 0.8413 | 0.0959 |
| Watchmaker's hands | 18.79 | 0.8530 | 0.0843 |
| **mean** | **18.55** | **0.8472** | **0.0901** |

## Benchmarking and Profiling

### End to end, on the tracked MI450 dashboard configuration

Both rows are from the same dashboard harness, same image (`rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm10-mi45x-20261020`), same day, same arm (**MI450-MC Hammer: DPX TP1 (A0), `--enable-torch-compile true`**). The baseline row is the arm as it ships today -- BF16, because `--quantization fp8` cannot be passed on this target without the crash above. The second row is this PR *plus* the flag it enables:

| Arm | Text encode (s) | **Denoise (s)** | VAE decode (s) | **Total (s)** |
|-----|-----------------|-----------------|----------------|---------------|
| DPX TP1 (A0) + torch-compile (BF16, today) | 0.0034 | 48.7215 | 3.0623 | 51.787 |
| + PR 45304 + `--quantization fp8` | 0.0031 | 36.0457 | 2.9947 | **39.044** |
| **Delta** | -- | **-26.0% (1.35x)** | -2.2% | **-24.6% (1.33x)** |

The entire win is in denoise, which is what the change touches; text encode and VAE decode are unchanged, and they are what keeps the e2e ratio (1.33x) below the denoise ratio (1.35x).

> Note for anyone reproducing: the `+ PR45304` row **must** carry `--quantization fp8`. Every line of this PR sits behind `Fp8LinearMethod.use_gfx1250_triton_fp8`, and that class is only constructed when the flag is passed -- so a "+PR45304" arm without it measures plain BF16 and shows no change. Also discard the first run after a cold start; cold Inductor/aiter JIT costs roughly 8 s of denoise.

### Isolated A/B on one gfx1250

FLUX.2-dev, 720p, 100 denoise steps, seed 42, one gfx1250, `--enable-torch-compile true --attention-backend aiter`, all offload off. Runs serialized on an otherwise idle box, two repetitions each, no profiler attached.

| Metric | BF16 s/step | FP8 s/step | BF16 e2e | FP8 e2e |
|--------|-------------|-----------|----------|---------|
| rep 1 | 0.7553 | 0.5553 | 87.77 s | 64.13 s |
| rep 2 | 0.7569 | 0.5592 | 87.93 s | 64.45 s |
| mean | **0.7561** | **0.5573** | **87.85 s** | **64.29 s** |

**-26.3% per denoise step (1.357x), -26.8% end to end (1.367x).** Spread across repetitions is under 0.5%.

The row-major weight layout is a further **-5.3%** on top of that, measured the same way (3 reps each, same GPU, serialized, warm compile cache):

| s/step | rep 1 | rep 2 | rep 3 | mean |
|--------|-------|-------|-------|------|
| column-major weights | 0.5522 | 0.5523 | 0.5565 | **0.5537** |
| row-major weights | 0.5234 | 0.5288 | 0.5211 | **0.5244** |

A matched pair of profiles (same step count, same GPU) attributes -174 ms of GPU time over three steps to the GEMMs, against a total of -108 ms; GPU-busy time falls 1791.5 -> 1683.6 ms, which tracks the wall-clock change. Cumulative against BF16: **0.7561 -> 0.5244 s/step, 1.44x.**

These per-step figures are the host loop average (`[DenoisingStage] average time per step`), while the dashboard's Denoise column is `[DenoisingStage] finished in`, which includes the GPU tail drain and runs ~20% higher on the same run. Compare within a table, not across the two.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the PR flow. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   * `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`, `/tag-and-rerun-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls to merge.

title: [Fix] observability: Log scheduler stats once per attention CP group
author: hunhokim
body:
## Motivation

With `--enable-prefill-cp`, every attention-CP rank logs the same scheduler stats as follows.

```
[2026-10-20 04:41:56 ATTN_CP1 TP1] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #token: 58560, token usage: 0.02, accept len: 3.33, accept rate: 0.47, cuda graph: True, gen throughput (token/s): 181.02, #queue-req: 0
[2026-10-20 04:41:56 ATTN_CP2 TP2] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #token: 58560, token usage: 0.02, accept len: 3.33, accept rate: 0.47, cuda graph: True, gen throughput (token/s): 181.02, #queue-req: 0
[2026-10-20 04:41:56 ATTN_CP3 TP3] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #token: 58560, token usage: 0.02, accept len: 3.33, accept rate: 0.47, cuda graph: True, gen throughput (token/s): 181.02, #queue-req: 0
[2026-10-20 04:41:56 ATTN_CP7 TP7] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #token: 58560, token usage: 0.02, accept len: 3.33, accept rate: 0.47, cuda graph: True, gen throughput (token/s): 181.02, #queue-req: 0
[2026-10-20 04:41:56 ATTN_CP4 TP4] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #token: 58560, token usage: 0.02, accept len: 3.33, accept rate: 0.47, cuda graph: True, gen throughput (token/s): 181.02, #queue-req: 0
[2026-10-20 04:41:56 ATTN_CP5 TP5] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #token: 58560, token usage: 0.02, accept len: 3.33, accept rate: 0.47, cuda graph: True, gen throughput (token/s): 181.02, #queue-req: 0
[2026-10-20 04:41:56 ATTN_CP6 TP6] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #token: 58560, token usage: 0.02, accept len: 3.33, accept rate: 0.47, cuda graph: True, gen throughput (token/s): 181.02, #queue-req: 0
[2026-10-20 04:41:56 ATTN_CP0 TP0] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #token: 58560, token usage: 0.02, accept len: 3.33, accept rate: 0.47, cuda graph: True, gen throughput (token/s): 181.02, #queue-req: 0
```

CP ranks share scheduler state, so these lines repeat the same numbers and clutter the log.

## Modifications

- Require `attn_cp_rank == 0` in addition to `attn_tp_rank == 0` for `is_stats_logging_rank` in `python/sglang/srt/observability/metrics_collector.py`. This matches the existing leader check for KV events in the same function.
- Effect: only CP rank 0 now logs stats and exports per-scheduler Prometheus metrics (unless `--enable-metrics-for-all-schedulers` is set).
- No change when CP is disabled, since `attn_cp_rank` is always 0.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] **(Not needed: logging-only change)** Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] **(Not needed: no user-facing docs change)** Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] **(Not needed: no change to model outputs or the serving path)** Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [Fix] [AMD] docker: Build Triton from source for ROCm 10.1 gfx1250
author: yctseng0211
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

The ROCm 10.1 SDK ships `triton 3.8.0+git669b31ac.rocm10.1.0` (ROCm/triton `669b31ac`, `release/internal/3.8.x`). 
On gfx1250, with `TRITON_HIP_USE_EXPERT_SCHEDULING` at its default (`is_expert_scheduling_enabled()` returns true for gfx1250):
- kills gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8 under load -- single requests answer, then a memory
  access fault in `_moe_gemm_a8w4_decode` 4 requests into a 600-request run

None of this is there with the Triton the rocm10 image builds (triton-lang/triton `76940ad3`, from main)
But `76940ad3` is past triton-lang/triton#10833 (`9debefe44`, merged 2026-07-15), which removed block pointers, and sglang's FLA kernels still call `tl.make_block_ptr`. So this builds `76940ad3` and reverts `9debefe44` on top.

## Modifications

 - build triton : 76940ad3
 - revert triton commit : 9debefe44

## Accuracy Tests
**gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8 TP1**
gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8 on `v0.5.22-rocm101-mi45x-20261020-test` (built from this
patch, `triton 3.8.0+gitc9230de6`), gfx1250, TP 1. No `TRITON_HIP_USE_EXPERT_SCHEDULING=0`.

```bash
ENABLE_CK=0 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path amd/gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8 \
  --tp 1 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --max-running-requests 512 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.9 \
  --attention-backend aiter \
  --disable-radix-cache \
  --page-size 64 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 3072 \
  --max-prefill-tokens 3072 \
  --port 8000

pip install sgl-eval
sgl-eval run gsm8k \
  --base-url "http://localhost:8000/v1" \
  --model amd/gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8 \
  --num-threads 64 \
  --temperature 1.0 \
  --top-p 1.0 \
  --seed 42 \
  --max-tokens 8192
```

| metric | value |
| --- | ---: |
| score | **95.83%** |
| stop_rate | 100.00% |
| truncated_rate | 0.00% |
| error_rate | 0.00% |
| examples | 1319 (single-shot) |
| duration | 204.3 s |
| throughput | 1270 tok/s |
| avg_input_tokens | 147.5 |
| avg_output_tokens | 196.7 |


**DeepSeek-V4-Flash gsm8k** 

| TP | gsm8k | latency | output throughput |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 0.943 | 287 s | 2435 tok/s |
| 4 | 0.944 | 261 s | 2686 tok/s |
| 8 | 0.941 | 262 s | 2692 tok/s |

Server (`TP` = 2 / 4 / 8; TP4 and TP8 also set `SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=0`):
```bash
unset NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS NCCL_MAX_NCHANNELS
NCCL_IGNORE_CPU_AFFINITY=1 NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1 NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=1 HSA_HOTSWAP_DISABLE=1 \
SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=max \
SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1 \
SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE=0 ENABLE_CK=0 SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 \

title: [Fix] [AMD] quark: Load MXFP4 MoE checkpoints on gfx95 and gfx1250 without SGLANG_USE_AITER
author: ZhengGong-amd
body:
## Motivation

`QuarkW4A4MXFp4MoE` imports its AITER shuffle helpers only when `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` but always calls them after loading, so outside `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` (the only place that sets it) every Quark MXFP4 MoE checkpoint fails with `NameError: name 'e8m0_shuffle' is not defined`; this PR binds those helpers and the matching weight layout on gfx95 and gfx1250 regardless of the env var.

`process_weights_after_loading` calls `e8m0_shuffle` on gfx950 and `moe_shuffle_scale`/`moe_shuffle_weight` on gfx1250. The scheme has no other path, since `create_moe_runner` accepts only the AITER runner. The failure also hits `--quantization quark_mxfp4`, which `test/registered/e2e/quantization/test_quark_mxfp4.py` launches without the env var.

## Modifications

- On gfx95 and gfx1250, `_use_aiter` in `quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py` no longer depends on `SGLANG_USE_AITER`. This binds the imports together with the weight layout (`_is_shuffle_moe_mxfp4`, AITER padding). Other HIP arches still follow the env var, because AITER defines no FP4 MoE layout for them; #41389 handles gfx1151.
- Binding only the imports, as #31805 does, is not enough: the weights stay unshuffled and AITER falls back from the FlyDSL kernels to CK 2-stage, which is 23–37 % slower at M ≥ 257.
- With `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` the expression evaluates the same, so the weights handed to the MoE kernel are byte-identical to main's.
- `TestQuarkMxfp4MoEShuffleImports` reloads the module without the env var for gfx95, gfx1250 and other HIP arches. main fails the gfx95 and gfx1250 cases.

## Accuracy Tests

MI355X, TP1, `SGLANG_USE_AITER` unset unless noted:

| model | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B `--quantization quark_mxfp4`, real weights | NameError | GSM8K 0.820 (200 q, 5-shot) |
| same, main with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` (reference) | GSM8K 0.835 | — |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B, MiniMax-M3, Kimi-K2.6, GLM-5.2 (MXFP4, dummy weights, 8 layers) | NameError | loads and serves |

The 0.015 gap is within the ±0.027 standard error at 200 questions. With the env var unset, attention and top-k also leave AITER, so the two arms differ outside the MoE as well.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MoE layer at Qwen3.5-397B shapes, median of 3 warm runs per arm:

| M | main, env=1 (µs) | this PR, env unset (µs) | Δ |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|

| 33 | 420.6 | 420.4 | −0.0 % |
| 257 | 733.4 | 731.4 | −0.3 % |
| 1029 | 826.2 | 823.5 | −0.3 % |

title: [Fix] inkling: Keep BF16 LM-head operands with FP32 output
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

BF16 projection output can round distinct token scores into a tie before the existing FP32 sampler-buffer cast. Inkling should be able to preserve FP32 projection output while retaining BF16 hidden states and head weights, without enabling the generic `--enable-fp32-lm-head` policy.

```python
# Preserve BF16 operands; produce FP32 projection output directly.
logits = torch.mm(hidden_bf16, weight_bf16.T, out_dtype=torch.float32)
```

Final sampler logits are already FP32 in either mode. Casting a rounded BF16 projection afterward cannot recover its lost score ordering.

## Modifications

- Replace Inkling's default `enable_lm_head_fp32` request with a separate `enable_lm_head_output_fp32` request.
- Use FP32 output for an unquantized CUDA head with matching FP16/BF16 operands. Keep the operands in their existing dtype.
- When this output-only path is unsupported, retain the existing projection path instead of promoting operands to FP32. LoRA and quantized-head dispatch remain unchanged.
- Preserve the existing explicit `--enable-fp32-lm-head` behavior, including its operand promotion fallback.
- Add CPU/CUDA regressions.

To opt out of the new Inkling output policy, omit `--enable-fp32-lm-head` and use:

```bash
--json-model-override-args '{"text_config":{"enable_lm_head_output_fp32":false}}'
```

The older `enable_lm_head_fp32` metadata hook remains available for existing models and explicit configurations; Inkling no longer defaults it to true.

## Validation

### Rebase validation

Rebased onto main `f05ad5ec0139d1a41e04115384f6f03b0ac4d19f` at head `af99a81cb885b3d724e22212f8f03ab8251454db`, retaining all five PR commits, including the latest comment cleanup.

The LM-head conflict was integrated with main's shared logits output buffer and its shape guard. FP32 projection output can reuse a valid buffer; an incompatible shape falls back to a fresh output. The output-only request and explicit generic FP32 policy retain their separate fallback behavior.

- All three registered CPU/CUDA regression tests pass on NVIDIA H200 with Torch 2.13.0+cu130.
- An additional 24-case CUDA integration check passes across BF16/FP16 operands, both precision-policy switches, and no/valid/incompatible output buffers. It checks exact values and dtype, valid-buffer reuse, untouched rejected buffers, and unchanged operand dtypes.
- Applicable pre-commit checks and diff whitespace checks pass.
- Full-model TP4/DSPARK replay was not repeated after this rebase. The previously observed output failures below remain unresolved; these targeted checks do not establish a repair of the repetition issue.

### Historical validation

At `f965976d3255b94e9d524948cac3f6b07cc476f6`:

- Two registered CPU tests pass: the output-only default preserves CPU BF16 projection, and the explicit generic FP32 flag still produces distinct FP32 scores.
- The registered CUDA test passes: BF16 operands directly produce FP32 scores and preserve the unique greedy winner with the generic flag disabled. The nested opt-out survives serialization and restores the BF16 tie.
- These regressions fail on the previous PR head `672b381ec5`.
- All 8550 regular Python/test source files in the validation export match the committed Git blobs. Applicable pre-commit checks pass.
- Fresh four-NVIDIA-B300 TP4 DSPARK/FA4 replay completed the original warmup sequence and six 192-request batches: all 1152 exact inputs produce 2048 tokens. **The original output checks fail:** request 84 repeats `[1202,4707]` for all 2048 tokens in the fifth and sixth batches; the first four batches have no known whitespace cycles. The precision-policy correction does not fully repair the original output issue.
- All four TP ranks record BF16 hidden states and weights, FP32 projection output, generic FP32 disabled, output-only request enabled, and unchanged head-weight storage. Driver exit 0 confirms workload completion, not passing output checks. GPU processes were cleaned up.
- Before this rebase, published head `aa21a07105` only removed the optional MDX additions; its Python/test tree matches the GPU-tested runtime commit.

GPU environment: Torch 2.14.1+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.1, Triton 3.8.0, CuTe DSL 4.8.0. Target: `thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small-NVFP4`, snapshot `b6a99534467840620d411e4cd4ad5819b2610d9c`; draft: `RadixArk/Inkling-Small-DSpark`, snapshot `736501c3901cfc6bbb53ba382781eb0e5d9ad66a`.

## Scope and limitations

This changes projection-output precision; it is not a full-model FP32 conversion. The [BF16 checkpoint configuration](https://huggingface.co/thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small/blob/8cc5877b44d343f88b92086aa1fb72897950f06a/config.json) and [Transformers implementation](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/5be474e9cc2c92acaa3ef14fe9e35ea9108b06c1/src/transformers/models/inkling/modeling_inkling.py) do not establish an FP32 inference-output requirement.

Earlier same-operand FP64 controls verify a rounding-dependent greedy winner change, and first-token interventions show that FP32 can avoid entering a whitespace trajectory but does not eliminate repetition once that trajectory is seeded. The new unforced replay also reproduces loop entry with FP32 output; the earlier successful six-batch result is finite mitigation evidence, not a reliable repair. The original output issue remains unresolved. Full-model reference parity, wider task quality and matched performance are not established; upstream CI is not claimed green. The broader default-policy evaluation remains open.

title: [Fix] glm-5.2: Record side-stream work right before its join to keep CUDA-graph replay on one stream
author: wenscarl
body: ## Motivation On GLM-5.2 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`), a CUDA-graph decode replay spreads across many CUDA streams, so a profiler trace is hard to read: each layer's indexer chain lands on a different stream row. This is the same issue as DeepSeek-V4.1 in #39420. That PR found that at graph replay a join node continues on the stream of its first-recorded parent. A side-stream block captured before the concurrent main-stream kernels therefore pulls the main chain onto a side lane at the join. Its fix keeps the fork where it is and captures the side-stream work right before the join. Inspired by and following the approach of #39420 ("[DSV4.1] Record side-stream work right before its join"). ## Modifications Two side-stream blocks on the GLM-5.2 decode path were captured before the main-stream kernels they run alongside. In both, the fork (`alt_stream.wait_stream(current_stream)`) stays where it was, and only the capture order of the side block changes. 1. `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/dsa_indexer.py`, `_fused_q_prepare_and_store`, stage 1: the `wq_b` GEMM on `alt_stream` is now captured after the main-stream `wk_weights_proj`, right before the join. 2. `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py` (decode graphs, DSA path): the `q_b_proj` block on `alt_stream` is now captured after the indexer, right before `current_stream.wait_stream(self.alt_stream)`. `k_nope.unsqueeze(1)`, a view with no kernel, now runs on the main stream. I checked the rest of the GLM-5.2 path and found no other active violation under TP4 / NVFP4 / `flashmla_kv`. In particular, `DeepseekV2MoE.forward_normal_dual_stream` already issues the routed experts before the shared-expert side block, and stage 2 of the fused indexer is already ordered correctly. Test: `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_dsa_indexer_stream_order.py` pins the issue order of the stage-1 block (fork, main GEMM, alt `wq_b`, join). It fails without the change and passes with it. ## Results GLM-5.2-NVFP4, aggregated serving, TP=4, CUDA graphs on, dummy weights, GB200 x4. One run per arm, rank TP1, same load for both. Distinct CUDA streams seen in the profiler trace: | | baseline | this PR | |---|---|---| | 10-step decode window | 123 | 81 | | 30 ms slice of the window | 45 | 3 | In the baseline, 99 of the 123 streams are tiny, each carrying a few kernels of the indexer chain (`fused_q_indexer_rope_hadamard_quant`, `sm100_paged_mqa_logits`, `topk_small_batch_cluster_kernel` and a TgvGemm kernel). With this PR those streams disappear: two main lanes carry about 13.3k and 9.8k kernels. The kernel count is identical (23,324 vs 23,319), so the same work runs. Median TPOT (`sglang.bench_serving`, random 512 in / 256 out): | concurrency | baseline | this PR | |---|---|---| | 1 | 10.51 ms | 10.43 ms | | 8 | 11.88 ms | 11.78 ms | | 16 | 13.33 ms | 13.28 ms | No regression. The 0.4% to 0.8% gain is within single-run noise and is not claimed as a speedup. ## Reproduce Model files only, no weights (config and tokenizer from `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`; weights are random via `--load-format dummy`): ```bash mkdir -p /path/to/glm52_cfg && cd /path/to/glm52_cfg for f in config.json generation_config.json hf_quant_config.json tokenizer.json tokenizer_config.json chat_template.jinja model.safetensors.index.json; do curl -sfL -O https://huggingface.co/nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4/resolve/main/$f done ``` Server (run once on `main` and once on this branch): ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server --trust-remote-code \ --model-path /path/to/glm52_cfg --load-format dummy \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 --quantization modelopt_fp4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --dsa-prefill-backend flashmla_sparse --dsa-decode-backend flashmla_kv \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --max-running-requests 16 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16 \ --context-length 32768 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 ``` TPOT at concurrency 1, 8 and 16: ```bash for C in 1 8 16; do python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --model /path/to/glm52_cfg \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 1.0 \ --num-prompts $((C*4)) --max-concurrency $C --warmup-requests 2 --seed 1 done ``` Trace of a steady-state decode window (start profiling about 6 s into the run, while it is decoding): ```bash python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --model /path/to/glm52_cfg \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 256 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1.0 \ --num-prompts 16 --max-concurrency 16 --seed 2 & sleep 6 curl -s -X POST localhost:30000/start_profile -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"num_steps":10,"activities":["CPU","GPU"],"output_dir":"/path/to/trace","profile_prefix":"run"}' wait ``` Count distinct streams per rank: read the trace JSON, take events with `ph == "X"` and `cat == "kernel"`, and count the distinct `args.stream` values. The full traces are 330 to 460 MB each. For Perfetto, cut a 30 ms window from one rank so it loads. ## Notes and limits - Dummy weights: this checks stream layout and latency only. It says nothing about accuracy. I compared TPOT, not generated outputs. - Single run per arm, one rank analyzed. The TPOT difference is within noise. - Stream assignment at replay is driver behavior. The result is from one driver and torch version here (torch 2.14.1+cu130, driver 580.x). - The `forward_mla.py` edit moves `q_b_proj` after the indexer. A reviewer raised a theoretical allocator-reuse hazard: tensors the indexer allocates on `alt_stream` are freed at return, and the trailing `q_b_proj` could reuse a block while a main-stream kernel still reads it. I did not reproduce a failure, and the A/B shows no change in throughput. I have not proven it safe either, so please look at this one closely. - The patched trace still has 78 streams that each hold one kernel, a FlashInfer RMSNorm, one per layer. They come from a separate stream hop that this PR does not touch. - This covers the CUDA-graph decode path (`is_decode_or_idle`). The target-verify and draft-extend graphs do not take the `forward_mla.py` overlap branch. ## Checklist - [x] Unit test added - [ ] Accuracy test (not run; dummy weights) The diff is still uncommitted on glm52-graph-stream-fork, and nothing is pushed. Two things to decide before you post it: - Allocator-race note. I disclosed the unresolved allocator-race concern about the forward_mla.py edit in "Notes and limits". I'd leave it in; the alternative is dropping that edit or adding a keep-alive fix. - Repeat runs. Repeating each arm a few times would let you replace "within noise" with a number. Perfetto screenshots (30 ms slice, rank TP1): before PR: after PR: --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #39392800055](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39392800055) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #39392800085](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39392800085) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #39392800119](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39392800119) cc. @nvpohanh @BBuf

title: [Fix] muse_spark: support unified KV memory with TRT-LLM
author: Fridge003
body:
## Motivation

Muse Spark's fused decode/verify KV store assumes contiguous per-layer cache rows. Unified KV memory interleaves layers in each token row, so this path rejects the strided cache during CUDA graph capture.

## Modifications

- When unified memory is enabled, reuse Muse Spark's existing prefill QK norm/RoPE preparation and the attention backend's strided KV writer for decode and target verification. Forward modes, speculative masks, and the `trtllm_mha` backend remain unchanged.
- Resolve the implicit FA4 draft KV dtype when deciding fused draft placement. A BF16 DFLASH-family draft now keeps a separate pool when the target uses FP8, avoiding a dtype mismatch at draft binding.

- Add `test_muse_spark_unified_memory.py` to `extra-b-test-4-gpu-b200`, using the validated TP4/EP4 launch settings and a full GSM8K accuracy gate of 0.93. Pass the existing gated-model credential to this suite and its named main-branch rerun, preserving the rerun PR-head restriction.

## Accuracy Tests

Tested on 4 B200 GPUs with `meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4`, TP4/EP4, `modelopt_fp4`, `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE, `trtllm_mha` attention, unified memory, FP8 KV, page size 128, layernorm SP and MegaMoE. DFLASH uses `RadixArk/Muse-Spark-Open-DFlash2`, FA4, and 8 draft tokens. Native context length is 1,048,576; multimodal features use CPU transport and HiCache is disabled.

The new registered GSM8K test passed on 4 B200 GPUs: **1285/1319 (97.42%)**, with zero request errors, zero truncated responses, and zero invalid answers. It uses 64 evaluation workers, a 32,768-token output cap, temperature 1, top-p 0.95, and xhigh reasoning. The unmodified test file completed its server startup, evaluation, assertions, and graceful teardown in 263 seconds. Pre-commit and actionlint passed for the new test and CI changes.

All three evaluations use temperature 1, top-p 0.95, and xhigh reasoning:

| Evaluation | Configuration | Correct / total | Accuracy |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AIME26 | 30 problems × 8 repeats, 400K output cap | 226 / 240 | 94.17% |
| GPQA Diamond | 198 questions, 250K output cap | 178 / 198 | 89.90% |
| Video-MME | 900 short questions, 96-frame input videos, no subtitles | 787 / 900 | 87.44% |

One AIME and one GPQA response reached the configured output cap; both remain in the denominators. Actual DFLASH verification counters were recorded for responses.

Existing cache-placement and kernel tests passed on the runtime implementation in this PR. Text and image server smoke checks passed; CUDA graphs are enabled. Pre-commit passed for all changed files.

Fixed-input CUDA graph replay checks passed bit for bit: original packed fused QK norm/RoPE/KV store vs the fallback with 16-layer GQA and 46-layer SWA strided FP8 views (1, 8, 17, 128, and 512 tokens); TRT-LLM decode and 8-token verify with packed vs strided caches at 8K/64K context lengths, including SWA. Each case replays three times with changed inputs and cache locations/page tables.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Isolated QK norm/RoPE/cache-store timings on B200, in microseconds per layer (10 calls per CUDA graph, 100 timed replays):

| Tokens | Packed fused GQA | Unified fallback GQA | Packed fused SWA/RoPE | Unified fallback SWA/RoPE |

| 1 | 1.23 | 3.07 | 1.23 | 3.08 |
| 8 | 1.23 | 3.48 | 1.44 | 3.69 |
| 128 | 2.21 | 4.31 | 2.25 | 4.51 |
| 512 | 4.30 | 5.53 | 4.92 | 6.27 |

The fallback uses the existing separate preparation and cache-write kernels. These are operator timings; no end-to-end throughput comparison is claimed.
