title: [Fix] eplb: Load all local replicas of each expert
author: zanes-ops
body:
## Motivation

With an a2a backend (for example `--moe-a2a-backend deepep`), a server started with `--init-expert-location` set to a `physical_to_logical_map` in which one EP rank holds two replicas of the same logical expert never loads the second replica. A rank that holds no replica of that expert can still dispatch tokens to that slot, so those tokens go through an expert whose weights were never written. There is no error; the outputs just change. Reloading the weights through the same loader (for example with `update_weights_from_disk`) skips the same slots.

Such layouts come out of EPLB: the packing step can put two replicas of a hot expert on one GPU (deepseek-ai/EPLB#22), and SGLang's copy of the algorithm does too. Passing a saved, rebalanced layout back through `--init-expert-location` therefore hits this. In two layouts that we saved from Qwen3-30B-A3B servers (EP2, 2 redundant experts) after online rebalancing, 16 and 23 of the 48 layers had such a pair.

Where it happens (main @ 78185f4b):

1. [`_compute_logical_to_all_physical_map`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/78185f4b3f565cbe0fec20d71bb5deb372428e80/python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_location.py#L557-L591): with an a2a backend, each rank replaces every logical expert's candidate list with [`_find_nearest_expert`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/78185f4b3f565cbe0fec20d71bb5deb372428e80/python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_location.py#L699-L737) (#10874). A rank that holds replicas keeps only its first local one. A rank that holds none keeps the full list (on one node).
2. [`FusedMoE.weight_loader`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/78185f4b3f565cbe0fec20d71bb5deb372428e80/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py#L1099-L1104) writes a checkpoint expert into the slots that `logical_to_all_physical()` returns, which is this narrowed list, and [`_weight_loader_physical`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/78185f4b3f565cbe0fec20d71bb5deb372428e80/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py#L1124-L1127) keeps the local ones. The rank that holds both replicas writes only the first. For unquantized weights the second one stays [`torch.empty`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/78185f4b3f565cbe0fec20d71bb5deb372428e80/python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/unquant.py#L787-L789).
3. [The static dispatch table](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/78185f4b3f565cbe0fec20d71bb5deb372428e80/python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_location.py#L612-L672) gives a rank without a local replica a [`_fair_choices`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/78185f4b3f565cbe0fec20d71bb5deb372428e80/python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_location.py#L662-L667) pick among all replicas, which can be the unloaded one. `static` is [the default with an a2a backend](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/78185f4b3f565cbe0fec20d71bb5deb372428e80/python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/parallel_hook.py#L751-L764); with `--ep-dispatch-algorithm dynamic`, [the same list is sampled per token](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/78185f4b3f565cbe0fec20d71bb5deb372428e80/python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_location_dispatch.py#L114-L153).

The narrowing has left rows unloaded before: #12866 removed it to fix NaN NVFP4 input scales, and #13162 / #13484 restored it with a separate path for those global scale parameters (`require_global_experts`). That relies on the other unloaded rows never being dispatched to, and a second replica on the same rank breaks it. #32962 skipped the narrowing when there is no a2a backend; the a2a path is unchanged.

## Modifications

- `ExpertLocationMetadata.logical_to_all_physical()` (`eplb/expert_location.py`): for a routed expert, it now returns every physical slot that `physical_to_logical_map` assigns to the expert, on all ranks, instead of reading the per-rank dispatch list `logical_to_all_physical_map`.
  - The draft-layer fallback and the `require_global_experts` branch are unchanged. They only read the map's shape, and `logical_to_all_physical_map` is padded to the number of physical slots, so both maps give the same values.
  - For a layer in the map and without `require_global_experts`, the lookup rejects out-of-range logical expert ids with `IndexError`, including negative ids, which used to index from the end. The draft-layer and global-scale branches keep their existing conventions.
  - The dispatch fields (`logical_to_all_physical_map`, `logical_to_rank_dispatch_physical_map`) are not touched, so the nearest-replica dispatch from #10874 stays as it is.
- `FusedMoE._local_routed_expert_ids()` (`layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py`, new) keeps the slots in this rank's routed range. `FusedMoE.weight_loader` applies it to a routed expert's slots (not with `require_global_experts`) before `_weight_loader_physical` maps them to local ids.
  - This is needed because the list now also holds other ranks' slots. After an elastic EP scale-up, a new rank's routed slot can lie past the `_num_global_routed` that an existing rank's layer set at startup, and `_map_global_expert_id_to_local_expert_id` maps such a slot onto that rank's fused shared expert.
  - From reading the code and a CPU test with a stand-in layer, this already happens on main for a rank that holds no replica of the expert, because its narrowed list is the full list. The filter covers that case too.
- `moe_wna16._local_expert_ids` (`layers/quantization/moe_wna16.py`) writes qzeros outside the layer's loader, so it applies the same filter to routed experts. A fused shared expert's id, which the draft-layer fallback returns, is not filtered.
- The third caller, `elastic_ep/expert_backup_client.py`, already keeps only its own range and is unchanged.
- New CPU test file `test/registered/unit/eplb/test_expert_location_weight_loading.py` (`base-a-test-cpu`, 8 tests). It is a new file because it drives the real `FusedMoE` and `moe_wna16` loaders through a stand-in layer, unlike the existing dispatch-table tests. The tests check that:
  - the lookup returns exactly each expert's slots: a same-rank pair, a two-node layout where a rank narrows to a same-node replica, random EP4 layouts, with and without an a2a backend;
  - the real `FusedMoE.weight_loader` and `_weight_loader_physical` fill every local slot with its own expert (the same layouts, random EP2 and EP4); the stand-in layer records the writes instead of copying tensors;
  - every entry of each rank's static dispatch table points at a slot that holds that expert;
  - after an EP 2 -> 4 scale-up, loading routed experts on the existing ranks keeps their fused shared slot;
  - a param with `_sglang_require_global_experts` still gets every slot, on every rank (the new filter does not apply to it);
  - `moe_wna16` picks the right qzeros slots: a second replica, scale-up on ranks 0 and 1, a draft layer with a fused shared expert;
  - the dispatch candidates are unchanged;
  - the draft-layer fallback and the global-scale branch keep their conventions, and out-of-range and negative ids raise.

Alternatives considered:

- Keep every local replica when narrowing. This fixes loading but changes dispatch: `dynamic` gets more candidates, and the static table draws its random picks in a different order.
- Change only dispatch, so that no rank picks an unloaded replica. After an online rebalance the lists are full again, and a slot that keeps the same expert is not copied (`update_expert_weights_single_layer` treats it as unchanged), so a never-written slot can still be picked.
- Copy the first local replica into the others after loading. That has to cover every load path and every parameter, including quantization scales.

## Accuracy Tests

**CPU repro** (script and full output below). EP2, 4 logical experts + 2 redundant, rank 1 holds both replicas of expert 3 (slots 3 and 4), rank 0 holds none.

- On main @ 78185f4b, rank 1 never writes slot 4. Rank 0's static table sends expert 3 to slot 4 in 1 of 8 layers, and with `dynamic`, 4047 of rank 0's 8000 tokens for expert 3 go there.
- With this PR, rank 1 writes slots 3, 4 and 5. Both ranks' static picks for expert 3 are the same as on main, layer by layer; this PR does not touch the dispatch tables.

**CPU tests**

- The new file: 8 passed, 42 subtests.
- Together with the existing `test/registered/unit/eplb/`, `test/registered/unit/model_loader/test_presharded_loader.py`, `test/registered/unit/model_loader/test_modelopt_loader.py` and `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_moe_wna16_ep_shard.py`: 123 passed, 2 skipped (both need CUDA), 88 subtests passed.
- With the fix reverted in place (the old lookup, a filter that keeps every id, the old `moe_wna16` code), 6 of the 8 new tests fail. Each of these partial changes makes at least one new test fail:
  - reverting only the lookup;
  - making only the new filter keep every id;
  - reverting only the `moe_wna16` change;
  - filtering shared ids in `moe_wna16` too;
  - applying the filter to `require_global_experts` params too;
  - dropping the lower bound of the id check.
- Lint with the versions pinned in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, plus `check_registered_tests`: clean.

**GPU.** We ran this change once, on an earlier `main`, with the two saved layouts; this was not a GPU run of 78185f4b itself. That tree also had the changes of #45341, which are inactive here because the weight cache is off.

- Model and flags: Qwen3-30B-A3B (BF16) with `--tp 2 --ep-size 2 --enable-eplb --ep-num-redundant-experts 2 --random-seed 42 --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode normal --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --deepep-dispatcher-output-dtype bf16 --max-running-requests 128 --mem-fraction-static 0.6 --disable-radix-cache --eplb-rebalance-num-iterations 1000000000 --expert-distribution-recorder-buffer-size 1000` (no rebalance during the test), plus `--init-expert-location` set to one of the two saved layouts above.
- Controls, in the same run: the same model, flags, saved layouts and disk-loading path, without this change. Their trees also had inactive weight-cache changes.
- After loading, we hashed every tensor on every rank, slot by slot for the expert tensors.
- A slot counts as an expert only if its hashes equal those of an expert in a server that used the default layout and never rebalanced.
- The reference is a server that routes with the same layout and whose 6240 expert slots all hold the expert the layout puts there. It received its weights through the weight cache from a server that had rebalanced into this layout (#45341).
- Greedy outputs: 8 fixed prompts x 32 tokens.

| | layout 1 | layout 2 |
|---|---|---|
| layers with two replicas of an expert on one rank (of 48) | 16 | 23 |
| slots that hold such a second replica (of 6240) | 19 | 27 |
| without this change: slots that hold no expert | 19, exactly those | 27, exactly those |
| without this change: expert slots equal to the reference | 6221 | 6213 |
| with this change: expert slots equal to the reference | 6240 | 6240 |
| greedy outputs equal to the reference, without / with this change | 7/8 / 8/8 | 5/8 / 8/8 |

All non-expert tensors were byte-identical to the reference on both ranks, in all four servers.

GSM8K (5-shot, all 1319 questions, 128 at a time) was recorded for context and was not a criterion. Correct answers: 1204 and 1210 without this change, 1205 and 1193 with it. Two passes of the never-rebalanced server on the same setup differed by 7 and by 9.

Not tested on GPU:
- quantized checkpoints (the `moe_wna16` path);
- elastic EP scale-up;
- `dynamic` dispatch;
- online rebalancing after startup, and weight updates after it;
- other models, EP > 2, more than one node;
- a repeat of this run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not measured. Only weight loading changes: the lookup compares one row of `physical_to_logical_map` per call instead of indexing the per-rank list, and a rank that holds two replicas of an expert now writes that expert twice. Dispatch and forward passes are unchanged.

## Related

- #10874: the per-rank narrowing.
- The earlier fix for unloaded rows of global scale parameters: #12866, #13162, #13348 (reverted #13162 after loading hangs), #13484 (reintroduced it with a race fix).
- #32962: no narrowing without an a2a backend.
- Open #45282 and #37923 also edit `eplb/expert_location.py`, in other functions.
- deepseek-ai/EPLB#22: the algorithm can put duplicate replicas on one GPU. deepseek-ai/EPLB#27 and deepseek-ai/EPLB#28 try to avoid that where possible; layouts that already exist are not changed.
- Open #45322 adds an `elif` right before the `logical_to_all_physical()` call in `FusedMoE.weight_loader`. Whichever lands second may need a small rebase.
- Different from #39580 and #18213, which are about wrong output after rebalancing without an a2a backend.

<details>
<summary>CPU repro script</summary>

```python
"""CPU-only repro: with an a2a backend (e.g. --moe-a2a-backend deepep) and an
--init-expert-location physical_to_logical_map that puts two replicas of one
logical expert on the same EP rank, the second replica is never loaded, while
another rank's static dispatch table can still route tokens to it.

It calls the real SGLang code; no GPU, model or server is needed:
  compute_initial_expert_location_metadata    what each rank builds from --init-expert-location
  ExpertLocationMetadata.logical_to_all_physical  the slots FusedMoE.weight_loader writes
  topk_ids_logical_to_physical                the physical slot a token is dispatched to

Usage: PYTHONPATH=<sglang checkout>/python python repro_same_rank_replica.py [--layers N]
Exit code: 1 if a rank dispatches to a slot its owner never loads, else 0.
"""

import argparse
import json
import sys
from unittest import mock

import torch

from sglang.srt.eplb import expert_location as el
from sglang.srt.eplb.expert_location_dispatch import (
    ExpertLocationDispatchInfo,
    topk_ids_logical_to_physical,
)
from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_context

EP_SIZE = 2
NUM_LOGICAL = 4
NUM_REDUNDANT = 2
NUM_PHYSICAL = NUM_LOGICAL + NUM_REDUNDANT  # 6 slots: rank 0 = 0..2, rank 1 = 3..5
SLOTS_PER_RANK = NUM_PHYSICAL // EP_SIZE
NUM_LAYERS = 8  # --layers
HOT = 3
# Same row in every layer: logical expert 3 has two replicas, both on rank 1
# (slots 3 and 4); rank 0 has no replica of it.
ROW = [0, 1, 2, 3, 3, 0]


def owner(slot):
    return slot // SLOTS_PER_RANK


def build_rank(rank, a2a_backend, dispatch_algorithm, num_tokens=1):
    """Return what one EP rank loads and where it dispatches, per layer."""
    shape = el.ModelConfigForExpertLocation(
        num_layers=NUM_LAYERS, num_logical_experts=NUM_LOGICAL
    )
    overrides = dict(
        device="cpu",
        ep_size=EP_SIZE,
        nnodes=1,
        moe_a2a_backend=a2a_backend,
        ep_dispatch_algorithm=dispatch_algorithm,
        ep_num_redundant_experts=NUM_REDUNDANT,
        init_expert_location=json.dumps(
            {"physical_to_logical_map": [ROW] * NUM_LAYERS}
        ),
    )
    # No model is loaded, so only the layer / expert counts come from the patch.
    with get_context().override_server_args(**overrides), mock.patch.object(
        el.ModelConfigForExpertLocation,
        "from_model_config",
        staticmethod(lambda model_config: shape),
    ):
        # ModelRunner.maybe_init_expert_location_metadata does this on every rank
        # before load_model(). With static dispatch it also builds this rank's
        # logical_to_rank_dispatch_physical_map (a seeded random pick, seed 42).
        metadata = el.compute_initial_expert_location_metadata(
            model_config=None, moe_ep_rank=rank
        )
        el.set_global_expert_location_metadata(metadata, allow_overwrite=True)
        loaded, dispatch = [], []
        for layer in range(NUM_LAYERS):
            # FusedMoE.weight_loader: for checkpoint expert e, write every slot in
            # logical_to_all_physical(layer, e) that lives on this rank.
            loaded.append(
                sorted(
                    slot
                    for e in range(NUM_LOGICAL)
                    for slot in metadata.logical_to_all_physical(layer, e)
                    if owner(slot) == rank
                )
            )
            info = ExpertLocationDispatchInfo.init_new(layer_id=layer)
            topk_ids = torch.full((num_tokens, 1), HOT, dtype=torch.int64)
            dispatch.append(topk_ids_logical_to_physical(topk_ids, info).view(-1))
        candidates = metadata.logical_to_all_physical(0, HOT)
    return loaded, dispatch, candidates


def run(a2a_backend, dispatch_algorithm, num_tokens=1):
    ranks = [
        build_rank(r, a2a_backend, dispatch_algorithm, num_tokens)
        for r in range(EP_SIZE)
    ]
    print(
        f"\n== --moe-a2a-backend {a2a_backend} "
        f"--ep-dispatch-algorithm {dispatch_algorithm} =="
    )
    for r, (loaded, _, candidates) in enumerate(ranks):
        never = sorted(
            set(range(r * SLOTS_PER_RANK, (r + 1) * SLOTS_PER_RANK)) - set(loaded[0])
        )
        print(
            f"rank {r}: weight loader writes slots {loaded[0]}, never writes {never}; "
            f"logical_to_all_physical(layer, {HOT}) = {candidates}"
        )
    bad_layers = set()
    for r, (_, dispatch, _) in enumerate(ranks):
        hits = {}  # layer -> tokens sent to a slot its owner never loaded
        for layer, slots in enumerate(dispatch):
            missing = [
                int(s) for s in slots if int(s) not in ranks[owner(int(s))][0][layer]
            ]
            if missing:
                hits[layer] = missing
        bad_layers |= set(hits)
        slots_hit = sorted({s for m in hits.values() for s in m})
        if num_tokens == 1:
            picks = [int(d[0]) for d in dispatch]
            print(
                f"rank {r}: logical {HOT} is dispatched to slot, per layer: {picks}"
                + (
                    f"\n        -> never-loaded slot {slots_hit} in layers {sorted(hits)}"
                    if hits
                    else ""
                )
            )
        else:
            n = sum(len(m) for m in hits.values())
            print(
                f"rank {r}: {n}/{num_tokens * NUM_LAYERS} tokens of logical {HOT} go to "
                f"never-loaded slot(s) {slots_hit} ({len(hits)}/{NUM_LAYERS} layers)"
            )
    return len(bad_layers)


def main():
    global NUM_LAYERS
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("--layers", type=int, default=NUM_LAYERS)
    NUM_LAYERS = parser.parse_args().layers
    print(
        f"EP size {EP_SIZE}, {NUM_LOGICAL} logical experts + {NUM_REDUNDANT} redundant = "
        f"{NUM_PHYSICAL} slots ({SLOTS_PER_RANK} per rank), {NUM_LAYERS} layers"
    )
    print(
        f"--init-expert-location row in every layer: rank 0 slots 0-2 = {ROW[:3]}, "
        f"rank 1 slots 3-5 = {ROW[3:]}"
    )
    bad_static = run("deepep", "static")
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    bad_dynamic = run("deepep", "dynamic", num_tokens=1000)
    bad_control = run("none", "dynamic", num_tokens=1000)
    print()
    print(f"layers that route to a never-loaded slot (of {NUM_LAYERS}):")
    print(f"  deepep + static (default with an a2a backend): {bad_static}")
    print(f"  deepep + dynamic: {bad_dynamic}")
    print(f"  control, no a2a backend: {bad_control}")
    reproduced = bad_static > 0 or bad_dynamic > 0
    print("RESULT:", "REPRODUCED" if reproduced else "NOT_REPRODUCED")
    return 1 if reproduced else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

</details>

title: [Fix] [AMD] gpt-oss: support EP for gfx1250 W4A8 MXFP4 MoE
author: sogalin
body:
## Motivation

On gfx1250, serving `amd/gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8` with `--tp 2 --ep-size 2` crashes with a GPU memory fault during decode CUDA graph capture (in `_moe_gemm_a8w4_decode`).

The gfx1250 W4A8 MoE path(gluon MoE) routes over all 128 global experts, but with EP each rank only holds its 64 local experts. 

## Modifications

- `aiter_mxfp4_w4a8_moe.py`: when an `expert_map` is given, route from the global logits with aiter's `ep_sort_routing`. Gates for non-local experts go to a sentinel bin (no GEMM blocks scheduled) and are masked out of the GEMM2 reduce via `gate_valid`. The layer's existing all-reduce sums the per-rank partial outputs.
- `quark_w4a8_mxfp4_moe.py`: build the global→local `expert_map` once after weight loading (before CUDA graph capture) when `moe_ep_size > 1`, and pass it to the forward.

Scope: all changes are behind the existing `_use_gfx1250_w4a8` gate (HIP + gfx1250), so other platforms and architectures are unaffected. On gfx1250 without EP, the original `routing()` path is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8, `--tp 2 --ep-size 2`, and `--tp 4 --ep-size 4`  gfx1250:

| | Before | After (TP2/EP2) | After (TP4/EP4) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Server startup | GPU memory fault | OK | OK |
| GSM8K (1319 examples) | N/A | 96.21% | 95.98% |

Kernel-level check: the EP=2 output (rank 0 + rank 1 summed) matches a PyTorch dequantized reference with ~2.5e-3 relative error for batch sizes 1–256.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This is a correctness fix; it was crashing before, so there is no prior baseline to compare against.

title: [CI] [NPU] precise-test: add recommendation summary & run artifacts, fix NPU-only coverage view, and quiet benign teardown noise
author: chenyang08056032
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

The NPU precise-test (coverage-based test selection) pipeline needs better run-page
observability and a quieter, faster teardown:

- **Opaque selection results.** The bucketing step only emitted machine-readable
  `GITHUB_OUTPUT` values, so on the run page there was no way to see which tests
  coverage recommended, which suites were skipped vs. ran a subset, and which
  recommended files matched no suite pool.
- **Broken NPU-only coverage view.** The NPU-only report relied on a separate rcfile
  with `[run] source`, but `source` does not filter at report time — the "NPU-only"
  view was identical to the full report, so the per-tree NPU coverage number was
  meaningless.
- **No per-run artifacts.** precise-test outputs (`outputs.tar.gz`,
  `test_case_map.json`) only lived on the shared publish disk under fixed names that
  race with concurrent runs; nothing was attached to the run itself for debugging.
- **Benign log noise masking real failures:**
  - coverage 7.8: multiprocessing workers that receive the teardown SIGTERM after
    their coverage already stopped die on `assert self._collectors`, printing a
    scary multi-process traceback per worker (tests still pass).
  - CANN `tbe` repository-manager queue-client threads flood the log with ~15-line
    `EOFError`/`ConnectionResetError` tracebacks per process during graceful
    teardown — vendor-inherent and benign.
  - The tbe atexit `rm -rf` of the shared `kernel_meta` compile-cache races with
    sibling ranks still writing `kernel_meta_temp_*` dirs, printing one `rm` error
    line per directory.
- **Slow teardown.** The 20s graceful-kill timeout adds dead time to every test
  run; teardown reliably completes well within 5s.

## Modifications

- **`.github/workflows/pr-test-npu.yml`**
  - Pass `--github-summary "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"` to the bucketing step.
  - Fix the NPU-only coverage view: copy the combined data to `.coverage-npu`,
    `touch_file()` every unexecuted `.py` under `sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu`
    (`os.walk`, so the PEP 420 namespace tree with no `__init__.py` counts fully),
    then filter with `--include`, which does apply at report time; same for the
    summary totals line.
  - Upload a `precise-test-outputs` artifact (`outputs.tar.gz` +
    `test_case_map.json`, ~300MB, 14-day retention, `continue-on-error`) before the
    publish step moves the files into the fixed `PUBLISH_DIR`.
- **`scripts/ci/npu/precise-test/bucket_recommended_tests.py`**
  - New `--github-summary` option / `write_github_summary()`: appends a markdown
    section with the precision-mode state, recommended case count, a per-suite
    table (registered / bucketed / action), and collapsible lists of recommended
    cases, files matching no suite pool, and per-suite buckets.
  - Keep raw case-level entries (with `::case` suffix) for the summary; write job
    outputs before the summary so a summary failure can never cost downstream jobs
    their bucket outputs.
- **`scripts/ci/npu/precise-test/run_tests_with_coverage.sh`**
  - Replace the one-line `.pth` with a `sglang_ci_cov_guard.py` guard module
    (inert unless `COVERAGE_PROCESS_START` is set): makes `Collector.stop`
    idempotent, patches `Coverage._on_sigterm` to flush via the stock atexit path
    and then die quietly via `SIG_DFL`, and installs a structural
    `threading.excepthook` that swallows only the known tbe queue-client teardown
    shape — any traceback with foreign frames still prints in full.
  - Filter benign `rm` errors on `kernel_meta` paths from pytest output
    (`grep -vE`; `PIPESTATUS[0]` preserves the pytest exit code).
  - Default graceful timeout 20s → 5s.
- **`scripts/ci/npu/precise-test/precise_test_coverage_plugin.py`**
  - Graceful timeout default 20s → 5s, kept in sync with the shell script.

author: JackChuang
body:
Follow-up to [#43363](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43363), merged today: it broke two CPU unit tests on `main`, and this test-only PR fixes them. Sorry for the breakage.
cc @Fridge003 (merged [#43363](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43363); added the dispatcher test in [#44666](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44666)) and @Jiminator (added the placement test in [#44518](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44518)).
Ready to run: `/rerun-test test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_flashinfer_dispatcher.py`. `test_moe_runner_config_placement.py` runs only in the Intel CPU suite (`stage-b-test-cpu-intel`), so `/rerun-test` on ubuntu-latest skips it.

## Summary

- **Fixes two CPU unit tests that fail on `main` since [#43363](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43363) merged.** Both call the FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE runner directly without publishing server args. [#43363](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43363) made the runner read the `disagg` config to size its tuning range, so they now raise `ValueError: config namespace 'disagg' not published`.

Since #43363, the CUTLASS MoE runner (`python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutlass.py`) reads `get_disagg()` and the prefill-chunk settings on every call. title: [Fix] modelopt: Correct NVFP4 TRT-LLM clamps for untied gate/up scales
author: Jiminator
body:
## Motivation

TRT-LLM applies one GEMM1 clamp to both raw gate/up projections. With unequal NVFP4 global scales, converting the limit using the gate alpha gives the up projection the wrong effective limit: the up limit becomes `L × up_alpha / gate_alpha`, so a configured limit of 7 becomes 28 at a 4× ratio, or becomes stricter when the ratio is below one.

## Modifications

Normalize the effective gate/up alphas to their maximum during the existing TRT-LLM clamp preparation, folding the scale ratio into the smaller-alpha half’s E4M3 block scales. Derive the clamp, beta and output scale from the shared alpha. The fold uses the resolved gate/up alphas and leaves the raw global scales as loaded. Block-scale rows in this backend are `[up, gate]`. The work happens at load time, with no added forward operations.

Extend the existing CPU post-load regression for both halves' effective clamp limits, weight preservation and SiTU behavior, with GPU packing mocked. The GPU regression used in the accuracy tests below was a development-only fixture and is not part of this PR.

## Accuracy Tests

On rebased `main` commit `c1c287a42928495166e14dbcef31b9e1f1dac199` (including #45289), the CPU scale suite passes 20/20 and dispatch suite passes 5/5, with GPU devices hidden. The CPU clamp regression fails on this base with an effective up-half clamp of 28 instead of 7 and passes with the fix.

The GPU and numerical results below were collected before this rebase, against `main` commit `afe3e1df3107b0487258cd4a3d8e625248a8f881` on GB300 with PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.2 and sglang-kernel 0.4.10. GPU runs were not repeated for conflict resolution:

- A development copy of the GPU backend test with a temporary unequal-scale clamp regression passed 5/5 with this fix; the regression fails on the base at cosine 0.9034 against the unchanged 0.99 threshold. That temporary regression is not committed.
- Exact power-of-two controls match tied outputs bitwise, including real GLM expert weights with synthetic activations, routed/non-routed execution, per-token activation, reload and CUDA graph replay. Tied, unclamped, SiTU and sibling-backend controls are preserved.
- All 14 non-binary cases match the unmodified backend loaded with the same normalized weights bitwise, on both execution paths.
- Public prompt check on `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` at revision `da920bb0b9f4a06727223a349e55468e38352348`: the untouched checkpoint gives identical responses before/after. Re-expressing gate globals as ×4 and gate block scales as ÷4 is exact for this checkpoint; the fix’s ÷4 rescaling of the up block scales is exact too. The base then changes its response from 373 to 95 tokens; this fix restores the original content, token strings and logprobs exactly. Each configuration was repeated twice, with separate logprob diagnostics and cache flushes.

All public prompt runs copied the final table correctly and contained no replacement characters; their raw content included reasoning. This checks representation invariance, not reproduction of the reported Unicode failure. The reported finetuned checkpoint was unavailable.

**Rounding tradeoff:** non-binary normalization re-rounds one half's FP8 block scales. In the synthetic sweep, that changed the half's weights by 2.7–3.2% relative L2 and the reference output by 4.7–8.5% with both activation quantization steps included (0.7–3.4% when both were omitted). Every tested case improved over the incorrect clamp. No underflow occurred in these fixtures, but sufficiently small scales can become subnormal or flush to zero, including with power-of-two ratios. This is not a general model-quality evaluation.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Before this rebase, sequential A/B/A/B CUDA graph measurements covered 52 points: 1–4096 tokens, routed/non-routed, tied/untied scales, 288 experts, hidden size 4096, intermediate size 512 and top-8, with L2 flushed before timing. All output controls passed. Candidate/base latency ratios were 0.9936–1.0031, within the pre-set `max(2%, 2 × baseline run spread)` criterion. The untied post-load step took 97–115 ms versus 90–105 ms on the base, once per 288-expert MoE layer at load time. Profiles confirm the TRT-LLM E2M1 GEMM/SwiGLU kernels.

## Checklist

- [x] Full `pre-commit run --all-files` passed without modifications on the validated tree, which also contained the temporary GPU fixture.
- [x] Added and ran the CPU post-load regression; isort, Ruff lint and formatting checks pass.
- [x] Ran GPU validation with a temporary regression fixture.
- [x] Provided numerical and operator-latency evidence.
- [x] Followed existing code style and backend preparation structure.
- Documentation: no public API or configuration change.

title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] deepseek-v4.1: Fix the breakable prefill CUDA graph in the late-layer tail on SM90
author: JohnZhao01
body:
## Motivation

On H200 (SM90), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with decoder SWA bounded replay (on by default; the [cookbook](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/76560713092795ac051d0411574c3a8d73145c2f/docs/cookbook/autoregressive/DeepSeek/DeepSeek-V4_1.mdx#L108) lists breakable prefill as supported with it) cannot serve with `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable`. The late-layer tail fails in two places, both on paths that SM100 does not take: SM90 has no in-graph low-ratio path (`low_ratio_prefill_graph` is false), so the ratio-1/2 sources run as eager breaks or, in one place, get captured.

1. **Warmup before capture.** The first faulting kernel is the device-side assert in `torch.repeat_interleave` (`Repeat.cu:20: result_size == cumsum_ptr[size - 1]`); the CUDA 719 and DeepGEMM errors that follow are knock-on errors. Call chain: `bcg_deepseek_v4_low_ratio_sources` → `forward_low_ratio_sources` → `token_req_indices` → `repeat_interleave(req, extend_seq_lens, output_size=positions.shape[0])`. Inside the tail, the eager break sees only the tail's live rows, while `forward_batch.extend_seq_lens` still spans the whole extend. The hoisted `low_ratio_req_indices` / `low_ratio_pos_i64` already hold the tail's rows (live rows first, bucket-sized), but they are only used when their length equals the break's row count, which it does not inside an eager break.
2. **Replay of the first real request.** With (1) fixed, capture and startup succeed, and the first real prefill asserts in a replayed graph: `the output_size argument (8) must be the same as the sum of the elements in the repeats tensor (6)`. The source-layer KV write at the start of the tail (`write_tail_source_kv`) is called directly from the model, not through an eager break, so on SM90 its `token_req_indices` and the host-side compressor are captured with the capture-time row count.

This still reproduces on `main` @ `c1c287a4`: without this change, the breakable launch below crashes while capturing the prefill graph with the same `Repeat.cu:20` assert.

#45381 fixes a different capture failure of the same low-ratio prefill-graph path on SM12x.

## Modifications

- `deepseek_v4_backend.py` (`forward_low_ratio_sources`): when the hoisted rows are longer than the break's rows in an extend, take their live prefix instead of rebuilding the rows from `extend_seq_lens`. Bucket-sized calls (the in-graph path) and calls without hoisted rows are unchanged.
  - The hoisted rows are longer only under the prefill graph, where both the prefill-graph metadata and the tail metadata store the live rows first and the padding after them. Outside the tail the live prefix therefore equals what `token_req_indices` computes; inside the tail it is the only correct value. The prefill-graph full top-k break (`_prefill_graph_full_topk_break`) already takes `low_ratio_req_indices[:real]` the same way. If a narrower condition is preferred, it can check the tail metadata explicitly; happy to switch.
- `deepseek_v4.py`: a new eager break, `bcg_deepseek_v4_write_tail_source_kv`, slices the source-layer input to the live rows like `deepseek_v4_low_ratio_sources`, with the same capture-stub contract as `_low_ratio_sources_capture_stub`. The tail's source-KV write uses it inside a breakable prefill graph when the backend has no in-graph low-ratio path; every other configuration keeps the direct call. The condition reads `low_ratio_prefill_graph` the same way as the existing low-ratio call site in `_forward_prepare`. With no live rows it skips the write but still sets `tail_source_kv_layer_id`, as `write_tail_source_kv` does, so the source layer's own pass inside the tail keeps skipping its compressor. Rebased onto `main` @ `c1c287a4`, where #45339 computes `source_x` at the same call site with a HIP branch; that computation is kept and only the call after it is dispatched.
- Tests (run on H200 against `main` @ `c1c287a4`):
  - `TestDSV4LateLayerTailLowRatioRows` checks that a tail-sized eager break gets the live prefix of the hoisted rows for both the compressor and the indexer. It fails before this change (`RuntimeError: allocated size does not match required size` from `repeat_interleave`, the rows rebuilt from `extend_seq_lens` not matching the break's row count) and passes after.
  - `TestDSV4WriteTailSourceKvBreak` checks that the source-KV break passes only the first `global_num_token_non_padded_cpu` rows of `x` and `positions` to `write_tail_source_kv`, and that with zero live rows it does not call it but still marks the source layer. It covers a function this PR adds, so it has no before/after comparison; it passes.

## Accuracy Tests

Setup: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 8×H200, image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261021-c1c287a4` (`main` @ `c1c287a4`), with this PR's commits applied to the image's source tree for the "this change" column.

Launch flags: `--tp 8 --attention-backend dsv4 --moe-runner-backend marlin --mem-fraction-static 0.70 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --prefill-decode-interval 16 --enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay --swa-prefix-tails 1024 --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 5 --speculative-num-steps 1 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 2 --language-model-only`, plus `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable --cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill 4096` for the graph runs. "Eager" is the same launch without the two prefill-graph flags.

| | eager (no prefill graph) | breakable, before this change | breakable, this change |
|---|---|---|---|
| startup | ready | crashes while capturing the prefill graph (`Repeat.cu:20` assert, item 1) | ready |
| GSM8K, sgl-eval 0.1.3, 1,319 questions, model preset (thinking on, reasoning effort high, T=1.0, top_p 0.95) | 0.9704 | — | 0.9697 |
| GSM8K, lm-eval with the InferenceX setup, 5-shot, flexible / strict | 0.9735 / 0.9742 | — | 0.9727 / 0.9735 |
| long-context retrieval, 6 prompts | 6/6 | — | 6/6 |
| `max_total_num_tokens` | 23,892,736 | — | 23,892,736 |
| smoke: 15 real prefills, 1 to 30,000 words (9 single, 6 concurrent, covering the padded bucket sizes) | 15/15 | — | 15/15 |

- Server logs of all runs of both columns have no assert and no CUDA error.
- Which requests exercise the changed path: under decoder SWA bounded replay every prefill extend runs the late layers over each request's last min(extend length, 128) rows, 128 being the model's sliding window (`SWA_WINDOW`), unless it asks for prompt logprobs or every hidden state; speculative verify extends do not run the tail. (`--swa-prefix-tails 1024` is unrelated: it sizes how many radix-cached prefix tails the SWA KV pool keeps room for.) In a separate run of this change with a counting log added (not part of this PR), sgl-eval GSM8K (200 questions) and the smoke ran 40 prefill forwards through the tail after startup: 31 were graph replays (up to 3,447 tail rows), which run the two eager breaks changed here, and 9 ran eager (batches over the 4,096-token capture cap, or chunks whose context exceeds the 16K replay limit).
- Earlier measurements on `nightly-dev-cu13-20261018-b234b5c3`, before the rebase: GSM8K (InferenceX setup) 0.9727 / 0.9735 with this change and eager, a second pair with `--max-running-requests 64` at 0.9742 / 0.9742, long-context retrieval 6/6, smoke 15/15.
- Prompt logprobs (on b234b5c3; 21 fixed prompts, 40 to 12,000 words, 76,144 prompt tokens, `/generate` with `return_logprob` and `logprob_start_len 0`, T=0): the graph-vs-eager difference (mean |Δlogprob| 0.158 / 0.160) is the same as the run-to-run difference of each configuration (0.159 eager, 0.157 graph). Requests for prompt logprobs run the late layers over the whole prompt rather than the bounded tail, so this check covers the graph's numerics but not the tail path changed here; the tail path is covered by the accuracy rows and the smoke above.

`--cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill 4096`: with the default capture sizes the graph pool takes about 29.6 GB at `--mem-fraction-static 0.70`, and the first eager chunk of a 128K cold prefill (chunks past the 16K replay limit run eager) ran out of memory in the eager torch indexer scoring (measured on b234b5c3). Capping the capture at 4,096 tokens keeps the pool at 8.75 GB with the same KV pool size. That is a memory-headroom setting for this configuration, not part of the fix: with the default capture sizes the fix also captures, starts and serves the same smoke prefills without errors, with the same KV pool size, long-context retrieval 6/6 and GSM8K 0.9697 (within the ±0.0047 standard error); only the 128K cold prefill ran out of memory.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

On `main` @ `c1c287a4` (single requests, same server as the accuracy rows):

| | eager | this change (breakable, bs 4096) |
|---|---|---|
| 128K cold prefill (131,071 tokens) TTFT | 6.30 s | 6.05 s |
| decode TPOT p50, B = 1 / 8 / 16 | 2.15 / 4.80 / 6.39 ms | 2.18 / 4.69 / 6.60 ms |
| 262K-token request with 4 short requests behind it: long TTFT | 19.68 s | 19.69 s |

Measured earlier on b234b5c3:

Cold-prefill TTFT (random-word prompts, no cache hit, `max_tokens` 1, median of 3; the nominal sizes are estimated at 2.3 words per token, so actual token counts are somewhat larger):

| nominal prompt | eager | this change (breakable, bs 4096) |
|---|---|---|
| 512 | 0.202 s | 0.079 s |
| 2K | 0.201 s | 0.150 s |
| 8K | 0.384 s | 0.368 s |
| 16K | 0.776 s | 0.784 s |
| 32K | 1.587 s | 1.605 s |
| 128K | 9.310 s | 9.380 s |

Short prefills lose a fixed ~0.2 s of eager launch overhead. Prefill chunks whose context exceeds 16K still run eager on SM90 (#43733 lifts that limit only on SM100), so long prefills are unchanged.

Load test, 900 s per point after a 600 s warmup, InferenceX agentic traces (SLO lines TTFT p90 ≤ 5,750 ms, TPOT p90 ≤ 34.5 ms), same flags as above with `--max-running-requests 64`:

| eager | 10 | 56,550 tok/s (TTFT p90 1,902 ms, TPOT p90 19.7 ms) |

title: [Fix] [Apple] mlx: Give the stub model a shared-expert layout
author: ItsOdeLeo
body:
## Motivation

Since #44913, every MLX server crashes during startup:

```
File ".../model_executor/runner/base_runner.py", line 250, in model_context
    shared_experts=self.model_runner.model.shared_experts_config
AttributeError: '_DummyModel' object has no attribute 'shared_experts_config'
```

#44913 made the eager and graph runners read `model.shared_experts_config` during warmup. The Torch model loader sets it on every model, but the MLX stub replaces the model with `_DummyModel`, which never had it.

title: [Fix] rust-server: Drop the fixed 64-item multimodal cap in favor of --limit-mm-data-per-request
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

The Rust frontend rejected any multimodal request carrying more than 64 media items (`MAX_ITEMS_PER_REQUEST` in `sglang-mm`), in both the prefetch layer and the driver. The Python frontend has no such fixed cap: the only per-request count limit it applies is the operator's `--limit-mm-data-per-request`, checked per modality in `TokenizerManager._validate_mm_limits`. A request with, say, 80 small images is served by the Python path and 400'd by the Rust path, with an error message no Python server produces.

The per-modality check also differed from Python in a detail that shows when several modalities are over their limit at once: Python iterates `--limit-mm-data-per-request` in its configured order and reports the first modality exceeded, while the Rust side iterated a fixed image/video/audio order.

## Modifications

- `sglang-mm` driver: remove `MAX_ITEMS_PER_REQUEST` and its check. The per-request byte budget (`MAX_REQUEST_BYTES`, 1.25 GiB) and the per-stream fetch cap stay as the memory bounds, so a request of any item count is still bounded in bytes. The README sentence describing the budgets is updated.
- `sglang-server` prefetch: drop the item-count rejection; apply `--limit-mm-data-per-request` in its configured order with Python's message (`"<Modality> count N exceeds limit M per request."`), still before a single byte is fetched. Unset means no per-modality limit.
- `ServerArgs.limit_mm_data_per_request` becomes `Vec<(String, usize)>` so the configured order survives the Python -> Rust handoff; `rust_server/config.py` passes `list(dict.items())`. `CoreConfig`/`CoreInner::mm_limits` and the test helpers follow the new type.
- Tests: the driver test now asserts that 100 images process in full while the byte budget still rejects; prefetch tests cover 200 local sources without a limit, the first-over-limit-in-configured-order message, the at-limit pass-through, and the Python unit test pins that the launcher forwards an unset limit as `[]` and a set one in its configured order.

No server behaviour changes for requests under 64 items with a single modality limit; `/server_info` output is unchanged (`ServerArgs` is not serialized).

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: request admission only, no change to model forward or outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

## Test plan

- `cd rust && cargo test --locked -p sglang-mm -p sglang-server`: 364 passed, 0 failed (sglang-server lib, 4 consecutive runs) and sglang-mm green, on this branch; the same suite on `main` 4/4 green.
- `python -m pytest test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_rust_server_dp_ports.py`: 28 passed.

title: [Fix] mamba: Keep prefill rows' checkpoint tracking through mixed chunked prefill
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

With `--enable-mixed-chunk` and the `extra_buffer` / `extra_buffer_lazy` Mamba radix cache, a prefill chunk that runs in the same forward as running decodes (a MIXED step) saves no Mamba state, but the radix cache still stores its checkpoint:

1. `prepare_for_extend` claims the request's next ping-pong slot and stamps `mamba_last_track_seqlen` for every extend row whose chunk reaches the checkpoint grid.
2. `mix_with_running` -> `merge_batch` resets every `mamba_track_*` field to `None`, and nothing rebuilds them.
3. The linear-attention backends gate the extend-side state copy on the track mask, so the MIXED forward never writes the claimed slot.
4. The slot is donated anyway at the stamped depth. A later request that resumes from that prefix restores whatever the slot held before. The output is wrong with no error.

## Modifications

- `ScheduleBatch.mix_with_running` saves the prefill rows' track tensors and host lists before `merge_batch` and restores them after it. The running decode rows are appended as untracked rows (`mask=False`, `seqlen=-1`, index `-1`); decode tails were never tracked in a mixed step, so their behavior is unchanged.
- Lazy strategy: `prepare_for_decode` may already have handed a decode row at a track boundary its next ping-pong slot (`mamba_lazy_prealloc_at_boundary`). A mixed forward writes no decode track state and its result path never frees that slot, so the new `mamba_lazy_undo_prealloc_at_boundary` frees it and restores the row's next index first.
- The row remembers the decode batch in which it rode a mixed step (`ReqKvInfo.mamba_untracked_decode_batch_idx`). In `_handle_finish_state_updated_req`, the lazy "boundary write was in place, skip the radix insert" shortcut no longer fires for a request that finished one step before that boundary, because no in-place write happened.
- `merge_batch` is unchanged; the post-forward running-batch merge must keep dropping tracking, `prepare_for_decode` rebuilds it.

title: [Fix] srt: Pin the source address of TCP ZMQ connects for the peer allowlist
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

#45250 added `SGLANG_ZMQ_ALLOWED_PEERS`: TCP-bound IPC sockets admit only the listed peer addresses, and a multi-node data-parallel deployment lists the addresses of its own nodes. The check is on the source address of the incoming connection, and a plain `socket.connect("tcp://<peer>:<port>")` leaves the choice of source address to the kernel. On a host with several addresses, for example a container on host networking that owns one address of its own while the host has others, the kernel can pick an address that is not in the allowlist. ZAP then rejects the connection, and a PUSH socket with no admitted peer blocks forever on its first send, so the deployment hangs after start-up with no error. Connections to a peer on the same node keep working, because a connect to a local address uses that address as its source, which is why the hang shows up only across nodes.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/environ.py`: new `SGLANG_ZMQ_SOURCE_IP` (default unset), the source address for outgoing TCP IPC connects.
- `python/sglang/srt/utils/network.py`: new `zmq_connect(socket, endpoint)`. When `SGLANG_ZMQ_SOURCE_IP` is set and the endpoint is a TCP endpoint whose host is an IP literal of the same address family, it connects with libzmq's documented `tcp://<source_endpoint>;<endpoint>` form ([zmq_tcp(7)](https://libzmq.readthedocs.io/en/latest/zmq_tcp.html), "Connecting a socket"), here `tcp://<source>:0;<host>:<port>`, so the peer sees the pinned address. A hostname endpoint, an `ipc://` endpoint, an endpoint that already carries a source, a source of the other family, an invalid source, and an unset variable all connect exactly as before. `get_zmq_socket(..., bind=False)` now connects through it.
- `python/sglang/srt/managers/load_snapshot.py`: `ZmqLoadSnapshotWriter` connects through `zmq_connect` as well, since its reader is one of the allowlisting sockets.
- `test/registered/unit/utils/test_network.py` (new, `base-a-test-cpu`): the endpoint rewrite table above, and a regression test with real sockets: with an allowlist of `127.0.0.2`, a PUSH client connecting to a PULL from `get_zmq_socket` at `127.0.0.1` is not delivered, and the same client with `SGLANG_ZMQ_SOURCE_IP=127.0.0.2` is. The second case fails if `get_zmq_socket` goes back to a plain connect.

A multi-node deployment sets the variable on each node to that node's own allowlisted address, next to `SGLANG_ZMQ_ALLOWED_PEERS`. With the variable unset nothing changes. Every connect made through `get_zmq_socket(..., bind=False)` (the data-parallel controller's REQ socket, the multi-tokenizer PUSH sockets, the encoder-disaggregation sockets, the tracing PUSH socket) now goes through `zmq_connect`, so a deployment that sets the variable pins all of them, and the rewrite leaves `ipc://` endpoints alone. The KV-transfer sockets under `disaggregation/common/conn.py` call `connect` directly and are not touched.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no change to scheduling, model execution or outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: with the variable unset the only addition is one string check per connect.

On this head: `pytest test/registered/unit/utils/test_network.py` passes (3 tests, 7 subtests), and fails on the pinned-source case when the `get_zmq_socket` hunk is reverted; `test/registered/unit/managers/test_load_snapshot_backends.py` and `test_data_parallel_controller.py` pass (54 tests). `pre-commit run` on the four files passes.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Fix] disaggregation: Keep a requeued optimistic prefill request's multimodal inputs
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

A PD prefill server serving image requests with optimistic prefill enabled (`--optimistic-prefill-attempts >= 1`, or `--disaggregation-decode-allocation-policy prefill_complete`) can crash with a device-side out-of-bounds assertion in the embedding lookup once a request is yielded and requeued.

`optimistic_release_and_requeue` released the request through `Scheduler._release_aborted_request`. Since #43475 that helper also calls `req.release_mm_inputs_on_abort()` and aborts a streaming session, which is right for a request that is going away but not for one that is about to be prefilled again. The retry then runs with `multimodal_inputs=None` while its input ids still hold the image placeholder values, which are outside the vocabulary by design, and the text-embedding gather asserts. #43442 made this path fire whenever the request slots are exhausted, so an overloaded prefill server hits it regularly; the log line `Req ... exhausted optimistic prefill attempts falling back to bootstrap queue` (or `... optimistic prefill yielded ...`) shows up right before the assert.

## Modifications

- `optimistic_release_and_requeue` now finishes the cache attempt directly (`tree_cache.finish(handle, CacheRequestOutcome.ABORT)`), which is the part of the abort release a requeue still needs. The multimodal inputs and the streaming session stay with the request, as before #43475. Real aborts still go through `_release_aborted_request`.
- `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_prefill_complete_integration.py`: the existing requeue test's fake request gains the `cache_request_handle` the requeue now reads, and a new `test_requeued_optimistic_request_keeps_multimodal_inputs` pins the regression with the real `Scheduler._release_aborted_request` and `Req.release_mm_inputs_on_abort` bound to fakes. It fails on the unfixed code (`multimodal_inputs` is `None` after the requeue) and passes with this change.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: the change only affects which request state survives a requeue; the retry re-embeds its images as it did before #43475.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

title: [Fix] [AMD] imports: Skip import-time device probes when no GPU is visible
author: Arist12
body:
## Motivation

On a ROCm build of torch, `torch.version.hip` is set whether or not the process can see a GPU. Several sglang modules query the device at import time on the HIP path, so a ROCm process without a visible GPU (a CPU-only worker, a router, CPU unit tests) dies while importing `sglang.srt`:

```bash
$ docker run --rm -e HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES= -e SGLANG_USE_AITER=0 <rocm image> python -c "import sglang.srt.layers.quantization"
  File ".../sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/fp8_kernel.py", line 102, in <module>
    if is_fp8_fnuz():
  File ".../sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/fp8_kernel.py", line 98, in is_fp8_fnuz
    return "gfx94" in torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).gcnArchName
RuntimeError: No CUDA GPUs are available
```

The CUDA path does not have this problem: `is_cuda()` already requires `torch.cuda.is_available()`, so the CUDA arch checks return False on a machine with no visible device.

## Modifications

- `srt/utils/common.py`: `is_hip()` also requires `torch.cuda.is_available()`, like `is_cuda()` and the platform layer's `_is_rocm_available()`. `is_gfx95_supported`, `is_gfx942_supported` and `is_gfx1250_supported` check `is_hip()` instead of `torch.version.hip`. In a process with no visible GPU, the `_is_hip`-guarded device queries and aiter imports that run at import time (`is_fp8_fnuz`, `ON_GFX950`, `CUDA_CAPABILITY`, ...) are then skipped, as the `_is_cuda`-guarded ones are on CUDA.
- `kernels/ops/attention/rocm_mla_decode_rope.py`: drop the local `is_hip()`, which asked Triton's active driver at import ("0 active drivers" without a GPU), and use `sglang.srt.utils.is_hip` like the rest of the kernels.

With a GPU visible, `is_hip()` is True as before, so every caller gets the same value; CUDA and CPU builds stop at `torch.version.hip is not None`. `torch.cuda.is_available()` does not run torch's CUDA lazy init, and `import sglang` already calls it (in the platform checks), so HIP is not touched earlier than before. Without a GPU, a ROCm process takes the paths a CUDA process without a GPU takes: `is_hip()`, `is_cuda_alike()` and the gfx probes are False, and `fp8_dtype` / `FP8_E4M3_MAX` are the `float8_e4m3fn` values.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: with a GPU visible, `is_hip()` and every value derived from it are unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the pre-commit hooks.
- [x] Add unit tests: `TestHipProbes` in `test/registered/unit/utils/test_common.py` (CPU).

## Testing

`python -m pytest test/registered/unit/utils/test_common.py`, CPU torch 2.11.0:

- main + the new test: `test_returns_false_without_querying_the_device` fails for all four probes (`is_hip()` returns True, each gfx probe raises `RuntimeError: No CUDA GPUs are available`).
- this PR: 13 passed, 2 skipped, 8 subtests passed.

GPU-less import check: 22 `sglang.srt` / `sglang.kernels` modules, each imported in a fresh interpreter, in `rocm/sgl-dev:miles-rocm10-mi35x-20261019` with no GPU device (`HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=`), aiter main (includes ROCm/aiter#6738). The list includes `layers.quantization`, `model_executor.model_runner`, `managers.scheduler`, `entrypoints.http_server`, `entrypoints.engine` and `models.qwen3_5`. 7/22 import on main (the rest stop at `is_fp8_fnuz`, `is_gfx95_supported` or `is_gfx1250_supported`), 22/22 with this PR, for `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` and `=0`.

I also imported every module under `srt/models`, `srt/layers`, `srt/managers`, `srt/entrypoints` and `kernels/ops` (1646 modules) the same way, with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`. On main, 681 fail at a device query. With this PR, no module that imports on main fails, and 2 still query the device at import: `kernels/ops/diffusion/norm/norm_triton.py` (fails the same way with CPU-only torch) and `kernels/ops/attention/unified_attention_3d_mtp.py` (imports `e4m3_dtype` from aiter, which derives it from the GPU arch; no module imports it at import time). The other failures are missing optional packages, NPU/XPU-only modules, import paths that current aiter does not have, and models that fail the same way with CPU-only torch (Mamba, DBRX, XVERSE MoE).

title: [Fix] http_server: Make SageMaker /ping reflect server readiness
author: shijie-lyu
body:
## Motivation

`GET /ping` (the SageMaker health check) returns a static 200, so SageMaker treats the container as healthy during warmup, after a failed PD warmup, and during SIGTERM drain. The AWS inference container contract says a 200 "indicates to SageMaker AI that the container is ready to accept inference requests", and recommends meaningful health checks over a static 200; the `/ping` request timeout is 2 seconds ([docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/your-algorithms-inference-code.html)).

## Modifications

- Add `TokenizerManager.is_healthy()`: not shutting down and `server_status == Up`. `is_ready()` becomes `not is_pause and is_healthy()`, and the gRPC `RuntimeHandle.health_check()` returns `is_healthy()`. Neither changes behavior (`ServerStatus` has three values, so `not in (Starting, UnHealthy)` equals `== Up`).
- `/ping` returns 200 with an empty body when `is_healthy()`, otherwise 503.
  - It stays an O(1) flag check. It is deliberately not an alias of `/health`: with the default `SGLANG_ENABLE_HEALTH_ENDPOINT_GENERATION=1`, `/health` runs a generation probe that takes 1-20s and mutates `server_status`, which does not fit the 2s timeout.
  - A paused server still answers 200, matching the gRPC `health_check`, so an intentional pause (e.g. a weight sync) does not get the instance replaced. `/ready` still returns 503 while paused.
- `checkpoint_engine/update.py` (package and example): `check_sglang_ready` treats a 503 from `/ping` as "listening". With `--checkpoint-engine-wait-weights-before-ready`, warmup waits on the weights these scripts push, so waiting for 200 would stall startup until `SGLANG_WAIT_WEIGHTS_READY_TIMEOUT`.
- Docs: `/ready` and `/ping` under Health Check; a SageMaker note on `ContainerStartupHealthCheckTimeoutInSeconds`.
- Tests: `/ping` for Up (200, empty body), paused (200), Starting, UnHealthy, and graceful exit (503).

**Behavior change:** `/ping` now returns 503 during warmup, during SIGTERM drain, and while `UnHealthy`. The HTTP server only starts listening after model load, so startup only grows by the warmup time.

**Known limitations (unchanged by this PR):**
- `UnHealthy` is set by a PD warmup failure or a `/health_generate` timeout and stays until a later `/health_generate` succeeds; this now also shows on `/ping` (documented).
- `/ping` is not exempt from `--api-key` auth (`utils/auth.py`); I plan a separate PR.
- Node ranks >= 1 keep the static dummy `/ping` (`utils/common.py`), which is what the checkpoint-engine script expects there.
- The Rust server has no `/ping`; see #41462.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A, no model output change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A.

## Testing

- `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_ready.py`: 10/10 pass (5 existing `/ready` + 5 new `/ping`). The three new 503 cases fail on the pre-change code (`200 != 503`).
- `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_grpc_bridge.py`: 5/5 pass.
- `check_sglang_ready` checked with an `httpx.MockTransport`: a 503 returns after one call, a 500 then 200 retries.
- `pre-commit` passes.
- Not yet run on GPU end to end (503 -> 200 across warmup, 503 after SIGTERM); this PR stays a draft until that log is posted.

title: [Fix] disaggregation: Synchronize deferred decode KV release across TP ranks
author: paulzhang-tm
body:
## Motivation

After a failed prefill-to-decode transfer, acknowledgments and timeout deadlines can differ across attention-TP ranks. Releasing KV capacity on only some ranks lets admission and transfer queues diverge, leading to mismatched polling collective sizes. Rank-local abort notification state can also make ranks disagree on whether to defer a release at all.

## Modifications

- Hold a failed transfer on every attention-TP rank when any rank needs to defer it.
- Release each held request only when every rank has drained or reached its existing device timeout. Host destinations still require a drain acknowledgment regardless of timeout.
- Require no local acknowledgments on ranks that hold only for a peer.
- Add a two-process Gloo regression covering staggered acknowledgments and deadlines, asymmetric notifications, per-request progress, host drain requirements, and disabled deferral. Preserve the existing upstream coverage.

## Accuracy Tests

title: [Fix] rust-server: Check only a client-sent max_new_tokens against the context window
author: metamergebot
body:
Stacked on #45431 (branch `oss-sync-d5268b39ae`): this branch is based on it and edits the `/generate` max_new_tokens tests it adds, so the diff against `main` includes that PR until it merges.

## Motivation

When `--preferred-sampling-params` sets `max_new_tokens` as large as the context length (a preferred `{"max_new_tokens": N}` under `--context-length N`, so that an omitted value means "as much as the window allows"), the Rust frontend returns 400 `Requested token count exceeds the model's maximum context length` for every `/generate` request that leaves `max_new_tokens` out, while the Python frontend serves them. A client that omits `max_new_tokens` on purpose, so the server's defaults apply, cannot use such a launch in Rust mode at all.

The cause is ordering. The Rust HTTP and gRPC adapters fill the preferred params (and, since #45431, the launch default) in beneath the request before decoding, and `check_total_tokens` then validates the filled value as if the client had asked for it. Python's `TokenizerManager._validate_one_request` checks only the request's own `sampling_params["max_new_tokens"]` and merges the preferred params afterwards, so a preferred or default value is never context-checked; the scheduler clamps it to the room the prompt leaves.

## Modifications

- `message/wire.rs`: `ClientMaxNewTokens` reads, before any fill, which requests of a `/generate` body sent their own `max_new_tokens`: one answer for a single or absent `sampling_params` object (applied to every item), one per object for a list; for gRPC, whether the protobuf field is set. A present JSON key counts, even an explicit `null`.
- `api_server/http/native_api.rs`, `api_server/grpc/service.rs`: each `generate` adapter takes that reading first, and after `into_requests` fans the body out marks the requests that did not send one.
- `message/request.rs`: `GenerateRequest::max_new_tokens_defaulted`, set by the adapters (the decoded request no longer shows which keys the client sent).
- `tokenizer_manager/to_scheduler_validation.rs`: `check_total_tokens` skips the input-plus-output check for a defaulted value, which reaches the scheduler as is and is clamped there, as in Python.

Unchanged: the input-alone check (an over-long prompt is still a 400); the rejection, or the `allow_auto_truncate` clamp, of a value the client sent; the precedence of an explicit request value (even `null`) over the preferred params and the launch default; the OpenAI endpoints. As in Python, an omitted `max_new_tokens` with no preferred params (the schema default of 128) is no longer context-checked either.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A: no model numerics change. The only requests that behave differently are the ones the frontend used to reject with a 400 although the scheduler would have clamped them.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A for speed: one read of the `sampling_params` key(s) per `/generate` request, before the JSON decode that already walks the body.

Tests run (`rust/`, toolchain 1.92):

- `cargo test --locked -p sglang-server`: 368 passed. New or extended:
  - `defaulted_max_new_tokens_is_left_to_the_scheduler`: a defaulted cap as large as the whole window is neither rejected nor clamped, with and without `allow_auto_truncate`; an over-long prompt is still rejected.
  - `over_context_request_deregisters_unless_its_cap_is_defaulted`: end to end through `drive`, the same `max_new_tokens: 64` under a 4-token window is a 400 when the client sent it and reaches the scheduler unchanged when it is defaulted.
  - `generate_marks_each_max_new_tokens_the_client_omits` (HTTP): omitted, other keys only, no preferred params, explicit, explicit `null`, a per-item list, and one object broadcast to a batch.
  - `omitted_max_new_tokens_takes_the_launch_default` and the gRPC `preferred_sampling_params_fill_unset_fields` / `unset_protobuf_sampling_fields_take_schema_defaults` now also assert the defaulted flag.
  - With the gate in `check_total_tokens` and the HTTP marking disabled, the three new tests fail.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Not run here: a live server (unit tests only). A client-sent value and the input-alone check keep their existing end-to-end coverage.

title: [Fix] constrained: Do not cache grammar poll timeouts as invalid grammars
author: shijie-lyu
body:
## Motivation

When a grammar request waits past `SGLANG_GRAMMAR_MAX_POLL_ITERATIONS`, `GrammarManager.get_ready_grammar_requests` caches `InvalidGrammarObject("Grammar preprocessing timed out")` for that key. `BaseGrammarBackend.get_cached_or_future_value` treats any cached object as a hit, so every later request with the same schema is aborted with `Failed to compile json grammar: Grammar preprocessing timed out` until `/flush_cache` (which needs an idle server) or a restart.

A timeout is not a property of the schema: the poll counter also runs while the compile waits in the shared executor queue, so one burst of load can permanently break a JSON schema or tool definition. This matches the symptom described in #17608, where `/flush_cache` was the workaround.

## Modifications

- Drop the cache write on the timeout path (`grammar_manager.py`). The request is still cancelled and aborted with the same message. Grammars the backend reports invalid are still cached.
- Rank consistency: the removed write ran after the TP all-gather and PP sync of ready/failed indexes, so the cache stays identical on every rank. The PD decode path calls the same `get_ready_grammar_requests`.

**Trade-off.** `Future.cancel()` cannot stop a compile that is already running.
- With xgrammar (default), the compiler cache shares an in-flight compile of the same schema and keeps its result (checked on xgrammar 0.2.7: 4 threads compiling one slow schema cost ~1 compile of CPU vs ~4x for 4 different schemas), so a retry after the compile finishes is cached normally.
- With llguidance, outlines, or framed reasoner grammars, a schema whose compile itself takes longer than the timeout (>= 50 s by default) is now recompiled on every request and can occupy the shared grammar executor under sustained traffic.
- The old negative entry did not bound this either: there is no in-flight dedup, so every request that arrived before the first timeout already submitted its own compile, and any whitespace change produces a new key.
- Per-key in-flight dedup would bound it; I'd do that as a follow-up. Caching the late result from a done-callback is not safe: it would write the cache at different times on different ranks and desync `grammar_queue` indexes.

Not changed here (follow-ups): the timeout abort still returns HTTP 400 (related to #45132); the `except Exception` branch on the ready path still caches unexpected exceptions as invalid.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A, control path only.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A.

## Testing

- `test/registered/unit/constrained/test_grammar_manager.py`: new `test_timeout_does_not_poison_cache` (real `BaseGrammarBackend` cache, executor returning never-completing futures). It fails on the pre-change code and passes after. `test_timeout_aborts_req` drops the assertion that pinned the timeout caching; `test_invalid_grammar_aborts_req` now asserts a real invalid result is still cached (a mutant that stops caching invalid grammars fails it).
- `python -m pytest test/registered/unit/constrained/`: 150 passed (CPU).
- `pre-commit` passes.

title: [CI] [AMD] miles: Fix the ROCm 10 nightly suites that never finish
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
## What

The 2-GPU and 4-GPU jobs of the miles ROCm 10 MI35X nightly have failed every night since Oct 14 and Oct 6, without reporting most of their tests. This PR changes how the workflow schedules those suites. No test code changes.

## Why

**2-GPU suite: the runner goes down.** Every night since Oct 14 the `linux-mi35x-gpu-2` runner stops about 2 minutes into `test_glm5_2_744b_a40b_5layer_ci.py`, and the job ends with "The self-hosted runner lost communication with the server" ([Oct 20](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39467587161/job/118782916394), [Oct 19](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39295602704)). The test moved from the 4-GPU suite to the 2-GPU suite in radixark/miles#4053 (merged Oct 13). Before that, it ran on the 8-GPU pool and passed in 729 s ([Oct 12](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38285672256)). The suite now runs on `linux-mi35x-gpu-8`, the same pool the 4-GPU suite already uses.

**4-GPU suite: the step timeout cuts it off.** The suite has 30 tests with ~22,000 s of estimated time, about 3.5 h of real time on MI355X, and the step timeout is 180 min. Every night since Oct 6 the step has timed out partway through ([Oct 20](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39467587161/job/118782916392): stopped at test 22 of 30). The suite is now split into two partitions with `run_suite.py --auto-partition-id/--auto-partition-size`, the same split radixark/miles uses for `stage-c-4-gpu-mi350` in its own ROCm PR CI. Each half is ~11,000 s estimated.

**MI30X.** The GLM-5.2 skip (its kernel needs more LDS than gfx942 has) moves along with the test from the 4-GPU entry to the 2-GPU entry. On MI300 the test now fails in the 2-GPU job ([Oct 19](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39325011628)).

## Notes for the reviewer

- On MI35X this takes four 8-GPU runners per night instead of two 8-GPU runners and one 2-GPU runner.
- Partitioning is deterministic (LPT on `est_time`, ties broken by filename), so the two jobs agree on the split without coordinating.
- `test_qwen3_4B_variable_gbs.py` fails with `HIPBLASLT Error: 6` in TransformerEngine. That is a real failure, and this PR leaves it alone.

## Test plan

Dispatched the MI35X workflow on this branch: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39542005262. All four jobs finished inside the step timeout and reported every test:

| Job | Runner | Job time | Tests |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2-GPU | `linux-mi35x-gpu-8` | 131 min | 33/33 passed, including GLM-5.2 5-layer (829 s) |
| 4-GPU part 1/2 | `linux-mi35x-gpu-8` | 100 min | 14/15 passed |
| 4-GPU part 2/2 | `linux-mi35x-gpu-8` | 148 min | 14/15 passed |
| 8-GPU | `linux-mi35x-gpu-8` | 160 min | 19/19 passed |

The two 4-GPU failures are test failures, not scheduling:
- `test_nospec_nor3_bf16_sgl_dpattn2x2_meg_tp2pp2.py`: the CI log-prob check failed on a difference of 3e-8 (`-0.4064931571` vs `-0.4064931273`). It passed on Oct 20.
- `test_inkling_small_6layer_lora_ci.py`: one SGLang engine failed to start because `cargo --version --verbose` returned non-zero while it was loading the Inkling Rust image processor. The rollout then got 503s until the 1800 s file timeout. It passed in 473 s on Oct 20, so this looks intermittent. The 30 min timeout is part of part 2/2's 148 min.

The MI30X change was not dispatched; it only moves an existing skip entry.

title: [Fix] attention: Restore block pointers on Triton 3.9 for FLA kernels
author: akhilg-nv
body:
[by Claude Code]

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Fixes #45426.

The `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-cu134-*` images from 2026-10-20 ship torch `2.15.0.dev20261005+cu134`, which pins **Triton `3.9.0+gitaad2a60d`**. That Triton includes triton-lang/triton#10833, which removed block pointers: `tl.make_block_ptr` and `tl.advance` now raise `NotImplementedError` at compile time. The vendored FLA kernels (GDN / KDA: Qwen3.5, Qwen3-Next, Kimi linear attention) use block pointers about 200 times, so these models fail at their first kernel compile. Qwen3.5 dies at prefill CUDA-graph capture in `l2norm_fwd_kernel`.

The MiniMax sparse attention kernels had the same problem, plus a Triton 3.9 autotune-key error. #46135 has since ported them off block pointers and fixed the key on main, so this PR now covers only FLA.

The Triton 3.8.0 release still has block pointers (lowered in its Python frontend to plain pointer loads), so the regular images (torch 2.14.1 + Triton 3.8.0) and Triton 3.7.1 are unaffected.

As in #40805, this is a guarded compatibility shim with a TODO, not a port.

## Modifications

- New `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/triton_block_ptr_compat.py`. It does something only when `triton.language` has no `advance` (the Triton build removed block pointers). It then defines `tl.make_block_ptr` / `tl.advance` on top of a small Triton aggregate, and wraps `tl.load` / `tl.store` so they accept `boundary_check` and `padding_option` for it. The lowering follows Triton 3.8.0's own frontend implementation: int64 shape / strides / offsets, per-dimension coordinates broadcast to the block, a bounds mask only on the checked dimensions, and `padding_option` mapped to `other`. On Triton builds that still have block pointers the module does nothing, so behaviour there is unchanged.
- The shim is imported from `fla/utils.py` and `fla/fused_norm_gate.py`. Every module that uses block pointers (the FLA kernels, including the XPU copies) imports one of them.
- TODO: drop the shim once the kernels are ported off block pointers, as upstream FLA did in fla-org/flash-linear-attention#1062.

Alternatives considered:
- Port every call site to plain pointers. Upstream FLA did this in fla-org/flash-linear-attention#1062, a diff of +6088/-5512 lines over 88 files.
- Use tensor descriptors. They can't express the transposed and strided 1-D blocks these kernels load, and they need 16-byte alignment.

## Accuracy Tests

These runs predate the merge of #46135. The MiniMax sparse tests below exercised the shim on MiniMax's old block-pointer kernels, which main no longer has.

**Unit tests**: FLA and MiniMax sparse kernel tests on one B300, run in the `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` image's tree (ab580b2e) with this patch applied. Each Triton version used a fresh Triton cache. The 3.7.1 and 3.9 builds were put on `PYTHONPATH`, ahead of the image's own Triton 3.8.0.

| Triton | Shim | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 3.7.1 (PyPI) | inactive | 143 passed, 2 skipped |
| 3.8.0 (image) | inactive | 142 passed, 2 failed\*, 2 skipped |
| 3.9.0+gitaad2a60d (torch nightly pin) | active | 142 passed, 2 failed\*, 2 skipped |

\* The same two `TestKDAVerifyDecodeParity` bit-exactness checks fail on Triton 3.8.0 **without** this patch and pass on 3.7.1. The failure is pre-existing and not related to this change.

Files: `test_chunk_gated_delta_rule.py`, `test_kda_kernels.py`, `test_gdn_prefill_layout.py`, `test_fused_norm_gate_strided.py`, `test_kda_gate_beta_cumsum.py`, `test_kda_track_state.py`, `test_minimax_sparse_decode_paged_tile.py`, `test_minimax_decode_topk_page_table.py`.

MiniMax sparse tests that sit at their pre-#45112 path in that tree (`test_flash_with_topk_idx.py`, `test_sparse_gqa.py`; these cover the decode kernels, including the ones that use `tl.advance`): 74 passed on Triton 3.9 + shim and on Triton 3.8.0. `test_minimax_sparse_fp8_attn_gemm.py`, taken from main: 10 passed on Triton 3.9 + shim and on Triton 3.8.0.

The same test list also ran natively in the `nightly-cu134-20261020-306ccf6` image (torch 2.15 + Triton 3.9) on GB200. That run found that zero-padded fp8 loads failed to compile (`cannot cast int32 to fp8e4nv`); the second commit fixes it and is what the `test_minimax_sparse_fp8_attn_gemm.py` result above covers. Everything else passed: 220 tests.

**Generated code**: I compiled test kernels to TTIR on a CPU-only machine with fresh caches. They cover 1-D, 2-D and 3-D blocks, transposed `order`, strided 1-D blocks, `padding_option="zero"`, partial `boundary_check`, and `tl.advance` inside a loop. Triton 3.9 + this shim emits the same TTIR as Triton 3.8.0's own block-pointer lowering. The one difference is the lowering of an fp16-to-bf16 `.to()` cast that isn't on a block-pointer path.

**End to end**: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (hybrid GDN) on one GB200, TP1, `--reasoning-parser qwen3`. sgl-eval GSM8K, n=200, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, max_tokens 16384, top_k 20 from the model's generation config.

| Image | Triton | This PR | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `nightly-cu134-20261020-306ccf6` | 3.9.0+gitaad2a60d | no | server dies at the first prefill: `NotImplementedError: Block pointers have been removed` (#45426) |
| `nightly-cu134-20261020-306ccf6` | 3.9.0+gitaad2a60d | yes | 80.5% |
| `dev-cu13` | 3.8.0 | no | 82.0% |

The 1.5-point gap is within sampling noise; the standard error at n=200 is about 2.8 points.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

With Triton 3.8.0 or older the shim is inactive and no kernel changes. With Triton 3.9 the shim produces the same IR as Triton 3.8.0's lowering of these block pointers, so I don't expect a speed change against 3.8.0. Not benchmarked.

## Checklist
