title: [Fix] rust-server: Answer health probes a busy scheduler skipped on the response ring
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

In Rust frontend mode (`SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1`) a scheduler that is busy with a long prefill fails `/health_generate` even though it is alive, so a router in front of it marks a healthy engine unhealthy.

A busy scheduler skips health probes and acknowledges them after its next step. That acknowledgement is sent to the zmq tokenizer socket, which nothing reads in Rust mode:

- the Rust probe counts only decode-batch frames as scheduler activity, so it sees nothing until the prefill finishes and the probe times out;
- every skipped probe also queues one message on the unread socket, which is unbounded (`SNDHWM 0`).

## Modifications

- In Rust mode the scheduler pushes the acknowledgement onto the Rust response ring as a new bodiless frame, `DISPATCH_TAG_HEALTH_ACK` (`Server.push_health_ack` / `RustServer.push_health_ack`).
- The Rust dispatcher counts that frame as scheduler activity, the same way the Python `TokenizerManager` counts `HealthCheckOutput`.
- Rust probes share one heartbeat, so one acknowledgement per step answers every probe skipped so far; the scheduler clears its pending-probe queue instead of answering them one per step. A skipped probe now passes within one scheduler step. A single step longer than the client timeout still fails, by design.
- The Python frontend path is unchanged.
- Tests: `skipped_probe_passes_on_health_ack_and_cleans_up` replaces `healthy_probe_uses_shared_activity_and_cleans_up` in `handle.rs` and drives the probe through a real `Dispatcher` with an acknowledgement frame instead of bumping the counter by hand; `test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_health_check_signal.py` pins the scheduler side for both modes (the Rust-mode case fails on `main`).

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no model-output path changes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: the new frame is one byte per scheduler step, and only while a probe is pending.

Run locally on this branch:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --locked -p sglang-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked -p sglang-server` (364 passed).
- `pytest test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_health_check_signal.py` (2 passed; the Rust-mode case fails on `main` with `push_health_ack` never called).
- pre-commit hooks for the touched files (isort, ruff, ruff-format, codespell, the registered-test checks).

Not run here: a real-server reproduction with a long chunked prefill while `/health_generate` is probed under a short client timeout.

title: [Fix] [AMD] MoE: Preserve CT FP8 Triton layout and reduction dimensions
author: lunarwhite
body:
## Motivation

With `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` and an explicit Triton MoE runner, compressed-tensors CHANNEL FP8 layers receive AITER-shuffled weights and lose 128 reduction elements in the non-block FP8 kernel (1024 → 896 in the regression). Both cause incorrect outputs.

## Modifications

- Shuffle CT CHANNEL FP8 weights only for an actual AITER runner.
- Match the non-block FP8 kernel's padding calculation to its existing caller when AITER is enabled.
- Add an AMD CI-registered runtime quantization test under `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/`, covering checkpoint loading, postprocessing, and numerical Triton/AITER MoE comparisons with 1- and 33-token inputs.

Related: [#41636](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41636) addresses the shuffle mechanism in `Fp8MoEMethod` block-FP8; this PR fixes the separate compressed-tensors CHANNEL path and the non-block kernel dimension calculation.

## Accuracy Tests

Tested on MI355X (gfx950), Python 3.10.12, PyTorch `2.9.1+rocm7.2.0.git7e1940d4`, HIP `7.2.26015-fc0010cf6a`, using the official image:

```
lmsysorg/sglang-rocm@sha256:8cb29fc407c2e46bdb1866c5edb91f109ac1acbbcb6905089beaa6c79b0813a2
```

Base: `9db58ab547516435b544ae050dd6c2f91b52bcf3`  
Head: `7d7d8b79eec61eda1884c54311b2580bd6159cff`

Layer controls use identical seeded weights, routing and test source, `SGLANG_MOE_PADDING=0`, isolated processes/caches, and verified import paths/hashes.

| Variant | Explicit Triton, 1 / 33 tokens | AITER, 1 / 33 tokens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base, AITER disabled | pass / pass | not run |
| Base, AITER enabled | fail / fail | pass / pass |
| Only shuffle guard | fail / fail (cosine 0.7757 / 0.8207) | pass / pass |
| Only kernel padding fix | fail / fail | pass / pass |
| Both fixes | pass / pass | pass / pass |

Both final test methods pass without errors/skips. The independent reference uses dequantized checkpoint weights and identical routing; fixed thresholds are cosine > 0.99 and relative L2 < 0.1. Controls fail numerically, establishing that both fixes are required.

A separate Quark per-tensor dynamic regression covers another shared-kernel consumer: base/AITER off passes, base/AITER on fails both numerical subtests, and patched/AITER on passes (no errors/skips).

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the GPU-tested revisions on MI35x</summary>

Run inside the image above, from outside the source tree:

```bash
git clone --branch lunarwhite/ct-fp8-runner-layout https://github.com/lunarwhite/sglang.git /tmp/ct-sglang
git -C /tmp/ct-sglang checkout --detach 7d7d8b79eec61eda1884c54311b2580bd6159cff
cd /tmp
export SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_MOE_PADDING=0 SGLANG_TEST_MAX_RETRY=0
export SGLANG_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/ct-sglang-head-cache
PYTHONPATH=/tmp/ct-sglang/python python /tmp/ct-sglang/test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_fp8_moe_layout.py
```

To reproduce the controls with the same test file (each command is a separate process):

```bash
git -C /tmp/ct-sglang worktree add --detach /tmp/ct-base 9db58ab547516435b544ae050dd6c2f91b52bcf3
git -C /tmp/ct-sglang worktree add --detach /tmp/ct-kernel-only 9db58ab547516435b544ae050dd6c2f91b52bcf3
git -C /tmp/ct-kernel-only restore --source=7d7d8b79eec61eda1884c54311b2580bd6159cff -- python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py
TEST_FILE=/tmp/ct-sglang/test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_fp8_moe_layout.py
# Pass: AITER-disabled control, one test method.
SGLANG_USE_AITER=0 SGLANG_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/ct-control-cache PYTHONPATH=/tmp/ct-base/python python "$TEST_FILE" TestCompressedTensorsFp8MoELayout.test_explicit_triton
# Expected numerical failure in Triton, with AITER passing:
SGLANG_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/ct-base-cache PYTHONPATH=/tmp/ct-base/python python "$TEST_FILE"
SGLANG_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/ct-kernel-cache PYTHONPATH=/tmp/ct-kernel-only/python python "$TEST_FILE"
```

</details>

The separate AITER-disabled + padding-enabled configuration is outside this validation.

### Real-checkpoint validation

`RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8-dynamic`, revision `10a439027a4fd228adc03a7bffb1aac10a179938`, was evaluated on the same MI355X image and base/head sources. All four arms observed actual CT CHANNEL execution in all 48 layers and verified the loaded source hashes. TP1, eager execution, AITER enabled, padding disabled; 200 GSM8K test examples, five demonstrations from the train split, greedy decoding, maximum 512 generated tokens.

| Configuration | Correct / 200 |
| --- | --- |
| Base, AITER runner | 180 |
| Base, AITER runner repeat | 179 |
| Base, explicit Triton runner | 0 |
| Patched, explicit Triton runner | 181 |

All 800 predictions were independently rescored and prompt/dataset hashes verified. Every base Triton output hit the 512-token cap. This is a configuration-specific sanity check, not full-dataset accuracy or statistical equivalence; default AITER is the known-good reference.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

A separate fixed-output probe (four prompts, 64 tokens each, three timed repeats after warmup) measured median output rates of 103.88 tok/s for base Triton and 104.75 tok/s for patched Triton; AITER reference runs measured 99.71 and 103.64 tok/s. This bounded probe is not a production throughput or speedup claim.

title: [Fix] spec: Take post-verify KV move targets from the verify window
author: hnyls2002
body:
- `move_accept_tokens_to_target_kvcache` takes each request's move targets from the front of its verify window in `out_cache_loc`, instead of rereading `req_to_token` after the verify forward
- The reread raced with the overlap scheduler: the target verify publishes its shared-read-done event inside the graph replay, before the move runs, so a request that finished by EOS or a stop condition in the previous step can have its row handed to a new request while the move is still queued. The move then copied KV into the new owner's slots, including radix-cached prefix slots, and later hits on that prefix read the corrupted KV
- Affects NGRAM and UNO tree verify (`--speculative-eagle-topk > 1`) on CUDA; EAGLE tree verify calls the same function but keeps the whole-forward barrier
- Add `test/registered/unit/spec/test_move_accept_tokens_targets.py`: rewrites the rows after the verify window is built and checks the move targets and sources for chain and tree layouts

No behavior change when no row is reused: the targets equal the rows' entries at verify time.

Verification with Qwen3-8B, NGRAM, FA3, page size 1, one H200 per server. A 4000-token prefix is cached, then for 120 s short requests that stop early run next to requests that reuse the prefix. Afterwards, bs=1 prefill logprobs over the cached prefix are compared with a server using the whole-forward barrier (`SGLANG_FORCE_COARSE_WAR_BARRIER=1`); both servers match bitwise before the load.

| server | probes with different logprobs (of 8) | greedy outputs matching (of 4) |
|---|---|---|
| main | 8 | 1 |
| this PR | 0 | 4 |

title: [Fix] data_parallel_controller: Fix active ranks update and simplify round-robin dispatch
author: minhdang26403
body:
## Motivation

This PR resolves a state desynchronization issue in `DataParallelController` and simplifies the round-robin request dispatch path:

1. **Stale Worker Cache in `update_active_ranks`:** In `DataParallelController.update_active_ranks`, the non-elastic branch (`get_exec().moe.elastic_ep_backend is None`) updated `self.status` directly via `list(ranks.status)` without masking against `self.dp_active` or calling `self._refresh_active_workers()`. As a result, `self._active_workers` and `self._active_count_cache` remained stale after rank liveness changes, and unprovisioned expansion slots (`dp_active == False`) could be marked active in `self.status` if `ranks.status` contained trailing `True` values.
2. **Redundant Iteration in `round_robin_scheduler`:** To work around stale `_active_workers` entries, `round_robin_scheduler` previously ran a defensive `while attempts < len(active)` loop re-checking `if self.status[slot]:` on each dispatch. Because `DataParallelController` runs on a single-threaded event loop and `_active_workers` represents the exact filtered intersection of provisioned (`dp_active`) and healthy (`status`) ranks, every entry in `_active_workers` is guaranteed routable once `_refresh_active_workers()` is consistently invoked.

By unifying `update_active_ranks` to always mask with `self.dp_active` and invoke `_refresh_active_workers()`, we enforce the `_active_workers` invariant across all paths and streamline `round_robin_scheduler` into a direct $O(1)$ lookup.

## Modifications

- **`python/sglang/srt/managers/data_parallel_controller.py`:**
  - Unified `update_active_ranks`: removed branching divergence between elastic and non-elastic paths, consistently intersected `ranks.status[i]` with `self.dp_active[i]`, and unconditionally invoked `self._refresh_active_workers()`.
  - Simplified `round_robin_scheduler`: removed the redundant `while attempts < len(active)` loop and inner `self.status[slot]` check in favor of direct $O(1)$ slot indexing (`active[self.round_robin_counter % len(active)]`).
- **`test/registered/unit/managers/test_data_parallel_controller.py`:**
  - Updated `_make_controller` to support `max_dp_size` and initialize `dp_active`, `status`, and `_active_count_cache`.
  - Updated `TestRoundRobinScheduler.test_skips_inactive_workers` and `TestStatusAwarenessInconsistency` docstrings to reflect `_active_workers` routing, and added `test_raises_when_no_active_workers`.
  - Added `TestUpdateActiveRanks` to verify `_active_workers` cache refresh, unprovisioned slot masking, and length-mismatch handling.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — Control-plane request routing and worker liveness tracking only; no changes to model forward passes or numerical kernels. Verified with unit tests:
```bash
pytest test/registered/unit/managers/test_data_parallel_controller.py
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A — Removes a redundant Python loop on the control-plane round_robin_scheduler dispatch path.

title: [Fix] sgl-router: Wait for the detached PD prefill in routing tests
author: ShangmingCai
body:
## Motivation

Four sgl-router proxy tests fail intermittently. In a loaded `cargo test --release --test proxy` run, about 2 in 10 runs fail on main, always the same way:

```
left:  [false, false, false, true]
right: [false, true, false, true]
```

Decode got the request, but the chosen prefill mock hadn't recorded a body yet. In PD mode the router sends prefill as a detached task, and `forward_pd` returns as soon as decode responds. The tests read the prefill mock's `last_body` right after the response, so under load the spawned prefill hasn't reached the mock yet. Routing is correct; the tests check too early.

Affected tests:
- `bucket_routing::decode_bucket_mismatch_falls_back_to_another_version_group` (#41613)
- `bucket_routing::version_group_capacity_fallback_preserves_decode_limits` (#41613)
- `chat_routing::reorg::full_decode_group_falls_back_to_another_version_group` (#41613)
- `chat_routing::reorg::default_pd_groups_apply_configured_inflight_admission` (#40766)

## Modifications

Before checking the dispatch pattern, wait for the expected prefill worker to receive its body. Each file reuses its existing pattern:
- `bucket_routing.rs`: the existing `wait_for_prefill` helper (2s timeout)
- `reorg.rs`: the inline `timeout(TEST_TIMEOUT, …)` loop its other PD tests already use

The assertions themselves are unchanged. If prefill went to the wrong worker, the wait times out and the test still fails.

Test-only change; no router code changes.

## Verification

Local runs of `cargo test --locked --release -p sgl-router --test proxy`, full suite with parallel tests:

| tree | runs | runs with a failure in these 4 tests |
|---|---|---|
| main (before) | 25 | 6 |
| #41613 commit (`41cbe65de05`) | 20 | 5 |
| this PR | 20 | 0 |

`cargo +nightly fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` pass.

Out of scope: one of the 20 runs on this PR hit an unrelated timing flake, `chat_routing::janitor_expiry_returns_504_stale_request_expired`, which races a 2s hanging mock against the stale-request janitor. It's a separate test with a different cause, not a PD prefill check.

title: [Fix] distributed: Prevent unavailable PyNccl enablement
author: rumitdesai
body:
## Motivation

`PyNcclCommunicator` tracks two related states:

- `available` indicates whether its NCCL communication resources are available.
- `disabled` indicates whether the communicator is currently allowed to handle collectives.

An available communicator may be temporarily enabled during device-graph capture and disabled afterward. An unavailable communicator, however, must always remain disabled.

Before this change, `change_state(enable=True)` could produce the invalid state `available=False, disabled=False`. Subsequent collectives could then enter a partially initialized PyNccl path and access resources that were never created.

This change makes availability a hard prerequisite for enablement, preventing the invalid state while preserving existing behavior for available communicators.

During device-graph capture, an unavailable `PyNcclCommunicator` could be temporarily enabled by calling `change_state(enable=True)`.

When NCCL initialization is unavailable, the communicator is only partially initialized and has `available=False`. Enabling it set `disabled=False`, causing subsequent collectives to enter the PyNccl path and access attributes that were never initialized.

An unavailable communicator must always remain disabled.

## Modifications

- Reject explicit attempts to enable an unavailable `PyNcclCommunicator` with a descriptive `RuntimeError`.
- Centralize PyNccl capability checks in `GroupCoordinator`:
  - Return the communicator only when it initialized successfully.
  - Provide a fail-fast helper for operations that require PyNccl.
- Update graph capture and collective-selection paths to use the centralized availability check.
- Preserve existing alternate collective paths when PyNccl is not selected.
- Make PyNccl-required operations fail clearly when the communicator is unavailable.
- Audit direct PyNccl consumers, including bootstrap, symmetric-memory, DSA broadcast, MiniMax indexer, and page-interleave paths.
- Add CPU-only regression coverage for:
  - Explicit enablement of an unavailable communicator.
  - Available communicator enablement and state restoration.
  - Exception-path restoration.
  - `GroupCoordinator` availability semantics.
  - Graph capture skipping unavailable PyNccl.
  - Existing pure-eager collective routing.

## Tests


```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/distributed/test_pynccl.py
# 6 passed

python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/distributed/
# 95 passed, 20 subtests passed
```

Two-GPU PyNccl CUDA-graph coverage:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 \
SGLANG_ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM=0 \
NCCL_RAS_ENABLE=0 \
python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/mock_model/test_e2e_tp.py::TestE2ETensorParallel::test_tp_lm_head_all_to_all_cuda_graph
# Passed
```

Additional two-GPU coverage:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 NCCL_RAS_ENABLE=0 \
python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dsa_layer_split_broadcast.py

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 NCCL_RAS_ENABLE=0 \
python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_page_interleave_shard.py

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 \
SGLANG_ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM=0 \
NCCL_RAS_ENABLE=0 \
python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/mock_model/test_e2e_tp.py::TestE2ETensorParallel::test_tp_no_canary_violation
```

All passed.

Pre-commit checks also passed for all modified files.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

title: [Test] [AMD] deepseek-v4.1: Fix the HIP breakable-graph unit tests for the default prefill context limit and the DSpark draft ring
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
## What
Test-only fix for the two unit tests that keep `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` red on main.

## Why
Both partitions fail on every scheduled run since Oct 19, e.g. [partition 0](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39421857090/job/118624623384) and [partition 1](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39421857090/job/118624623363).

- `test_dsv41_bcg_hip.py`: `AssertionError: 2 != 1` on the captured page-table width. Since #43733 the HIP backend captures and replays the DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill graph at `prefill_cuda_graph_default_max_seq_len` (16K) when no `max_seq_len` is configured, instead of the bucket's own length. The page table is that limit clamped to the `req_to_token` width (512 in the fixture), so 2 pages, not 1.
- `test_dsv4_hip_bcg_metadata.py`: `AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'swa_req_ring_size'`. Since #44673, `get_dspark_swa_page_indices` reads `swa_req_ring_size` and `swa_valid_from` from the KV pool, and the test's mock pool doesn't have them.

## Fix
- `test_dsv41_bcg_hip.py`: take the limit from `backend._graph_metadata_max_seq_len(capture_batch)`, which is what capture and replay actually use. Build the eager reference at that limit and expect `ceil(min(limit, req_to_token width) / page_size)` columns. This also turns on the existing limit branch (eager rebuild at the limit, overflow raises), which had no caller before.
- `test_dsv4_hip_bcg_metadata.py`: add `swa_req_ring_size=None` and `swa_valid_from=None` to the mock pool. These match the real pool's paged-SWA defaults.

No library code changes.

## Test plan
- [x] `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` on rocm10 via dispatch: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39541960302. Both partitions passed (31/31 and 32/32). `test_dsv41_bcg_hip.py` ran 1 test and `test_dsv4_hip_bcg_metadata.py` ran 19 tests, all OK.

title: [Fix] [CPU] memory: budget overestimation caused by filtering empty NUMA nodes
author: xinguozhu-2026
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.

Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

In #40066, empty CPU lists were filtered out via `if cpus` in `get_cpu_ids_by_node()`. However, after per-rank thread/NUMA core binding (e.g., running with `TP=6`), `get_cpu_ids_by_node()` only returns the CPUs within the current rank's bound NUMA node, reducing `n_numa_node` from the total number of NUMA nodes (e.g., 6) to `1`.

Meanwhile, `get_free_cpu_memory()` queries the **system-wide (or cgroup-constrained) available memory** via `psutil.virtual_memory().available` and `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.*`, rather than the available memory of the bound NUMA node. Dividing the global free memory by `n_numa_node = 1` instead of total NUMA nodes significantly overestimates the per-rank KV cache memory budget, while actual memory allocation remains strictly restricted by NUMA binding, leading to OOM errors (e.g., when running Grok-2 with TP=6).

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
Cache get_cpu_ids_by_node results to ensure consistent NUMA node detection across binders.

title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] docker: Build sgl-deep-gemm 0.2.3 for cu134 to match the sglang pin
author: nvrohanv
body:
## Motivation

`python/pyproject.toml` pins `sgl-deep-gemm==0.2.3`, but `docker/Dockerfile.cu134` builds DeepGEMM `v0.2.1.post1` and installs it with the pin removed. So the `nightly-cu134-*` images ship `sgl-deep-gemm 0.2.1.post1`.

Muse Spark's MegaMoE path (`muse_spark_megamoe.py`, `forward_megamoe`) passes `post_expert_norm*` arguments that only exist in sgl-deep-gemm 0.2.3+. With `--enable-megamoe-for-layernorm-sp`, the server fails at the first prefill CUDA-graph capture:

```
TypeError: bf16_mega_moe() got an unexpected keyword argument 'post_expert_norm'
```

Reproduce (no GPU needed):

```
docker run --rm lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-cu134-20261020-306ccf6 python3 -c "import importlib.metadata as m, inspect, deep_gemm; print(m.version('sgl-deep-gemm'), [r for r in m.requires('sglang') if 'deep-gemm' in r]); print('post_expert_norm' in inspect.signature(deep_gemm.bf16_mega_moe).parameters)"
# -> 0.2.1.post1+cu134 ['sgl-deep-gemm==0.2.3']
# -> False
```

## Modifications

- Set `DEEPGEMM_REF=v0.2.3` and `SGL_DEEP_GEMM_VERSION=0.2.3` in `docker/Dockerfile.cu134`, matching the pyproject pin and `docker/muse_spark/muse-spark.Dockerfile`, which already builds 0.2.3.
- Add a `check-dockerfile-wheel-pins` pre-commit hook (`scripts/lint/check_dockerfile_wheel_pins.py`). It fails if any Dockerfile under `docker/` sets `DEEPGEMM_REF`, `SGL_DEEP_GEMM_VERSION` or `SGL_DEEP_EP_VERSION` to a value other than the `python/pyproject.toml` pin. These wheels are installed with the pin stripped and `--no-deps`, so a mismatch is otherwise silent. Dockerfiles are found by these ARGs rather than by name, so a renamed or new CUDA Dockerfile stays covered, and the check fails if no Dockerfile sets them. On `main` it reports the current `v0.2.1.post1` mismatch.

title: [Fix] sgl-router: Bump rustls-webpki and webpki-roots for emSign advisories
author: ShangmingCai
body:
## Motivation

The router's tier-1 `cargo deny check` now fails on every PR that touches `sgl-router/` (e.g. [#45502](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45502), [job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39540580437/job/119065828194)). Three advisories published today hit our lockfile:

- [RUSTSEC-2026-0382](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0382): `rustls-webpki 0.103.15` may accept certificate paths through the distrusted emSign intermediates. Fixed in 0.103.16.
- [RUSTSEC-2026-0381](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0381): `webpki-roots 1.0.9` and `0.26.11` bundle the `emSign ECC Root CA - G3` root. Fixed in 1.0.10.

Main's own router runs skip tier-1 when no router files change, which is why main still looks green.

## Modifications

- `sgl-router/Cargo.lock`: `rustls-webpki` 0.103.15 → 0.103.16, `webpki-roots` 1.0.9 → 1.0.10 (`cargo update --precise`). No other lockfile changes.
- `sgl-router/deny.toml`: ignore RUSTSEC-2026-0381, with a reason, for `webpki-roots 0.26.11` only. `ureq 2` (via `fastokens` ← `dynamo-tokenizers`) pins it. 0.26.11 is a shim that re-exports `webpki-roots 1.x`, which is now the fixed 1.0.10, and it bundles no roots of its own. Drop the ignore once `ureq 2` leaves the tree.

## Verification

In `sgl-router/` on main + this PR, with cargo-deny 0.19.6 (the CI version):

- `cargo deny check licenses bans sources advisories`: `advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok`
- `cargo metadata --locked` ok
- `cargo check --locked --all-targets` ok

Only sgl-router runs cargo deny in CI; `rust/Cargo.lock` is not checked and is left as is.

title: [Fix] [AMD] attention: Pass the layer softcap to aiter unified-attention decode
author: siliangchen-amd
body:
## Motivation

`AiterAttnBackend.forward_decode` calls aiter's `unified_attention` with `softcap=0`, so a model with an attention logit softcap loses it on every decode step that runs unified attention (`SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1`, or the hybrid SWA pool). The extend paths already pass `layer.logit_cap`, so prefill and decode disagree. Gemma 2 has an attention softcap of 50; on Gemma 2 27B, GSM8K drops from 0.878 on triton to 0.213.

## Modifications

- Pass `softcap=layer.logit_cap` in the decode call. Layers without a softcap have `logit_cap = 0.0`, the value the call passed before.
- `test_decode_applies_the_layer_softcap` checks that the decode call passes the layer's softcap. It fails on main.

## Accuracy Tests

1x MI325X (gfx942), ROCm 7.2.2, main at `1c2f424` against this PR, TP 1, `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1 --attention-backend aiter --disable-cuda-graph --context-length 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.85`. CUDA graphs are off because on this path at page size 1, main's graph decode reads a stale page table (#34833). With #34833 applied and graphs on, the results match (Gemma 2 27B: 0.240 → 0.878). GSM8K is `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k` (8-shot, 512 new tokens, 1319 questions); passkey is 5 keys at 8128 tokens.

| model | GSM8K, main → PR | passkey, main → PR | GSM8K, triton |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gemma 2 27B it | 0.213 → 0.879 | 4/5 → 5/5 | 0.878 |
| Gemma 2 9B it | 0.841 → 0.848 | 5/5 → 5/5 | 0.849 |
| Gemma 2 2B it | 0.487 → 0.487 | 5/5 → 5/5 | 0.490 |
| Gemma 3 12B it (no attention softcap) | 0.901 → 0.903 | 15/15 → 15/15 | |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] DeepSeek-v4.1: scatter the replay tail before the prefill CP gather with DSpark
author: SAXEM1997
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on CUDA/SM90 supports prefill context parallelism
(`--enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave`) and decoder SWA bounded replay
(`--enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay`), and each works on its own. Enabling both
together with DSpark aborts the first large prefill:

```text
RuntimeError: Interleave CP gather received an unexpected local token count:
  rank=3, got=16, expected_at_least=4096, total=32768, cp_size=8
    .../srt/layers/cp/interleave.py:288 in _gather_interleaved_tensor
    .../srt/layers/cp/utils.py:246 in cp_gather_after_forward
    .../srt/model_executor/runner/eager_runner.py:405 in _execute_extend_cp
    .../srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py:650 in _forward_prefill
```

With replay, the late layers run over each request's 128-token SWA tail; after
interleave sharding a rank owns 16 of those rows. `DeepseekV4Model.forward` puts
the tail rows back into the rank's full layout only when `not capture_dspark`.
With DSpark (`capture_dspark=True`) the model returns the 16 tail rows (and
tail-only aux tensors), `exit_late_layer_tail` has already restored the full-batch
CP metadata, and `_execute_extend_cp` then gathers with the full layout
(`32768 / 8 = 4096` expected rows per rank).

On CUDA, `deepseek_v4_hook.py` does not reject this combination at startup: its
incompatible list covers the prefill CUDA graph and DP attention, not prefill CP,
so a `DP=1 + CP=8` configuration passes the check and crashes at the first large
prefill. With this fix the combination is supported for **eager prefill**
(`--cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled`); the breakable prefill CUDA graph with
prefill CP is guarded separately by #44141. On HIP, `validate_deepseek_v4_cp`
still rejects replay + CP until #43465 lands.

**Note for maintainers:** #43465 already carries the same tail-scatter block for
HIP, and #44730 builds on it. This PR is intentionally CUDA-only — the author of
#43465 has no NVIDIA hardware to validate this configuration. If you prefer to
land #43465 first, that is fine: merge it (and #44730 if it lands) and we will
rebase this branch on top. The two hunks touch the same lines and collapse into
one `is_cp_active` condition; this PR introduces no second design.

## Modifications

```diff
+def _needs_cp_tail_scatter(tail, forward_batch) -> bool:
+    return _is_cuda and tail is not None and is_cp_active(forward_batch)
+
+def _finalize_dspark_aux(aux, tail, num_tokens, cuda_cp_tail):
+    packed = aux.finalize()  # [tokens, K * hidden]; the packer has no __iter__
+    if not cuda_cp_tail:
+        return packed
+    return _scatter_tail_rows(tail=tail, rows=packed, num_tokens=num_tokens, zero=True)
...
-        if tail is not None and not capture_dspark:
+        cuda_cp_tail = _needs_cp_tail_scatter(tail, forward_batch)
+        num_tokens = input_ids.shape[0]
+        if tail is not None and (not capture_dspark or cuda_cp_tail):
             ...
-            if cuda_cp_tail and capture_dspark:
-                dspark_aux_hidden_states = [
-                    _scatter_tail_rows(..., zero=True)
-                    for aux in dspark_aux_hidden_states
-                ]
         if capture_dspark:
-            return (hidden_states, pre_hc_head), dspark_aux_hidden_states.finalize()
+            return (hidden_states, pre_hc_head), _finalize_dspark_aux(
+                dspark_aux_hidden_states, tail, num_tokens, cuda_cp_tail
+            )
```

- Add `_needs_cp_tail_scatter()` so the CUDA/CP gate is explicit and unit-testable.
- `_scatter_tail_rows(..., zero=False)` gains a zero-filled variant. The rows
  outside the tail are never read (`_check_late_layer_tail_readers`; DSpark's
  draft reads tail rows only), but the CP gather moves the whole rank layout, so
  they are zero-filled only as a defensive measure (the all-gather buffer stays
  finite); the fill can be dropped to match #43465 if preferred.
- Scatter `hidden_states` and `pre_hc_head` back into the rank layout before the
  CP gather. The DSpark captures are finalized into one `[tokens, K * hidden]`
  buffer first and that buffer is scattered (`_finalize_dspark_aux`):
  `AuxHiddenStatePacker` has no `__iter__`, so a per-capture list comprehension
  raises `TypeError` here. Both tensors are gathered:
  `cp_gather_after_forward` gathers the `(hidden_states, pre_hc_head)` tuple, and
  `pre_hc_head` is only dropped from the logits kwargs after the gather when aux
  is not `None`.
- Scoped to `_is_cuda`: this is the CUDA branch of the hunk already present in
  #43465/#44730. If either lands first, the rebase is one line (drop `_is_cuda`
  and keep `is_cp_active`).
- No CLI or config change: replay under CP still requires the explicit flag (the
  automatic resolution keeps it off).
- Unit test covers `_scatter_tail_rows` (indexed and contiguous tails),
  `_needs_cp_tail_scatter` (CUDA/CP/tail truth table) and `_finalize_dspark_aux`
  (finalize-only and scattered). The forward path itself is covered by the H20 run.

## Accuracy Tests

8×H20-3e (SM90), sglang v0.5.22 + this patch. 5 fixed prompts, temperature 0,
2 runs each:

| Comparison | Result |
| --- | --- |
| CP + DSpark + replay vs non-CP production (replay on) | 5/5 token-identical |

The CP run had block verification off while the baseline had it on, so the 5/5
match covers more than the CP-only difference. The C2bv A/B shows block
verification changes cold TTFT by only +0.2–0.5%.

The new CPU unit tests pass 6/6 on a CPU-only v0.5.22 image with the same
helper/scatter code mounted.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Cold TTFT, unique random prefix per request (2 runs each, spread ≤0.03 s):

| Config | 128K | 256K | 512K |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| CP + DSpark, replay off | 5.405 s | 11.710 s | 28.664 s |
| CP + DSpark + replay (this patch) | **3.369 s** | **6.864 s** | **15.954 s** |
| Speedup | 1.60× | 1.71× | 1.80× |

Decode replay, 36 real sessions, 256 output tokens (3–4 of the 36 runs do not
complete in each config; throughput counts completed sessions):

| Config | c1 ITL p50 | c8 ITL p50 | c8 output throughput |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Non-CP production, replay on (single run) | 11.8 ms | 23.9 ms | 149.3 tok/s |
| CP + DSpark, replay off (single run) | 18.4 ms | 27.4 ms | 176.0 tok/s |
| CP + DSpark + replay (c8 median of 5; c1 from C2bv #1) | 18.4 ms | 27.9 ms | **241.4 tok/s** |

The c1 ITL increase comes from CP decode, not from this change: it is the same
18.4 ms with replay off. c8 ITL p90 is noisy on this workload (157–386 ms across
5 runs), so p50 and throughput are the stable metrics. The replay-off decode
baseline is a single run; treat the +37% as directional.

Repro command:

```bash
sglang serve --model-path <DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash> --tp 8 --ep 4 \
  --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave \
  --enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \
  --speculative-dspark-block-size 5 \
  --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled \
  --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \
  --max-running-requests 12 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.75
```

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way — revert the commit; no persisted state or schema changes.

**Blast radius:** one model file plus one CPU unit test, gated on
`_is_cuda and tail is not None and is_cp_active(forward_batch)`; the DSpark aux
branch additionally requires `capture_dspark`. Non-CP, HIP and decode paths are
untouched; CP without DSpark now zero-fills non-tail rows, which are never read.

Validation scope: the server numbers above come from v0.5.22 with the same
change, `PP=1`. The patch applies cleanly to `main` at `bd5a445` and the touched
code path is unchanged, but the full server has not been re-run on `main`.

- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.

title: [Fix] mem_cache: Skip linker L3 lookup on PD decode
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

With `--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache` and `--enable-unified-cache-external-linker` on a PD decode server, `UnifiedRadixCache.match_prefix` calls `linker.match`, which reports an external-store hit as `host_hit_length`. Decode's prealloc folds that length into `decode_prefix_len`, so prefill skips sending those pages. Decode never loads them back: the linker load-back runs only from the extend path's `init_load_back`, and PD decode has no extend batch. The request then decodes over unwritten KV rows, and the hit marker is never released.

## Modifications

- `UnifiedRadixCache.match_prefix` skips `linker.match` when `disaggregation_mode == "decode"`. Decode still offloads through the linker. It just never claims an external hit it cannot restore.

## Tests

- `test_decode_match_skips_linker_lookup` (Python and Rust tree cores): in decode mode, a prefix fully present in the store yields `host_hit_length == 0` and no `lookup` call. Outside decode, the same prefix still hits.
- Negative control: with the gate removed, the test fails on both tree cores.
- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_cache_linker.py`: 66 passed.

title: [Fix] radix-cache: Order linker offloads behind the forward that writes the pages
author: hnyls2002
body:
- Mooncake and mori linker offloads now record one event on the scheduler's stream (the page indices) and one on the forward stream (the forward writing the pages), and the offload thread synchronizes both, so it reads a stashed chunk's KV only after that forward. The forward stream's own order is unchanged.
- Prefill read-done is on by default since #37958. With TRTLLM MHA prefill or DeepSeek V4 (no CP, no HiSparse), the scheduler's stream then waits only on the forward's pre-replay read-done, so an offload event recorded on it alone can let the copy read KV the forward is still writing. The read-done gate turns the fast path off for HiCache, storage backends, and LMCache, but not for the external linker.
- The registry passes the model runner's forward stream to the linker, as it already does for LMCache.
- Adds unit tests for the two events, the Mooncake offload thread waiting on both, and the registry wiring.

No behavior change without the external linker. Found by code reading; not reproduced on main.

title: [Fix] linker: Order loads behind the forward that may still use the pages
author: hnyls2002
body:
- Linker loads now wait for the forward in flight, as offloads already do (#45559). Under read-done the scheduler's stream runs ahead of that forward, and the pages a load writes may have been freed while the forward still uses them: a stashed chunk's duplicates, or a finished request's last decode slot. A load released only behind the scheduler's stream could write them under that forward.
- `UnifiedCacheLinker.record_offload_ready` becomes `record_transfer_ready`, shared by loads and offloads. It returns a `TransferReady` that owns the wait: the Mooncake and UMBP transfer threads call `synchronize()` on it, and the MLA dedup broadcast calls `wait(stream)`. Out-of-tree linkers calling the old name, or looping over its old list result, need the change.
- The earlier fence in `stash_chunked_request`, which made the scheduler's stream wait for the forward when a checkpoint freed duplicate KV, is removed; the load-side wait covers that case and every other way such pages get reused, without a scheduler-side wait.

Found by code reading and not reproduced. Behavior changes only when an external linker loads: the load starts after the forward in flight ends, so a batch that hits the linker waits longer in the existing per-layer wait, as it did before prefill read-done.

title: [Fix] [SM100] quantization: Honor `deep_gemm` for 32x32 block-FP8 linears
author: hnyls2002
body:
- `--fp8-gemm-backend=deep_gemm` now runs `[32, 32]` block-FP8 linears with UE8M0 scales (DeepSeek-V4.1) on DeepGEMM on SM100, instead of falling back to Triton. DeepGEMM serves this recipe there with `sm100_fp8_fp4_gemm_1d1d`.
- SM100 DeepGEMM casts the fp32 block scales to UE8M0 itself, which is exact only for powers of two. Weight loading checks that every block32 weight scale is a power of two (as the Hopper BF16 path already does) and the linear keeps any other layer on Triton, so a checkpoint labeled `ue8m0` with other scales keeps working. Pre-quantized `(q, scale)` input stays on Triton on SM100, since nothing checks its scales.
- Block32 weights without `scale_fmt: ue8m0` stay on Triton on SM100. An explicit `deep_gemm` that still lands on Triton for a non-128 block layout now logs a warning.
- `test_warmup_memory` now also covers the block32 kernel type on Blackwell.
- Verified on B300 through the real linear layer: UE8M0 weights run on DeepGEMM and match the Triton path within BF16 rounding over 5 shapes; scales scaled off powers of two fall back to Triton with output identical to Triton; pre-quantized input runs on Triton. Layer latency (N=4096, K=7168) drops from 135 us to 23 us at M=1, and from 1011 us to 56 us at M=2048.

Behavior changes only for `--fp8-gemm-backend=deep_gemm` on SM100; `auto`, the other backends, and SM90 are unchanged.

title: [Fix] dsv4: Write idle SWA stores to an idle request-window layout
author: hnyls2002
body:
- `DeepseekV4AttnBackend.get_swa_out_cache_loc` no longer reads attention metadata on an idle forward under `--enable-encoder-swa-bounded-replay`. It returns the write locations of `RequestWindow.activate_idle`, a cached layout whose rows land in the workspace past an empty history.
- Under speculative decoding, a padded idle forward (a DP-attention rank with no requests, padded to the busy ranks' token count) skips `init_forward_metadata`. The store then read the previous forward's request-window layout, or `None` after an unpadded idle. The result was either a `TensorMatcher` failure in `fused_k_norm_rope_flashmla` (the stale `write_loc` length does not match the padded rows) or `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'core_attn_metadata'`.
- Repro: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 on 4x GB300, `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --enable-encoder-swa-bounded-replay`, GSM8K through sgl-eval (200 examples, 64 threads, max tokens 4096, temperature 0, no thinking). The server crashed at 197/200 when one rank ran an idle verify. With this change the run completes 200/200 at 97.50%, the same score as without encoder replay.
- The repro above ran with the Engram idle fix of #40424 applied, since main then failed first with `engram serves extend, target-verify and decode, not 4` on the same idle forward; #40424 has since merged.

No behavior change outside idle forwards with `--enable-encoder-swa-bounded-replay`; idle rows were already discarded and never committed.

title: [Fix] diffusion: float32 Plucker rays for bf16 camera poses
author: OnePunchMonk
body:
Part of #43875 (item 25). Split out of #44888 as requested in review so it can be validated on its own.

## Commits and the bugs they fix

### 1. Plucker rays built in float32 (`811661cc89`, item 25)
- **Bug:** rays were built in bf16 when the poses were bf16. bf16 cannot represent pixel coordinates above 256, so neighbouring pixels of a wide frame shared a ray.
- **Fix:** `get_plucker_embeddings` computes in float32 (or wider). LingBot-World builds its poses and intrinsics in float32.
- **Test:** `test_camera_geometry.py`, bf16 poses on a 640-wide frame give the same rays as float32.
- **Behavior change:** conditioning values change slightly. On CPU at 832x480 (float64 as truth), the old path differs in 74% of values (max 0.032). The new path matches float64 after the final bf16 cast.

### 2. Fused QKV made a copy and ignored LoRA and weight updates (`37e49c88a1`)
- **Bug:** `fuse_qkv_projection` stored a registered `nn.Parameter` copy of `to_q/to_k/to_v` (about +6.3 GB at TP=1 across 40 blocks). After that, `_project_qkv` always used the copy, so in-place LoRA merges and weight copies on the original layers never reached the forward. The model also did not override `refresh_weight_derived_caches`, so a weight swap left the copy stale.
- **Fix:** the layers now alias one packed buffer, so no second copy is kept and in-place updates land in the fused GEMM. `repack_qkv_projection()` re-packs after a loader replaces `.data`. The model's `refresh_weight_derived_caches` calls it for every block. The fused path is skipped while a dynamic LoRA (`BaseLayerWithLoRA.lora_active`) is active, since that delta is applied inside each layer's forward.
- **Tests:** shared storage and in-place update visible in the fused output; repack after `.data` replacement; model refresh hook repacks. On `main`, all 3 fail.
- **Not covered by a test:** the dynamic-LoRA skip branch.

### 3. Causal attention applied RoPE twice on the no-cache path (`37e49c88a1`)
- **Bug:** on CUDA, flashinfer RoPE rotates `q/k` in place. The `kv_cache is None` branch then passed those already-rotated tensors to `super().forward`, which applies RoPE again. The model forward always passes a KV cache, so this is latent today.
- **Fix:** the no-cache early return runs before RoPE, so the base attention applies RoPE once. The sequence-shard `NotImplementedError` on that branch was unreachable (sequence sharding needs a cache) and is removed.
- **Test:** monkeypatched CUDA path; the q/k the base forward receives are the originals. On `main`, it fails.

### 4. Uneven sequence splits hang or corrupt ring and kv-gather strategies (`37e49c88a1`)
- **Bug:** `kvgather_replicated`, `kvgather_sharded` and `ring` assume equal per-rank chunks (plain all-gathers, `current_start // world_size`, equal P2P buffers). Nothing checked the splits, so uneven splits could hang or corrupt the KV cache. `ulysses` already handles uneven splits and is unchanged.
- **Fix:** `_check_sequence_split_strategy` raises `NotImplementedError` for those three strategies when the splits are not uniform.
- **Test:** the helper rejects uneven splits for the three strategies and accepts uniform ones and `ulysses`. On `main` the helper does not exist, so this fails.

## Validation

- Modal CPU, `test_lingbot_causal_denoising.py`: `main` gives 5 failed, 28 passed (the 5 new tests). This branch gives 33 passed.
- Ruff format is clean. The 11 lint findings are the same as on the PR head before these commits.
- GPU A/B for item 1 (fixed seed, one A100-80GB): main is bit-identical across reruns. This PR is 30.2 dB PSNR vs main (min 22.1 at frame 4), same scene and camera path. Details: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45638#issuecomment-6322863557

title: [Fix] mistral3: Subclass LlavaForConditionalGeneration instead of wrapping it
author: em-dreyer
body:
## Motivation

`unsloth/Mistral-Small-3.1-24B-Instruct-2503` fails to start since #44913, which breaks `test_vlms_mmmu_eval` in the `nightly-2-gpu-large` job:

```
File ".../model_executor/runner/base_runner.py", line 250, in model_context
    shared_experts=self.model_runner.model.shared_experts_config
AttributeError: 'LlavaForConditionalGeneration' object has no attribute 'shared_experts_config'
```

Failing job (nightly 10/21, `8e3e2980d`): https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39614482141/job/119271892420

**Root cause:** `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration` was a plain Python wrapper around an inner `LlavaForConditionalGeneration`, not an `nn.Module`. Loaders keep what `model.eval()` returns. The wrapper forwarded `eval` to the inner model through `__getattr__`, so the server ended up holding the inner Llava model and the wrapper was dropped. That lost:
1. `shared_experts_config`, which `_initialize_model` sets after construction. That's the startup crash.
2. The wrapper's `load_weights`, which normalizes transformers v5 Mistral3 checkpoint names (`model.language_model.*`, `model.vision_tower.*`, `model.multi_modal_projector.*`, `lm_head.*`). Initial loading still went through the wrapper, but weight updates after startup (from disk, distributed, or tensor updates) call `load_weights` on the kept inner model, so a v5 name like `model.language_model.embed_tokens.weight` would raise `KeyError` there.

## Modifications

- Make `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration` a subclass of `LlavaForConditionalGeneration`:
  - the base constructor already builds `MULTIMODAL_PROJECTOR_TYPE`, so the Mistral3 projector comes from that;
  - `get_image_feature` becomes a normal override instead of a method monkeypatched onto the inner model;
  - `load_weights` normalizes names, then calls `super().load_weights(...)`.
- Remove the wrapper's `inner`, the forwarding dunders (`__getattr__`, `__setattr__`, `__call__`) and the monkeypatch. Parameter names are unchanged (`language_model.*`, `vision_tower.*`, `multi_modal_projector.*`), so checkpoint loading is unaffected.
- `llava.py` imported `MistralForCausalLM` at module level only for `LlavaMistralForCausalLM`'s constructor. Move that import into the constructor to break the import cycle that motivated the wrapper.

## Tests

`test/registered/unit/models/test_mistral3_vision_feature.py`. I replaced the earlier test, which asserted that `eval()` returns the inner model, with regression tests for the full contract:
- **`eval()` keeps the Mistral3 model:** `model.eval() is model`, the same `shared_experts_config` object survives, child modules are in eval mode, and Mistral3's image-feature path still runs (the projector receives `image_sizes`).
- **Weight names:** transformers v5 checkpoint names reach the same destinations when loaded before `eval()` (initial load) and after `eval()` (weight updates).
- **Import order:** `sglang.srt.models.mistral` and `sglang.srt.models.llava` import cleanly in either order, each in a fresh interpreter.

The existing vision-feature tests are unchanged.

Before the refactor, `/rerun-test registered/accuracy/models/test_vlms_mmmu_eval.py` passed with the earlier `__setattr__` fix (MMMU 0.5598 against a 0.30 threshold). It needs a rerun on this revision.

title: [Fix] rust-server: Match Python's chat layer on templates, streaming and lowered-chat errors
author: sherlockwu
body:
Makes rust-server's chat (#45449) match Python's chat layer. Stacked on #45449.

DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 still renders through deepseek-recipe, as on main (#46243). This PR changes no DeepSeek rendering code.

Some fixes are in `sglang-processor`'s shared code, so they also change sgl-router:
- GLM-5.3 and Qwen3.8 prompts for requests with tools
- `usage.completion_tokens_details`
- error events for aborts and error frames
- `continue_final_message` given as `1` or `"true"`

#45449 already has the Jinja thinking default, the effort-implied thinking toggle, `n` list fields and the `/generate` error status. This PR builds on them.

## Modifications

**Template path** (Jinja templates and Dynamo's encoders)
- **Effort.** `reasoning_effort` reaches the template, as `_convert_to_internal_request` passes it. A non-null `chat_template_kwargs.reasoning_effort` replaces the request's; a server default effort wins.
- **Trailing assistant turn** (`_handle_last_assistant_message`). It is continued under `continue_final_message`, else asked as a user turn. Null content counts as `""`.
  - The renderers and the template path share `split_continuation`, and read the flag as pydantic's lax `bool` (`1`, `"true"`).
  - Continuing the only turn leaves an empty conversation, rejected as `apply_chat_template` rejects it.
  - Kimi K3 splits the turn off only to continue it, as its encoder does.
- **Tools.** A Jinja template gets Python's `Tool.model_dump()`: only the named tool under a named `tool_choice`, none under `"none"`, schema types normalized.
- **Forced reasoning.** Only the escaped `\n` in `<|im_start|>assistant\n<think>\n` marks a template as always reasoning, as `force_reasoning_pattern` matches. A real newline no longer does.

**Tool dumps** (GLM-5.3 and Qwen3.8 renderers, the template path, Kimi K3)
- Since #46133, Python's `Function` keeps the client's key order and drops an unset or null `strict` / `defer_loading`. One `function_dump` now serves all three paths. Before, every tool rendered with `"strict": false` and reordered keys, so prompts with tools tokenized differently from Python.

**Lowered chat** (rust-server)
- **Aborts.** A scheduler abort in a stream is Python's abort frame, answered as an error event under its status.
- **Header overrides.** The router's `x-override-*` headers apply, as to Python's `adapted_request`. A bad one is a 400 typed `"400"` (`HTTPException`).
- **Internal failures.** The server's own failure before the first frame, unary or streamed, is `handle_request`'s generic exception: `InternalServerError`, `"Internal server error: …"`. A scheduler abort keeps the `HTTPException` its status names.
- **Logprobs** are served through the processor, with a byte-level token's bytes for a partial character.

**Typed chat handler** (rust-server, for requests the processor declines)
- **Reasoning start** comes from the request (`_get_reasoning_from_request`), not the rendered prompt's suffix. A continued assistant turn's text is the parser's previous content, as `ReasoningParser` reads it.
- **Kimi K3** keeps its special tokens and leaves its generation stub out of `prompt_tokens`.
- **Grammar.** In thinking mode the grammar starts after the reasoning (`require_reasoning`).

**`/tokenize`**
- Chat messages tokenize to the ids lowered chat would send: both share one lowering, and `/tokenize` reads the lowered request's `input_ids`. So `/tokenize` accepts what chat accepts (a mixed-case role, a tool without `type`, a body asking for logprobs). The typed path stays for what chat leaves to the typed handler.

**OpenAI responder** (`sglang-processor`)
- **Streamed logprobs** are served. The count is derived when the frame omits it.
- **Abort statuses.** Every 4xx/5xx status is named as Python 3.12's `HTTPStatus` names it, so an abort with any status (412, for one) streams Python's error event, not an empty abort chunk.
- **Error frames.** Mid-stream, a non-400 error event is typed by its status name (`SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`), as Python's abort event is. A 500 frame before the first chunk is a host's own failure, answered as `InternalServerError` (Python's `/generate` sends only 400 error frames).
- **Usage.** `usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`, as Python's `UsageProcessor` reports it since #46133 (null without reasoning), for chat and completions, unary and streamed.
- **Model names.** A served model name with colons is not taken for a LoRA adapter (`_resolve_lora_path`).

## Tests

- Each fix has a unit test that fails without it.
- On this head:
  - `cargo fmt --check`.
  - clippy `-D warnings`, for the workspace and for `sglang-processor --all-features`.
  - `cargo test --workspace`: 577 passed.
  - `sglang-processor --all-features`: 68 passed.
  - `cargo check` of all 16 processor feature subsets.
  - sgl-router: 1462/1463 passed. `chat_render_parity_matrix` fails only because none of its snapshots are cached on the test machine.
- The parity and `openai_parity` tests pass on prompt text. Token ids were not checked on this head, because the pinned checkpoints were not cached; they were checked against the pinned tokenizers before the rebase.
- **Fixtures**, regenerated from current Python with the skill's generators. The stub servers gained `is_minimax_m3`, the model config `load_chat_template` reads, and `served_model_name`.
  - `generate_openai_parity.py` now keeps a case's recorded `created` times and `call_` ids where they line up, so a rerun changes only what Python changed.
  - Parity: GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash and the three Qwen3.8 checkpoints. Prompts change only in tool cases; the rest is Python's error wording.
  - OpenAI: GLM-5.3, Qwen3.8-27B and Kimi K3, keeping their recorded engine outputs. Changes: the new `usage` fields, Qwen3.8 tool prompts, and `mm_processor_kwargs` in `/generate` bodies.
  - The two DeepSeek fixtures keep #46243's recording and take only the new `usage` objects. Regenerating them fully also changes how some DeepSeek outputs parse (`chat_no_separate`, `chat_continue_thinking_stream`, the tool cases); that is for DeepSeek's owners.
- End to end, measured before the rebase onto #45449's current head and before the review fixes:
  - **Qwen3-0.6B** (`--reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser qwen25`), 1x B300, Rust vs Python:
    - `/tokenize` ids match on 7 request shapes.
    - Chat responses with and without thinking, streamed usage included, match field for field.
    - gsm8k 60.5% on both (sgl-eval 0.1.3, 200 examples, `enable_thinking=false`, temp 0.7, top_p 0.8).
  - **Qwen3.8-27B**, 4x B300, launch command from #45449:
    - gsm8k: Rust 98.5%, Python 97.5% (sgl-eval 0.1.3, 200 examples, temp 1.0, top_p 0.95, `enable_thinking=true`, max_tokens 32768).
    - Greedy `openai_parity` replay against Python: 11/13. `tools_required` stays on the typed handler, which constrains tool calls differently. In `chat` the prompt tokens are identical and greedy output drifts mid-reasoning.
  - **Qwen3's generic Jinja template:** `/tokenize` matches Python on 11 effort and trailing-assistant requests where #45449 differs, except parts-list turns (below).

## Not covered

- DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 rendering is in #46243. Its tool-choice constraints (xgrammar's `deepseek_v4_1` tag) are not in this stack.
- A trailing assistant turn whose content is a parts list is left as is. Python flattens it only for string-format templates.
- Legacy conversation templates ignore `continue_final_message`.
- `SGLANG_TOOL_STRICT_LEVEL` is not read by the Rust tool constraints.
- `--tool-call-parser` does not pick the chat encoder (Python's `resolve_chat_encoding_spec`).
- Tool parsers the processor has not ported (Qwen2.5's `qwen`, for one) leave tool requests to the typed handler. Its response shape differs from Python's (`content: null`, `refusal`, a shorter `usage`); the prompt and the parsed call match.
- Kimi K3's long-input chunking (`tokenization_kimi.py`'s 400k/25k-character splits) is not applied by rust-server's chat encode.

title: [Fix] bailing: Renormalize top-k routing weights by default for Ling-2.5/2.6
author: em-dreyer
body:
## Motivation

The nightly `test_ling_2_6_flash.py` (8-GPU H200 and B200) has failed GSM8K since #44904. On 10/21 (`8e3e2980d`) it scored 0.39 on H200 and 0.35 on B200, against a 0.825 threshold. The 10/17 nightly scored 0.87.

- H200: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39614482141/job/119271892494
- B200: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39614482141/job/119271892388

Root cause:
1. The `BailingMoeV2_5ForCausalLM` checkpoints (Ling-2.6-flash, Ling-2.5-1T, Ling-2.6-1T, Ring-2.5-1T) have no `norm_topk_prob` key. `bailing_moe_linear.py` reads `getattr(config, "norm_topk_prob", False)`, so the router gets `renormalize=False`.
2. The reference `modeling_bailing_moe_v2_5.py` always renormalizes the top-k weights, then multiplies by `routed_scaling_factor` (2.5):
   ```python
   topk_weight = scores / (scores.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True) + 1e-20) if self.top_k > 1 else scores
   topk_weight = topk_weight * self.routed_scaling_factor
   ```
3. Ling-2.6-flash (256 experts, top-8) used to take the FlashInfer `fused_topk_deepseek` path, which always renormalizes regardless of the flag. That hid the wrong default.
4. #44904 correctly gated that path on `renormalize`, so Ling moved to a path that respects `renormalize=False`. The top-k weights no longer sum to 1, the MoE output is mis-scaled at every layer, and GSM8K collapsed.

#44904 is correct and should stay; the bug is the model's default.

## Modifications

`bailing_moe_linear.py`: `norm_topk_prob` now defaults to `True`, matching the reference modeling. Configs that set the key explicitly are unaffected.

## Accuracy Tests

The CI test file was run unchanged (`test_ling_2_6_flash.py`: TP=4, NEXTN MTP, `extra_buffer`, 200-question 5-shot GSM8K) on 4×B200:

| Commit | GSM8K | Mean accept len |
|---|---|---|
| `4eb606b2ae` (10/17 nightly, last green) | 0.87 | 3.40 |
| `3a059de94c` (parent of #44904) | 0.86 | — |
| `48ea486928` (#44904) | 0.355 | 2.38 |
| `8e3e2980db` (10/21 nightly) | 0.43 | 2.68 |
| **`8e3e2980db` + this change** | **0.87** | **3.40** |

The first bad commit was found by bisecting `62cee1b15c..8e3e2980db`. The fixed run applied this same one-line change on top of `8e3e2980db`; this branch is based on a newer `main`.

Not covered here: `bailing_moe_v3.py` has the same `getattr(config, "norm_topk_prob", False)` default. I haven't checked whether its reference modeling also always renormalizes.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy).

title: [Fix] hicache: Skip empty auxiliary transfers
author: aurickq
body:
## Motivation

A buffer-only HiCache restore can need sliding-window KV while the full-attention KV is already resident. A deferred draft transfer derived from the full-attention pool then resolves to empty host and device indices.

`HybridCacheController._l2_transfers` skips the empty anchor transfer but still submits the empty auxiliary transfer. The CUDA copy can consequently launch with zero blocks and fail with `CUDA error: invalid argument`.

For example, when the transfer sizes are `FULL=0, DRAFT=0, SWA=64`:

```diff
- Submit DRAFT(0) and SWA(64).
+ Submit only SWA(64), preserving layer-completion notifications.
```

## Modifications

Skip an auxiliary transfer only when both resolved index tensors are empty. Unresolved indices still raise, and one-sided empty pairs are not silently dropped.

Extend the existing CPU dispatch tests to cover SWA-only restores, normal FULL/DRAFT/SWA restores, layer-completion notifications, and invalid inputs.

## Accuracy Tests

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_staged_write_back_dispatch.py
```

26 passed, 1 skipped. The new SWA-only subtest fails with the unmodified upstream `_l2_transfers` implementation and passes with the guard. It exercises deferred draft-index resolution and the real transfer submission loop with mocked physical copies; it does not launch a model server.

Pre-commit checks pass for both changed files.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run. Nonempty copies are unchanged; this removes empty copy submissions.

## Checklist

- [x] Format and lint the changed files.
- [x] Add CPU regression coverage to an existing registered test suite.
- [x] Follow the existing code style.
- Documentation: no user-facing API or configuration changes.
- Model accuracy and throughput benchmarks: not run; this is a transfer-dispatch fix.

title: [Fix] disaggregation: Avoid extra GPU contexts with PD
author: trevor-m
body:
## Summary

With PD disagg, an extra GPU context is accidently created on GPU0 by the other GPU workers which wastes about 1GB of gpu memory.

[by Claude Code]

## Motivation

A PD prefill rank whose GPU is not CUDA device 0 opens a second CUDA context on device 0 the first time it sends KV
for a request with a cached prefix. That rank then holds about 0.6–1 GiB on another rank's GPU (656 MiB in the repro
below, about 1 GiB with DeepSeek-V4.1 attention-DP2 prefill). The memory is taken after that GPU's KV pool was sized
against its free memory, so it eats into the headroom left for activations and graphs.

**Cause.**
- With overlap scheduling, `maybe_send_cached_prefix_chunk` (`disaggregation/prefill.py`) records a `torch.cuda.Event`
  on the forward stream for the early cached-prefix send.
- Mooncake's prefill `transfer_worker` thread calls `wait_event.synchronize()` on that event before it reads the KV.
- That thread never selects a device, so the CUDA runtime runs the call on device 0 and creates device 0's primary
  context in the process.
- Ranks that already live on device 0 reuse their own context. Every other rank gets a new one.
- mori's `_transfer_worker` does the same `wait_event.synchronize()`.

## Modifications

- `disaggregation/common/utils.py` adds two helpers:
  - `bind_thread_to_device(gpu_id)` sets the calling thread's device through `current_platform`. It is a no-op on
    platforms that do not implement `set_device`.
  - `run_on_device(gpu_id, fn, *args)` is a thread target that binds the thread, then runs `fn(*args)`.
- Mooncake:
  - The prefill `transfer_worker` threads start through `run_on_device(kv_args.gpu_id, ...)`.
  - The transfer thread pools bind each pool thread with `initializer=bind_thread_to_device`.
- mori: the `_transfer_worker` threads start through `run_on_device`.

The worker functions themselves are unchanged, so existing unit tests that drive them directly need no changes.

## Repro (dummy weights, one 4-GPU node)

Prefill runs TP2 on GPUs 0,1, so rank 1 lives on GPU 1. Decode runs TP1 on GPU 2. The same ~2k-token prompt is
sent three times, so requests 2 and 3 hit the radix cache and take the early cached-prefix send.

```bash
MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B
COMMON="--model-path $MODEL --load-format dummy --disaggregation-transfer-backend mooncake --mem-fraction-static 0.5"
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server $COMMON --tp-size 2 --disaggregation-mode prefill --port 30000 &
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2 python3 -m sglang.launch_server $COMMON --tp-size 1 --disaggregation-mode decode --port 30001 &
# wait for both /health, then:
python3 -m sglang_router.launch_router --pd-disaggregation --prefill http://127.0.0.1:30000 8998 \
  --decode http://127.0.0.1:30001 --port 8000 &
PROMPT=$(python3 -c "print(' '.join(['The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.'] * 200))")
for i in 1 2 3; do
  curl -s localhost:8000/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"text\": \"$PROMPT\", \"sampling_params\": {\"max_new_tokens\": 8, \"temperature\": 0}}" > /dev/null
done
nvidia-smi
```

On our nodes, Mooncake moved the KV over NVLink (`MC_FORCE_MNNVL=1 SGLANG_MOONCAKE_CUSTOM_MEM_POOL=True`). The bug
does not depend on the transport.

**Before** (main): requests 2 and 3 report `cached_tokens` 1984 of 2000, and the TP1 prefill scheduler now also
holds a context on GPU 0.

```
|  GPU   GI   CI              PID   Type   Process name                        GPU Memory |
|    0   N/A  N/A             492      C   sglang::scheduler_TP0                 (pool)     |
|    0   N/A  N/A             684      C   sglang::scheduler_TP1                   656MiB   |
|    1   N/A  N/A             684      C   sglang::scheduler_TP1                 (pool)     |
|    2   N/A  N/A             491      C   sglang::scheduler                     (pool)     |
```

The GPU 0 row for pid 684 is absent in `nvidia-smi` right after startup; it appears with the first cached-prefix
send.

**After** (this PR), same commands and the same `cached_tokens`: one context per process.

```
|  GPU   GI   CI              PID   Type   Process name                        GPU Memory |
|    0   N/A  N/A             494      C   sglang::scheduler_TP0                 (pool)     |
|    1   N/A  N/A             687      C   sglang::scheduler_TP1                 (pool)     |
|    2   N/A  N/A             495      C   sglang::scheduler                     (pool)     |
```

Both runs had 0 KV-transfer failures, and every request completed.

## Tests

- **New:** `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_transfer_worker_device.py` (CPU, 3 tests). It checks that
  `bind_thread_to_device` calls `current_platform.set_device`, ignores `NotImplementedError`, and that `run_on_device`
  binds on the worker's own thread before the worker runs.
- **Unchanged and passing:** `test_mooncake_transfer_batching.py` (16), `test_mooncake_deferred_kv_release.py` (9),
  `test_mori_deferred_kv_release.py` (11), `test_disaggregation_wire.py` (79).
- **GPU repro above:** run on 306ccf6f57 with this change applied. The diff applies unchanged to both 306ccf6f57 and
  current main.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [x] Accuracy: no numerics change; this only selects which device the transfer threads use. All KV transfers in the
  repro completed before and after (0 failures).

title: [Fix] lora: Preserve MoE projection identity and routing lifetimes
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* __->__ #45681
* #45917
* #45462
* #45916
* #45915

## Motivation

Independent gate/up A factors require matching rank halves during expansion. The stock virtual-expert hook reused the gate half for the up output: with `x=1`, `A_gate=2`, `A_up=3`, `B_gate=5`, `B_up=7`, it produced `[10,14]` instead of `[10,21]`. Inactive routes and absent/disabled adapters also need complete private outputs without consuming stale or NaN payloads.

## Changes

- Keep one full-`2R` shrink and select the matching A half inside the existing expansion. Internal rank/half-width constants and half-local masks support ragged widths without another projection launch or tensor. The default expansion keeps its original formulas.
- Bound raw virtual IDs and adapter slots before histogram, address or payload formation. Preserve borrowed inputs, valid adapter 0 and original-width int64 validity; shared routing retains negative routes. Missing, disabled and out-of-range adapters cannot read private deltas or contribute NaN scores.
- Complete owned LoRA outputs in their existing kernels and guard capacity-grid programs before grouped division/modulo. Empty helpers preserve their return/output contracts. Activation and shared-outer rank reductions retain active arithmetic and rounding.
- Prepare paired per-expert gate-B/down-A routing once on the main stream, aligning at each stage's actual block size. Release the shared raw owner before projection buffers and the side-stream fork. Existing cache contracts and staged fallbacks remain for unsupported pairings, including global-ID EP.

- Remove unused expert-ID sanitizers and the unused metadata-bearing activation branch. Keep the production three-tensor activation and existing producer/reduction contracts.

## CI cadence

The CUDA virtual-expert and experimental shared-outer LoRA suites now run in opt-in `extra-a-test-1-gpu-small`. CPU runtime checks and the core routing-kernel tests remain in base CI; the existing XPU registration is preserved.

Across the stack, six existing CUDA file registrations move from base CI to extra/nightly, removing 854 estimated GPU-seconds from the default gate (registration estimates, not a measured wall-time saving). All test bodies, cases, inputs, assertions and tolerances are unchanged. Full before/after discovery validates 2,535 files and 3,077 registrations, with every moved file selected in its enabled destination suite. Configured hooks pass; native tests were not rerun for this registration-only update.

## Validation

- At integrated `e6670af1ad`, the focused native Marlin/LoRA route suite passes 14 tests on 1× B300 with the pinned providers, including changing padded routes and output completion.

- Two additional direct Marlin output-ownership configurations did not complete within a 600-second cold-compilation budget on B300. No result is claimed for that extended run; it is separate from the completed route replay and producer-contract checks.

- The focused production activation/reduction suite passes 10 tests on 1× B300 after cleanup. The deleted helpers had no production callers; retained production Triton kernel bodies are unchanged.

Performance comparisons use main `b008ec3de6` before #44480, #44991, #44993 and #44994 merged. The integrated candidate also includes intervening main changes; the measured improvement is not attributed solely to this PR.

- Configured hooks and runtime/policy CPU tests pass. 1× NVIDIA H200 nonzero-LoRA tests cover real stock, factored and three-adapter temporary paths, poisoned inactive data, mapping/enabled changes and valid → inactive → recovery CUDA graphs. Runner unit doubles are separate from native/full-entry evidence.
- The final pre-rebase H200 comparison (`3c486bd6` versus `b008ec3d`) completed 60 workers and 384 fixed `rtol=0.01, atol=0.001` checks at M32/512, H256/I128/E8/topk2/rank8. Factored and multi-adapter outputs agree bitwise across revisions. Paired graph medians improve 1.82%/1.41% for factored and 4.72%/6.62% for multi-adapter paths; measured peaks do not increase. The nongated stock compatibility fixture retains bit instability on both revisions despite passing fixed-close checks; it does not prove a fully gated checkpoint.
- Four H200 factored memory workers retain 2 MiB/4 MiB graph-pool reservations, lower capture allocated peaks by 512 bytes and preserve replay allocated peaks. These are allocator/current-pool observations, not historical per-pool peaks or non-PyTorch memory coverage.
- B300 virtual-expert tests passed 19 cases/102 subtests, with five abstract-base skips. The final full-width route-factory suite passed six tests/12 subtests. title: [Fix] sgl-router: Do not abort forwarded requests on reqwest's default 30 s TCP_USER_TIMEOUT
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

The router's forwarding client is a default `reqwest` 0.12 client. On Linux, `reqwest` sets `TCP_USER_TIMEOUT` to 30 s on every connection unless told otherwise (`reqwest-0.12.28/src/async_impl/client.rs:307`). If an engine reads none of a forwarded request's body for 30 s, the kernel aborts the router's send with `ETIMEDOUT`. That can happen when the engine's HTTP process is busy with a burst of long prompts and stops reading request bodies. The router then answers 504 `upstream_timeout` after about 30.5 s, regardless of `request_timeout`.

We hit this in agentic trace replays: about 1,000 new 100K-token prompts arrive at once, and the engine's single HTTP process falls behind. Every send still in flight failed together about 30.7 s after the burst, and the client aborted the run. The error chain was `hyper::Error(Io, Os { code: 110, kind: TimedOut })` at `SendRequest`, and the `TCPAbortOnTimeout` counter rose with it. sgl-model-gateway, which `sglang_router.launch_router` installs, uses the same `reqwest` default.

## Modifications

- `sgl-router/src/proxy/mod.rs`, `build_client`: call `.tcp_user_timeout(None)` on Linux/Android/Fuchsia, the targets where reqwest sets the option. `request_timeout` and the stream idle and stale limits still bound a request.
- `sgl-router/tests/proxy/timeout.rs`: add `request_survives_worker_that_reads_nothing_for_over_30s`. A worker accepts the connection, reads nothing for 40 s, then reads the whole 16 MiB request and answers 200; the test expects a 200. It is Linux-only and `#[ignore]` because it takes about 40 s. Run it with `cargo test --test proxy -- --ignored reads_nothing`.

## Testing

On Linux (aarch64, kernel 7.0):

| Build | `TCP_USER_TIMEOUT` set on the forwarding socket (strace) | New test |
|---|---|---|
| Before this change | `[30000]` | fails at 30.51 s: 504, `x-router-error-code: upstream_timeout` |
| This change | not set | passes, 40.03 s |

- `cargo test --release --test proxy`: 224 passed, 1 ignored (the new test).
- `cargo test --release --lib proxy`: 36 passed.
- `cargo clippy --release --all-targets`: no warnings.
- `rustfmt`: passes (pre-commit).

title: [Fix] [Intel] diffusion: Restore copy offload for FLUX.2-dev nightly
author: arathi-hlab
body:
## Motivation

`TestFlux2DevXPU::test_diffusion_generation[flux2_dev_image_t2i]` in `nightly-xpu-kernel-main-4-gpu` has failed the e2e latency guard every night since 10-19 ([latest run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39663561647/job/119442565458)):

```
Validation failed for 'E2E Latency'.
  Actual:   83818.7248ms
  Expected: 49699.2100ms
  Limit:    69578.8940ms (rel_tol: 40.0%, abs_pad: 20.0ms)
```

Denoising runs at ~1.6 s/step against a ~0.93 s/step baseline in `xpu_b60.json`.

**Root cause:** #45013 set `UR_L0_V2_FORCE_DISABLE_COPY_OFFLOAD=1` in `scripts/ci/xpu/xpu_ci_start_container.sh` to work around a first-H2D-copy hang in 1-GPU text-model tests. That keeps all copies on the compute engine. FLUX.2-dev runs with `--dit-layerwise-offload`, which streams ~14.6 GB of pinned weights H2D on every denoise step and relies on the copy engine to overlap those copies with compute. Without copy offload the copies serialize with the DiT compute.

The timing lines up exactly, all on the same runner (`aicf-jf-cicd-06`):

| Nightly | Checkout contains #45013 | FLUX.2 result |
|---|---|---|
| 10-16, 10-17, 10-18 | no | passed (test 133-147s) |
| 10-19, 10-20, 10-21 | yes | failed (~1.6 s/step, test ~165s) |

FLUX.2 never hit the hang that #45013 works around; it passed on all three nights with copy offload on.

## Modifications

- `test/registered/xpu/test_xpu_flux2_dev.py`: set `UR_L0_V2_FORCE_DISABLE_COPY_OFFLOAD=0` in the case `env_vars`, so the FLUX.2 server gets copy offload back. Every other XPU test keeps the #45013 workaround.
  - UR's `getenv_tobool` only treats `y/yes/t/true/1` as true, so `"0"` re-enables copy offload.
  - The diffusion harness applies case `env_vars` on top of the inherited container env (`env.update(self.env_vars)` in `ServerManager`), so the per-case value wins.

The `xpu_b60.json` baseline is unchanged. It reflects the expected performance with copy offload on.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A. CI env change only; the CLIP-score guard in the test is unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not yet re-run on B60. Expected: denoise back to ~0.93 s/step, E2E ~50s, within the 69.6s limit. A manual 4-GPU run of `test_xpu_flux2_dev.py` on the runner will confirm.

title: [Fix] [NPU] tests: Restore evalscope GSM8K baseline via NPUGSM8KMixin backend
author: pllimax
body:
## Motivation

The NPU nightly pipeline switched the Moonlight GSM8K accuracy cases from evalscope to sgl_eval, which dropped measured scores from ~0.83 to ~0.73-0.82 because sgl_eval probes 0-shot with greedy decoding while the historical 0.83 baseline was calibrated with evalscope (4-shot chat, temperature 1.0). Forcing thresholds onto the sgl_eval scale loses the legacy calibration.

This PR adds a native `evalscope` backend to `NPUGSM8KMixin` so NPU accuracy cases can declare `gsm8k_backend = "evalscope"` and keep their historically calibrated thresholds.

## Modifications

* `NPUGSM8KMixin`: add `gsm8k_backend = "evalscope"` support via a new `_test_gsm8k_evalscope` method (delegates to the existing `run_evalscope` harness), expose the request concurrency as the overridable class attribute `gsm8k_eval_batch_size = 64`.
* Make the 1% accuracy tolerance idempotent: guard the threshold relaxation with a flag so outer retries (`run_suite --enable-retry`) cannot compound the 0.99 factor (0.83 -> 0.8217 -> 0.8134).
* Resolve the `run_evalscope.sh` install script relative to `__file__` instead of the stale `/root/sglang` hardcode (the CI image WORKDIR moved to `/sgl-workspace`).
* Require both the `pull_request` event and a non-nightly workflow ref for the PR smoke short-circuit, so PR-triggered nightly runs still execute the full accuracy cases.
* Point the two Moonlight cases (`TestDPAttentionMixedChunk`, `TestAscendMlaFiaHicacheBf16`) back to `gsm8k_accuracy_thres = 0.83` with `gsm8k_backend = "evalscope"`.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated on Ascend A3 (910B) in the nightly pipeline (run [39711641496](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39711641496)):
