title: [Fix] http_server: Apply SGLANG_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE to Granian HTTP/1.1 connections
author: nvrohanv
body:
## Motivation

While running high-concurrency benchmarks on SGLang, I noticed that passing `--enable-http2` makes SGLang ignore `SGLANG_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE`: it serves through Granian instead of uvicorn, and only uvicorn reads that variable.

As a result, Granian closes any idle HTTP/1.1 connection after its default 30 s. Connection-pooling clients (like `aiohttp`, which keeps idle connections for 300 s) that reuse a connection right at the 30 s mark hit immediate disconnections (`ClientOSError: Can not write request body` / `ServerDisconnectedError`). In long multi-turn benchmarks, one of these on a warm-up request can abort the whole run.

## Modifications

- When `SGLANG_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE` is set, it is passed to Granian as the HTTP/1.1 `header_read_timeout` (seconds to ms), which Granian also uses as its idle timeout ([hyper#3828](https://github.com/hyperium/hyper/pull/3828)). This covers both the single- and multi-worker Granian servers.
- Unset: no change (Granian keeps its 30 s default). Zero or negative values are rejected at startup.
- In Granian the same timeout also limits how long a client may take to send request headers.
- Adds a CPU unit test and a one-line docs update. Builds on the approach in #29560.

## Testing

- Unit test 4/4; `pre-commit` passes.
- Patched server: idle connections close after 30 s when the variable is unset, and stay open past 90 s with `SGLANG_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE=300`. Reusing pooled connections right around the 30 s mark, 1–9 of 41 requests failed before the fix and 0 of 41 after.

title: [Fix] encoder: allocate embedding cache resources only on rank 0
author: harrisonyhq
body:
Fixes #45770.

## Motivation

With the global multimodal embedding cache enabled, every encoder TP rank
currently creates an embedding storage backend and an `EmbeddingCacheController`.
Each controller allocates and registers its own vision/audio pinned host pools
with a default combined budget of 4 GiB, and starts a cache I/O thread.

The encoder's cache-data path is already owned by rank 0: it performs lookup,
prefetch, staging, output assembly, and insertion. Other ranks participate in
cache-mask broadcasts and model computation for misses. Cached embeddings are
final encoder outputs, so those ranks do not need a copy of the cached data to
skip the corresponding forward computation. Their independently allocated
host pools therefore remain idle.

This change limits cache-data resources to rank 0 while preserving collective
participation on all encoder ranks.

## Modifications

### 1. Separate shared coordination from cache resource ownership

Move cache initialization into `MMEncoder._init_global_cache()`. It initializes
`mm_global_cache_enabled` on every rank and starts with no local controller or
cache coordination group. When caching is disabled, initialization returns at
that point.

For TP greater than one, every rank first participates in creating
`global_cache_tp_group`. Its membership comes from the existing TP CPU group,
and it uses Gloo for the CPU hit/fallback masks. Group creation happens before
the nonzero-rank return because it is a collective operation.

Only rank 0 then constructs the storage backend and `EmbeddingCacheController`.
Consequently, only rank 0 allocates/registers the host pools and starts the
controller's I/O thread. The existing embedding dimensions and model dtype
are passed through to that controller.

### 2. Keep nonzero ranks in the cache execution path

Previously, `batch_encode()` selected the cache path based on whether
`self.mm_global_cache` existed. After restricting controller ownership to
rank 0, that condition would cause other ranks to bypass cache coordination.

Select the path using the shared enabled flag instead:

```python
use_global_cache = self.mm_global_cache_enabled and not is_health_check
```

All ranks therefore enter the same cache flow even when nonzero ranks have
`mm_global_cache=None`. Health probes retain their existing cache bypass.

### 3. Give mask broadcasts their own encoder-owned group

Update `_broadcast_global_cache_mask()` to use `global_cache_tp_group` rather
than obtain a group through the local controller. Both the initial hit mask
and the later fallback mask remain available to every rank.

The controller now creates its internal `prefetch_tp_group` only when
`all_rank_get=True` and TP is greater than one. The encoder passes
`all_rank_get=False`, so constructing its controller on rank 0 no longer
invokes group creation that would also require the other ranks. Callers using
`all_rank_get=True` retain the controller group and the prefetch-completion
`all_reduce(MIN)` synchronization.

### 4. Preserve the existing request-level flow

Rank 0 determines cache hits and broadcasts the hit mask. All ranks compute
the same missing items while rank 0 prefetches the hits. Rank 0 then broadcasts
the fallback mask so that failed cache loads are recomputed consistently.
Only rank 0 assembles the complete embedding and stages it for downstream
delivery.

For example, if A is cached and B is missing, every rank computes only B;
rank 0 loads A and assembles `[A, B]`. If loading A fails, the fallback mask
makes every rank compute A before rank 0 assembles the result.

Pool paging, eviction, GET/PUT, host/device copying, and assembly algorithms
keep their existing implementations. Cache flags, default capacity, and
backend selection also retain their existing behavior.

## Validation Results

**Test bed**: 8x H100-80GB, v0.5.22-based tree with this PR applied; Qwen3.8-27B (local weights); Mooncake master (HTTP metadata server) + standalone 8 GiB store over TCP; encoder/language split serving with `--encoder-transfer-backend zmq_to_scheduler`. Encoder TP2 (2 GPUs) and TP4 (4 GPUs).

### Unit tests

The unit tests follow the registered-CI conventions (`CustomTestCase`, `register_cpu_ci(..., suite="base-a-test-cpu")`, `__main__` entry point) and mirror the modified sources (`srt/disaggregation/encoder/server.py` -> `unit/disaggregation/...`, `srt/mem_cache/embedding_cache_controller.py` -> `unit/mem_cache/test_embedding_cache_controller.py`).

Each file, executed the way CI runs an individual registered test file:

```
$ python3 test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_embedding_cache_tp_coordination.py
Ran 1 test in 16.3s  OK
$ python3 test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_encoder_global_cache_rank0.py
Ran 4 tests  OK
$ python3 test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_embedding_cache_controller.py
Ran 25 tests  OK
```

What they cover:

- `test_embedding_cache_tp_coordination.py` — real two-rank Gloo coordination with CPU substitutes for storage I/O: only rank 0 constructs the backend/controller (call counts asserted equal to `int(rank == 0)`), every rank joins the mask group and reaches identical forward decisions; exercises all-hit / partial-hit / all-miss plus injected lookup/get/prefetch/completion failures for image/video/audio, and repeat-request local hits.
- `test_encoder_global_cache_rank0.py` — rank-zero-only resource ownership across {disabled, enabled} x {tp_size, rank}; mask broadcast uses the encoder-owned group with no controller present; nonzero ranks still enter the cache path and complete requests end-to-end without a controller.
- `test_embedding_cache_controller.py` — the controller creates its internal group only for `all_rank_get=True` with TP>1, the prefetch-progress `all_reduce` is opt-in, plus the retained pool/paging/eviction coverage.

Aggregate pytest run: 30 passed, 48 subtests in 36s. Existing registered tests that reference the modified modules (test_encode_server, test_kimi_k3_encoder_mode, test_mooncake_tenant_config, test_runtime_context) also pass after the change in our test environment (284 passed, 153 subtests).

### Per-rank resource ownership at runtime

Non-rank0 INFO logs do not reach the server log, so log lines alone cannot show per-rank behavior. I injected temporary probes (direct file writes, bypassing the logger) along the cache-init chain — encoder cache-init entry -> embedding-store construction -> mooncake setup -> controller entry / pool registration — and sampled per-rank process RSS:

| Run | rank 0 | rank != 0 |
|---|---|---|
| baseline (without this PR), TP2 | full chain; RSS 7.68 GB | full chain; RSS 7.77 GB |
| baseline (without this PR), TP4 | full chain; RSS 7.63 GB | all 3 ranks full chain; 7.62-7.64 GB each |
| with this PR, TP2 | full chain; RSS 7.64 GB | early-return; no backend / controller / pools; RSS 2.56 GB |
| with this PR, TP4 | full chain; RSS 7.63 GB | all 3 ranks early-return; 2.46 GB each |

Every non-rank0 rank drops from ~7.6 GB to ~2.5 GB (-5.2 GB each: ~4.1 GiB pinned embedding pools + transfer-engine client), the measured counterpart of the Memory impact table. Both TP sizes become healthy in ~30-40 s, same as baseline.

### Accuracy Tests

No change to model outputs — verified end-to-end with the cache enabled. With `logprobs=true, top_logprobs=20` over 8 decode steps (168 values), results are **bit-identical** (max |delta logprob| = 0) across all four paths: direct forward / local pool hit / global Mooncake hit (after an encoder restart) / cache-disabled control. Final outputs are byte-identical in all cases (temperature=0).

Mooncake flow on a fixed image (functional evidence):

- 1st request: `Multi-Level Cache Check — Local 0 / Global 0 / Miss 1` -> GPU forward -> `Mooncake PUT Finished: Stored 1/1`
- 2nd request: `Local Hits 1 / Misses 0` — no vision forward
- after an encoder restart: `Local 0 / Global Hits 1 / Misses 0` -> `Mooncake GET Finished: fetched 1/1` (cross-restart global hit)

### Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: the change only removes idle allocations on nonzero encoder ranks and does not touch the compute path. E2E request latency is unchanged within noise.

title: [Fix] scheduler: Publish KV metrics when idle
author: zhtshr
body:
## Motivation

When the scheduler becomes idle, it refreshes its local and Prometheus statistics without publishing `KvMetrics`. Consumers such as Dynamo can retain the last busy-batch KV usage and continue rejecting requests after the engine is idle.

## Modifications

- Publish refreshed KV metrics from `_maybe_log_idle_metrics()`, preserving the existing metrics gate and idle reporting interval.
- Add regression coverage for idle updates in regular, prefill, and decode modes, including nonzero remaining KV usage, rate limiting, and disabled metrics.

## Accuracy Tests

- All 54 related CPU unit tests pass. The added regression tests fail without the fix.
- Real-GPU Qwen3-0.6B 1P1D validation with a 60% KV threshold: the baseline completes the first request, then rejects three requests while actual prefill KV usage is 0% and reported usage remains 79%. With the fix, all four requests complete and idle KV metrics return to 0%.
- Three additional busy/idle cycles confirm that genuine busy-worker rejection still works and admission recovers after idle. Every successful request generates 256 tokens.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A: no model or kernel changes. The GPU checks above validate admission recovery.

title: [Fix] dp-attention: Pad extend host lists out of place so pre-planned DSA metadata keeps its rows
author: nvjullin
body:
## Motivation

TL;DR there is a bug in batch size padding when decode runs in eager mode. The attention plan holds inconsistent values: some are padded and some are not, causing assert to fire and crash the server. The padding is needed because some collectives expect the same tensor shapes on all ranks.

DP-attention decode with EAGLE MTP on a DSA model (GLM-5.2-NVFP4, DEP16, EAGLE 5-1-6, `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 32`) crashes every DP rank once any rank holds more requests than the draft-extend CUDA graph covers:

```
dsa_indexer.py  _get_topk_paged -> deepgemm_paged_mqa_logits_split
dsa_indexer.py  _chunked_fp8_paged_mqa_logits -> deep_gemm.fp8_paged_mqa_logits
RuntimeError: Assertion error (csrc/apis/attention.hpp:530): _batch_size == batch_size
```

In DeepGEMM v0.2.3 that assert is `block_table.size(0) == q.size(0)`: the indexer passes more query rows than page-table rows.

Mechanism:

1. When the draft-extend graph cannot run, `prepare_for_draft_extend` plans attention metadata on the local batch, before MLP-sync padding, and marks it ready. This pre-pad plan is used as-is (#27193).
2. The DSA backend stores `forward_batch.extend_seq_lens_cpu` by reference as `dsa_extend_seq_lens_list`. Its page table has `n*b` rows (`b` local requests, `n` draft tokens).
3. `ForwardBatch._pad_inputs_to_size` then grows that same list in place to the DP max `B` (`list.extend`, introduced in #33829).
4. The indexer's `q_offset = sum(dsa_extend_seq_lens_list)` becomes `n*B`, while the page table still has `n*b` rows. Every rank with `b < B` asserts. With `n*B` above the SM count, the failure is in the chunked branch, as in the trace above.

## Modifications

- `_pad_inputs_to_size` rebinds `extend_seq_lens_cpu`, `extend_prefix_lens_cpu` and `extend_logprob_start_lens_cpu` instead of extending them in place. The tensors and the mamba host lists in the same function already pad out of place.
  - Metadata planned before padding keeps the pre-pad lengths it was built from.
  - `extend_logprob_start_lens_cpu`, which `init_new` binds directly to the ScheduleBatch's list, no longer writes padding into scheduler state.
- Readers of the padded batch read the live `ForwardBatch` attribute, so they still see the padded lists.
- Regression case in `test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_mlp_sync_pad_unpad.py`.

## Validation

- Unit: `test_mlp_sync_pad_unpad.py`, 12 passed. The new case fails without the fix (`[2, 2, 2] != [2, 2]`).
- Reproducer on 1x GB300 node (152 SMs): GLM-5.2-NVFP4 with dummy weights, `--tp 4 --dp 4 --ep 4 --enable-dp-attention`, EAGLE 5-1-6, `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 32 --max-running-requests 192`, 160 concurrent `random-ids` requests.
  - Before: every rank crashed about 40 s after the server was ready, with the trace above (eager `_draft_extend_for_decode` -> MTP layer -> indexer, chunked branch).
  - After: 640/640 requests completed with 0 exceptions, across eager decode steps with per-rank batches of 26-45.
- Real weights, same shape, 64 concurrent greedy requests: draft extend in CUDA graphs vs forced eager (`SGLANG_DISABLE_DRAFT_EXTEND_CUDA_GRAPH=1`, which plans pre-pad on padded ranks). 3 x 512 prompts per arm, 0 errors. Mean decode-log acceptance length over windows with >= 13 running requests per rank, where padded eager draft extend runs: 4.168 (graph, n=180) vs 4.163 (eager, n=182). Bench-reported acceptance per repetition: graph 4.41 / 4.37 / 4.12, eager 4.26 / 4.32 / 4.12.

## Checklist

- [x] Unit test added
- [x] Reproduced and verified on GB300

title: [Fix] llava: Load LLaVA-1.5 CLIP tower
author: SKRohit
body:
## Motivation

llava-hf/llava-1.5-7b-hf fails at model init on every backend (reproduced on Intel XPU; the P1 accuracy matrix shows the same failure on H200):

AttributeError: 'Conv2d' object has no attribute 'num_embeddings'   (models/transformers.py)

LlavaForConditionalGeneration resolves its vision tower by arch name (CLIPVisionConfig → "CLIPVisionModel"), but clip.py only registered CLIPModel. ModelRegistry.resolve_model_cls does not raise for an unregistered arch — it silently falls back to the generic TransformersForCausalLM, which eagerly reads get_input_embeddings().num_embeddings; a CLIP tower's input embedding is a Conv2d. Fixing the registration exposed three further bugs on the llava-1.5 path that had never been reached.

## Modifications

models/clip.py
- Register CLIPVisionModel (EntryClass = [CLIPModel, CLIPVisionModel]) and give it the llava tower contract, mirroring PixtralVisionModel: forward(pixel_values, image_sizes=None, output_hidden_states=False) returning an HF-shaped CLIPVisionOutput when hidden states are requested (llava-1.5 uses vision_feature_layer=-2), self.config, and load_weights.
- CLIPVisionTransformer.forward gains output_hidden_states; the default path is unchanged.
- Move CLIPModel.load_weights body verbatim into a shared load_clip_weights().
- monkey_patch_weight_loader: add the allow_patterns_overrides parameter so the override matches DefaultModelLoader._prepare_weights — serving CLIPModel as an embedding model was crashing with a TypeError on every backend.

models/llava.py (each was masked by the previous one)
- load_weights: accept vision_feature_select_strategy == "default" (HF's spelling of "patch"; get_image_feature already treated it that way).
- _infer_image_aspect_ratio: a processor-recorded None means a plain square resize → "square", instead of falling through to "anyres" and padding to a grid the tower never produces.
- pad_input_ids: set per-item item.offsets (inclusive spans), required by general_mm_embed_routine; the legacy LlavaLlama/Qwen/Mistral classes use their own forward and were unaffected.
- get_image_feature: convert numpy pixel values from LlavaImageProcessor to a tensor before the native tower.

No device-specific branches; all changes are additive or behavior-preserving for other models.

title: [Fix] GLM: Preserve NextN PTPC quantization for excluded experts
author: lunarwhite
body:
## Motivation

With `SGLANG_GLM_NEXTN_MOE_PTPC=1`, GLM NextN adds a per-channel FP8 scheme for routed experts, but also maps checkpoint per-expert excludes into runtime names. Quark treats those leaf exclusions as excluding the fused expert module, so its quantization method is never selected even though the loader converts the expert weights to FP8.

## Modifications

Skip mapped routed-expert leaf exclusions when the existing PTPC predicate is enabled. Preserve checkpoint exclusions for loading, other runtime exclusions, flag-off behavior, and the shared-expert fusion guard. Add a regression using Quark's actual ignore predicate.

## Accuracy Tests

Using the same test file on base and patched trees:

- Existing registered PTPC suite: base reproduces the new assertion; patched passes all 12 tests without skips.
- CPU component check with real QuarkConfig and FusedMoE types: base selects no quant method with PTPC enabled; patched selects QuarkFusedMoEMethod and the per-channel FP8 scheme. The real parameter loader correctly places both experts' gate/up/down weights and scales. Flag-off and shared-expert BF16 behavior are preserved.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not measured; this fixes quantization configuration selection and makes no performance claim.

title: [Fix] [AMD] quark: Skip no-copy loads after MXFP4 quantization
author: lunarwhite
body:
## Motivation

With expert parallelism, the online Quark MXFP4 loader can receive a nonlocal expert after finishing its local weights. The underlying loader correctly copies nothing, but the wrapper compares the accumulated BF16 element count with the now-packed parameter size and raises an assertion. This affects online-quantized MoE loading, including the Qwen3.5 MTP path on ROCm.

## Modifications

Return after a zero-copy load, following weight-name validation. Local copies retain the existing completion and quantization logic. Add CPU regressions for both packed weight parameters and invalid names.

## Accuracy Tests

CPU test file: `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py` 5 passed. The two new no-copy cases fail without the fix; the invalid-name case rejects an incorrectly placed early return.

On an MI355X with real AITER quantization, compared base `9301ca37` with the three-line fix: six loading sequences and sixteen controls per version passed the expected base-failure/head-success checks. Packed weights and scales matched direct-quantization references and corresponding EP1/EP2 expert fixtures. Invalid names and duplicate local loads retained their expected errors.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: the change handles a no-copy call during weight loading; no inference-speed claim.

title: [Fix] [AMD] diffusion: Fix the first-step denoise regression from compiling ENABLE_CK=0 BF16 attention
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

**What goes wrong**
With `ENABLE_CK=0`, `AITerImpl.forward` calls `aiter.flash_attn_func` inside `torch.compile`. That dispatch opens a Triton config JSON and builds a Triton kernel Dynamo cannot reconstruct. The graph break is inside the DiT block loop, so Dynamo skips `Flux2Transformer2DModel.forward` on the first real step.

**Where it shows up**
gfx1250 already takes `AITerImpl._forward_bf16_eager`, which is `@torch.compiler.disable`, because FlyDSL's Python JIT is not traceable. gfx950 with CK enabled stays on `FlashAttnFunc` and is unchanged. The failure shows up on MI355 when the process sets `ENABLE_CK=0`, including the FLUX.2 720p run: the scored denoise's first step takes 11.8s retracing, then the rest of the steps run at 2.02 it/s. The profiled CK GEMMs and the Triton attention kernel match the previous image.

**Why #44671 did not cover it**
#44671 split the BF16 call into `_forward_bf16` (compiled) and `_forward_bf16_eager` (`@torch.compiler.disable`), and sent only `USE_AITER_GFX1250` to the eager helper. It kept gfx942/gfx950 compiled on the grounds that FlyDSL returns `None` there and the call falls through to the CK `@compile_ops` kernels, which Dynamo records as opaque graph nodes. That holds only while `ENABLE_CK=1`. With `ENABLE_CK=0`, gfx950 falls through FlyDSL into `aiter.ops.triton.attention.mha.flash_attn_func` instead, which Dynamo cannot trace, and `_forward_bf16` still calls it inside the compiled graph.

**How to fix**
Call `_forward_bf16_eager` whenever `ENABLE_CK` is off, so the untraceable Triton attention stays outside Dynamo and the rest of the compiled forward remains.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/attention/backends/aiter.py`: `AITerImpl.forward` uses the eager BF16 path when `USE_AITER_GFX1250` is true or `aiter.jit.core.ENABLE_CK` is false. `ENABLE_CK=1` on gfx950 still calls `_forward_bf16` from inside the compiled graph.
- `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_aiter_attention_impl.py`: compile `AITerImpl.forward` and assert `torch.compiler.is_compiling()` is false for gfx1250 and for `ENABLE_CK=0`, and true for the CK path.

## Accuracy Tests

The eager path calls the same `aiter.flash_attn_func` with the same arguments. The unit test checks that the compiled forward returns the attention output unchanged (`torch.testing.assert_close` against the fake kernel's `q.clone()`). No weight, scale, or kernel-config change.

`PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_aiter_attention_impl.py` — 8 passed.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Kernel time for the profiled FLUX.2 transformer forwards is not the regression. Oct 6 image total kernel time 1.512s, Oct 21 image 1.481s. The two largest CK GEMMs stay on the same tiles (`MT192x320` ~628ms, `MT256x208` ~310ms, 288 calls each).

The denoise wall gap is the first scored step. After that step the Oct 21 run holds 2.02 it/s, in line with the Oct 6 steady rate. This change removes that retrace. An after-fix end-to-end FLUX.2 number is not in this branch yet.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Fix] HiCache: bind captured KDA waits to live load events
author: hzh0425
body:
## 1. Implementation

KDA extend runs inside a breakable CUDA graph (BCG), so replay skips the Python pool accessor and its HiCache layer waits. This change captures explicit per-layer waits and binds them to the **current batch's load events** before replay.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Create completed external events per KDA layer"] --> B["Capture EventWait before Conv/SSM state reads"]
    B --> C["Retain raw graphs and identify owned wait nodes"]
    C --> D{"Before replay: load active?"}
    D -->|Yes| E["Bind waits to current slot's per-layer H2D events"]
    D -->|No| F["Bind waits to completed placeholder events"]
    E --> G["Replay with layer-wise dependencies"]
    F --> G
```

Binding uses `cudaGraphExecEventWaitNodeSetEvent`. Nodes are identified by their owned event handles; unchanged handles skip the update.

This is enabled automatically for captured KDA BCG. Other linear backends execute their waits at eager breaks. Full graphs retain their existing barrier; non-CUDA, graph dedup, and CPU/future counters use conservative waits.

## 2. GLM-5.3 Flash KL results

Tested GLM-5.3 Flash NVFP4 with two TP1 servers, MTP 2/1/3 + ReplaySSM, FlashInfer KDA prefill, HiCache, and memory fraction 0.85. The multi-turn test follows the cold-prefill logprob comparison in #44220: three groups × three branches × three turns, 512 output tokens/turn, two repeats.

Both arms start from the same token fixture and continue with their own generated histories. The **no-wait control** binds KDA waits to completed placeholders; other eager waits remain enabled. Slow loading uses `SGLANG_TEST_HICACHE_H2D_DELAY_CYCLES=50000000` per layer.

KL is a chosen-token estimate against cold-prefill scoring of the same generated tokens, with **18 final-turn samples per cell**.

| Condition | Dynamic: mean KL | No wait: mean KL | Dynamic: median KL | No wait: median KL |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Device cache hit | 0.010831 | 0.006793 | 0.000381 | 0.000436 |
| L2 load, no extra delay | 0.003277 | 0.004189 | 0.000351 | 0.000483 |
| L2 load, 50M cycles/layer | **0.007733** | **0.019290** | **0.000628** | **0.010370** |

Under slow loading, dynamic waiting reduced the observed mean KL by **59.9%** and median by **93.9%** versus no waiting.

NVFP4 samples still contain outliers. These results support reduced slow-load error, **not bit-exactness or equivalence to zero-delay loading**: the dynamic mean remains 0.007733 versus 0.003277.

title: [Fix] logits: Preserve lm_head precision with shared buffers
author: YAMY1234
body:
A matching FP32 logits buffer currently makes the ordinary FP16/BF16 lm_head produce FP32 GEMM output even when FP32 lm_head is disabled. Introduced by #45631, this skips the rounding used by the unbuffered prefill-scoring path and LoRA-wrapped heads.

Restrict the direct FP32 buffer write to heads that explicitly enable FP32. Default heads again compute in their original dtype before copying into the shared buffer. Explicit FP32 and MuseSpark's existing FP32 override retain direct buffer writes.

Add buffered/unbuffered equality coverage for FP16 and BF16, check direct writes for explicit FP32, and exercise CUDA graph replay with FP32 enabled and disabled. Low-precision test references now use the normal dtype GEMM instead of an FP64 result rounded afterward, which can differ by one output ULP. Existing tolerances are unchanged.

Related: #45846. This is intended to address the DSpark decode/prefill logprob mismatch and the contemporaneous LoRA/UNO parity failures; end-to-end confirmation is pending.

Validation:
- Changed-file Ruff, Ruff format, isort, Python compilation, and `git diff --check` pass.
- A local CPU control-flow check with emulated CUDA FP32 output reproduces the buffer-dependent rounding change before the fix and removes it afterward. This does not validate CUDA kernels or graph replay.
- GPU validation submitted for `9a9c369051`: [lm_head / RTX 5090](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39822486281) and [DSpark logprob, dynamic LoRA update, UNO parity / H100](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39822512516). Results pending; keeping this PR as a draft.

title: [Fix] ci: Reduce runner utilization scan overhead and bound API retries
author: alisonshao
body:
## Motivation

The [October 22 scheduled Runner Utilization report](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39746895425/job/119717497971) passed its unit tests but hit the 55-minute report-step timeout. The October 20 and 21 scheduled reports also timed out. Buffered stdout hid scan progress, so the exact stalled endpoint or timeout cause cannot be recovered from that log.

A sample of 1,000 run records immediately before the failed scan (October 22, 07:41:20–08:19:49 UTC) contains 233 runs selected for job fetching by the current code. Of those, 136 (58%) are PR Check Comment or PR Title: metadata workflows whose only job runs on ubuntu-latest. Their workflow_run / pull_request_target events bypass the existing short pull_request / push filter. The [last successful daily scan](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39222460273/job/117960743886) fetched 5,284 relevant runs and still exhausted retries on an HTTP 502 response.

## Modifications

- Exclude the two metadata workflows by exact workflow path, preserving GPU workflows whose PR-controlled titles mention those names and unknown workflow paths.
- Bound each `gh api` subprocess to 30 seconds and each endpoint's aggregate retry loop to 120 seconds. Keep transient-error retries, clip backoff to the remaining budget, and report the actual attempt count.
- Stream report progress with `python -u` and log retry endpoints/errors immediately.
- Include the report test file in the workflow's PR path filter.

The report's scan window, GPU job accounting, and existing incomplete-fetch handling are unchanged. This reduces measured redundant requests and bounds individual stalls; it does not establish that the full scheduled scan will finish within 55 minutes.

## Accuracy Tests

- Python 3.12: `python -m unittest discover -s scripts/ci/utils -p 'test_runner_utilization_report.py' -v` — 31 passed.
- Added regressions for metadata exclusion through collection, GPU title collisions, unknown paths, successful requests, permanent errors, transient recovery, hung requests, aggregate retry deadlines, and no sleep after the final attempt.
- All applicable repository pre-commit hooks passed, including formatting, import order, YAML/AST checks, and workflow job-name validation.
- Independent code review completed with no blocking findings.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No inference code changes. The full production scan has not been rerun; the 58% reduction is an observation from the bounded historical sample, not a claimed end-to-end runtime improvement.

Prepared for review. **Do not merge yet.**

title: [Fix] prefill-graph: Keep every DP rank eager when the replay tail captures behind rank barriers
author: hnyls2002
body:
- With DP attention and MegaMoE, `PrefillCudaGraphRunner._has_inactive_dp_rank` lets a rank replay the prefill graph while ranks with no tokens run an eager idle forward, when `prefill_graph_tolerates_sum_len()` holds. That is safe only if nothing in the captured graph's breaks waits on other ranks.
- The DeepSeek-V4.1 decoder replay tail captures its row-bucket graphs on first use, behind TP-group barriers. In a step where only some ranks have tokens (for example the first step after start, or lone requests), the replaying rank blocks in that barrier, the idle ranks return to the scheduler, and their MegaMoE kernels wait for it: the server stops making progress (DeepGEMM grid sync timeout, then the scheduler watchdog).
- The per_rank Engram host-table layout never hit this because its lookup records a DP gather at capture, which already forces every rank to eager in such steps; the shared layout (the default) has no collective, so it did.
- Fix: while the prefill graphs capture, the replay tail calls `note_rank_barrier_in_prefill_graph()`, which latches `DpFlags.prefill_graph_has_rank_barrier` the way the DP gather helpers latch `prefill_graph_has_dp_gather`. `_has_inactive_dp_rank` keeps tolerating an idle rank only when it is unset. The decision reads `global_num_tokens_cpu`, which is the same on every DP rank, so all ranks take the same path. No new server flag.

No behavior change for steps where every DP rank has tokens, or for configs whose prefill graph has no such break.

Verification: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash DEP4 with the shared Engram host table and the breakable prefill graph hung before the first prefill on unmodified main and serves with this change (lone requests and GSM8K pass); throughput of the per_rank layout and of steps with every rank active is unchanged; `test_prefill_cuda_graph_padding.py` passes.

title: [Fix] InstantTensor: return load-time GPU memory to the KV cache
author: Hrithvik-Alex
body:
## Motivation

With `--load-format instanttensor` (#40453), GPU memory after weight loading is higher than with the default loader, and the KV cache shrinks by the difference. On GLM-5.3 NVFP4, TP4 on B200, "Load weight end" mem usage was 108.89 GB against 106.88 GB for the default loader. That cost 812k KV tokens against 836k.

There are two causes:

1. **A lazily created NCCL communicator.** InstantTensor all-gathers over `get_parallel().world_group.device_group`. SGLang never otherwise runs a collective on that group (its world-group uses are CPU-group object collectives and barriers), so the loader's first all-gather creates its NCCL communicator. That communicator's buffers then stay resident for the life of the process: 0.77 GB/GPU on H100 TP4 without NVLS, and more with NVLS.
2. **Allocator fragmentation from the clones.** `copy=True` clones every tensor, unsharded, through the shared caching allocator. Long-lived allocations made during and after loading (e.g. `post_load_weights`' `w_kc`/`w_vc`) are carved out of the freed blocks of the largest clone (the 1.8 GB embedding for GLM-5 dimensions). `empty_cache()` then can't return that segment: 1.74 GB/GPU in a synthetic run.

## Modifications

`instanttensor_weights_iterator`:
- When loading over the world group (the default load group), it creates a temporary NCCL group spanning the world, passes it to InstantTensor, and destroys it when iteration ends. Other load groups, such as a PP stage's TP group, keep using their own device group, since `new_group` must be called by every rank.
- It pulls each tensor from InstantTensor inside `torch.cuda.use_mem_pool` with a private `MemPool`, so only the clones use it, and the pool's segments are freed once the consumer drops the last tensor. It falls back to the shared allocator when `use_mem_pool` is missing or CUDA is unavailable.

`test_instanttensor_loader.py`: the existing world-group test now expects the temporary group as InstantTensor's `process_group`, with `new_group` / `destroy_process_group` mocked. That's the only test change; no new tests.

## Accuracy / memory results

| GLM-5.3 NVFP4 TP4 + MTP, B200 | default loader | instanttensor before | instanttensor after |
|---|---|---|---|
| target mem usage after load | 106.88 GB | 108.89 GB | 106.76 GB |
| KV tokens | 836,352 | 812,544 | 835,648 |
| target load time | 91.7 s | 28.8 s | 31.3 s |

The fix costs about 0.5 s to destroy the communicator, plus a new communicator (~0.5 s) for a second load in the same process, such as the MTP draft. The pool switch costs ~3 µs per tensor.

H100 TP4, synthetic DeepSeek-V3-architecture checkpoint with GLM-5 dimensions:

| | mem usage | KV tokens |
|---|---|---|
| default loader | 9.459 GB | 6.114M |
| instanttensor before | 10.549 GB | 5.982M |
| instanttensor after | 9.434 GB | 6.117M |

Two consecutive loads over the default (world) load group, the target + draft pattern: tensors are byte-identical to safetensors, and GPU memory returns to baseline after each load (+2.28 GB before the fix).

End-to-end accuracy with this change (GLM-5.3 NVFP4 TP4 + MTP on B200, `--load-format instanttensor`): GSM8K (300, temp 0) 99.0% / 98.7% over two runs; IFEval (n=150) 0.88, against a reference of 0.85–0.87 from production serving with the default loader.

## Checklist
- [x] `test/registered/unit/model_loader/test_instanttensor_loader.py`: 9 passed (CPU, as registered) against current main (d67d1ae02c).
- [x] 2-GPU check on current main, default load path: 0 mismatches against safetensors, temporary group destroyed, memory back to baseline.
- [x] ruff check passes on the touched files.

title: [Fix] moe: Broadcast scalar block scales correctly with swap_ab on Triton 3.9
author: janbernloehr
body:
## Motivation

Fixes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/45887.

On SM90, block-FP8 MoE can select `swap_ab` while the weight scale is rank 0 (`BLOCK_SIZE_N <= group_n`). Swapping the operands also swaps their scales, so the current expression slices a scalar as `a_scale[:, None]`. Triton 3.9 rejects this after [triton-lang/triton#10429](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/10429), causing DeepSeek-R1 FP8 startup to fail during prefill CUDA graph capture.

## Modifications

- Add the scalar-scale `swap_ab` case: multiply the scalar weight scale by `b_scale[None, :]`, placing the per-token scales along the transposed dot product's last axis.
- Add a numerical regression test covering swapped and unswapped operands with `BLOCK_SIZE_N=64,128,256` and `group_n=128`. Nonuniform activation/weight scales, two K groups, permuted tokens, padding and routed weights check the output against independently dequantized PyTorch matmul.

## Accuracy Tests

The current kernel's six regression configurations were checked against the PyTorch reference through Triton's CPU interpreter on 3.8.0 and the 3.9 nightly build `3.9.0+gitfc8d31a5`, using FP8 inputs and FP32 outputs (`rtol=2e-4`, `atol=2e-4`). Offline compilation for SM90 with that 3.9 nightly passes all six patched cases. The unpatched upstream kernel fails exactly the two scalar-scale cases (`swap_ab=True`, `BLOCK_SIZE_N=64,128`) with `too many indices for tensor of rank 0`; the four other cases compile. This is kernel numerical and compiler validation; no full-model accuracy evaluation was run. The registered CUDA test has not been executed on a GPU in this chat.

Existing validation of the same arithmetic change on SGLang `c1c287a42` ran DeepSeek-R1 FP8 on 2×8 H100 80GB, TP16, with DP attention off and default MoE/CUDA graph settings. The unmodified server failed on Triton `3.9.0+gitaad2a60d`; the patched server started and served. That run predates this branch and does not validate every subsequent upstream change or the new test's GPU execution.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Existing paired serving measurements used the same public base-image digest, SGLang `c1c287a42`, checkpoint and launch flags. Benchmark: 8,000 input / 1,000 output tokens; one run per arm. Output throughput:

| Concurrency | Unpatched, Triton 3.8.0 | Patched, Triton 3.9.0+gitaad2a60d |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 76.24 tok/s | 75.62 tok/s |
| 64 | 734.19 tok/s | 737.21 tok/s |
| 256 | 753.10 tok/s | 755.11 tok/s |

Differences range from −0.81% to +0.41%; a single run per arm is not enough to establish a performance improvement. No profiling trace was collected. H200/H20, other models and DP attention were not run end to end.

title: [Fix] engram: let the hasher take idle DP-attention batches
author: yueming-yuan
body:
## Summary

Under attention DP, a rank with no requests can reach `EngramHasher.forward` with padded rows and an `IDLE` forward mode, and the hasher's mode assert kills that rank's scheduler. This brings Jiajun's fix (`7e74b31b26`, on `jiajun/dsv41-h200-rl`, never merged into `sglang-miles`) onto current `sglang-miles`.

## Problem

- In a decode step under attention DP, `DpPaddingMode.get_dp_padding_mode` (`layers/dp_attention.py`) picks `MAX_LEN` when `sum_len * 2 >= max_len * gather_width`. A rank with no requests is then padded to `max_len` rows but keeps `ForwardMode.IDLE`.
- `EngramHasher.forward` (`layers/engram.py`) handles extend, target-verify and decode, and otherwise asserts: `engram serves extend, target-verify and decode, not 4`.
- Seen on a 24-GPU DeepSeek-V4.1 engine (TP 24, attention DP 24, EP 24) a few minutes into an RL rollout, when one rank was momentarily empty.

## Fix

Every row of an idle batch is padding, so the hasher returns zero hash ids for all `num_tokens` rows and commits no history. The rows still join the DP lookup's gather and reduce-scatter; zero is the padding id the context-parallel path already uses.

`sglang-miles` has since added the extend fast path (`engram_hash_extend_and_commit`) at the same spot; the idle check goes before it.

## Validation

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash LoRA RL ran with this commit in the engine and no engram assert: the 4-layer slice on 8×H200 with `--sglang-attn-dp-size 8`, and the full model on 2×8 H200 with a 16-GPU attention-DP engine.
- Not reproduced: no run went without the commit, and none of those runs shows whether an idle `MAX_LEN` batch occurred, so they do not demonstrate the original failure.

title: [Fix] rust-server: Deliver scheduler-side aborts to Rust frontend clients
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

The scheduler ends some requests outside the output stream:

- aborted while queued (`/abort_request`, `SGLANG_REQ_WAITING_TIMEOUT`);
- evicted or rejected by priority scheduling (`--max-queued-requests`, priority disabled);
- aborted on retraction when the KV pool is full;
- aborted while chunked, or in the PD decode retracted queue.

It reports each one as an `AbortReq` on the ZMQ tokenizer socket, and Python's `TokenizerManager` turns that into the request's final frame (`_handle_abort_req`). In Rust mode nothing reads that socket, so these clients never got a terminal frame: a stream hung until the client gave up, and a unary request never received its status.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`: the nine abort sites now go through a new `Scheduler.send_abort_output`, the counterpart of `send_control_output`. With a Rust server it calls `rust_server.push_abort`; otherwise it sends the `AbortReq` to the tokenizer socket as before. Python mode is unchanged.
- `python/sglang/srt/rust_server/server.py`: `RustServer.push_abort` pushes a one-request terminal batch to the Rust egress with the abort finish reason (the scheduler's, or Python's `"Abort in waiting queue"` default) and no new tokens. The Rust frontend renders it like any abort finish: a final stream frame, or the finish's status code for a unary request, as Python does. The batch carries the request's own prompt, cached and reasoning token counts, so it does not reset what the stream already reported.
- Tests: `test_rust_server_extension.py` gains `test_scheduler_aborts_reach_the_rust_egress` (in Rust mode the abort becomes the one-row batch with the request's counts; without the Rust server it still goes to the tokenizer socket). Scheduler unit tests that build a scheduler with `Scheduler.__new__` or a `SimpleNamespace` now set `rust_server = None`, which every real scheduler sets in `maybe_init_rust_server`, or fake `send_abort_output` directly (`test_weight_versions.py`).

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no model or numerics change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: the abort path only; the per-token output path is untouched.

## Test plan

- `pytest test/registered/unit/multimodal/rust/shared/test_rust_server_extension.py test/registered/unit/utils/test_weight_versions.py test/registered/unit/dllm/test_gemma4_uniform_lifecycle.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_multimodal_abort_cleanup.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_priority_scheduling_disaggregation.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_chunked_abort_race.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_pause_generation.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_timeouts.py` on CPU: 134 passed, 47 subtests passed.
- Swept `test/` for every other test that sets `ipc_channels` on a scheduler fixture (`test_scheduler_flush_cache.py`, `test_scheduler_health_check_signal.py`): both already set `rust_server`, so no other fixture reaches `send_abort_output` without it.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks passed.
- `rust/`: unchanged; the Rust side already renders an abort finish reason from a decode result batch.
- Not run here: a live Rust-mode server. A manual check would start a Rust-mode and a Python-mode server with `--max-running-requests 1` and `SGLANG_REQ_WAITING_TIMEOUT=3`, hold the slot with a long stream, and confirm that a unary request queued behind it gets a 503 and a streaming request cancelled with `/abort_request` ends with an abort `finish_reason` and `[DONE]` in both modes.

title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] jit: Build sm_100f on CC 10.7 until the bundled CUTLASS supports SM107
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

On CC 10.7 devices, SGLang JIT kernels are built for `sm_107a`, but they include FlashInfer's bundled CUTLASS (`flashinfer/data/cutlass`, 4.5.0). That CUTLASS has no SM107 support (`struct Sm107` and the `CUTLASS_ARCH_MMA_SM107A_ENABLED` gates arrive in CUTLASS 4.8). Against it, an `sm_107a` build compiles cleanly but loses features:

- `CUTE_ARCH_TMA_SM90_ENABLED` is undefined, so every cute TMA copy compiles to `CUTE_INVALID_CONTROL_PATH` and asserts at runtime.
- `CUDA_CTA_RECONFIG_ACTIVATED` is off, so `warpgroup_reg_alloc/dealloc` (`setmaxnreg`) become no-ops.

This is reachable today. DeepSeek-V4.1 with DP attention and `--dsv4-attn-backend trtllm` runs the DeepSelect top-k JIT kernels. On a CC 10.7 device, the first request fails with:

```
cute/arch/copy_sm90_tma.hpp:189: static void cute::SM90_TMA_LOAD_3D::copy(...): Assertion `0 && "Trying to use tma without CUTE_ARCH_TMA_SM90_ENABLED."` failed.
```

FlashInfer handles the same situation for its own JIT kernels: `flashinfer.compilation_context.cutlass_supports_sm107()` checks its bundled CUTLASS for `struct Sm107`, and builds the `sm_100f` family target when it is missing.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/kernels/jit/utils/arch.py`: on CC 10.7, when FlashInfer's `cutlass_supports_sm107()` (present in the pinned 0.7.2) is false, the JIT target becomes `10.0f`. The import stays inside the CUDA 10.7 branch, because ROCm and MUSA installs don't provide that function. This gives `-gencode=arch=compute_100f,code=sm_100f` and `SGL_CUDA_ARCH=1000`, so the binary and the arch macro the kernels branch on stay consistent. The `sm_100f` family binary runs on SM107.

Every other architecture is unchanged. On 10.7, the JIT goes back to `sm_107a` automatically once FlashInfer bundles a CUTLASS that declares `Sm107`. The JIT cache key includes the target, so stale `sm_107a` builds are not reused.

## Accuracy Tests

On a CC 10.7 device: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4 / DP4 / EP4 with DP attention, `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe`, `--dsv4-attn-backend trtllm` and DSpark. GSM8K (200 questions, `sglang.test.run_eval`):

- Before: the DeepSelect top-k kernels assert on the first request and the server dies.
- After: 0.985. The JIT cache shows the DeepSelect builds targeting `sm_100f`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speed claim. This trades an `sm_107a` build with TMA and `setmaxnreg` compiled out for a working `sm_100f` build.

title: [Fix] deepseek-v4: Preserve decoder-tail token-count ownership
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #45681
* #45917
* #45462
* #45916
* __->__ #45915

## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4 decoder-tail graphs need the current live token prefix on every replay. A row graph previously owned only the LOCAL count, so a distinct GLOBAL MoE count could not safely follow changing replay sizes. This prevented capture of supported attention-TP-sharded tails; borrowing the parent counter would instead leave captured kernels reading another batch's state.

This change gives each opted-in graph its own LOCAL and GLOBAL count views. Replay updates both while preserving the parent batch's counters and the existing default row-runner behavior.

## Changes

- Pass the gathered tail's live row count from `DecoderReplayTail.run` to `RowBucketGraphRunner`.
- Derive the LOCAL count for the captured TP bucket and keep the GLOBAL prefix in its own graph-owned view.
- Pack both int32 counts into one int64 allocation and update them with one fill, preserving the single-allocation/single-update structure.
- Separate graph cache entries by count domains and attention-TP sharding. Custom MoE bounds without a supported owner continue to decline capture.

## Review order

1. `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4_replay_tail.py`: capture admission and the gathered GLOBAL prefix.
2. `python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/row_bucket_graph_runner.py`: count storage, localization, cache identity and replay updates.
3. `test_num_token_non_padded_localization.py` and `test_decoder_tail_moe_bound.py`: domain selection, parent-storage preservation and changing-prefix replay.

## Validation

Based on main `25ad569ff9`. Checks ran on the integrated source `f3a116529a`; all four implementation/test files match this PR's `f3d331d859` exactly.

- The complete 13-test localization unit file passed within a combined 181-test CPU suite.
- On **1× NVIDIA B300, SM10.3, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130**, the two CUDA counter-ownership tests and two virtual-rank subtests passed. They execute real captures/replays across buckets, changing and idle prefixes, scalar/vector counter shapes, and unchanged parent pointers/values.
- The CUDA fixture executes production batch-copy, allocation, fill, cache and tail-run paths. Decoder-layer math and distributed recording are substituted.
- Normal configured pre-commit hooks passed.

Full-model attention, real multi-rank collectives and serving performance were not tested. These checks establish count ownership and CUDA replay behavior, not a whole-stack performance result. Eager CPU submission overhead is outside the performance scope.

## Rebase validation

This five-PR stack was rebased without conflicts onto main `8b9f72417f`. All five patches retain their stable patch IDs relative to the preceding published stack; the newer main commits do not touch the stack's changed files. The existing removal of the unused `materialized_routing` parameter and its three call-site arguments in #45917 is preserved.

Each rebased PR commit passed its configured pre-commit checks independently. The final stack passes `git diff --check`, and all 72 changed Python files parse successfully. CPU test suites, native GPU tests and performance measurements were not rerun for this rebase. Previously reported results, including those at integrated `e6670af1ad`, remain evidence for those earlier revisions with their stated limits.

## CPU CI follow-up

Run [39935811691](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39935811691) exposed an upstream Flux2 import test registered in the CPU suite, whose environment lacks the diffusion dependencies. The import chain also queries the active GPU. #45915 moves that check to the existing CUDA diffusion unit suite, which installs those dependencies, while retaining its XPU registration and the real subprocess check that blocks Intel Triton imports. This registration fix is propagated through the stack.

The Flux2 import check passes on 1× NVIDIA B300 with PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0 and Diffusers 0.37.0; its five Intel-XPU numerical cases are skipped on CUDA and were not rerun on XPU. Full integrated registry collection validates 2,535 files / 3,077 registrations, including the enabled diffusion/XPU selections and the preceding GGUF MUSA fix. Configured checks pass for the changed files. Only three test files change across this follow-up; production code is unchanged. A fresh full CI result is not claimed.

## Merge preparation

Rebased this component onto main `9d7ad308bd` for squash merge. Resolved the overlap with #46040 by keeping the CPU registration removed and retaining the diffusion CUDA import regression alongside its XPU registration. No test suites or performance measurements were rerun for this merge. Earlier validation sections describe their named revisions.

title: [Fix] gguf: Preserve MoE routing, weighting and allocation budgets
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #45681
* #45917
* #45462
* __->__ #45916
* #45915

## Motivation

GGUF MoE must discard padded and nonlocal routes without consuming their expert outputs or NaN scores. Preparing safe IDs and clearing intermediate tensors on every call adds allocations and launches, while an unguarded native projection can form a weight address from a negative ID.

This PR moves CUDA vector-route safety into a local native consumer, shares its format math with the AOT implementation, and preserves per-slot product rounding before the existing MoE reduction. It also restores lazy fallback accumulation and repairs the shared native MMQ bounds/scale indexing.

## Changes

- CUDA MMVQ uses a local JIT entry with negative-ID checks before expert-address formation. Ordinary contiguous int32 routes retain their storage; exceptional layouts/widths normalize explicitly. The quantize/project structure and zeroed projection output remain intact.
- CUDA weighting excludes inactive outputs and scores inside its product kernel, removing activation-sized input copies and separate intermediate clears. Products still round to the output dtype before native `moe_sum`.
- Shared native GGUF code checks MMQ slack bounds before access and indexes Q8_1 scales with the same routed row as the values. Rebuilt MUSA providers can use the native in-place weighting operator; older providers retain their compatibility path.
- The slow fallback adopts the first valid expert result, adds later contributions in order, and zeros the existing final row only when all routes are inactive.
- A local non-flushing FP32 multiply preserves subnormal operands/results and signed zero in CUDA weighting, including SM90 fast-math builds. MUSA multiplication and the reducer are unchanged.
- Shared GGUF headers have one AOT source owner, with JIT forwarding links. Source-distribution staging materializes those headers so the runtime package remains self-contained.

## Review order

1. `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/gguf.py`: vector/MMQ/fallback selection, private-buffer lifetimes and final weighting/reduction.
2. `kernels/ops/moe/gguf_moe_vec.py`, `jit/csrc/moe/gguf_moe_vec.cuh` and the shared GGUF headers: preserved format math and negative-ID access guards.
3. `aot/csrc/moe/moe_sum.cu`, `gguf_moe_weights.cuh` and the weighting wrappers: validation, rounding and device registration.
4. `test_gguf_inactive_routes.py`, `test_gguf_moe_weights.py`, then `python/setup.py` for standalone header packaging.

- Define unused CUDA MMQ expert-map capacity in the existing alignment producer. This removes the per-call arange, multiply, comparison and masked-fill sequence while retaining the released provider and buffer sizes.

Full before/after discovery validates 2,535 files and 3,077 registrations, with every moved file selected in its enabled destination suite. Configured hooks pass; native tests were not rerun for this registration-only update.

This is a comparison to the reviewed stack; earlier original-main controls below retain their separate baseline and limitations.

The GGUF native-entry suite passes 7 tests on B300 with sglang-kernel 0.4.10. H200 uses PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 for the source-local JIT producer; this is not full native H200 GGUF admission.

Based on #45915 above main `25ad569ff9`. Blackwell checks ran on integrated source `f3a116529a`; the GGUF runtime, production weighting TU/header and registered kernel test match this PR's `b80e51a006` exactly.

title: [Fix] moe: Preserve CUTLASS routing metadata and execution budgets
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #45681
* __->__ #45917
* #45462
* #45916
* #45915

## Motivation

CUTLASS routing must define every permutation entry when routes are negative or nonlocal. Clearing maps, preparing activation-sized copies and materializing rounded scores separately adds work even when all routes are valid. The effective FP8 backend also needs to reach TopK and dispatch before they choose route layout and token-count ownership.

## Changes

- Publish the effective FP8 routing policy before TopK/dispatch, preserving raw signed IDs and the correct local token bound for native FP8/W4A8 consumers.
- Share one complete CUDA route producer between FP8 and W4A8. It writes invalid output-map entries as `-1`, unused input-map capacity as token zero, and the appropriate grouped-GEMM M/N layout. One CTA owns each expert cursor; no separate expert cursor allocation or clear is needed. Non-CUDA and DeepEP paths retain their existing producers.
- Reuse W4A8's existing maps, normalize exceptional ID layouts once, and mask dynamic scale loads before reading inactive rows. Valid inputs avoid the previous activation/ID copies.
- Use a native checked weighted reduction that excludes inactive payloads and NaN scores before access. The FP8 caller opts into the original score-to-output-dtype rounding before FP32 slot-order accumulation. Cached backend/type admission, strided-score support, the Triton fallback, current-stream execution and compile/fake behavior are retained.

- Complete the routing-policy interface for all four plain MXFP4 adapters without changing their inheritance or loading lifecycle. Derive native block-FP8 cardinality from materialized routes, including deferred finalize; widen FP16 scores to FP32 in one copy and preserve supported score storage. Keep Llama4's native per-tensor scaling convention after materialization.

## CI cadence

The mapped shuffle/reduction microbenchmark now runs in `nightly-test-1-gpu-large`. FP8 and W4A8 correctness, map-completion and graph replay tests remain in base CI.

- 1× NVIDIA H200 full native W4A8 comparisons at `d1990d57` cover M32/512 with E2 and M512 with E128, static/dynamic scales, strict `rtol=0.01, atol=0.001` checks, output bits and graph replay. title: [Fix] weight_checker: Make the checksum device-agnostic
author: HJSang
body:
Upstream of sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu#1578.

`/weights_checker` with `action="checksum"` calls `torch.cuda.synchronize()` around the checksum, so the action fails on every non-CUDA engine. That includes CPU, NPU, XPU and MPS, as well as out-of-tree platforms such as TPU, whose engines RL trainers (e.g. miles) checksum after each weight update.

This replaces both calls with `current_platform.synchronize()`, the existing per-platform hook:
- CUDA and ROCm keep calling `torch.cuda.synchronize()`, so their behavior is unchanged.
- CPU calls `torch.cpu.synchronize()`.
- Each other platform uses its own hook, or the no-op default.

The hashing already handles non-CUDA tensors through the host sha256 fallback.

Not changed: the `compare` action is still CUDA-only, since `weight_checker_comparator.py` calls `.cuda()`.

## Tests
- New `test/registered/unit/utils/test_weight_checker_cpu.py` (CPU suite): runs `checksum` with `torch.cuda.synchronize` patched to raise. With GPUs hidden, it fails on `main` and passes with this change.
- The existing `test_weight_checker.py` and `test_weight_checker_comparator.py` still pass on H200: 75 passed both before and after.
- The same change is merged in sglang-torchtpu and exercised on TPU v7x engines.

title: [Fix] disaggregation: Restart a lost prefill's heartbeat miss count
author: pengwu22
body:
## Motivation

The decode-side heartbeat checker in `CommonKVManager` drops a prefill after `max_failures` consecutive missed `/health` probes. `_handle_node_failure` then removes the prefill's connections, its `prefill_info_table` entry and its room tracking, but leaves `heartbeat_failures[addr]` at `max_failures`.

A later request that reaches the same prefill registers it again, and the checker probes it again. If the first probe after the reconnect succeeds, the count resets. If it misses, for example because the prefill is busy for a few seconds, the count becomes `max_failures + 1` and the prefill is dropped again at once. Every request in flight to it then fails. A prefill that is reached again should need `max_failures` misses before it is dropped, like any other prefill.

## Modifications

- `_handle_node_failure` also removes `heartbeat_failures[addr]`, together with the rest of the prefill's state.
- Tests in `test_nixl_backend_basic.py` (CPU):
  - The existing node-failure test now also checks that the failed prefill's count is removed and the other prefill's count is kept.
  - A new test runs the heartbeat thread through miss, miss (drop), reconnect, miss, success, miss, success. With this change the prefill is dropped once. On main it is dropped twice.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: this only changes failure handling.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

title: [Fix] scheduler: Make a Req's "__req__" self-reference weak
author: pengwu22
body:
## Motivation

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43181 stopped injecting `"__req__"` into `custom_params` for requests that have no custom logit processor. A request that does have one, such as a thinking-budget, DeepSeek-OCR no-repeat-ngram, LocateAnything box-grammar or user-supplied processor, still stores a strong reference to itself in its own `custom_params`:

```
req -> sampling_params -> custom_params["__req__"] -> req
```

Refcounting never frees such a request after it finishes. It stays alive, with its input and output token lists, until the cyclic garbage collector reaches it, and it adds work to every collection until then. On servers that tune or freeze the collector, these requests can build up.

## Modifications

- `Req.__init__` stores `weakref.proxy(self)` under `"__req__"`. The in-tree processors read `"__req__"` only while the request is running, and never hash, pickle or keep it, so they see the same attributes as before.
- Tests in `test_req_custom_params_ref.py` (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`):
  - With `gc` disabled, a `Req` that has a custom logit processor is freed when its last reference is dropped. This test fails on main.
  - `Qwen3ThinkingBudgetLogitProcessor` reads the request through the proxy and forces the newline once the budget is spent.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: processors receive the same values, and model outputs do not change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: the only hot-path change is one `weakref.proxy` call per request that has a custom logit processor.

title: [Fix] diffusion/ltx: Keep tiled VAE decode off the sharded convs under parallel decode
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

With more than one decode rank (CFG parallel, TP or SP), the LTX VAE installs spatially sharded convs that exchange halo rows with the neighbouring rank. Those convs expect each rank to hold its own height split. But:
- `_decode` checked tiling before the sharded path;
- `tiled_decode`, `_temporal_tiled_decode` and `decode_chunk` called the decoder on whole tensors while the sharded convs were installed.

So each rank blended its neighbour's copy of the same tile into its own edge rows.

Decoding a real LTX-2 latent (768x512x121) on 2xH200, with 2 decode ranks compared against 1:
- main: rank 0's max error is 135/149 levels, and 36.9%/41.7% of the pixels in the bottom 32 rows are off by more than 2 levels. Rank 1 mirrors this at the top.
- this PR: both ranks are identical, at 58.2–58.5 dB against the 1-rank untiled decode (bf16 noise).

This affects the LTX-2, LTX-2.3 and LTX-2.5 conv VAE on multiple GPUs with default flags, and SANA-WM's streaming `decode_chunk`. The Wan and Hunyuan VAEs are not affected.

## Modifications

`ltx_2_vae.py`: every decoder call now either runs on this rank's height split or bypasses the sharded convs (new `_decode_spatial`).
- With tiling on, the height split replaces tiling when each rank's rows fit in one tile. A rank therefore still decodes at most one tile's area at once.
- Otherwise every rank tiles the whole clip under `disable_spatial_parallel_decode()`, exactly as on one rank. Large frames keep per-rank tiling because at 1920x1088 the untiled sharded path costs 28–38 GB more per rank.
- Framewise decoding applies the same rule to each temporal tile, and the streaming `decode_chunk` bypasses the sharded convs.

`pipeline_configs/base.py`: drop the "vae_sp requires vae_tiling" check. `vae_sp` gates nothing at runtime, and the height split never uses tiles, so `--vae-tiling false` now works on its own.

New test `test/unit/test_ltx_vae_parallel_decode.py`: two gloo ranks on CPU decode a tiny LTX-2 VAE with sharded convs and compare against one rank on 5 paths:
- tiled, below the auto threshold;
- tiled with `spatial_shard`;
- height split;
- framewise;
- `decode_chunk`.

Follow-up, not fixed here: the diffusers 2D VAE has the same ordering bug, but only with tiling plus the opt-in `--vae-config.parallel-decode-mode spatial_shard`.

## Accuracy Tests

- Real LTX-2 VAE on 2xH200: see Motivation. Both ranks now decode identically, at 58.2–58.5 dB against one rank.
- `test_ltx_vae_parallel_decode.py`: main fails on all 5 paths, with max abs error 1.00–1.24 across the two ranks. This PR matches one rank exactly (0.0).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

LTX-2 on 2xH200. On main, the halo traffic on whole tiles made the tiled decode slower than on one rank.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| VAE only, 768x512 | 0.342 s | 0.135 s (1-rank tiled: 0.265 s) |
| pipeline decode stage, 768x512 | 0.665 s | 0.418 s |
| decode, 1920x1088 | 3.63 s, peak 82.4 GB | 3.07 s, peak 79.9 GB |

At 768x512, e2e is −4.7% / −2.8% over two interleaved rounds, and memory is 1.7 GB lower per rank.

title: [Fix] diffusion: Keep dynamic LoRA deltas on fused linear-GELU sites
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

`FUSED_LINEAR_GELU` is in the `"lossless"` tier, and `quality` has defaulted to `"lossless"` since #42370, so the fused linear+GELU epilogue mounts by default. With a dynamic (unmerged) LoRA, the site's linear is a `BaseLayerWithLoRA`. Its `.weight` and `.bias` forward to the base layer, and it passed every duck-typed guard. So `fused_linear_gelu_tanh(x, proj_in.weight, proj_in.bias)` multiplied the base weight only and silently dropped the adapter's delta.

This affects every GELU site that serves a dynamic LoRA:
- LTX-2 two-stage, stage 2, always: the distilled LoRA is applied dynamically on 1370 layers;
- LTX-2.3 in `original` device mode, which is the default on H100/A100;
- dynamic LoRA serving on Wan, FLUX, HunyuanVideo, GLM-Image, Qwen-Image and LongCat.

CI did not catch it:
- #42370 pinned every consistency-checked case to `quality="exact"`;
- the site unit tests used plain `nn.Linear`;
- nightly does run LTX-2.3 TI2V at the default tier with a dynamic LoRA on H100, but it measures latency only;
- the Wan2.2-A14B LoRA case uses layerwise offload, so the fusion never mounted.

## Modifications

`fused_linear_gelu_site.py`:
- `can_use_linear_gelu` takes the module forward while a LoRA wrapper adds output (`lora_active`). A disabled adapter, or a merged one without an output offset, keeps the fused path, because the base weight the epilogue reads already holds the update.
- The mount-time guard judges a LoRA wrapper by the layer it wraps. Before, the wrapper hid that layer's quantization, `skip_bias_add` and multi-rank `gather_output`.
- The module docstring still said the path mounts only for `quality="high"`. It now describes the lossless tier.

Tests:
- `test/unit/test_quality_fusion_lora.py`: every fusion in `_QUALITY_FUSION_HANDLERS` either runs on a site whose linears carry a dynamic adapter, or is listed with the reason it cannot drop an adapter's output. So a new fusion has to pick a side. On a site, the mounted output must equal the unfused forward and differ from the base weight alone. The file also pins the per-call guard to the adapter state and the static guard to the wrapped layer.
- New 1-GPU server case `wan2_1_t2v_1_3b_dynamic_lora_default_quality_1gpu`: Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B serves the Arcane-Jinx adapter unmerged, at 480x272, 9 frames, 8 steps. The adapter carries `ffn.0` (= `ffn.fc_in`) LoRA weights on all 30 blocks. The case needs no golden: the default-quality output must match a `quality="exact"` request to the same server, and differ from a request with the adapter off. Two `DiffusionTestCase` fields express these checks for any case: `reference_quality` and `run_lora_effect_check`.
- The case runs in the NVIDIA 1-GPU PR suite. It is skipped on AMD, whose PR lane parametrizes the same case list, because its thresholds are calibrated on NVIDIA only.
- The case's baseline is intentionally absent from `perf_baselines/h100.json`. Its first CI run fails and prints the block to add (the usual two-step seeding).

This PR and "[Fix] diffusion: Keep the linear-GELU verdict cache out of torch.compile traces" both edit `can_use_linear_gelu`. They merge cleanly in either order. The adapter check sits above that PR's compile branch, so it also applies while tracing; keep that order if either one is rebased.

## Accuracy Tests

**LTX-2 two-stage** on 2xH200, against a stage-2-only exact reference: stage 1 runs at `lossless` and stage 2 is forced to `exact`. Stage-1 latents are bitwise identical across arms.

| | PSNR vs reference | high-frequency energy vs reference |
|---|---|---|
| main | 23.4–24.0 dB | 13–15% lower (blurrier) |
| this PR | 31.3–34.1 dB | within 1% |

`quality="exact"` output is bitwise unchanged.

**New server case** on H200, per key frame. The case passes at mean_abs_diff ≤ 3.0 and PSNR ≥ 30 dB against `quality="exact"`, and mean_abs_diff ≥ 12.0 against LoRA off.

| | vs `quality="exact"` | vs LoRA off | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| this PR | mean_abs_diff 0.73 / 1.41 / 1.55, PSNR 45.9 / 42.1 / 41.3 dB | mean_abs_diff 15.0–16.2 | pass |
| this PR with only the guard reverted to main | mean_abs_diff 8.35–8.75, PSNR 25.7–26.6 dB | mean_abs_diff 9.1–12.6 | fail |

The case takes 79–88 s on H200 (also re-run on this branch merged with the compile-guard PR: same numbers, pass).

**Unit tests**: `test_quality_fusion_lora.py` 5/5 pass on GPU. On main, `test_linear_gelu_static_guard_reads_the_wrapped_layer` fails: the wrapper hides `gather_output` on a TP2 layer.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Only requests with an active dynamic LoRA change path: their GELU sites run unfused. LTX-2 two-stage e2e on 2xH200 went from 7.34 s to 7.51 s. Requests without a LoRA, or with a merged one, keep the fused epilogue.

title: [Fix] diffusion: Keep the linear-GELU verdict cache out of torch.compile traces
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

#44643 caches the fused linear-GELU verdict per linear in a module-level `WeakKeyDictionary`, `_VERDICTS`. Under `torch.compile`, dynamo guards on that dict's size. DiT blocks share one compiled forward, so every new linear a block brings changes the size and recompiles the frame. On 4xB300, an LTX-2 compile run logged this on both ranks:

```
torch._dynamo hit config.recompile_limit (64) ... ltx_2.py:1263 ... last reason: len(...fused_linear_gelu_site._VERDICTS.data) != 28
```

After that, the blocks ran eager behind failing guards on every call.

This fixes a regression introduced by #44643 (same author).

## Modifications

In `fused_linear_gelu_site.py`, `can_use_linear_gelu` computes the input-independent verdict directly while tracing (`torch.compiler.is_compiling()`), as it did before #44643. Eager calls keep the cache. The verdict is the same either way, so outputs are unchanged.

New CUDA test `test_mounted_gelu_sites_compile_one_frame_across_linears` in `test_sites.py`: 12 blocks with two mounted sites each must compile to one frame. On H200 it fails on main and passes here (`test_sites.py` 27/27; with the dynamic-LoRA PR merged in, `test_sites.py` + `test_quality_fusion_lora.py` 32/32).

This PR and "[Fix] diffusion: Keep dynamic LoRA deltas on fused linear-GELU sites" both edit `can_use_linear_gelu`. They merge cleanly in either order. The LoRA PR's adapter check sits above this PR's compile branch, so it also applies while tracing; keep that order if either one is rebased.

## Accuracy Tests

The same verdict is computed, so the same path runs and outputs are unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

LTX-2 two-stage, compile profile, 2xH200, two interleaved rounds (e2e):

| | round 1 | round 2 |
|---|---|---|
| main | 10.754 s | 10.487 s |
| this PR | 10.152 s | 9.915 s |

That is −5.5% in both rounds:
- stage-1 step time: 0.198–0.206 s → 0.185–0.190 s;
- server ready: 128 s → 104 s;
- the `recompile_limit` line is gone from the log.

LTX-2 under compile is still slower than eager on H200, because of graph breaks after attention. That is out of scope here.

title: [Fix] diffusion: Keep the N-rank IPC all-to-all's flags and staging out of expandable segments
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

#43584 moved the 2-rank IPC all-to-all's exported buffers and the N-rank `_PipelinePool` onto `ipc_shareable_zeros`, but the N-rank transport's signal flags, timeout flag and exchange staging (from #43164) stayed plain `torch.zeros`. Under `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` those can land in expandable segments, whose IPC import calls `pidfd_getfd`. Containers without ptrace rights deny that syscall with EPERM.

Seen on a RunPod 4xB300 container (2026-10-22): every sequence-parallel server with more than two ranks logged `IPC all-to-all (multi-rank) unavailable (pidfd_getfd: Operation not permitted); using NCCL` (24 warnings across 6 runs: Wan2.2-A14B, Cosmos3, MiniMax-H3 4-GPU), so the copy-engine all-to-all and the head-grouped pipelined attention never ran.

It can also hang. Whether a plain `torch.zeros` buffer lands in an expandable block depends on each rank's allocator history, so one rank can import its peer's flags while the other fails. Init then deadlocks: one rank waits in `_share(timed_out)`'s `all_gather_object`, the other in the all-reduce where ranks agree on the outcome, until the NCCL watchdog aborts both (~10 min). On RunPod all four ranks happened to fail alike, which is why only the fallback was visible.

## Modifications

- `ipc_a2a_multi.py`: the signal flags, timeout flag and staging buffers come from `ipc_shareable_zeros`, like every other exported buffer. If sharing the flags still fails, the init error now says so.
- `ipc_a2a.py`: one docstring line on why `ipc_shareable_zeros` matters (`pidfd_getfd`).
- The NCCL fallback for hosts that genuinely cannot do CUDA IPC is unchanged.

Tests:
- `test/unit/test_ipc_a2a_lifecycle.py` (CPU, mocked): every buffer the N-rank path exports must come from `ipc_shareable_zeros`. On main the flags, timeout flag and staging fail it.
- `single_test_file/test_ipc_a2a_multi_gpu.py`: reruns the 2-rank multi-rank worker with `expandable_segments:True` under a seccomp filter that makes `pidfd_getfd` fail with EPERM.

## Accuracy Tests

No numerical change: the same buffers, allocated outside expandable segments.

On 2xH200 with `pidfd_getfd` blocked by seccomp (reproduces the RunPod warning exactly):

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| multi-rank worker, expandable segments on, syscall allowed | passes, 3 `pidfd_getfd` calls | passes, 0 calls |
| pipelined-attention test, syscall blocked | RunPod warning on both ranks, FAIL | PASS, 0 calls |
| new 2-GPU test, syscall blocked | deadlock (713 s, watchdog) | PASS (~36 s) |
| 2-rank IPC test, syscall blocked | PASS, 0 calls | PASS, 0 calls |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Restores the IPC all-to-all on such hosts; the multi-rank GPU test file runs in ~48 s on H200, unchanged. Follow-up (not in this PR): `runtime/distributed/ipc_cuda.py` (scheduler↔client CUDA IPC) has the same exposure on the import side.

title: [Fix] dsv41: Keep MegaGate out of prefill graphs by gating on the forward mode
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

`should_use_mega_gate` relied on `get_forward().is_extend_in_batch` to keep DeepGEMM's fused gate on decode and verify. The prefill CUDA graph runner clears that flag before capture (`prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py:866,951`), so with `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_GATE=1` the gate also ran inside captured prefill graphs of up to 2048 rows. On GB300 (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DP2/EP2 MegaMoE, breakable prefill graphs) that produced an `unspecified launch failure` during prefill capture that disappears under `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`.

## Modifications

- `should_use_mega_gate` takes the `forward_batch` and admits only `DECODE` and `TARGET_VERIFY`; `None` means no gate.
- Unit test: the admission case now checks decode and target-verify admit, extend with the flag cleared does not, and `None` does not.

title: [Fix] true-on-policy: Sample from fp32 probs when logits are bf16
author: HJSang
body:
## Summary

Fixes a regression from #44517.
- **What changed in #44517:** the CUDA-graph logits buffer now follows the logits dtype, so under a true-on-policy contract (`qwen3_dense_true_on_policy_v1`) the sampler receives **bf16** logits in graph decode as well as in prefill.
- **Why that breaks filtered sampling:** the standard top-p/top-k path in `Sampler.forward` ran `logits[:] = torch.softmax(logits)` in place, so the probabilities came out bf16. Sampling and the sampling-support log-probs `log(p / support_mass)` then read bf16-rounded probabilities and no longer matched the trainer.
- **The symptom:** miles' `test_qwen3_0_6b_fsdp_sampling_support_replay_true_on_policy.py` fails its true-on-policy check: `log_probs (-1.38827, 8) != rollout_log_probs (-1.38723, 8)`.

**The fix:** upcast the logits to fp32 before the existing in-place softmax (`logits = logits.float()`, which does nothing when they are already fp32). Default serving is unchanged. In graph decode this restores the numerics from before #44517: fp32 softmax of logit values that are exact in bf16. It also makes prefill's first sampled token consistent with decode.

## Tests

**GPU, Qwen3 on 2x H200, CUDA graph on, miles e2e tests:**

| Test | SGLang | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `test_qwen3_0_6b_fsdp_sampling_support_replay_true_on_policy.py` | `sglang-miles` `412be60d96` | fails with exactly the miles CI numbers |

title: [Fix] kimi_k3: Use uuid tool_call_id instead of history-count id
author: yan-lgtm
body:
## Summary
Remove the `kimi_k3` special case in `OpenAIServingChat._process_tool_call_id` so Kimi-K3 gets the default `call_<uuid>` tool call id.

```python
if self.tool_call_parser == "kimi_k3":
    return f"{call_item.name}:{history_tool_calls_cnt + call_item.tool_index}"
```

## Why
- Kimi-K3's encoder treats tool call ids as opaque (the index comes from position), so it doesn't need the `name:idx` format. Only Kimi-K2's chat template requires `functions.{name}:{idx}`, and that path is unchanged.
- An id built from the history count repeats whenever the client sends a shorter history. Clients that dedupe `tool_use` ids (e.g. Claude Code) then drop the call.

- Added `test_kimi_k3_tool_call_id_unique_when_history_count_repeats`: two `_process_tool_call_id` calls with the same history count return different `call_` ids.
- Existing `test_kimi_k2_*_tool_call_id_with_history` tests still pin K2's positional `functions.{name}:{idx}` ids.
