title: [Fix] disaggregation: Poison the deferred abort ack when a NIXL or Mori write fails
author: livingshade
body:
## Motivation

With `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_DEFERRED_DECODE_KV_RELEASE` on (the default), decode holds an aborted request's KV pages and metadata slot until every prefill rank acks that its transfer drained, or until the release timeout.

Mooncake withholds that ack after a failed send (`poison_deferred_ack_room`, #43719). NIXL and Mori still send it after a failed transfer, although both engines can report the failure while writes of that transfer are still on the wire (see Engine code references below). The deferred-release ADR (#44186, Rule 2) rules this out.

- NIXL: the Python API raises on a failed post. The raised post never reaches `handles`, so once the other handles settle, the worker concludes the room and calls `_maybe_ack_drained_abort`. A failed poll is already safe: it leaves the batch unsettled, and that branch poisons.
- Mori: `_mark_transfer_quiescent` acks once the room's outstanding count reaches zero without looking at the statuses, and both the transfer worker and the drainer reach it with a `Failed()` status. `_arm_abort_ack` also acks directly when the count is zero, bypassing any poison.

Decode receives the drained ack, frees the pages, and a write that is still running can land on pages already reused by another request. Decode takes this path on a prefill-reported failure too (`ensure_abort_notified(force_arm=True)`), so both ABORT orderings reach the bug: mid-transfer, or after the Failed status.

## Modifications

NIXL:
- Add `_post_xfer`, used by all 11 `agent.transfer` sites. It raises `_NixlPostError` when NIXL raises or returns `"ERR"`, chaining the NIXL exception as `__cause__`.
- In the worker's failure path, poison the room on `_NixlPostError`, then conclude the failure, uncount the chunk and fall through to `_maybe_ack_drained_abort`, which drops a poisoned room's targets. This is the same order as the Mooncake failed-send path in #43719.
- The failure log also checks `__cause__`, so a NIXL transport error is still logged as a warning.

Mori:
- Add `_poison_failed_transfer`, which poisons the room under `_abort_ack_lock` when any status of the chunk reports `Failed()`. Call it where a chunk becomes quiescent: in `_process_transfer_chunk` (before concluding the failure) and in `_drain_transfer_statuses` (after `status.Wait()`).
- `_mark_transfer_quiescent` does not pop a poisoned room's targets, and `_arm_abort_ack` returns early for a poisoned room. Mori sends ACKs from these two places itself, not through `_maybe_ack_drained_abort`.

Decode then falls back to its release timeout (`SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_DEFERRED_DECODE_KV_RELEASE_TIMEOUT`, 30s) for that room. A new lifecycle of the same `bootstrap_room` clears the poison as before.

Cost: a NIXL post that raises, or a Mori status that reports `Failed()`, is poisoned even when nothing was posted for it (on Mori, e.g. a full send queue before the first WR), so decode holds those pages for 30s.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A, failure-path bookkeeping only. Regression tests, each driving the transfer worker and asserting that no ABORT_ACK is sent:

- `test_rejected_post_never_acks` (NIXL): only the NIXL agent is mocked. Two decode peers: the first post is `DONE`, the second raises a NIXL transport error. The ABORT arrives mid-transfer and again after the worker finishes. Fails on main.
- `test_failed_status_never_acks` (Mori): a `Failed()` status on the worker path and on the drainer path. Fails on main.
- Two existing Mori cases now pin `status.Failed.return_value = False`, since a bare `MagicMock` is truthy.

Results on one H200 node (`lmsysorg/sglang:dev`, `nixl-cu13` 1.5.0), at `e241c252e8`:

- The new cases fail on main (`8d8916815b`), each because an ABORT_ACK is sent. On this branch, the deferred-release, Mooncake, NIXL and wire unit files pass (122 tests, 106 subtests).
- NIXL 1P1D fault injection (a one-off script, not part of this PR): for one request, prefill's `nixl_agent.transfer` does the real post and then raises `nixlBackendError`; the release timeout is 10s. Decode reports `decode_deferred_kv_release_total{outcome="drained"} 1` on main and `outcome="timeout"` 1 on this branch. A follow-up request returns 200 in both.
- Mori: CPU unit tests only; no AMD machine was available.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A. On the normal path the only added work is one `Failed()` scan per chunk on Mori and a `try` around each NIXL post.

## Engine code references

- NIXL (UCX backend, `v1.5.0` and `c28061f9`):
  - `postXferReq` and `getXferStatus` call `throw_nixl_exception`, which raises for every status other than `NIXL_SUCCESS` / `NIXL_IN_PROG`; the `"ERR"` return in `_api.py` is unreachable.
  - With prefill's `num_threads = 8`, a request is split into chunks on separate threads and endpoints. When one chunk fails, the others cancel and free their UCX requests without waiting for them (`nixlUcxBackendReqH::release`).
- Mori (RDMA backend, `f39fa765` and current main):
  - With sglang's defaults, one `TransferStatus` spans 4 QPs. The first error CQE or post failure fails the status while WRs on the other QPs keep running, and `TransferStatus::WaitFor` returns as soon as the status is not `IN_PROGRESS`.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Fix] diffusion: Give every SP rank the same Wan TI2V timestep
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Wan2.2-TI2V-5B with an image input uses a per-token timestep: 0 on the conditioned first frame and `t` everywhere else. `expand_wan_ti2v_timestep` built that tensor only on SP rank 0. The other ranks took a different branch, so the ranks disagreed in two ways:
- The first-frame mask is in the DiT dtype, so rank 0 multiplies by a bf16 `t`. Integer timesteps above 256 do not all fit in bf16 (999 -> 1000, 995 -> 996). Ranks > 0 used the exact `t`. With the default 50 steps and shift 5, 37 of the 50 timesteps differ by 1–2, and the sinusoidal time features at those steps differ by about 24% (relative L2).
- Ranks > 0 also kept `t` on the first-frame tokens.

Wan uses sequence shard by default. Under sequence shard every rank holds the full latents, embeds the full-length timestep, and applies that `temb` to every token in the output norm after the all-gather. So with SP > 1 the ranks produce different noise predictions for the same tokens, and their copies of the latents drift apart over the steps. The model input for each token comes from the copy on the rank that owns its shard, but rank 0 steps its own copy with its own prediction. The video that rank 0 returns therefore mixes the two ranks' trajectories, and SP output does not match single-GPU output beyond reduction-order noise.

This affects Wan2.2-TI2V-5B with an image (`should_apply_wan_ti2v`) and SP > 1: explicit `--ulysses-degree`/`--ring-degree`/`--sp-degree`, or 4+ GPUs with default flags (CFG parallel 2 x SP). The rank-0-only branch has been there since TI2V SP support was added in #12926. It has made the ranks' latents drift apart since Wan switched to sequence shard by default in #19311. The original comment there says the rounding is applied "consistently before it's used by any rank", but the non-zero-rank branch used the unrounded value. The existing helper test uses `t=1000` in fp32, which does not exercise the rounding, and the only TI2V CI case (`wan2_2_ti2v_5b`) runs on one GPU.

## Modifications

`wan_ti2v.py`: every rank now expands the timestep from its own mask. Under sequence shard each rank has the full mask, so all ranks build the same full-length timestep. Under time shard each rank has its own mask shard (rank 0 holds the zeros), so the ranks' timesteps concatenate to the single-GPU one. Single-GPU output is unchanged.

`test_wan_ti2v_helpers.py`: new test with `t=999` and a bf16 mask. It checks that both ranks match the single-GPU expansion under sequence shard, and that the time-shard ranks concatenate to it.

Follow-up, not changed here: the diffusers and original Wan2.2 pipelines build this tensor from a float32 mask, so they use the exact `t`. Removing the bf16 rounding would change single-GPU TI2V output and needs a GT refresh for `wan2_2_ti2v_5b`.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test_wan_ti2v_helpers.py`: on main, rank 1 differs from the single-GPU expansion on all 16 tokens under sequence shard (999 vs 0/1000), and the time-shard concatenation differs on rank 1's 8 tokens (999 vs 1000). Both pass with this PR. Rank 0's output is unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A: same tensor ops on every rank.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Fix] diffusion: Offset LTX-2.3 BCG video RoPE by the SP shard start
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

The legacy LTX-2.3 one-stage path (LTX-2.3 with a non-two-stage pipeline class) passes `video_coords=None` to the model. The model forward then builds the video RoPE coords itself, shifting each SP shard to its global position (`start_frame = sp_rank * local_frames`). The shift matches `sp_video_start_frame` from `LTX2PipelineConfig.shard_latents_for_sp`.

With `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph`, the stage instead builds those coords before capture, because building them inside the forward does an unpinned host-to-device copy that capture rejects. `_prepare_ltx2_rope_coords_for_bcg` passed no `start_frame`. So under SP every rank > 0 encodes its frames as if they started at frame 0, its shard repeats rank 0's temporal positions, and the video loses its temporal order past the first shard.

This affects LTX-2.3 one-stage (the default pipeline for `Lightricks/LTX-2.3` when `--pipeline-class-name` is not given) with SP > 1 and `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph`. BCG is opt-in. SP comes from explicit flags, or from `--num-gpus 4` with default flags, which resolves to SP 4. Two-stage pipelines and LTX-2 are not affected, because their coords come from `prepare_video_rope_coords_for_sp`, which already applies the start frame. Audio is not affected because the legacy path does not shard audio. The bug was added together with LTX-2.3 BCG support in #34929. CI does not cover it: the BCG suites run Z-Image only, and `test_ltx2_bcg_coords.py` asserted the call without a start frame.

## Modifications

`ltx_2/denoising.py`: `_prepare_ltx2_rope_coords_for_bcg` takes `video_start_frame`, and `_get_ltx2_rope_coords` passes the shard start (0 when the latents are not SP-sharded). The start frame was already in the coords cache key.

`test_ltx2_bcg_coords.py`: the existing helper test now expects `start_frame=0`. A new test runs `_get_ltx2_rope_coords` on the legacy BCG path with a real `LTX2AudioVideoRotaryPosEmbed` for SP ranks 0 and 1, and compares against the coords the eager forward builds for that shard.

## Accuracy Tests

- New test: on main, rank 0 passes and rank 1 differs on every temporal coordinate (48/144 elements). It passes with this PR. Rank 0 and non-SP runs build the same coords as before.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A: same coords construction before capture, with a different start offset.

title: [Fix] rust_server: Give each plain-DP replica its own listener port
author: jain-ria
body:
## Motivation

With `SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1`, every DP-group leader embeds a Rust listener on `--port + offset` and `--grpc-port + offset`. The offset counts DP-group leaders inside one TP group's node-local range. Plain DP (`--dp N` without attention DP) runs N separate TP groups, each led by its own TP rank 0, so every replica computes offset 0 and binds the same HTTP and gRPC ports. Plain DP cannot start in Rust mode.

## Modifications

- `RustServer.launch`: under plain DP the listener offset is the replica index (`dp_rank`). Plain DP is single-node (`check_server_args` already rejects multi-node replicas), so every replica's leader is on this node. Attention DP and no-DP keep the existing formula.
- `check_server_args`: Rust-mode PD prefill with plain DP is rejected, since every replica registers its KV bootstrap rows with the `--port` listener.
- Test: the Rust server extension test gets the DP fields `launch` now reads.

## Dependencies

Independent of the other PRs split out of this one (sidecar, attention-DP idle, `node_listeners`). The `node_listeners` PR has a plain-DP test case that needs this PR.

title: [Fix] humming: adapt integration to kernels 0.1.18
author: huangzhilin-hzl
body:
## Motivation

Bump `humming-kernels` from 0.1.12 to 0.1.18 and adapt the integration to the newer quantization APIs

## Modifications

- Use schema-based weight quantization and preserve static, secondary, and per-shard scales.
- Handle Hadamard quantization when loading CPU checkpoint weights.
- Preserve both input scale levels and allocate buffers using each MoE sublayer's input dtype.
- Align indexed MoE routes separately when `w13` and `w2` use different M tiles; validate DeepEP and masked quantization compatibility.
- Place Humming cache and temporary files under `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR`, preserving explicit overrides.
- Add unit and GPU regression coverage.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K, all 1319 questions, [sgl-eval](https://pypi.org/project/sgl-eval/) 0.1.3 (zero-shot chat, `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=4096`, thinking off, 32 concurrent requests). 1 × 8-GPU H20-3e node.
A = baseline SGLang (container image) + humming-kernels 0.1.12, B = this PR + humming-kernels 0.1.18. Launch commands are under [Benchmark](#launch).

| Model | A | B |
|---|---:|---:|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (TP4, DSPARK) | 96.66% | 97.12% |
| GLM-5.3-W4AFP8-AWQ (TP8, EAGLE) | 96.51% | 97.19% |
| Kimi-K2.6 (TP8, EAGLE3) | 97.42% | 97.50% |

No request errors on any arm; one run per arm.

## Benchmark

1 × 8-GPU H20-3e node, A and B back-to-back on the same GPUs, `bench_serving` with `temperature=0`, one warmup pass per point.

### Launch

All arms set `SGLANG_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG='{"dtype":"float8e4m3"}'`. A and B use identical flags.

```bash
# DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (GPUs 0-3)
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 --tp 4 --trust-remote-code \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --mem-fraction-static 0.88 \
  --moe-runner-backend humming --quantization humming \
  --disable-radix-cache --context-length 270336 --stream-interval 1 --random-seed 1

# GLM-5.3-W4AFP8-AWQ
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path GLM-5.3-W4AFP8-AWQ --tp 8 --trust-remote-code \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --reasoning-parser auto --tool-call-parser auto --disable-shared-experts-fusion \
  --moe-runner-backend humming --quantization humming \
  --disable-radix-cache --context-length 270336 --stream-interval 1 --random-seed 1

# Kimi-K2.6 (also SGLANG_ALLOW_OVERWRITE_LONGER_CONTEXT_LEN=1)
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Kimi-K2.6 --tp 8 --trust-remote-code \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE3 --speculative-draft-model-path Kimi-K2.6-Eagle3-Long-Context \
  --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --reasoning-parser kimi_k2 --tool-call-parser kimi_k2 --disable-shared-experts-fusion \
  --moe-runner-backend humming --quantization humming \
  --disable-radix-cache --context-length 270336 --stream-interval 1 --random-seed 1
```

### DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731

`random` dataset; 3 rounds per arm in the order A1 B1 B2 A2 A3 B3; values are 3-round means. Requests per point = concurrency.

| TTFT, output 256, C=1 | A ms | B ms | Δ |

| 16K | 1194.7 | 1218.0 | +1.95% |
| 32K | 2506.3 | 2555.8 | +1.97% |
| 64K | 5493.2 | 5597.2 | +1.89% |
| 128K | 12947.2 | 13147.0 | +1.54% |
| 256K | 33964.1 | 34353.8 | +1.15% |

| TPOT, output 1024 | C=1 A → B | C=2 A → B | C=4 A → B |

title: [Fix] diffusion: Fail closed after local worker loss or multi-rank OOM
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Production fault tests for #45919 exposed an independent bug: a local GPU worker can exit while the HTTP server still advertises readiness. A multi-rank allocator OOM is worse: the failing rank resumes request dispatch while its peer remains in the previous forward, permanently desynchronizing the replica.

Both failures were reproduced on main (`4b273537dec`), independently of progress reporting.

## Changes

- Track launcher-owned worker process identities, including the WebUI HTTP child and locally launched disaggregated pools.
- Return readiness 503 after any owned worker exits, including zombie/PID-reuse cases. Keep HTTP liveness independent.
- Check owned processes once per second, terminate pending scheduler waits even without an RPC deadline, and reject new POST requests with 503. Completed job status/content remain readable.
- Treat allocator OOM during a multi-rank forward as fatal to the worker. Exit at the process boundary without potentially blocking CUDA/NCCL teardown; do not reuse the desynchronized replica.
- Preserve request-level OOM recovery for single-GPU replicas, including independent DP replicas.
- Document restart requirements and coverage limits. No extra GPU collective, per-step callback, CLI knob, or change to generated outputs.

## Validation

- Remote regression tests: the new client and multi-rank OOM cases fail before the fix (3 failed, 2 passed). Fixed related suite: **114 passed, 4 subtests passed**.
- Real 2x H200 tests, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 / CUDA 13.0 / Diffusers 0.37.0 / Transformers 5.19.0. Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers, 512x320, 17 frames, seed 42, 24 denoising steps after warmup.
- A separate GPU allocation leaves approximately 128 MiB free; an 832x480, 33-frame request triggers a real allocator OOM, not an injected exception.
- Ulysses=2: pressure on rank 0 and rank 1 tested separately. All three in-flight/queued jobs fail within **0.77 s / 0.66 s**, without an RPC deadline. TP=2 non-output-rank OOM: **0.94 s**. Readiness/new POSTs return 503; previous output remains downloadable and decodes to identical frames.
- Single GPU: three OOM/recovery cycles. DP=2: three cycles on **each** GPU. All nine recoveries preserve decoded frame hashes; normal readiness remains 200.
- SP outputs before failure match main's decoded frame hashes. No owned child processes remain after shutdown.
- Combined with #45919 on a detached validation head: real per-step progress and multi-rank OOM handling both pass. The independent fixes remain separate PRs.
- Earlier real worker-SIGKILL tests also covered the spawned HTTP bootstrap and a local encoder/denoiser/decoder pool with Mooncake transfers. Full Gradio UI was not tested.
- Pre-commit passes. No GT, tolerance, or performance baseline changes.

This is bounded failure handling, not transparent failover: restart the whole server and retry failed jobs. Arbitrary live-process hangs, remote-worker supervision, durable job recovery, and fatal CUDA-context errors remain separate concerns (#45065).

title: [Fix] pp: Post the first rank's output recv after its own forward
author: ehuaa
body:
The first rank posts its output irecv right after launching its forward, but the last rank sends only after its own forward, so the recv spins and holds an SM in the meantime. That blocks any kernel that needs every SM (e.g. flashinfer's MLA), so PP0 stalls each decode step; since #44453 the last rank's relay recv also spins through its forward, and the two stages deadlock.

Add `SGLANG_ENABLE_PP_OUTPUT_RECV_AFTER_FORWARD` (default off), which fences that recv on the rank's `launch_event` (depth 0, no spec relay). With it set, tp8pp2 on 2x8 A100 with flashinfer goes from a hang to TPOT 23.9 ms. It is off by default because triton pays +1.8% TPOT: rank 0 then processes an earlier microbatch's result after its forward instead of during it. With it unset, behavior is the same as main.

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

Under PP, the first rank posts its output `irecv` right after launching its forward, but the last rank only sends after its own forward finishes. In the meantime the recv kernel spins and holds an SM, which blocks any kernel that needs every SM to make progress. flashinfer's MLA kernel (FA2 on SM80, FA3 on SM90) is one example. Kernels that do not need every SM (e.g. triton attention) do not stall.

- Before #44453: PP0 stalls on every decode step (flashinfer: TPOT 36.5 ms). With this PR it no longer stalls (TPOT 23.8 ms).
- Since #44453: the last rank also posts its relay `irecv` before waiting on its own forward, so its forward can be blocked the same way. The two stages then wait on each other (the TP all-reduce couples the ranks inside each stage) and decode hangs. Reproduced 4/4 on tp8pp2 and tp4pp4, 2x8 A100. With this PR decode no longer hangs.

## Modifications

- Add `SGLANG_ENABLE_PP_OUTPUT_RECV_AFTER_FORWARD = EnvBool(False)` next to the other PP env vars. Off by default, so the default path is unchanged from main. The call-site comment says to turn it on when PP hangs or stalls on kernels that need every SM (e.g. flashinfer MLA).
- When it is set, before the first rank posts its output recv (depth 0, no spec relay), make the comm stream wait on`launch_event`, so the recv starts only after the rank's own forward and never spins alongside it. No host blocking. The check does not depend on the attention backend, and other ranks are unchanged.
- Add a unit test asserting that, with the env var set, only the first rank fences this recv (not later ranks, the specrelay, or depth > 0). The existing two-in-flight deadlock test is unchanged and still covers the default path.

## Accuracy Tests

Greedy outputs are token-identical with the fence on and off (flashinfer and triton, pp2 and pp4). With the env var unset, the code path is the same as main.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

DeepSeek-V2 MLA model (236B, bf16), 2x8 A100-80GB, evalscope `random` 7800 in / 2048 out, after warmup. The PR column has `SGLANG_ENABLE_PP_OUTPUT_RECV_AFTER_FORWARD=1`. With it unset, the PR runs the same code path as main.

| Config | Backend | main (TTFT / TPOT) | this PR (TTFT / TPOT) |
|---|---|---|---|
| tp8pp2, C=8 | flashinfer | hang | 4743 ms / 23.82 ms |
| tp8pp2, C=8 | triton | 7525 ms / 27.79 ms | 7541 ms / 28.16 ms |
| tp4pp4, C=40 | flashinfer | hang | 20296 ms / 50.88 ms |
| tp4pp4, C=40 | triton | 36262 ms / 56.04 ms | 34870 ms / 55.12 ms |

title: [Fix] docker: Pin sgl-nvidia-mega to 3333e4c so the megakernel starts on main
author: weireweire
body:
## Motivation

`docker/Dockerfile` and `docker/Dockerfile.cu134` pin sgl-nvidia-mega `d47deb33`. That commit predates two SGLang changes it depends on: the TopKConfig shared-expert field rename (#44912, #44913) and the kernel regrouping (#45112). This also blocks the DSpark megakernel path from #45450 in public images.

#45595 made the same bump and was closed in favor of #45389. #45389 is a larger refactor and currently changes only `docker/rocm.Dockerfile`. This PR is the standalone pin bump for the two CUDA Dockerfiles.

title: [Fix] diffusion/zimage: Stop serving a previous request's RoPE tables
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

The Z-Image DiT caches the fp32 cos/sin tables it derives from the image, caption and unified RoPE tables. The key was the source tensors' `data_ptr()`, shape and dtype, and the entry did not keep the sources alive. Once a request finished, its tables were freed, and the next request could allocate its own tables at the same address. With the same shape the key matched, and the next request ran on the previous request's positions.

The unified `[image, caption]` table makes this reachable in normal serving. Its length is the padded caption plus the padded image tokens, so a request with a different split of the same length matches the previous one. The server warmup (1024x1024, caption padded to 32 tokens) poisons every 1472x704 request whose caption pads to 64 tokens (4064 + 64 = 4128 = 4096 + 32).

Reproduced on 2xH200, TP2, eager: a 1472x704 request after the default warmup hit the stale unified table on all 9 steps on both ranks, and the image came out as horizontal streaks (PSNR 12.2 dB against the same request on a server started with `--warmup-mode off`).

## Modifications

- `_get_rope_cache` keeps its source tensors in the cache entry and matches them by identity, so a new tensor never hits an old entry.
- The unified table, previously rebuilt by every forward, is built once per request's pair of image and caption tables (`_get_unified_freqs_cis`), which keeps its cache entry hitting across steps.
- The caches are initialized in `__init__` (`_rope_caches`, `_unified_freqs_cis`).

Tests: `test_zimage_rope_cache.py`
- a new table allocated at a freed table's address gets its own cache entry (fails on main: the stale entry is returned);
- the unified table is built once per request and rebuilt for another split of the same length.

E2E guard, in the CI case `zimage_image_t2i_2_gpus` (2 GPUs, Ulysses 2):
- A lead request at 1360x768 is sent first after the server warmup, before the case's 1024x1024 request, and is checked against its own golden `h100/zimage_image_t2i_2_gpus_lead_2gpu.jpg`. 1360x768 has 85x48 = 4080 image tokens, which pad to the 4096 of the 1024x1024 warmup (2048 per rank) over another grid, so on main it runs on the warmup's image positions.
- It has to be the first request after the warmup. On instrumented main, the first request after the warmup reused the warmup's tables on 18/18 step-rank forwards (TP2 and Ulysses 2), while 1360x768 and 1472x704 sent after a 1024x1024 request ran on fresh tables. On one GPU the unified table missed on every step, so a 1-GPU case cannot show the bug.
- `DiffusionTestCase.lead_sampling_params`: a consistency-only request (no performance baseline) with the case's quality pin; GT generation saves its golden as `<case id>_lead`. Unit tests in `test_sequential_server_requests.py`.
- `SGL_TEST_FILES_CI_DATA_REVISION` moves to ci-data-diffusion `4188b35b`, which is the previous pin `252df495` plus this one golden. The golden was generated on H100 by the GT workflow ([run 40061167040](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40061167040)) and is also published on ci-data-diffusion main (`4aa2bacb`). The pin stays off main because main lacks the MiniMax-H3 references that `252df495` carries.

## Accuracy Tests

2xH200, Z-Image-Turbo, TP2, eager:

| request | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1472x704, caption padded to 64, after the default 1024x1024 warmup | stale unified table on 18/18 step-rank forwards; streaked image | identical to the same request on a server without warmup |
| 1024x1024 benchmark request (two inputs) | reference | pixels bitwise identical |

E2E guard, `zimage_image_t2i_2_gpus` on 2xH200 (Ulysses 2, the CI configuration), against a golden generated by this PR on the same machine:

| request | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| lead: 1360x768, first after the 1024x1024 warmup | stale image table on 18/18 step-rank forwards; SSIM 0.794, PSNR 16.4 dB, mean abs diff 14.3: **fails** (thresholds 0.95 / 28 / 8) | bitwise identical to the golden: passes |
| the case's 1024x1024 request, after the lead | same output on main and this PR | bitwise identical to the same request without a lead; peak allocated 15133 MiB (baseline 15131) |

On the H100 GT workflow run, the 1024x1024 request after the lead is byte-identical to the existing golden. H200 output drifts from the H100 goldens (PSNR 24 dB on the existing 1024x1024 golden, 21.5 dB on the lead), so the CI golden comes from H100, not from the devbox.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

1024x1024 benchmark request, client latency: 0.658 / 0.646 s on main, 0.655 / 0.645 s with this PR (the unified table's two concatenations now run once per request instead of every step).

title: [Fix] grammar: Give grammar accept failures an error status
author: weireweire
body:
## Motivation

A grammar `accept_token` failure in the shared result processor aborts the request with a bare `FINISH_ABORT()`, which has no status code ([L730](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/fa622d311d/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/batch_result_processor.py#L730), [L872](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/fa622d311d/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/batch_result_processor.py#L872)). `TokenizerManager._handle_abort_finish_reason` turns an abort into an HTTP error only when its status is 4xx/5xx, so the client receives a 200 whose finish reason is `abort`. The OpenAI streaming path likewise treats it as a graceful abort rather than an error.

The rejected token was sampled under the grammar's own bitmask, so the failure is a server-side fault, such as an FSM/bitmask desync or an xgrammar issue. Other grammar handlers already report it that way: the PD prefill handler (`process_batch_result_disagg_prefill`) and the PD decode prebuilt path both abort with 500. The sampling-mask INVALID failure in the same file does too.

Scope: these two sites run on aggregated servers and on PD decode workers. A PD prefill server never reaches them, because it processes extend results in `process_batch_result_disagg_prefill`. This change therefore does not affect how PD frontends cancel a paired decode request.

This PR originally made prefill send `KVPoll.Failed` to decode on prefill-side aborts. Following the review discussion, that is left to the frontend, and this PR only makes this abort report a status.

## Modifications

Both grammar `accept_token` failure sites abort with `HTTPStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` and `InternalServerError`, with the `accept_token` error as the message. This matches the PD grammar handlers and the sampling-mask failures.

Behavior for an affected request:
- Non-streaming requests get a 500.
- OpenAI streaming requests get an error chunk.
- Native `/generate` streaming carries `status_code` 500 in the final `finish_reason`.

## Accuracy Tests

No numerical change. Only the abort's status and message change.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (ruff with the repo's hook selection and ruff-format pass on the changed file.)

title: [Doc] diffusion: Fix documented snippets that cannot load a model
author: nankingjing
body:
Three copy-pasteable snippets that build a generator fail before producing any video: two import a name that does not exist, and one calls `from_pretrained` in a way that cannot set the model path.

### 1. `docs/cookbook/diffusion/LongLive/LongLive-2.0.mdx` (Multi-shot section)

```python
from sglang import DiffGenerator
```

`DiffGenerator` is not exported by the top-level `sglang` package: it is absent from `__all__` in `python/sglang/__init__.py`, and that module defines no `__getattr__`, so the import raises `ImportError`.

It is exported by `sglang.multimodal_gen` (`__all__ = ["DiffGenerator", "PipelineConfig", "SamplingParams"]`), which is how every other diffusion page imports it (`Kandinsky6.mdx`, `Kandinsky6-SR.mdx`, `progressive_resolution.mdx`, `plugin.mdx`).

### 2. `docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/support_new_models.mdx` (Implement the Pieces, step 1)

```python
from sglang.multimodal_gen.configs.sample.sampling_params import ImageSamplingParams
```

There is no `ImageSamplingParams` class. That module defines `SamplingParams`, `SkipSoftmaxParams` and `CacheParams`, and every image pipeline in the tree subclasses `SamplingParams` (`zimage.py`, `qwenimage.py`, `ernie_image.py`, `longcat_image.py`, `ming_image.py`, ...). The same page refers to `SamplingParams` elsewhere.

### 3. `docs/cookbook/diffusion/LongLive/LongLive-2.0.mdx` (same snippet, next line)

```python
gen = DiffGenerator.from_pretrained("Rabinovich/LongLive-2.0-5B-Diffusers")
```

The signature is `from_pretrained(cls, local_mode: bool = True, **kwargs)` (`multimodal_gen/runtime/entrypoints/diffusion_generator.py`). The positional string binds to `local_mode`, so `model_path` is never set and `ServerArgs.from_kwargs()` gets no model. Every other page passes it by keyword (`model_path=...` in `progressive_resolution.mdx`, `Kandinsky6.mdx`, `HY-Nomas.mdx`, `multimodal_gen/README.md`).

The same two mistakes appear in `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (lines 31-32); corrected there too.

### Change

Snippets now import symbols that exist and pass `model_path=` by keyword. Docs and comments only; no code or test change.

title: [Fix] function_call: Normalize GLM non-streaming tool names
author: goldenfox2025
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #45953.

GLM non-streaming tool-call parsing can silently drop a defined tool when the captured function name contains surrounding whitespace. A GLM-4.7/5 response such as `<tool_call>get_weather` followed by a newline and its argument tags is rejected as an unknown function; both `tool_calls` and visible content can be empty. GLM-4.5/4.6 has the same inconsistency for names with leading/trailing spaces, tabs, or CRLF headers. Both streaming paths already normalize function names.

This PR consolidates the GLM-4.7/5 fix from #45962 with the independently reproduced GLM-4.5/4.6 fix.

**Confirmed root cause (parser-level reproduction):** Both non-streaming detectors pass the untrimmed function-name capture into argument-schema lookup and `parse_base_json`. The latter matches registered tool names exactly, so a name such as `get_weather\n` or `get_weather ` is treated as undefined and skipped. The tool-call span has already been consumed from visible content, which explains the empty response. Normalizing the captured identifier before these lookups resolves the reproduced failure while preserving argument-value whitespace.

## Modifications

- Strip surrounding whitespace from function names in both `Glm4MoeDetector` and `Glm47MoeDetector` before argument-schema lookup and tool validation.
- Add GLM4 regression coverage for name whitespace and actual/literal newline separators, asserting that argument-value whitespace is preserved.
- Include the GLM47 newline regression from #45962, which exercises non-streaming and several streaming chunk sizes.
- Use `CustomTestCase` for the two modified regression test classes.

## Attribution

The GLM-4.7/5 implementation and regression test are by [potoior](https://github.com/potoior), cherry-picked from commit [0fb629b6](https://github.com/potoior/sglang/commit/0fb629b6bb7c6e09452ce27acd46721d4ae6433b) in #45962. Original commit authorship is preserved, and the cherry-pick records its source. The other commits on that PR's branch were not imported.

The GLM-4.5/4.6 fix and its regression coverage are by goldenfox2025. The issue and its initial GLM47 reproduction were reported by [LucianMincu](https://github.com/LucianMincu).

## Accuracy Tests

Focused CPU validation, without model weights or a running server:

- GLM4 before/after: the new regression failed in all 10 whitespace subcases before the fix; all 12 subcases, including the unpadded-name controls, pass afterward.
- GLM47 before/after: the imported newline regression reproduces the missing-call failure without the GLM47 fix and passes with it.
- With both fixes: **41 test methods pass** across the GLM4, GLM47, Ling3, and GLM47 schema-type test classes. Two additional GLM47 tests requiring xgrammar were excluded because that dependency is unavailable locally.

The local isolation harness executes repository test-class bodies using the actual parser and protocol types. It bypasses the shared GPU/server test lifecycle and an unrelated response-schema conversion helper. These results do not establish that the normal pytest invocation or the entire unit-test module passes.

Standard CI verification in a configured SGLang environment:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest \
  test/registered/unit/function_call/test_function_call_parser.py::TestGlm4MoeDetector \
  test/registered/unit/function_call/test_function_call_parser.py::TestGlm47MoeDetector \
  test/registered/unit/function_call/test_function_call_parser.py::TestLing3Detector \
  test/registered/unit/function_call/test_glm47_schema_types.py -q
```

Ruff 0.15.1 lint (`F401,F821,F823,UP037`), Ruff formatting, and `git diff --check` pass for all four changed files. GPU inference and full CI have not been run locally.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run. The changes normalize extracted names without changing model computation or the streaming implementation.

## Checklist

- [x] Check formatting and relevant static checks on the changed files.
- [x] Include regression tests for both affected detectors.
- [x] Preserve authorship and credit the source contribution.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.
- Documentation: no public API or documented format changes.
- End-to-end accuracy/performance benchmarks: not run; this PR is limited to the demonstrated parser defects.

title: [Fix] diffusion/server: Clean up rejected and cancelled video requests
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

Fix request-owned resource leaks in `POST /v1/videos` before background dispatch:

- Share the existing temporary-directory helper with the image API, using an async exit stack to transfer cleanup ownership from the request to the background job.
- Clean up rejected JSON/multipart requests and preparation failures, without deleting configured persistent input/output directories.
- Wait for CPU preparation to finish before cleaning up a cancelled request. Cancelling an await does not stop its thread.
- Let newly created background jobs enter their cleanup scope before shutdown cancels them.

No new flags or resource-management framework. Production code decreases by 13 lines; most diff churn is indentation around the cleanup scope. This fixes existing behavior on main, independently of #45919.

## Validation

- Regression tests fail before the fix for malformed JSON, invalid multipart fields, cancellation during CPU preparation, and immediate shutdown.
- 139 related tests pass on the fix; 161 pass when integrated with #45919 and #46025.
- Real H200 / Wan2.1-1.3B HTTP comparison: four bursts of 100 rejected requests at concurrency 8. Old code accumulates 400 temporary directories and returns 500 for invalid multipart fields. Fixed code leaves zero and returns 400.
- Each version completes eight valid video jobs, including one after every rejection burst. Decoded frames match between versions; persistent output files remain available.
- Combined real-server validation with #45919/#46025 passes concurrent progress polling, multi-output generation, malformed progress IPC, and deletion without late-update resurrection.
- Pre-commit passes.

This does not implement GPU job cancellation, durable job storage, or bounded cancellation of arbitrary blocking preprocessing.

title: [Fix] diffusion/api: Publish image inputs atomically
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

Fix input-image persistence used by image, video, and mesh APIs.

- Stage downloads in the destination directory and publish with `os.replace`, avoiding a cross-filesystem copy and partially published files.
- Remove unpublished temporary files in `finally`, including cancellation after downloading but before publication.
- Reject destination-directory collisions instead of returning a directory path with an upload hidden inside it.
- Remove redundant exception bookkeeping so a stale retry error cannot replace the final exception.
- Reuse one atomic byte writer for multipart/raw-byte and base64 inputs. A failed write or flush must not truncate an existing destination or leave a partial new input.

Existing size limits, retry behavior, input bytes, and remote-source bypass remain unchanged. No new flags or modules. Atomic publication requires a writable parent directory; newly staged files are owner-only, matching the URL-download path.

## Validation

- Two pre-fix failures reproduced: cancellation with a congested executor leaves an orphan temporary file; a destination-directory collision silently succeeds.
- 75 related tests pass, including partial-body retries and preservation of an existing destination.
- Upload follow-up: six pre-fix disk-write regression failures reproduced; 61 focused input/API/utility tests pass after the fix. The existing URL cases already pass and remain covered.
- A separate Linux file-size-limit test triggers real write/flush failures for bytes, bytearray, memoryview, file-like objects, multipart uploads, base64, and HTTP URLs. Across all 14 combinations of source and existing/new destination, the fix preserves the old file or leaves no published file, removes staging files, and successfully handles the next input. The original version preserves only the two URL cases.
- Real HTTP checks cover redirects, 503 retries, truncated bodies, oversized responses, streaming cancellation, and byte-identical inputs through the image/video/mesh endpoints. Model preparation is replaced at that boundary; these are not GPU generation benchmarks.
- Filesystem comparison: 28,333,361-byte PNG, 10 downloads per configuration, first excluded; nine-sample median:

| Destination | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Local filesystem | 61.66 ms | 62.62 ms |
| tmpfs, different from system temp | 70.19 ms | 60.12 ms |
| Shared filesystem, different from system temp | 70.12 ms | 60.20 ms |

These numbers cover HTTP download and file publication only, not generation latency. Small inputs remained around 6 ms. File hashes match and no partial files remain.

Atomic multipart/byte writes add metadata operations: in a separate 20-sample comparison, 64 KiB inputs increased by about 0.06 ms on local storage and 0.19 ms on shared storage. This is an input-integrity fix, not a claim of zero overhead or faster inference. Upload writes remain synchronous; event-loop latency and crash durability are outside this change.

Pre-commit passes. This does not change model-specific media loaders, SSRF policy, or download deadlines, and does not promise cleanup after process termination.

title: [Fix] rust-server: Keep a transfer backend's own bootstrap port on prefill
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

With `SGLANG_RUST_SERVER` set on a prefill worker, `handle_pd_disaggregation` aliases `--disaggregation-bootstrap-port` to `--port`, because the embedded Rust server answers the KV bootstrap registry on its API listener and every consumer of the resolved field (KVManager registration, `PrefillBootstrapQueue`) has to agree with it. That alias is only correct when the Rust registry really stands in for the transfer backend's bootstrap server, which is the case for the built-in backends: their `KVClassType.BOOTSTRAP_SERVER` is a `CommonKVBootstrapServer`, the HTTP registry the Rust server reimplements.

A transfer backend that brings a bootstrap server of its own, one that does not derive from `CommonKVBootstrapServer`, still runs that server on the configured bootstrap port. Rewriting the field to the API port then points the backend's registration at a port nothing of its own listens on, and a deliberately separate `--disaggregation-bootstrap-port` is rejected as a conflict with `--port`.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/managers/disagg_service.py`: add `rust_server_serves_kv_bootstrap(transfer_backend)`. It resolves the backend's bootstrap server class through `get_kv_class` and returns whether that class is a `CommonKVBootstrapServer`; a backend with no bootstrap server at all (`fake`) returns `False`.
- `python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/pd_disaggregation_hook.py`: `_alias_bootstrap_port_to_api_port` returns early, logging that the configured port is kept, when the helper returns `False`. The import is lazy so the argument hook does not import the disaggregation package at module import time and so a `get_kv_class` bound at runtime is the one consulted. The built-in backends take the same path as before.
- `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_rust_server_dp_ports.py`: `test_rust_prefill_bootstrap_port_alias` runs `handle_pd_disaggregation` on a prefill `ServerArgs` under `SGLANG_RUST_SERVER` with `get_kv_class` patched to a `CommonKVBootstrapServer` subclass or a bare `BaseKVBootstrapServer` subclass. The HTTP-registry cases keep the previous behaviour (default port aliased to `--port`, a port equal to `--port` kept, a separate port raises `conflicts with --port`); the own-bootstrap-server cases keep the default and a separate port as configured.

## Accuracy Tests

Argument resolution only; model forward and inference are untouched.

- `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_rust_server_dp_ports.py`: 37 tests pass on this branch (32 existing, 5 new parametrized cases of `test_rust_prefill_bootstrap_port_alias`).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: one extra class lookup at server-argument resolution time on Rust-server prefill.

## Checklist

- [x] Pre-commit checks pass on the changed files.
- [x] Unit tests added for the new behaviour.
- [ ] Documentation: no user-facing flag changes.

title: [Fix] diffusion/storage: Join uploads before request cleanup
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

Cancelling a cloud upload cancelled its asyncio wrapper, not the SDK thread. Request cleanup could then delete the source files while boto3 was still opening multipart parts. Concurrent image/video uploads could also return on the first cancelled child while another upload was still using the directory.

- Join the SDK operation before propagating cancellation, including repeated cancellation.
- Wait for every image/video upload before allowing caller cleanup.
- Preserve upload failures and the existing local-output fallback.
- Document shutdown grace-period and remote-object retention boundaries.

No new options, production modules, model changes, or changes to storage retry settings. Production diff: +27/-8 lines across three existing files.

## Validation

- Regression tests on Linux: six failures before the fix; all pass after it. Related standalone tests: **52 passed**.
- Real boto3 1.43.116 against a loopback S3-protocol fixture: successful PUT, HTTP 503 retry, HTTP 403 fallback, and cancellation during 16 MiB multipart initialization. Before the fix the source disappeared and zero bytes were published; afterwards the source remained until upload completion, then request cleanup ran and cancellation propagated.
- Integration with #45919, #46025 and #46057: **119 tests passed**.
- H200 / torch 2.14.1+cu130 / Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers, 512x320, 17 frames, four steps: two real server lifecycles covering persistent and temporary outputs, denied/blocked object storage, multi-output publication, recovery and shutdown during uploads. Health/status polling stayed responsive; unfinished uploads did not report completed. Repeated workload outputs matched decoded-frame hashes after recovery. Owned workers exited.
- Pre-commit passed.

The storage fixture exercises the real SDK and HTTP transport, not AWS service availability. Cooperative cancellation may wait for SDK timeouts/retries; it does not roll back uploaded objects or provide durable job recovery. The race also reproduces on main and is not introduced by #45919.

title: [Fix] rust-server: Start a transfer backend's own KV bootstrap server on prefill
author: metamergebot
body:
Stacked on https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46066: this PR's base is that PR's branch until it lands, so the diff shown here is only this change. It builds on `rust_server_serves_kv_bootstrap`, which that PR adds.

## Motivation

In Python mode the `TokenizerManager` calls `start_disagg_service`, which on a prefill node brings up the transfer backend's KV bootstrap server. The Rust server starts no `TokenizerManager`. Its own api listener serves the HTTP registry, which covers every backend whose `BOOTSTRAP_SERVER` is a `CommonKVBootstrapServer`, but a backend with a bootstrap server of its own was left with nothing listening. The `PrefillBootstrapQueue`'s `KVManager` registers to the bootstrap server synchronously during scheduler init, and a failed registration only retries briefly before logging, after which no PD request can be routed to that prefill.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/managers/disagg_service.py`: add `start_disagg_service_for_rust_server()`. On a prefill node whose backend's bootstrap server is not a `CommonKVBootstrapServer` it starts that server via `start_disagg_service`; otherwise it returns `None`. The note on `maybe_create_ascend_config_store` now describes both shapes the bootstrap server can take in Rust mode.
- `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py`: in Rust-server mode, call it from the main process at the point where the `TokenizerManager` would have started the server in Python mode: after the schedulers launch and before waiting for them to become ready, so the prefill ranks find it when they register. The handle is kept on `SchedulerInitResult.kv_bootstrap_server`.
- `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`: the comment on the rust-server prefill path now covers both the embedded registry and a backend-owned bootstrap server. The code there is unchanged: only the ascend config store is still created in the scheduler.
- `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_rust_server_dp_ports.py`: the two bootstrap-server test doubles now assert which of them may be constructed, and a new parametrized test covers the three cases: an HTTP-registry backend starts nothing, a backend with its own bootstrap server is started on the configured host and port on prefill, and decode starts nothing.

Built-in backends (nixl, mooncake, mori, ascend) are unchanged: the Rust server keeps serving their registry on the api port.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no model forward or kernel code changes.

- `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_rust_server_dp_ports.py`: 40 tests pass on this branch (37 existing, 3 new parametrized cases of `test_rust_mode_starts_only_a_bootstrap_server_rust_cannot_serve`).

title: [Fix] diffusion/mesh: Guard asynchronous job publication and defaults
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Mesh jobs currently expose their expected output path while still queued. If an exporter creates the file before finishing, `/content` can serve a partial export, including after the job fails. A worker-returned path that does not exist can also be marked completed. Request preparation failures leave a queued record with no background task.

HTTP replay additionally exposed that omitting the optional seed passes `None` into sampling validation and returns 500.

## Modifications

- Preserve sampling defaults for absent/null optional fields while retaining explicit values, including seed 0.
- Prepare the request before recording an accepted job.
- Require an existing output before marking completion, clear artifact references on failure, and serve content only for completed jobs.
- Document the mesh endpoint and its process-local metadata / deletion semantics.

All production changes stay in the existing mesh API (+27/-15). No new manager, configuration option, or model-compute change. Background-task retention and shutdown ownership remain separate from this PR; #34480 already addresses that work.

## Validation

On an isolated development machine:

- The publication/preparation regressions fail on the parent implementation: 5 failures, 2 passing controls.
- 91 related API, security, storage, and video-lifecycle tests pass after the fixes.
- Real TCP/HTTP replay with 64 concurrent mesh jobs: JSON/base64 and multipart, GLB and OBJ, successful export, partial-write failure, missing file, and empty worker result. All 64 premature downloads return 404; 16 completed outputs are byte-exact and 48 injected failures stay unavailable. Metadata deletion/listing also checked.

The HTTP replay uses native sampling/preparation, dispatch, stores, and file responses, with model generation/export replaced for fault injection. It is not GPU mesh inference or a model-quality benchmark. Existing unbounded queueing, durable recovery, and file retention are outside this patch.

Pre-commit passes. No model accuracy or inference-speed claim.

title: [Fix] diffusion/loader: Preserve checkpoints on read failures
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

Safetensors header validation currently treats every read exception as corruption, then deletes the file. For a symlink, it also deletes the target blob, which may be shared by other snapshots or replicas. Permission and storage I/O errors can therefore destroy otherwise valid checkpoints.

Remove this automatic deletion. Keep validation and duplicate-key rejection, report the original read error, and leave repair or re-download to the operator. Document the behavior in the deployment cookbook. No new option or production module; production code decreases by 22 lines.

## Validation

- Regression tests reproduce deletion on the parent for regular files and shared symlinks under malformed headers, permission errors, and I/O errors.
- Remote loader suites: 52 tests and 12 subtests pass, including retrying a transient read error without re-downloading the checkpoint.
- Real Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B HTTP inference on H200, single GPU and Ulysses2: 8 generations across 4 rejected updates and 2 successful reloads. Source files survive rejection, health remains ready, and weight checksums plus decoded-frame hashes remain unchanged within each configuration.
- Pre-commit passes.

This does not change checkpoint repair tooling, generation kernels, or the normal weight-reading path. TP/FSDP hot updates and hardware-level storage fault injection were not exercised by the GPU smoke test.

title: [Fix] diffusion/disaggregation: Isolate malformed request and result messages
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Production fault testing around #45919 exposed an independent disaggregation failure: one malformed worker tensor result can terminate the head's routing loop and stall unrelated requests. Invalid scheduler payloads and duplicate active IDs can also leave clients waiting without a reply.

## Changes

- Decode worker tensor frames once at the message boundary. An identifiable decoding error fails its request; unidentifiable frames are logged and discarded without stopping the head.
- Reply to malformed or duplicate scheduler requests without replacing an existing request. Make the existing one-request-per-message contract explicit.
- Treat missing decoder output as an error while preserving audio-only results.
- Return reserved receive slots when a worker reports an error, as well as its scheduling capacity.
- Extend the existing orchestration test across combined/split encoders, dynamic/preallocated buffers, malformed requests/results, duplicate IDs, worker errors, and recovery. No new production module or knob.
- Document the failure boundary and trusted-network requirement.

## Validation

- Remote fault matrix on the base revision: **24 failed, 4 passed**. Fixed related suite: **111 passed, 6 subtests passed**, including 44 orchestration variants.
- Real GLM-Image on 2x H200, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 / CUDA 13.0: external AR server, separate DiT/VAE worker and HTTP head; 1024x1024, 30 steps, concurrent `n=1/2` requests.
- A ZMQ relay corrupts the shape of exactly one real output tensor after a successful warmup. Before the fix, the routing loop exits and all four concurrent requests time out after 90 seconds. After the fix, only the affected request returns 500; the other three requests and a subsequent recovery request complete successfully.
- Repeat with in-memory and saved outputs: 12 generation requests, 10 successful responses and two expected failures. Each run returns six valid images; the six saved files match the API's encoded bytes. No worker-side image files remain. Malformed IPC requests return errors, invalid HTTP input returns 422, and subsequent generation succeeds.
- Both baselines include #46104 to avoid the unrelated missing-image transport regression. Its changes are not included here.
- Pre-commit passes. No model computation, GT, tolerance, or performance baseline changes; no speedup claim.

This is request-level isolation for malformed scheduler messages and tensor decoding errors, not general failover. Transfer-control validation, dead/hung-worker supervision, head restart recovery and durable jobs remain separate concerns. The internal pickle transport must remain on a trusted network.

title: [Fix] scheduler: Keep long prefill steps in the busy counter and exclude engine pauses
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

`Scheduler._record_step_counters` maintains `total_prefill_busy_us` and `total_prefill_uncached_tokens`. Both are published in the engine's load reports, and the router uses their deltas to estimate prefill throughput (uncached tokens per busy second) and, from that, the queue time of the waiting uncached tokens. Today any prefill step whose duration reaches `STEP_MAX_US` (2 s) contributes neither busy time nor uncached tokens, so both cumulative counters omit that work. With long prompts or large chunk sizes a single prefill step can exceed 2 s, and then the busy time an engine reports can be a small fraction of the time it actually spent in prefill forwards, while the throughput estimate is taken from the short steps only.

The cap dates from launch-to-launch prefill timing, where a long gap could be idle time. Prefill steps are now charged from the batch launch, or from the previous prefill's result when the two are back to back, to this step's result, and every idle loop iteration sets `_sched_idled`, which breaks the back-to-back chain. Idle time is therefore already excluded, and the cap only discards real work.

One wait skipped that idle flag: a paused engine. While `_engine_paused` is set the disaggregation prefill loops `continue` before setting `_sched_idled`, and the overlap loop holds an in-flight prefill result until resume. Without the cap, the first prefill after a pause would be charged the whole pause (in the unit test, two 0.125 s prefills around a pause of about 10 s would count about 10.25 s).

## Modifications

- Prefill steps are no longer discarded at `STEP_MAX_US`. The cap still applies to decode and target-verify launch cadence, where a gap that long is a stall and not a cadence sample.
- The scheduler records pause windows, from `pause_generation` to `continue_generation`, and subtracts their overlap from each prefill step, so a pause never counts as busy time:
  - An in-place pause starts its window at the call. A first retract starts its window only after the in-flight result has drained, because draining waits for that forward to finish. A repeated pause keeps the first start.
  - A result processed while the pause is still open (an in-place pause followed by a retract drains the held result before resume) excludes the pause so far.
  - Later prefill steps start at or after the previous step's end, so a closed window is dropped once a recorded step ends after it. `PAUSE_WINDOWS_MAX` (1024) bounds the deque; it would only lose a needed window if more than 1024 pauses happened inside one prefill step.
- Nothing else changes: where prefill steps start and end, the decode cadence cap, the load reports and the router's use of them are untouched.
- Tests: `test_disagg_idle_step_counters.py` gains cases for a long prefill step being charged while a long decode gap is not, a pause between prefills, a result held across a pause, a result processed during an open pause, many pauses inside one step, a pause inside an idle gap, and a repeated pause keeping one window. `test_scheduler_pause_generation.py` checks when a retract starts its window. The two unit-test scheduler stubs gain the new attributes.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no model or kernel code changes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: a sum over a bounded deque per prefill result, on the scheduler's host path.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (isort, ruff, ruff format and codespell at the pinned versions are clean on the changed files.)
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (`test/registered/unit/managers/test_disagg_idle_step_counters.py`, `test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_pause_generation.py` and `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_prefill_result_polling.py` pass locally on CPU.)
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [Fix] dp-attention: Align prefill graph buckets and decode padding across DP ranks
author: ispobock
body:
## Summary
Two DP-attention padding changes:
- With breakable prefill CUDA graphs, every DP rank pads to the same captured token bucket. An idle rank keeps the padded shape for the collectives; a backend that opts in also skips its attention metadata there.
- Decode picks SUM_LEN padding, one TP all-reduce of the summed rows, when the gather spans several ranks, every rank has tokens, the summed buffer fits the CustomAllReduceV2 buffer, and there is no MoE all-to-all or speculative decoding. Otherwise the existing cost-based choice applies.

## Changes to existing code
- `forward_batch_info`: `global_num_tokens` is rounded up to the smallest captured prefill bucket on every rank.
- `DpPaddingMode`: decode selects SUM_LEN under the condition above, both eagerly and in `get_default_mode_in_cuda_graph`, which now receives the captured per-rank token counts.
- `AttentionBackend.skips_prefill_metadata_on_idle_dp_rank` (default `False`): when a backend sets it, `PrefillCudaGraphRunner` skips `init_forward_metadata` and the read snapshot on a rank with no real tokens. No existing backend sets it, so their replay is unchanged.

The prefill change affects every model that uses DP attention with breakable prefill graphs; the decode padding change affects DP-attention decode without idle ranks.

## Verification
- test_dp_attention, test_dsa_backend_dp_padding (an idle rank still selects MAX_LEN), test_runtime_context, test_prefill_cuda_graph_padding, test_prefill_cuda_graph_runner, test_prefill_cuda_graph_runner_helpers, test_prefill_shared_read_done

title: [Fix] diffusion/server: Clean up workers on startup failure
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

The three diffusion launchers wait for startup pipes in rank order. If a later rank exits while an earlier rank is still initializing (for example, waiting in NCCL), startup can remain blocked. Pool and standalone-role launchers also retain parent-side pipe writers, hiding EOF. A failed later pool role can leave earlier roles running.

- Share one spawn/readiness helper across monolithic, local-pool and standalone-role launchers. Start every rank before waiting, then watch both startup pipes and all child process sentinels.
- Close parent-side pipe handles and terminate/reap started workers on startup errors, spawn failures or interrupts.
- Clean up previously started pool roles and the router when a subsequent startup step fails.
- Preserve the spawn bootstrap contract and rank/device mapping. No new flags, polling loop, runtime work or production modules; production code is 52 lines smaller.

## Validation

Tested at `3c1c895f8f94` on Linux with 2x H200, Python 3.12.15, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, diffusers 0.37.0 and transformers 5.19.0.

- Related shutdown, worker-bootstrap and load-inclusive timing suites: **38 passed, 13 subtests passed**.
- Real child-process tests cover out-of-order readiness, later-rank exit, explicit startup error, EOF while a child remains alive, a ready rank exiting, spawn failure and interruption. Pool tests also cover a later-role failure and router-bind failure.
- GPU fault injection reproduced blocked startup on `74c08f3dc5d` in all three launch paths. The fix reports the failed rank after cleanup in **90 ms / 81 ms / 83 ms** (monolithic / local pool / standalone role), with no live child processes on return. With an encoder already loaded, a failing denoiser is reported after cleanup in **2.29 s**.
- Real Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B generation passed for single-GPU, two-GPU, local-pool and independently launched encoder/denoiser/decoder paths: 512x320, 17 frames, 4 steps, seed 42, FA. The two-GPU decoded frames are byte-identical to the same-configuration baseline; the single-rank paths also agree with each other. No GT or thresholds changed.
- Pre-commit passed. No startup-speed claim is made from the single-sample smoke timings.

This handles observable startup failures, not arbitrary hangs in still-live workers. It does not add automatic restarts or durable job recovery. Runtime readiness monitoring remains separate in #46025.

title: [Fix] diffusion/disagg: Recompute automatic topology per role
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Disaggregated launchers clone an already-normalized `ServerArgs`. Resetting only TP/SP/Ulysses/Ring leaves automatic HSDP, CFG and K/V-gather choices from the parent in each worker. For example, a two-GPU parent with a one-GPU encoder fails before loading with `num_gpus (1) must be >= and divisible by hsdp_shard_dim (2)`.

The standalone launcher also duplicates topology validation without accounting for Ulysses/Ring overrides, and both paths overwrite explicit generic TP/SP with unset role-specific values.

## Modifications

- Share role argument derivation between pool and standalone launchers. Recompute automatic topology for the role's device count; preserve explicit user settings and use the existing validation.
- Apply role-specific flags before generic flags, then automatic defaults. Document this precedence.
- Cover shrinking/growing role GPU counts, CFG, HSDP, K/V-gather, explicit overrides, invalid layouts and parent immutability in the existing test file.
- Isolate the existing offload-policy test's mocked memory from the actual host GPU name. This test also failed on the unmodified base on H200; policy and assertions are unchanged.

Production code: 51 additions / 89 deletions across two existing files. No new flags, production files or request-path work.

title: [Fix] [AMD] dsv4.1: Fix decode graph capture with quantized low-ratio activations
author: kevin-mii
body:
## Motivation

sgl-project/sglang#45407 made `forward_low_ratio_sources` cut `x` and `q_lora` to the hoisted rows on every step (`x[:n]`, `q_lora[:n]`); before, it cut them only when DP attention padded an eager extend. On ROCm, `q_lora` (and on some routes `x`) reaches it quantized, as an `Mxfp8Activation` (q and scale) or an `Fp8GridActivation`: structs that refuse a slice. Since #45407, a DeepSeek-V4.1 server on MI35x fails while capturing its decode graphs (seen with `--monokernel-backend amd`; the failing call is SGLang's own forward, which every decode step of a plain server runs):

```
File ".../layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend.py", line 3402, in forward_low_ratio_sources
    q_lora = q_lora[:n]

title: [Fix] diffusion/serving: Reclaim abandoned shared-memory replies
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

Large local scheduler replies are spilled to `/dev/shm`, but only the receiving client removes them. If an RPC times out or is cancelled before the reply arrives, the scheduler still writes the result and no process deletes it. Repeated abandoned frame-return RPCs can exhaust shared memory.

- Scope reply files to a private directory owned by each sync/async RPC. Advertise its opaque name through the existing local ZMQ routing identity; no request payload or model changes.
- Retire the directory atomically before cleanup so a late producer cannot create new files during deletion.
- Keep inline transport for unmanaged clients, unavailable shared memory, and failed writes. Keep warning keys stable across requests.
- Extend the existing IPC/client tests and document cleanup boundaries. No new knobs or files.

## Validation

Remote Linux/H200 testing:

- 119 tests and 6 subtests passed, including timeout/cancellation before and after spill, invalid replies, write/cleanup races, concurrent ownership, and existing scheduler/health/video/disaggregation/CUDA IPC coverage. Two sync cancellation cases are skipped because synchronous calls use transport timeouts.
- 128 real ZMQ requests at concurrency 8, with 32 MiB replies: 64 completed, 64 cancelled after spill, no stale files or mixed-up replies.
- Real Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B generation (`768x512`, 33 frames, 4 steps, FA, seed 42): complete, cancel, complete. The old implementation leaves a 37 MiB file; this branch leaves none. All successful old/new frame arrays are byte-identical; health and liveness remain healthy.
- Repeated the generation/cancellation sequence with two H200 DP replicas, then drained both replicas with successful requests: no residual files, and old/new outputs are byte-identical under the same DP2 topology. DP1 and DP2 hashes differ on both versions, so cross-topology identity is not claimed.
- A 5,000-request short-RPC measurement adds approximately 29 microseconds median latency for directory ownership (147 to 176 microseconds). This is a correctness fix, not a speedup claim.

Timeout/cancellation stops waiting, not GPU work already executing. Hard process kills cannot execute cleanup; deployments should isolate their shared-memory lifetime. This does not change CUDA IPC tensor retention or the async progress API.

title: [Fix] diffusion/cli: Preserve explicit argv and registered aliases
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

`prepare_server_args(argv)` parses its argument list, but `get_provided_args()` then checks `sys.argv` to decide which values were explicit. Embedded launchers can lose their model path or flags, or accidentally treat unrelated process flags as user overrides.

Separately, the hand-maintained alias table misses `--pipeline`, so a parsed pipeline selection can be silently dropped.

## Modifications

- Pass explicit `argv` through argument provenance tracking; retain the process-argv fallback for existing CLI callers.
- Resolve aliases from argparse's registered destinations instead of a second alias table.
- Add focused regression coverage in the existing server-args tests, including explicit `false` and omitted defaults.

No new flags, modules, inference behavior, or default placement changes. Production code: +21/-16 lines; tests: +44 lines.

- Real Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B server with `--pipeline WanPipeline --mode manual --dit-cpu-offload false`: explicit Python argv preserved without modifying `sys.argv`; two consecutive 512x320, 17-frame, 4-step requests succeeded with identical raw-frame hashes. title: [Fix] diffusion/openai: Bound job lists and complete cursor pagination

Previously, omitting `limit` serialized every stored job. Responses also omitted `last_id` and `has_more`, so the OpenAI video iterator could stop after the first page.

title: [Fix] diffusion/scheduler: Isolate invalid IPC requests
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

One invalid scheduler message can discard unrelated requests received in the same poll. The previous exception filter missed errors such as an unsupported pickle protocol or a missing request module, and CUDA IPC reconstruction happened over the entire batch. On multiple ranks, a rank-0 decoding failure can also prevent the expected broadcast.

- Decode, normalize and reconstruct IPC references per message before adding it to the batch.
- Return an error for invalid payloads in complete REQ envelopes. A failed nonblocking error reply does not discard valid requests.
- Keep the existing valid-request broadcast and execution paths. Remove the redundant catch-and-reraise wrapper; production code grows by nine lines in one existing file.
- Extend the existing scheduler-client tests and clarify internal transport and timeout boundaries in the CLI docs.

This complements #46120 for the monolithic scheduler receive path. It is request isolation, not authentication, general GPU recovery, or backpressure. Pickle endpoints must remain on a trusted network.

## Validation

- Remote baseline: all six malformed-message cases fail. Fixed related suite: **110 passed**, including CUDA IPC round-trips and rejection-send backpressure coverage.
- Two real CPU/Gloo ranks: SP, CFG and TP request-broadcast paths each preserve the same valid requests across three malformed-payload cases. This is a collective transport test, not multi-GPU model inference.
- Real **Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B / 1x H200**, FA, 512x320, 17 frames, four steps, seed 42: pause the owned worker briefly to queue two HTTP video requests together with an invalid internal message, then resume it. Before the fix both valid jobs remain queued through their polling windows, while health is 200 and a later request succeeds. After the fix only the invalid message returns an error; both videos and the recovery request complete.
- All successful before/after videos have identical decoded pixel hashes. Both servers shut down cleanly without remaining child processes.
- Pre-commit passed. No model math, GT, tolerance or baseline changes; no performance claim.

The suite needs a writable Hugging Face cache. Internal RPC timeout/cancellation stops the caller waiting; it does not cancel already submitted GPU work.

Environment: Python 3.12.15, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Diffusers 0.37.0, PyZMQ 27.2.0.

title: [Fix] [AMD] rotary: Pass a query-dtype cos_sin_cache to the HIP fallback
author: rbrugaro-amd
body:
## Motivation

On ROCm, Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 does not start on current `main`  6d6c9cd4ae (main as of 2026-10-23 00:50 PDT). CUDA graph capture fails on MI355X with:

```
Exception: Capture cuda graph failed: expected scalar type BFloat16 but found Float
```

HIP keeps `cos_sin_cache` in fp32 for the fused QSA indexer (#41282). `main` already has `cos_sin_cache_as()` to hand kernels a cached copy in the activation dtype, but the HIP branch of the `fallback_rotary_embedding` path in `rotary_embedding/base.py` does not use it. It passes the fp32 buffer to `sgl_kernel.rotary_embedding`, which reads the cache as the query dtype.

#42483 fixed this by adding a private helper and using it at this call site. It was closed as redundant. Since then `main` gained the equivalent public helper, but not the call-site change, so the crash remains. This PR is only that missing half.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py`, fallback branch of `forward_cuda`:

- On HIP, pass `self.cos_sin_cache_as(query.dtype)` to `fallback_rotary_embedding` instead of the fp32 buffer. The fp32 buffer stays in place for the indexer. The cast copy is reused until the buffer is replaced (moved or extended), so steady state adds no cast.
- Only move the buffer when it is on a different device than the query.
- Non-HIP behaviour is unchanged: the buffer is still cast in place to the query device and dtype.

`test/registered/unit/layers/test_rope_hip_fallback_cache_dtype.py`: CPU unit test (`base-a-test-cpu`) that drives the HIP fallback branch with a mocked kernel and checks, for fp16 and bf16:

- the kernel receives the cache in the query dtype, with values equal to the fp32 buffer cast down;
- a second call reuses the same copy, and `cos_sin_cache` is still the original fp32 buffer;
- extending the cache invalidates the copy, and the next call gets a fresh one at the new length.

It fails on `main` with `AssertionError: torch.float32 != torch.float16`.

## Accuracy Tests

4× MI355X (gfx950), TP4, `Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8`, image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.20-rocm724-mi35x-20260929`, on `main` 6d6c9cd4ae with this change applied:

- Without the change, the server fails CUDA graph capture as above and does not start.
- With it, the server starts, and GSM8K 1319q (`python -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 1319 --parallel 256`) scores **0.942**, `Invalid: 0.000`.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Not a performance change. The fallback now gets a cast copy that is built once and then reused, instead of the fp32 buffer it could not consume.
