title: [Fix] diffusion/api: Do not publish failed generation outputs
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

Reject worker errors before processing any partial output in the OpenAI and Vertex generation entrypoints.

`GPUWorker` can attach an error to an existing `OutputBatch` when output finalization fails. The deferred-save path can also retain encoded file paths. The HTTP layer previously checked only whether output was present, so failed requests could return images or become video jobs with `status=completed` and `progress=100`.

Also harden the Vertex response boundary:

- Reject missing or empty output files per instance instead of returning an empty success.
- Serialize request metrics with the existing `to_dict()` contract, including denoising-stage sets and memory snapshots.
- Move file reads and base64 encoding off the HTTP event loop so slow output storage does not block health checks.
- Validate the whole input batch before creating scheduler coroutines. Invalid prompts or dimensions return HTTP 400 without leaving unawaited coroutines or dispatching earlier valid instances.

Successful outputs, control RPC semantics and empty-batch behavior are preserved. This does not add retries, delete user-owned files, or change model computation.

## Tests

- Extend existing tests for tensor, encoded-file/image-byte, raw-frame and empty error results, followed by a successful request.
- Exercise the real generation-result handler from image generation/edit routes, with and without persistent output, plus video-job failure state and Vertex output handling. Previously the image fixture mocked that handler out.
- H200 development environment: 159 related tests passed. Regression tests reproduce the original error-publication, output-file, metrics-serialization and invalid-input failures. The input fixtures use local metadata rather than downloading a checkpoint.
- Real HTTP/GPU validation with Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B, 512x320, 17 frames, four steps: inject finalization failures before/after output transport. The unpatched version incorrectly completes both jobs. With the fix, synchronous and `--async-output-save` serving each report both failures, reject content retrieval, and recover on the next request. Both recovery videos match the pre-fault decoded-frame hash.
- Additional real Vertex HTTP/GPU validation with the same model and dimensions, default seed 42 and 50 steps: nine input-boundary cases followed by recovery; missing/empty/slow output reads; and three instances with one failed delivery and two successful predictions. Twelve real generations total, three injected delivery failures. All nine successful outputs decode correctly and match the baseline decoded-frame hash. Health checks remain responsive during the stalled file read, and owned worker processes exit after shutdown.

This is bounded fault/recovery coverage, not a claim of durable jobs or cross-node failover. Legacy raw-output encoding and final JSON serialization remain synchronous; host-memory admission is unchanged.

The separate async-video-progress PR #45919 remains unchanged by this fix.

title: [Fix] diffusion/http: Allow bounded graceful shutdown
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

A client that never finishes sending a request body can keep the HTTP server waiting after SIGTERM. `--scheduler-rpc-timeout` cannot help: this request has not reached the scheduler.

Add `--http-graceful-shutdown-timeout`, forwarded to Uvicorn's existing graceful shutdown timeout. Unset preserves the current unlimited wait; zero cancels outstanding HTTP tasks without waiting. Invalid config values fail validation. No inference, kernel, or worker scheduling changes.

Document that this bounds HTTP draining only, not application cleanup/GPU teardown or asynchronous video job completion. Deployments still need a termination grace period and their own durability/retry policy.

## Validation

- New CLI/config/launcher regression tests fail against unmodified main and pass with the fix.
- H200, Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B, real HTTP, 512x320, 17 frames, 4 steps: generated and decoded a video before holding a multipart upload open and sending SIGTERM. With timeouts 0 and 2, shutdown took 0.36s and 2.42s without closing the client connection. No workers survived.
- With the default unset, the server was still waiting after 3s; closing the client let it exit. Decoded frame hashes matched across all three configurations.
- The full server-args/shutdown/load-time suite initially reported 246 passed plus one existing H200-sensitive LTX fixture failure. That same failure reproduces on unmodified main: the fixture mocks memory capacity but reads the real GPU name. No thresholds or test expectations changed here.

title: [Fix] swa: Start the SWA KV pool at its first layer under pipeline parallelism
author: Jiminator
body:
## Motivation

Under pipeline parallelism, a later stage's `SWAKVPool` holds global layer ids, but it reports `start_layer = 0`. Code that reads the pool's first layer through `start_layer` then asks for a layer the stage doesn't have.

For example, `TritonAttnBackend.__init__` reads `get_value_buffer(token_to_kv_pool.start_layer)` when the model isn't mambaish and the SWA and full value head dims match. On a hybrid-SWA model with `--attention-backend triton` and `--pp-size 2`, the second stage fails at startup (main at `1ced9a9eb0`):

```text
File ".../layers/attention/triton_backend.py", line 311, in __init__
    self.v_head_dim = model_runner.token_to_kv_pool.get_value_buffer(
File ".../mem_cache/swa_memory_pool.py", line 262, in get_value_buffer
    layer_id_pool, is_swa_layer = self.layers_mapping[layer_id]
KeyError: 0
```

Split out of #45256 at review; found while adding Beam (#44747).

## Modifications

- `SWAKVPool.start_layer` is now the smallest layer id the pool holds, as `routed_draft_pool` already does with `min(layer_ids)`. On the tested pipeline split this is the stage's first global layer, the value plain pools get from the configurator. Pools that hold layer 0 keep the same start, inner-pool indexing is unchanged, and a pool with no layers keeps 0.
- HiCache on later stages becomes stage-local. `_swa_layer_mappings` and the load waits (`KVLayerRouter._wait`) subtract the same `start_layer`, so they stay consistent. HiCache already worked with the global ids, because the layer counter is sized to the largest id plus one and earlier stages' ids are skipped.
- A draft pool for an Inkling MTP depth holds only layer `k`. It now reports `k`, with or without pipeline parallelism, which `layer_info.start_layer` (0 there) wouldn't. A CPU check of window-only and full-only pools at depth 3 shows that on main `get_value_buffer(start_layer)` raises `KeyError: 0`, and that here `start_layer` is 3 and reads the same storage as the router, with `get_v_head_dim` unchanged. From reading the code, draft pools get no load counter. I didn't run an Inkling model.
- Readers that go through a sub-pool (`trtllm_mha`'s native FP4 buffers, `aiter`, `get_v_head_dim`, the HiCache host pools) use that sub-pool's own `start_layer`, which is still 0.
- `TestSWAPoolVHeadDim` moves to `CustomTestCase`, which the contribution guide requires for registered tests.

Not fixed by this PR:

- **PD with prefill `--pp-size 2` and decode `--pp-size 1` on a non-MLA SWA model.** `_transfer_start_layer` returns `start_layer`, but the peer's KV list holds only full-attention layers. On the model below the second stage needs offset 6, the full-attention layers before it. Main gives 0 and this PR gives 12. A CPU probe of the real pool, `_transfer_start_layer` and Mooncake's transfer builder, with a recording transport, shows:
  - Main: the second stage pairs with the first stage's entries, with no error (rc 0).
  - This PR: `IndexError` before any block is issued.
  - Offset 6 pairs correctly on both.

  No PD server pair was run, and NIXL and Mori weren't exercised. From reading the code, that `IndexError` would stop Mooncake's transfer thread, and peers at the same `--pp-size` with the same KV entries skip the offset because their lists match. The fix needs layer-aware pairing for the full-attention and SWA-state entries, as `HybridLinearKVPool` has, so I left it to a follow-up.
- **`openai/gpt-oss-20b` (MXFP4) under `--pp-size 2`.** It fails earlier on main, in `_load_mxfp4_experts_weights`, with `AttributeError: PPMissingLayer has no attribute mlp`. That's a separate loader bug, and it's why the runs below use the bf16 conversion.

## Accuracy Tests

**Unit and neighbouring tests**

- `test_swa_pool_v_head_dim.py` adds a case for a second-stage pool (layers 2 and 3). On main it fails with `KeyError: 0` at `swa_memory_pool.py:262`, the same line as the startup crash. It passes here.
- Neighbouring tests give the same results on main and here:
  - All 17 related CPU-registered test files pass, including `test_kv_cache_configurator_draft_gate.py`.
  - 9 GPU-registered files, on one GPU, give 339 passed, 57 skipped, 1 error on both. The error is a Gemma 4 server test that couldn't start on either tree: it asks for `--tp-size 2` with one GPU exposed, and its weights weren't cached. It doesn't use PP. The skips and that error give no coverage.

**Server runs: NVIDIA B300, two GPUs for PP2 and one for PP1; `lmsys/gpt-oss-20b-bf16` @ `8de8d3dfa4`**

The model has 24 layers alternating sliding (window 128) and full. Requests are greedy `/generate` calls with frozen `input_ids` of 24, 320, 1200 and 3400 tokens, `temperature=0`, `max_new_tokens=64`, `ignore_eos`.

| Run | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `--attention-backend triton --pp-size 2` | startup fails with `KeyError: 0` | starts; 4/4 prompts give the same tokens as this PR at `--pp-size 1` |
| `--attention-backend triton`, `--pp-size 1` | 4/4 prompts give the same tokens as this PR | 4/4 prompts give the same tokens as main |
| `--pp-size 2`, default backend (`trtllm_mha`), `--enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-size 4 --max-total-tokens 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.6`: serve, evict with four filler prompts, serve again | second pass host hits 0/256/1152/3392, device 0; 4/4 prompts on both passes give the same tokens as without HiCache | same host hits; 4/4 prompts on both passes give the same tokens as without HiCache, and the second pass matches main |
| `transfer_layer_id_max` logged by that run, first / second stage | 12 / 24 | 12 / 12 |

Limits on these runs:

- The 3400-token prompt's output has long runs of token 1131 in all three Triton runs (main at `--pp-size 1`, this PR at `--pp-size 1` and `2`), so that prompt says little about PP. Their 64 tokens match. The `trtllm_mha` runs first differ at the third token, but they also differ in memory flags and page size (64 vs 1), so the cause isn't isolated. The other three prompts, including the 320- and 1200-token ones that exceed the window, give the same tokens on both backends.
- The 24-token prompt is shorter than the 64-token page, so it gets no host hit. The second-pass check rests on the other three prompts.
- These are four-prompt parity checks; I ran no accuracy benchmark.
- I didn't run Triton with HiCache under `--pp-size 2`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

title: [Fix] request_logger: Skip watermark redaction when watermarking is disabled
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

Request logging (`--log-requests`) redacts watermark secrets on every logged request, even when the server was started without `--enable-watermark`. The redaction walk copies containers and token lists, so long prompts spend tokenizer-process CPU on a feature that is off. #44692 made the walk cheaper when it runs; this change skips it entirely when watermarking is disabled.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/utils/request_logger.py`: read the resolved `enable_watermark` flag from the `exec` config namespace. When it is false, `_redact_field` returns the value unchanged and the scalar and list fallbacks in both formatters render the data as is, without calling the redactor. When watermarking is enabled, redaction is unchanged. Standalone formatting with no published server config keeps redacting, so callers outside a server keep the safe default.
- `python/sglang/srt/sampling/watermarking/README.md`: document that request logs redact watermark keys only when `--enable-watermark` is set.

With the flag absent, watermark fields supplied by clients are logged without redaction; request validation is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Logging-only change; inference is untouched.

- `test/registered/unit/utils/test_request_logger_redaction.py`: 7 tests pass on this branch.
- Local behaviour check (not added to the tree): with `override_server_args()` and no `enable_watermark`, level-1 Receive/Finish logs in text and JSON format never iterate a skipped token list; with `enable_watermark=True` the same requests and raw OpenAI request logs still render `<redacted>` for watermark keys, and with it false the original values appear. Both checks fail on `main` and pass here.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run end to end. The change removes the per-field and per-list redaction calls when watermarking is off; when it is on, the code path is the same as before.

## Checklist

- [x] Pre-commit checks pass on the changed files.
- [x] Unit tests for the formatters pass.
- [x] Documentation updated.

title: [Fix] flashinfer: Apply the sliding window in ragged prefill for hybrid-SWA models
author: Jiminator
body:
## Motivation

On `--attention-backend flashinfer`, a hybrid sliding-window/full model's sliding layers attend past their window during ragged prefill.

FlashInfer selects the kernel module at plan time: `window_left >= 0` picks the variant with the sliding mask compiled in, and a `window_left` passed only to `forward` has no effect on a module planned without it. Main plans one ragged wrapper, shared by sliding and full layers, without the window. On SM100 there is a second cause: for the head dims it serves, that wrapper uses CUTLASS, whose ragged attention ignores the window even when it is planned. This is unchanged in FlashInfer 0.7.3, which main now pins: `fmha_varlen`, the CUTLASS ragged path, still builds its module with `use_sliding_window=False`.

A ragged wrapper planned with `window_left=511` on B300 (FlashInfer 0.7.2, lengths [1500, 700], 12 q heads, 2 KV heads, head dim 128, bf16), max absolute error against an fp32 reference:

| Backend | vs windowed reference | vs full-attention reference |
|---|---:|---:|
| CUTLASS | 0.390 | 0.0081 |
| FA2 | 0.0084 | 0.466 |

This was found while adding Beam (#44747) and is split out of #45256 at review. It affects every hybrid-SWA model that takes ragged prefill on this backend, not only Beam. Multimodal models, multi-item scoring, deterministic inference and `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_USE_PAGED` use the paged path instead.

## Modifications

Merged with main after the FlashInfer 0.7.3 bump (#48468), where a sliding-window read is a `WindowRead`.

- Each wrapper (sliding/full, or decoder/cross-attention) gets its own ragged prefill plan in `prefill_wrappers_ragged`, built with the other prefill wrappers, so `skip_prefill` backends allocate none. Backends with two wrappers gain one more FlashInfer ragged wrapper and its workspace.
- The sliding wrapper's ragged plan takes `window.window`. `window.window_left` is -1 on this read because it belongs to the paged pass, which main keeps to the window with its custom prefix mask.
- The no-prefix ragged forward now passes the layer's `sliding_window_size`, as the prefix path already does.
- On SM100 the sliding ragged wrapper uses `fa2` where `cutlass` was selected, the same fallback the constructor uses for shapes CUTLASS does not serve. The override applies only to sliding wrappers otherwise assigned CUTLASS; full-attention wrappers stay on CUTLASS and other backend-selection rules are unchanged. It is still needed on FlashInfer 0.7.3, and the comment at the override names `fmha_varlen`'s hardcoded `use_sliding_window=False` and says to switch back to CUTLASS once that path honors `window_left`.
- The earlier paged-plan change in this PR is gone: on main, a ragged read already leaves the paged plan without the window.
- `test_flashinfer_window_verify.py` and `test_fused_draft_window_metadata.py` each change one line. They build the backend or updater with `__new__` and stub the single ragged wrapper, so they now set the list.

#34093 is open and overlaps this. It plans one shared ragged wrapper with the window, also passes `logits_soft_cap` at plan time, and leaves SM100 on CUTLASS. Both PRs change the same plan call.

## Accuracy Tests

### FlashInfer 0.7.3 (GB300)

4x GB300 (SM103), FlashInfer 0.7.3, torch 2.14.1+cu130, on this branch's current head. "main" is b966c2798e.

**Existing tests.** `test/registered/attention/unittests/swa/`, `test_flashinfer_window_verify.py`, `test_fused_draft_window_metadata.py` and `test_flashinfer_host_plan.py`: 40 passed, 78 subtests passed; one AMD gfx950-only case is skipped.

**Beam low-latency recipe.** `reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-NVFP4` (c5621fc926), TP4, with `reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2` (163b276be7), DFlash block size 8, cookbook flags. This branch and main on `--attention-backend flashinfer`, against main on `trtllm_mha`. GSM8K is sgl-eval 0.1.3, 1,319 questions, temperature 0.

| | main `trtllm_mha` | main `flashinfer` | this branch `flashinfer` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GSM8K | 95.98% | 96.21% | 96.13% |
| Accept length, c=1 / 16 / 64 | 4.61 / 4.48 / 4.18 | 4.58 / 4.49 / 4.20 | 4.62 / 4.50 / 4.20 |

The three scores are within 0.23 points (3 of 1,319 questions), so GSM8K does not separate the arms; the prompt logprobs below do.

Prompt logprobs for fixed token-id prompts of 700, 1800, 2600 and 3000 tokens, mean absolute difference (max) against main `trtllm_mha`, by query position:

| Query position | main `flashinfer` | this branch `flashinfer` |
|---|---:|---:|
| up to 511 (n=2044) | 0.0403 (0.86) | 0.0443 (0.80) |
| 512 to 1023 (n=1724), past window | 0.6675 (11.92) | 0.0425 (1.69) |
| 1024 and up (n=4328) | 2.4893 (15.43) | 0.0268 (0.63) |

These agree approximately, not bitwise: `flashinfer` and `trtllm_mha` are different kernels.

### Earlier: B300, FlashInfer 0.7.2

Measured on B300 (SM103) with FlashInfer 0.7.2 and torch 2.14.1+cu130, before main moved to 0.7.3. "main" is 3a345c0743.

**Existing tests.** On this branch, `test/registered/attention/unittests/swa/` passes (23 passed, 49 subtests). Neighbouring planner tests give the same counts on main and this branch (35 passed, 68 subtests; 232 passed, 58 subtests), including `test_flashinfer_window_verify`, `test_fused_draft_window_metadata` and `test_flashinfer_host_plan`.

Static trace: target verify, graph-replayed draft extend and full-graph extend use paged plans; eager draft extend can take the corrected ragged path. Non-SWA DLLM extend and cross-attention keep their existing masking arguments.

**Beam prompt logprobs.** `reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-NVFP4` (c5621fc926), TP4 on 4x B300, `--chunked-prefill-size 1024 --disable-radix-cache --mem-fraction-static 0.85`, token-id prompts of 700, 1800, 2600 and 3000 tokens. Mean absolute logprob difference (max) against `--attention-backend trtllm_mha` on main, by query position, with the ratio to the in-window row:

| Query position | Path | main `flashinfer` | this branch `flashinfer` |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| up to 511 (n=2048) | no-prefix, in window | 0.0824 (2.55) | 0.0898 (2.78) |
| 512 to 1023 (n=1723) | no-prefix, past window | 0.6627 (11.20), 8.04x | 0.0747 (3.54), 0.83x |
| 1024 and up (n=4325) | ragged + paged merge | 0.3419 (15.51), 4.15x | 0.0594 (2.24), 0.66x |

- In-window positions move with the kernel change: this branch differs from main's `flashinfer` by a mean of 0.0847 (max 2.33), about the same as either differs from `trtllm_mha`.
- Adding the cookbook's `--page-size 64 --context-length 1048576 --enable-unified-memory` gives the same numbers on both branches.
- A probe in all 4 TP processes shows main planning only CUTLASS with `window_left=-1`, and this branch planning FA2 with `window_left=511` for sliding layers and CUTLASS with -1 for full layers.
- `trtllm_mha` on this branch returns identical logprob values to main (8096 compared, max difference 0.0).

**Speculative decoding.** These check the draft side of the change. They are not accuracy results.

- Windowed draft: a draft model with a sliding window takes the same ragged path in its prefill. `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct` with `lmsys/sglang-EAGLE3-LLaMA3.1-Instruct-8B`, EAGLE3 steps 3, topk 1, draft tokens 4, `--speculative-draft-window-size 512`, `--dtype float16`, 8 prompts of 600 to 3300 tokens, greedy, 256 new tokens: overall accept length 2.151 on main and 2.160 here. Target outputs are identical on all 8 prompts, and 4 prompts change by one verify step.
- Hybrid target: Beam's prefill output on `flashinfer` changes, and the drafter conditions on it. Overall accept length with `reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2` (163b276be7), block size 8, cookbook flags, greedy, 256 new tokens:

| Prompts | `trtllm_mha` | main `flashinfer` | this branch `flashinfer` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 16 x 480 tokens (prefill inside the window) | 3.531 | 3.371 | 3.451 |
| 16 x 2048 tokens | 4.577 | not run | 4.271 |
| the 4 prompts above | 3.368 | 3.821 | 3.200 |

Inside the window this branch matches main within noise (1.02x; per-prompt mean +0.05, sd 0.30), and both `flashinfer` arms sit below `trtllm_mha`. Past the window this branch is 0.93x `trtllm_mha` on 16 prompts (higher on 5) and 0.84x main on 4; main's target logprobs are wrong there (table above), so its number is not a correct-output baseline, and why it is higher was not investigated. On the 2 prompts whose 256 tokens match `trtllm_mha`, accept length is 7.529 vs 7.314 and 7.529 vs 7.529 (this branch first). Each arm's draft ran on its target's backend (logged), so the comparison does not hold the draft backend fixed.

These are acceptance measurements, not accuracy or parity results.

Beam's cookbook recipes use `trtllm_mha` or `fa3`, not `flashinfer`. `trtllm_mha`'s target logprobs are unchanged here.

### Not covered

- Validated on Blackwell (B300, GB300) only. Windowed ragged plans on Hopper, where `auto` may resolve to FA3, were not run.
- This covers hybrid-SWA dispatch only. A layer with a window on a model that does not expose it to the runner still plans without it, as on main.
- `test_flashinfer_window_verify.py`'s `ragged_prefix` case checks the window the ragged forward receives on the prefix path. No unit test pins the no-prefix forward's window, the plan-time window, or the SM100 FA2 selection.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Measured on B300 with FlashInfer 0.7.2, before main moved to 0.7.3. Sliding layers' ragged prefill on SM100 moves from CUTLASS to FA2 where CUTLASS was selected. Full layers stay on CUTLASS. Main's numbers below are unwindowed, wrong attention, so these show the cost of the fix, not a speedup.

Kernel time: ragged `forward` with SGLang's plan and forward arguments, 12 q heads, 2 KV heads, head dim 128, bf16, inputs rotated over at least 256 MiB, 10 warmup and 60 timed runs, median in microseconds:

| Request lengths | main (CUTLASS, no window) | this branch (FA2, window 511) | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 36.6 | 44.9 | +23% |
| 1024 | 40.5 | 65.0 | +60% |
| 2048 | 52.1 | 52.1 | 0% |
| 8192 | 225.0 | 106.5 | -53% |
| 16384 | 726.9 | 184.6 | -75% |
| 32768 | 2500.6 | 349.6 | -86% |
| 8 x 2048 | 173.7 | 171.3 | -1% |
| 4 x 8192 | 675.0 | 329.5 | -51% |

`forward_return_lse`, which the prefix path uses, shows the same pattern. One plan takes 124 to 1506 us on CUTLASS and 69 to 163 us on FA2 at these shapes.

End to end: Beam TP4 on `flashinfer`, radix cache off, `/generate` with `max_new_tokens=1`, median of 5 runs after 1 warmup, in milliseconds. The two groups use different server flags, so compare within a group only:

| Prompt tokens | Server | main | this branch | Change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | chunk 1024, cookbook flags | 24.54 | 24.59 | +0.2% |
| 1024 | chunk 1024, cookbook flags | 29.43 | 30.58 | +3.9% |
| 1536 | chunk 1024, cookbook flags | 52.18 | 53.32 | +2.2% |
| 2048 | default chunk (16384) | 43.89 | 43.50 | -0.9% |
| 8192 | default chunk (16384) | 110.39 | 103.12 | -6.6% |
| 16384 | default chunk (16384) | 213.30 | 186.54 | -12.5% |
| 32000 | default chunk (16384) | 460.39 | 415.04 | -9.9% |

Prompts of about 1000 to 1500 tokens cost 2 to 4% more; the +0.2% at 512 is within run-to-run spread. The window limits the keys each sliding-layer query reads, which is the likely reason long prompts take less time, but this was not profiled. Both arms in the first group ran with the dispatch probe loaded.

title: [Fix] attention: Zero padded KDA/GDN recurrent outputs
author: Jzz1943
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

During padded CUDA Graph replay, the variable-length KDA/GDN recurrent kernel leaves padded output rows uninitialized. Stale NaNs in these rows can propagate through downstream operations and corrupt valid-token outputs.

For example, replaying a batch-8 graph with seven active requests writes only seven output rows, leaving the last row unwritten. This fix makes the unused output tail deterministically zero.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- Zero the output tail beyond `cu_seqlens[-1]` in the existing kernel, preserving valid-token outputs and recurrent state updates without an additional kernel launch.
- Extend the existing ragged kernel tests to replay the same CUDA Graph with different active-token counts for both KDA and GDN, checking zero padding, valid outputs, and recurrent state preservation.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

- Existing kernel test file: **9 passed**. Both added parameterized cases fail before the fix and pass after it.
- GLM-5.3-Flash, TP4/EP4 on 4 × H200 with BF16 recurrent states: GSM8K, 1,314 examples × 2 runs, **95.8% and 95.7%**.
- Pre-commit checks passed for both changed files.

```bash
python -m pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_kda_replayssm_ring_ragged.py
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

N/A — correctness fix.

title: [Fix] diffusion: Preserve metrics collectives after output save errors
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

Keep replica ranks aligned when output persistence fails with perf/memory collection enabled.

Only the output rank saves the generated file. Previously, a save error skipped its replica peak-memory collective while peers still entered it. The affected job failed, but subsequent healthy requests could time out because the other ranks were stuck. This moves the existing memory finalization into `finally`, without swallowing the original save error or changing the success path's collective count.

## Tests

- Extend the existing perf-report test: the output rank must still join memory collection on failure, propagate the save error, and avoid writing a successful perf report.
- Add a small Wan HTTP/GPU regression covering single GPU, dynamic batch2, DP2, Ulysses2, TP2 and CFG2. It exercises concurrent/multi-output jobs, queued deletion, output-save failure, RPC timeout, late results and subsequent generation. Recovery videos are decoded and compared with a same-topology serial reference.
- Single- and two-GPU CI lanes run their respective cases once, on diffusion partition 0. No new model family, GT, or relaxed thresholds.

The production change is limited to one existing finalization function. This is independent of #45919; it does not add progress reporting, persistent jobs, worker failover, or recovery from arbitrary CUDA faults. RPC timeout still does not cancel GPU work.

## Validation

Dedicated H200 development environment, Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers, 512x320, 17 frames, 4/12 steps, seed 42. PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, CUDA 13, Transformers 5.19.0, Diffusers 0.37.0.

- Before the fix: the targeted unit regression fails; the real Ulysses2 test reproduces a scheduler timeout on a healthy request after the injected save failure.
- After the fix (`b1071bde545`): 13 unit tests pass; real registered-entry-point E2E passes all six configurations (four two-GPU cases in 356.14s, two one-GPU cases in 153.43s). Recovered decoded frames match their same-topology serial references. The final GPU process list is empty.
- Pre-commit passes, including the registered-test checks. The 1-GPU and 2-GPU runs explicitly skip the other lane's configurations rather than counting them twice.

This is functional recovery coverage, not a latency benchmark or long-duration availability guarantee.

title: [Fix] [AMD] dsv4.1: Fix the V4.1 k-norm-rope store build on ROCm 10
author: kevin-mii
body:
## Motivation

sgl-project/sglang#45934 added a warp-per-token V4.1 kernel to `main_norm_rope.cuh` whose two reductions shuffle with `__shfl_xor_sync(0xffffffffu, ...)`. ROCm 10's HIP headers `static_assert` a 64-bit mask (wave64), so the V4.1 fused k-norm-rope store (`fused_k_norm_rope_flashmla`, V41 layout) no longer builds on gfx950.

Every PR's `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` shard 1 has failed on `test_v41_kv_store.py` since then, for example [on sgl-project/sglang#46151](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40030122510/job/120684541903). #45934's own AMD run was cancelled before that stage ran.

```
main_norm_rope.cuh:513:18: note: in instantiation of function template specialization '__shfl_xor_sync<unsigned int, float>' requested here
amd_warp_sync_functions.h:307:62: error: static assertion failed due to requirement 'sizeof(unsigned int) == 8': The mask must be a 64-bit integer.
RuntimeError: Failed to build JIT module sgl_kernel_jit_dpsk_v4_main_k_norm_rope_flashmla_bf16_t_512_64_256_V41_false
```

A 64-bit full mask builds but is wrong:
- HIP's `__shfl_xor_sync` traps unless every lane its mask names is active.
- This kernel returns per 32-lane warp, so an odd token count leaves half of the last wave64 idle.
- With that mask, 2049, 4097 and 4099 tokens crash with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION`.

## Modifications

- The two reductions call `shfl_xor_in_warp`, a forced-inline helper.
  - On CUDA it is main's `__shfl_xor_sync(0xffffffffu, v, mask)`, so CUDA compiles the same code as main.
  - On HIP it is the mask-free `__shfl_xor`, as `warp::reduce` already uses on HIP.
  - The loops and the reduction tree are unchanged. `kWarpThreads` is 32 on HIP too, so each 32-lane half of a wave64 holds one token, and every xor mask (2, 1, 16, 8, 4) stays inside it.
- `test_v41_kv_store.py`'s warp-per-token case takes 4097 tokens instead of 4096, so the last wave64 runs half idle.

## Accuracy Tests

MI350X (gfx950), ROCm 10.0.0, this branch on main 3c6a6c80:

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/test_v41_kv_store.py`: 8 passed.
  - On main it fails to build with the error above.
  - With a 64-bit full mask instead, its 4097-token case traps.
- The fused k-norm-rope store check at 2049, 4097, 4099 and 4100 tokens: bitwise equal to the unfused kernel chain.
- The other AMD-registered tests that build `main_norm_rope.cuh`:
  - `test_hip_flash_mla_aiter_sparse.py`: 7 passed;
  - `test_swapab_attention.py`: 5 passed, 2 skipped;
  - `test_dsv4_q_rope_store.py`: 4 passed;
  - `test_minimax_m3_qk_norm_rope.py`: 24 passed.

Not executed:
- CUDA: no CUDA toolchain here. Instead, expanding the helper's CUDA branch at its two call sites and dropping the helper reproduces main's `main_norm_rope.cuh` byte for byte.
- pre-commit: its hooks are not cached on this box. Every changed line is under the 120-column clang-format limit.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speed change intended: CUDA compiles main's code, and HIP runs the same shuffles without the per-shuffle mask check. Not measured.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Fix] diffusion: Route realtime cleanup to the session owner
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Realtime generation chunks are pinned to a DP replica by session ID, but
`ReleaseRealtimeSessionReq` currently falls through to round-robin routing.
Disconnect cleanup can therefore reach the wrong worker and return
`released=False`, leaving the owning worker's session state resident until it
is reset or evicted.

## Modifications

- Recognize session-release requests in the existing shared routing helper.
  Both synchronous and asynchronous clients use the same owner as generation.
- Keep replica-wide control operations on their existing broadcast path and
  ordinary generation on round-robin. No new routing state or configuration.
- Extend existing tests with DP1/2/4 coverage and real two-replica ZMQ
  round trips using `RealtimeSessionCache`: chunk continuity, interleaved
  stateless requests, duplicate release and empty caches afterward.
- Correct the control-protocol module description to distinguish broadcast
  operations from session-scoped cleanup.

## Validation

On a Linux development environment, using the unmodified routing code with
the new tests: **4 failed, 168 passed**. Both real-socket tests reproduced a
release reaching replica 1 with `released=False` while replica 0 owned the session.
With the fix: **172 passed** across DP routing, scheduler clients and realtime
tests. Pre-commit passes.

The tests are discovered by the existing diffusion unit-test suite; no new
server/model CI job is added. This fixes cleanup ownership, not worker failover
or durable session recovery.

## Accuracy and Performance

No model inputs, denoising steps or kernels change. No inference speedup claim.

## Checklist

- [x] Pre-commit
- [x] Regression tests fail before the fix and pass afterward
- [x] Updated the affected protocol documentation

title: [Fix] diffusion/realtime: Keep frame payloads contiguous
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Large realtime frame batches use two WebSocket messages: a MessagePack header
followed by the raw payload. Under send backpressure, the event listener could
insert an error response between them. Clients then interpreted the error as
video data. A failure while generating the next chunk could also cancel the
previous chunk's unfinished send before reporting the error.

## Changes

- Serialize frame output and invalid-event responses with a per-session lock.
- Finish pending output before reporting a subsequent generation error. Client
  disconnect and cancellation retain their existing cancellation paths.
- Extend existing realtime tests; preserve generation/send overlap.
- Correct the SANA-WM cookbook and client example to handle both inline
  `frame_batch` and `frame_batch_header` + binary payload.

No new configuration, output queue, payload copy, or model changes. Production
code changes are limited to two existing files (+15/-10).

## Validation

- Linux realtime suite: **2 failed, 152 passed** before the fix; **154 passed**
  afterward, including on the final head. The protocol regression uses the real
  WebSocket and output adapter with deterministic ASGI send backpressure.
- Real SANA-WM streaming server on **1x H200**, 256x256, 4 steps, seed 42:
  five sessions per revision covering normal completion, invalid events,
  disconnect and reconnect. A test-only 100 ms delay after header writes exposes
  the transport interleaving. Baseline corruption reproduced; with the fix,
  all four invalid-event responses arrived outside frame pairs and video
  payload hashes matched the clean baseline. Health remained HTTP 200.
- The optional refiner was disabled for this lifecycle test. This is not a
  full-quality benchmark, a speedup claim, or proof of failover/long-run HA.
- Pre-commit passes. No new GPU CI job is added.

title: [Fix] diffusion/realtime: Reserve generation slots after initialization
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Opening a realtime WebSocket currently reserves the only active generation slot before the client sends `init`. An idle connection, or one that keeps sending invalid initialization messages, can block valid clients indefinitely.

## Modifications

- Reserve the slot only after initialization succeeds. Keep the existing one-session limit, one-second wait, and busy error/close code `1008`.
- Send scheduler cleanup only for sessions that started a generation task. Always dispose local session state and temporary inputs.
- Add a WebSocket-route regression for idle and invalid-init peers, busy rejection, and release ownership. Document the admission behavior.

The production change stays in one existing file. No new setting, queue, or multi-session generation support.

## Validation

- Remote realtime suite: **154 passed**. Both new regression cases fail on the pre-fix code (**2 failed, 152 passed**).
- Paired **1x H200, SANA-WM Stage1** runs: 256x256, four denoising steps, seed 42, two chunks. An idle/invalid-init peer blocks generation before the fix and no longer blocks it afterward. A genuinely active peer is still rejected with `1008`; generation succeeds again after a disconnect.
- Successful requests produce identical raw-frame payload SHA256 hashes to the baseline. All five generated sessions on the fixed version are released; idle/rejected connections send no release RPC, and no input temporary directories remain.

This is a lifecycle regression check, not a throughput benchmark, full-pipeline quality evaluation, or long-duration HA certification. Initialization still stages inputs before admission; connection quotas and initialization deadlines are outside this change.

title: [Fix] diffusion/loader: Honor custom weight-loader overrides
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

The TP=1 linear storage-adoption fast path checks the loader's owner type, but a subclass can override `weight_loader` to transform a checkpoint. Matching shape and dtype do not make that override safe to skip: a square-weight transpose reproducer currently loads the wrong values without an error.

## Modifications

- Check the bound loader implementation before bypassing it.
- Preserve storage adoption for the six existing plain/merged/QKV linear loaders, including subclasses inheriting those implementations. Custom implementations run through their normal loader.
- Add a regression covering CPU checkpoints and explicit direct-GPU loading.

No new options, model allowlists, or changes to the default CPU-to-GPU loading strategy. This only tightens the TP=1 linear fast path; the separate MPS checkpoint-mapping path is unchanged.

## Validation

- Reproduced incorrect weights before the fix; the regression passes after it.
- H200: 310 loader/offload tests passed, 3 skipped, using the existing `single_process_model_parallel` fixture for the wider suite. Two existing test groups omit that fixture and fail identically on main when run alone; their repair is separate in #46254.
- Actual TP1/TP2 process groups: 96 exact weight comparisons per rank across six linear types, FP32/BF16, CPU/CUDA source and destination, and direct loading on/off. Existing storage-aliasing behavior is preserved for the supported implementations.
- Real H200 server requests: Wan1.3B single GPU and Ulysses2 (512x320, 17 frames), and Z-Image Turbo single GPU (512x512), all 4 steps with seed 42. Decoded output hashes match main within each configuration; allocated load/runtime peaks are unchanged. These are correctness smokes, not statistical performance claims.

This is a correctness fix, not a claimed startup speedup. An overridden loader may need its own allocation/copy; skipping that work is only safe when its semantics are known.

- [x] Focused regression test
- [x] Remote GPU validation
- [x] No public API/documentation change required

title: [Fix] MegaMoE: stop double-dividing the DP prefill budget
author: kushaldabbe
body:
## Motivation

MegaMoE's startup token-budget check can accept an undersized per-rank token budget when attention DP is enabled. The check is the guard that ensures `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK` covers the largest per-rank prefill / verify batch. When it under-reports, an undersized cap passes startup and the runtime later either fails its token-cap assertion during CUDA graph capture or silently falls back off the MegaMoE path for oversized batches.

## Root cause

`handle_data_parallelism` already divides `chunked_prefill_size` by `attn_dp_size` and declares the per-rank value:

`python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/parallel_hook.py:331`

```python
chunked_prefill_size=cfg.chunked_prefill_size // cfg.attn_dp_size,
```

`validate_mega_moe_token_budget` reads that resolved value through `resolving_view`, but then divides it by `attn_dp_size` a second time:

`python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/mega_moe_hook.py:206-212`

```python
elif attn_dp_enabled_of(cfg):
    token_partition_size = cfg.attn_dp_size
    ...
    local_chunked_prefill_size = cfg.chunked_prefill_size // token_partition_size
```

With `--chunked-prefill-size 16384 --attn-dp-size 2`, the real per-rank chunk is 8192, but the validator computes 4096. `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=4096` then passes validation even though each rank can receive 8192 prefill tokens.

At runtime, `mega_moe.py:440` asserts `num_tokens <= cap` during CUDA graph capture; outside capture, `should_use_mega_moe` falls back off the MegaMoE path for batches above the cap.

## Modifications

- Use the already-resolved per-rank `chunked_prefill_size` directly in the attention-DP branch.
- Update the diagnostic label to make clear the DP division was already applied.
- Add `test_megamoe_token_budget_uses_resolved_dp_chunked_prefill` in `test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py`. It declares an 8192-token per-rank chunk (the state after `handle_data_parallelism`), verifies 8192 passes, and verifies 4096 is rejected with `required_per_rank=8192`.

## Validation

- `python -m pytest test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py -k megamoe -q` -> 19 passed.
- `pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/mega_moe_hook.py test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py` -> all passed.
- The new test fails when the second division is restored (`AssertionError: ValueError not raised`), so it covers the regression.
- I also invoked the real `handle_data_parallelism` hook: it logs `adjusted from 16384 to 8192` and records `{'chunked_prefill_size': 8192}`.
- Branch is based on `main` at `1335d372f`.

## Accuracy tests

title: [Fix] diffusion: Keep each request's rollout trajectory and conditioning under dynamic batching
author: OnePunchMonk
body:
## Summary

Dynamic batching silently breaks RL rollout requests in two ways:

1. `Scheduler._split_batched_output` builds each per-request `OutputBatch` from an explicit field list that omits `rollout_trajectory_data`. Any rollout request batched with another compatible request (same sampling params, different prompt — exactly what `--batching-max-size > 1` is for) gets `rollout_trajectory_data=None` back, which fails the assert in `rollout_api.py`.
2. Fixing that exposes a second bug: `concat_rollout_trajectory_data` keeps only the first output's `denoising_env` for the whole merged batch. A trainer replaying request k's DiT forward then gets request 0's prompt conditioning, with no error raised — silently wrong importance ratios.

## Fix

- `rl_dataclasses.py`: generalize the existing single-index slice helper into `_slice_dim(start, end)`, add small recursive tree cat/slice helpers for conditioning dicts (mirroring `rollout_hooks._kwargs_to_cpu`'s shape), and introduce `slice_rollout_trajectory_range(data, start, end)` as the one range-slicing implementation. `select_output_rollout_trajectory` now delegates to it. `concat_rollout_trajectory_data` now concatenates `denoising_env` across outputs instead of keeping only the first.
- `managers/scheduler.py`: `_split_batched_output` now slices `rollout_trajectory_data` through `slice_rollout_trajectory_range` like every other per-request field.

## Tests

- `test_multi_output_rollout_trajectory.py`: extended the existing per-output fixture with an optional conditioning env, added two tests asserting concat/select no longer collapse or drop per-output conditioning.
- `test_image_response_bytes.py`: added a sibling to the existing `test_dynamic_batch_split_keeps_each_requests_image_bytes` asserting the scheduler split keeps each request's own rollout trajectory.

Verified both new dataclass-level tests fail against the pre-fix code and pass against the fix (CPU-only harness, pure torch, no GPU). The scheduler-wiring test matches the existing style of `test_dynamic_batch_split_keeps_each_requests_image_bytes` in the same file but wasn't executed locally — the full `sglang` package import graph pulls GPU-only dependencies that aren't installable in a CPU-only environment; reviewed by static trace of `_split_batched_output` instead.

## Risks / remaining

- Scheduler-level test not executed (see above); static review only.

title: [Fix] comfyui: Reject conditioning kwargs the SGLD adapters silently drop
author: OnePunchMonk
body:
## Summary

ComfyUI's native `QwenImageTransformer2DModel.forward` passes `attention_mask`, `additional_t_cond` and (via `**kwargs`) `ref_latents_method`. `QwenImageEditAdapter.pack()` in `apps/ComfyUI_SGLDiffusion/executors/qwen_image.py` caught all three in `**kwargs` and never forwarded them: the request sent to the SGLD worker was identical whether or not these were set, so a workflow using them silently ran with the worker's hardcoded defaults instead (the worker's `QwenImagePipeline` fixes `zero_cond_t` per checkpoint at load, and always applies reference latents the way native ComfyUI's default `ref_latents_method="index"` does).

`ZImageAdapter.pack()` (Lumina2 / Z-Image) has the same gap for Z-Image Omni's `siglip_feats` / `ref_contexts` (multi-reference conditioning): the worker's `ZImagePipeline` has no path for either, so a reference-image workflow would silently produce a plain text-to-image result.

This is the same failure mode #43404 fixed for `FluxAdapter`'s `ref_latents`/`control`: instead of a silent wrong result, both `pack()` methods now raise a clear `ValueError`.

I checked native ComfyUI source (`comfy/ldm/qwen_image/model.py`, `comfy/ldm/lumina/model.py`, `comfy/model_base.py`) before picking which kwargs to reject:
- `ref_latents_method` defaults to `"index"` (`self.default_ref_method`); the worker only supports that mode, so only a non-default value (`"index_timestep_zero"`, `"negative_index"`) is rejected.
- `attention_mask` / `additional_t_cond` for Qwen-Image are both genuinely conditional in `QwenImage.extra_conds` (only set when meaningful), so rejecting any non-`None` value cannot false-positive on an ordinary workflow.
- For Z-Image, I deliberately did **not** reject `num_tokens` or `attention_mask`: `Lumina2.extra_conds` sends `num_tokens` on every call (derived from the text context length), and native ComfyUI's own `patchify_and_embed` discards `attention_mask`'s effect regardless, so dropping either already matches native behavior exactly. Only `siglip_feats`/`ref_contexts` (confirmed to arrive only when a reference image is actually wired in) are a real silent-drop bug there.

## Test plan

Extended `test/unit/test_comfyui_adapters.py` (reusing its existing `_qwen_image_edit_adapter()` ComfyUI-stub helper):
- `test_qwen_image_edit_pack_rejects_unsupported_kwargs`: asserts `ValueError` for `attention_mask`, `additional_t_cond`, and `ref_latents_method="negative_index"`; asserts the default method and no extra kwargs still pack successfully.
- `test_zimage_pack_rejects_omni_reference_conditioning`: asserts `ValueError` for `siglip_feats`/`ref_contexts`; asserts `num_tokens`/`attention_mask` (sent on every real call) and absent `siglip_feats`/`ref_contexts` still pack successfully.

The full `sglang` package is too heavy to install for a CPU-only check of this isolated fix, so I verified the exact same logic against the modified source files directly (stubbing only the ComfyUI-side imports, the same technique the existing test file already uses) on Modal CPU: 9/9 checks pass, including regression checks that unchanged default-arg behavior (no new kwargs passed) is unaffected for both adapters.

No GPU run: this is pure Python kwarg validation in `pack()`, no model weights or worker round-trip involved.

title: [Fix] RL: Read output store parts straight into caller memory
author: guapisolo
body:
## Summary

Read output store parts straight into caller memory instead of Mooncake's local buffer.

## Symptom & Reproduction

- **Symptom:** Miles GLM-5 4-layer indexer replay at 256 samples per rollout (`--use-output-store`, Mooncake over TCP, 16gb local buffer) failed its first train step with `output store part not found: .../indexer_topk`, right after Mooncake logged `Failed to allocate buffer for key`. The objects were stored.
- **Reproduction, buffer:** on a live Mooncake 0.3.13.post1 master, `read_many` of 7 `indexer_topk` fields of 129 MiB through a 1000 MiB local buffer raised `KeyError`.
- **Reproduction, lease:** two readers, each reading 128 fields of 122-134 MiB with a 16 GiB budget, lost 119-121 parts each to `LEASE_EXPIRED`.

## Root Cause

1. `MooncakeBackend.get_many` reads with `batch_get_buffer` into the client's local buffer.
2. `OutputStore.read_many` sizes chunks by stored bytes against `buffer_bytes`.
3. Mooncake's `OffsetAllocator` rounds each part up a size class: 130 MiB takes 144 MiB.
4. A full chunk outgrows the buffer; parts without room come back `None`.
5. `get_many` reports every `None` as a missing part.
6. One `batch_get_buffer` per chunk outlasts the 10 s read lease over TCP.

## Fix

`MooncakeBackend.get_many` allocates one array for the requested parts, registers it with `register_buffer`, reads each part with `get_into` from 4 threads, and unregisters it. Nothing is rounded, chunked or copied, each call stays far inside the lease, and `get_into` tells a missing part (-704) from a failed read, so the backend raises `KeyError`, `ValueError` (size differs from the ref) or `RuntimeError` without another call.

`OutputStore` keeps one read path: `read_many` drops `buffer_bytes`, and the view-returning `get_many` goes, since its views were the reason for the buffer. Puts still use the local buffer, so a client that only reads can set `local_buffer_size` to 0. Miles' reader moves with it in radixark/miles#4267.

Four threads matched one `batch_get_into` over RDMA; more only shared the bandwidth. A single part whose transfer alone outlasts the lease (15 GiB over TCP) still fails.

## Verification

- `radix_transfer_plugins/tests`: 34 passed (fake Mooncake); read tests new or rewritten.
- Live Mooncake 0.3.13.post1, one host, two concurrent readers of 128 fields of 122-134 MiB:
  - `read_many` per reader: RDMA 12.6 GiB/s (before 3.2), TCP 1.42 GiB/s (before 0.94); client setup 0.59 s (before 1.41) without the 16 GiB buffer.
  - A never-written part raises `KeyError`; a ref 4 KiB off either way raises `ValueError`.
- Miles GLM-5 4-layer, 256 samples, 5 rollouts each way, with the radixark/miles#4267 reader: both runs trained; the read stage per rollout took a median 24 s (before 39 s, range 27-94); train/rollout log-prob diff 0.0446-0.0553 (before 0.0445-0.0560).

## Review Focus

- `MooncakeBackend._read_into`: the registration covers the whole array and is undone in `finally`; `_raise_failed_reads` maps the results to exceptions.
- `_READ_THREADS = 4`: measured on one host over RDMA and TCP; cross-host TCP is not measured.

title: [Fix] scheduler: Publish KV events while the engine is paused
author: sohom-cs
body:
## Motivation

An RL weight sync runs `pause_generation` in retract mode, then `update_weights_*` with `flush_cache=True`, then `continue_generation`. The flush queues AllBlocksCleared, but a paused scheduler never publishes KV events, so a KV-event router (sgl-router, or Dynamo) keeps that worker's whole pre-flush cache view for the entire sync and scores requests against blocks that no longer exist. The clear reaches the router only after resume.

#24003 added a publish at pause entry. It covers what was queued up to the pause, not what happens during it, such as the weight update's flush.

Found while following #24003's pause-time flush through a weight update.

## Modifications

Every pausable event loop (normal, overlap, PD prefill, PD decode, MLX) calls `_record_scheduler_state_for_paused_engine()` on each paused iteration and skips `on_idle`. This adds one `publish_kv_events()` call to that helper, which covers the flush and anything else recorded while paused. The call does nothing on ranks without a publisher, and on an idle paused loop it only drains an empty queue.

## Accuracy Tests

In `test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_pause_generation.py`:

- New case with a real RadixCache and publisher: pause (retract), flush_cache, one paused iteration, then AllBlocksCleared must have been published.

Results:

- main: `Lists differ: [] != ['AllBlocksCleared']`
- this PR: the file passes (29 passed)

CPU only, stub scheduler, Python tree core. I have not run it against a live router or an RL job.

title: [Fix] deepseek-v4: Complete the MoE output locally when the transport declares no sum group
author: wenscarl
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #46316.

With an a2a MoE backend (`--moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe`) DeepSeek-V4 fails while capturing the decode CUDA graph:

```
ValueError: transport finalize owes an undeclared sum group
  sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/row_transport.py, in finish
```

Two contracts disagree:

- `MoeTransport.__init__` requires `rows.group is None` whenever an a2a backend is set, meaning the compute already completed the sum.
- The layer still calls the MoE with `leave_output_sum=True`, so the MoE returns a `MoEOutput`. `prepare_output` wraps it in `MoeFinalize`, a `DeferredFinalize` whose `completion_group` is always `MOE_OUTPUT`.

With `rows.group is None` the declared `groups` are empty, so `TransportExit.finish` rejects the deferred finalize.

## Modifications

`MoeTransport.prepare_output` finalizes the `MoEOutput` locally (`complete(reduce=False)`) when the transport declares no sum group **and** `post_experts_output_is_complete()` says the expert outputs are already summed, as they are after the `flashinfer_megamoe` combine. This is the handling the `mlp_reduce_scatter` case already gets, and it matches the plain-tensor branch below it. `reduce=False` because the a2a combine already summed across ranks; reducing again would double-count.

`rows.group is None` alone is not enough. DeepGEMM `megamoe` can fall back to the standard dispatcher, which does not sum across ranks; finalizing that output locally would return partial expert sums without an error, and TP ranks other than 0 would also skip the replicated shared add. That case still reaches the transport's undeclared-sum check.

Why here rather than relaxing the check in `TransportExit.finish` or changing the layer's `leave_output_sum`: the check is an intentional invariant, and everything needed to decide is already in `MoeTransport`.

`test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v4_boundary.py` adds a CPU test: with `flashinfer_megamoe` the output is finalized locally with no all-reduce and the shared output is added on a nonzero TP rank; with `megamoe` it stays a deferred finalize that owes `MOE_OUTPUT`.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K, 400 questions, same server as in Verification (`main` + this change), default sampling:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 400
```

| | Score | Std error |
|---|---|---|
| `main` + this change | 0.9775 | about 0.0074 |

- Single run, legacy `sglang.test.run_eval` scorer. It is comparable to earlier MegaMoE runs that used the same scorer, not to sgl-eval scores.
- There is no "before" number: without this change the server cannot start in this configuration, so the check is that the output is correct once it can.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The change only affects a path that previously failed at startup.

## Verification

4x GB200, `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4`, FlashInfer 0.7.2 from the image, on `main` at `638374c389`:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --trust-remote-code --model-path nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4 \
  --dp-size 4 --tp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 8192 \
  --disable-flashinfer-autotune --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_megamoe --moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe \
  --max-running-requests 8192 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000
```

- Without the change: fails at decode CUDA graph capture with the error above (reproduced repeatedly).
- With the change: the server starts, and a greedy completion for `The capital of France is` begins with ` Paris.`.

Other MoE backends and parallel layouts were not tested on GPU. The GB200 run above used the first revision of this PR; for `flashinfer_megamoe` the current revision takes the same branch.

- The new test fails on `main` (`638374c389`) for `flashinfer_megamoe` and on the first revision for `megamoe`, and passes with the current revision.

title: [Fix] disaggregation: Send decode transfer destinations to prefill only after the in-flight forward
author: libertyeagle
body:
## Motivation

When decode reuses a finished request's KV pages while its last forward is still in flight, publishing the new destination immediately lets prefill write into pages that the old forward can still overwrite. #45328 orders the normal deferred-publication path; this PR closes the remaining device-destination paths under overlap scheduling, including staging, HiSparse, and configurations with the WAR barrier or deferred publication disabled.

PP currently disables overlap, so it keeps its existing synchronous publication behavior. Host destinations keep their existing H2D fencing.

## Modifications

- Hold inline device metadata behind an event recorded on the forward stream. Publish only after every rank agrees that its event is complete and its receiver has not failed, using a MIN reduction. This prevents partial publication across TP ranks during cancellation.
- Publish held destinations before the retraction and polling gates, and again after newly allocated requests enter the transfer queue. A retracted request cannot indefinitely delay an unrelated ready destination.
- Release unpublished failed destinations without waiting for drain acknowledgements that cannot arrive. If a peer requires a collective hold, the unpublished rank participates with zero required acknowledgements.
- For early-policy rebootstrap requests, submit prefill recomputation after the held metadata is actually sent, preserving the existing ordering and avoiding an abort before the receiver is armed.
- Initialize `chunk_staging_infos` in `CommonKVReceiver.__init__`, so staging cleanup is safe before `send_metadata`.

The existing deferred-publication and host-destination paths retain their ordering. Tests cover event readiness, agreement across ranks, retraction gating, failed receivers, acknowledgement accounting, staging cleanup, and recompute submission order. The delayed-conclusion test is defensive coverage; it does not claim that PP currently enables overlap.

## Accuracy Tests

Validation of `3f6f056ecbb977350ea9a97c9d4c7b5c74b4af50` against parent `fb9846d3e2d66811b372b28c73229e9dbbf54288`:

- Seven focused unit-test files: **100 passed, 72 subtests passed**. The new regressions fail before the fixes and pass afterward.
- All 43 disaggregation unit-test files plus the adjacent PP-outcome and retraction-backup files, each in its own process: **852 passing cases including subtests, one failure**. `TestPPConsensusStore.test_malformed_messages_are_dropped` also fails on the exact parent in this local environment; the same process hangs during ZMQ cleanup. It is unchanged by this PR.
- Real local Qwen3-8B serving on four NVIDIA GB300 GPUs, with TP=2 prefill and TP=2 decode, CUDA decode graphs, chunked prefill, decode radix caching, and KV checksums. Both inline and default deferred-publication configurations pass sequential and concurrent generation, one-token completion, 24 cancellations, 12 recovery requests, streaming, and final health checks. **All 12 sequential and 24 concurrent responses match the parent's token IDs exactly.** All 24 requests are cancelled and all 12 recovery responses match the sequential results in both final TP=2 runs.
- PP=2 prefill/decode control passes the same generation, cancellation, recovery, streaming, and health workload; its 12 sequential and 24 concurrent responses match the parent. Cancellation requests omit log probabilities to avoid a MiniLB `KeyError: meta_info` that reproduces on both parent and head.
- Heterogeneous TP staging (prefill TP=1, decode TP=2) passes generation, 24 cancellations, 12 recovery requests, streaming, and health on both parent and final source. All 12 sequential responses match; 23/24 concurrent responses match, with batch variation also observed on the parent.
- Single-GPU-per-role PD and unified-server controls also pass. These local transport tests use Mooncake TCP; they do not validate RDMA or NVLink transport.
- Focused follow-up: 16 publication/cleanup regressions pass in 12.36 seconds. A local NIXL/UCX TP=2 prefill/decode run with inline publication passes in 56.68 seconds: all 12 sequential and 24 concurrent responses match the parent, with 24 successful cancellations, 12 matching recovery responses, streaming, CUDA decode graphs, and KV checksums. UCX uses shared memory/TCP/CUDA IPC locally; RDMA is left to CI.
- Full PR-range pre-commit verification passes. Claude Code reviewed the final changes and reported no correctness blockers.
- NVIDIA [Base CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41243972189) and [Extra CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41243972132) are running on the final commit. Completed coverage includes all 20 CPU shards, basic/optimistic disaggregation, prefill-complete allocation, unified memory, HiSparse, SWA heterogeneous TP, DeepSeek heterogeneous TP, DP attention, and the previously failing canary test. A [focused H20 rerun](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41249851467) passed the selected staging/radix, NIXL, and decode-PP tests on the final commit. The full matrix is not yet complete.

This is bounded token-parity and lifecycle validation, not a full model-accuracy evaluation.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No formal performance benchmark was run. Held destinations add a nonblocking event query and a small Gloo MIN reduction while publication is pending. Queue scans return without a collective when there are no held destinations. Publication waits for the previously enqueued forward to complete and for rank agreement; no synchronous device wait is added.

title: [Fix] [Intel] diffusion/wan: Guard the CuTe DSL q/k norm RoPE imports on XPU
author: arathi-hlab
body:
## Motivation

#46228 added `can_use_fused_rmsnorm_interleaved_rope` / `fused_rmsnorm_interleaved_rope_` to the module-level imports of `wanvideo.py`. The lazy `__getattr__` in `sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion` resolves them from `rope/rmsnorm_interleaved_rope_cutedsl.py`, which imports `cutlass` / `cuda.bindings` / `flashinfer` unconditionally. On XPU, which has no CuTe DSL, importing `wanvideo.py` now fails:

```
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'cutlass'
ValueError: Model architectures ['WanTransformer3DModel'] failed to be inspected.
Error while loading customized transformer, falling back to native version
```

Wan then runs on the native fallback transformer, and the XPU multimodal job fails its perf check on `wan2_1_t2v_1.3b` (E2E 122149 ms vs 76292 ms baseline, 106809 ms limit) on all 7 attempts, e.g. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40161807926.

## Modifications

On XPU, skip the import of the two fused-kernel symbols in `wanvideo.py` and fall back to `can_use_fused_rmsnorm_interleaved_rope = lambda ...: False`. `_qkv_rope` then takes the existing unfused q/k RMSNorm path (the pre-#46228 behaviour).

The guard is caller-side because the kernel module applies `@cute.jit` / `@cute.kernel` at import time, so guarding only its imports would not be enough.

- CUDA: unchanged.
- XPU: Wan loads the sglang transformer again, unfused norm path.
- Other platforms (ROCm, etc.): unchanged, left to their owners.

#46247 then added two more symbols from the same CuTe DSL module (`fused_rmsnorm_interleaved_rope_into_blocks`, `rmsnorm_interleaved_rope_block_cols`); they are moved into the same XPU guard. Their only call site is behind `_fuses_qk_norm_rope`, which is False on XPU.

#46247 also added `torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()` to the guard in `WanTransformer3DModel._text_kvs`. On XPU torch it raises on every denoising step:

```
RuntimeError: Tried to instantiate dummy base class _cuda_isCurrentStreamCapturing
```

It now uses `is_device_stream_capturing(context.device)` from `sglang.srt.utils`, which checks the device actually in use.

- [ ] XPU multimodal CI (`multimodal-gen-test-1-gpu-xpu`) green on `wan2_1_t2v_1.3b`

title: [Fix] dspark: Draw the simulated-acceptance bonus at the simulated row
author: weireweire
body:
## Motivation

With `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN` set, DSpark replaces the accepted length with the simulated value `c`. The bonus token, however, stays the one the real accept computed for its own length: the target argmax at the real first-mismatch row, or the rejection-sampled token at the real reject row. That token is committed after `drafts[:c]`, at a position the target never predicted it for. It is also the anchor of the next draft block. The committed text degenerates as a result, and verify batches route to fewer experts than at the same acceptance length under real verification. Simulated-acceptance throughput is therefore overstated.

The only configuration that was correct is `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_GREEDY=1` with temperature-only requests, which has been opt-in since #45433. EAGLE/MTP and DFlash already take the bonus from the target at the forced row.

## Modifications

Under simulation, the bonus is the target's token at verify row `c`, drawn with the request's sampling law.

- `dspark_worker_v2.py`: every sampled batch now passes its sampling info as `simulate_bonus_sampling_info`. Before, only `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_GREEDY=1` with temperature-only batches did. The flag now only selects the greedy draft/accept, under the same eligibility checks as before.
- Sampling-accept region graph (`SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_SAMPLING_ACCEPT_GRAPH`): it stays eligible under simulation for the same batches as in real serving (all-sampled, temperature-only, no logit adjustments or grammar), so a simulated run keeps the graph that real serving uses.
  - Before the region runs, the worker stages the step's temperatures and seed with `begin_sim_bonus`.
  - Inside the region, the bonus is drawn at row `c` with the epilogue's graph-safe sampler (`sim_bonus`, renamed from `_sim_bonus`), the same kernel `SGLANG_DSPARK_SIMULATE_FOLD` uses.
  - The region's rejection accept still runs, as it does in real serving; under simulation only its length and bonus are replaced.
- `build_accept_outs`: when no sampled bonus is supplied, the bonus is the argmax of row `c`. This covers greedy batches on the eager accept and on the folded greedy accept (`DsparkVerifyEpilogue._accept` without `SGLANG_DSPARK_SIMULATE_FOLD`).
- `sample_simulated_bonus`: top-k/top-p batches sample row `c` from `build_speculative_verify_target_probs`, the target distribution the sampling accept uses. Greedy requests in a mixed batch have top_k=1, so they stay argmax. Temperature-only batches keep the existing Gumbel kernel.
- `static_accept_tail` (Triton kernel and torch reference): the argmax-id bonus is read at the committed length rather than the matched length.
- A sampled simulated bonus is broadcast on the `DSPARK_ACCEPT_SAMPLE` TP sync site, so the `rng` preset keeps ranks consistent.
- `test_dspark_simulated_bonus.py`: the sampling-info stand-in gains `need_top_k_sampling` / `need_top_p_sampling`.

Scope of the sampling law under simulation:
- Temperature and top-k/top-p are applied by the bonus sampler.
- Logit adjustments (penalties, logit bias) and grammar masks are honoured only because they are already in the verify logits when the bonus is drawn: `run_non_compact` / `run_compact` apply the adjustments and the worker applies the grammar mask. The sampler itself does neither.
- Batches with adjustments or grammar never use the region graph.
- min-p is not applied. The non-simulated sampling accept does not apply it either.

Simulated acceptance is a benchmark-only mode.

TP: a sampled bonus is broadcast from rank 0 when the `DSPARK_ACCEPT_SAMPLE` site is enabled. Without it, ranks draw from identical seeds, the same assumption the simulated-length draw and the non-simulated rejection sampler already make.

Non-simulated paths are unchanged. Every new branch is behind `simulated_correct_len is not None`, and the tail kernel's non-simulated length is still `num_correct`.

## Accuracy / correctness

Unit-level checks on GB300 run the real kernels, with drafts rejected at row 0 and simulated `c = 3`:

| path | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| eager accept, greedy batch | bonus = row-0 argmax | row-3 argmax |
| folded greedy accept, eager call and inside a CUDA graph | row-0 argmax | row-3 argmax |
| fused static accept tail (Triton) | row-0 argmax | row-3 argmax |
| top-p bonus distribution (T=0.8, p=0.7), max abs diff vs. the renormalized target, 200k draws | 0.21 | 0.0016 |
| non-simulated fused tail | unchanged | unchanged |
| sampling-accept region under simulation, bs 1/1, 3/3, 3/4 (padded); eager warm-up, capture, replays at fixed seeds | rejection bonus at the real row | equals the eager row-`c` draw; drafts at `[:c]`, bonus at `[c]` |
| region bonus distribution, 6,000 replays (T=0.8), max abs diff vs. softmax(row `c` / T) | 0.65 | 0.0099 |

Existing tests, before and after: `test_dspark_accept_tail.py`, `test_dspark_sampling_accept_graph.py` and `test_dspark_sim_draw_ahead.py` pass. `test_dspark_simulated_bonus.py::test_bf16_full_vocab_low_temperature` fails identically with and without this change on NVIDIA. It is registered for AMD CI only.

End to end: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash FP4, DSpark block 5, TP2 EP2, GB300, AgentX-style agentic traces at 32 concurrent, temperature 1, `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.51` (match-expected). The committed text is re-tokenized; about 1,500 turns are shared across runs.

| | real acceptance | simulated, before | simulated, after |
|---|---|---|---|
| token equal to one of the previous 6 | 0.070 | 0.375 | 0.145 |
| 4-gram already seen in the response | 0.282 | 0.387 | 0.197 |
| share of the most frequent token | 0.042 | 0.170 | 0.083 |
| distinct experts per MoE layer, B=4 / 5 / 8 / 10 | 75.0 / 84.9 / 116.2 / 123.9 | 53.9 / 62.7 / 85.0 / 94.9 | 71.8 / 85.3 / 108.3 / 121.9 |

After the fix, the remaining difference from real acceptance is in the drafted tokens. Simulation accepts them unconditionally, so repeats 2-3 tokens apart rise from 0.027 to 0.096 of tokens. Immediate repeats (0.0008 vs 0.0024) and repeats 4-6 tokens apart match real acceptance. An independent simulated-acceptance implementation that commits the target's token at the forced position measures the same statistics on this workload (0.148 / 0.182 / 0.087).

## Benchmarking and Profiling

The size of the change depends on the point: it is largest where MoE is a big share of the step and the degenerate text cut the distinct experts the most.

**TP2 EP2, 32 concurrent** (the end-to-end setup above), 3600 s:

| | total tok/s/GPU | output tok/s/GPU | ITL p50 / p90 (ms) | interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s, 1000/ITL) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| simulated, before | 122.2K | 697 | 3.43 / 4.40 | 291.5 / 227.3 |
| simulated, after | 118.9K | 683 | 3.85 / 4.92 | 259.7 / 203.3 |

Both runs measure AL 3.51. The "after" run is 2.7% lower in total throughput and 11% lower in p90 interactivity (11% higher p90 ITL). This is expected: the "before" run's degenerate text made MoE about 1 ms/step cheaper at B=4-10. Each number is a single run, on different nodes. These two runs applied the same change to an earlier nightly and use the eager accept (no sampling-accept graph).

**TP4 EP1, 1 concurrent, NVIDIA megakernel**, `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_SAMPLING_ACCEPT_GRAPH=1`, `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.51`, same traces, 1800 s, AL 3.51 in every run. At batch 1 with the experts sharded across four GPUs, MoE is a small share of the step, so the change costs about 1%. This table also shows why the sampling-accept region change is needed:

| | region graph replays | interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s, 1000/ITL) |
|---|---|---|
| this PR | ~110k per rank | 976 / 949 |
| this PR without the region change (sampled simulated steps fall back to the eager accept) | 0 | 939 / 863 |
| before this PR (region graph with the misplaced bonus), 3600 s | captured | 987 / 954 |

Keeping the region in the graph is worth 4% / 10% at p50 / p90. The remaining ~1% to "before" is within what the text change and the shorter run can explain.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Existing unit tests updated; no new test file (verified on GPU as above).

title: [Fix] [Intel] dp-attention: Skip the CustomAllReduceV2 import on XPU
author: arathi-hlab
body:
## Motivation

#46138 added a module-level `from sglang.srt.distributed.device_communicators.custom_all_reduce_v2 import CustomAllReduceV2` to `dp_attention.py`. `custom_all_reduce_v2` imports `sglang/kernels/ops/communication/all_reduce.py`, which does `import tvm_ffi` at module level. `tvm_ffi` is not installed in the XPU image (`intel/sglang-dev:latest`), and `dp_attention.py` is imported almost everywhere, so importing sglang on XPU now fails. For example, the XPU diffusion job dies before running any test:

```
File ".../sglang/srt/layers/dp_attention.py", line 20, in <module>
  from sglang.srt.distributed.device_communicators.custom_all_reduce_v2 import (
File ".../sglang/kernels/ops/communication/all_reduce.py", line 7, in <module>
  import tvm_ffi
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tvm_ffi'
```

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40179531469/job/121127481365

## Modifications

On XPU only, skip the import and bind `CustomAllReduceV2 = ()`. The class's only use is `isinstance(comm, CustomAllReduceV2)` in `_decode_sum_len_fits_custom_all_reduce`, and `isinstance(x, ())` is always `False`. That is correct on XPU, which cannot create a v2 custom all-reduce.

- CUDA / ROCm / other platforms: unchanged, the module-level import is kept as is.
- XPU: sglang imports again; the SUM_LEN shortcut is never taken, as before #46138.

## Checklist

- [x] pre-commit passes
- [ ] XPU CI green

title: [Fix] diffusion/flux3: Make TP and SP ranks agree on sequential CFG
author: Smallfu666
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #46429. `resolve_sequential_cfg` decides between packed and sequential CFG from each rank's own free memory ([L159](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/5971f47bc8eacd8989cb6dd67e46b4fc6dbec2ad/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/model_specific_stages/flux3_image.py#L159)). The two paths issue different TP all-reduces and SP exchanges per step, so when the ranks decide differently their collectives no longer match, and the request hangs or fails (details in the issue).

## Modifications

- Take the MIN of free memory over the TP and SP groups before comparing, as `_cache_fits` already does in the Qwen-Image 2.1 stage ([L351-L358](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/5971f47bc8eacd8989cb6dd67e46b4fc6dbec2ad/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/model_specific_stages/qwen_image21.py#L351-L358)).
- New test `test_sequential_cfg_is_agreed_across_ranks` in `test_flux3_image_stages.py` runs two CPU ranks, once as TP=2 and once as Ulysses SP=2, with rank 1 reporting 1 MiB free, and checks that both ranks choose sequential CFG. On main both subtests fail with `AssertionError: [False, True]`; with this change the file passes.

## Accuracy Tests

2x H200, `black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base` (base e262b44), TP=2, 2048x2048, 20 steps, with another process holding memory on GPU 1 only so that the ranks would split. Without this change the request got no response for 300 s; with it, both ranks chose sequential CFG and the request completed. Two runs with the change gave bit-identical images, and they are also bit-identical to the output without the change when memory is held on both GPUs, so that both ranks take the sequential path.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not measured. The change adds at most two CPU all-reduces of one int64 per denoise call, before the step loop.
