title: [Fix] dsv4: Keep a coordinated verify rank out of the decoder-tail idle replay
author: akhilg-nv
body:
[by Claude Code]

Fixes #46666.

## Motivation

Two DeepSeek-V4.1 serving features meet in this bug.

- **Decoder SWA bounded replay** (on by default where supported). Layers after 20 keep no compressed KV of their own: they read layer 20's, which layer 20 writes for every row. The only state these late layers leave for later tokens is each layer's 128-token sliding window (SWA). So on a prefill (extend) step, the layers from 20 on (`late_layer_start`) run over only each request's last 128 extend rows, the request's *tail*. #45059 and #45107 replay these tail layers from CUDA graphs, one per padded row count (a multiple of 128). Under DP attention every rank replays the same graph, because the ranks meet at every MoE layer. A rank without a tail joins with zero rows of its own (`DecoderReplayTail.run_idle`), on the assumption that it has nothing to compute.
- **DP spec-prefill coordination** (`SGLANG_ENABLE_DP_SPEC_PREFILL_COORDINATION=1`, #40118). One DP rank runs its speculative verify in the same step as another rank's prefill. Each rank keeps its own batch; the step is marked `is_extend_in_batch`.

On such a coordinated step the verify rank is not idle: it has batch size x verify width rows (6 per request with DSpark block size 5). It has no prefill tail, though, so `DecoderReplayTail.plan` sends it down the idle path. Its outputs of the late layers are then replaced by the replay of the other rank's tail graph, cut to the verify's row count by `RowBucketGraphRunner.run`:

- more verify rows than the bucket (22+ requests against a peer prefilling one request): DFlash verify raises `ValueError: next_token_logits row count mismatch for DFlash verify adjustments. Expected 192, got 128.` and the DP schedulers die;
- fewer: no error, but the verify accepts draft tokens against stale logits.

This PR makes `DecoderReplayTail.plan` return "no tail graph" on coordinated steps, so every rank runs the late layers eagerly on those steps, as all steps did before #45107. Coordination itself is unchanged: the prefill and the verify still run in the same step, each in its own batch. Every rank of a coordinated step carries `dp_spec_prefill_coordination_applied`, so the ranks still agree on skipping the tail graphs' host gather and captures. Uncoordinated steps, including steps with genuinely idle ranks, keep the tail graphs unchanged.

Impact:
- **Correctness (e2e):** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 2x B300, the InferenceX B300 DEP2 recipe under a load that forces
  coordinated steps. Main crashes on its first coordinated step (2 of 2 runs: `Expected 192, got 128` and
  `Expected 186, got 128`). With this PR the same load runs its full 240 s: 231 coordinated steps with 27-39 verifying
  requests, no error.
- **Accuracy:** GSM8K (sgl-eval, 1319 examples, no thinking, real acceptance, coordination on) 96.66% and 97.12% with
  this PR vs 96.29% and 96.44% on main; within noise (about 0.5 points standard error), because GSM8K traffic makes
  only 5-8 coordinated steps per run. The new GPU test pins the wrong-logits case exactly.
- **Performance:** no change on uncoordinated steps. On coordinated steps the tail layers run eagerly, as before
  #45107 (see Speed Tests).

## Modifications

**+5 / -0 runtime code (1 file), +190 tests (1 file).** No kernel changes.

- `DecoderReplayTail.plan` returns `(False, None)` when `forward_batch.dp_spec_prefill_coordination_applied`, before
  the host gather (`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4_replay_tail.py`).
- New 1-GPU test `test/registered/e2e/model_executor/test_decoder_tail_dp_spec_coordination.py`. It runs the tail
  plan and the model's dispatch for a rank without a tail through the real `RowBucketGraphRunner` and a real CUDA
  graph, with the peer's tail rows patched in (row step 8 standing in for 128), and compares the rank's late-layer
  output exactly with the reference:
  - coordinated verify rank, 10 rows (more than the peer's bucket): fails on main with
    `torch.Size([8, 1, 4]) != torch.Size([10, 1, 4])` (the crash's row cut);
  - coordinated verify rank, 5 rows (fewer than the bucket): fails on main with 20 / 20 elements wrong (the silent case);
  - an idle rank on an uncoordinated step still replays the shared bucket (guards against a fix that drops the
    graphs for idle ranks, whose peers capture behind rank barriers).
- Related: #46526 refactors `DecoderReplayTail` but keeps the same `plan` early return and the `run_idle` dispatch, so
  it does not fix this; the fix applies on top of it unchanged. If it lands first, the test's `late_dp_counts=` keyword
  becomes `late_dp_rows=`.

## Accuracy Tests

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 2x B300, the same server as the e2e runs minus simulated acceptance and the thinking defaults
(real acceptance), coordination on, one 34,000-token warm-up prompt so the tail graphs run. `sgl-eval run gsm8k
--num-examples 1319 --num-threads 24 --temperature 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --no-thinking --max-tokens 4096` (sgl-eval 0.1.3,
the test-extra pin; temperature / top_p from the model's preset, no thinking as in #45107's GSM8K check).

| tree | load | GSM8K | coordinated steps |
|---|---|---|---|
| main `66f79f1a907` | GSM8K | 96.29% | 5, all through `run_idle` on the verify rank |
| main `66f79f1a907` | GSM8K + background prefills | 96.44% | 8, all through `run_idle` on the verify rank |
| this PR | GSM8K | 96.66% | 8, eager tail |
| this PR | GSM8K + background prefills | 97.12% | 6, eager tail |

The scores are within noise of each other and of #45107's 96.29-96.89% (GB300, DP2 attention, MegaMoE). GSM8K
traffic produces too few coordinated steps to show the wrong-logits case end to end; the unit test above shows it
exactly (all 20 values of the 5 rows wrong on main).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No change on uncoordinated steps: the new check is one attribute read per tail plan.

On coordinated steps, every rank now runs the tail layers eagerly. Main is not a speed baseline for these steps: there
the verify rank skipped its late layers and crashed or computed wrong logits.

**End to end (estimate, not measured):** compared with a hypothetical correct graph path for coordinated steps, the
cost is the eager launch overhead of the prefill rank's tail layers on coordinated steps only. #45107 measured that
overhead at about 42 ms per eager 8K-token prefill step (GB300, DP2 attention, MegaMoE, encoder replay on: cold 8K
TTFT 208.4 -> 166.2 ms). That is an upper bound here, since the verify rank already runs eagerly on these steps and the ranks meet at every
MoE layer. Letting the verify rank's own rows ride the tail graph would recover it, but it replays TARGET_VERIFY rows
through graphs captured on EXTEND batches; that is left for a follow-up.

Repro of the e2e runs: image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261026-8252e3af` with the tree's `python/` first on
`PYTHONPATH`. Server: the InferenceX B300 DEP2 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash recipe (TP2 DP2 EP2, DP attention, MegaMoE,
DSpark block 5, `--disable-prefill-cuda-graph`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_DP_SPEC_PREFILL_COORDINATION=1`, simulated
acceptance 3.51). Load: one 34,000-token prompt (one full 32K chunk, after which the tail graphs run), then 64
closed-loop greedy generations (1,000 in / 8,000 out) plus one 3,000-token prompt per second, for 240 s.

| tree | result |
|---|---|
| main `66f79f1a907` | crash on the first coordinated step, 43 s in: `Expected 192, got 128` |
| main `66f79f1a907` (second run) | crash, 33 s in: `Expected 186, got 128` |
| main + `SGLANG_DSV4_DECODER_TAIL_GRAPH_MAX_ROWS=0` | 240 s, 232 coordinated steps, no error |
| this PR | 240 s, 231 coordinated steps (27-39 verifying requests), no error |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-and-profiling).

title: [Fix] diffusion: Resolve cached named weights without the Hub API
author: em-dreyer
body:
## Motivation

`resolve_weight()` in `multimodal_gen/runtime/weights/source.py` lists every Hugging Face source with `HfApi().model_info()`, even when the requested file is already in the local cache. That call counts against the Hub's **`api`** rate limit, which is far lower than the download limit and is shared by every process using the same token. When a scheduled PR Test run starts ~100 jobs at once, the quota runs out and diffusion servers fail at startup:

- Failed job: [`multimodal-gen-test-2-gpu (2)`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40417752787/job/121904415106) — case `wan2_2_t2v_a14b_lora_2gpu`
- `maybe_download_lora` → `resolve_weight` → `resolve_weight_inventory` → `HfApi().model_info("Cseti/wan2.2-14B-Arcane_Jinx-lora-v1")`
- `429 Too Many Requests: you have reached your 'api' rate limit. Retry after 94 seconds (0/3000 requests remaining in current 300s window).`
- The test's retry 12 minutes later hit the same limit, so the file failed.

The LoRA download right after this already checks the cache first (`maybe_download_model` with `local_files_only=True`); only the inventory step went to the network.

## Modifications

- **Cache first for named files.** `resolve_weight()` now checks the cached snapshot for the requested revision (`snapshot_download(..., local_files_only=True)`) when the caller names an exact file (a file reference, or `weight_name`). If that exact path is cached, it builds the inventory from the snapshot and pins the snapshot's commit, with no network call. This also lets the path work with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`.
- **Same behaviour otherwise.** It falls back to `model_info()` when the revision isn't cached, the file is missing, only a basename match is cached, or no file is named. A cached snapshot holds only the files downloaded so far, so it is never used to choose among candidates.
- **Unpinned revisions use the cached commit.** When no revision is pinned and the file is cached, the cached commit is used without asking the Hub for the latest, so a repo updated upstream isn't picked up on a machine that already has it cached. `maybe_download_model` already behaves this way; this makes the inventory step match it.

No retry on 429: the Hub API quota is shared by every process using the same token, and the test harness already retries a failed server start, so an in-process retry would add requests while the quota is exhausted. On a cache miss this path still makes exactly one `model_info()` call, as before. `resolve_safetensors_weight_set()` is unchanged; I've kept this PR narrow.

## Tests

- `pytest test/unit/test_weight_source.py`: the existing 18 tests pass with huggingface_hub 1.33.0 and 2.3.0.
- Locally against a real HF cache layout: a cached named file resolves with no Hub API call and pins the cached commit; not cached, file missing from the snapshot, a basename-only match, or no file named all fall back to `model_info()`.
- The multimodal-gen GPU suite (`wan2_2_t2v_a14b_lora_2gpu` resolves its LoRA through this path) is the end-to-end check.

title: [Fix] mem_cache: Clamp SWA tombstone recovery to the request's protected prefix
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

The unified radix tree could free FULL KV pages that a node still mapped. A request owns FULL pages only from its protected prefix (`prev_prefix_len`) upward; below it, the request's row holds the node's own canonical page ids by reference. `SWAComponent.update_component_on_insert_overlap` recovered an SWA-tombstoned fragment from the request's row starting at the request's SWA eviction cursor, and clamped that cursor to the protected prefix only for independent windows.

A single-chunk request has a cursor of 0, and a read-only FULL prefix match can leave the protected prefix strictly inside a node, so the recovery also covered pages the request never owned. Those pages were freed as if they were the request's duplicates (the swap branch's old FULL ids, or the locked branch's incoming ids) while the node kept mapping them. Once they re-entered the free list, the next allocation overwrote KV the node was still serving, so a later reader of that node could see another request's KV.

```
position     0                16            24      (page size 4, SWA window 8)
             |-- protected ---|---- own ----|
node N       [ p0 p1 p2 p3 ]  [ p4 p5 ]              FULL resident, SWA evicted
request row  [ p0 p1 p2 p3 ]  [ q4 q5 ]              p0..p3 borrowed by reference, q4 q5 fresh

before: recovery starts at the SWA cursor (0)
        locked node   -> frees "incoming" p0..p3     node still maps p0..p3   => double free
        unlocked node -> adopts p0..p3, frees "old" p0..p3                    => double free
after:  recovery starts at max(cursor, 16) = 16
        only [p4 p5] vs [q4 q5] is reconciled; p0..p3 untouched
```

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_cache/components/swa.py`: the recovery window now starts at `max(evicted_seqlen, prev_prefix_len)` for both window kinds instead of only for independent windows. A node straddling the protected prefix is clipped there, so the head keeps its canonical ids and only the tail is recovered. Positions below the protected prefix are never the request's contribution.

Behaviour is unchanged when the cursor is already at or above the protected prefix (chunked and decode inserts) and for independent windows, which were clamped before. No allocator, scheduler, or controller change. The Rust tree core under `rust/sglang-radix-tree` keeps its own recovery path and is not changed here.

## Accuracy Tests

Local CPU run of the unified-cache SWA unit tests on this branch:

```
python -m pytest test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_swa_unittest.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_swa_locked_full_recover_unified.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_session_unified_radix_cache.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_hicache_regressions.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache/test_unified_radix_cache_core.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_component_split_contract.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_buffer_swa_tail_only.py
518 passed, 59 skipped
```

Model outputs are unaffected on the paths that were already correct; the change only stops the recovery from freeing pages below the protected prefix. GPU suites were not run locally; CI covers them.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: one `max()` on an insert path that already computed both operands.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (No new test in this PR; the existing unified-cache SWA tests above exercise the changed path.)

title: [Fix] dsv4: Render null contents, trailing tool-call turns and numeric string efforts with deepseek-recipe
author: hnyls2002
body:
Fixes requests that rendered before deepseek-recipe (#45315) and now return 400 on DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1:

- A null message content renders as `""`, as `_process_messages` renders it for every model (a `tool` result, a `system` message, an assistant turn without tool calls).
- A trailing assistant turn's tool calls are discarded before it becomes a user turn or is continued, as `_handle_last_assistant_message` discards them; a null content there is `""` too.
- A numeric string `chat_template_kwargs.reasoning_effort` (`"30"`, `"0.3"`) is the number it spells: a budget on V4.1, a 400 on V4 as an integer is. `SGLANG_DSV41_REASONING_EFFORT` parses the same way.
- `sglang-processor` renders the same, and its DeepSeek tool dump now uses the shared `function_dump`, so `strict: null` renders as Python's `Function` (since #46133) does.
- Tests: the two DeepSeek parity fixtures are regenerated (the five cases above now render; `kwargs_budget_float_string` and V4's `kwargs_budget_string` added; `tool_results` no longer mixes strict and non-strict tools, which recipe rejects), and `test_serving_deepseek_recipe.py` covers the three fixes.

Behavior change: a request with `tools` (and `tool_choice` other than `"none"`) under `continue_final_message` keeps recipe's 400 ("Function call should not be used with prefix"), as DeepSeek's API rejects it; #45315 did not list it.

title: [Fix] cuda-graph: Keep attention metadata and SP workspaces alive across graph variants of a batch size
author: jybsuper
body:
## Motivation

Enabling the LoRA dual graph (a base-only `nolora` decode graph captured next to the `lora` graph for every batch size) made the graph runners capture two graphs per batch size. Attention backends that rebuilt their per-capture metadata keyed only by batch size then freed buffers the first graph still read, and replay refreshed only the table entry. The symptom depended on allocator recycling: zeroed attention rows on GB300 (full prefill backend), a wrong token at a later decode position on H200/H100 (breakable backend), nothing visible elsewhere. The LoRA CI graph tests caught it as an intermittent decode fault. The bug itself is in the attention backends and the sequence-parallel workspace and applies to any second graph per batch size (attention variants, verify tiers), not only to LoRA.

## Modifications

- `flashinfer`: share the CUDA-graph attention wrappers across the graph variants of a batch size (MHA and MLA decode with a one-time bootstrap plan, MLA verify reuse); replay refreshes buffer contents, never table entries.
- `attention` (TRTLLM MHA/MLA): keep per-batch-size capture metadata alive across graph variants, with regression tests.
- `sp_collective_gemm`: retain workspace generations that captured graphs still use when the workspace grows.
- `lora`: the dual decode graph becomes opt-in through `SGLANG_ENABLE_LORA_DUAL_GRAPH` (default off). The fixes cover the backends that exist today, but nothing guarantees that a new backend or runner keeps its per-batch-size metadata alive under a second graph, so the optimization stays off by default; the stacked PR (#46721) adds the tool and skill with which a deployment that wants it can check its own serving command before turning it on.
- test kit: the attention unit-test kit captures two real graphs per decode case, so a backend that drops the first graph's buffers fails in CI.

No tolerance, default graph backend or router precision changes.

## Accuracy Tests

- CPU regression tests (`base-a-test-cpu`): `test_attention_graph_metadata_reuse.py`, `test_trtllm_mha_paged_kv.py`, `test_layernorm_sp.py`, `test_lora_inactive_batch_skip.py`: 12 of 30 cases fail on the base commit, all pass here.
- Attention kit real captures (six backend files) pass on GB300 and H200.
- The standalone lifetime tracer of the stacked PR, run on Qwen1.5-MoE with a LoRA adapter, flashinfer attention and the dual decode graphs (TP1 and TP2): on the base commit three decode graphs read flashinfer wrappers freed while alive and the worker dies; here no dangling operand across 106 captured graphs per worker.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No kernel or scheduling change; the fixes keep already-allocated metadata alive across captures.

title: [Fix] cuda_graph: Release base storage held by empty break inputs
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

A zero-element accelerator view can still own a large nonempty base allocation. Breakable CUDA graph capture currently keeps these views unchanged in eager-break argument closures. For NoPE attention, empty Q/K RoPE views can therefore pin the projection outputs once per layer and captured bucket.

## Modifications

Replace empty accelerator arguments with zero-storage tensors preserving shape, strides, dtype and device. CPU arguments keep their identity, and nonempty arguments keep the existing weak-reference behavior. Add a regression for nested views and multiple graph buckets with changed-input replay after temporary-storage reuse.

This is independent of KDA, ReplaySSM and MoE optimizations. It does not address the separate nonempty-input lifetime issue in #37448 or change the eager-output ownership fixed in #30584.

## Accuracy Tests

Tested directly on main `def8f93212bd997ec19b1395e0d892b442374552` plus this patch, on one B300 (PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.2, Triton 3.8.0):

- New regression against unmodified main: **2 failed, 1 passed**, exposing retained base storage.
- New regression plus existing BCG capture/replay/copy unit classes: **18 passed**.
- Changed-input replay assertions are bit-exact. CPU empty-argument identity is unchanged.
- Pre-commit and `git diff --check` pass.

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/cuda_graph/breakable/test_empty_view_capture.py \
  test/registered/cuda_graph/breakable/test_breakable_cuda_graph.py::TestBreakableCUDAGraphBasic \
  test/registered/cuda_graph/breakable/test_breakable_cuda_graph.py::TestCopyOutput \
  test/registered/cuda_graph/breakable/test_breakable_cuda_graph.py::TestBreakGraphHelper
```

**Validation limitation:** isolated model-level validation remains pending. An earlier GLM-5.3-Flash experiment on `d1bbcbdc`, combining this fix with a separate convolution-layout change, scored 1281/1319 on GSM8K versus baseline 1286/1319; both had four truncations, and both passed 12/12 long-context retrieval probes. Long-input teacher-forcing also varied in repeated unchanged-baseline runs. Those results do not establish the cause or a model-quality pass for this individual patch. ROCm/NPU hardware has not been tested.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The model-free regression uses a shared graph pool with 512/384/256/128-row buckets. The old implementation retains 15 MiB of active projection storage; the patched test requires less than 1 MiB of additional active allocation and verifies replay after input changes.

An earlier isolated memory A/B on 4×B300 used GLM-5.3-Flash, a fixed 1627-slot Mamba pool and the same integration source/configuration in both arms; this empty-view patch was the only difference. Cumulative additional active graph allocation per GPU was:

| Last captured bucket | Before (MiB) | After (MiB) | Released (MiB) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16384 | 2481.26 | 369.26 | 2112 |
| 15872 | 4528.95 | 370.95 | 4158 |
| 15360 | 6509.62 | 371.62 | 6138 |

These are graph-allocation measurements on the earlier integration base, not whole-server VRAM or new-main serving-throughput results. No request-level speedup is claimed.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add registered regression tests.
- [x] Document memory measurements and their scope.
- [ ] Complete isolated model-level validation.

## Cleanup validation (2026-10-29)

Cleanup at `669fc03b`: simplified the storage-ownership explanation and checked shape, stride, dtype, and zero-storage metadata for both nested empty views. Production execution is unchanged. On RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, the regression and existing BCG capture/replay/copy classes passed **18 tests**. Changed-file pre-commit checks pass. The earlier B300 memory measurements above were not rerun.

body:
## Motivation

The ROCm 10.1 MI45x image (`rocm/sgl-dev:*-rocm101-mi45x-*`) is built without MORI, so the MORI tests (`test_umbp_store.py`, `test_mori_backend_basic.py`) fail on it with `No module named 'mori'`.

MORI was turned off because it used to need `rocm_smi`, which ROCm 10.1 no longer ships (only `amd_smi`). The MORI version we pin (`f39fa765`) already switches to `amd_smi` on ROCm 10.1, so it can be turned back on.

While testing, two problems in the CI install script also showed up for this image:

- `.github/workflows/release-docker-amd-rocm10.yml`: build the ROCm 10.1 gfx1250 image with `ENABLE_MORI=1`, same as the ROCm 10.0 one.
- `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh`:
  - Recognize `-rocm1010` images and install `dev_hip_rocm101` extras for them.

No change to model outputs. Tested on an MI450X (gfx1250) with ROCm 10.1, on top of `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm101-mi45x-20261026`: the Dockerfile's MORI step builds unchanged in ~3 minutes, then:

title: [Fix] [AMD] quark: Keep MXFP8 shared experts out of the MXFP4 fused slot on dense-first models
author: ZhengGong-amd
body:
## Motivation

`amd/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` crashes at load because its MXFP8 shared experts are fused into the packed MXFP4 routed-expert slot, so this PR makes the Quark fusion gate probe every named MoE layer and has the MiniMax-M3 hooks ask that gate.

```text
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (384) must match the size of tensor b (768) at non-singleton dimension 1
```

`QuarkConfig.can_fuse_shared_expert()` compares routed and shared specs only at layer 0 and the NextN block. When layer 0 is a dense MLP (MiniMax-M3, DeepSeek-V3, GLM-5.x, Kimi-K2.x), both lookups fall back to the global spec and agree, whatever the MoE layers hold. The MiniMax-M3 hooks never ask the gate anyway: they refuse only `modelopt_mixed` and `minimax_m3_nvfp4`.

## Modifications

- `quark`: `can_fuse_shared_expert()` also probes every target decoder layer whose routed or shared experts are named in `layer_quant_config`, so one mismatched layer refuses fusion in any entry order. Draft entries (`mtp.*`, NextN layers past `num_hidden_layers`, non-`layers.<N>` bases such as `model.mtp.0`) are skipped, so an FP8 MTP block still vetoes fusion only for the draft.
- `minimax`: both MiniMax-M3 hooks call `quant_blocks_shared_experts_fusion(quant_config)`, as DeepSeek-V2/V3/V4 do. The name list stays because `MiniMaxM3Nvfp4Config` does not implement the gate.

The checkpoint now loads unfused and logs why, the path `--disable-shared-experts-fusion` selects today. Across 13 local Quark checkpoints only this one changes (fused → unfused); MiniMax-M3, GLM-5.x, DeepSeek-R1-0528, Kimi-K2.6, Muse-Spark and Qwen3.5 MXFP4 exports keep their decision.

Correct output also needs the MXFP8 scale handling from #46693, #46587 and #44080 (on `main` 2160 `weight_scale not found in params_dict`). #46587 instead requantizes the shared expert to MXFP4 to keep fusion; Quark leaves lossy conversion opt-in via `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion`.

## Accuracy Tests

4×MI355X, TP4, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, `main@6393e66b86` plus the same scale handling in every arm. GSM8K via `sglang.test.run_eval`, 5-shot chat, temperature 0, 1314 items.

| Arm | Load | GSM8K |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | crash (fusion enabled) | — |
| `--disable-shared-experts-fusion` | ok | 0.9665, 0.9673 |
| this PR, default | ok, fusion disabled | 0.9627, 0.9665 |

Both loading arms run the same unfused path; differences are within noise (stderr ±0.005).

New tests in `test_quark_config.py` and `test_shared_experts_fusion_gates.py` cover dense leading layers, both entry orders, named routed experts, NextN drafts and a real `QuarkConfig` in M3.1's layout; 106 pass.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not a speed change: the fused path does not load on `main`.

title: [Fix] [Intel] gemma4: Bidirectional image attention on the intel_xpu backend
author: SKRohit
body:
## Motivation 

Same as #44225 for Gemma4.

On `--attention-backend intel_xpu`, Gemma 4 image tokens get causal attention instead of bidirectional attention. `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration.prepare_attn_masks` handles only Triton and FA4. On any other backend it logs `Bidirectional attention for image tokens requires TritonAttnBackend. Falling back to causal attention` and returns. Text is unaffected, so the only symptom is poor vision accuracy: `google/gemma-4-12B-it-qat-w4a16-ct` scores docvqa_val ANLS 0.349 on an Arc Pro B70.

## Modifications

- `gemma4_mm.prepare_attn_masks`: on XPU, hand `XPUAttentionBackend` the per-token image-block ids that Gemma 3 already builds (`Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration._build_xpu_image_block_ids`). The sgl-kernel-xpu FMHA prefill turns them into bidirectional image attention.
- Cookbook (Gemma4 "Configuration Tips"): document that the sgl-kernel-xpu mask has no sliding-window variant, so on intel_xpu a prompt longer than the 1024-token window loses it on the sliding layers. `max_soft_tokens` 560 fits; 1120 does not.
- Test: `test/registered/xpu/test_xpu_gemma3_bidirectional_attn.py` checks that Gemma 4 sets the same block ids as Gemma 3. It fails on the unpatched code (block ids left `None`).

title: [Fix] metrics: Avoid blocking the scheduler on KV metrics backpressure
author: dorado269
body:
<!-- REBASE-48K-20261102:BEGIN -->
## Current rebase and CI status (2026-11-02)

Head `840ddc2dab5e6bad4db7686e7d610a97a3310539` is rebased onto upstream main `23c6442cde7fb38230134ba0e3513ad2332aa5cf`. The patch is unchanged according to `git range-diff`.

Local validation: 4 real-ZMQ CPU regression tests and scoped pre-commit hooks passed; range-diff unchanged. No fresh GPU/model or performance result is claimed; earlier measurements below remain tied to their original revisions.

[Latest Base run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41402282474) (attempt 2) stops at **Require run-ci label (optional)**. The PR is Ready. A CI-authorized maintainer must add `run-ci` and issue `/tag-and-rerun-ci`; the author-requested retry ran but cannot grant the label.

[Repository-wide lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41402282458/job/125136503294) independently fails on `F821 logger` in the unchanged main XPU graph runner. [Upstream report and reproducer](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30980#issuecomment-6571123990). The PR-scoped local hooks passed; the full upstream check has not passed. Rebase after the main repair lands.

[Rebase validation and CI request](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46820#issuecomment-6570996215).
<!-- REBASE-48K-20261102:END -->

## Problem and root cause

Auxiliary KV-metrics publication runs in the scheduler loop. A missing or slow PUSH-socket receiver can exhaust its queue; the default blocking `sock_send` then stalls request progress. This remains present on main `8a455f1`.

Our archived GLM-5.2 run `c44a` hung at this call (py-spy, October 9, ledger R001); `c44b` advanced past it with nonblocking metrics. Later stack throughput is not evidence for this patch, and the historical throughput runs used simulated MTP acceptance.

## Fix

Send auxiliary KV metrics with `zmq.NOBLOCK`, catch only queue-unavailable `zmq.Again`, and warn once per publisher. Keep KV-event publishing on its existing separate path. Unexpected socket errors still propagate. A healthy receiver continues to receive the serialized metrics after draining a full queue.

## Validation

Registered CPU tests use real ZeroMQ sockets for an unbound receiver, full high-water mark and recovery, plus closed-socket and non-EAGAIN controls. These tests do not require GPUs or models.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/managers/test_kv_metrics_backpressure.py
pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-commit --files python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/kv_events_publisher.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_kv_metrics_backpressure.py
```

Local result: **4 passed**; all applicable pre-commit hooks passed.

## Review scope and CI

This change deliberately treats auxiliary KV metrics as best-effort telemetry: a full queue drops the current sample and warns once, so telemetry backpressure cannot stop request progress. Durable KV-event publication remains on its existing separate path. Please review this policy and the bounded logging behavior.

Author-side validation is complete for this CPU/socket-only change at `82176e70284c8d67b41de74b8e8005d148e57c8b`: the four real-ZMQ regression cases and applicable local pre-commit hooks pass, and upstream lint/title checks pass. No GPU or model execution is needed to validate this socket contract; no throughput improvement is claimed.

Ready for review. Upstream CPU test execution still requires the maintainer-controlled `run-ci` label; the existing gated/skipped test workflows are not claimed as passing. Maintainer review and required upstream checks remain merge requirements.

title: [Fix] dsa: Remove host syncs from rank-divergent eager paths
author: dorado269
body:
<!-- REBASE-48K-20261102:BEGIN -->
## Current rebase and CI status (2026-11-02)

Head `3c70f61f29731eb3b1a9da5e6b15be862b1f96cd` is rebased onto upstream main `23c6442cde7fb38230134ba0e3513ad2332aa5cf`. The patch is unchanged according to `git range-diff`.

Local validation: 3 CPU regression tests plus 2 subtests and scoped pre-commit hooks passed; range-diff unchanged. No fresh GPU/model or performance result is claimed; earlier measurements below remain tied to their original revisions.

[Latest Base run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41402508388) (attempt 2) stops at **Require run-ci label (optional)**. The PR is Ready. A CI-authorized maintainer must add `run-ci` and issue `/tag-and-rerun-ci`; the author-requested retry ran but cannot grant the label.

[Repository-wide lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41402508194/job/125137192923) independently fails on `F821 logger` in the unchanged main XPU graph runner. [Upstream report and reproducer](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30980#issuecomment-6571123990). The PR-scoped local hooks passed; the full upstream check has not passed. Rebase after the main repair lands.

[Rebase validation and CI request](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46830#issuecomment-6571015382).
<!-- REBASE-48K-20261102:END -->

## Problem and root cause

DSA declares `needs_cpu_seq_lens=False`, but its eager fallback still reads GPU lengths on the host when the host mirror is absent. Under PD + DP-attention + EAGLE/MTP, busy and idle ranks can take different host-mirror branches. A blocking `.max().item()` or `.cpu()` on only some ranks can prevent them from issuing matching collectives and hang the group.

The two offending paths remain on main `8a455f1`: page-table width selection without a host mirror, and DRAFT_EXTEND_V2 host-mirror materialization. The original report observed a first-routed-request deadlock; the fresh evidence below is a CPU contract regression, not a new distributed deadlock reproduction.

## Fix

Use the static request-table width when a host length mirror is unavailable. Keep actual GPU sequence lengths for per-row bounds, and retain the narrower width when a host mirror is already present. DRAFT_EXTEND_V2 uses its supplied extend-length metadata without constructing unused host mirrors. Existing graph behavior is unchanged.

## Validation

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_dsa_eager_metadata_no_host_sync.py
pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-commit --files python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa_backend.py test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_dsa_eager_metadata_no_host_sync.py
```

Rebased CPU result: **3 passed, 2 subtests passed**. Unpatched main: **2 expected failures, 1 passed, 2 subtests passed**. Tests run the actual metadata entry point, reject host reads of the device-length inputs, inspect decode/draft page tables, and retain a host-mirror control. GPU helper kernels use CPU substitutes; these are dispatch/data-contract tests. All applicable lint passed.

## Historical hardware evidence and port comparison

The production added/removed lines are identical to the original #33973 diff; this port changes placement to match main and adds registered CPU regressions. The original investigation reported that the first-request deadlock cleared on 8×MI355X with GLM-5.2-FP8, PD + DP attention + EAGLE MTP. It also recorded MI300X narrow-versus-static-width top-k checks: real selections and scores matched with per-row masking; surplus -inf slots for sequences shorter than top-k were present at both widths. See the [original verification and its limitations](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33973).

Rechecked the current source contracts: DRAFT_EXTEND_V2 still uses the supplied extend lengths; prefix checks/ragged dispatch remain restricted to ordinary EXTEND, and the additional automatic prefill-selection use of seq_lens_sum is guarded by ForwardMode.EXTEND. The added CPU regression exercises the current metadata entry point without host reads and retains the host-mirror control. Identical patch lines do not establish identical whole-stack behavior, so the historical deployment and current CPU results are reported separately.

## Review scope and remaining coverage

Ready for review using the historical hardware evidence, unchanged production delta, current consumer audit and current-main regression coverage. A full fresh PD/DP/MTP hardware run at this head has not been performed. Broader AMD/CUDA regression, long-context memory qualification and maintainer-enabled CI remain follow-up coverage; no new throughput or whole-stack accuracy result is claimed.

This replaces closed stale draft #33973. GitHub refused reopening that PR; its discussion links here. Required upstream CI and maintainer review remain merge gates.

title: [Fix] [AMD] aiter: Use the layer's softmax scale in MHA prefill and decode
author: chaojhou
body:
## Motivation

With the aiter attention backend (the default for MHA models on ROCm), a model whose softmax scale is not `head_dim**-0.5` produces garbage, with a bf16 KV cache too. The default decode passes the backend-wide `self.scale = 1 / sqrt(head_dim)` to `paged_attention_ragged`, and the NHD prefill (`mha_batch_prefill_func`, plus the two vectorized-5D prefill calls in `aiter_utils.py`) passes no `softmax_scale`, so aiter falls back to `head_dim**-0.5`. #38754 moved the `unified_attention` calls to `layer.scaling`; these four sites were left as they were.

Measured below: Granite 3.x (`attention_multiplier` 1/64 or 1/128, 8-11x below `head_dim**-0.5`) and Granite 4.0 (`GraniteMoeHybridForCausalLM`). By the same code path, also GraniteMoE, Phi-3-small (`1 / head_dim`) and models served through the Transformers fallback with a custom scaling. Models with sliding-window layers (Gemma 2/3/4 and others) take the unified path and are not affected.

On main, `ibm-granite/granite-3.3-2b-instruct` continues "The capital of France is" with " a fascinating number of times. The first time I visited a federal circuit..."; with `--attention-backend triton` it answers " Paris.".

## Modifications

- `aiter_backend.py`: pass `layer.scaling` to `paged_attention_ragged` in decode and as `softmax_scale` to `mha_batch_prefill_func` in the NHD extend; remove `self.scale`, which has no other reader.
- `aiter_utils.py`: pass `softmax_scale=layer.scaling` to both `mha_batch_prefill_func` calls in `forward_extend_vectorized_5d`.
- `test_aiter_fp8_kv_scales_paths.py`: the `paged_attention_ragged` decode and NHD prefill cases also run at `layer.scaling = 1 / head_dim`, and a new case runs both SHUFFLE 5D prefill paths (fresh prompts, and a cached prefix gathered from the 5D pool) with a bf16 cache, through `AiterAttnBackend` with the real aiter kernels against an fp32 reference. On main the `1 / head_dim` prefill cases fail (relative L2 error 2.1 to 6.1) and decode fails because the backend still reads `self.scale`; with this PR all pass.

For models whose scale is `head_dim**-0.5` nothing reaching the kernels changes: the prefill passes the expression aiter defaults to, and the decode kernel takes a 32-bit `float`, in which `1 / sqrt(d)` and `d ** -0.5` are bitwise equal for every head_dim from 8 to 1024.

## Accuracy Tests

MI355X (gfx950), main 132b0f0ae7, bf16 KV cache, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, CUDA graphs on. GSM8K with two harnesses: `python -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 1319 --max-tokens 4096` (chat API, greedy, 1314 questions), and lm_eval 0.4.13 5-shot completion (greedy, 1319 questions, strict-match):

| Model | Harness | `--attention-backend triton` | aiter, main | aiter, this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ibm-granite/granite-3.3-2b-instruct | run_eval | 0.2268 ± 0.0116 | 0.0122 | 0.2397 ± 0.0118 |
| | lm_eval | 0.6293 ± 0.0133 | 0.0023 | 0.6187 ± 0.0134 |
| ibm-granite/granite-4.0-350m | run_eval | 0.3478 ± 0.0131 | 0.0145 | 0.3425 ± 0.0131 |
| | lm_eval | 0.2654 ± 0.0122 | 0.0023 | 0.2691 ± 0.0122 |
| Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B (default scale) | run_eval | | 0.6218 ± 0.0134 | 0.6225 ± 0.0134 |
| | lm_eval | | 0.4230 ± 0.0136 | 0.4200 ± 0.0136 |

The two harnesses score the models differently in absolute terms, but agree that main collapses Granite and that this PR matches triton within one standard error. In the lm_eval runs, each site breaks Granite on its own: on main, aiter prefill with triton decode scores 0.0000 and triton prefill with aiter decode 0.0008. With `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1 --page-size 16`, whose kernels already receive `layer.scaling`, main scores 0.6194.

Unit tests: the new cases pass; the existing aiter attention tests (`test_aiter_asm_prefill_gather`, `test_aiter_cross_layer_kv_guard`, `test_aiter_fp8_q_unified_attention`, `test_aiter_gluon_h12_fp8`, `test_aiter_swa_kv_pool_resolver`, `test_fused_fp8_kv_write`, `test_asm_context_prefill_gather_indices`) pass, 53 tests. gfx942 is not tested.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No kernel, launch or argument change for models whose scale is `head_dim**-0.5` (see above), so no speed change is expected; not measured.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Fix] dspark: Keep the real verify accept cost under simulated acceptance
author: weireweire
body:
## Motivation

`SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN` is a benchmark mode. It should change only the accepted length. Every operation real serving runs in a verify step should still run at real cost, so a simulated run's step time matches a real run at the same acceptance length.

**What this PR delivers is parity in the accept region.** After this change, the GPU work a simulated step does in its accept region is the real accept plus one row draw. Step time from the batch logs barely moves: at 128 running per rank, simulation is ~0.6 ms slower than real both before and after this PR. The remaining gap is in MegaMoE, most likely routing on the simulated text, which this PR does not touch.

DSpark had three paths that changed the per-step work only under simulation:

1. **Eager accept (#45421).** `accept_and_finalize` passed `sampling_info=None` under simulation, so a sampling batch ran `AcceptGreedy` (row argmax) instead of the sampling accept that real serving runs: the draft and target softmax plus the rejection kernel.
2. **Eager simulated bonus (#41981).** `simulated_bonus_sample` drew a Gumbel-max sample over the full vocabulary for all bs x (gamma+1) verify rows, then kept only the row at the simulated length. This is simulation-only work, about 6x what one row needs.
3. **Fused static accept tail under `SGLANG_DSPARK_SIMULATE_FOLD`** (opt-in, with `SGLANG_DSPARK_FUSED_ACCEPT_TAIL`):
   - The verify graph skipped the row argmax that the greedy accept runs.
   - With TP > 1 and the accept-site broadcast selected (the default `SGLANG_SPEC_TP_SYNC=all`), real serving turns the fused tail off and runs `_accept`: 3 broadcasts, finalize, out-tokens and the static-buffer copies. Simulation kept the fused tail with 2 broadcasts.

Items 1 and 2 roughly cancel at large batch and do not cancel at small batch, so the error changes sign with batch size (numbers below). Fixing only item 2 would make simulation cheaper than real serving at every batch size.

## Modifications

- **Eager accept.** `TargetVerifyExecutor.accept_and_finalize` runs the accept that real serving runs, for greedy and sampling batches alike. `build_accept_outs` then overrides `correct_len` with the simulated value and draws the bonus at the simulated row, as before.
- **Simulated bonus.** `simulated_bonus_sample` draws only the simulated row per request. It uses `simulated_bonus_sample_graph`, the row kernel the graph path already uses, seeded from `random.getrandbits(31)` as the graph path is. The all-rows kernels are removed. The only simulation-only work left in the accept is this one row draw (+73 us at 128 per rank).
- **Fused static accept tail.**
  - `DsparkVerifyEpilogue` takes the same fused-tail decision as real serving: the tail is off whenever the accept-site broadcast is selected. Under `simulate_fold` with the broadcast, simulation now runs `_accept` like real serving and adds the in-graph row draw.
  - `_static_accept_tail` always computes the row argmax. Under `simulate_fold` the tail still takes the simulated bonus and does not read the argmax.
- **Test.** `test_dspark_simulated_bonus.py::test_bf16_full_vocab_low_temperature` accepts any token whose logit equals the row max. bf16 logits tie at the max, and Gumbel-max may pick any tied token, while the test expected the first argmax.

`SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_GREEDY=1` is still the explicit way to skip the sampling work. It sets the batch's sampling info to `None` for both the draft and the accept, but only for sampling batches that have:
- no grammar;
- no penalties, logit bias or custom logit processor;
- no top-k, top-p or min-p.

Greedy requests carry top_k=1, so a mixed greedy + sampled batch also keeps the real sampling work.

What does not change:
- The accepted length comes from the same CPU draw (`sample_simulated_acc_len`), so its distribution is the same as before.
- The bonus keeps the request's sampling law: a Gumbel-max sample at the request's temperature, argmax for greedy, and unchanged top-k / top-p handling. Sampled tokens differ from before only through the RNG stream.
- Non-simulated paths are unchanged.

**AMD / HIP.** Simulated runs on HIP get slower. #41981 skipped the sampling accept under simulation on HIP on purpose, and #45421 extended that skip to CUDA. With this PR the softmax and rejection kernels run under simulation on HIP too, as they do in real serving there. Set `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_GREEDY=1` to keep the old cost for temperature-only batches.

Other simulation-specific behavior I checked and left as is:
- `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_DSPARK_SIM_DRAW_AHEAD` only moves the simulation-only length and seed draw ahead of the draft launch. It skips no real work.
- The sampling-accept region graph (`SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_SAMPLING_ACCEPT_GRAPH`) already runs the full sampling accept under simulation, then applies the simulated length and the row-c bonus. The eager path now matches it.
- `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN > 1` requires a verify-all schedule. A simulated run therefore cannot reproduce a deployment that trims verify windows (cap-accept, or compact with a profiled SPS table).
- The block-accept estimator refuses to run under simulation. It is observability only.
- Grammar: simulation commits `drafts[:c]` without checking them against the grammar, so a json-schema request can fail with "Grammar accept_token failed". It is not caused by this PR. On TP4 at T=1, main under simulation failed 2 of 32 requests, and this PR failed 0 of 32 in the same run and 1 of 4 in another. Every request that completed produced valid JSON.

## Accuracy Tests

Existing DSpark tests on GB300:
- `test_dspark_simulated_bonus`, `test_dspark_accept_tail`, `test_dspark_sim_draw_ahead`, `test_dspark_sampling_accept_graph`, `test_dspark_kernel_parity`, `test_block_verification`;

title: [Fix] dspark/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash: Inject decode-step draft KV under the draft's TP placement
author: thanhhao98
body:
## Motivation

With attention DP, DSpark on MiniMax-M3.1-Flash (#45925) crashes at the first decode step at `--attn-dp-size 4`, and in a PD decode worker at `--attn-dp-size 2`:

```
  File ".../speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py", line 1296, in _forward_decode
    self._verify_executor.commit_hidden(
  ...
  File ".../models/dspark_minimax.py", line 172, in project_target_hidden
    return self.hidden_norm(self._fc_gatherer(self.fc(target_hidden)[0]))
  ...
ValueError: Mismatched mW.shape[0] on argument #1 when calling: `__call__(mX: Tensor([n0, 24576], bfloat16), mW: Tensor([24576], bfloat16), ...)`, expected to be 24576
```

Under attention DP a dense DSpark draft runs on the attention-TP group, which `DSparkWorkerV2` enters with `_draft_context()` to build the draft, capture its graphs, propose, and inject the prefill KV, but not for the decode-step `commit_hidden`. There the M3.1 draft all-gathers its column-parallel `fc` output over the whole TP group: 4 x 6144 = 24576 columns into the 6144-wide `hidden_norm` at `--tp 4 --attn-dp-size 4`, and 4 x 3072 = 12288 in a PD decode worker at `--attn-dp-size 2`.

Colocated `--attn-dp-size 2` happens to work: `MultimemAllGatherer` binds its multimem buffer to the group of its first call, the prefill inject inside the placement, which a PD decode worker never runs. At attention-TP size 1 it builds no buffer, and its NCCL fallback gathers over the current TP group.

## Modifications

Run the decode-step `commit_hidden` inside `self._draft_context()`, like the prefill inject. Without attention DP the context is a no-op.

## Accuracy Tests

MiniMax-M3.1-Flash with DSpark, 4x GB300 (PD: one tray per role), main and this PR on `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-cu134-20261026-5ef9901`. GSM8K with sgl-eval 0.1.3 (temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, `--max-tokens 32768`); cells are all 1,319 questions / the first 100 one at a time:

| Layout | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `--tp 4 --attn-dp-size 4 --ep 4` (MegaMoE) | crash | 96.36 / 96 |
| `--tp 4 --attn-dp-size 2 --ep 4` (MegaMoE) | 96.13 / 97 | 95.45 / 96 |
| `--tp 4` (TRT-LLM routed MoE) | 95.45 / 99 | 95.91 / 98 |
| PD 1P1D (Mooncake), `--attn-dp-size 2` on both roles | decode worker crash | 95.15 / 98 |

At temperature 1.0 one standard error on 1,319 questions is about 0.5 points.

DSpark acceptance length at `--attn-dp-size 4` is in line with `--tp 4`: 4.01 / 4.23 against 4.01 / 4.28 (SPEED-Bench coding / GSM8K prompts, T 1.0). Passkey retrieval passes at 126k and 503k prompt tokens, and `--disaggregation-enable-kv-checksum` logs no mismatch on either PD role.

The existing DSpark CPU tests in `test/registered/unit/spec/` pass.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No kernel or graph change: one more host-side context entry per decode step under attention DP.

<details><summary>Reproduce</summary>

```bash
SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=32768 \
sglang serve --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash --trust-remote-code \
  --reasoning-parser minimax-m3 --tool-call-parser minimax-m3 \
  --tp 4 --attn-dp-size 4 --enable-dp-lm-head --ep 4 --moe-a2a-backend megamoe \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-use-block-verification \
  --cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \
  --max-running-requests 128 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 128 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --tokenizer-worker-num 8

sgl-eval run gsm8k --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 --temperature 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --max-tokens 32768
sgl-eval run gsm8k --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 --temperature 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --max-tokens 32768 \
  --num-examples 100 --num-threads 1
```

Other rows: `--attn-dp-size 2`; `--tp 4 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm_routed` without the attention-DP and MegaMoE flags; PD: the `--attn-dp-size 2` command on both roles plus `--disaggregation-mode prefill|decode --disaggregation-transfer-backend mooncake --disaggregation-enable-kv-checksum` (`--enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-size 150` on the prefill), behind `sglang_router.launch_router --pd-disaggregation`.

</details>

title: [Fix] scheduler: Reserve member rows of beam leaders admitted in the same prefill
author: apex-mochen
body:
## Motivation

With beam search, the scheduler can crash with this assertion when a beam request shares a prefill with other requests and req-to-token rows are scarce:

```
AssertionError: Beam member spawn needs 2 req-to-token slots but only 1 are free; the admission gate (get_num_allocatable_reqs) must reserve them.
```

How it happens:

1. A `beam_width=k` leader takes one req-to-token row at admission. It spawns its `k-1` member rows later, at its prefill relay.
2. `get_num_allocatable_reqs` subtracts `pending_member_rows(running_batch)`, which covers groups that are already running. It does not cover leaders already admitted to the prefill being built (`adder.can_run_list`).
3. A later candidate in the same pass then fits into rows the leader has promised to its members. When the leader's prefill relays, `_spawn_member_rows` finds too few free rows and the assertion takes the scheduler down.

Example: with 3 free rows, a `beam_width=3` leader is admitted (it needs 3 rows in total), then a plain request is admitted too, because the gate still sees 3 free rows for 2 requests.

The rows only bind when the running batch is near `max_running_requests`, so this shows up under load.

## Modifications

- `BeamCoordinator.pending_member_rows_of(reqs)`: the existing `pending_member_rows(batch)` over a request list. `pending_member_rows` now calls it.
- `get_num_allocatable_reqs` takes `admitted_reqs` and also subtracts their pending member rows from the row budget. The admission loop passes `can_run_list`.
- `test_scheduler_held_row_admission.py`: its coordinator stub gains `pending_member_rows_of`.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable. No model-side change.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Not applicable.

How I tested: CPU only, no model, no server.

- On one H200, Qwen3-0.6B with `--max-running-requests 8192` and 16 concurrent beam requests of width 1000-2000 crashes on `main` with the assertion above. With this change, all requests complete and the scheduler stays up.
- I found the crash with a CPU scheduler driver. It runs the real `Scheduler` and `BeamCoordinator`, and calls `capture_pre_sample_logits` on fake logits that are a deterministic function of the tokens each KV row holds. It mixes beam requests (width 2 to 4) with plain ones. On `main`, 19 of 40 seeds hit the assertion above. With this change, none do.
- With the driver, I also found that priority preemption can preempt a beam leader and corrupt other requests' KV. That is a separate bug, so I will send a separate PR for it.

## Checklist

title: [Fix] [AMD] memory_pool: Keep K and V in separate allocations on ROCm
author: omirosh
body:
## Motivation

This ROCm bugfix, with no speed change, turns off the fused K/V allocation from #32272 on ROCm, because with it the MI35x PD disaggregation test `test_disaggregation_basic.py` returns garbage on every AMD PR.

#32272 changed `MHATokenToKVPool` to store each layer's K and V as block-aligned halves of one allocation, so `v_buffer[i]` now starts inside the allocation of `k_buffer[i]`. Only the trtllm_mha fmha_v2 prefill on CUDA reads that layout, but the allocation change has no platform gate. The test serves Qwen3-8B with Mooncake, prefill and decode on one MI35x node. The decode server now returns nonsense with no transfer error:

```
FAIL: test_gsm8k (__main__.TestDisaggregationAccuracy.test_gsm8k)
AssertionError: 0.005 not greater than 0.7
```

The MI35x 8-GPU disaggregation job ran on many PRs on 2026-10-27. Grouped by the main commit each run merged onto:

| main base | jobs | `test_disaggregation_basic.py` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `db90f584d2`, `2b36c718cb`, `e4d4a9a7de` (before #32272) | 9 | passed in all 9 ([example](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40464519661/job/122061186617)) |
| `1a120754e0` (#32272) and every later base seen (`d3a157a2f2`, `61a676125a`, `449617bc94`, `3927a73a34`, `8a455f1b90`, `a6f5bd397b`) | 9 | failed in all 9, GSM8K accuracy 0.0 to 0.01 ([first](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40468145469/job/122072975234)) |

Seven of the nine earlier jobs failed in `test_disaggregation_pp.py`, which also fails on main's scheduled runs. `test_disaggregation_basic.py` passed in each of them.

Three other commits sit between `e4d4a9a7de` and `1a120754e0`. They are #31286 (removes an unused HiCache field), #46366 (gfx1250 diffusion GEMM) and #33743 (flashinfer TRT-LLM MoE weight reload). None of them touches the KV pool or PD. Every job ran on a different runner, so one bad machine does not explain it.

Mooncake's HIP transport carries the same-node transfer. It registers each KV buffer with its own `hipIpcGetMemHandle` and maps peer addresses as `dest - entry.addr + shm_addr`. With the fused layout, both handles of a layer point into one allocation. I did not find which step then puts V at the wrong address, so the evidence here is the bisect, not a mechanism.

## Modifications

- In `memory_pool.py`, the fused allocation now also needs `not _is_hip`. ROCm gets back the two `torch.zeros` per layer it had before #32272.
- In `test_mha_pool_fused_kv_layout.py`, a new CPU test patches `_is_hip` and checks that K and V do not share storage. The existing fused-layout test still runs on the CPU runner, where `_is_hip` is false. Both tests build the pool with a shared `_make_pool` helper.

Off ROCm this change does nothing. On ROCm nothing reads the fused layout, because fmha_v2 runs only on CUDA, so the only effect there is the allocation from before #32272.

## Accuracy Tests

I have not run it on MI35x. The AMD disaggregation job of this PR is the end-to-end check, and I will post its result here.

The CPU unit test on this branch and on main:

| | `test_v_is_block_aligned_offset_from_k` | `test_rocm_keeps_k_and_v_in_separate_allocations` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| this PR | pass | pass |
| main | pass | fail (`AssertionError: 4573659136 == 4573659136 : layer 0`) |

Untested: same-node PD on CUDA through an IPC transport, which could meet the same layout.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

None. ROCm goes back to the allocation it used before #32272. CUDA is unchanged, so it keeps the fmha_v2 speedup from #32272.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (isort 7.0.0, ruff 0.15.1 check and format)

Pending the MI35x PD job of this PR.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Fix] diffusion: keep tied vocab tables on device under layerwise offload
author: OnePunchMonk
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #47297

With default flags, LingBot-Video-MoE (`robbyant/lingbot-video-moe-30b-a3b`) crashes in text encoding on a single H100:

```
[LingBotVideoTextEncodingStage] Error during execution: Expected all tensors to be on the same device,
but got mat2 is on cpu, different from other tensors on cuda:0 (when checking argument in method wrapper_CUDA_mm)
```

The auto memory policy puts the text encoder on layerwise offload, which parks the declared host-resident vocab table (`Qwen3VLTextModel.embed_tokens`) in host memory. This checkpoint has `tie_word_embeddings=True`, so `Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration.lm_head.weight` is the same Parameter. The head's matmul then gets a CPU weight.

## Modifications

- `_host_resident_tables` skips a declared table whose weight is also owned by another module (a tied output head). Untied tables are handled as before.
- One regression case in the existing `test_host_resident_vocab_table.py`.

## Accuracy Tests

Real checkpoint, 1x H100 80GB, `sglang generate --height 480 --width 480 --num-frames 81 --num-inference-steps 40 --seed 0` with the cookbook JSON prompt, default flags.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| e2e generate | crashes (above) | video generated |
| vs known-good placement (`--layerwise-offload-components vae --text-encoder-cpu-offload true`) | n/a | bitwise identical, 81/81 frames, max pixel diff 0 |
| `test_a_table_tied_to_an_output_head_is_left_alone` | fails (`[Embedding(4096, 64)] == []`) | passes |

Unit tests (`test_host_resident_vocab_table.py`, `test_gemma4_unified_layerwise_offload.py`): CPU main 11 passed / 1 skipped, this PR 12 passed / 1 skipped; on H100 13 passed (includes the CUDA-only case).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speed change intended. Tied tables now stay on device (the gather on host is skipped only for them).

title: [Fix] rust-server: Report the launched --tokenizer-path from the info endpoints
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

In Rust frontend mode, `/server_info`, `/model_info` and `/get_model_info` (and gRPC `GetModelInfo` / `GetServerInfo`) report the tokenizer path the Rust server *loads*, not the launched `--tokenizer-path`. The loader path comes from the scheduler's `rust_server_tokenizer_path()` hook, which a model-side override may point at a process-local copy of the tokenizer, for example a temporary directory holding only `tokenizer.json`. That path then leaks out of the info endpoints, and a client that loads the tokenizer from `/server_info` or `/model_info` gets a path that is temporary and may not exist on its side. The Python server reports the launched `--tokenizer-path` (`http_server.py`, `model_info` / `get_model_info`).

## Modifications

- `message/config.rs`: `ServerArgs` gains `public_tokenizer_path`, the launched `--tokenizer-path` as reported by the info endpoints. `tokenizer_path` keeps its meaning (the source this server loads) and its docstring now says why the two differ.
- `core/handle.rs`: `CoreMetadata` takes `tokenizer_path` from `public_tokenizer_path`, so every info surface (HTTP and gRPC) reports the launched path. The tokenizer, detokenizer and chat template still load from `tokenizer_path`; serving behaviour is unchanged, and when both paths are the same the reported value does not change.
- `rust_server/config.py`: passes the launched `--tokenizer-path` as the new required keyword next to the loader path.
- `http/info.rs` tests: the `/model_info` and `/server_info` route tests now give the loader a path that differs from the public one, so they fail without the `CoreMetadata` change.
- `test_rust_server_dp_ports.py`: two new handoff cases check `tokenizer_path` (the scheduler's loader path) and `public_tokenizer_path` (the launched path) separately.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no model forward or kernel code changes; generated tokens are unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run. The change adds one string field to the launch config.

## Testing

- `rust/`: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes; `cargo test --locked -p sglang-server` passes (394 tests); `cargo clippy --locked -p sglang-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- `python -m pytest test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_rust_server_dp_ports.py`: 42 passed, including the two new cases.
- Live check on a 1-GPU Rust-mode launch of `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct` with the loader hook patched to stage a temporary directory holding only `tokenizer.json`: before, `/server_info` and `/model_info` both reported the temporary directory; after, both report `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`, and `/generate` output is unchanged.

title: [Fix] dsv4: Build the DSpark draft block metadata without host sequence lengths
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

Since #45925, the DSpark draft batch carries no host sequence lengths when the draft attention backend sets `needs_cpu_seq_lens = False`. That is right for `trtllm_mha`, but the DeepSeek-V4 backend also sets it to False under DSpark on CUDA. Its draft-block prep, `init_forward_metadata_dspark_draft_block`, then read the lengths back with `seq_lens.tolist()`, which caused two problems:

- **The metadata glue graph turned off.** The first glue capture of each server fails with `Cannot copy between CPU and CUDA tensors during CUDA graph capture`, and the runner falls back to eager draft metadata prep for the rest of the run:
  ```
  Metadata glue-graph capture failed for key (1, '5', '5'); falling back to eager metadata prep permanently.
  ```
- **A device-to-host sync on every draft step.** From then on, every eager prep calls `seq_lens.tolist()` again.

On CUDA the draft-block prep does not need host lengths at all:

- The extend lengths are `[block_size] * bs`.
- The causal expand runs its Triton kernel from the device tensors and drops the host lists.
- Compression is off for the draft block.

## Modifications

- `compute_uniform_extend_lengths` accepts `seq_lens_cpu=None`. It then takes the batch size from `seq_lens` and returns no host copy of the extended lengths.
- The DeepSeek-V4 draft-block prep passes `None` through instead of calling `seq_lens.tolist()`.
- One CPU test for the helper, with and without host lengths.

## Accuracy Tests

The draft metadata comes from the same device tensors as before. Accept length is unchanged with real drafts: DEP2 with real acceptance gives a median of 2.0 to 2.2 on both arms at every batch size.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

GB300, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DSpark block 5, one node per arm, one run each. Main is `cb55d77d37`, and the fix is the same commit plus this change. sa-bench uses input length 1024. The output length is 4096 for TP4 and 1024 for DEP2. Forward occupancy comes from `SGLANG_ENABLE_METRICS_DEVICE_TIMER=1`.

TP4, EP1, simulated acceptance 3.51:

| Concurrency | Arm | Glue capture failures | Output tok/s | Median ITL (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | Forward occupancy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | main | 4 | 562.0 | 5.91 | 1.69 | 94.3% |
| 1 | fix | 0 | 655.5 | 5.01 | 1.44 | 98.7% |
| 8 | main | 4 | 2,081.6 | 10.08 | 3.25 | 97.6% |
| 8 | fix | 0 | 2,122.2 | 9.29 | 3.04 | 99.2% |

DEP2 with DP attention and MegaMoE, real acceptance:

| Concurrency | Arm | Glue capture failures | Output tok/s | Median ITL (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | main | 2 | 946.7 | 13.68 | 7.10 |
| 8 | fix | 0 | 915.9 | 12.90 | 7.26 |
| 64 | main | 2 | 3,829.6 | 25.64 | 16.17 |
| 64 | fix | 0 | 3,773.8 | 25.12 | 16.19 |

The gain shows where the step is short and host-bound: at TP4 batch 1, output throughput is 17% higher and the median ITL is 15% lower. DEP2 is within run-to-run noise.

title: [Fix] lora: Keep per-expert MoE LoRA buffers for experts already wrapped
author: HJSang
body:
## Problem
Since #45231, `LoRAMemoryPool._has_moe_module` checks each `FusedMoE` against `should_apply_lora(name)`. The pool is built after `init_lora_modules()` wraps the experts, so the `FusedMoE` is named `<name>.base_layer`, and patterns anchored at `mlp.experts` (gpt-oss, MiMo-V2) reject it. These models then get dense 3D buffers:
- gpt-oss MoE LoRA fails CUDA graph capture with `NotImplementedError: virtual-expert MoE LoRA does not support padded Marlin outputs`
- the MiMo-V2 Tinker LoRA test raises `IndexError: tuple index out of range` at `lora_b_list[0].shape[3]` in `virtual_experts.py`

This broke the miles nightly gpt-oss and MiMo LoRA tests (https://github.com/radixark/miles/actions/runs/40528466754).

## Fix
Match `should_apply_lora` against the name without `.base_layer`. Experts a model keeps out of LoRA, such as DeepSeek-V4's routed experts, are never wrapped, so they stay excluded.

## Tests
- New regression test `TestHasMoeModuleAfterWrapping` in `test_mem_pool_ep_unit.py`: fails before the fix, passes after. All 61 tests in the file pass.
- End to end on 2x H200, miles `tests/e2e/megatron/model_scripts/test_gpt_oss_20b_moe_lora_ci.py`: fails at sglang `b8d46f2`, passes at `8237a5b` (before #45231) and with this fix.
- Miles CI with this PR pinned (`ci-sglang-pr: #46894` on https://github.com/radixark/miles/pull/4484), both tests that failed in the nightly now pass:
  - `test_gpt_oss_20b_moe_lora_ci.py`: PASS in 839s, both the per-expert and the shared-outer + virtual-experts configs (https://github.com/radixark/miles/actions/runs/40602473473)
  - `tests/e2e/lora/test_tinker_mimo_v2_6_4layer.py`: PASS in 233s (https://github.com/radixark/miles/actions/runs/40602452095)

title: [Fix] dsv4: Let the DSpark draft prep run without host lengths on every device
author: hnyls2002
body:
- `ExpandPrefillCausally`'s torch path, used on devices without the Triton kernel such as XPU, derives `extend_start_loc` from the device extend lengths when the host lists are absent. The DSpark draft block has passed no host sequence lengths since #46891, so the DeepSeek-V4 draft prep asserted there. A parity case covers this input.
- The draft and target-verify metadata glue graphs, which the backend declares capturable, raise on a capture failure when `SGLANG_IS_IN_CI` is set. Outside CI they still log and fall back to eager. The generic glue (`SGLANG_ENABLE_METADATA_GLUE_GRAPH`) is unchanged.
- `DeepseekV4AttnBackend.init_forward_metadata_out_graph` no longer forces host sequence lengths for the DSpark draft and follows `needs_cpu_seq_lens`, so capture and replay pass the draft prep the same inputs.
- The DSpark draft batch drops its `nxt_kv_lens_cpu` fallback. It was unreachable, because a draft backend that needs host lengths makes the scheduler publish them, and it carried allocation lengths rather than sequence lengths.

No behavior change on CUDA or HIP outside CI, except that capturing the DeepSeek-V4 DSpark draft graph no longer copies the sequence lengths to the host.

title: [Fix] minimax-h3: Swap the fc1 halves of the Acc LoRA in build_minimax_h3_pdd_weights
author: yszhao2004
body:
## Motivation

`python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.tools.build_minimax_h3_pdd_weights` merges an Acc-8Step (PDD) LoRA from `alibaba-pai/MiniMax-H3-Acc-LoRAs` into the native MiniMax-H3 transformer. The LoRA is trained on the Diffusers SwiGLU projection (`ff.net.0.proj`), whose rows are `[value, gate]`. The native fused `mlp.fc1` is `[gate, value]`: the Diffusers checkpoint loader in `models/dits/minimax_h3.py` swaps the same halves when it loads `ff.net.0.proj`, and the tool already re-lays out `to_q` / `to_k` / `to_v` for `qkv_proj`. For fc1 it adds the delta unswapped, so in every block the gate rows receive the value delta and the value rows the gate delta. The merged Acc8 model then generates soft, blurry video.

## Modifications

- `tools/build_minimax_h3_pdd_weights.py`: `_diffusers_to_native_fc1` swaps the two halves of the fc1 delta before the merge. Every other target is unchanged.
- `test/unit/test_minimax_h3_pdd_offline.py`: `test_fc1_delta_is_merged_into_native_gate_value_rows` merges a one-block fc1 LoRA into a zero base and checks that the gate half lands on the native gate rows. It fails on the current `main` and passes with the fix; the other cases in the file pass either way.

Acc8 weights built with the current tool need to be rebuilt.

## Accuracy Tests

Weights: the FL2VA transformer merged with `MiniMax-H3-FL2VA-Acc-8Step.safetensors`, once with the current tool and once with this fix. Against the base weights plus the LoRA delta in the native layout (computed in FP32, rounded to BF16), the fixed merge matches all 258 merged tensors bit for bit. The current tool's output differs only in the 52 `mlp.fc1` tensors (5.2e9 elements, worst tensor error 12.7x the BF16 rounding of the reference). The 277 non-target tensors are identical in both.

Video: MiniMax-H3 FL2VA Acc8, t2va 768p 16:9, 15 s (362 frames), 9 sigma points, flow shift 12 / 3, seed 42, transformer attention `torch_cudnn_sdpa`, SGLang v0.5.21 (this tool is identical in v0.5.21 and `main`). The two runs of each prompt differ only in the transformer weights and their fused PDD heads. With the current tool, outlines of faces, eyes and hair are soft and smeared and flat areas look washed out; with the fix the same frames have sharp line art and detail.

| Prompt | Laplacian variance, current tool | Laplacian variance, with the fix |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 2D-animated character close-up | 190.6 | 427.1 |
| Live-action scene with a 2D-animated character | 399.1 | 631.2 |

Mean over 61 evenly spaced frames of the decoded RGB; higher is sharper.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not affected: the change runs once in the offline weight-merge tool.

title: [Fix] diffusion/ci: Keep final failure reasons at the end of shard logs
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Diffusion shards continue running standalone tests after parametrized failures, burying the failed cases and reasons under later output. Buffered parent progress messages can also appear after their child pytest output. See [the affected job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40494205576/job/122155684284).

Print a final failed-cases-and-reasons footer after all shard tests and the execution report. Read complete failure messages from the existing JUnit report, falling back to pytest output when no report is available, and omit failures recovered by retries. Flush parent stdout before starting each pytest process. Execution order, retry policy, and failure exit codes are preserved.

## Validation

Four targeted CPU runner regression tests passed with real child pytest processes; three reproduce the bug before the fix. Coverage includes later standalone output, recovered retries, complete multiline failure reasons, and buffered output ordering. Pre-commit passed.

title: [Fix] [AMD] aiter: Fix garbage decode output with unified attention at page size 1 under CUDA graph
author: jiaqiang-dot-liu
body:
## Motivation

With `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1` on a dense (non-sliding-window) model at the default page size 1, decode produces garbage output when CUDA graph is on. The first token (from prefill) is correct and every decoded token after it is wrong: with greedy sampling, `"The capital of France is"` continues as `" a ( ( ( ( ( ..."` instead of `" a city of romance, art, fashion, and cuisine. Paris is a must"`. GSM8K drops to 0.00. Nothing rejects this configuration, so it fails silently.

In `_apply_cuda_graph_metadata`, the unified-attention page table is copied into the captured `cuda_graph_page_table` only for sliding-window pools or `page_size > 1`. At page size 1 nothing is copied, so `unified_attention` reads an all-zero page table. Sliding-window models and Qwen3-VL (which gets page size 16 from its model override) are not affected. The non-CUDA-graph path builds the page table directly and is not affected either. The SHUFFLE 5D KV layout, the other decode path that reads this page table, requires a page size divisible by 8 (BF16 KV) or 16 (FP8 KV), so it never runs at page size 1. The AMD CI tests and cookbook recipes that enable unified attention all set `--page-size 16` or `64`, so page size 1 had no coverage.

## Modifications

- `aiter_backend.py`: copy the page table for every non-sliding-window configuration. `_transform_table_1_to_real` is the identity at page size 1, so the `page_size > 1` condition only skipped the copy.
- New AMD CI test `test/registered/attention/test_aiter_unified_attention_page_size_1.py`: GSM8K on `DEFAULT_MODEL_NAME_FOR_TEST` with unified attention at page size 1 (threshold 0.65).

## Accuracy Tests

MI355X (gfx950), single GPU, with and without this patch, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1 --attention-backend aiter`, CUDA graph on. GSM8K uses the same settings as the new CI test (200 questions, 5-shot, completion API, `max_tokens=512`), 3 runs each.

| Configuration | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| unified attention, page size 1 | 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.00 | 0.755 / 0.755 / 0.765 |
| unified attention, page size 16 (reference) | — | 0.765 |

A second dense model gives the same picture: Qwen3-8B scores 0.00 before and 0.95 after, the same as page size 16 (0.95).

The new CI test fails on `main` (`np.float64(0.0) not greater than or equal to 0.65`) and passes with this patch: 0.765 on MI355X, and 0.765 on MI300X (gfx942) in this PR's CI.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No change for configurations other than unified attention at page size 1, which was producing wrong output before. With the patch, page size 1 output throughput is within 2% of page size 16.

MI355X, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, `sglang.bench_serving`, random input 2048 / output 256, CUDA graph on, unified attention, patched build:

| Page size | Concurrency | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 58.79 | 4.24 | 224.5 |
| 16 | 1 | 61.89 | 4.25 | 223.4 |
| 1 | 32 | 572.97 | 7.48 | 3294.8 |
| 16 | 32 | 621.54 | 7.15 | 3342.5 |

## Reproduce

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1 python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct --attention-backend aiter --page-size 1 --port 30000

python -m sglang.test.run_eval --port 30000 --eval-name gsm8k --api completion \
  --num-examples 200 --num-threads 128 --max-tokens 512 --num-shots 5

python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 1 \
  --max-concurrency 32 --num-prompts 128 --seed 1
```
