title: [Fix] mnnvl: Match FlashInfer's arch-specific CuTe DSL AR profiles
author: leejnau
body:
## Summary

`_config_for_shape` decides whether FlashInfer's MNNVL CuTe DSL `DEFAULT_CONFIG` serves the current shape or SGLang has to supply a re-targeted single-profile config. It checked `StaticProfile.matches()` without a compute capability.

FlashInfer ships tp=4 hidden=8192 top_k=10 profiles keyed to GB300 (sm_103) and Rubin (sm_107). A profile keyed to one architecture never matches an unspecified (`None`) architecture. So on those GPUs SGLang found no match, discarded FlashInfer's measured tp=4 routes, and served the re-targeted GB300 tp=8 presets instead.

This passes the device's compute capability and uses `MNNVLCuteDSLConfig.find()`. That is the lookup the FlashInfer workspace's `resolve()` performs, so SGLang now re-targets only the shapes FlashInfer ships no profile for on this architecture. It also replaces a stale comment that said `DEFAULT_CONFIG` ships only GB300 H=8192/K=10.

`find()` and the `compute_capability` argument need FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1 or newer. Main has been on 0.7.3 since #48468. The tp=4/H8192/K10 profiles in 0.7.3 are still keyed to `(10, 3)` and `(10, 7)` only.

## Validation

All runs on 4× GB300 (dlcluster, sm_103), using `lmsysorg/sglang:dev` with `flashinfer-python` 0.7.3 and this branch overlaid.

- `test/registered/unit/layer_boundary/test_cutedsl_ar_fusion.py`: 33 passed. That includes the new `test_a_profile_shipped_for_this_arch_is_not_retargeted`, where sm_103 and sm_107 keep `DEFAULT_CONFIG` and sm_100 is re-targeted.
- On the device, `_config_for_shape(DEFAULT_CONFIG, tp_size=4, hidden_size=8192, top_k=10, compute_capability=(10, 3))` returns `DEFAULT_CONFIG`. It logs no "re-targeting" line, and `find()` returns the `(10, 3)` profile.
- Timing at 4 ranks, tp=4, H=8192, top_k=10, bf16, with RMSNorm. The method is the one in FlashInfer's `benchmarks/comm/bench_mnnvl_cutedsl_h5120.py`: 20 calls per CUDA graph, the median of 30 replays, and the max across ranks. It compares the shipped GB300 tp=4 routes (this PR) with the re-targeted tp=8 presets (before). Ratio = before / after, so values above 1 mean this PR is faster. The run was repeated twice, and both runs agree to within about 0.1 µs.

| M | AR after (µs) | AR before (µs) | ratio | finalize after (µs) | finalize before (µs) | ratio |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 3.79 | 3.89 | 1.03 | 4.10 | 3.99 | 0.97 |
| 16 | 5.20 | 5.84 | 1.12 | 5.32 | 5.53 | 1.04 |
| 24 | 6.04 | 6.04 | 1.00 | 6.14 | 6.76 | 1.10 |
| 32 | 6.33 | 6.14 | 0.97 | 7.15 | 7.24 | 1.01 |
| 48 | 6.76 | 6.65 | 0.98 | 7.68 | 8.10 | 1.05 |
| 128 | 10.08 | 10.03 | 0.99 | 11.16 | 11.06 | 0.99 |
| 512 | 24.68 | 26.06 | 1.06 | 38.09 | 38.04 | 1.00 |
| 1024 | 43.42 | 48.61 | 1.12 | 68.04 | 67.86 | 1.00 |
| 2048 | 79.71 | 87.97 | 1.10 | 118.32 | 115.41 | 0.98 |
| 4096 | 151.33 | 164.76 | 1.09 | 211.81 | 215.65 | 1.02 |

The all-reduce is 6–12% faster for M ≥ 512, and 12% faster at M=16. Finalize is unchanged or faster for 8 ≤ M ≤ 48 and otherwise within about 2–3%. The largest regressions are about 0.19 µs at all-reduce M=32 and about 2.5% at finalize M=1 and M=2048. Those come from FlashInfer's own GB300 tp=4 route table, not from this selection logic.

- Repository pre-commit hooks.

No Rubin hardware was available, so the sm_107 path is covered only by the unit test.

title: [Fix] hicache: Restore sub-window SWA L3 hits under a mid-tree anchor
author: pengwu22
body:
## Motivation

An L3 hit shorter than one sliding window, under a mid-tree anchor, is dropped in both host-memory modes. It is the usual hit when a reader holds a prefix on device and another writer stored its continuation, e.g. a PD decode offloading its output KV.

End to end (PD with decode KV offload, hybrid SWA + Mamba model, window 512, page 128; a 512-token prompt whose decode wrote KV up to 768), the next turn's prefill reuse:

| prefill host memory | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `cache` (`write_back`) | 512 (its own prompt; the 256 stored tokens are dropped) | 768 |
| `buffer_only` | 512 (the lookup is declined) | 768 |

Every turn's logprobs match a no-cache reference (max drift 4.4e-16). Run on a fork carrying this change.

## Modifications

- **Cache mode** (Python and Rust tree cores): `SWAComponent.prepare_prefetch` stages `min(span, window)` pages at any anchor, and the SWA prefetch commit no longer drops a short window under a non-root anchor. The window head is the anchor path's own SWA; the match validator (`create_match_validator`) accepts a boundary only after a full contiguous SWA window, so a short window whose head is gone never matches.
- **Buffer mode**: remove the full-window lookup minimum (`resolve_prefetch_threshold`). A staged hold pins FULL, not SWA, so the head of a staged short window can be evicted while it waits (the concern behind #39283); admission now refetches when this pass's joint match no longer reaches the window's start.

## Accuracy Tests

No kernel or forward change.

| test | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `test_hicache_l3_prefetch_attaches_a_sub_window_suffix_under_a_device_anchor` (new) | fails | passes |
| `test_buffer_only_hit_restores_a_window_shorter_than_full` (new; root, and mid-tree with `window - 1` and `window` pages) | fails (declined) | passes |
| `test_buffer_only_sub_window_hit_refetches_when_its_window_head_is_evicted` (new) | fails without the admission check | passes |
| `test_mid_tree_sub_window_swa_prefetch_is_attached` (replaces `..._is_released`; both tree cores) and Rust `prefetch_commit_attaches_a_sub_window_hit_under_a_non_root_anchor` | encoded the drop | pass |

`test_buffer_only_swa_window_semantics` is removed: it pinned the full-window minimum. `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache/`: 1080 passed, 0 failed (main: 1065, 0). `sglang-radix-tree` lib tests: 942 passed.

Not run here: the GPU suites (`test_unified_radix_cache_kl_hybrid_bitexact.py`, incl. `TestUnifiedHybridBufferOnlyBitExact`).

Related: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46934, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46935, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46936, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46940.

title: [Fix] custom-all-reduce: Keep integer all-reduces off the custom all-reduce kernels
author: hnyls2002
body:
- Custom all-reduce v1 and v2 now return False from `should_custom_ar` for dtypes other than bf16, fp16 and fp32, the only ones their kernels reduce. v2 reads the list from `SUPPORTED_DTYPES` next to its JIT loader (`FloatTrait` in `communicator.cuh`); v1 keeps it beside `_SUPPORTED_WORLD_SIZES`. Other dtypes fall back to NCCL.
- `_dp_gather_via_all_reduce` sends integer rows to the in-place NCCL all-reduce at every TP size. It did so only up to TP 8, a stand-in for "the group fits on one node" that no longer holds on multi-node NVLink.

Since #46853, a multi-node NVLink group of 2-16 GPUs uses custom all-reduce v2 without a VMM-backed allocator. With DP attention and a TP size above 8, `_dp_gather_via_all_reduce` sends integer tensors to `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce`, which picked v2; v2 then failed to JIT-compile its kernel for the integer dtype:

```
RuntimeError: Failed to build JIT module sgl_kernel_jit_custom_all_reduce_int64_t_16_true ...
communicator.cuh(128): error: class "sglang::device::distributed::FloatTrait<int64_t>" has no member "kNegZero"
```

One case: DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram lookups at DEP16 across four GB300 nodes gather int64 hash ids this way on prefill batches.

No behavior change for floating-point all-reduces. Integer DP gathers above TP 8 take the in-place NCCL path instead of `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce`; before #46853 both ended in NCCL.

## Verification

- With the v2 dtype check alone (`107bbf81bc`), on four GB300 nodes (TP 16, DP attention 16, one NVLink domain), an Engram DP lookup benchmark that failed with the error above on main now runs to completion with custom all-reduce enabled, prefill and CUDA-graph decode, outputs bitwise equal across `all_reduce`, `reduce_scatter` and `auto`.
- Unit tests in `test/registered/unit/distributed/`, `test/registered/unit/layers/test_dp_attention.py` and `test_dp_attention_cp_replicas.py`: all pass.

## Motivation

Python's OpenAI layer accepts a `skip_special_tokens` request extension on `/v1/completions` and `/v1/chat/completions` (default `true`). The Rust frontend's `/v1/completions` handler and the typed `/v1/chat/completions` handler dropped it, so a client sending `"skip_special_tokens": false` still had special tokens stripped from the output text, although the same request on the Python server keeps them.

## Modifications

- `/v1/completions` and the typed `/v1/chat/completions` handler read `skip_special_tokens` off the request and apply it to the request's sampling params. When the field is absent the sampling default (drop them) still applies. On chat, the request value is applied before the model-specific override that keeps special tokens for reasoning parsers, so that override still wins, as on Python.
- A detokenizer unit test (`special_tokens_follow_each_requests_flag_while_streaming`) with a tiny WordLevel tokenizer fixture (`testdata/special_token_tokenizer.json`, `<eot>` special). It streams `[a] [<eot> b] [c <eot>]` (final chunk: matched stop `<eot>`) through three co-located requests on one shard: keep, skip, and keep with `no_stop_trim`, and expects `a | <eot>b | c`, `a | b | c`, and `a | <eot>b | c<eot>`. This pins per-request decoder state, special tokens kept across chunk boundaries, and matched-stop trimming with special tokens kept.

The per-request plumbing of `skip_special_tokens` from the request to the detokenizer shard (`DetokMsg::Register`, `DetokenizerBackend::new_decoder`) already exists on main; this PR adds the OpenAI request fields that feed it and the regression test.

Local checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --locked -p sglang-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --locked -p sglang-server` (includes the new test).

title: [Fix] attention: Compute extend attention KV offsets in int64
author: xiaofei-zheng
body:
## Motivation

`_fwd_kernel` and `_fwd_kernel_unified` in `extend_attention.py` load a KV slot from `kv_indices` and multiply it by the KV buffer stride in the index dtype. With int32 `kv_indices` the product wraps once `slot >= 2^31 / stride`, which is 2,097,152 tokens for 8 KV heads x 128 head dim. The kernel then faults or, when the wrapped address is mapped, silently reads the wrong KV.

The aiter backend's CUDA-graph `cuda_graph_kv_indices` is int32 and is used as-is by the legacy target-verify path (NGRAM, EAGLE with topk > 1), so a long-running aiter server whose KV pool exceeds that size eventually crashes in `_fwd_kernel`. Spec-decode `kv_indices` built in `eagle_info.py` / `ngram_info.py` are also int32. The triton backend's own buffers are int64 and are not affected.

## Modifications

- `extend_attention.py`: cast the loaded slot to int64 before the address math in `_fwd_kernel` and `_fwd_kernel_unified`. This covers the `PAGE_SIZE == 1` and paged branches and any caller dtype.
- `test_triton_attention_kernels.py`: add `test_extend_attention_int32_kv_indices_above_2g`, which runs both kernels with int32 slots above `2^31 / stride` against the same data at low slots. The slots sit just below `2^32 / stride` so a wrapped offset reads zero rows in front of the buffer rather than faulting (~8.6 GB). On main both subtests fail (max abs diff 1.09 / 1.04); with this PR they pass.

## Accuracy Tests

Only addressing changes: for slots below 2^31 / stride the int64 cast leaves every offset unchanged, so outputs are unchanged.

MI355X (gfx950), torch 2.11.0+rocm10.0.0, triton 3.8.0, aiter `285579b62`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, CUDA graphs on, `amd/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-KV` with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --speculative-algorithm NGRAM`; the KV pool is 3,503,271 tokens. Every fault below is a `Memory Fault` in `_fwd_kernel` with grid `[24576, 32, 1]`:

- main `7fe5b127e4`, GSM8K (1319 questions, `--max-tokens 4096`): faults between questions 430 and 485 in three runs, when cumulative allocated slots reach about 2.1M.
- With the KV-scale fix (#47030) applied, `bench_serving` random 512 in / 4096 out, 600 prompts, concurrency 48: faults after 265 s. The same run on the triton backend completes.
- This PR, the same `bench_serving` run on aiter: all 600 requests complete (2.46M output tokens, 1792 s) without a fault.

Unit tests: `test_triton_attention_kernels.py` and `test_gemma4_unified_swa_virtual_ids.py` pass (18 tests, with `SGLANG_IS_IN_CI_AMD=1`).

MI325X (gfx942), torch 2.11.0+rocm10.0.0, aiter `285579b62`, main `cb55d77d37` with this patch: the new test fails on main and passes here (the two gfx950-only tests skip). NVIDIA is not tested.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`extend_attention_fwd`, 32 Q heads, 8 KV heads, head dim 128, bf16 KV, MI355X, median of 7 x 50 calls:

| Shape | int32 indices, main | int32 indices, this PR |
|---|---|---|
| verify bs 48, prefix 1024, extend 12, custom mask | 333.4 us | 332.2 us |
| verify bs 8, prefix 4096, extend 8, custom mask | 207.2 us | 206.2 us |
| prefill bs 4, prefix 2048, extend 512 | 231.9 us | 232.9 us |
| prefill bs 1, prefix 8192, extend 2048 | 873.2 us | 873.0 us |

title: [Fix] [AMD] aiter: Use the layer's KV scales in the legacy target-verify attention
author: xiaofei-zheng
body:
## Motivation

With the aiter attention backend, an fp8 KV cache and calibrated KV scales (for example from the checkpoint), speculative decoding produces garbage when target verify takes the legacy path, which every non-MLA target verify (NGRAM, EAGLE) takes unless unified verify applies (topk 1 with unified attention on, i.e. an SWA pool or `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1`); this is from reading the code, and only NGRAM is measured below. On that path `AiterAttnBackend.forward_extend` calls `extend_attention_fwd` with `k_scale` and `v_scale` hard-coded to 1.0, added in #19736 to fix a missing-argument TypeError. The cache holds `K / k_scale`, so the cached prefix is read back unscaled. #46528 fixed the decode and NHD prefill reads but not this call; the triton backend passes `layer.k_scale_float` at the same place.

## Modifications

- `aiter_backend.py`: pass `layer.k_scale_float` / `layer.v_scale_float` when the cache is fp8 and the layer has scales, otherwise 1.0. The Triton kernel always multiplies the cached prefix by the scale, so a bf16 cache must keep 1.0; this is the same check `forward_extend` already makes for its other paths.
- `test_aiter_fp8_kv_scales_paths.py`: add `test_extend_attention_target_verify`, three requests with 300, 77 and 512 cached fp8 prefix tokens and 4 draft tokens each, against fp32 attention over the dequantized cache. To support it, `_FakeKVPool` gets `get_key_buffer` / `get_value_buffer`, `_make_layer` sets `k_scale_float` / `v_scale_float`, and the causal reference mask is offset so the queries are the last positions of the sequence. On main the new case fails with a relative L2 error of 322.19 (threshold 0.15); with this PR it is 0.04.

## Accuracy Tests

MI355X (gfx950), torch 2.11.0+rocm10.0.0, sglang-kernel 0.4.10, aiter `285579b62`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, CUDA graphs on. Model `amd/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-KV` (per-layer checkpoint KV scales from 0.024 to 0.075) with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`; NGRAM uses its defaults. Main is `7fe5b127e4`. Only the main run used `--max-total-tokens 2000000`; the PR and no-speculation runs used the default KV pool. GSM8K with `python -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 1319 --max-tokens 4096` (chat API, greedy, 1314 questions after the 5 few-shot examples):

| Config | Main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| aiter + NGRAM | 0.0061 | 0.8037 / 0.8067 / 0.8052 |
| aiter, no speculation | | 0.8135 / 0.8067 / 0.8181 |
| triton + NGRAM (reference) | | 0.7968 |

On main the aiter + NGRAM outputs are garbage that run to the 4096-token limit (5.4M output tokens), and with the default KV pool those long outputs hit a separate int32 offset overflow in `extend_attention_fwd` (#47029), hence the smaller pool for that run.

Unit tests: `test_aiter_fp8_kv_scales_paths.py` passes on MI355X and MI325X.

MI325X (gfx942), torch 2.11.0+rocm10.0.0, aiter `285579b62`, main `cb55d77d37` with this patch: the new case fails on main and passes here. GSM8K aiter + NGRAM with `--max-total-tokens 2000000` on both arms: main 0.0050 (200 questions), this PR 0.7998 / 0.8174; aiter without speculation 0.8288.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MI355X, same stack as above. The kernel and launch are unchanged; only the `k_scale` / `v_scale` values passed to `extend_attention_fwd` differ. Kernel time on the legacy target-verify path (Llama-3.1-8B shapes, fp8 KV, 12 draft tokens, causal), 20 calls in one CUDA graph, median of 50 replays, µs per call:

| Batch | Prefix | Scale 1.0 (main) | Layer scales (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1024 | 35.0 | 35.1 |
| 1 | 8192 | 292.2 | 292.2 |
| 8 | 1024 | 38.0 | 38.0 |
| 8 | 8192 | 289.8 | 289.9 |
| 32 | 1024 | 160.7 | 160.7 |
| 32 | 8192 | 1387.8 | 1387.7 |

End to end, aiter + NGRAM with `--max-total-tokens 2000000` on both arms, `python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 --random-range-ratio 1.0` (fixed output length). Blocks main, PR, PR, main with one server each; each block reports the median of runs 2-4:

| Concurrency | Output throughput, main → PR (tok/s) | Median TPOT, main → PR (ms) | Accept length, main → PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 177 → 1066 (PR blocks 991 / 1141) | 5.66 → 0.66 | 1.04 → 3.70 |
| 32 | 1770 → 7010 (PR blocks 7120 / 6900) | 17.90 → 2.97 | 1.04 → 4.14 |

The end-to-end gain comes from NGRAM accepting drafts again; on main the garbage outputs reject almost every draft. The two main blocks differ by 0.1% (c1) and 0.8% (c32) in throughput.

## Reproduce

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path amd/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-KV \
  --attention-backend aiter --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --speculative-algorithm NGRAM
# Main arm: add --max-total-tokens 2000000.

python -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 1319 --max-tokens 4096
```

title: [Fix] disaggregation: Agree on each prefill KV transfer's outcome across PP stages
author: whybeyoung
body:
## Motivation

With pipeline parallelism on a **PD-disaggregated prefill** server (`--disaggregation-mode prefill --pp-size N`, N > 1), the PP stages can disagree on whether a request's KV transfer succeeded. When they do, they release the request from the radix cache through different paths, and their prefix caches diverge.

Each PP stage sends the KV of **its own layers** through its own `disagg_kv_sender`. The release consensus in `event_loop_pp_disagg_prefill` (`_pp_pd_get_prefill_transferred_ids` → ring → `process_disagg_prefill_inflight_queue(rids_to_check)`) only agrees on **which** transfers have concluded: `KVPoll.Success` or `KVPoll.Failed`. Each stage then concludes the request using its own local poll:

| local poll | path | radix cache |
|---|---|---|
| `Success` | `release_kv_cache(req, tree_cache, checkpoint=True)` | release |
| `Failed` | `handle_inflight_transfer_failure(req)` | release **+** `tree_cache.finish(handle, ABORT)` (`release_aborted_request`) |

A client abort (`/abort_request` → `disagg_kv_sender.abort()` on every stage) that arrives **after the first stage has finished sending but before the later stages have** gives exactly this split. Stage 0 polls `Success`; stages 1..N-1 poll `Failed`. Both states count as "concluded", so the consensus passes, and then:

1. Stage 0 releases the request normally. Stages 1..N-1 also run `release_aborted_request`. The prefix caches are now different per stage.
2. Later requests match different prefixes on different stages, so the stages compute different extend lengths and schedule **different micro-batches**.
3. A later stage receives hidden states from the previous stage whose row count does not match its own batch. In our case this surfaced deep in the model as a shape assertion (`Size mismatch for shape#0('batch_size'): expected 32768 but got 32722` in the DSA indexer on PP stage 1). If the token counts happen to match, the stage silently computes KV from another batch's hidden states.

### How we found and reproduced it
- A PP4 prefill (2 prefill instances, 1 decode instance, Mooncake, 4×8 B300) crashed with the shape assertion above under production traffic. The traffic was long multi-turn prompts with high prefix-cache hit rates, where client cancellations and timeouts are routine.
- We enabled `SGLANG_ENABLE_RANK_CONSENSUS_CHECKER=1` and ran a stress client with 15% client-side cancellations. The client mixes long prompts across the chunked-prefill boundary, short prompts, a shared-prefix family, and bursts of 64.
- **On current main the checker fires within ~2 minutes.** For the diverging request, the later stages log `release_aborted_request(rid=...)` and stage 0 does not.
- The per-stage `ReqTimeStats` for the same request confirm the split: `transfer_total` was ~2.9 GB on stage 0 and **0 MB on stages 1–3**. In the same window, every other request was either sent by all four stages or by none.

## Modifications

- `scheduler_pp_mixin._pp_pd_get_prefill_transferred_ids` now returns `{rid: failed}` instead of a list of rids.
  - The concluded set is still the intersection over stages, as before.
  - The failure flag is OR-ed along the pipeline, so **a failure on any stage concludes the transfer as failed on every stage**.
  - The returned dict keeps the membership semantics of `rid in rids_to_check`, so the ring code that forwards it is unchanged.
- `prefill.process_disagg_prefill_inflight_queue(rids_to_check)` concludes each consensus rid with the consensus outcome rather than this stage's own poll. A stage that sent successfully but learns another stage failed takes the failure path.
  - The outcome is recorded with `rank_consensus_checker.assert_same`. This is a no-op unless `SGLANG_ENABLE_RANK_CONSENSUS_CHECKER` is set.
- Non-PP prefill (`rids_to_check is None`) and the decode side are untouched.

This change is deliberately conservative compared with a scheme where every stage follows stage 0's poll (see #45085):
- A request is released only once **every** stage has concluded its own transfer, so no stage frees pages its sender may still be writing.
- A failure on a later stage is not overridden by stage 0's success. The decode side would otherwise wait for layers it never receives.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A. There is no model-output change on the success path. On the race path above, the request is now concluded as failed on every stage (it was already failed on the later stages before this change).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No measurable cost: one extra boolean per concluded rid in the existing per-iteration consensus message.

Stress test on the same PP4 PD setup (concurrency 96 plus bursts of 64, 15% client cancellations):

| image | first rank-consensus divergence |
|---|---|
| main | ~2 min (`release_aborted_request` on stages 1–3 only) |
| main + this PR | **none** in a full 30 min run (6,839 completed, 1,224 client-cancelled, 195M input tokens; no PP-stage divergence, no restarts) |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the pre-commit hooks.
- [x] Add unit tests (`test/registered/unit/managers/test_pp_prefill_transfer_outcome.py`).
- [ ] Update documentation as needed (no user-facing change).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results (see above).

title: [Fix] disaggregation: Agree on each decode KV transfer's outcome across PP stages
author: ShangmingCai
body:
## Motivation

Decode-side counterpart of #47045.

With pipeline parallelism on a **PD-disaggregated decode** server (`--disaggregation-mode decode --pp-size N`, N > 1), each PP stage receives the KV of **its own layers** through its own `kv_receiver`. The release consensus in `event_loop_pp_disagg_decode` (`_pp_pd_get_decode_transferred_ids` -> ring -> `process_decode_transfer_queue` -> `pop_transferred(rids_to_check)`) only agrees on **which** transfers have concluded (`KVPoll.Success` or `KVPoll.Failed`). Each stage then concludes the request from its own local poll:

| local poll | what the stage does |
|---|---|
| `Success` | commits the KV, admits the request to `waiting_queue` |
| `Failed` | aborts the request, releases its KV, streams a 500 |

A prefill abort that lands after the first prefill stage finished sending (the race #47045 describes) fails only the later decode stages. Decode stage 0 polls `Success`, stages 1..N-1 poll `Failed`. Both count as "concluded", so the consensus passes, and then:

1. Stage 0 admits the request to its waiting queue; the later stages abort it. The stages now schedule **different decode batches**, which PP cannot survive.
2. On top of that, `process_decode_transfer_queue` forwards only the rids a stage **admitted** to the next stage. A rid that failed on stage k is never forwarded to stages k+1..N-1, and since stage k has already dropped it from its transfer queue it can never re-enter the ring consensus either. The later stages hold the request, its KV pages and its metadata slot forever.

## Modifications

- `scheduler_pp_mixin._pp_pd_get_decode_transferred_ids` now returns `{rid: failed}` instead of a list of rids. The concluded set is still the intersection over stages; the failure flag is OR-ed along the ring, so **a failure on any stage concludes the transfer as failed on every stage**. The dict keeps the membership semantics of `rid in rids_to_check`, so the ring code that forwards it is unchanged.
- `DecodeTransferQueue.pop_transferred_with_outcomes(rids_to_check)` concludes each consensus rid with the consensus outcome rather than this stage's own poll, and returns `{rid: failed}` for every request it concluded (admitted, failed, or released as aborted). `pop_transferred` is a thin wrapper that keeps the old return value for the non-PP loop.
- `process_decode_transfer_queue` forwards those outcomes to the next stage instead of the admitted rids only, so a failure on stage k reaches stages k+1..N-1 and they retire the request through the same failure path.
- The outcome is recorded with `rank_consensus_checker.assert_same`, a no-op unless `SGLANG_ENABLE_RANK_CONSENSUS_CHECKER` is set.
- Non-PP decode (`rids_to_check is None`) and the prefill side are untouched.

A stage whose own receiver succeeded but learns another stage failed takes the normal failure path: `failure_exception` raises `is_from_another_rank=True` (debug log only), the fully written pages are released, and stage 0 returns the transfer error to the client instead of admitting a request the other stages cannot decode.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A. There is no model-output change on the success path. On the race path the request is now failed on every stage; it was already failed on the later stages before this change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No measurable cost: one extra boolean per concluded rid in the existing per-iteration consensus message, and one dict instead of a list down the release chain.

Unit tests (`test/registered/unit/managers/test_pp_decode_transfer_outcome.py`) cover the ring OR semantics, the forced failure path on a stage whose own receiver succeeded, the outcome forwarding, and the unchanged non-PP return value. The existing decode transfer queue tests (`test_decode_queue_cleanup`, `test_deferred_decode_kv_release`, `test_disagg_idle_step_counters`) pass unchanged.

- [x] Add unit tests.
- [ ] Update documentation as needed (no user-facing change).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results (see above).

title: [Fix] kernels: Hash tensors over 8 GiB in gpu_tensor_hash
author: g0djan
body:
## Motivation

`gpu_tensor_hash` computes each tile's offset as `pid * TILE` in int32. For a tensor over 8 GiB (2**31 words), the offset wraps negative and the kernel reads before the buffer: `CUDA error: an illegal memory access`.

`/weights_checker` with `action=checksum` hashes every weight with this kernel, so it crashes the engine on any model with a tensor over 8 GiB per rank. We hit it on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP 8, where each rank's engram table slice is 12.3 GB.

## Modifications

- Compute the offset in int64. Tensors under 8 GiB hash to the same values as before.
- Add a test that hashes a tensor just over 8 GiB (it fails without the fix), and one that pins the hash of a small tensor.

## Accuracy Tests

The change affects hashing only, not model outputs. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (8×B300, TP 8, EP 8), the `/weights_checker` checksum failed before the fix. With the fix, it succeeds in 6.9 s and the engine stays healthy.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Hashing a 4 GiB tensor on a B300 takes 2.94 ms before and 2.99 ms after (about 1.7% slower). The kernel isn't on the forward path.

author: ShangmingCai
body:
## Motivation

`main` has been red since today's merges, and it fails every open PR:

- **ruff F821**: `python/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py:885` uses `MLATokenToKVPool`, which is not imported. #39728 added that line while #46990 replaced the `MLATokenToKVPool` import with `MLAKVView`. The two PRs merged minutes apart.
- **cargo deny (sgl-router)**: the new advisory [RUSTSEC-2026-0414](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0414) flags `pulldown-cmark 0.13.4`. The patched version is 0.13.5.
- **base-a-test-cpu**: `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_dcp_host_pool.py` fails with `ValueError: config namespace 'memory' not published`. #46990 added `test_storage_shard_identity_follows_mla_layout`, which calls `_generate_storage_config()`. #39728 made that path call `get_memory()` and mocked it in the tests that existed then, but not in this new one.

## Modifications

- `cache_controller.py`: `rank_replicated=isinstance(device_pool, MLAKVView)`, the same check #46990 uses for `is_mla_model` in this file. `MLATokenToKVPool` subclasses `MLAKVView`, so MLA pools behave as #39728 intended.
- `sgl-router/Cargo.lock` and `rust/Cargo.lock`: `cargo update -p pulldown-cmark --precise 0.13.5`. Only the lock changes; `Cargo.toml` is untouched.
- `test_hicache_dcp_host_pool.py`: patch `cache_controller.get_memory` to return `hicache_storage_key_scheme="rank-suffix"` in that test, as the file's other tests do.

## Checks

- `ruff check --select=F401,F821,F823,UP037` and `ruff format --check` (0.15.1) pass on the file.
- `cargo deny check licenses bans sources advisories` in `sgl-router`: all ok. The same command fails on `main` with RUSTSEC-2026-0414.
- On a B200 devbox, `test_hicache_dcp_host_pool.py` passes 18/18; without the mock it fails with 4 failures and 20 errors, the same `memory not published` error as CI. `test_hicache_unified_key_scheme.py` (24) and `test_hicache_l3_object_layout.py` (25) also pass.
- `cargo check` passes for `sgl-router --all-targets` and the `rust/` workspace.

title: [Fix] diffusion: fix colored seams in single-GPU Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo VAE tiling
author: tristan-me
body:
## Motivation

Native single-GPU VAE tiling for Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo evaluates self-attention and convolutions independently within each tile, then blends overlapping outputs. Each position can attend only to that tile's keys and values, and some convolution dependencies are truncated. Native single-GPU tiling is therefore not mathematically equivalent to the untiled VAE, and can produce colored seams.

The default multi-GPU tiling path (`parallel_tiled_decode`) can also produce stitching artifacts. However, multi-GPU decoding also provides a separate `spatial_shard` path: it exchanges convolution halos at each layer and gathers the full spatial features for self-attention, preserving complete spatial dependencies and mathematical equivalence to untiled decoding. This PR therefore replaces only the single-GPU tiling algorithm, leaving the default multi-GPU tiling and `spatial_shard` algorithms unchanged.

The single-GPU text-to-image comparison below uses the same input at 3840×2144. Native tiling can produce grid-like stitching artifacts along horizontal and vertical tile boundaries, visible here as thin purple seams across the tabletop. These visible seams are absent from the untiled and patched outputs. The top row shows full-image previews; the bottom row shows matched crops at 1:1 pixel scale.

![Untiled, native-tiled and patched outputs with matched full-image views and crops](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/48aa6c17-6909-4ed2-a3ee-c1a639038a21)

## Modifications

This method is enabled only for single-GPU execution. It tiles convolutions by valid output regions before and after global attention, covering both encoding and decoding.

- Partition the pre-attention feature map into disjoint valid regions (cores). Compute each core with its required neighboring halo, then assemble the valid regions into the complete feature map.
- Attention continues to use the native `AttentionBlock`.
- Evaluate subsequent convolutions on the original core grid. Propagate each final output region backwards to derive the required input windows, retain complete halos, crop redundant edges after each stage, and stitch the valid outputs.
- Apply `clamp(-1, 1)` after assembling the valid output regions in single-GPU decoding.

## Accuracy Tests

Seven CPU regressions cover full-versus-tiled encoding and decoding at non-tile-aligned boundaries, output range, single-GPU-only dispatch and native fallback for non-residual architectures.

~~~bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_qwen_image21_attention_barrier.py
~~~

Validation uses Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo on one H20 in BF16: decoding at 1536×1536 and encoding at 1024×1024. Each case has one warmup and three formal calls, using the untiled output for the same input as the tensor-level reference.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Single H20, BF16, batch 1, PyTorch 2.14.1/CUDA 13.0, cuDNN 9.24. Component measurements use identical inputs and synchronized wall time, with one warmup and three formal calls per case. Peak GPU memory is measured with PyTorch `max_memory_allocated` and includes the resident VAE and input. Detailed settings, aggregation and individual measurements are in `validation.json` ([validation bundle](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34090707/qwen-image21-single-gpu-tiling-compact-pr-bundle.zip)).

### Encoding

All methods use the same input image. Differences are computed in FP32 across all output channels, and RMSE directly compares the encoded posterior moments with the untiled result.

| Resolution | Method | Time (s) | Peak GPU memory (GiB) | RMSE |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024×1024 | Untiled | 0.064 | 1.957 | 0.000000 |
| 1024×1024 | Native tiled | 0.201 | 0.727 | 3.533896 |
| 1024×1024 | Patched | 0.445 | 1.007 | 0.036352 |

### Decoding

All methods use the same latent. Differences are computed in FP32 across all output channels before conversion to 8-bit pixels, and RMSE directly compares the decoded output tensor with the untiled output.

| Resolution | Method | Time (s) | Peak GPU memory (GiB) | RMSE |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1536×1536 | Untiled | 0.650 | 7.607 | 0.000000 |
| 1536×1536 | Native tiled | 1.363 | 0.857 | 0.013966 |
| 1536×1536 | Patched | 1.813 | 0.813 | 0.000897 |

### Full requests

End-to-end inference uses the SGLang Python API: one H20, Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo, BF16, eight steps, guidance 1.0, quality="lossless", default VAE computation optimizations and text-encoder CPU offload.

The text-to-image case produces a 3840×2144 image. The image-to-image case uses three references: the output image and each preprocessed VAE input are 1536×1536, while all three original references are 1024×1024. Each row has one warmup and three formal requests. Time covers the full request and PNG saving; peak memory is sampled through NVML.

Compared with native tiling, the patched end-to-end requests take slightly longer with broadly unchanged peak memory, while restoring mathematical consistency with the untiled VAE and improving output accuracy.

| Request | Method | Time (s) | Peak GPU memory (GiB) | SSIM |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 3840×2144 text-to-image | Untiled | 117.05 | 64.54 | 1.000000 |
| 3840×2144 text-to-image | Native tiled | 80.30 | 35.82 | 0.983188 |
| 3840×2144 text-to-image | Patched | 82.66 | 35.78 | 0.999533 |
| 1536×1536 three-reference editing | Untiled | 34.26 | 52.40 | 1.000000 |
| 1536×1536 three-reference editing | Native tiled | 36.71 | 50.35 | 0.720972 |
| 1536×1536 three-reference editing | Patched | 38.66 | 50.61 | 0.996173 |

title: [Fix] responses: Merge replayed tool calls into the preceding commentary message
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

When the model writes text before calling tools, `/v1/responses` returns `[reasoning, message(phase="commentary"), function_call, ...]`. Clients such as Codex replay these items as-is. The `function_call` items carry no `phase`, so `_merge_consecutive_assistant_messages` keeps them apart from the commentary message, and one generated turn is rendered as two assistant messages, the second without reasoning. The history then differs from what the model generated, which also breaks prefix-cache reuse of that turn.

## Modifications

- A tool-call-only assistant message without `phase` merges into a preceding `commentary` message.

## Tests

Replaying `[reasoning, message(commentary), function_call x2, function_call_output x2]` now yields one assistant message with `reasoning_content`, `content` and both `tool_calls`. `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_responses.py` results are unchanged versus main.

<!-- pr-states:start -->

title: [Fix] rust-server: Admit a multimodal model's generations only once its MM processor is installed
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

The Rust frontend's listeners start serving as soon as the runtime is constructed, and the multimodal (MM) pool, whose processor supplies the media admission hooks (`check_media` / `fetch_media`), is installed a moment later by the launcher. A generation request that arrives in that gap is admitted without those hooks: media the model cannot take is accepted instead of refused (and can reach the forward pass, where a missing encoder takes the scheduler down), and a URI the processor's fetcher would have handled gets a misleading 400 "unsupported URI".

The generation-free `/health` had the same gap: with `--skip-server-warmup` it answered 200 as soon as the listener came up, before the processor existed. The Python server never does that, because it builds its processor before its listener binds.

## Modifications

- `CoreHandle::prepare_generations` is the single admission path for native `/generate` (single and batch), the OpenAI routes, gRPC Generate and the startup warmup. For a multimodal model it now waits on a `tokio::sync::SetOnce` holding the processor, which `set_mm_processor` fills when the pool starts (`OnceLock` → `SetOnce`). Early clients see no new error; they get their answer once the processor is installed. The wait has no deadline: the pool starts during launch, and runtime shutdown cancels a waiting handler with the api runtime. Text models never wait.
- `CoreConfig` gains `multimodal`, set from `ServerArgs::model_is_multimodal()` in `runtime::start`.
- Every other route serves from the start. In particular the PD bootstrap registry is never blocked: holding the listeners instead would let another TP rank of a single-node TP>1 prefill run out of its registration retries while rank 0 builds its processor.
- `/health`, `/health_generate` and gRPC HealthCheck share one readiness check, `CoreHandle::is_serving`: startup warmup finished or skipped and, for a multimodal model, the processor installed. `/model_info` keeps answering 200 as soon as the listener is up.
- Test fixtures that build a `CoreConfig` set `multimodal: false`; the Python `RustServer` docstrings describe the new admission behaviour (no Python code change).

Tests:
- `multimodal_admission_waits_for_the_mm_pool` (`utils/runtime.rs`) starts PD-prefill runtimes so the registry is mounted. With a multimodal runtime whose pool has not started: `PUT /route` gets 200, `/health` gets 503, and a `/generate` is not admitted; the same request is admitted after `start_mm_workers_with_processor`. A text runtime admits at once. A multimodal runtime shut down with a request still waiting returns in under 3 s and closes its port.
- `generation_free_health_waits_for_the_mm_processor` (`http/native_api.rs`) calls the generation-free `/health` handler of a multimodal model with warmup skipped: 503 before the processor is installed, 200 after.

Notes on where the hunks sit: this was written against the pre-#46181 layout, where the admission path, the health probe and the handle lived together in `core/handle.rs`. On current main the same lines sit in `handlers/handle.rs` (config flag, `SetOnce` slot, `is_serving`), `handlers/generate.rs` (`prepare_generations`) and `handlers/health.rs` (`probe_health`), the new test fixtures carry the `peer_endpoints` (#46181) and `openai_chat` (#45449) fields every other fixture carries, and every `CoreConfig` construction site on main sets `multimodal: false`.

Validation run locally in `rust/`: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --locked -p sglang-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked -p sglang-server`.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no change to model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: the only new work on the request path is a `SetOnce::wait` that returns immediately once the processor is installed, and text models skip it.

title: [Fix] rust-server: Answer media the multimodal processor refuses with a 400
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

When a client sends an image the multimodal processor refuses (a PNG whose IDAT checksum is wrong, a JPEG truncated mid-scan, a format the decoder does not support), the Python server raises `ValueError` from its processor and `http_server` answers 400 with the processor's message. The Rust server mapped every `Error::Encode` to `CoreError::Internal`, so the same request answered 500 with `encode failed: <message>`. A 500 for bad client input reads as a server fault to routers and alerting, and a disaggregated pair whose prefill and decode run different frontends answers the same request with different status classes.

## Modifications

- `MmProcessor::process` returns `Result<MmProcessOutput, MediaError>` instead of `Result<_, String>`, the type the `fetch_media` hook already uses. `Client` is what Python's processor raises as `ValueError` (refused media, a placeholder matching no item); `Server` is `RuntimeError` and any other exception. `QwenMmProcessor` maps the driver's failure to `Client` and a failed output encode to `Server`.
- `Error::Encode` carries the `MediaError`. Admission (`prepare_generations`) and the MM worker's failure (`translate_runtime_error`) both map it through one `From<MediaError> for CoreError`: `Client` is a 400, or an SSE error event with code 400 on a stream, with the processor's own message and no `encode failed: ` prefix; `Server` stays a 500. Only `Encode(Server)` counts as a server fault.
- The worker's own faults stay 500s: a malformed processor result, a failed `finalize` or a feature buffer that cannot be placed fail as `Error::Internal`.
- `payload.rs` classifies its errors: a malformed data URL, bare base64 or a blown byte budget is `Client`; a prefetch that disagrees with the walk is `Server`.
- Test processors return `MediaError`; `worker_returns_request_with_fsm_advanced` covers refused, failing and malformed processors, and a new runtime test `refused_media_is_a_bad_request` drives `/generate` unary and streaming through a refusing and a failing processor and checks the status, the code and the message.

Files: `rust/sglang-server/src/api_server/core/{error,prefetch}.rs`, `api_server/handlers/{generate,handle}.rs`, `multi_modality/{payload,worker}.rs`, `tokenizer_manager/to_scheduler_tests.rs`, `utils/{error,runtime}.rs`.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no model forward or kernel code changes. Unit coverage in `cargo test --locked -p sglang-server` on this branch (413 tests pass; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --locked -p sglang-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean):

- `runtime::tests::refused_media_is_a_bad_request`: through a running runtime, a processor returning `MediaError::Client("image decode failed: CRC error")` answers `/generate` with 400 and `{"message":"image decode failed: CRC error","code":400}`, and on a stream a 200 whose error event carries code 400; `MediaError::Server(...)` answers 500 / code 500.
- `worker::tests::worker_returns_request_with_fsm_advanced`: a refusing processor fails the request as `Encode(Client)` (not a server fault); a failing processor and a malformed result fail it as a server fault.
- `payload::tests::*` assert the class of each error: unsupported modality, no image sources and byte-budget overruns are `Client`; a missing prefetch entry is `Server`.
- `to_scheduler_tests::mm_failure_rejects_returned_request` keeps covering the rejection path with an `Encode(Client)` error.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: an enum variant in place of a `String` on the error path only.

title: [Fix] rust-server: Fix the metrics flush race and the default-priority label
author: metamergebot
body:
Stacked on #47108: this branch is based on `oss-sync-3af1aca65b`, and the new test's `CoreConfig` fixture uses the `multimodal` field that pull request adds. Only the last commit is this change.

## Motivation

Two small bugs in the Rust frontend's request metrics.

1. **Flush race.** `FrontendMetrics::flush()` snapshotted every counter and histogram family before taking the `written` lock. A `/metrics` scrape flushes too, so it could race the periodic flusher: the flush holding the older snapshot could take the lock second and write it over the newer multiprocess file, and a scrape would then see counters go down as if they had reset.
2. **Default-priority label.** `CoreHandle` picked a request's metrics label series before scheduler intake applied `--default-priority-value`. With `--enable-priority-scheduling`, a request that sent no priority was scheduled at the default but counted under `priority=""`, while an explicit request at the same priority was counted under `priority="<n>"`. The Python frontend does not have this split: `_set_default_priority` runs at the top of `generate_request`, before `collect_metrics` reads the priority.

## Modifications

- `core/metrics.rs`: `flush()` takes the `written` lock before the snapshot and holds it through the write, so two concurrent flushes cannot write an older snapshot over a newer one.
- `handlers/handle.rs`: `CoreMetadata` carries `default_priority` from `ServerArgs::default_priority_value`.
- `handlers/generate.rs`: `CoreHandle` applies it to a request with no priority in `generate`, `generate_internal` and `generate_batch`, i.e. for single, internal and batch generations, before the metrics series is picked.
- `tokenizer_manager/to_scheduler_validation.rs`, `to_scheduler_types.rs`, `to_scheduler_tests.rs`: the intake-side copy of the default is removed, with its `Limits::default_priority` field and the `unset_priority_takes_the_default` test. Every generation reaches intake through `CoreHandle`, so the priority the scheduler sees is unchanged.
- New test `unset_priority_takes_the_default_before_metrics` in `handlers/generate.rs`: sends a generation without a priority through `CoreHandle` with metrics on and a default of 5, and checks both the priority handed to intake and the `priority="5"` label on `sglang:num_requests_total`. It fails without the fix.

Out of scope: there is no test for the flush race itself. Making it deterministic would need hooks inside `flush()`, and a sleep-based test would be flaky.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no model forward or kernel code changes; generated tokens are unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run. The change moves one lock acquisition earlier in `flush()` and adds one `Option<i64>` check per request.

## Testing

- `rust/`: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes; `cargo clippy --locked -p sglang-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean; `cargo test --locked -p sglang-server` passes (414 tests, including the new one).
- No Python changes.

title: [Fix] rust_server: Record startup-time metrics in Rust mode
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

With `--enable-metrics`, the `TokenizerManager` records `sglang:startup_time_seconds` (per phase: `load_weight`, `kv_cache_allocation`, `scheduler_e2e`, `tokenizer_e2e`) and `sglang:startup_cuda_graph_time_seconds` (per capture phase) once the schedulers report their startup phases, and the engine logs the "Engine startup timings" line from the same values. Rust mode has no `TokenizerManager`, so a Rust-mode server exposed neither family on `/metrics` and never logged the timings. Everything else the frontend serves on `/metrics` comes from the scheduler processes' multiprocess files or from the frontend's own request metrics; the startup phases reach only the main process.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py`: in Rust mode, the main process records the startup-time metrics itself once `scheduler_init_result.wait_for_ready()` returns, through a new `_rust_server_startup_time_sink()`. The sink is a no-op without `--enable-metrics`; otherwise it builds the tokenizer collector class `resolve_collector_class(STAT_LOGGER_ROLE_TOKENIZER, ...)` picks, with `tokenizer_metric_labels()`, and returns its `emit_startup_time`. The default class is read from the `metrics_collector` module at call time, so a replacement installed after `engine` is imported (a stat logger, or a model package's own collector) still applies. The samples land in the main process's prometheus_client multiprocess file, which the Rust `/metrics` already merges.
- `Engine._set_startup_time` takes the sink callable instead of the tokenizer manager. The Python path passes `tokenizer_manager.set_startup_time` and behaves as before, including the timings log line, which Rust mode now logs too.
- `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_rust_server_dp_ports.py`: `test_rust_mode_main_process_reports_startup_time` replaces `metrics_collector.TokenizerMetricsCollector` after import, as a model package does, and checks that the sink builds that class with the base labels and forwards to `emit_startup_time`, and that it builds nothing without `--enable-metrics`.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no model forward or kernel code changes, and generation output is unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: one collector construction and a handful of gauge sets at startup, on the main process only.

## Testing

- `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_rust_server_dp_ports.py`: 44 passed on this branch.
- `pre-commit run --files` on the two changed files passes.

title: [Fix] multimodal: Preserve strong identities across VLM caches
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Multimodal cache equality must depend on actual model-facing content, not a short scalar or a caller-provided hint. The old GPU reduction admits structured collisions, composite keys lose information through `hash(tuple(...))`, and matching only part of a media placeholder can still reuse unrelated KV state.

This is a correctness-first fix across the shared VLM paths, not a model-specific opt-in or a universal speedup claim.

## Modifications

- Add shared CPU/GPU BLAKE3-256 with typed shape/dtype/container/metadata identities. GPU tensors transfer only their digests to the host.
- Preserve full identities through embedding caching, batch deduplication, sessions, EPD and native Rust sidecars. Rust output digests use full SHA-256 and bind the serving configuration at ingress.
- Namespace KV requests using ordered full media identities and `cache_salt`. Short or partial placeholder matches cannot substitute for complete identity equality.
- Stop allowing caller `mm_hashes` to override content identity, including precomputed embeddings. Keep the separate explicit `--trust-mm-content-hashes` boundary documented.
- Preserve Kimi source/config/grid protections; cover composite processors and finalized OCR metadata. Reuse full Qwen/Muse artifact fingerprints on cache hits instead of rehashing their feature tensors.
- Add common-contract, kernel, native/transport and real Qwen input regressions, plus documentation of compatibility and prefix-sharing tradeoffs.

The GPU BLAKE3 kernel is adapted from @xupinjie's #46028; author credit is preserved. Related narrower work: #44653, #46552, #46815 and #47066. This PR does not modify diffusion conditioning caches or include #37537.

## Accuracy Tests

Current conflict-resolution head `16b61eade952` normally merges pinned main `133f712a498e`. It preserves main's move of multimodal wire types into `managers/req_types.py` and relocates the complete strong-identity implementation there, without duplicate classes or an eager scheduler/identity import. Full BLAKE3 and typed-identity hashing remain unchanged from the preceding PR head.

Exact-head validation on an isolated B300 (driver 590.48.01, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0) passed:

- CPU-hidden identity/padding/cache and native Rust contracts: **114 tests + 81 subtests**, with one CUDA-only test skipped.
- GPU hash/IPC/request/abort contracts: **97 tests + 187 subtests**, no skips.
- GPU-visible identity tests plus the previously skipped cache case: **18 tests + 26 subtests**, no skips; 17 cases repeat CPU-covered tests in the GPU-visible environment.

All final phase exits were 0; changed-file pre-commit and scoped relocation checks passed. The first CPU-hidden attempt failed collection because an existing test helper indexes an empty `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`; rerunning the same source with an out-of-range GPU ordinal and an explicit zero-device assertion passed. IPC teardown emitted a producer-lifetime warning; ending GPU memory/utilization were 0 MiB/0%. This is conflict-integration validation, not a new full-model, performance, multi-node or leak-free-soak claim. Current-head targeted CI is requested separately.

Previous delivery head `48150838db03` normally merges the pinned main commit containing #47835, fixing the two unrelated diffusion fixtures from the old CI snapshot. It preserves @g0djan's #47066 diagnostic-checksum fix and leaves full BLAKE3/typed VLM identity unchanged. Isolated B200 validation on this exact head passed **244 tests + 241 subtests**, exit 0: hash/identity (28 + 197 subtests), request/abort/Rust interface contracts (103 + 44 subtests), and four diffusion fixture/cache files (113). Runtime imports and freshly built extensions used this checkout; driver 580.126.09, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130. This is merge-integration validation, not a new full-model serving or performance result.

Remote H200 validation, implementation `15884434708` (the following commit changes documentation only):

- **976 passed**, 23 skipped, 149 passing subtests: common CPU/processor/cache/session/encoder tests, including actual Python and Rust radix trees.
- **51 passed**, 133 passing subtests: GPU hash/IPC/VMM/encoder tests. One FABRIC test fails because this container returns `CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED`; POSIX fallback passes. The test is unchanged and normally runs on GB300.
- **2 passed**: native Rust encoded-sidecar tests. Native Python/Rust suite: 49 passed plus four PIL resize parity subtest failures reproduced on the pristine base; no tolerances or assertions changed.
- Real Qwen2.5-VL-3B: CPU and CUDA IPC, videos with caches enabled/disabled, raw/processor/precomputed inputs, A-B-A and concurrent isolation. Final existing input fixture: **4 passed**.
- Final native Rust HTTP and two-GPU Mooncake EPD: **23 requests passed each**, including ordered multi-image requests and identical caller hints. Earlier ZMQ EPD and global embedding store runs also passed 23 each.
- Real InternVL3.5-1B: **22 requests passed**. This is representative E2E coverage, not a claim that every VLM checkpoint was tested.
- CPU/GPU BLAKE3 reference agreement includes 15 crafted legacy collision pairs, length padding, noncontiguous inputs, streams, and a manual 8 GiB + 17 byte boundary check.

Qwen revision: `66285546d2b821cf421d4f5eb2576359d3770cd3`; InternVL revision: `2f71cf52542334823e48a46ffba0e2bc9add3446`. Environment: H200, driver 595.71.05, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8, Python 3.12.16, blake3 1.0.11, Rust 1.92. Multi-GPU EPD was same-host; cross-node and non-NVIDIA E2E remain untested. Zero observed collisions is not proof that collisions are impossible.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Matched Qwen serving: CUDA IPC, 64 MiB preprocess cache, context 8192, memory fraction 0.45, CUDA graphs off, max running 8, seed 37, one greedy output token. After three warmups: 33 changing images and 20 same-image requests. Baseline was repeated twice. Median milliseconds:

| Workload | Baseline changing | Candidate changing | Baseline same image | Candidate same image |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 224 image | 40.62-40.70 | 41.47 | 21.83-21.85 | 22.18 |
| 1024 image | 68.26-68.82 | 72.67 | 29.55-29.81 | 29.63 |
| Shared 2048-token text + 224 image | 41.07-41.14 | 42.66 | 22.44-22.74 | 22.74 |

Generated token IDs matched in these benchmark cases. Full identity checking adds work on changing-media requests. Different media deliberately no longer share their common text KV prefix; same ordered media still shares it. Long shared-prefix workloads can incur a larger prefill penalty.

Interleaved 100-sample GPU microbench, including host synchronization: 12 MiB raw BLAKE3 **0.099 ms**, typed identity **0.128 ms**, versus old GPU64 **0.100 ms** and D2H+CPU BLAKE3 **3.068 ms**. At 153 MiB, raw BLAKE3 is **0.301 ms** versus old GPU64 **0.237 ms**. This avoids feature-sized D2H, but is not uniformly faster than the old weak GPU hash. Dense hashing needs small scratch buffers; noncontiguous inputs require a contiguous copy. No saturated-throughput claim.

## Checklist

title: [Fix] mem_cache: Build an empty KVLayerRouter from empty layer maps
author: akhilg-nv
body:
[by Claude Code]

## Motivation

A KV pool's `KVLayerRouter` maps each model layer to the sub-pool view that stores its KV. `from_layer_maps` builds
it from one entry per token-KV sub-pool (name, view, layer-to-index map), and parts other than token KV, such as a
request's recurrent state, are bound to it afterwards with `bind_part`. `from_layer_maps` now defaults `owner` (the
sub-pool whose write ids are the request's token ids) to `layer_maps[0][0]`, so an empty `layer_maps` raises
`IndexError: tuple index out of range` (`router.py`, line 180) instead of building a router with no token KV.
`test_gdn_prefill_graph.py` builds its GDN backend's router exactly that way, `from_layer_maps(pool, ())` and then
`bind_part` for the state, so it fails on main in `jit-kernel-unit-test-1-gpu-large`
([log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40724349833/job/122944002696), H100). This PR defaults the
owner only when there is a layer map. Routing for non-empty layer maps does not change: same owner default, same
routes. Every production caller (`HybridLinearKVPool`, `SWAKVPool`, `RoutedKVCache`) passes at least one layer map.

The two changes met on main within five minutes: #46980 made the test build its router from `()`, and #46990 then
added the owner default.

**Impact**

- **Accuracy:** none. Only `from_layer_maps` with no layer maps changes, from an `IndexError` to an empty router.
  `test_gdn_prefill_graph.py` passes with this PR and fails on main (1x B200, both as CI runs it and under pytest).
- **Performance:** none. The change is in router construction, which runs once when a pool is built.

## Modifications

**+4 / −2 runtime code (1 file; 2 of the added lines are docstring), +31 tests (1 file).** No kernel changes.

- `KVLayerRouter.from_layer_maps` (`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv/router.py`): set the default owner only when
  `layer_maps` is non-empty. The docstring now says that no layer maps build a router without token KV.
- `test_kv_layer_router_parts.py`: new CPU test `test_a_router_without_token_kv_routes_its_bound_parts`. It builds a
  router from `()`, binds a state part at indices `{2: 1, 3: 0}` (not the identity, so a route that used the layer id
  would fail), and checks that the router lists no token KV sub-pools and that layer 2 reads index 1 of the bound
  view. On main it fails with the `IndexError` above.

## Accuracy Tests

CPU (`PYTHONPATH=python pytest`): 43 passed in `test_kv_layer_router_parts.py`, `test_hicache_auto_size.py`,
`test_draft_depth_state.py`, `test_registry.py` and `test_eagle_binding.py`, the CPU tests that build routers with
`from_layer_maps`.

GPU, 1x B200 (torch 2.14.1+cu130, triton 3.8.0). The "main" column is this branch with `router.py` replaced by main's
(f1a36c4789), which makes it identical to main for everything these tests import:

| Test | This PR | Main |
|---|---|---|
| `test_gdn_prefill_graph.py`, run as CI runs it (`python3 <file>`) | OK | `IndexError` at `router.py:180` |
| `test_gdn_prefill_graph.py`, pytest | 1 passed (10 subtests) | failed, same `IndexError` |
| `test_kv_layer_router_parts.py` | 6 passed | new test fails with the `IndexError`; 5 passed |
| `test_kv_layer_router.py`, `test_resolve_swa_kv_pool.py` | 9 passed | not run |

CI runs `test_gdn_prefill_graph.py` on H100, in the jit-kernel suite. On main the failure happens while the test builds
its backend, before any kernel runs, so it does not depend on the GPU. This PR changes no kernel paths, so its CI does
not run the jit-kernel suite; the new CPU test runs in `base-a-test-cpu`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A: the change only affects how the router is built (once per pool), not any per-step code or kernel.

title: [Fix] bench: Size the one-batch KV-capacity skip by the heaviest attention-DP rank for ragged batches
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

`bench_one_batch_server` skips a `(batch_size, input_len, output_len)` point when its resident tokens would not fit the server's KV pool, so a sweep does not spend a timeout on a batch the scheduler can never admit at once. With `--input-len-list` (per-request ragged input lengths) that check sums the per-request lengths, which is the right total for a single attention group.

With attention data parallelism the total is not enough. The DP controller round-robins requests over the DP ranks, so request `i` lands on rank `i % num_dp_ranks`, and a ragged list that cycles with the rank count puts every long request on the same rank. The batch can fit the pool in aggregate while that rank's share overflows, and the surplus requests queue behind the batch instead of running with it: the point is then measured as a smaller batch plus a second wave, which is not the shape the sweep asked for.

## Modifications

- `should_skip_due_to_token_capacity` takes `num_dp_ranks` (default 1). For a ragged batch on more than one rank it also computes the heaviest rank's resident tokens under round-robin placement and skips when that rank's share, scaled to the whole pool, exceeds the threshold. Uniform batches and single-rank servers are unchanged.
- `run_benchmark_internal` passes the server's `num_dp_ranks` (already read from `/server_info`) to the check; the vLLM path sets it to 1.
- `test/registered/unit/bench/test_one_batch_ragged_capacity.py` (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`) pins the uniform total, the ragged total, the heaviest-rank bound with a two-rank round-robin example, and that uniform batches ignore `num_dp_ranks`.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: the change only decides whether a sweep point is skipped before any request is sent.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Not applicable; no serving code path changes.

title: [Fix] dsv4: Capture the replay tail thread-locally while serving
author: hnyls2002
body:
- `RowBucketGraphRunner` captures the decoder SWA replay tail the first time a bucket is used, while serving. That capture used the default `global` capture mode, so a CUDA call from any other thread during it fails with `CUDA_ERROR_STREAM_CAPTURE_UNSUPPORTED`. With the external linker on, its load and offload threads call `event.synchronize()` at any time, and the server crashed at the first replay-tail capture. Bounded replay is on by default for DeepSeek-V4.1 on CUDA, so DeepSeek-V4.1 with the linker is exposed whenever linker traffic overlaps those first captures.
- The capture now uses `thread_local` mode, as the other captures taken while serving already do (metadata glue graph, DSpark sampling, EAGLE post-verify). The capture runs on its own stream, which no other thread uses.

Tested on one GB300 node with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP2, DSpark, `--enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay` and the Mooncake linker: the server crashed at the first replay-tail capture without the change, and every launch with it served linker loads without errors.

title: [Perf] dsv4: Fix amax8_varlen and mega MoE pre-dispatch grids for 1024-thread SMs
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

Two DeepSeek-V4.1 decode kernels lose time to grid shape on GPUs whose SMs hold 1024 resident threads (CC 10.7 / sm_107), not to memory bandwidth:

- `amax8_varlen` (two-level indexer block keys) sizes `grid.y` from the logits buffer width (`max_compressed_seq_len`), but rows only hold `compressed_seq_lens` keys. At 128K context about 85% of the 512-thread CTAs exit after reading `seq_len`; at 2 CTAs/SM that is dozens of waves of empty CTAs.
- `mega_moe_pre_dispatch` launches 640-thread CTAs for hidden 5120. Two do not fit a 1024-thread SM, so the quant CTAs plus the pad CTAs run in two waves.

## Modifications

- `block_amax.cuh`: cap `grid.y` at two waves of resident CTAs (occupancy API, cached per device) and grid-stride over key chunks.
- `mega_moe_pre_dispatch.cuh`: when two one-chunk-per-thread CTAs do not fit an SM (`cudaDevAttrMaxThreadsPerMultiProcessor`), launch half the threads with two 16B chunks each (both loads issued before the quant-group reductions) and two pad slots per thread. On 2048-thread SMs the launch is unchanged.
- Both per-device host queries are cached with `init_once`. The two-chunk launch is used only when `top_k <= num_chunks / 2`, so no previously valid `top_k` is rejected.

Both kernels produce bitwise-identical outputs (all outputs compared, including pad slots and the scale swizzle).

## Accuracy Tests

On sm_107 (CC 10.7), at this PR's head (merged with main, including #46090):

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_mega_moe_pre_dispatch.py`: 6 passed. The new `test_hidden_5120_two_chunk_matches_one_chunk` quantizes the same rows with `top_k=6` (two chunks per thread on 1024-thread SMs) and `top_k=384` (one-chunk fallback) and requires identical FP8 bytes and scales, plus correct top-k copies and padding.
- Both kernels are bitwise identical to main's versions at the decode shapes below (all outputs, including pad slots).

Not yet run: an end-to-end GSM8K run. CI hardware (2048-thread SMs) takes only the one-chunk path.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

sm_107 (CC 10.7), this PR vs main's kernels, one GPU, 43 calls captured in one CUDA graph (amax: 4-6), hot = one buffer set, cold = rotated buffers, ABBA-interleaved replays, median time per call, this PR vs main:

| kernel | case | hot | cold |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| amax8_varlen | rows 198, ctx 32K | -80.6% | -75.4% |
| amax8_varlen | rows 198, ctx 128K | -68.5% | -56.8% |
| amax8_varlen | rows 342, ctx 32K | -84.6% | -78.9% |
| amax8_varlen | rows 342, ctx 128K | -63.2% | -60.3% |
| mega_moe_pre_dispatch | rows 198 | -15.3% | +1.4% |
| mega_moe_pre_dispatch | rows 342 | -27.4% | -26.9% |

These two kernels are a small share of a decode step, so no end-to-end number is claimed. #46090 edits other lines of `mega_moe_pre_dispatch.cuh`; whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase.

title: [Fix] rust-server: Let an HTTP layer start a native /generate request's timing
author: metamergebot
body:
Follows #47112 (the native `/generate` hook's request, headers and outcome), which has merged; this PR is now based on main and its diff is the two files below.

## Motivation

An `HttpLayer` (the `http_layer` a server extension passes to `Server::start`) can do part of a request's work before the `/generate` handler runs, for example resolving the request's inputs through another service. Python's `TokenizerManager` does that kind of work after its request timer (`APIServerReqTimeStats`) has started, so it counts toward Python's `e2e_latency` and first-token latency. The native `/generate` handler started `RequestTiming` only once it had normalized the body, after any such layer had finished, so the same request's `meta_info.e2e_latency` and first-token latency read shorter than Python's by however long the layer took.

Without the new extension, nothing changes.

## Modifications

- **`RequestStart(pub Instant)`**, exported from the crate root next to `HttpLayer`, is a request extension. A layer inserts it into the request's extensions when it starts work that belongs inside the request's timing.
- **`/generate`** takes `Option<Extension<RequestStart>>` and starts `RequestTiming` from it when present (`RequestTiming::starting_at`), otherwise at the same point as before. This covers single and batch requests, unary and streaming. `e2e_latency` and the first-token latency move together; the decode latency (first output to last output) does not change.

Scope: the native `/generate` HTTP handler only. The Prometheus `time_to_first_token_seconds` and `e2e_request_latency_seconds` histograms keep their own start in the core handle and are unchanged. gRPC and the OpenAI routes do not read the extension.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no model numerics change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run. The handler reads one optional request extension per request.

## Testing

- `unary_http_generate_round_trips_through_frontend_handle` now sends a request whose `RequestStart` is 5 s old and checks that the response's `meta_info.e2e_latency` is at least 5 s. Without the handler change it fails.
- `generate_hook_keys_reach_every_frame` sends every case (single/batch, unary/cumulative/incremental streaming) with a 5 s old `RequestStart` and checks that `e2e_latency` appears on exactly the terminal frames and is at least 5 s on each, that a streamed request's `e2e_latency - decode_s` still covers the layer's 5 s (the decode latency starts at the first output, after the layer), and that a unary request's `decode_s` is unchanged.
- Ran locally: `cargo fmt -p sglang-server -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p sglang-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p sglang-server --lib -- api_server::http::native_api`.

title: [Fix] [AMD] docker: Remove implicit INT8 QuickReduce default as it causes accuracy issues in 800k+ long context evals
author: functionstackx
body:
## Human

QUICK REDUCE QUANTIZATION has been reported by multiple community maintainers & folks deploying in production an signficiant  drop in quality for end-user production workloads in addition to their private & public 800k+ long context evals.  On 1 eval, community maintainers and us ran, it drops the 800k+ long context eval by over relatively 10% from 34% baseline to 30.4%.

this shouldn't be an surprise to AMD as AMD has noted the accuracy effect of this option too in vllm recipes https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blame/e38b528a540f3bf79674960cae78173e775e7fdc/models/moonshotai/Kimi-K3.yaml#L710

since this is an accuracy effecting flag, it shouldnt be set as default

## Motivation

The ROCm image currently sets `ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT8` for every workload. Remove this image-level override so deployments opt into INT8 QuickReduce explicitly.

## Modifications

Delete `ENV ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT8` from `docker/rocm.Dockerfile`. No other defaults or runtime code change.

When the variable is unset, `QuickAllReduce.init_quick_all_reduce()` defaults to `NONE` and disables QuickReduce. Users can still enable it explicitly at container launch.

## Accuracy Tests

- `git diff --check` passed.
- Verified that the diff contains only the requested ENV deletion.
- Verified that the runtime fallback remains `NONE`.
- No image build or GPU accuracy tests were run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run. Removing the implicit INT8 QuickReduce setting may affect collective performance for workloads that previously inherited it.

title: [Fix] mem_cache: Default hicache_write_back_staging on MLAView
author: em-dreyer
body:
## Motivation

`test/registered/e2e/hicache/test_hicache_unified_memory.py` (`TestUnifiedMemoryHiCacheMLA`) fails in the scheduled PR Test Base run on `76d5b3ce0` ([job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40785158774/job/123156724989)). The server never starts:

```
attach_hybrid_pool_to_unified_cache failed
  File ".../hybrid_pool_assembler.py", line 225, in build_kv_host_pool
    write_back_staging=kv_pool.hicache_write_back_staging,
AttributeError: 'MLAView' object has no attribute 'hicache_write_back_staging'
```

`build_kv_host_pool` reads `kv_pool.hicache_write_back_staging` on the MLA path. `MHAView` and the `KVCache` base class default it to `None`, but `MLAView` (added in #46990) doesn't declare it.

## Modifications
