title: [Fix] diffusion: Preserve FP32 product rounding in Anima RoPE
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation and change

On RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, the existing Anima FP32 split-half RoPE kernel fails its first-use exactness check and falls back to eager. Triton 3.8.0 emits contracted arithmetic in the FP16/BF16-output specialization even with `enable_fp_fusion=False`: the inspected original cubin contains eight `FFMA` instructions, and the captured Q/K case has 90 differing values. The guard prevents incorrect model outputs, but leaves the intended fusion unused.

Use the existing `mul_rn_f32` helper for both products before their FP32 addition and output cast. The inspected replacement cubin has no `FFMA`; the existing exactness gate passes and real Anima serving uses the fused kernel. The gate, supported shapes/dtypes, quality policy, fallback and compile behavior are unchanged. The only other change documents the operator in its existing README table.

Frozen SGLang main: `af21e2b989e482cfdce39689126562f2209d53ac`.
Final tested PR head: `883ad602418f51dc406378e1a5aa0ba8438f6b27`.
vLLM-Omni: `817d4c17feb702289a2d2b2cbacfd594c262b7a7`.

[Evidence index](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/README.md), [numerical/codegen audit](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/evidence/preflight/anima-rope-numerics2.json), [existing tests](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/evidence/block-runs/anima-rope-final-tests1/final.log).

## Final-head model measurements

One RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, SM120, 97,887 MiB, 600 W, driver 595.84. The same physical GPU0 serves every arm; GPU1 remains idle. SGLang uses PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 / Triton 3.8.0; Omni uses PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. Dependency pins and NVML samples are archived.

Anima Base v1.0, 1024×1024, 50 steps, CFG 4, CPU seed 42, empty negative prompt, maximum 512 text tokens, batch/concurrency 1. Components run BF16; initial noise and solver arithmetic retain the native FP32 contract. SGLang uses its native pipeline and cuDNN attention, lossless quality. Omni uses native single-file loading plus components, cuDNN attention, and its default **28 regionally compiled transformer blocks**, retained throughout.

Primary measurements have no profiler and no added stage synchronization. A symmetric 12-process sequence contains two processes per configuration; each prompt has one warmup plus four measured requests per process (**n=8/config/prompt**). HTTP time includes the complete PNG/base64 response transfer and excludes client PNG decoding/disk writes. Throughput is serial requests divided by their summed HTTP time. Denoise below is from separate synchronized SGLang diagnostics, n=4/config/prompt, and is not subtracted from primary HTTP latency. Omni's API generation-stage metric also includes other stages; a comparable isolated denoise value was not collected.

| Configuration | Prompt | E2E p50 / p95 (s) | req/s | Peak GiB | Synchronized denoise (s) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| omni | short | 5.7682 / 5.7721 | 0.17342 | 11.494 | not collected |
| omni | long | 5.7998 / 5.8044 | 0.17248 | 11.494 | not collected |
| main_eager | short | 7.0910 / 7.1061 | 0.14097 | 7.576 | 6.8552 |
| main_eager | long | 7.0905 / 7.0949 | 0.14108 | 7.576 | 6.8496 |
| final_eager | short | 6.1622 / 6.1710 | 0.16225 | 7.531 | 5.9337 |
| final_eager | long | 6.1618 / 6.1659 | 0.16230 | 7.531 | 5.9304 |
| main_bcg | short | 7.0884 / 7.1109 | 0.14100 | 8.812 | 6.8205 |
| main_bcg | long | 7.0907 / 7.1012 | 0.14105 | 8.812 | 6.8154 |
| final_bcg | short | 6.1884 / 6.1985 | 0.16156 | 8.718 | 5.9190 |
| final_bcg | long | 6.1908 / 6.1973 | 0.16152 | 8.718 | 5.9198 |

Paired process-median comparisons, short / long prompt:

- **Main → PR eager:** latency **−13.10% / −13.08%**; all process pairs improve.
- **Main → PR BCG:** latency **−12.73% / −12.70%**; all process pairs improve.
- **Omni remains faster:** PR eager is **6.88% / 6.27% slower**. This PR does not establish a cross-framework win.
- **BCG has no net benefit here:** final BCG is **0.40% / 0.47% slower** than final eager and uses about **1.188 GiB** more peak memory. This is existing BCG compatibility, not new beneficial BCG coverage.

Before comparisons, native-main A/A had CV 0.037–0.058% and maximum half-run median drift 0.098%. The first V1 ABBA independently showed 13.15% / 13.09% lower latency. All samples, backend screens, negative comparisons and quality failures are retained in the [raw audit](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/evidence/preflight/anima-rope-final-compare1-audit.json); [summary](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/evidence/preflight/anima-rope-final-summary.json).

Cached launch-to-ready times were 44.03–48.04 s for PR eager, 44.03–46.04 s for PR BCG, about 46.03–46.04 s for main, and 38.02–38.03 s for Omni. These reuse existing disk/compiler caches and are **not cold-start measurements**. In a separate final-head observer run, native graph construction took 0.617 s on main and 0.587 s on PR; the complete warmup denoising call took 7.310 s / 6.402 s. These are single observed warmups, not repeated cold-start estimates.

## Profile and BCG execution

Separate synchronized profiles, representative GPU step 3:

| Configuration | GPU kernels | Sum of GPU kernel times (ms) | Fused paired RoPE calls |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| main eager | 3326 | 135.694 | 0 |
| PR eager | 2486 | 117.836 | 56 |
| main BCG | 3330 | 134.300 | 0 |
| PR BCG | 2490 | 116.026 | 56 |

These diagnostic sums are not primary serving latency. [Final profile audit and trace paths](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/evidence/profiles/anima-rope-final-profile-audit.json).

Final-head BCG checks switch short → long → Chinese → repeated short, then lossless → exact → high → lossless at the same shape. Each arm has one actual warmup capture with 57 segments, **17 serving requests, 900 model-level replays, and zero serving capture calls**. Exact/high use the native uncaptured path; returning to lossless reuses the existing graph. All 17 images per arm match the corresponding native-main PNG exactly. The lossless profile contains 456 `cudaGraphLaunch` events across its four captured GPU-step annotations; the fused RoPE is present inside PR execution. The counter observer adds no tensor reads or CUDA synchronizations and is excluded from primary timing. [Lifecycle audit](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/evidence/preflight/anima-final-bcg-audit2-audit.json).

## Correctness and actual generated images

The original single-file DiT is pinned to `circlestone-labs/Anima@f973fc41ec7545364ac9776c2440285f43ff2a30`; components are `circlestone-labs/Anima-Base-v1.0-Diffusers@073c3a9db359c31ad0e8aa268d15775473c2176c`. All downloaded files have verified hashes; the native converter establishes exact equality for all **685 DiT/conditioner tensors**. Both frameworks receive equal Qwen/T5 token IDs and masks, initial noise, timesteps and sigmas. Their native BF16 text-encoder/conditioner results have small numerical differences; these are audited rather than silently replaced.

Main versus final PR: byte-identical PNGs for short, long, Chinese and repeated short in eager/BCG and the tested quality transitions. Cross-framework admission was fixed at SSIM ≥0.95 and PSNR ≥28 dB:

| Prompt | cuDNN SGLang / Omni SSIM | PSNR (dB) | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| short | 0.983579 | 37.1984 | pass |
| long | 0.974539 | 30.4278 | pass |
| Chinese | 0.936743 | 26.5305 | **fail; excluded from performance admission** |

The Chinese prompt asks for a teapot scene and “慢慢喝茶”; both frameworks instead generate anime café figures, with differences in hands/text. This failure is shown below and remains in the matrix. English images preserve the same composition with small reflection/cloth differences. Native torch-SDPA screens also retain their Chinese quality failure. An explicit `fa` screen resolved to torch SDPA under the existing SM120 policy; it is not evidence of a FlashAttention run.

Real main / final images, 1024×1024, seed 42, 50 steps, CFG 4, BF16, identical prompts. Rows are short, long and Chinese; labels identify the commits and the failed cross-framework row. Original image pixels are unchanged in these panels.

![Anima eager: actual main and final PR outputs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/media/eager-main-vs-pr.png?v=883ad602)

![Anima BCG: actual main and final PR outputs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/media/bcg-main-vs-pr.png?v=883ad602)

![Anima final PR and native Omni; Chinese failure retained](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/media/pr-vs-omni.png?v=883ad602)

[Image manifest and visual review](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/media/manifest.json); [effective-input audit](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/evidence/preflight/anima-runtime-input-audit1.json).

## Cleanup, tests and reproduction

Reused the existing numerical helper and existing tests; no new wrapper, flag, test copy or gate bypass. Scoped review removed experimental code from the production diff. Final executable kernel bytes equal the pre-cleanup V1 bytes; the final commit adds the necessary operator documentation.

The original cleanup comparison gave final latency +0.1365% / +0.0884%. One fixed supplementary ABBA, two warmups and eight measurements per prompt/process, gave +0.0187% / +0.0108%. Keeping all four process pairs gives **+0.0776% / +0.0496%**, n=24 per arm/prompt. All four point estimates are slightly negative for the final version; we do not call the difference zero. Descriptive 95% process-paired log-ratio t intervals are [0.99813, 1.00032] and [0.99863, 1.00038] for V1/final, including no change and satisfying the predeclared 1% noninferiority margin. Only four process pairs limits precision. Final-head gains over main remain above 12%; no further favorable-result retries were run. [Complete cleanup audit](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/evidence/preflight/anima-rope-final-cleanup-admission.json).

- Existing Anima tests (`test_rope.py`, `test_model_fast_paths.py`, `-k anima`): baseline **3 failed / 5 passed**, final **8 passed** on SM120. Seven captured/synthetic FP16/BF16 numerical cases also pass exactly.
- Scoped pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` pass. Initial harness permission/root assertions and their corrections are retained; they did not alter model code.
- [Frozen workload](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/inputs/anima-t2i-workloads.json), [launch/request/benchmark commands per process](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/evidence/block-runs/anima-rope-final-compare1-03-final_eager/metadata.json), [reproduction instructions](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/0dd23c3b1eb0e9ef7d34e78513ec173eee4d4a21/README.md).

title: [Fix] hicache: Isolate NIXL storage tests from background eviction
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

NIXL storage round-trip tests assume written files remain available until readback, but `TestNixlUnified` leaves the default L3 cleaner enabled. At >=80% filesystem usage, its background thread can legitimately evict those files, causing `test_mla_mamba_round_trip_keeps_each_tp_rank` to fail at readback with `NIXL_ERR_BACKEND` and `[False] != [True]`.

The same signature appears on [main](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40785158774/job/123156630934) and in [#46395's CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40805636899/job/123234019350). With NIXL 1.3.0, simulating 99% disk usage reproduces the Mamba failure using the real background cleaner, without forcing a cleaner tick. The original jobs did not record disk usage, so their historical pressure condition is not directly verified.

## Modifications

- Disable L3 eviction in the round-trip fixture; cleaner semantics remain covered by `test_hicache_nixl_cleaner.py`.
- Allocate a unique temporary directory per test instead of sharing a fixed path.
- Register cache cleanup (including the optional OBJ cache), and remove the directory last via LIFO `addCleanup`. Previously the primary cache was not explicitly closed and `tearDown` removed the directory before additional caches were closed.

Production storage behavior and the existing round-trip assertions are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated on Linux with NIXL 1.3.0, using CPU buffers and the real POSIX backend:
- Existing storage suite with `HiCacheL3Cleaner._disk_usage_pct` patched to return `99.0`: before the change, both Mamba round-trip subcases fail; after the change, **23 passed, 1 skipped** (MinIO unavailable).
- Deterministically scheduling a real cleaner tick after writes under the same simulated pressure: old fixture fails; fixed fixture passes both copy modes.
- `PYTHONPATH=python python3 test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_nixl_cleaner.py -v`: **9 passed**.
- `pre-commit run --files test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_nixl_storage.py`: passed.

The pressure test loads the existing test module with `runpy.run_path`, patches only the disk-usage query, and runs its three test classes with `unittest.TestLoader`. No actual disk filling is needed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: test fixture only.

title: [Fix] [NPU] dspark: Avoid double-counting verify KV lengths in graph replay
author: qybnb
body:
## Motivation

NPU full-graph replay double-counts the verify block when DSPARK supplies a live CPU KV-length mirror. `DsparkTargetVerifier.run_non_compact()` already publishes `prefix_length + verify_width` in `batch.seq_lens_cpu`, but the graph replay fallback adds `captured_req_width` again.

For example, a prefix of 1000 tokens and a verify width of 8 should pass a KV length of 1008 to FIA; replay currently passes 1016. The MLA verify path uses right-aligned causal attention (`sparse_mode=3`), so the incorrect KV length shifts the causal boundary and can expose future candidates and cache positions outside the valid sequence. This corrupts target logits and speculative verification.

The existing metadata-list shortcut only handles `is_dflash()`, so DSPARK reaches this fallback.

## Modifications

Use the live CPU mirror directly for DFlash-family algorithms, including DSPARK, since it already includes the verify block. Other speculative algorithms keep the existing width compensation, and the device-length fallback is unchanged.

This PR changes only the graph replay length calculation; it does not include DCP changes or sampling-kernel changes.

## Accuracy Tests

Previously completed local validation on the `9f6678aa3d6b` baseline, before preparing this PR:

- CPU contract checks using the actual DSpark producer and graph-consumer code: 18 checks passed, including reproduction of the old double-add, CPU int32/int64 mirrors, padded graph batches, the device fallback, and non-DFlash-family compensation.
- Kimi-K3 on 4 Ascend NPU nodes, TP64, attention DP4, DCP1, DSPARK block size 7, attention mode `decode`, full decode graph, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95: the original run scored 4/20 on a fixed GPQA subset. With only this graph-length fix, 16 of the 17 completed questions were correct before the run was stopped at the user's request. On those same 17 questions, the original run scored 4/17. Both runs retained the same sampling compatibility implementation and other settings.

The fixed run is a partial diagnostic result, not a completed 20-question evaluation or a full GPQA benchmark. No additional tests or NPU service restarts were performed when preparing this PR, and no new test files are included.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run for this correctness fix. The change does not add device operations or synchronization.

title: [Fix] kernels: Support OOT fused ops under torch.compile
author: rumitdesai
body:
## Motivation

Before this change, out-of-tree (OOT) platform plugins register eager fused-op implementations through
[`BaseFusedOp.register_oot_forward()`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/46caa54562a97e71d9b937c62875c90b39274b0d/python/sglang/kernels/fused_op.py#L375).
[`BaseFusedOp._resolve_forward_method()`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/46caa54562a97e71d9b937c62875c90b39274b0d/python/sglang/kernels/fused_op.py#L539)
selects the function for the active platform and binds it to the operator with
`registered.__get__(self)`. This works eagerly without adding a
`forward_<platform_key>` method to the operator class.


Out-of-tree platform plugins can register eager fused-op implementations without defining platform-specific methods on operator classes. However, model compilation currently has no equivalent registration API.

Eager dispatch also binds registered functions directly to the operator instance. When PyTorch saves compiler guards, it can look up a bound method by name. A registered function may have no matching class attribute, causing serialization to fail.

Provide an explicit OOT compile registration API and store plugin functions in a form that supports both eager execution and compiler guard serialization. Plugins can choose their compile implementation independently while keeping normal PyTorch tracing behavior.


## Modifications

- Add `BaseFusedOp.register_oot_compile_forward(op_cls, fn, platform_key)`.
  Selection uses the exact operator type and active OOT platform, before the
  existing subclass compile-selection method.
- Store registered functions without binding them to the instance.
  `_forward_oot()` and `_forward_oot_compile()`, defined on `BaseFusedOp`, call
  them with the operator instance as `self`. The active and saved forward
  methods can therefore be resolved by name during guard serialization.
- Preserve eager dispatch precedence, rebinding of registered Python methods,
  compile fallback behavior, explicit/forced backend priority, trace labels,

title: [Fix] multimodal: Share typed identities for Kimi prepared inputs
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

#47120 has merged. This PR now targets main with only the three-file Kimi follow-up (+125/-13): the shared Kimi helper, its regression tests, and one valid-fingerprint test fixture.

Kimi's raw-image source/config/grid identity is still needed: a strong tensor hash does not identify preprocessing configuration or permit an early source-cache lookup. This PR preserves that fast path and uses the shared typed identity for prepared inputs instead of a second model-specific implementation.

The previous fallback snapshots a feature or embedding to CPU and combines it with the processor fingerprint and grid. Equal tensors can therefore alias across input formats or different deferred preprocessing metadata. The new regressions reproduce false embedding-cache hits on the parent implementation.

## Changes

- Use the common full identity for prepared/no-source inputs, including feature versus embedding role, input format, shape/dtype, encoder metadata and processor fingerprint.
- Keep raw-image source/config/grid hashing unchanged. Do not remove K3 preprocessing-cache protections or weaken digests.
- Preserve payload/grid validation and ignore stale scalar hints when recomputing a prepared item's identity.
- Add real embedding-cache hit/miss tests, including K3 deferred normalization/backend metadata, and common-identity parity coverage.

No new flags, decoder/resize changes, or radix-cache policy changes. Safe common-prefix reuse is a separate follow-up; the parent's whole-request media namespace remains intact here.

## Validation

Current head `afd322ee6827` normally merges the already-merged #47120 (`7828f5670110`) into the child. The three remaining diff files are byte-identical to the preceding child head; no new production behavior was added by the merge.

Exact-head validation on an isolated NVIDIA B300, Python 3.12.16 / PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 / Transformers 5.19.0:

- CPU-hidden Kimi identity, K2.5, common feature identity and artifact processor files: **106 passed + 37 passing subtests**.
- GPU Kimi/common identity, BLAKE3 and CUDA IPC files: **53 passed + 167 passing subtests**.
- The unchanged regression assertions against the exact merged-main Kimi helper still produce **4 expected assertion failures** (3 methods), covering format/deferred-metadata aliasing and the unwanted CPU snapshot. This is a helper-level negative control, not a full main-server run.
- The actual K3 prepared-input parser/finalizer -> pooled IPC -> spawned consumer probe passed: full identity, feature values, offsets and zero outstanding leases. Final validation exit 0; ending GPU memory/utilization 0 MiB/0%.
- Changed-file pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed.

The first negative-control harness attempt stopped because the test retry wrapper converted assertions into generic errors; the corrected harness preserves the original assertions and canonical snapshot-spy target. Both attempts are retained. An IPC producer-lifetime warning was observed; the results above are not a leak-free-soak claim. No new full-weight Kimi serving, cross-node/EPD or performance result is claimed. Exact-head targeted CI is requested separately.


### Earlier implementation validation

Dedicated NVIDIA H200, Python 3.12.16, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130. Candidate: `e496fcf587f3c70b2b212f3cbd3b41b859f88282`; parent production: `d33ea169ef09506b161df4c5ea54897435b19fb0`.

- Parent reproduced wrong cache hits for input format and deferred normalization/backend changes, plus the unwanted CPU snapshot path. These were assertion failures, not setup failures.
- Candidate CPU-hidden: **56 passed, 37 passing subtests** across Kimi identity, common feature identity, media artifact and K3 encoder-mode suites.
- Candidate CUDA-visible Kimi identity suite: **24 passed, 12 passing subtests**.
- Actual Python/Rust radix caches at page sizes 1 and 16: **16 hit/miss checks passed**. The parent reproduced a wrong KV hit when only the prepared-input format changed; same-input reuse is retained by the candidate.
- K3's real prepared-input parser/finalizer -> pooled CUDA IPC -> spawned consumer passed: full identity, feature values, grid/offsets and zero outstanding pool leases. This probe does not load model weights.
- CPU/GPU full identity agreement at 1, 16 and 64 MiB. Raw-source fast path still makes no feature-sized D2H copy.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks passed.

Prepared-input hash microbenchmark, 5 warmups and 30 synchronized samples per size:

| GPU feature | Parent median | Candidate median | D2H payload, parent -> candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 MiB | 1.100 ms | 0.184 ms | 1 MiB -> 32 B |
| 16 MiB | 22.304 ms | 0.179 ms | 16 MiB -> 32 B |
| 64 MiB | 112.802 ms | 0.244 ms | 64 MiB -> 32 B |

This measures only the prepared-input identity step, not raw-image serving, full-weight Kimi throughput, or cross-node EPD. CPU metadata and the feature remain identical; only the computed cache identity changes as intended. GPU hashing still uses temporary scratch space and synchronization.

## Checklist

- [x] Reproduce on parent and validate candidate on isolated development hardware
- [x] Preserve semantic structure and raw-source fast path
- [x] Formatting/lint

title: [Fix] diffusion: Check cancellation at stage and sampling boundaries
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #47055. Cancellation was coupled to progress-bar updates, which are not always sampling-step boundaries: some samplers update infrequently or once per chunk. A cancellation during encoding, decoding, or after the last sampling step could also miss the opportunity to skip later work.

## Changes

- Check at executor stage boundaries on every replica rank, outside rank-selective branches. Retain the original requests even when the final stage returns `OutputBatch`.
- Move sampling checks out of `ReportingTqdm` into `PipelineStage.check_cancelled`. Preserve the existing custom-sampler integrations and check inside SANA-WM streaming chunks. Grouped sampling checks the complete request group, not only its first request.
- Check after forward, before saving or handing finalization to a background thread. Sequential execution consumes the current output before checking, so cancellation cannot shift the remaining outputs between requests.
- Keep disabled checks lightweight. Reuse existing residency cleanup, cancellation transport, and all-members-cancelled semantics. No new options or production modules.
- Document checkpoint placement for custom pipelines and the API's cancellation limits.

Existing production files: +78/-39 lines. Tests and docs: +218/-56 lines.

## Validation

- Seven targeted test files on an isolated GPU development machine: **195 passed, 2 subtests passed**.
- Includes real two-process Gloo stage-boundary tests for replicated and rank-only stages, terminal `OutputBatch`, cleanup, low-frequency progress updates, sequential output ordering, deferred finalization, and SANA-WM inner-step cancellation. Also runs existing video lifecycle, executor, MOVA, SANA-Video2 and Kandinsky6-SR tests.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks pass.

**Native GPU validation:** Wan2.1 T2V 1.3B, 2 x H200, Ulysses 2, BF16/resident weights, FA, eager, 832x480, 17 frames, 8 steps, seed 42. Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, diffusers 0.37.0, pyzmq 27.2.0. The same warm process alternated non-cancellable/cancellable requests in A-B-B-A order, eight samples per arm, with conditioning caching, progress reporting and saving enabled in both arms and stage-profiling synchronization disabled.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Saved-output E2E median, checks off / on | 0.8208 s / 0.8261 s (+0.64%) |
| Cancel a 50-step request after progress step 20 | Stops before decoding; no output saved |
| Pre-cancelled request | Does not enter the pipeline |
| Normal request after both cancellations | Completes successfully |
| 17 comparable completed MP4s | Byte-identical SHA-256 |

This measures the check toggle on this head, not branch-vs-main performance or all-model throughput. GPU validation uses a diagnostic SDK harness through the real scheduler, ZMQ and distributed workers, not an additional live HTTP E2E test. DELETE integration is covered by the lifecycle/IPC tests. The diagnostic SDK logs cancelled outputs as errors, and shutdown emits the existing CUDA IPC producer-lifetime warning; neither is claimed fixed here. The development environment uses `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1`; CI remains the supported-environment regression gate.

## Limits

This is cooperative cancellation, not kernel preemption. Rank-only stages finish before their executor checkpoint; already-running saves/uploads are not interrupted. Disaggregated and multi-node cancellation remain outside the scope inherited from #47055. A new custom sampler must use the documented checkpoint API; arbitrary inner loops are not intercepted automatically.

title: [Fix] disaggregation: Bind NIXL transfer workers to the rank's device
author: yhyang201
body:
- Start NIXL transfer worker threads through `run_on_device(gpu_id, ...)`, as #45678 does for Mooncake and Mori.
- An unbound worker's current device is 0. The DCP pack (`try_pack_dcp_src`) switches to a gather stream on the rank's device; leaving that stream context restores device 0, which creates a CUDA context there in every prefill rank.
- Revert the per-call `set_device` in `dcp_pack.py` that this PR first added: with the thread bound, it is not needed.

Only NIXL prefill workers change: their current device becomes the rank's GPU instead of 0. Mooncake and Mori are unchanged.

Verified with a model-free check that packs DCP rows from a thread while the buffer is on `cuda:1`: a thread started like the old NIXL worker leaves 612 MiB on device 0; a thread started through `run_on_device` leaves none, and the packed rows match in both.

## Motivation
Qwen3-30B-A3B with TP8/DCP2, Triton attention and BF16 KV can write DCP logical slot IDs directly into a rank-local KV buffer through fused RoPE + KV storage. This causes incorrect output and can produce CUDA illegal memory accesses as the cache allocation advances.
<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
`enable_fused_set_kv_buffer()` checks `forward_batch.dcp_kv_mask` to avoid DCP, but eager batch construction only populates that mask on HIP. CUDA batches can therefore have DCP enabled with a `None` mask.

Qwen3 MoE then selects fused RoPE storage, whose `FusedSetKVBufferArg.cache_loc` is the unchanged `out_cache_loc`, and skips the attention backend's KV store. That bypasses the Triton DCP path's owner mask and `loc // dcp_size` translation. 
- Reject the generic fused RoPE KV-store path when `get_parallel().dcp_enabled` is true. The existing attention backend performs the DCP-aware store.
- Add a regression to the existing gate test for CUDA/HIP, DCP1/2/4, and an absent batch mask. Keep DCP1 eligible for fusion.

title: [Fix] diffusion: recover LTX eager performance without disabling fusion
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Fix LTX-2.3 eager regressions without globally removing the fused head-gate or RMSNorm/modulation kernels.

Image-conditioned stage 1 splits guidance into batch-1 forwards. Video retains per-token timesteps, but audio uses per-sample AdaLN and enters RMSNorm modulation fusion. GPU-only timings do not characterize this host-bound path.

The initial version of this PR addressed launch overhead but did not establish recovery against the original good revision. Further same-machine interleaved comparisons identified redundant AdaLN layout work and a separate Blackwell stage-2 sharding regression. Companion #47301 handles shared Blackwell attention routing; this PR alone is not the complete Blackwell fix.

## Changes

- Reuse `replay_launches` for head-gate and RMSNorm modulation, caching launch metadata rather than tensors or outputs. Keep both fused kernels.
- Move head-gate eligibility/fallback inside the cached operator instead of repeating it in the model.
- Avoid the value-major allocation for singleton AdaLN rows, which are already contiguous. Preserve per-token layout where the broadcast-only fused consumers cannot apply; retain contiguous batched broadcast rows.
- Use automatic stage-2 CFG-rank Ulysses on Hopper and on Blackwell with BCG enabled. Blackwell eager does not amortize the extra dispatch; disabling it for graph mode as well would lose an existing benefit. Preserve explicit sequence parallelism and the existing token threshold.
- Extend launch-cache, fallback, fresh-input, graph, compile, AdaLN-layout and CFG/SP topology tests. Document existing image-conditioned BCG warmup and automatic stage-2 platform selection.

No new knobs, kernel arithmetic changes, quality-tier changes, GT updates, or performance-baseline changes. Existing production-file churn: +35/-12 across four files; no new production files. Tests/docs: +174/-14.

## Validation and Provenance

Original good: `02b983603d34c6af09e554ed2b8bf8d85290d9ae`. Current base: `58214f648c812c70bfd57f0b4196de494f75c0bc`.

Same task-owned H200/B300 machines and dependencies, public `Lightricks/LTX-2.3`, 768x512x121, seed 42, official two-stage schedule, CFG2, TP/SP1, `quality=lossless`, compile disabled, explicit `--ltx2-two-stage-device-mode original`; DiT resident, text/image encoder and VAE layerwise offloaded. Stage timing synchronization is enabled identically. No profiler requests are used for performance medians. Each process has one warmup followed by changing-input measured requests.

Initial measured runtime candidate: `7ad0ae895ae701894dd68fc906362a51ff9a6c54`. Final combined head `02dc569408cd24bd6fee91086c93829cd076b1ef` includes model head `698a5afb05c3e9f0738df4a59b66acc5847d4360` and attention head `115643e05b80622fc0a887dc8a8dbec570cde35e`. It preserves Blackwell stage-2 sharding in graph mode and exact-quality attention routing. Each run records its SHA; intermediate results are distinguished below.

H200, five measured requests per run:

| Workload | Original good stage 1 / stage 2 | Fixed stage 1 / stage 2 | Fixed client E2E |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TI2V eager | 8.649-8.882 / 1.416-1.420 s | 8.665 / 0.962 s | 10.950 s |
| T2V eager | Not rerun on original good | 5.368 / 0.948 s | 7.604 s |
| TI2V, matching-image BCG warmup | Not rerun on original good | 6.100 / 0.844 s | 8.322 s |
| T2V BCG | Not rerun on original good | 5.288 / 0.805 s | 7.408 s |

The last three configurations are neutral against the initial #47270 head. Ranges are independent-run medians, not confidence intervals. H200 behavior does not depend on the companion Blackwell attention patch.

B300, 9-request good/fixed/good comparison: stage 1 **9.262 / 9.039 / 9.382 s**, stage 2 **0.767 / 0.749 / 0.767 s**, client E2E **11.355 / 11.148 / 11.446 s**. The fixed run uses the combined candidate `7ad0ae895ae701894dd68fc906362a51ff9a6c54`. Earlier smaller runs varied; the interleaved comparison supports recovery, not a hardware-independent extra percentage gain. Disabling both fused paths did not recover the original performance; attention routing and stage-2 communication mattered independently.

The execution mode matters for stage 2 too: B300 T2V BCG takes approximately 0.465 s with CFG-rank sharding versus 0.671 s without it. The final patch preserves this graph-mode benefit while avoiding the roughly 0.3 s loss in eager. Final combined head `02dc569408cd24bd6fee91086c93829cd076b1ef` passed both graph configurations with five changing-input requests each:

| B300 workload | Stage 1 | Stage 2 | Client E2E |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| TI2V, matching-image BCG warmup | 3.374 s | 0.487 s | 5.073 s |
| T2V BCG | 2.742 s | 0.467 s | 4.469 s |

The same final combined head was rerun for nine eager requests: stage 1 **9.161 s**, stage 2 **0.753 s**, client E2E **11.251 s**. This remains within the matched original-good range.

Accuracy scope:

- Focused operator tests cover fresh tensors, JIT-dispatch avoidance for warmed signatures, real graphs, Inductor, and CPU/strided/broadcast fallbacks.
- AdaLN tests preserve values exactly while checking the required layouts and avoiding redundant allocation.
- H200: five final-layout videos match the preceding candidate pixel-for-pixel; those five also match the original public PR head. Audio is not universally bit-identical (final-layout comparison MSE 0 to 4.52e-7); unchanged baselines also vary. No GT was changed.
- B300: switching attention backends and stage-2 reduction topology is not bit-exact. Against the initial PR head, five matched videos have full-video PSNR 25.63-31.31 dB and audio MSE 0.000328-0.008539. These are observed differences, not a quality pass or proof of closer agreement with the official reference. Fresh-input operator tests compare captured FA4 against cuDNN with the existing BF16 tolerance; full server consistency results are reported separately.
- These isolated comparisons do not establish bitwise equivalence against every intervening optimization since original-good, nor do H200/B300 establish recovery of all historical H100 cross-runner timing differences.

An additional B300 `exact` TI2V check isolates the model patch from attention routing: model-only head `698a5afb05c3e9f0738df4a59b66acc5847d4360` produces the same decoded video SHA256 as the preceding `61bb5547b67db0aebbcba15017e5e6921a56e9c6` (`2743239da33f0fdbd15c140fa33df165a52cb3c50f5b38b193ea39bae5c21482`). An ungated companion attention candidate changed this output and failed the existing official-reference CLIP threshold; it was fixed before publication. Final combined head `02dc569408cd24bd6fee91086c93829cd076b1ef` matches all 25 video frames and decoded audio samples bit-for-bit. Existing pinned official GT (`c7258eb56e9951878c66fc0fb3673d9f4775b0b2`) passes unchanged thresholds: CLIP 0.5749, SSIM 0.3431, PSNR 12.0377, max MAD 43.2833.

Standard-server limitation: B300's `b200.json` has no LTX performance baseline, and existing official TI2V images lack a `case_map.json` entry. The direct pinned-image comparison above uses existing metrics and thresholds but does not turn the standard server test into a pass.

Pre-commit passed. H200 focused tests passed at model head `15e7a2c8d8eedd2325b3d6613b61963060d794b1`; the subsequent model change only restores the Blackwell graph-mode branch. Final combined head `02dc569408cd24bd6fee91086c93829cd076b1ef` passed the full focused suite on B300, including real CFG/SP folding and registered graph routing. Additional shared-context/CFG/LoRA/cache/model coverage: 69 passed, 4 subtests. Exact CI status is reported separately; pending CI is not treated as passed.

title: [Fix] [AMD] deepseek-v4: Respect AITER selection for Q-LoRA quantization
author: lunarwhite
body:
## Motivation

On gfx95/gfx1250, DeepSeek V4 can select fused Q/K normalization and RoPE while `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0`. When the non-e8m0 producer is selected, both Q-LoRA prepare paths call the fused quantizer, although `fused_rms_fp8_group_quant` is imported only when AITER is enabled. This raises `NameError` before attention preparation completes.

## Modifications

Gate the AITER-dependent producer on the AITER switch and reuse the existing normalization/projection fallback when it is disabled. Keep the independent e8m0 producer available and preserve the downstream Q/K normalization, RoPE and cache-store path. Add a regression test for both prepare methods and the AITER/e8m0 choices.

## Accuracy Tests

On MI355X, PyTorch 2.11.0 with ROCm, using upstream `5007cbd6a57515bf5e008ff2fd2bdb834356b53c` and the patch:

- Both real prepare methods at batch sizes 1 and 5: all four AITER-off baseline cases reproduce the exact `NameError`; all four patched cases pass normalization, Q/RoPE, KV-cache and indexer checks using real block-FP8 projections.
- AITER-on: four base/head pairs complete, with all saved outputs compared byte-for-byte by the validation runner.
- Existing e8m0 tests pass: eight producer and two consumer cases, with no skips.
- The same 12-case dispatch regression yields four expected baseline failures and no patched failures.

These are fixed-weight component tests using DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 configuration dimensions, not full-model accuracy or gfx1250 hardware results. AITER is installed; the disabled-switch cases use the existing Triton block-FP8 path.

The branch is aligned with upstream `68e57f40057175ff22a17ea0bdbe7ecbc69d9d91`; the changed model file and regression test are byte-identical to the GPU-validated versions. The local dispatch control was rerun after alignment; GPU results belong to the stated baseline.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance improvement is claimed. This fixes a failing dispatch and leaves the AITER-on producer unchanged.

title: [Fix] attention: Skip the MSA-v1 QMUL4 prefill case when QMUL4 is unavailable
author: EricKing626
body:
## Motivation

`test_minimax_m31_page_row_views.py::test_prefill_indexer_and_attention_match[True]`, added by [#46141](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46141) (`4991bd33ae`, the only commit on that file), fails on every PR that reaches `base-b-kernel-unit` on a runner whose CUDA Toolkit predates 13.4:

```
RuntimeError: Q8KV4 prefill attention with QMUL4 requires CUDA Toolkit 13.4 or newer; selected /usr/local/cuda-13.0 reports 13.0
```

The failure is in the test, not in serving. `MiniMaxSparseNvfp4AttnBackend.__init__` feeds `prefer_qmul4` for both the decode and the prefill plan from `msa_v1_qmul4_decode_capability()`, which already rejects a toolkit below 13.4, so the QMUL4 wrapper is only reached once that probe passes. The test hardcodes `prefer_qmul4=True` instead. The decode cases survive because their plans record `qmul4_fallback_reason` and drop to the FP8 path; the prefill wrapper JIT-builds on
first use and raises.

## Modifications

One file, +8 lines. `test_prefill_indexer_and_attention_match` calls `msa_v1_qmul4_decode_capability()` for the `prefer_qmul4=True` case and skips with the reason the probe returns. The `prefer_qmul4=False` case and both decode tests are untouched.

## Accuracy Tests

No model or kernel code changes, so no accuracy impact. On a runner with CUDA 13.4 or newer the probe passes and the case runs exactly as before; below that it now skips with `QMUL4 is unavailable: QMUL4 requires CUDA compiler >=13.4, got 13.0` instead of failing the suite. The file's fixture already skips everything off SM100/SM103.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

title: [Fix] TensorMatcher: keep symbol device/dtype options; use kDLGPU aliases
author: DarkSharpness
body:
> (auto generated by Claude)

## Motivation

`TensorMatcher::with_device<Codes...>(sym)` and `with_dtype<Ts...>(sym)` called `set_options` even with an empty pack, which replaced the symbol's options with an empty list (= anything allowed). The common launcher idiom `device.set_options<kDLCUDA>(); TensorMatcher(...).with_device(device).verify(x);` therefore never checked the device type, so a CPU tensor passed. About 200 of 260 `SymbolicDevice` declarations under `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/` used this idiom. The same bug affected the dtype restriction in `distributed/nvlink_comm.cuh`.

Introduced in #14570, which added the `set_options` call to the symbol overloads; before that (#13453) they left the symbol's options untouched, so every launcher written with this idiom since has had an unchecked device type.

## Modifications

- `tensor.h`: `with_device(sym)` / `with_dtype(sym)` only override options when the pack is non-empty. `set_options` now re-checks a value that is already bound, so a runtime `DLDevice` / `DLDataType` passed together with a type list (e.g. `.with_device<kDLGPU>(x.device())`) is checked too; that path was also unchecked before.
- Replace hard-coded `kDLCUDA` / `kDLCUDAHost` with `kDLGPU` / `kDLGPUHost` in JIT launchers and headers (`jit/csrc`, `jit/include`, `kda_kernels/csrc`), so the check is correct on ROCm. `moe/paged_experts.cuh` needed `using sglang::kDLGPU;` because it only imports `sglang::host`.
- Left as `kDLCUDA` because they are CUDA-only and don't include `sgl_kernel/utils.cuh`: `jit/csrc/moe/tvm_ffi_utils.h` (`cudaGetDevice` + CUDA stream helper), the vendored `ops/lora/moe/trtllm_lora_temp/data/csrc/trtllm_fused_moe_kernel_launcher.cu`, and the device-name table in `tensor.h`.
- `add-jit-kernel` skill examples updated to `kDLGPU`, plus a note that options set on a symbol stay in force.
- New `test/registered/unit/kernels/test_tensor_matcher.py`: JIT-compiles a small launcher and checks that a CPU tensor or a wrong dtype is rejected through both the symbol path and the runtime-value path. All 4 cases fail on the old header.

## Fallout

No launcher started rejecting its inputs: no test anywhere hit `not in the allowed options`, so no call site or declared option needed changing.

Note: `moe/expert_specialization/es_sm100_mxfp8_blockscaled_{group_quant,moe_group_gemm}.cuh` are not referenced by any JIT loader and already fail to compile on main (`host` is not visible there). They were only touched by the rename.

## Accuracy / tests

- All `test/registered/kernels/ops/**` and `test/registered/unit/kernels/**` on 1x B200. Every failure reproduces on main with identical counts (`paged_mqa_metadata`, `q8kv8_sparse_prefill_backend`, `tilelang_dsa_zero_rope`, `model_fast_paths`, diffusion `test_rope`, `hy4_decode_kernels`, `lanczos`, `moe_topk_softmax`, `per_token_group_quant_8bit_v2`). The rest are multi-GPU or ROCm-only tests that can't run on a single CUDA GPU.
- Multi-GPU communication tests on 4x H200: `all_reduce_residual_norm`, `deterministic_reduce_scatter`, `fp4_allgather_moe_reduction`, `tp_qknorm`, `custom_all_reduce`, `symm_mem_all_gather` pass. `ar_fusion` and `beam_all_reduce` need 8 GPUs (left to CI).
- Every changed header compiled standalone for sm_100a on this branch vs main: no new failures.
- ROCm not run locally; relying on AMD CI.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

Hand-written checks that should become matcher expressions (`RuntimeCheck(t.dim() == ...)`, stride / contiguity / alignment checks, raw dtype `.code` / `.bits`, `TVM_FFI_ICHECK`) remain in about 90 files under `jit/csrc`, e.g. `distributed/custom_all_reduce.cuh`, `gemm/fp8_blockwise/fp8_blockwise_scaled_mm_sm120.cuh`, `elementwise/fused_qknorm_rope.cuh`, `inkling/inkling_all_reduce.cuh`, `deepseek_v4/hash_topk.cuh`.

title: [Fix] diffusion: select Blackwell subtile attention by execution mode and quality
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Keep the captured-kernel improvement from #46107 without imposing FA4's host dispatch cost on eager diffusion requests.

The original B300 E2E evidence used CFG parallel **with BCG**. In LTX-2.3 TI2V eager, routing a short audio side to FA4 reduces GPU work but increases request latency. This is a mode-dependent regression, not evidence that the FA4 kernel should be removed.

## Changes

- Use cuDNN for Blackwell sub-tile attention in eager `lossless`/`high` execution, including eager breaks during BCG replay.
- Keep FA4 within BCG warmup/capture so the measured captured-path benefit remains and the kernel is compiled before capture.
- Preserve the existing FA4 route for `exact` requests and contexts without explicit request quality. The two backends have different floating-point rounding, so this optimization must not silently change the reference route.
- Carry the existing request quality explicitly through forward context in standard denoising and LTX's model-owned context. Do not attach a request object to LTX just to read quality, which would also enable unrelated request-aware LoRA paths.
- Leave the existing long-self-attention SM103 heuristic, other architectures, masks, and failure fallback unchanged.
- Cover both short-query and short-key directions, real CUDA graph capture, changed inputs on replay, and return to cuDNN in eager. The GPU test is registered in the B200 kernel suite; CPU routing tests remain in the diffusion unit suite.

No new public flags or kernel arithmetic changes. Production changes: four existing files, +26/-6; no new production files. Tests/docs: +130/-5.

## Evidence

Same two B300s, checkpoint/cache/dependencies/inputs/placement/quality/timing method. Public `Lightricks/LTX-2.3`, 768x512x121, seed 42, official two-stage schedule, CFG2, TP/SP1, `quality=lossless`, compile disabled, explicit `original` stage-switch mode, DiT resident and auxiliary components layerwise offloaded. No profiler requests are included in latency medians.

- On top of #47270's original launch-cache head `61bb5547b67db0aebbcba15017e5e6921a56e9c6`, independently restoring cuDNN for the affected shapes (`5be34c8ddc10361d6f459aae7444271f40cac30d`) reduces TI2V stage 1 from 10.95-11.01 s to 9.60 s. This isolates the attention dispatch change from the separate AdaLN/layout and stage-2 changes.
- Matched diagnostic traces: original-good vs the launch-cache-only head has GPU active time 371.21 -> 341.92 ms but GPU span 2142.97 -> 2556.79 ms. The added 576 FA4 calls consume 313.91 ms host-inclusive. Profiling overhead is substantial; these numbers explain the mechanism, not the E2E speedup.
- With the layout and stage-2 fixes from #47270, a final 9-request good/fixed/good comparison records TI2V stage 1 at 9.262 / 9.039 / 9.382 s and stage 2 at 0.767 / 0.749 / 0.767 s. The recovery comes from the combined fixes, not this attention patch alone. The original good is `02b983603d34c6af09e554ed2b8bf8d85290d9ae`; the measured combined candidate is `7ad0ae895ae701894dd68fc906362a51ff9a6c54`.
- Final combined head `02dc569408cd24bd6fee91086c93829cd076b1ef` includes model head `698a5afb05c3e9f0738df4a59b66acc5847d4360` and attention head `115643e05b80622fc0a887dc8a8dbec570cde35e`. Nine TI2V eager requests give stage 1 / stage 2 / client E2E = **9.161 / 0.753 / 11.251 s**. Five matching-image TI2V BCG requests give **3.374 / 0.487 / 5.073 s**; five T2V BCG requests give **2.742 / 0.467 / 4.469 s**, retaining the preceding graph-mode benefit.

## Validation

- Pre-commit passed, including registered-test validation.
- Final standalone attention head `115643e05b80622fc0a887dc8a8dbec570cde35e` passed registered B300 GPU routing via the CI-style `python <file> -f` entry point, unit routing and unit selection. This includes exact FA4 preservation and both short-side directions.
- Final combined head `02dc569408cd24bd6fee91086c93829cd076b1ef` passed the complete focused suite, including real CFG/SP folding and graph routing. Additional shared-context/CFG/LoRA/cache/model unit coverage: 69 passed, 4 subtests. All three final performance runs above completed successfully.
- Fresh-input FA4/cuDNN tensors pass the BF16 operator tolerance. Full B300 videos are not bit-exact after changing attention backend and stage-2 reduction topology; combined results against the initial #47270 head have PSNR 25.63-31.31 dB. This measurement alone is not a model-quality pass or an official-reference comparison.
- A full-server `exact` check caught a real precision-contract problem in the ungated candidate: pinned official TI2V CLIP 0.520 < 0.55, versus 0.575 on the preceding head. The model-only patch matched the preceding video pixel-for-pixel; attention-only reproduced the difference. The quality guard fixes this by preserving the reference route.
- Final guarded `exact` TI2V: all 25 video frames and decoded audio samples match the preceding head bit-for-bit. Video SHA256: `2743239da33f0fdbd15c140fa33df165a52cb3c50f5b38b193ea39bae5c21482`. Direct comparison to existing official images at pinned ci-data revision `c7258eb56e9951878c66fc0fb3673d9f4775b0b2` passes original thresholds: CLIP 0.5749, SSIM 0.3431, PSNR 12.0377, max MAD 43.2833.
- Standard-server limitation: B300's `perf_baselines/b200.json` has no LTX baseline, so that test fails before consistency validation. The pinned official TI2V images also lack a `case_map.json` entry; the comparison above explicitly loads the existing pinned images with existing metrics and thresholds. This does not turn the standard server suite into a pass.
- No GT or performance baseline changes. This is not a claim of bitwise equivalence between cuDNN and FA4.

CI status is reported on the exact published head; pending CI is not treated as passed.

title: [Fix] rust-server: Serve /v1/loads from every listener under multi-node DP attention
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

Under multi-node DP attention, schedulers publish their load snapshots over ZMQ to a collector on node 0, so no scheduler owns a shared-memory snapshot file. The embedded Rust server (`SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1`) serves `/v1/loads` from that file, so in this topology every listener on every node answered 503 (`load snapshots are not published to shared memory`), and a router polling the listeners read every rank as idle, both for routing and for autoscaling signals.

The node-0 collector is of no use in Rust mode either: its owner is the TokenizerManager (absent in Rust mode) or a DataParallelController that reads loads only on dispatch, which Rust listeners bypass.

## Modifications

A Rust listener runs in its rank's scheduler process and reads only that rank's slot, so it needs no node-0 collector. `should_use_zmq()` now keeps the shared-memory transport under multi-node DP attention when the Rust server is on: each rank writes its slot of a file on its own node and its own listener reads it. Each listener still reports only its own rank.

Unchanged:

- Python mode (multi-node DP attention still uses the ZMQ transport to node 0);
- single-node deployments;
- the `SGLANG_LOAD_SNAPSHOT_USE_ZMQ` override, which still forces ZMQ, so a listener answers 503 there.

No Rust change: the fix is the three-line condition in `should_use_zmq()`; the rest is the docstring and module doc that describe the transports, the comment in `rust_server/config.py` that explains which writer the listener is given, and tests.

## Testing

- `test_load_snapshot_backends.py`: `should_use_zmq` is tabled over (node count, attention-DP size, Rust mode, forced ZMQ) with six subtests; the multi-node + Rust case is the one that flips.
- `test_rust_server_dp_ports.py`: a listener test builds the server args for the two DP leaders on the last node (single-node, multi-node, forced ZMQ) and checks each listener gets its own slot of a node-local file, or no file at all under forced ZMQ.
- `pytest test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_rust_server_dp_ports.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_load_snapshot_backends.py`: 72 passed, 6 subtests passed. With the `should_use_zmq()` change reverted, exactly the two new multi-node Rust cases fail.
- pre-commit on the changed files: passed.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no change to model forward code or outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: no change on the request path; `should_use_zmq()` is evaluated once at scheduler start.

title: [Fix] rust-server: End an /abort_request-ed request on the scheduler's abort finish reason, as Python does
author: metamergebot
body:
Based on #46961, now merged: the frontend abort output repeats the request's `cached_tokens_details`, which that change introduced. This branch sits directly on `main`.

## Motivation

Python's `POST /abort_request` does not fail the request it names. `TokenizerManager.abort_request` forwards an `AbortReq` to the scheduler and leaves the request's response state in place, so the scheduler's next step ends the request with its terminal output: the partial generation produced so far, the request's token counts, and `finish_reason` `{"type": "abort", "message": "Aborted"}`. A streaming client sees a final chunk whose `finish_reason` is `abort`, then `[DONE]`; a unary `/generate` gets a 200 with the partial text.

The Rust frontend's `/abort_request` (#45888) reused the gRPC `Abort` path, which cancels the request at once and ends the client's call with a cancelled error. Clients that abort through the HTTP route therefore got an error body and no partial output where Python's server gives them a completed-with-abort response.

## Modifications

- `handlers/generate.rs`: `CoreHandle::abort` takes an `AbortEnding`. `CancelledError` keeps the gRPC `Abort` behaviour. `AbortFinishReason` is what `/abort_request` uses: a request Intake has not claimed yet is cancelled before it starts and its call finishes on a frontend abort output; an accepted request is handed to the scheduler as an `AbortSource::Request` and its call keeps waiting for the scheduler's terminal output. The cancellation a `Generation` observes is now a `Cancellation` (`Error`, `Unstarted`, `Scheduler`) rather than a unit, and is remembered once observed so preparation, submission and the response stream can all read it.
- `handlers/handle.rs`: a `RuntimeCall` records the counts and cache split of the request's latest output. When a scheduler-handed abort gets no answer, because Intake closed the sink or the scheduler stayed silent for 30 s, the call ends on a frontend abort output that repeats those counts, is marked `abort_output`, and (on the deadline) tells the runtime to drop the request as a dropped call would.
- `tokenizer_manager/to_scheduler.rs`, `wiring.rs`: `AbortSource::Request` keeps the detokenizer entry so the scheduler's terminal output still reaches the client, and queues the `AbortReq` behind the request on the request ring, so the reserved control lane cannot overtake a request the scheduler has not yet seen. On a full ring it falls back to the existing abort path. `RequestAdmission` gains `cancel_if_pending` and `is_accepted` for the two endings.
- `http/info.rs`: `/abort_request` aborts with `AbortFinishReason`. `grpc/service.rs`: the `Abort` RPC keeps `CancelledError`.
- `Cargo.toml`: tokio `test-util` as a dev-dependency, for the paused-time deadline test.
- Tests: `abort_request_ends_requests_on_the_schedulers_abort` (native stream, unary `/generate`, and `/v1/completions` stream each end on the scheduler's abort output), `scheduler_abort_without_an_answer_ends_on_a_frontend_abort_output`, `unstarted_abort_request_records_no_finished_request`, `explicit_abort_ends_the_call_before_its_sink_closes`, `request_abort_keeps_the_sink_and_queues_behind_the_request`, and both endings in `explicit_abort_wakes_a_submission_blocked_on_admission`.

## Lines that exist only to fit the `handlers/` layout

Beyond the behaviour change itself, this pull request carries 14 lines whose only purpose is to fit the `handlers/` split from #46181 (the code this change touches used to be one `core/handle.rs`). None of them changes behaviour or a test body:

1. `handlers.rs`: `pub(crate) use generate::{AbortEnding, CoreCall, recv_indexed};` re-exports `AbortEnding` from `generate.rs`.
2. `grpc/service.rs`: `AbortEnding` added to the existing `use crate::api_server::handlers::{...}` import.
3. `http/info.rs`: `AbortEnding` added to the existing `use crate::api_server::handlers::{...}` import.
4. `handlers/generate.rs`: `enum Cancellation` is `pub(super)`, because `RuntimeCall` in `handlers/handle.rs` matches on it.
5. `handlers/generate.rs`: `Generation::cancelled` keeps the `pub(super)` the split gave it while its return type changes to `Cancellation`.
6. `handlers/generate.rs`: `Generation::try_cancelled`, which replaces `is_cancelled`, keeps that function's `pub(super)`.
7. `handlers/generate.rs`: `LastOutput` added to the `use super::handle::{...}` import (rustfmt wraps it to three lines).
8. `handlers/handle.rs`: `Cancellation` added to the `use super::generate::{...}` import.
9. `handlers/handle.rs`: `use std::time::Duration;` for `SCHEDULER_ABORT_DEADLINE`.
10. `handlers/handle.rs`: `RuntimeCall.last_output` and `RuntimeCall.abort_deadline` are `pub(super)` like the struct's other fields, since `generate.rs` constructs it.
11. `handlers/handle.rs`: `struct LastOutput` is `pub(super)`, as the type of a `pub(super)` field.
12. `handlers/generate.rs` tests: imports for `CachedTokensDetails` and `ChunkExtras`, which the new tests use and which no longer live in the same file.
13. `handlers/generate.rs` test `unstarted_abort_request_records_no_finished_request`: `peer_endpoints: Vec::new()` in the `CoreConfig` literal, a field #46181 added.
14. `handlers/health.rs`: `use crate::api_server::handlers::AbortEnding::CancelledError;` for the two `abort(None, CancelledError)` asserts in the health-probe and warmup tests that now live there.

Placement only: `SCHEDULER_ABORT_DEADLINE` sits in `handlers/handle.rs` next to `RuntimeCall::recv`, its only user.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no model or numerics change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: control-plane behaviour of one endpoint.

## Test plan

- `cd rust && cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- `cd rust && cargo clippy -p sglang-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cd rust && cargo test -p sglang-server`: 434 passed, 0 failed (includes the new tests above).
- Not run: a live server. The change composes the existing core cancellation registry, `Intake::on_abort` and the response path, which the unit tests drive end to end from the HTTP routes.

title: [Fix] Spec: Fall back to eager when the ragged-verify tier exceeds the captured grid
author: Qiaolin-Yu
body:
## Motivation

#34038 moved the ragged-verify tier resolution into `DSparkVerifyPlanner._resolve_verify_tier`, which calls `round_up_grid` on the token floor. `schedule_layout` now calls that helper before its `ragged_layout_exceeds_captured_grid` check, so when the floor is above `capture_num_tokens[-1]`, `round_up_grid` raises `ValueError` and kills the scheduler instead of falling back to eager.

This happens in COMPACT ragged verify with confidence scheduling (not verify-all) whenever a decode batch is larger than the captured CUDA-graph grid, for example `--max-running-requests` > `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode`. Before #34038 the exceeds check ran first and returned `None` (eager).

```
File ".../dspark_planner.py", line 432, in schedule_layout
File ".../dspark_planner.py", line 533, in _resolve_verify_tier
File ".../ragged_verify.py", line 38, in round_up_grid
ValueError: total 255 exceeds max grid tier 32; the caller must reject this batch before selecting a graph tier
```

## Modifications

- `_resolve_verify_tier` runs `ragged_layout_exceeds_captured_grid` itself and returns `exceeds_captured_grid`. When the tier exceeds the grid, it skips `round_up_grid` and returns `graph_num_tokens=None`.
- `schedule_layout` returns `None` (eager) on `tier.exceeds_captured_grid`, so the exceeds check and the rounding share one source.
- `_budget_aligned_to_graph_tier` already returns the budget unchanged when `graph_num_tokens is None`, so with `speculative_dspark_align_verify_tokens_to_graph_tier` on, oversized batches no longer raise there either.
- Added CPU unit tests in `test_dspark_scheduler.py`: tier resolution past the grid (no hint and DP tier hint), `schedule_layout` falling back to eager, and the aligned budget staying unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Not affected: the change only turns a crash into the eager fallback that existed before #34038.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

N/A.

## Verification (1x B300)

- Unit tests, `test/registered/spec/dspark/test_dspark_scheduler.py`: this PR 20 passed; `main` planner 3 of the new tests fail with the `ValueError` above.
- End to end: Qwen/Qwen3-14B + `deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_14b_block7`, `SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=compact`, an initialized SPS table (`--speculative-dspark-sps-table-path`), `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 4 --max-running-requests 32`, 32 concurrent requests of 256 tokens.
  - `main`: the scheduler crashes with the `ValueError` above; 0/32 requests complete.
  - This PR: 32/32 requests complete (8192 tokens); decode at bs=32 runs eager (`cuda graph: False`), accept len 3.54.

title: [Fix] model_loader: Neutral UE8M0 block scales for dummy weights
author: wwl2755
body:
## Motivation

`initialize_dummy_weights` only initializes floating-point tensors. MXFP8 layers allocate their UE8M0 block scales (`weight_scale_inv`) as `torch.uint8` zeros (`fp8.py`, MoE and linear `create_weights`), so with `--load-format dummy` those scales stay 0. In UE8M0, 0 means 2^-127, so every MXFP8 weight dequantizes to roughly zero. The MXFP8 layers then produce near-zero outputs, which can propagate to NaN downstream.

## Modifications

- `initialize_dummy_weights`: fill uint8 `*weight_scale_inv` tensors with 127 (2^0), the UE8M0 counterpart of the existing neutral FP4 global scales (filled with 1.0).
- Unit test `test_ue8m0_dummy_block_scales_are_neutral` next to `test_nvfp4_dummy_scales_are_neutral`.

## Accuracy Tests

Affects only `--load-format dummy`; real checkpoints load their own scales.

title: [Fix] disaggregation: Keep output ids during a PD rebootstrap instead of popping and replaying the last one
author: hnyls2002
body:
A PD decode rebootstrap (a retracted request whose prefix KV the prefill worker recomputes, e.g. DeepSeek-V4 retraction or `pause_generation(mode="retract")`) popped the last output id before the recompute and appended it back at the transfer commit, overriding the token the prefill sampled. While it was popped, `output_ids` was one shorter than what the client had already received, so an output row emitted in that window (overlap scheduling) reported a shrunken `completion_tokens`, and the replayed id and its logprob row were then streamed to the client a second time.

The last output id now stays in `output_ids`:
- The prefill payload sends `origin_input_ids + output_ids[:-1]`, the same tokens as before; the prefill's sampled token is still ignored, so the next token is sampled on the decode side with its grammar, penalties and logprob state.
- `_pre_alloc_fill_len` is one formula, `len(origin_input_ids) + max(len(output_ids) - 1, 0)`, and every decode prealloc length uses it (admission, capacity check, KV preallocation); KV sizes are unchanged.
- At commit, a rebootstrap that already emitted output appends nothing and commits no logprob, sampling mask or reasoning count; one with no output yet takes the normal path as before.
- `pd_rebootstrap_forced_output_id`, both pops and the commit-time override are gone. `pd_rebootstrap_in_progress` and `_rebootstrap_prefill_len` are gone too: the flag only told that helper to use the fill length instead of the prompt length, and the two now agree for every request in the prealloc queue (new requests have no output, rebootstrap requests had the flag set). The only other caller is the capacity check, where an offload-retracted request now sees its fill length (prompt + output - 1) instead of its prompt length; the check's `ceiling_fits` branch already used this length, and the request's KV fit the pool before the retract, so the check gives the same result.

## Verification

- CPU unit tests covering pause/retract, prealloc priority, the transfer commit, the rebootstrap payload, and the mem-cache paths that size rebootstrap requests. A new test checks that the payload length equals the decode-side fill length for 0, 1 and 2 output ids and that `output_ids` is untouched; the commit test checks the emitted ids and their mask rows survive and the prefill's token is dropped.
- GPU coverage runs in CI: `test_disaggregation_dsv4.py`, `test_disaggregation_basic.py`, `test_prefill_complete_allocation.py`, and the PD pause/retract tests.

title: [Fix] scheduler: Retire the beam group of an aborted chunked leader
author: hnyls2002
body:
- `Scheduler.process_pending_chunked_abort` now retires the aborted request's beam group through `BeamCoordinator.retire_group`, as the waiting-queue abort already does. A beam-search leader aborted mid chunked prefill left its group counted as live, so the coordinator's per-step scans, gated on the live-group count, kept running for the rest of the server's life.
- The leader has no member rows before its prefill ends, so retiring the group is all the release it needs. `retire_group` does nothing for a request without a beam group, so other chunked aborts are unchanged.
- Add `test_aborted_chunked_beam_leader_retires_its_group` to `test_scheduler_chunked_abort_race.py`; it fails without the fix.

title: [Fix] [AMD] scripts: Run and correctly test Dockerfile-only PRs (CI filter + AITER rebuild)
author: yctseng0211
body:
## Motivation

A PR that only bumps the AITER pin in `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` currently gets no real AMD test coverage, for two reasons:

1. **The tests don't run.** `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` starts the AMD workflow, but it isn't in any of the `check-changes` filter groups. Every test job is skipped and the run still shows green.
2. **Tests that do run use the old AITER.** CI runs on a prebuilt image, which is usually a day or two old. The install script is supposed to rebuild AITER when the image's version doesn't match the Dockerfile pin, but that check never fires. For example, in run 38779037426 (2026-10-15) the pin was `2bb549102`, the image had `e7d2453f2`, and the rebuild was still skipped.

## Modifications

- `.github/workflows/pr-test-amd.yml`: add `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` to all four filter groups, so a Dockerfile change runs the tests.
- `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` (gfx942/gfx950 only; gfx1250 is unchanged):
  - Read the AITER commit from the image's version string (the part after `+g`) and compare it with the Dockerfile pin. If they match, keep the image's AITER. If not, rebuild AITER and log why.
  - The rebuild repeats the Dockerfile's AITER steps, including the three patches the Dockerfile applies. All three are still needed at the current pin.
  - Kernels are not compiled ahead of time. Doing that takes about 2 hours per GPU type, which is longer than the job timeouts. Instead, each kernel compiles the first time a test uses it.

## Testing

I ran the real script sections on an MI355 machine:
- On an image whose AITER matches the pin, the rebuild is skipped.
- On an image with an older AITER (`2bb549102` vs. pin `285579b62`), AITER is rebuilt in 94s and the installed version matches the pin. After that, an AITER op test passes; its first run, including kernel compilation, took 60s.
- The last commit only reorganizes the script: on gfx942/gfx950 it runs the same commands as the tested version, in a slightly different order, and gfx1250 runs the same commands as on `main`. I checked this by printing the commands each version runs, not on a GPU.

title: [Fix] deepseek-v4.1: Fix bounded replay with CP and DSpark
author: BJWang-ant
body: rm:https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/42170 ## Motivation Enabling `--enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay` with context parallelism (CP) and DSpark could fail during prefill output gathering. Bounded replay keeps only the required SWA tail in the late decoder layers. With DSpark auxiliary hidden-state capture, the model returns compact tail outputs instead of restoring the full prefill chunk. However, `EagerRunner._execute_extend_cp` bypassed the model's tail-aware output postprocessing and gathered these compact outputs using the original full-chunk CP metadata. The gather therefore expected more local rows than the model actually returned. For example, with a 16,384-token chunk, CP4, and a 128-token tail, each rank returns 32 tail rows, while the original metadata expects 4,096 rows: ```text Interleave CP gather received an unexpected local token count: got=32, expected_at_least=4096, total=16384, cp_size=4 ``` CP configurations previously disabled bounded replay by default, but explicitly enabling it could still reach this incompatible path. ## Modifications - Add an optional model-specific `postprocess_cp_output` hook to the eager CP runner, allowing DeepSeek V4/V4.1 to handle compact outputs before generic CP gathering. - Preserve the original global token indices in `LateLayerTail`, alongside rank-local indices. - Gather compact hidden states and DSpark auxiliary states with the tail-specific CP metadata. Restore the original forward-batch metadata in a `finally` block. - Share tail-aware output postprocessing between the regular model forward path and the eager CP path. Preserve input-token alignment, logits metadata, and the global token indices used by DSpark. - Reject explicitly enabled bounded replay with CP plus prefill CUDA graphs, which remains unsupported. This enables explicit bounded replay for eager CP prefill without changing the default CP policy or the quantization algorithms. ## Accuracy Tests Validation used the original `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` checkpoint in the `abing-v4` environment. - CPU regression suite: 38 tests passed, including 34 subtests. - Four-rank NCCL validation: six cases per rank passed, covering long chunks, cached prefixes, mixed request lengths, padding, and zero-length entries. Checks verified hidden states, auxiliary states, global token mappings, and metadata restoration. - Full-model disaggregated serving on 8 H200 GPUs: - Prefill: TP4 / CP4, interleave strategy, eager execution, bounded replay enabled. - Decode: TP4 / DP4 with DSpark. - All nine functional requests passed, including chunked prefill, prefix reuse, mixed lengths, and prompt logprobs. - Prefix reuse was observed: 49,152 cached tokens out of 65,541 prompt tokens. - GSM8K smoke evaluation: 32/32 correct, with zero errors and zero truncated outputs. The GSM8K run is a small correctness probe, not a full accuracy evaluation. ## Perf Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. Hardware: NVIDIA H200, PD serving with four GPUs for Prefill and four for Decode. Primary workload: all input 65,536, cache hit rate 50%,70%,90%, output 512 tokens. Results are means of three runs with 512 requests each and 10 warmup requests per run. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #42354690953](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42354690953) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #42354690863](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42354690863) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #42354690941](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42354690941) > [!TIP] > Base CI only covers the core cases, and its workload may not exercise your change. title: [Fix] [AMD] quark: Fix the EP>1 crash in the Quark MXFP4 W4A16 MoE path and restrict it to gfx1151
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

**What goes wrong**
Serving a Quark MXFP4 MoE checkpoint with `--ep-size` > 1 on the W4A16 path added in #41389 aborts the GPU with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION: An HSAIL operation resulted in a hardware exception. code: 0x1016`. Under expert parallelism the standard dispatcher hands each rank `topk_ids` where experts owned by other ranks are `-1`, and `_apply_triton_w4a16` feeds those ids straight into `counts.scatter_add_(...)`, which writes out of bounds.

**Where it shows up**
Every GPU that takes the W4A16 path with EP > 1. It was reported on #41389 for both gfx1151 and gfx942, and reproduced here on gfx1151. The path was also enabled on every HIP GPU that is not gfx95x or gfx1250 (so gfx942/MI300X as well), although it was written and validated for gfx1151.

**How to fix**
Send `-1` ids to an extra bucket that sorts last, is left out of the ragged expert counts, and is zeroed before the top-k reduction, and enable the path only on gfx1151.

This PR also addresses the review comments on #41389 that were still open at merge time: log once when the W4A4 checkpoint runs as W4A16, register the opt-out env var in `environ.py`, and reject SwiGLU variants the path cannot compute (`gemm1_alpha`, `gemm1_beta`, `gemm1_clamp_limit`, `swiglu_limit`, e.g. gpt-oss, DeepSeek-V4, MiniMax-M3), which previously passed the `activation == "silu"` check and produced silently wrong output.

## Modifications

All runtime changes are in `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py` and only take effect on gfx1151.

- Gate: `_use_triton_w4a16` is now `gfx1151 and SGLANG_ENABLE_QUARK_MXFP4_MOE_W4A16` instead of "HIP and not gfx95x and not gfx1250". gfx942 and other AMD GPUs go back to the AITER path.
- EP fix in `_apply_triton_w4a16`: `-1` ids are mapped to bucket `num_experts`, `counts` gets one extra slot that is dropped before `make_ragged_tensor_metadata`, and the scattered rows of non-local slots are zeroed with `masked_fill` before the sum over `top_k`. Everything stays on device, so CUDA graph capture still works.
- Env var: `SGLANG_QUARK_MXFP4_MOE_W4A16` becomes `SGLANG_ENABLE_QUARK_MXFP4_MOE_W4A16 = EnvBool(True)` in `python/sglang/srt/environ.py` (AMD section), read via `envs.....get()`. The name gains the `ENABLE_` verb required by the env-var conventions; it was only on the #41389 branch, never in a release.
- `_process_weights_triton_w4a16` raises `NotImplementedError` listing the unsupported SwiGLU parameters instead of running plain SwiGLU.
- `logger.info_once` reports that the W4A4 MXFP4 checkpoint runs as W4A16 and how to disable it.
- New `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe_w4a16.py` (stdlib `unittest`, `register_amd_ci(est_time=40, stage="stage-b", runner_config="1-gpu-small-amd")`), entering through `create_moe_runner` / `process_weights_after_loading` / `apply_weights`:
  - `test_gfx942_keeps_the_aiter_path`, `test_gfx1151_uses_the_w4a16_path`, `test_env_switch_disables_the_w4a16_path_on_gfx1151` (gate, by reloading the module with a mocked `gcnArchName`)
  - `test_ep_rank_outputs_sum_to_single_rank_output` (ep=2 outputs summed over ranks equal the ep=1 output)
  - `test_tokens_routed_only_to_other_ranks_produce_zero_output`
  - `test_clamped_swiglu_config_is_rejected`

## Accuracy Tests

Setup for all tables: 1x gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S, 96 GB VRAM carve-out), tp=1, `amd/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4`, `--attention-backend triton --context-length 8192`, image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm724-gfx1151-20260923`. Before = #41389 as merged; After = this PR.

**EP crash (kernel level).** This GPU has a single device, so EP > 1 was exercised by calling `_process_weights_triton_w4a16` / `_apply_triton_w4a16` with the `topk_ids` the dispatcher produces under EP (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B MoE shapes: 256 experts, top-k 8, hidden 2048, intermediate 512; random MXFP4 weights).

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| ep=1 | runs | runs |
| ep=2, rank 0 / rank 1 | `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION` (code 0x1016) | runs |
| ep=2 rank outputs summed vs ep=1 output, N = 1 / 7 / 16 / 128 / 512 tokens | n/a | rel. error 2.26e-3 to 2.36e-3 (bf16 rounding of each rank's output) |
| CUDA graph capture + replay with `-1` ids | n/a | bit-identical to eager |

**New unit tests** (6 tests, 3.6 s, 29 s wall including import, on gfx1151):

| Test | Before (#41389 code) | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_gfx942_keeps_the_aiter_path` | FAIL | pass |
| `test_gfx1151_uses_the_w4a16_path` | pass | pass |
| `test_env_switch_disables_the_w4a16_path_on_gfx1151` | FAIL | pass |
| `test_ep_rank_outputs_sum_to_single_rank_output` | GPU abort (`HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION`) | pass |
| `test_tokens_routed_only_to_other_ranks_produce_zero_output` | GPU abort (`HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION`) | pass |
| `test_clamped_swiglu_config_is_rejected` | FAIL (`NotImplementedError` not raised) | pass |

**GSM8K at ep=1** (regression check for the default path). sgl-eval 0.1.3, 200 questions, thinking off (`enable_thinking=false`), `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, `seed=0`, 16 concurrent requests.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K score | 63.0% | 60.0% |

The 3-point gap is sampling noise, not a numerical change: at ep=1 the MoE output of `_apply_triton_w4a16` is bit-identical before and after (`torch.equal` on N = 1 / 16 / 27 / 512 tokens, max abs diff 0), because every id is valid and the new ops are identities. The end-to-end runs differ only through temperature-1.0 sampling with nondeterministic batching (200 questions give a standard error of about 3.4 points). With thinking off the model answers with `\boxed{N}` and little or no reasoning, so this run checks before/after equivalence, not the model's best score. For reference, before with thinking on scored 82.0%, but 31% of answers were truncated by the 8192-token context.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

`sglang.bench_serving`, random dataset, input 512 / output 256 tokens, `--random-range-ratio 1.0`, `num_prompts` = 10 x concurrency, `--seed 0`, one run per row.

| Concurrency | Metric | Before | After | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Output throughput (tok/s) | 8.45 | 8.34 | -1.3% |
| 1 | Median TPOT (ms) | 117.00 | 117.98 | +0.8% |
| 1 | Median TTFT (ms) | 458.8 | 491.2 | +7.1% |
| 16 | Output throughput (tok/s) | 92.53 | 89.78 | -3.0% |
| 16 | Median TPOT (ms) | 154.05 | 156.35 | +1.5% |
| 16 | Median TTFT (ms) | 5117 | 5534 | +8.1% |

The fix adds a `torch.where`, one extra bucket, and a `masked_fill` over the scattered `num_tokens * top_k` rows to every MoE layer, and they also run at ep=1, where they are identities. The single run per row does not separate that cost from run-to-run noise.
