title: [Fix] diffusion: Build the Cosmos 3 RoPE table on GPU so CPU offload gives the same output
author: JackZeng0208
body: ## Motivation With the DiT offloaded to CPU, Cosmos3 can return a different image or video than with the DiT resident, for the same request and seed. `Cosmos3OmniTransformer.post_load_weights` builds the RoPE inv_freq table on the DiT's device, and only when the table is on meta; otherwise it keeps the one the constructor built on CPU. With `--dit-cpu-offload` or `--dit-layerwise-offload` the DiT is still on CPU at that point, so the table is computed on CPU. CPU and CUDA `pow` function round 5 of Edge's 64 entries one ulp apart (also similar for Nano and Super). The resident path and original NVIDIA's cosmos code (https://github.com/NVIDIA/cosmos-framework) compute it on CUDA. Nobody noticed this problem because the offloaded output still looks fine, just a different render of the same scene, and the difference only happens at larger token positions. The Cosmos 3 GPU tests also run resident only. I found this while optimizing Cosmos 3 on DGX Spark (SGLang enables CPU offloading by default when serving Cosmos 3). Since Spark has unified memory, so I ran the experiments below on a 4090, which has separate VRAM and system RAM like most machines. ## Modifications Always compute `inv_freq` on `get_local_torch_device()`, then move it to the DiT's device. It stays float32 and non-persistent. On the normal meta-to-GPU load the values are the same as before. ## Accuracy Tests Settings: - RTX 4090 - Cosmos 3 Edge, BF16 - Two long prompts, each one paragraph repeated three times: T2I 640 * 640 and T2V 832 * 480 * 121, 35 steps | | T2I | T2V | |-|-|-| | main branch offloaded vs. main branch resident | PSNR 29.37 dB, SSIM 0.972 | PSNR 25.19 dB, SSIM 0.885 | | this PR offloaded vs. main branch resident | byte-identical | byte-identical | | this PR resident vs. main branch resident | byte-identical | byte-identical | ``` export SGLANG_DISABLE_COSMOS3_GUARDRAILS=1 sglang serve --model-path nvidia/Cosmos3-Edge --dit-cpu-offload true # resident: --performance-mode manual ``` T2I prompt: ``` An overhead view of a busy harbor at golden hour. Dozens of small fishing boats in faded blue, red and white paint are moored along weathered wooden piers, their nets piled in loose heaps and their hulls reflecting in the calm green water. Gulls circle above a row of stacked wooden crates filled with silver fish, while workers in yellow rubber overalls carry baskets between the boats and a small market of canvas stalls. Long shadows stretch across the cobblestone quay, which is lined with narrow three-story houses painted ochre, teal and coral, each with flower boxes under the windows and laundry hanging on lines between them. In the distance a stone lighthouse stands at the end of a breakwater, and low hills covered with olive trees rise behind the town under a sky streaked with thin orange and pink clouds. The scene is sharp and detailed, with realistic textures on the wood, rope, stone and water, natural warm lighting, and a calm, lived-in atmosphere. ``` T2V prompt: ``` A first-person view from a small delivery robot rolling slowly along a sidewalk in a quiet residential neighborhood on a bright autumn morning. Maple trees with red and orange leaves line the street, and fallen leaves drift across the pavement in a light breeze. Parked cars, a blue mailbox, low garden fences and front porches with pumpkins pass by on the right side as the robot moves forward at a steady pace. A cyclist passes on the road to the left, and a person walking a golden retriever appears ahead and steps aside. The camera motion is smooth and stable, the lighting is natural with soft shadows, and the scene stays realistic and coherent from frame to frame. ``` main branch T2I result (resident vs. CPU offloading, and pixel difference by 4x), main branch T2V result (resident vs. CPU offloading, and pixel difference by 4x) https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b76c2d5d-6e13-496f-a923-23b8a8d9c959 ## Speed Tests and Profiling Settings: - RTX 4090 - Cosmos 3 Edge presets from `bench_diffusion_denoise.py` - main branch code vs this PR in ABBA order. title: [Fix] ipc: Make multimodal payloads, hidden states and weight-update dtypes round-trip under msgpack IPC
author: hnyls2002
body:
Fixes for messages that do not survive the opt-in msgpack IPC (`SGLANG_USE_PICKLE_IPC=0`). The default codec is unchanged.

- **Object-typed multimodal fields.** `MultimodalDataItem.feature`, `precomputed_embeddings`, `model_specific_data` values and `PositionalEmbeds.embeds` are typed `object`, and msgspec encodes tuples as lists and dataclasses as dicts without calling `enc_hook`. Values msgpack would not decode back unchanged (tuples, `torch.Size`, `torch.dtype`, dataclasses such as Kimi-K3's `KimiK3DeferredPreprocessing`, PIL images, numpy scalars, dicts with non-str keys, transport proxies) are now pickled into one ext (code 6) per request, through one pickler, so objects shared between values stay shared. Tensors, ndarrays, arrays and plain containers of them still go as before, with no pickling.
- **CUDA IPC / VMM transport proxies.** Their msgpack ext (code 5) read `sync_data_meta`, which the proxy no longer has, and dropped state and the concrete subclass on decode. It is removed; proxies take the pickled path above, which carries exactly what pickle carries and keeps one `_packed_owner` shared by the packed VMM proxies of a request.
- **`OutputHiddenStates`** allows a row to be one vector, which `return_hidden_states="last"` produces; msgpack decode rejected it.
- **`Engine.update_weights_from_distributed`** sends dtype names (`"bfloat16"`), so `torch.dtype` arguments encode under msgpack; both receivers already parse names with `getattr(torch, name)`.
- **Scripted runtime**: `ScriptedTokenizerRecvProxy.recv` returns msgpack bytes instead of raising.
- **Tests**: the data-parallel controller tests pin pickle IPC (they send `SimpleNamespace` requests), the rid-cleanup test asserts no call on the socket under either codec, and two `test_io_struct.py` tests cover the shared packed owner and the object-field round trip.

Behavior under pickle IPC is unchanged, except that `update_weights_from_distributed` passes dtype names instead of `torch.dtype` objects, which load the same weights.

title: [Fix] nemotron: Accept transformers 5 layer types in NemotronHConfig
author: janbernloehr
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #47444.

For `model_type: "nemotron_h"`, SGLang loads its own `NemotronHConfig` through `_CONFIG_REGISTRY`. That config accepts only the legacy layer-type names `mamba`, `attention`, `mlp` and `moe`. transformers 5.13 renamed the NemotronH layer types to `linear_attention` and `full_attention` and writes those names into `config.json`. A NemotronH checkpoint whose config was saved with transformers >= 5.13 therefore fails at server startup, before any weights load. This includes a plain `save_pretrained()` and quantized exports made with transformers >= 5.13.

```
ValueError: layers_block_type contains invalid types: {'linear_attention', 'full_attention'}. Must be one of: {'mamba', 'moe', 'mlp', 'attention'}
```

The public NemotronH checkpoints load today only because their `config.json` was written by transformers 4.x.

## Modifications

- `configs/nemotron_h.py`: `NemotronHConfig.__init__` maps `linear_attention` to `mamba` and `full_attention` to `attention` in `layers_block_type` and `mtp_layers_block_type` before pattern resolution and validation. Unknown names are still rejected.
- `configs/nano_nemotron_vl.py`: removed `_nemotron_h_compatible_config`, which applied the same mapping only for `nemotron_h_omni`. Every VL wrapper builds its `llm_config` through `NemotronHConfig`, so the mapping now lives in one place. This also fixes `NemotronH_Nano_VL_V2` and `NemotronH_Nano_Omni_Reasoning_V3`, which had no mapping and failed on transformers >= 5.13 configs.
- Tests (`test_nano_nemotron_vl_config.py`):
  - New regression test: a `NemotronHConfig` with transformers >= 5.13 names has the same layer pattern, MTP pattern and Mamba/attention layer ids as its legacy-named equivalent.
  - New test: unknown layer types still raise.
  - The existing omni alias test now covers all three VL wrappers.

  On `main`, the regression test and the two newly covered VL wrapper subtests fail.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable. This change only affects config parsing. Layer layouts that load today are unchanged.

The issue's reproduction, run on CPU with transformers 5.19.0 (the pinned version), re-saves the public `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16` config with `AutoConfig.save_pretrained()`:

- On `main`, `NemotronHConfig.from_pretrained` raises the `ValueError` above.
- On this branch, it parses to the same 52-layer `hybrid_override_pattern`, MTP pattern `*E` and Mamba/attention layer ids as the original config.

End to end on GPU: a ModelOpt FP8 export of Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B whose config uses the new names, served on a single GB10 with `--quantization modelopt` and EAGLE MTP (5/1/6) on a `main` nightly. Unpatched, the server exits at startup with the `ValueError` above. With this PR applied to the same image, it loads the target and MTP draft models, starts, and completes a 2000-in/128-out benchmark at concurrency 1. Draft acceptance on this particular export is about 0 in both SGLang and vLLM, which points to the checkpoint's MTP head and is unrelated to this change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (Not needed.)
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Not applicable: config parsing only.)

title: [Fix] diffusion/bcg: Warm up LTX-2 two-stage at the output resolution
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

`LTX2TwoStagePipeline` with `Lightricks/LTX-2.5-Diffusers` cannot start with default flags. sgl-project/sglang#45977 turns BCG on by default for this pipeline, and the BCG warmup resolution is seeded from the model's sampling default, 960x544. That is LTX-2.5's stage-1 size, but a two-stage request carries the output resolution and `LTX2HalveResolutionStage` rejects anything not divisible by 64, so the warmup request fails:

```
[Diffusion BCG] enabled by default for LTX2TwoStagePipeline
[Diffusion BCG] --warmup-resolutions unset; capturing the model default 960x544.
ValueError: LTX-2 two-stage requires resolution divisible by 64, got (544x960).
Server warmup failed; aborting startup
```

The non-BCG server warmup path already aligns to 64 through `_resolve_representative_warmup_resolution`; only the BCG branch of `_resolve_default_warmup_resolution` returns the sampling default as is.

## Modifications

`warmup_request_builder.py`: add `_two_stage_request_resolution` and use it where `_resolve_default_warmup_resolution` returns the sampling default as is. For `LTX2TwoStage*` pipelines, a default the halving rejects is treated as the stage-1 size and mapped to twice its size (960x544 -> 1920x1088).

Unchanged:
- explicit `--warmup-resolutions`
- one-stage pipelines
- defaults that already pass the alignment check (LTX-2 768x512, LTX-2.3 HQ 1920x1088)
- a default that doubling cannot fix (for example an explicit `--warmup-sampling-params` override) is left as written and still fails loudly

That early return also serves warmup that is not server-based, so that path gets the same mapping.

Tests: one new case in `test_cfg_parallel_warmup.py` for the default resolution of each pipeline above, and one extra assertion in `test_server_args.py::TestBreakableCudaGraphDefault::test_ltx25_distilled_two_stage_serving_turns_bcg_on` that the auto-enabled path ends up with `warmup_resolutions == ["1920x1088"]`.

## Accuracy Tests

No change to model outputs: only the shape the BCG warmup captures at startup changes.

Unit tests (1xH200 devbox, this commit on top of main 9691e711cd0; `test_cfg_parallel_warmup.py` + `test_server_args.py`):
- with `warmup_request_builder.py` reverted to main: the two new assertions fail (5 failed)
- with this change: 292 passed
- the 3 remaining failures are identical on main and here. Without an HF token `test_cfg_parallel_warmup.py` cannot be collected (importing `gpu_cases` resolves every case's gated model info), so I stubbed `gpu_cases` with empty lists, which breaks 2 tests that index it; the third asserts no warnings and trips on a diffusers Flax deprecation warning in that image. I did not run them with a token.

title: [Fix] diffusion: Fail fast on offline runtime failures
author: Zeta-li
body:
## Motivation

Offline `DiffGenerator.generate()` catches scheduler errors, logs them, and continues with later prompts. An illegal memory access or device-side assertion can therefore return `None` or partial results and leave the same failed runtime available for the next call. If a local worker exits before replying, the synchronous client can also wait indefinitely when no RPC timeout is configured.

This complements #45065 by covering the synchronous/offline client side of the failure reported in #38167.

## Modifications

- Raise and latch `DiffusionRuntimeError` for recognized device context/allocator failures and dead local workers. Stop the remaining prompts and reject subsequent requests until the generator is recreated.
- Check owned worker health while polling for a synchronous response. Send each request once and preserve the overall configured RPC deadline.
- Give fatal device errors precedence over earlier recoverable errors in control fan-out. Both synchronous and asynchronous loops stop immediately on a fatal reply, so a later replica cannot hide it with a timeout or an unbounded receive. Successful replies, ordinary errors, and OOM still reach every replica.
- Route explicit client warmup and LoRA operations through the same checked request path, preserving pinned replica routing for per-replica warmup. Close the client's resources and terminate its owned local processes on runtime failure.
- Release resources for prepared video requests that are skipped after an unrecoverable failure. Keep recoverable request errors and OOM handling compatible.

## Accuracy Tests

Rebased onto main `e3ec98b15e6a`, retaining explicit replica routing from #47571 and the fatal-error/worker-health checks. CPU validation on Python 3.12 with injected device errors and worker exits: **463 passed, 2 skipped across 17 test files**.

The 16 related files account for **457 passed, 2 skipped**:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=999 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 SGLANG_DIFFUSION_PLATFORM_OVERRIDE=cpu \
python -m pytest -q -rs \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_diffusion_generator_errors.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_diffusion_generator_shutdown.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_scheduler_client.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_resolve_prompts.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_dp_routing.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_cfg_parallel_warmup.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_warmup_step_floor.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_qwen_image_layered.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_comfyui_generator.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_comfyui_adapters.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_sampling_params.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_health_warmup_gate.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_launch_server_shutdown.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_request_cancel.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_warmup_probe_degradation.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_auto_residency.py
```

The platform-bootstrap file accounts for **6 passed**. Run it separately without the forced CPU platform, so its fake external platform can be selected:

```bash
env -u SGLANG_DIFFUSION_PLATFORM_OVERRIDE \
  PYTHONPATH=python CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=999 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
  PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 \
  python -m pytest -q -rs \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_worker_bootstrap.py
```

CUDA was unavailable throughout; actual GPU faults were not induced. The two skips are async-cancellation cases that do not apply to the synchronous client. Test collection requires the public MOVA `model_index.json` cached under its default revision; no model weights were downloaded.

Regression coverage includes:
- Both control fan-out loops stop on a fatal reply, including after success/OOM/ordinary errors, before another replica can time out or wait indefinitely. Remote `set_lora()` also invalidates the generator.
- Explicit warmup forwards the new `replica` argument through the checked generator path and preserves optional worker-health checks. Both local and remote modes warm every replica without advancing round-robin real traffic. Three warmup cases reproduce the unexpected-`replica` TypeError on the rebased code before this adaptation, and pass with it.
- The manually constructed warmup generator initializes `local_scheduler_process`. Related suites exercise warmup degradation/auto-residency, layered images, ComfyUI, cancellation, shutdown, sampling, and platform/plugin startup.

Pinned isort, Ruff formatting/lint, codespell, and applicable test-placement/pytest-entrypoint checks pass. Community CI must validate the updated head.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Validation targets the request lifecycle. Health polling consumes an available reply immediately and checks for worker exits at most one second apart while waiting.

- [x] Document the runtime-failure exception in the generation API docstring.

title: [Fix] dp-attention: Trim MLP-sync pad rows from extend outputs before the draft extend
author: mattteochen
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #47490.

With DP attention + EAGLE, `--moe-a2a-backend flashinfer` on the target and a DeepEP draft (`--speculative-moe-a2a-backend deepep`), the prefill CUDA graph pads each prefill to the DP-wide bucket of the largest rank, while the draft pads only to its own bucket. The extend arm of `post_forward_mlp_sync_batch` trims the target outputs to `seq_lens_sum`, which also counts the cached prefix, so after the first prefill chunk the hidden states keep the pad rows. The draft extend then pads them to its smaller width and `_pad_inputs_to_size` fails with `RuntimeError: Trying to create tensor with negative dimension`.

## Modifications

- `ForwardBatch.post_forward_mlp_sync_batch`, extend arm: trim `next_token_logits`, `hidden_states` and `mm_input_embeds` to `_original_num_tokens` (the token count before MLP-sync padding), falling back to `seq_lens_sum` when the batch was not padded. The draft re-pads the real rows to its own bucket. This covers all spec-v2 workers, which pass the target hidden states to the draft extend unchanged.
- `test_mlp_sync_pad_unpad.py`: a regression case (29-token chunk after a 640-token prefix, padded to a 48-token bucket, must return 29 hidden rows). It fails on main and passes with the fix.

## Accuracy Tests

GLM-5.2 NVFP4 on GB300 with the 2026-10-28 SGLang nightly image plus this patch, EAGLE 3/1/4, prefill CUDA graph on, GSM8K (`few_shot_gsm8k`, 200 questions):

| Topology | MoE A2A (target / draft) | GSM8K | accept len |
|---|---|---|---|
| DEP4 | flashinfer / deepep | 0.960 | 3.29 |
| DEP4 | deepep / deepep (reference) | 0.920 | 3.35 |
| DEP8 | flashinfer / deepep | 0.950 | 3.25 |
| DEP8 | deepep / deepep (reference) | 0.905 | 3.33 |

Without the patch the flashinfer arm crashes at the first mixed-count prefill step. Re-checked on current main (`51d5502aff`, Python overlay on the same image), DEP4, GSM8K 20 questions: main crashes (`negative dimension -48` and `-32`), main + this PR passes (0.90, no errors).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No change on the default path: it only changes a slice length.

author: OnePunchMonk

Fixes #47515. Two small bug fixes in the Hy-Nomas pipeline.

- `_free_bytes` now adds `memory_reserved - memory_allocated` (same correction as `qwen_image21._cache_fits`), so memory the allocator holds from an earlier request counts as available. title: [Fix] scheduler: Abort retracted requests whose KV the recompute cannot rebuild
author: hnyls2002
body:
- **Abort a retracted request when the recompute cannot rebuild its KV.** `release_req` now returns whether the request can be resumed, and is the single decision point for every retract:
  - **PD decode rebootstrap** (`pause_generation(mode="retract")`, and the DeepSeek-V4 retract through `backup_kv_cache`): `Req.build_rebootstrap_payload` carries token ids only, so multimodal, `input_embeds` and `positional_embed_overrides` requests were recomputed with wrong KV and produced wrong output without an error. They are now aborted (`Req.resumable_by_rebootstrap`). `backup_kv_cache` already did this for multimodal requests under DeepSeek-V4; it now uses the same property.
  - **Local re-prefill** (non-disaggregated retract): multimodal inputs and embed overrides are applied again by `prepare_for_extend`, so those requests are fine. `input_embeds` cover only the prompt, so `reset_for_retract` restarts their generation. That restart is invisible until output has been sent downstream; once it has (a streamed token, or a non-stream request past the `SGLANG_FORCE_STREAM_INTERVAL` flush), the restarted tokens were spliced after the stale `send_token_offset`. Such a request is now aborted instead (`Req.resumable_by_reprefill`); one that has sent nothing still restarts.
  - `retract_all` returns the requests that cannot be resumed, and `pause_generation` aborts them with a 503. `retract_decode` already aborts when `release_req` returns False.
  - Every PD rebootstrap now has at least one output id, so the transfer commit's `resumes_output` is `decode_req.is_rebootstrap` with an assert.
- **One PD fill-length formula.** `len(origin_input_ids) + max(len(output_ids) - 1, 0)` was written in `DecodePreallocQueue._pre_alloc_fill_len` and again for the prebuilt `seq_len`; both use `pre_alloc_fill_len` in `disaggregation/utils.py` now. No behavior change.
- **`/detokenize` rejects out-of-vocabulary ids with 400.** A negative id or one above u32 returned 500, and an id at or above the vocab size was silently dropped with a 200. Ids outside `[0, model vocab_size)` now get a 400, as `_validate_token_ids_logprob` reports invalid ids.

Behavior changes: the aborts above replace silently wrong output (PD decode) or a garbled restarted generation (local `input_embeds` retract after output was sent), and `/detokenize` returns 400 where it returned 500 or dropped ids. Priority preemption still re-prefills a preempted `input_embeds` request from the prompt; that path is unchanged here.

title: [Fix] RL: Fix crash when returning routed experts under DCP or KV sharding
author: ByronHsu
body:
## Why?

With `--enable-return-routed-experts`, sglang saves each token's routed experts in a CPU buffer, one row per KV slot. The buffer is sized for one GPU's KV pool.

With DCP (decode context parallel) or KV sharding (`--enable-kv-cache-sharding`), KV slot numbers cover every GPU's pool. Slots past the first GPU's pool have no row, so the server crashes.

```text
Example: DCP 4, each GPU's KV pool holds 64 tokens

KV slots        0 ──────────────────────────────── 271   (4 GPUs' pools)
buffer before   0 ──── 67                                (1 GPU's pool)
                         └─ slot 68 → IndexError → server crashes
buffer after    0 ──────────────────────────────── 271
```

We hit this on Kimi-K3 with DCP16 during RL, about 20 minutes into the run.

## What?

- Make the buffer cover every KV slot the allocator can hand out:
  - no DCP, no KV sharding: unchanged
  - DCP: every DCP rank's pool
  - KV sharding: every shard's pool
- Only one function changes: `RunnerIds.capture_token_capacity`. The indexer top-k buffer uses it too, so it gets the same fix.
- The int16 buffer option that used to be in this PR is now #47833.

## Verification?

A new unit test fills the KV pool and checks that the buffer has exactly one row per slot:

```text
case            largest slot   rows before   rows after
no DCP               67             68            68
DCP 4               271             68 ✗         272
KV sharding 4       271             68 ✗         272     (observed, CPU)
```

## Test?

- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_runner_ids.py::test_capture_capacity_covers_widened_allocator_ids`: **observed** passing on CPU. It **observed** failing on `main` for the DCP and KV-sharding cases.
- All 19 tests in `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_runner_ids.py`: **observed** passing on CPU.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files: **observed** passing.
- CI: **pending**.
- GPU run with DCP and routed experts: **pending**.

title: [Fix] hicache: mlock pinned host buffers so page aging never scans them
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

`cudaHostRegister` keeps a host pool's pages resident for DMA, but it leaves them on the kernel's evictable LRU. Proactive reclaim (page aging) clears the accessed flag of every page it scans there, pinned or not. On GPUs that read host memory through the CPU page tables (ATS), the device's next access to an aged page takes a page fault instead of a plain read, so host-to-device copies out of a HiCache host pool can fault page by page once the pool has been aged.

Locked pages sit on the unevictable LRU and are never scanned, so making mlock part of pinning removes those faults at the source. There is no new flag: a pinned buffer is a locked buffer.

## Modifications

All in `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/common.py`:

- `_cuda_host_register` mlocks the buffer once all of its ranges are registered. Every buffer that `alloc_with_host_register` pins (`pin_memory=True`) is therefore locked too: the HiCache host pools on CUDA and ROCm, and the other users of that allocator.
- `_cuda_host_unregister` munlocks it once all of its ranges are unregistered, so a destroyed pool returns to ordinary memory. The locked range is kept on the tensor next to the registered ranges, under `_HOST_LOCKED_RANGE_ATTR`.
- Before locking, the `RLIMIT_MEMLOCK` soft limit is raised to the hard limit, which needs no privilege. The locked range, the time the lock took, the limits, `CAP_IPC_LOCK` and `VmLck` are logged at INFO.
- A refused lock (a memlock limit below the buffer size without `CAP_IPC_LOCK`, as in many containers) logs a warning with errno, the size, the limits, `CAP_IPC_LOCK` and `VmLck`, and says to raise the limit or grant the capability. The buffer stays registered and usable exactly as before this PR. Failing instead would turn deployments that work today into startup failures, for a lock that only keeps device reads fast and never affects correctness.
- Unchanged: `pin_memory=False` (nothing is pinned or locked), torch-pinned buffers (npu, musa, xpu) and `hipHostMalloc` pools, which the device runtime allocates.

Cost: the host pool becomes unevictable memory, which it is pinned for DMA anyway. Locking adds work during startup; the INFO log reports its duration. On ATS platforms a registered pool could previously still be swapped out; with this change pinned means resident there too, as it already does on non-ATS platforms, so host pools must fit in RAM as they already must elsewhere.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: the pool's contents and every copy out of it are unchanged, only the pages' LRU placement is.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not included in this PR.

## Testing

- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_host_register.py` and `test_mmap_allocator.py` pass on CPU (22 tests). The cases that hand the allocator a fake buffer take the warning path and pass unchanged.
- A direct check on a 64 MiB CPU tensor: `_mlock_host_buffer` logs the locked range and `VmLck` rises by 64 MiB; `_munlock_host_buffer` clears the attribute.
- `pre-commit` (ruff, ruff-format, codespell) is clean on the changed file.

title: [Fix] request_logger: Redact client watermark keys in request logs when watermarking is off
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

A client can send a watermark config that carries its key to a server launched without `--enable-watermark`. The received-request log runs before validation rejects such a request, so the key was written to the request log in plain text, at every `--log-requests-level` and in both the text and JSON formats. The request-metrics exporter had the same gap. The crash dump's `server_args` snapshot had a related one: the Python API (`ServerArgs` / `Engine(watermark_key=...)`) accepts a server key without `--enable-watermark`, and the dump then pickled the raw `ServerArgs`.

## Modifications

- `request_logger.py`: with watermarking off, `_has_client_watermark` looks only where a client can put a watermark config: `GenerateReqInput.watermark` (a single value or the per-request list), `sampling_params["watermark"]` (a dict, a list of dicts, or `None`; `EmbeddingReqInput` included), and the OpenAI request's top-level `watermark` after `model_dump`. `_redact_client_watermark` returns the request unchanged when none of those is set, or when watermarking is on (the formatters already redact then). Otherwise it redacts; for the OpenAI request dict it redacts only the watermark config on a shallow copy instead of walking the dict and its prompt. It is applied in `log_received_request`, `log_openai_received_request` and `log_finished_request`. A request without a watermark field is logged exactly as before, with no copy and no walk over its token-id lists.
- `request_metrics_exporter.py`: redact the watermark container fields of the exported request parameters.
- `tokenizer_manager.py`: `_server_args_for_dump` always writes the redacted resolved dict, as watermarking-on servers already did (that dict also loads under `safe_pickle_load`, which blocks the `ServerArgs` object). If the snapshot raises, the dump is written without `server_args`, as for the config snapshot.
- `sampling/watermarking/README.md`: request logs redact watermark keys whether or not `--enable-watermark` is set, and without it only those fields are checked.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: request-log, metrics-export and crash-dump redaction only; no change to model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run here. Per logged request the added check reads at most two fields; a request without a watermark field takes the same path as before, and `redact_watermark_secrets` is never called for it (asserted by the new test).

## Checklist

- [x] Format: `ruff format`, `ruff check` (F401, F821, F823, UP037), `isort`, `codespell` and the repo's local lint scripts pass on the changed files.
- [x] Unit tests:
  - `test/registered/unit/utils/test_request_logger_redaction.py`: `test_watermarking_off_checks_only_watermark_fields` runs under a watermark-off config, in both formats, through all three logging entry points. A key in each location (top-level `watermark`, `sampling_params["watermark"]`, both batch forms, `EmbeddingReqInput`, `ChatCompletionRequest`) is redacted, with exactly one `<redacted>` per entry point; requests without a watermark field never call `redact_watermark_secrets`; an OpenAI request with a watermark config redacts only that config.
  - `test/registered/unit/utils/test_crash_dump.py`: `test_server_args_key_redacted_with_watermarking_off` fails without the redaction (the key is in the pickle); `test_server_args_snapshot_failure_keeps_the_dump` fails without the guard.
  - `test/registered/unit/observability/test_request_metrics_exporter.py`: `test_redacts_client_watermark_keys`.
  - Locally on CPU: the three files pass (29 tests). The same test files against unpatched `main` fail exactly on the 4 new tests.
- [x] Documentation: the watermarking README's logging paragraph is updated.
- [ ] Accuracy and speed benchmarks: not applicable (see above).
- [x] Code style followed.

title: [Fix] tokenizer_manager: Do not dispatch a request whose abort was already sent
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

If a request is aborted while the tokenizer manager is still preparing it (for example while it fetches an image or publishes multimodal features), the `AbortReq` reaches the scheduler before the request itself. The scheduler drops an abort for a rid it has not received and keeps no record of it, and `abort_request` never resends one because `state.abort_sent` is already set. The request is then dispatched anyway and runs to completion while its caller waits. A plain server shows it with a slow image URL and a client disconnect: the request runs to `max_new_tokens`. In PD disaggregation a decode request in this state holds its KV until the transfer timeout.

The ordering:
1. The rid is registered and preprocessing is in progress.
2. `abort_request` sets `state.abort_sent` and sends `AbortReq`. The scheduler has no request with that rid yet, so it drops the abort.
3. Preprocessing finishes and `_send_one_request` dispatches the request.
4. Every later `abort_request` call returns early at `if state.abort_sent`, including the disconnect watcher's.

## Modifications

- `_send_one_request` and `_send_batch_request` check `abort_sent` after their last `await` and skip dispatch for such requests. Everything after the check is synchronous, so no abort can land between the check and the dispatch. The prepared transport features of a skipped request are released the same way a failed dispatch releases them: CUDA VMM items through `cancel_for_dispatch`, and CUDA IPC feature proxies (`feature` and `precomputed_embeddings`) through the pool's `cancel_proxy`, since no scheduler would ever acknowledge them. A batch still dispatches its other requests. The batch path is factored into `_drop_aborted_before_dispatch`.
- `_wait_one_response` finishes a skipped request through `_handle_abort_req`. That produces the same output the scheduler sends when it pops an aborted request from its waiting queue (finish reason `abort`, "Abort in waiting queue") and removes the rid from `rid_to_state`. It runs in the waiter rather than at the send site because the waiter looks its state up by rid and finishing the request removes that entry.
- `abort_request(abort_all=True)` marks every undispatched request `abort_sent`, so an abort-all (`/abort_request`, weight updates with `abort_all_requests`, pause with abort) also keeps requests still preprocessing from running. Requests held at `generate_request`'s pause gate are left alone (new `ReqState.waiting_at_pause_gate`): a pause holds them and they run after `continue_generation`.

Not covered: multi-tokenizer mode (`tokenizer_worker_num > 1`). If `/abort_request` lands on a worker that does not own the rid, that worker forwards it to the scheduler without touching the owning worker's state; covering that needs a record on the scheduler side.

## Tests

New tests in `test/registered/unit/managers/test_tokenizer_manager_rid_cleanup.py::TestAbortBeforeDispatch`; each fails without the fix (the waiter never finishes, `TimeoutError`):
- `test_abort_during_preprocessing_is_not_dispatched` aborts a request through `generate_request` while tokenization (subtest `tokenize`) or feature publication (subtest `publish`) is blocked, then lets it finish. Only the `AbortReq` reaches the scheduler, the caller gets an `abort` finish reason, the prepared features and CUDA IPC proxies are cancelled, and the rid is freed.
- `test_abort_all_skips_preprocessing_requests_but_not_paused_ones`: an abort-all finishes the request that was preprocessing and leaves the one held at the pause gate, which is dispatched after the pause is lifted.
- `test_batch_dispatches_only_requests_not_aborted` aborts one request of a batch during the batch's feature publication. The other request is dispatched alone, only the aborted request's multimodal items and proxies are cancelled, and its waiter gets an `abort` finish reason.

`test_request_class_override_points.py`: the stub request state gains an `abort_sent` field, which the dispatch path now reads.

Run locally on a CPU-only environment: `test_tokenizer_manager_rid_cleanup.py` and `test_request_class_override_points.py`, 55 passed; `test_multimodal_abort_cleanup.py`, `test_gpu_feature_transport.py` and `test_scheduler_pause_generation.py` also pass.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no change to model execution or numerics.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: the change adds a dictionary lookup per dispatched request.

title: [Fix] hicache: Withhold only protected bytes from page-cache credit
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

The cgroup host-memory headroom used to size the HiCache host pool credits reclaimable page cache back against a cgroup's usage. Since #42788 it withholds that credit to respect `memory.min` protection, but it withholds all of it as soon as any descendant cgroup has a nonzero `memory.min`. A single small protected child, for example a `systemd-oomd.service` under `system.slice` with `memory.min` set, therefore cancels the entire page-cache credit, and the host pool is sized as if gigabytes of easily reclaimable cache could never be freed.

## Modifications

- `_has_protected_descendants` is replaced by `_protected_children_bytes`, which returns how many bytes reclaim at a cgroup must leave to its children: the sum over its **direct** children of `min(memory.min, memory.current)`, with `max` counting as the child's full usage. The kernel caps a child's effective protection at its usage, and a deeper cgroup's protection at its ancestors', so direct children bound it.
- The headroom subtracts only that amount from the page-cache credit (`max(0, page_cache - protected)`) instead of zeroing it.
- A child without `memory.min` (no memory controller enabled) contributes nothing. An unreadable or malformed value still withholds the whole credit, as before.

Unit tests in `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_host_memory.py`:
- the sibling-protection case now covers a `memory.min` above the child's usage, below it, `max`, and an unreadable value;
- a service under `system.slice` keeps its cache credit when only a small `systemd-oomd.service` child is protected, and a child's protection is capped at its usage;
- a deeper descendant's protection is capped by its ancestor.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: this only changes host-memory budgeting for the hierarchical cache, not model computation.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

title: [Fix] diffusion: Server warmup reaches every data-parallel replica
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

With `--dp-size > 1`, `--warmup-mode server` warms only one replica. The warmup requests go through `forward`, which routes with the round-robin `_select_replica`, so one warmup request lands on replica 0 only and every other replica serves its first real request cold.

Observed on MiniMax-H3 fl2va, `--num-gpus 2 --dp-size 2 --performance-mode speed --warmup-mode server`: the log shows `Warmup requests 1/1`, and replica 1's first real request took 121.9 s against about 116.6 s warm. Its MP4 also differed from the warm output (video bit-identical, audio SNR 52.8 dB). A 1-GPU server with `--warmup-mode off` reproduces the same cold-first-request output, so that difference is a cold-path effect, not a DP bug; warming every replica removes it from the served traffic.

## Modifications

- `SchedulerClient.forward` / `AsyncSchedulerClient.forward`: new keyword-only `replica` argument that pins an ordinary request to one replica and bypasses `_select_replica`, so `_replica_counter` only advances for real traffic. Control requests still fan out to all replicas.
- `run_async_client_warmup` / `run_sync_client_warmup`: build the warmup list once and send the full list to every endpoint in `server_args.scheduler_endpoints`, replicas in parallel (asyncio tasks / a thread pool) and each replica's list in order. Every replica sees the same list, so `warmup_total` stays correct per replica, and OOM degradation retries independently per replica. All replicas finish before the first error is raised, so a failure does not leave siblings warming in the background of live traffic.
- With `dp_size == 1` behavior is unchanged: the single request still goes to `endpoints[0]` and the counter was never advanced in that case.
- Tests: `test_server_warmup_reaches_every_replica_without_skewing_round_robin` in `test_scheduler_client.py` (sync and async) asserts that with two endpoints both receive the whole warmup list with `warmup_total == 2`, and that real traffic then still starts at replica 0. It fails on `main` and passes here. `test_cfg_parallel_warmup.py` only gains the `scheduler_endpoints` its mock `server_args` now needs.

## Accuracy Tests

No model-output change: only which replica receives each warmup request changes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not measured end to end. Unit tests ran on a B300 devbox: `test_scheduler_client`, `test_dp_routing`, `test_cfg_parallel_warmup`, `test_health_warmup_gate`, `test_warmup_probe_degradation`, `test_diffusion_generator_shutdown` and `test_webui` pass together (149 passed, 2 skipped).

title: [Fix] megamoe: Allocate the symmetric buffers before KV cache sizing
author: hnyls2002
body:
MegaMoE's symmetric buffer was allocated by the first MegaMoE forward, after the KV cache had been sized. It lives for the whole run, but it came out of the runtime slack (`B * (1 - mem_fraction_static)`) meant for activations and CUDA graphs. The buffer covers the worst-case routing at `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK` and grows with it: at the default cap of 8192 it is a few GB and fits in the slack, but at a large cap it does not. With DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DP attention 4, MegaMoE, DSpark and a cap of 65536, the target's buffer (22.31 GB per GPU) is allocated during the first forward and leaves no room for the draft's (11.78 GB), so startup fails with `CUDA driver error: out of memory` in `symm_mem.empty` at `--mem-fraction-static 0.9`.

- `allocate_mega_moe_buffers` allocates the buffers of the model's ready `DeepseekV2MoE` MegaMoE layers through the same `_mega_moe_buffer` the forward uses, and logs their count and size. `ModelRunner.initialize` calls it after the post-load model changes, before the KV cache is sized, so the KV budget charges the buffers like the weights; the draft worker does the same before its own KV sizing.
- `_run_mega_routed` passes that buffer into `run_mega_routed_experts` (new optional `buf`), so the DeepSeek MoE path builds the buffer key only in `_mega_moe_buffer` and the up-front buffer cannot drift from the one the forward uses. Other callers pass no `buf` and keep building their own.
- The `--speculative-enable-w4a4-mxfp4-megamoe` help text and the server-arguments doc drop the advice to lower `--mem-fraction-static` for a draft buffer allocated after the KV pool is sized.

With MegaMoE on, the KV pool is smaller by the buffer size. Other MegaMoE models (Qwen MoE, MiniMax-M3, Kimi-K3) and AMD's FlyDSL path still allocate at the first forward.

## Verification

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on GB300, DP attention 4, MegaMoE, DSpark, breakable prefill graphs at 4096 and 8192 tokens, `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=65536`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.9`:

| Code | Startup | Buffers per GPU (GB) | 8K prefill step (ms) | GSM8K (%) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | fails, `CUDA driver error: out of memory` in `symm_mem.empty` | - | - | - |
| this PR | serves | 22.31 (target) + 11.78 (draft) | 87.34 | 98.00 |

GSM8K is sgl-eval, 200 questions, greedy, thinking off.

title: [Fix] diffusion: LTX-2.5 two-stage defaults to its 1920x1088 canvas
author: niehen6174
body:
## Motivation

On >=130 GiB GPUs (H200, B200, B300), sglang's own 2-GPU LTX-2.5 two-stage cookbook preset (`--pipeline-class-name LTX2TwoStagePipeline`) does not start:

```
LTX-2 two-stage requires resolution divisible by 64, got (544x960)
```

The cause is the default size:

- `LTX25SamplingParams` defaults to 960x544. That is the one-stage canvas, and the two-stage pipeline uses it too.
- `LTX2HalveResolutionStage` needs each side to be a multiple of 64, so 960x544 cannot be halved.
- On these GPUs BCG is on by default for `LTX2TwoStagePipeline`, and its warmup runs at the sampling default, so startup fails.
- A two-stage request that omits its size fails the same way.

This was found by serving the 1920x1088, 121-frame two-stage workload with the cookbook command on 2x H200 and 4x B200.

## Modifications

- `configs/sample/ltx_2_5.py`: `LTX25SamplingParams` names its two-stage canvas (`two_stage_default_size = (1920, 1088)`, the official two-stage default). `_adjust` applies it under the two-stage pipeline when the request sets neither width nor height; an explicit size still wins.
  - The change stays in LTX-2.5's own sampling params. The per-pipeline registry is keyed by class name alone, so registering `LTX2TwoStagePipeline` for LTX-2.5 would also have changed LTX-2 and LTX-2.3.
- `runtime/warmup_request_builder.py`: the LTX two-stage warmup path reads the same canvas, so BCG captures the shape two-stage serves. As a guard for any other model, the BCG warmup no longer takes an LTX-2 two-stage default that the halve stage would reject; it falls through to the aligned representative shape.

## Accuracy Tests

No numerical change. An explicit request size is used as before, and one-stage LTX-2.5 keeps 960x544.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

2x H200: the cookbook preset with no size flags, LTX-2.5 distilled, two-stage, 1920x1088, 121 frames. The harness warms up 3 requests at 3 steps, then times 2 requests by the client.

| sglang | Result |
| --- | --- |
| main at 3a01d4cc, preset | server exits during warmup (error above) |
| this branch, preset | 9.396 s |
| main at 3a01d4cc, explicit `--width 1920 --height 1088` | 9.435 s |

The same preset also fails at 3a01d4cc on 2x B200, in the same way.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). `test_cfg_parallel_warmup.py` has 3 new tests; 58 passed on this branch rebased onto d2cf2371b0, on B200.
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not needed: the cookbook preset now works as documented.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [Fix] diffusion: MiniMax-H3 warms up at the short edge --warmup-resolutions names
author: niehen6174
body:
## Motivation

`MiniMaxH3SamplingParams._synthetic_warmup_target` takes only the aspect ratio from `--warmup-resolutions` and always warms up at the 768 short edge. The flag is meant to name the canvas the server will serve, so this has two effects:

- **32 GB recipe.** The cookbook passes `--warmup-resolutions 864x480`, so warmup runs at a 768 short edge: a larger canvas than the server serves, on the tightest card.
- **544x960 workload.** A server deployed for the common 544x960 workload (`--warmup-resolutions 960x544`) still warms at 768, so its first real request pays the first-shape cost.

## Modifications

- `configs/sample/minimax_h3.py`:
  - When `--warmup-resolutions` is set, the warmup target's `short_edge` is `min(width, height)` of that resolution.
  - The aspect-ratio and duration handling are unchanged.
  - Without the flag, the warmup is still 768 / 16:9 / 5 s.
- `test_minimax_h3_admission.py`: the warmup expectations follow the named canvas: 832x464 now warms at 464, 864x480 at 480, and 960x544 at 544.

## Accuracy Tests

No numerical change. Only the shape of the synthetic warmup request changes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

- **Steady state is not affected.** Warmed request latency on the 544x960 workload is the same either way. Our benchmark sends 3 warmup requests at the target shape before timing, so it masks the difference. The workload runs at 56.6 s on 1x H200 and 27.6 s on 1x B200.
- **First-request latency is not measured.** This change is meant to move the first-shape cost into warmup, and that first-request latency has not been measured separately.

title: [Fix] [AMD] quark: Widen the Quark MXFP4 W4A16 MoE gate to consumer RDNA and fail clearly without aiter
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

**What goes wrong**
#47408 restricted the Quark MXFP4 W4A16 MoE path to gfx1151. On any other consumer RDNA GPU (gfx11xx, gfx1200, gfx1201) the gate is now false, so `process_weights_after_loading` falls into the AITER branch and calls `e8m0_shuffle`, which is only imported when `_use_aiter` is set. Without aiter the server fails at startup with `NameError: name 'e8m0_shuffle' is not defined`. The same applies to `moe_shuffle_scale` on gfx1250 when aiter is off, and to `SGLANG_ENABLE_QUARK_MXFP4_MOE_W4A16=0`.

**Where it shows up**
Every consumer RDNA GPU other than gfx1151. Reported by @vivienfanghuagood on gfx1201 (RDNA4, 32 GB, ROCm 7.2.3, no aiter): before #47408 the W4A16 path served amd/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4; after it, startup fails with the NameError. gfx942 and gfx1250 (MI455) must keep the AITER path.

**How to fix**
Gate the W4A16 path on consumer RDNA again (`gfx11*` and `gfx120*`, not `gfx12*` because gfx1250 also matches), inlined so this does not depend on #47254. In the non-W4A16 branch, raise a clear "requires aiter" error when `_use_aiter` is false instead of falling through to the NameError.

## Modifications

- `quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py`: replace `_is_gfx1151` with `_is_consumer_rdna = gcnArchName.split(":")[0].startswith(("gfx11", "gfx120"))`; `_use_triton_w4a16` keys on it. gfx1250 and gfx942 stay on AITER.
- `quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py`: `process_weights_after_loading` raises a `RuntimeError` ("requires aiter") at the top of the non-W4A16 branch when `_use_aiter` is false.
- Update the gate comment, the W4A16 `info_once` message, and the `SGLANG_ENABLE_QUARK_MXFP4_MOE_W4A16` comment in `environ.py` so they no longer say gfx1151 only.
- `test_quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe_w4a16.py`: gate cases gfx1100 / gfx1151 / gfx1200 / gfx1201 on, gfx942 / gfx1250 off, and the env switch off on gfx1151 and gfx1201. The EP, -1 bucket and SwiGLU tests are architecture independent and unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

The W4A16 compute path is unchanged; only the gate that selects it changes. Measured by @vivienfanghuagood on an equivalent gate (`startswith(("gfx11", "gfx1200", "gfx1201"))`, same behavior as this PR's `("gfx11", "gfx120")` on all current archs), amd/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4, tp=1, `--context-length 8192`, no aiter, Triton 3.7.0 + triton-kernels 1.0.0, sgl-eval gsm8k, 100 questions, thinking off, T=0.7. 100 questions is about +/-5 points of noise.

| GPU | main before #47408 | #47408 | #47408 + gate widening |
|---|---|---|---|
| gfx1201 (RDNA4) | 57% | NameError at startup | 61% |
| gfx1100 (RDNA3) | 55% | NameError at startup | 58% |

The `requires aiter` guard and the exact gate expression in this PR were not run on a GPU by the author.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Same setup and runs as above, separate server processes (c1 / c8 tok/s):

| GPU | main before #47408 | #47408 | #47408 + gate widening |
|---|---|---|---|
| gfx1201 (RDNA4) | 31.8 / 246.9 | NameError at startup | 31.1 / 237.6 |
| gfx1100 (RDNA3) | 17.0 / 192.4 | NameError at startup | 16.5 / 174.2 |

gfx1100 c8 is 9.5% below the pre-#47408 run, more than the other three deltas (-2% to -4%); whether that is noise or an effect of the #47408 EP changes was not isolated.

Unit tests (#47408's test file plus the new gate cases): 7 passed on both cards, including the two EP cases.

title: [Fix] rust-server: Give each attention-DP listener its own frontend cores
author: phphlio1
body:
Fixes #47598.

## Motivation

Under DP attention every DP rank hosts a Rust listener (`SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1`), and each listener runs `_partition_cores()` on its own process affinity mask. DP ranks launched with one mask (no NUMA bind, or several ranks per NUMA node with it) therefore all compute the same slice and pin their frontends onto the same first cores of the mask. GLM-5.3 at TP8/DPA8 on 8xH200: all 8 listeners log `rust server cores=[2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9]` out of 128 allowed cores. #47161 stopped pinning the scheduler thread, but the frontend sets still collide on `main`.

## Modifications

- `rust_server/server.py`: new collective `RustServer.gather_frontend_cpu_share(hosts_listener)`. Every rank all-gathers `(hostname, allowed cores)` for listener ranks (`None` otherwise) on the world group, and gets back its `(index, count)` among the listeners with an identical key. `launch()` takes it as `frontend_cpu_share` (default `(0, 1)`, i.e. unchanged behaviour) and hands it to `_partition_cores`.
- `rust_server/config.py`: `_frontend_cpu_key()` and the pure `_frontend_cpu_share(cpu_keys, rank)`; `_partition_cores(..., cpu_share=(0, 1))` cuts the mask into `count` contiguous blocks and partitions only block `index` (launch reserve + bounded pool, as before, inside the block). If a block would be under the existing 4-core split threshold, it keeps the whole mask and warns that the listeners overlap, i.e. the previous behaviour.
- `managers/scheduler.py` (`maybe_init_rust_server`): call the collective next to `gather_server_endpoints` (every serving rank) and pass the result to `launch`. Like `gather_server_endpoints`, an elastic-EP joiner stays out of the collective (the serving ranks never re-enter it) and keeps `(0, 1)`.
- Listeners whose masks already differ (per-rank affinity such as `SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY`, one listener per NUMA node) get `count == 1` and are partitioned exactly as before.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: thread placement only.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The bug was measured on v0.5.21 (where the scheduler thread was still pinned too), GLM-5.3 W4AFP8, TP8/DPA8/EP8, EAGLE, HiCache, 8xH200, same engine flags behind sgl-model-gateway 0.3.2 `cache_aware`, agentic trace workload at concurrency 64 for 900 s: Python frontend 859 requests / 475.5 output tok/s / 38.8 ms per decoded token (median), Rust frontend 179 requests / 96.6 tok/s / 217 ms. The end-to-end A/B of this fix, backported onto the same v0.5.21 deployment, is in the first comment below (+13% output tok/s and -15% decode time per token over a #47161-only baseline; back to the Python frontend's speed).

Unit tests (CPU), run locally with this branch on `PYTHONPATH`:

- `test/registered/unit/multimodal/rust/shared/test_partition_cores.py`: 8 passed. The two new regression cases (8 listeners on one 128-core mask; two sockets with 4 listeners each plus a non-listener rank) fail with the block split disabled.
- `test/registered/unit/multimodal/rust/shared/test_rust_server_extension.py`: 13 passed, including the new `test_gather_frontend_cpu_share_counts_only_listeners_on_this_mask` (also covers the elastic-EP joiner skip).
- `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_rust_server_dp_ports.py`: 50 passed; `test_listener_rank_installs_the_sigterm_drain` now also checks that every rank joins the CPU-share gather and a listener launches with its share.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass.

title: [Fix] PP: record received proxy tensors on the forward stream
author: Phoenix3334
body:
<!-- editorial-summary-20261107 -->
## Summary

**Fixes #47613.** In asynchronous PP decode, proxy tensors received on a communication stream may be consumed later on the forward stream. When the previous Python reference is dropped before the queued forward uses the data, the CUDA caching allocator can reuse the receive storage and corrupt model outputs. This was observed as long token-0 runs at `--pp-async-batch-depth > pp_size / 2`.

## Changes

- In `_pp_launch_batch`, call `record_stream(self.forward_stream)` for each non-CPU proxy tensor before `run_batch`, protecting storage until the forward stream has finished using it.
- Update the existing idle-counter fixture to return `None` for the simulated first PP stage.
- No global synchronization or new execution-order barrier is introduced: **`record_stream` records allocator lifetime, not stream ordering**.

## Validation

Kimi-K3, 8×B300, fake PD transfer; affected requests were identified by ≥20 consecutive token-0 outputs.

| PP/TP shape | Async depth | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| PP2 × TP4 | 2 | 51/192 | **0/192** |
| PP2 × TP4 | 3 | 98/192 | **0/192** |
| PP2 × TP4 + DCP4 | 2 | 59/192 | **0/192** |
| PP4 × TP2 | 3 | 6/192 | **0/192** |
| PP4 × TP2 | 4 | 19/192 | **0/192** |

Receive-vs-forward checksums mismatched in the unfixed runs (76 and 378 of ~7,500 comparisons), but not in the fixed runs. A later reported exact-fix comparison and dedicated-communication-stream experiments are documented in the archive below; those evidence groups are **not interchangeable**.

Existing 4×H100 PP GPU tests (2 compatibility + 6 speculative tests), and prior-head Base/AMD CI passed. The mocked-only `record_stream` unit test was removed in review because it could not reproduce allocator reuse.

## Scope and limitations

This is a correctness/lifetime fix, **not a performance optimization**. Historical 8×B300 experiments used v0.5.22 and fake transfer; real two-node PD, all PP event-loop combinations, and full post-merge GPU runtime coverage were not established. Historical CI passes are explicitly scoped to the corresponding tested heads.

Evidence: [Issue #47613](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/47613), [review discussion](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47614#issuecomment-6567604516), and the archived runs below.

<details>
<summary>Historical experiment matrices, CI runs and investigation notes (original PR body)</summary>

**Archive notice:** The sections below preserve the original investigation record, including earlier intermediate findings and CI statuses. The concise summary above states the final interpretation and validation boundaries.

---

## Motivation

Fixes #47613. With `--pp-async-batch-depth > pp_size / 2`, the PD decode loop returns runs of token 0 for many requests (Kimi-K3 PP2 × TP4 depth 2: 51–98 of 192).

A downstream stage gets its proxy tensors from `recv_tensor_dict`, which allocates them on another stream; the forward stream reads them later. `event_loop_pp_disagg_decode` drops the previous reference before posting the next recv. When enough forwards are queued, the allocator gives the next recv the same block and it overwrites data a queued forward has not read yet. Checksums taken right after the recv and right before the forward differ in 76 and 378 of ~7500 comparisons on two runs; with this change they never differ.

## Modifications

- `_pp_launch_batch`: before `run_batch`, call `record_stream(self.forward_stream)` on each non-CPU tensor in `pp_proxy_tensors`. Every PP event loop goes through `_pp_launch_batch`, so they share this fix location; runtime validation did not exercise every loop configuration; the first stage passes `None` and is unchanged.
- Existing idle-counter test: make the mocked proxy receive return `None` for the simulated rank-zero scheduler, matching the real receive path. A bare `Mock()` previously reached the new tensor iteration and caused a fixture `TypeError`.

- The earlier DCP CI fixture correction from mickqian’s [#47736](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47736), source commit `be43d568ca8115e173bd4b9f5d106a3060ae1f8b`, is now included in main and is no longer part of this PR's cumulative diff.

## Accuracy Tests

Kimi-K3, 8 × B300, fake transfer, C64 N=192, requests with ≥20 consecutive token 0:

| shape | depth | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| PP2 × TP4 | 2 | 51 | 0 |
| PP2 × TP4 | 3 | 98 | 0 |
| PP2 × TP4 + DCP4 | 2 | 59 | 0 |
| PP4 × TP2 | 3 | 6 | 0 |
| PP4 × TP2 | 4 | 19 | 0 |

A later validation report for this exact fix recorded PP2 × TP4 depth 2 and PP4 × TP2 depth 4 both 0/192, with 0 checksum mismatches in 7498 and 14499 comparisons, and PP2 × TP4 + DCP4 depth 2 at C384 N=3840 at 0/3840. The raw logs for that exact-fix rerun are not in the current local bundle; these figures are reported results, not independently rechecked here. The earlier fix runs and checksum comparisons above have retained local logs.

GSM8K (5-shot, 200 questions, non-PD, PP2 × TP4 + DCP4 depth 2): 0.985 before, 0.980 after.

### Additional validation: dedicated PP communication stream

Follow-up runs on 2026-10-31 used `SGLANG_PP_COMM_OVERLAP=1` on v0.5.22, Kimi-K3, 8 × B300, and fake PD. The server log confirmed `PP tensor communication overlap enabled on a dedicated CUDA stream`. Synthetic random-token prompts targeted 64,000 input tokens and 1,000 output tokens, with random range ratio 0. C is maximum request concurrency; N is the number of requests. The output check counted requests containing at least 20 consecutive token 0 (`!` for this tokenizer).

| shape | depth | C | N | affected requests, original | affected requests, fixed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| PP2 × TP4 | 2 | 64 | 192 | 73/192 | 0/192 |
| PP2 × TP4 | 3 | 64 | 192 | 109/192 | 0/192 |
| PP2 × TP4 + DCP4 | 2 | 64 | 192 | not run | 0/192 |
| PP2 × TP4 + DCP4 | 2 | 256 | 2560 | not run | 0/2560 |
| PP2 × TP4 + DCP4 | 2 | 384 | 3840 | not run | 0/3840 |

These runs used the earlier CUDA-equivalent fix: `record_stream(current_stream())` inside `forward_stream_ctx`, guarded by `tensor.is_cuda`. The submitted diff uses `self.forward_stream` and a non-CPU guard. This extends the output-level evidence to the dedicated communication-stream configuration; it is not an exact-diff rerun, a main runtime test, or real two-node PD validation. Checksum instrumentation was not enabled in these runs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

PP2 × TP4 + DCP4, depth 0, fake transfer, C384 N=3840, same node and session, runs in order:

| run | output tok/s | median TPOT |
|---|---:|---:|
| before | 3525.5 | 103.41 ms |
| after | 3507.0 | 104.04 ms |
| before | 3539.8 | 103.79 ms |

The patched run was 0.52–0.93% slower than the two baseline runs. This small sample does not establish statistical equivalence or zero overhead. With depth 2, the throughput reported before this change was inflated by the corrupted outputs.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit (all applicable hooks passed on both final PR files; repository-wide Ruff lint and formatting checks also passed on the updated base).
- [x] Validate with existing PP integration tests and B300 experiments; remove the mock-only CPU test as requested in review.
- [ ] Update documentation (N/A).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed results.

## Applicability to main

The lifetime-critical logic is the same in `release/v0.5.22` and main at `2f6e7f347526034a173424cad0e7a72a5fb61ad2`: the disaggregated decode loop clears `pp_proxy_tensors` before the next receive; `_pp_recv_proxy_tensors` wraps the received tensors without recording the forward stream; and `_pp_launch_batch` submits `run_batch` on the forward stream without recording those inputs. Main is therefore expected to be affected by the same allocator-lifetime race based on source comparison. The B300 runtime reproduction and fix validation were completed on v0.5.22; that B300 reproduction was not separately repeated on main. Upstream CPU and PP integration results are listed below. This comparison concerns the bug-relevant lifetime logic, not byte-for-byte identity of the entire scheduler file.

## Validation limits

The B300 GPU results above are historical reports from v0.5.22; upstream main-based CI results are listed below. PD tests used fake transfer; real two-node PD and ordinary PP at queue depths ≥3 remain untested. The token-0 feedback experiment does not independently exclude recurrent-state corruption.

Current preparation base: `768e56202b0ef523227fe8dc375937083194eccc`. Updated on 2026-11-02 in current head `9effc87527556ad4e8697b2e1de91bd2312d15c4`, merging main while preserving the PR commit history. The PP lifetime fix is unchanged; its explanatory comment is shortened to two lines. The DCP fixture correction from [#47736](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47736) is already present upstream and is no longer part of the cumulative PR diff.

On the previous head `6745437`, [Base CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41301682406) passed, including all 20 CPU shards and the GB300/B300 jobs; [AMD CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41301682373) also passed. Both requested PP GPU test files (`test_pp_parallel_compat.py`, 2 cases; `test_pp_spec.py`, 6 cases) [passed on 4×H100](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41291896395) at `1bd623e`. The production fix is unchanged from that run.

### Review cleanup (2026-11-02)

Per [BBuf’s request](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47614#issuecomment-6567604516), commit `b15b09e` deletes `test/registered/unit/managers/test_pp_proxy_record_stream.py`. It only checked mocked `record_stream` calls and ordering, and could not reproduce allocator reuse. The production fix, existing idle-counter fixture correction, and documented GPU evidence remain unchanged. The cleanup commit changes only that deletion (112 lines); no additional local CPU/GPU runs were performed.

The passing Base/AMD results above apply to the previous head, before the test deletion. [CI on the cleanup head](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41378151982) was triggered but stopped at the 120-minute per-user cooldown gate before tests executed. The logged previous accepted trigger is 2026-11-02 02:18:01 UTC; earliest retry under that cooldown is 04:18:01 UTC / 12:18:01 UTC+8.
