title: [Fix] hicache: keep the storage ack sequence on backend failures, stop workers in lockstep, fail the rank when a worker dies
author: xiezhq-hermann
body:
## Motivation

HiCache's four storage worker threads (prefetch query, prefetch IO, prefetch sync, backup) are started per rank in `HiCacheController._start_storage_threads` and nothing watched them. This PR is hardening for three situations that recent features opened up; none of them has a field report, and the symptom of the first is a silent freeze, which is why.

1. An exception could escape a worker and nobody noticed. The classic cache-mode transfer loop has nothing that can raise outside its inner per-batch guard, but the hybrid path (#20457 and its follow-ups) added call sites in front of and around it: the unified host layout lease taken around the whole transfer (poisoned on acquire, raising on release), the trailing sidecar chain (`_sync_trailing_keys`, `_resolve_sidecar_nonkv_derived_pool_transfers`) before the sidecar ack, and the trace initialisation of #37976 on dequeue. `prefetch_io_aux_func` ran `_page_transfer` under `try/finally` with no `except`, so an exception at one of those sites published the final ack and killed the thread. From then on the hit path kept allocating host bounces that only this thread's acks free: the host pool filled, hits parked forever, and under the default `timeout` policy requests kept being admitted with no L3 benefit; under `wait_complete` they never admitted. No log line said why, and on the hybrid controller the skipped sidecar ack also desynchronised this rank's ack sequence from its peers'. The response chosen here is to crash the rank: an escaping exception stays a rare event, keeping the worker alive by inventing the missing acks would hide it, and degrading to a detached state would make the ranks differ. Backend read failures (a sidecar read that raises, a hit query that raises) are a different matter: they are transient, they must leave the ack sequence intact by construction, and that is the first part below; an invariant violation in the controller's own bookkeeping (a sidecar key re-alignment that fails, a programming error) is not a backend failure and takes the crash path.
2. No rank could tell that one of its own workers had died. The MIN-counted drains in `check_hicache_events` simply stopped making progress on every rank.
3. Stopping could diverge across ranks and still called the backend. Flush and detach are gated on `is_fully_idle`, which checks `ongoing_prefetch`; a prefetch cut at admission (or mid-transfer by the stop policy) leaves that set while its IO worker still owes acks, so what a stop actually meets is an in-flight transfer. The IO worker kept issuing the remaining 128-page batch reads, the prefetch worker ran a live `_storage_hit_query` for every operation still queued, and the sync thread left its loop on the stop event with acks still coming: a peer already inside the completed-tokens collective for that ack position was orphaned, so one rank's stop hit the join bound and raised (`reset()` on a flush raised after the tree had already been wiped) while the peer's stop succeeded. The join was a fixed 10 s.

## Modifications

Three parts, no new collective, no new configuration knob (`STORAGE_STOP_JOIN_S` is a module constant).

**(a) Backend read failures keep the per-operation ack sequence by construction; invariant violations fail the rank.**

- The hybrid `_page_transfer_sidecar` keeps main's guard exactly where it was, around the backend read loop (`hybrid_cache_controller.py:1885-1906`): a sidecar read that raises publishes the sidecar ack with empty `pool_hits`, which the MIN in `_reduce_prefetch_ack` turns into zero hits on every pool for every rank; the acks each rank publishes for the operation (ceil(pages / 128) batch acks, the sidecar ack, `completed_req`) do not change. `_sync_trailing_keys` and `_resolve_sidecar_nonkv_derived_pool_transfers` stay outside the guard (`:1883-1884`): a failure there is an invariant violation, it propagates, the worker exits and part (b) fails the rank.
- `prefetch_thread_func` is restructured so everything after the dequeue (the `_on_prefetch_dequeue` hook stays in front) and before the hits reduce is inside one guard: a hit query that raises answers 0 hits and still joins `_sync_prefetch_hit_query` and publishes the operation (`cache_controller.py:1571-1608`).
- Nothing is invented on the other failures. An exception that escapes the transfer itself ends the IO worker as on main (`cache_controller.py:1479-1488` logs the request and re-raises); part (b) then fails the rank.

**(b) A dead worker fails its rank loudly in the next tick.**

- `HiCacheController` keeps explicit handles of the four workers it started (`None` in `__init__`, set by the single start helper `_start_storage_worker_threads`, `cache_controller.py:531-553`, used by both `_start_storage_threads` and the restart in `reset()`; each thread is started right after it is created, the IO worker before the sync thread that reads its handle; set back to `None` after a successful stop). Every worker runs through `_run_storage_worker` (`:555-564`): an exception that escapes the loop is recorded by thread name in `_storage_worker_failures` (reset when the workers start), logged with its traceback and re-raised. `dead_storage_workers()` (`:580-594`) returns the recorded failures always, plus, while the stop event is clear, any started worker that is no longer alive; a worker that merely finished while the event is set is not dead (a stop that hit its bound leaves the threads in the started set, and the retried stop joins them), a worker that crashed under the event is. `_storage_worker_threads()` skips a handle that was created but never started (`:566-578`), so a start failure cannot make every later stop raise from `join()`. The threads carry names (`hicache-prefetch`, `hicache-prefetch-io`, `hicache-prefetch-sync`, `hicache-backup`; the PP ticket thread is `hicache-pp-ticket`).
- `UnifiedRadixCache.check_hicache_events` calls `_raise_if_storage_workers_died` before anything else on the storage path (`unified_radix_cache.py:4216-4228`, call at `:4250-4251`, after the external-linker early return): `RuntimeError("HiCache storage worker thread(s) exited on this rank: <names>")`. `_stop_storage_threads` raises the same way after its joins when a failure is recorded (`cache_controller.py:639-647`), so a flush fails the rank there and a detach returns the error while the next tick raises. The check is rank-local on purpose: the rank that lost a worker exits in its own tick, and the peers follow through the engine teardown (the parent's SIGQUIT on this host, the NCCL watchdog elsewhere). No agreed word, so the tick's count row and the shm exchange are unchanged and there is no PP caveat.
- The PP ticket thread is deliberately outside the dead set (`hybrid_cache_controller.py:458-462`): on a flush PP0 stops it one relay step before PP1+ processes the same request, and PP1+'s copy exits on PP0's `None` ticket while PP1+ still ticks its current iteration, where the check would raise falsely. The existing `is_pp_prefetch_ready` check on the request path keeps covering that thread; its stop uses the same bounded join.

**(c) A stop drains in lockstep, without backend calls.**

- The IO worker runs until the stop event is set AND nothing more can arrive: `prefetch_buffer` is empty and no producer is alive (`_io_thread_should_run`, `cache_controller.py:1451-1462`; the base has no producer besides the scheduler, the hybrid controller's producer is its PP ticket thread, `hybrid_cache_controller.py:432-434`). Inside a transfer the stop event ends the backend reads the way termination does while every remaining batch ack still goes out carrying what completed (`cache_controller.py:1369-1374`); the hybrid sidecar read is skipped after the stop, its ack still published (`hybrid_cache_controller.py:1864-1871`). Those operations were dispatched by the scheduler's lockstep hit drain or by the ticket relay, so every rank publishes the acks of the same operations in the same order.
- The sync thread keeps reducing until the stop event is set and this rank's IO worker has exited with its queue consumed (`_sync_thread_should_run`, `cache_controller.py:1705-1714`; base loop `:1716-1718`, hybrid override `hybrid_cache_controller.py:2243-2245`): an ack it still owes is one the peers' sync threads reduce too, so no rank is left alone inside the completed-tokens collective.
- In buffer_only PP > 1 the ticket thread is a producer that may still be inside a backend query or the PP-wide hits reduce when the stop arrives. After the stop event it answers each ticket as a miss, without a backend query or a host allocation, but still runs that reduce so the stages stay paired (`hybrid_cache_controller.py:1544-1549`); `_stop_pp_prefetch_thread` sets the stop event itself before queueing the `None` ticket and joining (`:436-449`), so the flush path (`reset()` stops the ticket thread before the workers) orders the same way as detach.
- The prefetch worker answers every operation still queued as a miss without a backend call but still runs the hits reduce and publishes it (`cache_controller.py:1589`); a rank whose worker queried before it saw the stop is outvoted by the MIN. The backup worker stops issuing batches after the stop event and acks with what completed, in the base loop (`cache_controller.py:1660`) and in both hybrid loops, the KV batches (`hybrid_cache_controller.py:1943-1945`) and the sidecar chain groups (`:2002-2004`), which the production hybrid backup runs instead of the base loop. The hybrid `_stop_storage_threads` sets the stop event before joining the PP ticket thread (`:451-456`), so the four workers stop calling the backend even when that join hits its bound.
- The join bound is `STORAGE_STOP_JOIN_S = 60.0` (`cache_controller.py:279`), one budget for all four threads (`_join_storage_threads`, `:596-600`); at the bound `_stop_storage_threads` logs the threads still running and raises as before (`:630-638`). 60 s is one slow backend call: after the stop event a worker only finishes the call it is already inside, and the slowest single call we tolerate (a 128-page batch get/set against a stalled remote backend with the backends' own timeouts) sits well under a minute; a worker still inside a call after that is stuck, and the raise is the right outcome.

Known limits. A detach whose stop hit the bound leaves the rank attached with the stop event set, as on main: retry the detach or restart the engine; the tick does not report its workers as dead while the event is set (a worker that crashed is reported regardless). The PP ticket thread's join uses the same 60 s budget; a ticket join that hits the bound raises with the stop event already set, so the four workers issue no backend call meanwhile. A one-rank detach failure leaves the ranks diverged (that rank keeps `enable_storage`), also as on main; agreeing the detach outcome before flipping the flag is a separate change.

Tests adapted because the contract they drive changed: `test_pp_prefetch_ticket.py` drives the IO worker by counting completed transfers instead of counting `storage_stop_event.is_set()` calls (the transfer now consults the event per batch), its controller stub carries `prefetch_io_aux_thread`, and it gains the post-stop ticket case below; the controller stubs of `test_hicache_controller_request_id_unit.py` and `test_hybrid_pool_assembler.py` (`storage_stop_event`), `test_hicache_pp_sync_drain.py` (`dead_storage_workers`) and `test_hicache_storage_registration_hook.py` (the four thread attributes and `_storage_worker_failures`) gain what the real controller always has.

**Rebase notes (2026-11-05).** Rebased on main `9b6c796151`. Two conflicts resolved: (1) `cache_controller.py`, `prefetch_thread_func`: upstream #37976 added the `_on_prefetch_dequeue(operation)` hook right after the dequeue; it is kept at the same place in the restructured loop (after the `None` check, before the guarded query). (2) `test/registered/hicache/test_hicache_storage_file_backend.py` CI registration: upstream #48134 moved the AMD run to suite `extra-a-test-2-gpu-large-amd` and set est_time 1100; this PR keeps that suite and its own est_time bumps for the added random-delay class (cuda 160 -> 500, amd 1100 -> 1360).

**Rebase notes (2026-11-09).** Rebased on main `9fe1dbb8058` without conflicts. The test stubs follow #48013 (host-pool schema for the sidecar-ack reduce, string pool names: `_host_pool_schemas = []` and an `entry_map` on the host-pool stub). After the pre-merge review the scope was reduced to what is described above: the earlier cross-rank liveness word in the tick's count row (shm width 8 -> 9) is replaced by the rank-local check, the ack-replay machinery for a transfer that raised is dropped in favour of failing the rank (with the failure recorded so a crash under a pending stop is still reported), the stop-time progress diagnostics are dropped, the sidecar guard went back to main's placement, and the stop path gained the lockstep drain of (c), the ticket-producer rule and the per-batch stop in the hybrid backup (the review showed one rank's stop could hit the bound while the peer's succeeded).

**Rebase notes (2026-11-10).** Rebased on main `ae1347a5c36` (which carries the `test_rust_server_crash_dump` fix #49461 that failed shard 7 of the previous run) without conflicts. One test-only addition: the two-rank fixture of `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_storage_prefetch_lifecycle.py` (merged with #47620 after the previous base) builds the controller with `__new__` and now also sets `_storage_worker_failures = {}`, the record this PR's tick reads; the 19 cases of that file, the 19 liveness cases, the two GPU suites (302 / 341) and the ten unit files that touch the storage-worker lifecycle pass on the rebased tree.

## Accuracy Tests

New `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_storage_worker_liveness.py` (CPU, `register_cpu_ci`), 19 tests, two-rank gloo where rank behaviour matters:

- `test_backend_failures_keep_the_ack_sequence`: a healthy sidecar read agrees the window on both ranks; on rank 1 the sidecar read raises for the next operation and both ranks drain `[batch 4 tokens, sidecar zero hits on every pool, completed_req]`, the IO worker staying up; then rank 1's hit query raises and both ranks publish the operation with zero hits.
- `test_stop_answers_the_backlog_without_backend_calls`: three queued queries, rank 1 stopped before its first query and rank 0 stopped inside it; both ranks publish all three as misses, the fake backend saw one call on rank 0 and none on rank 1.
- `test_stop_waits_for_the_ticket_producer`: hybrid controller on a PP1+ stage with a live `hicache-pp-ticket` thread that delivers operation T after the stop event; rank 0's IO worker is idle at the stop, rank 1's inside W; both stops return inside the bound, no read after the event, and both ranks drain the same acks (W at one page, T at zero, each with `completed_req`). With the producer rule reverted rank 0's IO worker exits before T and rank 1's stop hits the bound.
- `test_worker_death_under_the_stop_event_fails_both_stops_in_bound`: with the stop event set, rank 1's transfer raises a programming error; rank 1's stop raises naming `hicache-prefetch-io (RuntimeError('bad operation'))`, rank 0's sync thread is left alone in the reduce and its stop raises at the (patched) bound: both ranks are out within the bound instead of one returning while the other hangs.
- `test_stop_drains_in_flight_transfers_on_every_rank`: at the stop event rank 0's IO worker is inside operation X's first batch and rank 1's inside operation W's first batch with X still queued; both stops succeed well inside the bound, no backend read is issued after the event on either rank (rank 0 read W's three batches and X's first, rank 1 W's first only), rank 1 takes the queued X and acks it, and both ranks drain the same eight acks: W at one page (rank 1's one read, by the MIN), X at zero, each followed by `completed_req`.
- `test_dead_worker_fails_the_rank_in_its_tick`: the tick check passes with no started workers and with live ones, raises naming a finished `hicache-prefetch-io`, passes again for a worker finishing under a pending stop, and raises for a recorded crash under that stop.
- `test_escaping_transfer_failure_kills_the_worker_and_the_rank_raises`: the host layout lease raises on acquire; the IO worker exits (logged), only main's `completed_req` is published, `dead_storage_workers()` names the worker, the tick check raises and so does the stop, naming the worker and the error.
- `test_invariant_violation_before_the_sidecar_ack_kills_the_worker`: `_sync_trailing_keys` raising is not a backend failure: it propagates, the IO worker exits, the tick and the stop raise naming `hicache-prefetch-io (AssertionError(...))`.
- `test_tick_calls_the_dead_worker_check_before_the_drain`: `check_hicache_events` on a cache whose controller has a dead worker raises before `_drain_async_work`; with the stop event set the tick proceeds past the check.
- `test_backup_stops_issuing_batches_after_stop_and_acks_progress`: the stop event set during batch 1 of 3 stops further writes; the ack carries `completed_tokens` of the one batch.
- `test_hybrid_backup_stops_issuing_batches_after_stop`: the hybrid KV loop writes one batch and stops; the sidecar loop writes the first of two trailing-chain groups and stops.
- `test_transfer_stops_reading_after_stop_but_acks_every_batch`: the stop event set inside batch 1 of 3 stops the backend reads, the three batch acks still go out at one page; a hybrid sidecar read under the stop is skipped and its ack published with no hits.
- `test_sync_thread_drains_the_acks_the_io_worker_still_owes` and `test_hybrid_sync_thread_drains_the_acks_the_io_worker_still_owes`: with the stop event already set, the base and the hybrid sync thread stay until the IO worker has published its two acks and exited, then exit.
- `test_stop_join_bound_is_one_budget_for_all_workers`: two stuck workers, the stop raises after one budget (0.4 s patched, elapsed < 0.7 s), not one per thread.
- `test_unstarted_worker_handles_are_not_counted`: a handle created but never started is neither in the started set nor dead, and the stop ignores it.
- `test_stop_raises_at_the_bound_naming_the_stuck_workers`: with the bound patched to 0.3 s, a stuck `hicache-backup` produces the error log naming it and the raise; the thread stays in the started set and is not reported dead while the event is set; the retried stop, which meets it finishing, succeeds and empties the set.
- `test_hybrid_stop_sets_the_event_before_the_ticket_join`: a PP ticket thread that does not stop within the bound still leaves the stop event set; the retried stop succeeds.
- `test_hybrid_liveness_set_excludes_the_pp_ticket_thread`: a finished `hicache-pp-ticket` thread on a hybrid controller leaves the dead set empty.

`test_pp_prefetch_ticket.py` gains `test_stop_event_answers_tickets_as_misses_but_still_reduces`: a ticket delivered after the stop event issues no backend query and no host allocation, runs its hits reduce once, and reaches `prefetch_buffer` terminated at zero hits.

title: [Fix] hicache: vote the prefetch timeout once per tick, not per admission poll
author: xiezhq-hermann
body:
## Motivation

Under `--hicache-storage-prefetch-policy timeout` (the default) the per-request deadline verdict is agreed by a collective issued from inside the admission loop: `check_prefetch_progress` calls `_can_terminate_prefetch`, which on main does one `_all_reduce(MAX)` per call (`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py:2480-2490` on `1ad0149814`). The scheduler issues that call once per waiting request with a live prefetch per scheduling pass (`python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:4543` on `b50d439494`), and the loop's exits around it (`batch_is_full` from `get_num_allocatable_reqs`, `scheduler.py:4406-4411` and `4528-4540` on `b50d439494`) are evaluated by each rank on its own. That is the shape reported in #30760 (TP=4, no PP): one rank examined one more candidate than its peers before its own `batch_is_full` tripped, called the collective one more time, and waited in it forever while the others had moved on to `recv_requests`. #44614 centralized the per-request budget (`_StoragePrefetchWait`, started at the first blocked poll, `_prefetch_deadline_expired`, `_mark_prefetch_deadline_expired`) but left the vote in the poll; #36425 had moved the vote into `_can_terminate_prefetch`; #33029 and #44340 (both closed, not merged) proposed a once-per-tick vote, and this PR reuses that part of #44340.

This PR removes the per-poll collective that #30760 reported and makes the remaining rank-consistency premise (every rank polls the same requests) fail loud in the same tick on every rank instead of hanging. Even when the counts match, the per-poll vote costs one gloo all_reduce per waiting request per pass (prior measurements: roughly 60-80 us at TP2 and 0.6-0.9 ms at TP8), paid for every request parked behind a slow storage lookup.

## Modifications

All in `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py`; no new flags, no new collective.

- `_vote_prefetch_deadlines` (lines 2812-2840) runs once per scheduler tick from `check_hicache_events`, after the storage drain, under storage only (lines 4319-4321). It packs one int per live prefetch, in `ongoing_prefetch` insertion order, evaluated on PP rank 0 with the existing `_prefetch_deadline_expired` (a wait that has not started yet contributes 0), does ONE `_all_reduce(MAX)` (line 2836: TP MAX on PP0, relayed along PP by `_pp_sync`, lines 428-462 (`_all_reduce` and `_pp_sync`)), and for every 1 calls the existing `_mark_prefetch_deadline_expired` and `cache_controller.terminate_prefetch` (lines 2839-2840), so every rank records the same verdict in the same tick and the transfer worker and the hit drain stop spending on the cut span at once (the drain already handles a terminated operation: `is_terminated()` at lines 3604 and 3732, with the `deadline` reason at 3737 and no retry at 3746). With no live prefetch no rank issues a collective. The vote runs only under policy `timeout`; `best_effort` and `wait_complete` never vote.
- `_can_terminate_prefetch` under `timeout` (lines 2802-2809) returns the recorded verdict (`wait.expired`) and issues no collective. It keeps `@rank_consensus(same_results=True)`: the verdict is rank-agreed by the vote. Since the vote also terminates, a poll on an expired operation normally takes the existing `is_terminated()` path (line 2953); retirement (`terminate_prefetch`, the `deadline` reason, `revoke_pending_prefetch` / `_handle_prefetch_result`, lines 2960-2969) is unchanged and still happens at the poll, or at the lockstep drain when the hit or the final ack lands first (lines 3732-3749 and 3770-3789). A parked hit cut by the vote is finished with the `deadline` reason before its revoke (lines 3604-3608), as the poll would.
- `check_prefetch_progress` is now collective-free for all three policies: `best_effort` returns True (line 2797), `wait_complete` returns False (line 2801), `timeout` reads the verdict (line 2809). The only collective reachable from an admission poll is the PP ticket path's own MAX in `_check_pp_prefetch_progress` (line 2876), left as is. The remaining `_all_reduce*` call sites in the file are the tick's own syncs (`_sync_hicache_ready_counts` lines 4030/4032, `writing_check`, `loading_check`, the linker round), the synchronous hit query helper (line 2573) and `drain_storage_control_queues`, which only the GPU test kits call.
- Rank consistency of the vote's shape, made fail-loud: `ongoing_prefetch` is filled by `prefetch_from_storage` (`@rank_consensus`, line 2580) and emptied by the lockstep drain and by the admission polls. The polls retire per rank, so the number and length of the packed vote would depend on the premise that every rank polls the same requests (#30760's maintainer position: `get_num_allocatable_reqs`, hence the poll sequence, is identical across TP ranks). `_hicache_sync_digest` (lines 2842-2860) folds the live prefetch set (rids and attempt ids in insertion order, crc32) into the digest the ready-count MIN sync already carries as `[digest, -digest]` (line 4004; asserts at 4012-4015 for the shm path and 4035-4038 for the gloo path, which also covers PP stages through the relay). A divergent set therefore raises on every rank at the start of the next tick, before any vote is issued, instead of one rank blocking in a vote its peer never issues or the two voting on tensors of different length. The row width is unchanged, so the shm fast path (8-slot table) is unaffected; the fold is active only when the vote would read the dict (storage on, policy `timeout`, non-empty). Main is exposed to the same premise one step earlier (the poll's own collective) and hangs; other policies keep main's behavior.
- In PP ticket mode (`buffer_only`, PP > 1) no entry is ever kept in `ongoing_prefetch`: PP > 0 returns at line 2603 (`get_prefetch_submission` returns an empty submission, `hybrid_cache_controller.py:1245` on `9b6c796151`) and PP0 returns at line 2735 (`submit_prefetch` returns `decision=True`, `hybrid_cache_controller.py:1316` on `9b6c796151`), so the vote never runs there and the PP relay of `_all_reduce` is only exercised in cache-mode PP.

Behavior changes to be aware of: a request whose budget ran out is cut on every rank at the next tick's vote instead of at its own poll, so the cut can land up to one tick later than before; between the vote and the poll the operation is terminated but still listed, so a hit or final ack landing in that window is settled by the drain (same outcome accounting path as a controller-terminated query: `revoked` outcome plus `deadline` reason) rather than by the poll.

Companion note for downstream forks that subclass the tick (prod_inference's Meta subclass runs its own packed buffer-mode vote and per-poll agreement before calling `super().check_hicache_events()`): after this change that subclass should either override `_vote_prefetch_deadlines` to a no-op in buffer mode or drop its own vote in favor of this one, to avoid two packed collectives per tick; both feed the same `_mark_prefetch_deadline_expired` / `wait.expired` state, so they agree either way.

**Rebase notes (2026-11-05).** Rebased on main `9b6c796151` without conflicts; no code change. The two `base-a-test-cpu` failures on the previous CI run (`test_decode_queue_cleanup.py`, `test_prefill_cuda_graph_dcp.py`) were main's and are fixed upstream by #47758 and #47736.

**Rebase notes (2026-11-09).** Rebased on main `9fe1dbb8058` without conflicts; no code change (the commit is byte-identical to the previous revision). #30760 was closed on 2026-11-04 by the stale bot for inactivity, not by a fix: the per-poll `_all_reduce(MAX)` in `_can_terminate_prefetch` is still on main `9fe1dbb8058`, so this PR still addresses it, and the issue should be reopened or this PR referenced as its fix. Scope: the legacy `HiRadixCache`, whose inline per-poll all_reduce appears in #30760's stack trace, no longer exists on main (removed by #40787), so `UnifiedRadixCache` is the only cache this PR needs to cover. Related: #38284 attacks the same admission-poll collective from the other side, adding a dummy `_all_reduce(MAX)` on the `request not in ongoing_prefetch` path so that ranks whose membership differs still enter the per-poll vote; it also patches the legacy `HiRadixCache`, and its diff no longer applies to main. This PR removes the per-poll vote altogether under `timeout`, so no collective is left on the poll path for a membership mismatch to desynchronize, and a genuine divergence of the live prefetch set is caught by the digest assertion in the next tick's ready-count sync on every rank at once instead of hanging. If this PR lands, the #38284 dummy should not be added on top of it: with no collective in the in-set poll, a collective on the not-in-set poll would recreate the asymmetry it was meant to remove.

## Accuracy Tests

No model-output change: the policy's verdict is the same `_prefetch_deadline_expired` evaluation, agreed by the same MAX, read by the same poll.

CPU unit tests, `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_storage_prefetch_lifecycle.py`, `TestStoragePrefetchTimeout` (line 466):

- `test_polls_never_reduce_and_the_tick_votes_once` (line 467): five live prefetches, four polled in one pass issue 0 collectives; the tick issues exactly one MAX over `[0,0,0,0,0]`; at a time long past the budget the four polls still return False and issue nothing, the next tick votes `[1,1,1,1,0]` (the never-polled request's wait never started), the four voted operations are terminated by the tick and the parked one is not, every polled request is then cut by its poll with no retry armed; `best_effort`, `wait_complete` and an empty `ongoing_prefetch` issue no collective.
- `test_expiry_is_agreed_even_before_a_peer_starts_waiting` (line 521, two-rank gloo, `_two_rank_prefetch_deadline` line 272): only rank 0 started the wait and only its clock ran out; rank 0 polls (returns False, no collective) while rank 1 does not poll; the tick marks the operation expired on both ranks with one collective each; the poll on both returns True; neither rank re-issues the prefetch. Adapted from main's version, which asserted that the poll itself returned True on both ranks: that assertion pinned the per-poll vote this PR removes, so the agreement is now asserted after the tick, and the polls are asserted not to reduce.
- `test_uneven_polls_before_a_verdict_issue_no_collective` (line 532, two-rank gloo, `_two_rank_uneven_polls` line 309): #30760's trigger before any verdict; both ranks start two waits, then rank 0 polls two requests and rank 1 one; no collective is issued by the polls, the tick votes `[1,1]` once on each rank, and both ranks retire both requests with the same verdicts. Against the old per-poll vote (main's `_can_terminate_prefetch` body patched in) it fails at its first uneven poll, which votes and cuts by itself.
- `test_divergent_live_prefetch_sets_raise_on_every_rank_in_the_same_tick` (line 542, two-rank gloo, `_two_rank_divergent_live_sets` line 346): #30760's shape after a verdict; after an agreed `[1,1]` vote rank 0 polls two requests and rank 1 one, so the live sets differ by one entry; the next tick's ready-count sync raises the digest assertion on both ranks (checked with `all_gather_object`), and the sequence of collectives is identical on both (`MIN, MAX, MIN`: no vote was issued with mismatched lengths). With the fold removed from `_hicache_sync_digest` (scratch negative control) the same worker fails differently: rank 0 issues no vote and the peer waits alone in its one-element MAX until the gloo timeout (`Timed out waiting 30000ms for send operation to complete`).
- The CPU fixtures these cases run the tick on (`_arm_tick`, line 226) also pre-set storage-worker state (`storage_stop_event`, the worker thread handles, `storage_workers_alive`) and backup-retry state (`_host_capacity_backup_retries`, `_backup_write_specs`) that nothing on main `9fe1dbb8058` reads on the tick path (the controller's own worker loops read `storage_stop_event`, and the fixtures start none); the sibling PRs of this stack (storage-worker liveness, backup retry) read them from the tick, so the lines are inert here and keep the fixtures valid with those PRs applied.
- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_pp_sync_drain.py`: `test_pp_relays_the_deadline_vote_after_the_counts` (line 90) runs the tick on a cache-mode PP0 and a PP1 stage, each with one live prefetch: PP0 reads its own clock, issues the counts (8-slot MIN) and then the vote `[1]` (MAX), marks and terminates; PP1 contributes `[0]`, never evaluates `_prefetch_deadline_expired`, receives `[1]` second on the same path and marks and terminates the same way. The fixture (lines 32-35) now carries `prefetch_stop_policy` and an empty `ongoing_prefetch`; the two existing cases are unchanged, and the buffer-mode follower's `_all_reduce.assert_not_called()` now also pins that an empty vote issues nothing.
- `test/registered/unit/managers/scheduler_components/test_shm_tag_exchange.py`: the `_hicache_tp_rank` fixture (lines 54-55) now carries `prefetch_stop_policy` (`wait_complete`) and an empty `ongoing_prefetch`, which `_hicache_sync_digest` reads inside the `_sync_hicache_ready_counts` the cases drive directly; the three cases are unchanged (the fold is inactive under `wait_complete`, so the 8/9/10-value rows take the same shm or gloo path as before).

Results on the development box (`python -m unittest`, on the committed tree `dd2c7e650c3` rebased on `9fe1dbb8058`; CPU unless stated):

- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_storage_prefetch_lifecycle.py`: Ran 19 tests in 41.330s, OK (main: 16).
- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_pp_sync_drain.py`: Ran 3 tests, OK (main: 2). `test/registered/unit/managers/scheduler_components/test_shm_tag_exchange.py`: Ran 3 tests in 24.746s, OK. `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_pp_prefetch_ticket.py`: Ran 18 tests, OK. `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_prefill_result_polling.py`: Ran 18 tests, OK.
- GPU, one NVIDIA B200 (CUDA 13.0): `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache/test_unified_radix_cache_storage.py`: Ran 302 tests in 38.763s, OK (skipped=63); `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache/test_unified_radix_cache_hicache.py`: Ran 341 tests in 14.611s, OK (skipped=46); both identical on untouched main `9fe1dbb8058`.
- Every `base-a-test-cpu`-registered file under `test/registered/unit/{mem_cache,managers,disaggregation}` (320 files), run as a script: no failure that untouched main does not also have in this environment.
- pre-commit clean on the changed files.
- Previous CI round on this PR (base `9b6c796151`, head `f11656d98e`, run 42136241276): success on attempt 2; attempt 1 was cancelled by the repository's fail-fast after an infrastructure failure (uv cache lock timeout on a shared runner).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Collectives per scheduling pass with N waiting requests under `timeout`: main 1 (ready-count sync) + N; this PR 2 (ready-count sync + one packed vote), 1 when no prefetch is live. The digest fold adds a crc32 over the live rids per tick on every rank (no extra slot, no extra collective). Not re-measured on GPU for this revision; the per-request gloo cost quoted in Motivation (60-80 us at TP2, 0.6-0.9 ms at TP8) is a prior measurement, not one from this revision.

Not run: GPU serving, PP > 1 end to end, PD disaggregation, mooncake/hf3fs/nixl backends; the two GPU unit suites above (one NVIDIA B200, CUDA 13.0) are the only GPU evidence. The repository CI re-runs on push.

title: [Fix] hicache: settle storage backups at the rank-agreed written prefix
author: xiezhq-hermann
body:
## Motivation

Addresses the storage-write leg of #39444.

A HiCache storage backup is written in 128-page batches. When a batch fails, `HiCacheController._page_backup` stops and the operation is acked with `completed_tokens` short of the request (`python/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py:1513-1533` on `b50d439494`). The tree's ack drain then treated the operation as complete: in buffer mode `BufferModePipeline.finish_storage_write_ack` fed existence beliefs for every key of the write and freed the staging; in cache mode `_drain_backup` released the node's host lock. The unwritten tail was believed stored, nothing re-wrote it, and a later prefetch of that prefix stopped at the failed batch. Issue #39444 describes this on both host memory modes.

Why the fix has to be rank-agreed: backup submission and acks have no collective of their own; the drain pairs operations by position across ranks after a MIN of the ack-queue sizes (`_sync_hicache_ready_counts` / `_drain_queue`), and the write-through trigger reads each rank's own tree state. A storage write can fail on one rank only (each rank writes its own KV shard; with replicated MLA KV only the writer rank writes at all). If every rank settled from its own `completed_tokens`, their beliefs would differ, the write-through trigger would fire on some ranks and not others, and the positional ack pairing would desync for good.

Scope, chosen deliberately small: this is a hit-rate problem, not a reliability one, so the PR does one thing. At the drain, every rank agrees the written prefix of each acked backup with one packed MIN, and settles its beliefs truthfully from that prefix. The unwritten tail is not retried: it is left un-backed and un-marked, so the next write-through through the path writes it (in cache mode, the next backup of the node after its host copy cycles). There is no retry state machine and no handling of host-staging allocation failures (main's behaviour stays: such a backup is dropped and the node stays device-only until its next hit). The collective runs only on drains that acked backups, which is also when the information exists.

Relation to other PRs: #39701 (open; its head still patches the removed `hiradix_cache.py`, and GitHub reports it as conflicting with main) retries a failed batch inside the backup worker (three attempts with 0.1 s and 0.2 s backoff), marks `StorageOperation.backup_failed` and counts `sglang:hicache_backup_failed_tokens_total`, while the ack drain keeps settling rank-locally, so after a terminal failure every rank still believes the whole span stored. This PR leaves the worker unchanged and settles at the drain; the two are complementary (worker-level transient backoff versus rank-agreed settlement), and the drain here reads only `operation.id` and `completed_tokens`, so #39701's worker changes can land underneath after a rebase. The one overlap to resolve is the metric: the counter here is `sglang:hicache_storage_backup_failed_tokens_total`, incremented once per settlement for the tokens that were not written, which differs from #39701's per-ack rank-local count, so only one of the two should remain if both merge. #38316 proposed an all_reduce of `completed_tokens` per operation at the drain; its review found that MLA `backup_skip` ranks report 0, which a MIN would turn into a zero verdict for every write. This PR reduces once per drain, not per operation, and makes non-writer ranks vote the requested length.

## Modifications

Agreed written prefix, once per drain.

- The drain reads nothing from an acked operation except `id` and `completed_tokens`, which every controller provides (a native controller's operation exposes no more). The requested KV span comes from a scheduler-side record: cache mode keeps the requested token count per operation id (`_backup_requested_tokens`, `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py:515-518`), set when `write_backup_storage` submits (`2523-2525`) and cleared with the backups at reset and detach (`unified_cache/storage_attachment.py:443`); buffer mode reads it from its `_UnifiedBufferBackupEntry` (`_backup_requested_tokens_of`, `unified_radix_cache.py:3847-3856`). A write with no KV pages (an aux-pool-only buffer intent) has no record and settles whole, as today.
- `_drain_backup` (`unified_radix_cache.py:3755-3800`) collects the `n_backup` acked operations, computes each rank's written prefix (`min(completed_tokens, requested)`), MIN-reduces the packed vector once through `_all_reduce_storage_drain` (`3784-3786`, `3837-3845`: the same reduction scope as the count sync, every TP rank of each PP stage in buffer_only mode, else PP0's TP verdict propagated along PP), checks that the agreed value is a page-aligned prefix of the request (raising on every rank in the same tick otherwise, `3788-3792`), and settles every operation through `_finish_backup_ack` (`3858-3912`). `n_backup` is already the agreed count, so the tensor has the same shape on every rank and every rank enters or skips the collective together; the local detach drain (`drain_storage_control_queues_local`, `n_backup=None`) enters no collective and settles from its own count.
- A rank that is not the KV storage writer (`cache_controller.backup_skip`, replicated MLA KV written by one TP rank) votes the requested span (`3766-3771`): its `completed_tokens` carries no KV evidence, so the MIN is the writer's prefix and non-writers never look like failures. Its own rank-sharded sidecars (Mamba/draft on skip ranks) are written whole or logged by the hybrid controller (`hybrid_cache/hybrid_cache_controller.py:1984-1992`).

Truthful settlement.

- Buffer mode: `BufferModePipeline.finish_storage_write_ack` takes the agreed `written_pages` and feeds beliefs only for `keys[:written_pages]` of every pool the write carried (`buffer_mode/pipeline.py:1212-1232`; a KV write's pools all share the KV key list), drops the in-flight marks for the whole span and frees the staging. The tail is therefore neither believed nor in flight, and the next write-through piece that covers it writes it (`enqueue_backup_intent` plans against `covered()`).
- Cache mode: the host lock is released as before. The tree has no per-node "stored in L3" flag in cache mode (`build_storage_backup_spec` only requires the host backup), so there is no belief to correct; the span is sent again by the existing write-through cycle when the node's host copy is evicted and the node is hit again.
- A shortfall is logged once (`3892-3898`) and counted in `sglang:hicache_storage_backup_failed_tokens_total` (`observability/metrics_collector.py:2375-2382, 2473-2477`); `backuped_tokens` logs what this rank wrote of the agreed prefix (`3899-3912`). A stale ack whose write was already dropped by reset or detach settles silently and is not counted.

Compatibility with controller and tree-core subclasses.

- `ongoing_backup` keeps its `dict[int, tuple[NodeId, DecLockRefParams]]` shape; the requested count lives in a separate dict. No abstract method is added to `UnifiedTreeCoreInterface`. `StorageOperation` is unchanged. A controller that pumps completions on the scheduler thread needs only `id` and `completed_tokens` on its operation objects and `backup_skip`.

No new configuration knob.

**Rebase notes (2026-11-05).** Rebased on main `9b6c796151` without conflicts; the only textual change was the `ComponentType` import path in the new test (`sglang.srt.mem_cache.unified_cache.component_type`), required by the new upstream pre-commit hook `check-indirect-imports` (#47990). The two `base-a-test-cpu` failures seen on the previous CI run were main's and are fixed upstream by #47758 and #47736. The `call-multimodal-gen-tests` lanes run on this PR only because it touches `observability/metrics_collector.py`; their failures reproduce on main's own runs of the same workflow. A local sweep of every `base-a-test-cpu` file caught `test_mamba_path_state_cap.py::test_backup_retry_after_mamba_cap_skips_tombstoned_state` against the host-capacity park this PR carried at the time (its device lock kept the Mamba path-state cap from tombstoning the unbacked ancestor); that park was first made lock-free and has since been removed altogether (see the scope note below), and the test passes as on main.

**Rebase notes (2026-11-10).** Rebased on main `ae1347a5c36` (which carries the `test_rust_server_crash_dump` fix #49461 that failed shard 7 of the previous run) without conflicts and without changes; the 7 settlement cases, the two GPU suites (302 / 341) and #47620's `test_storage_prefetch_lifecycle.py` (19 cases) pass on the rebased tree.

**Rebase notes (2026-11-09).** Rebased on main `9fe1dbb8058` without conflicts. Scope reduced after review: the previous revision also re-enqueued the unwritten tail identically on every rank up to a bound, kept the staging or the host lock meanwhile, and parked write-through backups whose host staging allocation failed for a tick retry. Both are gone. The tail now heals through the write-through path that already exists (the next piece covering uncovered keys in buffer mode, the next host-backup cycle in cache mode), and a host-staging allocation failure keeps main's behaviour. What remains is the agreed written prefix and the truthful settlement, which is the part that needs cross-rank agreement; everything removed was retry machinery on top of it. One packed MIN per drain that acked backups is the whole cost.

## Accuracy Tests

New file `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_backup_settlement.py` (CPU, `register_cpu_ci`): a real `UnifiedRadixCache`, a real `HybridCacheController` with its backup thread and the real file backend behind a deterministic proxy that fails the batch carrying chosen keys; only the D2H transfer engine is faked.

- `test_short_write_settles_the_prefix_and_the_next_write_through_covers_the_tail` (buffer_only, line 285): the second of three batches fails once; after the ack only the 128-page prefix is believed, the tail is neither believed nor in flight, nothing is retried or queued, the staging is freed, one warning line, `storage_backup_failed_tokens(172)` once, `backuped_tokens` logged 128; the next write-through of the node writes the uncovered tail, after which every page is believed and present in the backend.
- `test_persistent_failure_counts_once_per_settlement` (buffer_only, line 306): the batch fails every time; two write-throughs settle short twice, the counter is incremented once per settlement, nothing is held between them.
- `test_the_drain_reduces_only_when_it_acked_backups` (buffer_only, line 323): ticks without backup acks issue no `_all_reduce_storage_drain`; a drain that acked one backup issues exactly one, over a one-element vector.
- `test_short_write_settles_in_pages` (buffer_only, page_size 4, line 346): the agreed token count is page-aligned through the drain and the believed prefix is sliced in pages of the hash chain; the next write-through completes the span.
- `test_short_write_settles_and_releases_the_host_lock` (cache mode, line 375): the host lock returns to 0 and the request record is cleared on the short ack, one warning line, `backuped_tokens` 128 and `storage_backup_failed_tokens(172)` once, no second write enqueued; the node stays host-backed, as documented.
- `test_rank_local_failure_settles_both_ranks_at_the_agreed_prefix` (two-rank gloo, cache mode, line 524): only rank 1's backend fails the second batch; after every tick the in-flight operation ids and every enqueued span are all_gathered and equal on both ranks; both ranks settle at 128 pages, count 172 tokens once, enqueue nothing more and release the lock, although rank 0's backend holds all 300 pages.
- `test_non_writer_rank_vouches_for_the_span` (two-rank gloo, cache mode, line 527): rank 1 is made a non-writer (`is_storage_writer` False, its worker writes nothing and acks with `completed_tokens` 0) while rank 0, the writer, fails the second batch; the agreed prefix is the writer's 128 pages, not 0; both ranks settle and count identically; `backuped_tokens` logs 128 on the writer and 0 on the non-writer.

Results on the development box (one NVIDIA B200, CUDA 13.0), on this revision rebased on main `9fe1dbb8058`:

- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_backup_settlement.py`: Ran 7 tests in 27.940s, OK (the two-rank gloo cases included).
- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mamba_path_state_cap.py`: Ran 10 tests in 1.013s, OK (as on main). `test_hicache_pp_sync_drain.py`: Ran 2 tests, OK (its fixture is back to main's). `test_storage_prefetch_lifecycle.py`: Ran 16 tests, OK. `test_buffer_mode_sidecar.py`: Ran 7 tests, OK. `test_hicache_staged_write_back_dispatch.py`: Ran 28 tests, OK (skipped=1).
- GPU, one B200: `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache/test_unified_radix_cache_storage.py`: Ran 302 tests in 34.978s, OK (skipped=63); `test_unified_radix_cache_hicache.py`: Ran 341 tests in 14.701s, OK (skipped=46); both identical on untouched main `9fe1dbb8058`.
- Every `base-a-test-cpu`-registered file under `test/registered/unit/{mem_cache,managers,disaggregation}` (321 files on this base), each run as a script: no failure that untouched main `9fe1dbb8058` does not also have in this environment (pytest-style output, missing `parameterized`, no Rust toolchain, CPU stream).
- pre-commit clean on the changed files.
- Previous CI round on this PR (base `9fe1dbb8058`, head `6bbb5915bb0`, run 42713709604): the only failing job was a `call-multimodal-gen-tests` diffusion lane, which fails on main's own runs of the same workflow.

Not run: GPU serving, PP > 1 end to end, PD disaggregation and the mooncake/hf3fs/nixl backends (the GPU unit suites above did run); repository CI re-runs on push.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not benchmarked. The added cost is one gloo MIN of an `n_backup`-long int64 vector per tick, only in ticks that acked storage backups. No worker thread is coupled across ranks: the backup thread still writes ahead and only the ack drain, which was already paced by the MIN of the ack-queue sizes, carries the agreement.

title: [Fix] disaggregation: Send aux_item_lens next to aux_ptrs in PD registration
author: ShangmingCai
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #40107. The `aux_item_lens` registration frame was appended at the end of the message (Mooncake frame 20, NIXL frame 24 after GUARD) and only when customized-info transfer was enabled. Registration frames are positional, so any frame appended after it would land at a different index depending on whether the feature is on.

Rather than keep patching around a trailing optional frame, this puts the frame where it belongs, right after `aux_ptrs`, and always sends it.

## Modifications

- Mooncake: `aux_item_lens` is now frame 6; frames 6-19 move to 7-20 (staging fields move to 15/16, slot layer ids to 19).
- NIXL: `aux_item_lens` is now frame 7 (after GUARD); frames 7-23 move to 8-24.
- The frame is always sent, empty when customized-info transfer is disabled, and an empty frame parses as `None`. The builders return a plain list again instead of conditionally appending.
- `test_registration_wire_is_preserved_for_all_peers` expects the new frame right after `aux_ptrs`.

**Compatibility:** this changes the decode -> prefill registration layout, so prefill and decode must run the same SGLang version. Mixing a build with this change and one without it is not supported.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A, registration wire layout only.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A.

title: [Fix] disaggregation: Ignore a late STAGING_REQ for an already-scattered staging chunk
author: ShangmingCai
body:
## Motivation

`TestDisaggregationStagingRadixPrefillLargerTP` (in `test_disaggregation_different_tp.py`, 8-gpu-h20) can stall for 300s. On #47638's run, 17 of 200 requests hung, 12 of them timing out with `timed out after 300.0s in KVPoll.WaitingForInput`, and gsm8k latency was 302s instead of the usual ~3s. Decode logged `not complete 300s after all-ranks Success (a scatter never arrived)` and `releasing unscattered staging allocation`. The code under test was identical to main, which has passed this test before, so this is an intermittent race.

The race:

1. With prefill TP > decode TP, each decode rank has several prefill writers per chunk. Every writer sends a `STAGING_REQ` for each chunk. Decode dedups these through the chunk's live allocation in `chunk_staging_infos`, and broadcasts each `STAGING_RSP` to all of them.
2. Writers send `STAGING_REQ` from the scheduler thread over a prefetch socket, and `CHUNK_READY` from the transfer worker over a different socket. Across those two sockets, decode gets no ordering guarantee.
3. When every writer's `CHUNK_READY` arrives, decode scatters the chunk and resets its slot to `(-1, -1, ...)`. A writer's own `STAGING_REQ` that lands after this then looks new. Decode allocates a fresh slot that no one will ever scatter, and the room never completes.
4. Because the staging buffer is a ring, that pinned slot also blocks prefill writes for every later room until the room times out.

The window is widest right after start, when the prefetch sockets are still connecting, and for prefill radix hits, whose forward is short. All 5 rooms behind the stall came from the first ~80ms burst of the test, and all were radix hits.

## Modifications

- When a chunk scatters, mark its slot with a new `StagingAllocator.CHUNK_SCATTERED` sentinel instead of the free value.
- `handle_staging_req` drops a request for a chunk marked scattered. That writer already has its offset from the broadcast `STAGING_RSP` and has written the chunk, so no reply is needed.
- Readers that treat `info[0] >= 0` as outstanding are unaffected. The fix sits in the shared handler, so Mooncake and NIXL are both covered.

## Accuracy Tests

Not affected: data transferred to a chunk that was already scattered is unchanged.

## Testing

- New unit test `test_late_staging_req_after_scatter_does_not_reallocate` in `test_disaggregation_wire.py`: scatter a chunk, then deliver a late `STAGING_REQ` for it. It fails before the fix, with the allocator called once, and passes after.
- `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/` gives the same results with and without the fix, apart from the new test.

title: [Fix] mem_cache: Keep K/V in separate allocations under torch.compile
author: DarkSharpness
body:
> (auto generated by Claude)

## Problem

Since #32272 (1a120754e0), `MHATokenToKVPool._create_buffers_normal` allocates each layer's K and V on CUDA as the two halves of one tensor (`k_buffer = fused[0, :rows]`, `v_buffer = fused[1, :rows]`). With `--enable-torch-compile`, decode throughput drops by 12-23x: Qwen/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B bs=1 goes from 385 to 16.6 tok/s on B200, and to 22.8 tok/s on H100 in CI.

## Root cause

The KV store (`store_cache`, a custom op registered with `mutates_args=["k_cache", "v_cache"]`) is traced into the compiled graph. Its two mutated inputs are now views of the same allocation, so AOTAutograd functionalizes the mutation through a synthetic base: every layer, on every decode step, clones the layer's whole KV allocation and copies it back. A B200 profile shows two extra inductor kernels per layer, `triton_poi_fused_as_strided_clone_0` (numel 2,794,110,976, ~1.6 ms) and `triton_poi_fused_as_strided_copy__1` (~0.8 ms). Over 24 layers that is ~58 ms/step, which matches 16.6 tok/s. On H100 the pool is 1.6 GB per layer, giving ~44 ms/step and 22.8 tok/s.

## Why CI mostly did not catch it

The inductor / AOTAutograd cache key covers the traced graph and the input shapes, strides and dtypes, but not whether two inputs alias each other. #32272 does not change the traced graph, so on runners whose `~/.cache/sglang/inductor` was populated before 10-27 the old non-aliased artifact is reused and the test passes. Only cold-cache runs compile the slow graph. That is why `test/registered/moe/test_torch_compile_moe.py::test_throughput` fails intermittently with `22.8 not greater than or equal to 285`: 3 of ~130 `base-b-test-1-gpu-large` jobs between 10-25 and 10-31, with `h100-novita-host3-gpu-7` hitting it repeatedly (e.g. the scheduled run at 05fb1c98ad). Users who compile without a pre-10-27 cache always get the slow graph.

## Reproduction (1x B200, cold cache)

Server: `--model Qwen/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B --enable-torch-compile --torch-compile-max-bs 4` (the server args of `test_torch_compile_moe.py`), with a fresh `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR` per launch; measure bs=1 decode of 256 tokens with the same request as `test_throughput`.

| commit | inductor cache | decode tok/s |
|---|---|---|
| 8353f86f0b (parent of #32272) | cold | 385 |
| 1a120754e0 (#32272) | cold | 16.6 |
| 05fb1c98ad (main, 10-30) | cold | 16.6 |
| 1a120754e0 / 05fb1c98ad | warm, populated by 8353f86f0b | 385 |
| 05fb1c98ad + this PR | cold | 384.7 |
| 05fb1c98ad, no torch.compile | n/a | 475 |

The flashinfer and triton attention backends show the same 16.5 tok/s, so the slowdown is not specific to one backend.

## Fix

When `enable_torch_compile` is set, keep K and V in separate allocations, as ROCm already does. The trtllm fmha_v2 prefill path from #32272 then takes its existing fallback, which copies the batch's KV pages and logs a one-time warning. So only that prefill path is slower, and only under torch.compile. A fuller fix would pass the fused base plus an offset to `store_cache`, so the op never mutates two aliased views; that changes the kernel interface, so it is left as a follow-up for #32272's owners.

## Validation

- Cold-cache B200 numbers above.
- CI: `/rerun-test` of `test_torch_compile_moe.py`, `test_mha_pool_fused_kv_layout.py` and `test_trtllm_mha.py`. A warm runner cannot reproduce the bug, so the cold-cache table is the evidence for the fix.

cc @akhilg-nv (#32272)

title: [Fix] rust-server: Validate gathered listener ranks and address families
author: merrymercy
body:
## Motivation

A gathered Rust listener table can omit or repeat an attention-DP rank, leaving control fanout incomplete. A listener bound to `0.0.0.0` can also advertise an IPv6 address that it cannot accept connections on. Reject these configurations during startup, after the collective completes, so listener and non-listener ranks report the same failure.

## Modifications

- Require exactly one listener for every attention-DP rank when attention-DP spans multiple ranks.
- Gather IPv4 bind / IPv6 advertised-address errors with the listener records and raise on every participating rank.
- Keep the successful endpoint table format and elastic-EP joiner behavior unchanged.

Related fixes: #47541 handles advertised-address discovery and cross-node loopback rejection; #47519 validates the recipient DP rank on peer requests. This PR adds the listener-table and bind-family checks.

## Accuracy Tests

`uv run --no-sync python -m pytest test/registered/unit/multimodal/rust/shared/test_rust_server_extension.py -q`: **12 passed, 14 subtests passed**.

The seven new malformed-input cases fail on the unchanged base (`181380682b50`) because no exception is raised. They pass with these checks, including failures observed by ranks without listeners. Pre-commit checks pass for both changed files.

GPU and multi-node serving tests were not run. This changes startup validation and does not change model calculations.

Not run; the checks execute once during startup.

title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] fused-a-gemm: Check the selected backend's K alignment before taking the fused path
author: lingxling
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #47710.

On SM120 the fused-A GEMM dispatcher auto-selects the CuTe DSL kernel, which requires `K % 1024 == 0`, but `fused_a_gemm_weight_eligible()` only checks the JIT kernel's `K % 256 == 0`. A DeepSeek-style MLA model with `hidden_size=3584` (or 2560) therefore passes the check and then crashes in `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` on the first <= 16-token batch:

```
AssertionError: K must be a multiple of 1024, got 3584
```

The same shape works on Hopper, where `auto` resolves to the JIT kernel.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/fused_a_gemm.py`
  - Add a per-backend K alignment table (`JIT: 256`, `CUTEDSL: 1024`) mirroring each kernel's assert.
  - Factor the `auto` resolution into `_resolve_backend()` and use it in both `dsv3_fused_a_gemm` and `fused_a_gemm_weight_eligible`.
  - `fused_a_gemm_weight_eligible` takes a keyword-only `backend` (default `auto`) and checks K against the resolved backend. The dtype, `N % 16`, CUDA and SM >= 90 checks are unchanged.
- `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py`: pass `backend=self.fused_a_gemm_backend` to both eligibility checks, so the check matches the backend the subsequent `linear_with_fused_a_gemm` call uses. `nemotron_h.py` uses the default (`auto`) for both calls already, so it needs no change.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/gemm/test_fused_a_gemm.py` (new, registered on `base-b-kernel-unit` / `1-gpu-small`, i.e. the RTX 5090 runner, skipped elsewhere): on SM120, a K=3584 weight must be ineligible and the guarded path must match `F.linear`; a K=7168 weight must stay on the fused CuTe DSL path and match `F.linear`. This is a separate file because it needs the 5090 runner; adding that registration to `test_cutedsl_dsv3_fused_a_gemm.py` would also move its full kernel matrix onto the 5090.

Behavior:

| GPU | backend | K % 256 == 0, K % 1024 != 0 (e.g. 3584) | K % 1024 == 0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| non-SM120 | auto (-> JIT) | fused (unchanged) | fused (unchanged) |
| SM120 | auto (-> CuTe DSL) | **unfused fallback** (was: AssertionError) | fused (unchanged) |
| any | explicit `cutedsl` | unfused fallback (was: AssertionError) | fused |
| any | explicit `jit` | fused (unchanged) | fused (unchanged) |

Why gate in the eligibility check rather than fall back inside `dsv3_fused_a_gemm`:

- The kernel entry points keep their shape asserts as their contract. A silent fallback in the kernel wrapper would hide a caller that passes a shape the kernel can't run.
- On SM120 there is no fused fallback to switch to: the JIT kernel sizes its pipeline for Hopper's shared memory (see #29897), so the only fallback would be a plain torch matmul inside a kernel op.
- Callers already treat `fused_a_gemm_weight_eligible` as the gate (cached once per layer) with the regular linear layer as the fallback, so fixing the predicate fixes all of them.

## Accuracy Tests

Not a numerics change: shapes that run the fused kernel are the same as before, except the SM120 shapes that used to crash, which now use the regular linear layer.

RTX 5090 (SM120), CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, run before and after the fix (repro scripts are attached to the issue).

New test. It fails on unpatched code and passes with the fix:

```
# before
FAILED test_fused_a_gemm.py::test_eligibility_follows_cutedsl_k_alignment[1-3584-False]   (assert True == False)
FAILED test_fused_a_gemm.py::test_eligibility_follows_cutedsl_k_alignment[16-3584-False]  (assert True == False)
2 failed, 2 passed

# after
test_fused_a_gemm.py::test_eligibility_follows_cutedsl_k_alignment[1-3584-False] PASSED
test_fused_a_gemm.py::test_eligibility_follows_cutedsl_k_alignment[1-7168-True] PASSED
test_fused_a_gemm.py::test_eligibility_follows_cutedsl_k_alignment[16-3584-False] PASSED
test_fused_a_gemm.py::test_eligibility_follows_cutedsl_k_alignment[16-7168-True] PASSED
4 passed
```

Kernel-level repro (guarded fused-A linear vs `F.linear`, N=2112):

```
# before: K=3584 and K=2560 -> AssertionError: K must be a multiple of 1024 (6 cases), FAIL
# after
  K=3584  N=2112 M=1  -> path=unfused max|diff|=0 ok=True
  K=3584  N=2112 M=4  -> path=unfused max|diff|=0 ok=True
  K=3584  N=2112 M=16 -> path=unfused max|diff|=0 ok=True
  K=2560  N=2112 M=1  -> path=unfused max|diff|=0 ok=True
  K=2560  N=2112 M=4  -> path=unfused max|diff|=0 ok=True
  K=2560  N=2112 M=16 -> path=unfused max|diff|=0 ok=True
  K=7168  N=2112 M=1  -> path=fused   max|diff|=0.007812 ok=True
  K=7168  N=2112 M=4  -> path=fused   max|diff|=0.003906 ok=True
  K=7168  N=2112 M=16 -> path=fused   max|diff|=0.007812 ok=True
PASS
```

End to end: a config-only `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM` (DeepSeek-V3 MLA dims, hidden_size=3584, 4 layers, 16 experts), `--load-format dummy --skip-tokenizer-init`, one `/generate` request with `input_ids`:

```
# before
FAIL: bug reproduced (died during startup); server log contains 'K must be a multiple of 1024'
# after
server ready; sending /generate with input_ids
HTTP 200; output_ids (16): [...]
PASS: decoded 16 tokens with hidden_size=3584
```

Not run on Hopper. Eligibility there is unchanged (`auto` resolves to JIT, which keeps the 256 check), and the existing `test_dsv3_fused_a_gemm.py` / `test_cutedsl_dsv3_fused_a_gemm.py` run in CI on H100.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No change on non-SM120 GPUs: same predicate result, same kernel. On SM120, K values that are 1024-aligned keep the fused CuTe DSL path. K values that are only 256-aligned, which used to crash, now run the regular linear layer.

Possible follow-up, not in this PR: the CuTe DSL kernel's K indexing (`TILE_K=256`, split-K inside each tile) does not obviously need `K % 1024`. With the assert bypassed on the 5090 it matched `F.linear` at K=3584 and K=2560 (N=2112, M in {1, 4, 16}; max |diff| <= 0.016, same order as K=7168). Relaxing the assert to 256 would need a wider shape sweep and a perf comparison against the unfused path, so it is left for a separate PR.

title: [Fix] scheduler: Decide early result processing before scheduling the next batch
author: hnyls2002
body:
Stacks on #43900.

The overlap loops decided whether to process the last result early after the next batch was already scheduled, then processed it before launching that batch. A request the early processing finished was still launched with the batch. Two triggers reach this: `SGLANG_DISABLE_CONSECUTIVE_PREFILL_OVERLAP` on consecutive extend steps (including DP-converted decode steps and mixed steps), and spec + grammar for algorithms without grammar overlap (NGRAM), where an EOS or stop finish rides the next decode launch.

- `should_process_last_batch_early(last_batch)` replaces `is_disable_overlap_for_batch` and is decided before scheduling from the only result still pending, so the early processing runs before `get_next_batch_to_run`, whose filter then drops the requests it finished. Used by `event_loop_overlap` and `event_loop_overlap_disagg_decode`; the opportunistic unified-memory flush moves with it.
  - After a prefill, for its TTFT: `SGLANG_DISABLE_OVERLAP_AFTER_PREFILL` is set and `last_batch` is extend (`is_extend_in_batch` under DP, already synced across ranks). This renames `SGLANG_DISABLE_CONSECUTIVE_PREFILL_OVERLAP`, which still works as a deprecated alias: the next batch is not built yet, so the rule can no longer require it to be a prefill too.
  - Grammar: `last_batch.grammar_needs_sync()`. `grammar_needs_sync` now includes the non-spec check its only caller applied.
- The NGRAM worker decides per request whether to splice the previous round's accepted tokens: a request whose `inflight_steps` (from #43900) is above one at this launch still has an earlier round unprocessed. It used to infer this for the whole batch from `grammar_needs_sync()`, which no longer matches once the decision is made before scheduling, and which already double-spliced the old decode rows on the first decode after a prefill step under overlap (their previous result was processed one iteration earlier).
- The `not r.finished()` filter in `_join_launched_reqs` is removed: no processing runs between scheduling and launch, so no launched row is already finished.
- `test_scheduler_running_reqs.py` drives the overlap loop with an NGRAM grammar row and asserts on the launched rows (the finished row is launched on main) and on each row's unprocessed-round state at launch; `test_ngram_worker_prompt.py` sets the per-request count.

No behavior change in the default configuration. With `SGLANG_DISABLE_OVERLAP_AFTER_PREFILL` (or the old name) set, the last result is processed early after any extend step, also when the next step is decode or idle; before, only when the next step was a prefill too. With NGRAM and grammar, it is processed early whenever the last batch holds a grammar request, also when the next step is a prefill. NGRAM under overlap no longer splices tokens already in a request's output, which changes its drafts (acceptance only, not outputs).

title: [Fix] dspark: Stage each request's own SWA ring slot at batch size 1
author: weireweire
body:
## Root cause

When the DSpark draft keeps its SWA KV in a per-request ring (for example with `--enable-encoder-swa-bounded-replay`), the static verify epilogue (`DsparkVerifyEpilogue.run_static`) builds the per-row state slots like this:

```python
io.req_pool_indices.view(-1, 1).expand(bs, self.stride).reshape(-1)
```

At `bs == 1` this reshape returns a stride-0 view instead of a copy. The one-launch staging kernel (`stage_commit`, used when `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_DSPARK_ONE_LAUNCH_COMMIT_STAGE` is on, which is the default under `SGLANG_ENABLE_NV_MEGA_RUNTIME_OPTIMIZATION`) reads `state_slot` as a flat contiguous tensor. So rows `1..stride-1` pick up `req_pool_indices[1..stride-1]` from the graph's static buffer (stale or padding values) instead of request 0's slot. The deferred commit then writes those tokens' draft KV into other requests' rings, and the draft loses that context.

At `bs >= 2` the reshape has to copy, so only single-request steps are affected. Configs without a draft SWA ring pass `state_slot=None` and are unaffected.

## Fix

- `run_static` makes the state slots contiguous before staging.
- `stage_commit` asserts that `state_slot` is contiguous, as it already does for `cache_loc` and `positions`.

## Validation

- Extended `test/registered/unit/spec/test_dspark_deferred_commit.py`: the static epilogue now runs with a ring and the one-launch stage at bs 1 and bs 2, and the test checks that every staged row carries its own request's slot.
- On GB300 (CUDA) the file passes 6/6. Without the fix, the bs 1 subtest fails and bs 2 passes.
- End to end on GB300: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4, one concurrent request, real DSpark acceptance, `--enable-encoder-swa-bounded-replay` with deferred commit and the one-launch stage, GSM8K via sgl-eval 0.1.3 (300 examples, temperature 1). Both arms ran on the same node. Mean accept length went from 2.13 to 3.56 with the fix. Accuracy was 98.33% without the fix and 98.00% with it, the same within noise because the target verifies every token.

title: [Fix] kv_events: Offset ipc endpoints per DP rank and finish shutdown when the queue is full
author: ShangmingCai
body:
## Motivation

Two small fixes in `ZmqEventPublisher`:

- `offset_endpoint_port` only handles `inproc` and `tcp`. With an `ipc://` kv-events endpoint and `dp_size > 1`, every DP rank above zero raises `ValueError` while constructing its publisher, although the socket setup already supports `ipc://`.
- `shutdown()` enqueues the stop sentinel with `put_nowait` on a bounded queue. When the queue is full, `queue.Full` escapes and the socket cleanup after it never runs.

## Modifications

- Suffix `ipc://` endpoints with `_dp{rank}`, the same scheme `inproc` uses.
- Ignore `queue.Full` when enqueuing the sentinel; the thread exits anyway because `_running` is already false and the loop drains the queue first.
- One unit test per fix.

title: [Fix] kimi-k3: Honor initial expert placement in fused routing
author: Codoge
body:
## Motivation

Kimi-K3 does not expose the model metadata required by `--init-expert-location`. Its merged gate / latent-projection front also wraps logical top-k IDs without the ordinary placement remap or active-batch padding mask. A configured placement must agree with both checkpoint weight loading and runtime dispatch.

## Modifications

- Expose expert-location metadata for both the text model and multimodal wrapper, allowing the existing loader to place checkpoint experts according to an initial permutation.
- Pass the current routing inputs to the existing top-k post-processing helper after the merged front. Keep the existing capture / recorder behavior, including avoiding duplicate counts when mapping and recording are fused.
- Keep fake dispatch on the ordinary routing path because it transforms logits before top-k selection.
- Reject online EPLB and redundant experts, whose weight layout is not implemented by Kimi-K3. Reuse the existing `--init-expert-location` / `--ep-dispatch-algorithm static` options; do not introduce a placement heuristic, a benchmark-specific map, or a new flag.

## Accuracy Tests

Tested against upstream `b146a8576de930cf3adc104e601feb2790cdf3f6` with this PR applied independently:

- `test_topk_routing_inputs.py` and `test_kimi_k3_expert_placement.py`: **28 passed, 73 subtests passed**. Covers target/draft isolation, changes to the active padding mask, metadata for both model entry points, and rejection of unsupported relocation modes.
- `test_moe_front.py` and `test_expert_location_weight_loading.py`: **10 passed, 42 subtests passed**. The GPU case runs the actual merged front and model method with a non-identity permutation and padded tokens; mapped IDs, routing weights and latent output match the reference exactly. It also checks that fake dispatch declines the fused routing contract.
- `test_moe_front.py` and `test_eplb_map_record.py`: **4 passed** before adding the fake-dispatch eligibility assertion. Mapping/counting kernels filter padding correctly.

GPU tests used NVIDIA B30Z (B300), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 and Triton 3.8.0. Full-model output validation has not been rerun on this integration; the results above are operator and unit validation.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This change enables a valid initial placement and preserves the fused routing path where its contract is supported. No end-to-end speed claim is made for this branch. Earlier Kimi-K3 tuning motivated the change, but those results also depended on a workload-derived expert permutation and other patches; they are not attributed to this integration.

title: [Fix] linear: Keep replicated outputs out of TP symmetric memory
author: Codoge
body:
## Motivation

`RowParallelLinear` resolves `parallel_group="replicated"` to no TP group, but its output allocation still enters the global TP symmetric-memory context whenever allocation symmetry is enabled. Kimi-K3's replicated shared experts produce complete local outputs and do not need that collective memory window.

## Modifications

Disable the TP symmetric-memory allocation context when the linear has no TP group. Keep the existing attention-TP allocation path and the policy for sharded linears. Apply the fix in `RowParallelLinear.forward` so callers do not need model-specific allocation overrides.

## Accuracy Tests

Upstream `b146a8576de930cf3adc104e601feb2790cdf3f6` plus this PR only, CPU PyTorch 2.14.1:

```bash
python -m pytest test/registered/unit/layers/test_kimi_mlp_parallel_groups.py -q
# 2 passed
```

The existing test matrix runs real linear weight loading and forward operations across TP, attention-TP, shared-expert TP and replicated layouts. It now enables the surrounding allocation-symmetry policy and verifies that only replicated outputs disable the TP allocation context. Numerical comparisons still pass.

Additional distributed validation at `7861b6ce65` on 8× B300, BF16, with actual NCCL symmetric memory enabled: **PASS**. The 12 cases per rank cover replicated, TP and attention-TP outputs at nominal token counts 1 / 17 / 257 / 8192. `is_tensor_in_symmetric_mempool` confirms replicated outputs use ordinary allocations and sharded outputs remain in the NCCL pool. Replicated batch sizes vary by rank; sharded outputs complete the real TP AllReduce and match the reference exactly. This is a deterministic linear/allocation smoke test, not a full-model accuracy benchmark.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No standalone speedup is claimed. Earlier tuning combined local allocation with metadata and scheduling changes, so that aggregate improvement cannot be attributed to this patch. This PR corrects allocation scope without changing linear arithmetic. A full-model run with symmetric memory enabled has not been repeated on this branch.

title: [Fix] score: Validate logical item and MIS hidden-state row counts
author: mani1106
body:
