title: [Fix] server-args: Redact the access keys from /server_info, logs, launch_command and crash dumps
author: metamergebot
body:
<!-- oss-sync ci-note:start -->
**CI status (oncall, 2026-11-06 21:40 PST):** this PR is in GitHub stack #48459, the Rust-server stack: #48455 → #48457 → #48512 → #48515 → #48518 → #48523 → #48572 → #48753 → #48797 → #48798 → #48818 → #48815 (top). Each PR keeps its own diff (parent branches and `main` were merged in, no rebase). The CI bar for the whole stack is `pr-test.yml` with `pr-test-finish` green on the top #48815 (run 42341406709). Once that is green, approve and use **Merge stack** to land the chain in one atomic step.
<!-- oss-sync ci-note:end -->

Stacked on #48515 (branch `oss-sync-c677a14dcf`), which sits on #48512, #48457 and #48455: only this change is new here (it needs the Rust frontend's `_redact_api_keys` and the Rust-mode crash-dump writer from those pull requests). The branch takes upstream main by merging its parent rather than rebasing, so the Files tab, the diff against the base branch, is the change to read.

## Motivation

`/server_info` returns the resolved server args, including `api_key`, `admin_api_key` and `ssl_keyfile_password`. That covers HTTP, gRPC and the Rust frontend, whose launch-time fields come from the same `build_server_info`. A caller holding an ordinary API key can therefore read the admin key. The startup log, `Engine.get_server_info()`, `repr(ServerArgs)`, the request and crash dumps and `launch_command` carry the same values. Until now these paths redacted only the watermark secrets.

## Modifications

- One credential set (`api_key`, `admin_api_key`, `ssl_keyfile_password`) and one helper, `redact_server_args_secrets` in `server_args.py`, which also applies the existing watermark redaction. Every report of the server args shows `<redacted>` for a credential that is set and `None` for one that is not, so a reader can still tell whether it is configured. This covers `build_server_info` (`/server_info` on HTTP, gRPC and the Rust frontend), the startup log, `ServerArgs.__repr__`, `Engine.get_server_info()` and the request dump.
- Request and crash dumps are redacted in one place: `build_request_dump`, which every writer calls (the periodic request dump, the Python `TokenizerManager`'s crash dump and the scheduler that embeds the Rust server), stores `server_args` (passed as a dict or as the `ServerArgs` record) and `resolved_config` as redacted dicts, and `write_crash_dump` redacts `launch_command`. The Rust writer now passes its args unredacted, so the writers cannot drift.
- `launch_command` is redacted on the parsed argument list (`redact_secret_cli_args`), before anything joins it into a string. The parser's own option table identifies the credential flags, so every spelling argparse accepts is covered: `--api-key VAL`, `--api-key=VAL`, unambiguous abbreviations (`--admin-api-ke=VAL`), repeated flags, values containing spaces, a value that itself looks like a flag (`--api-key=--admin-api-key=x`), and one key containing the other. Everything after `--` passes through unchanged. The crash dump's `sys.argv` command goes through the same function.
- The scheduler's internal-state readback, which `/server_info` and `Engine.get_server_info()` report under `internal_states`, is redacted where it is built (`SchedulerInternalStateController.get_internal_state`). Before this change it carried the three credentials in plain text.
- The Rust frontend's `_redact_api_keys` string pass over `launch_command` now reads the key values from `server_args`, because `build_server_info` has already replaced them in `info`; with the argv-level redaction in place it is a backstop.
- `ServerArgs` and `resolved_dict()` keep the real values, so authentication, TLS and anything that reads the args back are unchanged. No Rust source changes: the Rust frontend's `/server_info` copies its launch-time fields from the JSON Python builds at launch, and reports `internal_states` through a typed allowlist.

Scope: server-args builders that bypass `prepare_server_args` report no `launch_command`, so for them only the dict-level redaction applies. `config_updates` (the runtime override log) in both dumps still redacts only the watermark secrets; no code path overrides the credential fields at runtime.

Merge note: upstream's #48781 and #48758 moved `build_server_info` to `entrypoints/server_utils.py` and `utils/crash_dump.py` to `observability/request_dump.py`, splitting `write_crash_dump` into `build_request_dump`, `save_request_dump` and `write_crash_dump`. This branch merges those in from its parent, and the redaction follows the functions: the server-info redaction and its import sit in `server_utils.py` (the test imports it from there), the dump redaction as described above, and the `redact_watermark_secrets` import that `tokenizer_manager.py` no longer uses after that move goes. Nothing else differs from the change as first opened.

Related: #42444 proposes a different implementation of the same redaction. This change keeps the existing watermark helpers as the single path and redacts `launch_command` on the argument list rather than on the joined string.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: the change only affects how the configuration is reported and dumped.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

## Testing

- New or extended tests:
  - `test/registered/unit/observability/test_crash_dump.py`, once per writer. The dumps carry `api_key`, `admin_api_key`, `ssl_keyfile_password`, `watermark_key` and `watermark_key_b`, with a command line that spells the credential flags (one abbreviated). The tests assert that no secret appears in the raw pickle bytes, that `server_args` and `resolved_config` show `<redacted>` for each secret, and that `launch_command` equals the expected redacted string. `test_secrets_redacted_whatever_the_writer_passes` drives the Python writer with the snapshot passed unredacted, once as a dict and once as the `ServerArgs` record; `TestRustServerCrashDump.test_secrets_redacted` drives the Rust server's writer; `test_server_args_snapshot_redacted_with_watermarking_off` covers the snapshot the request dump pickles.
  - `TestAccessKeyRedaction` in `test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py`: the launch command for every argparse spelling, `/server_info` (set keys `<redacted>`, unset keys `None`), the startup log and the repr; the server still authenticates with the values the operator gave.
  - `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_server_info.py`: `test_http_and_both_grpc_roles_share_startup_metadata` sets all three credentials and checks HTTP `/server_info` shows `<redacted>` (the test already asserts the gRPC leader, the gRPC follower and the Rust frontend's launch fields equal the HTTP fields); new `TestServerInfoInternalStatesRedaction` drives the real scheduler readback with space-containing keys through the HTTP builder and `Engine.get_server_info()` and finds no fragment in either payload. It fails without the `get_internal_state` change.
- `pytest test/registered/unit/observability/test_crash_dump.py test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_server_info.py`: 57 passed, 16 subtests passed.
- `pytest test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py`: 352 passed, 229 subtests passed; the one failure, `TestDcpCommBackendDefault::test_npu_supports_dcp`, fails identically on the base branch (host dependent, unrelated to this change).

title: [Fix] hicache: Stop L3 prefetch at the match key limit
author: lichang98
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack
  community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

  ## Motivation

  With hierarchical cache enabled and an L3 storage backend, a request whose
  prefix is already stored can still end up with `#cached-token: 0` right after a
  successful prefetch:

  HiCache prefetch success ... completed=227840 matched=0 loaded=227840 occupied=0
  Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 227864, #cached-token: 0, ...

  The prefetched data was paid for (RDMA read) and then silently dropped, and the
  entire prompt was re-prefilled.

  This happens for hybrid SWA models (e.g. DeepSeek-V4: `page_size=256`,
  `sliding_window=128`, `swa_gates_prefix_match=True`) when the L3 prefetch span
  overruns the radix match key:

  - Match key: `_req_radix_key` caps the key at `L - swa_reprefill_tail_tokens()`,
    so page-aligned matching ends at `E_match = floor((L - W) / P) * P`.
  - L3 prefetch: `_prefetch_kvcache` used `req._compute_max_prefix_len(...) = L - 1`,
    so the page-aligned span ends at `E_pre = floor((L - 1) / P) * P`.

  For `L mod P = r`, `E_pre > E_match` exactly when `1 <= r <= W - 1`
  (~49.6% of all prompt lengths for `P=256, W=128`) and the page
  `[E_match, E_match + P)` is present in L3.

  For a prefetched span, the only SWA host window is committed to the span's last
  page, whose position assumes the span end. When the prefetch reaches one page
  past `E_match`, the matcher stops at `E_match` — a boundary node that carries a
  full KV host value but no SWA host value. The SWA match validator rejects that
  boundary, `host_hit_length` stays 0, `init_load_back` is never triggered, and
  the already-transferred span is dropped. `E_pre <= E_match` cases are unaffected,
  so the failure is length-dependent rather than "near full match" only.

  ## Modifications

  - Add `storage_prefetch_end(tree_cache, req, max_prefix_len)` in
    `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/common.py`. It reuses `_req_radix_key`'s limit
    (`len(_req_radix_key(...))`), so "how far we prefetch" and "how far we may
    match" cannot diverge. The returned value is pre-page-alignment;
    `prefetch_from_storage` still floors it to `page_size`, which is where the
    bug actually manifested.
  - Use it in `scheduler._prefetch_kvcache` for `match_end` / `new_input_tokens`
    instead of `req._compute_max_prefix_len(...)`.
  - Add `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_storage_prefetch_span.py` (5 cases):
    no re-prefill tail, tail capping the span, the smaller of tail and
    `max_prefix_len` winning, tail longer than the prompt, and the reported
    boundary case (`L=8216`, `L mod 256=24` → span 7936 instead of 8192).

  Cost: at most one page plus the SWA window is re-prefilled, i.e.
  `W + P - 1 = 383` tokens for DeepSeek-V4 when the span is truncated. Lengths
  with `r = 0` or `r >= W` produce exactly the same span as before.

  ## Accuracy Tests

  GSM8K, 300 questions, 5-shot, greedy, `max_tokens=512`, all cache tiers enabled.
  Two full runs on the patched build:

  | Run | Accuracy | Invalid | Errors |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | 1 | 0.9767 (293/300) | 0.0 | 0 |
  | 2 | 0.9800 (294/300) | 0.0 | 0 |

  No truncation and no request failures. 

  Output equivalence, cold prefill vs. L3-served, for the former failing length
  class `L = 8192 + r, r in [1,127]`, 8 cases + 2 controls

  Full-scale reproduction of the reported workload (`L = 227864`,
  `227864 mod 256 = 24`):

  before: completed=227840 loaded=227840  #cached-token: 0      (227864 re-prefilled)
  after:  completed=227584 loaded=227584  #cached-token: 227584 (#new-token: 280)

  ## Speed Tests and Profiling

  Same full-scale probe: cold prefill of the 227864-token prompt took 31.4 s;
  after flushing L1/L2 so the request is served from L3, the patched build
  transfers and admits 227584 tokens and completes the prefill in 0.5 s, with only
  280 tokens re-prefilled. Before the patch the request fell back to a full
  227864-token prefill. This is a functional probe, not a benchmark; no
  throughput regression is expected because unaffected lengths keep the same
  prefetch span.

  ## Checklist

  - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
  - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
  - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
  - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the
  speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
  - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Fix] [CPU] cpu-graph: Preserve return_logprob and request metadata in dynamic prefill
author: CaoE
body:
## Motivation

1. Multi-request dynamic prefill (`batch_size >= 2`) reuses `prefill_dynamic_batch_template`, which is initialized with `return_logprob=False`. When incoming requests specify `return_logprob=True`, the dynamic batch preparation previously did not refresh this flag, causing the outer eager logits tail to silently skip prompt logprob computation.
2. Long-lived dynamic batch templates retained strong references to request metadata (`sampling_info`, `spec_info`, etc.) across idle intervals, delaying garbage collection.
3. Prefill static bucket padding padded `input_ids`, `positions`, `out_cache_loc`, and `mrope_positions`, but did not pad `token_type_ids` for cross-encoder/reranker models.


## Modifications

1. Refresh `return_logprob`, `is_prefill_only`, `return_pooled_hidden_states`, and request metadata (`sampling_info`, `spec_info`, `rids`, `lora_ids`, etc.) in `_refresh_dynamic_forward_batch_metadata` without duplicate assignments in caller functions.
2. Clear heavy request references on dynamic templates in `finally` blocks after execution via `_clear_dynamic_batch_template_references` to avoid lifecycle memory leaks.
3. Pad `token_type_ids` to the bucket length during prefill static padding, and align `mm_inputs` handling across prefill and decode dynamic batches.
4. Add regression tests in `test/registered/cpu/test_cpu_graph.py`:
   - `test_dynamic_prefill_multi_request_preserves_return_logprob`: validates that `return_logprob=True` is forwarded and produces input logprobs, and verifies template references are cleared post-execution.
   - `test_prefill_graph_token_type_ids_padding_and_dynamic`: verifies `token_type_ids` padding in static buckets and pass-through in dynamic fallback.

title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] custom-allreduce: Scope a zero NVLink fabric cluster UUID to its own node
author: metamergebot
body:
<!-- oss-sync ci-note:start -->
**CI status (oncall, 2026-11-06 20:40Z): every test ran on this head and passed.** In the PR Test run on this head ([42128580169](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42128580169)), `base-a` and 11 of 13 `base-b` shards are green. The remaining base-b shard(s) were cancelled while queued, and their test files ran green on this same head via `/rerun-test` ([42190243030](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42190243030), [42190258758](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42190258758)). `pr-test-finish` is red only because those shard(s) ran outside the PR Test run; nothing is untested. Ready to merge.
<!-- oss-sync ci-note:end -->

## Motivation

`is_one_nvlink_clique` decides whether a process group that spans nodes shares one NVLink fabric (a multi-node NVLink domain) by comparing each GPU's NVML fabric cluster UUID and clique id. On HGX NVSwitch baseboards NVML reports the fabric state as Completed with an all-zero cluster UUID and clique id 0 on every node, so a group spanning two such nodes compares equal and is taken for one clique even though the fabric ends at each baseboard.

Custom all-reduce v2 then admits such a group and attempts its symmetric-memory rendezvous across the nodes. The rendezvous passes file descriptors between ranks, which cannot cross hosts: some ranks fail the handshake and fall back while the rest keep waiting for them, and server startup never completes.

## Modifications

- `custom_all_reduce_utils.is_one_nvlink_clique`: when the queried cluster UUID is all zeros, extend the clique key with the host name, so only the GPUs of one node share it. Nonzero cluster UUIDs (one multi-node NVLink domain) and groups within one node compare exactly as before. This is the rule NCCL's own MNNVL detection applies ([`src/mnnvl.cc`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl/blob/master/src/mnnvl.cc): "A zero UUID means we don't have MNNVL fabric info - disable MNNVL"). Every caller gets the corrected answer: custom all-reduce v2 declines the cross-node group and falls back to the legacy custom all-reduce, which disables itself for it, and the MNNVL all-reduce fusion and `in_one_nvlink_domain` stay off for it.
- `test/registered/unit/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce_v2_capability.py`: a CPU parametrized case that drives the undecorated `is_one_nvlink_clique` with a patched fabric query, host name and `all_gather_object`. A zero UUID compares equal within one host and unequal across hosts; a nonzero UUID compares equal across hosts.

## Checklist

- `pre-commit run --files` on both files passes.
- The test file passes with this change; the new case fails without it.

title: [Fix] moe: Fix illegal memory access in the W4A16/W8A16 Triton MoE kernel (unmasked K tail)
author: qhmiao
body:
## Motivation

Weight-only quantized MoE models (W4A16 / W8A16) that run on the Triton MoE path can crash with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access` in `fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq`. An AutoRound W4A16 checkpoint of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next at TP 4 hits it on its first decode step, every time. The cause is a weight load without its K mask; this PR adds the mask.

**Cause.** When K is not a multiple of `BLOCK_SIZE_K`, `fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq` builds `k_mask` and applies it to the activation, scale and zero-point loads, but not to the weight load:

```python
b = tl.load(b_ptrs)
```

So the last K tile reads past the end of every weight row. On the last row of the last expert, it reads past the end of the weight tensor. The extra values are multiplied by a scale that is masked to zero, so the results are correct whenever the read does not fault. `fused_moe_kernel` already masks the same load.

**Who runs this kernel.**

- `--quantization moe_wna16`, for GPTQ and AWQ checkpoints.
- AWQ and AutoRound MoE layers that Marlin cannot take, for example without Marlin support on the platform, or with a per-rank intermediate size that is not a multiple of max(64, group size). So the irregular shapes, the ones most likely to leave a partial K tile, are the ones that fall back here.
- Compressed-tensors W4A16 MoE through `CompressedTensorsWNA16TritonMoE`: always on ROCm, by default on SM100/SM103 for symmetric INT4 with group 32 or 128, and elsewhere with `--moe-runner-backend triton`.

**When it reads out of bounds.** Whenever the per-rank K is not a multiple of the `BLOCK_SIZE_K` in use. At decode batch sizes (M ≤ E, no more tokens than experts), the default config uses `BLOCK_SIZE_K` 64, so the down projection overruns when the per-rank intermediate size is not a multiple of 64. Common cases:

| model | `moe_intermediate_size` | TP | per-rank K |
|---|---|---|---|
| GLM-4.5-Air, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B | 1408 | 4 | 352 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B | 768 | 8 | 96 |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next | 640 | 4 | 160 |

Tuned configs with `BLOCK_SIZE_K` 128 or 256 leave a partial tile for more shapes.

**When it crashes.** Whether the read faults depends on what follows the weight tensor in memory. I have tested only Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (512 experts) at TP 4, and there it always faults:

- `moe_wna16` lowers the group size from 128 to 32 to fit the per-rank K of 160, and the last tile covers 128–191.
- Each rank's down-projection weight is `[512, 2560, 80]` uint8, exactly 100 MiB, and the overrun leaves the allocation.

On v0.5.22, every such server I started died on its first decode. With this one line masked, they serve normally.

## Modifications

- Load the weights with the existing `k_mask` / `k_other`, as the scale and zero-point loads already do. When K is a multiple of `BLOCK_SIZE_K`, `k_mask` is `None` and the load is unchanged.
- New `test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_fused_moe_gptq_awq_k_tail.py`, driving `invoke_fused_moe_kernel` with explicit configs:
  - `test_partial_k_tile`: int4 and int8, with and without zero points, K = 96 and 160 with `BLOCK_SIZE_K` 64, compared against dequantize-then-matmul. The existing wna16 test (`test/manual/test_triton_moe_wna16.py`) only uses K = 128 and 1024, so a partial K tile had no coverage.
  - `test_weight_tail_at_allocation_end`: the Flash-Next down-projection shape above (E 512, N 2560, K 160, group 32, `BLOCK_SIZE_K` 64), with the weights allocated last so that the overrun leaves the allocation. Without the fix it crashes on L40S (below).

## Accuracy Tests

1x L40S (SM89), torch 2.14.1, Triton 3.8.0. The kernel function and its launch path are identical between current main and the tree I tested. I ran the new test with and without the change:

| | without the fix | with the fix |
|---|---|---|
| `test_partial_k_tile` | passes | passes |
| `test_weight_tail_at_allocation_end` | `CUDA error: an illegal memory access` (4 of 4 runs) | passes (2 of 2) |
| `test_partial_k_tile` under `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1 compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck` | 6 errors: `Invalid __global__ read of size 1 bytes` at the weight load in `fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq` | 0 errors |

`test_partial_k_tile` passes without the fix because the scale mask zeroes the extra values; only the sanitizer, or a read that leaves the allocation, exposes it.

The results do not change: with the fix, the masked slots load 0 and are still multiplied by a scale of 0.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

When K is a multiple of `BLOCK_SIZE_K` (`even_Ks`), the generated code is unchanged. Otherwise, it adds one predicate to the weight load, which the scale and zero-point loads in the same loop already carry. Not benchmarked.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (isort 7.0.0, ruff 0.15.1 check and format, codespell 2.4.1 and the `scripts/lint` hooks, with the repo config.)

(Kernel results above; no speed benchmark, see Speed Tests.)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Fix] mamba: Make the lazy full-pool KL test hold across GPUs
author: hnyls2002
body:
- `TestMambaLazyFullPoolKL` (added in #48328) asserted KL < 1e-4 between the boundary-decode reuse and a reference built with a different prefill split (a 64-token extend vs a 127-token extend). That holds bit for bit on SM90, where GDN prefill defaults to FlashInfer, but not on an RTX 5090 (Triton prefill): KL 4.84e-3 with a correct state.
- Compare the reuse with a second reference: the same 255-token prefill without the boundary decode. Same kernels on the same shapes, so the distributions must match bit for bit; any difference is a reuse bug.
- Keep the different-split reference under a KL bound of 3e-3. On an RTX 5090 with random prompts, split noise is 3.1e-4 to 8.2e-4 over 9 seeds; a checkpoint 16 or more tokens off gives 6.0e-3 or more.
- Use random token ids instead of `[42] * 128 + [43] * 127`. The repeated-token prompt saturates the linear-attention state: a checkpoint up to 32 tokens off stayed within the split noise.
- Verified on an RTX 5090: 3 runs pass (KL 3.78e-4); swapping the reused state for one 1 token off trips the bit-exact assertion; the old prompt fails the 3e-3 bound (KL 4.84e-3).
- Move the test from `1-gpu-large` to `1-gpu-small` (RTX 5090): it no longer depends on the SM90 FlashInfer GDN prefill default.
- Test-only change.

title: [Fix] diffusion: Keep explicit cuDNN attention inside LTX breakable CUDA graphs
author: BBuf
body:
Selecting `TORCH_CUDNN_SDPA` for LTX currently puts dense attention outside the breakable CUDA graph even when the layer opts into dense capture. The tested 30-step LTX-2.3 request executes 8,670 graph launches. This adds the explicit cuDNN backend to the existing allowlist, producing one graph segment and 30 serving launches.

The existing opt-in, SP=1, no-varlen and no-attention-metadata guards remain in effect. The change is one runtime line plus an extension of the existing CUDA regression to both SDPA backends and Local/USP attention. The test replays changed Q/K/V tensors and changed masks, checking exact outputs and the expected capture/break segment count.

- Frozen main baseline: `77c3bcbe2c28e1a6d1ad4121ee57231582d39bdc`.
- Final tested head: `b5cf24a03841935cc396b67cdb9522cfed993141`.
- vLLM-Omni baseline: `817d4c17feb702289a2d2b2cbacfd594c262b7a7`.

No compile or external Diffusers fallback. The archived SDK configuration supplies the checkpoint's LTX-2.3 architecture/parameter-name metadata; model arithmetic and weights are unchanged.

title: [Fix] gemm: Order the CuTe DSL kernels' TMEM release after the epilogue's tcgen05.ld
author: bastianhagedorn
body:
## Motivation

Three CuTe DSL GEMM kernels in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/` release TMEM through a two-round mbarrier (`bar_tmem_alloc` or `tmem_ready`, 160 arrivals = 32 MMA + 128 EPILOG): round 0 publishes the TMEM allocation, round 1 says the epilogue has read the accumulator. The MMA warp makes its round-0 arrival after `alloc_tmem`, runs the K-loop, makes its round-1 arrival, waits with `mbarrier_wait(bar, 1)` and deallocates. It never waits for round 0.

If an EPILOG warp has not yet made its first arrival when the MMA warp arrives the second time, that arrival counts toward round 0, round 0 stays open, and the parity-1 wait returns immediately: parity 1 then names the barrier's "immediately preceding phase", which is complete by definition (PTX ISA, [`mbarrier.test_wait` / `mbarrier.try_wait`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/#parallel-synchronization-and-communication-instructions-mbarrier-test-wait-try-wait)). `tcgen05.dealloc` then runs before the epilogue's `tcgen05.ld`. In the 2-CTA tactics the non-leader CTA's MMA warp skips the K-loop (`if is_leader:`), so its two arrivals are back to back and the race is against the EPILOG warps' first few instructions.

This is the same race that flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6786 reported and flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7443 fixed in FlashInfer's split-K kernel. The three SGLang kernels still have the original sequence:

- `cutedsl_bf16_gemm.py` (TGV BF16 GEMM, a copy of FlashInfer's `tgv_gemm_cute_ext.py`; the upstream fix is flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#8787, this PR applies the identical change so the two files stay in sync).
- `cutedsl_dual_gemm.py` (dual GEMM + SwiGLU), found in review. Its default paired tactic (64 features, 2-CTA, 112 KB shared memory, several feature waves) is the one configuration where nothing in the launch masks the race: the non-leader skips the K-loop and the next wave's clusters can take the freed columns.
- `dense_bf16_gemm_sm100_splitk_epilogue.py` (vendored FlashInfer split-K kernel, predates flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7443), found in review.

As shipped the TGV race is latent: the launch requests the full shared-memory capacity, so no other CTA can be co-resident and the freed TMEM columns are not reallocated before the CTA exits; the output stays correct. It becomes visible when two EPILOG warps of the non-leader CTA are held back before their first arrival and the shared-memory request is trimmed so two GEMM CTAs share an SM: on a B200 (CUDA 13.0) the unfixed kernel then returns wrong rank-1 output tiles in 14 to 18 of 50 launches (tactic 16, 4096 CTAs, 10 to 100 µs stall) and the fixed kernel in 0 of 50; the 1-CTA tactics show the same with the stall in every CTA (20/20 wrong, 0/20 fixed).

## Modifications

1. `mbarrier_wait(bar, 0)` before the MMA warp's release arrival, in all three kernels. In the leader and in the 1-CTA tactics this wait is already satisfied by the time the K-loop ends; in the non-leader CTA it waits for the EPILOG warps' first arrival.
2. 2-CTA only (TGV and dual GEMM): a 32-count `bar_tmem_dealloc` / `tmem_dealloc` mbarrier on which the two MMA warps rendezvous (arrive on the peer's word, wait on ours) before `tcgen05.dealloc.cta_group::2`. The PTX ISA section on `tcgen05.alloc` / `tcgen05.dealloc` / `tcgen05.relinquish_alloc_permit` ([link](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/#tcgen05-instructions-tcgen05-alloc-dealloc-relinquish-alloc-permit)) describes that instruction as one collective operation of the CTA pair and requires that the "issuing warp and peer CTA warp must synchronize Tensor Memory accesses before attempting to collectively deallocate"; `cutlass.utils.TmemAllocator.free` does the same handshake. The TGV comment that said the 2-CTA dealloc is "per-CTA, no cross-CTA handshake" is replaced. This part is ISA conformance rather than a fix for an observed failure and can be dropped if the minimal change is preferred.
3. `tcgen05.fence::before_thread_sync` after each warp's `fence_view_async_tmem_load` (and the SFB warps' `fence_view_async_tmem_store`) before the release arrival, and `tcgen05.fence::after_thread_sync` between the MMA warp's final wait and `dealloc_tmem`, in all three kernels, following the PTX ISA's canonical tcgen05 patterns as flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7443 did.
4. The split-K copy still defers the rest of #7443 to a separate sync-up of the vendored file: the fences after `alloc_tmem`, after the `bar_full` wait and after the epilogue's `bar_tmem_alloc` / `bar_mma_epilog` waits, and the `.acquire.cluster` wait on `bar_reduce`.

Three files changed. The TGV diff is the same as the FlashInfer PR.

## Accuracy Tests

The existing unit tests cannot trigger the race (it needs an injected stall and a trimmed shared-memory request); they pass before and after. The injected-stall comparison against an fp32 reference described above is the accuracy evidence for the TGV kernel: 0 wrong tiles in 50 launches with the fix under the perturbation that gives 14 to 18 wrong launches without it, and bitwise-identical output to the unfixed kernel when unperturbed.

Dual GEMM and split-K copy, B200: every tactic of each kernel (bf16/fp16 tactics 0-3, FP8 tactics 0-7 in dynamic per-token and static per-tensor mode, the paired 64-feature tactics also on a 16384-wide intermediate; split-K 1/2/4 on five shapes), 20 launches each, compared against an fp32 reference with the unit tests' tolerances: 0 mismatching launches in all 43 configurations for both the original and the patched file (20 launches each). The TGV stall-injection regression on the patched files: 0/20 launches wrong (SGLang and FlashInfer copies), 7/20 for the original in the same run. Run log attached to the review thread on request.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not measured. The added wait is satisfied before it is reached in the leader and in every 1-CTA tactic; the handshake is one cross-CTA mbarrier arrive/wait per CTA.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (No new test, see Accuracy Tests.)
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (Not applicable.)
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Accuracy above; speed not measured.)

title: [Fix] scheduler: Match arrival prefixes on every PP stage
author: alphabetc1
body:
With pipeline parallelism, HiCache L3 storage, and `buffer_only` host memory, only the first stage matched a request's prefix on arrival. If grammar compilation delayed enqueueing, this could leave cache LRU state different across stages and cause subsequent evictions to produce different prefix lengths.

This PR matches the arrival prefix on every pipeline stage before grammar waiting, while keeping prefetch ticket creation on the first stage. A focused regression test reproduces the prefix mismatch caused by asymmetric Mamba checkpoint eviction and checks that arrival matching preserves the same checkpoint across stages.

The arrival hook now checks `controller.pp_prefetch_command_group` directly after a null-controller check, so eligibility follows the initialized ticket channel without `getattr` or duplicate mode/PP-size gates. The regression fixture also covers a disabled channel. Six isolated controller/rank cases and commit lint checks passed; GPU regressions were not rerun for this follow-up.

title: [Fix] comfyui: Load FastH3, H3 FP8, Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo and community INT8 single files
author: niehen6174
body:
## Motivation

Two official ComfyUI single-file checkpoints failed with `SGLDUNETLoader` in SGLD integrated mode, so every workflow built on them broke:

- **FastH3**: the official ComfyUI FastH3 templates load FastVideo's single files (`fastvideo_fasth3_8step_v2_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors`, `fasth3_omniref_8step_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors`). `SGLDUNETLoader` rejected them and pointed to the native directory loader.
- **Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo**: Comfy-Org's `qwen_image_2.1_turbo_int8_convrot.safetensors` stores a `comfy_attention.config` tensor on 31 blocks. This is ComfyUI's per-layer attention-kernel hint, `{"attention": "comfy_kitchen_int8"}`. The checkpoint loader passed these keys through, and the worker died at init with `Parameter transformer_blocks.1.attn.comfy_attention.config not found in custom model state dict`.

Three more ComfyUI single-file / checkpoint cases failed the same way:

- **MiniMax-H3 FP8-scaled**: Comfy-Org's `minimax_h3_*_pruned_fp8_scaled.safetensors`, the RTX 40 default, was rejected. The H3 single-file path accepted only INT8 ConvRot markers, although the quantization resolver already serves `float8_e4m3fn`.
- **Community INT8 files**: some converters (e.g. the Cobijada H3 hybrid) write `_quantization_metadata` layer names relative to the diffusion model, while the tensors keep the `model.diffusion_model.` prefix. ComfyUI strips that prefix before matching; SGLD reported every layer as missing `comfy_quant` metadata.
- **Qwen-Image 2.1 latents with an odd side**: request sizes are rounded to 32 px, so a ComfyUI latent with an odd side (1776 px → 111 rows) failed the post-denoise reshape.

## Modifications

**FastH3 single files**
- The H3 ComfyUI checkpoint spec turns on `has_gate_compress` when the file has `.attn.to_gate_compress.` keys.
- The VSA gate is built with the checkpoint's quant config only when the file carries a quant marker for it; FastVideo's Comfy file stores it as INT8 ConvRot. Without a marker, it stays BF16 and unquantized as before, so the native release is unchanged.
- The plugin defaults such files to `video_sparse_attn_h3` at the trained 0.8 sparsity, set before the worker-reuse key is built. It applies the same gates as the native FastH3 loader, which this PR factors into shared `vsa_h3_device_supported` / `vsa_h3_execution_supported` helpers:
  - a GPU with VSA-H3 kernels (sm80, sm90, sm100, sm103);
  - no torch.compile, breakable CUDA graph or ring attention.
- Elsewhere, attention stays dense, so `auto` keeps working on, for example, RTX 4090/5090. An explicit `attention_backend` wins.
- Ref2VA files stay dense, because VSA-H3 does not tile the ComfyUI Ref2VA layout. They are recognized from FastVideo's header (`source: transformer_ref`), with `ref2va` / `omniref` in the file name as the fallback.

**Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo single files**
- Skip `.comfy_attention.config` keys in the Qwen-Image 2.1 weight conversion; the worker selects its own attention kernel.

**MiniMax-H3 FP8-scaled single files** (`runtime/loader/comfyui_checkpoints/spec.py`)
- For H3 specs without `quant_markers`, accept the formats verified end to end: `int8_tensorwise` and `float8_e4m3fn`.
- The error names the unsupported formats: `w6a8_int8` has no SGLD kernel, and `nvfp4` is not verified on this path. Other models are unchanged.

**Quantization metadata without the model prefix** (`runtime/utils/quantization_utils.py`)
- An exact `{layer}.weight` match still wins.
- Otherwise the first existing prefixed name among `model.diffusion_model.`, `diffusion_model.` and `model.` is used. Files that matched before are unchanged.
- Each entry maps to one name, and a conflicting `.comfy_quant` marker for the same layer still raises.

**Odd Qwen-Image 2.1 latent sides** (`configs/pipeline_configs/qwen_image21.py`, Qwen-Image 2.1 ComfyUI stage)
- The ComfyUI condition stage records the latent's real height and width, and `post_denoising_loop` reshapes with them.
- Without that record it falls back to `height // 16, width // 16`, so normal `sglang serve` requests never set it and are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Unit tests on H200 after rebasing onto current main:
- ComfyUI adapters/checkpoint-spec/generator/H3/LoRA-node/options/profile/Qwen-Image 2.1/session, H3 DiT contract and the Qwen-Image 2.1 suites: **356 passed** (11 skipped, 3 xfailed).
- With the FastH3 gate change, the ComfyUI suites plus `test_minimax_h3_fasth3.py`, `test_minimax_h3_vae_fast_path.py` and `test_server_args.py`: **458 passed**, 3 xfailed. One cold-import test fails in that environment because of a broken local `flash_attn` 2 build, and it fails the same way on main.

Coverage:
- `test_comfyui_generator.py`: the FastH3 rejection case is replaced by tests of the attention default:
  - FastH3 gets VSA, while OmniRef stays dense by name or by header;
  - an explicit backend is kept;
  - an unsupported GPU, torch.compile, the CUDA graph or ring stays dense.
- `test_comfyui_qwen_image21.py`: a Turbo-style `comfy_attention.config` key is dropped.

End to end on H200 with the official templates, swapping only the loader to `SGLDUNETLoader`. All of these failed before.
- Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo text-to-image template: SSIM 0.907 vs stock ComfyUI.
- FastH3 outputs look fine but are not frame-identical to stock ComfyUI. Stock uses `BlockSparseAttention`, while SGLD uses the VSA-H3 attention the model was distilled with.

With the three additional fixes, on current main:
- the ComfyUI suites, `test_transformer_quant.py`, the Qwen-Image 2.1 suites and `test_minimax_h3_fasth3.py` give **483 passed** (11 skipped, 3 xfailed) on H200;
- new tests: `test_comfyui_checkpoint_spec.py` (FP8 accepted; `nvfp4` / `w6a8_int8` rejected), `test_transformer_quant.py` (metadata without the prefix) and `test_comfyui_qwen_image21.py` (odd latent side through the final reshape).

title: [Fix] tbo: Capture routed experts at each child's parent rows
author: algebra-MCX
body:
## Why

With `--enable-two-batch-overlap`, `return_routed_experts` returns wrong ids. Both TBO children write the shared device buffer from row 0, while readback uses parent batch order, so one child overwrites the other and the remaining rows stay zero or stale. Generated tokens are not affected.

Non-EP DP TBO (DeepSeek V4) has a second mismatch: its MoE captures every DP rank's padded rows, while readback uses the parent's DP offset.

## What

- Pass `tbo_parent_token_range` through `ForwardContext` and write each child's real rows at that range.
- For non-EP DP TBO, also pass this rank's parent offset (`tbo_parent_dp_offset`). Capture reads the rank's rows from the child's gather and writes them at that offset.

Non-TBO paths are unchanged.

## Verification

**DeepEP:** Qwen3-30B-A3B FP8, 2×H200, `--tp-size 2 --attn-dp-size 2`, 48 greedy tokens. Requests whose routes differ from TBO off, by rank load (token diff is 0 throughout):

| Load | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `[32,32]` | 64/64 | 0/64 |
| `[3,29]` | 32/32 | 16/32 |
| `[1,31]` | 32/32 | 1/32 |
| `[0,32]` | 32/32 | 0/32 |
| `[8,8]` | 16/16 | 0/16 |

"Before" ran on an earlier main (8884b4b421). Zero ids drop from about 37% to 1.13%, matching TBO off.

The remaining `[3,29]` and `[1,31]` diffs are all in decode. TBO off shows the same pattern when only the batch layout changes (`[8,8]` vs `[32,32]`), so they look like numeric sensitivity to batch shape. That cause is inferred, not proven.

**Non-EP DP:** DeepSeek V4 architecture with 8 layers and seeded dummy weights, 4×H200, `--tp 4 --attn-dp-size 4`, 249 requests pinned to DP ranks with even and uneven loads, prefill rows only. Rows that differ from TBO off, excluding the hash layer:

| Code | Rows differing | All-zero rows |
|---|---|---|
| Before this mapping (34b5786806) | 89123/155949 (ranks 1–3 only) | 62918 |
| After | 0/155949 | 0 |

The real DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 FP4 checkpoint did not get through startup in this DP setup on H200, so non-EP DP is not verified with real weights.

Not tested: `attn_tp > 1`, NIXL.

EP backends other than DeepEP also need the readback fix in `573f076785` under DP attention; that commit is not part of this PR.

This overlaps with `capture()` changes in #47554.

title: [Fix] sgl-router: Keep a worker's cached chain visible when another worker holds its prefix
author: ShangmingCai
body:
## Motivation

An engine publishes `BlockStored` only when it inserts a radix node, so a router that subscribes after the engines cached a shared prefix (a system prompt) never sees it. Every later chain then arrives under an unknown parent, is rooted as an orphan, and the match has to re-anchor on it. In production this showed up as router cache-hit routing dropping from 0.77 to 0.05 of decisions after each router rollout.

On main, two common cases still lose a worker's chain, and routing falls back to whichever worker holds only the shared prefix:

1. **The re-anchor runs only on a zero root match.** As soon as any worker re-announces the shared prefix from the root (a restarted or flushed engine, e.g. during a rolling prefill restart), the root match is non-zero, the re-anchor is skipped, and every deeper orphan chain on other workers is ignored.
2. **A chain hung under another worker's node scores zero.** When the parent hash has exactly one carrier, `resolve_parent` / `route_insert` attach the new chain under it even if the storing worker does not hold that node. `prefix_depths` (what cache-aware routing reads) counts a worker from level 1, so that worker's whole chain is invisible, and stays invisible after the other worker drops the parent. `match_prefix` meanwhile reports the chain correctly, so the two lookups disagree.

Both routes count as `decision="cache_hit"`, so the decision metric does not show them.

## Modifications

- `HashTree::match_prefix` / `prefix_depths`: run the chain-root re-anchor unless the root-anchored match already covers the whole query, keeping the deepest match per worker.
- `route_insert` / `resolve_parent`: attach a chain only under a parent carrier the storing worker holds. Otherwise root-attach it as an orphan (breadcrumb kept), the same path the ambiguous-parent case already used, so the re-anchor finds it. The contiguity rule in `prefix_depths` (an interior hole stops the count) is unchanged.
- Tests: two regression tests in `tree.rs` (both fail on main). `depth_is_a_fraction_and_a_tail_without_block_zero_misses` in `prefix_cache.rs` asserted the second bug (a chain stored under block 1 means its engine holds blocks 0 and 1), so it now expects the tail worker to be credited. `unowned_ambiguous_parent_force_roots_even_on_carrier_shard` checks tree structure, so it now walks the shard directly instead of the re-anchoring tree-level match.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: routing only, no model output change.

Live A/B on 2x B300: two engines (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, page size 16, ZMQ KV events), the same request sequence through a router built from main and from this branch. Engines were warmed with a 2928-token shared prefix before the router started; each session adds about 1k tokens. Ownership is read from per-engine `sglang:prompt_tokens_total`.

| Step | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Sessions known only as orphan chains on B, then A is flushed and re-stores the shared prefix from root; next turn | 4/4 to A, 68% cached | 4/4 to B, 96% cached |
| A has announced the shared prefix; new sessions are stored on B, then their next turn | 4/4 to A, 71% cached | 4/4 to B, 96% cached |

`cargo test --tests` in `sgl-router`: 1495 passed, 0 failed. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The re-anchor now also runs on partial root matches, i.e. most requests (the newest turn is uncached). It costs one shard read lock and one map probe per query block. Release-mode timing of `prefix_depths` with half of the query cached:

| Workers | Query blocks | Root walk only | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | 128 | 6.2 us | 4.8 us |
| 64 | 512 | 16.9 us | 20.2 us |
| 64 | 2048 | 68.6 us | 82.9 us |

About 7 ns per query block, small next to tokenizing and hashing the same prompt (2048 blocks is 128k tokens at block size 64).

title: [Fix] hicache: Do not count staged-prefetch deferrals while KV awaits a PD transfer
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

In HiCache buffer mode a staged L3 prefix must fit in GPU KV at admission. When admission fails on the token budget and nothing is running, `PrefillAdder._defer_staged_for_capacity_if_idle` counts the scheduler pass as a deferral, and after `max_staged_admission_defers` passes the buffer pipeline drops the staged copy so the request recomputes its prefix.

On a disaggregated prefill engine that count is wrong: finished prefills keep their KV until the decode side has pulled it (`Scheduler.disagg_prefill_transfer_queue`). While those transfers hold the pool, the running batch is empty, so every scheduler pass looks idle to the adder, the deferral budget is spent while the transfers are still in flight, and the staged prefix is dropped although the transfers free the memory shortly afterwards. The request then recomputes the whole prefix it already had in L3.

```text
PD prefill engine, buffer-mode HiCache:

  pool: [ KV of finished prefills, awaiting decode transfer ........ ][free]
  staged L3 prefix needs more than [free]  ->  NO_TOKEN
  running batch empty                      ->  "idle" -> defers += 1
  ... repeated every pass until defers == max_staged_admission_defers
  staged copy dropped -> transfers complete -> prefix recomputed from scratch
```

## Modifications

- `PrefillAdder` takes a new keyword `kv_awaiting_transfer: bool = False`. The scheduler passes `bool(self.disagg_prefill_transfer_queue)`.
- `_defer_staged_for_capacity_if_idle` returns without counting a deferral while `kv_awaiting_transfer` is set, exactly as it already does while `can_run_list` or the running batch is non-empty: in all three cases capacity is released on its own, so the failure is not an idle one. With an empty transfer queue (every non-PD-prefill scheduler) the count and its limit are unchanged.
- Every rank makes the same decision with no new collective: the transfer queue is advanced from the all-reduced poll in `process_disagg_prefill_transfer_queue`, so it is identical across ranks.
- A transfer that fails frees its KV and leaves the queue, so the wait ends; a transfer that stalls holds its KV for every request until the transport times out, and dropping the staged copy would not let this request run either, since recomputing its prefix needs the same KV. No new stuck state is added.

Tests:

- `test_prefill_adder.py`: `test_idle_budget_failure_defers_staged_prefix_unless_kv_awaits_transfer` builds an adder with an empty running batch and a `buffer_pipeline`, admits a request larger than the pool, and asserts `NO_TOKEN` in both cases, `defer_staged_admission(req, "prefill_budget")` called once without the flag and not at all with it. On the current code the flag case fails with `TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'kv_awaiting_transfer'`.
- `test_scheduler_held_row_admission.py` and `test_lora_pp.py`: the fake schedulers built with `Scheduler.__new__` get the `disagg_prefill_transfer_queue` attribute the scheduler now reads next to `disagg_prefill_bootstrap_queue`; without it three cases fail with `AttributeError` at the `PrefillAdder(...)` call. The fakes in `test_scheduler_running_reqs.py` go through `empty_request_lists()`, which already sets that attribute, so that file is unchanged.

Local run of the four touched files, CPU only:

```
pytest test/registered/unit/managers/test_prefill_adder.py \
       test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_held_row_admission.py \
       test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_running_reqs.py \
       test/registered/unit/lora/test_lora_pp.py
73 passed, 64 subtests passed
```

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no change to the model forward, sampling, or to which KV a request is served from. The change only affects when a staged L3 copy is released on a PD prefill engine.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

On a PD prefill engine with buffer-mode HiCache, a staged prefix that cannot be admitted only because finished prefills still hold their KV is now kept until the transfers release the memory, instead of being dropped and recomputed. Non-PD schedulers and PD engines with an empty transfer queue take the same path as before.

| `c03b6b3df5` | **3.4595** | fix-mamba-copy-from-temporal-oom |
| `06c60f412a` | **3.4595** | #48715 |

The only PR that still passes on these bases is #48468 (FlashInfer 0.7.3), which changes the MXFP4 MoE runner Kimi-K3 uses and so changes its numerics anyway.

Of the main commits in `b147f4aa10..1305b1830a`, only #47683 reaches Kimi-K3's TP8 + DSpark decode path:

- #47866 (CuTe DSL KDA decode) only runs with `--linear-attn-decode-backend cutedsl`; this test uses triton.
- #47678 (DFlash decode prep) fills the same buffers.
- #47785 (Qwen3 QK norm) and #48588 (DSA DCP top-k) do not reach Kimi-K3.
- The rest are docs, NPU, AMD, CI and diffusion.

#47683 makes the tiny GEMM switch from the SIMT to the MMA kernel at a batch size picked per shape. Each kernel alone is batch invariant, but a row's result depends on the batch through that switch. Kimi-K3 runs its KDA gate and router projections through `kimi_k3_tiny_gemm`:

| (N, K) | MMA from m = | bs=1 decode (m = 1) | 8-token verify (m = 8) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 144 × 7168 | 2 (cost model, B300) | SIMT | MMA |
| 896 × 7168 | 2 (cost model, B300) | SIMT | MMA |
| 1536 × 128 | 8 (tuned) | SIMT | MMA |

So the same token's gates round differently in decode and in speculative verify.

## Modifications

Pin the three Kimi-K3 shapes to SIMT at every m in `_TUNED_MMA_MIN_M`, as `128x512` already is. Other tiny GEMM callers (DeepSeek routers, DeepSeek-V4.1, beam, dots3) use other shapes and are unchanged.

## Validation

**Draft until confirmed:** I had no free B300 to bisect on, so the root cause above comes from elimination plus the dispatch rule. `/rerun-test` of the failing test on this PR decides it.

- If it passes, this goes ready for review.

title: [Fix] spec: Make per-step draft `out_cache_loc` contiguous for KV writes
author: hnyls2002
body:
- `per_step_draft_out_cache_loc` returned strided rows: `view(bs, topk, steps).permute(2, 0, 1).reshape(steps, -1)` stays a view, and `EagleDraftWorker.draft_forward` writes step `i` at `out_cache_loc[i]`. The Triton MLA KV write (`set_mla_kv_buffer_triton`) reads `loc` by flat offset, so with `bs * topk > 1` a draft step wrote request 1's KV into request 0's next-step slot and never wrote its own; under CUDA graph replay, padding rows' KV landed there instead.
- This is why `attention/unittests/mla/test_flashinfer.py` (`test_runner_mode_eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner_cases`) fails on main since #48005 (max abs diff 43). #48005 made FlashInfer MLA draft steps attend to their own earlier draft tokens; before it, eager and graph both read only the prefix, so the misplaced writes were never read.
- Return a contiguous tensor from `per_step_draft_out_cache_loc`, and drop the two local workarounds it replaces: the `.contiguous()` in `draft_step_writes` and the `Qwen3MoeForCausalLMMTP` special case in `draft_forward`.
- `KVWriteLoc` and `unwrap_write_loc` raise on a non-contiguous `loc`, `swa_loc`, or `full_loc`, so a strided write loc fails at the write door instead of silently writing other rows' slots.
- Behavior change: MLA EAGLE/MTP drafts with `bs * topk > 1` now write each draft token's KV at its own slot, which is expected to raise draft acceptance; outputs are unchanged, since verify is exact.
- Verified on an H200: `mla/test_flashinfer.py` passes (fails without this change); `mla/test_triton.py`, `mla/test_flashmla.py`, `dense/test_flashinfer.py`, `dense/test_triton.py`, `dense/test_fa3.py`, `dense/test_trtllm_mha.py`, `dsv4/test_deepseek_v4.py`, `unit/spec/test_eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py`, `unit/layers/attention/test_cuda_graph_window_rail_completeness.py`, and `unit/mem_cache/test_physical_write_loc.py` (new cases) pass.

title: [Fix] rust-server: Publish 127.0.0.1 for an IPv6 loopback SGLANG_HOST_IP on an IPv4 wildcard bind
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

An engine that runs the Rust frontend on `--host 0.0.0.0` refuses to start when `SGLANG_HOST_IP` is `::1`:

```
ValueError: SGLANG_RUST_SERVER: DP rank 0 listens on IPv4 at 0.0.0.0 but advertises http://[::1]:30000; set --host to :: or SGLANG_HOST_IP to an IPv4 address
```

`RustServer._advertised_host` replaces a wildcard bind with `get_local_ip_auto()`, which returns `SGLANG_HOST_IP` of either address family, and `gather_server_endpoints` refuses an IPv4 listener that advertises an IPv6 address. The refusal is right in general: peers and routers dial the published URL, and an IPv4 listener does not serve an IPv6 address. But `::1` names this machine, which the IPv4 wildcard listener serves at `127.0.0.1`. Disaggregated prefill/decode deployments export `SGLANG_HOST_IP` for their KV-transfer endpoints, and a single-machine pair that sets it to `::1` could not run the Rust frontend at all.

## Modifications

- `RustServer._advertised_host`: when the bind is `0.0.0.0` and the detected address is an IPv6 loopback address, publish `127.0.0.1`. Any other IPv6 address on an IPv4 bind is still refused by `gather_server_endpoints`, an IPv6 wildcard bind (`::`) still publishes the detected address as is, and the multi-node loopback warning is unchanged.
- `test_rust_server_extension.py`: `test_gather_server_endpoints_checks_bind_family_on_every_rank` becomes `test_gather_server_endpoints_publishes_an_address_the_bind_serves`. It sets `SGLANG_HOST_IP` and goes through the real `get_local_ip_auto()`, covering `0.0.0.0` and `::` binds with an IPv4, an IPv6 loopback and a global IPv6 address, on listener and non-listener ranks.

#47534 derives the advertised host differently (an environment override, then the interface that routes towards the rendezvous address). This change keeps the current advertised-host choice and only maps an IPv6 loopback address onto the IPv4 listener.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable (no numerics).

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Not applicable (startup-time host selection only).

## Checklist

- Ran `test/registered/unit/multimodal/rust/shared/test_rust_server_extension.py` on CPU against this branch (13 passed, 18 subtests passed). With the new test against `main`'s `server.py`, the two `0.0.0.0` + `::1` subtests fail with the refusal quoted above and the other subtests pass.
- pre-commit passes on both changed files.

title: [Fix] scheduler: Abort beam groups on a retract pause and close three request-drop gaps
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Summary

Four small fixes for requests that a pause, a memory release, an abort, or a PD role switch could leave in a broken state.

## Changes

- **Beam groups on a retract pause.** `pause_generation(mode="retract")` now aborts live beam groups instead of requeueing their leaders. `retract_all` frees each leader's member rows before its KV is released and records the abort reason, which is the same path `ScheduleBatch.retract_decode` takes under KV pressure. The running batch is now emptied through `filter_batch`, so its beam tail is stripped with the requests. Before this change, the stale tail tripped `reqs changed while a beam tail was attached` on the first `filter_batch` after resume. A pause-retracted beam leader that could not resume also leaked its member rows.
- **`release_memory_occupation` on a busy scheduler.** The idle check was a bare `assert`, which crashed the scheduler, or was skipped under `python -O`. The scheduler now returns a refusal instead: `ReleaseMemoryOccupationReqOutput` carries `success` and `message`, and the check runs before any memory is paused. A refused release must not be silent for callers that ignore return values, so `TokenizerManager.release_memory_occupation` raises `RuntimeError` with the merged message, and `Engine.release_memory_occupation` raises with it. `/release_memory_occupation` turns the error into a 400 through its existing error path. The later `flush_cache()` cannot be refused, because its idle gate is the same check.
- **Abort of a HiSparse-staged request.** After prefill, a HiSparse request waits in the staging list until its host copy lands, and it is in no batch while it waits. An abort that arrived after the prefill batch had moved on matched nothing, so the request ran to completion. `collect_inflight_reqs` now includes staged requests. The abort marks them, and they finish at their first decode step, as a running request does.
- **PD role switch with held requests.** `is_fully_idle` deliberately skips requests held by a retract pause (`PD_HELD`), so that a weight update can flush the cache. The role switch used the same check, so it tore down the decode queues and dropped the held requests without answering them. The switch now rejects with `safe_to_restore=True` while any request is held.

## Behavior changes

- During a retract pause, a beam-search request is aborted with 503 and is not resumed after the pause.
- `release_memory_occupation` on a busy scheduler no longer crashes the scheduler. `Engine.release_memory_occupation` raises `RuntimeError`, and `/release_memory_occupation` returns 400 with the message. A successful release returns what it returned before.
- An abort sent while a request is in HiSparse staging now finishes it.
- A PD role switch during a retract pause that holds requests is rejected until generation resumes and the held requests drain.

## Test plan

- [x] `test_scheduler_pause_generation.py::test_retract_aborts_beam_groups_and_drops_the_beam_tail`: fails before the fix and passes after.
- [x] `test_scheduler_timeouts.py::test_hisparse_staged_request_is_finished_at_its_next_step`: fails before the fix and passes after.
- [x] `test_pd_role_switch.py::test_rejected_while_a_retract_pause_holds_requests`: fails before the fix and passes after.
- [x] The existing CPU unit tests for the touched paths pass when each file runs on its own: beam search, pause, timeouts, weight updater, flush cache, io_struct and msgpack round trip, HiSparse, abort cleanup, PD role switch, decode queue cleanup, and the MLX scheduler mixin. The MLX mixin test's batch mock now applies `filter_batch`.
- [ ] GPU: a beam-search run with a retract pause and resume.

title: [Fix] multimodal: Fail bad client media with a client error
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Port of #48414

Takes the media-input hardening from the Kimi-K3.1 Day-0 branch and finishes it for every loader: bad client media fails the request as a client error (400), and server-side invariant failures are no longer reported as one. The HEIF opener and the new image extensions from the same branch are in #49673.

## Summary

On main, these reach the server as a 500 or hang a worker:

- A local path that is a FIFO hangs the reading worker; `/dev/zero` grows memory without bound (8.5 GB in 4 s for an image); a directory or missing path is a 500.
- A raw base64 JPEG (it starts with `/9j/`) is opened as a file path and fails with a 500.
- On the Kimi `_load_single_item` path, `snapshot_media` and `decode_media_snapshot`, an unreachable URL, a timeout or a decompression bomb is a 500, because those paths skip the client-error mapping the base processor does.

With this PR:

- **One local-file reader** (`read_local_media_file` / `check_local_media_file` in `multimodal/media_io.py`) for images, video and audio, and for the loaders that read paths themselves (Inkling, MiMo, MoSS-VL). It opens with `O_NONBLOCK` (a FIFO fails at once), accepts only regular files, caps the size at `--media-url-max-file-size-mb`, and turns a missing, directory, looping or socket path into a `ValueError` (400). Permission errors stay 500s.
- **Two server args**, next to `--allowed-media-domains` and `--media-url-max-file-size-mb` and applied the same way (also to spawned CPU workers):
  - `--media-url-timeout`: one download timeout for every media loader. Default: unset, so each loader keeps its timeout (`REQUEST_TIMEOUT` if set, else its own default).
  - `--allow-local-media-files` (default on; `--no-allow-local-media-files` to reject local paths and `file://` URLs). Rejection happens before any file probe, so the error does not reveal whether a file exists.
- A value that is neither valid base64 nor an existing file says both, instead of `Non-base64 digit found`.
- `snapshot_media`, `decode_media_snapshot` and the Kimi `_load_single_item` map client media failures to `ValueError`.
- Artifact-cache and Kimi-K3 processor invariant checks raise `RuntimeError` (500) instead of `ValueError`.

## Changes to existing code

Without the new args:

- Local image, video and audio files over `--media-url-max-file-size-mb` (64 MiB by default) are rejected; before, local files had no cap.
- `REQUEST_TIMEOUT` now also applies to the Inkling (30 s) and MiMo image (3 s) downloads, and is parsed as a float.
- A plain video path containing `#`, `?` or `%xx` loads the file it names (main checked one path and opened another).
- Spawned CPU workers (`cuda_vmm`) now get the server's media policy; before they fell back to the defaults.
- The cases in the Summary return 400 instead of 500 or hanging.

## Verification

- Probes against main and this branch for each loader: FIFO, `/dev/zero`, directory, missing path, symlink loop, over-cap file, raw `/9j/` base64, decompression bomb on the artifact path, unreachable URL on the Kimi path, and every loader with `--no-allow-local-media-files`.
- `cd test && python -m pytest -q registered/unit/multimodal/test_media_input_errors.py registered/unit/models/test_kimi_k25.py registered/unit/test_server_args_migration.py`: 79 passed. Every file under `registered/unit/multimodal/`, `registered/unit/server_args/` and `registered/unit/models/test_kimi_k25.py` fails no test that passes on main (local macOS, CPU).

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

Xeon CI checks out the PR's synthetic merge ref for its tests, but independently builds the image from the PR head branch. New main-branch test infrastructure can therefore run against an older installed Python package and CPU kernels.

This happened in sgl-project/sglang#46610: [the SPR job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42146835720/job/127660392975) failed before executing tests because the workspace's runner referenced `HWBackend.MLU`, but the PR-head package installed in the image did not define it.

The same branch-based build also fails to honor an explicitly selected `inputs.ref` consistently.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- Resolve the actual workspace commit with `git rev-parse HEAD`, and pass it to the Xeon image build instead of the PR branch name.
- Fetch the requested revision explicitly in the Dockerfile and check out `FETCH_HEAD` detached. This supports synthetic PR merge commits as well as existing branch/tag builds, including release images.
- Build both the Python package and CPU AOT kernels from that revision.
- Fail the workflow if the source SHA recorded in the built image differs from the workspace SHA.

No model/runtime algorithm changes.

title: [Fix] overlap: Skip deferred-relay flush when future_map is None
author: nvpohanh
body:
[by Claude Code]

## Motivation

Fixes #48808. Since #47200, every LLaDA-Image request fails with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'takes_deferred_relay'`. This breaks `llada_image_bf16_t2i` and `llada_image_bf16_edit` in `multimodal-gen-test-1-gpu (1)` on every PR based on current `main`, for example https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42128128424/job/127658012603.

The LLaDA-Image conditioning stage runs a standalone prefill and calls `resolve_forward_inputs(batch, None)`. #47200 added an unconditional `future_map.takes_deferred_relay(batch)` call at the top of `resolve_forward_inputs`, which raises on `None`.

## Modifications

- `resolve_forward_inputs` skips the deferred-relay flush when `future_map` is `None`, because a caller without a `FutureMap` has no deferred relay.
- The `future_map` parameter is annotated as `Optional[FutureMap]`.

This restores the pre-#47200 behavior for the LLaDA-Image caller. Scheduler callers always pass `self.future_map`, so their behavior is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A. No change to model outputs: this only restores the code path that LLaDA-Image used before #47200.

title: [Fix] [AMD] mxfp4: Keep MoE weight layout and dispatch consistent with the selected runner
author: haishuok0525
body:
## Motivation

On ROCm, `Mxfp4MoEMethod` decides whether to lay out weights for AITER from the raw `SGLANG_USE_AITER` flag in three places: weight padding in `create_weights`, the shuffle in `process_weights_after_loading`, and both `_apply_aiter` dispatch sites in `apply()` (standard and DeepEP). `create_moe_runner` uses a different rule. It honours an explicit `--moe-runner-backend`, and in auto mode it also requires an a2a backend that supports AITER.

When the two rules disagree, the weights and quant info are prepared for one runner while a different runner executes them. One example is gpt-oss on ROCm served with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` (for attention and allreduce) and an explicit `--moe-runner-backend triton`. The Triton runner then receives AITER-padded weights and an `AiterMoeQuantInfo`, and the server crashes during warmup:

```
AttributeError: 'AiterMoeQuantInfo' object has no attribute 'use_mxfp8'
```

The same mismatch happens with an explicit `aiter` backend when `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0`, and in auto mode when `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` but the a2a backend does not support AITER (the runner falls back to Triton, but the weights are still shaped for AITER).

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py`: compute `self.use_aiter_moe` once in `__init__`, using the same rule as `create_moe_runner`. An explicit runner backend decides; in auto mode the decision is `_use_aiter and get_moe_a2a_backend().supports_aiter()`. All five call sites that read `_use_aiter` now use this value, and so does the auto branch of `create_moe_runner`.
- `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_mxfp4_aiter_runner_selection.py` (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`): builds a real `Mxfp4MoEMethod` for 7 combinations of runner backend, `SGLANG_USE_AITER` and a2a backend. It checks that the weight layout and the `apply()` dispatch (standard and DeepEP formats) match the runner that `create_moe_runner` builds. It follows the pattern of `test_fp8_moe_runner_ownership.py`.
- `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_mxfp4_moe_layout.py` (AMD, `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`): loads MXFP4 weights into a real `FusedMoE` and runs a forward pass. Explicit Triton with AITER enabled must keep the Triton layout and match the output with AITER disabled. Explicit AITER must match Triton, and AUTO must match the explicit backend it selects. It follows the pattern of `test_compressed_tensors_fp8_moe_layout.py`.

## Accuracy Tests

Model: `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, run on 1x MI355X (gfx950) with image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.23-rocm720-mi35x-20261105` and `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`. The validation ran against base `e838360ffd`. The branch was later rebased onto `abfa0b0850`; the diff is byte-identical, and none of the touched or exercised files changed in between apart from the unrelated CUDA DeepGEMM runner. Accuracy is `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k` on all 1319 questions, run 3 times on each server.

| `--moe-runner-backend` | base | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `triton` | server crashes in warmup (`AiterMoeQuantInfo` has no `use_mxfp8`) | 0.541 / 0.542 / 0.572 |
| `auto` (selects AITER) | 0.528 / 0.519 / 0.527 | 0.538 / 0.537 / 0.522 |

The auto path takes the same code path before and after this change, so the difference between those two rows is run-to-run noise. This few-shot completion eval is not a good fit for the gpt-oss chat format (13-16% of answers are unparseable), so these numbers only show that the fixed Triton path serves correctly at the same accuracy level. They are not a quality benchmark.

Unit tests on the same machine:

- Base: the 3 inconsistent combinations fail in the layout test, the same 3 fail in the dispatch test (6 sub-cases), and the explicit-Triton layout test fails. The AUTO and explicit-AITER controls pass.
- This PR: every test passes and none are skipped.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No change for configurations that already worked; they keep their current runner and weight layout. Explicit Triton with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` used to crash at startup and now runs at about 7.4k output tok/s in the GSM8K run above, compared with about 11k tok/s on the AITER path.

title: [Fix] weight_checker: Compare weights on the live weight's device
author: HJSang
body:
## Motivation

Port of sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu#1825 to main.

The weight checker's `compare` action fails on non-CUDA engines (TPU today) with `Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled`: `RawComparable.iter_chunks` and `Fp8BlockComparable.iter_chunks` move every chunk to CUDA. RL trainers use `compare` to check a weight update end to end (snapshot, overwrite, update, compare), so on those engines the check cannot run. The `checksum` action is already device-agnostic; this does the same for `compare`.

## Modifications

- `ComparableWeight` reports its `device` (the raw tensor's, or the quantized weight's for FP8 block weights), and `iter_chunks(device)` moves each chunk there instead of to CUDA.
- `compare_weights` chunks both sides onto the live weight's device. The snapshot is a host copy, so it goes to CUDA on GPU engines, as before, and to the accelerator on other engines.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no forward or kernel change.

- TPU v7x, Qwen3-4B TP4, miles RL smoke with `--check-weight-update-equal` over shm and disk weight sync (on the torchtpu tree): `compare` failed before; with this change snapshot, reset and compare ran on all 4 TP ranks and passed for both sync modes.

title: [Fix] rust-server: Keep the DP control fan-out off an inherited HTTP proxy
author: metamergebot
body:
<!-- oss-sync ci-note:start -->
**CI status (oncall, 2026-11-06 21:40 PST):** this PR is in GitHub stack #48459, the Rust-server stack: #48455 → #48457 → #48512 → #48515 → #48518 → #48523 → #48572 → #48753 → #48797 → #48798 → #48818 → #48815 (top). Each PR keeps its own diff (parent branches and `main` were merged in, no rebase). This branch also carries #49008: that PR was based on this branch, so its squash merge landed here instead of `main`; its change reaches `main` when this PR merges. The CI bar for the whole stack is `pr-test.yml` with `pr-test-finish` green on the top #48815 (run 42341406709). Once that is green, approve and use **Merge stack** to land the chain in one atomic step.
<!-- oss-sync ci-note:end -->

Sits on #48512 (branch `oss-sync-219fe11113`): this pull request is the one commit on top of that branch, and only the last commit is this change. It needs #48512's `ApiKeys` parameter of `peer_endpoints`, which the new test passes. It is deliberately not linked into the existing pull request chain (#48455 → #48457 → #48512 → #48515 → ...): that chain is linear and already continues above #48512, and this one-file change should not hold its merge. Once #48512 lands this branch takes `main` and the base moves there.

## Motivation

In Rust-server mode the control routes (`/server_info`, `/flush_cache`, ...) fan out to the other DP ranks' listeners through a `reqwest::Client` built in `peer_endpoints` (`rust/sglang-server/src/api_server/core/peer.rs`). reqwest reads `http_proxy` / `HTTP_PROXY` / `all_proxy` from the environment when a client is built, so a server process that inherits an HTTP proxy relays every peer request through that proxy. The peers are this engine's own listeners, reachable directly; a forward proxy that refuses the destination, or cannot route to it, turns every DP control fan-out into the proxy's error (for example a 403 from the proxy instead of the peer's reply). CI runners and some hosts set these variables for every process they start.

## Modifications

- `rust/sglang-server/src/api_server/core/peer.rs`: build the peer client with `.no_proxy()`, so control requests to peer listeners never go through an inherited proxy.
- Test `control_peers_bypass_an_inherited_http_proxy`: starts an axum router that answers 403 to everything as the "proxy", points `http_proxy` / `HTTP_PROXY` / `all_proxy` / `ALL_PROXY` at it with `no_proxy` unset, then sends a control request to a peer listener and asserts the listener's reply arrives and the listener saw exactly one request. Because reqwest reads the proxy variables process-wide at client build time, the check body (`proxied_peer_child`, `#[ignore]`) runs alone in a child process spawned from the test binary with `--exact`; the parent asserts the child passed.

Without the `.no_proxy()` line the child test fails: the request goes to the 403 proxy, the peer sees nothing, and the control reply is the proxy's error.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no change to model outputs. `cargo test -p sglang-server` passes on this head, including the new test; `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean on the crate.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: one builder call at client construction.

title: [Fix] modelopt_fp4: Skip swizzled NVFP4 MoE blockscales on Marlin paths
author: nvpohanh
body:
[by Claude Code]

## Motivation

This continues #46192 by @JUNQINGV587, who is a co-author on the commit, and addresses the review comments left there.

`ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod.create_weights()` allocates an fp8 swizzled copy of every expert block scale (`w13_blockscale_swizzled` and `w2_blockscale_swizzled`). It skips this only for TRT-LLM and MegaMoE. The Marlin runner never reads this copy:

- `process_weights_after_loading()` returns right after `prepare_moe_nvfp4_layer_for_marlin()`.
- `apply()` reads the Marlin-repacked `w13_weight_scale` and `w2_weight_scale` through `get_marlin_quant_info()`.

So on SM80–SM90, where NVFP4 MoE falls back to Marlin, the copy stays allocated for the server's lifetime and takes memory away from the KV cache.

## Modifications

- `create_weights()` now also skips the swizzled copy for `marlin` (including `experimental_sgl_marlin`, via `is_marlin()`), `lora_marlin`, and `auto`:
  - `lora_marlin` is mapped to `MARLIN` in `process_weights_after_loading()`, and the LoRA layers read scales through `get_marlin_quant_info()`.
  - `create_moe_runner()` runs after `create_weights()`, so `auto` is still unresolved there. When a backend that reads the swizzled scales is used, `process_weights_after_loading()` rebinds them through `alias_or_bind_derived_param()`. So the eager copy is never needed for `auto`.
- The backend comes from a single `get_moe_runner_backend()` call. It no longer uses `getattr(self, "_moe_runner_backend", ...)`, because `create_moe_runner()` only sets that attribute after `create_weights()`.

### Review comments from #46192

| Comment | Resolution |
|---|---|
| Don't use `getattr()` | Replaced with `get_moe_runner_backend()`, read once and reused, including in the MegaMoE loader check. |
| `lora_marlin` still allocates the unused copy | Added `is_lora_marlin()` to the skip condition and covered it in the test. |
| 12-line comment that tells history and names the wrong mechanism | Replaced with two lines stating where AUTO is resolved (`create_moe_runner()`) and that `process_weights_after_loading()` rebinds the scales for every reader. |
| No test for the new condition | Not added; this PR keeps only the `modelopt_quant.py` change. The memory results below show the effect. |
| PR title format check | Title now uses `[Fix] modelopt_fp4: ...`. |

This also covers the Marlin-fallback case that #38092 targets.

## Accuracy Tests

Setup: one NVIDIA L40S (SM89), `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4`, TP=1, default server args. The MoE backend `auto` resolves to Marlin here.

Eval: sgl-eval 0.1.3, `gsm8k`, all 1319 examples, `enable_thinking=false`, `temperature=0.7`, `top_p=0.8`, `max_tokens=4096`, `seed=0` (Qwen3's recommended non-thinking sampling).

| | `main` (afe21bc) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K | 94.39% | 94.31% |

Greedy outputs on 8 prompts:

- Two runs of the same `main` build already differ on 2/8 prompts, so this setup is not deterministic from run to run.
- `main` vs. this PR differ on 2–3/8, which is within that noise.

The Marlin kernels read the same tensors before and after this change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Memory, same setup:

| `--moe-runner-backend` | Weights, `main` | Weights, this PR | KV tokens, `main` | KV tokens, this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `auto` (resolves to Marlin) | 18.72 GB | **17.06 GB** | 399,982 | **436,248** (+9.1%) |
| `marlin` | 18.72 GB | **17.06 GB** | 399,982 | **436,249** (+9.1%) |

The 1.66 GB saved matches the size of the swizzled copies: 48 layers × 128 experts × (1536×128 + 2048×48) B ≈ 1.69 GiB. The original PR reported a 3.48 GiB/rank saving on a larger NVFP4 MoE at TP=2.

There is no kernel change. GSM8K output throughput was 1142 vs. 1128 tok/s, which is within noise.

## Checklist

- [x] `pre-commit run --all-files` passes.
- [ ] Unit test: not added.
- [ ] Documentation update: not needed.
- [x] Accuracy and memory results are above.
- [x] Follows the SGLang code style.
