title: [Doc] cookbook: Fix Qwen3.8-Flash-Next thinking-mode description
author: VoyagerXvoyagerx
body:
Update the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next cookbook page so its reasoning/thinking and sampling guidance matches the released HF model card and the checkpoint's chat template.

<!-- PR title: [Doc] cookbook: Fix Qwen3.8-Flash-Next thinking-mode description -->

## Motivation

`docs/cookbook/autoregressive/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.mdx` states that the model "**always** reasons — thinking cannot be turned off". That contradicts the released checkpoint:

- The HF model card has a dedicated `Instruct (or Non-Thinking) Mode` section and documents `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}`.
- `tokenizer_config.json`'s chat template branches on `enable_thinking` when `add_generation_prompt` is set:

  ```jinja
  {%- if add_generation_prompt %}
      {{- '<|im_start|>assistant\n' }}
      {%- if enable_thinking is defined and enable_thinking is false %}
          {{- '<think>\n\n</think>\n\n' }}
      {%- else %}
          {{- '<think>\n' }}
      {%- endif %}
  {%- endif %}
  ```

Two related claims were also incorrect or missing, so they are fixed in the same pass:

1. "Qwen has not published sampling recommendations" — the model card publishes a preset for each mode, and `generation_config.json` (`temperature=1.0, top_k=20, top_p=0.95`) only matches the **thinking** preset, not the instruct one.
2. `preserve_thinking` (default `true`) is not mentioned anywhere, although it changes the prompt on every multi-turn / agentic request — and this page has a whole agentic long-context section.

## Modifications

Single file: `docs/cookbook/autoregressive/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.mdx`. No page, navigation, or `src/snippets/configs/` changes.

- **§1 Recommended generation** — replace the "no recommendations published" sentence with the two presets from the model card (thinking: `temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95, top_k=20, min_p=0.0, presence_penalty=0.0, repetition_penalty=1.0`; instruct: `temperature=0.7, top_p=0.80, top_k=20, min_p=0.0, presence_penalty=1.5, repetition_penalty=1.0`), and note that `generation_config.json` covers only the thinking preset.
- **§2.1 Reasoning** — thinking is on by default but can be disabled; describe the pre-filled `<think>` vs the pre-filled empty `<think></think>` block; add per-request (`chat_template_kwargs`) and server-wide (`--default-chat-template-kwargs`) switching; note that the checkpoint's tags are `<think>` / `</think>`, which the `qwen3` reasoning parser matches; document the `reasoning_effort` constraints enforced by the template (`xhigh`/`medium`/`low` only, no effect while thinking is disabled, and only `xhigh`/`low` inject a system-prompt instruction); document `preserve_thinking` and how to disable it; add Qwen's note that a lower `reasoning_effort` does not reliably reduce total agentic task time.
- **§2.2 Tool Calling** — replace "Because this model always thinks…" with the accurate explanation: with thinking on, a turn that stops inside the reasoning block (e.g. at the `max_tokens` cap) leaves `content` empty and puts the partial reasoning in `reasoning_content`; with `enable_thinking: false` the answer lands in `content` directly.
- **Both `Example Output` accordions** — replace the two stale "Pending update — a sample transcript will be added here once the weights are public" placeholders (the weights have been public for some time) with real transcripts captured on the hosted `qwen3.8-flash` endpoint, each with a one-line provenance note.
- **§2.2 example snippet, two lines only** — `print("Content:", msg.content)` → `repr(msg.content)` (an empty string otherwise prints a trailing space, which the `trailing-whitespace` pre-commit hook rejects, and it is indistinguishable from `None`), and `print("Tool calls:", msg.tool_calls)` → a list of `(name, arguments)` tuples, because the raw value is an `openai` SDK model repr that varies across SDK versions and cannot be shown verbatim as a stable example output. Happy to revert these two lines if reviewers prefer the original prints.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable — documentation only; no kernel, model-forward, or serving code is touched.

The behaviour described was verified against the checkpoint's config files rather than by running a local `sglang serve`: the chat-template branches and the `reasoning_effort` validation come from `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next`'s `tokenizer_config.json`, and the sampling values from its `generation_config.json` plus the model card.

The two sample transcripts in the page were captured from the hosted `qwen3.8-flash` endpoint (which the model card identifies as the production variant of this checkpoint):

- Reasoning example (`reasoning_effort: xhigh`, "What is 15% of 240?"): `finish_reason=stop`, 73 prompt / 55 completion tokens (39 reasoning), `content="15% of 240 is **36**."`
- Tool-calling example: `finish_reason=tool_calls`, 351 prompt / 48 completion tokens (19 reasoning), `content=''`, one `get_weather({"location": "Beijing"})` call.

Both outputs are labelled in the page as captured on the hosted endpoint, not from a local server.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable — documentation only.

title: [Fix] watchdog: Let py-spy attach to watched processes in CI
author: leejnau
body:
## Motivation

When a server hangs in CI, the watchdog and the crash path call `py-spy dump` to record where it's stuck. On the NVIDIA runners, every one of those dumps fails:

```
Pyspy failed (py-spy dump --native --pid 2020632). Error: Error: Permission denied (os error 13)
Pyspy failed (py-spy dump --native --pid 325233). Error: Error: Failed to copy Py_Version ... Permission denied (os error 13)
```

Across 18 recent jobs on 5090 (`sm1`-`sm4`), B300 (`di-tor5`) and H100 (`computable-d`, `novita`) runners, about 250 py-spy attempts all failed, with no successes. So every hang leaves no stack. For example, the `test_disaggregation_basic.py` prefill servers that never became healthy on 11-06 ([job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42128580169/job/127658193873)) left nothing to debug with.

**Cause (inferred; I haven't read the runners' sysctl):** the containers don't have `CAP_SYS_PTRACE`, and under Yama `ptrace_scope=1` (the Ubuntu default) a process may then ptrace only its own descendants. A same-user dump would succeed under `ptrace_scope=0`, so the errors point to `ptrace_scope` being 1 or higher. (The AMD and XPU container scripts in this repo add `--cap-add SYS_PTRACE`; the NVIDIA runner containers are set up elsewhere.) SGLang starts py-spy in two places, `python/sglang/srt/utils/cudacore_pyspy_dump_utils.py:70`:
- **`WatchdogRaw`** runs it as a **child** of the process it dumps (its own PID).
- **`TokenizerManager`'s crash dump** runs it as a **sibling** of the schedulers it dumps.

Neither is a descendant relationship, so the kernel refuses both.

## Modifications

- **`allow_pyspy_attach()`** in `cudacore_pyspy_dump_utils.py` calls `prctl(PR_SET_PTRACER, PR_SET_PTRACER_ANY)`. That is Yama's built-in opt-in for "any same-user process may ptrace me", and it needs no capability. It does nothing on non-Linux systems. If Yama isn't enabled, the call fails with EINVAL and is ignored. It can't help under `ptrace_scope` 2 or 3.
- **`WatchdogRaw.__init__`** calls it when `SGLANG_IS_IN_CI` is set. Every process that can be dumped has a watchdog: the schedulers (via `create_scheduler_watchdog`), TokenizerManager, DetokenizerManager and the DP controller. So both dump paths are covered. **Outside CI nothing changes**, and deployments keep their ptrace restrictions.
- **`test/registered/unit/utils/test_pyspy_attach.py`** creates a `WatchdogRaw` with `SGLANG_IS_IN_CI` set, then runs `py-spy dump` on its own PID as a child process, the same relationship as the watchdog. Going through the watchdog means the test also fails if the opt-in call is dropped from it. It runs in `base-a-test-cpu` (ubuntu-latest) and on a `1-gpu-small` NVIDIA runner, since the NVIDIA runners are where dumps fail today. It skips when py-spy is missing or `ptrace_scope >= 2`.

## Testing

- pre-commit passes, including the CI registry and import checks.
- After: on `3045700820`, `test_pyspy_attach.py` (which opts in through `WatchdogRaw` under `SGLANG_IS_IN_CI`) ran and passed (not skipped) on the NVIDIA runner `5090-sm5-runner-0` ([job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42645373118/job/129263744204)), where the same dump failed with error 13 before this change.

title: [Fix] [AMD] imports: [sglang-miles] Skip import-time device probes when no GPU is visible
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
## Motivation

Cherry-pick of #45443 onto `sglang-miles`, which branches from `main` at 2a7987f (10-27) and so does not have it. On a ROCm image, any process that imports `sglang.srt` with no GPU visible dies at import:

```text
sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/fp8_kernel.py:102: in <module>
    if is_fp8_fnuz():
...: in is_fp8_fnuz
    return "gfx94" in torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).gcnArchName
E   RuntimeError: No CUDA GPUs are available
```

This is what currently fails Miles' `tests/e2e/long/test_qwen3_0.6B_verifiers.py` on the ROCm 10 nightly ([11-05 MI35X run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42119447202)): its SDK contract step imports SGLang with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=`. radixark/miles#4718 works around it in the test by keeping the GPUs visible on ROCm; with this change in `sglang-miles` that workaround can be removed.

## Modifications

Same diff as #45443, which applies cleanly:

- `is_hip()` also requires `torch.cuda.is_available()`, and the `is_gfx95_supported` / `is_gfx942_supported` / `is_gfx1250_supported` probes use `is_hip()`, so a ROCm process with no visible GPU skips the import-time device queries, as a CUDA one already does.
- `rocm_mla_decode_rope.py` uses `sglang.srt.utils.is_hip` instead of asking Triton's driver at import.
- Adds the CPU unit tests from #45443 (`TestHipProbes`).

With a GPU visible, `is_hip()` and everything derived from it are unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] Cherry-picked with no conflicts on `sglang-miles` 056f871a7.
- [ ] Not run on a ROCm image yet. The next Miles ROCm image built from this branch should let the Verifiers contract import SGLang with GPUs hidden.

title: [Fix] dspark: [sglang-miles] Target verify passes the forward's routed-experts, indexer top-k and KV-version captures on
author: adrenaline21
body:
## Motivation

With `--enable-return-routed-experts`, every token that DSpark's verify accepts comes back with all-zero routed experts.
The cause is in `TargetVerifyResult`: it kept only the logits. The target forward's `routed_experts_output`,
`indexer_topk_output` and `kv_weight_version_record` were dropped, so the scheduler never finalized them for the verify
tokens.

EAGLE's worker already passes these captures on. Without them, rollout routing replay in RL training gets no routing for
speculated tokens. Megatron's all-to-all then fails on mismatched split sizes.

## Modifications

- `TargetVerifyResult` carries the three captures.
- The DSpark worker puts them on its `GenerationBatchResult`.

## Accuracy Tests

None run: the change doesn't touch logits or sampling.

## Tests

- New case in `test/registered/unit/spec/test_dspark_accept_tail.py`. It fails on `sglang-miles` and passes with the fix.
- GPU, H200, an 8-layer DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash slice with DSpark (1,1,6) and `--enable-return-routed-experts`:
  - Before: 2032 of 2048 response rows had zero routing, in eager and CUDA-graph mode alike. Without speculation, 0 did.
  - After: 0 zero rows over 16 samples.
  - Three RL steps with routing replay trained, where before the first step failed.
- End to end: the run described in #48976 uses DSpark together with routing replay.

Also applies to `main` unchanged; the main version is ready as a follow-up PR.

title: [Fix] kimi-k3.1: Sync the PCP stack's CI fixes (DSA trtllm row plan, MegaMoE pre-allocation, DCP fixture)
author: Fridge003
body:
## Motivation

This syncs three CI fixes from the prefill-CP port stack (#48709 → #48712) back to the Kimi-K3.1 day-0 branch. Each problem is also present on this branch. The failures were seen in the #48712 CI runs [42190534284](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42190534284) and [42190534034](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42190534034).

## Modifications

1. **[Test] dcp: Give the Kimi-K3 override fixture `enable_prefill_cp`** (from #48709)
   - `_kimi_k3_overrides` refuses `--enable-prefill-cp` before reaching its DCP branch, so it now reads `cfg.enable_prefill_cp`.
   - The `SimpleNamespace` fixture in `test_dcp_target_verify_backend.py` lacked that field, and every `_kimi_k3_mode` case raised `AttributeError` (Base `base-a-test-cpu`).

2. **[Fix] kimi-k3: Pre-allocate the MegaMoE workspace only under prefill CP** (from #48710)
   - `post_load_weights` allocates every MoE layer's MegaMoE workspace up front, which charges it to the static memory budget.
   - The prefill-CP recipes are sized for that. The existing Kimi-K3 MegaMoE recipes are not: they take the workspace from the non-static slack, as on main.
   - With the workspace charged, `TestKimiK3B300MegaMoE` (TP8/EP8/DCP8, `--mem-fraction-static 0.85`) loses about 33 GB, and startup fails with `max_mamba_cache_size=-57`.
   - The eager allocation is now limited to `attn_cp_size > 1`.

3. **[Fix] dsa: Plan trtllm rows against the seq_lens the kernel reads** (from #48712)
   - `_forward_trtllm` planned its live rows on `metadata.cache_seqlens_int32`, which has one row per request.
   - The prefill / target-verify caller passes the per-token `dsa_cache_seqlens_int32`.
   - As a result, any extend with more than one token per request raised `DSA prefill q rows (N) exceed metadata rows (M)`, and every GLM-5.2/5.3 trtllm DSA server died on its first prefill.
   - The fix resolves `seq_lens` first and plans on its row count. A new unit case runs a four-token, single-request prefill through `_forward_trtllm`.

## Validation

- On this branch with the three commits applied (8× B300):
  - `test_dsa_backend_dp_padding.py`: 9 tests OK. The new case fails without fix 3 with the same assertion CI hit.
  - `test_dcp_target_verify_backend.py`: 6 tests OK.
- On the #48710 stack (`2-megamoe-bcg` plus fix 2), on 8× B300: `test_kimi_k3_b300.py TestKimiK3B300MegaMoE` starts with 105 mamba slots and scores GSM8K 0.985 (threshold 0.95).

title: [Fix] deepseek-v4.1: Run attention on the real rows of an MLP-sync-padded extend
author: hnyls2002
body:
DeepSeek-V4.1 with an all-to-all MoE backend (`--moe-a2a-backend megamoe`) under pure TP (attention TP > 1, no DP attention) crashes on its warmup request. MLP sync pads every extend to a multiple of attention TP, and DSV4 attention, which does not go through `RadixAttention`, mixed padded and real row counts:

- with decoder SWA bounded replay (the default): `RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (131) must match the size of tensor b (128)` in `make_core_attn_metadata`, because the one-request tail slice ran to the end of the padded batch;
- with `--no-enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay`: `Size mismatch for shape#0('num_tokens'): expected 193 but got 196` in the ratio-2 compressor (`c2.cuh`), because `raw_out_loc` kept the padding rows while the compressor input did not.

DSV4 now follows the rule `RadixAttention` already applies to such batches (`padded_extend_real_tokens`): the metadata covers only the real rows, attention computes only those rows, and the padding rows get zero output.

- `graph_utils.py`: factor the batch narrowing of `attention_input_scope` and `_attention_on_real_rows` into `real_rows_scope`, and their zero padding into `pad_with_zero_rows`; `padded_extend_real_tokens` takes the batch's row count instead of a query tensor.
- `deepseek_v4_backend.py`: build an eager, non-CP extend's metadata over its real rows, recording their count in `DSV4Metadata.real_num_tokens`; size the sparse prefill cache from it; bound the contiguous late-layer tail view to the tail rows.
- `deepseek_v4.py`: `DeepseekV4Attention.forward` runs on the real rows when the metadata covers fewer rows than its input, and pads the output with zero rows; the tail scatter writes only the tail rows.

No behavior change for batches without MLP-sync padding, for prefill CUDA graphs (their metadata keeps its padded layout), or for prefill CP. The HIP backend is not changed; #43499 addresses the same crash there.

Verification, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 4x B300, `--tp 4 --ep-size 4 --moe-a2a-backend megamoe` (`SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=16384`):

- server starts; greedy requests of 1, 2, 3, 5, 17, 127, 129, 130, 131, 133, 257, 1001 and 4099 tokens, alone and 16 at a time, all complete.
- `sgl-eval run gsm8k --load-preset-from-model-id deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --num-examples 200`: 97.0%.

title: [Fix] dsa: Accept metadata padding past q inside a breakable prefill graph
author: Fridge003
body:
## Motivation

This follows up #48977. That PR synced the trtllm DSA row plan fix, which plans on the per-token `seq_lens` the kernel reads. That change exposes a second case under a breakable prefill graph (BCG) with attention DP. The same fix landed on the PCP stack in #48712 (`8bfc730f0e`). CI failure: [job 128150071707](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42292599023/job/128150071707), `TestGLM53FlashB200HighThroughput` (TP4, `--attn-dp-size 4`):

```
AssertionError: DSA metadata rows (48) exceed q rows (34)
```

What happens:

- BCG replays on a `ForwardBatch` view that does not carry `global_num_tokens_cpu`.
- The DSA metadata was planned on the real batch, so `pad_dsa_cache_seqlens` padded it to the DP token count (48 rows).
- The eager attention bridge then narrows q to the live rows (34).
- `_plan_live_rows` re-evaluates `dsa_cache_seqlens_may_be_padded` on the replay view, gets `False`, and rejects the padding.

This branch has the same replay view, so the same failure applies here.

## Modifications

- `_plan_live_rows` also accepts metadata rows past q inside a breakable CUDA graph, where the surplus rows are that padding.
- Add a unit case for the plan inside a breakable graph.

## Validation

On 8× B300 with GLM-5.3-Flash and the `TestGLM53FlashB200HighThroughput` launch args, on the #48712 stack:

- Before the fix, the server died in warmup with the assertion above.
- After the fix, the server starts. GSM8K (1319 questions, thinking, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, max_tokens 8192) scores 96.89%, against a threshold of 0.96, with zero truncations and zero errors.

On this branch, `test_dsa_backend_dp_padding.py` passes all 10 tests.

title: [Fix] radix-cache: Use Rust TreeCore with PyTorch 2.15 in the cu134 image instead of slow python backend
author: trevor-m
body:
## Motivation

The Rust TreeCore is the default unified radix cache core (#39627), but `torch_build.py` accepts PyTorch 2.11-2.14
only. The cu134 image ships PyTorch 2.15, so every server on it silently falls back to the Python TreeCore:

```
Using the Python TreeCore: PyTorch 2.15.0+cu134 is outside the Rust TreeCore support range
```

The image also builds the bundled extension against the wrong torch. Its editable install runs in an isolated build
environment, which installs `python/pyproject.toml`'s `[build-system]` pin (`torch==2.14.1`). The TreeCore links
libtorch, so the image ships an extension compiled against 2.14.1 next to a 2.15.0 runtime. The image also leaves
`SGLANG_RUST_BUILD_MODE` unset. Its `rust/` sources then make the loader expect a cargo build, and the runtime stage
has no cargo. `Dockerfile.cu134` already carries a TODO for this.

On a disaggregated DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash agentic workload (one DEP2 prefill worker, 1500 concurrent sessions), the
Rust TreeCore on the prefill worker raised request throughput by 12.4% (47.09 -> 52.92 req/s). Mean TTFT fell from
12.7 s to 9.3 s, and prefill new tokens/s per GPU rose from 136k to 154k. In the Python TreeCore, radix tree inserts,
KV events, write-back acknowledgements and load-back bookkeeping kept the prefill GPUs idle between batches.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/rust_extensions/torch_build.py`: `_MAX_SUPPORTED_TORCH` goes from `(2, 14)` to `(2, 15)`.
- `docker/Dockerfile.cu134`:
  - The editable install now runs with `--no-build-isolation`, after installing `setuptools`, `setuptools-rust`,
    `setuptools-scm` and `wheel`. The Rust extensions, including the TreeCore, then build against the image's
    `torch==${TORCH_VERSION}` instead of the `[build-system]` pin.
  - The runtime stage sets `SGLANG_RUST_BUILD_MODE=never`, as `docker/Dockerfile` does, so the loader trusts the
    bundled extension.
  - The TODO is removed.

## Accuracy Tests

No model-output change: the TreeCore is cache bookkeeping. The existing shared tests cover Rust and Python TreeCore
parity.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

See Motivation: +12.4% req/s, -27% mean TTFT on the prefill-bound disaggregated workload.

Validation on an aarch64 node:

- Built the cu134 image from this branch with the `release-docker-cu134-nightly.yml` command: `BRANCH_TYPE=local`,
  `BUILD_TYPE=all`, `--target runtime`. The build succeeded, and the editable install ran with torch 2.15.0+cu134 as
  the only torch in the environment.
- In the image, with no environment overrides:
  - torch is 2.15.0+cu134 and `SGLANG_RUST_BUILD_MODE=never` is set.
  - The default TreeCore backend resolves to `rust`, and the supported range reads 2.11-2.15.
  - The extension loads from the bundled module.
- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_rust_tree_core_integration.py` and
  `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_write_back_eviction_parity.py`, run in that image: 577 passed, 7 failed. The 7
  are the TLRU priority and stale-inspection tests. They build the test-only `inspection` feature variant with cargo,
  which no runtime image has (the cu130 image fails them the same way).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Fix] scheduler: Honor pause_generation under PP and release aborted PD rooms and rejected sessions
author: hnyls2002
body:
- **PD prefill: clear the bootstrap room of an aborted request.** A prefill request aborted after it left the bootstrap queue is retired through `release_prefill_sender(abort_sender=True)`, which only called `sender.abort()`. Nothing polls that request again, so its room stayed in `request_status`, `transfer_infos`, `req_to_decode_prefix_len` and `failure_records` for the life of the server (every `CommonKVSender` backend). `release_prefill_sender` now also calls `clear()`, in its own best-effort block so a failing `abort()` does not skip it, and `CommonKVSender.clear()` pops `failure_records` too (`failure_exception()` reads the reason before clearing).
- **Streaming sessions: release the session when a turn is rejected.** `create_req` marks a streaming session in flight before the dLLM validation and the sampling-mask validation run. Both rejections returned without unmarking it, so every later turn of the session was refused with "Streaming session already has an active request" and closing it left the session registered. Both paths now call `session.abort_req()` (`Scheduler._release_rejected_session`). The sampling-mask case is reachable with `return_sampling_mask=True` and the default `top_k`.
- **PP: honor `pause_generation`.** The three PP event loops never read `_engine_paused`, so with `--pp-size 2` generation continued through an `in_place` or `retract` pause (about 11.8k tokens streamed during a 10 s pause with 6 streams on Qwen2.5-0.5B; 0 after the in-flight drain with `--pp-size 1`).
  - The PP loops launch no new micro-batch while paused; launched micro-batches still exchange and process their results. The PD decode PP loop also skips its retract, prealloc and transfer consensus rounds while paused, keeping every stage in lockstep.
  - A pause that arrives while a micro-batch is unprocessed is held, with every input after it, through the existing `ingest_requests(stop_at_pause=...)` mechanism, and launching stops. Once no micro-batch is unprocessed, the pause is handled and a retract pause retracts the requests of every micro-batch (it used to retract only the current `running_batch`). The held inputs then run in order, so a following `release_memory_occupation` or flush sees the retracted state.
  - Under PP, `ingest_requests` returns every input received in the pass, held ones included, so rank 0 relays a held pause to every stage. The PD prefill loop's `received_inputs` therefore also counts held inputs; its launch gate already checks the held queue.
  - The non-PP pause is unchanged: `pause_generation` keeps its drain, retract and metrics in place; the retract body and the metrics tail become `_retract_running_batch` and `_publish_paused_state` so the PP branch can retract each micro-batch and then publish once.

Behavior change only in these three failure cases.

## Verification

- Each new unit test fails without its fix: `test_prefill_abort_release_clears_room_state` (including an `abort()` that raises), `test_rejected_streaming_turn_leaves_session_idle` (dLLM and sampling-mask rejections), and `test_pp_retract_waits_for_in_flight_then_retracts_every_micro_batch` (the pause is handled only after the unprocessed result, both micro-batches are retracted, the PP state ends empty, and a later input runs after the retract). The PP test also fails when the hold, the launch gate, or the retract of every micro-batch is removed.
- On an H200 node with `--pp-size 2`, Qwen2.5-0.5B and 6 streams: a 10 s `in_place` pause streamed 6 tokens (first second only) and a `retract` pause 6 tokens. A `release_memory_occupation` (`kv_cache` tag) issued right after the retract pause succeeded, and after resume and continue all 6 streams completed with coherent output.
- PD with PP on both sides (prefill tp1 pp2, decode pp2, mooncake, router in front), 6 streams: an `in_place` and a `retract` pause each streamed 6 tokens in 10 s, then 0; 6 new requests sent during a retract pause produced no tokens until continue; after continue all 12 requests completed (3000 tokens each).
- Unit tests touching the changed paths pass. `test_minimax_m31_cache_transfer.py` fails the same 12 cases on main.

title: [Fix] [NPU] dsv4: Use explicit compressor state on Ascend 950
author: BourneSun0527
body: ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4 on Ascend 950 uses a request-local compressor state bank. A radix-cache hit can reuse the prefix's SWA pages under a different request slot. Using explicit state locations lets the resumed compressor find the C4 history associated with those pages. ## Modifications - Use the shared explicit state table and `torch.ops.npu.compressor` on Ascend 950. The paired kernel changes the `cache_mode=2` table from a vector of bank IDs to a two-dimensional table of physical state rows. ## Accuracy Tests ## Speed Tests and Profiling performance with change performance baseline 8k1k : performance with change without change ## Checklist - [x] Run formatting and lint checks on the changed files. - [x] Update unit coverage for the state ABI and PD layout. - [x] Document the ABI in the paired kernel PR. - [x] Add Ascend 950 accuracy and speed results. title: [Fix] [AMD] rocprofiler-sdk: fix torch.profiler hang on TP for gfx1250-rocm1010
author: yctseng0211
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation
On gfx1250-rocm1010, torch.profiler hangs on TP workloads. Right after profiling starts, the server stops making progress and the log keeps printing:
```
queue_interposition.cpp:470] Async signal handler still waiting on signal {.handle=...} after 5242880 iterations (value=1, starting_value=1)
```
The bug is in rocprofiler-sdk, and ROCm 10.1 does not have the fixes.
## Modifications
Rebuild ROCr and rocprofiler-sdk from the rocm-systems commit the SDK was built from, cherry-pick the commits below, and replace the SDK libraries, like the existing RCCL step.
- ROCm/rocm-systems#9984 (rocprofiler-sdk): fixes the hang. Before it, rocprofiler-sdk waits for kernels with only 4 threads, one kernel per thread, so all 4 get stuck when kernels wait on each other (for example, RCCL all-reduce on TP).
- ROCm/rocm-systems#8564 (ROCr): ROCm/rocm-systems#9984 needs it, as noted in its [review](https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems/pull/9984#discussion_r3760506500). Without it, `hsa_amd_signal_wait_any` writes out of bounds, and the server crashes as soon as profiling starts:
  ```
  free(): invalid pointer
  Fatal Python error: Aborted
  Fatal glibc error: malloc.c:2599 (sysmalloc): assertion failed: ...
  ```
- ROCm/rocm-systems#12957 (rocprofiler-sdk): a small upstream follow-up to ROCm/rocm-systems#9984, tested together with it.

On MI450, Kimi-K2 TP8 profiling now works without any env var workaround, and the traces are complete. GSM8K accuracy (Kimi-K2, gpt-oss) and gpt-oss serving speed are the same as before.


## Speed/Accuracy Tests

### Kimi-K2 TP8
```
unset NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS NCCL_MAX_NCHANNELS
export HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=1 ENABLE_CK=0 NCCL_IGNORE_CPU_AFFINITY=1 NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=1 \
  NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1 HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /data/amd/Kimi-K2-Thinking-MXFP4-v1 --tp-size 8 \
  --trust-remote-code --reasoning-parser kimi_k2 --tool-call-parser kimi_k2 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
  --max-running-requests 128 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 128 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \
  --disable-radix-cache --attention-backend aiter --prefill-attention-backend aiter \
  --decode-attention-backend triton --disable-custom-all-reduce --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3
```

### gpt-oss-120b TP2 (GPU 0 and 1)
```
export TRITON_HIP_USE_EXPERT_SCHEDULING=0 HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=1 ENABLE_CK=0 \
  SGLANG_GFX1250_W4A8_BACKEND=triton SGLANG_GFX1250_W4A8_KERNEL_GATHER=1 SGLANG_LM_HEAD_AITER_TGEMM=1
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /mnt/raid/models/gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8 --tp 2 \
  --trust-remote-code --max-running-requests 512 --mem-fraction-static 0.9 --attention-backend aiter \
  --disable-radix-cache --page-size 64 --chunked-prefill-size 3072 --max-prefill-tokens 3072 \
  --disable-custom-all-reduce
```
  
```
# warm-up, for C in 1 16 64 128
python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --dataset-name random \
  --random-range-ratio 1.0 --warmup-requests 1 --random-input-len 1024 \
  --random-output-len 32 --num-prompts $C --max-concurrency $C

# measured, for C in 1 16 64 128 (N = 8, 64, 256, 512)
python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --dataset-name random \
  --random-range-ratio 1.0 --warmup-requests 1 --random-input-len 1024 \

title: [Fix] moe: Match the Triton renormalize sum order in the warp MoE router
author: Fridge003
body:
## Motivation

The nightly precision regression test for GLM-5.2-FP8 (TP8) started failing after #47641 ([run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42041763217/job/127294296931)): `layers.16 rel_diff=0.00188 > 1e-3` against the rolling baseline.

GLM-5.2 fuses one shared expert (topk = 9), so `biased_grouped_topk_gpu` routes through `moe_fused_gate`, which #47641 now dispatches to the one-warp-per-token router instead of the Triton kernel. The two pick the same experts and their sigmoid scores are bit-exact, but the renormalization sum is reduced in a different order:

- Triton: adjacent pairs, `((a0+a1)+(a2+a3))+((a4+a5)+(a6+a7))`
- warp router: butterfly with xor masks 4 → 2 → 1, `((a0+a4)+(a2+a6))+...`

Each routed weight then differs by 1 fp32 ulp, and through 78 bf16 MoE layers the residual stream drifts past the 1e-3 threshold (diff grows from 8.9e-5 at layer 8 to 1.5e-2 at layer 77).

## Modifications

- `route_warp.cuh`: reduce the renormalization sum with increasing xor masks (`warp::reduce_sum<1, bit_ceil(K)>`), which reproduces Triton's adjacent-pair order. Same number of shuffles.

## Accuracy Tests

On 8×H200:
- `test/registered/debug_utils/test_nightly_precision_regression.py` (GLM-5.2-FP8, TP8) against the 11/01 baseline: reproduced `rel_diff=0.0018810335545530465` before the fix; with the fix it passes with rel_diff 0 on every layer and step (same as reverting #47641).
- `test_moe_route_warp.py` + `test_muse_spark_routing.py`: all passed.

Note: the softmax and sqrtsoftplus warp paths are also not bit-exact with the Triton router (different exp / polynomial math, not just the sum order). DeepSeek-V4 (sqrtsoftplus) went through the Triton path before #47641, so its numerics changed too; that is out of scope here.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [Fix] scheduler: Relay multimodal requests to later PP stages without raw features
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

Under pipeline parallelism, the first PP stage relays every newly received request to the next stage (`_pp_send_pyobj_to_next_stage(recv_reqs)` → `point_to_point_pyobj`, i.e. pickle + gloo send). Every later stage then rebroadcasts the object to its attention TP/CP peers and relays it again.

With `mm_feature_transport=cpu`, `RequestReceiver._finalize_shm_features` has already materialized each image's raw feature tensor into the request object by that point. For example, a 1080p image is about 6 MB of CHW uint8. All of it gets serialized at every hop on the scheduler threads.

Later stages never consume these tensors:
- `prepare_mm_inputs` embeds multimodal inputs on the first PP rank only ("Non-first pipeline ranks consume proxy tensors and return no embeddings").
- The PP-capable models outside that routine (`gemma4_unified`, `cosmos3_edge`, the transformers backend) also embed on the first rank only.
- On later stages the scheduler needs just the pad values, and those come from the item hash.

So the relay is pure overhead, and it grows with images per request. Agent-style traffic that resends the conversation's screenshots every turn makes every PP iteration slower. The whole pipeline then queues up, and **text-only requests slow down as much as image requests**.

## Modifications

- `mm_utils.strip_mm_features_for_pp_relay(reqs)`: returns copies of the requests in which multimodal items that already carry a `hash` drop `feature`.
  - Unhashed items keep their feature, because the next stage hashes it to derive the pad value.
  - The relaying stage's own request objects are left untouched (copies via `msgspec.structs.replace`), since the first stage still embeds from them.
  - Batched requests (`BaseBatchReq`) are handled.
  - Non-multimodal requests, and requests whose `mm_inputs` is an error, are passed through.
- `SchedulerPPMixin._pp_send_reqs_to_next_stage`: the three PP event loops (normal, disagg prefill, disagg decode) relay `recv_reqs` through it.
- Unit test `TestPipelineRelayDropsRawFeatures` in `test/registered/unit/managers/test_mm_shm_error_consensus.py`.

## Accuracy Tests

This change only alters what later PP stages receive; those stages never read `feature`. Measured on a downstream build that shares this relay path, VLM with PD disaggregation and 4-stage PP prefill:
- 8 image prompts with 1–6 images each, temperature 0, caches cleared before every run.
- Greedy decoding there is not bitwise reproducible: two baseline runs already diverge after 120–290 characters. So I compared the first output token's top-5 logprobs, which depend only on prefill.
- The first token matches on 8/8 prompts in every pair.
- Max |logprob delta|: baseline vs baseline 1.12; this change vs two baseline runs 0.87 / 0.51. That is within run-to-run noise.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same downstream build: 1P1D, prefill PP4 × TP2 (attention CP2), about 1.5 req/s per prefill. 45 % of sessions attach one 1080p screenshot per turn and resend the history, giving p50 8 images per image request. Same traffic and seed for both runs. TTFT is for requests with fewer than 8k uncached prompt tokens.

| TTFT p50 / p90 | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| all requests | 3.59 / 7.79 s | **1.38 / 3.35 s** |
| text-only requests | 3.21 / 7.48 s | **1.38 / 3.22 s** |
| image requests | 4.09 / 8.38 s | **1.36 / 3.42 s** |
| `scheduler_stage_seconds_total{category="process_queue"}` share, pp0..3 | 0.126 / 0.074 / 0.059 / 0.054 | 0.040 / 0.028 / 0.030 / 0.058 |

Before the change, py-spy on the last PP stage showed 56 % of scheduler-thread samples in `point_to_point_pyobj` / `recv_object`, i.e. receiving relayed requests.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). `test_mm_shm_error_consensus.py`: 19 passed on this branch.
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not applicable.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [Fix] hicache: Return int page slots from `_storage_page_index` without DCP
author: kpham-sgl
body:
Follow-up to #48877.

## Motivation

`HostKVCache._storage_page_index` returned its argument unchanged when `dcp_size == 1`. #48877 routed `DSAIndexerPoolHost.get_page_buffer_meta` through it, so without DCP the indexer's zero-copy metadata did its pointer math on 0-d tensors and handed tensors, not ints, to the storage backends (Mooncake, NIXL, NPU). This hits DSA models with an L3 backend that never enable DCP. The MLA pool is unaffected: it calls `indices.tolist()` first.

## Modifications

- `pool_host/base.py`: convert the index to `int` before the `dcp_size == 1` early return.
- `test_hicache_dcp_host_pool.py`: port the DCP indexer storage-page and L3 pool-check tests from #48414, which #48877 left behind. One change against the source: main rejects every `DRAFT` pool under DCP L3 (#48877 left out the DFLASH draft case), so the sharded draft moves from the allowed list to the rejected list. Adds a case that the indexer's zero-copy pointers are ints without DCP.

## Tests

- `pre-commit` on the touched files.
- The unit tests have not run yet; they run through `/rerun-test`.

title: [Fix] linker: Renew Mooncake read leases that lapse during a load
author: alphabetc1
body:
Original authors: @Fridge003, @alphabetc1

## Port of #48414

Fixes and guards for the Mooncake direct linker from the Kimi-K3.1 Day-0 branch (#48414), plus two fixes found while porting them.

- A long load can outlive its get-session leases, which aborted every request in the batch. The lapsed keys are renewed and their reads retried.
- New here: Mooncake reports a lapsed lease as `-707` only on the first read of a key; every later read of it, from the same ranged get (requests sharing a prefix) or from a concurrent layer-group read, gets `-600`. Both codes now count as lapsed; without it the renewal never ran on shared-prefix batches.
- New here: a renewal can race reads still in flight on the old lease, so an immediate retry can see `-600` again. The renew-and-retry runs up to four times with a short backoff, then fails the load as before.
- `local_buffer_size` in the Mooncake JSON or extra config (default 16 MiB) for transports that stage GPU data through host memory, and `MooncakeStore` honors `SGLANG_HICACHE_MOONCAKE_REUSE_TE`.
- The linker has no pipeline-parallel coordination, so `--pp-size > 1` is rejected at startup.

Against the raw port: the renewal sits in the ranged get of the parallel layer-group loads (#45106) instead of the per-layer loop. The branch's session cleanup after a partial start failure is dropped: `main` already tracks sessions before starting them (#46168).

## Modifications

- `mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store/mooncake_direct_linker.py`: lease renewal with bounded retries.
- `mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store/mooncake_store.py`, `README.md`: `local_buffer_size`, transfer-engine reuse switch.
- `arg_groups/hicache_hook.py`: reject `--pp-size > 1` with the linker.

## Tests

- Unit: `test_unified_cache_linker.py::test_range_get_*` (shared keys, keys another read reported, a racing read, bounded give-up, other failures not renewed), `test_mooncake_store_config.py`, `test_external_linker_factory.py`.
- Kimi-K3.1-Pro, B300 TP8, DFLASH, Mooncake linker, GSM8K with a 16-shot shared prefix and a cache flush every 64 questions:
  - Before the `-600` fix, about 90% of requests in shared-prefix batches were aborted (15/192 correct).
  - With a single renew-and-retry, 5 loads still failed over the full set (all `-600` right after a successful renewal).
  - With this PR on `main` (with #49042 and #49355): 0 failed loads over the full set, GSM8K 98.18% (1295/1319) vs 98.03% without the linker.

Touches the same spot of `mooncake_direct_linker.py` as #49355 (both add module-level definitions); whichever merges second needs a trivial rebase.

title: [Fix] megamoe: Accept FlashInfer 0.7.3 knob cache and enum config fields in startup autotune
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Why the tests broke

#48468 bumped FlashInfer to 0.7.3, which changed two things MegaMoE startup autotune (`flashinfer_megamoe_autotune.py`, from #43789) relies on:

- The megakernel config gained an enum field, `finalize_mode: flashinfer.moe_ep.config.FinalizeMode`. `MegaMoeTunedForward._geometry_key` passes every non-tensor config field to `json.dumps`, so startup crashed with `TypeError: Object of type FinalizeMode is not JSON serializable`.
- FlashInfer's MegaMoE knob cache file moved to format version 2 (`KNOB_CACHE_VERSION` in `flashinfer.moe_ep.core.tuning`; 0.7.2 wrote version 1). `_valid_native_cache` accepted only version 1, so once the first crash is fixed, every freshly tuned tactic was rejected with `RuntimeError: MegaMoE autotune did not record its selected tactic`.

Both break every server launched with `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_megamoe`. The tests that cover it run only in the nightly suite (`4-gpu-b200`), so #48468's PR CI did not exercise them; the nightly run on main failed `test_flashinfer_nvfp4_online_moe_backend.py::TestFlashinferMegaMoeBackendNvFp4OnlineW4A16` and the NVFP4 W4A16 MegaMoE case of `test_update_weights_from_disk_blackwell.py`.

## Changes

- `_geometry_key` records enum config fields by member name, which stays stable across processes for the cached autotune key; any other non-JSON type still fails loudly.
- `_valid_native_cache` checks against `_NATIVE_CACHE_VERSION = 2`, kept next to a note to bump it with the FlashInfer pin. The version-2 payload FlashInfer 0.7.3 writes has the same single-entry shape (it adds a `live_tokens` field), so no other check changes. Records cached under version 1 are rejected and retuned once.
- The CPU unit test's fake megakernel config gains an enum field, and its cached payload uses version 2. Each change makes 2 cases of `test_flashinfer_megamoe.py` fail without the fix.

## Verification

- `test/registered/backends/test_flashinfer_nvfp4_online_moe_backend.py -k TestFlashinferMegaMoeBackendNvFp4OnlineW4A16` on 4x B300 with FlashInfer 0.7.3: fails on main with the `TypeError`, then with only the enum fix with the knob-cache error, and passes with this PR.
- `test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_flashinfer_megamoe.py`: 29 passed.

title: [Fix] test: Keep a passed precision baseline row pointing at its own tensors
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Why the test broke

`test/registered/debug_utils/test_nightly_precision_regression.py` failed in the Nov 7 nightly (attempt 1) with `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8: FAILED - tensor=...model.layers.56.self_attn.inputs.hidden_states rel_diff=0.00117`, and passed on the rerun on the same commit.

- **The failure itself is a runner, not code.** On healthy hardware the dumped tensors are bit-reproducible: 16 fresh launches on one commit on a separate 8x H200 machine were bit-identical to each other and to the stored baseline, and passing CI runs report `max_rel_diff=0.0`. The failing attempt ran on one specific `8-gpu-h200` runner whose deviation (starting at layer 48, prefill tokens 11-16, largest on TP rank 1, growing to ~1.4e-2 by layer 77) is bit-identical across a month of nightlies on different commits; every comparison from that runner against a baseline from another runner has failed. That runner needs to be drained and checked; no threshold can separate it, since its deviation is as large as a real numerics change.
- **The rerun then poisoned the baseline store.** `push_run` skips the tensor upload when the same model + date + sha path is already in the manifest. Attempt 1 pushed its tensors with `pass_label="failed"`; attempt 2 passed and only refreshed meta and appended a `passed` manifest row, so that row now serves attempt 1's deviating tensors as the next baseline (`fetch` takes the newest non-failed row). The next nightly on a healthy runner will compare against them. The same reuse turned an earlier deviation into the baseline in October.

## Changes

- `push_run` skips the tensor upload only for a `failed` push. A passed push at an existing path uploads its own tensors, so a `passed` row always points at tensors from a passing run; a failed push still leaves the earlier tensors in place.
- The CI context records `RUNNER_NAME` as `ci_runner`, promoted to the manifest, so a deviation that follows one machine is visible from the manifest.

The baseline the store holds right now still needs one refresh from a healthy runner (`SGLANG_PRECISION_FORCE_UPDATE=1`); this PR does not write to the store.

## Verification

- Checked locally against a fake `HfApi`: a passed push after a failed one at the same path uploads its own tensors here and skips them on main; a failed push still skips them.
- The nightly test itself is not rerun from this PR: it writes to the shared baseline store.

title: [Fix] scheduler: Finish rejected requests and offloaded releases through the request retirer
author: hnyls2002
body:
Several paths ended a request without `RequestRetirer`, so they skipped what the retirer releases. They now all go through it.

- **Requests rejected before they are queued** finish through `RequestRetirer.retire_unadmitted`, which already served the PD unadmitted reject as `Scheduler.retire_unadmitted_request` and now lives in the retirer (it takes `stream_output`):
  - the PD decode door's KV-capacity reject (`DecodePreallocQueue._check_if_req_exceed_kv_capacity`) and the PD prefill one (`PrefillBootstrapQueue._check_if_req_exceed_kv_capacity`);
  - the sampling-mask, beam and missing-bootstrap-room rejects in `handle_generate_request`;
  - the EPD encoder failure reported by the request receiver, which now takes the `RequestRetirer` and is built after it.

  Before this they were aborted and streamed only. A streaming session's request was never detached, so the session stayed in flight and refused later turns; the request's media was not released and its cache attempt was not ended; a retracted request rejected at the decode door kept its host KV backup.
- **The dLLM reject** goes through `RequestRetirer.abort`, which sends the same abort output. `_release_rejected_session`, which released only the streaming session for the sampling-mask and dLLM rejects, is removed: the retirer's `_detach` does that.
- **A finished request released by the decode KV offload manager** (`_release_finished_req`) freed its row by hand. It now calls `RequestRetirer.release(req, checkpoint=False)`, the same release a finished request takes everywhere else. Before this, the release skipped:
  - `claim_kv_row`, so a streaming session's turn never finished: the session stayed in flight, its close was deferred forever, and its slot's KV record was freed under the slot;
  - `_detach` for an aborted turn, HiSparse's `request_finished`, and `on_release`, which on the unified radix cache cleans each component's per-request state (mamba, SWA).
  - No checkpoint: the offloaded host copy, not the device tree, keeps this KV, and the pages freed are the ones freed before. The manager keeps its own guard and still releases only after the request's device-to-host copy is done.
  - The manager now takes the `RequestRetirer`, so it is built right after the retirer (`maybe_init_decode_offload_manager`).

All these paths now record their exit in the exit ledger, so a second release fails in CI.

Two paths still release without the retirer because they do not end a request: the PD optimistic requeue (the request goes back to the queue) and the PP dynamic chunk sizer's synthetic profiling requests (released at startup, before the retirer exists).

## Verification

- A CPU repro of the decode capacity reject and of the offload release fails on main and passes with this change. One unit test per bug covers them: `test_capacity_reject_retires_a_retracted_request` and `test_streaming_session_keeps_the_row_of_a_finished_turn`. Both fail on main.
- Unit tests touching PD prefill and decode, the offload manager, the retirer, sessions, the request receiver and the intake rejects show the same failures with and without the change, with `SGLANG_ENABLE_RUNNING_REQS_CHECK` on.

title: [Fix] disagg: Fail startup when Mooncake rejects KV buffer registration
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Why the test broke

On a PD-disaggregation CI runner, Mooncake could not register KV memory on one RDMA device:

```text
rdma_context.cpp:905] Failed to register memory ... Resource temporarily unavailable [11]
```

The `EAGAIN` from `ibv_reg_mr` is a host-side condition (RDMA memory registration resources on that machine), outside sglang. What made it expensive is that sglang swallowed it:

- `MooncakeTransferEngine.batch_register` logged a non-zero return code only at debug level and returned it.
- `MooncakeKVManager.register_buffer_to_engine` ignored the return value.

Mooncake rolls the whole batch back on failure, so the server came up healthy with none of its KV buffers registered. Every transfer then failed with `AddressNotRegistered` / `KVTransferError`: `test_disaggregation_dp_attention.py` ran for about 30 minutes and scored 0.0 on gsm8k, and `test_disaggregation_decode_radix_cache.py` failed an assertion in `cache_hit_kit.py`.

## Changes

- `MooncakeTransferEngine.batch_register` now raises `RuntimeError` when `batch_register_memory` returns non-zero or throws, the same contract `register` already has, except `ERR_ADDRESS_OVERLAPPED` (-7, the region is already registered), which stays non-fatal and is now logged as an error. A memory resume re-registers after a deregistration that may have failed and been tolerated, and that path kept working before; this change does not turn it into a crash. The message gives the region count, total bytes, address span, RDMA device, and return code.
- Its two callers, both in `MooncakeKVManager` (KV/aux/state buffers at init and on memory resume, and staging buffers), depend on the registration, so the error now propagates and the server fails at startup instead of serving with unregistered memory.
- `batch_deregister` is unchanged: teardown still tolerates a failed deregistration.

Return-code semantics come from Mooncake v0.3.14 (the version CI installs): `batch_register_memory` returns 0 on success and a negative error code otherwise, e.g. `ERR_CONTEXT` (-202) when `ibv_reg_mr` fails on a device, which is the failure above.

## Verification

- Two CPU unit tests in `TestMooncakeRegistration` (`test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_encode_server.py`): a `-202` return from `batch_register_memory` makes `batch_register` raise, and an already-registered region (-7) only logs an error. Both fail on main.
- Existing Mooncake and PD unit tests (`test_mooncake_*`, `test_pd_role_switch.py`) pass locally on CPU.
- `pre-commit` passes on the changed files.

title: [Fix] cosmos3: Keep single-GPU BF16 CFG arithmetic under CFG parallel
author: Smallfu666
body:
## Motivation

`sglang serve --model-path nvidia/Cosmos3-Nano --num-gpus 2` produces a different image than `--num-gpus 1` for the same request and seed: on 2x H200, 304,392 of 399,360 pixels differ (PSNR 22.42 dB). With two GPUs and no parallel flags, Cosmos3 turns CFG parallel on by itself, and the CFG-parallel combine rounds differently from the one-GPU combine.

On one GPU the stage combines text CFG as `uncond + g * (cond - uncond)` on purpose, because the coefficient sum "rounds differently in BF16 and changes deterministic generation results":

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/46e296e628fc04c135f60eb35b8e93d9bef05ca0/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/model_specific_stages/cosmos3.py#L1876-L1879

Under CFG parallel each rank scales its own branch by `g` or `1 - g` ([L2334](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/46e296e628fc04c135f60eb35b8e93d9bef05ca0/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/model_specific_stages/cosmos3.py#L2334), [L2342](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/46e296e628fc04c135f60eb35b8e93d9bef05ca0/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/model_specific_stages/cosmos3.py#L2342)) and the ranks are summed with an all-reduce ([L2131-L2135](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/46e296e628fc04c135f60eb35b8e93d9bef05ca0/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/model_specific_stages/cosmos3.py#L2131-L2135)), which is that coefficient sum. Transfer control-CFG has three branches; two ranks add them as `(b0 + b2) + b1` instead of the single-rank `(b0 + b1) + b2`.

## Modifications

- `_predict_noise_cfg`: each rank still runs its round-robin branches, but the raw predictions are all-gathered (zeros for empty slots) and every rank combines them in branch order, as one rank would. Control-free text CFG is combined as `uncond + g * (cond - uncond)`. This is the idea of `CFGPolicy(parallel_uses_serial_arithmetic=True)` from #38549; Cosmos3 has its own branch executor, so it cannot reuse the flag.
- New `test/unit/test_cosmos3_cfg_parallel.py`: two Gloo CPU ranks run the real `_denoise_once` for 3 steps with a BF16 stand-in transformer, for equal and different prompt lengths and for control-CFG, each with and without the sound output, and assert that CFG parallel matches the single-rank result bitwise. Before this change all 8 cases differ (20-28% of elements, max abs up to 0.125); with it all pass.
- `test_cosmos3.py::test_control_cfg_parallel_distribution` patched the removed all-reduce; it now patches the all-gather.

To check on CPU:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= SGLANG_DIFFUSION_PLATFORM_OVERRIDE=cpu python -m pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_cosmos3_cfg_parallel.py
```

It fails on main and passes here; `test_cosmos3.py` also passes (143 passed with the new test).

## Accuracy Tests

Cosmos3-Nano, 2x H200, one T2I request (832x480, seed 0, 35 steps), SGLang main of 2026-11-08 (Python package on top of the 2026-11-06 dev image), `--warmup-mode off` and otherwise default flags; decoded RGB pixels compared with the `--num-gpus 1` image:

| `--num-gpus 2` | pixels differing (of 399,360) | max abs | PSNR |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 304,392 | 255 | 22.42 dB |
| this change | 0 | 0 | identical |

With this change a fresh 2-GPU server produced the same image, and repeating the request on the first server was also identical. With `--performance-mode manual --enable-cfg-parallel` the result is the same: main differs from one GPU by 22.42 dB, this change is identical.

Not run: equal-length prompts on GPU (one GPU then batches both branches, so bitwise equality is not claimed there), other Cosmos3 checkpoints, other requests or video, more than two CFG ranks, and speed, memory or profiling.

#48220 also edits the round-robin loop in `_predict_noise_cfg` (for multi-node FSDP); the two changes compose, and whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not measured. Per guided step and per output modality, one all-reduce becomes one all-gather per branch slot (one slot for text CFG on two ranks, two for control-CFG), and every rank does the combine.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentation](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentation).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (accuracy above; speed not measured)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Fix] rope/env: Remove the leftover Dual Chunk Attention RoPE, make env alias warnings visible, restore the DGX Spark b12x env
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Re-reading the example PRs for the code-cleanup skill (#49163) turned up defects on main that earlier cleanups left behind, including two of my own (#48366, #48399). This PR fixes them.

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| #32114 deleted the Dual Chunk Attention backend, but `get_rope` still built `DualChunkRotaryEmbedding` for any checkpoint with `dual_chunk_attention_config` (Qwen2.5-7B/14B-Instruct-1M). That RoPE returns a query five head-widths wide, which only the deleted backend could read. On main these checkpoints fail at the first forward pass (`mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (16384x17920 and 3584x3584)`; 17920 = 5 x 3584). | Remove the RoPE class, its `get_rope` argument, the plumbing in `qwen2`, `qwen2_moe`, `qwen3_moe`, `glm4` and `glm_image_vl`, the config check, and the `sparse_attention_config.json` download it triggered. Such checkpoints now run with standard RoPE, and startup logs that `dual_chunk_attention_config` is ignored. |
| Env aliases (`EnvBoolWithAlias` etc.) warned with `DeprecationWarning`. Python hides that category when it is raised from library code, so setting a renamed env var warned nobody. | Warn with `FutureWarning`, which is shown by default. The alias test asserts the category. |
| #34492 deleted `SGLANG_USE_SGL_XPU` without a `_DEPRECATED_ENVS` entry, so setting it was silently ignored. | Register it with a note naming `--moe-runner-backend triton`. |
| #48399 removed `SGLANG_SM120_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=b12x` and `B12X_MLA_SM120_DSV4_H16_NATIVE=1` from the three DGX Spark DeepSeek-V4 cells because main does not read them. Those cells run the preview image `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-v4f-2dgx-v2` (branch `b12x-vision`), whose FlashMLA selector does read them, so the cells fell back to the default attention backend while still marked verified as the b12x recipe. | Restore both vars in the three cells and the cookbook note. |
| #48366 committed `python/sglang/test/kits/moe_lora_down_b_kit.py.orig`, a merge backup. | Delete it. |

## Validation

GB300 (sm_103), base `51d8d1db` vs this branch, same node:

| Check | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-1M (`dual_chunk_attention_config`) | fails at the first forward (shape error above) | serves; logs that the config is ignored |
| ... GSM8K, sgl-eval 0.1.3, 200 questions, max 1024 tokens, greedy / T=0.7 top-p 0.8 | - | 29.0% / 30.5% |
| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, same GSM8K settings (reference for the 1M model) | - | 32.5% / 31.5% |
| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct greedy outputs (8 prompts x 64 tokens) | | byte-identical to base |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 greedy outputs | two different hashes over three launches | second launch identical to base's last two |
| `SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP=1` (alias read at import by `sampler.py`) | applied, no warning shown | applied, one warning shown |
| `SGLANG_USE_SGL_XPU=0` | silently ignored | one warning naming the replacement |

The absolute GSM8K numbers are low because sgl-eval's default prompt gets a direct `\boxed{}` answer from both Qwen2.5 models; the 1M model lands in the same range as its sibling under identical settings.

Unit tests, identical results on base and this PR: `test_environ`, `test_server_args`, `test_pos_enc`, `test_table_qk_norm_rope`, `test_fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate`, `test_rope_cache_invalidation`, `test_mrope_axis_map`, `test_yarn_cache_extension`, `test_rope_hip_fallback_cache_dtype`, `test_bailing_mrope_shape`, `test_laguna_config`.

Not run: GLM-4 / GLM-Image (the same parameter-plumbing removal as Qwen2), and the DGX Spark recipe (docs only; this restores the lines the recipe was verified with on that image).

Not changed: `docs/src/snippets/agentx/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.jsx` sets `SGLANG_OPT_USE_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE`, which main no longer reads, but the file is generated from external AgentX submissions and must not be edited by hand.

title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] dsv4: Restore SM120/SM121 to the DeepGEMM indexer gates
author: Kylinny
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #49173.

#48399 replaced `is_sm100_or_newer()` (device capability major `>= 10`) with a strict `current_arch().is_sm(10)` gate in `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/v41_indexer/__init__.py`. SM120-family devices (GB10, compute capability 12.1) were silently demoted to the torch prefill fallback: `FullTopKIndexer._torch_prefill` -> `scoring.prefill_requests` calls `Tensor.tolist()` once per layer, a synchronous device-to-host copy inside the layer loop.

The reporter's measurements on a 4x DGX Spark TP4 deployment of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (their numbers, not mine): **~125 ms/layer fixed cost, 8x prefill throughput regression** (4096-token chunks: ~480 tok/s vs ~4000 tok/s before), independent of chunk size. The reporter also verified that reverting the one-line gate to `is_sm(10) or is_sm(12)` recovers prefill on GB10, and that the SM121 DeepGEMM path ran in production for weeks.

## Modifications

Restore the `>= 10` gate for the **dense** DeepGEMM paths only, in `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/v41_indexer/__init__.py`:

- New `is_sm100_or_newer()` (`current_arch().is_sm_at_least(10)`, restoring the pre-#48399 semantics) gates `_use_deep_gemm_prefill()` and `use_deep_gemm_decode` in `make_full_topk_indexer()`. `DenseBlocksBackend` gets the same widened prefill gate via `_use_deep_gemm_prefill()`.
- `is_sm100()` stays strict `is_sm(10)` and still gates the candidate/sparse-table branch of `make_candidate_indexer()`, with a comment explaining why.

### Why the sparse path stays strict (the dtype subtlety)

I verified this against the pinned `sgl-deep-gemm==0.2.6` sources (`sgl-project/DeepGEMM`, branch `release/v0.2.6`, `csrc/apis/attention.hpp`):

- The **dense** kernels support arch 12: `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits` has an `arch_major == 12` branch, `get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata` / `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` dispatch arch 12, and line 50 asserts `weights.scalar_type() == (arch_major == 10 ? kBFloat16 : kFloat32)` — i.e. the fp32 weights/logits contract off SM100. That contract is already what `kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/index_logits.py` produces (`index_logits_dtype()` / `index_weights_dtype()` stay strict `is_sm(10)`; untouched by this PR), and `flat_index_logits_tiles` / `deep_gemm_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` convert weights through it.
- The **sparse** kernels do not: `get_sparse_mqa_logits_metadata`, `get_paged_sparse_mqa_logits_metadata`, `fp8_fp4_sparse_mqa_logits` and `fp8_fp4_paged_sparse_mqa_logits` all assert `arch == 10`. So widening the candidate gate would only turn the dense-blocks fallback into a startup `RuntimeError` on SM120 (`DEEPGEMM_PAGED_SPARSE_MQA_LOGITS` is `False` off SM100). On SM120 the candidate scheme therefore keeps dense blocks for prefill, which now use the restored DeepGEMM dense path.

The torch fallback itself is unchanged in this PR (Hopper / non-CUDA keep it, as before). Batching its per-layer `tolist()` is a separate follow-up.

## Reproducer

No GPU needed: the script patches `current_arch()` in the v41_indexer / index_logits namespaces and forces `has_dense_fp4_indexer` to `True` to simulate a box with the pinned sgl-deep-gemm 0.2.6 installed. Save as `repro_gate.py` and run `PYTHONPATH=<repo>/python python repro_gate.py`.

<details>
<summary>repro_gate.py</summary>

```python
"""Reproducer for sgl-project/sglang#49173 (run BEFORE and AFTER the fix).

Routes the DSV4.1 DeepGEMM indexer gates through mocked GPU archs and prints
which indexer path each arch takes. No GPU is needed: ``current_arch()`` is
patched in the v41_indexer / index_logits module namespaces, and
``has_dense_fp4_indexer`` is forced True to simulate a box with the pinned
sgl-deep-gemm 0.2.6 installed (``python/pyproject.toml`` pins it).

Run from a checkout of sglang:
    PYTHONPATH=<repo>/python python repro_gate.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest import mock

import torch

from sglang.srt.layers.attention.dsv4 import v41_indexer as idx
from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsv4 import index_logits


class FakeCudaArch:
    """Mimics sglang.kernels.arch._cuda.CudaArch for one capability."""

    def __init__(self, capability):
        self.capability = capability
        self.major, self.minor = capability

    @property
    def cuda(self):
        return self

    def is_sm(self, major, minor=None):
        return self.major == major and (minor is None or self.minor == minor)

    def is_sm_at_least(self, major, minor=0):
        return self.capability >= (major, minor)


class FakeNonCudaArch:
    """Mimics the plain DeviceArch returned off CUDA (all gates False)."""

    @property
    def cuda(self):
        return None

    def is_sm(self, major, minor=None):
        return False

    def is_sm_at_least(self, major, minor=0):
        return False


def clear_caches():
    idx.is_sm100.cache_clear()
    if hasattr(idx, "is_sm100_or_newer"):
        idx.is_sm100_or_newer.cache_clear()
    idx._use_deep_gemm_prefill.cache_clear()
    idx.has_dense_fp4_indexer.cache_clear()
    index_logits.index_logits_dtype.cache_clear()
    index_logits.index_weights_dtype.cache_clear()


def route_for(label, arch):
    with (
        mock.patch.object(idx, "current_arch", return_value=arch),
        mock.patch.object(index_logits, "current_arch", return_value=arch),
        mock.patch.object(idx, "has_dense_fp4_indexer", return_value=True),
    ):
        clear_caches()
        full = idx.make_full_topk_indexer(
            token_to_kv_pool=SimpleNamespace(), req_to_token=torch.empty(0)
        )
        prefill, decode = None, None
        candidate_note = ""
        try:
            prefill, decode = idx.make_candidate_indexer(
                token_to_kv_pool=SimpleNamespace(),
                req_to_token=torch.empty(0),
                page_size=64,
                candidate_topk_blocks=8,
                candidate_block_size=8,
            )
            candidate_note = type(prefill).__name__
        except RuntimeError as e:
            # On this CPU box the SM100 sparse branch is reached but the
            # paged-sparse DeepGEMM logits are unavailable, so the factory
            # raises before constructing the backend. Reaching this error
            # still proves the sparse branch was selected, not dense-blocks.
            candidate_note = f"sparse-branch ({e})"[:80]
        print(
            f"{label:>12}: is_sm100={idx.is_sm100()!s:5} "
            f"is_sm100_or_newer={getattr(idx, 'is_sm100_or_newer', lambda: None)()!s:5} "
            f"prefill_deep_gemm={full.use_deep_gemm_prefill!s:5} "
            f"decode_deep_gemm={full.use_deep_gemm_decode!s:5} "
            f"candidate_prefill={candidate_note} "
            f"logits_dtype={index_logits.index_logits_dtype()} "
            f"weights_dtype={index_logits.index_weights_dtype()}"
        )


def main():
    print("== #49173 gate routing (deep_gemm 0.2.6 present) ==")
    for label, arch in [
        ("Hopper SM90", FakeCudaArch((9, 0))),
        ("Blackwell SM100", FakeCudaArch((10, 0))),
        ("GB202 SM120", FakeCudaArch((12, 0))),
        ("GB10 SM121", FakeCudaArch((12, 1))),
        ("non-CUDA", FakeNonCudaArch()),
    ]:
        route_for(label, arch)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

Before (base `4003bf10`, SM120/SM121 fall to torch prefill/decode):

```
== #49173 gate routing (deep_gemm 0.2.6 present) ==
 Hopper SM90: is_sm100=False is_sm100_or_newer=None  prefill_deep_gemm=False decode_deep_gemm=False candidate_prefill=DenseBlocksBackend logits_dtype=torch.float32 weights_dtype=torch.float32
Blackwell SM100: is_sm100=True  is_sm100_or_newer=None  prefill_deep_gemm=True  decode_deep_gemm=True  candidate_prefill=sparse-branch (the candidate indexer needs DeepGEMM's paged sparse MQA logits (s logits_dtype=torch.bfloat16 weights_dtype=torch.bfloat16
 GB202 SM120: is_sm100=False is_sm100_or_newer=None  prefill_deep_gemm=False decode_deep_gemm=False candidate_prefill=DenseBlocksBackend logits_dtype=torch.float32 weights_dtype=torch.float32
  GB10 SM121: is_sm100=False is_sm100_or_newer=None  prefill_deep_gemm=False decode_deep_gemm=False candidate_prefill=DenseBlocksBackend logits_dtype=torch.float32 weights_dtype=torch.float32
    non-CUDA: is_sm100=False is_sm100_or_newer=None  prefill_deep_gemm=False decode_deep_gemm=False candidate_prefill=DenseBlocksBackend logits_dtype=torch.float32 weights_dtype=torch.float32
```

After (this PR — SM120/SM121 take the DeepGEMM dense path, dtypes stay fp32, candidate stays on dense blocks, SM100/SM90/non-CUDA unchanged):

```
== #49173 gate routing (deep_gemm 0.2.6 present) ==
 Hopper SM90: is_sm100=False is_sm100_or_newer=False prefill_deep_gemm=False decode_deep_gemm=False candidate_prefill=DenseBlocksBackend logits_dtype=torch.float32 weights_dtype=torch.float32
Blackwell SM100: is_sm100=True  is_sm100_or_newer=True  prefill_deep_gemm=True  decode_deep_gemm=True  candidate_prefill=sparse-branch (the candidate indexer needs DeepGEMM's paged sparse MQA logits (s logits_dtype=torch.bfloat16 weights_dtype=torch.bfloat16
 GB202 SM120: is_sm100=False is_sm100_or_newer=True  prefill_deep_gemm=True  decode_deep_gemm=True  candidate_prefill=DenseBlocksBackend logits_dtype=torch.float32 weights_dtype=torch.float32
  GB10 SM121: is_sm100=False is_sm100_or_newer=True  prefill_deep_gemm=True  decode_deep_gemm=True  candidate_prefill=DenseBlocksBackend logits_dtype=torch.float32 weights_dtype=torch.float32
    non-CUDA: is_sm100=False is_sm100_or_newer=False prefill_deep_gemm=False decode_deep_gemm=False candidate_prefill=DenseBlocksBackend logits_dtype=torch.float32 weights_dtype=torch.float32
```

(The `sparse-branch (...)` note on SM100 is the script's own display shortening: on this CPU-only box the SM100 sparse branch is reached but the paged-sparse DeepGEMM logits are unavailable, so the factory raises `RuntimeError: the candidate indexer needs DeepGEMM's paged sparse MQA logits ...` before constructing the backend. Reaching that error proves the sparse branch was selected.)

## Accuracy Tests

No model-output change is expected: the dense DeepGEMM path on SM120 runs the same fp32 logits/weights contract the dtype gates already selected, and SM100/SM90/non-CUDA routing is unchanged (see reproducer above). End-to-end accuracy on SM120 hardware was **not** verified by me — no SM120 GPU was available in this environment; verification on GB10 by the reporter or maintainers would be appreciated.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

I ran no GPU benchmarks (no SM120 hardware available here). The speed numbers in Motivation are the reporter's measurements from #49173 (~125 ms/layer, ~480 vs ~4000 tok/s on 4096-token chunks). The fix restores the pre-#48399 routing, so prefill on GB10 should return to the DeepGEMM path the reporter ran in production before #48399.

Covers the dense gates on SM90/SM100/SM120/SM121/non-CUDA, the strict candidate gate, and the fp32 dtype gates off SM100.)

title: [Fix] sgl-router: Count media in typed gRPC Generate, embeddings and rerank access logs
author: ShangmingCai
body:
## Motivation

#48801 added `images` / `videos` / `audios` counts to the router's `http_request` and `grpc_request` access-log lines, but only chat `messages` and `/generate` fill them in. Three paths that carry media to the engine still log 0, so those requests look text-only in the log:

- Typed gRPC `Generate`: `GenerateRequest` has `image_data`, `video_data` and `audio_data` (`proto/sglang/runtime/v1/sglang.proto`), which the router forwards, but `PreparedRequest::typed` hard-coded `MediaCounts::default()`.
- `/v1/embeddings` (HTTP and the OpenAI gRPC `Embed`): the engine accepts `MultimodalEmbeddingInput` items with `image` / `video`.
- `/v1/rerank` (HTTP and gRPC): the engine accepts `image_url` / `video_url` content parts in `query` and `documents`.

## Modifications

- `RoutingView` gains `media`. `GenerateRequest::view()` counts its three media fields; the other typed RPCs have no media fields and report 0.
- `PreparedRequest::typed` uses `view.media` on the generate path.
- `embedding_media`: counts non-null `image` and `video` of each `input` item. Text and token-ID inputs count nothing.
- `rerank_media`: counts media content parts of `query` and each document once, as the client sent them (the engine fans each document out with the query, but the access line describes the client request). It reuses `MediaCounts::add_part`, which chat already uses.

Logging only. Routing, forwarding and request bodies are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable; logging only.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Not applicable. Both counters walk an already parsed `Value`; the typed one reads three vector lengths.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit or integration tests: `generate_view_counts_media_fields` (grpc.rs) and `embeddings_and_rerank_count_media_inputs` (preparation.rs). Red/green locally: with the counting removed both fail (rerank checked on its own too); with the fix `cargo test --lib` passes 1129/1129 and `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` is clean.
- [ ] Add documentation if needed.

title: [Fix] ci: Update the rerun-test reply status when a run is rerun
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Why the status didn't update

When a `/rerun-test` run fails and is then rerun from the Actions page, the reply comment keeps the first attempt's ❌ even after the rerun passes. On #49151 the `ubuntu-latest` batch reran green, and the rerun's `write-back-result` job logged:

```
Marker <!--rrt:0:done--> already present; nothing to do.
```

`scripts/ci/utils/update_rerun_test_status.py` treats a line that already carries the `:done` marker as final for every status. That guard is meant for the start beacon (a late `running` must not overwrite a result), but it also stops a rerun's finalizer from writing its own result.

## Changes

- On a `:done` line, `running` is still a no-op, so neither a rerun's start beacon nor a late beacon of the first attempt changes the result.
- A terminal status (`success` or `failure`) now rewrites the icon on the `:done` line, so the latest attempt's result is what the comment shows.

## Verification

I ran the script against the body of the #49151 reply comment with a fake GitHub API:

| step | result |
|---|---|
| rerun beacon, `running` on the `:done` line | no-op, ❌ kept |
| rerun finalizer, `success` | ❌ becomes ✅ |
| another rerun, `failure` | ✅ becomes ❌ |
| a different batch's marker | only its own line changes |
| first dispatch: `running`, `running`, `failure`, late `running` | 🔄, no-op, ❌ with `:done`, no-op (same as before) |

title: [Fix] session: Defer a session close while an unfinished turn still reads its media
author: hnyls2002
body:
Follows #49204, which removed the session `replace` parameter.

## Problem

Session turns skip the per-request media cleanup: a later turn's prompt contains the earlier turns' images, so the session keeps those features and frees them when it closes. The close deferred only for a streaming session with a turn in flight. A non-streaming session closed at once, explicitly or by the timeout reaper, and freed the features while a turn that reads them was still queued or prefilling.

## Fix

- `_has_live_readers(session)` is true while the streaming turn is in flight or an unfinished turn holds media. A close then sets `close_on_finish`, as streaming sessions already did, and `maybe_reap` finishes it once the predicate is false. While the close is deferred, the session rejects new turns and its id cannot be reopened, the same as a deferred streaming close.
- A session without media, or whose turns have all finished, closes immediately as before. Its KV is safe either way: a running request keeps its own lock and row.
- The reaper skips timed-out sessions whose close is already deferred, so it no longer re-closes and logs them every second; the deferred close finishes them.

## Tests

- `test_session_token_share_unit.py`: a close, explicit and by timeout, waits for an unfinished child that reads its parent's image, then frees the image after the child finishes. It fails without the fix.
- Session unit tests pass locally (token share, streaming session, sampling-mask validation).
