title: [Fix] disaggregation: Unregister a failed staging room before releasing its KV
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Problem

When a PD decode transfer fails and is not held for deferred release, `pop_transferred_with_outcomes` releases the request (which clears `req.kv.req_pool_idx`) before it unregisters the request's staging room. With the default `SGLANG_PLB_SCATTER_DEFER=0`, the KV manager's receive thread scatters arriving chunks itself, so it can scatter a pending chunk for the still-registered room in that window. `_scatter_region` then indexes `req_to_token[None, start:end]`, which selects whole rows of other requests, and writes the failed request's chunk into live requests' KV.

The deferred path (`_do_release`) already unregisters before it releases. With `SGLANG_PLB_SCATTER_DEFER=1` the scatter runs on the scheduler thread and cannot interleave.

## Fix

- The immediate-release branch unregisters the staging room before the release, the same order as `_do_release`.
- `_unregister_staging_room` replaces the three copies of the registered-room check.

## Tests

- `test_deferred_decode_kv_release.py`: a failed staging transfer released at once unregisters its room before the release. The test fails on main with the order reversed.
- A CPU reproduction with the real `DecodeStagingHandler`, `ReqToTokenPool` and torch scatter path, forcing the interleaving with a thread, showed a live request's K overwritten by the failed request's staged chunk on main.
- `test_deferred_decode_kv_release.py`, `test_decode_queue_cleanup.py` and `test_staging_draft_kv_slots.py` pass locally.

title: [Fix] diffusion: Let FLUX.3 Image start with --num-gpus alone
author: Smallfu666
body:
## Motivation

`sglang serve --model-path black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base --num-gpus 2`, with no `--tp-size` or SP flag, exits before loading weights:

```
  File ".../runtime/server_args/server_args.py", line 1807, in _model_default_uses_cfg
    and getattr(default_params, "guidance_scale", 0) > 1.0
TypeError: '>' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'float'
```

Resolving `ServerArgs` on CPU raises the same error for 4 and 8 GPUs and for Klein. FLUX.3 Image leaves `guidance_scale = None` in its default sampling params because the package supplies it per request ([flux3_image.py#L79-L81](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4003bf1077debcca3fccfa6e0d7b56ed584aa727/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/configs/pipeline_configs/flux3_image.py#L79-L81)), and the CFG-parallel auto rule compares that default with 1.0 ([server_args.py#L1805-L1808](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4003bf1077debcca3fccfa6e0d7b56ed584aa727/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/server_args/server_args.py#L1805-L1808)). The two-GPU cookbook commands (`--tp-size 2`, `--ulysses-degree 2`) skip this check.

## Modifications

- `_model_default_uses_cfg` treats a `None` default `guidance_scale` as no default CFG. FLUX.3 then resolves `--num-gpus 2` to sequence parallelism (K/V gather 2) and 4/8 GPUs to Ulysses 4/8.
- Test: `ServerArgs.from_dict` on a local FLUX.3 package (base and flow-map) with `num_gpus=2`. It raises the `TypeError` on main and passes with this change.

```bash
pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_flux3_image_served.py -k num_gpus_without_parallel_flags
```

## Accuracy Tests

2× H200, `black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base`, default request (1024x1024, package-default steps and guidance), one prompt, seed 0:

| Server | Result |
| --- | --- |
| main, `--num-gpus 2` | exits with the `TypeError` above |
| this PR, `--num-gpus 1` | pixel-identical to main `--num-gpus 1` |
| this PR, `--num-gpus 2` (SP 2) | starts; vs 1 GPU: PSNR 61.1 dB, max abs pixel difference 5 (seed 1 vs seed 0: 12.6 dB) |

Not run: the distilled Klein, 4 and 8 GPUs (resolution checked on CPU only), speed and profiling.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

None; startup argument resolution only.

title: [Fix] diffusion: Use K/V gather when auto SP cannot split the DiT's heads (Z-Image on 4 GPUs)
author: Smallfu666
body:
## Motivation

`sglang serve --model-path Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo --num-gpus 4` starts, but every generation request returns HTTP 500:

```
File ".../runtime/layers/usp.py", line 389, in _usp_input_all_to_all
    assert h_global % world_size == 0, (
AssertionError: h_global (30) must be divisible by world_size (4)
```

With no parallel flags, Z-Image-Turbo (no CFG by default) puts all 4 GPUs into sequence parallelism, and for an SP degree above 2 the auto layout picks Ulysses, which splits the attention heads across ranks:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4003bf1077debcca3fccfa6e0d7b56ed584aa727/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/server_args/server_args.py#L1748-L1763

The Z-Image DiT has 30 heads ([config](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4003bf1077debcca3fccfa6e0d7b56ed584aa727/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/configs/models/dits/zimage.py#L19)), so Ulysses over 4 ranks hits the assert above. By the same code path, `--num-gpus 8` gives Ulysses 8 for Z-Image-Turbo and CFG 2 x Ulysses 4 for Z-Image, which cannot split 30 heads either. `--num-gpus 2` works because SP 2 already uses K/V gather. From the code, Ming-Image (its DiT reuses the Z-Image transformer) is affected the same way.

## Modifications

- `ServerArgs._adjust_parallelism`: when the auto layout would pick Ulysses but the DiT arch config's `num_attention_heads` does not divide `sp_degree`, set `kv_gather_degree = sp_degree` instead (marked auto, as for SP 2). K/V gather gathers K/V along the sequence and keeps every head on every rank, so it does not need the heads to divide. Arch configs that leave `num_attention_heads` at 0 keep the current behaviour, and explicit `--ulysses-degree` / `--ring-degree` / `--kv-gather-degree` are not touched.
- `test_server_args.py`: Z-Image config at 4 and 8 GPUs resolves to K/V gather at the SP degree (fails before this change, passes with it); at 3 GPUs (30 heads divide) it stays on Ulysses.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= SGLANG_DIFFUSION_PLATFORM_OVERRIDE=cpu python -m pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_server_args.py -k KVGather
```

## Accuracy Tests

Z-Image-Turbo, 4x H200, one T2I request (1024x1024, seed 0, default 9 steps), SGLang main of 2026-11-08 (Python package on top of the 2026-11-06 dev image), `--warmup-mode off` and otherwise default flags; decoded RGB pixels compared with the `--num-gpus 1` image:

| | layout | result vs 1 GPU |
|---|---|---|
| main, `--num-gpus 4` | Ulysses 4 | HTTP 500 (assert above) |
| this change, `--num-gpus 4` | K/V gather 4 | PSNR 47.75 dB, SSIM 0.997, max abs 36 |
| main, `--num-gpus 4 --kv-gather-degree 4` | K/V gather 4 | identical to this change |
| this change, `--num-gpus 2` | K/V gather 2 | identical to 1 GPU (unchanged) |

For scale, on the same request `--attention-backend torch_sdpa` on one GPU differs from the default by 29.14 dB, and a different seed by 15.16 dB, so the 4-GPU image is a close match, not bit-identical. Repeating the request on the 4-GPU server gave the same image.

Not run: Z-Image (base), 8-GPU inference, TP or CFG-parallel combined with SP, other models and resolutions, and speed or profiling; the 8-GPU and Z-Image (base) failures above are read from the code, and the unit test checks only the layout resolution.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not measured.

title: [Fix] CI: Avoid coverage fail-fast cycles on diffusion reruns
author: mickqian
body:
A failed `diffusion-coverage-check` can prevent an individual producer-job rerun from reaching its tests. Coverage consumes those producer reports, so treating its previous failure as a root cause creates a fail-fast cycle. This occurred in [#49078’s 5090 rerun](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42379972109/job/128458495252).

Exclude the coverage summary from sibling root-failure detection. Lint and actual test failures still stop sibling jobs; the final coverage check remains required and continues to fail for missing reports or failed cases. This change does not alter memory/performance thresholds or fix the original memory failure.

title: [Fix] scheduler: Retract every KV holder on pause and order a few releases behind in-flight steps
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Motivation

`pause_generation(mode="retract")` misses some requests that hold KV, and under PP it can retract one request twice. A paused scheduler then never becomes idle, so `release_memory_occupation` fails for the whole pause, and a dLLM request crashes the scheduler on resume. Separately, two operations do not wait for a step that is already launched.

## Changes

**Retract once per pause.** `_retract_batch` ran once per PP micro-batch but also swept scheduler-wide sources, so a chunked request that also sat in a later micro-batch's last batch was retracted twice. `_retract_batches` now takes every micro-batch's `(running_batch, last_batch)` pair, collects them and the scheduler-wide sources, removes duplicates, and retracts once. Under PP, every micro-batch's requests are now requeued before the chunked request.

**HiSparse staging.** A prefilled request waiting in `ack_staging_queue` for its host copy was not retracted. The retract now takes the whole queue, so every TP rank retracts the same set.

**dLLM.**
- A retracted request stayed in `DllmManager`'s queues, and `add_waiting_reqs` raised `Redundant requests detected in dLLM requests` on resume. A finished one stayed in `staging_queue` for the whole pause.
- `DllmManager.take(pred)` now hands over the requests that hold a row, after finished ones are dropped.
- `reset_dllm_progress` restarts a retracted request as incoming, with its FDFO state cleared; `init_diffusion_llm` uses it too. The incoming phase counts output as well as prompt, since a retracted request re-encodes both.

**HiSparse release.** `retract_req` is folded into `request_finished`, renamed `release_request`, so `release` and `retract` take the same path. A request still in staging always goes through `_release_staging` (formerly `abort_staging_request`).

**LoRA unload.** With overlap or `pp_size > 1`, the schedule stream now waits for the forward stream before the adapter's slot is zeroed. Today the step still running the adapter only carries finished requests, so no wrong output is visible.

**PP skipped output.** Its completion waited on `unified_forward_done`, which only the unified pool sets. It now waits on the forward event `_pp_launch_batch` records, for every pool, on a side stream.

**Cleanup.** A redundant `finished_output` guard in `DecodePreallocQueue` is removed; `stream_output` already skips it.

Without overlap, PP, PD, dLLM, HiSparse or LoRA, nothing changes.

## Tests

- `test_scheduler_pause_generation.py`: PP retracts a request found in two sources once; HiSparse staging requests are retracted; a dLLM retract takes every row holder, drops finished ones, and restarts the rest.
- `test_lora_lru_unload_unit.py`: the overlap unload waits for the forward stream.
- `test_pp_skip_output_retirement.py`: without the unified pool, the skipped output follows the forward.
- Related unit tests pass locally.

title: [Fix] cuda-graph: Pause automatic GC during CUDA graph capture
author: fengshaoyi-amd
body:
## Motivation

`freeze_gc` wraps CUDA graph capture unless `--enable-cudagraph-gc` is set. It collects once and freezes the surviving objects, but leaves automatic collection running. Objects allocated inside the capture loop, for example by `torch.compile` warmup and autotuning before each batch size, can therefore be collected while a stream is capturing. When one of them is a kernel whose finalizer unloads its GPU module, the unload is rejected on the capturing stream (error 900) and the capture is invalidated (error 901). Two finalizers do this:

- Triton's `CompiledKernel.__del__`. We hit it on MI355X with `--enable-torch-compile` (`rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm720-mi35x-20261008`): `Triton Error [HIP]: Code: 900, operation not permitted when stream is capturing` was raised in `CompiledKernel.__del__`, and the capture at bs=56 failed.
- Inductor's statically launched kernels, whose `__del__` calls `close()` → `_unload_kernel()` since torch 2.13. pytorch/pytorch#199117 reports the same capture failure from this path after max-autotune, and notes that keeping cyclic GC disabled during capture makes its reproducer pass. sglang's CUDA build pins torch 2.14.1.

Whether a collection lands inside a capture depends on allocation counts, so the failure is intermittent: the same command can capture cleanly on one run and crash on the next.

## Modifications

- `freeze_gc` calls `gc.disable()` after `gc.freeze()`. On exit it re-enables GC only if GC was enabled on entry, then unfreezes and collects as before, so garbage created during capture is collected once, after capture ends. With `--enable-cudagraph-gc` nothing changes.
- The `--enable-cudagraph-gc` help text and `server_arguments.mdx` say that automatic GC is paused during capture by default.
- `test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_freeze_gc.py` (CPU): cyclic garbage created inside the window is not finalized until the window exits, and a caller that had GC disabled keeps it disabled.

vLLM's capture path also pauses GC next to the freeze (`vllm/utils/gc_utils.py`, vllm-project/vllm#54646). pytorch/pytorch#199541 (open) proposes pausing GC inside `torch.cuda.graph` itself; this change covers the torch versions sglang pins today.

## Accuracy Tests

This only changes when GC runs; it does not change numerics. GSM8K, 200 questions, few-shot, Qwen3-8B, TP1 on MI355X:

| Config | Stock | Patched |
|---|---|---|
| Default | 0.965 | 0.950 |
| `--enable-torch-compile` (2 runs each) | 0.950 / 0.950 | 0.945 / 0.945 |

The differences are 1–3 questions in both directions, within run-to-run noise.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Capture on MI355X, `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.23-rocm10-mi35x-20261105` (torch 2.11, Python 3.12), Qwen3-8B, TP1, 52 decode batch sizes, cold compile caches for every run. Common args: `--mem-fraction-static 0.8 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --attention-backend aiter --disable-radix-cache --context-length 8192`.

| Config | Variant | Capture time | Capture memory | Peak RSS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Default | Stock | 10.05 s | 1.36 GB | 10.88 GB |
| Default | Patched | 8.63 s | 1.35 GB | 9.98 GB |
| `--enable-torch-compile --torch-compile-max-bs 64` | Stock (2 runs) | 303.6 / 291.9 s | 4.08 / 4.25 GB | 14.32 / 13.96 GB |
| `--enable-torch-compile --torch-compile-max-bs 64` | Patched (2 runs) | 284.1 / 265.9 s | 4.16 / 4.09 GB | 13.95 / 13.74 GB |

Capture memory and peak RSS stay within noise, and capture is not slower. All seven server runs captured without errors. On this image the natural failure does not occur with or without the patch, because torch 2.11's static launcher never unloads modules.

The reproducer below hands a loaded Triton kernel to a reference cycle inside the capture, so only an automatic collection can free it. On the same image:

- Stock: `RuntimeError: Triton Error [HIP]: Code: 900, Messsage: operation not permitted when stream is capturing` in `CompiledKernel.__del__`, then `CUDA error: operation failed due to a previous error during capture`.
- Patched: the capture succeeds, the graph replays correctly, and the kernel is unloaded after capture ends.

<details>
<summary>Reproducer (trimmed from the script used for the results above)</summary>

```python
import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl

from sglang.srt.model_executor.runner.base_cuda_graph_runner import freeze_gc


@triton.jit
def add_one(x_ptr, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
    offs = tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
    tl.store(x_ptr + offs, tl.load(x_ptr + offs) + 1)


x = torch.zeros(128, device="cuda")
y = torch.zeros(128, device="cuda")
graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
with freeze_gc(enable_cudagraph_gc=False):
    kernel = add_one[(1,)](x, BLOCK=128)
    add_one.device_caches.clear()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
        y.add_(1)
        holder = [kernel]
        holder.append(holder)
        del kernel, holder
        junk = [[i] for i in range(50_000)]
graph.replay()
torch.cuda.synchronize()
assert bool((y == 1).all())
```

</details>

title: [Fix] diffusion: Compute CFG normalization over the whole latent under sequence parallelism (Z-Image)
author: Smallfu666
body:
## Motivation

`sglang serve --model-path Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image --num-gpus 4` returns a visibly different image than `--num-gpus 1` for the same request and seed: on 4x H200, 1,017,344 of 1,048,576 pixels differ (PSNR 22.78 dB, max abs 255). The same happens with sequence parallelism alone (`--num-gpus 2 --cfg-parallel-size 1`).

Z-Image enables CFG normalization by default (`cfg_normalization=True`), which clamps the guided prediction by the norm of the whole latent:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4003bf1077debcca3fccfa6e0d7b56ed584aa727/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/distributed/cfg_policy.py#L137-L151

Under sequence parallelism the denoising stage shards Z-Image latents along height or width ([zimage.py](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4003bf1077debcca3fccfa6e0d7b56ed584aa727/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/configs/pipeline_configs/zimage.py#L308-L321)), so each rank computes the norm of its own half and scales its half by a different factor. With `guidance_scale=0`, or with Z-Image-Turbo (normalization off) even when CFG is on, SP output is identical to one GPU, which points at the normalization.

## Modifications

- `_apply_cfg_normalization`: when the stage has sharded the latents for SP (`batch.did_sp_shard_latents`), compute both norms on the latents gathered with the pipeline config's own `gather_latents_for_sp`, then scale the local shard. Without SP nothing changes.
- `test_cfg_policy.py`: `ZImageCFGPolicy.combine` on two height shards (SP world size 2 patched in, gather returning the full tensor) must equal the single-rank result bitwise. It fails before this change and passes with it.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= SGLANG_DIFFUSION_PLATFORM_OVERRIDE=cpu python -m pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_cfg_policy.py
```

## Accuracy Tests

Z-Image, H200, T2I 1024x1024, seed 0, default 50 steps and guidance, SGLang main of 2026-11-08 (Python package on top of the 2026-11-06 dev image), `--warmup-mode off`; decoded RGB pixels compared with `--num-gpus 1`:

| | default request (negative prompt "") | negative prompt "blurry, low quality, distorted" |
|---|---|---|
| main, `--num-gpus 2 --cfg-parallel-size 1` (SP 2) | 22.78 dB, max abs 255 | 21.74 dB, max abs 255 |
| this change, same | identical | identical |
| this change, `--num-gpus 4` (default: CFG parallel 2 x SP 2) | identical | not run |

For scale, a different seed gives 11.77 dB on this request. `--num-gpus 1` output is unchanged by this change, and repeating the request on the patched SP server gave the same image.

Not run: other models or requests that set `cfg_normalization`, `guidance_rescale` under SP (its std over the local shard has the same pattern and is not changed here), other resolutions, and speed or profiling.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

When normalization is on under SP, each step now all-gathers two latent-sized tensors (16x128x128 FP32 per sample at 1024x1024).

title: [Fix] mem_cache: Reset a reused request row's state in the next forward
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #49312
* #49311
* #49310
* #49309
* #49301
* #49300
* __->__ #49299

## Motivation

A request row is handed out again the moment its request ends, while the forward that ran that request last may still read or advance the row's request-scoped device state, such as the speculative ReplaySSM ring and its cursors (`replayssm_spec_write_pos`, `replayssm_cache_base`, `replayssm_is_flush`). The reset at hand-out ran on the scheduling stream, which the write-after-read barrier does not order after that forward: the old forward could advance the new owner's cursor, or the new owner could read what the old forward wrote after the reset.

## Modifications

- Handing a row out only marks it (`RowResets`). The next forward resets the marked rows on its own stream before its kernels (`ModelRunner.forward`), so the reset is ordered after the last forward of the row's previous request and before the first of its new one. It runs outside every CUDA graph; a replay reads the state through the row ids its batch already carries.
- Unified storage resets the row's whole request memory this way; static pools reset their ReplaySSM cursors this way.
- A restored retraction backup writes the row whole and is not reset.
- TODOs mark the request parts a PD transfer would deliver (none under unified memory today: it refuses DeepSeek-V4), whose reset must instead be ordered before the transfer.

- A retraction backup taken before a reused row's first forward applies the row's pending reset before it copies the row, so a request retracted before its first forward restores clean ReplaySSM cursors and ring, not the previous request's; a backup of state the request's own forward wrote is restored as is (`KVStorage.reset_row_before_backup`, `RowResets.apply_row`).

- MLX's auxiliary state pool declares the three ReplaySSM cursor fields as `None`, so the reset reads them directly.

## Accuracy Tests

No model output changes. Unit tests (B200, torch 2.14.1+cu130, flashinfer 0.7.2): `test_unified_row_state_reset.py` (the reset runs through `ModelRunner.forward`'s hook, for unified storage and a static ReplaySSM pool; a backup before the first forward restores reset cursors and ring, and one after the request's own forward keeps its state) and `kv/test_declared_parts.py` pass at the default invariant level and with `SGLANG_INVARIANT_CHECK=2`.

title: [Fix] mamba: Commit verified states into the slots the verify forward resolved
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #49312
* #49311
* #49310
* __->__ #49309
* #49301
* #49300
* #49299

## Motivation

The scheduler waits only for a forward's declared shared-read end before it
rewrites the request table and the state slots' virtual-to-physical map, for
example to free a finished request and hand its row to another. Several readers
ran later in the same forward and looked those tables up again, so they could
see the row's new owner and write its state:

- the post-verify Mamba commit (ReplaySSM circular, fold and KDA fold branches,
  and the generic scatter's checkpoint slots), including EAGLE's post-verify
  graphs, whose commit replays on a side stream;
- HybridLinearAttnBackend.update_mamba_state_after_mtp_verify on the
  pipeline-stable-rows path;
- Inkling's conv-state commit off the recordable slot gather;
- Qwen4-Exp's per-forward PLE preparation inside the model forward.

## Modifications

These now read ForwardStateSlots: the working and checkpoint slots the
attention backend resolved while preparing the forward's metadata
(`forward_state_slots`). EAGLE's post-verify graphs stage them with the round's
other inputs, so the captured commit reads fixed buffers refilled each round.

A speculative verify graph has no graph input for the checkpoint ids, so its
replay prep never resolved them; the decode graph runner now stages the batch's
ids in a static buffer that the replay prep translates with the other slots.
Inkling resolves a verify's checkpoint slots outside its recorded prep.

Qwen4-Exp asks the outer attention backend for the slots, whichever backends it composes. The Ascend verify commits write the checkpoint slots the same forward resolved, as the generic commit does.

A pipeline stage's relayed commit runs after its forward ended, while the
batch's requests still own their rows; it resolves the slots when it runs, so
it follows a compaction that moved them since.

## Accuracy Tests

Unit tests (B200, torch 2.14.1+cu130, flashinfer 0.7.2): `kv/test_forward_state_slots.py` (each late reader writes the slots the forward resolved after the tables change; the Ascend verify commit writes the resolved working and checkpoint slots; a speculative verify graph replay resolves its checkpoint slots; a relayed PP commit follows a move), `kv/test_declared_parts.py`, `test_inkling_checkpoint_indices.py`, `test_prefill_cuda_graph_runner_helpers.py`, `test_ngram_mamba_verify_update.py` and `test_eagle_post_verify_graphs.py` pass at the default invariant level and with `SGLANG_INVARIANT_CHECK=2`, except `test_eagle_post_verify_graphs.py::test_fused_tail_matches_stock`, which fails to build a FlashInfer JIT kernel in the test environment, as on `main`.

title: [Fix] scheduler: Apply the write-after-read barrier in the PP loops and on every unified-memory device
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #49312
* #49311
* __->__ #49310
* #49309
* #49301
* #49300
* #49299

## Motivation

The write-after-read barrier orders a page's next write after the forwards that may still read it. Under `--enable-unified-memory`, pages move and are reused across sub-pools, so the barrier is required, but it was applied only on CUDA-like devices and not in the pipeline-parallel event loops, where a micro-batch's pages could be rewritten while a launched forward still read them.

## Modifications

- Under `--enable-unified-memory` the barrier is on for every device; MPS and MLX, which cannot order the barrier's stream waits, are refused at startup.
- The PP event loops apply the barrier once per launched micro-batch, after its result is processed, as the non-PP loops do per step.
- `SGLANG_ENABLE_WAR_BARRIER` is no longer needed to turn it on under unified memory.

- The PP tests order the CUDA fixture's initialization before the schedule-stream writes and pin `SGLANG_ENABLE_WAR_BARRIER` and `SGLANG_FORCE_COARSE_WAR_BARRIER`, so they do not depend on the caller's shell.

## Accuracy Tests

No model output changes. Unit tests (B200, torch 2.14.1+cu130, flashinfer 0.7.2): new `test_pp_war_barrier.py` (the PP loops apply the barrier per micro-batch, CUDA cases included) and `test_disagg_idle_step_counters.py` pass at the default invariant level and with `SGLANG_INVARIANT_CHECK=2`.

title: [Fix] mem_cache: Signal a double free of unified pages when invariant checks are on
author: ch-wan
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #49312
* __->__ #49311
* #49310
* #49309
* #49301
* #49300
* #49299

## Motivation

The unified bands free pages lazily, without a host read, so a double free, or a free of a page never allocated, returned a tombstone to the free list unnoticed.

## Modifications

At invariant level WARN and up (`SGLANG_INVARIANT_CHECK`), every freed page is checked on the device to be bound, in both the end-band and float-band free paths (`band.free_of_bound_page`, fatal). The unused host-reading check of the removed eager free path is dropped. At level OFF nothing changes.

The fused free kernel (`free_unbind_inplace`) and its CPU reference skip the reverse-table tombstone for a page that is not bound, so such a free reaches the check instead of writing before the table.

## Accuracy Tests

No model output changes. Unit tests (B200, torch 2.14.1+cu130, flashinfer 0.7.2): `test_unified_free_no_host_sync.py` (the kernel writes nothing outside the table for an unbound page; a double free and a never-allocated free report `band.free_of_bound_page` through an end band and a float band, at both checking levels, the CUDA device-assert cases in subprocesses, in `test_unified_free_unbound_page_cuda.py` (nightly); a free of pages allocated again after a first free reports nothing), `test_unified_fixed_free_pages.py`, `test_multi_ended_allocator.py` and `test_unified_page_safety_stress.py` pass with `SGLANG_INVARIANT_CHECK=2`, with the check on, and at the default level.

title: [Fix] moe: Validate the scale grid and use logical K for even_Ks in the GPTQ/AWQ Triton MoE kernel
author: tiny-star3
body:
## Motivation

`fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq` has two K-tail problems when the per-rank K is not a multiple of `BLOCK_SIZE_K`:

1. **Packed int4 weights are loaded without a mask.** #48556 fixes this with the same one-line change, which this PR also contains (the hunk is byte-identical, so either order merges cleanly).
2. **Scales are read past the end of an incomplete grid.** The kernel picks scale group `k // group_size`. If a caller's grid has fewer than `cdiv(K, group_size)` groups, the K tail reads the next row's scales, and on the last row it reads past the scale tensor. A mask cannot fix this, because those K positions hold real data. compressed-tensors WNA16 builds such a grid today: at `moe_intermediate_size=640`, `moe_tp_size=4` (K=160 per rank) it creates `160 // 128 = 1` group while the kernel needs 2.

On Qwen3.8-Flash-Next W4A16 (compressed-tensors, group 128), 8× A800, `--tp 8 --ep 2 --moe-runner-backend triton`, every EP1 rank dies with `illegal memory access` during CUDA graph capture, and with `--disable-cuda-graph` it dies on the first prefill. **Masking only the B load does not stop the crash**: the scale over-read still faults.

This path is the default in two places: compressed-tensors WNA16 MoE always uses `CompressedTensorsWNA16TritonMoE` on ROCm, and selects it automatically on SM100/SM103 (`compressed_tensors.py:1003-1033`).

## Modifications

- Mask the B load with the existing K mask (same as #48556).
- Before launch, require `B_scale.shape[2]` (and `B_zp.shape[2]`) to equal `cdiv(K, group_size)`; otherwise raise `ValueError` instead of reading out of bounds. Existing callers already satisfy this: moe_wna16 halves `group_size` until it divides K, the tuning scripts size scales with `cdiv`, and aligned compressed-tensors shards have `K // group_size == cdiv(K, group_size)`. Misaligned compressed-tensors shards now fail loudly at the first forward; #49338 makes them build a complete grid.
- Compute this kernel's `even_Ks` from the logical K it iterates over (`A.shape[1]`) instead of the packed int4 width `B.shape[2]`. The old value was never wrongly True (K/2 % BK == 0 implies K % BK == 0), so this is not needed for correctness; it drops a redundant mask on shapes such as K=160, BK=32. The `even_Ks` used by the generic kernel is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

New `test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_moe_wna16_triton.py`:

- `test_packed_k_tail_stays_inside_weight_tensor` places the packed weight at the end of a CUDA VMM mapping followed by an unmapped granule, so any over-read faults deterministically (with a plain allocation the caching allocator's slack hides the bug). It also checks the exact output across a 128 + 32 group split.
- `test_w4a16_rejects_incomplete_scale_grid` covers the grid check.

On A800 (SM80); the kernel and `invoke_fused_moe_kernel` are unchanged between f6db18e and current main:

| Test | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_packed_k_tail_stays_inside_weight_tensor` | illegal memory access | pass |
| `test_w4a16_rejects_incomplete_scale_grid` | does not raise | pass |

With a 1-group scale tensor (the grid compressed-tensors builds at K=160) placed at the end of a VMM mapping, both main and a B-mask-only variant hit illegal memory access; this PR raises `Expected 2 scale groups for K=160 and group_size=128, got 1` before launch.

Old and new `even_Ks` give bit-identical outputs on 12 shapes (K 80–2560, BK 32/64/128), each within 2.3e-3 relative error of an fp32 reference.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The grid check runs on the host, once per launch. On shapes where K % BK == 0 but (K/2) % BK != 0, the `even_Ks` change removes the mask: K=160, BK=32, M=4096, N=2560 goes from 118.4 µs to 94.1 µs on A800.

title: [Fix] compressed-tensors: Size the FP8 MoE w13 by the layer's gating
author: Smallfu666
body:
## Motivation

`RedHatAI/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-FP8` (compressed-tensors FP8) allocates its routed-expert w13 at twice the size it needs, which on one H200 with the default launch costs 13.7 GiB of weights and about 17 % of decode throughput. NemotronH experts are non-gated (relu2, `up_proj` only), but `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8MoE.create_weights` always sizes w13 as gate + up (`is_concat=True`). The loader zero-fills the second half, so outputs are correct, but every MoE layer keeps that zero half and the first MoE GEMM runs over it.

`Fp8MoEMethod` already sizes w13 by `is_gated` (#36097); the compressed-tensors scheme was not updated.

## Modifications

- `compressed_tensors_w8a8_fp8_moe.py`: size w13 and its per-tensor / block weight scales with one shard for non-gated layers; the per-tensor requant loop follows the scale's shard count. ROCm AITER keeps the concatenated size, because `get_moe_weight_sizes` pads only a concatenated w13 to match the padded w2.
- New CPU test `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_fp8_moe_non_gated.py`: builds a `FusedMoE` from a compressed-tensors FP8 config (tensor, channel and block strategies) and loads weights through `FusedMoE.weight_loader`. On main the non-gated case fails (w13 has 768 rows instead of 384); the gated control passes on both. Run with `python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_fp8_moe_non_gated.py`.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K, 200 questions, 5-shot (`sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k`), 1×H200, default launch, two servers per side: before 0.845 / 0.850, after 0.840 / 0.855.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path RedHatAI/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-FP8` on 1×H200 (TP 1, default flags). Both sides ran the same SGLang dev image built from main on 2026-11-06, with `configs/nemotron_h.py` from main mounted because this checkpoint's config needs #47458; the only difference between before and after was the changed scheme file. Servers ran in the order before, after, after, before. Client: `python -m sglang.benchmark.serving --dataset-name random-ids --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 --random-range-ratio 1 --num-prompts 256 --max-concurrency 64`.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| weight memory (`Load weight end … mem usage`, GiB) | 43.87 | 30.21 |
| KV pool `max_total_num_tokens` | 7,518,520 | 8,778,721 |
| output throughput (tok/s) | 4,634 / 4,667 | 5,627 / 5,626 |

At concurrency 1 the median TPOT goes from 2.424 to 2.329 ms. A torch profile of 20 forward steps under the concurrency-64 load shows `fused_moe_kernel` at 365 → 271 ms and the relu2 elementwise kernels at about half, since they no longer run on the zero half.

Not run: ROCm / AITER, GPUs other than H200, TP > 1, and the channel and block strategies end to end (those two are covered by the CPU test only).

title: [Fix] scheduler: Record every PP result completion event after the local forward
author: hnyls2002
body:
- **PP:** every PP result's completion event now comes from one helper, `_pp_result_done_event`, which waits for this rank's own forward of that micro-batch and then records. A received result's device-to-host copy, which today follows that forward only through the other ranks' send and receive order, now waits for it on the copy stream; a skipped output keeps recording on a side stream so the scheduler's stream takes no dependency.
- Tests: `test_pp_skip_output_retirement.py` checks that both the received and the skipped result's event is recorded after the local forward.

Whether a rank may reuse what a step used depends on that rank's own forward, so the completion event now says so directly. No output change is expected: a received output arrives long after the local forward ends.

title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] mega_moe: Accept MXFP4 activations at DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's 2304 intermediate size
author: trevor-m
body:
## Motivation

`--enable-w4a4-mxfp4-megamoe` (the `mxf4xmxf4` MegaMoE MMA type) does not start on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
`check_mega_moe_shapes` asks every MMA type other than `fp8xfp4` / `fp8xfp8` for `moe_intermediate_size % 512 == 0`,
and V4.1-Flash's is 2304:

```
ValueError: DeepGEMM MegaMoE (mxf4xmxf4) needs hidden_size to be a multiple of 512 and moe_intermediate_size to be a
multiple of 512; got hidden_size=5120, moe_intermediate_size=2304. Use another --moe-a2a-backend for this model.
```

The 512 comes from the 16-byte token SF rows: 16 UE8M0 scales x 32 elements. The MXFP4 path stores and loads the
intermediate SFs MN-major (token-contiguous), as the FP8 x FP4 path does, so the intermediate only needs the
128-element SF grouping that `fp8xfp4` already gets. The input SF rows still need `hidden % 512`, and V4.1-Flash's
5120 meets it.

## Modifications

- `check_mega_moe_shapes`: `mxf4xmxf4` takes the same `intermediate % 128` rule as `fp8xfp4` / `fp8xfp8`. The hidden
  rule and the other MMA types are unchanged.
- `test_mega_moe_deepgemm_api.py`: `test_shape_check_mxf4_takes_intermediate_multiples_of_128` (CPU). It accepts
  (5120, 2304) and rejects an intermediate that is not a multiple of 128 and a hidden that is not a multiple of 512. It
  fails on main and passes here, along with the rest of the file (20 tests).

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K, all 1319 questions, few-shot, greedy. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, aggregated DEP4 (TP4 / DP4 / EP4) on 4 Vera Rubin
GPUs, MegaMoE with localized weights and MegaGate, DSpark (block 3), EPLB rebalancing every 60 iterations. Within each
stack only `--enable-w4a4-mxfp4-megamoe` differs. Each number is one server:

| stack | FP8 (`fp8xfp4`, default) | MXFP4 (`mxf4xmxf4`, this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| main e60f7e909 + this change, HiCache, 32k-token chunks | 0.913 | 0.898, 0.904, 0.904 |
| earlier main fe6a8a32fd + this change and a few unrelated open PRs, 4k-token chunks | 0.908 | 0.904; 0.906 and 0.913 with a K=128 MMA variant of the DeepGEMM kernel (bit-identical output) |

MXFP4 averages 0.905 over six servers, and FP8 averages 0.911 over two. Servers with the same configuration differ by up
to 0.7 points. MXFP4 activations are lossy, and the flag stays opt-in. Kernels are stock sgl-deep-gemm 0.2.6 unless
noted. On e60f7e909 the top-k v2 cluster paths were compiled out because they do not build with the cu134 image
(#49385).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MegaMoE kernel alone on Vera Rubin, EP2, 384 experts, sgl-deep-gemm 0.2.6, main-kernel time on rank 0:

| tokens per rank | fp8xfp4 (us) | mxf4xmxf4 (us) | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 32768 (prefill) | 2189 | 1813 | -17% |
| 8192 | 666 | 582 | -13% |

Disaggregated DEP2 prefill worker on Vera Rubin, 131k-token cold contexts, slot-swapped A/B (n = 2 per arm): MXFP4
activations raised prefill throughput by 10.7% (+9.0% and +12.5%). That A/B ran a local K=128 MMA variant of the
DeepGEMM kernel. Its output is bit-identical to the stock K=64 kernel's, and its speed matches it.

title: [Fix] http_server: Exit when a scheduler dies with multiple tokenizer workers
author: Kangyan-Zhou
body:
## Motivation

With `--tokenizer-worker-num > 1`, a server whose scheduler has crashed keeps accepting HTTP requests. Nothing is left to serve them, so requests hang until an external health check (for example a Kubernetes liveness probe) kills the server. With typical probe settings that takes several minutes.

The cause is in the multi-worker HTTP path. The main process runs uvicorn's `Multiprocess` supervisor, which takes over the process's signal handlers:

- `Multiprocess.__init__` replaces the handler for INT, TERM, HUP, QUIT and the other entries in uvicorn's `SIGNALS` with a function that only appends the signal to a queue.
- `Multiprocess.handle_signals` dispatches each queued signal to `handle_<name>`. There is no `handle_quit`, so SIGQUIT is logged at debug level ("Received signal QUIT, but no handler is defined for it.") and dropped.

sglang uses SIGQUIT to mean "a child failed":

- `run_scheduler_process` sends SIGQUIT to its parent when the scheduler hits an exception.
- `SubprocessWatchdog` sends SIGQUIT to its own process when a child exits non-zero.

Both are expected to reach `launch_phase_sigquit_handler`, which kills the process tree. In multi-worker mode neither does. The tokenizer workers' own `running_phase_sigquit_handler` is in the worker processes, which never receive the signal.

There is a second gap. After a scheduler exception, `run_scheduler_process` returns normally and the process exits 0. `SubprocessWatchdog` treats exit code 0 as a clean shutdown, so this crash path also slipped past the backup check.

## Modifications

- `http_server.py`: add `_SigquitForwardingMultiprocess`. It saves the SIGQUIT handler installed before uvicorn takes over, and its `handle_quit` calls that handler from the supervisor loop. If no callable handler was installed, it falls back to `kill_process_tree`. Both multi-worker uvicorn paths use it:
  - The default path calls the new `_run_uvicorn_workers` instead of `uvicorn.run(app_path, workers=N, ...)`. It takes the same steps `uvicorn.run` takes for `workers > 1`: `Config`, then `bind_socket`, then the supervisor's `run`. It passes `target=` on uvicorn < 0.51, because only the main `pyproject.toml` pins uvicorn >= 0.51.
  - `_ReusePortMultiprocess` now inherits from it.
- `scheduler.py`: `run_scheduler_process` exits with code 1 after a scheduler exception.
- `rust_server/shutdown.py`: `RustServerSigtermDrain.wait` used to start the scheduler-exit time limit only when a scheduler exited 0 without a SIGTERM, which is how a crash used to exit. It now also starts the limit on a non-zero exit, so a `--custom-sigquit-handler` that leaves the tree alive no longer blocks the launcher on siblings stuck in a collective. Unlike a clean exit, the subprocess watchdog stays armed, so the crash is still reported.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no change to model execution.

## Tests

- New and updated unit tests:
  - `test_http_server_reuseport.py`: a SIGQUIT raised after the supervisor is constructed reaches the handler installed before it.
  - `test_crash_dump.py`: `test_scheduler_exception_dumps_before_sigquit` now expects `SystemExit(1)`.
  - `test_rust_server_shutdown.py`: a crashed scheduler (exit 1) next to a wedged sibling still starts the time limit, the sibling is killed, and the crash is still reported.
- Standalone checks, with the code taken from the patched source (no GPU or torch needed):
  - `_run_uvicorn_workers` with a real 2-worker server on uvicorn 0.54.0 and 0.34.0: it serves (200), then exits through the pre-installed handler on SIGQUIT. With `handle_quit` removed, it stays up on both versions.
  - `RustServerSigtermDrain` plus `SubprocessWatchdog` with one crashed and one wedged scheduler: `wait()` returns after the time limit, with the crash reported. On the previous code it stays blocked.
  - The `run_scheduler_process` crash path: the updated test passes, and fails on the pre-change scheduler.
- `pre-commit` passes on the changed files.
- The new pytest cases themselves were not run locally (no torch environment). CI should run them.

Not covered here:
- The Granian multi-worker path (`--enable-http2` with more than one worker) owns its own signal handling and may need the same check.
- `/health_generate` still does not check whether the schedulers are alive.

title: [Fix] ernie55: Import FlashMLA from the sgl-flash-mla wheel
author: Fridge003
body:
## Motivation

#48789 removed the vendored FlashMLA build and wrappers from sgl-kernel, but the ERNIE 5.5 MLA backend still imports `flash_mla_with_kvcache` and `get_mla_metadata` from `sgl_kernel.flash_mla`, so its packed-fp8 FlashMLA path raises `ModuleNotFoundError` on CUDA.

## Modifications

Import both from `sglang.kernels.ops.attention.flash_mla_interface`, which wraps the `sgl-flash-mla` wheel behind the old sgl-kernel signatures (`use_legacy=True` by default, `get_mla_metadata()` with no args returns `(FlashMLASchedMeta, None)`), so the call sites are unchanged.

A scan of `python/`, `test/` and `benchmark/` found no other CUDA path importing FlashMLA from sgl-kernel. The remaining `sgl_kernel` flash_mla imports in `deepseek_v4_backend.py`, `dsa_backend.py` and `xpu_backend.py` are XPU-only branches that use sgl-kernel-xpu's own ops, and are left as is.

title: [Fix] logprobs: Bound top_logprobs to [0,vocab_size]
author: Kh4L
body:
## Motivation

`top_logprobs_num` (`/generate`), `logprobs` (`/v1/completions`) and `top_logprobs` (`/v1/chat/completions`) have no bound. The value feeds `logprobs.topk(k)` over `[*, vocab_size]` in the scheduler, so a single request with `k > vocab_size` (e.g. `top_logprobs=1000000`) raises `selected index k out of range` and takes the server down. Negative values are accepted with HTTP 200. Reported as item 1 of #31597.

## Modifications

- `TokenizerManager._validate_one_request` rejects `top_logprobs_num` outside `[0, vocab_size]`. This covers every entrypoint.
- The OpenAI chat and completions request validation applies the same bound, so streaming requests get a 400 before the stream starts.
- Unit tests for both layers. They fail without this change.

The approach follows #31567 by @v-code01, which was closed as idle; this is that change rebased onto current main, with the OpenAI-layer check added.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A. Requests that were valid before behave the same.

GPU check (1x GB300, `nvidia/Cosmos-Reason1-7B`, TP1, vocab 152064), main 6d143e51b2 with this PR and the `n` bound PR:
- Before: chat `top_logprobs=1000000` drops the connection, the scheduler logs `RuntimeError: selected index k out of range`, and the server is gone (`/health` unreachable).
- After: `top_logprobs` 1000000 / -1 / -7 (chat, also with `stream=true`), `logprobs` 1000000 / -1 (completions) and `top_logprobs_num` 1000000 / -1 (`/generate`) all return 400 in ~10 ms, e.g. `top_logprobs must be in [0, 152064], got 1000000.`. `/health` stays 200 after each request.
- Controls still return 200: chat `top_logprobs=20`, completions `logprobs=5`, `/generate` `top_logprobs_num=20`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A

title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] jit: Build sm_107a on CC 10.7, keeping sm_100f only for modules that use CUTLASS
author: trevor-m
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #49385.

#45911 builds every JIT module for the `sm_100f` family target on CC 10.7 (Vera Rubin) while FlashInfer's bundled CUTLASS has no `Sm107`. That fallback exists because of DeepSelect: built for `sm_107a` against that CUTLASS, its CuTe TMA copies compile out and assert at run time, and `setmaxnreg` is dropped. DeepSelect is the only CUTLASS user that runs on CC 10.7. The other modules that include CUTLASS are sm90-only (sparse MLA q8kv8 prefill, qprep), sm120-only (fp8 blockwise scaled-mm, the sm120 skinny GEMM), or refuse CC 10.7 (convrot int8).

Because the fallback applies to every module, all of them lose the arch-specific target. One consequence: ptxas caps static shared memory at 48 KB for family targets, and the DeepSeek-V4 top-k v2 cluster kernels (#47960, #48501) use 49-56 KB. Those kernels were built and tested for `sm_90a` and `sm_103a`, where the limit doesn't apply. On Vera Rubin the whole `dpsk_v4_topk_v2` module fails to build, and every DeepSeek-V4.1 server dies at its first warmup. With nvcc 13.4 the same source builds for `sm_90a`, `sm_100a`, `sm_103a` and `sm_107a`, and only `sm_100f` rejects it (`topk_candidates_cluster_kernel<true, 4>`: 51,584 bytes).

## Modifications

- `arch.MODULE_USES_CUTLASS = ["deep_select_topk"]`. On CC 10.7, `get_compile_arch(kernel_name)` applies #45911's `sm_100f` fallback only to these modules. Every other module builds `sm_107a`, as before #45911. The fallback still lifts on its own once `cutlass_supports_sm107()`.
- `load_jit` and the ninja `-gencode` (`toolchain.target_flags`) pass the module name, so a module's binary and its `-DSGL_CUDA_ARCH` agree. `sgl_kernel/utils.cuh` asserts that they do. The build key hashes the ninja file, so the target is part of the key.
- No kernel source changes. Of the `SGL_CUDA_ARCH` checks that 1070 could change, the only one is convrot int8's (900/1000/1200/1210), and that module refuses CC 10.7.

A new CUTLASS kernel that runs on CC 10.7 has to join `MODULE_USES_CUTLASS` until FlashInfer bundles CUTLASS >= 4.8, which declares `struct Sm107`. If it doesn't, its first launch hits #45911's TMA assert.

## Tests

- `test_jit_arch.py` (new, CPU): on CC 10.7, `deep_select_topk` gets `sm_100f` and any other module gets `sm_107a`; once CUTLASS supports SM107, everything gets `sm_107a`. `test_jit_cache.py` still passes.
- Vera Rubin (4 x VR NVL72, CC 10.7, driver 620.69), `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-cu134-20261109-e60f7e9` with this branch, sgl-deep-gemm 0.2.7, sgl-flash-mla 1.0.4:
  - `test_topk_v2.py`: 402 passed, 14 skipped. On main the module does not build. `test_dsa_dcp_topk_merge.py` needs 8 GPUs and skips at 4.
  - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 aggregated (MegaMoE, DSpark block 3, EPLB), GSM8K all 1319: 0.909, invalid 0.001, 0 errors.
  - Targets: `get_compile_arch("dpsk_v4_topk_v2")` is `10.7a` and `get_compile_arch("deep_select_topk")` is `10.0f`. The server builds DeepSelect in this configuration too (12 variants), so the `sm_100f` path is exercised. Keeping `-DSGL_CUDA_ARCH` in step matters there: a variant that passed only the `-gencode` fails `utils.cuh`'s arch assert when DeepSelect builds.

With the current pin (sgl-amd-mono e52803f9), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with DSpark and `--enable-amd-monokernel` does not run on current SGLang. #45406 and #48298 changed what SGLang reads from the draft sampler entry and how `begin_simulated_step` seeds the bonus token, and the pinned plugin predates both.

## Modifications

- Pin sgl-amd-mono at 7113024f (`python/pyproject_other.toml`), which includes sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono#118. The ROCm image checks out the same pin, so no Dockerfile change is needed.

title: [Fix] dspark: Write deferred draft KV only for carried requests
author: hnyls2002
body:
- **DSpark deferred draft KV store** (`SGLANG_DSPARK_DEFER_CONTEXT_KV`): before the draft forward writes the staged store, the host zeroes the commit length of each staged row whose request the draft does not carry (finished or aborted since the verify) or that was retracted since (`retraction_count` changed). A step then writes only into pages its own requests still hold, so a request's pages are free to reuse once the last step that carries it is processed.
- The prefill no longer flushes a pending staging: every row written later belongs to a request that held its pages throughout. `flush` becomes private, the static verify notes its staged requests in one call from the worker (`note_staged(reqs)`, replacing the batch size forwarded through the verify epilogue), and the module contract says the above.
- `DeferredContextCommit` is renamed `DeferredDraftKVStore` (module `dspark_deferred_draft_kv.py`): what it defers is the store of the committed tokens' draft KV. `commit_lens` and the env var keep their names.
- The store sets itself up: `maybe_build_deferred_draft_kv` (eligibility, the refusal log, the target's logits hook) and `attach_draft` (the draft graph hooks) move from the worker into its module, the worker keeps the store in one field, and the draft forward makes one store call (`after_draft_forward` folds into `before_draft_forward`).
- Tests: `test_dspark_deferred_draft_kv.py` covers rows left out of the draft batch and a request retracted and readmitted.

No behavior change with the switch off. With it on, a finished request's last staged draft KV is no longer written; outputs are unchanged, and when those pages are reused from the prefix cache the draft may accept slightly less on at most `stride` tokens (paged SWA drafts only).

Verification: the DSpark unit tests pass locally, and `test_dspark_deferred_draft_kv.py` turns red if the filter drops the retraction check or matches rows by position, or if the graph-written staging stays pending, and [`/rerun-test`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/49436#issuecomment-6759195394) runs them on GPU with `test_basic_sanity_dspark.py` and `test_dspark_draft_graph.py`. No CI test enables the store: it needs a DeepSeek V4.1 target with an MoE draft and a static verify.

title: [Fix] diffusion/qwen-image-edit: Run n > 1 edit outputs one by one
author: Smallfu666
body:
## Motivation

On a default `sglang serve --model-path Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511` server, our edit request with `n=2` returns HTTP 500, while the same request with `n=1` works. A request of the same shape:

```bash
python -c "from PIL import Image; Image.new('RGB', (1024, 1024), (200, 30, 30)).save('in.png')"
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/images/edits \
  -F prompt="Make the cube blue and keep everything else the same." -F image=@in.png \
  -F size=1024x1024 -F seed=0 -F n=2 -F response_format=b64_json
```

```
File ".../configs/pipeline_configs/qwen_image.py", line 573, in postprocess_image_latent
    image_latents = latent_condition.repeat(
RuntimeError: Number of dimensions of repeat dims can not be smaller than number of dimensions of tensor
```

The request's `n` outputs run as one batch, and the edit image latent is 5-D while `postprocess_image_latent` repeats it with four dims:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/a4b880119793c14c5b210c12655b54f612d28f90/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/configs/pipeline_configs/qwen_image.py#L567-L579

The edit `_prepare_edit_cond_kwargs` methods also require a batch size of 1 ([Edit](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/a4b880119793c14c5b210c12655b54f612d28f90/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/configs/pipeline_configs/qwen_image.py#L496-L497), [Edit-Plus](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/a4b880119793c14c5b210c12655b54f612d28f90/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/configs/pipeline_configs/qwen_image.py#L693-L694)). In our test, fixing the repeat and removing those asserts returned two images, but the second was a flat image, so this PR does not batch the edit path.

## Modifications

- `QwenImageEditPipelineConfig.supports_sequential_multi_output_inference()` returns True (as SANA-Video 2 does), so a request's `n` outputs run one after another through the single-sample path, with seeds `seed`, `seed + 1`, ... Edit-Plus (2509 / 2511) inherits it. Qwen-Image text-to-image and Qwen-Image-Layered keep batched outputs; Layered's first stage does not split the request.
- `test_qwen_image_edit_multi_output.py`: `InputValidationStage.iter_sequential_requests` with the real configs splits an `n=2` edit request into two single-output requests with seeds 0 and 1 (fails on main), and leaves Qwen-Image T2I and Qwen-Image-Layered as one request.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= SGLANG_DIFFUSION_PLATFORM_OVERRIDE=cpu python -m pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_qwen_image_edit_multi_output.py
```

## Accuracy Tests

Qwen-Image-Edit-2511, one H200, `--warmup-mode off` and otherwise default flags; one 1024x1024 input, one edit prompt, `size` 1024x1024; decoded PNGs compared pixel by pixel:

| request | main | this change |
|---|---|---|
| `n=1`, seed 0 | 1 image | 1 image, identical to main |
| `n=2`, seed 0 | HTTP 500 | 2 images: identical to `n=1` with seed 0 and with seed 1 |

Not run: `n` > 2, Qwen-Image-Edit-2509, the original Qwen-Image-Edit, Qwen-Image-Layered, several input images, multi-GPU, and speed profiling.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

An `n=2` edit now costs two single-sample runs; it failed before.

title: [Fix] diffusion/flux2: Size edit outputs from an input image that needs no resize
author: Smallfu666
body:
## Motivation

With FLUX.2 (`black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-4B`, `FLUX.2-dev`), an image edit without `size` returns a 1024x1024 image when the input is already a multiple of 16 and at most 1 MP, but follows the input when it is not. On a default `sglang serve --model-path black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-4B` server, `/v1/images/edits` with no `size`:

| input image | output on main | output with this change |
|---|---|---|
| 768x1344 | 1024x1024 | 768x1344 |
| 770x1344 | 768x1344 | 768x1344 |

`InputValidationStage.preprocess_condition_image` only sets the output size when `prepare_calculated_size` returns one ([input_validation.py](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/a4b880119793c14c5b210c12655b54f612d28f90/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/input_validation.py#L222-L240)), and for FLUX.2 that returns `None` when the image needs no resize ([flux.py](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/a4b880119793c14c5b210c12655b54f612d28f90/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/configs/pipeline_configs/flux.py#L583-L604)), so the sampling default wins. diffusers `Flux2Pipeline` takes the size from the input in both cases ([pipeline_flux2.py](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/v0.37.0/src/diffusers/pipelines/flux2/pipeline_flux2.py#L885-L905)).

## Modifications

- `Flux2PipelineConfig.prepare_calculated_size` falls back to the image's own size when no resize is needed. FLUX.2-klein and the fine-tuned FLUX.2 configs inherit it. An explicit `size` is unchanged.
- `test_input_validation.py`: `TestFlux2EditOutputSize` runs `preprocess_condition_image` with the real `Flux2PipelineConfig`; the aligned case fails on main (`(1024, 1024)`) and passes with this change.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= SGLANG_DIFFUSION_PLATFORM_OVERRIDE=cpu python -m pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_input_validation.py -k Flux2EditOutputSize
```

## Accuracy Tests

The table above: FLUX.2-klein-4B on one H200, `--warmup-mode off` and otherwise default flags, one edit prompt, seed 0. Only the output size was checked. Not run: FLUX.2-dev, multi-image edits, and image quality.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable (output size only).

title: [Fix] openai: Reject assistant tool calls without a function name (HTTP 500 -> 400)
author: nvpohanh
body:
[by Claude Code]

Original authors: @nvpohanh

## Motivation

A chat request can carry a conversation history in which an assistant tool call has no function name. For example:

```json
{"role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_1", "type": "function", "function": {"arguments": "{}"}}]}
```

Request validation accepts this. A chat encoder that looks the name up then fails while it renders the prompt, and the server answers **HTTP 500** instead of rejecting the malformed request with **HTTP 400**. Main has such lookups, for example `tool_call["function"]["name"]` in `encoding_dsv32.py`.

We hit this with Kimi-K3.1, whose chat encoder raises `KeyError: 'name'`. A vendor tool-call verification suite has a case that sends a malformed assistant tool call in the history and expects HTTP 400; all three of its requests got HTTP 500.

Nothing enforces the name on request messages today:
- `FunctionResponse.name` is optional on purpose, because streaming continuation chunks carry no name.
- `ToolCall` is shared by the response models and the request message model.

The OpenAI API also requires `function.name` on an assistant tool call (`ChatCompletionMessageToolCallParam`).

Developed as radixark/sglang-k31#218.

## Modifications

- `ChatCompletionMessageGenericParam` (`entrypoints/openai/protocol.py`) gets an after-validator: in an assistant message, every `tool_calls[i].function.name` must be a non-empty string.
  - It runs when the request body is parsed, before the chat template is rendered.
  - A failure goes through the existing `RequestValidationError` handler, so the client gets HTTP 400 with `tool_calls[i]: 'function.name' is required`.
- The response and streaming models are unchanged. Assistant tool calls with a name, tool messages, and requests without tool calls are unaffected.
- **Behavior change:** a request with a nameless or empty-name assistant tool call now gets HTTP 400 for every model, including models whose chat template would have rendered it.
- New unit test `TestAssistantToolCallNames` (`test_protocol.py`): a named call is accepted; missing, `null` and empty names are rejected.

## Accuracy Tests

Measured on the Kimi-K3.1 branch: Kimi-K3.1 (NVFP4) served with `python -m sglang.launch_server`, the `kimi_k3` tool-call and reasoning parsers, TP8 + DCP8 on GB300, and DFLASH speculative decoding.

| check | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| verifier case: malformed assistant tool call in the history (3 requests without `function.name`), expects HTTP 400 | 3 x HTTP 500, `KeyError: 'name'` in the encoder | **3 x HTTP 400, pass** |
| verifier K3 feature suite (118 items) | 66 pass / 50 skip / 2 fail | 67 pass / 50 skip / 1 fail |

The remaining feature-suite failure is a known-flaky check that fails with and without this change.

Model outputs are unaffected: the change only rejects requests that carry a nameless assistant tool call, and well-formed requests take the same path as before.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The change adds one Pydantic validator that runs only on assistant messages with tool calls.

## Tests

Run in `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13`, with the tree under test first on `PYTHONPATH`:

| | this branch | main |
|---|---|---|
| `test_protocol.py` + `test_serving_chat.py` | 217 passed, 344 subtests | 215 passed, 341 subtests |
| `TestAssistantToolCallNames` | 2 passed | 3 subtests fail (missing / `null` / empty name accepted) |

`pre-commit run --all-files` is clean.

title: [Fix] dsv4/topk_v2: Move the cluster kernels' top-k buffer to dynamic shared memory
author: akhilg-nv
body:
[by Claude Code]

## Motivation

`topk_v2.cuh` is the JIT-compiled top-k behind `sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsv4.topk`: the top-k of the DeepSeek-V4 sparse-attention indexer, also used by the GLM k-pool indexer (`topk_transform_kpool_v2`). On some toolkit and target combinations ptxas rejects the whole module, so the first call into it (for example `plan_topk_v2()`) raises. The cause is two cluster kernels, `topk_small_batch_cluster_kernel` and `topk_candidates_cluster_kernel`. Each declares two static shared-memory buffers: `impl::TopKCluster<C>::Smem`, the cluster selection's scratch (41.6 to 47.2 KiB for cluster size C = 2 to 16), and `int32_t s_topk_indices[kMaxTopK]`, an 8 KiB buffer that stages the selected indices. Together that is 49.6 to 55.2 KiB per block, above the 48 KiB static limit. The CUDA Programming Guide says: "Kernels relying on shared memory allocations over 48 KB per block must use dynamic shared memory and require an explicit opt-in". In our checks ptxas enforces the limit:

- with CUDA 12.9, for `sm_90a`, `sm_100a` and `sm_100f`;
- with CUDA 13.0, 13.4 and 13.5, for `sm_100f` only; these accept `sm_90a` and `sm_100a`.

#49385 reported this failure on CC 10.7 devices, where `arch.py` built every JIT module for `sm_100f` when FlashInfer's CUTLASS lacked sm107. #49420 (merged) closed it by building `sm_107a` there for modules that do not use CUTLASS. This PR fixes the kernels themselves, so the module also builds where target selection does not help: CUDA 12.9 for `sm_90a` / `sm_100a`, and family targets such as `sm_100f`.

This PR moves `s_topk_indices` to dynamic shared memory in those two kernels and launches them with 8 KiB of dynamic shared memory, so their static part is `TopKCluster<C>::Smem` alone. The selection code is unchanged. On B200, the PR selects the same index sets as main in all 52 cases we compared. They cover every output mode that reads the moved buffer: the small-batch kernel's page-table, dual-output and k-pool modes at both cluster sizes it uses on B200 (16 and 8), and the candidates kernel at cluster sizes 2 and 4. The order of the output slots varies from run to run on main as well, so the outputs are not bitwise comparable.

The 16 KiB `TieValue members[kMaxNumTie]` array that brought `TopKCluster<C>::Smem` close to the limit came with the exact cluster path in #47960; `topk_candidates_cluster_kernel` came with #48501.

Related: #49385, #49420.

**Impact**
- **Accuracy:** `test_topk_v2.py` on B200 (CUDA 13.0): 402 passed, 14 skipped (ROCm-only), 0 failed, the same as main. With the build forced to `sm_100f` on the same B200, main fails to build (8 ptxas "uses too much shared data" errors) and this PR passes the same 402 tests. The selected index sets equal main's in 52 of 52 cases, and in the 48 small-batch cases every row of both also matches `torch.topk`.
- **Performance:** B200 microbenchmark, 16 shapes: no shape is slower than main beyond the spread between processes. 8 of the 12 page-table, dual-output and k-pool shapes are 0.3% to 3.8% faster, with non-overlapping ranges; we did not identify why. The other shapes, including the index-only mode and the candidates kernel, are unchanged.
- **End to end (estimate, not measured):** no slowdown expected. The edited kernels are no slower than main on any measured shape, nothing else changes, and the largest gain is 0.47 us per call.

## Modifications

**+36 / -9 runtime code (1 file), no test changes.** Kernel changes: one buffer moves from static to dynamic shared memory in two existing kernels; no new kernels.

- `topk_small_batch_cluster_kernel` and `topk_candidates_cluster_kernel`: `s_topk_indices` is now a view of `extern __shared__ __align__(16) int32_t s_topk_dyn[]` (`python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/deepseek_v4/topk_v2.cuh`). `ptxas -v` reports 0xa650 / 0xa980 / 0xafe0 / 0xbca0 bytes of static shared memory for C = 2 / 4 / 8 / 16, where main has 0xc650 / 0xc980 / 0xcfe0 / 0xdca0.
- Each launch of those kernels (C16 and C8 small-batch, C2 and C4 candidates) passes `kMaxTopK * sizeof(int32_t)` bytes (8 KiB) of dynamic shared memory. Each also sets `cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize` once per device through `runtime::init_per_device`, like the existing C16 cluster-size attribute. For these instances, static plus dynamic shared memory per block is the same as on main.
- The small-batch kernel's two index-only instances (no page table) never use the buffer and were never over the limit. They now also launch with the 8 KiB of dynamic shared memory, so their per-block total grows by 8 KiB (static 48,288 / 45,024 B, unchanged); their `ptxas -v` statistics are unchanged.
- `device::enable_smem_spilling()` is removed from these two kernels: the PTX ISA does not allow the `enable_smem_spilling` pragma in a kernel that uses dynamically allocated shared memory. The helper emits the pragma only when built with CUDA 13 or later. `ptxas -v` for the eight instances that exceeded the limit:
  - CUDA 13.4 at `sm_90a`, `sm_100a` and `sm_100f`: the same register counts before and after the change. Spill-store bytes are also unchanged at `sm_100a` and `sm_100f`. At `sm_90a`, one instance (k-pool, C8) goes from 86 to 74 bytes.
  - CUDA 13.0 at `sm_100a`, with this B200's occupancy-probe values (the toolkit of the GPU runs below): the same register counts (64 for C16; 32 for C8 and for the candidates instances). The C16 and candidates instances spill the same as before. The three C8 small-batch instances (page-table, dual-output, k-pool) spill 4 bytes stored and 32 loaded, where main spills 8 and 2 (page-table) or nothing (dual-output, k-pool).
- Remaining headroom: the C16 static footprint is now 0xbca0 = 48,288 bytes, 864 bytes below the 0xc000 limit. If `TopKCluster<16>::Smem` grows by more than 864 bytes, the build fails again with CUDA 12.9 and on family targets; CUDA 13 `sm_90a` / `sm_100a` builds would not show it.
- Synchronization is unchanged. In k-pool mode, every rank of a small-batch cluster still writes its selected pools into rank 0's buffer through `cluster.map_shared_rank(s_topk_indices, 0)`, and rank 0 reads them after `cluster.sync()`. With a dynamic buffer, `map_shared_rank` still addresses rank 0's buffer, because every block of a launch has the same shared-memory layout. The k-pool check under Accuracy Tests exercises this path.
- Possible follow-up, not done here so that the tested code is what ships: `runtime::set_max_dynamic_smem_per_device<kernel>()` (`runtime.cuh`) could replace the three hand-written `cudaFuncSetAttribute` blocks, with the 8 KiB size as one named constant.

## Accuracy Tests

`test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_topk_v2.py` on one B200, CUDA 13.0.88, torch 2.14.1+cu130. The PR is commit 24b2d27f5a on main 1be97a0a63. `topk_v2.cuh`, `test_topk_v2.py` and the dsv4 `topk.py` are unchanged on current main; #49420 changed only target selection on CC 10.7. On this GPU the occupancy probes enable both small-batch cluster sizes: C16 for batches of up to 7 rows and C8 for 8 to 33 rows. So all eight instances that exceeded the limit are built and run (the k-pool ones through the standalone file below).

| JIT build | main (1be97a0a63) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `sm_100a` (the default on B200) | 402 passed, 14 skipped | 402 passed, 14 skipped |
| `sm_100f` (forced) | fails to build: 8 ptxas "uses too much shared data" errors, one per instance that exceeded the limit (0xc650, 0xc980, 3 x 0xcfe0, 3 x 0xdca0) | 402 passed, 14 skipped |

- The 14 skips are ROCm-only cases.
- **Forced `sm_100f`.** A pytest plugin replaced `get_compile_arch()` with `CompileArch(10, 0, "f")`, the target `arch.py` picked on CC 10.7 before #49420; it still picks it there for modules that use CUTLASS. The plugin is not part of this PR. It applies to the test process only. The two `test_topk_v2_modes` cases check modes 0 and 2 in subprocesses, and those built for `sm_100a`.
- **Same selections as main.** The PR and main ran on the same inputs on the same B200. For each row we compared the selected entries as a multiset, `-1` padding included:

  | Kernel, output mode | Shapes (rows x row length) | Equal to main |
  |---|---|---|
  | small-batch, page-table | C16: 1 x 65537, 4 x 131072, 7 rows of mixed lengths from 300 to 262144; C8: 8 x 98304, 20 mixed from 300 to 262144, 33 x 131072; k = 512 and 2048 | 12 / 12 |
  | small-batch, dual-output (page-table and raw outputs) | the same 12 | 12 / 12 |
  | small-batch, k-pool (pool size 4; pool counts per row) | C16: 1 x 32768, 4 x 65536, 7 mixed from 100 to 131072; C8: 8 x 32768, 20 mixed from 100 to 131072, 33 x 65536; pool-level k = 512 and 2048; page table with tail tokens, or offsets | 24 / 24 |
  | candidates, C2 and C4 | 10 rows, 0 to 65536, k = 2048, random and tied scores | 4 / 4 |

  - A mixed-length batch puts trivial rows, single-block rows and cluster rows in one launch. The single-block and cluster rows stage their selection in the moved buffer; trivial rows (length <= k) write their output directly.
  - In the 48 small-batch cases, every row of both trees also matches the `torch.topk` reference (for k-pool, the expansion of the `torch.topk` pools). No row had a tie at the k-th value.
  - The PR built for `sm_100f` (forced, as above) also matches main in 52 of 52 cases.
  - The output slot order is not bitwise reproducible: two runs of main differ bitwise in 52 of 52 cases, while their sets match.
- **K-pool check (not added to this PR).** `test_topk_v2.py` has no k-pool case, and the k-pool tests we found reach this module only through its ragged entry point, with 1024 pools per row, so they never launch the small-batch cluster kernel. A standalone pytest file runs 6 of the k-pool shapes above (one variant each). It compares the output with `torch.topk` over distinct pool scores, expanded per the `transform_kpool` contract, with tolerance 0: pooled columns as a multiset, tail columns by position. Scores past each row's pool count are larger than every valid score, so reading past the count would change the result. It passes on main and on this PR (`sm_100a` and forced `sm_100f`). It can go into `test_topk_v2.py` if wanted.
- **The tests reach the edited code.** We ran two mutants of this PR, with each case in its own process:
  - All three edited launches pass 4 bytes of dynamic shared memory instead of 8 KiB. `test_topk_v2_cluster_refine_page_outputs` (small-batch kernel) and `test_topk_v2_candidates_cluster_matches_one_block` (candidates kernel) fail with an illegal memory access. All 6 k-pool cases fail with a CUDA error at run time (5 illegal memory accesses, 1 unspecified launch failure).
  - The k-pool ranks write into rank 1's buffer instead of rank 0's. All 6 k-pool cases fail the selected-set check. Only k-pool rows above the cluster floor take this branch, so every k-pool case reaches it, at both cluster sizes.
- **Compile only, no GPU.** With this change, the module builds:
  - with CUDA 12.9 for `sm_90a`, `sm_100a` and `sm_100f`;
  - with CUDA 13.0 for `sm_100f`;
  - with CUDA 13.4 for `sm_90a`, `sm_100a` and `sm_100f`.

  Toolkits checked with this change: CUDA 12.9.86, 13.0.88 and 13.4.92. CUDA 13.5.37 was checked on main only, where it fails for `sm_100f`. Other toolkits were not checked.

Reproduce the build failure (compile only, no GPU). Run this from the repo root with CUDA 12.9's `nvcc` on `PATH` and `apache-tvm-ffi` installed:

```bash
printf '#include "deepseek_v4/topk_v2.cuh"\ntemplate struct sglang::TopKKernel<true>;\n' > /tmp/topk_v2_repro.cu
J=python/sglang/kernels/jit
TVM_INC=$(python -c 'import tvm_ffi.libinfo as l; print(l.find_include_path())')
nvcc -cubin -o /tmp/topk_v2_repro.cubin -std=c++20 -O3 --expt-relaxed-constexpr \
  -DSGL_CUDA_ARCH=1000 -DSGL_TOPK_MODE=1 -gencode=arch=compute_100a,code=sm_100a \
  -I"$J/include" -I"$J/csrc" -I"$TVM_INC" /tmp/topk_v2_repro.cu
# On main: 5 ptxas errors "uses too much shared data (0x... bytes, 0xc000 max)". With this PR: builds.
# Same result with -DSGL_CUDA_ARCH=900 and compute_90a / sm_90a.
# With CUDA 13.x, use compute_100f / sm_100f.
```

The first error from CUDA 12.9 at `sm_100a`, verbatim:

```
ptxas error   : Entry function '_ZN6sglang11topk_mode_130topk_candidates_cluster_kernelILb1ELj2EEEvNS0_20TopKCandidatesParamsEj' uses too much shared data (0xc650 bytes, 0xc000 max)
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This is a microbenchmark of the small-batch kernel in each output mode and of the candidates kernel, on one B200 (CUDA 13.0, default `sm_100a` build).

- **Method.** `marker.do_bench` in CUDA-graph mode with `replay_iters=200`, copying only the scores. It makes 20 warm-up calls, then captures one graph of at least 100 calls (`loop_count`) that rotate over up to 100 score copies. It replays the graph `max(replay_iters // loop_count, 10)` = 10 times, with an L2 flush before each replay, and records each replay's time per call. The per-process value is the median of those 10. Each score copy is read once per replay, after the flush; what a replay reuses are the inputs that are not copied (page table, lengths, plan metadata) and the outputs.
- Each process measured one tree. There were 8 processes in the order PR, main, main, PR, main, PR, PR, main. The table gives the mean of the per-process medians in microseconds, with the min-max range across the 4 processes of each tree.

| Kernel, output mode (cluster size on B200) | Shape | main | this PR | PR vs main |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| small-batch, index-only (C16) | 1 x 65540, k = 2048 | 5.089 [5.079-5.099] | 5.094 [5.079-5.100] | +0.11% |
| small-batch, index-only (C8) | 30 x 131072, k = 2048 | 10.898 [10.892-10.907] | 10.896 [10.892-10.907] | -0.02% |

| small-batch, k-pool, page table + tail (C16) | 1 x 32768 pools, pool k = 512 | 5.448 [5.448-5.448] | 5.432 [5.426-5.448] | -0.29% |

- A second run on the same GPU (12 processes, three trees interleaved) reproduced every PR-vs-main difference within 0.25 points, except the noisy 8 x 65536 k-pool shape (-0.07% there).
- **Why the page-table, dual-output and k-pool modes got faster: not identified.** The dropped pragma is not the cause. In that second run, main with only the two `enable_smem_spilling()` calls removed timed like main: every shape was within 0.11% of main, except three k-pool shapes whose differences (-0.31%, -0.44% and +0.63%) are smaller than main's own spread between processes there (0.32%, 2.9% and 3.0%). Its `ptxas -v` statistics also equal main's. So the difference comes with the dynamic buffer itself.
- The timing was not repeated with CUDA 12.9 or with an `sm_100f` build, because main does not build there.
- No end-to-end run. The edited kernels are no slower than main, so we expect no end-to-end slowdown.
