title: [Fix] GLM-4.7-Flash: Load compressed-tensors W4A16 checkpoints
author: koladefaj
body:
## Motivation Fixes #49369, reported by @HollowMan6. `cyankiwi/GLM-4.7-Flash-AWQ-4bit` (compressed-tensors `pack-quantized`, int4 symmetric, group 32) does not load. It quantizes `q_a_proj`, `kv_a_proj_with_mqa` and `kv_b_proj` from layer 1 on, and keeps layer 0 and the shared experts in BF16 through its `ignore` list. On a real `sglang serve`, it fails in five places, one after the other. Each one only shows up once the one before it is fixed: ```diff sglang serve cyankiwi/GLM-4.7-Flash-AWQ-4bit build model # (3) layer 0 + shared-expert gate_up_proj built W4A16; (4) BF16 shared expert fused into W4A16 MoE load_weights - fuse q_a + kv_a # (1) weight_shape -> [4] -> AssertionError + fuse q_a + kv_a # weight_shape -> [q_out + kv_out, in] post_load_weights - kv_b_proj.weight # (2) AttributeError + dequantize kv_b_proj -> w_kc / w_vc process_weights_after_loading # Marlin repack capture CUDA graphs - fused_a_gemm_weight_eligible(layer.weight) # (5) AttributeError + packed layer -> regular path serve ``` 1. **Fused QKV-A `weight_shape`.** `load_weights` fuses `q_a_proj` and `kv_a_proj_with_mqa` by concatenating every tensor of the pair on dim 0. For `weight_shape` (`[out, in]`), that gives `[q_out, in, kv_out, in]` instead of `[q_out + kv_out, in]`, and the load asserts. `DeepseekV2WeightLoaderMixin` has the same concatenation. 2. **`kv_b_proj` in `post_load_weights`.** The MLA post-load step reads `kv_b_proj.weight`, which a packed layer does not have. This is the issue's `AttributeError`. 3. **Empty `packed_modules_mapping`.** `Glm4MoeLiteForCausalLM` declares none, so `ignore` entries that name shards (`q_a_proj`, `gate_proj`, ...) never match the fused `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` and `gate_up_proj`. Layer 0 and the shared experts' `gate_up_proj` get built W4A16 over BF16 weights. With FP8 this fails silently: @HollowMan6 measured 3.4e38 outputs on `unsloth/GLM-4.7-Flash-FP8-Dynamic`, where 13.0 is expected. 4. **Shared-expert fusion.** On CUDA SM80+, GLM fuses the shared expert into the routed `FusedMoE`, but this checkpoint keeps the shared experts in BF16 beside W4A16 routed experts. 5. **Fused-A GEMM eligibility.** `fused_a_gemm_weight_eligible` reads `layer.weight` on the packed `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` during the first forward (CUDA graph capture). ## Modifications - `models/deepseek_common/utils.py`: a new `fuse_qkv_a_proj_tensors`, used by both the GLM and DeepSeek loaders. - `weight_shape` adds the output rows. - A shared act-order `weight_g_idx` is kept, and differing ones are rejected. - A pair of 0-d scales is shared, as before. - Only AWQ/GPTQ-packed tensors (`qweight`, `qzeros`, `scales` under `awq`, `awq_marlin`, `moe_wna16`, `gptq`, `gptq_marlin` or `auto-round`) stack on dim 1. A projection that such a checkpoint leaves unconverted keeps a plain `[out, in]` weight. `QuantTrio/GLM-4.7-Flash-AWQ` keeps `self_attn` in BF16, so choosing the dim from the config alone would break it. GGUF also names a tensor `qweight`, but it is row-major and stays on dim 0. - GPTQ's `g_idx` follows the same rule as `weight_g_idx`. - `compressed_tensors_wNa16.py`: `CompressedTensorsWNA16.dequantize_weight` unpacks the checkpoint layout to a dense weight in the scale dtype. - It supports symmetric quantization without act order. - The kernel repack marks the layer, and dequantizing a repacked layer raises. Sharded-state and remote-instance loaders copy kernel-layout tensors and then call `post_load_weights`. Reading those tensors would build garbage `w_kc`/`w_vc`. - `deepseek_weight_loader.py`: `post_load_weights` dequantizes a compressed-tensors WNA16 `kv_b_proj` before the `w_kc`/`w_vc` split, next to the AWQ branch. It also sets `_derived_weight_cache_error` on that layer: once repacked it cannot be dequantized again, so online weight updates are refused before they write any weight. - `glm4_moe_lite.py`: - `packed_modules_mapping` maps `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` and `gate_up_proj` to their shards. - The shared-expert fusion gate checks `quant_blocks_shared_experts_fusion`, as DeepSeek-V2 already does. - The loader pops cached QKV-A tensors even when the fused param is absent. - `compressed_tensors.py`: `CompressedTensorsConfig.can_fuse_shared_expert` is false when `ignore` gives any shared-expert projection (`gate_proj`, `up_proj`, `down_proj`) of a layer a different precision from the same routed-expert projection, in either direction. Each projection is resolved per MoE layer with `should_ignore_layer`, so names and regexes match alike. A `shared_expert_gate` entry does not count. It probes the layers the ignore list names; a regex, or a bare suffix that could match an expert, adds `model.layers.0-255`. That takes 1.3 ms on the FP8 checkpoint's 601-entry list. - `fused_a_gemm.py`: a layer without a dense `weight` is not eligible. **Behavior change outside GLM:** `can_fuse_shared_expert` is also read by DeepSeek-V2/V4, MiniMax-M3 and Qwen2-MoE / Qwen3.5. For a compressed-tensors checkpoint whose `ignore` keeps any shared-expert projection at a different precision from the matching routed-expert projection, these now skip shared-expert fusion. Fusing such a checkpoint would load BF16 weights into the quantized expert buffers, or quantized weights into BF16 ones. A checkpoint that ignores the same projections on both sides keeps fusion. ## Accuracy Tests 1x NVIDIA A40 (SM86) for the `cyankiwi` row and 1x NVIDIA RTX A6000 (SM86) for the `QuantTrio` row, image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261110-4a5c6b8f`. Every file this PR touches is identical between the image's tree and this PR's base `533c067689`. "main" is that tree unchanged, and "branch" is this PR applied to it. The launch command follows the cookbook (`--tp 1 --reasoning-parser glm45`): ``` sglang serve --model-path --tp 1 --reasoning-parser glm45 --port 30000 sgl-eval run gsm8k --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 --num-examples 200 \ --num-threads 64 --max-tokens 4096 --chat-template-kwarg enable_thinking=false ``` | Checkpoint | main | branch | |---|---|---| | `cyankiwi/GLM-4.7-Flash-AWQ-4bit` (this issue) | fails to load | GSM8K **0.850** (1/200 truncated) | | `QuantTrio/GLM-4.7-Flash-AWQ` (regression check) | GSM8K **0.910** (2/200 truncated) | GSM8K **0.890** (0/200 truncated) | All runs use the command above: greedy (temperature 0, top_p 0.95), thinking off. Every server that loads answers `17*23` with `391`. **SM90 run by @HollowMan6** (1x H20-3e, the same commands; [comment](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/49531#issuecomment-6769382079)): | Checkpoint | main | branch | |---|---|---| | `unsloth/GLM-4.7-Flash-FP8-Dynamic` | GSM8K **0.000** (200/200 truncated; `17*23` answers `!!!!!!!!…`) | GSM8K **0.890** (0/200 truncated) | | `cyankiwi/GLM-4.7-Flash-AWQ-4bit` | fails to load | GSM8K **0.870** (0/200 truncated) | This covers the FP8 case that SM86 cannot run, and the fused-A GEMM path, which is eligible on SM90. 1. **Truncations** are generations that hit the 4096-token cap. They happen on unpatched main too (2/200 with the AWQ checkpoint), so they are not caused by this PR. The cookbook's 0.845 is BF16 on H100 with the same `sgl-eval` command and 200 examples. It's a sanity reference, not a like-for-like comparison. An earlier A6000 run of the `cyankiwi` checkpoint on this branch is consistent: 0.874 thinking-off and 0.969 thinking-on, both partial runs without a token cap. 2. **The AWQ runs:** both trees build the same model: 17.52 GB of weights, the same KV size, the `awq_marlin` kernel and the same CUDA graphs. Answers flip both ways (10 questions right only on main, 6 only on the branch), and 51/200 greedy generations match word for word. That looks like batching nondeterminism, though I did not run main twice to confirm. 3. **FP8** (`unsloth/GLM-4.7-Flash-FP8-Dynamic`) cannot run on SM86 on either tree (`bmm_fp8 does not support backend 'cublas' with capability 86`); see the SM90 table above.
Before: main, cyankiwi/GLM-4.7-Flash-AWQ-4bit (the same assert on A6000 and A40) ``` File ".../sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py", line 1048, in load_model self.load_weights_and_postprocess( File ".../sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py", line 1057, in load_weights_and_postprocess DefaultModelLoader.load_weights_only(model, weights, target_device) File ".../sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py", line 1091, in load_weights_only model.load_weights(weights) File ".../sglang/srt/models/glm4_moe_lite.py", line 1043, in load_weights weight_loader(param, fused_weight) File ".../sglang/srt/layers/linear.py", line 377, in weight_loader AssertionError: param.shape=torch.Size([2]) param.dtype=torch.int64 loaded_weight.shape=torch.Size([4]) loaded_weight.dtype=torch.int64 ``` With fixes 1–4 applied but not 5, loading completes and the first forward fails: ``` File ".../sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py", line 2621, in prepare_qkv_latent and fused_a_gemm_weight_eligible( File ".../sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/fused_a_gemm.py", line 52, in fused_a_gemm_weight_eligible layer.weight.dtype == torch.bfloat16 AttributeError: 'ReplicatedLinear' object has no attribute 'weight' ```
After: this branch, cyankiwi/GLM-4.7-Flash-AWQ-4bit (A40) ``` [2026-11-10 09:11:58] Quantization keeps shared experts at a higher precision than the routed experts, so they cannot be fused into the quantized routed-expert path. Shared experts fusion optimization is disabled. [2026-11-10 09:12:18] Load weight end. elapsed=20.65 s, type=Glm4MoeLiteForCausalLM, quant=compressed-tensors, avail mem=26.22 GB, mem usage=17.86 GB. [2026-11-10 09:12:25] KV Cache is allocated. dtype: torch.bfloat16, #tokens: 360675, KV size: 18.19 GB [2026-11-10 09:25:22] Capture target prefill CUDA graph end. elapsed=777.75 s, mem usage=1.73 GB, avail mem=4.63 GB. [2026-11-10 09:25:34] Capture target decode CUDA graph end. bs=[1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32], elapsed=11.78 s, mem usage=0.29 GB, avail mem=4.35 GB. [2026-11-10 09:25:51] The server is fired up and ready to roll! ``` The 778 s prefill capture was the first serve on a fresh pod. The same code captured in 26 s on the A6000 pod after an earlier serve there, so this is most likely cold kernel caches; the log does not show the cause. ``` $ curl .../v1/chat/completions # "What is 17*23? Answer with just the number." "content": "391" ``` ``` sgl-eval gsm8k (A40, 200 examples, 64 threads, max_tokens 4096, thinking off): score 0.85, stop_rate 0.995, truncated_rate 0.005, error_rate 0.0 ```
### Unit tests New CPU file `test/registered/unit/models/test_mla_compressed_tensors_wna16_loading.py` (`base-a-test-cpu`), plus a GLM case in `test_shared_experts_fusion_gates.py`. I checked each regression case: it fails with its fix reverted and passes with it. The cases: - The GLM and DeepSeek loaders fuse `weight_shape` / `weight_packed` / `weight_scale`. - GLM stacks AWQ `qweight` on dim 1 and keeps unconverted BF16 attention on dim 0. - `dequantize_weight` matches compressed-tensors' own `pack_to_int32` exactly (4-bit group, 4-bit channel, 8-bit). - The real `process_weights_after_loading` marks the layer, and dequantizing it afterwards raises. - `post_load_weights` builds `w_kc`/`w_vc` from a packed `kv_b_proj`, and online weight updates are then refused. - Layer 0's fused layers, and an FP8 checkpoint's ignored layer-1 attention, resolve to their ignored shards. - `can_fuse_shared_expert` covers the checkpoint's own ignore list, gate-only, a single shared `up_proj` / `down_proj`, routed-only, the same projection on both sides, both-ignored, regex (including `re:.*mlp\.shared.*` and a layer-anchored regex) and bare-suffix cases. - GPTQ / AutoRound `qweight` stacks on dim 1, GGUF's stays on dim 0, and GPTQ `g_idx` follows the act-order rule. - `fused_a_gemm_weight_eligible` is false on a packed layer. ``` test_mla_compressed_tensors_wna16_loading.py + test_shared_experts_fusion_gates.py + test_deepseek_quark_block_fp8_loading.py: 67 passed on the A40 pod at 0a7a7e4175; 69 passed locally at f542238650 ``` f542238650 leaves the fusion decision of both real checkpoints unchanged (`cyankiwi`: off, `unsloth` FP8: on), so the accuracy runs above still apply. ## Merge Danger **Door:** two-way. Code-only, no format, config or API changes; a revert restores the old behavior. **Blast radius:** MLA checkpoint loading. - Every GLM-4.7-Flash and DeepSeek-family load goes through the new QKV-A fusion helper. Only `weight_shape`, `weight_g_idx` and the AWQ `qweight`/`qzeros`/`scales` choice of dimension behave differently; every other tensor concatenates exactly as before. The unconverted-attention AWQ case is covered by the `QuantTrio` row above. - Shared-expert fusion turns off for compressed-tensors checkpoints whose `ignore` keeps any shared-expert projection at a different precision from its routed counterpart (see "Behavior change outside GLM"). That costs throughput where fusion used to run, but such checkpoints loaded weights into buffers of the wrong precision. - A packed compressed-tensors `kv_b_proj` reloaded through the sharded-state or remote-instance loaders now raises `NotImplementedError` instead of computing silently wrong `w_kc`/`w_vc`. - Online weight updates on a compressed-tensors WNA16 MLA checkpoint are refused up front with a message, instead of failing in `post_load_weights` after the new weights were written. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No kernel changes. The fused-A GEMM change only makes packed layers take their regular path (before, they crashed). title: [Fix] diffusion: Stop normalizing bright edit inputs a second time before VAE encoding
author: Smallfu666
body:
## Motivation

Image edits whose input has no dark pixel come out darker than the input. With Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 (any edit) and FLUX.2-klein (inputs that need a resize: over 1 MP, or a side that is not a multiple of 16), the pipeline config already turns the input into a [-1, 1] tensor ([qwen_image.py](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/e0187268f64165fa6969fb166dd5c11f05462e3c/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/configs/pipeline_configs/qwen_image.py#L673-L688), [flux.py](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/e0187268f64165fa6969fb166dd5c11f05462e3c/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/configs/pipeline_configs/flux.py#L606-L630)). `ImageVAEEncodingStage.preprocess` then guesses the range from the values and normalizes again whenever the minimum is not negative ([image_encoding.py](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/e0187268f64165fa6969fb166dd5c11f05462e3c/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/image_encoding.py#L1104-L1119)). For an image whose channels are all at least 128 the minimum is not negative, so `x * 2 - 1` runs twice and a pixel value of 170 reaches the VAE as if it were 85. diffusers preprocesses the edit image once and encodes it directly ([pipeline_qwenimage_edit_plus.py](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/v0.42.1/src/diffusers/pipelines/qwenimage/pipeline_qwenimage_edit_plus.py#L706)).

On a default `sglang serve` server, `/v1/images/edits` with prompt "Keep the image exactly the same.", seed 0, and a smooth pastel input whose darkest channel value is 170:

| model, input | mean abs. difference from the input (0-255), main | with this change |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image-Edit-2511, 1024x1024 | 35.15 | 1.11 |
| FLUX.2-klein-4B, 770x1344 | 35.11 | 2.29 |

In the same run, an input with dark pixels (both models) and a bright FLUX.2 input that needs no resize (1024x1024) gave bit-identical outputs on main and with this change.

## Modifications

- `ImageVAEEncodingStage.preprocess` passes tensors through unchanged: the configs that hand over tensors produce [-1, 1]. PIL inputs keep their current handling.
- MOVA was the only config that handed over a [0, 1] tensor and relied on the guess. `MOVAPipelineConfig.preprocess_condition_image` now returns [-1, 1] itself, so MOVA's VAE input does not change.
- `test_image_preprocessing.py`: `test_vae_encoding_keeps_bright_edit_inputs` runs `ImageVAEEncodingStage.forward` with a recording VAE on a bright input prepared by the real FLUX.2 and Qwen-Image-Edit-Plus configs, and checks that the VAE receives the config's tensor unchanged. It fails on main (both configs, max abs. difference 0.745) and passes with this change.

```bash
python3 test/registered/unit/multimodal_gen/test_image_preprocessing.py -v
```

## Accuracy Tests

The table above: one H200, default flags, one image per case. Multi-image Qwen edits with a bright second image also change (output mean 185 on main vs 213 with this change). Not run: MOVA, Wan2.2 TI2V, image quality metrics beyond the difference from the input.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

title: [Fix] bench: Check the chat template on the tokenizer the benchmark loads
author: leejnau
body:
[by Claude Code]

## Motivation

#42752 T18: `test/registered/tokenizer/test_multi_tokenizer.py::TestMultiTokenizer::test_multi_tokenizer_ttft` hit its 1200 s file timeout ([job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42186654582/job/127793540031), `h100-novita9-gpu-23`). The server was idle. After the bench client's `GET /v1/models`, nothing reached the server for 17 minutes.

In `run_benchmark`, the only step between `GET /v1/models` and the next request (`GET /model_info`) is `check_chat_template(args.model)`. It loads the tokenizer with `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained` only to decide whether to print a warning. `get_tokenizer` then loads the same tokenizer again a few lines later.

Each load sends Hugging Face Hub metadata requests. CI sets `HF_HUB_ETAG_TIMEOUT: 300` (`.github/workflows/_pr-test-stage.yml`), so each one can wait up to 5 minutes. `popen_launch_server` puts the server subprocess in `HF_HUB_OFFLINE` mode once the cache validates, but the in-process bench client stays online. The same runner slot had passed this test 16 minutes earlier, so the tokenizer was already cached.

Main's scheduled runs from 2026-10-30 to 11-10 (23 runs) show the gap from `GET /v1/models` to `GET /model_info` is normally 4–6 s. The one outlier, 39 s on `h100-novita9-gpu-01` on 11-06, stalled at the same point.

## Modifications

- Replace `check_chat_template(model_path)` with `has_chat_template(tokenizer)`. `run_benchmark` now checks the tokenizer that `get_tokenizer` returns, so it loads the tokenizer once instead of twice.
- The check also looks at `tokenizer.chat_template`, not only `init_kwargs`.
- Remove the now-unused `AutoTokenizer` import.

This also changes which tokenizer gets checked: the one the benchmark actually uses (`tokenizer_path` from `/model_info`), not the served model name.

This removes the call that stalled, but the remaining load can still wait on the Hub. A fuller fix would run the in-process bench client offline when the cache validates, the way the server already does. That touches shared test utilities, so it's left for a follow-up if this recurs.

## Testing

- Compared the old check (`"chat_template" in tokenizer.init_kwargs`) with `has_chat_template` on real tokenizers with transformers 5.22.2. Both give True for `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B` and `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B`, and False for `openai-community/gpt2`. An object without tokenizer attributes returns False.
- `pre-commit run` passes.

title: [Fix] diffusion: MiniMax-H3 follow-ups: load the public H3-Image snapshot, keep H3 video conditioning, fix profiler test pollution
author: niehen6174
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up fixes for #49552 (MiniMax-H3-Image). On `main` after #49552:

1. **The public MiniMax-H3-Image checkpoint fails to load.** The public snapshot `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image@fbde899fff` ships `text_encoder/`, while `model_index.json` still names `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/text_encoder`. Server startup raises `model_index.json loads 'text_encoder' from 'MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/text_encoder', but the snapshot also has .../text_encoder`.
2. **H3 video regression.** `minimax_h3_ref2va_video_audio_2gpu_h100` fails its consistency check in `multimodal-gen-test-2-gpu`. Frame SSIM is 0.62-0.79 against a 0.92 threshold, and the failure cancels other diffusion jobs via fail-fast.
3. **Unit test pollution.** `test_sdpa_cudnn_priority.py` fails in the full diffusion unit suite with `assert 'unknown' == 'cudnn'` (main scheduled run 42920442894).

## Changes

### 1. Load a bundled copy of an external `model_index.json` component
`ComposedPipelineBase._resolve_component_path` used to reject a snapshot that both names an external component and contains that subfolder. The bundled `text_encoder/` files are byte-identical to `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/text_encoder` (all 23 sha256 match). The loader now uses the bundled copy, which also skips a separate 67 GB download. An explicit `--component-paths` override still takes precedence.

### 2. Keep the H3 video Qwen3-VL vision RoPE table unchanged
#49552 added `rotary_pos_emb.recompute_on_device_change = True` to the shared `MiniMaxH3Qwen3VL.__init__`. This rebuilds the vision RoPE table on GPU after offload, which changes the Ref2VA reference-video conditioning for H3 **video** releases, whose references were generated with the old table. The rebuild now runs only for image pipelines, from `MiniMaxH3Pipeline.create_pipeline_stages`, as Qwen-Image 2.1 does from its stage.

How it was found, on 2x H200: restoring single files from `170804b40a^1` into `170804b40a`. Restoring the DiT left the output different. Restoring `encoders/minimax_h3_qwen3vl.py` made video and audio byte-identical to pre-merge.

### 3. Stop the profiler window test from disabling CUDA kernel capture
`test_profiler_window_contains_requested_steps` moved from `test/registered/`, where it ran in its own process, into the diffusion unit suite. It patched `torch.cuda.is_available` to `False`, so the first profiler session in the process initialized CPU-only, and later sessions recorded no CUDA kernels. That broke `test_sdpa_cudnn_priority`, which runs after it. The patch is removed; the test only inspects CPU-side `denoise_step_*` ranges.

## Verification

- **Public checkpoint (fix 1):** `pytest test_server_b200.py -k minimax_h3_image` on `fbde899fff`. On 1x H200 and 1x B300 the server loads, and T2I and edit generate (T2I e2e ~3.0 s / ~3.1 s). Without the fix both fail at startup with the error above.
- **H3 video (fix 2):** `minimax_h3_ref2va_video_audio_2gpu_h100` on `170804b40a` plus this change produces video and audio byte-identical to `170804b40a^1`; without it, video mean |d| is 5.19. MiniMax-H3-Image T2I and edit outputs are unchanged.
- **Test pollution (fix 3):** running the profiler window test, then `test_sdpa_cudnn_priority`, failed before the fix and passes after. The CI-ordered unit files from `test_pipeline_stage_profiling` through `test_sdpa_cudnn_priority` pass (871 passed).
- `pytest test_minimax_h3*.py test_qwen3vl_vision.py test_qwen_image21.py test_hf_diffusers_utils.py`: pass. `pre-commit`: pass.

## Unrelated CI failure

`multimodal-gen-test-1-5090` fails on `main` too (scheduled run 42920442894), and it does not come from #49552. `turbo_wan2_1_t2v_1.3b` and `flux_image_t2i_layerwise_cpu_offload_5090` exceed `Load Peak Host Anon` by 0.15-0.7%, and the first `turbo_wan` decode is sometimes slow. The same job passed on #45730 with #49552 merged but without the later main commits.

title: [Fix] sgl-router: Render and tokenize off the async workers
author: Kangyan-Zhou
body:
## Motivation

Chat-template rendering and tokenization are synchronous CPU work, and today they run inside an async handler's poll. When one render is slow (a long conversation, or a template that does a lot of work per message), the tokio worker running it is stuck in that poll. The other workers stay parked and nothing polls the I/O driver, so the whole router stops serving: no new connections are accepted, HTTP/2 PINGs go unanswered, and in-flight streams get no bytes until the render returns. Under load, a single multi-second render can make clients and proxies drop every open connection to the router.

## Modifications

- New crate-level helper `off_worker::run`. It wraps synchronous CPU work in `tokio::task::block_in_place`, which hands the worker's core (and with it the I/O driver) to another thread before the work starts. On a current-thread runtime, outside any runtime, or on a blocking-pool thread, it runs the work inline.
- `TokenizerRegistry::encode_chat` and `TokenizerRegistry::encode_prompt` go through it themselves, so every caller is covered whatever route or task calls them.
- The chat route's request preparation (`routes::chat::prepare`: parse, render, tokenize, body rebuild) runs through it as a whole, so parsing and rebuilding a large body also stay off the worker.
- Routing tokenization of a raw prompt (`policies::request_tokens_for`) calls the tokenizer directly, so it goes through it too.
- The same goes for `/v1/messages` (Anthropic parse and conversion to a chat body, and the conversion of a non-streaming reply back to an Anthropic message), the `count_tokens` parse, and `/v1/tokenize` / `/v1/detokenize`, which call the tokenizer directly.

`block_in_place` is used instead of `spawn_blocking` because it works on borrowed data, so no signatures change, and it keeps the current task's context, so `tokio::task_local!` state stays visible. Nested calls (for example `prepare` → `encode_chat`) are harmless: the inner call finds no core to hand off. Each outermost call costs one core handoff (waking a blocking-pool thread to take over the worker), including on requests that end up not tokenizing; gating it on request size is possible if that shows up in profiles.

Not in this PR: any time or concurrency limit on rendering. With this change, N simultaneous slow renders each occupy a thread instead of freezing the runtime; they still share the blocking pool, so capping them is a sensible follow-up.

## Accuracy Tests

No change to model outputs: the same functions run, only on a different thread.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Each test uses a chat template that spins on messages whose content is `slow`. The message count doubles until one render takes at least 400 ms, so the tests also hold in release builds. With ONE tokio worker, a spawned task does the slow work while another task waits on a 20 ms timer. The test asserts that the timer fires long before the work finishes.

- `off_worker::tests::blocking_work_leaves_the_runtime_serving`, plus inline-fallback tests for a current-thread runtime, no runtime, and a blocking-pool thread.
- `tokenizer::tests::slow_chat_encode_leaves_the_runtime_serving` (through `encode_chat`).
- `server::routes::chat::tests::a_slow_chat_render_leaves_the_runtime_serving` (through `prepare`, asserting that tokens were produced).

Without the fix (`run` calling `work()` directly), all three fail: the timer waits for the whole render.

Local results:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pre-commit run` on the changed files | clean |
| `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo test --locked --lib` | 1135 passed |
| `cargo test --locked --test component -- --skip parity_matrix` (as CI) | 134 passed |
| `cargo test --locked --test proxy` | 226 passed |

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Fix] dsa: Give each FlashMLA decode graph its own schedule for native-head kernels
author: yhyang201
body:
Original authors: @BBuf

## Port of #48414

`sgl-flash-mla` 1.0.4 (#49362) ships the native-head sparse decode, whose partition count changes with the query-row count. `sparse_decode_num_sm_parts` on B300 (148 SMs):

| q heads | s_q=1 | s_q=2 | s_q=8 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 128 | 74 for <= 73 rows, else 148 | 37 for <= 36 rows, else 74 | 9 for <= 8 rows, else 18 |
| 64 | 148 | 74 | 18 |

1.0.2 always used `148 // s_q`. `dsa_backend` still shares one CUDA-graph FlashMLA schedule sized for the largest batch, so capturing the decode graphs of a DSA model with 65-128 padded q heads crashes once they span both sizes:

```
DSAFlashMLAMetadata.copy_: The size of tensor a (148) must match the size of tensor b (74)
```

Reproduced on main 6dc7e3ea7e with Kimi-K3.1-Pro, TP8 + DCP8: in decode graph capture (graphs up to bs 80) and, with DFLASH, in target-verify graph capture. This ports the Day-0 handling: each graph owns its schedule, which replay updates in place.

Against the raw port (first commit): dropped the pre-padded q branch, whose buffer setup is not on main; kept main's 64/128 head padding (the raw port also switched `flashmla_kv` to native head counts, which changes the kernel path for DSA models with other per-rank head counts and needs its own validation); added a test.

Left for later ports: native head counts for `flashmla_kv` (`_flashmla_kv_padded_heads`), FlashMLA prefill token packing and the in-place q padding buffer (`_flashmla_kv_pad_q_in_place`).

Not covered: a draft-extend graph replays with the accepted-row count, which can still give a different partition count than its capture on SM100 with 65-128 padded heads (MTP/EAGLE drafts on the DSA backend). That predates this PR.

DeepSeek-V4 is not affected: at 64 heads `sparse_decode_num_sm_parts` equals main's `max(num_sms // s_q, 1)` for s_q 1-8 and batch 1-512.

## Modifications

- `layers/attention/dsa_backend.py`: per-graph FlashMLA schedule in decode / target-verify capture, updated in place on replay.
- `test_flashmla_sched_meta.py`: graphs whose partition counts differ get separate schedules.

## Results

Kimi-K3.1-Pro, 8x B300, TP8, DCP8, EP2, fp8 KV, `sgl-flash-mla` 1.0.4:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| decode graphs bs 1-80 (74 and 148 parts) | crash (148 vs 74) | captured; GSM8K 97.80% |
| DFLASH (7-layer MLA draft, `cutedsl_mla`, block 8): target-verify graphs | crash (148 vs 74) | captured; GSM8K 97.50%, AIME26 x8 pass@1 98.75% (maj@8 100%) |

GSM8K and AIME26 via sgl-eval with the Kimi-K3 preset; no errors in either server log. The decode-graph row is on the final commit; the DFLASH row ran before the native-head padding was reverted, which is a no-op at these 128 padded heads.

title: [Fix] sgl-router: pass a streaming prefill's in-band 4xx through to the client
author: Kangyan-Zhou
body:
## Motivation

In PD mode, the router reports a request with an invalid `response_format` JSON schema or tool `structural_tag` as a server fault. Which status the client sees depends on which engine answers first.

Both engines reject such a request almost immediately. If decode's rejection reaches the router first, the client gets a 400. If prefill's arrives first, the client gets a 502 `prefill_failed`.

A streaming prefill has already sent its 200 headers, so it reports the rejection as an SSE error event that carries the engine's status code. `prefill_failure` treated every error event as a prefill fault and turned it into `prefill_failed`. As a result, a client error was counted as a 5xx, and clients were encouraged to retry a request that can never succeed.

## Modifications

- `sse::client_error_event` (`sgl-router/src/proxy/sse.rs`) reads the first error event in a buffered SSE body. It returns that event's status and a JSON error body when the code is 4xx. It understands the two shapes the engine streams:
  - OpenAI routes: `data: {"error": {"message", "type", "code", ...}}`. The event's JSON is passed through unchanged.
  - Native `/generate`: an abort `finish_reason` with a `status_code`. This is reframed as `{"error": {"message", "code"}}`, the same body a non-streaming `/generate` returns.
- `prefill_failure` (`sgl-router/src/server/routes/chat/forward.rs`) now returns that 4xx as the response, with `content-type: application/json`. This is the same path a non-streaming prefill 4xx already takes, so it gets the same handling:
  - the outcome is recorded as `client_error`, not `error`;
  - it is logged at DEBUG, not WARN;
  - it is not retried, except a 429, which is retried as backpressure.

  Decode is still aborted, as for any prefill failure.
- Anything else still becomes `prefill_failed`: a 5xx code; a missing, non-integer or out-of-range code; an event that does not parse; or a body that fails to read.

The gRPC prefill path (`Grpc::prefill`) also folds in-band errors into `PrefillFailed`. Passing a 4xx through there needs a mapping from an HTTP status to a tonic `Status`, so it is not part of this PR.

## Tests

- `forward::tests::in_band_client_error_passes_through`: an OpenAI-shaped 400 event and a native 422 abort each pass through with their status and body.
- `forward::tests::in_band_server_error_stays_prefill_failed`: a 500 event and a 503 abort stay `prefill_failed`.
- `forward::tests::unparseable_in_band_error_stays_prefill_failed`: covers a truncated event, a missing code, a string code, code 4000 and a bare-string `error`.
- `forward::tests::clean_prefill_stream_is_not_a_failure`: error-like text inside generated content is not treated as a failure.
- `pd_bootstrap_injection::reliability::prefill_sse_client_error_passes_through`: end to end, with and without reorg routing. The client gets 400 with the engine's body and no `x-router-error-code`, and the prefill worker's outcome is `client_error`.

The two pass-through tests fail on `main`; the end-to-end test returns 502 there instead of 400.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Fix] constrained: Reject a token in llguidance without poisoning the matcher
author: ShangmingCai
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #48117, reported by @paolo-perrone in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/48117#discussion_r4471961479 and confirmed with llguidance 1.9.1.

`GuidanceGrammar.accept_token` called `ll_matcher.consume_token` directly. When llguidance rejects a token, the matcher enters a sticky error state (`is_error()` stays set), so every later `rollback` / `fill_vocab_mask` raised through `_check_err` as well. `traverse_tree`'s prune-on-reject assumes a rejected `accept_token` leaves the grammar at its current state. That holds for xgrammar (`AcceptToken` restores its state on reject) but not for llguidance:

- a rejected draft token below the root still escaped as a `ValueError` from the parent's `rollback(1)` and killed the scheduler, exactly as before #48117;
- a rejected token at depth 1 did not crash, but every later sibling also failed on the errored matcher, so valid siblings were pruned and the request kept an errored grammar.

## Modifications

Validate the token first with `ll_matcher.validate_tokens([token])`, which is read-only, and raise `ValueError("Tokens not accepted: ...")` when it is rejected, before calling `consume_token`. The matcher stays where it was, so the handler in `traverse_tree` now holds for both backends. `validate_tokens` has been in llguidance since well before the pinned minimum (`>=1.7.6`).

## Tests

`test/registered/unit/constrained/test_llguidance_accept_token.py` (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`), using llguidance's built-in byte tokenizer and the regex `ab|ac`:

- a rejected `accept_token` raises `ValueError`, leaves `is_error()` false, and both continuations remain accept/rollback-able;
- `traverse_tree` over root -> "a" -> {"x", "b"} with all-allow mask rows (so the matcher is what rejects "x") no longer raises, masks "x" off its parent row, and keeps the valid sibling "b".

Red/green locally: both cases fail on the base commit with llguidance's `token "x" doesn't satisfy the grammar` parser error sticking; with the fix they pass, along with `test_llguidance_batched_mask.py` and `test_spec_utils_traverse_tree.py`.

title: [Fix] kernels: Synchronize AOT MoE prefix before expert lookup
author: jybsuper
body:
## Motivation

The CUDA path of `moe_align_block_size_kernel` writes shared `prefix[]` entries after its final synchronization, then binary-searches entries written by other warps. This race can assign an incorrect expert ID to a block of routed rows.

## Modifications

Write the final scan result directly to `prefix` before the existing `__syncthreads()`, matching the JIT publication fix in #45916. Remove the intermediate `scan_buf` copy. This keeps the original barrier count.

Use unsigned indices for the non-negative binary-search bounds, converting back to signed before subtracting 2 so the invalid expert keeps its `-1` ID. This avoids a measured compiler-code-generation regression from the direct-prefix rewrite; no architecture or shape special case is added.

Only `python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/moe/moe_align_kernel.cu` changes. The small-batch kernel and host dispatcher are unchanged. The HIP scan and barriers are unchanged, but its shared binary search also uses unsigned indices; AMD was not executed. Related: #43030 proposes an extra-barrier fix for the same race. This standalone AOT change is based on main `a6f190e8fe`.

## Accuracy Tests

Current source: `536af98f5f`, SHA256 `9aef6104decec35d5c49b41ff3afde3c6441d9579dfa9286c723cf2212262652`. GPU validation ran on `54a2b59e91` (source SHA256 `161cd0e24e626ccbb7748a5430a4283770a0c8a0cd9de6a7a986add53334028c`). Since that run, the commits were squashed and two comments were removed; kernel logic is unchanged. GPU tests were not rerun for the comment-only cleanup.

B300, CUDA 13.0.88, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130: independently compile the exact AOT translation unit and header with its unchanged production host dispatcher and minimal Torch registration (`-O3`, `compute_100f/sm_100f`). Each variant is loaded in a fresh process. This validates source kernels, not a complete AOT wheel or serving stack.

- Final unsigned version passes **4,080 CPU-reference cases**, including int32/int64, invalid/dropped IDs, padding, dispatch boundaries, non-vector-aligned capacities and up to 1,024 buckets. Four deliberately corrupted-output checker controls are detected. Pair order within an expert is checked as a multiset.
- Final **racecheck and memcheck** each pass eight cases, with zero reported hazards/errors. The original-main negative control previously reported the expected shared-prefix race (five reported groups), with wrong expert IDs in three of eight sanitizer cases. Both fixed publication variants were clean.
- Final **graph stress** passes **800,000 alignment invocations**: int32/int64, each with 200,000 invocations with concurrent GEMM and 200,000 without. Expert IDs, padded totals and cumsum are checked after every invocation. This is 200,000 graph replays, four invocations per replay. Sort output is checked in the reference grid, not on every stress invocation.
- All 185 files in the final investigation archive have verified SHA256 checksums; a read-only offline consistency/provenance audit passes 551 checks with no failures.
- `git diff --check` and changed-file pre-commit checks pass. `pre-commit run --all-files` passes every applicable hook except the unrelated Rust clippy build, which cannot find `cmake` on this macOS host.

Latest-main wheel/CI integration, Hopper, AMD and end-to-end serving validation remain outside this run; the PR remains draft.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same B300, **alignment plus sort**, two ID dtypes, six shapes each, three rotated variant orders in separate processes. Per round and cell: five samples, each with 200 captured calls replayed 100 times. Values below are microseconds/call, the median of the three round medians; a positive time change means slower. Main is the unfixed performance control, not a correctness recommendation.

| IDs | Tokens | Block size | Main | Extra barrier | Signed direct | Final unsigned | Final vs main time |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| int32 | 32 | 1 | 4.119 | 4.146 | 4.084 | 4.082 | -0.91% |
| int32 | 32 | 64 | 4.318 | 4.333 | 4.294 | 4.295 | -0.53% |
| int32 | 1,024 | 1 | 9.375 | 9.390 | 9.509 | 9.321 | -0.58% |
| int32 | 1,024 | 64 | 7.290 | 7.303 | 7.254 | 7.254 | -0.49% |
| int32 | 4,096 | 1 | 27.099 | 27.092 | 27.838 | 27.057 | -0.16% |
| int32 | 4,096 | 64 | 13.189 | 13.214 | 13.179 | 13.177 | -0.09% |
| int64 | 32 | 1 | 4.204 | 4.231 | 4.184 | 4.184 | -0.48% |
| int64 | 32 | 64 | 4.293 | 4.303 | 4.262 | 4.257 | -0.84% |
| int64 | 1,024 | 1 | 10.527 | 10.543 | 10.698 | 10.507 | -0.19% |
| int64 | 1,024 | 64 | 6.159 | 6.177 | 6.137 | 6.137 | -0.35% |
| int64 | 4,096 | 1 | 31.024 | 31.011 | 31.765 | 30.982 | -0.13% |
| int64 | 4,096 | 64 | 13.234 | 13.260 | 13.216 | 13.215 | -0.14% |

The signed direct-prefix version regresses at block size 1 on the two larger shapes. The final unsigned version removes that measured regression for both dtypes; all 12 median timings are at or below the main control in this run. These small differences are descriptive measurements, not a universal speedup or end-to-end throughput claim.

The regression is localized to search/control code generation:

- Per-kernel profiles localize the extra time to alignment; sort time stays essentially unchanged. Sort SASS is byte-identical across the three original variants.
- Generic alignment variants use the same 31 registers, 1,040 reported static shared bytes and zero stack/local storage; register count and spilling do not explain the result.
- The prefix rewrite changes machine code in the source-unchanged binary-search loop, including `VIADD` becoming `IADD3`. At block size 1, the 1,024/4,096-token shapes perform 8/32 searches per thread; tested block-64 shapes perform at most one. Repeated loop cost can outweigh the fixed synchronization saving.
- The unsigned variant preserves the direct-prefix publication code and changes subsequent search/control code generation, restoring the fast measurements. Four other equivalent source rewrites compiled identically to the slower signed version. The explicit final signed conversion leaves the successful candidate's machine code unchanged.
- Hardware performance counters are unavailable on this box. The evidence supports a search/control code-generation explanation; it does not isolate a single instruction's intrinsic latency or prove one GPU pipeline is the sole cause.

title: [Fix] muse_spark: [sglang-miles] Refresh derived weight caches after a weight sync
author: guapisolo
body:
## Summary
Muse Spark rollouts no longer turn uniform after the first RL weight sync on a colocated engine.

## Symptom & Reproduction
- **Symptom:** In the four-layer e2e of radixark/miles#4759, the engine's log-prob of its own sampled tokens is `-12.216` (`-ln(202048)`, uniform) from the first weight sync on. The trainer disagrees by 5.8 in `train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff`, and routing replay reports 50-83% zero-overlap tokens; [run 42921580351](https://github.com/radixark/miles/actions/runs/42921580351) at miles `ed610bc3` fails on `R3 mismatch tokens (1049) > threshold (20)`.
- **Reproduction:** `python tests/e2e/megatron/model_scripts/test_muse_spark_open_last4_ci.py` at miles `13946f02` on 4 H200 against this base (`5bcc5b2`). Expected about `-6.4`, which the same engine gives before any sync (`-6.49`); observed `-12.216`.

## Root Cause
1. `FusedPostNormResidualPreNorm._ensure_cached_weights` and `FusedRMSNormGate._ensure_cached_weight` snapshot norm weights and residual coefficients once, at the first forward.
2. `MuseSpark1xRouter._build_split2` keys its BF16 split on `weight.data._version`, which stays 0 across in-place updates.
3. `MuseSpark1xBf16Experts.prepare_trtllm_weights` returns early once prepared and leaves `_post_expert_norm_weight` as bound.
4. A colocated engine's memory-saver pause/resume zeroes these copies; `update_weights_from_tensor` rewrites only the Parameters.
5. `MuseSparkTextForCausalLM.forward` then runs on the zeroed copies and logits come out uniform; the weight check compares Parameters and passes.

## Fix
`MuseSparkTextForCausalLM.post_load_weights`, which runs after every load and every weight update, now refreshes each copy in place, so addresses captured by CUDA graphs stay valid. The boundary op owns its copies instead of aliasing the source tensors, so a refresh cannot write through to the weights. The logic is ported from `bc1c2ac7df` (`sglang-miles-muse-spark-open`) and is a subset of #48045, limited to the BF16 path verified below. Values without a weight sync are unchanged. Not included: online update of TRT-LLM-shuffled BF16 experts on Blackwell, and the FP4 / NVFP4 refreshes.

## Verification
- miles four-layer e2e (miles `13946f02`, 4 H200, 3 rollout/train/sync cycles) with this change: `train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff` 0.0185 / 0.0186 / 0.0187 (was 5.80), `train_rollout_kl` 2.8e-4 (was 4.9), engine log-prob -6.43 / -6.41 / -6.43, routing replay mismatch 0 on every rank. It ran before the comment-only edits and the added test in `4ed1298a98`.
- `test_muse_spark_norm_ops.py` at `4ed1298a98` on H200: 80 passed. The new `test_norm_residual_follows_in_place_weight_update` fails on the base, where the fused output is off by 1.39 (max abs) after an in-place update.
- `test_muse_spark_routing.py`, `test_muse_spark_router_gemv_cutedsl.py`, `test_muse_spark_moe_finalize_all_reduce.py` at `4ed1298a98` on H200: 128 passed.
- Not run: Blackwell, FP4 / NVFP4 experts, SGLang CI.

## Review Focus
- `refresh_cached_weights` / `_ensure_cached_weights`: the `_cc_*` tensors are now owned clones, refreshed in place under captured CUDA graphs.
- `refresh_split2`: no-op until the first `forward_split2` builds the split.
- `prepare_trtllm_weights`: refreshes only the finalize norm weight; shuffled expert weights still cannot take an online update.

title: [Fix] scheduler: Apply pending chunked-prefill aborts in the PP PD prefill loop
author: hnyls2002
body:
- The PP disaggregated prefill loop (`event_loop_pp_disagg_prefill`) builds batches without `get_next_disagg_prefill_batch_to_run`, so it never called `process_pending_chunked_abort`, and a client abort of an in-flight chunked prefill was never applied.
- The aborted request kept computing and sending its remaining chunks. While its bootstrap was pending, `process_prefill_chunk` dropped it from the chunked slot without releasing its sender or KV; only a later in-flight chunk result freed it.
- Call `process_pending_chunked_abort` before `process_prefill_chunk`, the order the non-PP prefill loop uses. Chunk results still in flight skip the aborted request through the existing aborted-result path.
- Add a test that drives `event_loop_pp_disagg_prefill` through an abort and checks the chunked slot is empty at admission; it fails without the fix.

author: hnyls2002
body:

Stage 0 relays its received requests to the next stage every iteration, while later stages receive only on the iterations the recv skipper lets through, so the stages fall out of step.
- Remove the runtime check in `_pp_init_stage_capacity` that rejected the same combination only under invariant checks with unified memory; the startup check covers it.
- Drop the sentence in the unified memory design doc that pointed at that runtime check.
- Add a unit test for the new check.

Behavior change: a pipeline-parallel launch with `--scheduler-recv-interval` above 1 now fails at startup instead of running with desynchronized stages.

title: [Fix] simulator: Keep the replaced HiCache storage workers alive
author: Saigyouji-Yuyuko
body:
## Motivation

Since #47617, `check_hicache_events` fails the rank when a started HiCache storage worker thread is no longer alive and the controller has not told it to stop. The simulator replaces `HiCacheController.prefetch_thread_func` and `backup_thread_func` with functions that return at once, because `handle_prefetch_operation` and `handle_backup_operation` do that work from the scheduler loop. `UnifiedRadixCache` builds a `HybridCacheController`, whose `prefetch_thread_func` calls `super()` into the simulator's replacement, so the `hicache-prefetch` thread exits right after it starts and the first scheduler tick raises:

```
RuntimeError: HiCache storage worker thread(s) exited on this rank: hicache-prefetch
```

Every simulation with HiCache storage enabled crashes there. On main, the scheduled full runs show the break:

| Scheduled run | Commit | Contains #47617 | `simulator-test-cpu` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-10 11:06 UTC | a2ffd21469 | no | [passed](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42804725184/job/129791160456) |
| 2026-11-10 23:05 UTC | 97abea64de | yes | [failed](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42920442894/job/130202596668) in `test_simulation_sglang_runner.py` with the error above |
| 2026-11-11 11:06 UTC | 7699e31092 | yes | [failed](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/43009217305/job/130484628407), same test, same error |

The simulator jobs did not run on #47617 itself: they are in the label-gated PR Test Extra workflow.

## Modifications

- The two replacement worker functions wait on `storage_stop_event` instead of returning. The threads stay alive, still do no work, and return once `_stop_storage_threads` (also used by `reset`) sets the event.
- `HybridCacheController` defines its own `backup_thread_func`, so on the `UnifiedRadixCache` path only the prefetch replacement is in effect. The backup replacement gets the same change; it applies wherever a plain `HiCacheController` runs with storage.
- `storage_stop_event` has the same name in v0.5.16, v0.5.17 and v0.5.18, the releases the simulator README lists, and each of them sets it before joining the storage threads.

## Accuracy Tests

Simulator-only change; no model forward or kernel code is touched.

The `simulator-test-cpu` file list from `.github/workflows/_pr-test-simulator-cpu.yml`, run locally on CPU (Python 3.12, `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""`):

| Test file | main b2568f706b + this PR |
|---|---|
| test_optional_aisimulate.py | 6 passed |
| test_train_latency_model.py | 1 passed |
| test_simulation_sglang_runner.py | 1 passed |
| test_simulation_sglang_serving.py | 5 passed |
| test_simulation_cache_hit_ratio.py | 2 passed |
| test_simulation_offline_blocking.py | 1 passed |
| test_aisimulate_predictor.py | 2 passed |

Without this change, `test_simulation_sglang_runner.py` crashes with the error above on 946cc59d11 and passes on 219b7e7a68, the parent of #47617's commit. `simulator-test-gpu` was not run locally; it passed in the same scheduled run that failed `simulator-test-cpu`.

The serving test above runs without HiCache, so the serving path was also checked with L3 storage on: `launch_server` with the flags of `test_simulation_sglang_serving.py` plus `--page-size 64 --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 2 --hicache-storage-backend file --hicache-storage-prefetch-policy wait_complete` (sim config `examples/sim_configs/aisimulate_sol.json`), driven by `benchmark/simulator/bench_serving.py` with an autobench trace of 4 prompts of 2048 distinct token ids each. Round 2 starts a new server process on the same storage key file, so its device and host caches are empty and every prefix hit comes from L3.

| | Without this PR | With this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Round 1, empty L3 | The scheduler raises the error above on its first tick and the server exits before serving a request | 4/4 requests complete; 128 pages written to L3 |
| Round 2, new process, same L3 | - | 4/4 requests complete; each hits 1984 of 2048 tokens in L3 (`kv_cache_storage_hit_ratio` 0.969, log: `HiCache prefetch success ... loaded=1984`) |
| SIGTERM to the server process | - | Drains and exits with code 0 in 4-5 s, the same as the identical run with HiCache disabled |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). The existing simulator tests cover this path; they fail on main today.
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Fix] lora: [sglang-miles] Keep kv_b_proj adapters off the MHA cached-prefix paths
author: Rockdu
body:
## Motivation

The DeepSeek/Kimi MHA prefill paths that attend a cached prefix (`forward_mha.py`: `_chunked_prefix_attn_mha`, its packed variant, `_fused_prefix_extend_attn_mha`, `forward_normal_prepare` under `mha_one_shot`) re-project the cached latent through `kv_b_proj` on **prefix rows**. With `kv_b_proj` wrapped by `ColumnParallelLinearWithLoRA`, that call runs the LoRA kernels with the forward batch's `LoRABatchInfo`, i.e. the **extend-token** segments. `sgemm_lora_a_fwd` sizes its grid from `max_len × bs` and walks `seg_indptr`/`seg_lens` without looking at `x.shape[0]`:

| prefix rows vs. extend tokens | effect |
|---|---|
| fewer | reads/writes past `x` / `output` / `base_output` → sticky `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS`, surfaced at the next launch (`flashinfer/trtllm/fmha/fmhaKernels.cuh:1338` in `trtllm_ragged_attention_deepseek`) |
| more | the delta lands on the wrong rows → silently wrong prefix K/V |

Only the absorbed MLA path adds the `kv_b_proj` delta per token (`deepseek_mla_correction.apply_q_correction` / `apply_v_correction`). On `trtllm_mla` every extend goes `MHA_CHUNKED_KV` unless `disable_chunked_prefix_cache` is set, so on Blackwell every prefix hit of a `kv_b_proj` adapter takes the broken path; on `fa3`/`flashinfer` it needs ≥ `SGLANG_CHUNKED_PREFIX_CACHE_THRESHOLD` (8192) cached tokens (silent corruption, no crash). With the flag, `trtllm_mla` falls back to the flashinfer MLA implementation for prefix-hit extends (`trtllm_mla_backend.init_forward_metadata`), which is why this is a flag-level rule and not a dispatch-only one.

Observed in radixark/miles `tests/e2e/megatron/model_scripts/test_kimi_k25_2layer_lora_native_ci.py` (Kimi-K2.5 2-layer, 4 engines TP2, `--lora-backend triton`, targets `q_a_proj,q_b_proj,kv_a_proj_with_mqa,kv_b_proj,o_proj`, adapter streamed by weight update): on a B200 runner (`trtllm_mla` auto-selected) 1–2 of 4 engines segfault right after the second weight update's first prefix-hit prefill; the same test on H100/`fa3` is clean because RL prompts never reach the 8192-token threshold. Not a regression of any sglang or miles change: the suite's runner moved from H100 to B200 between 10-31 and 11-09.

## Modifications

- `arg_groups/lora_hook.py`: when the CLI LoRA targets name `kv_b_proj` (or are `all` on an MLA model), resolve `--disable-chunked-prefix-cache` so every extend with a cached prefix dispatches to the absorbed MLA path, and reject the configurations that cannot get there: `--enable-kv-cache-sharding` (needs the chunked prefix cache, and its check runs earlier in the pipeline), the `dsa`/`nsa`/`aiter` prefill backends and `fa4` off sm100/sm110 (their dispatch ignores the flag). LoRA now also rejects `--enable-two-batch-overlap` for every backend: TBO children keep the parent's LoRA batch metadata, the same mismatch.
- `lora/lora_manager.py`: `init_lora_shapes` runs the same decision (`lora/utils.kv_b_lora_prefix_cache_error`, shared with the hook) on the final target set, so a `kv_b_proj` target that only surfaces from `--lora-paths` adapter configs fails at load with the flag spelled out instead of serving cached prefixes through the MHA paths.
- `kernels/ops/lora/dense/sgemm_lora_a.py`, `sgemm_lora_b.py`: assert that the input has exactly `batch_info.expected_tokens` rows before every launch (`lora/utils.check_lora_token_rows`; eager batches only — graph infos carry the captured width, decode routing infos carry no count). Every future mis-sized caller becomes a named error instead of memory corruption.

Cost: MLA + LoRA serving loses the MHA prefix path for cached prefixes (absorbed prefill), the same trade-off sglang already makes below the 8192-token threshold. Non-LoRA and LoRA-without-`kv_b_proj` configurations are untouched. A chunk-aware LoRA batch info for the MHA prefix paths (four call sites, three LoRA backends, DCP, prefill CUDA graph) is the follow-up that lifts the rule again; the row assert is its regression net.

## Accuracy Tests

- New CPU unit tests: `test/registered/unit/server_args/test_lora_kv_b_chunked_prefix.py` (hook rule, `all`-on-MLA, inferred targets left to the manager, backend / KV-sharding / TBO rejections, shared helper), `test/registered/unit/lora/test_lora_kv_b_manager_guard.py`, `test/registered/unit/lora/test_lora_token_rows_check.py` — 36 passed locally together with `test_deepseek_mla_dispatch.py` and `test_dsv4_mega_attention_lora_gate.py`.
- miles e2e `test_kimi_k25_2layer_lora_native_ci.py` on the B200 runner (`trtllm_mla`, `lora_backend triton`), miles main `2f627e0887`, image `release-v0.2.0-ci`, sglang pinned to this branch head `e05e2f6c72`: https://github.com/radixark/miles/actions/runs/43017817839 — PASS (537 s). Engine `server_args` show `disable_chunked_prefix_cache: True`; every engine logs `LoRA targets kv_b_proj: chunked prefix cache disabled ...`; 0 `Chunked prefix cache is turned on.`, 0 `fmhaKernels.cuh`, 0 `Segmentation fault`, 0 `exit code -11`, 0 `AssertionError` (the only SIGQUIT lines are the SIGTERM teardown after the last training step). The same test on the same runner with sglang-miles head crashes 1–2 of 4 engines (`fmhaKernels.cuh:1338`), e.g. miles nightly runs 42641258965 and 42840833452.
- Control (assert commit only, no rule, plus a trace line in `_chunked_prefix_attn_mha`; branch `rockdu/fix-kv-b-lora-chunked-prefix-assert-only`, 713c92715f): https://github.com/radixark/miles/actions/runs/43019796218 — the first prefix-hit prefill after the second weight update logs `kv_b_proj LoRA on cached prefix: chunk rows [64], batch tokens 1131` and the assert fires with `AssertionError: LoRA kernel input has 64 rows but the batch metadata describes 1131 tokens` (call path `forward_normal_chunked_kv_core → _chunked_prefix_attn_mha → ColumnParallelLinearWithLoRA.forward → run_lora_a_sgemm → sgemm_lora_a_fwd`); all four engines exit through the assert, the test times out on `no_available_workers`, and there is no `fmhaKernels.cuh` fault because the assert pre-empts the out-of-bounds launch. Reproduced by a second control run, https://github.com/radixark/miles/actions/runs/43019847082 (`chunk rows [64], batch tokens 1525`, same assert, same timeout). This is the parent failure the rule removes. An earlier control attempt (run 43017765625, no trace) passed because no prefix hit happened in that run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not measured: the rule only changes the dispatch of prefix-hit prefills for `kv_b_proj` adapters (absorbed instead of MHA); the e2e above runs at the B200 baseline time of the test (537 s vs. 535 s for the control run).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (isort 7.0.0, ruff 0.15.1 check+format, codespell on the touched files)
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (no user-facing flag added; the rule and its rejections carry their own messages)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (e2e above; no speed benchmark, see Speed Tests)
